It seemed like she treated her customers differently depending on how much each customer would tip. She never smiled and made us feel like we were a huge burden. Never again. Bathrooms were also gross and dirty.

The drinks were very creative and delicious. Food was good. The pig ears, pasta, and panna cotta were the best. I didn't really think the curry goat was good although it was the most recommended entree. Overall, pretty good dinner.

Fairly good. The hype for Korean Fried chicken has finally made it to Nashville. Haha with that being said if you want to try it this place will be the spot. Get your quick fix for Korean style fried chicken! They have marinated and fried style. Also they have variety of Thai dishes and sushi. Owners are super friendly and very accomedating.

Very authentic high quality Thai food ! Beautiful decor with tradional Thai carvings in the entire restaurant. Cashew chicken & green eggplant curry were excellent! The sticky rice with coconut ice creat was rich & satisfying end to a great meal.

I like this place, The food is good, I especially love their Mocha Bubble Tea. It is great for lunch, very inexpensive. The atmosphere is pretty typical, but luckily the lighting is not harsh. The service is excellent. I eat here often from work which is close. Authentic food. Try it out this is easy, fast and good.

This place if fantastic. I have a few other spots around town that I enjoy for Mediterranean cuisine (Tazikis and Kalamatas), but Blu Fig blows them away. I've been there a few times. I took my in-laws and some other family members last Christmas and they were all very impressed (and a few members of the group can be quite picky). I also took my parents to try it out and they live about 40 minutes away from the restaurant. We live on the east side of Cool Springs and take the back way through Concord Road and Nolensville Road to get there. It's worth the trip. The chicken is excellent, but I like the duo plate where you can get the traditional meat as well. The fruit tea is also very good. I believe that I've met both partners and they are both very friendly as is the rest of the staff. They make sure that we have everything we need and keep the drinks full. My only complaint is that they don't have a second location in Cool Springs. If needed, I can point out several establishments that they can replace.

This place is not close to my house, but its worth the 20-30 minute walk. Cheap and mostly authentic Middle Eastern food. The Gyro/Shwarma and Babaganouj were both great. Even better was the little market where I can buy a giant tubs of Tahina, grape leaves, and other hard to find Middle East foods.
First time visitors and we loved it! Seaweed salad was perfect. Then I had the fantasy roll. Amazing presentation and perfectly delicious!

Excellent drinks. Loved the fire and ice cocktail. Very spicy and great flavor! The apps were great too. Had the queso dip and shrimp ceviche. We weren't as impressed with our entrees though. I had the scallops with pork belly and my husband had the mahi mahi which was dry. We would probably opt for the tacos next time. Excellent service and will be back!

What an awesome way to spend Valentine's Day! Unique, different, & authentic if you can get the sofa/pillow table area. The Queens Eight Platter was very filling for two. We will def have to go back for their ceremonial coffee, the place was packed & service was slow, but totally understandable because they were packed. Thank God it was a unique place & I was highly entertained! Lol Their dark African beer is amazing (insert strange, unpronounceable name here) as well. Will definitely go again & bring a group of clean, well kept friends ;)) (gotta eat with your fingers)!!

I was on business in PA and craving Indian. Took a look around an made the drive to the Guru from Horsham. Definitely worth the drive. These guys made me feel like home. Quick service. Food was really tasty without being overpowering. Chicken Masala was very tender. Bring your own bottle of wine and they will pour it. In my case the owner was nice enough to share her own wine stash with me.

My fiancé and I have stopped here twice during lunch time. Both times we received exceptional service. During lunch hours, you definitely do get your money's worth. It comes with an eggroll and a side of soup, along with your entree for only $7.95. (You can't beat that). I believe the soup changes daily/weekly because both times we dined in, it was a different type of soup. We ordered papaya salad, (yummy with different texture of crunch) pad kee mao (noodle dish, had a kick of spice, but was a little too sweet for our liking) and the fish with Thai herbal sauce (fish was fresh, tender and crunchy on the outside; had good flavors).

Delicious ramen, duh. The dumplings (whatever the special is, just get it) were also tasty. The place is very, very small - I'd call it cramped - so be prepared. There's also often a long wait, though I was there on a Tuesday night around 6 pm and was lucky to get at able for two without a wait. Only other negative is I do think it's just a tad overpriced. I mean, it is still soup and noodles (with perhaps a little protein), so leaving down over $20 for a soup and a few dumplings is a little more than I would've liked. But it's by no means not worth it - if you're a ramen fan, or are thinking of trying it, Cheu is a fantastic choice.

Not bad overall, but lacked the complexity of flavor I enjoy from typical Thai food.The sauces were very similar and the spices needed some kick. However, some folks may really enjoy it if they want simpler flavors, and the service was very nice and attentive. I wouldn't say it's worth a special trip out to the Main Line, and there are other options worth trying if you're already out there. Pork/chicken/shrimp rolls - Steamed dumplings with a nice sauce, but very dry stuffing Evil jungle princess - Tasty, crisp vegetables and a generous portion of chicken with this Thai restaurant staple (forgot the name) - Chicken and shrimp in a tamarind sauce served in hollowed out pineapple half. Interesting presentation, crispy vegetables, but sauce was very similar to the evil jungle princess sauce.

Friendly staff, nicely decorated. Looked like customers were mostly nearby college students. Combination bùn was pretty decent, and the shrimp in it was good but on the smaller side. Also the beef was charred. Egg roll could use a little something. Like I said helpful and friendly staff, but I had to flag one down to get the check. Will go back to try their banh mi as they did not have bread today due to an family emergency.

This place is worth the glowing reviews and 5 stars it currently has. Small clean dining space but the important thing here is the food. The chaats are truly a flavor explosion that is custom built for you. I order spicy and find it perfectly so, not too mild but doesn't leave me in tears. The number of lassi flavors and combinations are impressive. I've only had Cardamom & Mango so far but both were delicious!

Being that I am addicted to Boba Tea, this place has the best Lavender Boba Tea I've ever had. We've eaten there a few times and everything is good. They don't rush, so make sure you allow plenty of time to enjoy your meal. The servers are friendly and the atmosphere is pleasant. About 11 tables if I remember correctly. I haven't had a chance to try the shaved ice yet, but according to the reviews, it's the best.
food is great and all at great pricing. don't mind eating here all the time. the variety of food is immense and you wont leave hungry. you gotta love the home style taste. thumbs up and 5 star
they have got to update and clean the ladies room!!!! Food was good, expected more after all the reviews.

I've been to this place twice now: once for the lunch buffet and one time for takeout. For the buffet lunch, I'd like to contribute our late arrival to the food being rather stale because other reviewers seem to love the buffet. The options that were offered were simply not fresh but the flavors were definitely amazing, don't get me wrong! For the takeout, I ordered the chicken biryani, which should have been really called biryani rice with 3 pieces of chicken. I could barely find the chicken in the mound of rice. The other dishes were flavored great and everyone was pleased except for the fact that we were also missing a couple ordered items that we were charged for. And by the time we got it home, it's too much effort to drive all the way back so that person wasn't able to get all their food. I really wanted to like this place as the reviews rave about it but honestly both experiences weren't amazing for me and there's a lot of other Indian restaurants in the surrounding area that may offer better service.
Our first experience at a Vietnamese restaurant and it was amazing. You can taste the freshness of the noodles, the vegetables and the meat. We are sold and will be back again.

Opening night! I love the rich, dark decor of the interior. Gives a great French bistro feel to the place. Staff was fantastic, very attentive. We had the calamari, which was surprisingly different than the norm. It was sweet and spicy! Pork lollipops were, well just redic! Great glaze and the portions were HUGE bites. Fried rice was very savory, we added pork belly to the fantastic Vietnamese sausage in it. Then the ramen... there are no words, but I will try! Pork belly cooked to perfection, crispy edges yet tender on the inside. Charred garlic, the ever perfect Sun noodles. Broth was rich and flavorful. Only drawback was the egg as it was over cooked, but that will be remedied soon enough I am sure. Going back next week, cannot wait, like Christmas in June.

Very poor service. The servers seem uninterested to serve you. The food quality though ok, has dropped since the last time we were there. They also have stopped serving dosas with the buffet which was another disappointment. The halwa served with the buffet was over..and not refilled. All in all..another average Indian restaurant now:(
We went for lunch on a Saturday. The food was delicious and the staff was so courteous. I really felt like I was invited in to their home to enjoy a homecooked Ethiopian meal.

This place is a good neighborhood Thai restaurant - mostly standard dishes, not fancy but good. I like the spicy eggplant. Very nice people who own it, and a nice place to sit outside on a summer evening walking home from the beach. Or better yet get takeout and head over to Island Brewing Company for a pint or two to wash it down while the sun sets.

This place is without a doubt the best lunch deal around. The food is fresh, hand made and delicious.... And only $10 for the buffet. I would strongly recommend it to anyone who enjoys Indian cuisine.

Absolutely horrible. I ordered grubhub for lunch today. I ordered chicken tikka masala and garlic/cheese naan. My order arrived not even 15 minutes later, (I work about a 15 min walk away). This really worried me because they have a menu where you can order your food and they have a lunch buffet. As soon as the driver called and said he has arrived I was not too happy because I was worried and assumed that my food was just scooped from the buffet. Well, I opened my food, COLD. COLD chicken, COLD naans. PISSED. being preggo and hungry and wanting a specific craving only to have it arrive cold and totally tasteless is such a let down. For 2 dinky naans and a 12oz container of food scooped from a buffet cost me $22. A freakin rip-off.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I tried this place for takeout last night. I called in and they said 30 min but it took almost an hour for them to get my food ready. I was not impressed with the lamb curry it was runny and just not what I was expecting. I have eaten indian food all over the PNW and I wouldn't eat here again.The owners were nice they did try and gave me tea while I waited but I don't think I would eat here again.
The best enough said. Quality food and service. Highly recommend. By far worth the trip to Tarpon Springs
Pho bistro is amazing! Every time I eat there I get great food and fast service!! I would highly recommend eating here!!
Never answer the phone, the website is impossible, the food is decent but you can't order it so that's irrelevant!!!! So annoyed.

- TIP: After you eat your meal -- they've got great prices on desserts ($1 baklava) and to-go containers of hummus. - CON: Closes @ 7pm most days. - BOTTOM LINE: Even if the food was mediocre, it'd be worth grabbing considering you get a big plate of mediterranean food for $8. But the food is far better from mediocre -- and I would be ordering it instead of my other go-to take-out mediterranean spots (e.g. Hummus Grill, Al Zaytouna) if it was open later.

Great variety at this $10 lunch buffet. Everything was very flavorful without being over the top spicy. The usual Indian buffet fare (chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, basmati rice, samosas) was present as well as a few dishes I've not tried before. Freshly made naan delivered to the table to compliment the buffet items. A refill on bread was provided at no extra cost. Buffet runs from 11:30am to 3PM. Our server was great. Will definitely go back.

In town for business and found this little restaurant on Yelp. It did not disappoint! The owner is delightful and helped us with our selections. Everything from the egg rolls, jerky, cucumber salad to our three different main entrees was made to order, tasty and had the appropriate heat. If we get back to the area, Phan's Kitchen will definitely be on the schedule

A fabulous little gem in West Philly! I was back in Philly for the weekend, and this placewas the epitome of what I love about the food scene in Philly. 8 of us arrived with a reservation at 8 PM on a Saturdsy night, and we were able to have a little corner of the restaurant to not disturb others while we BYOed. The servers were so friendly, gave us pitchers of water so we wouldn't have to wait for someone to come over, and uncorked out bottles of wine happily. The food came out quickly, and the portions of food were large for the price. A nicer place to come for a nice night out, without spending exorbitant amounts of money. Go here for a date night or a BYO with friends! ps the sticky rice is wonderful.

Super great food, nice family owned staff, multiple fresh options( fresh seafood, vegetarian including vegetarian broth which is pretty unheard of and plus it's good), and clean neat little restaurant would recommend 5/5.

Food was tasteless and dry. Delivery took awhile (combo of lunch time rush & the driver not knowing where to go). Oh and they charged me delivery when it's supposed to be free for lunch time. The guy who answered the phone was pleasant, however. Ehhh probably won't order from here again. Nothing to write home about.
Best Vietnamese in New Orleans. Clean, friendly, consistent. Literally everything is great from the spring rolls to the vermicelli bowls to the cocktails. Lychee mojito is perfect afternoon treat!!
the worst restaurant experience. we were ignored by the waitress

Great takeout (and sort-of eat in) addition to the Main Line. Pakistani owned with lots of sub-continent options from kebobs to curries. Prices are reasonable. They have a few tables if you want to eat in, but most of their business is take away.

My fav place to get the Spicy Beef Noodle soup, Thai Papaya salad, and shaved ice (see photo that someone else posted). Vietnamese Noodle soup (pho)? No Banh Mi? No Curry? No Pad Thai? No Summer/Spring rolls? Good I go elsewhere for the above. A Vietnamese Starbucks-styled cafe. Love the decor.
Very good , very limited vegetarian options , authentic and well done. I visiting twice and was happy ..... and the prices are great ... you can have a great dinner below 20 bucks ...

Food was good. Would have appreciated a more detailed menu. The store was very dirty. Floors dusty, not just snow dirt. Napkins on floor. Tables not wiped. Drink area messy. Soda sprayed all over my hand when I dispensed it. Store was nearly empty at 1:30 pm and 4 staff members behind the counter with few customers.

I live in Bala Cynwyd, and as hard as it is to maneuver to park at this place, it is my "goto" Chinese for a quick Saturday lunch. It never seems particularly busy (which is the only reason I have never tried the sushi / sashimi) but given the freshness of the ingredients used in their standard Chinese fare, I am about to give that a try. Though I sometimes take out, I really prefer eating in, because the dishes I prefer here (Orange Flavor Beef and Sauteed Pan Fried Beef) are SO crispy, travel would spoil the experience. I usually NEVER order beef in Oriental restaurants (except Korean) because it is inevitably the cheapest round money can buy. Little kitchen EXCELS at beef, though my chicken dishes have always been quite good as well. I don't know why this was listed as "Thai" other than they have Pad Thai on the menu. This is really standard Chinese, though the chef is very competent at Bento boxes, and some Indonesian style curry, and stuff like Roti Canai. What impresses me is when I taste fresh cilantro, real garlic slivers, real scallions and fresh broccoli, bell peppers, etc. in a $10-12 dish. There is real attention to detail here, and crispy stuff is crispy, and soft stuff is soft. Food is served PIPING hot. Service is very friendly, and English is well-understood (though they seem very happy to accommodate attempts at broken Mandarin.) Portions are so big that two people can easily split an app and a single entree and leave satisfied. Maybe it helps to be recognized as a regular, but I have never been dissatisfied with a meal, and I've eaten at Yang Ming, San Kee, Suzanna Foo, Han Dynasty, and dropped a lot more $$$ and left less happy. The only complaint I have is that when I order something "extra spicy" there may be an extra dried red and slice of jalapeno tossed in. I suspect the chef does not want to offend Western palates. Anyway, I have eaten in all the oriental restaurants on the Main Line and MOST of the well-know ones in Chinatown and S. Philly and I still come here at least once per month. Maybe I've been lucky with the dishes I've chosen, but I am ready to start checking out some of the less obvious ones. I'll append this review when I do.

Service is god awful! Food is pretty damn good! Living down the street it's hard not to go here for Vietnamese food. Every time I've been here the service is beyond short and rude.. But! The food has always been amazing. Having said that I've been to Asian noodle... My other favorite spot and the service isn't that great, so if you live in the area it's worth it for sure. Quick, easy, and tasty so don't avoid simply because it's attached to a gas station.

I ordered delivery which came in a timely manner. I recommend their chicken sandwiches, they use flavorful toppings and the chicken is juicy. I also got the chicken wings and mac&cheese which were also good! My only criticism is the pricing and the mac&cheese pasta was super soft.

Went with some coworkers on lunch. Food almost took an hr so we had to get it to go. Waitress did not apologize for the long wait or ask if we were doing okay. I was a little disappointed in my portion size of potatoes. (That's just me being fat I guess) Everything was delicious though. I would eat here again if I had to but it wouldn't be my first choice only because I feel like it's a little overpriced for the amount you get and I'm cheap.

I really wanted to love this place. The menu looked promising for a person with multiple food allergies. The items that can be made gluten free, vegan, and vegetarian are clearly marked on the menu. It was nice to have options to choose from. I settled on a few menu items and clearly stated that I wanted the gluten free, vegan versions of the dishes. Gluten Free / Vegan Buffalo Cauliflower - because their buffalo sauce is dairy based, this dish is not buffalo at all. The waitress said that the cauliflower would just come with the buffalo sauce and not the cheese. I was fine with that. When the dish arrived, it was just fried cauliflower, no sauce, no flavor. The manager came and apologized for the mix up. The buffalo sauce had dairy. Another downfall is that our party of 3 was seated in the bar area. It was very loud and difficult to hold a proper dinner conversation. I had a couple of other dishes but I think there was cross contamination. I left with major gastric distress. I probably won't eat here again.

I love this place and go here regularly. The food is consistently delicious and fresh. The waiters are always friendly and nice! If your looking for good Thai food this is the place to go. My favorite is the chicken pad Thai.

So disappointed. Brought a friend from out of town there because I heard it was great..... horrible all the way around. Cold air from floor vents the Tom Kai, bland at best. The muscles small, over cooked and cold. But worst they had me running for a bathroom an hour later. Totally got sick from it. :/ still sick from it. Please do yourself a favor don't eat here. Thai Phooket 1000 times better and half the price.

I am here on work travel, and in 4 days I've been here 3 times! I stopped in on a whim the first night and the food is out of this world. The owner recognized me my second time in and has been nothing but kind and gracious consistently every time I have gone in. I am very satisfied and would suggest this place to anyone. Too bad it's not close to home!!

Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me FOUR TIMES, shame on me! I don't know why we keep revisiting Land of Smile. Wait. I know. It's ridiculously convenient. It's clean. It's friendly. The food is just beyond mediocre. That, and it's overpriced. Thai isn't that unique anymore and I guess I'm too used Thai places being along the same lines as Chinese takeout places to put up with such prices. After giving it a couple tries, we're more than willing to drive another 5 minutes to the next Thai place that we feel are more worth it.

Had the lamb palau. It was extremely bland, not like the ones I've had in Afghanistan. I tried to add salt in the flavor, but it didn't help. I also ordered the garlic naan and I couldn't taste the garlic at all. I probably wouldn't go back

This place might serve the BEST Indian food I have ever had in America! We had the Bollywood dosa, railway cutlet, idli vada sambar n utthapam! Everything we tried exceeded our expectations by tenfolds. The flavors were so authentic that it reminds you of food in India. The place is small and quaint... very much a hole in the wall place. Will definitely return to try more amazing dishes!!!!!!
Food was really good and the staff was great! LOVED the live performer tonight! So talented!! Definitely coming back

We've eaten Thai food all over the world, including Thailand. This place is fabulous! The prices are right, the food is incredible and the service is excellent. They add a flair of 'Mom and Pop" to everything. I thought my taste buds were up to the 'Thai Hot' and they very politely schooled me to go for slightly less spicy, which I truly appreciated. My birthday is this week and this is my first choice for birthday dinners. Enjoy!
Amazing food!!!! Everything from the chutneys, palak paneer, Channa masala, and tandoori player... it's all unreal!

I've only had takeout that hubby picked up. My first order was curry goat, cabbage, rice and peas. It also came with bread. It didn't taste like coco bread, but had a sweet taste and was very soft and fresh. The portion was large (I ate for 2.5 meals out of it). It tasted fresh and it reheated well a few days later. Ordered another takeout of oxtails, peas and rice, callalo, beef patty, and patty coco bread. Will update this review after that meal. I see bad reviews, but so far I've been very satisfied and looking forward to today's meal.
Great place. Not a ton to it, just a noodle bar done right with innovation and little pomp. Price is right, food is delicious, service is great. Broccoli and brisket noodles are musts.

WOAW!! My brother brought me here to eat since he knows how much I LOVE Vietnamese food ! And we have tried every one of them in town but this is BY FAR the most delicious one yet. We had to drink Thia ice tea which was sweet and refreshing ,unlike saigons that taste like sand in water . We also had spring rolls as an appetizer . The service was amazing , the gentleman there was very nice and professional. When they brought the food to the table we couldn't wait to try it . I have the pho Combo with meatballs, beef and chicken . Which I have to say the broth was SOO flavorful and delicious . And my brother had rice noodles with beef . We both kept switching plates to get a taste of both since they were both so delicious. I would recommend this place to anyone who LOVES Vietnamese food as much as I do . I have nothing bad to say about this place :)

Quirky place with really good ramen! Got the miso ramen which was excellent. Every component of the dish blended well together but was also good when eaten individually. I went right before the dinner rush (~4pm). Perfect timing if you want to avoid the dinner crowds. "Weird" decor. Good music.

This place was kind of hard to find. The signage from the road wasn't fantastic and it's location is tucked in the back corner of the first building in the shopping center. When you walk in, however, you're presented with a nicely decorated, well lit (sunlight) indian restaurant with a buffet waiting for you. Having never been to India, I am unable to comment on the authenticity of the dishes presented. What I can say was that I really enjoyed the preparations. Everything I tasted had flavor and it seemed cooked very well. Even dishes that are the american staples tasted better here than I've had at other places. On my plate there was palak paneer (very delicious), a samosa, some sort of vegetable ball in a curry sauce and, of course, the ubiquitous chicken tikka masala. I liked it all. The masala, which I'm not normally a fan of had a surprising amount of flavor. The palak paneer still had some of its green characteristic and had a little tang to it. Nothing was very spicy here, and that doesn't surprise me since it's a buffet. Service was fine, not thrilling but it got the job done. At $10 for the lunch buffet I felt like it was well worth it. My co-workers, who normally aren't adventurous at all even liked it. I'll be back.

Expanded menu, little janky, and family run. However, amazing chicken kebabs!! Hands down, probably the best mediterranean chicken I have eaten in many years. Excellent and unique seasoned rice with a pre-meal spiced soup that was delicious. The menu is much larger than last year. However, stick with the chicken...for reals. It is better than any other med-food I have had in Boise with the exception of 1 Mazzah dish.

One of my favorites in town! I've tried almost everything on the menu... and love it alllllll! These are my favorite dishes: *Starters Shrimp and Pork Rolls Pork Belly Tacos STICKY CHICKEN WINGS *Soups Wonton Soup Pho Brisket add Meatballs Tofu & Tomato Pho *Entrees Lemongrass Chicken and Fried Rice (it comes with white rice so you'd have to sub it) Seasoned Noodles & Chicken (Pho Ga Co) Mint Moon Crepe (Banh Xeo) Chicken and Waffles *Dessert Pandan Waffle with a Scoop of Red Bean Ice Cream *Drinks Lychee Mule ------ something new and I LOVEEE it! This sounds like a lot, but I promise you won't be disappointed! For starters, I picked my three favorite but if I had to pick one, it'd be the sticky chicken wings! You must try how amazing it taste - fresh crispy fried chicken drizzled with this sweet teriyaki glaze and spicy mayo (sometimes I like to sriracha for another dimension of favor). For soups, you can't go wrong with pho - especially to cure a hangover! I first had the tofu and tomato pho during lent season and didn't expect to like it, but I did. The broth in both has really good favor so you can tell they put some love in their pho! For entrees, the most popular and my favorite is the Lemongrass Chicken - flavor, flavor, flavor! Most of the time sub the white rice for brown rice, but sometimes I treat myself and sub it for their deluxe fried rice! The Seasoned Noodles & Chicken is my go-to as well. It's basically the reverse of a chicken pho! You get a small bowl of broth on the side, so you can sip it in between eat bite. The bowl of noodles and sliced chicken is topped with lettuce and fried shallots/onion. There's a small sauce on the side (of soy sauce/sesame) that you can mix in your bowl to your likings. For dessert, pandan waffle and red bean ice cream! If you don't like red bean, don't knock it til' you try it! The green tea ice cream taste just as good. Warm waffles and ice cream, mMm. You can't beat that. For drinks, they have CHAMANGO smoothie! It's soooo good - you get: the tamarid candy straw, cubes of frozen mango, and apricot syrupy goodness! My experiences here have always been great. The food is delicious and made with some mad love. Sometimes they are super busy so be patient because the food is worth it! I heard they're adding some new items to the menu and I can't wait to try them. Highly Recommended!!

I have to revise my review after finding many bones and pieces of inedible meat in the meat/veg combo plate I took home. I usually get the vegetarian dishes with friends, so this was the first time I'd tried their meat. I don't know if it's the norm for them to have bits of bone and inedible fat/gristle, but it made me very sad. I've had the meat dishes from other Ethiopian places around the country and this is the first time I've encountered this.

I can't even tell you how much I love Delicia. I've been a number of times now, and each visit has been superb. Their food is always to die for, whether it's the vegetarian potato tacos or the empanadas. They also have the best margarita I've had in Indianapolis yet. Service was also A+. What more could you ask for?

I went to Thai Country Cafe on a Saturday night around 7pm. It wasn't especially busy that evening so we were able to get seated right away. The food was alright. We were starving so we order the Crab Rangoon as an appetizer and it was delicious. We order the Red Curry with Chicken and Pad See something with Chicken (#43...can't remember the name of the dish and they don't have their menu posted online!). The staff was friendly but never asked how spicy we wanted the Red Curry prepared, which is something you usually expect from a Thai place (scale from 1 to 5). And the Red Curry wasn't prepared that spicy to begin with...additionally there was no basil in the Red Curry dish, which is something that traditionally comes with the dish AND was stated on the menu. So that was a bit of a disappointment. Next time I'm craving Thai, I'll probably explore another restaurant in STL, but this place isn't necessarily black-listed from my future dining options.

Nothing fancy but it does have some delicious Vietnamese food. My son loves it here especially the shrimp rockets and shrimp & pork noodle soup. The beef pho is yummy. Perfect on a cold day too! Great service - quick and attentive but they aren't obnoxious about it. Love coming here.

The first time I ever stepped foot into Smiling Elephant I wasn't to impressed. It was very small inside and not a lot of room to wait to be seated. We waited for about 10 minutes and it took maybe 15 minutes to get our food. After the first bite, I was sold!!!!! The food was delicious. I couldn't believe it. Goes to how you cannot judge a book by its cover. If your looking for a small community type of restaurant the Smiling Elephant is the place to be!
The food was reasonably priced, and the service was fast and knowledgeable about the menu. I really liked the Pho and would recommend this as the best Pho in Santa Barbara.

This is my FAVORITE place to eat. The breakfast, lunch, and dinner choices are amazing. The past 7 years I have been enjoying this place's atmosphere and food. The owner/chef uses the local farmer's seasonal produce in his meal selections.

Stopped here for a quick lunch during the week while in area for work. Service was prompt and the food was tasty. I will say it was slightly more expensive then the Vietnamese I am used to getting in the city and I was disappointed to not find the usual condiments on the table to spice up my meal. That being said, the menu was clear and I ate the whole plate.

Amazing place!!! Went a couple of times for lunch, it's fast (except once during lunch hour where you I couldn't find a seat!!) Food was great and fairly inexpensive :0 Great vegetarian choices!! Will def become a regular at this place!

Wow this place is good! It's quaint, tasty, and well priced! They have a great selection of good food for all diet types I.E.: vegan, vegetarian, meat eaters, and pesketarian. They have something for everyone and trust me it will taste good. I really enjoyed their Pho

Large restaurant with a good amount of people seated inside when I walked in. Being alone, I just sat at the front (bar style area). Ordered the pho dac biet ($8.50) and the mango boba ($3.50). The mango boba was tall and skinny. Mango taste was definitely there, but there was so much sugar and I could taste powder. The boba itself was like biting into a stiff snow ball, rather than chewy. The pho featured a flavorful broth with a lot of LEAN meat, which is hard to find in most restaurants. Soft, slippery noodles here compared to stiff in another places. They gave me as much basil as I planned to use. Overall, good pho, but skip the drink.

I've eaten at several P. F. Changs locations and this one is by far my least favorite. Lack luster service. Not to mention the apple in my salad still had the sticker on it. With KOP only 15 minutes away and several other restaurants near you would think that they would attempt to be more attentive to their patrons.

My husband and I went there this morning for breakfast . soon after we parked our car and was up on the sidewalk a lady said to us " have a seat anywhere you like " . Very eager for us to sit . There was a sign of the breakfast specials and a breakfast menu that was brought to us . The menu was one sided single menu with few options . I ordered the Pumpkin pancake special with eggs and sausage . My husband ordered the 2 eggs with toast which came with potatoes. As we sat we noticed that the restaurant next door , ( it was so close that I thought it was all one place) there was a line of people waiting to sit over there . I should have known that was a clear clue to get in line over there . The breakfast arrived to the table next to us , 2 eggs , toast and sliced tomatos . The toast was a 1/2 inch thick by 4 inch x 1 inch wide piece of bread toasted . I swear , it was literally 2 bites of toast . Now our breakfast arrives , I had ordered my eggs scrambled with cheese . The pumpkin pancakes with about 4 inch round and just ok, sort of doughy .. my eggs were the fake eggs with barely any cheese . The sausage was 2 brown and serve links , I recognise the stuff as I buy it . My husbands eggs were real , he had them cooked over medium . His potatoes were served room temp... and very small portion . I looked to be about 1/3 of a cup if that . His toast was the same as served at the table next to us . 1/2 inch thick , 4 inch long by 1 inch wide . Literally 2 bites of toast . No butter on it so my husband asked for butter and jelly , she brought the butter which was a few cut chunks of butter cut off a stick of butter and the jelly was a pepper jelly . She said that is the ONLY jelly that they have . I fully see why there was a line waiting NEXT door . We also had 2 cups of coffee .... our breakfast cost $18 . I was waiting for our server to ask how our breakfast was ... no one asked how we liked it . Its not that it was any one thing that was just not right , the whole experience as a whole was just wrong . PLEASE NOTE THAT IF YOU LOOK ON THEIR WEB SITE THERE IS NOT AN EMAIL ONLY A PHONE NUMBER .
Place is small and service can be slow. But still excellent pho and beef stew soup. The sandwiches aint bad either.
Adorable small place with indoor and outdoor seating. Food was good with good portion. Service was top notch. Always had full glasses of water.

I ordered takeout: the combo special (jerk BBQ chicken and curry chicken) w/ rice and peas and cabbage along with festivals (2/$1) and man was i blown away by how good the food was. Definitely will be going there again. Though parking is a real pain though.

First off I would give this restaurant a 3 1/2 star for the food. But the service was amazing so this is based on my overall experience. I got the Pad See Ew with beef. The flavors of the dish were good but the beef was overlooked and dry. The establishment is family owned and the sisters were all nice and hospitable. Great for kids.

Went to this place based on online reviews and was not disappointed. The staff are very warm and helpful if you need help deciding what you want to eat. The chicken dumplings were average. But the whole snapper in spicy Thai curry was amazing. The portions are good and the taste was great. This is a beer and wine place with limited options but the food will keep you busy. It's a nice casual dining option in the heart of Chinatown.

If you are looking to stretch your dollar and get the most amount of decent quality food and live near the colleges; look no further. The food is good but defiantly not worth going out of your way to come here. If you don't have a choice and have to get something in the area then this might be a good option.

Here is the deal. I live close by this place and love the food here. When I feel like a hot Thai dish to go I usually come here and chill at the counter or take out. I have also been here with my lady to eat as well. Meun Fan Thai, (most will call it Mesa Thai, cause its on the mesa, has nothing to do with the old restaurant Mesa Thai) is a small mom and pop or I should say mom and daughter run restaurant, with great service and smiles. The Beef Salad is one of my favorites and the curries are all pretty tasty. This is great place to come and keep it low key and cheap. Very local place and we seam to love the new owners that have brought wonderful fresh Thai food back to the Mesa.

Nice environment, the bartender "Jason" could use some assistance with his people skills. But I must remind myself that there is a reason why guys like this are working low wage positions. That kind of soured my attitude. Sushi was delicious. And delivered quickly. I overall really like Fulins, particularly the Spring Hill location.
Amazing food, best Caribbean/Soul food restaurant in Delaware county. Great customer service, value, and portion size.
A little on the salty side for me. I think some of the flavors are overpowering in the food. I would prefer Han dynasty any day for Szechuan Chinese food.

Watch your statement!!! They changed my $11 tip to $14 probably thinking I wouldn't notice! I will never be returning. Food was okay, but lacking in spices so I might have given them another shot but not after altering my payment. Beware!

I came to this restaurant with very high expectations and was sadly disappointed. First, the positive: the food was delicious (esp. the sweet potato mezze was exceptional and the hummus was tasty). The venue was nicely appointed for group pictures, etc. However, parking was a pain (only available on the street in the area). The food was very overpriced (a $19 salad with chicken that was truly minuscule, for example, and $5 for 6 slices of rather odd tasting parsnips). The service was also perfunctory; we were first seated right by the door somewhere very cold and then moved to a table awkwardly adjacent to the hostess stand, not private at all, and the waitstaff was clearly annoyed that we needed to be in and out (for a flight) in 45 minutes. For a large group wanting to brunch together, I can see how this would be a nice spot, but generally I would not return unless a friend was desperate to try it.

The atmosphere is nice and quaint; it is not big inside, but you certainly don't feel cramped. Very good! I had Chicken Vindaloo and Bhindi Masala and my wife Chicken Tikka Masala .....it was extremely tasty!!!! The portion size was huge and came with rice. I also had the Garlic naan bread which was amazing . I couldn't finish it all, but certainly tried my best. The menu was very diverse and affordable. I highly recommend for anyone in the area who loves good Indian food.
Service was excellent and food was very unique. Really enjoyed everything we ordered. Love the decor and ambience! Nice addition to city dining.
The Thai basil is my favorite and if you don't order the Thai donuts for desert, you're missing out on life!

While traveling through Florida this restaurant came highly recommended and it did not disappoint! The service was quick I was in and out for lunch and under 25 minutes and the food was fantastic I will return here every time I am in the area!

Delicious Malaysian cuisine. There are plenty of soup and noodle dishes under $10 that are more than enough for a meal. I usually get the noodles in soup because the sweet and sour broths are really excellent and they're what keep me coming back. Favorites include the Prawn Mee, Java Mee, Asam Laksa, and Seafood Tomyam. The Roti Canai is as good as everyone says. Everything else I've had here has been good, the noodle soups are just my personal go-to. I like that you can spend upwards of $25 on a jumbo prawn dish (and I bet it's worth it) or $7 on a big noodle or rice dish that is just as filling. I like the tall window tables for two, which seem to usually be available. The service tends to be good, and I like that they will try to talk you out of ordering certain weird things if they don't think you can handle it.

Delicious, inexpensive, fast and very friendly service! We stopped by here the other day and were both impressed. I was really happy with the super chicken gyro with avocado added, and my boyfriend kept going on about how good the Z gyro was. We will definitely eat here again to try different gyros!

Will not eat here again! I must admit I have had some very nice meals here in the past. Their basil chicken is very good, tasty and nice bit of spiciness. Last night we ordered basil chicken and kung pao chicken. Could not eat it! The kung pao was tasteless and the meat was absolutely horrible. Not one piece of chicken was edible. Grizzle and chewiness in every bite. Basil chicken still tasted good but the chicken was the same as the other dish.
Worth the 10$ and worth the wait. Best food truck in Philly bar none.

Israelí food meets comfort food plus bacon. If you are looking for something light and a little different this is your place. Service was good and friendly. Ambiance was hipster and trendy. Food is tasty and not crazy over priced. Good if you don't eat meat, but there is bacon and other meat if you do. I went during lunch and sat at the bar. I didn't order a drink but there prices were in line with any other trendy bar. The cocktails looked fresh but not over the top. I ordered the whipped feta with honey and the country fried cauliflower. I probably could have stuck with just the feta as the pita are pretty big and filling but it was worth it to try the cauliflower. The cauliflower was a slightly spicy creamy on the palate dish. And the feta had a nice juxtaposition between the salty of the feta and the sweet of the honey. Overall I'm now stuffed, content and ready for a nap. Mission accomplished.

Wonderful Experience. This review is a bit long but covers everything. Reputation Smiling Elephant proudly displays many local awards throughout the years. They are known for their Pad Thai and they have a daily rotation of curries. Food Overall, excellent food that is not typical of other Thai restaurants. All original recipes of favorite dishes some nice new recipes as well. Tom Yum soup was a pleasant surprise. It contained large pieces of vegetables in broth, as opposed to a typical bowl of broth with tiny pieces of diced veggies. I added shrimp, which was one jumbo prawn with a little too much TSP, but tasty none the less. I needed chop sticks to eat the veggies and could have used a knife for the shrimp. Pad Kra Pao was a new dish for me. It is chopped Thai pork barbecue with a unique sauce. IT was a vinegar type yet sweet. It had some heat and was well balanced. The blend of mushrooms, basil and cilantro was wonderful. It was chopped just right to eat with chop sticks. The rice was great, but just too much for my blood sugar levels. Drinks This place is a tea heaven. For the first time in my life, I tried Thai iced tea UNSWEETENED and without the "milk". It was so refreshing. There were many varieties of teas served both hot and iced. Menu Layout/Pricing Even the server admitted it was hard to read. All meals are Prix Fixe, but that price is hidden on one page of the menu. So, as you read the menu, you do not find any prices except add-on prices for meat or shrimp. Some descriptions mention types of meats you can add, but do not describe them. You have to hunt them out later in the multi-page menu. My major disappointment was pricing on the drinks. I am used to getting free refills on hot tea. All drinks are single serving and there are no refills. hrmph Decor Wonderfully done with traditional Thai prints and artwork. The wood (bamboo?) treatment on the walls made me feel as if I were in a Thai mountain house, even though I've never been to one. Service Prompt, and polite Parking Now, this is interesting. There is a small lot out front that is not very well laid out. I squeezed my SUV into a space and hoped I could get it out. If not, I could have driven over the sidewalk. There is a lot of congestion in the small lot. It was not until after I parked and walked to the door that I saw there was additional parking in the rear.

Great portions. Kid friendly. Tasty food and awesome staff. My kids loved the carnitas tacos and mexicano hot dog. And they didn't make a big deal about my daughter wanting all the toppings on the side. Oh and don't forget the guacamole. Yum!

The food here was creative and very good. I had the Israeli salad and the mushroom "toad in a hole" and enjoyed both. However, it was pricier than I expected, with a lunch for 2 coming in over $60 (no alcoholic drinks on that tab). It really ought to have 3 $$$. The decor is kind of upscale warehouse but tastefully done. My main complaint is the noise level. We were there for lunch, and I had to raise my voice considerably so the hostess could even hear me even though the place was only about 2/3 full. I realize that noisy is (unfortunately in my opinion) the trend for new restaurants, but this was too loud by any reasonable standard. Get some sound battens up on that ceiling, guys!

I have been looking for the best Pad Thai since moving to Philly in June and, by jove, I think I've found it!! I tried to eat the food as slow as possible so I could enjoy every bite but man was it hard. Also, DJ is super sweet and very attentive. I will be back...probably tonight for dinner...

When you walk in to the modest street front, past the kitchen and 50 year old landscape photos of Greece your welcomed by the enveloping, appetite stirring smell of fresh baked bread - served still warm and with a real crust and you know you're in a place that cares about their food. Started off with a sampler of the hot seafood appetizers. They were all done to perfection. The octopus was probably most memorable for the way it was prepared - first chargrilled and then arriving bathed in a sauce... Just order it is all I can say. For dinner we split the chargrilled plate of heavenly meats. I don't think I've ever enjoyed pork kebabs or any type of pork as much as I just did. To finish off the waiter gave one of the most unique goodbye's - "when you come back be sure and try our lamb, it's a signature dish. See you again!" If the food wasn't so amazing I would give 5 stars for all around fantastic and sincere service that is hard to find and easy to recognize. Plus having sampled the lamb in our chargrilled mixed plate - I know he must be right that it's a signature dish.

The Positives: The food is delicious...loads of meat on the gyro and the gyro salad. I highly recommend both. Their pita bread is hot and irresistible. We have eaten there many times and I am sure we will return. The Negatives: It is a tiny place and tables/seating isn't very comfortable. They also do not offer free water. You must buy a soda or bottled water. This isn't a big deal for some, but drinking water is one of the ways we try to cut expenses so that we can eat out more often. (Really? You can't provide a small plastic cup?) They also ran a coupon in the Entertainment Book which they will not honor. Finally, on several occasions I have found small bits of bone in the meat. Again, not a huge deal, but not exactly ideal. Recommendation: Watch for a coupon and get food "To Go"

Hasan is one of my favorite people I've ever met. Expect him to go into great detail about what chaat is, with a huge smile. I've seen him give this spiel half a dozen times ("a little sweet, a little spicy...") and he clearly revels in it every time. I've been in a couple times with my father and he always asks how my "daddy" is. For my fiancé and I, a staple of weekends when the weather is nice is stopping into Mood Cafe on the way to Clark Park for a lassi, some chaat, and of course, some great conversation. The menu looks quite complex, but I'm pretty sure the only real differences are the types of meat and how spicy you want it (he always makes mine mild for me), and he basically makes the rest of it up. The salad chaat is amazing, although don't look for it on the streets of India, as he admits to it being a personal creation. The lassi choices are also a bit overwhelming, but don't worry, you can't go wrong. Personally I love the honey papaya. If you order mint, he will go pick it from where he is growing it under a tree outside. And always expect Hasan to give you a second cup with what wouldn't fit into the first cup, because that's just the kind of guy he is.

The chicken wrap lunch special with the fries was really good. I ordered it literally 7 days in a row, I then ordered the beef kabob platter the platter was tasteless with no seasonings and spices. The beef kabob meat was hard and stringy and not able to be eaten. Maybe they did not have fresh meat that day I am not sure. This place is an ok place if you are stuck for food.

This place was great! The food is spectacular and it just keeps coming (7 courses!) a little hard to find (as the door is locked which threw us off a little). Also watch out for the surprise show halfway through dinner! The only reason this isn't a 5 star review is because it took about 10 minutes for us to get a water refill (which was tough for some of us after spicy food!) otherwise extremely reasonably priced for a great experience!

A southern indian gem in a suburban setting. I go nearly once a week for lunch and have been on a weekend a few times. Delicious, savory, and well spiced southern indian dishes are a delight. The very simple decor is underwhelming but fod more than makes up for it. The staff is very friendly, attentive, and fast.

I drive by this place a lot and decided today I would try it. Pros- I ordered the Mezza w/ falafel, which is supposed to be a sampler platter. The hummus was very good, and so was the tabouli. Both tasted very fresh, as well as the feta cheese and black olives. The staff was friendly. Cons- I got my order to go, and didn't check the container before I left. The platter was supposed to come with pita bread to eat the hummus with, I didn't get any. And instead of kalamata olives, I was given black olives. Also, the music was a little too loud. Made it hard to hear the staff as he was making recommendations, and so probably not a place I would sit down to eat with someone and hang out. I still think this place has potential. I'll go back to try some of the other menu items. Hopefully I'll get whats described on the menu next time.

Una experiencia deliciosa! Un lugar pequeño con mucho sabor. Para ser mi primera vez comiendo comida de estos países, muy rica. El servicio muy amable. Hasta pudimos probar los gandules dulces! Se los recomiendo.
Thai Place is on the small side and fills up quick!, but the food is worth the wait and I am happy that they are busy in these economic times. Massaman curry never disappoints.

THE BEST restaurant in Philadelphia, period! We've been coming here for years & it is & always has been consistently AMAZING! Everything is fresh & made to order. It is always busy, which is great. The service is always friendly, efficient & smooth! Even when it gets crazy busy here, it's always "service with a smile!" Nothing is too much to ask for, more napkins, ice.. whatever! I love the staff, they work very hard! The chefs are also so nice & friendly. It's really cozy & friendly here, they always remember us & greet us with big smiles! I love these gals... and boy oh boy, can they filet a fish or what?! We LOVE the Shrimp Pil-Pil, of course the Octopus, salads are great....Branzino! Oh, & save room for the RICE PUDDING! The best I've ever had! THANK YOU D'mitri's!
Great atmosphere, friendly staff. Loved the Papas Rellena. A Caribbean potato appetizer similar to a knish but with a twist! & they were kind enough to host The Gathering's Bar Church tonight.

As a vegetarian, this place rocks!!! Their Brussels sprouts are awesome!!! To top it off the service was fantastic!! Our waitress suggested the bread pudding and we were blown away! We will be back soon!

This Dominican spot is delicious in every sense of the word. The food, the ambiance, the hospitality is all excellent. They have awesome lunch special prices for an enormous amount of food. Tons of different options. I love that they have food ready to go if you're in a rush or a bunch of other options the kitchen can make if you want to sit down and have a feast. You can bring your own alcohol and have a fiesta! I really love this place :) They also deliver which is awesome. I live and work close by so I eat here a few times a week and as long as their open, I'll be coming back!
Our party had Chicken Satay combo, Thai basil eggplant and pumpkin curry , loved it all. We will be back when in area.

If you're looking for a cozy, romantic atmosphere with a touch of traditional Greek comfort, this is your place. Zorba is snuggled in Fairmount in Philly, but something about the location makes it a hidden gem. Not only are you able to get away from the trendy side of Philadelphia, you can also find a nice neighborhood to enjoy quality food. I had the pita and hummus for appetizer- absolutely delicious. For dinner, Avgolemono (lamb shank with artichoke sauce) I have never had lamb cooked to perfection. It was so moist, the side of vegetables and rice was so filling. Totally worth the wait for it to be cooked. (Tip: If you want to try this dish, make sure to call ahead and check to see their availability for lamb). I must say, Greek coffee really hits the spot. It has a very rich, chocolatey taste to it. And the amount served is perfect for ending your meal. I assume the restaurant is family owned and operated, including the waiters. We had the same waiter the two times we went and he was VERY accommodating to where we wanted to sit, given the restaurant isn't that spacious. Here's one of the things I really appreciated: The restaurant is always busy, and there can be long waits for when you come without reservation. However, while you are dining waiters do not rush you to get out or to leave once you've signed the check. Cannot wait to go back!

One of the best meals I've had in Philly. Everything was great. Here are some of the highlights: * The squid * the steak * Good service * Good prices * Easy to access neighborhood In general, Philly is a foodie town and this place is one of the top food places in a foodie town.

Ate dinner here with a few friends last week and everyone enjoyed their meals. The Pad Thai isn't the 'normal' Pad Thai you'd find at other Thai restaurants but the Smiling Elephant's take on the dish is still great! Also had one of the flavored teas and it was very good with the meal.

This is just okay Thai food. I've been here a handful of times and I always ask for the food to be extra spicy and it never is. The prices are also high and the service is mediocre. It takes a long time just to place an order.

I can't say I'm a connoisseur of Indian food since my experience prior to visiting Spice was limited to the Darbar Indian buffet downtown, but everything I had was delicious. Started with the Vegtable Samosa appetizer which was large enough to serve as a meal in and of itself (only $2.99!) and then shared Naan, Chicken Tiki Masala, Tandori Chicken, and an eggplant dish (Bharta?) that the owner recommended. Dishes were perfectly cooked and made to our requested "medium" spiciness. (Just enough to make you break a few beads of sweat, but not painfully hot!). Food came out amazingly fast and both the server and owner were unusually friendly (I suppose this could be a plus or minus depending on your service preference). Prices were very reasonable and we had plenty of leftovers. The one and only downside about this place is the location. The strip mall offers plenty of easy parking but there is zero ambiance. Oh, and did I mention it's BYOB? Just to end on a high note.

Simply fantastic! I got here with my wife, in-laws and my 2 y-old daughter, at 5. We spent 2 hours, ate like kings, drank a few beers and the check was very fair. The paella was great. Thanks to Matt, we were incredibly well served. Get here early and get the upstair room. I will definitely return here.

I had lunch there. Portions are VERY small. Their kabob is so mediocre. Their rice is not good. This place is definitely not representative of delicious middle eastern cuisine especially for Kabobs. Sorry Sansom Kabobs you gotta increase your portions and quality.

Well what an awesome restaurant across from London Drugs in T&T Market plaza. I ordered the #27 Bun Bo Hue. Kim works the front and her business partner Thu is the chef. Kim is very friendly and recommended it to me. The broth is everything in a good bowl of Vietnamese soup and it didn't disappoint. It was delicious. The ingredients were fresh and I could watch Thu make the soup. I couldn't believe all the steps in a bowl of soup, but she was busy. I had a Vietnamese iced coffee and it was great. My bill was $15.17. They will definitely be welcomed in the neighbourhood. The restaurant, is new, clean, bright and nice. I would highly recommend this restaurant.

Lilly's is by far my favorite Vietnamese place in New Orleans. Not only is the family so sweet... The food lives up to all the great reviews. The pho broth is delicious and so flavorful, the sauce on the bun is awesome, and the shrimp and avocado salad is amazing! The spring rolls are also key. I haven't had a bite at Lilly's I didn't like. Also the coconut candies they give with your check are delicious!! I would give 10 stars if I could!

While visiting New Orleans, a few locals brought me here. Such a wonderful place! I ordered a mint lemonade, which was so delicious! And the Gyro which comes with hummus, pita bread and a salad. I was quite surprised to see the way it was presented, my past experiences have been of the gyro wraps, everything was seperate here, more of a build your own type plate. By far the best Gyro I've had. Attached is the market, with imported items, nothing caught my eye to buy, but it was a nice experience.

Really enjoyed our meal here. We had one beef dish and two veggie: the key wat was really good and the two pea dishes were one hit and one sort of miss. I'd like a little more variety on the veggie menu, but it's probably wise for a new place to keep the menu simple until the business justifies the complexity. I didn't feel the meal was over-priced at all; but then I'm usually suspicious of places where the food is too cheap. You know, like the places with dollar menus. I will definitely come back here and recommend it with no hesitation!

This place is a hidden gem in Mt Juliet! Wow! I am a die hard Woodlands Nashville fan when it comes to Indian food, but Persis has stolen my heart with their Gobi Manchuria and Bhindi Masala. Small and unassuming in a strip shopping center off the main drag by Providence, but don't let this fool you. The space is adorable and clean in white and gray decor, and the delicious smell hits you when you open the door. Our server was so sweet and friendly, and agreed with our decision of Gobi Manchuria for an appetizer. I will now get this every time I come. The spice is perfection. I always err on the side of caution and get mild spice, and it was perfect without being overpowering. The Bhindi Masala was a generous portion of tender chunks of okra cooked with tomatoes and onions, and the rice was cooked to perfection. My dining friend ordered the Vegetable Biryani, and I think I probably ate a lot of her food, too! Once again, a huge portion of food and the flavor was on point. I actually left my credit card here the first time I came in, and ended up ordering take out when I went to pick it up. If you do take out, call ahead. It can take 20-30 minutes. I have nothing bad to say--I'll be driving to Mt Juliet for my Indian cravings from now on. Yummy!

I came in from the city to visit family and we got take-out from this joint a couple nights ago. Let me just say, this is the best Thai I have had in all of Philadelphia and the surrounding areas. And I've tried a lot. And I've been to Thailand twice. Just great food. Had the: Mussels - I can eat them every single day. They were so perfectly balanced. Pad Thai (both chicken and shrimp) - reviews are correct. Spot on great. Yellow Curry Shrimp - my lady doesn't like the spice so we went with this milder version and I don't regret it for a second. Next time I'm doing the red curry. Cucumber salad - crisp and fresh with a hint of sweetness. Tom Yum soup - also really good. I'm coming back next time I'm in town to try different items and if they're as good as this first experience, my 4 stars will become 5 real quick. PS, even my family members who are on the fence about Thai food were completely converted. Great, great Thai spot.

My wife and I have been a few times recently and really like the place... The food has been great and the place is very nice inside... They have a great happy hour; but I typically still order off the full menu!

Ehh I'll round up from 3.5 stars. This place was alright. Didn't knock my socks off, but it was serviceable. The garlic naan was kind of a let down in comparison to the pictures I saw online. Didn't seem to match that but was moderately tasty. I had the lamb Marsala which was, again, ok. The meat chunks where a bit more fatty then I'd like. It's pretty fancy and the service was good. Can't complain about the price either. So overall, it's good for a meal but I wouldn't take a date there or anyone I want to impress.

I LOVE this place and the people there are very friendly. The food is very original and ingredients are high quality. Check it out next time you're in the mood for something fresh and out of the ordinary!

Literally worst service ever. Goodish food, very skimpy wine pours, cute spot except for the extremely creepy bathroom. Overall 2 stars because I repeat: worst.service.ever. We had to go inside to ask our server for wine after 12 minutes of sitting with empty wine and water glasses, mid meal. On a Sunday. Not super busy. Never going there again.

Food is exceptional, but their customer service is lacking! The reason why I stay away! As far as this place being better than miss saigon or pho & deli, just depends on what you are getting. Its all perspectives on the food.

Stopped in for Sunday brunch on a whim and really enjoyed my Cornbread Biscuits with Chorizo-Thyme gravy. The cornbread was sweet and moist; the gravy had a great flavor with th eight amount of heat. Sadly, only brewed coffee available. A legit Cafe con Leche would've been a great compliment.
Amazing food -- super flavorful. Highly recommend the chicken platter and the chicken patties. Owners are great (and very hardworking!). A must-stop place if you're in the Tampa area.
I popped in last minute for a quick bite! The spring rolls were delicious, and they do this thing where they make Tacos out of bao bun stuff. so yummy. super clean, great decor too. I'll be back!

We eat at Baguette Deli once a month, which is more than we eat at any other establishment. We go for the noodle bowls - they are delicious! Just the right combination of ingredients. I advise you to use the lime and tear the basil into the soup before mixing in all the sauces - they really add a great depth of flavor. 5 stars for the noodles! 4 stars overall because they don't put very much meat in their sandwiches, which are otherwise delicious, and their egg rolls had this weird rubber-like thing in it... maybe an overcooked mushroom? I pulled one out and it looked and tasted like rubber. The bread they use is amazingly crispy on the outside, but only a fine layer - not like hard like many other places. I prefer more meat and mustard, which they also skimped on. If they have biegnets, get one for the road - they are really yummy!

The absolute best place to go in West Philly! Hassan will make your day by welcoming you to his home! He will ensure you are happy with every choice of lassie or chaat, and always entertain you with something special. Hassan is a gem here in West Philly and I always look forward to being here. Let him suggest new Flavors and things if you're adventurous - hell always make sure you're happy with his creation. :)

Get ready to have some stale food with sad faces. The food served is of poor quality and seem like it was not freshly cooked. The host was also not welcoming . I wont suggest going to the place. Worst Indian food I ever had

I'm not vegetarian, which is why this wouldn't be my first choice for Indian. What I've had was very tasty though! Try the kofta! The food is decent, and offered mild or spicy. The Korma and Paneer Tikka Masala are on point!! The samosas are great as well. The location is convenient and prices are lower than most Indian Restaurants I've been to. It's authentic and the portions are large. I highly recommend for vegan or vegetarian people!

I used to dine at Albasha weekly in Baton Rouge. When I found out they were also in Metairie, I made my fiancée abandon our old middle eastern favorites. Albasha is all we eat now! It's worth the drive. Typically do take out. Love the big mezze platter of everything . Or the combo chicken schwarmA and gyros is my favorite ! We love Albasha!

Yay! I'm a fan, but not of their prices and cramped space. We opted to get ramen for dinner in the city. This was our first time venturing for ramen. I hopped onto yelp and decided to head over here. I remember reading about this place on foobooz before so i was curious. Plus it seemed more fun than the other ramen places. It was almost a perfect night. We got parking right across the street and seated immediately at the bar. Sad to say i kept on bumming elbows with the woman next to me. I wish there was a bit more elbow room. Note to the owners: elbow room is a necessity when eating noodles! Just try eating with your elbows tucked in, not so fun eh?!? Also, i would have to minus points for the bartender. He served me a flight of the sake (one was soju). However, he did not shake the sake. It was a nigori, i mean how could he not know. Sad to say i just let it go, usually i would have mentioned something but it was just a shot. Okay i've vented. We ordered the mung bean and the chicken bun. Both were delicious and the bun was not of the white dough kind that was expected. This one was more of the brown flakey kind. Nevertheless it was good and i would order it again. They did forget to bring out the special cheeseburger bun that the bf ordered. Next was the garlic flavored wings. The carnivorous bf devoured it. I had the smoked fish ribs. This has got to be one of the best thing i ever ate. It was a paku which is a cousin of the piranha. The dish was very flavorful. The skin was crispy and perfect. It was definitely a party in my mouth. We ordered the pork and miso cod ramen. The cod was cooked perfectly with a little crispness. The noodles were cooked al dente, it was great. The broth was mediocre, i'm trying to remember it but there was really nothing memorable about it. The bf finished his bowl completely. Yikes! we got the bill and for 2 people it was about 86 with tip. What a pricey ramen experience!

Worst pho I've had in a while. The tendon is harder than plastic. They need to take that crash of the menu, if they don't know how to cook it. It's an offense to be served it. The pho is also overly oily. The flashy ads on the front of the store are a facade hides that this place is rather bad.
Love this BYO Pho place. So glad it's getting cold again, just to have an excuse to go out for Pho here. Prices are very reasonable and the food is delicious.

Love this place! There's nothing like it in Nashville and if you're looking for authentic Greek food that isn't made up of the same typical menu, then you need to go here. The space is vibrant and fun with an amazing outdoor patio, and awesome Greek rap music! I got the Roka Salad and loved it, but next time I would add lamb or chicken. My husband got the Korinthian Lamb with fries and it was incredible! The lamb had so much flavor and was so tender. I'm still craving it! We went during the grand opening so it was insanely busy, but I noticed the entire family was working their butts off. I love that Greko is family run business and you can feel how much pride they take in their food and how much they want you to be a part of it. Great food, great service, and a fun atmosphere. The best part is that it's traditional Greek food, but not what you would get at all the other Greek restaurants, its truly unique!
If you like Mediterranean/Middle Eastern cuisine, eat here

Was pleasantly surprised with the Naf. Ordering was quick, easy and they had a friendly staff. Overall the food was delicious. Tasted very fresh and was very reasonably priced. They give you perfectly baked pita bread with your order which was a great addition to the meal. Naf, definitely will be back very soon

There are a lot of cool new restaurants popping up in Nashville and this one stands out at the top. My wife and I used to go out regularly but life with a baby has obviously cut down on that quite a bit. That being said, we tend to put a little more thought into date night. This was one of the best dining experiences we've had in Nashville. The menu is perfect for having a couple courses - very interesting, small starter options - they have a 4 for $16 option - perfect way to try multiple things, but still not fill up. Then for the mains... the Pork Belly Gnocchi was every bit as good as it sounds. Overall - I rarely take the time to review restaurants but really want to give this one the praise it deserves.
Great food and great prices. Delivery is always super hot. Delivery minimum is only $15 which is great!

Really good food at reasonable price. The restaurant doesn't look too appealing from the street, as it is below street level, and looks more like a take-out place from the front. However, there is a small, but nice dining room in the back. Food was delicious, and we enjoyed the rich use of spices - a nice change from Persian shish kebab, which we frequently enjoy.

I love a trendy place with delicious food. Pho was flavorful, didn't need to add any condiments. Banh mi was fresh, bread was perfect mix between crispy and soft. Tried salmon and lemongrass spring rolls, both good but loved the salmon ones. Peanut sauce was also spot on, most places screw this up badly. And service was so attentive and genuinely friendly! Prices are higher, but you're also paying for ambience, quit crying about the prices! Go eat at a crappy place, you get what you pay for, wah, wah, cheapos! Also, loved the presentation of the food. Everything was well thought out, well designed, if only this could be the future of Vietnamese food!

Great first experience! Everything tasted fresh and home made. I was able to speak to the owner Toni, and what a pleasure it was! No wonder why they are packed on lunch time. Came around 11:50am, no one was here. It's 12:10 and the place is packed! Keep it up Basil!!
This place is so freaking good! The owner is so nice as well, a genuinely hard working man who treats his customers like family! Definitely coming back!

For fast food, I love the options - the variety of healthier meal choices is a real bonus. The reason for the low score is due to the cleanliness of the tables. The dining area stays perpetually dirty, even when the restaurant is not busy.

Everything I have had so far is delicious! As soon as you walk in, your mouth will start watering because of the smells and spices that fills the restaurant! You can also order online and orders are ready to be picked up on time or sooner!

This was the first ethnic restaurant I ate at in Tucson many years ago. I had heard that it was serving Kurdish food, and I was excited to try it as I have eaten very delicious Kurdish food (homemade meals) in Phoenix. Kurdish food is actually more gourmet; the dishes can be very complicated, and the flavors are complex. I tried their Pillaw (a thin puff pastry type shell stuffed with cubes of beef, chicken, rice, and very delicious seasonings). When I told my friends (Kurdish) in Phoenix that I had tried Pillaw, they were very jealous, saying they had never made that particular dish. This was truly a gem of a restaurant (14 years ago). The most recent time I ate there, Pillaw, along with some of the other more ethnic Kurdish dishes, had been taken off the menu. Instead, it seemed to be more like a typical middle eastern type restaurant offering mainly gyros for the entree. Another disappointment was the change from authentic Kurdish music to heavy rock--a type of music played more for the enjoyment of the young servers, it seemed, than for customers seeking something unique or different. In essence, I wish them well, but it seems they have lost their way. If they were to go back to their roots, it could be a very delightful restaurant (again).
We came here for a family birthday dinner, delicious food, although small menu, cute atmosphere, only reason for 4 stars was once it started to get busy it got super loud!!!!

I came here for supper with some friends. My friends ordered pita sandwiches while I ordered the mozarella and tomato apppetizer plus a small Greek salad. No alcoholic beverage. The appetizers are sized to share between two people. My food was good, and the sandwiches were consumed, so they must have been good, too. The menu has a nice selection, and I can see myself returning to try other items. I just didn't feel like eating a full dinner that evening. The service was fine.
We are here today for the buffet lunch! It was fantastic! We will be back...the wait staff was quick and efficient the food was yummy!

I've been here 3 times. Loved it every time. Their food is so delicious. I loved their Qabli Paloa... The atmosphere is cool too. Although a bit small. Also the enterance is a little hidden. It's in the basement and sort of easy to miss...

Service- It is a completely self-serve restraunt which is borderline confusing when you first walk in. You approach the area where the food is being prepared to order, but pay after you're done eating in the back where it looks like the staff takes short breaks. Staff- They're present. That's about it, you barely interact with them or need them honestly. Food- Oh I couldn't wait to tell you'll about this, it's awful!!! Your food is ready in barely seconds after you order, and this is supposed to be a place that can compare to Tazikis( another meditteranean cafe that's great&fresh daily and consistently), but instead it's the complete opposite. The meat astes very microwaved along with the rice and unrealistic like mcdonalds meat. The basmati rice was not how I normally see it, it was over greasy& gooey!!!! Then the supposed tazikis sauce they gave tastes like runny mayonnaise, and their drinks were insanely overpriced. Their cream sodas were like 2.95 when they're a buck cheaper elsewhere. Overall the only good thing they have keeping them in business is their location& atmosphere, but the cuisine is . Save yourself

This place is quite new-- I noticed it the other day so I figured I'd stop in since we are looking for good non-chain restaurants in Largo. When I parked in the rear parking lot, one of the owners was hanging out in the back, outside the kitchen, tending to the jerk. It smelled incredible! I love being able to smell the food before you even walk into a restaurant. Everyone was extremely friendly, and the jerk wings and curry chicken roti I ordered to go were outstanding. I will definitely be coming back!

The gyros at this place are awesome! The gyros alone would make this a 5 star The rest of the menu is hit or just ok. This place is always clean, (in fact every time i've walked in there off peek hours they are cleaning.) but its not a fancy place and its loud in there when they are busy. I recommend taking the food to go.

Ignore all the negative reviews, especially from the people who haven't actually eaten there! My husband and I ate there with two other couples and stopped by an hour early to drop off our BYOB, and they were happy to hold our wine and beer while we walked around town. The service was friendly and attentive and the food was so good. We shared many appetizers and a couple of entrees and our bill was still under $100 for 6 people! We will definitely be back and I would highly recommend!
This place is great. Michelle is the best hostess. What I really love is all the food combos. It's amazing! The beef bulgogi is the bomb!

Full disclosure - I have only had Vietnamese food twice in my life and both times have been at Kien Giang. My total obsession with Anthony Bourdain had me reeling over the fact that I had yet to try Pho. Thankfully I have a knowledgeable co-worker who could assist in such a travesty of justice and take me to the right place on Charlotte Pike. I would not have known which of the four or five places to pick as there seems to be a two block ratio that houses the most authentic of Vietnamese places in town. I knew I was going to get Pho, there was no question about that. Instead, the only detail to iron out was which one? I am an adventuresome eater, of that I have no doubt. I've eaten a kangaroo filet so I think there is not a lot out there I am not willing to try. But since I was not certain which way to lean, I went with the Pho Tai. Again, this was only my second trip so I have nothing to compare this culinary excursion with so I just had to let my taste buds do the judging. Oh. My. Stars. Rare beef, noodles, bean sprouts, lime juice, basil, jalapenos, and chili oil - you are a party in my mouth!
