They asked if we wanted extra rice at no charge. So nice! I ordered the red curry with medium heat and it was perfect. My sister thought it was a little too spicy for her, but she's pretty sensitive to spicy foods. She still thought it was delicious no doubt. All the dishes around us looked good too so now I want to try everything! I live in Lenox Village so I will definitely be back very soon, and frequently! I actually like it better than Sushime. Give it a try if you are a fan of Thai/Korean/Japanese!

My friend and I decided to check this place out one night after hearing many good things. Oh what a disappointment it turned out to be. I ordered the Cold Sesame Noodle which came out first. First bite, bland. Mixed it around some more to blend in the sauce. Second bite, bland. Had to add in some spicy sauce to help myself finish the rest. My friend ordered the Yakisoba. He said the noodles were oily and bland. I was thinking to myself what's going on here?! I tried the noodles myself and indeed it was another bland bowl of noodles. Sigh. Cute, small place. Service is average. Atmosphere is chill. Food is just bland. Sad to say that we were not impressed w the food and don't think we'll be back again.

We were regulars at the family owned Japanese restaurant at this location and were sad to see them close, apparently due to a family emergency some months ago. So, when Yah Mon opened up earlier this month we thought we would give it a try. It was great to see that Ya Mon is another family owned and operated restaurant. Andre and Janise, the husband and wife owners/operators, are incredibly welcoming. My daughter and I originally stopped in just to have a quick look and grab a menu but were so taken by Andre and Janise, the menu, and what they had done to the place that we decided to stay for dinner. We ordered the Blackened Salmon with mango salsa and the Tilapia sauteed with vegetables, both dishes were served with a rice and beans and plantains. Both dishes were truly excellent in flavor, presentation and quality. We also tried the coco bread (excellent) and the Johnny Cakes (also excellent). We ended the dinner with an order of the homemade Bread Pudding and slice of Chocolate Cake, again excellent. With a hungry teenager waiting at home we added a to go order of the Jerk Chicken and a slice of the Coconut Cake - the chicken was very tasty (somewhat spicy but not too spicy) and the Coconut Cake, according to my son was so good that he didn't offer me a taste. So, it is without hesitation that I can recommend Yah Mon to anyone who likes great Caribbean food served well in a great little restaurant with a chic design by wonderful people. Make sure and visit Andre and Janise - Janise cooks everything herself and is originally from the island of St. Thomas! If you live on Bayshore, Downtown or Davis Islands, this is a must visit and also a great option for to go meals when you don't feel like cooking.

Sad disappointment. Shake was amazing and food is probably good but that doesn't make up for wait time. I waited so long for my food and when it came out some things were hot some where cold. Hence kitchen staff lacks timing skills or expediter was to quick on draw. They gave me a Greek salad with no dressing some food that didn't belong to me and water downed sauce for my falafel that tasted like old oil.

This is a review for a recent sunday meze. $30 vegetarian and $35 meat, and the portions are substantial! Bread w/ dip (lentil this time), really delicious dip! There was a side of picked vegetables that were pretty good too..but I only like olives (personal preference though) It was 2 of us (1 meat and 1 veg meze): 4 dishes for appetizer -- duck heart, boar sausage, grape leaf wrap with sauce, falafel, my favorite were the falafel (it was pink on the inside! maybe beets?) and the grape leaf. My boyfriend said the duck heart was really delicious, and the boar too. I'm particular about meats and did not try those. 7 main dishes - pork dish, bean dish, sea food (some sort of squid), chicken, spinach pastry, stuffed tomato, and beets. I LOVED the bean and the spinach pastry. Definitely delicious. The great thing was that all dishes had its own unique taste, no taste really repeated (except for the yogurt sauce that accompanied some). By the end I was super stuffed, but the desserts sounded delicious! Desserts aren't included in the meze, but at $5 a pop, they're a bargain! Had their home made baklava and some sort of custard/filo/orange thing. I loved both! So delicious. Their coffee was good too. I will DEFINITELY be coming back! Come hungry because the portions could have fed 4 of us well. Reservation would be good for the Sunday meze, as when we went there was only 1 free table. The location is very small. Our server was also fantastic! Very knowledgeable and sweet. Enjoyed him immensely. I've included pictures of everything for people who are visual.

This was another place suggested by some of my friends. Maybe they dont get out much. I heard that this place was just as good as my all time favorite place in Tucson. They come pretty close but I can name a few other places that are much better. Good thing is, they are not the worse. Me and my coworker decided to order iluv Pho for lunch to-go. I ordered the pho dac biet. I didn't know the number of my order, obviously, but every vietnamese restaurant names their "house" pho, the one with all the meats, Dac Biet. Which I explained very clearly and was still given the wrong order. Which is fine considering I'm not very picky. Upon opening my box, I notice there was no basil, the only herb I look forward to having in my pho. Disappointed, they could of told me they were out and not leave me with the impression that they dont serve basil with their pho. Lastly, the portions were ridicously small. Me, being the peitite little asian that I am, never finishes a small size of pho. Maybe if I'm starving (which wasnt the case this time) but I would be completely stuffed and unbuttoning my pants after I'm done. I finished my pho and soup and was still digging for more. Lets leave a better impression on me next time guys.

Pretty darn good for fast food. It's fresh and healthy and the flavors are good.i was able to satisfy my lamb and tofu craving so I was pretty happy! I reminds me of a Chipotle for Indian food but with greater variety. It's definitely worth trying I will return.

Can't beat the quality to value ratio. Stopped here for dinner after spending the day at Busch Gardens. We could not have been happier with the dinner we were served. Portion sizes of high quality meat and cheese are more than generous. The sauces have delicately balanced, authentic flavors. The hummus is to die for with its tahini forward flavor and silken texture. You can pay extra and replace the fries with the hummus and a pita which is worth every penny. The restaurant was clean and staff was friendly. Seriously- what more can you ask for?

I love this cute location right next to the Howard Johnson's in Tampa. Excellent service, there's a little condiment bar inside. Their pad Thai is truly magnificent. I got a tasty limeade and for a friend, a mango boba tea. Everything is fresh. Prices are good as well. Definitely worth a look.

OmG! El bistec encebollado con mofongo estuvo delicioso!!! El mofongo es tan rico como si lo hubiese comido en Puerto Rico!! Nos sirvieron super rápido y el servicio en general fue bueno. Definitivamente, volveremos!!!
The chicken red curry was very good and quite filling for lunch. The pad Thai is not very good. Mine was saucy, too sweet, and the noodles were chopped up. No thanks.
I got the #2, the lemongrass tofu sandwich...I didn't know what to expect going in, but it was affordable and tasty! Not a bad experience in trying new things.

Flavorful, steaming hot and non-generic; everything a roman bowl should be. I got the Miso Roman Bowl for lunch in the Philly Whole Foods. The pork shoulder, broth, half a soy egg and black garlic was the perfect combo. Highly recommend, even for the $14.

Decided to stop by and have dinner after searching my options and seeing that I only had two options that were open while on vacation While there. We had chicken pad see ew and fried rice with pork,also a wonton soup. Drinks we had was Thai ice tea. The chicken pad see ew was delicious. The chicken Fried pork rice was good but the pork needed to be a bit less tuff. The soup was delicious other than the chicken in it, chicken was way too hard. The drinks where good,too much ice though. The vibe in there was nice, clean and friendly staff. They asked if everything was good and if I wanted water refills. Price is right for location, I would recommend this to anyone wanting some good Thai in the area. Close to the beach as well. I would come back when in town again.

I've been to Momo's a few times now, only because my boyfriend loves the atmosphere and their chicken kebob. We went for (my) first time on Valentine's day. I made reservations several days in advance, but when we got their they said they didn't have a table for us, so we sat at the bar, which I found incredibly rude and annoying. I ordered a gyro, which was mediocre (try Fozzie's - best gyro in town IMO). Our goat cheese appetizer was all right- it was basically pizza sauce with gobs of goat cheese in it served with toasted bread. My boyfriend's chicken kabob was by far the best thing. They had belly dancing that night, and it was WAY too loud. I felt sorry for the poor fish in the tank in the corner; I'm surprised the noise hasn't killed him already. Since then we've been a couple times, and I've had a much more pleasant experience during the day (no insanely loud belly dancing music) and when I get the chicken kabob. Although I've had some pleasant experiences here, I just think there are much better places to get a kabob or gyro (e.g., The Vine, Cafe Natasha, Fozzie's).

Everything here was fantastic. Had a curry dish and Masala and both were phenomenal. The naan bread was crispy and we'll done. Service was very good considering we were there right before closing time.

Stopped in for the lunch buffet. Amazing! Great variety, quality, and service. Growing up in harleysville I know that most people in the area are probably unfamiliar with Indian food. Don't be scared, Aman's is awesome! Go try the buffet, it's a great way to get a little taste of everything and see what you like best.

I recently read somewhere that the best places to find ethnic food are those unassuming restaurants without fancy names or signage that you find in strip malls. African Palace was fits that description perfectly. I went here a few months ago with my adventurous restaurant buddy who had heard great things about it. It's waaay out in the county, but if you are looking for a different place to shake up your dining experience, it's totally worth the drive. I've never been to West Africa nor am I an expert in that type of cuisine, but the place screamed authenticity to me. Our very kind waiter recognized that we were first timers and made suggestions on what to order. We had a simple, delicious beef appetizer with onions and a fantastic sauce. My friend ordered a fish dish and I ordered beef, both of which were very different from anything I'd tasted before, and very tasty. If I'm ever in the area again I'll definitely go back to try the rest of their menu.

The Shawermas here are fantastic. Great seasoned Shawermas meat, tasty feta and cucumber sauce too served on very fresh lebenese bread. And only $5 for a very big portion. Also try the chicken with rice kabsa or the kebab sandwich. Everything made to order and worth the wait. The best Mediterranean food in town! The cafe is housed in a gas station complex and very unassuming but clean and neat. Hand printed menus stuck to the wall add to the charm. As authentic as it gets and the owner is very friendly.

4 1/2 stars! Even though we are now in NYC, we were back in Philly and had to review one of our favorites Penang, as we ate here bc we missed it so much. We got our regular, roti canai, chow kueh teow and penang pad thai. They are all excellent. The roti canai was 3x as large as the ones you get in NYC and the perfect combo between crispy and soft. Their noodles dishes are all great, but these two are our favorites. They never overcook their noodles, so the fried noodle dishes arent soggy. The chow kueh teow is spicy and a little heavier, while the penang pad thai (tastes nothing like pad thai at a thai restaurat btw), is lighter which is why we like the balance. Their mango chicken is also great, the sauce is soo good, while at other places the sauce tastes like glamourized ketchup. We also recommend the sauteed water convulus which has lots of garlic! The pork dishes, king pork buff and spare ribs are also so flavorful, we could go on and on as we use to frequent this place often.

Best Greek restaurant in Philly! My husband and I frequently go here with our daughters and every time the food is amazing, service is amazing and the price is right. Just writing this is making me crave their potatoes and saganaki!
The menu is limited, service is poor and right you will have to scrape food off since they don't refill
Loved. Loved loved. The biscuits. The pig ears-soft and addictive. Goat curry might be one of my favorite dishes. Ice cream churned every day.
Not as good as I expected. Waste of time and money. The lamp was very tough. And when the waiter gave us the dishes, his thumb touched the sauce in a disgusting way!

Chicken rice soup $3 - Big portion, great broth. It's a simple soup consisting of rice and chicken. The garlic flavor in the broth is very good. Panang Curry with Pork $11 - The curry base was creamy and delicious. I enjoyed the cucumbers in this dish. The pork were thinly sliced, but not that tasty. I would try chicken instead. My order was for take out and I ordered a Kirin to drink while I waited. They had a sushi bar in the back that looked good. Beside a small selection of beer, they also offer wine. The service was fast and friendly. The décor inside was elegant consisting with a lot of mahogany.

Basically, this is a convenience store that sells food along with cigarillos and condoms. Great reviews convinced me to give it a try. Visited at 6:30pm. After we paid, the owner brought our Butter Chicken after about 15 minutes, apologizing that he had run out of rice and so gave four extra pieces of naan. Food was tasty, but not super cheap at $12 each for takeout Butter Chicken without rice and a few pieces of naan.

Bhature. It's bread that they fry. Fried bread. FRIED BREAD. It happens to be absolutely delicious, too. Their other breads [naan, kulcha, etc] were good and to standards you'd expect from a good Indian restaurant. But that goddamn Bhature, I'll have that all day. Let me first say that it's very nice inside, feels upscale and is definitely a nice place to take someone out on a date. They even play Bollywood flicks on the TV there, great distraction if the date starts talking about the Kardashians or her ex, so just lose yourself in the food and 100 people dancing on the screen. Opened up with the Pakoda, and having been craving it since I last been to Zaika, it hit the spot. A plate of it is perfect for four, a bit overwhelming for two. Since I'm an eternal fatass, I polished it off, but it didn't leave much room for the dinner... WHICH WAS INCREDIBLE. It was the Paneer Bhurji, and it will go down as one of the most tasty items I've ever had at any Indian joint. The waitress asked what level of hot I wanted it at, and I foolishly said 10 at first, but quickly revised it to a 7 when I saw her next. The lady friend insisted a 5 was intolerable last time she ate here, so I moved the heat index accordingly from my understanding of her tolerance. Good move, the curry made me sweat, but didn't break me. BEAST MODE MOTHERFUCKERS. The great thing about food from this region is how exotic it is in comparison to the foods we eat here everyday, so it's a real treat when they take so much care in its preparation and the outcome is as bangin' as my dinner was. The place is entirely vegetarian, so the dish consisted of grated cheese, onions, and bell pepper with their special dash of spices in a curry. Wholly unexpected was the awesome dish placed in front of me, and staring down a dish of rice [it's included] and a whole basket of nom-tastic Indian breads. Having stuffed myself on the Pakoda, I had to force myself to eat the spicy dish until my stomach called it quits. Not sure if it was from the peppery goodness or just telling me that one man should not consume more than a couple pounds of food in a single sitting. Long and wordy, but you honestly just look at that star rating, and for there not being a lick of meat in the building, this place was unbelievably good.

Quaint delicious indian food cafe. We walked into this cafe expecting great food and service and that's exactly what we received. Almost everyone that walked in after us had the same story how they have heard of this well kept gem, yelp! The owner was very friendly and helpful. I let him know I was vegan and immediately he knew what should meet my requirements to make the food friendly. I actually never had chaat before but it sure was delicious. If it is your first time visiting the place then the owner will whip you up with a starter to get you familiar with the cuisine. A meal consisting of mangos, dates, dried cranberries, chickpeas, potatoes, and some other delicious combination of ingredients placed into a meal. You can have this as a salad or a regular meal. The meal was placed on top of fresh spring mix. Normally served with yogurt but he knew not to include it. For meat eaters they had plenty of options to go along with this as well, lamb, chicken, and beef. Don't forget to order one of their lassi drinks as well. They make it with yogurt usually but get it veganized with almond milk. Banana date was just what I needed to satisfy my sweet tooth.

All the Mezze, please! Butcher & Bee is one of the top spots in Nashville. Their food is fun and innovative while maintaining the integrity of a rustic dish. Their small plates - or mezze - are to die for. My favorite are the beets with lime yogurt and fermented honey. The hummus is also delicious with some toasted chic peas on top for texture. The roast beef with cheese sauce is a grown up version of a childhood favorite of mine. Like I said - so sophisticated but still true to what the item is as a whole. It's a hearty sandwich that will fill you up! The burger is not to be missed either - it's got a little kick of spice thanks to some jalapeños. The environment is lovely - perfect for a lunch meeting or date night. The cocktails are inventive and potent.

Lovely, fresh guacamole with crunchy chips. Sensational breaded eggplant cemitas with caramelized onions. Nice tight selection of beer on draft. Perfect little drink in the pear-a-mule. And right in my own damn neighborhood! Hoorah for Yelpers, hoorah for Sobro, and hoorah for me.

This place is on point! I went with the grilled octopus and it was excellent. All the dishes are very reasonably priced. BYOB makes it extra affordable. If you like Greek, do not hesitate to check this spot out!!!

With a crunchy bagette and delicious contents within said crunchy bagette, I am thankful that I live a good 20 blocks away from Café Nhuy. It is through that resistance that prevents me from eating there morning, noon and night.

Saigon is one of my favorite first choice of Vietnamese restaurants, I have been going there for so long ! great atmosphere, good food, very clean, great service. The owner is very nice, he remembers how I want my food to be cook. One of their best plates is Cm sng, super smokey grilled pork chop over medium egg, meat loaf & grilled shredded pork. It served Yasmin's rice with pickled carrots and daikon radish, of course yummy fish sauce with hot chili pepper. definitely recommend for people who first time want to try Vietnamese food. They also have bubble tea if anybody is looking for some smoothie, also special Vietnamese hot coffee great

Definitely won't be returning to this location. I parked in the lot directly beside Remedy and received a $50 dollar parking ticket... I was literally in the cafe for 5 minutes and my $5 Chai turned into $55. If the service would have been quicker I probably wouldn't have even gotten a ticket. The tea was fine but I could hardly enjoy it after that experience ruining my day. I wish they were more specific on their parking considering I asked an employee if I was allowed to park there.

March 13' walked in a late Friday night to a pleasant surprise. Since moving here from the West Coast 7 months ago I have a had a real struggle finding classy fine dining. There are only handful of nice places outside the onslaught of beach bars, coconut shrimp, and flip flops, the Pearl is one of those few. At 3/4 full the ambiance was very subtle and tasteful. I was immediately greeted by a nice fellow at the door and decided to eat up at the bar. I passed a man playing guitar and he was AMAZING! I ws then greeted by the bartender and she was very polite and attentive. The staff all at one point made an effort to greet me. I ordered a beer while looking over the menu. I decided on the ribeye. What I got was a steak the size of my thigh!! It was perfectly cooked along with sides of fresh grilled vegetables and scalloped potatoes. I had a delicious glass of Cabernet recommended by the chef. It paired excellently!! I hear gripes about pricing, but being from the West Coast this was exactly on par for a restaurant of this caliber. I highly recommend The Pearl to anyone who has had their fill of Hawaiian shirts and a deep fried menu. I will be a regular!

I order takeout from Ekta pretty regularly - My cravings are frequent and intense but I pat myself on the back after each visit. Tantalizing flavors, wonderfully aromatic aromas, and hearty, highly satisfying menu items are commonplace. My current favorites include Lamb Chettinad, Chicken Korma, Ekta vegetables, baigan bharta, and garlic naan. Each and every friend, family member, foodie, and fearless leader I've shared an ekta meal with has been consumed by south indian spice & everything nice and is eagerly awaiting their next ekta experience. Don't be upset but sometimes I enjoy savoring Ekta dishes alone - I love all of you but I'm addicted to Ekta leftovers - especially for lunch the following day. I may get Ekta tonight....it would be the third time in less than two weeks and there is nothing at all wrong with that! If your taste buds are craving some new flavors or wish to take a journey across the globe, I highly recommend giving Ekta a shot. You will leave with your very own Ekta-fied needs and desires - and as your relationship with ekta matures, your tastebuds will always get lots of attention and remain young at heart. Ekta OVER all other Indian restaurants around the Main Line. You will be amazed by all of the flavors!! This place is a gem and everyone should try it!!

I'm not sure what Mihir S is talking about. The chat here is out of this world. I'm Indian too, and Mihir's claims of the chaat not being Indian are exaggerated. Appreciating something novel is not for everyone I guess. The food here is amazing, the maker has a charming, effusive personality..and the price very affordable. This is better than any Indian chat ive ever had.

Great pho tai, tofu bun dishes. Vegan and pork spring rolls are perfect. Tofu spring rolls just OK. Only complaint is that the food came out too fast! Great prices and amazingly friendly staff, unflustered despite demanding environment.

Followed previous reviews to select this restaurant. Service was impeccable and timely. Water was never empty, feeling very attended to by the staff. The food was served beautifully with fresh Naan. It was a true delight

Like in traveling, when it comes to bars, it's never the destination, but the journey you always fondly remember. That's exactly how I feel about Queen of Sheba. The destination of most bars usually end in being drunk, laid, rejected, dejected, or just having a time of any sort. How you get there is entirely up to you. But back to Sheba! I really enjoy the simplicity of it all. All it is, is just a bar where people are here to drink, talk, share a dirty joke, bitch about the state of pop music, or to just enjoy yourself. The drinks are cheap and the people are terrific. This place is a gem.

I never write negative reviews on restaurants after one visit, this is important because everybody has an off day. Well, in Zoe's Kitchen's case everyday is an off day. I have tried to support this restaurant and each time they DESTROY basic Mediterranean food like a GREEK SALAD or FAIL to SERVE SOFT FRESH PITA. It's sad, because I think their goal is to be the McDonald's of Mediterranean food. If McDonald's decided to make the same dishes they would do better than Zoe's kitchen. I would not be surprise if this location is closed down in a year. Note to managers, spend time with your kitchen staff, stop hiring people who simply don't give a damn. P.S. I should have known something was WRONG when I saw DIRTY DISHES piled up around the garbage cans and the place wasn't busy. So disappointed.
We went there for pho. The broth was very bland and the garnish plate did not include any of the fresh cilantro or Thai basil. Sigh. Still schlepping to center city for good soup...

Yum yum yum ! This place is delish ! The decor and ambiance is so high classy you forget you are in the middle of Brandon. The staff presence is impeccable, and the tables! Oh my a piece of art ! Now to the food: delicious! I had the Chicken Masaman Curry and I loved it ! Really creamy and perfect portion. The Thai Tea was also really good. For a non-native of the country I loved it :) I will definitely come back - I love the fact that is so close to home - not that that will affect anyone's view of the place lol ;)

Never come back. It took them 40 mins to serve the food (I only ordered noodles soup). The noodles was bad compared to other Malaysian restaurants I have been to. The cut of pork is thick and dry. Tom yum soup is too sour.
Amazing good , super accomodative of food restrictions. If you around the area should definitely try it :) friendly staff too

This little gem still never ceases to impress. We love coming here for the delicious Thai flavors, the friendliness and hospitality of the owner and staff. Bella is our usual server and she is awesome! The food portions are generous for items like Thai fried rice, pad Thai, and other servings. The curry items come with one portion of white rice. We've tried a bunch of different options, which are all great. Our favorites are noodle soup, Panang curry, Thai legacy fried rice, and pad Thai. Veggie spring rolls are amazing. We order from the vegan menu. But we have also brought plenty of family member who are not vegan and they order from regular menu and enjoy the food just as much. You just can't go wrong here. This is the Thai place to eat. The tables are always beautifully decorated with real flowers which reminds us so much of our trip to Thailand.

Maybe I've built it up in my head during the time I've been away from Nashville, but right now I feel like Kien Giang's lemongrass chicken (ga xao xa ot) is literally the best thing I've ever tasted in my life. I've ordered it at plenty of other places trying to recapture the glory of this dish, but nothing comes close. The sauce is so garlicky and savory and a tad spicy, and I could actually lick it off the plate. The rice and veggies that come with it are the perfect accompaniment, and at only $6, it's basically a dream come true. Everything else I've eaten here has been delicious as well, and it's always super cheap. Everyone loves the hot chicken and southern places around town, but this is actually my favorite restaurant in Nashville. If you're lucky enough to be there, don't miss out.
Fantastic pho, though that's all I've tried here. In my opinion better than Miss Saigon and VN Pho And Deli. My go to pho spot.

I visit Seasons quite often. Sometimes just for boba and sometimes for a meal. Their blended boba is amazing; I always opt for one instead of a milkshake on a hot day. Honeydew is quite delicious. I've gotten hooked on their chicken pad Thai. It's great there or to go (holds up quite well in the box, as most noodles are usually soggy to-go, these are always great). The staff is friendly and it's always a very multicultural crowd there, so don't be intimidated to stop in!

What a great deal for lunch! My girlfriend and I we're in town for a conference, and we were very pleased with the selection and flavors. Only downside-- the lighting was cheap, bright, CFL, white! Time to upgrade those bulbs.

Not sure what all the hype is about. They succeed at being different, but not being flavorful. We had the dumplings in chili oil, the miso ramen, and the brisket matzo ball soup. The dumplings were the best and most flavorful part of our meal. The meat in the noodles were both very good but unable to compensate for the lackluster broth. All in all, our meal was not bad, but just not memorable either. There are way better options in Center City, especially with Chinatown so close by. The miso ramen brought me back to memories of my days in Japan eating $3.50 bowls of ramen. And even those had more flavor.

We came during lunch and the place was empty. Being the first time to visit this restaurant, we made reservations, just in case. The vibe was very laid back, but I really liked it. It's small, but cozy. It has a family vibe that really invites you in. Looking online, it says they have salsa dancing lessons for free on Tuesday and summer block party's on Sundays, as well. As for the food, it was PHENOMENAL!!! My boyfriend is half Puerto Rican and so I've had some of the food, but this place really impressed me! The drinks were stiff, but tasty and the food was to die for! I will most definitely be back!!!!

Came here during the Made in America festival and was tired of eating cheesesteaks :) I wanted some home cooking from the DR and that is exactly what I got! The food "estaba como EH" ....AKA the bomb! We got the specials for lunch (half a chicken and pollo guisado with rice and beans. Can't forget to mention that this place is BYOB. Overall this restaurant is one of my favorites in Philly and would definitely come back on my next visit fo Philly.

I really cannot compliment this place enough, it sets the bar for chaat. I never been disappointed there. The mix of flavors and textures always comes out just right. Also, the owner is the friendliest guy you'll ever meet. It's obvious that he loves what he does; he always goes out of his way to make the experience great. Sometimes I do not order anything off the menu and just tell him to suprise me. He is more than happy to just throw some things together, explaining as he goes along.

Large portions of authentic food at reasonable prices but ambience could use an upgrade. Can see the tenants if the contest restaurant that came before it but flavors are food enough to compensate. I had the chicken schwarma lunch special which was moist and filling. Hubby had the beef schwarma stirfry which he devoured. Lentil soup was amazing. Plenty of free parking and liked like there were quite a few take out orders when we were there.
Excellent Thai! We had a great dinner that was a great deal! We sat next to a table of St Louis police officers eating dinner-- which is a testament to the quality of the food!

We have eaten twice at Spice Finch now, and we love it! The food is delicious, creative, and filling. We had bean tangine (loved it), roasted cauliflower (best ever), and petite filet (tender and YUM) for our main course. Our server, Karen, was lovely and attentive. The presentation is exquisite. Nothing is lacking, and the prices are so reasonable. Ambiance is charming, cocktails are great, and the staff is extremely accommodating. This is a new gem on the Philly restaurant scene, and a very welcome one at that.

Stopped by on a Saturday afternoon for lunch, and was pleasantly surprised! My family is from Singapore, and we always love a good meal from the region. We ordered roti canai, nasi lemak, char kway teow, poh piah, and egg kway teow. The dishes were authentically made, and portions were huge! This was made better by how reasonably priced everything was. The total bill came out to $37 (not including tip) for party of 5, and we couldn't even finish everything. It's always pretty crowded, and I can see why. Best meal we had in Philly.

Let me just say O-M-G. Ok, so the menu is several pages long and daunting but what else can you expect from a restaurant trying to bring so much greatness to the ethnically-diverse, dive-happy West Side of Indy? My husband mixes it up and orders something new at each visit and he is always impressed--he's had duck, tripe, various Pho items, Thai selections too. He loves the bubble tea. As for me, I am guilty of ordering the same things over and over (but I order lots of things!). The Saigon Chicken Wings are to die for--I've never experienced such sweet and sassy flavor on a drumstick. Seriously, the best wings I've had. I always order Pho. I love Vietnamese. I've had the beef flank, chicken, and vegetarian Pho options. I am addicted to the intensely "raw" beef broth and they don't skimp on flavor in the vegetarian Pho. Broth (of any kind) can be dull and bland but Saigon Restaurant does not allow such characteristics in their fabulous Pho broth. The accoutrements are always fresh--basil, bean sprouts, jalapeno, lime. Don't forget to pop those into your steamy hot bowl of soup for added freshness and flavor. Fresh Spring Rolls are also pretty decent too, but not as superb as the Pho. The service is genuine, never over-the top/goober-friendly/fake-smiles. Always just plain Good. Indy needed a go-to Pho spot and I can't think of a more deserving side of town for its location. The West Side always impresses with ethnic dives and diversity! One comment (and I'm sorry to have to do this): the Thai tea could use some revamping--It needs to be richer and stronger. They do, however, make up for it with superb Vietnamese coffee.
Found on a whim. The food was delicious and is in a good location just off of main st. I will definitely go back and recommend. The Gyros are amazing..

Finally tried this place today after driving by probably 100 times. I ordered a chicken gyro on pita with everything. Delicious. And for about the same cost as a fast food burger, it boggles my mind why there wasn't a line out the door. Don't let the aisles of foodstuffs fool you upon first entering, Halal Meat Market & Restaurant is a great little take-out joint with friendly and prompt service. I will be a repeat customer for sure. Loved it, five stars!
Went to Nadia tonight around 7:00 PM, closed. Is it out of business? Seems strange to be closed on a Saturday evening.

Sher e Punjab isn't just a restaurant, it's a way of life. Look, I've been to all the Indian restaurants in Tucson, and none of them come close to Sher e Punjab. The food is outstanding and the family that runs it is a class act. The enforcer (a gentlemanly old Sikh man who is 55-60) keeps things running smoothly. His sons will make you feel welcome, even if you are a sociopath or otherwise rejected by society. While it is true that the shopping center is a haven for those down on their luck, I think they are all panhandling for the $7 they need to eat like kings and queens at Sher e Punjab.
We ordered takeout from here a while back and it was tasty. The salad was surprisingly delicious, but the Tom kha was bland. The curry was superb and the beef soup was tasty too.

We just had an excellent lunch here. I had the lamb curry and my wife had a beef shank in curry sauce. The meat just fell apart in our mouths. Some of the best Indian food we have had in town. From the outside it is not an impressive storefront, but the owners were extremely attentive and the food was incredible. I highly recommend it and can't wait to come back here.
The chicken shawarma sandwich was terrific! Can't wait to head back.

We honestly found this place on a whim, but my goodness was the food delicious and the service warm! My wife had the fried catfish and I had the fried chicken with sweet potato (pictured). They were crusted in cornmeal (which has a unique crunch and is very helpful for people with gluten allergies) and coated in a delicious spice blend. The prices were reasonable and every employee we met was awesome. We'll definitely be back soon!
Yum! Not much can be said that hasn't yet been said but great atmosphere, great service, food was great. Didn't get a cocktail this time but look forward to returning to try the brunch!
This spot looks fun, but that's about it. We had the chilaquiles and some tacos. They were just so so. We didn't finish our food or take the leftovers, which is rare for me.

I have been here many times and this is one of my favorite places to eat in Tampa. Kitfo would be part of my last meal. The variety of the Queen's Eight platter is amazing, and there isn't anything I've eaten here that wasn't delicious. They are accomodating with requests, and very friendly, and it's a dining experience that's hard to find elsewhere. It's very vegetarian friendly as well, although it's fabulous for omnivores like me.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Place is exceptional! Love the store/restaurant. Always very friendly and convienant if you want to try to experiment and make the food at home like I do. Wonderful experience every time! Love the culture and atmosphere!

This might be my favorite Indian place in Bucks County! The service is great, the food incredible and dietary restrictions are met by everyone at the table. (Gluten free, dairy free and vegan) all at the same table. The recommendations are incredible and never disappoint!

Love India's Kitchen. We usually go for their lunch buffet which is phenomenal but recently ate there for dinner and it was just as good and the amount of food you got made for plenty of leftovers. The service is great with everyone super friendly. The prices are great for both their lunch buffet and their dinners. If it wasn't for the fact that it takes 30 minutes to get there we would eat there a couple times a week.

Colorful atmosphere (literally) that's not favorable. Takeout, though possible, doesn't seem ideal by the spatial organization. My vegetarian Tom Kha had chicken in it which leaves me to believe they cook it with chicken and later fish it out and replace it with tofu when someone orders it vegetarian. The Pad Thai is baseline; Spice Level 3 is enjoyable and something I would go with on the reg here.

I'm calling this place the "La Colombe" of hummus. Like LC, this place takes you on a culinary tour of Lebanon and Turkey. The flavors are beyond fresh and unique. They're totally in a league of their own! The menu is slightly overwhelming, so I defaulted to the original hummus and green salad. The original hummus is soft and nutty just like Zahav/Dizengoff (sorry to pull so many restaurants into this, but I think alluding to them shows the high standard of quality Suraya meets). I blame that on the tehina, Soom Foods. It is served with a pita, fresh from the oven, and it's soft and airy with a subtle crust. The green salad included gem lettuce, raw fennel, watermelon radishes, a soft-boiled egg, yogurt dressing, and pita chips. The flavor profile was satisfying. The meal overall was light, filling, and nourishing! I went back for seconds the week after. Opted for the baba ganoush, pita, and the rest of the party got the gravlax. Overall, everyone was satisfied. While the ganoush was tasty, I think I'll stick to the hummus. I appreciate that particular spread much more. Again, service and atmosphere were 10/10!

I've only had the Banh Mi so far, but it was so delish, I'm craving it for lunch again today. So fresh and delicious and the bread is to die for! I agree with the other yelper, too....the carrots on it are so yummy!

Truly unique and amazing food. As I'm about to leave St. Louis, I can safely say this is the place I will miss the most. Cocktails are amazing, wine is interesting and fabulous (and the very well informed staff can help you understand it), and most of all the food is to die for. Every dish is fabulous - not overdone, but still innovative. Flavors are bold and balanced. The staff is friendly and attentive, but never hovering.

This place is awesome! I finally found a place where I can get a gyro that's actually good! Fresh meat, great pita. I wish I could put French fries in that ish like I did when I was in Greece. (2 times). Staff was very polite. Oh and the Greek salad is not the traditional Greek because the put lettuce which is fine but I wish they didn't. I will be back 100% though as this place is great
Best Thai food I've had in Philadelphia, definitely recommend anyone who loves spicy food to check this place out!

Finally a Banh Mi place in Wilmington. Yummy sandwiches, fresh and flavorful. Lots of bubble tea options. The owner and staff were really friendly and cute little sitting area to eat. Was going to take a pic of my Banh Mi but ate it too fast, was dying to try it. Will be a regular spot!

This is another gem in west philly. The decor is better than average. The service is decent. Food is good but not exceptional. This is a place I would gladly take any family members or friends from out of town.

My new favorite place. I've been three times already. (It's really close to my house, don't judge.) I've tried a good portion of the menu and haven't been disappointed yet. I only wish you could get the full menu for dinner as well. Drink the Pear-a-Mule, so good!!

Food is well flavored with some subtle flavors layered in. So curries are complex with coriander, star anise, different peppers and more. Service is prompt and polite. Lunch buffet has vegetarian and meat dishes plus a desert. Interior is well decorated with both tables and booths. You have to be going east on Tyrone to get in and if traffic is heavy, be patient.

We had high expectations for this place and it was just OK in comparison to all the great NYC or Chicago restaurants out there. Table of three ordered the following: 1. Arancini - interesting twist with the citrus sauce 2. Croquettes- awesome 3. Steak Tartare- it was ok; nothing to write home about 4. Oysters- small oysters full of flavor 5. Curried goat- disappointing; there's was barely any curry in the dish; least favorite dish of the night 6. Shrimp and clam pasta- nicely done pasta but salty AF. 7. Trio pork- pork belly was delicious
Nice cozy place with a decent beet and wine selection. Definately interested in coming back to the place, and as a completely strange compliment the counter tops rock.

I will definitely be back. The atmosphere is very laid back. I really wanted the mac and cheese but they were out, I ordered curry goat which was very tender but my only gripe was since I order a double order of plantains I expected more than four. My son loved his jerk wings and the patty seemed to be store bought. The young lady Terri who took my order was very courteous and even gave me suggestions on what to order on my next visit. Tried to visit today with my family 01/16/2017 but they were closed. They have a few kinks to workout but I look forward to visiting again

Update - New Owner - Used to be 5 stars, now 1 Unfortunately the owner of Joto's in Tampa bought this location. We have been several times since and it has gotten worse each time. We are very sad, it was our favorite sushi place. Cost cutting is in full effect, very little avocado on the rolls, rolls fall apart, fish was so cold like it just came out of the refrigerator. After our last visit, I told my wife I never want to go back there. As someone else mentioned, new sushi chefs and only a couple of the same people that used to work there. My wife and I have been going to Joto's for 4 years and it is one of our favorite sushi places in Tampa Bay. First off the sushi is great - we love the volcano (best ever) and the food is always fresh. They have a nice selection of sake to choose from as well. We have never tried anything off of their regular menu...just the sushi. The staff at Joto's is FANTASTIC. From the guys who seat people and bus the tables, the ladies who wait on the customers in their kimonos and the sushi chefs preparing the food. We have always felt very welcome and comfortable there. The atmosphere is great too. It is very calming and a perfect ambience for enjoying sushi with a special person!

You know it's amazing when everyone cleans their plates off and leaves no leftovers! We had a couple different naan breads and 4 different chicken entrees. If you like Indian food, this restaurant is a must in Florida.

Excellent Vietnamese cuisine! The Pho is phantastic. We started with shrimp spring rolls, which were fresh but unremarkable. A little crunch in the form of cucumber and a little punch in the form of say, cilantro, would have made these stellar. The pho itself was perfect, and my partner had their take on pad Thai, which was made spicy, just the way I like it. Service was friendly. Price was fair. I will definitely return.

Love love love this place. Eat here atleast twice a month. Do yourself a favor. If your not asian don't go out of your comfort level and order some crazy meal. Stick to rice or noodles. I have recommended this place to a few and they always wind up ordering some dishes that even my boyfriend who is chinese and eats basically everything snubbed his nose at. The Indian pancake and any of the satays are amazing! I highly recommend the satay tofu even if you aren't a huge tofu eater like myself. Looking for great eats cheap? Eat it!
Had a great lunch at Le Saigon. Tasty Pho, grilled beef with lemongrass and a nice strong and sweet Vietnamese iced tea. Nice quiet atmosphere, a clean and cozy restaurant!

Nothing to review. We were a party of 6 who walked in on Mothers Day for drinks and dinner. There were quite a few empty tables. We stood by the hostess stand for a while. A couple of waitresses walked by us and said nothing. The bartender stood there looking at us but not speaking. No one said anything like, "feel free to seat yourself" or "please wait, someone will seat you shortly." We just stood there for 10-15 minutes and left.

How To Eat Kickass Food For Almost Nothing 101: 1. go to Kien Giang. it's not scary, trust me. Miss Saigon is across the parking lot- trust me, it's a better musical than a restaurant. 2. order the Bun #3 and French iced coffee with milk. mix a little hot pepper sauce from the red squeeze bottle into the bowl of golden sauce they give you, and pour it over the bowl of goodness steaming in front of you. let the coffee steep into the cup, stir it until it's mocha-colored, and try to dump it over the ice without spilling. you'll fail- it's ok. 3. Eat till you're stuffed, pay $10 and thank me later. On your 20th trip, when you finally work up the nerve to try something other than the fantastic Bun, go for the pancakes, the fresh rolls, the Banh Mi (poboy sandwich) and the spicy tofu. Honestly- this is not my favorite Pho. It's good, not great, I've had much better. But everything else is pretty amazing. My kids love the fresh and spring rolls, the fried rice and of course the Bun. The poboys are killer and THREE DOLLARS. The food is full of fresh vegetables and flavors- it's one of my favorite eats here in Nashville. No BYOB. Serves beer, possibly wine. Closed Mondays.
True Italian cuisine. Great tasting food and very reasonable prices. Wait staff is very friendly. I would highly recommend.

Great cappuccino and other espresso based drinks. Plus good salads, hummus and snack-y foods. Free wifi and comfy, homey seating. Cute barristas (male & female) and well poured shots of eeeeeeeeeee. Comfortable homey environment. Beats the hell outta fourbucks. I'm a fan!

Dang. I've been on an Indian kick recently, and I was really looking forward to Amber once I saw the many many positive Yelp! reviews. I dined with a few people over the lunch buffet, 2 which know a thing or two about Indian food (since they are Indian) and they were very nice to go and explain what everything was. Like Tandoori King, I can't exactly state what I ate other than it was amazing, the garlic bread (naan?) was great, and the service was phenomenal. The guys always came around to refill water, a few times which was definitely needed after trying a few things blindly.

If I could I would probably give this place different stars based upon different parts of the menu. - Non noodle dishes: 2.5 stars. They're really pretty run of the mill. - Noodle dishes: 3.5 stars. They're pretty solid - good flavor, great noodles. - Curry: 3 stars. Good, not great. - Most of their appetizers: 4 stars (especially the chicken dumplings, the crab rangoon, and the gui-chai although there are additional items I loved from their appetizer menu). - Kee mao (prefer with pork): 5 stars. God, I love their kee mao. The delicious noodles soak up most of the sauce with the dish, so I taste the depth of flavor in every bite. Although I love all the veggies, I especially love the tomatoes and the egg in the dish. Most kee maos or drunken noodles I've had either have egg or tomato, and even the ones with both never live up to LOS (my beloved abbreviation). EVER. I have found significantly better Thai food in Chicago, but no dish lives up to LOS' Kee Mao. None. Also on a complete aside that may come across as totally non-PC and downright weird, I adore the girl who used to take my lunch orders. She is certainly worthy of at least 1/2 a star. I want to steal her and claim her as my own - not like in a involuntary servitude sort of way but in a rent-a-friend sort of way. I would love to have her around to say, "yes, I like that shirt better than the blue shirt," or "sure, I'd love to go to the mall," or "why, yes, I'd love to make you pork kee mao, extra spicy." And, on an end note for this review, I'd like to thank LOS for the philosophy by which I try to live my life: Kee Mao Me Now!!!!!

This place was terrible. One guy working all alone, so it took forever. Everything in styrofoam, including the cup of water that we asked or. The Gyro was just ok, a little dry, but better with more yogurt sauce. The french fries were literally the worst that I've ever had.

My friends and I absolutely love their chicken. The temperature and the seasoning are perfect and proper. One of my favorite items here is the cleanse drinks. They really detox and cleanse your system after eating the chicken and mac&cheese. My class had the honor to meet Erica Hope, their GM. She was full of energy and confidence, her stories were engaging and we were All captivated by her.
Quality South Indian restaraunt. Probably one of the best one I've eaten at and I travel all over the country. It's like getting quality food right in south india

I haven't been to this restaurant in a while, but the Thai food is quite good and definitely some of the best I've had in St. Louis. I like to order the curries and order them Thai Spicy, which is quite good. The Thai iced tea and banana dessert are also good.

Tried this place for dinner a couple of weeks ago and loved it. I brought my 17 year old daughter and her bf for the buffet yesterday. Still loved it although i thought the food seemed a little more spicy so i'll prob just stick to dinners that can be custom ordered to be less spicy (I'm kind of a wuss when it comes to spicy food-love it but it hurts.) My only complaint was another customer who shouted at my daughter's boyfriend because he went to get some extra sauce with a plate that he'd already started eating from. He's young and doesn't eat out very often & i wasn't paying attention to what he was doing. I know what he did was incorrect but that's still no reason to yell NO at another patron like they were a puppy about to poo on your persian rug. I told her she didn't have to be so rude which i guess she didn't like because after we got into my car, she literally POINTED out the window at us and we could see her complaining to the maître d'. I'm not sure if i even feel comfortable going back, as this woman seemed to be somewhat of a regular, but it has nothing to do with the food or service. It totally ruined what started out to be a lovely meal. At least the kids had something to talk about in their therapy groups last night.

These guys just opened a week ago. Awesome lunch buffet spread on a Saturday! Lunch buffet all week long which is pretty uncommon among Indian restaurants. This place is among the best Indian places I've been (in Cali, PA, and Boston) and it's hard to believe you can find something like this in Collegeville.

The food here is consistently exceptional. My husband has been a customer for 9 years whenever he is in town. Portions are generous, service is excellent, and the quality of food is outstanding. They source seasonal food locally. Highly recommend. BYOB.

This place is one of my absolute favorites. Although there's hardly been a time when I've gone and people have been there the food is excellent and the staff are very attentive. I absolutely LOVE the Chicken Korma. I can't say I've ever enjoyed this dish at any other Indian restaurants. In fact I compare every other places Chicken Korma to Ekta's.

Kanella is, hands down, the best new restaurant in Philadelphia. The food is impeccably prepared, every time, (I've eaten there a dozen times at least) it is imaginative, hearty, yummy, everything you could want, and all of it comes from a chef who truly understands his heritage. The service is excellent, the prices are very reasonable, and the menu changes often enough that you are guaranteed variety. What's nice about the decor is that it is full of light, and a feeling of being in someone's home, while still providing a chic place to get a little fancied-up at night. Great date restaurant, great for families, great even for the single diner. I will keep coming back here, no question!

Food was extremely salty, amost unbearably so. Was it an off day? I don't know, but i would not go there ever again, esp bc we got charged $29 for 2 buffets with no drinks! We had to go to the nearby chinese restaurant right after.

Vientiane Cafe - oh I love you dearly. Not only do you always provide an affordable meal that all seem to enjoy - you are consistent, every dish is made to order, and OMG can you accommodate all food preferences! This visit is bitter-sweet, as I am departing the Philadelphia area for a new career opportunity. While I know I will be back from time-to-time, as I do have family in the area, I still can't just pop on over to one of my favorites when I need a good friend's couch to sit on. Because of all realistic measures, that is exactly what Vientiane is - a good friend's couch that you can come hang out in a laid back and chilled BYOB atmosphere. It's that friend that makes you that big bowl of comfort food to help you celebrate the highs or to crush to lows... and for all of the amazing experiences I have had here - I thank you! I thank you for making eating out and being social a possibility for a gal who has multiple food allergies, is a bit of a food snob, and living on a budget. You are amazing and I will continue to spread the word that all of Philadelphia needs to come check out Vientiane, if they have not already! This evening, we were seated and handed the revamp menu - which, is visually much more appealing. It is also helpful that this menu consists of GF (gluten-free) codes so I know what is and is not safe for me. I ordered a good classic for a table share - Lao Porridge (jow-piek) or congee. It is a smooth and comforting bowl of heaven - not too many more ways to explain it. It is a subtle dish with simple flavors meant to heal. Good thing I planned on sharing and that I ordered the large because the entire table went nuts over it. P.S I order it with the soft tofu rather than fried - it is just a preference, but I think it makes a world of difference. Then, despite having a huge list of things I wanted to try (aka the casserole, Laab, any of their fried rice dishes, Banh-Xeo, a dessert, and more.....) I had to go out with the first dish I ever ordered....... Drum roll please..... the King Soup - or as I like to describe it as a Pho with coconut milk and much more spice! We all know I love coconut, love a creamy dish, and we LOVE spice - so win was always written all over this dish! Oh, and did I mention that they can make it gluten-free, vegan and it comes in a GIANT bowl for under 15!? A friend of mine did order the new dish, Bamboo Stew (gang-naw-mai) which is bamboo shoots mixed with pumpkin and mushrooms (very earthy) and served with their famous sticky rice. Note, while this dish is not marked gluten-free, I am sure that if you ask, they are able to modify it for us gluten-free folks! In conclusion, it has been real Vientiane Cafe and I will certainly be back to visit! In the meantime, keep making some more awesome additions to your menu and oh, if any of my readers try the other dishes on my wish list, PLEASE SEND ME REVIEWS! Until next time. Oh, and check out all my other reviews of Vientiane Cafe below: http://gf-flamingo.blogspot.com/
Got off a cruise and headed straight here en route to airport with luggage and all. Ordered pho and spring rolls. Its pho and spring rolls.. tasted fine, just nothing special.
Looking for an expresso and a cosy place without Starbuck ' logos everywhere? Nice coffee and nice location in a walkable area.

Came into this restaurant in a poor mood cuz I had to drop my car in Chinatown for unexpected service. Left this restaurant content with the world. 1/2 chicken lunch special with red beans + yellow rice is the BUSINESS. I could only finish half. Tasted great, washed it down with a milk+mango smoothie (get it w/ milk not water, if you can). Staff was super nice. A lunch special that's good for 2 meals and a mango smoothie for $10? Hard to find that in philly. Come here hungry, leave here happy and fighting off the post-big-meal-nap-syndrome.
Came to the Yunk to look for a place to eat, came across this place and boom! Now addicted!

First and last time visiting this establishment. I ordered to go and went in to pick up the order. Stopped at hostess stand and was told to go over to the bar. I stood there waiting and waiting. One guy was on the register and never acknowledged me standing beside him. I could see my food was sitting on the counter because my name was written on a piece of paper. Two other employees were on their cell phones - why that is even allowed is beyond my comprehension. Someone finally noticed me and rang me up. I get home and this might be the worst Kung Pao chicken I have ever had. The chicken is tough and chewy and the only flavor is salt. Nothing spicy in this at all. I can get better at the food court on the Army base in Clarksville.

After a memorable breakfast I am really looking forward to trying dinner when they reopen in a new and bigger location. This is a far cry from any breakfast I've ever had, to me that is a good thing. The chef/owner's presence even during the morning hours shows how much commitment he has for his traditions and craft. How can you not like a place that serves fried Halloumi for breakfast.

I've always been a little disappointed in the BBQ available in this town. Jamaican Style Jerk does not belong to that generalization. It's one of the best hole-in-the-wall (literally) establishments I've ever visited. Get some jerk pork or chicken, rice and plantains and let everything in life be OK for awhile.

I came here with a friend after a nice hike at Percy Warner and ordered the rare steak pho along with an Vietnamese Iced Coffee and was mildly surprised to say that it was just as authentic as the best pho places in Los Angeles (which is saying a lot). The steak came out rare (which for a lot of pho places is never the case despite the printing on the menu) and the coffee was served very uniquely in a drop container that I had to pour into a cup of ice myself. Not that the work was troublesome, but it was the first time I had ever seen the coffee served in that fashion and the pricing was pretty fair. But like some other people have mentioned, the service here can be a hit or miss. I've come several times before and on some days it's just the regular routine of ordering, eating, paying, and out. On some days however, service can be down right awful when the staff seems to be having a bad day and it almost seems as if they take it out on you. It hasn't happened to me often, but in some of the worst scenarios, they don't even wipe the table very clean before they "order" you to sit down. Despite that though, I'd still come back here to get a bowl of good 'ol fashion pho. Food: 5 Pricing: 4 Service: 3

The lunch buffet was quite varied, and overall, quite tasty. Naan platter was refilled continuously. Masala chai was surprisingly good, but desserts were mediocre. Parking was awful, and getting out of my parking spot meant reversing into a busy road. Dangerous!

Came here a few times. I love pad thai, so I can only speak on that. The cooks make the food to order, and it's come out hot (temp). Service is good, never felt like I was waiting a long time to get service. Nice ambiance at night. =)

Excellent food very friendly people... I really enjoy the Indo-Chinese cuisine. It has a decent seating area and the ambience is nice and very well maintained. We have also ordered food many times and the delivery was super fast.. Great place to take family and friends.

As someone who loves noodles, ramen, pho... I can't say I can understand the hype about this place. It's got a good vibe and the place seems to always be packed, but the taste and pricing don't jive with the ratings. I was really looking forward to trying out this neighborhood joint but after 2 visits, I cannot say that I would visit again anytime soon. The last lunch visit our group's bowls were all quite salty (and they were different orders/dishes). The salt dominated so heavily that adding a bowl of hot water didn't improve any and it was hard to enjoy even on a hungry stomach (btw, I think they were insulted that we thought it was so salty but that's what it was.) this would mark the 2nd time I thought my ramen was too salty (2nd time topped the first). The hipster interiors is vibrant, but if you sit at the corner of the bar table, be ready to be interrupted constantly and bumped on by people trying to get by. The salt was unfortunately too unforgiving for me, eventhough a little extra salt is my personal guilty pleasure.
Best vada pav ,pappadi chat, dabeli pav...basically everything we had!!! Its a must try restaurant
Excellent traditional Thai. The Pho to the duck, its all excellant. The staff are alwats very friendly.

Visiting from out of town, we used Yelp to help us select a restaurant for a party of 10 on a Saturday night. Given all the 4 and 5 star reviews, we figured this would be a good bet. WRONG! - Sat at the bar for drinks while waiting for our table. 7 white wines and 7 reds wines were listed on the menu, however when ordering we were told they were out of 10 of the 14 wines. The bartender seemed very confused and could not tell us which wine was dry etc. - After settling on a wine, we were told they were out of wine glasses so we got served wine in champagne flutes and high ball glasses. - After being shown to our table, we were not greeted, given water or menus, or even looked at for over 10 minutes. - By this time, most of the party was ready for a second round of drinks but at no point (during the entire dinner) were we asked if we wanted more drinks. When we specifically asked for more drinks our waiter seemed very annoyed and took upwards of 10 minutes to get them (in our champagne flutes). - The pacing of the food was terrible! From the time the first entree came out, to the time the last entree was served was about 25 minutes. This left everyone in our party eating at completely different times! For example, one person just ordered soup... They were the last person to get served, while everyone else was already done eating. - At one point when asking the waiter about the status of 1/2 of our entrees, the waiter's response was "yes, it's coming, I only have 2 hands!" While throwing his hands in the air in disgust. Throughout our visit the entire staff was extremely unapologetic, rude, and unknowledgeable. - Our waiter also seemed unknowledgeable about the menu and was unable to answer questions about it. For example, when asked "Is this soup spicy?" His response was "What do you mean spicy?" After trying to explain, his response was "Um, I dunno, sometimes it can be." - A few of our dishes were fine however, others were major disappointments. First, the Salsa salad ($12) the menu description detailed a delicious salad which included guacamole, fresh mozzarella, and tomatoes. However, the guacamole was clearly squeezed out of a tube, and the dressing (some tried Mango, others got balsamic) were extremely thick and also appeared to be squeezed out of a tube. When you pay $12 for a side salad.. You expect higher quality, fresh ingredients. - Next, the quality/preparation of the chicken dishes were unappetizing (I.e. Chicken and rice gumbo) The chicken was equal parts meat, tendons, ligaments, fat. One person in our party had to pick out all the meat from their dish evident was inedible. - Overall, our experience at Salsa's was extremely disappointing to the point of comical. From the rude, unknowledgeable, unapologetic staff, to the price for the low quality, poor prepared food; this restaurant is not recommended! However we did get handfuls of Rolos thrown on our table as we were leaving with a "Here you go, you all gets one chocolates"

I ended up here on the spur of the moment for a quick supper last week with a friend. I used to go to a restaurant by the same name on Jasper Avenue that served Middle Eastern rice dishes - I am not sure if this is the same one, but the menu certainly looked familiar. However, instead of a rice dish, we had donairs, and they were spectacular: lots of flavourful meat, a good sauce, fresh veggies - it was packed with meat and the meat tasted different than the typical pressed meat that is used by commercial donair places. Prices are very reasonable. I am definitely coming back.

We ate at Cheu Noodle for the first time last week. The place is small (10 seats at tables and maybe 10-12 seats at the bar) and it is a popular place but tables turn quickly. The energy is great, and the food is really good and affordable. My husband and I split these dishes: Lamb neck noodles, Chinese sausage and beef dumplings, Charred Brussels spouts. Each dish was tasty and well-prepared. They only offer one kind of beer on tap, but it was very good. We will definitely go back.

Truly terrible service. The hipsters have the urgency of a tortoise and couldn't be less engaging or friendly. We waited forever for an old fashioned cocktail and after watching a majority of the staff work to do menial work like stack crates I eventually called them over to tell them I had been waiting 20 minutes for a drink though the place was virtually empty. All were confused and them took another 10 minutes to figure out what to do about being slow and incompetent. Would never return.

The decor was nice and the service was prompt. Sadly, the dishes lacked flavor and the desert was the frozen kind that you find at the Asian market. The seafood was definitely not fresh. I will not be returning. I recall the dishes being much tastier years ago.

Very good Sushi and service! I really like the Crab Rangoon appetizer. It is very flavorful unlike most places which are kinda bland. My wife likes the Thai food a lot. After our first visit we have been back many times. I am writing this review from the Sushi bar.
Great food in the buffet and comfy atmosphere. The view of the river valley isn't bad either.

Mediocre Food The only reason this place even deserves two stars us because of the server Tom, who really took care of us. We did express our displeasure about the quality of the food to the owner but his attitude was a total put off. Never going back there.

Having eaten here twice, I can say that the food here is quite good and perfectly spiced. It's a very small dining room though, maybe 10 tables, so not great for larger groups. Also, the waiter could have somewhat more personality and attention. However, that would not stop me from returning.
Yummy Thai food. Chicken pad Thai is our favorite. Great service and very fast. Their dinner special is a great deal and they also offer a lunch special. Also the veggie spring rolls are delish.

The worst Indian buffet ever ! Save ur time and money ! Will never go there ! Went there for lunch buffet this afternoon, there was no customer ' not surprisingly nymore ! The Chen tandoori - cold , tasted like pee ! No kidding ! Medhu vada - hard as a rock !! Chicken and mutton had the exact same gravy ! I am a good cook myself and by the looks of it I could tell the chef made one gravy and jus mixed boiled meat in both ! Disgusting food ! If this place is still open after 3 months I will personally write a apology letter to yelp ! I hope the owner keeps my comment !

this might be my favorite place in the entire city. anything and everything is stellar. go early, wait for an hour if you have to. this is the way food should be made. the ONLY thing I would note is the extraordinarily cramped seating...however, the food STILL makes up for it and it deserves 5 stars anyway.
This restaurant is really clean and nice. The staff is courteous and friendly. The food is amazing especially the oxtail stew, and curry goat.

Great cocktails! Very good service. I had the dirty rice arancini which was really really good. The biscuits that are served with entrees were also delicious. Unfortunately my entree fell a bit short. I had the goat curry with sweet potato gnocchi. I was really looking forward to it, but the gnocchi was not so great and the curry sauce was very thin. Personal preference for a thicker sauce. I would go back for drinks, appetizers, and dessert, but probably not the entrees.

IThai Sushi is an excellent local Thai restaurant in an unassuming location. You don't really know what to expect judging by the outside. Inside, it's a cute little spot, a traditional Thai decor with tables in the center and booths around the sides in two rooms. On a recent Monday night there were only 2 other couples dining, but the take out business was booming. That's always an encouraging sign. It's an extensive menu with all of the traditional Thai dishes, plus a wide variety of sushi. Amy tried the pad thai with chicken. This was excellent, among the best we've had. The noodles were cooked slightly al dente, the peanut sauce sweet and creamy, the garnishes of scallion and bean sprouts crisp and fresh. A generous portion of sliced broiled chicken topped the dish. This was ordered medium hot, and the spice is what you would expect - resulting in a runny nose and rosy cheeks but tasty in every bite. I had the green curry with shrimp. The curry was smooth and creamy with just a little heat, brimming with red and yellow bell pepper slices and at least 10 nice sized shrimp. The shrimp were well prepared, a nice snap to each bite, firm and not mealy. A generous scoop of perfect sticky rice (molded into the shape of a star, a nice touch) is served on the side. The curry over that rice is to die for! The tab for two was $30 including 2 soft drinks, so inexpensive. If you're looking for excellent Thai food in a comfortable environment right here in town, try IThai. Recommended.
I have fallen in love with the Pho here! Broth is so excellent it does not need sauce!! Excellent customer service! That always seals the deal for me!!

I ate here, used to love this spot under Binder, I would eat there 2-3 a week, he sold it, then it was sold again to the current owners. The last time I was there, it was GROSS. The food was probably the worst tasting food I have ever eaten, there's tons of crap on the walls about specials, and you better eat all the food, or they will charge you for the food you didn't eat, I mean JUST CORNY and feels super GHETTO! I have eaten tons of Indian food, and I was so hungry, I just thought maybe they put these signs up, because people didn't like real Indian food, or maybe it was spicy or, I wasn't really sure, but I wasn't worried about loading up my plate, as I can take spice, I like flavor, etc. I literally had to force the food down, and only becuase I was worried about having to pay more than the buffet price, because the food was disgusting. I asked for my Naan well done, they served me cold Naan. I couldn't wait to pay and get out of there. Binder if you are reading this, please, buy this place back and restore the glory that used to be, SS Super and Taste of India. That place was the best.

I went here for the lunch buffet the other day and I need to come back and order off the menu. Like most buffets, the food has to appeal to a broad palette so it was a bit too bland and mild for me, but the variety they offered was good.

This place is really good! I've tried the beef and chicken shawarma and falafel in a pita and they're all great, but the chicken is probably at the bottom of the list. The restaurant is very bustling and has a nice ambiance. The prices are a little high but they are worth it. My favorite part is watching all the freshly made pitas tumbling down the speed oven. Note: the best base for chicken and beef is baba ganouj and for falafel you should use hummus

This is our favorite place for diners/ dooners or fries with feta cheese and a beer, or Burek with cheese and spinach! I'm so happy we found it in St. Petersburg ! Highly recommend!!! Prices also very reasonable. Also the lady working there is very nice and polite

My wife and kids decided to meet me for lunch today. Since I work few blocks from Bhann Thai, we decided it give it a shot. My coworker recommended to go early to avoid the lunch hour rush. My wife arrived at 11:30 at the restaurant so she can order for us in advance. When I arrived at 11:45, she was still waiting for the menus but the hostess did come over to tell us there's 10 to 15 minute wait after we order. We did not mind the wait but she never brought us the menu. We felt ignored after after making several eye contacts with the hostess, I decided to grab the menus myself. My wife mentioned that a couple arrived after her and they were already eating. The hostess never came back to take our order so I politely told her we were ready to order. She comes over to take our order but she tells us it's 30 to 40 minute wait now. My lunch hour would be over by the time they served us. Upset with hostess' rude behavior and bad service, we decided to go somewhere else. We ended up driving to the next closest Thai restaurant in St. Peters. That's the problem with some of these small restaurants as soon as they pick up some business, their service goes down the drain. It's too bad, we don't have another Thai restaurant in Earth City but we're never coming back to Bhann Thai. They need to take lessons in customer service and if they are so busy, hire more help.

The owner was super friendly! He claims that they don't serve anything that's not good and he was so right! I didn't get a chance to try the food because I was full, but I tried the lassi drinks in guava and mango flavors. Both were delicious! They gave the remaining that didn't fit in the cups in smaller cups, which were useful for swapping flavors with my friend and a very nice gesture of service since the goodness doesn't go to waste. I'd hit up this place every week if I live in Philly. Going to miss this place so much in the mean time =(
Big Fan here. Great Pho and other spicy soups. Clean and good service as well.

We were on our way from LA to Big Sur and we wanted to do dinner somewhere along the way; Siam Elephant came up on our radar in this lovely beach town. We were so glad!!! Spicy tofu basil, Pumpkin coconut curry, and Pad Thai was feasted on, and we promised each other we would surely return. Very friendly service, very sweet cozy atmosphere, and lovely vibe all around!
Place is ok .... Not all that. Venue is very tight.

We had a party of 23 for a rehearsal dinner on Saturday, and couldn't be happier with our choice. They make planning simple with very resaonable prices and plenty of choices for private event menus. And everything was delicious. Everyone especially raved about the seared salmon. No one had a single complaint about anything. How often do you get 23 people together with nothing to whine about??
Hidden gem. Friendly service and good food. The Banh cuon was very good. It reminded me of California.

Great atmosphere, friendly knowledgeable staff & very clean. Best of all the owner cooks authentic Thai, Laos/SE Asian dishes. Very easy menu for Americans to order from & staff will assist you with suggestions &daily specials. This is the third (3rd) Thai Phooket in Nashville area & the best Thai Food in Smyrna & Murfreesboro - a must try.

Couldn't be more disappointed. Was really looking forward to having a gyro. The lamb gyro is not a gyro. Plain Greek yogurt in a pita with chunks of lamb. Should be lamb cooked on a spit and shaved off. Should be tzaziki. Should have flavor. Gross. Where's the flavor?? Get it together. Do people here not know any better or do the just not care.

We've had this bookmarked for awhile but finally went for a late lunch today and so glad we did! Everything was delicious! The soups were amazing (hubby had Kozy, which is lamb-based soup, and I had the lentil soup. The soup and hot tea come with the meal, as well as a small salad. The chicken kabob was so flavorful and well prepared, and came with a generous serving of rice. I had the kubah halab, rice balls filled with meat, onions and spices - so good!! Mom is the cook and after we asked if we could take her home with us, she came out to meet us! Very nice people. We will be back!

I used to be a fan of this place because it had decent pho & fried wontons. But the last time i went there, i found a bone in my pho! I almost swallowed it. I will not be going there ever again. I won't miss their terrible service either.

Fresh quality food! This is the best restaurant to eat and safe for health), because many restaurants around do not follow basic clean tables and floors.. SO YOU CAN TRUST FOR FRESHNESS AND HEALTHY FOOD WITH MIXED GRILL GYROS! I took there my Mom, Sister and Baby), so the freshness and quality was important

Only giving two stars because the decor was nice. We were there for Sunday brunch and it was literally the worst brunch I have ever had in my entire life. I will recommend to go to a diner for more quality food. I got the 8th st egg Benedict and it was came with two very small pieces of eggs on English muffin plus a weird green salad and bland meshed potato on the side. Boy, their cook couldn't even poach eggs. The Egg was hard and solid inside, not runny at all. The ham was dark and over cooked. Too much acidity in their bearaise.
