Tonight we tried the Crispy Basil Duck and Pad Kra Pow (Tofu) and both dishes were excellent. I was particularly impressed with the duck, which had a lovely texture and flavor and was cooked perfectly, without a hint of gameyness that can often turn people away. It was also topped with a mound of flash fried crispy basil which resulted in a pleasant mild basil flavor. For me this dish really stole the show, but everything else was also excellent. I will definitely be heading back!

I can't get enough of this place!! I probably come at least 1 a week.. maybe have skipped a week here and there. Food is always so good. Bun bo hue with rice noodles are my favorite!!! Get it almost all the time. Their pho is probably one of the best here in Indy. Canh chua (sweet and sour soup) is one of my all time favorite Vietnamese dishes and they surely don't disappoint. Order it with their braised catfish or braised pork. Customer service is always great! Friendly people and they are always kind. I love it here! Must give it a try!! Oh and don't forget to start with the fried Vietnamese egg rolls!!

So two years ago, we attended our niece's wedding in Devon (we are from Arlington, VA). She married a young man who parents live in India, and they chose Desi to cater the rehersal dinner. The food was beyond excellent, so much so that no matter when we eat Indian, we always compare it to that delish rehersal dinner! Well, you can imagine our disappointment when we ordered take-out from Desi the night before Thanksgiving (last week), and the food was not even close to our past experience. The biggest (and most costly) mistake was to order 7 Butter Chickens, only to find out that the chicken was so DRIED OUT (not to mention, it looked like they took some left over Tandori Chicken and dumped it in the butter sauce, and voila...dinner!) Yuk. And the butter chicken sauce was watery and tasteless. My 10 year old kept saying, "but Mommy, this isn't what I remember AT ALL!" I guess more than anything, I hate being ripped off, and that is how we felt as we sat there eating $100 worth of not good food. So save your money, and go somewhere else. Our family (and we are a large one!) is done with this place.

My girlfriend and I got a groupon deal. The food was fantastic, so good in fact we got another groupon and will be back long after that too. We are both meat eaters but I left full and totally happy. Great food and service!

Best Afghani food in Philly, probably the most underrated restaurant I've been do. I've been going here since my college days and I am 5 years out of college now and I still love the food. The quality of their food is superb, the owners are very friendly. I've seen their daughter grow up, she was younger when I used to come while in school, she is now old enough to greet and sit the customers! The ambiance is great as well, you feel right at home as you walk in. The bread is cooked fresh and the salad is great. I love their lamb kabob platter, def. recommend it if you are a fan of lamb. Otherwise their chicken and beef is just as good.

Vegan Review! I have never been to a Puerto Rican restaurant before, and on a whim, my husband and I decided to try something different. Being vegan, we are always open to new ideas about trying different types and flavors of food. I started out by looking over the online menu before we arrived at the restaurant. Salsa is on Facebook, so I messaged them to see if I could clarify the vegan choices that would be available. They responded promptly to any and all questions I asked, so we were looking forward to a meal there. We arrived around 7:00pm on a Wednesday night. There was no hostess to greet us for the first 5-10 minutes. The restaurant was very busy at this time. They were completely full and there was a live Puerto Rican band in the back and dancing in the back outside seating. That is where we finally ended up sitting after our hostess waited on us. This turned out to be a fantastic spot to listen to the band and watch the people salsa dance. The female singer had a beautiful voice and the band was excellent. They even had a dance exhibition going on later that night for us to enjoy. Food wise..for an appetizer we got the Sorullos de Maiz (sweet corn fritters) vegan, but I think they would have been better with the sauce that was provided but alas, who knew if the sauce was vegan..bummer..so we didn't partake in the sauce that came it. Next we got Pasta Primavera with veggies-vegan-no cheese- and the Mofongo de Yuca-also vegan-The pasta and yuca were delicious. We both loved it. The only complaint that I have about this place is the SERVICE! After ordering our appetizer, it was delivered to our table in a timely manner........BUT our entrees..it was so incredibly ridiculous how long it took for us to receive them. Our server came out once and said she was telling the kitchen to hurry up with our order...then I had to go find our server to have her go ask again where our food was and find out if there was a problem. The people sitting next to us that came a long time after us finally received their food. They said that a member of their party went up to the front to see why it was taking so long preparing their food and all they said was that they had "forgotten their order". We had to ask a total of 3 times and wait over one and one-half hours before we received our food without any explanation as to why it had taken so long. Other that that, we loved the food

I love Lilly's!! Her Pho Ga with vegan broth is a heaven sent whether you're sick or just looking for a good filling yet light soup. Her rice dishes and egg rolls are also amazing. Plus Lilly her self is very personable and sweet.

This is the best Thai food we have ever had. Our son from LA and his friend said there isn't a place in L.A. As good as this! The owners and staff are very nice, and helpful. From fresh rolls to shrimp curry you can be assured it is the freshest. Have eaten there for 6 years and it hasn't disappointed us or our guest once. Try it, you'll agree.

I had been wanting to try this place that opened in Apollo Beach about 10 months ago. Their location is unfortunate, because unless you know it's there, it won't attract much drive-by service. I hope they can do some advertising to get more folks in the door. The owner was super friendly and freshly made our orders promptly. I got the Falafel platter, which came w/ tabouli, rice, pitas, hummus, and of course, the BEST Falafel! My girlfriend got the Seafood pita and also loved the flavor. I will definitely be a regular and encourage others to try if you're in the mood for authentic, homemade Mediterranean.

I made a last minute decision to stop here for dinner...and am so happy I did! I went in intending to get some food to go (I was by myself), but it was so nice and inviting inside I decided to eat at their bar area. They have a really welcoming set up and a nice big screen tv. The reggae music fit the tone of the restaurant and was not so loud you couldn't converse. The owner could not have been nicer when I let him know it was my first visit and he went over some items on the menu. I decided upon the oxtail which came with a side of rice and peas, salad and plantains. Everything was delicious! The oxtail meat fell off the bone and mixed well with the rice and peas. I also tried the beef patty which was similar to an empanada but even better - not greasy and perfectly seasoned. Needless to say I needed a to-go box to take some food home for seconds! I definitely plan to return! There were several items on the menu I wanted to try and enough there for all tastes (meat, chicken, fish and vegetarian options). Really enjoyed it!
Delicious Puerto Rican and Latin food. Plantains, yuca and empanadas that remind me of home. Friendly service and great atmosphere. Wednesdays are great with Latin live music.

Stopped here on my way out of Philly, I had to see what the buzz was about! The short rib tacos were sold out so I had to choose between the capn crunch burrito and chicken satay tacos. I chose the burrito and I think I chose wrong. Its just fried tilapia with spicy sauce. It was not nasty by any means but just really really basic. I also ordered the Mango Tea. Too too sweet for my taste. And they only take cash which was a bummer so I had to run to the ATM and pay an ATM fee. Service was fast and customer service was great.
Friendly cozy atmosphere. Loved watching the chef/owner doing his craft from the glass panel to the kitchen. We tried a bit of everything and were not disappointed. A must!

Why oh why haven't I had brunch here?!?! LISTEN UP! I live literally 10 houses away from Kanella. I've had their dinner and to be honest I wasn't too impressed. My neighbor asked if I wanted to grab brunch one saturday morning and I agreed... we arrived without wine and immediately sent the husband to the house for some good vino. We started with the dips app along with some falafel. They were fantastic!! :) For our entrees we both got the Cyprus Breakfast which comes with grilled halumi, two eggs, ham and bread. YUM YUM YUM it was so good! We also split an order of the potatoes which too were amazing. I will be returning this weekend for another yummy way to start the weekend!

Excellent fast food, great service, fast and inexpensive.Everything was fresh and tasted great. Next time I'm in North Tampa I will return. Good job Zeko's! Now place one in south Florida! We had: Beef Gyro & Greek Salad Small Falafel Hummus Shish-Kabob
Great Indian food always cooked fresh and to perfection. The owner and his wife are so sweet and will accommodate in any way they can! Amazing lunch buffet for $9.99!

Ordered the Turkish hummus and corn salad as appetizers. Corn salad was great. The hummus was the saltiest item I've ever ordered from a restaurant. But we then ordered the meatballs. It was like a salt competition with the hummus. Barely edible. Nice general vibe and the feel of a nice restaurant, but the food doesn't back up the experience. One and done.

If you're ever in the mood for vietnamese hoagies, Cafe Ngu Y is the place to go! I have been going to this hole in the wall place for years and they never fail to please my palate =) I usually go with the veggie, special or the meatball hoagie. I don't know what it is they do, maybe the bread...whatever it is, they're doing something right. Price is reasonable and service is great! Can't go wrong at this place.

So much has changed in our lives in the two years that we've been eating bacon egg and cheese with Bui Sauce. You quit Pilam. I quit Cobb. You quit smoking. I moved back home. You started a new job, then another new job, then another one. I did, too. You came into your own as an artist. I came out as trans to my friends and family. It's October and we wear turtlenecks almost exclusively now. (You joke that we killed a lot of turtles to get where we are.) Will we always wear turtlenecks? Probably not, you say. They'll come in and out of style. But they'll always be there for us when we need to come back to them. Mr. Bui was gone for a while, but he's back now. Bacon egg and cheese with Bui Sauce is a dollar more expensive than it used to be. But it's alright. The sandwich is the same, and it's always there for us when we need to come back.

Amber has the best Indian food in the U.S.! My husband and I have been to other Indian restaurants in Chicago, Seattle, Portland and so far none came close to the creamy goodness that's in our favorite dishes in Amber. Our favorites are: Malai Kofta, Vegetable Korma, Chicken Tikka Masala. The Malai Kofta stands out because of the creaminess and surprise sweetness from the grapes. It's definitely good to the last drop. I am definitely going to miss this restaurant!

I have been to this restaurant twice -- once with my 10 year old son, and again with the whole family, and each visit was a treat! Both times we were welcomed by Grace who operated as both hostess and server during the off times we were there. Grace made both experiences great with her infectious smile and laugh. She explained the different dishes and helped us through the all-you-can-eat Korean BBQ process. The food was flavorful and amazing. We will definitely be back again, and suggest this place for those seeking authentic Korean food in the central county corridor.

Fantastic indian place. Food is excellent and in good sized portions. Go for some of the vegetarian for a change of pace. Only down side is that if it gets a bit busy they loose the overview sometimes. And decore could use a facelift. But again if you don't want to look at it order out.

Delicious and different. No discounted lunch menu on weekends, but prices are reasonable and portions would easily serve two very hungry people. Flatbread type bread is addictive. We had the grape leaves entree with olives, feta, tomatoes, and cucumbers on romaine, like you would get in a Greek restaurant; and gheimeh, a beef lentil stew that was bitter and tart with dried lime, of which the server suggested I taste a sample before I ordered it since not everyone likes it (I did, but it is very bold). The owner owns the entire mostly empty plaza and another Persian Room in Scottsdale. It's one of the most sumptuously decorated restaurants in Tucson. Happy to have something different in town.

I went here on Friday night pretty close to when they were closing. They greeted us happily and we ordered our food. The waitress Mia, was very friendly and helpful. She explained everything to us and I settled on Pad Thai. We also ordered crab rangoon as an appetizer. The crab rangoon was crispy and had a ton of crab/cream cheese in it. When I received the Pad Thai it was beautiful. It was a light color and the vegetables that I ordered on it just popped. The chicken breast was cooked perfectly and complimented it so well. Everything was fresh. Seriously. Everything. The chicken and noodles had just been made and the vegetables, mint AND cilantro (thanks Mia) looked like they had just been picked. One of my friends had shrimp teriyaki and the shrimp were large. MK came out and introduced himself and told us that there was no rush for us to leave. Which was very kind. He talked a little about Saturday nights there and how they were going to add to the menu - and if we had any suggestions (I sincerely think he wants to know.). I gave them 4 stars because I think they should have a bigger menu. When we left he said goodbye to us each by name. Classy. I'll definitely be back.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Did a "Dinner on Don", we were hoping for great Indian a couple weeks ago. Checked out yelp and there were a lot of great reviews. It was downtown so I made reservations for it. Arrived around 6pm and there were only 3 tables full..the place was empty and we would soon find out why. We were quickly seated and ordered our food, took them about 40 minutes to get it out to us. The food was ok, but the price seriously! 1.50 for 1 nan! not for a basket or a few, but 1 skinny thin little nan!!! that was a bunch of crap! Would not recommend this place to a single soul!!!! The curry's were ok, I would have rather we go to the Indian restaurant on state and Glenwood! much better!!!!! 1.50 for Nan!!!!!

Stopped in over the weekend for lunch, beautiful setting right on the water. Sat and had a few cold ones and watched the boats out on the gulf. The food was really good, took a while to get but it was fresh so I don't mind a little wait for quality. Crab Cakes were very good, the grilled fish was very tasty as well. Beer was cold and the staff was very friendly and attentive. Jessica waited on our table and she was wonderful. She told us that weekend nights they have live music and it is pretty busy. Definitely going to have to check that out one weekend. Two thumbs up..

Of all the places I ate at when I vacationed in Hudson, the blew all the others out of the water. Hudson suffers from a serious lack of food chops but Sam's really holds its own. It's got a great atmosphere - sometimes they feature live bands with a bar area near-by, and have some great specialty drinks (heavy on the rum) I started with some oysters with some lemon, tabasco and horseradish - sooo fresh and succulent. Being that I am from NY, I tried to stay away from dishes that are more common to the north and go for something that is considered more southern - so I went for Shrimp and grits - a dish I had been dying to try. The Shrimp and grits at Sam's was out of this world! Grits were so creamy, shrimp perfectly cooked and the flavors of the dish all perfectly complimented each other. The portion was huge, and filled me up quickly, so I had plenty left-over. Great ambiance, great service, great drinks, and great food!

What a meal. I had visited Turkey last year and was looking to find some of those flavours again. Sofra exceeded any expectations I had. From fantastic wine pairings (great service all around) to the best in grilled meats, this restaurant made a good dining experience, great. The chef/owner even came over to hear about my recent travels. Genuine, quality food made from scratch is what you can expect here. Teşekkür ederim - thank you!

When I first moved to this area, I was looking for something different. Well I found it at Pho 36. I would give the food five stars and the service only three stars if they are busy. With that being said, it is still one of my favorite places to eat. The chicken wings are so amazing!!! I've have officially made this my favorite restaurant in this area. I finally tried the bubble tea and it was fantastic.
The food is wonderful the staff is very friendly they are very much a family restaurant if you want to try one of the best Thai restaurants in the Bay Area the come here

Food is good for an indo chinese place in the area. However, it feels slightly over priced when you factor in the poor service. The guy who took the order was paying more attention to larger groups. Messed up our order. That day their air conditioning system was probably down and they didn't even keep the door open for circulation and didn't care to inform the customers. The mango mousse was a flowing mess. All the good work in the kitchen is undone by bad service.

This is one of our favorite restaurants. We were so happy when we found out they were opening a location in Tucson. I highly recommend the nachos. I know it sounds weird to order nachos at a Mediterranean restaurant, but they have a really good bean mixture and top it with salsa and tzatziki and it's awesome!

Not a good experience. This is advertised as an upscale restaurant and is priced as such. Don't mind paying for good food and good service. In this case, didn't get either. We went for lunch during the week. They had one lady seating, taking orders and serving. While the place was not busy, it took a long time for everything. There was another lady walking around, looked like possibly manager or owner. She had no interest in helping out. The space looks like minimal effort was taken to convert this from a bar to a restaurant. Old tables and chairs placed randomly around the room and on a wooden dance floor. Would not go back.
The worst hookah bar, bad service and dirty hookah. They said only cash after I finish!!!

India Palace is a fantastic lunch spot with a good buffet. I normally shy away from buffets, especially for lunch... I hate over eating and then having to go back to work, but in normal indian style, this food is full of flavor and is so good that two plates with a broad selection on each will fulfill your palette very well. The staff are friendly and it is fast service with a smile.

The drinks are amazing, the scenery is beautiful and the service impeccable. What more could you want? Known for their variety of well hand crafted cocktails, Tryst does not disappoint. We arrived around 8 p.m. On First Friday in St. Pete, which if you are from Tampa Bay Area you know is a shit show all night long. Despite this we were greeted by friendly staff and sat inside at the comfy booths. We ordered the Tryst, "muddled raspberry, strawberry, fresh lemon juice & organic elderflower liqueur, shaken with deep eddy vodka & a hint of cranberry juice", and an Irish Grasshopper "Jameson black barrel whiskey, marie brizard white creme de cocoa, marie brizard green creme de menthe & heavy cream garnished with a mint sprig. Imagine St. Pete beach encapsulated in a drink and you have the Tryst cocktail. Imagine eating mint chocolate chip ice cream atop the mountains of Three Rock in Dublin and you have the Irish Grasshopper. I am huge fan of a great drink, so if you are in St. Pete Tryst is the right place!

Was sorry to see Kombo Kitchen leave so it was nice to see it replaced with more thai food! We ordered the larb gai, pad thai and nam sod. They were out of the eggrolls so we got the steamed pot stickers instead. Everything we had was good - will definitely be going back.

My husband, family, friends and I all love nadia. We especially love it for lunch because it's $8.50 for a soup an app/salad and an entree. I love their tofu lemongrass soup and I used to love the chicken lemongrass when I was a meat eater. My hubby loves the silver noodle soup. We also love their veg spring rolls, pad see you, silver noodles, and all of their curries! Yumm! For dessert we like the mango with the sticky rice it one of my favorite desserts of all time! Its also a byob which is great because you can save alot of money that way and there food is pretty cheap. I'm not sure if it's authentic because I've only ever had thai from 2 other places but I sure love Nadia! It's also great for takeout! It will always be our standby if I don't feel like cooking or we just want thai food!

The hospitality was really good. I had the jungle curry with fried tofu, and it was yummy. Nevertheless to say, the Thai iced tea they have is one of the best I have had! I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants to try Thai food!

Definitely a famous Malaysian restaurant in China town and probably my 1st one since I moved to Philly years ago. Love their food in general and they have good amount of flavor in each option. And the price is resonable.

4 stars because the Pho is authentic and delicious. To me an authentic restaurant like Pho An Hoa must first and foremost deliver an excellent product. The customer service in this case is truly secondary in my opinion, unless it's just awful- which it wasn't by any means. The food is wonderful and delicious. Only one other Pho restaurant in the Tampa area has gotten our approval. We ordered the Pho Ga with Shrimp, 2 orders of fresh rolls and Pho Bo. Each bowl of Pho was full of noodles and the protein's. The expected plate of sprouts, basil, lime and jalapeños was plentiful! The broth was tasty without being overly salty at all. The fresh rolls were tasty and indeed fresh. Chock full of pork, shrimp, noodles and veggies. Of course the accompanying hosin sauce was great too. I found the server- though only one- to be very attentive and sweet. We will most assuredly return to this restaurant.

Very pleasantly surprised! Ordered takeout: Shrimp Scampi, Clams over Linguini and the Fresh Mozzarella with Pesto over Greens. Neither pasta dish was over 'sauced' yet the flavor was way above average. The shrimp may have been a tad overcooked but it really didn't take away from the dish as the flavor of the shrimp was very nice. Would definitely order again!

Great food at reasonable prices! Really, people, 3 stars?? However, it is no surprise that this section has gotten some of the douchiest reviews imaginable. After all, South Philly is now festering with hipster douchery, and these people can't just experience a good thing and let it be. Here are my retorts to a few of the negative comments I read here: 1) Yes, plantains are generally a garnish. Especially when they're flash-fried or sauteed and not cooked slowly as to caramelize extensively, in which case they can serve as a sweeter side. 2) Jerking, like BBQing, softens bone (esp chicken bone) to the extent that the meat can be chopped with the bone after it is finished cooking. Hence the bones in with the pieces of chicken. If you can't figure out a way around them, well...Darwin. 3) $15 is reasonable for half a chicken and a huge container of rice, especially in the middle of a major American city. 4) Rice (and the beans and cabbage) served with jerk chicken is not in of itself meant to have a high flavor profile. You put the (extremely) flavorful chicken on top. The rice mellows out the dish. A dish is the sum of its parts; stop critiquing every single component like you're some sort of expert (which you're not, probably on anything, and definitely not on the way cabbage should compliment starch and protein in Jamaican cuisine). 5) This is how its done in Jamaica. If something did not turn out the way you expected, its because you were wrong . You know who wasn't wrong? The Jamaican cook who makes Jamaican food for a living. What are the sheer odds of you being right? Are you crazy? 6) Which brings me to my last point: Jamaican culture is on island time. This is a fact, not a silly stereotype. Jamaica is probably the only country the stereotypes surrounding which are all true. Which is fine because they're all pretty cool stereotypes. Ever see a Jamaican movie villain? Its impossible. So yes, the service might be a little slow when it gets slammed - as happens anywhere. BYOB to pass the time, and just try to sit and enjoy yourself instead of knit-picking at every tiny little thing around you. PS Maybe your server would approach your table faster if you didn't have a handlebar mustache and fedora on. You're not allowed to make culinary critiques while looking like you work at a carnival. Go back to the suburbs. Sorry, that's the rant of someone who worked in restaurants for 10 years, and who has also eaten some very good homemade Jamaican food. Bottom line is, the food is great. Kudos to the Jerk Hut for maintaining authenticity and deliciousness.

I'm really happy to see great reviews for this Dominican restaurant/take-out spot. The value you get for the money you pay is unbelievable here. It has become our go-to restaurant when we don't feel like cooking. For just $8 you can get an entire half chicken, rice, beans, and a side like delicious plantains. This is just one of what seems like hundreds of dishes and food combinations that you can order here. We have tried several, but still have many more to experience. The owners and employees here are fantastic and always willing to help. They are a great addition to the neighborhood, and bring a great familiar feeling to weeknight dinners.
Got the Brisket Kimchi ramen, the worst ramen I have ever had, tasted like watery kimchi soup with instant noodles. 2 stars because everything else other than the ramen was good.

From the moment you walk into this restaurant you are in awe. The atmosphere made you feel as if you were walking into Thailand. The hand-carved tables were beautiful and made for good conversation. I was with a small group of co-workers and we tried a few appetizers before ordering (spring rolls, Rangoon & edamame). They didn't last long as they were so good! As this was my first time eating Thai food, I asked for a recommendation. I got the shrimp and eggplant with the green curry. It was so good!!! Really enjoyed this restaurant and will definitely come back the next time I am in town.

Ordered the BBQ chicken entree for take out. Also got an order of the vegetable dumplings. Must say, the service is super friendly! The originally told me 30 min, then called me back 10 minutes later to let me know the food was already ready. I appreciated that. The entree was definitely enough to share, but the taste and quality was just "eh". I will say that the friendly service is enough for me to give it a second try on a different dish.

I went with the pad thai. The smiling elephant has green bean noodles for the pad thai. At first I was hesitant to try the green bean noodles as I know rice noodles are a solid choice. However these noodles were less heavy but still were amazing. They were lighter and healthier and I left feeling good,and not being weighted down by a greasy thai meal. I would recommend the rice dishes too, I tried my friends and the ingredients are fresh. You can't go wrong here, I would return for sure.

Expensive but the food is not the best- the area is very clean though and the service nice. I think that if I was going to have a salad, then it shouldn't cost what it does here. The hummus is all right tho

Tandoor is welcome newcomer to the neighborhood, with adequate portions, and reasonable prices. I found that Tiffin and Ekta have raised their prices and lowered their portions. I see people have given a lot of 3 star reviews, but then read and they chose the dinner buffet. I get take-out and it's delicious, but if you choose a dinner buffet you should not be able to review it, or at least take that into account when doing so

Husband and I ate here last night and both the food and service was EXCELLENT. He had vegetable fried rice, I had the tofu teriyaki dinner which came with miso soup and a small salad. The entry portion was huge so either go really hungry or be prepared to take food home. Vegetarian food is a lot harder to prepare than animal based food because there are so fewer requests for it. They did a bang up job! Everything was just perfect and a real pleasure to dine here.
Kids and husband love this place ! Best pho in Reno hands down . Love coming here . Friendly staff and always fast to bring out our food.

This is one of my best restaurants. The food was remarkably delicious, the waitress was so friendly and kind, the place is clean and neat, and the whole atmosphere a reality presentation of the Ethiopian culture. I would love to go again and again, and I wish if they had a branch in my state of living!
This place is excellent. I always get the basic Gyro which I love. My kids get the cheese pita with gyro meat and its excellent too. The service is great. Stop by, you'll be glad you did.

Nothing makes me happier than seeing GiGi and Big R's Soul Food Truck at the Mann Center for the Performing Arts. Honestly, I get excited seeing the other food trucks too, but this is the only place I've seen Gigi and Big R. This is serious soul food! Ask for a sample and see if you don't love the chicken...I normally get a platter, which includes 2 sides, for 15 bucks...when you pickup the platter you will be shocked at how much it weighs! I've had the fried chicken breast several times, and this past weekend at the Furthur concert, tried the Jerk Chicken...YUM! The jerk chicken had some serious heat. I got 2 drumsticks and the meat was just falling off the bone. It was NOT as much chicken as you get when you ordered fried...but plenty for one person... I *always* get the Mac and Cheese and Candied Yams as my sides...the yams are so sweet its practically a desert offering...and the mac and cheese is cheesy, and delicious. They have platters and "sandwiches"...the sandwich is basically the meat from the platter with 2 pieces of bread that you can use to make a sandwich...never made a sandwich, but have used the bread as a napklin in a pinch...very aborbent! If you aren't hungry for the sides, that's the way to go...the sandwiches run 10 bucks...to me its worth 5 more for the 2 sides and skipping the bread napkins... Going back to the Mann Thursday for BareNaked Ladies...I hope Gigi and Big R are there too!

I am so disappointed. I am a New Hope resident and a foodie. As such, I am always looking for new quality restaurants in the area. I especially love Cuban cuisine, and couldn't wait to try Mojitos. Well... Don't waste your time. The restaurant industry is so competitive to begin with...If a restaurant owner starts out by trying to cut corners, they'll NEVER succeed. We began by ordering drinks. Disgusting. My mojito was basically lime juice with mint, and it had an acidity flavor. My friend's margarita tasted like dirty dish water. It just got worse from there. We waited 1.5 hours for our entrees, and we were the only people there. The shrimp appetizer tasted very fishy. The guacamole had no flavor and was brown, indicative of old avocados. I can go on, but I'm sure you get the point. Basically, just another tourist restaurant in New Hope with bad food and over priced drinks, that will be closed within the next year.

First time here. Heard from a friend that it was great and it was!!! Ordered the special of the day, Clay Pot Tomato Beef with bean curd. Excellent. Very tasty. Also got the Walnut Shrimp. Incredible. Large perfectly breaded and fried shrimp in a rich, creamy sauce with crisp, candied walnuts. Our friends both had the Wor Won Ton soup which they enjoyed. Huge bowls filled with bbq pork, shrimp, won tons, vegetables and noodles. Will definitely be back!!!

A great place to go and get some caribbean food or bbq in philly. They have tons of different jerk options and a range of meat and seafood to serve anyone's palate. Also a great choice of non-alcoholic drinks including some weird green stuff and some awesome fruit punch. Bring your own rum so that you can mix it in. Nice choice of side dishes too including plantains. If you go between May and September they have an outdoor patio area in the back that has live music.

Nothing great. Another Run-of-the-mill restaurant that has nothing great to offer. The first 2 visits are good in terms of taste and quality. So i thought i found my next food destination. But, No, after couple of weeks the standards came down real quick. And last week, i ordered a onion dosa and the dosa came out snow white. I asked the waiter and he explained that since they opened an hour ago, the skillet is not hot enough, so the dosa i white. This is HEIGHTS!!! When they now, there is a problem, they shouldn't have taken orders for dosa and they shouldn't give me half baked product. The lady sitting next to me also got a snow white half baked dosa and she really got confused that she received a wrong order while she ordered Onion dosa. She was also told the same story. People don't come to restaurants to eat half baked stuff and pay $10 an item. Their Biryani is a real joke. I expected atleast this to be good as the restaurant name itself is Biryani Hut :) I'm not going again.
Wonderful little find in South Philly. The staff was very pleasant. The place was almost full on a Saturday late in the afternoon. The dishes we ordered were really good.

I'm obligated to leave a five star review because the beef bahn mi was the best I've ever had. The spicy tofu appetizer was AWESOME, and I don't even eat tofu. The waitress was attentive but not overbearing, and she was super sweet as well. The atmosphere is intimate but not too cramped. Very enjoyable experience and I will definitely be back for more!

Excellent food! I had the pad thai and it was excellent. They told us it would be a 20 minute wait (which we didn't mind) and it was actually more like 8 minutes. They turn the tables very fast and the service was excellent!
Authentic Thai cuisine, family owned and run. Dish's were fresh and very tasty. Level of spice hotness from mild to Wild!

This was such a great experience. The staff were absolutely delightful, attentive and genuine. The food was ridiculously delicious and the prices were very low for such high quality. Our experience honestly couldn't be faulted. Thank you so much

This is not a character assassination. The servers at the Jamaican Jerk Hut all seemed very lovely. But my first (and likely only) dining experience there was one of those that was tainted by the haze of mood-altering blood sugar levels from ridiculously long wait times which were compounded by loud and obnoxious clientele* that I think the management are letting ruin their establishment. In most cases any place is worth a second chance since I know there are always extenuating circumstances: their top server has mono, a shipment of Jerk seasoning is stuck on route 95, they had to physically go slaughter our dinners and the chickens were riled up from the flash mob on South St. But after reading past reviews apparently deplorable service has been the norm since they started riding the coattails of being in the film In Her Shoes. Additionally, even though the curry goat was pretty tasty two hours after I ordered it, I consider the pains I'm still having in my gut 8 hours later as punishment for not trusting my instincts and getting the hell out of there when we first arrived. The back of the house told us to check-in up front, the front told us to check-in out back, a reservation book inside had nothing written in it (funny, considering we all had a few to contribute by then.) All of this should have been a big warning sign. *In hindsight I realize that the additional charges (listed below) mentioned on page 2 of the menu were most likely created to discourage college kids from coming in to take advantage of the BYOB and 'drinking under the radar' (made obvious by the overly drunk girl who needed help both walking to the bathroom and holding her hair back.) Not only does it ruin the experience for the grown ups who can hold their liquor but it's ineffective and unnerving, especially in a place that seats at least 50 people and has only one bathroom. It's also absurd for already overpriced food, less-than-stellar service, wait times, plastic cups, etc. Then they don't even honor their own fees since the only add-on we were charged was 4 $3 corkage fees, which didn't even add up to what we actually consumed! - $12 minimum to sit on the patio, - 20% gratuity for parties of 6 or more, - $4 entertainment fee on Fri and Sat nights and a - $4 corkage fee for each bottle of wine and six pack Thank god I have generous Jamaican neighbors with a patio. I'll visit them the next time I want to eat jerk chicken and sit outside with my own alcohol.
The best thing to get here are the soup dumplings. The service is friendly and fast. I have not tried that much of the entree menu, but the couple of entrees I tried were just okay, too oily.

Ah. The ever popular Penang. It's a great inexpensive restaurant. I love the ambiance, it's a great place to take someone that's never had Malaysian food. I do have celiac and they were aware of gluten intolerance. They have one entree on the menu that is gluten free (or can be made gluten free) the Singapore noodles. Which was good. But for someone like me, I would opt to go someplace else. They do offer drinks! Wine and beer available.

Great owner great food. No complaints at all. I live on the special pho.and I order a Bahn mi and ask them to pack it for lunch tomorrow and they wrap the vegetables seperate so it stays fresh. I have tried over half the menu and the only thing I didn't like was the catfish soup.

BORICUAS UNITE. Lo mejor, this place is amazing. There is not a bad thing on the menu, all of the drinks are exceptional, and the atmosphere is great. They've got nights with live salsa music and those are my favorite. Puerto Ricans always do it best. Wepa!

Argh. I want so much to like the food in this cool little place, but it just ain't working for me. The fruit smoothies are not to thick and taste like fresh fruity goodness. The price is right too. The people who work there that I've encountered have been super-duper nice. Like really nice, not just smile for the camera nice. I somehow ended up ordering a super-size mix-it-all-up platter. It came with lots of food, and even subbed in something for something else. My problem was that the pita bread was so tough, it was almost inedible. It made it hard to scoop the other components. Left in the warmer to long. Although there was a lot of food, a large part of it was greek salad. I would have liked more hummus and tabbouleh, which were good. At $18.99, less salad and more substance. I am sure that they would be accommodating if asked.

You know how you fall in love with a person , will once you try this place you ll fall in love with it , except that every time you eat here it ll feel like your falling in love for the first time , and no I'm not exaggerating , like if your a believer then you ll get in touch with the holy spirit and if your into science stuff then you ll just understand the world and everything will make sense to you...... i just really love this place if you can't tell :)

I wanted to follow up to a previous review I posted as a result of poor service delivered to my family at the bar. The General Manager Candice reached out to me personally to discuss the situation and was empathetic to our experience. She handled it very well. We have since then eaten at Delicia and had an amazing experience. Thank you Candice! Restaurants need GMs like yourself.
Good variety of alcohol. Nice staff. PHO was over priced for the flavor wasn't the greatest. Cool setting, nice music.

Its nice to have a little variety of food choices in this areas location. I use to work in the area so a new place was a refreshing change. It may seem a little hectic at lunch but the staff are able to manage the crowd effectively. I've also come by at night and its empty so maybe a later meal would suit you if crowds are not your thing. The prices are the same as everywhere else hover around $10 or so. There is a large selection of food. the food tasted average to me but a co-worker of mine loved it and was nearly there daily. Would I be back? Meh maybe. I've changed jobs so location is an issue for sure. I would recommend a lunch meal even though it can get busy at times.

This place is pretty casual and quaint. The prices are quite good for what you get. They seemed a little understaffed maybe. They offer a lot of good options and I asked the staff which one between the curry and the chicken chili paste and he recommended the chicken chili paste. It only took a few minutes (5-10) for the food to come out. We also got a crab Rangoon appetizer. The crab Rangoon kind of had a strange taste to it, not sure what it was but I didn't care for it much and didn't finish my other 2 pieces. The chicken on the other hand was fantastic -a large portion and it was delicious. Not too spicy with plenty of rice to go with it. Would definitely recommend this place in the future for good eats

I wanted to try Vietnamese for a while so i tried pho at pho le and did not like it then i was told by a friend to retry pho here and it was great didnt disapoint glad i didnt give up on my quest for vietnamese food!

I really love this spot, if you can overlook the poor service. The pho and pork bahn mi are cheap and so, so good. I haven't had better elsewhere, and that's saying quite a bit. Get the beef pho and avoid the others. Runs about $5 for a bowl of pho and $2-3 for the bahn mi. Also - cash only!!

Starving and cranky after a workout, stumbled into this place because the rum bar was too packed and the hostess was annoying. So glad I did! The food was so freakin' good! I got a kifta hummus bowl- meatballs, hummus, cucumbers onions red cabbage pickles garlic sauce and a side of pita. It was refreshing, filling, fun to eat, flavorful and absolutely perfect. The staff were friendly, efficient, funny and pretty great. Only thing I would like to see differently in a perfect world would be better lighting and decor - it was too bright, put those fixtures on dimmers dudes! And hang some stuff on the wall, even the paper in the shwarma basket had a cool camel on it, throw that on the wall, dim the lights from full blast around dinner and you'll be the best spot in the new town center behemoth! will definitely return, that food is binge and crave worthy!

My coworkers and I came here while on a trip to Nashville and we really enjoyed the food. It wasn't in the walkable downtown area so we ended up taking an Uber. The food was really good, and we had a variety of options since we decided to share most of the plates. The appetizers were small, as expected. We ordered the corn, turnips, eggplant, and Caesar salad. I typically don't eat eggplant; however, it was amazing! The corn was also very tasteful. For main dishes we also order the grouper, avocado salad, the quail, and the carrots. I also really enjoyed the carrots. The quail was tasty even though I'm not a fan of quail and kind of spicy. For dessert we ordered tres leches, and the chocolate ice cream dish, which was rich. Overall, great dining experience, and I would go back to visit!
Delicious but pricey. Service requires improvement especially if the restaurant is not busy. I would try their lunch buffet sometime.

Zeko's is the best place to get a gyro or shawarma in the USF area! For less than $10, you can get both your entree and fries (or a drink). The inside is fine, not very comfortable but that's not a big deal. It's located near Busch Gardens so it's probably pretty convenient for people staying at the hotels over there. I definitely will go back here again!
The food is very good. The serves very good. Portion kind of small. Spicy sauce is very good. In a word, it is a good place to have Indian good.

Captain crunch burrito!! Veggie burger!! And Thai tea!! You cannot go wrong with those items. For 6 bucks, you get a burrito stuffed with fish, veggies, avocados, and some special spicy sauce.. amazing! My husband goes there whenever he Is working in the city and he makes sure he orders an extra one for me. It's a wait, but it's definitely worth it.

Our first time here. Took the server a while to seat us & get drinks but other than that the service was great. The food was pretty good too however for the price I do think was a little pricey. The parking in the back was provided but when we were leaving there was a green Jeep blocking our car in the parking lot, so be careful parking there ! Would come again.

Service was quick and very attentive. Never was my beverage glass empty. Food was very good. My dish was spicy. It was a moderate level spicy dish and it was hot like I like it. So be careful on the spice level of what you order if this is not your thing. If you're looking for lunch the combination specials are the way to go. Soup or salad and a main dish with a roll and deep fried shrimp. I would recommend the soup. It was a coconut chicken soup with mushrooms. Very good.

FABULOUS!! My husband I visited for Sunday lunch and it was packed. We only had to wait a couple of mins for a table. We each enjoyed the Pho, the child's portion was perfect for me, and we shared a Pancake, a pot of tea, and one Coconut (frozen) Bubble Tea all for less than $20. The food is delicious! and what a value!

My fav Vietnamese deli in Pinellas. Excellent Bahn MI (tofu of course) and chicken vermicelli. Awesome selection of Boba tea (ginger is my favorite but the avocado-coconut is also wonderful ). Only minor complaint is the spotty WiFi (works maybe once of every five visits) and could use a better Pho selection, but the food they do have is great and service is good.

OMG this place is the shit. Like it's not only easily the best Caribbean/Jamaican food I've ever had, but some of the best food in general I've ever had. Incredibly flavorful, spicy but won't melt your eye out, huge portion for 10 bucks. Jerk chicken, white rice with some bean gravy, Mac and cheese. 10 bucks for 2 pounds of heaven. Come here

I always come here and I'm extremely disappointed with the way everything is. I been waiting for my food for about 45 minutes they said they had no chicken. They never told us they didn't have any ready. We went to ask and they told us 15 minutes it's been 45 minutes and they still haven't bought our food out. Everything seems very dirty, I will definitely notify the county so that they can come check this restaurant. I'm definetely not coming back here anymore. Horrible service.

Delicious pad thai and good service. You would not expect this unique and serene atmosphere from the typical shopping center store front. I would definitely recommend the spring rolls, they basically melt in your mouth. We got the sampler appetizer, which was not very big but it's enough to give you a little taste for two. The woodworking is beautiful. We will go back.
Everything here tastes fresh. It may not be 100% authentic compared to those found overseas, but it's a solid 98% in my book.
After living Thailand for 3+ years...... I have found a great place to get my Thai fix!!! Arroy Mac!!

Surrounded by a sea of bad national chain food, these guys offer a welcome alternative. Flavorful and crafted food. Get off the hwy or the couch and give this a try. Veggie options. Good portions. Given the zip code, this is a welcome find.

I almost didn't want to leave a review since friends of friends own it and naturally, I don't want to be a black sheep for being honest... however. A lot of reviewers stated the same thing, 'welcome to SOBE'. That is how the lounge is laid out and the vibe it gives off. I'll give them credit. For the size of the location, the way the inside/outisde part of the bar is situated and the fact you can sit outside, they did a good job. I wont say I disliked the experience, but for how much you pay, it definitely was lacking. True that there are some odd menu items and a selection that some foodies would appreciate, but it seemed they were all over the place. Italian. Seafood. Steak. Asian. What was disappointing was that there were very limited selections in each group. If you wanted a steak, you had one option. That option did come with sides, but it was still more expensive and more lackluster than the equivalent at Ruths Chris. I realize I am comparing a 'lounge' to a 5 star restaurant, but if you are going to charge 5 star prices, then expect the same as far as critics are concerned. Wait staff was friendly. The attention they pay you is commensurate with the # of people at your table and how much it seems you are spending. Bigger tables, get 4 times the 'how are things' than if you are just two people enjoying an evening in DTSP. I get it - bigger spenders, more tips, etc... but don't judge a book by its cover. Would I go back? Not proactively. If I did, I would probably eat before hand and just have some drinks. 3 stars for both food/atmospher.

I normally avoid Chinese food. I tried this place on a friend's recommendation and it is great! Everything is fresh and loads of veggies. The chicken is always juicy and tender and tofu dishes have been tasty! Kid approved!

I was craving Chinese the other night and this seemed like one of the only Chinese restaurants that delivered to my area. I ordered the Kung Pao Chicken, which is supposed to be spicy. It was chicken but it had a fishy taste. I had to make my own dinner at home, which is what I was trying to avoid...

Order: Roti Canai, Chicken Satay, Curry Mee Price: $29 Pros: Hands down the best Roti and Satay I've ever eaten, Cons: The food was exceptionally spicy (I loved it so not a negative, just fair warning) Thoughts: As our final meal for the day we settled on Penang mostly due to the amazing reviews for Roti which we both love. It also got phenomenal reviews for almost everything else. Apparently we got pretty lucky because when we showed up the restaurant was mostly empty and, based on reviews, the place can get very busy at times. The interior design was very interesting; some of the tables were small round steel tables that almost looked like a wok with a metal disk as a lid. Overall it looked very much like a Chinese market, and led to a unique overall décor choice. I've seen it done in a similar way several times but this was the first one that did it effectively. Once we sat down and got our customary tea we put in our order we were surprised how quickly the food came out. We were unsurprised but delighted that both the roti and satay were delicious. The roti was thin but not too crunchy and the spicy peanut sauce was just mouth wateringly perfect, just the right level of spicy with plenty of flavor. The satay was perfect as well, crisp exterior with moist interior, tons of flavor cooked into the chicken, and the perfect sauce to accompany the chicken. We both loved the appetizers and would have easily eaten two of three of them. Once we polished off the appetizers we moved onto the main course. Once we dug in, we confirmed my suspicion that my wife basically just doesn't like traditional Chinese food. The Curry Mee was honestly good, if exceptionally spicy, but neither of us liked it. I don't want to talk too much about it because I don't believe it was the quality of the food that caused us to not like it, it was just the type of food and I really don't want to knock a place because I don't like their type of food. We absolutely loved the roti and satay, and I would go out of my way to eat here again. I'd probably try some other dishes as well and if you already know you like authentic Chinese then you should make sure to stop in,

This is tied (with Sabrina's and Pico de Gallo and Le Bus' sandwiches) for my favorite food in Philly. As in, I have my birthdays here so I can eat all their desserts at once with a valid excuse. So food: I started off ordering whatever sounded funny to say out loud. La Na -- amazing dish, even better cold the next day! All their egg noodle dishes are especially delicious, though it's hard to outshine their Penang curry. Also, appetizers, wow. So fresh -- the veggies the sauces! And then...dessert. Best mango sticky rice ever. Best rice pudding. Chocolate banana spring rolls. Truly fantastic. (Also BYOB, with no corking fees!) The spot itself is a bit out of the way for me, but there's a lot nearby, and it's not so bad a walk from CC in the end. Inside, it's cute, quaint and often packed, especially on weekends -- and they don't take reservations for parties fewer than 6. Final warning: cash only.
Great pho. Definitely add the chili sauce they have at the table. The Kobe short ribs rocked, but they pulled them from the menu. :( Great personalities!

If you've been to Marrakesh once, it's enough. Twice is too many. Reasons to go: 1. Fun dining experience, especially for groups. 2. Price is right. Many courses for $25. BYOB. 3. The spicy chicken is didic. As in ridiculously tasty. 4. They're very accommodating to vegetarians. 5. They're very accommodating to food allergies. Reasons not to: 1. If there was a fire in the building, everyone would die. 2. If you're claustrophobic, you won't be comfortable here. Three floors, low ceilings, small spaces. 3. If you're germaphobic, you won't be comfortable here. I asked for a serving utensil for our (whole) chicken and they wouldn't give me one. Hands only. 4. The pita leaves much to be desired. It ain't fresh. 5. One of the courses is a bowl of fruit. Like an unpeeled banana and a bunch of grapes. I would hate to see what this place looks like with the lights on.

I absolutely LOVE Kanella. I've only been for brunch but everything from the food to the coffee is perfect. BYOB saves me a TON of money on $12 Bloody Marys and $8 mimosas. The Cyprus Breakfast is a perfect combination of flavors! I wouldn't recommend their falafel or grape leaves. The falafel is really dense and the grape leaves are very sweet. But they do have really yummy Tzatziki! My favorite server is definitely Bill. What a sweetheart!!
Got my food to go through grub hub, no problems and food was made quickly. They have a whole lot of vegetarian options, very delicious, fresh, and filling

Taste of India is really, really good food. Like, really. The girlfriend says to give it a five because she loves it that much, but I'm waiting till I actually go to Punjab and try that myself. THEN we can come back and start assigning five stars. But for the $$, you seriously can't beat it. This is a awesomely good place to go if you're vegetarian/vegan. There are more veggie dishes than meat, and I'm all right with that! Service is always friendly and informative, music is nice, and according to the gf, "KEVIN IS THE BOMBDIGGY!" I actually liked him a lot, too. One of the better servers I've encountered. It's hard to find a white boy who knows his Indian food, and he does. Note: If you like hothot food, be sure to request it as superhot. They'll take care of you. Don't be afraid to sweat and let your nose run. Get an appetizer, some naan, some beer, an entree and a dessert. You wont, I PROMISE YOU, be disappointed. Oh yeah, and they're open till 11 most days, so you can wander in hungry and half drunk, and leave happy and less drunk.. or more so, whichever you like :)

If you're in the mood for some delicious sandwiches in UCity, Bui's is the way to go! After having heard so many good things about this food truck, I finally gave it a try. Since then, I have continued to come back almost every week! Bui's has cheap, great sandwiches AND they are prepared in a super fast manner. My favorite is the hangover special, a very popular choice among other customers as well. It's filled with a sausage patty, bacon, eggs, and their special Bui's sauce. The Bui's sauce is most likely a combination of Siracha and mayo sauce, but the way they make it has a tasty kick to it! It's a delicious addition to all their sandwiches! The owners are Vietnamese and friendly! You also have the option to call ahead and make a phone order for pick up. I've also called and asked them what their hours are and it actually closes around 2:30-3p. Bui's is perfect for a breakfast or lunch sandwich!

My stomach could not be happier. After a difficult choice of three different other pho locations, my friends and I decided to come to Pho An Hoa because of the previous yelp reviews we've seen. Coming from California, it's been hard to find authentic Asian food in the Tampa Area. Pho An Hoa is an authentic hole-in-the-wall that I would whole-heartedly recommend. The pho was delicious. The soup itself was very flavorful and was perfectly complimented with a large potion of meat. If you stop by, I would definitely recommend getting the large portion as I was still craving for more after I finished my bowl. This place is a budget-friendly location, for all you young-professionals and college students. Will definitely be back soon!
Pad tai is fabulous and the sushi is great. Huge portions and the friendlyest people ever.

Placed an order with them via this app with grub hub and this is the second time they failed to include the rice with the meal. I mean its thai food all I got was the eggplant with no rice. I think I will have to find another thai food place to get my food from. I heard the new spot downtown by the mx movie theatre is good.

Service, what service! He didn't even get my order right The food was tasteless and I'm 5'6 110 pounds, after a whole bowl of noodles I was still hungry! Their bubble tea was the worst! No customer service what so ever, if it was busy I can understand, but the restaurant was empty when we went! Never going back!! Not authentic at all!!

Best in the city. And by that I mean most authentic, most down to earth, least hyped, most flavorful, and well worth the trip to the East side. Make sure you try the jerky, papaya salad, and pork sausage! You know what else rocks? Phan's Kitchen! My top favorites of the night were her 10 chili papaya salad and that fantastic pork sausage! The sausage that Phan makes in-house has such a great crispy exterior to it, and a lovely flavorful interior. Like the best bratwurst you'll ever have, the skin gets a great char while the filling is lovely and juicy. That papaya salad ! Woo! Prepare yourself for a trip to flavor town! (Am I becoming Guy Fieri?) The way Phan crafts her papaya salad is unlike anything I've had before, and can only be described as authentic. Tangy, garlicky, and even vegetarian upon request, it's the best I've had in the city! The hand-shredded papaya is carefully hand-pounded in a mortar and pestle until the herbs and sauce ingredients are fully incorporated and the papaya is perfectly tender. I love it!
One of my favorite food trucks in St. Louis. The ingredients always seem fresh, and the gyros are always good.

I looove Thai food best of all, so of course I was excited to check this place out and try some delicious noodles. Boy was I disappointed! The pad thai was flavorless and overcooked, the Drunken Noodles were flavorless and overcooked, and the dumplings were flavorless and overcooked-- they were literally gloppy in texture and fell apart. Gross. Oh, and I forgot to mention-- overpriced. For yummy Thai food in the area, check out La Na down the street-- delicious!

Went for lunch on a Monday. Small place with a pleasant ambiance. A smattering of 3 or 4 other couples. The hostess/waitress was extremely friendly and was attentive enough. They have a very affordable lunch special where you get a soup or salad plus an entree for $9. (From the menu it appeared that entrees at dinner are around $12-$14ish without the appetizer.) I tried the Tom Yum hot and sour soup with chicken. Served hot on spice and temperature and very flavorful. For my entree I had the Phad Kae Mao spicy noodles with chicken Not the most flavorful dish ever and not quite as spicy as I hoped but it was still tasty and a hearty portion. Overall a fine experience and probably about 3.5 stars, though I'll give them the round up due to the friendly service. I would return to try other things, especially for the affordable lunch special.
Not bad, its a chain apparently. I had stay, the pancake stuff, and flat noodles i think. they were pretty good.

This place was busy but they managed to give us a table for two right away. We order a Yellow Curry special and Spicy noodles. The Chicken Tom Ka soup that came with our special was one of the best I ever tasted. Next time I will get the large pot of Tom ka soup. Everything we ate was delicious, the spices in every dish made them all uniquely tasty. Not a fancy restaurant but a great place to eat with family after a day at the beach.

We stopped in on 11/16/15 for a late dinner. My boyfriend ordered a beer and we both ordered their Angry Chicken- HOT and I went w/ the steamed rice and he added fried for $2.00. I took the leftovers home and enjoyed them today. The food is good and the hot wasn't overwhelming at all so I highly recommend going that route. The only thing I didn't like is that they don't have brown rice. The bathroom floor was sticky and overall, it was gross. The service wasn't overly friendly but not rude.

By far the best restaurant in treasure island. Great service and amazing food every time I come here. Presentation outstanding. Had lobster bites tonight and I am blown away. Best meal I have had and Allison was amazing. Highly recommend. Do yourself a favor and visit. After meal we went to sweets and treats just around the corner and had the best ice cream I have ever tasted

Don't let the appearance or location of this place fool you. Their Pho is amazing. I always order the Pho Thai, as it is perfection. Someday I will venture onto the bun no hue, as that is supposedly their specialty, but until then I am perfectly happy with my simple bowl of flavourful broth and good quality meat and sprouts. The restaurant itself could use some sprucing up, but that won't stop me from satisfying my pho cravings there on a regular basis.
Very unique/classy atmosphere. It's a tad expensive, bit the food is on par with the price. One of my favorite places in Broad Ripple.
Horrible service! All my friends were finished eating before I received my food. my chicken wasn't fully cooked and the rice tasted like cardboard. Will not be going back.

I get Mint at LEAST once a week, and they always have my pickup order ready within 15 minutes. Even when I was running late one time, they stayed after closing with my food warm and my drink in the fridge for me. The food is great and affordable, and the customer service is top notch. 10/10 would recommend to a friend
This seems like the unattractive sibling of Elaia. I tried several small plates. The flavors are good and chef is definitely experimenting but it doesn't leave its mark.

My new favorite place for pho. The other food here is good, e.g. tacos and the buns. The pho they make pretty well and I judge based on the broth and the proportions of the ingredients. They don't overdo the amount of noodle in the soup as well. The meat is fresh and I found that only a very little amount hoisin or sriracha sauce is needed, which keeps the simple flavor of the soup true throughout. Also, Mint has a very modern look and feel, as they self-titled. The combination pho is my favorite.

Ordered a Gyro and a Mini Greek Chopped Salad, It was all very good! They offered a sample of the potato salad and it was really good, that's what helped me to order a salad. They Gyro was good and fresh the meet tasted good and wasn't tried out. Everything is made to order, where the food is prepared is up front, you can watch your food being made, and the prep area/kitchen is very clean. All the guys that work there are helpful. I recommend this place if you want Greek food that's fast, fresh, and reasonably priced!! Also if your a vegetarian or gluten free they have options for you!!

Just left after celebrating my Grandma's 89th birthday dinner. We were a party of 17 with 5 small kids. Our server could not have been better and it felt like she was pArt of our party. In addition our food all came out cooked perfectly and in a timely manner. On top of that everything was completely delicious!! I never knew I could have Sea Bass this fresh and delicious in the middle of the country. All in all just a fantastic experience with top notch service.
Chicken Tish Kawook was delish! Full of flavor!!!!
LOVED this place. From the Mediterranean sampler to the Chicken and Lamb Tangine, the Morroccan coffeeAND the baklava. The flavors were just heaven! It's BYOB too. Service was great, too!
This was a wonderful place to have breakfast!! Really yummy food. We had the French toast. So good!!! And the people there at really nice and friendly!! Such a wonderful place!!!
Great little find - we ordered everything that was veggie-vegan and were really happy with it.

Was ok. Not terrible; not bad. But ok. It's a dingy hole in the wall that certainly isn't focused on decor or tidiness but the owner who served us was pleasant and prompt. If you're at this stripmall and hungry NOW, don't hesitate. But if you've got time to shop around and looking for something extra to your dining experience I think I'd go somewhere else.

We stopped in here after our initial lunch idea didn't go as planned. My wife and I both like Mediterranean food so we figured it was a good option. We ordered the Hummus which was very good to start with. I opted for the Caesar Salad with Shrimp and my wife went with the Grilled Lamb Gyro. My salad was quite good. The shrimp was cooked well and the spices were unique. My wife felt that the lamb was too tough and it may have been because it was sliced in a different way. Most often, with traditional gyros, you will see the meat on a rotating spit and it is then thinly sliced off. This was just thicker and it didn't work. I thought it was cool that they made a point of having shaved, chewable ice in their drinks.

This truly turned out to be a gem!.. just landed without much hope as there is barely any good indian food joint around here. But to our surprise food was nothing short of fantastic. Generous portions and spice levels true to the definition. They definitely need people to come give it a shot. We will definitely be back.. ordered kadhai chicken , jalfrezi paneer , sukka chicken and butter chicken for kids .. everything tasted plain awesome and totally different flavors of every single dish. Naans were perfect.. garlic and onion naans we ordered were satisfying..highly recommend folks to give it a try.if they maintain the quality and flavor we will be regulars here ..servers also deserve a mention.. dinner truly enjoyed.

One of my favorite Thai places in Philly. Mostly I go there because it's close to where I live, and the staff is really adorable -- they really care about their customers! I'm a big fan of their noodle dishes, the crab appetizer, and the duck fried rice. Their soups aren't my favorite, unfortunately, and I wouldn't recommend getting take-out/delivery, because it often arrives in a sub-par state. The fact that their BYO makes it a great place to go with a group!
Amazingly tasty Bahn Mi. The bread is really good french bread, the fixins are tasty, and the pork in the #1 sandwich rocks. All for $3.50. The fresh spring roll was also really good.
Love this place! No complaints. I tried the veggie spring rolls and loved their peanut sauce. Then I tried the grilled pork with noodles, also really yummy. And it's reasonably priced!
Stopped in for a quick dinner on my way to the hotel. I spotted this place when passing by and just figured I would give it a try. The food was fresh and plentiful. I will return.
Had the chicken gyro - superb......friendly staff, casual environment. The homemade baklava was the best I've ever had. We also tried the sampler platter - especially enjoyed the spanakopita.

It seems that this place switched mostly to a common lunch and dinner menu where you pick one item from three categories. While that simplifies the choices and standardizes the prices, that also takes away from what use to be a pretty good menu. Also, if you swap to this method, you better make darn sure the limited items you're serving are good. The food seems like a huge downgrade from the last time I stopped by, which is really disappointing...

So, I got the Thai BBQ chicken. All it was was fried chicken with a sweet and sour sauce on the side. Do not get it. When I wrote a review back to the restaurant they made it almost accusingly to me. They didn't really care what I had to say. I won't ever get that meal again. Might not even go back again. But!! The crispy chicken pad Thai. Yummy. The Thai tea... Yummy. I guess you win some and you lose some. I am putting an update on my review. This restaurant cares enough about its customers that upon seeing this less than satisfied review sent me an email and apologized. It wasn't needed but it was greatly appreciated. I will def eat there again. Just not get that specific meal.
Selection of lassi here are great! Definitely recommend the fig.
This place was great. The food was delicious and it is a fun place. I thought it was pricey for a byob. Still, I highly recommend it.

1) Unprofessional: The first thing that I had a problem with when visiting this location, is the fact that the servers are not required to wear uniform. 4/5 of the servers were wearing quite immodest clothes. I.e. tank tops, shorts. 2) Poor customer service: My server in particular was nice all around but lacked major customer satisfaction skills. I ordered the spicy chicken wrap and it wasn't terrible but also wasn't as good as I expected. My mom got the grilled chicken combo platter and her chicken was cold immediately after she got it and when she mentioned that to our server, she smiled and said "aw I'm sorry" WHAT!? She didn't even make an effort or offer my mom another item. And to top it off, the vegetables were stale. I would not recommend eating here and will not be returning.

Great Thai restaurant for the area. Phoenixville, as far as culinary adventures go, is definitely up and coming. The food here is always good - ingredients are fresh and they even have some very spicy dishes for you risk takers. Items I would recommend are the cucumber salad, any of their curry dishes and their pad woo sen. The only reason the Thai Place did not receive 5 stars is because they are closed on Mondays.

Service was friendly. I would ask the servers what they think about the different specials, since our waiter gave us an honest opinion, I followed his suggestion, and didn't regret it one bit. I can now say I ate a Partidge, and loved it. No 70's TV family bands were hurt in the act either. A+ place.

Came in for lunch with my husband, he works at Jefferson which gets him a 10% discount which was a plus! We got the pastrami dumplings for an appetizer, they were very fresh and tasty almost like a Reuben in a dumpling. For lunch I had the miso ramen, noodles were the perfect texture broth was flavorful and the pork was amazing. My husband had the steam yakisoba which he really enjoyed. Beer selection is lacking but okay, two beers on tap. We will definitely be back!

Food is good, not GREAT. We ordered the lamb, which cost $15. We expected a plate of food. Instead, we paid $15 for a tray 3/4 full of French fries and two slices of lamb. No salad, nothing else. In total we spent $40 on two dishes and a salad. We were just looking for some quick Greek food, honestly like what you would find in a food court, and this is not the place for it.

Wow!! This place is amazing!! I first heard about this restaurant at a yell event and had a taste of their guacamole! Had to then yelp them and check them out. Everything posted on their page looked amazing. Walked into this place about 15 mins prior to the kitchen closing, we had no idea. Saw that they were open until 11, however, the waiter was very kind and informed us we had until 10 to order. Service was particular! For appetizer I tried their ceviche with fish shrimp and octopus. That dish was delicious! Lots of flavor and the chips were a perfect vessel. I ordered the Brazilian Moqueca for my entree and every bite of this dish was amazing. It's a shrimp dish that was covered in a coconut curry kind of sauce with a scoop of rice. This dish is definitely a must have! I am sure I will have it again. My friend ordered the fish tacos and of course I had a bite. The fish was lightly under salted, but overall, the dish was fantastic! I love this place. Restaurant is gorgeous, ambience was so elegant and chilled. Service was perfect and food was amazing!!!

Solid tandoori chicken but it is a bit on the dry side. An order is comprised of 2 drumsticks and 2 thighs. The roti is very chewy and a bit tough, so stick with the naan. They also use quite a bit of butter, as well.

The best late night snack/meal ever. This would be the perfect drunchies (drunk munchies). Please come to California!!! My family and I were jet lagged and wanted dinner really late. This place was one of the only places open and I love Mediterranean so of course this is what we picked. I am so glad we did! This place is super inexpensive for the amount of food you get. I ordered the gyro pita and it was huge! They put so much gyro meat in it and it's just perfection. My brother also ordered a side of hummus and man that was good too. Loved the flavored of the hummus and the warm pita bread that came with it. I also ordered fries which I could've gone without because they just tasted like regular frozen fries you buy at the store. Can't wait to come back to Tampa to have this again!

Thai Legacy is amazing. Tom yum soup with coconut was incredible( watch out for the red peppers!) Pad Thai was great with a lot of chicken and a large portion. Yellow curry was the best we have ever had! Great service and reasonably priced. I can't wait to go back!

Olio: "a miscellaneous collection of things" Which is definitely a great description of the food and fun decor. I wouldn't have even known it was a garage until I read Christy A's review. Olio definitely did a great job renovating the space to make it feel warm and welcoming. I really enjoyed the abundance of natural light beaming in from the large front windows and garage door. There is a cute patio area outside, but when I visited it was way too cold to be sitting outside. Now ordering was a bit tricky as I didn't really know how large each of the dishes were. I actually found it a little confusing so I had to ask our server. We ended up ordering the following: "Famous" Egg Salad - I would recommend one per person. These aren't big at all, but are they tasty! They are known for their egg salad hence the "Famous" part in the name. I am not an egg salad person, but this was my favorite dish of our meal. Hummus "Deluxe" - This is a ring of hummus with braised lamb in the middle. Our server told us that this was one of their more popular dishes, but I actually wasn't that impressed. Don't get me wrong, it was good hummus and good braised lamb, but if it's one of their most popular dishes I would've expected a little more. This dish is quite large. It can easily be shared between 4 people. Oh and this comes with pita and bread. Roasted Cauliflower - I always really enjoy roasted cauliflower, and this wasn't an exception. The cauliflower is roasted so it's on the softer side, but I like that. Some people, like my wife, prefer their cauliflower more firm. Good to share for 3. Brisket Sandwich - Really enjoyed this sandwich. The bread had a crunchy exterior and very soft interior. The brisket was very nicely cooked and seasoned. We shared this between 3 people, but you could just eat this as a meal. Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area! Though they can get quite busy during evening hours. Note: See that front door at the front of the restaurant? Yeah that's not the door, go around to the back. I bet all 1st timers make that mistake.

OMG. I got some food delivered and it was so good. Here is what I got: Vietnamese tacos. I've never had this before. Delicious "taco shell". White doughy and sweet. Grilled summer rolls. Clear sticky and crammed with those white noodles and veggies. Loved it. Chinese egg rolls---the best egg rolls I've ever had. I could only eat half of everything except I ate BOTH egg rolls.

Staff was uncourteous and refused to provide us service because we only wanted snacks and not a full meal. If it is a policy, please mention it on your menu. Walked a minute to New Delhi restaurant and had the most amazing veg platter ever.

Our favorite Westside location for Pho. Their pork vermicelli is amazing. Tasty, fresh & delicious. The owner is super nice, but can be a little "over involved" while you are trying to eat. Overall, I HIGHLY recommend.

I have eaten hear three times in the last three years, and this time was my last. The food was bland. The manager hovered over us as we were looking at menus suggesting appetizers and entrees, to the point of turning the pages himself and pointing them out. Very annoying.

I ordered takeout despite knowing from reviews it would take a while. I had to call three times for someone to pick up the phone. Once they did, they were nice, took my order, and told me my food would be ready in 20 minutes. 45 minutes later, my husband came home with what he was told was our order- my husband confirmed what we had ordered too! We ordered two soups and ended up with one completely different one and a shrimp rice platter. We still don't understand how. Despite the food roulette that we played, we ate what we were given bc I'm pregnant and we have a toddler to also feed. The food we received was tasty- no complaints despite the wait and mixup- so we are hopeful that once this place figures out a system, it will be a staple in our foodventures in Fairmount. For now we have learned our lesson and will try again perhaps in two months. We can drive to south philly, eat, and come back in the time that we waited for our wrong order today.
