Highly recommended! The choices are amazing and the prices are better!!!! Tried the chicken with fries and rice and it was the perfect combination of sweet and salty. Ample room for big parties and the staff were so friendly and helpful! Dessert selection may not be vast but they are delicious!

Restaurant was only half full at 8:40pm Saturday night when we were seated. After waiting 20 minutes (yes I timed it), no one brought us a menu or filled our water glasses, in spite of the staff waiting at tables next to us multiple times. We stood up, & put our coats on, and remained standing at the table for another 1/2 minute - NO reaction from the staff. We walked to the door, stood another 1/2 minute, and again NO reaction. It was obvious that the owner was not there, + the staff I saw was very young...... I cannot rate the food as I could even order.

I loved how they had the courtyard misted on a hot day but the menu was generic and over priced and the drinks were not that great. The food wasn't terrible just not worth the price they had on their menu. Service was nice but hard to tackle the server at the end to get our check so we could go get a real drink.
I used to live in Jamaica and this makes me miss it less. The owners are lovely. Haven't had a thing yet that wasn't amazing!!
Best Red Duck Curry I've ever had! It was so good I made an account just to write this review.

I was so excited to try this place given how much I love Thai Phooket in Nashville. I order food for take out and when I walked in I asked if it was the same as the one in Nashville. The girl behind the counter said, "yes, but it's a different owner and we have different things on our menu". I was confused since it seems like that would make it not the same. Nevertheless I was excited to try the food I had ordered. I ordered the green curry with chicken, not spicy. However it was very spicy and very little chicken. I don't plan on going back.
Food took a long time to arrive. It tasted okay, but it wasn't very authentic, and it was somewhat bland. The ambience is nice, though.

I have been going here with my family since I was a little girl and the food is consistently good. The spanakopita and saganaki are among my favorites. The Greek salad is among the best I've had and the twice baked potato is so yummy. I also really enjoy the carrot cake and the various cheesecakes they feature. If you are looking for good Greek food and good service this is the place for you. I will mention the atmosphere is mainly families and older folks. Not a super young crowd, but it's never bothered me!

Absolutely the best Thai food I've ever had! There were 7 of us for dinner, so we had the opportunity to taste many different appetizers & entrees. Each was better than the last. The owner came out to talk with us, and was extremely gracious. This is definitely on my agenda for my next trip to NOLA.

Smiling Elephant: other Thai restaurants in Nashville do it well, but Smiling E does it the best. Their pad kra pao with pork (Thai spicy) is simply delicious. Do yourself a favor and try this masterpiece ASAP. It's so perfect in its simplicity. (It's barely 9 a.m. as I'm writing this, and I'm already craving it.) You can't go wrong with playing curry of the day roulette either. I've never had a bad curry here. It comes with your choice of protein, or go veggie-only. Their veggies are so fresh and crisp. The 8th Avenue South store front is quaint and cute, and the staff here are so friendly. They strike a nice balance between homey/traditional ambience and modern/fresh plating. I usually call in for carryout, but if you're planning to dine in, either go at off peak hours or expect to wait. The dining room is on the tiny side. Enjoy!

The curry is really good and gets 5 stars, the rest is meh and gets 3. Therefore we arrive at 4 stars. I may be biased though, it's really really close to home so that may make it slightly better. Ah, on second thought, it's an overall 3 stars but if you go, get the red curry!

Living only a few blocks away, I have eaten at Pho King many many times. The food is always very good and consistent. Service is quick and friendly, and it always seems to be full of regulars. I have tried many of the vermicelli dishes, pho, spring rolls, green onion cakes, and everything is excellent. This is my go-to place for Vietnamese.

*3.5-4 Stars* My first visit was on a Saturday evening for dinner with a friend and the ambiance was quite lively and a tad bit loud. The restaurant venue is versatile with many different sized tables, so it's a great spot for anything ranging from a first date to a medium-to-large sized dinner party. It was pretty crowded around the bar, but the bartenders were quality professionals and they kept the service coming at a steady pace. The service in general was just superb. Their cocktail list is extensive and each looks as exceptionally well made as the next. The beer selection is not extensive at all, it has everything you would expect from a Latin American restaurant and that's about it. The food and menu itself in my opinion is more of a Latin American-New American fusion than just a straight up Latin American offering. We ordered a chip+guacamole appetizer for starters and for my entrée I had the enchiladas de pato (duck). Overall I would give the meal a 3-star rating. The guacamole was really solid, but not the best I've ever had. The enchiladas were good and I was quite satisfied with the meal, but I've had better for cheaper. I will probably try something different the next time I go. Bottom line: Delicia is probably best for apps and drinks with friends or a first date venue on a weekday night. Though I would definitely recommend giving Delicia a thorough 3-course meal try if it is your first time.

Dinner here last night was amazing. This restaurant is definitely considered fine dining. We celebrated a birthday, and we had great service. Allison, our waitress was very hospitable. She was a great help when it came to recommending dishes, and was super funny. For appetizers, we ordered the escargot and fried artichokes. Omg, both dishes were delectable! I have not had escargot in years, and they were so yummy. Once you get past the whole idea that you're consuming a snail, you will see it is quite delicious. The texture is similar to eating a mushroom. They were served in a garlic oil sauce and sprinkled cheese on top that was divine for dipping your bread in. The fried artichoke came with a spicy chipotle mayo drizzled over it that was so yummy. For entrees we ordered chilean sea bass, monk fish, seafood crepes, and lamb shank. Everyone loved their meals! We were also served string beans and rice. My seafood crepe was filled with crab, scallops, and shrimp. I loved it. I never tried monk fish before, and I tried some of hubbys. It was very good and had a very different texture then typical white fish does. I also learned it is known as the "poor man's lobster". It was very good. Dessert entailed a berry profiterole with ice cream that everyone shared. This restaurant was beautifully decorated, service was great, and I highly recommend trying this place out if in the Treasure Island area.

This was a really good place to go for lunch. They were very fast in serving the food and you can order online in case you want the food to be ready when you get there. Seems clean and staff is friendly. It is a new place so hopefully service stays the same way.

Came here on a Friday. Cute decor and music. Service was great. Food was okay. I got the green curry and my boyfriend got the pad see ew. The green curry's sauce was a little to watery and the veggies and chicken were okay. Nothing to rave about. Boyfriend enjoyed the pad see ew. Too many noodles for me and no veggies. Overall okay!

Series of unfortunate events occurred during our visit to this establishment. I read from previous reviews that the spicy shrimp pho was phenomenal. When seated, we noticed that table next to us was delivered the a piping hot bowl of spicy shrimp pho, but in error. In spite of the fact that the beautiful bowl of spicy shrimp pho was sent back to the kitchen, I elected to order the same item believing that they would NEVER present another patron with the same bowl of rejected pho, especially since we ordered multiple appetizers and took some time eating the tasty spicy tofu appetizer and mediocre fresh rolls. When my bowl of much anticipated spicy shrimp pho was set before me, I noticed that my bowl of pho was not piping hot and the noodles were soggy and mushy. I didn't want to be a bother so i asked them for more broth with the hope that it would heat up the soup. They took the bowl into the kitchen and brought it back as it was returned. Frustrated, I asked the waiter to heat up the bowl because it was lukewarm. After some time I was presented with a bowl of pho our waiter stated was made anew for me. I was dismayed to realize that the "new" bowl was the same one I sent back since it had the torn basil leaves I had put into it! I should have walked out, but requested replacement with pho tai. After all that, the broth was sickeningly sweet and definitely NOT WORTH ALL THE TROUBLE!!! I will never return!
Delicious food and friendly owners but the place was significantly run down. Not comfortable and the atmosphere was bland. I would go back! Just don't have a first date there!

Looking for great and healthy food - perhaps to quench the obligatory late night snack? Vibe, no....but not needed QuIck, Yes Healthy food, Yes as long as you minimize the sauce Taste, great...i had the chicken breast souvlaki wrap, with diced tomatoes, onions and a heap of green olives. Portion size, not too much, which is good because you'll probably eat anything put in front of after a few pints! Price, reasonable
Vientiane is always reliably good. My favorites are the pad kee mao and the eggplant sweet basil.
Superb gyro deluxe. Great place to grab a lunch on the go. Prices are right, and service was fine. This place will not disappoint..

The lunch buffet was amazing! Definitely the best Indian buffet I have been to in the Indianapolis area. They had plenty of vegetarian options and everything tasted great. I had only had carry out from here before which had never disappointed. Glad I was finally able to make it to the buffet. Naan was perfectly cooked, definitely recommend the garlic naan.

My wife and I went here for an impromptu date night and it did not disappoint. Duck enchiladas -perfect execution with black beans. Wife had pork belly and Scallops. If I had to give a negative I would say server was aloof and tables were WAY too tight together. Besides the noise congestion the food was terrific!
Awesome Philly cheese steak sandwich. This place is a hidden treasure, the food is delicious.

Ordered take out and wish we had ate in the quaint little restaurant. The food when we arrived for pickup was placed in heat saving bags. The bags included extra hot sauce and peppers. Everything was cooked to order and was some of the best Thai food I've ever had. The authentic green bean noodles were so excellent, we didn't miss the typical rice noodles. The heat on the ground pork and chicken penang curry were also fantastic. Next time in Nashville, I plan to stop in again.

I had lamb biryani and it was not a biryani. In stead it was fried rice with some lamb chunks. I could see that the rice was Jasmine or even lower quality rice unlike in other Indian restaurants where they use quality basmati rice. Biryani did not have any biryani masala or smell. The rice was fried with cumin seeds. It was pre cooked like long time ago and they microwave in front of me instead of heating up in the cooking pan. The lamb pieces were so dry and over microwaved multiple times. Overall I was given some random foods. Certainly not biryani.

This place is busy. The price went up since the last time I came here. It's still the best place so far around Wayne area. The buffet selection is great, they have the mango lassi and chai tea included. A good selection of desserts as well.

While the food at Soco Gyro is very good, while dinning there today I witnessed the worst costumer service and poor ownership I have ever seen. The owner and his entire staff verbally attacked and berated a fellow costumer because his son spilled something. They call this place a family restaurant but they obviously don't want you bringing your children in. The poor young father continued to apologize and the staff went on to question his parenting. When he asked for his money back so he and his maybe 4 year old son could leave, they told him no. It was truly disgusting me and my family got up and left. The sad thing is the entire staff seem to think that this was ok and watched us leave. We will NOT be retuning.

Christ, this place is heaven. Between the beer and the food, I'm criminal. They have the beers only available in the most exotic of establishments. My favorite: Weihenstephaner Kristall Weissbier, which I could only get at an amazing bar in Old City in Philadelphia. The hand made noodles covered in shredded lamb and pecorino Romano the consistency of angel pubes is what was served at the last supper from what I was told. Christ said, "after this meal, I'm good! Crucify me." Come here. Eat. Drink. Be saved. Service is righteous. In fact, brotherly. Parker gets it. He knows what I'm saying. He appreciates what we appreciate. We fully sanction his righteousness. Come here. Know. See. Feel. Live. Yes.

I came to K&T because I've heard so many good things about the bahn mi sandwiches here. It's a real hole-in-the-wall that you might miss if you blink. So don't blink. The inside is in a word - nondescript. Very basic deli counter and a few dingy tables and chairs. But you come here for the food, not the decor. The basic pork banh mi was excellent. Very fresh vegetables and flavorful pork. The bread was toasted perfectly and provided just the right amount of crunch. Next time I will try their pho as staring at the pictures on the wall while waiting for my banh mi made me salivate.

I've been to Penang about five times now. The food pretty decent. The roti with chicken curry on the appetizer menu is the must try item here. There was never a dish that I hated. This place lost two stars because of how creepy the Hispanic men in the kitchen are. It's impossible to eat without them trying to make eye contact or blowing kisses. To get to the bathroom, you have to walk past them all. Three of my girlfriends and my little sisters have all felt uncomfortable eating here. I can't even get started on how much leering they do. This is my most negative review of service ever, and I'm a waitress so I'm very understanding of service workers.
Very clean place and was attended to right away. Food is good just a little to expensive but overall good place to eat.

Dining for only one should be easier. None of the entrees are served in smaller portions thus limiting my meal to just one item. As an out of towner doggy bagging is not an option when staying at a hotel without means to reheat the next day. 3 stars for service for not offering half portions, though the food was tasty and merited another star. Tuesday night, I was the only one in the restaurant, but 2-3 take out orders were picked up.

There are hardly any people at Pho 38 when I go during dinner time. The place serves decent Vietnamese food for a fair price. The wait staff is fairly attentive, and they definitely make good recommendations if you're not sure what to order. The decor is a little dated and possibly strange; however, you can't miss the mother-of-pearl one-of-a-kind inlay of Vietnam and "Pho 38" on all the tables. The dinner for two is a great value for the items offered though dessert is just oranges, and some of the courses are a little bit saltier than I prefer. Bottom line: Pho 38 is a good spot for Viet food if you're in the NJ suburbs and want to satisfy your craving. It's not the best, and it's not the fanciest, but it gets the job done.

I went for lunch on New Year's Day. We were seated right away to a quaint booth in a beautifully decorated room. The reasturant was extremely clean. The service was EXCELLENT. I started with the Tum Yum soup with tofu and it was tasty, hot and full of veggies. The Spring roll was also DELICIOUS, fresh, hot and crispy...YUM. For my main I tried something I've never had before it was the Siam with chicken. I really have nothing to compare this to but even though it was indicated as a spicy dish (I love my Thai food SPICY) it hardly had any heat in it at all. I was surprised at how sweet the dish was..I am more of a savory person so this disappointed me a little. But, the portion was spot on. The rice, chicken, and veggies cooked really well and I did finish my meal. I probably wouldn't order that dish again...not because of the dish itself or the way it was cooked but entirely due to my person taste preferences. I plan on eating here again and giving the Green Curry with Grouper a try next. I encourage you to give it a shot as well....nice place in Brandon to satisfy your Thai food craving.

Went there again tonight - and while the decor sure ain't 5 star - the food absolutely is!!! Shrimp Scampi . The world's BEST baba. Simple grilled veggies with chunks of feta. So cheap (cash only at this location) and so tasty. Killer waitresses - they attack - beware!

The Greater Reno Grub and Gripe Group gathered at Zagol for its latest Chowdown. Overall we enjoyed the food. The manner in which it is served was maybe a little off putting but we quickly overcame it. This is a restaurant that opened a couple of years ago on East Fourth Street near downtown Reno. It's in a new building in an area targeted for redevelopment by the city of Reno. I looked over the menu and found nothing I would object to so when it came to ordered I deferred to others. Robin pretty much handled the ordering and she did a good job. She made a point of ordering food that would be a contrast. She noted one previous dinner there where too much of the food seemed similar. But because Robin did the ordering I can't really tell you much about what we ordered. We had the combination dish and we got two beef dishes and three vegetable dishes. Robin also got some cottage cheese that was a nice mix with the spicier dishes. We placed our order and the food arrived a short time later. If you're not familiar with Ethiopian food it would help to look at my pictures. All five portions of food and the cottage cheese are served on a platter on a big sheet of soft bread called injera. Additionally, there is wrapped bread served in a plate. One member of our group asked, "Are there plates?" The answer is no. You take some of the bread on the side, tear off a bit and use it to pick up meat or vegetables. As the food gets mushed together eventually it's easier to pick it up together. I can't describe each individual dish, but all were good. And the cottage cheese is a nice addition, too. We didn't feel full after we finished the first so we ordered a lamb dish and it was also good. Also lots of good wine. Robin and Fred brought a nice 2010 Twisted Oak verdelho and a 2009 Dillian primitivo. I brought a 2010 Ametzoi Rubentis, a Basque rose that's a little more rounded than the 2009 I brought to the Chowdown at the Santa Fe. Service was good. Our water glasses were kept full. We didn't order anything else but the also offer Ethiopian beer and Ethiopian coffee.

I need to go back to this lovely place! I had an order of Pad Thai and it was beyond my expectation - light, fresh and delicious. Compare to more authentic Thai food I've had before, The Smiling Elephant is milder in seasoning, the menu is limited (which corresponds to the size and capacity of the restaurant anyway). Nevertheless, I love the food, service is good, and it's definitely the best Thai restaurant in Nashville.

Yummmm! This place is going to be my downfall this year. We went for a quick lunch today...I got a short rib taco and the bf got chicken katsu. Both were very, very good. My short rib was super flavorful and delicious. I probably should've gotten more than 1 taco, but I wasn't super hungry. The chicken katsu was delicious also...the chicken was perfectly cooked. Next time (which will hopefully be soon!) we will ask for extra sauce!
The Burger buns are amazing. I didn't even know you can make beef taste so good. Their dumplings are delicious. The Miso Ramen was okay. The bill does rack up.

I took my mother to mood cafe yesterday after seeing such great reviews on yelp, and we both really enjoyed our dining experience! Everything about it was a refreshing twist from the standard indian fare we are used to. We shared a chicken tikka salad chaat which was light, filling and delicious but there are so many other options that I need to explore. I've also never seen so many varieties of lassi (yogurt drink) ever. I grew up on mango lassis, but at Hassan's suggestion I ordered a rose lassi which was so good and memorable, I will definitely have to come back for more. My mother ordered a spicy mint lassi which was too spicy for me but my mother loved. Once it melted down though and it got a little less spicy, I took it away from her and downed the whole thing myself. Lastly and most importantly, the owner and his staff are wonderful to get to know and clearly appreciate their customers. Although mood cafe is a small place, it has a wonderful charm that makes it worth revisiting. I look forward to seeing some openings in NYC! (Hopefully, brooklyn :) )

I've been here two times and I love it -- the shawarma bowls are so good and the chicken is tender. The pita is pillowy and soft, the naf fries are perfection!! The whole meal + fries came out to only about 11 dollars, and I left feeling full with some to take home. The food is delicious and fresh, definitely worth a try if you're looking for vegetarian/healthy options.
I believe best food in town. best quality food excellent service my family love the india cafe

Just fantastic! The decor is pretty basic, but the wait staff was really friendly and charming. We had some great vegetable sides, the catfish (really incredible) and a slow grilled pork with rice. Will definitely be back!

Food was delicious! I got the veggie gyro- everything was fresh and portion size was good. My sister got the Greek salad and said that was the first time she's eaten every bit of a salad I her life. They serve their food as it's ready, so everyone gets it at a different time. I've never experienced that before but it didn't bother any of us. We even had a surprise belly dance show. Not awkward as belly dancing usually is at a restaurant! It was pretty cool!
We had an incredible dinner with the best waiter I have ever had in my life! His name is Ben from Minnesota! So impressed with the food and Ben's attention to our table. AMAZING!

My boyfriend and I came here by chance and we absolutely loved it. This place has great quality food. I had the chicken tikka Marsala and I think it was fantastic! I am very picky with Indian food because in the 3 Indian restaurants around my area I disliked them all. My favorite restaurant had burned down. Just found my go-to Indian Restaurant! Definitely this is a diamond in the rough!

Had the daily special with app, soup main course and drink for under $10. Food was tasty and while not as gut packing as an all-u-can-eat buffet, plenty of food for lunch. Staff was good, on my list for lunch places in Mount Juliet!

Truly amazing meal. Favorite part by far was the hamachi curry. Cocktails were excellent. Also ordered the smoked tuna tartare, conch croquettes, broiled shrimp and goat curry- the most tender meat I've had in a long time! Our server Claire was very knowledgeable and fun. Highly recommend for a special night out!

Came here with my parents a few months back and we had a great experience! My mom comes here all the time bc it has authentic, fresh southern Italian food for a good price. Love that the owner is Sicilian! U can definitely tell. Would love to bring my husband here in the future.

Blu Fig's food is so delicious that I went there 3 times last week. Their falafel is amazing. The hummus there is the creamiest I've ever had- I don't know how they do it! I always get the salmon plate with the salad and rice, the flavors are wonderful and the portions are very generous. I love how friendly the workers and owner are, it makes a huge difference when the owner is as involved as Blu Fig's is. LOVE this place!

Jasmine Thai is a Wonderful Place for Date Night. Bebe (our host) is one of the "most" pleasant individuals I have ever met. She is Spectacular. Visit Jasmine Thai ASAP, you'll be more than...Satisfied!

So a friend and I went to this Pakistani "hole -in-the-wall." Literally, feels like your eating in a supermarket aisle. The floor and walls and surrounding counter top space definitely need a good wipe down. The food however there is something to say. Choices of "American" mild, spicy and hot dishes that are bigger if you sit in and eat rather than use pick up. A friend and I noticed a man when we got there who just ordered pickup...left and about 15 mins earlier showed up since he received the wrong order from the guy behind the counter who didnt seem to be "with it," he proceeded to hand him the right order and he left. Now I don't want to sound out of place, but that food that came back should either been eaten by workers or just given to the previous customer for free and new food made. Im not a sanity freak but come on. Okay now.....I got that off my chest...Back to the food, dishes are bright colorful as well as flavorful. Setback that the starches (naan, rice) are extra for dishes that require something to rest upon as you enjoy the food. It is Halal (Middle Eastern for Kosher aka blessed). I would have to say trying new cuisine is an adventure for me both for my mind and palate.

Scannicchio's provides some of the best Italian food in the city! I have no idea what Daniel is talking about. Try the stewed figs with sausage in balsamic reduction. YUM, yum. A definite winner. It may not be as swanky as some of the Center City BYOs, but it is really quite good.

My co-workers and I enjoyed lunch here last Friday. I must have driven by the building a hundred times, but never noticed there was a restaurant inside before. We were greeted by a an older African lady who seated our large group right away. We were handed menus, but the Friday buffet was too good of a deal to pass up. She offered to walk us through the buffet to let us know what each item was, but we decided to take our chances and just try everything as a surprise. For our vegan friend, 9 items on he buffet were vegan/vegetarian friendly. I sampled a little bit of everything. The dishes were all full of spice and flavor. I particularly enjoyed the mushroom and collard dishes. We all enjoyed black coffee at the end. Who needs cream or sugar when the coffee is perfect on its own?

Stopped by here for lunch, but missed the breakfast that I heard so many good things about. There were quite a lot of choices on their daily specials, but I went with their regular steak sandwich called the Blue Plate Steak. It was delicious! Fresh chip steak meat, roasted peppers, and andruillo sausage, and covered with sharp melted provolone cheese. Personally, I would've liked to have a drizzle of some kind of sauce (marinara like) because it was a little dry. But other than that, it was filled with flavor! I also opted for the waffle fries instead of their homemade potato chips. May be the best waffle fries I've ever had! Fresh out of the oven, hand cut... Just delicious. I'm definitely coming back for breakfast, maybe even dinner...

Top notch Indian! We've had a dozen meals since we stumbled into Nirvana a week after it opened in this new location. We have never been disappointed. Everything we have tried has been excellent. We love the old stand-by Tiffin, but Nirvana is more authentic and nuanced. Tiffin has been quite anglicized...very hearty and delicious, but spices are a little too restrained. Nirvana let's it's spices loose and the result is delicious! Unqualified positive recommendation.

Simply remarkable....Although i have not tried the whole menu, what I have tried literally bursts with flavored happiness!! The red and panang curry are both taste explosions, and the chicken satee is a delicious way to start any meal!! The decor is bright and intimate simultaneously, and children are almost lulled into tranquility with the overall theme of the restaurant. So, pour up a nice cool chai tea or thai iced coffe and have a wonderful meal at this delightful place!!

This place is truly unique and awesome! When you walk up to the door, you feel like you are about to be transported to another country. You must first knock, before being allowed entrance into this enchanted middle eastern local. I suggest making reservations. Ambiance and food are amazing. A great place to bring out of town guest and to share some intimate time with your friends. All food is eaten by hand and family style. Will be back for sure!

Favorite place to get Thai in South Tampa. Cant go wrong with their pineapple curry or phad thai. They also have great soups, everything always tastes great and fresh. They are also quick at getting your order ready for pickup.

I've only been to Zorba's once, but I think about that meal all the time. It was so delicious. My friend and I shared the hummus appetizer and then I had Shrimp Tourkolimano and she had Shrimp Santorini. I don't think either of us said a word for a little while because we were so focused on enjoying the food. We had to have dessert, so we split the Revani, which was soaked in a delicious honey syrup. Of course I love that it's a BYOB. I think this would be a great spot for a date. It's small, intimate, and cute.

I find myself coming back here many times a week for their boba tea. Their milk teas with boba are very good. I generally get the vanilla milk tea with extra boba and egg custard. Very flavorful and still easy to drink with all of the extra ingredients added in. Their regular teas are also very good and I do recommend those as well. Their food is fresh and full of flavor and bite. The portions are large, the flavors are outstanding and every bite always includes a little bit of everything. The short ribs were soft and not tough whatsoever, the flavor was savory and well balanced. The meatball sandwich was a good size, very fresh with great bite from the vegetables. The meatballs were soft and perfectly seasoned. The bread for the sandwich was also fresh and very soft so the filling didn't spill out all over the plate. The spicy noodle and beef soup was a very large portion and came with the second plate of all the toppings you can add. The cabbage and bean sprouts gave it a very nice crunch and the basil added a nice touch to all of the flavors in the soup. The meatballs, once again, were soft and flavorful and the beef chunks were great as well. It's a great little spot for drinks and delicious food. The service has been good every time I've gone and the food always comes out quickly.

I came here with five friends one of whom is deathly allergic to cucumbers. We placed our initial order and asked the waitress to make sure our food did not contain cucumbers. She said that the beef normally comes with cucumbers but she would tell the kitchen to not include them. Our first round of food came without cucumbers. We then asked for an order of vegetable spring rolls. The spring rolls came on top of a bed of cucumbers so we politely reminded the waitress that our friend is deathly allergic to cucumbers. The waitress was clearly very angry and proceeded to yell at us saying we did not tell her that we did not want cucumbers. Although the food was good and the bus boys were excellent, my friends and I will never be returning. Safety should be a restaurant's top priority and customers should never be disrespected. There are many other excellent restaurants in Chinatown.

This place is a little iffy but I'm giving it four stars for a couple reasons: 1) Coconut curry noodles are GREAT. So delicious. 2) Happy hour. The $6 special happy hour cocktail is a really good deal in Philly and it's been awesome both times I've been here. Other things: My bf was not a fan of the brisket ramen. I thought it was ok, but it didn't blow my mind. Go to a real ramen place if you want real ramen. I got the sichuan spicy fat noodles another time with a friend, which were good, but the tofu in them was eh. Coconut curry noodles were much better. My friend got the special, which were dan dan noodles. Good, but such a small portion compared to my spicy noodles, it was bizarre! The wings are good, and so are the corn rangoons. Good prices on apps for happy hour too. Come during happy hour, get an app, the coconut curry noodles and the cocktail (my fav one that they had was a black currant mojito). You won't regret it.

Decent pho... would prefer lime instead of lemon and more cilantro as well but broth was tasty and cut thin. Not much for atmosphere or ambience... not a date night spot or anything to impress but more for quick lunch and go. It was empty when I went with my two sons which almost scared me away but service was quick and restaurant was clean. Outside has much to be desired but the pho is solid and that's all that matters.

Hands down the best phõ place in YEG. I do not say this lightly as I have a sample size of 10+ to compare with. The thing that stands out the most for me about Nam Kitchen is the quality and freshness of everything they serve. You will never see a wilted basil leaf here. Good service too, which is generally rare to find with Asian restaurants.

Yummy! I had the fried wontons which were the best I've ever had. I had a green papaya salad and my husband had the clay pot with pork - he ordered a 3 on a heat scale of 1 to 4. The waiter warned him - next time he'll try a 2. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal here. The host and servers were really nice and it wasn't too crowded. We love that it's BYO and we're coming back soon.
We go to this place often and the food is always outstanding. The massiman curryis the best in the city!

Excellent option from the norm. Super clean, very friendly staff. Had the falafel in a pita, very tasty and quite massive portion. The lentil soup is fantastic especially with a dollop of their hot sauce.

such a fun place for a group of people! before you read further, make sure you make reservations because this place gets busy, and based on the length of the dining experience, you might be waiting for quite a while to get a seat on a popular night. as others have said, the food is plentiful so come prepared to eat. though, i must say, the amount of food wasn't as scary as others noted in their reviews. for a group of four, we ate several bites of each dish but not so much that we tapped out after two or three courses. the highlights for me were the veggies (especially the eggplant) and the lamb. the staff were super accommodating and attentive but not overly so. they even accommodated my gluten allergy by providing me with a plate and fork (instead of the requisite pita) and modified each dish (except the dessert) with a gluten-friendly alternative. at 33usd per person for the amount of food served (and entertainment!), this is a steal. byob (with NO corkage fee) or purchase house wine per your individual preference.

Food is excellent and so is the service. We got there close to close and we're going to get carry out but the staff talked us into staying there. Wasn't sure what to get so we asked our server and they recommended our dishes. It was great!
Delicious Pad Thai. That is all. PS - Very cute location, small little dining area, and super good deal on the SB main drag. Perfect pre-bar dinner.

Let me start by saying this place was the second place my Mom and I stumbled upon trying to find some good food for the evening, myself having just gotten off a long flight. We both like trying new things and this place had so many good reviews we decided to give it a try. Superb, from the staff to the food! I had my first lassi and we both wanted chicken dishes so they gave us one salad (which has a lot to it!) and one chaat just to give us both a taste of different things. Both were splendid as well as the rice pudding we had for dessert, and I am not a pudding person :)! Our chicken we got medium spicy and it was so flavorful and just yummy!! Even the salad was bomb! When we stepped in we let them know it was our first time and they guided us thru the menu and everything. This place is a great find and we'll be back. Thoroughly enjoyed the food and would highly recommend it.

You must try two helpings of the Yedoro Wett (berbere-spiced chicken with hard-boiled egg) and lentils on injera bread. Indy is very fortunate to have this winning restaurant! Be extra daring and try the special authentic seating off to the side of the restaurant.
GREAT Food and good price. I ordered Reshmi Kabob and Daal Tarka (it came with Rice). Trying to stay away from Naan and Carbs in general. Portions were large and the Food WAS delicious.

2nd time here and it was as amazing as the first! Our group had a 30th birthday party here and they went above and beyond to ensure we have a great meal and celebration. The staff is always friendly and extremely courteous. I had the Caribbean platter with coconut bread as well as the jerk chicken wings. Highly recommended.

And the veggie pho is delicious...in case you were wondering, as is the spicy tofu appetizer. I've also tried their grilled shrimp items and YUMMY. Love that the place is so low key and that you are greeted like you've just arrived at your favorite aunt's house.

Yummy thai food with some pros and cons.. Cons: curry favored wonton wraps ..it's okay ..weak on the favors..but it was included with the lunch special Ice cream with fried banana ..they lied to me..the menu said homemade coconut ice cream..I got store brought vanilla ice cream that's been in the freezer too long ...u know u can tell when u feel/taste bits of ice in there ..my sister thought it was coconut pieces ..I sadly shook my head and said 'no it isn't' Pros: The chicken rice soup that was included with the lunch special.. The house fried rice...nicely done Duck pangang was delicious..extra crispy duck topped with that pangang sauce..hmm..yum Service & decor..awesome! .. definitely coming back when i'm around the area and craving thai..

Beautiful spot was great food. Our waiter was kind, quick and full of suggestions. The food was perfectly seasoned and plated beautifully. The proportions were just right. I left full but not overly stuffed. This is a keeper.
Had a Vietnamese roll and it was really worth the money!! Great service, really attentive but not too in your face. Great food great service- very impressed

It been like first impression back in 5 years ago,my friends took me @ pf changs and so yummy... Samething just happen now,i am order "dan dan noodle" and my girlfriend "singapore noodle" the taste so brave ...it just need more spicy...good job for PF
This place was AMAZING! Chef Nina Compton has put together some of the most tantalizing favors to ever dance across my taste buds! Hint- try the curried goat!

Order somewhere else. Too expensive and they give you a childs side of rice with your order. Not worth it when other places are a buck or two cheaper and actually give you a pint of rice with your meal.

Really, really good latin food with a modern twist. Got the stuffed pepper and the empanadas, both of which were outstanding. The outside doesn't look like much, but the inside is very cool too. We'll be back here soon.

We've just returned from our worst experience ever in a restaurant.(we are 64 and ate in countless number of restaurants in the globe) Siamese Princes used to be great in the past.In the present,I recommend to look for a better restaurant,with a decent service and food. The food was tasteless,a take away from the cheapest place,taste better.We ordered a special dish named "Love and passion",what we received was far from the description in their menu.Very far !!!!!! Instead of a stuffed chicken with all goodies ,they served a tiny chicken,size of a pigeon,bones and skin,no stuffing what so ever.I told the server,that this was not what we ordered.He insisted,that this was the order,told me that it takes too much time to make it stuffed,so they stopped making it. He argued with me and would not reduce any of the overcharged 17$ for this tasteless dish.It was so far from what it promised in the menu !!!!!!!!! Bad service,bad food.our anniversary dinner was the worst ever.

Hot and sour soup was good, combo rice tasty, very large portions. The menus are in terrible condition, table was dirty, wait staff was nice. Temperature inside the restaurant had to be upper 70s, a little too warm for my comfort. The place needs someone to clean it up a bit.
Great food!!!! Flavorful, reasonably priced, and perfectly spicy!!!! but sub-par service when it's busy. I'm so thirsty. The waitress had a pitcher of water then walked away. Help. I'm parched!!!!!!
Great Vietnamese sandwiches on house made baguettes. Fresh rolls were good as well. Prices are ridiculously low. Biggest bargain in Boise...

This place has tons of good reviews and for good reason - the food is delicious. The portion sizes are good. The prices are fair. Be warned, that the menu you see through yelp is apparently well outdated as the prices shown here are lower than the actual prices at the restaurant. You should expect to pay $9-$14 per plate which seems standard for Indian dishes of this size and considering the quality of the food, is well worth it. The. Food. Is, Delicious! Read that last line again because it bears remembering. This is some of the best food I have had in some time and some of the best Indian food I have ever had in St Louis. We ordered: Veggie Samosas Lamb Nihari (spicy) Chicken Palak (mild) Garlic Naan The Veggie Samosas were wonderful. They were soft and flavorful, perfectly seasoned, and incredibly delicious. I wanted to eat them all in one sitting but resolved to bring one home. And I succeeded partially. I had half of one left by the end of the meal. ;) Lamb Nihari was perfect. The lamb was tender and the sauce incredibly flavorful, and spicy as I asked for it. There was ginger sprinkled on top. The next day it was even spicier. Chicken Palak had a wonderful savory flavor and was well seasoned even though it was mild. It was great to have a dish that was both not spicy and not bland. The Garlic Naan is the only thing that something of a disappointment. It hard a bit hard on the bottom, like perhaps a bit stale. The flavor was good but the texture was not as we expected. I've seen some reviews saying the portions are too small and I think that's poppycock. Certainly you could order 1 dish, eat it all in one sitting, and be stuffed. Or you could order a dish and an appetizer and bring some home again. I do not think it likely that you order a dish, eat it all, and find yourself hungry. So do not concern yourself with this notion. At the end of the meal we had not come close to finishing all the food and had enough for 2 meals the next time. (The owner happily gave us more rice to bring home to round out our leftovers). It is worth noting that this place is run by the most charming couple. The husband runs the counter and waits tables and the wife seems to do most of the cooking. They are sweet, and welcoming. They make damn good food and being served by them is almost like being a guest in their home. I mean, if their home was in a crummy strip mall in a slightly run down area. I mention the above because the ambiance is not in any way fancy. There are only a few tables, the hallway to the restroom doubles as a storage area, and like I said, the location is not ideal. There are several Indian Places in and around St Louis, with similar prices, and better decor but none with service quite to match what you get at Spice-N-Grill. The food is, for the most part, amazing but I wish there were just one other factor to set this place off. If the prices were a few bucks cheaper probably more people would take notice. If the location was better they would surely get more traffic, but they don't have these things. All they've got is a kind older couple, making a great food, and the words of strangers to recommend them. So, consider them recommended. Don't dress up. Don't go for the ambiance. Don't worry about the run down strip mall they are in. Just go. Pick your favorite dish, as your favorite spice level, round it out with an appetizer and enjoy some fantastic food and the company of a kind couple cooking it for you as though you were at their home.
Don't come here in a hurry. It's like they move in slow motion. They pay more attention to talking to customers than time-sensitive matters and move so slow! Let's go, let's go, let's go!

I stopped in for a bite before a meeting and I've wanted to go back ever since. First, the place is very open and impeccably clean. Second, the guy at the counter was so sweet and third, the food was really delicious. I ordered the navy bean soup, mac and cheese and a ginger juice with mint and tamarind. All of it was absolutely perfect and I can't wait to try more things!
The food was very good. Big portions. Prices according to what you are eating. Fast service. Going again.
My Americano misto was Brutal. Great looking Cafe and the food looked really good. I guess I should of had a snack instead. Take a pass on the coffee

I liked the place. but taste is average. I think the quality of scallops are bad. my father ate a sea food plate but it was incredible spicy. hi likes spicy food but this was a bit out of taste. we 2 spent 95 including tip.

A fantastic find. We wanted to come here for a while, and then bam, groupon to the rescue...or maybe living social. Anyway, came here on Saturday night. Its a perfect spot - right on beach blvd in the fancy part of downtown st. pete. We were originally sat outside, but the weather didn't look like it would cooperate, so they moved us in when a table opened (and let that be your first tip boys and girls, when you make a reservation - and I would strongly suggest making one - make sure you request inside seating if its the rainy season). They don't have a huge menu, so we split 4 small plates. Girlfriend got something, I got angus beef and bacon sliders, and we split a spinach and artichoke dip and lobster rolls. Lets get past the sliders quickly - you'll want to eat 50 of them. The lobster rolls were good, but I was expecting a hot item, and they were cold like thai basil rolls. My fault for not being more careful when I ordered, but they were still good. As for the spinach dip...I worked at a Houston's Restaurant for 4 years and continued to eat there for as long as there was one in the vicinity I lived in. The Houston's spinach dip to me is the end all and be all of spinach dips and nothing has ever come close - until now. This spinach dip was fantastic. It may not have been the best, but it was so darn close. The décor is beautiful. Very romantic - my girlfriend called it like a French boudoir, and that's as good a description as any I could come up with. And while it is romantic on the inside, it isn't very romantic as in it is not intimate. The tables are set up for large parties, and though they can be separated for smaller parties, you're still going to be right on top of the one next to you. We were at a small 2 top, and we were right in the open with everyone able to stare at us (and they're always staring, and their eyes say, why in the world is that beautiful woman with you). The seating is also very limited inside, which again, is why a reservation is recommended. Outside seating would work well provided it isn't the dead of summer and about to pour. I should also point out that our server, Parker (no relation to Peter) was fantastic. He asked us if we wanted drinks, and after we said no, we checked in on yelp and saw we could get a free drink. So, of course, we got a free drink. We also told him we had the certificate from living social or groupon, and rather than treat us like a couple of cheapskates, he was terrific. Never missed a beat, food came out timely, water stayed filled, and I hope our tip reflected it. Perhaps he just realized if we checked in on Yelp, we were likely to review on yelp, or maybe he was just really good as his job. So thank you Spiderman...I mean Parker. And Tryst. We'll definitely be back (for more sliders).

Awesome Ethiopian food in a very cool environment. Get the vegetarian combo platter and let them take care of you. The owner and staff treat you like family. Great overall experience, and I encouage you to support this local business.

Highly recommend! Their food is always fresh and served with a smile. They always have a variety of salads as well! Completely authentic. Nothing like homemade Dominican breakfast on a Sunday morning.
The food is okay, great for a quick stop, not not earth shattering- I mean it's fast food with a tropical twist. Their Cilantro-garlic dipping sauce is awesome though!

Overall Gateway to India does a fine job. It is a basic Indian buffet. There is nothing fancy nor elaborate about the offerings. I simply suggest making less quantity and refreshing more often. All of the vegetarian dishes and the Tandoori chicken were very good. The chicken breast at the end was offered in two traditional sauces and it was just so so for me. The salad and the dessert both are in need of improvement. The mango lassi was very good.

I'm not sure if this is the same owner as the share e Punjab in media but I believe this location has a edge on the media one. The buffet offered a couple more dishes and the red chicken curry (forget name) was tastier.

Great place for live music and drinks in Hudson on the Gulf. Food is okay but my husband and I are not overly impressed by it. Be prepared for wind on the patio at night off the Gulf. There's people of all ages who come for the live music. Parking is limited so you may have to pay $2 for public parking next door at the beach and walk over. This place is always happening for a nice night out.

My go-to dishes by which I judge my Thai restaurants: tom yum goong, and green curry. Zen Yai did a great job with both, but more importantly, they complied with our "Thai spicy, not American spicy" request! Definitely exceeded my expectations, when I'm in the area I'll definitely be back. Bonus points for the John Lennon artwork and the nice local wine list - it all made for a comfortable atmosphere, not trendy, not divey, just right.

First time coming in tonight and our meal was great!! We ordered Korean fried chicken, pork and beef ramen, all of which were absolutely fantastic! Staff was very friendly and took great care of us! Can't wait to make this a regular spot!

I was staying at the Hotel Indigo two doors down and stopped in because I needed to grab something quick for lunch. Restaurant is clean and the waitress was attentive and very nice. I ordered the Lunch special which was a Half Bowl of Pho with a Half Po Boy. Both were o.k. but neither were anything special. Maybe it was just a one time thing or it could possibly be that it was the very inexpensive lunch special. Either way I would probably go somewhere else next time.

Don't let the location deter you dining here. In my opinion, this restaurant has the best pho in Tampa Bay. Other dishes are good, too, but when I come here, I get the pho. Prices are very modest, but food taste is top notch.

This business under new management! Rumor said been sold for $5 million So its not authenthic malaysian food no more. The owner now is fu chow chinese Taste is so so now... The owner look like don't know what to do or confused to take the order! Wish you the best Penang!
The lunch buffet is wonderful! Plenty of vegetarian options. I've been here multiple times over the past few years and have never had a bad experience.

They have relocated to 7023 Michigan Rd, Indianapolis, IN 46268 BEST Jamaican food yet!.. All other Caribbean restaurants in Indy are far from authentic, My parents are Jamaican... and Trust me... this is the real deal! They have also expanded their menu to include other Jamaican dishes! The new location is big and has seating for dine in customers as well. Nice relaxing atmosphere .. Reminds me of being in J.A. Love it!! Go check them out!

Went here with my boyfriend on a rainy day, we were both craving some good thai food. The place was pretty packed, and though we were seated immediately we had to wait for our menus and water and waited quite a while before they came to take our order. This place needs to hire more people, the waiters that were there were actually running from table to table. My boyfriend and I both got curries, $10 each, which, for the portion and the quality was quite excellent! I thought my yellow curry was on the thin side but still tasted delicious. 3.5 stars for the wait time, 4.5 for the food. I'd definitely go back, and I think this place would be great for take-out.

Came here for dinner Sunday night. There was no wait so we were seated immediately. It's hard to find good Malaysian restaurants in N.Y. so when I saw this one in Philly I must try. We ordered the roti (always good), steamed chicken dumplings (nothing special) for starters. The order the bah kuh teh (herbal soup), lady fingers, and half of the Hainanese chicken. It was just the 2 of us but we were a bit greedy. Oh and we each ordered a drink and rice on the side. The quality of the food is as I remembered. It was good but was slightly disappointed with the Hainanese chicken. What makes the chicken amazing is that thin layer of gel (fat) underneath the skin, it didn't have that. It was just a plain over cooked chicken in soy sauce but everything else was good.
Just had stopped in on a whim and it was a great find. Got the large spring salad with chicken and it was so fresh and a very large portion. Place is authentic.

Food was very tasty! I had a not so good experience with the lady manager of this location! She was constantly nagging the employee making my bowl even without knowing the order details! Food is definitely delicious and worth trying!

The atmosphere was nice but very loud! The spinach linguini wasn't really seasoned. The sauce on the veal was good, but it wasn't very tender. They also charged us a dollar more per drink than the price that was listed on the menu. The olive bread was tasty. It was pleasant, but for the price, I probably won't go out of my way to return.

Great Bahn Mi and a great Oyster Po-Boy was found while we were waiting for our bus. The Bahn Mi had a nice spice to it and the Po-boy was very tasty and was served on fresh delicious bread. This place was a total surprise. The place seems like any other convenience store but this great treasure of food is found as you venture to the food service area of the mart. My wife and I would definitely come here again.

Tried it for the first time today. The owner makes you feel very welcome and helps you decide what to pick, often not on the board. The description of all the items that go into a Chaat seemed like the result would be a little crazy, but the flavors blended well together. A unique snack, and surprisingly light. Will definitely be going back to try the Lassies.

While visiting friends in the area, I was able to try this Vietnamese restaurant. The menu was very expansive, with about 164 items. A lot of the things on this menu often aren't found all in one restaurant, so that was a perk. I am visiting with a friend who is used to eating home cooked Vietnamese food, and he was impressed with the length and variety of the menu. Tried the Canh Chua today, which is a dish I have come to like a lot over time. The tamarind flavor is unique and yummy. Also the spring rolls were good, and so was the avocado shake. Thumbs up from me for a good Vietnamese restaurant in the area.

Came in and the guy just looked at me like I was lost. wasn't phased so I asked him if I could sit anywhere. Took a seat and my partner and I got a menu. So far okay :) Asked for the drinks he had and he pointed at the fridge. Umm okay... So I got up and looked at the fridge and picked out a drink. He looked as confused as I did. Well anyway we got our order and the food was okay. I've been to a lot of Pho restaurants in town and I can safely label it a 3 star place to eat. Today I had the flame broiler pork; however it tasted like it had been sitting out for a while (since it was a little cold). The rice was on point today woo! Love good rice, there fish sauce is different, liked that. Hmm what else... Mmm that's about it. It was an okay experience the server/host is not the most experienced but he gets the job done. 4 stars if I would have had a hot meal, 5 if the service was awesome.
I was in reno for business for few weeks and just stumbled upon this place. The staff was great, the food delicious and ambiance fantastic.Ill make sure to stop here whenever i go back to reno!

Pho is cheap anywhere. If they try to charge you more than $10/bowl of pho in any city, there had better be flecks of gold settled in between your slices of beef flank and a sieve at the table to go panning for it all. It's a carb-loaded broth soup on a cold day, and usually this restaurant satisfies my craving for a cheap, hot meal because it's not as greasy as other Vietnamese joints. But, yikes... this time? This time instead of gold, I found a long hair. What was even worse was that we didn't even care enough to stop eating (or for me to drop a star on this review). It was a wake-up call that maybe my standards for pho in Indy have dropped. We had driven 15 minutes from downtown, starving. We didn't call the pleasant waitstaff's attention. No, instead we just left the bean sprouts surrounding the hair alone, played ignorance, and laughed at our own low standards. The kicker? When we did tell them later on in the evening, there was no discount. No, we paid full price - hair and all. This made me realize something: pho is like... a hot dog. If it falls in the grass, eh, it's probably still okay... right? Doesn't matter that a dog probably peed there earlier that day. And so it is with pho and a hair. And the owners here not cutting you a discount. Avoid the bubble tea here. Otherwise, the Chinese/Vietnamese dishes are mediocre-average. If you're new to Vietnamese - try the classics: beef pho (avoid tripe if you don't have strong masseters), or chicken bun (there should be an accent over the u - a dish served cold).
Great atmosphere in the Garden District. Service was exceptional. Food is phenomenal!

This place is awesome. It's a hole in wall authentic south Indian food place. For all those non Indian yelpers, dosas are Indian crepes that you dip in chutney and sambaar. Came here with my family while I was in town for the holidays. Loved the non veg thalli. Tried the other dosas my parents and wife had. Washed it down with a cup of chennai coffee. You know it's good if the majority of the clientele are Indians. The only complaint is the seating with the booths at the end of restaurant are awkward due to layout and spacing. Otherwise enjoy this nashville gem!

How can a restaurant offer mussels in red in a bowl of juice and run out of good bread? How can your delicious dishes have wonderful sauces and you constantly run out of bread on a Saturday night? My wife and I have tried both locations and each time you are stingy on the bread. For the record.....pita bread DON'T cut it to soak up sauce! Neither does microwaving your frozen or day old bread on a Saturday night. Last time to at your blue bell location we asked for more bread to soak up the delicious veal piccata sauce and you gave us microwaved bread.....on a Saturday night! Are you kidding!!!! I could see if you run out on a Tuesday....but you have been in business long enough to know better...Please provide fresh bread to your customers....

The food was amazing. I got the chicken tikka masala and the samosa chat. My husband got lamb curry which was so delicious. The portions were huge and the flavors were rich and delightful. The service was great and we enjoyed the selection of music. All in all, a great decision and we look forward to coming back again.

I ordered red snapper, peas and rice & cabbage. The red snapper was made fresh and worth every bit the wait. The peas & rice were very good and the cabbage with a mixed vegetable medley was nutritious and tasty. The portions were very generous. I was concerned about parking as there wasn't any the first time I drove around. I called and was told it was okay to park at the mechanic next door. The owner was friendly and very personable. I'll definitely be back again. Fish lovers should remember to call ahead so that your fish can be prepared. I really like that the fish is made to order. I'll definitely be back to try out other dishes.
An amazing place for spring and summer. It's great to sit outside with your dog and watch passers by. The kabobs are great. The wait staff is sweet and attentive.

So delicious! The chicken mango (light spicy) was sweet and tasty. I ordered coconut flavored rice since the server informed me that dish doesn't come with rice. It was the perfect complement. My companion's seafood with crispy noodles had more broth than he would have liked, and not enough shrimp or squid...mostly scallops. The atmosphere was lively and the service friendly.
The lunch special with the Tulip, the Tom Yum Gai Soup and Massamun curry was absolutely delicious! Great polite service for a fun afternoon lunch.

Best Malaysian food in town! Always serving my favorites and consistent in taste every time. I bring my Family and friends here all the time and they always enjoyed a good meal. Never cease to bore me with their cooking. I really love the dessert chendol but sometimes they make it smaller than usual. One time it's half the amount I usually get. I don't want to complain because I come here all the time but if I ever get smaller than what it's suppose to be again I will definitely say something next time If it's your first time here you have to try: haianese chicken, rotti canai, chendol, crispy golden fried squid, Malaysian bbq ribs, mango chicken, water crest, seafood tofu soup

Love this place. The good thing is the menu has a lot of good choices and the food is tasty. The staff is very helpful and nice. The bad thing is the chicken soup is just ingredients put together not slow cooked soup we are all used to. Sometimes the rice is old and ruins the meal but that has only happened a few times and I go there often.
What more can you say, food is great, high quality and heathy! Line takes a long time but what can you do, worth the wait for sure!

My god waiting for the kitchen is one thing waiting on slow service is another. Tonight was rare form of a totally inept waiter who literally seemed like they couldn't care less. Gave the typical lip service such as thanks for coming, but seriously this guy will starve if he plans to earn anything from tips. Sadly there's no way to get that message though to management except if they read these reviews. Enjoyed the menu items but that's about it.

This place rocks! The portions are well worth the price and the hummus and falafel are delicious. Also, I was given one less falafel than I was supposed to receive and one of the girls working brought me an extra when she realized the mistake (I had no clue). Definitely will be back.
One of my favorite places to eat in Indy! Food, atmosphere, and staff are all exceptional!

Overpriced!!!!! Horrible service, and shady business!!! They charge you an extra 10 dolars per person when u eat in. They also do not tell you this until its time to pay. Their menu does not have prices on it because they make up their own prices which change frequently. Worst of all. They dont give you enough food. !!! Not reccomended. -center city native

Top notch! I decided to go to Yah Mon for my birthday...and I was not disappointed. The ambiance was exceptional! The decor was sophisticated, yet homey (perhaps the perfect place for a date or for a celebratory dinner?). The homey decor is paired with Caribbean music. Lovely! During the meal, Andre was very attentive to our needs and made sure that we felt right at home. I ordered the oxtail plate and it was perfect! The plate comes with a hearty side of beans and rice and a salad. It wasn't spicy, but had a good ole kick to it. It took about 25 minutes to cook because everything is prepared made-to-order by the lovely and hospitable Chef Janice. Worth the wait! Gems like these I prefer to keep to myself, but I feel like I'd do an injustice to the lovely owners. I look forward to dining at Yah Mon again.

Worst service, food and prices possible. I have never written a review before but I just could not let this one go by. I made a reservation here for my birthday. My friends and I arrived there and were kept standing by the door for a half hour. The place seemed full and there was no place for us to be seated. Not sure what the point of making the reservation was...aren't they supposed to hold a table for us??? After repeated requests to seat us we were taken to a dimly lit backroom by a service restroom. Service was slow and the waiter took his time to come and take our orders. We had to ask several times for a performance by the belly dancer before she came and did a cursory performance. The worst part of everything was the food which ranged from completely bland to inedible.I just could not understand the combination of a sweet pie with almonds and chicken with powdered sugar and then lamb with honey on top. Even thinking about the food from last night makes me want to throw up. "Desert" was bananas, apples and oranges in a basket with a knife to cut it ourselves!!!! After sitting through the worst possible service and food, we were stuck with a bill of $520 for 8 people which included an $80 tip!! I would recommend everyone to stay as far away as possible from this place.

I came for lunch and honestly had some of the tastiest Indian food I have every enjoyed - off a buffet, at a hole in the wall, next to the half empty shopping mall that looks abandoned. I was shocked! Everything was delightful, service was impeccable and prompt, and everything was delicious. I am so glad my friend convinced me to come and try this restaurant. Come and try the food - you won't regret it!

The food here is bomb its so delicious. One of my fave places to eat in indy. Chicken satay, pad kra prow, and the fried rice are some of my faves. Sometimes spice lecel is less than what youd expect, i usually up a spice level here over most other places to get the heat
The chicken tikka masala is absolutely amazing!! Friendly people, delicious food. Two thumbs up!

Cool place. I love the gigantic enormous outside terrace with the Caribbean music. The atmosphere is really chill and relaxing. Makes me want to escape Philly and go to the islands! I wish they imported some sand to cover up all the rocks lol. The grassy area is nice. As much as I love the atmosphere, the food was OK. Was good, but not raving good. I'm surprised Guy Fieri came here for DDD, I didn't think the food was good enough for that. The collard greens were really salty. The roti was good, kind of dry. My friend had the jerk chicken, the rice and veggies were good, he really enjoyed the chicken, although it was a bit dry without the sauce (he got jerk sauce on the side because its very very spicy). I love plantains, and they were just OK here. Nothing special. People complain a lot about the service here. We actually had a really good waitress, she was totally chill, super nice, and helped me out a lot with the menu. She came back several times to check on us. Only slow part was getting our bill paid, but that's because the place was full by then and she had a dozen tables. Overall, I'd come back. But not for the food. I'm come back w/ my BYOB for some Jamaican music and groovin entertainment!

It was ok. Went here with co workers for their lunch buffet and i have to say i'm not a fan of their food but my co-workers were happy with the selection price and quality of the food. The lunch buffet was good and the staff was quite attentive at what we are getting and ordering. I personally would not go again simply because I didn't like the food but my friends thoroughly enjoyed it and were talking positively about it.

Food was quite expensive for portion sizes. Was charged 18.00 to receive two chicken legs in sauce. My husbands food was wrong took over 25 minutes to correct it. Service was so so, it was super loud, we were packed in and it was freezing every time the door opened. The owner did come and talk to us after we paid our bill knowing we were very displeased. He was nice but instead of making it right and reducing the bill he offered if we came back again he'd take care of us. No sir. That's not how it's done. The food didn't even taste good enough to return not alone all the other issues. Too bad because I love this type of food.

Small space but very cozy and great music playing. I enjoy they're happy hour wings definitely worth stopping by. Next time I will be having some of they're ramen I'll leave a review for that once I do. - NotTheChefRamse

Excellent biryani, the best i have had. Good and friendly service. I have been to india and dined at many indian restaurants in the philadelphia area; this is the best. Keep in mind very casual /small inside.
I love it here. Service is always INCREDIBLE. The food is always AMAZING. Go for the beef pho. Or the vegan egg rolls. Or the spring rolls. Or anything. It's all. so. damn. good.

When my fiancée said he found chef Nina's restaurant in NOLA and there was goat curry on the menu, we knew we would have to plan to dine there, so I between the Hermes and the Bacchus parades, we were able to walk over for a late 10pm dinner. As we walked to our table, we saw chef Nina in the open kitchen, and if we had had time for a drink, we probably would have grabbed one at the bar and watched her in action. But instead, we sat down at our table in the back of the restaurant and perused the menu. Drink of choice when in NOLA is the sazerac, and theirs was very good. The kitchen sent out some biscuits with 2 butters (chives and bacon) they were gone pretty quickly. For starters, I ordered a half a dozen oysters, and we shared the conch croquette and spicy pig ears to share. The croquettes were perfect and balanced out the saltiness of the pig ears. For mains, we ordered the Caribbean seafood pepper pot and the goat curry with the black eyed peas and roasted potatoes as sides. The pepper pot was too fishy for my fiancée, and the sour notes did not pair as well with the rest of the meal - probably wouldn't order it again. But, the goat curry, OMG!!!, it was melt in your mouth, nestled amidst pillowy sweet potato gnocchi, with a rich sauce, that we just scooped up until there was nothing left. Our evening was made extra special when Larry stopped by our table to check in on us, and we shared with him how we had seen him and chef Nina in Portland, about a year earlier while we waited for our table at BokeRamen. He explained to us what they were finalizing the investment for Compere Lapin, and that they come to Portland fairly regularly. Who knew!?! If you're in NOLA, this is a must on your adventure!

Came here with the fam after a 7-day cruise. All of us had pho tai. Very tasty and authentic broth. I personally appreciated the small bite sized pieces of beef. Generous with the dressings (I'm talking about green onions and stuff). Overall very enjoyable pho. 4/5 would eat again.

Pretty good. On the other hand, I am totally unconvinced there is any kind of "home cooking" going on here, which is implied in a really circumspect and roundabout way. When I mildly pressed the owners about recipes and ingredients, I got an odd mixture of sales pitch and something about the food actually coming from India. Judging from that, I think a very good part of what they offer, are the kinds of "heat and serve" or quick-prep prepackaged Indian dishes you can get at an Indo-Pak grocery or even Trader Joes. Really, its a great idea for what it is, kind of like a Hindu-Kush flavored Skyline Chili, but this is really and truly fast food.
Always worth the 20 minute drive from Franklin. ... Though I wouldn't complain if they were closer.
Best tortellini salad and chicken gyro in St. Louis! The place isn't much to look at, but it has me going back over and over because the food is that good.

Favorite Pho place in Reno!! Most places that serve veggie Pho the broth is very plain - not at SF a kitchen ! I ordered the veggie pho and it was perfect. My husband ordered the vermicelli noodle with pork and egg roll and it was addictively good. They have a nice lunch menu too. All the servers are super friendly which give the place a relaxing atmosphere

Pho King. Such a cleverly named restaurant. Have you seen their brand/logo design? Amaze balls (buy a t-shirt!). I've hit up Pho King a few times by now (good spot when you want something quick and easy before hitting up Rexall Place) but this was the first time I've been to their newly renovated digs. Everything is much cleaner and aesthetically pleasing. The right hand side of the resto now consists of a counter instead of seating area. A and I stopped in for lunch on a Wednesday afternoon. The place was reasonably busy with several tables full along with a few people popping in to pick up takeout orders. The menu is extensive with your typical Vietnamese offerings but they hilariously have a full page dedicated to Western foods/breakfast meals. Random but it must cater to the clientele in the area??? I'll never understand why so many other Viet/Asian places in town do this. Take a page from Pho Tau Bay's playbook and focus on one thing and do it well. Bonus, they're open everyday of the week (Sunday's now!). - Bun bo hue (P18) ($10.95 king) - I went with their bun bo hue because I've never had it here before. The broth was fragrant with a good depth and flavour profile. I found it to be a bit on the lighter/cleaner side if that makes any sense. The meat balls were delicious! A little bit of green onions and sliced onions gives their bowls an extra zip of flavour. Good stuff. - Grilled lemongrass chicken with kimchi (R23) ($13.95) - A was having some trouble deciding but eventually went with the grilled lemongrass chicken skewers over rice with a side of kimchi and vegetables. The lemongrass chicken had an odd texture to it that I can't even put in writing. It was cooked fine but it must have been the cut of meat that they were using. She only ate one skewer and I ended up taking the rest as leftovers. As for the kimchi, it wasn't very good - kind of flavourless and a chore to eat. Blah. This is why I rarely, if ever, veer from ordering pho at Vietnamese spots. On a previous trip, I went with a buddy before an Oilers game where we each ordered pho: - Seafood noodle soup (P17) ($10.95 regular) - a couple shrimps, kabuki, and shrimp balls. The broth was great - flavourful and clean tasting! Sort of sate style but with just a bit of spiciness to it. Definitely would get this again. - Rare steak and meatball beef noodle soup (P8) ($8.95 regular) - my buddy went to town on his bowl. There was nothing left after we finished devouring both of our bowls. Solid spot to grab a bowl of pho. Prices are reasonable and service is fast. Slightly ghetto area of town but that's part of it's charm. Don't let that hold you back from trying out Pho King.

Seriously one of the best gyros I've ever had. I ordered the chicken souvlaki. The chicken was tender, well seasoned, warm, and generously topped with tzatziki sauce. Mmm. I am sad my styrofoam box is already empty. Go Gyro Go is my favorite food truck so far. They do seem to have an ingredient problem - today they were out of tahini. Still, five stars, what I ordered was awesome. Further items of note: the owner (who took our order) and the cooking staff were really friendly. Also, there were two people in front of us, but I think we had our food within about 5 minutes of ordering - they worked fast.

I went here today for lunch with my colleagues. The place has a decent ambiance but most things look old and a tad pale. They could really use a fresh coat of paint and color. We sat at the enclosed booths that are nestled away in the inner sections of the restaurant. Do try sitting there when you go. It's not the best decor I've ever seen but is unique nonetheless. The prices at this place are very affordable. They do have a large menu (apart from a separate lunch menu) that contains everything from empanadas to pasta. The thing I liked about their menu was that they had at least 15 items separately listed on a 'vegetarian' section of the menu. That is always helpful for vegetarians. I had ordered a lamb gyro with a side of home-made chips off the lunch menu. The gyro was served on an open pita with a generous dose of Tzatziki sauce (Which I love). The lamb meat was well cooked and the whole dish was quite filling. The only thing I would criticize were the potato chips that were served on the side. They had zero seasoning and hence were bland and some of the chips had lost their crunchiness/crispness, which leads me to believe that they chips are just being held in an open container somewhere in the kitchen. Overall, a nice new place to have tried out. The server was nice and helped pick the dish for a friend when he asked for her help.
We really enjoyed the atmosphere, the great food, and delicious mixed drinks.

We've been here three times, sadly, this will likely be our last. While visiting from Chicago, we called Momo's on Sunday at 8:45 to be sure they were still open. We decided to make the drive from our hotel downtown. The gentleman on the phone stated that the kitchen was open til 10:00 (website stated midnight, but whatever). We figured we'd still have time to grab a quick bite. When we walked in, however, the tune dramatically changed. It seemed as though the bartender (guy with long beard) and staff was irritated we were there. We quickly took the hint and asked for the check after downing a quick appetizer and a couple drinks. We ended up at another place downtown, where we didn't feel rushed. We had looked forward to stopping at Momo's during our trip, so this was a letdown.

Loved this place! The service was amazing, they were busy but made us feel special, and we didn't even have a reservation or a special event planned. The owner came over and talked to us like we were friends, not strangers and he smiled a genuine and caring smile...something was so nice about this. He really seemed happy to be there and happy that we were there. This is so rare in many businesses and restaurants in Philly. The food was delicious. We had the flaming duck. It was not on the dinner menu, but we saw someone else with it, asked the waiter about it, and they were happy to make it for our table. It was tender and flavorful, really an A plus meal. The place is small and cozy but not too over crowded and it was relatively quiet for the number of people that were there.
