You could comfortably talk to your date without raising your voice, but at the same time there was an energy around you. The table in front of us had a large baby stroller with them and the waiter pulled out the chairs and removed them so that the stroller would fit comfortably into the dinner table. That is good customer service. I highly recommend this place for an affordable, special night. The price was good for the quality of food and service.

An impromptu drive thru Doylestown, landed us here. Ambience is fine, and food is alright(certainly not gr8), but the waitress/hostess ticked me off. My wife noticed pre-packaged curry paste in their kitchen, which is obvious from the taste too. One of the 3 curries we ordered was undercooked, and obviously so from the smell. When we pointed it out to her, she gave us a speech abt how massaman curry gets too thick if cooked well, and insisted that it was fine. We couldnt eat it, but i was curious abt the curry so boxed it. We added some water and let it boil, and it tasted perfect. The chef messed up, no doubts. The mistake is not a problem but the hostess' dismissive attitude is appauling and im never going back to this place. I discourage anyone from going either.

I came with a large party and they were very accommodating when I called before hand to make a reservation. The restaurant is pretty small and tight with a dark atmosphere. The service was pretty fast and the staff was very polite. We ordered quite a few dishes, but the chicken satay stood out. It was very moist and flavorful. All the other dishes such as the papaya salad, pad thai, pad see ew, green curry, and tom yum were decent. The green curry was particularly disappointing, it was basically flavorless besides the hint of spice and off-putting coconut flavor. Not to mention the chicken was extremely dry. The tom yum soup was extremely spicy even though we asked for it to be mild. Overall an average thai restaurant with decent prices. If you are in the Santa Barbara area I would recommend TAP thai over this place.

Drinks were great, food was delicious! The pasta is made from scratch and really makes the food outstanding here. One note: their pasta menu is designed in the traditional way where pasta is a small/medium sized course before a meat entree, so the portion size may seem small compared to some other Italian places. Keep in mind it's handmade pasta though so quality over quantity. But I will say I was very content with the pasta portion size after sharing a couple appetizers with the person I was with, especially since they serve complimentary fresh bread and dipping oil as well. Overall I left very happy and satisfied, definitely recommend this restaurant.

I have tried to visit this restaurant 2 times due to the good reviews on Yelp. The first time I looked on line and it said they opened at 4. I pulled into the parking lot at 330 and waited until 4. When I walked up to the door they had a sign that said "sorry we are closed today." I then tried to visit again. This time I called at 2pm to see if they were open for lunch. I said "are you open for lunch today?" The lady responded, "yes, at 2:30." I ran an errand and arrived at 3 - only to be told they are closed and only serve until 2:30! Language barrier, I guess. But regardless I will stick to the other Thai restaurants in Brandon.

Not a bad choice if you're right in the area and really want Vietnamese. The atmosphere is somewhat lacking, it feels like a quick serve cafeteria but it's really not that quick. Parking is very easy and I had some decent spring rolls with a pretty tasty peanut dipping sauce. The spring rolls (all that I ordered this trip) may have been made fresh but I wouldn't have a way to tell by looking because they brought them to me rolled tightly in plastic wrap.... So tight that it seemed like they might do an assembly line pre-roll prep or they wanted me to really work to get them unwrapped. If this were a to-go order this would have made sense to me, but they were brought on a tray with the cup of peanut sauce. Not a wonderfully appetizing presentation. Nonetheless it tasted decent. They also charge a .50 fee to use a card (debit or credit). I realize there are costs associated with credit cards, but I find it less annoying if restaurants just build those costs in.
First time here and the food was great. Great flavor. Got spice level 3 to try first, but I love a good spice level so would go higher myself for next time.

Sandwich is delicious and all home made except bread. They are so kind. They heard my daughter has a food allergy and they didn't want her to be hungry to go to church. They made another new sandwich for my daughter. My daughter loves it. Bubble tea is delicious as well. I love everything hot, they made warm Jasmine green tea with bubble for me. They are amazing. You won't regret it if you go there. Good luck.

After finishing my meal at Abyssinia, I sit here thinking to myself and wondering why I have never tried Ethiopian food before. I must say it was quite the experience. I live up on the North Side around 116th & Ditch road and it's a bit of a hike to get down there, but today I said what the heck and headed down to the little strip mall that houses Abyssinia and several other worth while "joints" as well! Having never done this I wanted to read up on it a little which actually helped me and I knew what to expect at least as far as tradition went. I chose the spicy lentil pouch to begin. Similar to a beef patty but triangular and stuffed with spicy lentils. This was awesome and piping hot! Then I got a recommendation from the server and ordered the sampler platter. This says, on the menu, that it comes with beef chicken and spinach in various ways of preparation. It sounded very good. Because I've never eaten goat and was a little apprehensive I wanted to stay away from it my first time out. When my order came out it had.... Well..... I really had no idea what it had!!! The dish came served on injera with rolls of Injera on the side. Injera is a very spongy almost rubbery flat bead that has little holes in it like an English Crumpet. The trick is to rip off a piece and scoop up whatever it is you've been eyeing on the dish! This was fun for me because I started to have wondrous flashbacks of all the times my mother would yell at me to get my hands out of the food and here I was digging, scooping and squeezing my way through an absolute heavenly plethora of spices, flavors and self made concoctions from my plate. I was a little afraid to ask what I was eating because it was so good I didn't want to know, YET! Of course I waited till the last piece of injera was gone and tried to eat the flattened out piece on my dish that had been there to form the wonderful spongy cradle soaking up all the flavors. The problem was I was stuffed and couldn't enjoy this last little tidbit. Just for the record, on my plate was some type of curried lamb. I love lamb but this was a little tough ( hence the 4 stars). I feel it could have been cooked to tenderize a little better. Chicken in a dark BBQ looking curry and cumin flavored sauce which was excellent. A sort of creamed but not creamed spinach, if that even makes any sense, at least that's how it tasted. Some curried potatos in the center of the dish several hot spices that I was warned by the server to go easy on (Really not that spicy ) But the best, to my surprise, was the Goat!!! It was extraordinary. So much that I could probably bathe in it. I'm mentally bathing in it right now while I recount the tender, full of flavor spiced Goat. Why have I not ever eaten this before. The server was extremely pleasant and attentive and the chef actually came out to my table and asked how I liked everything. I couldn't have like it any more. I will say this, I will come back. I can see me regularly ordering the spiced Goat and indulging with fingers grasping the injera to cradle the love on that plate.

Took a client/friend to lunch the other day and had the beef pho soup out of this world but what made it better was having the left overs for dinner. We have had the cauliflower burger there before and that was a 10. Will make it a point to frequent there more often
Where the pho you been all my life! Great food, great ambiance, great staff. Will be back soon!

Okay so I never write reviews but... I visited butcher and bee this past Saturday and thought it was a great atmosphere and menu. First things first, the bartender was extremely rude. Secondly, I ate the lamb meatballs (which I thought tasted funny) and proceeded to get severe food poisoning within 5 hours. I have a pretty solid stomach and it was horrible. No one else I was with had the meatballs and no one else got sick so it seems like a fluke but I don't think I would visit again.

I had my food delivered to me, so I can't comment about the ambience or the atmosphere. However, the person who took my order over the phone was extraordinarily friendly and nice, and the food was absolutely terrific. I got the vegetable samosas, Chana masala, and some naan. Everything was well made and tasted wonderful. I highly recommend this place.

Not that Mood needs another good review - but we are visiting from out of town and after finding Mood on Yelp we made it part of our vacation plans. Unfortunately we were still full from lunch and after telling that to the owner he steered us in a direction allowing us to have an experience without filling up. My husband,son and I shared a mango lassi and a lemonade lassi. We also shared a samosa chaat and a chicken chaat. He was very kind and chatted with us about the history of the food and his other restaurants. Luckily the busy dinner rush had passed and we were able to sit and enjoy our visit. Having this experience was a great ending to our day in Philly.

I eat Pho all the time, and it is by far the best Pho I've ever had. Lilly is a sweetheart and my husband and I enjoy eating there any chance we get. I am a bit worried that by writing another great review for Lilly's that everyone in Nola is going to know about the goodness, but Lilly is such a great person that she deserves the credit! Love the Rare Flank Pho with extra steamed vegetables!!!

Love this place! It's nothing fancy and is everything I want out of Vietnamese food. My hubs and I have had a few of their sandwiches (the meatball is our favorite) and most of the vermicelli bowls (I love the grilled beef with egg rolls). It's cheap, straight forward and completely delicious. We've been hunting for good Vietnamese food since we moved here 2 years ago and this place blows all of the fancy spots out of the water. Just as delicious (if not more) for less than half the price!

My wife and I brought some friends to Delicia for dinner on a Thursday evening (6-2-16). We were the first to arrive, so we were immediately seated in the area across from the bar. The restaurant was very stylish yet inviting. We also had great service with a combination of friendliness and knowledge that I wish more restaurants had. After all, the social aspect of dining with friends can be as key to enjoying the evening as the food. After ordering our beverages, we were brought a small cup of Sancocho as an amuse bouche. I am not familiar with the item, but the flavor reminded me of tasty bean broth. We then shared a guacamole for the table. Excellent flavor combination in the guac. My wife, who normally doesn't care for avocado, even thought it was good! The chips that came with the guac were light, but crisp enough to scoop. I ordered the "De Palmitos" salad (hearts of palm, field greens, roasted walnuts, butternut squash, hibiscus-lemon vinaigrette). It was my first time trying hearts of palm, so having all these other delicious flavors gave me confidence to try something new. I was very pleased. Finally, I ordered the Pescado Zarandeado (it comes without the fish head....I asked.) The sea bass was colored/flavored with green and red achiote which made for a nice presentation. Very tasty. The fish came with black beans and white rice to fill out the entree. With the great atmosphere, service, and food, it was plain to see why this restaurant was voted one of the Top 5 restaurants in Indy. I look forward to my next visit. Review #6

I went there to get a chicken kabob once and the guy working there was skewering the chickens like he was doing this job for years. I asked his name and he said Ali. He is the God of Kabobs, he is the best it was delicious. Everyone has to give at least a try and go eat at this place when Ali is working.

I have been to Butcher and Bee 5 times. I have had consistently interesting and delicious food. It is not a run of the mill menu. Very delicious flavors. Food comes out at the time it is finished so you keep getting new things to try and combine. I always over order. Love it. Haven't noticed a problem with service that some complained about.

My daughter and I had lunch here on a Tuesday . I had been here twice before, but since those visits, the menu has been changed. It is now a very Mediterranean menu. We ordered a zucchini salad and a smoked trout sandwich. It took 20 minutes to receive our food. The trout tasted very fishy and therefore I only ate a third of the sandwich . The zucchini was overwhelmed with dill and had a slimey texture, so almost that entire dish was left uneaten. We paid the $33 dollar bill and left. My daughter wanted to get the taste out of her mouth so we stopped at Taco Bell for lunch after lunch. I'm sad that the menu changed at olio and that the service was terribly slow with no apology . I also am sad that I did not leave when I discovered that the menu had changed .

Good food. Friendly staff. Very friendly owner. Went specifically to try the Lao cuisine. Nice fresh ingredients. Wasn't disappointed. Made spicy at our request. Did not hold back like many places in town.

The first time I went to pita jungle was in Phoenix. They had an amazing jalapeño cilantro hummus. It had lots of spice. The next time we went to the one in northwest Tucson. The jalapeño cilantro hummus was bland. We got a falafel and a salad. Surprisingly none of it had any flavoring. The salad tasted like lettuce with oil.

The food was good, but nothing blew us away. We started with the chorizo queso appetizer. For entrees, my husband got the empanadas and I got the tacos de papa. We split the churros for dessert which was probably the highlight of our meal. We each got drinks, which were pretty good. Service was just okay. Our server gave us menu suggestions but it seemed like she was only trying to pitch the more expensive items on the menu without actually asking what our preferences might be. And even though she wasn't super busy, she didn't check on us very frequently. We weren't asked if we wanted another drink until after we had already ordered dessert and our drinks were long gone. I think the biggest disappointment happened after we got home - I opened up my leftovers the next day and found that they had only given me a small portion of what had been left on my plate! I had eaten, at most, a third of my entree in the restaurant. My leftover container only contained one taco with none of my sides included. I don't mind spending over $100 on dinner but I'd at least like to keep what I paid for.
Really good, really fresh Thai cuisine. Definitely worth visiting Washington Square Mall. Friendly service and spiced just right. I had the Basil Chicken and my friend had the Red Curry. Yum.

Been to Tryst several times..... Great location and luv the decor. Food is typically cooked to perfection for such a small kitchen they do a great job. Luv the cheese plate with drinks. Crab cakes and salmon were excellent. Never had bad service. It can get busy. i am not sure that a small gem of a place be criticized because it is did not have seats available.

This is my favorite place to lunch solo. The people who work here are so friendly, and the falafel is always wonderful & freshly made. Plus it's such a deal for how much food you get. Did I mention I love this place?

I came to Cheu Noodle Bar after seeing it on a list of must-eats in Philadelphia, so I had really high expectations for this place! When I walked in, the ambience was pretty much what'd you expect for a Saturday night, with groups of friends sitting at tables and parties of 1-2 sitting at the bar. The wait was initially quoted as an hour, but someone finished up early and I only waited about 15 minutes to be seated. They had an interesting selection of beers and cocktails, but I wasn't thirsty so much as hungry so I passed on the drinks. The menu was very simple and straightforward, and I ordered the crab broth noodles and dumplings in chili oil. The dumplings in chili oil came first, there were 4 cute dumplings in a small bowl. They were very tasty, but were different than what I was expecting. Growing up in Asia, dumplings usually have higher fat content and are easier to chew, but I guess the meat in these dumplings were leaner and took a bit longer to chew through. The crab broth noodles came shortly after, and I must say I was pretty disappointed. I passed over the miso ramen for these noodles, and the soup in this broth was a bit spicy and sour, but wasn't as brothy as they claimed. The hand-drawn noodles were quite tasty and bouncy, but to me they were ruined by the broth. Overall, I'd give the dumplings a 4, the noodles a 2.5, and the overall experience a 3.5. If I do come back next time, I'll try the miso ramen instead!

We go here almost every week and always get the pho. As another reviewer mentioned, they have been out of the beef broth for pho before, but luckily we were calling for take-out. Other than that one time, we haven't had a bad experience here. You can't be in a rush or have a specific time frame here because it is a bit slow sometimes depending on how many people are seated.
Sushi was gross! And I've eaten a ton of sushi in my time. I'm sure the other food is good but do yourself a favor and skit the sushi!

Fantastically Fresh healthy food and great personable staff. My favorite part of Indian food is the flavor, which this place has nailed. My second favorite thing in Indian food is the cream which was naught to be found. I will say I enjoy the mouthfeel of full creamy goodness, but that would have me in the grave within a few years. This place is one that the epicurean and the dietician will appreciate. Though if you're like me you'll feel they're a tad stingy with the meat, I never leave there feeling hungry or dissatisfied, so they know what they're doing, no need to double down on the meat (as I would normally do). Delicious food, great flavor, without the heart palpatations. Two thumbs way up.

On a recent evening, some girlfriends and I went to Zeppoli for a night hopeful of good food and good company. They had just opened only about a month prior, so we were open-minded, but also knew the chef was reputable and a few reviews on here said everything was good (although, we were skeptical if they were customer written or employee written), but we were pretty confident that the food would be good. And in the grand scheme of things, the food was good. The other components though are what prompted me to write my first ever yelp review. And my girlfriends were all on board with me writing this, as they too felt the same way. First, I would like to say that the service was great. Our server had literally just started working there (a reddish-brown-blonde haired girl named Christina I believe) and she fared very well - checking with the kitchen when she couldn't answer our questions, raving about the desserts (and rightfully so) and also being very friendly and reading our table appropriately. The atmosphere was simple, nice, clean, kind of cute...definitely could use a little color perhaps. Our server told us that the plates were smaller and so do not expect heaping portions. This was ok with us, and how we preferred it usually. She mentioned that the chef suggests we order an appetizer, pasta and an entree - that was how the menu was created. We ordered appetizers, each an entree and each a dessert. The portions were indeed very small. But some of what we ordered definitely did not equate to any value whatsoever. A seafood dish - with a few pieces of seafood and some cous cous was $26. The special with lamb and gnocchi was similarly priced and also was a small portion. All of the desserts (although very good, except the flourless chocolate torte was very unexciting) were $8 each. That is expensive. We felt as though some of the prices were city-like prices, but we were in Collingswood. Our bill, including gratuity, came to just over $250. That's $50 a person...for a BYOB! Insane! We were all still hungry after dinner and hence why we all ordered dessert - which we never ever do. Overall, we each ordered one entree, one dessert and we all split two appetizers. The one appetizer was the antipasti, which we tripled (per the server's suggestion) because it's $9 per person and it was a very small portion, with very little cheese or meat. In the end, we paid $27 for an appetizer of mostly marinated vegetables and such. That is just ridiculous and absurd! All in all, we enjoyed ourselves because of the company of each other and we did enjoy some of the food, but for the price, I know I will never go back and having spoken to the others, I know they feel the same way. It's unfortunate, because the place has potential.
Had dinner there I got a chicken tikka masala, naan, and raita everything was awesome! Would definitely recommend!

We had a retirement party at this location for 30 people and couldn't be happier with our selection. We live out of town and John was excellent to plan with coming out of town. The staff went above and beyond during the event, we had multiple guests commenting on how good the serving was. I had the pork sirloin, which was excellent. The mashed potato sides where I thought the highlight of the food, in addition to the opening antipasti veggies. I would go back to this place Again, and highly recommend for special events. Our event was a lunch and was able to rent the whole restaurant for a very reasonable price.

The service was amazing thanks to Harry. They were playing Motown music, which is always a win. The food was pretty good. We had the carne asada tacos, shrimp tacos and cochinita pibil cemita sliders. The tacos were good. The sliders... eh. Good guacamole - maybe a bit too much lime and creamier than I like it. Delicious margaritas.

The dips of the day are always delicious and usually some type of lemony, garlicky mixture. The only downfall here is that if you ask for more pita, you will be charged a wee fee, but I think it is worth it considering how good the pita is. The first time I went here, I ordered the Greek salad. It's hard to go wrong with this choice at most restaurants, but Kanella really does give it that something extra. Everything was so crisp and fresh. At my most recent visit, I ordered the Arni for my entree, which is grilled top loin of lamb w/ bulgar wheat and stuffed zucchini. My boyfriend had the Poulerikio, which is organic baby chicken flattened and cooked under a brick, with tourlou tourlou and garnished with fava slatsa. Both of these I have put up in the picture section. They are both beautifully presented and tasted just as excellent. Sometimes the most simple ingredients make for the best meals. BYOB bomb boyeee! I forgot to mention the delicious french-pressed coffee! It was sooo good. A friend of ours makes this kind of coffee often, so he was very good and taking it nice and slow to press down. If I had done it, my coffee experience would have probably sucked. It gave us a little bit of pep in our step before going out on the town.

This is one of my favorite places in town. I come here so often and have introduced so many friends to it, that they knew it was the perfect place to throw me a surprise party. My friend made a reservation for 11, but two more friends were able to join. The GM came to our table and said he would not add extra chairs for them, saying they "don't usually do groups" and they "only planned for 11" and wouldn't add any more. So rude for my well-dressed, well-educated, and paying friends! The restaurant was at least 30% empty and they were not the least bit accommodating. The server later told us not to "move around" at all to talk to others in our group. The staff continued to make my friends feel uncomfortable and unwelcome throughout the night. I love their food, but I guess they don't need my business! If you don't like groups, say that upfront and don't take the reservation! Very disappointed with Delicia!

I read that this was the place to take out of towners. Since I was visiting, I took myself to this converted gas station. Olio specializes in small plates and good drinks, from hand crafted cocktails to a solid wine by the glass and bottle list. Probably most impressive was the friendly wait staff who clearly enjoyed working here and talking about good food and drink. Since I was eating at Elaia, next door, I only had the "olio" signature cocktail; it was memorable with the Arak and fresh mint. There were some really good small plate choices - will have to go back for those. Plenty of street parking, although they do offer valet.
This place is horrible I wasn't suggest this place to anyone. The service here is horrid I wouldn't advise anyone to come here and eat.
easily the best indian food I have ever had. The portions were large, the quality was amazing and the food was delicious. I will absolutely be back

Checked Tangelo's out for brunch on a whim, and was pleasantly surprised. I was in Gulfport for a Saturday event, and the allure of brunch with reasonable prices struck a chord. I has an opposite experience of some of the previous reviews. I thought the portions were just right, but the service was sporadic. I ordered the special: Shakshuka with a side of potatoes and a passion fruit mimosa. My husband ordered a veggie burger. Mine was excellent! Shakshuka is a middle eastern dish of poached eggs over spiced tomatoes and peppers. It was the perfect comfort food. My husband said his was pretty good, but the burger came on Cuban bread, which was odd. Even though the food was great, the service was lacking. We waited a while to order, and they forgot about my mimosa until I reminded someone. If you asked me who our server was, I wouldn't be able to tell you. There were four different servers we interacted with. Oh well. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, but I'd check it out again if I were in the area.

I have been to mostly all of the Caribbean restaurants in Philly and I have to say that Ron's is the best! Yesterday I visited for the first time and fell in love. There were about 5 people in line when I arrived and my order was taken within minutes. There were 3 people taking orders and the line moved very quickly. I loved the fact that they kept the food coming out. As I stood there, a new pan of mac and cheese and yams came out fresh and hot, not like some restaurants where they run out of food or make you wait forever for food to be made. The jerk chicken was well seasoned and moist, the oxtail was good, the mac and cheese was REAL mac and cheese and was delicious. The plantain was sweet, moist, perfectly ripe and the best I've had in the city so far. Candied yams are my favorite food so I am very picky and I must say that I was pleasantly surprised with the yams as well....fresh, sweet, real yams (not the canned stuff some restaurants give you). Ron's I will definitely be back even though I have to travel about 40 minutes to get there. Worth the trip! 5 stars!

Came for a little late night dinner after a long day of homework. Got the spicy crab with the hand drawn noodles and an added an egg. Excellent! The broccoli appetizer was excellent as well. Great service great food and awesome music.. Can't go wrong! Definitely coming back!

Eh. That's how I felt about the food. Not delicious, but not terrible. The portions are huge, so you get what you pay for. The rice and salad were tasty but my chicken and potatoes shared the same seasoning and they were both over seasoned. The pita bread came out of a plastic bag so you had some grocery store pita on your plate. Eh. Still in the hunt for some good Greek!

They served my daughter moldy bread on her Steak Stack sandwich. The mold I lie to you not was the size of a quarter and was paisley shaped. How could the kitchen staff miss that since the sandwich is grilled. That means it was assembled, buttered and grilled and no one saw that big piece of mold! Really Zoe's kitchen. Shame on you. She was supposed to get fresh fruit, they served her pasta salad instead. When I told the manager she confirmed that it was indeed mold on the bread and they the kitchen staff failed to inform her that they ran out of fruit. Then magically fruit appears and they say they made it just for my daughter. No, you made it because it should have been available to serve for customers according to the the menu. The manager gave us a free entree and hummus card. She should have compensated us our lunch. Like I would really come back!

I was thankful there was a few vegetarian options on the menu. During my last visit I ordered the Palak Aloo and just loved it! My only dislike was the portion sizes, a bit too small for the price. The staff is very friendly and I hope to see this restaurant grow.
Amazing gyro! BYOB, fast service and reasonable prices...I really love this place and would highly recommend it if you're looking for Greek food in Fairmount.

Well, I had my second go at Vietnamese food, this time at Kien Giang. (The first and only other time was at Miss Saigon in the same parking lot.) I thought this place was solid but maybe it all just isn't really for me? The ambiance is basically Vietnamese diner, definitely full of people. That's cool, I dig it. I also have to get used to the service that basically seems mad and also seems like they don't want to look at you. Also, they want to tell you no about things. Like the bbq ribs will take a long time so you don't want that. Someone else got ribs later on and my brother was soooo jealous. We could have waited! Anyway, probably just a cultural difference or they can tell we are Vietnamese newbies. I am not sure which. We ordered up a bunch of stuff. My brother got a chicken and noodle pot of some sort. It was pretty good and pretty spicy and the salad was in the bowl right there with everything else. I got pho with beef. The pho was good like before and I knew what to do with the side items and spices. I had to spice it up quite a bit to get it where I like it, but it was good and comforting and had quite a bit of beef. Definitely tasty. Spring rolls were ok. Meatballs were a random order my brother made and they were just...weird...texture and taste was just not for us. To me the entire experience was A-OK but not amazing....I think I need to go with someone that really knows the food and helps me figure it out, I dunno. Once you are done you get your check and go to the register to pay. Cash only so bring your dolla bills. There are desserts and bubble tea at the front too in case you want something sweet to go. Give this place a try for sure. As for me, i think I'm sticking to Thai from now on.
Excellent fresh large portions true North Indian vegetarian-friendly and great service. They supply complementary popadum as appetizer. Great garlic naan.

Jasmine Rice is a small restaurant, with a pleasant but simple interior and very nice and accommodating owner. We enjoyed really tasty dishes, as described below. Satay Chicken ($7) appetizers with a peanut sauce a little thinner and more subtle than is typical. The fantastic Thai Papaya Salad ($7) was very colourful and tasty decorated with a modest amount of chopped peanuts a seasoned with a delicious and a little spicy lime dressing- not a huge salad, but adequate for appetizer. The Chicken Pad Khimao contained well-cooked broad noodles, veggies, and chicken in a great, spicy sauce soy-garlic-onion-sweet basil, etc. The Crispy Duck Fried Rice contained crispy-crusted slices of duck over rice, with a sort of smokey flavour. Dinner entrees are adequate in size, but not large. We will be returning to try more.

I've been hearing about how good Ekta is since they opened on Girard Avenue, so I'd meant to get the place and see for myself. So we finally got to the Bryn Mawr location on a Saturday, and I was very disappointed to hear that they'd ended their weekend buffet a few months earlier. I'd been looking forward to trying a number of their dishes in the same meal. On the plus side, they do now give 20% off their menu and a free soda, ice tea, or lemonade at lunchtime. We started with a cashew roll, which was four small fried log-shaped fritters; fairly tasty. Then our entrees came: mango chicken and Ekta vegetables. These each had a (different) subtle and delicious sauce as I can ever remember having in a standard "curry" entree. Incredibly good. The chicken dish has chicken breast and fresh mango pieces, and the vegetables in the other were fresh, not poured out of a freezer bag the way Navratan Korma is made at so many places. Only a few tables were occupied, but the waitstaff was still very polite and attentive. I'd definitely return, but I'd go back even sooner if I knew I could sample more of the dishes at their (departed) buffet.

I got the falafel sandwich to go. Firstly falafel tastes great only if made fresh. The gentleman making the falafel took it straight out the freezer and tossed it in the deep fryer. I had an impression that this might not taste that good after all. Secondly, he did not wrap the sandwich properly before he put it in the brown bag. When I took the sandwich out to eat, a quarter of the portion had already said "Hello" to the bottom of the brown bag. The sandwich was really dry and tasteless. I was lamenting my choice to go to Kalamata's. I could have made a better sandwich in under 3 minutes had I had some pita and frozen falafels. I would rather goto the Subway next door.

We sorta happened upon Queen Of Sheba. The wife, baby and I began heading with hopes of hitting up Dock Street. Well, Dock Street is not open on Sundays. At that point we were committed to Baltimore Avenue, but both wanted something new. That cancelled out the usual good spots, The Gold Standard, Vientiane Café, and Vietnam Cafe. And, yes, those are two different places spelled almost the same, one Thai, the other Vietnamese. So, this brought us to Queen Of Sheba. We had talked many times about trying out some Ethiopian food, especially since there are several in the area. Sheba was more bar than restaurant. It was very empty, so we had the run of the place. There menu was very small. I was disappointed they did not have any meat combinations. We initially were going to get the chicken and lamb tidbits, as well as an app called Foul. The waitress was kind enough to tell us that was A LOT of food. She informed us each meat dish comes with a mess of veggies. So, we decided on just the chicken. Moments later we were told they were out of the chicken. Who runs out of chicken? It's not like there was a rush of people that came in before us. It was 1pm on a Sunday. We almost left, but got over it and ordered the lamb. When the food arrived, we were very pleased. It all tasted very good. The lamb was tender and there was hardly any fat. The bread was done just right, just the right amount of sponginess. The veggies were done just right as well. We also really enjoyed the Foul, which is not to be confused with Fowl. It's actually vegetarian and I believe bean based. All in all, the food was good. The decor was shabby. And the lack of chicken was a bummer.

Tiffin is one of the best places in the city to get Indian food (along with New Delhi and sometimes Palace at the Ben). And the fact that they have kati rolls on their dine-in menu for Tiffin Etc. doesn't hurt either. I was a bit confused as to how the menus worked when I first walked in, but that was cleared up after I figured out that people do take-out and seating is upstairs, where we could order from Tiffin and Tiffin Etc.'s menus. We ordered a papdi chaat to start, which was pretty good (chaat is one of those things that I love eating, but then I realize that it's not that hard to make). When I saw kati rolls on Tiffin Etc.'s menu, I was giddy. Kati rolls are basically constructed of roti that may or may not be fried with eggs and then wrapped around tasty filling of your choice (hopefully). I really don't know why I get giddy when I see kati rolls on any menu, but I have to try them when I see them. (I have this same knee jerk reflex towards papdi chaat, masala dosas, and sometimes samosas. Yea, I'm into unhealthy Indian food.) I got the shami kebab kati roll which was great! My friend ordered his dish and a Masala Pepsi; obviously he didn't enjoy it because he didn't like the mix of cumin and salt in his Pepsi. But it brought me wonderful memories of India :) I'm not sure if they still offer diners both menus, but I would definitely order at least one item from the Tiffin Etc. menu; besides the pizza options that I didn't try, I think Tiffin tries their best to offer street/vendor type food here in Philly.

This place has been in my neighborhood for quite some time and I just went there this morning for brunch. I wish I had gone here much earlier. We brought a bottle of Champagne, and the staff was very accommodating in making Mimosas for us to make our brunch complete. The service was very friendly and helpful with suggestions. The food was delicious. We ordered a bunch tapas and shared it family style. All were very good, the only problem was that I wanted to order more than I could have possibly eaten. So I will have to come back often. The price was very reasonable and we were all very satisfied.
Pretty good food especially salads desserts and belly dancing.

OK, I've been back to this place several times for dining in, and each time had been quite nice. I always get the seafood vindaloo. And wash it down with a salty lassi. The mango lassi is good too if u like sweet. Today i tried the mixed grill tandoori. .. too dry for my taste. I think I'll stick with the vindaloo from now on.

Simply amazing. Went there and was surprised by a group of friends for my bday...def best for groups! The food, the vegetarian meal was awesome ! A little on the expensive side but I'm a college student so it depends! Had a great time with great company

Best mediterranean food you can get in Florida. Great service, beautiful place to bring your family, and fresh food made with a tingle to your tongue. If you want a clean & healthy meal, you can count on Petra. I personally love the mixed grill, you get a great selection of meat, I usually pick hummus and salad. By far my favorite place to eat, COME HERE!!!
Carry out curb side pick up! Awesome dinner/ lunch combinations. Prices are great also! Today I had desert, they make home made rice crispie treats they have to be the best around. They are so yummy!

A hidden Jem!! Let me tell you this place has some Ah-mazing food! I mean everything is just amazingly fresh and simply delicious! The veggies are prepares fresh right in front of you and the meat is so tender, flavorful and spicy!! (Which I love :)) I've tried mostly ever mean on the menu. The rice and beans are awesome and the cucumber scotch salad is just the best! I've been every day since I discovered this place which is buried deep in a not so popular farmers market!

Truly delicious, especially the Captain Crunch tilapia (burrito, over rice, tacos, all incredible)! The people in the truck are always super friendly, quick, and organized. I wish there were some way to cut down on the wait time, though this is definitely one of the most efficient lunch spots around. It's just that popular, and with good reason. Go for a special lunch when you're okay with a long wait. You'll forget all about the wait once you have that amazing food in your mouth!

Excellent carrot ginger dressing salad; one of the best tempura ive ever tasted including dipping sauce. nigiri sushi pieces were small but very fresh and tasty; rice was a bit dry and some were hard as if it was old; but tasty nonetheless. excellent meal overall especially for chinese chefs. looking forward to trying their chinese food. i was salivating at the other diner's chinese dishes. I would definitely come back, perhaps on a regular basis.

Wonderful place. Helpful waitstaff who were easy to relate too. Our waiter was very knowledgable about the food and ingredients - almost as if he must have long discussions with the chef. The food was fantastic - high quality fine dining like. I had one of the vegetarian entrees - a stuffed pepper. It was just really super flavorful. Also had some great appetizers. The kicker was when we ordered coffee after - some of the best French press coffee around. Well done.

Well I hate to knock off one star, but the last few times we've been here the service hasn't been that great. Service was never that good to begin with but the last few times we've visited it's been even worse... so knocking off a star for that. Otherwise the food, ambiance, and prices are still great. We'll still keep eating here and do recommend the place-- just know that the service is probably going to be kind of bad.

The first authentic Thai restaurant in the south of gandy area and still the best. From the appetizers to the main course the authentic Thai cuisine will have you eating yourself silly and be sure to order a Thai iced tea while your in this sweet drink will brighten the mood of the whole table. The decor adds a subtle touch you didn't know was wanted

We walked in and several tables were dirty, not to mention it felt rather humid inside. I mean I get it's a tropical place.... but I don't want to feel the humidity. Lol. I order and found that they were widely backed up with the orders. I don't know if the were understaffed or just busy? It was rough. It's an open kitchen so I could see cooks standing around ‍. The drink area and sauces bar were a mess... obviously because they were busy? After waiting 15 minutes, they started on my order . I got my order 23 minutes after ordering it. ‍. This place needs some help. A for effort?
I love this place! My favorite is the chicken or beef shawarma. And I'm hooked on their TIRAMISU, a must try. The fresh mint lemonade is also amazing!!!

It's good to finally get back to what a real Thai joint is. I must admit, I was apprehensive since I never trust any restaurant, Asian or other, that has multiple cuisines under one roof (Thai...and sushi?). I did not try the sushi, but the duck red curry was fantastic. Crispy duck. Flavorful, real curry. Great service. Authentic decor. Delicious Thai iced tea. Home run.

Authentic Indian flavours and great prices! Tried the aloo paratha, garlic naan, and raita, all of which tasted great. The portions could've been a bit bigger, but I suppose it's fair for the price. Definite value for money. Can't wait to go back!

IMPORTANT NOTE: Their hours have changed, they now close at 3:00 PM This is my go to place for Latin Food. I think the quality of the food is great, they give you a good portion for the money, and the people who work there are very friendly. Great place to go for lunch or supper.

Had the biryani, tandoori chicken, and the chana masala + naan while visiting a friend down here. All was standard and fine. The food wasn't remarkable, but it wasn't inedible either. I'd probably go back again if I was down there and someone asked me to (after I try Cafe Poca Cosa first, though). In any case, Sher Punjab seems like a good, safe bet for Indian in Tucson (I'll have to visit Tucson more often before I can compare it to other Indian joints).

This was one of THE WORST restaurant experiences we have had. We ordered the chicken bahn. Asked for extra sauce twice. Got pathetic looking "sandwiches" filled mostly with cilantro and no sauce. Couldn't swallow even half. Also ordered vegetarian rolls which came with some type of spam like substance in it and the sauce was some kind of smelly, brown chunky gel. The staff could care less about customer service or quality. In looking around as our son finished his pho (which he says was ok), we realized how truly filthy everything was. We already had wiped off our own table before sitting down. We went to several tables first finding them all dirty. Consequently, we watched one of the staff lay food down without wiping the table first forcing the patrons to eat in someone else's mess. It looked like a daycare had gone through the place leaving slobber and who knows what on the walls and glass of the food prep area. Not sure what friends they paid to write good reviews. Here's hoping we didn't get food poisoning.

My wife and I decided to come here because they had some different stuff on the menu, for instance "Chandrakala -White flour dumplings filled with Dry fruits and fresh coconut stir fried" They were very sweet and unappealing as an appetizer. Another dish we also got "Kadai Paneer", and didn't like, claims to have homemade paneer. The paneer was so chewy and terrible that we asked after the meal, and NO they do not make their own Paneer. There are way better places to go for Indian food.

Food was decent for the price. Place is nice looking. However, the biggest downfall was our waiter "Tom Tom". His job is waiter yet he must've thought his job was side show comedian. He was super obnoxious and kept trying to make lame jokes and kept repeating the same joke over and over. The same punch lines to nearly every person in our party of 8. It was really annoying and very distracting to enjoying our meal and have a great time. He was trying way too hard and I literally dreaded every time I saw him approaching our table. If I wanted an eye roll worthy comedy show, I would go to a comedy club, not a waterfront restaurant.

We were just looking for a lunch spot after church and found this Jamaican café on Yelp. Reviews looked good, and we've never tried Jamaican before. They have live jazz at night but it was very quiet at Sunday noon. Only one other table being served when we arrived. Very lovely décor, candle light setting. We skipped the appetizer and ordered our entrees. Wife got a waffle with fried chicken tenders on top. She said the chicken was very good. I went more Caribbean, ordered fish tacos, which came with a mango, avocado, queso fresco, and additional seasonings, also a very savory sauce--some combination of mayo and tomato base--they were fantastic! While we were waiting, they brought us a freshly baked big roll and a pesto sauce that was incredible! Had some pesto left over and our waitress, who is also cook and partner in the business, Erica, put the leftover pesto in a little styrofoam cup to bring home along with the leftover chicken from the missus' meal. I asked and she told me she makes the pesto. They do not have a liquor license, but Erica told me customers can bring their own beer or wine and they will serve it. They do have some distinctly Caribbean drink offerings such as licuados, Jamaican sorrell (hibiscus petals steeped like a tea, with ginger added in), and a number of flavored fruit teas such as mango or pomegranate. I went for the pomegranate. It was super sweet--I normally drink unsweet or barely sweetened tea, but this was really great. We finished lunch off with a bourbon vanilla bean bread pudding. We had to wait a bit longer than expected for it to come to the table, because it was just coming out of the oven. Each pudding is baked in its own personal sized iron skillet, so it arrived sizzling! A couple small scoops of ice cream accompany the pudding. I dug out a hole in the center of my skillet and just plopped the ice cream on top to form a small white lake. Seriously, this pudding is to die for! We will most certainly be back again.

Been craving for banh uot and I honestly must say it's pretty good...I just wish the have varieties of stuffing but meat will do just fine for now. Their sandwiches is pretty good besides the pickles being a little sweet for me....sugar cane was yummy and banh batexo was definitely good, it tastes fresh and the seasoning was perfect.

This place is my Vietnamese jam. I've probably eaten here around 20-30 times now. Enough that the waitress just asks me if I want "Same?" Unfortunately, its hard for me to make many recommendations regarding the menu because I cannot stop getting the same thing over and over and over and over... Thats the #3 BBQ Pork Bahn. This consists of Sweet Salty BBQ pork over rice vermicelli, daikon, cucumber, scallion, mint, peanuts, fried garlic, and house made fish sauce. Add Sriracha to taste, pour the fish sauce on top, stir it all up and pat yourself on the back for being so damn smart as to be eating this delicious dish. The #3 comes with a crunchy egg roll(Summer Roll), but these are not the ubiquitous egg rolls found at so many asian eateries, these are a whole new ballgame. I believe they have ground pork, garlic, fish sauce, carrots, black pepper, wood ear mushrooms, and cellophane noodles. So fricking good and so damn addictive. I dont think I could ever get tired of these things. Food is great, service is.....serviceable but has gotten better as of late. Food comes out promptly now, but don't expect them to warm up to you immediately. Give it time and no hard feelings if they don't offer you a warm southern welcome. Go for the food and remember, CASH ONLY.

Wonderful food! Great service! We are visiting from out of town - wish we lived closer. Paneer Butter Masala had wonderful mild flavor. Samosas also delicious and loved the Masala Chai Tea. Try it! You won't be disappointed.

Hands down, my favorite restaurant I have been to in any city I have traversed to (ie: New York, San Francisco). From the first time I tried it, I was hooked and became a "regular" there (sometimes going twice in one week). The beauty of this restaurant is not only the amazing food (you can't go wrong with any item but my personal favorites are the Greek Salad and Quail) but the hospitality from not only the Head Chef/Owner (who's there and greets every single table), but the whole waiting staff as well. Every single time I go, I always feel at home. I love this place and will always be the first place I go to when visiting Philadelphia. If you're here for a short time, let this be the first thing on your itinerary. Thank you for all the memories! You guys have done a magnificent job :)
So glad to finally have some good Indian cuisine in Wilson County! I will definitely be back here again!

I have eaten here 3 times this month. The com bo luc lac (it's a different name on the menu) is awesome and the prices are fair. I ordered the pho today. The meat did not taste cheap like most Vietnamese restaurants today. I expected the bowl of pho to be small since that's what a lot of these "hip pho restaurants" are doing now and days, but it came out to be really decent portion. The egg rolls are also good. You can add 2 egg rolls to your meal for just $2. It comes with duck sauce. Not a fan of duck sauce, but if you really like egg rolls, you should eat them plain. Service was good. The restaurant is nice and clean.

The food is good and imo better than the other Thai places in the area. They now do deliveries also which is convenient. However they are so popular that on a Saturday evening they have warned us that delivery might take 2 hours. But they tell you when you call so you can either plan accordingly or pick up. As a vegetarian I like that they offer tofu fried or steamed. Usually you only get fried at other places.

This feels sacrilegious, but I can only give Cheu 4 stars instead of the 5 I so badly want to give it. To be clear, many of Cheu's dishes are at least a 5/5 and to this day, it remains one of my favorite restaurants. So why the beef? I've had a number of dishes over time that simply haven't been at the high caliber I expect. Particularly, given my satisfaction at Bing Bing, I'm surprised that many of their dumplings are not as bold and scrumptious. I thought their wings also were good but not great. Now thats off my chest, there is so much cheu does right. Their miso and matzah ramen are staples and should be added to the food pyramid. Follow them on instagram for new menu additions, because some of their specials are unique and unprecedented in true definitions (as opposed to my usual hyperbole). Pro-tip: order takeout!
This is probably my favorite Thai restaurant! Food is amazing and service is great. The place is deceiving you may pass it by driving and not know the true gent it is.

My wife and I took my mother out for dinner for her 89th birthday. She doesn't always want to go out and she's not always interested in eating much so we're very careful where we take her and we always try to find someplace that we would look forward to again. Mom already had her birthday cake at home and balloons and all kinds of things but but my wish is to keep having more good memories and give her a sense of different things so she can try to forget the aches and pains and other things that age brings with it. When I read online about this Blue Plate restaurant and the chef's commitment to his dream of this kind of business where he has this good food and a relationship with local farmers it sounded like a kind of dream worth trying. This was their lunch menu Sunday afternoon it's not huge but on those two pages I knew I want to try every different thing if it was good as it sounded on the menu and believe this was so good not only did the chef have his dream but when I was eating I felt like I was dreaming! Mom loved her pasta dish with sausage. My wife ordered the same thing and added shrimp to it! I had a Rueben with their homemade corn beef mmmmm! (they offered four choices of Rueben's in menu!!! which really surprised me because I'm a big fan of Ruebens!!!! The pumpernickel bread is toasted on the skillet to perfection it was also good!!!! I just wanted to give Mom a good time out and this place is a cute little place but it's so much more than that to come and visit. The hostess waitress came to our table at the end of our visit with a huge mocha chocolate slice of cake with a candle in it Singing Happy Birthday that just topped off our evening she was so gracious and good and the server of beverages.... So attentive, everything is first rate here! Thank you All!

We've driven by Pita Jungle multiple times on our way to Park Place Mall and finally decided to stop in and give it a try the other night. We first ordered the jalapeño cilantro hummus. I could eat a plate of this hummus every day for the rest of my life and never get sick of it. The flavor a were incredible! My husband and I ate it with hot sauce, but our five year old daughter was able to eat it on its own and it wasn't too spicy. We ordered the grilled chicken off of the kid's menu for our daughter and were so impressed when it arrived to the table. There was so much food and it all looked fresh and healthy! Grilled chicken, cooked carrots, potatoes and one other thing that I have now forgotten. She loved it and had enough food to take home for lunch the next day. Words can't even describe how insanely delicious the chipotle lavosh pizza that I ordered was. It was so spicy and loaded full of toppings! My husband ordered the chicken platter and just wasn't in love with it. It came with rice, beans, onions, and garlic sauce. It was yummy, but he loved my pizza much more. My favorite part about this restaurant is how huge the portions are! There's nothing I love more than ordering a great meal at a restaurant and then being able to take it home and have it again the next day. We're looking forward to coming back and trying even more things off of the menu.

Great food, atmosphere, and service. We enjoyed the family style dinner with meat and vegetables. The Ethiopian beer was also nice and refreshing with the meal. We have eaten from Michelin starred restaurants to McDonalds. This food is definitely one of a kind for Tampa and is one of the best restaurants in Tampa. Despite what other reviews say, our food didn't take too long to wait for. But all I have to say is that good food takes time to cook.

Don't be put off by the exterior! We heard about Parisa's and drove up and down the street for a good 15 minutes before we found it, this gem is hidden inside of a very non-descript exterior which advertises hamburger's and breakfast. The food is Iranian, not americanized- but real Iranian food! It is prepared lovingly by a delightful couple who never fail to bring you a sample of something on the menu they think you might like. I have never been to the Saturday buffet, but we have eaten there 4 or 5 times- after trying nearly everything on the menu, my favorite is Kabob-e-joojeh (chicken kabob), but I can't say I was unhappy with anything that I had there. This is, in my opinion, the ONLY truly middle eastern restaurant in Reno- make sure you try it at least once

I come here to eat pho special every week. All the servers are nice and helpful. Joe is always chilled and easy going. Food wise, the broth is quite clear yet a bit on the plain side. The portions are very satisfying. The Vietnamese sandwich （meat lover）are on par with some of the best I've tasted. Nothing goes wrong with it. Overall, a decent place to meet your desire for Vietnamese food.

This is the first Ethiopian restaurant that I've had since moving from Atlanta, Georgia. I have to say back home we have the benefit of a more diverse population, so we have quite a few places to pick from-they carry more sauces like Awaze and some even have breakfast! The one thing I've noticed in all of the Ethiopian restaurants I've tried is the kitchen staff is a family, so these family recipes differ a little bit from one to another. I would've preferred a little more garlic and maybe a few more menu options, but the meal definitely satisfied my Ethiopian fix. The older lady who runs/owns the shop was so sweet and had amazing customer service even on New Year's eve. I ordered gomen, (collard greens), miser (lentil soup) and kitfo (seasoned ground beef) and they were all pretty good. Originally, I wanted shiro instead of the collard greens, but they were out. Maybe you should call in advance for that one, since the side is considered a delicacy in their culture. Good experience overall. Hopefully in the future they'll add fish and a few more veggies to their menu :)
Cubano is fantastic, pork cooked to perfection coated in cheese and amazing in-house mustard. Good guac, heavy on garlic and cilantro but not too creamy or chinky.

Loved, loved, loved this place! Spinach pie and hummus appetizers were wonderful! The tomato basil Florentine soup was out of this world (especially when enjoyed with a garlic knot). Friends really enjoyed the traditional and chicken gyros while I sat in reverent bliss savoring the obvious and subtle flavors of a Persian lamb kabob on a green salad. Outstanding! The last pieces of our feast were the chocolate mousse, tiramisu and baklava which we paired with fresh, strong coffee. I was surprised that we ordered at the counter; but, everything was brought out to the table to us. Customer service was welcoming, attentive and informative. Everything about our experience was terrific - just great.

I have not dined at the smiling elephant but my office folks ordered some for our monthly meeting. I did order some fried rice. It was good but not as spicy as I expected it to be. Rest of the colleagues said the food tasted good. They are pretty good. I cannot say much about it. I will update my review soon as I have a plan of going to this place.
We only had drinks, but it is worth stating that the bartenders were awesome! Very friendly and fun to talk to. Made for a nce evening. Thank you!

Food was decent, but does not stand up to the Smile Cafe - Erawan standard. The drunken noodle was flavorful but quite greasy. The pad thai was good. Very courteous staff. Will definitely return if Smile Cafe is closed.
Great vibe! Cool gastro lounge on beach drive! Great people watching spot inside or out! Dog friendly and super music! Wednesday night is 1/2 off appetizers - just bring a lady!
Lunch...had the $6 eggplant Thai Basil with seaweed soup. Outstanding value and taste! Will be back for dinner. Excellent service, too.

This is my favorite Indian place in town! A great selection of dishes, favorites that many folks will recognize and the wonderful addition of many (really tasty) dishes that the typical Indian buffet in America doesn't serve. Service here has always be great. And be sure to ask for Dosa at your table, in addition to or as an alternative to the standard naan. My particular favorite is Mysore Masala Dosa (spicy potato stuffed dosa).

If you like the smooth creamy texture of Palaak Paneer, do NOT order it here. The paneer has small chunks of diced ginger and pods of spices. I found the texture off putting, and would not order again. I've had the tiki masala before and that was good. So will go towards meat if you go here and the garlic naan is good.
Just about every restaurant in New Orleans have amazing food. they use just the right spices to dazzle your taste buds. I highly recommend....

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Waited almost 2 hours for a to-go order. Got home and they forgot the appetizer I ordered. Good was subpar consider I no the dishes are almost $20 a pop.

Wow an incredible lunch spot!! The owner is very hands on and personally makes all the food with his wife. It's clean, authentic and top notch middle eastern cuisine. I highly recommend this family friendly establishment. I got the chicken kabob platter and it was amazing!!

Honestly, one of the best buffets I've been to. I'll be back in Indy at Christmas, and I'll be sure to make a stop! It's pretty standard Indian fare, but it tastes extremely fresh. This place is definitely the best Indian I've had in Indy!

Pleasantly surprised by this little gem located in SoBro. Both management and staff were friendly and tentative. The food arrived at our table piping hot. I had pork tacos with black beans and green rice. Yes the rice was green and it was an explosion of flavors. I'm so glad my husband and I stumbled upon this place. I can say we will be regulars.
Really great fresh food, great service, owners so friendly & welcoming. This will definitely be our regular place for Indian food.

This place was delicious! We had a few different appetizers and everything was delicious. The dumplings were so good! I had the green curry, which was so flavorful. I got to try the Thai beef noodle bowl and that might be my next order. The staff is very friendly and the restaurant is beautiful. The menu has everything and they even have a vegan menu.

The Yelp reviews led me here and was not disappointed. Elegant, comfortably atmosphere, friendly staff. I ordered the eclat chocolate, delicious. Very fresh ingredients which makes eating a pleasure. I also started to order coffee and then when looking up at the menu, noticed the chai latte and changed my mind. Again, not disappointed. Fresh ingredients made with attention to detail. I will return when in the area.

Zagol is delicious, relaxed, definitely not a chain, and not too expensive for the rarity of the flavors. It was a lovely surprise to find it. The restaurant is spacious and very colorfully decorated. Parking was easy. The woman who served us was genuinely warm and very attentive for being the one woman operating the entire floor. My friend and I chose a beef and chicken dish, which was served over a huge plate of delicious injera. A salad came with the meal. Everything tasted fresh and rich. The spice balanced pleasantly with the amazing cottage cheese. After digging in greedily with our hands, the meal was gone and we were both comfortably full. The Ethiopian beer was a nice touch. The baklava wasn't exceptional, but the rest of the meal was so much fun to eat and so delicious that I'm not put off at all.

We came for my wife's birthday. We sat in the mezzanine. The lady serving forgot one of the seven plates we ordered and gave us a free cocktail to make up for it. Every dish was amazing. The dessert was fantastic. The coffee and cocktails were outstanding. This is a must try if only for the whipped feta and the gnocchi.

Been there three times. First time wasn't so bad, second time took my son and his fiancé and my wife. We all ordered at the same time but we all are at different times. The kitchen couldn't get our food out together. On a $150 bill I was a little disappointed. Manager caught wind of our issue through FB and told us to come back and drop her name and they would take care of us so we did just that. The food took 45 mins and was cold. The reason was they forgot we were there and bypassed our order to serve later customers. The poor waitress didn't get to find out I tip in $20 intervals meaning if the service is great I'll throw an extra twenty on top of the tip. I appreciate good hard working employees and waitressing isn't easy at all. Underrated really. There's some guest that grace restaurants with eating at those establishments. It's bad for business when you can't meet a basic standard. Our standard is high. This restaurant is not to par. Sound "Snooty"? No. Basic expectations aren't Snooty and if a person considers it snooty then it shows how low the standard is for them. It's ok to expect your food within 45 mins. Of ordering. It's ok to expect the food to all come out at same time. It's a gamble to eat at Sams. Gamble my people won't take again.
This place has delicious food! The serving is hefty and well worth the $14 for the medium - I had the oxtails, beans & rice and cabbage. the service was nice and warm. I will be going back! Loved it!
Wow . Thank you for the 20 5 star review because this would be the last place I would look for great Thai food. Simply delicious and amazing .

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Some of the reviews have mentioned how long it takes, and you should listen to them. We sat down at 7pm and ordered two vegetarian dishes and by 8pm there was still nothing coming from the kitchen. The restaurant only had a couple other tables filled, it was mostly empty. When I complained, the owner talked to me and said they make everything from scratch. I get that, that's fine with me, but at least tell me when I sit down that it will take a couple hours so I can leave and never come here again. We sat back down and five minutes later the owner came out to tell us our order was just being started, after an hour! We told him forget it and left. I mean, making each meal from scratch may take a while, but it takes even longer when you don't actually start preparing the food for an hour. They need to fire the cook and get somebody back there who knows how to run a kitchen. So, I haven't actually tried the food, but if you read some of the other reviews for this restaurant, neither have some of the other reviewers, for the same reason. I can't believe this restaurant is still in business. Three tables filled and we have to wait over and hour for some indian food? That's not a recipe for success. Plus it's expensive, $7 for a mango lassi, are you serious? $15 for a vegetarian entree? It's too much. I'm glad we left, we ended up going to Sawadee in Meridian, and it was awesome.
What's not to like, the food and drinks are good, the service shows the staff are treated well. Love being a repeat customer here.

So many asian fusion places popping up in this city, unfortunately this one is not one of the best ! It has a wide ranging menu from Vietnamese to Thai, taco's what not, but, overall food was average. Flavors of asian cuisine were scarce to say the least . Owner spent a good amount of money on the ambience( a bit gaudy) to have it qualified for a fusion restaurant , but, still doesn't get the score right. Service was slow and mediocre. The shrimp fried rice is definitely a must at this place , rest of the items were sub-standard . Hopefully, Reno starts getting some restaurants that stay true to its cuisine !

Finally had the chance to check out the infamous "falafel cart Nazi" at 20th and Market. What an experience! If you're not familiar, this guy has been in this area for close to 10 years, maybe longer, and he has a reputation for making high end restaurant quality meals with whatever he's got in the cart that day. There's no menu. No alterations, unless you want all veg. No bag. No utensils. Just the ridiculous meal (about 2 lbs. of food), all for $10. Today, he had fresh made turmeric semolina pasta in a slightly sweet and spicy sauce that I can't quite pinpoint is the base, with freshly grilled chicken, the most perfect falafel, grilled peach, strawberries, grapes, and sprouts / micro greens. The balance of flavors and textures from the platter blew me away. The sweetness from the sauce and fruits on the front end is brought back a bit when the spices from the falafel and chicken and the smokiness from the charred bits from the grilled chicken and peach kick in. What a meal (honestly, two meals), for $10! Also, if you plan on checking out his cart make sure you have a little extra time because there will be a line, and he only makes one platter per person at a time.

I have no end of superlatives for this place. I had seen it on my very rare trip to this near ghost town of a mall. If anything could save it, I believe it will be the lovely Phan and her kickass flavorful egg rolls, food and hospitality that made us feel as though we were in her kitchen at home. We had the pork egg rolls to start, as per her suggestion. I think they are the best I have had in Indy perhaps ever, and I lived in Asia. The pork blend was incredibly flavorful on its own, but a healthy amount of black pepper with the vegetables made it fantastic, and they were perfectly fried, crisp and not too greasy. I could literally eat my weight of these, twice. My boyfriend had a red curry, which was a perfect blend of coconut and curry and didn't overwhelm the vegetables, it was fragrant and delicious. I had the Pad Prik (?) spice level 5. It was delicious, savory and spicy and fresh with loads of fresh Thai eggplant. Phan was very concerned the spice would overwhelm me, and when it didn't she offered us Kim-chee on the house and chatted with us like we were in our house. I cannot wait to try the Pho and the Laotian curry soup that are weekend specials. Go there now!

We went for Sunday Brunch, highly recommended. They take reservations which was great for us since we were a group of 7. This was my favorite restaurant in Nashville. I had the breakfast burrito and I have been craving another one ever since! But really, I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu! The service was great, a little slow but it was a busy Sunday morning. I'm looking forward to the next time I am in town so I can try it for dinner!

On the original advice of my Chinese file clerk, after hearing my woes of finding great Pad Thai in downtown Philadelphia, she told me to head to Panang. I would have never considered a Malaysian restaurant for my favorite noodle dish. Indeed their Pad Thai is great, and the price is less than $10, which further makes it so addictive. I also love their Chow Kueh Teow and often order both dishes for take-out. I've also been and had some of their more unique dishes, often denoted by "ask your server" on the menu. My boyfiend and I are quite adventurous in our eating styles, so nothing was too scary or weird for us. That said, you really have nothing to fear. My boyfriend enjoyed their curry dishes as his main, and I stuck to my usual. Perhaps its the Leo in me that is quite loyal, but I cannot go to Penang and not have their Pad Thai or Chow Kueh Teow. It is just that good.
I prefer Baba ganoush on the smokey side but this one was very good! Fresh and tasty. Ordered the mixed grill, very good too! Good amount of food. I'll be coming back!

This used to be my favorite restaurant in the city, but a couple of months ago it started to deteriorate starting with the mango lassi. We just visited again and it is now called Mayuri. The (buffet) dishes overall are lacking the flavor that Ruchi once served, and even the naan was unappetizing. What a loss. They still have the best variety of Indian desserts though.

We ate Sunday Brunch there and I promise I saw angels and heard harps playing. The chorizo omelette was THE BEST omelette I have ever had.... so creamy... so smooth... so perfect. The potatoes were also heavenly. We've had dinner there previously and that's what brought us back for more. Everything about their food is wonderful! And, trust me, my hubby is a fabulous cook and we both love to eat, so we KNOW good food. Seriously, there is ABSOLUTELY no reason you should not go to this place immediately!!!!!!!!
Very good Pho and a nice quiet, but busy, place. Could be a little more prompt with drink refills but overall very much worth the trip.

Summary: Unfriendly server/host, frozen vegetables used and sub-par tikki masala sauce. Naan was excellent. Host was very awkward, unfriendly, seemed miserable/borderline angry and stared through my soul like the grim reaper. Seems like kids were running the place..Horrible first impression. Two diners, we ordered tikki masala and vegetable korma. Tikki sauce was too thick, sweet and tasted like it was store bought. 6 chunks of chicken for $15?? Rice wasn't flavorful at all. Tasted like long grain white rice. Vegetable korma tasted like frozen vegetables that had been reheated. Naan was excellent--only reason I'm giving 2 stars. Maybe lunch buffet is better?

Can't beat it! The huge selection of lassi's are outstanding (fig lassi mmmm...) and the samosas are great, but the real thing to come here for is Hassan and his chaats. Chaat is kind of hard to describe. It's a South Indian street food that is a medley of a whole bunch of things: crunchy noodles and puffed rice, dried fruits and nuts, chutneys and sauces, and other things. There's a menu of about 15 different varieties, but Hassan is always helpful and will make you exactly what you want. So much love for this place!

Souvlaki, tzatziki, feta in olive oil, crispy fries, heirloom tomatoes ... order at the counter and seat yourself, or enjoy a full service bar. There's an outside dining option in the newly established gravel garden with a large wall mural and olive trees in containers. Plenty of parking. Cool staff. Greek owners. Kitchen in full view. I became a fan day one. And the octopus is the most delicious I've tasted outside of Greece.

Cannot say enough nice things about this place! We've been to the lunch buffet a number of times and the food is always fresh and delicious. Often you'll find the wife of the chef waiting tables-- she's delightful. We get a kick out of the Indian cooking shows on the TV and the music is great. Make sure you save room for desserts, they're first rate.

So we found our way back here now 3 months later after my previous review. The wife and I chose to eat here(vice carry out) this time and it was a little after noon. It was quite loud and there were a lot of people here, but that shouldn't come as a shock given the time of day and proximity to the base. Big menu, but we chose the BBQ pork noodle soup(her) and the chicken pad see ew(me). I really liked my pad see ew and ended up eating the whole plate. It was a pretty decent amount of food that I didn't think I'd be able to finish. My wife had the same thing she had the last time we came here, and still loved it. Our total pre tip with two soft drinks came to $25. Not a bad place at all. I believe we'll be back again, either after the lunch rush or picking up takeout.

I inquired about there only being three pieces of meat on my $7.95 gyro sandwich and was told that's how it is. The manager had no desire to improve that situation. In fact he told me they used to put four pieces on. It tastes great but the value is not there. I'll be going else where for gyros. Most of the other items are fine, just disappointed on the gyro. The place at the Park Place Mall gives enough meat for two gyros for $6.95. Ask for another pita and you can feed two people.

The dining area seemed like a pleasant place to dine and chat, but I chose to get take out for my first experience. I ordered the Sambosas- delicious with a spicy dipping sauce, good portion for the price. I also got Chicken Tikka Masala- the sauce was OK, but the chicken chunks were delicious. I ordered a side of Naan that was pretty standard. Next time I will be trying the kabobs. The chicken was the stand out of this meal and it had been cooked on skewers, so I have to try more. My meal was a little over $20, so next time I will also make sure to go during the lunch buffet (Thurs-Sat) for $8.99/person.
The curry is soupy. The pad thai is too salty/saucy. I like that they have a lunch menu special, but it feels like they're catering to the "American" palate.

Had the place to myself. Of course that's what happens when you eat a late lunch. Ordered the lamb gyro. It's more like a gyro salad. It was piled so high on the pita that there was no way to pick it up and eat it without making a terrible mess. But that was okay. It was a good mix of meat and lettuce onions n sauce. I really likes the sauce. It came with homemade chips on the side although not really enough but then again there wasn't really enough room on the plate! So I ordered extra chips. Service was good...how could it not be? I was the only one there. They should really get new plates. The ones they have are wooden and are showing ware. Will definitely come back again.

Update: this is still my boyfriend and I's top sushi place. It's our go to. They've got us hooked, line and sinker with the blue crab tempura roll, spicy crawfish roll ( they brought it back!!!), and various other rolls. Their service has always been quick every time we've gone and the waitresses know us by heart! They even customized a dish for us when we asked about udon stirfry which they didn't have but gladly substituted in the udon with a similar stirfry dish! Small detail that I like about the sushi here is that it's rolled nice and tight and firm. Some other sushi places, the rolls are rolled loosely and the rice and filling just crumble so easily. It's the small things!

Best Asian/Chinese in St. Louis hands down! I'm glad this place opened up in Florissant. Everytime I come back, the family and I have to visit this place. My favorite items are the fried gizzards (best seasoning), jerk chicken anything, and the philly cheese wontons. My wife always gets a St. Paul sandwich, either the Ultimate or the Angry Bird. The kids get the typical - fried rice, crab rangoons, and wings. All in all, everything are must-haves. The owners are friendly. They are a husband and wife team. The place have always been busy on weekend nights but they always get it right and serve fast.

Just stopped here for some lunch. Everyone there was very friendly and the food came out super fast. I had the combo Pho and it was delicious.
