If I lived in the area I would make this a weekly stop for sure. The broth was fantastic. After trying the combo, it was the rare flank that I would choose to have again. Very tender.

This is without question one of the best kept secrets west of Manitoba! The food is consistently great and believe me I have eaten here more times than I can remember! Hand made pita, best lamb sirloin I've ever had and this place knows how to cook a steak! The prawns are to die for and the value for money is outstanding! I eat here at least once every time I come to Edmonton. The rice pudding is delicious and the baclava has the right amount of syrup. Tried the tuna the other night and left me thinking what can't this guy cook!!! The lahmacun is a must try period! Yuksel the owner /head chef puts a great deal of love and passion into his food...I love this place! Lastly, the service is consistently great with the staff ready to help with any questions u have regarding the unique Turkish cuisine.

I went twice with my friend and I as we are Busch Garden cardholders (literally like this restaurant is visible from "Monti" the roller coaster)! We decided to check this place out and my! do they have such great customer service! The owner gives us free samples and makes us feel so welcomed which is absolutely wonderful! The prices are incredible 20 wings for $10! Such an amazing deal! We are definitely going to come here and try more things on the menu! Very generous with the food and excellent with the customer service. Also, it has a drive-thru which is AHHH-summmm! I am definitely a fan! Oh and by the way- supper clean placee with awesome shakes and good looking dessert that I cannot seem to buy because they put me so much food that I leave so frikkin stuffed!!!!

I've been going to Sister Muhammad's for a very long time. Before the remodel, and they've always had GREAT food. The best Fish sandwich/hoagie in Philadelphia hands down... I give it 4stars because not only is the food good, it's clean, service is good, and did I say they have the Best Fish Hoagie in Philadelphia?

This tastes like what McDonald's would try to pass as Thai food. I swear their curry had corn syrup in it. It was way off and like no other Thai food I've eaten- in a bad way. Also, as another reviewer said, the restaurant smells odd and the water tastes strange. Just very disappointed. Stick with King and I when on S. Grand.
Everything I've had here has been great. You can't go wrong with their Pho soups. Hope to be back soon.!

Conveniently located across from Busch Gardens, this fast food Mediterranean restaurant serves some yummy falafel Sammie's! Made fresh so you can customize. Comes with hummus if you like and Mediterranean style pickles. Also got a Greek salad that I saved for later consumption. Kareem is a jokester and kept me laughing while taking order. They serve up all kinds of chicken and shawarma type dishes as well.
Very happy I found this place! I love Indian cuisine. In this area, this is some of the best. Chicken tikka masala, paneer masala, gobi 65. All incredibly well done. Best Indian since California!

I hate leaving a bad review, but maybe I can save someone else's night out. First, it's so loud in here when it's crowded that unless you're skilled in lip reading you won't be able to have a conversation with the people you are with. The squid appetizer was so heavily battered that you can't taste the actual squid. Everyone else's dishes were so-so and too spicy. We had the honey butter chicken, crab watermelon salad and sweet potato side. Staff was nice though!

Just one word: authentic, just like you would find in a restaurant, market or street stall in Thailand or Laos. Recomend the laos style papaya salad, (made correctly with fermented fish), beef jerky, larb nuea. We didn't order from the menu, we just told the one of the owners what we wanted, a mixture of Thai and Laos dishes, delicious(seap) and a good value. Couple that with BYOB, outside table service, it makes for great dining experience. The service comes straight from the owners, with warmth and from the heart. If you are weary of self-important posers that wait on you in other resaurants, then head here. Tired of watered down Asian food, then head to Vientiane Cafe. My wife was born near Vientiane and has a culinary degree from Suan Dusit in Thailand, and she was so happy that I brought her here, because after a year, we finally found a restaurant that has food that is as good as what we can make at home!

Thought we were going to a nice restaurant, but the overall feel was douchey club. Jimmy was a great server, the food was on point, but the whole vibe was very douchetastic. There was a 4 year old sitting at the bar. I'm not kidding. He may have been 3. Seems like they cater to douchebags and whores. Too bad because the food is good, and at least Jimmy is a good server.

Admittedly I don't write reviews typically. However this place a gem! I've been here twice now and both experiences were excellent. My girlfriend and baby boy went there tonight for Mother's Day and once again the staff was as friendly as can be! The ambience is amazing (both inside and out on the patio). For anyone looking to have a romantic dinner or quiet outing with a few friends I highly suggest the patio on the side. Last but not lease the food is excellent as well, and for as classy a joint as this is, very moderately priced. For what it's worth my girlfriend and I both are calling Pan D'Olive our favorite restaurant in STL!

This place is very nicely decorated and the food is excellent ! It's a seven course menu so make sure you come with an empty stomach !! Great ambiance ! I'll definitely be back- I wish they had one in NYC !

Iris Bay, this place is the jam! I've read some of the bad reviews and can understand where they are coming from. I've eaten a couple sub par meals here but overall this place is great! At least we know it's real home cooking! The curry goat is fire! And the older woman working is my girl. Always have a good laugh with her! And just remember don't worry, about a thing!

I just woke up and want this shit for breakfast. My go to Thai, they can accommodate to veganism really easily and are super nice about it. The waitress is such a sweetheart and always the same girl. She's super quick to serve you and always deserves a wonderful tip! Just remember the hours cause they're kinda odd and I often go on the wrong days. Overall, wonderful place and great food.
This a great Moroccan restaurant in Philly! Very authentic food and atmosphere! Set course menu with large portions, great for a group.

We really enjoy this place. Wonderful flavors and aromas from this food. Service is usually excellent. The buffet on the weekend is a good value and a great way to try new things. Highly recommend. BTW - butter chicken is yummy!

This is great Thai! We tried it because it was close to our house and it's worth a drive folks! We tried the crab ragoon (delish! Super crispy and loaded full), the chicken pad Thai and the red curry. Meals were great, fresh, right spice levels. Also got some of the ginger tea and that stuff was yum. We will be back. Thank you!

Delicia is one of the gems of SoBro. Not only is the food very good, but the cocktails are amazing. They don't have very much selection in the way of beer, but after you've had the Fire & Ice drink it's clear why. As others have already stated, the duck enchiladas are fabulous. The prices are a little on the higher side, especially the cocktails, but not bad at all considering everything about this place feels high-end. This is more of a date night spot than an every day place. I can't speak to the breakfast options as I've only been here for dinner.

I really wanted to give a 5 star review and on some of the dishes I can but others were average and others a bit below. The sausage and broccoli rabe was very good, clearly housemade. The sardines were huge and nicely grilled. The lemon pasta, the reason I was so excited to go, was awful! The delicate homemade noodles were completely lost in what appeared to be straight lemon juice! The seafood stew with a Moroccan vibe was delicious and the bass was ok. The almond pannacotta was light and lovely but the zeppoli were large and really just sweet. It's a lovely little place, very friendly and helpful staff but tiny and with really hard, uncomfortable chairs (maybe a way to move diners along to make room for the next batch). When our check came we were told that the credit card machine was down and they could only accept cash. Would have been nice to know BEFORE we ordered almost $200 worth of food.

I wish that the consistency would be a lot better. I first went to Spice Kitchen during the grand opening and the experience was pretty bad (hour plus long wait plus food that was not fully cooked) . I usually give places one second chance before crossing them off the list. The second visit was almost perfect, the Kashmiri Chicken was one of the best dishes i have ever eaten at any Indian restaurant. Unfortunately, during my last visit of ordering the same dish, It had the wrong gravy (It had a strong fenugreek aroma) very sour and the Peshwari naan's taste was like licking a salt lick. It seem like the food quality depends on if the head chef is at your location when you dine there. Spice Kitchen has three locations btw. This place could be amazing with better quality control/ consistency.

Neat, fast and great tasting. Had a very delightful lunch with the wife here the other day. The service was quick, correct and very good in taste. The Tziki sauce was well done. Had good options in regards to meat. Just like a Chipotle kind of concept but locally owned and operated. Try them out!

I went here for the lunch buffet. As I have experienced with many lunch buffets, this one is honestly just bad. I think the ingredient of the year here is water. The chicken curry left a small pool of water on my plate. The "sauce" was washed away by the water. The kheer also had way too much water. I have to say the naan was the saving grace at this restaurant and was quite good.

Teeny-tiny BYOB, tight quarters for dining indeed (is this the reason behind it not taking reservations?), especially if you're eating at the bar tables by the windows. Teeny-tiny tables with teeny-tiny wine glasses. Had to put bottles of wine practically on the floor because it wouldn't fit on the table. They barely fit our dishes, water glasses and wine by dinner time... Came in around 7:45 and waited about an hour at New Wave before we got a table... Small price to pay for good food you say? Meh. The food was good, not outrageous-pump-your-fists-in-the-air good. Simple flavors and seasonings - I wasn't pumping my fists. I was Meh. Had a few of the small dishes. Shrimp Pil-Pil stood out. Had the Ciopinno steam seafood combo. Broth was decent, seafood was good - but shrimp were tasteless and rubbery as was the calamari... Tasted the escarole and rice accompanying the scallop dishes (and the other dishes too, I presume) and it was a resounding bland meh- both needed salt - and god almighty - some Oomph - somewhere - please - although the scallops (both grilled and pan-fried) were pretty tasty. Still... an overall resounding Meh it my book. Had dessert, meh once more with the almond cake (other picks were rice pudding and a flan - Yawn!), looked sloppy - tasted alright. Served turkish coffee - in gasp! - coffee mugs. Service was hurried, but pleasant. Always refilled the water. They didn't rush us out of there after we were finished and let us drink our bottle of iced wine and gave us new teeny-tiny glasses with which to drink.

High prices for what it is. I got a chicken salad and it was terrible. SOAKED in dressing with some gross dark meat chicken on it. Also got a pita that was very mediocre and also drenched in salty sauce. Won't be back!

My sisters, my parents, my sort-of boyfriend and I came here for dinner after a nice evening stroll in Tower Grove Park. We ran into a ton of dinner choices on this street, a kind of Berkeley or Santa Cruz-esque strip in the middle of St. Louis. There was an Afghan joint, I believe some Iraqi, the lovely Pho Grand, another Thai place. But ultimately we settled on Basil Spice. I got pad kee mao with pork, my sister got pad kee mao with chicken, and my dad got - you guessed it - pad kee mao with shrimp. We weren't that creative, but at least we picked a good dish. Our food showed up piping hot, fresh-tasting, and very spicy. I guess they are true to their name. I had to keep sipping water to make to make the faint burn go away - maybe I'm a pansy - but that's a good thing as far as I'm concerned. My other sister got something so spicy it caused her to remark, "I'm too white for this shit." Finally, the boy's creamy kang pa nang was delicious, with just the right amount of sweetness. I caught him licking the plate. We left with full hearts and tummies. The End.

This place has pretty good food for a decent price and it's close to my house. Sold. As some other yelpers have said, the atmosphere is a little ...off, so I prefer to get it to go. It's very casual, to say the least. It's very open and usually quiet/empty, so you almost feel like you're intruding on the employees when dining in. Each time I've dined in we've been the only occupied table. It's a little awkward. And the TV on the wall is always playing pop music videos... The menu is limited, but the hummus, salad, homemade chips and "yee-ro" (as they call it) are all pretty good. I saw a sign the other day that they have added falafel to the menu - it's about time! The staff has always been very friendly and helpful. One employee recognized us and somehow remembered that a few weeks before we had ordered the same thing and brought us samples of a couple of different things to try while we waited. Hopefully she just has a really good memory and they don't just have that few customers! The menu seems to keep growing and it seems to be getting more popular, so I may have to reevaluate after my next visit!

I first heard of Spice Kitchen after visiting their original location in Trooper, PA (which is closer to my parent's house so I went there pretty frequently). Since moving close to the Lansdale area, I heard they opened their second location recently and was anxious to try it since I had a good experience at the other location. I invited my non-Indian friend (who loves Indian food)with me since she and I have been wanting to explore a new Indian restaurant together for awhile. Since this was going to be the last time I see her before she moves, I decided to pick one of my favorite North Indian restaurants and hope the experience would be just as good if not better than their other restaurant location. One negative right away is the fact that after plugging the address into my GPS it took me to the intersection of Forty-Foot Rd and Allentown Rd...since there was a shopping center near there, I decided to trust my instincts it would be in there. I drove around and most of the shops were empty, so I almost was going to turn around. Fortunately, my friend got there a few minutes before me and I called her and she helped me find the restaurant since it was not labeled/listed on the shopping center sign from the entrance I came in from.Upon arriving we were greeted by a very personable and bubbly blonde haired American woman (whose name I later found out is Johanna). She really brings the restaurant to life with her charm, stories, and sense of humor as she keeps you entertained throughout your meal as she frequently checks in on the guests in the restaurant. (A definite positive to keep me coming back here), can't believe she's only been there for less than a year - she makes you feel like family and is a natural at what she does. A true gem at this restaurant. The ambiance is small and charming with a classy interior design, perfect for a quick get together during the week for dinner with friends, date nights, or family outing. We sat down and shortly after we got settled in, an Indian gentleman, named Mr. Sharma came to our table and brought us papadam that came with 3 assortment of chutneys - most other Indian restaurant in the area don't do this - so bonus to this location! He was very nice as well and personally took the time to meet each guest it seemed like him and Johanna have been working for years together, they are quite the entertainment with their funny comments flowing back and forth throughout the night. My friend who came with me is a vegetarian and found it easy to pick something off the menu with a large selection of options to chose from. She ended up getting the Kashmiri Dum Aloo, and aloo tikka chaat as an appetizer. I, being a Punjabi (North Indian) was craving my favorite, chicken tikka masala (which comes with rice) and I decided to split some fresh naan with my friend. The food came out without waiting too long although one mistake that occurred (which is minor - and my friend didn't make a big deal about) was that her dinner came out before her appetizer. The portions were definitely generous (another reason I would come back) - because not only can you enjoy the meal in the restaurant, chances are you will have enough to take home for lunch/dinner the next day. We both thoroughly enjoyed our meal. I thought the chicken tikka masala was perfectly cooked, in the rich tomato, buttery gravy with aromatic spices. I enjoyed it with the rice and also ordered a side of raita since I always eat Indian food at home with some sort of yogurt on the side for digestive purposes to calm any sort of spice level. The restaurant was nice and cooked the food to my tolerable spice level which was another personable touch I liked. The only thing I wish was since this was the first time I was there - I was a little taken aback when I was charged for the raita when my bill came. Usually, for something small like that I thought it would be complimentary to gain my repeat business in the future, oh well. As our evening was wrapping up, Mr. Sharma brought us some boxes to wrap up our leftovers, although I do suggest instead of just assuming styra-foam would be sufficient to pack the dinner, Mr. Sharma was kind enough upon special request to dig up some Tupperware since I did have some of the raita and chicken tikka masala to wrap up without wasting any of the delicious food by using styrafoam alone. I really wanted to get the rasmali for dessert, but I figured I would try it out the next time I came in. Before leaving since it was a special goodbye dinner planned with my friend, the staff was super nice to take some pictures of us and then I even had Johanna get in a picture with me too for the memories. The staff really goes above and beyond for their guests to make it a enjoyable experience. Overall, the prices were reasonable, and I left the restaurant with a positive impression - and can't wait to bring my family here to try some new dishes together from our native region. Good job, Spice Kitchen Lansdale!

Good. Not amazing or anything, but good. Ask for a booth and enjoy the intimate setting. Service was above average. The wine list was moderately priced. We had four different good dishes. The trout - good. The lobster ravioli - very good. Seafood linguini - good. The cannelloni - good. The desert sampler - good. Overall, good. We'll go back after checking out the rest of the neighborhood.

I had a pretty tough time locating the place. Thankfully went back to the reviews and read that it was INSIDE the farmers market. The farmers market in itself has eclectic stores. After a while walking around the market, I found Masala Kitchen. I had Sev Puri that was awesome - spicy and flavorful. The Mothichoor ladoo was the yummiest ladoo I have had in a loong time! I'm not a great fan of sweets but I had two of them!

Food was delicious. Been awhile since ive had good indian food. Had chicken tikka masala, vegetable biryani, vegetable samosa and garlic naan. All was great and made with care. Definately a place ill be returning too again and again. The rice was very good. Good job
Great food at an affordable price best pho around! Huge many with many options to try.

The boyfriend was craving a freshly squeezed sugar cane drink so I googled a place and found Seasons Cafe. He was so happy and really liked the sugar cane drink that we had to go back the next day to grab 2 more just for him. I tried the pomegranate flavored iced tea with no sugar and it still had minimal sweetness to it. It was really good too.
Friendly and welcoming staff. Food was very good and flavorful. Tom yum soup was easily one of the best I had.

Delicious and perfect. My friend and I went and brought two bottles of wine. We ordered all food and desserts to share. Service was great. Food was delicious. Space was tight, but that was expected. I wouldn't suggest this place for a large party but for a small intimate meal with friend or family, it's perfect :)
OK Pho, really all i have had there. I think the biggest thing is the portion is not big enough for the price. But i have Pho in WC, can not beat that.
Great sandwiches for cheaper than average prices in Manayunk!

David and I stopped in for dinner on a Friday night. We decided to do take away instead of eating at the restaurant. The food was very good, we had a combination appetizer and the giro platter. The giro was our favorite. Portions are generous! Go hungry!

Well for starters the service was non existent no one came to even refill waters after being there for 30+ mins and not even the egg rolls had come out yet. I watched three tables get up and leave due to no food and messed up orders. Maybe I'll try again in a month when they figure out how service works.

Don't let it freak you out, but the goat is amazing! I had the "lunch" special. For $9 I also had black beans, a huge portion of yellow rice, and a canned diet coke. Pretty legit Latin cuisine for being in the heart of Philly!

I have been to Thailand numerous times, this place is OKAY. They consistently drop the ball on authenticity/flavor for quite a few of their dishes, including pad Thai, which is sad. It's not terrible food, it's okay tasty, but it's not anywhere close to the flavor of Thailand that I'm looking for. If you're looking for authenticity, go to Tong Phoon in Fairview Heights. Much better and actually cheaper....and.....AUTHENTIC!
Didn't love my experience the day I went. Smaller portions and inattentive staff. Will have to try again one day.

Great food when I got to try it. Their vietnamese dishes are just as good as their Chinese dishes! Hard of understanding the service when they speak English but they try hard and its still soooo good! Must try!

It's the perfect neighborhood gem -- inexpensive, fresh, and great-tasting. They make the curry, fresh, every day. If you've ever made your own curry, you know that it is 100x better than any of the jarred paste or anything you are getting at other generic, run-of-the-mill Thai places. This stuff is bursting with flavor. So go and enjoy real food. I also had a minced pork dish, which was also great. My only complaint? The dishes are too small! I had rice everywhere.

We had a group of six for dinner Friday night. We were a talkative bunch and took our time catching up and having drinks before ordering food. Timmie the manager came by our table to make sure everything was going well and to give us some ordering advice. Timmie knew his menu in and out...ingredients, the cooking process for each dish, and the source and freshness of the seafood. Timmie surprised us with an authentic Greek fish dish for an "appetizer on the house". Needless to say, the dish was awesome and our group quickly gobbled it up with delight. Every person in our party exclaimed how great their food was when our main courses were served piping hot. Our glasses were never empty, and the wait staff was top notch. Timmie's father even came by our table to say hello and thanks for dining with them. After we finished eating, Timmie once again surprised us with a round of a classic Greek liquor. We all toasted to a great night of friends, food, and drink. In summary, excellent food, atmosphere, and customer service. Spiro's rocks!

Now this is a place I expect to be returning to many times! The food is great, the value is quite reasonable, and the Owners (Andrae & Janise Thompson) are very welcoming, and deserve much success! The biggest issue one might have with Yah Mon is finding it. While it has a Platt address, you can't see it from Platt. IT'S BEHIND THE UPS STORE. Miss it and you will miss a GREAT experience! We wanted to experience as many tastes as possible, so we ordered the Taste of the Islands ($19.99) and the Curried Tofu ($8.99 small plate). All entrees start with a salad of mixed greens, and even that was a hit. The thing that jumps right out at you is the value proposition. With one exception, all the entrees are under $20.00. HUH!? Many of the entrees can be served as small or large plates. If our $8.99 Curried Tofu was the small plate, the large must be huge. The food really is the star here, thanks to Chef Janise. It's been at least 15 years since I enjoyed Curried Goat that much. The Ox Tails truly were tender with meat just falling off the bone. The Jerk Chicken could easily be the very best in the Tampa Bay area. Even the condiment selection is authentic! Just when we thought we had had enough, we decided to have a crack at dessert. We thought we would split a piece of the Rum Cake, and it was GREAT. Chef Janise offered a tasting of the Bread Pudding, and it was FABULOUS!! Don't leave without trying at least one of the desserts! There are scores of places to get your meals in and around the Hyde Park area. If you are not adding Yah Mon to your short list, you might as well stay at home.... When you do get there, please offer my warm regards to both Andrae and Janise!
Beautiful decor. Great service. Food was yummy. I got the bang bang shrimp and the green curry with fish- both were very good.

We went for dinner last night and this was my 1st time dining here. My only disappointment was that they didn't have anything available from the children's menu and my kids are picky eaters. But anyway, the food is really good and the portions are big! It's much cheaper then going into the city too. The owner was very nice as well. My only recommendation would be to offer pitchers of water or soda instead of buying each bottled drink separately. But overall I was satisfied and happy that I found a place in the northeast.

Although a little pricey, I think the food quality offered is great. I have not been around for the buffet, so my experience is limited. Their dinner menu, however, is good filled with your typical curry and tandoori varieties. I don't come here for anything new, but get my regular cravings satisfied.

Went here for lunch yesterday, this place is amazing. Service was spectacular. Prices very reasonable. Corn Beef sandwich melted in my mouth, but the best part of the meal was the Greek salad, it was amazing, Better then when I was in Greece.

I enjoyed the lamb curry. The rice doesn't come with the food so you might want to order it as a side. They are generous with it though. I ordered medium and could still taste the spice so be careful with that. The service was good and the food came out really quick.

Hadn't been to this chain in years, can honestly say we won't be back. The food was waaaay too salty and just not that good. I ordered the chicken pad Thai, it was the worst pad Thai I've ever had. I could barely eat it, but I was starving so I sucked it up. I felt like I was eating straight salt and hot sauce. So gross. Our server was strange and not very friendly at all. The hostess girls were so sweet though and extremely friendly.

The fried chicken (I tried all the types of pieces they had) was pretty good, but as other reviews have noted, overpriced. Tender on the inside and not dry at all, crispy on the outside. The interior of the place was beautiful, and the food/pastries were meticulously laid out and all looking absolutely mouth-watering. I also like the focus on a quick grab and go takeout - struck me as high-end, hip takeout. The hand pies all looked amazing and delicious, but the pecan pie one I got didn't really taste all that special. I also had a lemon cheesecake cookie, which was also ok. I will definitely be back to try the other desserts though, since I was getting major choice anxiety about all the sweets to try. My favorite items were probably the mac n cheese and biscuit. The biscuit was probably the best I've had, with a firm, buttery shell surrounding the pillowy, soft interior. Mac n cheese had complexity of flavor and a bunch of different ingredients, including tomatoes, that didn't distract from the yummy cheesiness but rather enhanced it. Perfect combo of ingredients and liked that there was chicken in it too. Overall, food presentation is great and honestly I would just go back for the mac n cheese and biscuits. They also had a cool soda fountain with unique flavors. Pricey, but if you're not averse to shelling extra $ for nicer takeout, Wishbone is definitely worth checking out.

Ok, after a month in Philly, this is my favorite pho place. Pho Hoa is part of an international chain, which mostly sucks, so I've been surprised. They have also changed their menu from the generic Pho Hoa menu (they have the logo with the woman with noodle hair) to what seems like their own, and one that is much more extensive and like a typical Vietnamese do it all restaurant. (Maybe they left the franchise and went off on their own?). In any case, their pho is consistently good, and, for a Vietnamese place, their service is consistently good as well. One time I was eating there an older white man came in. When the manager came to take his order, he said he couldn't, that he needed help from his favorite waiter who always chose for him. This guy had gone out to the grocery store to pick up some ingredients. The manager said he would be back in a few. When he got back, sure enough, he picked out a dish for the guy (eggplant) and the guy was happy. It was a kinda surreal moment because it reminded me of being in Thailand or Vietnam, where it's not so uncommon for the older white man to have a boy do simple things for him...

As someone who resides in the Logan Square neighborhood, I was happy to see Pho Street open its doors after being under construction for several months. At last, I can have some quick Vietnamese food within walking distance and not need to take the subway ride to Chinatown... or an even longer subway ride to Washington Ave. The ordering kiosks were easy-to-use and it was fun to customize my bun or pho. Ample room to ease your way from the kiosks to the self-service station where you could grab some nuoc mam and other condiments. The staff was friendly and helpful, and they put a lot of care into each order they received (a lot of communication behind the kitchen line). The menu as of now includes pho, bun, com tam, banh mi, and goi cuon. I'm excited to see their menu expand in the next months to come as business picks up. I recommend their bun and pho. I liked being able to carefully choose the meats and toppings I wanted through the ordering kiosk. The bun was big and it was delicious with their house-made nuoc mam pha. The pho had a tasty broth that didn't need any additional seasonings. Lots of good pieces of tripe, beef meatballs, tendon, and flank steak. I did not try their com tam, but my SO did have the pork chop com tam. It looked quite tasty with generous portions of bi (shredded pork skin) and cha (egg meat quiche). I also tried their banh mi but something was off. The bread tasted bland/unseasoned and it made the rest of the banh mi tasteless even though all of the components were there. Not a deal-breaker whatsoever - maybe my taste buds were wonky that day. Looking forward to see the continuing growth of Pho Street in Center City!
its all right but seems to cater itself as more of a fast food place. the dishes are good and i like greek. the place is not ideal but the nice food and interior is all right

My new favorite in Wilmo! The former Union City Grille has been totally redone and rejuvenated. A super cool spot to hang out and enjoy some drinks and the Asian-inspired menu. Best of all, the vast majority of items are gluten-free (or can be made GF) with lots of vegetarian or vegan choices too. The kitchen is really aware of gluten intolerance issues so it's an absolute pleasure to dine there. Everything I've ordered has been so good. I especially enjoyed the huge pot of mussels in delicious spiced lemongrass broth, served with fries. I love the small share plates to start with, especially the soy-orange bok choy. There's so much to choose from, and even the dessert menu has 2-3 GF options, as in real actual desserts (not just "you can have the sorbet") made by a very innovative pastry chef. Small details like the cayenne-cinnamon popcorn and sparkling water at the table add big bonus points for me. Also, every server I've encountered has been relentlessly nice, friendly, and helpful. All around this place is really enjoyable. PS. Apparently there's brunch on Sundays, so here's one request/challenge for 8UK - please add some brunch items for my vegan friends so we don't always have to go to Home Grown. ;)

A couple of clients mentioned this place was pretty good so I was fine as Im pretty cool with Mediterranean pita places. They also warned us that service here could be quite slow so I was prepared to have a so-so experience for lunch. We arrived and I liked the place as soon as we entered. Very well lit and a nice decor with glossy, glittery pictures of cats and other strange things on the wall. They gave us a huge table for our party of 9 along with a big vase centerpiece lol. We started out with two big plates of hummus (roasted red pepper, jalapeño and regular) along with cucumbers and pita bread. The jalapeño hummus was the show stealer as expected as it was delicious with a slight kick to it. There were 2 pita's that I was very interested in: The Chicken Shawarma pita and the Philly Steak Pita. I am a huge chicken shawarma fan, but could not resist the Philly. The Philly was so delicious that I don't recall ever sitting it back down on the plate...yeah it was that good. The service was stellar as we never waited a long time for anything and they kept the water glasses full..I assume whatever service issues they had in the past have been addressed. Good place here and I look forward to going back on my annual work trip to Tucson.

I agree with previous reviews, portion sizes are small but service is attentive. The sangria was SO bad, my friends ordered a pitcher and when offered a refill, one cringes, "Do I have to?" It tasted like it had been sitting in ice all day: watered down, weak wine, no brandy, no cinnamon...nothing that makes sangria. The salsa is good (not sure if it's home made), the burger was well seasoned which I appreciate. Beautiful location but truly none of the bars or eateries in Gulfport are stellar.

DO NOT COME HERE- Dishonest Business We decided to check this place out because of its good reviews. I asked the waiter for a few suggestions, took his advice and he ended up bringing out ALL three dishes I asked about. I gave him the benefit of the doubt thinking it was just a language barrier and miscommunication. He picked up our Naan basket without one word, bring back more Naan and charged us for two baskets. Without even asking! We wouldn't mind paying for 3 meals but it's the principle of doing business. Do not rip your customers off and you will get more business in the long run. This place is an authentic Indian place, it was all Indians in the restaurant and they took advantage of us because we are not familiar with the cuisine/language! HORRIBLE PLACE, do NOT come here unless you're Indian or have Indian friends who will prevent these people from TAKING ADVANTAGE of you!! Wish I could give this place negative stars!!

Good food. Regular options but done right. The complimentary bread could have been better. Got the Chicken Souvlaki and it was great. I wish they had options to chose for the side with the entree. The veggies were not that great.
A wonderful vegetarian option. We loved the veggie phone and split a respectable tofu bahn mi. Oo. don't miss the avocado rolls.
This place has great fresh and delicious food. It's clean and the staff very courteous. What else would you expect?

I came here because I wanted to introduce my vegan friend to a great restaurant instead of the opposite way for a change. Even though this isn't a vegetarian place, a lot of Indians are vegetarians so Mumbai Bistro was perfect for her. She loved the food and I did too! I'm a meat-eater but I also hate spicy food. The cashier was kind enough to cater to my tastes, assuring me that their Chicken Tikka Masala would not be spicy nor would they add any spice for me. The workers had the patience of saints for putting up with my weak tongue. The space is also nice and cozy, adding to the homey food.

Awesome melasian food! I went here with a friend of mine who is Melasian... and he helped our whole group order. The indian pancakes were SO SO good! Everything everyone ordered was good except for the pho (or something that looked like pho). I ordered my shrimp lo mein without spices and it was very very good. They weren't the fastest place, but other than that... one of the best places in chinatown for sure! I plan on going back very soon and will add more...

very clean and an infectiously polite owner... she's a true Ethiopian lost in the wilds of cowboy Nevada. ... an oasis of cool in a edgy industrial area... personally i don't like the "flat bread" (it's called Teff and is grey and spongey) but that's what they eat in Ethiopia... it's definitely worth a visit... the lamb and salad and cabbage/carrot dishes are not bad. the decor is very hip and dead on authentic... and if you want to see where the Teff grain comes from, just check out the big grey brush in the back of the dining room... the owner might bemoan the lack of diversity in cowboy land, but hey if I moved to Addis I wouldn't expect to find a Rodeo crowd.

Overrated in my opinion. The st. paul is delicious. The chinese menu items are lacking in taste. I had the jerk chicken sandwich and it wasn't anything near what jerk chicken tastes like. It was just super hot with peppers. Friendly and fast service. Not a favorite.

This place has changed for the better. There is a new waitress named Jahnna, who is wonderful. The manager remembers you. They really wait on you hand and foot. I went for the first time in years to their lunch buffet. Excellent! Although the sweets were too sweet and there were some dishes too spicy, this is to be expected. They will make to taste though. There are so many great dishes to choose from, that you can find wonderful things to eat. The ambiance is so lovely there. They also bring Naan to table, a nice touch. Wish they had more chutney choices, UNSWEETENED Chai and not-too-sweet desserts. One Buffet I attended in CA had a soft serve Mango Ice Cream. I would LOVE it if they would get this! Their Orange Kulfi dessert is fun.
The norristown area has a lack of good chinese places so P.F. Changs always fits the bill. Wish I could find a local place with just as good food but this place always delivers!!!

Recently had a great meal at this charming, byob restaurant . Everything from the appetizers to the dessert were delicious and the service was top notch! The pacing of the courses was spot on. This is a very small place and sometimes you are thisclose to your neighbor or against the wall but somehow they make it work. I would imagine though if you are a large person, it may be uncomfortable. Have the namesake dessert, the zeppolis...they are to die for! That and an espresso were a perfect way to end a great meal.
The food is tasty, they have a full bar. I had the shrimp po' boy without tomatoes; it is full of favor. The fries are yummy.

I love this little all you can eat Indian restaurant! Delicious food, small restaurant but the staff is very friendly and nice. The food is delicious and is hot. The staff continued to make sure the food was in good supply. I can't wait to go back.

Excellent food in a really cool space with a lot of warmth is the best way to describe this restaurant. It's located generally in the Central Business District at the edge of the Warehouse District near many hotels, galleries and not far from the French Quarter (between Poydras and Canal Streets) First off the vibe is wonderful and the service is lively, fun and full of energy. We enjoyed the service as much as the excellent cuisine. The food has a Caribbean bent as the chef is from St. Lucia. The menu reflects both New Orleans and also Caribbean style cooking. Having some well made cocktails to start was a good preface to the great fare that followed. Starting with several table appetizers I must say that everything, and especially the croquets, were amazing. The accompanying sauces were tangy and delicious. I had oysters as an appetizer and they were absolutely succulent and delicious. They weren't Gulf but the smaller Northwest cold water type that deliver a lot of flavor. Some special hot sauce in a small bottle, custom made, was wonderful on them. With all the tantalizing selections for entrees I branched out and had the Curried Goat. Amazing! It was like a stew but not full of sauce or fluid but just the right amount to scoop with the meat, veggies and potato. It was really delicious and just enough spice for a nice kick too. By time dessert rolled around we were far too full to partake All in all this became my new go to NOLA restaurant. A 'must' go.'

This is my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia. First off it's a BYOB (yes!). I've loved everything that I've gotten. We always get one or two apps, one of which includes the trio of dips with grilled pita. I always get a different entree and try a bit of my date's so I've tasted a lot on the menu. As for the menu, it changes frequently but fundamental the flavorings are very "Kanella"... can't explain it because I don't have the lingo, but I know a Kanella dish when I taste one. This place is tiny, which my husband and I have concluded is why the food is always consistently deliciously seasoned and cooked to perfection. But the small size means you need to have a reservation. No such thing as walking in and getting a table. Even if you call an hour in advance you might catch a cancellation, but don't waste your time trying to just stroll on in on a Friday or Saturday night! Just go!!
One of the best Italian seafood dinners I ever had. My wife's pork chop was perfectly cooked and delicious. Service was excellent. The Sunday drive from NE Philly up River Road was beautiful.

Dropping one star for a ridiculous experience I had here. We went in on a Friday to a half-full dining room at 6pm. We told the host we were 2. He turned and looked into the dining room then turned back to us and said we could not be seated because all of the tables available were for parties of four. There were at least 6 four tops empty. We laughed, I said, "Are you serious?" Probably not going back.

Food is average. Wait time is long. Very hot and crowded. Size of drinks have been reduced. Management makes excuses. Say they have a new menu coming but, after asking what is being added to menu only a couple of insignificant items are to be added. Basically if you want to melt in the heat to eat there for the view and reduced size of drinks I say go for it. All that is right about this place is the view. My family from out of town insisted on going there while in town recently. The hostess said it would be a 45 minute wait. Over a hour later we still weren't seated. They were so hot and exhausted from standing and waiting at 7-8 p.m. We called CATCHES WATERFRONT RESTAURANT. They said they could seat us immediately. We drove to Catches 12 minutes away and had the best meal you could ask for. And the bill was cheaper than we would have spent to melt at Sam's Hudson Beach bar. Live music was playing on the water at Whiskey River across from us. Service and attitude by Management at Sam's Beach Bar is ridiculous. The servers are real troopers for continuing to work for Sam's. I feel for them. And from what I have heard and seen at Sam's, management is NOT their friends. Even the servers complain about The manger. They don't like the way the manager makes excuses for poor food. If you're wondering why it always busy there??? It's not for the food or prices.....it's only for the view of the water.
I LOVE the Smiling Elephant! The place sure is small, but that's what makes it cozy inside! The staff is so friendly, and the menu has healthy options. Definitely recommended!

Their Thai food is the best I've had yet. The service was a bit off and so was the appetizer but the pad thai, duck curry, and tom yum really made up for it. It is a bit pricey but what could you expect when you're in Santa Barbara.

Tried this place for the first time and it was really good! A bit spicy so ask for them to make it medium - they were happy to do so.l and actually recommended that to my friend. I had chicken tikka masala and my friend had an eggplant dish that our server recommended. Both were great. I had regular naan and my friend had garlic naan. Both of those were also great. I will be going back for sure!

Yes, I am once again writing another review for an Indian restaurant. Time for a flashback: years ago, I recall meeting the owner and chef (Madhan Lal) of India Sizzling II when he used to manage Passage To India in Columbus, IN. I never forgot how tasty the food was! Some years passed by, and I discovered that Madhan Lal was up in Fishers, IN at the original India Sizzling, and so I would drive 30 or more minutes just to indulge in the best non-vegetarian Indian food I've ever had. Fast forward: it's now 2013 and I get a call from Madhan, and he tells me that he has taken over what used to be Bombay Garden and opened India Sizzling II on Lafayette Rd. I was his first customer and I'm privileged to be able to eat such good, home style food and not have to drive to Fishers every time I want authentic, non veg Indian. I am unapologetically an Indian food addict! Ha. So, if you like rarefied North and South Indian food; if you like exotic spices and herbs and unique breads (dosas, nan, utappam, appam), and if you're not afraid to feel a little butt burn the next morning, then add this restaurant to your repertoire of awesome ethnic eateries and eat good! I'm telling you, you can't find Indian food this tasty outside of an Indian's home kitchen; there are only a few authentic Indian restaurants around Indy and this a top notch choice restaurant!

This was my first time eating Malaysian, went to Penang because of a friends suggestion. Had the Roti Canai, it was very tasty, friend in our group had the octopus or squid? It was a bowl of tentacles and grossed me out, but he loved it, so if that's your thing it's good too. We had good service, I'm curious about the items on the menu that you have to talk to the wait staff about before ordering... but not curious enough to order them!

Saturday night and every place is packed. It's 7:30 and really didn't want to wait an hour to get seated. We saw Rosemary's Grill on our way to another restaurant. That restaurant had a hour wait so we decided to try Rosemary's. I knew they just opened and saw Steaks on their sign (which is exactly what we wanted) I was surprised it is Mediterranean. We have never had that type of food so we stuck with the steaks. We both had the T-bone. My husband's was med well and mine is well done. It came with soup or salad bar. My husband got their chicken pasta soup. I got the salad bar. There wasn't a huge selection on the salad bar but everything was fresh! I was very happy with my steak. Even though it was well done, it was tender, very flavorful and didn't need steak sauce. My husband liked his also. I was very pleasantly surprised. I hope they add more things to their menu but this place is definitely a place to go.

Siam Elephant is a chill little Thai nook by the beach in Carpenteria. A friend of mine loved it and recommended it to me. The ethnic decor enhanced the delicious meal. Our friendly server presented us with the most outstanding spring rolls. They were wrapped tightly with perfect lettuce and two dipping sauces. Spring rolls are take time to master and the flawless presentation demonstrated a high level of finesse. My red coconut curry entree was delicious and I ended up eating the last of the broth with a spoon after inhaling every morsel. I will be back, it may take me a while but it is on my radar.

My favorite food is thai food and I only eat Thai food. Basil spice hands down has the best thai food ever. I've tried thai food at other locations in saint louis, Chicago, Nashville, Boston LA, NYC, etc. Basil spice will forever be my favorite thai restaurant. Nobody makes pad Thai and pad see eiw better than them. Interior is not the best but you come to eat right? Other locations may look better but basil spice has the best food.
Small place, inexpensive ..... Mediterranean in style but not my type of food. Service was slow Had a place to sit inside... Casual , more for younger crowd ..... Quick bite

Got a gyro pita and chicken Caesar by delivery. Delivery time was faster than the estimated. I usually try another place around here for gyros but I must say the gyro pita blew that one out of the water! The chicken caesar was good, but maybe chicken is not my style. Highly recommend if you're into gyros.
The service was excellent. The food was great so many different curry at buffet. The naan was really good.

Visiting from Connecticut, didn't know we had to make a reservation. They were very friendly and welcoming. They found us a table and served us right away. The food is delicious! I would recommend dining here if you are in the Philadelphia area. The intimate setting makes you feel like family :) (don't forget to make a reservation)
Fresh salads, fresh fish, great marinades and dressing, seasoning in the meats, amazing garlic knot bread, and baklava that's out of this world.

I give this place an A for effort. You have to tell them that you want the cha gio egg rolls Vietnamese style so they can give you lettuce and the fish sauce nuoc mam, rather than sweet n sour sauce. But they are nice about it, so I don't mind. The pho is pretty good, at least they prepare it fresh. I am pleased with my food, but sorry, I already picked my favorite Vietnamese spot in Reno.

Outstanding little find in Philly. Here for the DNC and staying in an apartment on the corner of 9th and Pine. Walked nun this place and decided to drop in. Wow...am I glad that I did! This place is fantastic. Ordered the Feta Watermelon salad, Yakisoba and the Black Peppered Wings. Every item was as tasty as the next. Lunch hour closes at 2:30 pm and reopens at 5 pm for dinner. Go...you won't be disappointed. Yummmmmm!
El dente vegetables , flavorful sauces, and reasonable serving sizes. VERY tasty! I will be back.

Went last week! Very good just like the one uptown. Looks like they are getting a full bar license. A friend of the owner shared his "Vietnamese beef stew" which he said they eat at home and it was amazing. The dumplings were good too and the rare beef Phó good as always
I forgot to mention they charge .50 cents for onions on your cheesesteak, only in Mullica Hill!

Be sure to have quarters for the parking meters if dining here as I found no free parking in the area. The restaurant is attractive and comfortable and the city of Media charming. The staff members did not go out of their way to make me feel welcome or appreciated, but plates were cleared and my water glass was refilled. The lunch buffet, $9.95, is a small selection of tasty items, mostly chicken dishes. Missing from the buffet was a staple Indian dish, my favorite: cauliflower and potatoes (aloo gobi). There is a small salad bar which includes good rice pudding (kheer). The chicken tandoori was not hot nor as succulent as I have enjoyed at other Indian establishments.

This was the best restaurant experience I've had in recent memory. I went on Tuesday evening with my boyfriend. There were no tables available, and they said it would be a 15-minutes wait, and we were welcomed to wait near the bar, but I felt like we'd be in the way since the place was hopping. They took my number and we had a beer at Varga while we waited. Within the next maybe 10 minutes they called to say the table was ready. Every interaction and every morsel of food was amazing. Kudos to our server Emmy for being awesome. We ordered the broccoli, the dumpling special (pork and beef in chili oil), the pigtails, and for noodles we got the short rib and the miso. There's not much point in describing the taste of each except to say they tasted amazing. Emmy made a point to tell us that there are best sellers, and then there are staff favorites. Go with the staff favorites.

The food was really good and it was great that they could make some dishes vegan. The service was a little slow, but the staff was very nice. The food was very tasty and the portions were larger than other thai restaurants I have been to. We ordered the vegetarian naam salad, Thai Basil Tofu, and Pad Kee Mao Tofu. I'd order all 3 again. My favorite was the naam salad.
Worst place in philly for hookah and drinks.. Pathetic service..we waited for 30 mins to get out order placed even placed was not packed.. Beer was not chilled and servers were rude..

I would definitely come back to this restaurant! The entire menu had markings on it to show which items were gluten free, vegan, and lactose free. The food was delicious, and they even had a gluten free flatbread which was fluffy and tasted like real bread! We ordered one flatbread to start, but then ended up buying two more because they were so good! We ordered several other dishes, all of which came out fast and packaged in plastics containers so that it was simple to pack up to take home.The restaurant had an a la carte menu as well as a buffet, so there were many options to choose from. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who has dietary restrictions, as well as those without.

We stopped by Spice-n-Grill last night. I had this place bookmarked for some time but didn't really know that they focus more on carry-out orders than dine in. You can eat there, but the space is pretty sparse. There are a handful of tables. We arrived at 8 and the kind man said that he would be closing early due to take care of something with his family. He said he can whip something up for us to take to-go which was fine with us. We chose samosas, chicken tikka masala, beef nihari, and alu gobi. He asked how spicy we wanted the dishes. The wife isn't keen to heat so we said mild. All the dishes still had a good kick to them. So much that she didn't eat the beef or cauliflower. The food was good, and I really liked the flavors. The samosas were hand-made but the naan was straight out of a bag. In fact, it was a little hard in a few spots where it must have dried out. All in all, I'd revisit this place, and loved that the couple working inside were clearly the owners. But I don't think it beats places closer to my home.
Very good food and generous portions. Homestyle Vietnamese cooking. Highly recommend.
Totally worth the drive from south jersey. Good food, reasonably priced, & good service. Will be back.

Having participated in top chef and tasted ninas food during the competition, I was disappointed. Granted we went to eat for Sunday brunch but I found the menu unbalanced and uninspiring. The service was also very sub-par considering how vacant the restaurant was. I have to say I will think twice before visiting this place again.

Visited on a Wednesday afternoon. Was a weekday after lunch rush hour so we were the only ones in the restaurant. We were given prompt service. We started off with the steamed pork dumplings which were delicious. Then I had pad Thai with shrimp. The food tasted amazing. Loved everything about it. Will be back to try more.
Great food and service. I highly recommend this place for dinner due to awesome ambience and food choices.

I found the food here to be excellent and sublime. I have been here for lunch and dinner. Just go - taste & savor. Go for the specials, the appetizers, and to taste something unique. I predict the chef will become a food celebrity in the years to come. One side note - the place is busy so be patient. It is worth it. The waiters can be a little distracted at times, but they are effecient.

I have been trying to find a restaurant that sells Banh Mi sandwiches around SB/Goleta area and I am do happy I finally found this place. Compared to LA(626 area) the price is a little expensive but the quality compensates it. If you need a quick fix for the love of sandwiches, this is the place to go. :) :) :)

Food at Oriental Pearl was delicious! Waitress was very helpful. Enjoyed Pan Fried Noodle, grilled pork with broken rice, Pork and Shrimp in Caramel Sauce, and Summer rolls for dinner. Went for lunch last week and had Pho! Very good.

Just leaving this place ... we came here because of the reviews ..it is a good place but couldn't Give it more stars .. we did the tasting menu . It was good but some of the food is super spicy that you can't even eat it and they don't tell you that at the beginning so our mouth is on fire . Also you can't order a Irish coffee and actually get it hot because is cold when you get it . They had redo it for my friend the. I order one and it was cold the server did it care this time she said it was because of the whipped cream. So they need to work on their service I think and explain everyone what they are getting ! How the food is .

Made a reservation for 4 for a double date with my bestie and his girlfriend. Atmosphere is lovely and welcoming with a beautiful wine feature, although devoid of many selections. Server arrived quickly but with bad news; almost every option (lamb, salmon and filet mignon) was unavailable due to a busy previous night. Umar, our waiter was visibly shaken with having to relay this bad news to us. However with aplomb, he made the best of a bad situation. We ordered our meals with my friend, asking for soup as a side, to be told that soup was not an option. All good. Meals ordered, all of a sudden Umar arrives with a soup for my friend, stating that given the lack of options for our dinner, he wants to provide us with something extra. The soup was delicious, well seasoned and not too salty broth. Our meals arrive, with extra tzatziki as requested. Umar, was gracious, accommodating and a consummate professional in all all his dealings with us. All in all the food was very good, besides an over seasoned falafel. The appetizer was very well done with steaks that were perfectly cooked. The lack of traditional Mediterranean fare (lamb and fish) was compensated by Umar, our exceptional server. He went above an beyond to ensure our evening, including comping our desserts. Thank you Umar!!! That being said, we will it be returning to this restaurant.

I will definitely be back. They're food was terrific. The samosas were delicious and so was the potato pancake appetizer (not sure the name). I went with the lamb vindaloo. The serving size was good. The lamb was in a nice tomato sauce that was pretty spicy. I tend to like Indian food towards the hot side. Other dishes tried were the chicken tikka masala and lamb dish with spinach and fenugreek. The tikka masala was a little sweet for my taste, but very good none the less. The food was five stars, but our service was somewhat bad. We eventually had to get another staff member to help us out. It isn't good when you have spicy food and you can't get one refill of your drink.

Searched high and low for a place that was halfway between Delaware and Cherry Hill & Philly area to meet up with a friend and settled with Blueplate and it was a nice experience! The parking situation was a bit funky but Mullica Hill is a quaint little town and I appreciate the parking availability! Now to the food and experience... The waitresses are attentive and helpful through the meal and the food was simply amazing. I had a vegetable and shrimp risotto that was fresh, filling, and flavorful. Easily one of the best I've had and the quality of everything they make here is local and top notch. My friend had crab cakes and their potato "fries" we're beautiful. We finished off our meal with a fresh blueberry crumb pie and nothing disappointed me about the experience! My one only qualm is that the waitress mixed up our to-go containers (imagine our portions) but it's an honest mistake xD I would love to come back if I'm in the area!
We've eaten here twice in the last week and it has been exceptionally good both times. The prices are great as well. This is a new go to spot for us.

The Pearl is outstanding and consistent. I have eaten there many times and never had anything less than an outstanding meal. My friends love it too. Its basically high end modern international. Karim, the Chef, and his team of waiters are dedicated to providing outstanding food and excellent service. Karim is Moroccan but his food is truly international. They also have an excellent wine list. In terms of indiviidual items, the blue cheese pate is not on the menu but they always have it and it is delicious. The olives are some of the best kalamatas i have had. Ask for them with garlic. The lamb chops are cooked to perfection, the ostrich comes with a delicious sauce, and his steaks are right up there with the best steak houses. He makes a salad with a dressing like none you have ever tasted. Interestingly, he also offers sushi which is some of the best we have ever had. They can make everything for you tapas style. If its just a small group, sit at the bar, you will get personal service from Karim. If you live anywhere in or around Treasure Island you need to go to this place.

Pita Kebob is a very promising addition to Apollo Beach food variety. We saw the signs and stopped in. It turned out to be the first day of a soft opening. They told us they would have a grand opening mid January. We tried Kofta and shawarma pita sandwiches and tabouli salad. The sandwiches came with seasoned fries. We were impressed with the tastes and spices. We noticed the gyro on a spit and will try that next time.
We love the Red Curry, my wife orders it every time we visit. Pleasant atmosphere,prompt courteous service.

Best BYOB Italian spot in LoMo, hands down. I like the setup there, it's a little loud, but not to the point where you have to shout to reach the other end of the table - just people having a good time. The meatball appetizer is a must, brings back memories of Sunday with my Grandma.

I was really excited for this place, we gave a month to work out the kinks before we went. We finally walked over and it took maybe 20 minutes to get our water and order. We ordered and everything came out...45 minutes later. Scalding hot but not fresh. I could have bought the beef patties (appetizers that the got put on the wrong table then brought to us) at publix. The jerk chicken wasn't a jerk at all. Bland. Good vibes, people at the bar. Servers were nice but not attentive. My water was never refilled and I was there for over an hour. I really hope they can take a look at how to do better. I would love for this business to thrive in downtown largo. Let's get it together vibes!

Came back to Tampa just for this place. It was as good as I remember. Had the bread pudding this time and it was perfect! Love the music playing as well. (Good volume so you can still hold a conversation.) We'll be back... again and again

I have been here a few times, due to its close proximity to where I live. The pho and spring rolls are pretty good, and the prices are ok. The service, however, leaves something to be desired. I have been told twice they were out of cilantro (I love cilantro and basically use pho as a vessel for it.) today I was told they were out by my waiter so I decided to pack everything up and go home, where the cilantro is plentiful. Then suddenly, someone found some cilantro. Dude just didn't want to miss whatever was playing in his phone long enough to ask. Also, they are right next to Rouses where bunches cilantro is about a dollar. I just don't get it.

This review is for their new, next door sister restaurant, La Mulita. HOLY COW! Or VACA SAGRADA!! After attending a tasting of some of the menu items for the new establishment I am beyond sold on both Delicia and La Mulita. Every single item I tried was incredible. The cocktails: Wow! If they're serving Pear-A-Mule when you're there, you MUST get it. It's a light, refreshing drink with pear, ginger beer, tequila, and (I think) lime. I could drink those babies all night. I tried another raspberry drink that was the perfect amount of tart. It's easy for cocktails to be a sugarfest, and this drink was not it. The food: Just order one of everything on menu to be safe. My favorites were: The sancocho which was like a stew. It was full of flavor and the perfect thing to warm you up on a cold night or a chilly spring or summer evening. Yucca fries. There's no longer a need to eat a fried potato when you can eat fried yucca. There was a dip/meat mix of some kind on it with the perfect amount of heat to keep the dish from being bland. Chimichurri sliders: These little guys pack a punch! Lots of flavor and a good amount of spice to keep your taste buds interested without being overwhelming. The bun was nice and toasty. Beet pastelito: I don't know if I've ever eaten a beet in my entire life, but I've been missing out for the past twenty-something years. The beets used in the cake are marinated in orange juice and jalapeños. If you're slightly adventurous, try it! Writing this review has made me hungry. I can't wait for La Mulita to open! I have a feeling I'm going to be a regular!

The name is Nhu Y (roughly "as you like it") not Nhuy. A tiny banh mi shop, we ordered the combo and the vegetarian (which others on here have raved about). The deli counter was a bit bare looking (not a good sign) and they took a long time to make 2 sandwiches (not a good sign, generally the faster they whip them out, the better it is - high volume and lots of practice). Anyway, the sandwiches were fine. They had a good moistness level. The vegetarian was surprisingly good for not having meat (I'm a former-vegan turned carnivore). However, we found both sandwiches to be too salty, and I'm a big fan of having more pickled veggies, cilantro, and chili in my banh mi than was the case. Not saying too much, but the best banh mi I've had so far in Philly.
Great food better Service. Alan and his crew are awesome and I love their breakfast!
Really good food, prices are reasonable. Recommend to try it out if you haven't. Friendly people serving you.

So happy I found this place, some of the best Asian food in Indy! If you like a little spice, I would highly recommend the Curry. The food was prepared fresh and made to the level of spiciness that suited me. The owner is very helpful in explaining the dishes and she is very passionate about cooking. I will definitely be back!

When La.Va first opened on the corner, I have to admit that I felt like the heavens were parting and delivering a ray of sunshine on angel's wings. Living very close by, the very presence of La.Va really felt like it transformed my corner of the city from a blank, quasi-gentrifying wasteland, into a real community. Perhaps over stated, but I stand by it. La.Va has been just about the biggest single improvement to the neighborhood since it opened and it really has become a place at which people stop being adjacently domiciled and start becoming neighbors. All the same, my near-daily frequenting of La.Va a few years back has transitioned to my maybe having gone in once this year. Why? I think it just doesn't seem to have a soul. The few novel Israeli items are fun, but much of the israeli food-stuff is sourced from Cafe Ole--another Israeli-owned cafe which also seems to have contracts with most of the cafes in CC and the surrounding area. So it's not really too unique. The coffee is okay. It's LaColombe, which is a great standard. But it's also pretty much the standard of half the cafes in the city and not particularly well-served at La.Va. Similarly, the decor is a sort of a strange middle-ground between bohemian kitch (Victorian couches), and upscale cafe (the really comfy wooden chairs). It always feels a little gloomy in the day (compared to, say, Java Co on 2nd and Christian), but way too bright at night. It's not really fast or sleek enough to be a fun take-out spot (such as Ant's Pants), but it's not really accommodating enough to encourage lingering. I truly have a great affection for the owners and am so grateful that it simply exists, but I really wish they would breath a little new life in the place. It just seems like the passion that was once there has faded.
Try a little of everything! You won't regret it! Would be a good place for a date, quiet and attractive interior. Friendly staff, great food.

Mood Cafe is always my first stop when I visit Philly after a nice drive from Brooklyn. The Lassi flavors range from traditional to ecstatic. It's always great to bring a friend or friends to share because they always make enough to fill your cup and have enough left over to fill a smaller cup that you can trade with your friends. I have a hard time choosing anything other than the Pistachio/Almond Lassi. It's a great balance of rich yogurt, creamy almonds, and nutty pistachios that almost adds an umami flavor to the combination as the pistachios that they use are toasted with a bit of salt. I've recently ordered off the menu. Pistachio/Dates. Also a winner. The chewy pieces of dates sink to the bottom and wait for you to finish your drink before you can pick them out with a straw. It's hard to go wrong here. The owner is very vocal and knowledgable - if you order flavors that he doesn't think will work well together, he will recommend something better. Also, he's originally from Brooklyn. Bonus points for that.
Ekta deserves 5 starts - SO much better than Tiffin and others nearby. The chicken tikka masala is great, and the customer service here is even better.
Jesus! This place is a sleeper. The Food, LIFE CHANGING! The Service...couldn't be any sweeter. The Fried Pickles are so good, they disappears before I could take a picture.

The food here is great! With reasonable prices and good customer service, this restaurant is better then most in the area. The Greek salad was a real Greek salad and the hummus was top notch. I would definitely come back and eat again.

Aside from their business being extremely busy during the weekends and their lack of space to wait when there is a rush of people, they serve pretty good food. However, it is kind of difficult to know which ones are good and which ones arent. Their menu is a variety. I've ordered many things from their menu that lacked a lot of flavor and taste. Their curry was basically a blob of brown sauce on top of shredded chicken, their duck with ginger and scallion rice was bland and tasteless, the ginger duck noodle was meh, and their hainanese chicken was ok. But crispy golden friend squids and their fried noodles were pretty good! When it comes to their appetizers, their home made roti canai is amazing with very delicious chicken curry! Same with the beef or chicken satays with the peanut sauce and the crispy pork intestines.

Ever-changing selection on the buffet means you can visit twice a week and eat totally different lunches. The staff is unobtrusive and service-minded; your water glass will not go empty and you will not be pestered as you dine. The food is flavorful and not greasy, the naan is fresh-made and aromatic, the vegetables are crisp and fresh. Each dish on the buffet tastes of distinctly different seasonings than do the others - unlike some buffets where it seems everything is the same flavor, Amber Indian chefs must pride themselves on producing a variety of dishes each unique. If you are new to the cuisine, you can't go wrong with the buffet. If you find yourself facing a menu, the chana masala is my recommendation. Both the menu and buffet have a full compliment of vegetarian options also. Finally, you can be entertained by the frenetic bollywood-style media available on the multiple tvs as you eat.
A wonderful place to eat. Amazingly fresh and outstanding customer service. The menu has a nice eclectic selection. Be hungry. Prices are always reasonable.

The food here was "just OK" in my opinion. I had the Pad Thai and it just didn't have that authentic flavor I've had many times before. It wasn't a stand-out. Spring Rolls were very good. Friends had the fried rice and stir fried veggies with brown sauce and they have had better at other Thai restaurants. They weren't impressed either. Nicely decorated restaurant....food wasn't that great.
Fast, affordable and friendly. Nice healthy lunch on the go. Had a falafel but will try others. They were generous filling it.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We were visiting from Portland Oregon and wanted to get something other than a burger in our road trip. Called in a takeout order,was quoted 45 minutes wait. We got there to pick up 45 minutes later and were accused of being early and my wife waited another 15+ minutes for the food. The restaurant was fairly empty so she couldn't figure out why our order took an hour. We requested mild because we have a 2.5 year old. It was fairly spicy so we washed the veggies and chicken in the sink. Palak Paneer...paneer was below average. Chicken tikka masala was ok. Naan was below average. Rice was great. Overall averageish Indian food, but fairly overpriced for what we got and the wait. Will not return.

Go get their Nasi Uduk Special! Or their Nasi Uduk Pecel Lele! Located at the corner of 16th and Ritner St, Sky Cafe is a cozy small cafe with good food and get-you-in-the-mood music. Their food price range are in the low side. Cheap and affordable. But their food taste and quality, easily one of the best out there. It is cash only and they do deliver now. This is also one of the best Indonesian restaurant in Philadelphia area. The only down side is that they close at 8pm..
Huge portions for the price. The sancocho is on the thicker side but their avocado salad, plantains, rice and beans is always good.
Worth the wait! I got homemade noodles, I think some were sweet potato noodles. The best falafel I've ever had! Melts in your mouth

Great atmosphere warm with rustic decor, excellent service, excellent food, drinks, pastry , tea variety and Coffe so well rounded on all front. Had fun meal with friends, and Will be back again and again

LOVE this place, right in Chinatown (also visited the one in NYC). I have been at least 6 times the roti kani (I think) is awesome, its light and a great way to start a meal. typically I head from that into the beef rendang, and wash it all down with a Malaysian iced tea (dunno what they put in that stuff). The peanut sauce served with the satay is amazing, I could eat that alone all day if I wanted. I don't have a ton of experience with Malaysian cuisine, but this place to me is absolutely great.

My pita was pretty good. My girl's salad was blah. The food is good and our waitress was nice, but with the name like Pita Jungle, I expected a place that specialized in pitas. Chicken Pita, Pizza Pita, Brisket Pita, Desert Pita! This place was just a Greek Restaurant . If I am in the mood for Greek I will be going elsewhere. Things to note: I could not tell who worked there, There was no uniform what so ever. Maybe it was Halloween night, but there was a Cowboy with a Metallica shirt, a girl with a tank top that had her bra sticking out, a guy with his worn through shirt tucked in only under his gut. If there was a uniform, I would guess it was "Dress as if you just woke up" The Baklava is made with something like condensed Rose water and Orange blossom. It may sound like something cool, but its kind of gross and dry.

Seriously one of the best experiences that I've had at a restaurant/food joint in a very long time. To start off the owner of the cafe, Hassan, is absolutely wonderful. A few friends and I wandered into the shop after another friend recommended we get lassi after brunch. I personally thought that there would be a couple interesting flavors, but I wouldn't have any because I normally don't like lassi. Oh how wrong I was. Not only were the lassis AMAZING (esp the rose, almond and fig) but the atmosphere was absolutely amazing. Hasan is so personable, charismatic and nice that we ended up spending well over 90min at the shop just talking to Hasan and enjoying the lassis. I'm not from Philly but when I come back to the city one of the first things I'm doing is heading back here!! P.S. the make vegan lassis too which I've personally never seen, but I tasted them and they were delicious. Plus all the samples that Hasan gives are basically a glass of lassi, so he is very generous and will also make you a new lassi if you don't like your original order

I love Chinese food and as a newbie to Tucson, it was recommended that I give this place a whirl. It's close to where I live so I thought, why the heck not?! To start, I would not call this "traditional" Asian or Chinese cuisine but it's not Panda Express style either. You have a great fusion of Asian/American cooking that is just oh so tasty. I have eaten here about 4 times (take out only) and each time I have managed to sneak in an order of Walnut Shrimp. I keep telling my self to try new things, but I swear those guys just end up in my bag!! The Orange Peel Chicken gets a repeat appearance in my house also. My husband and I can make dinner and lunch out of the portion you are served....ok sometimes just dinner, but again, it's just that good. My only complaint and I mean ONLY complaint would be their presentation. It kills me how much cabbage and orange slices go into the padding of the take out box BUT it's all fresh, and I do mean fresh, and edible. So it's more of a personal preference than a restaurant error. It's also easily taken care of, so if you're like me, just request less. As far as customer service goes these guys are pretty epic. I have not managed to get in for a sit down yet, but every time I have ordered out I have always gotten great phone service and personal service. These guys really do look and act happy to see me. Dave is one of the managers (or the manager?) and he will greet you just like you're old friends. It's a nice and the icing on the cake of a great place to eat if you're in the area.
Great no frills, sit down Greek restaurant. They make their own pitas and even the salt is from Greece! Delicious food, I love the veggie pita. I just wish they had falafel.

The food is definitely authentic. Even the "mild" version is really, really hot... so be prepared. But regardless, their curry dish was excellent. Soups and dessert were excellent too.
