I don't like they do charge corking fees and I think an "entertainment" fee on Fri...I would go during the week. But great authentic food, the best I have found in the local area.

Not super authentic food but close to it. I ordered the panang curry and my husband had the pineapple chicken dish and they were both fantastic. The presentation on the pineapple chicken was beautiful ( it was served in half a pineapple). The tom ka kai soup was hardy but the coconut flavor was a little weak--overall a 4/5 on the soup. The server was friendly and respectful. The place was dimly lit for a romantic feel. Overall a great place for a date night. It's BYOB. Will definitely go back.

I would recommend Nirvana for folks who love Indo-Chinese food. We had ordered veg Hakka noodles and Veg Manchurian. It was delicious! Restaurant was very clean and the ambience of this place is welcoming. Won't mind coming back again.

Wow, this place has gone down the drain. I used to actually like Pho Bistro because of their amazing noodle and fried rice dishes. After their re-opening due to management issues, the entire place has changed. The servers are still slow, but my regular order of the combo fried rice was disgusting. The rice was yellow and there were very few pieces of meat. It was so salty, I couldn't even finish half of it. The new chicken popcorn is not chicken popcorn. It's f*%king soggy chicken nuggets that's been frozen and breaded so badly, that you can't tell if you're eating toilet paper or food. Won't be coming back.
Decent food for a great price with lots of vegetarian/vegan options at the buffet. They also have an awesome topping bar, which I enjoy.

If you're in the mood for something out of the ordinary, Mood cafe is the place to go (sorry, couldn't resist the pun). I came here entirely based on Yelp reviews, figuring that a near-perfect rating from over 200 reviewers couldn't go wrong. The cafe itself is in a rather charming part of town, and although it is rather small, it also screams cleanliness and efficiency. The owner greeted us immediately, and let us peruse the various items on the menu with an amused look on his face before we finally gave up and admitted we had no idea how to order. He explained what chaat was, and that we shouldn't be overwhelmed by the multitude of choices written on the board - we should just tell him what type of meat we wanted and our desired spice level, and he'd take care of the rest. My boyfriend got lamb, spicy, and I got chicken, medium spice. We also ordered mango and pineapple lassi. The lassi was amazing - I don't think I'll ever be content with a smoothie ever again. Mango taste was light and airy, not too sweet, but enough to satisfy any craving. The Pineapple lassi was very refreshing, and offered the perfect blend of flavor and sweetness. Even better, with our lassi we got a little cup with the leftover drink (I'm guessing they made extra), which was perfect for sharing. When I got my chaat, my first instinct was to say "Eeww, how do these even go together...?" Radishes, cilantro sauce, mangoes, honeyed dates, chick peas, fried dough strips, chicken pieces, several types of mystery sauce? I then dubiously mixed everything together and took a tentative bite. It was an absolute explosion in my mouth, a taste sensation I've never had before. Sweet, sour, savory, salty, spicy, and everything in between - all in perfect balance. Saying that it was delicious would be an understatement. My chicken chaat was seriously awesome, and my boyfriend's lamb chaat was even better. It literally comes down to personal preference what meat/veggie you get, but I don't think you can go wrong. This place makes the 2.5 hour drive from Maryland to Penn worth it. Would I recommend this place? Absolutely. The owner is super friendly, helpful, and service-oriented. The food is a mind-blowing culinary experience. My only qualm with this place is that if you don't order a lassi, the serving sizes for the chaat might not be enough to fill you up completely (but since I did order a lassi, I ended up staggering out the door due to how full I was). The do offer other awesome desserts like gulab jamun and carrot halwa - I'm currently doing stomach expansion exercises so I can fit those as well next time I'm around.

I had to stop by this place for Viet food. I was told that NOLA has a pretty large Viet population so I expected good food. Meh. When you sit down and start noticing the other types of patrons and what they order, you realize you've made a mistake. (Pho with vegetables[???] and no noodles[?!?!?].) The owner came out to talk to all the customers, but when she got to our table, she just said hi and moved on to the next table. When I ordered in Vietnamese, the man looked at me like an alien and said nothing. Rude. As for the pho, it was soooo salty. If it hadn't been salty, I would've said the broth was delicious. I couldn't finish the soup, fearing death from hypertension. Wouldn't return. And wouldn't recommend to anyone else.

South Grand has many delicious good offerings; currently, my brother and I are trying as many as we can. This particular place was the next on our list. The restaurant was inviting but only a few tables were occupied on what should have been a busy Friday night. After dining there, my guess is because the service is not the best. It took a bit for someone to come over and take our drink order by the time they did, we were ready to order our food from an extensive menu. The menu has many great offerings for those who are vegetarian or love seafood along with other meat options as well. We tried the Shrimp spring rolls which were excellent. You get five of them for about $6 and it is the perfect amount for an appetizer. Our main meal arrived and it was delicious as well, though it was not quite enough to eat for my brother. He ordered one of the seafood items while I went for a vegetarian option. I ordered a Pad Sun Wen which was a perfect amount for me; I even took some home. The Thai iced tea is also delicious and was my favorite part of the whole trip. We never were asked if we wanted refills and the only time someone came by, was to drop off our food, drinks or the check. I did observe that this place seemed to do a lot of carry out and perhaps that is the way to go.

One of my favorite restaurants ever. Ingredients are simple but the outcome once they are prepared is exceptional. Got a last minute reservation last Friday after my sister checked into Pennsylvania Hosp to give birth! We wanted to give her some space as her inducement was delayed and also wanted a nice family meal. Arrived for a 5:30 pm res and the only table was outside in direct, bright sunlight. We decided we would cope bc we know how good the food is. As soon a reservation cancelled and a table was free in the shade, they moved us. Between three people split the dip trio, kanella platter, lamb stew, pork souvlaki, and a galaktaboureko (sp). More than enough food. On the dip platter was an outstanding pumpkin dip with scallions and chives that I am currently try to recreate at home. I raised my eye at pumpkin in the spring, but the added herbs/green onion made it light and springy.The lamb was extremely tender and did not have the oiliness a lot of restaurant lamb stews drown in. The serving of stew extremely generous and we each got several large pieces of meat, in addition to plenty of sauce for dipping pita into. The pork souvlaki was cooked perfectly, and plenty favorful, but I would go for the brick chicken if it's on the menu when you go. Can't wait to go back many more times. Servers were sweet and the food came out with time between so we could share and enjoy. Do not skip dessert. Split at least one among the table and order a greek coffee.
It's been fantastic for years and love that I can grab a bottle of wine from home and walk to the restuarant. The rack of lamb has been my favorite. Thanks.

I came here for breakfast one morning. In the spirit of a true Honduran breakfast, I ordered baleadas and horchata (which is good at any time of day). I absolutely loved both of these. Tortillas really make the baleada, and these tortillas were the SHIGGIDY. My boyfriend, not a native baleada-eater, said the tortilla was his favorite part. And I found the horchata was simply amazing! Disclaimer: horchata has a different taste by country, but THIS is how horchata is supposed to taste and is how typical Honduran horchata tastes. As the daughter of a Honduran woman, I have been to Honduras many times and have a true perception of authentic Honduras cuisine. All the dishes, exclusing non-Honduran dishes (sopes, Mexican tacos) look 100% authentic. And I would bet that they are delicious! Notes: DON'T expect anything fancy. This restaurant has the essence of hole-in-the-wall restaurants. DO expect to catch up on your soap operas while dining.

I like the food, and often pick up on my way home late, but the surliness and lack of manners from the drive thru staff just irritates me. There's never a please, thank you, nothing. I've actually stopped going because the lack of common manners (especially from a service based business) just irritates me.

Not impressed. I love their other locations in Metairie but it bothers me that everything is more expensive at this location. I can't believe they charged me for a to go order!! That's crazy. I'm going to stick with Magasin Restaurant instead.

Food is good, but the staff gives off a "wish I were anywhere else" vibe, even when the place is empty. Last time I was there I waited 20 minutes in the car for opening and when I walked in, it was apparently 10:28 and not 10:30, so they showed me the door with a bit of side-eye. I went home and made my own delicious pita sans attitude. If you come well past 10:30, hungry, and with a thick skin, you will love this place.

Until recently I had not tried Thai food, and now some of my favorite dishes I've discovered from this place. Their lunch specials are a great price with two appetizers and a main course. My favorites are the cucumber salad, chicken satay (Tuesdays and Thursdays), and Thai tulips. Their Chu Chee red curry is delicious! I tried it at a "one star" spiciness and now order it at "two stars." It's spicy, but comfortable and the flavor is rich and not masked by the heat. I definitely recommend giving this place a try!

I had the Pad Thai and my girlfriend had the Gai Yang. We also ordered the Fresh Rolls and Tom Yum soup. This place was excellent. Food outstanding, service great, and the place was super cool. I will tell people about this all the time. I look forward to going back.

I ordered lunch here last week and they said it would be ready in 30 minutes so I came 30 minutes later and it was not ready yet. So I waited patiently while they ran around serving the people who were eating and I was looking at them like is my food ready yet? And 20 minutes went by and thet hadn't even started cooking it yet. Another five minutes later, the old lady who works there said to me "we can't serve you." So I left. This is the worst service I have ever seen. I waited almost an hour. I will never be back. The first time was great but this time was the worst service ever.

From a person that ate at Noodle City every time I got a pho craving, this place is SO MUCH better. I mean the place looks way more presentable. Cleanliness is key in my book. Also the seating area is more spacious and you don't feel like you're sitting on someone's lap while waiting for your food. The moment you walk in you can smell the freshly baked bread used for the Bahn Mi. I got the P1 (combination pho) and the S1 (combination Bahn Mi) and an order of spring rolls. The pho is delicious! So much meat and noodles in my bowl of pho and the broth was flavorful. No complaints here. The Bahn Mi is to die for. Bread straight out of the oven and the veggies are super fresh. The meats were seasoned well and cooked perfectly. The spring rolls were delicious as well. All the ingredients were fresh and the peanut sauce was perfect. To top it off, the service was amazing. Very friendly. Food came out pretty quick. I will definitely recommend Phamous Cafe to all my friends and family. 5 stars hands down!!!!
One of the best Thai food in town. Inexpensive, great service and very good quality. We ordered panang curry with chicken and drunken noodles with chicken. They were delicious.

Farmer's markets are really just the best places in the world, aren't they? When I'm away from center city & unable to explore every nook of Reading Terminal, I come here to get my fill. Outside of the fresh, gooey Amish pretzels served at Barbie's (just TRY one), King of Falafel is always my second stop at Newtown Farmer's market. They carry a wide selection of Middle Eastern & Greek cuisine including gyros, falafel, hummus, spinach/feta pie, knish, as well as a variety of homemade salads (my favorite being the marinated beet, carrot and couscous salads). YUM. Service is quick, friendly & sincere - I especially love when the owner's adorable son works the front counter, always with a grin playing across his face. They accept cards here, too (everything except AMEX, I believe). The only reason it's not a five star establishment is the fact that the prices are a tad high and the "fresh" pita is disappointing (a bit too flaky & thin for my liking). Nonetheless, highly recommended. You seriously need to try that beet salad.

Phenomenal & delicious! I have eaten here multiple times and have yet to be disappointed. The food is so fresh and memorable. They are doing it right! The staff have been friendly + attentive as well and the level of care isn't easy to come by. Love it!

We were made to wait 30 min and even then the table was not set up. The hostess was condescending and did not even apologize. Even after that, only 6 out of 8 of us were seated because two earlier guests never left and the restaurant would not ask them to leave because they were 'chef's friends'. The food is great and the service is good but this is unacceptable.

Get the tea - clove, ginger, spice "secret recipe" goodness! The lamb was incredible, & if you like garlic, you'll love the collard greens. The table over ordered lentils - definitely getting them next time. Really good ethnic if you're feeling a change from Indian or Thai - quiet inside, family- owned, and the cook (the mom, I think) brought the food straight to our table.

A gem of a storefront restaurant. Staff was friendly and polite, prices are great. My wife and I split a to-go lamb kebab meal, with a couple falafel added, and baklava. Lamb was quite good; she preferred hers straight, but I thoroughly enjoyed mine with the cucumber yogurt sauce and succulent onions. The two kebabs were served on a bed of delightful smoky rice. The falafel was not what we're used to: they were covered in toasted sesame seeds, which obviously changes the flavor - fortunately, in a very pleasant way. The baklava was tasty, and not overly sweet and gooey, yay! Great price, large portions, and wonderful flavors. We now have a restaurant we love in Boise, as we head back and forth between Colorado and the Northwest. Salaam, y'all!
Love this place.....I order take-out at least once or twice a week! Pho Ga is the best in town!

Gotta get the oxtail. Limited menu, but every thing they do is good. They have modest accommodations but don't let that fool ya. try the sorel. At night it is a night club with some of the best carib selectors. *******They are closed due to a flood. I'm told that the building is to be torn down. Visit the mobile location in the Haddox Pharmacy parking lot on Charlotte. **********

I've been to lunch twice, once on a weekend and another on a weekday. Being very busy on the weekend visit, I was never offered naan and had to ask for water refills several times. The service on the weekday was much better, as the restaurant wasn't 25% full. Both times the buffet was heavy on chicken dishes and sadly one dish tasted very much like the other. They weren't bad, just nothing that stood out. On the first visit the paneer was dry and firm, but was soft and much better on the second visit. The cashier being in the corner and surrounded by tables was very awkward while checking out during the busy weekend. Not sure I'll be back.

This is the best Indian Buffet in town hands down in my opinion. Very clean, elegant atmosphere and professional wait staff for a buffet. The food is superb and served hot. The desserts are very good. I have been eating the lunch buffet here for years and have never had a bad experience. I have eaten dinner here once and it was good, but I highly recommend the lunch buffet.

As a Greek looking for a nice restaurant in Philly, I stumbled upon Zorba's which was excellent!! The food was spot on, and reminded me of the food I grew up with. The service was wonderful and the food was amazing. We came in on a busy Saturday night and were seated right away and taken care of all night!!
I highly recommend the kitfo, gored gored, and gomen. Don't miss the spiced tea or the dark Ethiopian beer either. And the injera is always fresh. Very enjoyable!
cute. small. staff was slow. food was good. egg and peppers on kaiser roll was good, apple oatmeal pancakes were great!

Dooners is a delicious hidden gem that no one really gives a chance. Get the Turkish naan. Get extra tzatziki, and all the veggies, maybe a splash of their magical green hot sauce. The food is incredibly flavorful. Eat it while it's hot, grab extra napkins, and enjoy. This place is perfect after a late night downtown or for a quick lunch.

Not bad at all. The name conjured up images of the rainforest cafe but it was tastefully decorated and the food was good. I wouldn't make bring out of tow. Guests here but might add it to the lineup of places to stop for a quick lunch. Quinoa salad was good and filling

Great addition to St.Albert! We accidentally showed up at 3pm when they were closed, but the guy running it kept it open for us and was nice enough to make our order. What a great place!!! You have to try their wings and meatballs. They use rice flour for the chicken and WOW is it great. Will definitely be back!!

Not a bad place at all!!! We ordered the captain crunch fish platter. The give you a nice size fish, a lot of rice, some salad and avocado. Unfortunately this time they not only forgot the avocado on but didn't give us the extra avocado. They didn't say if they ran out- they just didn't give it to us. We didn't realize it until we got back to the office. We definitely didn't want to go back. We also asked that the one platter have less rice more salad and it seems like the complete opposite was done. Nonetheless, the food was still good. They were very nice and pleasant. Fairly quick service. With the cold, I wonder if they take phone orders.... I would definitely go back- but next time, I will check my order.
Food is very good. The restaurant itself is so hot and humid. It makes it difficult to enjoy your meal.

Mojitos is a great place for date night my girlfriend and I have eaten there several times. They offer indoor and outdoor sitting which in new hope is always a nice option. Not surprising based off their name the mojitos are very good and they offer a lot of very good Cuban and Mexican dishes. When I go I usually get the flautas which are delicious my girlfriend always gets the fries plantains and they are very tasty. I've tried the mexican bowl they serve there which is a mixture of rice beans protein and a few other Mexican flavors which also full of flavor. All and all Mojitos is one of my favorite places to eat in new hope which is saying a lot.

LOVE this place. Delicia is my favorite restaurant in Indy so I'm pretty excited about La Mulita. Got Croquetas De Pollo as an appetizer and it was so filling and delicious and plentiful. I got the chorizo pizza for dinner. WOW! It was gorgeous and I didn't want to touch it but when I did, it was gone instantly. Their drinks? fantastic!
Teeny tiny place. Crazy busy during the lunch rush. We got there a little after 12 and waited maybe 20 minutes for a table. Very good Thai food. Full and happy, we will be back!

Stay way from this place if you want to stay healthy. I have visited this place for couple of time and both times i have experienced different problems. In my fist visit, i found a piece of hair in my food. And in my second visit i just had a egg puff and pastry which upset my stomach instantly. They need to consider this seriously otherwise these guys will be in big trouble.

I can't even lie when I say this place left me with the biggest smile ever! Between the incredible employees and manager (Smiley) and how outrageously flavorful and generously portioned the food was for the price, I definitely plan on going back. To those who love Greek food, this will set a new and delicious standard for you.

Just ate a delicious meal at Tagine. It was a prix fixe menu, $45 per person for a 4 course meal. You can choose amongst different options on the prix fixe menu, but as of yet there is no a la carte menu. There was a very limited kids menu consisting of chicken fingers and fries but the staff were very accommodating when I told them my daughter did not care for meat and they were able to prepare a meal of a hard boiled egg, chick peas and cous cous. The food was very rich and tasty. I'm not understanding previous reviews complaining that the food was bland. All the flavors I experienced tonight were intense and satisfying with the exception of the soup du jour which was Bronzino and Orzo - basically it was vegetable soup and there was no fish to be found in the bowl. My 4 year old liked it though, so I'll let it slide. My friend ordered the traditional Moroccan soup and it was quite good. I had the chicken tagine which was very tender served in a hot decorative pot. Delicious. The dessert was a yummy green tea with a couple slices of a pastry I had never had (not baklava) and it was ok. My friend chose the Turkish coffee which is very strong and bitter. Overall the food is rich and tasty but not very spicy. I did add some salt to a couple things and it really made the flavors pop. This was a great meal and I would recommend to friends

Like the convince of this place to the Residence Inn hotel. The food was excellent and service was prompt. The server brought desert on the house at the end of my meal, which was a nice touch. I will definitely be back for more of the delicious Indian food.

We had our last meal on our recent trip to New Orleans here. The food exceeded our expectations. Everything was absolutely delicious; especially the appetizers--marinated shrimp with jalapeño au jus and the smoked tuna tartar. Definitely well worth a visit.
Red curry is AMAZING! Fresh ingredients. They cater to vegetarians and vegans. My go-to Thai delivery place! Excellent prices for food quality and portions.

The food is consistently great - flavorful and authentic. We had a group happy hour there and the atmosphere by the bar was perfect for everyone to comfortably socialize and snack. I would definitely have another event here!
Delicious!!!!! Friendly staff. Exceptional food. Always looking for a good flan, they didn't disappoint. Everything was very well seasoned.

I love one block from here!!!!! All the food I have ever ordered is DELICIOUS and an incredible value. The roti I ordered was good, but the oxtail blew my minnnnnddd. It was so savory and meaty and full of bones. I wish there was more room to sit down, but we went on a crowded Sunday. I have also tried the cranberry breakfast pastries and the coffee. They're delicious. I can't wait until I have some weird disease so I can go order their tailored juices!

Definitely bring a friend and try a platter if it's your first time. The staff were friendly and timely and the food was just amazing. They were out of ethiopian beer, but I imagine it is a difficult thing to import. I've now tried another ethiopian place in Indy, and am deducting a star simply because this place is more pricy. We were given a plate of injerra and were charged if we wanted more. Unlimited injerra might be too much to ask for, but considering it is what you eat with it was a bit off-putting.

Wow, with all the fab reviews I had been looking forward to trying Bitar's for awhile, but we ended up quite disappointed. We saw a Groupon, nabbed it and gave it a try. We each got combination platters take out. I got the gyro combination. It came with a box that had veggies (lettuce, tomato, onions), gyro meat with tzatziki, as well as bread, a side of hummus, and a side of tabbouleh. I will give it to them, a big portion. I was actually confused whether I should use the bread and make a sandwich or use it for dipping in hummus. With no other options for dipping I used the bread to dip in the hummus and ate the gyro and veggies on their own. Unfortunately, I wasn't enthralled. The gyro meat didn't taste very good, almost burnt, and the tzatziki didn't cover it up. I guess it's a matter of taste, but the tabbouleh was so overwhelmingly filled with garlic that I couldn't eat it. Even the bread was disappointingly very thin, not the nice thickness that I'm used to with pita. I rarely leave a plate unfinished but I just coudn't do it with this one. My girlfriend's platter was also disappointing as she only received two balls of falafel. The hummus was the only saving grace, The hummus was very good, and my girlfriend got a side of a different style of hummus that was amazingly tasty. But, sadly, that only gives one extra star. Because of the great reviews I may willing to go back another time and try something different.

I'm so glad this place is in our neighborhood!! New, hot, a gorgeous room, a solid bar, AND it's open all day. Admittedly the food can be quite rich (check the menu) but it is ALL delicious. They have PERFECTED avocado toast and a sublime biscuit, so even the simple things are amazing. The coconut French toast....will probably kill you but you will die happy. It's so sweet you probably want to share with a few peeps. Dying to try the curried goat next!
Shrimp and Chicken pasta with macaroni and cheese, candied yams and fried cabbage.. it was the best take out I've had in a while! I wish I could give it 10 stars!!

This place is a hole in the wall at US-19 and gandy next to the honeybaked ham store. If you blink you'll miss it, but don't. I ordered the typical bahn mi and was not disappointed. Service was very fast and the restaurant is really clean (if you're familiar with this strip of vietnamese restaurants, you know how rare that is.) Best of all, I think it was about $5 for the sandwich and it was wonderful!

The food is delicious! I had never tried Indian food before and am very impressed. We have already gone back for more! The ginger chicken appetizer is great and we love the chicken tikki masala, as well as the naan bread. Try it!

I am unable to review the actual experience because the restaurant does not stay open as indicated by the hours posted on the door. The kitchen is supposed to be open until 11:00 pm, and the bar until 1:00 am. We walked in at 10:40 pm and was told that the kitchen was closed and that the hours posted on the door are wrong! WELL CHANGE THE DAMN DOOR AND YOUR WEBSITE!

Mood cafe est un des meilleur Chaat que j'ai mange a Philly. Le patron vous accueille et vous conseille avec gentillesse. Il nous a meme offert different lassi a gouter avant que nous passions notre commande et après notre diner pour nous en faire gouter d'autres. J'adore cette place et je la recommande vivement. One of the best place for Lassi and Chaat in Philly. Love this place. The owner is smiling, he customized our food and offer us samples before our order and after to make us discover his food.
Their Mac n cheese sucks because it's not Mac n cheese and they didn't warn me. It has meat in it and doesn't taste anything like real Mac n cheese. I recommend Annie's if you want anything good

This is the second day in a row I've come here to eat. I travel from across town because the food is so good! My go to place for Vietnamese food in Nola! Great food and drinks! Staff is friendly and the bartender makes the best drinks. Prices are reasonable and you get a lot of food. You will bring home a doggie bag. I started with a blueberry caipirinha & shrimp and avocado rolls. The best in town.

Not to be missed. The onion bhajis were huge. Crunchy, tasty. I had the pistachio tandoori chicken, my boyfriend, the butter chicken. Both dishes were delicious. Sometimes in restaurants, butter chicken gets the tougher or dried out pieces, but here the meat was succulent. The menu has classic dishes, as well as a few new ones neither of us had seen. Between the two of us, we've sampled a fair number of Indian restaurants all over the continent. The naan was fresh, the raita a little more salty than sweet, the mango chutney delicious. My mango lassi was refreshing, not too sweet or overly thick. Both of us liked the decor and the service. No complaints. We thought our meals were worth every penny. We look forward to returning.

I order delivery from here all the time and it is always delicious, quick, and affordable. I love the pad Thai, Roti canai, and beef skewer. The food is always great, never any complaints! The delivery is always quick and the guy who delivers it is super friendly and nice. I have nothing but praise for this place. I've never eaten in the restaurant itself, so I can't speak on that, but the delivery and take out food is great!
The best soft shell crab I have ever had! The sautéd mussels were amazing too! Great service. A bit small, very loud, and cash only.

I started coming here for the delicious coconut curry soup and gyros. The happy hour prices on drinks and food are also a plus. About two months ago, I began my journey into vegetarianism. Pita Jungle is now one of my "go to" places to eat out. The food is always tasty and service ia consistent. You can even bring your carnivore friends...plenty of options for everyone.

My favorite place in St. Louis. The foods are delicious, the servers are very considerate, the ambience is elegant. They just renew their lunch menu which has a starter, a main course and beverage for just $9.95. The quality of the lunch is even better than other restaurants' dinner! Highly recommended!
The Oysters are the best I've have ever had Scott the master chief has a real passion food

The service was fine and the food was tasty but I thought the ambiance was a bit lacking. The menu reminded me a bit of Taco Bell.... A few key ingredients shuffled around to make a variety of different options. We ordered the cold appetizer platter. It was so small that people at our table thought it was something that was compliments of the chef. This was a fine place but will not be a go to staple for me.

One extra star for atmosphere. Come here for the atmosphere and to drink only. Don't even get an appetizer. The entree's were horrible too. Bland, not very creative, and beyond the sides nothing tastes flavorful at all. Atmosphere is nice. Service SUCKS.

I've been here like 4 or so times and have been very satisfied with the service and quality of the food. Most of the dishes are $9-15. I would recommend going here for some cheap and tasty thai dishes.

Good food, poor service. This is the type of place I want to like. I really want to support more adventurous restaurants in Isla Vista in hopes to garner more businesses that will try something more brave than the standard pizza, burger, and burrito that our town seems to know and love more than is healthy. Unfortunately, I just can't give this place my business. #1 It's dirty. I'm all for a hole in the wall where everything isn't spic, spam, shiny, and chrome, but this place made me uncomfortable to eat inside. It's just straight up not clean, not to mention visually unappealing. Lotta grey and brown and weird spots everywhere. #2 It's slow This might not be such an issue if #1 wasn't a problem. But since it's an uncomfortable place to sit and wait, waiting 15-20 minutes in an empty restaurant where I'm afraid I might catch something isn't fun. Now that I've vented... The food here is actually not bad. The meats are juicy, tender, and fresh. The portions are large. The hummus is excellent. So, if you can wade through the atmosphere and experience, and are craving some mediterranean food, then call in your order and make sure you get it TO GO. Otherwise, try somewhere else.
This place is fantastic. The staff is always friendly and helpful and the food is amazing! I have yet to have something that was "ok" from here, highly recommend.

Came here for lunch, been back ever since. I have eaten at many local Indian Restaurants in the area, and love the fact that this restaurant has fresh to order Nan, friendlier wait staff, and all the food tacked on more flavor that its competitor up the street on the 11th floor. Our waiter was very nice, kept our drinks full, and made sure that the buffet had everything we wanted. I would highly recommend the Chicken Tikka Masala here, the flavors in the sauce were nice with a small kick to keep you coming back. I hope to see this restaurant take off, it was very slow when we were in at 11:30 during the week.

Tried this place for lunch. The specials are reasonably priced with an average of 9.00 that comes with 2 sizes. I chose chicken pad Thai with salad and egg roll.. I was surprised to find the salad dressing was strong with a cinnamon bite to it. The egg roll very tiny but good ! My lunch date had the chicken fried rice with soup ( chicken rice) and an egg roll. Food overall tasted fresh and hot!!! I would recommend for lunch definitely!!

Waited over 30 min for my carry out order. Never again Zoe's. That's totally disrespectful to your customers. And my cauliflower bowl was put together so carelessly, like it was literally thrown together (picture attached). I feel ripped off.

Well, I don't mean to be rude in any way. This place had a friendly server, fairly quick service, and lots of great outdoor seating if I'd wanted to sit there. I got a large jerk chicken platter, which was covered in a delicious, almost teriyaki-ish sauce and came with plantains (mmmmmm, plantains), But in all honesty, I've become a regular customer at Gigi & Big R's, in University City or by 30th Street Station. If you've ever eaten there, you'll probably understand why I'm bringing them up. Their menu is very similar, but their meals are bigger, cheaper, and fall-off-the-bone tender. If you're on South Street and you have a craving for spicy food, Jamaican Jerk Hut will do - but I'd recommend you man up and take a walk to try the real deal.

I'm not an expert in this specific cuisine but it was what I expected based on other places I've been. We ordered the meal for two where we had a large selection of different items to choose from. Everything was good, nothing really stood out. I just kept going in a circle when choosing what I was going to try next. I really enjoyed the coffee and the tradition they shared with us after the meal. I would highly recommend it. This place is casual but more on the quiet side. It's a good spot to catch up with friends and to take your time and really enjoy the experience of this cuisine and culture.

Amazing place hidden behind the neon lights. I found this place via Yelp and gave it a try. I tried the egg rolls and a main dish. I was not to please with the egg rolls but the main dish was amazing. I will return in a few weeks. Great place for a cold fall night or winter

The Good: We had such a great time when we visited Olio recently for a lovely ladies dinner. The service during our meal was impeccable. Our server was totally sweet and fun. The cocktails were brilliant. The wine list had begging for more (literally begging - they were out of our choice wine that evening). The food was outstanding and we savored every morsel. The Not-so-good: OLIO! I wanted to give you 4 stars but I simply cannot. Blasting Bjork with 1 1/2 hours until closing time just wasn't cool. Does that trick ever really work?

This place was pretty awesome! I had the pan seared grouper with wild rice and charr grilled okra while my roommate had the burger. The flavor of my grouper dish as a whole was spot on. The sauce was palette filling and the freshness of the grouper balanced out any extra umami I had. I had a super refreshing drink called mucha muchacha. Tequila with chartreuse and cucumber and lime with smoked salt. Clean cut with a very bright finish and supple smoky flavor. The only reason I'm giving four stars is because when I hear pan seared I'm thinking crispy skin. My grouper had semi crunch to the bite, which may be due to the mustard seeds that were plated on top. And my roommate burger came out first and she finished half of it before my dish came out. Even though we were at the bar I still had certain expectations. Overall great drinks, great dish, and a cozy atmosphere. I just moved here to east Nashville about a mile down the street so I will definitely be back!

I had the Cap'n Crunch Tilapia Burrito (with hot sauce) and the Taro Milk Tea. I really liked the burrito! It was filling, the ingredients made a good match and it was hot. The Taro Milk Tea was perfect too. Not too sweet but sweet enough to taste refreshing! And most especially, the guys in the truck are the best - super nice and had a good time conversing with them.

Just ate here, service was great! D place was quiet, it seems very unknown . It's a little restaurant at the side of an Iraqi market. At first I was a little concerned about the 12. dinner plates, but my waiter pointed out the $5 sandwiches on the back menu. Had a lamb kebab sandwich for 5 bucks it was very tasty and filling. This restaurant is an unknown hole in the wall, lacks ambience despite the Middle Eastern pictures and decor . Nevertheless, it is very delicious and you cannot beat the price!

I really wanted this place to be awesome. I eat pho very often. I arrived at 11:30 and they told me that the kitchen wouldn't be ready for another 20 minutes. Okay, I had some coffee at mugshots and went back. I ordered the steak and tendon pho. It took 20 minutes to come out, and it didn't have tendon. I brought it up and they brought me out a plate of tendon. The large is very large, so I asked for a container. They had me wrap it up. The check came and it was for 2 entrees I didn't order. I brought it up and they refunded my card and charged the correct amount. All in all, it took about 1.5 hours to eat a bowl of pho. It should take 30 minutes, tops.

Hi everyone. This is my first review ever. I gave this place a 5 star for three reasons. 1. The food, which is excellent. 2. The price, well within my modest budget. 3. Most important the feeling I get when I come here to eat. I feel like I have walked into a friends home for dinner. The man and his wife who own this place are so nice.(other staff also are all great). I am so happy with this place. I take my friends from out of town to eat here because out of all the choices in the UCD they ask for this one. So, if you haven't tried it yet, give it a whirl. You will not be disappointed.

We visited Zeppoli on a weekend to celebrate a birthday. I made reservations and we were seated 5min early. The staff was friendly, attentive, well spoken, and checked in on us several times during our meal. The mixed green salad was good, a little overpriced for greens with shaved cheese on top. The spinach and ricotta gnocchi were amazing, pillow soft and really flavorful despite their light texture. Our entrees were rib-eye steak and the fisherman stew. The stew was really delicious, and he loved the rib-eye. The desserts were good (Zeppoli and sorbet), but were very overpriced at $9 each. It's BYOB, but you'll still ring up a bill. The small, intimate dining room is really nice, and although the tables are close, you still feel like you're having a private conversation. I was very pleased with our dinner and will return again, probably forgoing the dessert next time.

We have always loved the banh mi sandwiches here but our experience this weekend was disappointing. I got a noodle salad with shrimp, spicy pork and an egg roll. The pork lacked that char grilled flavor. The egg roll (which contained ground shrimp and pork) had a funny smell and tasted off. When my husband tasted it he said the meat was bad and not to eat it. We told the server and he brought out Lilly who insisted the egg rolls are made fresh daily and it was the taro root in it that tasted that way. We didn't say anything else but my husband, who is Vietnamese and owns his own restaurant said it was not the taste of taro because it's something he eats. He knows the smell of bad meat. I'm disappointed she did not at least offer to take the uneaten egg roll off our bill or replace it. Not surprisingly I got sick that afternoon from that one bite of egg roll and was in the bathroom and felt awful the rest of the day. I typically have a cast iron stomach but not this time. I don't think I'll be eating egg rolls again there.

Very watered down version of Asian cuisine... These are the owners of the original SK noodle in sparks. It sucked when they were there, but luckily for them they didn't have any competition close by. Now the tides have changed and less than a mile away you have Golden Flower and Pho 777... I went to SF kitchen once and I told the owners they needed to step up their food game cause crappy fails when you have the option of excellent... Avoid SF kitchen

We spent our New Years Eve at Gastro and had a wonderful time. Friendly waitstaff and bartenders, relatively cheap drinks, and a wonderful atmosphere with great music. Gastro is clean, gorgeous, and also has delicious good. It is small, but doesn't pack people in, so there is definitely enough room to order drinks and dance. A great place!

I could eat the Naam Salad every day for the rest of my life. The Paneng Duck is out of this world. They recently expanded into the adjacent building and for good reason. The food and atmosphere is perfect.

This place looks a little clubby on the inside and that's not really my bag anymore, but the outside is so lounge-y and inviting! There are sofas and umbrellas and even bar seating outside to enjoy the amazing Beach Drive people watching. Their wine list is extensive, so don't let the place fool you! I've only had some appetizers there including the truffle parmesan popcorn and the pickled veggies; both delicious. I'd come back and cocktail al fresco anytime!

Haven't had better food in Tampa, this place is delicious and highly recommended. The food and atmosphere is great but the staff and owner are extremely kind, genuine, and proud of their operation. Go and you'll enjoy the experience.

I went to Jasmine Rice on a Friday at 8pm. It was empty when we got there, but boy did it fill up! There were three of us at a very cozy table. We had the spring rolls and the ginger scallion dumplings. I loved both. The lighting wasn't great, and the door kept opening and it was COLD in there. They have a curtain, presumably to keep this from happening, but it was open and not in use while we were there. I would imagine (and hope) that they use this as we get deeper into winter. I hate eating when I'm uncomfortable. I had green curry, which was good, but not the five pepper spice I had requested. If you really like your Thai food spicy, ask for more than the five on the menu. I couldn't taste the spice at all. The food was good, and the portion appropriate. None of us had leftovers, which happens to me more often than not at Thai places. My dinner mates also noted that the spice level was extremely low in their dishes. We probably won't go back, but it was fine and the location was super convenient.

For me long awaited and much anticipated and it exceeded expectations. I quit watching Top Chef after her season because of the obviously rigged ending. When I found out she was coming here it was very exciting. The cocktail list is so creative and will vemiently compete with the market here. The food was everything I expected from Chef Nina and more. The service was surprisingly smooth especially for a restaurant only open for over a week. Look out locals.....this one is a must dine and will easily be rotated into your go to places.
Who would think there would be great sushi in Nashville! Umami nailed it with their Umami and Roulette rolls

Pretty good lunch buffet but not my favorite in town. I came here on a Monday because my usual go-to was closed. The food is good, but I think the flavors are better (and the naan) at Flavor of India!

the place is a bit small so my party of 4 thought we would be served pretty quick since it was after the lunch rush and we ordered 3 Pho's and 1 beef cubed plate. after 10 mins the waiter came to our table and said they don't have the beef cubes so we ordered fried rice. then after another 20 mins. he said your food will be out shortly....waited another 10min. finally our food came the pho did not have enough noodles or beef and the taste was sour.
Very good place to dine out. The quality of dishes ordered was really nice. Would definitely recommend this restaurant for Vietnamese-Thai food lovers

I waited six weeks before moving walking distance away from Parada Maimon to try it after living the area for a few. SIX WEEKS! I can't stress that point enough. What a mistake! If you are in the area, definitely stop in here for some comforting Dominican food. That half chicken lunch special is all sorts of wonderful. Very, very flavorful although some may find it to be a bit salty. Both the fried and the sweet plantains are great, but I am partial the sweet ones. The fried ones could be a bit crunchier. Those rice and beans are very hearty and comforting. Can't go wrong with desserts or the patties. I did try delivery via GrubHub once and the delivery guy was unfortunately not that friendly, but the food made up for it. When I did GrubHub pickup orders, I believe the person I spoke to was the owner upon arrival and he said that he wants me to call the restaurant instead so they get to know their customers better. Now that is great customer service!
This place is excellent. Pricey but excellent. It has a unique ambiance. Its an unexpected treat in narberth.

An amazing place to sit and listen to live music during the week. They have delicious burgers, and their signature cocktail really adds to the whole experience. Sitting outside is really where it's at, you can people watch, listen to music, make new friends, or just fill an empty stomach all from the comfort of their shaded, air cooled couches outside. The weekends are fun as well, although it gets much busier at night, and they have a DJ outside to keep the night lively. People watching is the best on a Saturday night.

Decided to come here for the first time and it definitely did not disappoint. There was one server/host and she was very friendly, greeted us with warm smiles and consistently checked up on us and the other tables to make sure we had everything we needed and handled it very well. I tried the Curry Goat and it was delicious; the meat was falling off the bones and was very tender and flavorful. But if you get this, just be warned that you really have to love curry because it's packed with curry flavor! :P My boyfriend got the jerk turkey and loved it, also very tender. And the plantains were done just right. The chef (or possibly the manager - I'm not entirely sure) came out to check on us as well. The food is also very filling because I could only eat half of my plate. I didn't even have to ask for a box, our server saw that I was done and asked if I needed one. Also the byssop drink is fantastic. I highly recommend it.
This place sucks. The food is way overpriced and comes in small portions. My burger was $13 and didn't even come with fries. The service was slow and the food wasn't even that good. Never going back.
Very friendly staff. Clean and updated interior. Excellent Pho Tai(steak pho). Extremely fresh bean sprouts, lime, and basil. Tender steak with no gristle. Delicious.

Ate here for the first time recently. Quaint atmosphere, somewhat dark inside. They do have a few outside tables. The octopus was fabulous!! Very tender and great flavor. However, they need to update the menus. They have pasta with grated cheese as an option with the meatballs. When we asked for it they said, "no pasta" I pointed out that it was on the menu. The server simply said "Oh those are old menus". Also, lunch and dinner are on the same menu. We arrived at 4:30pm and were told it was time for the dinner menu. The lunch menu offered the octopus and the "spread" sampler at one price and the dinner menu offered the same items at $2 & $3 higher. I would definitely go back for the octopus!!

Okay, this place isn't perfect. The atmosphere isn't particularly fantastic, but it is cute, clean and comfortable--aside from it usually being semi-deserted. However, I think the food is fabulous! I've always LIKED Miss Saigon; however, all of their pho is made with chicken or beef broth. As a vegan, I don't appreciate that there isn't any way to enjoy pho there! At Iluvpho, they have vegetable broth, and the pho is pretty good. What I'm truly addicted to is their spring rolls. Miss Saigon has absolutely nothing on these crispy tofu, cilantro and lettuce rolls. And the peanut sauce is deeeeelish. I usually get these and the number 33-- a vegetarian bahn mi (lalalala- don't care to ask if the bread has butter in it because I'm pretty sure it does). Also, did I mention the prices? An order of huge spring rolls and a bahn mi with tax sets me back less than $8. As far as bahn mi goes, this place has it down. The bread is warm and soft while crunchy on the outside, the vegetables are semi-spicy and pickled, but not soft, and the tofu inside is also awesome. They also have great noodle dishes, a few of which are vegan friendly. As for meat dishes, they have plenty, many of which looks fabulous. My non-vegetarian friends regularly enjoy accompanying me here. As a side note, the LARGE pho is really large. If you get an appetizer or a boba tea, I'd recommend the small pho, which is usually more than enough for a hearty eater like myself. Anyways, I think this place is great and deserves more business. The service has always been more than adequate. I like that the main server periodically checks to make sure water glasses are full and customers are happy, but for the most part, helps out in the back and doesn't hover. I gave this place 5 stars because I'm super impressed by their fresh, clean vegan dishes, addictive appetizers, decent prices, a comfortable-enough atmosphere and, what I consider to be, nearly perfect service.
Ok food. Bad attitude... Sat here for 20 mins, and didn't even know who our server was. No one even came to ask if we need water... The restaurant was only half full at the time. :)
Worst pad Thai and "white" rice ever. The white rice I got is the same color as my ORANGE pad Thai

Let me start off by saying YUMMY. Absolutely amazing food located on Busch the area is a bit sketchy but inside the atmosphere is clean and homy. Came in around 1pm during lunch time it was a bit busy staff was short with only two waitresses who were hustling and bustling with Takeout orders on the phone in the store writing checks and taking care of a full store manager had to come out and help although thats a feat for anyone unless your superman, so it was understandable for the food owing out a little later then usual. Staff was very friendly although busy, manager was very friendly as well drinks and bread were refilled even though it looked like the staff had no time to spare. I felt terrible for one of the young waitresses in the headscarf on staff probably 17 or 18 being berated by a customer and his friends for the food being slightly late as she continuously apologized he asked her to quiet down and "respect herself" as though he was some paternal figure! called out the manager and rudely expressed himself to the manager along with 3 of his friends the girl was a child in comparison to him who could pass off as her grandfather very uncivil and very arrogant which led me to want to write this review felt very sorry for her indeed. Had i not been too busy enjoying my food i would have said something to him personally. My Order was Sampler Appetizer 2 Chicken Shawirmma Sandwiches and lentil soup Dessert was Chocolate covered Baklava fingers with chocolate drizzled on top amazing with Hot mint tea! A M A Z I N G

The food here is not atrocious, it's no better for worse than a typical Indian restaurant. The 1-star rating is definitely for the management attitude. I will never return to that place again. First the pros: - The mango lasse is tasty. - The wait staff is usually very polite and attentive. Cons: - There were only 3 small pieces of naan, and they were rock hard. The naan is my favorite part of the meal, but they wouldn't bring out fresh naan until the pieces of cardboard with gone, so we took it and put it aside. Then, 30 min late, they brought out the naan, and although we initially tried to wait, we were pretty much done with our meal by then. - The management is downright rude and awful. I had called to ask for the buffet price about a week before we went to eat there. We went in for the buffet and before we started eating, we informed the waiter that we were planning on using a Groupon. When we got the bill, we were charged a higher price than what I was told over the phone. I asked them about it, and they rudely told me that I must've heard wrong. Then, we tried to use a Groupon, and was told that it didn't apply to buffets. However, our waiter never told us that the Groupon couldn't be used (but in fairness, he might not have known), and the FAQ portion of the Groupon specially said that it could be used for buffets, which I pointed out and showed them on my phone, but they said that it was a mistake on part of Groupon. They further explained that they don't make much money off of the buffet (which I don't believe when you charge $17/pp and serve luke-warm food and rock hard naan), and so they can't allow the use of the Groupon, but they offered to allow us to use at a subsequent, dinner dine-in visit. Oh How Nice! NOT!!! I think it was a bait and switch, so we paid, contacted Groupon and received a refund, and I will never, ever, go back to that place again.

My son absolutely had to take me to this adorable little restaurant in Manayunk. It is GREAT. There's an incredibly comfortable dining area with couches and tables. Kind of how I would imagine the perfect casual restaurant. Plus tables out front. But more than the atmosphere is the incredibly good tasting food and truly wonderful people who run the spot. Delicious, inexpensive, huge portions, all the things we tried were great. We ordered a bit too much and had to take some home. The owner added more pita and stuff to the take out bag just because he's a nice guy.

Family owned thai restaurant. Service, food, ambiance all have been consistently excellent. One of the BEST thai Food I have eaten in America. I have been there several times and taken back guests. Never been disappointed. Since they have limited seating we best enjoyed it on weekdays. However, they are very efficient even when it is crowded. Expect to wait for 20 minutes or so if you go in peak hours. So make sure if you visit Nashville or are living here eat here a few times ! This place should not be missed out.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: Good place for lunch, portion is good and service is decent. Food quality is so-so. Soup was just aweful thou, tasted like soy suace with hot water with some cabbage in it. Bwwaaaa. Thai food was okay, had pad thai. I also tried spicy tuna rolls (good way to camofulage the bad tuna. hahaha), but it was decent. Will I go back? Maybe, but for lunch.

Very good Asian mix of Japanese, Thai and Chinese food. Coconut soup is very good and staff is very nice. Owners changed a few months ago but food still seems very good. Staff is very friendly. Update: moved to 5 stars as the food is always excellent quality. Best Asian food in the Mt Laurel area

As a professional photographer who relies on meeting clients outside of my place of business I find La Va Cafe to be one of the friendliest. The staff is helpful, generous, and nice. The coffee is stellar as is the food. Weekends are crazy crowded but as long as I get here 30 minutes before my clients a table large enough for my group always opens up. I always tip the baristas for being so accommodating to my circumstances.
Simply the best. A reason to get up in the morning. I don't even know what to eat when this place is closed.

This is probably going to be my gold standard for Indian restaurants. No place I ever went to before Amber Indian Restaurant could compete. I went there for their weekend lunch buffet and the selection was enormous. I also really liked the fact that they brought you fresh naan to the table. That was really awesome as well. I had went there for dinner once and thought the Amber Special (Chicken) was delicious. There was enough for leftovers (2 additional meals spread over my own home-made basmati rice).

I had passed by Bui's a million and one times, but never really thought much of it. I don' know why, but I just was not drawn to trying it. So, the other day, like I often do, I whipped out my I-phone, pulled up my Yelp app, and decided to see what was near by and rated well. I was surprised to see after 40 reviews Bui's Lunch Truck had 4 1/2 stars, with a healthy littering of 5 star reviews. So, I had to try it. A lot of reviews mentioned their breakfast sandwiches, but I am usually not the breakfast food for lunch type. So, I decided on the Mr. Bui special sandwich. In a nutshell, it's a cheese steak with peppers and teriyaki sauce. The bread was a little on the crisp side. It tasted okay, but I prefer it a little softer. And, to be honest, for the extra buck, the peppers and teriyaki sauce were not worth it. But getting past that, the steak and cheese were good. If I was to go back, I'd get a basic cheese steak. Not one of their variations of a cheese steak. Either that, or I go for breakfast and find out what all of the rave is about.

Came in for a Bloody Mary. I asked if they make good ones and the waitress said yes. All they did was use the liquor store mixer and added Vodka. It was pretty gross. We didnt get coasters with our glasses and it didnt seem like the people at the bar really knew what they are doing. I checked in on Yelp and got a promo that said "with check-in free dessert". I showed this to the bartender and she had no clue what I was talking about. She said she will ask and never did. I never got my dessert. I didnt try any food but hope the kitchen is better than the bar. Service wasnt that great and neither were the drinks.
Ordered pad Thai, pineapple chicken and an order of wings as takeout..... yummy yummy yum! Next time I plan to dine in- it's very casual and chill inside

I really feel like I need to give Mint a solid 3 stars. Because I think it is just that - 3 stars. A review recently came out that suggested Mint should stick to the "Vietnamese" cuisine as opposed to the "modern" that's also in their name. I completely disagree. The more traditional Vietnamese dishes were... flops. The egg rolls were almost inedible. No flavor, terrible texture, super watery peanut sauce. Blech. However, the fried chicken and waffles? Yes, please! The Kim-chi Burger? Another!! This was all so good. The flavors were modern yet very Vietnamese inspired. The atmosphere inside is beautiful - such a great renovation. Service was fine, nothing bad.

Ate here last year and I was disappointed this time to see that much of the Lebanese influence has been dropped from the menu. Pizza is still great, although on the expensive side. The dinner entrees are now mainly steak-type selections supported by only one middle eastern main.

Ali Baba has been my savior once or twice post-Pat'Os/Boondocks liver assault/battery. And that's all it's been good for! Because it's nowhere as delicious as Lebanon's and the others, but when you're "in need," everything tastes awesome. I am fairly sure this is one of the first places I visited in the French Quarter, ever, immediately post-Katrina. But I had abstained from consuming the goods because I had not yet learned to trust French Quarter eats. Anyway, the owner/employees here are a bit odd. The couple of times I resorted to Ali Baba, I distinctly recall feeling awkward, as if I should NOT be there. At any rate, I've only tried the falafels, as fried chickpea mush balls always seems like a clever intoxicated way of ingesting something fatty, yet protein-y (so I don't feel completely awful about myself). They were always a bit too mealy and crumbly, and over crisp. Not completely horrendous, but as someone who has consumed falafel all over the place, they were just average. I'm pretty sure the last time I ingested the falafels, I refused the finish the last two and convinced my starving friend to consume instead (just wasn't feeling it after the first few!). Nonetheless, Ali Baba is a most excellent vegan/vegetarian choice in the quarter, especially during those late nights.

Where do I begin? At the less than decent service? The sketchy part of town? The fact that I'm pretty sure the two ladies talk about you loudly in Vietnamese while you're paying but you don't understand a single word? No. I'll start with the INCREDIBLE food they serve. I mean, I drive all the way out from Brentwood to eat there. Hands down the best Bahn Mi I have ever had in my entire life. Even the bubble tea (which is not really homemade) is great. I can't stress enough. The Bahn Mi is better than any other sandwich I've had ever. I'm not kidding. Get the Steamed Bahn Mi, not the barbecue. You'll see. You'll see. Favorite restaurant. I promise you'll love it.

The thing about Kanella is strange. The restaurant is only half a block to my apartment, so I pass by it all the time and after trying it for the very first time when it first opened. I couldn't honestly call myself a fan. What can I say? I ordered the kebob and everybody who knows anything about Greek/Turkish food is that kebobs are the most generic thing on the menu and can't really reflect the skills of the chef. On top of that the restaurant is popular and the space is small with tables arranged very closed to each other and I'm a bit claustrophobic. At the end of the meal I freaked out a little and had to run out of the restaurant to catch a breath. After that experience I was a bit afraid to go back. Then there was a pretty long and angry respond to a newspaper review that got pasted on the window of the kitchen, I'm sure I'm not the only one who got weirded out by it. It wasn't until Food Network's The Best Thing I've Ever Ate that got me pay more attention to my Greek neighbor. I went back for the Cyprus breakfast promoted by the program and it was good, real good. Everything on the plate was done perfectly; Eggs are fried to a crispy edge with the center remains raw, bread is toasted to a crunchy goodness, lounza ham is salty and dry is a good way. and can I just scream how I love the Halloumi cheese especially when it's fried to a crispy outside and a melty inside? I can have that everyday and be content. A second visit to the same plate proves that it's better to visit on weekdays when there are less patrons and the cooks can pay more attention to the food. On weekends, the quality can suffer because of the rush. The wait staff is knowledgeable and friendly, the decor simple and homey. I think they took the kebob out of the menu and I remember the dip being stellar. They also seemed to have a cooking class held on weekends sometimes, check their glass window. Even off-putting at times, a grouchy Greek chef may signifies a chef of standards. Now only if they can find a bigger place to host their restaurants.
Wow. This might be my fave restaurant in all of Nashville. I will be back next time I'm in town...

My daughter and I came recently for lunch on the recommendation of a local shop owner. My cucmber mojito was refreshing. The salad was typical. The ropa vieja was great. The tres leche cake was superb. The service was fast, a little too fast, as we were not finished with one course before the next. The music was okay and the atmosphere was nice. Lunch was about $40 including tip, which is typical for New Hope. We would return.

Went here for dinner last night with two friends and we all love Indian food. Everything was fantastic and I am just sad that I don't live in the area anymore so I can't eat there more often. The butter chicken is amazing and I would highly recommend it.
Had the pho ga bowl and the roast pork Bahn mi poboy and both were great. I will definitely go back.

Disclaimer: I am not an Indian cuisine aficionado but I do like a nice chicken vandaloo or chicken sagwala! With that in mind I will proceed. Finding new restaurants has become our newest game at work. A co-worker of mine suggested Ruchi for their lunch buffet. Compared to other Indian buffets in the area they have a great selection. The atmosphere was pleasant and the decor very tasteful. It looks like a great place to go out for dinner in the evening. They definitely know their customers. Each piping hot dish was nicely labeled and told you what was in there - a definite plus! One drawback - when we went hey didn't have rice pudding for dessert and considering that is one of my favorite dishes it was a big disappointment. Everything else was pretty good. Next time I would try them for dinner so you can get some real unique Indian dishes instead of the typical buffet fare.
I had the chicken wings with the sticky rice with a chocolate peanut butter boba tea and I have to say this place is fantastic.

I have been seeking a pho & bahn mi place since arriving from Chicago. So happy to have landed here thanks to a recommendation from a Chinese Market employee. Haven't tried the pho yet but the prices and bahn mi were just right!

I can't say enough good things about the food here! I didn't realize until lately how often I stop in when I'm craving a spicy snack. Their Jamaican beef patties are out of this world. The combination of the flaky crust and spicy beef filling are enough to turn any skeptic into a true fan. I learned today that they are moving to 70th and Michigan in a few weeks and nearly shed a tear! I still plan on making the drive there to get the fall off of the bone oxtail and sweet plantain. Do not let the exterior or location of this place fool you. It's a true gem!
Service is a little bit slow but the food is wonderful every time and the prices match similar Indian restaurants. Would definitely recommend.

This is probably my favorite family owned Indian restaurant for lunch. The large selection of authentic food is so delicious. All of the food is prepared with fresh ingredients and great spices. The ambiance is very nice, while listening to Music that is befitting to your experience here. Joy, my serve is always friendly and happy to see me on each visit. I like having my meeting here for business and meeting my friends too. You have a choice to enjoy the all you can eat buffet or order from the very nice menu. The restaurant is tucked away in the strip mall in front of More than coffee drive thru shop. This is a must place to visited if you are in the West county area. I love tasting food from all cultures. Yes, I will be back to enjoy this nice food again! Gloria~

Hey! So the manager reached out and made it right. The new batch of fries were amazing as well as the dipping sauce. Mistakes happen and unfortunately the chef never took responsibility for the bad batch but as a manager she made it right. And the new batch was next level- light with just the perfect amount of crisp....really hot and fresh. Completely different from the previous experiment. Overall wishbone makes great quality food-but like I said maybe that day we just had a bad batch.

Great food, great service! Overall a great atmosphere and delicious Greek food. Price is great, though bringing your own wine eliminates the alcohol portion of the bill. Win/win really. You may have difficulty getting a table so get there early. Also, bring cash, no credit cards.
I always get their chicken biryani. Medium spicy is very spicy! Their naan and goat karahi is delicious too!
Small hole in the wall with delicious food!

Another local gem. I go here for take out at least twice a month. They have an indo-Chinese section in the menu that is amazing & it's something I don't always find at Indian restaurants. I'm a veg head & I've not been disappointed by any of the choices so far.
I love the fish dishes. For the price, the food is absolutely delicious and staff have always been friendly!

This place is SO GOOD. Seriously, go here. It's "modern Israeli" food which is absolutely delicious and they have small plates that are perfect for sharing. The Deluxe hummus and the octopus are a must try! Also, my fiancé took me here on the night he proposed and there was some mishap with our table but the staff was so awesome and totally made it up to us. We were able to dine in their private room downstairs which was so cozy and wonderful and they even comped part of our meal. We've taken out of town guests here as well and it's always a hit!

I have never tried Vietnamese food before and I must say my first try was pretty tasty. We ordered a take out, I got rice noodle salad with fried pork egg rolls and chargrilled beef and a bunch of other stuff in it. It was very good, I absolutely loved the egg rolls. Next time I order I'll probably ask for more fried egg rolls. The prices are also relatively cheap for fairmount area. I will definitely come back
I have celiac and they Have excellent everything. Had the calamari and fish and chips. Yum! I heard one of the chef's have celiac.

We were in Nashville for a conference and wanted to get out of the resort and get some Thai food. We happened to pick this place based on the reviews. 5 thumbs up. Saved my job as the execs liked it. The ginger tea, followed by the Tom yum and red curry. They were all excellent choices. Finished the meal with the coconut ice cream. The hostess was very nice and accommodating with the "spice level" requests. Awesome place.
Do not let the name fool you! This is the worst pho I have ever had in my life. I did not try the Chinese food so I can not comment on it. They place is also kind of dirty

Lilly's cafe is amazing! The service is super warm and extremely fast, and the food is delicious. There's a great vegetarian menu, and everyone should try the vegan egg rolls -- they have taro and they taste like little savory donuts!

I went here about a year ago for my birthday. We had a very large group--over 20--and were assured we would have a room reserved to ourselves. When we showed up, the previous party booked for our room wouldn't leave. There's no bar area to wait in at Marrakesh, so we were relegated to our entire horde milling about in the cold outside. No worries, however--the manager brought out glasses and wine bottles while we were waiting in the alleyway. We also had all our wine comped for the evening, a nice gesture considering the fact that we were waiting outside for a good 50 minutes. Once we finally got our room, everyone had to crowd onto the various seat cushions and ottomans, but the experience more than made up for the tardiness. The 7-course meal was awesome and delicious, but definitely briskly paced--a downside if you have gustatory ADD, such as myself. I would have certainly preferred to have more time to savor each dish as it got brought out. Oh, and there are belly dancers, if that's your thing.

Our favorite place for pho in Tampa. Be prepared, it looks like a dump. In a very unassuming strip mall off Waters it is worth braving the wonky parking lot and awkward intersection to get in and feast on the most delicious pho Tampa's got. They were notched down one star because they don't carry ANY vegetarian options. I asked once why and the owner said they used to but never sold any and it kept going bad. I get it. But that sucks. I order the large bowl of Pho Ga EVERY SINGLE TIME. I order it without chicken and extra veggies. I've never strayed and I've never been tempted to. It's delicious. I crave it when I'm sick, I crave it when I'm well. It's so damn good. The large bowl (they aren't kidding around with "large") comes with perfectly cooked rice noodles and fresh veggies simmering in the rich chicken broth. It's pretty good on it's own but you should never have it on it's own. With each bowl of pho comes a plate of fresh sprouts, limes, jalapenos, and basil. You need to add all of it. Then scoop some condiments in. I usually just add some garlic chili sauce and call it perfection. Also available though is Siracha, teriyaki sauce, soy, fish sauce (blech), and chili oil. The service is great and the bowls come out really fast. We've ordered the spring rolls before and they are good but I've always asked for them without shrimp and they always come with shrimp. They are very fresh so I don't think they are pre-made but something gets lost in translation. Even after removing the shrimp it still tasted shrimp-y. Bottom line, go here. For around $6 you can leave with a full belly, no MSG headache (we asked), and a serious craving to come again.

This place has for a really cool vibe to it. We started our morning out with there coffee bar that did not disappoint (super friendly barista) then we had dinner there that night. The food was awesome, the manager came out to checked on and greet us, and their wine selection was more than expected. We will be visiting again.

Tried the stuffed chicken wings and Panang curry this time.... The stuffed chicken wings were a definite no go. Never heard of something like this...especially at a Thai place so we were dying to try it. Plus this item had good reviews. First off, they took forever to make and when it finally came out, it was just barely cooked. I don't know what it's stuffed with, but it was squishy on the inside and too much fried outer layering. Definitely disappointed with this item. The Panang curry on the other hand was 5/5! Thick coconut cream with sufficient amounts of chicken and veggies. Definitely what I expect a Panang dish to taste like. I would re-order and recommend the Panang curry but not the stuffed chicken wings! I got a Pad Thai entree and this was standard but a tad bit more dry than I'm used to. Big serving and lots of pork and tofu though. I also had a Thai tea again this time but it wasn't as sweet as last time and I saw chunks of cream floating atop so it wasn't blended all the way through. But still enjoyable and I finished it. I don't know what it was (maybe because it's Sunday and we were the only customers at the time), but I definitely enjoyed my first visit here more so than today's. Still exceptional service from the sweet lady who owns the place and the rice chips/prawn sauce alwaysw on point! I'd definitely be back for either the Red curry, Panang curry, or Drunken noodles as those menu items are still really good!

The Vietnamese sandwiches here are sooooo good. So good in fact that my boyfriend and I haven't tried anything else on the menu because we can't pass up a barbecue pork Banh Mi sandwich!!!! The sandwiches are fresh tasting and perfect balance of meat and vegetables. The prices are very reasonable .... If you get a 12" sandwich they throw in a can of soda. The one bummer is that the restaurant shares space with Port O Subs... So it has a low end / fast food vibe.

This is a convenient location for me as it is near my home. They have some of the most flavorful chicken meat in their chicken pho here. Generally the food here is decent to good but it doesn't seem to always be as good as their other two locations in terms of service and consistency of food. In this area I generally prefer Pho Cam Ly, Lilly's and Mint Modern over this place but you can certainly satisfy your Vietnamese cravings here. They don't seem to stay open late here usually and tend to close right at 10pm or earlier.

Jerk Chicken. Oxtail. What more in life do you want? I've been trying to find a decent Jamaican spot in Philly and I think I've found it. Rice and peas is delicious. Jerk chicken is a little too spicy, but a little spicy doesn't do any harm! However, patties isn't as good as other places.

I was visiting Tampa bay with my wife for pleasure and selected this restaurant when we wanted to eat Indian food. The outside facade got us nervous as the building looks old. However, I did notice this trend with many other restaurants in the area. Inside, the decor is splendid- a lot of embroidery, artifacts and decorative items. Indian restaurants can go overboard with Indian decorations sometimes, especially when it's not realistic but, gaudy. But, Gateway to India made a good effort and combined it with fine dining upholstery. Food and service was very good. Both veg and meat dishes were delicious. All Indian breads were good quality. The staff looks well trained, professional and cordial. They honored any request we had. Overall, the food, service and experience were all more than satisfactory. I will return to eat when I am back in the area.

I don't understand how this place has so many stars. I just had the most disgusting meal of my entire life. I ordered the beef gyro platter & a strawberry banana smoothie for delivery. The platter had hummus & a Greek salad with it. The gyro wasn't even on the pita, the pita came on the side. I could barely chew the pita and it was as tough as cardboard if not tougher. The hummus was half water and the salad was horrendous. The dressing had my eyes squinting and the lettuce tasted VERY old. The rice was good but that's about it.

My cousin and I found this place underwhelming at best. We ordered some deep fried porky wonton appetizers, a pad thai and a pad sieu. The sauce that came with the wonton appy was too watery to adhere to the dumplings- I think a thicker sauce would have worked better. The pad thai and pad sieu was severely under flavoured- I think the pad thai needs something that makes it taste more distinctly tamarind and the pad sieu was quite dry and not very saucy. I found it peculiar that the restaurant was so packed... I liked Syphay and Boualouang much better even though they are in sketchier Chinatown. I highly recommend making the trip for more flavourful food.
This place is awesome! And our waitress, Theresa, went out of her way to make sure I could have what I wanted after having a minor setback. the wood fired veggie wrap is sooo good! And the hummus mmm

THE BEST Indian food I've ever had! Their menu has many different dishes outside of my standard orders and after trying several I'll never order Indian anywhere else again. The Gobi Gopura is so delicious I craved it day's later. Their Chicken Makhanwala has an amazing sauce and the chicken is not the common cubes but a delicious boneless tandoori chicken. It's my 3rd takeout order and I've loved everything I've tried! The interior is really pretty and I look forward to dining in soon.
