Love. It. Take out is quick and always hits the spot. Owner is super friendly and if you bite the bullet, the Thai spicy burns in all the right ways. Brown rice is extra though =(

If you're looking for great Thai food in Santa Barbara - look no further than Zen Yai. The panaang curry is amazing, the service is great and it's dirt cheap. It's everything you want in a good Thai food spot and nothing you don't.

We saw this place on our way to Dosa hut, decided to give it a try. It is a beutiful little place.. well maintained and well designed Having spent a good amount of time in hyderabad, the first dish I try in any indian restaurant is a Biriyani.. Sadly it was not great.. The sheek Kebab we ordered came in a hot plate. covered in green peppers and onions.. . The kebabs were soggy and was falling apart.. For me thats was just wrong. But they did hit the ball out of the park with the Dosa we ordered for our Son... it was delicious, so was the chutney and Sambhar

Best gyro I've ever had in my life. My boyfriend had the zingers and we had left overs for our trip home. If you're in the area I highly recommend stopping by. The owner of the restaurant is super friendly makes the place inviting. I will be stopping by Zeko's every time I'm in the area. I live in Orlando and there's no place that sells gyros like Zeko's.

My gf and I stumbled upon this place randomly while walking back to our car after attending the Philly Auto Show. The menu is extensive, and they have a number of ready-made dishes at the front for quick-eating or take-out. The staff is very courteous and friendly, including the owner, although the service was a little slow. We ordered the half-chicken with rice and beans, and a few pastelitos de res: the chicken, and the rice and beans were very tasty; the pastelitos were a tad aggressively seasoned, but still good. The prices for lunch run between $5-10, and for dinner anywhere from $7.95- 25.00. They are a BYOB, and they have a decent selection of batidos and aguas frescas. I will definitely have to go back to this place and try more things. You should too.

Kim Chi burger was enormous and excellent. Lemon grass chicken baguette is full of flavor, perfect for lunch. One of the best sandwiches I've had in a while. Too hot for pho, today. I'll have to try it in the fall. Service was slow, but friendly enough. Will be back.

So disappointed. This was my go to place in Tampa. Last time, our waitress seemed very annoyed and sarcastic when asked why we couldn't make a small alteration in our menu and I don't tend to like that. To make matters even worse, I got what seemed like an onion salad, sprinkled with tiny pieces of octopus. The owner brought me some more, but I declined, I was already annoyed by the waitress. The waitress brought the menu without even offering desert. I love flan, and at that point, I settled for none. Too bad...I sent so many people there in the past. Not anymore.

This is my go-to Indian food spot. For delivery is fine, but you get the most for your money if you go in and hit the buffet. Most things are gluten-free, and are specified. The food is all fresh and thickened with yogurt (making it gluten-free). The ONLY thing I hate is that I ALWAYS crave them on Mondays and sadly they are closed. Such is the way. Check out their website for the buffet's daily menu. Everything else can be made a la carte. Check them out!

This place was pretty good - it was a little too noisy for my liking. I had the falafal and that was delicious. Their hummus was tasty too - but the customer experience was a bit off as they don't have their processes down quite yet. I'm going to return in a few weeks and see how it has developed.
Roll appetizers were solid and the Pho is best I've had since moving from LA. Best Pho in Greater Indy area

My experience kinda sucked. I have to cross off the pad Thai from my favs here. Tonight it was dry and had too many bites with egg shells. My previous time I got the pad Thai, again it was dry. Not sure what happened. Change of cooks? And I was given the wrong order too. Got to my car and checked the box and it was something different. Went back inside and swapped food with the woman at the register and was on my way. Hate leaving this review, but I will come here for the boba tea and Bahn Mi only. Kinda bummed.
Some of the best Pad Thai that I've ever had! This is cool little restaurant in West Philly worth checking out. Make sure you bring cash though!

We were in the mood for pho and this place was closest to our hotel. What a find! The pho was good but the bright shining star was the spring rolls. I had the grilled pork and shrimp and they were big, fat, and tasty....just excellent! We liked them so much the next day after we checked out of our hotel we stopped by to pick some up for on the way out of town but unfortunately they don't open until 11am. We couldn't stick around so no tasty rolls for us..next time. Definitely!

This is by far the best pho and banh mi I've ever had in the United States. Price is great, the food is magnificently seasoned and the bread is baked on the premises! It's a very casual spot and my best friend took me there for the first time today and I cannot wait to go back!!

We were in New Orleans for a conference and we are big Top Chef fans so we decided to try Nina Compton's restaurant. So glad we did. Food was amazing. We had the cucumber salad, the hamachi, the black drum, and the trio of pork. All were amazing. Best food we had the whole time we were there. Service was also exceptional. Ended the meal with the strawberry shortcake which was really delicious. Anyone traveling to NOLA should plan a meal here. Excellent.
Veggie spring rolls with a delicious peanut sauce, followed by a Beef banh mi that was also great dipped in peanut sauce. Ugh, BEST iced coffee yet.
The food here is good, but the customer service is excellent. I had a problem with a door dash delivery, and Tara went out of her way to make sure that the problem was corrected. Thank you.

I love Nadia Thai! So delicious, so reasonable, especially for the lunch. More often I have come for dinner with friends or family (including a little celebratory dinner after I finished my dissertation) and enjoyed everything. They make a fantastic Massaman curry (my curry of choice) and have delicious appetizers too. It's BYOB: the first time I came here I saw people leaving with a semi-case of Miller Lite!
I just love the panang curry and garlic pepper chicken. Thai tea is delicious. Wonderful service. Lunch special comes with egg roll and chicken rice soup. Everything on the menu is amazing.

Five star for customer service. Food is good too, but my review is about the customer service. Today I ordered the $5 "Vietnamese sandwich" and their credit card reader/machine wouldn't read my card. I have no cash today. It gave an error that the counter guy didn't understand. Rather than send me away hungry, he said he would buy my lunch for me today. Never say no to free lunch, but be sure you go back AGAIN another time to show your appreciation for great service.

This place is fantastic. I was a bit weary, considering Ethiopia and food, you think, they have food? Horrible to say but anyhow, not only will they tell you what everything is, but it's fresh and tasty. They cook everything in clarified butter and I would recommend this place to anyone wanting to try something new!!

I have only been here one time, but it was phenomenal. The service was excellent. I had no idea what I wanted, so they took the time to explain the menu to me. The suggestions they made were spot on. Delicious!

This is my go-to Vietnamese restaurant! Their shrimp spring rolls are the best around, and peanut sauce is amazing. My favorite dish is the tofu pho. It's enough for 2 meals. Lilly is such a nice lady, too.

We have been wanting to try Delicia for Sunday brunch for a while now and finally got around to it. The biggest surprise was that the brunch items were reasonably priced for the quality of the offerings. The food was delicious just like their dinner offerings, and most offerings are unique items not found at other brunch places. Service was very good. We will most definitely be back soon

Okay, okay I'll give it another try already! (Note to self: ALWAYS check Yelp BEFORE your first visit to a restaurant which serves food that is totally unfamiliar to you.) We must have ordered the wrong stuff. I would not normally eat anything named "______ paste" and am not sure why I did today. Shrimp paste. Never again. It's just not for me. I had a dish with white rice, a fried egg, and 4 pork based items. The shredded pork was served cold but would have been better warm. The pork chop was ok, but the other 2 items are still a mystery to me. I'm pretty sure their ingredients included entrails of some sort. Again, just not my thing. She had a skimpy sandwich. Blah. Lemonade was good. French coffee with milk over ice was good. The service was consistently bad during the entire visit. We were one of only 2 tables when we arrived and there were maybe 8 tables active when we left. I only ever saw 1 wait-person. She was surly, but had the food been tasty it wouldn't have been that big a deal. CASH ONLY.

Great place to come for breakfast! They make some of the best pancakes! They have a praline butter that I wish I could smother on everything. Great eggs dishes. Eggs benedict, eggs normandy, breakfast poutine are all pretty solid choices. 4 stars for breakfast and would only come back for breakfast or brunch. Not a bad place for lunch. Their sandwiches are ok. Have had a reuben and lobster sandwich...nothing I'd go back for. Appetizers. They have an excellent onion fontina tart. Tried their lobster potato "beignets" tonight..pretty much a croquette. Disappointed. You get 4 tiny balls with sour cream...for $11.50? Rip off. In dire need of salt. Wouldn't come back for dinner. First off, their compimentary bread was...meh...well the one that I assume was foccacia was ok...they had some sort of tomato bread that tasted AWFUL...it was almost like rusted sweet tomatoe paste on to....I judge places by their complimentary bread and they failed that terribly. Tasted stale. Better off without. Also came with a plate of...balsamic peppers? Wasn't sure what that was supposed to be for...Also ordered a small order of the Sweet Pea Carbonara with Crispy Bacon and an order of the Fresh Pasta with Shrimp and Sausage. Everything lacked taste. A little salt goes a long way. The shrimp from the fresh pasta with shrimp and sausage was cooked alright...but not seasoned. The pasta, although they made it, looked like spaghetti from a can...no fresh or bright flavors. The Carbonara looked clumpy...like when you bring home fettuccine alfredo and try to reheat it in the microwave (huge NO NO) and it gets clumpy. Blah and bland.. As much as I wish I would have enjoyed their dinner...it was overpriced for the lack of quality we received. I'd stick to visiting this place for breakfast. They make great pancakes and praline butter.

Probably the best restaurant experience my fiancée and I have had in years, and we eat out all the time. The place is small and loud but it's not packed in, the tables are not too close to each other. There's an open kitchen but the restaurant doesn't smell like food. There's nothing I hate more than coming home from a restaurant and my clothes smell like food. We got two small portions of the gnocchi and they were as good as I imagined - well no, better! Not like any other gnocchi these are made with ricotta instead of potatoes - they are little pillows of heaven. We got the shrimp appetizer and it was the best shrimp I've ever had! The lemon pasta was amazing as was the ribeye. For dessert - the cannoli and the zeppolis were both amazing. All the food arrived in nice intervals - we didn't feel rushed but we also didn't have to sit and wonder where our food is. I have to say the whole operation is very organized. I just can't say enough good things about our dinner. The atmosphere is great with the rustic feel and the dim lighting - just perfect.

I ventured to Taziki's on Sunday after church let out and decided that I was going to break out of my norm and try something new! Well, sort of. I stuck to my favorite hummus plate (~$4) but then mixed it up with a Veggie Gyro (~$6). Despite the awesome description, it was totally bummed. I guess I was expecting more flavor similar to the salads or the Cucumber and Tomato salad. I actually ended up putting some hummus on there to help out. The weird part was the Greek slaw which was mildly dry. The hubs-to-be got the Tenderloin sandwich smothered with melty cheese and this awesome dijon-esk sauce. I think I'll go for that next time. After sampling the pita for the gyro, I thought how wonderful this would be for the hummus plate rather than the crunchy pita. Hint Hint Taziki! Overall it was $21.00 for two for lunch. Kinda pricey which was weird because we once took a friend it was $2 more. I shall not abandon ship. I shall not abandon ship.

in our search of tasty indian food in west philly, we walked away disappointed. the malai kofta balls were like clumpy cream of wheat. not so good. it seemed to cater to the university student crowd with it's overemphasis on the buffet. give me some love, not buckets of food. ok, enough knocking it. the baigan bharta was decent. but we'll keep searching.

When we arrived, I used the restroom and that totally turned me off for the whole experience. It was disgusting. We sat on the outdoor deck by the water and it was a nice ambiance. The food was fine. Tap water is not served; you must buy bottled water. Service was fine. It is not easy to park. On the whole, I would avoid this place in the future.

Tucked away in a strip mall, small joint. Been here twice, both times for lunch. Looks and feels like a family run biz. Food was very good, and plentiful portions. Not much else to say. I like these smaller joints. Usually places like this serve up more authetic fare than a big and fat chain. It's definitely a place I would stop by for a bite to eat whenever I was in the area. My only recommendation would be a bigger sign out front. Food: 5 stars Ambience: 3 stars Service: 5 stars

Tried the hangover sandwich. It was good but nothing special about it... The food is more expensive than other trucks. I'm not really picky (an egg sandwich is just an egg sandwich), so I'm not really benefiting from the more expensive, "higher-quality" ingredients in this truck

I normally get the vegetarian pho, and I pick it up (yes, they charge extra for pick up). It's normally okay, but there's better places around the "area" like Lily's or Magasin (the latter is AWESOME). The last time I picked it up, I waited FOREVER. They said about 15 minutes, I got there twenty minutes or so after the phone call, and waited for another 15-20 minutes. It's okay if you're in the area, but if time allows, trek to the other Vietnamese places.

Customer for 10 years this store has gone way down hill. Drive thru is extremely slow and inconsistent. 0 stars when I go through the drive thru and still have to go in 10 mins later to find out where my order was.

Great little restaurant! Note that the outdoor seating is not open yet, but will be soon. However, my girlfriend (a Spanish teacher and discerning Latin foodie) and myself (regular foodie) agreed it was somewhere we'd have to visit again. The staff were very polite and eager to make sure we were enjoying our time there. It's run the way a restaurant should be run, prices are reasonable, and the food is tasty! Great place to spend some time. Also, since it's misleading in the restaurant info, this restaurant does not serve alcohol but IS Byob. PS. The bad lighting is from my phone's camera lens, which is cracked and has seen better days....it's actually warmly lit and a perfect for picture-taking because of the wooden walls!
Closed as of 1/3/13. If you bought a Groupon you can redeem it at Marhaba across the bridge in Lambertville

I'd give it 4.5 stars if possible, but it's not. Host station needs some work on greeting customers, i.e. we're patrons, not trespassers. Arrived three minutes early (you're welcome) for an 11 am brunch reservation. Hostess asked us to step aside until called, to the largely vacant dining room. We weren't alone, she dismissed others that arrived as well, curtly. We politely waited until a few minutes after our reservation to be dispatched to a table at the back of the restaurant. Our waitress arrived in short order. We ordered the punch of the week and a couple entrees. The burger was outstanding. Truly outstanding, including the brioche bun. Getting ketchup and mustard, not so much. Wife enjoyed her meal as well. Waitress refilled the punch without asking which was a nice touch. A little over one hundred bucks for brunch in a cool venue. We'd go back but the hostess stand could use some retooling. They set the tone for the experience and simply failed. I hope the 5 star review with some advice helps the bad attitudes improve.
Must haves: zen Yai salad, smoked tofu stir fry, pumpkin curry, poor man noodles, sticky rice and mango

We were looking for a new place to go in the area and really enjoyed our time at Flambo. Very mellow pace. The appetizers were good. We had wings and the mussels. Great sauces with a nice balance of flavor. We should have brought a bottle of wine. We will next time! Our server was very polite and the place has a good feel. There is a big staircase to a more private room upstairs with a table that could seat probably 8? We had vegetarian dishes and chicken dishes. Everyone loved their food. The owner is a nice gentleman who looks to have built the place himself with a lot of care. We are going back with a couple bottles of wine and some friends in the upper room. Cheers all! Enjoy the meal!

AMAZING. great selection of vegetarian options, a little expensive but perfect for a "treat yourself" kind of night. + recommendations: whipped feta dip, mushrooms, corn, "we can pickle that", root vegetable salad.
Introduced me to the vietnamese sandwich (super nomable!!), and also to my all time faveorite condiment sriracha hot sauce. SUPER friendsly staff. Also great pho, and decent rice dishes.....

Great atmosphere right on the water. We went on a Saturday night and the place was packed. We waited about an hour for a table, but we had a party of 7 so it wasn't bad. There was a live band playing that was really good and added to the fun. The food was good. Lots of seafood options, but they also have burgers and wings. Overall, great place. Definitely one of our local favorites now.

Came here on a mini-vacation in Santa Barbara. My husband had the pumpkin curry (since everyone on Yelp seemed to love it) and he really liked it. I had the praram rongsong, which was about 85% spinach and 15%. It should definitely be in the 'salad' portion of the menu. Usually the ratio is reversed. It was good, but I was a little disappointed. For an appetizer, we couldn't get egg rolls or calamari because their fryer was broken, bummer. The thai iced teas were good. I'd like to go back to try a different dish because the quality was good.
We were looking for good hot Pho on one of the stormy snow days in December 2013. Only had the beef Pho and Vietnamese coffee - double yum for each.

One of the best restaurants in the city, in my opinion. The appetizers are light and flavorful, desserts are fresh, complex, and just sweet enough, and the main courses are well-crafted and creative. If they have the Iman Bayaldi pasta as a special, be sure to order it; you won't be disappointed.

They have tasty food on the lunch buffet. The wait staff is attentive, especially if you left them a nice tip on your previous visit. This place has been around for a long time and the decor shows it. If you're in the neighborhood give it a try, but, don't go out your way to make this a destination.

Everything about our pad thai and pad ginger was perfect, except for the part where they entirely failed to season it. A couple of out-of-towners both agreed it was the blandest Thai food we've ever had the misfortune of encountering. (And while we're used to ordering it 'white people mild' when we go to Thai restaurants, here we didn't even specify.) That being said, the tofu was perfectly fried, the vegetables were cooked just right, the portions were reasonable, and the presentation was nice. but when you order, try asking for it with a little bit of flavor, because the default seems to be none.

Great selection, fresh food, quick and friendly service. My favorite is the hummus appetizer which you can order as a trio (regular, red pepper, and cilantro). There is also a nice open dining area. A great lunch option!

I have been to Momo's several times and have tried almost all of their tapas. Some of my favorites are the sea scallops, sea bass, meatballs, falafil, garlic shrimp, the beef tenderloin and the roasted broccoli. It's great for a girls night out and pretty fun on the weekends with the belly dancers. The reviews on here are pretty inconsistent. Some great and some are horrible. I haven't had a bad experience and would continue to visit Momo's.

I stopped in around 8:30pm for a to-go order. I had a gyro with and order of falafel and garlic mushrooms. The food was absolutely delicious. I would definitely stop by the next time I am in Tucson. The guy serving me was friendly and accommodating.

I had never really tried Vietnamese food before a friend suggested Pho Hoa a few years back. We sat down and ordered vermicelli bowls with chicken and veggies and it came out quick and hot and was a great deal at just over $7. We used to go all the time, but over the years, life got busier and I found myself going less and less. Not because the food or service sucked, but because it was easier to hit places closer to home or work instead. My family and I went to Chinatown recently to satisfy a craving for ramen and because the place we normally go to was closed, we went here instead. The visit brought back a lot of pleasant memories - the pho was great and I had my usual, the vermicelli bowl with veggies and BBQ chicken. It was fast, cheap and tasted great! The spring rolls were even better - crispy on the outside, juicy and delicious on the inside. Sure, the prices have gone up slightly (a buck or so), but the food is still great, the service still lightning fast and the prices affordable. If you're in Chinatown and looking for a quick, refreshing bite, stop in and you won't be disappointed.
just reviewing places I have enjoyed in my visit...this is yummy, with enough variety of dishes to choose!! Thanks to M.W. to be someone just so special to take me to places...my great moments!!!

The pad Thai is their specialty here, but it is pretty expensive man. Like pad Thai is 12 bucks and it is okay but somewhat dry. It's in that old traditional style I mean nothing that special. I would say it's overhyped. My friend got the drunken noodle and it was too wet. Parking is also impossible and you get tickets if you park at other places

I experienced the Jamaican jerk hit the past Sunday for the first time and let me tell you. Amazing! I had the curry chicken which was absolutely delicious. The cabbage was just right and the rice and beans added the perfect flavor. We had the beef patties as an appetizer and they were great. The flakes were to die for. My favorite was the plantain that came with the meal. The best part was that they were on groupon. I love s good deal. The downside was that the restrooms were way in the back but it was no big deal.

Best Indian food I've had since moving to Florida! Server/water person was a awkward, didn't make eye contact, didn't say hi, when we said thank you she didn't acknowledge us, but the food freaking amazing. You're going to pay more than other Indian places in the area, but it's well worth it.
Enjoyed the spicy soup and the pork banh mi is delicious.

At the mall and we were looking for a quick lunch. Were seated right away and found the lunch menu on the back of the regular menu. There were two of us so one got the egg drop soup(very viscous and not flavorful) and the hot and sour soup(decent flavor, what you would expect). Entrees were sesame chicken, which was moist and sauced nicely with sweetness and a bit of heat and the Sichuan beef, which was fried strips of beef with jullianed carrots and celery. A bit salty with too much celery for my taste, but satisfying and portions large enough for a second meal. Service was attentive certainly a cheap meal, nothing great, but perfectly adequate.

Zabiha for those of you who follow Z-Club (i.e similar to Kosher). I get the Kabobs every time I go, and I must say, their blend of marinade is excellent! It's a relatively simple restaurant in an historic part of town. The waitress looks like Selma Hayek!! There are two tables covered in Afghan decor that makes the experience of eating Afghani food much more cultural. Nice to go to with a group of friends. Gave it 4 starts because the service was a bit on the slow side (but that's only because 3 people are running the show....pretty impressive actually). GO!
The restaurant is very clean, the atmosphere is phenomenal and the food is to die for. Believe it or not the last time I had Indian cuisine this good was in Durban, S. Africa.

Really great jerk and curry chicken. I've never had the festival side anywhere else so get that too. Great patties if all you need is a snack! The ladies behind the counter are friendly and take you order and payment as soon as possible. Having said that I just have two issues with Hummingbird. The wait for your order is unbearable. Even when you try to order ahead, you might still wait in the restaurant for your order or wait to pay. This is annoying when you've got limited time for lunch. They do serve generous portions and it's a lot of carbs for the lunch hour. I do have issues with finishing my meal here as it usually results in nap time for me at 3 pm. Take that into consideration when you choose between the sizes that are available. If you have some self control, perhaps some of it can be saved for dinner.

I absolutely love this neighborhood gem. The reason I took two stars away was because I was recently here and the lady working there totally messed up everything. I placed a take out order which I was told would take 10 minutes. I arrived 15 mins to give them some extra time. The woman charged me wrong and over charged me on my order. She didn't even had a clue on how much a side of hummus cost. I kept repeating what should have been charged rather than what was charged. She credited my receipt but not for the right amount. She then had to give me the remaining amount on cash. After this I was told it was still being made. It turns out I waited another 25 minutes for the order to get made. This is normally not like them. I come to find out that the woman preparing the food had my order and was all ready when I came in but the Cashier overlooked the order and had her make a new one. There was no communication for the woman working on the register. She needs to be trained better. Overall it made me mad because I was late returning to work for this entire mix up.

This was our third Ethiopian dinner (prior stops were in Philadelphia, PA, and Evanston, IL), and we think the best so far. The pastry appetizers and two dinners we had were flavorful, slightly spicy, and nicely done. We liked the ground beef pastry a bit better than the lentil stuffed one, which was a little dried out. The TA2 meat combination sampler (for one) was a great dish to try ($16.95) , with good-valued portions of lamb, chicken, beef, spinach, and a couple of lentils served on the traditional tangy and vinegary injera flatbread. Son also tried the gored gored - raw beef cubes served with a spicy sauce and powder. He liked it, and I was ok chomping on a sample of it, but I'm not sure I would have enjoyed the whole entree, just from the idea of it. We also liked the bottomless servings of the injera bread, as I'm not remembering having that at the other Ethiopian places. Note the Dashen Ethiopian beer is $5 per bottle (it was a nice, light lager like beer) , as opposed to the Bedele beer advertised at $4. We're finding west 38th street in Indy to be quite the mixing pot now for various ethnic and good-valued cuisines. This place has been in business for 8 years now.

Should be 3.5 stars. Had pho ga (chicken) which was above average but not out of this world. Service is great and prices cheap so would definitely recommend it if you're in the neighborhood and craving Vietnamese.

Slow service and cannot handle a large party of 15 to 20 people. The food was good but we had one person in our party that received their food after everyone had eaten. Excuses were made by the chef.....

I called up Queen of Sheba to place an order. "Hello?" "Hi, is this Queen of Sheba?" "No." I apologized for calling the wrong number, checked a different source, then tried again. "Hello?" "Hi, is this Queen of Sheba?" "No." "Oh, sorry. The Web keeps giving this number for an Ethiopian restaurant." "Yes, this is an Ethiopian restaurant." "But you're not Queen of Sheba?" "No." She told me the name the restaurant was Asmara and then hung up on me before I could place an order. So I went there. Food's ok, atmosphere is kinda horrible--bar with two TVs blaring sports so loud that it's difficult to just eat in peace. At least the other Ethiopian restaurants offer seating that's free from dismal dive bar cacophony. The only reason to go here is if you NEED Ethiopian for lunch and you're confined to Baltimore Ave. Otherwise, head to Kaffa Crossing.

I've tried to keep going here but ever since the owner stopped working there, the quality of the dishes, the quantity of food in the dishes and the cleanliness have gone way down. The folks he has working in there just don't have that same "Best of Yelp" mojo going. We've tried numerous times to go back, thinking we just got off days with a new staff member. Sadly, Mood has killed our mood for chaat. We're done.

Decor is typical for a Thai restaurant around here- outdated with carpet flooring. But the food is amazing and that's what keeps me coming back. Thai food is so easily made vegan, and easier when the waitress knows what it means (she did!)! I veganized the salad rolls with peanut sauce, sweet and sour soup (all soups can be made vegan), glass noodles dish, and red tofu curry with both jasmine and coconut rice. Everything was amazing but the curry itself was exceptional. So unbelievably creamy, and stayed warm thanks to it being heated over a candle. It was my second time here and I'll be back again!
Cashier was not friendly and rude. My wife's pad Thai (1/5) was too spicy for her to eat. Thai Luanna is far superior.

Tangelo's offers good, solid food for a reasonable price. It's not my favorite, but the staff could not have been more friendly. They went above and beyond to accommodate our, frankly spoiled, children's additions and substitutions to each dish. The restaurant is lovely. We felt as if we were on vacation, and who doesn't want a bit of that on a sleepy Sunday afternoon?! Give it a try!

I have been coming here for nearly 2 years and the food and service are second to none! All of the food here tastes like your long lost India mom made it from scratch! I have eaten India and Curry all over the world and this place cannot be beat! Monte is a top notch guy and makes sure everyone leaves happy!

Just added Magasin to my rotation. I had their grilled pork with rice which came with a fried egg on top and a nice mix of greens, julienned carrots, cucumbers and cabbage. Their nuc cham (sp), the fish sauce with vinegar, is superb and goes great on the salad or the rice. Simple food done well at a price you cant beat.
Every dish we tried was delicious. Service was attentive and well timed. The lamb ribs is to die for. Will be going back for sure!
I've been there twice and I love their chicken shawarma. The service is fast and the servers are nice. I'm a fan!

The food here was good, I had the escovitch fish and it was very tasty and spicy the way I like it. he cabbage was also very good. Also it is a BYOB which is always great in my book! The service was ok a little slow and the front dining area is very small and it took a while for a staff member to tell us there was a back room. Other than that I would return anytime.

Delicious!!! I get the Pad Thai everytime because it's just so yummy! Make sure to ask for extra spicy sauce. YUM!! The spicy fried rice and egg rolls are wonderful too!! If you ever pass through the little beach town of Carpinteria, this is a must stop for all you Thai lovers!!! While this is not the BEST Thai place I have ever eaten at, this is definitely one of my top 3 favorites!! The prices are great too!

Place is quite which is good if you want to enjoy your diner in quite atmosphere. Nice design. FOOD! Food was delicious. Chicken masala - the best! Also you have choice to have it spicy or not. Grill was tasty too. All food was fresh and they really cook it fresh . Price is good too. It was my first time in this restaurant and I ll come back there for sure. Thank you for tasty diner !

Absolutely love to go with a bottle of white (Byob) and get the grilled octopus, every time! The mussels sauté is amazing! The shrimp scampi is out of this world! The pita bread and olive oil are great! Sharing a whole fish with your date is fun as well, I like to get it deboned ! A must go for seafood and Greek food lovers!

I used to live around the corner from a PJ back in Scottsdale, and I just can't get enough of it down here. I usually hit up this spot once a week - it has such a diverse menu I'll never get tired of it! Go-to items that are beyond delish: - Lavosh Shawarma Wrap - Seared Ahi salad with mango and strawberries - Chicken Philly Pita - Chicken Combo Platter (basic lunch staple - beans aren't stellar but they're "good") and my all-time fav - the mediterranean platter with hummus, tzatziki, filafel, and I substitute the taboule (ew) for a basic greek salad. The hummus trio is the bomb, and I actually don't think it's on their menu anymore but you can still order it --- its the best. Seriously, the BEST hummus. the cilantro hummus is what dreams are made of. I also love the staff here. They are so emo and cute. I kind of want to feed them all carbs to get fattened up in their skinny jeans, but it fits well with the hipster ambiance of the place. Love you Pita J! OH! They also have $4 and $5 glasses of wine from noon-4 and a reverse happy hour --- great selection of organic wines that are typically $11 a glass, you can't go wrong.
Awesome food. Try chicken curry,biriyani. Service is also good. You will really love the food.

Small BYO. The restaurant is very very casual. The food was good. Nothing amazing. There was nothing that I said "wow! that is really good!" that would make me want to rush back. We went for UC dining days so $15 for three courses = a great deal. We ordered the crispy spring roll with pork (just ok), papaya salad (light and refreshing), tilapia, pad-kee-mao (tasty! nice medium level spice), and banana chocolate spring roll for dessert. The highlight was the dessert! It was just the right amount of food. The service was good - they kept our water glasses full. For a cheap dinner, and byo, this place hits the mark. But the food can't even compare to Trio in Fairmount. I wouldn't rush to go back or go out of my way to go there, but I am glad I tried it. Don't forget that this is cash only. Our bill came to $32.40 before tip.

My boyfriend and I stumbled into this place because it was the only place in Carpenteria opened past 9pm on a Tuesday. We were so pleasantly surprised. First of all the service was amazing, such nice and attentive waiters. And then the food was so delicious. First we had the wonton soup which had an amazing garlic flavor...different from other wonton soups I've had. Then we shared pad Thai and pad see ew...just delicious! Will definitely always come here on trips to carp!
Consistently great seafood at decent prices.

Went with a group of friend on. Friday night. Reservation is recommended. We tried various kabobs and side dishes which were good. The service was little slow but that didn't stop us from enjoying our food. He kabobs were little salty but I didn't mind it as much.
Started by ESL student of mine, Bina,who has improved decor and, although menu remains solidly delightful.

Mmmm....Chickpeas. Best sandwich I've had in my life. Or at least in the past few weeks! I stopped by this joint last Friday for lunch, and was blown away by the sheer deliciousness. I tried the Kufta Pita (ground beef and lamb with spices and onions) and it was warm and tender and melted in your mouth....SO GOOD. The chef even asked me how I wanted it cooked...pretty impressive for a takeout joint! There's also, as others have noted, a pretty impressive fixings bar, with everything from hummus and tahini to grilled eggplant, corn, fresh salad and more, which the man behind the counter heaped on for no extra charge. The service was a bit slow even though the place was empty...but I'd rather my servers take their time, and do it right! The atmosphere is simple but cozy...ten or so tables, and a long bench with cushions. I'll definitely return again, and check out the falafel as well!

I like the idea of fresh ingredients, but not when it sacrifices taste. I have been here a couple times, and maybe half of the items I have had have been quite bland and greasy. The only flavor provided was from the sauce, which itself was delicious, but I personally prefer when the food's flavor is not 100% dependent on it. Also had a chicken pita pizza, which sounded good, but ended up being far too salty. I understand feta can be a salty cheese, but this was over and above the normal saltiness for feta. That being said, I have had some food, such as the chicken kabob, that were absolutely delicious. Prices here are a bit high, unfortunately. Staff is very friendly; zero complaints there. Overall, I don't hate it, but i don't love it. I might go back.

This is one of my favorite Thai restaurants I've been to. And considering that I've been to nearly 50, that's saying a lot. My favorite Thai dish is Tom Yum soup and this is one of my favorites. It's very rich in flavor and is a very generous portion. I've also gotten a couple different curries here and the Massaman and Penang are absolutely delicious. Check this place out. You won't be disappointed.
A little higher end in the spectrum of Thai but the quality shows through in the food. Solid option and the byo aspect bumps keeps this at a 3 star. Soup and an entree for lunch runs about $15.

Stopped in for a quick lunch in-between rounds of golf, and wanted my playing partners to experience a spot with unique food. As it turns out, we all ordered the same dish (albeit with different sides)...jerk chicken. The meal came with with sides, I choice the fried plantains and rice & beans. The food took a while to come out (even though the place was unfortunately mostly empty)...but had a nice presentation on the plate. There were three pieces of cut-up chicken alongside my two sides. The jerk chicken was spicy but moist and tasty. The fried plantains could have been a bit more caramelized but had a good, sweet flavor. The dirty rice and beans were mildly spiced and complimented the chicken well. Server was very friendly but a bit absent during the meal. Would definitely return if in the area.

Sorry to say the service was just awful!!!! Really waitresses couldn't be bothered to get extra napkins, change plates in between courses, wipe off a table with water all over, bring take home containers ..So besides being placed at a tiny table for two ( we were three) the noise level being above normal , and terrible service I'd say the food was as good as any other Greek restaurant.

The restaurant was very clean and the service was good and friendly. The tastes were interesting. I had Buddha Dumplings as an Appetizer and they were very nice. My Three Friends Entree was very watery with little meet and fish and overcome with vegetables. I would not recommend this. The size of all the portions was too big and made both me and my group feel uncomfortable. No finesse. It is also a BYOB establishment which I have a particular dislike for. However, not very pricey and situated in a very pleasant location in Ardmore.

Took my mom for an early Mother's Day lunch and she chose here. This is usually one of my favorite pho spots and hers too. And their food really is great but their customer service is horrible. The girl who comes to our table hardly speaks any english at all and it makes getting out order made very difficult. We Started with me ordering my soda and when she asked my mom my mom said she wasn't ready yet. The server said "2 cokes". We said no. She doesn't know what she wants yet. The server then says ok two cokes. No! We don't know yet! The server just gave us a blank stare and walked away. When she came back to take our order i had to ask for my diet coke again and then just told my mom to order the same thing because based on our experience that's what she will end up with anyways. (One time the server came back with 4 different drinks before she finally brought the diet coke that my mom ordered) Then we order our meals. An order of spring rolls which are always great and each of us ordered the flame broiled pork and shrimp vermicelli bowls because we figured it would be too complicated to have different orders. We Were then ignored for an hour and had to flag down the server to get a to go box. (Last time we were here they grabbed our dishes and left for the kitchen to dispose of them when my friend and I just stood up to get our coats on when we weren't done eating. Its always cold in there.) I go up to the register to find the total and pay and the same girl says "21 and 42 dollars" umm wait. What? "21 and 42 dollars". I looked at her with confusion asking if she had the right ticket. She held up the ticket to show me it said $21.42. I would hope that the people they have talking to customers and handling money would at least be able to communicate with us.

I went in to order a take-out dinner but the host / owner (not sure) was too busy on the phone speaking with her cell phone provider! Took her 5-10 minutes before she decided to try and 'multi-task' by taking my order! The food was ok but the service is awful !!!

My friends and I visited her for dinner after a really big test, we love thai cuisine. We were the only ones in the restaurant. The atmosphere ass really nice. I ordered the cashew nut chicken no cashews with a 4 spice level. My friends ordered the red and yellow curry. The food presentation was lovely. The cashew nut was really good. My only comment was that it was too spicy. I love spicy food but that level 4 would be considered a 5 in other restaurants. My friends also complained that their food was too spicy and they had level 3. I ended up sending mine back and they tired to water it down. It tasted alright. We had plenty left overs. I really liked my meal I think next time I would have to order with a lower spice level.
This review is for the bar only. Bar tenders were not friendly at all. Drinks were ok. My main issue was how dirty the bar area was. It is also a tight space.

Everything and everyone here, from the hostess through our waiter to an earnest conversation with the manager would best be described as "superlative". The menu is not as lengthy as many - and we were grateful for this. As we savored our meal we came to appreciate this allowed each plate to be prepared masterfully. Creative, beautifully presented, sophisticated yet relaxed. The attention to detail and complexity of flavors made this a memorable meal and an even more worthwhile experience.

Went here with a friend, the ambiance is very nice and they did a huge overhaul of the interior. We sat at the bar and the service was pretty slow despite there being only two other groups there at the time with a majority of the seats empty. The buffalo cauliflower was good but my pork banh mi was absolutely terrible. It had very little flavor, the vegetables weren't pickled like you would expect of this type of sandwich and the pork was basically mush. I only ate about half of my sandwich before giving up because I couldn't fathom eating anymore of it.

I absolutely love Ethiopian, I'd eat it every day if I could. This place excels at quality food and kindness via the waitstaff, but unfortunately falls behind in regard to attentiveness. And this is coming from the MOST laid-back, low maintenance person. I don't need to be waited upon hand and foot by any means. When I went with my group of friends, there was only one other table of eating, and it took a long time for everything in general. It wouldn't have mattered if the restaurant wasn't ice cold, but the combo of tensed up ice cube and hangry bitch isn't good on the brain! I'm guessing they just had less staff that night or something. Understandable. That being said, I was in great company, the people working there were amazing when they finally showed up, and the food was wonderful. I got the Vegetarian Platter, which was so, so good and it's also something I'd recommend to first time Ethiopian diners. Honey wine was better in theory, but you be the judge! So long story short, dine here when you've got time to graze and enjoy someone's company. It's absolutely worth it. And maybe bring a jacket if you're always cold like me. ;)
Fairly good Indian fare especially for this wasteland of Philly
The fried chicken is great. The sides are interesting but not to my taste. The cookies are perfect. The atmosphere would be great for a lunch girls date or studying. Cute overall.

Love this place. It's my neighborhood go-to for takeout. The food is really good quality and the staff is friendly. I have always gotten the buffet items - the dal is delicious and I can also vouch for the saag paneer.

I've been to this restaurant five times, because of it's attractive decor, inside and out, I love Thai food and walking into town for dinner, and because it's on Narberth's main shopping street and I really like to support local businesses. On my first visit, the food and service were excellent, though more expensive than any Thai restaurant I've been to. Since then the food has been meh and the service has been inconsistent. Even a standard like Pad Thai barely resembles what is served at any other Thai restaurant I've been to on the Main Line or in the city. When I eat in Narberth it will now be at the new Vietnamese restaurant, Pho Ever Yours, or the Greeks. For Thai food I'll go to Thai Pepper in Ardmore where the service is always excellent, the food presentation beautiful and consistent, and whatever we've had has been delicious and authentic, or in the city. I do hope that Coco Thai gets it together. It's a lovely place to eat.

I honestly have to say that I was a little hesitant to come here. I am a super picky eater. I even told my husband that if I didn't enjoy the food that he would have to take me somewhere else afterwards! I had a beef tenderloin that was cooked to perfection. Absolutely perfect! The seasoning was tasty. The side dishes were amazing too. The service was fabulous. Everyone was attentive and could offer lots of information about the dishes. I ended up eating more than my husband. Needless to say, there were no stops to get any more food when we left.
Fun find in the CBD - fresh and tasty. Enjoyed eggplant dish! Staff friendly. They had a brisk take-out business on a Friday night

I love this place! Welcoming staff and relaxing atmosphere that's truly transporting. We've been here for the extremely reasonable lunch buffet several times and have always been pleased with the array of scrumptious offerings. The naan, rices, chicken and veg options are all delish! There's several dipping and toppings for you to enjoy with your food on the buffet! Don't forget to try the authentic desserts.
This place was excellent. Largest choice of an Indian buffet I have ever been to and everything was excellent. Will definitely be back!

The most legit Thai food in Canada. This place beats a bunch of places in the USA. And trust me I've been to a lot of Thai Restaurants. -Tom Yum 4/5 -Som Tum (mango) 5/5 -Panang chicken 5/5 -MANGO w sticky rice 5/5

Fantastic food! I became addicted after my first visit. We were in town for 2 weeks and I ended up coming here every day. Couldn't get enough of the freshly made good, especially the sirloin beef kabob. Service is very good. Casual place, but truly high quality food.

I really wish this was in Chicago. I always trust yelp when I'm traveling and this...fine Philly yelpers, you have done so good by me. I can not express my delight in what you have lead me to. The owner put together what was essentially a perfect meal, and since I mentioned I'm only in town for a week, promised to up the crazy of my chaat if I managed to come back in since he normally eases people into new and exciting chaats but you know, only a short while left. I hope that I can make it back because such delicious food. Aah!

We got hooked on Chopstix when they had a location on Oracle Rd. and now if we want fantastic calamari we drive on over to Marana to eat at chopstix. They calamari is our favorite but all the food we've had was delicious, the quality is consistent, good service, nice decor, and prices are appropriate to the food. Highly recommended!

Really disappointed with my experience this time around. We ended up being there for about 2 hours and not by choice. While they were busy it didn't help that I could see our server shooting the breeze at the bar. I am familiar with the style of the restaurant but was aggravated by how long it took everyone to receive their food at our table. The butternut squash was amazing as always but my main dish literally tasted like gruel. We saw our actual server maybe 3 times during the entire visit. When we received our main dishes it took about 5 minutes before we could flag down someone to give us forks so we could actually eat our food. When we were brought the utensils the server made a rude comment. We finished our food and patiently waited for the server to come and check on us and give us the check. Since we weren't asked if there were going to be separate checks at the beginning of the meal we asked if it was possible to split the check. (On a side note we have had our check split before there). Our server said I can only split it evenly as many times as you want. He repeated it again and this time he was more rude. I understand that this place is busy and popular but the service has totally ruined the place for me. It's a shame that they care more about being cool and hip over treating customers kindly.
Great jerk burger. Also good selection of carribean beers.

Service was pretty slow. Sat at the bar outside...there were three people at the bar and 2 bar tenders. They spent most of the time chatting with each other and ignoring the customers. Then, the female bartender wearing a sleeveless shirt picked up the bar towel and wiped off her dirty, sweaty underarms off with it. As if that's not bad enough, she continued to use the bar towel to dry her hands, wipe the bar, and then put the towel next to the vegetables that were being sliced up. Disgusting. Won't find me here ever again.

The pork vermicelli is amazing and love the veggie pho. I've only picked up, but have to say, it's pretty awesome. Staff is very nice. Gentlemen working there opened the door for me since I had my hands full. Would definitely recommend.

Consistently one of the best Greek/Lebanese restaurants around. This has become one of my favorite stops in Metairie. The service is quick and friendly, perfect for a work day lunch. The food is always good. I'm partial to their chicken shawarma, but the gyro is good too. Pita is always severed hot to enjoy very flavorful hummus. The menu is extensive with lots of things to try and enjoy. The only reason it isn't 5 stars is for lack of atmosphere. The dining area has no warmth and at times seems like it could be cleaner at times.
Chicken noodle soup I am feeling like just drop bottle water nothing test like on Delaware ave !!!!!! Chicken very dry !!!
O M G the lemongrass chicken vermicelli is delicious! The flavors are perfect! The pork belly taco was amazing as well. I found a new fave for Vietnamese food!

Always looking for new places to try and after reading previous reviews thought this sounded good. Not! Ordered spring rolls w/plum sauce and was disappointed when it was served w/duck sauce like a take-out place. Chicken &Shrimp pad thai was way too sweet also disappointing. Husband and I both had stomach aches later on. Will be going back to Thai Nana from now on.

I've recently made Indian food a bit of an adventure. I will try just about anything. This place was on the list. This hole in the wall delivers great food, friendly service, and an odd since satisfaction you wouldn't expect from a farmers market vendor. The mango lassi is fresh. The samosas are huge and made to order. The mix pakora is tasty and affordable. The one negative I will mention it is slightly noisy. But a little noise will not stop me from coming back for more delicious!
Good sushi place conveniently located across from Countryside Mall.

This is one of Tampa Bay's oldest and best Cuban sandwich restaurants. The favorite for me is the Chicken Mojo sandwich with black beans . Add some hot sauce for extra kick !! If you're hungry , ask for the " Sonny Charles " version .... that's double meat and cheese !! The owners , Lisa and Mike , are great folks and add to the friendly , casual vibe . This is a guaranteed winner in Gulfport !!! Enjoy !!
Had a quick hour in between meetings in the area so I stopped by on a whim. Got the shabnam veggie curry. SO GOOD. Fast friendly service. Will definitely come back next time I'm in the area.

After reading the reviews decided this was a great place to take a major meat craving and wow was it! We ordered a half slab of ribs, white meat jerk chicken and chicken curry to round out our taste test. The rice and peas of course (and sorry to correct y'all but they are peas and not beans very similar to the crowder or lady peas we have down south. Contrary to popular belief all peas are not green.) an order of plantains and plenty of hot jerk sauce. I only wish more people had been explicit about the size of the portions. My husband and I ate like pigs and still have enough left over for at least another meal if not two. The hot jerk sauce was very tasty, even thought it was not quite as hot as I hoped it would be. Oh, and of course we washed it down with Ting (refreshing grapefruit soda) and a pineapple soda for my husband. The service was friendly and decently fast and we will definitely be repeat customers. We so much prefer to spend our food dollars supporting local businesses.

I cannot say enough good things about this place. First, the ambiance is perfect- the decor, the smells, everything. I was greeted warmly and assisted without needing to ask. I got takeout so I didn't personally experience the service at the table, but the managers/owners (?) were around and active in helping out. I ordered the butter chicken "very, very mild" and it was perfect. Very, very good. I already can't wait to go back.

Just like its sister location up in Green Hills the food here is great. Finally a chain that knows how to do fast and friendly Italian (as well as Asian and American) pastas! And for the price, you can't beat it. The food here is really good. For example, for me at least, the chicken noodle soup here is perfection in a bowl... seriously, just add some matzo balls and it tastes as good as what I make (my fiance will can vouch for how good my matzo ball soup is as she often requests it)! Finally, unique to this location is a semi-automated, touch screen, beverage dispensing system for Coca-cola product. If you want more than just the typical Sprite, Coca-Cola, Dr. Pepper and 1 or 2 other random Coca-cola options, this has an immense selection. Maybe this is the first of many of the future soda fountain machines?

Worst Indian restaurant I have ever been to. Everything is bland. If you want to be able to taste any kind of flavors in your food do not come here. The chicken "tikka" masala is essentially thick sweet tomato soup. The "tandoori" chicken is literally plain ground chicken. The samosa contains ground chicken as well?!? My grandparents are from India and we decided to try this place together. My grandmother called this place shameful and we left hungry. My grandfather had to put the complimentary mints on his samosa to "give it some flavor." The "fresh" naan was cold. Overall a terrible restaurant and I do not recommend it. Not even worth posting pictures.

This place is awesome. One of East Nashville's true treasures, in my opinion. All the dishes I've had there so far have not disappointed. I highly recommend the half chicken. It's cooked to perfection and the honey sauce is incredible. The oregano, mizithra fries are also really good too. I also really dig the layout and design of the place. One downside to being such a desirable spot is that the parking is limited, so be prepared to circle the lot a time or two before you can get in.
I always buy food here. The food is good the service could be better they always seem to be rude or have attitudes. Other than that it a good place to good Jamaican food.

I haven't had Ethiopian food too often, but the times I had it I somehow felt it was a better experience. The service was actually great. The waitress was attentive and checked in on us multiple times. She was very patient and good with explaining menu items to us. I just thought the food was... kind of blec... All mishy moshy and so forth. Most of the stuff was too bland. Then another one was like very spicy. It was a strange contrast going from something almost tasteless to something that was so spicy that I couldn't actually taste the food content. Not that it was too spicy either, because I can handle that level of spice, but there just wasn't any flavor "behind" it. If you know what I mean. Also... the bread was served cold and it seemed dried out at the edges. I know I've had it very very moist in the past. This place was worth trying, but I won't be going back. One of those rare times when the yelp reviews haven't guided me to the right place for me. It has happened a few times because I'm vegetarian. This place actually had TONS of veggie options, so that wasn't an issue at all. Oh well, the quest for trying new places continues.

I love Nooddi Thai - it's one of my go to Thai places in the greater Philly area. I especially love the veg massaman curry - this is also good with rice noodles (which you can add to any curry dish). Their triangle tofu and spicy peanut dipping sauce is scrumptious. They have always been quite prompt in their service time as well, which is appreciated. I also love that there are several vegan options, as you can switch out many dishes with tofu. My only recommendation would be to offer the thai iced coffee or thai iced tea with a non-dairy alternative such as soy, coconut, or almond milk.

On our last day in Nola we were dying to eat anything other than the usual fare in the city so we opted for Vietnamese! We found Lilly's on yelp, walked fron the warehouse district on Magazine street to the cute neighborhood. We were a little worried about safety because you walk under the freeway bridge but going back at night we realized there were plenty of lights and cars so we felt comfortable. There is a smell of incense? When you first enter but once the dishes came out we got over it. I had the awesome garlic chicken dish which I tried to recreate at home! My husband had the bun which he liked. When paying the bill I realized how expensive dining in the city is because I felt like we got an awesome deal at Lilly's! We also walked by a filming of Nola NCIS!! We thought it was cool but I am sure the locals are used to it!!
Great staff, awesome interactive entertainment (belly dancer took photos with us and asked people to dance), great food and fast service. Ask for Zach and say Sal recommended him

the BEST thai food on the main line. slash greater philadelphia area! i will drive out from center city just for a meal at this little place. the interior is adorable, service is always stellar, and the food is very authentic. portions are huge, the specials are ever changing, and all in all a consistent, satisfying meal every time. a wonderful place for date night, meal with friends, etc (really, any occasion) and on top of all this-- it's a BYO! encore and applause for siamese princess!

So good! We had rainbow spring rolls (tofu, avocado, vermicelli noodles, strawberries, lettuce) and then I had the tofu and veggie pho and my husband had the meat combo pho. Big portions for a great price. Loved it.
Absolutely delicious! The grilled pork sandwich is unbelievable. The bubble tea is delicious as well. The staff is helpful and friendly. This is one of our new favorite family spots.
Some of the best Indian food I've ever had in the U.S.Their goat palak was great, the meat very tender and moist. Very glad I learned about this hole-in-the-wall!

Love this place - great environment, very sweet & friendly staff, amazing food, and very affordable. My husband and I moved to the area about a year ago and have been frequenting this place since we got here. It's our number one go-to anytime we want a night out or don't have time to make dinner ourselves. We use their punch card and get yummy perks every once in a while, too.
By far the best food truck I have ever had! It was so much food for $10! The falafel were absolutely amazing and so was the chicken!

It's been about 7 months since I came here last and picked this spot for guys dinner for my one buddies bday. The other 3 are not as food centric as I am but was open to what the menu had to offer. I was hoping the lamb chop that I read about would of been available as one of the nights special but sadly it was not ): but no big deal lol. I started with the Gamberetti e Fagioli, 3 whole shrimp with beans were solid, but not like the Antipasto or Finocchi Salsiccia, the bursting fennel sausage with broccoli rabe. For my pasta I went with the Pesto Trapanese which was pretty good, but not as good as the Gnocchi which melts in your mouth. My buddies enjoyed the sausage, and the gnocchi as they should. The entree I opted for instead of either special tonite as the Fishermans Stew which was pretty fucking good, the broth deep with flavor and full of that delicious seafood mix of clams, mussels, fish (cod,swordfish), calamari, and shrimp with couscous, another meal I could eat endlessly. My buddy whose bday it was got the Ribeye which I tried...it was so tender n juicy good! The lone down spot was our one buddy getting the veal special which he didnt enjoy since he imagined it being something else. I tried that also which I thought was good but perhaps the weakest dish tho I only had a bite. I should of mentioned who the birthday was for since when we ordered dessert my chocolate chili gelati came out with the sparkler which I then gave to the bday recipient and his zeppoli. While my first overall meal here was one of the best meals I've ever had, this time around was just as exceptional but maybe slightly so since this place seems to set the bar so high with their first impression. One of the best places to try for sure!

My friends and I took a trip around NOLA to basically eat all day. One of our must go stops was for the phorrito. We didn't see it on the menu so we had to ask the guy behind the counter if they had it. We didn't think it will live up to all the hype. However, it was the best thing we have eaten on our trip! This is a must try!! It comes with a side of pho broth for dipping. You have an option to add an egg and whether you want it spicy or not.

What a neat little corner store in Mid-City! Come in for the gatorades and red bull, stay for the bahn mi, pho, breakfast or po-boy. The po-boys are on some of the most delicious French bread I have ever had and run about $3.50. Everything is made to order and you can call ahead and scoop it up if you are in a hurry.

Went to Delicia to celebrate our Granddaughters 23 rd Birthday. The food was great and good service but I will never go back. I brought in a decorated Birthday Cookie for my Granddaughters Birthday and was scolded like a child that we could not eat that in their restaurant. Really!! I did not ask for any plates or utensils, just wanted to celebrate her day. I am a medical professional but have done cake decorating for years. Have taken cakes etc to restaurants for years. They have even been gracious enough to bring out as a surprise. Anyway if that's not there rule they could of handled it better. Come on let's have some common sense. We should of been allowed to have our dessert and just informed us for the future! Poor customer service!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Very bad place ! Very bad service ! I don't recommend this place to anyone ! Even with few customers , the hotel management was very lazy ! In ordered a biryani, and it took more than an hour !! No update and communication with the customer at all . And the taste sucks !!please don't waste your previous time n money ! Y
I've only been once and the food was pretty good I'd probably give it another chance when I have extra money though I felt it was overpriced.

Great food, excellent drinks and great music/entertainment. They provide authentic Greek food mixed with belly dancing with creatively named drinks to create not only an inviting but delicious atmosphere.

We tried the Smiling Elephant on a busy Friday night after rave reviews from friends that this was the place to go for Thai in Nashville. The restaurant is super small so we ended up waiting about 30 - 40 minutes for a table which was alright since we came at peak dinner time on a Friday night. Sad to say, we were seriously disappointed in the food. None of it was very tasty. Not sure if we're just used to a different style of Thai, having moved to Nashville from Southern California. Be that as it may, the taste of the food still was not to our liking. Our search for good Thai in Nashville continues!

Food is just mediocre- dry/bland. Cocktails are something special though. However, not sure when I'll be back next. Last time we tried, the entire restaurant was busy but hostess told us the bar tables were first come, first served. Luckily we spied an open two top and started to sit down. We were promptly told to get up after another couple noticed us take a seat. What?! Not my problem they didn't think to ask about open seating in the bar first! I'll try again as soon as they step up their customer service.

So many stars. Food was on point and huge for the price, service was smiley and fast. One gentleman was backing his jeep up and unloading a huge cooler right after we were seated. I had to look, and it was one snapper that filled the cooler I believe he said it came from Milton, FL, but I am not sure. The shit was fresh, that's for sure. It was smiling at me. We tried two lunch specials, beef drunken noodles Heat level 2 and garlic and pepper chicken heat level 5. Both came with rice soup and spring roll. We also tried iced green tea and iced thai tea. If I had any recommendations, none would be complaints, for sure. Maybe more napkins on the table (my dish was hot and my nose runs) and maybe a thinner soup (I ate most of it and couldn't eat as much of my entree as I wanted. A good problem to have, for sure). I love this place!

So this isn't the best boba you're going to find anywhere. But it's remarkably solid. Which for Delaware(???) warrants 5 stars. We went here on a whim on our way out of a day trip to Delaware and it was honestly just solid boba. The pearls themselves were a little over cooked and soft but it was better than being undercooked. Drink wise we had lychee delight and the piña colada. The latter was my favorite, it was a perfect combo of tea and fruit flavors. The lychee delight was good, but texturally has a bit too much going on. Both were a little sweet but you can specify sweetness while ordering so you can correct on my mistake. Additionally, the staff was VERY friendly and welcoming even to two out of towners.

I've been going here regularly for about a year, and this place never lets me down! Best pho I've had in Reno so far. Consistent quality, good prices, and great service. The women who runs the place recognizes me and my boyfriend every time we go now and she and the waiter are total sweethearts. I highly recommend this place.

After seeing Mark P's picture & review of the spicy tom yum noodle soup w/ seafood, I knew I had to get me some of that ASAFP. Well I can say it lived up to the hype, and thensome! It came in huge pho-sized bowl, steaming with an amazing aroma with lots of shrimp peeking out. Along with the generous amount nice-sized shrimps, there were also mussels, scallops, and squid, about 4-5 pieces of each. And then the broth, oh my god, this broth. Perfectly spiced, tangy, savory...just freaking amazing. Best $12 I've ever spent. I'd suggest you go alone when you get this, so you can just focus on the flavors and moan with pleasure without judgment or distraction. This soup commands your full undivided attention. Mark P, I owe ya one!

I didn't know what to expect before I got to Wishbone since I had read some of these reviews, but I'm definitely one of those people who has to see for themselves. So, I came in the other night and it was quite busy. The staff was very helpful even though there was a bunch of fraternity brothers yelling out their orders and asking numerous questions. A cheery college aged girl who took care of most of my order explained how the sauces may taste given that there were soo many options to choose from, so that was nice. I ordered a mix of white and dark chicken with chipotle lime mayo and this yellow curry sauce. I prefer the dark as it was much juicier. I think it will be hard for me to try the other sauces since I was pretty pleased with the chipotle lime mayo which was both smokey and fresh tasting while the curry was on the sweeter side, so I really enjoyed the difference in my sauce flavors. Luckily, I had enough room for just one of their pies. They had many on display and from what I was told they bake them all in house. I chose the chocolate peanut butter one and boy did that feeel good. I'm a big chocolate girl, so I'm not sure I was surprised that I loved it. As for my drink, I just asked for some water. The young gentleman at the register politely handed me a cup. I should mention that the decor is pretty enchanting and you can tell the owners care about presentation. I dined upstairs and it was pretty spacious. I will certainly come back and bring my husband and my sisters, so that they can see and eat for themselves.

I had never eaten here before, but after a fun-filled Sunday, my boyfriend suggested this place for an early dinner. We each ordered a beer, red pepper hummus, the BBQ Chicken pizza and the gyro sandwich. The pizza was good. At first I was worried about the cheddar cheese with the chicken and the onions, but with the caramelized onions it was really good. I definitely was glad for the onions because they provided a sweet factor so the otherwise really salty dish. The hummus was alright. It looked really watery, but it had flavor when we tried it. The pita it came with was delicious, though! We had to get some more, but it came out soft and warm. The gyro was also good. It had all the right fixin's and all. All in all, the food was A-Ok. Nothing was bad, but nothing stood out special for me. It was a nice place to end our day, and I would go back if we were in the area.

Great service + great food = return customers I recommend the house salad and the grilled pork chop. Coworkers also had house salads with either lamb burger or grilled salmon. Everyone left very happy. Can't wait to go back!

Best Indian in Tampa Bay. Have a little patience. They could not have guessed how successful they are becoming... the service will catch up. They are very sweet, good people. We will definitely eat here again and again.
Authentic Greek food. Love the octopus. Love the bronzino. One small critique, whenever we order the horiatiki salad, the tomatoes are never really that fresh. But overall really good.

Well you know how cafes are. Some are strictly coffee shops. Some are eateries. Some have couches. Some do not. Some are hipstery. Some are bougie. But essentially all cafes can be judged on 3 things: coffee, atmosphere, and the presence of wi-fi. So let me begin with the obvious. Yes, they have wi-fi. I didn't use it but they have it. From what I understand, it's not timed. So YAY, PRODUCTIVITY!!!! B) The coffee was good. Not great. But good. I'd get a coffee here again. 3) The atmosphere is conducive to meeting up for a chat or for getting work DONE!! I found the volume of the space to be fairly low, as nearly every person in the place was busy on their laptops, peeping over the edge of their screen every so often, taking a sip of their coffee and reverting back to their business. There were a couple groups of people quietly talking of steamy beverages, but most people were focused on their computers. I think the tables are spaced pretty tightly but I found it to be an optimal meeting space, with bright lighting and a nourishing, warm vibe. The couches looked comfy and the option of table space is nice. It's a cafe so I'm not here to write about HOW MINDBLOWING THIS PLACE IS....as it's not like it's a cafe with a Cirque Du Soleil show in progress as you sip on a latte with a sparkler in it. But for a cafe, it's certainly a nice one. If I lived in the area, it would certainly serve its function as a nice chill place to work, or read, or meet with decent coffee and a lovely change of scenery from my normal workspace. I like it. That's all there is to it.
Went downhill. Dirty dishes small portions food wasn't good. I always loved PF changs but not anymore.
Love, Love this place. Everything is good. Seriously. The waitstaff is friendly, and, in my opinion, the calamari is the the best in the city. Try their bluefish - fish lovers won't be disappointed!

This was a really great place to eat. It looked like a small family owned reataurant and the food was excellent. I had the brisket and beef pho and my girlfriend had the chicken pho. Both were exploding with flavor and our two servers were on point with water refills and anything else we needed. I'm glad we found this place bc I think it's our new place to eat Vietnamese. I like going to small business restaurants instead of the everyday chain restaurant.

I love to eat the food, especially the Pho, when I visit New Orleans. The seafood is so fresh and delicious. The atmosphere is nice and the seating is always ample. The service is quick too. It is highly recommended to come back here to enjoy it.

This is an excellent place. We came here and from the moment we enter and leave the place the customer service is awesome. The food is fresh and very very delicious. I have mo complain as this is the best Mediterranean restaurant I found in Nashville. First of all you can easily notice the place even when your driving down the road. The place is very very clean. Their grilled chicken is super delicious and their shrimp and salmon. My husband had the beef but then because the food is so delicious he ended up wants more pita bread. I will come back here over and over again now that I found one of my favorite Mediterranean Restaurant in Nashville. I very highly recommend this place. As well if you're a bodybuilder this is an excellent place to come get your healthy food. Whenever you're visiting Nashville or even your local don't missed one half of your life to come and stopped by and had their delicious food. Thank you Blue Fig for putting up this awesome place and for your awesome excellent service.

Hmmm, a little overpriced (15 bucks for a bowl). The hostess prepping my hookah had a bad cough and kept sniffling. He was also yelling into the phone for quite some time. Another man was sitting in the corner watching a program on his computer very loud. Hookah bars are supposed to be relaxing and this place on this night was far from that.

Me and my girlfriend had dinner here and the food was awesome. The service was excellent and the quality of the food was outstanding. The prices are very accessible and worth it. I had the Chicken Makhani and it was delicious. My girlfriend had the Channa Masala and was equally great. Has its own parking lot in front and back of the establishment. Definitely coming back.
Delicious food! excellent service, very unique and shic atmosphere, clean and progressive! This is defanitly the best Asian fusion restaurant in the area,!!! Boomy gave us excellent service!!

Smiley's is my ideal local restaurant. It has excellent customer service, delicious food, and good character. Smiley himself is very personable and likes to engage in conversation with all of the customers who walk through the door. The young dark-haired girl who often works the register is also super sweet. The food has always been fresh and delicious, whether I have eaten in or taken it to go. The chicken shawarma sandwich, hummus side with pita, and tangy raspberry smoothie are some of my favorites to get here. There is a seating area with a TV and bathroom on the lower level in case you want to sit down and eat. For me it's the perfect place to grab lunch to go or bring friends for a casual dinner. They are also pretty quick. The one time I had to wait (not even that long), Smiley apologized for the delay and stuck an extra pita in my bag. Unexpected and not needed, but very nice! Overall, I really like Smiley's Cafe and will continue to eat here.

NO MORE SAMS BEACH BAR FOR ME AND MY FAMILY. Have gone there many many times since I live within blocks of this place for the sunsets. Not the food. Food is low quality. Drinks USED TO BE PRICED OK BUT, AS OF FATHERS DAY THE DRINK SIZES HAVE SHRANK AND THE PRICES HAVE INCREASED. ALSO, THE DRINKS WE HAD TODAY HAD VERY LITTLE ALCOHOL AND WERE ALMOST 1/2 the size of what they were serving in the near past. Price of the drinks we had today on FATHERS DAY rose $2.00 each. If you want to PAY TO SEE THE SUNSET by ordering expensive low quality food and expensive small alcoholic beverages then this is the place to go. Spoke to the manager about the increased cost for less product. He just tried to BS his way around the question. I told him the restaurant had gone to crap under his management. FROM NOW ON MY MONEY WILL BE SPENT at the INN ON THE GULF ACROSS THE STREET.......WHERE I GET QUALITY FOOD AND DRINKS. The manager pretty much let me know so what, we can do without your business. Also, I can say as many times as we have been to Sam's Beach Club bar that the employees are miserable and are embarrassed by the way management is treating customers. I feel sorry for the employees.
