A good 3/4 of the dishes are vegetarian, and almost all of them sounded great. I got the avocado sandwich, with a side of hummus and carrots. Everything was delicious, and the service was great. (I didn't catch the waitress' name, but she had blondish hair dyed lavender and other colors, and was very helpful and great.) Even though it was a touch more expensive than I wish it were, there are a lot more items on the menu I'm eager to try, so I will be back there soon.

My partner and I live in town and go out to eat at least twice a week. Avalon continues to be our favorite restaurant in town. The new space is growing on me and I love the addition of the bar. The owner/chef is usually in attendance and makes everyone feel welcome. The one thing I really miss from the old location is the wider variety of selection during the cheese course.
Driest chicken known to man. Its like chicken jerky! And pricey.

Most underrated Mediterranean place in town. Been going for years and never been disappointed with any dish. If you like Hummus, you must try the Hummus and Lamb on the menu. Dip that pita bread away! Meat and tomato stew is also great. So is the new stir fry. Lunch platters are all good too. And I love their falafel.

Fez, is a great chill out venue!! Tucked away right off South Street ( I almost want to keep this to myself) . Anyway, I love the Venue, Moroccan themed, Belly Dancing, and Hookah! I have yet to eat here, but will update when and if that happens. The Hookah is decently priced compared to some of the other places in Philly. Oh yes, they do serve wine. Definitely cool for casually hanging out solo, with the girls, guys, or 'Cupcakin' with your significant other. I put this on my iLove List. Check it out and let me know what you think...

The first time I've ever been here and was immediately welcomed when I walked through the door. I sat up at the bar and enjoyed a great cocktail while I waited for a friend to arrive. On his arrival we were immediately seated and waited on. I did like the fact that I was able to choose wherever I wanted to sit. We didn't go too crazy on our food but decided on a couple salads which were very tasteful and healthy so that was definitely a plus!!!overall great experience... The only thing I believe would improve this restaurant is to have had some organic free range chicken. They're promoting a healthy lifestyle so why not go all the way and do it the right way. #organic #freerange
Very good, authentic Indian food in the heart of Philly. Be sure to order the Butter Chicken with plenty of naan bread.
Bad service. Bad food (I ordered bun bo hue). I don't recommend this place. Not authentic by any means!

My husband and are so excited that we found this place! While living in Arlington, VA we tried Ethiopian for the first time and fell in love with it. We had a favorite restaurant we would go to often so when we moved here earlier this year we wanted to find a new favorite. We tried St Yared and that experience left us disappointed. Our experience here was a complete 180! Service 3/5 Service was as expected. Our waitress was friendly and got our order right. The restaurant wasn't super busy but I had to flag her down a couple times because she just didn't check on us very often, not a huge deal though. Our food didn't take too long and it was hot when we go it. Atmosphere/Ambiance 3/5 The restaurant feels very dated and not very warm. But it was clean and the seats were comfortable enough. They also have a bottle of hand sanitizer at each table which is nice. This is probably a strange thing to mention but they had an electronic sign at the back of the restaurant that blinked between the word "coffee" and the picture of a coffee mug in neon colors and that was fairly distracting actually. Next time I'll try to remember to sit on the opposite side of the table, my husband isn't bothered by things like that as much as I am! Food 5/5 Let's be honest, we didn't come here for the service or the atmosphere, we came here for the food and the food was most definitely the star of the show! We got our usual entrees...my husband got the Kitfo and I got the beef Awaze Tibs (mild) and both were absolutely delicious! They tasted exactly the same as what we got at our favorite restaurant in Arlington. We are beyond excited and will absolutely be back!

Not a good experience. When I went up to the sauce station to get the cilantro garlic sauce there was hair in it, which completly made me lose my appetite. When the server/floor attendant came and dropped off my food, I asked how he was doing and he said he was sick but fine. Not cool to have a sick person working especially around food. Lastly, the chicken avocado wrap and fries he brought out to me were cold. Sucks that it was bad service because I work close to the location and its very convenient. Will not be returning.

They seem to have fixed their problems with the wait staff. The current servers are personable and knowledgeable. My only gripe is now the kitchen is inconsistent. I've heard that the head chef splits his time between the two restaurants. If he is there the food is good, otherwise it could suffer. I'm not sure if that is what I have experienced, but I have experienced inconsistencies. The great news is that there is always Groupon or similar coupons out there for Spice Kitchen, so you can really get a good meal for a great bargain!

I came here solo one night because I had gotten all dressed up for a date that cancelled at the last minute. I was all ready for good food and didn't mind trying it out on my own! The bartender was an absolute sweetheart and my waiter was kind and attentive. The decor isn't anything to write home about, but you're not there for that, are you? You know you're in for something good when you want about 12 things on the menu and really have to agonize over what you want. Add to that the fact that there were at least 4-5 specials that sounded equally delicious and it was a tough choice. I had the sausage and figs appetizer and one of the specials, a garlic crusted salmon with tomatoes and crab meat. The sausage and figs was a really interesting introduction. I found it just a tad too sweet for me, but the figs were absolutely fantastic and the sausage flavorful. I think what pushed it over the line was the balsamic sauce. Even so, I ate the whole thing. Let me say again that the figs were incredible. The salmon was pretty darn incredible as well. Everything was fresh, perfectly seasoned, balanced, and the crab meat was present in huge chunks. So nice, since a lot of places tend to skimp on the crab. Prices are reasonable and the portions won't leave you feeling like a beached whale for the rest of the night. Definitely felt like great, traditional family food. I will go again to try the other 11 things I wanted!

So we moved to the Main Line from the City a few weeks ago. We've been in search of good Thai since. Based on the Yelp reviews, we tried Siamese Princess. The food was incredibly oily and not very tasty relative to the better Thai places in Philadelphia. Maybe we're spoiled but I don't think we'll be going back to Siamese Princess.

Great food. Ate here for the first time with a few friends. The service was great, the ambiance was nice, and the food was delicious. A variety of options for vegetarians, and an easy to understand menu. I will certainly add this to my rotation of restaurants.

New restaurant..beautiful and modern inside. Very courteous, friendly service. We were seated quickly and our food came right away. Customer service was first rate. Food is EXCELLENT and great prices! For appys we got spring rolls, torpedo shrimp, fried squid (calamari)..For mains we ordered the beef stir fry with crispy noodles (my fav!), seafood pad Thai, BBQ short ribs and fried rice. You cannot go wrong with your order, everything is delicious!! It was a full house when we were there at 5:30pm on a Sunday. I'd recommend making a reservation for weekend nights (Fri/Sat).
Absolutely amazing Thai food!!! The Crab Fried Rice is to die for! And the basil Thai is amazing as well... pretty much anything you order here you should expect to be WOWED!!!

We stopped here for lunch on New Years Eve. Our waitress took very good care of us, and the food was yummy. Our group ordered pot stickers, Beef Salad, Ginger Ginger, Sweet and Sour, Pad Thai, and a coconut milk based soup. Everything was wonderful. I can't wait for summer to sit out on their patio by the water.

I was hesitant to eat here due to some of the other reviews, but they could not have been more inaccurate. I lived in Bangkok for 6 months and wanted to introduce my picky boyfriend to Thai food. I was nervous but the food was incredible. I had the coco Thai basil -- the veggies were fresh and the meat was perfectly tender. My bf had the drunken noodles and they were very flavorful. I highly recommend this place and intend to become a regular!

Disappointed to say the least. Used to be my favorite place. It seems it has gone down hill with cleanliness. Our silverware was dirty, both sets, one had dried on rice stuck on it. A fly on the rim of my beer as it was brought out, I immediately told her and she took it back immediately and said it was last nights bartender who left fruit juice out and it attracted them. Our date night was spent making sure the food was okay. I know things happen, but when we have only a couple date nights a year, I like them to be enjoyable. We weren't even offered a beer credit. Nothing. Won't go back. ***Addon 1/7 I found out yesterday my mother also had a bug in her lettuce wraps, and emailed to let them know what had happened. We both have emailed the contact email regarding this issue, I having no knowledge of her experience until yesterday, and we both have had ZERO contact regarding this bad service. We will not return to Fulins at any location.

We came here after the southern women's show. The location is great, reserved parking. We ate out on the patio. I ordered the mofongo and skirt steak (churrasco). I've had mofongo before and usually it is very dry, but this mofongo was a little more moist and came apart easier. The steak was absolutely delicious. We shared the dessert sampler with the tembleque, flan, and tres leches. All three were delicious, but my favorite was the tembleque. It was gelatinous like a flan, but much more dense. The entree portions were great and the sampler is a good choice if you want to share with friends. I would definitely come back.

South Indian is a style of cuisine we have too little of in the greater Philadelphia area. Dosa Hut and Chaat House is doing a great job in representing it. If want a Dosa.. go here. The restaurant is in the first floor of a house. Two sided dining room, with televisions showing Indian soap operas. Menu is extensive but I was there for the Dosa. I had a Mysore Masala Dosa. It is a generous portion, served with several sauces to accompany it. Service is a bit slow, but not to the point of being annoying. Worth a trip.
Incredible food and service. Lunch special it worth it. Chicken Satay or Tues and Thurs worth checking out. Overall a 5star.

I have been wanting to try this neighborhood spot for some time, so this Sunday morning my guy and I went around 9:30am for breakfast. Parking was easy and we were seated right away. The decor is very Mexical cool with a beautiful bar, white brick walls, and benches with lots of throw pillows. We ordered coffees to start and decided on a 1/2 order of the Cuban toast (aka French toast) to share. Perfectly cooked and just the right amount of sweet and crunchy! For the entrees, we had the CHILAQUILES ROJOS with chicken and the STEAK & POTATO TORTA. My guy goes for quantity, and the Chilaquiles was the winner in this category. I found the Torta to have more flavor. I noticed they offer a generous mimosa carafe and the drinks being served to our neighbors looked very good. Looking forward to going back for dinner soon!
Nice people, but food is very sweet. We had the pad Thai and massaman curry, and couldn't stomach either.

We purchased a Groupon and decided to give this place a try and were not disappointed. Unfortunately, we had a little trouble finding the place even though we live just a few miles away. We almost gave up after passing it twice before finding it. Walking in we were impressed by the beautiful copper tables and romantic ambiance. The waitress was friendly and helpful and the food came quickly. The food was delicious and reasonably priced. The dessert (peach bread pudding, chocolate filled phyllo dough dessert) was so good my boyfriend and I asked if they could cater our upcoming wedding.

I was really craving their roasted veggie side and decided to stop for lunch. I ordered the Salmon wrap with roasted veggies as a side. For the price, I did not feel the wrap was worth it. The wrap did not taste bad, but it did not really satisfy me. If it was a lower price, I might have been happy, but it should come with more. I should have ordered 2 veggie sides and a cookie. The place was very clean and the service was wonderful. Everyone was happy and it was a relaxed environment. I would definitely come back, but try something else on their menu or just eat roasted veggies till I am sick of them.
Love their green curry! The restaurant is very clean and the service is always great. One of the best Thai spots in Santa Barbara!

Pita Jungle is a great place to go for healthy and fresh food. My advice is to schedule your lunch prior to noon so you can get a seat. My only complaint is that the order of hummus only comes with one pita bread. Really???

After reading the other posts I was a bit apprehensive about going here. Went around lunchtime, place was not busy. The waiter was great, attentive and answered our questions. I had the chicken Pho, partner had the vegan noodles. Make sure you ask your waiter, he stated that almost any noodle dish can be made vegie or vegan. Food arrived very fast, good flavor, nice sprouts, basil and lime to add to the soups. I will definitely go back here, the price is good and the service as well.
Not to bad for $5; I liked everything except the ground chicken patty. Next time I will try the beef or lamb.

Yes the interior could be a bit more appealing but the food is whats important. Eggs rolls are great, the veggie spring rolls are even better! Pho is very good, not too greasy and not saturated with MSG like other pho places around tucson. I dunno if the shrimp curry is still on the menu.. Maybe made by request only, but gotta try it, soooo good!! :)

Great place for a late night snack and drink. I went w/ the Black Angus Sliders and they were perfect. Great wine selection and service to go with it. Great spot for 'people watching' in the St Petes waterfront.

Wife and I went in with a Groupon which sparked a thread on Yelp Talk - worth looking up if you are a Groupon user or hater, interesting feedback to some basic questions. Why did we try this place? Mainly because I used to live within a five minute walk of Greektown in Chicago and have been missing those restaurants ever since we moved out of the Chicago area in the 90s. One overarching comment is that the flavors, while delicious, were still a bit different than what we were seeking. About the food: + Baby octopus was good but I would have preferred a bit more simple seasoning - there's really nothing more needed than olive oil, salt, pepper and fresh oregano in my opinion. + Baklava was quite possibly the best I've had in the last decade! Something about the fact that it was served slightly warm, topped with a drizzle of clover honey and had sliced fruit as an accompaniment. + Saganaki was the best that we've had in St. Louis! Flambe done table-side and doused with the lemon to finish the dish. Really loved the resulting crispy edges and corners. +/- The "gyros" was good but different enough from any gyros I've had anywhere in the world that it would have to be something magical to be a positive. Unfortunately, the lamb got lost in everything else they piled onto the pita. - Pita bread really would have been much better had it been griddled instead of lightly warmed as wound up being a bit bland. This actually dragged down the enjoyment of both the saganaki and the gyros somewhat. - The service kida sucked! Our waitress couldn't seem to escape the table fast enough. I told her it was our first time there and expressed an interest in the various offerings but received a healthy dose of indifference that dragged this review down by a star. Next time around...no mention of a Groupon and we will dodge that waitress. Maybe a revision will be in order...

Great Groupon deal & high hopes. My salad w ginger dressing was crisp & fresh. The dressing just fair. I've definitely had better. The sushi was very good. We had the "crazy dragon" roll (or "mad" something!?) Please see the pix! Here's where we go downhill & the rating was killed. The chicken in my Yaki Udon almost tasted freezer burnt! Vince thought maybe a brine. Ruined my otherwise excellent dish. I loved the actual Udon noodles & mushrooms & egg in the dish. Vince felt the same about the chicken in his moo shoo. I'd return but would NOT get that chicken again!!!!! (I took it for my dog!)
Very nice service, and comfortable atmosphere. Food is quite tasty and well-presented. Location and setting is nicely close on the Mesa, but off the beaten path with good parking.

Went with a group of 9 people total and it was a GREAT night! I never would have found this place on my own, but I'm glad I went because I will be back. It is a total experience while you eat. From walking up the tiny steps to the every inch of the walls being covered in decor. We ordered 1 of everything off the menu and everything was DELICIOUS. The only tricky part was trying to eat a chicken with no utensils. The only downside was that they never gave us the rose water so we were constantly going to the bathroom to wash our hands and the towels they gave us smelled musky. It was a great time and the belly dancers were awesome and stuck around to show us some moves. I will definitely be back here with more friends for them to experience it.

Very disappointed! The service was horrible. I was in the restaurant for a takeout order of 4 fishes. I waited for nearly an hour. It turned out that three of the four dishes were made long before the last one was made. The taste was disappointing.

Zen Yai is the best Thai food in Santa Barbara, and one of my favorite restaurants in SB, period. The food always tastes fresh, and not as greasy as other Thai food can sometimes be. The Zen Yai Online Noodles are amazing - I get it everytime. Love their Thai Iced Tea - not too sweet. The staff and owners are always friendly and pleasant. Great ambiance. Great date spot. @Lauren C. - it's a small space and they only have so much room to work with.

Ariana is a long-established Afghan restaurant in the heart of Old City Philadelphia. It's been around a long time because it is well-run and the food is good. I attended a Yelp event here last evening that confirmed these facts. For starters, we had the famous and delicious Afghan Sambosas and Aashaks. I could have eaten a lot more of these but then I wouldn't have had room for the entrée. An ordinary salad was served in between courses but my entrée of the Afghan national dish of Kabuli Palow was perfectly put together and with the addition of Chatni hot sauce, it was def tasty. A desert of Firnee (cardomom and rose water custard) concluded the meal - that is if you don't count the hookah as a course. Of course for many people in the restaurant, I think the belly dancing was the true desert!

One of the best Thai places in the area, if not the best. Good service, good food, good atmosphere, good signature dishes and drinks...have no complaints. The restaurant was packed when we got there but still got seated right away. Throughout our stay there and while we were leaving, the restaurant rarely had a empty table for longer than 5 mins. Clearly I'm not the only fan.
Worst Thai food and service I've ever had. Will not be back. Quite disappointed since the review were great.

If you are looking for delicious Thai food come here! Just be aware that they do not take reservations and you can expect a wait during dinner times. The place is small and always packed! However, the wait is worth it! Their Pad Thai is delicious and we have never been disappointed with any of their curries. We will come back!

I was really excited to come here but was sorely disappointed. I ordered the grilled pork and rice. The seasoning on the pork was tasty but the meat was chewy and so fatty. My kids ordered pho and I had a quick sip of the broth and it was tasteless and full of fat too. I will say that my friend got the adult size and the broth looked way better. Darker and richer. It would be a shame if they have the kids a poorer quality broth just because they are kids. I've had so much better in the Bay Area that there is no need for me to come back here.

I went here for a BYO a few months ago, but I figured I would give review it as I feel like it's often forgotten about in West Philly. I came with a group of about 8 people, and everyone enjoyed their food, even people who were a little bit unsure about Thai food. The service was great, and the place is open pretty late, and didn't kick my group out immediately after paying. Also, can I mention how insanely cheap Vientiane is? It was ~$7 per person in my entire group, including tip which is pretty insane.

Great Vietnamese food. Very generous portions. I'm Chinese and not Vietnamese so I don't feel entirely qualified to judge how authentic it is. However, I see a lot of Vietnamese patrons when I go so that gives me some level of validation. The boba teas are not that great. The tapioca balls are too hard - the balls should be quite soft. Other than that, everything is great.

Most reviews on here already sum up Butcher and Bee nicely: small plates intended to be shared served up slowly with an expensive price tag. A few pointers left off: Pro Tip 1: this place can be tricky to find. It shares a small parking lot with Edley's and Fat Bottom. It's a grey building with the words Butcher and Bee painted on in a lighter shade of grey. It's EXTREMELY easy to miss from the road. Pro Tip 2: free parking lot across the street (North side of Main) Pro Tip 3: let's talk bathrooms. Specifically, hand dryers. The faucet has two wings jetting out on either side. Powered by hand motion, which of course means they're a b**** to turn on, the faucet's wings are in fact the dryer. Yes, you'll feel like an idiot as you look around confused to find no hand towels or obvious dryer... You may even laugh at yourself as you return to your table with wet hands and explain to your fellow diners that the bathroom is lacking an essential component... Only to realize later you should have known better when dinning at a hipster restaurant. Three stars given as its a fun experience, but in one visit my interest and appetite are satisfied (and wallet exhausted).

I've been here on two occasions, one of which featured the tasting menu. I for one never had a particular affinity for Greek food, largely because my experiences have been limited to, like, Philadelphia foodcart kabobs or something. Really though, I know that was not representative, but still never had a more "authentic" experience until Kanella. Fabulous food. I cannot recommend the tasting menu more highly, which featured such unusual but delicious bits as roasted rabbit kidneys and grilled octopus. The waiters are kind of hipster. Also, my table was particularly close to the next table, which was particularly close to the table next to that, causing a minor water spilling fiasco to which the table next to me responded with a stilted upperclass "oh dear!" bit. That was amusing, but they should split the tables up a bit more.

This noon time, I have a bowl of noodles in Phamous Cafe. I ate out a hair about 2 inches long. I picked up and put aside on the table and go on eating. Then I found ANOTHER hair that is as long as a FOOT. I am so upset about the hairs noodles since I have been this pho restaurant almost once a week and always have a bowl of it. I don't know what I had eaten before and what were hidden in the noodles that I ignored. I pointed out the hairs issues to the manager but they are very impolite and doesn't show any sorry to me. I will never be Phamous Cafe ANYMORE!

I live in Delaware, and I was told by my Honey that live in Philly that Sister Muhammad's Kitchen was open after renovations. Let's just say I was excited to eat there because he raved about the restaurant soooooo much!!!! We went last Sat 7/12/2014 and was very pleased with the welcoming service that was pleasant and friendly, the menu selection was exciting, the restaurant very clean, and of course the food we ordered was well prepared, seasoned just right, scrumptious and the desserts we had later were heavenly OMG . My Honey ordered his favorite fish steak hoagie with all his favorite trimmings along with fries. I was undecided for a while because they have so many awesome dishes on the menu...I settled with fried whiting platter. They were generous with portions and my sides were fresh glazed carrots not can carrots, and some awesome mac & cheese OMG!!! We were very pleased with our meals and our desserts. We left with our desserts which were a whole bean, cheesecake bean pie, and 3 bread puddings lol!!!! Just want to end by saying we are fans of Sister Muhammad's Kitchen and We are spreading the word out about Sister Muhammad's Kitchen. We will be returning soon!!!! Thank you for sharing your blessing!!!

I've ordered take out from here a bunch of times and always thought it to be delicious. My first time dining in, and I'm impressed. Very clean, nice tables and chairs and decor. Our server was very polite and welcoming. It was a great meal. Tried something new, too. THE FOOD: Started with Chinese egg rolls, which I LOVE!!! The in-house hot mustard kicks butt! The heat just pops in your nose..love it. The egg rolls are fat and crispy and burst with flavors of cabbage and veggies and pork. I tried fried tofu for the first time. Very bland on its own, the sauce is also mild. Little slices of red and orange peppers don't add much. It was good the next day mixed with other leftovers. My entree was Kung pao beef. Disappointed because it was not spicy at all. Added some hot mustard to give it kick. The beef was tasty. My girlfriend had Sweet and sour chicken. Which was great. Chicken was moist and coating was good. She also had fried rice which is always good.

One of my favorite restaurants to eat at. The food is always amazing and delicious. I live tbd little drink perk you can get after filling up your card. The fried rice is full of flavor and they serve you a huge portion so you're never hungry after a meal.

My wife an I had an absolutely outstanding New Year's Eve dinner at Pan d'olive. The food and service were terrific. Our server, Mark, was knowledgeable, helpful, courteous, and affable. I ordered a whole branzino and it was one of the best fish dinners I've ever had. My wife's trout was equally superb. The restaurant is very comfortable and relaxing. We had a perfect meal and the prices were quite reasonable for such high quality food and service. I have spent much more at other restaurants for meals that were no where near as satisfying.

Best Mediterranean food ever!! I love the chop chop salad, the humus and felafel are fantastic!! The menu is reasonably priced and you definitely get what you for!!! Don't pass this place by if you're in the mood for a satisfying meal, plus convienant with the drive through !!

Definitely a place that I will take many friends to. I don't remember anything I ate, but it was all incredible. Make sure you go with an empty stomach because they serve several servings/courses. I love how I don't feel pressured to leave as soon as I get the final course. This place is somewhere I can come eat and lounge for awhile after I'm done eating. Make sure you make a reservation if going with a large group because it's quite popular and can get crowded. Also, cash only. I think our bill came out around $70 for food, house wine, and 18% gratuity for 2. This is a staple place to visit if in the area!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: They moved and it is even better: http://www.yelp.com/biz/taj-mahal-boise-2

I was looking for some gluten free Thai or Chinese food in Tucson and Chopstix came through! First of all, the location is an unassuming store-front in a strip mall with several other restaurants. Inside, the decor is zen and open with plenty of seating. We came on a Friday night and it wasn't too busy which is surprising for how good the food and service ended up being. Chopstix offers a nice selection of gluten free appetizers and main courses. I chose the chicken lettuce wraps and curry noodles with chicken. To say the portions were generous is an understatement -- I could have eaten the lettuce wraps alone and been satisfied. Needless to say there were leftovers. My dining companion had the pot stickers and Thai Basil special with chicken which he thoroughly enjoyed. Service was friendly and prompt and I felt like we got a ton of food for our money. I would highly recommend Chopstix for anyone who has gluten free needs or not.

Normally they closed for two hours, during the middle of the day on Sunday but today they had so many customers they stayed open.From the minute you walk in here, your mouth drops opened. Not only by the wonderful scent of different spices and herbs. But, the aroma of coconut milk and Curry is in the air. Very subtle though not overpowering, you feel such peace and serenity in this beautiful environment. What you may envision a someone's beautiful home,in Thailand. The pics speak for themselves. They are well worth looking at. That's only the beginning the atmosphere, the food is unbelievably good. Actually I do not want to underestimate my opinion and observation, the FOOD IS AWESOME, OUTSTANDING! I have sampled quite a bit of tight food. Had some good, very good an aaah... The typical run-of-the-mill stuff. Having lunch hour our server was wearing the traditional garment that the Thai women wear, she truly looked like a princess. She smiled, brought me Thai hot tea that I ordered, and it was served the traditional way with the small teapot and the customary small cup. Actually there is a very good reason for the small teapot, and the small cup.It's obvious, keeps the tea fresh and hot much longer then what most restaurants are doing now giving you a mug. I ordered the pending chicken, my husband had another curry dish. We were in a bit of a rush, and unfortunately I did not get to really review all the selections on the menu. I wish I would've had more time, so definitely I will go back. I noticed on one of the peaks that they have yellow curry tofu and it looks really, really good. By the way, IF IT INTERESTS YOU THEY HAVE A FULL BAR. WITH BEERS FROM THAILAND. For those That Enjoy Exploring Beers from other FAR AWAY LANDS. Of course they do have a good selection of Saki. Much to our surprise we were still able to order from their lunch menu. And the total cost of our meal was incredibly reasonable. A bonus, was that I took a box home. And had a wonderful tree the next day. CAN'T WAIT TO GO BACK AND ENJOY, A GREAT MEAL WITH A + SERVICE. Thank you YELP!
YUM! Food is great. And excited they deliver!

It's been too long since I've been here. Had the lunch buffet. I got there just after it opened, and all the food on the buffet was extremely fresh. Impeccable everything. The curries seemed a bit spicey, as in authentic and not toned down for the North American palate. Either that or I've turned into a spice wimp. (Hint: use rice to "dilute" a curry if it's too spicey.) They have both vegetarian dishes and meat dishes. The vegetable fried rice is unlike the veg fried rice you get at Chinese restaurants. I thought the rice was elegant. It served as a good base to soak up the sauce of the curries. The various chicken dishes are classics, chicken curry, chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, and another roasted-type chicken which I think was labeled as BBQ Chicken. There was also a goat curry, but I didn't try it this time. An interesting dish was "Chicken Manchoorian", which tasted great, and was an Indian take on a Chinese preparation. The naan was perfect, and seemed made in house. The fruit on the dessert table, white grapes, red grapes and cantelope, was very fresh. I loved the mango pudding. There was also gulab jamun, but I didn't try it. There was a delicious item called vegetable samosa chaat, consisting of a fresh salsa, and veggie samosas. The construction of the samosas was unique, almost like a mini veggie-burger, which I thought was excellent. Ambience and cleanliness (including the men's room) continues to be high-end. Ceramic plates, stainless steel utensils, quality paper napkins for lunch. Servers are well-dressed in uniforms, and very professional. Lunch price was $7.99 plus drink, plus tax, plus tip. Well worth it. Lunch clientele includes South Asians, so I assume the food is authentic. Overall, they continue to be a classy joint. Very worty of impressing the boss/wife/gf/inlaws. If you are looking for a 100% vegetarian Indian restaurant, that would be "Passage to India" in the same building, but a few doors down, where you enter into the "Om India Plaza" grocery store. India Palace has been in business a long time. No wonder, they are excellent. (They also run the catering hall next door.)

I find it hard to find pho with white meat chicken. This is the second location in the city where it's been pretty good. The broth is simple and you can build the flavor profile as you wish. Staff was friendly and food came fast.

Just left this place and I will never go back. We walk in at 8:30pm and order are meal. At approximately 8:40 the manager, who only identified himself as I. Johnson comes out from the back and tells us, "this store goes dark at 9pm". So I ask him do we need to take are food to go. His professional reply was "No just eat fast". I immediately asked for a refund and advised him that I will not spend my hard earned money at an establishment that treats their guest this way. But wait it's gets better. As he is processing my refund the girls who took are order walks out with are food, and I. Johnson tells her "throw that shit out", in front of my 10 year old daughter. At that point I told him not to curse In Front of a child and he says "I can do what ever I want". I asked for the manger and of course he is the manager, so I asked for the owner names, which he said he could say because he could pronounce it. I hthe owners number and plan to file a complaint with the owner in the morning. Update on Pita Kebob incident: Owner, Khalid Abouelhouda, reached out to me and we spoke at length about the situation. I am satisfied with the outcome and can move forward. The employee and I also spoke and he personally apologized to me and my family for his actions, which we accepted. Khalid and his employee made this right and we are satisfied with that. I wanted to update everyone because many only put out the bad news and not the good. -- feeling relieved at Pita Kebob.

We tried almost everything here, and it was all good, but not excellent. Soft shell crab: Very ordinary. Good, but difficult to screw up soft shell crab. Pot stickers: Very ordinary. Curry salmon: Good, but nothing special. Seaweed salad: Could have come from CostCo's large container of seaweed salad. Spicy chicken wings: Good, but very difficult to screw up fried wings. Overall, a good meal but nothing really stood out.

We were here early on a Sunday - around 5 it was empty. Much bigger inside than the front of house suggests. We had the lamb w humus, babaganouj, zucchini, and kale. All were excellent! Attentive service, music a little loud but nice ambiance otherwise! Go here!!!

I thought Cucina Zapata was my well kept secret but it looks like the cat is out of the bag now. Ever since I tried Cucina at the Vendy's, I've been amazed with their fusion cuisine and quality of food. When I found out that they were located in my part of town (UC), I was elated and immediately tracked them down! What is not to love here? I've tried everything on their menu and they're all sooooo good! +Thai short rib or chicken satay taco ($3 a piece): great flavors, not too heavy, avocados aplenty, and delicious spicy mayo sauce +Chicken Katsu ($5 + 50cents for egg): substantially-sized, crunchy chicken strips with rice, tomato chunks, and sesame seeds in tonkatsu sauce +Red veggie curry ($5): potato and pumpkin chunks with rice in a creamy curry broth, DELICIOUS. Spice level is perfect. +Cap'n Crunch encrusted tilapia burrito($6): slightly sweet, crunchy, and flavorful; generously portioned. Don't miss out on this one! +Mexican veggie burger ($4): I'm not a vegetarian but I really wouldn't miss meat if I could eat this daily. Love the spicy mayo! +Thai ice tea/thai green tea ($2): refreshing, not too sweet, waaay better than starbucks Owners are super gracious and friendly. They really care about their customers since they make an effort to engage in conversation with you. Only downsides: -Some of their menu choices take a long time like the Tilapia, especially during the lunch rush (~15 minute wait) but totally worth it -Random closings. I've been here a couple of times only to find them closed. A few weeks ago, I dragged my friend after class to try my favorite food truck. We were so disappointed that we trekked all the way from Penn only to find Cucina to be closed. I wish they were a bit more consistent with their schedule. All in all, Cucina Zapata is a safe bet for an affordable and delicious meal. I'm a huge fan!

Beautiful restaurant, lots of sparkle, good food, and wonderful service. Our waiter made several trips back to the kitchen to make sure the food we ordered was lemon free (allergies) and he came back every time with a smile on his face.

One of my favorite Jamaican spots here in Philly. Their Pepper steak is to DIE for! I love coming here because it's not only affordable but they bless your platter with plenty of food. I can say at time the steak can be though but usually it's perfect. Their cabbage is very flavorful and fresh. I love their Mac and cheese and their rice and beans are amazing. They add to your experience with amazing customer service as well. It's definitely worth it ! Now since it's a hot spot there can be a wait but it's WORTH IT! So don't let that stop you.

I've been to the restaurant a couple times but just got delivery with skip the dishes (spend 20 and free delivery- wahoo!) and was pleasantly reminded that their food is the bomb. How do they make the fried rice taste so good? Also, they put in a very decent amount of meat in their vermicelli and rice dishes and it's the good stuff too! Only giving 4 stars because I wasn't super in love with their salad rolls but they were still pretty yummy. Gonna have to sit on my hands so I don't spend my money ordering this in every night cause dang.

The Pearl-ein ansprechendes Restaurant in Treasure Island. Zählt zu den hochpreisigen seiner Klasse. Für Heiligabend wollten wir uns das gönnen. Zumal nicht überall geöffnet war. Die Reservierung war auch gut, ohne hätte es wohl kaum einen freien Tisch gegeben. Atmosphäre: 4 Essen:3 Freundlichkeit: 4 Die Vorspeise war ok. 3,5* Die Hauptspeise, die Linguine mit Gemüse, Aufpreis für Shrimps, vollkommen übergart. Bei einem Preis von 36$ nicht akzeptabel. 1* Auf Nachfrage reklamierte ich das und auch die Linguine mit Lobster meines Mannes waren nicht wirklich al dente. Es wurde Nachbesserung angeboten, die ich ablehnte aufgrund des mangelden Zeitfensters. Mein vllt zu 1/4 geleerten Teller wurde dann u.a. auch abgeräumt und bei der "Saalchefin" vorgezeigt. Auf der nachfolgenden Rechnung war mein Gericht dann gestrichen worden. Danke dafür! Hungrig in die heilige Nacht dank der Vorspeise blieb mir dann doch erspart ;-)) FAZIT: überbewertet!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: They make their own paneer! And it's really good! I'm still stuffed full and have been thinking about the paneer since I left the restaurant two hours ago. Little expensive, but my comparison is cheap veggie Indian places in Vancouver, a maybe this is the norm here. The dishes were slow to come out but we were forewarned that it'd be made from scratch. Totally fine. Pleasant atmosphere. Tasty roti, naan was soooo buttery and delicious. Really nice to see vegan food identified on the menu as well as local goat meat. We had the halibut which was really tasty, I'd never had dish curry before. Staff were super pleasant, welcoming and friendly.

I love this place more than I can probably express in a short review. I came here for my birthday dinner with a group of 6 people, and my friends still talk about it as an amazing place. The owner was also very gracious about allowing us to BYO, although technically it is NOT, which was a nice gesture. As for the food, it is very much a family-style, all of us dig-in, type of place. While great for my crowd of friends, I can see other people not really loving that vibe, so keep that in mind when you are making reservations. Also, I would keep in mind the size of your group-the restaurant seems pretty tiny (unless there is another room they are hiding?) and the portions don't seem to increase any whether you have 2 people or 6 people as we saw a couple sitting near us. As for the "event, not a meal at a restaurant" other people have said, I think that's pretty unfair. The food was delicious, so it did feel like a meal at a restaurant to me.

food was bland, outdated, and expensive. this is not an innovative restaurant. octopus was chewy, rubbery, tasteless, and lacked any grilled flavor. we had the blue fish which was like a greasy fishy stew. everything was just pretty awful. sad we wasted our money there. definitely do not recommend to anyone.
I've been by three times and have a a great experience everytime. Friendly staff and great food at good price .
SOOOO GOOD!!! This place is proof aliens are real! No human could make such good food!!!! I.really wish I was talking this up, but I'm really not!
One of my favorites. Thai tea & beef meatball soup is my go to! Recently beef has been a bit more fat on meat. Otherwise delicious! Staff is EXCELLENT!

I wish we had a Pita Jungle in NYC. This is a casual spot with some great Americanized Mediterranean food. I ordered the quinoa salad with the cilantro hummus. The cilantro hummus was great - I wish I could have taken some home. I sat at a table outside and did some work for a few hours and was not bothered at all. I'll definitely be back if I am in the area.

If you like Ethiopian then you will love this place. Great injera and super fresh food. They use super fresh, higher priced ingredients so they must charge a little more. Ethiopian is nothing like Indian food so do not expect it to taste like it- aside from them using lentils and greens in many dishes.
I dine at The Hummingbird at least twice a month for lunch usually on Fridays. Everything I have tried has set the bar high especially the Ox Tail. I think I cant wait for Friday I'm going today.
Delicious food and generous portions!! Definitely authentic and worth the trip out of the French quarter!
Pho Voorhees has the best pho in the area. They have great service and the restaurant is very clean. My family enjoyed the food and since it is close to our house we will be coming here often.

Pretty darn good. Nice, quaint dining establishment. The lamb ribs were phenomenal, but I would not recommend eating it all by yourself. It is a rich dish that was too heavy for me to eat by myself. My friend enjoyed the sheepshead dish. Just a heads up that many of the dishes have shrimp or seafood components, so if you are allergic this may not be the best place to go. It would be best to go with a group of 4 or larger so that you can do family style. I will be back to try some of the other dishes. The chicken looked delicious.
My oldest son loves this place. His favorite is the wings. Not bad, I love their yuca fries.
Raw Oysters,good beer and beautiful sunsets. It makes their little beach park a worthy destination. I liked the Cuban pork quite a bit, but the Mahi Mahi tacos were a little disappointing.
Great people. Great food. Love this place. It's very authentic. I tried lots of meals there and were all tasty and lots of flavor.

Only tried one other Pho place in the city that was all but forgettable so i am thrilled to have stumbled upon Lillys Cafe! Its a cute little place with bright colors on the walls and smiles on the faces of the staff. The staff is attentive and friendly. The seating is well spaced and uncrowded. It wasn't furnished with comfort prioritized but its not a lingering sort of place to begin with. It is clean and quiet as well. Menu is concise. All of what you would expect and some great vege and vegan options. I went with the summer roll and spicy shrimp pho. The summer roles were nice and light. A touch heavy on mint but refreshing. The peanut sauce was just a soupy peanut butter. It served a purpose and with a little Sriracha was fine. The pho was nice. Just enough heat, plenty of shrimp which were most likely frozen but at least plentiful. A lot of salt though, in fact my mouth was noticeably dry from it. The portion is enormous and it is priced well considering it is easily two meals. Overall i enjoyed it. It is quick, well priced and the environment is great. Ill be back and they do takeout as well which i can definitely see taking advantage of.

Went here for dinner last night upon a recommendation from a friend! It was just lovely!!! Everything full of flavor and perfect amount of heat! Ordered: shrimp/pork shu mai -I am Cantonese so I can be really picky about my beloved dumplings. These were on point!!!! Egg rolls: crispy delicious filled with glass noodles and dipped in a sweet and sour sauce! Super yum! I had spicy noodle with chicken... perfect blend of spice and fresh veggies I ate the whole plate! Partner had the prik khing with chicken. He ate the whole thing and said it was full of flavor... Friend had the basil garlic with shrimp and gave me some shrimp to eat too. Spicy yummy and all super fresh! Best Thai I've had in a long time... Highly recommend The restaurant is quaint and decor is funky eclectic and would be great to bring a date! I found it to be quiet and romantic.
The food wasn't very good. I have no idea why there's currently 4.5 stars. The wings were the best but not great. The Greek food was way below average. Yelp rarely lets me down but it did this time.

Meh is right. I've been here a few times because I work nearby and I've never been blown out of the water by it. Their springs rolls are ok, a bit small and not cost comparable to other Vietnamese restaurants. In fact, all of their entrees are smaller portions...not that this is necessarily a bad thing but I'm just used to take home portions with most of the Asian cuisine around town. The prices are higher too. I was charged $20 for an order of egg rolls and one of their specials. That's crazy. I've had the Lemongrass Chicken Bun and it comes with a wide assortment of veggies...more than just the cucumber and carrots you may expect. That was nice but again, the portions are small and higher priced than their competitors. The Mom's Country Fried Beef is good, too but sometimes there is too much pepper in the rice. I dine here because it is convenient for pick up orders (or if my boss is paying!) but if I have more time to spare I'll go to Viet Orleans down Baronne.

The pork belly steamed buns are amazing, best I've had. The pho, bahn mi, and fresh rolls are good too. I love all the use of fresh herbs. Decent beer selection. The prices are fair and the service is alright. It's definitely my favorite lunch spot on Freret St., just wish they were open on Mondays!

I went to Aroma for the first time today to check out their lunch special and I was very pleasantly surprised. For about $9, you get to choose 2 entrees from a list, rice, and a basket of naan. I had the chicken tikka masala and the chicken curry. The chicken tikka masala was some of the best I've ever had and the chicken curry was just the right amount of spicy. The staff was friendly and attentive. I'm so glad to have aroma in town and I can't wait to try everything else they have!

Ate here for the first time for dinner, and loved it! Papadum, Veg Samosas, Aloo Mattar, Chicken Makhani, and Naan split for two...everything was delicious and so much food! Great service, great price, will be back for sure when I'm in the area.

This place already has way too many reviews saying how wonderful it is, but here's one more. I've been here twice -- the first time Hassan made all the yummy chaats for my group and let us sample various lassis. He was very personable and asked us for feedback on our chaats as well. The second time I came here, someone else made my chaat. It wasn't as good as when Hassan made it but still great nonetheless. Make sure you get a lassi! They have the best mango lassis I've ever had in my life, made with fresh mango. It's pretty small and quiet, which is great for enjoying yummy food with a few friends.

Absolutely great restaurant. The people the ambience the food all great. For sure a 5 star for value, service and ambience. The only reason I gave it a 4 star was the bread. Maybe a bit harsh to do but a 5 star restaurant had to has the basics at a 5 star level- bread and coffee. Didn't have coffee but had the bread. Martini was fabulous- halibut was wonderful and the butter lettuce salad was delicious. Will come back and highly recommend.

I went in to try the new shop, and I was blown away by the food. The pita was soft and had the right texture, and the garlic sauce and chicken were seasoned perfectly. You definitely need to try this new business. The employees were very patient and kind to me.

This place was actually magical for us. The staff were sweet, knowledgeable, and made our first visit very special! The ambiance was magnificent, the food was wonderful, and we will be back every time we are in Carpenteria.

This place is awesome! Food is delicious and tastes really fresh. I order to-go here regularly and dined in recently, the quality is always great and I've yet to be disappointed. My favorite is the Gyros Plate. Just writing this review makes me hungry! And don't forget to check out the store while you're there... lots of select foods, fresh veggies and hookah supplies.

Nadia Thai is a quaint little BYOB located in the borough of Lansdale. Not being open for very long that have shown there knowledge and passion for Thai cuisine. With and extensive and unique menu Nadia shares heaping portions of authentic Thai food. You get more then you pay for. The restaurant is located right off the Lansdale train stop in the cutest spot of Lansdale. Would make a great date night especially in the summer with the water globe on the other side of the tracks.

I have been here twice and were quite disappointed by the inconsistency in quality. The first time everything was great. We ordered grilled chicken, lamb, and shrimp. The last one is exceptionally well done so I ordered it the second time I was there. But it turned out to be burnt and a little too salty for my taste. Besides this, I love the atmosphere and the price is very reasonable. Will give it another try.
Had the pan fried dumplings and the cashew chicken. Very tasty! Been here a couple times and will continue to go back. Friendly staff and clean environment.

Awesome!!This was my boyfriend and my first time. We asked alot of questions. And still our waiter was awesome. Ohh!And he was training by the way.and still rocked. We had pork belly sliders,crab cake platter,mussels. Omg etc. I cant wait to go back. 7-5-16 awesome day

Great experience. I think we have found a new favorite place. Loved the vegetarian sampler and the coffee ceremony was a sweet surprise. Very nice place. Great service too. They also brought out spices for us to add some heat to the meal. We like it extra spicy. We hope to visit again soon.
The BEST Greek Food in Nashville !! Love everything here! Great food , prices and service with a smile!!! You have to have the Hummus and homemade fried pita chips !!

Don't bother coming here for happy hour. It doesn't exist. We had read a NOLA.com article raving about their happy hour. However, when we asked about the small plates served at happy hour, we got glared at as if we had 3 heads. "Um, the kitchen only serves dinner...and it doesn't open for an hour...do you have a reservation??...and could you speak up because I can't read your lips because of the glare from the windws?" You get the picture. Rude bartender, rude hostess, rude atmosphere. Tip: be nicer to locals...we tip better, can be regulars when otherwise the tumbleweeds are rolling in your bar, and we can spread a good or bad word very fast.

Zoës is absolutely, by far, the best Mediterranean/Greek food I've experienced. It's slightly expensive for my taste, but it's worth it. The kebabs, salads, cucumber, vegetables, and basically everything on the menu is AMAZING. I would come here every day If I could afford it. The atmosphere is what makes Zoës so unique and interesting. It's a modern, fun, exciting twist on Mediterranean/Greek food. The colors are bright, fun, and contemporary. I would 100% recommend. PS: The shrimp kabobs are a little spicy, but still great.

Can't beat their $10 lunch special. Great selection of curries and noodle dishes, with a delicious soup and spring rolls to start. Fast and friendly service. Only downer is both times I've ordered coconut rice I've been served plain rice.

Lilly's Cafe is absolutely amazing! If you've never tried Vietnamese food I would highly suggest Lilly's to be your starting point. Everything is fresh and full of flavor! The wait isn't that long unless you go during peak hours. My go-to dish is the Chicken Vermicelli with an egg roll.
Came for the tom ka, but the phad se ew was incredible. Can't go wrong with the tom ka though. Actually has galangal unlike most places I've found. I'm going as far to say the best in tampa!

this sushi place is truly my favorite that i have tried! i am extremely picky with sushi and they always accommodate to the sushi i want! they are always friendly and have great service! my favorite roll is the salmon lover and i add spicy tuna in it as well so yummy!!!!

I am very hesitant to write poor reviews but I do not think I will be coming back. Although I thought I would like the "Asian fusion" idea of this restaurant. It seems to be poorly executing the cultural appreciation of different ethnic foods and generalizing to culture appropriation. If this is your first time having Vietnamese, Thai, or Japanese food please do not judge these different cultural food based off this restaurant's adaptation. I got their Thai Chicken Coconut Curry and Lychee cocktail. The chicken was dry and had mediocre flavoring and same goes for the curry. My previous experience with Thai Curry usually runs thicker, here, it was watery. The price was more than $10, which is ridiculous. I guess I was paying for their American adaption. My friend got the Ramen and was upset that the flavors doesn't run deep either. However, best thing about my experience here was the Lychee Cocktail, it definitely tasted like fresh lychee juice with a kick.

Don't let the unassuming strip mall fool you. This is HANDS DOWN the best Thai food (I have tried them all) place in Indianapolis. Did I mention they deliver? Thai chili sauce is made in house at this mom and pop. Amazing Pad Thai and veggie spring rolls.

I dont wanna be mean but theres a lot of hipsters if you know what I mean by that..... doctorate degree in arts those types of people.... and that's a fact! Always If you go to south philly around Washington square, you'll find alot kite asians with way more better pho at a good price. When you first walk in you are greeted by a waiter and you are given water and menu. I ordered the goi cuon as my app. It was like your normal tasting goi cuon. For my pho, I ordered pho dac biet. The wait time was about 20 minutes because there was only one guy working in the back so I felt empathy for the guy and I didn't want to bother the waiter. When the pho came out, it looked good. The key thing for a pho is the broth. You can have waygu beef but if the broth is not good then be ready to file for bankruptcy lol. This place broth didn't have that sweet broth to it. Kinda tasted watery. The meat was actually very good but again, the broth has to be good. The prices for these bowls is not what you'll find at a normal pho place. Price for large is $11 and the bowl is not big. With more hipsters moving into fairmount ruining pho, expect overpriced, tasteless broth, good meat, and tiny bowls. Service here is actually better than other pho restaurants which is pretty rare in philly for pho. Overall rating: 3/5. Could've went to 2 but service and the meat saved it.

We ordered the lamb hummus and it was absolutely delicious!! The pitas that come with them are pretty small but super soft. I would recommend 1 pita per 2 people. I ordered the Arais (lamb sandwich), which was to die for. It was so flavorful with every bite! The inside was super trendy and hipster. I loved the decoration. There's plenty of indoor and outdoor space. I would recommend calling a reservation if you can. I believe reservations can only be made with 6+ parties. The server was very attentive and checked on us often. We had a member of our table who is very allergic to nuts and reiterated this to the server on multiple occasions. Despite checking if the meal contained nuts, the meal still came with them! Eek.

Years ago this place was much different.. now you have all this bone in your platter, and the prices are ridiculous. I can definitely agree with people about the service... its terrible. The people roll their eyes, and don't hide at all they're anger that you even exist. I just go once in a extremely blue moon for take out bc they're curry isn't super spicy like some places.. the quality isn't as good as it used to be though. I'd say, save your money for elsewhere on South st. Oh and the bathroom is around the block... how ridiculous! That should be illegal for a restaurant. I wash my hands before I eat, and i have to travel around the block and reenter the restaurant, by that time I'm contaminated again!!!

I cannot get enough of this place. I first stopped by after an evening downtown of bar hopping and specifically told the guy behind the counter "this is my first time, give me something amazingly awesome." What he gave me was the most mouth-watering, alcohol soaking, tasty looking, and tasty tasting piece of god-liness that can only be compared to sitting on a cloud and eating with angels. It was ::cue heavenly music and light from above:: The Dooner Box. HOLY CRAP it was good. It was shaved lamb and chicken...on a bed of fries and smothered with tzaziki and hot sauce. This thing was monstorously sized for about $8. A+ for the staff member who knew what to do in my fragile state. Alas, I couldn't give Dooners a review after that because I wasn't fully in my right mind. So, I went back BEFORE bar hopping and got the Dooner Box again and ya know what? Everything I said above stands. Bravo! Lastly, after my two fantastic adventures, I took some friends back for the Burek (which they get delivered from http://www.yelp.com/biz/european-bakery-and-grocery-pinellas-park) and where I've normally gotten it from, but it was still very very good. And I like that you can order it in halves. Sidenote: for the first time I had my Burek w/ tzaziki and sriracha sauce and it they were blissful additions (usually I just eat it as-is). So yes, I recommend this place and looking forward to destroying their menu one-by-one.

Thai fried rice is good and Gen Tso's chicken is ok. Hot and sour soups are nothing like the Chinese version. It's definitely an acquired taste. Food is expertly prepared and looks great on square plates.

OMG this tastes just like food made at home (Puerto Rico) and it's fairly cheap. They even had mofongo and their flan is delicious. I'll definitely be coming here more often. We had their pernil which was okay and the bistec was really good!

Please visit...If you have never had Ethiopian food before, do yourself a favor and get here quickly.The owners are very cordial and will make sure that you enjoy your meal, Ethiopian dining is a very intimate experience, your food is served without utensils, you use traditional injera (bread) to scoop the food which is served in little piles on an injera. The vegetarian entrees are plentiful and the vegetarian sambussas are amazing, filled with lentils and spices, then deep fried in somehing similar to a wonton wrapper. Try the vegetarian platter which has a multitude of dishes to sample, including lentils, chickpeas, potatoes, cabbage and green beans. You will be happy that you have stepped out of the norm, make sure you have a coffee or tea at the end of your meal. YUMMY :-)

Food is always great and people know it. Ive made it a habit of ordering to go. It seems like the employees are always on their cell phones speaking very loudly. When there isn't anyone to help, they like to come out to the dining tables and sit there to have their noisy conversation. Makes for an interesting lunch. 2-28-16 I am changing my review to five stars. I own a business in the area and am ALWAYS going in here for a good lunch. They have cut back on the cell phone usage and have honestly never had a bad meal come out of the kitchen. I'd die just a little bit if this place ever went away. #16 with spring rolls, you won't be disappointed.

Two words to sum up my Delicia experience: On Point. I absolutely love the dimly lit atmosphere with exposed brick and high beams. We didn't have any cocktails this time around, although they all looked amazing. Next time I'll definitely be trying the Fire & Ice. We started out with the guacamole appetizer and although the guac itself had a great fresh flavor, the portion size was slightly lacking. I had the duck enchiladas and I honestly can't wait to have them again. The portion size was very filling and the taste was incredible. Bravo Delicia!

I have only been there for their lunch buffet, and it's excellent. There's a pretty wide variety and the food is of fairly high quality. My favorite is the lamb curry, which is chopped up lamb with bones in a savory sauce that's excellent with the rice or the naan (garlic, of course). For about $9, it's a very good deal. My only issue is that none of the dishes are really spicy. That's not atypical in the midwest, but it would be nice if there were some spicy dishes. Quite a few of the patrons appear to be ethnic Indians, which says to me the food has not been Americanized too much.

First of all, I'm the type of guy that will only give 5 stars when I have a dining experience that absolutely blows me away. 4 stars would be considered top notch. I"m giving 3 stars because the food was very good, but our server was terrible and really was the reason my experience was filled with frustration. I really like how this is a strip mall joint. Good ones are usually 'hidden secrets'. Nothing ruins a good restaurant quicker than popularity. I know it's counter intuitive, but as Yogi Berra said "nobody goes there anymore, it's too crowded". Well, we arrived at 7 on a Wednesday night and the place was packed. We were, ehem, pointed towards a table (I would say 'seated', but the employees were too busy to actually greet us and show us to the table) after about 15 minutes. I really love the atmosphere. I'd call it "Traditional Indian kitsch" with its Taj Majal architectural flourishes and the paint-by-number Indian artwork. The last time we dined there, which was a few years ago, I loved how it seemed to be run by an Indian family with the grade-school kids sitting quietly doing their homework, and a turban wearing grandfather manning the door. This time, however, it seemed like the crew from Los Betos took over, and our particular waitress had no clue how to provide table service. We were not greeted once we sat down. Several minutes later a charmless lady approached us and asked if we were ready to order. After going around the table taking our entrees, I had to point out that we would also like to order some drinks. The food came out pretty quickly, and then the beers, and I had to ask twice for the white rice that was supposed to accompany our dishes. Not surprised that she messed up our order, but in a way that worked out to our advantage. She brought a random extra dish that we didn't order, but was delightful nonetheless. We were not checked on again until about 10 minutes after we were all finished, with napkins on our plates. When you go out to eat it's not all about the food. You are paying for the experience and bad service can be like a little too much salt in the curry. In this case, again, the flavors were great, but the service left me frustrated. She was lucky to get 15%.

I typically don't like yogurt or smoothies, but I really, REALLY enjoyed the Melon lassi here. The taste isn't in-your-face strong which is what I usually don't like about smoothies. I also tried the mango and honeydew and enjoyed those as well. UPDATE: RED WATERMELON IS MY FAVORITE. =D Owner will make you a new lassi if yours isn't great, but I've never had a sub-par lassi. I also prefer mine more icy, and he satisfies this preference.

Amazing! My wife and I are visiting from Nashville. This has the feel of an upscale restaurant, but the prices are so reasonable! You can really tell that they care about the food and ingredients. We got the hummus, and it was so perfect. Service was really great too! So friendly! I would give 10 stars if I could!

The 4.5 star rating this place has somehow managed to garner is not legitimate. Nothing about this place is a 4 star establishment from the sticky mess on the tables, to the inconsistent food and awful service. If you go in here expecting a good meal you're going to be disappointed. Don't bother ordering takeout, it comes on time but it's not good.

This place gets a five from my husband and a four from me. I am going with his rating because he loves Thai/asian food, and I just like it, so I am not the best judge. The interior of the restaurant is really beautiful. I loved the intricately carved wood artwork. I sat down and felt transported to a different world! I am not familiar with Thai food so I ordered a basic Tilapia dish. It was phenomenal! He had a curry dish and he thought it was delicious. We also shared dumplings and they were so good!! We are definitely going here again. And best yet....it's a BYOB! I am looking forward to returning and trying something more adventurous!
This place is on right off bourbon and I've been here sober 3 times and counting. That should be all you need to know. Great gyros.
My experience eat here was great fresh ingredients and services was great on slow days or rush hours time
Fantastic. Best Indian buffet I have been to. Must try the lunch buffet. Fresh and flavorful. The staff is also lovely.

We checked out Momo's last night for the first time as we're new to the neighborhood. It's nice to have a Mediterranean place within walking distance but the food here is just okay for the price you pay. Service was friendly but very busy - they could use several more staff members especially for the outside area. My husband's gyro was "okay" but my falafel and spiced hummus were very tasty. We will most likely be back but will be exploring other places first.

I was craving Ethiopian food. This being the only place in town, of course I ended up at Queen of Sheba for its lunch buffet. Overall, the taste of the dishes was pretty good. My injera was served cold, which was not optimal. The stewed cabbage and carrots was tasty, as were the lentils. The chicken breast in spices was quite tender and good, as were most of the stews I tried. I felt that the beef with gomen (bitter greens) was a bit too bitter for my taste. Overall, Queen of Sheba helped satisfy my cravings, but it lacked the soul that I have found at restaurants in little Ethiopia in Los Angeles or at little places in Oakland and Berkeley. I was a little disappointed that they had no Diet Coke.

I visited this restaurant on a Sunday after church for brunch last min reservations , it was awesome I luv this place Excellent service and delicious food our waiter Corey was awesome! We will be back
We have been eating here for years and the food has always been great. They will customize the spice for you and usually make substitutions as requested. It is one of our favorite places to eat.

Just had lunch here with my son and his girlfriend and it is outstanding. Super clean restaurant and nice decor. I had the walnut shrimp and absolutely loved it. Orange chicken gets 5 stars also, along with the Pho!! What a delightful surprise!!!

Another Beech grove hidden jewel. As many times I have been by this place I only wish I had tried it earlier. Very clean, and the food was hot and so flavorful. If only the crab ragoon had more crab in them. Egg rolls were great, portions well worth the money! Put this on you must try list!

After the change in ownership, I'm happy to report that this place tastes more authentic, fresh and amazing. The new owner takes the extra mile to serve only fresh food. My wife and I always start with bolani (flatbread) and/or sambosa, which is kind of like an empanada but with Middle-eastern spices. The tekka lamb kebabs are the highlight, tender and perfectly seasoned. The shami kebobs are legit. Chicken kebobs are surprisingly tender and flavorful. The rice is just the perfect compliment and the green dipping sauce is something I am always scraping to get every last drip of at the end of each meal. It reminds me of good Argentinian chimichurri. The baklava is also balanced and perfect here as they're topped with the crumbled pistachio. One of my favorite places to dine out in Boise. It's a travesty that this place is quiet.
I'm sad to say we tried to go tonight & this gem has closed down. Hopefully they'll spring up again somewhere else!
One of my favorite places to get take out! The portions are always very good size and you don't have to sacrifice the quality and the taste of the food, to have it at home:)

Great place! Good food!! Very eclectic menu. The staff is very friendly and efficient. We went there for lunch today. A group of 16. The orders were taken very systematically and that attention to detail meant everything arrived exactly as ordered. We also thought we would wait sometime to be served due to the large size of the group. That was not the case. We were pleasantly surprised to be served in just about 15-20 minutes. Thank you Blue plate of Mullica Hill, NJ!!!! I hope to return again someday soon!!!!

A group of friends from work had a taste for vietnamese. Our normal go to is Bai Chi but they were closed so we decided to give Mint a shot. I ordered the pork belly bacos and the grilled shrimp rice dish with a fried egg. Everything was really good. The food tasted fresh and light. The only reason they didnt recieve 5 stars is bc service was slow for some reason..we were a bit late getting back to work. They r worth a return visit tho.

This review is just for Tiffin Etc. 1/2 Star for food: This place had ( yes I said it had) the best Kati Rolls. Loved the variety of rolls, with lot of chicken/lamb ...just under 6.50$. Amazing!!! Later they started reducing the size of the roll and the meat! Pizza is so so average. Don't ever order Pizza for delivery, you will get it cold!! I'm not kidding...read other reviews too. 1/2 Star for In Restaurant Service: Service is avg and most of the time it would take 30 mins to bring in the Appetizers, 30 More mins to bring in Main course . 1/2 star for Staff : Not very courteous. 1/2 Star for Amebiance 0 Star for delivery or take out : Never.. never... the order food for pick up or delivery!! You go there and have to wait for 15 -20 mins. If you prefer delivery ...you select the delivery time. But the food will there only 20-30 after that time. They fail hands down in this category
Hands down the best Greek restaurant in Philly. We love this place. Sea bass, grilled vegetables, olive oil w pita, not too noisy and not over crowded. Best neighborhood spot around!

It is really difficult to find a veggie pho that has a flavorful broth but at Lilly's they really nail it every time. Lilly's is hands down THE best and freshest Pho in New Orleans. Flavorful, satiating and the owner's are beautiful people that make spending your money there even more enjoyable! Once you try Lilly's you won't go anywhere else.

OMG, the charcoal chicken pita sandwich was magical! It has chicken, lettuce, onion, tziki sauce & fries inside. I omitted the tomato. So delish! My guy had the charcoal chicken platter with potato, vegetables & rice. He ate it all! Thank you Zorba's for a magical meal in Philly! They were so nice that after complementing the meal the chef sent out a free custard, phyllo honey dessert who's name I can't remember. Everyone's so nice in Philly!

Really great food. This place always draws me in just by smell. Long line around lunch so be prepared for that if you don't have a lot of time. If you are looking for a standard falafel then go down the street to Mama's but if you are looking for falafel or shish dressed up and with a few amazing twists than it is completely worth it. The portion is HUMONGOUS and always filled with fresh veggies. Great food, great guy.

The chai lattes are by far the best in the city, perfect every time. Your quintessential hipster hangout, Remedy is definitely geared towards university students and local cool kids. I took away one star because this location always has their (often terrible) music turned up much too loud for a coffee shop, and the baristas are a bit standoffish. I just bring my noise cancelling earphones and smile as big as I can at the grumpy baristas! Still worth it.

Well, we have been waiting an hour and forty minutes for a simple sushi roll and general tso's. When we call, they rudely say that it's "busy" and that the driver is on the way (for 40 minutes). Also, the food was very mediocre the last time we tried them. Won't be making this mistake again!

We visited this place while touring the city of Philly. To our surprise this place is mind blowing. The mango lassi is out of the world. Its the best mango lassi I have ever had. Over 70 lassi flavors on the menu. With around 70 more in the making. I would definitely recommend this place!!

My wife and I live in Tower Grove and have been very excited to try Olio ever since they opened. I drive past them every day on the way to work and it's refreshing to see that people are taking action to fix up what has historically been a blighted neighborhood. Unfortunately, my wife and I had a very disappointing experience there today. We arrived early this afternoon and were seated on the back patio, which was great because it was a beautiful day! We each ordered a drink from the first server who visited us. While we waited for our drinks, two additional servers visited us but we politely informed them that we had already been helped. After waiting for approximately 30 minutes and speaking with 3 servers, our drinks had not arrived so we left disappointed. We both sincerely enjoy the fact that we can walk and ride our bikes to fantastic eateries, bars, and other businesses. I had high hopes for Olio, but will not be back for a while (if ever).
Saturday night was our first time there. The food was great along with the sevice and cozy atmosphere.

This is our favorite Greek restaurant in St. Louis. We usually just get gyros and/or chicken gyros, but we also love their hummus and pita. I have also had them cater for me once, and we even loved the leftovers. The only complaint I have is their hours. We would go more often if they were open during standard dinner hours.
Ate there a while ago, can't remember what I got but it was something vegetarian and delicious!

This place used to be five star. The waitstaff is attentive. The ambiance is great, pretty decor, authentic cuisine. However, in the last few months, the food has changed so i'm wondering if there is a new chef? The food is entirely too salty.
Amazing food. Clean. Great staff and just impressive food. The foid is well priced and just tastes amazing. We eat here often and are so excited that they expanded.

Very good food and very good service. My wife and I randomly decided to stop in here and we are so glad we did. The Sag Paneer was amazing. Same with the chicken tikka masala and paal appam. Seriously. So good. Try this place if you want amazing Indian food with very reasonable pricing and great service. Thanks to India Sizzling 2 for making our dinner portion of date night a success!!!! Update: We have been here many times since I last posted. Every. Single. Time. The food is amazing and so flavorful. We love date night here. Tonight was Dosa night, which was really good. But the buffet is still my favorite. I HIGHLY suggest this place to my friends and family. So. Dang. Good.

Their drunken noodles are incredible. The menu is humble yet filed with exceptional Thai classics. The servers have always been very nice and welcoming. Erawan appeals to dinning alone, couples, and large groups. I've never left unhappy! I strongly recommend this establishment. Plus, you can't beat a nice BYO place...amIright? Solid spot, keep up the great work Erawan!!!!!!

A great find in this culinary desert! We haven't been impressed with restaurants in this area, but we like Thai Place. We've come here a few times, so its easy for me to give 5 stars. You can tell Thai Place pays attention to the details. The decor, general presentation of food, and the fact the thai iced tea comes with a straw wrapper twisted into a cute origami :) Also, the staff are friendly, and the prices are reasonable, especially for the quality of food. The one concern I have about Thai food in general is the grease level. But the food at Thai Place has consistently been not greasy, even the fried foods, and quite flavorful. The last time we came here, we had fried taro root, vegetarian pad thai, and vegetarian green curry. I'd recommend all those dishes. The vegetarian pad thai was delicious. The vegetarian green curry was a bit spicy, but it came with a chock full of vegetables and tofu.
Being from Arizona, I guess I am not use to restaurants charging for chips and salsa. This place does. We didn't enjoy our tacos and thought that they were too expensive.

Such a humble location. Yet such delicious food, excellent service, and an atmosphere that just permeates you with a feeling that takes you away from the shopping center through which you entered the restaurant. I have yet to eat from the dinner menu. But the soup danced in my mouth. The meats were well cooked and well seasoned. And the vegetables were delicious. And to top it off they served Thai iced tea.
