Like I said, I expected it to be soaked in honey, but it was just the right amount and none of it stuck to my teeth. The fillo pastry was airy and the filling was the perfect amount and not too strong. The sausages were so moist and aromatic. I'm also not a big fan of beets, but it was done well. I didn't feel like I wanted to spit it out. I also got to taste the Papia (duck leg) - very juicy and tender too with a crunchy skin. Arni (lamb) - medium actually means med rare, which was perfectly done to me. It wasn't gamey. Katsaki (braised goat) - very soft. The meat practically falls apart when you pick it up with a fork and filled with delicious flavors. I keep reading about the brunch, so I will definitely be back!!!
The best place for pho and banh mi in Boise. Fresh and delicious.

A solid 3 if 3 is meh. The chicken gyro sandwich was flavorless. Typically gyro meat (chicken or traditional) is cooked on a vertical rotisserie and carved off in thin slices. This had giant chunks of chicken meat which made for a different experience as the chicken to sauce/ingredient ratio was off, disturbingly so. They cut the top off the pita and stuffed it inside giving the impression of abundance. The lettuce and vegetables went in first with the meat on top. So after those first few bites you're left with just meh lettuce and veggies. They taziki was even flavorless...and I don't know how you accomplish that given the ingredients therein. The decor is rustic but nice for a fast-casual.
Very good food. Great environment. Took a bit of time to eat but worth the wait. Can't wait to go back.

My wife and I went to Zeppoli for our Anniversary on 9/13/14 and we were anxious to go because of all the great reviews. To say the least, we were not disappointed the food and wait staff were excellent! The bread and olive oil sent out before the meal was delicious. We had the Pesto Trapanese (Sicilian style fusilli pasta with almond-pistachio pesto) for an appetizer and it was great we both enjoyed it very much. For entrees my wife had Rigatoni alla Disgraziata (Mezze rigatoni with eggplant, tomato, ricotta salata and basil-breadcrumbs) which was fantastic. I had the Bistecca Enna (Marinated rib-eye steak served with arugula and tomato salad ) which was unbelievable and probably the best steak I have ever had. To finish we ordered the Cannoli Classico for dessert and it was a great finish to a fantastic experience. Lastly, a lot of reviews about the small dining area and noise level being moderate are correct, however, it didn't in any way take away from the incredible food experience and professional, friendly staff. Zeppoli was easily one of the best restaurants we have ever eaten at and will definitely be returning.

Earlier I wrote:I loved my heaping portion of pulled pork, my beans and rice, my sweet plantains and guava cake. My gang let me taste their Cuban sammich, chicken and potaters. We were also with a vegetarian in tow who opted for an egg sammich and loved it as well. Luckily we speak Spanglish, but if we didn't, I don't believe I'd have trouble ordering, since a lot of the food was sitting behind a buffet-type window for easy point and grunt ordering if need be. The guava cake was outstanding and fresh. The steak Sancocho peasant soup looked great, but with prices these low and portions so huge I had to take it easy. Well, I did go back, and it seems they did make some price amendments. Three Cuban sandwiches of some sort were listed all at three different prices. One was at 4.00, another at 4.99, and I was charged 5.00. I did utilize the pint and grunt method, although I fully understood when the front desk girl asked the chef for the price and she threw up five fingers. Still a good experience!

The only thing I don't like about Lilly's Cafe is that they aren't open on Sundays, which is when I am most craving pho to take care of my two day hangover. The Lilly rolls are the best spring rolls I have ever had because the strawberries are so unexpected. I always get the vegan pho. Best broth on the east bank, hands down!

Just re-discovered this place after forgetting about it for many years. Food has been consistently excellent: spinach pie, shrimp pil pil, bluefish, octopus, grilled squid, etc. Unadulterated classic clean flavors. Only reason I give 4 and not 5 is that these guys could invest in some infrastructure like cutlery that does not easily bend, glasses that aren't chipped, chairs that don't feel like they will wobble and give way any moment. All that said, great place to people watch, may be too loud to actually talk to your companions. Don't worry, the deliciousness will offer enough to amuse you.

Will not eat here again. Gave it a third try, as our good friend keeps talking it up, but each time our experience was worse. The people that run it are probably very nice, hardworking people, but the staff is so poorly trained that it is almost comical. Especially if you are sitting at the outside tables. They forget about you entirely! They bring the food and forget the silverware. Bring water glasses, forget to fill them. Forget items on the order/then charge for something you didn't order. We keep coming back because we want to believe this was just bad luck, with "new" staff, or something, but each time the experience grew more absurd. Had a couple of "OK" dishes (a pretty good red curry) and coffee was pretty good (after reminding 3, count 'em, 3 times to bring it!) but it too pricey compared to better Thai a mile away. I ordered a red curry duck the last time and it was the worst duck (dry, stringy, no flavor) I have ever eaten- and it was pricier than the other options. I don't usually like making a fuss or complaining at restaurants, because that just adds to the stress of it all, but I just won't be spending any more money there.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Loved eggplant curry . And great costumer service . I Will definitely like to go again.
Amazing masala dosa, lamb curry and garlic naan! Really enjoyed everything we tried.
Best south indian food in the east coast, better than that i found in edison and even in INDIA!!!!!! If u are indian, and u want good indian food, this is the place to go, PERIOD!!!!!!!!
Friendly staff, amazing food, amazing prices. Yucca done perfectly, soft and sweet plantains, delicious pepper grilled chicken... Everything is decadent. I could live off their food.
Wow, love the design and decor. The food was just as delicious. I had Tom yum soup with tofu, and amazing chicken. Yum yum. Thanks for the great service and an enjoyable lunch.

Hands down the best food & drinks during my stay in New Orleans... I eat here many times while staying at the old 77 hotel & they never let me down... I could go on & on about each dish but just take a look that the pics the food speaks for itself then go try it for yourself...

If The Smiling Elephant had more seating and less of a wait, it'd be 5 stars. The food is great though: even though I want to try more things on the menu, I always end up ordering their pad see-ew because it's so delicious. They give large portions, too! Their curry is really tasty, too. Also check our all their floral teas, the honey-hibiscus is noteworthy. This is my favorite Thai food in Nashville!

ordered takeout today. pad khee mao was really good, the noodles were perfect consistency and tasty. but we got beef added to it and it was extremely, extremely dry and gross. the noodle to vegetable ratio was off too, it needed more noodles! we also ordered the green curry and it was way too watery. the flavors were good and had a decent about of kick and spice to it but sooo watery. it could have used some cornstarch. lastly, the pineapple fried rice, never disappoints! three stars because I normally enjoy their food and their flavors are always on point but there were some disappointing factors.

This is by far my favorite place in Carp!!I highly recommend, the fresh rolls are my fav. The food looks fresh and most importantly tastes fresh. I would let them know how hot you prefer. Vegetarian options are available.

HORRIBLE food and staff!The take away food was YUCKY!!..Raw uncooked food!! Lime served with the dish was pre-used by someone else .. Can you imagine???Absolutely DISGUSTING!! They take orders until minutes before the kitchen closing time and end up serving absolutely shitty food. The manager is super rude and cant speak English..Responds rudely to customer concerns ..Serves terrible food and gives excuses to customers that the poor quality is due to high number of orders..This has happened several times...Guys avoid this place!!!!.. There are a number of better Indian restarants in and around Nashville.

If McDonald's did it like this, I might be a chain restaurant fan. I was a little reluctant the first time I encountered a Taziki's. Chain Mediterranean food? My only prior experience was with the horrible chain Greek place in the Chicago airport where I immediate food poisoning. Anyway, back to the relevant facts. Taziki's is DELICIOUS. Fresh, relatively healthy, well-priced, and with plenty of gluten-free options. Back in my younger, care-free gluten-eating days, I was a giant fan of the chicken gyro; now that I am older and digestively weaker, I tend to lean towards their grilled chicken, which is always well-seasoned and tender. I am also a huge fan of their rice, which is slightly, but not overly, lemon-seasoned. It's not traditional, incredible Greek food, but it is a fast and cheap way to get fresh and nutritionally sound food. There is a patio, there is fast service, and there is baklava; what more could a person want?

Heard about the attention from the James Beard folks. Went for lunch with high expectations. Kitchen could not get five orders all out within 10 min. Food was overly complex leading to interesting but sometimes strange combinations. Prices are very high for lunch. With tip we averaged out at over $65 per head. There is so much good food in New Orleans I just don't get it. Parking is extra. Nice ambience. Very good bar. Just not good value.

My office recently ordered samosas and tandoori chicken for an event from Mumbai Bistro. The food was great and everyone loved it! The staff was also very accommodating for our need to pick-up the order prior to their opening time. Great food, great prices and service.

Very underrated food. The chicken plate is phenomenal along with every item I've had there. My child loves the hummus. We usually get our orders to go since the onsite eating is kind of sterile and during the summer it is pretty hot inside the restaurant.

At least on the day I went in, PR smelled bad, and the sandwich makers were not wearing hair nets or hats or anything. Whether you find a hair in your food is left to luck. I ordered the power pita. It was alright, but the falafel was a little too soggy. The only thing about my experience that I liked was the price. I went on "Meatless Monday," which meant that my vegetarian pita cost only $4 + tax.
Excellent Indian food Chicken saga (spinach) is a must try As are the veggie somosas as a starter
A great option for a meal if youre on campus and in a rush! Pretty fair portions and the beef meat is very tender. The fries here are also seasoned very well. Pita bread for every meal you order.

Before one thing got under my skin, I would say they have wonderful food. My friend and I tried fish kabob and chalaw banjan on July 4th night. Both of them are delicious, though the portion of chalaw banjan was comparatively light. The waitresses were nice as well. HOWEVER, when I paid for the bill, I noticed the suggested gratuities they calculated for you on the bill are "TAX CREEP". Tips should be based on the total cost of food before tax, but they included 15% to 25% of sales tax in recommended tip amounts. In other words, they calculated tips based on after-tax amount. If you just tip the numbers they calculated for you, you overpay them. I never hesitate to tip more on waitresses if the food and their services are nice, as it's just a matter of a few cents to a few dollars. But I don't like the feeling of being scammed. I have been a waitress before and I majored in accounting when I was in school. Please be mindful when you pay the bill.

Very good hookah! The bowl itself is made of green apple and fruits all around it. They put a lot of effort into making their hookah top quality and use the less harmful coal. The people that work there are very nice and gave us great service. Since it was Cold outside, we got complimentary green tea which was delicious and flavorful. I hope this place can stick around for a long time and ill definitely come back again.

Lady at the counter was very kind. She went over the items with us and explained what they were and also gave us a sample to taste whatever we wanted... Service was great!! The curries was so delicious and very flavorful!! Buy the flat breads to eat with your curries. Yum!

I ordered from Blu fig for Christmas party, the service from the start over the phone was amazing! They had every little detail of our correct! Their customer service was impeccable even carrying the food to my car and most importantly the food was delicious!! Fresh, warm, and very large portions! Thank you!

The USF area lived in harmony, that is until the fire nation-- oh i mean-- Orchid Thai attacked. After eating here, I felt a shift in the Tampa Yelper landscape. What I tasted was the rise of a new super power. The appetizer we ordered was pork strips, a meaty appetizer, the equivalent of ordering american wings or japanese karaage. It was rich in the marinade and fat. It was delicious, but I really see it as an entree(add rice). Enter the Pad Thai and Khao Soi and nothing was left thereafter. The plates were emptied. I've never had Khao Soi before, but this is the beginning of a long standing affair. Served with chicken and as Jenny C aptly reviewed, was falling off the bone. The crispy noodle played on top of the soft noodles. The coconut/curry flavor was light and heavenly. I was swimming in the goodness. Pad Thai(choose beef!) is a golden standard for many Thai enthusiasts. The dish was very herbal, the lime gave the oils a clean zest. The texture was smooth and comforting. The peanut flavor was subtle in the sauce, which notably was not too sweet, but harmonious. My astral body was eased out of me and I have was taken to the mountains where I spoke to their priests. They introduced me to Siddhartha Gautama and he too hasn't had better Pad Thai. The light pouring from the window told me I have found the anointed one. I have full confidence to send anyone here, whether they hail from VA, NY, CA or Thailand. They knoooow nothing. After tasting this dish, I have pledged fealty to Orchid Thai's Pad Thai. I know no king, but the King of the North, named Orchid Thai. P.S. one of the best thai teas.

Don't let the name fool you into thinking this is a one stop shop for egg rolls. Egg rolls yes; but the variety is fantastic. Not, it's a really cozy place. 3 (maybe 4 tables max?). You'll want to order ahead, as it can take up to half-n-hour or more depending on the day. They have breakfast eggrolls (bacon, egg, cheese, etc) that are sprinkled with "everything" topping (like an everything bagel!). The menu is huge - everything from cheese steak egg rolls to chicken cheese steak to Rubin to vegan to...you name it. The only thing they don't have is a Pierogi egg-roll but I'm hoping people will suggest that!! They also have dessert egg-rolls. Smores and cannoli and pbandJ (I believe). They have an assortment of picnic salads (potato/mac), and an assortment of beverages and a coffee called "Death Wish." The price for one eggroll is 3.00 BUT WAIT - For 3 eggrolls - the price is 6.00!!!! (Value right there!) (it also might be 6.50, still, a good deal). Very kind sweet staff. I hope they do well!

I ordered the whiting, candied yams and fries. Probably the most satisfying full meal I've had in Philly, well seasoned and perfect portions. My only issue is that they didn't have tartar sauce. This is not unique to this spot--does Philly have something against this humble condiment? Word of caution: This is end of the day/weekend food. If I'd had it for lunch I would have been knocked out at my desk. This is real soul food.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: We tried it because if the yelp reviews. the tempura rolls were delicious. They have a $1 drink refill policy which is not really welcoming when you dine in. Besides that drink fee, pretty decent place to eat.

I just had my first experience at the Mood Cafe! The owner was kind and charming. He took the time to explain chaat to me and sold me a delicious melon lassi. I'll absolutely be buying a chaat next time I come in!

This place is beyond strange. This was me and my boyfriends second time coming and the first time was a pretty nice experience. The first time we paid full price so when I saw a groupon my bf and I were excited to get a good meal for a great deal. The food isn't terrible but we did feel ripped off when the "Ghobi Pakora" came to the table the appetizer consisted of 2 pieces of cauliflower, 2 pieces of egg plant and piece of potato. They were tasty but there wasn't enough! We also ordered mango lassies and I cannot find it on their online menu but I think they were $4 a piece and the wine glass it came in had about 70% ice and 30% lassi. That was a bit ridiculous! The entrees weren't bad a tad expensive but for location and quantity we understand! The most upsetting part about our experience is when went to pay I presented my groupon and I felt that the cashier tried to pad the bill and if I didn't quickly noticed his error he would of gone on and tried his best to rip me off. I don't know if the Philadelphia location has anything to do with this place but I do not recommend coming here. I honestly don't think the business is doing too well and if I have a bad feeling about management. I have a feeling they will be shutting down !
Great Banh Mi, boba, & Shaved Ice desserts!! My favorite place. Wish there was one in Tampa.

Omg... I just had an amazing dinner here!!! Everything we tried was delicious!!! We had reservations and were seated promptly. We had the antipasti and shrimp to start... We shared a variety of pasta next (braised calamari squid ink pasta, ricotta gnocchi, spaghetti with clams, lemon pasta, the pesto pasta).. And for our entrees we shared the fisherman's stew and the swordfish. Save room for zeppolis!!!!

I had high expectations for this place, but it fell short. We started with the wontons which were pretty typical. They weren't spectacular but that's not to say that I still didn't enjoy them. The boyfriend got the pork and egg roll vermicelli dish, which again, seemed pretty average. I got the banh mi burger, and I felt that there was no real flavor that set it apart. Disappointing because I thought the pickled vegetables would brighten it up. The fries were delicious however. I don't know what their seasoning is but i like it!
Fresh, yummy, good portions for reasonable price! Family owned and friendly. Recommend for a filling heart-healthy lunch!
This is a great place to go if you want a nice, quiet dinner and a large, tasty pile of meat. (The pitas/hummus/tzatziki are, of course, also delicious).
Food was horrible. Flies all over the place. It stinks in his place. Never again never
Delicious! Best Korean around! They have Thai, Japanese as well but we only tried Korean and Thai tea. Loved it! We are definitely going back! Wonderful service too!
I loved the calamari appetizer. I would come back again just for that. Their drink menu was interesting. I had a great lychee-tini. I had the pho. It was very good.

Started out with matzo ball soup, very good. Had mushrooms and shrimp risotto which had butternut squash in it, it was amazing. Husband had half of roasted chicken over garlic mashed potatoes, very good. Son had a burger and said it was one of the best he's had. Dessert was a chocolate Carmel crisp cake, it was ok.

The service here is terrible. They charged us for a corking fee, but did not uncork our bottle of wine. The dining room is small, but it took us over an hour to get our food. I got the Jerk Chicken Breast and it was mediocre at best. After we finished our meal, we waited another 30 mins before they brought us the bill. They never removed a plate from the table after anyone was finished. And they automatically charge a 20% gratuity fee for parties 6 or more. What a joke. I don't mind paying 20%, but at least give me some service. This place is BYO so I guess they count on people getting really wasted before they eat the food.
Best boba tea in town. Beef noodle soup is great too! Bathroom is not clean, hopefully not a reflection of the kitchen cleanliness.

It was late on a Friday night and all I wanted was some light appetizers and dessert. Since Tyrst is open late and I have walked by often, I thought to give it a try. I was pleasantly surprised by the roasted vegetable flatbread. It was delicious and unexpected. The dessert was great as well, although they could have worked a bit more on cleaning it up. This is definitely a place that I will visit often and I love the fact it is open late and is a three minute walk from home.

My absolutely favorite Indian buffet in Tucson. They have a great selection of food and it's all delicious. The naan is great, the chicken tikka massala wonderful and doesn't just used flavorless chunks of breast meat. The rice pudding and gulab jamun is the best I have had. You can't beat the price!

Whatever you do, make sure to go here! I don't know think you can go wrong with anything on the menu! I've never been disappointed when dining here (this is probably our 4th time)! Stopped in after church for a meal before errands! Had the guacamole as a starter and it didn't disappoint! Absolutely fresh and tasty! It has pistachios in it, and it was a splendid addition! The chips tasted like they are house-made! I forget to ask, but the appetizer in its entirety was great! I had the chorizo hash and my husband the skillet de la casa! Both dishes were very tasteful and we literally cleaned our plates!!! Both dishes had unique authentic taste to them! Fresh avocado atop mine and the spicy ecuadorian aji chile salsa.....oh my goodness! Loved it!!! amazing dishes! Our waitress Irma was attentive and polite! We will be back again! ;) oh, the mimosas are tasty! And the price is reasonable!
Not a good place at all - we saw a cockroach BEFORE we ate. Decided to leave ....and informed the manager about issue .... poorly run _ overall this place should be avoided!!!!!!!

Food is pretty good, if you can look past the worst service possible. On several accounts, whether pick up or delivery they "don't have time for you." The woman who is always taking the orders has broken English which, if you're like me and don't know Chinese, makes it really hard to order because of her lack of patience and horrible customer service. I've been hung up on twice for asking about menu items. Also not the cleanest place ever, unfortunately.

Last nite, I ordered take-out. The Appetizer 'samosa chaat' left me craving for more. The entrees 'chicken tikka masala' and 'lamb rogan josh' were prepared just the way I requested 'medium & mild spicy.' Chicken tikka masala had all white meat pieces and lamb rogan josh was succulent. However, the entrees had a home cooked taste to 'em. It's a new restaurant so I will definitely try more selections from the menu.

We were very excited to have a bowl of pho during our trip in New Orleans. We walked from the Lafayette Cemetery No.1 to try their highly Yelp rated pho, but it turned out that it was a mistake.... It was a twenty minute walk! At Lilly's Cafe, the pho I had was overwhelmingly sweet (I have no idea why) and my friend's pho was overwhelmingly salty. Maybe they accidentally put some sugar into my soup? I dunno.. But... Sorry, Lilly's. You just made me miss our New York pho so much.

Living on S. Grand, I've tried just about all the Asian joints, except for Basil Spice. A friend wanted to try it, so we went for dinner. I can't exactly recall the name of my dish, but it was basically beef, lettuce, and rice covered heavily with what I guess were crushed peanuts. Everything kinda had a funky smell/taste to it. Not very enjoyable to say the least, and not only am I Asian, I eat just about everything. My friend ordered what I was assuming was like a Jasmine tea, but they gave her hot water and and an assortment of English breakfast teas to choose from...A great pairing to any Asian platter. I look to my left, and amongst the Buddha's and other Oriental decor, there is a worn down looking medieval castle with toy dragons and Lego dragons around it covered in dust. I think the majority of people who eat here are Caucasians that basically don't know any better.

Welcome to the small yet lovely Sizzling Wok. When I first ventured into this cozy, small, family owned restaurant, I was amazed by the quality of the Vietnamse and Chinese dishes. I can't recall who referred me or what motivated me to eat here, however, I'm glad that I discovered this small gem. Their food is tasty whether you order Chinese or Vietnamese-and reasonably priced I must say. Their food items range from 3 to 17 dollars depending upon what type of appetizers or main dishes you order. They offer plenty of tasty lunch specials up until 3 p.m. For Vietnamese novices, I suggest the Pho Gha (Chicken Noodle soup); it's big enough to feed two people!

I've been going to Dmitri's for the past 8 years or so a few times a year. The food has always been delicious, fresh, and consistent. The hummus is amazing. The lamb is worth writing home about. The beets, the calamari, the whole fish...the list goes on. Part of the fun of the experience is checking in to wait for a table (very small place) and going across the street to the New Wave Cafe, a great little place in its own right, for a drink or two before dinner. The staff has even remained the same for years, something you rarely see these days - and they are all awesome. If you're looking for a personal, fun little place for dinner with reasonable prices and a great vibe, check them out. Quick tip - they are BYOB and cash only, so plan ahead. The closest ATM is a few blocks away in a market...
Great food. Practically licked the bowls clean. Great service and inexpensive prices. I would recommend this to anyone. You will like it I promise just give it a shot.

I am super surprised that this restaurant is listed as good for groups. We went here for my birthday and was told that the system was down and they couldn't do separate checks. We had to spend 30-45 minutes calculating what everyone owed by looking at the menu and calculating our own tax and telling the waitress what we owed. We went back tonight for my friends birthday and they just flat out wouldn't split it at all. Very frustrating and a lot more work for their customers! Also, they seem to keep keep changing their menu and taking the best items off! This used to be one of our favorite restaurants, but now we don't even want to go back. So sad!
My first time here - great great food! Love it! I was the second in the line but still waited for 20 mins. That's how good the food is.

I really like this as a fusion restaurant- I can bring my friends who aren't psyched on Indian food because they also serve Chinese (and Nepalese). Very vegetarian-friendly (We love the Bhajai appetizer - we put the little pakoras in our navratan korma, malai kofta, or the Nirvana shahi paneer (which I love and I don't find in a lot of Indian restaurants). The Hakka noodles are also great. It's a good place to dine-in or take-out. They are very friendly and attentive and it's got a great atmosphere. We love having this place so close!
Idk why da faq it's taken me so long to come to this place. I pass by it all the time. Dooners salad was on point. The fact that I ordered a salad sounds pretty lame but it was on point.
Reservation? Ya we don't honor those. You will have to wait a while outside before you are seated despite a reservation, but you get a ton of delicious food for a very fair price.

Ate here for the first time a few days ago with my husband and two young boys. Atmosphere was ok, waitress was super sweet but took awhile to come back and check on us. Seats and table were dirty when we were seated and the hostess ran off before we could request for it to be cleaned.... The chicken dumplings were awesome! And my kids and I ordered simple chicken dishes, everything was good, although the chicken was heavily breaded. But sauces were great. Husband asked for his dish to be extra spicy and he almost couldn't eat it.... So ask for extra spice on the side. Overall, decent place, will return but not highly recommended.

Fresh french press coffee + the Cyrpus breakfast = one very happy girl. The cyprus is a delectable breakfast dish comprised of grilled lounza (ham), pan fried haloumi cheese, 2 slices of crunchy whole grain bread and a kalamata olive/green pepper mix as a refreshing touch. Each bite is perfectly salty and savory. Yum, this dish never ceases to please. Great brunch spot!

The food was about 4 stars but the service was great!! We had the veggie platter and the lamb tibs! Initially the lamb was not cooked to our likening. Without hesitation Aunt Selba (spell check on the name) cooked us more lamb and did not leave the table until we were satisfied with it. Initially service started off very slow we ordered injera and asked to have it warm and they forgot to bring it back to the table. However, she apologized quickly and made up for it! The rest offer service was great!! I'm definitely eating at Queen of Sheba again!

Fantastic food here! We came here for brunch and shared the dip of the day, which was amazing and highly recommend. I got the zobra burger which has a lamb patty with this feta yogurt side. It's a hefty burger and def fill you up! My friends got the Cyprus breakfast, octopus, and shakshouka. We also shared two desserts - the crepe and galatopoureko. I really liked the galatopoureko which is this amazing custard filled puff pastry . The samolina custard is warm and melts in your mouth. Would def come back here for dinner dishes. Also byob so you can have your Sunday brunch with momosas
By far the best vegetarian Indian food I've ever had! Prices are incredibly reasonable, so be sure to try out at least a few different things! You won't be disappointed!
We've had dinner here a few times, but it is my absolute favorite place for a sit down lunch. Food and service are always top notch. Evil jungle princess , mussaman and som tum are gottahavits.

Delicious and nutritious! I usually stick around the rice with chicken or beef plates (w/egg), but I'm a couple of days away from trying the Pho dish which I've heard are very tasty. Perfect hangover cure from what I understand. Tip: Try the Thai Coffee... So, So, So. Delicious.
My favorite place for pho in all of Uptown. I enjoy walking here and getting the spring rolls and the rare beef flank pho with extra vegetables. Oh yeah!
The roti canai is bangin. Very friendly staff and for the most part the food is great. Also very fairly priced.

Best food truck in Philly. The food is gourmet, chicken is grilled to perfection, and falafel is amazing. Worth the wait and well worth the money ($10, cash only). The chef only makes one dish per day, but I'm sure all are delicious. I've been here twice, both times there was grilled chicken, falafel, greens, and grapes. Once there was pasta, and the other time there was rice. Sauces were different, both were delicious. Second time there were also blueberries and a whole apricot! Be sure to get there early, because he does run out and starts to turn people away. And bring utensils and drinks. As previous reviews have stated, you could pay way more at a restaurant and get less food that isn't as delicious!

The Nepali manager shamelessly makes a pinky promise that he cannot honor Groupon coupons on Fridays and Weekends. Ok, it does not end there. One of the worst customer service experience. Nepali manager was focusing on 2 other larger group tables and completely forgot about the two of us. He took 2 hours to serve 3 dishes of which... Sweet corn veg soup was way too sweet and Tom Yam was excruciatingly hot. We ordered Indo-Chinese Main courses which were served cold. Carryout may be a better option but definitely NOT A GOOD RESTAURANT TO DINE IN

{ International Wednesday Post } This place is definitely delicious and fun!!! We set out into the city looking for a food adventure and I would say this place definitely satisfied. Its a dimly lit romantic spot with exotic music and tantalizing aromas. The flavors were super fragrant and fresh. I didn't recognize the spices but they were really yummy! I would totally recommend both my entree and side dish: Kabuli Palow: Delicately seasoned chunks of lamb or chicken under brown basmati rice. Topped with almonds, pistachios, carrots, and raisins. Buranee Kadu: Sauteed pumpkin pieces topped with yogurt and meat sauce. Definitely try the pumpkin! BYOB
Best Gyros I've had stateside. Lots of imitations out there but this is as authentic as it gets. Get a gyro deluxe with some baklava and you'll be in heaven.
I love this restaurant they have great service and nice atmosphere great food , I come aa much as I can i really enjoy their food.

The place looks nice from outside but terribly disappointing on food, even dangerous. I ordered some meat balls made with grinded beef and the couscous salad. The salad was fresh but the beef was not well cooked! We all know that grinded beef must be well cooked, not the same for a good piece of steak. Not coming back here, I threw my food on the garbage! Don't go there, could be dangerous.
Can't beat the view! Food was ok, a little pricey. Wait staff was friendly and attentive.

Definitely one of the best Jamaican Joints in Central New Jersey. A tad bit americanized and missing the heat and spices you would find in Jamaica but still close. Very clean restaurant and only one of two in Trenton where you can eat in comfortably. Prices are very reasonable and I highly recommend this place.

Excellent food excellent owners overall excellent experience. I highly recommend the curry! But anything you order will be excellent. They also have a grub hub deal that allows you to get fast delivery of excellence Indian food for a reasonable price!
Horrible customer service. Check your receipts before you leave. This is a must skip.
The massaman curry and the coconut soup are very good! The panang curry has a kick to it, so if you're sensitive to spice this one might not be the one for you.

Wow! This place is dirty and has the worst service ever! I really wanted to give this place 1 star but the food isn't bad. Service -0. no greeting, when the server came up to take my order he just stares at you awkwardly without a word. Hmmm okay, guess I should order now. When they got us our food they just left it and took off without a word, no checking up on tables with extra napkins, water or tea. They also forgot our tea we had to remind them. No courtesy, no smiling, and of course no apology. Food 2- I was hungry so it didn't taste too bad but it was not great either. Atmosphere -0 dirty and I heard other customers were complaining that they found something in their bowl so the server took back that bowl to the kitchen. I didn't hear anyone apologizing or offering anything for the customer. And I found a strand of hair in my bowl as well. The sad thing was I was almost done with my food. I didn't want to bring it up to the server because it wouldn't make any difference and they probably wouldn't do anything about it based on what I saw.

It was a bit hard location to find for an out of towner and the interior of the restaurant wasn't so welcoming, that I was almost ready to walk out. But all that impression vanished once the food arrived. The food was amazing. We ordered dosa and vada and it was one of the best we had in our trip. Kudos for the food and service.

I chose to order take out for Jaipur for lunch since my girlfriend doesn't really eat Indian food and their online prices looked to be cheaper than that of my favorite local Indian place (Desi Village). What a mistake. I picked up an order of meat samosas, pakoras, chicken tikki masala, and a side of raita. My first complaint is that the prices that they have listed on their site are definitely outdated. Those items together came to almost $30.00. The samosas were decent, but the seasoning was a little on the overpowering side. The pakoras were cold and not very good at all, and the raita pretty much tasted like bland yogurt water. YUCK. Another peeve was that I ordered the chicken tikka masala - which was $14 on it's own. Generally, anytime I order this, a side of rice is included. This was just a small plastic bowl of mostly sauce with maybe a cup of chicken chunks in it. Seriously? What am I supposed to do, drink the sauce? I wouldn't have ordered the side of yogurt water (which there was alot of) had I known I'd have no rice to put it on. I'll never go here again - another girlfriend of mine and I dined at an Indian joint on Friday night last week, got twice as much food, and only paid $45 for the both of us. Don't waste your hard-earned $$ on this crap. February 15, 2011

Definitely a new experience, eating with no utensils. Instead of utensils, you're given a fluffy rolled bread (pictured) that has a sour dough- esque flavor. We got the queens platter, which comes with 2 beef, 2 chicken, and 4 veggie portions. Plus a veggie platter that come with 4 veggie portions. I really enjoined the lentils and beef portions. The chicken and other portions left a lot to be desired. Flavor profiles were unique and vastly different for each portion, so everyone is able to enjoy something. Service was ok. It was slow in a Wednesday night, so we were surprised how long it took to get more water, the checks, and to go boxes. We had to go ask for the check and for to go boxes 2x because they thought 1 box was sufficient for 2 plates and a basket. Worth a try, at least for the experience.

If this place was next door to me, I'd weigh 400 pounds. Great Indonesian food. Great prices too. We usually get two appetizers, two rice or noodle bowls and two coffees for well under $30. It's such a steal. The food is delicious. And for two people that regularly spend $120+ on brunch, eating here is nice for a change of pace for us.

Wanted to plan a surprise birthday dinner, with about 15 people, almost all yelpers who have been to most of the great restaurants in Philly...Marrakesh to the rescue. I went here a few times in college, and remembered that it's a great, affordable option for a group (BYO), and its a cuisine most of us don't eat on the regular. I called the restaurant a few weeks ahead of time to reserve a room for our group. The staff was always very friendly and helpful on the phone. They even went the extra mile to play along with the surprise and lead us through a series of dining rooms so that even I was confused about what was happening. Oh, and my friend has a nut allergy which they easily accommodated. The no utensils threw a few people off, but everyone got into the spirit. The spicy chicken was ridiculously tender and delicious. The lamb was good, but a little fatty. The beef kebabs were a little on the dry side. All in all though, the staff, plus the ambiance, plus the food made for a fantastic dinner. A good time was had by all.

I was shocked to have a terrible meal from this establishment. They have really gone downhill. Used to be my go-to, and as a guy who works in a thai restaurant and has traveled to thailand, that says a lot. I ordered beef salad and green curry. Two Thai staples...both were all but inedible. Oversalted is an understatement. The green curry tasted salty and had virtually no coconut flavor - I have seen some Thai places use cream to cut cost on curry, but this seemed like pure heavy cream and no coconut milk at all...and soooo salty. The beef salad had uncooked beef to start, and was even saltier than the green curry...could hardly get it down. even the white rice (which was sushi rice and not jasmine rice) was very salty, which I just don't understand. My wife (from Thailand) agreed 100% and said that she couldn't eat it either. Sorry to say, but I will never go here again. Too bad.

Two stars because the food is good. They lost three stars because the delivery guy is a greedy, entitled bastard who begged for a tip and refused to leave our doorstep, claiming he works off of tips. Yeah okay buddy. I refuse to believe that the restaurant isn't paying this dude for delivering food. When restaurants have delivery fees that usually goes toward the driver. Well that's not true for this restaurant. When I called there to complain the woman who answered the phone told me that the delivery fee goes to the restaurant. Sheisty af. I may order pick up from them again but for someone to complain about not getting tipped for driving less than a mile down the street (literally) makes me question the integrity of Pikpon Thai.

While on the west side, my wife and I decided to give Pho 36 a try. I must say I agree with a number of reviews that mention that the service is friendly and pretty efficient (even though the owner/waiter was the only one covering the front including the cash register.) The food we ordered, and we ordered a lot, came out pretty quickly and I enjoyed everything I tried. I started with an order of Egg Rolls (3) that were nice and crisp and filled with ground pork, egg, long rice, carrots, and onions. There were a couple types of veggie strips along side and a dipping sauce. The sauce was on the thin side and didn't add a lot of flavor, but it was enough to add some depth to the taste. I also had the Vietnamese Chicken wings which had five pieces of crisp breaded chicken drumettes or flat/tips and covered with a sticky "fish" sauce which tastes like a combo of sweet and savory flavors. (I didn't find it pungent, salty, or hot. The flavors seemed like honey and sesame seed to me.) My wife liked these too! I also ordered the "Special" Bahn Mi - a baguette sandwich with sliced pork, pate, mayo, carrot, daikon, cucumber, sliced jalapeno, and cilantro. My wife thought it tasted hot, but I didn't notice the heat at all. The ingredients are served cold, but the flavors were refreshing and quite good. The bread was very fresh too. My wife was new to the cuisine, so she played it safe with the stir-fried chicken with mixed vegetables. The dish was plentiful and the rice with chicken and shrimp stayed moist, not overcooked. Plenty to eat for the money. I also sampled a bowl of Pho - Chicken Noodle soup. I noticed a small plate of sliced jalapeno, cilantro, and bean sprouts, but completely forgot to add them into my bowl. The bowl itself was huge and was loaded with noodles and large (almost more than bite-sized) pieces of chicken. The soup itself was on the bland side, like broth with just a hint of seasoning. Maybe if I had remembered to add my side veggies/herbs, the flavor would have had more depth to it. On the fun side, I ordered a strawberry bubble tea. This was very cold and I did get a bit of brain freeze. The bubbles are black tapioca beads that have the texture of gummy bears and were odd to watch slide up through my straw. The flavor was exceptionally good and the drink stayed icy throughout the meal. Overall, it was a fun place to stop and try another cuisine that is hard to find around town. Although it has items that are similar to those offered at nearby restaurants, the business did a brisk business the entire time we dined there. it must be the service and food being a high quality. p.s. For additional flavor, they have Sriracha sauce and Hoison sauce bottles on the tables. p.s.s. Although the website leads me to believe this is a franchise of a chain, the ownership appears to be local and works in the restaurant. Review #376

Love this place! I had a banana and date lassi (on the owner's suggestion) and it was awesome. If you don't see something that sounds very good just ask him what is very good and he'll make you something perfect! Can't wait to get back there!

This is one of the best restaurants I have been to. Every thing they use in their recipe is super fresh. Fatouche salad is very fresh and tasty and I liked the dressing. The BBQ pizza was great and chicken and meat skewers tasted really good and were a good amount for the price. The garlic sauce also tasted amazing. Our waiter Omar was very helpful and friendly and tried to help us in choosing our food. I had a really good experience in here and will definitely go back.

Phenomenal food! I've been going here 2-3 times a year for the past 7 years. I don't even look at a menu any more. Their appetizers are great, I usually go spicy feta dip, and their hummus. And for dinner My wife and I always get the Kapama (lamb shank in red sauce) the bone bone lifts right out, and the meat is sooo tender. And leave room for desert, I recommend the baklava (I get random cravings all the time). And my wife loves the honey cake and a frappe. I also want to make a side note about the staff. The cook is very nice and always greet us when we come in. And the 2 brother waiters are awesome. They are such nice guys, and always go out of the way for us.

I tried this restaurant because I got a groupon for it. It was one of those restaurants that is always on groupon so I did not have high expectations. Turns out, it was much better than expected. We went on a saturday night around 8 and the place was very crowded. That being said, we ( party of two) were seated within 15 minutes or so when they told us 30 mins of waiting so it started off well. They have a nice couch to sit on near the entrance and I liked the decor of the place.Once we were seated our server was kind, prompt and helpful. I'm one of those person's that always asks questions about the menu and what the waiter's favorite is. I ordered the falafel and my bf ordered some sort of garlic shrimp I think. My falafel plate was very good and it was a good sized portion for 9 dollars. My bf liked his shrimp I think? It looked decent... but then again I never have really liked seafood. Overall, I was impressed with this place. good food, atmosphere, and great service. Bonus point: they have a large room in the back which serves large parties that my server said you could reserve. Always a good thing to have in STL and a rare find. Minus point: minimal parking available, but better than downtown? Neutral: since when do greek restaurants have belly dancers? Overall, a great find, I will go back!
Not authentic but good. I would recommend Buddha dumpling, Evil Jungle Princess and the Green Curry.

This place was a wonderful surprise. I moved to St. Pete, but would still make the drive for their delicious Thai! I had chicken panang and egg rolls and it was absolutely amazing. Can't wait to try more!

I had the Smiling Elephant Pad Thai for lunch and it was excellent. I tried to finish the entire plate but it was a large lunch portion. Hope it makes a good leftover. While the food is excellent the place is very small and the parking is poor. I will be going back again to try something else.

Sad to say, I think it's closed. This place was my go-to Vietnamese place, always consistently good. I loved the Seafood soup and papaya salad. I was sad to see no tables, all the lights off, and a hefty lock on the door Sunday morning when we were rolling up to satiate our Pho craving (always served at breakfast in Vietnam). I hope they may be remodeling, but I surmise that this is the end of an era. Maybe the place a few shops down from them will come through. But are they open at 9:30am? Cheers Pho 38.
Expensive, but a unique dining experience. Food is terrific.
Adorable atmosphere and most of all, the food quality is amazing, and inexpensive. Sold!

Outrageously inflated price (lunch buffet) for a standard Indian food. Perhaps a 'Mainline' price range? Naan is best when you see it come out. Otherwise, skip it since it is barely edible (hard & tasteless). Chicken Tikka is less creamy compared to other Indian Restaurants in the area; Tandoori is missing the grilled smoky flavor, but its aesthetic 'red dye' is there. Mango lassi is excellent, but would be perfect if it was chilled a bit more. Flavor wise it is authentic mango and smooth consistency. ***Customer service is as stale as spoiled food. Owner/server/receptionist/cashier barely acknowledge us, smile or replenish water. Gives you the impression that you owe them a favor for eating at their place. I will not come back anytime soon. There are other excellent Indian places with superior customer service and very friendly staff.
Fantastic spot for lunch if you are in the mood for Indian food. The specials are of a good variety and at a good bargain. The dinner options are not really anything special, and a bit over priced.
Good, fresh food, great service. Best Thai on the Main Line and maybe in the entire Philadelphia area!

Disappointing afghany restaurant in olde city. The Ariana kabob (chicken, beef, and lamb) was served on a large platter that was predominantly rice and a few small pieces of meat. The meat wasn't good. The service was very slow. Can't think of any reason to come back here.

I am a person of Jamaican descent and sometimes you can get good Jamaican food OUTSIDE of your own home. Not in this review. Ron's is cafeteria Jamaican food at best. Everything was super SALTY! I per chased ox tails, curried goat, and jerk chicken. PROS-OX TAILS were tender. CONS-they were very small. The very end of the tail. salty and the gravy tasted like a doctored version of the real thing. The best gravy however of the three. PROS- GOAT was tender. CONS- goat was SALTY. No other veggies in the pot. If they added a carrot or some potatoes it would have helped with the saltiness. Would have been the best gravy if it was not so salty and inedible. I threw it away. PROS- JERK CHICKEN was a good serving size. CONS-Not enough jerk flavor. They need to marinate the chicken in the jerk sauce. It was just plain bland. The worse part is they added some cheap barbeque sauce on the chicken and called it jerk sauce. HORRIBLE! Ruined the entire meal! If you get the jerk chicken DO NOT get the sauce! Cabbage was BLAND! Beans and rice a big disappointment. A poorly made version with poor ingredients. Tasted like minute rice. The give you a lot of rice and beans especially in the extra large serving of ox tails. The meat to rice ratio was just unfair. I felt cheated. I will not recommend! There was a short wait considering the place was crowded. It looked like organized chaos. The servers were clean, in uniform and their heads were netted. GOOD. They were pleasant also because the masses were kind of difficult. The cooks were dressed in chef whites. Nice touch. Well stocked variety of drinks and desserts. Very clean. I left thinking I have found my new Jamaican cuisine home. NOT! THE FOOD WAS JUST BAD. REALLY BAD! BAD!

First off, My overall experience was '3 stars' - I am adding the extra star to express my excitement of (finally) having an Indian Restaurant in the area with a nice and fine ambience, a good menu, and being a BYO. My wife and I stopped by for lunch on a Sunday. We were instantly greeted by the hostess, and taken to our booth. RIght away, we both noticed the fine setting, and the expansive menu. The Good: 1. Nice setting. Both my wife and I instantly thought that it would be nice to gather here for a nice dinner with friends , especially since it is a BYO 2. Good menu. The menu is good and slightly more expansive than most Indian restaurants in the area. Was pleasantly surprised to see Indo-Chinese on the menu as well 3. The Buffet. I opted for the Buffet while my wife opted to order Indo Chinese from the menu. The buffet food was good, tasted fresh and the curries weren't swimming in oil The Bad - I realize they have just opened, so I wouldn't focus too much on these. I am ready to give them another chance, but here were a few things I noticed. 1. Bread took 20 minutes to arrive after I sat down with the food from the Buffet. I actually finished one serving of curries, without any bread. The waitress did apologize - and again I am cutting them slack since the restaurant has just opened. This is Indian Restaurant 101 - the bread 'must' be available if not with the buffet, then may be just a few minutes after. 2. Indo-Chinese food, didn't taste like Indo Chinese at all. The Hakka Noodles tasted like any other noodles cooked with veggies, and the Manchurian , while were good, didn't have the Indo-Chinese flavor. 3. No Daal! - The buffet had three types of rice, Chicken Biryani, Tawa Rice , and Plain Jeera rice - but there was no Daal in the Buffet. C'mon! The Daal (Lentils) are essential to any Buffet. 4. The service - The waitresses were very sweet and seemed to be on top of everything while I saw them working with other tables. May be because we came in late, but not sure why we didn't have the same experience. After getting us seated, had to wave to one of them after a while to take my wife's order from the menu. After the food was served, our next interaction with the waitress was when we paid for our check (which was at the register). No second serving of water , or someone to ask us if we needed something else. I for example, wanted a Diet Coke right when I was at the end of the meal, but after waiting for a few minutes, decided that it wasn't worth it to get someone's attention. Overall - I will be back, and I want to give this place a chance. I am excited about the potential of there being a nice Indian restaurant in the area.

I am by no means a pho expert.. or a pho snob. I know what I like, I'm pretty easy to please.. and Lilly's is pretty damn good. I've been fighting this cold for a while now, and I finally decided.. enough was enough. It was time for some spicy pho. Lilly's is down the street from me, and it's a shame I hadn't been until now. I picked up some chicken pho to go, some egg rolls, and the grilled beef bahn mi. The pho is just what I needed (and currently, I'm finishing the 2nd half of it for lunch today.. just as good in round 2).. fresh taste, great broth, and a LOT of it. Great egg rolls too. My boyfriend didn't love his bahn mi, but he can be picky about his sandwiches. But the meat was well seasoned and delicious. The staff is really friendly too.. and great lemonade. All in all.. I'm excited about this little addition to the Lower Garden!

I love the smiling elephant. I've eaten here a couple times (I normally do before I write a review) Everything is good but the real standout in my opinion is the pad Thai. I normally do not like pad Thai because I find the American version is really sweet... This is not like the pad Thai you've had before in the very best way!!
Wonderful! My family has been coming here for years and it was amazing every time! They have kosher meat and very clean place. Good halal food too! U defiantly recommend this 10/10

I have been to this place for three times, I am a big fan of the Thai Iced Tea, this is not like any other Thai tea that made from powder in Bubble milk tea places, I believe they brew it themselves. As for food, I love their Pad Thai and Tom Yum Rice Noodle Soup (the more spicy, the more tasty, so I order then awakening level for spicy). I have also tried other dishes, included the Exotic Pork and Thai BBQ Chicken. On the menu, it says TENDER, but it came out dry... Although the sauces taste delicious, but still it is kinda disappointing. As for dessert, Mango Sticky Rice is a must to try!!! Fresh mango with warm sesame topped sticky rice, and also coconut milk on top. Yum yum~~

I havent had the pleasure of trying any of PM's other dishes, but I will tell you that the daily special with the half chicken and rice is completely and utterly off the rack. Seasoned to perfection, u barely want to use salt or pepper on it. Rice and beans are fantastic and the plaintains are tremendous as well. Great guy that Juan is. Love this place. Don't get me started on the fruit juices.

Yep. It's all that. I'm usually a restaurant hopper, never eating in the same place twice. And if I do, never eating the same dish twice. But since there are not very many Ethiopian restaurants it's not hard to narrow down a favorite because Abay has the best tasting hands down.

Sure, it's good...if you even get what you ordered. I've ordered from this place several times from work through PostMates. I don't know what it is about this restaurant, but I would say at least 75% of the time they don't send us even half of what we order, always leaving out at least two of our entrees, if not more. I've all but given up on ordering from this place cause it's too much of a hassle to have to order the missing food yet again from PostMates after we undoubtedly don't receive half of it. At least the other Thai places we order from remember everything. Basil Spice...not so much. They need to do a better job of verifying that what they send out is everything that the customer has ordered. Done with this place.

Went there with the wife and kids based on Yelp reviews. Lives up to the rating for the most part. Food was very good - had the grilled chicken shishkabob - perfectly cooked and delicious! Kids liked the Spanikopita as well as the meatball's over penne. Waitress was not helpful at all - maybe caught her on a bad/off day. Great table bread and pita with the humus. My Ratings: 5* - Unfreaking believable. Just the thought of going makes me drool. 4* - Very good. Would recommend to anyone. Would be happy to return again. 3* - Meh 2* - Not very good. Would only return if there were no other options. 1* - I know its arrogant to say it, but they should really close up shop. They've proved to me they don't give a sh@t.

It's heaven smothered in tzatziki. Maybe Im naive, maybe I'm just not cultured enough - but as far as I'm concerned this is crazy good greek food. Like make out with the pita bread kind of good. We had a cold appetizer sampler and then I had eggplant stuffed with feta and tomatoes. Both were out of control delicious. Those two items plus my friends entree totaled to about $30. And it was BYOB. Crazy good food and relatively affordable? sold. done and done.

Went there to celebrate a special occasion. There were 7 of us. The waiter was outstanding--fast service, very attentive, offered great information about the food. We sat outside on a gorgeous day and really enjoyed it. Everyone liked everything they ate. The highlights were definitely: 1) The dips of the day. Holy cow, I can't say enough good things about these. If they served an entree-sized portion, I could definitely eat just these. 2) The phyllo/honey/feta appetizer concoction. Unreal. Must order. As for the entrees, I really enjoyed my veal dish. Everyone at the table ordered something different--lamb, veal, suckling pig, stuffed vegetables, fresh fish of the day. All were very tasty--there was nothing left on anyone's plate. The desserts were also surprisingly tasty, especially given that I'm generally indifferent about Greekish desserts. *Very* impressed with this meal. If I weren't moving in a few weeks, I'd go back. That said, it's a teensy bit pricey. But at least it's BYO, so you save a bit there.

I cannot believe I have lived 5 miles from this place for as long as it's been around, but I just tried it for the first time a month ago. I've eaten quite a bit of Thai food in the STL area, and to say this is the best I've ever had would not be an understatement. I've only had the pad thai with chicken and the green curry with chicken (multiple times over the past month), but both are absolutely delicious! Everything is fresh, and the people who work there are very friendly. Two thumbs up!

Flambo is simply majestic!! Truly a hidden gem in Philly and the only place you can find authentic, mouth watering Trinidadian cuisine. The service is impeccable and the owners are very welcoming. Once you walk in you'll feel like your in the islands and the food is beyond delicious. I recommend Flambo because the food is flavorful and prepared freshly. I'm never disappointed and did I mention how amazing, owners Kevin and his dad are? I will be returning!
Excellent food, excellent service (thanks Christian!). Definitely a new favorite.
it's cheap & goooodd. the place is soooo nice & the staff is really helpful !! definitely going back soon !!
im from dc came to visit a day yelped places to go ended up at wishbone....loved it the wings biscuits mac and cheese on a next level... #travelchannelworthy a must vist when in philly
Atmosphere is very weird...lighting is harsh, tables, carpets, etc are jankety but the food is pretty good. Not my top pick, but it's acceptable.

The Buffet was pretty mediocre. Chicken makhani had sugar in it. Goat curry and chicken curry was average. The dessert (gulab jamun) was good and masala tea on a cold night added a nice touch. The appetizer (Samosa and pakoras) were ok. We had to ask the staff to refill the empty dishes though. Maybe the restaurant was having an off night so I will try it again during daytime and order from the menu. I'm a New Yorker and have given up on finding a decent Indian restaurant in university city. My suggestion if you're craving Indian food, skip it!

Stopped here on our way through to Pennsylvania. Located in the historic part of Trenton, this order at the counter style restaurant was clean and had good vibes. I had two beef patties and a side of mac and cheese. My eating partner had jerk-style wings and festival bread. All came out in under ten minutes and were hot and delicious. The wing sauce was delectable and the festival was perfect for sopping it up. The only drawback I would say would be that there seemed to be only one person working. She was answering the phone (which seemed to ring every 20 seconds), trying to take care of customers at the same time, and also preparing the food. It seemed like a bit much for one person but she handled it well enough. Definitely worth the stop.

This is my favorite Vietnamese restaurant! I have been coming here for years and the food is top notch. The original owner sold it to the cook and the cook sold to the waitress and her husband. so there is continuity in the cooking and has stayed excellent over the years. if you like quality Vietnamese food, eat here. The other restaurants just ate not as good.

The food quality at Naf Naf is great. It's easy to see why they are growing really fast. The meats are super fresh, and the veggies are high quality too. Probably the best thing here is the fresh Pita bread. The service is hit or miss. I don't think it's the employees fault, I think they lack direction from management. Every Naf Naf location I go to, I always end up having to wait for fries. There is definitely room for process improvement.
Awesome food .and byob they do a great job with everything . I would recommend getting the hummus plate and the braised lamb dumpling for your appetizers .

I've been to probably a hundred Thai places and more than half of the top 50 restaurants on Philly mag. This is the best Thai restaurant I've been too ever. Period. No discussion. Little old Thai lady in the back makes everything by hand. Does it taste like homemade? Yes. That's the point. I don't know what these other reviewers are smoking... Best place ever. The dumplings are ridiculous. The Pumkin, Salmon crock pot is to die for. And like most Thai its inexpensive. I think this is the beginning of a new relationship with Coco Thai Bistro.

If you're looking for a quiet hole in the wall, something unpretentious and untrendy with drop dead delicious food... And you're craving pho... Come here. Thinking I'll make myself a regular. Tip: I had the Dac Biet Pho and I was pleased. They bring a plate of fresh toppings. Just sat by myself and watched CNN with the server.

Went here for my birthday dinner with my mom and daughter and had wonderful time. The staff and manager was accommodating and friendly. The food was very good and fast. Would like to try a date night with my hubby to enjoy more of the drinks and entertainment. We hade the regular gyro and one with the andouille sausage. Both were great!

We were instantly greeted and asked if it was our 1st time in. When we answered yes they gave us a sample of their rice and beans mixed with a tomato and cucumber salad. We ordered a Greek salad with gyro meat it was huge. The beef gyro sandwich, Hummus with pita, Falafel all were very tasty. The serving size was abundant for the price. We had to take a lot with us it was so much food. We had excellent service also. My son said this would be a place to go weekly if we lived in Tampa. Very pleased with our experience.

Yes, the biscuits are amazing, the food creative and flavorful with Caribbean notes and very fresh in a very upscale exposed brick decor. Here's where they failed: ambience ruined by loud music that caused everyone to raise their voice just so your dinner companion can hear you. Wait staff was inattentive and inexperienced. Wine paired with a meal arrived after the meal despite three separate requests. Coffee arrived well after dessert was done. Good restaurant but lacking in the small nuances that could make it great.

Lunch buffet is gross and has not much variety. Chicken tikka masala is Campbell's tomato soup base. They replenish buffet by dumping bowls of refill into trays, not replacing the whole tray. Ambiance is pretty so it's a shame. It's basically Indian fast food.

Yes, I'm a fan. But it's not "Hearty" approved in terms of a healthy selection. The menu when I went was fixed. I'm almost positive it's like this all the time. But damn, what an awesome experience. A 7 course meal, rose petal hand wash between dishes, a belly dancer (she's only there certain days)... so cool! The fact that I had to walk down a quiet (but safe) alley to get there and ring the door bell for a staff member dressed in Moroccan garb to let me in was fun as hell. 5 stars for the experience, but 3 because there's not much control about what you can eat. It's also expensive. Around $60/person... not including drinks.

I Love this place! The food is always great. Its easy to get a table and the owner is so sweet. The runs a tight ship. This is a family owned business, her mom is the cook. This is a great story you have to ask her about! I have tried something different the past 10 or so times and have never been disappointed!

Not only do they take FOREVER to get here (they are right up the street from us) But this is the second day IN A ROW that they messed up our order and forgot parts of it. The Sushi is amazing...but have herd bad things about the rest of the food. Our office will no longer be ordering from them. Menu removed!

I come here at least once a week on my lunch break, and have yet to have anything less than great. Their rice dishes are consistently fresh and delicious. The inside is clean and cutely decorated with differently Lilly-themed artwork. Service is good and the food is solid. Check out Lilly's

Like eating dinner at family's house. The owner greeted us warmly and treated us like family throughout, and he went out of his way to care for the 11-month old in our group. And ah yes, the food. I had the Halwa Poor Package, which featured the chana masala, al bhaji, halwa and fried puffy bread. Great spice on the al bhaji (a potato dish), and the halwa was sweet and delicious, like cream of wheat with honey. My wife's lamb nihari was phenomenal, and the owner catered to our desired spice level. Best Indian/Pakistani food I've had in STL. Would definitely come back.

The Caprese sandwich was pretty tasty, if $8.50 for a sandwich sits ok with you. It's also a cute place. As other reviews mention, however, they won't give you a glass of water to go with your meal. You have to buy a bottle of it or go without. I have a problem with bottled water in general, and with a restaurant that skips an amenity most restaurants offer without charge, so... meh.

Flavorful, well made, 5 star food with no attitude or pretense. One of the most amazing dining experiences I've had in a long time. Definitely the best I've had in South Jersey. The restaurant immediately gets you into a nice relaxed, romantic mood with the intimate close settings and candle light. The staff is incredibly polite, knowledgeable and friendly. The food was the absolute highlight though. I've never had a more perfectly prepared stewed rabbit in my life. The pasta dishes (we had the Rigatoni alla Disgraziata and Spaghetti Vongole) were mouth watering. The sauces were unbelievable. The appetizer we had was the Gamberetti e Fagioli....awesome. (caution, they only give you three, so you might have to fight to steal the last one from your date haha) Even the bread they serve is yummy. And of course, a Zeppoli and espresso to finish the meal. Absolutely recommended for a date, or even just to get together with a few close friends/family and chat. Friendly, comfortable environment that welcomes conversation and laughter. Just like being at a big Italian family dinner.

Great Pho and great service. Tofu veggie bowl was delish. Tons of veg and noodles. Tofu was crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside. Big portions - definitely enough for leftovers. Very clean as well.
Good pad Thai and spring rolls. Fast service even when crowded. Great lunch spot. Highly recommended.

I'm not a huge rum fan but I've had really great mojitos before so I said I'd try my husband's before I ordered one for me. It was 'ok' but not worth raving about so the waitress said, "I don't have to make it with rum, I can use vodka!?" Mmm...ok!? Honestly, I think that was a mistake. It was fine but also meh. The salad I ordered had an entire avocado sliced over it and it wasn't quite ripe - a ripe avocado would have made the difference. The dressing was fresh tasting but a teeny cup was all I was given. The fish tacos had store bought soft tacos which were lackluster and very wet cole claw under the fish which was tilapia. I ended up just eating the insides as the tacos themselves had no taste and fell apart from the liquid. There was a teeny cup of guacomole which I could make so much better and there was so little salsa picante I couldn't really review it. The waitress (who also filled as the bartender) forgot our water, delivered hubby's tortilla soup (dull) a long while before my salad arrived, forgot my drink order (also for a long time) and when I asked for a second teeny cup of guacomole she said, "sure!" and never delivered it. She was friendly and apologetic for every wrong turn but with the cost of dining out (which we love to do), we won't be back.

Ben (chef/owner) from Salume Beddu and Andrey (General Manager) from 33 Wine Shop have taken an old 1930's gas station and turned it into a trendy little wine bar. The bar area is compact, cozy and all the windows give it a felling of being larger then it really is. Great wine by the glass, tasting flights measured to perfection and an impressive selection of liquor as well. I went craving a red wine, but when I saw they offered Tito's Vodka my favorite I was swayed away. We enjoyed a sampling of artisan cured meats and hard cheese served with fresh bread and oil. A great place for Happy Hour or after theater drinks.

If I could give zero stars I would. They were so rude. My order was wrong and instead of being nice and bringing me the correct food they threw together something that I didn't order again. Never going back although I hear the food is good.

This was a fabulous place. Had the appetizer platter with an assortment of dips and warm pita bread. YUM.. Tangine lamb and chicken was phenomenal! Freshest fish with mint sauce..gotta try! A must have is the Rose Tea. Turkish coffee, and home made Baklava..perfection! Everything was perfectly seasoned. If you are a Moroccan food lover...this is the place for you...
Great restaurant. Food is great, service is great and it's always quiet - even when packed. Definitely recommend!

Absolutely love it here. I have eaten in or taken out here at least a dozen times. Food is really delicious, the waitresses are always sweet, and they have really great lunch special deals! My favorite pad thai and spring rolls around.

Chicken pesto pita is my favorite. The cucumber and tomatoes salad is fresh and tasty. The hummus Is filling with the veggies. I just find it a little pricy for the portion of food. But the good quality and taste is consistent each time I come. I was just at a bunco party with my friends and someone catered from this restaurant I was surprised at how delicious the pasta chicken salad was it had feta cheese and balsamic vinegar that was just so tangy! Yummy! The pita chips and yogurt sauce was so good, garlicky and lots of cucumbers. I actually ran into this place again a few weeks later at a farmers market event and they had some more menus item samples that tasted delish. I have realized they are not just in Mount Juliet and have lots of locations. If you are in the mood for a dessert you have to try the chocolate cake it's so good and not too sweet, yummy!
Ok, this place grows its own chili peppers in buckets in the backyard. their young coconut/avocado salad is so amazing I don't even know what to do with myself.

We keep coming back for lunch buffet on the weekend. Our favorite in the neighborhood. Home made carrot and cauliflower pickles, all the usual entrees, and my daughter's favorite - at least 3 deserts.

What a surprise! Deliciously prepared Thai cuisine. The broad noodles with egg and broccoli and the yellow curry with potatoes were particularly good. Nice decor, good service. The Air Force has discovered this joint and it is always busy over the noon hour and full of blue uniforms. I have yet to make it back for dinner, but as they have a full bar, you can be certain that I will soon. Tell them to leave the whipped cream off your Thai Iced Tea.

Queen of Sheba is hands-down one of my new favorite restaurants in Tampa. Yes, it's true, this is the first Ethiopian restaurant I've ever tried, but--oh my goodness--it was SO cool. Four reasons why this place is so ballin': 1.) When you enter the restaurant, you enter into a little living room area before you wander into the dining room. It's not just a living room. It's an ETHIOPIAN living room. Tons of cool stuff to look at and read. 2.) The food was outstanding and unique. I had dinner with my sister and her husband. We ordered the Queen's Eight for three people ($40). This is a large platter of foods chosen nightly by the chef. Lamb, beef, chicken... cabbage, lentils, chickpeas, eggs... and maybe some other food as well. All were wonderfully spiced and cooked to perfection. 3.) Injera. You don't use any utensils during the meal. Instead, you pick up food from the center platter using a piece of injera. Injera, as described by our server, is a cross between a crepe, a tortilla, and a pita. My definition: it's a roll of elastic deliciousness. Yum yum yum. (for more about injera: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injera) 4.) The service was excellent. Our server (Monica) was helpful and gladly explained everything to us. She made our first Ethiopian meal very enjoyable. Seble, the owner, came to our table and talked to us for a while after our meal. I was impressed by the team of folks running this place. By giving five stars here, I am wholeheartedly giving five stars. Out of all of the new places I've tried recently, this might be my favorite. I am already looking at my schedule to figure out when I can return.
I LOVE this place. My favorite place for pho. I try to go at least twice a week.

Not sure why this place has five stars across the board. Was hungry so shared a large jerk chicken plate with my boyfriend. It was OKAY. Average chicken, rice wasn't fabulous, caramelized bananas were okay, and we passed on dessert. A bit overpriced considering the portions. Probably won't be back.

Always looking for different foods in new cities. The reviews of the place were for the most part very accurate. Great tasting Ethiopian food! Service a bit slow but nothing that was annoying. Will be back when in the area!

First night in Philly. Six of us walked from our hotel to this restaurant. They had their specials of the night displayed and looked delicious. As good as it looked it was. Everyone's food was hot and tasted amazing. We had fresh juice and fresh made desserts. Authentic Dominican food. One even dropped her purse without realizing and the owner ran two blocks to return it to her. Made our first night in town perfect.

It is not the only the best Vietnamese in Indy, but the BEST RESTAURANT in AVON by far. The vegetables are always crisp and fresh. The store is immaculate. Their spring rolls and Pho (soup) are as good as it gets.

This restaurant is now called Thai Smiles , new ownership recently. The food is delicious. I had the chicken garlic and pepper and it was fabulous. Ordered it two separate occasions. Very fresh and the service is outstanding. Check it out!! :-).
Had the (unlimited) lunch buffet. Highly recommend it. Great lunch in clean restaurant for less than $10. Wonderful service by friendly staff.
Excellent menu and vibe that provides an incredible sensory experience, at a price that is worth paying.

Stopped in for a quick lunch. Girl at the counter helped me pick out my meal. Veg Med sammich and tossed salad. Ratio of bread to stuff was off, too much bread. Also too much cheese on the sammich. Salad was good. I should have just got that. Fast and cheap so i'm happy.

My sisters and I had a fun weekend trip to swim with manatees in Crystal River. We found a few fun restaurants to enjoy in this part of Florida for the weekend. Sam's was one of them. We chose it because 1) it overlooked the water at sunset, 2) it was decorated like a great beach bar and 3) there might be live music. The food was decent. The view was amazing! The vibe was fun and festive. There was a DJ the night we were there so we moved over to the Tiki bar/dance area after dinner. It was so much fun to watch people dance and have a great time. The mood was joyful and the music was fun too! Overall it was a great experience for a Friday evening on the water.

Lilly's has delicious food and fast, no-nonsense service. I kept hearing about the great Vietnamese food in NOLA, but I felt some FOMO-induced anxiety when deciding where to go. There are a ton of options, so I was afraid of making the wrong choice. Well, I had nothing to worry about at Lilly's! As soon as I tasted the rich pho broth, I knew I was in the right place. I had the combo pho with quail eggs and the honey aloe drink, and we also ordered spicy shrimp vermicelli and obligatory spring rolls. Everything was delicious! The owner even made the time to stop by our table and crack some jokes. This is the place!

I lived in Thailand for six years, 1998 to 2004, and loved the Thai food. This restaurant, The Thai House, is excellent! Their kitchen is able to cook true Thai food and NOT Americanized-Thai when requested (and ordered in Thai). This is a quick trip from South St. Louis County. The food is GREAT.
