The staff is friendly. The prices are right. Give it a try when you are in the mood for something different or want to taste REAL Thai food.
Blown away by the incredible service and fresh tasty food. Classy place to bring someone for a unique dining experience. Check it out mon!

Some things I love: - eating with my hands - spices - being messy - expertly seasoned vegetables - trying new ethnic food This Valentines weekend, Abyssinia provided me and my husband an opportunity to enjoy all these things and more. As it was our first visit, our server took time to explain the menu, recommending the vegetarian Taste of Abyssinia option - a delectable combination of seven different vegetarian dishes, running the gamut from spinach and mustard greens, to potatoes, carrots, and cabbage, to both red and yellow lentils. We chose the "for one" option, and it was PLENTY of food for the two of us. We also tried the lentil and cabbage sambusas - both were fantastic with complex and well-melded flavors. We used a Groupon, so not only was our meal delicious, warm, and flavorful, we got a fantastic deal. Abyssinia - you rock my world (and my tastebuds).
Great Indian food for a decent price. Located right down town so makes a great lunch spot.

Our second time back. We were there for the first night of their soft opening and it was great. We went back tonight for their full menu and, if we could eat EVERY meal there, we would! Chicken Tikka Masala, Paneer Butter Masala, Plain/Butter Naan and Garlic Naan - all totally delicious. Wonderful rice - perfectly prepared.They were pretty busy and we are happy to see that because we want Persis Biryani Indian Grill​ to be her for a long, long time.

BYOB made all the difference! Food was just okay, nothing to write home about but not awful either. Stay away from the calamari. Ours may have just been overlooked but my goodness, they shouldn't have served it. Curry was tasty but they give you such a tiny scoop of rice you'll have to ask for more multiple times. I'm sure there is better Thai around but if you find yourself in the area and you have a bottle of wine, check it out. Maybe...

I love the wide selection of phos! The egg rolls are yummy. I'm a spoiled baby when it comes to pho so not too many Santa Barbara pho restaurants have blown me away but this place is still pretty good. Not a huge fan of the broth but its a good place to stop. Still recommend to give it a try if you live in SB and you haven't tried all the pho options!

Pho is good and has good amount of meat in it. Broth is rich and flavorful. The service is not that great; can take a while to order but food comes out quickly. The one lady working there always looks so unhappy to work there.

I believe that food is a channel from which we learn about our own lives. When I want to feel inspired, I go to Compere Lapin to eat and to learn. I went for the first time with my girlfriend for brunch and it was incredible. But last night we had dinner and I was truly blown away again. From the moment we walked in, we were treated with a hello and eye contact from everyone. Our server Lyndie was influential, non-invasive, and polite as can be. Her smile and her accent sold us as she described the Hamatchi, Goat Curry, and Jerked Drum. As a captain in the same industry, I learned so much from how Lyndie treated us. I couldn't wait to get to work to give that back. Larry, visited with us and entertained us and went into detail about the details of the restaurant. From the bitters bottles filled with hot sauce served with oysters, to the way our table was helped by multiple staff in the restaurant, I have never felt the way I have felt when I left dinner last night. At a certain point, I got into doubt, "This is all incredible but when will the ball drop?" It didn't. Our final course was Coconut and Mango Ice Cream (I'll take 30 pints), and Chocolate Ganache with Jackfruit. It was out of this world. But what really made it for me was the young man who didn't take care of us but still told us goodbye as we left. That's a feeling you should give to anyone no matter what your field. #RunRabbitRun

This was my first time coming here and it did not disappoint. The food was delicious and the service was good. Everytime I eat at an Indian restaurant, I must order the samosa and nan. The samosa was crispy and was seasoned nicely, the 3 sauces that came with it made it even better! The garlic nan was piping hot and was topped with the perfect amount of herbs and garlic. I was hesistant on what to order for my entree so I played it safe and ordered the chicken tikki marsala. I asked the waiter to make it hot because I love spicy food. Lucky for me, it was spicy but not to the point where I couldn't enjoy and taste my food. The chicken was juicy and there was surprisingly a good amount of it because I couldn't finished and had to packed it to go. I can't wait to eat my leftovers tonight, so what does that tell you?

Went on Saturday evening to eat dosa that was served through non-veg thali. I loved thali especially the goat mutton was cooked so well that it reminds authentic flavor. The thali comes at $ 16.66 and you can order unlimited different types of dosa mentioned in the list. Samosa was also good. And by default they give bottled water which was nice. Ambience is not great, don't expect anything on service but a good restaurant to try out.
Delightful experience. We enjoyed a lot the food. The Pad Thai and the coconut soup are my favorite dishes. The banana and chocolate spring rolls are also amazing. Best BYOB in the area.
Amazing food, literally everything on the menu is amazing. Highly recommend the roast pork and of course pho. They even make homemade soybean drink and sugar cane drink!

This is still our favorite Thai place in Nashville, but we are dropping them down a notch to 4 stars. The last few times we've been the flavor had been slighlty off - less delicate - and on some nights there is only one, dramatically overworked, server for the entire dining area, so service is slow. Come on Siam, step it back up!

Had the crispy chicken and 4 pan fried shrimp dumplings for lunch yesterday and I was horrible. The spicy crispy chicken was anything but spicy. There was hardly any sauce, no spicy and absolutely tasteless. This. Town rice was no better. The dumplings were no picnic as well. Supposed to be pan fried but soggy, confused! Hardly any sear and very bland and the dipping sauce tasted like spicy oil. Crappy lunch for $17 dollars

I went with high expectations based on reviews, service was excellent , food not so much. Rice was to sticky I had ordered la Chuleta Kan Kan which is a giant pork chop. Puerto Rico where they make these although they deep-fry them , the meet is moist but the skin is toasty . Here the hole pork chop was hard over cooked . Flavor wise the beans were a bit "Soso" not very tasty . Very clean good presentation , we may have caught them on a bad day , I definitely see there potential. If you are having a Birthday and you bring your own cake , don't ask for plates because their is a 10$ service charge ! Cleanliness I would give them a 10 Hands down . And for that I would give them a second chance in the future .

wasn't blown away by how good this place is. its close by so thats a major plus. but as far as the food goes, it was nothing super special. its on par with the other main line indian places. i should note that i was VERY disappointed with the portion size for the price. the only reason i would go back here is because its the closest indian place to my house.

I'm a huge fan of spicy. I started out weak but I feel like I have a decent resistance to anything high on the Scoville Scale with the exception of the hottest ghost pepper sauces. I walked into this dimly lit establishment and decided to sit and their bar area. I was craving curry chicken... The place was fairly empty for a Saturday but the Yelp reviews reassured me that this is decent Indian food. The bar tender quickly set me up with the cold Coors Light but I assured him that I did not need a menu. "Curry Chicken, extra spicy...throw in some Naan too". He seemed to hesitate for some reason but none the less put my order in. Shortly after, a gentleman came up to me to clarify that I did in fact ask for this curry to be extra spicy. I confirmed and sealed my fate. I shook hands with the devil. This was some of the spiciest chicken curry I have ever eaten...but not unfairly spicy. I seem to have a problem finding an Indian restaurant that has tender chicken but this place got it right. Each bite was a fiery inferno of deliciousness. I chatted for a little while with someone who seemed to be the manager. He told me about how they grow their own chilli peppers and some other ingredients as well. Oh, and the naan was fluffy and perfect for dipping. I haven't eaten Indian food too many times unfortunately but this place ranks up there as some of the best I've had.

This sushi place is the best! They have great drink specials and the food is amazing! We love the sushi here and the udon soup is great. My mother is a vegetarian and she loves the options they have. And The staff is very welcoming and quick! We live around the corner and we were so happy to see them reopen after their renovation. The patio is very modern and adorable! This is def the best sushi near Lenox village!

Olio is a St. Louis gem nestled away in McRee. Originally a Standard Oil Filling Station from the 1930's, the building has been retrofitted into a small, cozy wine bar that has a timeless, comfortable feel. Whether you are in the garage or bar room, both are a great atmosphere to relax, enjoy your company, and drink really good wine from a thorough selection.

Lovely Atmosphere! We ordered a bit of everything! Presentation was on point! * Small bites - Spiced Pig Ears * First - Marinated Shrimp/Roasted Jalapeño Jus & Pork Belly Croquette * Second - Duo of Beef/Parsnips/Shitake Mushrooms/Foie Gras & Ricotta Stuffed Pasta/Truffle/Granny Apples * Desserts - Honey Panna Cotta/Grapefruit/Pinenuts & Roasted Banana Zeppole/Rum Caramel * Drinks - Moscow Mule Okay, so the pig ears are now a favorite, so tender yet crispy! The marinated shrimp app freshness paired nicely with the fried dishes we ordered. I obviously love my pork, but the pork belly croquette was very different.. Maybe not my cup of tea? Oh and you get warm fresh biscuits with butter, yum! Our entrees were very tasty! The duo beef (sirloin and short beef rib) was cooked to perfection! The sirloin served at a medium rare and the braised caramelized beef rib were both topped with shaved foie gras in front of you. The flavorful parsnips puree and shitake mushrooms gave balance to the dish. Now to my favorite dish of them all, the ricotta stuffed pasted with TRUFFLE - melts in your mouth goodness! The small chunks of apples add a touch of sweetness that makes this dish just amazing. I recommend the Banana Zeppole for dessert! Similar to a beignet - fluffy and crispy. It had a squeeze of chocolate inside each one topped with powdered sugar. The honey panna cotta was good as well. However, the toppings of pine nuts had rosemary in it so that one bite overpowered the entire dessert. The grapefruit layer was interesting, but was a bit bitter for me. So, the panna cotta alone was good enough for me. Overall, the atmosphere and service was great! I would recommend this place to anyone in town!

Nice little place but the food needs some work. Portions are waaaaay to big. Sandwiches come with no sides. The apps with cream cheese have waaaay to much cream cheese ( I never thought that was possible). I'll be back to try something new. Big winners we had at our table was the Ahi Tuna and Salmon. The Pho was awesome as well. Worth coming back again, I love new independent places in the Florissant area.

Went there Sunday , My family and I all being Greek know what Greek food is suppose to taste like. Hands down the best Greek food we have had here in the USA, Waitress was excellent service was great.

Ok. I'm sure it's supposed to be fine dining but wow it's not good. Tiny overpriced portions and infuriatingly odd in the way it's prepared and served, one item at a time. Three TINY meatballs for like 15.00 or about five pieces of okra for 12.00. Even the "entree" options are barely even enough for one person much less to share with others. One of the vegetables we had was corn. And it was supposed to be a creamed corn but it ended up being more of a sauce. Light brown baby poop looking sauce we referred to as goulash because it looked disgusting and didn't taste like corn. The lamb was served on top of what looked like quinoa but it was some type of strange fat grain but had no taste and a yucky texture. The quail was about the size of the palm of my hand and was greasy with a thick skin. And the cocktails were terrible. The one I had tasted like it had Worcestershire sauce in it. Bleecgh! Short version... Way overpriced. Tiny tiny portions. Food not that good. Sharing tiny portions made it even less enjoyable. Cocktails sucked. No chance I would return. The waitstaff was really nice and the place looks great and there were a few things that were fun like the fact they bring you your check in an old book. That was cute. The appetizer we had of whipped fetters cheese and pita bread was delicious. And the spicy habanero sauce for the meatballs was good and the taste of the meatballs was delicious but they were so unbelievably small!! But those few tiny little details could hardly ever outweigh the bad food and cocktails so over priced.

Well this is my first time. My first impression was nice clean and well lit inside. The ladies were very polite. I order chicken wings with cabbage and Mac&cheese. I really like the Mac&cheese! The chicken and cabbage needed some salt but over all great. I would eat here again

We live almost right beside Remedy, so it's a neighbourhood staple. Best to come first thing in the morning, when it's super quiet, or else you might be hard pressed to get a seat. Remedy did some renovations and expanded their space, and it's honestly beautiful. Their gluten free, dairy free, sugar free options for nearly everything makes Remedy super accommodating for nearly everyone to frequents there. The artwork on the walls are from locals which jazzes up the place, and supports local talent. Also, they make amazing naan bread. I definitely want to try more menu items, especially their butter chicken!
Delicious food and fantastic service! Great for date night or taking people out for a special dinner.
Best soahi in Nashville amazing tempora vry good food parking have free and service be very good I will back here for sure

Literally nothing here is bad. I don't even usually like veggie burgers, but I like theirs! Go earlier in the day if you want to make sure they will still have everything in stock. You can also get burrito or taco fillings put onto lettuce for a salad if you're on a diet.

Best Thai I've had in the city out of the four places I've tried. The service is amazing. The owners are extremely nice and will cater to whatever you need, especially food allergies. I've only had lunches there but have never had a problem with the food taking too long. Since the owner's wife is the only chef, I imagine if it's really busy, it would take a little while but it is worth the wait in my opinion. My favorite dish is the green curry fried rice with shrimp. It's pretty spicy but has a great flavor and the shrimp is always tender. It's a lot of food to eat but somehow I always manage to finish. I've also had the duck fried rice and that's also very good. The papaya salad is my goto appetizer as it has a great crunch and tastes great. They do theirs slightly different than most places as it doesn't have any dried shrimp or fish sauce. As far as I know, it's vegan. Doesn't detract from the flavor at all and I actually prefer it. My coworkers love the crab nuggets. They tend to sell out of those quickly though. The prices aren't too much different than other Thai places. If they're slightly higher, it's cause they're food is slightly better. One day I'll go there to dinner with my fiance and add onto this review.

This is a nice enough place, but I did not find it to be outstanding. I ordered Pad Thai with shrimp. The shrimp were a little overcooked and tough. The Pad Thai was flavorful, but would have been better with the addition of cilantro and lime. I think I've had Pad Thai with pickled cucumber slices, too. This was not bad, but could be improved. I would like to return and try something different.
The food was great, authentic thai food. Very small restaurant, so be prepared for a wait during peak time. Service was fine.

Generally good service, very tasty food, and a really good place to take your vegetarian friends, since they offer basically all of their dishes with a tofu or gluten option. I especially like their eggplant. I'm only giving them 4/5 stars because the last last time I went there with my fiancée, the waiters were really rude to us. We arrived, famished, about half an hour before closing, figuring we'd just get our order as take-out because it was so late. Well, instead of telling us that they were not taking any more orders (which we would have been totally fine with), the waiters just completely ignored us. Literally. We could not get anyone to talk to us, even though all three of the waiters we saw very clearly saw us before retreating into the kitchen to hide. After waiting over 15 minutes, we gave up and left. We ended up going to China Pavilion because it was the first restaurant we came across that was open. We got there right before their closing time, but the waitress there was really nice and straight-off told us we'd have to get take-out because it was almost closing time (which was totally fine with us!), and even gave us hot tea while we waited. It's too bad that that happened, because I'd been going to Meun Fan pretty regularly before then, but couldn't bring myself to go back there for a long time after it did. I've been back once since that time, and the service was ok, but I can't really bring myself to be as enthusiastic about the place as I used to be. Nonetheless, I'm giving them 4/5 stars, because they do have the best Thai food I've had in SB, and my experience with them other than that one time has generally been good.

So I have figured out how to get the best chicken rice bowl at Naf Naf grill. To begin with.. you don't order the rice bowl.. you order the salad bowl. That begins with a nice bed of crisp romaine lettuce. From there add the chicken shwarma, and then the cucumber/tomato salad and the cabbage. (Optionally you can add pickles and onions but I didn't). Then ask for the garlic suace which is a more flavorful version of the halal guys white sauce, and ask for the s'hkug on the side. (They have hotter sauces too for those of you who like to like the world or your mouth on fire.) But wait you say, where is the rice? Here is the key. They offer upgrades that include a drink and a side dish. Get the rice as your side dish. When you get to your table, simply dump the rice into the salad bowl and voila. You have a great rice bowl using better ingredients than the halal guys, and lots of flavor to boot! Now it will cost you a bit more, but believe me the price is worth it.

Out of my five long years in Edmonton this place is one of the (very) few things I REALLY miss about the city, other than the wonderful people. I sometimes have dreams about the chai lattes, no joke. Oh, the chai, the chai.... how I miss that delicious elixer of chai-y goodness. I have hunted high and low in many other cities across Canada for something that remotely approximates the magic that is Remedy chai. I have not found it. So yes, Remedy chai is amazing (both soy and milk versions). And the dahl. And the samosas. And the vibe. Love the crowd here. Sometimes I consider hopping on a plane back to E-town just to get a fix. And that's saying something.

Found this restaurant while out at the beach. Was very impressed by the decor and cleanliness of this restaurant. Does not smell like curry when you walk in. The service is excellent and the food gets 5 stars. They offer a buffet or you can order off the menu. My family had the buffet and enjoyed the various choices. I ordered off the menu and my food was cooked fresh to order and was very tasty.
Delicious. Great service. Clean atmosphere. If I lived here I would visit frequently!

Kao soy was basically curry water soup with no flavor. I didn't get asked what spice level I wanted. Service was the absolute slowest I've ever received. No sense of urgency. They couldn't figure out how to split the check. Everyone working there was old and slow(no offense). But it was bad. Just horrible awful service with mediocre food. I'm done with this place for good. Don't waste your time. Go to king and I instead. They never disappoint.

At one time, this place was the only game in Town, for Thai Food here in Brandon Florida. Of course, there were always better Thai restaurants, and they were either in Tampa, or Lakeland. But, food here WAS reasonably priced, and 1/2 way decent. Pad Thai was always 6.95 here for lunch, your choice of Chicken or Shrimp. We stopped here a few hours ago, sat down, and asked for a Lunch Menu. To our surprise, the lunch portion of Pad Thai has increased in price from 6.95 to 8.50, but wait, it gets even worse. Shrimp Pad Thai is now a dollar extra. That brings the price of a lunch sized serving up to 9.50 a person, not including drinks or tip :( Service was fast and friendly, until I started questioning the owners prices. First, he basically called me a Liar when I told him I used to get the Pad Thai WITH Shrimp for 6.95 on the lunch special. But when I asked him if he was calling me a Liar, he said "That was long time ago". Thanks, but no thanks, we got up and left. We drove up to the Thai Boat Restaurant on Parsons here in Brandon. They do not offer any Lunch Specials, but we got heroic sized plates of Shrimp Pad Thai, absolutely loaded with Shrimp, for the same price as Ploy Thai wanted for a smaller lunch "special", w/o Shrimp.

This is our go-to spot in town for Thai. In fairness, we live right around the corner. But the staff is super friendly and the owner is too. She always remembers us, even if it's been a while. I've tried probably 40-50% of the menu and have never been disappointed. And it's inexpensive!

This place is a mess. Literally. If you like slop this is it! They just slop your plate/pita & douse it w/ liquid so by the time it gets to the end of the sandwich line it disintegrates in your hands in about one minute. It smells like it might be good if you eat it IMMEDIATELY, but if you go get a drink & walk to your car... it's over. Gone. Also, I don't know how it's possible to wrap a sandwich upside down, but it happened. Maybe they are left-handed handling pitas.
Always good food, yea I know it's at a gas station, but hands down one of the best PHO places around. Try #43 , you will be pleasantly surprised.
A notch above food court Asian grub. Having tried it once, I won't be back for another go.

When this first opened it was wonderful. The service was outstanding and the food was fabulous. However, something has changed. The crew that worked at the restaurant to open it is no longer around and the people who are working there now don't seem to understand restaurant service. Really unfortunate. The vibe of being greeted by name and having your favorite naan combo delivered without question was wonderful. Now you have to hope they remember you're at your table...

As others have said, the owner of this place, Hassan, is what tips it over into being a 5-star place. He closes at 10pm, but my brother and I got there at 9:55, and he stayed open for us. Was honest with us about which lassi options were the best, and gave us extra tastes in little cups of the flavors the other got. I got the coconut lassi, and he got the blueberry lassi. Both very good and very fresh. He also gave us a free small order of chaat when he heard we'd never had it. The chaat was good, but we were even more impressed by how nice he was. Definitely hit this place up.

W. O. W. !! This is it. Our go to Thai spot. And they are open later than anyone. Thank GOD we decided to retrace our steps to a place we used to frequent as a food trailer attached to the side of a once abandoned building. The food? A 5+. Friendly? 5+ the portions? 5+ the price value? 5+. They should change the name to Thai 5+. A small,quaint and comforting dining area with tables outside as well. I love lil mom and pop dives like this one. Plastic silverware and dishes but what comes in those dishes? Delicious! I had the pineapple seafood red curry and what??? It has crabmeat in it? That's a first! Fresh shrimp scallops just the right sweetness and spice! The Tom Kha soup was perfection! The girls were so nice and accommodating. This will be our go to place for Thai from now on.

I've had three meals there over the past few months and never been disappointed. The food is excellent and service very good. On my last meal, I brought a friend who had lived in Pakistan for decades to get his reaction. He loved it. I've stayed with curries of various degrees of spice, all were excellent. Parking is easy.

I have eaten at most of the Pho joints in the city, and also nearby in Marlton, Cherry Hill... Pho Hoa is my favorite, (even though it is a chain) because the broth is the most flavorful. They also are generous with the lime, which makes a difference. Service is friendly and fast, and the Pho is very hot. I give it five stars with Pho 75 in Chinatown coming in 2nd.
Finally found my pho place! I have tried almost everything on the menu ans its never a dissapointment. Highly recommended!

As much as I love living in South Philadelphia, I'll be the first to admit that we're seriously lacking in terms of having a variety of ethnic food. I love my tacos and burritos as much as the next person, but my major weakness is Middle Eastern/Mediterranean food. Thus, when I succumbed to curiosity and checked out Bitars, I was in heaven. That was about a year ago, and I haven't stopped going since. Bitars is a very unassuming place, despite the burgundy exterior and hookah-filled window. When you first enter it, it's almost hard to notice that it's both a market and a restaurant. That being said, the atmosphere is very cozy and reminds me of some of the places I went to get food in Israel. The store aspect of Bitars offers a wide variety of fresh and delicious products at a way better price than the supermarket conglomerates. The middle contains bins of fresh, delicious, and fluffy pita bread of all sizes; the coolers offer home made hummus, baba, tabouli, falafel, grape leaves, juices, delectable feta cheese and olives; and the shelves house a variety of spices and herbs that normally cost a bajillion dollars at Acme but are extremely reasonable. On top of that, they also have a dessert case that offers some of my favorite baklavah and halvah of all time. I'm not exaggerating in the least when I say that I was here religiously once or twice a week when I lived at 9th and Tasker buying their hummus, tabouli, and desserts. It's absolutely phenomenal. The grill part of the restaurant is equally as good. They offer a really good amount of both vegetarian and meat sandwiches, as well as delicious and big salads. I personally recommend the falafel, although you really can't go wrong with anything there. They are also willing to customize a bit so your sandwich or platter becomes exactly what you want. Unfortunately, it's probably better to get your food to go because it really only has two small tables in an already small room. Bitars really is one of the best gems that South Philadelphia has to offer. Their food rivals some of the bigger names in Middle Eastern cuisine, and their market selections give you the opportunity to create your own versions of traditional favorites. The owners have created a gold mine and you'd be doing yourself a disservice to not check it out. Seriously.

Their sage brown butter sauce with cheese ravioli has been a favorite dish for years. At $15 it's a steal, plus in the new location, it even feels fancier. Not many modern, seasonal, hotel restaurants where an unbelievable entree is less than $20. The raviolis are pillow soft and the crispy sage topping adds perfect texture. I had happy hour there this week. $5 local wine and beer, plus a $5 bartenders choice drink of the nite. $3 got us the most amazing house made potato chips I have ever had, lightly truffle oiled and perfectly salted. Served with a fry sauce. We recently went to a weekend brunch, a new service since the location move. I wanted to try everything on the menu. I stuck with the scrambled egg sandwich, with gruyere and spinach. It was fantastic, on a super soft focaccia bread from ACME. My husband had the polenta and sausage, which he also loved. Can't wait to return for more! The service is friendly and attentive.

First off it's no longer a Thai restaurant but the sign is still up. Very deceitful. We order fish and chips. It took over 40 minutes to cook. The cod was BLAND and served with white vinegar. It had been frozen. The salad was wilted and the fries were frozen steak fries. Horrible service and outrageous prices I wouldn't give it a star at all. Warning do not go there. They need to go out of business. The worst ever and i am not exaggerating
the 2 stars aren't for the food (a so-so banh mi sandwich) but because of the surly service I received... excuse me for bothering you - it won't happen again

Excellent thai food, far better than anything else I have had in the area, including Thai Orchid. Nice setting in downtown Lansdale. All the food I have had has been very good - the duck curry is my favorite. Service is pretty mediocre - servers are disinterested. I don't expect too much from a thai restaurant but they could improve on it a bit. Portions aren't huge but I think they are reasonable for the price. But overall a great place.

We went to this place after we heard it was owned by the same owners as the Pho place near the Target. We love the Pho place, and this place is just as good with an even bigger menu and friendly staff. Had the ramen -- was big and very good. Wife had vegetarian pho -- also a winner. Friendly staff. Will be back.

Tasty traditional Thai dishes in the middle of Chinatown. I've had the veggie pad thai and the veggie red curry. Both were very good! Prices are decent as well. I can't wait to try more things next time.
We get lunch here every Saturday. Delicious food! The potstickers are amazing and I love the spicy chicken Caesar sandwich. If you haven't been you should try it out.

Such a great West Philly staple. The owner is so wonderful... It should be called Good Mood Cafe. The chaat in itself will put you in a good mood. But then there's the samosas and lassis and the flat out experience.. Freakin awesome. Thanks for being a great local business!

Came here to our anniversary dinner loved the food and the service nice atmosphere that put you somewhere else for an hour. Highly recommended the food if you like a different kind of food. Now I'm here a week later to eat again. Love it you must try.

I've been going to Palace for ten years now and nothing compares. Granted I only go for the lunch buffet but it is an absolute fact that Asia's various dishes are more divine than the many arms of Ganesh. Their vegetarian Korma is perfection meeting the dance floor of my tongue. Sad that the "Joes" are moving back to India soon. Been waited on by them for years now. We will miss you. Love you Guys !

By far some of the best Indian food I've ever had. The wait staff has impeccable service and they are very friendly. Most importantly, each dish is flavored with the perfect spices. All dishes can be made at your request of spiciness. Perfect for a date night or group dinner!

Atmosphere was great but all the tables were full and food took 45 minutes to come out. We were told Naan came with our meal but ended up having to order it after it did not come out with our food and was not included in the meal. My chicken tikka masala only came with rice so I was disappointed after waiting so long. You must make a reservation and not be in a hurry to eat to enjoy your time!

Decor and ambiance did not match the name. This is a local bar trying to be different and failing badly. American 70's hit music in a Cuban bistro? Really!? Table cloth had stains. No Cuban beers on menu. Only Cuban mixed drink is the mojito. The menu was no different that what I would expect from Chipotle. I ordered the burger. Ordered my burger medium. Got a piece of charcoals. I couldn't finish it. My daughter ordered a "cuban sandwich". She left half on the plate.
Awesome food! My favorites are salty spicy shrimp, udon, and so many other good dishes... love Sang and Fiona! Great wonderful people! We followed them... ;)

So...it wasn't bad. That being said, it wasn't good. The drinks were strong but poorly executed. The nachos were good but nothing to rave over. One of our party ordered Mahi and got salmon in its place, when asked about it the response was "we are substituting the swordfish with salmon, you're server should have let you know" like, what?! The Ropa vieja was delicious but nothing I couldn't have done in a slow cooker with a can of del monte. Chicken fajitas were good.

A human does not need to sell THEMSELF as that is not an act of self respect. As long as the Food is yummy and a suitable atmosphere is offered requiring someone become your "friend" is a demeaning request to make. Social customs vary from place to place and an ethnic restaurant which seeks to be authentic should retain the customs and comfort of the proprietors and the staff.

I was looking for a healthy dinner option and found Seasons Cafe across the street from Target. The menu had lots of options and an amazing assortment of Boba tea. I ended up ordering the fresh spring rolls and the green papaya salad with their green tea. I asked about the spice levels for the salad, being advised that mild would be "one pepper" and medium would be "3 peppers." I chose two pepper strength and am glad I didn't go hotter! It was fresh, delicious and super spicy. I like spice but this one actually built in heat so I had to take a few breaks. The spring rolls came with a peanut dipping sauce and even extra peanuts. The green tea was lightly sweetened and the perfect strength. This small, hard to find cafe was worth all the turning around I had to do to get to it. If you are looking for fresh, healthy, and quality Vietnamese food, check out Seasons Cafe and Bakery!

I ordered a Greek salad for take out. It was very fresh, great quality ingredients and was flavorful. Great dressing. Great quality tomatoes. My one critique keeping it from 5 stars is the $1-2 overpriced for serving sizes. It was $9 pre tax and tip for a salad with two small pita triangles. It would have been nice to have a full pita without having it order one on the side for an additional $2.

Don't be discouraged by the hole-in-the-wall nature of this place! We have walked past it several times and discounted it (unfairly) due to it's small nature. Because of Yelp reviews, we decided to give it a try (and have now had it three times in the past week!). It's delicious, affordable, and super convenient being that you can order online. Be warned, the medium spice is still very spicy (but delicious!). We've always taken our food to go since we live close and the seating at the restaurant is limited, but every time I've gone to pick food up, there have been people sitting as well as a steady stream of people picking up.

Great large menu with lots of choices. Fun bubble tea flavors! I loved the crab and chicken rolls appetizer as well as the lemongrass beef. Both were very tasty. The noodle bowl I got was okay. I'll order a different main dish next time.

the lunch buffet here is very solid. i was pleasantly surprised by the amount of vegetarian options! usually i find buffets are half meat half veg, but this was like 75% veg. i don't know if i just caught them on a veg heavy day, but i loved that. there was so much to try! all the food was super tasty. i'll definitely be back.

Take out. The food was ready in 15 minutes. The Thai basil stir fry with chicken was very watery, too spicy, not flavorful. There was so much liquid in the dish that my side of rice was not able to soak everything up. This is not what I expected to see. It was spicier than I expected as well - on the phone the restaurant said it was a little spicy. I think the extra spice hid the fact that the dish was not flavorful. It was almost as if the stir fry was done half heartedly and then water was added after the fact. Maybe with another dish or dining in the food quality would be better. I'm willing to give this place another try but I was not impressed with what I had.

My bf and I had a groupon for $25 worth of thai food at Erawan, and I was really excited to try it. It's in chinatown right around the corner from greyhound, and if you blink you may miss it. They share a building with an insurance company, so my bf almost walked right past. The food was delicious. I had mung bean noodles with shrimp in a stone pot. My bf had mango duck. GET BOTH AND SHARE!!!! PS it's BYOB and they will provide ice buckets and uncorking gratis :) Now for the reasoning behind my 3 stars..... The couple next to us was getting ready to pay their bill, and all of a sudden the waitress told them that they could not use it because they ordered from the "chef's specials". When we walked into the restaurant, there was a sign up saying "Groupon: please let your server know before ordering". If ppl are expected to show they're groupon to you beforehand...you need to tell them what is not included BEFORE they order! They brought this to the head waitresses attention, and she let it go.....but not before she had a mini-argument with them. Apparently it was in the fine print.....but the "chef's specials" were not labeled. How the heck would they know what the insert was supposed to be with no labels??? I told her my mobile app for groupon does not show the fine print, so they should let ppl know and she proceeded to argue with me. I hate when ppl have smart mouths in any capacity that involves me paying....I'm paying for this food.....respect please? Bottom Line: Food delicious, one "rude-ish" waitress. Yummy food....but a bit pricier than I expected (sans groupon). PS the coconut soup with seafood. OMG. I might go again for that alone and just get take out lol

Came to CL on a weekend trip to New Orleans and was very pleased with my experience. The interior is inviting and warm, the service was exemplary, and the food was wonderfully prepared and presented. The curry goat dish was a highlight. My server, Claire, was incredibly attentive and we were definitely in great hands. The team was very knowledgeable and learned a thing or two about Madeira's. Damn fine hospitality. Definitely coming back.

I'm writing this review because I have a huge craving for an egg and cheese right now. I'm a Penn alum from several years back, and a day of studying/cramming for an exam would always start off right with the perfect blend of the egg, cheese, and hot sauce on a toasted roll. I wish I could get one now, but I've unfortunately moved to the west coast and can't quite make it over. Definitely the best place to get breakfast around there. Can't wait to make it back! Their cheesesteaks I can still remember as well. They are on the dry side. This place is where I went for breakfast only.

Since I recently had a small lifestyle change that precludes my driving out to Himalayan for my weekly Indian Lunch Buffet treat, I started going to Devi in Exton. While I like Devi a lot, they have been victims of their own success and lunch on the weekends can be very crowded and loud. Further, I have missed the spiciness of the food at Himalayan that just isn't present at Devi. Also, Devi is always lackadaisical in replenishing the bread, which is an annoyance. Long story short, we decided to try Taste of India. And we are very glad that we did! Their lunch buffet offers more selections than Devi, is kept well refreshed, and the food is excellent and lively! 2/3 of the buffet is Vegetarian and on weekends they have 2 types of breads and 2 soups, as well as salad, desserts, labni, pakoras, samosas, and a compliment of excellent entrees. The staff is pleasant and the interior, while generally kept on the dim side, is clean and nicely decorated. They offer a broad and equally delicious full-service menu for night-time dining. Taste of India is now our new "go to" place for Indian Buffet Lunch and the guests that we've brought have been as happy with the place as we (and have returned to prove it). Located in Fairfield Shopping Center in Exton in the corner between Giant and Ross, parking can be a bit distant depending on what time but there are always spaces. Their prices for buffet are currently $12 weekdays and $13 weekends. See Also: Devi: http://www.yelp.com/biz/devi-indian-restaurant-exton#hrid:HAWnuDFWjN3piH6HTxQ5-A Himalayan: http://www.yelp.com/biz/himalayan-exotic-indian-cuisine-malvern#hrid:Ah0OAxmaZRNWNDg9JmY_fA

I came here for the first time based on a recommendation that it was the best Greek food in the city. We had reservations during prime dinner time during the week but was running about 45 minutes late given traffic after work. The hostess was flexible with us and was able to keep our table, so when we arrived we were seated immediately. That was a nice accommodation. We ordered the lamb dumplings and the hummus for our appetizers. To be honest, the dumplings tasted like something I could get at a Chinese restaurant but they were pretty good and the spicy sauce was very tasty. We liked it so much we dipped the bread they provide in it. The hummus was also very good but not enough pita bread is provided given the amount of hummus you get. So we asked for a few pieces of pita bread to finish the dish but found out when we got the check it was $3 extra, so that was disappointing. For our entrees we ordered the lamb stew and Greek meatballs. Both had good spices and had a variety of vegetables in them. The meat for both dishes was tender which was another plus. The lamb stew was a pretty big portion and they didn't skimp on the lamb. The one significant downside of our experience was the customer service. Our waiter hardly checked on us and never made eye contact when we tried to get his attention. We found that he was actively waiting and checking on other tables so that made it frustrating. It took about 20 minutes before we were able to wave him down to get the check.

The food is to die for and the prices are great! There's always a special and I've never been disappointed with anything I've gotten. My only con would be the neighborhood... it can be kinda dicey, so I'd only recommend coming here for lunch.
Great food! It's very busy during the lunch hours and they are kind of short on staff! But visiting again is worth for the food! Would love more if they have lamb instead of beef!

I frequent this restaurant often! the Food, and Environment is Amazing. The Owners treat You with the utmost Respect and Loyalty. The Food is top notch, and rather affordable, especially when compared to other Thai restaurants. I highly recommend this place... Enjoy!

I've been a few times when they first opened. Food was good not great but good enough for me to return. The wait is ridiculous and that's why I stopped going for like a year.. Went today and ordered cheesesteak rolls and beef egg foo young. They changed the cheesesteak rolls. It was mushy inside and it was some type of pasty sauce and onions. Not a piece of steak at all. I cut open my 2nd roll because I wanted to examine it and again no steak. The it had a chicken bouillon flavor. So weird didn't want to finish it. The beef is the egg foo young was tough and flavorless.. The egg part was also mushy. I normally eat at the Chinese store across from overbrook hs but they are a cash o my establishment. I didn't have any cash on me. Their food may not be halal but their food is 10x's better. Not going back to Chan halals again... waste of my time and money. Now I'm sitting here hungry.

If you like Korean food, then this is a good restaurant. I took some friends here to try it and they liked it a lot--they kept eating off of my plate! I think my favorite entree is the bulgogi. They have several different types of kimchee that they serve with it. I will say that this restaurant is a little unpredictable however. They hardly ever serve me the same side dishes or relishes with my bulgogi. I suppose it is based on what the chef has prepped in the back. Admittedly, I feel as if I haven't had the full Hangook experience because I haven't had the big family style serving of dishes the way Korean restaurants serve it. It's looks great on the other tables, though. lol. If you go, try the bulgogi and enjoy.

I was not greeted when I walked in. The customer service was not the best, they got my order wrong, I asked for a certain type of noodle and they gave me the wrong kind, when I asked them to fix it they made me take out the noodles myself and put the new ones in. There was also a small spider on my table as well there was also a number of flys flying around me as I ate. But the food was exceptional.

Marrakesh is an amazing experience and unique place to dine with a large group. I had reservations for 14 people and they attended us with no hiccups. All of the courses served were delicious and incredible! The house arak was really good as well. I highly recommend this gem of a restaurant to anyone who wants to a a unique, tasty and entertaining experience with their friends.

some good food. got the butter chicken. the masala has great taste, however the chicken was a bit chewy and stiff to eat. husband got the non veg Thali which he seemed to enjoy. had some great spice to it as well. try the bhatura, was so fresh and delicious! would eat here again

Yum! I was here today for the lunch buffet. I can tell they turn the spice level down a bit, which is understandable, being in the suburbs, but overall, every item was delicious. They make the best gulab jamun I have ever had!

Pork belly tacos. Do yourself a favor and get them. Vietnamese pork tacos. Do yourself a favor and get them. That's all I ate and I have no ragrats. Little sister had the kimchi burger which smelled yummy! She said it was a little salty but it's kimchi so it's to be expected. Her friend got the fried rice which was good too. Fried rice is fried rice but I'll would order it again from Mint! Waitress was great, she checked up on us and brought out drinks and food out right away - which is a big plus for me. Our server, Julie, was like our very own butler! Food is top notch, service is top notch! I would come here again most definitely!
Great food, especially the fig sandwich and the Brussels sprouts, but it's definitely a little pricey for what it is. The ambiance and the service were both excellent.

This is the perfect name for this place...every time I walk in I'm greeted with tons of smiles :). Seriously love love love Smiley's! The food is super fresh and delicious and most importantly it's consistent. The Greek salad is really big and really yummy. Top it off with some chicken and your belly will thank you for it. The hummus, baba ghanouj, grape leaves, and warm pita are all on point! Recently I read a tip about the beef gyro platter and I'm so happy I did. It's definitely going to be a new go to...you get a little of everything which is perfect! Get your smile on and stop on by :)

This place has INSANE food and the guy working there is ridiculously nice. Everything is reasonably priced and you can request exactly what ingredients you'd like in your chaat. So delicious. Stop dawdling on yelp and go!

People who compare this to fine places in NYC, Philadelphia, and/or San Francisco haven't lived much, IMHO. :-) During a weekday lunch, the place was completely empty most of the time. the waiter/host was monosyllabic, but competent. Tom Ka Gai soup had plenty of chicken and mushrooms, but had zero seasoning and was flavorless. The "drunken noodles" (forget Thai name) that people are raving about was fine, but nothing amazing. Decor seemed OK. Lunch was pleasantly quiet, which was nice, and the place appeared to be reasonably clean.

Pretty good experience. Food was better than expected. Cup for hot tea came or filthy though. Sticky residue all over it. Another gripe was that the dumplings were cold upon arrival. Beef and broccoli was too salty. Would return again though.

From the 3 dishes I've eaten there so far, here are my thoughts: * Great flavors on their stir fries. * The coconut soup was very unique and tasty. * It's very crowded in there so I just get orders to go. * The $13 price tag for dinner dishes seems a bit steep for some chicken and veggies over a bed of rice. * I can't stand when I'm eating chicken and bite into that chewy fat stuff. When I cook at home I cut all that out, but apparently it's not cost effective for eateries to do the same. The quality of meat leaves something to be desired.

I was excited to try this place due to the great Yelp reviews, but I have to say: was underwhelmed. I was concerned that the wait times were almost non-existent -- almost like fast food. That made me uneasy. What of the quality of the food? Just okay at best. It wasn't bad in the least, but I suppose it wasn't what I expected. The green chicken curry I ordered was a lot "soupier" than I am used to, and it looked -- dare I say? -- bland with just bamboo shoots and barely there other veggies. In other Thai places in the city, the green curry is much thicker and brimming with a variety of veggies including mushrooms, giant bell pepper slices and exotic eggplant. This seemed relatively anemic in comparison. I did enjoy the stir fried pork with the garlic pieces, and that was the highlight of my meal. My husband, a giant Tom Yum fan, was gravely disappointed in his bowl. I tasted it, and it was fine to me, but I agree -- it wasn't our favourite, either. Still, the food WAS tasty, just not worth four or five stars, in my opinion. Interior is clean and pretty, service is fast and friendly, but no one came by to ask how our meal was or to top off our water. Don't think I'll be rushing to get back.
good place to eat stay in or take out. the staff is nice and it's clean. the wings are cheap but good definitely get the honey barbecue.

This place is beginning to be a problem for me. It's right on my path, they have abundant vegetarian options that are always amazing, and the prices are totally reasonable. For a while I played it safe and ordered veggie samosas and vegetable biryani. Then I heard about something called Gobi Manchurian, and heard that it was like sesame chicken for vegetarians. Not untrue! Battered and fried crispy cauliflower in a spicy sauce. Really really good. Then I ventured over to the Samosa Chaat, a kind of deconstructed veggie samosa on a bed of seasoned chickpeas with a mildly spicy yogurt sauce. Holy smokes! And finally, tonight I tried the Paneer Masala Dosa--a ginormous crepe filled with curried potatoes and paneer cheese and maybe some shredded white cabbage. It comes with three types of equally delectable sauces for dipping. Delicious! As another reviewer noted, you tip well and/or they see you with some frequency, they throw in a little something sweet for dessert. No charge, friends. No. Charge. The place lacks ambience and may be more comfortable as a takeout scenario, but give them a try. Not far from I95 if your looking for a place to stop that's not McDonald's or Wawa.

What a great find in Spring Hill! Delicious lunch today with great service. My server Dee was very friendly and welcoming. I ordered the Panang chicken mild and it was delicious... It also came with a fried wonton and a Thai wonton soup. Everything was very flavorful. I couldn't pass up dessert, as it sounded wonderful and it was. I got the Bangkok ice cream. Sweet sticky rice with homemade coconut ice cream. Yum! Just do it:). Everything is made to order, so you can have as much or as little spice as you want. I will definitely be back.

Ron's is my family staple restaurant for Caribbean food. We absolutely love the place. The food is phenominal, the portions are HUGE and no matter how long the line, this is our place for the best Caribbean food. We have friends that are Ron's enthusiast and have made it their number one spot. I'm about to order some catering for an aunt in New Jersey cuz she can't stop thinking about the food she had months ago from Ron's.
Vegan mango lassi! Good, but too sweet. Actual food was good, also. It's also very decently priced if I remember correctly.

Haven't been to this truck in some years... rarely downtown at lunch. No menu... no signs... had to be the Falafel Guy. Freshly made falafel with garlic, guy described every topping as falafel fried. Couscous, hummus with poblano, but the most incredible addition... sliced grapes. Taste Perfection. $4.

One of the best meals I have had a NOLA this year. This new restaurant lives up to the hype and anticipation. The marinated shrimp had beautiful complex flavors - none which overpowered the other. I still wonder where they get bonnet peppers in Nola. The Roasted Brussel Sprouts and roasted beets were next level. The hamachi & melon was an unexpected yet perfect pairing. From the hostess to the bus boy the staff was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu and ingredients. The restaurant is in a comfortable space and the crowd was energized and vibrant. I will definitely return
This place is amazing. Tasty soups. Really tasty food. Very reasonably priced
Food was decent but a little pricy for what it was. We could have spent $20 more and ate next door at Delicia! (Which is fabulous if you haven't been!!)

Best Puertorrican food in Tampa. Very authentic. 5 stars are for the food. However, the service can be very slow at times. I highly recommend "mofongo de biftec." It is fantastic. The red snapper "chillo" is excellent as well. For churrasco I would go else where.

Based on 4 bowls of the Pho Tai, we were not impressed. The broth was ok, not as layered and flavorful as I'm used to. The side plates with lime were good except for the lime on two plates: the end pieces with less juice than needed, and the bitter liquid from the rind squeezed out too. But most disappointing was the "rare steak." It was very tough and chewy, not pleasant to eat. Two of our party left most of it in their bowls. One of our party kept casually listing all the pho places she knows that are better, not intentionally slandering this place, but saying what she preferred about other places, which turned out to be everything... Except the egg rolls, which she liked a lot. The Thai tea was good. Best about the experience was the service. All of the girls working there were great, kind and helpful. I'm not going to have the pho again, but will likely come back to try the banh mi.

I heard friends talk about the food here but I just never tried it out bc maybe I was scared maybe I was just lazy bc it is in the county. But man, when I did go the first thing I ordered was the fried tilapia and jollaf rice. It was so good. Came right out.piping hott and so authentic. I thought I had landed in Africa with my first bite. So I continue to come to AP about once a week and I have since then had just about everything on the menu and off. For first timers I would recommend the beef, jollaf rice, and plantains. So good. And I'm telling you once you eat it you will get periodic cravings which you will just have to fill. I really enjoy the place and it really feels like a little family when you walk in. Everyone is so friendly and the staff is pretty great.
Yes I loved it I am a fan of there shawerma. And the falafel sandwich taboly salad to I am not sure if they have the Jordanian mansaf. But I am going to be back for more things to try

So good and cheap. The flavors compete with the best restaurants in the city. My personal favorites are the chicken and sweet potato curry, the short rib taco and chicken satay taco. All are outstanding. When I can make it there I always get 2 tacos to eat for lunch and then an order of curry to put in the drug for dinner. I only wish that I knew about this truck when my office was around the corner in the Cira centre!

My kabobs were really tender and I have never eaten middle eastern food so this was a treat. Since I am not into lamb, I went safe and got chicken and beef. Both were delicious and literally blew my expectations for it. The rice was yellow and tasted like uncle bens rice. The gentleman that helped us was very nice and friendly. I like the atmosphere and how it is set up. Gives a nice middle eastern vibe.

I'd only been for pho twice in my life before checking out this Pho Hoa the other day. For some reason I was mega craving pho over the weekend, so my lovely friend Dianne took me out for some on Monday night. The place wasn't very busy around 6:30pm. The service was quick - tea came out right away and was refilled quickly when needed, and our food also came out very fast. I didn't even look at the entire menu, but skipped right ahead to the pho page. It's cutely split into three categories: pho for beginners, just the regular, and the adventurers' choice. At this point I think the only two things I'm not ready to try are tripe and tendon, so I got the Ph Tái Nm off of the "regular" menu - round eye steak and well-done flank. You can get your pho in one of two sizes, regular or large. I got the regular (I think around $7.50) and it was still huge! I couldn't finish the whole thing. There was a ton of meat in there - too much for me, I had to leave some. The broth was so flavourful and kind of sweet and yum. I'm not a pho expert, so it's hard for me to describe the flavours, but I loved it. So good, hot and fresh. I've been craving pho ever since. Pho.

My husband and I decided to go to this restaurant to celebrate completing a home renovation project. We stood inside the door for approximately 15 minutes while being completely ignored. We tried to amuse ourselves by looking at the wines. Servers and other people buzzed past us without so much as giving us the finger. Finally we gave up and left. We went instead to Earls, a much better-run restaurant. Since I have learned that Parkallen clients apparently are invisible for the first fifteen minutes after they enter the door to this restaurant, I recommend that you use this facility as a washroom rest stop. However, if you want to dine or have a little wine or a celebration, go elsewhere.

Amazing. Worth the wait (30-40 min at 12:30 midweek)--it doesn't hurt to bring some friends to pass the time! But hey, you're coming here for the experience. May want to avoid if you're a picky eater because there's no menu, and it seems like he throws in whatever he feels like that day. The food was so much better and more unique/interesting than the other food trucks around, and tasted really fresh! Looks like he puts falafel in everything, and that falafel was incredible. Go for it!

Oh me, oh my, the Cap'n Crunch-Coated Tilapia Burrito was well worth the walk across the Schuylkill river and the relatively short wait. Because you see the Cucina Zapata food truck is a well-oiled machine: place your order at the window, join the anticipatory crowd, and before you know it, they're calling out your name. I took my lunch over to the seating area of The Porch, outside of 30th Street Station (see, we do deserve nice things in Philly), and this is where the true magic happened. From first bite until last, it's one mighty, mighty fine burrito. The fish is fresh, it stays crunchy, and it melds perfectly with the other ingredients--without a doubt it's a "two thumbs up" burrito.

So it's an old Bob Evans from what I can tell which throws me off a bit. But they have an extensive menu which is very impressive. The wife had hu tieu nam vang which she loved and we also tried their bot CHIÊN which was good, but can't compare to the real thing on the streets of Saigon. Overall a great find with pleasant service (which can be rare when it comes to Vietnamese owned and operated places), fair prices and a wide selection.
This is our fav near by destination for Dosa and Snacks.. Staff r very friendly.. Comparatively small place with good food.. but price is very high..

awesome brunch at Kanella! The French press coffee is so good - not something you see very often. I was looking for something sweet like pancakes or waffles. Unfortunately, their sweets menu did not really appeal to me, so I ordered the Cyprus breakfast. WOW after eating that, I did not miss the pancakes! Everything on this plate was delicious, 2 eggs fried in olive oil where they're still a little gooey...lounza which is kind of like Taylor ham, a delicious tomato salad, bread, and ... the best thing on the plate - halloumi cheese - wow is this stuff amazing?! If you do not get this breakfast, do yourself a favor and order a side of the halloumi. My husband had the lamb burger which was delicious as well. Great place, would love to try their dinner.

Of the many places I've tried in Nashville for brunch, Butcher & Bee remains top of the list. Presentation is a big part of a meal, and B&B does this phenomenally. My date and I sat at the chef's bar and were treated to great service while watching the staff craft each dish with care. The biscuits, bowl dishes, salads, and tapas all looked like pieces of art. Very impressive. We ordered the breakfast burrito (which has been very tasty both times I've been to B&B), the Avocado Rice with Shawarma Chicken which was spicy and delicious, and the whipped feta appetizer which is honestly so good... it's worth returning for just that!! Overall a great brunch with a great atmosphere. Butcher & Bee keeps me wanting more!!
Really didn't like the food here. Wasn't warm at all. I looked like it was leftover food. Very few options to choose from.

I went here for lunch because truth be told I had a free hummus coupon. The food was average. I was really looking forward to some falafel but they did not have it on their menu so I had the veggie pita with a side of rice and hummus. I couldn't figure out why my plate came with potato chips. The hummus and the rice had an overload of lemon. The place is nice, the food is decent but not authentic.

Sunday brunch was very satisfying. Food was tasteful. Portions was perfect is size. I thought I wasn't going to get full when I saw the portions but it was just enough for a big eater like me. It wasn't very heavy on the belly. For me this is the place to go for brunch. Tried the bloodly Mary with spice on it and it was amazing. I have an off the menu food and it was cook perfect. Chef is good. Love to go back!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Taj Mahal is a lovely dining experience, with friendly staff and delicious food. I will be returning for sure.

Basil Spice Thai is a new restaurant that is still working out the kinks, but there are hints of greatness here. The staff was friendly, but seemed a little stressed as they were busy when we went in for dinner. We started with the spring rolls, which I believe have their origins in Vietnam rather than Thailand. Nevertheless, they were very tasty and quickly disappeared. There was nothing new or innovative about them, instead the focus was on perfection of a classic. For my entree I got chicken skewers, and I loved it. There was some spice, but the overall heat was not intense. My palate enjoyed the many layers of flavor of the chicken. The main reason I ordered was the peanut sauce, and it did not disappoint. This meal was delicious. My friend ordered some spicy dish, but it did not bring the bulging eyes and head sweats that some other Thai restaurants do when he orders spicy. I'm therefore wondering if they safe the real spice for Thai customers, if they stray from extreme spice or if his resistance has simply grown over the years. Service time was a little slow, and there was confusion when we had questions about the menu. Still, the staff tried very hard to give us a great experience, and I attribute these very minor flaws to being a new restaurant that has a lot to live up to.

Very nice people, clean and great food. We switch back and forth between here and Pearl Cafe. My husband prefers their pineapple fried rice. They use white potato instead of sweet potato in the yellow curry which is a nice change. I like it both ways so it's nice to have options.

I'm definitely glad the restaurant was there now that we can enjoy a wide variety of Chinese, Japanese, and Thai food. So my mother had the Pad Thai with chicken, medium spice. It is good with the spice factor; not too mild, not too hot. My order was the Chef Special General Tso chicken with the small side of hibachi fried rice. This plate was fantastic and would highly recommend this dish for those who love spicy Chinese food. Fantastic was the food, and we would definitely return to the establishment whenever staying north of Nashville. Hibachi fried rice - recommended side dish for chef's specials. General Tso chicken - nice presentation with decorative broccoli as creativity. Taste is spicy and perfect. PS - Service is excellent, and adding to returning to this establishment some time, I would include that too.

this place was delicious! i went with 3 others and we all shared the cashew chicken, green curry with chicken and seasoned vegetables. we swapped brown rice for white rice ($1 more) and were all amazed! i also ordered a small garden salad before that comes with either ginger or peanut dressing...i ordered ginger and loved it! highly, highly recommend going here. the atmosphere was relaxed, service was great and the food was oh so good!

The food is great and the typos on the menu are endearing - rack of lamp, anyone? They're biggest fault is their inability to handle large parties or more than three or four tables of four. I think there is just one guy in the kitchen and I think they're down to one waitress. They stay open though and as long as they do, I'll be visiting.

The octopus is a must get. I love they offer whole wheat pita and gluten free options (veggies) for dips and such. They also are very considerate when altering orders for dietary needs. Large menu and they are pretty much all great options. Good prices too, the happy hour is great. Warm and laid back atmosphere great for a date or friends. I wish they had another restaurant a little closer to the city :) Regardless. This is a nice option for good food at a good price. There's something for everyone!

Hubby and I have differing opinions on this place. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal, but hubby wasn't so lucky with what he ordered. We started off with the smoked tuna tartare, which was fresh and delicious. Then I ordered the pici pasta with lobster and squash. I loved my dish. It was creamy and rich. Hubby got the curried goat and it was watery and not tasty. He was not a happy camper. More disappointment for him at dessert as he ordered the chocolate cake, which didn't wow him, but I got the delicious zeppole. Don't worry, I shared so he wouldn't be so sad. Overall, not one of the best meals we had while in NOLA, but a fine place to dine. I'd recommend skipping the goat curry, though.

love love love that there is a new indian place downtown! yippee!!! the food is great! a nice selection on the lunch buffet both times I've visited. both veggie and meat lovers will be happy! garlic naan is to die for. nice thick and tasty paneers and masala. great opportunity to try some new dishes such as turnip or cabbage or chickpeas. VERY nice and prompt service. hopefully they're working on atmosphere, but everything else is top notch! don't let the "interesting" storefront from the previous owners scare you off! hopefully I can try something off of the large menu soon, but the buffet is a win!
Beautiful space and great food. The cafe offerings such as coffee and pastries are great, and all the food we've had there are too.

Everyone already knows how fantastic the lassi is. The real sleeper hit is the chaat, which is an incredible mixture of savory and sweet in a single dish. As the owner explains it, it's an Indian/Pakistani street snack that he's adopted and enhanced into a full sized meal. Savory lover? We got that. Walnuts, feta, chick peas, figs, potatoes. Sweet fiend? Mango slices and dried cranberries galore, a few dates for good measure. Want it spicy? He can do a variety of flavorful mouth burners. Vegetarian? All of them can come with an optional vegetarian protein in lieu of the tasty tasty meats. Screw kale, eat more chaat. Or eat both? I dunno, you're a grown-ass man who makes his own decisions, or a grown-ass woman, or a grown ass-woman, hell chaat is totally PG, enrich your kids' palates and stuff and junk and whatever I recommend the salad chaat option for the most efficient meal in history.

What a friendly place! I've never eaten here, but a few of my friends are staple 'weekly members' on karaoke night and everyone here seems to know each other and have a great time. I was reluctant at first as this place is pretty far from my house, but after going once I have to admit I will definitely return on a Thursday to take part in the karaoke/dance party that seems to always ensue. Also- the drinks are crazy cheap, and I'm interested to try the food. Overall, I think this place is great and definitely worth a repeat visit- possibly tonight as it is Thursday.

I have not eaten much Indian food, but my sister took me here while we were in Tucson. She did the ordering, so don't ask what we ate, but it was all really good and now I am looking for a good Indian restaurant near where I live. It was a great place, food and service very good and the prices quite reasonable. Can't wait to get back to Tucson to eat here again!!
Definitely a different twist on falafel that you'll find anywhere else in the city. This guy knows a thing or two about flavors!

I usually go to Petra Express in New Tampa but thought I would try this place since I was in the neighborhood. I thought the food at Petra Express was much better: crispy fries & moist chicken. The fries here were not crispy & the chicken was a little dry. The service at Petra Express is also friendlier & has a better atmosphere. This place was absolutely dead at lunch time. Will not visit here again, I definitely prefer the food, service & ambience at the New Tampa location.

Their smoothies keep getting better and better. I highly recommend the taro smoothie with boba. It's wonderful. Do not go here when it's busy and that is starting to be every evening. My food came out five minutes before my friend's and we finally got a water refill after asking at the end of the meal. I ordered noodles, paid a dollar extra than my friend's, and it was this fried onion thing. Kinda disappointing. I would go back for the drinks though.

Pretty awesome food. Went to try it. I'm a very picky eater when it comes to tilapia based food since a lot of places butcher the fish. The fried tilapia fish burrito was amazing. Definitely a go to for this place. Crunchy, not dry but juicy fillets, and the mixture of the fixins and sauce complimented each other perfectly . Went to try it on a good friday so I wasn't able to taste the short rib tacos. Perfect reason to come back again and see these extremely friendly guys again! Keep it up!

I am in town on business for a week and ended up eating here three out of five days. If you'd asked last week what my favorite meal was I would've thought it was my mom's shepherds pie, or civiche. I now know it is oxtail butterbean stew. I feel like I've wasted years of my life not eating here. The food is amazing, the staff is attentive. The only downside is all beverages are by the bottle or can, not enough to knock out a star when everything else is top notch. Hope to be sent out this direction again soon.

Update... The first time we went here, it was amazing. The second time was a completely different experience. Things definitely went down hill after they had been open for a few months. This time, the food was just okay. We ordered the scallops and they were very overcooked. Definitely not worth the price. Also, the service was very slow. I'm bummed because I loved it the first time. For two of us the bill was well over $100 when an app and a couple drinks were added with entrees. Probably wont go back. Original review: Quite possibly one of the best restaurants in Indy. We tried it for the first time tonight and the food was amazing. The Tamal with Barbacoa was crazy good. Churros for dessert was the perfect end to a perfect meal.

The Blueplate is a dinner that charges upscale restaurant prices. I've been here a few times, always for take out, and always felt disappointed with the food and service. Their cheesesteaks are $10, now that's just silly...and they hardly have any meat on them. With that said, the last time I went to pick-up a take-out order no one would speak to me, I literally had to flag down a waitress after standing there for 5 minutes and the place was relatively empty (mid week afternoon), after flagging her down I was left waiting another 10 minutes without anyone apologizing or telling me what the delay was. As with most places in Mullica Hill I simply don't understand how they remain in business let alone seem to have a loyal following (can anyone say captive audience?). I won't be back.

just like the others said, the wait is long. but boy is it worth it! the seafood is great, the service is a little weird at times but in all in all they were friendly, polite, and they definitely don't rush you out.. that is what i can't stand. i recommend grilled scallops and fried calamari. the reason this place gets 4 stars is because the rice tasted microwaved. i could make better rice at home. and the sides were overly cooked greens identical for the calamari and scallops. if you don't want to wait and can afford to buy booze then go to the non-BYO location near rittenhouse. peace young ninjas, k

I'm slightly more impressed every time I come here. I've waited to make a review based on how my experiences have been. I usually come for lunch or Sunday when I get that craving for something delicious and exotic. It's Mount Juliet so kudos to this place for making a little haven here in our culturally restrictive neighborhood as far as food is concerned. This places impresses you as soon as you walk in. Everything is white and looks very pristine, which at first threw me off for an Indian place, now I've learned to love the bright lights. The Feng shui is definitely balanced in here. Now about the food. It's clean and healthy feeling Indian food. Is that a thing? It must be because they did it. They're ingredients are fresh and you can taste it in everything you eat. The food is delicious and has never been disappointing whether I eat in or get take out. The service is charming and no one is ever rude. And if you ask for suggestions they give it to you. Yes even those new to trying Indian food. It's worth your while. I live in Mount Juliet and I know we have a a lot of Indians in our community which I love. Come to this place for something different. You won't be disappointed.

This was a horrible experience. Although the restaurant was clean and our takeout order was prepared quickly (the restaurant was empty) the food was awful. We ordered Vietnamese spring rolls, beef lo mein and catfish with eggplant. The rolls were supposed to contain shrimp and pork, but there was no shrimp in either, and only one dry, flavorless scrap of pork in each roll. Nothing else but lettuce and rice noodles. My husband couldn't eat the lo mein, and the catfish was so over-cooked, it was chewy. The eggplant was simply inedible. If their goal was to prevent us from returning, they achieved it! We will never go back. Too bad -- we were looking for a nearby good restaurant, and we'll have to keep looking. Frankly, I'd give it no stars, but the site won't let me do that!

Lilly's is hands down the best Pho on this side of the river. I love Lilly herself, always working hard and providing the best service and serving the best food! Have the spicy tofu and the shrimp and beef ball pho. The absolute best!!! Amazing!!!

I'm visiting from out of town, when I saw that this had a Mediterranean theme I thought I'd give it a shot. I ordered the Mediterranean chicken and it was delicious. I didn't feel like a fat pig when I was done. When travelling, it's tough to find places to eat where you feel like you had something good yet full after. I realize now that they are a chain...they seriously need to expand to Connecticut.

The food was fantastic but the service terrible. I understand that there are few workers, which I am fine with, but a smile and politeness goes a long way. The waitress was rude and not accommodating. If you like and/or want Ethiopian this is your only option so grin and deal with the terrible service for the great food.
Very good Indian food after a long time. Location is convenient and decor is not overwhelming too. Good place to go for lunch or even dinner.. lots of choices veg and non veg in buffet.

The food is excellent and their lunch special is a great value for the money. For $9.99 you get a soup and an appetizer or salad plus a full-sized entree. I love feeling like I'm getting a great deal. The decor is really beautiful and the staff is polite and attentive. This is my favorite Thai place in the area. I've never had anything less than a great meal here.

Had lunch here a week ago and had the buffet. On the positive side, the food was flavorful and seemed to be replenished at a good rate. There was a decent crowd and the staff was courteous and friendly. On the negative side, a few of the pans of food were lukewarm at best, and a couple of the dishes weren't the best Indian food I've ever had. But then again, I used to live in NYC and have eaten some pretty impressive fare so I'm using a high bar. Bottom line: I think the buffet is OK and a decent value at $9. I didn't need to eat dinner the night after I had lunch here :-) But don't expect to have a gourmet Indian experience. The decor is a bit tired and the food is not completely authentic, but if you want to fill up on some decent food, then I think it's worth a visit.
Stopped in after a day at the Botanic Gardens. Everything we had was absolutely delicious. Very cool store - cool staff - all around great service.

Went for lunch on sunday. Foods were not as good as before when i visited few years back. They changed the location so I don't know if they changed the cooks too or not. My server never smile and looked upset,seems like she doesn't wants to work.

We were in town visiting from California and were on our way to Thai Lana but found it's odd hours left us standing outside. Still in the mood for Asian food we walked a couple store fronts down to Pho 36 and we couldn't be happier. Good bubble tea and vermicelli, tasty spring rolls. Great prompt service. Go here.
