The buffet station consists of: 2 meat curries (chicken and lamb I think), saag paneer, cauliflower and potato curry (to die for), tandoori chicken, basmati rice, samosas, naan, chickpea curry, 2 salads and freshly made side dips of green chiles and tamarind sauce. Didn't manage to try the dessert...was too stuffed. Will definitely be back once the craving for Indian food comes....which is pretty often :)
Pasta dishes are excellent & I highly recommend the hummus appetizer. I didn't order a steak but the table next to us did & they looked delicious.

Great little place for Vietnamese sandwiches and soups. I've tried both their pho and their bun bo hue (hue beef noodle soup). Was not disappointed. Everything was authentic, tasty with lots of herbs, and most importantly, fresh! The noodle soup dishes are a standout at $8. K&T gives you a lot more than King Wok, Sizzling Wok, or Saigon which are all in the area. The sandwiches are really good but are a bit on the pricey side at $4.25! You can get an entire meal at King Wok or Sizzling Wok down the street for about $5 for weekday lunches.

I have only ever ordered carryout from them. They never miss a beat. From every sauce I may want or need to the napkins and chopsticks. After so many times I am still suprised at the portions. I can eat leftovers for two days after my order. For $13.95 I received a fresh a hearty portion of the Wonder Tony soup with egg noodles and the most delicious egg rolls. You guys are the best. Thank you for all that you do in the industry. You set the bar high.

I really wanted to like this place more. I tried the vegetarian feast and the concept was sound but I wouldn't call it a feast. I got an extra falafel and two pitas with it and I was still a bit hungry. (This was for dinner -lunch would have been fine). The falafels were pretty small - about 1 inch circumference. I'm used to places that offer a little more. The spices were all there for this kind of food, but it still seemed bland. If you're in the mood for this kind of food check it out, but it's not worth a trip to the area just for this place. It's trying to be chipotle meets Mediterranean.

We loved the ambience as we sat outside and enjoyed a nice evening. Our waitress when asked what drinks are good she answered in a short, curt way that she can't pick that sort of thing. When asked if they have any Fall beers she said it's not really Fall yet. It was September. To be fair at the end she apologized and thanked us for being understanding. They strongly encourage you to share plates and we really didn't want to share everything in our party of six. We ended up sharing most of it. The food was fancy, expensive and tasty. I liked the experience but might not come back now that I have tried it.

Food here is delicious! For appetizers we had fresh shrimp rolls, calamari, and chicken satay. For the main course, the Larb pork, massaman beef curry with coconut rice, pad Thai with shrimp. Arrived around 6:30pm and found it empty. It's a small place but filled up with ppl by 7:30pm.
We have been coming this restaurant for over ten years. The food has consistently been great. The staff is nice.
Foodies! It is time to be adventurous. You must try this good Thai restaurant for food cooked and served by the chef and owner. The food was good and authentic.

Excellent Indian food in Clearwater. Dave W. setup a wonderful UYE here, and several Elite Yelpers showed up. We had a good time, talking about travel and food mostly! Thanks to Deccan Spice for a good time, and to Dave for setting it up! The food was very good, we did some family style sharing, and there were a lot of different dishes that were ordered! There was some delicious Lamb Tandoori, Chicken Chendatti, Dahl, Chicken Vindaloo, several different appetizers, and a lot more I didn't get the names of. I had ordered Chicken Korma (Indian hot spice level) and it was on point, VERY spicy... one of the hottest restaurant dishes I have had to date... and it was very good. Normal Korma is not served spicy, but I love it that way. Garlic Naan... was ok, but have had better. Apparently a serving of naan here is one piece of naan... so that didn't last long! The Mango Lassi I ordered was good also, not overly sweet like some restaurants do it... very delicious. Service was good, although there were some hiccups. Some things (Biryani) arrived at the table long after the rest of the food had gotten there... and while Biryani is a time consuming dish to make, I thought it was a little unusual. But it was good Biryani! Location is very nice... nice design and decor. Great time! Good food! Fun yelpers!

Dear sweet yelpers. If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have given this place a second thought. We were looking for someplace different. And I have had an aversion to Indian food since my first trimerster of pregnancy, which was well over two years ago (No, I'm not an elephant. I've given birth since then). But since having an aversion, it wasn't something that has interested me since. I'm not really quite sure where the wild hare came from, but when I saw the reviews, I really wanted chicken makhani, which pleased my husband to no end, since he's been denied Indian food for the last two years. We went in around 6 and it was dead. Like, I heard crickets in the background dead, which made me worried, because I tend to avoid restaurants that are in shopping centers. I know this has no bearing on the restaurant, I'm just an odd bird. At the same time, we dragged the toddler with us, who is still good in restaurants, but you know that people are always staring at you like you're one of THOSE people, but I digress, and I'll shut up now and tell you how mother effing GOOD this place was. Did I say mother effing good? Because, sweet merciful heavens, people.... this place was fantastic. The chicken makhani was so good that I wanted to make it into a makhani flavored breath mint, just so I could have that taste in my mouth, forever and always. The vegetable korma was really good too. The only slight mishap was that my husband was really stoked to have some gulab jaman, but they forgot to put the order in, and by the time the server remembered, the toddler was making us out to be those people. So we didn't get to have any of the gulab juman. But thankfully, we have makhani leftovers. I will say that it does fill up quickly around dinner time, and the restaurant is small, so getting there around 5:30-6 is probably your best bet.
Best freakin' vegetarian Pho ever! Service was great and the food came out fast. I was also reading a book and they didn't make me feel rushed to leave while I was finishing my green tea.

For the price and the amount of food, this place gets 4 stars from me. Definitely not "authentic" Thai food at all. I got pad Thai, and it was kind of watery. My sure why...anyway, this would be a great place for drunk Thai food. They should consider staying open later for those of us who crave Thai food when the clubs close! Honestly, the food wasn't anything special, but you get large portions. My pad Thai ended up being two meals. It's cheap too, I believe around $7 for the entree. No complaints about the service or the ambience.

Just tried Indonesian food for the first time here. Pleasantly surprised both by how familiar (N8 is basically drunken noodles) and new (N1) the food was. Both were very good especially on a gloomy day - comfort food at its finest. Our total came out to $16 including tip. What a deal. We'll be back!

I'm eating vegetarian for navratri, and I figure what's a good place for vegetarian.. Indian! How can it go wrong. I ordered vegetarian biryani-- it was not good. Greasy and bland. I also got paneer tikka pakodas-- tasted like paneer nuggets. Also bland. Eh.

Absolutely amazing . . . To say the least. My only complaint is that I wish I had found it sooner as I am in town for business and definitely would have ended up eating here almost every single day!! Walking in the door, the atmosphere was great. Immediately I was greeted and provided a comfortable environment to enjoy great tasting food. As I sat at the bar, I was impressed at the attention I received by Kirsten despite her impressive multitasking ability to take care of everything else happening at the bar at the same time. After hearing her dinner suggestions, I leaned to the guest next to me and asked for her suggestions - immediately she said everything was amazing and was surprised to hear this was my first time. I ended up with the Chipotle Chicken Pizza and was delighted beyond belief after tantalizing my taste buds with their hummus trio appetizer. If I could, I would have tried everything on their happy hour menu, but decided my figure should stay in check - but not enough that I couldn't pass up take home carrot cake. Overall I was very impressed and would suggest Pita Jungle to any and all!! Healthy but very tasty too.

We love this place however tonight on our anniversary my husband ordered the ribeye. Five minutes later he got a menu shoved in his face telling him they were out of it. The guy next to us ordered the same thing AFTER him and got it. Terrible terrible service. We ordered first, he should have been the one eating steak not sitting here with a sad order of gnocchi. Never again

What a great culinary experience for someone wanting to step out of their comfort zone. The ingredients and eating style might seem too exotic, but GO, seriously. All the dishes we had were so tasty, try their sampler dinners to get a real enjoyment of all the flavors. ALSO, don't miss out on their traditional coffee, I'm telling you...don't miss it.

Eating with your hands? Sharing Food with friends? A belly dancer? BYOB? STOP! I cant take this much excitement! We got together to celebrate my husbands 31st birthday and I wanted to take him somewhere different and exciting. Insert Marrakesh, a little Morroccan spot right off of South Street. When we got there, we were invited to wash our hands as a group and were given towels for our laps as there are no utensils given. I love the atmosphere, the music and if you go with open minded people who don't mind close quarters and sharing a meal, you will enjoy it. The Food.... OMG The Food! For starters we had the salad trio, which was tomatoes and cucumbers, carrot salad and eggplant which came in on the expressway from heaven! It was delicious! The second course was the Phyllo dough stuffed with egg and chicken topped with powdered sugar. I was not a huge fan, but everyone else loved it. The third course was a whole chicken with olives and various spices, well seasoned and falling off the bone. Fourth, we enjoyed lamb and almonds in a honey sauce, and of course they kept the flat bread coming. The fifth course was couscous and chicken with potatoes and carrots, and the sixth course was a bowl of fresh fruit. LITERALLY. The followed it up with mint tea and baklava for all. During the meal, a belly dancer came out and each of us took turns dancing with her, having a great time. The staff was friendly and because it was our first time, they took the time to explain the entire "Marrakesh experience". My only complaint, is that they need to have a Vegetarian option. We had one vegetarian in our midst and they brought out a spinach pie for him during the chicken course, and they brought him hummus and chips during the lamb course, and they made a plate of couscous without chicken for him, which was nice. However, if they come up with 6 truly vegetarian dishes patrons could still have the Marrakesh experience without meat, while TRULY sampling Moroccan style food. Just a suggestion. 6 people 6 courses costs $192.00...( plus the cash we gave to the Belly dancer) NOT BAD.

Very good food for a good price. Long wait time during peak hours ~ 11:30 AM - 4/5 PM and tends to sell out the special very fast. Worth the wait, good experience, nice people. You can get the short ribs and chicken satay over rice too. You can ask for the food in anyway you want: burrito or over rice and can mix and match for additional cost.

The worst Thai food I have ever had. Ordered masaman curry and the potatoes were raw. Took about 40 minutes to get our food. Our plates even came out over 15 minutes apart. The chicken pieces were disgusting and looked like they were hand picked from the carcass.
Banh mi extra spicy...yum. owner gave us a sample of their roasted potatoes and a piece of orange chicken while we waited. Not bad. Want to try their pho now that its chilly outside. Thanks yelpers!

Amazing restaurant that can make anything. We are extremely picky and health conscious, basically we are a waiter/cook's worst nightmare. But the great team at Singha was able to create some menu items for us that not only fit our annoying requests, but tasted amazing AND they did it all with a sincere smile on their face and real concern to make sure we were happy! Oh and the presentation of the dishes were beautiful as well. For a great meal, thats served quickly and fairly priced, Singha Thai is a perfect option. This has got to be one of our new favorite neighborhood restaurants.
Delicious! We had the lunch specials, which were a great value, including soup, appetizer and entree. Wonderfully seasoned! Nice portions. Cant wait to go back!

Went with a friend around 12pm for lunch. I got their #11 Pho Tai ($7.95)and their Thai tea with boba(around $2, I don't remember quite what the price was), friend got vegetarian fried rice($7.75). The place was a little claustrophobic, tables and counters were greasy. Mostly two and four seaters. Chair cushions punctured and not wiped. The pho broth was pretty watered down, a lot less flavour than there should have been, but all in all it was just the right amount of noodle for lunch. The beef wasn't anything special but it wasn't terrible. Distinct lack of bean sprouts. Friend's fried rice was unevenly salted. The portion was big enough that he couldn't finish; got take-away. According to him it was a little bland. From my end of the table, definitely did not look like it was worth 8 bucks. The Thai tea was actually quite good, but their boba was hard(undercooked, not old) and not sweet once bit into. Get your drinks without boba, or perhaps go later in the day so it's had more time to cook. It seems like they begin to cook the boba when they open up at midday, rather than cooking it during their prep time.

I'm a huge fan of Vietnamese food and was thrilled to find a great place close to home (we usually frequent Vietnam Restaurant/Cafe the city). We had several excellent experiences here however we ordered takeout tonight and I have to say, I was not impressed. Ordered the pork vermicelli...cold noodles, brown lettuce, no pickled carrots. The meat was still flavorful but everything else was very bland. Made me wish I ordered my usual pho. It makes sense now that I'm reading that there's a new chef. So disappointing! Won't rush to order from here again.
Love, love, love this place! Delicious food and the family that runs it is so friendly and hard working! My favorites are the summer rolls with yummy peanut sauce and pad thai of course!

I've done takeout here a few times an everything has been damn good and the spice levels have been just right. I was impressed with the goat biriyani ($12). The chunks of goat meat were nice and tender AND there were no bones at all, a nice contrast to the tough bony goat meat I've had at other places. However when the delicious goat is gone, you're left with a ton of rice and not much else. They were also kind enough to stay open a few minutes after close for me one night. This is very much a mom n pop operation. Mention the carryout discount when ordering and you should be able to get 1 dollar off. They take credit cards but prefer cash.
This is a carry out styled place. Very nice clean location
We ordered west lake soup, #4 pho, lunch special mixed vegetables with chicken, lunch special Mongolian beef, and shrimp spring roll. Everything tasted good!

I stopped in for lunch here while shopping with my Mom on Magazine Street. And the staff was lovely and attentive. The space is really open and attractive. The food was good and the prices were inexpensive compared to other Vietnamese places. And the food is more traditional than some of the other spots uptown/garden district. I had veggie avocado spring rolls and they were perfect. My Mom had a small pho (which was huge for her) and she really enjoyed it. I also had the bun with tofu and it was OK. There were definitely regulars who must be in all the time since they were greeted and asked if they wanted their usual dishes, which I would appreciate if I were a regular. The porch seating seemed to be dog friendly too. The steps were a bit steep and my Mom did struggle with them a little but she had been walking all over the place for a few hours.

Our food here was amazing. We had the lasagna and shrimp pasta and both were very, very good. The server (who I think was also the owner) was nice and very helpful. The prices here were also extremely reasonable.
Good Indian food (punjabi) and reasonabe prices. the food was fresh, and not overly spicy. their vegetable korma dish is great!
Coco Thai never disappoints. Everything here is amazing and just thinking about it makes me hungry. I wish Narberth had more spots like this!

Came here on 5/27 at around 2am and ordered the beef shawarma with fries (forgot to put the fries in my bag) my sister ordered the 5 piece honey BBQ wings and fries and those were really good. Really good flavorful food. Will be coming back here again when I come and visit Florida again!

A very small, cute shop with excellent tacos and margs. It's almost never too busy to find a table. Service can be a bit slow because there are usually not quite enough servers, but it's worth it. The taco specials are usually fantastic. And the most important criteria is that the guacamole is hella good!

I stop by here every time when I am in town. Their lunch specials are amazing and pretty filling too. It comes with a cup of soup as well. Depending on the day it is either hot and sour soup or egg drop soup. Both is very tasty. I like the egg drop soup best with a little chilly oil in it. . But if I'm not craving for their lunch specials I would order their pho. They even allow customers to customize the pho. I usually get their number 4 pho with the spicy beef broth instead of the regular pho broth, just because I like the spice. Oh and their ox tail pho is amazing as well. It seems they run out of it pretty quick. Have to be here early if I want the ox tail. A good majority of the food here is made fresh and from scratch. Their pho broth tastes authentic. Unlike some other pho places that uses powder to make their broth. Big difference in quality.
fyi- this place is closed!!! my friend and i tried to go here today but it's all boared up :(

When looking for Thai food in the Phoenixville area, do not be filled by the fancy decor of Thai L'elephant. Although seemingly upscale, the food is sub par at best. Thai Place, on the other hand, is phenomenal. The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. The Thai Green Curry is my favorite, along with the Vegetable Pad Thai (ask for extra tofu, they gladly give it). Their portions are great and everything is cooked fresh. The coconut ice cream is also homemade and delicious. Definitely eat here!!!! Oh, and the lunch special is unbeatable!! Soup, appetizer, and entree for $8.

So disappointed in this place, we always tell everyone it's the best pho around which brings more service to them. Well unfortunately, the service has gone way down hill. If you want to go to eat somewhere where you will feel like they don't appreciate your business, give you dirty looks, and ask you "what are you waiting for?" after they forget your food this is the place for you. When they forget your food and tell you they forgot not once, but twice and don't try to fix the situation that's just bad service. I sat there while my family ate there food finished and had to get a refund cause they were almost done eating and I still didn't have my food. I gave one star cause they still have the best pho but there literally is no service just bad attitudes.

1st timer, loved everything - get the iced coffee (and don't forget to stir it before you pour it over your ice!!). So maybe the service isn't great, but it's not that kind of place --- it's known for the food -- and really, wouldn't you want it that way? Don't forget it's CASH ONLY!

I really liked the flavor of the pho , the freshness of bahn mi, and the unique taste of coffee here. All of these were only 15 dollars. I am so glad I have found this place. I hope I can come here frequently.

Stopped here because the reviews looked good. The Pad Thai my wife ordered had a sour, rotten smell. She was able to choose a different meal which was fine. My Pad see Ewe was ok but could have used more fresh veggies. With just a few bites left, I found some raw pork. Not real impressed.

I loved the food here!!! Smiley is an awesome guy who knows how to take care of his customers. I had the chicken schwarma platter with a small Greek salad and it was excellent. I'll definitely be back.

Two full pages of a variety of specialty, ice tea, milk tea, smoothie and fresh fruit smoothie drinks plus a ton of add ons (boba, popping bobas, puddings, jellies and basil seed) to add on to your drink! Another two full pages of foods that you can order from, including 10 different types of banhmis. I think Season's Cafe might have the most extensive menu list I've seen from a boba cafe. Ordered a white tea with basil seeds with a Season's special banhmi and it did not disappoint! It was the first time I tried basil seeds and I like it! Texture is similar to granadilla. The banhmi had a flaky warm baguette with melt-in-your-mouth meats (pork roll, head cheese, jambon). It tasted even better because it was so dang cheap ($3.99). Love it and cant wait to come back to try the other items. Pro tip: you can ask for different levels of sweetness for you drinks. I asked for my white tea to be 50% sweet which provided just a hint of sweetness to the tea. Note: they say that this is a work/study spot but on a gloomy day, the lights are dim so it might be a little bit too dark for a good studying environment.

This is the BEST Thai food we have ever had. My boyfriend and I have been coming here for years and the food is always superb! We would suggest the coconut chicken soup, jasmine rice soup, basil fried rice with chicken and thai basil with chicken. The entrees can be a little spicy so we ask for not spicy. No other Thai place we have tried compares to this one. Highly recommended! Love the decor inside too.

We eat here regularly. I ordered takeout for the first time last night. I wasn't sure how takeout would compare to dining in. Silly, but I've had bad experiences elsewhere. Order was correct and just as good as dining in. The location is sketchy, but I say this is hands down the best Indian food in Tucson. The staff/owners are super friendly and very accommodating. Masala is phenomenal!

Let me start by stating that I am a vegetarian and it's hard for me to find options here in Nashville. My husband and I stopped by to see if there were any appetizers or something that would work for us. To our surprise they had more options than we expected. They had an amazing lasagna made with sweet plantains. It sounded strange but it was fantastic. We also loved their tostones, vegetarian mofongo and yuca appetizer. This place is at the top of my favorite restaurants to eat in Nashville. We have gone back since and will be back again for some great vegetarian options.

The atmosphere is low key with few amenities, but the food is the star of the show. Good for a quick bite or inexpensive week night outing. Would make perfect picnic food. The drinks in the case are a must, especially the peach malt drinks. The food is fresh and crisp with a spicy bite. The shish taouk and and lamb are both great.
don't expect to see any basil in your meal. in fact all the veggies are cheap and frozen. it shows in the bland flavor.

I was very glad to find his place. They have a very relaxed environment, the customer service is super friendly, and their menu is huge. They have something like 60 types of drinks, a (non-alcholic) variety unmatched by any restaurant that I know of in philly. Most importantly their food is absolutely delicious. I especially liked the fact that instead of wasting the extra lassi they made, they gave it to me in a smaller cup, a small but nonetheless humbling gesture. I will be coming back soon to try the 76 items I haven't tried yet. This place is awesome!

The food is definitely 5 stars! Absolutely amazing service and great atmosphere! I only give it 4 stars because I found out it was cash only AFTER dining there with my friends for an hour. $34ish bucks also seemed steep for a $$ yelp resturant, but considering there were 7 courses it's more understandable. If you're ready to spend a little more than the average place (and have cash in hand), this place will not disappoint!

Awesome place! The food was delicious. We went there for a small event and ordered food for about 40+ people. Everyone enjoyed the time and delicious food, specially their Shahi Paneer. Great service, Great people.

I actually can't say anything bad about the food. The food, indeed, was delicious. I think a few of the staff members, however, could have been a bit more happy about being there. The daquaris, the Pina Colada and the strawberry (?) were both delicious. The pig ears were crispy and the aioli was a very good contrast. I emailed the establishment, and no one bothered emailing me back. So, I would have to give a rating of a 3.

If you never had papa Maimonis u never happened / have lived. Srsly where have u been if there hasn't been a papa mamas in your back door I'd probably say CHECK YR GOT DAMN REAR VIEW MIRROR AND BACK UP TO SAN JOSE. cause ur in for a wild ride. If you ever had hav the wild berry pop tarts just imagine that success in a meal n u have papi moomoos wow ok
This place is amazing. I've tried several things on the menu and have enjoyed them all. I like the spicy soup they bring you to get a taste of the flavors they use. I love the seating and vibe.

Went for a quick dinner before a show at the Kimmel center, so the place was relatively empty when we arrived but quickly filled up as it got closer to dinnertime. Service was quick and decently professional although our waiter was a little odd and over-eager...we shared the bureki (I didn't prefer the sweetness as an appetizer, but being Greek my mom and I agreed it was definitely authentic), the fattoush salad (yum, and refreshing!), and the dips of the day (babaganoush, a white bean spread and hummus - better than having to choose just one). Bread was served with our order too. The place is a little small (we were put in the corner even though we were the only ones there at first...), but music and food are totally authentic. Apparently it's a BYO, which I didn't know before, but the food is amazing, filling and fresh so would heartily recommend it to any Greek food / Mediterranean cuisine lovers out there.

We ended up here because we got a parking spot right in front of the place and since I hadn't done Moroccan in awhile I figured what the hey. We walked in and it was tres dark with cool brass round tables and big couches. Due to the xtra weight i gained from eating so much, I had to lay down. I'm sure I wasn't the first. I figured the soup and the seafood Bastille would be enough for me; watching my weight and all that. We were approached by the waiter when we walked in and even though the place had only 2 other tables filled, he still asked us if we had a reservation. That sleighs me. Anyway, The soup was delicious; tomato with lentils, chick peas and spices.. delish! My partner ordered the chicken Bastille; but i make it a point to never order chicken at restaurants. I tasted it but it wasn't great and really sweet. My seafood Bastille wasn't much better but it did the job. Great ambiance and music. The waiter was not very good. But he had so many tables to wait on.... I wouldn't really recommend this place unless your a newbie foodie.

All about that N4! Broth is so delicate! Noodles are so chewy and perfect! Pork roasted to perfection! I eat here via delivery, take-out, and eat-in. Waiters and delivery drivers are sweet as pie too.

Asian Chef's food is always consistently excellent. They have solid special sushi rolls and a broad variety of pan-asian specialities. Their noodle soups are amazing as well. Not only is the food great, so is the service and attention to detail. We order delivery from AC at least a few times a month and they've never once gotten anything wrong with an order, they are very prompt with delivery, and are always welcoming and helpful. Great spot to order out or eat in!!

Absolutely my favorite place in the Broad Ripple area. By far one of the best dinners I've had. It's a must to get a desert after your dinner. Highly recommend the churros and cafe de olla. The inside is beautifully decorated! Service is fantastic ! I love Delicia!

Absolutely love both the inside and outside of this place. It has a very pottery-barn-meets-eclectic feel. Amazing little romantic date place, in my opinion. Although, it is in kind of a remote area and doesn't seem to fit there. It seems like it should sit in a neighborhood like Clayton or the Central West End, but regardless, it's a phenomenal place. The drinks are a tad pricey, but the wine pours are generous. Service is great and the set-up is just perfect. You won't be disappointed.

Disclaimer: this is only my 2nd Pho experience but thank goodness it was better than my 1st... This is a small little place, located right next to Campbell Nails. It does meet one of my top requirements for a restaurant though...it seems super clean. A lot of times I think the true test of a restaurant is how they handle to-go orders. I ordered a large beef pho and when I got home and unpacked it I found a large amount of noodles, bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, onions and beef. There was a small container of oyster sauce & Sriracha but if you like it extra hot make sure you get some extra on the side. The only downside I really saw was the broth seemed really really greasy. I swear, I meant to take a picture when I first opened it...but somehow it disappeared before i could....hehe. Oh, and the iced Vietnamese Coffee was super yummy but also super concentrated. I was able to take it home and almost 1/2 it with some skim milk to stretch it out some more. Pho is offered in small & large sizes, from 5.99-6.99.

Today was my first time here and I absolutely loved it. It was a 45 minute wait but the waiting area is really cool. It was a comfortable wait that didn't include standing awkwardly in the way of the servers. I think this place really benefits from having so much extra space. The decor was really cool. So our party was three. So we three decided to try a bunch of things on the menu. Everything from mushroom hummus, yogurt, to the falafel. Then we got seconds. We spent a good amount for three people but it was money well spent. I don't regret it and I'm eager to go back and try dinner sometime soon. P.S. don't leave without trying the French fries!

My review is for delivery only, so I can't comment on the restaurant service or interior. Liked: *Food arrived earlier than promised - in about 35m vs the quoted 60m. I always appreciate that. *Item ordered "spicy" actually was spicy. *Good quality chicken used in my dish Meh: *Naan really wasn't naan at all - it was a roti which is floppier and chewier. It was ok. *I ordered vindaloo and it really wasn't a vindaloo sauce. I'm guessing they took their standard "curry" sauce, threw some potatoes in and called it vindaloo. Nope: *Tiny portions. They sent "maybe" a cup of rice and there were only 6-8 chunks of chicken in my container of "vindaloo" sauce. *Samosas are super bland and boring. Dipping in the curry/vindaloo sauce helped somewhat. *The delivery guy didn't bring any utensils or a plate despite my note on the order that it was going to a hotel. Hey guys, I'm at a HOTEL - meaning I don't have a kitchen. I wasn't thrilled at having to schlep down to the lobby in my jammies to beg for a plate and fork. Overall - "meh" sums it up. Haveli wasn't the worst Indian I've eaten but it wasn't anything I'd voluntarily order again. They do deliver though, so that's something.

I've been going here for a long time (just a few weeks ago in fact) but today's lunch was a really poor experience for me. It was a half full restaurant with only two workers on the floor - one male (who I assume is the proprietor) and a young Asian lady. Attention was lacking the whole meal and when we were addressed, we were rushed (literally asked if we were ready to order within 10 seconds of receiving the menus). The soup was great, the boba in the Thai iced tea was extremely old and overcooked and not flavored (tapioca should be soft by have some bounce and is supposed to be stored in warm syrup to infuse). The curry rice was good but too salty. We wanted to order dessert but without asking, a check was dropped off. When we were done with our meal, we looked over to the gentleman which he interpreted as wanting the check. He brought over the (duplicate) check and looked like a deer in headlights, eager to move on from helping us. I made a hand motion to slow things down, told him we already had the check and asked him for a box and .... Before I got a chance to tell him we'd like to order dessert, he ran off to get a box. Then he came back and yelled at me, telling me he's swamped and he does "not appreciate hand signals". That's the first time I've ever seen those words uttered together. You don't appreciate hand signals? I told him we didn't need anything else (our appetites changes at that point) and asked for the check. This took another 5 minutes with another 5-10 minutes for him to pick up the card to run it. He apologized but reiterated he was busy and didn't "like hand signals". I work for a large company in Goleta, just down the street from their second location Calle Real. I've been waiting for this second location to open since I heard it announced. I would be hesitant to recommend any branch of Meun Fan Thai if this man is working when we visit. As a side note, the table next to us not only ate a portion of their dish and sent it back, but they asked for an entirely different dish as a replacement. He could not be friendlier and more accommodating to them, while he jumped on us for wanting to get a box and _order more food_. God forbid.

Hands down the best Thai food in town, and I've literally ate at every Thai establishment in Tampa. The second best part, next to the food, are the people that work there. They will go out of their way to get to know you and treat you like family. I can't say enough great things!!!
The decor of this place is really unique. Food and service have always been very good. This place is on the pricey side.

Do you like tacos?? you'll love these!! I have only had the tacos, quac and salsa here but have been told the rest of the menu is delicious. This is the baby sister to Delicia so some of the menu items and drink list are shared between the two places. Recommendations! Tacos: Fish, Pork, Carne Esada and Shrimp. the tortillas and the toppings are fresh and pop with flavor. (all the tacose are great, these are just my favs) Guacamole: probably one of the best in the city and made fresh. besides the normal guac they add in fresh jalapenos and pistachios. its amazing! Salsa: nothing fancy just darn good salsa! Drinks: their margaritas are made with no store bough mix, they create it in house. not too sweet not too sour. there are a couple of other drinks that are from the Delicia menu like the fire and ice that are pretty great. The bar is small but they have a nice beer selection with some locals on tap. The place is small but quant and fun to dine at. I have been many of times and only once did we have an issue. It was slammed busy and the waitress that was working our section was horrible (not purposely just couldn't keep up). A few tables left without ever getting anything ordered and our order got screwed up. All the other times i have had exceptional service and great food.

Excellent Service, Excellent Hookah - Period! I travel frequently to many cities and always visit Hookah Cafes and I found this to be among the top 5 out of 100's in the United States. The personal care and service of the owner and staff makes the whole difference. Anytime I'm back in Philly this is my spot for a casual relaxing place offering the highest quality tobacco, food and great atmosphere.

Nice authentic feeling spot. Platter was a bit small and had to order a gyro afterwards, but for first time in a real Greek restaurant I was pleasantly surprised by the flavors and quality. Awesome service as well
Great food! Delicious Pho with lots of fresh toppings. A friend and I split summer rolls and each got Pho and it was $8 each - very inexpensive and a healthy, flavorful lunch. I highly reccomend!

My friends and I were looking for a place to eat and stumbled upon this while walking in old city. We were pleasantly surprised! The place is gorgeous, the service was very accommodating, and the food was delicious. We all ordered something different so we could share our plates. IT WAS ALL DELICIOUS. Can't wait to go back!

I always have so much fun when I come here. Love the food and the atmosphere and the prices are so reasonable! My favorite menu items are the carpaccio, calamari, and the beef tenderloin. They have a great Happy Hour too!

Sky Cafe is right across the street from my favorite pastry bakery, Potito's, but I only noticed the sign recently. When one thinks of 16th and Ritner Sts. Indonesian food doesn't spring to mind, but Sky Cafe is excellent. (Don't let the blind drawn over the door window deter you, go in!) The food is spicy, delicious, plentiful, and cheap! My wife and I went there for dinner tonight and two entrees, wonton soup, salad, and some passion fruit nectar was $23! Service was excellent, too. They will make dishes to order, so vegetarians needn't worry. I'd give this place 4 1/2 stars, if I could. I hope they add delivery in the near future.

No "atmosphere" at all, but I drop in often to pick up a package of spring rolls for an instant, delicious lunch. I do sometimes wonder about how long they might have been sitting there on the counter, but so far, so good! I've also tried some of the strange little custards in the refrigerator case, and found them to be pretty decent. I've never tried their bobas or baguettes, so I can't comment on those.

First visit last night. Food was delicious, from the house-baked olive bread, served warm and crusty, to dessert of limoncello cake and crunchy-topped creme brûlée. The caesar salad was crisp, with a wonderful twist on the traditional dressing...maybe a little more lemon. Lamb shank was succulent and flavorful, as was the shrimp scampi. Can't forget the light tender breading of the calamari appetizer. Service was tops, and the understated elegance of the modern decor made for a perfect evening. To make things even better, I think the prices offer great value.

I love meat, but decided to try a vegetarian dish and am so glad I did! The bengan burthu (creamy eggplant with peas) was incredible. Nice texture, mellow flavor, nicely spiced. The restaurant was packed, so while the staff was friendly,I was neglected for awhile in the corner. I ordered two dishes, rice, and a samosa appetizer and have plenty to take home! Looks like tables are set up for two to four, though did see a larger group of six seated. By 7pm, things calmed down. Will return here soon with appetite and friends.

This place is amazing!!!! The portions are huge for what you pay for the only reason I'm giving it 4 stars is because I called in to order and my food was not ready 30mins later but it was worth the wait though
Cute and cozy! The staff was very nice and the Pho was great. They also had things you can use in your Asian cooking. Will be going back.

Great little local Thai restaurant! I went there off of the recommendation from my brother who is a total foodie. It is located in a pretty boring strip plaza and very unassuming when you walk in. It's a little weird as it guide you through some decorative screens that lead you to the hostess counter/check out area. When I called over the phone the girl was very courteous and friendly. When I came to pick up my food they were even friendlier. I did not dine in, I only got takeout for lunch. Looking at the dining room it looks pretty plain Jane for a Thai restaurant but it does seem cozy. I have to say for $7.95 the lunch was a great deal and was super yummy! I got that pang on chicken with vegetables. It came with a very small side salad with a peanut vinaigrette dressing and a mini spring roll with its own dipping sauce. Everything was fresh and tasted very delicious! I'm not a huge eater and it was plenty for me but if your are a large eater you maybe asking for more. From what I know from my brother who recommended this place the dinner meals are much larger portion but still for the price this was a rockin deal! Will definitely go back again for lunch one day soon!

This place is nice and clean! I had dinner here and ordered Drunken Noodle. The Drunken Noodle was great, and it was spicy to my liking. My boyfriend ordered Green Curry and thought it was mediocre. The service was alright, but the waiters talk too soft.

Been eating here for years. Love it. Silver noodle and Tom Yom soup, spicy Drunkin noodle, Pad Thai, slivered Ginger , Curry shrimp with smoked paprika. Shrimp roll, fish cake, All Outstanding. Don't get the tea!

Ordered through Groupon. Service is good, but food is meh. The poh-taek soup is not nearly worth the $13 price. It's way too sweet and salty and not at all tart nor spicy. Definitely not worth it for the half quart of soup I got. The shrimp pad thai was decent, although there were only 3 shrimps. Chicken pad basil was not that great, some of the chicken weren't fully cooked. Probably would not order from here again.

Yup - if you've found yourself to this yelp page, I see some mediterranean goodness sometime in your very near future. This place is family run and darn good down to the bones. You're not getting a fancy Starr establishment but I can tell you that you will leave full of some amazing hummus and Tzatziki. We came here a few weeks ago with some friends that were moving to NYC and wanted this to be one of their going away meals (you're now starting to understand more...) and we couldn't be happier that they chose it. I'm ashamed to say that we lived in Fairmount for 3 years before heading here but we plan to make up for lost time in the coming months. Everything was very well seasoned, fresh, and well priced. We came here late on a Sunday evening and ended up needing to sit out front and wait while a table became available but luckily this is a BYO and we came prepared. Highly recommend anyone to make a venture to Fairmount to explore this gem!
Pho broth tastes fine, on par with other places. However, the grilled pork lacked any flavor and was not very hot and freshly made. Iced Vietnamese coffee was delicious though.
I was with my Dominican friend and she liked it! the lechoza and tostadoes were really good. I liked the ox tail too but its a bit salty to me. The worker was really nice. bueno restaurante!

For over 3 years, I've been a customer at this little foodtruck near the university's campus. As a family run business, they make their customers family as well-- getting regular customers, knowing orders, and hitting it out of the park every time. I haven't ordered in a while, so today I figured I'd see if I could get my favorite-- bacon, sausage, egg and cheese with salt pepper and bui's sauce! She stayed open an extra 5 minutes when I was a bit late and she was closing up, and had my sandwich waiting for me with a smile! The bread is soft and perfect with the breakfast meats and buis sauce, which gives it an almost spicy flavor with a a great texture that isnt dry at all! Ask and you shall receive- if you want extra bui's sauce to make it saucier, do it! If you want more meat, order extra. Customize it the way you want and you won't be disappointed. I've also tried the chicken salad, tuna salad, and cheesesteaks, and they are all so full of flavor and packed with toppings. It's worth the extra few bucks to get the bigger, real meat, real toppings sandwiches.

I've been stalking the suburban Philly area for good Indian food for over a year and last week I hit the jackpot. My boo and I went to Shere-E-Punjab last Saturday night for dinner, we brought a bottle of wine and were ready to hunker down and enjoy some saucy Indian goodness. We arrived at about 7:30 and were seated right away. With us, the dining room was about 3/4 full. They seated us at a table for two but the table itself was miniature. Just with the bottle of wine, water glasses, and wine glasses, and place setting it was kind of precarious. Once our naan and entrees showed up there was seriously no room and was tough to pour wine and share our food. With that being said, the limited space was my only complaint. The food was awesome, albeit a tad mild for me: when asked how much spice we wanted when ordering the waitress talked us out of our answer of "hot" , so we went for "medium"...we should have stuck to our guns, we'll know for next time. The portions were pretty small, but that's nothing new with Indian restaurants. The garlic naan was light and crispy and they replenished our rice without hesitation. Vegetable samosas were flavorful and crispy without being greasy. and the clincher for me was that they had Kheer (rice pudding), a hidden gem of Indian cuisine. We'll definitely be back!

The buffet is fresh and each item tastes deliciously different from the others. The best fresh naan I have ever had is brought to your table. There are usually 3-4 meat dishes and a bunch of vegetarian options. There is a cold chickpea dish that is amazing. They have masala tea on the buffet and it is the perfect ending to the meal. Just as amazing as the food, the two folks (owners?) who seat you and provide checkout services are always so friendly.
You are going to leave disappointed. From the dirty seat cushions to the under cooked steak, all around poor experience.

After months of not being able to find an eatery to brag about, we finally found another place we'd recommend to our friends. The list of restaurants that have blown us away thus far is rather small, so we're excited to have tried Delicia. Everything from the service to the freshness and variety of flavors was great. As briefly mentioned above, Patty, our waitress, must have overheard me say 'happy birthday' to Sean. She didn't say a word, but took note and brought us the flan unprompted. While this is a minor item, we think it showed incredible attention to detail. She was also very knowledgeable about both the food and drink menus, and was able to answer all of our questions. The atmosphere was fun and sophisticated, and it's clear that this place is popular for a reason. This is one of the few places that lives up to all of the positive Yelp reviews. The fabulous food and drinks are enough of a reason to come back, but add to that the service and overall feel of the restaurant and they won't be able to keep us away.

Meh, the buffet was standard Indian. Naan was good. My son said he didn't like tandoori chicken. I thought the vegetarian options were okay daal, paneer curry etc. They also charged my 7 yr old full adult price. Apparently they don't have children discounts...

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I love this restaurant. I moved away from Boise 10 years ago but I still keep coming back whenever I'm in town. My best friend and I always come here for lunch or dinner at least once during a visit. The staff is friendly, the service is quick, and the atmosphere is perfect. The food is great and I will keep coming back. I highly recommend this restaurant.

The service was sub par - my wife is breast feeding and can't do dairy. Instead of asking and finding out the waitress just said "I don't think it has dairy" food was solid but you are in a hipster joint so expect the typical hipster vibe.

Went there this summer. There isn't really a seating area for dining in its a take out delivery place. Anyways had 5 different dishes all of which had excellent flavor. Their schechuan beef is to die for. The staff are so nice, the lady there made absolutely sure that everything was good. Again, there really isn't seating area designed for eating in. Love the food, love the people... I'll order again.

Every now and then I'll come in here for lunch during the week. It has a very cozy location in a small shopping plaza right across the street is a huge shopping complex off Pinellas Boulevard and U.S. 19. The parking lot is relatively small so getting there early enough to beat the lunch crowd is recommended. There's some minor seating outside and also seating indoors, but not much. I can describe this place is more of a takeout Vietnamese place. The quality is still the same as any other Vietnamese restaurant/cafe, but with a limited menu for food. Hence the reason it is called a café. If you plan on sitting down, they give you a number to place at the table and they will serve the food to you. So far from my experience there, there has only been one person back there serving the whole place and another one taking orders. I also learned that even though they serve the food to you, you would still have to bus your own table. There is a garbage receptacle with plastic bins where you can place your dirty dishes and utensils in after you dump your food in the trash. For me, it makes tipping confusing. The food in my opinion is pretty good. What they specialize in our their drinks though. They have a wide assortment of milk cheese, regular teas, shaved ice drinks, and fruity or milky slushy's. I cannot really judge on too many of those drinks because all I've had so far is there a really good lavender milk tea with Boba. It's worth giving this place a try.
Chicken Panang curry was very good. Two of us split 2 entrees, 2 apps, and a large sake and it came to less than $50. I would definitely go again!

Half star deduction for sharing a space with a 7-11 gas / mini mart and Wendy's....was expecting a standalone restaurant. N Order pho with rare thin steak snd tripe. Half star deduction for cooking the raw steak over the flame instead of letting the heat of the soup cook it. Otherwise, the flavors we on the mark. The special looked great....sad that my stomach wasn't big enough to try more.

I had a good time here. The atmosphere was pleasant, although my friends for some reason wanted outdoor seating in mostly 50 mph winds. I still enjoyed this place. After seeing the Avengers a couple times, Shawarma had to be the first thing to get here since I've never been here before. It was a good dish, although I feel that in a more original place I'd be able to have a more delicious Shawarma. The service was good. No complaints there. Even though we were outside, the waitress didn't forget about us.

My friend recommended we check this place out for brunch, since it's new, the menu sounded delicious, and the owners have an impressive pedigree. It did not disappoint! The mimosa and bloody mary were outstanding, as was my meal of the Lebanese omelette and citrus yogurt. It's only open for brunch now (dinner to follow sometime this Spring), but it was an open, bustling, and welcoming atmosphere, with a friendly and attentive staff. Can't wait to go back!

I love Ethiopian and this is the best Ethiopian restaurant I have found in Indy. Their injera is fantastic and pairs perfectly with all of their toppings. Highly recommended. You will not be disappointed. Also, the wait staff is extremely nice, helpful and quick. Great people at Abyssinia.

Delicious dinner of unique small plates with a variety of textures and flavors. Our server was attentive and friendly and the atmosphere was lively. Lots of vegetarian and meat lover options. Try the Whipped Feta, the Kale Slaw, and the Grilled Cucumbers.
Food was ok, nothing special about it. I ordered the panang curry with tofu and it came with four cubes of tofu, less than 1". It did come with about 20 pieces of zucchini.

Excellent. I came here recently and on the suggestion of my dining partner, we sat outside. I normally don't sit outside but this evening it seemed like I could break that rule. First off, I loved the bread with tahini. It was so good, we actually got a second plate of it. Downright delicious. Our appetizer was the flatbread and it was a revelation. It had all of those wonderful greek flavors and when you're able to eat that with a nice bottle of wine while sitting outside, life is good. My entree was the stuffed calimari. It was light and delicious. It was served over a bed of sauteed veggies in white wine. At the very least, pepper and olives. The squid itself was stuffed with rice, pine nuts, feta and some other goodies. It was cooked perfectly and cut like butter. Our waiter was very friendly and did a great job answering our questions. I'm definitely coming back here.
Warm song called beer on the water what more could you ask for foods gray get the fried calamari it has a surprise

Went here on a Monday night at 8pm with two friends. They do not take reservations but luckily had a table available. The table was shared with another couple and VERY small. To eat we had the tomato and mozzarella salad, hummus, spinach pie, grilled octopus, shrimp pil pil, and seafood combination. Everything was very tasty. It is a byob. There was no room on the table for all the food. And the servers were not that friendly. I would go back for the food and hope the server is having a better day!

We had a very disappointing meal here the hummus was flavorless and overly thick. The lemon soup was overpowered with lemon flavor. Gyro meat was dry, and the pita bread is not homemade. Finally the tabouleh was made of large pieces of tomato and cucumber. It was lazy preparation. Lastly, the meal is far from moderately priced.

In n out experience. Just wanted to get a sandwich somewhere. Got a grilled pork Banh Mi to go. It was good, fair price, quick service. It is what it is. Would def come back if I never needed a quick sandwich to go.

This is a hidden gem in Kenner. The food is authentic and fresh. The restaurant ambience itself isn't what you go for... you go for the fresh authentic food. Recommended dishes: chicken shawarma, falafel, baba ganoush, and baklava. We've never disliked anything here.

Keyword: Authentic, Northern Thai, Unique I believe the above word define this restaurant. They are the best Thai now in my book in the Bay Area. This restaurant just open less than a month but it does have all the unique food that you will not find any where. One thing I have to warn you is their food is spicy when you have the chef select the medium hot. For me I like very hot. They serve street food that only can be found in the northern kingdom of Siam - Khao Soi. This is a unique dish that only this restaurant have it. The dish include crispy and egg noodle with chicken in coconut milk curry. The chicken include the breast and chicken drumsticks. They also serve Pla Koong that I like. I have this dish when I am in Miami from an authentic Thai restaurant. I have try many Thai restaurant but non have come close. Now I found my favorite again. This is broil shrimps in very spicy mixed of lemony base spices. It include lemon grass and kefir lime leave. Yum. Very spicy. Love it. We also order the crispy duck in basil leave. The spice they use is difficult to describe. Very good dish. We order a drunken noodle. But this time the noodle is too soggy. I have this noodle at their lunch before and it is better. We also order another northern Thai - ginger curry. It is pork shoulder in long hours braised cooking. This is a sweet dish. For the rice you can order the white rice or the sticky rice. I never thought the sticky rice go very well with curry. I hope all yelper make an extra mile to support new and unique restaurant. The menu is still evolving since they can cook many northern dishes of the Thai cuisine. This restaurant do not serve alcohol but they allow you BYOB. I brought my sake. Very convenient and saving.

Finally, a really good Jaimacan restaurant...elegant and inexpensive. The curry goat was perfectly cooked and spiced, the rice and peas light and fluffy. A strange location but wonderful food...go quickly and make them a success!

Having been to over 50 Indian restaurants across the USA I can say that this is my least favorite of all. To start, while the restaurant only had one other table filled, the service was very slow. The menu lacks even the basic papadum. We ordered three entrees- butter chicken, chicken tikka masala, and lamb korma. The butter chicken was bland to the point of tasteless. The chicken tikka masala had a decent sauce but the chunks of chicken were dry and tough. The lamb meat was good but the korma sauce was off - not sure how but it didn't taste like any korma I've ever had. The final insult is that it is more expensive than most other Indian restaurants for subpar food.

Awesome place, cheaper, great food, easy parking. What more could you want? Service is great, we've only come during the slower times so they were a bit understaffed but always polite and reasonable food times. We've been a few times and haven't been disappoint yet!
This place is an authentic laid back and delicious restaurant. The service was very friendly and the food was filling, hot, and fresh. Definitely coming back- order food to share.

Excellent food and service. We had the dips of the day (lentil, fava bean, and Tzatziki), the grilled octopus, and the roasted goat. Everything was wonderfully prepared and very good. No wonder this place is so hard to get a weekend reservation at.
Favorite brunch spot -- and an awesome place for dinner. Perfect place to bring family & reasonably priced.
Terrible service!!! 20 minute and no food yet. Everyone around us is getting food but us. Servers on cell phone. Especially Dennis.

Amazing service, love love love the bartender Tony! Tony makes you feel welcomed and always brings a smile to our faces! The food is always fresh and tastes amazing. The atmosphere is wonderful. Our favorite restaurant to come to.

I love this place! I believe the chef is from the Ritz Orlando. I have been here several times for dinner including their first night open and also for lunch. The food is always great and our servers have all been cute and knowledgeable about the menu. I would recommend everything! Ha ha The atmosphere is cool and hip and the copper tile wall is magnificent. I think it is a little pricy but so far it has been totally worth it! I have had the pleasure of meeting the owners as well and they actually thanked my partner and I for being there! Imagine, a restaurant owner actually being appreciative for your business...what a novel concept. Try lunch, it works! Sit in Rodney's or Danny's sections...they're great

The best combination of North Indian and South Indian food I have had in Indiana. Specially the dish 'Appam' which is a speciality nowhere else available, which is included in the buffet. The buffet is all encompassing with food for all courses. And the restaurant staff has great attitude. Strongly recommend this place to anyone wanting to try unique food.

Negatives: 1) Food took 50min to come out. 2) Wine took 30min to come out after reminding the owner/waitress that I am still waiting for the wine 3) After 30min of waiting she told me no more duck and I had to order something else. Clearly the only waitress I see is scrambling to take orders, clear tables, bring water, food, stand at the cashier. Some customers were seated and left because she never came to take the order. She was also telling in coming customers that the place is full and can't handle more customers. I asked her if she is the only waitress for today and she tells me it's that way every day. she says there is only one chef too. so 2 people are managing 15 tables (x 4 seats more or less). I am giving it a one star. because if it is everyday, HIRE someone to help out. It's not like food is priced super cheap. If you are paying $12 for Pad Thai noodle dish at a Thai place, it is average. and it is Nashville, TN. they should be able to afford to hire a waitress by just looking at how much they charge for food. The only thing I liked about the place was that they give generous portion of rice. Hats off to those from Nashville who are patiently waiting for food and didn't seem to complain even if their friends' food arrived 15min ago and u were still waiting for yours.

Consistently the best, most authentic Thai food Nashville has to offer. Run by a small staff and decorated in a charming and fun manor, Smiling Elephant is usually a bit of a wait, but always worth it. If you're branching away from Pad Thai, try the Cashew Chicken, my favorite item on the menu. I eat here every week !

1st visit. got the cajun shrimp sandwich & a boba thai tea. can't believe i'm going to say this but the boba tea had to many pearls for me. flavor was strong & good just a whole lot of pearls. the sandwich was good, i'd never had one before but i am very surprised at the lack of flavor. it was fresh & the baguette roll was both crisp & soft. it just didn't have much flavor. when reading cajun shrimp i am thinking some heat & spice. i was not bad. the cucumber was crisp the cilantro fresh liked the little bits of carrots & the jalapeno was a bright green color not overly hot. the shrimp was fried nicely & not oily. just didn't make me make yum noises. would like to give 2& 1/2 stars but will go ahead with 3 because it was very fresh.

I Like It ! I ordered the chicken shawarma, it comes with salad and humus. All of the items were good. I was the only person there at the time and the waitress was nice to make recommendations upon inquiring. Next visit I'll try the gyro platter.

I stuck my chopsticks into the pad thai noodles, slightly turned my chopsticks to a 45 degree angle, and lifted my hand up. To my surprise, my entire plate full of pad thai noodles lifted up together in a bundle. The noodles were dry to the point where it made me thirsty just looking at them. I literally had a ball of noodles at the end of my chopsticks - pad thai on a stick? Some concoction they would serve at a state fair... It's very seldom that I don't finish a thai dish, but I took two bites and no more.

We have been here a few times now. One taste of this delicious, perfectly spiced jerk chicken, and you'll keep wanting more! My son LOVES the jerk chicken wrap... it is so fresh & delicious. The staff is wonderful & very knowledgeable. Very upbeat in their colorful chef's hats . The food is fresh & delicious. Authentic Jamacan fare. Owner, Grace, is delightful, full of energy & infectious smiles. I took home a side order of the Caribbean slaw... absolutely delish.... Large selection of drinks... many are imported from Jamaica.... This is the REAL deal! Can't wait until tomorrow....so we can go back! Thanks Grace!

We just moved here from overseas (Japan) and we have been trying Thai restaurants that we see in the area. I don't mean to sound rude but we have not been impressed with any of the Thai restaurants we have been too so far here in Tampa. We have also traveled to Thailand (4x) while living overseas. The food here doesn't and can't compare. When we do eat at Thai restaurants, we don't order Pad Thai like most people order at Thai restaurants. The night we ate here we ordered: Pad Gai Gaprow (basil chicken), Pad Pak Boom (morning glory) and Tom Kha Gai, my kids ordered chicken fried rice, and chicken satay. The food here is ok but not authentic.

Service is THE WORST! After placing my order for pickup and talking to someone who clearly shouldn't be answering the phone I already was a little ticked off. She had the biggest attitude as if I as bothering her by placing an order. I was told 15min wait. I get there 25mins later still not ready. 45mins later still not ready. I finally just gave up and left! Slow service while eating in, even slower with carryout!
I use to love this place, food was amazing. However I do not appreciate watching cockroaches walking on the table next to me. Need to say I lost my appetite will not be going back.

The chicken tikka masala was very good. The sauce was a bit creamier than what I'm used to but I enjoyed it all the same. The paratha was nice and crispy and not overly greasy. I'll be coming back to try more of the dishes but I'm happy with the food quality and service thus far. It's small but very clean, and the servers are friendly and helpful.
Amazing ! Went for the first time last night and had a fantastic meal and great service. Gnocchi was the best I've ever had. Fisherman stew excellent with perfect amount of spice. Will 100% be back.

This is the envy of Brandon. If you are not here, you are missing a great place to relax and enjoy incredible food and drink. When you are here you feel like you are home. The cozy feeling that you get from the staff is like mom giving you your comfort food. The food is authentic dining with fresh taste and smell. The Thai tea is a great mixture of ingredients that come together to make your taste buds jump. The pineapple fried rice with chicken is a combination of flavors that tempt you to keep eating. The order is made fresh. The garnish on the plate shows the detail that is put into your dining experience. I had a carrot butterfly. Desert was just incredible. Sticky rice and mango. Talk about a great taste in your mouth!!! Wow, what an experience. Don't know what to eat, they try to satisfy your taste buds. This place is golden. Highly recommend and will be back. Thank you for such a great evening.

The pho beef was very monotone, and everything in it was very beefy even the noodles.once you added sauce to the soup it tasted good. And then the noodle gained all of the sauce flavors. The beef was really Dry wasn't that great the soup was bland the spring rools had an overwhelming amount of lettuce, with no meats, or herbs. With the soups they did not give us the plate of herbs Ether. They had a lot of thing other then pho, and there lunch special did not even include pho
No ambience, nice food, nothing overly exciting or innovative. Pretty good, but not rushing to return.
Best Indian food we have found in St. Louis. It is very small and therefore the food may take awhile if there are many orders. We will be back regularly.

What's super sad about this place is the new owners don't seem to understand what made it great. For what it WAS I'd give it 5 stars, happy fast service, great food! They have the best gyros, certainly the best in Boise. The Z is delicious and the super is huge and excellent every time! Lamb, bacon, pita bread and veggies are always fresh and on point. What made it popular was that it was talked about by everyone, and I mean everyone, how it was such a great deal. A place with low overhead that built its loyal clients by actually passing savings along to them. I like the new menu concept simplified with pictures and all. The new owners raised the prices of all the gyros and specials etc. I think the sides are all the same but .50 for a couple tomato slices or peppers is overpriced anyway. Overall it's still delicious and I'll come back for sure, just not as often. You used to be able to feed two people for about $10-12, now it's over $14-17. I get it, just a few bucks but that's a 30-40 percent increase. I guess I just think it's too bad the prices are the same as a if they had a restaurant overhead. Mazzah down the street is $2 less for nearly the same gyro, and way more overhead, no kidding. Bottom line: still great flavor and quality, but it seems the new ownership has put price ahead of its loyal customer base. (Maybe they had to, I don't know, but I hope they stay in business and I hope things work out!)

Defined lines and smooth curves. They slip into your conversation. Communal seating, resting, eating. The crew is well prepared to listen. Delicia, delightful. Knowledge in food is a wonderful thing. Sharing the preparation and gift of that knowledge elevates everyone's dine time. -Raised stone benches with sturdy bolsters -Simple rounds of 6-8 tables -A smattering of stand alone tables -Skinny beams and full glass All are reflective of the effort leading to a fantastic dining experience, or tasting a better than average margarita. They're close to 20,000 margaritas and close to their 1 year anniversary. Who's the lucky person to taste that one? Me, I was lucky to pass the Beet Pastelito between my lips. Supposedly it had a little too much chile. I liked the finish of the small cake, but agree the normal diner might feel a delightful shock above average. Love the beets...

Authentic Vietnamese food! Got the seal of approval from the BF who is Vietnamese. We landed at 12:15pm and went directly to Lilly's Cafe for lunch as we were hungry and it was an amazing first taste of New Orleans. Pros: -Located on Magazine St, very central and accessible location - Owner Lilly welcomed us and spent a few minutes chatting with us - vey sweet woman - Fast service - Nice space, lots of tables - Fresh ingrédients and very good portions Cons: None!

This is my fiancé and I's favorite Vietnamese place!!! The service is great, they are very attentive and they remember you when you come in more than once. The food is great, and affordable as there are some other places that sell the same food for more. Love them!

I haven't gone here in about 6 months, but I've been coming here since they opened. We ordered some takeout today and noticed things have changed. The prices have risen, the portion sizes have dramatically decreased (containers of steamed rice and beef with broccoli were only two thirds full!), and the food quality has also declined. We will no longer be eating here because of this.

Ordered take out. Kati rolls were extremely salty to the point where we couldn't eat them. Sev puri chaat was good. Falafel was ok. Bombay sandwich and veggie burger were really good. Guy at counter at pick up was nice and friendly.

I had probably the best sandwich ever here, but the customer service leaves something to be desired. The two gentlemen behind the counter were accommodating and courteous but the lady at the register was crude, offensive, and beyond unprofessional. When there was a mixup over our order, she stomped outside and yelled "I'm gonna punch this bitch," (and other expletives) to the customers dining outside. For that reason alone, I will never dine here again unless the management seriously reconsiders the individuals representing their brand.

Being Indian myself, and a very picky one too, I went to this place for dinner last week and I went there again the next day for a late lunch too. They had a buffet which we missed but we still ate there again. I must say I have never had such good almost authentic and "homemade" tasting Indian food here in the USA. Further I like to add the fact that even though I overate both times, I did not feel any bloating or discomfort that one would normally feel after eating heavy outside food. My first impression upon entering the restaurant was not very pleasant as the air was not fresh and had a very very heavy and BAD curry smell. The only reason I didn't walk out was that I was tired to go out looking for another restaurant. And I was really glad I didn't. The place was not busy as we went there at almost very odd hours but it was run by very good and corteous people. It could definitely use a new HVAC system alongwith a high power exhaust hood in the kitchen to get rid of the curry smell. Also We ordered the exact same food both times but it was totaly different looking and tasting. The fact that it tasted really awesome both times took all my anger away. To me, not being consistent in product was the bigger "turn off " than the "not so fresh air" or the curry smell. Once again although different tasting, it was "awesome" both times. Might have been something to do with different cooks for dinner and lunch times. The place was kept clean and I would like to give a special mention to the "extra clean" restrooms. Its very rare find those anywhere anymore. The fact that I went there again the next day says it all. I am really looking forward to going there again and changing my rating to 5 stars in the future. I HAVE REDUCED MY RATING BY ONE STAR NOW. I WAS THERE AGAIN, RECENTLY AND DIDNT LIKE THE OWNER'S CUSTOMER SERVICE. SHE REALLY NEEDS TO LEARN HOW TO HANDLE THE FLOOR. SHE STAYS TOO FOCUSSED ON SOME CUSTOMERS AND IGNORES THE REST OF THE DINING ROOM. ATTITUDE HAS WORSENED TOO. IF IT WERENT FOR GOOD FOOD QUALITY, I WOULD HAVE REDUCED MY RATING TO 1 STAR.

This place is crazy good. The service is amazing and the food is delicious and well presented. The portions are more than adequate and you get more than you pay for. There is nothing on the menus I would not have again and again. If you like Indian food this is the place to eat in Mt Juliet. This is place is flat out delicious!

My kids and I love eating here. I have also held several business meetings here as well. The atmosphere lends itself well to both. Nice contemporary decor, great Thai/Laos/Vietnamese food, boba is the best in the Tampa Bay Area hands down. The service is impeccable and everything is very clean. Wifi available, I have ordered a snack open my laptop and gotten work done w little to no interruption from staff. There is also an outdoor space.

This has been one of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans so far. We ordered the dirty rice and tuna tartare to start, and then the curry goat and seafood pasta as an entree. The service was personalized and exquisite. Don't leave without the banana zeppole for dessert either. Would highly recommend for someone looking for a rich food experience!!

Went on a HOT summer day for lunch. I had the Chicken Katsu, spicky. It was pretty decent! Not a huge portion, but just the right amount for lunch. I was missing some spice, though. My friend had the fish tacos, which were also tasty, but lackin' the spice. The rice was great, and there were some other menu items, including a burrito with captain crunch on it that I might go back to try out. Will I go back? Maybe! The best part on a hot summer day? A few food trucks down the street there was a place selling big ole water ices for $1 that really made our days. Can't remember the place, but hitting up Cucina Zapata followed by that was pretty sweet.

This is my favorite time restaurant in Nashville. And there are plenty to choose from. The house special duck is my favorite along with the house spring rolls. I always order this when in town. It is conveniently located near the Opry Mills mall and right next to an interesting go kart racing track. The atmosphere is intimate and the food is delicious! I highly recommend it

red curry was more of a different taste than what we were expected. I was thinking along the lines of a curry type dish but instead it almost was like a sauteed taste... not bad though, it was actually very tasty! green curry was less creamy than most that i've tasted. it was oiler as well but i did have it with pork so maybe it's just from the meat i selected. I enjoyed the dish the way it was prepared since i demolished it! I would recommend some mushrooms since i was pretty jealous of the red curry's mushrooms. the spring rolls were also delightful. it was fried in some kind of oil that didn't leave a greasy residue. also, the inside was filled with a lot of glass noodles (one of my favorites). the size of the roll itself was larger than average than most places. I also enjoyed the fast of the sauce they gave us.

This is a great local bar that has many different drink specials (listed on the website newtavernbar.com ). They have DJ nights, karaoke night, open mike night and they also have a second room up from the bar. They are very friendly! And can hold birthday parties and give you a free cake.

Probably the most authentic Thai restaurant in Rittenhouse with friendly service and very good food. Some highlights: 1. Pad See Yew: Made with Chinese broccoli and plenty of egg in a savory sauce. Very very good. 2. Red Penang Curry: Spicy and creamy with fresh veggies, plenty of beef, and the best curry broth. 3. Ginger stir-fried chicken: Amazingly savory and cooked with tender pieces of chicken breast. Great if you are looking for a non-spicy dish. 4. Crispy duck fried rice: The duck definitely rivals Morimoto's with tender meat and a crispy skin. The rice is delicious with plenty of veggies and egg. 5. Siam Salmon: Great tangy sauce with a delicious fillet accompanied by crispy, fried crab. Love! 6. Salt and Pepper Shrimp Rolls: Filled with actual whole jumbo shrimp and served with a delicious dip. This is unique to Jasmine Rice so highly recommend trying. 7. Papaya Salad: Good but not differentiated from the other versions. 8. Chicken Lettuce Wraps: A great spicy version of a classic. It's a Gar pao accompanied with large Romaine leaves. I would recommend getting a bowl of sticky rice and having the chicken with the rice. Service is very attentive but the seating is pretty cramped so definitely book reservations for a party of more than 2. It was a Tuesday night and packed! Will be back to try more of the curries but so far so good!

Don't understand what all the hype is about. After moving from the Bay Area and eating great Thai food, a friend suggested Zen Yai. Very disappointed. Normally I finish my plate, but couldn't at this place. Everything was either way too salty or bland. Stick to Tap Thai or Your Place Thai instead.

This place is great! We started with the lava tempura which was amazing! Then I had the pad thai and he pad kee mao, both delicious. We also had a Thai tea that was sweeter than I expected but still good. Finished with fried bananas! The atmosphere is nice, nothing too fancy, but you could bring a date here.
FYI; the menu that is on their website is not current, as evidenced when I tried to order take out and was told that they no longer carry noodle soups. BUMMER!

I was a little wary of this place since its Yelp reviews are so wildly mixed, but I figured it was worth a shot with a Groupon, so last Thursday evening I drove out from center city to meet a friend who was coming from Norristown. Much to my surprise--and rather unlike many earlier reviewers--I neither loved nor hated it; I thought it was very much just "okay." The food was good, but I don't think I would have been too thrilled about the prices absent my Groupon. The service was remarkably friendly, but I think that was in part because we were new faces and the restaurant seems to be trying very hard to elevate their image and attract regulars.
