The interior of the restaurant itself isn't great--the lighting is weird (sort of a muted fluorescent?), and the tabletops are plastic--but there was nothing really "wrong" with it and we were plenty comfortable. If I lived closer to KOP, I'd probably hit it up again for takeout. Highly recommend that if you go, you either bring or at least mention the Groupon deal to get a nice discount!

I haven't eaten here yet, but had their samosa at one of media's street fairs. Anywhere I see a samosa I will buy it, so I have tried a lot of samosas. This was by far, the best one I have ever tasted. Light, soft, fluffy potatoes, gently spiced, lightly fried, with a side a tamarind sauce I never get anywhere else. Unbelievable. Most samosas are heavy, greasy, oily, ultra spicy. Which I also like of course, but this was just a huge step above that, never knew a 5 star gourmet samosa existed. Can't wait to try their other stuff.

Have been twice; once for buffet lunch (which was good as Indian buffets go...good choice and flavored) and then a second time for dinner. Dinner was the real revelation. We had the chicken madras and lamb saag and both were excellent. The poppadums were light and free of grease. The garlic naan was amazing--light and fluffy with the right amount of crisp. Both meat dishes were really flavorful...the meat was tender and the sauces yummy. We got medium spice which had a bit of a kick but not too much. Had a salad and mint chutney too both of which were great. Spent more than we had anticipated.,.this is not your average cheap curry house but we got several drinks. My husband and I lived in London for years and miss the Indian restaurants there. Gateway to India is a happy find for us!
Good: bread, sandwiches, soup, service, prices. Nice place to go in a pinch. I go frequently. Bad: small, kind of dirty, too, but acceptable.

I've been hesitant to share my love for this place because I don't want it to get too popular and never be able to get a table... I was fortunate enough to live in India for a time and loved the street food of the North and South. Since coming home to the states I have been looking for that same authentic experience. The paneer 65 is delicious. The masala dosa is crispy, spicy and so savory. The Briyani is good but the speciality here is the fresh dosa and chat options. They also make excellent lassis. The mango is my favorite. The dosa sandwich is also yummy but I prefer the simple curry, and potato magic of the more standard fare. The staff and service is also very good. The one thing I might change is this slightly bizarre smell of urinal cake in the entrance way. I'm not sure why it's so strong or smells of it in a hall way but it's always a bit of bracing oneself when you walk in. In any case the food has soul and the experience as a whole is outstanding.
We come all the way from upstate NY to eat here!

I was so thrilled to be able to get a great gyros sandwich when Kalamatas opened some years back. But the last three times I've been there (2015-2016) have been disappointing. I don't know what happened. The lamb should be heated -- not. The pita should be warm -- not. I had heard that the owner is no longer on site and gone to another restaurant. Fine, except I think people currently in the kitchen may need more training.

One of the best Dosa and filter coffee(too good) I ever had. Very creative Dosa range, we had Basil Dosa and it was yum.. My friends were drooling over chicken biryani. Very economic meal, owner is very cool and nice guy. The place needs some uplift in terms of infrastructure but owner mentioned he is looking for some funding
Simply so good! Whipped feta and roasted carrots are amazing! the Butternut Squash ice cream is a solid choice as well.

Our group ordered a dozen oysters and shared several of the small plates. We loved our waitress and the floor manager was attentive and pleasant. The restaurant and hotel have a unique atmosphere, but doesn't feel as if they've tried too hard to be cool. It's a beautifully restored space and the food is amazing.

Damn...the banh mi is so good, I have to say so again. I picked up one for my boyfriend, and he too thought it was one of the best banh mi he'd ever have. This is coming from someone who dated a Vietnamese girl for several years...so he knows good Vietnamese food.
Well, noodles are our best friend when you are too lazy to cook or go anywhere else to for a dinner. Their boba is quite tasteful.

I wish I could have finished my platter before I had the urge to write a review, but alas I cannot. My disappointment has overwhelmed me. After moving to the area a few months ago, I have been searching out a good Middle Eastern restaurant to satisfy the craving of my Lebanese roots. I could live on hummus, fatoosh salads and garlic sauce all the days of my life. So I decided to try this place with the hope I would find "my spot". I got the Chicken Shish Tawook platter with a side of hummus and grape leaves. Chicken was cubed, chewy and lacking spices.... as was the rice it was laying on. Hummus? The exact same flavorless disappointment as the chicken. No.Flavor.Whatsoever. I was hoping the garlic sauce would help me ignore the frustration that was my platter......until I realized the garlic sauce was made with mayo. MAYO, people!! I nearly cried. What a freakin' sin. The best thing on my plate you ask? The 2 little grape leaves sadly sitting atop a small garden salad. They were pretty lackluster, but after the atrocity that was the rest of my platter...my palate welcomed a little flavor. The small salad was served with a container of generic oil/vinegar dressing. Blah blah blah Overall.... Not happy. I probably won't be returning unless I forget the sadness I felt after tonight's meal. :(
Great variety of vegetarian and vegan soups, appetizers, entrees. The waiter was informative, attentive and fun. Will definitely be returning,

Best Indian food in Tucson when you can't be in India itself. Very good curry and butter chicken. Atmosphere in restaurant is okay but it's really the food that I go for. Prices are reasonable. Solid place.

I got a groupon for this place and finally decided to use it yesterday. My boyfriend and I both got the vegetarian combo platter and it filled us up so much we couldn't order the soup. The platter came with a delicious tabouli salad, two falafel, hummus, baba ganoush, pickled turnip strips, and pita. Very delicious! The only thing was the disinterest flowing from the staff. Not rude, they just didn't seem to care that I was in there. It kept me from wanting to stay and try more things. Next time, I'll get takeout.

Today a coworker and I ate lunch at Dosa and we were pleasantly surprised. It was empty, there was only one other table eating at lunch time. At the recommendation of the waiter we ordered the lunch special for a value price of ~$6.99. There was SO much food and it was all delicious! The service was great and everything was served very quickly. The only drawback is that they didn't have ice for our drinks, but that wasn't significant enough to warrant a loss of a star.

This is a really great place to get great Indian food. Not so kind to your wallet but your stomach will thank you. The service is impeccable, anything we needed came out super fast and delicious. I would definitely recommend to at least go once especially if you're a vegetarian. They have lots of options for vegetarian and non vegetarian a like. I would personally bring anyone here to enjoy the experience my husband and I have experienced. I just wish they would get with groupon they would attract a lot more customers.

3 stars overall homey, courteous, hard working people. The food here is solid. it's good given it's in nashville... but otherwise its a-ok... The lamb/chicken gyro is ok. not authentic meat, sauce, texture... the meat is chunky and comes with mumbo jumbo of sauce/seasoning.. it's still a hearty meal.. but not a "classic" gyro at all~ They do have good falafel, hummus, and *salads. I do admit I crave Kalamata's once in awhile when I'm stuck in nashville... but definitely not when I'm out of state~ oyea- Don't forget your baklava! that I can vouch for :)

Came here with a large group of 12 people and the service for our party was great. We got there around 630 when it was a little less crowded and must have gotten nearly every appetizer, the Chicken 65 + grilled shrimp were so good we ordered a 2nd round. I really liked the Apollo fish too. The waiters kept the beers coming and we all did family style for the entreès with my favorites being the butter chicken, goat vindaloo (its spicy) and the chicken tikka masala, which was one of the best I've ever had. The garlic naan was on point and I had to roll myself outa there I was so full afterwards. Definitely check this place out, I think its pretty new. They also have 2 TVs behind the bar and were showing the MLB wildcard games.
I stopped because of all the positive reviews I'm giving 3 stars because it was good not great. Tom kha soup was yummy the rest was okay

Great, great dinner this evening . . . Pan D'Olive at 1603 McCausland - near the Olympia House Greek Restaruant in midtown St. Louis. Sam Kacar, owner, and previous owner of Trattoria Branica of Frontenac and Kirkwood, has created a masterpiece. We ordered the Pan D'olive flatbread (pizza) which comes with chicken, mushroom, olive, shaved parmigiano, spinach & pesto. Normally $10, but during Happy Hour - until 7 PM each evening during the week - only $5! Absolutely delicious! Also had the Phylio Cigars - phyllo dough stuffed with feta and herbs - they were only $1 each during Happy Hour. Our great neighbors, Steve Gant and Emily Howard joined us too and had the mushroom risotto - cremini, porcini, arugula and also the baked cannelloni, consisting of bolognese & bechamel. Great atmosphere, absolutely delicious food, and service out-of-this-world! Get over there before it becomes VERY popular!!!! We will be back soon and often . . . just such a great environment, amazing food, and Sam, the owner, has the BEST people skills of any restaurant in St. Louis, MO!!

Had dinner with my husband on 5/31/2015. We've been regular diners since the restaurant opened. The food is always very satisfying. My husband favors the Tandoori Chicken. I am partial to goat, the Gobi Gulistan and Spinach Paneer. They serve fresh Naan to the table. Chai tea is also available in the buffet. The condiments are excellent: mint chutney, onion chutney, tamarind chutney, and raita. Some Indian restaurants water down the chutneys, but this is not the case at the Tandoor India. We also like the Indian desserts. Great value and delicious. A great place to satisfy your desire for authentic Indian food. We bring out-of-town guests here often. The staff are friendly and attentive. Great location.

Stopped by last night for a drink and dessert. Bartender was quite nice. We asked about dessert from the restaurant and got the deer in the headlights "look". she informed us if they were not "too busy" we could order them. She then excused herself and went to ask then brought back the menu, then could not describe any of them to us? We ordered 3. Shortcake, nothing special, lemon curd, disappointing. It had too much gelatin and lacked that true lemony punch that one would expect in a lemon curd dessert. The chocolate came and it too was lacking. The two squares of chocolate like brownie tasted somewhat dry and the quenelle of mocha (?) was basically flavorless and a loss on the plate. The presentation was beautiful. Very disappointing at 10.00 each and 6.00 for the shortcake. What was really surprising was the action behind the bar. Twice we observed the same server, once over pouring a taste of champagne and then realizing the over pour, poured the champagne back into the bottle from the glass! The second was her marrying two open bottles of wine together. Had we been excise, well.... The owner and possibly partner were seated next to us working on some plans of some sort. Perhaps attention to details in the existing establishment need to be worked out first?. In short, Cool place, pricey, weak staff and pretty disappointing pastry.

Oh my yummy! This place is perfect for a date or friends night out! Super yummy food...ESP the scallops...The fire n ice drink is amazing! A little noisey due to the open floor plan so probably not the best place to go if you want a quiet intimate place. The service is excellent! Please open for mondays! If you are looking for something different and unique this is the place to go!

The burger was thin and bun was dissolving under some heavy tomato sauce and it had melted cheese?...the lamb rib is good, spiced ok and crispy but no sauce offered with it or anything else. The humus are mixed with carrot....??... the bread is like a pancake, it should be lafa or pita bread, crispy not soft cake like. The shredded wheat is actually konafi but was very dry and inedible. Surprisingly bad for its location and all the buzz about the chef.
Everyone says feels like your on vacation! With Excellent food! Fun and great kid friendly atmosphere! "Best Fresh Pork Cuban EVER!" THIS IS WHY WE ARE REGULAR'S!!!!!!
I have no idea why this place is so highly rated. The menu is confusing as hell. The guy just kind of makes you whatever he feels like and it's super bland. Overall confusing and not good.

I'm a long time fan of Patties of Jamaica on Allisonville Road. They're still my favorite, but Jamaican Style Jerk is a delicious change of pace. Their patties (ground beef, chicken or veggie) are rectangular and thicker than Patties of Jamaica. The ground beef patties are delicious - they've been out of the veggie ones everytime I've stopped by. The rice and peas can't hold a candle to Patties of Jamaica's wonderfully subtle version, but they're quite tasty. The fried plantains were perfect - as fine as I've ever had. The staff is friendly and the prices very reasonable. Highly recommended.

This place is sort of hard to find. It's back behind, and just to the left of, Patel Brothers market, and it's totally worth it. It has outstanding Dosa, and a nice variety of different types of Dosa to try. All of the chutneys served with the Dosa are delicious. The staff is pleasant, and I enjoy the lively Indian videos shown on the TV.

I am here once every couple months and it is always a hit for the lunch specials. Soup or salad, app and main dish for under $12. Sold. Very friendly service. You can be in and out in 40 minutes if you know what you want fairly quick. Very nice portions and they will cater to the level of spicy you prefer (1 thru 4 I believe). Go with a 2 if you want some spice, but not enough to distract you from your meal. My favorite dish currently is the Vegetarian Pad Thai. Tons of colorful veggies and tofu to boot. I'm drooling just thinking about it now. I find the Drunken Noodles to be a bit on the oily side, so I don't typically order this one there, even though I it is one of my go to dishes for thai food. They are closed Mondays. Chicken Satay special for app. on Tues. and Thursdays only. BYO as well.

Liked everything about this restaurant, very clean, decorated nice, waiters second day on the job and doing quite well he was very friendly, food arrived fast and the Mongolian pork was excellent. A bit of an expensive lunch by my standards but worth it.

This place is just fantastic!! The service was friendly and outgoing and the food was marvelous! Started with the spring rolls. I seem incapable of remembering that spring rolls are fried. I was actually wanting the summer rolls in rice paper but it was my fault (dummy) and the fried rolls were excellent. Not greasy at all. We followed with entrees: he had the green curry, spiced to medium, and it was pleasant to his spice level. Huge portion, we really should have split a few things. I had the lemongrass soup with tofu and the duck salad, spiced "Thai hot". Maybe my palate has bottomed out or maybe Thai restaurants are hesitant to crank up the heat. Although delicious, I would have liked it to be much hotter. Finished with the coconut ice cream- mine topped w lychee and his with wonton wrapped, deep-fried banana. Then we staggered outta the place and I immediately passed out in the car. Great experience. We will definitely be back!!!

Of all the ears of I've gone there , I finally got a friendly attentive waiter (I wish I could recall his name ). The food is just ok , but my whole family races that they have the best Clam Chowder anywhere . The drinks are just ok . The bar service is slow . It's always full because the restaurant is all outdoors and have a great view (The Gulf). They have live music on certain nights and the local love it . I only go there if someone's asks me to.

Just left this place... And wow!! It was amazing!! My boyfriend is Puerto Rican and has been dying to bring me here for well over a year. He did agree with some of the reviews that said the service was not great but he had not been here in a long time. Well they clearly have been working on their service. The place was very busy but we were sat very quickly. Now... I did time things because of what the reviews said. I wanted to see how long everything took. We were greeted at our table with 2 minutes and the server said she would be right back to get our drink order. She came back within a minute or so and we ordered our drinks as well as food, since we already knew we wanted mofongo. Our drinks were at the table in less than 5 minutes followed by our food in under 20 minutes. The presentation was nice and my boyfriend said they even changed their plates to something much more appealing from when he was there last. Some of you may be thinking that we must have just had a good server or got lucky on this particular night but you're wrong. We watched the other tables and their service was just as good. Food was out quickly and servers were all over the place making sure the tables were happy. The owner walked around and checked on things and my boyfriend said there was a new lady there that seemed like the manager. He agrees they have definitely stepped up their game. We were in and out within 1 hour. Some reviews mentioned that they served tap water and this was true but it did not taste bad. They do also have bottled water on their menu now. The sangria was quite tasty! Now time to talk about the famous mofongo... It was the best I've ever had! I've been to many Latin restaurants and to Puerto Rico a few times. This was by far the best mofongo! My boyfriends is a close second, seriously! :) we also ordered tostones because I love them and these we very good as well. I prefer my a little more crispy but they were delicious and the dipping sauce was to die for! Just the right amount of seasonings and fresh cilantro. I highly encourage people who have had bad service here before, to try it again. I think they have been working on this. They even have iPads to take your order now. I guess they did not used to have these. The restaurant was very clean and I liked the decor. I can't wait to go back and try the soup! I heard that is pretty good as well. 5 stars for sure!!

If I had the choice, I would've listened to my fellow Yelpers about this place, but my aunt swore it was good, so we ordered takeout. After that experience I'm seriously questioning my aunt's definition of good Chinese food. I ordered chicken & broccoli with brown rice and fried pork dumplings. Their chicken and broccoli had a clear broth instead of brown. For most that might be incredibly weird, but I've had it once before, so I wasn't completely turned off. It tasted fine, but not the same as the brown broth. The brown rice was AWFUL. It had a sweetness to it that reminded me of avena (spanish-style oatmeal). Definitely not a could pairing with the chicken and broccoli. My aunt had ordered white rice too, so I ended up just eating that instead. The dumplings might as well have been steamed since they packed them in the same type of container as the rest of the food. You could tell they had been fried from the markings, but they had no crunch to them anymore. The filling was very bland and the dumpling sauce did nothing to make it better. Apparently the crispy orange beef was pretty good, but I never got around to trying it. It looked over cooked to me and after everything else, I just didn't want to try it. Next time my aunt recommends a place, I'm definitely gonna have to follow the Yelp universe's opinion.

Stopped in here earlier this week for a bite to eat with my lil sis and her bf. Nicely decorated, wonderful service, and decent food. I arrived a little late so my sis and the bf had already devoured most of the calamari. They seemed to enjoy it. I managed to sneak one bite and I thought it was fine - not outstanding but not bad either. Wines were well priced and I sipped a lovely glass of pinot noir with my meal. My sister and I both started with caesar salads. Salad was standard but good. My sister tried to order the lobster ravioli but they were out. Her second choice was the seafood linguine and she was pleased. I didn't get to taste but I from the looks of the sauce splashing around I think it could have been reduced a little more. Her bf ordered the chicken tortelloni and he devoured it - meaning I didn't get a bite. Again I thought the sauce could have been a bit thicker but that's just what I gathered from the appearance. I went with the veal scallopine picatta. I absolutely loved the roasted veg on the side and thought the sauce had a pleasant lemony caperyness to it (yes, I made that word up). The veal I thought was okay but if I were to order the dish again I might go with chicken. We all shared the tiramisu for dessert and it was another standard but tasty dish. We were there 5:30/6ish and were the only ones in the back dining room at first but as we were finishing up the room was getting more crowded. This place looks like it caters to an older crowd as we were the youngest table in the restaurant. All in all - decent food but I'm not sure I'd go out of my way to return. If you're in the area though it is definitely worth a visit.

I ordered delivery and it was faster than expected which is nice. However, the food was over-cooked, so everything was just brown, the broccoli, the green beans and not appetizing to look at. The shrimp were small and as overcooked as the vegetables. Still searching for good Thai food in Philadelphia.
Fast takeout. Staff was friendly. Food was fresh, flavorful and plentiful. All I could ask for!
Good food. Good service. Authentic West Indian food. BYOB. Quiet Atmosphere. Mussels were very tasty. Curry Goat Roti was delish.

Gateway to India... more like Gate to Heaven! When I die I hope to go to heaven where I can eat Indian food everyday, live in a mansion, watch sports, drive around in a Tesla, and hang with the gf all day (I may or may not have been forced to say this). Jokes aside... The restaurant is clean, nicely decorated, and has nice ambiance (pretty dim inside which is not a bad thing!) As for their lunch buffet, there were only about 8 different dishes, 2 of which had protein -- tandoori chicken and chicken masala. It's pretty limited compared to other Indian buffets I've been to but it has the essentials that I look for in an Indian restaurant. Chicken tandoori was one of the best I've ever had and they were frequently restocked. They do lunch buffet everyday (11:30 AM - 2:30 PM) including weekend so I will definitely return soon!

I'm Eritrean and I've been to plenty of Ethiopian and Eritrean restaurants! And this lady is full of S#!! She charged me for items that were suppose to come with the entrée...when you order an entree it's suppose to come with salad and a side or 2 sometimes but noooo she charged me individually for each item on my plate and my girlfriends plate which ended up being 50 dollars which anywhere else it would of been 30 never going back and I will have a lot to tell Oakland and San Francisco about her crappy attitude she had...and her customer service is garbage....i had to call the restaurant from the restaurant to have her come out and attend to me from the back I was there for almost 10 mins

Normally we enjoy this restaurant but not today. After waiting for nearly 30 minutes for our food, my pizza finally arrived...it wasn't burnt, it was incinerated... The waitress offered a new one, but after a 30 minute wait, I chose to not eat rather then wait again. After we got the bill, we waited for a bit and decided to just pay the bartender and go instead of sitting around.. First bad experience here, but I think I'm done with this place.
Chicken in peanut sauce is delicious. Pad thai was great. We ordered 3 desserts and split them. All of them were delicious. Coconut ice cream was amazing!

Best Southeast restaurant in Philadelphia. These folks started out in their backyard selling Pad Thai and three colors of Coconut Curry for three bucks a bowl till a fricken SWAT team shut them down. Now at three times the price the food is just as good with TONS of amazing veg options. Best bets: Tom Yum Soup (spicy and sour--a real sinus cleaner), Green Papaya Salad (nice and tart), Ban Xeo (rice flour pancake made with coconut milk and turmeric, veg version stuffed with mung bean sprouts and tofu), Yum Salad (crunchy and spicy), King's Soup (like a Pho noodle soup mixed with Red Coconut Milk Curry--wow!) Their desserts are fab, especially with a ginger tea, and be sure to try the Guava Candy you get with your check. Simply fab.

Wishbone has a great small location in University city. The design and theme is great. When I went the woman working was very friendly. She explained the whole menu. I went with the southern chicken sandwich. It was great. In fact, I have since ordered it a second time for delivery. The jalapeño cornbread was decent. The real star was the sandwich. It was a big soft bun, a large piece of fried chicken, crunchy southern slaw and a really tasty sauce. This sandwich is a bit more expensive than Hatch and Coop, but from my experience MUCH better and twice the size. Great sandwich, great location.

Came here for lunch and it was a pretty good experience overall. Place was fast, clean and well run. I had the half chicken with tomatoes in balsamic and fries. Chicken was grilled and a little dry but had good flavor. Tomatoes were really good. Potato wedges seemed like they we under a heat lamp for a while. Sauce and salsa bar was clean and had a lot of choices.

This place isn't that bad for dinner. Went on a Thursday evening, and we were the only customer there. They give you free chips with mint and tamarind chutney, the mint wasnt that good but the tamarind was. Everything was great EXCEPT for one thing. About 20mins into our meal, a family came in to eat. I don't know if the restaurant have only 1 mint and tamarind chutney or not, but a server came over and reach to grab the chutneys I was still using, THEN he asked if i was still using it. I don't know why the server would take the chutneys i was using unless it was to be giving to the other table. Beside this incident, it was great, but due to the fact that i have to experience such thing, i give it a 3 star instead of 4.
Great food, nice staff, fresh ingredients. I was very impressed, the store was clean and bright. Will definitely come back here

I liked this place. It is authentic and family run. Not sure what i was eating but it was fresh and tasted great. Minimal items on the menu which, I think, is a good thing. Location is a little different but the place is clean and has plenty of breathing room. Will return to try some of their other selection. Desserts are homemade and great tasting too. Another very authentic restaurant. I think is Greek or Bosnian.
We had the brunch menu, not extensive but very tasty and unique. The tartar was great with the right touch of spyce. The pasta was really good and the Wayu burger really nice.
Fantastic meal and fantastic service. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious. Will be eating here again soon!

Perhaps when a nut allergic patron asks about getting a sandwich without the curry peanut sauce, the chef or owner could educate the staff to say something other than "Oh, it will be really dry without the sauce."

Love the new location! They used to be hidden around a dark alley a couple blocks over where there's zero foot traffic.. it had to have been hurting their business so I'm happy with the move (it's also closer to home ) You have to try the Panang Curry. Simply the best around.
This was my 1st of many times... The best food I had in St. Louis yet reminds me of New York..

What a wonderful new idea for a restaurant! It's Indian food in the style of Qdoba. This is the perfect spot for lunch. It's very fast, friendly, and delicious! Don't come here expecting the same Indian food you have grown accustomed to. It is a new twist on Indian food, and very delicious! I have been here many times while working in Wilmington, and I absolutely love it. Quick rundown of the menu: You get a choice of dish: rice bowl, salad, or naan roll. The rice bowl is rice with your ingredients on top, the salad bowl is salad with your ingredients on top, and the naan roll is your toppings on top of a piece of naan bread, rolled up like a burrito. Your next choice is protein, where you choose Zaikka chicken, tandoori chicken (my fave), lamb, or paneer. Then, you choose your curry: Zaikka (really spicy), Korma (my fave), Tikka masala, or spinach. Last, you choose your ingredients. I normally get a tandoori chicken rice bowl with korma curry, red onions, green onions, boondi, lettuce and cilantro. To the other reviewer who gave one star: You shouldn't have come here expecting an authentic Indian cuisine. One look at the menu would have told you that it is not authentic. Sure, there are Indian flavors, but you can't expect to see butter chicken, palak paneer, or anything of the sort. Also, you should have anticipated that the spiciest thing on the menu would actually be really spicy. I'm surprised you said you were looking for real Indian food and turned away from Zaikka due to it being to spicy. Real Indian food is spicy.

The food was good but the service I am a regular visitor to the restaurant in media but this time I had a bad experience and hence fort I doesn't want to visit again to that restaurant I ordered my dish and having my dinner with my family from India and within 10 mins the barer came without information started taking the plates and gave me food packaging container then I realized there was an birthday party gang the management allotted me a table and immediately if they had a crowd of local customers the service was bad on the existing one
Been here a few time when I visit Indy. Always a good meal. The lunch buffet looks good, but sadly I've never tried it, always come for dinner. Try the goat, not many other places have it.

The kitchen is very overwhelmed in their first couple weeks open. The restaurant was very busy and everyone was waiting 45 minutes to an hour for food and overheard customers considering leaving. Unfortunately, when it finally came the food was very average - nothing close to what you would get in Chinatown or Italian Market, for example. Meat in the pho had fat that should have been trimmed off. It might be a good idea to hold off on offering delivery and take-out until they can get the sit down restaurant part figured out. Sad to see the big Blue Cat mural painted over with bamboo mural. Hoping with time IPho might improve? What a great idea for Fairmount but just not executed well yet.

What a mess. This place's time is over. Micro wave is used constantly - we could hear it dinging non stop in the back Forever to get even a drink -- about 40 minutes to get our food. Prices partially scratched off the wall sized menu, different prices on to-go menu. So you don't know what it will cost No change to give to customers. Not sure if they have a bathroom. The food was dried out, old and miserable. We took a few bites and walked out on $46 worth of food. I would bet that the lady I saw on TV hasn't been there in awhile. Went to McDonalds - It was better

Stopped in last Friday night - great surprise! New favorite Vietnamese. I love the lent menu - we had shrimp spring rolls, shrimp & curry with bread, and a shrimp vermicelli bowl. Everything was spot-on, especially the shrimp curry. Good prices, nice decor, great service - nothing negative to say!

Most of the time, I like to try different dishes, but here I usually just stick with Pad Thai. It's nice that they can customize the spice level, and the portion to price ratio is not bad at all. On occasion, I have their black rice pudding and certainly no complaints there!

My wife and I's favorite take out spot in Carmel. We get it almost weekly. Every dish is so flavorful, and always has a balanced heat no matter what level you choose. The lunch buffet is fine, but every dish on their menu is better if you order off the menu. I have a feeling the mellow out dishes on the buffet to appeal to a wider audience. Food is always ready on time and still plenty hot when we get it home.
This place has a great atmosphere, they make pisco sours (thumbs way up), and the food is excellent. The problem...I always leave hungry. Too much money for not enough food. Oh well.

Ohhhh how I love Coco Thai! It is Thai food done to perfection with seemingly simple dishes packed with layers of flavor. The portions are perfectly sized so that you don't over-indulge. If you are looking to keep things on the lighter side for your diet, I recommend the Jasmine Rice Soup and sharing an order of the Vegetarian Dumplings with a friend. When you're in the mood for something spicy, the Evil Gaga is the answer. Make sure that you have plenty of time to relax and enjoy. The service is a little slow at lunchtime.

For my Indy friends who like to experiment with interesting - but delicious - food. My husband and I tried a place on West 38th street tonight called Jiallo's It's an African/Caribbean cuisine and very authentic! The food was amazing and the owner, Mr. Jiallo, came out to check on us more than once to make sure we were happy with our food. I really would love to see this place succeed and thrive! If you are looking for unique and delicious food, you should give this place a try! So glad we did!

We made a reservation. We went. We were seated promptly. It was 100 degrees outside. It was 99 degrees inside. They sat us next to the food warmers on the edge of their open kitchen. My armpits were drenched by the time our lovely waitress poured out water. I got up and politely asked the hostess if there was a better option since we were there celebrating our 6th anniversary. She apologized saying they were having issues with the air lately. She moved us to the back of the restaurant, and we decided it was still too warm to shell out $100+ for drinks and a meal for 2 in a sauna. So we snuck out the back door by the patio before they even poured out water again. It was the SAME temp outside except slightly more humid. The service was great from what I can tell. The hostess was drenched even though her hair was up she had no sleeves. I felt bad for her actually. Dear owners & management, if you can't keep your restaurant below 85 degree, you need to hire a HVAC guy. It speaks volumes about what you think about how much you value your customers and employees.

I love the area, S.Grand its loaded with international cuisine. My wife and I really enjoy Thai food and having tried numerous spots this is pretty much our go to joint for Thai. The staff speaks pretty much zero English lol but its cool they haven't jacked up any of our orders as of yet. We usually go for their generous portion of delicious Pad Thai and the price is right, its a win - win in my book. Go for it!! you wont regret it.

Please disregard my last review as I believe I am now hooked on their kung pao tofu which comes with enough food for two meals, lots of veggies, peanuts, and a good spicy sauce. Sigh, now that i work across the street I keep eating it!!

This restaurant was absolutely a wonderful gastronomic experience. Our group of 9 shared the following appetizers (we chose the top 5 on the menu for ease) and we didn't go wrong. relleno de papa de carne (ground beef stuffed potato puff), sorullos de maize (sweet corn fritters), croquetas de garbanzo (chickpeas croquettes), empanadillas de carne (ground meat bite size turnovers), empanadilla de jueyes (crab meat bite size turnover). I ate the entree of mofongo relleno de pollo. This was a cooked plantain rolled up inside chicken with a light gravy. I chose the side of mofongo de yuca. Everything was seasoned perfectly! We ended the evening with a sampler of their three desserts.....amazingingly delicious. One of the best food experiences I've every had in 10 years living in Nashville!
This couple is SO sweet! Very gracious hosts. The decor is beautiful inside. Next time I'm back in Tampa I'm coming back!!

My husband and I relocated to Brooklyn, NY after Hurricane Katrina but come home at least twice a year to visit our family and friends. Our friend Mark from UP/Unique Products recommended Lily's Cafe for lunch. We usually get our Vietnamese fix from Dong Phoung in the East, but to our surprise the food here was as good. Besides the food being delicious the service and staff were amazing. Lily gave our son some Mardi Gras beads and a stuffed blue bunny for Easter. Our two year old son loved his special treats and it helped keep him in his seat for mommy and daddy to eat lunch. It was such a treat to find this special gem with great and personal service. Eating here made me want to move back home! Thank you Lily!

This is a very good Thai food restaurant that we stumbled across. We've been going there since they opened. Great variety and very nice family. Its great for take out.. If you're looking for "ambience" ..look somewhere else. Love the spring rolls and the satay..always have to order two seperate orders.. First order never seems to make it home!

Best Iraqi food in US ever The owner is very nice, the food is authentic Iraqi food Kebab is the best, I tried the kebab in Virginia, texas and here. No need to tell, here is the best The prices are very good for I have never eaten any Iraqi food in US as delicious as this place, you rally feel that you are in Iraq I live in NY, if I was living here I would eat at this restaurant every week if not more than that My wife also loved their food, 10/10 is your score guys, friendly people, tastey food, clean place, and cheap prices. No need to tell more

I've been going here since I was little. This place is one of Indianapolis' first Indian restaurants and holds a lot of history for several Indian and Sikh families. The food's alright, it's your typical Indian food seasoned down for Americans :)

Love the new location! Staff was very friendly and helpful. Our standby is the pita and hummus trio, but the gyros are extremely flavorful. Will keep coming back! One note though- they only have single stall bathrooms, one for men, and one for women- huge lines! Kind of ridiculous for that large restaurant. Management- do something, maybe change them to unisex?

Fantastic Indian food. Great curry sauces. Dont know what else to say- i have never dined in at the drexel hill location but i have in the media location and its even better when you sit down. I love their take out too.

My wife and I had dinner there on Friday night. nice atmosphere.. We really liked the food ...especially the Ginger Chicken as good as it gets.. the Shrimp Pad Thai. was very tasty and we had the Spring rolls the kind that isnt deep fried. the sauces were really tasted good. they had a great selection of Asian Beers. we intend to bring out gang there for Date Night. the owner came out and greeted us. very nice touch.. check it out if your in the neighborhood out by Opry Mills . Until the next time.

Mood Cafe is still delicious, even two years later! My best friend and I went back yesterday to celebrate her birthday and, yet again, the owner asked if it was our first time and offered to make us lassis until we were satisfied. As always, the food was delicious and I only needed my lassi made once. I ordered the Queen lassi - yes, based on the name alone - and could not have asked for a more delicious drink.

We've been here few times over the years; primarily when craving Dosa - as its name suggest. Just like any other cuisines, try to order food that is its house special . Being that it is a dosa and chat house, please everyone stick to those items - you won't regret it. As compared to some who tried various chicken items and were less than thrilled with their order. I only get Dosa here and this is the only place i go, to stave my dosa cravings!!!! That being said, I am giving it a 3 start for their lackluster service. Over and over again, I'm thoroughly disappointed with their service. But, the food keeps drawing me in.... and that too driving 30-40min way out of the way to just eat there... Next time you are visiting this place, stick with dosa only. Some of their chaat items can be disappointing.

I heard this place was pretty good and I got a Groupon and tried it out. I will 1st rate the food and then the other items. The #4 Spring Rolls with Pork were wonderful and the 2 different Pho's were great that we ordered. Very Happy with the food! Was not happy with the staff nor wait. 1. I had to get my own menu when I sat down as the English speaking waiter when into the back and the other just smiled at everyone. Very nice but.... 2. Then I ordered Spring rolls to start and asked him to start them as I waited for my daughter and it took 35 minutes to get them. 3. The table next to me also took 35 minutes to get theirs and it took us all about 1 hour from start of order time to get the Pho. When I arrived there were only 5 tables, so I think the Kitchen staff is not up to handling more then a few tables at a time along with their takeout. This is the only reason I will not go back in the near future. Maybe I have to try the order on phone and take out.
First time here and the food was not memorable. The Thai flavor is not there at all compared to many other Thai restaurants.
The best Thai, until today. Ordered Pad Thai, was pretty good. Also ordered summer rolls. The best was green tea ice cream.
Lovely at home feel with delicious food. Vegan and vegetarian choices too! Great choice with great service

Ordered the chili chicken appetizer, garlic naan, and chicken saagwala. While waiting on my food I took note of the number of patrons; me and two tables of 4. Very slow and very quiet. The chili chicken arrived first and it delivered. The chicken chili had a good amount of heat and was tender with crunchy bell peppers and onions. Half way through the water works turned on and the heat got to me. Glad they left the water because two glasses later and I was done. The waiter cleaned up my appetizer plate and I asked him to leave the chili chicken as I was going to eat more. He then brought out the saagwala and garlic naan. The smells were overwhelming. The naan was good, crisp but not too crispy and great flavor. The saagwala, a chicken and spinach dish, contained fork tender chicken thigh pieces, almost a creamed spinach and a mild spice consisting of turmeric, cumin , garlic, and a hint of cinnamon. The rice was seasoned with some sort of flower and I got a pod and stem. The pod, which I accidentally bit into, left a bitter taste in my mouth and reminded me of potpourri. Found out that it was a cardamom pod. Only reason this place did not get five stars was because of the location and the decor. While sitting in the restaurant I saw numerous motel occupants walking through the parking lot and they looked shady. Plus 2 police cars drove through the parking lot, one even turn on his spot light and shined it towards the restaurant, oh so glad I walked here. The decor was exactly what others had stared, straight out of the 70's or the golden girls. The aunt of the owner, sitting at the table near me, complained that the woman's restroom had a broken toilet, but the men's room was fine and in working order, again just dated I'd like to come again and try the chicken tandoori and a different naan. Looking forward to another good meal

I was here on Monday and the manager was yelling at his employees and saying they needed to be faster and that they needed to run their own orders because he didn't want to. The servers were all doing great. Horrible management! For working in walking distance, I will NOT be back!

Tried this place bc I was craving some pho and my boyfriend is obsessed with Vietnamese food. We were excited to have a new place uptown for Vietnamese bc we usually venture to Kenner for some good pho. Atmosphere-wise...ehh. The place was a little too bright and too loud for a Sunday night crowd. We tried the egg rolls as an appetizer- they were pretty delicious (served with fish sauce). Then tried pho and banh mi as entrees. Banh mi was good. Meatlovers pho just wasn't as good as we were expecting. Being picky pho eaters, we would probably try something else if we go back. Overall, good but not great.

We love Smiley's! Fantastic middle eastern food and the best service you could ask for. Love that you can sit outside. The owner is so friendly. I had the Shwarma pita and it was made quick and delicious. The hummus gives it a great flavor. The lemonade was the best lemonade I ever had (when I was a kid my parents used to take us for Rita's water ice before they franchised when Rita herself used to make it by hand. We always got the lemonade flavor. It had bits of lemon rind in it and was slightly sweet with a delightfully subtle bite. Smiley's lemonade tasted just like that. This was our second or third time at Smiley's and we will be back again for sure.

Great restaurant inside of a hip hotel. We had the conch croquette, steak tartar, curried goat and the mousse for dessert. The bread at the start was awesome! biscuits with chive butter. soo good. I had the noble gardens drink (gin, tequila, poblano, cilantro, celery, cucumber) - refreshing and interesting. The food was very good - although we thought the curried goat was overhyped. We totally love goat, and this is their signature dish - but it just didn't do it for me. Service is really good and coming on a weekday early made for a chill and enjoyable experience.

I've been here a few times while in Clayton on business. The cuisine is pretty straightforward and I have found the quality to be consistent. The service is accommodating and pleasant and take-out is prompt and accurate. I enjoyed the pad thai. You can ratchet up the heat as you like it.

Very good food and very good service. My wife and I randomly decided to stop in here and we are so glad we did. The Sag Paneer was amazing. Same with the chicken tikka masala and paal appam. Seriously. So good. Try this place if you want amazing Indian food with very reasonable pricing and great service. Thanks to India Sizzling 2 for making our dinner portion of date night a success!!!!

I've been to Fulin's at different locations before, but at this location, my experience wasn't all that. I went on a Sunday evening and I had a party of 4. It wasn't busy at all there were maybe 5 tables at that time. The booth we got was so small & the table wasn't very clean. The menu's were flthy. They were really sticky and had stuff on it. The food took forever. I probably won't be going back to this location.

I fell in love with this place when I moved to Philly about 8 years ago and for good reason. The fish is amazingly fresh and the restaurant is, shall we say, an experience. It's very small with an open kitchen so you actually feel the heat. This location is BYO which is always a plus. The hummus is fantastic and the octopus is one of my favorites anywhere. If you're not local, parking around the place can be as hard as Chinese arithmetic. Also, expect to wait for a table most nights as the place is popular, crowded, and tiny. They'll likely send you across the street to New Wave Cafe to wait for your table. Don't worry, they won't forget you.
A bit of a dive, but that's part of its charm. Food was good and well priced, service was what you would expect.

My boyfriend uses Yelp to find places to eat sometimes, and he had found this place back in September or October and we went. It's tucked away in a commercial area from what I remember, and not all that large, but that's part of the charm. The owners are wonderful, and the wife is so your Greek mother type (if you've seen My Big Fat Greek Wedding .. the mother .. THAT). My boyfriend and I were pretty well stuffed but trying to finish off the little bit we had left. The wife came over and said "You need more rice?" and we tried to say no thank you but she said "I get you more rice!" and ran off. I was in no way offended, mostly amused. We did try and eat the rice that she brought as not to be rude though. The kabob platter my boyfriend and I shared was wonderful. It puts all kabob I've had since to shame. Actually writing this review is making me want some. I would recommend this place over Kabab & Curry any day. They do have a high chair, and it's not your industrial style highchair, but a real high chair. The chairs and tables are ones you would find in someones dining area. I likely wouldn't go there if I were in a rush to eat and get out, because it's seemed like a very relaxed type of environment when we were there.
Awesome Grape Leaves and Falafel. About time something successful takes over this spot. Will be back for sure!

Seeing as there was not one Indian working in the place (we were served by all Nepalese and one Bhutanese guy) it was one of the BEST Indian restaurants I've been to in awhile! I'd give the fennel bread a pass but my veggie dishes were great and the rice was just supurb along with with above board service, friendly atmosphere all topped off with a BYOB.. this vegetarian is going back for more!

This BYOB uses mostly organic ingredients plus makes everything in-house. I wanted to try as many dishes as possible so I opted out of the entree and instead ordered several appetizers. For our main dishes we ordered the calamari, saganaki and bureki and the lamb kofta entree. The Calamari was served with a side of Armenian tomato dip. It was perfectly cooked and tasted light, crispy and tender.Next up was the Saganaki- a favorite of mine. The pan friend halloumi cheese was served in ouzo and lemon sauce with a delicious caramelized fig and side salad. This was one of the best I've had...including those which were devoured on many restaurants in Athens, Mykonos and Paros. The Bureki was served next: a fillo pastry parcel stuffed with feta and thyme drizzled with honey served with a side of roasted beats. The presentation was so beautiful with a taste to match. Crispy layers of fillo oozing with feta cheese. The Count found that the honey made it more appropriate for dessert but I loved it, especially the presentation. The lamb kofta was served next. It was a skewer of ground lamb kofta mixed with apricot and pistachios served with a side of pomegranate salad, lentils and Greek yogurt. The lamb was excellent filled with magic flavors. But what truly made it special were the side dishes. The pomegranate salad was so original. I've never had pomegranate served as a salad as in Iran it tends to be eaten as a fruit or juiced. The mixture of pomegranate with onions and spices was excellent. Then there was the lentil salad which was again a first for me. I mixed spoonfuls of the kabob, pomegranate and lentil salad together and found the combination to be intoxicating. The quality of the ingredients are present in each spoonful. You can tell that the chef really prides himself on his food. For dessert we ordered the pistachio and olive oil cake and warm chocolate mousse. Both desserts were out of this world. I really loved the pistachio cake it was light yet intense in flavors served with a side of pistachio ice cream and cherries. The Chocolate mousse was baked to perfection oozing with warm gooey chocolate served with a scoop of ice cream. Wow. Is all I can say about this restaurant. I loved the food, the presentation and the friendly chef. Kanella offers rustic home-made dishes with fresh and mostly organic ingredients. I was very impressed and can easily say this was one of the best places I've yet to dine

Wow! Maybe because I was overdue for south of the border cuisne but Delicia hit it out of the park. A unique, eclectic but comfortable dining room, super friendly staff and unique and v-e-r-y delish food. Can't wait for a repeat!
Cute and romantic little Thai place. The food was tasty but both my boyfriend and I felt sick immediately after leaving the restaurant. There is definitely better Thai food in the area.
We love this place. I go every time we are in town. The food is great and the scenery is cool. Our server was awesome and the prices are fair. Order the mahi mahi tacos!

The food here was one of the best Indian places in the area. The restaurant was decorated beautifully with some nice Indian accents. The place seemed very clean and the wait staff were friendly. We ordered the lamb korma and then butter chicken. Both were delicious. The korma was a bit sweet for my taste but the dish is known for that. My girlfriend loved the food here. We'll definitely be coming back to try some other dishes.

So, the sandwich I had, Wishboner is a funny name unless mom is ordering and then it's just awkward. The vibe of the place kind of turned me off because the young lady that was working didn't have the best example of customer service and the seating area outside was kinda messy. Luckily my friends and I were more focused on eating than what the service on the other side of the counter was. I will say that a combo is a better bet if you're hungry but if you're a bigger person and really want to fill up, it'll cost more than the food is worth. As far as flavor, the Wishboner was good but the potato salad was overly saturated with dressing and very small size. The tomatoes in the sandwich were sad and old, that was disappointing too. If you just want a flavorful chicken sandwich, try it early in the night or around lunch time maybe with hopefully more energy at the counter and in the dish presentation, but move on. The highlight of my visit was the option for Birch Beer at the soda machine.

I ordered the falafel wrap & fries & the food was quick & fantastic!! I completely recommend this place for anyone who is in a hurry & doesn't want a lucky dog or a slice . The photos on the walls show a piece of boxing history with a personal touch. There were plenty to look at while I waited for my meal. This restaurant is cash only with an atm inside for your convenience. A few tips for a better Mardi Gras experience- 1)bring cash or use an atm. This is not the time or the place to be cheap. 2) tip your bartenders/servers/parking attendants generously. They deal with a ton of craziness & have bills to pay. 3) A please, thank you & a good attitude go along way. Everyone is here to have a good time. Lines happen. Please be patient & don't sweat the small stuff!
Came here for lunch and the food and service was great. It's cash only at lunch. I can't wait to come back for dinner with a bottle of wine!

Really enjoyed this little gem of a restaurant. Had the Shish Tawoo...it was amazing. My son had the Hummus and Meat. It was a little small of a dish for him, but, I had so much chicken he did not go hungry! Cannot wait to go back.

Ok, I really wanted to like a neighborhood ethnic restaurant, and after reading the reviews I was excited. BUT..who is reviewing this place? Relatives? From the second we walked in, I wasn't feeling warm and fuzzy. The place smelled like Clorox and dirt. There was a drill gun sitting out on the bandstand. Not good signs, but still had hope for the food. As I was sitting down (butt still not on the chair), waitress asks me what I would like for an app. OK. Ordered the spring rolls. Mind you, I've had spring rolls from Mai Lee, Webster Garden, etc., so I know a decent spring roll. Their's was not. Shrimp was pretty much absent, or if it was shrimp, they weren't whole. Ok, still hoping for a turnaround. I ordered the Spicy Steak, gf ordered fried rice. I tried her fried rice, and I've had better from Chinese takeout, but still edible. But my dish? NOT edible. The meat was like jerky. A couple pieces I had a hard time sticking my fork into it. Rice was not fresh. Maybe they were having a bad day. Everyone has one right? Yes, but as the restaurant should then try to make amends, right? After our meal, I told the waitress "Can I just say a few suggestions?" Well, I wasn't expecting anything free, but maybe a sorry or something. Nope, she just said, "oh" and took our check. We then waited 10 minutes for our change and we were 1 of 2 tables there. This is Stl. You have to have your game face on when you open. Yes, there are growing pains, but if your missing 2 legs, football might not be the sport for you. Effort goes a long way with subpar food, and when you lack effort and good food, hmmmm, hope the lease isn't long. All the people who gave this place a good review, go to Mai Lee or Webster Garden and be truly gratified.

it makes no sense how this delicious of food can come from a food truck... but holy crap is it delicious! To all those food truck skeptics, you must try this one. Cucina zapata is a Thai-Mexican fusion, featuring dishes from all over Asia. They're known for their captain crunch tilapia burrito (which is phenomenal!), as well as their Thai short rib tacos and their chicken satay tacos. They also offer chicken katsu; get this with an egg, extra avocado, and "bossy" you will literally not regret it.

Went to Mo' Ziki's due to the reviews on Yelp, I wasn't disappointed. My wife and I entered the restaurant and checked out the menu. Well, we must have looked baffled because one of the employees walked over and helped us navigate the menu. Turns out his name is Jeff, and he is the owner. He explained it all to us and away we went. I had a Gyro wrap (on wheat) with cooked peppers and onions. Down the line I added Kalamata olives, classic feta cheese, and Roasted garlic Ziki sauce. My Bride opted for the Hot Veggies Pita with cheddar cheese, Romaine lettuce, and Ranch dressing on the side. We also had a side of Original Hummus with warm Pita bread, mmmm good. We had a nice conversation with Jeff. He told us of his experience in the food industry. This is his first rodeo as an owner, he's been in business for about a year and a half. Franchises are available for this unique restaurant. My wife (she's the real critic) and I agreed this was a great value and even better meal. We will return for sure.

My girlfriend and I went to eat here she was there a few times. Small friendly in the neighborhood to locals. For it's size they were busy with takeout dining in. The staff friendly authentic Indonesian food. Spicy dishes tasty new for me but liked it all great prices would recommend if you can find it lol, parking is tough but worth it. Enjoy.....don't take credit cards bring cash.
Great Jamaican food that everyone should check out for sure. I ordered a jerk chicken platter and beef patties. Delicious and hot.

Whoa...the biggest food truck I've ever seen. You can probably fit a bed in there! That probably reflects Mr. Bui's success. He (and others) serves things on a long French-like roll in large portions. I got something with egg, sausages, and mushrooms plus some Bui sauce. It was a short wait in the rain, and Mr. Bui had a yellow umbrella set up outside. Even at 10 30 AM, there were about 5-10 people at any one time on a Sunday morning at 10:30 AM. This place is open even on the weekends, an affordable and convenient way to cure a hangover.

When we moved from the east coast we lost our favorite Korean restaurant :( but luckily found Hangook Kwan!! Delicious Korean pancake and traditional bibimbap (salivating!) make this spot a fave! Seems like it might be a slightly hidden gem as it rarely is full so give it a try you'll love it!

Solid joint. Walked in for lunch. Portions are generous. Had the yellow rice, black beans, stew chicken, and fried plantains. Everything was exactly what I was looking for, flavorful Dominican food! Service was fast and friendly. Only thing missing is better drink options.

My boyfriend and I were still craving Indian since the failed attempt to try clay oven from the night before, so we read reviews and tried Gateway to India and were not the least bit disappointed!! The atmosphere was inviting, the staff was very friendly and I hate to say this but we felt better about the fact that they were actually Indian; so we knew "authentic Indian cuisine" would be accurate. We got an appetizer of barnarsi samosa & peshawari (cheese) naan & both were delicious! Then we both got chicken tikka masala and I got veggies in it with no extra charge. We ordered more naan to eat with our meals so we went with garlic this time. I took a couple bites and was full from the appetizers but I have awesome left overs to bring to work now =). Then we were asked if we would try a complimentary dessert and we felt bad saying no so we did; they looked like two soggy munchin donuts in a small bowl and tasted like buttery coconut goodness..really the only way to describe them. We will definitely be back!!!
I absolutely love this place! Fantastic food! Good service! And great ambiance. I would refer anyone! They will love it! You can find something tasty.

Oh Momo's where to start....this was my first time here. My siblings many times here. Service was not as great as expected. We saw our server a couple times. Others had brought our food out. I would rate this establishment as a 2.5 if that was an option. What we ordered... Roasted Red Pepper Hummus: absolutely delicious! The best hummus I've had in awhile! The bread was nice and warm. Downfall, they should provide more pita. Grilled octopus: first bite was good. Second bite wasn't so sure. Third bite...I just wanted to throw up. I love octopus but and this was something different....perhaps spoiled octopus? The only dish that just sat there because no one could eat it. Bacon Phyllo: I love phyllo in general, the people in my party do too! The description is BACON phyllo...and non of us were able to taste the bacon at all! Lobster Mac n Cheese: we all enjoy this dish! Way super creamy and cheesy with chunks of lobster! Yum! For the dish we expected the noodles to be a little softer for Mac n cheese style. Traditional Gyro: this gyro was absolutely delicious! We all enjoyed this very much! A matter of fact it we killed this dish before all other food lol. The meat is very flavorful. And all the veggies and tzatiki were superb! Overall, some food was good, some was ehh. What bothered me the most was that there's a trash can right next to the soda machine with ice. The ice was not covered. The trash was next to it. I saw employees throw trash in it and some bounced off into the ice. Yuck! And very unsanitary.

The restaurant was beautifully decorated. A great spot for a date! Portions are huge so we split a larger entree and added on a skewer. Everything was delicious! Baklava is made on site! We will definitely be back.

Finally tried this tonight for dinner. We love Indian food! And this one just became one of our favorite. Having just recently moved from Orlando, we love finding great places to eat at our new hometown. The butter chicken is soo good. The Gobi 65 is aahhhmazing with just the right amount of heat. And the Rasmalai - my favorite!! We'll be back for sure.

A big 2 thumbs up!!! We were hesitant at first because we've never been to this place before. But I have to say that the food exceeded my expectations! The portions are not big but everything we ordered was tasty. We ordered Pad Thai, Pad See Yew, Tom Yung Gung (sour soup with shrimp), Basil Beef, Chicken Curry and the Spicy Eggplant. I've been to a lot of Thai restaurants and I can honestly give this place a good recommendation. The server was also super-friendly and kept checking on us. Give this place a try...you won't be disappointed!!!!
This place is so yummy! Try the pho and the spring rolls, also the vegan eggrolls are very delicious! Also quick and friendly service! It's our favorite place in town! We love it

My wife orders catering and takeout from this place all the time and also goes there for happy hour and takes our kids there for dinner sometimes. The owner, Pushpinder, is always extremely accommodating and kind. The service is great, food is delicious and with the recent remodeling, the ambiance is wonderful too. They work hard to ensure that you enjoy your dining experience. It is so nice to have a great indian restaurant nearby.

I order from here at least once a week. The food is always good and service is friendly. They don't have massamun curry on the menu but I asked for it a couple times and they had no problem making it. My go-to now is panang curry with chicken. I've also had their mango sticky rice and bubble tea smoothies -- they're good as well!

My wife and I were here this evening after buying a LivingSocial coupon. Between the two of us we ordered the Tulip Dumplings, the Plah Kung Salad, and one of their special items of the day - an "Evil Jungle Noodles." Of these three dishes, the dumplings were very average and the plah kung salad was also ho-hum. As I was writing the review, I went back to their menu and noticed that the description of the tulip dumplings says that they include a mix of chicken, shrimp, and crabmeat. Well let me tell you that I did not find the taste of crab meat in those dumplings! Certainly when compared with Chinese restaurants in Center City, the tulip dumplings were quite disappointing. The Plah Kung Salad which was a "regular" salad served with grilled shrimp and bell peppers was fine but as my wife pointed out, it had a little too much of the spicy lemon & lime vinaigrette in the salad itself and the dressing could have been given on the side. The other issue which I had with the salad is that I am used to having salads that are served cold (or at least not warm) but that was not the case here. I am not sure if it was on account of the grilled shrimp or because the ingredients had been kept outside a fridge, the salad appeared *warm* to me and that threw me off a bit. For all of their shortcomings though, there was one dish which really hit the right notes and that was the evil jungle noodles. Think of it as drunken (rice) noodles but one that also uses coconut milk in its preparation, which gives it an extra kick. W.r.t. the spiciness, although the dish was shown as having 3 chills next to it which translates to pretty spicy, we found the spiciness very manageable. Granted we do have some serious spicy food, but compared with what we might cook ourselves or even some Asian dishes that we have at restaurants, this dish was not particularly spicy. Besides the food, we appreciated the service which was quick. Also, our waitstaff were courteous and attentive in ensuring that our glasses were full all throughout the evening. They handled the LivingSocial coupon promptly as well. We left shortly before the restaurant closed at 10:00 p.m. but did not feel rushed at all. In fact, one of our servers asked us (possibly around 9:45 p.m.) if we would like to order something from the dessert menu, but being too full we passed up on that. As we were leaving, we noticed that there was another party (possibly parents with their daughter) also seated and chatting away comfortably. Lastly, we enjoyed the ambience of the restaurant and felt that it fit well with the food. Overall, our experience was pretty positive and hence the (relatively) high rating. Things that take a star away are some of the issues I mentioned earlier with the dumplings and the salad. Also, when I did call them to make a reservation, they said that they don't seat patrons beyond 9:15 p.m. Now when the restaurant says that it stays open until 10:00, it seems a bit too much not to have patrons come in after 9:15. I would have certainly liked the ability to come in by say 9:30 because we did have to alter our plans slightly to make sure that we were there at the restaurant before 9:15 p.m. However, all things considered, I know that we will be back here again for some good Thai food along with good service and recommend that you also give this place a shot.

Man was this food fantastic and a welcome change from standard Indian fare. No tikki masala, no saag paneer - nope, none of that. Instead, TiffinEtc was a wonderful way to spend my lunch hour and my coveted lunch money. I split three dishes with a friend, and this was the perfect amount. First, the Indian Pizza. We split a personal sized Saag Paneer pizza - the size would have been perfect for one very hungry person as your only meal. The pizza was pretty good - I would only give it a three, but that might be because I was spoiled by amazing Indian Pizza when I lived in SF (http://www.zantespizza.com/). There was a bit too much ricotta and not enough strong indian flavoring for my taste. Next we had the Gobhi Paratha, which was pretty fantastic. The Paratha was a bit soggy, but not terribly so. The innards of onions and cauliflower were amazing and the chutney was great (although not plentiful enough). The raita was bizarrely tangy - I'm not sure if that was intentional or not, but it wasn't my thing. Finally, we had a Masala Aloo Kati rolls, which were fantastic. It was basically an indian burrito (or is a burrito a mexican kati?) with delicious spicing and amazing potatoes. All in all, this was a fantastic meal, and all for $14.50! I can't wait to go back to try the masala pepsi!

I was feeling a little under the weather, and the Spicy Shrimp Pho here helped revive me! I've only ever had pho made with beef parts, so this was something of a revelation to me. The shrimp broth is clear, savory, and a little sweet; it tastes clean and comforting, and was very different from a typical beef pho broth. There were plenty of rice stick noodles, scallion bits, fried shallots, and shrimp (7 fairly large shrimp in my bowl), and of course, the accompanying Thai basil, bean sprouts, jalapeno, and lime. I also liked the slick of chili oil over the top of this pho, which is the "spicy" component -- the broth itself isn't really spicy. I didn't add any hot sauce or hoisin to this broth, so it was really good stuff. I came in here during a weekday lunchtime and the place was pretty quiet -- maybe 5 other parties, so service was quick. The soundtrack left something to be desired (acoustic guitar covers of the worst 2000 era soft pop songs) but I can't really give them too much grief for that. All in all, this was a great comfort meal for $12 with tax and tip, and it's too bad that the people of New Orleans can't experience how wonderful this hot pho would be on a reaaaallly cold day!
Has the veg I roll and veggie kebabs. Suffice to say I won't BA back. Too salty and nothing homely about the food. Rather bland. Nothing soulful about the food. Ambience is like

This was the first Thai place we tried in Boise, about 3 weeks ago. I liked the inside of the restaurant, but I did not like the food. I had a bad experience with the the spiciness. See, before I lived in NYC and Phoenix and all the Thai places we were to there had Mild Medium Hot and Thai Hot. So I always get Medium. They have 1-5 stars here. I asked for Medium, 3 stars on my curry. Oh, my mistake. Apparently 3 stars is NOT Medium. I can handle spicy but I couldn't eat this. It was burning my mouth. I felt awful because I never return food, but I really could not physically eat it. Another waitress (or manager, I'm not sure) came and helped me out. She got me a new one with a much more manageable spiciness level. Unfortunately the flavor was not really good. She helped me with my burned mouth by giving me really, really hot water and saying to sip it, that it will burn, but help the problem. It really did help. I guess just because of the traumatic experience that I will not be returning here. My husband says his food was good, but nothing special. He gives it 3 stars.

Tried Jamaican Jerkhuts food at the PHS pop up garden. Food took forever. It came from a take out window that was unattended most of the time. Couldn't figure out the system, whether they would bring me my food or call me. After waiting forever, another patron came to my table and said the Jamaican Jerkhut people had my food. I walked up and no one was there. I had to bother other people dining there to track down an employee to get my food. For $17, I got a single skewer of tiny over cooked spiced shrimp and a big container of rice and cabbage with two tiny pieces of fried plantain. The poor service already ruined my mood. The food just added insult to injury. I don't think I'll ever dine there based on the meal I got tonight.

Ring the doorbell to be let into what seems like another world, get seated (hopefully with a group of good friends) around an intimate table surrounded by authentic Moroccan decor, and enjoy a fabulous 7-course meal for $25. I kid you not. Such a place exists right off South Street. Part of me wants to give you every last detail of our experience at Marrakesh, and yet another wants to keep quiet and let you be surprised, just as we were. In fact, we originally planned on an Italian restaurant for the night, yet we were not sad for long upon realizing it was closed because the night then took us to nearby Marrakesh, where we were absolutely delighted by every detail of the dinner. Because life is all about expectations, and I don't want to boost yours too much, I'll divulge only select details of our experience. We were taken up to the third floor (all of us giggling all the while, thinking "where the puck are we?"), and sat down by a server who very kindly and briefly went through the seven courses. They happily accommodated for the vegetarians at the table. Then out came course after course of deliciousness, all of which went perfectly with the red wine that we brought. Towards the end, a belly dancer came around to each of the rooms. I am only slightly ashamed to say that I was absolutely mesmerized! From what I can tell, it was very authentic dancing. Never having experienced anything like this, and having had my share of libations, I sheepishly held up a $1 bill, only to be grabbed by the hand and danced with! We were all hysterical. I slipped the bill into her waistband. Just come here. Don't waste your time reading too many reviews. Call up your favorite friends and bring them here without telling them what the deal is. We had an incredible time and enjoyed great food for an even better price, and walked outside only to see a line of the next eager customers waiting.

The food was excellent. But the waitress was not friendly at all, and it wasn't busy. Maybe she was just having a bad day but it wouldn't kill her to smile once in a while. But the salad was delicious I'll definitely go back.

Yet another awesome business that might fall victim to the curse of this location. I've seen several young, empasdioned chefs open up here and have an empty restaurant. This pork ramen is REALLY GOOD. I've also had the fried rice and the garlic prawns. Both are amazing. Check them out and help them stay afloat. It's empty on this Monday night at 7:30.

I haven't been to the buffet yet, only for dinner. Menu is very detailed in what to expect four those unfamiliar with the cuisine. Huge portions that are great to share and take home to eat the next day. Friendly staff and clean restaurant. I will have to try the buffet next!

My husband and I visited Smiley's right at opening time on a sunny Monday afternoon. We were greeted by pleasant staff and the restaurant seemed very clean and orderly. My husband got the beef shwarma pita and I had the falafel pita. Both were very good and had wonderful flavor. I took off one star because the food was not quite as warm as I would have liked; certainly not cold, but more lukewarm. Overall, very delicious and we would definitely return!

We went here twice in one weekend... it was SOOOOOOOO GOOD!!! The service was great, fast and the portions were PERFECT. I had the param rongsong-- steamed spinach, peanut sauce and pork. Hubby had pad thai and sticky rice. The presentation was impeccable and the service was fast!! I would HIGHLY recommend Zen Yai Thai Cuisine for anyone in SB!!
I have came here 3 times for lunch, the service is good and food delicious. It is always empty, not sure why because the prices are very reasonable and food was good.

One of my favorite places to stop when driving to Clearwater. I purposely take a detour to get their bahn mi sandwiches and bubble tea. The sandwiches are delicious and the bubble tea flavors are great. I really like supporting this local shop and you should as well! Only downside is that service can be slow at times so you should be prepared you won't be getting fast food speeds.

First time here. It is amazing. Sat at the bar - which was nice - and had cocktails and dinner. Fresh made chips and three salsas were paired nicely with a fresh, homemade margarita. The Fire and Ice lives up to its name. Best followed by a cold, draft beer. And the food ... not sure what I expected but the food surpassed expectations. I need more duck enchiladas. The scallop tacos were good but my husband will be trying something new next time. Cannot wait to return. If you go, be prepared for on street (parallel) parking.
Very good Thai at a reasonable price. Standard walk up counter order and they bring to table. 7 tables, quiet on a Tuesday night but many people picking up take out. Recommend.
Siam is the best place in Carpinteria for Asian cuisine.

Sheri Punjab is deliciano. Tandoori chicken is good so is the aloo matar. Since we were kids, we ate there off and on. The waiters always fill your beverages really quickly. The food was ready quickly and delicious. I would highly recommend Sheri Punjab to all who like this type of cuisine.

If grandma is Dominican, Cuban or Puerto Rican, you won't be disappointed. It's not exactly as can be had in Miami but very close. There is a Cuban and Dominican in the kitchen so the flavors are very close. If you've never eaten Cuban / Dominican / Puerto Rican food, take the drive. It's very good food. Huge portions. I don't expect the kitchen to be large and not built for high volume so a group of 15 plus a regular dinner crowd could have caused problems with food delivery. There were four of us - not as fast as an Applebee's but then again, it's not an Applebees. Waiters are college kids so they aren't familiar with the different plates available..

I've had my eye on the Mood Cafe for months. Every time I log into Yelp, there it is sitting in the top 5, eye balling me. I passed by it several times, and though that place looks interesting. After awhile, my mind starting asking, "Why haven't you gone to Mood Cafe?" So, I finally took these thoughts out of my mind and tried to get my wife to go. At first, she was a skeptic and did not want to go. On my third attempt, she finally gave me the why not approval. After going, we both should be asking, what is wrong with us. This place Amaze!
