It looks like a small place with not much to offer. The two main menu items are Lassis and Chaat. I've had a Lassi before, and it's always been Mango. But this place had like 25 Lassi flavors. But what is a Chaat I wondered? The owner who was working there on our visit explained. There is so much that goes into a Chaat, he lost me somewhere along the way. But what was not lost was my intrigue. I go the Crazy Chicken Chaat. The crazy was their way of saying it's a chicken and beef combo. The beef reminded me of taco meat, but the kind that is seasoned extremely well. Watching him make the Chaat was like watching an artist. It was like Jackson Pollack at work with the piling on so much stuff. A threw a bunch of stuff down. Then he added 3-4 sauces. He threw more stuff down. Added more sauces. And then he threw more stuff down. Not sure I remember it all, but there was mango, almonds, crispy noodles, dates, potato, and, and, and... yeah that's what I remember. But I know there was more. When I put this goodness in my mouth, it was like a party of flavors. It tasted so fresh and nothing like anything I had tasted before. I was in love. I also had a peach Lassi which was excellent. My wife had the same dish as me, but got the blueberry Lassi. I liked her Lassi even better. I so am going back to this place. You should go too!

Decent place for food, cheap and the quality is okay. But the wait for the food is absolutely unbearable, it took them 40 minutes to make a chicken quesadilla wrap which is normally a 3 minute process. However I did get to bond with some other customers because they were also waiting for over 30 minutes. Not worth the wait in my opinion

I loveeee indian food, but I haven't ventured to many Indian restaurants since moving here...at least not as many as I would have liked to try at this point. This is hands down the best I've had outside of the south philly/center city area. Although the decor inside is sparse borderline looks-like-theyve-been-robbed, I've eaten at hole in the walls like this before and I know that decor definitely does not make or break a meal. The service was great and attentive...and I should hope so because we were the only ones dining in. There were a lot of customers in and out with take out and ordering meat (they sell raw meat that is purchasable for religious customs of how the meat was prepared, but I am not sure if it is Halal or Kosher or...?) The food was excellent, esp the okra dish and the chicken tikka masala. The garlic naan was awesome and thin / light, and the rice was steamed to perfection. Love everything we tried. Will be back!! The food also came out quickly.

Love this place! Glad they were able to expand cuz the customers were piling up - spilling out the door!!! I always get the Carondelet Shrimp (R-8) at lunch - well, I've tried other dishes which are good - but just keep going back to R-8 !!! I wish they would give me a bigger chunk of eggplant cuz I just LOVE that stuff!!! It is a very tasty a little spicy dish!!

Delicious Thai in this established clean and friendly restaurant that has been serving it up for many years in this locale. For appetizers the spring rolls are very good and the fried tofu is light and tasty with the dipping sauces made from scratch. We had several variations of Pad (beef, pork, chicken) and it was done expertly and the spice ratings are spot on, and spicy means just that! The chicken w bean sprouts and tofu is another nice mild dish when you want light and healthy eats. A big difference for me is that if requested they will not use msg and if your allergic it does matter alot. Wish more yelpers would spread that word around when doing reviews. I would like to see some table appetizers and something to close the meal like cookie or snack. Other than that the prices are very good and the entrees are on the mark. You will enjoy!

I was so excited when I found this place on Yelp while visiting Tampa for a conference. The first thing that struck me was the ambiance. It feels like luxury the moment you walk in. Then when we were seated the waiter was so friendly and made us feel at home. To top it off, the food was out of this world! I had the sampler which included jerk chicken, oxtail & curry goat. It was like I was in heaven! I'm sorry that I'm only here for one more day.

I live in Kanella's neighborhood and it is my favorite place to eat in the area. I have nothing to add to all the praise in the other 5 star reviews except to note how friendly they are to people dining with well-behaved dogs. The waiters have always brought out water for my dog along with some for me - which is a really good greeting.

Love this addition to the neighborhood. Great space, amazing food, and friendly, helpful service (which is something that has unfortunately felt lacking in east nashville lately). A little pricey once all is said and done, but still one of the best night out options around. P.S. Definitely get the whipped feta.

For my money this is the best Pho in New Orleans - the ingredients are fresh and the noodles have a nice spring to them. The broth is really the star - a lot of people will dose their Pho in all kind of sriracha and sauces and I feel like that would be an insult to the broth here. It stands on its own as not needing anything. It has a good mix of salt and fat without being overly heavy. I recommend getting the steamed vegetables added to your beef pho.
Great experience. The food and atmosphere were perfect. I wish that we were told that credit cards were not accepted. I had to go to an ATM in a Vape shop down the alley.

Had the pad thai with extra chili powder, and had an episode of sensory overload such that everything else tasted bland for two straight days. This is a serious joint with seriously good food. Besides the taste, the exotic smell, the sight of a choreographed kitchen routine and sound of chattering, this is a total immersion experience. Come early and hungry, and be ready to be dazzled in ways you never thought possible. Highly, highly, highly recommended.

Parkallen Pizza has consistently served my great pizza for a decade, both in restaurant and delivered to my door. The crust, the quality cheese, the sauce and all the toppings have always been top quality and generously applied to my pizza. Does it cost a little more that a super cheap two for one deal?... yes, but the pizza tastes three times as good and has twice the toppings.

The Mizu Asian Bistro team is consistently courteous. Staff remembers customers and is attentive to all aspects of the meal. They make everyone feel special whether it may be a mother or date with a mate. Freshness and presentation was great. We were even given a surprise app. roll with a unique name. Clean is also important to me, the place has been open since late winter early spring remaining neat and orderly. The mainliners and people from King of Prussia should check this spot soon. It is perfect for Pre- Cirque du Soleil!!!
I tried the vegetarian dooner, it was awesome. Friendly staff, generous portions, good ingredients.
Authentic and delicious food, very attentive service. Will go back for sure to taste different dish.
Been here a couple of times and the service is always friendly, helpful, and prompt.The Best Lamb Gyro ! One of the best place to eat Mediterranean in Saint Louis !
First time hitting them up and I was not dissapointed, I enjoyed the food and the total was not bad either. I highly recommend this spot!!

Brunch at Tryst was fantastic! We were promptly seated outside. It was a hot Florida day; we asked for the fans to be turned on and that allowed us to enjoy outdoor seating in July. Their kitchen does not open until 11:30 am; we put in our orders and while waiting for 11:30 we got ice cold water with lemon (note- we didn't have to ask for lemon, greatly appreciated!) The highlight of the brunch is definitely the Hangover Bloody Mary. It is a meal in itself. A very good Bloody Mary that comes with olives, a pickle, celery, bacon, cheese, tomato, and a delicious Slider! The special of the day was blueberry cornmeal pancakes. Although I'm not a huge fan of pancakes in general, those were excellent! They were filled with real blueberries, and lots of them. Amazing! I'll definitely be back!

Foodie Bunz here! This is a great Thai restaurant! Couple dishes we ordered... Pad Chan with shrimp, Tom Kha Gai & iced coffee. Overall all dishes are quite good n not super spicy if you are not into spicy food. Lots of flavour! Customer service is good 5/5. Very family owner type of restaurant. Interior is simple with a touch of Thai-ness 4/5 Food is very good 5/5 Prices are quite responsible n bill was around $30 for 2 of us Hope this helps-!! Foodie Bunz out!!!!
Service was great. Whipped feta and dates were great. Served partially raw chicken and the did take it and fix it but did not discount at all which in retrospect feels flawed.
Their Banh mi are tasty and juicy. Great for lunch! I also already had pho which has a good flavored broth (not just watery tasting).

I cannot get enough of this place. The service is always quick and the food is spot-on. Not a super busy place, which I think is a plus, but it's not for lack of deliciousness! Highly recommend the Mussamun Curry and Pad Thai. Also, the Crab Rangoon is perfection.

i had buffet was excellent ,specially chicken tandoori rice goat meat was soo good and had some takeout too ,i been there 3 /4 times had good experience with service and food , we had last time reservation around 80 peoples had very good discount and best food .I think you should try one time there .i recommend the best food on the area . i am planning to go next week , with my family too. thank you

My girlfriend and I just stopped by this place, we were looking for a new place for Boba Tea. I had a Jasmine Green Tea, Lychee and almond milk tea, absolutely delicious! The staff was very professional and welcoming. The layout is very modern and clean. We will definitely return!

I was a bit disappointed. Ordered the spicy beef soup and it wasn't hot or spicy enough. The soup had a flavor to it I didn't like. Their iced tea was great. Like that you can customize flavors. The place is very clean and the staff are friendly. I would go back just for the tea.

Boise needs this taste of the Middle East!! Growing up with this food, this is very authentic. Lunch kabobs specials for $7. Seriously, my kids ate every bite. Rice, salad with a perfect lemon dressing AND kabob... We had chicken, koobedeh, lamb, masto kahir, mango lasse, bakleva. The warm, kind man who waited on us was the cherry on top. This place is a must. We will be back.

Awesome spot , especially if you like to "choose your own adventure." I'm picky about what I can order since I try not to eat a lot of carbs, so rather than ask to "hold the rice, etc. , I can simply choose exactly what I want (as a salad for example.) For those that would rather just let the menu speak for itself, there's plenty of options there also.

Had a lovely experience there with my family. I've been to the one in Chattanooga so when they opened one in Cool Springs I was excited. First time my mom and I go in to check it out they gave us a coupon for a completely free dinner for a family of four - perfect for us! We were so pleasantly surprised... Not only did we love the food but the people there are so nice! This place is the best for a quick, delicious dish at a reasonable price with the coolest drink machine you've ever seen! It's become a favorite!

Great little Thai place, super casual and bright. Pad Thai left something to be desired, the flounder in an egg bath (don't remember the name) was actually good, something I've never tried before. The best part of the meal was the mango sticky rice - I will be back for that!

QUEEN OF SHEBA is an INCREDIBLE & unique find in a city inundated with thousands of restaurants. It is an Ethiopian restaurant and i have been here now about 6 times over the past couple years. I have NEVER even seen a glimpse of disappointment. It is absolutely DELICIOUS!! The restaurant is family owned and ran and you feel like you are transported from the moment you walk into the front door. It is very well laid out with a large table overlooking the street, then a small bar area with a larger area behind that housing a bunch of tables, both conventional and also traditional (low seats with a center coffee table high area for setting food into....VERY authentic & FUN). The service is GREAT and everything can be well explained to you if you are not familiar with the cuisine or style. Everyone is incredibly friendly & helpful. The food is EXTRAORDINARY on every level....taste, scent, preparation & presentation. It is very similar to a stew appearance on most items and so VERY flavorful in the best way. You do not have utensils (available if requested) but instead you are presented with a multitude of crepes which you use as a utensil by tearing off a piece, using it to pick up food & eating it. It is so much FUN. We have tried a sampler tray several times and it is a highly recommended way of trying out an array of items....the tray can be done as a meat tray or a vegetable tray or combination of both. There is a bar.....our consistent favorite is the TEJ WINE, a honey wine that perfectly compliments the Ethiopian flavors. Just Go & Enjoy the UNIQUENESS of Queen of Sheba. They do take reservations and it is well worth the trip to it!!

Love this place I am a big fan of the chicken pad Thai and spicy beef and pork noodle definitely recommend the smoothies the mango strawberry with strawberry jelly is the bomb staff is always friendly and clean establishment
Sushi was delicious and sooo fresh. This will definitely be my new go to spot for some great rolls!

Probably the only reason I am giving this place 3 stars is because I didn't have pho. I decided to grab the house friend rice, and it was lackluster, small portion, big price and no flavor. The pho my girlfriend was having seemed to be good and a great size portion! Service was good, and friendly staff.

I eat here at least 2 times a week. They have a celiac Menus and the staff are super helpful. They know me when I walk n and are prepared to take care of me. I appreciate their help and dedication to my safety when dealing with my allergies

The best Middle Eastern food I have ever had in Nashville metropolitan area. The food was tasty with real middle eastern flavor and spices. Great food, reasonably priced, and friendly hospitable owner and staff. We had Kozy and half chicken entrees, and they are all served with delicious rice, green salad and soup. We all, as well as our stomachs, left very happy and fulfilled for the rest of the day.

About as good as Thai food in Smyrna can possibly get! Great service, great appetizers, and great Pho! Stopped in after reading Robert S' review and had high hopes going into the dinner. I ordered up 3 apps to test them out, Fresh rolls, Won tons, and Eggplant. All 3 were great! Ordered the Pho Kai (Chicken) and the Pho... Fried Bacon! Lots of fresh garnishes, SUPER yummy broth! Really good Pho, especially considering the area. Service was AWESOME!! Our server helped up with the menu, ordering, and doctoring up the Pho (I thought I was an expert at this, but she was better). Perfect heat and flavor. More people stopped by to top off water and check on us, everyone was super friendly and made you feel at home. Our server brought us a sticky rice custard dessert with coconut. Perfect end to a great meal! I know it might not be the best Thai food in the world (that's in Thailand... duh) Or maybe not even in Nashville (but I bet it's close) But dang it all to heck, it's the best there is in Smyrna, and that's good enough for me! FIVE STARS!!!!

I've only been here for lunch during work and the food was great at a great price. Great and prompt service. However, the quality of the food has been a little inconsistent, but nothing below a 4 star. This will be my regular Thai joint in carp for sure.
This place is so amazing- I've been to Many authentic Greek restaurants over the years, and this one takes the cake. I come to Nashville twice a year and this place is a MUST!

Excellent food, friendly and helpful service Visiting Tampa on business. Took a few colleagues there after reading Yelp reviews. Everyone loved it. Fabulous flavor and very inexpensive. Highly recommend trying this place. For most in our group this was a 1st try at Ethiopian cuisine and Queen of Sheba did not disappoint!

I can't say if the food was good or not because we didn't get any! I called 2 days ago and made a reservation for noon on Wed. for a party of 8 for our company's Christmas luncheon. We all arrived in our Santa hats, in a festive mood only to find the place locked up tight and no one around!! REALLY!!!! It would have been a big check with a big tip. So we went around the corner to Sante Fe Mexican Grill and happily gave them our money. NEVER AGAIN.
very solid fare. definitely feels like a chain though. delicious food, but i would go elsewhere if you want ambiance.

Went a few weeks ago with two other couples. Service was slow and waitress was nearly invisible. Food was good, however portions were tiny. I mean Very tiny. The crab dumpling appetizer came with six gumdrop sized servings. The spring roll app was just two little, cut in half, rolls so you got 4 very small servings. Sure they were appetizers but I'm telling you it was a joke. My drunken noodle entries was good, but not any better than the 6 or so other Thai places I've tried. And ... surprise - it was finished in maybe 10 minutes, and I eat very slow. Was still Hungry when all was done. My (vegetarian) friend who highly recommended the place justified the tiny portions by saying it is Thai FRENCH. That's Hysterical. What wasn't Tiny was the 19+% they added to our bill because we were 6 or more people. Yes, I checked 4 different ways, it was 19+% which would be Fine if we saw the server more than 5x all night.

Dining experiences can be good for the food or for the service. At Thai Orchid, it's both. Delicious curries and other goodies await your hungry stomach. The staff are amazing friendly and make you feel as though you're a friend coming over for dinner rather than just a patron. From portion size and taste, to the charming staff, you're going to enjoy your dining experience at Thai Orchid!

Remedy is a really cool place to kick back and relax. The majority of patrons are students, art folk and bohemian hippie types. The reason for this is the atmosphere at Remedy - it's very chill and laid back. My fondest memory of Remedy is their apple pie. Oh, how I love apple pie! A lot of people go to Remedy for the chai. If you are a big chai fan, you need to check out Remedy because it is their claim to fame. Delicious! The food at Remedy is, for the most part, Indian food. It's a great snack and the spices will keep you warm on a cold Edmonton afternoon. Remedy also serves desserts, beer, coffee, and some other drinks. It's really just a great place to relax. If you haven't been to Remedy, I recommend giving it a try.

My second time trying this place out. Only because I saw the four star reviews. Well, I must say this place was delicious! My first mistake in trying this place was: I ordered take out. If you want the whole experience you MUST dine in. The menu was very lengthy, but I must return to try other things on the menu. We started with the appetizer which was the combo plater. I was able to taste the egg rolls, shrimp rockets and the marinated lemongrass beef. I ordered #92 and my kids ordered the stir fry chicken/chicken/carrots. My partner ordered the pho.My goodness it eas incrediable! They also enjoyed their meals. What I mostly enjoyed about the meals was that you could taste the freshness of each ingredients right down to the fresh broccoli! Oh, my we shall dine again there and many more times to come.

Our lunch group tried the lunch buffet today. The restaurant was clean, nicely decorated with Indian decor and had friendly service. The buffet items were superb; flavorful, exotic and a little spicier than other local Indian places, which is a plus for me since I like things hot and spicy. It wasn't over the top hot so don't let the slight heat scare you - it's more "generously spiced" rather than "burn your mouth hot" - although the eggplant masala did have a little "hot" kick. They had several dishes I haven't seen at any other Indian places in town including something called "Chicken 65" which was like boneless buffalo wings with a tandoori twist. very enjoyable. They also had old favorites like chicken tiki masala, several types of rice, dahl and many more plus about every type of chutney you can imagine. The only thing that was a little disappointing was the Gulab Jamun, usually it's my favorite Indian dessert but it wasn't up to par at this place. Give it a try - I know I'll be back!

I loved this place already but I needed to update my previous review to highlight their new brunch offerings: A group of ten friends and myself treated ourselves to brunch last weekend and sampled as much of the Delicia brunch menu as possible. Our orders ranged from Cuban Toast and coffee to Thyme biscuits and gravy with spicy (and very popular) Fire n' Ice Cocktail. All were delicious - I would know because my friends and I eat quite communally. As noted in my previous review, the service was spot-on. Lastly, I would like to note that I thought brunch menu prices were very reasonable. All meals ranged from $9 - $12 and were beautifully plated.

We love experimenting with food and Ethiopian being a cuisine we hadn't been exposed to, Abyssinia was a natural place to try. We walked in just after noon on a Saturday and the restaurant was empty. There was one other table in the side room. We were greeted right away with menus and water. The staff we encountered were all very friendly, but not overly so. We started with a crispy pastry filled with ground meat. It was delicious! Crispy without being greasy. Full off flavorful meat with just a hint of spice at the finish. For our entree, we tried the sampler #2. It came out on a large round crepe and the lovely women indicated what each dish was. We dug in with our ample amount of bread. The bread was cool to the touch, which may be perfectly normal, but it was a little odd. Most of the items on the tray were delicious. Very flavorful and not too spicy. We found that if I liked something, my husband didn't as much and vice versa. ... and then, the best way for me to say it, is that I was just done. The texture of the bread was unappealing to me. The food was flavorful, but soft. I hadn't eaten much, but I didn't want to continue. When I said this, Philip agreed that he had hit the same wall. So, we wrapped it up. On the way home, we were talking about it and I decided it left us with what I will forever call "food confusion." It liked it, but I didn't want to keep eating it. If it appeals to you and you're an adventurous eater - you must try it. I'm glad we went and I want you to try it, too.
It was okay. Since there is a lot of Thai in Nashville I kept comparing it to Thai esanse which is my favorite but generally the food is not bad but Thai esanse is better.

Very healthy food. Good price. Very Very beautiful inside. The only issue is time... It took so long to get my food They really need more chef....... Therefor, 4 / 5 is fair score due to slow service (cooking)
Best Indian you can get in Tucson and for a good price but there isn't a dinner buffet, which really is the shinning piece of places like this .
This is the best Indian food I have ever had. Really incredible!! I love the samosa, chicken tikka masala and just about everything I have tried on the menu.

Love this place, I'm from Detroit where delicious Mediterranean food is everywhere & always fresh- I haven't tried any of the fried food, but the Beef/Chix Shawarma is sooo delicious w/the garlic sauce & basmati rice! Excellent Service as well-

Went there for lunch with a co-worker. No lunch specials! But I got the Red Curry and it was awesome, yummy, spicy and warm! The spring rolls were good but the shrimp inside tasted rubbery. A bit of dim lighting and worn chairs but probably because each seat is full, and sat on alot. Service was so so - only 2 women working the lunch rush. Parking can be limited and alot of people park on the shoulder of the road. I'll be back the food make all those other small issues go away.
Great sandwiches made on fresh baguettes. Loved the cucumbers and cilantro on the barbecued pork sandwich.
Yum! They made me a special Banh Mi sandwich with tofu !

Cute bar area. 2 big screen TVs. Plenty of beer on tap. Tina tartare & ceviche were okay but not my favorite ever. The Asian pickles were actually a variety of pickled vegetables - carrots, cauliflower, cucumbers, & onions. Very good. My friend had the burger & said it was amazing. Other friend had the brisket pho & loved it.

We had the combo plate. It included lamb, beef, chicken, lentils, corn and spinach. While it was tasty, the spongy bread is EXTREMELY filling. Of course, this is the traditional way to eat Ethiopian. I loved experiencing the culture and food of Ethiopia, but it isn't my favorite world cuisine. If you enjoy eating with utensils, it may not be for you.

This is one of my favorite Sunday brunch spots. It is quiet and cozy. The restaurant is clean and the wait staff is very friendly and attentive. The buffet always has a good variety. The buffet does not go heavy on spice so you may want to order off the menu if you want spicy. They also always have several desserts and mango lassi on the buffet which is my favorite! Highly recommend.

We have eaten here twice, including today. I give it 4 stars because it is the best indian restaurant outside of philly downtown. I say this after living in downtown and southeast philly for almost a decade (& also haven eaten authentic indian in India !). I dont give it 5 stars only because we ordered malai kofta this evening and the kofta wasnt fresh. To the extent that we had to exchange it for Dum Aloo (which was great !) But I would still go to only two indian restaurants in the philly region - one is Cafe Spice in downtown and the other is Sher-e-punjab.
Each time I come I get the same thing.... A kabob with chicken and sausage. Just get it. Slide it off of the stick and mix it all together. You'll love it trust me.

Had dinner here, the servers we very nice and knowledgeable on the food. I think the problem is the kitchen, the food takes forever to come out, the food is all over the place on the plates and the fees they have are ridiculous.Also they were out of so many things. its a BYOB place and they charge $3 PER bottle or 6 six pack and $3 per person for entertainment fee?!? If you come with a group of people the fees exceed the price of the meal total. Also last but not least I would NEVER bring my kids or the elderly here we could smell the WEED smoke coming from somewhere from the restaurant, yes I said WEED! SMH never have I ever!!!!! And this isnt the first time i came and i smelled it. Very Unprofessional! The place is just a dump! I wish I could give half a star. Would not recommend anyone to go!

This place is delicious. Definitely one of the best restaurants in the area. And definitely the best Indian in the area. The buffet was huge, much bigger than other Indian buffets I've been to. There are a ton of vegetarian choices. Getting take out is really fast. They have it ready in less than 15 minutes, and it still tastes really good. In comparison to the other local Indian places, which I won't mention, the staff is friendly.
Was delivered quickly. They did mess up my order. Not bad for delivery Chinese food in Southern NJ.

First off the food here was amazing! However I can only give a review at 3 stars because of the service 3 individuals in our group received from the white female bartender that was short in height (don't know her name, she obviously didn't leave a positive lasting impression). We ate there at 530 on Saturday coming with a large group. While we waited for everyone in our party to arrive we got drinks from the bar. We were there to celebrate my moms birthday. My Dad, my husband, and my brother each received horrible service from this bartender. This restaurant has strict policies where you can't buy more than one drink unless the person you are buying an extra drink for is physically standing in front of her. She made this clear in her condescending and abrasive delivery. Granted I was sitting at the hostess desk with our son bc children aren't allowed in the bar area. Another example was when our table was ready she told my father "you're going to pay for that beer before you leave right?". The manager did come over and try and resolve (we expressed or disappointment with her service) but we clearly did still see her complaining to the manager in full presence while we were getting seated. Being in the service industry I was appalled that this is how my family was treated and that they wouldn't take that conversation to the back versus in plain site for us to still see.

Yes! Another great place to eat if your feeling like something different. I was hesitant to try this place- wasn't sure what to expect. I've never really tried Thai food but I was pleased to find they serve dishes like wonton soup, Chow main, sweet and spicy pork- classic favorites! I tried the spicy curry noodle and it was delicious! I can't wait to go back and try more things off the menu.

This was seriously a great surprise! Passed by many times but never went in. Inside is clean and well decorated. Washrooms are big bright and very clean. Best Pho' ever in my opinion. Chose Veggie and will come back soon for another yummy bowl. Flavor was perfect!
Pleasantly surprised was really good. Officially my go to spot for affordable Indian food.

It's a good quick lunch buffet with consistent food. Like it best when they bring out the fresh naan bread to the table before putting it under the hot light. They are very welcoming after I was there often enough for them to recognize me. Mango Lassi is good.

I've been to La Mulita for both lunch and dinner and it is quite good. The cocktails are very reasonably priced, the cermitas are excellent, and the tacos are very, very good. My complaint is regarding the dinner menu compared to the lunch menu. The dinner menu is more than half the size of the lunch menu. Having young kids are adventurous eaters, I think we'd come back for dinner more if the lunch menu was available in the evening-just for the variety. Additionally, I think the portions at La Mulita are great for sharing---I think people would probably order more food at dinner if the lunch menu was available.

Was happy to see this restaurant had opened so we stopped in for lunch. We were greeted and seated in a welcoming way. This rendition of the building feels much more comfortable and light. We both ordered the Vietnamese BBQ pork and rice which came with hot sour soup. We also ordered spring rolls. The spring rolls were fresh but not overly inspired. Peanut sauce was great. The soup had just the right viscosity and perfect heat to sour flavour. The BBQ pork and rice was so very well cooked to melt in your mouth tenderness and deep rich flavour, we enjoyed it very much. Service could not have been better and all very friendly. I know we will be back often as it is on our way from here to there and everywhere.
This food was very good and the service was fast and friendly. A wide variety of dishes, chicken, beef and vegan.

I really loved this place a lot the first time we ordered delivery, but since then it's been all down hill. Their food is well made, but very inconsistent. The 4 times I've ordered their chicken curry twice it's been as spicy as I would want it to be which is very spicy, once it was tangy and today it was the most bland curry I've ever tasted. The rest of the meal was good, but they are always incredibly stingy on the rice for delivery. It was hardly enough rice for one dish let alone enough to split for the two dishes we ordered. The worst part is their delivery people, they have never once come to our apartment door like every other delivery place I've ever ordered from. Most recently they arrived with no money to make change and never offered a total on the phone... I ended up tipping a little more than I wanted, but if I happen to order from them again the tip will be whatever change their is which in the last two orders was $2. All of that said I'm still giving 3 generous stars because the food has been good every time even if bland the last two times we ordered. I'm afraid I may move to only ever eat their in-house because it seems you get far better food and service if you dine in, but as a new parent that isn't very easy for us to do. We'll see if future impressions warrant an update, but as it stands I'm debating ordering ever again.

If you're expecting the regular brunch foods, don't come here! The menu is decent but maybe we just weren't in the mood for such heavy meals. My boyfriend and I both got eggs and biscuits (two sides) - way over seasoned with pepper and made us feel like crap after. It got busy at noon but at 11am there was barely any wait. Staff was friendly and we didn't have to wait long for our food. I give it two stars because I don't think they use quality ingredients and there's no reason to dress up an egg so much.

Spice-N-Grill might be the best Indian-Pakistani food you can find in St. Louis. It is a tiny establishment run by a husband-wife team who are so nice and aim to please. The biggest factor in my 5-star review is that the food here is made to order; you can taste that freshness. In addition, the flavor of the food is consistent! I doubt there is a bad item on the menu, but my family's favorites are: Chicken biriyani, daal masar, aloo gobi, chicken tikka masala, and chapati (always hot off the stove!). I've had one of the nihari dishes too and the meat was just as tender as the chicken dishes I enjoy. Just be mindful of how much spice you request, as medium spicy can be too much if you have a sensitive palate. My 4-year-old loves this place too, and that's telling of its deliciousness!
the pho was excellent and the restaurant clean who knew this was a franchise. i could not notice any franchise type shortcuts here

I would like to first note that just because one does not enjoy traditional Japanese food is not reason to rate Joto poorly. Their food is authentic Japanese, very delicious and fresh, and their wait staff are very friendly! My favorite Japanese restaurant.

This is one of the best Indian restaurants around. I was so disappointed when they closed their location in Conshohocken and was very excited to learn that they were reopening in Lafayette Hill. I drive from Skippack to get some Chicken Korma. My wife loves this place too. Their appetizers are amazing. Especially the Bhel Puri is awesome. Chicken Korma with Garlic Naan bread is the best combination for me. I give preference to authenticity when it comes to Indian food coz I grew up eating Indian food and I can tell you that this place has the best authentic Indian food.

Kirsten was awesome server. I was totally surprised by the quality of the food. Had the coconut curry soup, to die for. Grilled chicken salad was so fresh and delicious. I am hard to impress with food and i loved the food here. Fresh, fresh, fresh. Can't wait to go back and try the Carmalized Califlower and the Carrot Cake.

This is one of my favorite Thai places in philly! I love their Pad Kee Mao, it was perfectly flavored and left me wanting more. The only thing is that it's not the cheapest dinner option, but the price is worth it. I am looking forward to trying everything else on the menu.

What a great find. Headed to Chili's to get some work done over dinner on a business trip, I spied a little Thai place a few doors down and decided to take a chance. I'm glad that I did. What a fantastic restaurant. Beautiful decor, great service, and fantastic food. Tom Yum soup was perfect (ordered spicy) as was the Ginger Thai Chicken Curry (also ordered spicy). If you're in the area and like Thai food, definitely check this place out. I'll be back....

First time having a chaat and tried both the beef and chicken (for 2 different meals). When I said it was my first time the owner was super friendly and explained to me that if I didn't like it he would have it be on the house! He also asked what kind of spice level I wanted and packaged one chaat so that the "crispies" wouldn't get soggy for the next day. The beef was ground beef and although I enjoyed it, the chicken was even better - I think it was a tandoori chicken (not quite sure but was an orangish color from the spices) which was delicious. I also tried a samosa which came with a chickpea salad and mint chutney..had to eat the entire thing right there because it was so good. The only reservation I had about the chaat was that it was overfilled with what the owner calls the "crispies" which are fried dough pieces- it consisted about half the take out container. I'm not sure whether that's what a "chaat" actually calls for but I would have preferred less of it, personally (not too into fried dough as a meal). But if that's your thing go for it.

I am not sure why this restaurant has such high reviews. The quality of food is okay and the prices are high. They do not have a lunch menu and most Thai restaurants serve soup and egg roll with lunch. I will not go back because there's too many Thai restaurants with lower prices and better quality food as well as a nice lunch menu with lots of options.
This is the best Thai I've ever had... personal favorite is the drunken noodles... great lunch specials. .. they chicken satay on Tues and Thursday. A must visit

Tried this place for the first time. Food was ok. Nothing to shout about. However, the service was horrible. I had to get up and flag the waitress down for a napkin after my food was served. Had to do the same for a drink. Can't see myself going back.
Starters are good, food 's good and looks authentic. Service is very slow though and not the best...
What a great little find! The food was delicious and the staff was extremely friendly. We will definitely be back!

I went with a few co-workers. We had a great dinner. The waiter was very informative about each dish and suggested his favorites. We were able to share each other's dishes. Everything was oh so good. Definitely a place to eat for something different.

I am absolutely pleased with this place! EXCELLENT customer service from the time I walked in the he door. FOOD WAS AMAZING! Shrimp and Sauce...with the rice, beans & Roti & such a relax atmosphere but still family friendly! I will be mentioning to family and friends and I WILL be back! #Greatfood
Perching food, chill ambiance, HORRIBLE service, it makes me angry and my food doesn't taste as good

The reviews barely do any justice to this place! We had reservations, reached very late and the owner couldn't accommodate us. He personally assured us of seating if we checked back with him after an hour, and he lived up to his word! Fabulous 7 course meal, very intimate homely ambience, friendly servers and the live belly dancer who taught our birthday girl a few moves! The bit about washing your hands with rose water, towels instead of napkins, eating from the same plate, hot mint tea at the end are few of the many highlights! The cash bit could be somewhat inconvenient, but come prepared and you are in for a fabulous 2+ hours at Marrakesh!

Solid food with a Mediterranean inspiration. All of the starter dips were delicious, the whipped feta stood out. Dates wrapped in bacon were yummy, the burger was really good, Avocado sandwich was good. Only complaint were the fries were a little soggy. I wouldn't go out of my way to go back, there wasn't anything we ate that WOW'd anyone but the food was good.

I ordered the gyro salad & my husband had the deluxe gyro. They definitely don't skimp on portions. The grilled pita bread on top of the salad was wonderful, the meat tender and flavorful, and the deluxe gyro was huge. We also shared a piece of baklava for dessert. Everything was delicious! We were very impressed by the quality of the food. It is a little strange that they only serve canned sodas and bottled water, but not a huge deal. We will definitely be back for lunch again soon!

I have been here twice now and just absolutely love it. I'm from out of town, but whenever I am in for a visit, I make sure to come on by. It's great food, amazing atmosphere and decor, and good people. It's definitely a healthier and more fresh choice than I'm used to seeing out here in the Midwest! I absolutely love their bread and know that everyone I take her has loved the drinks, sandwiches, and appetizers. We are always MUCH too full for the desserts, but I can't wait to one day try their pies in a jar. I definitely would recommend eating outside on the patio for lunch or dinner. If the weather is nice enough, it's a great setting! Love love love this place. The artichoke or speck sandwiches are always a hit. As well as the olives and cheese plates.

This is the kind of place that showcases what St. Louis has to offer. Rarely do I give five stars. Five stars are for those rare places that excel expectations. Olio did just that. What you need to know: the bar staff are knowledgeable and friendly. If you chat with them about wine they will recommend something for you. Same with beer, whiskeys, or cocktails (and that's just what my group ordered). Don't hesitate to drop by and peruse the extensive, but not overwhelming, drink menu and ask for recommendations based on your preferences. As for food, the different items on the menu were perfect to nibble on while enjoying our drinks of choice. We ordered the jamón, olives, cauliflower, and kale. The kale was shredded and dressed to perfection with an anchovie dressing. One of the bar staff then surprised us with cherry tomatoes, garlic, and herbs over French bread--my description does not do it justice. It was beyond delicious. And it was on the house. After listening to my thoughts on the wine flight I tried, our waiter suggested a wine pairing with the tomato herb bread and it was perfect. I was skeptical at first but was surprised at how much I enjoyed the pairing. Cannot recommend this place enough for those looking for an urban experience similar to what one would find in San Francisco or Seattle.

Food is okay but the reception is bad! They used to make good chicken biryani few months ago but it doesn't taste great anymore. Also, they need to respond properly either on phone or at the restaurant.

I've been going to Zorba's for greek food for as long as I can remember. I'm greek and anytime that we feel like going out instead of cooking, we go to Zorba's. The family who owns it is really nice and the food they serve is quality. I really enjoy the grilled octopus and the saganaki. This place reminds me of the traditional tavernas you can find in Greece. The outside seating is really nice when its nice out and the service is always great!

One of my favorite restaurants in Boise. Don't let the sparse decor turn you off; the food is amazing. So far I've had the lamb and the shish taouk sandwiches and the lamb is my favorite. Very decently priced too. Do yourself a favor and check this place out

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: "Whenever I see, ''made from scratch' at a restaurant, I get nervous. It always takes too long" -mom. The food at Taj Mahal was tasty, standard Indian fare. The ambience was a bit dark for my taste (heehee), but the service was excellent. The servers were kind and communicative. Best pro: SO MANY vegan options. So many. So good. Worst con: took a while for food to arrive, but mom, it is made from scratch!!
Excellent value, flavorful but not overly seasoned, light fare as well, good service, high quality fare which is rare for a reasonably priced asian/fusion place in this area.
My son and I stopped here for dinner on Sunday night and had some excellent Pho and the salt and pepper squid. Quick Service without feeling rushed. Very Good, would definitely come back.

If you're in South County this is a hidden gem. The food is always tasty, fast, and hot. Portions are generous and the staff is apt to help you with the menu. Only nitpick is I wish the decor and seating was a little nicer.

I love it here! The service is warm and welcoming; they're always by the door ready to greet you. I feel like I'm walking into one of my Auntie's houses and she's about to serve me a delicious dinner. I love the buffet at lunch and dinner, everything is delicious. It's like Indian comfort food for me.

If you want to feel like you have been transported to Morocco and enjoy an extremely unique dining experience then definitely try this place. A fixed SEVEN course meal that is amazing from start to finish. Come hungry because you will leave completely full. Be aware it is cash only. A true hidden gem in Philly!

I really had high hopes for a great Thai restaurant in the area...I've gone here twice since it's closer than driving into the city ...my first visit was years ago when they first opened...the food was disappointing...How do can you screw up tofu pad Thai and Thai ice tea...I gave them a second chance and tried it again nothing changed...I vow never to return...every time I drive past I look to see if they have closed down yet...apparently not...

The food in this hole in the wall restaurant was incredibly flavorful. I came with a group of 10 people and shared curry mussels- divine, jerk and tamarind wings- literally fell off the bone, oxtail-wasn't able to try as it was eaten too quickly, and curry lamb and chicken with roti- perfectly cooked and properly made. The prices are a steal for the abundance of food that you receive. The place itself is smaller and colorful and easily missed if driving past. Service was slow and leisurely (but recall we had a party of 10 in addition to another large party of 10 already there). The waitress was patient and helpful. Overall, they proved that they deserved their 5 stars and best Trindadian food in Philly. Also, the place is BYOB, so don't forget the wine.
Have never had a bad meal here! I love the Tom Sum soup and always get the Basil Chicken or Fried Rice plus the Thai Ice Tea. This place is small but nice :)
Can't figure it out, but this was experince will not make my best of for Indian food in town.

My go to dosa spot! Authentic indian food with scrumptious paper masala dosa and fluffy idli. Whenever I come home, my family goes to Dosa Hut and we leave with nice full bellies! The paper masala dosas are the best, very large (about 2 feet or so) and crispy! The aloo potatoes, sambar, chutney are delicious and add flavor to the savory dosa. Since the paper masala is a specialty and so good here, I recommend getting it over the onion or rava dosa (which are standard and not as good). I highly recommend getting the 3 Idli/Mendu Vada deal and going with 2 Idly and 1 Vada. The idli is very fluffy, fresh, and well-made. It's hard to find good idly as there are usually quite dense. The Vada is nice and crispy. The weekday lunch combo for $7 is a pretty good deal for a small plain dosa and idli or vada. Even without the deal, it's only $10 for a dosa. I also really enjoy the homemade ginger chai, just like the way my dad makes it at home! Not only is the food great, but I really appreciate the genuine humble service. Every time my family comes here, we are greeted by a warm smile and delightful service. Typically, authentic (not fusion style) indian restaraurants aren't known for their service and your lucky if the servers crack a smile, but here the staff is always so friendly and nice. I've had such a great experience with Dosa Hut that my family got our rehearsal dinner catered from them with a mobile dosa station and a variety of North Indian dishes (naan, palak paneer, choola, etc). I wish I took pics of all the mouthwatering dosas. It was a big hit, everyone enjoyed it! All the dosas came out crispy and were customized for each order. There were a lot of options to choose from with different types of batter and veggie toppings. I definitely recommend the mobile dosa station and catering (it's a 3 hour minimum). Come hungry and you'll leave with a satisfied belly and a delightful food coma!
It was vvv good....And I like their vegetarian options....Gud bubble teas too...........
Best Afghan restaurant in the area!!! Great food, lovely decor, and amazing service. Highly recommend!

Last Friday when i went to Art hill for their summer film series Go! Gyro! Go! was by far the best food truck out there. They had a really great selection of eats and their staff was really nice. I had their Classic Gyro and man it was good, like maybe the best gyro I have every had! It was served with potato chips and was $7.50. The were also serving great lemonade that went fast. I would highly recommend eating at this truck if you see it by you. They had some other options chicken gyro, greek meatballs, veggie gyro and chicken or pork shish kabobs. If they are there next week I can't wait to try something different. They only negative thing i can say is they serve their food in styrofoam containers and that's not as environmentally friendly as I like to eat.

I came here twice, the first time, I ordered pho and and a BBQ beef sandwich. The sandwich is delicious! The large size is huge! As for the pho, it wasn't my favorite. Portion was small and a little too oily. I went back for the sandwich, which didn't disappoint. Their boba tea is pretty good Also, however, their prices are a little high.

Lilly's has the best Vietnamese food I've had. It is excellent. The vegetables are fresh and crisp; the beef, tender and delicious. The crab rangoons are excellent! They use real crab, which is a rarity, I find. The rangoons come with or without bacon. They use a different sauce than the sweet and sour or duck sauce you see at most places but it is delicious. Lilly's is a must try.
Great, healthy food. Fantastic bartenders. Award winning wine program... One of the best in the country. Eat here as often as you possibly can.

I've been here for lunch several times and the lunch portions are huge. You're going to bring home leftovers. I usually get the gyro plate, my wife the chicken shawarma. Both were delicious and came with hummus, rice, a salad and pita bread. I really like the salad, mostly romaine lettuce with celery, an olive, feta cheese and a light yogurt dressing. Even the rice was good. Go and enjoy.

As a person that comes from a very similar cuisine background (West Turkey), I love to go to this place! The small plate dishes, the fish, all the seafood... everything reminds me of the good old mediterranean cuisine back at home! Since it is a BYOB restaurant, of course I dont forget to bring my Turkish Raki to accompany it! I even brought my parents from Turkey to this place during their visit and they loved it as for them it was the taste that they were used to at home... :) For food recommendations, I would not recommend just going for the big entrees not because they aren't good but more because you want to taste more stuff than going for a one big meal. That's the mediterranean spirit! My usual combo is: Half hummus, half babaganoush (yes you can do that if you ask for it), the grilled octopus (a must!) and either one of the shrimp plates (I m a fan of the garlic one), a small portion of the calamari (they make big plates in small and if you are more people also maybe an entree per 2-3 person to share. This way you can taste much more and still pay a reasonable amount!! :) P.S.: 4 star is because of the waitresses because they are sometimes super rude and not friendly... but the food makes it worth!

My first experience with a co-worker impressed me. We ordered off their happy hour menu, and the fish tacos and flatbreads were an instant hit, esp. for the price. We ordered four appetizers and six glasses of wine, and our bill was only $36! I returned for two more happy hours and remained fairly impressed. However, we noticed with the dipping sauce for the phyllo cigars and arancini, it tasted like a can of Campbell's tomato soup. Since we enjoyed their happy hour three times and the ambience, we decided to go there last night on a double date. Our friends ordered the seafood pasta and capellini (in a spicy sauce) entrees. I ordered the lobster ravioli which our server said was one of the most popular dishes, and my husband ordered the special--described to us as a whole white fish in a lemon butter sauce and capellini. First off, the capellini appeared to be all pasta but not enough flavor as our friend had to shake so much Parmesan on it. The seafood pasta seemed okay, but the lobster ravioli proved to be underwhelming in portion and taste for $17. My husband's whole fish looked smaller than we had imagined it to be and full of fine bones, and it tasted bland. He had to reach for salt to make it somewhat more tolerable. Also, his side included asparagus, not capellini as described to us. Oh, and the bread basket strangely does not include butter but only a low grade of olive oil without Parmesan at first. The Parmesan arrived only with the pasta entrees. We had purchased the $35 for $60 Groupon, and our bill was $96. This also included a glass of wine, two iced teas, and a soda. The final total was $36. It still seemed too much for the bland taste and portions. While the ambience looks tasteful, the entrees were not. It did not make me want to return for another forgettable, overpriced dinner. My advice is skip dinner and only go for the happy hour from 4-7 during the week.

This was my favorite dinner that we ate on our trip to Nashville. We made late dinner reservations for the counter overlooking the kitchen. We arrived and had to wait a little bit because the prior diners were taking their time. This was pretty annoying, but the food luckily made up for this annoyance. We decided to do the choose 4 mezze, and we selected the whipped feta, fire roasted carrots, brussel sprouts, and turnip. The whipped feta was the best of those 4, full of flavor and beautifully plated. It also seemed to be ordered by most of the other diners. For our meal, we split the seared mushroom, octopus poke, and the meatballs. While all 3 dishes were good,the meatballs and the seared mushroom were amazing. The flavors in both of those dishes popped. I was feeling like I might pop, but I could not stop eating either of those dishes. Also, I am pregnant, and they made me one of the cocktails in a virgin style so I could partake in some "drinking". We really set the bar high with this restaurant as our first place we visited!

The service isn't the best, the food is always good. So at times I struggle with coming here because it's hard to get a person on the phone to order and there have been a few times that I had to check my food before I left because the order was wrong. I tried to call ahead so that I don't have to wait so long for my food. If you decide to come, get ready to wait a while for food.

As soon as you walk into this small building you are surrounded by wood. everything is wood paneled which isn't bad makes the whole place bright and clean. I was impressed with the friendliness of the owner and staff. My family felt extremely welcome and taken care of. We all ordered the Thom Ka soup which was excellent just the right amount of heat and flavor. They have a special everyday and for Friday was the red curry. I of course went with that. It was superb. I love curry and this one had the depth of flavor and the right amount of heat that didn't take away from the dishes real flavor. Very few places can do that. I would reccomend here in a heart beat.

I like to order the tropichop with a side plaintains and this location did not disappoint. Sauces were filled up at the sauce bar, service was awesome, location was clean and parking was easy. Up north we do not have Pollo Tropical so this is nice chain fast food restaurant with pretty decent food.

this place is a hole in the wall and somewhere you would think would never be good. (from its appearance; it's also in the basement of the same building that houses pulse for god's sake) but the food is AMAZING, and the portions are a really good size. definitely coming back here, and hopefully regularly!

Their Chinese Sausage are delicious! Portions are a bit small, but it is priced pretty cheap for great tasting food. I wish they have bigger portions.. but hey, since it is cheap.. go order more food!

Hit or miss on this one. I'm spoiled on Thai having grown up eating from Bangkok in Sarasota, FL (Super Authentic). I have eaten here a hand full of times. The Curry is always good, the Pad Thai is the worst I've ever had anywhere. I love Taro boba, so today I gave theirs a shot and it was below average at best. Fast, Easy, and Cheap so you can't expect much I guess.

I can't here for the first time with my sister and her boyfriend for a late dinner. I got the bamboo pho and found the soup to be excellent and delicious. The service was fast and courteous and would love to come back again.

First off, Don't even bother with the menu, just grab some adventurous friends and order the 'QUEEN 8('Meat/Veggie Combo for 2-5 people Immediately identify AND SAMPLE THE the deep dark maroon DoroWot. put on your poker FACE!!! Otherwise the other members of your Party will realize the treasure you've found. Soon your peers(competitors) will get over their initial aversion of eating with their Fingers, and like any hand-food such as Pizza slices This meal will have been devoured and you'll be asking for a second course. Dear Floridians, I assure you Authentic Ethiopian Food is much less exciting than you might fear Possibly the most American meal you'll eat all week, if you consider how much Tilapia/etc China is dumping on the U.S My Dad initially, absolutely refused to eat with his fingers and demanded silverware. Eating with your fingers is no more abstract an idea as some would like to make it out to be Tell those less adventurous members of your party to simply compare it to Pizza or tortillas or even egg rolls for that matter. It's disappointing how quickly we dismiss different cultures. However, I need my Tampa Floridian Yelp Foodies to Embrace and support restaurant. Otherwise Cuban sandwiches will be the most ethnic food available to us many people compare this food to Indian Food, I understand. To a certain degree you might find Ethiopian seasonings akin to curry. And, of course, the use of their bread is similar in the 'usage of naan bread. However, let me be clear, Indian Food and Ethiopian food are as different as American Breakfast and American Dinner. In closing "Queen of Sheba" sets the Bar for Ethiopian dining, The fact that you're going to be or have been disappointed at other Ethiopian Restaurants is simply a Testament to "Queen of Sheba"'s Superiority in all of Florida(Jacksonville to Orlando)

The usual PF Chang's.... Great service. The only thing is the wine list. They could revise it a little bit more. They don't have good selection like all other PF Chang's. Otherwise, if you are from out of town and looking for place to eat, this one is safe.

I would venture to say you will not find as unique of food at any food truck. He cares about making a complete, quality meal. I just followed what the person in front of me did an magically got a delicious, heaping plate of food. It was great.

I recently returned to Taste Of India and liked it better this time. While the food remains spicier than what I prefer, I'm a wimp in the hot chili department. This last time there was an option of goat meat. I didn't like the looks of it, so I didn't try it and can't comment on the taste. I should mention that I'm also a wimp about funny looking food. One item, the rice, was not as good this time. It was stuck together, as if it had sat out too long. I wasn't interested in eating more than 2 bites of rice anyway, so I didn't much care. I discovered something wonderful in their condiments section -- it's a thin cucumber yogurt that helps to dampen down mouth and throat burn from the hot spices. The reason they can't get 5 stars from me is their inferior Chai Tea --practically devoid of the pungent and flavorful spices unique to this drink. At $6.95, the buffet remains one of the best bargains in town so If the Chai Tea ever improves. then so will my rating.

Sought refuge from the rain and spent an afternoon on their patio. A lovely live singer braved electrocution to keep us entertained, so credit to the dedication of the staff. Very sweet service and yummy poboys. It's a little cheesy, but we had a great time.

Best sushi I have had when it comes to presentation and taste! Peters sushi in Brentwood gives them a run for their money taste wise, but wow the rolls look incredible. Highly recommend either the umami, mango tango, or spicy hulk. Its an incredible treat for sushi lovers

I have no idea how this restaurant has such a high rating. I am Indian-American and therefore know the cuisine very well, and this comes nothing close to quality food. Went for lunch buffet and the chicken was bland, dahls were old, and the naans were undercooked. If you don't know any better, you might think this is representative of Indian food, but believe me, it's not authentic. I'll give it 2 stars though since the buffet is affordable (~$10).

I went here for drinks.. I liked the decor. The drinks were on point but the outdoor seating were so uncomfortable. Overall, it is a really chill place to go for drinks. It has a pretty chill vibe. (mostly techno) I have to go back here for drinks.

We had a great Saturday lunch (with margaritas!) at La Mulita. Arrived right at noon and there was only one other table, but when we left at 1:30 it was nearly full. Great, prompt, informative service by the bartender. They're serving Saturday brunch items from 11-2 and we ordered from that menu. The chilaquiles verdes were exactly as advertised and my friend loved the biscuits and chorizo gravy skillet. Solid guacamole 27th really nice crispy chips to start the meal, fabulous churros to wrap things up. HIGHLY recommended Broad Ripple lunch option.

I REALLY wanted to love these cupcakes (at the Ardmore, PA location) and still do... My kids could not wait to try out them out. It's such a beautiful store, wonderful people who work there, but the cupcakes were just ok. Generous size, lots of filling, neat flavors.. but the taste was just ok and the consistency of the vanilla cup cakes ... not so great. In fact, they fell apart when the kids bit into them. Then they had a mess of cup cake pieces, much of which fell to the floor and ended up in their laps. The chocolate was a better consistency, but the flavors were just off. The Orange chocolate icing tastes like children's aspirin, which made me so sad because the idea is perfect. The choc/peanutbutter was pretty good.

Food is always delish! Order a head of time to avoid the wait. Fish hoagie, blackbean burger, salmon burger and fried wings are my go to items. The bread puddin is the best! If you can't get your granny to make some for you... You can't go wrong!! Just remember to check your order before leaving to make sure you have your condiments

The food here is alright, nothing special stuck out to me while eating here. I would probably only give it a 2 star but the cute server named Christina bumps it up to a 3. The pricing was decent as well but the pho has little to be desired. The store is pretty clean on the inside though and has ample seating and T.V.s, I would definitely recommend this place to people who are in need of a good Pho place in the area because I honestly think it beats Miss Saigon from down the street.

This is a fantastic seafood place. The food is simple, fresh, and delicious. You won't be able to mess it up the way they prepare the food. I havent had better calamari in this city and I've had a lot of calamari all over this city. The waitstaff is fantastic even when you go late. This place has great decor and ambiance. Perfect for a nice bottle of wine and a hot date.
Stopped I'm here after a long day of driving. What a fantastic place. Food and service were top notch!

I really like Sher-e Punjab. Their dinner is better than the buffet, but the buffet is a great deal! My only complaint is that the buffet is a little americanized - creamy and mild dishes being the predominant offerings - but what can you expect? Tucson is predominantly white people without a tongue for spice. I've sat in and ordered take-out several times and have always had a pleasant experience. All of the naan is good, I've had several dishes that I liked and when I've asked for it spicy (8/10), it comes with a good kick. Once I was adventurous enough to order it as spicy as it came and it cleared my sinuses out. Score! All in all, I would recommend this place and I definitely consider myself a regular. I tried to branch out and try another place in town and was so disappointed... Sher-e Punjab sets the standard in Tucson! Just do yourself a favor and get dinner there before trying the buffet.

Went here for lunch. Prompt and friendly service, food was very good and fresh. One person had the chicken gyro and two of us shared soup, salad, and 5 of the 8 traditional foods, all of which were delicious. Will definitely go back

The flaming saganaki sold us! Loved the food and ambience. Good place to go to if visiting the eastern state penitentiary. It's a good enough place for vegetarians. Not overloaded with options but not too few either. I had the grape leaves dolmade, which tasted good! Only minus was the price range. As a student is complain!
Best Place hands down!! The lunch buffet is great! I love coming here with the family for dinner as well.

Our food was served on paper plates, the utensils are plastic forks and knives. The hummus wasn't very good at all. I have had store bought hummus that tastes much better. The falafel was fresh, but pretty tasteless in my opinion. The pistachio baklava was allright, nothing spectacular though. However, one really nice touch was the musician who played his guitar in the corner. It definitely contributed to a nicer atmosphere. Overall, this place seems to charge 3-4 star prices, but it's really about a 2 star restaurant. It was much too overpriced for the portions and for what you get. I will not be back. It's not recommended.

I went tonight with my wife. The calamari and ginger salad are very delicious and while my wife enjoyed her meal I did not. At first I ordered the Pad Thai, it smelled like wet dog amd tasted just as horrible. I sent the dish back and then ordered Spicy Noodle. My second bite in I bit into a small piece of metal. When mentioning to the waitress she tried to get me to get yet another new dish. She didnt get a manager and my wife had to get her to delete it off the check. That piece of metal could have serooisly injured me or someone if they got the dish. We are very disappointed in this experience as I've heard great things. We wont be returning and will be sticking to our normal Thai place, Thai X-press

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Look up for this amazing Indian joint (it's on the second floor). The trek up the escalator is worth it for attentive and happy service. The food is amazing, leaving your mouth watering for more. What's even better they are on Grubhub and Uber Eats. The food is authentic, flavorful and amazing. Having had the pleasure of being in Southeast Asia recently, it felt like being back on vacation. A hidden Boise gem worth trying your next venture down Eight.

During one of my trips to Belfast to visit the in-laws, I had lamb for the first time. Since then, I've made this protein as my first choice when I try out a restaurant that offers it. I was absolutely thrilled to see lamb on the menu at Taziki. I had their grilled lamb plate, which came with a salad and a choice of either rice or potatoes. The Asian in me always chooses the rice. It also comes with a "skordalia" sauce -- it looks like hummus, but it's made out of bread. I sincerely hope that I didn't make the guy who took my order feel bad -- when I asked what this sauce was, he started off saying it was made from kaiser roll. I thought I misheard him; he thought his accent made him say the wrong word. He was fine -- I was simply doing a double take on a sauce made from bread. I've heard of this type of sauce before; I just didn't expect it. They gave me a sample with a crunchy pita. It was heavenly. Frankly, I expected the lamb to be chopped up. When my order came, and I saw 3 fillets (fat strips) of lamb, I was dumbstruck and pleased. Both the salad dressing and the skordalia sauce came on the side, which I appreciated. The crunchy pita seemed homemade. But it was slightly on the salty side -- but I've also noticed that in general, prepared food around Nashville tastes saltier than what I'm used to. The lamb was slightly pink in the middle (the way I like it) and was great. While I enjoyed the skordalia sauce with the pita, I think the next time I get this dish, I will ask for tzatziki, instead (or order it in addition, since I sincerely like both sauces). I also like the interior. The tables and comfortable chairs seem more expensive than the type of casual, cafe dining offered. There are also salads and gyros on the menu.

Great place for take out Thai! Awesome lunch specials. Prices are comparable to other Thai places but I like how it's more of a fast food experience compared to a formal dine in, which most Thai places are.

Very disappointed in the service and food at this location. Sadly would not be able to recommend it in good conscience. I absolutely love the location in Rittenhouse Square, and will continue to frequent them. However, nothing seems to be going well at this new location in Norristown. Tonight was my second experience-the first being a take-out order of zil zil tibs. The beef was tough and not flavorful, the vegetables were undercooked. This evening I ordered the vegetarian combo plate, and it was better on the whole, but not to the standard that I expected from the Center City location. The vegetables tasted like they were at least a couple of days old, and the Njera tasted the same. Not fresh, not warm, and not soft. It actually left a brown residue on my fingers when I tore small pieces off of it... Strange, this has never happened before anywhere! Added to the subpar quality of the food, I made the mistake of using the restroom. Neither of the stall doors of the women's restrooms locked, and it was a nightmare trying to keep my one-year-old son contained during the process. There was no toilet paper in my stall either... The man who appeared to be the owner was very friendly, but our waiter was a bit... Preoccupied? The food came out relatively quickly, no more than 15 minutes, but as we were the only year diners in the entire place I had hoped for something a touch faster. When I told the waiter I was finished, I expected him to return with the check. After about five minutes passed and I saw him still standing behind the bar talking with the only other patron, I decided to pack up and take matters into my own hands. I went up to the bar and asked if I should just pay there - he replied, "yes" and I finished up our evening with a bit of a bad taste in my mouth. I really hope this location picks up, and that they begin to spend a bit more time on their food and on their environment. I absolutely love the Center City location, and I was really hoping that this location would provide the same high-quality food and good service that I was used to there.

This place has EXCELLENT food. I love Indian and my friend likes Thai so it's the perfect opportunity to enjoy both as well as the restaurant being a BYOB. The food was so fresh and the Indian cuisine is the best I've had in a long time. They have very comfortable seating and great booths. Also, the staff is very, very friendly and accommodating. Highly recommended!

I came here on a Saturday for lunch since there was an event nearby. I ordered the egg roll appetizer and that was very crispy and delicious. I genuinely enjoy the egg roll wrap skin they used. The pho was decent but the beef was over cooked. It's not the same as pho in Philly if you're Vietnamese.

This is the best Indian buffet in Tucson. The Offerings are limited in number, but large in taste. It draws a multicultural crowd, including many who speak Hindi, all of whom has made a conscious choice to go here. I usually go in early when I have the time, as the restaurant can get crowded during lunchtime but owing to quick turnover the wait is never long. Since it is owned and operated by Sikhs there is always Tandoori chicken, curried beef and either Butter chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala. Always they have a creamed, but not with cheese, spinach dish which is great, oftentimes a chickpea dish, recently a coconut flavored green bean-plus other stuff (amazing) dish and a rotating vegetable dish. They always have basmati rice and naan bread, seasoned salad, rice pudding with fruit and a melon ball. I've gone here for years.

We had a coupon for this restaurant. After hearing good reviews, I went to try. So, we got in on a Wednesday evening. There wasn't much crowd. The waitress was friendly. And where I sat, I could see the kitchen. We ordered a veggie tempura for appetizer. For $8.95, that is the skimpiest plate I have ever seen. It was OK. My friend ordered Chicken and Shrimp Pad Thai. I ordered tofu green curry. The noodles were burnt and shrimp wasn't fresh. For the 13 bucks paid, at least the shrimp should be fresh. Whereas, my green curry was mediocre. My office cafeteria serves a better green curry. On top of it all, me and my friend had after effects. So I highly doubt the cleanliness of this place. Overall score 2.5/5.
Great sushi the spicy tuna was awesome and inexpensive and drunken noodles native thai was the perfect level of flavor and spice will come back!
The fried avocado sandwich was good! No wi-fi , and slow to serve the coffee. But, they were able to seat 12 of us for brunch!

My partner and I went at 6pmish on a Friday night. We ordered an appetizer, which was good but not great (potatoe ball things). I had a guava mimosa which was really tasty. I ordered the special which was grilled snapper, my partner had the Ropa Vieja. Mine was just ok - good but not interesting or special. His was delicious, but the meat was greasy and both our dishes were barely warm, not hot. The server was very friendly and made recommendations but she couldn't answer several questions. Maybe this place is newer than I thought..? At one point she asked a coworker what something was (we asked her and she didn't know) and the coworker said "I have no idea." I did not like that most of the entrees did not come with sides. The side options were good (the potato thing stuffed with yuca was yum!) but I don't want to spend $15 on an entree and another $6 for rice or veggies. It was all just okay and the little things (like the entree and sides, or that my veggies were obviously boiled and not steamed) sort of added up in terms of making a not great experience. I thought it was overpriced: Before the tip it was about $58 for two drinks, one appetizer and two entrees. For that price I would have expected knowledgeable servers and hot food that was delicious. I would consider going back if they had happy hour (which I didn't see signs or menu for), but I wouldn't go for another meal.
Good food around the area, one of the best Indian restaurant around here. Been here many times and go again when in the area. Good job guys
The food tastes like home. The staff is friendly and attentive. Every time I come to Tampa i bring the family to eat here. I recommend it highly.

First of all when I think of Thai food I think fresh. Not at Aroy, they use frozen veggies! I had the Basil Chicken, except I don't think they really put any Thai basil in the dish. Although the sauce was very good, the dish was a disappointment. Now onto the appetizer, their soft spring rolls were a complete rip off. They were made up entirely of lettuce with 1 basil leaf in each roll. Their dipping sauce was basically a sweet and sour sauce with peppers and ground peanuts added to it. A real disappointment considering it was highly recommended. Maybe the people in the area haven't really had good Thai food before.

My first experience with Ethiopian cuisine and I was not sure what to expect. The food was fantastic especially the lamb. The bread used to pick up and eat the food with was different and delicious. Everything tasted freshly made and full of flavor. The house roasted coffee was a treat. Service was excellent. I'm a fan
I haven't even finished moving into the neighborhood and already my goal for the summer is to try each of the 30 flavors.

Had the mangu (buttery mashed plantain YUM) breakfast with eggs, fried cheese, and Dominican style salami. It was DELICIOUS! My husband and I always have this whenever we're in the Washington Hts area of Manhattan, and we're so happy we found it closer to home. The portion was more than generous, especially for the price. We also had a delicious creamy morir soñando drink. The service was super friendly, and the atmosphere was relaxed and very charming. Can't wait to come back and try the Mofongo (among other dishes!)

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We stopped here during a quick trip through Boise on our way to the mountains. The buffet was fantastic and the price can't be beat! Lots of veg options and it was all delicious. I also loved the atmosphere. The place is family run and filled with love. We chatted with the owner for a bit after our bellies were happily full. He was warm and welcoming. If we ever make our way back to Boise, we'd definitely come back!

I have found a new restaurant to add to my list. This place is off the hook. I ordered the Chicken Schwarma dinner plate. It was awesome. The prices were very reasonable and the portions are big. Be prepared to either bring your appetite or ask for a to go box. There is enough food for two meals. I will be returning.
The hummus is AMAZING! I eat a lot of it and this is the best place for it. I had the veggie meal with the bed of rice and I couldn't get enough. They are renovating so I could eat in but who cares?

Food was rich and amazing. The half bagel with lox and sauce was really amazing spin. The chef did a great job for the prix fixed menu on brunch. The Bloody Mary was great flavors with the right amount of spice. The restaurant is a must go in NOLA downtown. It is attached to a hotel as well, although we didn't stay there. Highly Recommend.

In short, the atmosphere doesn't do the food justice. But for a quick meal or takeout, it's wonderful. Cons: 1. Ambiance: There is none. The tiny dining room, fluorescent lights and blaring music that sounded like a cat being strangled in another language made for an uncomfortable dining experience. I was VERY disappointed as I prefer an intimate setting when dining out. Perhaps I was expecting too much. 2.
