So I'm not a big fan of credit card minimums, but the awesome problem solvers at La Va Cafe have found a loophole! You can buy a gift card with your credit card so you don't feel obligated to buy more food to meet the minimum. And since I come here whenever I have class at Loop or Spool down the street, I will definitely use it. Aside from that, I love that they have loose-leaf tea. I love that they have VIOLET loose-leaf tea. I love that their seating area appears to be a direct replica of Central Perk. I love that you can usually still get a seat in said seating area even during peak hours. The pastries aren't bad but the egg sandwiches are better.

Manayunk has been needing a place like this. The hangover cure - their Pho is awesome! Noodles are just right, plus the broth and meat are very flavorful. Very clean and new. They also have a number of other Asian dishes plus Asian groceries which is unique. Recommend coming if you have a delight or interest in Asian foods.

To all who haven't had it, all I gotta say is y'all are missing out. From friendly staff to soft bread to succulent meat and rice, this place is lit. I like middle eastern anyway but this place takes it to the next level. Plus, the woman before me ordered vegetarian options so if that's your thing, you're most certainly in luck.

If you're looking for solid Thai food in Nashville, Bangkokville delivers (literally). I've eaten in and carried out from here, and both experiences have been excellent. The staff is very nice and the food is delicious. A couple things that I've gotten and liked: - Yellow Curry: Bangkokville's curries are EXCELLENT. I especially like the yellow curry, as not all Thai places offer this. The yellow curry here has sweet potato in it, which is really tasty. - Pad Thai: the Pad Thai here is very good. I wouldn't say it's the best I've ever had, but it is very, very solid. If you're wanting a really good, down the middle Thai dish, the Pad Thai from Bangkokville is a great choice. Call in orders usually take less than 15 minutes to be ready. I've never had to wait for a take out order; they are always waiting for me right at the front counter. Again, the staff is very sweet and I really enjoy eating here. It is a staple in my normal "don't have anything at home...want something good fast" restaurant rotation.

Sky cafe never failed to please my appetite. While other Indonesian's eatery around south Philly starting to decrease their quality, sky cafe has successfully to remain the same. I hope they keep a good job, and stay consistent with their good food.

Just had dinner at this place and it was definitely a 5 star for me! The service was great and food was amazing ! Will definitely be back when in town! Had the Chiken Tikka Masala, garlic naan, samosas and of course the ride pudding!

The food here is amazing. I will admit that so far I haven't been able to stray from the tried and true Jerk Chicken, so this review will not cover other food items besides the side dishes. I have had my fair share of Jamaican food and I have yet to come across a jerk chicken dish that even comes close. The mac is creamy and delicious and there is no hint of bitterness to the collards. In fact, I find the collards quite sweet and well done. The portions are huge and amazing -- a small is plenty for one person and I have yet to finish one myself. While sometimes the service can be a little slow, the food here is WELL worth the wait. From what I hear about the fried fish, wings, and ox tail, it seems the rest of the menu is up to par with the jerk chicken. Also, you know winning a Vendy is no coincidence -- the food is that good.

Blu Fig has the best Mediterranean food in Nashville hands down. its not your typical gyro place. The food is absolutely delicious, its not greasy, the restaurant is clean, and staff is very friendly. Its a little out of the way, but I come here all the time because I just can't keep myself away from there hummus and falafel. Definitely worth a try for anyone that the fan of Mediterranean food.

The food is inexpensive, and the service is quick, so I really appreciate that. Though the convenience factor is here for sure (for a quick meal or delivery), I was not wowed with the food. The sag paneer was sub-par at best, and the chicken tikka was not very good.

Went there on a whim, just trying to get something else other than burgers or pizza, thought we'd give this a shot. Food is good, staff is a little disorganized, the guy working as the host brought us to our table, which was dirty and so we stood there while he cleaned it, which was quite akward. Very low key place, quiet, not too busy, food took quite a while to get to us. We hadnt had Ethiopian food in quite some time and when I asked for a reccomendation the server quickly reccomended the highest priced item...ploy to get the most money out of us? Maybe, who knows. Overall if youre looking for something different this could be a nice change.
Great food and very quick!! Had the summer spring rolls, chicken satay, and #24 soup between the table...all was great! Will be back!!

Excellent breakfast sandwich (get the Hangover Special...DO IT!!) and a decent Philly cheesesteak. Prices are very reasonable and Mrs. Bui (if that's her name...) is so sweet! There is this one creepy dude though who speaks in a really high voice who works there (Mr. Bui?). I actually never really noticed until a friend pointed this out to me. But I digress...this is probably the best breakfast sandwich truck on Penn's campus, so go!

For all you Vietnamese cuisine lovers this is probably the best you will get in Indiana. However I left rather unimpressed. Granted I do have a high standard when it comes to Vietnamese food since I am Vietnamese and I've been spoiled by having eaten Vietnamese food in Los Angeles, Chicago, and Vietnam itself. I'm not saying the food was completely horrible, but for being owned by Vietnamese people I would've thought it would just be tastier and better.

This is the best Thai food I've ever had. Been coming for years. The coconut curries are fabulous. Also love pad kee mao. Byob and cash only but that keeps it cheap. Good place to make a good impression with great food and not go broke.

Such good food - I am from Atlanta, and always get take out from here when I'm in town. I love the chicken tikka masala and their garlic naan....yum!!! Oh and the owner is from San Francisco and is super nice!

This was the best food experience I had in New Orleans. Everything was absolutely delicious. The avocado toast..... absolutely amazing!! Ended staying for 3 hrs with bottomless punch and ordering different stuff on menu. The tuna tartar, the burger, the French toast, all delicious. I have never reviewed any restaurant good or bad before, but the food was so good here that I felt obligated. Must go for anyone looking for an epic brunch.

Hands down the best Pho in Indianapolis. We've tried many, but Saigon restaurant gets it right. The decor isn't anything special, but you are here to loudly slurp up Pho! We get take out Pho as well every few weeks. One super pho bowl can easily fill up two adults! It is super healthy, too!

We were meant to be friends. We were actually meant to be best friends I ordered (by phone) last night a beef pho with flank, meatballs, tripe, etc and it was SO great! I ordered tonight (yes, I have an addiction) and this time, it only came with flank and the wrong order of spring rolls (I ordered summer rolls). I'm just so confused as to how I could have said the same thing on two different nights and this is how different the orders were. I think this place needs to get sorted out (according to other reviews as well) but if it is a paying service, they would have figured this out sooner. I'm just disappointed but oh well. Maybe its different dining in?

The food is good but agree with reviews on food temperature. They fix that and this would be a 5 star place. Great service. Pretty authentic food and good variety. This review is about 6 months old. I'm hoping things have changed.
Amazing food, great happy hour, and a very cozy patio to match. But the reason I come here the most is the bartender Tony. Fun and friendly, always very attentive.
Had the Panang Curry and it was just hot enough to be good. It was a good amount of shrimp which were well cleaned. Liked the crab rangoon.

So I've lived in Palm Harbor for over 20 years. This place has been in Oldsmar for quite a few years and I hadn't gone to try it out. My husband and I finally went this past week. Big disappointment. The counter clerk was an old man that never cracked a smile. When I said it was my first visit, he looked at me like who cares. When we sat down to wait for our food. This young kid yelled out numbers, my husband looked at me and he said I wasn't told what our food number was? The food was not good. My husband got a chicken sandwich and didn't enjoy it. I got a grilled chicken breast. I tried to cut it with a plastic knife, really? It was dry. We will not be back.

This is probably my favorite Thai restaurant, the food and owners, employees and waiters are equally and hands down five stars! Order anything you wish to, you can't go worng here !!! We ordered Thai ice tea, veg spring roles, veg hot n sour soup, red curry, fried banana and coconut ice cream for dessert. They all were treat for taste buds, I would definitely visit this place again. Thank you!

4+ stars, almost 5. Super cool location, almost hidden from the general population. Amazing setting reminiscent of something you'd see in the MIddle east. Very authentic. and the food - wow. Endless, delicious, too much. Bring your appetite and 8 of your best friends. Wear dockers with the elasto waist. Be prepared to gorge yourself silly, then nap before you pay your bill. One of my favorite spots in Philly. Bring lots of friends. A hidden gem. Way recommended.

I loved this place. The hummus was very good. I loved the cauliflower - I've never had better. My husband enjoyed his corned beef sandwich. His complaint was the price of the dishes. Okay, it was pricey but everything was tasty-- and to me that's what counts. Check out the menu.
I love their pad Thai! Their quality is always the same and the food is delicious. Nice people as well in an average setting.
Best falafel in town. They also have great wings, arabic food, tabooleh.

Restaurant.com users beware.... Meal was nothing special. service wasn't good. Was told that they will not honor restaurant.com certificates even though there is no expiration date on the certificate .... just left mine behind and told them I won't be back. Also, a $5 fee for BYOB. Honestly, I don't mind paying for good food but this place isn't good .

Born and raised on the beautiful island of Trinidad and Tobago, I was craving some authentic home cooked Trini food that wasn't cooked by me. And this hit the spot! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this restaurant. Beautiful, unique ambiance, excellent service, great food I had dhalpourie, curry chicken and curry channa with some pepper sauce on the side and it satisfied my craving. Met the owner Adesh and his staff Ajay and Kevin very warm and friendly people. Cant wait to go back to eat there! DONT WAIT TRY IT!

Never have been a fan of Bob Evans. Sure glad they left the building, Saigon Restaurant took its place. We had lunch on a Saturday, a big bowl of fresh Pho, Basil chicken, clay pot pork and the OMG Crab Rangoon! Enjoyed it very much. The sauce in the clay pot made ya want to lick it clean - plain and simple. The place could use a good cleaning and updating, but I (you) do not go there for the ambiance. I want good food and little dives (this place will never be on DDD), so what! I will be back. Ever since Pancho's left Its hole in the wall place on Michigan we have needed a new place for good fresh made food. This is the real deal! I will return.

My first foray into Ethiopian food was right here at Zagol in Reno. I've read the other reviews and found that some of the service problems seem to be solved (or perhaps we were simply there on the right day at the right time!) We tried the vegetarian combination (my friend doesn't do meat, sadly for me). However I can be quite happy with vegetarian and th combination worked. There are four dishes on the interesting platter made of sponge-like thin Ethiopian bread. One is a cold salad (tasty and unusual) and the other three were a carrot/onion/ginger combination (hot) that was very good as well as two different starchy dishes (hot, one spicy the other not) made of peas and vegetables in a mashed-potato like consistency. You eat with the bread of course (no utensils unless you ask as mentioned prior). I liked to take a scoop of two of each dish with each mouthful of bread. I really enjoyed the entire dish. We also tried the two Ethiopian beers; the "Dark" and the "Light". Both also very good. The light was a lot more flavorful than your run of the mill light beer, and the dark was rich and sweet with a good mocha flavor. Service was just fine. Very friendly Ethiopian woman served us and she was humorous and welcoming. The atmosphere is trendy and city-like and we enjoyed it; the restaurant has hardwood floors and tables (no booths) set a good distance apart from eachother. I imagine it could get loud in there but there were only five tables in use by the time we left and only two when we arrived. To sum it up, four stars, I would absolutely return. Perhaps I will get myself one of the appetizing-looking beef dishes next time!

The good is just so good. And the prices are very reasonable for what you get. I love their Chicken... honestly some of the best chicken I've had. I come here often now with my friends. You can't go wrong. Great addition to IV. Hope to see it become a go to spot!

Popped by on a very hot afternoon for a late lunch on Sunday with my wife and 4 y/o daughter. We had the Greek salad (loaded with toms and cucs), the charcoal chicken platter (comes with roasted veggies and rice and a buttery, skinless, soft potato), and the Gyro platter. No complaints with this good, healthy food!
I love this place. The gyros are amazing, the Mediterranean one is my fave. The baklava is also delicious. And their prices are fantastic. I just wish they were open a little later.
Great food, great decor, great environment, and even better service! Our waitress, Pamela, was super sweet and attentive! We'll def return, esp as westbankers (Algiers)!!

A Friday night light on South Broad street. Get the grilled romaine. Order the calamari, chicken parm, gnocchi, but not the garlic bread. This restaurant, opened 11 years ago by no one named Scannicchio, is family owned and it feels like it, in the best possible way. BYO vino, but not any pretension. Time slows to a soft Mediterranean breeze at Scannicchio's, and we could all use a bit more of that.

Very solid Thai place in a sort-of misfit building (looks like they shoved it into an old Dairy Queen or something) in an odd part of the metro area (Delicious Thai food north of 270? Really? Shouldn't this be on Olive or Grand?). Service is good and quick here. Appetizers: Grilled pork and sticky rice is amazing. Satay, spring rolls, and crab rangoon are good, would not recommend the banana thing; I appreciate that it's different, but in eating Americanized Thai, I don't want something that comes with honey. It seemed like a good idea at the time, but really, I want something with soy, spicy thai chili sauce, etc. Entrees: The noodle dishes are delicious. I've had Pad Mee Dang (red noddles: they brought it out and the people at the next table asked what it was because they thought it looked good), Pad Woon Sen, and Pad Thai and all were very good. I got some fried rice dish here that was good. The Masamum curry I got here wasn't the best I've had, but it was still good. If the worst thing I can say about a place is that it was in an inconvenient location for me, I think that's a pretty good compliment.
Finally tried the award-winning Pad Thai from The Smiling Elephant in Nashville and it did not disappoint! The pad Thai at this gemstone in Nashville is legendary!!!

Okay, I hesitate to review this because I'm not sure I want everyone knowing about this awesome truck. The first time I was intrigued that everyone was standing in line and no one knew what they were getting. Gus told me he was one of the best and that if I don't like I don't come back. Well I said what the hell. I tried it and loved it the first time. Got three meals off on one platter. Wen there today since we were not busy at work and again it was great. Got enough for lunch tomorrow!!! It was amazing!!!! My favorite part is the grilled chicken. I like it because he uses charcoal!!!

Two places in one - both hoping Thursday through Sat - loud enough and long enough into the nights that the folks living in the apartment just west of it, frequenly complain. The inside is very chique - a great mix of color and texture in art, furniture and wall coverings. Service was great; food was good. The only things I'd change is the menu - some of items appear to have two names...this or the supporting description text does not seem to tie back to item title. Outside is lounge time: great seating, cool lighting and music (live or DJ). On select nights they run a red carpet to raise money for local charity's. That said, the clientele could stand to be a little more genuine - just my take. The average customer seems (to me) to hang longer then at other outdoor patios.

Best lunch buffet in Tucson, hands down!! I was first introduced to this restaurant by my roommate (of Pakistani heritage) in grad school. The buffet is reasonably priced, and it's easy to stuff yourself full of spicy goodness if you've been living on ramen for a few days. The buffet has a nice variety of dishes, including several without meat, at any given time. There's plenty of warm naan to soak up your leftover sauce, and when something runs out, the staff is quick to bring in more food. You may be a bit disappointed if you like things spicy, since they tend to prepare the buffet food on the milder side, but everything is still very good. There's nothing fancy about the decor, but the food is more than enough to make it; there's a good reason the place is usually packed in the afternoons! Give it a chance, even if you've never had Indian food before; you'll come away full and happy!

Best happy hour in town, me and my boyfriend frequent it often. They have delicious food for reasonable price. Belly dancers are fun to watch, I never knew what to do when they approach the table? tip? watch? anyways, always makes for an interesting meal. The spreads are half price at happy hour with $2 sangrias

service is poor. Came in and there's a white guy who looks like he owns the place, did not greet me nor even smiled. Ordered phad thai on the lunch menu, and spring rolls as a side order from the cashier. The phad thai taste bland, did not even comes with a soup and salad as offered by other places such as Thai Orchid in Plainfield. You also need to get your own utensils. The spring rolls does not have shrimp and meat like they do at Pho 36 in Avon. And the peanut sauce is watery and taste awful. And the worst thing is they charged you refill for drinks. .I won't be back on this place. .it's a waste of time and money.
Pretty freaking good. Great customer service. Gyro was filling. Wings are also tasty. The soft drinks are cold and wet on a hot day. I'll be back.

I came in on Wednesday for the first time to try out pita jungle. I'd heard good things, so I was excited. The service wasn't that great from the beginning. The hostess was smiley and nice but after that it declined. Our waitress was cold and very unfriendly. At this point I was still hopeful to try the food. Unfortunately, I've been sick ever since and can't keep anything down. I ordered a falafel wrap and potatoes as a side. The food was just ok and def not worth being sick over. Will not return.
Have been here 2 times now and the food is amazing . You can't beat a good deal . I love the jasmine rice soup they have , so delicious !

The chef evidently enjoys what he does and it really shows in his product: your lunch. Today was my first time getting food from this truck and there was about a 30 minute wait. The food today was pasta with chicken, topped off with grapes, blueberry, and apricot. Needless to say the food was delicious. I ate it all in one sitting even though the portion was huge! The chef is very enthusiastic and wants to talk to you as well.

Tried this place twice, and had an awful experience both times. First time, their card machine was broken, so he ended up charging me twice on my card, then tried charging me cash again. Had to argue with the guy for 10 minutes before we cleared the issue up. Second time was even worse. The main cashier guy wasn't there, so the cook was taking our order. Took forever to explain to him that we each wanted the 2 item combo that was advertised on the big sign right next to him. There must have been a huge communication breakdown, because he seemed to pull the price of our meal out of thin air. Not one person in our group of 4 got what we actually ordered. Food was ok. Pretty greasy but a ton of it. Would never go here again though, sick or arguing and bantering with the cook just to get the food I want off their menu. Go to Aladdin Cafe down the street instead, the food is much cleaner, the staff is awesome, and they have hookah to boot.

Went to the new location on Kennedy,was amazing. The flavors in the rice and chicken were outstanding. The waitress was the chefs wife and she gave us a complimentary serving of his mothers rice recipe. During Ramadan they are serving a buffet at 8 15 each night highly reccommend it

This place has delicious food! For our appetizer we got the Jerk wings, excellent flavor and fell off the bone. I got the Curry Goat & Red beans and Rice, Tender and Amazing! The staff was very nice. I can't wait to come back and try something else!

I had the pleasure of attending one of the preview dinners and I can honestly say it was one of the best meals I have ever had from start to finish. I started with the conch fritters which transported me back to amazing times I have spent in the islands enjoying them. Next I had the beet salad which is getting overplayed in restaurants these days (even though I love it) but Nina put a different spin on it. Candied pistachios, ciabatta, and goat cheese mousse took this dish to another level. For my meal I had the picci with crawfish and squash, and while I normally don't love crawfish, Compere Lapin has officially changed my mind. For dessert I had the horchata panna cotta with melon salad and melon sorbet. The whole thing was perfection.
Great food, quick and easy. staff was very nice and helpful. I can't wait to eat there again.
The real deal! True authentic Greek food in a cozy casual atmosphere. Fresh and delicious just like Yia Yia makes it!

Simply amazing. Wife and I shared the Korean Fried Chicken, Pork Shoyu Ramen, and Chicken Fried Rice. Best chicken wings I've ever had in my life, without hesitation. Will become our regular neighborhood spot moving forward. Kudos Michelle!

I've been craving thai food for awhile now, and was very happy to have found this place. Had tom yum soup, spring rolls and dumplings for appetizers, and the pad thai and red curry as entrees. Overall, it was pretty good. My only gripe was the lemon for the pai thai - that lost me on the authenticity right there. It would have been so much better with a slice of lime - so the pai thai came out a little sweeter and not as tangy as I'm used to.

I had the grilled chicken salad with a side of hummus & pita & it was delicious!! I wish I would of tried this place sooner. It was clean & the staff was very friendly. My only complaint is it took a little long for the food to be served but seeing as it was made fresh & to order,I'm not going to complain about it or drop the star rating. The food was worth the wait!

Just very poorly managed. I'm talking about the bartender named Ashley that thinks she is a manager. I ordered Fulin's noodle soup and a seaweed salad to go. When I arrived to pick it up, I told the young lady at the pick up area that I wanted to use an "expired" Groupon (which is the actual amount of money you paid for the Groupon-your money). She took the Groupon information down and went back in the back. This Ashley person came to the bar and told me it couldn't be used because it was for lunch. I said no because I'm using the money I paid for the Groupon (which is my money) and it doesn't matter when it is used because it actually MY money. This person argued with me over a $13.00 check. I told her she could keep the order and I would call her GM. I left the store and went back to get the GM's number and she was laughing with two other girls over my order and she refused to give me their GM's number (of course). So, I wrote a letter to the BBB. Let this woman that is so rude explain to her management why the restaurant lost a customer over $13. Oh yeah I'm also writing a BBB report on Groupon for having establishments get Groupons without their employees knowing how to use them. Maybe Groupon will stop supporting Fulin's and they will lose more business. This employee was very, very rude and always had to be right.

Love this place ! It's byob, first come, first serve, and hard to find parking. However, when all the stars align and you manage to get in and seated, this place knocks it out of the park! Service is fast and friendly. The atmosphere is lively and you can see the cooks doing their magic right behind the bar. The food was fresh and overall tasty. They start with bread and the chimichurri type sauce. (I don't know what it is but its parsley, herbs, and oil) it's by far our favorite. We had the tomato mozz salad which was relatively large portioned and delicious. The only disappointing thing was the hummus. The texture was fine, but the flavor was bland. I asked for more of the herb dipping sauce and mixed it in for flavor. I had the shrimp scampi which was so good! I rarely eat shrimp and this was delicious. I also ordered the plum pasta but was so full I only ate a bite. I will be enjoying my leftovers today for lunch ! My friend got the escarole pasta, and my boyfriend got the octopus platter. All had rave reviews. We left stuffed , reeking of garlic, and fully satiated with promises to be back soon! Eventually I would like to make it to dessert but that hasn't happened yet ! Next time!

I went for the lunch buffet and the food was great! My favorite was between the Curry Chicken and the Butter Chicken. The Chai Tea was also good. My only qualm is that the food could have been quite a bit spicier. Surely this could be requested if I'd come for dinner rather than the buffet. Will definitely have to return sometime!

Nice ambiance. Lot of food. Didn't like the egg dish that they gave. Everything else was really good. The towels that they give to put on the lap are old and smelly. It's time to replace :) cash only!

This is a SUNDAY BRUNCH Review. I have eaten Sunday Brunch at 8th & Union Kitchen many, many times. It is the perfect, casual space for great food and great music on a Lazy Sunday. There is a GIANT selection of sauces (Hot & Mild) for your "Make Your Own" omelets. Everything from the kitchen is absolutely as fresh as can be. Beer selection is considerable. Wait & bar staff are relaxed but attentive. The "Summer Roll" omelet with Prosciutto, Shrimp, Avocado, Scallions, & herbs is OUTSTANDING. PLUS, as an extra added BONUS, if you go to Sunday Bruch, you will be entertained by Bruce & Sam; the areas finest Jazz Duo. 8th & Union Kitchen Sunday Brunch is a "Can't Miss". If you love good food and great music, this Sunday Brunch is worth the trip.

I don't know what Alanna's problem is but its not the food at Petra. Go back to Michigan. We need less tourists and haters in Tampa anyway. Every time I come here the service is slow (hence the 4star review) but it is forgiven because the food is on point every time! I have been here over ten times. Only one time they brought out a dish late for one of our lunch group members that we had to take it to go, but they apologized and comped that person's meal to make up for it. Crappy customer service seems to be the norm elsewhere lately, but this is a great place where the staff treats you with respect and kindness and happens to have delicious food. Well worth the cost. I always have to take some home for a second meal. It's not like you're going to break the bank to try it for yourself to make your own decision on the food and service!
Nice place for gathering with friends or family. The innovative japanese fusion dishes are great , so are the service. Will come again very soon.

I go here every time I visit St. Louis. The gyros and Greek salad are AMAZING! I can't get enough of it. The portions are great and delicious. I find it slightly expensive, but I am a fan! I hate that they are not open on Sundays.

Sadly, since my initial glowing review Dooners as gone way down hill. Disregard my previous rating and remarks. It's no longer the hidden fresh treasure it once was. Apparently a change of owners has occurred. Hopefully they can get back to the quality and fresh standards that used to set them apart and earned the high ratings.

Loved this place. Went to it based on word of mouth reviews from several friends and we were extremely pleased. The lamb tikki masala was so tender it literally fell apart in my mouth. Best Indian and Pakistani food I've had in St Louis. Comparable to the genuine homemade curries I've had. We will definitely be going back soon!!

This is a cool fast food alternative when u are hungry for Indian food. Sure it's not authentic but the flavors are actually pretty good and it's relatively inexpensive. Similar to other fast food alternatives that are around for other cuisines... Moes, Chipotle, Zoe's kitchen etc ..
Jessica is great!!!! And the mussels are fantastic, either red or white. Go! Nice happy hour as well...

I ran over to wishbone in late October back when they first opened up and the only thing you could get was chicken and hand pies. Haven't been back since they rounded out their menu to include other sides, so this review is for the chicken alone. The chicken was tasty, but definitely over-hyped. Thumbs up for being boneless. Thumbs down for the breading itself being mediocre. The most interesting part of the experience I would say is the dipping sauces. But I'm biased. Dipping food into lots of different sauces almost instantaneously makes my eating experience so much better. I liked the bbq and the chipotle lime mayo. I think if they wanna stick around longer they should keep making different and new sauces (with having a few of the regulars always there) and making thicker juicier tenders. My chicken was definitely over cooked. Adding sides to the menu is definitely a step in the right direction for this place.
Been here probably over 20 times. Every time the food is amazing. Good fresh Thai food and great service.

Gateway to India is my favorite local Indian spot. It is slightly pricey, but the quality of the food makes up for it. We shared several dishes at my last visit which is my favorite way to experience Indian food. As an appetizer, we had the chili paneer . It was spicy, sweet and robust in flavor. The standout dish in my opinion in the lamb korma. The lamb is unbelievably tender and pairs well with the creaminess of the korma. The garlic naan, mango chutney and cucumber raita are great additions to the curries. We also ordered the shrimp madras and found it to be bland and not nearly as impressive as other dishes I have had. We finished with the pistachio malai kulfi which is an Indian ice cream that is slightly thicker and creamier than the ice cream I am accustomed to. It was topped with finely crushed nuts and possibly shredded coconut which gave the dessert a great texture. I would definitely come back to try more flavors. I find that Indian food intimidates many people. The lunch buffet is a great opportunity to experience Indian cuisine and see what dishes you prefer. If buffets are not your style, simply share a few amongst your group. You will not be disappointed.
The BEST Indian restaurant in the greater Indy area (and I have been to them all)!!!!!

So, I went here with a friend for dinner on Friday and I remained impressed with this place. The service is always great. The breads that we ordered were the best I've had. The dishes were perfectly spiced and my water glass was kept full. On a Friday night, good service is hard to find. On another note, I just noticed they serve Indian beer...that will be something I try next time since I usually bring red wine.

Recently went for lunch. There were four options for lunch, ranging from $6-8. The buffet apparently does not run during the summer months. I ordered the chicken kabob. The meat was tender and flavorful, the dipping sauce was delicious, and the rice was very good, no need for extra sauce.

when i was in new orleans the second time post katrina (this was october of 2005), we were able to actually stay in the city (still camping out in parking lots and occasionally on generous folk's couches) and a few restaurants had opened back up. this was, at the time, the only restaurant in new orleans that served tofu. and you know laura b. be needing her tofu especially after a solid month of living off clif bars and bruised apples (damn, i lost a good amount of weight though. i mean, i was looking GOOD. and by GOOD, i mean skinny. i am totally fucked up in the head. i must say though that the people of new orleans, in the most fucked of situations, would still stop rescue workers all the time to offer us whatever food, drinks, or company we might need. it is really humbling when a person who is going through their destroyed house trying to salvage whatever they can asks the privileged humane society worker from california if YOU need anything. families would go out of their way to cook vegan for me when i only met them the day before! the kindness was bordering on insanity...it was so overwhelming. and i only had to tell one person that alligator isn't vegan.) ANYWAY, back to singha. i ate here maybe 15 times. delicious thai curries made vegan with tofu and veggies and FANTASTIC spring rolls. the KINDEST service under the most horrible of circumstances...it must have been soooooo hard to open up in a basically destroyed city where running water had been up for only days. the restaurant itself is super cute too, with a long bar up front and a couple rooms in the back...feels like you are eating in little secret nooks no matter where you are. an awesome place to eat when you're in nola. 5 plus plus plus stars.

I went here for Mother's Day last year because it had many options for gluten free diners. My family came with me. We came in the middle of a shift change, so the service was slow and the food was just okay. I am thinking of trying it again because the menu sounds so delicious and because many of the menu items (like the calamari) I can't find without gluten.
Delicious fast/casual gyros and such --- love the salad, the hummus, and the tabouli too! Very small dining area and a bit exposed...but for takeout, Yum,

I can't stop thinking about the meal I had last night at Compere Lapin. We made a last minute reservation which left us eating quite early. We must have arrived at happy hour, as the bar was packed and the restaurant was unbearably noisy. Our waitress was friendly, efficient and very professional. She suggested a cocktail, the Chin music, based on my desire for something similar to a Moscow mule. Well, after reading the ingredients I was super worried about what I had ordered, but when it came... wow it was delicious! For dinner I ordered the special which was a lovely pasta with a wonderful truffle sauce, and shaved truffles. It was $45, a small plate, but worth every penny! If I could have it again tonight, I would. My husband had the duo of beef, which was delicious. I have two complaints... One is the timing of the food and the drinks. I wasn't even finished with my cocktail when our bottle of wine showed up. It was okay that it was opened and could breathe, but our meal came right on top of that. It felt incredibly rushed. I know, it is silly to complain about, but really the place was not busy and we could have used a few more minutes to just enjoy our drinks, biscuits and conversation. My other complaint was how noisy it was. It was quite hard to hear the waitress and I had to ask her to repeat several times. This was when the restaurant was empty and the bar was full, and it did get better as the evening went on. Overall, I highly recommend this place. I truly cant wait to return.
The food lives up to the hype. We had three different dishes and they were all delicious.

This is a convenience store. So don't expect fancy service or the type of ambiance you'd get from a restaurant. There are people walking in and out of the store constantly and their TV is always on. At the back of the store is a counter where you can order Vietnamese food, poboys, and a few other things. And trust me, it is damn good. Combination banh mi - I'm not sure what makes this banh mi taste so much better than other places I've tried. But it is. They give the perfect amount of veggies and meat and the bread is perfectly toasted. Grilled pork banh mi - I didn't have the chance to try it, but my brother ordered it and he gave me a thumbs up when I asked about it. Shrimp poboy - On Vietnamese French bread, dressed with mayo, pickles, tomatoes, and lettuce. It's not super stuffed like other places, but it's also not skimpy on the shrimp like a few places. It's not my first choice when I come here, but it satisfies my cravings when I do order it. Phoritto - The hype is REAL. I saw a post about it on Facebook and bam! The next day, they're selling it at Eat Well, so I had to come try. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much when I ordered it. But wow! This is really good. It's filled with brisket, pho noodles, bean sprouts, basil, basically everything you'd put in pho, you'd find it in a phoritto. Pho wrapped in a tortilla and you might think it would lack flavor, but it's not. You've got to try it for yourself. Hurry! Because this is a limited item.

I went to this restaurant last night and the service was horrible. 1st, I called my order in ahead of time (which is difficult to do because there is no menu available online) and told the guy I was 2 spring rolls, vegetable dumplings and 2 orders of Crispy Thai Tofu. They had NO brown rice so I had to order that from the Chinese restaurant next door. When I arrived at Oriental Pearl they hadn't even started my order! That was the 2nd strike! Once I got there I was able to look at the menu and noticed they had tofu teriyaki, I asked if I could swap out one of the Thai tofu's for that and was told no because they ran out of teriyaki sauce. So I said forget it just make me what I asked for. I then asked the host if he could have the cook add bean sprouts to my dish....there was some back and forth confusion between the host and cook as if she (the cook) had no idea what a bean sprout was!!!!!!!! I was shocked! I sat there for a good 15mins while the hostess had her boyfriend at the counter having small talk! My order was finally done, the host took a pic of my Groupon to redeem it. I asked him was this everything I asked for? he frustratedly responded "yes everything is there" I get home and open my food and find a box filled with 6 spring rolls! I specifically asked that FOOL for 2 spring rolls not 2 orders of spring rolls! Being as though there is no online menu you would think the idiot would have some sort of customer service and say each order comes with 3! And.....my vegetable dumplings were NOT there. I then called the restaurant back and got him on the line! I let him no how much he screwed up my order and he sarcastically responded "well, I'm sorry". From beginning to end the service was poor. My food was great but they need to make some changes with the kids they have hired for the front of the restaurant.

Best Indian restaurant, and def. a contender for best restaurant on the main line. This is not a mediocre review that you see on most of yelp and then go to places based on that and leave disappointed. This place is more than legit. I have never been to the Middle East, but I'm confident enough to say that this place TASTES like India! I'm confident enough to give it a 5 star rating, which there are only a few others that I hold in that regard in the Philadelphia and surrounding area ( I. E. dim sum garden, el jarocho, the good dog bar). I've tried numerous Indian places including overseas and this IS IT! Do yourself a favor and get to this place...you will love it! Recommend the appetizer chicken pakora and both chicken vindaloo and chicken korma ( my personal fab and standby). Oh, and it's a BYO!!

Who cares about the lackluster Vietnamese-style decor. or the random Asian entertainment playing on their T.V or even the random loud old men and women patrons talking, I'm here for their Pho and only that. The BEST in Tampa and it's coming from a Vietnamese, so you know it is legit. Just order The Pho and forget about everything else (Pho Quyen). The rest of the menu is your typical Vietnamese dishes that aren't worth mentioning. The Pho is robust in flavours! The ratio of fat and connective tissue makes the broth perfect! It's about *$8 for a large Dac Biet (special combination).

Love pollo tropicali! It's fresh delicious the chicken is excellent I love all the sauces especially the creamy garlic cilantro sauce and the yucca .. Steak is very tender and delicious and of course the mango iced tea is the best! They're open till midnight and it's fantastic addition to the neighborhood which has very few restaurants. Will be returning frequent as possible! Try the tres leches for dessert
I'm addicted to this place.....mainly for the fresh spring rolls, Thai fried rice and chai tea

i have been coming to the taste of india buffet for a decade.i have rarely ever been disappointed.the food quality is always consistent,the service is good and the kheer and chutneys are to die for.i have introduced many people to this hidden gem.
These people are paying attention! This is our second time here. Actions speak louder than words, these people all act like they want to be in the restaurant business. We will be back.

I always drive by an Afghan restaurant in NYC that I've always wanted to visit, so when I saw this place in Philly I made it a priority. It's a nice low key place with hookah and some great scents from spices. My friend and I shared some sambosa with cilantro and thinking about it makes me want some right now. It was really good. After that we enjoyed the chicken corma and lamb with eggplant. The corma has such a nice seasoning to it that I would try the lamb corma next time. Both dishes were very good, and makes me want to try more food from that region like Iranian cuisine. You can also bring a bottle of your favorite drink, which is always great.
Love their veggie samosas, chicken curry and lamb korma. Just an FYI, one plate of rice was not enough between two people for two entrees.
Amazing food and service. We got the spicy beef noodle soup (Bun Boh Hue) and Beef Lemongrass! Loved the Thai Iced tea! Will definitely be back for more!

We celebrated a family event last night. The Saag, Veg. Korma, Kulcha Onion Bread & Yellow Dahl were SUPERB - better than ever. How do they keep besting their best meals? Keep it up! Orange Kulfi Ice Cream Dessert is an amazing sensation. They say it is painstakingly made. When it comes to the table, it looks like fresh orange slices. Not! Surprise - must eat to fully appreciate. Simply The Best

This was certainly not the worst type place I had been. It is very clean on the inside, appears to be well-kept. People were very nice when I picked up my order, prices were reasonable. This is not the place to go if you like spicy Thai food, or less Americanized food in general. It was OK, so I gave it a three out of five, I would not recommend this to anybody looking for authentic Thai food

Excellent place giving a feel of mumbai street food in US with much more cleanliness. One of the best vada pav I have had in US. Chaats (samosa and aloo tikki) as well as dabeli are equally delicious. Very courteous owners and chefs. Absolutely worth it and highly recommended!!

Unsure about the previous reviews but I will say the decor was great. I had high expectations from this but l was soon disappointed unless you have had true authentic Caribbean food then you have nothing to go off I'll start with the beef patty which was very good and Flaky but the oxtails tasted more American then Caribbean they did not have the brown stew sauce then they were tough. nice people nice decor but Americanized food

Food is decent. Portions are a little small. I work nearby so it's a convenient place for a change from fast food. It was a much better place when it was Thai Bowl. Portions were larger and prices were cheaper. The "hostess" has the customer service skills and temperament of a wet honey badger. On my last visit, I walked into the place, which was completely empty, at 2:15. I asked about the free soda with lunch entree special and was told "No that only til 2:00." Uh ok. Guess that free 20oz Coke bottle was too much to expect 15 minutes late with their bustling business. If you are in the immediate area, have the need for Thai and aren't big on customer experience, check them out. Other than that, I'd suggest driving on down the road to one of the other Thai places nearby.

Came with my family yesterday to eat pho - my parents were in town from out of state early that day and were famished. They are pho enthusiasts so I decided to check out this place: the crab rangoons were on point and the pho tai was delicious - the broth has a thick, rich flavor which I liked. The meat in the pho nam however was a bit too tough and had a weird smell to it, but it was still great aside from that. The lady was courteous and DID not delay in bringing out the dishes and other side dishes we had asked for (most pho places are very lacking when it comes to promptness). Overall I was pleasantly surprised to discover this hidden gem in Indianapolis. I will be back again in the near future.
Definitely one of the best places for Kashmiri Chai! The perfect blend of steamed milk with pistachios in perfect harmony makes for a lovely treat!

Spiro's is a fantastic little gem. The food is Greek and really delicious. I think it's "authentic" but I can't say for sure, since I've never been to Greece. I've come for lunch several times and always enjoyed it. The bread they bring out is warm and fresh. Service is friendly and top notch. Prices are extremely reasonable and you get great value for your money. Definitely get the saganaki (flaming cheese) as an appetizer. It's extremely tasty and they set it on fire right in front of your table and make a little show of it (Opa!). Make sure to squeeze a little lemon on it, it really kicks it up. They also have an really nice outdoor patio, perfect for good weather days. The interior is also very pleasing, sophisticated without being stuffy. You'll love it. Just go.
Loved it! Incredible authentic food. Delivery was on time. Portions were massive. So darn good!

My wife and I ate here a few weeks ago. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal. The waitstaff was very friendly and knowledgable. The food was presented well and tasted excellent. The overall downside is that I left this restaurant hungry, and there was no shortage of courses that were ordered. A growing trend in New Orleans seems to be trending towards appearance rather than portions. I still highly recommend this place. The chef is doing great things. I just personally think the portions should be large. But maybe that's just me.... I have heard great things about their brunch, and plan to try it out in the near future.

O.M.G. delicious!!! Ordered delivery and all I can say, is WOW. Delivery process is effortless and quick. I ordered through the yelp app. Paneer tikka masala was great. The paneer tikka biryani even better. I have never seen anything like it! Naan is delish. I would say that the menu items are very unique. Only negative, prices are steep. But portions are good and food is even better.
Bar none, this the Best Eastern Indian food in and around Tucson. Curries and spices are great. Ingredients are fresh. Ate Indian in London. These guys have it nailed........

We stopped in here for a weeknight dinner, and were pleasantly surprised. It's BYOB (wish we had planned ahead). My husband's Pad Kee Mao was tasty (leads us to believe they do Thai classics well), but we both agreed that the real star of the meal was the Vegetarian Nam Salad - a sticky marinated rice with a bunch of toppings served with lettuce wraps. The flavors in this dish were exquisite and unique.

Hours after becoming an official Fairmount resident, I walked into Zorba's with a party of three. Two of us had been to Greece before, and the pictures on the wall brought us back! Zorba's is pretty small, but it's bright and has character. The food is fairly priced and delicious, though it took a little long to come out. It was okay, however, as we wanted time to decompress after unpacking boxes all day! I chose the honey mustard chicken sandwich, which came on a pita with the circular fries on the inside. The others chose the seafood salad and the charcoal chicken and both really enjoyed their dishes as well. We shared the baklava dessert and that was also on point. The meal was a nice change of pace, and I'm so glad to have this place down the street now! I'll most definitely be back soon.

The buffet at India Palace is the largest I've ever seen, and it's packed with fine renditions of all my favorites. Love their vegetable lentil soup - what a subtle, satisfying dish! I always get the chicken tikka masala (chicken in a distinctive tomato sauce, nav rattan korma (veggies plus cashews and raisins), and their spinach dish, along with whatever else strikes my fancy. Great stuff! I used to be finicky about veggies. India Palace taught me to appreciate them.

I don't know if they changed their name of the restaurant. As I read below that they have new owners. The name I found on Restaurant.com was Pho' Xe Lua Vietnamese Restaurant and the address is the same. It was Mother's Day and my family decided to eat Vietnamese. We were very disappointed with the food and the service. We were the only family along with another family who had already been there. I would think that the service would have been much better. I had Vietnamese food several times to be able to tell how the food should taste like. I did not like the taste at all. I have been to another Vietnamese restaurant and the food served was much better in texture and presentation. The shrimp was overcooked and not the amount that should have been in the meals we ordered. I cannot rate this restaurant except for a one star.
Food is pathetic, service is worst. Place is shabby and bad.. I recommend not to go. You will get sick..

I went with a group of 7 and we did not have to wait long to get a table. We had pho and banh mi. The pho was the best I've had in New Orleans (so far). The owner was really nice, she came by and introduced herself. I would go back to this restaurant for pho!

I've been here a few times and always find something enjoyably different each time. I recommend the spinach pie, much like many of the earlier commenters. From the main course selection you should try any of the clearly marked authentically Albanian dishes. They are house specialties you probably won't find anywhere else in St. Louis. They are quite tasty too. Be aware: The front of the restaurant is the bar area where friends and family hang out and it can be a little intimidating to walk in and ask for a seat if you don't feel like you're 'in' with the owners. I encourage you to go anyway. Once you are seated you'll feel at home pretty quickly.

A good restaurant, it has generous portions. But it is not exceptional; the plates are flavorful, and the meat well done but not memorable. Given the size of the plate it is a good place for a family. I do recognize that exceptional Middle Eastern food is very difficult to findin the US, unless you're willing to pay big bucks or to travel to New York or LA. But it if you need a hummus fix or some reasonable grape leaves, this is the place.

Awful...horrible..a bad idea!!!! horrible food, me and my gf didnt even bother to eat even 25% of our entrees or to get the remaining 75% packed! Service is horrible too!...nobody to check us in or to find us a table. Even after we found the table nobody bothers to get us the menus! we had to look around the place (tiny and very shabby) and finally had to go into the Kitchen to get the menus!!! That is unacceptable! I have no idea how can this place even average a 3.5 on yelp!!!

To be upfront, I'm not going to take too much time to write this review; rather, I'll probably put the same amount of effort and interest in writing this that the waitstaff spent on us this evening. First, the ambience is neither funky nor hip, but it is odd. The seating consists of folding chairs at used office desks, and tonight, dying roses were adorning the table. The menu is limited; when I asked for brown rice, they informed me that they serve just one kind - white. Well, I'll deal, I thought and hoped that the entree itself, a ginger mushroom dish with tofu, would be worth it. When they brought out my meal, it was filled with unexpected surprises that were not listed on the menu - broccoli and zucchini. Now had I known that zucchini and broccoli would be added to the dish, I would never have ordered it, but I just figured I'd remove them. After taking those out, there wasn't much left to the dish, since the tofu portion of the dish contained just 5 tiny tofu cubes. Once I had removed the offending vegetables, I proceeded to start eating the entree, which turned out to already be cold... and bland and watery as well. I have yet to figure out where the ginger entered into the dish; it seems like that was forgotten. Or replaced with extra water, I couldn't tell. My companion had recommended that I tell the server, but she was far more attentive to a gentleman visitor to the establishment, and I realize that to do so would likely have gotten me nowhere, regrettably. Would I recommend this restaurant? If cold, bland, watery dishes with surprise ingredients are as enticing to you as servers who are all over the customers at the next table, have I got the place for you!
I luv there Fried Whiting, cabbage and string beans!! Best I've had in a long time!

I always used to want to try Numchok Wilai but wasn't often nearby. Now that I work across the street I've been three times and have been happy each time! The restaurant is spacious and very clean. I love the way it is decorated simply, yet elegantly at the same time, with golden statues and wall hangings. Twice I've had the absolute cutest waitress - so polite and always smiling, asking if everything is alright and filling up water. All of the staff are friendly and happy, but she is just the best. I've had the Pa-Nang Shrimp ($13.95), Green Curry Chicken ($11.95) and Stir Fried Lemongrass with beef ($11.95), as well as bites of Cashew Chicken, and the veggie spring rolls. Rice costs extra - $1.50 for steamed rice, $1.95 for coconut rice. Everything always tastes fresh and comes out hot. The flavours are nice and the portions are perfect. The leftovers are really good the next day, too. One of the best things about this restaurant is the daily lunch special. A limited selection of items from the dinner menu all priced lower at $9.95, plus a small bowl of lemongrass soup, two spring rolls and rice! An amazing deal for sure.

What a find!! We were looking for another place and drove passed here and noticed the crowd. Yummy! I still have delicious flavors in my mouth. We split a Greek salad which was enough for 4 people. The greens were so tasty. The dressing was good. We split a chicken pita served with delicious French fries. This is a cool East Nashville place!!

Even by NOLA standards, this was an incredible meal! Two of us had the CL Pimms Cup - way to easy going down, very nice! The third tried the Andromeda (I think that's the name) - made with green chile vodka; we weren't sure at first about this one, but decided it was a definite winner. We didn't want to decide so the three of us decided to share a number of dishes. We started with Conch Croquettes and Steak Tartare Profiteroles. The Croquettes were fine, good but paled by comparison. The Profiteroles were unbelievable!! Had to convince the two I was with that raw meat donuts were a good idea at first, but OMG!! Incredible! Next we had the Marinated Shrimp with Roasted Jalapeño Jus, Roasted Beet Salad with Kale Pesto and then the Curried Goat with Sweet Potato Gnocchi. So amazing!! The Shrimp was very much like a ceviche with lots of onion and avocado and perfectly "cooked" with the jus good enough to eat like soup. The beets were earthy and sweet and the kale pesto got mopped up with the crostini that came on the side. The goat was tender with minimal heat, but plenty of warm cinnamon/clove flavors and the sweetness of the gnocchi was a great counterpoint to the richness of the meat and curry. Finally, for dessert we had Banana Zeppole and Lime Cheesecake. The zeppole had chocolate bits in the middle which were a pleasant surprise and the caramel sauce it was served with had enough burned sugar flavor to add some great depth. The lime cheesecake wasn't a key lime flavor - it was more true lime so not as much grab you by the throat tartness that allowed the creamy sour of the cheesecake to work very well with the citrus. INCREDIBLE!! We were also given a few herb biscuits with bacon butter and honey butter - not even remotely impressed, strangely enough.
I loved this place the food is excellent and the service was perfect. Everything I had I liked. My family and I came here on a slow night and ordered all the aps and shared. We had a great time.

Soooo ..... I had high expectations for this restaurant. I flew into Tampa to spend thanksgiving with my best friend. She told me about this restaurant several months ago, knowing that I'm Jamaican and that I would really appreciate this restaurant. During my second night in Tampa, my friends and I reunited at Yah Mon for dinner. First, the interior decor was divine! Rarely do you see an upscale Caribbean restaurant in Tampa .... if at all ever. I immediately got excited and looked at the menu to order the "Taste of the Islands" with a side order or corn, mac n cheese and the Virgin Islander drink. Let's start with the GOOD - the cocktail drink was amazing; the customer service was great; I loved the menu's concept; the brown stew chicken was delicious! The BAD - the service was extremely slow, the remainder food lacked flavor - my friends and I added salt to a lot of the food, the corn was canned corn, the macncheese was mediocre, and the jerk chicken wasn't what I expected ... it was baked jerk chicken, not the authentic jerk chicken cooked on the grill; and the rice & peas was the worst rice & peas I've ever had at a restaurant. Now, my friend that dined here previously said the taste and flavor of the food wasn't the same as when she dined her last time - and I wholeheartedly trust her taste and opinion. So I have to assume it was a different cook in the kitchen. I've discovered over the years in my dining experience that consistency in quality and flavor of food is very important to a restaurant's continuous success - I recommend that the owners ensure their food and quality remains consistent. Do not have too many hands in the pot.
Very good cuisine in a very cozy atmosphere. Overall the food was great. I had the stuffed tofu which was prepared very well. If you're in the area definitely check out Green Basil!
All in all my favorite restaurant in Philly. Great prices, great service and great food. I recommend the spicy fish

I'll jump on the review train to offer my thoughts on this Indy gem. For those not acquainted with the Ethopian way of eating, I'll do my best not to spoil it. Suffice to say, it'll be communal, and if you don't like eating with your fingers you are out of luck. But, you should like eating with your fingers... right? Best option if you bring a group of 3 or 4 are the sampler dinners. They offer a variety of dishes to try, with unlimited bread. Don't go for the largest option with your quartet. the "sampler for 2" will feed double that, with room to spare. Save some money for their Ethopian beer, which is in stock on occasion.

We absolutely LOVE coming to this restaurant !! We've been to many Thai restaurants in the area, and Thai Place is by far our favorite. Everything on the menu is very decently priced and delicious ! We have some favorites that we keep going back to (Pad See Ew, Massaman Curry, Tamarind Duck...) but also love asking for recommendations and have never been disappointed when trying something new.

A very good spot for fresh, well made African food in the Philly area. There's two locations (Upper Darby x West Philly) and they both offer quality options. No complaints on food/service but I have a tendency to order online and I've made several complaints about the limitations of the online menu. For example, the dry fish will just come with dry fish and rice BUT if you were to call in there's an option to add the veggies for an optional $3-4 (a bit steep for some veggies) so because they won't take cards over the phone I continually have to maneuver my order by adding items that add an additional price and then commenting what additional items I really want. It'd be nice if their online ordering was a bit more user friendly and reflected the menu options you would have in store. Other than that no issues. Large portions, fresh ingredients and reasonably fast delivery. Try the homemade ginger drink (if in stock) it's the best!

Since the two of us had to utilize a $50 Groupon, we had a feast last night with plenty left over. The stand outs were: Lobster Tikka Masala, Lamb Korma, Daal Soup and Keema Naan. Service was friendly and attentive. I can hardly wait to return.

Delicia definitely, without a doubt, deserves a 5 out of 5. It's a Nuevo Latino cuisine which basically means a little bit of above/everything since it has some Cuban, Mexican, Argentine, Peruvian, etc flair to the dishes. The ambiance was inviting. It reminds me of restaurants that I will go to in LA. Dark mood lighting, exposed wood beams, huge bar, Latin music playing...whoever designed the place deserves a pat in the back. The food was amazing. We ordered tostones con longaniza and empanadas as appetizers, beef with chimichurri and paella for the main entree. Then for dessert, we settled on a flan. They were all delicious. We'll definitely go back to this place. Sunday supper is the perfect time since there's no wait time.

The fact that I no longer work at Drexel and thus have no more access to Cucina Zapata makes me so incredibly sad. I have never had a bad meal from this place - everything is fresh, delicious, and innovative. Red curry is always good, thai green curry is even better, and the short rib tacos are amazing. The chicken katsu with egg is my go-to comfort food, but you haven't lived until you've tried their Captain Crunch tilapia burrito. The guys here will modify it any way you like (I always get mine over rice with extra sauce and avocado), and are friendly even through insane lunch rushes of up to 40 min wait times. Go there now and get something, and if you're unsure, either your fellow customers or the truck staff will help you out.
Good food at a good price. The $7.99 lunch buffet is almost unbeatable for lunch downtown. Great service, too!

What's not to like about a place where you can walk in, get a totally satisfying lunch in a matter of minutes from the buffet (plenty of vegan/vegetarian choices, traditional Indian dishes), all for $4.29. Mostly a takeout place, it's also handy for that quick lunch. For eating-in, you can also order from their menu, as the buffet is somewhat limited compared to the full menu. Seating is somewhat limited - as I say, it's mainly a takeout business - but stopping in for a late lunch recently, there were several empty tables.

Overall experience, drinks were great and food was good. Service has always been good there. I have been there several times but for the price point there are other places I would rather go. The sides on the dishes were a little redundant and some of the entrees are a little small. But definitely try for yourself and the drinks alone are worth the trip!

Had the best wings I've ever tasted! Not overly sauced and the skin is crispy. The tacos were just as good, but sadly they no longer offer the combo (one of each kind of taco, chicken, beef, and pork). We spoke with the manager (I'm assuming) several times. She made it a priority to speak with all of the customers. The food here is definitely too notch. My only criticism is that our food was slow coming out. Our server was nice enough to inform us that an appetizer was not going to be ready until near when our entrees would be so we just cancelled it. Overall a great experience and worth the try.
Clean, great falafel and awesome Shawarma!!! People are nice and friendly too.

Visited this place today on the occasion of my moms bday and had a very bad experience!! Inspite of today being a Sunday, we were the only customers there and I should have probably taken the hint!! After ordering we waited for 40 min for the food to arrive and though we had ordered starters, entrees and main course it was the main course Lamb Biryani that arrived first the taste of which was pathetic. The kebab that we had ordered as starter came in time for the dessert and believe me when I say that I have never tasted any kebab worse than this one!! It was half cooked and did not have even the basic seasoning of salt and pepper! Never will be back to this place!!!

Eat here. Trust me. I live down the street. Just tried for the first time and will be going back many times over. Had Pad Thai, roti canai, and sesame chicken. So fresh. Fast (like 5 minute wait), and the flavors are incredible. The people are nice. Cheap too. Do yourself a favor and stop looking for other options. (I'd add photos but we destroyed our food....)

I usually dislike saag paneer, but I took a chance and it was so flavorful and rich! I'll definitely order it again. The portions were filling and I had leftovers for lunch. I look forward to trying all the other dishes in time.

Found out about this place from a good friend. It's a very small place, there is ALWAYS a line but when I get my OXTAIL!!!!! All that fades away The best Caribbean food I've had so far. I order the same thing ALLLL the time. Oxtail with cabbage/corn and white with the sauce alllllll over my rice.. And my husband loves their Jerk Chicken... Portions served is worth every buck.

Best Malai Kofta curry in Tampa bay, Period! Blended with mouthwatering almond and tomato base. The koftas are close to perfection and the service is top notch.. finally one good Indian restaurant in St Pete and Clearwater area.

So I stopped at Jiallo's for a quick late bite to eat and ended up with a whole lamb. They definitely don't skimp on the portions. Their rice and beans is super yummy and the plantain is awesome. I went only 30 minutes before they closed and they still catered to me like I was there in the middle of the day. My server even offered to refill my drink a few minutes before closing time.

A co-worker bought me food to go from here on Tuesday of this week for my birthday (last week) and today I got a dish I used to enjoy at a restaurant owned by the current owner's parent in the mid 90's, which I thought or was led to believe was the reincarnation of that dish, more on that in a minute. I will start my review on Tuesday with the to go order for myself and two coworkers, I arrived and waited about 7 minutes for the order when I arrived on time for pick up. I got the food, it was quite messy when I made it to the office, I was confused as to why, but when I opened my dish I found out why there was at least a cup or two of sauce in my Generals Chicken, I would say it was filled up to halfway in a standard to go square box. That immediately turned my off, because I am not an super saucey person. The portion was decent and it came w/ steamed rice. I dug in, I was hungry, it was super bready, another turnoff for me. Overall the flavor okay, not mind blowing but good, but with the volcano sauce (which again made a mess in the bag, getting on everything, which I needed to wash off) and the super breading, I would give it 3 stars. Also, I asked for hot mustard and never received, found out they only have cheap packets here, no real mustard! =( The reason I went back so fast, was I found out the new owners, parent's used to own Golden Flower on Virginia Street by Sports West. I fell in love with the Lemon Grass Chicken there, and would get it at least 1x per week. This was when I was young and had little money, so if I spent money consistently, that was MONEY that DELIVERED to me in all the ways possible. I used to love that dish, and I have never found a replacement in town that even comes close it, in taste or value. When the new owner implied she had the recipes before Golden Flower was sold in 1995 to the current owners, who I found out just sold it this year, invited back to see if I agreed, which I readily accepted. I arrived today to sit and order, but it was 12:15PM, so prime lunch time for Friday, and it was about 10-15 tables, and many looked like they just sat, so I decided to take it to go thinking it would be faster. I didn't look at the menu, ordered Ala Carte, paid and then was told 15-20 minutes. Not my favorite thing to hear, but I already paid, so I waited patiently, again expecting a LONG LOST FAVORITE DISH RESURRECTED FROM A CHERISHED TIME REMEMBERED, READY TO REEXPERIENCE WITH THE MOST LIKELY PERSON TO RECREATE THE DAUGHTER OF THE OWNERS WHO WAS THERE DURING THAT SPECIAL TIME! I got to the office, and started paying attention to my food I was anxiously anticipating eating, and I noticed the weight was light, it didn't feel like a meal, I was hoping I was wrong. I got to the lunch room opened the bag, and looked it over and it didn't look like a big portion nor did it have lemon grass. It didn't look WOW, just like HUH, so I dug in hoping the flavors were there, and sadly they WERE NOT! The chicken was overcooked, no lemongrass, a few scallion were there, some onions didn't taste garlic or ginger, and the curry was abundant, but little flavor except salt. This DISH FELL FLAT! It was edible and okay, but I would never order again, and that's the reason for the two stars. When it comes to food I hold in high regard, it needs to hit me in a sweet spot, and this food did not. My biggest complaint besides overcooked and dry chicken is NO LEMONGRASS in LEMONGRASS CHICKEN? I just do not understand, when this was the daughter of Who's Famous in my Book of the Best of the Best, and I remember the delicious and unique flavor of the abundant Lemon Grass in the dish back in the mid 90's. Also, the portion was 1/2 size, it wasn't a dinner portion it was like a lunch portion plus. Last but not least the curry was super weak it's kind you buy over the counter, maybe don't seal after using maybe at the end of shift and after 2-3 months of this lack of respect, it's stale, and you can taste salt only and just see the yellow of the curry, and that's about it. Two more thoughts, as I put much thought into my reviews and do not take giving out reviews lightly, my coworker order the BBQ Pork and Shrimp w/ noodles. They put 2, count 2 shrimp in her dish. She didn't volunteer the information, but we were having a conversation, and I was telling her I get scared to order shrimp most places because of the freshness, etc. I then asked to see a shrimp in her dish, to judge, which she just started eating, and she said, I don't have anymore, and I said, WHY? She said well there was only 2! Last thought, my coworker on this visit order spring rolls, we had two, not very large springs rolls for $6. Value sucked, and I would never order these again! Overall, SF Kitchen is a nice place in somewhat awkward neighborhood, but it's just not for me, but it might fit for you!

Dinner for four with friends in the Meridian-Kessler neighborhood. We started with some of their signature cocktails including the Fire 'n' Ice, Margaritas and the Botanica Sour. We then started with a couple of safe options of calamari and guacamole which did not disappoint. The entrees were even better. We had empanadas, orders of the chile relleno with roasted vegetables and shrimp and the short ribs. Everyone was delighted with their dinners. I had the empanadas which were stuffed with a spiced up beef with the consistency of a pot roast. It was fork tender and juicy and nearly melted in my mouth. My wife's relleno vegetables were roasted near perfection. She's not a vegetarian but thought it was a great substitute for the meat. Our server was very helpful with making the selections, quick to bring the drinks and food and checked on us regularly without being the least bit intrusive. The vibe was fresh and upbeat and the crowd was diverse and lively. We will definitely be back.

I took my son here for lunch today. We had to wait 20 minutes after being seated before the waiter even brought us menus. We then ordered and were never even asked for drinks. We were finally brought waters as an afterthought, right before our food came. EJ's soup and salad that he should've received prior to his meal never even came out. My food was bland and did not taste good. I had ordered the chicken noodle soup and a medium spaciness level. It was completely bland and the chicken was low quality and did not taste good. I did complain, which I rarely, do and did not eat any of it outside of my initial two bites to try it. However, instead of making it right, they still charged me full price for my meal which was bad, uneaten, and I did not get a to go box to take it.
Friendly and fast service. Great price for the amount of food you get and really yummy!

Lunch buffet has a wide variety of food. Many curry dishes as well as fried food, salad and dessert. The service is quick and friendly. The restaurant has a nice atmosphere. It is fun to visit Indian market next door after eating there.
This place is amazing food comes fresh from the I oven. Beef patties are made here and they make their own jerk seasoning no walkers wood here.

Ordered the pho dac Biet and beef spring rolls. Pho isn't over the top. Their tendons are a little off-putting. Trust me, I love me some tendons in my pho, but it wasn't happening for me here. I have cats tongue and usually can't eat scolding pho, but I do expect it to come out as so. Unfortunately it came out probably a little too late. The service was friendly though. Location and decor is pretty cozy. Will I come back? Only if someone drags me back to try something I didn't order. Then we can have further debate. But out of my own time, I don't think so.

This new restaurant was recommended to me. Went there with friends. We all thoroughly enjoyed our appetizers and meals. It's a small restaurant location which doesn't have much seating yet. They also do takeout. The chef was trained in France, and it showed with all the ingredients being very fresh and lots of great, interesting flavors. Most of the group had the Mixed Grill, and it was delicious! Everything was cooked perfectly. I highly recommend it. The pita bread was delicious and perfectly heated when served. This little Mediterranean gem's food will definitely please your tastebuds!

I found this place one day while shopping for furniture in Brandon. I was pleasantly surprised of the quality of their rolls, affordable prices and the great service. After that I've been going there with my husband every week. The staff is conformed by Thai girls that are very welcoming and professional. I recommend this place 100%.

Amazing food. I'm sort of becoming a regular. The gyros are always delicious, and the owner is super friendly. Whether you love gyros or you've never tried one, you need to give this place a shot. Admittedly, I generally get my order to go 99% of the time. The decor is nothing to celebrate, but there is a TV in case that matters to you. Not necessarily a place I would take my wife for date night (though we have eaten here for lunch!), but the food is second to none.

The ropa vieja with Spanish​ rice and beans and is always so good. The mangu is also​ delicious​. I also recommend the guanabana juice (although sometimes is super sweet). Big portions, good price, ​and friendly staff. ​

the food here is just alright, i'm not really a fan of white meat chicken in my food so that was the first problem. the pad thai was just blah. kinda tastes like something you can pick up in the frozen section at trader joes. the panang curry we ordered was lacking some flavor, but i can't really say anything was bad.

Sarah is a great bartender, her drinks were spectacular. While we were there there was a shift change and the difference was so obvious with the quality of the drinks. There was also a helper behind the bar, Riane was a great help, I would recommend him for any job. Great attitude.

Boise's newest food truck makes a noble effort to introduce Central American, South American, and Caribbean street food into a dining scene previously lacking in this this department. Latin Twist opened on July 12, 2014, with a prime permanent location at the corner of Boise Avenue & Beacon Street. Their menu is in flux, as they're still working out kinks regarding ingredient supply, prepare-ability of dishes in the truck, and customer tastes. They had a rather ambitious menu written on a whiteboard, but only about half the items were available today. On offer was jerk chicken, Argentinian ribeye, Peruvian linguiça, a Sonora dog, and several sandwich options -- a large enough selection, and enough of a variety to showcase their kitchen skills. The S.O. selected the jerk chicken, smoked over Jamaican pimento wood (though the owner's claim that he's the only guy west of the Mississippi with authentic Jamaican pimento wood seems dubious). This was a tame jerk [unsurprising for Boise], with less herbaceousness and kick than we tasted in Central America. But the flavor was nonetheless pleasant and the smokiness was entrancing. It was served with rice, beans, and some lovely grilled summer squash. My Costa Rican ribeye sandwich was also tasty -- tender shaved ribeye, pepperjack, black beans, grilled peppers, and shoestring potatoes on a fluffy bolillo. The pepperjack wasn't the most authentic decision, but it worked well enough. Same for Latin Twist's grilled corn -- topped with a poblano crema, it's not authentic elotes with chile-lime and cotija, but it still tastes good. Skip their version of escabeche, though, which is a strangely sweet mixture dominated by large slices of colored bell peppers.
