Since this is Boise, I worry that they might have to deviate even more from authenticity to suit customers. But hopefully the owners' passion for Latin cuisine and solid talents in the kitchen can maintain their quality products for a long time to come. Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/latintwistboise Hours: Daily, noon-9pm (later on weekends) Pay: Cash, plastic (they even take AmEx, you corporate expense-accounters!)

The best Food you can have in Edmonton! It is always fresh, with the best quality you can imagine, The restaurat is always full even on week days, so that explains a lot! The owner/chef/ master is a very nice talented man whose focus is on the quality. I always enjoyed dining there when I was living in Edmonton, miss my regular dining in Sofra

My husband and I always enjoy our food from A Taste of Jamaica. The food is always fresh hot and delicious. I appreciate the different sizes offered because I am not a big eater so I can order a Taste(small) and enjoy all the different items on the menu.

What a wonderful place to spend with the Family and friends....the food is insanely GOOD! Real Boricua food and the prices are low! I travel from Orlando to tampa on the weekeds just to go est at this place. The service is GREAT!!! The flavor is real Puertorrican Cuisine! And the Mofongo wowwww..... Is A-W-E-S-O-M-E !!!! And if you like Frituras... Try the Alcapurrias!!! Un lugar verdaderamente Boricua con saber del verdaro Borinquen!!!
Great neighborhood spot. The food is very good and not too expensive. It's got a casual vibe with good decor. We eat here all the time.
It's a really cute little cozy place, with super friendly staff and very prompt service. The food was very good, as well. No complaints!
Really liked their food - very tasty, and the servers were able to change our orders a bit due to some dietary restrictions that we have. Great place, and we'll definitely be back! :-)

Coolest dining experience I've ever had!!! I have been telling everyone about this place since I got back home. Sadly, there is no place nearly as cool as this one in Miami (that I know off). Anyway, you walk into the restaurant in a back ally kind of way, it definitely doesn't look like a restaurant from the outside! It reminded me of a house and each room had tables. The tables were all like a couch with a round table in front of you. No utensils- you eat with your hands! Such a cool place for groups of friends or even an intimate date. You can take your own alcohol since they don't serve any there - also cool! They give you pita breads to eat with your food and towels as napkins. Each course comes looking cooler than the last! I absolutely loved my experience at Marrakesh!!

Me and my boyfriend went here for the first time on Friday, from the start everything was fine and the service was good too. We ordered two rolls off of their specials menu and the presentation and all was great. The sushi was okay, it wasn't bad but it wasn't great. The next day my boyfriend and I both got sick, and 4 days later my boyfriend is still sick. This place has pretty good reviews so I'm not sure what happened with ours but we won't be coming back

Hoping they close this joint so that something worthwhile can take its place. $10 gyros (nothing special), odd atmosphere, it's hot as hell inside, and during my last visit, there was rap music playing?! Wish I had gone to Subway next door (and that's saying something...)

Nice ambiance for a Jamaican and African cuisine restaurant. Spacious rooms and seating. Warm, welcoming staff, made the wait comfortable. It is wise to call ahead. The wait for some dishes was exceptionally long. The waiters spoke several languages including French! I had the beef jerk ribs, they were tender and tasty. We also had jerk chicken, which was the best dish out of all the choices. Dinner is a little pricey, $16 for a plate but the jerk is worth that cost.
Great atmosphere, friendly wait staff, and awesome food! We really enjoyed sitting out on the patio, the weather was really nice. Every small dish we tasted was fabulous!

I deleted my last review - Due to Wishbone making things right after a bad experience. Warning - the chicken tenders sold by the pound and for half a pound - you get 2 for about $5.00 The fries are very good when fresh. Customer service - was poor but Erica (the Manager) made it right after what happened to my last order. I give Erica 5 stars. The biscuits are next level - but very small for 2.25. Should be 1.25. Many people have mentioned and I would agree for the price of the food - more food should be given. I would order again.

I gave them a 2nd chance and went there today and the service was night and day amazing!!!! The guy (hispanic) was just a pleasant and breath of fresh air! And the food was amazing! Great service and great food!

I would say this one is the best restaurant for all kinds of food. Their appetizers are delicious and all delivers what the customers need. I have almost tried each and every item of their menu. Trust me ppl...its realy a worthy meal. Give it a shot and you wont regret it. Good customer service, neat, clean restrooms. Whatelse can we say..!! 5 /5 i will say.

They get 2 stars because of the food. Otherwise it was a HORRIBLE experience. First off, took forever to find the place since the sign along the main road was so worn out it was almost gone and undistinguishable. There was only one family dining and yet when I walked in, there was no greeting let alone a friendly one. I was not offered a menu either, especially since it was obvious I was getting take out. It was a lackluster environment with visible flies. And when I went to pay, they then decided to tell me it was cash or check only. What? OK....So I had to use their ATM, which took me 3 tries to get it work and when I asked for assistance from the cashier, she ignored me. I was less than 5 feet from her. Cashier was not friendly at all. She even started to walk away from me as I was inquiring about the available boba tea flavors. Definitely not coming here again.

This is a great fast-n-healthy concept for Indian cuisine. I love that it is affordable and well portioned. Also, pretty unique dining experience for this type of cuisine. I love this place and they are vegetarian-vegan friendly. The owners are very hardworking and nice. Keep up the good work! I wish they were open on Saturdays.

Visiting the area, checked yelp. Hit a homerun. Had the "tuna amazing roll", and the "house special duck" The tuna roll, had three different tuna: incl a spicy tuna and a cooked pepper tuna, topped with avocado and a sweet (mango?) sauce on the inside!. The duck was boneless on a bed of veggie and delicious mellow brown sauce. Good flavor, and NOT chewy. Excellent Ordered too much, but that happens when traveling alone on business. Service was attentive, and exact.

By far the best Indian food I have had! The spices were well balanced. In some restaurants everything tastes the same, but not here. There is a great variety, especially for vegetarian and vegan options. We've been here twice and we will definitely come again!

Ate here tonight with my wife, we got take out. Let me start with the SERVICE because thats what stood out first and foremost. The women took the time to give us samples and explain to us EVERYTHING on the menu and encouraged us to mix and match all we wanted. Everything was EXTREMELY fresh and flavorful, oh and HEALTHY!! all of their meals are under 600calories or less. My wife loved it more than I! I ended up giving the women a $10 tip on a $19 order JUST because of how nice and awesome she was. We will return, alot.
Didn't look like much from the outside but an interesting cafe with very good Chai Tea, great deserts and a HUGE tea selection. Many beers and scruffy hipster loco locals abound.
I ordered uber eats wishbone. Food was stone cold. I had the southern sandwich, gross. The chicken is bland and overpriced. Beware do not spend money here if you like chicken.

Loved the atmosphere in the newly renovated extension, very cozy but still very busy. Ordered samosas and a coconut London fog. The drink was amazing! Loved the sweet hint of coconut. The samosas were spicier than I'm used to, and I don't think you can ever find two samosas made the same way, but these weren't my favourite. Willing to try other things on the menu though. The sauce on the side helped a bit with the spice but I didn't care for it. All in all, good experience and will come again. Oh! And I think their custom cups are absolutely adorable!

My co-worker took me here for lunch and the food was unforgettable. SO STINKING GOOD. I had the paella and didn't leave a single piece of food on the plate. The plantain fritters are also pretty spectacular!

I agree with everyone else that this place looks shady from the outside... but in the back, there is a raised area where there are nicer tables and better ambiance! I think this place is truly a gem because it's unlikely a ton of people are going to walk in on a given night, weeknights especially. Ate here on a weeknight. I had the lamb kebabs and a friend had the chicken. Both were great, but I am def partial to the lamb. We had the hummus as an appetizer, and that was delicious as well. I judge places on their hummus... so this place passed with flying colors! Attentive but not overwhelming service.

I really should branch out and order something other than pad Thai, but I didn't have it in me, once again. The pad Thai here is not my favorite I've ever had, but it's pretty good. The vegetables were fresh and tasty and the noodles were nicely cooked, but I think it was just slightly lacking in flavor. I ordered the medium level of spiciness and it just wasn't that memorable. I also ate the papaya salad for an appetizer. This was good, as far as papaya salads go. I think I totally just miss what most people like so much about the consistency of the raw green papaya strands. To me they are....ok.... but nothing that I crave or order of my own will. Every time I've eaten it, it's because someone else wants to share it. The place itself is super cute and BYOB so you should check it out. They are open until 10PM on weeknights, so it's convenient for late night dinner eaters. Cash only!

Very mediocre at best. Figured I'd try some delivery from here to see what the hype was about as I love pho and feel a cold coming on, wanted something spicy. Ordered spring roles, green onion cake and extra spicy beef satay. The spring roles were alright as well as the green onion cake however nothing special. The soup was not spicy at all And rather tasteless. I ended up spicing with my own sriracha hot sauce at home. Pretty disappointing. Service was friendly and delivery was quick, the food was very hot on arrival which is always a plus but I probably will skip on pho king again!

Deserves their 5 star rating! Yellow pancake is a must. Husband loved the Pho (I don't do beef so I didn't try it). Also loved the curry and vegetables. I can't wait to go back again. I'll order the yellow pancake right away!!!

Decent food and nice ambience. It's overpriced for the quality and portion sizes, especially the appetizers and kids menu. But service is friendly and fairly quick. It is pretty Americanized (e.g. chopped broccoli carrots and green beans in the tom yum, which incidentally is labeled lemongrass soup on the menu), so hard-core Thai food buffs used to authenticity probably won't like it.

We were visiting Nashville from NYC where we eat Asian/Indian fusion often. The food at Bamboo Garden was outstanding and on par with our cuisine in NY. If you have never had this type of fusion definitely give it a try as it is addictive and full of flavor. The staff was friendly and place is spotless. 5 Stars!!!!

I came here with my girlfriend last night after reading a lot of great reviews, and it really lived up to its hype. The owners name is Hasaan, and he greeted us as we walked in. He explained to us what chaat is and how he makes it. He asked us a few questions and custom made 2 orders of chaat for us - one with chicken, and one with lamb. Each bite had a totally different taste and texture. It was incredible. I'll definitely visit again.

New improved location at 2730 W. Waters. Telephone number: 813-490-9157. Some of the best Pho anywhere in the world. And I can back that up with passport stamps. Rich, flavorful and satisfying pho broth. I'm partial to #23 which has sliced beef and brisket. This food gives me the same comfortable feeling I get when I eat my mom's food. You'll also want to try the chicken and cabbage salad, pork chops over rice, pork skin rolls and the chicken with egg noodle soup all equally delicious. I've run into my favorite vietnamese waitresses and waiters from other Tampa bay area vietnamese restaurants dinning at Pho an Hoa. phoanhoatampa.com

One of the top three meals I've ever had in New Orleans... And that's with fierce competition! The ambience, the service and the food... The grouper, the curried goat and the steak tartare. Fantastic! I highly recommend chef Nina's amazing restaurant.

My friend raves about this place and decided to pick me up dinner for work. She got me Samosas rice and chicken tikka masala. Rice wasn't very flavorful but I don't expect a lot from a chipotle like place. I'm not an expert but I think I know a good Indian dish or two. Chicken tikka masala lacked a bit of flavor I was actually shocked Bc Indian food to me had one of the best strong and delicious flavors I have ever had. But I do Love the options that you can get you can mix it up which I think I will do next time. Really excited to try the naan. I will def return (my self this time) to try something different and give this place another try. I Love the concept of custom meals and I think I just have to play around with the combos. Will Def update my review for better or worse.

NEEDED TO IMPROVE!! as an international foodie. These are my honest opinions: 1. Menu items don't match! For example, #32 and 33. If 32 comes with a small size. Then why 33 even exist says: all above the same expect for a smaller size pho. Then small 32= 33 right??? Also the 81 pic doesn't match! The pic says its avocado smoothie and in the menu it's another thing:((( 2. Environment. Please seriously Decorate the place. Not just replacing with cheap decos. Use your heart to make this place nice. Put more cultural decos! Think more before you open. 3. Service. The waiter doesn't even know which item is which he has to use numbers to replace. SAD... I'm sorry I don't want to be rude but he need to ask us which one we ordered... And he doesn't even know which pho is which... Please be more motivated and familiar with the menu. 4.FOOD. The most important thing. First, in a good papaya salad, the papaya should NEVER be shredded should be chopped. And shouldn't have so much watery underneath!! It's a salad not soup. The salad is badly chopped ;( don't mean to be rude here. And the color doesn't feel like exciting. I ate great papaya salad before and it has mango, red radish and shrimp and spice. It should be a colorful appetizer not watery something. I ordered a small delux pho and it doesn't even come with everything says in the menu:(( SAD...it's doesn't have beef meat balls which says on the menu. Also the taste. It's not bad but NOT GOOD either. It doesn't trigger appetite. I mean it's not a bad cooking pho but also not a good cooking pho. Please have glasses instead of plastic cups to serve. I may says too much negative things but I really want you guys improve. Thanks! Not mean to be mean.

Maybe it has changed since i was there. Very pretentious way to much attitude. Food was eh. Expensive when compared to quality. Close to the river but they really dont take full advantage of the ambience. Just ok, could romantic enough for a date. No booze (something that they really need here).

I have been there twice and my husband and I both think the food is really good. It is different than our 2 fav Thai places in town ( Pad Thai House and Chiang) but different in a good way. The prices are a tad steep especially compared 2 my 2 favs. But because of the prices being higher I went both times with the restaurant.com coupons. I used one in Feb and bought another last Wednesday because one of the restaurants I had one for closed. The first time I used it was fine but the second there was an issue. I told the waitress I had the coupon right when I sat down before ordering and she said "ok" so when I got the check I went to give it to her but all of a sudden she comes out and says they don't take them anymore because they don't make any money on it. Well you should just be happy people are coming in to your restaurant and trying the food and maybe they will write a good review or tell their friends about it. I was pissed and told her that I told her about it at the beginning. Finally after some persuading she said she could honor it. She also said that they can't get restaurant.com to remove their company from the site which I don't buy. Call and talk to a manager and demand that they take it off. I got green curry and I got it between hot and Thai hot and it was pretty hot. I would say that it would be a 5 star on the hot scale at Pad Thai or Chiang. It was good and had lots of fish sauce which for me I do not mind. My husband got Rad Nah and said it was really good as well. The Chicken Satay was excellent as well and we thought their Thai ice tea was the best we have had. Even thought I am happy that they did end up taking the coupon. I am annoyed at the situation and how it seemed like it was almost my problem they don't make money on the coupon. They have to make something even just on the tip.

I've never actually left a review on any place because it feels really mean but honestly I'm so poor and those $10 I spent were really a lot so I want to save everyone else from making the mistake I did. The name of the place is pho bistro, don't get the damn pad Thai. Literally do not do it. The name is PHO not Thai food, there unfortunately are very very limited options in the area so I was desperate but honestly just do not do it. I wanted authentic Thai not made by a lady named Sharon and...it was honestly the most disappointing and depressing pad Thai I've ever had. And I pretty much try to get pad Thai wherever I go. It was literally bright orange noodles with zero flavor and I feel so mean saying that because I work in food/service whatever (starbucks for over a year) and I get it, I know sometimes shit happens and the service was honestly great! Super nice, really friendly, food came out fast...it just sucked :( it was bright orange you guys what even is that, the chicken was...weird and scary, just had a bad taste, it didn't taste like pad Thai at all and I'm really bummed bc I can't even afford to be spending money like that and I should've just gone with their pho. I've had their pho before, that shit was hella dank I recommend that 100% the place is great their pad Thai just...I'm scarred tbh. Should've known better than to go for Thai at a place literally called pho bistro. Excuse me while I cry over the $10 down the drain (I couldn't finish it, honestly it just wasn't pad Thai the noodles literally looked like angel hair pasta I'm really upset and sad mostly sad because I feel like if I was a dish I would be that sad sorry excuse of pad Thai) anywho, their pho is great and they give you a good amount too. Don't get the pad Thai though. :-)

The food here ranged from reasonably good to quite mediocre. At the forefront, the coconut soup with seafood (the special of the day) was spiced just right with lovely shrimp, only slightly marred by some rather tough squid. My friend ordered spring rolls which she found satisfying. My main course of green curry was merely passable -- the accompanying sticky rice was too tiny a portion to soak up the sauce, and the curry itself was pasty with minimal flavor. On service the restaurant utterly failed. The waiter (proprietor?) only came over to us when we either walked across the restaurant to get him, or loudly called out his name. (We actually learned his name from another patron; as we attempted every possible way to attract the waiter's attention, this patron said "His name is Sam. Just yell out Sam and he will come".) Eventually, using this strategy we got Sam to come over. At that point we had waited a half hour for him to take our initial orders, including drinks. As the meal progressed the problems with service persisted. Several times we walked over to Sam and asked for additional items. Furthermore one in our party noticed that her tea, for which she had patiently waited 40 minutes, was lukewarm -- not hot enough to brew with a teabag. She eventually received new tea, but no apology. I won't be going back.

This place is ok. The food quality was good, but it just wasn't out of this world. We tried it on a Wednesday (apparently they do a buffet that night), which was cool because we got to try a lot of different dishes. However, we still like IndeBlue in Collingswood better.

Was my favorite Indian place in town. Finally went and braved the lunch buffet to try it out and DEEPLY disappointed. They bought the name, but the rest is totally different. TATER TOTS?! On the buffet mixed in with the sa(lt)mosas (yeah, that'd be salt-mosas, not samosas). No channa masala on the buffet. The mint, tamarind sauces were not good, and there was no red- "mcdonalds onion" sauce either. What was even sadder is that the new owners and their daughters seemed very attentive and concerned but have just missed the mark SOOO much. Not as many veggie options on the buffet as before and overall, just not good, bland and salty. The peas palao (or however you spell it) was just oily and tasteless. What a shame. This WAS the restaurant that I used to compare all others to as a my favorite. Now, I simply won't go back. Pictures soon to follow of new ridiculous menu- "we got delivery" and "when you google dining in the fine dining capitol of reno-sparks-tahoe-carson" (or something to that effect). Thanks new halal owners of taste of india for informing me that I live in one of the fine dining capitols of the world, I had no idea?! Oh yeah, they seem to have bounced around with the name since going under new ownership- it was india kabob something for a while and is now back to being called taste of india. There seems to be some confusion about this being a move from another location, it's not. It's been here for at least 8 years (since I started going) - it's just an ownership change that will probably ruin the place.

Went on a date with my husband and since we love Thai food we knew we had to check this place out. We live in NY so have tasted so many and since we were visiting my mother and had a guaranteed babysitter we came here. It was small but a very nice atmosphere. Decor fit the environment perfectly and the art was quite beautiful. Service was great they were kind and very fast. And since we love trying foods and love to share we ordered the drunken noodle with tofu, basil rice with beef and eggplant with chicken. Sauce from the eggplant was great and so was the chicken and rice but the eggplant was a little mushy for me but still tasty. The basil rice was our favorite it was spicy but not too much and the flavors hit the spot! The drunken noodle was good but my husband loves the spicy overload he gets in the city but still liked it. For me it was perfect for me. Everything was delicious and a great experience! We will be coming back!

I'm not that familiar with Jamaican food so naturally I went the jerk chicken platter. It was absolutely delicious. I cleared my plate. I like that the place is BYO, has good food, and a nice outdoor seating area but.... The service was horrendous. When my roomate and I walked in, the girl behind the counter acted as if she hadn't seen us. When I asked if we seat ourselves, another customer informed me that you do. So, we moved to the outdoor and sat ourselves at a table that looked clean enough. 20 minutes later, as we were about to get up and leave a waiter ( I think the only waiter) came over to greet us . Because I was determined to give this place a chance we stayed. It took about 45 minutes for our food to come out and there were only 2 other tables seated. When our check came, we were shocked at the corking fee, but we were ready to leave. As I said, the food was absolutely delicious but because of the service, I don't know that I'll be back.
Great food, huge portions, and friendly attentive service! The pho is very flavorful.

THEIR FOOD IS AMAZING!!!!! I absolutely love this place. This is the place I take people who have know prior experience with Indian food because I know they'll love it :D Don't be fooled by its looks. This place rocks!!!!!
Food is good, we order Maybe twice a month, very close to us. Love trying different foods, friendly staff would recommend to others.

First of all, Indian food is my favorite, and I have been to all the Indian restaurants in Tampa bay. I have been to this place a few times, and every time I go it gets worse. I came for the lunch buffet with my husband (who is Indian). When we arrived the host/waiter seemed to act annoyed to seat us. When the bread came, the only plus was that it was hot. It was a small portion and too crunchy/not soft. Seeing that naan is a staple food in Indian cuisine, it should be cooked right. I asked if they had chai masala, the waiter gave me a weird look and said he didn't know what it was, then said they don't have any, and acted annoyed to be bothered with the question. Chai masala (or chai tea as I clarified) is a staple drink in all areas of India, and pretty much every Indian restaurant has it on the menu. I was pretty shocked that he said he didn't know what it was and was kind of rude about it. The buffet food was definitely not worth the $....the two chicken dishes, chicken tandoor and chicken jalfreezi were dry and the chicken was obviously not freshly made, just reheated. The chicken tandoor was just really sad, just a few strings of dry, reheated meat, on bones. They were completely out of the palao rice, but the plain rice was ok. The vegetable dishes were just ok--not a lot of flavor or spice. Since the reheated chicken was gross, I just stuck to the rice and vegetable dishes. Last but not least was the kheer (rice pudding). It was soupy, flavorless, and had hardly any rice in it. It tasted like slightly cold mik with sugar in it. None of the food here was worth the money. This place used to have great waiters and the food was awesome. Now it seems like they just don't care anymore. Never going again.

Great experience! Had lunch outside on Christmas eve day....and had very cheerful waitress. The special, Crab and Shrimp Burger with Seafood Gumbo was very tasty, espcially followed by Key Lime Pie. A great place to watch people and dogs go by.

Disappointed to say the least. Used to be my favorite place. It seems it has gone down hill with cleanliness. Our silverware was dirty, both sets, one had dried on rice stuck on it. A fly on the rim of my beer as it was brought out, I immediately told her and she took it back immediately and said it was last nights bartender who left fruit juice out and it attracted them. Our date night was spent making sure the food was okay. I know things happen, but when we have only a couple date nights a year, I like them to be enjoyable. We weren't even offered a beer credit. Nothing. Won't go back.

My husband and I stumbled across this place by chance after wandering about Rittenhouse Sq. for half an hour trying to find a suitable, reasonably priced place for dinner. (We're from out of town.) I would give this restaurant 5 stars based on service alone. We went in because we saw "drunken duck" on the sidewalk menu (and I love duck more than anything). I tempered my expectations though, because I have a gluten allergy that prevents me from being able to eat dishes made with normal soy sauce and duck is usually prepared with soy sauce. When I asked about it inside, the owner came over and explained that there is indeed soy sauce in the base. But before my heart even had time to break, he told me that he could make a special version of it for me without the soy sauce. A few minutes later, he brought out a ramekin of the sauce for me to taste test for spice level. It was *delicious*. Needless to say, the dish was fantastic. The sauce was a perfect mix of sweet, and spicy and the duck was crispy skinned with moist delicious meat inside. Even the Chinese broccoli on which it was served was smoky and wonderful, having been doused in brandy & rum and set on fire! (Extra credit for flair.) And lest I feel guilty that the chef/owner went to all this trouble for me, he came out again after we ate to tell me that he enjoyed the challenge of preparing the dish without soy sauce. If only all chefs reacted that way to customers' dietary restrictions! Talk about above and beyond... We will be back here for sure when we move to the city. (Oh, and my husband, who claims not to like Thai food, had a beef dish involving oyster sauce and he enjoyed it thoroughly.)

The food was not inedible, except the crusty appetizers that had clearly been sitting on the buffet since lunch. And they advertise their kababs but none came with the buffet. Fresh naan was delivered and that was quite good. The "waiter" was grim, but responsive. The capper is that they have their own brand of beer, a light lager, but I wanted something else (we were already regretting our restaurant choice so I was leery about the beer) I asked him for a menu with their selection of beers (East Asian Village has a wonderful selection of beer) and ordered a Kingfisher. A man, I assumed to be an owner, came over and told me they have only ONE beer, their own brand. He brought me 330 ml of beer in a elderly looking pint glass that was clearly bought at a thrift store. We couldn't get out of there soon enough.

And the search goes on for a Thai restaurant I can call home. I came in during the weekday around lunch time and was surprised I was one of the only tables there (an impending sign of doom or did I miss the rush?). But I went straight for the usual Thai fair, after all it was my first time there. I ordered family style dishes which consisted of chicken panang curry and vegetable phad Thai to keep it as simple as possible. Pro: all white meat chicken. Hell yes, no picking out the fatty reject chicken tidbits. Fast service (after all, my sister and I were the only ones there), friendly staff, and quiet atmosphere. Con: everything else. Meh. The food was OK, but nothing that brought me back to California nostalgia of awesome Thai restaurants. Like I said, I tried to keep it simple, right? Thai Country Cafe is worth another shot, though. Hopefully I'll be there on a good day.

Typical Indian buffet, but definitely on the high end of the scale. For a self-serve place the service is very good, they bring out naan, silverware, and drinks. The food is all fresh, warm and very good. The atmosphere is cozy, it's dimly lit with traditional Indian decorations and soft Indian music. 10/10 EDIT: I had tripped on my way to take a photo and was on the ground for a few seconds, as I got to the buffet I felt something crawling on my elbow, I slapped it and two bugs about stink bug size(but with the body structure of a ladybug) ran towards the the buffet and disappeared....literally seconds after I posted my original review. I was in shock for several minutes but took the photo of the buffet nonetheless... 3/10 because the food was nice and the decor was good but bugs on the floor...

At first I was a little confused by A Taste of Thai. It is located in a little strip mall which led me to believe it would be like some of the Dive Vietnamese places around town where I could get some cheap barely authentic food. Once inside I realized I was not in a Dive. It is clean and well decorated with modern music playing (could have done without that.) It was dinner and I ordered a curry with soup. Still not sure what to expect from this place my hopes for a good dinner were shattered when the waiter brought a very typical americanized egg flower soup just slightly pimped-out with cubed tofu. I thought "oh great! Another stereotypical American Asian place." But I was wrong, the curry was AMAZING. Very well balanced. I haven't had Thai that good since I was in Bangkok years ago. Taste of Thai isn't quite as authentic as a road side Pad Thai vendor in Bangkok but it is really close considering we are in Boise Idaho. I will go back to try some more of what they have to offer

We live in Havertown. Our good friends live in Allentown. About 3 or 4 times a year we like to get together for dinner and usually meet somewhere in the middle. The first time we did this about 3 years ago, we went to Nadia Thai - a total fluke that we found this place. We have never met anywhere else since that first dinner. The food is amazing - the best Thai we have ever had. The service is great and the prices are extremely reasonable. We always over-order and share everything. We have NEVER been dissapointed. This is well-worth the 45 minute drive. Every three months I look forward to catching up with our friends but look forward to going to Nadia Thai even more.

Came here with my roommates and man-friend for dinner on a Sunday. Not too busy and was seated quickly. Mulled over the menu and ordered: Pad Kee Mao (Spicy Noodles) - Spicy indeed! Made the way I like, but lacked the huge slice of tomatoes I usually find. Seaweed Salad - Thrown off by the lettuce/arugula mix on top of the seaweed, but otherwise good Chicken Mussuman - Not the best mussuman I've had. The curry had a spice that overpowered the coconut milk, which gave it a tangy aftertaste. Tangy isn't good when I expect something rich or creamy. Ate all this with jasmine rice and shared among four people. Still managed to have left overs. The restaurant is small, and by the looks could get crowded on a normal weekend. Dim lighting for those who think dim equates to romantic, but people weren't too dressed up to eat here. Overall, a nice place to grab some Thai food.

We have been long time patrons of Pita Jungle and today will be our last time at this establishment. The cook (I refuse to say chef) messed up twice on basic ass chicken breasts. Our server (the only familiar face in the building) told him twice to pay attention to the ticket and he returned her feedback with a dirty look... does he realize it's an open kitchen? We waited 45 minutes for two chicken breasts and a manager comes over to say she's sorry and to give me a free meal on my next visit. I don't need a free meal, I just need the meal I ordered in a timely manner. There must have been a management change because it's sloppy now. PS: the busser brings your food out after scratching his head and playing on his phone, do you know how many germs and feces phones have? He wiped his face and then used the same hands to prepare silverware without washing his hands... has the health Dept been here?

Mi caribe is a solid 4, but could be a solid 5 with the addition of more mexican style cuisine. In order to attract more college students you should add mexican components to your menu such as: chips & salsa, simple tacos, burrito, QUESO etc. I believe this will immensely increase your sales. Often I go to eat with my college friends and they don't know what to order. Still love this place!!!

A basket of plain or garlic naan for your table is included in the lunch buffet price. That is all you need to know, guys - garlic! The lunch buffet is $1 off with a coupon from their website. Lots of delicious options, including a good selection of vegetarian fare. Everything was well labelled, frequently refilled, and delicious. I was too stuffed to even attempt dessert. Compared to the other Indian buffet downtown, I slightly prefer this one. I think it has more options overall.

Best resturant in the Narberth. Great food. The atmosphere is terrrific whether you are sitting amoungst the fresh flowers inside, or watching the world go by outside. Pros- really fresh ingrediants, flavorful, sweet people, nice enough for a date night and casual enough to bring the kids. Cons- A little expensive and slow service.

I've been by this place many times before but I never trusted it because it was by seedy motels. But I checked out all of the positive Yelp reviews and we decided to check it out. When we first walked inside I was pleased by how quaint and cozy it was. The dining area is slightly larger than Syphay's. The food was really good, however. . .the portion of spicy beef curry was small while the bowl of Jasmine rice was huge. There was like four cups of rice, way too much for both of us. Too much rice and not enough meat. The chicken pad thai and Tom kha gai soup were also delicious. Despite the small portions, we really liked the food and service. Well definitely return in the future.

We saw our server twice the whole time we were there, to take our order and bring the check. We each started with a cocktail and would have liked to order more but she never came over to ask. We did see many other servers and managers, however, stoping by our table just to look at the outside customers. None of these employees asked us if we needed anything. My raw sushi was served on a very hot plate. My friend didn't get his dinner until a good 5 mins after mine was brought out (not that I felt safe eating mine anyway). Overall, we wish we just stayed in and ordered cheap Chinese food.

The one star in my review is specifically for terrible service and the awful entrée that my husband received. We had dinner with friends last night at Zorba's . Poor service started with the table they placed us at. We had made a reservation many weeks in advance. When we all arrived, we were directed toward two roundtables each for two people, stuck together to somehow create a table for four. Picture trying to sit at a figure 8. It was awkward and uncomfortable, and our friends' chairs were in the walkway where waiters and waitresses had to rush back and forth. My husband and I were crammed next to a table of five, who turned out to be the loudest diners I have ever sat near in a restaurant. We asked for another table but none was available. Our order was taken after a bit of a wait , and our appetizers arrived after not too long a wait. The appetizers were tasty. One hour after we received our appetizers, our entrées came. There was no apology for the delay with the entrées. The restaurant was jam-packed, and it looked to us as if the waitstaff and kitchen were overwhelmed. Three of us ordered the same thing, the octopus, which was tasty. My husband ordered the charbroiled mixed grill. It was actually inedible. Picture charred shoe leather warmed in the microwave. His vegetables were also awful, mushy and tasteless. My husband never ever sends food back to the kitchen. He should have sent this back but he did not. When the waitress came to clear our plates much later, instead of noticing that my husband still has 3/4 of his entrée on his plate, and asking if everything was all right, she whisked the plate away. My husband told me that was the worst entree he had ever received in any restaurant in his life. Between that inedible entrée and terrible service, one star for you , Zorba's.

Worst gyro I ever had. EVER. The tablespoon and a half of meat was chopped up like ground beef- WRONG! Two paper thin slices of tomato, a pinch it lettuce, teaspoon of fine crumbled feta and a ginormous pita. Essentially the pita was 70% of the gyro. First (and last) time there. And the owner should have know it since we used a coupon. And before anyone says I should have complained- I should NOT have to complain to be served decent food. Especially if I paid for it. (The coupon essentially covered the fountain drinks which is cost negligible)

This buffet is so good. I am not sure what people are referring to when they say their buffet is sub par. Every time I have been in for the buffet, the food has been plentiful, fresh, hot, and delicious. I have been in at various times, so those negative reviews are doubly confusing. The service is very friendly, and the price during the week is unbeatable. If you're looking for good Indian food in the area, try this place first!

Wonderful ambience and very nice place to have authentic South Indian food. I was at Nashville, from San Francisco, for an official visit and found this place in yelp while searching for Indian food. Menu was very tempting so decided to give it a try. I reached there around 4.30 PM but the place was closed. Looks like they close at 4 PM till 5 PM but Yelp showed this place is open all day till 9 PM. I called the phone number listed in Yelp. The owner attended my phone and I told him my story. He was a very nice guy and allowed me to dine in. I ordered chicken kothu paratha. It was so so good!. My god !!. After around 5 years I happened to taste the best chicken kothu paratha !. I was so full as the quantity was a lot (I think two people can eat one order). I talked to the owner, he was a very young guy and super friendly. Very satisfied with the food and so happy for visiting this place. A must try place if you crave for real authentic South Indian foods. Highly recommend.

I was told by a very close friend that we had been sleeping on a very good restaurant, Simply Thai, I had always seen this place but had never stop by, my jobs main office is very close by so Im in the area often. So I decided to give them a try to day for a change & man I am so happy I did! I had the spare ribs & the duck fried rice very good I really enjoyed it! I also got the Chile stir fry that i haven't tasted just yet I plan to take if for lunch tomorrow I will let you know how that was but this will not be my last visit I would love to try more Items from this menu.

I had my first Jamaican Jerk Hut experience while enjoying the PHS pop up garden on a Thursday around 6pm. After seeing it featured on Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives (odd that's what they picked to feature in Philly) we got excited to try it. We ordered from the window connected to the garden. Dining Partner ordered the jerk chicken wings, and I ordered the chicken leg platter with rice, plantains, and cabbage and a side of cornbread to share. It was expensive! $26 and we waited almost 25 minutes standing at the window for our food. There didn't seem to be a register in the back so every time someone gave the woman payment, she disappeared for a bit to bring back change. It seemed very inefficient. The chicken was very juicy and had quite a kick to it. Overall though, it was nothing special and not filling. Won't be back for more.
Prefer Indian Garden! Love Indian Gardens food and service! Indian Garden is just amazing and we love it! Been going for 7 years!

I absolutely LOVE Bui's. It's my go to place for breakfast and lunch, and I'm never disappointed. I always get the egg and cheese sandwich, which I know is very simple and plain, yet it's still so delicious. And it tastes even better with meat on it. I love how they have the option of wheat bread, as I prefer it over white bread. This is one of my favorite food trucks on campus. If you haven't tried it, you're seriously missing out.

Generations of Penn students have frequented this lunch trucks on weekend afternoons as a hangover cure for a reason: Bui's serves the best Sunday brunch grease-bombs hands-down. Whatever you order, make sure to get it with extra Bui's sauce.
It was alright. Very little rice and overall small plates. Naan tastes good.

Perhaps you have passed by this sumptuous restaurant because its outward appearance is so unassuming--but that would be a big mistake. This is a little gem of a thoroughly authentic Thai restaurant that fulfills all expectations in sushi, sushimi, and cooked cuisine. Everything I have tried has completely pleased my guest and I. The atmosphere is pleasant, the staff is the same. All the soups are outstanding and the seafood tastes as though it just came from the fishing dock. Next time I will try their curry dishes. The prices are more than fair as well. One not to miss on busy Seminole Blvd!

This place is excellent. The decor was nice especially w/ byob. There's a liquor store across the street. The food was amazing. The spice was enough for me to be hot but it could have been kicked up a notch so don't be scared of the 3 pepper meals if you like it spicy. Started with the Aaloo Aur Papri Chat. It was very fresh and a great light way to start off. I got Kadai Lamb which was 2 peppers spicy. It was a couple notches below too spicy but had great flavor. My fiance got the Chicken Vindaloo that she modified to 1 pepper spicy from 3 peppers. It was really good but not hot enough for me. We also went with the onion naan. That was freshly made. Tasted amazing. Overall the best Indian I've had in the area. Will be back.
Food is always amazing! Everyone there is very nice! I highly recommend that you try this place if you haven't already! The lula kebab is my absolute favorite!

***********100th Review********* For my 100th review I made sure to make it for someplace worth it and Zeppoli was all that. Of course it didn't hurt that in our dining party was our waiter Tommy's mother and uncle (who is fellow Yelper Lawrence K.) so a reservation was maybe a little easier for our night out. The restaurant itself is very small but dimly lit and romantic if I say so myself. We set up shop at a large table located in the front window. BYOB nuff said. With many bottles of Perseco and various whites and reds we came loaded for bear..I'm so glad I wasn't driving that night. After perusing the menu we decided our party of six would choose a few plates and let the chef fill out our order. For our first course we ordered the Antipasta Siciliano, Panzanella Catania and Finocchi Salsiccia. The chef sent out two of the specials. One I cannot remember but the second was a white anchovy in linguini which was a highlight of the first course along with the Antipasta. The second course we ordered the Tagliatelli al Limone, the Rigatoni alla Disgraztiata, and the Pesto Trapanse which was awesome. I believe there were a few more dishes but the night starts to get a little hazy after the first of four bottles of wine. All were fantastic and well enjoyed by the entire party. We still had room for the third course and went with the Bistecca Enna (cooked to perfection and melted in your mouth), Sicilian Seafood Stew (mmmmmm), and the Conigilio Spada alla Griglia (we should have ordered two of these). Perfectly flavored and all delicious. Since we went this far we had to have dessert right. Zeppoli Siciliano, Torta Cioccolato e Mandole, and a housemade Spicy Chocolate Gelati that was out of this world. Overall I have to say that this was one of the best meals that my lovely wife and I experienced in the last year. Excellent friendly service, food that was heavenly and good friends to share it with. I know I am looking forward to our next visit.

First visit. Came in for an early dinner. Not at all busy. Service was pleasant but minimal. The booth seat on the far wall felt awkwardly bumpy to sit in until I adjusted a little to the left. The food was okay. A little bland. I've had better. I feel the portions were lopsided. The huge pile of rice, which is the only reason I walked out there full. Right now, the rating is middle of the road... and only because I want to come back to try the lunch buffet. But not in any rush to make that happen.

The food was delicious, but I left hungry after spending a ton of money. Also, while their cocktails were refreshing, the juice to booze ratio seemed really off. Between two of us, we drank five cocktails and left without even a buzz which means they were probably skimping on the alcohol. I'll head over to Holland House instead next time.

A nice night out with a friend was sullied by a really horrible experience with the wait staff. We sat, ordered our drinks, were given menus, then literally once a minute a rotation of at least four different servers stopped by our table, asking if we were ready to order yet. We explained we were still looking, and that we would need a few more minutes, and as soon as that server would leave, another would appear. "Are you ready? What are you having? Why don't you know what you want yet?" Ten minutes of this was maddening, and finally we picked something just to get them to leave us alone for a bit. When we were seated, there were three other people in the restaurant. A two top, and a single person dining solo. So, while annoying I was just chalking it up to extremely over eager servers on an incredibly slow night. The food was the saving grace. I had the Amazing, which is a peanut sauce sauteed with shrimp and chicken served on steamed veggies, and the funny title of the dish didn't lie, it was pretty amazing. and a nicely balanced thai ice tea to wash it down. My friend ordered a noodle dish, the Spicy Noodle with chicken, and it came with basil & chili sauce stir-fried with rice noodles, chilies, basil leaves, scallions, bell peppers, onions, and mushrooms. The vegetables and chicken were nicely seasoned and just right on the heat. While we were eating our meal another table had come in, with 4 or 5 people, obviously friends of the people working there. All of the wait staff crowded around and they were shouting, laughing and being incredibly loud in a big group. As we were finishing, one of the women from this new table got up and came to ours, and started badgering us, telling us this was her friends place, they own it, they run it, and asking us if we liked it. It's good isn't it? Best place. How do you like it? What did you order? What did we think? Finally, I politely replied, that the food's good, but I'd like to finish this meal and our conversation uninterrupted. Then the bill came. We were both paying with a credit card and asked them if they could split the bill down the middle. They obliged, and when it came time to sign the receipts, I started signing "mine" and discovered they'd accidentally rang my friends card twice, and mine not at all, since her name and card number was printed on both receipts. She had already signed one, so I took the other to the counter, explained the error, and asked if they could void it and charge my card for it instead. They came to the table, got her receipt and disappeared for a few minutes. When they came back to the table they had voided the receipt she'd already signed, and made her sign the one I started signing by mistake. We asked why, and they said, and I quote, "she didn't leave a tip, she must leave tip, no tip not allowed." I tried explaining I was leaving the entire tip on my receipt since I'd ordered the thai iced tea and owed more on a bill we were splitting and they just kept yelling at her that she must leave a tip. I left a tip on my bill for the both of us, as planned, and we couldn't get out of there fast enough. I love locally-owned and operated restaurants, but I refuse to tolerate rude and demanding service, no matter how good the food is.
Great food! I eat take out and at restaurant and its good always either way. Great choice also. Try it you will agree!

This place opened for a few months now before summer. I'm surprised no one reviewed this place yet! When I came here, I never had African dishes so I asked for recommendations from our server. We were clueless af, but she got our backs. I got dry rice and fried fish, but I forgot the actual name of the dish, unfortunately. My boyfriend got lamb over dry rice. The proportions of the food are hugeeeeee!! It fed me for another three days. The lamb was delicious! The meat was tender and soft with enough fat left on it for some flavoring. The fish had lots of meat in it, so I didn't really have to worry about eating all bones. The rice was seasoned very well. Overall, I'd come back to try other dishes for sure.

Zorba's is the perfect dinner destination on a cold winter night - the decor is very cozy and homey, and the authentic Greek food is warm and comforting. I had the stuffed eggplant, which was stuffed with grains and veggies and topped with a tomato sauce and feta. It was delicious, and the perfect portion size (and very reasonably priced at $10). Our waitress was great, and after my friend asked about the portion size of a dish (and ultimately ordered a different one), the waitress came over to show us the dish when another patron ordered it. I really appreciated her thoughtfulness, and it definitely made us want to go back (both for the service and to try the dish!).

I'm only giving two stars because I didn't have pho. I heard from a person at work that this place was the bomb, so I decided to do some take out. The lady that was taking the orders was pretty disinterested in my questions which left me a bit confused. After a while pondering the menu, I ordered vegetable fried rice and chicken chow mein. Both items were OK, but nothing to write home about. The vegetable fried rice was more vegetable than rice and the chow mien had large hunks of vegetables in it, yielding little noodles. I'm not a real fan, but maybe it's my tastes.

Outstanding in every way. Kristen was extremely attentive and all the staff as well. Food outstanding and they brought me a sample of the red shrimp dish, all I can say if that for this So Cal girl used to shrimp, it was one of the best ever. Since I can get that at home I opted for the Porkchop arguably the biggest one you've ever seen so it would require 2 to 3 appetites. Again another outstanding dish. Truly everything including vegetables potatoes salad was five star. And then to top it off They had a classic guitarist who entertained the entire time. As a single female traveler it was an awesome experience
This place, as are most Indian restaurants are, is amazing! Thank you for providing a clean and delicious family friendly environment for us to enjoy! Great service! Soo delicious!

this is a great place to hang out with friends (on one of their 'comfy' couches) or study (at one of their scattered tables). they make good sandwiches and serve la colombe coffee. play $3 for an ice coffee (after tipping) is a bit much for me, but if i am going to sit here for a couple of hours, it is totally worth it.
The food here is simply amazing. It is not spicy like Indian food, and they have several vegetarian specialties which is great.

Awesome meal and experience. Started off with a delayed seating, but our server was very apologetic and brought some apps. Changed the whole mood. She was very customer focused. Food was amazing! Whipped feta is of the charts!! Awesome server, ask for Olivia.

i just moved to STL and was looking on yelp for places by my house and a saw this place on yelp that had pretty good reviews so I thought i would give it a shoot. It is a small Indian restaurant that seams like it probably does more takeout then eat in service they only had 5-7 tables. I eat in as that was my plan the waiter I think also the owner (it's a mom and pop type restaurant) was very nice the my food came out relatively fast and it was amazing for the price my meal was lamb tikka masala and it was only about $11. and it was good. i have had better indian food once but it was at a fancy restaurant and like 25-30 buck. This was a close second and only $11. The only reason i did not give it 5 stars is the portion size was a little small they served me enough to get full but if I had wanted to stuff myself i would have had to order more. I highly recommend this place it's a great little mom and pop Indian restaurant.
The food was amazing! It was my first time ever eating there. My favorite dish was the chicken and the lamb. You eat everything with your hands, and sit around a soft couch like seat. BYOB too!

Very friendly staff. Now onto the food. I did not enjoy the curry at all (green curry with tofu), there was little to no hint of coconut, basically it was a salty green soup. The salt itself overpowered the spice and all vegetables in the curry. The tofu itself had not soaked in the full salt, thankfully, but nor did it any of the fragrant full bodied flavor a curry should have. A firmer tofu would have been recommended as well to make this dish heartier. Friend had the curry noodle and it looked like a platter of minestrone soup with tidbits of noodles. He mentioned flavor was alright. I won't be back again and have given up hope on finding a decent Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara to satiate my cravings. Perhaps the other dishes are tastier but since I will always by default order a curry to start off, it's a dish that the restaurant has to get right.

I'm a loyal Yelper, but have never felt impressed enough at a restaurant to write a review until tonight. I was blown away by the service we received - our server was extremely knowledgeable and handled all our questions about the menu with thorough and detailed answers, very friendly!! The managers were out in the open, carefully surveying the entire dinner service, visiting tables, and making sure every guest was satisfied. They were unbelievably attentive - Our food took a little while to arrive, and both the manager and server apologized, and even removed our appetizer from our bill !! The food was exceptionally tasty - the new jicama crab cakes were delicate and packed full of flavor. The chile relleno with shrimp was delicious (Although it would have been even better accompanied with a side of rice, crostini, or bread to soak up all the extra yummy sauce!) I will DEFINITELY be returning to Delicia - I'm super impressed with the quality of food and exceptional service.

Staff was amazing. They were so friendly and actually took the time out to make sure we understood the menu and they let us try different things. The lamb was so delicious. The only thing that didn't like was the acheke which was very dry and hard other then that it was pretty good

Yay! I was so excited to search for Greek food in Metairie and find out that an Albasha had opened here :) I love the Baton Rouge, Hammond, and Covington restaurants. I got my usual meat plate and it was just as great and tasty as the one I usually get at the other locations. I also highly recommend the fried cheese as an appetizer. If you are seeking out good Greek food in Metairie, definitely check out Albasha :)

I ate here for the first time tonight with my sister, and I have to say, it might be one of the BEST greek restaurants I've ever eaten at! The gyro was amazing! All the appetizers were so good! They have a ton of candy you can't find anywhere and Omg the dessert! I will definitely be going back!

The food was ok. You can find better food in may places. But the service was terrible. We were seated to the table right away. After that lady just took the order and the short guy put the food on the table. That was it!!! That was the last time they gave us what they might call service. There were 4 of us. They gave us 2 water. I had to ask him for water for my son. Asked for small bowls to share the food for 4 persons, got only one bowl. I had to ask him twice. I let him know that there was no spoon in the container on the table. He told me "I know!" And walk away without even look at me. That was the only word i heard from him in 40 minutes. We sat in there about 40 minutes, they did nothing except took order and put food on table. That's it. Nothing else. Never check up, never ask how is the food. It was how they treat their customers. I just got one question, why they bother work as servers, instead they should do the dish or something else they happy to do.
Open late, food quality is a bit lacking. None of the entrees really stood out. Prices are pretty high for what 'cha get. Not a repeat.
Our first visit at the new Clearwater location and everything was perfect. The Mexican roll was delicious and the Tamago and Unagi were the best we've ever had...

We have eaten here several times and enjoyed it every time. My favorite is the hummus; I always order some to take home. I am a huge fan of thelentil bisque with and order of falafel. My husband usually orders the duo so we can have a sampling of everything. The furnishings are not very comfortable, so we usually do take out. It is a little pricey, but it beats the greasy stuff you get at less expensive places so it's worth it to us.

interesting flavors, not what i'm used to at all, but good for sure! portions for take out were a little on the small side as i almost at two and i'm 135lbs soaking wet. looking for more thai to compare to in st louis, but this one's on the win list!

Enjoy the coffee, vibe, and friendly service, regularly. Need to try some of the food specialties. Nice selection of pastries. Hope they bring the coffee club back. Love being able to bring dog in while ordering.

I've been here 2x, once with a group and once for an anniversary dinner. The food was pretty good, we mainly just wanted somewhere that was BYO. The reason why I only give them 2 stars is because of the atrocious wait staff. The first time I was there we had such a hard time flagging down our waiter for anything but assumed it was because they were somewhat busy (only about 60% full). The food also took forever!! The second time I went back with my boyfriend the food also took over 35 mins (and it was a monday night!). After we were finished eating I repeatedly asked for the dessert menu from 3 DIFFERENT WAITERS and yet none of them brought it! Finally after 25 mins of waiting for it our waiter just brought us the check! Incredibly rude and inefficient. The food is good and the place looks cute, but not worth it.

Sadly we have been walking by for 2 years, each time saying " we need to go! We live a block away!" Finally we did this evening. Shame on us!! Food was fantastic- spices were simply amazing! Service was perfect- they obviously understand the delicate balance between allowing the diner to enjoy their meal while never waiting to ask for extra xyz. We even ordered dessert which we typically don't order but cardamom pudding (excellent). Go- I don't believe you will be disappointed! Ps- byob and discount with cash pay

I came to Ariana with a bunch of friends and I am sorry to say I will never come back. The staff was in attentive, slow and un-accommodating. There was no one on the floor most of the evening, and another couple left after 20 minutes since no one greeted them. One of the two hookahs we ordered didn't work, and we had to flag down the waiter for drinks, food menus, and anytime we wanted to order anything. It was as if they didn't want our business or money. I will say the food was delicious, but serving sizes were small and definitely not worth the abysmal service we received.
I travel the world and eat at a lot of places and this place has the best Indian food I've ever had!
Just amazing. Much closer than Philly for my Pho fix and way better. Tried a variety of items from the menu and everything has been top-notch. Can get jammed. BYOB too :) If you haven't, you should .

My second time picking up to-go order. Foods were good especially the KFC spicy wings. The bartender however was always rude. I don't know if being Asian has anything to do with. The reason I say that because the first time there was a Caucasian person picking up the order ahead of me and she was courteous to him. When it came to me the smile and politeness were gone. This time I walked to the bar towards the right end and asked for my order. She said, "your order is at the end of the bar" (the left end). So I followed her then she placed my order on the counter and gave me my bill. While she rang me up she made jokes with the couple (Caucasian) on my left. Then when she handed me the receipt there was no thank you or anything. I shouldn't have tipped her but I did. All she did was handed me my damn food and I gave her money for it. I never understood why sometimes servers/bartenders get upset when they don't get a tip. If you don't provide service then don't have the nerve to ask for a tip. Overall, good food, just don't sit at the bar if you're Asian.

Not bad. Not in a rush to go home, so as this was conveniently located 2 doors away from the Patco train stop, it was easy to pop in here for dinner one night. There is a very small buffet, with perhaps 6 or 7 different offerings. You load up your take-away container and it is weighed and you pay by the pound. They offer free water if you are not in the mood to buy a drink. Pricewise, it was perfect because I was hungry but not too hungry, so I paid under $10 for my plate. Tastewise, it was AOK. Nothing too spectacular, but tasty enough for whatever 3 or 4 dishes I lumped together. Tiny storefront with seating for about 20 people max. Sat by the windows for entertaining people-watching.
It's our favorite restaurant. Delicious Vietnamese foods, there're other Asian food such as Chinese and Thai foods in the restaurant too. Plus bubble tea. We go there often.

Had a great meal last night at Yah Mom...The staff is friendly, the service excellent the favors beautiful and the food fantastic. I will go again next time I'm in Tampa. I almost missed going in though for I thought it was closed from the outside because the entrance is on the back side of the building. I don't know what they can do but it would make a big difference if it looked open when driving by. Thank god for the positive yelp review for I might have missed this gem of a restaurant.

Very finest food quality and price. Lilly is a fantastic and caring host. Portions are grand and the veggies are as just picked from the garden. The Pho is a well executed delight. I have never had a better overall feeling about a meal. Lilly is always there and asking if the food is what you wanted. I keep coming back. Real comfort food.
Hidden gem! The curry and appetizer platter wonderful....the atmosphere nice for a plaza setting..wonderful service...will return..
A really nice healthy meal reasonably priced I would definitely come back again the staff are extremely friendly and they have free Wi-Fi

Wow. This review will come in stages. We just finished appetizers and they were so good that I had tonstop and write about them. The Sopes de Pato were a play on richness and spice. The Ceviches were executed perfectly. Service , bybthe way is excellent. This is the first time in a.long time, that I have had a good server on a Sunday in Indianapolis

Saigon restaurant is a top notch Vietnamese restaurant. It is a nice size place that is clean with a fairly plain décor. However, what it lacks in looks it makes up for in excellent quality food. I have eaten here several times and will detail some of my best meals. I am not an appetizer person. I usually believe that it is a waste of money to order appetizers that are nothing more than frozen food that restaurants drop in a fryer and charge you $7.99 for what you could make at home for $1.50. I don't throw my money away on average or below average appetizers to make myself feel good like we are trained to do by TV commercials. I reward restaurants with my hard earned dollars when they produce something that is worth ordering. I reward Saigon with $11 for an appetizer every time I go because they will produce something that is worthy of my money. If you order nothing else get the #16 Saigon Sampler platter. It is so awesome. It has the following items: egg roll, spring roll, crab Rangoon, dumpling, rocket shrimp, grilled beef lemongrass and grilled pork spring roll. The best thing is the grilled beef lemongrass. This is one of most flavorful things I have ever had. On to the main courses: 1. My new favorite that I just had last week is the #107 Saigon Grilled Platter. It is so good. You use rice paper to make your own spring rolls. There are three types of meat, vegies, fresh herbs and a couple types of noodles. It will be hard to not order this over and over again. At this time this is my number one highly recommended dish for this restaurant. If you have a big appetite like I do, you will not leave disappointed or hungry. 2. The #52 is my favorite Pho. I am sure they are all great. The broth is full of flavors that just dance on your taste buds and the fresh vegies and herbs just add to the enjoyment of the dish. This is also an excellent choice. 3. My third favorite is #101 is a stir fried noodles with meat and seafood. This was excellent. All of their seafood is high quality and fresh tasting. I went here for lunch one day and enjoyed the cheaper option of lunch specials. While this was good, I would rather just pay more and really enjoy myself. If this was near my work. I would spend $15 once a week for lunch to get my #107 as it is really worth the price. If you are bored of chain restaurants and think for yourself and are not manipulated by millions of dollars in TV commercials to make yourself believe you have to eat average to below average overpriced food at some chain restaurant, I am one of you. Let's all keep supporting the true food scene in Indiana.
Fantasic restaurant. The eggplant is the best I've ever had, and the mint tea just doesn't get any better in the US.

I travel weekly for work and have eaten at many a Taziki's across the South. I've never been disappointed. I have to give credit though to the Mt Juliet Taziki's for the best salmon cooked in the entire franchise. I had the Mediterranean Salad with the grilled salmon on top and it was absolutely delicious. I'm used to getting it slightly overdone and even a little to raw for my taste. The entire meal was the highlight of my experience eating with these establishments (and I started at the original in the Colonnade in Bhm). Great job! I will be sure to stop in on my next trip through. Oh for credit to the cook, June 6th 2:56 PM.

The fact that Harleysville now has a legitimate Indian restaurant to accompany the myriad of middling pizza shops and marginal Chinese joints makes me happy. I love Indian food and it's rare to find one that's truly good. To be honest, we have only got takeout once from Aman's, but it was delicious. The tandoori chicken was tender and full of flavor. It was a tad spicy for my wife, but I liked it a lot. My dish was a biryani and it was awesome. They made it nice and spicy, but the flavor still came through. The only ding I have is the naan, it's more of a chip than a flatbread. The flatbread stuff is what I have had in the past and prefer. No big deal here. We've only had a small portion of the menu as well, so there's plenty more to try. I'm willing to bet we won't be disappointed. I'm by no means a culinary expert or someone who demands authenticity of international cuisine. If it tastes good, I'm down with it. That's exactly why I like this place already.

Great pho! The lilly rolls and crab rangoon were not impressive, though. Fast service and turnaround. A real happening spot with a very non-pretentious outdoor facade. It's easy to miss, when first entering the cluster of Magazine Street storefronts and restaurants from the direction of Downtown NOLA. Overall, one of the best and freshest phos that I have had in the NOLA area.

Omg!! Everything is over priced! $10.00 for a "LARGE" bowl of pho that my skinny 7 yr old son finished.. Dont mention the creepy young emo guy who takes your order. This will be my first and only visit to this place.

Best Indian food in the Nashville area, and we have tried all of them. Service is disorganized, not enough wait staff, but the food makes up for it. Samosas and chutney are excellent. Butter chicken and chicken korma are excellent.
There are many Indian restaurants in the area but Guru's is by far the best!

Great food. Introduced to Barwarchi takeout several nights ago while working late. Colleagues ordered a variety of dishes and we had a wonderful buffet in the office. Care was taken by Barwarchi staff in the packing the food in the takeout containers. Taste, spice level and fragrance was amazing. Ready to stay late in the office again for more late evening Barwarchi food!

I have been coming here for years ( at least 10 I believe ) and have really never been disappointed. Yes things have gotten quite expensive but the food quality has never gone down in my opinion and the entertainment has stayed consistently awesome ! I have had many good times here and ALWAYS recommend the 7 entree 25$ option. How can someone go wrong with that ?!???
Food is great and fresh. The owners and staff are awesome ! I recommend Thai 5 to anyone that loves Thai food.

Having gone to India twice I can say that Tandoor India is on par with typical Indian cuisine. I am fiercely partial to the lunch time and dinner time buffet options. The selections for the meat eater include goat and chicken. I am particularly impressed with the meatless options that I had to choose from ever since becoming vegetarian. Available during my visit were chick peas, hot spinach dishes, steamed cabbage, vegetables fritters all very very tasty. The staff is present attentive and well mannered but not intrusive and pushy. I like the traditional Indian music that plays from the PA system. The current decor consists of framed currency from all over the world. It's spacious enough that I have had several staff in-service meetings here but have also come here alone to feel as if I am transported to India for the length of my low lit flavorful meal and you can comfortably and not be rushed to leave. This would be an ideal place to bring a date because the food is great and you will not feel crowded or overloaded with the modern day dining added amenities like a booming drowning television. -BUFFET- When you arrive and are seated just know that you then have to get up, get a plate and serve yourself. When you are done with your food leave your plate on your table, remove your eating utensils, and get up to get more food and your used plate will be removed by the staff. The buffet is around $9.00 until 4:00pm and $11.00 after. Shafi, the manager has always been good with me and aims to please his customers. If this place ever renovates I hope it does not lose its attention to service that keeps so many people coming back for seconds.
Food is delicious and fresh. Beef gyro and falafel are fantastic and the homemade baklava is out of this world. ... and the prices are super reasonable. Super nice owner and staff!!

Never been to an Asian restaurant of any type which specializes in stir fried meats and veggies where I could not smell Asian food cooking. Ordered sweet and sour chicken that came out cold with chicken that appeared to be from a can. Plus the manager insulted me by stating I did not know the difference in Thai and Chinese in spite of the fact I've dined here and other Thai restaurants numerous times. What's more the manager refused to take the dish back-charging me for something I did not eat! This used to be a good restaurant with really fresh and seasoned food...not anymore.

This is my favorite Moroccan spot in Philadelphia. It's clean and very nice. Sometimes parking can be difficult but never too bad. The staff is friend and man men. Not man speak complete English but they can understand you. This place is excellent for groups and just couples. My recent visit was with my boyfriend. We had the Fez feast. It's $30 pp and comes with a few dishes which is fulfilling but I would've love to have more chicken and a half chicken could feed one person especially if both don't eat all meats served. We had the lemon chicken and I was so delicious, full of flavor. The lamb was tender and good. I enjoyed this other dish which had chicken and scrambled eggs inside a warm dough with sugar. The mint tea is good and was included. This is a good spot to relax mingle and smoke hookah. I would recommend to anyone who wants to try something different. Since I've been to Morocco I would say this is very authentic!! Go, have fun and enjoy yourself!! No drama just a good time!! Food is goo! Excellent service.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Enjoyed a fantastic chicken tikka masala here the other night and just couldn't have enjoyed it more. I was promptly greeted and felt welcomed immediately. While I was being seated I was told that it was a family place and that everything is made from scratch and without additives for color, etc. I have to admit some of this made me think they may be overcompensating for quality with their back story....I was wrong...the food was terrific and the people fantastic. The atmosphere was every bit as welcoming as the employees/family. It's always an interesting discussion trying to get the spice levels right when you can "customize" that and my server was very helpful and funny as we dialed it in...and the spice level was exactly what I needed...hot, but I didn't die! I had the opportunity to chat with the owners for a while as well and what a lovely couple they are! I truly enjoyed hearing of how they came from Pakistan to Boise and their bit of history in town. It almost felt as if I was welcomed into their home. I had a concert to get to that night, but if I hadn't I would have definitely stayed and chatted more. The location, upstairs, was a bit hard to find, but when I really looked it was actually quite easy. Do yourself a favor and check them out...I doubt you will be disappointed.

I'm a vegetarian. I get their veggie burger and this burger is so good, non-vegetarians have recommended it to me.. Try it before judging it! Just wish they had more vegetarian options-Fridays they have veggie curries but it tastes just like the curries you get at lemon grass.. Etc. I've also had their Thai tea which is a bit too milky for me but it's also really good. And to top it off, they're very friendly and they're Drexel alumni!

Delicious food here! Cheerful staff. I ordered a vermicelli bowl with pork (not sure what the official name is) and it was delicious! Also got some spring rolls and they were good too! Tasted one of the other dishes someone ordered (it was lemon chicken with crunchy noodles or something!) Really nice flavor but if you aren't used to those noodles you might not be a huge fan of them. They're kinda leathery textured when they get wet! Great prices here!

I stopped by on my way back to Orlando after a hair appointment. I couldn't decide between the crab fried rice or the drunken noodle with beef. Both were excellent and have lasted me all weekend! I ate an order of fresh spring rolls on my drive home and woo! Some of the best I've had. Would definitely come back to try more. Wish they were here in the Orlando area.

Outstanding South Indian food. Not at all fancy and very little seating inside although we've never had a problem when we go there for dinner. My sense is that many people do takeout. Try the delicious dosa which are hard to find in the suburbs. The food is halal and also great for those who are vegetarians and gluten-free. Friendly service.

We came across this place in the "dine and dial" catalog and thought it sounded interesting! Even though it is located in a weird spot and is quite small, the food is fantastic. Parkallen serves traditional Lebanese food, with a large menu and a huge pizza menu! The food is fresh and delicious. This is definitely one of those "do not judge a book by it's cover" places. It's wonderful.
