The reviews stating that the portion sizes are too small are very confusing. I ordered the salmon plate and my husband the duo plate for dinner tonight and we both struggled to finish. The food was wonderful and staff was very friendly!

I don't usually write reviews, but I personally have to recommend this place to everyone. Owners are very kindly and it's really awesome that it is open kitchen. I had this particular food called Nam Prik Ong and Khao Soi and it was really tasty. I ate a lot of Thai foods before, but I can confidentially say that it is the most authentic Thai restaurant I had so far. Lastly but not least, the way they give out sticky rice is cool! Comes in a little box :) also tasty.

I first tried samples of the food from Salsa at the Yelp Evolution event at the Adventure Science Center. I was sooooo excited to hear there's a new Puerto Rican restaurant in town and had to visit the first chance I got. We went yesterday for lunch and were not disappointed! The food is authentic and, frankly, I'm stoked to find a place that serves mofongo! I would give Salsa 5 stars, but the prices are a little high for the portions.

I would give a zero if I could. When you go through a drive thru, you expect quick service. I've been asked to pull forward to get out of the window. It's been 10 minutes and I still have no food. The employee at the window was extremely rude and disrespectful. Lots of eye rolling and disrespectful. Extremely poor customer service all the way around. Didn't want to give us water. 17 minutes later we have food. We won't be back.
Bumping these guys to 5 stars from my previous review of 4 stars. The food has been outstanding this past year. They just keep getting better.

Wonderful! Looks can be deceiving from the outside, but this place is beautiful inside. The food was delicious. We started with some of the best spribg thai rolls I've had, and then had a pumpkin curry chicken entrée and a green chicken curry entrée. Both were fabulous. I would highly recommend the pumpkin curry. The green curry tasted exactly like the thai curry cashews at trader joes. We will definitely visit again!

My Daughters favorite place in St Pete. We eat there about once a week. The food is great, The staff is unique and friendly, they all pretty much know what our order is when we walk in the door. You can grab a cold beer if you want. Not the absolute cleanest place to be honest but not bad either. The food is great for the price.

At the suggestion of others, I did take out. Unfortunately I did so near close and the meal suffered because of it. I was greeted when I walked in by a very sweet woman who seemed to be working alone, so forgive if service lacks, it seems like a family business. I ordered the Doro wat and queen's 8 sampler. While the Doro was as delicious as my Ethiopian uncle makes, the meat in the sampler was extremely dry, clearly it had been cooking too long. With that in mind this place gets 4 stars (I will revise after my next visit. Yes I will definitely be back. The Doro was delicious and cooked perfectly. The spices perfect, even though I am used to it being much hotter, I'll be sure to ask for more next time.

Traditional style Japanese restaurant that's my fav in the bay area. Love that you can sit on tatami mats or tables. Waiters/waitresses wear kimonos and their green tea is excellent :) My fav appetizer is the Agedashidofu!!!! I coudl order it 10million times and never get sick of it. mMmm! Sushi is the best around and prices arne't terribly bad. Salmon teriyaki is really good too. I love JotoS!

I went to Marrakesh with a group (9 of us total, including Gracie B who reviewed below) and we had a great time. Definitely great for groups. We chose it because we were told they would be able to accomodate our vegetarian friend, and it fit into everyone's budget. Heed the other reviewer regarding the directions. And if you drive a big SUV with a navigation system, don't drive down the alley to get to the restaurant - it's ridiculously narrow. OH, and if you also have parking assistance, you'll find your car beeping at you madly while you're scared half to death that you're going to take off the sideview mirrors of several parked cars. ;-) Once we made it to the restaurant (unscathed), though, the food was great. I mean, it was great for Moroccan, which I'd never had before so really have nothing to compare it to. They did a GREAT job with our veggie friend's courses, creating special things just for her (not just giving her more cous cous or something.) My only complaint would be that there's basically no selection for wine. Your choices are red or white, who knows what brand, and the white I had wasn't very good. If you care about wine (and are dining with others who share that opinion) it might be worth it to call ahead and ask about BYO.

I have been going to this place for about six months now. I have finally had it with the amateur, cold, rude counter help. The service absolutely sucks. The seating is not very comfortable and not laid out well. Parking lot in front in Fred Meyers is a real cluster as well. Taking your life into your own hands just trying to walk across it with the crappy way the traffic patterns are laid out., With so many other great Pho places in Boise why waste another minute or any more of your hard earned money at this place.

Was in the area craving a shawarma so I rolled the dice and checked this place out. I ordered the chicken shawarma plate. The meal came with hummus, salad, rice and pita. The meat was seasoned very nicely and the food was delicious. Only being able to stop by once on a fluke I wish I'd had time to explore the menu more but it was a nice meal that really hit the spot.

The veg offerings are remarkably few... whatever options I've seen in other reviews are not offered anymore. After a long conversation I found something I could eat, and it was palatable, but it's not a happy place to go if you don't eat meat.

Got carryout. Prices are much better in restaurant than through Total Takeout (price per dish plus no delivery fee or tip; you'll save at least $2 per dish). Food was ready at promised time. Pad Thai was slightly above average. Lava Tempura and Crab Rangoon were excellent. Garlic Pepper Chicken was awesome. I would go back.

I was staying in a hotel for an extended period of time in Conhohocken and not thrilled with my selection of restaurants in the area. Then I found Ekta, the closest reputable Indian place on yelp. I was blown away with how amazing the food was. I did takeout both times and the first time I accidentally ordered from the wrong location as I went to the other to pick it up. They were very nice about it and put a rush on making my order. I only had to wait less than 10 minutes. The food itself is outstanding. I think one time I ordered a channa masala-like dish and the other time I tried something I had never had before. I definitely will be going back soon.

Ermagahd. So good. The buttermilk chicken strips that are boneless are pretty salty. B But the mac and cheese is hands down some of the best Ive had in my life. Four chicken strips and mac and cheese was filling and not coma-inducing. They're really fast for take out, and the staff are super knowledgeable about what pairs well with what, offering great suggestions. Now if only there was ketchup...

I have only eaten there today for lunch and it was really good with a nice staff. I cant give it a 5 because the one visit but it is a must try for dinner. The crispy duck sounds great. chicken and vegetables an easy 4 eggroll a 5 fried rice a 4 miso soup 3 soup krispies 4

I've been meaning to get here since I saw that they were coming to West End. I finally did last week and was very impressed. Very nice space, good vibe, friendly and efficient service, and delicious food. I had the Greek grilled chicken salad and my friend had the gyro. We both thought the presentation was very nice, and the food tasted very fresh. I will be back!

I was really hungry when I got there, so I decided to order 2 dishes which were Gang Tai Pla (traditional Southern food) and CK padthai. Both tasted really good to me especially Gang Tai Pla. Love this place!!!!
This buffet leaves a lot to be desired. I find that if you order off of the menu, you will have a much better experience.
Our favorite Shawarma place. Awesome Owner. Always Fresh! Fries are Great too, very good seasoning, but not sure if it's suppose to be soft. I think if they were more Crispy, it would be even better.

Excellent food! Very nice and clean place. The staff were great, the prices and portion sizes were very good compared to other Thai and Asian restaurants I have been to. The Green Curry and Pad Thai were delicious! This will be my new spot for Asian food!

From out of town, looking for good Thai food near my hotel and settled on Numchock Wilai. Wow! From Seattle, I am aware of what good Thai food tastes like. And this place is great. Fresh, great flavors, all of it. It's not much to look at from the outside, but your taste buds will thank you if you go and sit down (or to go I guess!).
Mimosa was good for only $5. The Korean Fried chicken is worth the trip to try. Definitely recommend a place for a different type of fried chicken

Friday night, giving my out of town friends a tour of downtown. We passed by Tryst walking down Beach Dr. There was such a huge crowd of people outside and what looked like a line going in. Is this place a club? It sure sounded like one w/ the thumping music. We ended up coming back because they wanted to check it out. We walked in and ok, so it's not a club. The bar was crowded, like people were lined up elbow to elbow. All of the tables had reserved signs on them, but I asked the host if we could sit and he promptly seated us at a table inside, even though I told him we were not ordering food. Sweet! Someone came by to get our drink order as soon as we sat down. I ordered the Tryst, which was good. Not too overly sweet. Only complaint about this place was the volume of the music. It was LOUD. Like, we had to yell at each other to have a conversation or to order our drinks. Service was great, we were checked on often. She even gave us 25% off our drink tab for their service industry discount. Awesome deal, and I believe she said this is every night at Tryst. Food menu looked interesting, will have to try next time. Overall, we had a good time here and it was a great way to end our night out.
Pretty good kafta, babaganoush, and maneesh w. Zaatar. Nice to have somewhere local serving good food !

Calling all foodies! This amazing eatery is definitely worth it. I know when I find a jewel of a foodie restaurant and this is one of them. I was so excited that I found it so quickly on Yelp and it actually surpassed my expectations. It was exactly what I was looking for in a lunch spot although I think it would be an even better dinner spot. We were told that the whipped feta dip is out of this world so we had to order it. I must say it's a very unique appetizer and I haven't found anything like it anywhere else. I am not even a huge fan of feta cheese so I wouldn't have ordered this in most situations but the server convinced us that we had to. The combination of flavors - feta, honey and cracked pepper - mixed with the warm pita bread definitely surprised me with how good it is. The fire roasted carrots sounded so intriguing that we also ordered that dish and it is just too hard to explain in words but amazing. My boyfriend and I also split the crispy avocado rice bowl with shawarma spiced chicken thigh on top and once again I can't even begin to describe the combination of flavors that you will experience with this dish. It's obvious that I recommend this place so please try it and share several dishes if you can.

I was in Indy on business and took to Yelp looking for some dinner ideas beyond the downtown places I usually frequent near the Westin. I ended up at Delicia and was very happy I did. Service from Brent the bartender was perfect. friendly and talkative but not intrusive. gave good personal menu recommendations. he was a great ambassador for the place. as for the food...the amuse bouche of the Dominican "welcoming stew" was awesome! still not sure what was in it but boy was it tasty. some guacamole was also good. not over seasoned and with some big chunks of avocado. on Brent's and another bartenders recommendation I got the scallops and they were also very good. wrapped in Serrano ham and served on top of a sweet potato mash and with roasted veg. my only complaint was i think the veg was cooked earlier and held so they were a touch dry. I threw caution and my diet to the wind and got the churros for dessert. simple, perfectly fried and with a nice chocolate dipping sauce. next time the pork or snapper Veracruz I think. there will be a next time for sure.

Me and my wife used to go to this place quite often(2+ times/week) few years back for their different types of kabobs and their good menu. The food was decent and the Manager nice. It all stopped when we took their coupon from that current year's entertainment guide and they said they don't accept it knowing pretty well we are frequent visitors and the coupon was actually printed in that guide! After some discussion, they said they will accept it and when they brought the bill, the prices of our items were all jacked up to compensate for the coupon! Not sure how they could shamelessly do it since the actual prices were clearly listed in the menu! It's been 4 years since this happened and we never went back. 10 years back they could have gotten away with it, but there is no dearth of good Indian restaurants in the Western Suburbs. Horrible customer service. And don't let anyone tell you this was done by the old management. It was the new management-old management was worse than this!!

I love it. My girlfriend and I wet there for a early afternoon bite to eat and sure are glad we did! The decor is great, tons of natural light good tunes, very friendly and attractive staff and surrounded by some pretty hip foodies. (i believe other chefs from the area) I'd love to come back here in the spring and try out the patio. I drank a Corpse Reviver #2 cocktail and it was on point. It might as well have come straight from The Varnish in LA! I ate the spicy gravy and toast and couldn't believe how good it was.

I was finally able to make it over to Singha last night for dinner. I had heard it was a good place to go for lunch from some co-workers. We had both kinds of spring rolls and they were both pretty great. I had the shrimp pad thai and it was pretty good. A decent place to go when you want something different. And a great local option for Thai food.

It's good food. Maybe not original Thai but it is good. I saw that someone says its not flavorful. I call BS. I always ask them to make my food Thai spicy which is something you have to do at most Thai restaurants anyways because most Thai restaurants try to cater to Americans that don't have the spicy taste bud. I don't know about them having the best Pad Thai though. Growing up on Thai food this place does have a Thai flavor.
Authentic. Friendly staff. Delicious fresh food. Green curry is exceptional. So is Pad Thai! Excellent experience every time I go! Which is atleast once a week!

Awesome Thai BYOB spot in downtown Narbeth. They have some cute outdoor seating and are dog-friendly. The staff is super attentive and nice. Food here has all the Thai staples, but the best are their daily specials --- broad noodle pad thai, crab fried rice, fish curries. Unfortunately its the only ethnic restuarant in Downtown Narbeth, but this place is awesome and BYOB (there is a liquor store and beer shop nearby).

Let's get this out of the way: This place looks like a total dive from the outside. The type of place I try to avoid eating food from. However.... They serve up some AMAZING food. Any amount of apprehension you might have dissolves the second you walk thorough the front door and are a greeted by the smiling, friendly staff and the smell of delicious grilled meats and spices. I usually order the chicken kabob which is perfectly spiced, charred to perfection and served over a bed of fragrant rice. It is accompanied by a side salad (get the "cucumber salad" if it's available) and a slice of fresh afgan bread that is baked fresh in-house throughout the day. A (somewhat) healthy, filling, quick, consistent and satisfying lunch for about 8 bucks. If it's cold out, give the Chalaw Kadu (pumpkin stew) a shot. The perfect thing to warm you up on the coldest of days. Slightly sweet, slightly savory tender chunks of pumpkin served over rice and topped with a dollop of yogurt sauce. Different and delicious.

Big in flavor but small to medium portions. But you'll forget about the size of the dishes once you start eating. The desert is just OK. I would skip out on desert and just order another appetizer or dish. Go here!

Sometimes I get a little nihilstic about reviewing places like Delicia. Like, does anyone care what the 327th reviewer has to say about a very well-established, well-loved 4 1/2 star restaurant? Probably not, but I'm going to give it a shot regardless. I came here (finally!!!) for brunch with a large group of friends. Delicia doesn't take reservations, or at least not for brunch, so you have to be prepared to wait. In our case, it only took about 10-15 minutes before we were seated. The service was spot-on, especially considering our large group. The food was outstanding. I tried samples of several dishes, and don't think I would have been disappointed in very much on the menu. The food is rich, so the smaller than average (and by average I mean oversized American) portions are actually perfect. So, even though my review is not all that important in the grand scheme of Delicia's Yelp existence, just wanted to let you guys know ... Delicia is still awesome.

The food was very good. I'm saying it was very amazing however I have recently moved here from Illinois and I expected to spend Illinois prices for a family of four. I spent $45! This is unheard of but it was good. So is the price worth the taste??? See for yourself on the next episode of Yelp review... One thing that really made me laugh was when my wife asked for a to go box we packed up our food only to find out that it was a Chili's to go box we thought this was hilarious.

I was in Reno with family and decided to visit this restaurant again. The food is very nice & the owner is very friendly as usual. My only advice is that they may consider placing knives & forks with small dishes on the table for the diners. I know it is customary to eat with your fingers, not only eating with fingers has sanitary concerns, it gets messy. Some people would still prefer eating with knives and forks. Just a thought. Oh, I'll come back next time I am in Reno. I like the food, beer & wine.

All the takeout food was great from here. Ordered it spice level 8 to 9 which was perfectly spicy to my taste Can't wait until they have the tandoor installed Standouts include Vegetable samosas Lasooni gobhi (favorite item) Paneer Chile ( not on menu but they made it great) Paneer makhani Palak paneer Channa masala Baingan bharta Bindi masala Will be back to try more

Very good! I've gotten delivery a few times and I think its by far the best Panang I've had in a long time. Not too expensive at all. The crab rangoon is also delicious! They're stuffed generously and not overly cheesy. Its a great balance of crab and cheese. Its very difficult to find good crab rangoon - if any at all. The chicken satay is also delicious. The peanut sauce it comes with isn't too sweet and has just the right amount of kick to it. Their delivery is always much faster than the time they quote me and everything comes exactly as I ordered it. My only complaint would be that they occasionally don't have delivery available. I've called a few times at about 6 PM and their delivery driver had already gone home for the day so I couldn't order. I wish they had more regular, dependable delivery hours. Other than that, I'm likely to become a regular for them.

As a Cuban-American, I was excited to hear that St. Louis once again had a place to go for Cuban food. I have had the food at Mi Caribe on three occasions (twice in the restaurant, and once as a to-go order)--overall, the quality is hit and miss. I understand that this is more of a Dominican restaurant instead of a Cuban or Puerto Rican restaurant, but there is some cross-over in cuisine with distinguishing features for each country. The mofongo is good here, and a sure thing. The Cuban sandwich is quite good and I have had it twice. The tostones and maduros are also great. Ropa vieja--fair at best. We were asked by the manager how we liked our meal, my husband (who--like I--is one of those people who cannot stand cilantro--even the smallest sprig makes an entire dish taste like dish soap) expressed that he did not enjoy his rope vieja because he did not expect to find cilantro in it. The snarky reply from the manager was "we're Dominican" and he walked away. Fine...but don't call it rope vieja. Call it Dominican carne ripiada or Dominican Ropa Vieja, but don't tell a Cuban that it is OK to contaminate our national dish with the offensive herb. Rude. Needless to say, I did not ask if they made Cuban coffee, and we asked for our check. I guess Mi Caribe is not my cup of Caribe and we will probably not return.

This place is great! Please check this place out if you like good Jamaican food. From what I hear this is pretty close to or almost the same as the food you would get in Jamaica. A co-worker introduced me to this restaurant a few weeks ago. I had oxtails, rice, and peas my first time there. It was pretty good. I went there today for my second visit and had a combination of Jerk Chicken, Jerk Pork, and Festival's. The food was delicious and the portions are big. I plan on making this place one of my new favorite spots to get Jamaican food.

Great restaurant and service. Ordered special - bone in pork loin with grilled brussel sprouts and potatoes. Also tried goats curry, which came with unique plantain gnocchi. Both dishes were very good. Oysters came with hot sauce dropper bottle. Nice touch. The only complaint is that the white wine was served too cold.

I personally do not like the food here. There are other better places to go if you like genuine indian food. I have visited this place a couple of times. On my first visit i found one of the service staff to be rude & having an attitude. On my second visit, i decided to try the buffet & found some food items on the buffet to be cold. The food isn't that tasty either.

Wow!!!! Indian at it's very best. Service adorable, my server was struggling with English, he just got here. So Sweet of course worth the extra moment to clarify. Mild, Medium, Hot. I suggest medium if you like heat (Red Hot's or Sriracha), I can't imagine what Hot would actually be like. 4 stars cuz only limited bottled beer selection BUT will frequent to keep them in the business they are pleased at serving us at.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Quite poor even for cheap Chinese. They can't even make fried rice that isn't bad. The sushi counter also has a really strong fish odor which it never should.

Orchid Thai is delicious. They have a wonderful lunch special including an appetizer and entree for a set price. They offer generous portions for both lunch and dinner, and the food is very authentic.

This is the Thai restaurant that I judge all others against. Try the Bael-Fruit hot tea. It's delicious! All of the meals here are wonderful, but don't forget to save room for Thai Donuts afterward. Be sure to ask for "Dee" and let her know Kevin sent you :)

I went here with my boyfriend last week on a cold winter night and we had a great overall experience at Fransisco's. We were given a great seat in front of the fire to keep warm, and our server was knowledgable and attentive. We ordered two appetizers: scallops and mussels- scallops were excellent in a light but delicious lobster cream sauce. He ordered the Hawaiian butterfish and I got the fra diavlo seafood pasta, both very delicious, although take caution when ordering the butterfish if you have a sensitive stomach (they do warn you!). We finished off the meal with cappuccinos and a homemade coconut dessert. I loved the meal so much I am taking my mother there tomorrow night to celebrate her birthday. Would recommend this place to anyone, it's a little gem tucked away on the side of the river. Will definitely like to come back in the summer to get a nice view of the river at night.

Fantastic! This place has authentic Avgolemono soup like my mom makes! Pastitsio is excellent. I called the day before and he made me three portions! Delicious and fresh. The Horiatiki salad (no lettuce) was excellent too. I am looking forward to trying his lamb chops, moussaka, and spinach pie!

High quality and reasonably priced home cooked food and atmosphere. The owner is extremely nice; his humbleness alone would want me to come back to eat at his restaurant. I had passed by this restaurant so many times because I thought the area was a little sketchy, but after I kept hearing positive reviews on this restaurant I had to come try it and I was very pleased.

Here in 3/2012, had the tuna martini to start- very good, great portion size for an app- then had the lamb tagine for dinner- excellent! great service from nick- ask for him as your server n he won't disappoint :) food was worth the extra $

Great place!! Owner is super cool and serves with his heart. He makes food as if he was making for himself. The mango lassi are amazing but they have millions of choices for lassi and chaat. Definitely recommend going and we will most definitely be going back.

Inedible! I just ordered take out lunch, the chicken sweet basil and the panang curry. Just those two dishes, almost $30. I could not eat either dish, way too salty and at the same time, bland. No basil or thai flavors, just salt salt salt. ugh. I'll not return.
Food is awesome. Went here for date night with my girlfriend. Best Thai food I've ever had! Its a must try

As a lifelong fan of Indian cuisine, India Sizzling (II) came very highly recommended to me by a true expert. The expert, who is actually from India, advised me that the food at India Sizzling was the most authentic he has had in the Indianapolis area, and was totally "un-Americanized." Since I have never been to India, I decided to take his word for it--and since I could think of little else other than sumptuous, authentic, un-Americanized, Indian food, I had to make my first visit immediate. Needless to say, I was 5-star impressed. My visit to India Sizzling (II) came on a Saturday night. I was politely greeted and shown immediately to my seat. On the weekends, the restaurant does not offer their main menu, but has a full dinner buffet. I had hoped to actually order off of the menu--as I like to make sure that my food has adequate spice. From my experience, much of the Indian food in the United States has considerably less spice than its authentic counterparts (especially when buffets are concerned). If one truly wishes to experience Indian food, then he should experience it properly. Kinda-sorta doesn't cut it for me--it's like buying a Harley-Davidson Sportster. Yes, it's a Harley; yes, it's wimpy. To my surprise, the food on the buffet at India Sizzling had a nice, spicy kick to it. In the end, I was glad to have been able to sample various items on the menu. The buffet at India Sizzling far exceeds those of other area Indian restaurants. It is much larger, the food is better prepared, and as already stated, is spicier. They offer a full selection of meat dishes, and they serve plenty of vegetarian options. As I was in the mood for meat, I meandered through the various chicken and goat curries. India Sizzling also had a large selection of Chaat, with the Pani Puri being my favorite. Even though I was completely stuffed, I saved room for the many dessert samplings. The restaurant staff was extremely friendly, and the service was impeccable. If the service was this outstanding during buffet hours, I can only imagine what it must be like when they are only serving from the menu. I was further delighted to have been greeted by the general manager, who was able to give valuable information regarding the foods that his establishment served. India Sizzling will establish your tongue in Nirvana. The only thing left to worry about is your soul.
Pretty decent food. I got the lunch special with the pork dumplings and the red curry and both dishes were okay. I am going to try it for dinner to see if it is better. Service was great.

Tourists feel free. Locals -sigh- try once and then go back to your local favorites so at least you can say you visited here once. Pro Tip - skip happy hour here because it doesn't really exist. Had I reviewed this placed when we were here for Todd Price Taste Club, 5 stars, though that's not necessarily a fair reflection of the resturant - so I waited. Had I reviewed this place the last time I went to dinner here (1 year ago), there would've been 4 stars because the food was perfection, but portions were small and wait staff that night was a bit off. Today, there are 3 stars. When I paid my bill it just didn't feel worth it - and I hadn't even had the dinner I'd anticpated to have (we ate entrees elsewhere). We enter to an empty restaurant, but still have to wait a moment to be seated. We're then told that "yes it's happy hour, but you can only order happy hour drinks at the bar". OK fine. We move to the bar because you can get the full menu there (no wonder no one was sitting at a table!), and were told they have 3 drinks on the happy hour menu, Old Fashion, Daiquiri, and wine (saying that from memory - if I'm wrong, I'm sorry; I was in shock). Basically we should've never moved from the table because none of the good drinks are on their Happy Hour list. The bar staff were decent, but not as attentive as they should've been. The food was good, not as amazing as the last two times, and as others have said, if you're actually hungry, the portions are super small. I'm going to be super honest that I was so disappointed in this experience, after two apps and each one drink we got up and left to enjoy dinner elsewhere in the area.

So I'm pretty sure I haven't stopped raving about this truck since I first tried it after work a couple of months ago. Finally got around to writing a review for it! The chicken satay tacos are SOOO good. Get two and a thai tea and you will be full! The chicken is very flavorful and the tacos are pretty big, topped with lettuce, red cabbage, tomatoes, some sort of sauce and avocado slices. Very fresh, crunchy flavors that balance out the curry chicken satay. 2 for $6. Maybe a little steep for food from a truck but trust me, the tacos are even better than some that I've had at a sit-down restaurant! for real. Next, chicken katsu over rice. Again, very flavorful and unexpected from a lunch truck. Around 5 bucks and so worth it! But as a heads up, they are always out after the lunch rush... I have yet to try the captain crunch talapia because I've been sticking to my tacos but next time I stop by, I'll give it a try. I can understand why there was hype about this place. They definitely use quality ingredients and does not taste like food from a lunch truck! Kind of more expensive compared to the ten other trucks on the same block but its the only place you can get your thai/indian/mexican fusion fix!!

To echo most other Yelpers, Marrakesh is a fun place to come with a big group. They give you plenty of food, so you know you will walk away with a full stomach. If you arrive before 7:30, the place will be on the quiet side bordering on dead silent, but it's a good time to have conversations where you can actually hear the other person. After 7:30, especially on a Friday, this place lights up. Keep in mind, this also means slower service, so you should either order drinks or BYOB. It's difficult to say anything negative about this establishment because they are quite hospitable and accommodating. It would be a bum deal to come here if you were vegetarian, but if you don't eat red meat (lamb, in the case of my boyfriend), they can make you a veggie plate on the lamb course. Now, I don't have too much experience with Moroccan food (unless you count Hookah), but, for me, the dishes that combine both savory and sweet flavors still take some getting used to. For this reason, I was not a fan of the "phyllo dough dish with egg and chicken" nor the lamb. My faves are the eggplant from the salad course, chile chicken, and the couscous (more soupy than what I've seen, but I like it). I will definitely come back when I have friends visiting from out-of-town (they should also be adventurous because I know people who don't particularly like eating with their hands), but dinner here on a random weekday seems a little excessive.

I had been going to this restaurant on and off for 2 years. Each time I went there I would tell the server that the green beans and carrots were too hard (uncooked), beef pieces very tough with veins (impossible to chew). The last time I went there was yesterday and the same thing happened. Seems like their standard of cooking can never change or improve, even after numerous and constant feedback from customers. The servers also have bad attitude. After I talked to my server about the food, the other server asked her what did I say? When she told her, the other talked something back in their Thai language, and she sounded very rude. This is what is called NO CLASS or Mom & Pop restaurant! I have made up my mind not to go there again, enough is enough!
Absolutely disgusting cold Shawrma sandwich that couldn't take more than 2 bites! Not recommended at all

A Vietnamese friend of mine clued me in to a whole new way of experiencing pho here: order extra meat and extra noodles. Get a sandwich to go for later. Warm perfect, crispy-chewy french roll with delicious, perfectly tender meat, cilantro, and tangy-sweet pickles. And you get a big sandwich for under 3 bucks. Screw the five-dollar footlong, Id make the drive out to Charlotte Pike from Vandy just for the sandwich.

The meal was excellent. I had Chicken Tikka. We also had Onion Kulcha. The wine is a little expensive. It is always a lovely experience though it is better to avoid their busiest times as service can be slow.

Very good stop for breakfast. I had an omelette with spinach, tomatoes and cheese. It was nothing special, but it was very good; you'd be amazed at how many places can mess up an omelette, so this was very nice. Also had home fries that were pretty good too. My favorite thing? Oddly enough it was the wheat toast. It was perfectly toasted which is a surprise. Most places just throw the toast in with your meal and it comes out way under done. But this toast was probably the best I ever had. I know, weird that I am raving over toast, but it really was good. Good coffee, friendly staff and inexpensive. Nice breakfast spot if you are in the area.

When they first opened they had a couple problems. But now that they've been open for a bit I think they have improved a lot. Their food is tasty and super cheap, and the service is fast so I'm giving them 5 stars. That's all I can ask for! The people leaving negative reviews must have come when they first opened or they are those stereotypical stuck up yelp people who expect a 5 star dining experience from Mcdonald's.

So after months and months of passing this place. I finally gave them chance, and man was I lucky that I did! I called in my order ahead of time for pick-up after looking at the menus that customers posted here on Yelp. The menu that the link goes to is not for the 38th Street location. Anywho, I called, and the girl that took my order was very friendly and professional while taking my order. My food was ready and waiting for me at the front counter when I arrived. I was able to the lovely young lady who took my order. She opened up each dinner that I ordered in order for me to check it to make sure it was all there. My order was perfect, and smelled and looked amazing! I couldn't wait to get home to rip into our beautifully prepared meals. I ordered the Beef Jerk Ribs with Jollof rice & Plantains. My boyfriend ordered the Oxtail Stew with Beans & Rice and Plantains. We also ordered the small order of Jerk Chicken Wings from their appetizer menu. After taking one bite, I wanted to smack myself for waiting so long to eat here. It was AMAZING! The food was very flavorful, and the portions were huge. We shared our meals with eachother, and still have plenty left over. The only reason why I didn't rate them at 5 stars is due to the lack of green vegetables on the menu, the Jerk wings were good, but they had a sauce that was more of a spicy barbecue, rather than the traditional spicy dry rubbed jerk chicken that I was hoping for. Also, they don't sell liquor which is pretty much a no-go for me to sit down to eat dinner. I must have wine and cocktails available. The atmosphere was pretty dead as well. There was only one table of diners (2 ladies) when I arrived around 6:00 pm on a Friday evening. There wasn't any music playing or any kind of excitement going on to make you want to dine there. I will continue to order take-out, but probably won't seek to dine here if the atmosphere doesn't brighten up. Overall, the phone is excellent, and you're missing out if you don't give them a try.
Great food, Lamb Masala is my favorite. The ice cream is not my favorite, but anything knew is worth trying once.

Abyssinia was my first Ethiopian food experience, and it was a great one. I split a vegetarian sampler with a friend. I enjoyed the communal eating environment and loved dipping the bread into different stews and vegetables. It was a great entree to split with two people.

Meh. Ordered the General Tso's chicken lunch plate to-go. The food was ready in a timely manner and the staff was pleasant. The chicken was average, the fried rice was below average, and the egg roll was good. Would try many other Chinese restaurants before is return here.
Ordered green curry, chow mein and sticky rice. delicious.

Hummus was good, but served nothing like the picture. When I asked, the waitress said,"it's just for the picture." Had shish kabob that tasted like a hamburger on a stick dipped in propane and set ablaze. Jasmine rice covered up with chop chop, not on the side as pictured on their menu. Dinmer for 2, $35, wasted. I'll stick with Louis Pappas.
Real authentic middle eastern food .. Loved it! Try the chicken or beef shawarma, shish kabab or any of the appetizers.

My favorite go-to place for excellent Vietnamese food in Indy! The Pho, bahn mi sandwiches, and other dishes are as good as the ones I enjoyed in southern California. Service is always friendly and fast.

We eat at Vientiane all the time and often bring our friends and family here when they are visiting. The food is flavorful and delicious. Some dishes that you don't see on the menu at every Thai place. Service is hit or miss, but I've never had any problems. Fresh vegetable spring rolls are incredible. Laab is yummy. Steamed red bean dessert is like nothing you've ever had before. There's some ginger basil something rather that is probably my favorite thing there. We eat there a lot and I'm trying to work my way through the menu. I've knocked them down a star because the spiciness level varies. That being said, I've requested my food Thai hot and, after an "are you sure?" from the server, was served an incredibly delicious super spicy meal. I have found that, unless you specify that you want it very hot, though, that the food will come out mild. That's certainly fine for a lot of people and they've probably done so to Americanize some of the authentic spicy dishes but just know to ask for it hot. Since the recent renovation, the interior decor is much nicer and the cafe has doubled in size. Lunch special is a great deal too! NB: it's cash only, BYOB, and they don't take reservations.

This place does look kinda sketchy from the outside but it is clean & bright on the inside. The food was FABULOUS!!!!!!!!! We had hummus app & Petra mixed grill. Could have had a little more beef but AWESOME!!!!!! They serve pickled veggies with the hummus, I'm not a big fan of pickled veggies but you must try them with the hummus - it completely negates the vinegar- AMAZING
GREAT lunch buffet. Haven't ever ordered from the menu though. Great place for a quick, delicious lunch!

After all these years, we finally tried Pita Jungle tonight. Upon walking in, I wondered if we had just walked into Hooters or the like due to the lack of attire worn by several servers. Stuff was poppin' out all over, if you know what I mean. Anyway, we ordered a couple margaritas which clearly tasted like they were made with soda pop. It had that carbonation thing going on plus it was just too sour. Asked our server (Megan) to please add some triple sec, which she did gladly. Being my first time there, I was pesky and asked a lot of questions and the server was very patient with me :) So...I ordered a small greek salad with a side of chicken. The salad was a good size for me, but since it was on a small plate, quite a bit of it kept falling onto the table as I tried cutting the oversized pieces. This is frustrating cuz whatever lands on the table, I won't eat. Call me a germaphobe. I think the 'cook' forgot to put some salad dressing on as the lettuce was bland, bland, bland. The chicken was.....interesting.....was it supposed to be warm or cool? Some pieces were chilled (like out of the frig) and other pieces were warm (but not hot). I guess I watch too much Chef Ramsey, but dang it, I was expecting my chicken to be 'cooked to order'. Definitely wasn't. Plus, I'm just not sure how I'm supposed to be loving on cold and warm chicken at one time. Hubby ordered the gyro, which he said was dry, but otherwise tasted ok. We got the tiny happy hour side of tzatziki sauce and 3 hummus. The tzatziki was yummy, but c'mon! $1.50 for that tiny amount? Pappoule's doesn't charge a penny for extra tzatziki (plus the chicken is HOT too!) The pita bread that came with it was cold and all dried out and you could tell just by looking at it. Why would you put that on a plate for a paying customer? We told the server and she replaced it quickly. Overall speaking, the service was fine, but the food wasn't anything to warrant another visit. If you are looking for real Greek food, this isn't it. The menu is all over the place, so it's kinda hard to determine what Pita Jungle is really all about.

Our foodie group met up here recently; this time only 5 of us could make it. I may have been the only one who had not been here before. We were waited on by a woman who was very friendly and had a great smile, but she did not tell us that much about the food. We asked if the combo meat / vegetarian plate would be enough for all of us, and it just about was. We later added the Ethiopian cottage cheese (yum) and an order of the spicy lamb stew, and that was a perfect amount of food for 5. I left feeling satisifed, but not overly full. The stand-out of the evening for me was the spicy lamb dish with green bell peppers. Next time I might just order that. Suggestions for improvement: since all the meals are communal and shared, easy access to the round dish that the food is served on can be tricky when there are more than 2 people at a square or rectangular table. Would make much more sense to have round tables for easier reach. It was pretty funny to watch all of us try to figure out how to eat with our right hand (in this culture, you never use your left hand to eat or touch food - that hand is reserved for bathroom duties, if you know what I mean). I can guarantee that some of us left with stained shirts from food falling out of our fingers. Loved that it was quiet enough that we could all hear each other and have conversations without screaming. Yay! Cost: About $15-$20 pp. FYI - $30 corkage fee. Final thought: I still prefer to eat with utensils.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: service wasn't that hot, appetizer forgot, so these four stars are due, not to the pad se-ew, which was fine, but something else was so truly divine, though hard to eat, a most gluttonous treat the best thing they make, rapturous fried cheesecake!
Great Greek food, fresh pita and nice people. I love food that is made with love and with bold flavors.

Love love love this place! Their Pho, fish in clay pot, etc... are wonderful. I always try something new here on their extensive menu, and I've never been disappointed. Oh, and don't miss the vietnamese coffee as long as you don't need to sleep tonight.

Of all the Thai places around the St. Louis metro (and a few in other cities) that I've eaten at, this has got to be in the top 2. (King and I is pretty good too). Was a resident of Columbia, and ate there regularly, and now that I've moved I still make the trip back to relive the tastes. Definitely worth it!

Love this place! Been there twice this summer and it's been awesome both times. I love the option to sit inside or out on a nice night. It's in a great location, walking distance from most residences in Fairmount/Art Museum area and the food is terrific. If you like greek, you definitely have to check it out.

Delicious and excellent Thai food and despite its location, is very affordable. Three of us ate dinner for $60 (without alcohol) and we all enjoyed our food. There is something about their tofu and its prep that makes it different than other restaurants. We had pineapple curry with shrimp; fried tofu as an appetizer; glass noodle salad with chicken and shrimp; another tofu dish; and the funny-named Crouching Tiger salad that is just delicious steak, dressing and greens. All in all, a great meal in a small, cozy restaurant.
The boba was too hard to chew and inedible. The bread for the bahn mi seemed store bought and pork was not grilled but steamed maybe. Tofu vermicelli was good however.

This location is closed and will not reopen, At first blush, Thai food from a French kitchen seems unlikely but Nadia's makes it work to perfection. Every dish is well thought out and made to perfection. Don't be afraid to order the spicy dishes for an authentic taste of Thailand but there are enough milder dishes on the menu to suit any palate. Prices are commiserate with the quality of the ingredients and the skill of the kitchen staff buare still a great value for what you get. The $10 lunch menu is an especially good value.
Love this place! Good food, good service, relaxing atmosphere and wonderful sunsets. What more can ya ask for! Try it you would have to be a stick in the mud to not have a good time.
This place makes me feel like watching the Kite Runner was totally worth my time. The food was incredible. Enjoy yourself and be merry... you won't be dissappointed!

Like other reviewers, I was initially a bit put off by the decor (it really is a market) and they don't serve alcohol. However the food was AMAZING they ask beforehand and spiced exactly to our specifications, authentic and delicious, plus reasonably priced (they accept credit cards). The staff was very gracious and friendly. We will definitely be returning! In fact, I cannot wait to go back. YUM YUM

Ok New chief to me...been three months..maybe more since I have been here.. Sweet Thai basil with chicken has always been my stand-by love here. I have to say cudos to the new chief...by-far the best I've had here and have been coming here for 6 years
Had a good Cuban sandwich here They also gave out guava pastries I enjoyed this on way to the Keys and very much enjoyed

Nice decor but probably the worst Thai food I've ever had. We had the green curry, pad Thai, and massaman curry. None of them had the authentic flavors the dishes usually have. We will go back to our regular spot Ploy Thai and will not be coming back. Service also took a very long time. Also keep an eye out for how they put all dark skinned diners in the back room. That kind of prejudice is completely unacceptable.

I cannot speak to it's authenticity - I just know it tastes my good. My friend who lived in Thailand for 3 years said it was wonderfully reflective of real-time food cooked there. I wasn't big on the ambience but the food is good. The prices are reasonable.

I'm addicted to Indian food so of course I had to try this place. The naan was soft and wonderful but some parts were burnt. The chicken in the chicken tikka masala was VERY good - soft, juicy. Usually its dry in other places and I'm picky about that. But the main reason why I wrote this post is because after I had some of my boyfriend's chicken vindaloo, we both had...let's just say, "digestive issues" for the next 48 hours. Go there to eat, service is good, parking is easy, BYOB...just stay away from the vindaloo
The hummus is so good here; I buy it for home on a regular basis. Hands down the best I've had! There falafel is phenomenal too. For traditional Arabic food this place is as good as it gets!

Great neighborhood spot for cheap drinks alongside locals. I ordered my food around 8:30 on a Friday night, definitely drinking time, so I think the food was more or less so warmed up and the injera was cold. I still enjoyed it as I love a Ethiopian food and like to support a local place!

As so far I have only compared this to Gojo, I'd say for the Nolensville area, I enjoy this more. You definitely get more food for the money, its less crowded, and the sauces seem to have a bit more complexity (especially the beef sauces). Lots of vegeterian options as well. Definitely something to check out. My girlfriend and I usually just split one of the sampler dishes as its enough for two.

The lunch buffet is awesome!!!! We accidentally walked in today and found out the food is so great! Chicken is so tender and the curry sauce taste just perfect(I don't like spicy. The sauce here is mild.) I'll definitely go back again.

One of our favorite restaurants in Indy by far. A bit pricy compared to other restaurants and service is slow, but the food tastes amazing and authentic. I love ingera the unique bread they have made from Teff flour - it's great, chewy and slightly sour, soft and glutinous all at once, and to top it off it is gluten free so I can actually eat it! I would come back again, and again.

I have been to La Va numerous times and think this last time was enough for me. I just don't think it is set up for someone who wants to work a few hours away from home. I understand the concept of flipping tables or not wanting people to linger, but it is a coffee house, and since there is a $10 minimum on credit, I just put the rest on a gift card (not something they suggested, something I heard from someone else one day, I use to just buy over $10 worth of food each time) I don't think wanting to be able to sit is a bad thing. I sat on a couch waiting for a table to open next to an outlet and the only one open was a four top. A mom came in with a husband and two kids and told me she needed the table and would only be a half hour. The couch I was sitting on was taken, so I sit at one of those middle two tops waiting and doing what? No thanks. Kids were running around and one came up and started coughing on me. I don't hate kids, but staff need to find a delicate way to tell parents that I hate kids. I can look over the BLT I could make better at home, the salad with too much dressing and the spending of over $10 each time I am there, but the layout, the rushed feeling and the crowdedness I don't think I can deal with anymore. Or just the space set up to where being a single patron isn't look as down upon as dinner at my Aunt's house. Fortunately, my boyfriend writes there sometimes, so the gift card won't go to waste.
Excellent traditionally prepared food. Family owned and operated. Isn't in the best neighborhood but definitely worth it.
Amazing service, professional and couteous staff and a large menu. Try their amazing fries! Milkshakes and platter is heavenly as well. I highly recommend this new restaurant.

My wife and I love this place. We have tried various foods and everything we tried was outstanding! The people that work there are extremely nice (I believe the one lady is the owner). The kids loved it too, they brought out an amazing orange ice cream drink for them which they loved. Highly recommended, nice people, great food and relaxing ambiance make for an amazing experience!!

I went to Bittersweet for the first time a few weeks ago with some friends for lunch. Had read the reviews and had the muffaletta. Gigantic portion and enough to take home for later. It was a great sandwich. Today, I returned with another friend. Not feeling too hungry, I ordered one of the specials, the Turkey Chili. It was rather dry and was more like nachos and cheese with meat. Perhaps, it was the turkey but it had almost no liquid or moisture. I like Bittersweet, but the chili wasn't a hit with me.

The chicken salad I had reminded me of the very best vietnamese chicken salad I ate, in a small vendor stall in Singapore... wow. Sweet, tangy, salty and very mildly spicy. The tiny circular cut fried shallots were a wonderful touch.

Right on State Street, we walked into this little gem of a place. It is dimly lit and looks family run. The food was fresh, hot and delicious. First, we started out with the Spring rolls and the plum sauce and the coconut veggie soup. The spring rolls were fresh, a touch on the oily side and the plum sauce was extremely sweet. The coconut soup was unbelievable. The veggies were cooked just right and the broth itself was amazing. The entrees were standard fare and we ensured we devoured every last spoon. This brings us to the dessert. We ordered the fried banana and coconut ice cream. I've honestly not had anything like it before. The dessert itself was mild and not overpowering. It was also very light. The bananas had the perfect amount of crispiness and heat to them. This complimented the house made ice cream perfectly. All in all, it was a great experience. I'll make sure I pay this place a visit when I come back. PS: Just a side note, my friend ordered a chicken entree and told me the chicken was not processed chicken but of higher quality. I'm a veggie so I don't really understand.

This was my first time eating Vietnamese food, and it could not have been better. My roommate and I had been eyeing this place for a while and finally decided to try it once it started raining last night. We went to Mint with three friends and everyone had an amazing time. I got the Spicy Beef Soup which was heavenly and everyone at the table would steal from me. I highly recommend this restaurant!

So very glad I bookmarked Delicia and made a special trip over to Indy just to experience what all the great reviews were stating. From the time we sat down to the moment we left, every little detail was meant to make you feel like you were the only one there. The Sebastiani Cabernet Sauvignon, Sonoma was exceptionally smooth. Then, our appetizer came, which was guacamole and ceviche and we both could not stop until it was gone. I would have never thought to put spicy pistachios on top of guacamole, but that is what made it taste so good. When our entree came, we both could see the presentation looked like a work of art. Then, the taste was the same, a work of art. We will definitely be back and bring friends to enjoy the experience with us.
Awesome gyros. Spicy bacon avacado are so good. Join the club at their website and earn your way to free food.

A race finished strong is always good. Mumbai Bistro is not a restaurant experience, it is an eating experience. They host a buffet line by the weight or you can order from the kitchen in a standard portion. Do they deliver? Yes! Are they good for take out? Yes! Was the Lamb Vindaloo with extra spicy curry delicious absolutely awesome? Yes! So what puts them from 4 to 5 stars, killer service. I would never expect great service from a small joint that strikes me as a drive by take out but the gentleman working the cash register proved me wrong. He did all the right stuff, greeted me when we came in, asked if I had any questions and offered to explain the menu. He gave us the best thorough yet fast lowdown on everything and was very friendly about it. I was so stunned by his service, I thanked him for it. I'll be returning.

Avoid this restaurant if you are looking to eat food. 1) it wreaks of the cigarettes the chef smokes in the back, as the food twirls around in the microwave. 2) the entrees come out before appetizers 3) the entrees are flavorless,& served cold and hot in spots. 4) the restaurant was cute, the service was really slow, and the waitress tried to make it all come together. It just didn't.

A group of coworkers and I dined here the friday before Halloween. I loved how most of the staff was dressed up for this festive occasion costumes ranged from male hulu dancers to female elvis. Food was good i really enjoyed my jerk chicken pasta. I would even say that it was better than some pastas that ive had at Italian restaurants. For $25 you can get a might tasty ribeye with chimichurri sauce. Do not order the black paella. The ooey gooey cake with caramel was a big hit at our table. i would recommend this place to others!

Went for breakfast / brunch. Pros. Amazing ambiance, decor, and set up. 5 stars for that. I've been to Lebanese restaurants all over the country and they hit it out of the park when it comes to the decor, but unfortunately it ends there. Cons. As has been highlighted by other users, Value - 8 bucks for a mannouchee with cheese and a sprinkle of zaatar... let's get real... and please don't eat it with a fork and knife, fold it in half and bite into it the way it was meant to be eaten. Lebanese omelette was great but not 14 dollars great. Glad I tried it but not worth the visit if don't happen to be in fishtown for whatever reason, especially if you're driving in (parking issues)

This is my families favorite restaurant, hands down. We eat here at least once a week. The food is dependably excellent, I always clean my plate. They do fun theme menus for different seasons and holidays. My favorite thing about the Blueplate is the staff, they are always so friendly and accommodating. My husband and I have been going here since before we had our two small kids - we still love going out to eat (which is not always easy with babies and toddlers), the team here is always patient and understanding. We go for all meals, but breakfast is our favorite.

Awesome food simply awesome. Reminded me of old Amans in Norristown. Tadka Daal had me salivating and with lachaa paratha it was excellent. Mango lassi was less sweet than Iikes but they said it was just made and was not in cooler. Panir kali mirch had that sweet peppery taste and the spice level was right on. I ordered a samosa chaat to go and Saag panir with garlic Naan. They next day I was in heaven. One less star because I had to wait rather longer than usual
Good food, at a decent price. Excellent variety, including multi ethnic!

After months of discussion, my boyfriend and I decided finally to go to Zorba's tonight. I must say, I'm very happy that I went. The service was excellent. Within minutes after we sat down, we had our bottle of wine opened (yes! It's a BYOB!); fresh, moist bread delivered to our table, complete with extra virgin olive oil-and-herb dip; and our order taken by a friendly waitress. (The bread was delicious.) Within two minutes after she took our order, we had our salad. The dressing was a light vinaigrette--my favorite--and there were lots of fresh vegetables. The lettuce was the watery kind, but that was my only gripe. For the entree, my boyfriend ordered grilled skewered chicken and I ordered grilled marinated chicken. They were both absolutely perfect... perfectly seasoned, moist, and just really flavorful. The sides included potatoes (yummy), rice (a little soggy, but pretty good), and mixed vegetables (pretty gross, which is partly why I docked them a star). They were quick with refilling water, but were a little slow in giving us the check. However, the waiter was apologetic and cute, so I can forgive them for that. :) I would definitely go here again, especially since it's a BYOB and there is a lack of good, fairly healthy restaurants in the area.
The best tikka masala I've ever had!! The chicken biryani was delicious and the yogurt sauce that comes with the biryani was fantastic! Would definitely recommend

My daughter's were in town and wanted seafood so we headed down to Sam's for the first time. Even though it wasn't that late, about 9:45, they were getting ready to close. They staff went out of their way to accommodate us and it was fantastic. The staemed mussels with garlic and wine were delicious and fresh. The steamed clams were great as well. For us the best part were the Pulled Pork Nachos. They were amazing and unique. We will definitely go back again.
Great Buns, I recommend getting the grilled pork with egg sunny side up with steamed veggies! Fresh spring rolls with peanut sauce are amazing too!

#NinaCompton is the new queen of New Orleans cuisine. Depth, breadth, zing, pow, bam and allllll that jazz! She performs at such a superior level in the kitchen that she can be likened to a super hero. Foodies will be delighted. One can absolutely taste and appreciate the multi-levels of preparation, care, skill and love in the food. She is a true craftswoman! You MUST visit and take part in the pleasure, from starter to finishing liqueur. **I highly recommend the cold smoked tuna, curried goat, and roasted banana zeppole.** We also had a fresh tasting salad with peaches and cucumber but I forgot the name and it may have also been a special. Stephan, the server, was prompt, knowledgeable and pleasant making the most perfect recommendations, all of which we tried and did not disappoint. Located in the Old 77 Hotel right across the Tchoupitoulas Street from cruise line ports and the newly redesigned Riverwalk Shopping Center, Compere Lapin is a must when in New Orleans for work or play. St. Lucia is well represented by this native daughter.

WORST MANAGER EVER!!! I've been here quite often and made this place one of my fave places to go. However since they changed the manager a while ago, I dont think its a good place to eat at no more. I had dinner with my family and my sis left an empty container on the table. It was EMPTY, it had no smell or disgusting leftovers inside. When we were about to get into the car (coincidentally we parked our car right in front of the rest.) sudennly the manager (even tough I dont think its appropriate to put a manager title to such an ignorant man like him) came out holding the container and asked us whether its our belongings (with a high tone and rude impression on his face). I said no thats just trash, and he said it out loud (again with the rudest face I've ever seen in my whole life) that I cannot leave my trash there. To cut the story short, I came back in to the rest and asked about it, and he argued with high tone. Right after I said to him that he needs to watch his attitude, he right away pointed his middle finger to me! Okay, my patience's gone. I didnt think I deserved any crap like this. Whats the big deal of leaving a container on the table??? Its just irrational and super crazy for a "manager" to make such a hassle about it! A true manager would've just shut up. He even still arguing and kept pointing his finger at me while we were walking out from the rest. He kept on yelling to leave the place and never come back no more. Not enough for that, as we're getting into our car, he AGAIN pointed his middle finger and shook his ass!!! He then made a gesture like he was about to f**k me! At that time my bro was so mad and approached him, telling him to go back into the rest if he didnt want to get hurt. WTF! Hellll what kind of manager is that! Such an ignorant, uneducated, and snobbish person like him doesnt deserve to work in any fields especially being a manager!!! I will never ever come back to that place and ooohhhh its not gonna surprise me if the restaurant will crash one day with the attitude of "THEIR GREAT MANAGER." People pay not only for food but also for its SERVICE!

This is by far the best quick service Greek restaurant in the Tampa area. I have never been inside (only drive thru) so I cannot comment on the interior or ambiance of the place but wow is the food good. The gyro and greek salad are my usual go-tos. They even use the real blocks of feta on the salad....very impressive! The freshness and quality of the food never disappoint. Now if only they would open one in South Tampa!

Great Middle Eastern Food in Center City PHiladelphia! My friend Keri introduced me to Bitar's a few months ago and I am so grateful to her. It was very helpful to order at Bitar's for several events that I had planned. The food is fresh and tasty and all my guests who had it loved it as much as I do. The service is friendly and accurate. For the luncheon I hosted recently I ordered their spanakopitas and their chicken sandwiches as entree and when I went to pick up the order I also was able to grab at the store olives, feta cheese, humus and pita bread without needing to order these in advance. They have three kids of feta cheese, the Greek one which is a bit more hard and very salty and is great for greek salads, the Bulgarian which is less salty and more moist and the French feta which is very moist and creamy. I usually get the Bulgarian one but I think I will try the French next time for a change. I have tried other middles eastern restaurants and this is the best!

I had the house special sandwich which is the original banh mi sandwich and eggrolls. The sandwich was good just seemed a bit skimpy. But still pretty good considering it is Idaho. Eggrolls are a buck a piece and pretty dry but average. First time in the store so forgot to get a drink and after I ate the first eggrolls I was ready to drink a river. Told me they didn't have water cups and that I had to buy which isn't a issue but just inconvient as people started coming in. Overall the good is good. But service is below average and store seems a bit dirty and cluttered. Food in my opinion is also a bit on the expensive side but that definitely would not be too much of an issue if service was up to par. I might come again to give them another shot. Next time I'm trying the pho.
Great Italian food. Reasonably priced lunch menu with all the essential staples. Service was warm and accommodating. Would recommend.

My new favorite pho place in town. I heard about a new pho place that opened up so I thought I'd give it a try. I was not disappointed. The food was amazing!! I had the pho (if I remember it was P14 on the menu). What set this pho apart from the competition was the amazing broth. If you are looking for the best pho in town, stop by Phamous cafe

I have eaten here many times, the latest yesterday. It is always consistently delicious and excellent service. The lunch menu is a spectacular deal: soup or salad and a plate with your entree, rice, spring roll and won ton. My husband tries a new dish each time and has always enjoyed them. I love Pad Thai so alternate between shrimp and tofu. The service is fast, polite, and friendly. The patio is cozy, shaded and an excellent choice when you are traveling with dogs.

leaving new orleans, we decided to hit another pho place... cajun food is just too heavy. southern food just too much deep fried... funny, end up eating more pho in new orleans than anything else... i dont even eat this much pho in southbay.. in any case, it was pretty good. nice and refreshing in contrast to all the deep fried grease. need pho to de-grease from last night's fried chicken...
Succulent rack of lamb and chicken souvlaki. Will try to get back soon to try more from this restaurant!

This place can be defined as a Thai place with a twist. The owner cum chef uses his heritage and combines it with the modern. You can be assured that the food that comes on your table is as fresh as it gets. Extremely child friendly and warm people made this an amazing lunch for us. Though the dessert menu could use some more items, you mustn't miss the white elephant. Can't wait to come back and try the drunken duck :)
Food is great!! Very clean and everyone was friendly. We will be coming back the next time we are in Nashville

This use to be a Cajun Restaurant. The owners have completely redone the interior. Beautifully decorated in black and white. The food is Carribean and delicious. This is a family run business and I sure hope it does well. You can rent a booth for special occasions. I will be back!

Surprisingly very good food! Had the tomyum soup and appetizer crepe-both were very delicious. The soup had a strong flavor and mildy spicy. I did family style with 3 other people. We had the chicken pad thai, red-colored curry (forget the thai name), pineapple fried rice. All were excellent! The pad thai was very savory and the curry had a kick, the way I like it! The fries rice was very fresh tasting with fresh looking veggies. The decor was nice and the restaurant seemed pretty clean. The place was pretty busy, but the staff members were still nice and attentive. I was pleasantly surprised with the place.

You would think that with their grand opening, they would have prepared better for loads of customers! I entered Bambu and was told that if I wanted bubbles, I would have to wait 30 minutes. I said no thanks and ordered my drink with one specific instruction (no milk). Shockingly, I spent more than 30 minutes waiting for my drink and they messed it up anyway. What if I were lactose intolerant? I realized maybe I should have waited the "30 minutes" because I spent much more time there! I also kind of felt as though they were serving people that they knew first. I decided to give them another try because I went during their grand opening. Drinks are great but I do think it gets a bit unprofessional. There are customers that walk behind the counter and hang out to talk. One time, one of the customers walked behind the counter to chat and I had to wait because the worker was chatting to the customer. I don't know...it just makes me feel as though there should be some boundaries regardless if you know the owners. They do take debit which is awesome and they don't require a minimum which I do appreciate! I just wish there was more of a professional atmosphere and listening skills.

Irie Bay is a small Jamaican cafe in the plaza behind Hooter's on Adamo Dr. When I came in, the man working there just told me what they had that day. There wasn't a menu handed to me so that limited my options to a couple things. I ended up ordering the jerk chicken dish with rice and plantains. It was OK, nothing more, nothing less. As I was eating, the older lady was just chatting me up and watching me eat. It felt like visiting a Jamaican neighbor's home and having her cook up a dish. You tell her it was good, because she's sweet, older and she's your neighbor but deep down, you know you probably won't go over her house for dinner anymore. Not that it was bad but you just don't see yourself going back. But if you're Jamaican, maybe this place might remind you of home and you might like it more than me. One thing to note is that they have live reggae and dancing on Friday or Saturday nights until the wee hours of the morning so you can call ahead to find out their schedule. That may make the whole experience better.

The food is very consistent and it is reasonably priced. The bun is great especially pork with egg roll. Service is good and a very clean tidy place. They do have outdoor dining as well which makes it nice right on Magazine Street.

Delicious! My husband brought me here for my birthday and it was fabulous!! Everything was so fresh and authentic! The spinach ricotta gnocchi was the best I've ever had the the zeppolis for desert were to die for!! It is a little pricey for a byob if you do the 3 course menu but well worth it. Great for a special occasion and you know you're going to have an excellent meal. This place is a great example of quality over quantity. You get plenty of food but it isn't overwhelming portions like some other Italian places which I like! Trust me, we left stuffed and satisfied! Will definitely return! Just be sure to make a reservation because seating is limited.

Okay so here's the thing about August Moon... The food isn't great, however I am giving it 4 stars because it is cheap, fast (if you eat there or pickup), and has great service. The food isn't bad, it's just very Americanized Chinese food. Which is something I like time to time. The General Tao's sauce is syrupy and super sweet, but I like it! The fried spring rolls are greasy, but super crunchy and delicious. They will refill your water like 5 times during a short meal and your server will check on you. They are helpful and attentive. I wish all places had this great service. I used to work nearby and we would go there on our 1 hour lunch breaks, because they were That Fast! If you want a place that has great service, decent food, and is pretty darn cheap... Then August Moon is your place to go!

Not in love with this place. It's pretty clearly geared towards an old folks clientele (there are notes all over the menu about extra charges for sharing), though we were able to walk in on Saturday night at 8 with no reservation and be seated almost right away despite a pretty full house, so that's always nice. Service was quite good, my water glass was never empty, but the food was mediocre. I had the Mirna's Soup, which is shrimp, potatoes, spinach and basil all in a kind of strange broth that was neither good nor bad. One of my shrimp hadn't been cleaned/de-veined well, but other than that it was a decent soup. The bread was fine, the pita was extremely dry. I also had a seafood caesar salad, which wasn't very good. The crab was a little fishy and the dressing was a little strange, not caesar-y more like an olive oil dressing. Also there was one olive in the salad, I guess as like a little bonus. Odd. Also tried the fried calamari (chewy but good marinara sauce) and my husband's Penne Vodka, which I thought was perfectly good. I guess the trick is to get the pasta here. We had desserts that were fine but nothing I would order again. Neither the apple cake or the cheesecake tasted very fresh. Overall, the price was pretty high for the quality of the food, and while the general restaurant scene in Jenkintown is pretty abysmal, I think you can do better than this place. Not planning to return.

I come here so often and the servers are always friendly and super amazing. The pho is the best around and the atmosphere is great. I always used to go to Noodle City down on Hollister but this place has much better service, are way friendlier and the pho is better!

I'm afraid to share the good news, but this place is my go-to. Any day of the week, I can be in the mood for this delicious Thai cuisine. The larb always has that heat you love to hate. The pad Thai is exactly what you want it to be, and the curry is packing tons of flavor. Such a nice spot, get excited for a delicious meal in your future....

I really hate giving out one star to a place where folks are obviously working hard and trying to make a living, but the food at Basil Spice is not good at all. I went here shortly after they opened and had a noodle dish (pad thai) that was cooked in so much oil that the noodles nearly oozed off the plate. It was an inedible mess. Naturally, it took a while before I went back. But, after hearing friends say good things about the food, I gave it another try. This time around my dining partner's Pad Thai was not nearly as oily, but it still lacked something important: flavor. The same went for the Pad Basil I ordered. (I also asked for this dish hot, 4 out of 5 stars on their heat scale, but I would rate the heat I got a 0.) And then there was the thing they called Chicken Satay: is chicken supposed to crack like a bread stick when you bit into it? One of the things I love about Thai food is the expert balancing of flavors that is present in so many dishes. At Basil Spice, however, there is really no flavor to balance. This is Thai food dumbed down in the same way that Chinese food has been dumbed down for American palates. There are much better places to get good Thai food in town.

WE went to eat here in April 2017. Very nice beach bar but when our food arrived I went to the mens room to wash my hands and there was no soap in the container. No big deal at first--I just let them know and waited for it to get filled. Well 10 minutes went by so I went back up to the front to ask again for more soap and the person said someone was on the way. When I got back to the mens room two other people were waiting to wash their hands and finally a guy came. However, I was SHOCKED at what he said----THEY WERE COMPLETELY OUT OF SOAP in the whole restaurant. I could not believe that and asked what about the kitchen---any soap will work, again he said they had NO SOAP! Again I went up front and told the counter person that the guy said you were out of soap. This person went back and checked and YES they were really out of ALL soap. GROSS, how are the employees washing their hands I asked and they had no answer. In 57 years I have never seen this happen on a Friday evening before the weekend. This means all meals for their customers were being made with kitchen workers with dirty hands. We never ate our meals and walked out---will never be back.

This is our third time at the restaurant and, unfortunately, it wasn't a charm. The beer is cold; guacamole and chips were good; the enchiladas were okay. I expected more for the money spent. It's probably best as a drinks and apps place for us.

This is by far my favorite Indian restaurant around. Such a creative menu and some of the best tasting dishes ever. Get the chili paneer and mulligatawny soup every time. All of the dishes I've tasted are outstanding. The staff is super friendly and always very attentive too. The chef (Guru) and his wife are so nice ! I would eat here once a week if I could.
Beautiful restaurant! Delicious food! Totally enjoyed the experience! The ground lamb kabab was excellent. Lots of lemon. Perfect Lebanese experience!

After going through few of the reviews I decided to visit this restaurant with couple of my friends...This place turned out to be the WORST ever food joint in my list till date...The lunch buffet menu offered very few varieties...There is just one dessert in offer... Taste was bad, wish I could give 0 rating for this..service was bad ( nor I cared about it after having the food there)...Tandoori chicken was cold, mutton curry is pathetic, chicken tikka masala is a disgrace to its creator.......At $11 it's looting,cheating .... I have had food in many Indian restaurants(Being an Indian)...I have had some bad experience as well...But this restaurant stands tallest among all...in short PLEASE AVOID this place... The only good thing about this place is they have some good paintings in their walls...
