Consider places like Aman's(Norristown), Bawarchi (Wayne), Indian Kitchen(Exton).few in philly downtown etc. if you want to have decent indian food...

Very good option for Indian in the area and they deliver. The chicken Tika Marsala was very tasty. The chicken was perfectly cooked - not dry at all. Butter Naan was a perfect way to scoop up the tasty sauce.

This is one of the brightest pho restaurants in Edmonton. Their walls are painted a bright sunny yellow and with all the windows, makes it a bright and happy looking place. Thankfully, their food and service also seem to be on par. I ordered a bowl of pho tai which came loaded with lots of slices of beef- too much I dare say! Their broth was pretty good. I was happy with this dish. My boyfriend ordered a vermicelli bowl with pork which had great flavours. Oh, I almost forgot, we started with an order of spring rolls which were crispy and tasty! Overall, a solid place to go in Chinatown if you're having a Pho craving. Their service is pretty good, and even friendly from one of the male staff members =)

I can only comment on the already made to go food. I got the red curry and a drink for $9.75 which is a steal. I took it home and heated it up later for dinner and the curry was delicious. The market is small but definitely convenient if you don't want to trek to an HMART. Will definitely be back.

This was my go-to place for Thai. Order came out quick and I would usually take it back home. I think I tried most of the dishes and all were great. Customer service was great, can't believe all that came out of a food truck.

This place is awesome. Delicious food--some of the best Indian food I've had and certainly the best on the mainline. Incredibly friendly host/waiter who seems to know every person who walks in. It is so kid friendly--the host cleaned the high chair before we used it. I've never experienced that elsewhere. It's small but we've never had a wait. It's a great little gem. I highly recommend it.
This is hands down the best Thai food I have ever had. The service was fast and every dish was prepared nicely and tasted amazing. I recommend the fried bananas for dessert!

Only thing holding Delicia back from 5 stars at moment: exterior appeal. I'm hoping this is still in the works based on the sassy and sleek interior? Or maybe the exterior serves as an intentional camouflage for the awesomeness that it's inside? Yeah...that's probably it... Now that you know Delicia is sporting some prettypants, you must also know that their cocktails are mindblowing. I opted for the fire and ice cocktail which was spicy in a borderline "ooo, that hurts" kind of way - I mean this positively. Good pain. Feel the burn. Get me? Even the spherical ice cube was well thought out with herbs frozen into the center. The drink was delicious from beginning to end. Highlights: friendly waitress that was well-informed and long high top booths - perfect for a meeting (as was the case for my first of many visits). Here's the catch, this review is going to have to have a part two because I didn't have a chance to try the food...but I can tell you the menu was a beautifully innovative approach to Latin American food.

My rating would be 3.5 if I could choose that. I've had take out there twice: the first time I tried one of the box specials that day, the crispy duck with papaya salad. At $12 it was a little more than I am used to paying for a Thai lunch but it was a lot of scrumptious food and came with white rice, a crab Rangoon and a Thai egg roll. Definitely good value for size and taste and probably would have covered two meals for me if I wasn't 7.5 months pregnant :) . That box alone was a solid 4 stars. The next time I tried the crab fried rice and my husband got the drunken noodles, both Thai hot. If you regularly eat spicy the Thai hot here is no problem. He said his was "ok" and my fried rice had good flavor and heat. I wish it had more crab in it, but the reason I didn't give a 4 star review is because my husband ordered tofu in the fried rice and there was no tofu. I was a (still preggy) sad panda. Nice thing is the portion of rice is so large that I stretched it to three meals! Everyone there is super friendly, taste was good and generally good value for the price. We'll go back, but disappointing that the one order was wrong.

Went here with my date on a Wednesday night. While the exterior is underwhelming, it makes for a great surprise once you walk inside. Fantastic friendly and attentive waitstaff and host. Great variety of Greek plates, all quickly and deliciously prepared. Entrees offer great value, plus it's a BYOB. Dessert was fantastic. Huge fan and would absolutely return again.

Although the food was delicious, the fact that several servers repeatedly tried to snatch our unfinished food away was unacceptable. They dropped the bill while we still had glasses of wine that were half full. For $350, two people should be able to take all the time they need. Not to mention we weren't there that long, about 1.5 hours- and they rushed us through four courses. Will never return, which is unfortunate.

Not really my kind of joint. Loud in here, hipster music and full of hipsters. Did not eat but looked at the menu and everything was sorta crazy looking trendy hipster food, not your usual bar staples.You cannot order wings but you can get roasted beets with lime yogurt or hummus. The beer I believe they get next door from Fat Bottom so that was good. Otherwise, would not make a point to find this place again.

Great staff. High end cocktails and decent wine selection. Many beers on tap and in the bottle. On street bar rocks and the lounge on the sidewalk is very cool. Staff very friendly and service outstanding. Great mixed crowd young and old. Cool place to meet new friends.

The appetizer sampler is a must!-- although go in open minded; the flavors are really interesting. The atmosphere is so lovely. The outdoor seating while the sun is setting in the summer is blissful. Servers are efficient and kind
AMAZING! My favorite Indian restaurant in Tucson. Try the navaratan korma. Just be warned that you might find yourself developing a weekly habit

Ordered by phone today ( Valentine's Day 2018), called at 5:15pm for 7:15pm pickup. Arrived at 7:15pm to a very busy restaurant. A great sign as we've eaten there many times however, this will be the last time. They acknowledged my order & said be right back. 10 minutes later came by to confirm my order & cell#. Said they'd be right back again. Waited 10 more minutes as another guest came in and received their take away order. The server came over again to say the cook didn't cook my order with shrimp but with chicken, as I'd waited for quite awhile I said okay. Waited total of 45 minutes, not sure what to do, then asked a server if they've completely forgotten me. She came back saying they needed to make fresh spring rolls as the other rolls were cold from sitting, I agreed to wait one minute. 10 more minutes passed, I'd now been there 55 minutes and was going you walk out when the server brought my order. I indicated that I'll happily pay if my food is hot & fresh and that I'll not be adding a TIP. Server was very apologetic, I did appreciate that & I did tell her that. I did mention that I usually TIP 20-25% however since a TIP means 'to insure prompt service', I was not TIPPING today. I left the Thai Orchid at 8:14pm, 59 minutes after I'd arrived and basically an hour after I'd requested my pick up time to be. That is not satisfactory. Brought the food home and yes the Spring Rolls were warm, the rest of the food was cold ( not a surprise)and a disappointment. I will not be returning. I think they gave my order away or they simply forgot about me. The food was just satisfactory. I wouldn't recommend the Thai Orchid for Take Out on Valentine's Day.

The best quality of this place is that it's absent of that huge spinning Lamb Hot Dog that is disgustingly displayed at most Greek places. The yeerohs are actually stuffed with real lamb. They execute their dishes very well and the brand new restaurant has a great environment to sit in. The prices are expected. However, I'd think a better business approach would be to offer a larger portion on the sides to make ppl feel like they're getting a better deal, and it's doesn't break the bank to offer more potatoes or rice. The girl taking our order was terrible. We were the only ones in line and she wanted to rush us. She had the "I just work here" attitude and wasn't any help on what to order at this brand new restaurant. However the rest of the staff was great. It very much had the "Grand Opening" feel; where they barrage you with attention. Kinda the like the way Chipotle was the first 3 weeks of its opening. If I wanted a yeeroh, I'd come here. But it's just another Fast Casual eatery like Chipotle, Noodles&Company, or Pei Wei. As soon as the "New Cool Place" aura dissipates, they'll have to fight hard to keep a strong customer base between Panera and Chipotle, which are on the same street. So I recommend that you come and try it, cuz we often make the mistake not appreciating things until they're gone. And this is one of the only places in Nashville that DOESN'T serve a shredded up lamb hot dog and then calls it a Gyro.

Phenomenal location with great prices and delicious food....whenever we are travelling nearby we make it a point to stop there for a meal - -I only wish that we did NOT live 173 miles away because we would definitely be there to eat on a weekly basis = it is that YUMMY!
Tried the pho today, very good and great price. Also tried a dessert, good too

Got the chicken pad Thai lunch to-go. I'm not sure if this comes with anything like a small appetizer or anything for sit-down but nothing for "to-go". I will admit the portion is huge for about $9. I put it on a plate and it seems about two portions. I got "spicy" and it's not that spicy in my opinion but it's not bad. The taste is good I mean it's nothing crazy but probably the best in this area. It doesn't have that ketchup-y/sticky taste other pad thai's seem to have. However this lemon I received looks like it was definitely used- now I'd just be petty pointing something small like that out but... that's pretty gross
The pho was super yummy and the staff is always nice and courteous! I've stayed to eat and have also had my food to go.

Yay! I enjoyed August Moon as take out (3 stars), but loved the quality of the food as well as the numerous vegetarian options once I ate at the restaurant (4 stars), probably because it was super fresh and hot when we at there, unlike when you order take out! I can honestly say its the first time I've loved a tofu dish ordered at a restaurant! They have so many lunch options, reasonably priced with large servings, you def cannot finish alone, our table ended up passing around and sharing everything, and everyone really enjoyed each menu item ordered. They also have a full bar and the restaurant was rather large, so I cant imagine there ever being a wait. I loved how nice, quiet, and peaceful the restaurant was! I will say our server, though super sweet and friendly, was SLOW. Slow, slow. Like so slow we started to get that hungry, agitated, b*tchy attitude. Not good with four hungover girls! At one point I think I started sizing them up, wondering who would taste better w/ soy sauce, out of straight hunger! Besides the speed, or lack there of, I do look forward to returning to August Moon for chill and casual Chinese food.

Amazing Family Owed Thai Restaurant! I love the Thai iced tea! I also always get the Pad See Ew with beef. The vegetables are also so light and fresh. Not a ton of sauce. Doesn't feel heavy when you eat it. Always get the mango sticky rice if it's in season! I hope this place never closes!

We went twice because the food is reasonably priced and good. The service is slow because it seems to be cooked to order. There are small tables and chairs to eat at. Be patient, the older man taking orders doesn't speak a lot of English. The first time I ordered Pho-ito, not on the menu but highly recommended. It had the ingredients of Pho but in a tortilla, that you dip in broth. tasty but the Pho is better. The second time I ordered fried oyster po-boy. Really good.
Taza has outstanding food and the owners are so nice. I eat vegan friendly meals that are delicious! Had the Mediterranean vegetable dish

I logged into Yelp to write a review of our first dining experience at Bangkokville Thai Cuisine. As it turns out, Summer C. wrote my review for me. The only edits I can make are we had red curry chicken instead of the yellow curry ordered by Summer C. and we discovered this awesome place four months later than did Summer C. I encourage the owner and staff to carry on delivering a fabulous dining experience in the food, the service and the value! Great job folks, we'll be back.

I really like this small Thai restaurant in the heart of Narberth. I am boring and always get the same thing: the coconut soup with chicken (DELICIOUS!) and pad thai. I want to try other dishes but like those two so much that I just can't stray. My husband has tried a greater variety of dishes (including some of the very spicy ones) and has given them rave reviews. The food is flavorful and the service is very friendly. It's great for slightly more upscale takeout; they also have small outdoor tables that are fun to dine at (and people-watch from) when it's nice out. The only negative is that the prices are a little steep. However, at lunchtime they have an affordable special: $10.95 for an appetizer and entree.

This is a place you pay for the atmosphere more than the food, it seems. The wait was 30 minutes for a walk in, which is the too too bad, but the place was swamped with large parties and quickly escalated much past 30 minutes. We had the pickles, which were great, but were SUPREMELY disappointed by the grease fest that was the chicken biscuit. The plate was swimming with orange grease, the biscuit was more Pillsbury than Southern, and the chicken was KFC quality. Our server, while sweet, forgot about us several times over. Our six dollar bacon was 3 slices large, and 1 out of 3 were carbon coated. Over rated and over priced.

Short and sweet: fresh healthy choices combined with good service. Very small and tight space. I didn't like the idea of seeing the a box of cubed ice floor level near the coat rack. I had the broiled scallops, it was good.

This was a fantastic experience. Hassan is a great guy, very passionate about his food. And the food, omg, it is something! We had a guava lassi, a strawberry-pineapple lassi, and of course the famous chaat. So many flavours in one dish! It tastes like nothing else, truly amazing!
Wonderful, wonderful cocktails. Asked for something with cucumber and they gave exactly what (I didn't know) I wanted. Boyfriend got a whisky 7- SO MUCH whisky. :)

Really good service. Very friendly clean environment. I ordered spring rolls and iced green tea. The spring rolls were good. I especially liked the mint in it. The iced green tea... That's a different story. HORRIBLE! This drink is beyond a reasonable doubt, spoiled. I can't get the taste out of my mouth. I didn't tell the owners anything because I hate making a scene and I always have the thought of "what if they spit in my new drink" thought. Pretty disappointing to say the least.

I was pleasantly surprised with this resturaunt. It was in a seedy area of town off 4th street but a friend treated me to lunch and I was blown away at the flavors. I ordered a dish with lamb and ate it with a special ethiopian bread which is totally gluten free. The staff was really attentive and sweet. We tried some baklava dessert and that was also good. This place is a hidden gem in Reno. It is quiet and the food is delicious. I highly recommend it.

There are a few changes that would make a big difference here. The good was good, fresh but... Garlic scallop and shrimp - shrimpy alright! For $16, more Food please! Luke warm and mild- no response to our request about how spicy it was- it wasn't! $1 charge for vegetables instead of chicken curry? Come on Train the staff! They brought one Tea cup for two, failed to wipe the table, cluttered dishes when clearing and then suggested the coconut ice cream ( which was good) was too 'expensive' The ambience is good, excellent lighting and I appreciate the acoustic tile ceiling, now I wish they'd get it together with every meal or I don't think it'll last

My friend and I just tried this place for the first time and it was pretty great. I have a severe allergy to gluten and have to watch what I eat which, let's face it can get pretty boring. We ordered the family style kabobs with a salad and rice. The meat was really tender and juicy and favorful. I loved the dipping sauce that they had with it. The hummus was awesome also! We will definitely be coming back to this place with more friends! Also great if you are doing low carb or keto.

I'e eaten here before, but this is my first review. This time I had the Grilled mushroom rolls with the Lime chicken rice dish. It was kind of spicy and good. Well cooked. I recommend the Mint if your ever in the uptown area.

It is South Indian food which differs from the other well-known dishes such as butter chicken. Are they the best? No but they offer good food for a reasonable price. The restaurant is basic... can even call it a "tiffin" concept imported from southern India. The dosas are good. They are large, crispy yet soft and come with an acceptable sambar and chutney. I would rate the food 3.5 out of 5. The service I have found to be good but could be better. They are packed around dinner on weekends, therefore, the service is slow then. The service is 3.5 out of 5. They earn an extra half a point for their fried fish and lollipop chicken. They are delicious and are loads better if you dine in. They are like fries... Not made for takeout. They lose their crispness! Definitely recommend it!
I haven't gotten any prepared foods here but love their stock of pita, zaatar pita, grape leaves, tahini.
Very cozy place and good food. Had the jasmine fried rice and vegetables and tofu.

This cart is worth the visit/10 bucks. The guy himself is worth the 10 bucks because he's a pure crack up.Funny yet strange. The Chicken is good and so are the falafels. the rice and yogurt sauce, well its OK, I have had better...Its true , he has no menu. I had the nerve to ask for 2 orders. He did not like that , He said that he'll sell me 2 orders only because it was my first time. But he gave me lecture about ordering 2. But he had no problem in takeing my 20 bucks. He was driping in sweat and he was even eating chicken off the grill while talking to me.I doubt that I'll ever go back. But for some reason I found it to be fun.
Prices are high for mediocre food. Very disappointed in meal.

B+ I went to try this place out as my friend who is a local told me that it is a hidden gem. Cucina food truck was lined up with all other food truck, but this one stood out from the rest due to the long lines formed by its customers. I ordered the Tilapia Over Rice and it was one of the best food truck food I have had. The fish was not over fried and was still soft on the inside. The portion is very generous so this can be an option for students on a budget. When you order any of their food, you can ask for it to be "Bossed Out" meaning to put all the sauces in it. Make sure you are comfortable with all of their sauces first. I would definitely go back due to being so close to my work. One more tip, if you are in a rush, go there by 11:45AM as they take pre-orders before they actually open.

This place looks great. super authentic looking food. a lot of people during a weekend lunch time. Unfortunately that was all we did, we just looked. We got in the cafeteria style line, I had ordered the breaded fish filet and rice while my cousin got the goat(chivo) with rice. The goat was in a heated tray so her meal was packed already. Mine came from the back (either to be made or was not stored up front). We waited and we waited (At this point, I was thinking they were actually fishing with a rod out back and having trouble reeling it in). Somehow, my cousins box disappeared. Perhaps it was packed into someone else's order accidentally. After waiting 20 minutes and seeing a whole different crowd go through the restaurant we decided to leave. This place looks promising. One day I hope to get past its looks.

This is definitely the best Indian restaurant in Saint Louis! Every time I try a new dish it becomes my favorite! This time it is Neeraj's delicious tomato soup. It is so rich and the texture is fabulous. The flavor is absolutely perfect and it even tastes good cold! You know it is a great soup when you can enjoy it cold!! I also love the chilli chicken meatballs, keema samosa, sweet corn soup, chicken curry, potato and bell pepper curry, dal soup, sambar, vegetable pakora, tandoori chicken, chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, the kebabs of all kinds, and so many more dishes. Everything is delicious! I love this place and the people are awesome. They really care about their customers and serve us well. The servers are very diligent and will do their best to be sure that you always are pampered. I believe that once you experience this place, it will become your favorite Indian restaurant. See you there! I am in about twice a week for lunch.

Excellent, locally-owned Mediterranean/Middle-Eastern restaurant. The food is at least as good as Ali-Baba's, the local favorite that's more centrally located. A bit pricey, but not unreasonable for the zip code. Very comfortable atmosphere. Even if you just want a coffee to go, a good alternative to the nearby Starbutts.
I love this place. It's one of the only places you can get real Boba Tea and Shaved Ice in the area. We frequent it often and look forward to returning. Plus the staff has a great sense of humor!

My boyfriend and I went once and we loved it! We cannot wait to go back again. The food was absolutely fantastic and the service was great! I highly recommend Thai Orchid for Thai food lovers and for those who want to try it for the first time. You will not be disappointed!
Third time here and as good as always. My favorite drink, Padras, mofongo con churrasco, sorullitos (sulluritos), empanadillas de jueyes, tripleta. Food coma. Excellent as always.

After giving it a few more tries, I'm willing to give it a better review. I think the food is def. passable and the people that work there have also begun to warm up. ON Pardall, you can't expect much, but this is certainly passable in college town.

First time eating here. The food was really great and did not disappoint. I had the tasting menu (chicken, mac and cheese, and a BBQ dipping sauce) while my friend had a sandwich and biscuits and we shared. The chicken was delicious and not too heavy. The biscuits were soooo good. The Southern sandwich with coleslaw was great too. On my way out, I picked up iced coffee and a chocolate chip/peanut butter/brownie cookie concoction which was just perfect. The server taking our order was very friendly and prompt. I will be back soon!!

Food and service excellent! I've been trucking around the states looking for good pho and vietnamese food and this is one of the better places I've gone to so far. The food is more refined than a typical viet restaurant and the way everything is served is more refined. You'll see when you get here. We got the banh bo (hue style) it was delicious.

For informal Vietnamese, you can't beat Pho Hoan Pasteur! I have to admit, I've only eaten the vermicelli here, but I've had it several times and it's the best I've eaten. Same with the bubble tea. Top notch! Staff are friendly and table service is quick.

I had the pleasure of sampling the Gyro at a Food Truck Friday at Tower Grove Park. Since the other reviews cover my views, I'll just ask a burning question that has me confused: If "Gyro" is pronounced "Yee-ro," wouldn't the company be pronounced "Yo! Yee-ro! Yo!"?
Weird small restaurant next to go-kart track in the middle of hotel row near opryland. Food is pretty darn good. Service is pretty darn bad. One surly server but,she's been nice to me. I'm eating!

A favorite place for lunch for our office group. We have been there more times than I can count and we always get the same waitress, Terry. She always knows what everyone eats...no one has to open a menu. One of my favorite places for Chinese food!

The food was extremely tasty for it's price point. I am the happiest woman when I can get chicken tikka under $10 and actually enjoy it. I will definitely return again. I only wish that they delivered past Washington Avenue!!

I'm a nacho addict...and I would never have dreamed that a place called Pita Jungle, which bills itself as a 'healthy food' joint would have the best nachos in town, but it's true. With multi-colored tortilla chips, excellent cheese, beans and a side of tzaziki, it's unusual but totally delicious! Oh, and the pita-type-stuff is pretty decent, too.

I found Bitar's when looking for a Greek restaurant, and the food was great, staff very helpful, but if you dine in, recognize that it isn't a restaurant so much as a Mediterranean grocery with 6 tables to sit at. The only reason they don't get five stars is the setting, great food in a grocery store.

We've been here many times. Only downside is that it's cash only. If you are looking for Thai food that is more authentic than other places, go here! I am told from my Thai friend that the food is more northern style Thai but I can't comment on that. The place is clean and the service is good. There's a large parking lot in the back. Everything I've had there was good except the mango sticky rice dessert. The mango was sour and hard. Other than that, the food great! Try the Laab pork. Soooo good! We keep going back! 5 stars for sure!
Wanted to like it. Has gotten some good reviews. Can't say that it was a positive experience. Not going back.

Finally got to stop in Suraya. I had a hard time deciding if I should go for brunch or dinner. Brunch this time but definitely need to go back for dinner in the near future! Brunch on Saturday and Sunday is table service unlike during the week when it's counter service for breakfast and lunch. There are no reservations for weekend brunch but there are for dinner. We had to wait about 15 minutes but not too bad. The place is beautiful and very spacious. We talked to someone behind the counter that gave us some helpful information about the menu items while we waited. If you are interested in trying the pastries and the very popular rose pistachio cruller, get a pastry basket... they set a certain amount of the crullers aside to include in these baskets. Also at around 1 on Sunday the pastry baskets were running low. So go early for best selection of pastries. Try them! Order the varieties and take them to go! In addition I got a falafel platter. This included spicy fries, hummus, pita, and tabouleh. Everything was delicious. The tehina yogurt was also very tasty. Leftovers were yummy for dinner. Oh and I rarely get specialty drinks while out but the clementine ginger soda was sooo good! Staff was great and personable. Our server was cheerful and fun. Great way to end the weekend, Brunch at Suraya on Sunday!
I had the breakfast tacos and the coconut pancakes. Everything was cooked perfectly, fresh, and delicious. Yum!
Beautiful atmosphere, very peaceful! Waitresses wore beautiful traditional uniforms, and the food was fantastic! Much better than others in the area!

Palace of Asia is the best of the best as North Indian is concerned. The only way to get anything better is to make a trip to Edison/Iselin. They even occasionally have Indo-Chinese on the buffet. I visit other buffets for variety, but POA is my go-to Indian joint.

What a gem! It's super clean, decor is very nice, the waitstaff is very attentive and the most important part, the food is so good! Coming from Boston, I'm not a stranger to Vietnamese food and needed a place that had authentic food. Also after a long night of drinking and I'm Chinese, we typically have something on the lighter side in the morning or lunch and most of the time it consists of something with soup in it, not bacon and butter. Don't get me wrong, love those foods too but not my body! Anyways getting back to this place, we ordered the summer rolls, fresh and moist and you can tell it hasn't been sitting around and it's freshly made, if it were sitting around, the wrapping tends to be a little drier. Then I had to try their pork ham banh mi with extra pâté...hmmm mmmm this sandwich was also made on the spot and the French bread was crusty yet chewy and the ingredients were flavorful and the veggies very fresh. 2 bowls of beef pho and although its a bit on the sweet side, that's what you'd expect since its definitely Saigon style pho. Plenty of meat and scallions ( I'm in love with scallions) noodles were cooked just right. Before we left, I had to take another banh mi to go and boy was it worth it because we ended up drinking again later that night and needed a midnight snack. If anyone has ever needed a late night after drinking snack, a banh mi is the way to go! Prices were cheap, but for food like this, I'd pay double! The waitstaff were very attentive and we got there just as they were opening and by time it was 12, the place was packed to full capacity with many take out orders ( growing up in restaurants, i always notice if a place is busy, its no joke!) Such a nice feeling to be eating where the locals eat, we're going back again today I hope! A must try!
A friend recommended this place and it did not disappoint. We had the pad Thai which was great and the coconut pudding for dessert was the perfect size.
Pretty underwhelming. I didn't get part of my brunch, and the service left a lot to be desired. A shame, because it was a nice space.
First week open and super busy. The Pho is the best I've ever had. So clean and healthy. Try the grape leaf rolls.

Love that this place is opened at 8:30 am to get an Asian breakfast. The full menu is available. Who wouldn't want a pho for breakfast?!? The decor is really nice and you feel your somewhere other than downtown Clearwater. People have complaints about the hours but I'm sure it's due to the area...most traffic comes during lunch. I ordered Vietnamese iced coffee and it was good...used a lot of cream. Also got beef pho.

As far as Thai food goes in Nashville, it's amazing. Best Thai food I've ever had- it's pretty good. Dishes are served family style (big portions) so I recommend sharing. The service was amazing and they are all so nice. I will come back to try different things next time.

First visit was a great experience. The fried dumplings and nice and crispy. The Pho was very clean and flavorful. Only got the regular size, but you can upgrade to a Large for 3 bucks. Ended with a Bubble Smoothie 50/50 which was also solid. We tried both the Taro with Tapioca bubble and Mango with Pearls. Both great flavor and great bubble. Will definitely come back as the prices were decent too.
Wonderful variety Mediterranean menu and huge portions. Attentive service. Highly recommended for family dinners, Romantic dates or group of friends.
Excelente , vinimos de vacaciones y lo probamos . Muy limpio y fueron muy amables . Se lo recomendamos a todos

BEST LUNCH TRUCK EVER. Delicious. So friendly. Learn your order after you come a few times. And the prices are incredible. One star off for being closed when you say you are open! Makes me so sad! Why do you close at 3 pm ?!??! SO SAD.

Man the food was good. I've worked in several fine dining Vegas restaurants with superb meals, and Richards was great. My wife had Alaskan Halibut seasoned great and delicious raviolis. I had love/waygu flat or steak (med rare) and was super tender and flavorful. Just a tip for those who eat steak above med.... Eat burgers. I wish the dessert menu had something to catch my eye but we went somewhere else for that. Only critique I'd say. DRESS CODE. You got a nice dining experience, make people dine. Highly recommended. Don't waste your time at Barbacoa

I met a friend here Friday night at 5:00 and we were the only people in the restaurant. I was shocked. We started with a mojito and a glass of wine. The mojito was fresh and she said the wine was good. We got the guacamole as an appetizer. I thought it was a small portion for $8.00. For entrees I got the Tamal Corn Cakes (thanks to the mouth-watering Yelp pictures) and she got the Pescado Con Poblano Crema. Both of them were very fresh and very good. Good portion size as well. I gave it 4 stars because the waiter was just "meh." He wasn't very enthusiastic nor very cheerful. Flat affect would best describe him. Regardless, the food was good and the price was comparable for Broad Ripple. I will be back for Brunch! Check out the brunch menu before you decide to go for dinner!

We stopped here after A Taste of Pinellas. I agree with other Yelpers that the location of Tryst is great - Downtown St. Petersburg certainly has that South Beach feel. Unfortunately, we also experienced some of that South Beach pretentiousness at Tryst. We stopped in at around 4:45PM on Saturday for a drink. The bar was full and we asked for a table (we also had a kid with us) and the waitress gave us an attitude when we couldn't confirm whether we were ordering food or not - claiming tables are only for customers who eat. Nevertheless she sat us since they had over 6 empty tables. The waiter was attentive, but not very helpful to newcomers. They have a pretty large list of beverages and shifting through it was a bit difficult. My fellow diners ordered their $10 Banana Bread beer and a mixed cocktail. I went with Sea Dog Blueberry beer $5.50. The beer was good - nice and cold on a hot Florida day. We decided to order the Ceviche which was...$18? It took forever for our Ceviche to arrive at our table. We joked that they must have gone fishing for the fish because normally that dish is a quick creation. When it finally came out it was served in a small martini glass with hardly enough fish for one person. The ingredients were certainly fresh, but for $18 I expect much more than veggies and a little fish. It wasn't worth the price and it gave me too much of a reminder of dining in Miami and seeing a California Roll for $40. The shrimp cocktail appetizer (also $18) my sister's fiance ordered fared no better and was also an arm and a leg in price. The bill for 2 beers, a cocktail, and two small appetizers? $72+tip. No thanks!
Absolutely delicious dinner !!!! Unbelievable service. It is just a wonderful place to have dinner. Everything we have tried was perfect.

Everything at this restaurant is incredible, from the food to the service to the price. Both the manager and the head chef stopped out to check in and make sure everything was okay. The food was mind blowingly delicious, with shockingly low prices for the area. This is going to be a regular spot for us.

Loved this place! The people were nice and the pho was delicious! It was a decent pho place especially coming from the SD/Irvine area. If you are looking for a pretty good pho place this is the one for you!

While I've found tapas menus that I like better, I really don't have anything bad to say about the menu. The steak over spinach is my favorite here, and they make a good gyro that I've picked up carry out for lunch a few times. The decor is cozy. I like that there is a bar space, couch area, patio and booths in a slightly more private area. My biggest complaint is I could do without the belly dancer who suddenly appears in the evenings. The music is way too loud, cutting off conversation, and having dancer come over to your table uninvited is intrusive. I would rather just eat my food and enjoy the conversation with my dinner companions. The staff is friendly and attentive too...quickly taking my order when I wander in and want carry out. They don't have a parking lot, but it's easy enough to find a spot within a block. But I really don't have an excuse for driving there since I live just blocks away.

Right now, they're experimenting with the menu, so it's a cheesesteak quesedilla, a pineapple/rotissarie chicken quesadillia, their famous Cap'n Crunch Burrito, and a veggie thing (sorry, my eyes were on the Burrito!) for now. At six bucks a piece, you can't lose! (BTW, one of the guys is experimenting with deep fried dried long hot peppers. If you like hot, you like crunch, these can be addictive. There's not a lot right now, because it's time intensive to get them dried just right. Try them while you can!)

Zorba's is easily my favorite Greek spot in the city. On top of having a great location in fairmount with plenty of outdoor seating, they deliver FOR FREE! And the delivery is super fast. Here's what to order if you need some suggestions: Cold apps appetizer- sampler of all their cold apps and every single one is amazing, it comes with pita Saganaki (if dining in) - fried halloumi cheese so it's guaranteed deliciousness For vegetarians: umam baldi- stuffed eggplant comes with a side of rice, veggies and potatoes I don't know what they put in their veggies and potatoes but they're the yummiest veggies and potatoes you'll eat For meat eaters: the octopus platter or the charcoal grill sampler And finally PLEASE eat the baklava. It's amazing and everything you'll ever want.

I thought this place would be super awesome, but I was wrong. Atmosphere was actually good; not too crowded nor empty. Customers walked in and out while we were eating there. Our server was almost friendly, she didn't smile that much but she wasn't that bad either. I ordered Pho combo Lg, shrimp paste wrapped around sugar cane, iced coffee, and Thai pudding. Being an Asian who lived in SoCal for over 14 years, I had eaten lots of awesome and nasty Vietnamese food. Their Pho was just ALRIGHT!! The soup didn't smell good nor convince me at all. The coffee was okay, nothing special. The shrimp pasted didn't impress or anything. Overall, it was okay. Definitely not going back even if there is only one in the area.
Two words. Grilled. Octopus. 'nuff said. And try to get Sammy as your waiter 'cause he's the best.

Have great selection of pho and taste great. The broth is tasty. Downside is the service. They don't stick to hours posted and they try to rush people out. Pho takes time to enjoy and I do not like burning my mouth. Please stick to the hours posted or change them.

Would not return even if they were giving food away. Never in my life ever experience a place that loud. The servers could not talk, they had to scream to be heard. My chair was bumped so many times by the servers and the customers. Could not wait to leave.
The restaurant is full of delicious Indian food. You have always had a wonderful time there the kids love it the buffet is outstanding.

Loved it! Here on vacation we found this spot on yelp. Went in for an early dinner and people were pouring in by 5 pm. On a Monday! My husband had the strip steak. He loved it. Cooked perfectly. With amazing sides. He's one of those guys that if a place has a great review he hates it. But not here. He loved! One of the best meals he has had in a long time. (And we are from a major city and eat out way too much!) Service was great. Ppl were so friendly. I'm so glad we found this place. They have amazing early bird specials. We had to idea so it was def a happy surprise!

I love you Remedy Cafe. I love your Veitnamese Ice Coffee and your Masala and your homemade Chai! I love your chilled out atmosphere and your late evening hours. I also love your take home food! I always feel at home with you and I miss you when we are not together. I think I'll start spending more time with you.....we both deserve it.

Great food as always. Come here for the tortilla soup and fish tacos. Love the atmosphere! Servers are always friendly and fast. Food is fresh. Katherine is very friendly and attentive. Kids are welcome here. Sure they will enjoy the fried bananas and flan!!! Love this place will always come back! Been here at least 3x and every single time I order something different. Never disappointed! Music is great too.

The scenery is nice. That's about it. I was not a fan of the food at all. Fish and chips was on the specialties section of the menu. I don't know why. They weren't terrible, they were just no different than anywhere else. French fries were good though! We had calamari for an app and it was nothing special. Disappointed in the food. I was hoping for something better than any bar could make. I guess I paid those prices for the view of the gulf? And what's up with having to pay for water?!?!

Its very upsetting how in the middle of the afternoon delivery of 2 small dishes has taken one hour and 40 minutes.... and we are still WAITING!! Not only that but in the comments I asked for fried noodle chips IF POSSIBLE and they changed my order charging me 2 dollars for them. I would not have wanted them if they didn't come with the soup which was expected. Still have not received the food, but can only imagine I am going to be even more disappointed when it gets here. We order Chinese about 3 days a week and they have lost our business before we even tried their food. Update: Food has gotten here and to NO surprise its cold and uncooked. You had two hours to cook the food how is it uncooked? NEVER EVER EVER EVER AGAIN! Forgot all utensils, our soda, and duck sauce which I asked for in 3 separate places. I'M SICK! PLEASE DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE!

I am really picky with Indian food, so bear with me here. The prices here were reasonable, and the service was pretty good. The problem is, I like my Indian food when it's a blend of savory, spicy, and sweet. Sadly, Shere Punjab just doesn't have that sweetness I'm looking for. I got the same thing I get at any Indian restaurant -- chicken tikka masala -- and usually the dish has some sweetness to it. This dish was more savory and salty than I have come to expect, and I've eaten a lot of chicken tikka masala! My wife, the vegetarian, had the shahi paneer, and had a similar complaint -- although the cheese was plentiful and had the right consistency, it just didn't taste sweet. They also didn't have Peshwari/Kashmeeri naan, a sweet naan with nuts and dried fruit. Maybe the owners don't like sweet things? Not everyone is going to want that sweetness in their Indian, and if you don't want that then this place is probably going to do more for you than it did me. But it's just not my cup of tea.

Loved this place, food and services were great. We had a group of 5 and we were seated straight away, waitress was very attentive and friendly. I had the chicken and lemon grass which was very nice. Everyone was very happy with all their meals. Fairly priced as well.

Panang curry was amazing. I ordered pork medium spicy. It was very good and had just enough kick to it. I had a glass of the plum wine they carry with my meal. Very good stuff! Inside is a bit small for seating. It holds more people than it looks like it should, but they do have outside seating when its nice out. This will be the go to place when I'm in town.

Dmitri's is another one of those "must go there while home" places I never miss on a trip. The octopus is done perfectly, and the fish selection is always fresh and fabulous. Philly just doesn't get much better than this, friends.

Gave it a try.. not for me. I thought the food was bland, especially the SOS. Irks me when a place uses canned sweet peppers meant for a hoagie or sandwich and puts em in my omelette. Completely ruined it for me. Service was good.
I have been to Thailand and have had authentic Thai food, and this is exactly that. A taste of Thailand in stl. Highly recommend it!

This place is a magical and full of wonder, amazment and delicious food! My wife and I made it to our reservation early only to find a line out the door with the host letting people in as people left because the place was jammed packed! I immediately knew we were on to something special. He was very quick to seat us it seemed like, in front of a lot of the people making us feel special and vip. We climbed up to the third floor through a narrow stairwell to find an intimate room with seating only for 4 couples. We had brought our own alcohol that was served to us with a smile. You can choose not to bring and just order if you prefer. We had to wash our hands before we started on the first course because there was no silverware to use, only our freshly cleaned hands. Each of the 7 courses were amazing and the service was also exceptional. I would recommend everyone to visit if you are in Philly!
Went there during my stay in New Orleans, the staff is super friendly and the food was really good. I had the spicy tofu/rice noddle yummy. I'd recommend this to place to anyone

The La Va panini (tuna with hot sauce) is quite good, but the coffee is pretty terrible. The space is always jam-packed and isn't really conducive to a productive afternoon. Worst of all, though, are the blank-faced, seemingly disdainful baristas. Some of the male baristas are perfectly nice, but the female baristas (and I hate saying this about my fellow females, believe me) - watch out, you will get ATTITUDE.

As soon as we were finished our main meal, my husband said, I'm definitely coming back here again!" The service was amazing, so pleasant and attentive. The food was delicious! For people who are hesitant to try new foods, I would highly recommend this place b/c the cuisine isn't too overpowering, but it has many subtle flavors, at least in the meals we ordered. We started with the Aashak, which were these steamed dumplings with meat sauce. I don't eat beef, so I did not partake, but my husband seemed to like them. I ordered the Badenjan Chalow (chunks of chicken and eggplant, cooked with tomatoes, onions, garlic and spices. Served with white basmati rice) I wish I could recreate this at home. The chicken was so juicy and tender and the basmati rice was perfectly cooked, not mushy at all. He ordered Ariana Kabob (lamb, chicken, and beef on two char-grilled skewers. Served with brown basmati rice) and seemed to enjoy every minute of it. Also, it's BYO!

Came to Philly for the night and decided to explore South St. After walking for a bit we came across this restaurant and decided to try it out. The waitresses were friendly and decided to accept us 5 minutes before closing, and as a result, the service was extremely fast. Besides having a central and navigable location, the restaurant presented a clean and traditional Afghan environment upon walking through the door. I ordered the Qurma Chalaw, a chicken or lamb dish with traditional rice and chutney sauce. The lamb was absolutely delicious and I would highly recommend.

The worst sushi I've had and I love Florida sushi when I visit from California. Fish was so beyond fishy, didn't taste fresh. Even smelled fishy. I ate my meal and was instantly sick after. Management didn't really care what so ever that our food was not fresh and just kept telling me it was fresh. It absolutely was not. Thank you for the stomach ache and terrible service from management. Maybe that's why our table was the only table there...

Heard about this place for years, finally went today for lunch. $7.50 for a Gyro with feta is a little steep considering the quality and the size. I used to live in Chicago and this was sub-par and more expensive than I'm used to. 10 minutes to get my food. No clue what could have taken that long. You just slice the meat and put all of the ingredients in a pita. Jesus. There wasn't even a line when I ordered. No water cups. No reason to go back.

This is as good as it gets. By far, the best Indian food that I have had. Me and friends wanted to try this place out after reading reviews online. This was not a disappointment at all. The drinks are amazing, especially the nimbu paani. The taste of the food is very authentic as well. I have been surprised how finding good Indian food in Philly has been difficult. This place takes care of that problem. The menu is limited (7-8 options per course, except desserts), but very delicious. Do try bhelpuri and chana chaat, Mumbai masala nimbu paani and the flan. Vegetarians have very limited main course options though. The place is very small and I would suggest going well ahead in time because there is a wait time. We had to wait for 30 min to be seated for our dinner. Sadly, the service is a tad bit slow. Nevertheless, this place is amazing
Check it this spot! if you are looking for that good rice! The food is great and the egg rolls are delicious......I had the sweet & sour chicken combo and it was sooo goooood! Check them out today!

My friend decided to go eat at Mint today and I have always heard of Mint Modern so I always wanted to come try this place out. So today is my first time trying out Mint modern. Our waitress was nice, friendly & really pretty. She came to check on us about the food, refilled our drinks and talked to us in the end when one of our friend didn't finished his food. I forgot what he ordered though, sorry about that. We ordered two orders of the pork belly tacos, two orders of sticky wings and two orders of sweet fried shrimp (I think that's what it's called) for appetizers. The appetizers were amazingly good. Pork belly tacos were on point, the wings were good & HOT, and I'm not too fond of shrimp, but that shrimp was good. Also, the sauce for the shrimp was delicious. For the entrees,we ordered the Sizzle Beef steak & eggs, Kim chi burger, lemongrass chicken & the shaken beef. Everything was great. My friends said their food were good and they are all of it. So, going back to my friend who didn't finish his food. He ordered something with noodles & soup, but the noodles were way too cooked so it was soft and kept breaking apart each time he picked it up. However, he did say that the broth and everything else was good.

This is my second review for Phamous. I popped in for my usual bahn mi binge yesterday and I am never disappointed. I was with a party of 10 and the service was supreme from the servers being attentive to our orders coming out in a timely manner. As I returned to Yelp to write a second review, I couldn't help but notice the many comments regarding the "plain" broth, so I thought I would focus my review on that to give my perspective (you don't have to agree with me) as I've had pho here many times (just not yesterday). First off, I am not an expert on pho nor am I Vietnamese, but I've tried pho all over California from various restaurants, family, and friends from various ethnic backgrounds (yes, not only Vietnamese make pho) and I also make my family's version of pho quite often at home. What I will say is that I am very familiar with the variations of pho and ingredients that make for different types of broth. The first thing that people should know is that there are two main variations of broth, one from the Northern regions of Vietnam, and one from the Southern region. What' the difference? Northern pho typically focuses on more plain and simple broth. Southern pho typically has more bold flavor. Many pho eaters are served Southern style broth the majority of the time. Ever wonder if Phamous might be sticking to the traditions of Northern style pho? My pho, for example, fits in with neither of the two as it has tremendously rich broth by use of ox tail and beef bones, something I am sure the average pho eater has never heard of or tasted. Maybe because I make the broth personally, I see pho broth on a spectrum from plain to rich with different pho places like Phamous falling in between. I hope this may help to explain why this broth may seem simple compared to others.

This place has some really good food but terrible service. Honestly it's some of the best Pakistani food I have ever had but the owner is extremely rude. I came here one time with my father. When we walked around 8pm, the owner told us (in a very rude way) that he closes at 9. He seemed preoccupied while taking our order. A group of 3 people walked in and he completely cut us off to greet them and seat them. He eventually made up for his rude attitude and was being friendly. The food was amazing so I gave it a second chance and brought my husband. This time he was rude again. We came in at 7 45 and he told us he closes at 8 30, even though online, on the menu, and on the door it says it closes at 9. He rushed us to eat. While I love his food, my husband was extremely unimpressed. The amount of food is very little for the high prices and his attitude and rudeness make it not worth coming here anymore. Also, he gives special offers for good reviews on yelp. And he told us he needs us to write a good review.

One of my latest addictions has been vietnamese food. No matter what part of the city I'm in - it seems to be easy to find, light and delicious. Luckily, I live downtown, and Thahn Son is one of my most favorite places to go. The restaurant itself is a dive - old furniture, sparsely decorated with a few dying plants and some faded wallpaper. It's run by a family and I love them - the husband is always smiling and always working and the wife is one of the nicest most hospitable women I've ever met. Definitely don't come for the atmosphere - much like many other restaurants in Edmonton, this place is a hidden gem. No flash, but great food. I love all the vermicelli bowls and their 5-color vermicelli is my favorite - lots of great meat and an amazing price. My boyfriend always goes for the Pho and it never disappoints. The spicy beef soup is the perfect blend of spices and comfort, and it's cheap at $6 a bowl. I also love the spring rolls and the salad rolls, all hand made and very fresh. The service is consistently good and the food has been great every time I've been in - even at 9PM at night. Don't let the location and appearance of the restaurant fool you - if you like great vietnamese food, you'll like Thahn Son.

This place is the bomb! Veggie green curry and Thai iced is my usual order but everything is delicious. The curry is surprisingly spicy and rich in flavor. The guys working the counter are super friendly and the food is always ready, hot, and delicious.. a must if you're in queen village area!
Hummus deluxe was awesome. Ask for more bread though. Roasted cauliflower is an underrated sleeper. It was fantastic. It is served warm, but can cool quickly on the bread. Eat quickly!
Great place for curry dishes, they customize the spice to your liking. Staff is always friendly and atmosphere is calming. All in all, a great little Thai restaurant.
this is my favorite place to get pasta. i love their penne! i am a huge fan of pasta, so i love to come here and treat myself. plus, the inside is super cute and the strip mall isn't too busy at all.

Recently moved to the area from So. Cal. and this place is awesome. Perfect sunset spot with spectacular views. Comfortable chairs. Had the blackened Mahi and it was cooked perfect. Grilled veggies with an awesome seasoning. Rice was meh, but I didn't need it anyway. Came with some of the best clam chowder I have ever had. Angel was our waiter and he was great! Offered great suggestions and talked about the history of the place. Nice little tiki bar on the side for while you are waiting on a table. Definately will be going back. There was a management presence and it showed!!

I can honestly say that everything my family and I ordered here was delicious. It tasted fresh, was brought to our table quickly, and the drinks were even free that day. We had the chicken quesadilla kids meal, the veggie pita pizza and the chicken pita pizza. I especially liked the veggie pizza and the salsa that came with the quesadilla, but I'll say it again, everything was delicious. I'm so pleased to have found a place that provides a relatively healthy, affordable, and fast meal near my house!

You know, strip mall dining takes a lot of abuse but when you find a place this awesome, it makes up for the bad experiences. If you've never experienced Ethiopian cuisine, be prepared to step out of your comfort zone. Silverware is not used and it's not even needed. They have a good selection of meat as well as vegetarian dishes. We went with the vegetarian sampler which is unbelievably big. Just take the left overs to the drive-in movie like we're doing tonight. It was very cold in there and I'm not sure if that is normal so you might want to prepare for it. It is 57 degrees in Addis Ababa as I'm writing this review and that's probably what it was in the restaurant. I guess that helps with the authenticity!
Yelp and their website both say open on Sunday. Drove across town based on reviews and they were closed. Won't come back.

While I enjoyed the experience of the falafel truck, I wasn't blown away by the food. The line really does take a long time, but we enjoyed the soup to hold us through our wait on a cold and windy day. I'm vegetarian and was given basically an assortment of sides. The falafel was good, but not as good as Mama's Vegetarian. Then I had a somewhat sweet pasta salad with grilled grapes and two kinds of bread that had been heated on the charcoal in the truck so long that they were overwhelmingly smokey. I always enjoy the smell of the truck as I walk by, and I will probably give it another try, but I'm guessing the food is better if you get the chicken.

This was our first time having Ethiopian food. I brought my three kids for them to experience something different. We live in the NE area so the restaurant was a bit of a drive but it was worth it. The food was very good and the kids enjoyed eating with their hands. Overall we had a good experience and it speaks a lot when my 11, 17 and 19 yo kids enjoyed the food and experience.

This is my favorite restaurant in downtown St. Pete. I've been pleased every time I've been there; I was there four days ago, and I didn't think they had "cut back" at all. The toppings are fresh and are unlimited. Just tell the staff what toppings you want, and they'll keep loading up your sandwich. I'm a vegetarian and am delighted by all the choices. Staff is friendly and accommodating. Don't miss this one. It's really a nice change from all the other places downtown. Prices are very reasonable, too.

I've been coming here a few times a week for the past few weeks. The atmosphere is chill and is very conducive for a casual date or a study session. Their coffee here is very good (I don't know much about coffee) by my standards. They have pretty bomb breakfast food and their homemade hot sauce is pretty tasty to boot. Only con is that power outlets are at a premium... a majority of my trips have been study related and charging my phone can be a challenge. Overall, this is my staple neighborhood coffe joint!

Palace of Asia is a journey: it transports me to another world and time-- the food and ambiance is classic royal Indian. I know my review sounds more like a drooling poem over their food... but Palace of Asia addicts will know why. I've been a loyal fan of this place since its prior incarnation as Bombay Cuisine. When Palace of Asia bought out this place, I was very dismayed.. but over time, they restored the classic ambiance of before and brought new charms of the very popular Palace of Asia branches. So it certainly won us over. The food is superb and sublime, to say the least. I am especially fond of their saag paneer (spanich cream) and paneer veg (cheese cube curry). Unlike most Indian cooking, the food is not heavy or greasy-- nor in the other edge- mild or bland. It is fresher and lighter with the true authentic Indian spicing touch. I find this combination of authentic spicing blend with lightness rather rare, actually, among Indian cooking. Their lunch buffets and dinner outings by the Cooper River is a highlight. Extensive and the best buffet ever. Being a vegetarian, I love the variety. My non-veg friends love this place too. The best part is eating by the Cooper River, a charming area of this city. Palace of Asia is famous with its many branches.. but this one holds a charm of its own. The service is warm.. they treat everyone like family. They remember what you like and want.. and go out of their way to please you next time. They cater the menu to what we like.. as we often do take outs to eat by the river. I found some photos on their websites, which I posted. Note on the photos: I got it from their website before they revamped their place-- they did remodeling, and it's a lot more luxurious. But I think the window views of the park is the same gorgeous Cooper River, luckily. :) It does close a bit early, even on weekends (10:30 PM)-- that's not nice. And it's a bit far away located in a silent almost hidden area, but that's plus in my view- like getting away from it all.
This wad one of ther best Thai restaurants I've been to. The food was great, great service and beautiful presentation. I'll be back

Went here with my husband on a Friday night . We ordered chicken 65 which was fantastic,; the chicken was full of flavor and very tender; it was great. Also, the garlic naan was very good, we have to go back for it. my husband ordered the hakka noodles they were so tasty. They gave us a complimentary dessert which was rasmalai [fresh cheese balls soaked in sweet milk syrup] this dessert was delicious. Must go here, this place is a great welcome to this community. Service was VERY professional.

This was out third experience at this restaurant. The first time we went they had an a la cart menu and I loved everything I ate! The branzino was delicious and so was the shared appetizer platter. The staff is very sweet and helpful though inexperienced. The second time we ate inside to see the belly dancer on a Saturday night. She was really awesome and the atmosphere was great! However there was no more a la cart menu and you had to choose a $45 or $35 prix fix. Sadly the branzino was in the $45 one so we all choose the $35 instead. As stated by other reviewers the food was extremely bland and the chicken was overcooked and tasteless. The staff was lovely and the coffee and baklava was great! Tried it for dining under the stars last night and was even more disappointed. Service was extemely slow but our server was so nice and apologetic. The apps as usually were great but the main dishes were bland and tasteless. They need to spice it up!!! Also the coffee was awful but the manager/owner was sweet and offered to make us another pot. I will still go back because the staff is so nice but hope they read this review and aren't afraid to give us true morracan flavors!!! Take a hint from some of your local competitors! We can take the heat!!!
Best chicken salad anywhere! Put it on a pita with some cheese. YUM!

Place was beyond dead, and yet service was still negligent and slow. Took ten minutes to get water and an additional ten to get extra napkins. Aside from service, the food is satisfying and flavorful, at least the entree was... the sides were sub par, the potatoes and cauliflower being under cooked and over cooked respectively. Side note: The kitchen was WAY too loud for literally having only two occupied tables.

Great lunch buffet; food is tasty and lots of authentic options. My second time here and becoming a favorite. The chicken tikka is fantastic, spiced and marinated well and cooked perfect. The various options are fun for an adventurous eater.

Really enjoyed trying this place out for lunch with a friend! The staff was EXTREMELY friendly and very attentive. We had basically everyone in the restaurant ask us how our meal was going. Their version of a Bloody Mary is to die for! I'm a huge bloody fan and it did not disappoint. The Pho was really good and they didn't skimp out on the meat! It honestly was too much for me though, more of a sharing dish. The calamari you must try it was some of the best I've had and so different. My friend tried the Lobster sandwich that he really enjoyed (although he's picky and wants lots of lobster) but he said it was on his top 3 for sure! But great date spot or lunch spot the inside decor is very chic. You won't regret checking them out :)

I decided to check this place out because of the rave reviews I've heard from my friends. I did enjoy the delicious falafel with everything on it. I also like the fact that they grill their falafel instead if frying them. However, the service was awful. The guy who took my order was acting like someone stole his blankie! Minus the poor service I would still go back. Who knows? Maybe he was just having a bad day.

Very Good Food and exceptional Service. Very Friendly owner! You can tell people around the area come here and eat often. We were passing by and saw the reviews and stopped in. Good food fast with clean Ambiance.
Amazing food. Probably the best Jamaican restaurant in New Jersey . It has very good service, and the employees are very kind. I personally loved the curry chicken.

I came here for lunch buffet on a Saturday. All food was fresh and hot, and service was great. They were very friendly to my (small) children who were trying Indian food for the first time. All of the dishes tasted unique with great spicing. At some Indian restaurants the spices taste similar in every dish, but not here. I ate way too much!

The service was friendly and the atmosphere was nice, but the food was very average. I met people here for brunch, so I can only speak to that meal. The portions were on the smaller side, and everything is severely under seasoned. The food wouldn't be worth eating without adding your own salt and pepper. The waffles another person got in my party we're quite undercooked, or rather one piece was cooked and the other was anemic looking. Coffee could have been warmer as well.

Went at 12pm on a Friday with my office colleagues. I love Middle East food. It's a small decent place. I ordered Chicken Shawarma in Pita with Baba Ganouj (too good) and Harissa (very hot excellent) and fries (will not order again). Taste- I like it. Will definitely come again. Price- It's for $7.25. Worth it. Quantity- full filling satisfies your tummy Areas of improvement- the food was little cold. Should have been warm. They add just 1 spoon of Harissa which is at the top. Once you reach the middle portion it's gone. Ask to put a little more. The fries $2.25 are okayish you can make fresh and warm at home.

I went with a group of 8 friends, all middle aged professionals. The waitress didn't put in half the order and when we asked her what was going on, she kept saying it wasn't her fault. The manager came over and tried to get things straightened out. She did a good job and had great customer service but people had waited almost an hour for their food. Then the owner came over and escalated the situation. His first words were, "I hear you want to talk to me." He was very rude, condescending and confrontational. We will never visit this business again nor any other business he owns.

The food here is fantastic and you will find items on the menu you cannot easily find elsewhere. Great for vegetarians and carnivores alike. I had a visitor from out of town who was a vegetarian and had health issues that limited what food she could eat, Pita Jungle had plenty of options for her. Another plus is the kids meals. They treat children with more respect than most restaurants who act like the child is a necessary evil to get the parents business. Their children meals reflect this. Some restaurants you will get a hot dog and fries. Here the meal is plentiful and healthy. Best children's menu we have ever seen.

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would! Absolutely delicious, very affordable and super healthy. Spring rolls are amazing and fresh, I've tried the shrimp, the pork and also the lemongrass chicken. Perfect for a light lunch. I sometimes get the veggies and broth to go and add my own leftover pork loin or chicken. The beef brisket pho is off the chain, a large will easily feed 2.

Do not order the coconut soup! It's a very sweet watery version of what it should really taste like. It was so bad that I sent it back and ordered the eggplant tempura appetizer. The eggplant was better but nothing special. I only ate a small portion and told them to take the rest away. I ordered the Hot Basil Shrimp as my entree and it was OK but not spicy at all. The shrimp seemed like they were previously frozen and not as fresh as I expected. I was a little disappointed with this entree but it was edible. I felt as if the service was super slow. I waited longer than I usually wait in a Thai restaurant to receive my food. When I finally received it, I was disappointed it wasn't all that great. There was no good reason for the long wait as the restaurant was not crowded. Waited a long time pay my bill too. The wood carvings on the tables and chairs are unique but I wasn't too impressed with them. I would have preferred better food over the carved wood furniture. I don't plan to ever return and will have to continue my search for a very good Thai restaurant in the Tampa/Brandon area.

Surprisingly good Thai restaurant in a strip mall area. The dishes we ordered are very flavorful. We order the red curry, pad thai, and pinapple fried rice which are normal dishes in thai cuisine but they did a very good job with the flavors.
Lunch was delicious, I can't wait to try dinner.

I was traveling from the northeast and found Thai house on Yelp. I rolled in, was able to order quickly at the window, and had my order in less than 10 minutes to take back to my hotel. I got the penang curry with beef. Wow! And, for dessert, I ordered the Black Rice pudding. It was not what I expected but in a good way. I loved it! My only complaint was that I wish they included utensils (or at least asked if you needed them).

"A Kick in the Lips" And that's just the description for the low end of the heat spectrum. At Thai Orchid you can dial it up for "tingling sensation" or ratchet it all the way to a "raging fire." However you like it, Thai Orchid is perfectly tuned to even the most discriminating tastes. I recommend the Thai Dumplings (pork, bamboo shoot, black mushroom, sesame soy sauce), Tom Yum with chicken, Tutti Frutti Duck (crispy and tender, with a sublime raspberry and Chambord sauce), and masterful Thai Eggplant with chicken and garlic. Whatever you get, you can't help but to enjoy asking for your favorites by name, when the names are like these: Fortune Bag Crying Tiger Evil Jungle Princess Heavenly Curry (who can dispute a name like that?) Love & Passion Lady's Slipper After your entree, settle back into a ice cream dessert with the power to produce multiple thunderous lady orgasms. Service is efficient, calm, and never rushed. Eating on the railed platform makes the experience extra fun, delivering the kind of surreal thrill you get when stepping onto a (Thai) Tilt a Whirl. The only thing more surreal is exiting this palace of pleasure onto a blank strip mall parking lot.

Ok the lemon chicken soup is awes me!!! Wow I am from New York City , and this is damned good !!soup was FULLof chunks of chicken and spices . We also had a Greek salad and it was as huge proportion and fresh nothing wilted . Great service and clean very clean.
Quiet venue, fast service. Nice puri, lamb. Mushrooms super too. Goat a bit bony but when not? Service excellent.

It's a good thing they are at a great location with a great view because the service is terrible and the food is just ok. The first time I went, I sat in the corner of the bar to get a view of the sunset. There was definitely drama going on between the bartenders and the wait staff. The bartenders openly complained to me about individual wait staff and continued to talk poorly about them behind their backs. The second time I went, the bartender served one beer and asked me to close out because it was the end of her shift even though I was running a tab. She also asked a couple the same thing as they ordered their meal. The third time, I called ahead to check hours on Christmas Eve. The person on the phone said they were closing at 6. I got there at 4 and was only told, "we are closing now. You got some bad information." No apology, just a rude tone. They do have cheap beers and a beautiful sunset view. I keep going back for these, hoping the service will get better. So far, it hasn't...

Sigh. I miss Bui's. I've graduated from Penn and am now many miles away and I still find myself dreaming about bacon egg and cheese with extra Bui's sauce. For the record, Bui's sauce is the only way to go, don't let the saltpeppaketchup camp tell you otherwise. For $3.50, this deal absolutely cannot be beat. Until we meet again, Bui...

Truly enchanting. None other like. English fails for the words necessary to describe my continuing, wonderful experiences at this establishment. I shall, however, attempt: I've been a fan of Ethiopian cuisine since I was a child, and being a flight attendant, have enjoyed this type of dining all over the nation. I can truly say, since I've been going to Abyssinia since the day they opened, no one in the U.S. can beat their quality, flavor, generosity, charm nor price. Even if you think you don't like 'curried' foods or spicy fair, you owe it to yourself to indulge in Abraham's creations. But, bring your appetite, because apparently it's against the law to leave there hungry. You'll not regret the experience. Cheers

When I'm feeling Vietnamese and I happen to be Cherry Hill, it's gotta be Pho 38. Especially great for takeout, if you can resist the delicious smells on the way home. I do not recommend trying to eat a fresh bowl of pho in a moving vehicle. Fast, friendly service. Quality, fresh food. Huge servings. I can't resist their huge, well-packed summer rolls! Banh mi is one of the things they do best (although I haven't tried everything on their extremely expansive menu, of course!). They're made with love here. And then there are those days when you just want to dive into a huge bowl of pho. Pho, pho, pho. They don't skimp on the fixins here! More recently, I had their bun. Their lemongrass sauce has a bit of a kick, and they put a variety of vegetables for toppings.

Remedy's a great place to hang out and enjoy a bite to eat. I love the atmosphere here, very laidback and fun, and the food and drinks are excellent. They just got a very nice new paint job as well :)

I am one of those that have lived in Philly for years and has heard all the rave about Dmitri's and never made the trip into Queen Village (4 blocks from my house!). I was not disappointed! The food was amazing, the service is speedy, and if you are not the waiting around type (there are no reservations allowed), put your name in at the door, head across the street to New Wave, have a beer or two, and they will come get you when your table is available. I will say if you aren't prepared to wait 40-50 minutes, eat in a relatively loud and boisterous environment, and come out smelling like grilled seafood, this isn't the place for you. As for me, all these things remind me of meals I used to eat with my family at home on LBI, so I thoroughly enjoy this atmosphere. Our group of four started our meal out with 3 appetizers, the tomato and Mozzarella Salad, Hummus, and Olive and Feta plate. All were large portions and I wish we had only ordered 2 between us, as it was a little too much food. Every one was amazing - the best was the Hummus, with the Caresse Salad in a close second. If I could pick one to pass on it would have been the Feta and Olives. For my main course, I had the Seafood Linguine, the seafood was plentiful, large, fresh shrimp with the tails already cleaned off, clams, muscles, and a white buttery broth. My only comment about this dish was I wish they would ease up on the broth, it overcooked the pasta by the time I was halfway through the dish. My husband got the grilled salmon, which came plated with rice and steamed escarole. It was perfectly cooked and seasoned, one of the best pieces of salmon I have tasted while dining out in Philadelphia. Our friends ordered the grilled scallops and they couldn't have been more perfectly cooked and seasoned as well. Most of these dishes come plated with a hefty portion of rice and escarole.

I'm not a fan at all. Not one little bit. What a waste of 40$. Not going here again. The food was cold, flavourless. The salad rolls were just textured warm and yucky. The greatest thing we got was our Coca Cola.

Went there for their "burger night" and was seriously disappointed with this place ! The burger my friend and I had amounted to just the bun, cheese, and a few mushrooms. We had the cauliflower burger and actually had to open up the sandwich to see if there was anything there...What we both saw was indeed a tiny amount of cauliflower that was burnt crisp. We both left hungry and wondered what the heck happened to this place ....It used to be good but I really can't see myself returning to this place again. The waiter seemed very distracted and not all that helpful....The thing is......there were only several people in the entire place....I guess others have found out that this place sucks and perhaps the management will get a clue to step it up or lose all of its business.

Dissapointed due to the fact that we were led to believe that they would be open until 12 am in the morning. We took a fifteen dollar ride there to be ignored by their closing staff. Left in the rain we left broken and wet from the rain.
Great authentic Dominican food. El mofongo estaba ricisimo y tienen mucho para escojer. La salsa al ajillo was delicious. Will come back con frequencia.

My favorite at this restaurant is the Lamb/Beef Gyro Plate. If you are used to a Gyro plate at the typical Greek restaurant, this is going to be different. It is a step above the typical Greek, both in ingredients and taste. This place is alive on the weekends, unlike most other similar restaurants. The live music is usually very good and a nice touch for an affordable restaurant. The Gyro plate comes with a side salad which is small, but excellent. Everything is very fresh including the mixed greens, veggies, sheep's cheese and peppers. The Gyro beef/lamb mixture is not shaved, but is very tasty. It goes well with the rice and the Tzatziki sauce. Their Tzatziki is made from Cow's milk, to which I am allergic. However, they have a non-dairy Tzatziki which is very, very good. If they did not tell me that it was non-dairy, I would have never known. This is a great place for a quick meal or an impromptu dinner date with your spouse. If you find yourself hungry in Green Hills, give this place a try. I recommend it!

Nashville has amazing food all around however this place was by far my favorite. I think I had the trout, whipped feta hummus, Brussels, bacon wrapped dates, and a drink. Everything was amazing. My server/bartender was 1. A FLY CHICK. her look was everything 2. She was Knowledgeable about everything on the menu. I don't like cheese but whipped feta was absolutely amazing. If you are in Nashville this place is a MUST. I wish there was one of these closer and to me.

Great vegetarian options! Nearly every dish can be made with either silken or hard marinated tofu. My family just loves the food here. We usually get Chang's Spicy Tofu and Singapore Street noodles. Both are great.
