good food, great service, reasonably priced. descriptions of all food on the menu. friendly welcoming people. will definitely be back!

This is our go-to in the area. We have never had a bad meal from them on delivery and they are possibly the nicest people I have ever dealt with at a takeout place. They are so upbeat EVERY time we call and I swear I'm cracking up after I hang up because it's almost comical how nice they are! Whenever we order they always tell us 45-50 minutes and it typically comes within 20-30 minutes. Also, the roti canai is beyond amazing - but honestly all the food is so good!
Had the pad see-ew last night. About two hours later it was evident I had food poisoning. It's been a miserable 24 hours........ never, ever again.......

Parking was a bit of a challenge, and there was a bit of a mixup with our order so the soup came much later than the food, but it was worth it. I ordered spanakopita and roasted red pepper soup... Both delicious. My husband ordered baked feta and loved it. Nice atmosphere and friendly server with delicious food. We will come back to this restaurant

in order to keep our post-fire-dollars in town, we ate at Siam 2 times this past week and had take out in addition. The food is good, the service kind. A good place to go for a good dinner. If only there could be some kind of HEAT in the place. I recommend to bring a sweater when you go eat there.

What a beautiful establishment! Nice music, excellent customer service and the food was phenomenal. My Jamaican mother enjoyed her oxtails and I enjoyed the curry, brown stew and jerk chicken dish. We also had the spicy jerk wing appetizer and beef patties. So much food, so little stomach. Large portions with left overs for tomorrow. Definitely recommend to anyone in the Tampa area.

I went here with my husband today and I order a number 7"the Korean beef sandwich and it was amazing. The bread was nice and crunchy with a good amount of veggies like cilantro, carrot, jalapeño and cucumber. Also picked up a mango bubble tea and it was pleasantly good not a powder flavor like other places I tried but more of a fresh almost slushy flavor. We will be coming back for more !!!

This place was an unexpected pleasure. Amazing octopus appetizer and great dinner. Terrific cocktails and a comprehensive wine list. Service was just what you want. Attentive but not hovering. Don't miss!

Amazing Vietnamese/Asian Fusion. I had the spring rolls, papaya salad and Singapore noodles. All were on point. They also have a great wine/beer list and Happy Hour from 3-6. I work down the street and we will definitely be checking it out again.
i've heard this was the best thai in Nashville so I finally tried it. definitely a nice selection of dishes and tasty but not sure it's worth a return trip.

I have dined at this restaurant many times, but an finally getting around to doing a review. Beginning with the apps, I have sample every app, at one time or another, and they are all spot-on. My favorite is the crab ragoon, which is the best I have ever tasted. Regarding entrees, my usuals are the combination pho and the variety of vermicelli bowls. They're pho broth was excellent. I would put it in the top tier with Doung Phoug, Tan Dinh, and Pho Tau Bay. The one area that is in need of improvement is the limited menu. I would love to see some bacos or some other Vietnamese fusion items. With serious competition in the New Orleans Vietnamese cuisine realm, this restaurant continues to stand fiercely competitive.

Thanks, Taste of India, for the recent paint job. Your place looks fantastic! SUCH an improvement! As promised, I will now bump you up to five stars, because nothing now distracts me from how much I love your food!
Excellent upscale Indian food without the upscale prices. Service is absolutely on point at all times. And its BYO!!! What's not to love? In my opinion, the best all around restaurant in Newtown.

I love a good Vietnamese dish every so often. But when it is uninspired and there is no service, it really takes away from the experience. Now I get it. Everything in Indianapolis closes early because everyone has to be in bed by 8pm. But just because the restaurant is closing in an hour doesn't mean that you have to neglect the tables that are there. And then the food, well, let's just say Siagon has been doing good to earn it's 1 star. The rocket shrimp were okay, but the meal soon went downhill from there. Meanwhile the server was nowhere to be found, so complaining about it was out of the question. Overall, I can say I've had better dining experiences.

Went to pho36 for the first time this evening. The pho was excellent and my companions enjoyed their vermicelli and sub. The egg rolls are excellent and the banana desert is a must. The owners are super nice and double as servers and cooks. We will definitely be making this a regular stop for us

Want delicious Vietnamese food- it's Saigon in Indy hands down. Good pho (rich soup base with traditional options such as tripe), bun (Vietnamese noodles with spring rolls pickled vegetables and meats), subs; Saigon has it all. Their food is as traditional and authentic you can get too for a great price.
Absolutely the best sushi. We came from Orlando to eat here. Outstanding service, very clean and DELIC! We will be back.

Found Taj-India when looking for a place via Yelp iPhone app :) I love Indian food, especially trying new places, so I checked it out. The location is in a strip mall, maybe not too inviting, but whatever. I'm a big fan of the little side places. The inside isn't anything to write about either, but it is clean and that, my friends, IS notable. The music is kind of weird, yes, but I felt like it added something. The place was totally empty and it was lunchtime on a Sunday afternoon. Weird, considering the place has to offer some great food. Our server was very nice and our food got to us quickly. I tried two soups, both were great, especially since I requested spiciness and received it! One customer did come to pick up something while we were eating, so it does seem like take-out is more popular. Would go back!!!

I kinda stumbled into Gigi's today because my usual go-to food truck was closed due to Penn's spring break (I guess). My food took a while to order but the guy was nice and said he was making up for it taking so long. I got the $10 chicken breast platter with mac and cheese and green beans and I would have bet money that my bag weighed more than 5 lbs. I'm from Georgia--I know Southern food can take a while to cook. But dude hooked me up for what amounted to a 15-20 minute wait and I will definitely be going back. Not to mention the food is excellent. The breast was gigantic and had a ton of meat on it (giggity), and the sides were both great. If you've got a few minutes to wait in line for some excellent food you should check this place out.
Literally my favorite place for spring rolls and pho!! Also very classic Vietnamese. Everybody is so nice there!

DEFINITELY OVER RATED!!! Never really cared for their food. Definitely far from authentic Jamaican food. Ordered oxtails extremely tough needed a knife to get meet off of the bones. The meat is supposed to come off the bone with ease by merely lightly sucking on it. Won't be going back there for a meal. Maybe a patty or quick wings. Service was cool. They were moving rapidly!! PEACE

The Smiling Elephant possibly has the best Thai food in metro Nashville. I ordered the somtum green papaya salad and their house pad Thai with glass (rice) noodles (it should be noted, I did not request these and they are an option. I think the kitchen may have made a mistake). The ambience is one of my favorite features of this establishment. The warm, wooden-ceilings, floors, and tables complement the spotless, white walls perfectly. Gilded picture frames with elephants and royalty fit nicely with elements of greenery spotted throughout. The noise was raucous and joyful. The staff here is no-nonsense and speedy. Don't feel too offended if they are rushing, they just have so many patrons to serve and get through. That being said, hospitality could be improved. When I asked for a customer receipt, the hostess stared at me for a few full seconds before printing one out and tossing it at me wordlessly. Our waitress also served a table which arrived after us, leaving us to ourselves for an hour without food on a Tuesday night from 7-8pm. The food is good, but not that good. Our entire table felt slighted, and we were not alone. All around us, patrons were asking for receipts, requesting service, and requesting boxes. While the waitstaff succeeded in getting people glasses of water, that fulfilled the minimal requirement. The lines were exorbitant for a Tuesday excursion, and the service did not warrant the hype previously given. The parking is atrocious. People will meander around the lot because they don't want to stand in the crowded, claustrophobia-inducing line at the entrance. There is a private lot down a long, sloping hill which is near impossible to get out unless you grit your teeth and say a few prayers. Yikes. I will try again via takeout, please. Not the best Thai place due to location by a long shot, but you could do worse than the Smiling Elephant. Plus, they make a MEAN, green somtum salad. That alone should entice you through the parking lot from hell.

Yesterday was my second time eating at this location and it will be my last. I ordered the veggie gyro and my mother the Mediterranean salad. The food was okay. The veggie feast is better. It was brought to our table quickly, which is nice. But that's where the good parts end. The tables were sticky and the staff is never friendly. On top of all that the place has roaches. As my mother was trying to eat her salad, I see a roach crawling on the chair behind her. Immediately I lose my appetite. However, she tried t forge through. So, I moved the food to another table. ANOTHER roach then comes from the bar to try to come toward us. That was our limit so we left the restaurant.

Moving back to Indiana was not on my 'want-to-do' list but here I am. Now what if I were to tell you that Pho 36 makes that move worth it? I had Vietnamese while I was down South and it was not the same. I was disappointed every time I stepped into a Vietnamese restaurant, longing for more flavor. Pho 36 is simplistic in its decor and so peaceful, their decor on the amazing food coming out of their kitchen. It's been awhile since I've gotten around due to work so pardon my juvenile names for what are amazing dishes on their menu. The egg roll noodle bowl complete with a plethora of bean sprouts is amazingly fresh, a mix of every kind of taste you could ever desire. Sweet and savory and sour and spicy. It's all in that huge bowl they place down in front of you that I don't imagine I could ever finish in one sitting. The bahn mi! It's become a bit of a fad in the past years to have bahn mi but you have to make it right. Crispy bread with a soft inside. The floral notes of cilantro. The sharpness of jalapeño. The sweetness of carrot and daikon. All coupled with amazing pate or pork roll or even a tofu option! And on days when I simply can't take the additional spice of jalapeño or I'm not feeling cilantro, the chef is always happy to accommodate. Even if the server does joke about adding extra cilantro every time I do it. Lol I love a personable staff! My brother is a fan of the clay pot (I think that's what it is?). It's so warming and delicious. My mom's favorite is the tofu bahn mi. Now that they have moved from Indy, I enjoy bragging about the delights of this place that I alone get to enjoy. A special treat is their bubble tea! Traditional flavors but with an icy finish that is unique to anything I've had before. Try this place out guys! You won't be disappointed. They even do takeout!
Very delicious, affordable, and vegetarian-friendly. Perfect. Will be ordering again in the future.

Worth a trip to the Parish from anywhere in New Orleans, (I never thought I write that about a restaurant), this place is a gem. The Mediterranean dishes were superb, the service fast and welcoming, the prices were very fair, the place is spotless. After years of settling for mediocre Middle Eastern food at New Orleans' usual restaurants we were very surprised to find this oddly named place tucked away in St. Bernard. We had an array of dishes each one tastier than the other. Can't wait to go back. If you like Mediterranean cuisine, Stella Maris is a must.

Stopped in here today for a quick lunch, after driving by everyday. First off, I was really impressed by the interior. It's in a smaller strip mall, and you don't expect much based on the exterior. I was impressed. The waiter looked over the menu with me, and when I told him I'm a big Malai Kofta, he told me it was their specialty, so I ordered it. I was NOT disappointed. The lunch special also came with naan and a samosa, which was also fresh and tasty. Service was great and fast. Definite repeat

Food and service was very mediocre. It was so awkward because we were clearly ordering each dish to be an entree, not doing the tapas option, and yet they served out dishes to us tapas style, as they were prepared... while I think it's great to do this when you order tapas, you should be able to adjust your kitchen to accommodate how your patrons order. Also, the food was really just kind of unremarkable. I've had better (much better) Mediterranean in St. Louis.

I love Pho. This is THE place to go if you want some. It's been over a year since I was last here (finally learned how to make it myself), but what I remember is that it was terrific. I went with my brother in law. I think he was a bit disappointed with the bahn mi, but the Pho was amazing. As he scoffed at his pathetic sandwich, I basked in the glory of a perfectly prepared bowl of piping hot Pho. I cannot vouch for anything but the Pho here, aside from their spring rolls (maybe they're called fresh rolls). Those were okay, but nothing to write home about. The Pho is where it's at. The other stuff may be good, but the Pho WILL be good. I have had Pho all over Boise, and this is by far my favorite. I am not sure what set this one above the others. Maybe it was the broth. Maybe it was the beef. There was not one specific thing that really stood out as better than its competitors, but there was something magical about the whole. Something I hadn't experienced since living in San Francisco.

So good, so good! If you like indian food at all you have to try this place. If you're not sure if you like indian food, try this place. Be careful, with the spice, hot is HOT! Mild is hot, but good. The owners are the best, you will feel welcome and well taken care of. Oh, it's a BYOB too, that's nice.

Tandoor India is the best Indian food in the city, hands down. Whenever I went to New Dehli, I felt like I was being shadowed by the Indian mafia. Besides that, their food was lackluster. Never been back. If you're vegetarian or vegan, you absolutely have to get the Vegetable Shahi Kofta (they only serve it on weekends in the buffet) or get it from their menu. It's amazing. Everything else there is highly flavorful and the staff is super accommodating.

Very very good Indian / Paki food at reasonable prices. They could use more of a drink selection, and it is not fancy or anything, but our server BeeBee was super friendly and TRY THE FRUIT SALAD FOR DESERT which was really delicious. Portions are very large and the spices in the Goat Vindaloo and Chicken Biryani were authentic and well-balanced. We will be back. My friends from Pakistan seemed pleased.

I had to update my review for Erawan because I just wrote a review for Tamarind and I don't want to contradict myself. Erawan (THIS Erawan, not the other one) is a real treat. I always get the red curry with seitan and/or tofu. And when I come here, I am always blown away. I leave here wanting more. It's so good I have considered ordering two of the same dish. To me, they have the best recipe and method. Even though I love Erawan slightly more, I go to Tamarind more often. This is honestly mostly due to proximity from my apartment. When I am jonesing for red curry, which is several times a week, it's just easier to get to Tamarind. And if Erawan is a 10, Tamarind is not much lower. Here are the key differences between my two favorite red curry joints as I see it: - Tamarind is slightly spicier by default (not a problem, as I can tell Erawan a little hotter than normal, although I really like Erawan's default.) - Erawan is slightly more flavorful than Tamarind. They really nail it. - The rice at Erawan is better. It's sticky Jasmine rice cooked perfectly. Not sure what Tamarind uses. - Tamarind's portion is slightly bigger. I've left Erawan wanting more, which I think adds to my sense of preference. I'd rather leave lusting after my next experience than totally full, so it's not a big deal. - I don't need to make any vegetable substitutions at Tamarind (At Erawan I have to say hold the eggplant and add broccoli. This is the default at Tamarind.) - Tamarind has more vegan appetizer selections, and overall those selections are better, but I don't feel the need for an appetizer at Tamarind. At Erawan I really feel like I need something else. But like a good lover, you want more. - Tamarind is 4 blocks closer to my apartment. So overall, I end up at Tamarind a bit more frequently. But if I could have the recipe for what either one of these restaurants serve me, I'd choose Erawan's.

I came here at night and the place was dimly-lit. While it might make for good atmosphere, I would like to be able to see what I am eating. It's not a huge deal, but it might bother people who already have trouble seeing in areas without much light. Service was good - the lady who served me is very polite and sweet. Anyway, their Coco Pad Thai, a lower calorie version of Pad Thai made with mung bean noodles, is quite delicious. The lemongrass soup was good but I can't say how it compares to other restaurants because this is the first time I have had it. What I do know is they use actual limes and not kaffir lime leaves. Those two items ended up costing $21.10 with tax included (but not the tip), so it is kind of pricy.

Really cool decor and atmosphere. We shared the Turkish hummus, whipped feta, pickled shrimp, cucumber salad, and turnip. For the tres leeches cake for dessert which was a perfect level of sweetness. Great food and awesome staff. Very attentive waiters and waitresses!
Fresh, well prepared food. Good service. It's becoming one of our favorite local Asian restaurants.

When I have Asian food cravings this is the only place nearby that will satisfy them. I always get the vegetarian pho and its usually great. One time the soup was too salty and sometimes the veggies aren't too fresh, but the service is great and the taste is usually on point.

We are semi-regulars are Shere-E-Punjab. The service is usually good, and the food is always delicious. It is very decently priced as well, and is usually never busy when we come for dinner. The only reason I am giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because there are only maybe 2 vegan entree options.

Not much to add to the many positive reviews, but yes, the chaats and lassis at Mood Cafe rock! Hassan is wonderful at making you feel truly welcome and introducing you to new varieties of the signature food and drinks you might not have tried yet. Always a smile, highly responsive to feedback, and quick to offer you samples, you can tell he cares about his customers, his offerings, and the neighborhood Mood Cafe is embedded in. A fantastic addition to the thriving Baltimore Avenue corridor of West Philly!

Excellent find! Food is made with and served with love. The chef cooks authentic Punjabi food. New management has turned this place around. We had the best palak paneer with aloo parantha. Highly recommend the daal soup too. Bring your dessert appetite as well.

Yelp let me down a little on this one. Maybe I had my expectations too high, but I thought Dooners was only average. When I walked in, I sensed that the falafel wouldn't be very good, so I decided to go for the hummus sandwich. I had the option of regular hummus or spicy hummus. I chose the spicy hummus. It came with a tzatziki sauce (or something that looked a lot like it), which was fine. Luckily, I saw someone order before me and saw that the sandwich is usually LOADED with that sauce both before and after the main ingredients are put in. So I asked for the tzatziki to be put on lightly. I don't remember anything too special about the sandwich; it was an average hummus sandwich on pita bread. PS: I don't eat meat, but I saw the lamb shawarma roasting behind the counter. It didn't look very good. The chicken looked normal, but the lamb looked like a giant solidified, sweating mass of formerly-liquefied lamb that had been pressed through a tube. Needless to say, if I was ordering meat, I would have gone for the chicken, not the lamb.

This is one of those oft sought out moderately priced, but supremely delicious joints. The atmosphere is nothing special, but the service was attentive and polite. There was a misunderstanding about the serving of our orders. My friends had ordered appetizers as their main course, but the servers brought out their food as a first course and waited to serve everyone else until we asked about the rest of the food. It was an understandable mistake and the servers had been keeping their eyes on the table, waiting for us to finish the "appetizers." I'd definitely recommend the place and would return.

I enjoy this restaurant a lot. I've been going there since they opened - I have never had a bad or unpleasant experience. Once when ordering takeout there was a mistake but it was inconsequential and they happily fixed the problem. Other than that, everything has been great. I really like the food, and I'm not a stranger to Indian cuisine - I used to live in the San Francisco Bay area, and ate at many authentic Indian places there. I enjoy the food here, and I also feel at home here. The staff is friendly and helpful. In fact, one time my daughter left her handbag (with her wallet inside) here - I was not informed until after they had closed for the day, so I sent them a Facebook message asking if they'd found it. Someone wrote back very quickly and informed me that they had it, and that I could come in at my convenience the next day to pick it up. I thought that was very kind of them to take the time to put me at ease.

I took my husband and 7 of our friends here last weekend for my husband's birthday. The service was great, our server Ashley was so accommodating and nice. The live music on the weekends is a great touch, and while you feel like you're in Philadelphia, you kind of feel like you've been taken to the caribbean for just a few hours. The food was delicious, their plantains were the best ever. And when it started to rain on our outside dinner celebration, Ashley and the rest of the staff without flinching set up a table for us inside in the veranda, and we were still able to enjoy the outside music. It was a group consensus that we all can't wait to go back!

When I lived in the Fairmount area, this is a place I wanted to visit. I moved and it never happened...and then UberEATS came into existence and I had it delivered to me. What I had was the braised lamb shank with red sauce and my goodness, it was such a well cooked piece of meat. The meat fell off the shank and then melted into my mouth and then I smiled and repeated the process. The vegetables, potatoes, and rice were also delicious. A small area of contention I had was the bread. I received half of a loaf, but am I supposed to dip it in something??? Or am I supposed to eat it straight? I suspect it's meant to dip in olive oil or something. If that's the case, it would be nice to receive a little somethin' somethin' for bread dippin'. The kataifi is incredibly sweet and incredibly delicious. If you're not trying to go into diabetic shock, avoid at all costs. Nonetheless, I would definitely come here in person with a cheap bottle of wine since this place is BYOB and try other things on the menu.

This was my favorite Pho place in Clearwater. When the first opened up I ordered 2 to 3 times every week. The broth and chicken were delicious and they always got my order right. Months later they have been consistent but for all the wrong reasons. My order has been messed up multiple times with extras being left out that were paid for. The chicken has become veiny soggy small scraps that I couldn't even eat without gagging, I threw it away. The have stopped giving out lime for the Pho or if not, keep forgetting it. It's a shame because I really loved this restaurant but I don't plan on eating there again. I hope you guys start treating your customers better and go back to the high quality service and ingredients from when you opened.

The food was fantastic! Full of flavor and spice but not all the cream at some Indian restaurants. The place was inviting and had a great location, even large enough for events. They even have an outdoor The wait staff was diligent and our food came out quickly! Overall a great restaurant that I will be bringing my friends back to.

I think The Smiling Elephant is just great! Everything I've tried has been very fresh and not greasy at all. The meats are lean and cooked perfectly. I'm not a vegetarian, but the tofu is excellent. I must admit I don't eat Thai food often. I was expecting spicier dishes, but the flavors were still good. Oh, and awesome lemongrass tea! The vibe is very cool as well. Quite small, so waiting on tables can make one claustrophobic, but the stained wood is a nice touch. It really does feel like hut - a nice, new, clean hut. I usually just call ahead for pick up since I am close by. The staff is also very friendly. The prices aren't the most inexpensive, but you get a quality product. When I'm in the mood for Asian food, I would much prefer The Smiling Elephant over any cookie-cutter Chinese restaurant.

While it may be that the spicy food is better, thus reflecting the high Yelp rating, I will say that my family and I were disappointed with most of our meal. The pros: the service was good and the decor was nice. The waitress offered us kids sized forks and spoons when the food came (dessert sized?). The dumpling soup was very tasty and the kids loved it as well. The fried tofu was bland, but well fried and crispy. The ok: I felt the shrimp Pad Thai was cooked to the right level, the sauce wasn't especially tasty, but it was edible, just not amazing. Similarly, the massaman curry was ok, but the quality of the white rice that it came with was subpar. The fried rice was fine. The bad: I felt the chicken Pad Thai had slightly over-cooked noodles in too much mediocre sauce, while the chicken pieces were tough and difficult to chew through. The coconut mushroom soup was interesting, but I found the pieces of chicken in it to be extremely tough to the point of being basically inedible. Fortunately, there were only one or two big pieces of chicken. I didn't like the salad at all - heavy lemon/lime dressing with cabbage type "greens" and a few chunks of tomatoes. The annoying - they automatically added gratuity to our party of 3 adults and 2 young kids. I thought it was normally parties of six and up? I didn't notice this when reading the menu, but in going on their website, it is prominently displayed that a gratuity if 18% is added for parties of 5 or more. They were very professional and refilled the water constantly, so they would have gotten a good tip anyway. Still, it's the presumption that I wasn't a fan of. Overall, there was nothing atrociously bad about the meal but it left me feeling lacking (and much poorer, $95 for 3 adults and 2 toddlers).

Our family LOVES this place! The pad thai and fried rice are divine. They happily adjust spice levels to please everyone's taste buds. Such a silly thing, but their crushed ice and sweet tea are so good too!

First time ordering here, pad thai was a bit dry but still good. They packed a lot of beef into the beef pad thai which is rare. Beef was nice and soft and not chewy. Chicken wing nice and crispy and Seafood salad was flavorful. Came on time and nicely packaged. would order from here again.

I would love to comment on the food/drinks but unfortunately we were never served despite having a reservation and being there over an hour... Long story below: Things started off alright, we were a large group (around 10 people) who were looking to go out for a hookah, some beer/wine, and some tasty food on a Saturday night. I called ahead that afternoon to make a reservation and the guy who answered was pleasant on the phone but asked a couple of times if we would for sure be getting food. It was strange, but I assured him yes we would get food to go along with the hookah and wine. Then things went downhill. We arrived 10 minutes early for our 9pm reservation and had to wait *outside* on a chill mid-September Edmonton night since there was no room in the foyer. Alright, fine, and we were assured that someone would come get us when our table was ready. Our reservation time came and passed, so we sent someone in to inquire... turns out another group who had walked in earlier was seated at our reserved table and were not finished yet (wait staff said he couldn't ask them to leave because they were making a lot of money off that group). Fast-forward another 15 mins of waiting outside getting colder and colder to finally being seated at another section of tables. No hookah set up (even though I said on the phone that we wanted one), only half of the places were set with glasses, and there we sat for another long while. It took 20 mins to get water and even then, half the group was missed because one pitcher only goes so far. We stopped the man we were dealing with earlier on his way into the kitchen to ask about getting some drinks and food and he started to push the pizza on us. He disappeared into the kitchen and reemerges with two pizzas for another table, stops at ours to show us how "delicious" they look and push some pizza sales on us again, then wouldn't come back to take any order whatsoever. Ridiculous considering the place was *maybe* half full, and it's a tiny place. We decided to ditch and sent one poor representative from our group to tell the only other wait staff working that night (I feel bad for the waitress, actually, the look on her face was near panic when we told her we were leaving - and yet I don't feel too bad since she was just cleaning tables the whole time...). Most of us made it out without facing the awkwardness but my fiance got caught by the same man from earlier. The guy was desperate for us to stay and tried to make excuses and explain that he was *about* to come deal with us, but too bad. Headed over to a bar on Whyte instead and got some poutine. No one in our party was impressed.

Great experience! I have seen this place in Manayunk for awhile now and was always curious to check it out, but to be honest it look like a hole in the wall and was nervous about trying this place out. All I can say is that me and my wife were so glad we did. I ordered for her the gyro meat platter with tzatziki and they gave a huge portion on the side of pita bread for her order. I ordered for myself the beef shawarma and it was awesome. It had a tahini sauce poured over the meat and also came with a huge portion of pita bread as well. It was less than 30 dollars for both plates (not including drinks) and we were both very full. With each of the meat platters they give you a small Greek salad on the side. The salad had some really good feta cheese and tasted fresh. Would definitely recommend this place to anyone local or if you are dropping by Manayunk to go shopping. The place is small and you may have a problem finding seating and the wait is a bit long after waiting for your order, but it is definitely worth the wait.

This place is really good. I lived in the Caribbean for several years. This was very true to the flavor. The staff was super friendly. The food here is delicious. Would highly recommend to anyone. A true hidden gem.

The best pho I have had in a while. The broth is what makes it the best. We wanted to try the banh mi but they said the bakery where they get their bread from was closed :(. Hopefully next time we are in town we can try it :). And the waiter was very friendly, I asked her if there were any good asian haircut places in town and she recommended the one I went to and was very happy with the haircut I ended up getting.

Benefits of working at Wash U. (medical campus), Food trucks line up in front every day! Go Gyro Go is one of the food trucks that I look for. If Lamb, is too daring for you, I highly recommend the Chicken Souvlaki with their salad! Definitive amount of Tzatziki sauce with cooked chicken (moist and perfectly seasoned) in a soft pita bread! Craving gets real!!! Go Get it!!!

Great News! Queen of Sheba has opened a restaurant in Sarasota. Food was great and the conversation with the chef / owner was enjoyable. Great combination of flavors without being too spicy, sweet, or salty. Can't wait to go back.

For an all around great Vietnamese food experience, Pho 36 is hands down the best! However for the best Pho in town, it's Eggroll #1 on 465/Emerson. The owner is very friendly, and they serve authentic Viet dishes. My only critique about their food is with their Pho and bubble tea. Broth needs more of that meat/bone flavor and definitely need beef tendon and tripe! The bubble tea would be spot on if it was more smoother. The blender they use does not blend ice well, therefore you will get little chunks of ice. OK, so here is my biggest peeve with this place. I have been there not once, but TWICE where they were closed on a NON HOLIDAY Friday. I live 40 minutes away and we will drive for good food! It's such an inconvenience to get there and find that they are closed. In my opinion, this place needs to find the help or staff that can run the place so they are OPEN! No restaurant should operate like this! I've been to many smaller and family owned restaurants in town, and NEVER have they been closed. It should not be the NORM to call a restaurant to see if they will be open on a Friday night.

I hate to leave a negative review for this place because the service was good, the waitress was very friendly and tried to explain the dishes to us. But the food was such a disappointment. We ordered tom yum soup, which was very good. Then the sweet chili fish and pad thai, which were very disappointing. The sweet chili fish was way too sweet, and the pad thai just had some weird taste. I mean, it's a Thai restaurant, how can you screw up the pad Thai? The worst part is that after we left the restaurant, our stomachs started feeling weird... We liked the tom yum soup, the service was good. But might not go back :(

Solid indian food, typical buffet. Sometimes the people who are taking-out, pick the big pieces of meat our of the curries, but that is not the restaurants fault. Nice place, since it was re-done inside. Good place to come for quick tasty food .

I love that there is an option for great Thai food in North County! I have only been able to eat here during lunch hours, so I can't say anything about dinner service speeds. There is a wonderful lunch menu that comes with an entre, rice, and either fried spring rolls or Thai butterfly (similar to crab Rangoon). My go-to order is the Tom Kha soup with chicken. I add a side of rice so that I can make more a meal out of the dish. There are varying levels of spice from 1 to 5- I typically order spice level 2 or 3. I think that spice level 1 is not enough (my soup tasted more sweet than spicy). I think that typical white people cannot handle a spicy level of 4 or 5- so be aware before you order the hottest option. I usually call my order in and it is ready when I pull up to the drive thru 10 minutes later. When I forget to call in my order first, I still go to the drive thru and my order is ready in about 5 minutes. I find that if I go inside to place a to-go order it takes a little bit longer to prepare.

Ordered take-out. Great steamed chicken dumplings. Loved the Kung Pao chicken. The Dan Dan noodles with chicken were ok, but I will probably never order it again (not a big noodles fan). Overall, it was good experience.

Delicia was delightful. The service was good. The food was delicious - Queso fundido and corn cakes-yum! My friend had the fish tacos and really enjoyed those as well My only negative, which wasn't worth a star reduction, is that it was Monday night, they weren't busy at all and they wouldn't seat me until my friend arrived. I certainly can understand that policy on a busy night but it seemed out of place for a slow evening.

the bahn mi at pho cam ly is awesome. the french bread is crunchy and fresh and the sandwiches have a unique flavor to them that i'm not finding at other places in town. i prefer the lemongrass chicken to the others, and make sure you add an egg - over easy. now, i've been on a vegetable kick lately so i ordered the veggie spring roll with avocado. i've got to say that this spring roll and description did not match up. when i think of veggieS, i think of carrot, lettuce, maybe cabbage, cucumber... this spring roll was lettuce, noodles, and two very thin slices of avocado. the word i can best use for it was weak. very weak. but that's no reason to not go for everything else on the menu. the staff is very nice and the place is clean.

I was working on a recording session in Wilmington for the weekend and had the chance to eat here for a few different meals and every dish we tried was amazing! I highly recommend the Saag. The service is very quick as well. One of the better Indian restaurants I've eaten at!

You wouldn't think it by seeing the place, but it is a true gem. I love this place. The atmosphere is excellent, they have the place decorated nice and even make little flowers out of your straw wrappers. The food is superb. I recommend this place to everyone that mentions they are in the area or if they want Thai.

This place nails it on the head with every aspect of their business. They make delicious food quickly, and the workers are more friendly than you could ever expect. I have tried about half of the things of the menu and they were all terrific. I have settled on the beef shawarma and a walnut baklava when I go, but you can't really go wrong. Do yourself a favor and give this place a try.
THe Papaya salad was ridiculously good! The Pad Thai was amazing as well. The service was great and the prices were very reasonable. I absolutely loved it and will go back very soon!

All around good quality. Falafel was crunchy on the outside and creamy inside. Gyro was great, with enough lamb to make a second. Hummus was hummus- good, smooth, hummus with delicate flavors. I recommend.
Always great. One of the very best in Tampa Bay. Terrific lunch buffet every day. Great vegetarian options too! Very personable staff and lovely atmosphere.

I have been craving Lebanese food for a while and finally made it here. It has been substantially dressed up since I was last here and the prices reflect that. They now have an extensive wine cellar housed in a glass-walled closet that dominates the place. The entree plates are around $25. Staff do not seem very familiar with middle Eastern cuisine and weren't very able to describe the dishes. I had a starter of hummus which was good, a little more garlic and sesame flavour wouldn't hurt. Pita bread was cold and little dry. Clearly not made in house, or that day. Chicken on skewers was very tasty and consisted on four metal skewers, another pita and a very tasty garlic spread. Dining mate had pizza which was very thick-crusted, but the ham was very good. So all in all, the meal was good but I left still craving my shawarma fix.
Waited in line at the Philly Food truck festival two days ago and the Curry chicken, brown rice and beans along with the yams were amazing!

GROSS. If you're a germophobe, this place is not for you. Be warned. Ok, where do I start: (1) The restaurant is on a side street which is off another side street. So difficult to find if you're not from the area. (2) We had to wait 15+ minutes despite having reservations and showing up early. (3) Finally got inside. It's basically a 3-level townhouse thats been converted into a restaurant. Very very dingy and dark inside. They say they have been at this location for 30 years (go figure)... We were part of an unfortunate group that had to climb 2 flights of stairs to have dinner on the 3rd floor (basically in a bedroom of this house). Scary stairs, scary walls. Over-decorated with rugs and stuff on the walls. Everything seemed dusty. (4) Finally got to the room. There were no dinner tables, just side tables. It's not very comfortable to eat off side tables. Anyway, we sat down. (5) There was a fixed dinner. Therefore no food menu was provided, because you have no choice in the matter. It is 7-courses, yes. But 7 fixed dishes. The waiter announced to those of us in the room (3 separate parties of 2 people each) what our dinner would be, and that was that. I wasn't expecting this. But there was more shock to be experienced. (6) All the plates were SHARED. In the LITERAL SENSE. Yes, you heard me. For each of the 7 courses, the waiter would provide the table with ONE large plate of food. You're expected to all dig in and eat off the same plate. No forks, no knives, no side plates. Just one plate in the middle of the table for everyone. So you probably don't want to go to this restaurant with someone you're not comfortable with (either from a germs-perspective, or otherwise). And by the way, these were not "finger foods"... We are talking about lamb dishes, spicy chicken dishes with sauces, salads...Yes, SALADS! ....So just to reiterate, you are expected to use your hands for everything AND share off the same plate too. Two layers of freaking out. (7) At some point, I couldn't take it... so I asked for a fork and a knife... The waiter brought back plastic forks only, no knives. He said there were no knives in the entire restaurant except what the kitchen was using. (8) Before you eat, they make you wash your hands. They come by each table with a kettle of lukewarm water and pour it over your hands, with a bowl underneath. Yes (you guessed it!), some of this water is splashing into your drinks which have already been served by this time. (9) They serve a flat bread to eat the dishes with. Waiter walks around with a basket of bread and offers each table. You are to use the bread to pick up the pieces of lamb/chicken/veggies. However, no side plates, remember? So you are expected to place your bread directly on the table. We asked for little plates and they said they didn't have any, but that the table was "nice and clean"... Yeah, nothing so far had given me confidence that the table was "nice and clean". And besides, by this point, the glasses of ice water were forming pools of water around them on the table. So the bread would've been wet if we placed it on the table. So I just held onto my stash of bread the entire dinner. They encourage you to take multiple pieces of bread, because you will use it to eat all the subsequent courses. (10) Only cash accepted. Again, wasn't expecting this. (11) Mid-dinner, there was an unexpected belly dancer. Sudden loud music, so we all looked up... and a belly dancer walked in and started dancing in this already crowded, small dingy room. It was unnecessary and interrupted our dinner. Everyone had to stop to watch because the music was deafening and the room was so small (it lasted about 10 minutes). We couldn't carry on our conversation. And because I don't want to be a hater, I will say that the food actually tasted good. I loved the lamb dish especially. It was a lot of food, it was tasty, and it was reasonably priced. However, I just did not have a good experience here at all, so it was hard to enjoy the meal. Take-out option might be better.

My boyfriend spent some time in Thailand and when we first started dating suggested this thai place across from his apt, I had never really eaten thai (save pad thai) but was too shy to say no. but it's AMAZING. I reccomend the sausages, the fresh spring rolls are good, the papaya salad was amazing, tilapia with curry, crazy stuff i had never tried before as well, and i loved every second of it. It's also got that quirky west philly thing going on which makes it fun. BYO for sure. A crisp white wine with your meal will make it even more enjoyable.
One of my favorite lunch spots!! The servers are friendly and attentive everytime I go! I love the portion of food they give you. I always leave happy and sleepy!!

Creazian was surprisingly quiet during lunch hour on a recent Friday. We were quickly seated and given ice waters with lemon. The waitress did a great job helping us navigate the menu, which has a number of items that our older crew wasn't familiar with. After lighting-fast consensus, we decided to start with the pork belly lollipops, which really do live up to the hype. I feel that a lot of pork belly dishes are too fatty and gummy, but the pb pops are tender, cooked to perfection and ideally balanced between sweet and savory. I could literally chow dozens of those badboys. I split the papaya salad with prawns and lobster bahn mi with my mom and neither of us were disappointed. The salad had a crisp, refreshing texture. The sandwich had generous chunks of lobster that we learned had been flown in from Maine. Both had a subtle hint of spice that only elevated the taste of both dishes. The other oldies in our crew had the beef pho, and although they struggled to identify some of the ingredients at first, they both blasted through the hearty goodness in no time flat. I'll be back for sure.

My favorite Thai restaurant right now. Went in on a Sunday afternoon with family, clean, friendly, good service, great food. Told my colleagues about it. Since I'm gluten-free, they have Silver Noodles dish with any meat you like which was fantastic with chicken, medium hot.

Food - 4+ Prices - 4+ Service - 4 Ambience - 3 Le Saigon offers high-quality, authentic Vietnamese cuisine with reasonable prices and good service. Located in a shopping center on Route 30 in Paoli, they've been in business for many years and seem to have a loyal local customer base. They do a brisk takeout business as well as a steady lunchtime crowd. Fresh ingredients and a quiet (perhaps too quiet), friendly setting make for a relaxed meal that won't set you back too much. BYOB is fine. I have tried several things on their menu, but favorites are Pad Thai with Chicken and Chicken with Lemon Grass. Nice selection of appetizers, too. I see some other diners have complained about the food being "bland", but if you ask, the owner is more than happy to accommodate any special requests for amping up the spices or adding ingredients that you may have in mind. Haven't had their pho and I know fellow Yelpers give that mixed reviews, so my overall 4-star rating is based on my experiences over the last several years with their classic menu items.

Bar Avalon shines because of their attention to detail and effort to please and accommodate their clientele. This is our go to spot in West Chester for just about any night out, whether for a midweek meal, a Saturday night with friends, or just a few cocktails to close out the night. Their food and service never disappoint. The menu is innovative and fresh - signature staples and creative features. Try the mussel bakes, roasted beets or the gnocchi. Great wine list and clever craft cocktails. I truly can't say enough about John and his staff.

Hmm. I never thought I would give this rating. I guess all the glitz and glam have gone down, since the opening. I went once again to try their buffet. It was very average, including the customer service. The food was OK. And I had to ask multiple times for water refills. I guess it lost its charm.
I ordered a Pho and it did not taste like traditional Pho at all. The noodle is uncooked and very hard. I don't recommend this restaurant at least its Pho.

My wife and I went there with Groupon...ordered the $8.99 LARGE combo pho each and shared an order of spring rolls. The texture of the spring roll wrapping was harden, tell tale sign of them pre-made sitting in the fridge...The pho was a joke: the portion of the noodles was about half the size of any other place in town, the topping "everything" consist of 1 thin slice of overcooked meat, 1 slice of tripe of sort, 1 slice of something, and a meatball cut into 4 quarters, may be 1 shrimp, don't even remember...for $8.99? We can go to any Asian all-you-can-eat buffet place for the same money, and some actually has pho! Even without counting buffet places, it was not even worth half of the price (with Groupon), I can't imagine how bad it must be for the folks paying full price. If the owner is trying to get (scam) people coming in expecting them to pay half price with groupon and make everything half portion...it is doing a miserable marketing job. People usually don't like to be suckered.

I don't know if I should actually post a review because I haven't actually been there. A family member picked up a Banh Mi from there for me. It was the tofu and it was delicious. The bread is perfect and the price is low. I am on a bit of a tofu Banh Mi kick right now. I saw from the menu that they do pork and a Vietnamese sausage one as well.

I love this place. Its not the greatest thai food I've ever had, its not even the best in St. Louis, but it is in my neighborhood and they make very good food for a very affordable price. I love being able to walk to a place and have lunch or dinner for less than $10. If you want something a little more upscale you can always go down the street to King & I, but this place is the best bang for the buck in the Thai genre.
Nope. Never again. 13$ for 8 bites of pad Thai. Never again. Menu pricing online is outdated. No thanks.

Good food, poor service. Food here is great. Always fresh and well prepared. The problem this place has, and the reason for the rating, is the weak service I get every time I order food here (usually take out). The gentleman usually at the counter spreads himself too thin and at times lets it get the best of him. He has little patience and does not have time for substitutions or modifications to accommodate dietary restrictions. If you are vegetarian or vegan, your limited to one entree and 2 appetizers. He sometimes tries to put on a friendly facade but it never works out. The place has 4 stars because it's city-quality in a town that lacks variety. The rating says 2 but if you're in a pinch, and stick to the menu, it's worth it.

Oh, Momo's... I want to love you, but you need to clean up your act! Everytime I go here, I feel like the place is dirty. Bar near an open trash, garbage on the floor, cheap decor, cheap silverware. My hubs likes your food but I feel it is inconsistent at best. I wish there was a way to combine your menu (properly and consistently cooked) with the cleanliness and decor of the neighboring establishment.
i have only had takeout, but the food is absolutely delicious. i've had a few different things and have liked it all. good portions too.
We go to this restaurant whenever we want thai food locally. Recently, I got tempura basa in panang sauce. It was fantastic. This place has great service, lovely decor, and consistently good food.
Good drink specials (half off beer & wine) during Happy Hour (even on Saturday), and the Hookah was $10 during Happy Hour. The bartenders were very nice.

Visited Jasmine Thai over the weekend...it's been some time since my last visit, but their service and food are consistent. The Chicken Pad Thai is still excellent with a huge portion (that I somehow still manage to eat). My sister had their Thai Curry, which was also great. The food took almost no time to make it our table and the waitresses were great. Still one of the best choices in Tampa Bay and a great choice in Brandon next to Ploy Thai.

What a gem. This place is great. Quick service, nice ambiance, and WOW good food. The prices are very reasonable and the portions are perfect. I had the chicken tiki masala and it didn't disappoint. Only caveat- the street parking is metered, so bring quarters. Totally worth it.
Love this place!! So happy it opened up on Calle Real!! They are great for all diets, omnivore, vegetarian and vegan!!!

We were looking for a new place to celebrate our anniversary so we asked our kids for suggestions. They said Butcher and Bee was highly rated and we couldn't go wrong there. What can I say! The food was absolutely delicious! Each of the 4 mezze items we chose was individually brought to our table with a bit of fanfare and rightly so. These were not just a bowl of carrots, turnips, feta and dates. No, each one had been specifically prepared to bring out the best flavors. And the braised lamb/couscous, wow!! My husband really enjoys lamb and this by far is now our favorite! If that wasn't enough, we topped our meal off with the dark chocolate pot! I can't even....! The ambience of the cozy patio and an exceptional server made this special time very memorable. Thanks Butcher and Bee!! We'll be back!!

In an area w casual beach bar/beach restaurant type places this stands out with Black tablecloths, attentive service and a slightly classier ambience. Several specials offered daily. Everything we tried was delicious. The lobster bites app, done kind of as a lobster escargot were the highlight of the meal and terrific. Lobster was incredibly flavorful and the sauce it was dunked in complimented it perfectly. Tried a crab cake app special as well (very fresh) along with the Seafood Crepe (shrimp scallops crabmeat and fish) and the Bouillabaisse. The restaurant is Moroccan themed, with a section of the menu devoted entirely to Moroccan style dishes, which we unfortunately did not get to sample, but I would if I returned again. Best food in the area, and top notch service. Would return.

La Va is just a little too inconsistent for me. A lot of the times, I LOVE it here. The coffee is solid, the treats are delish, and the atmosphere is adorable. However, sometimes they miss big. Whenever I order iced tea, it is definitely weak. Also, I hate flavor change ups--when people love something, they want to see it all the time. Additionally, the bagels are less than excellent, which is to be expected in Philly, but embarrassing for a coffee house. Lastly, I hate this new little formal dining thing they're doing. If it works for them, then that's awesome. But IMO, it would be best reserved for Fridays and Saturdays. This is one of the most enjoyable coffee shops at which to do work in G-Ho, and for some people, Thursdays are for working, not dining.
Another delicious meal at Compere Lapin. So sad that they no longer serve the Harvey Jones a wonderful coffee flavored after dinner drink.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Was not sure if i would like this place at first but boy did i change my mind! I cant even remember what i ordered but the food was OUTSTANDING. At a reasonable cost with large servings you cant beat this place. Awesome food and the owner is really nice! He even gave us free food haha. Doesnt seem like much but this place is amazing!

Pad Thai....delicious! Drunken Noodles....delicious! Crying Tiger salad....dear god best thing ever delicious! Fortune Bags....yum yum belly jiggle yum! Everything we ate was great, service was friendly/attentive, and we left knowing we'd be back again. ALL HAIL THE SPICE!!! oh yeh try the thai iced tea + thai coffee!

Stop #4 on the NOLA food + cocktail tour... me thinks we should've quit while we were ahead. We were lucky to grab two seats at the bar on a Saturday night. My "Wry Smile" cocktail was fine (rye, rhubarb, grand poppy, sherry), but my gf's "Louisville Slugger" was too smoky my taste. I was thinking "smoked vanilla" would be smoky-toasty, but it was smoky-scotchy. Not for me. We ordered the stracciatella, one of my fave cheeses, which came with roasted squash and hazelnuts. Unfortunately, the nuts had a rancid flavor that ruined the dish. The server was totally cool about it, took it away and didn't charge us even though we had already taken more than a few bites. IDK, maybe it's just me since the place was busy, but not a place I'd go back to.
Came here with a small party and we had a really good time. The food is really good and so is the atmosphere. Would definately come back! The pad thai was amazing as well as the stir fry tofu!

This place has outstanding food. I come from a part of the country with lots of good Indian food but this place had the best Pala Paner I've had. The rice and garlic Naan were both good also. Decor is nothing special but the food is worth the trip.

Delicious Pad Thai! Very small parking area, so be prepared to park elsewhere and walk. Parking behind the building is available, but be ready for a steep hill! Food is worth the weird parking or walking required to eat here!

This place is definitely worth trying once, and it's especially fun with a large group. The food is average/decent, but there is a cute appeal to the unique presentation. Also, it's easy for communal bonding to ensue when everyone's eating with their hands and sharing family portion dishes. A bit of advice: during the first course, hoard up on pita slices when the server passes around the pita basket. While most of us politely fished out a couple wedges of pita and passed the basket on, the wise one who'd eaten at Marrakesh before stowed away an impressive amount of pitas in his towel. Ten minutes later, he came to our rescue when the rest of us all ran out of pitas while being far from finishing the platter of great eggplant dip/veggie platter. The pita basket only gets passed around once, so remember to stock up!

Impressed at how pulled together everything was, considering they'd been open less than a month when I went. Brussels and Oxtail grilled cheese were EXCELLENT. Octopus was also good but not AS delicious. Was too full for the gnocchi with egg, but that looked great on the next table over. Cocktails were also tasty. Nice atmosphere and looks like they have a small patio for warmer weather. Would definitely go back for more.

Excellent food! My favorite dishes are the kilkil (green beans), gomen (with cabbage), and beef alicha. I'm someone who likes flavor but not spicy and these dishes fit the bill! The restaurant was practically empty tonight which was a shame. You should absolutely try this restaurant! Get your hands messy!

We have eaten at the old location a number of times but the new one is MUCH more convenient so we've been super excited for it to open. We sat at the bar and ordered a sushi roll to start, pad Thai and drunken noodles. Everything was really good! We saw a number of other rolls and also the ceviche prepared and now can't wait to return to try more!

Wicked good. The guac was small, as others have noted, but the flavor was excellent. Sat at a table by the bar on a very busy Saturday night, but service was top-notch - server checked in enough to keep the drinks fresh but didn't over-do it (and that's not always an easy task). I'm typically more of a beer kinda guy, but went with the cocktails here and was not disappointed - strong pours with balanced flavors. And, as others have also mentioned, the interior is really nice and very surprising given the outside appearance of the building.

Another grand hole in the wall for many who have no clue about what they are missing! Yes it is not much, but the food was so good! and price cheap!!! They do things a little different since they are a market as well. So this is how it works cause when you first walk in you are not sure. You begin in the market go ahead and walk through to your left and grab a table, wait for the waiter and then go back into the market and pick your drink and sit back down. order your food and experience the only middle eastern food worth eating in Boise!

I'm honestly just incredibly excited that a "real" Chinese restaurant has opened in UCity, esp one that serves soup dumplings (!!!) It is slightly pricier than their Chinatown counterparts, but that's probably to be expected, given the location. Their dan dan noodles were a little strange, as some other reviewers mention. The sauce was good, on par with Han Dynasty, but the noodles themselves seemed a little overcooked and oversoft. Probably not my favorite thing on the menu-the dumplings, however, were very solid.

One of THE BEST Thai places in Nashville. I'm in love with this place. If you like curry, definitely get it here! Everyday is a different curry day, but my favorite is the green curry. The pineapple curry is also very good as well. If you want noodles, GET THE PAD THAI. When my boyfriend and I come here one of us always gets it. It's fricken delicious. Also, their thai tea is super good! MOST IMPORTANTLY: GET THE MANGO STICKY RICE. Usually it is sold out by dinner. I always order it first, or go during lunch, so that doesn't happen.

I am not a touchy-feely-aura-voodoo-new age type person despite being from California or having Louisiana lineage. However, this place had a bad vibe. The hostess was nice. She sat me, my friend and her dog on the patio. About 5 minutes later she apologizes for the waiter not having approached us yet and stated she would remind him. Another 10 minutes passed and our waiter charged the table chastising us for having sat ourselves. I explained that the hostess had sat us. At that point we should have left. We still didn't have menus, nor did the table next to us who had been there before we arrived. The band was fine. The decor was nifty. The patio was lovely, even at night. Our server's attitude did not improve, nor did the frequency of his visits to any of the tables. Parts of our order were missing or incorrect or far from tasty. My pal had a Mojito assuming it would be fabulous given the name of the establishment. In fact, that was the only thing that was NOT tasty. The rest of the meal was tasty enough for her to return the next evening. She informed me that despite a different wait she had bad vibes and a not so nifty experience but I'll let her review it. I do not see myself returning here on my next visit. To quote a wise lolcat, "do not want."

I had terrible customer service when ordering delivery through doordash. I payed for a vermicelli bowl with egg rolls but only received egg rolls. When I called the staff, they said it wasn't their problem it was doordash's.

Not a great experience. Our server was so quick to walk away and not helpful in answering our questions about the menu. When I ordered, she told me that was "brave" for my choice. She never came back to ask us how our food was or if we needed anything else until the end of our meal. Another server / bartender was walking around with his stomach out... like no undershirt... his shirt was too small, so his stomach and underwear were visible. The food was okay, but they charged $4 for an 8oz cup of less than mediocre coffee.

Humble establishment, but the best gyros I've had in the area. Generous amount of tasty meat in the sandwich. Unless they're really busy, some of the meat will have nice bark. You actually get more meat on the gyros salad. Pitas are made local and always very fresh.

If you're looking for somewhere a little different to go for dinner, you should definitely try Zagol. It's great to bring a group of friends to, and good for vegetarians. I usually get the 3 choice one, which, if I remember correctly is $25 to share between 2 people. However, the thing I enjoy most about coming to Zagol is the service, which is fantastic.

The food and drinks here are great and it's beyond cute, but it needs to up its game on operations. The hostess tells you the bar is open seating, until, after waiting for 20 minutes for a seat and one opens up, the bartender tells you there's a list and you can't sit there. So you ask to be on the list that you should have been told about in the first place by the hostess. Then, a server tells you that those seats at the bar are for you, until someone sits down in one of them and for whatever reason the server won't tell that person to get out of your seat. Then, when two seats finally open up, maybe 45 minutes later, and really are for you and your date, a group of four angles for that corner and you have to nearly fight with them to take your seats because they too have been misinformed about this being first come first served. You finally take your seats and enjoy the food, drinks, and ambience, but you are all around pissed off by the experience and poor execution by the restaurant. I'll go back but I'm hoping for a better experience next time around.

Delivery took nearly 2 hours and arrived with only two thirds of what we ordered. Food was good. Came hot despite the long wait time. Manager said she would refund us for the missing part of our order as we weren't going to wait another 2 hours for it to arrive. With so many other options for Chinese food, we don't plan to order from here again. Beware of a long wait time and potentially a messed up order.

I recently discovered this place while driving through the Northeast and was pleasantly surprised. The dining area is nothing special, but the lack of interior charm is more than made up for by the food. I ordered my Indian restaurant standard - Saag Paneer - and it was among the best I've had. The portion was large, as was the side of rice it came with. In addition, the prices are fairly low and the service was friendly and accommodating. Don't let the strip mall setting fool you and check out Zaika the next time you're in this area.

I have to drop my rating to three stars - only because of the poor service. The service was a little slow on my first visit (after which I wrote this review), but having been there a few more times, the food is as good, but I'm sorry to say that the service really needs to pick up. The one waiter there could use a little tact too; instead of handing me the check to sign and tip once he'd swiped my card, he proceeded to ask me how much of a tip I wanted to enter. Given that I was a little miffed by the already slow service, I wasn't amused by this lack of etiquette.

The Pork banh mi was mediocre at best. The French bread was harder than I'm used to eating from any Vietnamese restaurant. The flavors weren't there. The sandwich was bland compared to other Pork banh mis that I've tasted in the city. I also had the avocado and green bean rice. Basically it was white rice with black pepper. Placed On top of the rice were three slices of avocado and a handful of whole cooked green beans. There was also a fried egg. The egg was hard cooked instead of runny. It wasn't that tasty. All I could taste was black pepper. This was very disappointing.
I had the chicken pad thai. I mark this place as a "2 star" because I have had better pad Thai in areas of west county. This place isn't bad. It is just sort of "mehhhh." The service is good.

As we all know NOLA is famous for its unique cuisine. We have been here for a week and the combo of cajun food and a strict drinking regimen have left our bellies in need of some healing soup...We are big fans of Pho back home in CT so we found the closest spot and gave it a shot. The broth is clean and fresh with unbelievable flavor. Sometimes the meat in Pho can be chewy and fatty. The beef was tender and delicious! We also had the fresh spring rolls with shrimp and pork. YUM. This is a great option for those in New Orleans looking for a break from the traditional New Orleans food and heal their aching tummies from the night before.

I came here on a whim with my sister to find a cozy place to sit while filling out my applications. Hungry, I ordered a sandwich to go with my vanilla coffee and boy was I in for a surprise. I never thought I'd find spinach on a sandwich to be fantastic, especially when served as a panini. There was a mistake made but was quickly fixed along with a free coffee on my next visit. I'm normally one of those chicks who slide through Starbucks and think 'welp, that's coffee'. I can truly say coming here has changed my perception of what a coffee shop is. I'm definitely going to go back if I'm ever in the neighborhood again.

This place is essentially the chipotle or qdoba of Indian food. You choose your style, weather it be bowl, naan pizza, or wrap, then choose meats, sauces, add ins, etc. Being a steamed table, the temperature and freshness of the food varies between choices. For example, I ordered one chicken samosa and one veg samosa, and both were barely warm. The quality of the chicken was not the greatest either, but did like the vegetarian options (Chole and paneer). The sauces were decent as well. Prices for the quantity are very fair, especially at dinner time. It is somewhere to go if u want something cheap, quick, and decent, however is by no means rivaling other Indian restaurants in terms of quality.

Bui's is legit, I always get the breakfast sandwiches which are really cheap and the eggs are fresh. I get them with srichicha or bui sauce and sometimes with coffee or a juice. It is really cheap and when the line isn't long for lunch, i get a chicken sandwich gyro or chicken parm which are all on point. Mr. and Mrs. Bui are really nice people and wonderful cooks

Honestly , i only give this place a 2 star because the food is great . What really upsets me is the owner/waitress . I have been eating at this restaurant ever since it has been open . The owner first was very very nice when she takes orders , serves etc . I have realized that she is only nice to other ethnicity that are not Indonesians & her friends . She has a totally different personality when Indonesians come to eat there . For example , when someone else ask for water , she'll say oh sure , do you need anything else ? But when I ask for water , she'll just walk away , or just gives me attitude . She'll come back give me water & i'll say thank you , & she would just give me more attitude . I have noticed today when I went there , someone asked for more chilli & she screamed what?! You already asked for some ! She said it in a very rude upsetting way . But someone else that was Caucasian asked the same thing & she was glad to give it to them . I hope you read this Betty .
We love this restaurant. The food is delicious and the service is good. Good prices. The interior is truly Indian decor. We have been regular customers since it opened.
The best panang curry! Both vegan and meat options. We come here weekly during lunch time. Service is always on par.

Easy place to look over and never see. Glad we tried it out! Many options to choose from with the specialties being Indian and Chinese. I went in with my wife and MIL on a quiet Saturday night, only one other group dining. We were treated very well by a staff that genuinely seemed happy to serve us. Our server recommended the fried cauliflower appetizer and it was amazing!! Highly recommend it! It was chunks of breaded, fried cauliflower in a spicy/sweet sauce with onions, garlic and green pepper. Again, it was awesome, we all loved it. For entrees we had tikka masala, curry and a coriander/ginger chicken served with two servings of garlic naan bread. The tikka masala was the favorite. Very flavorful and perfectly creamy. The others were also good, but a touch on the salty side. The naan was delicious and pre-cut up, which I like. Prices are reasonable.

Yup, the food is as good as everyone says. Love the flat bread and bright green olive oil, love the whole fish specials, love the sauteed mussels, love the hummus, love the desserts. Things I'm not crazy about - the wait (we live nearby and will only go if we can get there by 6 on a weekday), the cramped quarters, the rushed feel you get from the servers occasionally. Hint - if you forget to BYOB, you can pick up something 'to go' at the New Wave across the street.

Came with a party of 9, the restaurant is byob, so it's nice to be able to bring a few bottles of wine. I was also accompanied by my girlfriend, we decided to split the charcoal platter for 2. I'm Glad to say the platter was excellent, great charcoal taste and a wide variety, with a good portion of proteins. I will definitely return. Furthermore, Yani was our server and was excellent our whole party enjoyed the food, the atmosphere as well as the service.

First time and really enjoyed it. The tofu soup was excellent, tasty with yummy tofu and vegetables. We didn't have reservations but they found a place for us anyway ... Thank goodness because we loved the food and we will be back again.

I honestly don't see what the hype is about here. The ONLY thing that is good there is the gnocchi. That's it. I don't mind the tight atmosphere, but the tables are low so your knees hit it and if you are anywhere 5'4 and above forget it. So uncomfortable. For as hard as it is to get in there sometimes due to availability I was hoping for better food.

FOOD: + + + LOVED the Whipped Feta, Roasted Carrots, & Outsider cocktail, but the Tiger-Style Brussels and Burger were just OK. VALUE: $ $ $ 4 shared small plates + 1/2 burger & brussels + cocktail = $30+ (Pst! If you want extra pita for your Mezze that'll cost you $3.) SERVICE: + + + Staff were pleasant, but we did have a hard time getting checks split. VIBE: Fun, young, hip. Lighting was dim so it was hard to read the menu. TIPS: B&B is located right next to Fat Bottom Brewing. (You might miss it since there isn't a prevalent street sign.)

What an experience! Usually, I am not that adventurous when it comes to trying foods, but I had only heard good things, and they're perfect for large parties, so it made sense to book a bachelorette party dinner here. And did they deliver! First, it's a flat rate of $25 per person and BYO. That's basically all you need to know. Second, the staff is super friendly and accommodating. We asked if the last few courses could be rushed (we were late for another reservation) and they did not mind. But let me tell you, if we didn't have to be somewhere else, I could have stayed there for another 2 hours. You definitely lose track of time as they bring you course after course of delicious, fresh food (7 courses altogether). And you get to eat with your hands! Super fun atmosphere and great food. Definitely check out this South Street gem!
They serve up a good cheesesteak and also have great specials. This is by far the best food truck in the area and they are fast.

Usually when I want Jamaican food I drive to Philly and I will continue to do so! Ordered from here online than get a phone call they don't have oxtails!! What Jamaican restaurant runs out of oxtails? So I said ok I don't want a replacement. We will just order the one platter curry chicken, please put gravy on the rice. I called 2x to make sure I wasn't being charged for two platters! The chicken was ok but minimal for the price and of course no gravy on the rice!! Food was ok but I can get way better from most places in Philly for less money! More food and they never run out of oxtails !!! Don't waste your time! And of course I was charged for food I didn't receive so now I have to deal with that!!!!!

After living 25 years thinking Greek food was like the kind served in Daphne's Cafes, I was blown away by Zorba's. Each dish has obviously been nurtured to the best possible quality and flavor, seasoned and cooked into perfection. You're probably discarding my opinion since my comparison is like Kraft Singles vs. smoked gouda, but hey, I love Daphne's and fake cheddar slices. They remind me of college :) The service is also great. I've been there twice, the first time as a save haven from the soreness and cold from visiting the Eastern State Penitentiary in winter. I had no idea I'd walk into Greek heaven! It also happened to be Valentine's Day, so we got free heart-shaped ice cream dessert!

Glad I discovered this place, thanks to Groupon! The orange smoothy was so good! It wasn't too sweet and it was nice and cold after being outside in the sun for hours that morning. I ordered the Ginger Thai noodles with chicken, and oh good heavens was it huge! I filled up at lunch then took the rest home, and had dinner and two lunches out of the left overs! The servings for the other dishes I saw brought out were equally huge! And the turtle cheesecake 0-0 so. dang. good. Lots of tables, not too crowded, the wait staff was very nice and attentive. It was a really good lunch!
Disappointing chicken pad thai. Very dry and lacking flavor. I sadly wouldn't recommend this place. Fortunately i ordered take out, but the restaurant itself is quite small, cramped, and rather loud.

A wonderfully quaint little restaurant in an otherwise nondescript shopping mall, La Saigon punches way above its weight. The curries are hearty and delicious, the spring rolls full of flavor and the service fast and polite. Highly recommended for a night out seeking a touch more adventure than your standard Thai or Chinese night in. BYOB. Try the Princess Platter for a full tour of the appetizers, the eggplant & shrimp in a garlic sauce and any of the rice noodle wraps for a fun twist.

We came in on a tip off from a co-worker in love with this place. We had really high hopes but were pretty let down. The best thing about this restaurant is the very kind staff. Not very attentive, but very kind. He ordered a tea that never came out, but was still on our bill. They happily fixed it but he went the whole dinner without his drink haha. I ordered the massaman curry with veggies and tofu. It had been a long time favorite Thai dish of mine but I was greatly disappointed with this one. The curry was a really strange sour taste, and I barely ate any of it at all. There was zero spice to it either. Husband got the Pumpkin curry with beef and shrimp. He expected a much better taste as well, but was let down. He said his was at least more flavorful than mine, but really wished they had asked how spicy we wanted our dishes. Neither dish was spicy at all. I see a lot of reviews hailing this as the best in SB. I am so sorry to have to vote differently.

A great little place for pho on Jasper Avenue. The prices are in line with what you can find in Chinatown, and the quality is excellent. The beef in my pho tai came already cooked (it should be pink and cook in the bowl), but was tender and lean. The flavour of the broth was excellent and multi-layered. There were no herbs or bean sprouts served to the side (maybe you have to ask?). I also started with an order of onion cakes. They were very crispy, almost to the point of shattering in the a few spots, and needed a lot of the sweet and hot sauce for flavour. I like them saltier and chewier on the insides. Service is quick and friendly, and the place is very clean and bright. I would definitely come here again.

This was my first time to Suraya and it did not disappoint! I went with a group for brunch and we loved everything about it. The market at the front is super cute and a great place to look around while waiting for a table or your reservation. The decor from the mugs and plates to the wall decor was super cute!
