Now for the food, it was all great. We all had coffee and a cortado. The cortado could have been hotter, but it was still delicious. We started with the Za'atar, Labne, Olive, Cucumber, Tomato, Mint which came out rolled up like a burrito. Delicious! Next, we had the babba ganoush and slow-roasted Lamb hummus which both came with pita on the side. We finished off with the gravlax, which was the tables favorite dish. Overall, the food was amazing and I cannot wait to return to try more!

Been here many times through many owners. Still pretty good for a cheap Indian buffet. What I love is that they still hand write the names of the food on a paper placed in front of the dish. So unpolished! I guess that makes it the real deal. It's fast and good and cheap.

Haven't been to San's for a long time so we went for lunch the other day. Linda was our waitperson and she really did a nice job. The reason we haven't been to Sam's is because we eat at home a lot, we both like to cook. When we go out there are a lot of choices and Sam's ends up as one of many in in a very long rotation. Our lunch was good and the view and the smell of the Gulf is great, hard to beet. We don't come here at night anymore because of the noise level and it's just too busy for my taste. I can't handle smoke anymore and I found that at night there's a lot more smoke then at lunch. Want to have good food, not great, but good and on the Gulf; Sam's is as good as most in this area.
We really enjoyed our lunch there. Very tasty and reasonably priced. Look forward to going back. Service was perfect.

I've been going here for years, but am just now writing a review because I love this place! First, the owner is AWESOME! I love him. He is sweet and funny. Second, the food is amazing and fresh. I always get the pad thai with tofu. I love it. Last, the place is tiny and parking is a pain.

The pad thai with tofu was excellent! And a generous portion, took half home for lunch the next day. I was there for a late lunch on my own, so had missed any normal lunch crowd; it was quiet but the service was good. It's nice inside, would make for a good date night place. My only negative was that the fried tofu appetizer was undercooked and soggy. Would like to go back to try the crispy basil duck, and think the soups will be very tempting on chilly days...

I haven't been here in a few years, but I was pretty hungry and stopped in here for dinner last night. I got the octopus plate which was quite awesome. Rice, vegetables, potatoes mixed up with slices of octopus. It was very, very tasty. My only complaint about the meal was that there wasn't more. I finished off the meal with a desert I forget how to pronounce. It was like shredded wheat, but much more tasty. Every time I go here I leave nice and satisfied.

Awesome food, small place. There are only 10 or so tables in this tiny restaurant, but the wait is well worth it. The food is delicious, the prices are fair, the portions are fair. The portions are decent, but the food is really great! I highly recommend the spicy fried rice with chicken and the pad thai. Yumm! The service is bleh though, nothing special. We had to ask for water after dying of thirst from the spicy fried rice, lol.

Started with four small plates the roasted carrots, kale salad, bacon wrapped dates and "hot potatoes." All four were amazing. Followed with the whole trout and the octopus poke'. Both were fantastic. I can't speak highly enough of this place, really enjoyed the atmosphere and environment as a whole. Will def visiting again shortly.

The best spot to eat on campus!! Unsure if it's just beginner's luck but Santorini's is insanely good for it's price. I don't know much about Greek food but I've tried both Aladdin's and Lovin Oven and have to say that this one beats them both in quality and value. The portions are huge, I got the gyro plate and they actually stacked that meat up to the top. I usual eat like a fatass and had a hard time finishing the meal. It's the only place to eat on campus that won't make you feel like you just gibbed for 7 bucks. Try it out now cause I just don't believe any food place on campus can stay this good before it becomes corrupt.

I was pleased to find a solid take-out Middle Eastern place in Manayunk, especially considering most of the takeout food in the area is average at best. While Israel set the standard for me for falafel and obviously can't be topped, the falafel at Smiley's has a nice mix of flavors. Though the size could be better, the price is reasonable. My only real complaint is the falafel balls are not crispy. An added crunch would be great. The chicken gyro pita was just okay. Will definitely put Smiley's in the local take-out rotation. Bonus for good smoothies. (I have been twice and have yet to see Smiley himself)

We happened to visit this restaurant by accident! And my-oh-my wasn't I surprised!!! The decor appealed to me majorly coz I am a huge collector of Buddha idols!! ;-) Coming to the food... I was quite apprehensive about the food, so my husband and I decided to pick some safe options... We had the Masala Soda, Mango lassi, Chicken 65, Chicken biriyani, Kerala Pepper chicken gravy and Garlic Nan... The mango lassi was simply delicious!! 5 stars for the lassi... However the masala soda was a disappointment... They use coke or pepsi and add very little chat masala and that's supposed to be masala soda!! That's silly!!! Chicken 65 was very different but really good! Chicken biriyani was decent... Kerala pepper chicken gravy was amazing!!! Garlic nan wasn't the best we've had... It wasn't as soft as a good garlic nan should be... but it wasn't bad! We'd love to visit this restaurant again if we're around that area again!

Yet another restaurant I love to frequent because of the delicious food and cozy atmosphere. I especially love the curry dishes--from red to yellow to green, they're all superb. The cream of mushroom soup is heavenly, as is the Jungle Queen (vegetarian option), Jungle King (meat-lovers option), Wild Ginger with stir fried vegetables and pretty much everything else on the menu. In fact, I find Nadia Thai to be better than several of the Philly Thai restaurants. Definitely a great spot for quality Thai food in the 'burbs that's fairly reasonably priced!

I hadn't had Indian food before going here the first time, but I am obsessed now. I've only had their buffet at lunch, but it's all I ever need. The food is incredible. It is a small place so try to avoid going right at noon or you'll have to wait. I seriously cannot say enough good about this place though. I dream of the food here.

First off, I love Pollo! LOCATION This Seminole location is great because it's conveniently located to the newer shops at the Seminole City Center. Parking is fairly simple (private lot) and they have drive-thru of course. FOOD I am addicted to their mango iced tea - love to mix the sweet with the unsweet. Their wings (a mere $2.50 for 5) are delicious - but a bit skimpy, which must be why the entire portion is under 300 calories. My usual order is a Lite TropiChop - grilled chicken, brown rice, tomato and onion - perfect size and always tastes great! My hubs loves the chicken with beans and yellow rice, Dad loves the chicken and ribs, rice and beans while Mom loves the chicken with string beans and mac and cheese. Trips to Pollo have become a Sunday dinner family affair ... No idea how that happened. LOL. SERVICE Upon my latest visit (11/6/17) I realized they no longer have table service. They now call you up Panera-style which is fine since we weren't really supposed to tip and that makes me feel uncomfortable anyway. Though the service is great and managers are always helpful, I feel as if both this location and the Largo Mall (Ulmerton) location could really use an extra employee or two. They seem somewhat understaffed to me.

I would have given it five stars but they no longer accept restaurant.com coupons and it still shows up on restaurant.com. They definitely should remove that because I'm sure I was not the only person who had a coupon and was disappointed when it could not be used. Now on to the good part, the food. Oh the food, and the price, fantastic. Don't forget to get the hibiscus drink, you won't be sorry.
Several of us ate here for my mother-n-law's birthday. WOW - great food. Everything was fresh and delicious. I'm a big fan of Thai food and this may be as good as it gets.

The food itself is pretty good: falafel and lentil soup are both very good. Chicken and steak are fine. The staff are friendly but can get flustered easily. Though that may go away in time since this place is relatively new. My only real complaint is how often they are "out" of one of the main three (falafel, steak, or chicken) ingredients. And it's not only when they're overloaded with people. I've come during the lunch rush and other times when it's slow. Always hear "it'll be five or ten minutes for ____". There's 3 things to keep track of, not 20.

Good place, Just in the intersection of E Bush and n rentew. Mind the GPS it might take u to Walgreen a block away, and you'll save some precious time. It is a bit expensive for Middle Eastern food, and it is defiantly not for weekday visit, but more like a weekend visit, Bush garden is just across the street, and that's the only nice thing to see really. Good food, but Over priced.

Vegetarians everywhere, rejoice! There are so many delicious veggie options here that are not a salad or a veggie burger. Our group shared a ton of mezze plates and a few mains. The menu rotates but this is always their style. The whipped feta (ask for pita AND cucumbers) is not to be missed! The brussels were also delicious. The atmosphere is lovely. Reservations are accepted and I think are a good idea! we went on a tuesday and it was pretty busy in there, i'm sure weekends are jam packed.

Came in for the food, came out with no food. I was very excited to try out this place. My cousin and I passed by it and decided to try it out on a whim. We were excited when we walked in seeing how authentic it was. I ordered the goat and rice and watched it get packed into a container but when I reached the register - it never showed. Or none of the workers even acknowledged me as a customer at that point...... We waited for 20 minutes as we saw customers ahead of us order their food and pay for their food while my goat and rice disappeared and my cousin's order of fish never even made it to the front. I had a lot of hope for this place but the way they totally ignored us or were just disorganized in keeping our order together was a big turn off in ever coming back.

So, we saw that this place had good ratings and 1 $ pricey. But it's been a few hours since we've eaten and two of my friends have gotten food poisoning, and one is in the ER right now. I'm sitting in the waiting room, furious. They done fucked up.

My absolute FAVORITE restaurant in the city. I know the family personally and I love them they are authentic Greek folk! The menu is delectable and wide. Any and everything you could choose from the menu is the best thing to order, seriously! Whenever I go, I get the lamb and potatoes--YUM! The calamari is pretty great too.

Super place. Vegas look and feel inside and out. Exceptional service, Food was great, owner came over to make sure we were happy-which we were. Well worth checking out. One note, avoid the tables in the middle isle by the bar, way too noisy.

My partner and I were overall fans of the Jamaican Jerk Hut. Small, quaint place with a long wait - but definitely worth it if you're into some spicy, unique food. Definitely beware that when they say spicy - it means SPICY! I usually like hot wings, but they were over the top a bit for me. My partner loved the heat, though (even though he was sweating from it). The coconut shrimp is delicious - well battered, tasty, crisp, with sweet coconut milk. Also loved their chicken soup. The wings were SUPER spicy, couldn't get through them, but my boyfriend loved it. The flavor beneath the heat was divine. The quarter jerk chicken was also good - but we definitely should have gotten the sauce on the side. The wings were hot enough, so we couldn't get through the chicken. We loved it here, but I actually don't think we'll be going back. It seemed like after you tried a few things, the flavors meshed together, and weren't quite as unique as they first seemed. A good find in the city, especially if you like to try different food - but not necessarily my go-to place. I was expecting a bit more, but was still pleased!
Om om om om! Tasty lamb, rice, and salad with yogurt sauce two minutes' walk from work? For $5 you say? Yes please. An added bonus: sub-5 min wait.
wonderful! great price. not disappointed The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating

Wow what a treat! We were really blown away by the service, the food, and the cocktails! We got the pork belly pops which were phenomenal! The ramen and the pho were absolute delicious. Our waiter, Alex, was super friendly and knowledgable about the food and he gave us great recommendations. We both got the Japanese Old Fashioned...amazing!!! This place is absolutely worth the visit. Prices are extremely reasonable too! We will be back!
Our favorite Thai restaurant in town. Every meal we've had there has been great. Good food, good prices, and friendly service. They also have a separate vegan menu which is awesome.

Delicious food and great service! Went here for dinner tonight and had such a great experience! I love great Indian food and this place really exceeded my expectations! The restaurant was very clean and everyone was so pleasant! I will be coming back!

I've been going here since high school, which is 40 years now. I've gone to all the locations but recently the Chesterfield. Last night we had dinner and I had Athenian Filet and it was the most tender, flavorful and hard to beat the price. My husband had the Mousaka, which I sampled and also delicious. Most importantly, the service is awesome. It's almost like you are being served like you are the only customers there.

Tasty, tasty. I love the grilled meats and veggies. I like the Sansom Kebob the best, it's got a mix of lamb, chicken and beef along with onions, peppers, and tomatoes. This place is a little hole in the wall. You have to walk downstairs to enter it, but once inside you'll see the place is clean and the service is very good. I like the relaxed way the place feels, and the things on the walls, from maps to ethnic clothing, are interesting to look at. So are the Christmas lights...there's always time for a festival.
This was an amazing dinner! Great fresh foos awesome service ! The best Indian restaurant I've ever eaten!thank you!!

This is easily my new favorite restaurant in Philadelphia. Not only is the space absolutely breathtaking (& I can't wait to return when the courtyard opens), the food is spectacular and the wine list amazing. They have Middle Eastern wines that are exquisite and difficult to find anywhere else. Was happy to spend my birthday here are this year!

The Saganaki appetizer is amazing the ambiance with table clothes while listening to "The Morgantown Duo " live entertainment is great! Amy is an awesome professional waitress while address our every want and needs! The sea bass was fresh with an great taste. Mr.Harry is the owner who greeted us with a delightful smile and hand shake! Thanking each and everyone for selecting his awesome restaurant! Most of their professionals waitress & waiters has been at this location for over 18 years or more! I love their great caring services with a smile while have amazing food!

Not great. The pad see ew was bland both in presentational color and flavor. Pad see ew is literally bursting with flavor. The noodles are to be allowed to brown, if not almost partially blacken on a griddle and a VERY rich sauce including fermented soy bean is to be added throughout cooking - making the product slippery in texture and dark brown. These are grey at best and there is ZERO flavor. The chicken is all dry. The pineapple fried rice was good, but a monkey can make pineapple fried rice. Thai Basil dish was soggy - green beans were flaccid and tasteless. Sauce was overly oily and salty. Just bad.

Nice looking place and good service yet, coming from P.R., we didn't get what we ordered / were expecting, i.e. ordered a skirt steak ("churrasco") and received cube meat ("bistec"). The same happened with a "Mofongo" that we ordered that was actually a "Mangu" presented as a "Mofongo". Aside from the misinterpretation of these two typical Caribbean entrees, the rice with chicken ("arroz con pollo") and "sancocho" were very nice. Also, a bit pricey for the quality of food we received.
We like the atmosphere, food was ok , our server seemed like she had a bad night! Can you serve wine in a wine glass not a water glass please ?

I went to Layalena Hookah Lounge for the first time today and I enjoyed it thoroughly. it was a great place to warm up your night. Where do I begin...the hookah was magnificent (we tried the Peach and the Guava). I highly recommend to order the hookah with fresh fruit. The fresh mint tea was a great compliment to the hookah.The ambiance was mellow and best of all the service was as best as it can get. Sherif (the owner) was very attentive and tended to our every need. Music was relaxing. You will enjoy it. I will definitely go back for more.

Such a bad place! Would never want to come back to this place! The food was extremely trashy. The server forced us to get the feast which is $25 per person but he gave us food only for one person each. Firstly, it took them almost 30 mins to get the first appetizer and then they got the next course which was extremely salty. They didn't care to make us feel comfortable. People were straight up popping pills. This spot is super shady. They served us fruits as dessert. They gave us a knife and we were supposed to cut the fruits ourself and eat it. Ridiculous place! Gross. Please don't waste your money here. Rather go to any of the other places nearby!

Marrakesh is a great atmosphere for a group. All of the food is served family style and you eat with your hands, so if you find this uncomfortable, this is not the place for you. You should bring a small bottle of hand sanitizer and lots of wine! The food was delicious, and they will accommodate any vegetarians in the group. A belly dancer comes around as you are eating. Minus one star because it was SO HOT when we went in the summer that most of our party was uncomfortable.

Delicious Greek!! I have eaten here several times and the quality, service and taste were very consistent! Tzatziki, Mussels and the Kalamari were perfect starters!! All three were excellent!! For entrees we had the samplers which gave us a little bit of everything. Side note-the Gyro meat is a thinner cut, for those looking for bigger slices-though very tasty. Ultra clean restaurant with super efficient and friendly staff! I would recommend reservations as larger parties seem to fill the back rooms. Lastly, don't forget dessert!! Just finished my leftovers!! Happy customers here!!

Very glad this place is in town as a dining option. Love taking a walk on the beach or in campground, get a beer at Island Brewing, and then come in here for an early dinner. Nice combination dinners, good variety, excellent flavors, ample portions, and reasonably friendly service. This place can get very busy, especially on a weekend evening, but they do take reservations. Another plus is an outdoor dining area. We enjoy taking visitors and friends here for dinner, and they seem to enjy this place quite a bit, too.

From the rustic bells hanging from the beautiful stainless-steel cart to the garlic surrounding the counters, to the music and singing and dancing of the chef -- you know you have stepped into a special microcosm divorced from its surroundings, then the food, warm pungent deep-green falafel, charred, perfectly-spiced chicken, amazingly fresh salad with large green grapes that look like they were picked from his own garden. In return, you have to learn and accept the rules of this mad genius of food. Pay attention to the patrons before you then go boldly to your turn. Don't ask for Hummus unless you want to be banished to Mama's.

Really loved our dinner and appetizers. The Scallops, and Butterfish were to die for. Such a wonderful place BYOB so bring your bottle of wine and enjoy. We really enjoyed the flourless chocolate cake which was rich and amazing.

Why is it that when there are more than one location for a restaurant that they can't both be good? Maybe once upon a time, Erawan was good but as of late, it is dark, dead and cold. The service isn't terrible but the food could use a pick me up. Depend on what you order, some items are better than others. My first time here, I ordered Pai Thai. I don't know why I keep ordering Pad Thai at Thai places and hope they would be amazing. Of course, the Pad Thai ended up a disappointment as the noodles tastes like straight up peanut butter sauce and not the light lime, fish sauce that Thai cuisine is known for. (For the best Pad Thai go to Circles Contemporary Asian 1516 Tasker St or Jane G). Anyhow, on my latest visit this year, the seafood salad I ordered was terrible. It wasn't cold or warm but somewhere in between making you feel bleh. Also didn't taste fresh and the sauce was lacking. Overall, the location has potential. However, with new places popping up daily, you have to really consider if it is worth it.
Dont come here! Service sucked, food sucked. This is nothing but a tourist trap. Enough said.

Really good authentic Puerto Rican dishes prepared fresh daily. Relleno de Papa de Carne 8 (Ground Beef Stuffed Potato Puff) One of my favorites and Empanadilla de jueyes 10 (Crab meat bite size turnover) Always a winner in my book, I would highly recommend this to anyone looking for great authentic Latin cuisine.

For what it is (Indian take-out), I love this place. It is cheap, easy, clean, and the food is always tasty. I live very closeby, so I'm here at least a couple times a week. I'm in and out in five minutes with some tasty food from the buffet and usually some mango ice cream ($2, ask for it at the check-out). It is always spotlessly clean and I feel like the owners take a lot of pride in it. The selection is a little limited in that they do not serve meat aside from chicken, but what they do have they do very well. Plus, I like that it's probably a little healthier without all the butter.

I went here on a saturday night at around 7:30, the place wasn't that crowded. We waited about 40 minutes and the food still wasn't here. We complained to the waiter and finally recieved our food 15 long minutes later. The food was subpar at best. With the service slow, I WOULD NOT recommend this place.

Four of us tried this new place. The location has had a succession of failed restaurants including the excellent Ming's. It may be the location. You only see the back of the building and have to rely on limited signage . At first, I thought it was a diner-style restaurant without the huge menu. Once inside, it is clean and open. The menu is American and has a lot of choices but not many pages like a diner. It also has a limited selection of Turkish specialties on a separate card. The friendly owners visited with us when they heard that we knew and liked Turkish dishes. We ordered an eggplant appetizer and two entrees, including calves liver. Delicious and authentic! Americans might like a beef kebab option even though the lamb and chicken are truer to Turkey. There were comfort foods. We ordered meatloaf and Turkey with stuffing. They come with two veggies like potatoes and peas. Also you get choice of soup or a really good, fresh salad bar. Oh, and delicious little garlic rolls too. And I almost forgot...choice of cheesecake or apple pie. The servings were extremely generous. We took a whole lot home. We liked everything about the food which is amazing for a fussy bunch like we are. Service was fast, friendly and enthusiastic. Our server was always there when we needed her and yet did not seem to be bothersome. She even had the thought to tell the owners that we were familiar with the Turkish menu. They have some flaws which were more from being overzealous. For instance twice we received small square side plates which took up a lot of space and weren't much used. The appetizers, soup and our salads were still on the table when the entrees arrived. But I would rather have a table covered with food than sit around with an empty table waiting for my dinner. They are new and will sort out these serving flaws over time. I would like this restaurant to survive because I want to keep coming back often. I wouldn't mind if they exercised a little portion control to maintain a viable profit margin. Their prices are reasonable. Just don't cut down the portion too far, guys, I enjoyed the leftovers a lot.

I've had pho all over the country, it's one of my favorite foods. I've lived in Tampa for 3 years now and have always wanted to try this place. For my first experience... Awesome! The waitress was shy but very polite. The pho was probably the best I've ever had. The broth was excellent, the meatballs were delicious with just the right spices. If you like pho go here!

When you first walk in the restaurant you feel welcomed. You are greeted at the door and the ambiance is nice. The music in the background makes you feel like you are in the Caribbean right away. I ordered the Caribbean organic trio which is the Jerk Chicken, Curry Chicken, and Brown stew chicken with rice and peas with a Ginger Beer. The price is great especially knowing that everything is organic. It does take a few minutes for the food to be prepared because it is made fresh as you order but it is well worth the wait. The chicken just falls off the bone. It was very tender and filled with amazing Caribbean flavors. Also very filling. The Ginger Beer was awesome as well. The best part about the food is that it is organic so it taste that much better. At the end I had a chance to meet the owners and I must say that they are Great and Warm folks. Had great Conversations with them and they have done very well with the establishment. Yah Man is a must visit! I don't live in Tampa but when I am in town this will be my go to restaurant. Wish I could give it more than 5 stars.

I was at a conference in NOLA for a week, and Compère Lapin was one of the restaurants I planned to visit. I came in and I was seated right away. I did my typical thing by ordering an entrée, a cocktail, and a dessert. Entree: Pici Pasta/Lobster/Squash Cocktail: TCB Sour Dessert: Toasted Coconut Tres Leches It was all very good. I will totally go back the next time I'm in NOLA!

We held a 80+ person party at Amber. The food was not bad but the service was horrible. The staff and the owner's attitude is that they are doing you a favor by having you there. We asked for more tea first they refuse to serve after some argument they told it will take 1.5 hours. I understand there are not too many options for Indian food in Carmel but given the experience we had, I will not go back to the place and not recommend it to anyone.

This place is a hidden gem. I ordered their green curry with vermicelli, and it was DELICIOUS. I also ordered a medium coffee (from their large list of beverages) and to my delight they use an Aeropress! The coffee was amazingly tasty and smooth. The vibe & decor is hip, minimal and elegant without feeling stuffy. We spoke with the manager afterwards -- he and the rest of the staff are very friendly and thanked us for stopping by. I'll definitely be going back. (I signed up for Yelp today specifically so I could rave about this place!)

Just an update on my visit today. Went with the Deluxe Veggie Wrap. It differs from the straight wrap in that you do not get roasted red peppers and hummus. I snapped a picture of the deluxe veggie wrap and posted it. The deluxe wrap is quite good. I even like the added touch that they toasted the wrap a little bit. I will definitely make sure this happens next time, I liked it so much. I was a little annoyed with the napkin and water situation. First, bathroom dispenser towels had to be used for lunch napkins. Perhaps they ran out. I hope, anyway. As far as the drinks, they have a nice selection. I am not always a soda drinker though. That said, I have to buy water too? I think a water cooler or pitcher of water with cups is not too much to ask for your dine-in customers. But if you want some sort of liquid on your tongue, it will cost ya one buck. I have been back several times and quality has been consistent here.

Stopped by for a quick lunch before a hearing at the nearby courthouse. There's a good variety of lunch specials to choose from. I tried the beef pad Thai. It was solid but not spectacular. I ordered mine extra spicy and it delivered on that front. The portion was a bit small but not surprising considering it was the lunch special portion. The soup and salad that comes with the special was a nice touch. The salad came with a tasty dressing. I would try it again if I'm in town for another hearing or trial.

I love this place. Usually when I go get thai and they give me the options for hotness, I casually wave and say "whatever's hottest." However, the number 5 on the hot chart is not for the faint of heart here, ladies and gentlemen. I had just as much of a hard time putting this Pad Soba down as I did putting it down my throat. Easily one of my most intense conflicts to date. The flavors at this place are unbeatable, and the service is a joy as well. I want you to eat here. You need to eat here.

It's not bad...not super memorable, and not too overpriced. It's hard to really describe green basil as a restaurant, but rather as a very acceptable thai restaurant with all of the classic menu items you've come to expect. While this generalization seems like a cop-out, I will say that I did try a lot of dishes: tom ka soup, egg rolls, coconut fried rice, pad thai, yellow vegetable curry with chicken, fried tofu, and sweet and sour chicken, and the only unique dish was the seafood tom ka soup, since it had a nice tang and was subtly flavored. Everything else tasted as I would expect from a takeout Thai place. The one dish I'd advise against is the banana icecream: it had an incredibly manufactured, non-authentic, flavor that left me drinking two more glasses of water. o Food - 3 stars o Service - 3 stars o Ambiance - 3 stars o Price - 3 stars

I've just realized that I forgot to write a review on this spectacular Greek gem in Fairmount. The staff was incredibly nice & the food was incredibly tasty! In all honesty, this is probably the best Greek restaurant I've been to for the price range in which it's listed. I highly recommend anything on the menu! The calamari was superb! The Fisherman's Platter was mouth watering. My girlfriend and I loved every bite! The bread rather enjoyable as well, and refilled quickly. If you enjoy mushrooms you must try their marinated mushrooms! We will be back, and quite often!

The first thing we noticed was the dirty carpets. I was expecting a nice interior from the other reviews (not sure if Essie reviewed the right restaurant - what table decorations), but it was not impressive at all and the wall decorations very bland. It was early and we were the firsts guests, yet they had to seat the next couple of guests at the 2 tables right next to us. Food was nothing special. We will not go back.

Worst service ever. Overpriced fast food that's worse than basically every restaurant in university service. Wants to charge money for water- just greedy owners who should be put out of business. Recommend to avoid!

Fantastic food and service is steadily improving as they get their feet under them. The owners and servers are as nice as can be, and they anticipate their liquor license being approved soon. All in all, it's now the favorite restaurant in Mount Juliet for me and my wife - we've taken out or eaten there 5 times since they opened less than a month ago! The clean white decor gives a great ambience - I'd call it "fine casual." We have tried all the chicken entrees - they're equally delicious, though could use some diversity. The vindaloo is the most different from the others, which all resemble butter chicken. The biryani are all very-well prepared and makes a great side dish. Naan is so fresh, crispy-yet-soft... I want some now! The flavor absolutely comes alive in your mouth - if you've not tried Indian food, or it's already one of your favorites, you will love the experience at Persis.

So this is my second time in and I've got to say that I have a new place that tastes on my why didn't I come here earlier list. People of Boise we've got a great place to eat with bold flavors that harken of the mideast. If you're tired of the same old same old then come enjoy and rejoice that you've found this gem.

Meh...this place...Given it so many chances and its failed every time. Food is OK...it's the sloooow service, dirty tables that stay that way for way too long, unfriendly hostesses that give the customer a blank stare instead of greeting them as they come through the door, etc. The servers/bartenders openly on their cell phones rather than waiting on guests ready to order. Just don't get it. Management needs to train their staff.
We've ordered the pineapple fried rice and green curry and seriously love the two together. Great service, quick, and so tasty!
Amazing food. Amazing serice. Vadapav is the best and in fact any item on the menu is great. You must come once to taste.

This has been my favorite find since moving to the Indianapolis area. Phan's Kitchen has delicious, well seasoned food that is rich with flavor. No matter what your favorite dish you will find a flavor to fall in love with here! Excellent service, friendly atmosphere, and mouth watering dishes are everything you could hope for in this establishment!
The food was pretty good but not awesome. The service wasn't top notch either. My favorite part was probably the Thai spring rolls. My pad Thai was ok and my wife's yellow curry was about the same.

WOW! 6 of us wear walking around down town Santa Barbara, and we found this nice clean looking Thai restaurant.........OMG! this was the best Thia restaurant I have ever been to......We started off with the Tom Kah soup,that was soooo good and the shimp red curry and brown rice,with some poorman noodles,and more other stuff.......I wish I lived here in Santa Barbara so I can come here offten.......

Best Indian cuisine that I have had since moving to the Nashville area. Great choices but be careful, some dishes may be too spicy for the uninitiated. Service was great and they will always provide recommendations based on your wants. Interior decor is stark but the food quality and taste more than make up for the lack of decor. Highly recommended.
Comical pricing for shisha. 25$ a shisha. Horrible surroundings. I hope this place goes out of business.
Steam soup dumpling tastes good！so juicy! Noodle is a little bit over cooked, but the soup was tasty~ Meatball over rice was very flavorful~

Probably my favorite restaurant in Philly. BYOB, right in Fairmount, yummy food and amazing prices. We always get the lamb dishes here because they are delicious and it's incredible how reasonably priced it is. We frequently get appetizers and desserts here as well and I have never had a dish here that I did not like. We recommend this spot to all our friends
Excellent pho, unpretentious place. Needs a slightly better ambiance but otherwise it's a great place to make a quick stop-and-eat. Definitely recommend.

I just want to say the short-rib and chicken katsu tacos are sooo delicious and contain the freshest blend of veggies and meat that can be found in the city of brotherly love. The food is excellent and made stellar by the service of genuinely friendly home grown folks! Much respect to Cucina Zapata!

As a Top Chef fanatic, I was super excited when I heard that Chef Nina Compton was moving from Miami to New Orleans to open up her first restaurant. Nina is a bad ass bitch who TOTALLY should have won Top Chef. I mean, she kicked butt all season and then lost during the finale. I'm still not over it. I went here for brunch this morning and I'm already trying to convince my boyfriend that we should go back for dinner tonight. It was that good. I love absolutely everything about this restaurant. The decor is simple but striking, the service is spot on, and the food/drinks are heavenly. My boyfriend and I decided to split a bunch of things from the menu instead of ordering our own entrees and I'm SO glad that we did. We ordered the Avocado Toast, Coconut Chia Seed Pudding with Fresh Berries, Corn and Zucchini Fritters, and the Chicken and Smoked Mushroom Hash with Poached Eggs. Everything was exciting and flawless! I eat avocado toast on the reg, but this version takes it to the next level. I love the chunks of avocado mixed with radishes and pickled fresno chilis. The toast was buttery, crisp, and not too hard. A great way to start the meal. The Coconut Chia Seed Pudding was an absolute show stealer! I also eat a lot of chia seed pudding-esque meals, but this one was different. It was smooth and creamy as opposed to tight and almost clumpy like most chia seed puddings I've had. The best part by far was the crunchy toasted coconut on top. It was really interesting texture-wise and not too sweet. Possibly my favorite thing I ate today. The Corn and Zucchini Fritters were super light and fluffy with a bit of crunchy cornmeal in the crust. The dipping sauce was tangy but didn't over power the delicate taste of the zucchini in the fritters. Again, score. The Chicken and Smoked Mushroom Hash was a bomb of savory goodness. Juicy dark meat chicken with caramelized onions, smashed potatoes, smokey mushrooms, and two perfectly poached eggs. Winner, winner I could eat this chicken brunch for dinner. I also really dug the drinks. I ordered the B&B which was a mix of an IPA, Grapefruit, Elderflower, and Aromatized Wine. It was bitter, citrusy, sweet, fizzy, and floral all at the same time. An absolute must. The bartender also made my boyfriend an off the menu Irish Coffee. It was the best I've ever had. The final thing I would like to talk about was the incredible service. Our waiter was super professional and laid back at the same time. He knew SO much about the menu. When we asked about Chef Nina he responded by saying that she was "the shit" and that she works doubles nearly every day. It was really cool being able to peak into the kitchen from our table and see her working like a complete machine. I cannot wait to come back for happy hour, lunch, and dinner! Chef Nina certainly has more delicious surprises up her sleeve, and I'm excited to try them all.
This place is great! Banh mi and pho were very good. The milk tea was spot on as well. Really good prices for what you get!

I am local to this area and have visit this restaurant many times. Each dishes they making very fresh. All dishes have tried here has satisfied me with test. Must visit this place specially for south indian dishes.
Amazing Pho for being pub noodles. Don't sleep on the noods! It's cooked to perfection! And Thomas over here won't order this shit but that's okay, cause this shit is the FUCKING BOMB

Food was nice, service was very attentive. For two people, our total meal was $19. We were the only people in the cafe at the time and got to talk to the owner a little bit. Very nice man, very cool story. Before we left, he said, "welcome to your home away from home" -- treats his patrons like family, truly

Phamous is hands down the best pho restaurant in the sb area. The food is prepared very well and will tingle your taste buds with every bite :) the service is impeccable with all servers exemplifying the epitome of high class service (especially Nick and Dan). Definitely a restaurant you do not want to miss out on if you're in the area.

I was beginning to lose hope...thinking I was never going to find an Indian restaurant that would make me say WOW! After nearly 2.5 years of trying various restaurants all over the Indy metro area and adjacent counties, it is safe to say that Amber Indian Restaurant in Carmel is the best you'll find anywhere. The moment we sit down, someone arrives with our waters and the papad and chutneys. All three were delicious, with my favorite being the green chutney. Scott ordered a mango lassi which quickly arrived and was thick, not too sweet, and had just the right amount of mango flavor. Our main dishes also arrived quickly and they were piping HOT! I ordered the chicken korma while Scott had the lamb korma. The garlic naan ... just wow. It was hot, fluffy yet crispy, and was seasoned with an ample portion of garlic and oil. This is the best naan you will ever find in the greater Indy area. The naan was easy to rip apart and served as the perfect vessel to sop up the leftover sauce. This is truly soul food for me. The jasmine rice was cooked to perfection and the chicken was juicy and tender. The tomato-based sauce was extremely well seasoned and wonderfully thick and rich. I wish I could have ordered dessert since carrot halwa is my favorite but I was just too full! We finished our meal a little over an hour ago and I am already looking forward to our next visit. The service was fantastic - everyone was friendly and my water glass was always full. I really enjoyed the meal here. I just finished a pretty difficult work week and a dinner at Amber Indian Restaurant was just what I needed!
Small place, but delicious food. We tried paneer tikka, malai koffta and Mumbai chicken. Food was amazing. The most delicious was their garlic Nan(bread) , very soft.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Just discovered this gem, tucked away in the Acme shopping center. The staff aims to please, giving me tea while I waited for my Takeout (a mere 10 minutes). This is the BEST Chinese restaurant I have been to in a long time. The space is small but beautifully appointed, one of those feel good places to sit and sup. We enjoyed out Takeout at home this time. But I plan to visit in future. The Wonton Soup is a fantastic broth I cannot get enough of. The noodles are supple vs rubbery. The flavor is perfect. The Chicken Corn Soup was like an Egg Drop with sweet corn and bits of chicken. Where's the Chicken? The Shrimp with Mixed Veggies - I always ask for the sauce separate. Wonderful brown sauce. Shrimp were large. I can't get over the clean, light taste to all the food and the beautiful presentation of it. Highly recommended!
Great Food, Great Service. The owners are extremely sweet. Ordered my food through Yelp for pickup and my order was prepared and ready quicker then expected.

I ate here last night. I had the drum it was good. The other three people with me were very disappointed with their food. Pasta dish had little bad flavor. Shrimp did not seem fresh at all. Grilled prom belly dish was a very small portion and mostly fat. Drinks were good but very over priced. We ordered desert and waited 30 mins for it. Waitress forgot to turn in order. She was unapologetic. Manager didn't even bother to come over and apologize. I would say service is very poor. Food is overpriced and not very good. Very poorly managed restaurant.

My Daughter and I enjoyed after the short trek here to Lafayette Square area from Broadripple area. I did question the location for after dark visting..but, it was fine. Good service and the Pho was quite good as expected. $8=reasonable too. I added shrimp for $2.Spring Rolls were decent...but, I forgot they come cold...came with a peanut sauce. healthy eating. Daughter had a Jasmine Bubble tea..and to me it tasted good..but, a bit like eating an air freshener...HA. Overall, good ratings..we will go back to sample their extensive menu.

The food is delicious, so far the best Pho I have had in the New Orleans area. Full of veggies and hmmm tastyyy. We got a waiter right away that brought as our drinks and even turned down the air a bit after we told her we were cold! Parking can be a problem since it's on Magazine St. Get there early to snatch one or you might have to walk a bit. I want to try EVERYTHING on the menu, this place is awesome!
Just had Grub Hub deliver a delicious meal. We got butter chicken and a tandoori chicken dish with garlic naan.

I don't know what I just ate, it was not good. I mean, I know what it was, some rice dish, but it lacked any real flavor, especially that Thai flavor, and it was just not good at all. It was also overpriced and $14. Why does this place have four stars today??? Do that many people in Santa Barbara have no taste??? I'm sorry but the food at this place is not good and you are missing out on what this truly amazing cuisine is!!!! Won't be coming back here

Atmosphere was very casual-elegant and the service was AWESOME. Our waiter joked with us a lot. The food is a little pricey, and the portions a little small, but the quality is excellent & we definitely recommend this place for a little taste of India.

MMMMM...delicious! They do not offer my favorite Thai dish (Pra Ram), but my standard backup order of pad thai was excellent. I ate every bite, didn't leave a scrap, and wished for more when I was done - not that the portion was small, I just wanted more because it was so delicious. Very nice service, surprisingly nice atmosphere.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I ordered Korma with Goat there was a mistake and I received chicken instead. It was a disappointment as I really have come to enjoy the succulent flavor of goat and was really craving it since trying it in Seattle a few months back however the dish was still very delicious. Full of spice and flavor, the chicken was cooked to perfection, it was tender and juicy which is sometimes lost in a curry dish. The Basmati rice was also cooked perfectly, it was savory and aromatic. To accompany my dish I had the "Taj Mahal Premium Lager" imported from India it was a cool crisp and refreshing lager and not too light. I brought the mistake to the owners attention and he was very apologetic and offered to make the dish I ordered correctly, I graciously declined as the dish that was already prepared was very delicious, he offered me a Kheer dessert on the house for the mistake which is a traditional rice pudding. A new found love of mine. The dessert was very interesting, creamy, savory and sweet; the perfect combination. I would have given an additional star regardless of the mistake had the server checked on me sooner. Was the service bad? Absolutely not, the owner greeted me at the door with a very kind and pleasant manner and seated me right away. He obviously enjoys what he does and takes pride in his establishment and his food. I hope the next time I will be able to enjoy that delicious, tender and succulent goat meat with my dish.

Good quality food! My sister raved about their Muslim fish hoagies so I finally stopped by to place a order. The serving sizes are well worth the price. i also like that they have all natural products in the store (popcorn & juices). With all the overly processed foods & fast food restaurants Im thankful that I found this spot! This place deserves 5 Stars. I believe in great service & a great product. This place has both. Trust me you wont be disappointed.

I wish I could rate this 4.5. Our first experience at this restaurant on a Wednesday night. Only one waitress was working so service was a teeny bit slow. Despite being slow, she gave us great guidance on ordering the honey wine and which spice level to choose for food. We loved the food! I will definitely return to eat more of the chicken dish and the yellow lentils. We also really loved the lentil sambusas!
Amazing service & chaat! Had the veggie salad chaat mild with fig&banana lassi! Delicious !!!
very good viet in Tampa area. the spring roll and eggroll were delicious. the eggroll was tasty and light. enjoyed the rare steak pho. service is good, friendly and prices are reasonable. :)

It is really clean and tidy in here. That's what first caught my eye because it was a nice change from other places I frequent in the area. You can tell the guy in charge cares about the way it looks and feels inside. By the way when I talked to him later he mentioned how pleased he is to also have an open kitchen so that people could see exactly what was going on as their food was being prepared. I had the lamb meal with eggplant appetizer and it was really good. There was also a nice portion of pita bread. Although I enjoyed the meal, I think it was a little overpriced. If it were the only lamb that good in the area, I'd consider paying those prices again, but it's not, so the price is a big 'con'.

Poor food with poor service. This place is run by Chinese people who don't know how to make real Thai food. We ordered pad Thai, which was too sweet and we ordered yellow curry, which was too blend and watery. There are better options out there. Also, what's up with forcing a gratuity fee of 15% on my receipt when we had only two people dining there? Service wasn't even that great and there weren't even a lot of customers there to justify the poor service.

Worst service I ever had.... not sure Chuck knows what authentic Greek food is, for example.. tzatziki is not sweet. Take out is a joke the orders of hummus and tzatziki were wrapped in foil not a put in a container. ???Spent more time scraping the food off the foil than eating or enjoying it. What a joke. Sad that Chuck could care less about it. We will take out business to..OLYMPIA KABOB HOUSE and TAVERN! Olympia kabob house is wonderful, superb authentic Greek cuisine and friendly service with outstanding neighbourhood crowd. Good wine & spirits too!

We really like middle eastern food and read the reviews which were all favorable. Taking into consideration that this place opened just 5 days ago, it is great. They are on the ball and keep the line moving. It's a good idea if you have not been here before to read the signage straight ahead to the right as you walk in the door. You can have your meal in a bowl or in a pita pocket. Then you choose a base layer and then a PROTEIN layer. There's steak, chicken and falafel (vegan). You are then moved down to the next station where you choose your fixins. Both the falafel and the steak shwarma were good. The sauces go from mild-garlic to fire engine red. Word about the fries......................they are thinly cut potato quarters that are fried.................but if you like your fries crispy, you might not like this. I'm wondering if I asked if they'd leave the fries in the cooking oil for a few extra minutes? Everyone is in a good mood and trying really hard to provide service with a smile. I would really like to see them recycling..........such a waste. We'll be back. We were surprised to learn this is the 23rd location of this chain. Parking is a pain at this moment, but hopefully will get straightened out.

We came here for lunch after our play date at the kid gym next door. The staff was very inviting and helpful in making our menu selection. We have recently started eating much healthier and have to look for "plant-based" meals and have found it to be tough to do when we eat out. It was easy to do at Taza! Thank you so much for such a great experience! :) And the kids loved the Pita's :) Definitely get the Falafel Wrap!

UPDATE!! I am changing from a one to a three star review because service has become EXCELLENT. Pho is good - Magasin Cafe is still better. One bad experience on a hectic night is understandable, but our most recent visit sealed the deal. The staff is non-communicative, if not downright rude, and because my order took THREE TIMES as long as promised, I was able to witness how badly managed and chaotic their staff truly behaves. The food is bland at best. Go to Ba Chi instead.

Most diverse lassi selection you could ever imagine! The owner is friendly, creative, and obviously is passionate about his business. The chaat is an explosion of flavors, and if it's your first time trying it, the owner will be kind enough to explain the reason behind the different flavors. I used to live across the street but moved away. I miss it terribly! Stop in for a lassi if you're driving down Baltimore Ave.!
This was so salty I wanted to die. There was so much green pepper on the rice it was horrible it tasted like what Chinese food made by your aunt from southern Indiana would make. M

I stopped in hopping to have a good cuban sandwich. But was unable to enjoy the sandwich and beer due to the fruit flys, they were everywhere. When I asked the bartender about it he just said " ya we have that problem we did get rid of them a while ago but they are back now". I am not sure that is how it should be addressed. I wont ever go back at this point.

Momo's Greek food is OK at best - I don't think its terribly authentic. The tzatziki sauce is sweet, which I'm not a fan of, but maybe some folks are. The lamb gyro isn't very tasty. They took avgolemono soup off the menu which depresses me. I probably won't go back. The restaurant itself is quite cute tho - I think the outdoor seating area is nice, and the indoors is warm and colorful. The folks are nice. So - "good food" is a matter of opinion - you might like it!

Had a groupon for this place, and it was a pleasant surprise. The server was very sweet and attentive. No sushi on the menu. Tempura was great.,I think they used panko in the batter. The yellow curry was delicious. I could see the zucchini and kale that was added in. I've never had yellow curry with kale in it! The red curry tasted even better but i.noticed it was not really as red as other restaurants. I would return again. I think this is better than most Thai restaurants in the area.

My first time at Ekta. I LOVE. Indian cuisine and Ekta exceeded my expectations. The Sag Paneer was definitely the best I have had anywhere. Excellent butter chicken and the garlic Naan was just right I will definitely be back and I will recommend Ekta with no reservations! An excellent dining experience
Kind, fresh, classy, home cooking. Highly recommended authentic food experience. The owners go out of their way to make you feel at home.
I tried their chicken and their meat shawerma, simply put, it's the best I've ever had. No wonder they're the number one in the area! Smiley's makes me wanna just keep smiling :)
Sparkly atmosphere. There is a good variety of cocktails, wine and beer options. The chimichurri sauce in the Filet Brochette is delectable.
This is awesome!!!!!!! I go to this spot every week. The Bon bu hue is so great!!!!!! I love it !!!!!!!!

Went here for a work dinner and we had the best time. Tried a little bit of everything! The whipped feta is incredible, as well as the chorizo gnocchi. Cassie was our waitress and she was lovely! She had great suggestions and we really enjoyed everything. Definitely suggest it!
Authentic Puerto Rican Cuisine. If you want to experience the Puerto Rican meals that I have always enjoyed this is the best place in Nashville.
We frequent the Kabob house regularly for lunch. They have great staff, food is wonderful, atmosphere is just o.k., but for a great Persian meal, it can't be beat.

I've been searching for this type of a deli for a while, and finally came across after reading about it in Boise Weekly. Their sandwiches are fresh and very tasty and the baguette are wonderful - crunchy and fluffy at the same time. Add a smoothy with Boba (green tea is my favorite) and you end up with a satisfied belly after a cheap lunch. I'll be back!

Went by the food truck today for a Gyro (lamb/beef). This gyro was yummmmmmy. Lots of meat. The meat had good flavor and was moist, sometimes that's rare cause the meat can get dry. usually have to ask for extra tzatki sauce but not this time....just overall a great sandwhich. Will put a note next time the food truck is here to bring my lunch money, EVERYTIME

Food & Drink (4.0) Usually as an Indian I am very clingy to my favorite Indian restaurants (Aman's Indian Bistro) because there are many bad places for Indian food, but this place could be a new favorite. As a drink my cousin and I went for Thumbs Up, an Indian coke made with cane sugar (taste like Mexican coke). For apps we got their chili paneer: crispy, and gravy was amazing. We also got the manchurian: it's not the type of manchurian with gravy, it's not wet but so good, the cauliflower was light and scrumptious. For the main course since I don't like dosa, I got the paneer butter masala, great flavor thick gravy and paneer was great. Garlic naan was amazing, so flavorful, could eat that alone! The parents had dosa and they loved it, they said it was crispy and light. they were huge, but since they were so light they were able to finish it. *** Keep in mind, hot is spicy as sh1t!!!, I'd go for a medium if you can handle some heat and mild if not so much. Environment (3.0) Very cheap, mom-and-pop type restaurant. Not decorated well, but they food was the center price so that didn't matter. Seating was enough for the size of the place. Also parking would've been hard to get if you came on a busy day.

I gave the Rt 202 location a try based on a suggestion from a friend, and I am guessing I won't return. The service was attentive, but the food was a weak representation of thai cuisine. The Tom Yung Koong tasted like Mama noodle base, and they had italian basil in there with a ton of sugar! The jungle beef salad was also too sweet, and the toasted rice powder that was sprinkled over the salad was under toasted to the point that it ended up as sharp flavorless pebbles in your mouth. Portions are decent, and BYOB , but the cooking at this location leaves much to be desired, (and I would rarely be that critical about a restaurant) even when considering that most American Thai restaurants are cooking in the Bangkok style, but tailored to farang taste.
Loved the lemongrass curried shrimp. The flavor was intense and the textures were perfect. Everyone in my party enjoyed their meal. A new place on our regular list.
Delicious, fresh Middle Eastern food. They don't skimp on the ingredients, real feta, real falafel, tasty hummus. We will definitely be back
The seating on the inside of the place was a little too hospital cafeteria, but the food was delicious.

I was working in Tampa a few weeks ago and needed to grab a quick lunch from a place within walking distance, so I walked into Queen of Sheba. Service was wonderful, and there was a lot of vegan and vegetarian options to choose from at the buffet. It may be that lots of spices are par for the course with Ethiopian food, but I found there to be too many different spices among the foods I'd chosen. I felt like I needed a palate cleanser a few times just to clear out one flavor before eating something new. I'd totally eat there again on my next trip.
Seating is uncomfortable. Food fair overall. Enjoyed my chicken fried rice but chicken was not warm. Bartender took a bit of warming up but ended up being nice overall.
Fabulous. Enter, sit, say "Pho Combo, add vegetables", wait a few minutes, bask in pho heaven. Spring rolls are also excellent.
Food is good but really small portions and with that being said, the price is really high compared to other Thai places here in Brandon.

Manager called me a bitch... 43 minutes for take out! Walk-in take out order of 1 chicken madras and naan. Told 10- 15 minutes, waited 43 minutes. Kept asking where food was after 25 minutes. Too long for take out. The manager was a real jerk and when I left he called me a bitch under his breath... Now do I even eat the food or did he spit in it?!?! Wow.. NEVER AGAIN!

As someone who has been coming here for the Tikka Masala, great pakora, excellent cultural atmosphere and near flawless service for years (lunch buffet only because of the excellent deal!), I found myself a new favorite dish here. The Vegetable Majestic is an incredible, spicy dish with dumplings and chili peppers for you to dip naan in (garlic of course!). I have never eaten such great Indian cuisine for such a bargain, despite the dozen or so places across America that I've tried. I hope to keep coming here for years to come and will always recommend it as the best restaurant in Carmel. 5 stars.
Took my mom here today for Mother's Day brunch and I loved it! I will definitely be back! Pleasant people wonder food and a great atmosphere!!!!!!!

Disappointed the last couple of times. My order was wrong for two of the four dishes that arrived. I just find the flavors disappointing as well. We also had to ask for extra accoutrements that should already come with certain typical dishes.

Waited in drive through for 30 min.... And there was only 1 car ahead of me. Super slow service. Definitely not the "fast food" that they claim to be. Falafel was good, but does not come with hummus and they are unwilling to substitute white sauce with hummus even if you have food allergy. Menu is very limited and honestly very over price.
Good, quick food. Service was very good. Portions are generally quite large. Prices are good, especially considering the portion sizes. The potatoes were super crispy and delicious!

Simply put, this is an amazing restaurant. There is one negative that I just need to get out of the way: it's small. I'd say intimate. Reservations are necessary, even during the week. People may complain about the noise, but to me it was more like the authentic Italian experience. People talking, laughing, saying "mmm..." A LOT. I decided to go here for my 26th birthday. My father footed the bill, which I can tell you though I don't know the amount, was high. That is because he said, "We'll have everything on the menu, and all of the specials." (Yes, my dad rules!) From start to finish, my family of 6 shared course after course of phenomenal cuisine. Fresh, simple, perfectly cooked. Everything was passed around the table. Everything was tasted, even if it wasn't under my normal comfort zone. Take the braised rabbit in red sauce over broccoli rabe and orzo. IT WAS PHENOMENAL! Yes, I had to get my childhood memories of Thumper out of my head, but sorry buddy, you were beyond delicious. Tender, moist, and far less gamey than I anticipated. Another highlight was my grandmother's swordfish. Prepared skin-on (obviously), it had that beautiful dense texture without any of the "fishiness" I was expecting. Some yummy secret sauce was also part of that equation. My roasted chicken (I know... so adventurous) was out of this world. I savored it from the fridge for the next few days gladly. Desserts.... Pistachio gelato was a highlight as well as their simple Zepolis (fried donuts with sugar.) Let's not forget our service. I'm going back to November, but I remember his name: Zach. Knowledgable, anticipated our needs, stood back because he realized we were the kind of table who wanted to drink our wine and eat, eat, eat. He always made sure I had a full pitcher of their phenomenal limonada. This restaurant changes their menu seasonally and it is BYOB. I guarantee you will not be disappointed. It's as if they took everything simple and homestyle, and sprinkled some magical food fairy dust on it. I guess that's what you call excellent dining!

Im giving up on ever eating here. I've tried three times in the last week to eat here and have been turned away to go elsewhere every time. I was looking for a place that delivered Pho. I was surprised to find this restaurant. I had never heard of it & was excited to find something new. However, when I called, I was told that there were no deliveries that night (Wednesday) because their delivery driver only works part time. ??? The following Monday I had family in town. I thought we could try again, this time we would go to the restaurant. When we pulled up (at 8 o'clock) the lights were out, door locked, and the open sign flashing obnoxiously in our faces. What does that mean?? I really wanted to eat there too... I had since come down with bronchitis and tried again last night for a delivery. This time when I asked if they could deliver, they simply said no, with no apology or explanation. I would think a small shop in an often overlooked location, surrounded by competitors (Pho 88, Miss Saigon) would try just a little harder. I'm wondering if my review is even valid, since I still have never eaten the food?

I've been dying to try out this restaurant because I love Caribbean food but this was a disgrace! I'll admit that the service was incredible and my waiter was amazing. The food on the other hand was not up to my expectations and it took forever for them to make it. My roti was horrible and I'm ashamed that they even served it to me. The jerk chicken had good seasoning on it but it was dry. The ox tails were good though. Don't order the Sorrel! I don't mind paying 12.99 for legit Sorrel but this stuff wasn't up to park.

This is our "go to" spot for sushi and Asian food in Mt Juliet. We could eat here once a week (and typically do). Give their orange chicken a try, nice sized portions and the level of consistency is always on point.
Food is really good here - my favorites are the Evil Jungle Princess and the Drunken Noodles! Service is also very good. Definitely a good Thai place to have in the suburbs!

An average place for Thai food having lived in Los Angeles and East bay I know my expectation is high. This restaurant is in downtown prime location wiling dishes priced average $11. The portion could have been bit more. Ordered chicken pad see ew and green curry. The pad see ew was good but the green curry was bland and too watery. Bottom line won't be visiting this place again for thai food as there is too many other cuisine options in Santa Barbara. I will stay with my east bay restaurants for Thai food
Excellent Vietnamese cuisine! They can get busy at times, but definitely worth the wait.
Medium Jerk Chicken, rice and red beans and festival cole slaw. Amazing Taste and very fresh.

Everything was excellent!!!!! This is definitely a hidden gem, tucked back in a little plaza. The owners (I assume) were very nice and went out of their way to make us feel welcome. The food was prepared fresh and everything tasted so good. We will be back!

my husband has ordered fish bronzino in many good restaurants and has never been satisfied that it was made the way he likes it, which is the whole fish nice and crispy, until he happened upon the siames ;princess. he is 85 and now looks his happiest when when eating their fish. wow

Chipotle style rice bowl topped with indian curries. I took rice bowl added mint paneer and masala chickpeas and added vindaloo curry. Amazing food. Many options for vegetarians and non-vegetarians. must try place.

WOW! What. gREAT place!!!! Really nice staff! Delicious food. The Greek salad was wonderful. The hummus is excellent and vegetarian Dolmades delicious. Fair prices. Clean restaurant and a nice dining experience. Five Stars! The Pita bread is likely baked fresh and was delicious. Call ahead was fast but I ate in house. Highly recommend and I'll be back each time I have to pass through Clearwater!

One of those restaurants I didn't want to share because I wanted it it all to myself. Delightful decor, super service, plenty of parking and fabulous food. A must if you are a curry house fan or if you want a very enjoyable dinner

Sweet falafel adventure explosion! Hot damn cornucopia of deliciousness! I love this little plant-friendly cart. I love the singing, smiling man behind the cart. I love his delicious falafel constructions. This place isn't for the weak-hearted or the tender-stomached. Be prepared to reek of garlic for the remainder of the day so co-workers be warned. Perfect green fafalel balls and char-grilled chicken and every time a different mix of delicious components, be it a beet hummous, a mix bag of salads, a myriad of vegetables and fruits, raw or cooked or both, coucous and a melting fusion of sauces and who-knows-what- all I know is that the finished product is a marriage of taste perfection. Falafel truck does abide by a couple strict rules, only two items either a sandwich or a platter can be ordered here, and only one item per person. The wait on certain days can be lengthy so come early. And yes, $10 is a bit steep (why does he keep raising the prices?) but it's worth it. His food is so scrumptious, and the portions massive so you'll be stuffed, guaranteed . Best Cart/Truck food in Philadelphia, no question.

Two filling and delicious bowls of curry and stir fry, and two iced teas, made for a delicious lunch! The price was great, the employees were friendly and welcoming, and the decor was lovely. I like how it looked like a garden nursery outside. ^^ it was very welcoming and friendly!

I've visited this restaurant a few times before leaving my thoughts (just to give them a chance). Each time I've ordered, I leave with the same feeling. The food is great, however the service is TERRIBLE. Each time I've ordered, the person that took it, half listened and over talked me; only for me to get to the restaurant to find that the wrong order was taken. Initially I would wait, until finally I just walked out. I would eat in, if I had time or lived closer, until that can happen I will pass for now. There's a cool place around the corner, Fanta International, that's amazing!! For whatever reason they're not on Yelp, well maybe they are now!!!

A real gem of a place. Excellent Mediterranean cuisine served by a family always willing to please. They make fresh salads and have delicious gyros and various platters. Some popular items are the lamb and chicken gyros, the various pita wraps, and greek salads. My favorite is the king's vegetarian platter which is always super fresh, savory, and healthy. You can't go wrong with this place. If you have a sweet tooth, they have some exotic sodas too.

Had a great experience here! The prices were great and the service was excellent. We didn't have to wait very long from the time we put our orders in to the time our food got to the table. We had our 3 year old with us and got his meal within 10 minutes of the order. I ordered the combo Lo-mein and enjoyed every bite of it! Would definitely come back here!

I actually came here because King & I was closed when we tried to go (Monday). I got their pad thai, which I actually liked more than the one at King & I. Their Thai iced tea is also good as well - different than other ones I've had but still very good. Portions are medium-sized. I was full, but I think a few of my guy friends were not. Overall great good!

Well the food was just okay. I'm not sure why this is the "go to" Pho place. The Pho soup was average and the rice noodles were hard and not completely cooked. The rice dish with pork chop was okay. But everything else we tried was pretty bad, especially the seafood chicken with clear noodle soup, just plain terrible. And as many people mentioned already, the service was really slow and the cashier was mean. She couldn't smile if her life depended on it. I don't need a smile but don't give me the death stare, I only want to give you money. Then she kinda throws the change and receipt in my direction. Not sure who pissed her off but I'm glad I got my change and ran. It may be best just to call ahead and order take out but you'll still have to deal with the gatekeeper cashier. Be prepared.
Good service and quality of food; did not realize it is a BYOB; good on lamb and chicken dishes; not as much available for fish eaters
Excellent. The food (I had shrimp saute) and the service were great. A little short on space, but well worth it.

I have an intense addiction to Indian food lately. Friends introduced us to Shere Punjab recently and it is doing a fantastic job of feeding my addiction. A couple heads up: 1) The strip mall it's in looks super shady. Do not fear - inside is like a little oasis - very nice and clean. 2) The restaurant is cold - bring a sweater. But holy wow - is the food good. The service isn't quite as good - but tolerable. Our go-tos are: Chicken tikka masala Palak lamb Beef vindaloo Aloo Matar Rice A mix of naan - garlic, onion, cheese Just went last night and I could go again tonight!

Lightening fast service and a decent amount of meat do not make up for a pretty average bowl of pho. I am glad to have tried the pho at Pho Hoa, but I don't think that I'll bother to make a return trip.

A friend told me we should have lunch here, am always open to new cool places, but was surprised by how cool and good this place was. Great interior design, exposed brick, cool bar area, etc. I ordered the Chilaquiles with the fried egg (+$1), super good, it's a little pricy if you get the steak (+$3) but the egg was the perfect amount to get full with. All in all my bill would have been around $9-10 for a pretty good lunch but they accidentally forgot to make mine so get this, they gave it to me for free for being late, that is stand up and something you really dont see much in Indianapolis. Big fan of La Mulita and will eat here again, also excited to try Delicia!

Went to Butcher & Bee while visiting Nasvhille for business because I loved the concept and wanted to see a bit of East Nashville. We called to make a reservation for 6:45 the same day and they were booked but stopped in anyway they got us a table right away. We started with the 4 plate mezze, a great deal at $16/4 plates. The bacon wrapped dates are a must. Delicious. They are almost a dessert with the way the sugar from the dates soaks into the bacon. We also had the hummus (meh) and the whipped feta with honey (yum!) and the sweet potatoes (good). The hummus and whipped feta should have been served with more pita bread. It wasn't quite enough! For dinner ordered the braised lamb. It wasn't anything remarkable and I wished I had ordered the shwarma instead. Ambiance was OK, though the music was ... different (tracks included Whitney, rap, and country) and entirely too loud near the bar. Bathrooms needed work, and service was fine though not memorable. We would definitely come back here and try some other plates as well as cocktails (we stuck to beer)
I have been to this place hundreds of times in dallas and it feels so good to find same salad place with same good taste here in tampa.. nice new place with good ambience and fantastic taste!!

Queen of Sheba is a must if you're a fan of trying new things. The moody lighting, quiet music and African decor were a nice change of pace from your average hectic fast food joint. We ordered a huge plate that had little portions of everything on it. We weren't provided silverware at first, since Ethiopian dining etiquette included using injera, (a crepe-like bread material), to scoop up things up and eat it. I can't tell you half the things we ate but it was fun and delicious. With The Queen of Sheba, we got a taste of a new culture and refined our palates that much more.
This has become my favorite Indian lunch spot. Always great and fresh. Vegetarian and meat options. The chicken meatballs are totally unique and delicious.

I wouldn't waste my time coming here again honestly. The food isn't horrible, but it's definitely not great either. The Mac n cheese is disappointing (mushy with no flavor) and they didn't have any rolls or cornbread available to go with the platters (major let down).

If I've learned anything in life, it's that gas station restaurants have not disappointed me. My husband and I met some friends for brunch at this small intimate restaurant and we instantly dug the vibe. We learned that the Tower Grove neighborhood was in the process of being revitalized and were shown old pictures of the locale before its renovation. We were very impressed with the restaurant's dramatic transformation. The staff was friendly and the service was adequate, a little on the slow side but it wasn't terrible. The food was delicious. My husband had the lamb tartare and I had the short rib stew with poached egg. Both were extremely delicious and satisfying. We've been looking for a good tartare dish for a while, and this one delivered. I highly recommend trying this dish if you're looking for something different. My short rib stew was very rich, but very good. I love the creamy element the poached egg added to the dish. This may be why it was so rich, but every bite was worth each and every calorie. Olio also had a great drink menu for brunch. While I stuck with just coffee, my husband tried the Greenfly and our friend got the Desert Island. Both drinks were good, although be warned, the Desert Island comes with a lot of ginger beer. Our friend still enjoyed his drink despite the ginger beer and my husband loved the Greenfly. I'm kind of sad that this place isn't in KC, because I would definitely be a regular. But I do come StL quite often and will plan on trying to visit whenever I can. I enjoyed Olio a lot and will recommend it to many of my friends living and visiting StL.

Great quality. Very clean. Really, really good food. We split a sampler-type platter and it was very, good. I'm being picky but the salad at Gojo is much better. The salad here seemed to have dressing from Kraft and that is my only complaint. Great recommendation on Yelp or else I would have never tried this restaurant.
Awesome place. Stopped here several times when passing by this area. Great experience very time. Mutter paneer and Zera rice a nice combo here.

Oh, how disappointing. We were really excited to try this place, but our experience left us quite disappointed. Let me explain... It's a fairly easy concept, order at the register, food is brought to your table. We ordered a chicken pita with fries, beef souvlaki pita with side salad and 2 cokes. I asked for a side of tzatziki to dip the fries in. Our total came to $31.68. After sitting down, I realized our total seemed a little high. I had to add together what we ordered in my head (b/c we declined a receipt) and could not figure out why things were not adding up. As far as soda choice, only cans were available, no soda fountain. Typically, this would not be a problem but since the restaurant is exposed to the elements and kept in an open style cooler unit, our Cokes were barely cold. The restaurant itself is clean, with a decent amount of seating (there is a patio) with an open view of the kitchen (always appreciated). Our food arrived promptly. After all the food was set down, I realized that we were charged for tzatziki dip (w/ pita) and not a small version for dipping fries in. They charged us $6 for one pita with a side of tzatziki sauce that they already put in the pita!!! $6 for one pita and sauce!!! I specifically asked for a side to dip the fries in. I read another review that stated they were charged $4 for a side, which is still outrageous. Back to the food. I thought the food was good, not the greatest I ever had, but still tasty. I do have to say, this is one of the worst values in Nashville. While tasty, the beef souvlaki was the size of a hot dog (no that is not an exaggeration). There was barely any toppings on the beef pita. Side salad was a good size, but having to cut up giant slices of tomato with a knife could have been avoided by just cutting the tomatoes smaller.
