The chicken pita was tasty, moist, and better portioned than the beef pita. The fries were your average frozen fry with cheese sprinkled on top. Also, you need to order a side of ketchup, as there are no bottles anywhere to be found. Even by avoiding the tzatziki side debacle, our total would have still been roughly $25. I will pay $25 for a meal for 2 all day long, but for the amount of food you are actually served, it leaves you feeling taken advantage of. The staff was friendly and seemed attentive. They had a lot of people working, which is why the service was great. All in all, tasty food that is no where near the price. We may give it another chance down the road, but are probably good on Greko for a while.
Pretty good food, decent parking available in the lot, and clean, but service can be slow.
Taste-wise ok. Service not so good. Price varies...some of the dosa items are more pricey.

Another great meal. Excellent food, service is outstanding. Joseph (the manager) even delivered a delicious appetizer (on the house) Folks if you are craving GOOD Chinese or Japanese cuisine this is the place. And please do not let the fact that it's in a strip mall fool you. This restaurant is right up there with any high end stand-a-lone Asian restaurant.

I went to the wrong restaurant. I was hoping this was Passage to India, but ah well...Apparently it's a common mistake to make. :) Service was attentive with the water glasses never dipping below half full, but the food was merely 'meh.' Not enough flavour. The saag was mild, delicate, & creamy-pretty good, but the rest of the offerings just seemed like they needed to have the spice level cranked up. Not necessarily to up the spiciness, merely because everything was a bit dull & bland. Most everything needed some brightness added to the dish. The naan was also chewy like it had been sitting for a while & we arrived at 11:30. What's with all the cream-based dishes? I've rarely added cream to an Indian dish, but at least half the buffet featured cream-based dishes & half contained meat, leaving only 1 or 2 vegan options.

Don't listen to any other review. This is the one you need to read. Zeppoli is my overall favorite resturant in the eye of the cosmos. The crowd? I loved it. Looking around at everyone there is amazing. Everyone is always having a great time, and the conversation always goes back to their perfect food. The medium cooked steak couldn't have been better. Thats also because I specially ordered a side of potatoes, in which blends with the meat in the most amazing way. The waiter was AWESOME. So nice to children, never got annoyed, handled the situations at hand. It's just... Hard to explain how perfect this place is... If you EVER want to do something special, here's the meal to conclude it. Completely recommended.

My fiancé and I really like this place. The pho is really good, and the menu is quite large. The only reason for not giving this place more stars is the lengthy wait one must go through till the food arrives at one's table. But once the food is there it really is good. Probably going to use this as a take out location rather than sit in the restaurant waiting.

Past two times here have been mediocre at best. Service is consistently bland & slow. The food quality does not match the price tag. I ordered a pizza that was nearly 20 dollars. The pizza I get at Fired Pie for $8 was better than this one. They got rid of the specialty cocktail menu which was a neat thing they had going on for a while and a plus of going here. Overall, entrees are not impressive, service is poor, and there are just so many better places to go eat dinner in Tucson. This one doesn't stand out at all.

Carry out order was ready right on time. There were both large bones and shards in the chicken roti ($13), although I was previously told it was boneless when I asked... Good portion size and tender meat so otherwise tasty, but that just would have been nice to know up front. Fried plantains ($4) were a very small serving and only 1-2 of the pieces appeared to have been properly fried. Overall satisfied my roti craving but overpriced for what I got, so will likely explore other options before returning.
I am never disappointed when dining at Saigon. The food is delicious and service is always what you expect when eating out.

I could not wait to come here after yelp did a piece on this restaurant! Very open, clean place with super friendly service. The menu is expansive, which made it that much harder to choose... And a reason to come back :) We had a decent strawberry bubble tea, and a tofu and veggie Vietnamese noodle dish ( very fresh) and a duck and mushroom noodle soup! Pic attached :) fresh and packed with flavor and veggies, I cannot wait to come back.

Everything here is pretty good. Ambience, food and service. But what I really wanted to say is try their Coconut Creme Brulee. Maybe you already ate somewhere else and you're craving some dessert. Come here and get their creme brulee because it is legit.

As soon as I walked in I knew I was in the right place. Andre greeted me warmly and I could tell he genuinely wanted my entire experience to be pleasant. I opted for the Island Chicken platter. Each dish was more tasteful and brilliant than the last. The portions were very fair - I'm a large guy and I only finished maybe half of my entree. The chicken bursts with flavor and is very tender and juicy. Even though the AC was on, sweat beaded down my body from the jerk and the curry chicken. All the while, reggae music kept the vibe light and Andre was all too happy to indulge me with Tampa highlights and sports talk.

Food is good for the price, and the staff is friendly. The buffet is set up so you rarely have to wait in line more than 2 minutes, which is nice. I'm not a fan of their dessert items, but the entrees are great. Be sure to ask for more napkins since you only get one per placemat setting and you're likely to need one with all the curry they serve. Great spot for a colder day when you're looking for food to warm you up, and the dishes are all labeled vegetarian or vegan so you know which ones contain meat/animal products and which don't.
Overall, we had a pretty good lunch here. The naan/bread wast very good...pretty dry. And the atmosphere is really odd. But, the beef/lamb schwarma wrap is amazing and service was good!!

Just found our new favorite place in town. Vegan and Vegetarian options galore. We had the Mediterranean salad which was delicious and filling. The owners were very nice and friendly. We opted the dine in. It's a small little place and it looks like they're trying to renovate. It's so nice to have a good place to eat close to valrico. Small businesses always have the best food. We'll definitely be back because there are so many other things on the menu we want to try. And we saw they are on UberEATS so that's a plus for nights in. Don't hesitate and try this place.
I can't get enough of this place. The Pho is wonderful and the bahn mi is delicious. And it's priced pretty low.
will NEVER go back - would not honor a coupon clearly marked never expires. Manager called and was rude to my wife saying they don't need our kind of customer. Maybe they don't need your kind either.

I admit, I was skeptical about this place. It's not in the best part of town and the name is a little strange. But the reviews were all good and I was craving a fried shrimp salad and one of the reviews said they had this even though it's Vietnamese. This skeptic has been fully converted! First of all, the menu has SO much variety - salads, soups, sandwiches, Chinese food, Vietnamese food...all kinds of things. I ordered my salad and was very impressed. The shrimp were huge!!! It also came with eggs, pickles, and tomatoes all arranged in a line. I adore eggs on my shrimp salads so bonus points! All I had to pay with was Amex and they don't take that so I had to leave my delicious salad while I ran home to get something else. This isn't their fault though. I've gone back 2 other times for the shrimp salad and once for their chicken pho. This wasn't the best Pho I've had, but it wasn't awful. I'm definitely looking forward to trying more things on the menu here.

If you live/work in center city and haven't had lunch here, I feel bad for you. You'll pay what he says, and you'll get what you get. You won't be disappointed. Falafel, smoky grilled chicken, wonderful fresh salads and sides--riffs on all of these as the best ingredients are available. Oh, and it's a gem, but not a totally hidden gem. Endure the line. It'll be worth it.
Best Thai in Delco... Good reasonable prices too. BYO so bring some drinks or stop and have a few on one of the bars on state street.. Nice place to walk around also.

I was so happy when I saw this place pop up on Grubhub! Our area is in sore need of diverse and high quality takeout places, so welcome to the neighborhood, Pikpon Thai. The food was fresh, well-made and authentic. I ordered the pork larb and LOVED it! The pad thai and drunken noodles were also excellent. We'll be sampling all the other menu items in the near future. Two thumbs up!
Simply thai is one of my favorite thai resteraunts in town i always order number 81 with chicken and beef

My food was so good I almost cried. Maybe that's a little bit emo, but....there hasn't been good Indian food in this town since I've lived here. We've always had to drive up to Udupi in Tampa. Anyway, I had garlic naan and matar paneer and my girlfriend had the baingan bharta, a soup (I can't remember which) and chai tea. Everything was really delicious. The space is also very pretty, clean, and smells terrific. ALSO the entire wait staff was very friendly. They gave us a free dessert, too: pistachio ice cream, which was also great. Great experience from top to bottom. I can't wait to go back.

I used to love this place when Binder owned it, it was my favorite, I would eat there 2-3x a week. Then it was sold, the first owners did that Pink/Aqua Blue remodel, my first time dining under the new owners, I noticed something on the spoon I was using in the cold area, I then realized they had price tags they didn't remove from the spoon, I told the owner, who had the spoon taken away, but didn't toss the items who knows what contaminants were on the tag, and were probabbly never washed, then I found 3 more spoons, I told her she needed to discard the items, she didn't care, my other complaint, was the food wasn't temp, I told her very nicely she didn't like hearing it, then other diners complained, and she wanted to charge them, so I was glad when the new ownership took over, wasn't great, but wasn't horrible as they first used Binder's recipes, then the last time I went, it was DIGUSTING, I seriously only ate my food because of all the notes about you must eat all your food or we will charge you extra BS. I ate, didn't know if I was going to throw up it tasted so bad, and have NEVER been back, wouldn't EVER go back!

We live practically around the corner from Pita Jungle, but have never really considered going because my husband and myself aren't really hummus/black bean/falaffal eating people. But it's a new year, and we're trying to open ourselves up to new experiences, so this is where we found ourselves on Friday afternoon. The interior is nicely done, very open. The bar (where we ususally hang out) was huge and had some nice flatscreens, one tuned to Sportscenter (what we usually watch), so we were happy so far. It looked like we got there just as the shifts were changing, because 3 or 4 bartenders were switching out money at the till, and it took a while to get anyone's attention for a drink order. But we eventually got ourselves a beer and some menus. My husband had a pasta dish with grilled chicken, and I ordered a hot pita with chicken, veggies and garlic sauce. At the last minute I requested some tatziki sauce on the side, and boy am I glad I did, because the garlic sauce (paste) was pretty disgusting. The rest of my pita wrap was pretty good though. My husband liked the pasta as well, but at $10.99, it was a bit expensive. So, we really liked the atmosphere, kinda liked the food, but what we didn't like was the service. While our bartender was very nice, getting her to refill our drinks was a real struggle. And we weren't the only ones. The people sitting next to us had to yell and wave their hands to get their final bill. Improve the service and I could see ourselves back for some drinks, but overall, I still don't think we're the hummus/black bean/falaffal eating type.

A better rating would be 3.5 stars. The service is fast and friendly. The food taste pretty much the same as their counterparts do. Their soup stocks have a but more flavor to them though. In my opinion their menu is just to large. They offer so much more than soup and noodle dishes. But so do the 1/2 dozen other places around town. If they streamlined their menu and focused in on the Pho the place would be fantastic and also set them selfs apart from the others. IMO

They need to get a better solution to there phone service or upgrade they're system online for online ordering. Trying to get through can be a maddening/frustrating experience that's also the reason for the low rating. Turns out that they are temporarily closed for renovations.

The prices were very reasonable (if not cheap), and the service was good, but the food was lacking. We had two appetizers and two entrees and the bill was only around $27. The food was not authentic thai food though. It lacked any complexity of flavor that you would experience at other restaurants. The vegetables in the entrees were strange as well including water chestnuts, which you won't find in any thai dishes. Even though the price was right I wouldn't return because the food just really wasn't good.

Hands down favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Indy. Very cheap, delicious food. It is my go-to Vietnamese spot. Although I think that the pho is better at King Wok, for everything else I would go here. Everything is authentic and it is family owned.

I find the place strange big rustic mirror on one wall giant medal flowers on another wall. WHY are you trying to sell the art!! This is something highway diners do!!! The food was OK it didn't stand out or make me want to come back. The details seemed to be missed (pits in the olives) simple things that make a difference I asked the server "what beers they had on tap?" she gave me that look and turned my menu over and pointed at the drink section. If your place is called "PITA JUNGLE" and you serve Pitas from a box you have to have the amazing service and make sure all the little details are taken care of

Great flavorful Pho! Spring rolls are perfect. Newer place in Reno however not new to the business. These are the old owners of SK Noodle (when it was good which is now mediocre at best). Warm welcoming atmosphere and fantastic customer service. Come check it out!

I tried this place out recently, and enjoyed a flight of wine, hummus, and figs at the end of a communal table on the patio with my K-9 friend at my feet. Yes - this place is dog friendly! The servers are very knowledgeable and informative. The food is delicious and the wine selection is vast. Service is top notch, and the servers are friendly. The atmosphere on the patio is relaxed and calm, great place to wind down after a long work day/week.

If you're in the area and looking for Vietnamese food, just come here. Great location. When I went there for lunch, there were only a couple customers inside and the environment was very tranquil with the zen music, natural lighting and soft spoken staff. I got some shrimp spring rolls, Vietnamese coffee, a pineapple juice and a large bowl of rare flank and brisket pho. I went a little crazy. Even crazier is I ate every bit of it.

New Thai restaurant!! I was not that hungry when we passed Green Basil but i had to try a new place that just opened and write a review! I am in love with thai food and i got some of the basic items just to see how it is all prepared! everything came out fast and it was delicious! the service was excellent and that really what matters the most. I was very happy with my experience.

Having tasted NY's version of Indian Fusion, I was excited to see that we finally have a place in our backyard that serves it. I've eaten at the buffet in the Chonshy location and it was good, Nirvana Fusion just seemed a bit better. I ordered the Chicken Tikka, Butter Chicken and Veg Manchurian lunch specials. The specials came with rice, your chosen entree (choose from traditional Indian or Indian Fusion), dhaal (lentils), and an extra side. Oh, and dont forget the soft, flaky naan. Sure, add in some gulab jamun to while you're at it. Food was well seasoned and had the right amount of heat. Did I mention that they don't skimp on the portions? If I had to find a complaint, it would be that their soup was on the salty side.....still edible. Between this place and Biriyani Bowl, Hatboro is starting to dominate the Indian food scene. Looking forward to experience more "nirvana".
Delicious and insanely vegetarian friendly. We went with a groupon and can't wait to go back without one.
Always a smiling face when you go here, excellent customer service! Joe the bartender is the best! Wonderful atmosphere! I love all of the tofu dishes!!! A must place to visit!

My absolute favorite restaurant in Tucson! The food is incredible- the flavors are all intricate and delicious. I was so impressed with both of the appetizers I ordered as well as my entree. Everyone else in my party couldn't stop raving about their meals as well. On top of the excellent food (which was one of the best Persian restaurants I've been to) the service and decor were also incredible. With different vegetarian options I'm sure this place will work for all different types of eaters! Can't wait to continue coming back to this spot!
Loved it! Other reviewers nailed it - flavorful food, casual intimate setting, attentive friendly service. Did I say delicious food! Yum!

Leave now! Service wasn't good, drinks weren't good, they delivered the wrong food, & when we notified the management/owner he didn't care. He said, "Sometimes people fall through the cracks." And did nothing to remedy the situation or improve our experience. My friend and I who are servers at another restaurant in New Orleans were so surprised that our experience had been so bad. We almost didn't say anything but it just got worse.

Met my college chum for early dinner Friday night. Not too many patrons for the duration of our visit. Our reception and the service were quite nice throughout. Water refills were always at hand, as was plate-clearing, offering of dessert and delivery of to-go vessels. We ordered meat samosas for appetizer ($3.95) -- triangular pastry filled with ground beef and spices. Two sauces were served in a condiment caddy -- one green (quite spicy) and one maroon (less spicy). We selected the samosas for two reasons: description and the order comes with two -- figuring that wouldn't be too much of an appetizer! These things were huge! Extremely crunchy on the outside and tasty meat/spice soft on the inside. After I tried both sauces, I just ate my samosa naked. It was quite flavorful, and NOT spicy hot. I would not call the outside a pastry as I know it; I'd call it more like a hush puppy outside (but harder), but not cornmeal like a hush puppy. The menu did not call these deep-fried (as it did for other appetizers), but my guess is they were deep-fried. Entrees: Chicken curry ($11.95) -- chicken cooked in tomatoes and spices Lamb sagwala ($12.95) -- lamb cooked in spinach and herbs Heat: we were offered a scale of heat beginning with medium, then spicy, very spicy, hot, and on and on. I opted for medium for the lamb sagwala. She opted for one step above medium for the chicken curry. She got garlic cheese naan ($4). I got garlic naan ($2.50). We got a lovely share platter of rice garnished with peas. Great presentation and nice thought to spiffing up the look of a white platter full of white rice. Our entrees were in individual casserole dishes. She liked the chicken curry, but said it wasn't as thick as she liked. The taste was fine. But I did notice that it looked a little runny. She loved the garlic cheese naan. I tried her chicken curry, so I understand about the consistency, but the flavor was delightful, albeit a bit spicy for my palette. But it didn't make me delusional. The lamb sagwala was spectacular -- thick, lucious, deep flavor, wonderful mixed with some rice, or I could have eaten it by itself. The garlic naan was the garlickiest I've ever had -- and that's a good thing! We were both stuffed, and half the food was still sitting on the table. I got it all, since she was eating out all weekend. So we put our food in the styrofoam containers, wrapped the naan in foil, and I'm trying to open the plastic bag to put it all in. It wasn't happening. The guy who took our orders came by, gently took the plastic bag from my hand, smiled big (which he hadn't done the whole service), and opened that derned think in a New York second. Then he smiled bigger as he put all our containers in the bag and tied it in a knot!! Yippee!!

We've been looking for a fantastic and amazing Indian restaurant since we moved to Florida in November, and so far this is as close as we have found. My husband ordered the chicken tikka masala, and I got the kadahi paneer. We also ordered vegetable pakora and garlic naan. Everything tasted pretty good, no complaints. The serving size was smaller than what we're used to at the other Indian restaurants that we've been to, and the cost was higher as well. The service was good, a little slow, but very friendly. Overall, Gateway to India is the best Indian restaurant that we've found in St Petersburg so far and unless we find something better, we will definitely be back.

This place is horrible in every way.. When you walk in, it definitely doesn't feel like the most clean eating place with the salad and other condiment bar not being covered and just all around dirty, sloppy look inside. When i walked up to the register, both employees could not understand anything i was saying.. i asked for a gyro pita wrap with fries and the employee told me no? he turned around and started making my pita wrap.. this was very odd i began to think.. so after he started my meal he went back to the register to ring me up.. my bill came out to $9.21, when the menu clearly states $6.99 plus tax- this does not compute! i didnt even decide to argue since it was only a dollar and some change over. i tried to pay with a credit card, and they have the most ghetto credit card machine ive ever seen that didn't even work properly, i decided to just use cash. as i was waiting for my food, i saw them pull the french fries out of a freezer container... my friend ordered a side of dolmas (stuffed grape leaves).. the employee went to the back and grabbed ice and two cups and tried to charge him for drinks?? finally he got the order right and tried to charge my friend $3.99 for the dolmas, when the menu says $2.99 . I received my food, which didn't take very long, but the food was horrid. two small slabs of gyro meat, and a whole lot of pita. i couldn't even really taste the meat. i got to give it to them though, their pita bread is pretty good...lol anyways, end result.. if you are in IV and looking for a place to eat, dont bother with this place, just go to freebirds.

Pretty good Indian food. I had the Tandoori Chicken. There wasn't really anything wrong with it, but it just wasn't really to my taste. The garlic Naan was good, but had a LOT of garlic on it. Service was prompt, friendly, and attentive. Only real gripe is the price which seemed a tad high. Coming in for their lunch buffet is probably a good deal.
No. No yogurt in the Tikka Masala and the chicken was Tandoori. Naan was hard - inedible. Everything poorly executed and cheaply made. I ordered because of 4 stars. Not deserved.

They have the best Bun with egg roll and BBQ pork. Bun is a bowl of thin white rice noodles, topped with shredded lettuce, julienned cucumbers, bean sprout, carrots, and a goodly amt of bbq pork and two yummy and crispy fresh still warm egg rolls. Then you pour a sweet mildly spicy sauce all over it and inhale it. Soooo gooood. They also have other good dishes, but Bun is my fave. Service is very courteous and quick. Place is cozy and clean. I come here for Bun, and it's a great place. Lots of parking out front.

Always love coming here and the owner is a nice, friendly, guy. The chicken tikka masala is better than any other I've ever had. Reminds me a little bit of butter chicken but better! Beef nihari is excellent also and the beef is super tender. Naan could be improved however we always get the chapatti which is a nice change of pace and very excellent. My favorite Indian food in STL!

Before I even got my food, I was already impressed! The atmosphere was very welcoming and I was recommended some items to choose from on the menu. They have Turkish coffee :D and many vegetarian options. I am glad I stopped in! After I received my food, I was again impressed with the portion and tastes! Fantastic!!! I will certainly return.
The spring rolls were huge, the fried rice was delicious, and it all tasted so fresh. Can't wait to finish it off with taro boba tea! We've found our favorite local hole in the wall!

The Kabob & Grill just opened today. The place was very busy. I ordered take out. It took a little longer than expected, which is not really a surprise on opening day. The food was very good. We had the lamb curry and onion kulcha. Both were very tasty. We will definitely be back. It's great have a place with such tasty food so close to home.

At least 90% of pho places throughout SoCal are likely better than Pho Bistro. In hindsight, every time I ate here I thought it would have been better eating nearly anywhere else in IV. The pho soup is terrible: - the broth lacks any dimension - the sprout and veggie toppings are lacking and not fresh - the meat is skimpy in portion too - the meat choices are limited, with mostly a few types of tough meat as your only options. If you like less common cuts of meat like tripe and tendons you are out of luck here. The meatballs are the most flavorful option available. As a UCSB student, I ate here a couple times out of desperation for pho, and I can now happily say I will never dine here again. One recent night I was craving pho and Pho Bistro was the only place still open in town, so I went on in. A waitress asked my party if we would like to dine in or order take out. We chose the latter and were promptly seated. The same waitress came around again about five minutes later and asked if we knew what we wanted to order. I asked for a few more minutes, and eventually we placed our orders. Well, the girl came back from the kitchen asking if we minded ordering take out. If you haven't tried it, to-go pho, in particular, is not very palatable, especially in large styrofoam cups. This place closed early and led us into thinking we could dine in. Being led on like this was very upsetting. This misleading service on top of terrible pho is why I'll never go back.
So good!!! The owner is so welcoming and warm and his food is truly delicious. Definitely try the walnut baklava for dessert!

Just when you didn't think you would desire to eat whipped feta with breakfast, go to Butcher and Bee for brunch. I'm a big fan of their creative menus, bold and savory items and pleasant non-pretentious vibe. If you haven't given this joint a try- do it!!!

Service was meh for the money. We slipped into the bar around 5:30pm on a Saturday evening. Took 20 minutes to put our dinner order in. Saw someone eat something behind the bar, saw hostesses drinking coke/tea behind the stand often... just not something we're used to seeing at other high-end restaurants. Ordered a cocktail, it was prepared well. Had to ask for a napkin since I squeezed the grapefruit into the drink and had nothing to wipe my hands on. Had to ask for silverware, salt and pepper. Proscuitto wrapped cheese stuffed figs were wonderful. Beet salad just okay. Ordered the Gnocci for dinner, it was nice but portions were small. I'd rather eat somewhere else.

My first impression walking in was-- Wow, this place is tiny. It has only about half a dozen tables. Thankfully, a table of six was already in place. If you need to bring more than six people, I'd definitely call ahead. There only seemed to be a few people working (one lady serving as the waitress who likely was the owner, a delivery guy, and I'm assuming a chef or two). The lady was very nice and fairly attentive. We being weird Chinese girls and given that it was pouring rain outside, we requested some hot water, which the lady served with a pretty black teapot set. The portion sizes were generous. One person ordered shrimp pad thai, which came with several decent-sized shrimp. My stuffed eggplant dish was delicious. Everyone was pretty pleased with their food. Like I mentiomed, it's a little cramped here but the food and portion sizes well make up for it. Welcome to Philly, Green Basil!

So I had pho + fresh roll here today. The pho here is actually quite good. Of the three places that I went to this week this one had the most flavorful broth and the freshest plate o veggies for the soup. The fresh rolls weren't as good a story though...There was way too much lettuce in them and it overpowered the roll. There was no green onion. The pork was rather stiff, as if it was overcooked and the wrapper was chewy. Oh yeah, and the fish sauce was a bit too fishy, but not as much as the place that starts with an S down the street. The ice coffee was also way too sweet. I didn't feel like i was drinking coffee anymore. I also wasn't a big fan of how it was presented. They brought it out pre-mixed and over ice already instead of dripping at the table. I don't normally care about this, but when it comes out so sweet and there is a lot of condensed milk still floating around, you know something didn't go quite right. The people were kind, and while one of them could hardly speak english, we were still able to communicate and my meal came out exactly like I wanted it. There was a mother/daughter pair at a table near me that seemed rather concerned that I had gotten raw meat on the side. It was fun hearing their conversation, I suppose they thought that me being 6 feet away would stop me from being able to hear the conversation.

I must start this review by thanking the lady at the counter. We came in and my little daughter needed to use the bathroom which is behind the counter (really not for customers). The kind lady went in and cleaned the bathroom to make sure it's clean for the little girl; thank you! We would have loved to stay in, unfortunately it was a hot and humid evening so we opted to take the food to go. We had the gyro, the chicken shawarma, grape leaves, falafel and babaganoush. Everything was truly tasty. The chicken shawarma tasted as in between pulled chicken and shawarma, but delicious nonetheless. The lemonade was refreshing as well. The only let down was the tahini, but the humus and Tzatziki sauce were tasty. Had this place been slightly bigger, it would've easily earned a five stars. Great food and excellent service despite the size.

This was a big disappointment. My husband and I love Thai food, but the food here was average at best. The curry dishes were small and unfulfilling. Also, we were a group of 8 that had to wait for over an hour for our order. When we asked the waiter about it he was indifferent and didn't try to apologise or compensate us.

Was looking to try Indian food and this place was recommended by a friend - and boy was I glad they did. The 7 day a week lunch buffet is a great way to try different things and everything is always hot and fresh. The naan is made fresh and served to your table and can get as much as you would like. The service is always excellent, very friendly and prompt. Highly recommend the mango lassi along with all the delicious food on the buffet. Have also done take-out and the food quality is still top-notch.

Here's a quickie review for my quick stop in: Super chill place. Open till 3, so great place to keep the party going after the bars. Great service, they changed and stoked our coals without being asked. No alcohol. Comfortable couches. Reasonable prices. What more do you need? You can mix the flavors as well, I'd recommend the mint with berries. Mmmmm.
Good experience! Brunch was AMAZING! No service issues but it was really slow when I was there, had their signature drink and really enjoyed it too! Will be back!

A great place to eat with your hands, if a little pricey. We usually get one of the combination platters which allow you to choose a number of items, served on a large platter. Some of the items can be a bit spicy, but most are fairly mild. The lady running this place works like crazy and is nice as can be. Try the Ethiopian beers: Hakim stout especially. Yum. My only complaint, they never seem to give enough injera initially; we always have to ask for more.

their pho ga is pretty good. their beef pho is average. can't comment on anything else but coming from NYC.... their broth is definitely bone boiled and but bullion types. summer roll is fresh and refreshing. peanut butter sauce has a stronger than normal hoysin taste. I'm okay with it because i enjoy the taste but maybe off putting for others

Well, folks, this is the pinnacle. Exquisite Medi-Italian cuisine Calm, warm atmosphere Friendly, knowledgeable, professional staff Affordable when compared to restaurants of similar quality Okay, let's get into it! I went for an anniversary dinner a couple of nights ago. I made reservations a day in advance (I recommend you do the same) and when we arrived, we were seated at a lovely white table. We were in time for the Happy Hour special, which got us each (for the normal price of an entree) an entree, soup or salad, and a dessert. My date and I got different desserts, entrees, and starters so we could share and try everything. We also got an appetizer of dolmades; I wanted the flaming cheese, be my date is crazy about dolmades, so I obliged her. The dolma were terrific, though hey did go a bit mad with the bechamel sauce. The Greek salad was crisp, Avgolemono soup was delicious and smooth. My date's Pasta ala Greco was perfectly al dente, and my souvlaki was tender and flawlessly seasoned, my pilaf was fluffy and her coffee was very good (I had tea). For our dessert, we got baklava and Greek custard, and split them both in two so we could both have them together. I don't really need to say it, but they were spot-on. The finest date I've been on. Terrific.

Fair-to-middlin'. This is my new favorite southern expression. It's also how I'd describe by experience at Kabob House. I've dined here a few times over the years, but I'll stick with my latest experience, which was tonight. I shared the lamb kabob and pumpkin stew with my gf. One thing about my gf: she likes her meat juicy. So we made sure to ask the server to cook the kabobs rare to medium-rare. (What did you think I was talking about? Sheesh!) Alas, the kabobs we received were more like medium-well; they still had flavor but definitely lacked the desired juiciness. (It may be they aren't able to cook lamb that rare. But, if so, they should have told us so we could order something else!) The pumpkin stew was fine but a little disappointing. I've enjoyed pumpkin dishes at other Afghani restaurants, but this stew was much sweeter -- to the point that I wasn't able to fully appreciate the pumpkin flavor. Like I said, "fair-to-middlin'."

An excellent restaurant! Please come visit because you will not be disappointed! The yellow curry is fabulous and comes with Japanese pumpkin, onion, and bell pepper. I ordered it with chicken and ate the entire thing. My friend ordered pad Thai which was also delicious

I went with a friend to check it out. Great location, beautiful views and the waitress was friendly. However, the food was horrendous. I asked for the wings to be cooked extra crispy and ordered the hottest sauce. The wings came out soggy with soft chicken skin (disgusting) and the sauce had no discernible heat. I had also ordered a pound of peel and eat shrimp served cold. The shrimp came out in a galvanized can full of water, no ice cubes remained and this is how they served my food. The wait for the food was 35 minutes. I drank my beer, barely touched my food and made a kind complaint to the waitress who replied "I'm sorry", took my card, ran it and offered no further apology or any kind of discount. My advice: If you want to have a drink this place is fine. If you want to eat - go somewhere else!! I won't be going back
Great local spot. Seriously good food at a reasonable price!
Good tasting food and value. Having been spoiled by Jasmine in West Chester, the lack of ambience and rather typical menu disappointed a bit. But it was quick and reasonable and quite busy.

Went for a buffet lunch with office guyz. They say sometimes the best things come in small packets. Its so true to this place. Limited but fresh and tasty spread. Meat cooked just right. Eggplant pakoras just right with green chutney. Fresh rotis yes garlic rotis nice and fluffy coming right on to ur table. Non greasy non diabetic prone gulab jamoons...overall perfect lunch buffet. Service with a smile makes a lot of difference. Thru this resturant u can see someones dream coming true,infact the chef and his wife's. Best of luck Mr and Mrs Ashni Guru....plz keep walking...will keep coming again for sure

The staff was extremely friendly. I wanted the chicken satay tacos but my eyes were drawn to the chicken katsu platter. The platter was tasty and the portion was decent for $5. I was content. Coming back for more.

Great place for fast Indian food. The best part is that You have the options to customize your order based on your specific choice of tastes. Customer service is great too and was quick on making my order and suggesting what to get! It's a must try!
Had the chicken gyro for lunch today. Everything was so fresh and flavorful. This plus an extremely friendly & helpful staff and owner makes this place awesome!
Love it! Keep up the good music & im sure you will do great & im referring you guys to all my Latino friends!!! This is our new spot now! Love it! One suggestion better & bigger margaritas

The restaurant is very neat and clean. The owner is cordial and service very good. The pho was excellent and if you have a sweet tooth, you must definitely try the fried bananas in coconut sauce. I would recommend to anyone who enjoys Vietnamese cuisine.

God I love their grilled octopus appetizer. Just thinking about it now is making me salivate. It is cooked in a little bit of lemon and olive oil-- pure, delectable simplicity. Which could be Dmitri's motto if they had one. Their style of Greek cooking is basic--there are no fancy twists on things, but when you have something that is this good to begin with, why change it? The Dmitri's on 3d Street is a BYOB and there is always a wait to get in. In partnership with New Wave, which is the bar directly across the street, they've come up with a great method of dealing with this potential problem: Dmitri's patrons can sit at the bar at New Wave, have a cocktail and wait for the server to come and get them when their table is ready. For entrees, try the bluefish or in fact any whole fish they have on the menu. It comes with a rice dish and collard greens. Absolute yumminess!

I was not very impressed with this place. I got the two things I always get at Thai places: green curry and pad thai. Green curry: I feel like they use corn starch or something to thicken the curry because the consistency was icky and it didn't taste like other green curries I've had. Pad Thai: the noodles were kind of sticky and gooey... not sure why. Also my friend and I ordered mild or medium spice I forget, but these noodles were flaming!!! I can handle spicy, it just wasn't what we ordered so it was kind of disappointing. It does depend on the chilis though because every day is different.

This place was awful. If you want good Vietnamese food go somewhere else. The bahn mi sandwich was tasteless and soggy. When I asked for a vegetarian sandwich he said he would put soy sauce on the sandwich which would make the bread soggy. I said no. The grilled tofu was tasteless and soggy. The chicken my friend had was also bad.
Very well designed, good food, great prices. We had the chicken vermicelli bowl which was much better seasoned than Magasin.

I got delivery from this place when I was in Philly a few weeks ago. I wasn't expecting much, but what I got was shockingly good. I still think about the soup with the coconut milk. So creamy and mild. I don't know if I can find that soup back home. :(

We came here on Christmas Eve and this place was packed! We had a great time here, good food and good service in a cozy restaurant. The Tom yum soup was delicious, which was a good start to the meal. We ordered two entrees from the specialty section, both had huge portions and a abundance of vegetables. Get the coconut rice. It's absolutely delicious. I can eat it by itself for a meal! The spring rolls had wraps a little too thick for our liking, but still well flavored. The best part is obviously the BYO. Don't forget to bring a bottle of wine when you come. Service was fast, courteous and pleasant. This is not one of the fancy restaurants, rather a comfortable, cute Thai place. But can be a great stop for a casual date night or family/friends outing!
Fresh and delicious! I am middle eastern and I was worried this would be very Americanized. But it was actually delicious and has a good authenticity to it.

Great little spot for dinner and drinks! Located in the more relaxed SoBro area, this place is very comfortable with dimmed lighting and soft Spanish music playing in the background. We had the salsa trio with house made chips. Great flavor and fresh tasting. For dinner, try the tamal! A little different from tradition, but the smoky savory flavor of the meat on top of the sweet corn cake is to die for! The portions are larger and great to share. Great cocktails too!

Where do I start? They try to cut cost all around and the food and service suffers. Pricey and service sucks. The Tortilla soup was extremely salty, I informed waiter and he just said Oh, OK. Did did not offer to bring me a salad or side dish instead. Tostones(fried plantains), did not come with the traditional olive oil/garlic sauce, instead they serve them with a cheap green mayo based sauce. The black beans were sweet, traditionally, they should not be sweet. The burger was char-coaled to death and bread partially burned. No cheese! I've had better at Outback Steakhouse! Do not recommend this place at all, All hype and no substance, their website makes it appear way better than it is. You were warned!! THIS IS NOT CUBAN FOOD, MAYBE MODIFIED CUBAN AT BEST, TRUST ME I HAVE CUBAN FRIENDS AND BEEN TO LITTLE HAVANA.

I bookmarked Sky cafe a little while ago and finally got around to try this place yesterday evening. The place is pretty small and was pretty crowded but we got sitted right away. Our waiter was really nice and helpful. When we placed our order, he pointed out stuff that could throw us out as it was our first time trying Indonesian food. I ordered the "Mie Udang (Emie)" and my best friend ordered the "Mie Belacan" We both were very happy with what we picked as it was very tasty and had a very interesting taste. This place is very cheap given what they serve. I am excited to go back again. Fyi - They do not accept debit/credit card

Great bahn mi and pho. They also have a great selection of rice and noodle dishes. The best part, unlike most Vietnamese joints in the area, Seasons is open late and caters to late diners. The best place for a late night noodle fix is here!

Place seemed nice food was ok but didn't realize how cheap and stingie they are. Got a Togo order. My pho and a lemonade. Asked for a lemonade with no ice and she proceeded to give me half of a glass of lemonade, I asked for it to be filled up and argued with me said no. I said whatever I'll pay.. she charge me a extra dollar to fill up which was ridiculous. Even after I tipped her $2.00 for a togo meal. So basically gave her more money and still... watch out for the older lady who runs a restaurant ha ha Ha

If it is happiness that you seek, visit Mood cafe. The food is good. If you are from the subcontinent, stick to the basics. But whatever you do, spend up some time to strike up a conversation with Hassan. You will step out feeling good about life and all the joy it could offer you if you stop and look :)

The services was amazing! Our servers name was micheal! Very attentive and friendly, he was the only server and managed to answer all our questions without making us feel rushed. Food was so good. We ordered way too much, but still delicious. Will be coming back! As the back of their shirts say."I love umami!" ;)

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: South Ocean's website is most definitely deceiving. It gives the impression of a lush Asian Experience. Reality is much different than the Matrix... I would call this dive sushi in a Chandler-esque manner. This place is not for the faint of heart...or even the local food inspector. While the Lexis Roll really is a fantastic creation (tuna, salmon, avocado, spicy sauce and an exotic presentation, the rest of the really sushi is just passable...if you can't get sushi anywhere else. The staff is courteous. The clientele is amusing. Don't come for the sushi. I'm still on the hunt for good sushi in suburban Philly. I may have to break down and actually head into the City. More to follow...

This Thai food is incredible. Everything is fresh, veggies are crunchy and they make the best curries. The portions and prices are very fair. They could be more generous with shrimp, but they are large and never overcooked.. The owners are there every time and make sure to greet each guest with a smile. The Chi Chee and Panang curry are personal favorites. The Gai Tom Kai is excellent. They make their own ice cream (coconut or mango). Both are excellent. Lunch is still a bargain at $10. You get soup, appetizer and an entree. Reservations recommended on Fri and Sat. Fresh, fast and excellent quality of ingredients

I LOVE Marjie's Grill. First, I walked in and the place smelled amazing. And when I tasted the food, I was still just as impressed. My friend L and I ordered a bunch of stuff that I can't remember anymore, but everything was very tasty. If they are serving grilled sweet potatoes, get them. I also really loved the pork knuckles. Do yourself and favor and eat here!

Walked over half mile and stumbled upon this restaurant. Being Indian, I got excited looking at their menu. Due to the fact its janamastmi hubby n I were vegetarian for the weekend. Came into the restaurant n there was a talk Punjabi man who was cleaning the buffet area. He didnt greet us til we sat down. I asked for paneer tikka masala just instead of paneer masala. He instantly said no. Hubby and i ordered navratan masala and paneer masal and two whole wheat rotis. I saw that he was Punjabi, I had no doubt in my mind the food would be chat pata (spicy). The food was brought out in 10 ounce plastic containers, rotis were in individual foil paper and they were reallll thick rotis. My mom would've kicked the @$$ of the persi n who made rtve rotis. Anyway the entrees tasted exactly rhe same and it was sweeter than most Gujarati food I've tried. I askes for a green chilli they gave me achar. A white man walks in n he was greeted instantly. Really Punjabi man? Anytime we asked him for something, he had the ched type of guy cone out n give it to us...how dare he move. Not worth the walk. I should've went to Minar instead
Ordered food at 9pm on a Friday and it was here within 25 minutes! The Pad Thai was simply amazing and the guy who delivered it was very friendly. 10/10 would recommend them for delivery.

I was here this week for lunch. My dining partner was well-greeted by one of the servers. Then I found out she's been there many, many times to enjoy both lunch and dinner. So, I asked HER for a suggestion from the menu. THE BURGER! Works for me. We both ordered the steak burger ($9) -- Stuffed with gorgonzola, arugula and balsamic onions. I believe it was a brioche bun. You could get THE BURGER with fries or a salad. I chose salad. She chose fries. We opted for a booth, which are so delightful and private. They're totally enclosed on three sides. You slide in, and you're in your own world. Back to THE BURGER. Quite rare. (They didn't ask about how you wanted it cooked, but I think that's because it's steak.) Full of flavor, really a nice, rich beef taste. I should have ditched the bun. I didn't see the arugula, but the gorgonzola and onions were in perfect proportion with the beef. The challenge with this rare of a burger is the bun gets soaked with juices when you put any pressure on the sandwich. And you DO have to squash it a bit to get it to fit into your mouth. Or just to cut it. That's when the bun gets in the way and becomes superfluous. The menu didn't say how big THE BURGER is, but I'd suggest it was into hefty ouncedom. The salad. Torn romaine (not massive leaves that required cutting), Kalamata olives (sans pits), tomato and cucumber (no seeds) pieces, red onion, and feta. Italian (light?) dressing. So flavorful. So good. I could have eaten a platter of this salad. It was delightful! The fries. I tried a few of my dining partner's. Flavorful, battered (?), seasoned with something lucious (I'd guess paprika from the look and the taste). They were fabulous and cooked just right -- plenty crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside. I took half my burger back to the office and had it as a snack late in the afternoon. As such, it became my dinner. Service was lovely. We were never wanting for water refills. I like this place . . . the food, the ambiance, the service, the happy greeting when you walk in the door and the parking lot.

Yum!! My husband & I just left - absolutely delicious! I had the pork souvlaki. It was perfectly seasoned and charred to perfection. The street fries are covered in a Greek dry cheese, similar to pecorino - we didn't leave any on our plates. My husband had the beef souvlaki - he ate it so fast I didn't get a bite :( but also really enjoyed it. We shared some Greek red wine as well... my Dad was Greek, and would have given this eating spot an A+!

This place smells super strange. That's my only bone to pick with pita jungle. I have no idea why but it smells awful. The food is pretty good I had a small Greek salad and a gyro and I would return just get my food to go next time. Cheers!
Food was tasty, ambience is beautiful, and staff was friendly and nice. Their lunch special was reasonably priced. I will definitely be back!

This place is so good! We did appetizers---lettuce wraps, tacos, and salad, dessert---banana fried something, and drinks-pear mojito and Mai Tai. Everything was fresh and piping hot! Our hostess, Sierra, was very sweet and attentive. We were there forever and kept ordering, ordering, and ordering and she never once seemed bothered or annoyed by it (which some waitresses certainly show the oposite). If you have never been to PF Chang's--it's worth giving it a shot. If you have been to PF Chang's then you shouldn't be reading this because you already know what it's like. Spoiler alert--tacos are really really spicy.
Terrific! Alu Gobi, navratan Korma and chicken korma. Really good! Medium heat can be spicy still so be careful!

Interested in a new, light, and tongue pleasing experience? Then look no further than the Saigon Vietnamese Restaurant. They have the flavors and freshness to please you and enough variety to keep you coming back for more. This was definitely one of my better dining experiences in the last year and I'm looking forward to my next visit. The only thing that keeps me from giving the them four piggies is that I didn't get goose bumps, but don't worry there are still plenty of dishes left on the menu that could give them to me! In summary: The Saigon Restaurant definitely lives up to its namesake.

The roti was great. The coconut bun was great. The provision with saltifsh was a little imbalanced, but in part that's my fault for getting provision when I know that's not my favorite dish. I feel confident enough that the roti and coconut bun are representative that I'm comfortable giving five stars.

Judging by its interior you would have never guessed this place serves hookah. The hookah is horrifying, this is the place to go with someone U hate. :p The bar is total random and the interior table seating is completely setup wrong.

Dinner before theatre. We were seated in a beautiful, private booth. My husband started with a Caesar salad which he enjoyed. I had the Shepherds Salad...lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, olive, feta in a vinegar and oil dressing! Husband enjoyed lobster ravioli. ..I had the trout, which was served with spinach. Dessert...shared the apple pie. Very good service and experience. Reasonably priced.

Can you say YUM?!!! I have had Cucina Zapata bookmarked for some time now, but I finally made the trek to Drexel to grab the famous tilapia burrito last Friday. We made the mistake of going right during lunch time, but despite the busyness, our food was ready in about 10 minutes. I loved my tilapia burrito - perfectly cooked, perfectly crusted, and tons of flavor bursting with every bite. I wouldn't say that this was a fancy burrito per se, but for $6 it was delicioso in my tummy. I'd love to return soon for some of their tacos! One tip is that they're parked on Ludlow, which is under the bridge in this area. Be sure to turn onto Ludlow from Market (not Chestnut) if you are driving or else you'd be very confused.
The interior is a tad off putting but don't let that discourage you. The food is great... No frills, but still delicious.

I was looking for a great hookah bar with great environment that isn't already have thousands of burned holes in their furniture. I feel like Aladdin's is fairly new so environment is quiet fresh! However, hookahs are $23... it's quiet expensive when you think about it! They have happy hour from 4-7pm where hookahs are $12, but honestly, who will go there that early? But overall it's a good place with gentle Arabic music playing in the background. 4/5

Very modern decor. Menu is good but very limited. Very cute date spot. Food lacked bold flavors, I rarely use salt. I wanted salt and more heat. I wasn't overly impressed by anything. For the Midwest it is great. As a west coast person it was just ok. Culver City appeal minus the flavors.

Just had breakfast here and everything was fabulous. I ordered the bacon, egg and cheese quesadilla with home fries with 1 slice of french toast . All the food was super hot and fresh. I will make it a point to eat here when I visit my friends in south jersey. Also, the earlier you get there the better. They get very busy! Oh, and our server Alexis was great! :)
Great place!! Enjoyed the Trip Through Puerto Rico and had a little bit of everything. Shari was a fantastic waitress!! Will definitely be back!

A gem in the city. There are dozens of cool places on South street but this has to be one of the tops. The restaurant itself is very modest in space and design. It feels very private and warming, a great spot for a date or conversation. Our waitress, Victoria was very charming and helpful. I wanted to order stuffed eggplant and tofu supreme but she told me both had very similar sauce and toppings and I ended up ordering the cat fish, which was awesome! We had thai fish cakes for appetizers and they very perfect. Golden brown and crispy on the outside and juicy in the inside. Think delicious juicy nuggets with fish and lemon grass seasoning with sweet thai dipping sauce. Victoria suggested I should have my fried fish with sauce on the side so they stay crunchy. It was a brilliant idea! We didn't finish so I took the fish home and rebaked it in the oven. Then drizzle the sauce over it. It tasted exactly like how I had it in the restaurant, crunchy and fresh. Terrific idea from our wonderful waitress. The stuffed eggplant surprised me the most, in a good way! I'm used to having mashed shrimp stuffed inside eggplants. They're both soft textures the shrimps and eggplants. Here however, they stuffed minced fried chicken. Oh man it was yummy! The stuffing is crunchy while the eggplant was soft making a very exciting contrast. Check this place out, you will not be dissapponted!

I've been to this place 7-8 times thus far - driving nearly an hour each way. So, I really go out of my way to eat at this place. I think this place has the best Indian food in the philly area. I only had their lunch buffet and they never seemed to disappoint. Malai Kofta is to die for. Some of their other dishes come very close to authentic indian taste - not the taste most indian restaurants cater to american consumers. Plus, they have masala tea & mango lassi part of their buffet. How can you beat that??? The atmosphere is so so - not bad for a restaurant in a shopping center. Their sweet deserts can be a hit&miss time to time.

I would give this place no stars if possible. we ordered delivery at 8:40pm, it was supposed to be delivered by 9:30pm. I called at 10pm when it wasn't here yet and they said it was on it's way. (half a mile away) By 10:40pm I called when it still wasn't here and they told me that I wasn't the only person ordering food. If this wasn't bad enough, when the food finally got here it was cold. I will never order from them again.
Great Thai food in Doylestown! We had the Phad Kae Mao and the Phad Thai. For an appetizer we had the Wheel of Fortune. Very nice staff. Definitely recommend
Yeah! Great food in Apollo Beach. Excellent family run business. Delicious schwarma, gyro & baklava!!! Fresh, healthy & tasty. Service is fast & friendly. Great for lunch or dinner.
Ordered the Hue Soup (#62) and the Catfish in Stone bowl. Both were delicious. The soup was spicy and hot, and the fish was delicious. Would definitely come back next time through Indianapolis
Love this restaurant! It's a must have for our family once a week. We always get two of the number 10's, number 5, and number 3. Must try restaurant!

My wife and I stopped in for dinner recently on a Saturday night and were pleasantly surprised with the food here. we actually meant to go to the vietnam cafe, which is around the corner but popped in here by accident. Its a pretty small place with the tables packed in tightly together so you can pretty much hear what everybody around you is talking about and it got pretty loud when the dining room filled up. The servers were very attentive and friendly. I got the pad thai which I thought was fabulous but I've never had it before so I don't really have anything to compare it against. The amount of food for the price was great as well. My wife got the sweet thai basil shrimp and that tasted wonderful. She doesn't really like spicy food and they cooked it up sans spicy-ness with no fuss. Hers was a little smaller portion size, and it was perfect for her but might leave you wanting a bit more if you're a big eater. The neighborhood was nice, with a major "portlandia" vibe lol. I would be careful about straying too far though because the area gets real sketchy if you go to far in the wrong direction

We have such a great eating experience every time we come here. The Vietnamese food is really good. All tge dishes are very fresh and flavorful. I live in South Philly were there are plenty of Vietnamese restaurants I've eaten at there. They don't compare to Oriental Pearl. I just wish they were in South Philly.
Finally! Good Indian food in downtown Indianapolis. Hilarious placement by the bars though haha.

Great buffet with a pretty decent selection. I enjoyed everything I tried...which was a little of everything on the buffet! My dinner companion and I agreed that it was better than most of the buffets we have been to in Philly. Service was also excellent.

Very disappointed. I have been craving Pad Thai and decided to order from Little Kitchen tonight. The food took a little over an hour to be delivered (only ordered pad thai and an egg roll) and when I ate it, there was absolutely no flavor. The noodles were so bland that even adding some spices from my own kitchen could not make it edible . . . so I threw it out. Really disappointing for someone that has been craving pad thai and still hungry!

One if the best thai restaurant in town..travelled all the way from northern jersey to relish their food. Ambience: 4/5 Food: 4/5 Quantity: 3.5/5 Service: 3/5 Love the chicken satay and the drunken noodles. The service is good and personal attention too detail is commendable. Will be back..

Hands down... Best place EVER to get a cold treat with great customer service. I've visited this place 4 times and was never disappointed. If I lived in west Philly I would gladly visit this place every week (everyday if I could afford it!) My favorite lassi flavors are Rose and Apple fig. The owner is amazing at helping you decide and makes each lassi with great care. The next time I visit I'll try the chaat!
#15 was as good as I've had in LA. If you're adventurous and would like to try some pork blood sausages :) I would highly recommend. A bit different from pho but really good nonetheless.

Absolutely the BEST Caribbean restaurant in Tampa by West Platt ave before Bayshore Blvd. It's located inside the area of Wallgreens and UPS Store. The curry goat was so delicious for my lunch and ate it all and the plantains are very tasty. I ordered another to go for tonight. They have authentic varieties of food and also drinks. The whole interior was a bright white very chic and classy clean look. You will enter this place and you will say WOW...Try it and you won't regret. It's a family owned so the whole family put lots of love on this restaurant business. Chef Janice and the whole family member are all polite and really give the best customer service.
Came here with a group. Good food. Sambosa was delicious. Chicken kabobs were great and flavored nicely. Friendly staff. Good place to try out afghan food

All I have to say is dat feta dip doe. Probably one of the best dishes in Nashville. Everything is very easy to share with friends. Great service and we were seated quicker than the time they had allotted for our wait on both visits.

We have patronized this restaurant for years and it is as good now as when we started. The food is always fresh and prepared to order. The House Special Biryani, the Chicken Tikka Masala, and the Mushroom Saag, are always great choices. The weekend buffets have a lot of variety. The owner and staff are friendly, accommodating and have always made us welcome. The restaurant has been redecorated and updated. It is very clean and comfortable. This is a real treasure tucked away on the west side of Indy and well worth the trip to try.
Eureka!! Found a very authentic and delicious new spot tonight. Flavorful, nice portions and super friendly staff. Not much else to say. Will definitely be going back.

Service ok. Food is good. It is right next to the train station so it gets a little loud but the food makes up for it. They are very nice people who own it but they just need to work better in providing service. BYOB which is a plus.
Really good food -- really pushes their drinks, which I've heard are also good. Good pricing, probably the best Chinese food you can get in University City, if you like Shanghai food.

I've lived in Nashville for 15 years and eat out everyday. I love trying all the new places and have had different Thai favorites over the years. I can honestly say that the Smiling Elephant is by far the best in my opinion. The owner, Sam, is as cool as they come and cares about your experience there. He truly wants you to be happy. Excellent staff as well. I give it two thumbs up without question!!
This will satisfy your curry cravings. Not as many selections but they are good. Really cheap lunch buffet . Friendly service. Yeah I'll come back for lunch.

Pad Thai was bad. Curry was bad. Slow service. Never coming back. It's pretty hard to mess pad Thai up... yet the noodles are undercooked, the sauce needs more tamarind sauce. Not worth the calories. Oh the tom yum soup was alright though

Even though the food is over priced I have been a loyal customer here since they opened because of the frequent customer punch card they had. A few weeks ago I tried to use my punch cards for the three free coffees and one sandwich that I earned. To my surprise they would not keep their end of the deal because the program was canceled a couple of days before I went in for a coffee and sandwich. After discussing my loyalty and all the times since they opened I came in and also brought many other people in to eat/drink there, the owner and managers still insisted that I was not getting what I earned for being a loyal customer. It seems odd that they would prefer to lose me as a customer as well of my guests over a coffee and a sandwich? They have already lost more business from the three times I have stopped in so far. Their unappreciative attitude has led me to boycott them and never stop again. There are many other choices in the neighborhood that COST LESS and hopefully appreciate their customers more.
Service is very nice...but all the food are way too sweet, feels like americanized thai rather than mix of sour and sweet thai authenticity....

The whyte avenue remedy is my favourite location to swing by for a chai - it is definitely the smallest location that I have been to - but it has never had a long line up and is the easiest location to get to for me, the chai has got me hooked. I don't know if I would sit and study or hang out there for longer than the time it takes them to fix my drink - but I'm a "to go" kind of girl and that's why this location suits me just fine.

This is a Chinese Restaurant with some Vietnamese dishes. I usually just get the chicken pho here which is pretty good but probably the most expensive pho in the whole New Orleans metro area. The other dishes I've had here are decent for the most part with the sauces being not the most flavorful to me. They seem to give good portion sizes and the service has always been good. My biggest negative for this place is I really find their hot & sour soup to be the worst example of that dish I've ever had and I just don't find it edible. The location is very convenient to where I live and the nearest place to get my pho fix (for now but I've seen TWO new pho places opening on Magazine so huzzah!!!) When new pho options appear I doubt I shall be returning very often if at all...

Went here while visiting New Orleans. From the New York area and enjoy good meals. Parts of our meal was amazing. The smoked tuna app was a great mixture of flavor and texture. My wife had the Brussels sprouts, which was so good I hope to reproduce at home. Parts of our meal were amazing. I had the smoked tuna, which was really a great mixture of flavors and texture. My wife had the Brussel sprouts, which I would love to make at home. But that is not why I am writing. My entrée was the dual beef, very good, but the portion could have been larger. Even if you doubled the amount of beef, you would still have a great food cost. The real issue was with my wife's entrée. The chicken dish. Cooking the thigh cassoulet style was/is an interesting idea...but it failed. Of course it works with duck and duck fat. The chicken was not improved by cooking it in olive oil chicken does not have the fat content of duck and it suffered. The breast meat could have been considered inedible. Breast is really difficult to cook correctly, without overcooking, which makes it dry. The Breast was dry, lacking flavor the chicken part of the dining experience could be described as inedible. I would suggest you take the chicken entrée off the menu until you figure out how to cook it correctly or change the dish altogether. I mentioned my concerns to our sever. She was great, well informed(though I think you could improve their "uniforms.") She was well versed on what was supposed to come out of the kitchen. However, I am not sure she mentioned my feedback to anyone in the kitchen. Not sure if she was just tired of hearing a tourist complain about food(one she would not see again) or the kitchen staff, like most are less than receptive on criticism from a server, vis a vis a customer. You should learn to listen to your servers, they usually know what the problems are in the kitchen. Yes, I am a tourist who will probably not be back to New Orleans any time soon. But I have more influence on restaurants because almost anyone I know defers to my knowledge of food, not just in the New York area but other places. For example, Grey in Savannah don't waste your money, and I was really looking forward to it, Red Rooster in Harlem...one of my all time favorite places and Marcus Samuelson does a great job . Now improve your chicken or take it off the menu. Tourist stay away. I sent this review to the restaurant. They did not respond. I was not looking for a comp, just offering a suggestion or two for a better dining experience.

Macarons & Goodies is a sweet little shop located in a not-so-sweet part of town. I have high hopes that the recent revitalization that the arena is bringing to downtown will liven up this location in coming years. I hopped over here after lunch in Chinatown with my husband and good friend to grab dessert. The shop is really pretty, with bright pastel colors, beautiful display cases and comfortable furniture to sit and relax with a coffee or meal. Along with baked goods, there are full menu options available, including soup and sandwiches. Since I had just had lunch I wasn't too interested in the savory options, but it looked like there was a good variety. Between the three of us we got quite a sampling, including macrons, Madeleines, a brownie, a small cake and an eclair. Everything was very pretty, and the care the owners put into preparing good looking desserts is evident. I was quite pleased with my Madeleine and macarons, they had nice texture and sweetness, and were fresh. We all agreed that everything was good and that we would return, but we wouldn't make a special trip downtown just to visit.

Ok I found my go to Phó spot every time I'm in Reno! Literally down the street from GSR. Service is excellent and very friendly! The food is awesome! I highly recommend the Ox Tail Phó!! If only they were located inside GSR then omg I can just go downstairs and voila!! So next time you're in Reno come and stop by.

Last weekend we checked in pretty late , heard that they only serve to go food at that hour, but the hosts were very kind to have us and agreed to serve dine in. Food was absolutely delicious particularly the goat curry and jerk chicken . Also gave us complimentary patties :) . Lastly they even agreed to drop us to our car considering we had walked quite a long way . Such considerate people . Would definately return again

My husband and I checked this out last night with another couple. We got there just about six and were seated right away. They are not accepting reservations so we wanted to get there on the early side for dinner. Loved the interior. We were seated just inside the bar area. Our server greeted us right away and explained the cocktail list to us. I chose the margarita. I have to say, I'm not typically a tequila fan, but this was made with higher end tequila and also had orange blossom water. It was a very strong drink and a great way to start the night. We opted for the guacamole and the trio of salsas. The guacamole had pistachios in it and that was a great combo. The salsas were great too, very fresh tasting. I liked the roasted pumpkin one the most. My friend and I opted for a bottle of wine and they have some great choices. We went with the Columna Albariño and enjoyed it. Our table water was refreshed constantly. I ordered the tamal corn cakes with barbacoa and my husband ordered the empanadas. So delicious! It was a flavor party in my mouth! We ended with the plantain dessert and the churros. The plantain was like an apple crisp with ice cream. The chocolate for the churros was just right. Next time, I would try the flan. Consensus? Run, don't walk to this restaurant. I hope they start taking reservations as there was a 45 minute wait when we left.
One of my favorite places to go for appetizers and drinks! Gorgeous sunset's and good music!

I am a huge fan of caribbean food, so I was excited to try this place. The jerk chicken was pleasantly spicy; however, the star of the show was definitely the peas and rice. We tried one of each type of patty and they were all great, though the vegetable and beef stood out for me. They even deliver (and quickly) which is great. I'll definitely be back to try some of the other things on the menu.

What a find. Indian buffet that is reliably fresh, quick and cheap. Can it get any better than $5 for a POUND of food? I'm a big fan of the chicken tikka masala. It may not be the best you'll find in the city, but few indian food places in Philly are better. For the price and the convenience, it's a great choice for lunch or a low-priced takeout dinner.

Yeah, this hut has great outdoor space. Probably it's only saving grace. I make better jerk chicken and peas and rice. And I'm BAHAMIAN. (if I said "white" it probably would be more emphatic. but, still. just sayin') Whole foods has better cornbread. And they're WHOLE FOODS. The only reason why this place doesn't get one star is because I enjoyed watching my mom dunk her shrimp in her water glass because it was too spicy. And the waitress didn't even flinch. Love it!
This Restaurant is CLOSED. India Gate restaurant is opening on Friday June 26th, 2015 at the same location.

Upon walking in we were not greeted, I'm not sure of it was because we were in workout clothes or what but the service was not the best. We came in 10 minutes before a group of cops and they got served before us! They were getting food before we even got water. I like cops too, but the service inequality was noticed by more than just us. The food itself was pretty good, don't suggest the curry but I'm just not a green bean fan. You really can't go wrong with any flat noodle dish or soup. So as my personal non-professional opinion I would suggest ordering it for take-out, rather than eating there.

Delicia has the best mojitos in town! Cool and refreshing! We started our meal with guacamole and chips. Gauc was yummy, but needed more to serve two hungry diners. I had the seafood paella which was the best I've ever tasted. This is Latin comfort food at the top level! My husband had the pork which he said was tender and full of flavor. We had no space left for dessert, so we WILL be returning! By the way, we were seated immediately on a Saturday evening around 6pm.

This place is beautiful and one of the best Indian restaurants I have ever gone to. I was in town for business and ordered the vegetable tikka masala to-go. It was late but they brought my food quickly and the concierge was super nice while I waited. If I am ever in town again I will be sure to visit.

King of Prussia, PA I didnt know how to rate. I called them and their buffet is closed for an event. Im on the lookout for new spots not explored yet. U never know some of these places no one really knows of...might have the most amazing food...and yet to be discovered. Im up for the adventure always. Will be back.

Went here for the first time on a busy evening. Atmosphere is cozy with mismatched chairs, medium lighting, and quiet background music. Wait staff were all very friendly, but service was far too slow, even for a busy night. Our water glasses were empty for most of the dinner, and our food took an unreasonably long time to come out. Our table ordered a pot of tea, but upon pouring, we were surprised and disappointed that the water in the teapot could barely fill two mugs. I ordered the masaman curry, which was only okay - cooked well, but not rich in flavor and had far too little rice relative to the size of the dish. The portions are also smaller than what you'd get at an average restaurant, which is perfectly fine if you're not ravenously hungry. All of this would have made for an okay dining experience, so I have only two complaints that knock my review down to 2 stars - the first was the very slow service. The second is that the smell and taste of our food was intermixed with the pungent smell of Windex. My tablemates and I noticed and identified the smell before we saw a wait staff member cleaning an adjacent table with the stuff. A few tables were cleaned throughout our meal, which filled the restaurant with cleaning solution smell each time. We bashfully did not mention this to the wait staff, so perhaps they would be receptive to fixing this problem in the future. Overall, I likely won't return. Pros are the nice atmosphere, nice wait staff, and BYOB. Cons are slow service, Windex smell, and slightly below average food.

Mariela speaks the truth. Don't go here expecting a real hookah lounge, it's a place where frat boys and girls come to hang out, drink, and smoke hookah. The selection of shisha that Aladdin's offer makes up for the shabby decor, the excessively loud torrented rap videos, and the rowdy crowd of drunken college students. This place is the only 21+ hookah lounge in town. So if you're young, a fan of loud music or sports, and also a fan of hookah, this is the place for you! If you're not.. Look elsewhere.

With a name like Pita Jungle, I expected to walk in to a lunch-type setting.....informal seating, lots of to-go orders, etc. Nay, this is a full-blown full bar hostess seating place! I went in to get something quick to go and quickly realized that while they do offer to-go meals, it's not their standard option so I think I threw the staff for a loop. I ordered the California (I think that was the name?) pita and it was LOADED with fresh veggies, although next time I'll probably skip the onion. It also came with a dill pickle spear and a few kalamata olives. The pita bread itself was perfect- fresh and delicious. The tatziki came on the side and I wished I'd had more. Things just got kind of.....dry after awhile. It was a lot of food for my money and I would probably go back, but I'd go for a sit-down meal.

Great food, not too far for a stop off the turnpike on our road trip. Had several pokestops near by along with a cool park nearby for exercise for the kids after a brunch. Great service good food would go there again.

Absolutely incredible. Started with drinks at the bar CL Mint Julep and a gin/tequila/cucumber drink that were beautiful and delicious. Moved to dining room and had cold corn/crawfish soup which was fantastic. Very knowledgeable waitress. Both the curried goat and fried catfish sandwich were top notch. Did I mention the biscuits and flavored butters? Yummy! Best food of the weekend so far!! And located in a trendy, industrial haunted hotel.
