Really cute place. Food was good but small portions for the price. Our server was a little busy but she did a good job. It's a very small place which is a double edged sword. I look forward to trying again at the patio area.

The only reason I go here is because the food is authentic and there is a good variety. Besides that, the location could not be worse, the interior is old and dated, the servers and the cooks yell between the dining area and the kitchen in Vietnamese very loudly. The last time I was there, I was on crutches and when I went up to ask for my leftovers to go, the server handed me the container and bag to box up my own leftovers. Would not recommend it if you are trying to impress anyone or anything....
My first time here and l loved it. Food is amazing, I had the Thai Spaghetti...it was so full of flavor and the staff is super nice...will be back and recommending to friends

I just had my first experience with Chaat and have to say that it was one of the most delightful things I've ever eaten! So many different flavors and fresh ingredients. If you have not tried it before, allow Hasaan, the owner, to choose for you. He will not steer you wrong! I recommend the Salad Chaat with lamb. Choose a level of spice and pair it with your favorite Lassi and you are set. If you have any room left, the sweet carrots or rice pudding are outstanding for dessert. I look forward to returning to this wonderful establishment the next time I am in Philly. If I lived here, you could definitely count me as a regular.

Siam Cafe is a fantastic find in South Nashville you should certainly add to your restaurant rotation. The place itself is small and comfortable. The dining area is tables and cushioned booths. The ambiance is not much but it's kept neat. The food though is absolutely top notch. They offer a wide selection, that includes well executed standards like Green Curry and (based on other reviews) Pad Thai along with some more adventurous options like a duck curry and various squid options both of which I'll be going back for. Various spice levels are at your disposal. I enjoy a good spicy dish so usually go medium at Thai places. Surprisingly I'd recommend hot here, if you enjoy heat. My dining partner will recommend the "native" spice level but I suspect her tolerance is a bit higher than most. This night my Curry was excellent flavorfully prepared and served with Jasmine rice the spices were fresh and the bamboo shoots were crisp. I'd recommend the steamed dumplings and spring rolls as well. The basil in the rolls was striking and opened up the senses to get you ready for the entrees. The alcohol list is limited to a tasty plum wine that had an excellent nose and was not overly sweet, various beers including the usual Asian selections and some sake. Service was friendly and unobtrusive which facilitated good conversation in the intimate booths. Don't let the location or slightly tight parking lot scare you off try Siam Cafe and bring your friends.

The food here is really good. But they are painstakingly slow. I mean, I once waited 45 minutes for a fish sandwich, when the estimated time was 10 min, and I was the only one waiting around. I did notice something though: the faithful patrons tend to do sneaky things. For example, they'll place an order and then walk over to Wawa. Or they order and then hang out in their cars. Or, the three people ahead of you actually order for the 55 members of their family reunion. Giving you the 'impression' that there's only 1-3 people ahead you when there's really 58. BUT, if you manage to fight the good fight and your patience wins, what you take home will likely be worth it. For me, the fish was perfectly seasoned, crunchy golden batter on the outside and flaky juiciness in the inside. Mac and cheese was good as well, creamy and cheesy the way it should be. I will say that not all my experiences have been like this. A few times the fish was bland, but still cooked well (hot sauce fixed the former issue right up). And a few times the cooks seemed intent on pissing each other off (the food always takes a hit in this case). But most of my experiences have been positive enough to make me come back again. Beware that they are cash-only. I understand it's a food truck, but it's university city and it's 2014. Gotta knock off a star for the cash-only situation and inconsistency. Otherwise, bring cash and lots of patience! Note to Owner: I have seriously driven to your location, found parking during the lunch rush (quite a feat on its own), only to remember that you are cash only. Subsequently drove home and made a PB&J in place of your fish platter. You are likely losing good business because of this. Get one of those swipey thingys that attach to cell phones...hell, something so I can get my fish platter! Please and thank you. Sincerely, Me
Great food...Great service! Must have the Singapore Rice Noodles or the General Tso's Chicken!!! The waiting staff is great there's always a great happy hour crowd.

Vegetarian deli meat?! Is there anywhere else in Idaho that serves this? There may only be one option, but it's not half bad and they're decent slices. Their baguette is nice and crusty but soft in the center, so it's not too dense or chewy. I don't think I'd use it just for cheese given those qualities, but it makes an awesome sandwich. The Thai boba tea wasn't my thing; too sweet. They probably made it right and I just don't like Thai Tea, but I found the milk tea much better. I think we confused the poor lady at the counter asking about the meat content of the spring rolls that were sitting there already made, so we dropped it and didn't end up trying any. Either way, the sandwich alone is enough to keep us coming back! *Update* + They will make up fresh spring rolls for you with only the veg meat and/or shrimp, so veg- and pesc-etarian rolls are an option. They come with a dark peanut sauce. + One earlier reviewer was unhappy with the Cajun shrimp sandwich's shrimp content; we tried one recently and it was pretty packed with shrimp. Improvement or inconsistency? I'm not sure.

This review is only for the service. No idea if the food is good or not yet because as I'm writing this review, the food has yet to arrive after being here for 1 hour and 15 minutes. The staff seems overwhelmed and keeps forgetting to bring out anything we asked for. And when I asked about the status of our order they just made excuses about being busy (even though the table that sat down at the same time as us is happily eating their dinner at the moment). Hope the food is gonna be worth the frustration and wait.
Summer roll is my favorite,good service ,my friends and my family love this restaurant

Tryst is a great spot to hang out and relax. We enjoyed the specialty drinks, and the cheese platter.....was a nice place to stop in and chill. Great looking bar, very modern and despite a crowd seems pretty quiet And relaxed. Bartenders were friendly, but not exactly Johnny on the spot when your empty..... Although we didn't order them, looks like the giant pile of seasoned fries is the golden ticket here.
I had lunch at Nadia's it was excellent. I had the Tofu eggplant dish, it was delicious. I will be back.
If only there were more stars to give!! AMAZING food, atmosphere and service! It was as if we were living back in Puerto Rico.

I'm rounding up. The Queen of Sheba stands in its own category as there are not many similar restaurants. The atmosphere is intimate yet not cramped. Service was friendly and fairly quick. Like many who visit here, we opted for the Queens 8 platter. @ $15 per person I was surprised at the small sample sizes. While it's a sampler platter I'd think it should constitute a dinner. If two people are sharing a sampler platter it would seem logical to provide portions that can be easily shared - not one small chicken drumstick and one hard boiled egg for two to share. Aside from the portion problem - the food is tasty. With the platter we were able to enjoy the very distinct flavors and spices. After reading others reviews, I would like to go back when the buffet is offered. The Queen of Sheba is definitely worth a visit -- if for nothing else than to get your culinary passport stamped.

The restaurant table was you could tell - cleaned but not well, crumbs, residue on table upon being seated. Booths are not comfy, older, worn, dated. Carpet/floors are old and dirty. Menus were tattered/worn on the edges like an old book and not very clean. Restaurant food is ok, tried the pad thai - waiter couldn't say whether it was a traditional pad thai or a modified version. Could've used more "sauce" and more noodles, but the veggies on it were great, it was cooked properly and seemed fresh. However it was supposed to be without meat and there was some unidentifiable shredded textured item throughout the dish, looked like shredded chicken but no idea if it was or wasn't meat, couldn't tell what it was. Service is just ok at best, almost no one in restaurant and still had to ask to get the check brought over. Asked for ice water with NO LEMON and brought ice waters WITH LEMON then instead of replacing the drink, he reached and took the lemon off the glass and set it on the table. Just...don't!!!! Restaurant really needs updating and cleaning pretty bad!
This place was great. The atmosphere was relaxing and very pretty. The staff was professional and was attentive. There was a lot of food and it was delicious! Definitely will be by again!
We went there for the first time since it was Tomitillos. Service was great. Great music. the Shrimp Ya-Ya was very yummy.

Food is ok, nothing great. The real reason this review is low is service. I've been here more than once during lunch and twice its taken over 45 minutes for some kind of food to make its way to the table.

Fantastic Thai food in the heart of Philadelphia. It's a small restaurant, so definitely make reservations if you're coming on a peak night. You can customize the protein and spice level in almost all of the menu items, so their food is definitely vegetarian friendly. I would recommend their soups, which are all packed with flavor (my favorite is tom yum), and their basil fried rice. Try "Thai-spicy" level is you really want a kick!

Found this place by accident - Nashville, do yourself a favor and get here. They do need to advertise and get the word out more, I expected the place to be packed. The food was excellent, almost too much to eat for reasonable prices. Good mojito. The decor is interesting if understated, and service was good if not great. There were a few lulls. All in all, a memorable experience and hoping they can get the word out and have some crowds!

Went for valentines day with the SO and it was a fantastic choice (go me haha!) Waiter/staff were incredibly polite and attentive Service was perfect, not too fast were we wouldnt get enough time talking with one another but it wasnt too fast where we would get bored and antsy. We had a table downstairs in a booth. Definitely not too loud, wasnt overcrowded (we went at around 6-7) Setting was very romantic :) Food: She got the lobster ravioli which was DELICIOUS, but it really wasnt filling and we thought about ordering something else like a salad but we didnt. I got the walnut encrusted salamon. Totally delightful. Very bright appearnce, perfect mix of crunch and savory but tangy. Really really good. Drinks: She got a chocolate martini (i think thats what it was) It was great! Packed a helluva punch. I got a Guiness. Regular run of the mill guinees. It was served nicely.

Went here for dinner recently, it was really great! We started with spring rolls and then had the shrimp pad thai. My only complaint was the pad thai was kind of a smaller portion. But it was really good. Also the service was excellent. So many BYOBs you are constantly rushed out the door. But not here. Will definitely return.

Went here based on reading other Yelpers' comments and I was not disappointed. I had the rare steak and beef ball Pho. It came with peppers, fresh Thai basil, and fresh, crispy bean sprouts. Flavor was excellent after I added some red chile paste. Everybody is right about the unfriendly service though. One word of advice. If you like to use a lot of red pepper, be careful not to let the noodles splash into the soup. I had a chile flake splash into my eye and I thought I was going to pass out. I had to rinse it out with water and then proceeded to sweat and cry from the one eye for the rest of the meal. Next time, I am bringing safety glasses!!!
Food is delicious but why is it so expensive! an 8.99 delivery charge when the chicken tikka masala is already 22 dollars! And why is that 22 dollars! It's delicious but...come on!
Great live music! Tasty and strong beverages!

My fiancé and I went to Sansom Kebab House for an early dinner. The restaurant was empty so the service was very good. We ordered the bolani appetizer which was much smaller than expected and slightly bland in taste. We ordered Mantoo and Sansom Kebab - the entrees were delicious and very filling.

Love this place only gave it four stars cuz sometimes if you get the wrong ppl at the drive through you could get half your order or missing sauces or something gotta be wrong. If the manager is there everything is awesome , food is great and I love the grilled shrimp it's spicy good :)
Simple, quick, healthy, tasty and fairly inexpensive. Enough said. Oh, and you need to try the orzo salad. Yum. It's Greek and there you go.

Sometimes I wonder how places that are totally up my alley, go totally under my radar even when I drive past them nearly every day. I love tea and Asian food and how did I never make it here? I think I helped write a weekly yelp about this place even! I digress, this is my new favorite place to go for lunch. Everything I've had has been great. Pho, Beef Salad, Chicken Curry, banh mi, so good! Everything is fresh and made to order. Service is really nice and prompt. At lunch, the pastries call my name, and they look awesome, I have not had one because I try to limit calories during lunch, but man I do want one... so bad. Please have one on my behalf. I have had the shave ice and boba tea. A lot of people have not had REAL shave ice, like Hawaii shave ice. NO NOT A SNOW CONE, it is different. Seasons has really awesome shave ice. Highly recommended. I even lost track of time once while eating it, put a lid on it to get back to work, and it was still ice even when I got back to my desk. Awesome. I love tea. You know it is a good tea place when the whole leaf tea is displayed in jars for you to sniff. Lychee, passion fruit, jasmine, green, all tasty. Jellies, bobas and exploding bobas are all really good. I also really like the the cups and assorted items for sale and the tree mural painted on the walls is really pretty. A very comfy spot. I recommend it!
I always order #7 Lunch. Rice noodle with sliced beef, chicken, shrimp and hot n sour soup and egg roll. Been coming for YEARS

I eat here once a week but that might increase once winter hits. Nothing's better then a warm bowl of Pho on a cold night. This place is authentic Vietnamese cuisine that's best in St Albert. I prefer the Pho or the Vermicelli bowl over their rice dishes. I still haven't had their salad rolls but the spring rolls have a nice crunch but leave a little to be desired. I usually don't have room after dinner but I really enjoy Vietnamese iced coffees and they do it exactly how I like it. I haven't seen any Nam-wiches on their menu and I wish there were cuz they are quite tasty and normally well priced.
I'm so glad this place is in Boise. The baguettes are so yummy (I like the BBQ pork) and the vermicelli noodle dish is fantastic. Great cheap place to eat.

Ate here for the first time and we loved it! We enjoyed our meal (chicken kabob & beef curry). It was amazing to try a different taste of culture! We definitely will come back! And the fact that they had a hookah section inside blew my mind! Never before seen!

They have a great selection of grocery items, all at low prices (tahini and rose water anyone?). The falafel is pretty good but just a tad on the bland side, which the hummus hides pretty well (at least in the sandwiches, which will only cost you about $3.50). The owner is very pleasant so plus 1 star for service. The place itself is small but you can rest assured that everything is freshly prepared. The baba is pretty good too. I will return to try the kabobs and gyros.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Amazing food with full flavor!! The curry +cut option on the menu is great for two to share or for one very hungry person. Definitely would come back here!!

Smiley's is truly a neighborhood gem. The food is absolutely amazing; I have never had falafel quite as delicious anywhere else in my life. Everything is always so fresh. I always get hummus, falafel and baklava! The walnut baklava is amazing, but if you can catch them on a day they are serving pistachio baklava, do not pass it up!! The service is absolutely outstanding. And the prices are unbeatable! The portion of delicious hummus and pita you receive for $4 could last you a few days!

(4) ~ very good overall food & service. NOTES: You order at the counter and they'll give you a Table# and bring the food to you. When you're done, they'll clear the table after you leave. They also do Take-Out too. OUR MENU: STARTERS ** Classic Hummus = (4.5) Very Good & Fresh! They also sell it in Tubs-to-Go! ENTREES: ** Steak Kabob w. Roasted Vegetables & Grilled Potato Salad = (4) very good * Steak Roll-ups = (3.5) good * Steak Stack Sandwich = (3.5) good * Veggie Pita Pizza = (3.25) pretty good...might try it w/o the cheese & spinach next time... * Greek Salad = (3) ok SIDES: ** Braised White Beans = (4.25) Very good...probably the best white beans I've had...really like the Rosemary notes;) ** Marinated Slaw = (4) very good * Pasta Salad = (3.5) good * Roasted Vegetables = (3.25) pretty good * Potato Salad = (3.25) pretty good * Rice Pilaf(side) = (3.25) pretty good, but a little salty. * Pita Chips = (3) ok...kinda stale DRINKS: ** Unsweetened Iced Tea = (4) very good * Limeade = (3.5) good DESSERT: ** Chocolate Chip Cookie = (4) very good..although it uses Margarine instead of Butter:( * Yaya's Chocolate Cake = (3.5) good...but not great...

Had the Lasagna last night with friends...WoW! It was excellent! A small and cozy but quaint restaurant on the river with a nice view. Prices were a little on the high side but, the meal was well worth it. Staff very friendly and accomodating....Caesar salad nothing to write home about but, not terrible either. Overall, the entree was very good and worthy of a return visit which will be sooner than later.

I've just moved to Broad Ripple and I've already been to this place 5 times. The staff is kind and helpful and the food never disappoints. My favorite: Tacos de Pastor - a great sweet but savory flavor. Just the right amount of tortilla to taco ratio. The pineapple pico de gallo is also AMAZING!!

Think the Chipotle of Middle Eastern food: stuffed pitas rather than burritos, hummus bowls as well as rice and cous cous bowls, instead of beans and rice. In general, everything is fresh (and unlike Chipotle-free of salmonella) and mixed to order. The meats are well seasoned if not a bit too well done and falafels are an option for the vegans/vegetarians. All the salads used to top pitas and bowls are crunchy and flavorful. And the selection of sauces/condiments that you can top off your custom concoction are tasty. And a special mention for the hummus and the pita bread; the hummus is creamy, smooth and I'd gladly eat it with the pita bread as a great Middle Eastern breakfast. Although, the pita must be made using yeast-no pita could be so fluffy without resorting to yeast. Is it authentic? It's not compared to all the Middle Eastern food I've had in my travels. But it is a great fast food option. And while their fries are definitely not traditional Middle Eastern fare, these homemade potato chip-like fries were delicious. If you get them to go, they become ice cold within minutes. If you'd like something a bit more authentic, but really no more expensive or less convenient, head to Kabob Cafe in Gateway Shopping Plaza. In my opinion the food will be more authentic and somewhat better.

I really don't know why I waited so long to try this place. I really love Thai food and I normally go to Pattaya (which is also very tasty.) My friends recently went there during University City Dining days and had a great experience so I was looking forward to trying it, too. My opportunity came when my friend wanted to "go out" to celebrate her completion of the bar exam that day. At first I thought she meant "go out" like to a crowded bar somewhere downtown but when her husband explained that we were going to Vientiane Cafe I was more than happy to tag along. I think one of the reasons I had never gone there was that it doesn't look like anything special from the outside, so I was surprised to see just how large it was inside when we got there. The ambiance was nice. I felt like we could be ourselves, talking about the "bag lady" at the bar, and be boisterous without being awkward. But it was still quiet enough to enjoy a more relaxing meal. We had a group of 7 of us and they easily and quickly accommodated us. Between the seven of us I think we all ordered either the Panang Curry or the Pad Thai. Both were delicious but the panang curry was truly something special. I really don't know how they made it so good but it was SO good. It makes me mouth water just thinking about it now. One thing I will say, though, is that the spice levels really don't matter at all. The have a scale of 1 to 5 with 5 being the spiciest. I got a 4 and most of the others got 2, however they all tasted the same, which was not so spicy. Normally I would have been really upset that it wasn't very spicy but the flavor was so good I didn't even care. On the downside, prices were pretty high and the service was only so-so. Also, they are cash only which I find really weird and inconvenient. With that said, the deliciousness will definitely draw me back again!

Instead of using hot sauce, this place uses chopped red chili peppers. I know this because upon ordering my asparagus dish - hold the tofu please - "Thai" spicy, and having read Yelp reviews asserting that the spice level wasn't to par - I kindly asked for a side of hot sauce. Presented in front of me was a plate of chopped stir-fried asparagus without oil oozing and slopping around my plate. The perfectly formed, succulently sweet sticky rice retained its form all the way to the bottom. And an aura of chili enveloped the table. Next to my plate of perfectly spicy, sweat-inducing food was laid a tiny bowl of chopped chili peppers. Chili peppers. Not sauce. Chili peppers. Win.

Sometimes you have to dress up to go for a Sunday work out then skip it, think about getting burgers but then drive like 30min out of the way to go and eat at a place where Kebabs remind you of home and you drool over the food 6 hours later. Yes, thats what Shishkabob house did for us. It was like eating at home just paying for it. The food is homecooked by owners and their son is at the front desk. We had chicken and goat kebabs, while goat wasn't as tender as i am use to but it was delicious. Chicken was just out of this world so juicy, succulent, just amazing. The best part was the salad, grilled veggies and humus was as amazing as the main entree. A lot entrees have a bunch of sides as "sides", not here. As we were walking out and about to pay, we saw one of the owners bring in 5 pieces of dessert just out of oven. They told me its "Katayef", made with walnuts. I am not a fan of dessert but i ate 2 while they were swiping my card. It was the best thing ever. If you ever crave mediterranean food, please make the extra hike and go here. Check for 2 would be around $30 max. Thanks for making our Sunday a memorable one.

Just had a very pleasant late lunch at Momo's. The staff was very friendly and prompt to refill drinks and take our orders. At the table we started with the goat cheese dip (yum!) followed by the falafel and a lamb gyro. The falafel was flavorful and crisp and my husband had no complaints about his gyro. Will go back again!

I gotta say, I wasn't terribly impressed. I had the BBQ Pork sandwich. It was good, but not great. The sandwich felt very dry for the most part, which isn't how I typically like my sandwiches. People have raved about their bread. For Boise, it was great. For New York or Philadelphia, it's below average. The pork imparted an underwhelming amount of flavor to the sandwich. For the price, it's a good meal. I have to imagine, however, that there are better sandwiches in Boise. Keep in mind that 3 stars is "A-OK". I liked it, and I understand why it's rated highly. I just can't say anything will bring me back.

Visiting from out-of-town and this was recommended by our Airbnb host. We walked into an empty restaurant with a party of six and they said the larger tables were reserved and did not offer to combine two small tables, instead asking us to sit separately at two tables, which we did. That was the beginning of terrible service for the rest of out experience. Water glasses were not refilled. They gave us tiny plates to share the main courses. Etc etc. The food was only OK. We ordered Sambosa and they were soggy and only a bit above room temp. The rice that came with the Kabobs was delicious but the lamb was overcooked. They then added a 20% gratuity automatically to our bill. We will not go back and would not recommend this place unless they work on the service experience.
The pho is always delicious and it's always great on a cold winters day. The new locations offers the same great tastes as expected from the other two restaurants. Beef satay is my favourite.
Good lunch buffet. Large selection. The bread is tasty. Decent price.

Phamous Cafe has the best pho in the Santa Barbara and Goleta area. The broth is extremely flavorful and it has the perfect amount of noodles. My favorite dishes are the rice dishes, which come with a small bowl of pho, which is delicious to pour over the rice to give it that amazing flavor. The meat in the rice and vermicelli dishes is seasoned nicely and is great with a little siracha. In terms of appetizers, the egg rolls are absolutely delicious. Definitely would recommend getting some. The workers are all super friendly! Any one of them will help you out; they seem to be very cohesive group.

Food took 35 mins and place was dead. Then from the time the first plate out of 8 came to the table to the time the last one came it was about 20 mins. Unfortunately everywhere else had a long wait and we were in a rush... Lesson learned.

I picked Bangkokville for a family birthday lunch and couldn't have picked a better place! From the moment we arrived, the staff was super-nice and attentive without being overbearing. Everything we ordered was outstanding (we had to share with each other), prices reasonable, and portions big enough to have leftovers. We LOVED the fresh spring rolls, especially the sauce. We also had crab Rangoon, cashew chicken, orange chicken, red curry, and massaman curry. Since it was my birthday, staff brought me a complimentary coconut rice/mango dessert (complete with candle) and told me Happy Birthday! We were also impressed that the owner came out to check on us. We told all the staff how much we loved it! Most of my family drove from 70 miles away and will be back despite the distance. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!! I have nothing negative to say, other than the fact it's hard to get out of the parking lot back onto Nolensville Road. Can't wait to go again!

I have mixed opinions on Wishbone - I've been here quite a few times since it's close to campus. The food - The chicken itself is pretty good. I wouldn't say it's the best fried chicken I've ever had, but it's good. The sauces are the better part - there are 5 or 6 of them ranging from BBQ to Pesto to Thai peanut. I also tried the mac & cheese which I definitely recommend, it has bacon and other things mixed in it. Some things annoy me here though. For example, they advertise their homemade pies in the store, but then you can't actually buy them unless you get a combo meal. They also would not give me a glass of water which is really just unnecessary - it seems like they even have cups for water but they just won't give it to you! This sort of thing just makes me feel like they're trying to earn that extra one or two bucks from me, which doesn't make me feel good about coming back.

This place isn't bad but there's a few other options in the area that are superior. I think it tastes like they water down their curries or just don't add the same amount of spices that other Indian restaurants use. Maybe catering to what they think the American palate likes?? Inside is very nice and service was good, but for flavor I'd go elsewhere.

The ambiance is very modern and fun. The service is always incredible, especially at the bar. They have a very unique and tasty cocktail menu, and most importantly the food is the best in broadripple hands down. (order the fish tacos and don't skip dessert!) I would go there again and again!!

Great place with tons of different foods. Like salems but a lot better! Gyros, salads, wraps, hoagie, seafood, wings, and more. Great deal on wings now. Definitely worth giving a try. I know I will be going back.

I'm writing this review after my 3rd lunch visit here. I admit part of the reason for the delay is because the first 2 times, I chose the wrong entree. Don't get me wrong the Bahn Mi are good, but the PHO is way more impressive. The one constant I've had each time is an order of the spring rolls. They have a very "fresh" taste. I think it's due to the cilantro. They also serve them with an awesome dipping sauce with peanuts in it. Back to the PHO. It's definitely a must. You should also try a Bubble Tea!

This unique restaurant describes itself as New American and Southern cuisine with a Middle Eastern influence. The mezzes or sides are only $5 each or 5 for $20. We opted for the fried avocado sandwich and five sides. They were all unique and very tasty, but my favorite was the whipped feta with fermented honey and pita bread. Dessert was a moist cake, Buttermilk tres leche with Louisiana strawberries, and espresso coffee. The service was prompt and cordial, and our waitress was very helpful in explaining the myriad of side dishes. The food comes out as it is prepared and was paced perfectly. We had a long, leisurely lunch, but never felt hurried to eat and go. This would have been a five star review except for the almost total lack of parking. Your check comes to the table in a book. No rhyme or reason, but a nice touch. When I can get up the nerve to tackle the parking dilemma again, I will certainly return. They have another location in Charleston, SC, and both restaurants use fresh ingredients and buy from small, local suppliers, not giant conglomerates. Everything is fresh, well prepared, and beautifully presented.

Of all of the things I find frustrating about dining out, number one on my list is bringing the entrees while the appetizer is still on the table. This is a mistake on the part on the part of the kitchen and the server. How hard is it to coordinate things? It usually happens in restaurants that are half full and the kitchen has time on its hands. Rather than waiting for the appetizer plates to be cleared, the kitchen occupies itself by making the entree and sending it out. The diner has three choices, to accept the dish and have the table jammed with dishes, have the half-finished appetizer plates cleared, or send the entrees back to the kitchen only to sit out until the server comes back to pick it up and serve it. We were less than half done with the appetizers when we were confronted with the choice at Zorba's and elected to send the entrees back. If restaurants and servers only realized how irritating this is for some diners. Of course you can lower the tip to convey the message to the server and send back the tried out food to the kitchen where the chef may notice it. In this case the owner did and brought us out a complimentary dessert. Notice to chefs and owners ... a free dessert does NOT make up for a crappy meal! Try waiting until the appetizer plates are cleared before sending out the entree. It's not hard to do, just be a professional and notice what's going on. Don't worry about fixing things for me. I won't be back. .

Great little place to feed your Indian food craving. Buffet was not so spicy and that translates to my kids loving it too. Menu items came out fast and over all the place was clean, well kept and the staff was friendly!

This place is delicious. I go here often for the Thai Green Tea even if I don't order any food. So refreshing. My favorite dish is the vegetables with garlic sauce. Staff is always so nice and welcoming!

Great Place for outdoor Live Music (Band was great), Mojito was very good, and service was great. Unfortunately, Food was very bad. This is not by any stretch Cuban food. The Cuban sandwich was not hot, and bread was old & crusty. Fries were cold, and Black Beans w/rice side was not Cuban at all. Bottomline, until they get someone who can cook in the kitchen - come here for drinks only and you will enjoy.
Best Thai food around. Everything was great! Especially love the Basil rice! Wonderful for dine-in or take-out.

My wife and I were in a group of eight people. The humus was great, but the back of the house did not ensure that all of us got our meals at the same time. Butcher & Bee was not busy at the time and we got our meal 5 minutes after everyone got theres. The "bearded iris" IPA I ordered was the best I have ever tasted. I'm not sure if it was called the "bearded iris" though. My wife called Butcher & Bee later in the day and they told us that they were to busy to look into the exact name of the IPA. Great food though!

I will admit that Dmitri's is very good, but I don't get the cult-like following this place seems to have. The fish preparations are very basic, which allows the full flavor of the fish to shine through. You're not going to get a macadamia nut encrusted trout or anything exotic. Just plain broiled or grilled fish. All the entrees come served with escarole and rice. I really don't have much to say about this place. It's a nice BYO, but it's boring. The menu isn't that exciting, but if you're in the mood for just a piece of fish, then I would suggest this place.
Good food but prices and serving size way less. They should also work on customer service.

My absolute favorite Chinese food around. I've been eating here for years and love the variety they offer since they also offer Thai and hibachi food. The food is always cooked to perfection and the flavor is spot on. The portions are very large and I always have more food than I can eat. The staff is very friendly and the food always come out quickly when dining in. The restaurant is spotless and the restroom is also very clean. When I order takeout I always get everything I ordered and the food is always hot and delicious.

I was craving Indian food and this place was nearby. I was pleasantly surprised to find they offered a dinner buffet (Friday-Sunday I think). Most Indian places only offer a buffet at lunch. The staff was very friendly and made sure my glass was never empty and continually checked to see if I needed anything. I liked that they had more than just the usual popular options in the buffet. Sometimes Indian buffets get a little boring and generally only offer the popular dishes like tikka masala, butter chicken, etc. They had both of those options but many other "off the beaten path" options as well so I was able to try some new things that I would never think of ordering. If it's your first time having Indian food, I'd personally recommend that you go with someone that has been here before because there isn't much direction or "handholding" from the staff. For example if you want something that's not at the buffet (naan, etc) you have to know to ask for it.
Excellent! Awesome food, and the owner is great. Hassan said that he's going to start serving dosas next week. Looking forward to it.

Really creative fusion of SE Asian and southern cuisine. We had a few highly discerning foodies with us and everyone left happy and full. Favorites included the smoked mushrooms, the wet batter chicken, sweet potatoes, and pork shoulder. It's a very casual spot (think paper towels, jam jars for glasses, etc.). Looking forward to getting back and trying additional items on the menu.

Lunch buffet had a wide range of vegetable and meat dishes in chafing trays. Good flavor with some tending on the more ordinary and others flavorful. Nothing wowed me nor was anything a true turn-off. Maybe ordering off the menu may prove more enticing. Doesn't compare to Ethiopian in say the Adams Morgan area in DC, but then this isn't DC.

Francisco's on the River has a great location for a restaurant. It's all by itself, right on the Delaware river, and has great views during the day throughout the seasons. I wish the décor inside had more of an effort behind it. I realize that décor does not mean much if the food is amazing, but I was hoping for a rustic style, or maybe even a cottage-chic look for this place. It would make the dining experience that much better if it looked a bit prettier in here. Also, carpet in a restaurant is just always a no-go for me :( The food though, is very nice! Simple Mediterranean cuisine, my roasted beet and goat cheese salad with a lemon vinaigrette was crisp and the candied walnuts were a great touch. It's a simple salad, I get it all the time because I'm obsessed with beets, but you can mess it up, and this place did not. For dinner, I went with the filet pasta con gorgonzola. Filet mignon, fettuccine in a cream sauce, and gorgonzola cheese? How can you go wrong with that creamy delicious concoction!! You can't. I asked that the filet be medium rare, and it was definitely more medium than medium rare, but even with the minor mishap, still a very flavorful dish. Very good meal overall
Visiting from Brooklyn and couldn't have been happier with eating at chaat and chai. The murals and decorations themselves are worth the visit but the food by far is the highlight. Simply amazing!

This is absolutely the best restaurant in the area. My fiancé and I regularly make a Saturday night out of going to dinner so we are always looking for cozy places to post up. When you walk into zeppoli, you are transported to what seems like a dining room in an old Italian house on the biggest holiday of the year. You open the door and it is literally bustling. At first glance it may seem a bit overwhelming with all of the noise, but rest assured, when you sit down at your cozy little table and have your first glass of wine you will adjust quickly! The restaurant is byob so bring a bottle (or two.) The waitstaff rotates and you will never be assigned one particular person as they typically all work the room together. The staff is incredibly friendly and warm. Expect to be seated right away, but relax and unwind as you may not get immediate service. This is NOT an "in and out" experience. Come and plan to dine and stick around for a few hours. They will pour you water and open your wine while you absorb the menu. The menu is small and the courses are simple and fresh, but they never change. This is one of the best things about this place, they have literally mastered every item on their menu and they do it right again and again and again. The consistency in this place is unmatched. I have been coming here for at least 4-5 years and the meals are exactly the same every time. After you order, they bring bread and olives to your table. Usually, you will receive 3 types of bread which are all delicious. Use it to soak up the oil from the olives and enjoy. Do yourself a favor and order the antipasto and you'll get something for everyone as there are probably 13 different bite sized samples of heaven on this plate. The gnocchi-I can't even describe. You won't be able to either. This is like no other gnocchi you have ever had. And a word to the wise, try to keep the plate from them and use your bread to soak up the amazing sage brown butter that is left-unless you already licked the plate clean, because you will want to. Trust me! Everything here is great. The shrimp, pasta options and every entree. The portions of meat and fish are huge, the saffron sauce on he seafood stew is out of this world, the whole Branzino is flaky and buttery. There are no shortcuts here. Again, the food is simple. You can really taste the flavors of every item and enjoy for what they are without the flavors being masked with heavy salts or sauces. Desserts, of course, are wonderful. Order the zeppolis and a coffee and savor the little donut-like soft pillows covered in crunchy sugar! Or any other dessert which will also parallel the deliciousness, I'm sure. The way you get lost in the atmosphere of this place, you can easily sit here and dine for hours. You will leave wanting to go to Italy. And a quick heads up. Take a minute and watch the staff and the kitchen. These people hustle and never stop. The way they work together is something to behold. A true team! It's pretty neat. Cheers and enjoy!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I absolutely love this place! I loved in India for two years and this place brings me back every time. Such a great staff also, very corky but nice. Great food and authentic. Love it. I go to this restaurant more than anywhere else!!
The staff was extremely friendly and the food was amazing! Very family friendly too! I got the falafel and I highly recommend it!

I went to Fez Morrocan about 9 years ago on a trip to Philly. I had seen it in a travel book as good for groups and organized a group from the conference I was at to go there. We took a taxi to the restaurant and were really impressed by the neigborhood. From what I could tell it was what you might call Bohemian and definitely cool for a guy who has lived in Texas his whole life. Entering the restaurant is like entering a tent in Morroco, they have material on the walls and ceiling. We were seated on pillows on the floor around a large table. The waiter came and explained how the restaurant worked and gave us water to wash our hands (you eat with your hands). He then brought out mint tea which was amazing (I'm not a tea drinker). The dishes came out one by one and I remember everyone being timid at first to use their hands and to try the sometimes strange foods (our waiter explained each dish as it was presented). By the end, when each dish came out, we all grabbed at it, not wanting to let someone else eat our portion of the wonderful food. A specific dish I remember was a pastry covered scrambled egg dish with cinnamon and other spices. As explained, it sounded suspect and one of our group had to be the guinea pig and try it first. On his approval, we all dug in and it was VERY ho, but SOOOO good that we all burned our fingers pulling out the next bits to stuff into our mouths. I see members of this group on occaision and we all remember our meal here even nine years later. We've tried to recreate it by going to other Morrocan places, but this was definitely a moment in time not to be re-lived. We were all so impressed by the city that we walked (quite a good distance) back to the hotel. I guess this review is mostly for Fez Morrocan, but also for the night to remember...

I have wanted to try this cart for AGES and he did not disappoint. The wait was really no longer than any of the other food carts, and the food quality was KILLER. Perfectly grilled chicken, saffron rice with chickpeas and spices, wonderful falafel, amazing hummus (I'm very picky about hummus), and WATERCRESS (mmmmspicygreens). Honestly, split it with a friend. It'll be PLENTY. I couldn't finish the rice, there was so much of the rest. $10 well spent. I will be back.

Yesterday me and my partner went this place to try their food, and we do the Togo order. Being an Asian I did not feel the Asian way of hospitality, the one who took my order sounds not like happy what her job is. Food are alright not that great. I hate giving a bad review but this is my experience.

Well worth the wait for an ever-changing selection of grains/pastas, flavorful hummus sauces, and pieces of fruit, over which he places a generous portion of marinated char-grilled chicken and four garlicky falafels. He then ladles a spicy sauce over the hefty meal and crowns it with a handful of fresh leafy greens. All the flavors and textures are balanced perfectly. High-protein, low-carb, healthy, and satisfying. It is the best lunch in town!

Good The service was friendly The food was fresh Food came out quick I appreciate that they wrapped up the bowl in saran wrap to prevent leakage on my ride home. Nice to see that they have indoor and outdoor seating Bad Way too expensive for a truck. I was disappointed. The portion sizes were too small
Best Indian food in Tucson. The price you can't beat the value you get. The service is very friendly

First timer here and came here for the experience of trying Ethiopian food for the first time. Came with a groupon and Service was good! Servers explained everything and walked us through what we were having as the dishes were served. (This was on a busy Friday night too!) I feel like the people who work here genuinely want to share their culture. I even overheard a server trying to teach a family some Ethiopian phrases. Family friendly. You can sit on a standard table or a more traditional Ethiopian setting. We had the appetizer sampler and the 8 dish Queen of Sheba plate both of which allowed us to try a variety of food. I'd recommend this for a first timer. The 8 dish shared plate is $15 per person. For two people who got the 8 dish shared plate, an appetizer, and 2 Ethiopian honey teas, our bill was $50. Overall, I had a great time just trying something new!

As far as Carmel Indian food, this is the best! Hey quick, very good, and great portions. Let's be honest, I only order naan and chicken tikka Marsala...so my suggestions beyond that are limited. I like my food spicy and go 10/10 & they take the cake. Some other places, I'll still need to add sriracha to get it spicy enough. Also helps to order over yelp and pickup within 5-10mins.

The banh mi at Pho Bistro was huge and stuffed with grilled meat of your choice, cucumber, jalapeno, carrot, mayo, onion, tomato, and cilantro. At under $4 each, it makes a great meal for hungry students. The grilled pork and beef had a sweet robust marinade and were more flavorful than the other Vietnamese places in town. The downside was that the grilled meat had too much char. A little char and smoke is great for flavor, but in this instance, there were several pieces of meat that I had to pick out because I didn't want to put that much polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in my body. The cha gio was generously sized, but the filling had an unappetizing sour note. I don't know if they purposely seasoned it that way or was it because the filling wasn't fresh. The nouc mam was nicely concocted, not too watery, with a good balance of salty and sweet.

This was the worst food I'd ever eaten in my life. It was like eating slop. The only thing good was the naan bread. The service was good and prices were way to high for such poor quality food. I started feeling sick before we got home. I was in and out of bathroom all night with pain and digestive tract issues. Missed work the next day, and did not feel better until two days later. I believe I had gotten food poisoning from the food at India palace. Because of that, I will not only never eat at India palace again, but I will never eat Indian food again. If I wanted to eat slop, I'd go to a dumpster at a good restaurant and eat out of it. It wouldn't cost me what eating at India palace cost me. Losing a days wages and spending the night miserable in the bathroom made this meal the worst meal of my life. My poor fiance felt so bad that he had taken me to a place that poisoned me and he had paid for it. Never eat at India palace, save yourself.

From the day I've come to Nashville, I've heard Thai Phooket this, Smiling Elephant that. Those are both okay destinations, I suppose. However, it is evident to me that neither of these constitutes Nashville's best Thai option. Thus far, I have to hand that trophy to Siam Cafe, whose rich flavors and quality ingredients have come the closest to reminding me of what I can get back in my native CA. One product that I've had a tought time finding in Nashville is a really good flat noodle. However, Siam's Pad Kee Mao indicates that at least one place knows how to make them right. Furthermore, I was really impressed with this place's intuition on spice level. I wanted something medium-highish and this place knew right where to go. Perhaps the most special thing, though, was their squid. I loves me some fresh squid, and it was one of those rare times in Nashville where it didn't taste like it had been frozen for three months after having washed up on shore after Deepwater Horizon. Room for improvement? The service was unattentive...waiting for water when you're burning up on Thai chilis isn't the most pleasant experience. Also, the onions were cooked a bit sloppily...I was getting occasional whiffs of undercooked onion which I personally don't enjoy. Above all, though, Siam Cafe is my new go-to spot for Thai in Nashville until someone can demonstrate that there is a better option.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: this cute little jem we have in Flourtown. This place is perfect! the Sushi is great and they have amazing food never once rejected anything from here. Right down the street from me too and i wouldn't go anywhere else.

Superb! What a great surprise: a lovely authentic restaurant with delicious variety and great service. We were very impressed with everything we ordered. Bread, appetizers: we couldn't believe how great it was. The staff was gracious and made good suggestions. At the end of the meal they brought a delicious dessert. We will be back for sure!

First time eating from here, I ordered through ubereats. All I ordered was 8 wings , Mac & cheese , & a sauce for my wings. My total including uber fee and tax was $21.84. The food got to me in less than 35 minutes which I really appreciate however I only received 7 wings.. On top of that it had no fork in the bag for my Mac & cheese and no napkins ! This place is a little to pricey to be acting so cheap, I will not be back.

One of my favorite places in the area. The food is quite good, and I would highly recommend the falafel pita. However the best part of this place is the nice couple that owns it. They always seem genuinely happy to see customers. If you're in the mood for a gyro, pita, etc. you should definitely stop in.

Off the beaten Nashville path is the Restaurant "Salsa". At first impression it would appear that I stumbled upon a dud of a eatery. The decor is seemingly minimalistic and the white walls provoke the thought that the establishment is either new OR unpopular. This however, couldn't be further from the truth. Little did I know that the restaurant plays one aspect of your experience against the other. The minimal walls are clashed with the vibrant and colorful food that tastes as good as it look. The menu spans two sides of a 12x24" page ranging from simple Puerto Rican and Latin food to more expensive and exotic foods. Rest assured, everything is good. The server was very helpful and very knowledgeable about their menu. Food came at an good pace and never let us waiting anywhere near other restaurants. now for the best part: Dessert. The dessert sampler was delicious and gave diners the taste of each of their dessert options. The Coconut Flan was perfect. The texture went nicely with the whipped cream topping and caramel sauce that was drizzled over it. Usually I am not a fan of Flan but this has changed my mind. The Tres Leches Cake was cool, refreshing and moist as ever. I would definitely order it again given the chance. Not only was it great by itself, it paired nicely with the Coconut Flan. The trembleque was intriguing and above all... delicious. At first taste I was not sure how to feel about the dessert. The consistency was a mixture of firm but still had a consistency that would compare it to spreadable cheese. As for the taste, it didn't seem like there was much to this delicious dessert. If you love coconut, you will love this. It's not too sweet and no too tame. It was the perfect mixture of the two. Again as with the other two desserts, each one paired great together as well as played against one another. I cannot wait to come back again and try more from their creative and delicious sounding menu.

I busted my car's tire driving into the Olio parking lot (BE careful if you park in their lot)! I was super bummed/annoyed and really embarrassed about it. But the employees of Olio literally made my day! They came out to check on me right after the incident; they offered to call AAA and later the chef came out and offered me something to drink. I was so distraught by the tire situation so I wasnt really paying any attention to them- but I really appreciated how considerate they were. My family and I decided to still go in for lunch while we waited for roadside assistance. The staff was wonderfully helpful and super sweet! We had so many questions about the various ingredients and they were really quick to help us with everything we needed. The service was phenomenal! The food was great! I really enjoyed the toasted sandwiches and their soup of the day. One thing I didn't realize before was: their food menu is limited and consists of mostly small plates. This was GREAT for me and my family because we enjoy sampling a little bit of everything. But if you are someone who is more into large portions- you might want to check out Elia (their adjacent restaurant). Overall, I loved my experience here and definitely want to come back for brunch. I'm also SO appreciative of their amazing staff; the staff just radiates kindness and compassion and for that reason alone, this place is worth your while!

In a nutshell, the food is very good. I've had better spring rolls, but these hold up really well against others. We enjoyed lunch there today, my husband had a ban mi sandwich and I had a vermicelli bowl. Once again the food was great. The service is awful. Staff wouldn't make eye contact with us when we entered and we didn't know if it was seat yourself or wait...we seated ourselves. Then we waited for about 11 minutes for the server who simply dropped off menus, no speaking to us. 6 minutes later she comes back and speaks to me, but not my husband. It was odd and just rude. They were not busy, not even half the tables were occupied. No refills on our drinks and no return service after our food was delivered and we traded plates, because they just put food down in front of us. We didn't know if we should wait for a ticket or walk up and so we waited for a server to appear and we eventually just walked up to a display case. The woman who checked us out, didn't care how the meal turned out for us...she just wanted the table number. ***If VN Pho & Deli is closed, I'm stuck on that side of town, and I'm starving for Vietnamese food; I'll go back. The food was very good.
Loved the food and Ambiance! It was definitely worth going to. Many vegan options as well!

This is my go to take out when I don't feel like cooking and get a craving for Vietnamese. It doesn't feel too heavy and tastes great. You definitely get your money's worth. Dinner for less than $10?! I always get the Lemongrass Tofu vermicelli bowl (vegetarian) and the avocado rolls are delicious!!!
The service is completely horrible. Waitstaff seem uninterested in providing any service. Multiple tables continue to need busing.

When I couchsurf in Indy, I make it to cajole and beg my hosts to cater to my culturally deprived palate. The dearth of spice and subtlety in Muncie is characteristically appalling. That said, my dining buddies and I grew weary of Shalimar and their predictability. Amber offered us, for my money, a superb lunch buffet. $7.99 is a tick high, but the vast expanse of their steam table more than made up for the price. I'm a glutton, hands down, but I frequent buffets not for the sheer volume one can stuff down his craw, but for the breadth of flavor combinations. Amber has more options than any other buffet I've seen in greater-Indy. All the standards were up to and above my expectations. Veggie options seemed substantial (dal, sag paneer, aloo chat, veg korma, et al) and chicken and lamb entrees were aplenty as well. Samosas were conspicuously absent, but the pakoras and aloo tiki were solid. While it seems some competitors deep fry their naan and throw it willynilly on the steam table, Amber serves their naan - plain or garlic - fresh to your table. I've seen piping hot naan come right out the oven from Paki cab stands, and Amber's is just as good. This little touch goes a long way to please. The deserts were all tasty (I never eat that mango pudding), especially the gulab. I make a better carrot halwa, but I was pleasantly surprised. Based on plaques by the register, the owner/operators are Punjabi. If ordering off the menu, consider Punjab specialties. All in all, this was a great find. I hope they don't succumb to pressure to bastardize their recipes for Carmel's dumbass tastes.

Just met a few girlfriends here for lunch! I have seen this place for years and have heard great things but I've never actually made it in. Well today was the day, and life is now a little bit brighter. There was 5 of us, and with the lunch specials we ordered it was 54$, so around 11$ each! The lunch special included soup, a small appetizer, and an entree. The entree was a large portion and it was absolutely delicious. Everyone was super happy with their meal. I wish I took a picture but I was too excited and forgot lol. I had the ravioli soup, crispy wontons, and Yakitori noodles with shrimp. We were all too full for dessert. The waitress was very friendly and helped me decide which entree to get. The ladies in my group had meals which included; Pad Thai, drunken noodles, chicken teriyaki, and a special fried rice. Every single one of us throughly enjoyed our meals! I'll for sure be returning and trying lunch takeout!

I stopped in here for the first time a few nights ago after listening to my friend rave about it so much, and had an amazing experience! If it's your first time, say so. The owner is great and if he knows you're unfamiliar with chaat he'll give you the low down. Great customer service from this guy. I had him decide what to give me and he threw together something he called "Crazy" chaat. Awesome. It's got pretty much everything in it. And it was exactly how he described it, no bite ever tasted the same. I cannot recommend this place enough, especially if you've never tried chaat. This is definitely the place to have your first taste.

The food was delicious! My husband and I just discovered this restaurant, thanks to yelp. We ordered a variety of things to try and everything was amazing! Everything was perfectly seasoned. We found our new favorite spot. We ordered the Stella Maris special (appetizer), #9 beef shawarma and the chicken kabob.

Wow. Easily my favorite restaurant! Authentic! Literally everything on the menu is delicious. It's like they've got some kind of Thai savant chef in the kitchen that they just pulled off the streets of Bangkok from their street food stand. They don't have to-go menus and that doesn't bother me, I just took photos of the menu. This is one of those places that when you discover it you feel like you have a big secret, like a secret club of Thai food that's cheaper, with larger portions, and the authentic flavor that the Thai restaurants in either direction can't hold a flame to. I'm worried that this review might have an adverse impact on the place. Maybe it will go to their heads or make them too busy to keep up the amazement. Change nothing! Once I was waiting there for a few minutes while they prepared my food. The lady said "sorry about your wait." I thought to myself, oh please, I'd gladly wait longer and pay more. I just knew the chef back there was making it with the utmost freshness and authenticity! I'm calling it the best Thai restaurant. You know it's good and authentic when there's fish sauce at the table in the spice tray. Ps, I'm pescetarian, so the meat may change my opinion (if I ate that stuff)

Food is O.K. but nothing special. It is not bad by any means, just forgettable. However it is the service and the unknowledgeable, slightly rude staff that earns this place a poor to average rating. Been here 4 times and there was issues 3 times with the bill or the order. It is too bad because it is nice inside and a great atmosphere.

I so wish they are closer to NJ! Finally made my pit stop on the way down south. They serve Chinese style Indonesian food, especially the noodle dishes. Got the Mie Komplit #1 and pretty darn close to what I used to eat in Indo (Mie Kriting style to my fellow Indonesians). The Pecel Lele was also good... Especially with the fried Sator and sambel. Ayam bakar is a bit over seasoned for my taste so next time I'll just get the Ayam goreng seems like everyone ordered that. Service is fast but not as 'ramah' (friendly) as I was expecting. Good luck finding parking.
It took 2.5 hours for all of our food to come out, and my friend found a BULLET in her meal. Do I need to say anything else?
Great little place. We had the tostadas and the island jerk sandwich. Both were amazing. The pineapple mango sauce is so good. Definitely recommend this place!

I love this place , the food is very fresh and tasty, very good atmosphere and nice background music. I get a change to eat here at least once a month , I love the Salmon it comes with a Greek salad and baked potatoes. Price is reasonable very recommended.

Come here!!! This is delicious. I got the hibiscus tea, pad thai, and the sticky rice with mango. All of it was so good. The pad thai took a while to cook, but it was worth it. My mom also got the coconut custard for dessert, which was amazing. I highly recommend trying everything on the dessert menu. The building is tiny, so come before the dinner rush. I also suggest not going in large groups, it will take a long time to get seated. This is better for 2-4 people. Whenever my friends visit Nashville, this is the place I recommend to them!
The Falafel is no where like a falafel. Instead of Pita bread, they serve it like a wrap. Totally disappointed.

I hope this new place gets a fair shake in Goodlettsville. I took my first order from here to go, but the place seemed decent. Surprisingly, there are some really great Asian spots in Madison and Gville. I hope this place turns into something special, too.

the service was poor. Many items where not available on the menu. The cooks in the kitchen where loud and rude and I was sitting no where near the kitchen...the crab cakes where uncooked, the scallops way over salted and to top it off served cold. Was so glad I did not bring my business client in for a meeting. way over price not even worth a groupon

We use to order from their location in Apollo Beach, and were excited when we discovered that they relocated down the road from us. I love the fact that we are starting to build a diverse committee & they are bringing their foods with them. It's a bonus for everyone! Pita Kebob always delivers on flavor and their food is hot & fresh. I had stopped doing chain restaurants, including fast food, years ago. I had found that at a lot of those locations if you got food to go, they wouldn't care about the product they put in their bag to take home. Never had that issue with Pita Kebob. Food is always made the same way, whether your eating there, or picking it up, it's fresh ingredients. Our reg order is two Gyros, which comes with fries. That's a full meal for us.

My husband and I visit the area at least once a year. When we discovered Compere Lapin, we arrived with high expectations. Our server/bartender, Ricky, was very knowledgable on the menu entirely. We had the pig ears as a starter. Delish! Next we had the beet salad with ricotta that was to die for. For dinner we had the curried goat, followed up with the "Quattro" leche dessert. We will definitely be returning! We had the pleasure of meeting Larry and Nina, the manager, chef, and owners of the restaurant. Such nice people! Thank you again for the amazing hospitality!

Decided to try out this place as a recommendation from a co-worker. First, we made a reservation and whoever took the call sounded genuinely excited for us to come. That sentiment carried into the night we showed up. We were warmly greeted immediately, as if we've known each other for years. We were seated and our bottle of wine was opened before our jackets were off. The waiter was extremely friendly and read us the specials, and was happy to answer any questions. I came into the night not being a fan of artichoke...I left loving artichokes. Their stuffed artichoke appetizer was phenomenal. My girlfriend was instantly hooked. Next, our entrees came out in the perfect amount of time, and they were absolutely delicious. Fresh pastas, chicken, sausage and sauce. The menu was just large enough to have a wide variety without being over bearing. For dessert, we each had a nice cannoli with extra creamy filling. Topped off with an espresso and the meal was complete. The meal was a good price for everything, and having it as a BYOB allowed us to bring exactly what we wanted. the service was attentive, and extremely friendly. It was quick, but we never felt rushed. When we got the bill the waiter assured us to simply take our time and not to rush, a nice touch from service in a very busy restaurant. First time diners, but they've made loyal patrons out of us for years to come.

We enjoyed this very nice spot in Mullica Hill several times. The food is always fresh. I will say the lower level tables don't get the same service attention as the main floor. Given the choice, eat upstairs. We recently tried for dinner but found out that there place was closed due to a fire. Supposedly it occurred in late August. Hopefully it will reopen

Hassan now has dosa, an indian favorite similar to a crepe that is made of lentils and then stuffed with delicious things! such a great addition for the chilly weather as they are served piping hot and fresh... i think that hassan may be the only one making these in the philadelphia area so it's worth the trip. hassan the owner is one of the kindest people i know!
Clean, on the big street, safe , big space,food delivery fast, delicious and no tips required; -)

The best Thai restaurant I've gone to in a very long time! Reasonably priced! Large portions! Very clean! Bartender was welcoming which made my experience greater! I enjoyed the medium red curry and shrimp tempura! Umami was a very pleasant experience!
just a visitor in here, but love this place！love the tranditional thai food！and tom yum noodle soup taste good too

Thai food is one of my favorite types of ethnic food and of course, Pad Thai is a tried and true favorite dish at any restaurant I'm at. I'm am serious when I say that the Smiling Elephant truly does have the BEST Pad Thai ever! There are no words to describe how fresh, flavorful and melt-in-your-mouth delicious it is. I could taste and savor all of the herbs and spices and sauces individually, but at the same time, they all combined beautifully. I also go the lemongrass hot tea which was relaxing and refreshing at the same time. As an appetizer, we ordered lightly steamed vegetables with an incredible peanut sauce - this was just as good as the Pad Thai! The staff is genuinely sweet and you can see all of the cooks doing their thing - I caught the eye of a cute little old Thai lady in the kitchen and she waved and smiled enthusiastically at me. The only downside is that the place is *tiny* and gets really crowded fast - so get there early! I can't recommend this place enough. :)

Octopus Falafel Truck is an amazing concept! One man show cooking up whatever he feels that day, usually a gourmet chicken and rice dish. Today it was with a turmeric ginger sauce with blackberries, grilled peaches and asparagus. The portions are HUGE!! I could make 2-3 servings from this so it is a great value for $10. I got there at 11:50am (he opens at 12pm) and there was already 12 people on line waiting. He's located on 20th and Market on the northeast corner in an unmarked food truck. He makes each persons dish one by one and calls you up when the platter is ready. Took about 35 minutes to get my food - a bit lengthy since most people are using their lunch break to come here. Overall, the food was delicious. The sauce with the rice and chicken was my favorite part. The blackberries added a great sweet component. The larger asparagus could have been cooked a bit longer as well as the peaches. I will definitely be visiting again to give it another go as I want to try his hummus and falafel and wish him the best of luck on his amazing, fresh food!

The dishes are huge, you can easily share one dish for two, they have very diverse persian cuisine, atmosphere and ancient Iran pictures are Beautiful. Food is tasty & home made Doogh puts you in a deep sleep :)

Food is fresh and very quick. The establishment is clean and orderly. However, if you're looking for southern pho or pho nam, this isn't the place. The pho broth is very simple and is served with a tough meat (I think it was lean flank), no brisket or other beef options, and garnishes are minimal. Buns are fresh and good, and what I keep going back for. Fish sauce and spring rolls are good. Not at all a bad place, especially if you aren't particular about your Vietnamese food.
We really enjoyed the brunch menu here! Perfect portions. Delicious food and extremely helpful wait staff.
My wife and I eat at Pho Hoa quite often. The food is great and it has a very nice atmosphere. This is a definite place to grab an inexpensive, filling meal.
Wow, I went with the Dolmades and a gyro. Both were very well done with excellent flavors. I highly recommend this place!

Recently opened Vietnamese spot to deliver more choices of Vietnamese cuisine on top of the popular King Wok & Saigon in the Indianapolis metro area. Location is fairly close to Saigon & King Wok near the cross walk of 38th street & Lafayette Rd. The place is named "deli" but they do serve pho and other rice dishes similar to typical Vietnamese restaurant. In addition to typical dishes, they also have the Vietnamese sandwiches, boba, and some creative drinks. We ordered summer spring roll, #1 of Vietnamese sandwich, #10 of Pho in the menu, #30 of pho in the menu. Among 6 friends, all of us liked the pho a lot as it has great flavors in the broth and a lot ingredients. #10 has a bit of sour taste (kind of like Tum Yum soup) and sweetness on top of the beef broth. Summer spring roll has great smoky flavors with the bacon inside. #1 of Vietnamese sandwich is definitely recommend since not many places in Indy serves Vietnamese sandwich. Boba is recommend as well!

i have a thing for eateries/restaurants where you can eat with your hands. it is like there are no rules and it is a free for all for the food. i dig it. my friends i went here on a busy friday night. we had reservations, but that didn't really seem to matter. we ended up waiting over 1 hour! granted, the owner was wicked sweet to bring us wine to keep us warm, but the waiting outside in the alley and smelling the aroma of delicious food was torture. i felt as if i was trapped in my own personal inferno. the atmosphere of this place is lavish. pillows and you are all sitting close to other tables. an intimate place. i felt like we were at a harem sans the million wives. the chicken with olive and lemons was delicious. the chicken was so tender, it slid off the bone. some of my peeps are vegetarian. if you tell the staff ahead of time, they can accommodate. the pastry with eggs and Cinnamon and powdered sugar was decadent. also, when they come around with the bread, take a bunch because you need it for all the courses. the mint tea at the end was really good, but too sweet for me. the staff is friendly and we were there for a belly dancer. but, my friend totally served her! our meal took over 4 hours and due the wait, all our wine was comped. it was my first time having morroccan food and i loved it. although i did not eat for the next 2 days! i think they have pillows there because after you eat, you wanna nap and dream of more Moroccan food!
Love this place! The food is always good and the staff always friendly. Only downside is it is not wheelchair accessible so I come as much as possible for the outside seating.
Had the falafel, grape leaves and hummus. Very good! Wish the food was house made instead of imported.

I found this restaurant over a year ago while looking for a good mofongo; which is hard to find in Tampa. The mofongo and any other dish on the menu was terrific. My business partner and I visited this restaurant frequently and shared our experience with co-workers and family. In my last visit on Saturday, September 12th I wanted to share the food and La Casona experience with my family. We arrived just past 4:30 PM and we were seated right away. However, the waitress showed up about 10 minutes later to take our drink and appetizer orders . 20 minutes later we still didn't have our drinks and I had to ask another waitress to check on our orders. We finally received out appetizers at the same time as our appetizers made it to the table. We ordered alcapurrias, fried yuca, and french fries. The alcapurrias were deicious, but the yucas were raw and we never received the additional sauce we requested. The waitress never stopped at our table to check on us, but was chit-chatting with other people at the bar. I had to shout at her to get her attention and get a glass of wine and a cup of water which we had already asked for the first time she came to the table. Finally our food arrived and it was good, but not as good as I had experienced in the past. In addition, the 3?out of the 4 mofongos we ordered had raw chunks of plaintain and they lacked flavor...especially garlic! Our whole experience was very dissapointing. The flavors of La Casona used to be awesome, fresh and memorable. Now, I am not sure I would spend my hard earned money on crappy service and average food.
Excellent food, fair prices with friendly service just a bit slow. Would recommend to others.

Went here with a group of friends last night, and would definitely go again even though I found a few things lacking. Good: the chicken with lemon and olives. YUM. And the lamb with honey and almonds was delish. The atmosphere was relaxed and casual, but dress comfortably because you might be sitting on a very low cushion. Meh: the bread. Instead of pita, they brought around these thick wedges of a cake-y white bread. It was impossible to scoop up our food with it, and our hands were all covered with sauce. Also, the Moroccan wine by the glass -- really really chewy. Better to splurge on a bottle of better wine (around $30). To people who want to see the bellydancer for entertainment -- if you enjoy her dancing, tip her. Our poor girl danced her heart out 3 times, with people from several tables, and we were the only table who gave her a tip. Get up and wriggle with her for 30 seconds, and give her $5... It's the correct thing to do.
Our first time here with the new owners and the food was great. A little slow, but we had time and didn't mind the wait because the food was worth it!

It was great! Wings were extra crispy, I recommend the chipotle lime mayo - dirty bird is a little messy but I should have expected that with chili as a topping, bun was nice And the fountain sodas are extra good. Oh and the Mac and cheese is a must.

I loved the garlic naan, butter chicken, and saag paneer. The food had a lot of spices used, which I really enjoy. Service was good, fast & courteous. Will be back for sure. $10 for all you can eat lunch & a drink.

The wait for our food was unacceptable, people who came in after us were served before us. Mind you we only ordered 4 egg rolls. The front counter seemed to not be in touch with the kitchen. All in all it was chaotic. For the food, the Chinese vegetable egg roll wasn't good. But we did enjoy the cheesesteak roll, sausage egg and cheese roll and the broccoli cheddar roll.
The place to go for authentic Thai! Family run for 30 years. Must visit in south Tampa. Very close to MacDill AFB. Great food and excellent service.

Trendy place- nice interior esthetics without being too hipster. We sat at the bar with a view of the kitchen and spoke to some of the chefs. We had excellent friendly service. We had four of the small plates and each was delicious, and we were also given an extra small plate by one of the chefs. Everything was light and delicious. We then shared the braised lamb with couscous, which was really good. For dessert we had the phattycakes - awesome! Wine selection was small but decent, and my only critique would be to expand the drink selection. Overall this was a great date night!

My mother and I stumbled upon this quaint little BYOB when we were looking for a place to eat before seeing a performance at the Scottish Rite Auditorium. It was total fate. We walked in the door to this tiny little restaurant and stood somewhat awkwardly by the door as there is no reception area. We were soon after greeted by Tom, who asked to wait patiently for a few minutes to see if the restaurant could accommodate us seeing as we didn't have reservations. Lucky for us, a 5:45 p.m. reservation was already 2o minutes late and not answering their phone. Win for us! We were on a tight schedule to ensure that we would be in our seats before the performance began, which is a shame since this is the kind of place you really want to savor. Rachel and Tom, who took care of us, were the epitome of what you look for in service. We ordered the artichoke appetizer, which was a special that night. While we were waiting (which really wasn't long) we enjoyed various focaccia breads and a sesame bread slice with olive oil. It was superb, especially the olive focaccia chunk. The appetizer was good and was shortly followed by the Rigatoni alla Disgraziata for my mom and the Tagliatelli al Limone for me. The food was very good. My Tagliatelli was homemade and very good but very lemony. Definitely more sweet than savory. We finished the meal when Tom approached and asked if we wanted to squeeze in a dessert. Man after my own heart, absolutely! My mom had the delicious lemon tart, which would also have been my order except my main dish had lemon. I, in turn, had the chocolate almond cake which was the perfect way to end the meal (if only it had a small scoop of homemade vanilla gelato, it would have been to die for!).
