We finished our entire meal, desserts and coffee and were out the door by our marked deadline of 7:15 p.m.! And it is all due to the kindness of the waitstaff and the kitchen here. I am so grateful to them for making this night extra special for my mother who deserves nothing less. Thank you! I would definitely return. And next time with a good bottle of wine.

The SO found this place while staying up in Philly for a workshop. She went a few times during that week and the whole fam tried it out the day we came to pick her up. Don't let the humble appearance of this little hole in the wall fool you. The Dominican food was fantastic. We had the chicken, rice, beans, and plantains. Yeah, it sounds pretty non-descript, but it was great. Very succulent, very good. Everybody left happy! If you happen to be nearby you should definitely give them a try. The next time we're up in this area I will definitely be coming by to sample more from their menu. Take it from a guy who likes to eat.
Amazing food and wonderful service! We ordered the Peruvian ceviche for an appetizer, and we shared the Fanesca and Veracruz style fish (a special that day). All of it was superb!
I loved the old location and was excited to try to the new one. The brunch burger was the worst burger I may have ever had. Truly disgusting. My friend who had one too felt the same.

I was in New Orleans for about 3 days. I ate here about 5 times.... It was close to my hotel, and every time the drunk munchies hit I just gravitated to this spot. BRING CASH. Their ATM charges $3 and they dont take plastic.

If you have eaten in Thailand or tasted real authentic Thai food in New York or LA, you will find this place very disappointing. Food is tasteless. You can order your food requesting level of spiciness. I asked for "Thai level" spiciness, the red duck curry and chicken green curry were still bland. The Thai beef salad had well done chucks of beef instead of rare slices as it should be. The dressing for the this beef salad was ok. The Chicken coconut soup (Tom Ka Gai) was again tasteless. The best thing with this restaurant is the service. Very friendly and efficient.
A little taste of Greece in Philadelphia, this restaurant is a gem. Will be back to try more of their dishes!
Good food and drinks were offset by small portions and an inflated bill. A good spot for those in search of a chic night out in downtown St. Pete.
Tom Kha soup to die for. Drunken Noodles were amazing. Wonderful food and great service!

Completely speechless! Not really because I will tell you all about the delicious food I just put in my belly. Started off with the queso fundido con chorizo. It tasted so cuminy and delicious. It was also a huge portion! There is so much cheese in there that the chip has a hard time picking it up. Then I order the fish tacos. YUM! The dish came with three fish tacos, this incredible cilantro rice, and a very yummy side of black beans. I also ordered white sweet potato mash. Lastly, I topped it off with a plantain bake. WOW. That may be the one of the most incredible desserts I've had in Indy (at least in the top 3). I also had a rosemary daisy (pretty good) and Fire 'N' Ice (I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS DRINK!!!) I spent about $60 but I am very happy about all the leftovers that I get to eat tomorrow. I cannot wait to eat here again.
Good food and clean! I was unsure of the noodles thing so I ordered the cheese steak . YUMMOLA!! My hubby had the Spicy Ceaser Wrap and that was also the jackpot!

Ordered take out on 02/26/2016 while I was in the area for some work. The service was quick as always. The manager at the register is polite and professional. I love the prices! More affordable than any other Indian restaurant i have gone to. Of course, the food is not the greatest, but it's never totally disappointing either. Having said that, I don't think i would order chicken biryani again. It's not basmati rice, and the taste is simply not authentic biryani. The chicken curry had a pool of oil floating at the top -- not very healthy. But the chicken was perfectly tender. The tandoori chicken appetizer was good, but it does contain red food coloring. I do like this restaurant -- it's clean, cozy, quick, affordable, and has a simple menu with gluten or lactose-free labels.

Very good. The portions are very big. They might not look like it, but that noodle bowl has some depth. This is my first time here, and so far, it's been great. I recommend. Their prices estimate around the same as any other Thai place I've been to as well.

Ordered take out, everything was warm, well cooked and I thought a decent serving amount. Very good, medium spice versus mild spice is noticeably different. The tandoori chicken wings were very tender and flavorful. Their paneer was dense, naan thin and a bit crisp. The palak paneer was thick with spinach. I liked the shahi paneer I've only found a buttery sweet creamy dish like this in one other restaurant.

Bland. With all the wonderful flavors of NOLA, this little spot is disappointing. The service is fast and friendly, so I'll give them that. But their quintessential dishes: the bun & pho are just white bread versions of the really good dishes at other authentic Vietnamese restaurants. My 2 cents: find somewhere else.

The fam and I decided to grab some food before going to watch a movie. I usually eat around the tampa Bay Area but today we ended in Saint Pete area. This is how we stumbled upon seasons cafe. I ordered the barbecue chicken wings and they are to die for. The dish comes with sticky rice and a side sauce. I wish the dish came with more chicken wings. Next I tried the papaya salad. I ordered the three pepper one and it was spicy. If you can't handle spice I wouldn't suggest this dish. Taro boba tea tasted great! Definitely a must try for my saint pete peeps.
Great kabob meats. Great basmati rice; maybe the best in Treasure Valley. We took home two different orders with an appetizer, added our own steamed broccoli, and had an amazing dinner.

Friendly attentive staff and very patient with the crowd of people in line. I got the salmon with corn and rice n peas. Also roti skins were delicious and freshly made. Huge aloof food for a low price. I will be back

For a place called mojito they should probably learn how to make one. It was terrible. We got the paella which was a bowl of rice with about a dozen mussels on top and some dry chicken. It was not good. The fried avocado appetizer was very good. I wouldn't go back on our next visit. Boy that drink was bad. The person next to us complained about the drink they had and it was not a mojito.

It took us a long time to try Zagol, and we were really excited for our dinner there; unfortunately, we left really disappointed. The main reason for our displeasure was the really, really terrible service. From the brusque greeting we got upon entering the restaurant, to the twenty minutes it took to cash out the check before we could leave, we spent our entire time in Zagol feeling totally unwelcome. When we were seated, there were only a few other people there, but several groups came in after us and many of them were getting their food orders taken before we had even seen the waitress. It got so bad that when she went to help the table next to us, they spoke up and told her, "That other table has been here a lot longer than us." Thanks, other people! If you hadn't been so kind, we might still be sitting there! Ordering our drinks turned into a long list of what they were out of that night. Even so, we should have each ordered multiple drinks because once we got our food, she disappeared again, leaving us to eat a pile of spicy food WITH NO WATER REFILLS! To highlight all of this, the dining room was too cold. Most of the people in the restaurant left their coats on at the table. Bad form, Zagol. I know heating that big space must be pricey, but that's one of the costs of doing business. Pump up the thermostat a bit. If it hadn't been for the service, we probably would have really enjoyed our meal. We tried the Key Wat, Beg Tibs, and Mesir Wat. Everything we ate was delicious, and the flavors quite different from anything else available in town. We enjoyed eating with the Injera, although about halfway through the meal it became a bit too much, and I just wanted to finish off the remainder of the food with a fork. We would have asked for utensils at that point if we had someone to ask. Daughter was particularly fond of eating with her hands: a warning to other parents, though--if your kid isn't into spicy food, they probably will be very unhappy here. Overall, we probably won't be back, which is unfortunate, since Zagol has a tasty offering, and Reno is really lacking for diversity in ethnic foods. Unfortunately, they are a bit too costly to bother with that poor of an experience again.

The food is really good but giving it 3stars because of the line average wait is about 30mins and when you call ahead of time they either do not pick up the phone or you still have to wait when you get in the restaurant. For a pretty busy place like this would think they can hire more people.

Maybe our favorite Thai Food ever. And we lived a half mile from Thai Town in Los Angeles for 12 years so we've had a lot! Papaya salad, drunken noodles and chili basil chicken (or whatever the closest thing to that is) are our favorites. And they understand "Thai spicy". Wooo!

This is one of my favorite Indian places in St. Louis (my other being Cafe Everest). This one is within walking distance so we come here a lot more. The food is delicious. We love coming on Sunday to get the special (Halwa). I am a huge fan of the Poori that comes with it. We also enjoy the Alu Gobi (a cauliflower curried dish). It is a small, unassuming storefront but with very friendly service and delicious food!

Wonderful experience here. Stopped in because there were good reviews and I was looking for a place with vegan options. Not only was I pleasantly surprised by the price, but also by the owners. Not only were they lovely and caring people, but they genuinely wanted me to come back and enjoy my food. They asked about my diet/lifestyle to make sure everything was okay. Also pointed me in a cheaper direction for my order: guaranteeing everything I wanted and more. I plan to make eating here a thing at least once a week and will be back tomorrow with my mom!
I come here a lot. Just had a birthday here too. Love the girls dancing and the customer service is amazing and quick. Drinks are always so good here and the mood and setting is perfect!!!

It's been a while since I've been in, but I was in the area around lunchtime today and decided to stop. So glad I did. I ordered the gyro salad and an order of hummus to go. This isn't an especially comprehensive review. I've only ever had the gyro salad and hummus from here, but there's a reason I haven't tried anything else...I really love that salad. It's nothing fancy. Good lettuce (green leaf, I think...I hate iceberg so I appreciate good lettuce!) some cucumbers, olives, red onions, feta, tomatoes, and delicious gyro meat. Served with pita and tzatziki sauce. Having it to go was a new experience. I was a little worried about it. Sometimes to go orders just don't taste the same. This one did. It was a nice touch that they wrapped the gyro meat separately from the salad. It was still warm when I got home and the salad wasn't warm or wilted from the heat of the meat. The only reason I can't give this place five stars is that they close so early we can't go very often.

Strictly based on their Boba, it's just ok. The smoothie part of the drink was tasty, not the best Mango Boba I've had but certainly not bad. The tapioca though was no good. Far too soft to be a part of this drink. They also should consider using a slotted spoon to get the pearls into the cup, that way you don't have a layer of liquid at the bottom that really isn't a part of the drink. I'll return to try some of their other things, but hopefully there are better boba spots in the area.

LaVa is my neighborhood cafe. That's why it's easy to go there for a cup of coffee or a surge of internet when mine craps out on me. Yesterday's latte was served to me in what looked like a small bowl. The drink was entirely flavorless, and cost me almost $4 (I know, I know, typical price). HOWEVER, I had a Mediterranean hummus plate for about $7, which was bitchin'. Pita, cucumber salad, stuffed grape leaves and so much hummus I took it home and it lasted me the rest of the week. Seriously. The amount they give you is almost equal to a small store bought container (only this is homemade!) They offer day-old pastries for half off, which came in handy the other day. Out of bread and dying for a good old breakfast sandwich, I ran to La Va and picked up a croissant. Sliced it in half and put it on the grill pan, which revived its staleness. Yum. Good to know: you have to ask for the wireless password, which I"m pretty sure they change everyday.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I ate here twice. First visit I ordered goat achari curry which was really good and Shrimp biryani which was okay. It took them over 60 minutes to bring me my food after my order. Second visit I ordered Chicken Biryani (spicy level - hot). They served me food after one hour. Biryani was not spicy, was not hot. Chicken was dry. I thought I will ask the server to get me some spicy sauce or chutney or raita to go with Biryani. But the server never showed up after giving me food. No one stopped by to even ask or check if I needed water or if food was ok. I want the OWNER to read this. Since no one checked on me I decided to walk to the counter and talk to someone. I spoke to the Owner and he mentioned that because it was little busy no one could stop by to check on me. I want the OWNERS to know that because it was busy you guys did not give me free food neither did you guys tell that to me before me placing order. So I expected quality food or at least good service. But nothing was even close to what any decent restaurant would offer. The owner took off $15 from my $100 bill (I think to compensate the average quality food and bad service) but I want him to know that things DO NOT work that way. After I expressed my concern he gave a weird look to the server (as if it was entirely her fault). It would help if they treat their employees well. It was not her fault, may be if you hire more people it will help manage situations like these. I will never return.

Usually, I am very weary of high rated Thai restaurants because the reviews are hardly accurate but this place was a gold mine! Goodness it was delicious and the service was absolutely on point! I had the stuffed chicken wings, Pad Thai and Drunken Noodles. Chicken wings: they were okay. I wish they didn't batter it though and just deep fried it with the skin. It was okay. Pad Thai: I've searched Florida far and wide for a place of high standards for Pad Thai and this place hit the nail! It was so good and creamy unlike the other pad thai's that I've had that is dry. Definitely hit the spot! Drunken noodles: on point as well too! I was skeptic about getting two noodles dishes but they both did not disappoint one bit at all. Overall, it was such a great experience and I am so happy to have found a Thai place to go to for my noodle cravings for Thai food. Here I am in a food coma with a happy tummy and that's more than what I could ever ask for. Longest review I've written because this place was worth it!

The service here is absolutely terrible. I did not feel like an appreciated customer in the least bit. We came in and had a seat, the lady with long hair came and slammed some forks and some napkins on our table and asked what we wanted to drink. We both asked for waters. Mine arrived with something black floating on the bottom. Gross. Then the lady with the short black hair came and took our order. When the food arrived it looked like we had one extra order of spring rolls so we told her we didn't order that and there was some kind of miscommunication. She took the plate away with a huge disappointment on her face and rolled her eyes. After that she never once came to our table to refill our drinks and we waited forever for the bill. Though she walked by about 10 times to go gossip with what looked like family or friends seated nearby us. They rudely stared at us the entire visit. Since it was impossible to grab her attention I finally walked to the counter to pay the bill and get out of there. The food is delicious, but the service is horrible. To go orders are probably the best option if you plan on going here.

The place is located near Opry Mills , in a not so classy location, but don't let that fool you. The interior looks good. The food was amazing ! I ordered the pacific Thai noodles and they were great. We were in a group or 6 people and each one of them liked their food. I only wish the service was better. There was only one lady taking orders and serving food and that meant our food took a good 30 minutes to come out. The lady was also not very helpful , when my friend asked for vegetarian suggestions. However, the food was very very good and I will definitely go back.

The most disgusting dishes I have tested ever.goat curry was full of bones..didn't like at all.. no taste at all for any curries.. we ordered chicken and Goat with rice .. and regarding their customer service ?? The guy at the front desk ??? Omg , He was treating his employees with no respect.. horrible experience from this restaurant .. never going back and not recommended..
Visited 2 times for a lunch buffet. Liked the food overall. Ambience is good. Waitresses are friendly. As it's near to the place we live, I may visit more often

There was a time I was addicted to this place. It's still great, I just moved to Franklin so I don't eat here as often. I actually really love their fruity chicken salad pita pockets. The traditional greek items are really good as well. And they have really good baba ghanoush and desserts. I like the ambiance and decor as well. It's busy during lunch hour and ordering can be chaotic if it's your first time.

At first glance the restaurant looks astonishing. Very well lit, beautiful decor. The hostess took our order and she was very nice and helpful. The food was by far the best Indian food I've had in Indianapolis. The samosas were delicious and left us wanting more. We couldn't decide on what to order because everything was very enticing. I highly recommend this place for any occasion from casual to formal.

Classic overbooker, you fooled me once so shame on me. Won't be back. If you want to leave me standing for 45 minutes past my reservation time in a rush-hour-subway-crowded freezing anteroom with a drafty door that opens right up onto the street, please make sure that you're about to thrill me with the best food I've ever tasted in my life and not the merely OK fare that I was eventually served. At least have the decency to pass out complimentary drinks or hors d'oeuvres to the dutifully (stupidly?) waiting hordes of shivering 50- and 60-somethings who, after a quarter of an hour or so of being cooped up together may have begun to believe that they were being watched by hidden cameras as part of some Penn PhD candidate's psychology project. I can live with rejection, but not with being lied to. If you don't have the seats, don't take the reservation. It's that simple.

I can't say enough about how wonderful this place is. I am in love with their Thai fried rice, chicken satay, pad see iew, and my husband loves their crab delight. The waitresses and the servers are so kind and a pleasure. The wait is never long. The food is always fresh. If you are looking for good authentic Thai food, this is the place. They also have high levels of spice if you are into that kind of thing. I always go for no spice.

Food is as bland as the ambiance. We were asked how spicy we wanted our vegetarian dishes. We asked about 1-10 scale and were told that "8" would be very spicy. We couldn't taste any heat whatsoever. If you like spicy food, ask for a 15 on their 1-10 scale and you might get lucky. We won't be going back, especially with the TVs playing sports in the corners. Is it an Indian restaurant or a makeshift sports bar?

Pretty good food and service. They put meat in my spring rolls accidentally last time. But I'm sure every restaurant makes errors. Convenient location for the many people who work on longley and want something relatively healthy on their lunch break
Pretty tasty slant on pitas and wraps. Healthy and homemade. German / Mediterranean influences. Delivery to downtown. Parking is pretty much a pain.

I LOVED THIS RESTAURANT. My friend and I were visiting St. Louis for a girls' weekend this past weekend. And we decided we had to eat at Olio after seeing the menu. In a converted gas station, Olio is beautiful. It's small and intimate and really exquisitely lit and decorated. It felt like restaurants in NYC - very elegant and modern, yet casual and homey. Great wine list (we stuck with wine rather than trying their cocktails which also sounded very good), and great service. BUT THE FOOD. Olio is Israeli and Middle Eastern food, and they offer dishes that you don't see often in upscale restaurants in the United States! We started with the muhammara - a Levantine dish made from red peppers and walnuts. Olio's came with liberal amounts of pomegranate molasses as well. It was a delicious starter - they asked if we wanted more bread, but were content to eat it straight from the dish with our forks. It was that good. We then shared the Moroccan carrots: roasted and raw carrots with harissa yogurt, and carrot tops. This was the only slight miss of the night for us. The roasted carrots were COLD. I think it's meant to be a cold dish (not served warm), but these carrots were ICE COLD - like just off ice - which was a bit unappetizing. The harissa yogurt was AMAZING. Other than the temperature, this was a really good dish, too. (I think it just need some time or heat to get to room temp and then it would be a good dish.) Then we shared the "Sinnia" (chicken kofta with tahini, pickled onion, and tomato). Koftas are essentially Middle Eastern meat balls. And these were AMAZING. The dish was perfect. The koftas weren't dry at all (and using a leaner meat like chicken can be tricky for this reason), and they were so so so so so so tasty. The tahini was nutty and smooth, and there were herbs all over the dish. The bread was SENSATIONAL. I would go to Olio RIGHT NOW and order this dish all over again. It's that good. Having said that, we sat at the bar and got to watch all the food prep while we drank and ate (we weren't in a hurry because Olio is such pleasure to dine at). And I would eat everything that comes out of this kitchen. My friend is a chicken and fish only eater, so we stuck to veggie dishes and chicken, but WHEN I go back, I want to eat the rest of their menu dish by dish! Wonderful dinner!

We absolutely love Joy Cafe. It's a small, cute, unique, family-owned business. Joy Cafe is in a little strip mall, and unless you're looking for it, you would never know it's there. The menu is short but eclectic. They offer an interesting mix of food for lunch, including wraps and several Asian sandwiches. They also offer coffee, boba tea, Thai iced teas, and milkshakes. Everything we have had has been delicious. Every time we've been there, one person (presumably the owner) has done all of the work -- taken the orders, made the food fresh, etc. She's great and very nice. Highly recommend checking this out and supporting a small local business.
This is one of my romantic, trendy favorites in SB, although the ingredients have slipped a bit, and the wait staff is unpredictable.

Came in recently w/ some girlfriends to check off another bookmarked restaurant. Olio is beautiful inside, yada, yada, on to the food... The good: -Olio's specialty...Egg salad...hell yes! Especially w/ the anchovies. -hummus deluxe...all my hummus from now on has to be served w/ pulled lamb! I could've had just this & a glass of wine & called it a night! - lahmacun...Turkish flatbread, tastes better than it looks, but don't let the ground dog food appearance get you, it's quite delicious! -wine...it's a wine bar after all The bad: -grilled zucchini carpaccio...everyone at the tables least favorite item. For being grilled you'd think it'd be warm, but served cold & tasted like it was marinated in pinesol (not how I like my zucchini). -beets & ricotta on a baguette special...lacked flavor overall. We also ordered & split the brisket sandwich, but I was already too full to try a bite. I'll be back for the wine & hummus & anchovy egg salad!

I've been to other PF Chang's which are pretty average, but the food was not very good quality... I do know that this isn't really Chinese food, but merely Chinese-American but, I've had food from some Pei Wei(their "lower" end restaurant) that was much better.

I don't understand how this place is rated as 1 $ in price. Dinner here will cost a single person about $20. I went alone last time and that's what my bill (including tip, probably) came out to. To get my fix of Viet food in IV, this is the place to go. But I've definitely experienced better and for cheaper.
Well, its one of my fav Indian restaurants in STL... the Chicken Tiki Masala is orgasmic! YUMMY! GET IN MY BELLY!!!
Some of the fakest Thai food I've ever had, and it doesn't even taste good. Who puts cabbage and sugar in tom yum?! Or eggs in drunken noodles? Never going back again.

Outstanding and creative menu matched well with the drinks and wine. Highly recommend sitting at the bar or counter - you get a real feel for how the kitchen works and chat with the staff! I still long for the squid, which is a taste and textural wonder. All the dishes are flavorful and thoughtful. Love it.

This place is amazing! Such a hidden gem. My fave is the curry shrimp platter; it's huge and you get two sides included for $12, which to me is an excellent price. The fish platter and salmon platter are also great; ask for the fish gravy, yum! One tip: there is ALWAYS a line practically to the door so expect to be waiting in line for at least 15 minutes; plan accordingly because it is SO worth the wait!

Ordered veggie avocado spring rolls and chicken curry via Uber Eats. The listing for veggie spring rolls included a selection for peanut sauce at an additional cost. I chose this thinking the rolls weren't coming with any. I ended up with 2. I love peanut sauce so it certainly won't go to waste but the menu was misleading. The rolls themselves had brown lettuce and barely any avocado, especially for calling out the avocado in the name of the dish. The curry came with bread but not rice. This was not mentioned and there was no selection to add rice which I would have if I thought it wasn't coming with any (see peanut sauce above). It is spicy but not particularly flavorful. I will not be eating here again.

This is by far my most favorite restaurant in Nashville. Great for any time of the day! I do all my "special," occasions here. Great wine selections, changing menu, and the whipped feta has me always coming back.

Are we really on Frankford Avenue!? This place is amazing. I was dumbfounded when I walked into this beautiful and inviting space. I ordered a traditional Lebanese flat bread with an egg on top, over medium. Absolutely delicious!! I spoke with one of the owners and I am excited to return to try the diner menu. There is an amazing outdoor space that being completed now, with a bar and seating. What!!!? Love it. Folks for real. You have to see this space. The lunch menu is perfect and not overpriced. Coffee is on point, fresh and hot! I think I found a Homerun!!

I love Phô so when I try a new place, it better be good. Today really surprised me because their Phô wasn't just good it was great. The bowl was so full of noodles and meat, that I couldn't even finish it; and I always order the smaller size! I have to give an honorable mention to the iced coffee too ! It was very good. The service was phantastic! ( a little humor there)There are many choices for Phô , but now Phamous is my go to place!
Known primarily for its Bar & Single Scene. This place actually has really Good Food! Your gonna pay though! Beach Drive Prices! Fun Place, Good Staff, Amazing Food. :)

We stumbled upon this place by a complete accident while looking for sone where to have dinner while visiting my daughter in Philadelphia. Between the experience , music , decorations , hospitality I have to rate it s perfect five stars.
Absolutely the best! From the service to the delicious food, highly recommend this jewel!

Was very impressed with the taste and presentation of almost everything. Didn't enjoy the cauliflower but it was comped as our waitress noticed we didn't touch it after the first bite. Wait staff was very attentive and helpful. Bruschetta, zucchini, and dessert were all perfect. Will definitely return.

Terrible food. First off.... The meal starts of at 9$ and that doesn't even do Justice to the Quantity served. Went in ordered a lamb and naan bread extra meat. So the break down, the basic price was 8.95 and too less a quanitity. extra meat 2.95, Extra naan 1.50, So called Raita a hot sauce quanity container 1$ total went up to 15$.. Secondly, This is coming from an indian who worked in DC and often dined at MERZI, that is a perfect example of a sumptious Chiportle style Indian meal and value for money, being in DC they are so Reasonable Compared to the Cost of living there. Thirdly the taste, YUCK! Bland, half coocked meat and the chutnies are Extreme. Do yourself a favor SKIP THIS PLACE AT ALL TIMES! there are better out there.

Although this food truck is hidden behind one of the small streets on Drexel's campus, this is one of the best food trucks around. I ordered food here for the first time today and the short rib tacos are delicious, not to mention they're cheap too. The guys working the food cart are really nice and talkative. They even let me try a sample of the mango tea which was very refreshing. Since I went around lunch time, there was about a 10 minute wait before I got my food, but it was well worth the wait. Their Thai Tea was really good too, and totally worth the $2. I can't wait to go back here and try something else.

I have never had a bad meal. What I love is that it's always so fresh. The portions are just right....I have no complaints and always make it a point to stop by for lunch when I'm in the area. Well, if any complaints at all....it would be that parking is difficult.

My favorite greek in the city. Inexpensive, family run, BYOB. And the food is delish. I recommend the cold dip appetizer sampler (really, a MUST), grilled octopus, and the baked eggplant dish....mmmmm....i'm hungry just thinking about it!

The food was not only late, but cold and extremely tasteless. I ended up throwing the food away, and I am not that picky... the sushi tasted like cardboard and the miso soup had absolutely no taste and was watered down. I called to complain about the order to the owner and was hung up on.
Very good food, and friendly service. Nice selection of foods, with some of the dishes having adjustable levels of spiciness.

I saw the reviews for this place so I thought I'd give it a try- they were absolutely right! This food is AMAZING. Everything is freshly made and has PERFECT taste! To top it off, the service is amazing! The people who work here are so cute and friendly. The server took the time to explain to me how to make sticky rice because I love cooking. I just got done and I already cannot wait to eat here again!

I usually get food from them atleast 3x's month so I was extremely disappointed when they gave me burnt salmon and the girl that served me put gravy on top so I wouldn't see that it was burnt. I don't even know if I would go back there now.

Tried it on my lunch break because a coworker had said it was good. Service was pretty quick, I thought the tea was pretty good although I had never had Boba tea before, so had nothing to compare it to. But the main problem was the pork banh mi. Barely tasted the pork and what pork I did see looked dehydrated. Most of the flavor was in the cilantro and the jalapeño. Also, was not a fan of the bread itself, which was dry/stale tasting with nothing on the sandwich to balance it out. I may try it again and get something other than a sandwich.
Visiting Nashville. Last thing I expected was to find awesome Puerto Rican food. Atmosphere good. Food good. Pricing just right.

Kindness goes a long way in my book, and the management at Desi treated me with kindness. They treated me with care and respect. I had their buffet lunch that was delicious. The fresh naan and authentic chai were a real treat. Give Desi a try. I hope that you'll have as pleasant an experience as I did.

It's really nice to see good Thai restaurants in the suburbs. With a good location and a great menu, I can't find anything wrong with this restaurant. The service is great and the food comes out fast. The food is delicious as well. The place is clean and large enough for a party. We've been there six or seven times now and my girlfriend and I love fried tofu so we always order that. One thing that makes this place stand out is the whole fried fish. We go there just for that! If I had to keep this review short, I would just say excellent food and fast service!

My wife and I ate here a few nights ago and it was very, very good. The service was excellent, the manager was friendly and made certain we were pleased with everything. They have a great sauce bar where you can formulate your own special sauce or go with one of the many they have available. It's a great spot.

I've been waiting for this place to open for weeks, and I was not disappointed! It was packed, as expected for a new place, but there were plenty of extra trainers on hand to keep the line moving. I ordered the falafel pita with the works. Pita was soft and fresh, the falafel was flavorful, and all the toppings worked great together. If you like it spicy, I recommend the s'khug sauce over the harissa. Based on other reviews, I expected the naf naf fries to be some sort of transcendent experience, but I thought they were just okay, like a limp thick cut potato chip. This place definitely goes into the rotation of lunchtime options.

I came here with a group of 8 people for dinner on a weekday night. When you arrive, you ring the doorbell and are greeted by the host. The place itself is very cozy and consists of several round tables where you share your meal family style. The menu consists of 7 courses (pre-fixed) with vegetarian options available. Our meal started with a washing our hands with rose water and then a salad plate that was really yummy (I really enjoyed the eggplant). We then had the spicy chicken which was essentially an entire chicken, with a spicy sauce that was my favorite. Our next course was a honey almond lamb, followed by couscous and a fruit platter, baklava and mint tea. I think the menu may change, but regardless it was great! All for $25. Definitely an experience worth having at least once!
The food is consistently great and the pleasant wait staff is always on the ball! Great curries!

Amazing place, I cannot say enough good things about this restaurant. The staff take care of you with great care and are super nice. The atmosphere is very authentic with dim lights carpeted walls and seats with dozens of pillows. The food itself should make you come here. We had 7 courses and we should have paced ourselves but everything was just so delicious it was hard to stop yourself. All in all 10/10. Super traditional and authentic but guaranteed that everyone will like it. They are conscious of any allergies or if you are vegetarian so it caters to everyone. I will definitely come here again !!!
Takes a really long time and they'll close spontaneously for the day. It's a huge inconvenience.

Update 1/13/18: Got my usual falafel bowl to go tonight. The baba ganoush tasted weird, and they only gave me ONE falafel (instead of four)...! I was also informed by the people who picked up our order that the employees were disorganized and careless. Hate to deduct a star, but this was not a great experience. Still love it, but it seems like they're slipping. * * * * Tried this new place for lunch today (got it to go). I went around opening so it wasn't busy, and the place was immaculate. I ordered the falafel bowl with baba ganoush and rice, onion, chopped salad, and 2 different sauces. I also ordered their fries, not realizing my bowl came with a pita. It was a lot of food, but it was SO yummy! The fries are more like chips, though some are on the soft side. They were well-seasoned and warm. I had to try them, though I probably won't get them again simply because the rest of the food is filling enough. The pita is perfectly soft and fresh, and was a delightful surprise in my bag when I got home! The main thing I cared about was the falafel. It did not disappoint, and I cannot wait to eat it again and again. There were 5 in my bowl, nicely seasoned and not overly greasy despite the fact that they're fried. All the stuff it came with was delicious, too. I liked the spicy green sauce (s'khug). I thought the tahini sauce was too watery. My hubby had the chicken shawarma in a pita, and couldn't stop raving about it. He got the chopped salad, hummus, and garlic sauce with his. The service was great. There's no signage on the food line so I wasn't sure what some items were (namely the sauces), but all of the servers were patient and friendly. One of them was a bit difficult to understand, as he kinda mumbled a lot, but he was still very nice. Parking is a bit confusing right now, but will hopefully improve as the shopping center gets completed. I just parked inside the edge of the Wegmans lot and crossed the street in the crosswalk -- no problem. I will most definitely be back!
Very good food . i had the fried seafood platter and my family had the lamb gyros. The food was delicious and very filling. And it was allot if food

I looked on Yelp for the best Indian in St. Pete. We got right in and had a great meal. Super nice people and top notch Indian food. A hidden gem. If you want good Indian this is the place. We're here from NH for a month, and we'll be sure to go here several times.

Nashville, not sure that you can handle the flavor and spice that is coming your way but brace yourself because it's happening!!! Don't let the modern sleek decor fool you, this place is as authentic as an Indiana restaurants gets. Dishes start at $10 which is a great value for the portion, quality, and taste. We ordered two vegetarian entrees and naan. -the baby eggplant in sesame sauce tasted like an eggplant purée. Although I couldn't really taste the sesame, the dish was well seasoned. If you are new to Indian food and like eggplant this might be a good beginners dish. -the okra is literally a flavor bomb lots of onions in this dish, delicious caramelized onions that have been simmered in tomato sauce. I always order this dish and this is probably the best I've had. -naan and rice are classics that are done really well. Watch the spice level you request. If you want to be able to taste your food request mild. If you don't want to chase every bite of your entree with a piece of naan (not that there is anything wrong with that) request very mild.

So it's a Tuesday when we decide to order to-go food from here. We would have never had to go here, but our favorite spot, King Wok, down the road, is closed on Tuesdays. My boyfriend placed the order to go on the phone and told me they were rude and they said the food would be 20 minutes because they were busy. I didn't see it as a big deal because even though 20 minutes is a long time in Asian take-out land, it's nothing in any other take-out land. I walk into the restaurant and the guy on the phone wasn't lying, it was busy. But when we order to-go food from King Wok, it is always busy and they always have our food ready for us at the door. There was a young kid checking me out at the front and he honestly had no idea what he was doing. He had to ask each customer that was paying their bill what hey had ordered instead of having some type of ticket system with the other waiter. It was a disaster. I added on two drinks to my order. My iced coffee came out immediately, then I waited about 10-15 minutes more for the food, granted it took us 15-20 minutes after my boyfriend ordered to even get to the restaurant. When the food came out, they had forgotten to make my frozen drink, so then I had to wait another 5 minutes to get that. When we got home, I asked my boyfriend if their vermicelli dish and spring rolls were even comparable to King Wok's. He replied that it wasn't. All would have been forgiven if the food was better, but it wasn't. Needless to say, we will be resisting our Vietnamese urges on Tuesdays and won't be returning.

If you're non desi, you'll be fooled. Of course majority of the good reviews are left by Americans who don't know chaat. What you're eating is not chaat. Not even close. You don't put sweet things like date, cranberry, mangoes in a chaat. I guess they're doing it so non desis can handle it with burning their mouth. There are no chickpeas in this chaat lol. That's the very first ingredient in a chaat. So nothing is authentic and nothing tastes like a chaat. I'll give them props for adding keema, chicken, lamb to make it different but no chickpeas in a chaat is like no tuna in a tuna salad/melt. Those of you who have never had a chaat should go as you can't do the comparison and don't known what you're missing. Don't order mango shake. It's nasty. It's not a real mango. It's nectar with some unripe mangoes.
a hole in the wall place tucked behind a subway. not the best location, but the food is great. very good value for money. highly recommend any of the Dosa and Porrota.
After 30 mins of waiting they said we forget to register your order and want us to order again. Worst experience .

have stopped by 2x for lunch and the specials are a really good deal. you get an appetizer, soup/salad and entree for ~$10. the entree is a dinner size portion as well. i got the thai basil with beef and wife got shrimp pad thai, both of which were very tasty. service was very friendly and fast. very lunch spot if you're in the area.
I do come here quite often and i always enjoy the food in this place. I only get the platter, but the food overall is good here.
Great pho place! The soup is tasty and has a lot of beef. The grilled pork chop was spot on and the spring rolls were very crispy. 10/10 would come again

While Wifey was in NYC enjoying her post half marathon shenanigans, I decided to treat myself to what I consider the best Latin restaurant in Indy. Located in SoBro, I can literally walk to the "heaven sent". I enjoyed the pulled pork tacos w/tasty green rice and black beans. A but mojito was soon summoning my name which I promptly answered it's call. I sat at the bar as the bartender was attentive to my every needs while I watched the 2nd round of the NCAA tournament. I ordered fish tacos to go, knowing that I would want to revisit my dream state later that evening. A must visit by all.

I come here every time I have a Tucson layover. It's walking distance from the hotel my flight crew stays at. I can honestly say that I have never had hummus more delicious than their cilantro jalapeño hummus. I always order the red quinoa salad with cilantro hummus. It comes with hot fresh pita bread. A filling and healthy option.

Loved this place, the food, and the owner! The Saag Lamb was delectable and mouth-melting, the bhel puri was crispy, tasty, and smooth and the Paneer Kadhai smelled and tasted like a spicy tomato soup (delicious!). I also had a lassi - ungodly good! The owner is a sweetheart; we got to talking to her because she and the staff brought over a sweet pomegranate drink and a tasty vegan cupcake for Valentine's Day gratis. We didn't expect it and it was such a nice gesture!

I'll bump Momo's up a star, based on my experience last night. Momo's was pretty empty on a Monday night, which means we got our choice of seats. We chose one of the secluded rooms in the back. Beautiful! I guess Monday is half price wine night? Every bottle of wine was 1/2 price. Sweet. We ordered a pretty decent white that I kinda loved. Food-wise, I went with the chicken kabob. It came with roasted potatoes, and the chicken was also skewered with veggies. Super yummy (and way better than the tough lamb kabob I had last time!) We also had the skordalia (potato puree with garlic, served with pita). I would have liked this more if it was warm (Fozzie's makes a WONDERFUL skordalia spread). But it was cold and kind of mediocre. Dessert time! Momo's has TWO kinds of bread pudding: Chocolate and peach. As much as the BP fanatic in me wanted to order both, I settled with the peach bread pudding. It was super tasty. It was simple, yet delicious. It was topped with a deliciously sticky caramel sauce, which I loved. It was garnished with whipped cream, strawberries, and peaches. I liked it a lot. Service was friendly, even though the waiter seemed to disappear at the end of the meal. Oh, and there was bellydancing this night. The belly dancer was good, but it was so awkward at points. It's weird to have a half-naked woman dance in front of you in such close proximity. I've never been to a strip club, but I imagine the feeling must be similar. It made me really uncomfortable. Anyway, I'll be back. I gotta try that chocolate bread pudding, after all!

This is my favorite Thai restaurant. It is very small but getting a seat is usually not a problem. The food is delicious and their waitresses refill tea and water quickly. I love their red curry dish! Can't beat the lunch specials either.

Everything about this place is absolutely 5-star. We reserved a spot at the chef's counter on a Saturday night. We enjoyed watching the kitchen staff create delicious plates, and we even chatted with one of the chefs who was very friendly. Every dish we ordered was delicious. To start we ordered the bacon-wrapped dates, the whipped feta, and the turnips--all incredibly creative and delicious. We later had the lamb meatballs and for dessert, the banana pudding. During dessert our server (who was lovely and friendly) surprised us with the chocolate pie and two glasses of champagne because we were celebrating our anniversary. This is definitely outside the realm of "southern" cuisine (bbq, fried chicken, etc.), but it was a welcome change after lots of heavy meals. It's also off the beaten path, also a welcome change if you're in town for a few days and tired of the relentless party atmosphere of the strip.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: I was very impressed by the food here, I had the spring rolls as was suggested by other reviews and they were as good as they said. I also had the wide noodle dish with chicken and was happy with the choice. The server was very attentive and when he saw me on my phone offered me the WiFi password for the restaurant. I would recommend this place highly.

I ate lunch on Monday at Aroy Thai. It was completely filled at 12 when we got there and the whole time we were there at least 2 tables worth of people were waiting. We ordered 2 drunken noodles, 1 chicken potsticker appetizer and Pad See-Eew. It is always fresh and excellent. My Pad See-Eew was a lunch special. You get the large portion of protein and noodles and 2 crab rangoon for $8.99. Great value, fast service, and really great food if you're in O'Fallon, IL at lunch time.

The reviews need to come down to planet earth. I'm a transplant from the D.C. region where one can't swing a dead cat without hitting three different Thai places. Being a Thai FANATIC imagine my withdrawal pains when I find myself in the cosmopolitan and sophisticated Spring Hill (shudder). I needed a Thai fix, there isn't much Thai here, so I thought I'd give this place a shot. I've been here twice. Both occasions were underwhelming. I had a beef and bamboo shoots dish. The bamboo shoot to beef ratio was about 349 pieces of bamboo shoot to 1 piece of beef. Seriously. They *really* skimp on the meat here and the bamboo shoots piled 1 soda can high out of the bowl with nary a piece of meat to be seen. The sauce was, well, the word "meh" fits perfectly here. Meh. Nothing to write home about..that's for sure. The same review applies to the other dish I had here. Exchange bamboo shoot with whatever the theme ingredient here is and ... you get the picture. Also, inordinately pricey. Their combo pad thai was 15 dollars. 15 dollars for a noodle dish. Never in even the snobbiest, Congressmen frequented Thai places in D.C. was a noodle dish 15 dollars. Blew my mind. I will keep going to this place on rare occasions when I need a Thai fix, but not because it's great...as the old saying goes "Even muddy water puts out a fire."

I love Ethiopian restaurants, and have been to several. I was so excited to see that Reno has one now.... We went for my birthday; I we were just about the only people in the chilly, cavernous restaurant. Service was prompt. We ordered two large combo meals, expecting something special. Unfortunately, they were out of collards, so we ended up with green beans (frozen???) The other dishes were okay, but small. We also ordered Ethiopian tea (remember, it was chilly in there.) The waitress brought us more bread when we asked, but never did refill our teacups. Maybe it's $2.00 per glass? I enjoyed our dinner, but the total was way out of our price range. We haven't been back.

Super delicious food - both vegetarian and chicken choices / fish were great. Chicken Chettinaad was the best South Indian flavor I ate in almost 17 years. Good chaat, entree and dessert. Masala tea was a bonus. Will definitely come back again. Not many places have Sat evening buffet!

Best in the city. The pancake we had today has a mixture of sprouts and shrimp. Wrap that joker up in some lettuce, add some mint, dunk it in the sauce and it's like a funky burrito from Vietnam. Pot of tea to finish it all off. We'll be visiting again. PLUS, anytime there's a line to get in and the majority of the patrons were Vietnamese, it's gotta be good. **CASH ONLY

Absolutely amazing experience. The food, staff, atmosphere (the 3 owners decorated themselves which is impressive). These guys are awesome, made my girlfriend and I very happy. They were funny and made us very comfortable. Food was tasty and flavorful. No issues, everything came out on time and presented well. The bill came out for $35 for two people and we're stuffed. Indian food favorites are here if you're craving chicken tikka, samosas, tandoori etc.it's all here. Highly recommend this spot :-) I don't leave that many comments here on yelp but this is absolutely necessary haha. Wishing these folks the best. We'll be back often.

3 star rating interpreted by Yelp is A-OK. The definition is rather ambiguous. A glass half full? Or, a glass half empty? In the case of Petra Restaurant, I go for the glass half full. Call me an optimist. Our lovely host Tiffany H. suggested an UYE events at Petra, a Middle Eastern restaurant. With her help, we six curious-yelper-fellow managed to maximize our orders of appetizers and main courses. As an optimist, I pick dishes I liked in this review and leave the rest for others. Babagahanoush, this starter cooked with my favorite vegetable, the eggplant. The mysterious seasoning blended with rich flavor of eggplant, it reaches the initial goal of liking this restaurant. Served with warm pita bread and salty pickles, this dish is definitely in the alley of healthy eater's choice. Vege plate is the another starter I highly recommend. It is a large portion enough for a table of 4 to share or as a main course. The combination of hummus, grape leaf wrap, falafel, babagahanoush and salad gives a great introduction to guest like me who is not familiar with Middle Eastern cuisine. Kalayah is the main dish I picked. The sauteed lamb flavor soaked into a rich tomato sauce gives a unique taste that I am very fond of. The hidden spiciness from jalapeno is another shot to the flavor. This dish with a bowl of rice or pita bread brings equilibrium. If you are not into eating lamb, chicken is an alternative. Rest of dishes on our table fell into the pessimistic gap; most of them are grilled meat. Compared with the big juicy American steaks and burgers, these dishes are way across the line of 'medium well.' Other than my disappointment of the meat dishes, I like this restaurant a lot. Due the natural of its original region the Petra represents, the presence of the culture is obvious. I was in my typical Floridian outfit that is as much as some of the dishes, way across the line, in this case, their culture. As a native Chinese, I have been taught to respect others culture no matter how different they are. I was not living to that standard at that moment. Nonetheless, our waitress disregarded this factor and kept me well served. I appreciate that. After all, I like the restaurant. I am an optimist. I will return to find more goodies.
The grilled cheese sandwich w/ tomatoes is awesome. They use some sort of hot chutney that thrills my Indian taste buds to the max.

The worst Indian we've eaten. We tried to find an Indian takeaway close to home. This place got good reviews so we finally tried it out. Chicken tikka masala for my wife and chicken curry for me. Neither tasted anything like the dish we ordered. The naan bread was tough and chewy. The only positive note were the lamb semosas. Crispy, large and full of minced lamb and peas. This was such a disappointment!

Yeah, they make their own tea. Yeah, the portions are large. Yeah, they check on you repeatedly. Yeah, the prices are fair. Gordon Ramshackle would probably change their decor, but why be picky? Thai Taste is a "win."

Delightful. If you're interested and small plates and cocktails this is your spot. The plates tend to have meat but they do have good options for non-meat options. Everything is pretty rich so order less than you think. Been a few times, would go again.
fish curry for days. slightly sweet, crispy, and spicy. kindly sack up and move to the empty storefront next to jimmy johns in the central west end.
This is hands down the best Thai food around. Service is friendly restaurant is very clean and the prices are reasonable. No need to say more, you won't be disappointed.

Saw the reviews and I got excited. Unfortunately I was let down. Went to Nashville for some shopping and wanted to take home some delicious thai food, since my town doesn't have any. The place had a decent amount of people, but not packed. Waited about 10 minutes to even order my food. The woman told me it would be a 30 minute wait for the food, which is understandable. I ordered dinner sizes of pad kee mao, massaman curry and sukho fried rice. After standing then finally sitting, I finally got my food 1.5 hours later. NOT JOKING! My phone almost ran out of battery, just waiting. She kept telling me "almost ready." Please don't tell me that was all I could think about. Food was okay, but they forgot to make my orders spicy.

I was really excited to check this place out. Overall the atmosphere is cool and laid back. It goes well with the "street food" vibe. The staff is really friendly and you could tell that the owners were very involved as well. My fiancé and I got two entrees, split a salad and had two glasses of wine. This cost us about $50 before tip. We both felt like the food was good and really flavorful but it was a little overpriced for a fast casual restaurant that advertises "street food".

I had been told repeatedly that this was THE PLACE in the Media area for Indian food, and for my buffet lunch, I found that to be true. I trucked over from Frazer during my last week working there, when I wasn't concerned about how long my lunch would take. The ambience was very nice, not cheap looking like recent finds in Frazer, and there were lots of options for veggie or meat eaters.

Wow just dined there and all I can say AMAZING... Great staff very attentive manager the food was outstanding I had the lamb tikka masala highly recommended if u like tomato base sauce my boyfriend had the rogan josh and loved it for appetizer we had the sher e pujab sampler and for dessert the pistachio ice cream which is home made it was unbelievable probably the best Indian I have tried ever and don't forget to order some naam !! Can't wait to go back

Coming from the area of Fremont in the Bay Area and have tried many Indian restaurants, this one is on my top 3. First, I'm not used to the nice ambiance for this cuisine. Rarely would I consider taking someone on a formal date to an Indian restaurant. They're usually very quick, noisy, or it's something I grab and go. This one is very quiet and definitely a sit down restaurant. Now for the food. My coworkers like butter chicken, I'm more of the traditional Chicken Tikki Massala or lamb dish. I ended up getting the lamb dish with the medium spice level. It was great. The butter chicken was surprisingly good, sweet, and savory. We also ordered the lamb samosas (3.5/5). Garlic naan was great! Other naans aren't bad either, just really what you're in the mood for. Other than that, the only thing that I can see improving in this establishment is the mango lassi. It's too thick for my liking and also too sweet. If you like that, then go right ahead and order it. This is one of the few good places to eat outside of Philly, and we're staying in the suburbs so it's a gem to have something like this available. I'd like to try the lunch buffet if we have time.

On a train ride back home from a stressful weekend in NYC, I needed some comfort food - which for me means Middle Eastern cuisine. There are so many tasty places around Philly, but I hadn't tried Bitar's and so many people I know swear by them. Yay for online ordering! Placed my order, and their delivery guy pulled up to our building right after my taxi dropped me off - talk about fast delivery service! My husband was eager to chow down, and thankfully the food I ordered was more than enough for the two of us! The Mediterranean Combo had everything that I love: hummus (two servings!), babaghanuj, tabouli, dolmades with tzatziki sauce, feta, tabouli salad, and pita, we got ours with falafel. But since my man is a carnivore we also had the grilled chicken platter, with tomatoes and onions over rice with tahini sauce and pita. Everything was delicious and fresh, just super tasty traditional Middle Eastern food that really, truly hits the spot and satisfies. Even with a small delivery fee, I will absolutely order from Bitar's again!

Service was very slow and received my food cold. I had pepper steak and it lacked flavor, very bland, and tough. I also had their crab ragoons, to sweet for my liking. I've had better Thai and this place doesn't qualify as Thai food to me.
One of the best buffets in Tampa Bay that I've been to. I have no recollection of what I got from the buffet but they were all good. Looking forward to the next time.

I was finishing my shopping and needed some food I was wanting soup Which they had three on their menu They offer salads and pasta I love that one can do with or without meat You can do a small or regular serving The servers offered suggestions and even deliver to the table Very friendly place

I have to agree with most of these reviews. The food is great! Best Tom Ka soup I've had in Tampa. I've visited almost every Thai restaurant in the Tampa area, and this is really good. This "hole in the wall" place is on my top favorite places to dine.

I am always seeking out places that work for a large group to BYO on a weekend. Banana Leaf is my go-to, but sometimes you need to spice it up. I am happy that Erawan's new location can be added to that list. The space is very cute and the staff is attentive and put up with us staying after closing. And they deserve credit for totally tricking us and saying it was too late to order dessert and then bringing out coconut ice cream with a candle for the bday boy. The flavor in my spicy been salad was great though some of the pieces were too chewy. Entrees are very big. I liked the drunken noodles and their curry was even better. They also make a good Thai Iced Tea. Take your group here!

Looking for a place to eat in New Orleans can be overwhelming. Tonight we were looking for a place that had music. We decided upon Mojito's, and what a pleasant surprise. We sat out on the courtyard, listening to some great live jazz music, and the food was really better than I had anticipated. I might add that we brought 3 kids and Michael took real good care of us. The Frenchman Mojito was excellent.

Place was really quiet when we arrived ( on friday night ) so we were skeptical initially. The food took some time to arrive but it was so delicious that it was totally worth the wait. I would totally recommend the dal makhani. Out of the world. The naan, unlike the soft chewy naan at other indian restaurants, was very well baked with just the right crispiness. Will definitely visit again.

This was some of the best Mediterranean food we've had in a long time! Don't let the unassuming decor fool you. This is authentic, fresh and delicious Mediterranean food! We had the mixed vegetarian platter which we split - fantastic! Wonderful hummus, baba ghanoush(so?) and amazing falafel! Also great salad and grape leaves. We took home some baklava which we just finished - yum! I rarely give five stars, but this place deserves it!
I don't have a lot of other Vietnamese places to compare it to, but the chicken noodle bowl I got was delicious. It's not terribly busy so you will get your food quickly.
It was our friend's anniversary and the meal was outstanding. Ended up there because Lemoncello totally messed up our reservations, but Avalon and their staff saved the day.
This is our favorite spot. Both the food and service is always outstanding. If you like Thai food, don't pass this by!
My husband and I eat here at least 3-4 times per month we are big fans of the drunken noodle. I would say it's the best drunken noodle around. The fried rice is also phenomenal.

If you follow any of my reviews, you know pho is my favourite food and I eat a lot it lol. Imagine my delight to see this restaurant opening up literally at the end of my block! We noticed they finally were open and popped in for lunch. It was busy and the servers were new, but very friendly and very attentive! I ordered a Vietnamese iced coffee which is premade for you. Maybe a little too sweet doe my liking, but it can always be touch and go. We ordered the shrimp cakes and spring rolls to start. The spring rolls were very large! Great potion size doe the price! I'd never had shrimp cakes before. I was thinking they might be crispy but they weren't - more of an omelette texture. My husband didn't like it but I thought it was tasty and an interesting texture. For the main course, I ordered the P6 Pho. Tripe, tendon, rare beef in a flavourful broth. It was delicious! The large is a little smaller than other places, but the price was right! I prefer my broth spicy and the server was happy to bring me out a little jar of chili oil. My husband ordered the beef on rice and he said was absolutely delicious and seemed to be a good sized portion. I will be back. A lot!

If you are looking for late night comfort food, than you have found it. My favorite place to go after a night out on the town. The fried chicken is soo good and even the mac and cheese is irresistible. I actually wasn't a fan of the mac and cheese originally as it is not very traditional. It is more like a mix of mac and cheese and chili which at first I thought was weird but now I have grown to love. I crave the biscuits as they are soft and buttery. The place can get very lively after midnight as it is a popular late night restaurant. The staff can be very sassy and not the most friendly at times but usually not that bad. The prices are also pretty reasonable and what you would for a place like this.

Went tonight for the first time. The staff were welcoming and gracious. The food was divine. I think the best pad Thai I have ever had. I love Thai food and this equaled the best I've ever had. Great spot, beautiful decor, fine and attentive staff.

Do you want to impress some out of town guests with your super hip vibe? This is the place for you. Also, the waitstaff are amazingly attractive. All of them. Even the chef was a bespeckled, handsome culinary magazine model, with that touch of wisdom-added gray flecks. You'll also be paying $22 for a small sandwich that is filled with a little bit of chicken but mostly french fries. Did you want a side of hummus? Not possible. Did you want a side of falafel? Not possible. But you can spend $18 for a plate that has some of what you wanted. We had the chicken sandwich and beet salad with falafel. The falafel was definitely the best part. The fries LOOK good, and taste lemony but all the food desperately needed salt to make the other spices come out. Dress in your hippest sideburns and tattoos and make a reservation, you'll be all set. If you want better food and don't need the price or the atmosphere, tried Saad's in West Philly.
I'm from Cali , plenty Thai food over there but here in Brandon ( fl) this is the best Thai restaurant around here ... the best . Great service great food

I really enjoyed the food here. I recommend the pork belly taco. Pork belly taco - served with some veggie in a sweet white bun (like the ones you eat with Peking duck). I highly recommend this. Bahn mi burger was good. Definitely worth a try. Lemon grass vermicelli was good. I wanted a bit meow vegetables in it. Kimchi burger was awesome. I got mine medium rare, it was really juicy and mixed really well with the kimchi. However, I thought the sweet potato fries were too salty.
I was in Tucson and made the mistake of eating here. I love Greek food and ordered what they said was Moussaka. burnt,dry and unrecognizable. This place should be closed.

The initial words that come to mind as my family and I dug into the Gobi Manchurian and the samosa chat was wow but not sure that was enough. You can tell this food was made the right way by someone who caters to the pallet. Everything we ordered was close to if not the best we have had and their curry tastes like it was home made........Make sure you save room for desert.......service was outstanding..........Well done gentlemen, my family and I will be back very soon.

Magical pickup wonders. Imagine being jasmine, on a Persian rug, flying through the currently soaking wet disgusting hair bashing low lying weather compartment, and picking up your meal in old city - suddenly hair don't care, wet don't sweat but food is THE MOOD. this place has bangin afghan food, especially for newcomers.

We don't explore South Grand often enough. Basil Spice is certainly one good reason to do so. I had Hang Ge-rhee with pork. Yellow curry paste, coconut milk - yum. Great spice not so much burn. My wife had Pad Khee-Mao. Very well composed. A little sweet for my taste, but she enjoyed it greatly. Both portions were adequate for a lunch. Service was efficient and friendly. The decor was clean and in keeping with cuisine

I was only in the Tampa area for 2 days or I would be here all the time. The food was great. The foule was delicious. I never heard of it before or had it before. I'm going to be making this at home soon. The fried cheese was excellent too. I ordered the tikka chicken. It was moist and flavorful. My friend had the baba ganoush sandwich and liked the smokiness of the eggplant. My only complaint was the pickled veggies they give you was too salty.

Good coffee. great pastries, best bagels and a terrific breakfast sandwich with turkey bacon. My friends from Israel were very impressed that the staff speaks Hebrew! La Va Cafe took an abandoned old corner in my neighborhood and turned it into a beautiful cafe that has helped transform South Street West. Recently I met a friend there who asked if he could afford lunch because it looks so pretty - he ended up paying for lunch. The art shows are always interesting with a young spirit.

I had the avocado crispy rice and the pickled fried okra. The rice was very good, though it could have had more rice; they were hard to find amongst the avo. It was enough food for me (a 120-lb light eater), but it seemed a small meal for many. The okra was exactly what it sounds like-- they opened a jar of pickled okra, dipped it in breading and fried it. Most of the breading fell off by the time it got to my mouth, so then i was just eating pickled okra. I like that, but i would hardly call it a "dinner" as they do on their menu.

This is the best Indian cuisine I have had in Indianapolis! Our server was extremely helpful and the food was beyond delicious!! We had the chicken makhan walla and lamb Rogan josh. Both were excellent. The onion kulcha bread was incredible as well. Highly recommend India Cafe!!!

What a Great new discovery in Reno. I was looking for some delicious Asian noodle soup for late lunch. The two different types of noodles we ordered were simply delectable. The staffs were friendly and kind too. Highly recommend for anyone.

I live in Clarksville and I drive 45 minutes to this restaurant almost once a week just to cure my pho cravings. They only take CASH, so make sure you have paper money with you. Let me just tell you why this place is worth my gas and time EVERY week I go there. 1. Their pho thai is $5 for a large bowl. Who can beat that price?! Their eggrolls are like $2. Their big vermicelli noodle bowls with marinated meat is like $6. Yes, I usually order all 3 just for myself haha! 2. You would think their price is so low because maybe they don't get a lot of business?! Nah, they are usually very busy (have slow days just like every restaurant) with many new customers waiting to get their food to see what all the Yelpers are yelping about haha! For the cheap price of their meals, THEY HAVE AMAZINGLY AUTHENTIC FOOD. I had pho in so many different areas, states, cities, and this place is by far my favorite. If you are new to this restaurant, my tip to you is to seat yourself (because I see new people with their blank faces standing by the door waiting for someone to come out and seat them but sometimes that doesn't happen lol). Do not expect outstanding service but DO expect delicious, affordable, authentic food. Happy eating!!!
Considering we really haven't eaten at any other Thai reaturant for quite a while in brandon should speak for itself. haven't been dissapointed so far.

Great first experience here. A lot of the fun comes from sharing everything, and scooping up the food with the delicious spongy sour flatbread. The people in our party took to it pretty quickly, though the honey wine may have helped lubricate the awkward learning process. I was glad to see the place busy but not crowded on a saturday night, though I don't completely understand how the owner was able to run the whole place on her own. Given that it was a one-woman show, service was reasonably prompt, and the food was wonderful. Of the vegetarian options I tried, the Mesir Wat and Kik Alicha were best, very flavorful but not too heavily spiced. Next time, I'll try the Shiro.

I have been to this place countless times, and I still can't seem to get enough. I have tried many things on the menu and I have NEVER been disappointed. The atmosphere itself is perfect. It is very modern inside with a nice looking bar and plenty of seating, but I often choose to sit on the patio and enjoy the sunshine. For a drink, I never stray away from their White Peach Sangria. It is AMAZING! I've even tried recreating it at home because I love it THAT much. My interpretation is pretty close if I do say so myself. Now for the food! The thing I love the most is that Pita Jungle uses fresh ingredients, refrains from making your dish unhealthy AND posts all of the nutrition information on their website. For an appetizer, my favorite has to be the Gambas con Aho. This is five large shrimp sauteed in a delicious garlic tomato sauce served with warm pita triangles with pesto and melted cheese on top. I swear we lick the plate clean every time! My top three entrees would have to be the veggie wrap that they have on their special menu which I've ordered about 10000 times, the Grilled vegetable salad (asked them to go light on the oil!) and the Glazed Chicken Lavosh Pizza. Seriously, everything is FANTASTIC. I can't wait to come back again. Not to mention, our service is always friendly and fast. I've truly never had a bad experience and I hope I never do. =)

Average food! There is some sort of animosity from Lao owners toward Thai people? After learning we are Thai the service went through the floor. Waitress took our order then didn't see her again until time to leave! Tiger tear was below average. Nothing special here!
This place is fantastic. The people who work there are accommodating and great to chat with. The pho is delicious and affordable. Highly recommended!!!

Lovely place! Great friendly service and lots of options for food (breakfast all day, sandwiches, wraps, smoothies, and soups). I had the grilled cheese and strawberry/peach/pineapple smoothie and loved all of it:) price is right too

Really small joint with excellent Indian food. Authentic music playing at a pleasant volume with extremely friendly staff. This place wasn't super busy so expect to get seated fairly quickly. Good price and large portions of wonderfully flavorful food!
Food was great! The tenders were perfectly seasoned. Not too salty or too breaded the organic soda was also interesting

I really enjoy the food here. The prices weren't too bad for fresh food. If you are addicted to pho, like me, please give this place a try. The broth was so flavorful that I did not need the usual array of sauces (which this place does lack). My only complaint is the location as I am not a fan of strip mall joints. Great chicken wings, outstanding Spring and Summer rolls, plus a damn good jasmine tea. It's worth a visit if you're in the area and would like to try something new.

I really hate leaving bad reviews. We used to be regulars at this place prior to the change and we're very excited to try it out. Sadly for us we had a very terrible experience here tonight. The service was beyond slow. We watched people get up and walk out and we should have taken that as a hint. We then watched a couple wait about 30 minutes for their check and then they even had to get up to get a pen in order to sign the check. We pressed on and ordered an appetizer which was calamari. There were exactly nine rings. That doesn't seem like a whole lot of calamari for the price. My husband ordered Pad Thai and my mother ordered curry chicken. I ordered the lime prawns. While the presentation it was very nice what they neglect to tell you is that they bread the entire shrimp with the head and legs still attached....shell and all. When you pull the heads and the legs off of the shrimp you obviously get the shrimp guts still left inside. Honestly, that's not very appealing unless you're partial to eating shrimp guts in which case you will love this dish LOL. I was too disgusted to eat it so the waitress said that she was very sorry and wanted me to have a good experience so she offered to replace my meal. She asked me what I would like in place of the prawns. Honestly, I was ready to just go at that point as we had been sitting for 45 minutes without our food. I agreed to chicken Pad Thai. Instead, I got shrimp pad thai and my party was already done eating so I just boxed it to take it home. We waited about another 15 minutes or so to get the check even though I asked for it when the shrimp pad thai arrived. They were kind enough to not charge for the shrimp pad thai or the prawns with lime. The only reason why this is getting two stars it's because they did try to fix the issue however due to the slow service and the very small portions of appetizers we will not be back here.

First time ever at an Indian restaurant so the 10 dollar lunch buffet was a great place to get acclimated. That said, I thought they could have had a larger spread. An extra dish or two would have been nice, but it's 10 bucks so can't really complain there. Every dish I had was very good except the tandoori chicken was a bit dry which is to be expected at a buffet since its not sitting in sauce like the other dishes. The lamb dish and chicken tikka were excellent and the rice was flavorful and not dry. There were these potato and veggie balls were very good too. Rice pudding and honey ball desert was nice too. And the best part was the hot and fresh naan bread to dunk in the sauces. Service was excellent. They don't bother you, but are constantly walking around clearing plates which is exactly what you want at a buffet. Also, leaving a pitcher of water at the table is key instead of having to wait for someone to fill you up every time. I can't speak for authenticity or how it compares to other places, but I enjoyed my meal and will be back again. Not sure I would go when it's not a buffet, but I'm sure their main courses are very good. Oh and no immediate bathroom trip afterwards either!!!

This place would not make it in most major cities with superior restaurants. To start off the layout is very strange with too much room dedicated to open kitchen in a warehouse type atmosphere. The cooks should focus on cooking and not performing. Many tables are communal style with just a few booths or very small tables for 2. Our group of 4 was initially seated at a table right by the kitchen entrance and near a prep area with food heat lamps. We asked to be moved to one of 3 empty booths and were given dirty looks and guff about the booths being intended for 5 and that they had other reservations. They condescended after our insistence to move and emphasizing that we also had reservations and were on time. Not a good start. A hipster couple with 2 small kids were in one booth. Guess we weren't young and hip enough. Then we ordered drinks. Wine pours were super small and we insisted on more. We received a few drops more. Pathetic pours. One member of our party sent his cocktail back because it was undrinkable. When we ordered we were told our food would come out at different times which it did, thereby making some in our party wait while others ate or let their food get cold while they waited for the others food to come out. This is meant to be hip cooking I guess, but it's just laziness really to not time things properly in the kitchen so that it comes out at the same time. Our food was super salty and served in tiny little serving pots. The Brussel sprout appetizer tasted like they had cheese wiz on them and had virtually no sauerkraut as described. In fact none of the dishes looked as described on the menu. My wife sent her steak tartare back because it had some fried substance on top. Pretty hard to mess up classic tartare. Service was poor, and the food was simply too salty and not very tasty for the most part. The braised lamb and couscous was OK but still pretty salty and more couscous than anything.
