If you want to hang out with the tattooed hipster crowd, go. However if you want fine dining and good food, go somewhere else. Nashville still needs culinary help. We need less trendy stuff and less farm to table or "elevated" southern type food, and instead just finely prepared and creative food in a more luxurious atmosphere.

The Chaat is the BEST. I'm sure the other food is delicious, but I love their chaat so much that I can't help but order it every time. Veggie samosas are dope too. Love the staff. Hard not to eat there every day.

I found a bug in my food and water I pointed it out to the waiters and they told me sometimes that just happens they can't control their bug problem. Stay far away from this place. They then had the nerve to give us the full bill with no compensation for us finding the bug. I will not be visiting again!

Very good food, freshly made, with some unique dishes I've never eaten before. This place is small, usually packed with people, and it's clear that it's family owned and operated. All good signs. I've had a number of different entrees and they're all delicious. Sometimes the curry can be a little watery for takeout, but usually it's not. I'd recommend anything stir fry (even if it sounds like there's too many vegetables, it's still very good!), and the pad woonsen is very flavorful.

It doesn't get much better then Olio when it comes to hand crafted specialty cocktails. It still amazes me that this cool, relaxing little bar is a renovated 1930's gas station. I wish Edward Hopper was alive today, because I'd love to see his vision of this classy bar. It would be so cool to see myself and Norm H. enjoying one of the amazing drinks made by our favorite mixologist John. I just call my vodka and let John create whatever he thinks I'll enjoy and he has never led me wrong. Sitting at the bar and watching the bartenders mix, shake and serve up cocktails is like watching the Food Network for booze live. The music provided by a turntable playing vintage vinyl records, adds to the magical atmosphere. One of my favorite treats to enjoy while sipping my cocktail is the Egg Salad. Be sure to add the white anchovies for an additional $3, it is totally worth it. That salty little fish, adds a boost of flavor to the creamy egg salad. I so want this in my lunch sack for work. Happy Hour or late night drinks, Olio is the place to be seen and enjoy. It is good for romantic couples or groups of friends out for fun. Hope to see you the next time I'm at Olio.
Delicious! Highly recommend the Spicy Beef Pho. The broth is different from the others and has a great flavor.

I wish there were more options on the menu. I ordered naan, sat down, opened the foil, and it was pita bread they just warmed up. When I asked about it, he told me all they had was pita bread (not sure if he meant all the time or just today). If that's the case, then naan and pita bread shouldn't both be on the menu, and I should have been informed when I ordered the naan that they only had pita bread because they are two very different things. The mango lassi didn't really taste like mango. The chicken tikka masala wasn't bad, but also wasn't great. The portion was also very small for $9, and then I still had to pay extra for the "naan" on the side. I only got a few chunks of chicken and a bunch of rice, and ended up throwing out the whole pita bread because that's not even what I ordered.
We had the combination bowl with vermicelli and the pork and shrimp with fried rice. Everything was super fresh and delicious. The restaurant is clean and the service was excellent!!
Dosas were okay, though I thought they were lacking a bit in the amount of filling. I'd like to come back and try out their other dishes; it looked like a great menu.

Great place to take out the family while grabbing a beer or a glass of wine. Hip and chic without the price tag. And who doesn't like Chinese food. Ok, so it's not "authentic" Chinese but the food is very good nevertheless. The service is consistent and the ambiance is memorable.

Thought the service was great and the atmoshere was warm and cozy, listening to soft guitar while eating was a definite plus.The food was very good as well however not quite worth our 123$ bill 150 $ with tip. we took our 9 yr old daughter and there really wasnt much for her however the waiter did mention they would be willing to make a pasta just for her ...she opted for the soup du jour and to sample our food...she really loved the escargot appetizer.Overall it was an enjoyable evening
Wonderful and fresh Mediterranean. Food. Loved it. My new favorite place!!! The staff were very nice and gave great service!! Baklava was awesome!!
Had an amazing salmon salad and mezza platter! The service was excellent and the food was delicious.

AMAZING. EAT HERE, NOW! We saw this place on yelp and decided to give it a try. Fantastic experience. Friendly, prompt service. The food was perfect. Imaginative, well spiced, generous portions and all around excellent flavor. We will definitely come here again!

Tried the vegetarian hoagie here today. At $3.75 it was fine, but nothing special. I found the fillings (the veggies especially) a bit paltry and completely bereft of jalapeños, so I don't know if you have to request it spicy or something. In a fight, the tofu hoagie at Fu Wah would totally beat Nhu Y's to a bean-curdy pulp. Too bad, I love bahn mi and am always open to finding a delicious new place. Maybe their meat hoagies are better?

Finally went back after a three year hiatus. I know that certain Dishes here aren't good so I avoid getting the pho or the rare Vietnamese dishes that nobody really orders. Their best dishes are grilled or sautéed. My favorite is the grilled pork with rice. No other Vietnamese restaurant grills their pork so at Saigon you get this unique smoky flavor that you can't get anywhere else. It is marinated with a unique Vietnamese seasoning and served with eggs, pork meat loaf, and pickled vegetables. It is a little pricy so my favorite here is the lunch special for $7 which gives you a dry dish along with a soup and a Vietnamese spring roll. My favorite is Pad Thai!

Quick , tasty, cheap pho! Lots of options, all the authentic add-ins. I haven't yet tried the bahn mi, but soon.... Clean diner type setting. The single server, waiter, head of house (owner?) is very nice. I've heard him explaining dishes (no, he's not Vietnamese). I last tried the bubble tea last year--it was ok, but not the best. But I'll definitely be back.

It's hard for me to find anything I didn't like about this restaurant. I am prone to veggie options my hubby is a serious carnivore - we were both quite happy with our orders. In fact we ordered extra so we had lunch for the following day. We also had a hard time deciding on a meal so we kind of had a couple each. Some of the better hummus I've tasted, really nice lemony fresh taste and milky smooth texture. Pizza was a thick crispy crust loaded with toppings. Mediterranean salad with chicken skewer was the right mix of veggies and not too heavy dressing. The Caesar salad with shrimp skewer way fresh and crisp greens and lightly dressed. Lovely, cozy warm atmosphere. Interesting wine/liquor room as a focal point of the dining area. Service was friendly and professional.

Went in the summer during lunch time for the buffet. It was pretty warm in there not sure if their AC was broken or if they even have it. The food was good, I enjoyed that. However the waiter hardly ever made it over to our table to refill drinks the whole time we were there. I'll give it another try though to see if it changes, based on other reviews of this place.

Love this place! One of my favorites so far are the Scallion dumplings, lovely raviolis stuffed lightly with scallions in a delightfully light tomato meat sauce. It's drizzled with yogurt. I liked it so much on my second visit I got the entree size, and honestly would have licked my plate if there were no other diners there! Also of note, the vegetarian entrees - cauliflower and the eggplant. Their kabobs are nicely cooked and still juicy - not dried out like some other places. It's a BYOB and most dishes are under $15, so you can order to your hearts content and still go home with some $$ in your pocket
Just eat whatever he gives you. If you can't go every day...go at least once. Don't be scared off by a line...that just means its worth it.

Let me say straight up that I am extremely picky about my Middle Eastern food (well, let's be frank, I am extremely picky about ALL food). I am not a fan of shawarma or doner kebab, and that is what this place specializes in: doner kebab. They basically mound "mystery" cuts of meat onto a spit and slice it and make a sandwich out of it. The spit of meat looks basically like Greek gyro meat but here they slice it thinner. They have lamb or chicken. However, my idea of good kebab is not this "mystery meat" on a spit, with all due respect to the Turkish people. My idea of good kebab is fresh, IDENTIFIABLE chunks of marinated chicken, beef, lamb or pork, roasted over a fire and served with rice and/or bread. Slices of mystery meat is not my thing, so I can't give this place a rave review. However, if you are from Turkey or Germany or other parts of Europe where this mystery meat thing is popular, you will likely love this place. It's clean, the toppings are very fresh, the people are very nice, etc. Hey, at least we have a doner kebab place in Tampa Bay. I have to give them 2 stars just for injecting some culture into our region.

This used to be a good Indian restaurant, with an excellent buffet. Since their renovation and new management, they have really gone downhill. The food is okay, although there is less variety on the buffet than there used to be. The service is awful! I have been sitting here for twenty minutes waiting for my check. The staff never brought us drink refills, never came back to the table after we were seated and given our initial drink order. They are mostly concerned with talking to and waiting on their friends/family. It is terrible. Go elsewhere, unless you have plenty of time to be completely ignored!

This had to be the fastest service, outside of fast food joints, I have ever had. The employees, who are probably all family, were polite and quick. Definitely on top of their game. The place was clean and inviting with nice decor. I didn't visit the restroom in this visit so can't say about that. The food was excellent. I had the Thai fried dumplings and the Noodles with Basil (aka Drunken Noodles) and they both were delicious. I will definitely be coming back.

This place is a wonderful hearty fast food alternative to its fast-food-giant neighbor Chipotle (which I also love for their value). I have only had the hummus bowls with either falafel or chicken and I greatly enjoy both. I always get all of the toppings available because the flavors that amass on the resultant pile of deliciousness are vast, original, and vibrant. All their Mediterranean toppings are fantastic - I promise you (so long as you don't have dietary restrictions nor picky eating habits). Come give them a shot. The pricing is more between 7 and 10 dollars. Overall perhaps 50 cents to a dollar more on average than Chipotle but the food is just as filling and id argue more flavorful! Definitely worth checking out.

Zen Yai is our favorite place in town! The freshest real Thai veggies and the most pleasant service can be found here every time, and doesn't hurt that the two owners are always there keeping an eye on the place. They are two sisters, one in the kitchen and one on the floor. Their staff is like family and are some of the most hard working girls I've ever met!!
Mango chicken was delicious. Veggie tempura was on point. Thai fried rice was poppin'

We stopped in for lunch and were wowed. It's a cute little place, with crisp blue & white decor. It's simple, but the food is simply sensational. I had shakshuka, a hot mix of tomatoes, peppers, onions, eggs with some great lamb sausages, all served with an ample supply of pita. My husband loved every bite of his lamb gyro. Service was warm and friendly, and even though only one guy was handling the room he was always there when I needed him. The area's food scene is getting better and better, and BLU is our best find yet. We seriously talked about the meal a bunch of times. We'll be back.

Finally a kids menu geared towards kids with healthy options. Greasy kids food has its place but my children enjoy fresh veggies and grilled proteins, with minimal grease, options that are far too rare on most kids menus. The waitress even happily cut my daughter's juice with water as asked without making a face like most waitstaff does when I request this. We dined a little past 5 pm and enjoyed the happy hour menu, particularly $5 wines. We ordered the hummus trio and baba ganoush plate and I was a bit surprised at how stingy they were with the pita. We dined with our three children and there wasn't even enough pita for each of us to have a triangle. We asked for more and were told it was $.39 a pita. Fine, but that all seemed cheap to me. But the food was fresh and delicious and definitely plan on returning.
Just an Ok store front meal. The crispy rotisserie chicken tasted par boiled and then put on the grill, it was anything but crispy or juicy.
Best Thai food around! Having lived in Thailand for a number of years, I can absolutely vouch for it's authenticity! Amazing food and amazing Thai hospitality! I feel at home every time I visit!

I'm a fan! I came for lunch and wanted to have it to-go. Although it's a lunch buffet they allow you to do take-out for $8.99. There's a decent amount of choices for the lunch buffet and they had all my favorites -- chana masala, chicken tikka masala, and spinach paneer. They also bring you warm naan! Def worth it to go for lunch
Great food, Fast and clean , read all the reviews and was well worth a try.

I was really excited about visiting this restaurant. As others have said, the service was very slow. I ordered the beef cubes, only to be told five minutes later they don't have any. Not the end of the world. I ordered the Pho. The sideplate came out with only one stallk of basil leaves. Again, not the end of the world and I'm sure if I had asked for more it would have been provided. The broth itself was exquisite. However,it was a little light on the meat. That is unacceptable! It was almost impossible to get my waitresses attention. There's also a serious language issue. And as others have mentioned, my water glass remained unfilled throughout the course of my visit. I'll wait a month and give it another try.

I am from Little Saigon, where there is a pho restaurant on every corner of every block. After moving to Indy I desperately looked for a pho restaurant that could satisfy my weekly cravings. After trying Indy's pho at Pho 36, King Wok, and Saigon Restaurant and walking away disappointed, I found this little restaurant on Yelp. The soup was herby, full, and flavorful (unlike Pho 36) with not too much MSG (unlike Saigon Restaurant). The portion was filling (again unlike Saigon Restaurant).

I love Naf Naf! For the convenience, it's amazing. Sure, there are better Mediterranean restaurants in the area, but not as quick and easy as here. I usually do a hummus bowl with chicken, maybe some falafel and then mix and match the different toppings and sauces. It's quick, not TOO unhealthy and very delicious. I wish I worked a little closer so I could come here for lunch more often! Staff are always very friendly, too.

She serve me a soft Sandwich this morning. Terrible! Normally she would put the bread on oven to heat it up and make it crispy. But definitely not today, not for me. And there is not much people there in the line, so basically she is not that busy. But still. Terrible sandwich I have ever had. I will never ever buy sandwich there anymore!

This place is definitely bigger than it appears on the outside. I often walked by here and never went in thinking it was a carry-out place with some seats, but there are two large back rooms. It is definitely one of those awesome family-run places with awesome food and not a lot of "show". I took my friend here because she is taking a trip to Greece next month, and found our new favorite neighborhood BYO. We started with the Zeus appetizer, which could easily be a meal in itself if you want to try a little of everything. The grilled octopus was phenomenal and the sauce was so good, I had to use the crusty bread to sop it up. I also highly recommend the stuffed eggplant. I have never tasted anything so good and will definitely be ordering it again! Overall, great food, inexpensive, no frills neighborhood gem!

I happened to be in the area and decided to try out this restaurant for a quick lunch. Reviews on Yelp were mixed on food quality but consistent on service quality. I hesitated to try but needed to get back to the office so I decided to give it a try. Well, this appears to be a classic family run restaurant. Service was not what I would expect in Canada, but consistent with my experiences having meals at similar places in Asia. Do not expect hellos on your way in, prompt checking in, and even the simpler things like having your meal placed out in front of you by the waiter - they just silently slide it on the side of the table for you to reposition all on your own. I'm less fussed about these things and was more interested in the quality of the food. How was it? Well, bland. Flavourless pho with very skimpy meat portions along with very dry and tasteless spring rolls. A disappointment. I probably won't come back given the many other Vietnamese options in St. Albert.
Great food and service!! Thank you for the great time and stopping by to check on things Mohammed! Try ANYTHING!!

My two stars are for the service -- very nice and accommodating. However the bathroom and area just before the bathroom (which looks like a play area for the workers' children) are really too gross. My husband almost couldn't eat imagining what the kitchen may look like. Both my husband's Pho and mine (different types) were surprisingly lacking in flavor. I had to add outrageous amounts of soy sauce and chili sauce to eat mine, and I'm a Pho lover. I can't bear to go back.

So yummy! FYI the pitas are deceptive, they look small but they're very dense and filling. The staff greeted us and talked us through the menu since it was our first time visiting. Will definitely go back!

They have the best pho in town! Went to the Lilly's pho place at first but it was closed on Sunday. And ended up here, which is better than Lilly's! The flavor is original, the service is good, and the way they serve coffee is creative and fun. I've been to at least 20+ pho restaurants, this one definitely one of the best.

I had a good first time experience here after the place being recommended by a friend. However, we only went for drinks. They have specialty drinks and a good selection of craft beer. I was in the mood for an Irish coffee and although it wasn't on the menu, the bartender made one for me anyway. He was very friendly and attentive. The atmosphere is "upscale" which isn't really my style, but I liked the experience here and would be willing to try the place again.
The best Bánh Mì in Santa Barbara. One of the best in southern Cali. I always order less meat but more đ chua (Vegie and Pickes).
I went here with my husband and daughter a month or so ago. The food was okay but I was not blown away by anything we had. The service was also a bit slow.

Not a bad place to get a burger. 8th and Union (named after its location, 801 North Union Street) prides itself on tons of gluten-free food, which I couldn't care less about considering I can eat gluten and it's perfectly safe; and vegan food. While my brother would get excited about the dairy and meat free options, I opted for a cheeseburger; comprised of my two favorite things: meat and dairy. The burger was great. It had bacon and caramelized onions on it. If that doesn't sound delicious, you're probably either my brother or a nutritionist. The fries were hand-cut, and probably the best fries of my life. The atmosphere was a mix of cozy and bar-type. The outdoor section looked cool but we ate inside. The only thing holding this jawn back from 5 stars was the spotty service when the place was empty. Our waiter was nice enough, but he looked like he has spent too much time in bathrooms- and not because of an upset stomach. Whatever the reason, we didn't see him enough. I really liked 8th and Union and will be back when I'm hungry in Little Italy.

So the bf wanted something different so he suggested Taste of India and I must say I was not disappointed. We went on a Saturday evening and were seated right away. He ordered the chicken tikka marsala with a side of naan and I ordered the lamb tikka marsala with a side of naan. Our food arrived in a reasonable time and our server was very nice. My only complaint is I wish I had a bit more lamb, his chicken was overflowing where my lamb only had a few pieces. I'm assuming because it is more expensive but I feel that the extra cost for it should makeup for that. Either way I enjoyed my experience and would come again ! Perhaps for the lunch buffet

Flawless in my opinion. Delicious, flavorful food obviously cooked with love and pride. Service was top notch. We got the chicken curry, jerk chicken, and yummy fruity drinks. Great experience in a fun atmosphere!

A dining experience comes together like a classic recipe - chances are if you're like me, food is never the only reason you dine out. You want to savor the experience. Especially true for ethnic cuisine, you open your mind to ways you never knew existed and redefine the norm. Marrakesh takes a leaf straight out of the Arabian nights to give you a truly exotic culinary experience. A set 7 course meal is guaranteed to give you a plethora of options, some you may immediately take to, some you may not. (personally, powdered sugar on meat wouldn't have been my first choice. different strokes for different folks) Go there on a weekend when there is a live belly dancer. Be prepared for a long evening and pace yourself. Go there with friends and celebrate. Take a date (ok maybe not the first) and reminisce the experience. Stock up your wallet; it's cash only. More of a 3.5 really. I'm rounding this one up.

Zorbas is a fun little Greek paradise on the food-desert known as Fairmount (I kid...we're getting better...). If you're a vegetarian, carnivore or omnivore, you're sure to find something appetizing here. The cold appetizer plate is small-ish, but loaded with different Greek delights including, hummus, other hummus, yogurt hummus type of thing, babaganoush and spicy feta, which looks like all of the other stuff on the plate, but is spicy and wonderful. The hot appetizer comes with calamari that is more scrumptious than any onion ring you'll ever eat. It actually tastes like calamari...that's been breaded...not breaded that's been calamaried. There's some octopus dip too, but the tentacles were a little much for me...now that I want an octopus as a pet. Order two pitas - fluffy, light and warm, these are absolutely the quintessence of Greek pita. And the artichoke dish for a main course will make you feel healthy and guilty at the same time...smothered in some sort of butter sauce that's lemony, these hearts will win you over. Oh, and share a piece of giant baklava. It's pretty huge, and sticky, and flakey, and everything that baklava should be.

I love the service of this place, they were very friendly. However, their food was kinda bland. It wasn't spicy and made me feel full but unfulfilled with what I ate. The place made me feel empty, although, the servers were kind I wasn't a huge fan of their food. I recommend other places for Vietnamese cuisine.

Wow, now we can enjoy excellent Vietnamese food without having to drive down to Washington Ave. Loved the vermicelli... The pork and chicken were so nicely flavored and the portion was monstruous. As a suggestion, though, I enjoyed the summer rolls on two occasions so far and would prefer a thicker more peanutty sauce if that is at all possible! Thanks.

This is my Carmel friends' favorite Indian restaurant. (I haven't checked to see how many Indian restaurants there actually are in Carmel) It's in a strip mall, but that's Indy. The ambiance is generic, but that's most Indian restaurants in the U.S. What matters is, the food is good. My carnivorous friend raves about the meat selection, which apparently is wider than in other Indian restaurants. And for those who can't spare a minute away from a game, they have a TV so you can have some football with your chana masala.
The best Pho in the area. Very flavorful hearty broth with all the right fixings. Their grilled shrimp pho is great Bc it is grilled as opposed to boiled in the soup.

Dinner was incredible! Started with the calamari & chorizo appetizer. Had the Brazilian shrimp entree, it was a bit spicy which made it even better!!! Then finished with a Tres Leches dessert. Oh yeah, had two margaritas... They were delicious & smooth. I enjoyed the ambiance & service.

Being SE Asian and eating pho my entire life, I was extremely disappointed at the pho restaurants in Reno. Until we discovered this little gem. Their broth is on point! The bean sprouts were fresh unlike what we found at pho 777. The service isn't great but what pho restaurant has exceptional service? The authentic taste makes up for it. Sure it's attached to a gas station but I still highly recommend this restaurant. We found this place by accident and we will be back!

So happy one of these popped up in Center City! This location is set up fast-casual style, so you order from a kiosk then pick up your food at the counter. The restaurant is huge and clean with plenty of seating, and food comes out quickly even during the lunch rush. My boyfriend and I like to meet here for lunch during the work week, and we'll split a bowl of tofu pho and a vermicelli bowl with pork. The portions are huge and reasonably-priced (roughly $22 for both) and we always leave stuffed and happy.

The food is very tasty! Very fresh! Arguably the best Indian food in Pinellas County. The service is courteous and the staff is very good. The restaurant was very clean and nicely set. The only drawback was the food did not come out in a timely manner. One entree came out much earlier than the other one-at least 10-15 minutes earlier. For such a nice place, that really was unacceptable. We will definitely be coming back because the flavor of the food was so great but we hope they have fixed the time issue and have all of the items offered (they were out of lamb).

Excellent place to relax and enjoy a drink and small app. I've trusted the drink experts to guide me to uncharted tastes for me. I've not had a bad choice yet. It is very comforting to find a place where you can relax and explore. Have a few drinks then head up stairs for an awesome meal.
The hookah flavors tasted great and lasted for a long time. The service was kind of shitty at times but everything worked out. I had a great time here.

By far the cheapest Indian take-out I've found in my travels. $7.50 for Paneer Masala, Garlic Naan, and rice (including tax)? Sign this girl up. Like the other reviews, it's middle of the road as far as quality. It's great for what I needed it for: a night in with no frills. I appreciated the vegetarian options, although I'm not a strict vegetarian, simply because I wasn't pigeonholed into getting the typical chicken. It was expediently made, and that's more than I can say for most places with such a cheap menu, but the masala was really watery and super safe as far as spices go. The naan was definitely microwaved. Don't expect all of the lesser-known dishes, but you can count on the old favorites. All in all, it's a great place to visit if you're looking for cuisine that's quick and yummy (think fast-food Indian), but maybe not if you're looking for traditional, homestyle Indian.

business_name: OPA! of Greece West Edmonton Mall - A
text: I have to agree with the previous review. This Opa is one of the best in town. It's really strange how a franchise can differ depending on what spot you go to. Personally I enjoy them all but this one is the best I think. The food tastes the best and seems like it's prepared the best as well. I always get the #1 with chicken and they load everything on. The plate is usually overflowing with potatoes, chicken, pita, vegetables and rice. It's almost too much food. I have trouble avoiding it whenever I go to West Ed.

Solid Indian buffet located very conveniently to many working in the Wayne / KoP area. I have been here twice and both times have been pleased with the quality and taste of the food. The Naan is excellent, as well as many of the chicken and vegetable dishes. Very good flavors. The service is a little bit of a drop off considering that there is usually 1 person refilling water and oftentimes they do not even fill the glass to the top. I appreciate a nice amount of refills, especially when eating spicy food. That being said, I don't think they have much of a reason to change anything as the place is typically packed to the gills. If the service was a bit better, I would give it more stars.

So glad this family decided to get back into the restaurant business again and open SF Kitchen. The pho is great. The Vietnamese egg rolls are perfectly crispy like they are suppose to be. There are so many good dishes to list. My favorite would have to be the Asian beef stew (hotpot). The place is clean and decorated nicely. Plenty of parking. The staff and owners are very nice.

I used to live near Grand in St. Louis and frequented many of the thai restaurants, however, Thai House is above and beyond better than anywhere I've eaten in St. Louis. The inside is nothing fancy so don't judge the book by it's cover. The pad thai is one of the best I've had. Great for takeout, too.

My favorite Thai food in the area. I've eaten here several times with different groups of people and it's always good. I love that it's BYO. I also really like the easy parking; much better than trying to park in downtown Phoenixville.

Eggplant and okra on the lunch buffet at the same time! They were both delicious. The paneer tikka masala was good too. On the chilled side they had a cold potato chaat salad with a tamarind sauce I'd never tried before, it was yummy. This is a great place for a veg lunch or dinner. On the weekends they serve Indo-Chinese and South Indian chaat for the dinner buffet. I will definitely go back for that.

I had to try their lamb gyro plate. After having strips of lamb served at another Mediterranean place, the julienned lamb was too perfectly cut to me. I personally don't care if my meat is shaved or not. But it was delicious. I especially loved the rice. Rice is usually very bland, but their version was a stand out. The salad came on a very thin paper plate. Thankfully, it wasn't heavily laden with too many olives and peppers. The salad was lightly dressed, which I appreciated. The meat to rice ratio was more than I expected. I was using the pita bread as a sandwich maker when I ran out of rice. I was hoping to try the cheesecake, but because they asked me to pay after my meal, I kind of forgot about getting a slice. Not entirely sure if what I heard the workers speaking was Greek or some other Mediterranean language, but it sure lent some authenticity.

Chipotle style Mediterranean which is a killer idea. The chicken shwarma was delish but if you want a SPECTACULAR pita, head down the road to Kabab Cafe. It's the absolute best, not just on the main line but in the greater Philly area

Joy cafe is one of those great little secrets in St Pete. The woman who works there is super nice and the food is all very reasonably priced with great flavor! Definitely worth a try, because once you try it you'll want to come back again

A cute Thai place with lots of unique energy and character. It was packed and the hostess said it wasn't unusual. We got the veggie pad Thai (with original green bean noodles I never had anywhere else - really nice texture) and the curry of the day (green) which was as spicy as they promised. Our sinuses are clear! We'll be hitting the gong by the door on our way out to tell the chefs how yummy the food was.
I love this place. I love the lobster mac n chesse and peach bread pudding. Drink specials are awesome and service is second to none.
Awesome lunch buffet every day - but wish it had more meat dishes. Menu has all the expected dishes and the sauces are tastier than the buffet. Place is always busy.

The reviewes are all true:)!!! We listened and went to mood cafe. It was simply one of the most amazing things we've ever eaten. First, the owner is delightful, takes pride in his cooking, and really and truly wants to ensure you have an amazing dinner. He asked if it was our first visit, it was.. And even our first time having Indian food. We luv middle eastern food, but wanted to try Indian, so we turned to yelp. They listed mood cafe#1. And not your usual reviews....over the top incredible reviews!!! We had to go and try. The food was amazing by itself, so yummy.... But the owner makes the experience. You feel like he's cooking just for you, home cooking, and what he puts together is heaven on a fork(or spoon) My husbnd had beef chaat, I had. Chicken chaat. And there were lots of things in it with a delicious sauce(s). We each ordered lassies, and ofcourse never had those either. We understand some enjoy them salty? But we ordered a coconut lassie, and a pineapple lassie, creamy.. Light... Cool. Think it's yogurt and milk really? But to us, better than a traditional smoothie. We will be coming back, and recommend this place to everyone.... Especially if your in a mood for something? But don't know what it is? Lol.... Apparently you want chaat!!!! You just don't know it yet:))) A definite 5 stars, but we'd give it more if we could. The owner is a class act, and it isn't every day you come across that type of warmth and hospitality. He's charming and cares that his customers ate happy!!! Oh, and dessert was on the house:)!!!!!! Go there, you'll be SOOOOOOO happy you did!

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: It's easy to overlook this place because your eyes are most likely searching for the St. Pete pier, or Jannus Landing, or some bar... the dark wood exterior doesn't demand attention unlike other Thai places in the Bay. But inside, it's like a competition of different visual styles that doesn't seem to work well. There's two rooms, and I've never seen anyone in the side room--always the area with the sushi bar. This place is run by young'uns--and it shows in the sushi. Nah, I'm not bashing on the flavor--it's good (but I've had better elsewhere). The fishy flavor I want in my sushi was covered up... but there was a Thai noodle salad with shrimp and pork that I've never had elsewhere--and it was simple but delicious! Prices were typical for a sushi restaurant. Also with Asian young'uns running a restaurant, they were ALL BUSINESS! Always brisk, running around... not too friendly... but very attentive. What's with the artwork inside? You see the serious wood/green suddenly pushed against a modern art wall with cube paintings... did I mention the bathroom? It was a psychedelic trip into an orange galaxy of orange lava. I'm sure some lucky cousin was asked to paint the murals, but it didn't fit the casual business atmosphere of the menu and servers.
I wish every restaurant was like this one. Great food, friendly prompt service. Reasonable prices. What a Gem!

The Thai tea was amazing, I think that's the only compliment that I will be able to give. was craving Thai but the food was bland. I asked for extra spicy and was very disappointed. don't think i will be ordering from here again

Happy to see spots like this in my old hood. We only waited about 10 minutes for a table, and that was just enough time to grab a margarita (good tequila, but a tad sweet for my liking). After being seated, we started with the harvest salad which included seasonal grilled veggies and fruit accompanied by a herb goat cheese mousse;he split plate was more than enough for two. Our entrees included the shrimp mofongo and carnitas tacos, both of which were cooked perfectly and full of flavor. We were so full we skipped dessert, so will definitely return.

fantastic food, don't let the mundane look of the mini strip mall bother you. Once inside a quaint & contemporary décor awaits and the food is very tasty . Lunch combos are small but they happily made me a little extra . Don't skip the Lamb Rogan Josh and the Goat Curry.

I recently moved to Florida and I miss this spot so much. The best Dominican restaurant in philly hands down. I use to drive about an hour and a half just for their food! The prices are great, love the atmosphere ,and the owners always gives a warm welcome.

Location is really convenient for people living in grad hospital to stop by for some caffeine and a bite. Offers more than your usual cafe, with a more ethnic spin. My favorite pastry are the savory burekos. Coffee is decent too. Cozy workspaces.
Food is great service is great! You must try this place if you're in Carp. This is also our favorite restaurant in Carp.

I love Ethiopian food and was excited to check this place out. We walked in at 7:15 on a Saturday night and were the only customers, but still had to wait a few minutes to be seated. Once seated, the service was prompt and the right level of attentiveness. I ordered my staple, the Doro Wat with extra injera, and my companion ordered the Gored Gored. Both dishes were heavy on the spice and low on flavor--exactly the opposite of what I've experienced elsewhere. The portions were also pretty small--I easily could have finished all mine, plus the extra injera (which has never happened to me before at an Ethiopian restaurant), had the food been so underwhelming. I felt the price was a bit high for the what we got. I probably won't be back.

I REALLY enjoyed the Thai Orchid. I wasn't expecting to find Thai this good in a strip mall, but my, was I surprised. They were pretty busy when we got there, but we had reservations so we rolled right in and got a table immediately (sweet!). I was really taken aback by how nice the hostess and the waitress were. They were genuinely very friendly and even laughed convincingly at my usual offering of lame jokes. The restaurant is a BYO and we brought a bottle of wine, which they promptly uncorked and put on ice. Their menu has a heat/spiciness scale that goes up to 4 peppers. I got the drunken noodles (marked as 3 peppers) and asked if they could make them "at least a 4." They were happy to oblige and I found the heat level to be perfect. The spring rolls were also very good. Overall, I was extremely happy with our experience at Thai Orchid and will definitely go back. Highly recommended.
Came here from out of town. The service was great! Gave 3 of us Free drinks. Clean and yummy!

Thai Cuisine & Cafe was empty on the Friday night when we ate here, and for good reason. The waitress didn't seem to know the menu, and the food was really run of the mill. The red curry was runny, and the drunken-noodle had an off flavor. To top it all off, the rice was dry and the prices high for low-quality food.
The vegan options are slim--tofu with lemongrass or tofu with curry (orders WITHOUT fish sauce)--but delicious! If you're an omnivore, this place has a ton of delicious options.
Nice place, Slow service... food like fancy 'tin drum'. Not remarkable. Barely any chicken in noodle bowl. Not Indian, not Chinese...smelled good walking by, their sauces make the food flavorful.
Nothing beats a zorba greek salad and their fresh bread. The place is super small but the food is 100% authentic and fresh. Highly recommend

Yummy. Brings back memories of Mamoun's on Bleeker St. NYC. Appetizer sampler enough for 4+. Chicken shawarma and shish kebab sandwiches were outstanding and the falafel was tender and moist. Very subtle, authentic flavor all around. The server Rakhee was a stunning young women with a charming and sweet personality. Petra is a keeper for both eat in and take out.

Loved the feta olives and the baked Brie. The chicken kabobs were dry and unappealing. I went for my birthday for my second trip and about fifteen minutes in, we were interrupted by CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CHING CHING CHING CHING. Yes. The bellydancer. SOOOO obnoxious and entirely too loud...You can barely hear yourself think over that racket. I thought it was never going to end. If I do go back, I'll definitely schedule it around the performance times.

This is your standard Chinese fast food. Friendly staff and clean. There are a lot of choices on the menu. I went with the General Tso. Good flavor to satisfy that craving. The sauce was thick the way I like it. Nice spice. I was disappointed on the 2 pieces of broccoli. Ask for more if you like. Overall a great place. $5.75 lunch. I watched them whip it up. I always like to see the kitchen.

A co-worker and I just had lunch at the Kabob House and it was so good I wanted to come straight here and write a review. They were slammed when we arrived but took the time to thank us for coming and apologized that the food time may be a little longer than usual. If our server hadn't of mentioned it I truly wouldn't have noticed so I look forward to the even faster service in the future! We split a turkish coffee, the Bolani appetizer, and each got the lamb kabob lunch special. Everything tasted fantastic, was beautifully presented, good portions, and the service was thoughtful and kind. I definitely recommend the Kabob House and look forward to returning for dinner too!

*i went here Thursday night for dinner* the woman taking our order was adorable and extremely friendly. They had a lot of Asian snacks like chips and pocky near the register which looked cool. The restaurant had a chill and relaxing atmosphere. The food was very good and prepared perfectly. The pork pho was well seasoned and the grilled chicken was delicious. Perfect for a weekday dinner or lunch.
Yuuuummy. That was really good. But I think its a bit expensive tho. I got a falafel with rice and chicken inside.

I wasn't expecting much from the place when we walked it (looked to me like a little bubble tea cafe), but was pleasantly surprised by the food. We tried the Lentil Bisque, Plate-O's Delight and a "Yee-Ro" Pocket. I subbed a side salad for the chips. The chips looked tasty, but was glad I made the change when I got the food. Their salad is well seasoned, dressing is refreshing, and it includes kalamatas (not those black jarred olives that some local places try to dump on your salad). Everything is made fresh and it tastes like it. It certainly isn't purely authentic Mediterranean, but it's Americanized in a good way. It's not at all like most of the gyros I have eaten either downtown or near Vanderbilt that come in a big fat piece of pita bread with a half cup of sauce spilling all over the place and a bunch of white flavorless tomatoes. I have to disagree with the other reviewers about the flavor. I don't want a bunch of greasy meat on my gyro. Theirs is thinly sliced, crispy on one side and rich in flavor. The wrap is also relatively thin which is exactly how I like it. They don't overdo it on the labin and tahini. You can add more if you're someone who really wants sauce running down your arm while you're trying to eat. The bisque was liquified but still had a nice lentil texture. Also lemon-y without being too acidic. The Plate-O's Delight was a real surprise. It's a briefly pan fried edamame corn succotash finished with a little white wine deglazing. It's nothing fancy, but just tastes great. Tried some baklava for dessert and it was also pretty good. It's also very affordable. "Yee-Ro" Pocket is only $5.99 and most of the small plates are under $4. The most expensive item is the $10.99 Salmon Filet. Many of the entree plates are $8.99. More than reasonable for the food quality. Like others I really wish they had falafel and baba ganoush. I'm guessing they could do these well. As other have mentioned this is a small cafe style place. They are limited in the number of seats inside because of only having one bathroom. They said they want to put a couple of tables out on the sidewalk for the spring/summer. While we were there we noticed quite a few people coming in for take out, so that seems like a good option if you're local. Whoever owns this place is lucky to have a couple of the most enthusiastic staff I've almost ever met in a restaurant. The guys who co-manage this place are all about making sure you have a great experience. We placed our order in a short line of a bunch of take out orders, and I think they assumed we wanted it to go. After 10-15 minutes when our food was ready they had a bag ready for us on the counter. I told them we would just eat it here and they apologized at least 5 times. It really wasn't a big deal, but they said they should have asked us and comped us some dessert. I tried to put some extra tip in the tip jar and they swiped the jar off the counter and pleaded with me to keep my money and enjoy the food. Ended up chatting with them a bit after the take out rush subsided and was surprised to find out they weren't the owners. These guys really want to make sure you have a great experience. This is also a bit of a drive for Nashville folks. Probably not so bad if you're near Brentwood. Would be awesome to see a location up in Nashville.

Just moved to Gulfport and I am trying out all the restaurants - so many options so much good food. My visit to Tangelo's was the worst so far. Went there on a Wednesday evening and it was so, and so was the service. The employees seemed to want to talk to the musician more then the customers. The Chicken Mojo sandwich came out cold in the middle and the bread was hard as a rock, like when you microwave bread. My water never was filled and they did not care to give me the time of day. With so many other restaurants to chose from in Gulfport, I am thankful I will never have to visit this place again.

I first stumbled upon Bitar's on a sweltering August day. Having just moved to the city, I was on the search for something that would fit my student budget. I ended up settling on pizza in the Italian Market., but little did I know I only had to walk half a block from home to delight in the best falafel in the city. A little family-owned corner store at 10th and Federal, Bitar's houses exotic Middle Eastern treats, fresh and satisfying pita bread, various cooking and bulk items, and a manned grill that produces $3 falafels and proportionately inexpensive lamb and chicken gyros, vegetable platters and authentic toubouli salad. For dessert try the baklava; pistachio is my favorite. At Bitar's service is fast, and the staff friendly, but seating is minimal. If there's no space for you to enjoy your chicken and feta gyro, there are several neighborhood parks that are ideal for two common urban activities: people watching and eating great food.
Been here twice! So good great family run business - really excited to see it packed on a Thursday night!

Best Thai food in Santa Barbara area. Well priced, great outdoor area. Casual and easy. Takeout is always on point. What more could you want from a mid-priced Thai restaurant in a small beach community?
Hummus is not good as expected, but Lamb Kabab and cheese Mano'ushe were delicious and taste well.
Totally happy with this indian buffet. Nothing to write home about but go every time i spend a few days in indy.

Expensive but worth every penny. This is quality food, and I have never had so much as a sub-par course here. And this is coming from an American who scoffed at Indian food till just a few years ago. In fact, I brought my dad (who never eats anything other than steak) here, and by the end of the night, the tender, perfectly spiced Lamb Korma had won him over. I'll be back, and when dad feels like a respite from steak, he will be too.

Have been going here since i was 15 with my grandparents. Since they've passed i make trips up here with my wife every time i visit FL. Lauren (a manager) didn't comp anything after they have my wife and i bad oysters. I had to go into the bathroom and "pull the trigger" like Back in the wrestling days to get the oysters out. Horrible experience and i will never come back. Horrible managerial skills. I will possibly be opening a law suit if i get sick from those oysters. Awful. Steer away!

Yum! Hit the spot, went for a Saturday lunch buffet, and was glad we did. Plenty of parking, friendly staff, clean, Nice decor, authentic tasting Indian! Very good variety of items at the buffet: Chix Tika massala, Chix Tika, Goat Curry, A bunch of Vege dishes, Salad, all the typical condiments: chutneys, Raita, etc,2 desserts! Very fair prices. Looking forward to returning soon!

I really don't know why this place has so many good reviews because I didn't have that experience. I got oxtails, rice and peas, Mac &cheese and 2 beef patties. I take home food every Thursday for dinner for my son. The oxtails were suppose to be falling off the bone. The were tough like they didn't cook long enough. Very chewing...got stuck in my teeth. Mac/ cheese was dry. I haven't ever needed to put seasoning on Jamaican food. But I did yesterday. Bland. The rice was ok. I have been on a diet almost a year but decided to treat myself and was so disappointed. The good wasn't good for 14.00$...not at all and it sent me to the bathroom 5 times between 1 and 4 on. It destroyed my stomach. Guess it was to greasy. Beef patty was ok..but they aren't baked which I thought. And they didn't have chicken soup.

We ran into Parada Maimon a couple of days ago and have to say that the pork mofongo really hit the spot. The food is very authentic, just like in the DR. We also had 2 of their fruit juices, the tamarindo and guanabanam they were kinda sweet but they were freshly made. Parking is for free, prices were good too. Will definitively come back to try a few more dishes.

I was lucky enough to just happen across this place while doing some shopping at London Drugs. Its fairly new I learned from the lady at the counter. It's not much to look at inside or out, the term 'kitchen express' in the title almost out me off, assuming it would be some greasy mall version of Vietnamese. I did venture in, its a small place with around 10 tables and is definitely reminiscent of a cafeteria. But when I'm looking for pho, dining ambience is of little or no consequence to me. It was clean, that's all I need. Now to the phone, which was spectacular. Like I said, I was certainly wary of what I was getting into but once the big steamy bowl of pho came out my mind was at ease. The broth and meat, the key phone ingredients, were both excellent. Good quality meat and a fragrant, flavorful broth, not too oily or salty. The pho had both green onion and red onion and the nice addition of cilantro. Served with the usual suspects, basil, lime and sprouts. Around $10 for the bowl. There was quite a bit of foot traffic for takeout coming in and out so I'll take that as a good sign. I'll definitely be back!

One of the worst burgers I've ever eaten in my life. I have eaten a burger here before and it was obviously handmade and juicy and delicious. This time I came in and got a burger special. The burger was obviously a frozen patty which came out burnt to the point where it was crunchy. The worst part of the service is that they still charge me full price after hearing my complaints and I sent back a burnt burger. Will never visit this establishment ever again.

Have visited this truck numerous times and just getting to review. The whiting dinners are delicious, I usually get Mac and cheese with collards for sides. I probably get 5 or 6 pieces of fish with the large. It is more than enough food for 2. The Mac and cheese is excellent. It's worth the wait, and won't break the bank.

I hosted a book club meeting at Pan D'olive. The service was excellent. We were given appropriate time between courses. Our drinks were kept full. They food was great. They asked us how we wanted the bill split without giving us the death stare that some places give. Everyone was very happy and mentioned returning with spouses and friends for follow up visits.
Almost 40+ years and still going strong. Very honored and proud to be a part of such an authentic piece of Thailand in the heart of Tampa Bay Always delicious food and always made with a lot of love

Freshly made from fresh ingredients. The naan must have been seconds out of the tandoor when it arrived at our table. The bangain had onions and ginger with some crunch left in them. My husband had a lamb dish which was a little stringy and not what he had hoped for. We both feel that we'll give them another shot as everything else was just so good. FYI: mild, medium, hot is on the Indian scale. Medium is pretty darn hot for my American palate (but the raita was delicious and took down the heat).

Um...well what can I say? They are traditional Japanese style restaurant, however, they have very average sushi (I don't even think the fish is that fresh, at least it didn't smell/taste that way). I mean come on they didn't really even get the Edamame right (it was very soggy and overcooked). Some people with me got the Seafood Iron Pot which was pretty good. Overall not really impressed at all.

One of my favourite places to stop for lunch in the South. I get the Jerk Chicken and its the best ever. The portions are large and your licking your plate clean. Also get the beef patty I think it is, cant remember. Even that was fantastic so good it wiped my memory. You are so full after you finished your meal. The staff is super friendly, love to talk. Its very inviting. The issue is it is by two highschools so it can get pretty packed. If you can go a little early I would recommend it.

Got takeout from Nadia's today. The green curry was average for Thai food. I agree that with one of the reviewers that my curry had more bamboo shoots that any of the other vegetables. Also, I had ordered tofu curry but received vegetable curry instead. Was already home by the time I noticed. Seemed like a nice enough place - willing to try again, but not impressed yet.
This place is awesome. Love how they have vegan/vegetarian options. Lunch specials are great!

Since there aren't a lot of non-chain restaurants in Green Hills, I end up here a lot of the time when in that part of town. I think this place is firmly okay, but certainly not great. The food is okay, the service is okay, the atmosphere is okay. Although the atmosphere is actually great on some Friday/Saturday nights when they have live music. My main dislike here is actually the lamb/beef gyros. Most of the gyros I've had before feature thin slices of meat. The gyros here feature thick chunks of meat, which actually have kind of a mushy texture. The texture of the meat is really unpleasant to me. If you like gyros that are thin slices of flavorful meat, skip the ones here. If you want that kind of gyro, you're better off with Anatolia (Turkish, so a little different seasonings, but at least good meat). Other dishes are much better than the gyros - the falafel is reasonably good and some of the other ground lamb dishes are seasoned really nicely. Their hummus is pretty decent, but served with really uninspiring pita bread that taste like the Wonder Bread of the pita world. I wouldn't call any of the main dishes here particularly authentic - just "not bad for Nashville". The baklava is actually the only thing served here that seems authentically Greek. They serve a wide variety of different baklava styles and I've enjoyed every version that I've tried here. Kalamata's is a reasonably good choice for a fast non-chain meal in the Green Hills area, but not a place I would deliberately drive across town to get to.

Anywhere that involves pad Thai and boba tea is a place I will frequent often. Third time here and I got the same thing Chicken Pad Thai. Now my first experience was diff. All places I've been they cut their noodles on half, and this place had the first time. This time around the noodles were full length so it was rather hard to eat with chopsticks since I could grab hold to noodles without picking up a tennis ball mound of them at once. And I prefer not to use a fork for Thai or Viet foods. My meal was still pleasant as always, it did have more large chunks of the scrambled egg the 2x vs it being tiny pieces, but protein is protein. We all have weird odd quirks but this isn't making them lose my business. I've been happy the 3x I've been here! I always get a Thai Boba Tea or Taro Boba. Both have their own unique, addicting flavor and yes, I always get extra boba. I love those chewy things! I want to just go and buy them for my home! Not sure about the jelly grass and fruit things yet, but they look tasty in the photos. I've also had their pork Bahn no, and I was pleased! Flavorful, meaty and down right comforting to my hungry belly! The fresh crunch of the carrot And cilantro and then the pork all blending in your mouth and just a kick of the jalapeño. Oh yes, I love this spot! I should be more open to trying more on their menu, but pad Thai is my fav!

Excellent Thai food. Fantastic green and red curries with chicken. The staff are very nice, quintessential Thai hospitality. We regularly order take-out from here as the food quality is as good as it gets

This was an amazing experience for my family! My husband, 3 year old daughter and I decided to try it this week for my birthday. The waiter was extremely attentive and the food was AMAZING. There was so much flavor infused in each course. My picky toddler even loved the experience. I dont think this place is usually a family spot, but my 3 year old loved the variety and colorful decor. I would reco making a reservation. Especially earlier than 7. People really seem to start streaming in around that time. I will definitely be back for my next birthday or another special occasion!! Thank you Marrakesh!
My first visit and had Buffett. Even though food tasted good, it was cold. May be one should go at noon and not 1. Chai was cold as well. I was disappointed as Norristown location is exceptional.

What can I say I love everything thing about this place. They have great food and the service is wonderful! I always get the same thing so they know exactly what I want to order when they see me enter the restaurant lol very nice atmosphere and very clean as well. Thumbs up all across the board, I have nothing bad to say about this restaurant at all. The fish curry is amazing if you love spicy foods you'll love that dish :)

Treat yourself and give Ethiopian food a try. The food was very unique with wonderful flavors. We had a bigger group and ordered the Queen's Eight (for however many people you have dining). It's eight different items on a plate to share. No utensils (though they will provide if you ask). You use the spongy bread (injera) as your means of eating. It didn't look like any bread I had had before but was good. The Queens eight gave us the opportunity to taste so much. We had the tray with meats, so had beef, chicken and veggies but you can order the tray in a vegetarian/vegan option. And try the honey tortilla dessert, sprinkled with confectioner's sugar. Service was good and the staff was happy to give you insight into the traditions and cuisine.

Given the chance to actually come here this place is utilizing every thing they can for business.....and..it's amazing! Why is there not a line out the door??? Why aren't the prices in the low $50??? I don't know but between the manager/cook-- Lamont And the delivery guy....I won't be shocked when they head right into center city! Fresh, great portions...and unlike some Caribbean places this food isn't salty...and been sitting there all day! I have to say of all the places in my neighborhood I support, they have my business 100% Sidenote: call, or order on line or get take out or delivery.....they accommodate for everyone's needs!
Good taste , fresh product . However the meat portion they put in the sandwich is so little . About spoon size . If I wanted to eat only salads I would ordered salad

The first dish with the eggplant is the best! Second dish (bastilla?) is also very good (flakey phyllo dough with powdered sugar, cinnamon, and egg). The chicken, lamb, and couscous were just ok. The baklava at the end was also delicious. Really cool atmosphere. Will definitely go back!

I went to Fez for a birthday party. I had zero expectations and overall I had a great time. I went on a Saturday night, so the only option was the 7 course meal. The belly dancer was great and got the crowd involved. The drink prices were reasonable for the city. My only complaints were the super slow service. We arrived at 8:15. My husband and I left at 11:15 and the last hadn't been served yet. Of course this drove up our bar tab. Also as a morrocan newbie it would have been nice if someone explained the dishes. They stated in the beginning they would, but that never happenend. I was in a group where peope didn't really know each other, so I know a few peopke felt uncomfortable eating with their hands though I absolutely loved that part. This was a unique dining experience. I really enjoyed myself and I'm looking for a reason to return in the near future.

After our recent carry-out experience, we still give this place 4-stars, with caution. We realize that there can be personal preference, and food sensitivities anywhere, so we often "learn" what to order at the places we enjoy. We recently "learned" that the Chicken Tikka Masala is extremely oily, and it provides an after-"taste" of cheap/soy oil. This is a public service announcement... LOL Anyway, every other component of our meal was agreeable and tasty. We will continue to support this restaurant, although on a rare/less frequent occasion (that, too, is unchanged.)
Very good Caribbean food. The jerk chicken was very flavorful and the customer service was very good as well!

This was our second visit. The waitress took our order wrong and brought us Shahi paneer instead of Kadahi paneer, which in most places is a dry dish. The manager insisted that theirs was creamy. (their baingan bharta is also creamy which is uncommon). It turned out not so bad after all. The channa masala, however, was like a BP oil spill. The Kashmiri pulao was also pretty mediocre and oily. The naan and rotis were good. It was overall a bit disappointing, given our first experience was quite good.

I was a frequent visitor, but the past year or two I've been more disappointed than pleased. The waitstaff is barely adequate. The food frequently tastes off and even, at times, burnt. Yet, the bill is always increasing. My weekly/biweekly visits have dwindled to a handful of times a year. So sad to watch it's decline.
I really like their vegetarian option, choose 5 items for $12.99. Very good. I come here often. My hubby loves the lamb chops. I like the waitstaff, nice quiet atmosphere. We will be back again soon.

Like most people who live in Fairmout, I've been waiting for a Pho restaurant to open up. Sometimes traveling to China town or to Washington Ave to hit up the usual suspects is a little too far and a hassle on its own. But thank god, we finally have a spot in our little town that's walkable and delicious. With that being said, I've read some of the reviews and I'm confused with all the bad ratings. Not to insult you, but if you gave this place a bad review, you are an idiot. I'm putting this place up there with some of the greats. The quality of ingredients and the authenticity of the taste is way above your average pho, and better than your moms kitchen. If you get a chance stop in and see what I'm talking about! Ps: Have fun in Niagara!
bombdiggity! Chicken Katsu was freaking delicious. Wait times are going to be about 30mins during peak hours but go catch some pokemon while you wait.

Very friendly staff. So friendly infact, that the waiter told me I wouldn't like what I ordered. And then when my food was brought out, someone from the kitchen came out and told me I didn't like it and asked me what I would like instead. I thought it was fine, but this was a very strange impression to leave on a first-time diner. What had I ordered? Curry goat and kassava sauce. Are these flavors a typical American palate would like? Probably not. But they didn't ask me if I've had dishes like this before, and I do not have the typical American palate. Having actually recently visited Jamaica and eaten there, the goat and cassava sauce were pretty typical of what I was expecting, and I did enjoy it. A strange experience, but I would come back for the food.

I cannot get enough of this place. Once you try their Pho Gha (Chicken Noodle Soup) and their Goi Rolls (Soft Spring Rolls) the flavors reach your soul and you are addicted. I can't tell you how many people I have introduced to this gem and they all continually ask me when we can go back. It's so fresh and seems to have a healing quality to the food. The owner is so kind! He always greets me with a big smile and knows when it's my order for takeout without even leaving a name. I go out of my way to eat here and the Bubble Tea is a great treat as well.

I used to frequent this place and the food was delicious. Tonight while at the theater, I went there and ordered brown stew chicken. It was horrible. THe gravy was bland and thick. The cabbage tasted like paper and the plantains were dry and pasty. THey must have changed chefs or owners. Definitely not the cuisine of the past. The only good thing was that the staff were pleasant. I will not return.

Food is good. This has been our neighborhood restaurant for almost 20 years. Unfortunately we will not return. The service is rude, indifferent, and unprofessional. There are plenty of other places to go. We were a party of three and seated at a 24' two top. When asked to be seated at a four top instead we were abruptly told no and that four tops were reserved for larger parties. In almost 20 years we never had to cram ourselves in a two top when we were three guests. One in our party left disturbed by the attitude. Two of us stayed, and during the hour of our meal there remained four open four tops. Sorry to manager Ann. You lost not only one cover tonight, but three local regulars. Have a nice day.
Good Thai food in Nashville ,TN Mango salad is the right taste from Thailand ; its perfect make me feel at home again ! Thanks

Leaving the art museum, my husband and I were looking online for a place to eat near our hotel. We saw Ariana and thought, "hey, let's try something new." Great decision! The decor is really nice, and the service was wonderful. The best part though was the food. We both had lamb dishes, each very different but equally delicious. The sambosas were amazing and we finished with baklava. Couldn't have asked for a better dinner. Definitely adding it to our list of favorites.

This is GREAT takeout. I'm used to being spoiled by Cafe Bombay in Bristol whenever I want Indian, so I guess I was expecting...well, not this. Great food. We ordered the samosa chat, which is smashed samosas with yogurt, chickpeas and tomato chutney on top. Deeeeelicious! It was sweeter than I thought it would be and this was definitely a pleasant surprise. Also, I ordered two thinking they would be small, like samoas, but in reality these appetizers could probably feed three people each. Whoops. Also ordered the chicken madras and the dal tadka, which is stewed lentils. We chose mild spice level, and it was still a little spicy...which is great for me, since I love spicy foods (my boyfriend does not share my enthusiasm), but might not be so great for someone very sensitive to spice. The delivery guy was almost on time - he was almost ten minutes later than what grubhub suggested, and he promptly apologized for being late. No big deal, we're in an apartment complex and most people have trouble finding us, and the food was still very hot so no harm, no foul. I imagine the food tastes great the next day, too. Very, very happy this place is here!
This is exactly what I wanted when I went. Elevated street style food, and it's totally that. I highly recommend the lamb pita, and don't miss the fries. Thanks y'all!
Excellent spicy chicken noodles. Not quite as good as authentic hand pulled but overall superb flavours.

good food and quick friendly service. The pot stickers had a great thick and cooked perfectly dough and were amply filled with a tasty pork filling. They were also served with a good dipping sauce. the sauces on the entrees were very good without masking the food. All of the chicken and shrimp were cooked nicely as well. A very solid option especially for the price point. I'd like to try the Pho next time.

This was Media pizza and its the same owner. He had crappy pizza and food before now bought a sign hung up some rugs and now thinks he can charge a boat load for more crappy food. I give this guy credit for the shear balls he has to try and scam Media with the price fix and only ala cart style price for take out and when you get the bill are shocked. Dont go there if you dont want to blow a ton of money on crappy food. You can easily find way better food in Media without the scam tactics.

The service here was awesome. The guy running the place was super nice. I LOVED THEIR SWEET CORN PUDDING. Please get this. It is sweet corn with tapioca and coconut cream. It's to die for. The pho and chicken pho broth were too sweet for my personal preference. I don't know if they use MSG because I didn't feel the effects after. The egg rolls were good too. But definitely get a Bahn Mi sandwich!!! Holy moly... These were so good!!!

Nice and cozy interior, and it usually doesn't get too loud unless it's super busy. The coffee is a bit more acidic for my tastes, but I enjoy the chai lattes. The pastries and bagels are also pretty good. My only complaint is that their items are a little overpriced, in my opinion.

Great addition to the neighborhood! I tried the tea leaf salad which was crisp and refreshing and the beef Rendang was very tender in a rich sauce. The menu is pretty comprehensive and includes favorites like roti canai, Hainanese chicken rice, nasi lemak, etc. On top of that the service is pleasant and attentive. Looking forward to my next visit.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Authentic, Authentic, Authentic... we toss that word around all the time in regards to food. It's the buzz word that makes us feel as if we're enjoying food that is made with a lot of love, passed down through generations, and sometimes labor intensive or difficult to make! That's the kind of food we can't make for ourselves at home, and flavors we go out seeking. Thai food, a cuisine made up of complex flavors and dishes, was one of those for me because it just seemed too difficult. But now, thanks to Chris M and the instruction of Pim Marshall at the Lanna Thai Culinary School, I realize authenticity can be simple, and I can now make not one, not two, but three authentic Thai dishes at home! Thanks to Reno Bites Week and the Yelp Passport program, Chris M, a good friend of mine, won a group cooking class at Lanna Thai Culinary School and invited me to tag along! 12 of us gathered around the big island in the open kitchen to make spring rolls, seafood yellow curry, and pad see ew (drunken noodles)! I couldn't help it, so before we got started I gave everyone a red Yelp doggie bandana to make us look official, and keep our hair back of course. The cooking classes here include a glass of wine or beer, and you can also BYOB, which we all made sure to take advantage of, sampling different wine and beer throughout the day. We started with spring rolls, which are actually quite simple. Rice paper, carrots, cucumbers, bean sprouts, rice noodles, chicken or shrimp, and the Thai garden of basil, mint, and cilantro. These herbs are what make Pim's spring rolls special because they impart that strong herbal flavor that, when eaten, seasons the veggies and meat, and compliments the rich peanut sauce. I was a master roller of these beauties, if I do say so myself. Pim agreed! We then moved on to the seafood yellow curry. Here's where I thought things would get tough, but alas, even this dish was straight forward, fun and simple! We started off with some oil in the wok, which to that we added Mae Ploy yellow curry paste and some fresh Thai chilies. This product is available at most Asian markets in town, and a little bit goes a long way. Once the paste and chillies cooked in the oil a bit, we added coconut milk and stirred to incorporate the two together. The coconut milk turned a brilliant yellow color, and then we added in the seafood and allowed it to simmer until done. Mmmmmm. This was perfect with steamed rice. We finished up with Drunken Noodles, another simple and tasty dish! I can't give away all the secrets or you won't go check this out for yourself, so all I'll say about this dish is that the ingredients are few, the prep time short, and the results are awesome. I was most surprised by how early we put the meat in, and how tender and flavorful it remained at the end of cooking. The afternoon was incredibly fun, filled with jokes, good friends, great food, and plenty of wine and beer! I would not hesitate to do this again in a heartbeat, but I'd ask her to dig deep in her recipe books and find me something her mom made for her in Thailand. I'm dying to see what that looks like!

The interior is amazing and the atmosphere is authentic. Overall, the service was good. They dumped a pound of sugar in my Moroccan mint tea and there was a huge film of the sugar resting on the bottom, which was a turn off for me. Also, they did not play much Middle Eastern music but instead played random outdated mainstream songs. However, one thing that I did not mind being overly sweet was the belly dancer. She was amazingly kind and friendly, I couldn't help but dance with her. An overall comfortable atmosphere and belly dancing lessons!? I'll take it.

My husband and I just visited Thai Tanic for the first time and really enjoyed our food. I had the Exotic Shrimp which was very good (though not so spicy as the little symbol on the menu indicated ... fine by me) and the hubby had Kang Dang (red curry). That dish was recommended as one of the spicier ones. He enjoyed it with a glass of their Thai iced tea. Other than the delicious food, I was pleasantly surprised by the atmosphere inside the restaurant. The shopping center it is located in is a little run down on the outside, but they did a nice job of making their space warm and inviting. My advice? Skip the Outback (same shopping center) and try something new at Thai Tanic.

Excellent fresh made middle eastern food. We had the chicken shawarma and hummus. Yum!!! The hummus is some of the best I've had with generous amounts olive oil and whole chickpeas and paprika and a bit of pickles. Family run business.

It's the little things here. Homemade pitas, tazitiki sauce laid down first over the whole pita, followed by well grilled slices of gyro. Not overstuffed. Love the crunchy edges on each slice. Plentiful, Crisp, yet thin, onion, topped with red ripe tomatoes, and wrapped neatly in foil. You can eat this thing without missing any ingredient with each bite and not be wearing it afterward... Love the salads, they are Greek, they are chopped, they are great. Had the baklava today and it was delish.
We really enjoyed our dinner. E even added all of his rice to his green curry so he could get every last drop. My red curry was fantastic. I can't wait to go back and try the lunch specials!

"Welcome to Nirvana," he said with a open faced smile that hinted that he had practiced this line many times as an owner of Nirvana Fusion. He waited for his words to penetrate and for our reaction. Magically, we were transported to the Himalayas in Nepal, where we would dine this night. You see, the "fusion" in Nirvana Fusion comes from the fact that the owners and chef of this mountain house are from Nepal, where they are at the cross currents of north Indian and southwest Chinese culture. Fusion comes naturally when you grow up in it. Both cuisines roll over each other, mix and retreat with each human tide; leaving behind something that is both informed by their neighbors, and creative of a new reality where turmeric and curry meet chili and dragon fruit. The similarities are undeniable. The uniqueness, extraordinary. The menu read differently than those of similarly named restaurants. Extra time was needed to penetrate, and many questions had to be answered by our hosts. We were curious. They were patient. We ultimately ordered the Chili Chicken (Dry) and Gobi Manchurian (Dry) appetizers, the Chicken Zafrani traditional Indian dish, and the Vegetable Hakka Noodles from the Indo/Chinese/Thai Fusion section, to try a cross section of their offerings. Both the apps were spicy hot and looked surprising similar in deep red amber sauces. The Chili Chicken tasted of both Chili and Tumeric in the thick sauce coating the small morsels of chicken. It was very good and left our mouths burning without reaching numbness. The Gobi (deep fried cauliflower) in another dark sauce with pieces of clumped spices sticking to everything, was excellent in that the vegetable flavor and texture remained although bathed in the heavy float. The cross fertilization of cultures was most evident here. The Chicken Zafrani was more straight forward North Indian with a softer curry infused with the sweetness of Almonds, Cashews and Saffron. There were also Kashmiri Chilies in there, but they did not dominate. Finally, the Hakka Noodles really seemed more a straight up Chinese dish very akin to a chunky Lo Mein. Very nice. Nirvana Fusion took me by surprise - a pleasant one. It is definitely deserves returning for more adventures. We weren't in Hatboro anymore, Toto.

Love this place. A very unique Ethiopian dining experience. Nothing fancy about the interior but the food is authentic and wonderfully crafted. The staff always have a big smile and are very welcoming!

Another home run on Magazine St. Walked here from home for lunch. The restaurant has a couple of outside tables on the porch. Inside....beautiful, clean decor. A couple of TV's were on, but it wasn't noisy here. Smiling, happy server came to the table. I ordered by number, because ....its easier than speaking Vietnamese, lol. THE FOOD: The #5... Gi Cun, Fresh spring rolls w/fresh shrimp & pork. A very tasty, fresh bite for $4.95. The see- through wrap shows shrimp, but its cut so thin that you taste it as an afterthought to the greens and herbs. Did not taste pork. The peanut sauce was silky and lovely. A great appetizer. The #54..Ph Chín Beef soup w/brisket 7.25 (Sm) 8.25 (Lg). I had the small size, which is plenty. A plate of fresh basil, sprouts, jalapenos and lime is brought in prep for the pho. The Pho is light, a little oily, and a lot of flavor. The vermicelli noodles are light. I added sprouts, basil, and jalapenos and let it steep a bit.
