The sauce was Prik Khing - a gingery paste - without coconut milk like a curry. It tasted like the shrimp and chicken were cooked in the sauce. It was good. I've had Thai food all over the world, including Thailand. This place does not rank among the best. But locally it is among the best. The space is indeed small and the tables are close together. By the time we left (6:45 or so) it was fairly full. The crowd was mostly composed of concert goers. So, the too-cool-for-this-planet hipster crowd was not in evidence. If that is what you are seeking, then Monk's is only a block away.

I honestly waiver between a 3 and 4 stars mostly because of the poor service I have received at night. The food is pretty good, I personally think it is a little expensive, but good none the less. I have been eating here for easily 8 years Or more. When I was pregnant I ate here a Lot (it's up the street) unfortunately they didn't seem to like us here as much as we liked the food. There is one awesome server who knows that I love limes with my meal, I love them so much I ask for a few, but the last four times we have gone for dinner, I ask for my usual limes and my server is on his way to give them to me, when another server stops him and takes them away, so then I have to ask another time for limes, there have been a few times when my husband had to walk up to the counter and ask for limes again. If you want me to pay, just say that, but don't not bring me my damn limes. You would think because we eat here so often this wouldn't be an issue, but it consistently is and with the same servers. One night, it was pretty empty in there except for maybe 6 other guests and I asked for limes TWICE and got one single wedge once. My husband had to walk up again and ask for a few more limes for me. AND then no one checked on us for a good 25 minutes, they were very busy doing something with plastic bags. I did go for lunch the other day and the service was great, I believe the owners were the ones running the show. So, if you're there you'll be in better hands otherwise best of luck. Probably best to order out and eat at home.
If you haven't been here you're missing one of St Louis's best lunches! $9.95 for a 2 course lunch with drink included! WOW!!!

I've eaten here twice. The food was delicious; one of the top Thai meals I've had outside Thailand. The servers were very attentive and polite. The restaurant is somewhat plain, but it looks very clean, So why four stars? Timing; I ordered an appetizer, soup and a main dish. The appetizer and soup arrived together and I had barely started the soup when the entree arrived. So by the time I got to my main dish, it was lukewarm. I can highly recommend the Tom Yum soup, the chicken with basil and the spicy green curry; they're all very delicious. The entree portions are large enough to share.

Went here with a Groupon. Won't return. The Queen and I was a disappointment: 1) They advertise having sushi, but don't 2) I wouldn't even describe our dishes as mediocre; they were gross. The sauces were really watered down.

When I come in here, I feel like family. Staff is incredibly courteous! Good variety of shisha, including their own "Layalena Mix", which is the best one that I have tried so far. You can also mix the flavors or use various fruit bowls to your preference. They are very knowledgeable, as other reviewers have stated; the coals get changed consistently without having to ask. They also have food (which, especially if you know me, is a big plus! ;) ) The tea (which has a sprig of mint in it) is also good. I tend to do my studying here, which is no problem as they have huge comfy couches; can literally just chill here for however long you like. Favorite hookah place since moving here for college :)

Tangelo's has revamped their menu. Old favorites are still there and the new additions are flawless too. They continue to offer incredible food at an exceptional value and service that is always prompt, attentive and courteous. Brunch on weekends is as good as you will find in the continental US. I lost track of the number of times I heard, "this is delicious" from adjacent tables on today's visit. Today I enjoyed a fritata, salad, and gazpacho. Every morsel was just delicious.

I pretty much get straight to the point. Fish sandwich (would be a tad better if was on something else than regular wheat bread, but who is complaining!) salmon burger and mac & cheese were really good. The bread pudding... should be a crime! Great place to go if your in the germantown ave/nicetown section of the city.

The food was good but nothing that really stands out amongst Indian food. The service was incredibly slow and I had to continually ask for refills of my drink. My friend and I went for lunch and we each had the tandoori chicken and were super happy with the value of their lunch combo. My friend got mild and she was absolutely burning up. I got mine much spicier and it was fine with me. I'm not sure if my friend was just extra sensitive to the spice or if there was just really not much difference between the two levels. Overall experience means that I would go back but maybe just go ahead and ask for two glasses of water.
Excellent, Will recommend to all who enjoy fresh, seasoned, well priced food!! Recommend some pasteles and arroz con gandules to lock it in Thanks

Oh local breakfast places on the east coast. I miss them. So maybe every time I go to one, I think they are better than they really are. Sentimental value is worth a dime, right? Blue Plate has a standard breakfast menu. Omelets, eggs benedict, sandwiches...make sure you ask for the seasonal menu or the specials. They seem to have a more interesting choice there. I had the chicken apple sausage with grits and was pleasantly surprised with the grits. Hmm-hmm even better than Cracker Barrel. The place itself is very quaint looking, nothing fancy. Like I said, a neighborhood place. However, if you happen to be in the neighborhood craving some brunch food, this is a good place to start (apart from Wawa ;)).

We carried out from the Spot House tonight and tried four different items. The chicken tacos, the fish tacos, nachos and the fried rice. The chicken tacos and the fish tacos were very good. The nachos were not that great. Some of the chips were a little burnt and the cheese sauce was average at best. The fried rice was just OK. We definitely had more flavorful rice at other restaurants. We would definitely go back for the chicken and fish tacos and to try other items on the menu.

A bunch of my Iraqi friends mentioned that this was the best place to go for Iraqi food. So I went there with my friend and OMG I could not stop eating! We had the lamb kabob with rice and the falafel dish served with hummus and bread. This restaurant recently got new management and it is seriously the most authentic place to have Middle Eastern cuisine. You know it is an excellent place when you're a minority and there's Arabic subtitles on the TV. I will definitely be returning!
fast and efficient service. the food was amazing, the best panang curry I've ever had! great soup. the atmosphere is nice too!

I'm so glad to have found this place!! The food was delicious and for a tapas heavy restaurant, the portions are surprisingly generous. Pro: - grilled octopus. Absolutely delicious. - lamb shanks. So tender and just the right amount of fat (which is little but enough for the flavor). The sauce is a miss. - traditional lamb gyros. They do a great job of using real lamb chunks (instead of the sliced meat which doesn't really have much lamb flavor) and additions like olives. -live jazz and belly dancers on select days of the week. Con: - the eggplant spread was bland and there certainly were not enough pitas. We asked for extras, which were an additional $2. - outside patio was a very tight squeeze and the furniture was dirty.

As I sit here and type I have been here close to 30 minutes. 15 minutes I spent waiting in line for the only cashier to take my order. You have three cashiers, use at least two. This is crazy. If I had not already paid I would leave. Very disappointing experience.

The food was good, but the wait seemed forever and ever. We were one of two tables in the restaurant. We got one platter to share; no drinks, appetizers, nada. We were in a hurry because we had to do something after so we thought this would be a quick bite. Nope. A kebab platter took 25 minutes to come out. We probably won't be back.
Great service and great food. Lamb ribs are fantastic!

This kind of sets the standard for what I consider to be an awesome hookah place in a strange new city. We rolled in around 10pm on Sunday, knowing from the Yelp app full-well that they were going to close at 11pm. So we get seated and get right to it - we want the tequila sunrise hookah because that name just sounds awesome. The decoration is legit & authentic. The walls are covered with cloth, the windows are blacked out from the street with the same cloth, there are the cloth hangings coming off the wall, and the lighting is dim to make it seem authentic, something straight out of one thousand and one nights. The tables are round and are organized in a lavish lounge sort of setting. The waiter guy was nice, friendly, and was doing a rockstar job of checking in on us and the coals. Hookah for three people came out to $27. Not exactly cheap, but at least not exorbitant compared to some hookah places across the country I have unfortunately visited. My return visit scheduled and on the books has already incorporated this place into the itinerary. I look forward to trying the food. And getting some more time with the hookah before the music gets turned off which is a clear indication we need to GTFO at 11:00 exactly - would have appreciated a little more gentle approach and a few extra minutes to hang out, but hey, I bet real important shit was about to go down you had to attend to rather than letting us hang out for a few extra minutes.
They have more assortments of rice than before. Good hot naan. $13 For one lunch buffet. Very busy. Good service. Nice and spicy!
Fresh tasty and reasonably priced. Authentic Indonesian food. The coconut curry soup is very good and the chicken or pork noodle dishes are also homemade. This is a hidden gem.

Very impressive! We are repeat customers. Atmosphere is so 'city-like,' I love it! I am stuck on the tamales which are amazing, and the lime rice. Bar is chic, drinks are great. Love, love, love. Need many more restaurants of this caliber in Indy!

I haven't had Thai food since our goodbye dinner at our favorite Thai place in Omaha back in May, so I was kinda starting to go through withdrawal and was grateful to discover this place only a few minutes away. We were a little nervous when we walked in to discover that we were the only customers on a Friday night, but we soon realized that they do a brisk take-out business. The menu is primarily Chinese and Japanese, but there is a small selection of Thai dishes. We ordered the Pad See Ew, which wasn't the best I've ever had, but was good enough to satisfy my craving for now, the Basil Chicken, which was okay but a bit too sweet for my taste, and the Beef With Broccoli from the Chinese menu, which was pretty standard. In short, adequate but not memorable in any way. Prices were pretty reasonable, so between that and the convenience factor I'm sure we'll be back, but the hunt for great Thai food continues...

Solid meal here tonight. Our server was funny and friendly. We started with samosa chat and gobi manchurian- haven't had either before and we inhaled it. Then we got our usual, for the sake of comparing these to other places I've eaten. My malai kofta were a bit pastier than I like, but had good flavor. Hubs seemed to like his tikka masala. The rice is fluffy and flavorful and the onion kulcha was tasty. Felt like we got a lot of food and we left stuffed....and only $48 lighter in the wallet.

One of the best restaurants in Reno, my absolute favorite. I have yet to have a dish that wasn't delicious. I recommend getting the Enat honey wine, and if you don't drink, then their tea. Both are great accompaniments to their spicy dishes (they also have non-spicy meal that are crazy flavorful). Embrace eating with your hands, it's a wonderful experience.
This food here is amazing!! My boyfriend and I tried the lamb kabob, beef kabob, lamb kafta, and gyro meat. It was all really good and you get a lot of food for about $10.

I've been at this restaurant before four years ago by coming back here I remember the food was good went back today looks like new management food was nasty have no taste the rice was sour like it's overnight food could not eat the food end up throwing it away

Came here on a Wednesday night. There was only a couple of people so we didn't have to wait to be seated. We started out with a couple of Mango Sunrises - think tequila sunrise, but with rum and mango purée. Delicious, but the drinks are small. Our waiter was pretty preoccupied but friendly - not very attentive but it's a new place. Our food took a LONG time to prepare, but there is a warning on the menu so I can't really complain that it took such a long time - even though I want to. Our meals were delicious. Everything was seasoned well and delicious. I only gave 4 stars because our waiter didn't come and ask us how our meals were or to ask us if we wanted anything else to drink with our meals. I had to get up and ask for a drink. No bueno but not the end of the world. Overall - if you have a lot of time to kill, this is a decent place to do so and the food is worth the wait. If you're expecting a fast meal, this isn't the place for you.

Fast, friendly, consistent, convenient, DELICIOUS. Simple as that. Have had better spring rolls, but the pho is spot on as well as the best hangover cure (depending on how much sriracha you can stomach, that is). Not to mention the unusual and entertaining conglomerate of patrons ranging from elderly Vietnamese couples to tough looking crowds of young Asian teens to marathon eaters to hipsters. Overall - LOVE.

My extended family love our Vietnamese food, so before driving back to the Bay Area we all came here to eat lunch. Well, the place was SO packed that we had to wait 45 minutes to get seated. That meant that this place must be good, right? Not so. The place is VERY noisy and hard to hear one another over the din of the workers cleaning up dishes, just throwing the dishes into their clean-up cart. Then the same workers would take your order...? Anyway, after finally getting to sit down, we ordered but then had to wait another half hour to receive our food. My dish hadn't come out yet and we wondered what happened to it but it turned out that the waiter forgot that I had made that order... By the time I got my dish, everyone else was well on their way to finishing the meal. Thus, I had to take half my dish as carry-out. Taken into account the service, the quality of the food, and the place, their prices are relatively more expensive for pho.

The food is terrific!! you get what you ask for and that says a lot for me. I like my food extra spicy and all other Indian places just don't do it right. Bawarchi makes the food very spicy when you ask them, they give you generous portions, and the breads are fabulous!! if I want Indian food in Delaware I want it from Bawarchi!!!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We absolutely love this restaurant, one of our favorites in Boise! The owners are so nice and the food is authentic (the wife is cooks in the kitchen while the husband hosts up front). We always come back for the chicken madras and the butter chicken! The lamb dishes are great too. The garlic naan is out of this world, we usually order two! We've tried the other Indian restaurant in Boise and much prefer this one.
I literally cannot get enough naf naf (pun intended). The fresh pita, hummus, and falafel bowl was amazing! I can't wait to go back!

Did a Yelp filtered search by highest rating in my area and this place came up. I'm not sure I have ever seen a 5 star overall rating with over 100 reviews, so I proceeded to come with a co-worker. You would never find this place without looking very hard as it is tucked away. All the previous ratings and comments were spot on. Both food and service were exceptional. I also had blackened mango salmon and it was excellent with great presentation. But the service really set it apart. I felt like I was treated like a guest at their home (owners). Too bad I don't live in the area, or it would be on my favorites list.
The very best authentic pho soup in NJ, very generous amount and top notch quality. Highly recommended!

Had been waiting to get into this place for a while.. as seating is limited and it's usually booked. Finally made it last night -- and it was worth the wait. One of the best Italian meals I've ever had. The bread basket-- a home made array of yum.. included ricotta bread & tomato pie. Do yourself a favor and DON'T MISS the antipasto - not your usual standards- but a flavorful array of unique choices. Also loved the homemade spinach gnocchi and pasta w/ pistachio pesto sauce. Their panna cotta dessert was perfection. Can't wait to go back!
This place Rocks. I highly recommend stopping into this hidden gem. Try the Frozen Yogurt

The prices are a bit on the high side for a Vietnamese restaurant, but the quality is also high. I tried the Cambodian Noodle Soup called "Nam Vang" and it was amazing. I chose the rice noodle as my server recommended, and it is a chicken bone based soup with shrimp, fish cake, pork, etc. The soup was excellent and I loved all the ingredients in the soup. It was worth $10 + tax & tip.

This place was okay. The portions are huge. I agree with mike b. that the broth is definitely very well-seasoned. What I found lacking is other things in the soup. - meat. I usually get "everything" pho, the ones that have tendon, flank, brisket, tripes, etc. Their meat was tough, especially the brisket and flank: it felt like they didn't cook it low and slow long enough. The cut was a bit too thick which probably contributed their toughness. -noodles. they were a bit too overdone and soft. When I was picking up the noodles, they were breaking...which is never good. My wife got their vermicelli noodles with bbq pork. The BBQ pork had a very good bbq flavor, but overall the dish was a tad too salty. (And I like to eat things on the saltier side). Their bubble teas aren't so good either. Their tapiocas were tough and congealed. Their milk tea was a bit too thin for my taste (perhaps too much ice). So overall the experience is probably right around 3. It's not as good as the places on Washington Ave in South Philly. But it's worth checking out for those of you in South Jersey who don't feel like venturing across the state line. Just don't have too high expectations.

My boyfriend and I went here for an early Valentine's Day dinner. We made reservations but it turns out we didn't need them. There was practically no one there when we arrived, except for another couple. More on them later. The food was excellent - some of the best Thai food we've had (not that we're connoisseurs or anything, we just like yummy Thai food.) I got the duck fresh rolls and pork drunken noodles, and my boyfriend got fried calamari and pad see ew. We enjoyed it all. He even tried the duck (not too adventurous is he.) My biggest beef was the set up of the room. We were seated so close to the only other couple in the restaurant that we felt like we were on their awkward second date with them. They were definitely talking alot, and talking loudly. I tried giving them the side eye, but to not avail. Next time we'll just ask for a different table. And there will be a next time, unless we can find a way to have them deliver to Manayunk.
Best chicken Marsala I've ever had in my LIFE! Ghada and her family make you feel like you're an extended part of the family. Wonderful place with amazing food.
Usually have only positive things to say about this place, but sadly, vegan buffet was non-existent tonight without any explanation.
1st official Cute place, great food, awful parking, mediocre value (small portions)... but glad we checked it out!

A great Indian food experience. Variety menu and the staff very friendly. If you have any first time diners with you they go out of the way to explain dishes and levels of spices to make all diners at your table enjoy their experience. Have been several times and all items tried between our group were very good. BYO, small with lot parking

The service I just received here was exceptional! From opening the door for me, preparing my food extremely fast to coming around the counter to hand it to me! I was super impressed!! Great company!! Food is beyond exceptional!!

Food: 3. Good amount of food for the price. Nothing really great. Hot and sour soup smelled weird. Service: 1. all of our waters were empty most of the time and had to track down the waitress. My husband found a piece of metal string in his hibachi and they didn't offer to refund or anything. Still looking for a good Chinese place to eat
The chaat is great and the customer service is superb. The quantity and quality of this small restaurant is unmatchable. For those in or visiting Philly I highly recommend it!

Love the gyro salad; we always get our order to go, and they wrap the meat separately from the salad, and put the dressing in little covered containers so everything stays fresh. The spanokopita is very good, although you get a very small serving. They frequently sell out of baklava, but offered us other pastries that were just as wonderful.

Great food here with a cozy environment. I always start with panang curry at a new Thai place to get the feel for the food. The one here is served with more veggies than most and a medium is right where it should be on my heat scale. The thai iced tea is a good strong blend here too. The place is cozy but not crowded most nights. Just a nice calm and quiet environment. The only thing that surprises me about Thai on Grand tends to be that it's a bit pricey which I suppose means I should venture into the neighborhoods further away from my house to look for a deal but I just don't want to when the food is this good.

It's not just another Caribbean restaurant - it's a real Trini restaurant in Philly - finally! Having lived in NYC, and having many Trinidadian friends, I've tasted and enjoyed the upscale and street food cuisines of Trinidad and Tobago. Sadly, Philly lacked Caribbean options beyond jerk chicken and plantains.. until now. What a gem did I stumble on today! We had the goat curry and curry shrimp roti with bussupshot. Flavorful? Of course, it's a curry.. Quality? Great! You know quality when your curry has chopped up little pieces of all the peppers and spices used to make that rich flavor. We also asked for their hot pepper sauce and got a nice tangy sauce of freshly chopped habanero peppers. As other reviews have mentioned, the best part is that Caribbean hospitality Kevin and Anthony provide. Not even NYC places could match this. And well, if you know anything about Caribbean culture, hospitality and good vibes is quintessential of the island experience... and somehow tucked not to far from center city, I found the islands. It's a great place for a romantic dinner, with some great Caribbean tunes softly playing in the background. Large enough for group get together and also has a separate area for private parties. Can't wait till my next visit !
Went back again recently.... NOPE Hasn't changed, Still Outrageous and excellent... Please visit this place...
Great jerk chicken plate for lunch. Friendly lady behind counter. I'll be coming back next time I'm in town.

Being a Hawaii native, it's hard to find good Asian cuisine in the Midwest but this place hit the spot on Vietnamese cuisine. The food is reasonable priced and the pho portions are HUGE! they offer a Super Bowl which is even bigger. I haven't tried it here but they have this Vietnamese pancake which was something I ate almost every Sunday after church back home. Looking forward to the absolute deliciousness. The only reason they got a 4 out of 5 from me is the waiter dropped my straw (that was wrapped) on the floor and preceded to give it to me thinking I didn't see him lol.
Good food and good prices. Don't have much choice on drinks though. Only beer and soft drinks.

The first time I dined here over the summer, I was seriously impressed. The food was outstanding. But perhaps it was just because I was practically starving after Bastille Day festivities. When we returned recently for a friend's birthday dinner, the food was probably just as good, but the service was strange. Awkward and kind of inattentive. I'll cut them some slack since it was a busy Saturday night and we were a large party (of which there seemed to be several that evening.) That being said, I still really like Zorba's would definitely be back. Especially in the warm-weather months, it's nice to walk around Fairmount & BYO is always good with me.
This place is so much fun great cocktails as well as food. I love the ambiance and the food choices that make you push the envelop.

I have been to many Indian restaurants. India Sizzling II remains at the Top 1%. There are many other restaurants serving Indian food that are more Americanized. If you want real South Indian food, you should try India Sizzling. Chefs are from deep south India and bring out the best authentic Indian food at the affordable price that you can imagine. Their non-vegetarian food is really delicious. Especially, Mutton (Goat) Biryani is too good to miss. Recently, I went to this restaurant with bunch of friends for Lunch buffet. They have introduced many more items on the buffet and for the price they are charging, I can only get a "Foot-Long with drinks" at sandwich restaurant. India sizzling II-way to go.
Delicious food, Trinidad and Tobago stylee. They just added an amazing smoothie bar. I recommend the peanut punch, with extra peanut butter.
Good basic Indian, but stay clear of the fried appetizers (a bit heavy). Breads are great too. Good service, comfortable.

Food is nothing special. There's plenty of better Indian restaurants nearby (especially Saffron at Manchester & Barrett Station Roads) and the last time I ate there, I definitely had a cockroach crawl up the wall next to me. Haven't been back since, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

I was excited to come after all the great reviews but I ended up being quite disappointed. My mother got the rad na which contrary to one of the reviews was way too sweet. I got the veggie fried rice and my boyfriend got the basil fried rice. Both these dishes tasted fine and they had a lovely variety of vegetables. What disappointed me the most was the service. We had four different people serve us and they ranged from very nice to outright rude. One of the waitstaff kept ignoring us everytime we tried to ask for the check. Food was alright, atmosphere was okay (a little on the dirtier side), but the service is the reason why I will not be returning.
Really enjoyed this place. My favorite dish was their specialty. I forgot the name, But it's obvious on the menu what I'm talking about. The garlic naan was really good too.

Stopped here after looking at the great reviews. Ordered the garlic chicken, beef gyro hummus and falafel. I don't know if it was the time (8:30pm) or day of the week but everything seemed to be over seasoned. The garlic chicken had some sort of garlic paste on top that was entirely too potent. Same thing with the falafel. The gyro sandwich was toasted? Hummus was okay though.

There is a poem by Charles Hoffman that states, SPARKLING and bright in liquid light Does the wine our goblets gleam in, With hue as red as rosy bed Which a bee would choose to dream in. =============================================== It has been a while since I have had the food. (pre-yelpness) However it is the place I frequent after dancing late nights at The Spotted Cat! Once the tourists start piling in and we need air and a beverage; we meander down to Mojitos. They always have bands playing. First there was a Lounge Jazz singer and after her was a brass band. The bar staff is always quick, appropriately conversational, and deserving of tipping. The outside patio space is wonderful: water fountain, plenty of seating, and a bar.
Consistently good Vietnamese food. On par with vietnamese restaurants in NYC or Philly. Great customer service, large portions, and very reasonable prices. I've been coming back since they opened.

I've had delivery from Tandoor India a few times. Some of the vegetarian dishes I've tried are GREAT and definitely better than others I've had in Philly (including TIffin). The meat dishes I've tried (chicken & lamb) have been disappointing, except the fish, which was tasty. The raita & veg samosa are not bad. I'd heartily recommend: - saag paneer - channa masala - malai kofta 4 stars for the veg dishes but I'd avoid the meat dishes in general.

I came here for a quick Thai lunch on New Years Eve, mainly picked this place because it is in a very convenient location to Rittenhouse Square Park and Liberty Place. This is also close to the residential parking as well, because lets face it, putting paying for parking just sucks. The lady, probably the owner, is very friendly and the food came out quick and prompt. Everything we ordered was very flavorful and good: lemongrass soup, which is a chicken broth type of soup, not creamy; chicken pad see eww, very similar to chow fun in Chinese restaurants but way better tasting and more flavor; chicken pad thai, very good perfectly cooked. A place that I'd definitely return if in the mood for Thai and recommended for others to go!

Dear sweet Pollo Tropical why don't I eat with you more often? There's no denying my Hispanic heritage when you are around! I love to use your creamy black beans as sauce mixed with your cilantro mayo. I don't think there's anything you offer that I wouldn't rip apart in seconds. You sammiches are fresh, if a bit small, but you serve beer, and sangria. I don't care that you are a chain because every time you have done just fine.Your staff is friendly, your restrooms clean, and even your sauce station which is a disaster of modern engineering is impeccable. Hasta luego my fine feathered friend!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Stopped by this great restaurant while in Town on business. The food was fantastic and the host was very gracious and even sat and talked with us for a while at the end of the meal. The ghost pepper chops were absolutely delicious and had a great flavor and a wonderful spicy kick. If you are a fan of Indian food do not miss this gym.
Had takeout a few times from hear. Really nothing special. Flavor profiles of my lemongrass soup and pad Thai were very basic and bland.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in the city. As for Mediterranean I am torn between Dimitri's and Kanella. I've been to both Dimitri locations and really like both a lot, maybe too much. I've enjoyed everything I've ever had there which is probably more than half the menu at this point. My biggest dilemma is that I always want to go back to my comfortable favorites of grilled shrimp, mussels or shrimp pil pil but also want to try something new which leads me to always having leftovers. My bf and I came here on memorial weekend which was great and hardly a wait since half the city was missing. Memorial and labor day weekends are a great time to dine here since the wait will be much less. The shrimp pil pil is spicy with a great texture, slightly crispy. Recently we also tried the seafood Fettuccini and lamb entree dish. Both dishes were delicious and big. And the hummus is a must. I've also find the service to always be good. Only downside is cash only and the place is pretty small.

Nadia's is one of the best places in Lansdale hands down. Lunch is a great deal. Love the coconut soup and pad thai! Though their curry dishes are great as well. I've have dinned here many times and am always treated to a great meal that is consistently good.

2.5 stars for ambiance and decor--it's nothing special. 3.5 stars for pad thai, 2 stars for massaman curry--it was thick as if reduced or thickened and not particularly flavorful. Summer rolls were ok, not the best we've had not the worse. I doubt we'll return.

A friend and I decided to stop by for happy hour and dinner . Great atmosphere and perfect for both hanging out with friends or casual date . I was really happy to see that their was a labeled vegan burger on the menu . A tad pricy ($12) , but I expected it being on Beach Drive . Unfortunately , it was disappointing but a good effort on their part . The burger patty texture was mushy and in need of seasoning . The sauce was a little too runny for my liking . A thicker mayo consistency would have been perfect. The fries were thin and crisp . Absolutely delicious ! Our server was attentive , friendly and very helpful ! Would definitely return for happy hour . Half off their house brands!

I was a bit surprised I felt like the food didn't taste authentic I felt a bit of flavoring sweetness in the chicken tikka masala dish I was excited to have found something close to where I live but unfortunately the food didn't beat royal Indian cuisine and Bollywood spice . However The workers were super nice and the place was very clean it's just the one dish that I tried that I was disappointed with maybe other dishes taste different I don't know but the tikka masala is usually a signature dish for all Indian restaurants
This food is pho king pho licious. I will be back with my pho amily soon! (Sorry for the pho nny puns.)

La Va is a great little neighborhood cafe. Naturally, it has the typical selection of caffeinated beverages. I've tried only a few and they've been fine. But better yet, aside from the expected minor menagerie of pastries (which I haven't tried), they have tasty hot food options. My favorites, so far, as the jachnoon (available Saturdays only) and the burekas (with egg). La Va has a nice range of seating options (I know, not something you usually think about, until you go there). There are outdoors chairs and tables for enjoying the occasionally nice Philly weather. Inside, there are small tables, medium tables, and a variety of comfy sofas. Their operating hours are pretty good, prices reasonable, and staff generally friendly and competent.

Have been coming here for years, best boba in town! And they have great food too! My favorite is the Brian Special Banh Mi! And my favorite boba is the Melon Lovers. Great casual, little pricey but honestly not too bad! I come here often so I spend quite a bunch... They also have a punch card for boba purchases. Get a free boba slush for every 8 (I think) boba slush you get. Visit this place! They also have pho ;)

I don't think I've ever had such bland Asian food in my life. I guess that's what I got for ordering sushi at a little Chinese spot, but it really wasn't that good. Especially when they are charging sushi restaurant prices. I also got hot and sour soup. This was disappointing as it tasted watered down. And I didn't get any of those delicious little cracker noodle jawns. Even though delivery was quick, the food was lukewarm. Quite a feat. The only good thing I had was the egg roll, which are pretty hard to screw up I'd imagine. Unfortunately this was one and done for this kid. I prefer Fresh Grocer Asian food to what I just got.
Very nice restaurant hidden off gateway . Food was good and priced reasonably . There was not lots but it was tasty . Will try this place again at another date

We visited Manayunk for the first time because of the festival that was happening and we stumbled upon this wonderful and humble Mediterranean restaurant on Main St. The food is delicious and the service makes the experience even better! We had the beef gyro and shawarma and they were great especially when you pair them up with their pineapple or original lemonade. We would definitely come back to this place and if you're ever in the area, i recommend giving this place a try!
Hands down the best Chicken Döner I've had in America. Wow, it was amazing. Yes yes yes! I recommend this place to anyone. Hot, fresh and juicy.

I expected a great experience at this restaurant mainly due to all the great reviews we read online. Sadly the experience did not live up to the hype. The service was so-so. Our waitress was nice but the attention and service was lacking from the group as a whole. Appetizer and pasta (antipasto for two and spinach gnocchi) were pretty good but the entrees were so salty and otherwise lacking in flavor. The restaurant was also so ungodly hot that it became very uncomfortable and we were trying to get our check to leave which took about 10 minutes. We finally left the restaurant completely covered in sweat and in need of a shower. I found That's Amore and The Kitchen Consigliere much better, and their air conditioners work properly.
Amazing baklava!!!!! I loved the food it was delicious. They don't allow kids under 11 which makes it hard for me to go there as often, but other then that I loved it
Delicious food and the staff was excellent. Couldn't have asked for a better date night. Oh, you have to try the Thai Tea. DamnGood!!

The food here is absolutely the best. Been dreaming about coming back for weeks after trying out the Nashville location and then hearing that this location was even better. I wish I could give it the 5 stars it deserves, however with the experience I just had that's not possible. The young male working the phone and take out service knew literally nothing about the menu and was literally no help answering any questions that we had about the food that they served in the restaurant. When we got there to pick up our order he asked us what sauces we would like, but couldn't name any sauces they had nor did he ask where he could find the ones we requested from another person who worked there. We had to repeat everything we wanted multiple times, and had quite the difficult time with the menu as they were just pictures someone had taken and posted. Finding the menu online was also incredibly difficult, and I had to download the Yelp app to even look at it once I finally found it. All in all if you're going to work somewhere just please be knowledgeable about your products. Still love the food and will always come back, but will be saving the menu on my phone to save time and aggravation.

I've never had Ethiopian food before, and we were on the West side for an event and decided to give it a try. I must say, I was impressed with our server, the food and the decor. I honestly can't say how the food compares to other Ethiopian food, having never had it, but I WILL say it all tasted good, was fresh and hot, and quite unique. Our server was attentive without hovering, and the price was reasonable for what we received. I can see this as being a really fun place to try with a group. We'll be back.

The food was pricey, the atmosphere was too much (It was very crowded and loud), and they seemed to be shortstaffed, because the host was also delivery boy and a waiter at the same time? Food was pretty good, even though taste was overshadowed by everything else.

Drove clear across town (almost 20 miles) to try this place based on the other reviews. Mediterranean food has a special place in my heart and I was so stoked to give it shot. The place is small, with only about 10 tables, but the intimate setting was reminiscent of some of my favorite ethnic joints in NYC and San Francisco. The place was very clean and the decor had some cool pictures of Syria and various artifacts which were interesting to look at. The girl working the counter was very attentive and helpful. The food came out pretty quickly. So service was great, even though there only seemed to be one person working the front of the house. I orderd the Beef Kifta plate (Beef kabobs, dolmades, falafel, hummus, pita) and my husband had the Beef Kifta sandwich with fries. I'm extremely picky about hummus and thought it was some of the best I'd had in Tucson. Everything was extremely tasty, even my husband loved it. The only complaint he had was that he wished there were more food. But at less than $9 per entree, I definitely think it's a bargain. Next time we'll just order some extra hummus and pita as an appetizer (which is only $3!!) Can't wait to go back and try some of the other dishes! Big huge thumbs up :)

one of my favorite spots to meet up with friends, nice interior design, cool & friendly bartenders, just wish the outside seating is more organized, they have such a way to tell a 2 hours waiting for a seat outside that 2 empty tables are reserved then some group were setting inside the bar got out & just sat with no problem, other than this food was great service was good except you have to ask for another drink while they can see that you have an empty glass in hand, but I gave the servers the excuse for being really busy.
Food is OK. Nothing on menu stood out as special. Only ordered take out so cannot offer opinion on sit down dining.

We went and picked up take out from this place. We had ordered the channa chaat and the bhel puri - fairly standard chaat options at Indian restaurants. We had called ahead, and the food was ready to be picked in a timely manner. This was good since there isn't any on site parking, so had to illegally street park for a few minutes so we could quickly run and in out of the establishment. The ambiance inside looks fun and casual - perfect for lunch or dinner The space is hipster-ish, with bright walls and intimate seating. The decor has eastern influences, and there are some authentic la carte items for sale at the register (Thumps Up soda anyone =D). I was expecting a little more from this place from the reviews on Yelp. The food was "meh" at most. Both chaat items were missing the sev which is the best part! The spice level was bland and the dishes required some ad hoc home additions to spice up the taste. I don't think there was anything necessarily wrong with how the food was prepared, more the taste and execution of the dishes were sub par for Indian food (and my palate.) We also got some iced chai which was more milk than anything else. I was hoping they'd add more masala to get that "wake me up" feeling. If I HAD to...I would probably give this place one more shot, this time as a dine in experience in case the other menu options live up to the other reviews on Yelp. Otherwise there is probably better fare elsewhere.

We sat in the wine room part of the restaurant. The only negative was the loud disco music piped in from the happy hour bar. Otherwise an excellent meal was had by each of us. The Hangar steak was perfect. Olivia was our server. Very friendly and professional as well as attentive to our every need.

I'm going to go out on a limb and say that this is my favorite restaurant in Philly. I don't usually like to limit myself to only one favorite (when it comes to anything), but there's just something so magically right about the cozy space, open kitchen, and WONDERFUL food here. Every time I've come here, we've ordered the hummus, grilled octopus, and snap peas (usually snap peas are nothing to rave about but the ones here are crisp, tender and come with the most delicious tomato sauce and feta combination). Coming here is kind of an event and it might take multiple hours (but hey, it's the mediterranean way) so put your name down, get a drink across the street at New Wave and wait until they come and get you. Then once you're sitting down, you can pop open your preferred BYOB wine and order a buttload of the most delicious amazing fantastic food to share (it's the best way to do it). Then hours later, you'll realize you're in a food coma and you might need to undue the top button, but it's okay, because everyone around you will be so content and happy they won't care.

We've moved to st.louis 8 months ago.since then we've been there 4 times, because its close from my apartment and its cheap..we only been there for launch buffet..I am a culinary student so I know how does the buffet work..So I have no complain about their quality but I do have problem with their service..their food trays are empty and it takes them 10-15 mins to refill the tray..the server will never talk to you unless you ask them something..they offer free refill for sodas..but the server will never let you know that..but the good thing is they have more items compairing to other indian restaurants who serves buffet..

The customer service was great, but the the food was average! We tried many dishes: Pad See Ew, Pumpkin curry, Yellow curry, Spicy fried rice, Pineapple fried rice, and the Spicy noodle tofu. Each dish seemed too salty and nothing stuck out as being particularly noteworthy. It's a cute little place though!

I wanted to love Palace of Asia, but I can only give three stars since I either loved or really didn't care for the dishes that we ate. We started with the Mixed Appetizer for Two, which I didn't love at all. Everything on the plate was battered and fried. The only thing I really liked from this appetizer was the Harabhara Kabab (spinach ball). Yes, that was deep fried as well, but it wasn't coated like a McDonald's chicken nugget, like the rest of the things on the plate. I mean, really, you take a potato slice and deep fry it? That's it? No, thanks. For our entrees we got the Tandoori Mixed Grill and the Panir Masala (note that I actually ORDERED the Palak Panir, which is a spinach-based dish, but what came out was the Panir Masala, a tomato-based dish). We also got some garlic naan. I didn't love the Tandoori Mixed Grill as much as my husband did. I really liked the chicken, but I couldn't get on board with the lamb (it was ground lamb, and to me, it looked like sausage). The shrimp was also pretty tough to chew. I have to say that my favorite part of the entire meal was dipping the garlic naan into the Panir Masala. While I wasn't super fond of the cheese cubes in the sauce (because of the texture), they were OK in moderation. The flavors, though, with the garlic naan and the tomato sauce...mmmm, that was good. So, in the end, dinner was OK overall, with three components combining to make two stand-out dishes (the spinach balls and the tomato based cheese cube dish/garlic naan). I don't know if I'll be making any desperate attempts to return, but I don't regret going. Also - this place is f'ing GIGANTIC. The end!

Zagol's food is absolutely delicious, but you have to be willing to try something new. There are no forks, spoons, or knives - you use the flat/spongy bread as your utensil. The injera (the flat bread) was not what I expected it was going to be. It is served cold, and it reminds me of a sponge, but you quickly get over that once you taste all of wonderful food! A large group of us went and we ordered a lot of food - Doro Wat, Alicha, Key Wat, Gored Gored, and Zilzil Tibs all of which were amazing. The only thing I would change is to have more of the bread, because in my opinion they didn't serve enough of it in comparison to the amount of food they give you. The owner was very nice and talked a lot about the background of the food and the tables all have interesting facts about Ethiopia on them, which are fun to read while you wait for your food.

Followed recommendation of the server in last visit and the results were great. Have visited 3-4 times including take out. Usually great, sometimes when venturing into unknown dishes just okay. Especially like the freshness of the ingredients. Friendly staff and prompt service.

We went because of the good reviews. I'm disappointed. The shredded pork Banh Mi was mainly bread & pickled onions. The shrimp paste on sugar cane appetizer was good. The French iced coffee with milk was good. My man got the pork chop, which was the best tasting part of the visit. The service sucks & they were kinda mean. We actually heard the waitress tell the man next to us that he wouldn't like several items on the menu because the description on the menu wasn't what the dish actually was. What?! The women's restroom needed a good scrubbing...or two. If this place is one of the best Vietnamese restaurants, Nashville's got some 'splaining to do. (I always try to give a place at least 2 visits before I write it off. I will go back and try the Pho...eventually.)

This is my first time writing a review ever. This place is one of the best Ethiopian places I have been to. The owner and staff are very very welcoming and attentive. The food is amazing!!!!! I am from Dallas and heard a lot about this place. Finally got to try it... As soon as I had the first bite - left me speechless. I am sure I am going to crave this food as soon as I go back! Definitely a must try!!!!

What a great place, staff was amazing. If you have the chance to meet David ask him to show you a trick! The view is stunning. It's a great Florida hidden Jem, if you are looking for something off the beaten path, hang with some locals, look no further.

As locals,we have ordered food to go twice. Both times, it was delicious! The Vegetable Samosas, Shrimp Curry, Chicken Korma were all good. I am not giving it 5 stars only because we have only ordered take out thus far. But we plan to eat there soon. I am thrilled that there is a good Indian restaurant in Newtown!
Amazing! Best Indian food in town. Low key and super cheap but the food tastes like a million bucks. Perfect for a lunch break or cheap dinner.

Loved eating at Aman's, since they opened the first restaurant in East Norriton. Unquestionably the best Indian food in the area, excellent service, and very clean restaurants. It's also nice have a branch open up close to home for takeout. The only reason I do not give it 5 stars is the dinner portions relative to the price. Lunch is all-you-can-eat amazing food for $13/person, so spending twice that on dinner where the entree portion is frequently small enough that you find yourself counting the pieces of meat is a bit disappointing.

I love this place for many reasons but the first is that they don't laugh when I point to a letter on the menu to order. The second is that I love Pho, but despite it being a beef broth soup I prefer it to be made only with vegetables (Pho Rau Cai). Not only do they cater to my specific want but they do it well. The Pho Rau Cai is loaded with veggies like broccoli, more so than at any other restaurant around. They also bring a hearty offering of condiments (bean sprouts, basil leaves, cilantro and jalapeños). Oh, and the better part is that the small bowl of Pho is $4.95! The small bowl is all I've ever needed to fill up, but for only $1 more you can get the large bowl. It's fantastic. Remember to bring cash though, they don't accept cards. Also, they only carry Pepsi products for all you Coke snobs.
Great service and delicious Thai food. Large selection of vegetarian options. Would definitely recommend this restaurant !!

The Smiling Elephant has been on my radar for a while, but for one reason or another I just never made it there until recently when a sweet friend of mine wanted to have her birthday dinner there. Good food and good birthday celebration = win-win! This was really a kick in pants for me that made me re-evaluate everything. What have I been doing wrong for the last five years that caused me to miss eating at the best Thai place in Nashville? WHY DIDN'T Y'ALL TELL ME I WAS WRONG!? Smiling Elephant is, in my humble opinion, the best Thai food I have had in the south. Located on 8th Ave South, the Smiling Elephant feels like a retreat. The front is adorable and there's a little patio where you can enjoy your curry al fresco. Inside, the dining room is small and heavily decorated with wood. I was surprised by how small this place truly is. We were there pretty early, about 5:30pm and the place filled up quickly, and it was just a Tuesday. This is a sign that you are on the right track for a good meal. To start, we ordered the fresh rolls. I love these things, but you would be surprised how many places mess them up. These rolls were great; sticky on the outside but crunchy and fresh on the inside. The chili sauce gave a nice little spice to balance out the mild vegetables. For my meal I ordered the "set" which comes with soup and dessert. I chose the Tom Yum lemongrass soup and I was impressed by its mild and pleasing taste. It was full of fresh vegetables that were still crunchy. I love that they threw the spinach in at the last minute so it was just barely cooked. For my entree I ordered tofu pad thai. I know it's boring and the typical Thai food go-to but hey, it's a good way to find out if a Thai place is solid. They warn you in the menu that this is not the sweet/sticky "Americanized" pad thai that you are are used to, so I was intrigued. Their pad thai is prepared how true pad thai is supposed to be. It was filled to the brim with bean sprouts and egg and I could taste the vinegar in it. The best part was the wider-than-average green bean noodles. The texture of these was sublime and makes me never want to go back to regular rice noodles. Steve ordered the Karee curry, which was the curry of the day. The Smiling Elephant only does one type of curry a day to ensure the freshest and best taste. This is an idea I can get totally behind. The Karee was a variation on a red coconut curry and it was delightful. The sauce was smooth and the vegetables once again were crisp- not soggy and overcooked. I really enjoyed the pickled cucumber and red onions that accompanied the spicy curry. For dessert we both had coconut custard. At first I was surprised because it was really tiny, but it was so rich I don't think I could have eaten more than one. It was full of coconut flavor and very creamy and sticky- the perfect consistency where it sticks to the spoon and your tongue. Overall, I was very impressed with the Smiling Elephant. The staff was friendly and the food came out super fast. Everything that we had was delicious, the best Thai I've had in Nashville. I can tell that this is the beginning of a long love affair with the Smiling Elephant.

Worst restaurant in the area. This is an expensive, Bangladeshi restaurant with no quality of food. Even Veg Biryani costs $15 that too with all frozen veggis. I hope another good Indian restaurant or franchise takes over this restaurant which is at a prime location. Unfortunately they make the worst, tasteless, unhealthy food on this planet. If you happen to be from south Asia you would curse them badly before you come out for sure. Even after reading this review you wanna try out then you are the craziest guy.

Okay, if I close my eyes for a second- the second I take the first bite... alright it kind of feels like home. It does. I know that's not you dad behind the counter, but he does a damn good job at making those sandwiches I'd bring to school and get the quizzical looks from my fellow third graders. They know what they are doing here.

Have been here several times, I really enjoyed the hummus plater. I also have had the chicken pita sandwich, it was also very good and the chicken was tender. I wasn't too crazy about their potato salad, but their slaw is really good so are the rosemary beans. the salads are made with a vinaigrette dressing instead of mayo. It's a good place for fast food that's healthier than the usual.

As good of Thai food as you get in Nashville. If you are used to food from somewhere with larger Thai population then this will not thrill you but you won't go home disappoint with the right expectations.

Gigi and Big R serves up Caribbean or soul food that's all right -- it's not the best but also not bad. Fried fish: okay, but too dry 2.5 Jerk chicken: flavour was fine, chicken was overcooked 3 Curry chicken: flavour was okay, chicken was stringy 3 Mac & cheese: not very good, I wouldn't get this again 1.5 Candied yams: very nice, soft and sweet 3.5 Collards: basic but done right 3.5 Out of what I've tried, my favourite foods are probably the candied yams and collard greens (these are side dishes).

I've been a fan of Indian food for as long as I can remember, and am always up for trying new restaurants. Generally I gravitate toward places with buffets so I can sample as many dishes as possible, however during our visit to Haveli there was only waiter service, so I had to... decide (gasp!!) Thankfully our server was incredibly helpful, and steered me toward a dish that was absolutely perfect - panir makhni - cheese with onions, tomatoes, and fresh herbs. The garlic naan, mango lassi, and Indian tea were also completely flawless. No complaints here, just lip-smacking appreciation.

I recently moved from Hawaii and Thai food among other asian cuisines are very common. It all comes down to which restaurant serves the best Thai, Chinese, Korean and Filipino food. So I had high expectations for this small Thai restaurant. As I walked in the restaurant I noticed the cool decor. Tables were covered in multi-colored fabrics, It was pretty busy. Most importantly It looked clean. Cleanliness is big with me. I decided on trying something small. I tried the summer rolls. The summer rolls were ok, but it had very little shrimp and chicken. It had a whole lot of lettuce, but the sauce that accompanied the rolls was delicious. I would have given this place five stars if it wasn;t for the extra small peices of chicken and shrimp. I will be returning soon.:)

Ate here while in PA for work. What an absolute treat! The restaurant is beautifully decorated and has a very nice dining atmosphere. It's pretty cozy despite seating a good amount of people. The menu has a ton of variety and if you're a fan of Thai food you'll for sure find all the go-to yummies you're accustomed to. I was only here once so unfortunately I was only able to try one of their dishes but my entire group of 15+ people all enjoyed their meals. I ate one of the specials for that evening and was blown away. Thai cuisine uses curries, coconut milks, fish sauce, chilies, and has several dishes that feature that signature Thai sweetness. Thai Orchid was definitely a step above the rest when it comes how their food is prepared and the quality of their ingredients. The flavors are absolutely top notch. Last but certainly not least, I have to bring up how great the service is here. I'm giving Thai Orchid 5 stars because my dining experience was wonderful from start to finish. The service was fantastic. Very friendly, very attentive, prices were great, food was phenomenal, and I'm very sad that I live all the way out in Texas. Be sure to check them out if you're in the neighborhood!
Very good food. Great vegetarian options, but the summer rolls are average. The sauce on the summer rolls is delicious, which helps make up for it. We always have good service and a good experience.

The pho broth is excellent. This place is very popular and very fast. The restaurant is clean and they serve you very quickly. I ordered the #1 which has a lot if off-cuts of meat, like tendon and tripe with beef balls... Not testicles but actual meatballs. I wasn't really ready for unusual (gross?) cuts of meat but it tasted so good! They carry sliced regular meat (I think it's TRI-tip but I could be wrong). The menu also has an assortment of other meat and noodle items. This is now my favorite pho because the broth is so tasty.

Fantastic food!! I had the tacos and they were delicious. My daughter has the bun (noodles) with tofu and it was amazing. My son had the pho (soup like) and even though it was a tad salty, it didn't stop him from eating all of it. It was a huge bowl as was the bun. There were four of the "bun type" tacos and they were filling. We also has the egg rolls and they were just as good as everything else. The place is small and quaint. Service is great. Anything you don't know is explained to you. We will be going back again and again. Price is perfect!
It would be wrong to put this in the same category as common street food. Be prepared to wait, but know that it is well worth it.

We have been here twice and both times we have had a great meal and at a great value. The place is byob which means you can bring your favorite wine or go hard and a little boozy , they will provide juices to mix with. Our first time there a few months ago we tried the lamb that was juicy and flavorful and fall off the bone good. Our second time there we had the beef kabob , again flavorful and delicious. The staff are very friendly and attentive. This will definitely be our go to spot every time we come to philly.

With a name like this, it is unsurprising that Pho King has T-shirts and ballcaps for sale. The food was certainly worth it! I enjoyed some fried tofu and a curried chicken on noodles dish on my latest visit and the food was really quite good (that fried tofu was delicious!). I also enjoyed my tea. The bathroom was clean if a bit bizarre looking aesthetically. A popular place to visit in this area, I am pretty happy with the food quality and would certainly return.

I have enjoyed all my dining experiences at the Pita Jungle. The staff is friendly and the place is clean. I also have enjoyed the food here. It's a bonus that it is conveniently located just up the street from where I live. I look forward to my next dining experience at Pita Jungle.

Hands down the best Thai food I've ever had. My boyfriend and I split a "set" of the Pad Thai, which means it came with coconut soup, and a small dessert. I loved that the Pad Thai was gluten free. It's authentic, so not like the Americanized Pad Thai that's really sticky and a lot of sauce, so keep that in mind. The coconut soup was creamy, with large bites of vegetables. I normally don't like coconut soup and made a face when my boyfriend ordered it, but was thoroughly surprised by the light flavor, and could have eaten a whole bowl myself. The dessert was a custard. It was warm, and only a couple bites. A nice end to the meal, but not something I'd typically order or think it worth to order by itself if you're not getting it with your meal. Portions are large and you will be taking some home, unless you split a meal like we did.
Very generic Gyro. Asked for lamb, but it looked and tasted like steak. Won't be coming back here again. If your food is going to be generic, at least serve it with a smile.....

Fun atmosphere and great for groups! Came here for a friend's birthday and were thrilled that it was a BYOB. We had to be moved several times unfortunately, but once we were settled we had a great time. The music and decor are awesome and make it feel like you're definitely not in Philly anymore. As for the food, we enjoyed everything we ate. Just hope the people you're with are clean and all about that hand washing since you all eat with your hands. The dancers were a fun touch as well and after some wine we were all up dancing. Great experience overall! Head's up though it is CASH ONLY- come prepared also, parking is a pain the butt so just take a cab or patco over wherever you're coming from

I gave this 5 stars just because I'm so excited that there's pho in IV, but I have since reviewed my rating because they close at 8 PM on saturday. What kind of restaurant does that? I'm from the bay area so I'm accustomed to much better pho for way less, but since I can't be there, this is really good for IV standards. It's perfect for a rainy day and you can't go wrong with the brisket pho. Last time I went I came around closing time and went next door to IV drip and when it was ready he brought it over to me. I think I'm going to have some pho tonight. Wish they delivered or let SB menus deliver though : /

This was a delicious foodie experience. The food was five-star. I ordered the vegetarian Queen's Eight (chef's choice, 8 tastes) so that I could try many things and have a variety of spicy and mild. I also ordered the Ethiopian tea which was different and yum (a cinnamon tea). It's imported and delicious. My great 8: salad (wet, soggy delicious), a chickpea type "hummus" (great), atkilit--cabbage, tikiki-carrots, taters (mild, tasty), mushrooms wot (a favorite, but bitey), ye misr wat-red lentils, ye kik alecha-yellow split peas, gomen-collards. A single vegetable meal was $8, the Eight was $13 and I took half home. The injera is made with an African flour (grown in the US) called "teff". It soaks in the stew broth and is fabulous. (gluten-free). They have beef, chicken, lamb and seafood options and a great appetizer and African wine list. Most foods are sauteed or stewed, your choice to amp it up with spice or go mild. I took a star for service--both doors are marked "use other door" so it's unclear & unwelcoming to get in. The waitress appeared exhausted and seemed very slow to take my order and others, check on you, etc. Dirty tables were not being cleaned off. Butcher paper is laid across cloth table cloths but there is food between the layers-kinda icky. Each table has hand sanitizer on it--that's a nice touch. Cloth napkins. yay. Bright orange walls, African art. The place has a homey feel and a great "spirit". It needs to fix some rough edges to be fully a "class act". I am anxious to try more of the menu. Go when you have time so the speed of the experience doesn't become a problem! July 2014. Had a delightful lunch. Food is still excellent. Service was swift. Veggie options are excellent. Meat options are "fall off the bone" (which is a little overdone for me). Friday lunches they do a $10 buffet. A great cultural experience.

Hours say they are open for lunch until 4pm, showed up today at 1pm and not a single soul in sight. Really disappointed that I didn't get to try their food. Wish they would operate true to their hours posted.

Out of this world. Upon entering, we were immediately seated despite not having a reservation. My favorite part was the complete lack of menu - the waiter just arrived and told us that we would be enjoying a 7 course meal that was pre-set and simply gave us the choice of lamb or chicken for our main course. I am not a picky eater so I really liked not having to choose and having the opportunity to enjoy what the restaurant thought were their best dishes and this enhanced my experience. The first dish was my favorite, composed of three different salads and was my favorite part of the meal. The carrots and eggplant were perfectly spiced and I could have eaten the portion meant for 3 people entirely by myself. The spicy chicken was probably the best chicken I've ever had. I know that sounds like a stark exaggeration but I kid you not - go try it. The lamb was perfect and fell off the bone, and the spicy sauce that we had served on the side is what made the dish perfect. I especially enjoyed the ending note - baklava and moroccan mint tea which was delicious and perfectly balanced. Along with this they give us a huge bowl of fruits and let us take it home when we were too full to even touch it. All in all this is a place where I would bring friends, family, etc for the ethnic and cultural experience unlike anything I have enjoyed before and the food was mouth watering as well. Never have I been able to eat so much in one sitting. I will most definitely be back!

We tried to order from here the night before. They never got our order.... but we were really craving some good thai... so we tried again. I ordered 1 vegetable tom kha and 1 chicken tom kha. They sent 2 chicken.. so I had no soup. My husband got the singapore noodles and enjoyed them. I got the massaman curry with tofu... and it was a giant tub of soup... with a few vegetables floating around in it. I'm used to significantly more vegetables and tofu... more like a stew consistency. That being said, if it were good, that would have been doable. It was so saccharine sweet that I threw the whole thing away, had a few bites of rice, then just went to bed. It was a total bummer of a meal... sorta ruined my night. I've had Massaman Curry numerous times from several places... so it wasn't an expectation thing. We won't be back ordering from here again...

looked forward to this joint due to how close it is to my place on the loop. the tikka masalas are only OK compared to the other indian restaurants in saint louis. usually, these are made with a LOT of tomato sauce but is cooked with enough spices, other ingredients, and in such a way that you no longer taste the tomato sauce. that is not the case here, as the tikka masala was unfortunately more tomato sauce than anything else. to add insult to injury they included but a small portion of rice. for a place that is in the hole-in-the-wall segment, every little thing counts. extra rice cost more, that is a no-no in my book for hole in the walls. compared to the 4 other indian restaurants within half a mile away on the loop, and house of india in the other direction, this is at the bottom of that list.

The food here was amazing. I had the: 1. Fried calamari 2. Tomato and Mozzarella Salad 3. Seafood Combo (more like seafood soup). Everything was prepared just to the point of deliciousness, nothing too fancy or over-thought. The smells coming the kitchen could almost be an appetizer on their own. The only fault I have with the restaurant has to do with space. We went with a party of 8 and were crammed into 2 tiny tables (I think because they were simply trying everything they could to get us in- which is great!). So, it is probably more suited for small, intimate groups.

Had the carrot and crab bisque which was delicious but was served warm by the overwhelmed Sat night waitress. Ordered the Rack of Veal special which was very very fatty, undercooked and like chewing a rubber ball. I sent back for additional cooking and it came back no better. Recommendation to Francisco - remove this item from the menu. I much prefer their sister restaurant in Newtown.

Had a great experience here for our anniversary dinner :). Love the ambiance, and our waiter and busser were so polite and attentive. I had the lobster ravioli which was piping hot and decadent, and my boyfriend had the lamb shanks with spaghetti - the lamb was very flavorful. We each had Caesar salads to start, and for dessert we split the chocolate lava cake a la mode! The best dinner I've had in a long time. Upscale comfort food. I will be back to check out the bar side very soon!

Eating here is like dining in a 7-11. Horrible atmosphere. The food was pretty decent though. Especially the basmati rice, vegetable samosas, and the naan. The chicken tikka masala was quite heavy (but delicious) I am kind of big on atmosphere though. This establishment needs to hire a decorator, ASAP.

Try the stuffed chicken wings and the curry duck. I've never been to Thailand but I've eaten Thai from coast to coast and this is about as good as it gets. Next time I go to Santa Barbara I will make it a point to eat here again.

Fair little Thai place - the owner was away, and the Taiwanese lady kept selling "Taiwan". If I had wanted Chinese I would have gone to a Chinese place. Seemed like Thai dishes were cooked in the Chinese style - wrong ingredients and poorly seasoned. There has to be better Thai in the St. Louis area, but I have not yet found it. While the food is palatable, maybe once the owner returns from Thailand the quality and flavor will improve.

Thai food is not in my normal rotation, so I don't have a great frame of reference for this review. That said, I thought the food was very good, the service excellent and the prices reasonable - what more could you ask!! We started with the shrimp in a blanket appetizer and find it quite delightful, crispy yet light and flavorful; I then move to the curry - I opted for gringo hot - the heat built nicely without being overwhelming and interplayed well with the sweetness of the coconut. Finally, we finished with the cinnamon chips and found them to be just a bit liberal with the powered sugar, but otherwise quite wonderful and, unfortunately for me, quite "cravable."

I have a strange love-hate relationship with the Remedy Café. I love the location, the energy and intention of the staff, the promise of the menu, and the design and décor: the big, bright windows and comfortable chairs perfect for lounging are a great counterpoint to the cold and chill out-of-doors. I hate that the menu doesn't deliver the excellence it promises, the food is just 'good', the flavors are very westernized without the subtle touches I've found in Indian / Pakistani restaurants. (Remedy is still better than many other lunch offerings, but not as good as it could be.) I hate that the chai varieties are good, but not great, with a pre-made flat flavor that completely lacks the subtlety that a really good chai delivers. On the rare occasions that I make a simple chai at home, I can get a better flavor with only a handful of spices, toasted before make the brew. I know Remedy can do better. Still four stars: Remedy is a comfortable and pleasant place to spend time, with a good selection of coffee, chai, and juices. All it would take is one inspired manager to make Remedy a five-star happening.

My go to viet place in town! I'm Vietnamese and this is the best spot for viet food in Edmonton. I only wish I had found it earlier. The place is always packed which is a great sign. Reasonable prices and generous portions. The grilled beef (and grilled pork) salad rolls are to die for. Seriously - try them. Better than my mom's! Hot, quick, delicious food at a decent price. Nice people. Would and have recommended to friends and family. The only "cons" are the tables are really close together but it doesn't bother me personally.
Excellent food. Could eat there anytime! Googly recommend if younge ever in Tampa! Everything is good!

The food here is flavorful and fresh, with decent prices. The lunch buffet (offered 7 days a week) is a great value. The Drexel Hill location is BYOB. The service is always adequate, ample parking is available, and the restaurant is clean. The decor is so-so, and the ripped up booths could use a little bit of TLC. However, this doesn't get in the way of their great food, so I keep coming back.

UPDATED as of 4/30: After a misunderstanding with GrubHub and Nirvana Fusion, Grubhub gave me a small coupon for a future order. My boyfriend and I decided to try out Nirvana Fusion again on a night we knew they were open as their menu still looked really delicious. I was estimated a little over an hour delivery time, and they showed up in only 25/30 minutes. I wasn't able to answer the door, but the man who delivered the food was actually the owner. He came to personally apologize for the mix-up and even gave us a free appetizer. After hearing his story (the incident was the same day of the Nepal earthquake, and he is from Nepal), I realize that I acted extremely harshly when I first had an issue. Granted, in hindsight, I was just REALLY hungry, and really looking forward to delicious food and was really disappointed when I found out they were closed and could not deliver my order. The manner in which Nirvana Fusion handled this situation went above and beyond. On top of that, the food was AMAZING. I will certainly be ordering from here again. Previously: 1 Star. I was promised food delivery by 8:30pm today. I figured I would give the restaurant a call when it hit 8:40pm, just to check to see if our order was out for delivery, and for an update on how much longer it would take. I called, and the line simply rang several times, before going to a standard answering message stating that the voicemail box was full. I tried calling again, hoping that someone would answer so I could find out where my SEVENTY DOLLAR food order was. This is extremely unprofessional. If my food does not arrive within 15 minutes, I will be filing a formal complaint through Grub Hub. Turns out the restaurant is closed on Mondays. Would have been nice to know by their website. Grub Hub had them listed as being open Mondays, and apparently the restaurant has "tried to get them to change this, but failed." Hard to believe when so many other restaurants who are closed on Mondays have the correct hours posted.
Food was really good. We were the only people there, lol. I have a feeling that weekends are much more crowded.

Wow. What a find. This is not your typical meal - so be advised you need a reservation in order to get a table. We made our reservation a few weeks in advance. Once you walk in you automatically get a great feel for the type of service and knowledge the staff has of the menu. You are encouraged to ask questions to learn more and to ensure the server will recommend the right dish for your appetite. We started with 3 apps: antipasto (see picture), grilled shrimp, and fennel sausage. All were amazing. The antipasto was one of the best spreads I have ever seen. For the pasta course we had the gnocchi. Again, out of this world. For mains we had the rabbit and the swordfish. See pictures below. I couldn't believe how amazing the food and service were. I was not expecting this in colingswood but cannot wait to come back and try it again. The server also mentioned on Mondays they have a bbq out back which sounded really cool.

This was a delicious dinner. We got Thai iced tea..best I've ever had... an appetizer, 2 entrees and the mango ice cream dessert for $35. E got the drunken noodles with beef, I got the ginger chicken with black mushrooms. I can't wait to go back.. E might not be in as a big hurry...I spent much of the car ride home chanting, "We found yummy Thai food! We found yummy Thai food!"

I don't get the ravings. I'm not a tea drinker, so I can't comment on the chai. My ex seemed to like it. The service I had was always friendly enough, if slow, but but the samosas and masala are terrible. This is not Indian food. I have had Indian food (the home cooked kind), and this is not it. It wasn't even good by regular standards. The desserts were meh. Then again, I'm used to having home made desserts by a very talented French man. Am I spoiled? Maybe. But this place is nothing to rave about in my books. I ordered a chocolate milk from them once, and I asked if it was going to be just plain and simple. The girl at the counter said yes. It came out all spiced with cinnamon and god knows what else. I left with a massive headache. If this is your thing, and you like fake ethnic food, be my guest. Remedy is not my *ahem* cup of tea.

This is the best Vietnamese food in Indy. They have everything I've been craving for since I moved away from Southern California: banh cuon, clay pot, hot pot, banh xeo, even freaking durian shakes! I love this restaurant so much I would marry it.
I love the staff here, they went out of their way to make sure we were happy. 11/10; will dine again. Oh, right, the food was great, lol.

I've been to this place a few times over the past two years. Not the best food in my opinion. They have a lunch and dinner buffet, but the options are slim compared to some of the other places around. Good thing is that its never very busy -- so finding an open table is fairly easy!
I've had the Pa-Nang Chicken from the lunch menu many times, it's sooooo good I can't bring myself to order anything else when I eat there.

I really want this place to be great - it just isn't.
