I live about a block from LaVa and have a serious obsession with coffee (one of the only excuses to really live, if you ask me) but LaVa is just mediocre. The cappucinos are ok and the coffee is fine just nothing is worth choosing this coffee spot over the abundance of others in the city. The few times I have tried food it has been horrid. I don't know if maybe I am just getting the burekas on a bad day or the quiche a day late but I have never walked away satisfied with the food. All in all, this is a good spot to meet a friend for a coffee or grab a quick cap to go. In my opinion, for what it's worth, it's worthwhile to find another spot you may be happier with. The barristers, on average, are pretty nice and the service is always good so they at least have that going for them! Oh and FYI they have a credit card minimum that exceeds the average purchase so bring cash!

Took a chance by showing up at 5:00 with no reservations. Walked in and there were about 10 tables open. The nasty hostess wouldnt seat us without a reservation. She was rude and had a puss on her face as if she didnt want to be there.
Food is good. Chicken Bryani best I've had outside India. Service not so good.

I'm indonesian and this is our go-to place for affordable, missing my mom's home cooking, meals. I even introduced my co-workers (who never had Indonesian food) and they thoroughly enjoyed their meals. The place is small so I usually go at off hours (late afternoons on weekends) to avoid the crowd, or do takeouts. Parking is a street parking but i never have to spend more than 5 minutes looking for a spot. The food comes out quick, and service is decent. I've had most items on the menu, but my favorite are: * mie komplit - it really is complete. i usually add very little of the broth * bubur ayam (weekdays only) - similar to congee, and the official comfort food * sky pork rice platter - delicious platter of various pork yumminess * nasi uduk - great if you want a lighter portion, and it's only $4! On a side note, these are still delicious, but: * soto medan is thicker than the soto i'm used to * satay padang medan is spicy * lontong sayur is super spicy. i had to take breaks to cool down my mouth

Yay!! Third time is the charm! I had tried coming here twice before, and the wait was too long (45 min one time, 1 hour the second time) so we went elsewhere (they don't take reservations). This time, a friend and I arrived early, 5:30, on Sunday evening in kind of yucky weather, and we had no trouble getting a table. I had to try the much talked about Fire and Ice cocktail and was not disappointed! Slightly sweet, slightly spicy, and very good! We split an order of guacamole, which was plenty large enough for the two of us. It was made with good fresh avocado, tomatoes and jalapeños and came with a large portion of chips. Our entrees came out a little too fast; it was maybe 10 minutes after the guacamole arrived, and we we were still enjoying our guacamole and chips but now also had our beautiful looking and wonderful smelling entrees. So, we dove into the entrees while still grabbing a chip and guacamole here and there. I had the enchiladas de pato that so many other Yelpers have been raving about, and they were absolutely wonderful! Three tortillas with a surprisingly large portion of tender tasty duck in a delicious, flavorful sauce. The tres leches cake is also as good as everyone has been saying. The lime topping is an amazing delicious twist on this traditional dessert. Prices are really very reasonable for this quality of food. I really hope they decide to start taking reservations at some point! It would make it much easier to come here more regularly, particularly if we're headed to a movie or a show at Clowes after dinner.

The atmosphere is really cozy, I absolutely recommend making reservations for the table on the window. It has a bunch of pillows and you sit on the floor. It is also a byo, which is great. I had a lot of fun here, their hookahs are really good. The food wasn't amazing but I am giving it 4 stars because I really enjoyed the place.

One thing that comes to mind after entering the place. Clean! It does not smell like an Indian restaurant like Sitar, Karma or Samosa. The place has a seating for only 12-15 and the place is perfect for a quick in and out buffet. I would recommend this place only if the group is small and do not care about the ambiance as much as the taste of the food. The menu is very limited for the buffet. The price is per pound of food you take. If you are super hungry, 1.5 pounds of food will be perfect for you. Bread is extra. Overall - great food, hole in the wall.
This place is absolutely amazing - hands down the best panir masala I've ever had. The prices were very reasonable, as well. I'll definitely be stopping by again the next time I'm in Indy.

Awesome lunch special, would come back for sure! Soup or salad, entree and appetizer for $9. We were very pleasantly surprised and the service was great too. Out side patio has comfortable seating and shade. D. Davis Newport Beach
Not sure what the negative reviews are about. Our food came out fast and super fresh. Everyone enjoyed their meal and the service was great!
Very clean, nice people, reasonably priced. If you like good Indian food then this is a great place to try. For take out they charge by the container, not the pound. The naan bread was PERFECT!

LOVE LOVE LOVE! we are regulars here. Healthy, delicious, lots of options. They usually have a special of the day. The salmon is very good and I love the greek salad- the dressing is fantastic. Great gyro plate, rice and excellent hummus. Garlic knot roll is totally sinful! Sometimes the chicken kebab is dry or so-so, but the steak is always awesome. Love their grape leaves and tabouli. Seriously I love everything here and it's fast and healthy. Grab a baklava on the way out, it's tasty, too!

I would be perfectly content to eat a platter from Gus' falafel truck every single day. A couple of co-workers introduced me to his food a while ago, and I have been several times since. At first, I was really nervous because they forewarned me of Gus' particularity when it comes to proper "ordering etiquette." By now, I've realized that Gus is just an eccentric guy who appreciates good food and loves to share it with others. He chats extensively about the "quality" of his food....quality quality quality....but I have to hand it to the guy - he's earned it. With garlic bulbs and plants decorating the truck as its only identifiable aspect, there is an element of mystery, which I tend to enjoy. There's no menu and you will never get the same thing twice, which is part of the appeal. About his food - you get chicken, falafel, hummus, a grain, and veggie/fruit combo of sorts, with a piece of bread or pita, but he always switches up the variety. His chicken is charcoal-grilled and marinated to perfection, hence why you can smell his cooking from blocks away. If you are a garlic lover, you will be impressed with his falafel. It is SO garlicky and so amazing. I'm not usually a hummus lover, but this hummus is creamy and rich. Here are some of the different components I have been given: grilled grapes, avocado salad, fresh strawberries and bananas, watercress, grilled asparagus, a tomato tahini dipping sauce, a dessert hummus, and a fresh golden beet salad. For grains: cous cous, pasta, rice pilaf, quinoa, buckwheat, or any other type of grain. There wasn't a single dish I was upset with. I can rave about the food for hours, but I'm equally excited about the value! You get a huge platter (the amount of food usually lasts for 2 reasonably sized meals), with plenty of charcoal-grilled, marinated chicken, some sort of grain (usually pasta or rice), a fruit or vegetable combination of his choice, and a wild card (usually either another fruit or vegetable, a sauce, or something completely different you've never seen before). Sometimes, he serves a drink of his choice with the platter, too. When it's cold out, he also provides free, homemade soup for his shivering customers, which I find to be the most endearing aspect of his customer service. Many other reviews find fault with the quality of customer service here, but I just can't be upset with a cup of soup in the cold, a drink, and a huge plate of for that price, and some entertaining chatter. Eat what he gives you and you will not be disappointed. Biggest bang for your buck at just $10. And if you don't believe me, just ask any customer waiting on line in the worst weather conditions for 45+ minutes.

My expectations for a fast-food, subway-type sandwich shop were totally blown out of the water. I met a friend here for lunch and was pleasantly surprised to step inside such a classy Mediterranean cafe. There was unfortunately a wait to sit inside (the lunch hour was packed-a great sign!) so we chose outside, but our location away from the water misters and hot Tucson breeze made it a rather toasty lunch. Oh well. They were quite busy so we waited longer for service than we would have liked, especially sitting outside, but it was worth it. I am typically a very decisive person but I was actually torn about what to order-everything looked amazing. I finally decided on the grilled veggie wrap and was not sorry. The veggies were freshly grilled and the pesto complimented them perfectly. I am definitely dragging my hubby and a group of friends here for happy hour; fresh Mediterranean food is invaluable.

The chef, owner, waitress bartender of this restaurant serves up some awesome Ethiopian food. It is on par with Ethiopian food you will find in major US American cities such as SF, Seattle, New York, Philly, etc,. People of Reno or visitors need to put this restaurant on your regular rotation, we are lucky to have it here adding to the diversity of our restaurants.

Very friendly staff but the food just didn't hit the spot for me..the pho seems to be lacking the authentic pho flavor...guess I'm used to LA style pho and the places here just don't cut it...still I go there to get my fix because it's not bad.
Oh yum. All four of us loved our dishes and the flan was outstanding. Fabulous drinks too.

It took me forever to make my way to this little gem. This tiny spot, and I do mean tiny, has been producing some excellent restaurants that go on to bigger spaces: Blackbird, Indie Blue, and now Zeppoli. I've known about it since it opened but, again, its tiny and hence reservations are require weeks in advance and honestly I'm not great about thinking that far ahead when it comes to dinner plans. So my first suggestion to you is, pause reading this, pick a day and make a reservation now! Then come back because, of course, I have more to say. Welcome back! I finally made my reservations too and went. Then months later driving by it I realized I hadn't written a review. Oh no, you say? Oh yes, I was surprised too because while I don't remember everything I ate that night beyond that it was all very good there is one dish that stands out in my mind and I think of often. I will take my dramatic pause here to list the restaurants one draw back now because it's not the way I like to send you off- It's not romantic. This is due to one simple fact, it is LOUD, very loud. I'm talking lean in so you can hear the person sitting across from you at the small table, loud. Though tiny, the joint has high ceilings and hard surfaces and all 35 seats are filled. Laughter and chatter bounce around the restaurant like its the inside of a retro pinball machine. I'm just saying...Now back to the good stuff. I am not a steak kind of guy. I've never been a fan of that gut busting gotta lay down kind of feeling that inevitably follows such a meal. But for whatever reason, call it kismet, fate, divine intervention, I decided to go for it. GOOD GOLLY that Bistecca enna was good, no AMAZING. In fact, without question, the best steak I've ever had and one of the best meals. Like I mentioned at the top I still think about it. It is a staple in the banks of my food porn collection. Perfectly cooked and full of flavor it was sweet and spicy (not the heat kind) without sauce or gravy and accompanied by the perfect counterpoint an arugula salad that was fresh and lite. And here's the kicker, no gut busting I gotta lay down, after effect. I know all the reviews mention it too but it bears repeating. You will not be disappointed. Chef Baldino is making magic it that tiny little kitchen. Great food, and excellent service equaled a good time had by all.

I've been ordering from Little Kitchen for 3 years now, since I started working in Bala Cynwyd. I have never had an issue, received cold food, bad food, etc. I don't understand the bad reviews here. I've had the sushi and while it's not Morimoto quality, it's pretty good for what it is! The staff is always pleasant and willing to accommodate requests, the prices are reasonable and the food is always good. It's a sure shot for Chinese in this area!

I love this place. I was here with my Hubby and sis. Pita Jungle has healthy and great tasting food. I had the Mahi Mahi with jalapeño hummus which was really good. My hubby loved the glazed chickening pizza. We wined on The Hybrid Pinot (nice and silky). It paired well with our entrees. We've been here a couple of times and will definitely keep coming back. This is a nice place to dine with family, friends or a date.

I have been craving for papaya salad for quite some time now. I have a friend that really makes good papaya salad which is really spicy. But this papaya salad is really good too. They have big portions, and as much as I want to indulge myself and eat it on one sitting, I just can't lol, so saved some and I'll have them again tomorrow for lunch. Food is good and I hope that it will continue that way.

Just ordered from here under the restaurant's new name. I've been ordering from this location for a couple of years now, and this review is reflective of my overall experience. Let me just say-- they dont often get the order right, especially when it's To Go. They've forgotten to put in key features of dishes before (even forgetting the rice today, which is supposed to always come with the chicken tikka masala I ordered), and will not tell you if they are out of something but still charge you for it (like their homemade "lime soda"). The only reason I tolerate this as much as I do is because there arent as many other good flavored indian options in the area, and this place has a good location. Often, they drop the ball on your order and you pay for it. The management doesn't seem to take their business seriously. How sad! Oh well. Not sure of I'll keep ordering from here since they keep wasting my time with incomplete orders. On top of that, one time I ordered the chicken tikka masala and they delivered me a completely different dish. Also, if you're ordering two of the same dish and want them to be at different levels of spicy such as one mild and one medium or hot, they both will just be medium or hot. Bummer.

We used to love ordering from here.. But things have changed.. Foods not as good and the delivery time f**king sucks.. The last two or three times we waited 45 minutes or more for our food.. Unacceptable! It's not like it's on a Friday or Saturday night, it'll be like Tuesday or Thursday... And when you call they claim the order is on its way.. Bullsh*t!! They don't respect the customers time.. If I pay you for a service I expect it to be delivered in a timely fashion.. So we are done with them, they suck now..

I eat here probably 2xs a week. Definitely my favorite pho in Tampa! The girls are super nice here. Sometimes you may run out of water but that's ok! Just drink your broth...unless your like me and you make it super spicy. I always get tripe and rare beef pho. The broth is always tasty not needing much additives. Spring rolls are always fresh and cold. Rice roll things (62) Delilah. Vermicelli bowls are awesome as well. Authentic for sure!

Love this place- get #16 sweet orangey rice with lamb- I just wish there were a few more lamb chunks. I love the salad beforehand too, and I also recomment the eggplant veggie dishes, pumpkin too. Always incredible service here and the owner personally thanks you for coming. Bring your student advantage card and get 20% off!
Very nice staff. Food was amazing! We are until we could not eat anymore. Nice family lunch buffet for a Saturday.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Stumbled onto this place after a work meeting in the area last week. Had lunch here with two co-workers, and we were all impressed. The service was fantastic, and the food was quite tasty. I had the turkey club sandwich with potato salad on the side. The sandwich was fresh and very good. The potato salad was fantastic! Each of my co-workers reported their meals to also be very good. I will certainly give this place another shot if I find myself in the area during their hours again.

My first time at the restaurant was last week. And since then, I have gone there 4 times already! It's that good. My only comment is that the food is a bit on the spicy side so don't be too ambitious. As other posters have mentioned, the biryani (I've tried the lamb and the chicken) is delicious! The interior is pretty bland--the good stuff here is the food!

I have always been a frequent diner at Momos but think after today's visit will not go back. I got a to go order when I called they informed me they no longer have a menu item I ordered I went ahead with the rest of my order. When I got home everything was different the kids mac n cheese was completely changed and dry it used to be creamy and rich the tenderloin sandwich was 95% bread and onion mind you there never used to be onion on it and there was mayonnaise on it this time too. So maybe when I ordered they should have said we changed everything on our menu. It was a waste of time and money!!!!

Love this little place! I had the beef gyro, but I've had their chicken and falafel before too, and they're all equally tasty. You know you'll get a fresh meal here, and it's so cheap! The owner chats with everyone, and the atmosphere is welcoming. This is one of my favorite Manayunk spots.

Came here for University City Dining Days. Service was friendly and attentive. Dinner service is candle lit and dimly lit. Very romantic. $16 for a one piece crispy spring roll, regular entree sized curry, and a mango rice pudding. Great bang for your buck. Curry was significantly better than what I had over at Erawan, less coconuty and more aromatic. If you're looking for a place to grab a bite to eat during UCDD, come here.
I love the red curry and tofu! The new décor is so beautiful and really adds to the dining experience.
Have been there since, and while the service was good the quality did not match our initial review.

Eat here every time we are in town for business. The service is always fantastic year after year and the food is always outstanding. Huge range with salads and seafood. If you are in town it is a must visit.

It's open... and it was disappointing. Ordered food and after a hour and half i was still hungry because it never came. I guess the place has new management well they don't have a clue how to run a bar. We had to get our money back...we went to support some friends who were performing they were great and the crowd had good energy. Parking was rough circled the block like 5 times. But the new management need training classes ...they definitely are not ready to serve Philadelphia! Doubt I'll ever go back. Service was not good at all. The manager actually told my boyfriend she wasn't a waitress. Umm shouldn't be aware of how to do all positions if you were needed? Yeah not going back ever
Tofu salad with peanut dressing and any soup, minus the fish cakes...The staff is friendly and will remember your name. Only minus, wish the hours were extended.

Ridiculously good! I would've never found this place on my own, but having been recommended by someone working nearby, I am SO happy we stopped in. When I saw how many Yelp friends had given this great ratings, I knew we were in for it. I had the gyro plate and mango juice, and was blown away by the texture and flavor of the lamb/meat gyro plate. It was so smooth, delicious, and paired so beautifully with their amazing hummus! This is a tremendous amount of food, so this definitely doubles as at least one full other meal of leftovers. Tip--they share a wall with a nail salon, so if you can choose the room on the side of Severn street, I'd opt for that, as the varnish smell was a bit strong on the left side of the room.
Food was unbelievable. Flavor explosion. They were super nice and accommodating. Wish I lived nearby. Prices were reasonable. Best ever.
Excellent flavors and legitimate foods. Very nice in a little strip mall. We had a chicken kabob gyro and an appetizer sampler. You are definitely encouraged to visit this spot.

Great food and a great location. Right on the water so if you time it right you can enjoy a beautiful sunset. I had the Mahi Tacos and they were delicious. The onion straws the group shared were also yummy. Service was a little slow but we were there at the worst time and it was packed, so not surprising.

Jasmine Thai is one of the few restaurants in Brandon that never disappoints. The food is always served quickly and it is always very tasty. You can't go wrong starting with Thai Egg Rolls. Their curry dishes are awesome and their Chili Snapper is delicious. The place is always clean and the staff is very attentive. You can't go wrong with this place.

zoes always hits the spot! steak kabobs or greek salad with chicken are my go to's. the white beans- amazing! love the pesto hummus as well. zoes is great food & priced well. It's one of my favorite go to spots!!

Flavor of the stock was good! If I were to compare it to the other pho places I've been (around the Indianapolis area), I would say the flavor of the stock tops it. I ordered pho with beef and brisket. Now this is why I gave them 3 stars: the amount of "stuff" they put in was a bit scarce. They put in an adequate amount of noodles; the amount of beef and brisket, however, was very scarce. I took a look at the bowl and I could only see a piece of brisket, noodles, and the stock. Compared with the other pho restaurants, this place had to have given the least amount of "stuff" for the same price. Otherwise, food was good. Service was a mixture of "ehh" and good. There's a young lady who seemed a bit too shy and moved a bit too slow. What seemed to be the owner however was cheerful, made jokes, and wasn't afraid to chat.

Have been to Pan D'Olive three times and have enjoyed each visit. Every food item has been interesting and well prepared. Emphasis on large meat portions which I think are enough for two or three people. Friendly service and the owner, I believe, is often helping serve and seems generally appreciative for the business. Seems a little pricey however not out of line with other similar restaurants. Never seem to be able to get online reservations to work here so a phone call is probably the best option.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Simply the best Thai food in Reno by far....maybe on the west coast; authentic, prepared fresh and super tasty. Outstanding blend of flavors prepared exclusively for each individual order and served with care and great presentation. I don't think anyone would be disappointed with the experience, service or price. The restaurant has a warm atmosphere and nicely appointed dining area with suitable ambiance for a great meal; sufficient menu variety to suit anyone willing to delve into a tasty Thailand experience. I highly recommend you try it - you will be glad you did and you will return for more.

Great unpretentious place. Ordered the curry chicken, roti and Mango Juice to wash it all down. I'm normally not a cabbage guy but I ate all of the cabbage on my plate. Everything tasted fresh and well seasoned.
Was wonderful but is now Permanently CLOSED. Sorry to see it go. Bala Cynwyd location only

I stop here on my way home from the gym a lot. Good portions, fine prices... really good food. 4 stars because the ambiance could be a little better and the rice was just OK, and the prices could be a LITTLE cheaper. nothing fancy but overall the food is awesome for being in the middle of a strip mall in franklin. I like the gyro mix plate.

Desi Village has been in business for years, but after sampling it I think that speaks more to the lack of Indian options in KOP proper. When I walk into an Indian (or any type of predominantly ethnic) restaurant and see mostly gringos, it makes me raise my eyebrows. I will say that nothing was particularly offensive about the food and I've had far worse North Indian fare in restaurants, hence the three star rating. However, my meal wasn't something that would keep me coming back. The spicing and seasoning of the various curries is surprisingly vibrant, but these sauces feel quite heavy. The meats here aren't the best, as my lamb was overcooked and a bit tough. The vegetables in the Jalfrezi were the frozen, supermarket variety, which was not enjoyable at all. Naans are average, rice is prepared well. Everything is overpriced. The food earns 2 stars, but the service was friendly enough to warrant another. Desi Village's food is simply average, and fairly costly for the quality. I won't be returning any time soon unless I'm magically stranded in KOP with few other options.

We ordered takeout here tonight. The veggie egg rolls were out so I ordered the crab Rangoons appetizer based on reviews. They ended up being the highlight of the meal. Also ordered spring rolls and Tom Ka soup with shrimp. The Tom Ka soup was quite good and the spring rolls were large -- as others have said, the peanut sauce was flavorful. We ordered 2 entrees; I neglected to ask for the pad Thai mild and so it was a bit spicy for me. Likely for no one else! We also ordered the green curry with chicken. My husband thought it was good as well. A good solid takeout place for Thai.

Delicious food. More intimate setting at night but the afternoon buffet is on point. It has a terrible location, but I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it. The staff is courteous and professional and the restaurant is very clean. But seriously. The food is so good. And they're open pretty late!

If I could I'd give this place 10 stars. I come here so much that it might even be unhealthy. Who am I kidding, pho is never unhealthy for anyone. Pros: it smells amazing. super fast service. Consistency in food quality. Not as Americanized as the other pho place around the area. Good quantity for the prices. Reasonable. They have WiFi if you ever need to work. Oh and the coffee is strong. What more could you ask for? Cons: I honestly couldn't tell you a single one and I've been coming for about two months. Tips: if you're new to Vietnamese food just ask an employee for a recommendation, they're always helpful in describing what is what and how everything taste. If it isn't busy play around with the kiosk like Another reviewer said the build your own option is the best because you get to pick and choose what actually goes in.
Went in the late afternoon, about 4.30. The bartender was pleasant but said the chef wouldn't be in for a while so a meal was not to be had. Too bad.
Ate there with a friend during off peak hours, it was ok. I've had much better in Nashville. Prices were kind of high for what we got. I will say that the employees were very nice.

Arrived a little after 6, was told to sit where-ever we wanted, they were not busy. Sat on the patio, waited 10 minutes - no hi, hello anything. Waitress finally came but went to the table next to us, took their order and walked away - still no acknowledgement. Waited another 5 minutes, nothing. We left, will never go back.

I knew from the first time I walked in and saw a half butchered lamb staring at me with it's tongue hanging out that this was the place for me. The portions are large, the food is tasty, and the service is extra friendly. I have eaten here at least once a week since I discovered it 6 months ago. If you like your Indian spicy you'll have to make sure to specify that. They tend to go easy on the heat unless you mention it. With all that said, I do have to agree with the comments on the inside of the place; but since I just grab my food to go it doesn't bother me.

I absolutely love their chais, I recommend the Ginger or Kashmiri especially. I would drink three a day if I were able. The menu overall is quite large and features many Indian-based dishes that are well prepared and tasty (try the samosas and their butter chicken). The staff have always been polite and friendly to me even when they're super busy. I typically wont stay and eat/drink if it's busy but that's ok cause I'm close enough to throw rocks at their building from mine lolol.
Everything on this menu is delicious. Drunken noodle and their fried rice are so delicious. They also offer great lunch specials that include pad Thai!

What a great kabob food restaurant! Clean, the staff is friendly and the food is great. Location might be hard to find due to being in a strip mall, west of blimpie in the same complex north west corner on maple grove and emerald. Lunch is the best value try the lamb kabobs, portions are good and the taste is soooo good. I would recommend The beef and chicken curry. Wife and I come for lunch often so we might see you there.

The Queen is a great dive bar for de-stress and chill out time. This is *not* a trendy dive bar. It's actually a dark, kinda dirty, tacky bar with cheap TVs blaring sports. This is where you go for an irresponsible number of city wide specials with friends

Finally had a chance to come here for brunch after much anticipation. Suraya blew us out of the water! The inside is massive and beautifully decorated. It looks like there is a beautiful and large outdoor area with which has yet to open which will be amazing come summer. Service was great, our waiter was friendly and helpful. The highlights of our meal were the mushroom hummus and the "Gravlax." The mushroom hummus was sooooo incredibly umami. My boyfriend thinks it is better than Zahav's hummus--I think it is on par but the two are definitely different. The Gravlax was literally heaven on a plate. Finely sliced salmon on Lebanese flat bread topped with trout roe and amazing olive oil--it managed to be light and fresh and decadent at the same time. It is the sophisticated cousin of lox and cream cheese on a bagel. I'm super stoked to come back here when it opens for dinner service this spring! Suraya is sure to impress.

Most disappointing St Paul sandwiches ever! I'm always looking for a good St. Paul. For those who don't know what these are, it's an egg patty that contains meat, onions and bean sprouts usually served on white bread with mayo and pickles. Sounds plain, but can be quite tasty when prepared right. The two I've gotten from here thus far were way too over cooked and burned and quite soggy. I haven't tried any of the specialty St. Pauls like the Angry Bird one, but I won't be going back.

Nothing will get me to go west beyond 270 quicker then an International Supper Club gathering. What motivation to expand my horizons, eat with fellow Yelpers and enjoy some international cuisine. The hospitality of Spiro's was outstanding and my entree was so good, I will be venturing west of 270 without the need of a ISC gathering. 10 vivacious foodies arrived at the Chesterfield Spiro's around 6:30 PM. I do not think Harry the Maitre d and Stacy our sensational server knew what they were in for, but they handled us all like champions. They made each one of feel special and unique. Stacy was incredible, that girl knew how to sell not only the steak, but the sizzle as well. Or in my case, she sold me on the Scallops. I love scallops, but already had selected what I wanted this evening. My mind was made up, so I thought. Then when Stacy in her perky, animated way described the grilled sea scallops on top of linguine, I was persuaded to change my order. I was so glad I did, those six huge sea scallops melted in my mouth. The grill marks were like I was eating a meaty steak. The bed of linguine underneath the scallops was filled with various fresh vegetables. Harry kept stopping by the table to check on us and making sure everything was good. However, with an outstanding server like Stacy we were in good shape and enjoying our night of Greek Cuisine. After a night at Spiro's, I'm creating two new list; Sea Scallops and Sensational Service.
Chicken Tika masala, Lamb vindaloo, naan, and a tandoori mixed grill-- all was delicious! Our family of four certainly enjoyed and had a bit leftover for lunch.
We go here all the time, bring friends and family and really love it! Lunch is much cheaper than dinner. The cold dip plate is great. Plan to order extra bread.

We eat here several times each week. If you're not sure what to order get a 1/2 chicken with a side, or try the tropachop bowl. We start with yellow rice, black beans chicken and onions. I order the large and have enough left over for the next day. There have been some growing pains like all restaurants, but all in all we love it!

Numchok Wilai is one of my favourite Thai places in the city. I've been there at least half a dozen times by now, both for lunch and dinner, and have always had an excellent meal. You know it's going to be good when half the people you invite aren't even aware of it's location. Never judge a restaurant by it's exterior. Or in my books, the shabbier looking, the better. I think part of it's charm is that not many people know how amazing it really is. Numchok has a killer lunch deal ($12.95) which includes your choice of a dish, two veggie spring rolls, a small bowl of lemongrass soup and rice. There are 21 items to choose from (nine are vegetarian, couple curries, pad thai, etc.). There was a recent hike in price of $1.00 but what can you do? 'errbody needs to make a living. The staff are always friendly and service is both fast and efficient. On our most recent trip, we ordered and received our food in less than 10 minutes. Ridiculous. *** Very important (hence the asterisks) - if you want spicy, make sure you ask for it (three options: 2 (spicy), 3 (hot) and 4 (very hot)). First time, we forgot to tell them so while all the food was very flavourful, it lacked in the heat department. We could probably just blame this on Bbop with his pale, white skin and the staff taking pity on him and having no faith in his eating abilities. Second time around, we ditched him and made sure to get the 4 star experience. The staff didn't believe we could handle the heat because they checked with us twice to make sure we wanted very hot. If you like spicy, do it. It's actually not that hot - you can still taste all the flavours but you'll get lingering bit of heat with each bite. Still nowhere near as hot as what I've had in Thailand. - Veggie spring rolls and lemongrass soup - a nice little appetizer to start our meal off. The lemongrass soup is delicious - you can really taste the lemongrass flavour, just don't eat the lemongrass piece that they usually leave in it. - Thai hot basil beef (#8) - stir fried beef with garlic, chili, mushroom, carrot, green pepper, red pepper and basil leaves. The beef was tender and moist, soaking up all the juiciness from the sauce. - Stir fried eggplant (#20) - stir fried eggplant with garlic, carrot, red pepper, basil leaves and vegetarian sauce. Eggplant is one of my favourite vegetables so I decided to try out Numchok's take on it for the first time. Really tasty and the eggplant along with all the other vegetables were cooked perfectly. - Coconut rice ($1.00 extra) - nice presentation. The coconut rice was light, fluffy and fragrant. You'll eat this up easy. On a previous lunch, we had the pad thai tofu (#18) and green curry chicken (#3) which is easily one of their best dishes. The pad thai is well balanced and not overly sweet, which I am not a fan of when that happens. The green curry is a staple and seriously, you can never go wrong with ordering it. Overall, Numchok Wilai continues to deliver and is one of my favourite spots in the city to grab Thai food. If you haven't been yet, goooooooooooooo.

A hidden gem in the Girard Estates neighborhood! Authentic, friendly, delicious and CHEAP. Whoa is this place inexpensive. Went with a friend on a Tuesday night - I had the Mie BBQ Pork noodle soup, which the waitress explained you can either eat "dry" (without adding the broth, which comes on the side - although the noodles are served over a savory, thick sauce at the bottom of the bowl, so i use the word "dry" with leniency) or pour the broth over. Delicious either way, but i had wanted it to be a noodle soup so I poured a generous amount of the broth over the noodles & pork and vegetables and, oh man it was awesome. Super filling and savory. Broth had a great flavor, not too oily or heavy. I added a nice-sized dollop of their house-made chili paste and - ahh, perfection. Dinner friend had the Nasi Lemak special with the fried chicken - also a generous portion and super tasty. I actually didn't get a taste of this because we also shared an order of Nasi Goreng which was hands-down our favorite dish. Savory rice with fried egg, tons of pork and fried sausage slivers, pickled veggies, fish balls....yum so amazingly good. We cleaned the plate on this one! In total, for three dishes our bill came to $18. We couldn't believe it - how could it be so inexpensive. But it's true - get a full, satisfied belly with some awesome Indonesian food on the cheap. Just how it should be.
Excellent Pad Thai! As fresh as it gets. Loved the atmosphere. Can't wait to eat there again.

I moved to delaware county from Philly, and gave up on getting good Asian food of any type. Last night I tried to get the BF -as he drove down to visit - to pick up thai, but I was too late and he was already on the 95. So began my search for thai food in my own neck of the woods. How unexpected to find this little place in boothwyn! Ok, four stars because it's BYOB, the ambience and servers are really low key but the place actually feels kind of classy. The spring rolls were overlooked but the chicken basil thai dish was spot on and they brought me two very small chillis, I believe they were Thai hots, when I asked for some extra spice with my meal. The prices are extraordinarily fair for hot, fresh, authentic Vietnamese and Thai in my hood, and I hear the pho is outstanding. All is not Lost out here in the burbs.

Please tell me how this place is still in business. The service tonight was terrible, the bread on my FGTBLT was freaking burned. Why she tried to serve it to me is a mystery. None of our food arrived at the same time. I had to go to the bar to get drink refills. It wasn't all that busy either. I don't know why we keep coming here. The table was so wobbly I thought the top was going to fall off. Apparently this experience is par for this place. I wish the owners would read this an invest in better kitchen staff, servers and furniture.

The east side of Tucson has only a few Mediterranean / Greek restaurants. Pita Jungle fills in that void. While not as good as say, Zayna, it is good never-the-less. I usually get their dolmades and their shawarma wrap. It is good but not the best I have had. Their pricing is fair, between $9-11 per plate. The ambiance is something I enjoy. It is a nice, modern, feel with a light decor. Overall, it isn't a bad choice, just not the best either.

Cash only, don't bring plastic. Lots of food, bring your appetite! Very group friendly, I wouldn't recommend going solo or on a date. Service is always excellent, food is delicious, not your everyday meal. Great atmosphere, Both times I went were during the weekday, early dinner time, so its pretty quiet and relaxing, and you can share a meal and talk with your friends easily. Would love to see this place on the weekends and get the full experience with the belly dancers.

The restaurant is now under a new name called Palms restaurant and bakery. The food is delicious. I am Lebanese myself, and I can tell you that they serve authentic Middle Eastern food. Don't forget the toum (toom) garlic sauce on the Chicken Shawarma!!
Ordered the lamb kebab and it was excellent! Others in my party ordered chicken dishes and they were just ok.

So my friend used to play here. Then the city noise ordinance stopped that. So a place I would rank 4 stars now doesn't have live entertainment and now goes down to 2 stars. Why is it just 2 stars, well the drinks are expensive, bartenders lack any personality, and there is nothing really great about it at all. The outdoor seating is nice.... That is about it.

I come here a couple times a month, always great service and food. Lots of options to choose from, love all of their vegetarian options and everything seems to be real healthy and fresh. Place has a good vibe, great beer on tap, very modern.
Just as everyone else said: GREAT FOOD SO SO SERVICE CHEAP AND TASTY BRING CASH

Such yummy food here! Best massaman curry in the city. Massaman is like a cinnamon-y, creamy Thai stew that is definitely worth the try if you've never had it! Very reasonable prices and great service!

Was really excited to try this restaurant after changing from Media Pizza. Still no improvement. We waited about 90 min to only receive one course of the 4 course meal we had to get. The four courses was completely over priced and we were not impressed with our room temp, bland food. The staff never even addressed the long wait and no water in our cups. We had to leave after 90 min of no food or updates on the status of our order, we paid for what we received and the staff did not even apologize or try and find our order. I don't mind sitting and enjoying the atmosphere but 90 min to only receive room temp soup seems a little excessive for me. Probably won't try again. Same owners as Media pizza, same bad, low quality food. On the plus side, those that received their food around us seemed to be enjoying it and it looked appetizing.
This place is awesome. Great service, great food and finally, a restaurant that offers some variety in its Vietnamese menu.

My cousin asked me and my mother to go to lunch and he suggested this quiet African restaurant. Great choice! The prices were reasonable and the menu had pictures for those not familiar with African food. I had the Yassa fish. It was delicious!
Excellent service and delicious arepas and cachapas and very reasonable price !! Must try!
I'm obsessed with this place!! So excited they moved to Ruskin!! I could eat there everyday!!

Tried this place for dinner last night and enjoyed the food. Called at 6:30 to make a reservation at 7pm for 2 without a problem. The food was great! My friend said she probably prefers it to magasin, which is also a great Vietnamese spot on Magazine St. We shared the avocado rolls and I had the fried chicken and green waffle, and she had the vermicelli bowl, all of which was great and I would definitely go back. They seem to be understaffed though as service was quite slow. Everyone seemed to be running around frantically, bumping into chairs and tables at times. Even the hostess took on bus boy and waitress duties.

This was great thai food. Quick, easy and flavorful. Ordered a curry. Pad thai and basil chicken. The pad thai was a little sweet for my taste but we ate it anway! Very all place but if I lived here I would definitley get takeout from here a lot#

An update to my previous review(s) about this restaurant - they are open again and it appears as though there's been a little bit of a facelift in the dining room. We got there early because previous experiences have told us that the one waiter gets in the weeds bigtime after about 7 - typically if we get there after seven there's dirty tables and a 30 minute lead time on entrees. He works as hard as he can but he's got the whole restaurant. This time there was a second server; I arrived about 5 minutes early and was seated immediately and greeted promptly. This time there was two servers and it was obvious that service standards had improved. I got a shrimp entree off the spicy side of the menu - the shrimp was served tail on so I had to use my hands. Taste was excellent; my guests all enjoyed the meal but we were a bit disappointed that they only had Heineken (no Tiger beer.) All considered, a great visit that was enjoyed by the whole table, including guests who have lived in Thailand and Cambodia.

I decided to have a delightful brunch on Saturday morning and accidentally ran into this unique corner cafe in Edmonton. The atmosphere is a grand blend of uptown business class and hometown offerings of couch seating. It was suggested to me to have the Masala Dhosa with spicy vegetables smothered with a light curry, this lentil bread had an 'old world' flavour that was a unique surprise. I loved the presentation as it came along with the tangy mint/cilantro, curried yellow lentils with chilies, and the sweet coconut and sweet tangy sauce. These dipping elements added a refreshing opposition to the spicy hotness of the curried Masala Dhosa. In my opinion I think that this offers nutritive choices from the old world that makes this cafe special.

This was delicious Thai food. The Pad Thai I ordered was perfect. The toasted peanuts on top added a nice crunch to the dish. It was accompanied with a few appetizer tasters as part of the special combination meal I ordered. The shrimp rolled in an egg roll wrapper was delicious as well; the shrimp tasted fresh! For dessert we ordered a fried banana with ice cream. The banana felt a little spicy and unflavored. Personally, I would have used plantains instead of the run-of-the-mill banana because they fry better and retain the flavor. Either way, I was still very pleased with the food, and for the quantity and price of the meal, it was all worth it. I will definitely be going back, and if I live there I'd be a regular.

An explosion of flavors! After enjoying the banarsi somosa appetizers, we shared mixed vegetable curry and naram garam kofta. Both were spectacular. The kofta was to die for! And we loved the peshawari naan, a dessert in itself. Given we were celebrating my wife's birthday they brought us a pistachio kulfi dessert. It was the perfect ending to a delightful meal. The service was attentive.

Born and raised in Vietnam, I must say that this place is really good for what it does: Vietnamese food. Why do my American friends just love here as much as I do? Many reasons - to name a few, their Pho broth is really flavorful and rich and their banh my is really awesome too. But, here are some drawbacks: (1) they only accept cash, and (2) sometimes it takes forever for the food to come out (maybe they did it intentionally, who knows?) Anyway, highly recommended...

We were in Nashville for the weekend and found this spot. Food and service was great. Not many hookah flavors but happy with service and quality of hookah and food. I like the ice hookah hose they have.

How many good things can I say about this place? It would never be enough You can literally try anything on the menu and you will be satisfied. Forgo the traditional chicken tikka masalas and try something different like the dum aloo or hariyali chicken or my personal favorite, the malai kofta. Slow simmered vegetable balls in a rich and spicy malai sauce, perfectly accented a drizzle of coconut flakes, raisins and vegetables on the bottom. Its, wow. Do the malai chicken seekh kabobs and harabhara kebab for appetizers and you'll immediately see why this place is one of the best Close your eyes and just point to something!

Pretty eh experience here. I stopped by for dining days one night to try the 3 course option for $15. I chose the fresh spring rolls, Pad kee mao with chicken (+$1), and the mango sticky rice. Portions were small and relatively skimpy. Service was slow and servers were hard to get a hold of. I asked for the noodles to be "very spicy" but they came incredibly mild, no spice at all. I didn't bother to send them back since we had already been waiting a while. Pretty subpar experience, I would't go back. Cash only.

I'm kind of conflicted about this place, and am giving it a 3 for that reason. Will try it again, and maybe move up to a 4. The problems with this place are kind of subtle. First, as others have said, it's a bit pricey for what you get. Usually when I order Naan ( I got the garlic, and it was really good, with enough garlic and plenty of cilantro) it comes with a sauce, or 2 or 3. Not here. Likewise, the complimentary papadum, although coming with a very tasty onion sauce, had so little of it that I was left wondering if I should ask for more. The extras that I contemplated--spicy pickles, mango Lassi, and mango chutney would have added between 10 and 12 dollars to my lamb vindaloo, so I opted not. At that, with just the Naan and the main, I reached $20. So, the vindaloo was good, but a little too tomato-ey for my taste. And although the lamb was good, and well cooked, there wasn't that much of it. And, even though I told the waitress that I love spicy food, it wasn't particularly hot. And this was vindaloo! Nor was I offered the choice of heat level. So even though the service was very pleasant, and attentive, and the food served pretty quickly my experience was kind of iffy. I like the decor(particularly the fresh rose on each table--a sweet touch), service, and convenient location, and will try it again, but just not impressed on the first visit.
Slowest service and received a completely Raw boneless wing. I couldn't eat any of my food after waiting half an hour in line. I would not recommend anyone eat at this location

Good Indian cuisine a few blocks from Bryn Mawr College Best dishes were chicken korma, bootie kabob and saag paneer. We also had fancy sweet nan (which did not go with all of our dishes), mango chicken, mango salsa and butter chicken. Reasonable prices

My special someone and I went here a few weeks back for date night and had a great time. I thought it was five star, and she thought four - so 4.5 I guess? Either way, we had a great time. The space itself is...eclectic? I think the best way to describe it might be as a place where the owners don't take themselves too seriously, but are very proud of their business and are deeply committed to the endeavor. When we arrived they were pretty busy, but we were seated quickly by an older gentleman that I believe was (one of) the owner(s). Despite the fact that I assume the business would do fine without him there seating customers, there he was working away to do his best to make people happy. Once we were seated we received prompt, friendly service. We started off with an order of the veggie dumplings, which were the only low point of the meal for me. The flavor of them was fine, but I believe they were steamed and thus just kind of soggy. I wish that they would finish them off with a quick pan-fry to crisp them up a bit, but I feel like that might just be a preference thing. For our mains, we ordered their curry of the day (green) with tofu & the Pad Kee Mao, both of which were delicious and came in quite generous portions. Through a herculean effort I was able to eat all of the curry somehow, but we had quite a bit of Pad Kee Mao left to take home. I did kind of wish that they either served alcohol or let you BYO as a nice pilsner or a lighter wine would have gone well with the meal, but, then again, it was kind of nice to just focus on the food for a change. All in all, I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for some decent Thai food and a great dining experience. At least for my part, after eating here this might now be a contender for one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville.

I'm Trinidadian therefore, I love Caribbean food and absolutely loved this place, everything was delicious. The family that owns it couldn't have been any kinder and accommodating. We'll definitely be back!
This Vietnamese restaurant is great. I've had several soups (vegetarian, beef brisket, beef balls) and the pork buns and they're always delicious. They're consistent and fast as well.

A very good restaurant in which my wife and I attended. Parking is easy and next to the restaurant. The restaurant is new, clean and with quiet Indian background music. We were seated quickly and the server was very nice and attentive. I told her we were not familiar with Indian food so she was very helpful in selecting from the menu. We had spring rolls for an appetizer and they were very tasty. For our main course we had the Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala...prepared with a mild sauce. We also had a cheese bread order (4 slices) enough for 2 people. All the food was prepared with excellent presentation and very flavorful. We will definitely come again.

Beautiful place, waitress was very knowledgeable and sweet; food was mixed- my chicken tangine was delicious but my husbands couscous royale was just ok. Soup appetizer and salad very good. I would definitely go back

We have waited a long time for Samson Kabob House to relocate and open at their new location. They opened today and their new location at South street is even better then the last one. Looks like some kinks need to be worked out but I am sure they will get there. Did wait a long time for the food but it was delicious. Looks to be a family business but they sure could use outside help.

Yummy little place on Beach Drive. Excellent staff of bartenders- hilarious and engaging. Food was superb for a gastro restaurant. Would recommend this to visitors. Hours could be expanded for lunch...

Much as this place is a recent entrant to the Tampa Bay Area, it is already drawing big crowds. The location is great and so is the ambience. It's not congested like a lot of other Indian restaurants in the area and has plenty of parking. The food is authentic and tasty. The chili paneer, gobi Manchuria and breads are some of our favorites. In general most of the food we've tried has been tasty and spicy. Service is decent. A little chaotic the first few months but it looks like they are working on it now. I would say it's among the top 3-5 Indian joints around Tampa Bay.
Great menu! We have been a few times and it's been great every time. Also, they give military discount. Staff is super friendly.

This review if for the Sweet&Sour fish - it's aweful! Thai Sweet&Sour fish is usually a breaded and fried white flaky fish. This place serves God knows how old frozen salmon that tastes like a fish flavored hockey puck. I know they do decent padthai and curry, just stay away from the fish..

Excellent addition to the neighborhood. Could up their game a bit. I was excited to have this come into the neighborhood. Have eaten there or taken out 3 times. As others have said, the roti canai is excellent. However, in some ways it seems like they are trying to offer too many cuisines at once and some of the sauces end up muddy. Mind you, this is very good. But, a slight sharpening of tastes by the chef could easily take this to a new level.
First time visiting yesterday, had the Combo sandwich at the recommendation of Dan.... he was so right! It was really damn good! Service was quick and very polite, I highly recommend.

Completely disappointed. Sat outside on the curb in the hot sun with limited to no service from our less than friendly waitress. I'm not sure she even remembered that we were outside waiting for her. Portions for dinner entrees were more like appetizers from a jar of ragu sauce. My boyfriend actually had to pull the complimentary donut ball dessert (donut holes with honey and sprinkles) out of his mouth it was so awful. My pasta was terrible and I could not regret more our decision to spend Saturday night for dinner here.

Transcendental. The best Indian food around, hands-down! Everything is fresh and delicious, the service is so friendly and nice. We have been traveling to the other locations in East Norriton and Chalfont for years and are beyond thrilled to have this new spot closer to home! My family loves Indian food, we have tried it all, and keep on coming back to Aman.

Baguette deli is a small place located on the side of a Fred Meyer in Boise. They offer Ban Mi sandwiches, Pho, and a few other items. The Ban Mi and the Pho are the reason to be here. The crusty bread, very fresh, crunchy vegetables, and delicious meats, along with a $5.00ish price tag make this place a winner in my book. They also offer bowls of Pho, which again are delicious, and very reasonably priced. There is not a lot of sitting room here, and it can be a little messy (tables not always cleaned quickly), but it is still worth it. If you are lucky, they will have some beignet's . They go fast, so look for them on the counter display. MMMMM. If you're looking for a healthy, delicious lunch, go here.

Great new place in Hyde park area. I had no idea they were even open here in the neighborhood. Food is much better than any regular takeout place, more for dining in. Everything we tried was just perfect. Definitely coming back.

I tried their Nasi Goreng / Fired rice couple months ago but it disappointed me. The rice is undercooked and it doesn't taste as I expected. Earlier this evening, I gave another try. It seems they added more variety to their menu. I tried their complete or special noodle, it taste great.. more than I expected. The price is really cheap. Now I can see they focusing more at the quality rather than the quality. I give this 4 star.

I'd been itching to go here for about a year, as it was recommended highly by friends and colleagues. Coming in with high expectations and anticipating portions similar to those of Dmitri's and Audrey Claire, I was suprised how tiny the portions were for the price. The Zeus Plate read like a feast on the menu, but on the table each appetizer sample was 1/3 the size of my fist (except for 1/2 plate full of fried calamari, which neither of us wanted). Still, the food is flavor-packed. Delicious octopus (but not as good as Dmitri's or Audrey Claire) and juicy charred chicken. The baba and hummus were also scrumptious. The BYOB restaurant has many rooms with nooks and crannies for tables large and small, for communal or intimate gatherings. Our server was awesome and amiable. I'd go back if someone else was paying, but my dine-out dollars will keep going to Dmitris.

We really enjoyed our brunch here on Christmas Eve. I had the Spinach and Sundried Tomato on a puff pastry. It was like eggs Benedict but on a puff pastry. Very tasty special. I would give it 4 stars, but service was a bit slow for not having every table filled....it could have been because they didn't have full staff for the holiday, but not sure. I would love to go back for dinner.

I really like this place. As a first time visitor this past Sunday I can say I enjoyed my meal. The food was very fresh and the atmosphere is clean. I bought a large meal with Jerk Chicken, beans/rice and string beans. They have a variety of sauces you can add to put onto of your rice. I got the ox tail sauce. I also added some fried fish on the side for only $2.00. The meat was tender and fresh just like I expected. The only downside is that the meat is missing that special spice I was expecting to taste with Jamaican food. It taste great but not very Jamaican flavored. The fish was sooooooo good and crunchy. I could probably eat all day. It could of used a bit more spice but I'm not complaining for the price and quality. I split my meal and side fish with a friend and we were both full. Next time I will probably get a small meal or large (if I'm greedy) for myself. I will visit this place often because food is great and the prices are amazing. I went on a Sunday at about 4:00 and they were really busy. I waited for maybe 15 - 20 or so min. in a line. The staff was nice from what I encountered as well.

I was disappointed with my selections at this restaurant. I ordered the honeydew mojito, expecting it to be bursting with summer flavor, but the melon was not detectable. I could see muddled honeydew in the glass, but it was flavorless and tasted like a plain mojito. It wasn't bad for a plain mojito; it just wasn't a honeydew mojito. For my meal, I ordered two small plates. I expected these to be a shareable size. I got the jerk chicken and the vegetable plate. The chicken had a nice flavor, however there were only four small skewers. For the price, I expected twice as many. The vegetable of the day was zucchini. It was sliced very thin and over seasoned. Again the portion was pitifully small - there was probably a quarter of a zucchini on the plate. Needless to say, I was still hungry at the end of the meal, but didn't want to spend any more than I already had just to get a few more bites. Other people I went with enjoyed their food more. The grits were a winner. I was left disappointed and hungry.

i was a regular here and honestly, i like their Pho i like the service. the problem is this place is filthy. every time i go i use the hot tea and my napkin to clean the dipping cups used for sauces and the spoons used to eat Pho. the walls are splattered with food and the place is just plain gross. i wish they'd clean the place up a bit because the food is really decent.

I tried this place one night on a limp I wasn't sure what to expect and I was amazed on the quality, quantity of the food. It was really good I had their basic spaghetti meal and it was great, looking forward to going back and trying other meals!

Yea. So probably the best indian food I have ever had in TUCSON. Anyways, ate here this past weekend and had a "spicy" dish. When they say spicy they mean it. Naan is delicious. Chicken Vindaloo was good. I will definitely be revisiting this place. I think next time I will get take out though because the restaurant is very small and you can hear other peoples conversations. Service was okay, the staff are not friendly at all but the food makes up for it. Another reason why I will only be ordering take out that way I don't have too see the waiters bored, unhappy face. :)

Went here with the wife and she loved it. Beef patties were fresh and delicious. We also ordered the Taste of the Islands which consisted of curry goat, oxtail and jerk chicken with rice, peas and plantains. Along with some jerk bone in wings to go. If you love spicy jerk wings you'll really enjoy these. Overall my wife and I really enjoyed the food and thought the staff was very nice.

We have been going here for years. The best Mediterranean fast food you ever had. The only problem are their hours. They recently removed some of the actual grocery and added a few more tables. Start with the Stuffed Grape Leaves, the Babaghanuj, the Hommus or one of their fantastic salads. My personal Fav is the Grilled Chicken Angelo Cataldi Sandwich (yes named for the Morning Show host after he stated public ally that he did not like Mediterranean food). Roasted pepper spread, marinated string cheese and lettuce but you can't deny the Grilled Fallafel or Gyros. SO basically what I'm saying is everything here is delicious. What are you waiting for, get there for lunch or before 7 (or 6 on Saturday).

Bahn mi, a perfect sandwich. And Pho 36 overall, it's "eat here 4 times in 3 days" damn good. Here's what we tried in those visits: Grilled beef bahn mi ... 5 stars Lemongrass tofu bahn mi ... 5 stars Hot and sour soup w/ shrimp ... 5 stars Spring rolls ... 4 stars Spicy shrimp w/ rice ... 4 stars Love this place. Not sure why it took us a while to try it, but now that we have, it's an immediate first option (alongside Chipotle) for quick and tasty food on the west side of Indy.

Merry is the only reason we tried this place twice, she's a gem but beyond that the waitresses tend to have an attitude as if you're bothering them and food is inconsistent. Both times my over easy eggs were undercooked, ya know - slimy... The Mimosa flight is great but Bloody hit or miss. This basically is an overflow place of Stella's which is always packed. Oh, and don't bother asking for extra hollandaise sauce apparently the cook only makes so much and stingy, out of the waitresses mouth. In other words, "no" you can't have extra sauce! Seriously, what kind of restaurant that serves food does this?!? We won't be back, sadly.

Wow, the folks at Go! Gyro! Go! really, really care that you're happy with their food. So refreshing! Today, a coworker and I headed out to finally see what the fuss was about. We peeked at the online menu and each found several things that we wanted to try. Twitter told us that they were down the street from our office. My friend ordered her desired gyro just fine. However, they didn't have my veggie gyro listed on their handwritten menu board. They had a salad, but I really wanted a big honking sandwich with the side of potatoes that I'd heard so much about. I asked the really nice lady at the truck window if there was any way that I could get a gyro without meat. She gave me a mischievous look and said that that's what she always wants to eat, but her partner (husband, I think?) is a total carnivore and never remembers to put it on the menu. They bantered good-naturedly for a bit and worked out what to put on my gyro. The lady pushed the man to make sure to give me extra feta and really stuff it. So kind! And then she told me that they're testing selling spanikopita and might try fish gyros at some point. I only waited a few minutes before the man called my name, and as he was building my gyro, he kindly asked me if I wanted certain things on it or left off. I really appreciated that. We also chatted about the potatoes that I was excited to get. He said that they were his pride and that he worked really hard to adjust the recipe for the masses of people and cooking them in the truck. My gyro was stuffed with dark and light lettuce, chopped tomatoes, chopped onions, chopped cucumber, parsely and tzeziki (I can't spell it) sauce, and it was all on a fluffy round pita, surrounded by foil and served with a side of potatoes in a rectangular styrofoam container. My meal cost about $8. They took Square for credit cards - yay! I dug in back in the office and was in heaven. My sandwich had a lot of onions and cucumbers, something I was uber happy about. The tzeziki sauce was a little heavy - maybe a lighter hand would help next time, but it was still tasty. And there was so much feta on this thing that I was moaning with joy. Cheese me up, and I'll be yours forever. The potatoes were no less stellar. They looked like some combination of fried and roasted, and they had delicious seasonings. Seriously, the potatoes made me rub my belly like cartoon people do. I lovedlovedloved that Go! Gyro! Go! had sides to round out the entrees, something that other food trucks don't do. I'd love to see them add a falafel gyro to the menu. I'd also love for a vegetarian gyro to be added to the menu permanently. Can't wait for them to come back near my office. This might become a weekly lunch!

I don't write reviews often, but this place is too good not to. The Samosas, Butter Paneer Masala and Bhindi Masala are out of this world. I'm a huge fan of Indian food, but it's not often I find a place that blows me away like this. It's undoubtedly worth the drive from Nashville and will be in the regular rotation of my favorites from now on. (Side note: the first time I went, I got the Vegetables Korma because it was recommended to me. That's the only dish I haven't been blown away by.)

So this is my 3rd time getting food from the Nooddi Thai Chef and it has not disappointed me yet!! Previously I got the Yakisoba & Mee Goreng. Both very good! This time I tried the pineapple fried rice which was really good! The spring rolls & fried chicken dumplings have become a necessity for my boyfriend & I each time we order. He also always gets the drunken noodles which is very flavorful! I hope to try more things from the menu and love them just as much as what I have already tried!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Best Indian in town.....hands down!

Hands down the best Thai in the St. Louis area. Their dishes are all perfectly seasoned and spiced, and their curries especially are exemplary for several reasons - overall flavor, freshness, speed of service, and your ability to select the spice and protein of your choice. Seriously, these will be the curries you judge all others against. Pad Thai is a favorite, as is the chicken satay and any of the fried rice dishes. At lunch, enjoy a complementary bowl of chicken vegetable soup. Again - freshness and flavor abound. Finally, their service is always friendly and fast. Best place for Thai in the area. Worth the trip over the river.
Best falafel I've ever tasted! It honestly lasts me two meals so $5 per meal is great. The chicken is flavored great and he puts a sauce on every day as well.

Wow! First time here last night and I cannot wait to go back! We stormed in here with very little time to spare. (Pho is always a good idea if you need to eat delicious food and get the hell out of dodge). We were seated immediately. Placed an order within five minutes. I told the waitress we were in a hurry. Five minutes later....lemon pepper chicken vermicelli! Veggie pho! Both delicious and incredibly filling. The chicken was insanely good, and the light dressing they bring with it is superb. I put the credit card down while we were still shoveling the food in our faces and Wam! Bam! Thank youuuuuu Ma'am! We were in and out in 20 minutes! Seriously, though. This place is nice! Great ambience, good for small groups, kids (if they are so inclined), dates, girls night out....really just an all around nice place to be.

Wow where do I begin? I called for a delivery and both gentlemen that I spoke to offered great suggestions and were very nice! I ordered something that was not ready yet but they offered to make it for me anyways! Food is AMAZING the food was sooo delicious I had to say it twice it was that good!! Between the amazing customer service and the even better food I will be a frequent customer here now and reccomending them to everyone! Thanks Guys!!!

Overall: authentic, delicious and inexpensive Indonesian food. Some context: I'm American, but have lived in Indonesia, so I'm familiar with the culture and food. Sky Cafe is an example of Chinese-influenced Indonesian cuisine. That is, this is distinctly Indonesian food, but Indonesia is a huge and extremely diverse place, and the menu at Sky Cafe tends to focus on the dishes you would encounter in a city like Jakarta where the ethnically Chinese population (~10% of the people) has had a significant influence on the local cuisine over the years. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Indonesian_cuisine The food here delivers the goods. I went with a group and we ordered a bunch of dishes family style. Some of my favorites: - Kewtiau Goreng: mmm, fried flat noodles... - Nasi Goreng: practically the national dish of indonesia, a good starting point for anyone - Satay Ayam: Juicy morsels of chicken on skewers with a peanut-based sauce - Nasi Lemak with Beef Rendang: this is actually a dish from Padang cuisine, another culinary tradition based on the island of Sumatra that is more influenced by Indian cuisine. - Nasi Ayam Sambal Hijau: this was an outstanding example of Indonesian fried chicken with a spicy green sambal (Indonesian chili sauce) - Soto Medan: a coconut-broth chicken soup, this is another non-Chinese type dish, but was perhaps my favorite of the night, really savory and delicious.
I've been here twice now. Comfy, decent service, and very yummy. Plus 20% off with a movie ticket! Good deal to me!
Arrived at 1130, meat was already prepared and tasted great. Not the most helpful staff (spoke so quickly i couldn't understand a word they said) but the food was worth it.

Just got delivery from this place, and it was wonderful! I had the naan, lamb biryani, and gulab jamun. The naan was great, the biryani was a HUGE portion with just enough spice for me (have PLENTY of leftovers - it was packed to the top of the container, almost bursting) and included TONS of lamb and a small container of yogurt sauce, and gulab jamun is just one of the greatest things ever. So good. They're also really good with delivery. Everything was in containers and wrapped on a bunch of plastic wrap, then put in the bag, so it stayed hot enough. Yay!

Delicious middle eastern food. The baba ghanoush is possibly the best I've had! The falafel was very fresh and the texture exquisite. Lamb kebabs and chicken shawarma was tender and spiced to perfection. The khubz iraqi pita bread was light and fluffy aromatic. Superb quality food at a very reasonable price, this is a restaurant I will put on my "come back" list for sure!
The food was fresh taste delicious the hummus was great the chicken was great the falafel's went great the baklava was great it was all great!

They have great customer service, but the portions are becoming smaller as time goes on. Me and my wife drove out to eat here expecting the salad that I normally have to be the same, but instead it was decreased significantly in size. The people who prepare the food are very nice and high energy. Great customer service. Wanted to give a full five stars but the adjustment to the portion size ruined it for me.

I came here for a quick bite and was immediately attracted to this place because it wasn't busy at 6pm on a Saturday ...but I kind of see why. It's nicely decorated & sets a nice ethnic vibe inside, plus the front windows open to Whyte ave for a cafè-like feel as you watch pedestrians pass by. There's also a TV and Middle Eastern music playing overhead to add to the ambience. Staff are friendly, but service is a bit slow...but I think it's because the food was made to order. The nice thing is that they serve the food up to your table after you've ordered. Unfortunately most of the tables were not cleaned up /wiped down from previous guests. I also don't think my meal was good value for cost. I ordered a donair poutine and a can of pop and it came to about $16; taste-wise it wasn't anything amazing either, but at least they had a good ratio of donair fillings to fries. I think this would be a great place to socialize and linger while you wait for your order. I think if I came back here, I'd probably order something more authentic on their menu than fusion flavored junk food.

The place isn't in the best area in town, but it is nice and clean inside. Food was really good so definayely worth grabbing and going. The ambience and service inside was lacking quite a bit to bring down the whole experience. TVs had sound on and they were battling each other and the waiter dropped off our food we didn't see him again until the check came.

Great breakfast & lunch at good prices. During dinner it converts into a high scale restaurant with a more expensive menu, so you know the quality/ taste of the food for breakfast & lunch is really good. my review applies to their breakfast and lunch menu, not dinner. highly recommend. the place is really busy in the mornings until about 11am. so i would recommend going after 11am but before 4pm, which is when the waitress start preparing the restaurant for dinner mode and the staff are not as attentive. the food is really good, coffee is awesome. i like how they offer unique items on their menu like they are a trendy California eatery. for instance, they had a salmon chowder on their menu for lunch so i decided to try it. ever since, i constantly ask them if they have any salmon chowder available - it was amazing and the taste of the salmon was shuttle but really good. i do not eat salmon often but this made me a fan of salmon chowder.

The $2.75 banh mi are pretty good but the options are limited. They seem to come standard with carrot, daikon, onion, cilantro + "shredded or steamed pork," bbq pork, or carrot stewed beef (for a couple more dollars). The french roll is pretty standard, crunchy (good jaw exercise) and a little wider and shorter than the Mr. Lee's baguette style sandwich. Wash it down with a cà phê sa á (iced coffee w/ sweet. cond. milk) but be sure to mix up the coffee / milk before pouring because it won't mix when cold. The afternoon (off hour) is likely to see mostly customers of non-Vietnemese origin and the surly waitress may be surlier than usual. If you are in the neighborhood and decide to stop by spontaneously, you can get last-minute cash from the ATM down the street at Kroger, for a $2.50 surcharge.

I'm leaving you Meatloaf. I've found someone else. First a little background on who I am. Irish American. Raised on Meat, Potatoes and Kraft Macaroni & Cheese (or is it Cheese & Macaroni?). So my taste buds have lain dormant for years. Fast Forward 30 years ahead... I work in Oaks, PA. I have a couple of Indian friends that suggested we go to the Dosa Hut for lunch which is about 5 minutes away. I go there and I tell them I like Spicey (Hot) foods. They tell me to go for the Chicken Biryani. 10 minutes later and I'm sweating. This stuff is pretty Spicey. I like it but I am not sure I like the sweating. I go home that night and suddenly realize that I crave the taste! Since the first visit I have gone to Dosa Hut 4 times in 3 months. I have tried the other dishes and they are good but i recommend an order of Samosa and the Chicken Biryani. Its real good. The CONS: The place is very small and there is no real decor. The food is served on plastic plates with plastic forks. To CONSIDER: The food must be that good if it lacks any presentation whatsoever (see: "The CONS")

This is very specific but this place used to have really good Churros. They were covered in cinnamon and served with a rich chocolate sauce. Came back and they now dip one side in chocolate so when they come to the table that side is soggy the other side is flavorless. And they have what appears to be fruity pebbles on the chocolate end. They are dusted with powdered sugar but it is wrapped in a wax paper so the paper is sugared and your churro is dry. Why, just why? The explanation given was it was more traditional. I lived in Chicago and had many a churro - never was it dry as a bone one end and covered in cereal on the other. Other than that tasty and little more expensive than it needs to be but it'll do.

This place is awesome. My wife and I visited this place and ordered lemon grass soup, satay chicken, green curry and jatujak stir fried. The server asked for our preferred spice level on a scale of 1 to 5 while his suggestion being 2-3. It's pity I tried to challenge their spice level and asked for 4, should have listened to him. Anyway, it was really hot and we started sweating soon. However still we could feel ta flavour and it was amazing, one of the best places that you can have in Philly. The service was awesome and the server was repeatedly asking if we are doing fine. Will visit there again.
Delicious! First time eating there tonight . The people are friendly, the prices are cheap , and the food is great . I'm not even vegetarian and the food was quality. I would 100 % recommend it.
Although I liked the appetizers we got there was not impressed with their version of Phad Thaii but that could be personal preference. It's honey based and a bit sweeter then I normally like.
