During our meal, 3 different managers came over and apologized, but I come back to the hosts - we were seated right next to them, they saw that we were not being served (we could hear them talking about the fact we weren't getting service), according to the manager they are the ones who overloaded our waiter and they could have helped out a lot. My suggestion to management - tell your hosts that they are part of the team (my guess is that they receive a percentage of the server's tips) and need to assist when necessary, not just stand around chatting.

I'm a big fan of Sky Cafe. I've ordered so much from them, and it is always really good. Also, not to make it a big deal, but you should know that it always seems to be the same delivery guy and he is full of smiles and haste. In any case, I strongly recommend that you try Sky Cafe at least once if you live in South Philadelphia. They are very consistent, the noodle dishes in particular are great (Mie complete has lots of different tastes included like meatballs, broth, egg, wonton and soup broth.) I don't want to dissuade you from ordering something like nasi goreng (fried rice) from here though because I really think they make it the best - the pickles in particular are awesome. I'm going to tag on a few tips: The wonton soup is awesome - they make their own wontons and I think they use a combination of pork and dried shrimp which yields a toothsome dumpling! Gado gado is not on the menu, but they will make it if you ask (I get the impression from the telephone receiver that this is often). It is a lot better than the same dish that some of my favorite other Indonesian options in the area make. Seriously, if you like gado-gado, they make a really good one and I do recommend it.

Excellent food with quick and friendly service! My daughter literally asks for it once a week. The only thing I'm used to from one of my dear friends who was from Pakistan is a little more "heat" when I order the dishes spicy. Overall, def one of our frequent go to places!

I visited this place Friday night, expected a larger restaurant but was pleasantly surprised at the smaller space, high ceilings make it seem bigger. Had made a reservation but instead of a hostess assisting with seating were told simply to choose a seat from a server behind the bar. I was a but nervous as it took sometime to get menus and drinks ordered- the food was excellent. I had the plantain lasagna (spinach). A plentiful portion however I wouldn't have turned down more as it was so delicious. The passion fruit sangria was quite syrup based in my opinion. The service with a shaky start ended excellently, friendly & helpful to me as I had not had Puerto Rican food before, I'd definitely return to Salsa
The food was excellent. Service was reasonably quick. Wish they had a better selection of beer on tap.
Had the pho and spring roll for lunch. Broth was creamy and rich in a good way. What more can you ask.

I have a friend that loves their Tom Kha Gai and currey so I probably should have tried one of those but I went with another noodle dish, Pad (Pawt) Woosen ordered spicy with fried tofu and broccoli, a thai tea and a salad. I knew I was in for a wait because there were two young guys running back and forth with a look of stress though the place was not busy. They offered a thai tea refill which was kind. A single to-go container came out of the kitchen twenty-five minutes later. He didn't charge me for the salad so I didn't mention it. I checked my noodles and I could tell it had no spice. I asked for a container of pepper flakes as I was signing my receipt but told him never mind when he said to give him five minutes. During transit my to-go container ended up on it's side which actually helped drain the excess oil out of the dish.

My dad and I came here for lunch one day since we were in the area and I heard it had vegetarian options. He got a burger type sandwich and I a salad. The service and the food were so good! Fast forward a couple months and we brought my mom and brother for dinner after raving about it since our last visit. It was more busy during dinner than at night. We were sat outside even though it was surprisingly chilly. The waitress was slow. Slow to even get our drink orders. I ordered the grilled veggie salad again, my family different meals. It was like a whole other restaurant. The food was bland, not warm enough, just altogether not great. My brother and mom looked at us like, "this is what you were excited about?" Nobody was impressed. Even the garlic potatoes weren't good! I'm so disappointed I doubt I, or my family, will ever go back again. There are better options in Tucson, especially in that area. I think Sauce is down the street if you would like a good salad.
Some of the best Indian food I've had. The samosas were good everything we ordered was great. Good vegan options too.

Food was very good. I expected the menu to be "more" Greek (no lamb) but besides that I would recommend it for something different and fresh. I ordered their take on the Ruben. It was made with turkey and feta. It was very good. The potato salad was my choice of side and the red potatoes were firm and the dressing was very light and citrusy. Very good too and it didn't need any salt added as most potato salads do. About $10.00 with bottled water. The service was very quick. You order at the counter and they bring you the food and clean up after you.

I will never return to this place. I went there close to lunch buffet closing time. I asked if food was still available, and so it was. The food was horrendous. Dry, nasty, almost taste like left over from the night before. This was my second visit here (first time buffett). If the food was to be trashed or taken back to the kitchen, why didn't say so? I will not go back.

This is a remodeled Bob Evans so you can imagine how huge the place is. It's not a pho house...it's a pho mansion. It's fairly new, so it's super clean inside and well-appointed. There is plenty of seating (as you can imagine) and can easily accomodate large groups. There's even counter seating (a carryover from the building's Bob Evans days). I went for lunch on a Thursday and only one side of the seating area was being used. That's not to say it wasn't busy, because it was. On to the food. I had the pork spring rolls as a starter which were quite fresh and tasty. Of course I had pho for my entree. All the bowls come in 2 sizes ($8 for the medium, and $11 for the large). I opted for the medium as I had an appetizer. Pho is all about the broth. Saigon gets it right. Savory and slightly sweet, with a little oiliness. During weekdays there's a $5 lunch special which comes with soup which I will have to try next time (if I can resist the pho).

Five stars for karaoke. Three stars for food. Come here if you want to eat while singing and watching others sing. Go somewhere else if you just want good Ethiopian food. This place isn't the worst, but it's just not as good as the other options within walking distance. Das dat good ole American com-per-tition. Yee haw. Lol.

Ok you can eat with your hands and watch belly dancers all in a restaurant whose windows are covered from onlookers outside. Very cool! From the outside you'd probably be weary of entering, as was I. The inside is covered (walls and ceiling) with colorful Moroccan fabrics and from the ceiling (aka: draped fabric) hangs a few Moroccan lanterns. The tables (circular cushioned benches around a small circular table) are low and line the walls. Before eating you everyone at the table puts there hands in the center over a basin and the water pours warm water of them. This is preparation for dinner because you are eating with your hands. For those who'd rather not but were still dragged here (or scared 1st dates) , they will also give you utensils. (Boo!) I was weary of the food as well, but I loved it all (I have to admit I wasn't sure what exactly we were ordering at some part). You can get a dinner of eight courses for $25 a person. Get this. Don't question what you are eating. One of the courses is beef with powdered sugar on it (I'm pretty sure) and it is amazing. Actually, all the courses taste pretty sweet. Oh yea: you can also smoke a hookah (it is encouraged) while you are enjoying your belly dancing. HINT: After dinner DO NOT think you are funny by asking your hot date to "smell my finger."
I went here twice. Ordered the PHO and later ordered a noodle dish. Both were well under par and lacked flavor. There are much better Vietnamese restaurants in the suburbs for true foodies.
Cozy little restaurant with very friendly staff. The steamed dumplings were delicious and the panang was savory.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Most amazing India/Pakistan food I have ever had in the US. Staff is EXTREEMLY helpful and they make every thing from scratch, so they can work around any food sensitivities. Really amazing and delicious night.

Nicest waitress and great food with plenty of spice!! Started with the chicken wings; the sauce is really awesome!!! Main course was goat curry and lamb byriani. Both were really tasty. They hooked us up with plenty of rice and fresh paneer kulcha. The restaurant is really nice too. Cheers!!

I wish there were in between ratings or you could split them by category, but alas, only whole star ratings. The food here is good for sure and the menu is really good as it specifies what is vegan, vegetarian and gluten free. Though the staff here is hit or miss. The manager, or who I assume to be the manager, was polite and courteous, but the second we got in I got a bad vibe from the initial person to greet us. The waiter, who wound up being alright, started out upset that we changed the number of guests (albeit something I'm not happy about myself, but things happen). There was some initial complaining, a bunch of it, which we could easily hear. Eventually he warmed up and wasn't bad, but not a particularly enthusiastic waiter. The other staff was way too comfortable chatting and hanging out. I started having flashbacks to kitchen impossible and whatever show that is where they install cameras to observe the staff. Definitely could use some work in that regard. The fact it was a Wednesday night in Wilmington DE and we had a sizable party, despite losing some guests, and we were spending a fair amount of money there, just seemed to be lost on the staff. We could have easily gone somewhere else and spent our evening, and money, elsewhere. Be thankful for our patronage and we'll be thankful for your service. Serve good food while doing so and we'll even come back, plus maybe even recommend the place.
Waited an hour and half for delivery. All I can say. I travel significantly and use eat24 consistently and this has been the poorest service and response to date

I ordered delivery. They did not give me utensils or napkins. When I called the delivery guy and said "I think you forgot to give me utensils," he replied, "you didn't add that to the comments." Are you serious..? Since when do delivery/take out need to explicitly ask for UTENSILS to EAT the food? He didn't even apologize for this mistake. Additionally, the samosa was not good. I'm usually a big fan of chicken tikka masala but it was NOT good here. Would NOT order again.

Absolutely horrible. So we come in and order our drinks. The server was great. She was friendly and sweet and all. However, when I told her that I ABSOLUTELY cannot have cilantro and proceeded to order things, confirming once again they don't have cilantro, they came with cilantro... I mean come on! Anyways, my paella comes (for the second time because the first time it has cilantro) and holy hell. The shrimp were, I kid you not, the size of quarters. The scallops were the size of dimes. DIMES! There were 4 buckle sized chunks of chicken and two (TWO!) Nicole sized chunks of beef. Maybe like 6 mussels on top. If you like seafood, DO NOT GET THIS DISH! For $21 I feel like I was robbed. It was literally rice with frozen bagged shrimp and scallops (again, the size of dimes...) with the tiniest amount of meat. Fun fact: the tortilla soup and black bean soup have cilantro Finally, we finished with the Cuban cake. Oh my god. I cannot tell you how absolutely disgusting this piece of garbage was. Imagine somebody takes a stick of butter, half a cup of sugar, and a cup of flour and bakes that. That's what it is. It's like literally eating a stick of butter. Where was the cake part at all!? It sounds good, I mean butter is always good, but this was the devil. So our bill comes and after having to swap out our soup (that had cilantro despite my allergy) AND me having to wait for my entire meal to be sent back (sans cilantro), we were not given any discount nor did the manager come over. Just don't go here, okay?
The falafal sandwich was really good.
Our family of 15 went for dinner the other evening and the food was fabulous! Authentic Dominican selections, no one was disappointed. Reasonable prices. Would highly recommend!
GREAT FOOD! It was our first time trying Dominican food. Dishes served there were very tasty, the portions were big and the service was really nice. Everyone left full and happy. Highly recommend!

My colleague and selected this place randomly on Yelp. And I didn't walk in with any expectation since the night we were here was right before the Thanksgiving. Thought any extraordinary type of chef must be home with their kinds and family. But oh boy. They nailed it! We ordered three dishes they all are fresh and stunningly delicious. You must see my photos to find out what they are and try them when you can. I don't want you to miss anything! My waiter Nik is such a wonderful cute little soul. Swirling around the place and tentatively stopping by our table and ask if we need anything.

This was my first time here. On a weekend night, the hostess recommended that we have a reservation, however, tonight we were able to get seated almost immediately. The food was absolutely excellent. We shared 2 traditional dishes, "Chicken Tikka Masala" and "Chicken Tikka" they were fantastic! The service was really quite good, and their recommendations for entrees gave us a place to start on our next visit. We liked the long grain rice that they serve with your meal - perfectly cooked, it did not stick together. It had a light and nutty flavor. As a starter, you get very thin Lentil "chips" or "crisps" that are freshly made in house. I had never tried anything like it. These "crisps" are my new favorite - and since they are made of a vegetable, it is guiltless. Next time we will explore the menu a bit more, and we are already planning another visit this week.

We went to this restaurant for lunch. Ordered Spicy chicken fried rice, panang curry and coconut soup. Portion was good, food was decent but service was horrible. Waitress had no smile, she didnt bother to come and ask if we needed anything. We had to get walk to waitress and ask for rice, water and bill.

This is another great, hidden gem in Philadelphia. This Trinidadian eatery is tucked away at on Baltimore Avenue near 53nd Street. The oxtail platter cost no more than $6 and included a flavorful accompaniment of beans and rice and a cole slaw flavored with horseradish. I highly recommend this place to any ventursome foodie who is looking for an inexpensive and exotic getaway for their palate.

Food is good but the service is terrible. Takes forever to be acknowledged by wait staff. Sometimes i get my food before they even bring a drink. Forget about "check back" during your meal. Seriously lacking.

I'm going to go ahead and rate this as a 5 for hookah and a 2 as a bar. Let's go over the former first. The hookah here is great flavor and variety, and the prices aren't bad either - 13 for standard flavors and 8 on sundays and happy hour every day. Hookah last FOREVER too. Last two times I've gone, party of 2 and 3 respectively, the hookah lasted for 3-4 hours, partly because they do a great job coming by and replacing the coals and using several smaller ones instead of one large cylindrical one. Overall great hookah and lasting flavor and smoke thickness. I'm no hookah snob but I did really appreciate the quality of this place. Now for the bar, I've gone here for the bar as well and they're relatively quick with drink orders but pretty bad about getting you a bit of water when you need it. Which probably wouldn't matter so much if you didn't also smoke hookah here. Also, I feel they could use a couple more waiters/servers for weekend nights, since that's when their service starts lacking a bit since I assume they make more money on drinks than on hookah. Also, if you ask for a rum and coke, its pretty funny how they charge you the 7 dollars for a shot (at most) of rum, and the 2 dollars for a full can of coke. So yea, don't come here for the bar.

Wow what happened! We usually LOVE this place, but tonight it was such a disappointment. It was tasteless. Maybe they changed cooks...so sad. Curry chicken boring, beef vandal of boring. And these are the go to dishes for us. Chili chicken dry and hot. Tandoori shrimp dry tasteless served over raw onion and raw green onion. Weird. Never got the last two dishes before, never again.

I have been to a numbers of Korean BBQ restaurants in my living area and eventually found Corean House. They offer all you can eat BBQ for $19.99 which is lower than other ones (the AYCE prices is $23 in average these days). The price is lower but their service and food quality is way higher than others! Maybe because they don't have too much business now 'cause it's under a new ownership recently. I hope they can keep their quality service. Why only give them 4 star? They don't change pan for you! If you eat there for 5 plates of meet you will get a black and burned grill pan. One star is gone! Improve this minor issue then I will give the star back to you!

PF Changs issues: 1: gritty plates, like all the detergent wasn't rinsed off, 2: serving plates were not warm, so the food cooled off quickly, 3: long wait (10+ min) from when our dinner plates were cleared and dessert was served, 4: Table was not cleaned after dinner. I've experienced better.

Best food truck hands down. I've been here twice and both times I ordered the Cap'n crunch burrito - spicy. Words can't even describe how tasty this is. The Thai tea is also amazing. I want to try the tacos next time I'm here. Their prices are very reasonable for a gourmet food truck.
Friendly family owned small business. I really love bubble tea. I tried the coffee bubble tea and it was really good.

The family that runs this place is very sweet. The location feels a little odd because it looks like it's in a condo complex, but the food was worth the jaunt. We were comp-ed an appetizer and dessert just because the woman running the place liked my outfit and had a nice conversation with me. Looks loved by the locals in the know as well.

We had the lunch buffet here on a weekend. Although its gross, I have to tell you this. After the buffet, my poor roommate puked out everything he ate. And I had a stomach upset the very next day. The whole selection of food, floats in oil. I would not recommend to anyone, who has a good knowledge of Indian food.

Best Thai restaurant in STL. They're owned by the same family of the other Thai restaurants in the Loop, but this is the one to come to! Want Lao style Papaya Salad with crab and fried pork rinds? They got you! I love the servers here as well. They always remember how I like my papaya salad. Oh and of course the other dishes are good. Love their duck curry, tom yum noodle soup, pad thai, etc... The last time I ordered their Nam Tok, they used a sweet and sour sauce, which confused me. I hope that's not how they are making it from now on. I think they might have given me the wrong dish. Whatevs. I love this place so much that even when their credit card machine is not working at the moment or the service is a little slow because of a packed house- I never get mad. Food is too good!

I was driving down Germantown and saw the grand opening sign several times but never had time to stop. Finally I had some time and tried this fish hoagie ,everyone talks about . I am a super fan now ! fast forward to NYC SOBS in April album release party of Pharoahe Monch PTSD . Came down to see his manager and the show. An Awesome show with heavy hitters of Hip Hop and R&B . So I was talking with some of the performers and we started talking about Philly and Food . And Sis Muhammad's food came up and we all got hungry. lol They where coming to Philly soon to do a show at Milk Boy and where gonna stop by to get some of her famous Fish Hoagies. Rock of Heltah Skeltah was very familiar with her foods and came to find out he knew a lot of the same people I knew in Philly. Hip Hop and good food unites so many people. Sis Muhammad's food is known by some of the best Hip hop Artist !!

I wish I could give negative stars. DO NOT GO TO THIS PLACE. For starters there was an infant seated at the table next to me despite the fact I was carded while entering. Unless the child was stricken with the same affliction as Benjamin Button, I'm pretty sure she was not legally allowed to be in there. Normally i wouldn't care, but the child would not stop making noise. More importantly, I WAS OVERCHARGED FOR MY DRINK AND INVOLUNTARILY CHARGED OVER 20% GRATUITY FOR A PARTY OF TWO. NO WHERE ON THE MENU WAS THAT POLICY STATED. Once I brought this to the waiters attention, he initially did not want to correct the problem, but after 10mins of me explaining basic 2nd grade math to him, he had no choice but to remove the FRAUDULENT charges. No apology, no comp, nothing. I won't be back and I will be taking legal measures to resolve this matter. This is not over. STAY AWAY!

I just love this place! All the good things about it: + for people who cannot handle spicy but still enjoy Indian food, they offer all their dishes in a mild version and unlike in some other restaurants, it really IS mild + The Chicken Tikka Masala and the Keema Naan are my favorites, so yummy + for lunch, they have an all you can eat buffet. It's not the greatest variety but it usually has naan, rice, salad, samosas, and about four or so entrees + you can get take out + the main waitress is not the most cheerful but is pretty quick, always notices when glasses are empty, etc. + service is pretty quick. doesn't take long for the food to come out + very affordable and generous portions (I can never finish my dish, always have some leftovers) + very pretty interior, you would not expect that from the outside
Keeping in mind this is mostly a take out place or really casual eat-in, I love it. I've only been here a couple of times, unfortunately, but it has been great. A simple place with delicious food.

This place has some of the best Thai food in Nashville. It's pretty small so probably not the best option if you're going with a group but perfect if you have 1-4 people. The staff are pretty nice. As some of the other reviews said, they are down to business and are trying to get you in and out as soon as possible. While annoying, it's understandable since they have limited seating. The food is great. They don't cut any corners and give you very high quality tasting food. Here's my one issue with this place: the lunch and dinner portions are the same. But... the prices are not even close. While I understand restaurants raise their prices for dinner, they usually increase their portion sizes as well. I found that to be annoying. All in all, this is a great place to try. You won't be disappointed if you love Thai food.

We are in Nashville for vacation and my birthday! I love Thai food and this was walking distance to our rental. It was the absolute best Thai I have had. You will have about a 20 minute wait, but it's worth it. The service was great especially for how busy they were. We started with the peanut fresh rolls. The dipping sauce had just the right amount of heat. I had the Pad Thai and I know what you are thinking! This place is known for its authentic Pad Thai. No sweet American sauce here AND they use green bean starch noodles. It was like no Pad Thai I've had before. Very good and a huge portion so you can share or take it home for another meal! My hubby had the red curry which was also very good. If you're in Nashville you must go and try it! Reasonable prices too.

Fish and chip restaurant during day called Marina. Had wings with fries and shrimp racos with fries. Hot wings had interesting and tasty sauce which surprised me. Shrimp tacos were also good and not fried which is heathy. The inside of restaurant is confusing with different themes going on...like someone was going to belly dance. I wish i could order food from patio from window cause i dont want to get involved with sitting down cause it really complicates thing...Fish and chips or seafood is better when its takeout...otherwise you want to be able to order lobster or crab and expect Louisiana style or Pacific pier or Maine etc. I tried to explain how the owner could improve but i felt like Jerry Seinfeld when he ate at Babos restaurant and kept telling to change his restaurant concept until he blamed him for going out of business. So Food is excellent but ambience is confusing so 3 stars.

Wowy Kazowy!!! This place was awesome!! So after battling a month long craving for a falafel I decided that if I was going to have one that it was gonna be the best in the city. After spending a shameful amount of time reading review after review for every falafel joint this city has to offer (Mama's, Maoz, Alyan's etc) and being even more unsure then before I had done some investigating,my boyfriend put all the names in a hat and by a stroke of what I can only see as Divine Intervention Chickpeas was the one I picked. It was amazing, the pita was soft and fresh and the hummus warm and full of flavor. We got 2 falafels a side of hummus and 2 drinks for under $20 and we were stuffed! Only negative is that they were out of ALOT of things, basically everything but falafel and humus

So I'm not sure why this place has uptown in the name when it's clearly in the Garden District. But that's just me being picky. I stopped in during the 1st weekend of carnival season and they were serving a limited menu and all orders were handled at the bar. No problem. I ordered a couple of bahn mis for me & my family and they came out quickly. Both sandwiches (grilled shrimp and tofu) were delicious and huge! Staff was very nice and gave me a huge glass of ice water which was much needed on that warm first Sunday. 4 stars for life-giving food during carnival. Now I'll just have to get back over there for a meal when they have regular service.

Love the food here. I always get the lunch special drunken noodle to go... love it! the woman there is always very pleasant and prices are really good, too. i never eat inside but it's cute, little and cozy!

If you want a hoagie that is not laden with enough cholesteral to choke an ox, a Vietnamese hoagie from Cafe Huong Lan is worth a shot. Good for veg-heads and carnivores alike, there are many different options, some of which Americans may find a little intimidating. My usual was the vegetarian hoagie because it was so damn yummy. With seasoned tofu, fresh cilantro, some sort of buttery mayo and jalapeno peppers on a very fresh French baguette, it is so deliciously light and perfect. If you really want to reduce the fat, get it without the buttery stuff. It's still good. I'm also a big fan of their tapioca-like plantain pudding dealie. I know that's not the proper terminology but that's pretty much what it is. It's delicious.

Bacon, egg, and cheese. Enough said. Been at Penn for three years and I come here a couple of times each week for a quick breakfast/lunch/I'm hungry moment. Bui's has some pretty solid specialty sandwiches (e.g. Ms. Bui), but none of them beat the simple perfection that is their bacon, egg, and cheese. If there is one specialty sandwich I would recommend though, it's the Turkey BLT...the amount of turkey bacon they put in there seems extremely generous. Quick tip: If you have no idea what the dude is asking you after you place your order, he's most likely asking if you want "salt, pepper, ketchup" on your sandwich. :)

Not gonna lie, Asian restaurants will have bad to mediocre service and that's more normal in the Bay Area with the influx of Asian owned restaurants. That being said, the pho here is my favorite pho in all of Reno. I really enjoy their banh xeo that is only available on weekends. The pho is flavorful and they give you sooo much meat and noodles in your bowl for the price. A medium is definitely more than enough to fill me up but I can't resist a good banh xeo either. The banh xeo is superrr crispy. They definitely know how to make these but the ingredient preparation is a little time consuming for those who complain they run out or won't do it later. The actual making isn't that long and should be easy for them, but when they run low on shrimp/pork/other items in their dish, they probably only allocated so many. I also had their 3 bean dessert and their Vietnamese coffee. The dessert is good with the coconut milk, pretty typical in taste. The coffee is a bit sweeter but still strong.

My favorite pho. The broth is so savoury and satisfying! The family is so sweet and the Dad (Owner) always gives a Mr Freeze to the kids after their meal. Diamond in the rough! Support local business!

I've described this food as one of the best Indian meals I've ever had, not just here in Florida, but all over the world. I'll be returning here just to make sure I'm right. The bread was delicious, the saag paneer was superb, the chicken tika masala was the best. Just a great place.

Some of the best Indian dishes I have ever had. Compares to the best places in Philly and NYC. The food took a little while to get to our table, and this is because it is made freshly with fresh ingredients. We had our three kids and the staff was very accommodating and helpful. The decor was very nice. Great place for a date, or lunch meeting. Must see- best restaurant in town by far. BYOB, so don't forget to bring a bottle or 6-pack before you go.

Rarely write a review but gotta do this one. the food with the price is completely perfect. Lassi taste super natural, feeling like you're eating real fruit. chaat is perfect for a small dinner. taste delicious the seat at the corner was quite and beautiful for hanging out, reading, chatting. owner was super friendly and gave me rice budding as a treat as he knows I'm leaving town. Definitely remcommend this place and definitely come back to Philly just for this.

Wooo second review for Cucina!! Back at again why? Because they're the best food truck that I have tried, obviously. Who needs more food trucks when you have Cucina? I'm just going to reiterate what I said before about Cucina Zapata. They are incredibly friendly, won't get mad at you when you take a little too long to decide what sauce you want (hehe, guilty), and their food is prepared with love. I will willingly wait for half an hour before they open just to have their food early in the late morning/early afternoon. bon appetit/bon bon feet/bon whatever-floats-your-boat!

Stopped into this restaurant as we were passing through Philly based upon the great reviews and ordered the lunch special to go. It was: Beef stew, yellow rice, black beans, some plantains and a salad. The lady behind the counter with the curly hair was super sweet and more than generous dishing out our rice. We are talking heaping spoonfuls!! She also gave us some extra broth to go and packed everything so well that it wouldn't spill all over the car! Bonus! Needless to say, this lunch special was enough to feed two people. And --- it will only cost you 7 or 8 bucks!! The owner overheard us debating which juice to try and gave us a sample of the passion fruit juice and of course we ended up ordering one. A little on the sweet side, as juices tend to be, but really refreshing on a warm day! This place was a great value if you are looking for some authentic and fresh Dominican food in Philly! It is obvious that the owner puts his heart and soul into this operation. Support local!!

Got dinner here with my boyfriend twice so far. It was two of three times I've had Indian food and I think it's great. My bf has had a lot of Indian food before and he thinks it's the best place around. Service there is great. It's ran by brothers and they're both very nice! I love their chicken mango, now I crave it every few days. For the price, we've always had great food for it, there's plenty of times where I've spent more money on bad food but never here!

Used to be great, but service has been really slow the last few times I've been, not to mention messing up orders the last two times. Also, they seemed to have a roach problem on my last visit (8/10/2012).

I have only been here once because I thought everything was below average. Me and my boyfriend ate here on a Friday at the bar. I really don't like the paper place mats they put down in front of you, but that an aesthetic thing. I ordered the fettuccine in a marinara with a meatball because I was feeling pretty traditional that night and my boyfriend got red mussels over pasta. I was so disappointed. The gravy had so much oil in it, I actually couldn't finish it and the meatball was very hard. My boyfriend had the exact same experience with his gravy as well. I have heard from people whose tastes I trust that my experience is outside of the norm, but unfortunately I can only base my review on my dining experience and I have to say I was just generally underwhelmed.
Amazing food!! Clean and beautifully decorated restaurant with great service. Highly recommended for fresh, flavorful and authentic thai food.

Went here for dinner on a Monday night after attempting to go to Sweet and Stuff Sushi on Olive St. and found out it was closed. ( after calling and they confirmed they would be open!) Always wanted to try here and I wasn't disappointed. We were there in time for the weekday 5-6 pm 3 course meal. I tried the hot lemongrass soup which was delicious. It was tangy and spicy and left me wanting more. I have though about getting the soup take out since then. My friend had the coconut soup which was nice. For the appetizer, I had the fried wonton and my friend had the spring roll and they give you two of each. It was nice to try each one and not be completely filled by the time your entree arrived. I had the drunken noodles which I would recommend and my friend had Massaman curry which I tried and was delicious. I also tried the Mango drink, which is mango juice which apparently is heated with some sugar cane and then cooled...or at least thats the explantation I got from my server. This place was a definity win and I will go here again, and I also want to try the Glen Mills location too. Its BYOB if your into that.

I like Pollo Tropical a lot. It's a good alternative for fast food that's actually healthier than typical fast food. I love their 1/2 chicken with a large selection of dipping sauces with corn and rice & beans on the side. When I really want to eat healthier, then it's time to go with the skinless chicken breast. Very tasty. If chickens not your thing, Pollo Tropical also offers ribs and pulled pork as well. They are pretty good as well.

First time trying this place and I was not disappointed. I ordered the fish platter with mac&cheese and cabbage. The cabbage was a little bland and it seemed as if they threw the entire head of cabbage in the pot without cutting it. Overall great food and great customer service.

Awesome food. And this is coming from a fat guy who loves to eat. I've eaten at a majority of the Jamaican food places in Trenton, and I would consider this place the "gourmet" of Jamaican food. Would get 5 stars if they had their own dedicated parking. Top notch food, great service!

Best Thai food in the Tampa Bay Area! We have been coming here for years and even after moving from Valrico to Tampa we still make the drive at least twice a month. The wait staff is very friendly and the restaurant ambiance is very calming. We've tried other Thai restaurants and this is by far the best. I love their pineapple curry, it's the perfect combination of sweet and spicy. This is one of my favorite restaurants!

We visited Pho 79 because we're close to Garden City and Pho Bac was closed. I wish I could say I've found a great pho place, unfortunately it's not the case. The noodles are steak were fine, but the broth was not. They use too much anise, so there's a heavy black licorice flavor. And they char the white onion before adding it to the soup, which at first intrigued me, but ultimately added a strange burnt flavor. I won't be returning.

I would normally rave about this place. They do have great food, however, I stopped in to order some lunch and the lady at the register seen a had a soda in hand that I had purchased earlier and said I can't order any food from them if I have a drink already. I thought she was just joking but I was mistaken. I was asked to throw away my drink or leave. It was a can of Pepsi.... I wasn't even asked if I wanted it to go. I will never attend this business again. It's sad because they were so rude to someone that ate at their place at least 2-3 times a month and raved about their food and service. In fact I work at a nearby businesses and many of us go there to enjoy. I'm going to ask everyone to be aware of what happened and hopefully they will choose to not patronize them either.

What luck, today I wanted Gyros and I see Go! Gyro! Go! pull into the parking lot. Excellent Gyro. I got the Greek Salad with Gyro Meat and a side of Homemade Tzatziki. Yum. I look forward to their return next Tuesday!!!

i have only had their baklava and hummus. THEIR BAKLAVA IS GREAT. or it could just be that i am obsessed with baklava. my boyfriend tried their gyro the other day. it was not special but it wasnt bad either. very nice people. i wish they were open later than 7 though.
They have really good selection of food! My favorite ones are panang curry, drunken noodles, and red curry! I come back here every time I crave for Thai food! This is the best food truck.

In the midst of a random greek food craving my partner and I drove an hour and a half to get to zekos and it was worth every second of the drive. The staff was inviting the price was fair and the food was served quick and in generous portions honestly no complaints

I wanted to like this place sooo badly! Thai Mexican fusion? Food truck? Sounded so awesome!! Unfortunately, the food was below my expectations. (Or my expectations were just too high, having just spent last weekend, and years before, in California and all). I got the 3 taco deal ($8 for 3, or else it's $3 each). I ordered 2 shortribs and 1 chicken. I'm glad I got two of the shortribs b/c they were by far better (maybe just personal taste). It was a sweet glazed BBQ flavor, yum! Only problem was that the beef was too tough, wayyy overcooked. The flavor made up for it. The chicken was a curry satay flavor, not so sure how I feel about it in a taco. The soft taco shells were so-so, nothing special, but not bad, probably store bought. The semi spicy mayonnaise was pretty tasty though! I also ordered mango "tea", which is a slight misnomer. It's more of a really sweet yogurt (condensed milk?) drink... So something like a mango lassi, no tea in it. For $2, it's not bad, but they reAlly should call it something else! Add 50cents to add boba to your drink. So why 4 stars when I thought the food was mediocre? Friendly service goes a long way, and they just seemed like really nice people. It also led me to discover a whole row of food trucks on Ludlow serving the Drexel community, which I otherwise wouldn't have known about, even though I pass by the area on my walk home every day! They have a few other items I still want to try. Will update as I make my way through the menu!

Tonight is happy night to see my pal. Over the weekend I was able to meet up with Anna. But today I am meeting with three yelpiest friends to try the 7 course beef dish from my last review. I have seven beef dishes on other Vietnamese restaurant before. The first course is the raw slice beef in the vinegar onion broil. Then beef is wrapping in rice paper with veggie. The sauce inside the wrap can be hoisin sauce and dip it on the fish sauce. The second course is herb marinated slice beef to be cooked in butter. Then it is wrapping with rice paper with vermicelli. The third course is the slice beef in peanut. The first three courses require some work to wrap it. Some is skill with the wrap. The trick is not to over fill with material. The fourth course is the ground beef in tea leave. The ground beef is marinated then grill on the frying pan. The fifth course is the beef balls with shrimp chip. The beef ball is cook with clear vermicelli. This ball can be break into pieces and pickup with the shrimp chip. With the crispy of the shrimp chip and ground beef, it create the sensation of the crispy and meat flavor. The sixth course is the Sherrard beef with porridge. It top with some fried onion and the parsley. By mixing it provide some mixture of the flavor. The seventh course is the slice pork on the outwardly roll around the raw green onion. The slice beef is marinated and grilled outwardly. This course can be improved if they caramel the onion first before the slice beefs rolling will be better. It will take away the onion spiciness. Overall the food is good but challenge. It is a good meal to have when your group likes to have the long and good conversation. It will take time to finish. The two people for the seven courses are $35 and the 3 people are $45.

I love Sofra. It's probably my favourite Mediterranean + Middle Eastern food in Edmonton. The Adana kabab is amazing. The hummus is the greatest I've ever had. Their bread is all freshly made so their appetizers even better. Everything here is amazing from the appetizers to the salads to the kababs to the steak to the bakhlava. I'm not even a big fan of bakhlava but this restaurant has the best I've ever had. The turkish coffee is also to die for, be sure to try it. I just wish Sofra was less expensive and didn't require reservations so I could visit it more often. But the food is definitely worth it.

Usually a decent place to eat but this time around the food was disappointing. The doro wat was the worst thing I have ever seen. Little strips of meat, no egg, a total scam. The food didn't taste fresh. The kitfo and tej were both good. The music next door covered the entire atmosphere, you could barely hear the person next to you. Also, the service was disappointing. I would probably come back, but wouldn't sit inside and would probably order just either kitfo or gored gored to go.
I really enjoyed the fried mushrooms and the steak hoagie I got from Zeikos and the chicken salad but my favorite thing is the pina colad milk shake was delicious

This was my 1st time to CZ at DREXEL main campus. I had read up on them in advance. This was one of the best things I've eaten in a long time. The staff was super friendly and fun! I had the Cap n' crunch tilapia burrito with spicy sauce! A party in my mouth of flavors, textures, heat. The tilapia was a lush piece of fish that was cooked correctly! Especially since fish can overlook in no time. The crust was fun but wasn't crispy - that was the only criticism. The slaw was fresh and the sauce was balanced with heat. It was a lush, filling, flavorful experience. I chose the Taro bubble tea - which was a beautiful lavender color and touch sweet of deliciousness. This was a meal of tasty proportion! I can't wait to go back for more.

E X C E L L E N T !!! And above par cuisine from the northern part of India. Perfectly cooked to order and very very very consistent. I recommend the A la carte menu which is significantly better than the buffet although the buffet is 3 stars by itself. WORDS TO THE WISE:- as Confucius always wanted to say to Buddha " as now the bubba liketh it spicy(th) the bubba will do well to remember that what shalt burn going in so shalt it burn coming out "
Kudos - management has come through. Now the dining area is cleaned and the food is consistently good. Way to go!
Delicious! Rivals NYC Indian restaurants I frequented while living there. A definite must in downtown Indy. The Black dal was amazing and the chicken tikka masala was sumptuous.

First time eating Indian food and I must say the food selection was nice and it tasted good. The food was not over powered with flavored like I thought it would. The atmosphere was really nice and I got the feeling like I was in a palace with all the wonderful decorations. I would definitely go again!!!

We came here on a sunday night and it was crowded inside, but no wait. We ordered the vegetarian pad see yew and the chicken curry noodles with a thai iced tea and chrysanthemum tea. The food itself was pretty good, nothing too impressive. The service was mediocre, as we kept on having to flag down the waitresses to bring us more water, the bill, etc.
A neighborhood secret. I always get the pad Thai and spring rolls. I always think I'm going to try something new, but those items are just so good.

I can't speak to their food, because it hasn't arrived. I placed an order online more than an hour ago. When I didn't get a confirmation email after half an hour, I called to make sure the order went through, and was told that my food was ready and the driver was just leaving, and it would be 10-15 minutes. 20 minutes later, with no sign of the delivery person, I called again. I live less than 3 miles away. Again I was told that it would be 10-15 minutes. When I asked to cancel the order, I was told that it was too late because the driver already left.

Best Chaat hands down! This was my first time ever having it with my husband and it was the most flavorful meal I had in Philadelphia! It was perfectly spiced and extremely tasty. The owner, Hassan, is super nice and friendly and very accommodating! I def recommend you come here if you want a fantastic, spicy, tasty, flavorful meal. The owner even made us a mango lassi that went perfectly with our Chaat bowl. Thanks Hassan! We ll be back for sure!

Wife and I made reservations for dinner with friends and this place was great. I won't list endless details about what we ordered. You can see from other reviews that pretty much everything is good. I'm very pleased that my 'hood has yet another "wow" restaurant (i.e Wm. Mulherin's).

We found the place going the back way to my in laws. Small place in a strip mall, service solid food at reasonable prices. More of a place to 'get food', than to dine. The Pita Nachos were special. Spinach Pie was solid to. You can order online, so take advantage. My wife really like the fries!

It's my first time to try mid east food, but it is amazing. Hummus and Labaneh are very nice. Pita is also very delicious. I like lamb, because lamb is rare to see in grocery. I recommend this restaurant.

This place has pretty good Vietnamese food. The sweet fried shrimp was delicious. I also had the shrimp vermicelli bowl which was fresh and tasty. The ambiance here is casual nice little spot. They have a full bar and the staff is pretty friendly. I would definitely go back
Fast, delicious mediterranean food right on my way home from work! Their hummus is to die for and everyone is very friendly and professional.

Best Indian food!!! Nice atmosphere and great service!!!! Specially Owner was very customer friendly. If anyone loves Indian food then highly recommended this restaurant!!!! Welcome to the neighborhood and best wishes for them!!!

What a great place!! The only way I can describe it is as an Indian version of Chipotle --- you choose your meat and curry sauce and pile on the condiments to your liking --- only WAY more choices than Chipotle, and immensely more tasty. You can see the owners take great pride in their food and space. Everything we had was delicious and everything tasted fresh and hot despite being pre-prepared. We had naan and samosas as sides, all the chutneys were wonderful. And they have beer! The dining area was clean and beautifully decorated, with colorful art all around. I'm so happy we gave it a try despite Yelp's mixed reviews - and very happy to find an affordable Indian place close to home!

Ordered the #19 tom yum soup, very spicy. The new mango and sweet rice was splendid. Servers were nice and helpful. Bring a date here and if you're a single guy flirt with the waitresses. Good looking people! The inside store is homie, food was great; the reason why I didn't give the restaurant five stars is because I'm not a big fan of thai food. I had to go due to friend recommendation.

The best Indian restaurant in tow hands down (along with India sizzling I). The weekend buffet (lunch and dinner) is delicious with over 35 items for just around 10$. Yummy food. Can't get over the chicken 65, biryani, veg Manchuria, chicken tikka masala and deserts we had. 5/5 for quality of food. 4/5 for quality of service. Very amicable staff.
Great sandwiches and Pho, at reasonable prices.

based on you fine people, we made this our latest stop in the Saturday Indian Buffet Lunch Tour. I can't believe we've been here a year and this is the first time we're eating here. damn! all those wasted afternoons at House of India... Anyways, like everyone's already said there's about 600 dishes and they're all great. I like the following: A) there's a jug of Mango Lasi in the corner - don't miss it B) the serving dishes are smaller, so stuff doesn't sit and dry out C) when you go for the buffet, you can avoid the legendary horrible service. Who knew St. Louis would be the spot for quality Indian food?

I have a confession, this was the first time I have ever had pho! I know, I am very behind. But at least I can now say I have tried it. It was late on a Saturday and my husband, sister and I were HUNGRY. We decided to try out Pho 36 because my husband and I have been wanting to do so and my sister is always down to try new food. We got there about a half hour before they were to close and I felt a bit guilty but the owner did not care at all! Perfect start. We spent some time with the menu and asked a couple questions and prior reviews have described him perfectly, nice but witty and the conversation was fun. We started with a couple of bubble teas, I tried mango, my sister got green tea and they were both delicious, my only small complaint came from these though, there were definitely some large chunks of ice that were a bit annoying but honestly, the rest of it was so tasty, I didn't mind. We also tried the spring rolls and they were fresh and delicious. We all got pho, though I think we all got slightly different versions. I didn't really know what to do with everything but I just put some stuff in and dove right in. It was very good and perfect for a cold night. We all tried to finish as much as we could and the large size is definitely large! We wished we had saved some more space in our stomachs for dessert, but that will have to be next time. I will definitely be back soon to try more of the dishes on the menu and get some more bubble tea! I really want to try the avocado one!

I came here looking to try their Vietnamese sandwich. I like their options of 6" at 5 bucks or a 12" and a drink for only 2.50 more. Still, not worth the price.The sandwich sucked. The carrots and radishes were shredded and lacked the crunch and crisp. The bread was too doughy and buttered. The meat was cold. Never coming back for a sandwich.

My husband and I tried their special lamb dish and the chicken tikki which came with white basmati rice. Phenomenal! Homemade. We also tried the naan. So good and so hot! Friendly service as well. We had a salad at home with our meal but could not finish eating either dish. We both had the leftovers for our lunch the next day. I saw a few complain about the entree size but it seemed perfect to me and it was exceptional quality.

Ramen plans were foiled (don't you just hate when places are closed on Sunday) so we decided to check out Trang Tien instead. I've seen this place around for ages but never dropped by until recently, on a late Sunday afternoon. Edmonton was freezing, stomachs were hungry, people were sick so what better cure is there then some phooooooooooooo? Trang Tien is in the same strip mall area as the deceased Mirama (RIP dim sum buddy). I had no idea that Syphay (Thai resto) is located right beside them! I'll have to try them out soon. The place is much bigger than I anticipated with booth seats on both sides of the restaurant. Décor is bare, your typical Vietnamese minimalism, but I am a fan of the kid that served us. Seems like he's running the show up front. Respect. Anyways, we decided to order: - Fresh salad rolls with seafood ($8.50) - the peanut dipping sauce was tasty. I couldn't figure out what the difference was between seafood and the shrimp rolls, I guess ours had a piece of kabuki in it. But they were good. Typical appetizer fare. I guess we should have tried their tapioca dumplings. Next time! - Bun bo hue with pork ($11.25) - definitely a winner! Spicy, lemongrass broth combined with a deceivingly massive amounts of noodles and pork? How can one go wrong? If you're a BBH fan, then you shouldn't think twice about ordering this dish. - Special pho ($11.25) - apparently you can't go wrong with ordering the special (aka. you get a sample of all the meat types). Especially for those friends you know that cannot make any decisions to save their lives. Indecisiveness is a curse, indeed. Trang Tien is a great spot. Drive the extra two minutes outside of Chinatown to check them out. Trust me, you'll thank me in no time.
This is my favorite restaurant! It's casual, pleasant and the food and service are excellent!

Amazing service and food! Felt like I was in Italy again. Started out with the Figs and sausage in a balsamic glase and the calimari - both were delicious! For entree i got the Veal Saltimbocca which was outstanding. Thank you Scannicchio's for a great dining experience.

Totally a five star hidden gem. Me and my husband stopped by this place since we were around neighborhood and we were starving at that time. We wanted to have something light and fresh, so decided on greek/middle eastern food. Although I have tried so many greek food, this place still made me WOW. First of all, the owner is very friendly and willing to answer any questions you have on the menu. Secondly, their food is very fresh...we ordered one falafel platter and one platter combo. The portion is great and we felt so full after finishing the food. The hummus amazing!! The only thing i would suggest them to do is to make pita bread a bit soft. Will definitely go back to try other stuff on menu next time.

Ok so apparently there are like 5 Indian restaurants on Main Street now but this place has a great lunch buffet! It's been here for a while and I just never got around to writing a review. The food has flavor! And it's good and the Hakka noodles are great! The only thing I didn't like was the samosas I orders it just didn't do anything for me. It's not apart of the buffet menu but I ordered it and they were eh. Service was great people are super nice.

I was offerrd To Go as the only option when I arrived in a Saturday afternoon. Food is okay for a quick weekend lunch. Restaurant is fairly small, it offers both Chinese and Thai cuisines. The restaurant does offer lunch specials which is not a bad deal. I may return to try other items in the menu but it's not attractive enough as a must go place.
Large plates great Tabbouleh Fatuous. I liked the lamb Kabob. reasonable price large plate. Halal meat. Quiet and location is good..
Great lunch. Gai Jee/hot with rice. Service was good and the staff friendly. A bit pricier than other Thai restaraunts but everything was very good and fresh. Try it!

This is a place I bring my friends after every night out downtown--I can't count how many times I've come here. It is hands down the best Greek food and conveniently located less than a block from Bourbon. You can never go wrong with the gyro wrap or falafels. Most impressive of all is the staff that works there. They're incredibly nice and will bend over backwards to make sure you leave happy. It usually isn't a big deal because there's an ATM near the counter, but they only accept cash.

Very cozy and quiet little cafe on South St on a weekday. Something very charming about the sometimes mismatched chairs and Victorian sofas. It really felt like tea time at an antique store. Solid cup of chai tea latte.
It's a go to. I highly recommend getting take out. I love EVERYTHING on this menu. The owed is amazing and makes me SMILE every time I am in there. Also, its great inside and you can BYOB.

Always a yummy option. I tried their brunch this past weekend. And it did not disappoint. I had the Huevos Rancheros. My eggs were cooked perfectly. The tortilla was crispy as it should be. If I could change anything, I wish it was a bit more spicy. But that is just my personal preference.

Only one another review? Come on, Trentonians! This little cafe seems to be a popular enough place during the lunch hour, and it stays open until 7p, which is later than most places in New Jersey's economically depressed state capital. Thanks to its generous portions served with good spirits, The Hummingbird has become a twice-a-week routine for me. Sure, the place could use some polish--the dry-erase board menu is often too smudged to read very well, and I wish they didn't keep their bathrooms hidden. But the meals are never bad, and the sides are often fantastic. Their Festival could have been bland, but this doughy confection made a nice accompaniment to the flavorful jerk chicken. The curry goat could use a bit more intensity in my opinion, but when the meat is this tender I can manage with a problem that is otherwise easy to rectify. And the Jamaican patties are irresistible. Be warned: The Hummingbird does tend to run out of its items late in the day, since it's primarily a lunch place (like just about everything in Trenton), but even if you're settling for whatever they have left, your odds of a hit are just too favorable.
Of the 4-5 Thai places I've tried in Nashville, this is definitely the best traditional place. Not an issue for me, but others find it a downer that they rotate the currys on a daily basis.

If you are a Thai food fan, hurry to the Thai Orchid. Was there for the first time yesterday and can't wait to go back. Shared Thai dumplings and fortune bags--both crisp, not greasy, and filled with delicious ingredients. I had the drunken noodles with shrimp--large tender shrimp, noodles and sauce just right. My friend had the shrimp pad see yew--another tasty dish. The food is not only delicious, but the presentation is very attractive and the service is friendly and efficient . We both requested that our entrees be just a little spicy and we got exactly what we requested. This is a BYO so bring your favorite white and enjoy your meal.

The food is enjoyable enough, and the experience of eating with your hands can be fun. The service could be improved, however. And don't go looking for a variety of menu options or for any kind of customization in your order either. This is not a place for the particular.

I love to go here for lunch. I've not traveled to India (yet) so I can't speak to the authenticity of the food. But I do see diners who appear to be of Indian descent, which is a positive sign. The lunch buffet is huge, and nearly everyone can find something they enjoy. My favorites are the chicken tikka masala, mushroom saag, and saag paneer. I've actually tried to create a few of their dishes at home, with varying levels of success. The waiters can be a bit slow on refilling drinks, but otherwise are generally friendly.
Excellent lunch buffet. Fresh and delicious food. I stop by here every time I'm in the area.

Visited Spiro's multiple times since my initial review. If you do not sit at the bar, service is terrible and food comes out cold. Experienced inexcusable rudeness by an employee. Manager did not handle complaints effectively and it was so awkward that we will not be back.

I have been coming to this place since they have open. There food is amazing it reminds me off the food back home in Puerto Rico. Well cooked always fresh food portion are not the largest but are well to fill you up quickly. Very knowledge people family oriented I highly recommend this to anyone trying to get a taste of Hispanic culture.

I absolutely love this place. Their Beefball pho is amazing! Their Thai basil chicken is outstanding and I can't wait to try their oriental pearl pan fried noodles, next. We eat here at least once a week!! Super friendly staff!

I've had Pho...this is VERY good. The broth may be a TAD bit weak...but the FRESH Thai basil, sprouts, cilantro, and jalapeno slices (served with..not in..the Pho)...combined with a GENEROUS squirt of Sriracha and Hoisin (both at the table) makes the GIGANTIC bowl of Pho MORE than satisfying. I order LEAN brisket for mine (Mike will be more than happy to accommodate you), and the result was a hot, slurping FEAST. OH, and DO NOT PASS the shrimp rolls with the delectable peanut dipping sauce!!! I have been going there for over 2 years, and I look forward to going again (ESPECIALLY now that it's cols out). Go....just go. For the Pepperheads: Sriracha is my ketchup, so the infusion of HEAT n SWEET is UMAMI! They will also serve a special pepper relish if you are silly enough to try it. THIS PLACE IS PEPPERHEAD FRIENDLY! GO!

I love eating here. Coco Thai makes it very easy to order vegetarian versions of food and exclude fish sauce from their dishes, which I've found can be difficult at other Thai restaurants I've visited. It is a little pricey, but I think it is worth it. My favorites are the Coco Ave noodles & Thai Bubble Tea :)

Washington square mall is alive again!!! Absolutely delicious dishes all around and by and far the best chicken fried rice I have ever tasted (and I've had a lot of chicken fried rice). During our last trip in, the owner/cook even brought us some complimentary pho broth just for us to try. Can't wait to go back and get that for my main entry.

The foods here are taste so good... Nice price for this amount of food.. Except one thing is.. The bubble tea.. It suppose to be smoothies but is more like a splash ice drink with bubble inside.. Other than that.. Everything is good ^^

It was easy to find with its own parking. We sat on the back deck and they had music playing. Started with the beef empanadas, so good we had to order more! My aunt loved the crab ones but they're not my favorite. I had the mofongo with shrimp, good flavor with the garlic sauce. My kids split the arroz con pollo, it was a good portion for them and they ate a good bit. Drinks were good too. So surprised this place is not busier.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We loved the Taj Mahal when it was on Fairview and Five Mile, and we were sad when they closed that location. We hadn't realized that they had reopened at a new location downtown until we were looking for somewhere to eat dinner. The food was excellent and the service was friendly and relaxed. We are glad to see them back in business!
Simply wonderful! Very courteous service. Perfect balance of coconut and hot spice. Appropriately portioned for half the price.
Been back here a few times recently and have tried many things on the menu. Their food is top notch. No joke, anytime you take a bite you can't believe how delicious it is. Highly recommended!
Awesome. Everything was delicious. Went "medium" spice, not as spicy as I though. Will be back.

We went there tonight. Not a lot of selections of wine by the glass and a nice limited food menu with some interesting selections which I like as opposed to a large menu of a lot of things that the chef can't accurately cook. We had the three dip bread and I really liked the (heavy on the tahini) hummus. My friends liked the cheese dip and the pepper dip but I thought they were mediocre. It comes with thin bread as opposed to pita so you don't fill up on bread. I was confused as to whether the bread was supposed to be soft or crispy because it was a combination of both. The table really liked their meat dishes (meatballs and chicken). My tuna dish was pretty good but I thought it was a bit over cooked. Each plate comes with grilled veggies which were good and some Bulgar which I thought was tasteless and gave to my husband to finish. The service was friendly but they could have made more money off us by being more attentive. Overall, fairly good but I thought it was pricy for what you get.
This was our first experience here. We loved it!! The food was fresh and had great flavor. The staff was friendly and helpful! Great presentation of sushi! We will definitely be back!

There is no Indian restaurant like this one in St Louis. I mean literally. We ordered navratna korma and it came with half plate potatoes, barely cooked bell pepper and tomatoes. Not only we had bad experience with food, but we also had bad experience with employee. The employees use men's restroom and keep the door open. The ladies restroom too needs highly skilled employee to open it's door from outside using a rod!!! Overall, I think the cooks and other staff are highly unprofessional and unskilled.
Love the atmosphere. There's not many places, if any, in Philly that have authentic Dominican food. It was clean, the food was great, and the music was straight from DR. Really can't ask for more.

Walked all the way there from 38th and Walnut and it was worth it! Tried the Satay Taco and the Thai Taco which were both awesome and had wonderful distinct flavors! The guy that works the window is also very friendly! Will definitely make the trek back soon. In terms of Asian fusion tacos...this place is far superior to Tyson's Bees.

Located in UCSB's university center, this is an excellent place to pick up high quality food on the run. I'm in love with their falafel. Further, today I forgot my credit card and the very generous owner let me pay via IOU and said to come back later to pay. The gesture really made my day. In summary, good food and good people.

I've been to Umami twice so far and I can't wait until my next visit. I am so happy this place moved into Lennox Village! The food.... man, the food! The Bibimbap is amazing. The Pad Kee Mao is amazing. The sashimi I've seen go to tables next to me looks amazing. They also have a great bar selection. The décor is clean, cute, and modern. I especially love the giant screen playing the Asian music videos. Michelle, the owner, took care of me for lunch today and she was quite delightful. Very attentive and friendly. All in all, I think this restaurant is a great addition to my usual eateries in the neighborhood and I would definitely recommend to anyone looking for some fresh sushi or authentic Asian flavors!

Great sandwiches with REALLY great french bread and interesting non-standard veggies. I've heard tell that the bread comes from a Bosnian Deli down the street ... more investigation needed! The price is very reasonable as well. Another review said get the BBQ pork and order extra meat ... i agree. I would not call these sandwiches "Amurican Sized" so you go ahead and add more yummy BBQ pork for $1 and it's still a $6 sandwich. Why 3 stars and not 4? Not many options for sides and no water cups (have to buy a bottled water?!?!). A winning sandwich none the less.

Pretty solid family-owned desi restaurant. The location is a little sketchy and there isn't a lot of seating inside, but the service and food makes up for it. The chicken tikka masala and lamb tikka masala were delicious. The only negative thing about the food was that the naan isn't fresh. If you're craving desi food this place is a good option!

Service is so slow. I can forgive when its a busy night, but we were literally the only people there! I was told, as our server was handing out dishes to everyone else at the table, that they were out of what I had ordered. Which by the way, was over an hour ago. My food then came out 3 minutes later. That to me means microwaved food. Yum. The food is generally bland and over priced. We were asked if we wanted dessert. Once our server finally came back we tried to order, but were told the kitchen was closed.
Just went there. Had appetizers that were the bomb. Great staff and cocktails. Oh did I mention their food. Eclectically excellent.

This is like the Chipotle of Indian food! Pick a rice bowl, Naanwich, or naanpizza and customize with your choice of protein, curry, toppings and chutneys. I had the naanpizza, which was surprisingly delicious! The best part is that the food is super authentic, spicy and delicious, from the channa to the chai. I think this place puts the other Indian fusion place in town to shame. There are basically an infinite number of combinations so I feel like I would not get sick of coming here. The only critique would be that the sheer number of options can be overwhelming when you are tired and just want decisions made for you. It would be nice if they developed a few preset "favorites" as examples to choose from. Really excited about this spot, spicing up the options in this little plaza.
Came here for our anniversary. Prompt and personal service. Rack of Lamb and Salmin were mouth watering delicious. Highly recommend.
Good and fast. Ordered the medium hot chicken pad Thai and wasn't very spicy, get hot. Also got the steamed dumplings. They were good. Drink was free for Military. Overall was pretty good.
Love this place! Fantastic food, service, and atmosphere. Very healthy options and generous portions. Have never had anything other than a great experience here.
another awesome meal & service was excellent!¡!... we had pizza de tostones & pork-chops
The food here is the closest you will get to Caribbean food in indianapolis. The flavor of the food is great. We took the whole family there and had a wonderful time.

While the place is usually fairly empty when we go in (6-7 on a Saturday night), it's extremely yummy. We generally go with the two person combo plate. If you're ordering an appetizer, you may want to split a one person combo as it is a ton of food. The combo has a little bit of everything and comes with a side (we always go with the hummus). They have dancers later in the evening and used to have hookah but I'm not sure with the STL county smoke regulations if they still do.

The food is incredibly cheap here (I didn't see anything on the menu that was more than $7) and if you are looking for a restaurant that serves Indonesian food with a home-cooked flair, look no further than Sky Cafe. Jared J and I started with the fried wontons, which were perfectly crispy and plentiful ($3 for 6 pieces). I probably could have eaten at least another plate, which brings me to my next dish, the N1, or the Mie Komplit. It came with two wontons on top, which made me very happy. This was the combo dish (~$5) and came with chicken, barbecued pork, mushrooms, and homemade noodles, plus some greens, a pickled egg (brown--maybe soy?), and chicken broth with meat and fish balls. I didn't see much chicken--but there was plenty of pork. The noodles were tasty and the egg was definitely not my jam, but there was a ton of food in the portion and I went home full! Very tiny (one server could easily handle the restaurant, even if it's full) and very authentic--the TVs were playing an Indonesian new station.

Food was awesome. Owner/server were more than accommodating. They made special fresh dishes for our vegan and Jain diets. Never expected to be treated so kindly. Favorite dishes so far: Tofu Makhni, Tofu Saag, Chana Saag. Palak chaat. Definitely a Must Go Place if you are in Newtown, PA

Yum yum yum! My husband and I just relocated to this area and are staying at the hotel next door. One evening, i ran out to my car and I could smell the Indian food from the restaurant next door. We were in India for a year and suddenly I craved Indian food! We walked over the next evening. If your into authentic Indian food, this is the spot!! We had the samosas to start and they're just like the ones we had when we were there...ok, maybe not as spicy hot, but truly delicious. We also had the butter chicken and the chicken korma and the garlic cilantro naan. All were wonderful and I think we're going back again this week. They actually have goat on the menu! Lots of goat in India and it's delicious! Just like Mumbai!

I had dinner here and it was wonderful. It's a very nice, intimate place. Perfect for a date night! The service was great, quick but not rushed. I am a huge fan of Thai food. They offer the best dishes without having an overwhelming long menu, which is good. I will definitely go back very often.
The experienced milk cruises. The futile subroutine sweeps before the conceptual temple. The wombat flags the prior prefix. A chase dies above an unhealthy parameter.

Could be the best Pho in town. I love me some Lilly's and this place definitely gives it a run for its money. The broth is so well balanced I don't add a thing to it. If your really into Pho and think your a boss, do the Pho challenge!
I ate here really quick one night when out in Tucson on business. I was in and out pretty quick but the food was fine and the service was prompt.

I like this restaurant because it's convenient and has decent food and because I admire the hard work of the family who own and run it. The food is not gourmet or fancy - it's "solid" Greek food that is satisfying. I like the cold appetizer platter to start, a mix of classic Greek appetizers such as hummus, tsaziki, and other spreads. The ambience is casual. The physical space is a bit worn but they spruce it up with white tablecloths. The prices are reasonable. The family members who cook and serve are probably some of the hardest workers I've ever seen. The kids have pretty much run the restaurant for years as they grew into adults, and their work ethic is next to none. I think that's the real reason I like to go there. It's an honest hard - working immigrant family and their pride comes through in the food.

This was a great Italian restaurant! If you want a twist on Italian this is your place. The restaurant itself is beautiful the decor is very trendy. It feels like you're in downtown Philly. The lights were dimmed low (could be lower, but for the suburbs, I'll take what I can get). All the food that we ordered was delicious and had really great flavor. We started with a few apps - the calamari, beets, and corn chowder- all amazing! Then we split pizza (it was a special that evening) and the gnocchetti pasta and the carrots as a side. They were all delicious. And the bread they give you is hands down the best bread I've ever had at a restaurant. I know that's silly but I feel compelled to talk about the bread because it was SO. DAMN. GOOD. Drinks were on point too!! Will definitely be back! So happy to have a place like this in the suburbs.

Food took almost two hours to get here and ended up being soggy and every roll I had was falling apart. Also the miso soup tasted like lukewarm watered down chicken broth. Will never be ordering from there ever again.

Well I guess I learned my lesson for not reading yelp before stopping here. What pulled us in what the nice open lawn/outdoor seating area, and the fact that Pico di Gallo up the street is closed due to "maintenance issues". Let's just say previous reviews of "laid back" atmosphere don't quite describe a 90+ minute meal (wait) for two basic entrees. This place took feeling ignored to a while new level (in fact, we saw at least one couple get up and leave after waiting for a menu they never even got). Once the food finally arrived it was so so, mine was ok, his was so filled with gristle he couldn't finish. We didn't complain, just cut our losses and got out of there. It's sad because it's a great space.

First time at Siam Cafe was for dinner on a friend's recommendation. Food was delicious. I had the Tom Yum Koong and my dad had the Ginger Pork. Medium spicy on our entrees was plenty approachable. Good size portions. Prepare for their tiny parking lot. It's narrow and quite the adventure filled with cars. I did not see any nearby street parking available.

Enormous platter for 10$. You get so much food. The food is really good, packed with flavor. I ate there twice, I didn't order anything specific I just accepted what he gave me and I had no complaints either time. I had chicken, hummus, bread, a chickpea dish and an orange. The man loves to talk as he cooks, he's very friendly with a big personality. The line is long, there is so much smoke coming off the truck that as you wait in line your clothes will smell like this smoke all day. The line takes a good half hour at least, but worth the wait!
Decent Afghani food. Good Aushak and various pilafs. This is our usual place to eat before orchestra concerts at the Kimmel Center.

Being an avid Indian cusine enthusiast I couldn't wait to give Mahoor a try. I'm thrilled to say the food and service surpassed my wildest expectations. The samosas were freshly made and robust with flavor. My vegatable biryani lunch was large enough for leftovers to be taken home and enjoyed the following day. Mahoor is a hidden gem in Zephyrhills, & by far the best Indian cusine for miles around. Im sure I'll become a regular here.

We had the 2 signature sandwiches and they were amazing! Highly recommend this little hole in the wall! Great Vietnamese flavors that are easy to eat and totally munchable. The Vietnamese coffee is good as well. Great customer service and ultra friendly.

We have been loyal customers ever since they opened. Today we stopped in for lunch and noticed that the menu had changed. Ok..I'm good with change. When I tried to order for my son they said they no longer had cheese pies...or any kids menu items. He said 'we aren't kid friendly anymore'. Ok...how about a plain flatbread? No they are pre made. Really disappointing. I don't consider my son that picky but he is a kid and also has a few dietary restrictions. This was a great place for us all to enjoy. He loves the fruit, cheese pie, falafel (taziki recipe has changed as well and isn't as good) and rice (also seems to have changed and is more bland).
Perfect! Great food, great price, and great big portions. It's becoming difficult to find a meal worth the price in this city - even for casual dining, so I will definitely be back to Chickpeas.

I love the lunch buffet here, but also enjoy visiting for dinner. The food is always fresh with the right amount of spice. Nothing like bland Indian food -- right? Try the saag -- with or without meat is no matter. It is always bursting with flavor!
The food is great, good flavor and big portions. It is also priced right. Not enough servers and you have to keep asking for more napkins.
Out of the 8-or-so Indian restaurants in town we visit, this is always our favorite. Just great flavors and (for an Indian restaurant) good atmosphere.
