So good, I enjoy their foods, especially the curries! I am a vegetarian/vegan and I had no trouble finding food on the menu. I am never displeased when I order take out or order at the table! Great service, great food!

Unique. Fresh. Friendly. Possibly the best food truck in the city. Tucked away in a random street on Drexel campus is a food cart unlike any other in Philly. I feel it makes other food trucks jealous because the lines make it look like a fancy restaurant is opening. Some clanging inside, and the metal awning lifts at noon (or sometime around there). Out pours the Captain Crunch crusted tilapia burritos, short rib tacos, chicken curry, and other savory treats. While the menu only contains 8 or so items, each of them are prepared fresh. For the price, this is really hard to beat. Long line but absolutely worth the wait. Cheers.

I know I don't write a lot of reviews, I usually let the gf handle that. However, I have to review Mi Caribe. This is now one of my favorite restaurants. I have been here quite a few times and have no bad words. First off, the food is amazing, exquisite and delicious. I have now tried several items on the menu and every one of them has been a revelation. The chivo is so tender and reminds me of home. As great as the food is, the service is probably better. All the staff Ihave met are courteous and personable. They are knowledgeable about yhe food and can give you great help with choosing, if you need it. Also, the owner, Warren, is usually on hand and very nice and helpful. We had a birthday dinner for the gf there and he was amazing. Very helpful and accomodating. He even threw in some drink specials for the party. Overall, I am very happy with this addition to STL dining and I know I will be eating there innumerable more times.
Great variety, excellent flavours. Unique concept with a sit down cafe style menu and a specialty grocery store

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: As a Yelp Elite this is the first time I used a free E-Coupon from Yelp and yeah it worked I got a free Samosa even better than that the owner gave us two. The Food is great I had the Tandoori Baba Fish it was the best Fish from an Indian cuisine I have ever had, and very good the owners the woman chef and her husband who is host, waiter etc. The menu is going to run you over $25 a plate but when my lady babies eat everything off their plate I would have bought 4 more plates. The service is slow so you are going to get the true international experience go to India, Africa, Caribbean etc things don't move fast but all the food is cooked from scratch and worth the wait have a nice drink from exotic mango non alcoholic drinks to exotic beers if you enjoy such things. The decor is Awesome I would have not expected this jewel in Boise. I am Loving Boise this is on my list of cities to discover
The only reason I am giving this restaurant two stars is the view is beautiful, the food is overpriced ,the service is slow, the parking is atrocious

This place was recommended to me by a friend. We came in on a Saturday before the dinner rush. Service was excellent. We had the green tea and Thai tea. The green tea was very sweet for me. I didn't try the Thai tea so I'm unsure if it was sweet. We started with the calamari as an appetizer. For the entrees my friend and I ordered the scallop penang and pineapple duck penang both of which were on the specials board when you walk in. Scallop was perfect and not overcooked. The duck was crispy and tasty. I did not see a spice level on the menu. The entrees did not seem spicy at all, but they gave me 4 containers of hot sauce and peppers to make the entree more spicy. Will definitely be back to try other things.

Yum! I went here with a friend and we got Lamb Gyros. They were huge and full of flavor! The waiter was extremely nice and attentive, and the atmosphere was very laid back and relaxed. I heard there were belly dancers, but they weren't there when we went. I'd go back!
Oh man, Dooners! Love the food here. Great mix of authentic gyros to create your own - lamb, chicken, beef, with all the fixins. Pop in and mash - yummmm!

Very well prepared and delicious meal. I had the lamb chettinadu with garlic naan but also tried the dishes of the others in my group and each and every one was delicious. We'll be back to try the other dishes on the menu!

This 4 stars are for food. I tried their chicken kadai and it was one of the best chicken kadai i ever had. Naan is also very good. Haven't tried other items, which I am going to, hoping to nit get dissatisfied. But the place is small to sit so better take out.

The restaurant formerly known as Tommy's Tea Pot is now Mizu Asian Cuisine. The interior of the restaurant is still going through a remodeling phase, so eat in at your own risk. However, their take out is available and very delicious. Their crab rangoon is so creamy and sweet. Make sure you get a new menu before you order, as there have been some significant changes since their re-branding.

The food was very good, although a bit on the spicy side -- I didn't mind it but a word of warning to anyone who might have issues with that. The service was also good, but we were the only people in the place so I can't say how it would have been if it was busy. I did feel that the prices were a bit on the high side, especially the section captioned "Entrees." Unless two people are ordering from that section, rice is extra, at an additional charge of $2.99, which I also feel is too high for a side of rice (considering 32 oz of Basmati is less than $5). Anyway, that's why I'm rating it 4 starts instead of 5. Good food, but expensive for Vegetarian Indian Cuisine, IMO.

Wow, this place is insanely loud. I mean Bleeker Street on Saturday night loud. Conversations with the bartender and waitress required many repeated sentences for both parties. Difficult to have a conversation. The cocktails are very good, as is the food. The empanada's, while good, bear little resemblance to the south american or mexican real thing. They are puff pastries with meat (and no vegetable filling). The Tamil corn cakes seem to be popular and were pretty good. A bit heavy. The house salad was light, fresh, and balanced.
There is nothing better in the world than the chicken korma curry here. Pairs amazing with peshwari naan. Service is always attentive and portions are good.

I thought it was only proper to try Delicia without the Yelpers, without the tequila shots. A new friend and I both love foods of the Hispanic kind, so getting her to agree to this new place was easy! I will admit, on a busy evening, parking is a b#@&*. Good luck trying to find a spot in their area, or maneuvering in the alleyway to the back "lot". Once you find a spot, you'll want to make sure your entire party is present, otherwise you cannot be seated. Fair is fair in that case. I was still giddy from the Yelp Swizzle Stick Party so I made sure our waiter Oscar knew I'd been there, hopefully that info didn't scare him! The "welcome soup" was UH-mazing. The guac was UHHH-MAZING. Our dinners [Empanadas & Tamal Corn Cakes] were FABULOUS. Margarita made me feel like I was back in Key West on the beach. I definitely wanna return, and try the other restaurants in the Delicia family.

Really good dinner buffet on Fridays and Saturday. Love the Chicken Tika Masala, samosas and all of the veggie dishes. Attentive service and everyone is very friendly. Last night we tried the fried cheese balls in warm syrup for dessert... wow!!

I am a big fan of Thai and this restaurant definitely stayed true to the fresh flavors that make the cuisine so good. Fish and chicken were both tender and well prepared. The thing is the food had no oomph. Wonton soup looked great bit the base was too sweet. Same with the pan seared tilapia meal. I ate it all but couldn't savor it the way I've had Thai at other restaurants.

I had been here some months ago with a groupon and enjoyed it thoroughly so I went back last night for dinner. I got samosas, butter chicken and garlic naan. The chicken was "medium" spicy and was just a touch too hot for my sissy mouth, but the flavor was yummy. Overall I was pleased and would go back.

I'm disappointed because I love Thai food and this place is close to home, but the food is mediocre and there was only one person running the whole place. My friend and I had to find her just to get our order in and get a glass of water. The prices are fair, but the food just wasn't great. I'd rather drive across town to one of the other thai places I like for a better meal and better service.

Slightly overpriced for the Lou, but high quality Greek food that makes it worth the trip. Pretty frequently, Groupons are available which take $15 off a $30 bill -- keep your eyes out for one of these! It is frequently quite empty inside, depending on when you go, but this only makes the service more attentive and the food arrive more quickly. Highlights include: The spreads. All of 'em except the one that is basically mashed potatoes (skordalia). All are served with fresh pita and tomato, cucumber, red onion, and pepperoncini. I especially enjoy the htipiti (roasted red peppers, feta, garlic, olive oil, capers) but as I said, other than the skordalia, you can't go wrong. Roasted Red Pepper Soup ($4) - absolutely delicious soup, topped with feta cheese and a large pita chip crouton. I would eat this any time of year, regardless of the weather, because it is just that good. The Elleniki Salad (traditional Greek) and the Traditional Gyro Salad (lamb + standard Greek salad ingredients + balsamic vinaigrette, tzatziki, and feta) are my faves. It is worth noting that the lamb in the Gyro salad can be substituted out for Shrimp or Chicken for no extra cost, if lamb isn't your thing. The Steak Salad is also excellent. Saganaki (cheese flambe, lit on fire right in front of your eyes at your table). Cheese is always great but FLAMING cheese takes cheese to a whole new level. Roasted Salmon, served with sauteed garlic spinach. Yum. A great Greek food option with plenty of delicious menu options! Check it out.

Please don't go to this place if you want to taste real Indian food. I got biriyani from here and it tasteless. If you want to have real Indian taste find some other place but not this shit restaurent

What a great value! Lunch and dinner buffet by-the-pound take-out place with seating available for about 20. There is a rotating menu and I like the variety they offer for such a small buffet. I was able to sample 3 or 4 dishes, in little 5oz or so portions in my container. There was a little spicy tang to the food but overall it was mild and would appeal to many. Only spent about $8 and got served a quick fresh 17oz lunch ($6) with a side of small mango juice ($2). This location is brand new as of July 2010 and they hope to expand to other locations soon. Their to-go containers are self-sealing, and recyclable plastic, and that is thoroughly useful.

Great food. Great service. Fire Ice Cream is BOMB! The Golden Bags are awesome as well. Deep Fried Bags get all crispy to perfection. But watch out how hot you ask for things. Had the Wild Boar and asked for "pretty hot" and it was very very hot. Not unmanageable, but definitely hotter than expected. Still tasted great, just wicked hot! Seafood extravaganza is delicious. We made reservations but absolutely didn't need to. They were very attentive to us.
Awesome, clean and straight up, bring cash and enjoy!

The food was flavorful and scrumptious down to the Naan. I had the Sunday buffet and everything up there was delicious (and we did try EVERYTHING). A perfect place for any occasion. My 18 month old ate everything with no hesitation and my husband who is an extremely picky eater had an extraordinary meal. The people were Definitely will be coming back with more family!

Great place we got breakfast today and was awsome!!! Cannoli cream french toast Zacs special omelet The cannoli french toast was out of this world the omelet was fantastic and the home fries are the best i had in a long time. can't wait to get back congrats guys the food and the service was exceptional.
Super friendly staff and great service! I love the spring rolls. The pho is good and the portion size is satisfying! My vietnamese go-to!

Nice place for lunch. I had the chicken shawarma pita and falafels - very tasty and not too heavy. My wife had the chicken shawarma hummus bowl with NafNaf fries and she also liked it. Would definitely come back again.

Food is okay type, sometimes all food taste same no matter what you order... Recently I had very bad experience with them, I enquired about their banquet hall for a get together, the man on phone replied very rudely and was showing attitude, they don't know the meaning of customer service...I will never recommend anybody to go there... Such disappointing experience.

Consistent food, friendly staff, and okay atmosphere, Nooddi Thai Chef is the better of the two Thai restaurants on State Street and in the general vicinity. Their Panang, Red, and Green curries are rich and flavorful, as is their Tom Yum soup. Mango sticky rice is available (though best in season). Their foods lack a depth of complexity that I've experienced in other Thai restaurants, and the atmosphere leaves a few things to be desired: it's usually cold in the winter and the chairs aren't terribly comfortable. Still, there's a lot to be said for consistent curry and a happy staff!
So good! Had the grilled chicken with a side of chickpeas & rice and beans. Wish you guys were closer to Tampa!!

This place is close to where I work. It's on the second floor of Grace's Plaza in Green Hills. They have lunch specials, which is awesome! I have not been for dinner. Everything we have ordered from there has been amazing! The jerk chicken does not disappoint! My mom had the fish tacos which were also amazing. The service has been great as well. It seems to be a bit hidden away but if you're ever out in Green Hills give this place a try!

We came here for lunch and over all it was fairly good. Mediterranean inspired dishes for the most part. The hummus and baba ganusoh where very good, as wad the tajine. However I was disappointed by the braised beef sandwich I got. The beef itself was very good, but they put way too much mustard on it. The mustard was good but it overpowered all other flavors on the sandwich. Even after scrapping much of it off, the mustard was the main flavor. It was so much that my nose started running and about an hour later my stomach actually hurts. If it weren't for the mustard situation I probably would have given 4 or 5 stars, but that almost ruined the entire meal for me.

We've lived in the area for about 10 years, and are big into the various worldly cuisines that this side of Nashville has to offer. Bangkokville used to be a Thai restaurant under a different name, with different ownership, and back then, the food was hit or miss. I am SO glad that the restaurant changed hands in terms of ownership - because it's amazing now. It's our go-to Thai spot now (along with Ginger Thai, on Thompson Lane - but Bangkokville is closer to home!). I always get their Massaman Curry, and my husband is a fan of their spicy pad kee mao. Great flavors, fabulous service on the rare occasions we have dined in, and friendly owners. This place is a gem!

Decided to check this restaurant out for lunch last week. The space is fairly small but nice and clean. The menu is smaller than what you normally see at a Vietnamese restaurant, but I don't mind that if it means the dishes are better. I asked what was good and decided on the grilled pork chop and egg and egg rolls. I also asked if I could get a small cup of broth to get an idea of how their pho might be. When the food came out I was instructed to put the fried egg on top of the rice and to pour sauce over that and the pork chop. The egg breaks and mixes with the sauce to add flavor to the dish. I was very impressed by the food. It came out quickly and had a lot of flavor. The egg rolls were packed with taste. The broth was yummy. Could taste the pepper and cinnamon infused in it. The pork chop had a nice char to it. Check it out.

I was excited about their grand opening. The cashier was really nice and the place looked great. But they didn't give us our ice for our desserts, and we were missing a drink. It was a bad first impression for me.
This pho is pretty good. They give you more meat than Miss Saigon and the broth is tasty.
Prices are fantastic for the food you get! Falafel sandwich was phenomenal. Everything was delicious!. We intend to be repeat customers! Thanks!

The portion sizes are large and cheap! Called in to order the Pad Thai, Crab Wontons, and Spicy Drunken Noodle for a nice night in - and everything was ready to be picked up within 15 minutes. We were very satisfied and still had leftovers the next day!

I really have to give credit to the workers here! I have made a few new friends that felt like I've known for years. I felt really welcomed when I first walked in...it was a rather slow day, but that made the whole experience that much more enjoyable. I sat with the staff and really got a feel for the environment this restaurant has to offer. Nicole and Shaina were very welcoming and I loved their excellent customer service and the aura that was ever so welcoming from the start of my meal to the finish. When it comes the meal as a whole; as I fore mentioned, the atmosphere was welcoming, I had next to no wait time on my food! The presentation was beyond superb, the love for the culinary arts is depicted quite clearly when I had my entrée. I had gotten hit with that, "where have you been all my life?" moment when I had the first bite. I had gotten lost in casual conversation as the day went on. I ended up being late getting back to my office due to an outstanding staff and meal. If you want a great time, decent prices, and ultimately amazing food...Come give this location a visit. I guarantee that you will fall in love and keep coming back as a valued repeat customer.(Also, they love giving free stuff, just for taking pictures of your receipt! So added bonus)

Haven't really had the chance to try out an entree but when I was here the staff is welcoming and fun. I ordered the wings and to my surprise they were SOOO GOOD! I chased each bite with a sip of the mangonado! I will be back to try other meals.

If I could give no zeroes I would. Hummus was chunky and flavorless. Fries tasted like the oil had gone bad. They do not have greek dressing for a Greek salad??? I threw away all the food. I called to let them know I was concerned for the taste of the fries and hummus. They were polite with the criticism I hope they take it to heart and improve some things because it is a good location.
Great food but it takes too long to get it. Call ahead and if they pick up the phone you will save yourself a lot of time.
Great food, generous portions, very friendly staff and extremely decent prices. I had beef kabob platter, can`t go wrong with that one!
I went here with my family a couple of weeks ago. We go the buffet and it was really good. Not excellent, but really good. I plan on going back there again.

Delicious Lebanese food. Perfect addition to the neighborhood. They have tons of space, a full bar, and super friendly staff. The food is out of this world. The hummus, especially the mushroom hummus, is so good. THe flatbreads are great too as is the lamb and the falafel. If you like Lebanese food this is a cant miss spot.

For a zabiha option, better than the steak and cheeses at Saads with fries that are just as delicious. Small but comfortable, not too long a wait, nice staff, delicious food. BBQ chicken calzone was the incredible, next time I'm getting the cheeseburger. Each portion is enough to tide you over for two days. Definitely going back.

By far the best Greek food I've had. The staff is helpful and friendly. The owner is heavenly and his passion is evident in his quality menu. Every time someone wants amazingly fresh food, I point them right to Smileys. Whenever I'm on Main Street, I always have to stop by and get some of their amazing hummus. A true favorite!

I really enjoyed the food here. I tried the bahn Mi burger and the pork belly taco. Pork belly taco - served with some veggie in a sweet white bun (like the ones you eat with Peking duck). I highly recommend this. Bahn mi burger was good. Definitely worth a try. I want to come back and try the lemon grass vermicelli and the kimchi burger.

I'll start by saying we went on a Friday night around 7:15pm, arguably the busiest time of the night. Luckily it was just 2 of us so we got a seat right away, the place was completely full at that point. First person to greet us is the chef, which is a nice surprise, but as time goes on we realize it's just because his waitress staff is very busy. Menu looks great, we order Salt and Pepper Shrimp Rolls, the King and I and Jatujak Stir Fried Shrimp. Salt and Pepper Spring Rolls came out fast. They were honestly just ok, they had mushroom in them, which wasn't listed as an ingredient, but the taste was very sub-par. Didn't really fit the flavor profile of salt and pepper shrimp with cilantro. The citrus lime dipping sauce was just thinned out duck sauce. By the time we finished that we had both drank our glass of water and for the next 45 minutes we were ignored, no refill of water, no food, not even a look. Again I know they were busy, but when they would sit a table near us, they would bring them water and not even glance at our table. Ok, 45 minutes after the appetizer, dinner comes. I'm eating the King and I which is basically Pad Prik King, string beans are undercooked which is actually how I like them in my Pad Prik King, very crunchy. But they taste dirty and the sauce doesn't seem like it was cooked with the food, just poured over at the very end. I like the flavors somewhat marinated with the protein and vegetables. Girlfriend is eating the Jatujak, which said it was spicy, but wow it really is hot. Hotter then the 10 at Han Dynasty in Old City. I have a pretty high tolerance for spice so we switch plates. I get to a shrimp in the Jatujak that is right on the line of undercooked. I figured with the temperature hotness of the food it is probably fine, dumb mistake. The next day I was writhing in stomach pain. Like I said before, they were busy, the chef even had to come out to help a little (which is an admirable trait for someone in the kitchen), but ignoring a table for 45 minutes when all they wanted was some more water (yes we did ask) and then serving undercooked seafood due to the pressure of getting the food out is inexcusable. On paper the food looked amazing, but on my plate and in my stomach it disappointed. There is plenty of other delicious Thai Food in that area the I will stick with.

Not much to add beyond what has already been shared - great atmosphere, great service, and great food and drinks. We arrived at 6pm on a Friday and we're able to get a table right away (just beat the rush!) For drinks, we ordered Margaritas and Manhattans. The appetizer, Mofongo, was a great starter (awesome plantain cups with pork, pineapple relish, and onions.) We ended up sharing three incredible entrees - the duck enchiladas, the pork tenderloin (a special), and the braised short rib. The portions were generous, and we were all stuffed by the end. There were many other options that I'd love to explore in the future!

Gave this place a try for dinner, sad to say I didn't love it. It was okay/ decent but the menu descriptions did not live up to the taste I was expecting. The crab cake almost had a pumpkin, cinnamon taste, 2 out of three of us did not like it. The goat cheese croquette was a huge let down as well. The braised short rib was very good I will say. The service was very good and the two deserts we shared, the apple crisp and the peanut butter mouse were incredible.

You broke my heart, Dmitri's. I was a loyal and frequent lover who made no demands. In return, you always gave me a satisfying experience: consistently delicious, fresh and simply-prepared dishes. Perhaps you fell victim to your own success and spread yourself too thin. Maybe you got a new sugar daddy. Or it could be that you just got bored looking at the same four walls day after day, year after year. I understand. But clearly your love for me has faded. Your octopus, once plump and perfectly grilled, with the texture of lean, tender beef, now is limp, chewy and cold. Your fish, when available, is prepared with none of the care or love of years past. And your once-famous generosity, too, is nowhere to be found, your classic plain white plates dwarfing your once-ample portions. Saddest of all is your coterie. Oh, how your ladies-in-keeping-us-waiting have changed. Once energetic and full of the charm of knowing they were slinging the best hash around, the new breed seem sullen and annoyed, more interested in the intrigue of their court than the satiety of their courtiers. Alas, nothing lasts forever, nothing gold can stay. 'Tis better to have loved and lost, than never to have loved at all.

Very nice place on Treasure Island. The atmosphere and lighting is cozy and intimate. The night we stopped in a very talented guitarist was deep into his music. We sat at a hightop table in the bar area and had drinks and appetizers. Two of us had the lobster bisque and two had a salad. Both were excellent. We also split a middle-eastern sampler which was very good. A little weak on the tap beer selection but the cocktail drinks were generous and tasty. We would definitely return if we are in the area again to try some of the entrees which looked amazing.

I eat here weekly. I cannot say enough good things about orchids Thai. My fave dishes are the Lad Na, fried rice and peanut sauce chicken. The pan fried dumplings are exquisite. My hubby like the beef and mushroom with steamed brown rice. I wish I could live here. It is a beautiful restaurant with excellent service. The take out is great as well. Lunch specials are priced great.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This place has Amazing Indian food! We went for the Saturday morning buffet and fell in love with the salad with yogurt dressing and the chicken dish. The naan and tea choices were superb too. The owner and his son talked with us for a while: both very nice and welcoming. I recommended this place to all of my friends.
Their yellow rice isn't to die for. I've had their steak with white rice and that was much better.
This was my first time to this place. Good Indian street food, nice service. Must try their vada pav. I am gonna try pav bhaji next time , i have heard its really good as well.

Great Thai Food, friendly staff and a great place for take out especially if its later in the evening. They never close early which is nice. They stay true their hours and consistent with their dishes.

Decent food, probably the best Indian Cuisine that delivers in the area, though a bit overpriced; either the portions or quality of food needs to be increased to make up for the higher price to make this a 4/5 star place for me. As it sits now, it's just alright, I'd recommend it if you want indian delivery, otherwise there are many better options in the area with a much better taste/dollar ratio. The portions really are quite small. Ultimately for $15 I'd expect more than a few small pieces of chicken and a side of rice. It's not like we're talking steak or shrimp here. Food: We felt the chicken tikki masala and tandori chicken were alright, not the best, but good. Though the rice was pretty dry, and the garlic naan wasn't great, almost seemed like they used a lot of egg in making the dough, just seemed odd. Service: We just did delivery, so keep that in mind, but it was very quick, and the driver was very friendly.

Food was okay at best. Unappetizing display but it tasted fine. Service was absolutely terrible. They rushed us out of the restaurant even though there were only two other families. Started clearing our table while we were still sitting. They forgot to give us bread and acted rudely when kindly asked. I highly discourage people from going here. It's ridiculous. They give Indian buffets a bad name.

My maiden voyage to this new Thai restaurant located in Broad Ripple was not a disappointment. This restaurant offers delicious Thai food with a pleasantly surprising atmosphere that took the space of the old Midtown Grill. I will add this to our list of favorite restaurants.

Pretty solid thai food with reasonable prices and good portions. I had the duck curry which is touted as one of the specialties of this place as pointed out by the other reviewers. Sweet, sour, and spicy flavors envelop your tongue with every bite, although their curry is a bit sweeter than curries I've had at other places. This place is small, so make reservations or come during non peak times. Also, get the thai tea!

It's a bit of a dive and a little tacky but I thought I'd give it a chance. After I ordered and paid for my food and I was waiting what seem to be a long time I was thinking I was going to be very disappointed with what was to come. I took my food to go and when I got home I was pleasantly surprised. The chicken kebabs potato salad and Greek salad were all very good. The taziki sauce and pita bread also excellent. The only thing I didn't like was the salad dressing that they included however it was on the side so I did not have to use it. I will definitely try them again and recommend them!

Jamaican Jerk Hut definitely deserves more than 2.5 stars. Sure, the service was slow (and apparently always slow), but the friendly staff kept us updated as we waited for our table & food despite how crazy busy they were. I had the jerk chicken thigh platter, my friends had the oxtail stew and curry goat, and we all shared 2 orders of the chicken patties. Everything was delicious. I especially love the spicy sauce that comes with the jerk chicken. It's slightly sweet and extremely hot, so make sure you get it on the side if you're not sure whether you can handle it. Bring good company, a couple six packs, and hang out in the courtyard while you wait for an available table. Don't go too hungry or if you have somewhere to be after your meal. Do go if you have patience & love good food!

Had a great dining experience here yesterday. The place is newly renovated and equipped with both a bar and a karaoke room. Decided to go with the basics and got pork soup dumplings, dan dan noodles, and chicken fried rice. Everything was delicious and it came out really quick too. The dan dan noodles were even better than han dynastys in my opinion and the soup dumplings were oh so juicy. Will def coming here again.

I must have high expectations compared to most. When I see 4 stars I would think the food would be above average but not a wow that was really good. I ordered the falafel pockets. It was ok. The falafel was good. The sauce was better than most but still watered down. I would rate Fatoush higher in this area. The restroom could be cleaner. I may go back for a quick eat but it's not 4 stars.

I haven't posted a Yelp review in a long time, but this one is warranted. This was the worst restaurant experience I have had in a very long time. The service was terrible, and the food wasn't far behind. Some co-workers and I went for lunch, and when we walked in, no one was at the host stand to greet and seat customers. We waited a while, and eventually someone spotted us and ran over to find us a table. When we sat down, it took at least 15 minutes for anyone to acknowledge we were there. We tried to flag servers down, to no avail. After we ordered, it took forever for any food to come out. We ordered very simple lunch special items, which includes soup, salad, and spring roll. People who had ordered long after us were getting their soup, salad, and spring roll first. No consistency at all. At this point, it had been 45 minutes, and no food yet. Finally, we got someone's attention, and the first part of our meals came out. The soup and salad were HORRIBLE...the soup tasted like sour vinegar, and the salad was literally just a bowl full of bean sprouts with vinegar. Completely inedible. The spring roll was the only thing that tasted halfway decent. Finally, the entrees came out (not at the same time, but randomly, which is always awkward when you're with a group of people), and we were very underwhelmed by the taste and quality. Edible...but only if you're in the mood for some strip mall dive Chinese takeout place that loads all their food with sodium to mask the blandness of it. And the clincher: all the sauces at our table expired over a year ago! Yes, expired. I thought that, perhaps, it was a fluke and only the sauces at our table. However, I walked over to an empty table on my way out the door, and the sauces at that table had expired too. Totally gross. The Health Department should take a look at this place. And this is a franchise, so someone needs to take a hard look at how this particular franchise is being run. The servers are totally clueless. I've never been to one of these places in another city, but I have to believe that this one is probably a rogue outlier. Either way, we will definitely NEVER be going back to this place. If you want Asian food for lunch, go to Golden Coast, Goten, or P.F. Chang's instead.

I called to see if they had a website or could fax me the menu and the answer was no to all of the above. I drove down there to check it out. Almost everything on the menu looked good so I ordered the Roast Beef with Blue Cheese on cibbatta bread, breaded zuchinni, hush puppies and an Avacado smoothie. The portion of meat was small on the sandwich and I expected melted blue cheese crumbles, instead I got a packet of blue cheese dressing squirted on it. They were out of hush puppies, the zuchinni was bought at a store and tasted freezer burnt. The smoothie and service was really good though. I also ordered a meatball sub to go for a co-worker and was informed that they were out of provalone so she had to have an italian meatball sub with swiss. Not to mention that the meatballs were cold and came out of a bucket. I am sorry but I would not venture back unless it was for one of the Avacado smoothies or freshly made tea that they let me sample. Once again, very nice people but the food was sub-par at best.

-Decent Pho flavor broth, but the place does provide good portion of vegetables. -The rice vermicelli noodles have good shrimp and vegetable portions but lacking flavor in the sauce. -The rice dishes are ordinary and nothing to brag about. The one things I do like about this place is the weekend special it has. That is the crepe. If you never heard of crepe, it's like pancake/omlette-Vietnamese version filled with chicken, bean sprouts. It's a lettuce wrap form where you take some of the crepe and wrap it in a mustard or lettuce and dip it in a special fish based sauce filled with shredded carrots. The main reason I go here.

A friend and I were shopping at Southgate last weekend and headed to the food court for a break. We checked out the options and had almost decided on Opa when we saw... New Asian Village in a food court? Yes please! We split the 2 curries plate with rice, potatoes and salad, and some naan, about $11. Saffron rice, roasted potatoes, butter chicken, lamb curry, fresh naan, and caesar salad. Umm... 5/6. Not sure why they decided it would be a great idea to include a scoop of caesar salad on top of a plate of tasty curry. Next time I'll pass on that. They have a reasonable selection of curries and some wraps and rice bowls too. Their food was comparable to the quality at the restaurant buffets, although I was sad that I wasn't the one controlling my lamb curry portions. Still though, for the price, and the fact that you're in a mall food court, I was pretty impressed.

We've been waiting for this place to open and they did not disappoint. Great food and healthy portions. We got the kids meal with the chicken for my son...like little Indian chicken nuggets. Phenomenal! Yes, I ate most of those. The best thing is you can tell these guys are working hard. It was nice to talk with one of the owners and get to know him a bit. We'll definitely be back. Whoever you have in the kitchen is NICE. I can't wait for the leftovers...always better the next day!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: First time last night. Good neighborhood Asian restaurant. Had the avocado salad, some sushi rolls, edamame dumplings, hot and sour soup and Shrimp Pad Thai. Everything was good. Pad Thai could have used a little something to spice it up or add some flavor. Great service and very reasonable prices. BYOB

This is our fav pho place in the south of the city! The service is not the best because every time we come they always forget something. The soup is definitely worth it. It's always busy no matter what time or day. The set up is super tight, you can almost hear that next table to you. We don't mind the tightest as we always come back. Free tea is a plus !!
The owner and waitress are pretty nice. We had some great Korean fried chicken there. I'm a big fan of Hattie B's and I'd say the fried chicken there slays.

Like I said in my previous review. The food is great here, it was the staff that was issue. Well, I decided to give this place another try and to my surprise, staff was super friendly and helpful!! I met the owner and you can tell he is trying his best to make this place work. Great Job Andrew. I'll be coming back here anytime in the area.

Food: Very good, above average Thai cuisine. Price: I hate to say it but the prices have risen from how they are currently shown on the online menues, to the point of entrees being about $3-5 more in the restaurant. Service: Impeccable! Couldn't be nicer We started going here when they opened and thought we had found our new go-to Thai spot. As time went on we started realized our bills were getting bigger but our orders were staying the same. I hope this will be corrected soon because the menu on their website & menupages list entres for about $3-5 cheaper then they cost when our bill came in the restaurant. Food is great, service is great, just make sure you pay attention to your bill or double check the final order price if your placing an order for pick up.

This is the best restaurant on campus. There's also a few locations in San Diego, which made me sad because I thought we were special to have this place. It's located in the UCen, and it shares floor space with Romaine's. There's plenty of tables and booths inside, but it does get crowded during meal times. There's also tables in the UCen, as well as a patio area. The prices are pretty high, but the portions are great. I got the Santorini platter, which has meat, sausage, two wings, pita bread, and two sides. Everything tastes great and is well-cooked. The meat is juicy and tender. I'm not a big fan of the wings, I find it a little dry. They also have fries, which are pretty tasty. My favorite Greek food item is pita bread. They don't make it as nice as the bread at Daphne's, but it comes close. Service is top-notch. The workers are very quick and pleasant. Even when the line gets long, the service I receive does not change. Great food, great establishment.

I did not eat at the Jamaican Jerk Hut so this post has nothing to do with the food, although it looked decent. I came here for a small going away party for my friend. The place is a BYOB so my friend purchased a keg and paid a $50 corkage fee to allow us to drink at his expense. I think they have a reasonably small corkage fee for wine/6packs/etc. and while $50 seemed semi steep I guess its not too bad to bring a whole keg to a restaurant. Clearly this is a summer time place with 90% of the seating being outside and a large grass area for hanging out, people were passing a soccer ball back and forth while we were there. The outdoor space is simply amazing and unmatched by anywhere in the city. It's so amazing in fact that I don't understand how this place even exists since the piece of property has got to be worth millions. While we hung out on a perfect night a reasonably decent reggae band played which only added to the awesome outdoor space and the summer vibe. Several of my friends got food and it looked surprisingly good. I will definitely return on a nice night for some byo beers and some grub. One weird thing I thought was for a short while I thought this place was owned by Guy Fieri. The restaurant I think was once visited by the restaurant reviewer on one of his TV shows. They obviously took great pride in this and put Guy's face on the back of their servers t-shirts. I just thought it was weird that the place was so proud that some dude happened to come to their restaurant. Overall a good place, with a great outdoor space, and a fun vibe. I'll be back.

Authentic Puerto Rican and Latin cuisine in Nashville, whoo hoo!! The mofongo was AMAZING...I have not had any this good since I was last in PR...wow. Blown away by the flavor and moisture, spiced to taste just right! We also had delicious tostones and loved every bite of crispy goodness. We went on a quieter night, sadly for us, but they are known to have fabulous live bands play music you can dance to, and then it turns into a DJ-driven dance party as dinner service winds down. Lots of fun, casual atmosphere, just right for a great meal and a good time!

I prefer Cafe Cuong over Nhu Y. Maybe because I was working on my third hoagie within an hour... Hmm... it sucks having a high metabolism. I'll be back to try their infamous Vegetarian special. Hopefully, I won't interrupt the owner's beauty sleep the next time I come. He was snoring pretty loud. I thought it was cute when he frantically stood up as soon as he woke up to see me smiling at him. :)

Best falafel sandwich in Philly possibly the best in the US too (I'm Lebanese and yes I've been craving a real falafel sandwich! You'd think it's simple enough but no..no sandwich was a falafel before I ate Bitar's) HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
Small plates for sure. Very good but small portions. Cocktails are great. Everything is pricey. Food though is excellent. You can taste a difference at a high price.

We eat here all the time and the food has never disappointed us. It is our favorite Vietnamese restaurant by far. The service is excellent - they totally know what they are doing and they all have worked here for years. Unbelievably fast service too. I seriously have to question the few reviewers who commented on the slow service as to whether or not they are reviewing the right place. Their rice vermicelli with chicken is to die for!
Dude! Amazing little old lady running kitchen knows her shit got several dishes there beef noodle level 4 spicy broth cooks all day long authentic my go too but can't go wrong with anything there
Second time here. Meals are very lightly made and very fresh. They put cute decorations on each plates. Young waiter had some problem communicating but was very polite.

We sat outdoors and the waitress was kind in turning the music down for us. They had just opened and it was a bit too loud. For an $8 lunch, this was a true bargain for a lunch entrée which included soup, salad and a spring roll. While me entrée was "Thai hot" spicy as requested, the other entrée was not spicy at all. We will be back as the service was excellent and the food was very good.

The moussaka I had would've tasted so much better if it wasn't reheated from the night before. Besides the constant dinging of the microwave in the background, my rice turned rubbery in less than 5 minutes. On the bright side, the Greek salad was fresh.

HOT pappadams... i got the mango lamb & it was yum! love their garlic naan bread, too... others in my party got lamb with spinach (& loved it!); beef vindaloo (& loved it!); & curried chicken (good!) the pappadams were too peppery for my taste - but everything else was yum, including the ubiquitous basmati rice... ...& also including the mango lassi & pistachio kulfi... tucked into a corner of a strip mall on the south side of w. manchester rd....there's a median so turn left at the light where if you go right, you end up at the new, ugly wal-mart...

Wow, we just had such an unexpectedly 5 star meal here. This is a relatively new Indian/Pakistani restaurant located inside a perpetually vacant shop (sometimes restuarant, sometimes bodega) across the street from Marrone's in Ardmore. The kabobs are competitive with Kabobeesh in West Philadelphia (something I never thought I'd say about any restaurant anywhere) and the Chicken Makhani is the best I've had outside of India. Definitely try the grilled Resham Chicken (I think on the menu they are Seekh Kabobs). The bread is a bit drier than ideal I think, but the seasoning and flavor of the food is spot on. The mint sauce is spectacular. Service was terrific and they comp'd a small mango lassi for my 3 year old. Nice guys and great food.

The Blue Plate is excellent for breakfast. Portions are huge and for a great price. Staff is courteous and tend to your needs quickly. I highly recommend the omelet special and scrapple. Thanks to chef Jim and his staff.

Service was good, food was good as well. Eating with your hands is a bit weird (even though a tradition). Probably not a good place for a first date haha. Has hookah which is a plus. Overall a pretty cool place to hang out. I would go back.

Well yum! I've got three small kids, so rarely do I eat at restaurants anymore. Instead, my husband and I have become takeout experts. Went to a lovely east side park, then called from there to get takeout on the way home. Sure, it was cold- ish by the time we got hone, but that's our fault. Grill sampler:yum! Everything was good, but the best were the lamby things on skewers. Lovely with a sprinkle of mint. Two kinds of chicken kind of tasted the same, but both good. Vegetarian sampler, even more yum! Falafel, delish, round balls with sesame. Dolmas tasted good, but my guess is they are canned. A very time consuming food that is usually not hand made anymore. Great hummus, tahini, etc. I wish a littleb aba ganous had been included, but no such luck. We got a side of fries, by tbe tine they got home there was little crispness left to offset the tart lemon and seasonings, so they were just OK. But this is a good place! Eat here!

Came in to order take out. I got the famous Pad Thai to go. It was $11.75 after tax. Pros: -Staff was very friendly and did not make me feel rushed or uncomfortable that you may experience at other Asian restaurants. -Food was prepared very fast -Inside was very clean and well taken care of -The Pad Thai was much better than the average places in the area -The quantity was very large and more than I had gotten anywhere else Cons: -This is just an opinion, but I feel it lacked a little flavor. However, I did enjoy the spice. I ordered medium and it was amazing. I just feel it lacked a particular flavor that other places use. Overall, if I am passing by in the future I will definitely come back. The spice and quantity is definitely worth $11. I will try some of there other dishes next time.

I ordered delivery from Haveli last week and OMG was it delicious! I ordered chicken tikka masala and chicken korma. I origionally ordered the chicken korma to get to the minimum $20 order but it ended up being my favorite! The smooth rich gravy with just a hint of coconut and cinnamon really hit the spot. The food came piping hot and atleast 20 minutes before the 45-60 minute quoted delivery time. The chicken was moist white meat perfectly cooked and the sauces/gravies were so flavorful! My only wish is that na'an would have come with the chicken dishes. I thought this was a given but I guess I'll have to pay for the na'an extra in the future.
Food was delicious The food was brought promptly My girlfriend enjoyed the ambience of a the restaurants and we will likely return back here for the buffet

Hole in the wall places...usualy are good. This place qualifies! Entrance/lobby is dark and kinda scary but... Oxtail is good but the curry chicken is very flavorful. Combo plate came with beans and rice and choice if plantains (yummy) or cabbage. Wife had fried tilapia and jerk chicken which she enjoyed. They also have Jamaican sodas. Service was friendly even if waiter forgot my beef pie order. Definitely better than the place in Farmer's Market. We will be repeat customers and will bring family members...but probably not at night due to the location.

I'm pretty sure the cutest woman on the Planet works at this restaurant. The service is super friendly, the food is great, try the Spring Rolls!!! They have fresh yummy noodles and rice as well. It's for sure a diamond in the rough. They also have a $7 or $8 lunch special!!! Hollllerr!!

This is under a new management which is worse than the past. I attended a reception yesterday. The appetizer was all gone within 30 minutes. The management did not bring more appetizer. The dinner items were just bland. The chicken and mutton curries were probably the worst Indian dishes that i have ever tried. I am not going back to this restaurant!

Had the best Indonesian lunch in Philly! The spiciness are perfect and match with our Indonesian tongues. We ordered: Beef Satay Padang )) so tender! , Fried Chicken with sambal hejo, Soto Medan, Mie Ayam with homemade noodle made us feels like at home, the Fried Dough also great when served hot (suggest: please make the special cuko sambal just like in Indo). We dreamed about having batagor or siomay Bandung also, could you make it as the future menus, please..? We wish you would open a branch with at least the same quality in NYC, soon..!

This is the elegy.. Mojito is closing today (March 18, 2018), the workers report. Mojito was a beautiful restaurant, with lots of natural lights and decorations. The food was good overall. It was not exactly authentic Cuban, but it was flavorful. The rice bowl was great, and the fried avocado was amazing too. It will be missed!

Saison: Love that it's basically the only Vietnamese eatery opened late for us Californians. There for to-go. Condiment section was filled with all the yummy sauces: soy, sate, jalapeños, sugar, pepper, sriracha, etc, just ask for the to-go containers. Good selection of food. Banh mi was good. Pho ga was a bit too sweet for our taste buds, milk tea was just right. Papaya salad included sticky rice and do not expect the original kind of Thai papaya because there's no dried shrimp or salted crab, which is the way I'd prefer. I elected for mild spicy level which was still pretty spicy, but I can handle it. If you can't handle spicy at all, say, "No" to adding chili peppers. Customer service was interesting. They're really nice people which made the extended wait time not too bad. Added an extra 15 mins wait time because they forgot 2 items on separate orders. No biggie, just check your orders and make sure they follow through even if they acknowledged it was missing or you'll be waiting for a long time, especially when it doesn't take long to make Banh mi & you're standing there watching. Thought the guy had to attend to some other matters in the middle of making it but he never returned to the sandwich station

The cap'n crunch tilapia burrito is excellent. No rice filling lots of protein and veggies. Just the right combo of sweet and spicy. Tacos are very good, but a little too greasy and over sauced for my taste. Definitely a top 5 west Philly food truck.

Heard a lot of good things about Sofra and glad I finally decided to try it! It may look pretty simple on the exterior, which makes the interior look quite unexpected. Burnt orange walls and dim lights everywhere, it's rustic and earthy inside. There's a big stone horse sculpture on a ledge in the centre of the restaurant, no doubt the masterpiece of the place, that resembles the legendary Trojan horse. But enough of ambiance and decor, and onto the food! I had the shrimp casserole which was delicious. Large prawns cooked with all kinds of veggies -- tomatoes, squash, mushroom, peppers -- sitting in a slightly spicy sauce/broth, and all covered with mmm mmm melted cheese on top! Highly recommended. My friend had the chicken skewers which were really moist and tender, grilled to perfection. All entrees come with salad and rice pilaf. Service was courteous and friendly, our waitress came by to check up on us often. They also didn't kick us out when we decided to linger a little longer to chat. A great dining experience at Sofra and I would definitely go back!
This was really good! We had pancakes and a sandwich. You order up front and the food is brought to you so it is faster than a sit down

This was my 1st and probably the last time i will visit. Its not that the food was bad but it wasnt great either. The inside was dated and dark. The carpets were old and looked dirty but i couldnt tell because it was so dark. The food came out VERY quickly - thai chicken basil. It was avg but ive had better. I said medium spicy but there was no spice at all. Guess my quest 4 good Thai food continues...
Delicious dosa and good service. We really enjoyed our meal. The lunch prices are such a bargain. Usually no line before 12 then they fill up.

This is a great place I'm from Houston and I can honestly say they have some great hookah here. And any drinks a pretty good as well with good prices I would definitely be coming back when I come back to Nashville .

The Amgen Bike race was in town..the heat was on and Zen Yai had NO A/C. .But that did not stop us from enjoying creative fun Thai food. We used the " induce sweat with really hot food-trick..IT Worked. We had a bit of wine open from happy hour and we know that this style of Rose would pair with certain Thai food ..the hot and sweet food was a "marriage in heaven' We shared with the Chef owner and he made us a fun " not on menu" dessert REALLY enjoyed our meal will return.

It's Thanksgiving eve. No food. Me and my boyfriend are starving. DOH! What were we thinking?!?!??! Awwwwww SNAP! Let's try the Asian Pho restaurant down the street! And I'm so glad we did! Delicious, well cooked, tasty pho that was extremely reasonably priced. The lemon grass beef was so perfect and was so mouth-watering even before we got to taste it. Appetizers were just as delicious as any high-ranked pho restaurant in town. And a big thank you to you guys.... you were about to close, and still let us in with a smile! I'll definitely be back!!!!!!!!!
The food here goes to show there is definitely a Vietnamese chef in the kitchen. Pho was perfect, Vermicelli was perfect, and rolls were perfect. The decor of the place was also nicely done.

I went here with a friend on a living social deal. Needless to say I will never come back. The food was not even authentic west indie food (I know because my family is from Trinidad). The curry chicken was too Americanized and lacked the flavor and spice that authentic west Indie curry has. My friend had the jerk chicken and the chicken was spicy but lacked flavor. Wont be back, even with a deal.

I'd been wanting to go here for some time since they'd opened and finally got the chance. While this is a cute little quaint spot, I didn't have the best food experience. The first issue for me was My appetizer. I had ordered a spring roll with shrimp, however the shrimp did not look nor taste like shrimp at all. It actually looked like tofu. When I'd asked about it, the waiter couldn't tell me why it had that consistency. My entire was noodles with shrimp, it had no flavor whatsoever. Now the shrimp in my noodles looked and tasted like shrimp, so idk why the ones in my spring roll were different. My friend had some dish with beef in it but there seemed to be some unfamiliar looking piece of meat. He didn't eat it and again the water couldn't describe what it actually was. The fact that our waiter couldn't answer any questions left a really negative taste (pun def intended) in my mouth. Idk if this is normal Pho cuisine and I am just not familiar with it, but I'm certain I won't be returning here.

Friendly man behind the counter made me a wonderful falafel sandwich. Light and airy it is just as good Zatoon -and I will be back when I'm in downtown Saint Pete. $4.99 for the falafel on Mondays. Don't miss out.

Okay, so after a while of eating here, I've started to notice a decline in customer service. We went as a family one day and ordered after waiting in a long line. So the waitress was bringing over our "Naf Naf Chips" (basically kettle-cooked potato chips) and dropped it on the ground, spilling some. She just picked it up and gave it to us with an unenthusiastic "sorry". Mind you, the cup of chips is rather small, so a few chips is like half the cup. She didn't bother replacing it. But I let it slide because the food was good and fresh. The next time, however, was my last time. I stood in line and ordered, asking everything to be well done (I don't eat rare meat). My meat was all rare. I went back and told them I wanted well done meat, but no one was responding, even though a group of cashiers (one of them being the manager) were just standing around chatting. So I waited for them to come over (because they had noticed me long before) and told them my predicament. They offered no help and said "sorry, we're out of well done meat". That was the straw that broke the camel's back (get it, the logo is a camel). I threw out the rare meat and left unsatisfied, never to return.
Great food, well presented, but did not refill our water and the glasses are dreadfully small.
I had the holy chicken at a spice level three out of five. It was excellent although a bit hotter then anticipated. Spring rolls and general tso's chicken were great also.

Man o man, I go here all the time. I have been to numerous greek places around town and this is my favorite. Its so fresh and clean feeling here. I love the open kitchen feel so you can see them making to food. everything I have eaten has been really good. I have had the lamb kebab salad, which was super tender well spiced lamb and I love the salad dressing they use. You can tell they make most things from scratch here. My main go to item is the lamb gyro pocket, its under $6 and full of meat veggies and sauce. For me its the small things that count like the tahini dipping sauce and tzaziki. So many places around town have these sauces and they just don't faste too flavorful. But not kalmatas, they season everything so perfectly weather it is the tahini or meat or salad dressing, they just season things so perfect. They are all so nice here at the green hills location. Give this place a try if you have not been there.
Love this Thai place. Good food and friendly service. The restaurant is clean and enchanting music. Definitely come back for more.
Lunch buffet was very good. Lots of choices and food was fresh and delicious .Naan was served hot at the table and were very good.

Updated score due to poor customer service experience. Was offered three different excuses in the span of a 2 minute phone call regarding a problem that could have easily been resolved. ------------- We order out from India Grill about once a month, but I sincerely think that I could eat the butter chicken at least three times a week. They appear to marinate the chicken (in coconut milk?) before cooking it and add in a bit more tomato into the sauce. My god, it's good.

My friend and I were trekking along Market street in search of a good place to eat. We passed Pho street, and it seemed like the most appealing option. Pho street has a simple interior design, with orange and purple colors - sounds funky, right? But it actually looks cool In person. Stepping in, we perused the menu on the wall to the left, and made a selection. We placed our order via a touchscreen a little further back, and we ordered the beef noodle soup with eye round steak and brisket to share. There were other options to customize the soup (I.e. more noodles) or building your own pho from scratch. We waited for our order number to be called, which took about 10 minutes. We collected our soup with the fixings (bean sprouts, jalapeño peppers, and basil) and grabbed our spoons and chopsticks. For starters, the pho was large enough to properly feed 2, so if you plan on having a bowl, come hungry! The broth was very tasty and light. The noodles were the perfect texture and I appreciated that they were generous with the steak and brisket - both of which were nice and tender. This place was great for a for quality pho in a timely manner. Truly a pho-nomenal experience (okay I admit that was pretty terrible).
Excellent street food when you are drunk on bourbon! Fast, fresh. Very good!

We love to eat here, my husband gets the shrimp po boy, it is huge and the shrimp are always fried perfectly. I went with the mahi mahi and it was cooked perfectly blackened. Mussels were yummy in the spicy marinara. I will tell you it is hot if you sit outside which is expected in Florida during the summer. If you come at sunset, it is beautiful but usually very busy.
Love their veggie pizza.. LOVE LOVE that they stay open late. Totally recommend if you're hungry later in the day or even past midnight sometimes . Their fries is absolutely amazing! Must try!

Food was very good, but service is very slow which is unusual for an Indian restaurant. We've eaten in the restaurant and also gotten takeout. Last time they forgot to put part of my order in the bag, I didn't realize it until I got home, so be sure you check carefully before leaving.

I really don't understand all the 5 star reviews. Maybe the bar is set lower in Apollo Beach. We moved to Riverview last year and have been trying all the local spots. I was excited to try this place, based on other reviews. It was mediocre at best. I am a real lover of falafel, and theirs was OK, but not earth shattering. I really love babganoush, and their had a strange tang - like it may have turned. It is mostly a take-out place - a few tables for eat ins. Everyone was very friendly and food was made to order. I would not go out of my way to come back, but might try it again if I am nearby and need a quick bite.
The smell in this restaurant is horrible, the food is pretty good but the stench is overwhelming.

Visited the Vientiane Cafe on Sat night. Nice little place in the heart of West Philly. My wife and I both ordered a appetizer of veggie steamed dumplings and Pad Thai. She ordered Tofu Pad Thai, I opted for the Shrimp Pad Thai. The dumplings were nicely cooked and the dipping sauce was excellent. The Pad Thai was very good. I thought the spice level was nice (I ordered a 2 out of 4 on the heat scale) and they definitely kicked it up a notch! The shrimp were good, but you have to peel as you go, and I'm not the biggest fan of that serving method. Nice portion size and quick service. Its also a BYOB, so thats a plus as well. The two down sides to the place is 1. Its a little run down inside, and its completely no frills and 2. Its a tight dining room. If you like some elbow room, this isn't your place. However, all in all, nice little Thai place. 3 stars. Recommended.

Delicious! This was my first time here and my fourth time having Thai food overall I went with the Pad Thai. It was very good some of the best pad Thai I've had. The food was piping hot and the came out very fast. Like the other Thai restaurant I had been to this one was elegantly decorated. The atmosphere was very calm and relaxed The staff was very friendly and greeted us at the door. The price was pretty good and the portion of food was enough to fill me up without being to full

My boyfriend and I decided to stop by and try Persis today after a day of running errands. What a wonderful surprise! We both truly enjoyed our meals. I had Chicken Tikka Masala and he had Chicken Curry. Both were amazing! So much flavor! We felt like we got a great meal at a great value. We will definitely be back to sample the dinner menu soon.

Food is excellent. The prices are about what they should be. I haven't been disappointed yet here. The service is a little unpolished as others have indicated. But they work hard and are very friendly. Food always comes out timely as well.

After reading all the reviews for Thai options on the Mainline I took a chance with Siamese Princess. I ordered take out - spring rolls and pad thai. The spring rolls were decent, the pad thai was HORRIBLE! TERRIBLE! INEDIBLE! I will not be returning to SP!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: I give this 4 stars because of the outstanding value -- considering how reasonable the prices, the quality of the sushi is good and fresh. i wouldn't put this up against expensive sushi in the city center, but far superior to what i've found in Chestnut Hill. great to bring the kids -- nice vegetarian selection as well

I wandered into this place one day on my lunch hour, and I really enjoyed it. Unfortunately, there 's no one at my work that I can get lunch with, so I tend to stick to take-out places for lunch where I don't feel weird eating alone. However, I braved my lunchtime solo-ness and got myself a little table in this tiny basement restaurant on Sansom Street because I was curious about how the food was. The waiter was very nice and attentive, and I ordered a chicken kabob over rice with an eggplant and pita appetizer. Everything was delicious, and I think the chicken had saffron on it, a very expensive and tasty spice. I was able to read my book in peace, and I enjoyed listening to the large and boisterous group of people at a table in the back (up a few steps), who seemed to be enjoying themselves on some sort of business lunch. I really enjoyed my meal, and it was really pretty cheap, so I would definitely go back again, with friends this time so we can be the boisterous group at the back table.

My husband and I went to JAS Himilayan for dinner recently. The employees were all very nice and I feel bad writing them an iffy review, but the food was just ok. To start, we ordered samosas. They were your average samosas, to be expected. For my entree I decided to order something new. I got the JAS Himilayan Special Kebab. It had potential, but it was so incredibly salty that I couldn't taste anything else. I wouldn't recommend this entree. Since we were paying $20 for it, I ate it anyway- but I was not impressed. I wouldn't mind trying their buffet if in the area again.
Very negative experience. Red curry was substantially watered down and very thin soup-like consistency. They also shorted us a side of rice in our take-out order.
A wide variety of Mediterranean/middle Eastern eats. From humus to a Kafta burger to the fruit Fantasia you will be pleasantly pleased.

Overall, we were satisfied with the meal. The dishes were flavorful, everything was fresh, it was prepared to order, and they made accommodations for various tastes. The restaurant was very clean, and the price point was reasonable. There wasn't really a downside; it was pretty much what we expected. And so the stars reflect that - not terrific but not bad at all.

As soon as you stop here, you can see what makes this place stand out: a lovely view of the river, at least outside winter and if you are seated within the glass-enclosed front porch. We did, and it was delightful, cheerful and spotless. The staff is perky and friendly, but Josh B.'s comments in his closing graf are spot-on. Not just one, but two waitresses would chime together about how this or that is absolutely the greatest, best ever, unbelievably good and so on, but with no specifics. All they needed were pompoms to complete the cheerleading effect. Southern Italian food is supposed to be America's favorite, and by that popular standard we had nothing but pleasant dishes. However, if you prefer the more elegant northerly Italian offerings of, say, the excellent Il Melograno's in nearby Doylestown, Francisco's may come off as culinarily less exciting. Indeed, it was the nonstandard dishes that excelled. Shrimp bisque, if not outright memorable, was very good, and the Hawaiian butterfish was simply scrumptious. Lasagne, that old standby, used superior ingredients and is stacked high -- a tad clumsy to cut through but very nicely prepared, and you won't need to eat another thing for hours. Another warhorse, tiramisu dessert, is homemade and equally enjoyable. Even the standard bread (garlic bread is extra) and butter were above average, and we enjoyed the espresso. If you are a big fan of southern Italian eats and lovely romantic views, you'll probably fall in love with, and maybe at, Francisco's. A thirtyish married couple next to us was holding hands and cooing like starstruck teenagers, so this may be just the place to create or rekindle that special relationship. And what a great place to make your guests feel renewed! So we'll almost certainly be back now and then, provided we can get seating on the porch. As to the reported practice -- outrageous if true -- of asking diners to vacate their table after two hours during rushed periods, best is to go weekdays when there are plenty of extra tables to be had. If we go weekends, we will do so only if they agree in advance not to ask us to vacate our table to make room for others. You may wish to do the same.

In a city where there are several great choices for Indian food, this place has the best Indian I've ever eaten! I also have to bring up how friendly and attentive the service is here. Not all the staff know good English, but they will be extra helpful in trying to answer any questions you may have. My favorites are the tikka masala and palak paneer. Pure heaven... the naan is always hot , and fresh -- it has to be made to order. One day I will need to try the lunch buffet, until then I'm content ordering for dinner. Give this place a try, your taste buds will thank you!
Great price! Great food! Best ribs I've ever had. Yummy! Rice and beans are great as well. I look forward to trying the chicken!

Based on other Indian restaurants in St. Pete, I was skeptical of the reviews. My partner and friends actually "test drove" the restaurant before bringing me. I have to say that this was a very good experience. Gateway to India seems unassuming from the outside, but walk through the door and you take a step into authentic place. Service is warm and welcoming, but not intrusive. The selection of items is impressive and samples a wide array of Indian cuisine. My lamb vindaloo was delicious with the right mix if spice and vinegar. The Pista murg, butter chicken are also very well prepared. I would recommend the tamarind chutney is you want to compliment the pappadums. Overall a very nice experience.

My office recently moved to the corner of 41st and Powelton. Due to our move, we have been checking out different restaurants for lunch and were excited to try "craft chicken" at Wishbone. Not only was the white chicken delicious and a healthy alternative to the usual greasy mess we are used to receiving in tiny white boxes, but the dipping sauces made it that much better - the pommery honey mustard being the favorite at our table. Added to the simple menu was a delicious three cheese macaroni and cheese worthy of a meal itself as well as flavorful coleslaw. Strangely enough, however, my favorite item at Wishbone was the SNAP bottled black tea with fresh lemon, lemon zest, and agave - refreshing, sweet enough, and completely addicting. I wish they had it available by the case. The customer service was impeccable and friendly and the décor was inviting. Special thanks to Sophie for explaining the menu options and the ingredients in each choice. The only disappointment I experienced was not being able to try the thai chicken mentioned in the other reviews!

I absolutely love Indian food, so you could say that I have been around the Indian cuisine block. Gateway To India is spectacular! From the food to the service to the atmosphere, it is all around a great place to drink a glass of wine after a long day with some delicious food. I highly recommend this restaurant for a date night!
Tiny little place with some Indian chaat and smoothie options , staff is not friendly and too small to accommodate a big group!

Our second visit to this small, but amazing restaurant in Collingswood. Our party arrived slightly late due to traffic issues but the staff was accommodating and we never felt rushed. We tried to sample as much as possible so ordered small plates - fennel sausage and broccoli rabe, gnocchi and my personal favorite, tagliatelle al limone. Several times we all held ourselves back from licking the plates.. Just sayin' it was that good.

This is a SUPER unfortunate situation, as I REALLY like this place.. I ordered from Parada today. Normally everything is super on point and I get stuff pretty quickly...However today was no good. My initial order was not on time, and it was stated it was delayed by 15 minutes.... It was then 15 minutes after the 2nd estimated time. (so over 30 additional minutes late) I was like ok it's cool I like this place a lot, so it's cool I then opened my food (Cubano, Pasteles, and pinto beans) and everything was cold... not like cold from the delivery like everything was CLEARLY sitting. So I called... and spoke with a nice young lady who informed me that the delivery guy was out when my order came in and by the time he arrived my sandwich "had already been sitting like 15 minutes, and then the delivery time"... Not sure why a fresh one wouldn't be made... you wouldn't feed that to an in house guest.. I was told to call tomorrow and they would resend it (cause at this point I don't have time to wait.) I know you're saying well you could warm it up... NOBODY warms up pasteles or a cubano... it's meant to be enjoyed as fresh as possible.

Wow - my fellow Yelpers rarely let me down but was I disappointed with Thai Country. I started with the "fresh" meaning not fried spring roll. It was HUGE but that's about all it had going for it. Filled with iceberg lettuce, bean sprouts and vermicilli there was no spice, no basil, nothing but the heavy, salty peanut sauce on top. My green curry with pork arrived almost immediately - light on the pork, heavy on the bamboo shoots, it was spicy but not very flavorful. Very disappointing! Service was decent which gets them the 2 stars, one the food alone, I would have been tempted to give only one (something I rarely do!).
I absolutely love this place! The food is fresh and absolutely delicious. The market itself has tons of awesome goodies and their baklava is the best I've ever had!

9 out of 9 free tables were dirty and we had to have one of the cashiers clean one off for us. And the floors weren't any better. The lemonade came out as water, the Dr pepper was 95% soda water, I was scared to try the coke but at least that was okay. We had a coupon for 2 meals for $10. So that was good. And everything was tasty. The ratings for this location seem legit, NOTE TO MANAGEMENT: THESE SEEM LIKE VERY FIXABLE ISSUES.

Tried the chicken wings here and they were perfectly crispy, hot, and juicy! The sauce on them was perfectly tangy and sweet as well. The pho combo was delicious and a great portion for the price. I had enough to take home. The great music and atmosphere was a plus too!

One of the best restaurants I've been to. The food is amazing. The staff are like the best people in the world. They are very nice and friendly. They are always smiling. There's a good vibe in that place. In collegeville PA they have outside seating which is nice. And did I mention the food is so good? They have a hood variety of healthy food that is all elegantly served. That's my new favorite spot. Try it, and you can thank me later :)

Really well done Indian food in a really beautiful setting. They've taken what looked to be an older restaurant with dark wood, and booths and brightened it up with colorful artwork and saris. The staff was warm and friendly with multiple people servicing our needs and checking in with us. Service starts with a few complimentary pieces of pampadum and onion chutney. We opted to share orders of Banarsi Samosa ($4.99) and Vegetable Pakora ($5.99). Both arrived nicely played with tamarind and coriander sauces on the side. The Samosa was listed as having two pieces but arrived with four smaller pieces; while easy to share this gave more pastry than filling, which was delicious - lots of potato a touch of peas and LOTS of fresh herbs ... which you don't often see. The Pakora were excellent; light brown, crunchy, lots of shredded vegetables and someone understands the importance of finishing freshly fried food with a little salt. Probably the best we've had! My husband selected his usual Palak Paneer ($14.99) - medium spiced. He was presented with a good sized bowl of creamy spinach with lots of Paneer (nothing annoys him more than paying fifteen dollars and setting tiny portion with no cheese). His only disappointment was that their 'medium' is quite a bit spicier than most. My entree was my favorite, Zafrani Rogan Josh ($16.99) - ordered hot it delivered on spice but also on flavor. Lots of layers of flavor and heat topped of with fresh herbs. There were a decent number of cubes of lamb (something I order out because we don't make it at home) .. it was tender and moist and absorbed a lot of the flavor of the sauce. We also share an order of Butter Naan ($2.49) - plenty of bread for the two of us to mop up all of the delicious sauces. Servers kept water filled, checked in on our dinners and were very friendly. I especially liked the little touches where sugar for my iced tea ($2.49) was served in a tiny, brightly colored, jeweled box. This place has ample parking; but I'm sure gets pretty busy based on the food, service and value... can't wait to check out their lunch buffet!

Eat at Yah Mon and you will be happy, mon! It took me a few minutes before I could talk after biting into the Jerk Chicken Wing appetizer because it was an explosion of wonderful flavors. I could have stopped there and started writing my 5 Star review but we got the Island Sampler and the meal got better. Ox Tail - WOW! Curried Goat - so good! And more Jerked Chicken which, as I mentioned is amazing. We also got some snapper Stew Fish, fantastic, of course. Our hosts were there to make our meal a memorable experience which worked because I'm not going to forget it anytime soon. :)
I love hummus wrap---its always full of fresh tasting vegetables. I'm addicted to it! I have also had the gyro platter and enjoyed that too.

I don't often choose Vietnamese restaurants when going out to eat, but if I do, mint modern is one of my top choices. The restaurant is a little small and seating is limited, so when you walk in you kind of awkwardly stand there until seated. I'm pretty sure I've liked everything I tried here. For starters, the sticky wings are a MUST! They come out crispy and hot with some delicious sauces I'm not sure of, but hey it's good so I'm not one to complain! The spring rolls & baos are pretty standard to me and taste good nonetheless. As far as drinks, the mangonada or chamango is a MUST!! It's a mango smoothie with fresh mango chunks on top, garnished with chamoy sauce and I believe tajin seasoning. You also get a tamarind candy straw. It's the perfect blend of sweet, tart and spicy.
