If this isn't your cup of tea, they also have lots of options for bubble tea, a full bar, and the standard sodas and teas. Entrees include traditional banh mi's, vermicelli bowls, rice dishes, pho, etc. Some specials include the sizzling steak & eggs which comes with side of baguette, kimchi burger, chicken & waffles! I've had it all and none of the dishes honestly disappoint. I'm a rice type of gal so my favorite is the rice with either beef ribs or lemongrass chicken. It comes with white rice but you can sub for fried rice or brown rice, side of fish sauce, pickled veggies and do yourself a favor and add fried egg! The popping yolk on rice is soooo good. Food comes out pretty quickly and I've never had a problem with service even when they're busy. The vibes are casual and the decor actually looks pretty elegant. Give mint modern a try! It'll definitely become a regular spot for ya

Called a half hour ahead and order wasn't even started when I got there. Kid that made the food was sweeping the floor when I walked in then started making the food without washing his hands. He then proceeded to go to the sink and fake wash his hands in plain site. Absolutely disgusted and will not be going back to one of my former favorite takeout Mediterranean spots in Manayunk.

Phenomenal food in the relative wasteland of Asian food in the Santa Barbara County. Given the comparatives of Noodle City and Saigon Noodle, Phamous Cafe is a refreshing change of pace that has much more friendly prices than the general food scene in Santa Barbara and sticks to more a more authentic style. Through multiple visits I have found myself to be satisfied time and time again as their full-bodied soup stock in their pho has brought me comfort and joy on every occasion. The meat is well prepared, noodles well prepared and the price is more forgiving than the rest. Despite my ravings of the pho, my initial opinion of the restaurant came from their Bahn Mi. Their meat preparation, Vietnamese bread and pickled vegetables bring a refreshing addition to the Santa Barbara food palate. This delightful sandwich priced the best for a quick bite is beyond fantastic. The garlic pâté is undeniably the glue that holds together the sandwich to excellence. Overall an excellent experience that should not crumble to the lowest denominator that is often found around the area.
great Greek food! We always get the charcoal sampler...AWESOME! Tried a few of the lamb dishes that were really good also. Every dish is seasoned to perfection.

Awesome foods and occasion. Clean and nice attitude, I will be back for Goat carry ( They said it took longer time but even lamb carry was excellent for me) I am Asian, bit prefer here than the one in downtown close by Vanderbilt, but little expensive. I am living here so overall it was good experience and be back soon.

Great entertainment, great food, and to top it all off, the decor is really gorgeous! Momos has belly dancers most nights of the week, and the dancers are great! They're from St Louis's own Belly Dance Mirage. The tables are not super-crowded, so the dancer has room to move easily from table to table. The last time I was there, the dancer came through the bar area with a tray of lit candles balanced on her head. (Remember, tipping the dancer is good, but put the money in the side of her belt or the back of her bra straps, don't be crude! Trying to cop a feel offends the dancer and makes you look like a jackass to the whole rest of the restaurant.) The decor is pretty, with a lot of rich colors, and painted tables. If you have a group, come a little early and ask for a booth. Since they're set into the wall, #1) they look really cool, and #2) it's a lot quieter and easier to have a conversation. The food is served in Mezedakia style, so small plates like tapas. Some dishes are more authentically Greek, some less so, but they all taste great, and I just really enjoy the whole small-plates style eating experience. I like getting to nibble at a bunch of different things. The bar has a selection of foo-foo fancy martinis, but what's at all Greek about that? If you like Ouzo, they have a selection to chose from, otherwise, they have a good wine list. And the mead is worth trying once, though I don't think it's the kind of thing everyone would like. The crowd is young, the food is modern, and the place is a lot of fun. Go with a group, so you can order some of everything.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: This place just re-opened after strip mall renovation Looks real nice inside, good job.. however it was an odd choice to go with red and white checkered table cloth like the stereotypical Italian-American cliche. Service was good, (was a Tue eve at 6) 5 other tables eating We had the Tom Yum Goong Thai soup: Very good, I suspect a tad above many folks preferred heat/spice limit. I liked it. Good blend of flavor, not overly acidic as so many can be. Only negative comment is if you list "prawns" as an ingredient, dont use the some of the smallest shrimp available. Prawns imply big shrimp (in this country) Won Ton soup was very nicely done. Basic Pork Goyza (fried dumpling): was also good. These seemed to be steamed first then lightly fried. Green salad with ginger dressing Very basic, but good The SO Special Duck: (crispy duck,jumbo shrimp, chicken,pork ,beef, Peking sauce) I'm a fan! Great flavor. Duck a little fatty (as often is the case) Jumbo Shrimp were medium large, but tasty. Very balanced. Sweet and sour chicken: Good, very basic (sorry to me this is the chicken mc'nuggets of the asian world) We will return to try more of the Thai and Japanese offerings FYI: They do not offer the combo dinners listed on take out for dining in

We got take out so can't speak to the dining experience but the food was really good. The Massaman curry chicken was delicious and they give you a good portion. My girlfriend got the vegetable drunken noodles and those were ok but not as good as my dish. We also had the corn cakes which were fine, fairly basic but the sauce was good that came along with it. Pay cash and your bill will be cheaper. Good experience here and would definitely come back.

This will be my new regular. A friend of mine introduced me to this place a few days ago and I got a lamb roll to go. From the first bite I could tell that this place knew how to cook lamb for once. The lamb was cooked until it nearly fell apart , you could tell that it was young because it didn't have that smell of a stinky grown sheep. You know exactly what I'm talking about. Came back again for some more take out a few days later and then the next day and they remembered who I was. I like when you go to a restaurant and it has the feeling that you welcome and respected. I ordered the lamb shank with vegetables. Perfect. The lamb was fresh and tender, coming right off the bone like lamb should be. The the vegetables,beans, potatoes and rice all had a distinct flavor. The rice you could tell was not of cheap quality because it didn't turn into mush when you ate it. We never ran out of water to drink and bread to dip in the sauce. Bottom Line- The owners care about the food, fast service, food is all home made except the fries good for lunch because its cheaper. P.S if you come to a family owned restaurant right before they close and complain about them not serving you. Give them a damn break, they work all day preparing fresh food and some people like to go home and relax. So stop being a baby and tell them to have a good night and leave.
Best indian ktichen in town! I will definitively come back! First time here and I don't regret it all!

My family and I have been going here for years, and this is hands down our favorite Indian restaurant in the Carmel/Indianapolis area. The food is authentic, the service is fast, and the restaurant is never too crowded (so it's enjoyable to sit in). They also offer take out which we've taken advantage of a few times. I recommend the Chicken Tikka Masala or the Chili Chicken. If you actually want your food to be spicy, I recommend asking for medium or hot spice!
I was surprised! Decent food, good selection, not greasy. Not the best, but I was pleasantly surprised to find solid indian food in Reno. Thanks guys!

Yes, I'm a fan, though it's a bit hit-or-miss depending on the dish. The dosas and vadas are awesome and a great value, but the idli left and the buffet me disappointed. Still, it's great to have some South Indian veg stuff in Philly, which has had a lack of really good Indian restaurants since Ravi got sick and Samosa Vegetarian closed some years back.

Wish they had falafel, but satisfactory veggies on the pita wrap. I went when they first opened, and every time I drive by, I want to stop but I remember that they didn't have falafel and I keep driving :(

I left Philly for good a while back and this guy has raised the bar of a good falafel soo high for me, that I dont like any falafel I have :( I'm too spoilt. He has the most flavorful falafels with very creative and complimenting side dishes. Enjoy you ppl in Philly!

We came in as a loud, large party, who kept them open late. Everything was perfect, from the wait staff to the food. The food! I don't even remember everything we had but it was delicious. Samosas were perfect, the tikka was excellent, a cauliflower dish that was to die for, all as appetizers. Entrees were butter chicken and two types of biriyani - goat and shrimp. I have to say the goat biriyani way favorite dish of the night. Everything was wonderful.

Vientiane's food is just all right & not especially good. The Pad Kee Mao (Thai Drunken Noodles) were soft and tasty for the most part, but the meat was overcooked & not enjoyable. The Laab (Laotian) was bland, with overcooked meat again, though it wasn't as badly overcooked as in the noodle dish. I've had a fish dish (tilapia?) which was edible -- meh. This is a charming little restaurant that's nicely decorated and comfortable to sit in. The food is around 2 or 2.5 stars, so with the decor and ambience, I give it 3 stars all around.

This is another modern Vietnamese restaurant that has popped up in New Orleans; these restaurants seem to be pretty trendy here. The food and menu here aren't quite authentic, but the food is still tasty. Don't expect the food to be homey, mom's kitchen type of fare, and you won't be disappointed. I went with a group of friends and we were pretty indecisive and took a long time to order, but the waitress was still patient with us. I split the pork belly tacos for an appetizer and had the kimchi burger for my entree. The tacos and burger were both good. The "tacos" are equivalent to what other places are calling "sliders:" peking duck buns stuffed with pork belly and garnished with carrots and cilantro. The sweet potato fries that come with the burger have some sort of salt and pepper seasoning which was really good. The burger is pretty heavy and messy, so be warned! I think Mint is definitely one of the best Vietnamese places in NOLA; I would definitely rank it above Lilly's cafe, Pho Bistreaux and Magasin. I like that the menu is more creative here, with the chicken and waffles and burgers. It's also a big space, which I imagine would make it less hectic during peak hours (that's what drives me crazy about Magasin - it's too small!). Prices are average here, running about $9-$10 for entrees and $4-6 for appetizers.
Let's just I ate the half chicken meal in 14 mins! This's has come up a lot for you too lol lol
Great service and amazing food. I cannot get enough of the Pad Thai.

As others have pointed out, what seperates Momo's from the everyday Greek restaraunt are the belly dancers. For about 15-20 minutes the restaraunt stops as everyone takes a look at the spectacle. The dancers are fun and entertaining. Have some cash ready to tip them. My only complaint with the dancing is that the music is turned way up at this time, making it difficult to converse with anyone at your table. The food is good but not the best Greek food I've had in St. Louis. I usually get the baked brie which comes with fruit & nuts on top. The selection is extensive and most items are served tapas style so that you can try 2 or 3 items.

I love this food truck. Top five places to eat in Philly. I'm from California and love fish tacos. They do GOOD fish tacos! Also their fish burrito is amazing too. Only complaint is the eatability of the burrito. Toppings fall out and the sauce seeps out of the wrapping covering my hands. Kinda messy. And one other thing is the truck is not always open on time. Since I have such a small time window for lunch.... If they don't open on time I have to rush lunch. Still love them though

This was one of favorite lunch spots, so I deliberated about doing this update. Lemongrass Soup and veggie spring roll were as good as always. The beef Pad Thai was sour - as if someone had squeezed a whole lemon into the plate. The beef was a bit over cooked, but edible. The few sprouts I could find appeared to be mixed in. I ate about a quarter of the dish. They did ask me if I wanted to take the rest home, and I said "No, it wasn't very good." End of conversation, apparently.
My favorite Thai place for years! I love the amazing peanut sauce and pad Thai. Had it tonight and it is delicious as always!
if you like middle eastern food like kabobs and rice pilafs this place is great. Great for vegetarians too, they have a really good spinach dish, eggplants, etc. good stuff.

Land of Smile is a great place to go for good Thai food when aren't in any mood to wait for a table- because this place is NEVER full. I have eaten here a few times with my parents, and family friends and every time we have been one of the only people in the restaurant. The food is pretty good, definitely not GREAT...but good. Everything is much more authentic then any other Thai place near by...The Chicken Satay is great...and so is the spring rolls...The hot tea is pretty standard, but I love hot tea- so I always indulge a little a drink a few cups...Also the Thai Iced tea really is incredible! Try it out...its not so shabby...

Best Thai restaurant on the loop! In case you didn't know, ALL the thai places on delmar are owned by the same people, but for some reason this one is the best. They serve reliably delicious thai food with fast service, making Thai Country a great place to come with a group. Portions are large and usually involve yummy leftovers the next day. My recent favorites include the panang curry and crab rangoons. The noodles and rice dishes are also a safe bet. Just make sure to be clear on what level spice you want!
The food here is of the best quality and the decor is so calming. I love this little place but be sure to reserve a table as they seem to fill fast often.

Service was excellent, very attentive and friendly. Food was delicious, we ordered the lamb korma and a chicken dish with ginger (forget the name) and both were great. Also the garlic cheese naan was awesome. I'm super excited to see an Indian restaurant open in the neighborhood and hope they stick around.

When we went there, there were nobody. Probably most of people wouldn't wanna try Ethiopian food. We ordered lamp and beef, they were all served together with some sour African bread. I didn't like that sour bread at all. The beef was not bad. The portion was not so big as well. Overall, it's a little bit expensive and you just need to experience once if you want.

i go here whenever i want to have some good sushi, and i mean sushi, not a roll of rice drenched in spicy mayo. in this part of town and i would even go as far to say the Tampa area, they have the best fish and a wide variety of fish at that too. have been eating at other places but nothing that has topped this place yet. def recommend this place for real sushi lovers.

This is my go-to place when I have visitors in the city. The Afghan food is something a little different but is very approachable. And Ariana's does it right! A couple can eat here for easily $35 including tip. My favorites include - Appetizers/Sides: Aashak, Burandee Kadu, and Buranee Badenjan (you can pick three as a sampler kind of thing) Entrees: Lamb Corma, Norange Palow, and Badenjan Chalow. Go for the lamb over chicken, it is so tender! Also, they have delicious ice cream that is definately worth trying. The service is very unassuming but great. It is also a BYO, so don't forget a bottle of wine. Side note: if you have a group of four, ask for the table in the window. It is traditional style dining (sitting cross legged on the floor).

roast duck pho was outstanding, with a fine, clear broth and generous meat. cafe sua da was perfect. i really don't understand what the detractors were looking for.... pho in a hole-in-the-wall doesn't get much better. atmosphere is for pho houses with lousy food.
Best baklava I've ever tasted!!! Thanks :) I can't wait to try the saganaki next time I'm at the restaurant.

I have been back to Smiley's several times and have not once been disappointed! I'm officially obsessed with their Honey and Walnut Baklava. I'm a sucker for desserts and it is heaven in my mouth. I've been getting the Greek Salad which is so fresh and the house dressing is light and complimentary to the salad. The Orange Passion smoothie is my favorite so far!! I genuinely appreciate a place that has fresh, delicious food and great customer service. Their staff is always SO sweet and upbeat it will brighten your day up. Keep it up Smiley's!!! :)

I got take out today for my first experience with this restaurant since it was Thai Taste. The dish I ordered was described as spicy and the lady behind the counter asked me if I wanted it spicy, to which I replied yes. Unfortunately, there was zero heat to my dish. Was very bummed about that. I was also disappointed in the serving size. For slightly more money, you get slightly less food than comparable establishments. In fact, I have never seen this size styro container before but when I first picked it up, could tell this was not the typical portion size. So, here it is about 2.5 hours later, and I'm legitimately stomach growling hungry. I would give them another chance as a dine in option to see if that helps the cause.

Have been here for buffets, great selection and food tastes awesome. Different spices and aroma in each of dishes and specializing in north indian food. Sat/Sun buffet is much better with much more choices than the weekday buffet.

Bbq pork bhan mi was dry and flavorless. Even the pickled veggies on it didn't have much flavor. Asked for mayo and it was oily and runny. No chicken pho available. Service was weird, they were calling out table numbers and sandwich numbers, I almost got the wrong sandwich. They forgot my husband's eggroll, so he had to go stand in line again to get it. I would not go here again.

I predict this to be the next, greatest casual Asian eatery of the bay. Across from the busy Park Plaza, Season's sits in a small, unassuming plaza. The décor is rather plain... the menu and items for sale are straightforward--totally reminds me of the little Asian cafes in Southern California. Me likey. Small tables for groups of four and lounging areas for chatting. Honestly--I haven't gotten anything besides the banh mi and shaved ice... and always on the go. But do you need more? Right now the banh mi is on sale for $2! Oooh that crunchy and soft contradiction of a bread housing the pickled veggies and shaved meats. You can taste each ingredient yet it all works in harmony. The shaved ice is light, fluffy snow with lots of variations on toppings. There's always some special to get a free cup of it. The menu is a collection of Asian fusion: Boba, designer wedding cakes, phad thai, spring rolls, baked goods, and probably a pony ride too if you ask. It always feels like the staff is wanting me to create familial conversation with them. They're cool. Due to its central location and awesome weekend hours (closed at 2am?) plus the ability to just run in and out, I will be haunting this place more in the future.

My gf and I came to check this place out tonight after reading good reviews. We ordered a decent spread of food: the Bhel Puri, Indian Bread Basket, Lamb Vindaloo, and Dhaba Chicken. The first few plates arrived and the food was fairly enjoyable up until my gf noticed the decorative liner under the bowls on the plates. To our horror and disappointment the chef was using folded JOSS PAPER (religious ceremonial paper used traditionally in Chinese culture to pay TRIBUTE TO OUR DECEASED FAMILY MEMBERS) to line the plates. After we mentioned this to the waitress she quickly apologized and removed the paper telling us she will inform the chef. Sadly, as new customers arrived we noticed the chef was still using Joss Paper as decoration. After such ignorance and disrespect to our culture its safe to say that we will not be returning to this restaurant.

2.5 stars. The truth is that this place is no better than the string of other mediocre Thai restaurants in West Philly (ie, Lemon Grass, Pattaya, etc). I started with the Thai Coconut Soup. It wasn't bad, but it lacked the subtle tartness that makes good Tom Kha good. I always judge a Thai place based on the quality of their curries--a fundamental aspect of Thai cuisine. I ordered the Green Curry, and it can be described as a few carrots and broccoli stems floating around in a soup of watered down coconut milk. With tax and tip my bill was $18, and I don't see any reason to go back. As my friend said at the end of our meal: "The search for a half decent Thai restaurant in Philly continues."

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Wonderful people who take care of my orders and load up my car for me. The food is always fresh and hot! I plan on stopping in to try the lunch buffet soon. Yummy

Last night I was in the mood for Vietnamese food - specifically a nice big bowl of pho - and we ended up Kien Giang. The food was OK, not great - and lacked some of the more complex flavors that I've experienced at other Vietnamese restaurants. But, this place is cheap - $5.50 for a bowl of pho, $2.00 for an order of 2 Vietnamese eggrolls, and $2.00 for a coke. The service was a little slow and there was a huge language barrier between the server and myself - ultimately, the numbered menu helped. I'd go back, but only if Miss Saigon was closed for the evening. One other potential issue is that they don't accept credit cards, so be sure to bring cash or your checkbook.

This WAS a great place to eat ; the buffet and the regular food was superb, I used to go here with my colleagues from work almost twice a week regularly. The cook apparently changed a few weeks ago and so did the manager, and it has not been the same after. I love Indian food and I eat it all the time. I have not visited this place for two months, since the change. Sadly the prices have gone up and the quality and gone down. To add insult to injury they have a new blonde manager who barely knows Indian food, but is loud and uncouth in her interactions. Nothing against her, just that a Indian manager in a Indian restaurant sounds a decent expectation. Hopefully the owner gets a better cook and an Indian manager is not a tall order !

I am from Thailand. My husband and I decided to try this place out for lunch. We got the drunken noodles and we were so disappointed. The flavor was sweet and not tasty at all. This is NOT a real Thai restaurant whatsoever. I suggest not to go here at all. If you are wanting REAL Thai food in Boise, go to Thai Cuisine off overland Rd

Worst customer service. You walk in and they don't even greet you with a hello or a smile. Almost shout and ask you if you have a togo order. Waited 25 minutes for a small grilled beef sandwich. This place was close to my work for my only 30m lunch, won't be returning here again.

I had the combination Pho and my girlfriend had the rare steak and lean brisket Pho. We love Pho and have tried quite a few places through LA - this place definitely compares with the best. I suggest you check it out.
They were open late around 2:30am and the decor and presentation as well as the ambiance lovely. I had the Chicken Wings and Fries. The food however was subpar. Sadly it looks better than it tastes .

I really like this place, and visit frequently. Fello, the owner, is amazing and provides excellent customer service. The restaurant is very homey and family friendly. The food is delicious and fresh, not frozen. It is by far the best bang for your buck in Center City. The pastelillos (turnover pastries) are the best I have had in Philadelphia.

This is a charming little restaurant right off the busy main drag. Thai spring rolls were fried to perfection and served with a delicate dipping sauce. The mussaman curry was rated a 2 out of 5 for heat and it was on the money. Generous bowl with a side of sticky rice, this fulfilled all of my Thai cravings. I also love the elegant decor, which is not immediately obvious from the exterior. Highly recommended. Iced coffee with appetizer and entree was $19.
Great all round!! Food was awesome, service was great and atmosphere and sunset view were amazing!! Loved it!

This is without a doubt one of the best Authentic Thai restaurants in the area. Food is Outstanding..! FRESH.. Cooked just the way I like it... Yeah it's a small 10 table place... And they don't make you feel like cattle on the feed.. Owner is always on hand making sure your food is just how you like it.... Always with that personal touch.. If it sounds like I like this place... You would be right!! Price is a value.. If you want real Thai food... from receipts passed down from generation to generation.. This is the place.

The food is good. I've only been here twice the food is good but the falafel has these small hard pieces in that would get stuck in my teeth. The service was really good as well. I went the first week that they opened so I hope they keep it up.

I've visited a few times now. Each time my food has been prepared excellent! The portions are large and well worth the price. I enjoy the fried catfish the most. It's not your average Andy's cornmeal (although I like Andy's). The jerk chicken is well seasoned and tender. I can't compare the jollof rice to any others but it was good. I'd have to say the red beans and rice are my favorite of the two. If you love fried plantains, you'll love these. They have just the right firmness. I must add that the staff is very polite. Overall if you're looking for African/Caribbean this is the place!
Always amazing. My absolute favorite Thai place. I travel from the mainline to get here!!

Awesome! I went last night having never had chaat before, and Hasan (the owner) was so great! He asked me what I liked and made the perfect dish just for me. The dish was colorful, crunchy, creamy, meaty, savory, sweet and sour all at the same time, and it works together in a way I never imagined food could. The lassi was great as well (mango and honey), and Hasan let me try a rice pudding that was so so good, not thin like most puddings I've tried before but creamy with a subtle spice. I will definitely be a regular from now on!

The ambiance is nice, the staff friendly and the burgers juicy (and halal!), but the owner/manager keeps the place far too warm. Maybe it's the heat from the kitchen.....but if they want customers to be comfortable and sit for a while, esp. when it's crowded, they need to crank up the AC!

I came here on a Saturday night with reservations. I would definitely suggest making reservation as the dining room is very small. As many people have noted, it was a bit loud also probably because of the size. I had the Siam Square Salmon which was very good. My mom had the Pad Thai which she said was very nice because it wasn't oily. Additionally, the price is right. I will definitely be back.

From the moment I arrived at Casa Blanca I felt unsafe and displeased with service. We paid for our entry, hookah, and food which he said we must buy because my friend who was with us did not have his ID. We waited roughly 15 min just to be seated, or even acknowledged by staff. When the server finally seated us at a table, I sat down trusting that our server knew the table was OK for a customer. When I sat down I smelled a foul oder, only to realize I had stepped and slid my foot across a pile of vomit. My boyfriend returned from the restroom and after I told him what happened, he politely brought up the situation with management. Which they proceeded to tell him "well we didn't know" & "where are you from? Oh, well in Tucson it's not like that" ..... There is absolutely no excuse for this. First of all, IF YOU SERVE FOOD THERE SHOULD BE NO VOMIT ON THE FLOOR. BOTTOM LINE. WE WILL BE CONTACTING THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT FOR THE SAFETY OF ALL OF OUR HEALTH. DO NOT GO HERE! !!

This place is legit. We walked in at 8 on a Wednesday night and it was packed. We got the shrimp and avocado roll (served with peanut dipping sauce) and a pork belly roll to start. We each got a pho, one veggie and one spicy beef. Everything was amazing. We might go back tomorrow again for lunch.

I loved the iced Thai tea but the food felt like it came from the microwave. My cousin came back to the hotel throwing up from the spicy chicken noodles. She's a bit picky but I knew we just stuffed our faces with the food because we were so hungry. The taste was nothing I'm used to. I lived in Hawaii so maybe I developed higher standards for Thai or maybe I just love spicy food. I don't know but to me the food was not spicy it was sort of baby spiced like if they skipped or got stingy with spices. Like others mentioned the curry was runny. I ate it and took all the carrots out because it had way too much carrots. I recommend ask for super duper spicy or for hot sauce. I guess if you are desperate need of Thai food eat here other than that just skip this spot

I was in the area and hungry so I decided to stop in and give this place a try due to their high Yelp ratings. Surprisingly I was the only person in here. Generally not a good sign though wanted to give this place of shot. While waiting for my combination drunken noodles two separate people came in to order take out. Found out they have a vegan menu as well and do not offer a military discount. I was served a 3 chip dish after ordering. This may have been because I got there after lunch and had to order off dinner menu. As far as their heat scale it was med, hot, and thai hot. I asked for hot but waitress said since I hadn't been there before to just order med. Shrimp was served with tails still on. The Drunken Noodles was very tasty and as far as the heat level a medium is what I would have considered three stars on a 1 to 5 scale. Would definately come back.

I ordered a take out and the word that describes the quality of food - pathetic. Chana masala was tasteless, Bhatura was half cooked, paneer chilli was sweet and tasted awful, chicken lollipop terrible. I am running out of adjectives to describe the rest. Punjabi Kadhi was the only edible item. Will never go there again.

This is one if my favorite restaurants to eat. On the corner of Mill and Kietzke, you will find plenty of parking. The food is delicious. My favorites are Salt and Pepper Shrimp Chef Dish that comes with a serving of steamed rice and the Flamed broiled pork and steamed rice. Who am I kidding, almost everything i have ordered as been delicious, I've had their Spring Rolls, Vermicelli noodles, Pork Fried Rice and Walnut Shrimp and have never been disappointed. It's a family owned business, Fiona and her husband run the restaurant and are such friendly people. Call your order for take out or dine inside, you won't b
Finally! I love this place. Cute, small, tidy, clean, quick. The staff was great. Food was super tasty. Def making this a spot to frequent. They deliver too!

First the good: nice atmosphere and quick service. Now the bad: the lamb was extremely tough, small servings for the price point I give it 3 stars only because of the atmosphere and service. Don't waste your hard earned money on this Mediterranean hack. I have eaten at at least a dozen better Mediterranean restaurants severely disappointed

So happy to have found this Puerto Rican restaurant here in north Tampa. The food was amazing and the staff are very welcoming and super nice. Love the decor. You feel like your in Puerto Rico and the price of the food is affordable. You can't find that price anywhere except for Puerto Rico. We will be regulars. The food was that good
Got the chicken kabobs. Texture of the meat was sort of gross. Didn't seem fresh. Had that rubbery restaurant texture like it was precooked and then seared before serving. Won't be going back

Asian cuisine isn't my favourite. I find a lot of the food slimy, over-sauced and unappetizing. But some Vietnamese dishes are exceptions. I always have the salad rolls here. They have amazing peanut dipping sauce. Also, their Imperial rolls, which are deep fried yummy spring roll goodness, are to die for - in fact, they're what keep me coming back. I like getting Imperial rolls on rice noodles. It comes with fresh bean sprouts and other veggies, and a tangy sauce that soaks into the spring roll well. The ambiance here is rather stark. It's just a few tables and chairs, a magazine rack, a fish tank with some over-sized and cramped looking fish in it and sea-weedy floating stuff, and a crowd that is culturally-mixed. The neighbourhood's not the best, but I've never witnesses anything untoward here. Service is fairly fast, asian efficient and friendly, and the shop is clean.

Great food, service, menu, and decor. It's been around for a long time with a customer base that has a lot of Thai influence. So, it met and exceeded expectations. Owner answered level of spice question perfectly.

Surprisingly wonderful! It looked a little questionable from the outside but the owner gave us excellent service and the food was delicious! It was my friend's first time trying Indian food and I am so glad she was able to have such a perfect experience. The chicken Tikka masala was tender and flavorful, and the garlic naan was a perfect accompaniment. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for a quick Indian meal in the University City area.

My wife and I had drinks for Labor Day here at Mojitos and we had a really great time. As a bartender, I've made mojitos before but these folks REALLY know what makes a mojito a fantastic anytime drink. My wife had a Strawberry Mojito while I had their NOMo (New Orleans Mojito). Both were made with New Orleans Rum which I always thought wasn't an especially great rum, but in this case, it turns out I was wrong. Our bartender was especially courteous and friendly and made our night that much more memorable. The only thing I will say is that the drinks were a bit on the pricey side. But other than that, we had a great time and will definitely be coming back!
Great food a really fast and friendly service. I loved this place.

Unique and different concept of serving delicious traditional Indian food like fastfood. The platter is cheap and lots o variety- 2 curries, rice and bread. The curries all have different flavors. The chicken Frankie personally was different and good. Vegetarian options available too. Their menu changes everyday. Biryani (special rice) available on weekends. Overall thumbs up!

I really enjoyed the hummus and shawarma on my first visit. All of the food looked fresh and it tasted delicious. Unfortunately, on my second visit an employee coughed without covering her mouth or turning her head while she was preparing some pita. They were out of shawarma, and said it would be at least another 45 minutes before it would be ready. (This was around noon). I think this place has a lot of potential, but I think the employees and management could be better trained in safe food handling (eg not coughing on food), and be better prepared. Mistakes happen, but it's a real bummer if you are missing half of your meat options, and an item that is literally on your sign isn't available for lunch.

(Tip: The special combo menu is a fantastic deal) A great place to go during one's 40 days of lent! The girls and I had a wonderful time here with the servers (who were not only friendly, but gave us a few tid bits to try since it was our first time hearing about a couple of the dishes). We have been back a couple times since. The prices are reasonable (what first caught out our attention, though these would also reflect the flavor but it is surprisingly quite good considering they have no competition in the area).
Pretty good cupcakes, not too many flavor options but it changes regularly and you can get a few unique ones. The baked donut was really good and it isn't fried, so bonus for that!

Not bad, not good service mediocre I ate mine but was dreaming of pf Chang's frozen dinner i had left in freezer and regretting the trip. Someone nearby was having a dish that looked great. I've been to the Hendersonville location and it was a similar experience just less crowded

I'm from California and there is an abundance of places to get my favorite Vietnamese dish pho. I'm here in Jersey visiting and I'm very skeptical to try new places. I brought my friends who have never tried pho before too. I walked in and was greeted immediately by the owners. We made small talk and then ordered. it didn't take long at all until our food arrived and our pho came with all the condiments and veggies just like back home. Of course I had to try the broth first before adding anything and it was really good and didn't need much at all, but i do like my pho spicy so siracha and sauté was added along with hoisin sauce, peppers, bean sprouts, and lime. I was really scared that they catered to an American pallet but it is 100% authentic. The PHOod was amazing and the owners were very nice! I will definitely come back while I'm out here.

I was really impressed with their selection! The staff was nice enough and able to answer any questions I had. This is definitely the best Arabic market in the area and probably the best in Tampa. I'll be back when I'm over that way for sure.

I've eaten here before, my girlfriend had never had Ethiopian food before. The waitress was pleasant and helpful, we ordered the sampler for two people. It was delicious and a generous portion of food. In her words, A+!

The Vietnamese food is on point, and the batch of Rare Pho (beef) was fantastic today. Maybe it's because it's a cold, rainy day and I was hungry. I ordered coconut milk, and that was sweet but tasty. It had shaved pieces of coconut meat in there as well. You get a fortune cookie at the end of the meal. The servers never seem nice and sometimes come off as quite straight forward (with no smiles on their faces), but as often as I've dined here... I appreciate the culture. They get to the point and get you what you ask for. They're there to make and serve you food, not to do cartwheels and overextend service as our culture feels so entitled to. I like it. The restaurant is quite small, and everyone tries to get the table furthest from the door because it gets cold in there. I watch a lot of folks carry-out as well as come in for bubble tea or some sort of smoothie.
First off, this was the best gyro and freshest hummus ever! But more importantly, the warm welcoming environment made me feel right at home. Smileys truly lived up to its name!! Would 10/10 recommend

Sky Cafe was my introduction to indonesian food and I must say, what an introduction. I can't say enough about how welcome I feel in this family run restaurant. From what I understand, a lot of indonesian food can be a bit on the sweet side, however, the cuisine here mostly originates in southern Indonesia (Jakarta), which tends to be a bit spicier. The food is very addicting. I initially explored a lot of their egg noodle soup dishes which they offer with a variety of different meat and seafood. The soto medan (coconut chicken soup) really hits the spot, very flavorful. The pork platter is a wonderful example of the indonesian treatment of spice. This might be south philly's best kept secret, but really shouldn't be. Check out Sky Cafe.

Great food depends on who is in the kitchen. Love the soup it's delicious and great for this time of the year. I recommend the frozen yogurt with all 3 toppings supper yummie. The chicken with lemon honey sauce is yummie

I was impressed with the decor as I walked in this cute little restaurant in Mount Juliet. My friends and I were served right away. As I looked around I was also impressed that the restaurant was so busy for a rainy Sunday night. Lots of choices on the menu. All the reviews talked about the amazing butter chicken so I of coarse had to try it. We also ordered the Shrimp Biryani, chicken fried rice and 2 orders of Nan. (1 butter nan and 1 cheese nan), the cheese nan was amazing! Butter was great too. We also ordered the egg rolls to start with which we really liked. It was enough food for 4 we had left overs. The entrees are served family style easy for sharing. Everything was great and all went together well. The water tasted really good, I know it's odd to say but I always order water and I don't usually drink it down, it was tasty. We will come back again for sure!

Love this place! I typically get the Greek Salad with chicken (which is shredded), and it's amazing. I get the small size, and it is enormous. The grape leaves are fantastic, as is the hummus. I have never been disappointed by the food or the service.
4 stars mean Yay! I'm a fan, and I am. It has good, fresh, food at a IV price. I get #31, because a friend showed me it, it looked good and it taste.

Sorry to say, I'm revising my previous 5 start review. My favorite dish had changed, the staff had changed, the food and feel of this restaurant had changed and I'm not happy about it. While it still looks like it always has, the food is definitely not what it was a year ago. My sizzling duck didn't sizzle like it used to. In fact it seemed the dish almost completely changed. Not happy to write this review but mall to the drawing board for the best Thai that's comparable to what this place used to be. :-(

I cannot say enough about the owner. She is incredibly sweet, kind, and always smiling. Everyone I've ever dragged here has never had any complaints when leaving. I usually get the pick 8 vegan platter. It is amaze balls. My meat eating friends have all liked it, too

One of my new favorite restaurants! The salmon fish special was magnificent beyond words. I'm telling ya it blew me away. I had always heard their fish specials are dreamy but man it was amazing! Food was fresh and fast! The mango tea was delicious! The garlic knot was so good that I wanted another one. I know a lot of people said stuff about how they use styrofoam or whatever. They use real plates and silverware now so that's not a valid argument anymore. I plan on eating here on a weekly basis because I'm telling ya once you try it you'll be impressed. There was nothing bland about this place! Price was well worth it!

Wow! Ultimately a true Punjabi restaurant in St Louis! I don't have to go to Chicago now! lol Chicken Rogan Josh and Kadhai Lobster were really delicious. The Samosa also was the best I've had in some time. The menu is pretty big and am sure there are lot of great items to be discovered here. (Chicken Sharabi, is something Im curious on) The prices seemed very nominal Faluda kulfi was decent I won't give high rating to the ambience but hey, as long as I'm getting authentic Punjabi food, I swear I won't complain!! Thanks!

So we came here for a Sunday night dinner to enjoy good Mediterranean food + wine. Had Grilled Octopus and Shrimp Pil Pil. I really liked them both. It was first time trying Pil Pil and I am glad I chose it over the scampi. (it has a little spicy kick) For entrees, we had Seafood linguini, Grilled scallops, Steamed seafood platter and Grilled chicken kabab platter. All pretty good. The scallops were my favorite and then the steamed seafood platter since it had everything in the delicious broth. We asked for bread at least 3 times. Lol We were seated right away probably since it was a Sunday night (around 7pm) and the service was great. Food came out pretty fast and of course we enjoyed BYOB. Strongly recommended! The price isn't that bad either. ;)

Great service, food, and price. I came with a party of five, which was too large for the restaurant to accommodate indoors (four or less) - but the outdoor seating in the back garden was cuter anyway. At lunch we ordered the satay (5 skewer) combination, the yellow curry combination, and the spicy fried rice. We were surprised that the combinations came with spring rolls and fried shrimp (we were expecting to make a choice) as well as either soup or salad. In the end we had so many types of food on the table it looked like a feast - and it was all delicious. Our total for all of this plus 5 nonalcoholic drinks was just $55 ($11 each) and we were all satisfied, so it was a great value. Highly recommended!

I Love Sam's on the Beach in Hudson! They have made some beautiful changes, new tables, dressed it up a bit, and the service and food are better than past experiences! Love their Cheesy, spicy grits and Rum Runners are delish! I had the fish and chips and always great! Brought a friend who was visiting from New York for a Gulf view and we had absolutely no complaints, except their seating protocol has changed and it made it a slightly longer wait for open tables because we had to wait for a certain server to seat us instead of anyone being able to seat us. Just a minor complaint. The ice cream in a made to order waffle cone made up for it! :)

We missed this place when it closed on Sansom Street and were happy to find it at its new location. Excellent Afghan food, in a very pleasant environment - which is a definite step up from the "local joint" ambience at the prior location (although that was fine for lunch or very casual early dinner). The service is very pleasant, attentive. BYO. Its a very nice addition to the neighborhood
We ordered delivery from this restaurant and it hit the spot. The sushi was good and the pad thai was pretty good, too. The staff was friendly, delivery was quick and we were happy overall.

Amazing little place! They have so many unique flavors of lassi (yogurt drink) and chaat!!! They had a chicken Tikka Chaat which was amazing! And the lassi was really really good too! The price was also very reasonable. Can't wait to go again when I visit Philly!

I would actually give 3.5. I like the new size and the ambiance is vastly improved by the rehab and expansion. My kids loved everything. The Tom Yom soup was not the correct flavor I have had before, but all of the dishes were very very fresh beautiful ingredients. Dumplings and spring rolls were excellent.. Everything was just a little too bland for Thai, but on the other hand that made everything accessible to my kids. It was very reasonably priced, especially for Thai. Love the BYOB and they even brought me the right kind of glasses for my booze. Very friendly staff. I plan on going back without my kids and asking them to kick it up a notch and see what happens. Maybe they can get me to fork over another star.

Dosa Hut has good service, the best Indian food ever (besides homecooked), is BYOB and has lots of vegetarian options! The ambiance is plain but it just reinforces the overall value of the foods' goodness. A meal here outweighs any cosmetic weakness a critic could dream up. It's simply not a factor after you've had the food. It's a comfortable, low key, cafe-style space and the owner and staff are hospitable with a no-fluff approach to the business of lunch and dinner. After about my fourth time eating here I finally feel like I can give a comprehensive review. But just eat here and find out for yourself. You won't regret trying the lunch specials, the spinach/potato dosa, channa massala, or the fried rice dishes. We can't speak to the meat choices but it sounds like other reviewers recommend them highly.

This is my all time favorite Thai/Laotian restaurant in Philadelphia. I am not much of a salad person, but I absolutely adore all of their different salad dishes here. Papaya Salad, is probably my favorite food...ever. There is the Nam salad (vegetarian) and the Yum salad, which I get with beef that is also very very flavorful and delicious. My favorite entree there is the Pad Kee Mao, similar to the Pad Thai, but it is flat rice noodles with more flavor (in my opinion). More perks: friendly staff, BYOB, perfect place for a date. :)

I was so surprised when I looked this restaurant up on here and it already had 4.5 stars! I feel like it only just opened... but now I see why. Service was great and food was delicious! We will definitely be returning :)

This restaurant has a very unique and exotic food offerings for food in South Tampa. I've never had Ethiopian food in my life, this is my first time eating Ethiopian food. I'm a vegetarian, there's an entire Vegan menu at this restaurant. They serve lots of different vegetable offerings but with familiar ingredients like potatoes, carrots, collared greens, kale, etc. I enjoyed the vegan appetizer plate and the #8 plate, which featured potatoes and carrots. Despite waiting about 30 minutes (not offended, it was a fresh meal) on a friday night, we enjoyed our meal and especially enjoyed Injera. Injera is a type of African bread and it's very similar to a rolled up pancake that's less heavy.

I've been going to Marrakhesh Express every week or two since it opened and can't say enough good things about this place. To me, this is easily the best "ethnic" restaurant in West Philadelphia and one of the top few in the city. The owner is incredibly friendly and lovingly prepares everything himself from scratch based on his own Moroccan recipes from back home. He's extremely proud of his food and with good reason. Unlike so many ethnic restaurants in Philly, the flavors at Marrakhesh Express are not toned down for American palates - this is the real deal prepared by a genuinely excellent chef. This is not generic "Middle Eastern" food, but is uniquely Moroccan, including amazing lamb and chicken tagines that cook for hours until the delicious meat is falling off the bone, and served Moroccan style over a bed of the tastiest fries to soak up the sauce. The homemade Merguez sausage sandwiches are also not to be missed, but I'm yet to go wrong with anything on the menu. On Fridays, Brahim prepares couscous the old school way, cooked for hours with vegetables in a couscousiere. You must eat this. This place deserves to be, and is going to be, packed as soon as The City Paper or Philly Weekly finally gets around to reviewing it, so go now!

Great Ethiopian food. I've only ordered take-out, so I can't comment on the dine-in experience, but anytime I've been there to pick up food I've been taken by the atmosphere and I'm sure I would enjoy eating here. I was close to giving this a five-star rating, there have only been a few times where I wasn't over the moon about the meat they served -- it was good, it just wasn't always QUITE five-star quality. A completely forgivable inconsistency; it never kept me from coming back. The staff is incredibly warm, friendly and fun here. I have since left Tampa, but I miss this place and I definitely recommend it!!

Numchok Wilai, where have you been all my life? This is an awesome place to go if your craving Thai food. Went here on a late Thursday evening and both of us were starving. Place has a nice Thai-style décor to it but man, when we first walked in, the place was hot! Also, there were only a couple of tables occupied...which I thought was pretty surprising. Anyways, for the food, like I said, we were starved so we ordered a couple of dishes to share: - 2x coconut rice ($2 each) - nice and fragrant. Coconut rice was da bomb. - Pad thai ($14) - noodle with shrimp, chicken, egg, bean sprout, green onion and crushed peanuts in a separate tiny side bowl with a lime on the side. Super tasty, slightly on the sweeter side for what I've had pad thai-wise. - Stir fried eggplant ($11) - awesome delicious. Make sure you order this dish! I'm a big fan of eggplant and these were perfectly coked. Came with garlic, carrot, red pepper and basil leaves. - Green curry chicken ($14) - came with bamboo shoots, green and red peppers and basil leaves. Green curry is my fav and this one was excellent. Nice bit of heat to it (maybe it was slightly more spicy than I thought - that's what my friend said) and perfect compliment to go with the rice. I can't stress how good Numchok Wilai is! The front of the restaurant is very deceiving (meaning you'll pass it without even noticing if your not on the lookout for it). And did I mention how fast our food came out? Not even 10 minutes and everything came out piping hot and all at once. Wish I worked nearby so I could get their super cheap lunch deals! GO GO GO. Good talk.

Visited Amber Indian on 11/25/2013. Wonderful food. Can't say enough. Service is fast, your drink is always full, the variety on the buffet is nice. I'd have to agree and say this is one of the best, if not the best, Indian restaurant. Their buffet had all kinds of goodies that would satisfy both vegetarians as well as meat eaters.

Came here recently after grandpa took the kids for an overnight and they don't care for Indian food. My wife and I tried a large variety of appetizers including the Vegetable Pakora (spiced and lightly fried in batter), Vegetable Samosa, and Aloo Tikki (fried spiced patties) along with some Naan. All of the above appetizers were delicious and we felt the Samosa and Tikki had the same insides, but prepared in different manners. The Pakora was not over fried and really tasted nice. For my main meal, I had the Lamb Karahi (w/fresh tomatoes, herbs, and pepper). wife had Chicken Tikka Marsala. I asked for spicy, wife did not. The color was quite a vibrant red with the Tikka Marsala and we both felt it had too much of a cream flavor which was overpowering. After the chicken was all gone, there was still quite a bit of the sauce left. Since I asked for spicy the wife did not even try it. It had a lot of lamb and I felt it could have been even hotter. Tasty, though. As others have said, there is hardly any ambiance here as a sit-down restaurant. Very basic tables, uncomfortable chairs, and a view of some refrigerators for sodas and desserts. There is a television. A few others came in for sit-down meals, but I think this is a better take-out place. Overall, for Indian food this is a good choice!

so amazing! love the food choices. really healthy and the prices aren't too bad. definitely is not fast food...maybe more like quick dishes because this is too healthy and yummy to be called fast food. I love Zoe's! everyone try this place out you won't regret it! their spinach and chicken roll ups are amazing and their iced teas are too good. instead of going to panera. go here!!!
Eastern Mediterranean version of chipotle. Very good fast food. Worth the quick bite. Careful of the hot sauce

Used to eat here when it was Zayna's, now it's under new management...still same great food. Husband gets the gyro and fries, I get the chicken shwarma and fries - both excellent! Staff and owner are very friendly. Will be trying their breakfast next - lots of great options.

The person who took and served our order was someone who has always been so nice to us, but not today. There was a hair in the breading on one piece of chicken (Sweet & Sour Chicken). We asked him if it looked like a hair to him, he said NO, it was off a brush that was used for the coating. I've been cooking for over 40 years and you "dip" the chicken pieces in coating you don't "brush" the coating on!!!! This server immediately showed anger when we pulled the coating away from the chicken piece he could plainly see that it was a hair. He raised his voice and angrily asked what we wanted him to do about it! We explained we just wanted them to be aware of this hair, it could happen again. At this point, now we are upset because of his rude response. This escalated to the manager coming over. I have been to this restaurant many times and have never seen this kind of unprofessional behavior. We will NEVER go back there. He was obviously having a BAD day, and we just happened to be the catalyst to the explosion!

I found the Bryn Mawr PA location by accident I was actually going for Mexican lol found this place and I have had lunch there 3 times this week love this place the staff are so friendly and the food is awesome it is so fresh and healthy. Highly recommend this place their chicken salad is amazing

I have been to the Thai House two other times . It is wonderful ! I went with a friend this time and tried their spring rolls and a sweet potato puff ( the name is not correct, sorry) as apps. For the main entree I had the Angel chicken and my friend had the Cashew chicken . We had the Thai iced coffee to drink . All of it was wonderful . The food was so fresh and seasoned to perfection . The coffee was smooth, creamy , sweet perfection, they need to bottle it . I would by them out . I will be back soon I am sure .

We need to branch out and try more here. The people who work here are always friendly and eager to make sure you enjoy your food. We generally order the lemon grass tofu ban mi. The vegetables and herbs are fresh, bright, and crisp. The tofu has a great texture and nice complex but enjoyable flavor. The bread it's on? Light and crisp on the outside, nice soft and chewy on the inside. Really delicious! I'm so glad to have this great place in west Nashville.

This is my favorite carribean spot! All of their food is delicious. The only reason they don't get a 5 star review from me is because they run out of beef patties way too fast and the wait time is ungodly sometimes. But other than that the food is sooo delicious that I will wait for it. And the prices are great for the amount of food you get a small platter can easily feed 2 people or be used as two meals!

I really like this little hole-in-the-wall place my sister introduced me to...I like their chicken banh mi's with everything on top, but also their special and vegetarian ones are awesome too. I think the highlight is really the bread...it's crispy and the crust gets everywhere so be careful eating it in your car if you care about that kind of thing :) I wouldn't say it's the best banh mi I've ever had, but pretty close! (Fu-Wah is a close competitor...) Plus, the owners are super nice, and humble too. Try to swing by here if you're in the area!

After reading the other posts, I had to double-check to make sure this was the same place. Maybe there were more changes than just location when they moved from St. Pete to Gulfport. I did not visit Tangelos at their old location so maybe that explains the discrepancy in my visit versus the other posts. Here's the good: Decent location, friendly staff, fantastic drinks. Some of the best Sangria I've had in a long time. The bad: the food. I ordered the daily special, a shrimp po-boy. It was served with a side of rice and beans. Maybe it's me, but I expect a daily special to be filled with fresh ingredients. The shrimp were frozen popcorn shrimp. Serious. Not just frozen shrimp but the cheap popcorn shrimp with more breading than anything that actually resembles shrimp. They put a ton of these pseudo-shrimp on the sandwich but unfortunately they weren't anything I wanted to eat. The side of rice and beans were sub-par. They came with an overabundance of onions on top. I get onions on top of black beans and rice but this was a little much. Maybe it was an attempt to add some sort of flavor to the beans that tasted like they came straight from a can? My husband had the conch fritters and soup. The fritters were a miss. Some were almost well-done and others were undercooked. Not good. I don't recall which soup my husband ordered but it was off as well. Neither of us could place what was wrong with it but it wasn't anything either of us wanted to eat. While it is possible that other menu items provide a different experience, overall I felt like I had just paid to eat a meal full of yucky processed foods. It didn't feel or taste as if there was anything actually cooked on site, just reheated from a can or fried from a bag. Nothing fresh on the plate. Would I go back? Eh, probably not. Maybe for a glass of sangria at one of the tables outside but certainly not for the food.

I've come here several times for the lunch buffet. It is very nicely done with many great options. The vegetable curries are my favorite, especially the cabbage one! Some of the food doesn't retain its original texture while being kept warm on the buffet line, particularly the naan (which is the case with pretty much ANY bread on ANY buffet), but is excellent if you get the opportunity to snag some when it's brought out fresh. You could also buy some as a side order to make sure you get a warm, fluffy piece. I also really look forward to the samosas and chutney here. For those of you used to the presence of strong Indian spices and heat, you may find the buffet a bit bland, but may have good luck with ordering off the menu instead.

Incredible night at Zeppoli! First, it very small. They don't try to fit more people in than it can handle, but some of the seats are very close together. We were very lucky to get a same day reservation, and even luckier to get a 4-person table as a couple. I was very happy about that! There was a duo of muscians playing last night, which we both really enjoyed. I felt like I was in The Godfather, in a completely complimentary way. Service was very friendly and accomidating. Our waiter, Tom, was very kind and knowledgable. We appreciated his good service. Wine was opened quickly, glasses of water presented, and we ordered a cask of the orange bloosm lemonade. It was AMAZING! A really nice treat for an expecting lady :) We had 2 appetizers, small pasta courses, in additon to our mains. We enjoyed the complimentary olives and bread. I had the artichoke special, and my husband had the Finocchi Salsiccia. Mine was nicely baked with lemon, cheese, and a dot of red sauce. It was perfect for me, artichokes were nice and juicy. It was fairly large. My husband was raving about Finocchi Salsiccia. The rabe was delish, we were fighting over the last pieces. It had 3 large pieces that were very hot and nicely grilled. We could have left happy after just the first course. Next, we each had a small Gnocchi pasta course: Gnocchi alla' Argentiera and the special that night, with calamari and peas. They were very different, but both very good. The Gnocchi alla' Argentiera was out of this world. The brown butter sauce was incredible, and the gnocchi themselves have been correctly descibed by other yelp'ers as little fluff pieces from heaven. I had a 2nd small pasta as my main: Tagliatelli al Limone with prosciutto. I have never had it before, and it is my new favorite. Just the right amount of salt from the prosciutto, and I loved the fresh lemon flavor. I was completely stuffed by the time I finished it. My husband had the rabbit, which he enjoyed. It was fork-tender, and dressed with a nice red sauce. I could not find room for dessert, but I did sneak a piece of his Zeppoli. The smell was too good to resist. Overall, we had a very romantic and enjoyable experience. We can't wait to share Zeppoli with our families!

The food was decent, if a little bland, and we didn't quite get what we ordered, and the bread wasn't as good as we had hoped for. I think it wasn't that fresh, and it definitely wasn't warm. We were also there at a funny time. While the staff was trying hard, they were obviously distracted by other duties. The recycled Chapalas booths are amusing. We may try it again during a more "normal" time of day.

Thank you for smiling! What a way to be greeted every time you walk in the door! Love the chicken gyro, the tzatziki is phenomenal and so flavorful. Great tabbouleh. And the hummus is fantastic. I just love this place so much and highly recommend. Great for take out (ready in 15 mins normally!) and on our regular rotation!

I've found better Pho elsewhere, but the Bun Bo Hue is pretty delicious here. It's a bit different from the one at Saigon, enough so that I practically consider them different dishes. The dining room is small, and the seats by the window are cold in the winter, but the service is pretty friendly and the soups are quite large. This is definitely on my regular rotation of vietnamese restaurants in the Indy area.
Best Vietnamese in town. I love the combo plates wgere they serve you the rice wrappers and you can make your own spring rolls at the table a great event of eating.

Who said you have to eat gumbo and oysters in New Orleans??? What a great little find. Authentic Vietnamese food served hot and delicious! Started out with the grilled pork spring rolls which were fresh fresh fresh. Also had an order of the pot stickers which were delicious. End of the meal with the stirfry pork noodles with egg, salad and soup. stop in today and eat at this wonderful little restaurant!
1hr 1/2 or more waiting for food to be delivered. "Fried rice " more like cooked rice with a few pieces of onion and carrot. Overall not worth the wait.

Great food, ehhh service, cute ambiance. I gave this place a 3 namely because our waitress was kind of quick and impatient, but overall, everything else was pretty nice. Great place for first dates (unless you're into a bougie-er atmosphere :) or small group meetings. Very dimly lit inside. Don't get the octopus like I did (unless your're into chewing the hell out of your meet :). Try the leg of lamb!! They were VERY good with splitting the check 7 ways. And there you have it. Short, sweet and hopefully helpful :)

Went here for a late lunch. The crab rangoon is great and the only problem is figuring out how to split 5 of them between 2 people! I got the bimbop, which was more than enough food. My gf got the shrimp vermicelli, and I'd probably get that next time instead (don't tell her that).

decor is nice. Took a long time to get our appetizer though. We ordered pita with feta dip. The pita was fantastic: thin, with sesame seeds. The cheese dip was okay but a bit too overpowered by the salt. The entrees were good and those didn't take too long to come after our appetizer. Expensive but the meats were flavourful and you get a decent amount of sides to fill you up. Overall, great place if you don't mind possibly waiting a while for your appetizer and paying in the $20s and $30s for your entrée.
Butter chicken was really good, came with rice and nan. Easy and convenient location. Looking forward to going back and trying other items on the menu.

My daughter and I went here for lunch today. The interior is beautiful, bright, and modern. We ordered cocktails (highly recommend-white cosmo and 3 springs mule) and our drinks were yummy as well as pretty. We started with avocado toast without the crab, and it was very good. My daughter had the blt and I had a Margherita pizza. The blt was the best I've ever tasted, made with homemade bread that was made in house and heirloom tomatoes. The pizza dough was so light and also made in house. The crust was as good as the rest of it, super delicious! Our server was Liz and she was excellent. We will be back!

So we've heard that this is a great Chinese restaurant, and had to try it. Somewhat surprised to find, yet another, decent restaurant on Kietzke Lane (actually on Mill). The restaurant was clean and the food was good. But I didn't think it was anything better than just good. I enjoyed my sesame shrimp. They have a luncheon special which offers "soup of the day" and entree. Every Chinese restaurant I've ever gone to you have an option of the hot and sour or egg drop soup. Their "soup of the day" was simply hot and sour soup and if you wanted the egg drop soup it would be $3 extra (come on... they must have a vat egg drop soup in the kitchen at all times). And in their effort to be efficient (or just plain fast), it is somewhat annoying when they take you plate away while you are holding your egg roll over your empty plate. Would I eat there again... sure, the food was good, the place was clean even if the service was a bit overzeaous.

a review by www.fitwithdelicious.com (Food and Health Blog), who went in search for diet style kabobs.. Appearance : With few tables and chairs.. It will not be much pleasing.. But, neat. Excellent Tasting Food : Tandoori Platters, Naan and Kabobs.. They have a good variety of starters.. Their Seekh and Chapli - Outstanding.. Moderately Tasting : All the Gravies.. They are medium spiced and sweet at times.. I never suggest you to order a gravy here.. Below Average Tasting : Biriyani.. Yes, I will visit this restaurant for the second time for their Kabobs(very very less oil).. I feel takeaway is a better option than having it right there.. We found it slightly difficult to park the vehicle..

Quantity over quality. Big portions of pho but average tasting. While there is some sheen there isn't that delicious fatty sheen on really good pho. This place is like a chipotle for pho except instead of picking what you want through a case, you do so on a kiosk before waiting for your number to be called and receiving your bowl on a brightly covered tray. The atmosphere is a dorm cafeteria vibe. If you want real Mexican food, you don't go to chipotle. If you want real pho, maybe don't come here. Don't get me wrong it's still good but it definitely does not taste like the love put into some dishes in a real, hole in the wall delicious pho spot where grandma is in the back making the good stuff. If you're drunk or are aching like a fiend for some basic pho, this big bowl will do the trick.
First time here and I was disappointed. Tea tastes instant not brewed and phyllo was tough on my spanakopita. Close to work so I'll try again; hope it improves.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I've been going here since it was located on the corner of 5-mile and Fairview. Very good indian food. Fresh Nan, wonderful spices, and I loved their Tandoori. They have notorious slow service, but it's worth it. The Owner is very friendly and has a good sense of humor. The decor and atmosphere has changed a lot, most for the better. I do miss the Indian dance videos in the background when I eat.

WONDERFUL. I hail from Phoenix, where Vietnamese restaurants are on every other corner. Now I live in Terre Haute and I crave good restaurants. I was really excited to come here, and it fulfilled all my expectations. I got the lemongrass chicken dish (basically making your own spring rolls) and my partner got the Shaky Steak. Both were excellent. The waiter was very helpful, kind, and friendly. Perfect food, perfect service. The place was clean, fast, and delicious. No complaints.

It pains me to write this review. When I saw a Thai place steps from my apartment I couldn't wait to try it. And when I saw the yelp reviews I was ecstatic. I judge a Thai place on pad Thai, yeah that's right! its a staple dish that clues you in on the rest of the dishes. I used to order in once a week while living in Boston because they have great ethnic food options (*sigh*)... I noticed comments about vegan/veggie options. Although this is true, most places will accommodate if you ask (again, at least in Boston they have). I ordered tofu/veggie pad Thai, spicy. To-Go. The veggies were obviously not fresh/overcooked. The tiny pieces of tofu were overcooked and chewy. The noodles were more on the dry side (which is fine) but the sauce lacked depth and was overpowered by the red sauce they used to make it spicy (sriracha??). The Tom Yum soup smelt like sweaty gym socks and was out right disgusting. I couldn't even eat it. No idea what made it that way but it could have been the shrimp because when I ate the shrimp it tasted off. The lady on the phone and at the restaurant was nice but the prices are higher than other Thai places I've seen around. I'd probably try something else on the menu, just to give it another shot, but I'd bet its not going to be much better. I'd suggest you go somewhere else.

We can walk there so obviously it's a great choice for us. Food is fine - last visit it was actually very good. And spicy as requested. However waaaay overpriced for the portion size. Three solid stars and an additional star but the great kids menu. I miss our Thai favorites from when we lived in DC but being able to walk there and the nice kids offerings makes it a perfectly passable place. The apple salad is excellent. Update: sitting down to take out, items ordered are missing. Vegetarian ordered items have meat. Super disappointed. Be sure to check everything on your way out.

I spent a couple of hours at Tryst with some friends, and we all loved it. The place is beautifully decorated and the vibe, and service are superb. I had a mojito, which was not the best I've had, but was not terrible. My friend had a drink, which I thought would be fruity, but was outstanding. Love the sidewalk seating!
Good food. The service wad OK. I really enjoyed the noodles. It's in a really good spot. It's small so don't expect to bring a big crowd but good for a nice date.
Awesome place. Got the Caribbean jerk chicken w/ rice & beans and plantains. Was just passing through and saw this place. Staff was super nice too!
Homey atmosphere with excellently fresh food. We had the butter chicken, vegetable samosas, lamb saag, naan, and gulab jaman for dessert. We will definitely come back, and try their tandori chicken.

I can't believe we haven't been to this place before! The food is delicious and the ingredients fresh. The place itself feels like a piece of Thailand, beautiful and intricate decorations - not cheesy at all. Service is fast and very friendly. We had Thai butterfly, cucumber salad, tom kha as appetizers. Especially the cucumber salad was outstanding, I would come back just for that. Chicken pad Thai and drunken noodles as entrees...the pad Thai was a bit boring (add some chili flakes and additional peanuts to it), but the drunken noodles delicious. I definitely recommend this place and can't wait to go back to try the curries! ..... Updated review: the curries are now my favorite. Chu Chee curry mmhhhh, spicy and delicious!

The novelty of a dark, smoky Moroccan den is tainted by the sub-par food and terrible service. Been here twice and twice was enough to get my fill. Pass through the painted and cracked glass doors to enter a dark, vaguely musty room draped in velvet tapestries, thick dingy curtains and bordered by plush, half-moon couches and low metal tables. An 8-course menu, at $25 per person, is a fairly traditional offering, though lacking in any sort of distinguished flavor. You can order a hookah here (also $25) in a dozen fruity flavors; possibly the biggest draw. It's relaxing to sink back into the cushions, inhale deeply and pretend you're the caterpillar from Alice in Wonderland. Whoooo are youu? It appears servers are hard to come by during dinner service, as are any drinks from the bar. Savor the first glass of water they bring, as it may be your only. Sure, you'll enjoy the novelty of washing your hands in rosewater tableside and later eating with flat breads, sans utensils. A bellydancer may briefly sashay through the aisles on Saturday night and underage diners may be slipped a glass of wine. That could entice you, sure. And true, your meal will feature uncommon dishes by American standards, like lamb with honey or chicken wrapped in sweet, powdered pastry -- but in the end the food is lacking real spice, flavor and memorable taste. It's average, and just so. You'll do better at Marrakesh in all senses.

I'm Vietnamese, and I can say that their food is authentic vietnamese. I travel to large cities and eat at other vietnamese restaurants, and I can say that this vietnamese restaurant is just as good, if not better, than other places. I come here often for their pho.

I have been here for both lunch and dinner. Love the atmosphere of the place. I loved their tom kha coconut soup. The eggplant salad was interesting, tasted botanical. Any way, this place is worth a try if you are in the mood for Thai food.

The food and hookah were fine, but what upset me was the fact that despite having an eye injury and being visually impaired from a car accident, I was told to remove my sunglasses otherwise I wouldn't be allowed inside the establishment. The lady saw my bruises and injuries but said if she let me inside with sunglasses, she'd have to let others do the same thing...despite the fact that it was the middle of the night. I won't be returning.
Solid pho offerings and other specialty bites. I like the meatball pho the best and find the atmosphere modern but warm. Great place for a cold day, girlfriend lunch.
I had the mahi mahi with pita chips. Very good, but I could have used a little more fish. The mashed potatoes were great. Service was good.

The Chicken Shawarma was mediocre. The meat is not sliced to order, like it would be at any other Mediterranean restaurant that I have ever been to. Instead, the meat was sliced in advance in very small pieces, and it is sitting in a warming tray, for who knows how long, until a customer orders it. I doubt that I would eat here again given all of the other nearby restaurants in the King of Prussia Town Center.

Tonight we called our order in ahead to help speed dinner along for our kids. Noodi went above and beyond to accommodate our kids when we arrived. They served our Pad Thai in a large bowl, because they knew we would be serving our children "family style". I am pretty sure the serving size was twice as big as what we have had in the past. They were so kind and helpful. We will definitively return again soon.
Ekta is a local mini-chain that serves pretty good Indian food. This spot is BYOB. All of the classics are good - Saag Paneer, Malai kabob, lamb vindaloo, etc.

We tried a ban mi as well as the pho. Both were good and best of all unique for an area lined with every chain restaurant under the sun. The ambience leaves something to be desired but service makes up for it. A much better alternative to endless string of Avon choices serving "chicken fingers & fries"!

The environment is great. The food are well-decorated. I hope they have bigger portion but I have my fill with Thai Tea. Overall, the place is great. I am just disappointed with a mosquito stuck on the plate. It is mildly disgusting.

This was a great experience. I had never had Ethiopian food and I found it and the atmosphere quite enjoyable. There was a large party next to me and the staff was as attentive to them as my table and the others that were dining. Customer service is very important to me and the wait staff delivered. My funny moment was that I thought the bread they bring out to scoop up the food was towels. Yes, it's either the bread or use your fingers. I opted to use my fingers after a while as I did not like the taste of the bread. The food on the other hand was awesome. I had the goat dishes and thoroughly everything I had. The seasoning was great and definitely look forward to my next trip there.
