Very unpleasant, disinterested and unhelpful service - a hostility unlike anything I have ever experienced in a restaurant so highly rated by Yelp. I asked if they had saag chat, and the man behind the counter looked at me like I was speaking Chinese. "Spinach chat?" I translated. It was all he could do to wave at the menu board, which in no way explained what each dish had. When we paid, it took him several minutes to be able to change the $20 bill for our order. Once the owner arrived (after we had ordered), this same man suddenly became friendly. STAY AWAY -- there is a lot more friendly food just down the street at Aksum. They don't hate the customer!!
This is probably my favorite pho place in town. They have a fantastic service and a wide range of menu selections including Thai. Really great service as well. I will definitely be coming back here.

Everything I have ever gotten from Siam Cafe has been great. Service is always good. I have been coming for years and will continue to for as long as I am in Nashville. Best Thai in town. Don't let the shabby looks of the place fool you. Definitely try the Tom Kai soup it's amazing.

I am a huge fan of pho and, coming from the west coast, have had my fair share. In my opinion, the pho here is authentic, except it is a hit or miss. I ordered the same thing on two different days and the first time the soup was very diluted, but the second time was perfect. I would not recommended getting grilled meat with pho and do NOT get chicken, as in both cases the meat is dry and overcooked. If a first timer, go for the deluxe..dont let the tripe scare you! It takes on the flavor of the delicious broth. Also, portion sizes are impressive and prices are reasonable for the area. I'm glad to see this in the area and hope they work on their consistency.

FYI: Spicy scale is 1-4 So this is a nice little place off the state st. -the main street in downtown Media (its a cool lil town check it out if you haven't). I've been multiple times, with many take outs in the past year. This place is great for an easy dinner or when you have a curry craving. Staff is usually warm and nice. Sometimes service is a little slow when they are working with alot of pick up orders, but when in good company its generally not a bother. I've had multiple items off the menu. The curry is good. Their peanut sauce is perfect. The mango curry is super tasty! They offer an early bird special which is a great deal, soup half appetizer and entree. The rice is always spot on and fresh. Best of all they usually don't charge us for substituting or adding extra sauces. I'll admit some of the appetizers do have some inconsistency in pricing, but all of them are under 9 dollars which is great. Great for those living in town. Its definitely a casual joint, they have a big paper light star in the window, signs up with tape. So no candle light romance here, just good food. Public street parking, public lot around the corner. Easy to get to.

2 of us went for lunch however, we left without being seated. The hostess said there were 4 tables available but the manager said not to seat them because the kitchen was too busy. She then proceeded to seat a table of 10-12 who came in after us. Seriously?!?! We will have to think long and hard before we want to subject ourselves to that ignorance! Food may be good but the management sucks!

Order Delivery and I couldn't believe they delivered to Fishtown. I'm sick so all I wanted was soup. But there's a $15 min for Delivery so I ordered Wonton Soup, Seaweed Tofu soup with Vegetable, and Basil Fried Rice. The wonton soup was BOMB DIGGITY!!! Get it. And you can probably get it delivered!
A really bad place. Food is super sweet and sticky, not even remotely what Thai food should be
We had a delicious authentic Thai dinner here last night. All foodies must check it out. Kind of an odd location but worth finding.

Lots of pretty people, great drinks, and a great beer selection. The do also sell food, imaginative small plates. A little pricey, but worth it. Always a great place to people watch for pretty ladies.

If you are looking for some good Dominican food this is the place nice and fast service! The price is amazing won't regret it I take my hot sauce with me because they only have mild Other than that it's great

Really mixed...fundamentally I don't think it my kind of food - the seasonings, the sauces, etc. We took my adult daughter protesting. Her husband and I were more open to it. Wednesday night quiet at the restaurant and no one watching front of the house and seating people. Finally seated on patio which is nice. Ordered nachos. the kids ate them but said they weren't what they expected. Their steak wrap and black bean burger were delivered but they weren't excited by them. My seared tuna with fruit and Vinaigrette were outstanding. I never would have paired the tuna with fruit. But that being said, one out of three happy customers isn't enough so we won't be returning.

This place was delicious!!! We ordered the special "ginger stir fry" and it was fantastic! The small Japanese mushrooms were really yummy and made me feel like I was eating real authentic Thai food. They give you complimentary little rice chips and a red sauce which was a good palette cleanser to start. We ordered the fried egg rolls which came out steaming hot and delicious! I also ordered a papaya salad which came with cabbage and a side of rice in a cute bamboo container. We also ordered the basil stir fry which had a delicious natural basil flavor! During our meal, the waitresses were all willing to help out and the manager went around asking tables if they needed anything. She was an adorable little lady. Overall, the place seemed very clean (don't judge the book by its cover-- the outside is in an older plaza) and had a wonderful atmosphere. I took a take out menu for the future. Delicious!
Basil fried rice is bomb. Everything looks delicious. I'll be picking up from here frequently
This is such a great family owned establishment. We've been going here for years. The food is great with such a welcoming atmosphere. Love the pad Thai here! Highly recommended!

I was visiting Philadelphia for a week long training in King of Prussia. I visited Ron's last June and I have dreamt about it ever since! One knows that whenever the lines are long you k ow the food is worth it! I'm a foodie and this place did not disappoint. Freshness, good seasoning, and delicious. The worst thing is I live in Maryland.

Wow!! This noodle soup is the most delicious I have ever had. I always go for #30 - roasted pork and wonton with egg noodles. It is to die for, perfect on a cold night. We also enjoy the grilled chicken meat rolls, spring rolls, and shrimp rolls. My fiance loves their clay pot chicken too. I wasn't sure what Vietnamese cuisine would entail, but it feels like a healthier version of Chinese food. The very friendly staff can give you suggestions if you're not sure what to order. I love having this restaurant up the street. This winter it's made many cold nights much better with a bowl of noodle soup!
Delicious and quick. The buffet helps you get in and out even faster. Not much sitting area inside, but I doubt most people stay there to eat like I did.

This unpretentious little place is stuck in the middle of a down-scale strip mall (or, no, it's too small for a mall; it's just a strip of shops), but don't let the location fool you. There's good food to be had here. I had the buffet lunch, reasonable at $6.95, and enjoyed the food, but I can't rave about it. Tandoori chicken was dry and stringy, and the vegetable dishes were mundane, as if mixed from a box of Tasty Bites from Trader Joe's. Not bad, just unremarkable. The server, though, a young woman who said she was new, was fabulous, constantly checking to see if we needed more naan, more tea, more water, anything at all. She was impressively trying to do a good job. I too loved the Bollywood videos playing at the back of the place. The decor was fine, and the videos--combined with the fragrance of exotic spices and a nose-full of curry--completed the escape-to-another-planet idea. The naan (choice of garlic or plain) came fresh and hot from the kitchen within minutes of our sitting down. I'd go back for the bread alone; no, for the bread and the music; and a jug of wine and thou . . . (only kidding . . .). I still need to visit "the other" Indian restaurant, India Kabob, for a comparison, as others seem to like it very much. Till then, I hope to enjoy Taste of India again because of the attentive service, the OK but good dishes at a fair price, the great bread, and the wail of the music in the background.

Stopped on the way back to California from Las Cruces about lunch time. the place was about 1/3 full. It's off the beaten path as it's not near the freeway but not so far away. Lots of vegetarian choices and settled on a black bean burger. The black bean patty was a little bland but the rest of the burger (bun, tomato, lettuce) made up for it. Had to put on some mustard as the cook didn't put enough spread on the burger. I'd give the burger 2.5 out of 5 stars. The potato's that came with the burger were awesome though and the seasoning and spices had amazing flavor. Someone in our group had a falafel and said it was the best they had ever tasted. I should have gotten that instead. The service was good as the waitress was very attentive and refilled our drinks more than once. Very comfortable atmosphere with wait to be seated hostess when you walk through the door. I would say it's a bit more middle class and not a place to get a quick bite fast food style. Very nice. Food came quickly

The pho was so watered down, it's not beef broth for sure, I think it's chicken broth that I had to make my own seasoning to make it edible but it can't help. I would never go back to this restaurant again.

We've had take out from here before in the past, and it has been decent. However, we dined in for the first (and last) time last week. Our waitress forgot multiple different items throughout our meal, even after multiple reminders. Our food was mediocre at best. The icing on the cake, though, was the mouse running around the dining room that the employees seemed to think added to the ambiance. We'll stick to King and I...or literally any other restaurant we've ever been to...before going back.

This place has really good fusion food. My love is in the Kim chi burger with sweet potatoes fries. It has good flavor and the Kim chi does not overpower the burger. The Pho here is really good too! The place has a very modern vibe to it. The staff are very friendly. All in all a really good place to try.

Delicious, quick service, lots of options for lunch. My family enjoyed the bowl and the salad, all with chicken. We also had the french fries and pita- so good. The fries had a great blend of seasoning on top, but we did have them without the cheese. There was lots of indoor and outdoor seating, although the location was a little interesting. The food was ready quickly and the portion size was good for the price, which seems hard to find in Nashville. Overall, a great place for a fast and filling lunch.

This place is legit! We had a big group so I got to try a couple of different items that the gang ordered. Their beef noodle soup can give the Thai Temple a run for their money. You definitely have to try the stuffed chicken wing appetizer! The Pad Thai is straight from Thailand.

I am vietnamese. This is my least favorite of all the vietnamese restaurants in the indy area. There have always been rumors of behind the scenes msg use, dirty kitchen, people getting sick after eating there etc. Too many rumors for me to get excited about going. I've had the pho there in the past and it never tastes quite right. The same family owns the grocery next door which is why I try to avoid that parking lot altogether but I'll spare details for the grocery's seperate review. Price is okay and alot of people gather here and because of it's name I notice a lot of american people come here to try out vietnamese cuisine for the first time. Most of the other Vietnamese restaurants are country-neutral as they also serve Chinese food there so you wouldn't be able to tell that they specialize in Vietnamese cuisine. Saigon was the Capitol of Vietnam until Communist took it over and renamed it. The southerns still call it Saigon. For some viet people they come for the convenience of lunch and groceries next door. My tip is to have lunch elsewhere and get your groceries at one of the other 6 international/asian grocery stores on the same road. I give it 2 stars because if I was craving viet food and this was the last place still open i'd probably still try and go. Well lucky for me there are at least 5 other restaurants within driving distance that I would choose.

P.F. Chang's. In a city and suburbs overpopulated with Chinese restaurants of all calibers, one could easily wonder, "Why P.F. Chang's?" After eating there, one will definitely ask that question. I imagine intergalactic aliens landing for a brief time, just long enough to wait 40 minutes for their buzzer to buzz, be seated, and eat at P.F.Chang's, a needlessly two hour process. They eat, zoom off in their starship, and think, "Hmmm. so that was Chinese food?" Then I'd imagine a great race for the only toilet on the ship, as the comically-applied doses of oil hit them. What the hell is it with this place and oil? Do they have stock in peanut oil futures? To start with, your waitstaff will come to the table with a tray holding three bottles of colored liquids. In front of each bottle is a small dish, each also containing three colored liquids. Your waitstaff will mumble through some memorized incantation, inaudible to anyone at the table mostly because the noise in the place sounds like a dozen ice-cream trucks just pulled up in front of recess at an elementary school fro starving children, and mix into the center bowl, a small portion of colored liquids from the other two bowls. If you're waiting for a magic trick, here it comes: the liquid in the center bowl then gets stirred up, and it CHANGES COLOR! Then the tray is left on your table for the rest of the meal, with nobody having the slightest idea of why it's there in the first place, what's in the three bottles, what was in the two outside bowls, and what is now in the center bowl that has received the magic spell. They might be sauces or components for sauces, they might be oils, but who needs more of that with this food? Maybe they're massage oils. Nobody knows. They can't be dipping sauces since there's nothing into which can be dipped into them. Are they finger sauces? Nobody knows. Ancient Chinese secret. No one tell. It Big Mystery. Our waitress was terrible, slow in coming, hard to find during the meal, and was certainly not happy when we returned all three dishes, after finally finding her to tell her that nothing was hot, not even the dried-out rice. Before the entreés arrived, we ate two of the worst egg rolls I've ever had; small, soggy, tasteless, and filled with what looked like recently mown grass. And at the price they charged, I felt as if they should have come with options in those peanut oil futures. So...the food? Nobody was thrilled. As mentioned,the food is swimming in oil, fine tasting but nothing special, and not close to worth the price. It's so easy to get better Chinese food at half the price in a third the time...why bother with this dump? After all that, I would like to mention the one redeeming factor about eating at P.F. Chang's. If I ever think of one, I'll let you know. Go anywhere else.

Fun evening with adventures in Trinidadian food. Our server was excellent, knowledgeable and personable. The food was a real revelation, truly a crossroads of cultures. BYOB with nice ambiance, reasonable prices and generous portions. Loved the ice cream tartuffes! Definitely worth a return visit.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We had the lunch buffet - and it was amazing. Got there right as the place opened and they apologized for taking a minute to have everything out - but we got everything warm and had a mango lassi for the few minutes we waited. The fresh Naan with oil was absolutely fantastic and we were stoked to be having high quality Indian food in Idaho - the owners carried a great conversation with us and really helped the ambiance by being so available and caring.
Amazing food and they accommodated a very large party, service was great and their homemade greek yogurt for dessert was perfection

Delicious dishes, outstanding cocoanut cake for dessert, service was friendly, prompt, and informative, water glasses constantly refilled. Seating a little tight, but a popular place, and a lively room. Very pleasant experience.

So my friend and I were walking around Rittenhouse on a weekday night looking for food options, and this cute establishment beckoned us to come in!! We were seated quickly, but after that the service was mediocre even though there wasn't much of a crowd! We got the crispy spring rolls to share, and they were A-OK and lacked seasoning! For mains, I got the green curry with veggies and tofu and they were definitely not worth the price I paid for it!! I mean, I had no leftovers, one thing that always happens to me at Thai restaurants as the portions are generous! Overall, this place needs an uplift with regards to their seasoning and portion size to make a stronger mark in the culinary world of Rittenhouse Square!

Really great salad dressing! Awesome service. The chef is very friendly. All the food was delicious. Had the lamb targine and my wife had the shrimp provincial. All great, lamb literally fell off the bone. You need to visit this place if u are in the area. Very nice and relaxing atmosphere as well. Can't go wrong here.
They must have changed their chef, the food tastes horrible and not at all close to how it used to be #yuck

I went here in good Friday, so unfortunately I didn't get to try the beef shwarma, but it looked fantastic! I did have a falafel pita. They menu is a little difficult to navigate but the girl at the counter was able to help my boyfriend and I make some decisions. The pita I had was delicious and not too messy like they usually can be. I was tempted to order grape leaves to go but I was too full after my meal. This is definitely a cozy lunch spot to check out in manayunk for great Mediterranean!
Good food. Great employees. Prices are a little high. I suggest that they have a punch card for those who go there frequently (5 visits for a 50% off your next meal or something like that).

Tried this place out only because my favorite pho place is closed on Tuesdays. Had Bun Bao. It wasn't good at all and there wasn't enough lime or basil to kill the smell of the broth. The meat was tough and inedible. My husband had the house special pho, which he ate reluctantly. The salad we ordered with noodles and peanuts was dull and flavorless. The server was polite, ergo the two stars. Won't be going back.

Some of the best Indian food I've had and definitely the best in the area. Service was fantastic and prompt. The butter chicken was delicious but came out a little more spicy than anticipated. The basmati rice was also buttery and fluffy. Don't forget the Naan, it was as light as air and fantastic. Unexpected delight in a strip mall near the turnpike.
Freaking delicious!!!! I spent a year in Italy, where Turkish döner is everywhere. This is as real as it gets. I'm so happy!!! The owner is so nice and the food is fresh made to order. Go there now!!

This particular restaurant has a nice atmosphere and is quite comfortable. The food was well prepared and delicious. Nice ingredients and flavor. Servings are moderate, however the Pad Thai is the smallest serving size I have ever received in a Thai restaurant, in this country or in Thailand. The sequencing and timing of the food coming out of the kitchen was poor, totally confused and entirely syncopated. We mentioned it to our servers which didn't seem to make any difference. The fault most likely lies with the management and kitchen staff. There doesn't seem to be a prescribed plan of how to sequence the food service. We had ordered food for six. Several salades, pad thai, several curies and the spicy eggplant. The first items to arrive at the table were the pad thai. Perhaps 5 minutes later followed by the curry, then in another 5 minutes the salad and in another 5 minutes the eggplant. The food as I mentioned was great. The service was average to poor. The atmosphere was nice. A tricky one to rate.

This is the place to go if you do not want a long drive to Philly. Their food here is very good. Their pho and rice platters are amazing. I wish they would have options on their drinks here but overall. This place is very good.
Joe the bartender waited on us. Super nice guy. Shrimp fried rice was good. Joe made it worth the trip :). Definitely worth the trip.

Loved it! Nice modern interior although a little too dim. The tomato cappellini I had was delicious! complimentary bread basket had a great selection of white, olive and pita breads. We sat at a semi-private booth, which I highly recommend. Only thing that kept me from rating a 5 is their vegetarian options are very limited.

One of the best kept secrets of Chinatown? I found this restaurant to be highly satisfactory on all levels for lunch. First, they do a lunch special menu, about $11 which includes small lettuce salad, starter (I got the 2 veggie spring rolls), and entree (Panang curry with tofu). I liked the curry, which had several very fresh vegetables in it, not at all over cooked. The curry itself was spicy, but not too much, and had a nice lightness to it. Not at all heavy. Note: they also serve brown rice ($1 extra), so I was pleased they don't serve only white rice. The staff was incredibly nice, and the food arrived at our table promptly. I'll be back.

Excellent Thai/Pan Asian food. Friendly staff and great quality food. Seating can be difficult during peak times but it is totally worth the wait. Moderately priced. Portions are large enough to have great leftovers the next or after. Spicy levels are from 1-5 and are very noticeable between the levels. For me and my family, we look no further than Aroy. Everything on the menu is beyond reproach. 100% masterfully done Thai food.

My husband and I had dinner there tonight. The food was amazing and very authentic. The amount of food you get for the money is insane. We had to take home 3 boxes because we could not finish all of it. I can't wait to try the other location on Kennedy Blvd.

The food was delicious and tasted really authentic. Moving to Indy from LA, I've been missing authentic Asian food! We will definitely be coming back. This is a family run business and the owners were really nice too. Update: I was super pregnant and just wanted to go into labor already. We decided to seek out some spicy food to get things going. Phan customized the food to the spiciness level we wanted. We had the most delicious spicy papaya salad, so spicy it made my ears ring. That night my water broke, baby was born 2/3/18. Thanks for the help Phan and family!
Love this place! Simple yet delicious dishes never disappoint. We crave almost everything on the menu that we end up always ordering way too much food. Makes for great leftovers the next day.

After reading glowing reviews for the place, I simply had to try it myself. A date night with the bf led to some disappointment. I got the idea that the atmosphere here would be more on the romantic side but it wasn't at all. It's more of a bar and grill with a vietnamese flare rather than a restaurant I can take seriously. Too loud, overcrowded and kinda dirty--if I wanted that I would elsewhere! The food, too, was a letdown. I had the steak and veggies rice entree and him the shrimp. After, again, reading nothing but glowing reviews on this place I found the taste of it all to be really sub-par. Nothing special, no complaints about the preparation but the flavor just really didn't have me rolling on the floor in delight. To be fair, I'm a bit new to the vietnamese food scene, but regardless, food should always be delicious and here it most certainly wasn't. The only exception is their Pandan waffle which we had we red bean ice cream. Very delicious, perfectly sweet with the red bean flavor on top to compliment it. It could have used some whip cream, but that's my two cents.
Every meal has been a wonderful array of flavors and excellent service. It may not be for everyone as it is authentic preparations, but we make a point to stop in when we can.

Ordered their cold samosa chat for take away. It was amazing. It tasted great and completely worth the price!! Interesting place. Will come again for sure. The staff was very courteous as well. Keep up the good job!!!

Got to love fez! They offer a great deal with the prefixed $25 feast menu (7 courses served family style). Really good if you want to bring a group together. They have a full bar and some nice house specialty drinks (feztini). Don't let me forget to mention their hookah! One of the best places I love to visit when I'm in the city.

Great independent restaurant lost in a sea of mediocre chain restaurants. The owner and his wife are very friendly and love chatting you up. It's truly a family business as all the cooks are related to the wife. Extremely reasonable prices, but the true test of a pho house is the broth and Pho 36 comes through with flying colors. Rich and flavorful without being salty. There are also several banh mi sandwiches to choose from and they are all priced $3.75. For fans of bubble tea, they have a small, but well-chosen selection of drinks. Next time I'm lost in the food desert that is Rockville Road in Avon, I will seek out Pho 36 as my oasis.

Anytime we're looking for Thai food in our local area we always come to this restaurant! I've been coming here for years and I'm never disappointed as we always get the same great service and same great food consistently! Food: For those that are familiar with Thai food many of the dishes come with rice or noodles and some sort of spicy curry or broth sauce. Jasmine Thai takes the time to adjust to spiciness and you can even get it mild for those that don't like anything spicy. My favorite dishes would be the pad Thai, Which is what hubby gets every single time with chicken. My other favorite is the pad sei eu. This this is very similar to the pad Thai but it comes with a brown sauce broccoli and wider rice noodles. I really enjoy the food here because going gluten-free if you're doing only rice items you can eat rice noodles or rice itself. Service: The service is always wonderful when we come here! The waitstaff is familiar with our faces and even when we come get food to go they know who we are. The food is brought out very quickly and the staff is extra pleasant! For those in the Brandon area I suggest going to Jasmine Thai if you're looking for authentic atmosphere for Thai food and awesome food to boot!
Ordered the trip through Puerto Rico with the 3 pork dishes with yucca, and the dessert sampler. Highly recommend all of the above! Great service too!
Damn good bowl of pho The atmosphere is not like what you would expect but the pho was cheap and good and perfect after a day on the hill in the snow.

It takes them 2 hours to deliver food and when it comes late and cold they are unsympathetic. They are very rude and have very poor customer service. They do not understand how to treat people. Do not order they are awful and don't deserve your business.

A young lady from Jamaica opened up a small struggling restaurant in south philly about 22 years ago. Her name was Nicola and she was my friend- her jerk chicken was FIRE. It was Hella good. It was the first time I ate Jamaican food. I took my husband here for one of our first dates. There used to be Bob Marley music playing in the background, it was a magical place. Over the years I came back often. Then it changed drastically. The platters got smaller and the prices got bigger, food quality suffered. Yesterday I paid $30.00 for 2 jerk platters- it was a dry boneless skinless chicken breast a cup of rice and about 2tb of cabbage. It was terrible. So disappointing. I won't be coming back.

Thanks for yelp. It gave us another great restaurant to go to. The service was impeccable. We arrive 10 minutes before closing and they were still gracious and accommodating. We had the naan-bread garlic, plain, and sexy. Sexy was hot with jalapeno peppers. The chicken Teaka masala was delicious. The temperature of the food was perfect when it came out. The establishment was very clean and decorated beautifully. This was the best Indian food I have had in Florida.

Thai taste is the place to go for good Thai food. The building is simple, the parking can be tricky but what awaits you on the inside is worth it. Friendly staff and your glass never goes empty. The food is delicious and always prepared quickly and correctly.

Wow, I never realized that a healthy, delicious, independent, fairly authentic Greek restuarant was hiding in this otherwise typical, corporate shopping plaza. My chicken kabob salad was light but satisfying, the meat was tender, well-cooked and lightly seasoned. The hummus was satisfactory. Live music "Mediterranean" style the Friday night I was there -- kind of a cheesy touch but I liked it. Friendly staff; I will be back.
Omg the chicken salad sandwich and the beef tenderloin Caesar salad are to die for. Highly recommend this place. Quick and delicious

I have been wanting to eat here for quite a while. Momo's has good dark ambiance. There was a band there on the Monday I went and we ate outside. We were seated promptly and our waitress was helpful. For an appetizer we had bacon wrapped shrimp. It was grilled and it was served with purée sweet potatoes and apricot slaw or something of the sort. All were good together, but nothing to die for. I had one of the Greek salads with lamb. All ingredients tasted fresh and appropriately prepared. I would definitely go back.

The beef kabob was amazing. Very juicy and tender, I'm coming back for more. The grape leaves tasted like they were soaked in pickle juice and then the inside had chicken and rice. They're also served cold. The rice was slightly flavored which was nice. Their fries are thick and fresh and well as their pita bread. The lamb and beef kafta (ground meat thing) was the one thing my bf and I didn't like so much. The owner tried to convince us to try the kafta so we did half and half combo. The lamb was a little softer than the beef but they both didn't have much taste alone. It was like a dry plain meatball taste and texture with no flavor. But, when you wrap it with the pita bread, grape leaves and Cucumber yogurt salad, it's amazing :) I still highly suggest the kabob bc it was perfectly seasoned and you don't need anything else with it.

If this place ever goes out of business, I will cry like a baby! We eat here at least once a week, now. We've tried other places, but they are never as good as this place. Yes, the service is "different" but if you mind that, just get it to go. The food is outstanding. We tend to stick with the Green Curry chicken and Mansumun Curry chicken (Christmas in your mouth!) Some of the best food I've ever eaten and we are addicted!

A new Vietnamese restaurant has entered the sb scene and honestly I can say that it beats the competition. I always get the pho tai bo vien with the meat on the side because i like to be able to control how rare my meat is. Also the broth here beats the other Vietnamese restaurants out of the park. The broth here has a thin layer of fat that the other restaurants don't have. This layer of fat provides a depth of flavor that most authentic pho dishes have. I understand what good pho is because I am Vietnamese and grew up eating pho almost every week. It's as close as you can get to authentic pho. My only gripe about this place is the price. It is $10 for a large bowl of pho in comparison to the other Vietnamese restaurants which average about 7-8 dollars for a large. However I will gladly continue paying this price because I prefer the quality of pho here but would prefer to pay less. The banh mi here also is better than other Vietnamese restaurants here. They bake their bread in shop it seems with the giant oven they have in the kitchen. Honestly this restaurant is a godsend from the other Vietnamese restaurants because it actually encaptures real Vietnamese cuisine. Although the service here is slow as expected of new restaurants and the workers seem like they have never worked in the food industry the owner has his best interest in the customer. It is obvious the owner cares for his customers and quality of service. I actually got to talk to him and he seemed like a nice guy. He actually forgot one of my orders and made it up by giving our drinks that we ordered for free! I honestly waited a few weeks to write this review and have gone here at least 5 times before I wrote this review.
This place has all sorts of modern-take-on-asian treats. Try the Bahn Mi for great flavors at bargain prices. I've had many good lunches here, and the smoothies are tasty as well.

Continues to be a great choice in my mind. Have been twice recently and fully enjoyed both meals. Both the pasta and main courses have been excellent. Last time in we got a cheese/meat plate and the longhots for an appetizer. Both were fantastic and I would highly recommend. Wine and drink selection is good and not overpriced. Service has been hit or miss but nothing bad. I ate at both Avalon and Mercato this week and would chose Avalon every time for almost every reason- food, drinks, service. I did think Mercato was more interesting inside.
The restaurant is very nice but the food is mediocre. It tastes ok at best. I walked in thinking it was going to be a really good meal L and left disappointed. We definatelt won't be going back.

Used to be my default because they have vegetarian broth for the pho. Now that my pho is sitting on my floorboard I have decided to stop supporting this place until they figure out how to do a to-go order, Jazmine is better anyway, the location convenience is not worth the trouble with this place.

New place just opened by the former chef/owner of Sola (Dave Clauser). He just opened Wishbone, a "craft" fried chicken take out with limited seating. Excellent fried chicken - no bones. This is gourmet fingers. They are fresh, hot, crispy, delish - as are the dips. No veggies or sides. We did dine there - cozy seating up a few steps. It is in the building where Lee's Hoagies was - big improvement. You should try it. Adult food but if you work at or near Penn and want to bring home a real treat for your kids - make the stop and pick up. He also makes a "pie of the day." Sort of pockets - today was pumpkin. Didn't try but they looked tasty. Also an interesting assortment of beverages. I had a SNAP - lime, agave, cayenne. Oh -- ask for the "secret" sauce. They sometimes have something special if you ask. This is going to be a new addiction for us.

WOW, I wish I could add another star. I usually never do reviews but I absoutly fell in love with this place. The owner and staff took the time to make me feel like this was my second home and took the time to explain each item on the menu to me, since this was my first time ever having Mediterranean cuisine. After my first bite I was hooked I ordered the beef gyro and a side of hummus with the most refreshing orange pashion smoothie. Between the great food and good laughs I would defintley be coming back again.
Super good, super cheap. Found it on Yelp because I was craving Chinese - got the Mongolian Beef which was a very high quality, excellent meal for about $8. I'll be back for sure.

I've tried to eat at this restaurant twice before but each time the servers would accommodate older people who would arrive after me, so both those times I just left and ate elsewhere. Well, considering my boyfriend and I live around the corner from Dmitri's, and it is frequently a busy restaurant so we assumed it must be good, we gave it a third shot. It was a rainy Thursday evening so we were promptly taken to be seated elbow to elbow with another table of two. Considering there were other tables available, I requested a different table in which I waitress politely said she'd prepare. When we were seated we received our water, had our bottle o' red uncorked and unpoured into small rimmed glasses that only allow you to take the smallest sips(I feel sorry for those with BIG noses!) and were verbally given the specials. My boyfriend is hearing impaired, so he did need them to repeated, and considering it's such a loud atmosphere, they should offer the specials on paper. Soon after we were brought some warm, grilled pita bread, which would have been tasty if it wasn't burnt on the grill, accompanied with a low quality olive oil, red wine vinegar and some herb which did nothing for the tasteless dip. There was also some bread in the basket so I asked if they had butter, and they said they had no butter. Okay, fine. We ordered our appetizers, shrimp scampi and steamed mussels. The shrimp was very fresh, yet the dish very salty. The mussels were served in a SOUP of bland garlic broth, topped with giant slices of tomato, spinach, green pepper and onion. Interesting to say the least. I thought maybe music could tone down the loud atmosphere, and when I requested some be put on, I was told there was music on but the noise inside exceeded it. There wasn't any on though because we were seated below a speaker, and would have heard atleast a faint sound at any more silent moments. Finally we get our entrees, Fried Flounder and a Mediterranean whole white fish, which came filleted as a requested, both served with sauteed spinach and yellow rice. The flounder was very fresh, but like our other dishes, bland. However, my white fish was incredible. A very rich, savory, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. My white fish aside, the service, portions, food, prices were just good. It's too loud, small, and nothing on the wall that is appeasing to eye. I think next time I want some fresh fish at a BYO, I'll head a few blocks down and try to get a table at Little Fish. Mmmmm.

I like Mumbai Bistro because it's a place you can go to when you get a craving for Indian food on the cheap ($4.95/lb bar, $1 samosas) or even something hot and more substantial than a sandwich, that's not chinese take out. I congratulate it for tapping this market! There is a hot bar with daily meat and veg courses that rotate- stocked with all your standards...chicken tikka masala, paneer masala, chicken korma, some lentil dishes, potato and cauliflower curry. All these hot bar items were pretty fresh. That being said, the quality of the dishes isn't quite Palace of the Ben worthy and they don't make their own naan (it's sorta weak). My favorite offering was the Chicken Korma- avoid the dry Chicken Tikka Masala. As far as Indian food goes, it's a little on the safer side with the spices pretty muted. You also have to remember that for lunch (depending on how much you load in your to-go box) you could pay just a few bucks more and get an all you can eat buffet at Palace of the Ben with amazing naan and dessert included in the cost. As I said above though, the ability to get pay-by-the pound Indian food in the neighborhood is pretty freakin' sweet for lunch!

This place has been one of my favorites for a few years now. The atmosphere is a bit kitchy and filled with cliché, but fun and light hearted at the same time filled with cool wood carvings and Thai theater dolls. The food here is excellent and lately the service has been impeccable, wasn't always this way. I always order the same thing when I come here, the mussaman curry, which simply is to die for. Also recommend the tofu Todd for a starter and especially their Thai tea if you don't mind something sweet. Reasonable prices + excellent food and service = win.

Went here on Monday with some friends and we all had a blast. The food was great and the atmosphere was awesome as well. We had AMAZING soup dumplings and then split 4 entrees, but ended up taking some home because we were stuffed. I had the jumbo shrimp with chili pepper. Will try to add a picture of it if I can figure out how to do it from my phone.

The green beans were obviously canned, and, even worse, something in the dish tasted rotten, like it was going bad. I think it was the coconut milk. Being too much of a wimp to say anything, I ate it anyway, and felt lucky to not get sick.

Loved this place when it was Kombo Kitchen and love it even more now as Thai 5 owned and operated by Chanel! It is easily the best Thai food I've ever had. My personal favorites are the green curry chicken and pad thai. The love and care that Chanel puts into the business is evident. From what I've witnessed, everyone there really cares about making Thai 5 successful. Great food, great atmosphere, and I will miss this place greatly when I move out of Tampa.
Weird name, but great Pho at a decent price.
My first time having Thai food. I wasn't overly impressed. I had chicken and shrimp Pad Thai and Thai dumplings. It wasn't bad though.
First time ordering here, ordered jerk chicken wings. Thought I heard them putting them in microwave, food came soggy and cold.
VERY good food!! It's pricy but worth it. The service is terrible. But the last visit the service was great, so maybe they fixed the issue.

I've been here 5-6 times but probably won't come back...I ordered a banh mi thit nuong. I've had banh mi at many places and this was prob one of the worst. the bread was too crispy,the pork was too fatty and had a weird flavor. I should've just gone to Thuy Cafe (their lemongrass chicken banh mi is very good). I'll give them 2 stars, which is generous, because the boba tea was good and they have a variety of things to eat/drink. Also, it shouldn't take nearly 20 min to make a banh mi. crazy. I was just about to walk out and wish I had earlier....edited: stomach was hurting bad an hour later, bad customer service

the food, everything we had was great, the salads particularly. It is like walking into another world. Created by new,young, visionary leadership of our community. A great collaboration of architect, developer and Great space, an old gas station that really works! Missouri Historic Tax credits helped to build this place and helping to bring back this great neighborhood.

My favorite Vietnamese place in New Orleans. I like the mix of traditional and modern cuisine. The portions of pho are pretty big, and the pho/vermicelli dishes here are a lot better than they are at other Vietnamese places in New Orleans in my opinion. This is one spot that I would be at almost every week when I lived there because I liked it so much. Definitely worth a try, especially the pho/vermicelli dishes.
The owner is very friendly and HONEST! Thank you! It is relatively small, but it is great place to shop. They sell delicious indonesian foods and snacks.
We ordered lamb and chicken biryani..... chicken was a bit dry but the lamb was very very delicious. .. The biryani rice was good too....
Good, quick, inexpensive lunch spot. The dals and paneer were all very good. The naan didn't taste so fresh but it was wrapped in aluminum foil, so it might just be the wrapping.
SUPER Expensive and food is EXTREMELY small portions and not that great. Some food salty some not enough flavor. Service is alright.

So happy to find a great Thai restaurant in Indy (I know, there are a lot of favorites out there, but it has always seemed to me they are overrated). We had the green curry, the Masaman curry and the duck and they all were not only wonderful but also presented beautifully. We also had the chicken satay which was not dry as in other restaurants, but moist and meaty. Well done!!

This truly is the best food truck in Philadelphia. I love watching the grill master go to work as he prepares each serving completely fresh and unique every day. Hard to know exactly what he's going to provide on any given day, so those with food restrictions/allergies should be aware, but those without: you're in for a treat! The hummus built in to most of the dishes is often slightly sweet, largely from the garlic mixed in, and it fantastic! The falafels are the best in Philadelphia (yes, better than Mama's, which is great) that I have had, but it's the fresh cooked meat each day that is truly fantastic. The chicken is always tender and loaded with flavor. Pro tip: Cash only, and don't stand in the middle of the sidewalk or too close to the cart. You will get chastised. Otherwise, he is a very nice man!

This is possibly one of the worst Indian restaurants I've ever tried. Food tastes below average but the prices are sky high. They chose a good location but not good service to fit in. Also, the restaurant itself is too small to accommodate a buffet. I have been there for 3-4 Times just to give it a chance. I'm done with this place forever. The buffet food is no where near to what you get at other places for $14. That menu has 140 items and I don't know who in their right mind have written it. You can't expect a chef to cook those many dishes, and I definitely will not be going to this place again ever!!

We ordered a 5 piece of regular crab Rangoon last night at the Maryland Heights location for pick up. When we got home and I bit into the first one, there was no filling. Literally, nothing. So we opened the other four and it was exactly the same. These had absolutely no filling at all. It was just deep fried breading. The picture I attached proves it. The chicken fried rice was decent, nothing special, and the buffalo chicken fried rice was identical but with hot sauce poured on top. On top of the fact that it is ridiculous to pay for an item with zero filling, this was our first time in the restaurant and we were hoping to finally find a decent Chinese food restaurant in the area. I had a great experience at the Florissant location in the past but this was nothing similar. Very disappointed.

I only give it stars for service. The service was excellent but the food was pretty bad. Ordered chips and salsa and we couldn't even eat them. I had the plantain salad and the dressing had a horrible taste to it. Everyone was very friendly but they allow dogs inside, and I would rather not have dogs all over while I'm eating in a restaurant.

Bang! The flavors are a fusion of yummy from around the globe. The broccoli tabouleh was a delicious twist on a standard. Best hangar steak ever. Felt like our server, Eric, was an old friend having us over for dinner...yet never intrusive. This place is a winner!

I give this place a 3.9 (hence the 4 stars) out of 5. Good solid taste and texture. Flavors have some boldness and the it doesn't taste flat (to the non foodies that means having no seasonings). Spring roll was very crunchy and it was accompanied by a nice sweet sauce which id imagine is their version of a sweet sauce. It's a little too heavy on the oil side. The food sat well in my stomach and didn't cause discomfort; unlike other Thai places I have eaten at. Portion is not the largest but then again it was take out. Thai tea was good. Little bit too much on the condensed milk side. Overall I was satisfied with my meal. The chicken pad Thai was a 3.8 out of 5. Thai samurai is still my top rated place. Noodles were consistent, bean sprouts were fresh but the peanuts seemed a little too mushy. They lacked that crisp texture to them. It could have been from the humidity of the dish though so that will be undecided. It is a passable place to eat if you are craving Thai food but not something I highly recommend if you have other options. Price is on the higher range. I only had a chicken pad Thai and Thai tea. It all came out to 13.81 which I find pretty expensive for a small portion meal. The front desk girl was very nice. Had my food immediately ready upon arrival. Bon appetite my fellow yelpers.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Food: ***** Service: *** Wait time: * I was so excited to try this place out. Some of the other reviews mentioned that it can take a really long time to get your food, so I expected to wait about half an hour or so, I was prepared for that. Well, I go in at around 7:25, get my drinks at about 7:35 and place my order at around 7:40. The food didn't come to the table until 8:50. I was about to get up and pay for my drink to leave when they finally brought out the food. Everything was delicious, but I will NEVER eat in the restaurant again. For the amount of time it took I could have eaten at Pita Pit, gotten a beer at some bar and been back at home. Take out might be the only way to go for this place.

Great Asian food! Japanese, Thai, Korean, even Hawaiian. We had: Kimchi fries (they were ok, the sauce was a little too much for me - I guess I'm more of a purist when it comes to fries) Musubi - a Hawaiian appetizer made with sushi rice, seaweed (nori), and Spam! With a bit of teriyaki/hoisin sauce. This is a staple for Hawaiians! Firecracker and Spicy Hulk rolls - these were outstanding! Huge rolls, very fresh and full of flavor, and beautifully presented. Korean Fried Chicken - half spicy and half soy garlic. The chicken is on point, with a delicious crispy coating. I preferred the spicy, the soy garlic has a bit of sweetness, (and I'm more spicy than sweet), I'll ask for it to be even spicier next time as it was still pretty mild to me. Had craft beers and cocktails to drink with this feast. Can't wait to go back and try more items in this menu! Highly recommend!

Monday dinner was takeout for first time, disappointed first time too. portion sizes are smaller, pad thai had NO shrimps, curry was watered-down. thinknwenwil drive into fown next time we crave Thai food.

This is my first review I've ever written in my life because never feel inspired to. I am not a huge advocate for fast casual but this place is the bees knees and specifically this location. Nicole rocks first of all . . all staff is eager to be friendly, make suggestions, clean up, etc. I never go to a fast casual place for the service but this place I do! While it is a chain it provides a homey vibe that is perfect with the menu concept. enjoy!

This is a neat place. It's a hole-in-the-wall place, but the food they serve is really special. It is like nothing you've ever had! I don't remember what all of the dishes I loved were called, but I enjoyed them. Some of the food can be quite spicy--which I like, but others do not. The staff was extremely friendly and were a great help in deciding what to order. This place seems authentic--there were plenty of native Ethiopians dining there. This is a must try!

I recently went here for the second time and just realized I hadn't reviewed it but that's a good thing because I actually enjoyed the food more the second time. We went in a group of four and the waiter easily convinced us to order 4 different things and share it in one giant tray so that we get to try more things. Someone order the Lamb Tibs (that's the only one I can remember because it was spoken of so highly). We also got a beef dish, a chicken dish...and I think another chicken dish. When you look at the descriptions of the food, they all look very similar. I chose one that had the word "spicy" in it. In the end though, I didn't think any of them were spicy. Ethiopian food is interesting because you eat it by scooping it up with the spongy bread that they give you. The bread is kind of lemony tasting but it starts to grow on you. It also grows INSIDE you and makes you VERY full. I'm not very good at the scooping so I feel like I end up eating a lot of bread and not as much of the good meaty stuff. They will give you a fork if you ask for one but I was trying to embrace the culture. Overall, all of the dishes were very good. One came with a hard boiled egg which was kind of random but we ate it. The "tibs" come out fajita style on a sizzling plate and then was poured into the tray with the rest of the food. I do wish there were more vegetables in the middle but we couldn't even finish all our food so I probably shouldn't complain about the lack of food! The waiter we had was very nice and I liked that he helped us decide what to order. I like this place but my because of my personal preference, I'll stick to only going there once ever year or so. I definitely think it's worth giving it a shot!!

This place was great. We had the chicken wings, and a lot of them. Tried three sauces and loved them all. Staff was beyond pleasant. The place had such a great multi cultural vibe. We felt very comfortable.

ya man welcome to jamaica. i have been here twice and both times the food was great. the place kinda looks shabby but the food is great. so if your going for looks then its not the place to go, but if your like me and there for good jamaican jerk chicken and caloulou then its the place to go, hey the price is good too.
Excellent breakfast and clean, quaint place! We'll definitely stop in again the next time we're in the area. Highly recommend the peach pancake with the praline butter....YUMMO!

We came here for lunch but we did not have enough time for the lunch deal so we ordered some soup and the steamed dumplings and spring rolls. The staff is friendly and the food was out pretty quickly but unfortunately it wasn't that good. Yeah there was a lot of garlic but the actual food fell short of my expectations. I am giving three stars because we did not try their entrees and who knows maybe they're amazing. If I were to base this strictly on the food I got today I would give two stars but it seems unjust to judge only by appetizers. This place is cash only.
We just left after enjoying an amazing lunch! Chicken shrimp fried rice and chicken stir fry! Mindy was sweet and was very attentitive. Plus the entire menu and Thai tea was the best!

The food is good but the service is so bad. Every time I go the servers are rude and slow. They roll their eyes and talk back when you ask for something, and they even snatched my glass to give me a refill with the straw still in my mouth. Never going back just because of the service.

We ordered from the Vegan menu and every dish was so delicious. Tom Yum soup was the best I've ever had, must order dish. Get the rolled noodle meal, something I've never tried elsewhere and very delicious. Drunken Fried rice, Penang curry all up to par. Papaya salad also very very delicious. I was peacefully eating knowing there wasn't any fish or oyster sauce in my vegan dishes. Also very affordable and large portions.

Mahi mahi tacos were superb. The view is as stunning as you will find just about anywhere on the Gulf Coast. The seating was spacious and clean. The waitress was very apologetic about their soda dispenser being on the fritz and suggested we try their fresh squeezed lemonade.. Great choice! All in all a nice out of the way place.. An oh that view!

The bar tenders are great, drinks reasonably priced with many different beers. What's the deal with paying for water? Seriously $1.50 for water at a restaurant?!? Chris made an excellent Long Island! The food wasn't good. We had the calamari which should be just fried chili peppers because the were the BOMB! The calamari however was fried to death. I had the blackened Mahi which was wayyyyy over cooked and had almost zero flavor, fortunately it didn't taste old or way fishy just meh. The veggies were good but not great under seasoned if at all. The rice wasn't seasoned with the minimum salt and pepper. My friend had wings which we're fried crispy (thumbs up) but then tossed in a super salty seasoning. We couldn't eat them between three of us. We also had a shrimp and grits... Seriously would salt and pepper kill you to season this stuff?? It's was just okay. The best of that meal was a good amount of shrimp and sausage. The service was good no complaints. Three stars for good service food one star because there's no negative numbers. :(
Amazing food and great service...so glad they re-created from Sansom Street even closer to my house!

One of the best all around Indian restaurants in all of the US and here it is located in Carmel, Indiana! Even now that I live out of town we make it a point to come back here when we are in town because there food from start to finish is so consistent. We usually order a wide variety of dishes but my Indian boyfriend raves about the Dhaal and how the lentils are the best around. The Chicken Tikka and their paneer are hard to beat alongside the best samosas around. Great place!

This was my first time here. I read several reviews that complained about service. Agree the service is not 5 stars but they were friendly. Our server recommended the curry and it was great! The food is wonderful! I am willing to go ask for an extra fork or remind the server i need water for the experience of the meal :) We will be back.

I love Asian food like so much that my friends joke and say that I was Asian in my former life. So when I saw Umami's menu I was intrigued. I came at happy hour expected happy hour but there are no specials except on Thursday for ladies. So lesson learned there. I ordered a margarita which was average but I didn't come here for Mexican cuisine. Now for the appetizer I ordered calamari. It came with lime and spicy mayo so a nice touch. The calamari was over cooked and definitely from a frozen bag. I'm sure of it. I eat enough calamari to know. For dinner I had the chicken pad Thai medium spice level. I thoroughly enjoyed it and the portion was very nice. Come for the pad Thai not for the calamari

I love this coffee shop. I have never gone at night though (I am starting to think I should, after reading these reviews!). I used to go here every morning for a coffee and a bagel. The bagel had egg, cheese and bacon on it and my god was it the best breakfast sandwich I have ever had in my life. I would walk in and the man behind the counter (I am pretty sure he is the owner) would call out "coffee and bagel?" like it was my first name. Keep this in mind though-- it is clear that breakfast is not their strong point because it does take FOREVER for them to whip this marvelous thing up. There was once a time where I told the guy working I had to leave to catch my bus, and he realized he forgot to start my sandwich. He told me to get a free one next time. The next time I went in, he remembered and gave me a coffee and bagel for free (well, I guess not for free, because I had paid for it the day earlier..) It really does have great coffee though, and wonderful food. It is an awesome place to go and read or study. BUT bring an ipod. It can get pretty loud in there and if you can't concentrate with background noise, you're screwed.

Disappointed. I just moved to this area and the Zoe's by my old house in NJ was sooooo good. I had high hopes for this one but was disappointed. I ordered a tossed Greek salad with extra grilled onions and a cup of chicken orzo soup to go. I got home and the salad did not have the extra grilled onions, and all the other ingredients in the salad were skimpy. They didn't shake the Greek dressing before filling the togo dressing cups, so mine was straight oil. The worst part was my soup (which mind you is usually my favorite). There was not ONE piece of orzo in it. It was an entire container of shredded chicken and a small amount of broth. You could hardly see the broth because there was so much chicken. It was definitely the bottom of the soup pot. I wish they would have told me they were running out of soup and I wouldn't have ordered it. Biggest disappointment as a nurse that just wanted a quick, nice meal after a 13 hour shift. I have been a frequent customer of a few Zoës Kitchens over the past few years and I will definitely not be returning.

Cute little restaurant with graffiti on the wall. I stopped by for a quick bite to go. The server was really sweet, giving recommendations and making sure I was comfortable, assuring the order will be done soon, offering water etc. I ordered the bahn mi with pork and the fried chicken with rice. The bahn mi was A-Ok but smaller than what I'd expected / what I'd get at other places. The chicken had good flavour but too bad was a little pink on the inside :(

Great Thai food. Go to the Siam Cafe on McCall street. There's another in town (near/on Whitebridge), but this one is cheaper, and more authentic (same ownership). Our favorite dishes: duck salad, tiger tears, green curry, spicy eggplant, pad thai, lad na.

The McDonald's of Pho. It's a chain so bc of that I only have a few expectations. I expect it to be consistently good. I expect it to stay cheap. I expect the service to be mediocre. I expect the food to come out quickly.
A family favorite! Kids and adults love it. Gyro plate and kids chicken & rice meal are our favorites.
I never liked falafel before Blu Fig. I decided to give it one more try, and now I know what I've been missing!

I visited Desi Village on a week night to use a Groupon I had purchased. I was pleasantly surprised. Everything we ordered was absolutely delicious. The vegetable samosas were good, pretty similar to others I have tried at other Indian restaurants. My boyfriend and I usually order regular naan but we decided to branch out- best decision ever! You have try the Village Naan. It was sooo good. Please- try it. My boyfriend ordered the garlic naan and his was pretty tasty as well. Both naan orders were nice and soft. I have had naan in the past that gets a little burnt and crispy. I usually order the standard Chicken Tikka. I asked if they did Butter Chicken and was pleased that they did. It tastes relatively the same except they use dark meat instead of white so the chicken is more tender. I also really liked that the server asked what spice level I wanted. I ordered medium and was very happy with the choice. The Butter Chicken was one of the best I have ever had : ). My boyfriend felt the same about the Chicken Tikka. As far as atmosphere, as other reviewers have mentioned it was pretty quiet. The servers were extremely attentive and my water was never low. I will definitely be back!

Yum! I love a good bowl of Pho and this place does it right! I met a friend here for lunch and was excited to add another place to my "NOLA Pho" list. We started with a plate of the pork tacos. The pork was tender, tasty and delicious. It was cooked in a typical Vietnamese fashion and it was quite tasty. I also decided to the "combo" pho which comes packed with New York strip, brisket and meatballs. WOW. This was such a delectable bowl! They were not stingy with the meat at all and the entire serving was huge! The broth held a lot of flavor and didn't leave the meat to do all of the "flavor" work (as it sometimes does). The atmosphere here is pretty casual. We stopped in late on a Saturday afternoon and there were only a few other people in the place. Unlike some other Vietnamese places, Mint serves alcohol and even has a happy hour Tuesday through Saturday. I will definitely return to Mint for a tasty bowl and some apps!
The food is fresh and delicious, I highly recommend the shrimp pil pil!! The hummus, grilled scallops and broiled tilapia are also amazing! I also love that it is a BYOB!!
We just found our new favorite place to eat on the Eastside. This is a must eat at place even if you're not on the Eastside it's worth the drive.
Sub Par Service I ordered a beef dish and it was like deep fried meatloaf. I didn't enjoy it at all. The naan was good tho.

Such a great dining experience outside. So charming. Food was delicious. Tom Kha to die for with chicken. Pineapple fried rice was good and hearty with a bit of sweet. Not a fan of rice but I indulged here.

What a find. The food was delicious. Started with dolmades and falafel. Flavorful and so good. I had the beef gyro. I love the amount of lemon in their sauces. Perfect. The pita is a bit crisp on the edges, which I love. The two young women at the counter were fantastic. Sweet and welcoming. I believe they did all the food prep. Perfectly balanced. Cannot wait to go back. Bravo Smiley's!!!

This place used to be my go-to restaurant for Thai food. I think they changed chefs or something because it no longer has the authentic flavors. I always come here for the pad see ewe and the pad Thai. The last time I came here, the pad see ewe lacks flavor and the pad Thai has a strong ketchup flavor. Sad that I have to find a new Thai place.

Last nite my family went for dinner at this restaurant and we really enjoyed the food. We liked the 2 appetizers we ordered - fried fish fritters and lollipop chicken. They were well marinated with spices and not at all oily or spicy. They were served piping hot. I also enjoyed the rewa dosa along with its chutneys and lentil gravy. The service was quick and professional. Our overall experience was good except I found the price to be on the steep side.
Nirvana Fusion is a great restaurant. They are very friends here. The food is delicious. One of the best Indian restaurants in town. The food is great for the price.

Staff is friendly and helpful. Drinks are the star here so many Boba options. I usually just go for a drink but wait the food is good too! The fried rice was yum and the pho was a big hit too, surpise :)
Crazy I read all the reviews and tried to go here and they were closed before their stated closing time! Really frustrating and unprofessional!
I came here for my anniversary and thoroughly enjoyed my meal. The jerk chicken and wings were excellent. They definitely had a lot spice but loved it. The service was also great.
Jerk chicken is always good just enough spice!! Love the cabbage & beans & rice too one of my favs whenever I'm in the city!

This is a nice place. The food was good, personally the place was really hot and there was no parking for us. We had to wait for a while for a car to leave and for us to park. Then inside, the place was really really hot and it took forever for our food to arrive. We got there at 5:44pm and we left at 7:45pm. It was a really long wait, especially with a toddler. Also, the place is really expensive for the food.

This place was one of my favorite meals during a recent visit to Nashville. I first hesitated to go, b/c it is part of a chain, and I was really trying to stick to local spots during our travels, but the craving for Mediterranean food was strong, and this happened to be minutes from our hotel. They have done a very nice job of keeping the space clean. I've been to the Taziki's in Charleston and found this one to be cleaner and nicer. The decor is simple and chic with dark wood tables and chairs to go. The service is friendly and fast. Food came out minutes after ordering. We also appreciated that the manager walked the floor and checking in with everyone, very nice touch. The food was THE highlight though! We liked everything so much we ended up eating here twice in just a short three day trip! I had their grilled veggie gyro the first day and split a dolmades plate with my friend. The second time, had the spicy pimento sandwich. The food was DELICIOUS and hit the spot, both times. Loved everything but have to say the dolmades was the star. Just perfectly seasoned, nice and fat and juicy, and the dips that were served with it, particularly the cool cucumber one, was amazing. Even if there was a great local Mediterranean spot in Nashville worth going to, I still wouldn't hesitate to go to this one again on the next visit!

This place is pretty good, it's a bit small, but one of the top pho places I have found here in Tucson. There is also photographs taking by one of my favorite photographers Neil, posted on the wall! The only downfall to this place is I don't see no public bathroom, so if you need to go, you got to go! lol
I had lamb ketban. It was tender and goooood! And the chicken sandwich was awesome. Ha a vegetarian friend, so they suggested vegetarian sandwich that's not on the menu. Delicious~ um um um~

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: The food is amazing!! My boyfriend and I work for the airlines a travel for food all the time, this is pretty legit! We came is 30 min before closing and the hosts were not very kind of helpful but the owner was extremely awesome! He was kind and informative and even extra food to take with us at the end. 100% recommend for flavor
Very good lunch--good choices and reasonable prices. however AVOID the Mirna's Soup---DREADFUL I had the kafta roll--it was delicious and out of the ordinary. Seasoned very well and not too dry.

Stopped through Nashville on a road trip and ran across this place. It didn't look like much walking in but the hookah was fantastic! And the food was great! I got the ice hookah hose with the fruit top! By far the smoothest I've ever had and I smoke a lot of hookah! Moral to the story - never judge a book by its cover, or a restaurant for that matter!

I go there all the time and it never disappoints. I'd suggest going either a little on the early side or a bit later, so like 5:30 or 9. If you have a big group, this location is not the best..so take it to their No Libs location. Usually, there is a bit of a wait, so we put in our name then took a nice stroll to get some wine and beer. By the time we made it back 17 mins later our table was patiently waiting for us. Hummus is a must have, the pita is always so warm and fluffy. usually get the grilled octopus too, pretttyy pretty prety good. Other apps that cannot be missed are the meatballs...they are SooO good. And last night we tried the shrimp pil pil cause all these yelpers were raving about it so we went for it. it lived up to the hype. We split the seafood combo. It wasn't bad at all. It was a nice steamed medley of everything in the sea. Probs won't get it again, and go back to my go to of the salmon. *HOT TIP:!*&%* Hummus, octopus, and meatballs are perfect for takout on the weekdays , S & P

I have been to ALOT of Indian restaurants, all over the country. This is more of a 4-star restaurant, but for this area, it's a 5. Indian in the Philly area, and the Main Line in particular, is sub-par. This place is definitely the best I'm aware of in this area. The atmosphere is above average. It's clean, neat, and has a definite Indian feel with paintings and photographs. The staff is both more competent and less intrusive than typical Indian-restaurant staff. The menu has all the usual choices, plus some more unusual offerings and even a few dishes I'd never heard of. Every table around me was ordering chicken tikka masala so I figured that was good and went for something I'd never heard of, as did my husband. We were both wowed. They have an especially large bread selection-- like 10+ different naans. We had the Peshawari which was very sweet, almost dessert-like, which I loved.
Fish clay pot is to die for. The red sauce is full of flavor and the kimchi gives that perfect hint of sour. The stuffed grape leaves are also MANDATORY. Great service and great drinks!

A good food restaurant! Was not super busy which made for a long week of so much going on a place to slow down and have conversation. The kids loved the low pillow table and the family dinner experience. Will definitely go again! The lamb was soooo delicious and cooked to perfection.

For me, worst pho I've had in a long while. The soup stock was way too salty (maybe because we came after 2pm). The meatballs were terrible (spongy kind made with byproducts rather than meat), and it had way too much beef oil floating on top of the soup. Being somewhat of a health nut, it just wasn't my style of pho.
Love this place ! Great food . I go at least once a month for their lunch buffet. Saturday's are great to go , it's never packed.

The food at this place is amazing. It's a little bit of a strange experience, though. I've been there a couple of times and both times I felt a little bit unwelcome when I walked through the door. The entire interaction with staff was uncomfortable and I felt like they weren't really happy to be there. I'm not expecting people to be cheering as soon as someone comes through the door, but a smile would be nice. As I said, though, the food is amazing. I got the delicious chicken, which came with rice and I also ordered hummus and some extra pita. I will definitely go back!

Not the same as china towns pho or all the Pho places by little saigon city on Washington ave. It's like you just can't have Spanish people cooking Italian dishes, this pho tasted blandish as if it was cook by Christmas elf's or something, the whole thing was just off. Not enough Ginger Spice lacks proper taste. Very bland.

I would highly recommend if you are a vegetarian or love healthy food that also tastes delicious. I would absolutely recommend the falafel pita wrap, it's a great idea that tastes even better than it looks. The hummus is perfect, and I have never tried anything here that I don't like! One of my favorite chain restaurants in Arizona!
This guy has a lot of nerve - but the food is worth the wait and the lecture.

I've been a repeat offender of this place. It's solid Indian fare, that tastes great and is inexpensive (pay by weight). I am usually leery of weighing stations because, I don't like the idea of my price being contingent on how greedy I am. They make a variety of dishes but the standard is the buffet style set up, which has basmati rice and whatever vegetarian and meat options for the day. They have a mango chutney that's absolutely delicious! One complaint- their naan is great, but sometimes you can tell its not fresh. For example, today I ordered the garlic naan and its fairly obvious that it was made yesterday. Honorable mention is the fact that the food doesn't send you running to the lavatory, which- If we're being honest, is a concern with spicier cuisine.

We wanted to try a new Caribbean restaurant in the Tampa, Yah Mon was within walking distance from our hotel. The food was amazing, we had to stop ourselves from over eating because of the portions given. I would recommend coming here to experience fine Caribbean dining.

I had the pernil and arroz con gandules. It reminded me of home. There is not much to say just that the food is amazing and the crew is friendly. The prices were great as well. Just to give a recommendation, I would say that you should play some music in the restaurant. I will return soon!!

Went there with a group of 7, we kept hearing about this place so decided to give it a try...service was very very slow (the place was almost empty, no excuse to be that slow)..everybody ordered and we waited 45 minutes for our orders..they didnt come out at the same time either...got my food and my wife and a friend didnt get theirs almost 10 minutes later..I got the mushroom burger and beef tacos. They were very average. Wife got the salmon, she said hers was blah, she ordered asparagus with it, it didn't come out til she was almost done eating..guy next to me got the beef fried rice, there was two little pieces of bland meat on top of what looked like 3lbs. of rice. They don't make their own iced tea, came out of the soda dispenser. The atmosphere was bad too. The music in the bar area was so loud we couldnt talk to each other..the place needs a decor upgrade or something...probably wont go back unless some things REALLY change

First, I eat a lot of Pho. I have spent many years in Seattle and San Francisco. Entering this restaurant, I knew it was a first and last visit from the smell, not sure if it was the kitchen or carpet the smell came from, but it was awful! The food taste the exact same as the smell, the end. Soup=dirty dishwasher Phad Tai=old cheese? Springroll=really old shrimp smell? Icetea=water brownish color? Honestly we all took a few bites and did not say a word, couldn't leave fast enough. On the plus side, stale mints available to at least get you to a toothbrush. I will find Pho in Boise.

I wish this was in my neighborhood! I was on my way to the Tower Theater with a friend and we decided to stop in here for a quick meal on the way. It was a short walk from the Frankford el and the yelp reviews had me very very interested. We arrived to this not so fancy fast-food-like dining room that was too clean to be fast food so we stepped up to the counter and received a friendly greeting. The menu looked good and really affordable. My friend ordered the Marquez lamb sausage platter with really great fresh hummus. I had the Lamb Ketban platter which was so tender and delicious. I liked the Zaalouk appetizer I chose for my platter. The platters are a decent size coming with salad and sauces and saffron rice. When I asked if what we ordered was enough for hungry guys, the man taking our ordered ensured us it was. I was impressed with honesty over the opportunity to up-sell. The food was really top notch and the vibe is friendly, clean and very affordable. WHY oh WHY cant this be in my neighborhood??!!?!?! PLEASE, come east! Fishtown and N.libs needs you! *the last dramatic portion of this review is inflamed by the deficit of a variety of eastern/middle eastern foods. I love ekta and tiffin but C'mon!

Called Zorba's at 3:o'clock on a Friday and after a few minutes of juggling, they were able to find us an Table, good start to what I will say was superb service and food grilled to perfection. It appears that they expanded since my last visit (2 yrs ago) but this is still a cozy intimate place that is awesome for a nicely prepared experience. Started out with the cold combination appt. and it was definitely worth it. Refreshing and flavors that excites your taste buds to no end. Plenty for two but be adventurous and try the grilled octopus. You will enjoy whatever you take home tomorrow if not later that night. Moved onto the "Fisherman's Feast" good golly miss Molly every bite was a party that had me tapping my feet under the table. As I looked around the room I noticed most were digging in with yum written all over their face. Sorry didn't do dessert, I just wanted to savor the flavors I had just experienced. Come you will not regret it. I suggest you call and make a reservation.

DON'T GO! We have been there many times in the past but not since the holidays. We had always loved it but not this time. It was worse than bad. I'm not sure what happened but the quality of the ingredients now is disgusting. Just awful. Spent the rest of the afternoon in the bathroom...

Another perfect dinner at Bamboo House of Noodle Soups. We have enjoyed visiting Bamboo for many years. We started by going to the Frazer, PA location but were thrilled when they opened a new restaurant in West Chester. We bring our friends on many occasions and have never been disappointed. Our favorite dishes are the Clay Pots and Salted Fried. You will love Bamboo House of Noodle Soups!

Ever since my Indonesian friend recommended this place to me a few years ago, I've become a regular. I love 'hole in the wall' family restaurants like Sky Cafe. Everything is under $7, portions are just right, and food is very satisfying and tasty. The fried wontons and beef/pork satay are great. Wontons are super crispy on the outside, and soft on the inside. The sweet sauce goes very well with it. The beef and pork skewers are perfectly grilled.
