I eat it without the peanut sauce because I'm allergic, but my friends love it. The cucumber dices on top of the satay are a nice touch too. My favorite dish is the Mie Komplit. It consists of egg noodles, veggies, beef & mushroom, bbq pork, marinated egg, and smaller versions of the fried wontons. It comes with a side of soup that you can pour over or drink separately (I prefer separately). It definitely hits the spot. If you prefer a (coconut) rice dish, I recommend Nasi Lemak! I've also tried some of the curry and spicy dishes. I'm fine with Chinese and Korean spiciness, but WOW Indonesian spicy is on a whole new level! Gross but my nose starts getting runny and tears roll down my cheeks after 2 bites haha. I can't handle it, but those who have high spicy food tolerance will be very happy here! After the meal, I usually like to buy their homemade snacks that they have stacked up on the shelves in the back. Not sure what it's called, but I love their mildly spicy, fried noodles/fish/sesame thingy. I can snack on them all day. Their thousand layered cake (lapis legit) is also good! It's a small place (about 7 tables), but service is quick and you usually don't have to wait more than 5-10 minutes for a seat. Only complaint is that I always get extremely thirsty after eating their food. That doesn't stop me from returning each time though.

The service was outstanding and staff very friendly. Now I went with a friend who grew up eating this cuisine and is a chef. We both agree that the food was right on point and as authentic as if his grandma was cooking it. We will be returning as soon as possible to eat our way thru the menu.

I can't say I've been to many Greek-themed restaurants so I can't judge the flavors of Greek inspiration. What I can say is that in comparison to other fast food/sit down restaurants such as Subway or Panera, Mo ziki definitely sits above these joints. Although their prices are a bit costly, the amount and value for the price paid is worth it. Mo ziki starts you off with a type of dish - pita, wrap, salad, etc - and from there you get to select ingredients for your meal . Their food choices are all relatively healthy, also vegetarian-friendly, and very delicious and flavorful. The interior is bright and inviting with simple green and blue. A more classy version of Subway.
THIS LUNCH BUFFET IS AMAZING!!\o/ even the items that are usually "throwaways" like apps & veggies are friggin DELICIOUS! I HIGHLY recommend this new location.
I came here at 8:40pm and the door was locked, a man walked up unlocked the door and told me they closed early cause they ran out of food please tell me how a restaurant runs out of food.

I understand that they just opened and there can be kinks to be worked out but I still found the service to be completely unacceptable. In no way should it be ok for it to take over 45 minutes for an appetizer of spring rolls to come out and then another 20 minutes for the main dish of pho to come. It also took an additional 15 minutes just for a server to take our order to begin with, and even longer to get the check. The food itself was alright if you like poor quality fatty meat and mediocre broth. Given the circumstances I'd much rather head to Washington ave or Chinatown for far better pho and service.
Tiny little place hidden away near the train tracks. I was pleasantly surprised by the food though. Great food even if the place is hidden.

My son and I visited this restaurant yesterday for lunch. We love their Cashew Chicken entrée so much we travel from the Los Angeles area to Santa Barbara every so often when we get the urge for this delicious food. We get it with their wonderful brown rice. The sauce in which it is made is so good! We've been to a lot of Thai restaurants and this one is the absolute best-- no other one comes close and no one can make Cashew Chicken like they do. We have always found their service to be excellent. Oh, and their prices are most reasonable. Marge and Don Martin
By far the best hookah lounge/bar in Nashville if not Tennessee! Great atmosphere, AMAZING FOOD, the hookahs are absolutely phenomenal! Must Check them out! Tangerine Dream is my flavor!

My go to Pho place for the Goleta area. The restaurant is clean, food is good, staff is helpful. The Pho here is above average. Also try the banh mi (Vietnamese sandwiches), they are very good as well. This place bake it's own baguette and you can buy them fresh twice a day. I hope they expand their menu in the future to include other popular dishes like: bun bo hue, banh xeo, and che ba mau (sweet beans and coconut dessert). Overall a good place for lunch or dinner.
The perfect spot on a cold, gross day! Chai was perfect (I got the ginger one that they had that day), and their curry bowl hit the spot. Would definitely recommend for some yummy comfort food.

After a year hiatus we needed middle eastern food bad. 7 of us arrived to eat on a Saturday night. Plenty of room to be seated but the service is still painfully slow. ONE HOUR AND 20 MINUTES after ordering I got a falafel sandwich and a bowl of soup. And not at the same time. Sandwich was eaten and I had to remind them I ordered soup as an appetizer! The food is just ok. So waiting this long is outrageous for next to nothing ordered. A table of 6, a middle eastern family, were seated next to us. They came in after us by 30 minutes. They ordered and were gone before we saw any food and they had some of the same things my group ordered. I suggest that you need to wear a headscarf and look middle eastern to get good service and that is truly sad. I have traveled all over the world and have never experienced anything like this in any country. I eat on the economy in most places so this is not cool Petra....

Amazing service and the food was AWESOME!! My husband and I went here the other night and the woman that greeted us was awesome. The ingredients were fresh and we took our food to go, which is exactly what we wanted on a Friday movie night. This place is awesome if you want healthy to go food. Love this fresh and low cal concept. We will definitely be back!

We had lunch here on a Friday afternoon. We were the only ones there most of the time. I can't say enough good things about the food or the friendly service. We were offered free hot tea upon being seated and ended up ordering some hummus (amazing and obviously homemade) and some main dishes. Everyone loved their food, especially the soups and meat. If you're ever there and you see Kozy on the menu (made with lamb broth), order it immediately. So good! Will definitely be back.

Delicious!! Will definitely be going back again! Ordered the green curry with the coconut rice.. It was to die for! Also ordered the seafood sour soup, and seafood was sooo soft even for the squid! Definitely worth going and price is average, not so expensive!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: What an incredibly wonderful place! The man (owner?) was so great! I don't even need to say anything about the food - it was phenomenal! We all passed our dishes around and everyone tried everything - it was delicious. Hands down though the best part was the service. We arrived just before their afternoon break and he insisted we stay- glad we did! The guy was a riot! Cracked jokes, never missed a beat, and took incredible care of us. I'll be back without a doubt.

Just tried take out from here last night. I ordered the Tom Yum soup, drunken noodles and pad thai. The Tom Yum Soup was decently prepared but the only flavor that stood out was sweetness. A great Tom Yum Soup is very fragrant and flavorful and contains sour and sweet flavors combined. This soup also had an abidance of jalapeño peppers swimming around and only 4-5 shrimp for a large soup. I was a tad disappointed. The pad thai was decent and they gave a large portion, but it was a little on the dry side and I was unsure where all the seafood went as I only found two calamari and 3 shrimp in the entire dish. The drunken noodles were a disappointment. There was barely any sauce on them and they stuck together in giant clumps. The seafood factor was also lacking. Overall, it was an OK experience. I was hungry and craving thai, and was not able to drive a further distance, therefore for what I needed it satisfied my hunger. However, I do not think I would go out of my way to dine at this restaurant according to the dishes I had.

Phonomenal!!!!! This is probably the best Pho in the east bank! Best $8 you'll ever spend. The Pho comes with plenty of meat and noodles, along with one of the best broths I've had in quite a while. Third time in two weeks, so glad I discovered it!
No orders over the phone? What's so hard about taking my order and preparing food for a pick-up? Good luck in this pick up and delivery dominated food industry.

I recently moved to Nashville from Miami, and my girlfriend and I have been desperately craving a good local option for Latin Food (not Mexican Food.) We've tried a couple of other Cuban, Columbian and Salvadoran places with mixed results. When we heard about Salsa, I was cautiously optimistic. Let me first start by saying, the service was great. Our server was attentive and polite. No complaints whatsoever with the service...the food on the other hand, was a wholly different story. My girlfriend ordered the churrasco and I went with my all-time favorite the ropa vieja. We both ordered the maduro as our side. I naturally assumed that rice and beans came along with the ropa vieja, but was surprised to find that they were an additional charge. When my plate arrived it was a small portion of meat with 4 small plantains on the side. Serving ropa vieja, "in the Cuban Style" without rice and beans is equivalent to serving spaghetti without the pasta in my opinion. I have eaten this dish all over Latin America and the Caribbean, and at $17, Salsa's take on it ranked very low on my scale. Not much flavor and somewhat odd without the standard black beans and rice. My girlfriend's churrasco did have great flavor, but reminded me more of a traditional American steak in flavor, almost an A-1 steak sauce sort of sauce. Overall, I left feeling unsatisfied with the portion size and overall flavors of the restaurant.

I'm a great fan of the Pakistani cuisine at this casual place in northeast Philadelphia. After chatting with the new owner I learned that it's undergoing renovations and the appearance will improve soon. The quality of food is amazing and the owner would like to maintain the consistency of food that the customers have always enjoyed here.

Beautiful decor. Very good food. Please dont tell Jasmin Thai we cheated on them. The coconut soup was made with sweet sour chicken giving it an extra kick. Everything can be ordered in mild, medium or hot so wimps like me can devour their pad thai (I know im spelling that wrong sry) without needing to stop for water every few bites. Their homemade spicy mustard was also very nice. The sauces complimented to egg roll very well with my preference being the sweet sauce. Very friendly amd prompt staff. Clean bathrooms. We will definitely be back.
Super good! I'm quickly becoming a regular. I personally like the yellow curry (with a side of white rice) & also the fried rice

I love the atmosphere for drinks even if they are pricy. I like the outside deck because I can smoke. It gets really crowded on the weekends and the live music is usually too loud and sucks. I like going during the week to chill and decompress. I really like their fried shrimp basket, it's a lot of food and yummy but, I'm usually half in the bag by the time I order it. I do use Uber btw. I have gone there for straight lunches and the food, generally is quite good. There's usually a wait for a table outside but, kill the time at the bar. Great place, I recommend it.
Great meal for 3 under $50 with tip. Everything was great. Get all the appetizers: tofu spring rolls, dumplings, satey, wontons, noodle dishes were amazing. Curries rock!
One of the best food truck there is. The food is high quality, the crew is nice, always smiling and prompt. I eat here almost everyday.

This is only 2nd time I've had Thai food so I do not have many experiences to judge them against but this was VERY good ! I would definitely come back. What we had lemongrass soup, Coconut Soup, drunkin noodles w/shrimp, and Red curry w/chicken all very very good. The only thing that was just ok was a shrimp corn appetizer. What was even better it was BYOB. Will return.

I think it's a dangerous proposition to offer so many different types of Asian cuisine under one roof. I naturally think it's going to be a lot of mediocre options instead of one very good thing. I asked the waitress what she recommended or what their specialty was. She threw out a few of their popular roles and mentioned a few other things including their Korean fried chicken. I got their Ramen knowing full well that it wouldn't compare to what I have had so my expectations were where they needed to be. It was decent. The noodles were nice and firm and the egg was great. The broth lacked the creamy richness that a specialty ramen place in Little Tokyo would have. My friend got the bimbimbap and we shared a mix of the spicy and soy chicken. Why 5 stars? Their amazing Korean Fried Chicken! We ended up talking to the owner and her Korean husband is the chef so there you go! This chicken is authentic and awesome. Crispy but ooey gooey in spicy sweet sauce. In a town known for its love for hot chicken, I feel like this place should forget everything else and just be a Korea meets Nashville chicken place! Go check it out and get yourself some chicken!

One of my favorite, if not my favorite lunch spot in KOP. Service is always friendly and quick. Every menu item is fresh and crisp. The bread is baked and prepared in house. I always been treated with kindness by the staff here. The chicken shawarma is my personal favorite over the beef. The reason why is the seasoning of the chicken is a more traditional Za' Tar spice, it's one of my favorite ingredients in my own cooking. When you eat it, and taste that flavor you can't place, it Za' Tar (pronounced Zah Toe). The main flavor component is sumac. Word of warning though, if you are gluten free, the chicken is not. Za' Tar had roasted wheat in it. Overall delicious here and very clean as well. I sampled the falafel today. Although not overly impressed, as I've eaten better, it is still tasty.

I've been to Zorba's twice now and had good food both times. The exterior does suggest a cheesy college town version of a Greek restaurant. However the food is anything but mediocre. On my last trip I had a soutsoukis pita sandwich and a greek salad. The Greek salad had an abundance of vegetables, a flavorful dressing, and delicious olives(watch out for the pits!). The soutsoukis pita sandwich was good, if a bit messy. The waiter was very attentive and filled my water numerous times. My only complaint was that it took a little long to get my sandwich, considering that there were not that many people in the restaurant.

Ok so the hubby and I are visiting SB for our 10 year anniversary. We are huge lovers of Thai food, after checking out the reviews we thought we would Try it.Man! was it not good at all. We had the Tom Kah which was way too milky, then we ordered ( feeling adventurous) duck roll.... More like the yuck roll. It just tasted bad and it was wrapped in tortilla, what?!?! We ordered 2 orders of sticky rice. They only had one order left which was ok. We also ordered the spicy basil beef. The beef was grey and tasteless. All in all this was the worst thai food we have ever eaten. Happy Anniversary!
Another fantastic evening at Desi Village. They treat everyone like family. The food is great, we just let the staff order for us.

I came here for a friend's birthday dinner with a total party of 8. I was really excited to try Zagol because I've heard they have tons of options for vegetarians (which they do!). I felt like we had to wait a really long time for pretty much everything: to order our food, to get the food, to pay for our food. That did put a little damper on the evening for me but I will say that the food is absolutely delicious and I will definitely be going back again. The wait could have been because we had such a large party so perhaps if it's just a couple of people it won't be so bad. Also, they waited until after we ordered to inform us that they would not be able to split the check at all which meant that one person had to pick up the entire bill (I mean, who carries cash now-a-days?!). To sum up - great food - not so great customer service but not so bad that I won't be back again.

This restaurant is located on the first floor of the hotel I was staying at and my first stop during my first time in Philadelphia. I got in late and went to straight here to grab a bite. The restaurant had a dim light modern vibe and it could be a numerous of eateries. I like asking for recommendations from the servers and it did not disappoint! I ordered the lamb ribs, a side of yogurt sauce and baby greens salad. They were all delicious!

I've frequented Siam Elephant on a consistent basis for the past four years. The lunch menu that is available during the week is great! You get more food than you pay for. Everything is beyond delicious and the employees are always so kind. They recently renovated the inside, as well as the patio outside seating area. It looks phenomenal. I wish there was more outside eating available since Siam is located in a beach town with a lot of corporate offices and tourists. I have also noticed that service is not what it used to be - they used to be a lot more attentive. Now you have to literally get their attention to get the check or order something. If you live in Carp, vacationing in Carp or driving through - Siam Elephant is one delicious Thai restaurant that is a must try.

Awesome and very kind people run this place, so I'm glad to review it. I had the chicken satay taco, spicy style. It was great and the avocado was tasy. No line later in the day so if you walk by after two then its not busy. The guy liked my hat, so that was pretty sweet! I would try it again.

Delicious and very affordable! Must try. We had the chicken kabob and the hummus plate.. The hummus was fresh and delicious, and the portion was huge for the price. I eat this type of food regularly and this was very affordable in comparison. I will be back next time I am in Santa Barbara.

Great go-to Thai joint. The food is good, but won't blow your socks off. It's a wonderful, "Hey let's grab some Thai take-out and watch Stranger Things" place to go. I like the Pad Thai, the missus thinks its so-so. We both agree that the Green Curry is yum yum.

Loved it! Waited to long to try this gem! Went for the lunch buffet and everything was fresh and had great authentic flavor. Decor was nice. Had traditional Bollywood videos. Management was very welcoming and friendly. Can't wait to go back!
food was not hot.. But went a friend, who is a regular and said we got their a little late for the hot stuff..
Another great night at Dmitri's Shrimp Scampi - I love that slightly burnt garlicy taste and the huge Greek Salad w/ greens was so fresh and delish. So good.
Awesome food and even better people. The sandwiches are great and the summer rolls and bubble tea are he best around town.

Food was decent but the service was below par. Cashier didn't know any of the price or anything about how the combo system worker, best part was that the manager was next to her just chilln and didn't offer any assistance.
Food is pretty excellent. Depending on who you get your service can be from a 4 to a 10. Drinks r ok. The food and free parking after 5 is what keeps me coming back

I so wanted to like this place. I was really looking forward to my first visit. I had reserved a table for 12 but gave management warning that we might end up with closer to 20. They were ready for a dozen of us, which is the number of our group who actually arrived. The drinks were not what we were expecting. The papayack and pina coladas were lacking. For adult beverages you'd be hard-pressed to convince me there was any alcohol in either. The calamari was deep fried to rock-hardness. The empanadillas were so-so. The pernil was pretty good, as was the mofongo relleno de pollo. Our visiting house guest had the fricase de pollo which was all fricase and no pollo. He went home and immediately made a sandwich. If you're looking for Puerto Rican cuisine, this place is hit or miss. Just don't go hungry because the service is EXTREMELY slow. Our waitress put on a good show of being attentive when you could actually get her to the table...but once she left, it was "out of sight, out of mind." A few more staff wouldn't hurt...or maybe just train the existing staff on how to wait tables? The best part of the entire evening was the live music.

This place is amazing. I had the vegetarian special, my husband had the sardine special, both were completely delicious, and our total with two drinks was $10. $10! Seriously, don't go here unless you like eating delicious food and not paying tons of money for it. A+.

The food is so good here! i had my first Pad Thai here and it was great. We had the fried spring rolls too which were delicious and also grilled veggies with a peanut dipping sauce. Everything was great! The place was really nice and the servers were very friendly.

My girlfriend and I walked in tonight (Saturday) at 8:30 and ordered two falafel sandwiches with what I assumed came with, bag of lays and fries. First time here, I assumed that the sandwiches came with a side. They don't. That's fine... but I didn't know that sides were outrageous (3.89). 8 bucks for a bag of chips and fries? Cmon. Also, it comes on a pita, not the bread they're known for and that the cashier sold us on. $23 for two sandwiches, bag of chips, side of fries. Anyways, the falafel didn't taste like any falafel I've ever had. Bland, with a side of disappointment. This place is good to soak up alcohol. That's about it.
Amazing shrimp biryani and swee corn chowder soup. The place is immaculate and lovely and the food is wonderful. I picked up my order but next time will go back to eat in!

Hidden gem alert! My friends and I enjoyed an absolutely delicious dinner at Golden Triangle last night. The selection was an extensive array of Malaysian, Burmese, and Thai foods. We started by splitting the roti and Burmese salad; both were very flavorful and delicious. Each of us LOVED our entrees. The green curry was one of the best curries I've had! To top it off, the deep-fried ice cream was quite a treat! The waitstaff was very attentive and made us feel like we were guests in their home. It was an all-around wonderful experience. I highly recommend Golden Triangle and can't wait to go again soon!

Food was...meh. I guess on the up side, I didn't eat too much--diet win! Service was interesting. Before being seated, I asked about separate checks, and with reluctance the lady running the place agreed. As I sat I asked if a credit card was okay, and again was met with a less than cheerful response with something like "now that you're seated I won't turn you away." With that, I should have left. As an optimist, apparently, I never learn--I stuck it out. We ordered a combo vegetable and meat platter, intended for multiple people. The bill arrived. I again asked about separate checks, and since other restaurants seem to have no problem splitting group meals, I was surprised to learn than the combo order meant there would be no split bill. She did agree to put a designated amount on my card. I so didn't want to have to think or calculate that night, but I did the math was able to use my card (not my AmEx--visa and Mastercard only). I didn't actually really like any of the food I tried, and we had several items. I also wasn't fond of the Ethiopian tea or the honey wine I took a sip of. It was nice to try something different. There was some fun décor.

Glad We Went Through this Gateway We visited their restaurant on Bay Pines Blvd. It was quite good. We started with the Kerala Shrimp appetizer which needed a little more zip. My wife had the Butter Chicken which was heavy and needed some brightness but was otherwise good. I had the Tandoori Platter which was great. The chicken was very tender and flavorful. We got a side of Tamarind Chutney which was fantastic. It brought the brightness that some of the dishes needed. We also got a nice Mango Lassi which should have been tarter but was nice. The Garlic Naan was terrific. Service was very good and the restaurant is nicely decorated and comfortable. I would definitely return and I would slather that Tamarind Chutney on everything.

I love this place. Really good food. Really nice people. They will make things genuinely spicy if you ask them to. The regular menu is rather extensive and full of good things, and they always have some excellent specials. The staff is very friendly and service is always quick. I wish they had more space, and I wish their beer list were more extensive. But this is hands-down the best Thai place in Santa Barbara.

Look for Thien the friendliest dude here...the staff are courteous and there beside you on a wave of a hand. They have great Pho compared to Pho 75 and have a great new menu that really makes them more than just a Pho place. The Fried Rice is the best its a meal in itself and the spring rolls never fail to delight your glum summer day. The Pho Hoa soups and noodles are there to refresh you and indeed cleans your system. Yes the restrooms have that newly cleaned scent to it . order a YANG CHOW fried rice a Number 24 and the Number 5 or 6 and get a coconut juice to wash it down the hatch.

One my favorite places to grab take out. They have really good fruit smoothies, and the baked mac n cheese is one of a kind lol. The platters are always paked with delicious food, so I normally grab a mini unless I'm sharing with my lady. Hands down a true gem in the city of Philly!!! #currygoat #oxtails #beef/cickenpatties
I hate most foreign cuisine but I'll never turn down a trip to Palace of Asia. Best Indian food around, friendly service and great prices- especially the buffet. Go immediately!

Sher-e-Punjab's DrexelHill location is much better than the Media one (food tastes better and prices are a little cheaper), though it doesn't yet have a liquor license (the Media location has a sprawling bar). I stay in Media still drive all the way here. The ala carte prices are expensive (for the quality of food and sloppy service), but the buffets are always a good deal. The buffet offers a large variety of veg and non-veg dishes, so that you can always find something that suits your palate. The service is bad (no one refills your water, no one bothers to take dirty plates off your table) unless one of the owners is present to supervise.

This place is really delicious-- the best Chinese food I've had. We usually go with a group so we can order a variety of things, but two things we always get are this delicious spicy fish stew and the spicy green beans. Before I had them at Golden Szechuan, I felt pretty meh about green beans-- they're just one of the more boring vegetables, right? But the ones at Golden Szechuan are life-changingly awesome. They're crispy and salty and spicy, and when I recommend them to people they usually look kind of sceptical, but everyone ends up loving them. So trust me, get the green beans.

This place used to be really good until a few months ago. The food doesn't taste as good and the service is getting worse. Also, they don't ask if you want anything to drink. This place was much better when it was Souksavanh

We celebrated our daughter's birthday at the restaurant and the staff was very accommodating, the food at the buffet was delicious and our guest enjoyed the meal. I found the food authentic and reasonably priced.
One of my first stops since moving to Philadelphia. Wonderful cafe, warm and inviting environment - delicious food! Great coffee.

Was a huge fan! But I should have know something was a miss when we sat down. First off let me say that I really like there food! I was so excited to show my friends a great Greek restaurant in Philadelphia ( as I managed one in NJ ) I had to use the rest room there was no toilet paper. Hey it happens!! There was paper towels instead. I told the waiter. Then when we asked for more bread and oil the server said NO I don't want you to fill up on bread! I have never been told NO by a server when asking for more bread 30 years in the business as a chef and manager I was appalled and embarrassed. Next he forgot my friends diet coke no big deal. I had to ask for pita 7 times which they do charge you for. No problem I don't mind paying but when I tell you to bring out lots of pita we are pita people bring it out! Our one guest is limited to certain foods so she orders salad and never comes. Waiter ( order taker) looks at us like we are lying and says we never order it. We get more dips xtra octopus I have to tell you I have been cooking and managing for years the food here is good Greek food. I started to feel sick I ate dips, octopus and artichokes as my meal. I went to the ladies room and got sick. Again no toilet paper. Again on my way out I paid cash and generous tip ( which should be lower due to the smirking order takers) I said to him I told someone about the no toilet paper he said there is paper towels cause we ran out! Are you serious? Go to the store and get some! 2nd reason I won't be back. We then leave. One more person gets sick eating the dips after ordering a second fish roe dip. The 3rd gets sick 2 hours after him. The 4th got sick an hour after. The only one that didn't get sick was the person who didn't eat any dips. I called and who ever answered the phone seems not to believe us. It happens in every restaurant I understand you get defensive it's natural. I really love there food! But I won't be back and it's not so much we got sick all 4 of us. It's because of the wait staff. Being told NO for bread was wrong. I'm paying for that bread it isn't free it's worked into the bill. Plus you don't tell a guest NO. The no toilet paper really bothered me when the server said they were out. Go buy some. Health Hazzard plus really you are asking ladies to use paper towels. Forgetting our coke was okay it happens. But forgetting someone's dish for there meal is something else. ( there is another review about this) I'm saddened by the turn of events that happen last night. I won't be paying cash anymore either I learned my lesson. If I paid by card I would have canceled it due to us 4 getting sick. So they are lucky I paid cash. The bill was low 105 $ but it was all apps. I gave 26$ tip. ( always tip cash for servers because they sometimes have to wait a week to get there tips) Again love the food just won't be back. They need to tighten up on line checks and temps and rotation of products so people don't get sick. I wouldn't question if it was just me but 4 of us??

This was a pleasant surprise! The food is tasty, servings generous and the calm ambience friendly for children. The bubbly wall and twirly lights were delightful. (We thought the 5-star ratings were staff-generated, but this is the real deal. A low cost 5-star experience.)

We are from the Bay area where great Indian restaurants are abundant and Shere Punjab stands up well to the competition. They have a small buffet with a very nice assortment of the standard choices, Good vegi Samosas and Pekoras. Excellent Vindaloo, do Piaza, Tikka Masala and Kormas off the menu. If you like Indian cuisine you're going to like Shere Punjab.

Highly recommended by friends... Decided to check out the Yelp reviews.. Stars galore!... Good sign... My wife and I try not to expect too much and set ourselves up for disapointment.. Kinda like that movie everyone seems to rave about, the one you struggle to get through.. Well this was not the case with Nadia Thai. We totally enjoyed the experience..Understand we are not experts in Thai food so we don't have a point of reference.... My wife had the Drunken Noodles, she's already looking forward to going back... We tried the Lemon Grass Soup for starters which tasted very fresh... I ordered the Bangkok Fried Rice w/chicken. I asked Pong our waiter to kick-up the 'heat' a bit on the dish.. It turned out to be spiced just right.. Very good... It's a rather small place, maybe 15 tables.. We didn't need reservations at 8PM..The Sat night we were there even-though there were only two open tables the noise level was very low. Two servers were working the floor, service was efficent... We left I little after nine, diners were still arriving.. There's street parking available .. We thought it was a good value.. BYOB We'll be back..
The bamboo pho here is excellent. Well priced and decent portions.

Aside from the delicious food (beef gyro and chicken shawrma) and amazing, fresh lemonade, Smiley himself may be the sweetest man in Manayunk... or the planet. So happy to have Smiley's in the neighborhood!
Best massaman curry I've ever had. Creamy and delicious, perfectly spiced. They put tomatoes in it for some reason, and I hate tomatoes, but I didn't even care. Delicious.

This place has a really nice appearance, so I was expecting great things. I have heard wonderful things about their brunch, so my friends and I decided to try out dinner. Boy was I let down!!! I got the veal special with butternut squash and spinach ravioli. The veal was bland as was the sauce it was drowning in, and the ravioli was very undercooked and almost had a "play dough" taste to it. They charged us 6 dollar side salads when it was implied that they were accompanied with the entree. The server was very odd, and made us feel very uncomfortable. Of all things, we left with our clothes reeking of grease. I will not be coming back again!

First I was little skeptic when I saw the shop. Once I went in there, it was super clean and the food was AMAZING. He is nice and caters to your needs (spicy, sweet...). I highly recommend a visit. You will be surprised.

I am a huge fan of Ethiopian food. I was interested to try out this place in comparison with Major - Abyssinia is far better! I got vegetarian platters at both restaurants, and Abyssinia definitely took the cake. The main distinction for me were the sides served on injera along with the dishes we ordered - at Abyssinia, the sides were larger, more varied, and tastier.

The dinner option were a little spendy so we opted to try Sunday brunch and it was amazing! I had the special, which was some kind of breakfast sandwich that was just full of flavors! They also had free valet, which is nice, and rare in Boise. Service was great (also rare in Boise) and so was the food. There's a reason Richard's is legendary in Boise.

Our favorite local restaurant. The only reason we don't give them 5 stars us because they don't serve wine & liquor. We go to this restaurant more than any other. Love their steamed dumplings and hot sour soup. It's the best around!

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: My husband and I ate there last night and had a fabulous meal! The service was great and the food was authentic Thai The restaurant was clean, the employees were friendly and the food was to die for! We had eaten there once before and had slow service but they seemed to have improved that over the past few months. I would definitely recommend this.

Wish the original owner were still around.....things have slipped a bit of late. Not the quality of Pho I'd like it to be, as it's less complex in taste and more expensive than one should expect......but it's still far superior to other offerings of this type in WC!!

Atrocious. I've never been treated so rudely at a restaurant, especially one with such a reputation. We had reservations for 7:30 on Saturday, when we got to the restaurant, we were told our table would be ready in 5 minutes. We ended up waiting outside in the 85 deg. heat for a half hour. No ice water or bread with olive oil was offered to us while we waited. When our table was ready, we were notified of that fact by the rude waiter peeking his head out of the door and proclaiming, "you can come in now..." We can? Thank you so much for allowing us in your restaurant! No apology whatsoever. When our waiter offered a meek and halfhearted apology, I told him that we were very upset and not impressed this being our first time at the establishment. I said that a few appetizers "on the house" would make us feel a bit better. This suggestion was taken with great offense and immediately shot down. At this point, if I was dying of hunger in the Saharan desert I wouldn't have opened my wallet for this place. We walked out without eating, an unfortunate end to a highly anticipated evening. Zeppoli, here's a tip: People who come to your place that look under 30 years old... We have money too.

We had an excellent dinner here. Food was plentiful and very tasty. We had a chicken/shrimp/pork entree and pork dumplings and had more than enough for the two of us. Our waitress was quiet but very attentive and we had no complaints about the service.

I was craving Indian. My boyfriend loves Indian food and took me to a joint in Trooper. I wasn't too fond of that place and we figured we would give this one a try. The poppadoms were delicious as well as all the chutneys. The lamb samosas were amazing. We had the chicken tikka masala. Sauce was good. I didn't like the chicken breast... wish they would have used thigh meat. Very very laid back service. I will most likely come back to try their other dishes :)

Continuing our quest to try local Asian restaurants my fiance and I came to Little Thai Cafe for dinner. It is a bit of a drive for us but we enjoy trying new places. We ordered hot tea and spring rolls and wonton soup to start. The wonton soup is very hearty and has lots of veggies. My fiance really enjoyed it and said it was his favorite part of the meal. The spring rolls were light and the dipping sauce was flavorful. I ordered the pad thai with tofu and he ordered the green curry. Both dishes were good. The portions were large. The service was initially very prompt but we had a difficult time getting refills once we were given our main courses and had to wait a long time to get the check. Given the distance from our place we probably won't return but if you're closer to Tarpon Springs then I suggest it. It was not a bad experience by any means but it's too far for us given that it's just an ok thai place.
As good as I remember :D I left Tampa 4 months ago, and was glad to be back. Got the short ribs rice that I love so much, and they brought back memories.

Great food and not overly expensive. Everything tastes freshly cooked and the tables are kept clean and organized. I highly recommend getting the Rasavat Lemonade as it tastes great with anything you order.

The best quality of food Indian restaurant hands down. Very very good South Indian food but catered to a multicultural audience. Chicken 65 (appetizer), naan (especially garlic naan), vegetable biryani (best in town), chicken biryani are very good. Service and ambience are ok. Going by just taste of the food, hands down the best Indian restaurant in Indianapolis.

Asian Chef's menu says they offer "fusion cuisine." I'm not sure if the actual dishes are fusion, but I think it's more like they offer several types of asian cuisine, including (from what I've noticed- there may be more) Japanese, Chinese and Thai. I have honestly enjoyed every style of food I've had here. The meat in the wonton soup didn't creep me out like it does at some places, the shrimp with broccoli has plenty of sauce and large, perfectly cooked shrimp, the sushi was fresh and delicious, and the drunken noodles were so yum! When we go with a large group during our strict 1 hour lunch, we call ahead so our food will be ready when we get there. Asian Chef always has a big table set for us and our drinks and soups/salads are served immediately. They keep up with all of our requests, and are always ready with the bill so we can pay and jet. I've tried a bunch of the other Asian restaurants in Mt. Laurel (most serving only one kind of cuisine), but there really is no reason to go anywhere but Asian Chef. Well played with your Fusion Cuisine, Asian Chef. Well played.

We decided to stop in for lunch around 2:30 or so. There were only three other tables full at the restaurant, yet it took forever to sit down. Then when we decided to order something on the menu it was either run out for the day or they didn't have it at all. I ended up getting their hibiscus drink- it tasted like it came from a high c Bottle. My husband got the fried catfish and I got the curry chicken. Disliked both-Chicken was cold and pink on The inside. The only good thing about the meal was the black beans and rice and fried plantains. Not very impressed nor will we be back.

Foods up and down but mostly up. Decor is recently renovated but a little quirky with multiple chandeliers and unfinished booths. Service was slow despite a not full restaurant but requests for specific tea were definitely honored. Don't miss naan stuffed with raisins and nuts. Plenty of parking in front.

As a former restaurant worker and current nurse (service industry), I regret to say that despite the reviews on yelp, this place was probably the worst experience I've had in a few years. The service was slow, and i mean- you are wondering where and who your waiter is, drinks left empty for maybe 15 min., and no one dare ask how your food is- bc even they know it's probably cold. Now for the food, it was cold, tasteless, and sparse. What a waste of time and money. No offense, but anyone rating this place higher than a few stars is probably coming from true middle east (2nd world) service and food. It def belongs in the pawn shop ghetto complex is currently resides in. This was the final insult to the Tampa area we visited. PS: the water park in tampa is for the neck tattooed only. You want good middle eastern food, I don't know what to tell you- but it isn't here. And yea, I've been to the middle east, and Michigan. Yum.

Went here a couple weeks ago, as it is a newer establishment and we like to support local business. First off, this place was formerly a Smashburger and basically nothing has changed in terms of decorations and ambiance (there's a few random rustic signs up, but it kind of seems out of place given the contemporary feel). Anyway, service was awful! We waited about 10-15 min to even get noticed after we were seated and then went up to the hostess counter to get their attention. The waitress promptly came over and apologized stating that the hostess never notified her that she had a table. Based on this, there seems to be lack of communication between all employees. All of the employees should be communicating and helping each other out and whatever personal matters they have should be put aside. However, after this hiccup, the service got better and the waitress was pretty attentive. Food was pretty decent (not mind-blowing but acceptable). All in all, I'd chose this over ihop.
Excellent pad Thai! Delicious Thai iced tea, definitely recommend. Very small space, doubt they can accommodate more than 6 in a table. Nice people, slow waiters.

hidden hole in the wall with the best gyro in st louis. i had the gyro with hummus and it was stuffed with lots of meat. the portions were generous to say the least and the pita bread and hummus is perfect. pick up some excellent greek food to go!

Good food. Prices are a bit high but the quality of the dishes ss worth the small amount more. My curry wasn't as spicy as I like, even after asking for very spicy hot. I'd consider their spicy as medium hot. We'll go back for sure!

I've tried this a couple of times, and I was not impressed either time. The first time I tried it was the first day it opened in 2010. I decided since they were new, I would give them time to get all of their kinks worked out and then try them again. Unfortunately, the second time was not any better. As another reviewer said, their food is healthy, but because fat equals flavor, the result is flavorless, dry food. There is very little moisture in the meat, so you need a lot of water to supplement your meal. I love rice of all sorts, but sadly, their rice is also too dry and has a flavor of overcooked peas and carrots. The smoothies are not made from real fruit, and as a result, end up being a bit grainy. The bubble tea was also misses the mark, as the bobas are undercooked and the drink itself lacks in flavor. I really wanted to like Blu Fig, since there are no other Mediterranean restaurants close to my house and I love to support local businesses, but this was just not very good.
The best Vietnamese food around. Don't be fooled by the name, this is good eats. I recommend the pho and BBQ pork rolls.

I was craving Greek food, but didn't have the time to run out and get it. Ordered delivery from Yia's Yia's Greek Express and it was DELICIOUS! I was very happy with my food and the delivery time was very fast. I will definitely be ordering from here again.
Delicious food without any belly problems, which tells me that they make a good selection of ingredients. It is also fairly cheap. Went there for dinner and the other day for lunch, was that good!

Taziki's has made me believe in second chances. Let me explain. I first had Taziki's as take-out. Twice, in fact. They were mildly disappointing both times- I had gyros and the taziki (in the name of the restaurant!) was too sour and the sides were not impressive (particularly the rice). They were skimpy on the lamb and the pita wasn't as soft as I was hoping. But this was also when the restaurant just opened, and I am comparing to Athens, one of the better Greek places in the area. But then, this week, I ate in at Taziki's and it totally redeemed itself. The service was prompt, the hummus was delicious and I ordered the oven-roasted pork tenderloin, which was amazing. The salad with the dressing, first off, was really quite good- the dressing was perfect, not too sour at all. The pork was cooked well and the aioli was SO good. Perfectly complimented the pork, rice and asparagus. Wow! I am so glad I went back. I probably will stick to the entrees like the pork rather than the gyros, but I was happy to get a great, delicious, satisfying meal eating in.

Hot Stuff! "Spice", I believe is the key word here. If you like it hot-n-spicy, you will not be disappointed. Those seeking more timid Thai should head down the street to King & I, but if you think you're up for the challenge, give Basil Spice a try. Service is exceptional.

Nice Thai place, particularly for this part of the country. Tom Yum soup witch chicken was delicious..the half portion was very large. Chicken basil was decent..nice portions..the medium was mild. Chicken was was good, green beans were clearly frozen, could have done without. Very friendly staff. Clean modern but cozy interior.

The vegetable naam salad is soooo good. And banana chocolate spring rolls - why isn't the entire world making/eating these??? Such a cosy place, and perfect for byo since the liquor store is less than a block away! A +
The best Pho I have found in Reno. I usually get my order to go and they are quick and efficient. They pack my order beautifully and I get more than one meal out of it.
Horrible service I have gone here multiple times and they always mess up the order. Tonight I ordered a tropical chop and I asked for gravy twice and they said ok and surprise surprise no gravy.

Love the food, good and so delicious.We drive all the way from DC and stop here for lunch..bit hard to find the place specially if u not from PA area.i'm definitely come back what ever I got the change
Excellent food, service and atmosphere. Prices are low.My wife even loved the food even though she thought she wouldn't like Indian food.

went thru their drive thru, horrible experience, like the first poster mentioned, it took an hour for something that shouldn't have taken that long considering it wasn't peak hour. On top of the long wait and lack of manners of the managers when asked why it was taking so horribly long, the food wasn't up to standards when serving people, our 2 meals were warm when we received them, the only thing that was hot was the soup, which tasted like they put half a galon of curry paste
A Must Try awesome people and great food. Chicken and waffle "So GooD MaKe U WaNnA sLaP yA MaMa"

As a newcomer to Narberth, I was very enthusiastic about trying this place. I sure wish I liked it more. The food is decent: the pad thai is good and my kids loved the turkey dumplings; the lemongrass soup was underflavored, and the curry we ordered was underspiced. But as many other customers have noted, the main problem with this place is that it's really expensive for what you get. $17-19 for an ordinary Thai curry strikes me as high, and I do not share another poster's judgment that the portions are large. The kicker was a $1.50 charge on our bill for "extra rice." Well, we hadn't ordered any extra rice, and the only rice we received was 2 scoopfuls served on the curry dish. So we asked about the charge. The answer? The curry comes with only 1 scoop of rice (not a bowl, a scoop), but because that's so little, they gave us 2 on their own initiative and charged us for the second. Well, I'm not going to cry over $1.50, but I must say that left a really bad taste. It's bad form, in my view, for an Asian restaurant ever to charge for extra rice. But it's crazy to charge for "extra" rice that isn't even requested. And they tacked on a 20% gratuity for our party of 6. That's what I ordinarily tip so no big harm done, but added to the high prices, and the "extra rice" charge, we left feeling rather ill-used.
Nice place... alittle on the expensive side but you cant beat the view

Delicious and so affordable! I love going here as everything on the menu is great and most everything is $6-8. I haven't tried anything I didn't like so far. The portions are also very reasonable. This is a family owned restaurant and the owners are so friendly.

I can't believe nobody has reviewed Bitar's. They have very inexpensive falafel sandwiches which are grilled and not fried, some of the best hummus in Philly, a little grocery area where you can buy dried fruit, beans and middle eastern pastries. The food here is very consistently good. I'm a huge fan of the Angelo Cataldi chicken sandwhich whish has this very yummy red pepper sauce. It's actually making me hungry just thinking about it. Mmmm. I just found out that they opened new locations in W. Philly and Society Hill. This is good news for folks in those neighborhoods. Definitely stop by and check it out.

This little hole in the wall is the best. No liquor license but you can sit across the street at the local bar and have the hostess come over when your table is ready, What a treat. Do not miss the grilled octopus it's the best I ever had and I've had it just about everywhere. Fabulous grilled whole fish, the Pompano happens to be my favorite. And the Greek salad is wonderful also. If you love fish, the bluefish, Greek style will fit your bill. Be patient...because the wait is worth it. Enjoy!!!

My wife and I have been going here for over 5 years. We are definitely regulars and go here at least every 2 weeks. I also go to their buffet during the week once in a while (FYI- go on Fridays or Sundays for the Chicken Tika Masala). I was surprised to read that some folks have received poor service. The service at Shere Punjab is nothing to write home to mama about, but we have NEVER been ignored or received slow service. I cannot figure why that may have happened, but my guess is it may be because Rashpaul (one of the owners) was short staffed that day. The food is consistently good. We have never had a bad meal, and it is reasonably priced. Give them a try!

This is a nice little Middle Eastern market in the same plaza as Mays Ulreem Pita, a large hookah lounge and a Marine recruiting place.. Boon thinks he's a tough guy? They have date cookies, halvah, ginger honey and lots of other interesting snacks and foods as well as some prepared chicken, meat and spinach pies, plus baklava.type desserts and a few other prepared foods. The owner is friendly. I believe he's from Jordan. We enjoyed our visit.

The service was fast and the restaurant is located on the busy delmar loop, so it has a good location. Tried a noodle dish and a stir fry. Waaaaaaay too much salt. Given the fact that there are a few other Thai restaurants within walking distance, I can safely say that we won't eat there again. Too bad, because the staff was super nice. But again, if your food ain't good, can't expect to get a good rating

My wife and I went here on Saturday for a late lunch. We had seen the relatively good yelp reviews and were looking forward to trying somewhere new, it seems like the city has been loosing good Asian style fare for the past decade, so I am hopeful when a new place gives it a shot. On the upside the whole staff there was relatively friendly and attended to us right away. They have a patio and I do like to sit outside in nice weather, it did not look like they allowed smoking outside so that is an even BIGGER plus. Unfortunately, this is all I can say to their favor. The inside appeared sparsely decorated and was not welcoming or comfortable so I was even happier that there was outdoor seating. The menu is simple, maybe too simple? But ok and rolled with it. It was a build your own Pad-Thai or pho or Asian wrap. We and started with apps. I wanted Crab Rangoon and my wife ordered wantons. My CRs were cooked well, but the filling was very bland. They brought my wife what I would call "crispy noodles" covered in powdered sugar. When we asked why we received a desert, the waitress was like "oh..those are our wantons". Uh..ok. She explained that other people had mentioned that app won-tons were "maybe a thing in St. Louis"....Yep... Look I love experimentation, but it would have helped if they had a blurb on the menu. I had a Pad Thai w chicken & avocado, egg, tomato, sweet pepper & broccoli. My wife had tofu, tomato, egg, spinach and snow peas. Let's just say they lapsed on the details. HINT: make a little cheat sheet for your waitstaff to use so they don't forget stuff. Memorizing an order may seem cool and hip, but screwing it up makes you look silly. But to conclude, and most importantly: The food was bland and tasteless. It killed them to put a piece of snow pea on a dish? I do not want to go further as the rest of the meal was disappointing. I ate because I was hungry, but was glad to leave. Clearly this restaurant is off to a poor start and I did not get the impression it would get better. The staff were wonderful and kind (and is the only reason I gave it an additional star) so this does not rest at their feet, this is a management and owner issue. I do not recommend at this time and I am not willing to give it a second chance.

I was visiting my daughter in Clearwater when I came across this restaurant. I love Indian food, so I decided to stop and dine. The lunch buffet was outstanding! The vast variety on the buffet included vegetarian as well as meat dishes. Everything I sampled was delicious. The restaurant is roomy, spacious and well kept. The service was wonderful as well. I will be back to enjoy this scrumptious food every time ai visit my daughter in Clearwater.

We went to Masala Kitchen for Lunch today. We like spicy indian food and I must say we had best indian food ever in delaware, may be better than restaurants in India. I suggest you should definitely have Pav Bhaji and Vada Pav there. Will plan to go there most often.
A great find! Staff was exceptional and the food was delicious. Definitely deserving of 5 stars!

Crap Ragu was very good nice Thai style type prep,pad see EW chicken curry #2 heat nice was also excellent that is a 5-star however for the price the portions are small and they do not serve rice with it which is very untraditional for any Oriental restaurant not to do serve rice ,alsos took over 30 mins and they were not that busy at all im fair guy , also pop was very FLAT ,overall I'd give it a three-star because the food was good .

Wonderful place for lunch. Pan D'Olive had it all - great food, wonderful decor, personable and attentive staff (Sarah), fantastic value, wide array of culinary choices, ample parking and various seating options. I'm scoring Pan D'Olive way above my previous encounters with 'small plate' establishments. Indulged in aracini, spinach salad, eggplant and hummus. I can't wait to go back and then, maybe a 5-star rating! (just don't want to jinx it now)

The food is simply amazing! We ordered lamb vindaloo, mixed tandoori, and a couple of other small dishes. The amount of butter and oil was just right and the taste was very authentic. The food came a little slow but it was worth the wait.

If you are into food and cooking, sit at the counter near the grill. (It is hot but the A/C is adequate). The whole grilled sea bass was the best I've had in years. The grilled octopus, scallops and tomato basil salad were excellent. Every dish that came by made us wish we had ordered it. At $68 for two people without drinks, it is not cheap but well worth it. I plan to return with my teenagers who are now fascinated with cooking. Otherwise it is not a place for kids.
Genuine Authentic Real deal My favorite lunch spot. Appetizer and soup are worth the wait.

Probably my fav Thai restaurant. Their green curry is on the hotter side but so flavorful. I also like to order the garlic beef and their fresh spring rolls. I love that they have a pickup window/drive-thru for when you want to call your order in. We tried Thai iced tea for the first time the last time we were there and it was a nice sweet treat.

yayy. I go here on a semi-regular basis with my bf. Their service is always fast and impeccable, pho is hot and filled with delicious noodles and goodies, and we always have a wonderful selection of hot things to add to the pho. The prices are also quite reasonable.

Although my experience with Vietnamese food in Nashville is limited, I will say that this place is comparable in value to some of my favorite Vietnamese restaurants in New York (e.g., Nha Trang Centre). Pros: The pho has just the right proportion of noodles, mysterious meats, and broth along with a healthy side serving of bean sprouts, mint, and jalapenos. They also have Che 3 Mau (3-colored sweet ice drink) and other treats to satisfy the sweet tooth who craves something a little more than an icee flavored with sugar water. With regards to ambience, let's just say I can't fully enjoy my pho experience now without a large picture of a black panther against the backdrop of the twin towers. Cons: Service could be a tad faster. Our order for two banh mi's took so long I could've finished two bowls of pho in that time.

Undeniably one of our favorite spots in town. Greek home cooking by a wonderful Greek family. Decor and atmosphere is exactly what you'd expect from an unpretentious spot like this, so come for the food not the red carpet. The cold and hot appetizer plate is amazing, everything on there...though it can be very garlic heavy. Every other dish we've tried has been excellent. Perfect spot to drink and eat too much. Love this place beyond words.

Great Chinese food, presented beautifully. Maybe the best in the city. My visit should have ranked four stars, but a few matters got in the way. They were busy, even for a 1 p.m. lunch, which affected service. The single waitress was harried and forgot the first course of my meal, which was delivered after the entree, only when I reminded her of it. In some ways a typical neighborhood Chinese joint with unoriginal art and furnishings out of the Chinese Restaurant Supply Mega Warehouse. But in other ways a superlative experience. The menu is a bit unique, and even the lunch menu, with very modest prices, held gems like tofu with lemongrass, which I ordered and enjoyed very much. Their eggrolls are crisp, fresh, and delicious. As I mentioned, the place was bustling, but I was utterly distracted by the young adults at the table next to me. Notably loud and foul-mouthed there was no way I could remove myself from their influence, other than leave the place. I realize that this isn't the fault of the restaurant, but it did contribute to a diminished experience. And maybe the restaurant does bear some responsibility for recognizing when patrons' behavior becomes obnoxious and ask that they exercise courtesy.

Good food. First time here. Liked the Lava Tempura app, good amount of heat and a nice sweet dipping sauce to complement it. I also had Tom Yun with pork. Very good, mild spice (they ask when you order how hot you want it) with juicy pork, a few meatballs, lots of noodles and fresh baby bok choy. I'll be back to try more menu items.

Nothing I can add here that hasn't already been said. The friendly owner will guide you through the menu like a champ and introduce you to the wonderful world of lassi and chaat. A delicious, flavorful, fresh meal to go. Choose the lamb - it's heavenly.

We just tried the Persian Room tonight for dinner and it was wonderful from start to finish! The hostess staff was very friendly when we called ahead as well as when we arrived at the restaurant. Inside is decorated so beautifully, our kids loved the fountain wall and the painted ceiling! Our server was very helpful and took great care of us all night. When you first sit down they bring you a basket of Persian bread with a plate of fresh herbs, butter and onions. We were all surprised at how wonderful all the flavors were together! Such a simple and welcome start to our meal. We decided to try their appetizer sampler and one of the combination plates to share since it was our first time. Portions are very generous and everything was so amazing! The stuffed grape leaves are a must try! We somehow had room for dessert and ordered the baklava with saffron and pistachio ice cream. Again just blown away by how good it was! Needless to say we will absolutely be back! So excited to have this wonderful restaurant right up the road from our home!

Great kabsa and mandi; we drive around 45 minutes to get to this place. Portions are excellent for the price. The guys don't speak fluent English, but are generally nice. Seems like they're always out of chicken kabsa and/or mandi. Tried calling around noon for chicken kabsa or mandi and they'd be out already. You'd think they would make more considering they sell out fast, but feedback is not generally not even understood, so that's a waste.

We had catered from Tandoor for a club event, and were incredibly happy with not only the food but also the awesome service! Brian, the owner, brought our food to our location himself and helped us rearrange our tables several times! He made sure to constantly check that everything was ok, and whether Tandoor could do anything else. I really think they went the extra mile! Tandoor offered the best price by far! We have already placed our next big order with Tandoor, and look forward to catering from them for many more events to come!

The food is excellent. So far I've had the pad Thai, the green curry, and the panang curry. Each as flavorful, delicious, and plenty hot enough! The Thai hot is tasty and extremely hot. The hot is extremely hot, and the medium has plenty of flavor. They have a wonderful family atmosphere. My family and I keep coming back and so far everything that we've had is delicious. My father can't get enough of the fried rice, and he's a 75 year old man stuck in his ways!

Having been to little Ethiopia in L.A. many times, , every Ethiopian restaurant in Berkeley and many in the Bay Area, was so pleasantly surprised to find this place in Reno. The food is awesome.....I am a vegetarian so Ethiopian food is nice as it provides one of the few tasty choices for vegetarian food. The owner is super sweet and nice. She is always there herself working, every time I have been there. The food is on par with the best Ethiopian restaurants in larger cities, which in Reno, for ethnic foods, I have found to be extraordinarily rare. Great food, good environment, great people. Recommend this place highly.

This is my new favorite place to eat in Nashville. The food is absolutely amazing, and the atmosphere is awesome! How can you not love a 90's nightclub themed restaurant with K-Pop playing on the projection TV? This place is so much fun with friends! The menu is a wonderful mix of Asian-fusion with some of the best (and biggest) sushi I've had. Try the Korean Fried Chicken and the kimchi fries, you won't be disappointed. Every time I go I try something new and every time they knock it out of the park!

My post from Seamless: I think Little Kitchen has "Jerry" the toothless meth addict cooking for them, Greedy McGreederson setting the prices, and Fred Flintstone on delivery. First of all, I had very low expectations ordering a Japanese dish from a Chinese place. But they even underperformed my low bar. The miso soup was just gross. It looked like they got all the ingredients right but still managed to make it taste like crap. Quite an accomplishment! Then the chicken teriyaki...OMG, I think Jerry ran out of teriyaki sauce last week and has been subbing it with the broccoli beef sauce. I've got this hoisin/oyster sauce taste in my mouth and it won't go away no matter how much chinese white rice I force down my throat. Ahhh someone help me please? And they have the gaul to charge $16 for this bullshit and deliver it 20 minutes late. NEVER EVER AGAIN. Sorry, but you guys suck, royally.

I went there looking for a great donair poutine and had a hard time finding parking. once that was solved go in and just saw the top banner with meal deals but not full menu in sight. I knew what I wanted and asked if they had it. poutine donair. was served hot but had it for take out so no salt and vinegar for the fries and white sauce was on the donair meat. was good healthily potion, but taste wise was not out standing but ok. if near there would go again and try something else. service was fast and efficient and they cater to the bar after crowds. was small clean place. I think they will do well in their location.
Great food at an affordable price. Portions are large. They are a little cheap with their pita but still a great place.

The food here is REALLY good. I was extremely surprised considering the location. (Next to a gas station) Anyhow I totally recommend this place. Warning: There is a gentleman there that is super grumpy and short when answering you. Don't mind him, he's harmless! Lol.

What a disappointing evening out! After waiting an hour and a half, being promised repeatedly that our food was cooking, the owner/waiter finally admitted that he had made a mistake and not put our order in at all. While we were there, we watched other tables receiving the wrong orders and leaving without eating. We eventually did the same.

I came here the other weekend and ordered the chicken pho and the chicken vermicelli bowl. This order was for take out - the place has about 7 tables and it was pretty busy when I got in there, my order took about 20 minutes which is average . Once I got home I dug in, honestly I wish the broth for the pho had more flavour, I felt like I had to add more than usual. Also the noodles I wasn't a fan of. The chicken was cooked fine and I liked the bag of add ons. For the vermicelli, the chicken was amazing, veggies fresh and the noodles were great. The fish sauce was perfect, I would order this one again.

We had a date night at the Persian Room last Thursday. I'd been seeing neighbors post on our local Nextdoor and we wanted to see what the hype was about. We were NOT disappointed. The location had us leery that there would be anything to see, but they've managed to turn a boring facade in a run-of-the-mill strip mall into a delightful update on ancient Babylon. From the moment you walk in, there is no question about the cultural affiliation of the restaurant and the restaurant is set with homey old-fashioned heavy wood tables with ornate carvings. The chandeliers and wall sconces are very ornate and the booths are dark wood and quite comfortable. The tables would be amazing for family-style dinners and I was incredibly impressed with the large groups (families?) we saw dining there. My husband and I were shown to a comfortable booth near the door. Our waiter immediately asked if we'd been there before and explained the different entrees. Sadly, we had made the mistake of eating a late lunch, so after hearing about the entrees, we decided that we needed to split one. The waiter agreed to permit us to order the koobideh for two with one chicken and one lamb. Yum. He also explained the different types of rice for us (they have 4) and we selected a combination of saffron and dill flavored rices. We were going to start with both the lentil soup and the hummus, but decided to just do hummus this visit. This was a good plan. The hummus is a delicate fava bean hummus with a lighter taste and color than a traditional chickpea hummus. It is DELIGHTFUL. The pita bread with which it was served was obviously fresh-made in house and was served at the perfect temperature. We almost licked the bowl. If you don't order a starter, the pita bread is served with butter, fresh herbs, and onion. We tried it (mine was without the butter because it seemed odd) and were super impressed! Who would've thought eating herbs and onion raw would be that good! Not me, for sure. The koobideh was HUGE! Even after cutting out one appetizer, we couldn't finish the plate! The chicken koobideh, I found to be better seasoned than the lamb, but they were both quite good. The rice was EXCELLENT. We finished the leftovers and the lamb was far better the next day! Our waiter and the manager were attentive and checked in to verify that we were enjoying the food. The service was impeccable. Sadly, we were too full to try dessert, but the pistachio baklava was calling to me. This restaurant has an enormous menu and even has vegetarian options. We cannot wait to go back, though it'll, take us years to eat through the menu!

This business is now under new management. I felt that I could feel the difference in the improved service I found this round versus previous visits. Our visit included the lunch buffet and a fresh made from scratch mango lassi. I really appreciated how the staff kept mentioning that it was made from scratch. Even if it were not, it mentally made me enjoy it even more. Smart marketing and product pride! The lunch buffet featured two soup options, several light and healthy salads, desserts and at least ten entrée options. My favorites were the daal and paneer masala. Unfortunately, the galub jamon could use a little work. It appears that they mixed a fresh batch with an old one which resulted in dense and dry balls rather than the fluffy fresh combo. Maybe it was just my perception with the new management, but the space felt a little more clean and inviting this round. Rumor has it they have some fun events planned for the catering space that is behind the restaurant. Keeping my eyes peeled!

This was my first experience with Carribean food and it was fantastic. The service was excellent (thanks to our fantastic waiter, Luis Angel), and the food was both beautifully presented and full of flavor. I had the generous serving of arroz con pollo, which comes with tostones, slaw, and beans and would highly recommend it. If you're in the mood for an appetizer, both the chicken and the ham and cheese empanadas were superb. And to top it off, all of the food was reasonably priced. I will definitely be back soon!

Best Jamaican food I've had in this area! The ambience was very upscale, classy, and romantic. Everything is white and doesn't have the usual tacky Jamaican restaurant theme. Great place to take someone on a date. The service was awesome, our waiter was so helpful and sweet. He made us feel very comfortable and was clearly passionate about the food. Now the best part- the food, get the brown stew chicken- huge portion, perfectly cooked and seasoned, and comes with salad and rice. Also get the Mac and cheese it's beyond amazing. Just wish we would of had enough room to get rum cake, we will definitely be back!

Best sushi I've had since I've been in the Nashville area. The sushi is actually FRESH! Yes, finally!!!! The plum wine is great and the atmosphere is cozy! Not only do they serve sushi but also other asian inspired dishes. Regardless of what others may say there got to be something good about it since there are many locations in surrounding areas! :)

After trying all the Indian offerings in the area and Aman's having been recommended by an Indian friend who is picky about food, this is now my go-to place! Fabulous food (great veggie options!) and excellent service (dine in and take out) with customizable spice levels. Waitstaff is cheerful and attentive, which is in stark contrast to many of the other establishments in the area. Make sure you BYOB!

Yum! Went today on a whim as we had coupons and I'm glad we did. I've remember when this place first opened and thought "cool name, strange local". It's out on that stretch of Nolensville Rd between Lenox village and Concord rd (its become more popular as of late) So now almost 2 years later went with 2 buddies from work and tried a few of their specialties. Started with their Mezza appetizers, a bit of everything, falafel (one of the best in Nashville!) hummus (super creamy) dolmas, feta and olives with pita. Their grilled chicken is apparently marinated for 36 hours, which makes a world of difference in the flavor and keeping it moist. The gyro meat was nice as well. I had their fruit ice tea that is sweetened only with the fruit, a little sweet for my taste (i'm a non sweet ice tea-er) but you could really taste the fruit. So as if that wasn't enough, we each got a delicious smoothie for the car ride back to work. I had the creamsicle and the other 2 had a fig/peanut butter/berry smoothie. All great! the owner/chef was a nice guy who came out and chatted with us a bit and even let us keep our coupons for next time. I hope more people go out and visit this great, healthy dining place, although i hate when my favorite places become well known...le sigh...
Gnocchi was amazing. All around a very solid meal and reasonable BYOB

Totally delicious, well worth the trip -- better Italian than anything I've had in Philly in the past year. The lamb ragu was rich; the bistecca perfectly cooked and seasoned. Even the raw ingredients accompanying it, arugula and tomato, were so tasty. My only complaint is the noise level. I would love to bring my parents here, but I know that it would be too loud for them.

There are restaurants and then there are experiences. Today I had the latter. I stepped into Nirvana's modest dining area, was greeted and promptly shown to my table. The menu was extremely diverse, featuring dishes from all parts of the Far East. I ordered several courses which were brought out to me immediately, much to any hungry diner's delight. I ate lavishly, like the maharaja of old. When I was partly through my meal, one of the waiters placed a dish on the table before me and spoke quietly thus: "something sweet". He had left a gulaab jamoon, a type of middle-eastern confection, like a donut hole or "munchkin", but this was lighter, and positively doused in honey. When I saw the check I was shocked to see they not only had they given me a free dessert, but didn't charge me for the soup I had ordered as well. The bill was only 14 dollars, but I paid 20, not out of courtesy, but because the staff had earned more. The restaurant is often times empty at lunch, so for diners who prefer a quiet restaurant experience, I recommend that time most. The lunch menu is also modestly priced.

Ploy Thai is by far my families favorite restaurant. We have probably eaten here 100 times. The crispy duck is incredible, so is the fried eggplant and green curry. I have never been dissatisfied. This is the only place I we have sushi now. If my husband and I want to go alone for a date night we actually have to lie to our children.

This was close to a 2 star review... I chose this place because it was the closest place to work with Indian food. I called ahead and the order took little time to be ready. I ordered the Lamb Saag and some samosas. As this was purely a take-out order I won't comment much on the service but I did witness some freebies being given to a group of customers dining in. The dining area is minimal but I personally don't mind for this kind of place which likely is focused on take-out. Also, I give smaller places a pass because of what they might be able to afford. The real test is the food which was very tasty. Note that you can customize the spice level to your liking. I chose medium and there was just enough spice for me without leaving me numb in the mouth. The saag was different from what I've had before but I think this might be a regional variation (in India and Pakistan). I didn't love that the samosas were cold but perhaps this is the way they are supposed to be (thinking street food). This does mean that they are made in batches and are kept in the dining room waiting to be served. I personally would have preferred them warmed up. Things to note: $10 minimum was what I remember seeing posted and the order did not come with utensils. I did not ask for them and didn't notice when the order was bagged right in front of me. In a pinch I would go again but I've had better (mostly in New England though). If Indeblue (in Center City) had a location in Northeast Philly I'd go with that.

It's tough to find a decent falafel in the suburbs, probably because there's not enough demand. But the Lebanese owners of King of Falafel -- and, please, forgive me if they're not Lebanese; I've been known to be off by a few thousand miles -- these guys show up at the Newtown Farmer's Market day in and day out and serve up a very good product, despite the fact that the locals don't exactly support the cause. When I was a young wandering Jewish boy, I spent a long summer on a small kibbutz near Israel's West Bank, and my friends and I used to take a long, baron road into the town of Afula a few times a week for falafels that locals called the best in the country, Falafel Gulani. Here's what I learned from those treks. 1. A great falafel ball must be extremely crisp on the outside but very, very moist and flavorful on the inside. Dry falafel balls are not just lackluster; they're downright icky. 2. A phenomenal falafel sandwich must be topped with the richest tahina, a thinned out sesame seed paste. King of Falafel is spot on in the tahina category. In the ball category, they can't compete with the falafel superstars of the world but they manage to avoid "ickyness," which, in the suburbs, is all you can really ask for.

I was anxious to try this place ever since it opened. I went during the week and the girl that was working there was extremely nice and attentive. I ordered the chicken gyro which was not only delicious, but it was big enough to last me three meals! I plan to go back soon to try other things in their menu.
