I also love that they offer smoothies so I will keep that in mind. I did not meet the owner, but I have friends who say he is the nicest man you can meet. I hope this place survives in Manayunk because it's a great addition!

This is one of my favorite new spots...I love how authentic the food and atmosphere is...there is some old reminders of past restaurants but all in all a great place. I tried the chicken tikka masala...yumm! Just enough spice to remind you that you are alive! All of the staff including the ladies in the back are mediterranean, reminds me of an old grandma cooking for the family, straight awesome! Fyi...lunch buffet is thursday-friday for 8.99/person. Go try it...you won't be dissapointed!

Great price, great service, great food. Can't ask for more!!....EXCEPT TO BE OPEN MONDAYS! Haha I give them 5 stars because the food is always perfect, the service is wonderful and always on time, and you can't beat their prices. I just wish they were open on Mondays!

First let me state that I am from the islands, so I have a certain standard that has to be met. I went to Jamaican Jerk Hut and had a goat roti. I thought it was OK. The roti was a little on the dry side, so the dahl puri was falling out of it. The curry goat had a little too much potato and not enough of a kick to the curry. If I need another fix, and can't wait to get to Brooklyn, I will go back. I wanted to try the meat patties, but they were out. Service was not bad. He wasn't the most attentive, but he did his job. I find that it served as a quick fix.
Food is pretty good, staff is incompetent. It's unfortunate because the place has a cool vibe and the concept it cool.

I had lunch here with a bestie not too long ago! We started out with the hummus which lacked a bit in flavor for me. I think it needed to be seasoned just a little more. Its blandness definitely worked well with a bite of the olives on the plate though! The pita bread is wonderful, nothing to complain about there! She got a greek salad and I had a gyro. She didn't complain about the salad, which is good for her because she is always complaining, hahaha! My gyro was delish, but hard to eat! I had to go at it with a knife and fork! Both their lamb and tzatziki sauce had fantastic flavor. My FAVE FAVE FAVE part of the meal was our dessert. OH EM GEE. I'M TALKING TO DIE FOR. It is this chocolate phyllo dough pastry with chocolate ice cream, whip cream, chocolate syrup and fruit. Phyllo dough has a wonderful flaky and crispy texture about it and combined with the chocolate filling...yum. Thinking about it is kinda making me salivate, hahaha. So if you are a lover of phyllo dough and chocolate, and can stand super super sweet desserts, definitely give this a try. It completely satisfied my sweet tooth for the week! Phenomenal! The place itself is also really cute! Will definitely stop by for drinks and that dessert again soon!
Average to very good food, but WAY too expensive: $43(!) for two small entrees and two pieces of naan.

Best Greek food in This area. they deliver fast, and it's consistently great tasting. The gyro meat is super thin, which we like, and the tsatziki is refreshing and well made. The chicken filet is juicy, and the side of roasted potatoes and rice and veggies makes my meal seem healthy.

Wow! This has to be one of the best authentic Indian restaurants in STL. They offer a wide variety of food on their buffet and it's always hot and fresh. The flavors are very traditional and the atmosphere is comfortable. If you like Indian food defiantely try this place out!

The best baba ganoush that I have had in a really long time. The lentil soup is also wonderful- although sometimes they run out of it because it's so popular! I am so glad this place bounced back after the tragic fire last year. I continue to frequent Petra for lunch and dinner and service is always great.

We had the Tiger Tear salad, panang curry with chicken, and disco chicken. Everything was fantastic, only two suggestions: One, the Tiger Tear salad was SO good and SO spicy! But it's a salad! Not a chunk of meat with lettuce sprinkled it in. Love the amount of beef, but give me some lettuce too! We actually popped this in the fridge and I'm making a larger salad with the leftover beef tonight. The panang curry (my personal favorite Thai dish of all time) was DELICIOUS but it needed some veggies. Put some carrots, green peppers, etc. into it. Not just shredded cabbage/lettuce. My husband fully enjoyed his disco chicken and there were generous portions. Seriously, don't be turned off by the appearance, it was really great! Do it!

UPDATE: The owner called twice to apologize, and offered me a free meal to give the restaurant another shot. (I didn't even tell him that his delivery driver drove over my lawn when he finally showed up - an hour and 15 minutes after I placed the order.) I took him up on his offer, though I opted for pickup instead of delivery! The woman who took my order hung up as I was asking what time my order would be ready. I allowed 30 minutes since it was a Friday night, and my food was waiting when I arrived I tried the lamb kalimirch, which was lovely. It was hotter than I anticipated, but not overpowering. The decor inside the restaurant looked nice, and about half of the tables were full. While it wasn't the best Indian dish I've ever had, it was good enough to go back for more. I'll be interested to see if the service is better for dine in customers than it is for takeout/delivery. Bottom line - the food is good but I wouldn't trust the delivery service! The 3/5 stars reflects the poor service, which will hopefully improve as they gain experience.

I have been to lot of Indian Restaurants and this is one of the worst for two reason - all curry tasted the same and mandatory 18% gratuity for shltty service. We were just 2 people and wanted try out this restaurant.... after going through the menu we order Chicken Kolapuri (special of the day) and Lamb Bhuna with some Naan & Paratha. The Chicken Kolapuri was not even close to the original dish, was very turmericy and missing ethnic Kolapuri spices. The Lamb Bhuna is NOT SO Lamb Bhuna...it is suppose to a dry Lamb Fry...but it was as gravy as Chicken Kolaphuri and was almost the same taste. The naan and partha were okay. We had also ordered the Mango lassi...they charged 5 bucks for that and it was not even half as good as the lassi from Palace at the Ben or other good restaurants.The mandotary gratuity of 18% was outrageous for the service...they just cane to take the order and delivery it to the table.THATS IT! Shame on you guys...worst service ever!! So CHEAP!

Found this restaurant, when we were really hungry and no clue about which restaurant to go. Although it is situated in a run down mall, the ambiance was amazing inside the restaurant. Probably, they should replace their old roof, which doesn't go good with their pretty props. We got Buddha dumplings for appetizer, which was amazing. Thai ice tea was usual. I got Jungle to Jungle for main entree, where as my friend got a dish which was a medley of beef, shrimp, chicken and vegetables with red curry. The only turn off is the dessert. The fried bananas were battered like double stuffed tempura and deep fried. As far as I know, from my thai friends, the fried banana will be slightly breaded and shallow fried. I would have given 5 stars, if it wasn't the only case. I would definitely go here again.

This is a welcome addition to Passyunk. My first experience with this restaurant was ordering delivery. The food was excellent and delivered quickly. The second time was dining in. Service was prompt and attentive. The food was again excellent and combined authentic Indian flavors with accessibility. Like most Indian restaurants, it is very vegetarian friendly. The nan was great and the samosa chaat as well. They have a large outdoor patio similar to the magic garden on south street. When I went it was too hot to dine outside but I'd like to try it some day.
I got the quesadilla salad with chicken. The chicken was so juicy. The sauces are great and people were very nice working there, cannot wait to try more of their menu!

Queen of Sheba is the 3rd Ethiopian restaurant I have tried over the years. Ethiopian food seems to me to incorporate spices and preparation that is similar to Middle Eastern and Indian food - combined. The appearance of the restaurant on the outside is not the best, nor is the parking situation good. There is very limited parking in the adjoining lot. However, the food is very good and the best I have had at an Ethiopian restaurant. Our group had a vegetarian dinner buffet that consisted of 7+ items, rice, Ethiopian bread, salad, fruit, dessert and strong Ethiopian coffee. Rule # 1 at an Ethiopian restaurant - wash your hands before dinner! The customary way to eat this food is to use the spongy Ethiopian bread to scoop up food with your right hand and put it in your mouth without dropping it in your lap! Or, this restaurant will provide a fork. Do know that this type of food is well-cooked and more like a stew than a stir-fry. The man and woman serving the group did a good job. The restaurant is very small but they managed two larger groups including picking up used dishes at the appropriate time. While in the restaurant, I noticed that the back door near the kitchen was propped open. I checked out the health inspections of this restaurant by the state of Florida, and it appears Queen of Sheba has had some challenges over time. Thus the 2 star rating rather than a 3 star rating, since this issue is important. Check out your favorite restaurants at the link below: https://www.myfloridalicense.com/wl11.asp?mode=1&SID=&brd=H&typ=

Beautiful lunch experience at Zorba's this afternoon! We shared a charcoal chicken sandwich and a lamb platter--both out of this world. Zorba's scores well in flavor, ambiance, service, and pricing. The sandwich was crafted perfectly with fresh ingredients and their homemade dressing. Both meats were moist and flavorful. (To my surprise, the chicken was more noteworthy than the lamb.) The platter was filling and memorable as well. The lamb was served over rice and accompanied by mixed vegetables and a boiled and buttered potato. Perfection! Thank you!

I'm South Indian with a very high standard for Indian food and I loved every single thing I had here, especially the idlis (Indian rice pancakes). They melted in my mouth especially in combination with the two delicious chutneys (coconut & onion/tomato) they came with. The sambar was very flavorful as well. The plain dosa (rice/lentil crepe) was as good as any I've had. The vadas (savory rice/lentil donuts) could use some work, but were good nonetheless. My American boyfriend (who's very new to Indian food & had never had South Indian food up until then) enjoyed the idlis as well. He especially liked the vegetable cutlets and the chicken manchurian. The mango lassi was delish - much more flavorful than what you get at a lot of Indian restaurants--and this was real lassi, not just a mango milk shake. The service we had, despite what some of the reviews here say, was top notch. The restaurant was crowded--almost all the big tables were full--and yet our food came out quickly and the waiters were very attentive. The one con was the noise level. The restaurant was loud, even by Indian standards. It didn't help that there were 4 tables with more than a couple of small kids each. If you're looking for some quiet dinner time, probably not a good idea to come here on a Saturday night. It also seems very popular for takeout food, which is another option.

I've been here a couple times now and always been satisfied. The pho is very good with a flavorful broth. I usually accompany a large bowl (the portion sizes are massive, so don't feel shy to go to the smaller bowl) with Vietnamese iced coffee. The coffee is served rich with sugary, condensed milk at the bottom. This is probably one of the best bang-for-your-buck places. And I do mean buck, as in a physical dollar bill, because you'll have to pay with physical legal tender. No, sliding the MasterCard here, Ms. Futureman. The food is good, cheap, and the one of the best available Vietnamese places in town! Would recommend!
Love the food here! The decor is beautiful the prices are reasonable and the service is delightful. Tasty, fresh dishes at great prices! How can you say no?
Get the Sesame chicken! This place also puts Shirley Temples in the menu which is so fun. Plan for leftovers. The meals have a lot of food.
For $14 the burger should be grass fed and antibiotic free. It's very good but should be grass fed and antibiotic free.

A place I use to rave about to my friends and co-workers disappointed me today. Made a to go order along with a dine- in, I ended up canceling the to go order before it was made. When I was about to pay they rang me up for the canceled order as well. They gave me crap about it, and told me next time to tell them. Well I did and there won't be a next time. I ended up paying out of disgust...take my $8 in exchange of over $100s being lost from this consumer. I'll make sure I'll tell my friends and coworkers about it. Happy holidays!

Stopped in last night for a quick dinner at the bar and had the most incredible dinner I've had in Philly in the last year. Magical and still thinking about it the next morning. The lebna and taboule, chicken and shrimp were off the charts. We were too full for dessert, but took home the insanely good cardamon "Kouign Amann" which I'm now having with my coffee. Can't wait to go back again to try the grilled fish dish that I saw pass by.
Tried the baklava....yum! Crispy but soft, sweet but not cloyingly so, really delicious. I like that it was cut into small pieces....finger food if you don't mind licking your fingers, and I didn't!

Had a hearty meal at this place. The owner is very friendly and it felt like he really cared about feeding us. We had the aloo paratha and halwa poori. Though a little oily, the taste was outstanding. We polished off 4 plates of halwa poori in no time (we were 4 of us). Only problem I had was that the halwa was too sweet.

While I am not usually a huge fan of buffets, they do quite a good job here. It is not the most extensive buffet but it is consistently great tasting. They have also recently spruced the place up. They closed for 10 days and re-did everything including the kitchen.If you're looking for good food in a very casual atmosphere, this is the place to come for lunch. Also they are very popular and you never know to whom you will run into here. I have often shown up to find friends I haven't seen in a while enjoying a meal.

Absolutely loved this place. This is a family owned establishment. The atmosphere is very cozy, and intimate. Perfect for a date.I loved the fact they stay open until 11pm on Saturday night. Even with them staying open late the food was fresh. There were many options for vegans. We ordered a platter for two, and the portion sizes were plenty. Make sure if you do not eat meat to specify, as the choices on the platter are from the chef. There is also gluten free injera! I will be back for sure

Food is good, but not great. Portion sizes are a bit on the small side. Prices are high for what you get. We've been here a few times since they opened and would go much more often if the prices were lower or portions were bigger. When my family gets take-out from other places we usually get at least 2 meals out of an order. Here, we always finish a dish easily in one sitting. Favorite dish- vegetable masuman curry

They have excellent happy hour tapas for $1-3. I don't drink much wine but their selection is great and whenever I take friends they are happy. All of their prices are cheap and their portions are huge. I love the mediterranean platter which has a little bit of everything! Be prepared to share or take 1/2 home! They also have very tasty Vegan dishes so my non-meat eater friends are happy. As an omnivore I am happy there since even their spinach and cheese quesadilla is out of this world - not your boring quesadilla. My only complaint is the spotty service. Sometimes it is really good sometimes they forget you are there and forget what you ordered. Their decor inside is really interesting but most people like sitting on the patio. I don't like the patio it has a view of the parking lot.

This is an absolutely wonderful and authentic Indian restaurant. The food is top-notch, and the staff is very friendly and helpful. I got the chicken tikka masala, and my wife got the paneer butter masala. Both were exquisite! Prices are a bit high (no buffet here), but you're paying for quality --- it's worth it! This is an absolutely wonderful and authentic Indian restaurant. The food is top-notch, and the staff is very friendly and helpful. I got the chicken tikka masala, and my wife got the paneer butter masala. Both were exquisite! Prices are a bit high (no buffet here), but you're paying for quality --- it's worth it!

I came down with a bad viral infection thats making the rounds. Throat closed up, the works. I swear by hot spicy tumeric laden food to help what ails me. The staff was very friendly and took pity on me. They custom made my order as hot as is possible. It did the trick for one night and helped me feel better for a while. They are a tad pricey, but otherwise I have no complaints. I like their curries best and their duck dishes are also good.

I was so excited to see another Greek restaurant in Carrollwood Center...right where the previous Greek restaurant had been. I ordered a chopped Greek salad to go with chicken breast. It was over $10. When I got home with my meal there was no chicken...and no potato salad. And even worse, there was barely any feta cheese to be found. All other toppings were in abundance, but without the potato salad, chicken (which I paid extra for), and very little feta cheese, I was very disappointed. However they did give me enough dressing for three salads! On a positive note, the place was clean and the service was very fast.

Best Thai food around!. Well worth the price. The staff is amazing they are quick to bring out your food and the portions are massive. Everything tastes so fresh i literally drive across town just to eat there.

Loved going here with my girlfriends for happy hour! The atmosphere is amazing, the service is great and the menu has great selections! The prices were up there but the quality of food was really good. I thoroughly enjoyed the happy hour and especially the fact that they had half off select appetizers and drinks. All in all great just wish the prices weren't so high for small plates.
Awesome food. Loads of vegetarian options to choose from too. Staff is very courteous and friendly. The combos are a good way to taste most of the dishes on the menu.

This lady smiles while she cooks! I love her! She's zipping around pulling bread from the oven, flipping a pan of shrimp on the fire, frying egg rolls, and dressing our banh mi all with a grin! Sadly due to my lack of enunciation, I asked for a banh mi with bocca but was given banh mi with PORKa. Boo. We ordered them to go and did not know until we were on the road out of Nawlens. We scraped the meat out and enjoyed the jalapeños, cilantro, cucumber, sriracha, carrots, pickled radish, and toasty bun. The veggie egg rolls were not special. Boo. Also, we each were given free Arizona Ice Tea.
Thank you for introducing me to fried tofu as crispy as a chips on the outside and soft in the inside! The bowl (salad) was delicious! I'll definitely come back.

We loved it. The food was delicious. The Pakora was perfectly fried. The Rogan Josh and Karahi were excellent, especially the green peppers in the Karahi. The Naan and Kulcha were warm, toasty and crispy. The service was also top notch. They were very friendly. Our water was always full.

I hate myself for not getting on here 3 years ago to review this place the very first time I had it. And to make matters worse, I've been back EASILY a dozen times and still hadn't reviewed. SMH at myself. Now that my whining is out of the way, let's talk about this food. I'm a Jamaican-American and it has been really difficult to find truly, authentic Jamaican cuisine in Indianapolis. I've tried every Caribbean spot this city has to offer. This place though... it's not an Afro-Caribbean hybrid, one dish stop or food truck that doesn't have set times or locations (which I've tried them ALL) but it's a Jamaican eatery that reflects the island and is accessible and available. Next to my own kitchen, this place is it. I tell everyone I know who likes Jamaican food to try this place. First of all, it's owned and operated by native Jamaicans. You cannot go wrong there. Next, while the location is a little unorthodox (it's located at the end of a liquor store), the food that is produced from said location is unmatched anywhere in this city. Their food tastes exactly like the street vendors found on winding, mountainous roads in Jamaica. Whenever I eat here I'm immediately transported to my uncle's kitchen in Jamaica esPECially when I have their jerk chicken or oxtail. Granted, there's nowhere to sit down and eat your food once ordered at Jamaican Style Jerk, but there aren't on the streets of Jamaica, either. When you hit the 5th star to review something on Yelp, it says, "Woohoo! As good as it gets!" and as far as Jamaican food in Indianapolis goes, this genuinely is as good as it gets. And just typing about it right now is making me want to stop by there this week and grab some oxtail, ripe plantain and rice and peas...

Very small hole in the wall take out with 2 tables and small bar style seating. Located in the heart of South Philly right by Pats and Genos. The food is very good! I had a falafel sandwich loaded with veggies and a white sauce. For dessert I had a piece of halva, which is a Mediterranean dessert. It was delicious, I even bought a 1/2 lb to take home. Also, for checking in on Yelp I saved 10%. Would come here again for sure.

My husband and I ate there at 7pm on a Friday night. We had a reservation but it wasn't necessary. The tables are a bit close but it wasn't too noisy. However, the college guy behind us was impossible not to hear telling his table mates he was considering taking beef out of his dietary repertoire because he can feel love for cows, but fish could stay because it's not possible to develop an emotional attachment to fish. Ahh college days. Anyway, the service was very good without being obtrusive. Our water glasses always topped off...a requisite of the Indian dining experience. The basic samosa was quite nice as the outside was crispy and tender, but not greasy, even on the ends. The potato and pea stuffing could have used a bump up in spices. The tamarind sauce was the best I've had because it had a nice sour finish to it. The garlic chicken appetizer my husband ordered was right up his alley but over the top on the garlic scale for me, and I'm a garlic enthusiast. We ordered garlic naan and mint naan. Both were good. My husband ordered the lamb saagwala and I had the mint chicken. The complexity of the sauces was excellent but both dishes were let down by being too sweet and the spinach in my husband's dish did not come through at all. It was a mediocre dining experience, but the prices were reasonable. We will try Tiffin next time.

Delicious springrolls. I'd be happy with 3 of those for lunch anyday of the week. Pho is really good. Everything was fresh. Nothing overpriced, in fact, I felt like I was getting a deal. Loses a star because parking isn't easy - it's at the end of a small/older shop strip, like you see all over Tampa. And the decor is pretty sparse. But if you're in for a great Vietnamese at a good price... Pho An is all you need.

Growing up in NYC Puerto Rican food was a staple. Salsa is a great reminder of those days. The pernil was tender. The mofongo with yucca was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. My favorite was the tostones with ceviche appetizer soo good! I only wish they would include wine as part of their happy hour specials.
I have always had great service here. The food is wonderful, and a good value. This is one of the best places to eat in town.

Went with a former colleague for lunch, and really enjoyed it. She had a BBQ pork sandwich (bahn mi) and I had a roast pork bahn mi. Each of the sandwiches came with chips and a soda for like $6 all-in, which is a real bargain considering the amount of food. You could split one if you wanted a lighter lunch. The sandwiches were fresh, the fillings were tasty, so no issues at all with the food. The restaurant is in a strip mall next to Fred Meyer, so not much ambiance at all, but still...the food... I should add that one of the issues with the freshness is they tend to run out; I went for dinner one evening and they were out of bread. I'd suggest making this a lunch destination if you want to ensure you get your choice of food. I wish it were closer...I would be a regular! Still worth the stop if you're anywhere close for lunch, and want some good Vietnamese sandwiches.

Terrific authentic Indian restaurant! I had been to its previous location, originally the old 401 Dinner in Conshohocken. I wanted to try the new location on Germantown, formerly Lucky Dog. Possibly my new favorite restaurant in the Conshy area. We had grilled mushroom appetizer, Peshwari naan, Lamb Madras Curry and Chana Masala. Everything was excellent! You can also find good deals on restaurant.com app. We saved $25, so BYO date-night check came to a wopping $28, including desert and chai tea. They have online ordering, so it's going right to the top of the take-out options in the area.

Is hard-to-find if you don't look for it. It's in the corner by a tire place. It is well worth it to find this place. I went because of the Yelp good reviews. I was not disappointed. I took two buddies and they also had a great experience. I ordered a Boba Ice-T for the very first time and relished in the taro and boba balls in my drink. The drinks were a little pricey @ 3.50. The dishes were hot tasty and plentiful for lunch. My friends had a pho dish and another had a Thai curry, both were extremely delicious and very satisfied. They adjust the spice level. The place was well attended but had seating for the lunch crowd as they have inside and outside seating. I would come back and try and another dish at this place.
Good food, very clean, nice atmosphere, good service. Loved the samosas, my husband had the chicken tikka masala and really liked it. The mango lassi was delicious!!! Highly recommend it!

Love love love this place!!! A little slow paced but if you are patient, it is phenomenal and worth the wait. The stew chicken was the best part of the entire meal so I would absolutely recommend ordering! Was a little bummed that they ran out of johnny cakes but we will be back to try again! Andre was so attentive and very friendly. I can see why everyone was raving about this place. I honestly hope this place lasts. We WILL be back with friends :)

Its MIND BLOWING that this kind of food can come out of a truck. Everything on the menu is genius and delicious. The only problem with this place is everyone knows about it so it gets mobbed like a cheerleader on prom night. There's just no space anywhere and you've got to wait your turn. There's no such thing as stopping by Cucina Zapata real quick for your lunch hour. You've got to spend the whole damn hour here. Trust me, it'll be worth it.
The tom kah soup with chicken is delicious. The honey pork ribs don't have any honey but are also very good. The service is excellent. We will return for sure.

The house crispy fried noodles were special and delicious, with beef, shrimp, chicken, bamboo, carrots, peppers, baby corn, and a tasty light gravy. The vermicelli with bbq pork and spring roll was also great. Kind staff and calm and pleasing, clean ambience with nice mood lighting. Casual or fancy, comfortable for families with littles too. We'll return!

Love this place. The food is always tasty and the portions are a good size, allowing for leftovers. This trip tried the platter which includes hummus and pita with a side salad. The meat is super tender and fresh. The owner is usually there with a huge smile on his face eager to chat with customers. He told us how to say "thank you" in tons of languages. You can tell he loves being there, and loves his customers. Sometimes I forget this place is here since it's off of main street, but it is definitely worth remembering.

I have heard of this new coffee shop from a couple of friends, and have been looking forward to trying it. I got the chance a couple of weeks ago at Karlie M's UYE and it was definitely everything I had heard and more! I really like the minimalist feel of the decor and furniture. The only drawback is the the stools along the window bar were a bit uncomfortable. That would be an easy fix and is a small price to pay given everything T.H.I.S. Place has to offer. The space is inviting and comfortable due to the warmth expressed by Tom & Co. In addition to making everything from scratch to order, they are friendly and chatty so the environment is fun and social. :) I had an iced coffee that was beyond delicious. It was perfectly chilled, not too sweet, and very strong (how I like it!). After a couple of yelpers were kind enough to let me try their HOMEMADE POPSICLES (yes!!!), raspberry lemon and blueberry, I had to have a whole raspberry one of my own! There is so much more on the menu I would like to try, and I think I'll be coming back for more popsicle soon despite the freeze!

I ordered the Pad Thai, which seems like it should have been a safe bet. When I received the plate I noticed a very strange smell as I pulled out the spoon - not dissimilar to this one time when my dog rolled around in dead carcass and I tried bathing her but the smell wouldn't come off of her, so basically it smelled like rotting carcass and wet dog. Somehow I managed to try the Pad Thai and it amazingly tasted worse than it smelled. I quietly placed a napkin on my plate and set the dish aside. When the woman asked how everything was I nodded and whispered, "Not good." she quickly took my plate away without apology and I was astounded when she brought the bill that she charged the full amount. Oh, and then there was the spider that I swatted off the wall inches from our table top. RISK TAKERS: I STRONGLY ADVISE THAT YOU ORDER FROM THE PINK SIDE OF THE MENU. My friend said that her pecan chicken was edible and not the worst she had ever had, so that's a plus.
Need to update their hours for Friday and Saturday when you turn up at 9:30 on a Friday and they say they closed at 9 but their hours say 10!!! V poor

Tuesday night's the jazz is smooth. It is like outdoors but no bugs or rain. A few weeks ago I went and the food was--Jamaican food. I adore it. The service was well-meaning but horrid and the music was painful. At the behest of good friends, I went back. They took people's advice. Much better service. Perfect music. And Jamaican food. Most improved restaurant EVER! I hear they are having reggae and callypso for Mother's Day. Can't wait! Mother's Day update: excellent music, which is good because it took me 22 minutes to even be acknowledged in the nearly empty courtyard. The food was excellent once I finally got a menu and my order taken. It took so long the band went on 2 breaks before I ate. The music is worth coming for, but they can't stay open as a restaurant if they don't care to feed people!
Greek Gyro for $5.95, tastes amazing. Ive been getting one every week recently. I like to add lettuce to mine, as it doesn't typically come with. Also has great Baklava and Hummus!

Came here on a week night with my best friend to pick up some pho. (with this cold weather, I feel this is the only thing I want to eat!). Called to order and drove there 15 min later to pick up. The people on the phone were really not the nicest and when we got there the food was not ready so we waited. The food was really good but lacked some meat in there for my taste. Beside that, the broth was tasty and overall was pretty good. I will probably go back once I am around.
Love them too pieces and every where else I have eaten has a hard time to compete with them
Great selection (we had raspberry) and drink specials, WiFi, comfortable seating, and attentive staff: coals continually supplied.

Amazing restaurant! Greeted by husband and wife owners..reggae tunes playing in the background. Started with Jerk wings that was jerked to perfection! The Chicken platter was the best choice!!! Curry, Jerk and brown stew...yummy!! I throughly enjoyed the Sorrel! My family and I were beyond happy!!! If you haven't been here...get here FAST!

The Squab brought me a Pate Banh Mi and a Pork one (which did not taste anything like pork, and was probably fish). The Pate banh mi was okay. The pork one was bland and was spicier. The strips of meat (which probably wasn't pork) was meager in portion size.

Really good food! I wasn't sure by the looks of the menu, nothing really stood out to me but we loved everything we got and it was perfect for takeout. Highly recommend the butter chicken dish. The best feature is the dishes are served with rice and choice of naan which was delicious. Will definitely go back!

Love it! Great addition to East Nashville. The village salad is ridiculous. After eating it, I went straight to the store and bought a whole bunch of cucumbers to make it at home. The beef gyro is out of this world.

What a great little hidden place in Temple Terrace!!!! We ended up getting take out and man were we surprised by the flavor and quality the food. The kibbeha were so tasty with a slight hint of cinnamon. My wife had a kabob platter which was more than enough for two people to share. The spices and flavor of the meat were spot on and made our meal very enjoyable. As for the hummus it was also amazing with the spices adding that special Lebanese touch. I will defiantly return hear and I highly recomened checking out this little Mom & Pop place for a true taste of the Middle East...

Truly one of the best Kabob houses as well as one of the best restaurants all around. Not only the place had friendly service, but the food was top notch. We got the family dinner which came with different assortments of lamb, chicken, beef, and ground meat thingy. Everything was well balanced and perfectly seasoned. We also got the samosas and the dough was light, flakey, and not doughy at all. The ingredients inside the samosas were also well seasoned. The cumin which I was usually not a big fan off was not over powering. Superb dining experience all around. A must go-back-to destination.

Yes this is a Thai restaurant that actually serves Jasmine Rice! And yet again like the other restaurants in downtown Philadelphia, this place was BYOB with NO uncorking fee! It was a nice little place but the seating was pretty condensed and could probably sit about 35-50 people. It was hot outside and they had an AC but I didn't feel like it was working too well. The service was excellent with the waiters coming around every 5-10 minutes and they were very friendly and helpful when it came to recommendations. We got the green curry, the jasmine rice and it was delicious. The best part is that they have one to four chiles for spiciness and then they have another option: thai spicy. I ordered two spiciness and then asked for how spicy is thai spicy. He brought out some chopped chiles and I had a little and it was pretty spicy. I love spicy food so I didn't think it was diabolical spicy but it did have a nice kick. I thought the food was excellent. It was rich, full of flavor, and all of the curries had that coconut sweetness with that thai spiciness that makes thai food so delicious. I enjoyed the ambience and the service, and I would enjoy returning to this restaurant if I'm ever back in the area.

Great food! Great drinks! Service can be hit or miss...tonight was a hit! Thanks to our server (who happens to be the GM!) we had a great meal tonight! Dog friendly...great location...a little pricey. Good to great people watching!

Can I please just live here? I've only ordered from the lunch menu a few times so I haven't experienced their full menu yet but the lunches are heaven on earth. I always get the vegetarian spring roll and mushroom soup with my lunch and I adore them. Every entree I've had has been deeelicious. I recommend you get a pot of tea, slow down, take some deep breaths, eat a fabulous lunch and go back to work with a smile on your face.

Had a wonderful dinner Saturday night (May 14) @ QOS. The ingera bread is addictive. The warm decor is authentic and service was informative and helpful. We loved the lamb, the spicy beef, and the lentils, potatoes. All authentic spices, with African wine selections, like Stellenbosch & Kanu. Highly recommended. Couldn't move! Ask for a wonderful lady server named Sinait.

Marjie's grill is a great concept executed well. Southeast asian flavors with an emphasis on the grill and a little funk. I have been in twice so far and plan on making it a regular stop. The changing menu means I find new and interesting dishes every time I go in. A highlight was a cross-section of pork shoulder grilled and served with a light fish sauce dipping sauce and a variety of herbs and leafy greens for wrapping. It was intensely flavorful and a great dish to share among the table. Sharing really is the emphasis and I highly recommend order an assortment of plates for the table and trying it out. I would like to see an expansion of their happy hour - although advertised as running until 6:30 we were informed it finished at 5:30 when we arrived - which isn't much for a working stiff such as myself. That being said the pig tail happy hour special is utterly ridiculous goodness so I still left full and happy.
Incredibly authentic Mediterranean food. I can't consume fast enough! First time here and simple got takeout. Will be back with the wife tomorrow to indulge again!

So, I was quite disappointed as a vegan. Maybe they're great if you eat meat. And I'm also from out of town so maybe my standards were too high. I did takeout, too, so that affects the quality, of course. But I say if you have vegan options on your menu then you should probably know better than they did. I ordered several things and most all of it came without any sort of sauce or toppings at all. Just plain. But when I ordered these things over the phone no one mentioned that. For instance: I ordered buffalo cauliflower bites. They came as plain cauliflower. Totally plain. Which would have been fine if they had mentioned that when I ordered them.

This is a small, casual, inexpensive place with good food. When we have been there most customers are Vietnamese and the food seems authentic. Banh mi here are $4.25. They also serve a handful of other dishes.
Finding Kabob House was such a pleasant surprise. The food is so delicious. They have the best Sambosas! The meat in the Kabobs is moist and tender. This is my new favorite place to eat.
By far and away the best Indian food I have had. The lamb curry and garlic naan is the way to go. A lot of great food for the price.
Nice n comfy ... Deli style with some seating. Very flavorful food n good portion size. Prices are also low. Recommended for a causal quick bite for sure

Love the unique menu. Great for veg leaning ppl and meat eaters alike. I enjoyed the cauliflower burger, on a soft brioche bun and my wife's shrimp pad Thai was good. Excellent drinks round out the meal, and the kids menu is very good. One of our new favorite places!
Great Pho with good service. Plenty of options on the menu.

My absolute favorite restaurant in Nashville. $2.75 for a Bahn Mi Thit Nuong sandwich.. Hell to the yes. Then throw in some spring rolls for $2 bucks and kid bowl of PHO then you are absolutely set for the night. Follow it up with some Avocado Bubble Tea and you good in da hood.

The food was not at all what we expected. It was cold so we didn't eat more than a couple bites. Our service was AWFUL!! She wasn't even concerned with why we barely ate any of our food and didn't offer a box. I'm not sure we'll ever go back. The atmosphere gives it the stars though. For such a cute place I wish the food and service had been better.
I went back for the food and there were only people dining there, yay! The food is great and I really like the atmosphere.

Two descriptions come to mind of my dinner here, expIosions of flavor and balanced taste. They may seem contradictory, but they are not. I went with a few friends and we shared the "Famous" egg salad, the hummus "King of Kings", and the baba ghanoush. I love anchovies, so we got those on the side of the egg salad dish. These were the good kind. Soft, white, and fishy, the sharp sour flavor of the anchovies complimented the creamy egg salad served on bread. The hummus was fantastic as other reviews may explain, but I was honestly more impressed by the egg salad and baba ghanoush. The baba ghanoush was smoky and flavorful vs. the smooth, creamy hummus (much lighter flavor). I also tried the Emerson cocktail. Fresh and summery, this cocktail was a balanced blend of flavor. Slightly sweet, but not cloying. The restaurant itself has a great ambience. A renovated garage, it has a fun eclectic feel. We sat outdoors and enjoyed the warm evening.
Very good food. I have tried multiple things and not been disappointed. Will be returning often. The mango bubble tea is on the sweeter side than I am used to, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing!

My two friends and I visited to celebrate a birthday. The entire visit was terrific! Our food was delicious, our waiter was very attentive (he even put a little candle on the birthday girl's baklava) and he was knowledgeable about the menu. My friends were extremely pleased and they have traveled in the Middle East. Kudos!

mmmm, this will likely be an unpopular opinion, but i thought the chaat was okay. it wasn't amazing or addicting like i was anticipating it to be. it is a yummy mix though! the owner is super passionate and seems very kind, which i really admire. also - best mango lassi i've ever had!

yummmmmm- my favorite weekend brunch- the most common craving my boyfriend and I get when we're waking up on a weekend and don't feel like making any food. the tofu hoagies here are awesome, never fail to please. we usually get 3 and split them- and for $3.50 each that's not a bad deal at all. the bread is great, tofu good and flavorful, plus with yummy pickled veggies- quite tasty. just prepare to get them to go- not much room for eating in here.

I was over at Grant Mac doing some work at the library when suppertime was approaching and I started to get hungry. I love Turkish food, well what I've had of Turkish food, so I though Sofra would be a good choice. The restaurant was quite busy when I got there, and it probably would have been best to call ahead for a reservation, but I was able to get a seat at the bar. It was pretty cold outside when I went so I got the lamb casserole, which was sort of like a shepherd's pie with lamb and topped with cheese. It doesn't look like much, at first, but the dish has lot's of vegetables and lamb and was very filling. So much so that I didn't have any room for baklava (which I love). The only thing I didn't like was that there were bones in with the lamb - the pieces were pretty small and so I wasn't really expecting bone. It wasn't a horrible experience, but it would have been nice to be warned. Aside from that the waitress was nice, and the food was really good. It's a little pricey, but not unreasonably so, and considering how delicious the food was I'd say it was worth it. I do wish that Sofra was open during lunch - it would be nice to go there during lunch breaks at school, but coming here for dinner was a nice treat.

Sunday, my wife and I went to Godavari for their lunch buffet. There were lots of different kinds of foods out and, according to her, were mostly different than her previous visit. I really liked the dal and a fruit mango custard, didn't care for another dish, and the remainder was...just a mixture of Indian food. My sole complaint was- no goat. We decided to return for dinner. The very next Monday found us at Godavari for dinner. Once we were seated, our server brought us a dish of crispy papadums with dipping sauces and our menus. For an appetizer, we ordered the Mamsam roast (special goat fry). I attempted to order a mild goat curry, but was informed that there was no such animal on the menu. So, I settled for a the Anchari Lamb Josh. My lucky wife ordered the Andhra Mamsam Kura (goat curry with andhra spices). My appetizer, the fried goat, was really good and there was a lot of it. Heck, there was enough there for a party of four. It was, however, so good that just the two of us finished it off. The spices in my anchari lamb josh really brought that dish to life. It may have been hotter that i liked, but I'll order it next time and take the spices as I find them. My dessert dish...three pastry ball in a sea of sugary syrup- Bengali Galub Jamun- was simply scrumptious. It was a great finish to a wonderful meal. Now to rate Godavari Brentwood. Last Sunday was my first visit to an Indian buffet. There were many dishes, most of which I've never tried. My wife, who cooks the Indian food in our home, said that: [there was a tremendous variety in the dished presented. Their use of the spices was masterful]. The service at our dinner was first rate. The dishes served, from appetizer to dessert, were excellent. There are so many items on their menu that it'll be hard to pick one on my next visit. If a mild goat curry was listed on that menu, I'd award five stars. But there isn't, so I shan't. Four stars for Godavari

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Edit: THEY ARE NEXT TO THE BALCONY DOWNTOWN! WOO HOOO!! With unusually fast food this time. Open Monday-Saturday, tajmahalboise.com There are at least two other Indian places around town, but this is our favorite. Veg Samosas with chutneys. Paneer Mahkni or Palak Subzi Dal. Naan. Mango Lassi. Lamb Biryani or fruit and nut Biryani. Together, the perfect meal (and another the next day). Oh, there's beer, too, seems like a lot of it, am not a beer person, so i stick with the lassi (yogurt drink). The chai's good, too, served hot only. Dinner takes over an hour to complete, don't plan something RIGHT AFTER that you HAVE TO GET TO because it won't happen. Just relax, watch the Indian musicals, and drink your lassi. Anticipate your delicious food. Then, eat your delicious food. Seriously delicious. Have taken several people who've never had Indian to very positive responses, so go and order what I outlined above. This is one of our favorite places.

For great Thai food on the Main Line, this is the place. It can get really crowded on weekend nights, but that's just a testament to the deliciousness of the food. Come here on the early side, and it's surprisingly empty. The service is fine- friendly staff. The only negative is that they seem to have trouble dealing with lots of people waiting, and large crowds in general. But that's really the only downside to this otherwise charming restaurant with scads of wonderful-tasting Thai food.

Good service...sent my first meal back because the Mongolian beef was dry with no sauce...I got the Shrimp with Mellon balls it was better but the food and service out in Marlton New Jersey is so much better I will go to my regular spot in the future

Great spot to get some North Indian food at. As many people on here said, the lunch buffet will put you into a food comma without a little bit of restraint! In getting dinner the wait times can be a bit much but it's all well worth it!

This place is so amazing, clean, fresh, the staff was so pleasant. I've been to other Thai restaurant's and this place blows them out the water! Very good prices, and a large variety to choose from....

We loved the food here! We definitely will be coming back:) Both of us got the Taste of the Islands platter with Curry Goat, Jerk Chicken and Oxtail....wow. delicious. The owners Andre and his wife are excellent, they know what they are doing!

I absolutely love the Metairie restaurant so I was stoked when this place took over Le Viet Cafe. The owners did a great job fixing up the interior - it's easily 1,000% better than before. Decor is modern, minimalist and most importantly, clean! I only got a spicy beef noodle bowl to go - so I can't speak for the dining service or any of the other dishes, but their to go packaging was AWESOME. They really take that extra step to maintain presentation and I really appreciate that. I got a styrofoam container for the hot broth, a fancy plastic bowl with the noodles and meat and ziploc bag for sprouts and herbs. The soup was not as good as the Metairie restaurant, but overall, I was still satisfied. Looking forward to trying more of their dishes and hitting up the happy hour. I appreciate that they employ servers who speak English. I wish that they would add delivery to their services, which would definitely make this a 5-star joint!

When I get a craving for Pad Thai, Siam Cafe is usually my go to place in South Nashville. It's convenient and affordable. It's also delicious so that's what keeps me coming back. They always throw in extra peanuts and lime for no charge. The staff is friendly and welcoming every time I come in, which is a bonus. The only down side is that the parking lot is tiny, but I usually get it to go anyways.

This is one of the best Thai food restaurants in Santa Barbara. The restaurant is small but it is cozy and nice that there aren't empty seats in it. They do offer to-go. I have gotten the Red Curry, Zen Yai Online Noodles, and the Shu-Mai chicken and shrimp. I am excited to try more options. They definitely know how to make yummy noodle dishes. Way to go! I have not had a bad experience at Zen Yai yet and I look forward to my next ventures there.
Such an amazing mix of awesome flavors. And the owner is the nicest shop keeper ever. Guided us through the menu and made great suggestions. Well definitely return!

Ok, the food here was not bad. Had to the vermicelli and the pho and the pork salad. The food in general was OK, however, the wait for the food was very long tonight. Almost 25 minutes before we got our dish. We went through entire pot of tea before getting there. I guess they must've been busy tonight. Will try them again another time and see if wait times are any better.
I absolutely love the chrispy duck fried rice. Not sure if there's a size difference between the lunch and dinner portions but even though it looks small, it filled me up pretty well.

Have loved Albasha's Baton Rouge location for years now & was happy when found out a Metairie restaurant would be opening. My faves are: hummus, spinach & shrimp, chicken shawrama & moussaka. Pleasant atmosphere.

Every bit of a funky feel, warm and welcoming. Great service. Indoor and out door seating. Fast service. The chef will come by to see if all was good. The hostess came by to say goodbye. Order the mimosa flight and the banana strawberry pancake special!
If you're a buns guy or gal, bless your soul and feed it this spots fried oyster buns.

Friendly staff and decent Buffet. We try and get out for a curry at least once a month for lunch at work. This is our new spot of choice, not only is it convenient in downtown, but it's a step above the other close Indian food in downtown. Buffet always has a good selection and while they keep it on the mild side there is a little spice and lots of flavour. They always have chicken tikka masala, usually some aloo gobi, a goat fish. Rather than a pan with naan, they bring fresh naan to your table. Great stuff and reasonable price.

Yes, it's real. Yes, you aren't going to be wowed with a smile, but the food is fantastic, the portions are great for the price you pay. Oxtail, goat, or chicken is great. I like the cabbage its sweet yet seasoned. Hands down my place for Jamaican food. I had to get my Jamaican fix and they did the job very well. Support the local business in Chester, especially this small gem!!!

Hmmm... what to say about Abyssinia Ethiopian Restaurant. I've been knowing the owner of this restaurant, Abraha, for many years. The prices have increased over the years, however, the food quality and taste has improved accordingly. The interior art work and coloring has changed quite a few times too (a new traditional seating section with nice wood work has been added). My Ethiopian friends agree that this is the best Habishi (Ethiopian) restaurant in town! I recommend the vegetarian combo so that you can sample all of the tasty veggie dishes. For meat lovers, I suggest Awaze Tibs (juicy tender pieces of lamb or beef sautéed with red onions, tomatoes, jalapeno peppers and berbere sauce). This dish is the most popular because they have to cook it fresh per your request. All of their food is served upon injera (a unique, exclusively Ethiopian type of moist pancake-like substance made from a grain called tef). They have good imported bera (beer) from their homeland, as well as Tej (traditional honey wine, aka mead). Go and enjoy the food and lovely milieu! As long as you're okay with a little butt burn the next day due to the spices, you're in for an unforgettable taste bud journey to Ethiopia!

Vietnamese coffee $3.48 ... came in 8 oz plastic cup filled with ice cubes, the liquid content is probably close to 1 oz. I finished this treat in 45 seconds after 10 minutes of waiting. What I envisioned was a big tall glass filled with crushed ice in the middle and sweet milk at the bottom. On the glass top, a Vietnamese coffee dripper, slowly dripping hot dark liquid down into the glass. Once drink is ready I mix coffee and milk and ice, and enjoy it over good 30 minutes. Unfortunately, it wasn't what I got. Perhaps everything is suited to to-go pack only. The place is tiny. Stalk interior ... mismatching chairs and only 3 tables... blasting cable TV, kinda run down, and no guest wifi. I asked for the passcode and the lady said it is not offered any longer. I surmised that this is not a place for working on your project or for reading books while eating. In and out, chop chop, but you have to be patient for your 1oz Vietnamese iced coffee.

Loved the ambiance of the place. Very laid back and casual. The chicken tortilla soup was fantastic. The blackened grouper was excellent and the cosmos were a delight. Watching the sunset was the icing on the cake!

Have been here several times - lunch and dinner. With my 2 and 4 year old and without. This place is super. Kids love it too. It's small and gets crowded but it won't keep me away. DO NOT leave here without getting the fried egg appetizer - don't read it just order it and immerse your taste buds in joy. I also love the beef vermicelli. So yummy. My 4 yo loves the pork vermicelli - perfect kid portions too. Btw, the owner is super nice and takes pride in what they serve. That ranks high on my list of cool things about the places I eat.

Great gyros! They only serve "taziki sauce" not ranch or yogurt like American gyro places, but it's pretty much ranch anyway. So good, very fast, and friendly. The only thing I was wondering about was if we should have found a place to put our plates and trash (like Panera) or expect the cooks or cashiers to do that. We didn't see a place to discard, so we just pre bussed...which was awesome.

View was very nice, service was friendly, location was great, my dad and i went for lunch and there was no wait which is always awesome . I asked the server what he recommends and he told us the mahi tacos so we had that along with the coconut shrimp- OH MY GOODNESS- the mahi was so good we had just the mahi instead of one of the tacos (came with 3), the shrimp came with a few and the sauce it came with was amazing. Would definitely recommend this place, i am not a local and would definitely go back when ever i'm in that area.
We live in Ca so we eat Thai food all the time. The noodles at this place are so tender I can't believe it. Good curry and one of the friendliest waitstaff ever.

I've never had Pho anywhere else. Honestly, I don't know if I ever would. I'm not sure how others compare, but this is absolutely perfect in terms of flavor, texture, and everything else that goes along with food. The noodles are perfect for slurping, they don't stick together in the slightest. The sprouts are perfectly crunchy and fresh, supplying a much regarded texture. The beef is succulent and tinder and sliced thin enough to almost see through. The basil is the most aromatic I've ever experienced, but subtle enough in taste to not overpower. The broth brings it all together. Hell, one time I even got tripe by accident and it was equally as delicious. My biggest regret of moving to Broad Ripple from the west side is now I have to drive 30 minutes to get my to go order.

Went to Zorba's over the weekend when my boyfriend and I were just walking around the Fairmount area. I think he was tempted by the frappes that some people were drinking just outside the restaurant. Not much to look at from the outside, but the interior is cozy. We were seated promptly and after enough time to peruse the menu, we gave our order to our waitress. She came back after a few minutes with a basket of bread and some olive oil, and our frappes - these are so much better than regular iced coffee drinks! I'll have to ask next time if they serve traditional Greek coffee (made with a briki and served in demitasse cups). Since we were there at the start of dinner service, our food arrived before I even finished a slice of bread. I had the spanakopita (one of the specials) - it was absolutely perfect! I didn't care that I burnt my tongue with the first couple of bites because it tasted so good! The phyllo dough was golden and flaky, just as it should be, making a mess on my plate each time I cut off a bite, and the spinach and feta filling was creamy and delicious - more often than not, I've had spanakopita that tasted really bitter because canned spinach was used. It tasted like fresh spinach and phyllo to me! My boyfriend had the grilled octopus with a side of Greek potatoes and vegetables - the octopus was tender and seasoned well, and the potatoes/vegetables (looked like green beans and tomato) reminded him of the potatoes that his mother used to make. We were too full to try any of the desserts, but I hope to try them another time. Definitely a hidden gem in the Fairmount area, I'd definitely recommend Zorba's to anyone looking for tasty Greek food.

Good food and good service. We ate lunch at the bar during an Eagles game recently. The waitress was very nice and we couldn't beat the $2 Buds even if they did come in a can. Lunch was good and very authentic. The atmosphere is a little less than desirable. Very basic plastic bar chairs and an old 70s-dive feel. Not a good place for a first date if you're trying to make a good impression.

This ish is bananas...great food, great service! KFC is addictive...my mouth is watering talking about it. The K-pop ambiance is the best!!!! Sat with the owner once at the bar, he's a good dude who really takes pride in this place, and it shows. He made me feel like I was a guest at an old friend's house for dinner, it was cozy and the food as always was delicious.
Very good Panang Curry and even better Spicy Fried Noodle with Tofu. Have always enjoyed the good and friendly atmosphere here.

Wow! I've NEVER eaten a food before that actually makes me happier as I eat it! But this place makes some wicked home-made egg noodles! From the outside, Sky Cafe does not look like much; in fact, it doesn't even look like a restaurant to me! But once you step inside of the corner store, you are just filled with the delicious aromas of Indonesia. Based off all of the helpful Yelp reviews, I decided to try Mie Komplit (N1 on the menu). It is there famous combination Homemade Egg Noodle Soup (the soup is actually served on the side). It consists of their homemade egg noodles, with shredded chicken, mushroom, barbeque pork (char sui), boiled egg, vegetable, 2 fried wontons, and a meat ball and fish ball served in a separate bowl of chicken broth. it's a lot of food and you get it all for $6.50!!! As I was eating, I just grew happier and happier as I ate! I don't know if it was because of the company I was with, the fun music they played in the background, or if it was those amazing home-made noodles (it was prolly the noodles) that just made me get in such a happy mood. I wish I knew about this place earlier, but I will definitely have to stop down here every time I am in Philly :D. Pros: - Relatively inexpensive....most plates go for around $6 - Home-made egg noodles!! You can definitely taste the difference! - Huge portions! Made me feel really full for a loooong time (I ate at 2pm and I didn't really eat dinner that day) Cons: - Parking is a little tough...you either have to back-in and park or parallel park, but there are a ton of spaces around Why I gave it a 5..... This is authentic Indonesian food (if you removed the pork products since Indonesia is mainly a Muslim country). Wonderful home-made noodles and you could really taste the difference while eating this :D i will definitely be stopping at this shop again for another meal in the near future!!

Ordered some takeout from here today. This was my second visit since I have been in Philadelphia and couldn't remember if I liked it or not the last time I was here. Well that was the answer: so-so. I had a lunch special and was very disappointed with the amount of food provided for an almost $10 kabob dish. There were literally 5 bites of meat, with some rice, a small salad and some bread. The meat and the rice tasted great, but geez, I'm not a bird. I also decided to try the "Special yogurt drink" thinking it might be similar to an Indian Lassi. Boy, was I wrong. That thing tasted like salty, sour ass. I could only drink a few sips of it and was completely repulsed. I tried to salvage it by adding 5 (!) packets of Splenda to maybe sweeten it up - didn't work and still tasted foul. I ended up pouring it down the drain. I bet that stuff works better than bleach in clearing it out. Also, this restaurant is subterranean and the small dining area has no windows, so it feels like you are in a closet. Food Quality/Taste = 3/5 Stars Portion Size Given Price = 2/5 Stars Experience with Staff = 3 Stars Decor = 2 Stars
Very clean and professional place. I would recommend the oxtails they're the best. This has to be the best Caribbean restaurant in philly!

We were on a two day visit to Nashville from Cincinnati. We were looking for a south Indian restaurant and bang, found Dosa Hut at Nolensville Pike. We did read the review and found it to be a mixed one. But, we wanted south Indian food and wanted to take a chance. Take my people, this place, the food is way good. They exceeded our expectations. My son is a Paneer person. We ordered Garlic Naan and Paneer masala. The gravy dish was awesome. Extremely tasty and flavourful. We had vada which was freshly fried and was very soft. Bollywood dosa is something you need to try. New concept and filling. Sambar and chutney was just like I have it back in India. Very flavourful. Coming to Filter coffee. For the first time ever in the US, having a coffee like we have in Chennai, India. It was pretty good. Overall, although the ambience was a little cramped, the food blew us away. Must try when you are in Nashville!

We are very cautious of where we go for any Asian cuisine. Our daughter is severely allergic to MSG and every derivative of it. So the day we tried SF and she didn't have any problems was wonderful. The summer rolls are one of my favorite things to get every time we go. My go to dish is the vermicelli noodles with bbq pork and I steal my husbands been sprouts. Having a place we can trust every time we go or when they are sick and are looking for pho is amazing.

Have you ever heard the acronym K.I.S.S.? It stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, and I suspect this is the driving mission behind the original Dmitri's in Queen Village. BYO and cash-only, Dmitri's gives you only straight, pure flavors in elemental preparations. Complimentary pita is charred on the grill, the scorchy lines bringing out the comfortingly homey bread's aroma and fluffy bite. A generous portion of chopped octopus tentacles swims in lemon and olive oil, tenderized by double cooking. A new menu item, spinach pie, was delivered to the table piping hot, steam escaping from its flaky onion, spinach and feta-lavished layers. If you need fancy preparations and upscale atmosphere, this is not the place for you. If you love a great deal on tasty, healthy food and enjoy pairing your own wine or beer to save mad ducats, take a date here and exploit the footsie potential of your cozy nook.

Another amazing BYOB spot in Philly. Le sigh. We ordered a few plates and shared for an hour long frenzy of lip-smacking, pita-dipping, appreciative-groaning good times. The Grilled Octopus- VERY generous portion for $12. Whatever it was marinated in was so so tasty. The meat may have been slightly overcooked as it was a bit chewy, but my dear Dmitri's veteran friend assured us that it is usually more succulent. Still delicious. The Shrimp Scampi- Ahhhh! Scary good. This was my favorite of everything we sampled. After the shrimp was gone, the extra oil/sauce was quickly obliterated by pita bread. The Fried Scallops- HUGE scallops! So silky, juicy, lightly fried. Just delicious. Chicken Kabob- Yummy yummy, juicy chunks of chicken that I unceremoniously slathered in tzatziki. Mmm, so much dill. The service was great as well. Our waitress was friendly and prompt. She immediately corked our wine and asked if we'd like our bottle of white to be kept in the fridge. By the time we finished it was almost closing time, so she sent us away with a few loaves of bread. Ace! *Cash only!

People who know me, know my love for hole-in-the-wall eateries. They have the best flavours, even if the ambience is a bit sketchy :). Finding Indian hole-in-the-wall eateries in the US is what I specialize in :) and am delighted in my finds! Dosa Hut is a tiny place, which is big on the taste of food it serves. I was stunned to find authentic dishes (Biryani, Kotthu Parotta, Indian railway cutlet) side by side with innovative ones (hara bhara kabab) in this small place. The cutlets did really remind me of the ones the Indian Railway used to serve .... There are several more interesting dishes on the menu, that I'd love to try on other trips. The place has only been open for 8 months at this point and the menu is a bit of a mish-mash, which works for me.... but the food is delicious. And what's more... the person who owns the restaurant is very courteous and gives you personal attention (and bottled water!). This is one place I'd love to see grow. We were deciding between the Chauhan Ale and Masala House (which had left us underwhelmed the last time, we were considering giving it another chance) and this one, we're glad we chose Dosa Hut.

I was in the mood for a lot of lamb so we decided to stop in and grab a few take-out dishes. We got the keema naan (soft, fresh, and stuffed with plenty of minced lamb, garlic, and onions - very good!), lamb kabab (okay but not as well-seasoned as Persian's; the slightly grilled onions and peppers gave it a nice, crunchy boost of flavor, although we definitely got a lot more onions than peppers), and the ubiquitous tandoori chicken (juicy, tender, and very thoroughly marinated - every bite was flavorful). Of course, when I saw the coconut barfi listed in the dessert section, I had to get an order of that too. And am I glad that I did! The coconut flavored cheese was creamy and indulgent; this was the first time that I have had this dessert and I really liked it a lot. It was a delicious combination of 2 of my favorite foods: nuts and coconut. Will definitely return for this since I haven't seen it at other Indian places in the area. Overall, I was pretty satisfied with the dishes and portions. They also gave us a 10% discount, which was really nice since we weren't even aware that there was such a promotion. It was about $40 for everything, which was packed carefully with plenty of accompanying fresh, aromatic basmati and chutney.

Been back twice since and they are doing a $1.99 special to celebrate their grand opening. The sandwiches are still good but it isn't as pretty as the first sandwich I had there. This time, the bread is the Publix hoagie roll. Don't get me wrong, I love the Publix hoagie roll. The veggie on the inside wasn't cut with the crinkle knife. I had the BBQ pork sandwich and it was kinda bland. (I am not a big Chinese red BBQ fan.) The meat wasn't cut smaller so that the BBQ seasoning goes all the way through the meat. You see this ring of red and this brown of flesh. There wasn't anything to take the bland away. The grilled sandwich was very good. It was seasoned nicely and the meat was cut smaller so the lemongrass flavor was all around. The sandwich is still fat with meat and filled with veggies and herbs. I asked for extra pickled veggies because there isn't enough to cut through the richness of the cold cuts and mayo. The guy wanted $3.99 for a small tub of it. That is cut throat pricing but I felt I had no choice. I ordered the chocolate cupcake and it was very expensive. It was almost $4.00 for the cupcake. Plus it wasn't good because it must have sat in the cooler too long or the cupcake was old. The icing was hard. The white decorative drop on the cupcake was rock hard when my sister bite into it.

I was quite pleasantly surprised by the quality and atmosphere of this inexpensive Mediterranean eatery. The owner is a jovial and likeable fellow who greeted us immediately and cracked jokes. He seemed to know many of his customers on a first name basis, as he served a few in front of my party. The classic gyro was glorious and huge, marking the first time I have not finished one in years, as I am a big dude. Pretty much everything my group had followed the same model of huge portions and top-notch quality. Seriously, you get half a pound of fried shrimp and fries for $7.99 on their daily special (and it is still only $8.99 normally). The aforementioned fries were the only average part of the meal, but they not bad either... just average and thus fine. It seems many Mediterranean places serve greasy and unpleasant fries, so I am happy here with average. Definitely check this place out for the seafood if nothing else, as you won't likely find it anywhere else for this speed, quality, and price.

This place was a pleasant surprise. I never new that "fast food" indian existed! I had the Tiki and Butter chicken. Both were tasty. And I found the prices super reasonable for the amount and quality I got. If you are in the area, this place is worth checking out. The only reason I gave it five stars was because the staff was just ok. The service was a little slow for no one being in the restaurant, but overall not enough to prevent me from coming back.

It was one of the few places still open nearby my hotel when I stopped by for a late dinner. I had the chicken kebab dinner and enjoyed every last bit. The chicken was moist and flavorful and the rice was well-seasoned. The best part of the dining experience was the informative and adorable waitress of all 9 years of age. Customer service with a smile goes a long way!
Great food with lots of variety. Everything on the Sunday buffet was fresh and looked appetizing. Service was excellent.

Food here is delicious. My company orders lunch from them every other week so I've been lucky enough to try a few of their dishes. I've gotten the Naan (of course), Chicken Tikka Masala, Vegetable Spring Rolls, Gobi Machurian, Chicken Saag and Navaratan Korma. They are consistent with good food, on time with delivery and the owner is extremely nice and helpful. Thank you for the excellent service and awesome food!

I went here on a Saturday afternoon with a vegetarian friend of mine. Reading the reviews I was expecting a crowd but it was only a couple of tables occupied. It could also be that it was 3pm. I got a large bowl of phó with taro milk tea and boba. Food arrives ten minutes later. The waitress seems to be in a bad mood and I dont bother much. The pho smells good and I'm more interested in diving into my bowl. It does taste good but not worth four stars for a review and definitely not worth five stars. I've had way better phó during my time in the dfw metropolis in Texas. I notice my milk tea with boba is frozen and not the way I ordered it so I call the waitress. She asks me 'what is it', from the place she is sitting expecting me to yell across the hall. I get up and walk towards her to explain what she got wrong about my order. She told me they don't serve milk tea any other way but frozen, and that's not possible. Why? Coz you blend it with ice and it becomes frozen. Duhhh!! I did not want a scene so retreated my steps back to my table and tried to enjoy what I had not ordered. To conclude, I'd say good Vietnamese food, but pathetic service. Such service can kill your appetite, so be ready for this and you'll be good. Had it been for better wait staff I'd have given this place a rating of 3 stars.

I have been to this restaurant a year before and loved the food. So decided to go back this Sunday. I ordered Veg Noodles, Chicken Noodles and Aloo Paratha. Veg Noodle was half cooked and Chicken pieces were not fresh at all, chewy and hard to swallow. As a Indian, first time I found that Paratha became Roti at this place. Horrible experience. When mentioned the same to the waiter (the guy serving, may be the owner), he smiled and not even bothered to take care of that. Just left, never faced this before. Before dining order, I placed take out order for Lachha Paratha and Chicken Vindaloo. No surprise, Lachha Paratha and Aloo Paratha both are actually tasted same. It does not make sense to discuss anything about the Vindaloo. They have changed the Chef as well as the management may be from my earlier visit. That guy could have shown some more concern when a customer does not like the food or say the food is not fresh. But no, he is just damned confident. I will never comeback.

Came into town last night and after going to the Bulldog we came here. Surprisingly the French Quarter was completely dead. Theres not much of a selection but I ordered a Beef & Lamb Gyro. I think the best tasting part of the gyro was the pita. It was soft and had this chewy texture. The meat didn't have much flavor and I couldnt tell what was beef and what was lamb. Skimpy on the lettuce and tomatoes and the white sauce. I dunno, maybe because I'm from New York City, which has 100s of places to get gyros (competition is a good thing), that I didn't find this place that awesome. Actually the friends I went there with said that this place wasn't as good as it used to be. Plus this is the only gyro place in the area so I guess they don't have to really make awesome food because ppl will come anyway. Oh did I mention that the gyro cost me $7?!?! Its only like $5 in NYC (and they give you more too)! And a can of soda was $2.....SMH

A slice of pizza is lunch. A hoagie is lunch. Falafel from Supercart is a force of nature, a tsunami cleverly disguised as ground up, deep fried chickpeas. As such, eating here is not to be undertaken lightly. Set aside about half an hour to wait in line, half an hour to eat, and a week or so to recover. You can order either a sandwich or the platter, though the sandwich is just a platter wrapped in pita. The exact contents of either is best left unknown, but always seems to involve falafel and chicken, along with some sort of starch. On separate occasions I've gotten rice, bowtie macaroni and what I believe (without evidence) was couscous. To top it off there's generally some sort of vegetable, sauce, spices and a few pieces of fruit thrown in. One last note, don't eat more than one a month. A fellow I know did, and he hasn't been quite the same ever since.

A delightful little spot in a strip mall, unassuming from the outside. Decor is charming, service is friendly and competent, and the food is delicious. Good variety in the menu, with all the classics and some good specials. LTC's "spicy" is not very spicy at all, so describe how hot you like it and they will happily meet your request. Prices are very reasonable, and the lunch specials in particular are a bargain at $6.95 including rice, as well as two extras (salad, soup, egg roll). And it is really nice to be able to have a cold beer with the meal.

How does this place have so many stars?! Seriously, they must be fake. Only thing going good for this place is location and crab Rangoon. Other than that they have bugs, I've seen them myself, it's dirty and the food is terrible. I'm sorry, but I've tried twice and both times I was discussed and pissed about how much I spent on food my dog literally wouldn't eat. The chicken they used for the general chicken was super cheap and had big fatty grissle pieces and it was soggy not crispy even a little. The sauce was terrible too. The first time was peanut sauce and the seafood mix and both tasted terrible. Don't waste your money
Best place to feel truly welcomed and wanted. The food is delicious and the hospitality is warming. I recommend Flambo to all who enjoys great Caribbean food along with a relaxing atmosphere.

Of course most people only know this place from the movie In Her Shoes. If you are one of those people, you may be surprised that the backyard is not, in fact, a summer wedding paradise, but you will not be dissapointed with the food. I recommend going when it is warm. My friend took me there in June so we could sit outside and it was like being on a little vacation from the city. The backyard has a lit path that leads to an outdoor hut-esce eating ground. Things you NEED to order: some sort of fresh tropical fruit juice, their beef patties appetizer (although a bit spicy) and DO NOT GO unless you plan to order the BBQ meal. Don't Miss: Outdoor movies nights. Want Jerk Hut's Jamaican food in the winter months? They deliver!!

Being someone who really enjoys Thai food, I would highly recommend checking this place out! My bf and I came and both ordered the special, he got chicken yellow curry and I got chicken red curry. Both were absolutely delicious! The specials also came with a coconut soup, spring roll, a shrimp spring roll, and wontons (all fried), and a nice side of rice. All of it was delicious and it was a lot of food! The service was also good. We received our food in a timely manner and the woman service us was very nice! We will definitely be coming back!

The minimum for delivery is $15 here, but the guy on the phone insists it's $20. He just called me back and continues to insist on a $20 minimum. As a courtesy, they should've let me slide, as my order was $16.14. Screw these folks! I'm hungry and angry.

Sometimes when there is only one restaurant of a cuisine you go there because it is the only one. That is not the case with Queen of Sheba. Queen of Sheba offers unique food that is well prepared in a nice setting.
