It is a good place to go for lunch although I hear that they will be closing for lunch except on Friday and Saturday starting in June. I have come to all of the reincarnations of this restaurant over the years and I think this is the best. I like the decor and sometimes if you get there early for lunch they have had incense burning which made the experience even more enjoyable. They are also open for dinner! They offer a wide array of appetizers and some are exceptional. If you like spicy foods I would recommend the Singe Karya which is a stuffed jalapeno. It is not only spicy but has an excellent flavor that is not overwhelmed by the spiciness. The Fire Shrimp were also very good and spicy, but I prefer the stuffed jalapenos. The Ana-Babro which has jalapenos and injera is also a good appetizer to try, but I prefer the Singe Karya. The Veggie Sambussa, is a good option if you are into fried foods. I also have tried the Buticha which is like a type of hummus made from chickpeas and the Azifah which is similar but made with lentils and mustard. Both were good when I had them last. Whenever I come I always have a cup of their hot tea. It is done really well with a lot of great flavors in it and is a perfect accompaniment to your meal. For people who have never eaten at an Ethiopian restaurant, one of the unique things is that you use your fingers and rip off pieces of a thin bread called injera and use it to scoop up your food. This way you have the taste of both in your mouth. I find the smell of injera a bit strange by itself, probably because it is fermented, but the taste is great. Injera is made with teff flour. Teff is a really tiny grain that can withstand a difficult climate and is common in Ethiopia and Eritrea. I usually get the vegetarian, meat or mixed combo platter. I think it is a great way to experience a lot of the different foods. All of the food is served in the traditional way on a large bed of injera, the Ethiopian bread, in little saucy piles. It is important to remember that you do eat with the bread and scoop your food with it. They do offer utensils if you prefer, but it is good to give the traditional style of dining a chance. It is a nice change. My favorite veggie dishes are; Ye Misr Wot (red lentils), Keiy Sire (beets), Ye Shimbra Asa Wot (spicy chickpeas) and the Mushroom Wot. I like the red lentils the best. My favorite meat dishes are Tibs Wot (beef and red peppers), Doro Wot (chicken in a stew with a hardboiled egg), Queens Beef Tibs (beef with jalepeno), Ye Beg Woti (lamb with berbere spice - I really like this one!) and Chicken Tibs (made with jalepenos ) I have never tried their seafood entrées but have had the shrimp appetizer. I think this is a great restaurant to go to and try something different. Please give this place your patronage it would be sad to see it gone from the community.

Pho King opened up in the neighbourhood about a year or two ago. Since then we've ordered in/picked up a couple of times but had never eaten in the restaurant. Whenever we ordered out, me, my dad and husband would get one of their vermicelli noodle bowls that come with spring rolls. I was always impressed with the taste of the food, as certain Asian restaurants have been really hit and miss for me. We finally decided to go into the restaurant this past weekend to try out their namesake, pho! I went with my husband and a girlfriend. We shared green onion cakes ($2.25) and six dumplings ($4.95) to start. I really love dumplings, and quite enjoyed these pork and veggie filled ones. I had the P3 - brisket and flank pho - regular size. very reasonably priced at $6.45. The bowl was a little bit smaller than others I've seen, but still huge and I still didn't finish it! Nothing to complain about with the flavour - I enjoyed it! Service was quite fast when we first got to the restaurant. The waiter took our order and our food came out quickly. Once we had our food, though, we didn't really see him again. Maybe once. The restaurant is small and he was never far, so if we did need him for something we could have gotten his attention easily. This might bother some people, but it was kind of nice that we were left to just linger and chat for two hours on a Friday night.

YELPERS, DO NOT OVERTHINK THIS! The food is fantastic, spice levels are appropriate (my wife ordered it mild while I ordered my food spicy), and the owners are fantastic people! Come out and support this gem, the place was nearly empty when we ate there. I do not get to this area often; however, I do not want to see it closed the next time I go due to a lack of business! Five stars, all the way!
Outstanding and delicious. My curries were out of this world..and the naan was so perfect. My mouth is watering... Can't wait to go back!

Labels itself mediterranean /Lebanese cuisine. In that case, I expect chopped fresh liver with mint, raw kebbeh etc etc. The place has a poor selection of Lebanese junkfood that is lesser than LaShish. Drove there for nothing....I mean middle eastern restaurant that serves all dressed pizza....what's next? Canellonis à la crème ??? Dude...seriously? This place needs to revamp the menu or it will close down

I cannot say enough amazing things about this food truck. I have yet to have better food from a truck in all of Philadelphia. This truck is better-than-restaurant-quality food, and is willing to customize the dishes that they have. If you want the best food for your buck, come to Zapata. Make sure to try the thai iced tea or coffee, the tilapia burrito, and the mexican veggie burger (and yes you really must try this, even "only eats something if it has meat in it" friend loved this). I came here a couple years ago at the behest of a friend, and after that first time the owner knew my name.

Quality food, only disappointment is not being able to get to them whenever I want. The food is consistently good 4 visits so far. Twice in one day to bring home dinner for the family after a great lunch. I've had Mofongo - Pork Chops, Chicken and Steak also Crab and Beef Empanadillas.

OMG! What a delightful treat it was to eat here!! Wish I could of ordered everything on the menu! It's hard to find good Asian food and this place had a nice variety to choose from and absolutely delicious! Was so full and satisfied didn't want to over indulge in my first visit so didn't order any shaved ice. However the shaved ice menu looked heavenly! Can't wait to go back!

We ordered the combo plate with four kebabs rice and extra naan. The lamb was phenomenal the chicken exquisite the steak fantastic. Funky little tables if you like that sort of thing and really good random beer. The prices were great and the experience will make us come back many times. Killer food!

My boyfriend and I (yup the guy that took me to Relish on our 1st date :) ) decided to go to Jasmine Rice on a whim before we headed to the Kimmel Center for a show. We absolutely enjoyed our food! I got the Pad Kee Mao with chicken and he got Fried Jasmine Rice with chicken. We didn't bring a bottle of wine because we went on a whim but we will definitely go back with a nice bottle of wine in hand since it's BYOB.

Food is yummy! I usually get the chicken salad sandwich with the slaw or the kabobs. Stay away from this place at lunch time unless you have an extra 25 min to wait for food it is usually a very long wait. However I believe they do have a call ahead option which I may try next time.
Delicious. Finally a decent pho place. I've tried all of them in the area, and this is definitely the best. We tried the pho and the pork plate, and both were really good. Definitely coming back!!

I like the Remedy Cafe because they can accommodate vegetarians, vegans, gluten free, and meat eaters! Not many restaurants lay claim to this kind of consideration. However, I just feel like all their food tastes the same-- maybe I'm just not appreciative enough of East Indian dishes... Their chai tea latte is amazing though! And I love how they give you the option of soy, almond milk, or dairy milk! All in all, a nice little place! The music was a little loud though!

The food was OK, but with really really poor service especially to Asian people. Both of the ladies were putting on a face like you owed them millions of dollars. The cashier lady was extremely rude and disrespectful, no verbal communication at all and asking me for tips like giving an order (pointing to the table with her finger, emotionless look). I was really hesitant but at last gave them a dollar, which I regretted so much. I came to this place because of the grocery I wanted to go and the other Vietnamese restaurant was too crowed. Apparently, I made a mistake and it ruins my day. I don't know if it ever happened to anyone else, but at least for me, NEGATIVE PLUS EXPERIENCE and WOULD NEVER RETURN AGAIN!

The food was so-so-not hot as in warm when it came. When the waiter put our waters on the table, which i hadn't noticed since it was behind my menu so when he said are you ready to order I knocked my water all over the table, myself and the floor. So most waitstaff would be like-oh let me wipe that up!!. Nope not this guy he continued to take my order (the water was dripping off the table-we grabbed our napkins and had a lake going on the table) and then walked away! He could have cared less! Oblivious to the disaster which was our table. Everything was soaked! So I asked for some napkins and he brought them--obviously it was to clean up all the water--he dropped them about 5 minutes later and walked off. THEN I had to request water!?!? Really?? The water all over the floor was wiped up by a bus person, who used a towel he was using to clean the tables--hopefully he threw it into the needs to be washed pile when he was done. Won't go back.
5 Stars! Best meal I had in a long time. The staff was helpful and friendly. That food was so good. Wish it was open more!!

Probably a 3 or 3.5 based on the food and price point but as other reviews have mentioned the service and hospitality is indeed very good so I bumped them up. After a trip to the Camden aquarium we wanted to try some of South Philly's famed Italian food. The highlight of the meal was the Pollo saltimbocca which had a delicious home made flavor, good portion size and tasty mushrooms. Penne vodka was a bit of a letdown by comparison. It's hard to explain but the taste wasn't as good as I've had at other restaurants. It tasted home made but not in a good way, unlike the chicken dish. The mussels and clams appetizer in spicy red sauce was another high point. The clams and mussels were small but tasted fresh and the sauce was great enough to want to keep dipping bread into. We also had the house salad... twice. The first time it came it was a bit too drenched in salad dressing. This would have been fine if the dressing weren't so salty - the ample amount of black olives didn't help with that either. Second time around we asked for the dressing on the side. Atmosphere and decor was a bit dated though warm. It got very busy as we were eating, which is a good sign. One weird thing I noticed was that tilapia is the only fish on the regular menu (though they did have a bronzini in the specials). Given how tilapia is not exactly known for its health benefits they would do well to offer health conscious customers better fish dish selections. Total price including tax and tip came out to $95 which is just a touch high in my opinion for what we got.

Best Vietnamese Restaurant in Nashville and the only one that seems to take credit cards. A win-win in my eyes. Their Pho and Bun Bo Hue broth is flavorful. Their prices are low and I love their Banh mi sandwiches.

extremely charming,intimate and plain old nice place to go and have an excellent traditional italian meal. i went the first time last year with mom,aunt cher,and cousin same age as myself 30. we all had a wonderful time and exceptional meal.we are all foodies and were extremely satisfied with both the quanity and quality of the food.in addition to an excellent meal served by a very friendly and polite staff,the owner was on location and truley made us all feel like family.he was a true gentleman and offered us each a drink,and suggested what meals may be best for each of us after a short discussion to enlighten himself with each of our individual tastes.i had the veal shank over risotto with some grilled italian vegs,which quite honestly was the most delectable shank i've ever had and def the lowest priced.im not one to concern myself with the price of a meal thats worth it,but a low price for a meal u'd gladly pay more for,is a definate perk.the eggplant and seafood is also very good and plentiful.the meal was finished with a complimentary shot of lemonchello which is a delight all its own homemade daily,and was paired with a very sincere thankyou from the owner personally.classy touch... 2 thumbs up for sure, the atmosphere is intimate,dim lights,quaint place maybe 7 tables,traditional white table cloths,very clean,simple bar fully stocked.great for a date, maybe better to be with someone special as there is not much distraction,its very quiet.great for family like granny or mom or husband especially such a nice place.. do try you wont regret it.
Excellent food and service. The Bhindi Masala is superior to other Indian restaurants.
Great food and service. Try the Nasi Goreng Special and thank me later.

Great cheap desi food which can be catered to all spice levels. Came in on a Tuesday evening on my way to Chicago, was surprised at the remoteness of the location and then furthermore surprised by the crowd inside. I had the chicken vindaloo - a non traditional dish but very spicy and not too oily. The bhindi (okra) was average. Rice was good. I am kicking myself for not going for the biriyani. All in all good for Indy if you are near I65.

Go here. It's Southern and seasonal ingredients filtered through a Southeast Asian prism. We had: * the wok-fried shrimp with ramen-style noodles--I kept eating the jumbo shrimp well after I was full, because they were too good not to finish; * grilled mullet, a whole fish that looked great but, according to the person who ordered it, didn't have a lot of meat on it; * the cracklins, little fried squares of skin each with its own quarter-inch of fat attached; * the som tam salad, like a Thai green papaya salad but with local winter-vegetable ingredients; * charred broccoli, the only dish that came up short for me--too much topping obscured the flavor of the broccoli; * coal-roasted sweet potatoes, delicious. Things tend to be a little to a lot spicy, so beware if that's an issue for you. I took one star off because my companion asked about the fish and was told it was not spicy at all, but it was. Not very, but use that as a baseline--"not spicy at all" here means "a little bit spicy."

I think this was one of the first Japanese retaurants in Pinellas county. It used to be THE place to go back in the day. They always serve consistently good, if not great food. It is always a fun place to go. The 3 sided sushi bar lets you strike up conversations with other diners easily. The staff are awesome, especially the sushi chefs.

First time here and I love it ! It's hard to find good Spanish food in the city . The service was fast, prices are reasonable, and the food was delicious. Plus they have a parking lot so you don't have to pay for parking and they are open until 9pm. Will definitely be returning ! I had the chicken and white rice platter with a pacha juice which was all great !
Food is amazing, however the missing fifth star is because the staff could be a little friendlier.

Favorite breakfast sandwich truck in Philly. You can't go wrong with a sausage egg and cheese (I'm not a fan of bacon) or the veggie special. They can easily do egg whites and wheat rolls for the health conscious, and I always ask for extra ketchup instead of their mayo-based Bui's sauce. If you're in a rush, call in and place your order. No matter where you're coming from, it's generally ready by the time you get there. Or if you have a minute to enjoy the sunshine, you can chill in their lawn chairs and make some new friends. I would definitely call this place a University City staple.
Ate here twice while on a business trip. Nothing fancy: simple, very good, and affordable. The owner was very friendly. When in the area, I will go back

Had Gigi and Big R at the Wawa Welcome America Fest on July 4th. Awesome Jerk Chicken (big portions enough for two), Mac and Cheese and Collard Greens. The jerk chicken was slow cooked, very tender, along with the spices it was marinated in. Definitely hot and spicy, but some of the best jerk chicken that I have had.
Good Job ! Megan ... Service was Grrreat .... Food was special... It is what you look forward to when you are from out of town..... Good Old Fashion Courtesy.....

Very nice and spacious place the food is amazing we enjoyed the curry goat, oxtails, plantains, cabbage, red beans n rice and both of the refreshments ginger and the hibiscus it was a large portion and nicely seasoned n yummy. So spoiler alert the bar is an illusion not an operating bar and service is awesome but may be slow due to one server but it's all worth the wait he is amazing.

This was my third visit (2 dine in, 1 take out.) I have nothing but good things to say about this place. Food was delicious and fresh. Staff was friendly and fast each time. I was pleasantly surprised to learn that they offer a lunch special including soup, app and entree for $9.99. It is a good amount of food and everything I ordered was served hot, and fast. (Important since I was on my lunch break this time around.) My waitress was pleasant and attentive. It was a little chilly in the restaurant and I thought it was just me, until I heard others mention it as well. I ordered the Thai dumplings, Thai ravioli soup and the chicken pad Thai... All were very good. Pad Thai is always my go to! Overall, very good. I will for sure be back.

Great coffee, great pita bread with gyro meat and taziki sauce. My husband had the beef kabab and yellow rice. We both shared a walnut baklava. Very good over all. Great decor with cultural influence from the Kurdish nation.

Very disappointed with the chicken pad Thai. There just wasn't enough flavor. I've had a lot better elsewhere, but then again this is a Vietnamese food restaurant and not a Thai food restaurant. However, their pho soups are pretty good.

I traveled to south India recently and had the opportunity to eat in several hotel restaurants. A few of them had good food but none of them had the great food that I regularly enjoy at my favorite Indian restaurant in the world. The quality and flavor of the dishes at India's Kitchen in Saint Louis far surpasses all of the restaurant fare I tried from Hyderabad to Khammam. Neeraj's cooking is consistently excellent!! Only the home-cooked meals lovingly prepared by my friends in India were on par with the delicious cuisine available at India's Kitchen. Now that I am back in the US, I am so glad that I can still enjoy the wonderful foods I love so much! I highly recommend this establishment to all. Not sure whether you like Indian food? Try the daily lunch buffet. It is a great bargain and so tasty!

Honestly, I was really looking forward to this place being great. Last week I was in Birmingham MI and had excellent Indian food, so when I got back to Saint Louis I still had the crave. So going off the reviews this seemed like a no brainier. I ordered Lamb Biryani, Chicken Tikka appetizer, and Garlic Naan. The biryani looked great but end up being dry and the lamb was tough & the yogurt was not good tasting at all, The tikka tasted better but again very dry, however, the garlic naan was very good. I may give them another try in the future but for now, I'll just go to my aunties house for biryani.

A friend of mine was passing through town, and we wanted to go to a fast, casual place, with good food. Since I live near campus, this seemed like a good time to try this- its located super close to the IUPUI campus, which is definitely convenient for a college crowd. The staff was super patient and friendly as we decided what to get- we both opted for paneer naan pizzas, but with different toppings so we could try out different combos. The idea is similar to chipotle- you picked a dish style (Bowl, Pizza, or Sandwich), a sauce base, protein, toppings, and chutney. There are tons of options to choose from, so it's very customizable. The staff offered suggestions and their own ideas, and their feedback definitely helped. The paneer was shredded, which seemed a bit unusual, but it worked! Both of us really enjoyed our dishes, and we had plenty to take home. seen people say its a little overpriced- I think its very comparable to Chipotle in terms of price. This is a new, small business, and a great addition to the Indy area- I hope it continues to thrive!

This restaurant is recommended by my client. He grew up from Puerto Rico and he has indicated the food is close to his mom cooking. The Spanish music play in the background with lively atmosphere. This the first time I try Puerto Rican restaurant in USA. I have Puerto Rico cuisine at Puerto Rico before. I can said the restaurant at La Casona has interesting Puerto Rican menu. It include traditional Mofongo. Mofongo is a fried plantain-based dish from Puerto Rico. It is typically made with fried green plantains mashed together in a with broth, garlic, bit fried pork belly. It can be filled with vegetable, meat or seafood. This restaurant open since 1999. It have Spanish base customer. Today we have the seafood Mofongo and churrasco. The seafood Mofongo came with half of the lobster tail, shrimp, salty fish, muscle. I was impress of my Mofongo serve with a bit wine base seafood broth. When you bite the olive they have cook with it, the wine juice came out and it is tasty and left wine fragrant in the mouth. This normally different than the Wikipedia description to prepare it. The broth base mix with the fried green plantain neutralize the salty of the broth. The two materials balance each other is the beauty of cooking. Good chef skill. The churrasco is ok. It can be better. Churrasco is Argentina food. Most of the time the Cuban restaurant prepare this dish better than anyone in Miami. You have choice with rice and bean or salad and sweet plantain. The service is good and friendly. However, the close out and bring the check is slow. This restaurant customer tender to speak louder due the natural of the Spanish customer. Food is good portion. Most of time you will have enough to take home for the remained meal.

This is a particular kind of Vietnamese experience - I agree with other reviewers who have noted it's lack of authenticity, but I kind of like that about it. It's mild, but reasonably priced and has great service. The bubble drinks are fun, the spicy beef soup is yummy - just ask for extra heat and they'll give you some great house hot sauce.
Awesome!!! Literally every bite is a new sensation in your mouth. I came once, by yelp suggestion. I came back and bought my family because the taste was indescribably good!!

Food was very good and authentic. Music and service was great as well. Family owned business and they all work there. Only bad thing I would have to say is that the furniture was a little too modern for it to be a West Indian restaurant. Nonetheless it's a very clean and beautiful place. Will definitely be back again.

This place is a family tradition we Always look forward to coming every year and sitting outside in the beautifully carved wood hutches. The staff here is incredible and food is even better. I always order the pumpkin curry-- I can't find it like this anywhere else!

We celebrated my husbands birthday at The pearl last night, and couldn't have been more thrilled. The Pearl has a lovely cozy atmosphere when you walk in, and there was a very talented guitarist playing throughout the evening. We decided to ask our server about the Special 4 course option combo with a bottle of wine. This included, 2 starters of our choice, a house salad, Chateaubriand steak and lobster tails, and dessert of our choice. We went for this and were so happy we did. We choose the escargot and mussels for starter which were both delicious. The dressing on the house salad was very tasty. Our steak was a very large portion and cooked to perfection. The lobster tails were fresh and delicious. Served with the most creamy and tasty potato soufflé, and oven roasted vegetables. The staff at the Pearl were incredibly friendly. And the chef came out and met us and served our main course at our table. 100% would go back and highly recommend you try this hidden gem!
Horrible Service. The Food was barely Tolerable. My overall experience with the waiter has just horrendous. Not going back.

It's probably a really good thing that this isn't located anywhere near me! Indian fast food?!? Dangerous for my waistline and my wallet. The variety wasn't huge and the establishment small, but it was definitely worth the money. for the price you pay, you get a heaping plate!

I have been going to Nadia's since they opened over 5 years ago and their quality has always been excellent. Nothing has really changed over the years which makes them consistent and reliable. Their silver noodles dish is my favorite and their soups are very flavorful. They're also vegetarian and vegan friendly - they always ask of eggs are okay which is something I always appreciate. They're great for a quick lunch or a casual dinner.

This place deserves every single star. It is so incredibly good. I've tried a lot of their dishes here and every single one never fails to be flavorful and delicious. I recommend the Salmon Panang as that has become my go to. The place is small so not recommended for large groups. However, if you're grabbing dinner with a friend, consider this place! It's very clean and the staff is super sweet. The dishes take a while to come out but you know they're cooking it fresh so no complaints from me!

The Tryst is one of many reasons to go to Downtown St Petersburg. It is across the street from The Museum of Fine Art. Service is always friendly but can be really slow on overcrowded late nights. Inside and outdoor dining options are wonderful. The cheese tray with a bottle of wine is one of my favorite items to share.

Add to the list of terrific places on Freret Street to have a nice lunch: The baguettes that they have here are delicious. My fav's are the grilled beef and also BBQ Pork. Delicious! Their appetizers are also very tasty. My GF always gets some sort of noodle dish which are also positively endorsed. Has a nice clean tight appearance inside.
Pho is inexplicably flavorless. Vermicelli and rice plates are better. Banh mi are excellent.

Taste is not authentic. . It was a tuesday night. Only 3 tables were occupied. Still the service was very bad. Meat was half cooked and smelled raw. Chicken kadai masala was a disaster. Murgh shorba was ok. Naan was good. Service and food are not at all worth the money. India villa serves better food. I am never going again to this place.

Ohhhhh the green curry. I could drink it! (And try too if I finish the vegetables before the sauce). I always want to try other things, but the green curry is so good it's hard for me to stray from it. Good service, the Thai tea is awesome, and the food is yummy.

I don't know about the other dishes, but I wouldn't recommend the Pad Thai. This was only a poor approximation of what Pad Thai should be. I ordered the lunch portion and received noodles swimming in what tasted like store-bought Pad Thai sauce. The chicken was cooked well and nicely spiced. Overall, the dish was a brown mound of noodles and chicken, not the bright, light, and wonderful culinary creation that Pad Thai has the potential to be. That said, as "just food", it was tolerable and I didn't leave hungry. If you are just looking for a quick lunch and don't care about getting a good Pad Thai, it'll do. The service was quick and businesslike, the prices are reasonable.

When I proffered my companion the option of a "Vietnamese place down the block" or ordering in pizza, the choice was the former. Now we both feel very strongly about pizza-it's easy and almost always delicious. But I'm glad we decided on dinner at Vientiane Cafe because it reminded me that it's probably my favorite Thai restaurant in town. I'll mention that I love that this restaurant is especially friendly to vegetarians, which is likely a calculating move given its location in the transition zone from University City and West Philly. The service was just the tiniest bit slow, but nothing egregious. After all, Friday night is bound to be busy. We got the Tofu Skewers for appetizers (4 perfectly grilled slabs of Tofu) and the Green Curry and King Soup for entrees. Since we're both suckers for fever-inducing food, we were slightly disappointed that the Green Curry, which was marked with their highest spice rating, didn't register a temperature for us. Which is not to say it wasn't flavorful. The King Soup was, well, majestic. The curry-coconut broth was rich and chock full of noodles, bean sprouts, cabbage and adorned with the perfectly crispy-soft pieces of tofu. The wait staff, while not overly attentive, was prompt in responding to our various requests during the meal. A final note is that the place is cash only!

Took my family here on a Sunday afternoon who came to visit from CA. We were seated immediate waiting for the rest of our party 7 to show up so we were put to the overflow side on the right. We got our menus and water and the rest of the family showed. Took them a while to come back to take our order. It was a good 15 mins til we flag someone to take our order. We ordered a variety of appetizers, some rice dishes, and a few pho bowls. They were all wonderful. My sister and I order the bun bo hue and it was terrible! Super salty and level 10 spicy. Not sure what went wrong with this dish, but not even the herbs can save it. My sister literally has to steal her husband pho broth to dial down the spiciness. We get that bowl is spicy but omg you could kill someone with how spicy it is. I love this place don't get me wrong I would be back but kind of bum that they actually serve bun bo hue and it was terrible. Not to mention service was a little slow. It might be a while til I'll be back. They were my go to Vietnamese restaurant, but seeing it's growing in Indy, I'll be going else where.

Sometimes you just want a big, greasy gyro, wrapped both in wax paper and foil, and a mound of fries. That's exactly what I got here, for under seven bucks. It was amazingly good. The people were extremely friendly, and my food was ready a lot faster than I thought it would be. The meat was savory and juicy. The tzatziki sauce was deliciously creamy. The tomatoes and lettuce and cucumbers were fresh and cut thick. And, best of all, the pita held everything together nicely - until it didn't. There's a very good reason they put a fork in the bag. It may not be totally authentic. It may be a bit Americanized. But you know what? I don't care. I'm not looking to do field research for a culinary anthropology dissertation. I want a good meal that's also fast and affordable. And that's exactly what I got here. I think I've found my new weekly indulgence.

I had Afghan cuisine for the first time ever and absolutely loved everything I ate. 'Ashak' is a must try item on the menu, 'Qurma Chalaw' is simply delicious with the perfect blend of spices. I finished the meal with 'Firni' and 'Sheeryakh.' I am definitely coming back when I visit Philly again.

Friendly, fast and delicious. Food was presented beautifully and promptly. The appetizer sampler was perfect to share and gave us a taste of Puerto Rica....the well seasoned fried chicken dish with beans and rice was excellent (sorry can't remember the Puerto Rican name)! We didn't have much time to spare as we were in the area for a show at Mercy Lounge.....but Salsas was the perfect stop for us to have a quick supper before the show. We will definitely return to this fun, casual restaurant. Looks like a nice place for a cocktail too, although we didn't partake.
Great service, wonderful food and setting. My only reservation would be prices for the wine. A modest meal became a $100 night by adding a few glasses of vino. That said, I look forward to returning.

We were going elsewhere for a Vietnamese lunch when our original location was unavailable and we drove 45 minutes to come here. It was well worth it! The Pho, bahn mi and stir fried noodles were delicious. Planning on making the drive up from Indianapolis at least once a week.

Good lunch buffet. Not so great service. Polite but not around often even when not so busy. Food is fresh and taste great. Cheap too. Decent selection of food as well. Naan bread is hot and fresh. My favorite part.

How have I not eaten here until tonight? Because I wasn't sure I still liked Indian food. Shame on me, new favorite restaurant in MJ! Justice (waitress) talked us through the menu with perfection and we ordered all of her suggestions and were not disappointed!!! Butter Chicken, some vegetarian "fried rice", tikka chicken with mint sauce and a buffalo friend cauliflower app. Not to forget the cheese stuffed naan (add garlic) was amazing....everything! Plus bring your own wine without a corking fee! We made it out for $14 each plus tip! Not going to lie I will probably go back this weekend!

In our quest to find the best Indian luncheon buffet, we stopped by to see how their's was. The restaurant is in Feather Sound in a location where a number of restaurants have before resided. This restaurant has several franchises: New York, San Francisco and Jersey City to name few. We arrived at a little after 11am on a Sunday. They were not ready for us. It was about 25 minutes before we were given the OK sign to start the buffet. The offerings were abundant and varied. This buffet had, by far, the spiciest food selection we've had in Pinellas Co. The Tandoori chicken was particularly succulent. There were a lot more varieties of rice and vegetarian dished than we've seen at other restaurants. The soup was spicy and delicious. There were two dessert dishes that were offered, one warm and one cold. Overall, we did eat some great Indian dishes. The service was a bit slow. As with some other restaurants, please don't say that you're ready to open for business when you aren't. I would have appreciated that the hours were stated to be 11:30am rather than 11am. We didn't appreciate sitting and waiting for a buffet to be set up. The interior was clean and upscaled except for the restrooms. The buffet prices are in line with comparable buffets that we've visited.

Not going back. Really below average in quality, flavor, and service. Vegetables were limp and I feel were definitely canned. The buffet selection was very limited. The salad bar was unappealing, which I wasn't concerned about as that is not what I am going to an Indian restaurant for. The chicken entree at the buffet (and we did arrive right when they opened so presumably everything was just made) was dry and tough and the sauce was uninteresting. Remarkably, even the traditional white basmati rice wasn't good. How is that possible?!! On the plus side, the lamb was edible and the Naan bread was actually good. I would give the service a 3 on a scale of 1-10. Highly recommend you try somewhere else.

Should be good, but just isn't. To be honest, sometimes the food is actually good. However, it's also very inconsistent. It can go from mild to very spicy on the same order on different days. They have continually gotten my take out order wrong as well. Would love it if the quality and consistency improved.
Baigan bartha and bindi were spiced beautifully without being too fiery Garlic nan soso

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This place was really good! They have an extensive Vegan menu. The vegan coconut lassi was so flipping good! We ordered Chana masala and aloo gobi. We also got free samosas for checking in on yelp! Everything was so tasty, while the owner was friendly, funny, and welcoming. The owners wife does all the cooking and does a great job!

The scrumptious eats at Momo's will have you coming back fo mo! There are three types of gyro- lamb, chicken, and veggie. I had the lamb gyro which was OVERSTUFFED with meat, latteuce, tomato, feta cheese, and of coarse the necessary tzaziki sauce. Their tzatiki sauce was a little sweet, which was new to me, but still delish. I also got a great caesar salad to start. The atmosphere is pleasant and decor is spunky with a hot red ceiling and warm tones through out. Service was friendly! Greece's economy may be in ruin, but Momo's is a Greek joint I'd happily invest in again!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We stopped at Taj Mahal while visiting Boise and wandering downtown. They are some of the nicest people anywhere. Extremely personable, and very happy in general. The service was excellent, and the food was fantastic! We all tried the buffet, and having sampled everything that was available I can say the flavors are well-balanced and authentic. Reasonable prices, great food, and good people. What more can you ask for? Highly recommended and would eat here again many times over.

Leaving Busch Gardens we decided to try a local joint!! We were not disappointed!! Ended up trying out the Zeafood Platter which was AMAZING!! The fish was grilled to perfection, the calamari was tender and not chewy, beans and rice were full of flavor, and the chop chop side salad was fresh. We also ended up trying the boneless fried wings. Really liked the honey BBQ, solid flavor. The falafel's were pretty good, but not exceptional. To finish off the meal we had Baklava, which hit the spot and wrapped up a nice meal. We like how it feels like a fast food Greek place at first but the food is more like a higher end restaurant with solid colorful plates instead of a "Captain D's" type presentation of the food. They did not have store hours posted on the door and Yelp said they were closed when they actually were not. Glad I decided to tempt fate and see if they were open anyway....... You looking for an authentic Greek resturant close to Busch Gardens in Tampa, this is the place to go!!
Good service, Beef w/ Lemon Grass was good, meat was tender and plentiful. I'll have to try the Pho next time as that's probably a better indicator...
Great reataurant. Excellent location on the water. Watched the sunset over the water from our table. Fish tacos were very tasty. Onion straw appetizer also good.
Have done the Tandoori chicken and biryani takeout atleast 100 times and never been disappointed. Don't bother with the typical chicken tikka masala and curries. That's not why you come here.

I would get takeout here for lunch. Everything I've had here has been excellent. Although they sometimes forgot things or added and/or changed your order unexpectedly, it was never so drastic that I didn't enjoy my meal. Anyway, I'm a fan of the drunken noodles! If you like spice, make sure you ask for it because sometimes they don't make it spicy at all. Nonetheless, even with all their quirks, it's easily one of the best restaurants in the Lansdale area.

Second we've been here. We love it. Great service and great food. There's a special board as you enter that you might want to take a look as before sit down as those things aren't on the menu. We ordered two items from that board - smoothies and the chicken dish.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This is my favorite restaurant in Boise. I've never in my life had food that tasted as good as the Chicken Korma and the Rogan Josh dishes here. And the naan is to die for. Seriously good. Take your time if you go there for dinner, she makes everything from scratch, but it is well worth the wait. Lunch buffet is also fantastic. I'm usually not sure what the dishes are in the buffet, but I'm never disappointed. Everything is delicious.
Food is great. Nothing compared to city where competition pushes. I ordered pick up and got no receipt, condiments or even a paper napkin. Used to be great, now service is going downhill.

When you eat at Zeppoli you are eating in someones home. This small BYOB in West Collingswood has established themselves as the best Italian restaurant in the area. All the food is prepared fresh and the ingredients are seasonal. The cuisine is traditional Sicilian. The servers are knowledgable and friendly and the decor is rustic and quaint. This no frills approach to service and design lets the inspired food at Zeppoli take center stage. Appetizers here are delish. The fresh seasonal antipasto will satisfy everyone at the tables desires. Fresh arugula salad, marinated vegetables, sopressata, cheese, and a scoop of their tuna white bean salad that is so good you may have to fight over who gets the last bite. Second course is homemade pasta featuring spinach and ricotta Gnocchi and an awesome Rigatoni with tomato sauce, eggplant and breadcrumbs that is good enough to have as an entree. For entree free range chicken, and Mediterranean fish stew thats packed with a variety of fresh seafood is my personal favorite because you get something different in each bite. The only downside is that the place (although totally worth it) can get a little pricey, and I wish I could afford to eat here every week. So it will be a special night out kind of a place for us. Chef Baldino has a real passion for the dishes he creates and he and everyone at Zeppoli are a welcome addition to Collingswood.

I have to say the owner/operator of this establishment does good by his word. Since I wrote my review, I was sent a few coupons to try the food again. I have to say, the portion sizes have significantly improved. Excellent customer service!

A rare bastion of Eastern Europe in the Nashville area (another is in Mt. Juliet) with simple home cooking. The menu is a bit scaled down from when they first opened but the dishes that were cut were largely the non-Bosnian ones. For simple grilled meats, turkish coffee and super home-made soups at low prices, this can not be beat. The language spoken by other customers attests to its authenticity.

The food at pollo tropical is decent, nothing out of this world. I recommend the grilled chicken breast, and the regular chicken dinner with sides. The Caesar salad was not as good, just ok. And the riblets were ok as well, not my favorite. I probably won't be ordering those again. As far as the side dishes, the rice, beans, and corn had good taste. The restaurant is new in the area and this might be the reason their service is slow.

Was really impressed by Dmitri's. Sometimes simple is best. Dmitri's does simple very well. Dmitri's does seafood well. A good amount of the reviews talked about the Grilled Octopus ($12) here and those folks did not lie. That is an amazing dish. Along with that we got a plate of Hummus and Baba Ganoush ($7.50), the Citrus Salad ($8.50), Mussels Saute ($12) and Seafood Fettuccine ($15). This is definitely a good place to order a bunch of dishes and share. That is exactly what this group of 3 did. The salad came out first. Needed more avocado, but the slices of orange and grapefruit were a nice touch. Next up the hummus and baba ganoush with bread and pita triangles. The baba ganoush was especially good. Might be the best I have had in a long time. From there we went more into the entree section of our meal. The octopus and mussels come from the "Little Dishes" section of their menu. Not large, but not small by any means. The mussels were a bit on the dry side, but that didn't seem to take away from the dish much. The dark horse here (not really a dark horse as a few of the reviews I read highlighted this dish) was the grilled octopus. I could eat this dish forever and ever and ever. It is that good. I couldn't even tell you what kind of sauce this was. It was very light. Possibly just some white wine and lemon and some garlic. Nothing crazy. Doesn't take away from the taste of what you are actually eating. Sometimes places go crazy with their sauces and you lose all the flavor of what you are eating. Not here. For the main main course we had the Seafood Fettuccine. Fettuccine in a garlic and white wine broth (I think) with mussels, clams and shrimp. Again, very simple but oh so good. Dmitri's seems to be a local Philadelphia chain. There are 2 others scattered around town. That certainly shouldn't dissuade you from coming here. If you sit at the bar area you can watch them make the seafood right in front of you. The action is right in front of you and the smells are just amazing. Seems like they've been doing this for years. Seems like they will be doing it for quite a few more.

I have to say I was a little disappointed at Jasmine Rice. My BF and I go to Smile Cafe way too often on Saturday night date nights so we were in the market for a new Thai place. On a recent visit my boyfriend informed me that Jasmine Rice had just opened and that it looked cute inside. OK he didn't exactly say that, but the interior designer definitely did a good job making this a cozy place. By the way, their bathroom is very clean which is always a plus. To start things off, we ordered our usual fav appetizer, Chao Phraya Express, which was a solid version of a summer roll. We tried Pad Khimao (Drunken Noodles) and Massaman Curry for our entrees. Boring I know, but we like to stick to the standard dishes when we're trying out a new restaurant. We both were impressed with the food here. BF said that the Pad Khimao was the best he's had yet in Philly. I thought the curry was tasty and spiced nicely. I was also impressed with the presentation. So why the 3 stars? I admit that I had gotten used to the cheap Thai restaurants in Chicago where you could get a great plate of Pad Thai for $7. Portions at Jasmine Rice are on the smaller side, and the prices are a little bit more than I like to spend on my student budget. Additionally, the place is kinda cramped--even for a small Asian like me. Tables are stacked right next to each other, and this made the dining experience a little uncomfortable. I guess I was hoping this would be the cheap, neighborhood Thai place. One where you could quickly stop by any day of the week and get a filling dinner. This is not that kind of place, but the food is still good.
If I could go here everyday I would! Ambiance, friendly service, delicious Chai tea and food, cute café, lovely décor. If you haven't made your way here yet, "chop chop"!

Probably my favorite place in all STL to eat. Food and drinks are always delicious and I love the atmosphere being in an old service station. When it's nice outside, the side patio is pretty especially at night with the lights, and the garage door that opens is nice too!

Love this place! I'm a college student living in Manayunk, so nothing beats great food, great prices, and great service. I got the hummus and veggie sandwich along with a Tangy Raspberry smoothie. The vegetables were fresh and the pita bread was wonderful. Not to mention the hummus--so good!!!! My friend got the beef gyro and loved that as well. There is a cute little area in the back with tables, couches, and t.v. Will definitely be back!!!

Loved, loved, loved the food! So much to choose from and taste. Each dish was uniquely seasoned, with a layering of flavors..all were delicious. After an amazing dinner the dessert was equally special. Can't wait to go back and try more. Great fun to share with a group of family/friends.

Wow-what a pleasant suprise Lists itself as serving Mediterranean Food. Purchased a Groupon after I had heard some positive statements about the restaurant. Food was amazing and at very reasonable prices. Where to begin? Bread basket had whtie bread, olive bread and some wonderful fried pita pieces. The building itself was much more modern and larger than I anticipated from the store front. The Arancini appetizers were crisp, and a nice blend. The entrees were an interesting mix of Greek and Italian. I had the kofte iskender which was a delicious Turkish entree which was lamb served with pita, marinara, yogurt . The lamb was covered in marinara sauce, over cut up pieces of pita. Very unique. My husband had the lobster ravioli which had rock shrimp, spinach , tomato, sherry cream. So creamy and so good. Our dining companions had the Grilled Salmon, which was a large size piece, and one had mussels which she said were small, but some of the best she has had since some other StL restaurants have closed. 2 of us had asparagus sides, and 2 had the spinach salads which were a bit unique with the cranberries, candied walnuts and pomegrante vinagrette. All entrees under $20, so entire meal very reasonably priced. Shared dessert was a very nicely balanced piece of hazelnut teramisu. They also have a sign for a happy hour offering their flatbreads and Arancini at very reasonable prices, along with discounted wines and liquor. The reason I took one star off was for slow service. I am assuming they have gotten increased business due to the coupons. Our wait for our entrees was a bit long. Water refills were good, as was service for wine. Oh, and one last thing, the two males were especially thrilled to find Paulaner Hefeweizen on tap, apparantly a real treat. Will definitely make a return trip. Great, great, meal at such good prices. Put it on your "To Try" list definitely!

Could be my new favorite Indian restaurant in St. Louis. I'm no expert, mind you, but when there's a table full of Indian guys watching India vs. South Africa in cricket, I think it's a good sign. Although the name sounds like fast food or some kind of chain, this is the ultimate Mom and Pop joint. He's out front providing attentive and friendly service, she's in back preparing an impressive variety of Indian dishes, plu a few Americam items. It's small - there is seating for maybe 16 or 18. Take a seat when you arrive (there is no sign instructing you to do so). Per the recommendation of the RFT, I tried the Beef Nihiri, noted as a "Specialty Dish." I saw some other people get their biryani, which looked just excellent. I'm pretty sure this was my first time having beef at an Indian restaurant. It was awesome. I ordered it spicy, although I was a little scared when he said, "Are you sure?" It was hot, but not bad, at least for me. She might have Americanized it a bit. Anyway, it was probably the best dish I've had at an Indian restaurant since the Lamb Vindaloo at India Palace a couple of years ago. There is a lot of variety on the menu (chicken wings, Philly, fries...), so expect a bit of wait. I don't think I would have wanted it any other way. This food is obviously prepared with care. Ifyou like Indian food, go.

This place deserves a chance! I thought the spring rolls were excellent, tightly round, equal part rice noodle and meat, I think it could use more cilantro. The dipping sauce was the best I've had in boise! The pho was good too, very hearty, the broth was delicious, everything was really good! Friendly service. The place had okay decor but nothing that would scare me away. The people took a lot of pride in their food and I love that feeling. I would recommend getting the pho with beef and spring rolls!
Service was OK. The drunken noodles was OK, but not at all spicy.

I love the veggie food here. My absolute favorite dish is the kadhi pakora. It reminds me of my aunts kadhi pakora from back home. Then there is samosa and the eggplant potato dish - always perfectly seasoned and cooked. The chats are great too - the explosion of tastes you expect - never lets you down. The mix of the crispy papad followed by yogurt and date/tamarind chutney then mint chutney. The only chicken dish I like is the tandoori chicken wings. Why don't I like the other chicken dishes - well that would be because the chicken is always dry. I have tried kadai chicken, chili chicken, chicken madras, chicken biryani.

I've been tandoor a few times for lunch with my family. The staff is always very friendly, and playful with my 3 year old son. My son says it's his favorite restaurant (even though he only drinks the mango lassi). Also, the food is stellar, and I enjoy that the bring out fresh naan bread to the table. Keep up the good work!

Excellent food! Try the jerk chicken - it was amazingly spicy! I was also pleasantly surprised by the upscale decor in the restaurant. The owners are super friendly and give excellent customer service.
Aromatic, authentic, and well worth whatever they want to charge. Really good buffet full of options you're used to seeing and some things you need to try. The coconut rice is exceptional.

Best crab rangoon probably ever!!! Tasty lychee martini - strong but still good. Had some drunken noodles- big shrimp , got it made spicy which was just how I like it - spicy enough to make my nose run but didn't burn my tastebuds. Great wait staff!! Didn't care for the mochi ice cream but probably just an acquired taste ... definitely recommend this place!

Very good Thai food. Tonight we had: Starters: Spring rolls, shrimp salad, and chicken satay Entrees: Prik King Pork, Pumpkin Curry with Chicken, Pad Thai, and steamed rice. Desserts: Fried bananas with ice cream, sticky rice with mangos I particularly enjoyed the Prik King Pork and Pumpkin Curry with Chicken. The Prik King was nice and spicy with a hint of sweetness; the green beans were perfectly cooked. The desserts were a nice finish to a spicy meal. Other notes: okay wine list with decent pricing; service was good as well.
Excellent food. Had the yellow chicken curry. The fried banana with coconut ice cream was superb

I've been craving Dominican food for a while and I read a lot of great reviews about this place. For appetizers, I ordered sweet plaintains and beef patties. For the main course I ordered boneless pork and yellow rice with black beans. My boyfriend ordered salmon and yellow rice. We also ordered a side of oxtails. I was quite underwhelmed with the food. My pork lacked flavor and was very dry. It was really hard to eat the meat cause it was so bitter. Ultimately, I ended up throwing out most of it. The rice was bland. The beef patties and plaintain was ok. My boyfriend didn't really like the sauce the salmon was in. We probably will not eat here again.

I would say that this is a standard Chinese take-out joint. The food will satisfy your cravings for take out. I got the General Tso's Chicken and hot n sour soup. I posted a picture. First the hot and sour soup. This was tasty. Not as good as Ho Ho to Go on Armenia but it was fine. Good flavor and not too sour or thick. I hate that. Would have liked it a little more "hot". The General's chicken was good. I saw the cook mix the sauce. It was not our of a jar. Again, a little more spice but the flavor was good. They need to add a little more broccoli. 2 pieces is stingy. I will go to this place again since it is close and the food was good. The place was very clean so that is a bonus.

fantastic sandwich. I had the veggie special hoagie - it has grated vegetables, spicy peppers, and very flavorful tofu (and you thought tofu couldn't be flavorful!) Sandwich is on a french roll that is light and not overstuffed. The perfect sandwich! Its a tiny shop, with no seating. You order at the counter and pick up your sandwich as take-out. If you like spicy food, like me, I had them add shiracha to my sandwich but it was definitely not needed for flavor.

I felt terrible walking in at 925pm but I had a craving I had to get tackled. They welcomed me in without problem! Soup- Tom Kha Gai- tasted like the used instant paste for the flavor. Idk but it was too sour, not enough coconut milk for my taste. I love thai for the 3 flavor balance (hot, sour, sweet).

The prices are high for somewhat meager, unexceptional portions. The shrimp dumpling soup had a nice garlic flavour to it, but for $8?? I was expecting much more. They also don't have any eggplant dishes, which is disappointing. It's a pretty place, and it's fine, but not a destination in my book.
This food is delicious. I have been here at least times 5 and everytime, the food has been spot on. I have brought many people, clients there and they loved it everytime. I definitely recommend it.

Amazing food and service!! I was a bit hesitated before the visit since some reviews mentioned their bad experience with the service. They must have improved their service since then, as we were being very well served. The server warmly greeted us at the door, and also checked on us to refill water quite frequently during the dinner. I also really like their interior decor. My boyfriend even thought their price would be at a higher end at the first glance of their decor, but it turned out to be very affordable. The food is amazing and is the best Indian food I've have so far (I don't try Indian food very often so my base might be low...). Defiantly order their Naan - they were freshly baked and great with any curry. We are very satisfied with our visit and will come back to try their lunch buffet some day!

We've always ordered carry-out from Thai Fusion and enjoyed everything so far. Thai Fusion is attached to the Family Video building with the restaurant entrance facing Raceway Road. The restaurant has a small footprint, with 5 4-top tables along one side of the main isle which doesn't provide much privacy, or distance, from foot traffic. Some can tolerate but we're not one of them. Hence, carryout. I highly recommend you phone your order in. One man just waited 40 minutes for his Pad Thai and he's a regular but ticked off tonight. Due to my schedule, I had to order at the counter, and I know better, and like him waited 45 minutes for carryout tonight. Excellent crab rangoon ($4.95) with 6 to an order. If you enjoy crab rangoon you want be disappointed. The Thai Spring Rolls ($1 each) have a really good flavor. The Thai Spring Rolls are deep fried and filled with pork, onions, carrots and clear noodles. We also enjoy the regular Pork Spring Rolls (3 for $4.95). I've had the Drunken Noodles several times which on the menu is #21 Pad Ke Mao ($8.95). The heat gauge here ranges from 1-5 and I asked for a 4 which was perfect for me. The wide noodles are served with eggs, bean sprouts, green beans, onions, carrots, broccoli, mushrooms, bell peppers and basil in a spicy brown gravy/sauce. All of the vegetables were cooked perfectly, tender crisp, with tender slices of chicken. The Fried Rice w/Beef (8.95) was enjoyed by my husband. The rice was light, not overcooked and the beef was tender and a generous portion. Tonight I asked for #39, The Massamun Curry but she was out of again. The only two Curries available were Red or Yellow Curry. I chose the Yellow Chicken Curry, asking for #4 heat, and if you've never had before is simply Chicken Curry in coconut milk, with potatoes and onions. This is prepared as mildly spicy but I requested she kick it up to a 4. I'm sure this didn't get relayed because it had only a HINT of spice. The Yellow Curry was loaded with boiled, white potatoes, just as I like, light on the onions and the chicken was large diced and mostly tender. I thoroughly enjoyed the tender potatoes, a hint of onion with the mild curry and chicken. I will certainly order again. I also order 4 Thai Spring Rolls (for 3 people) which I thought would come with 4 sauces since their 1 per order. Instead, 1 sauce was packed and I was told each additional sauce would be $.40! I was dismissed and she walked away. Regardless of her attitude, the Thai Spring Rolls were quite tasty even lacking the sauce. Two different things tonight, no three. First, was the unenthusiastic girl taking and packing orders who apparently felt 5 spaced out orders was overwhelming. We could hear the Chef asking her to keep on top of the appetizers for each order but she continued to stress how busy it was. She didn't appear rushed with taking or packing the few orders, just reluctant and hurting business. Second, you can no longer upcharge from white rice to fried rice as noted on bottom of menu. I was told I'd have to order a full size Fried Rice ($8.95) with or without meat. That's new!! Third, now you purchase cans of Pepsi instead of fountain soda. The Chef appears to busy preparing great food to totally see the impact at the ordering window. Going forward, I'll avoid the minor annoyances and return to phoning in our order, asking her to repeat order, and enjoy the Chef's hard work at home.

yes i am a fan of Thai Orchid, Blue bell. The service is excellent the waitress are very friendly and in spite of me go there just once or twice a month they remember and even remember what i like. The food is excellent. My work place is not very close or else i would def go there every week... Great Food, Great service ...

To sum it up: Good food. Priced Right. I saw some negative reviews on here and I was shocked. I had to think to myself, well I guess the cook's not in then, because when Jeff is there, the food is incredible. Whenever I'm in town, I make sure to stop at Tangelo's. In an area that seems to have new restaurants every month, I hope to see them there for a long time.
Buffet was terrible. Food was not hot. Chicken was not well cooked. Very less options for vegetarian people. Only good thing here is the ambience.

Ok, My fellow yelpers. I giving them 5 stars based on the reviews. After seeing all the reviews and pics of this place, I'm hoping this place is gonna be a good one. I'll let you all know how it goes when I stop in this week. Im hoping to keep the 5 stars. Crossing my fingers

Definitely one of the best and most reasonably priced restaurants in the area. The waitstaff was incredibly friendly and really gave the restaurant an enjoyable ambiance. The menu had most of your basics on it--I like the vegetarian bun the most. My only issue would be that whenever I ordered a meal with chicken in it, the chicken was dry. I would try a different protein if I were you. Overall, I would highly recommend!

Love this place! It's a favorite for drinks after work. The appetizers are classic with a unique flair (my favorite). Drinks can be very inexpensive if you hit the happy hour. Everything is always displayed with artistic elegance and the service is supreme! Enjoy sitting outside!
Favorite Thai resturant in Tampa. The shrimp pad se ew is amazing

Consistently good Thai food. The ugly strip mall gives way to a pretty well decorated dining room, with details right down to the Thailand sourced bronze flatware. Service is good, it feels like there's not much turnover in their staff. They don't have great glassware, but it's not like the sparkling we brought was any worse for wear. Entrees are great, I love a blazing heat that is cut down just a bit with some cooling coconut milk. The green curry dish hits it right on with some serious intensity and more than enough sauce for immersing the accompanying rice. Bold and spicy shrimp was exactly what my wife was in the mood for with its own kick. We used to come here more frequently a few years ago. It's a bit of a drive from where I currently live, but I'm more than happy to pass a few other Thai restaurants to come here.

Really great addition to the neighborhood. Stopped in one day when i got home too late to cook dinner. Ordering from the kiosk was super efficient, food was tasty (we got Pho and Vermicelli) and packaged well for take out. Staff was even very friendly with my rambunctious, chatty three-year-old. We'll be back. My only complaint is that I wish it was open on weekends, but the cashier told me they will probably expand hours soon. Fingers crossed!

I recently went to this restaurant with a good friend who wanted to have Moroccan food. She had it before in Morocco and wanted to see what this restaurant was like. This place is right off of South street, which made for some difficulty parking. However, we decided on a late dinner at 7:15pm or so, and so got lucky with close parking spots. The service was super duper friendly, although not extremely fast. This did not really bother us as I get the impression that Moroccan culture makes a meal a slow experience in itself. Although we found out later that all our servers and even the owner were not Moroccan. However, do not worry, the chef is (and is not that the most important part? hahaha). We had coupons so we had to order the Fez Feast (7 courses). We started out with a trio of cold salads. They were all very good. There was a cucumber salad, a carrot salad and eggplant concoction. This was served with all you can eat warm bread, which was delicious. The servers bring by the bread in this gigantic woven basket; I felt a bit bad on how often I asked them to bring us bread, but it really was delicious. Then we had a puff pastry with a meat like mixture. I have to admit neither I nor my companion really cared for this. The dish was sprinkled with powdered sugar, and meat and powdered sugar just did not work for me. We both had the olive lemon chicken (I think you had a choice of several different types of chicken, but it was hard to understand the server). The chicken was fairly tender, but the dish overall was too salty for me. The server asked if we would like it mild or spicy and we decided on mild. However, he made the ingenious suggestion of getting the spices on the side so we could at least try it. The server informed me that there was harissa in the spices, which is an ingredient I have been dying to try. The spices ended up being too spicy for me, but I was really glad to have gotten the chance to try the harissa, and the flavor was quite good. The fourth course was a choice between beef kabobs and honey almond lamb. My companion and I ended up split over this choice; she got the kabobs and I got the lamb. She was generous enough to allow me to try her kabob, which consisted of green peppers, onions (I think) and 3 chunks of beef. I did not really think it was anything special. It did not really seem specially seasoned or flavored. The lamb, however, was quite tasty. I was a little disappointed as the lamb was not super tender and the honey taste did not seem really infused into the meat. But overall, it was a pretty tasty dish. I had this same (I believe) dish YEARS ago after finishing my first year of undergraduate education. I remembered it being amazing. Of course that was years ago, and memories get warped throughout the years. So I liked this dish but was a bit disappointed because it did not live up to the memories. The fifth dish was a couscous with roasted vegetables. There is not much to say. It was okay, a bit bland, but okay. I know my companion thought it was a bit too dry. There were a lot of good vegetables in there, however. I am not sure how they counted the last few courses. There was fruit that was brought to us in a basket. A generous 6 pieces; two each of apples, bananas and oranges. It does not sound like much, but considering how much food preceded this, we were full just looking at the fruit. There was also a very, very delicious cup of sweetened mint tea. This was followed by an eclair looking pastry. I found the pastry to be a great light and sweet ending to the meal. My biggest complaint and word of caution is that later at night it seems like a lot of customers come for the hookah. Since I am allergic to smoke and the dining area is one big long room with nowhere to hide, this was a problem. I would say, if you think that the hookah will bother you to come earlier in the evening. When we first got to the restaurant, there was traditional Moroccan sounding music playing, later when the hookah customers came, the music all of a sudden changed to a disco-techy musical selection. I guess they think hookah goes better with disco-techy music. Hahaha

The beef pho here is very good, as is the boba tea. The boba and tea varieties are staggering. There's a large variety of shaved ice flavors, textures and toppings as well. Sometimes it can be a little slow, but service is otherwise good and the food is worth a visit.

Eh, I guess three stars is the right rating for me...middle of the road. I wouldn't say it was "A-OK" - but OK would work. I just popped in for a quick lunch and got green curry with medium heat. The dish came out after just a few minutes, with what seemed to me to be the right amount of rice for the curry dish. I thought the flavor was pretty full, not bland as other reviews have stated. Same with the rice volume - it was sufficient for the amount of curry dish, which also seemed reasonable for the $10.95 price. It's not necessarily inexpensive, but Thai food always seems to run about like this. The medium heat also was just about what I wanted. It kept my nose running, but didn't make me cough; and when I was finished my lips had a slight tingle. The one downside to the food was that there sure were a lot of carrots in it - more than I wanted, and crispier than I like. I wound up picking out the last dozen or so slices. I can't really say there is any atmosphere. I think there were four tables for four, and two tables for two. All in a simple, unadorned setting. This place is really more like a carryout spot with some room for table service. However, the waiter/manager/whatever was attentive, if not very talkative. One kinda gross item, tho, was that he was hacking his head off whenever he was back behind the bar. Oh well, at least he wasn't in the kitchen doing it.

My husband and I decided to try this place out the night we came from NY. For appetizer we had chicken 65 which was not great but alright, I've had better, for entree we ordered the Kerala parotta with egg curry and mutton sukka, both of the dishes were really good. The egg curry had a homemade taste to it-A plus and mutton Sukka was so succulent and the masala in which it was cooked was delicious. Lastly we had the filter coffee which was very authentic. Highly recommend this spot for authentic South Indian taste.

Really cool people, nice clean place and legit good food. I'm a big fan of pho P2 and I've also had their chicken which was good. It's so great to finally have a place in SB to get quality Pho well worth trying.
I've been a few times now. I like their food. So good to have a selection of places now serving manakeesh in the city. This place is pricey but the food is good quality.

Great variety on the menu with plenty of vegetarian & meat dishes. Large portions you can share. The Naan was great and the spice level medium is not shy & has heat. Low spice was a little bland but that maybe because I too lower the heat they lowered the overall seasoning. I'd highly recommend this place!

If only there were more stars to give!! AMAZING food, atmosphere and service! It was as if we were living back in Puerto Rico. We had the sampler; three meats, rice and beans and yucca, we added a fourth meat.

Amazing and all organic! First time stopping in for date night--quality decor and relaxing vibe. Andre gave us a warm welcome and made sure we were well taken care of. Ordered the Caribbean Chicken platter which was three heavenly bowls of Jamaican style chicken (curry, brown stew, and jerk) and a beef patty which was perfect for two to get a taste of everything. Finished it off with a caramel rum cake topped with rum raisin ice cream which was divine. I'd definitely recommend and come back again!
This is a cute thai restaurant in the Brandon. The people who served me were friendly and the food was tasty.

BEST PHO I have found ANYWHERE to date. No doubt about it. I've compared it to all other Vietnamese restaurants in Nashville, and especially to the 2 other Vietnamese restaurants in the vicinity. I have now made it a point to try Pho in every city I go. DC, LA, NV, FL.... Kien Giang has THE MAGICAL PHO that beats them all! No joke. This place is a hidden gem that is out of sight from those driving down Charlotte Avenue. FIND IT. It's Vietnamese food at it's finest. THE FOOD is #1. Whether it's by myself or with friends, I go to Kien Giang OFTEN. Recommendations for Kien Giang to improve to the next level would be a credit card processing machine. I mean seriously come on, this is 2011 and you're a popular restaurant, GET A CREDIT CARD MACHINE! Id like to see more attentive service, also. Id like to get a refill without having to ask. I know the food is awesome, you know it's awesome, so come ask me how it is! Ask me if there is anything else that I need! Those are the only areas for improvement I could suggest for Kien Giang. Closed on Monday? So what, let'em relax. I'm cool with that. GO TO KIEN GIANG. GET THE PHO. Their #1 Pho is really THE #1 PHO!

Always a great time! Small plates are anything but small. Great sized portions for tapas. Favorites are the bacon wrapped olives, baked feta and falafel. Only disappointment was the sangria, which is too sweet for my taste.

Casual Middle Eastern delicious and extremely generous portions! We started with the Hummous & Foule and it was so good and so filling! There were 4 of us and we were all full after the super tasty appetizer! We also ordered the Fattoush Salad which was really good although the deep fried pita on top was a little greasy for me. I might ask for less dressing next time but it was really nicely tossed and everything was cut up into just the right size. I liked the Greek Salad a little better because it had feta cheese and lacked the over fried pita chips. We had the Petra Mixed Grill with babaghanoush and rice and they were good, a nice variety of chicken, beef and lamb. Both the Chicken Schwarma and the Kebab were good. We also enjoyed the lamb special with rice and soup. Although we are all really big eaters, we had a LOT of food to take home! If you are incredibly hungry, this is a great spot to try! The service was friendly and good also though keep in mind this is not fast food. It appears that the food is made with care to order so it takes a little bit of time.

Better Indian food than there should be on the Main Line, Kabob & Grill Indian Cusine offers above average Indian food bordering on greatness. I'll be the first to admit I don't know a whole lot about Indian food, and I don't have it too often due to that ignorance. But I walked out of Kabob & Grill Indian Cuisine very satisfied with what I had and eager to try more of the menu. One of the best parts of Kabob & Grill is the online ordering - I love a well thought out and robust ordering system, either through the website or through the Yelp24 app. It's a small hole-in-the wall with some tables and modest decor. But enough about that let's talk food - my girlfriend and I ordered the Tandoori Chicken ($13), marinated in fresh spices and cooked in clay oven with onion, peppers and basmati Rice, the Chana Massala ($11), chickpeas simmered in a tomato-onion gravy and flavored with spices and basmati rice on the side, and the Mango Lassi ($2), a mango flavored yogurt drink. Some reviewers complained about serving size, but for what we got it was perfect for two people. The tandoori chicken was flavorful but a little dry in some pieces of chicken (overall it was still delicious). The chana massala was my favorite, cooked hot and served with a side of rice, the chickpeas were bursting in flavor in the tomato-onion gravy. The mango lassi is an acquired taste I think - it had the consistency of a milk shake but tasted by a mild yogurt. IT would be perfect for super spicy Indian food (we ordered mild, which had no spice), but I doubt I would order this again. Overall, I really enjoyed Kabob & Grill Indian Cuisine and I'm eager to try every item on the menu. I'll be back and you should go too.

New ownership hasn't meant much, this place is pretty much the same as before. I still come here on a regular basis. Not too long ago they announced that they got new ownership. That meant that the bar opened up again and the worn/torn booths were replaced with new fresh ones, yay! Don't expect a fancy Asian cousin. But do expect to find "traditional Amercan/Asian" dishes served the way you like them. Fulin's is not an expert on the Chinese, Thai or Japanese kitchen, but the mix of dishes are perfect and they do each and every one of them with style. I think we keep coming back because here we know everyone in the company will find something they like, that includes kids! Thai red curry dishes, Sushi roles made right in front of you, extra spicy General Tso's chicken (if you like real spicy, ask for it!)
BEST Gyro in town. Hands down. Breakfast is GREAT as well. Be sure to try the southern style potatoes. BOOM goes the dynamite.

I'm sad and a little surprised by the negative reviews. We came to Tryst for Mother's Day lunch. It was a lovely day, and the outdoor seating might have been nice, but we opted for air conditioning inside. The decor is very nice. Modern and homey at the same time. The cocktail and beer lists were impressive. We tried the Tryst, the Walk on the Pier, and the Pear Lycheetini, and all were tasty and strong. Our table shared the coconut shrimp, which was thankfully not overwhelmingly coconut-y. It was served with an orange ginger marmalade which was too thick and glopped into one piece. The shrimp was good enough to eat alone. For my entree, I had the bleu cheese BLT, which was okay. My husband seemed to like his burger. My mother in law had the grouper sandwich, and she seemed to like it, although the chef put on the remoulade that she specifically asked to be on the side. Service was phenomenal. Brian was very attentive and over-the-top in his helpfulness. When our first appetizer (the charcuterie plate) was sold out, Brian offered us another appetizer on the house. He seemed distraught that the remoulade was served on the grouper sandwich. It was nice to see a waiter who takes his job so seriously. I'd say that the food isn't phenomenal, but it is tasty. And the cocktails were excellent, as was the service. This would be a fun place to come for happy hour.

This hotel has a good ambiance and helpful staff, on top of that they offered a free lassi and sampler of kheer at the end. Who doesn't like freebies :) We ordered chicken kolapuri w/gravy and chicken tandoorti w/ gravy. Chicken kolapuri was soft and juicy. We were highly disappointed with tandoori chicken, it was super dry -like it was cooked for lunch buffet and reheated for dinner order. A tandoor is supposed to be 400-500C(800-900F) and cooks chicken in under 10-15 mins. We informed our server about the problem and dryness with the chicken and after some conversation, we ended the conversation before turning into an argument. Don't order tandoori chicken!!!!
Quick! Easy! And delicious! Definitely worth giving it a try!! There was no wait on a Sunday afternoon which is amazing!

I would have liked to give it another 1/2 star. The gyro I had was HUGE, almost too much meat. Another downfall is not offering a free cup of water....yes they force you to have soda by the can or bottled water. Call me cheap, but I don't drink soda's, and am quit frankly too cheap to pay for something they can get out of their faucet for next to nothing. The gyro was good, but there was so much meat, you didn't taste much else. I love gyro's, and have had them all over STL. Seating is VERY limited, and uncomfortable.

Tried carry out only once on Friday at 7pm. First impression, skimpy on the ingredients and portions.
