She got the coconut soup with shrimp, small dinner portion, overly sweet, almost no heat and consisted of soup and shrimp. No other ingredients. Additionally, the rice which accompanied the soup was...rice mash. As my first go i tried to play it safe with pad thai. This consisted of the lightest coating of finely chopped veggies and herbs. Dime size chicken pieces, so overly cooked they turned to dust when pierced with my fork. It was terrible. Service was .. palatable. .

This is my 2nd time trying Naf Naf. I am a huge Middle Eastern food fan. The first time I came, the line was HUGE. It moved at an "ok" pace, but compared to a Chipotle or another similar establishment, I was not impressed (especially when most people are on the their lunch break from work.) Both times I got the Chicken Salad bowl. It was good. The garlic sauce is delicious. And the side pita is fantastic. What I will say may even prevent me from coming back are 2 things: 1.) The staff: Don't get me wrong, some are vey nice. The guy making the pitas was friendly and worked hard. The guy at the register was HORRIBLE. He was not friendly. He just rang you up and threw the pita in the bag and that was it. He didnt ask, if I wanted a drink or anything else, just $10.89. He also said to a co-worker while I was waiting for my receipt to print "yo, I gotta wiz." The co-worker said - "You have to go to the bathroom?" Mind you, this was just 30-45 mins ago and the restaurant was crowded. I couldn't believe it. There is just a level of unprofessionalism with some of the employees. 2.) HAIR NETS: Several of the women did not have their hair pulled back and were reaching over the food area with their hair just ready to fall into the food. I think that it should be required that their hair is either pulled back AND OR in a hair net. That is very unsanitary. So, all in all, the food is good and some of the staff is good but based on today's experience I think I'll try somewhere else next time.

Ok guys! I went back and had the food this time. As you can see it's definitely a 5-star establishment. The pho is amazing very similar to some of my other 5star reviews. Great portion sizes and as always the staff and environment was all great. They have an amazing dessert menu and a huge food menu as well. Come here you will not regret it.

AMAZING FOOD!! the comments that are expressed here are far from the truth. The ambience was on point, the staff was SUPER helpful and courteous. The food was freshly made and I was just overall pleased.

Went last week after I read the reviews on yelp. I ordered the spring rolls and red curry. The portions were very large and probably enough for two people. The service was also very fast so if you want appetizers you may want to delay your entree order a bit. All in all, a very good little Thai place.

Simply put, its great food, speedy service, reasonably priced, and glad I stopped in! The gyro was huge and very tasty. The falafel plate was more than I could eat (after the gyro)! I'm visiting for work but will recommend to others.

Excellent food, both sushi and Thai. They're able to make things vegan for me too. Prices are reasonable as well. The sweet potato roll is amazing. I can't wait to go back. Everyone that works there were very friendly and welcoming.
I love their sandwiches, I normally get the #1 and their pho is really good. The place is small, so if you can avoid the lunch hour rush I recommend it.
This is the only Thai resturant in Carpinteria. The Phai Thai falls short from good. The curries are watered down. It is very unimpressive. I'd rather drive out of Carpinteria for a flavorful meal.

This is down-home, good Pho. Do not expect fancy decor or warm service. Do expect a great bowl of Pho that pleases on every level. Better broth than Miss Saigon. The noodles are way better than Vn & Pho Deli. The Banh Mi are really good, too, and ridiculously cheap.

pho at this place tastes like it was really cooked in a pot on the stovetop rather than in the microwave....if you like lots of bean sprouts in your pho like i do, you may have to ask for extras when you place your order (most pho shops don't charge extra and not knowing the amount of sprouts i'd get at this place, i didn't ask for extras)... seasonings in their entrees are strong enough for this Asian w/an aversion for bland and mild flavored foods... impressive menu selection at this place...w/an Asian grocery store next door, you can get your shopping done while waiting on your food...and i suppose having a grocery store next door allows this restaurant to offer such a diverse selection of dishes... family friendly atmosphere... if you love the 3 bean dessert like i do, this is one of the few places in Indy i've found to have it....not as great as what i'm used to back in the heartland... overall, an excellent place to fill up on reasonably priced (well, for being in Indy anyway) and tasty, authentic Asian cuisine...
Erawan has consistently great food and friendly stuff. I think there're price are good too.Oh god I'm getting hungry again can't wait to go back.

We drove from Tampa on vacation as our friends parents know Katherine (Karim's wife). They are both amazing and the food was amazing. I had never had Moroccan food before so was a little weary on the flavors originally. We started with the mussels and soft shell crab, and then got the lamb tagine and lamb kabobs. This was one of those meals where everything was so good that you didn't think the next thing could top it, but it did. Everything from the salad dressing was insanely good. Go and try this place even if you're not sure if you'll like the flavors. They have seafood, pasta, chicken etc. there is definitely something for everyone. Also, you are only steps to the beach!

I'm really surprised at the low reviews for this place. In my opinion, it offers the best valued Ethiopian food in the Philly area, a place where competition is steep. The food here is a good $2 or so per item cheaper than in most restaurants, and the service I have found is consistently better than average. The quality of the food does not at all suffer from the lower price--instead, you just give up the fancy atmosphere, and that's cool with me. This place is a little divey, in a 70's cafeteria sort of way. There's an eating area on one side, seat yourself, and a bar on the other. The bar is dark and the seating area is brighter, but not exactly the most brightly lit place. But I like it. There's a positive vibe in here. They're often playing energetic hip-hop music. It's the sort of place that I feel very comfortable, and I'm not quite sure why. But I always like the food, especially the vegetarian food. I especially like the Foul and Vegetarian platter here. Food is cheap, portions are good, quality is consistently good, service is consistently good. Seriously, what is there to not like about this place? The only thing I can imagine is if you're looking for something fancy...which I almost never am. Epic win!

Amazing food. Don't be intimidated by the foreign names, the food is delicious. The owner is super friendly and is enthusiastic about discussing what goes into his food. The ingredients are the freshest and some of the best quality "street" food. It's so easy to grab and go at this place.

Our 1st dining experience here, it was the season opener LSU vs BYU game. Upon entering, we were not greeted and waited. Clearly one employee was talking to the table closest to the door, but still did not acknowledge us or say to have a seat anywhere we wanted. After sitting, we waited to be greeted again. This time, same server passed and saw us and kept walking. I gave it another few minutes and almost placed our order at the to-go counter, but we were then taken care of by the 2nd server. The food was good. I would return to give it another try ONLY because it was game day....but don't count on the service folks!

I've been frequenting Zen Yai at lunch for the last year. It's still the best Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara. The staff are all very friendly and attentive, and don't seem to mind when splitting the bill with colleagues on our lunch break. One thing that I have noticed is that the food seems to be better at lunch time than it does in the evening. I've taken the fiance here for dinner on several occasions and it just never seems to be as good as lunch. Thai iced tea and Pad Thai is my go-to. Their soups are also very good.

One of my favorite Thai restaurants. And it happens to be close to home. How convenient! Great for dining in or carrying out. Delicious! I love the Crab Delight, all of the fried rice dishes, and Phad Thai. Another great dish that few people stick around for: the fried ice cream. Covered in strawberries and SO good! I've had a lot of friends say that Thai House was better than the Thai restaurants in the city. I have to agree!

I absolutely loved this place. They had live jazz music and the owner was our waitress. You won't find that at Applebees. We let her pick out our food selections and everything was amazing. There were whole jalapenos in some of the dishes and I love spice so I was a happy camper. The dishes are served family style so you can try multiple menu items which was awesome because they were all delicious. Great atmosphere. Great service. Great food.

First experience with Ethiopian cuisine was in D.C., the food was bursting with flavor, my tastebuds were dancing to a symphony of herbs and spices that till this day I am still searching for. This place not so much, it looks like Ethiopian food but, one taste of it and you'll right away that their spice rack is limited to salt and pepper . The place is a bit dingy, and the wait staff clueless. This place makes me sad : (

Ok for lunch. Lots of customization available with making a bowl or pita sandwich. I went with the veggie bowl, exactly how it came. I felt like the bowl seemed so large compared to the food that was placed in it, but I guess that could be because the hummus and baba ganoush which were two of the items seemed smeared on the sides of the bowl. I was confused if pita came with my meal because when they ask during ordering I said no thank you but then the cashier said he threw in two extra pitas. So after talking to someone else they said oh they always give pita with meals....I'm still confused. I thought it was good food but it didn't excited me and make me want to rush back to try more. I do love using naf as a noun, verb, adjective, etc. As I was walking in I said I'm ready to get my naf on thinking that I made it up and then of course right over the menu it says get your naf on. Well, great minds think alike.

There is a bit of a wait but it is well worth it. I got my usual Cap'n Crunch Tilapia Burrito. It's been a long time since I had it and it still tastes the same. It can be a bit messy to eat- especially towards the end. I always end up with a gloop of sauce as my last bite.

Coming from Chicago, we are really lucky to have this place nearby. The servers are friendly and always dressed well. The restaurant is very clean and has a blend of the usual silver, gold and crystal, it has a modern touch with some fresh flowers and did I say it was clean? The food is fresh and plentiful. We usually get vegetable samosas, mutter paneer and biryani (I like the lamb, but we also have had goat.) Take out or dine-in, it's all good.

I had never had Indonesian food before, but was super impressed. It is a mixture of Chinese and Thai flavors, but also unique in many ways. It's really cheap (cash only, byob) and a bit of a hole in the wall, but totally worth the trip. If you are adventurous, just ask them to recommend some dishes and you'll leave happy!

Four words. CAPTAIN CRUNCH TILAPIA BURRITO. I was a little skeptical at first, but it lived up to every raving review. The staff is really friendly, and they are willing to correct the order if there is a mistake (despite how busy they are). The line is usually pretty long, but it moves relatively fast, and it's totally worth it!
Quick and tasty A little dirty tho. I wouldn't want to see the kitchen based on the dining room appearance

This is a fantastic place for Thai food in Edmonton. We are so glad we found it! It is a very nondescript restaurant on 124 street, but don't let that fool you. The interior is nothing fancy, but the food is so darn good. "E" is an expert when it comes to Pad Thai. She has been lucky to eat it on many continents and places this particular version near the top of her list. "D" had fried chicken, which was wonderful. It was very moist, cooked just right, and the portion was very large. I could not eat it all, and my plate cleaner "E" could not finish it off! The prices were very fair. The food is very well presented and prepared, as well as being fresh. Service was excellent. It was not packed, but there was a fairly steady stream of people coming in to dine, leaving, and being replaced with some new customers. We will certainly be back. We have eaten at a lot of Thai places in Edmonton and this one has to be the best to date.

I came in late at night so there was no wait. I went with the Duck and Pineapple curry. This came out pretty quickly and was delicious. There was a bit of a spicy burn that warmed me right up, but not too much that I couldn't handle it. The duck meat was a little on the dry side, but still pretty tender with no bones in it. The curry was flavored perfectly and I wish I had more rice to soak it in and then more curry to soak that additional rice in. It was sweet and spicy and delicious.
amazing menu, fast service, cheerful staff...a definite must if you find yourself in Mullica Hill

A little place just a few steps away from Nodding Head and Oyster House, I walked by at least a handful of times before realizing the entrance, you go down a flight of stairs, pass the little girl doing her homework on the right, the kitchen on the left, then back up a flight of stairs to get seated. There were another flight of stairs going down on the right, and a set of stairs on both sides going up, the left side was roped off, on the right the stairs led to a wall, I can't help but wonder what this building was originally intended, and after so many years came up with the current layout, but I love these old buildings. There were a few solo diners like me at the time so I didn't feel uncomfortable, the waitress was pleasant and attentive, she quickly took my order and soon returned with some thin bread and hummus. Soon the cook came up from below with a few trays and buckets, and proceeded to cook my kabob my the grill, he was artfully putting the side dishes on the plates while keeping watch on the kabob, constantly darting back and forth to rotate the kabobs. At last my lamb kabob was in front of me, the veggie cooked on the skewer were equally delicious, I devoured everything eagerly, and before long I was ordering desert, I went with sherry akh, which she explained was vanilla ice cream with rose water. She went down the stairs and got a small empty dish from behind the front counter, came back up the stairs, past my table and went up the stairs to the right, voila, there was a hidden door that led to a small room, she went in and returned a few seconds later with my ice cream, was it homemade or did it come from a box, I couldn't tell, the ice cream was okay, but after watching her effort getting it, I made sure I finished all of it. The food was good, service was nice, and the price was right, this place didn't disappoint.

With a buffet during the afternoon hours India sizzling is a great place to go for something new and tasty. They serve fresh naan and the food is very flavorful. . Some Indian restaurants have multiple items with very similar tastes due to the spices used. India sizzling dishes are delightfully different in taste due th the variety of spices. A thumbs up!
Still the best gyro in the city and they give you a ridiculous amount of gyro meat. Come hungry

I've heard good things about Zorba's, so I thought I'd give it a try. I placed a delivery order, I live just a few blocks away. Delivery was surprisingly fast, and the food was excellent! I chose the Pork Souvlaki, hearty portions, and the sides were delicious as well. I look forward to eating at the restaurant!

My favorite Thai food in all of Nashville. I'd often get take out rather than eat in the restaurant. Their food can take awhile to prepare so call with ample time. Check out the mini golf course and go karts next door while you wait. When I said make it Thai hot, they'd never disappoint. Fantastic curry!
Tried this place for the first time today. The restaurant was very clean and the food was good but the portions are pretty small for the price.

I've only been here once so I can't write much but it was a nice change to the Chinese noddle soups I am so used to. [Pagoda anyone?] The waiter was super friendly and they even made me a bowl with tofu, which I didn't notice on the menu. Free tea and two bowls of Pho cost us only eleven dollars or so and we were full 'till the next day. It's a fun place with a mixed environment of locals and college students looking for a cheap meal. Can't wait to go back so I can write more. ________________________________________________ Update: So after a day of feeling not-so-well we headed to Pho Ha on our way home from work for something filling and that would settle my stomach. I had the intention of ordering some soup but found the rice noodle bowls more appealing to my senses. I surprised myself by ordering meat for a change and I was in no way disappointed. The spring roll appetizer with shrimp and mint was even more of a delight, especially paired with my fresh limeade soda from the juice bar. Divine! There's nothing like a homemade soda on a hot afternoon. The portions as usual were enormous for my tiny stomach so I would up taking a plate home for the evening, a plate I wound up sharing with our dog and one of our kittens who kept ogling the tender strips of pork. No worries, though, there was plenty to go around!
Great food. Will make as spicy as you can imagine, but watch what you ask for. Very pricey.

This was pretty mediocre Thai food in my opinion. I was excited to try it out because the decor is so fun - there were these giant Thai bench type things that were super fun and made me feel like I was back in Bangkok. I got the duck yellow curry and was excited to try it. It came with some egg rolls and other kind of weird, quasi-Chinese stuff on the side. Eggrolls and other side dishes I couldn't remember were ok. Honestly, there was like no meat in the curry. It was all skin and duck fat. Really don't like duck fat or any other kind of fat so that made me a little bit of a sad panda. Customer service was decent - the main lad was super nice and made me want to like the restaurant more. Just couldn't get past all of that duck fat. My friend got the tofu pad thai. I had a bite and it was actually pretty good. Maybe I just ordered the wrong thing.
Wasn't impressed with the pick up and the fact charge is different from the yelp menu and no one wanted to compensate ... Not very welcoming/ service was dismissing ...Hoping the food is great

Great food, great service, great all around! When we arrived they were in the middle of closing up for the night, but Hasan graciously stayed open a bit longer so we could put our orders in. Since I was overwhelmed with the selection, Hasan put together a delicious beginners meal. The rose lassi was A+, and the veggie samosa chaat was so so good. I will definitely make the trip back!

Jasmine Rice has the perfect ambiance for a small byob - its tucked in the heart of center city, but as soon as you walk inside you feel like you are visiting a friend. I have been eating here for the past 3 years and the food has never been disappointing. My favorites are the lemongrass soup, pad thai and all of the curries. Writing this review makes me want to go back tonight!

Based on the reviews we read we went for dinner. We ate there. The gentleman who waited on us was very nice, and honestly the food was good...BUT...the place is filthy dirty. The floors, bathroom, glass where you pick up your food, the doors to the beverage coolers, the front entrance. So it really makes me wonder how clean is the cooking area!!! C'mon dude we all clearly like the food but clean the place up!

I live right by Doan's so it is a regular of ours. They have the best fried rice I have ever had. It is fluffy, sweet, salty, and just delicious. While they don't have the greatest service, they do put a lot of effort into their food.

This location on our first visit was attentive, pleasant and accommodating--as though the place had just opened even though it was a half-hour 'til close. I was surprised that they didn't turn us away and cooked our orders up hot and fresh quickly! My wife had the Fulin special Lo mein and I had the General Tso's Chicken. Both very tasty and eventful to my palette throughout. Chase was out server and conscious of anticipating where he could provide us anything we may have been lacking and offered alternatives where applicable. And then after all that, they reassured us we didn't have to rush out meals. In the was of Chinese cuisine Fulin's is generally pricey but the stellar service and focus from staff make this location stand out to us, thus far. Definitely stop in and see for yourselves.

Arrived just 20 minutes before closing time but We were greeted very warmly . We chose to place an order to go and everything was made fresh and quick. Got back to our hotel room and enjoyed the food . Taste was great home cooked style Thai food. Great people. Definitely want to go back again if visiting Tampa next time.
Eaten there a couple of times now. Haven't had any better Thai here in Nashville. Good stuff!

This is my second time here. They are open at the Christmas Day night. Not too busy compared to many other restaurant open at that day. The interior of this place is beautifully set up. I like their decorations. We were sit immediately on second small room. Including us is about three tables of customers. We have ordered Black pepper basil crispy duck and Spicy noodle with squid. Food delivery is on time. The black pepper basil squid is average. The spicy noodle seem like not cook in high heat because I cannot taste the burn oil. Both dish is actually made for American Thai flavor. The local may like it but I am looking for good Thai which is average. The service is not measured up. We were not able to get attention of our waitress. But the other two tables was able grab her attention. Some how we got ignored. The three stars for the food and the service we have experience.

This place is just OK. I grew up in Orlando (2nd largest Vietnamese population in the US) so I am a bit spoiled when it comes to pho. The broth was a little fattier (saw oil on the surface) meaning that it was not skimmed very well. It was also a bit salty. The bean sprouts provided were old and looked like they were going bad. I probably won't be coming back here if I have a choice.

Came here for a birthday dinner. Ambience and decor was really nice. We had a long table in the back. Waiters were attentive and friendly, food and drinks were good. We loved our appetizers(calamari, won tons, popcorn, etc) and drinks. Just about everyone at the table enjoyed their meal. I got the skirt steak which was a little over cooked and the sauce on the steak wasn't great but that didn't negatively affect my experience. Someone got the chicken sandwich which they loved! Looking forward to going back soon.

Where to begin? This barely got a second star. Oily pho broth, low-quality meat (tendon would best be classified as scrap), surly service, stingy sides, and small bowls (though cheap). VN deli is too close, too good, and too reliable to ever try this train wreck again.

Just had dinner here, and we had a great meal. The place was empty when we came in, and food arrived very quickly. We had chicken biryani and Kerala Pepper Chicken, medium heat both. Medium here is plenty for American palates if you are not a pepper-head. Portions were generous, the rice was moist, and both dishes were full of flavor. Keep an eye out for whole spices, as an unexpected cardamom pod can be an intense bite! We also had the Peshawar naan, which was tender and flavorful. We're happy to have a good Indian place in the neighborhood, and we look forward to coming back.

Amazing Indian food! Reasonably price, well made Indian food in a very casual atmosphere that I wish was closer to the city. My friend introduced it to me for lunch once. We loved everything we had-- dahi aloo puri, vegetable biriyani and spinach masala dosa-- and were stuffed. I am definitely looking forward to going back for more. It was also encouraging to see a lot of Indian families filling the restaurant. Update: I've been going here for well over a year and have never been disappointed. I usually get one of the biryanis. All the appetizers are great. Recently, I have also had the palek paneer, chicken marsala and one of their curries, all of which were wonderful.

Best Thai food in stl!!! Delicious food, great service, big portions! We had several types of curry-yellow was amazing and not spicy. The pad see ew was also to die for. Ask about spice level because some dishes have a lot of heat!

As far as Ethiopian cuisine goes this is the best I've had. It blows away most places in DC and NYC. Only exception is in DC U St. Service is a little slow but that is normal for the type of restaurant.

Have to agree with some of the other reviews here regarding the staff. The women preparing my sandwich was literally eating a French fry when making my order. She was also eating when I left as well. Overall the restaurant just seemed unkept. I also think it is misleading that the signage advertises the food as healthy. The sauce they add on the sandwiches is loaded with calories.

Authentic African food, well prepared and well presented. Jerk wings as appetizer were great. Oxtail stew is a very good choice, spicy but not unbearable. Chicken kabobs have nice char flavor complemented by the African spice. Ginger drink is flavorful but very strong. All in all, highly recommended.

This isn't even the best Indian food on the Main Line, and it is certainly below standard for the Philly area. I ordered Mattar Paneer and Gulab Jamun. The basmati rice was mushy, wet, and overcooked. The sauce for the Mattar Paneer was bland, lacking any spice. The Gulab Jamun was all right, but a bit too heavy on the cardamom. Cardamom overwhelmed all the other flavors. I expected better, especially for the price.

Went to the grand opening and I was blown away. Great food! Great service! What more can you ask for? The chef/owner truly has created something special. The menu had so many choices that i couldn't decide at first. However, I ended up getting the sausage and broccoli rabe app and the swordfish. Both were out of this world. Take the drive to Collingswood and get a great meal from chef Joey, you will not be disappointed!

Came here for Friday dinner. Atmosphere is cozy and appealing. Service was good, with who I presume to be the owner checking in on us as well. Food was good but nothing exceptional. Will have to try again and order something different to see if it lives up to the hype.

I've never written a Yelp review before, but I now feel inclined to share with others that I ate it for dinner last night and got terrible food poisoning. Haven't been this sick since I traveled to India! I will not be going back.

Our family loves Desi Village. When my wife and I were younger we wanted to find a restaurant the knew our names. Who would have thought it would be an Indian restaurant. Now my children also feel like this is "our" restaurant. The staff is wonderful, the food is very good. We often let the staff surprise us and are never disappointed. I highly recommend Desi Village if you are near King of Prussia.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Unbelievably good! Try the very reasonable lunch buffet ($9.99) and then come back to splurge on dinner. Very good gluten free options including naan. And don't miss the cherry cider on tap. It pairs perfectly with the spicier dishes!

Great Thai spot, chef is actually from Thailand and cooks at a spice level like you were in Thailand. Recommend getting mild or medium and then going up as you can handle it. High quality Thai food and best in Brandon!
This is definitely the best pho I've had in Tampa, though it is extremely hard to find (no thanks to the incorrect address on yelp). They have a pretty decent menu.

Walking into Ariana feels like being invited into your extremely cool friend's living room. Beautifully ornate rugs, padded chairs, colorful wall hangings, sweet shisha smoke hanging in the air, delicious smells wafting from the kitchen, and a hip, diverse crowd in deep states of chillness and relaxation. It is an unpretentious, thoroughly warm and welcoming oasis from the madness of Old City. I had two great friends visiting me in Philly for a weekend. After a nice day of walking around the city and checking out the Mütter Museum, we decided to take a breather with a movie at the Ritz and then have a late dinner. Around 6:45, I called Ariana to ask if they took reservations. They did! And yes, they could seat the three of us at 9pm on a Saturday. Score! It was an easy walk from Ritz at the Bourse. We walked in and were welcomed by a lovely, smiling woman who, it turned out, would also be our waitress for the evening. Our table was spacious and comfortable (those padded, upholstered chairs!) and we could tell right away this would be a great place to while away the evening. One of my friends had the pulao with chicken, which turned out to be this intoxicating blend of sweet, acidic, proteiny and savory. It was excellent. My other friend had a chicken kabob and was very happy with that. I had a dish of split-pea daal topped with lamb stew. It was incredible, and the quality of the lamb was top-notch. Oh, I almost forget that we also split several appetizers, different varieties of dumplings, and those were extremely good, as well. My favorite was filled with fresh chives. Afterwards, we smoked a hookah. The hookah pipes are attractive and clean, and there was a ton of shisha in there. We ordered a second coal but we finally had to end up leaving unsmoked shisha because we were all starting to feel a little light-headed! The shisha was good-quality and delicious. I should also say that the air had the light smell of sweet smoke, just enough to be atmospheric and pleasant, but Ariana's must have a very good ventilation system because even with a hookah on practically every table, it was never oppressively smoky or remotely close. The crowd was great. It was diverse--mostly Black and Brown with a few White people--and very chill and friendly. Everyone was happy and having a good time. Ariana is BYOB, so some people brought wine. One table made the power move of bringing a bottle of Jameson along! When we finally left, our waitress smiled broadly and wished us a good night and told us to come back some time. The service was friendly and warm, from beginning to end. The next day, my friends were still raving about Ariana, so this is definitely a keeper for entertaining out-of-town guests. But for us Philly folks, there is no reason not to make Ariana a regular stop. It is an excellent alternative to some of the more pretentious/fratty places in Old City and more to the point, a fantastic establishment in its own right.
False advertising, they DO NOT DELIVER. As far as the food goes, will have to wait to write a new review.

AUTHENTIC PHO in NOLA!! The restaurant is very clean and service is fast and friendly. Pho Orchid combination was a little bit of everything. Broth was amazing and was a great cure for the morning after. Pork summer rolls & duck buns(?)- amazing!!! Can't forget the Vietnamese iced coffee! Prices were reasonable! Make sure to get a large since the small looks kid size.

My favorite local spot. The menu always has some new specials with local ingredients. Service is excellent. The homemade chips are delicious. The Owner/Chef is creative in utilizing the local ingredients. Looking forward to my next visit!
Go to for Thai in south tampa, but be prepared to wait. Definitely best to call ahead and add 10 mins to however long they say. Love everything on menu! Beware- closed Monday's and now also Tuesdays?

It's shocking to me to read the bad reviews of Shere-E-Punjab, because every time I've been here it's been a great experience with good service and delicious food. I've been here twice for the lunch buffet, which is a great deal. Last Sunday I went here for dinner with my family. The one slightly annoying element of our visit was that we had called the night before to make reservations, but when we showed, the restaurant was unaware of them and had no tables set up to fit 7 people (other reviewers have mentioned the small size of the restaurant). It ended up working out though because my parents were late, and by the time they arrived a table had cleared. We got the veggie samosas as an appetizer (very spicy! yummmm) and then each got different dishes to make our own kind of buffet by passing stuff around. Vegetarian dishes ordered: palak paneer, dum aloo, and navrattan korma (very buttery, very good!). Meat dishes ordered: lamb vindaloo, lamb korma, chicken makhani, and malai kabab. All of these were delicious except for the malai kabab, which was a bit dry. We also got the mixed bread basket, which had plain naan, garlic naan, onion kulcha, and tandoori roti. Every time I've been to Shere-E-Punjab the naan has been very fresh, and brushed with a little ghee. When you go for lunch they bring it to your table instead of having it on the buffet, which is a nice touch. Overall, I'd recommend Shere-E-Punjab to anyone, and it's one of my top dining choices in Media.

Have been a fan of Thai food for a while. This place, although small in seating ares, has wonderful food. Wait staff has been pleasant and prices are respectable. I am a bit of a wuss on spicy food, so they have various levels. From no spicy, my favorite, to way spicy. Big fan of their Pad Thai. Sauce, while not runny like some places, is tasty and thick enough to be noticeable without concealing. Atmosphere is nice, as there was some attention put into the decor. Recommend this place

CLOSED - Was craving this for lunch today, as I'm in town. http://www.stlmag.com/Blogs/Relish/June-2012/Long-Faces-Land-of-Smile-Closing-June-24/ "Nanthavong had been been leasing the space at 9641 Olive from landlord Harman Moseley on a month-to-month basis. Moseley has apparently found a tenant (a Subway sandwich shop, we're told) ) that's willing to sign a long term lease. Efforts to reach Moseley today were unsuccessful." I think Harman Moseley is a dick.

We had dinner last evening 1- excellent service( Tom the server) 2- the food was fresh , delicious & amazing in tase 3- to see all employees working to make every guest feel special was such a warm feeling, the Resturant is small but very carrying for @ guest , We can not wait & return

As authentic as you can find in philly jamaican fare. This is not for the faint of heart the jerk here is serious spice. No liquor license but that is ok there are plenty of great places to drink on south street. I have had the whole menu i have never been disappointed.
So yummy! They were also very patient with me as it was my first time to an Indian restaurant! The garlic naan...

The atmosphere here is kind of dark and romantic, so don't bring someone here when trying to keep them in the friend zone. Just saying. Overall: love the curry, pad thai is not great. Hate that they only take cash. Not my favorite Thai in the world, but I've yet to a find a favorite Thai place in Philly.

I'm not the biggest fan of Ethiopian food, but we went there for a family birthday and the food was delicious. She works awfully hard because she is the only one their, but the service was fairly quick and everyone really enjoyed it. Would go again.

I have been eating at Thai Place for at least 8 years now, and I can say with 100% certainty that I have never had a disappointing dish. Everyone I've recommended this place to has had the same thing to say about it: incredible food. I've had many different entres, including various curries, drunken noodles, pad thai, me grob (sp?), etc. And everything is extremely flavorful and fresh. I hate going to thai joints where you know they're using a bag of frozen veggies in their stuff. The family who owns Thai Place is super friendly. To the reviewers who gave it any less than 5 stars... Seriously? I'm sure if I read your other yelp reviews, you'd have the same snooty, uppity remarks about every other restaurant you go to. Your self-important, condescending attituds are getting a little over-the-top.

Wir haben hier wirklich gut gegessen! Leider war der papayasalat alle :-( bedienung war okey! Das essen kam sehr rasch! War wirklich alles gut! Ginge hier wieder essen! Es ist angenehm nicht kalt nicht laut! Super!

The family and I enjoyed our dinner at Pan d'Olive very much. I called a few hours early to make reservations, however it was probably not necessary since the place was 3/4 empty when we got out there at 7:30. The ambiance was great though, and the servers attentive and willing to accomodate our food modification requests. We are not picky eaters by any means but it is always nice when restaurants go out of their way to ensure that even the slightest customer's desires are fulfilled! They serve a basket of sliced bread and olive oil and cheese as a starter. We ordered 2 appetizers: hummus and calamari. Entrees were flatbread napoleotana, veal marsala and lobster ravioli. As dessert we had the baklava, new to us but we enjoyed it very much. Everything was super delectable, however my favorite thing was the hummus and pita bread. I don't know what magic ingredients they put in that hummus but it was astonishing!! Um um um. The happy hour at Pan d'Olive sounds pretty amazing, so I will be checking that out soon!

Came here on a Saturday night for dinner with my boyfriend. We were greeted and seated automatically and our server came right away. Since it was our first time there she had no problem giving us a few minutes to look over the menu. I ordered a mojito to start and I have to say it was absolutely delicious. My boyfriend and I ordered guacamole to share and it was pretty good, tasted freshly made. Our entrees were excellent and the service was great. Such a great place to get food and relax. Everyone there was so friendly and the prices aren't bad. I will definitely recommend this place and will come back.

Absolutely delicious. I was surprised at the quality and quantity of a $10 meal. I'm sure if you sized up to a large two people could easily share. I had jerk chicken, rice/bean and cabbage every item was delicious

Second time having traditional Ethiopian. Abyssinia was unique in a few ways. First of all, the whole place looks like a normal ethnic restaurant when you walk in, but the Ethiopian guy in our group requested to sit under the indoor porch area with traditional animal skin chairs and woven straw tables. He said it was similar to his style of eating at home. Secondly, the food. Now I love meat, and we made sure to get plenty of awassi tips, lamb, and chicken dishes, but the lentils...oh my, that was my favorite dish between the TA1 sampler, awassi tips, and a spicy chicken dish. They served everything on a large injera bread with rolled up injera to scoop with. Nothing like eating with your fingers :) Finally, the coffee ceremony at the end was not only a cultural experience, but delicious and plentiful. Our waitress brought out the green coffee beans she was roasting in order for us to smell the coffee we'd be drinking soon. She then ground the beans and brewed the coffee in a clay pitcher which she served the coffee from into small cups. Since it was a slow evening, she even sat down an chatted with us for a while. Great food, great atmosphere, great service. Nothing short of excellent at Abyssinia.
The ambiance is ok. The place being connected to hotel is different I have had better the food was ok buffet was 10.95

The owners (Paul and Leah) have been doing such and excellent job with their Thai jewel in Carpinteria. From the cozy interior to the Thai huts outside. When you stop by for lunch their special combinations are a great value. I don't believe you can go wrong which ever items you pick. I love the pra-rahm and the seafood option for any of their dishes is very nice and abundant. And for those with a sweet tooth. The mango sticky rice is THE best dessert options (when in season of course!)

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: When I want quick Indian food to-go, I think of St. Louis Halal Meat. I was craving some Indian, but didn't want to dine-in at the 12th floor of a hotel or pay an arm and a leg. Google, a friend to us all, informed me that only a couple of miles away I could find St. Louis Halal Meat on Page Ave. A halal butcher shop that also has a limited menu. I actually passed it the first time I went - it is tucked back off the street in a nondescript strip mall near a license bureau. I ordered and the friendly man on the phone described the few select offerings. After that first order, I was hooked! Fresh, fresh, fresh, and absolutely delicious! The portions are heaping, and the spices are exquisite. Chicken biryani - Perfectly tender seasoned basmati rice with marinated spicy chicken. Delectable Indian flavorings, and comes with a delicious yogurt sauce to quell the heat. My #1 favorite from here. Chicken curry - Delicious traditional curry flavored sauce with chicken and rice. Not too spicy, and no veggies like carrots or potatoes. Very good. Naan - Once when I called in I asked if they had garlic naan, and the guy said it wasn't on the menu but that he could make it, no problem. What I got was their usual flaky, chewy flat bread - tasty as always - with the heavenly scent and just the right flavor of garlic. Not overpowering nor barely noticeable. Ask nicely and you should be able to try. :)

We went to Mint about 6:15 on a Wednesday and it was packed. Soon discovered why, the food is very good. Started off with shrimp avocado spring rolls, mint special rolls,and pork belly tacos. All 3 were very good , my favorite were the pork belly tacos. the moon crepe was very good as was the grilled shrimp and the Mint combo pho. The pho had lots of meat and the broth was very good. A nice dining experience and the restaurant gets very loud when its full. Service was good and our server did a great job even though the restaurant was full. Value was good as well. Glad to see all the wonderful dining options on Freret Street.
First time ever here and hands down the best fish tacos ever! Highly recommend this place. Prices are very reasonable.

I've ate here and ordered take out multiple times, each experience has been great. The owner and staff are extremely welcoming and pleasant. The food is reasonable priced and delicious. I tried the ginger scallion and veggie dumplings last night, they were delightful. I ordered my standard Pad Kee Mao (Broad rice noodles stir fried in Thai basil chili paste with onions, red bell peppers and tomatoes) and added chicken with extra vegetables. Spicy food and I tend to disagree, and I'm known for ordering "wimpy sauce wings" but this dish had the perfect kick to it that even I could handle.

I can see why this restaurant is in the top 50 of new restaurants in America. The food was spot on and our server Laura was great. She knew about the various dishes on the menu and could also pronounce each dish correctly. The decor and atmosphere is also pristine. I hope to come back before the season changes to enjoy their open air space.

I decided to try this Thai place for the first time a few weeks ago. I ordered Pad Thai very mild because I have a sensitive pallet. I ordered it a "1" on a scale of 1-10 and it was burning a hole through my mouth. So I don't know if they accidentally put too much in there or what, but I couldn't barely eat it. I know this can happen at most Thai places, so I gave them a second chance and ordered it again, the same way. This time it was mild, but bland. Almost no flavor. Other thai restaurants I eat at still have a very flavorful Pad Thai even at mild, so I was disappointed that this place didn't work out for me. It's closer to my house than my normal place and would've been nice! On a better note: their fried veggie spring rolls are amazing. So they will be seeing me for those. But if you have to have mild dishes and like Pad Thai, this place isn't for you.
Never had a bad meal at Polo Tropical..Everything is always fresh. Wish they would bring back the chicken fajitas as they were my favorite...

I heart this place. They're really friendly, the food is great, it's simple and uncomplicated and price to portion ratio is extremely fair. They take credit cards, you could byob it, order a smoothie or just do takeout. I realize these things individually aren't that impressive, but really think about how many places you know that have all of these attributes? I've had their garlic chicken and falafel platter each time I've been there (sharing of course). I'll eventually get the gyro and shwarma but the garlicky flavors beckon me each time.

If you haven't tried Ethiopian food, please try the vegetarian (vegan) combo. It is extremely tasty and healthy, not overly oily or salty. I find that Ethiopian food is almost the healthier alternative to Indian food, they use similar spices and make similar styled dishes. Healthy, unreasonably tasty, and made by good people. Great place I would eat here more often but the veggie combo is a bit expensive, I wish they had a smaller veggie combo plate for cheaper
Super fresh and clean Vietnamese food. Service was great and interior was modern and clean. Would definitely visit here again.

The jerk chicken was fabulous. The other food items where good, but you come here for the jerk. They have their own version of their jerk seasoning, which is a nice change. Service and seating is rudimentary (just like Jamaica), but you're not there for the seating.
The Nasi Lemak Ayam Goreng "Coconut rice with fried chicken" with the special sauces were great

Go for the food, which is okay. And because it is BYOB. Otherwise the place is just downright depressing. I sat on the verandah area getting mauled by bugs and wondering why oh why does the owner not think of hiring an interior decorator. I GET that they are going for the authentic feel, like you are sitting on a beach listening to reggae music and eating yummy food, but it feels dingy. Like I said though, the food is okay. Oxtail was pretty delish. My friend found her jerk chicken fair. I would not recommend this for anything but a hungry person with a craving for the specific type of food they serve.

The food is really good. Went there once and had the pad thai and thought it was delicious. I called ahead and took my order to go and it tasted fresh. The only reason I wouldn't give this restaurant 4 stars is because the second time I went, I ordered the same thing...and they told me they were out of pad thai. How do you run out of a staple at your new restaurant? Puzzling to me. The server offered me curry...which I don't eat so I just got up and left. When I go back next time I'm hoping they have s full stock of rice noodles.

I am adding a star because the owner of the store took the time to contact me and apologize for the my last experience there (95 degree day, broken air conditioning, rude worker, etc). 1-star for good follow up customer service. It means a lot to an unsatisfied customer, that he took it upon himself to right things. He even offered me a free sandwich of my choice. I will visit here again, but no free sandwich needed. I will pay for what I consume, since the food IS pretty good.
This was the worst !!!!! There was a long line don't know why!!!!!....sorry guys Ron is not even close to the real thing....u better off going to Golden Crust....

I was really intimidated to come here, since other reviews said he may be grumpy and will send you to the back of the line, but not the case!! He talked about quality, quality, quality, and freshness. Came at 11:30 on a Monday, one guy just got his food so there were two people in front of me. Line got long REALLY quickly, by the time I left (11:42) there were 12 people in line. Chicken - So soft and tender chicken, ahhhhmazing charcoal taste, and the amount of chicken(!!!) Falafel - crispy and FULL of flavor Pasta - a little too soft and mushy for me but goes perfectly with the chicken Dates - super super super sweet

Soooo good! I know it's not really your first thought to get great food inside the Washington Square Mall-but GO TO Phan's Kitchen!! My family loved the curry and Phan's beef jerky. A surprising find on the east side and we will be back! Everything was made fresh to order and obviously with pride!

This is my second favorite pho place, with the top one being noodle city. It's a little on the expensive side for a large bowl but it's probably the only shop near ucsb that can make a decent bowl of pho. Sometimes their soup tastes a little off, and it can be crowded especially on weekends /night. I have gotten my order mixed up a few times, which gets annoying. The rice dishes are also very lacking and on the expensive side.

The staff was friendly, attentive and helpful. We started out with the mixed appetizer platter, which together with soft, hot, fluffy pita bread and pickled vegetables they serve at every table really was enough for the two of us. We ordered entrees without knowing how much food we would get. The seasoning of the chicken shwarma is excellent, as other reviewers have noted. Great flavor! The hummus is the best I've had anywhere, and the falafel is second only to those I ate in Egypt. delicious!!!

We came here for the first time. The service was great and fast. Everything we eat was great. I'm originally from Montreal and their twist on Poutine was really good. I will definitely come back and try their other specialty
Great place and prices. We will definitely be back! The salad was amazing and the cheese was to die for!

My friends and I went to media on a Wednesday night, for "Dining under the stars", and we ate at Shere-E-Punjab, at an outdoor table on the street. It was a nice setting, and there was a live band, which was fun. The food was very good, the waiters & waitresses were prompt and courteous. We had vegetable samosas, coconut soup, tandoori roti (so so), and they were all good. The samosas could have used a little more spice however. I had shrimp tikka masala, which was tasty, my friends had lamb dishes. Everything was good.
Absolutely delicious! I had the falafel appetizer and my husband had the best gyros sandwich, which are not on the menu.
great food, outstanding service, good prices. even when we come into town it's tbefirst place i go for panaeng curry.
Decent selection of food in the buffet. Let down is not much dessert options and you have to order them from the menu. Worth the try for a weekend brunch.

I walked in based on the other reviews. Place was dead quiet. Noone there. The carpet was very dirty. I figured if the carpet looks like this and there is Noone even there, how does the kitchen look? So I left. Maybe it is a good restaurant but they certainly should clean especially when they have nothing else to do. Then went directly across the street. That place was busy! Wonder why!

Meh, the food seems to be a bit off and a little bland. Prices are decent and the vibe just seems weird to me. If you are really craving Vietnamese food and nothing else is open, you might give this a try. It wont kill you but might not satisfy your craving either.

Best chicken bacon ranch gyro I've ever had in my life. To be fair, it's the only one Ive had in my life but Gyro Shack gets a 10/10 for high quality, great tasting food & because I don't normally like mixing. Hi Ken with bacon with ranch.

Very cute and cozy small local restaurant! But apparently they are closing April 30th (may possibly move to another location on Main St) so that's kind of sad. I got the mango curry and it was very good and only slightly spicy, which works for me. My husband got the pad thai and that was also very good and sweet. Both dishes were nice, portions were not too huge but definitely satisfying. Too bad they are closing!

Came here for dinner tonight with my now fiance... we again got the drunken noodles and a different curry dish (the Red Curry) and it hit the spot. Both dishes were just as delicious as they were the first time we came. The restaurant was busier this time around but the waitress was still friendly despite having to run around to serve everyone. This place is a diamond in the rough. It doesn't look like much from the outside, but the food is excellent.

We have gone here on many occasions and it's always been great. The food is consistently on point and the staff behind the counter are friendly and welcoming. I have referred several people and will continue to.

One of the best meals that I've had in a long time. We were a group of 8, so got the $75 per person tasting menu. Tried so many great dishes (too many to list). Excellent service and very friendly staff...The only drawback to this place is that the kitchen and dining area are one room and it's very loud. If you live in South Jersey, I totally recommend going to Zeppoli for dinner.

Yah Mon is an exquisite dining experience that pairs a beautiful ambiance, delicious flavorful food, well-balanced drinks and decadent desserts. I have never experienced a dining experience where the food is delicious, the service attentive AND the atmosphere feels elegant but also like home. Yah Mon has managed to create high quality food, service and ambiance into one incredible dining experience. We celebrated my dearest friend's 40th birthday on a Sunday afternoon with a party of 24 - including 3 small children. Andre and Ruth provided superior service while Chef Janice created a culinary experience that literally transported us to the kitchen of our island grandmothers. The jerk chicken is seasoned with just the right amount of spice, tender curry goat, well seasoned stew chicken, whole snapper, amazing fresh juices and signature drinks AND the desserts will blow your mind! Sometimes you visit restaurants and the food is amazing but the desserts are subpar - that is NOT the case at Yah Mon. The food AND the desserts are both exquisite! You will be sooooo glad you came!!!

My husband and I tried Spiro's finally for our anniversary. It was a Friday night around 7pm, and we were seated right away. Our server was good. We did have a couple of times when he had disappeared for a while, but he was also waiting on a couple of large groups. I ordered the combination plate, because I love both moussaka and pastitsio. It was a bit more than I like to spend, but the bechamel was amazing! This is definitely more a special occasion place vs a regular stop for me, but it was an enjoyable night for our anniversary. Attire: on the nicer side.

You can tell that the broth is made from scratch. Apparently took 12 hours! Love the side plate with fresh peppermint, bean spouts, lime and hot peppers. Healthy food, delicious flavour. Restaurant is clean and service was courteous and prompt. They have had a few health inspection violations this year and for this reason they get 4 stars (if not I would have given them 5 stars). They weren't huge health violations but important nonetheless.

We ordered their lunch special and were pleasantly surprised - everything was very fresh and tasty. The service was over the top - all staff was very helpful and courteous. The restaurant was very clean. We'll be back.

This was my first time having Vietnamese food. The experience was amazing. I enjoyed the service that we received. The attention and answers to our questions were awesome. The food and the staff make this experience awesome and this location has some really great food.

I went to fez with a friend got humus and a Side of rice, the worst rice I have ever tasted , it tasted like a microwaved 3 or 4 day old rice. Asked our server to remove it and he informed us he couldn't, okay and when we preceded to get the bill he had given Himself a hefty 8 dollar tip, okay? Never coming here again.

Amazing prices for stellar food. I tried the pork and shrimp vermicelli bowls. Very generous meat portions with excellent seasoning, lots of veggie toppings too. The shrimp and pork rolls are very fresh with the best peanut sauce I have ever tasted. I also had the Vietnamese coffee which was freshly pressed and absolutely delish. Great variety on the menu. Definitely coming back here.

First time here, we were a group of 7 plus 2 babies for brunch. I live in Philadelphia, but Wilmington is a good half way point that we meet with some friends from MD. I was a little leary because we turned out to be the only people here, but I was very pleasantly surprised! First off, I am not easily impressed. I've been to some really "nice" places, with prices moderate to high, and and often find the experience mediocre or moderately above average with all things considered (price, quality, service, etc.). This establishment delivers grade A service and quality at affordable prices. Everything I had was fantastic. Expertly prepared, presented, and service with a smile. I wish this was in my neighborhood in Philadelphia, as I would be here frequently. We will most likely be meeting here again in the future!

Tonight was the first time I ate at Vientiane - even though I have lived at 44th & Baltimore for almost a year. It was delish and I will definitely go again! Split the veggie spring rolls and dumplings with my friend and then she had the House Special Fried Rice with chicken and I had the Crazy Pineapple with chicken. We thoroughly enjoyed all the food! Oh, and I had the Thai iced coffee and it was fantastic! The waitresses were nice and kept refilling water which is super important to me. Don't forget it's cash only and relatively small. But it's a nice meal and I recommend it! Enjoy!

Best Indian food in Wilmington, everything was super tasty,vegetable biryani was the weakest dish and that was still good. The aloo mutter was excellent, well spiced and flavorful. Masala dosa was the best, finally a place in the area that does this. Great spot
The service was very attentive and friendly. The food was delicious with just the right amount of spice. The only down side was there was a musty smell in the restaurant.

Went here for the first time tonight! I had never tried Indian good but my friend who is from India invited me and recommended it so with an empty stomach and open mind I happily trailed along! Firstly, the place is super clean and nicely set up. There was Indian style music lightly playing over the speakers that was actually very catchy. Secondly, the service at first was a miss. My waitress spoke too softly and mumbled and slurred all her words together and I didn't find her to be especially polite. Not mean, but also not the type to give you warm fuzzy feelings either. BUT the service was saved during checkout when the gentleman working obliged my five guests by splitting our bill 5 ways after the original waitress put it all on one tab and he did it all very quickly and with a smile! Thirdly, the real reason you're still reading this review: the food. I ordered the chicken tikka masala (you can order it different levels of spicy-mild, spicy, extra spicy, etc) I got mine spicy and didn't find it spicy at all (although I am from a Mexican family where habaneros are topped on food like its salt). And it was delicious! It's tomato based but to me tasted a lot like red chile chicken. I added a side of steamed rice and one piece of naan (naan is bread and is a very good size). My friend ordered chicken curry and that was equally as flavorful but I still have to say my dish was my favorite! Can't wait to go back here perhaps for the buffet to try more things!

Great service, delicious food and a cozy atmosphere. They have 8 or so tables outside, some under cover. Lots of vegetarian and pescatarian options. Three of us split an appetizer and two entrees. The grilled eggplant topped with tomatoes and feta was outstanding. Planning to come back the next time I'm in Philly

I came for lunch with a small group from work. All our food looked amazing and I can certainly vouch that the Sesame Chicken was the best I've ever had from anywhere. We got there shortly before 12 and it was pretty empty, but the place started filling up just after noon rolled around. 'Will definitely be back!

This space, in the Mesa neighborhood of Santa Barbara, has hosted three Thai restaurants. Meun Fan is by far the best of the three. The co-owners, Jan and Hollis, are very personable, as is their waitstaff. Although I'm always very pleased to dine there, it would be nice if they added some specials, some items that would not commonly be on menus of Thai restaurants I've been to. That aside, I'm always eager to go there.

I received food that clearly had soap or some sort of cleaner mixed in it (ordered from GrubHub). I called repeatedly throughout the day (3xs) asking for someone to address this issue, leaving my phone number, name and a complaint. I was told that the manager would call me. After waiting all day I called again and was told the manager left and that I would just need to "catch her" when she gets back. Totally unacceptable and disgusting. Thankfully GrubHub is understandable and working with me to get a refund.
Food is good. Service is so bad, I sought out another Indian restaurant to make my regular lunch spot.
The Chinese food I have had is good, but I haven't tried the Thai, or Japanese yet.

Stopped in to Top China during that whole Tropical Storm Debby nonsense. The lady wanted Chinese food so I braved the storm to go find some. My advise is to drive past this New York style Chinese place. Their food is so saturated with sugar that that it felt I had brought home a take out bag of diabetes. I know that General Tso's chicken is normally very sweet but this was ridiculous.
Not your typical Caribbean restaurant. Much more than I'd expected. I would call it high end caribbean. Nice place, great food, friendly people. I'm definitely going back.

4/5 you'll smell like smoke when you leave but you'll have a happy belly! i'll admit skepticism when i first heard about this, and easily avoided it because i don't normally stop at this point on broad. but a colleague and i made a try once, and recently went back with a bud. i'm going to say that this is fair game for solid rotation. the big dishes in the $20ish range are easily shareable (hello, pork steak!) and are bright and fun. if you offered me that pork knuckle dish we'd achieve a new level of friendship. i think the glasses and silverware are also fun and quirky and contribute interest like all the bold flavors and spices in the dishes. there were chill on my recent trip and let me order a "lunch" dish during dinner, so you might try asking to see what else they may have! i need to come for proper lunch to try their set plates - that kind of offering is definitely my jam. parking can get a little tricky - if you're lucky there will be something on broad, but i've also been able to park along the side street next to ideal market. also, be mindful of what you wear in because it'll smell smoked by the time you finish your meal!

I went to Saigon Corner with my fiance on a late Monday afternoon. We were the only ones there at the time. The service was slow, surprisingly. We ordered Summer Rolls and Chicken Satay as our appetizer. The Chicken Satay was a bit over fried and skinny on the stick. The sauce for the chicken was not bad. The summer rolls were so-so. For our entree, we both ordered Pho Dac Biet (combination). The broth was bland! Nothing near flavorful! We were both disappointed that they did not add tendons in our pho. Each of our pho bowl had one meatball and very little meat in it. I am Southeast Asian and I can tell you that Pho is not supposed to be made like that. Other than that, I'd rather use my money on gas to drive to Tampa where pho is at least AUTHENTIC and fulfilling!
The ground beef kabob was delicious and juicy. We were in a rush and the food came out quickly.

Jasmine Rice was a simple, elegant way to spend an evening with my family. I came to visit from New York and my father picked me up after making a reservation for 7:30pm on a Wednesday. We arrived 5 minutes early and were seated (the restaurant was half empty due to rain). We brought with us a growler of beer and bottle of wine to share, which was more than enough for us. The host was very kind and made sure we were well hydrated while we waited for our food to come out. It did not take too long before appetizers and soups came to the table, followed by the main course. I had the crispy duck fried rice, which was quite tasty, and all other meals were enjoyed as well. Overall a wonderful place for a meal, and not too expensive!

the food here is exceptionally amazing. the service here, however, is a hit or miss. slow days, the wait staff is very friendly and the food comes out lightening fast! busy days, staff is unorganized and unattentive. made reservations for a table of 15 on mother's day. upon arrival to restaurant, "hostess" first denies anyone making reservations and then admits she didn't think our party was going to show up. what the ???!!! large abundant of dishes to choose from. my recommendations? the crab ragoon, peppered calamari and fried fish (with sauce on the side) is a must try. I would only return here if there are barely any diners. what's the point of reservations? it's useless here.
Delicious summer rolls and traditional banh mi, loved the bubble tea. Can't wait to go bavk

I come here for hang over cures with big groups of friends. The service is great, as is the pho. Parking is a little difficult (but we always park in that little viet plaza across the street, shhh), but totally worth it! It's cheap, it's the epitome of the typical pho place, and it's great. I'm always satisfied.
Lunch buffet has horrible service. If you plan on getting your check and paying then you need to block off an additional 30 minutes.

I just tried this place yesterday after many times of walking past it and saying "Hey, we should try that." I was really excited--mostly for the mac n cheese--however was slightly disappointed. Before I begin, my review does not reflect the staff. They were perfectly nice and explained the menu with ease. We went around dinner time and got four chicken strips, a container of their mac n cheese, 2 handpies and 2 sauces. The best thing about our meal was the parmesan pesto sauce and that is it. The chicken was cold and stale, the mac n cheese was spicy, but not to the fault of the place--it just didn't fit my palate. The handpies were cold and not over the moon amazing. *Sigh* Wishbone, you didn't make my wish come true.

i was really excited about trying this place. i had visions of noodles, tofu, pesto, and other yumminess dancing in my head. then, i ordered....a spinach salad with creamy tomato soup and chicken wonton things for an appetizer. the husband ordered a pesto-y with noodles and pork dish. his was awesome...well, the noodles and sauce were, i didn't try the pork...did you know pigs don't sweat, they're filthy animals. i should have ordered an awesome noodle bowl. what i ordered was average, nothing to jump up and down on a couch about, but nothing to mope and complain about. the menu here is healthier with lighter fair, so if you ever find yourself on a miserably hot day, and want a lighter meal, give this place a try, it'll be good. anyhow, it was good, but lately, i've been a bit loose with my 4 star ratings, so i only gave it 3...i don't want to get a reputation and all.
Every time I eat here the food is really good. They go above the ordinary to make sure you liked everything. It's all cooked to order, but worth the wait.
Great Thai food! My family loves ordering from here. Food is great and portions are large! You won't be disappointed!

it is impossible that every review here is not 5 stars. It's amazing! If you like spicy food, you can't beat Dosa Hut... let them know you want to cry, and you will :) We love it here for dining in and for take out. The coconut rice is insanely good, and there are plenty of options for meat eaters, vegetarians, and gluten free dosas!

The pork belly steamed buns are amazing, best I've had. The pho, bahn mi, and fresh rolls are good too. I love all the use of fresh herbs. Decent beer selection. The prices are fair and the service is good. It's definitely my favorite lunch spot on Freret St., just wish they were open on Mondays! I tried something new, the crispy hen rice dish...it was awesome!! But, the pork belly buns are definitely one of my most favorite foods ever, gotta get them every time!

I have eaten Indian food on four different continents and I feel absolutely comfortable saying that Gateway to India is up there with the best of them. I have been here countless times and never once had an experience less than great. The food is delicious, from the samosas to the naan to each curry they serve (I highly recommend the tikka masala or the korma). The service is stellar and everyone there is so warm and nice. Go and treat yourself or bring someone to impress them.

I really kinda love this place. I used to go to the location on 10th and Jefferson back in the day, and always get the lunch special- shrimp lo mein, wonton soup with extra crunchy noodles, egg roll- because I was non-adventurous. Now, I'm just as stuck in my ways, but my dish is catfish with ginger sauce, and it's right what it says on the tin- a whole fish, fried crispy, served with this wicked sauce that has chunks of ginger floating in it with red pepper flakes. Spicy? You betcha. Good? Oh my goodness, yes. Served with rice, it's the perfectly filling option for lunch or dinner. Plus, either bubble tea or soda lemonade, with crispy spring rolls- yes and yes. I just wish I lived closer or they had longer hours, but that's pretty much my complaint about every restaurant. I'm sad i don't get to eat here more often.

Ignoring all previous reviews a coworker of mine recommended the food here even though he said they were a little rude but anyway I decided to give them a try and order when my huge Caribbean family came in from NY and we don't have many options for carribean cuisine in Philly as we do in NY... Before I could even order I called in to ask about online ordering... Long story short it's not worth it to me.. The staff or whoever is answering the phone for that matter is extremely rude and unaccomadating so I would never therefore afterwards, experiencing the way they speak to customers, give them my hard earned money.. We didn't want to go out to eat but we will be headed To reefs lounge were they treat their customers respectfully. BTW + in my household we order food pretty much everyday between my husband and my work schedule and of course we don't always have a wonderful experience but I've never signed up for yelp to leave a review given the issues We've had . I came on here to specifically leave this review. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone

This place is great! We tried Wishbone by getting a delivery order using the Ubereats service. The food was at our door in under 30 min. The chicken tenders are outstanding. My wife is a chicken tender aficionado and says they are some of the best she has ever had, and I agree. The dipping sauces we got were great too! (honey mustard, buffalo bleu, Donfire) As a chilihead I appreciate when things advertised as spicy are actually spicy. The Donfire sauce was just that. Good habanero flavor and plenty of heat. The Autumn salad was a well balanced blend of flavors and textures. Very yummy and good on the tummy. Finally, the Southern sandwich was SO bomb. Tangy sweet tomato jam, tasty slaw, gourmet pickles, and of course the amazing fried chicken! A must-have. Needless to say, we will be getting food from here again very soon. Thank you, Wishbone!

Really delicious food. My friends hate lentils but loved these lentils! I don't eat meat so it's nice to look at a menu that actually has a wide selection of delicious sounding items. That being said, they have meat too. Beer and wine, and really friendly kind staff made this dining experience truly lovely.

First Thai restaurant ever. I was craving (fairly cheap) food and wanting to try something different. Thanks to Yelp & Urbanspoon I quickly located this 'something different' only a few minutes drive from work. I scanned the menu (and Yelp of course) before I left work so I would have an idea of what to order. The $4.99 lunch menu is awesome and plentiful - I honestly wish I could've eaten more. My first attempt at Thai was Pad Khing, 2 on a spiciness scale of 1-5 as suggested by the cashier. My taste buds were lit up just a tad too much, so next time (I know there will be)... I'll just stick with 1. I also opted for a $1 spring roll - awesomely tasty too! So for $6 I got a spring roll, ALOT of chicken + veggies & a plentiful serving of rice. Perfect overall serving for lunch. When the lady owner asked how I found them, I told her thru Yelp/US and she was very appreciative of the reviews already posted and that I chose them (because let's be honest, they're not really near anything but Family Video). I can't wait to go back and try something different from there soon!

Place is legit AF. Owners very nice. Fast service. Price is very reasonable considering it's all you can eat. Food is delicious. They rotate the desserts to mix it up, but always have 3 to choose from. Tea is included. 2 different kinds of rice, salad, appetizers, soup, etc. all included. My favorite Indian buffet by far.

This is one of the best places to go in Philly for Moroccan food...the coffee is amazing as well. Sundays are the best time, at least for me, to go in and get my favorite foods. Everything is great here, as is the service. The best part about it is that they have many vegetarian dishes to choose from and the food is less spicy than Ethiopian cuisine (I only state this because some of my friends do not take kindly to hot spices and vowed never to trust me regarding food recommendations). The Servers and staff are friendly and efficient, and they don't mind if you use your netbook or laptop after a meal or even a cup of coffee. Having wi-fi is also a huge bonus. If your objective is to have an inexpensive and wonderful meal, do some work, or visit with friends, Marrakesh Express should be on your list.

Perfectly seasoned tofu bahn mi. Mmmmmm. My gf enjoyed her pork bahn mi as well. Restaurant is at back of convenience store. If you're coming from the French Quarter, just hop on the trolley up Canal Street.

I would ideally give Tandoor a 2.5 rating, but since that's not an option, I'll go with a 3. Summary: It has slightly above average food, decent ambience, but below average staff. Longer version: Tandoor is one of the few Indian restaurants close to where I live and I've gone there many times. My principal reason for going to Tandoor is that it offers a reasonably priced dinner buffet and definitely has better food than the New Delhi restaurant next door: for about $10 it's all you can eat, which I think is a pretty good deal. They have a wide variety of foods to choose from, and most of them taste about adequate, but their gulab jamuns in particular are delectable. It's also usually clean, and not noisy, so it's a decent option if you just want to spend an evening conversing with friends. However, set against their above-average food and ambience is their dour, almost-hostile staff. They were never particularly welcoming or courteous, but on my last visit, they were actually rude. Besides, they don't bring out food on time either. Now, I expect this behavior from an inexpensive place like the nearby Dana Mandi (which by the way has the best Indian food in this area), but not from Tandoor. I see from other reviews that take-out is perhaps a better option; maybe the food tastes better and you won't have to deal with the staff. But for dining in, I wouldn't really recommend the place. And the sad part is that Tandoor can so easily fix their problem: all they need to do is to give their waiters some basic lessons in courtesy.

Love, Love, Love this place! I last ate their a few months ago. The decor is simple, but the food TOTALLY makes up for it. So far it's my favorite place. The wine list is not extensive, but they have good choices and decent prices. The food is very inexpensive for what you get. The food is soooo good! I love their mango chicken dish. They have a lunch and dinner menu. For lunch you can get a great meal for under $10. The wait staff we have every time have been very nice. Oh, my favorite part.... ask for their hot sauce (Masoula - sp?). It's awesome if you like hot stuff. Just ask for the hot sauce! Try it.... you won't regret it! They also have a sangria that's yummy. On a hot day, it's quite refreshing.

My boyfriend and I came in for lunch on a weekday and had a pretty unpleasant experience. There were small flies buzzing around inside the restaurant and there was only one employee and an angry older woman helping all the tables. The older woman stormed over and said 'what do you want' to take our order and when our food arrived she slammed our plates on the table and walked off. We ordered chicken pad Thai and shrimp curry noodles and the shrimp and chicken were both overcooked. Not to mention it costs an extra dollar for five small overcooked shrimp. After the food was delivered no one came to check on us or refill waters. We noticed the same with other tables who all had empty glasses and had to wave over the one employee to get boxes. We ended up having to go to the front and wait around to pay because we couldn't get our check. It's a cheap meal but I'm sure there are a lot of better options on state street to choose from.

Picture this: idyllic, tropical courtyard filled with palms, multicolored fairy lights, and a fountain, with a bar to the side where the 'tenders are slinging rum drinks and music pouring out from the interior of the restaurant. Are you with me here? Yes. And please, this is how you need to enter, through that courtyard on Frenchman, rather than through the restaurant itself, which is much more modest, bare bones, even, and is where you'll often find a variety of bands playing (last night, Thursday, was a Blues jam). It's just not much to look at when you consider the outside and if outside was not available, I'd be hard pressed to stay. First impressions are everything, as they say, and luckily mine was of the environs. Although I can't speak for the food, I can speak for the drinks (you know me by now, right?) They have a fair selection of three red wines, one of which was organic but two of which were Cabernets and I avoid Cabs like the plague.
