I settled for a decent Shiraz, but really, this scene is just begging for rum drink sippin', so I can't fault them for their wine selection. The mojito list is impressive and Old New Orleans Rum is an option (and I highly recommend over that Cruzan stuff). There are plenty of fruits to add in to your drink, too. Blueberry, anyone? The bartenders are swift, friendly and because the bar is called Mojitos, you know they won't roll their eyes at you for ordering one. I'm such a sucker for ambiance, that I will gladly return just for a drink in the courtyard. They'd even get me drinking rum and that's a pretty rare thing.
Absolutely delicious! Olio gave my husband and I the best restaurant experience we've had in years.

This place looks nice but the service is absolutely terrible. We came here not knowing any better. The waiter seated us and didn't even give us a menu. After waiting 15 minutes we had to ask for a menu. I could understand if they were busy but they only had 2 other tables with customers there. The food was just bland. I had the Pollo Taormina and it was just so so. I had to ask for the menu and had to ask for the check. Service was terrible.

I have visited this wonderful place a few times and have loved it every time. My sister and I always get the pho. We used to order the pork pho, but if you value reducing your saturated fat intake, there is a chicken pho available too. The super bowl is $11 and can feed three people. It comes with a plate of bean sprouts, basil and limes which enhance the pho's flavor #16 is a great appetizer is a option for trying multiple items. It has crab ragoons, two kinds of spring rolls and a fried shrimp roll. There are three kinds of sauces that come with this particular appetizer. One is fish based so double check with the server if you or other guests have an allergy. The peanut sauce pairs with the spring rolls really well because it's a thicker, creamy sauce and the spring rolls are light. Drinks: hot tea comes in your own white kettle so you can keep your tea warmed up at any given moment. The jasmine tea is really good too. It has a slightly floral taste to it. The menu has a vast variety and the staff is very helpful so it's a great place to explore the menu time and time again.
This place is great! The price is right and so is the food. I don't want to sit inside because it's too tiny, but that's ok with me because I prefer take out. Check it out!
The meat patties were delicious, the chicken and goat curry was average, The collard greens were great and fresh, and the rice and beans were pretty good.

Delicious food, and the man who runs this cart is great! He is nice, generous, and makes a lot of jokes when he's not too busy. There is no menu cause you just get what he's serving. It varies day to day, but definitely includes a few falafel (which I thought were great, really garlicky!), the rice of the day (I've had like a tomatoey rice with peas, or combination white & wild rice), hummus, watercress, and charcoal-fired chicken. Yes, he grills over charcoal in his tiny food truck (!!!), which also is impeccably clean, festooned with probably 100 garlic bulbs, some healthy looking plants, has a radio playing Greek music, and smells mouthwatering from 3-4 blocks away. If you've walked through the area around lunchtime in the summer, this is the truck you are smelling. Once I brought a container home, and it emanated that same delicious grilled kebab scent all the way home on the trolley. It's a tiny bit more expensive than many food trucks ($7), but you get a piece of fruit, a roll or pita, and a LOT of food. I ate as much as I could, felt completely full, and it looked like I had only eaten half of my styrofoam container. Totally recommend!!

Long weekend May 31st 2010. I will remember this was the worst food I ever ate in my life. We were enjoying everything we were doing but this dinner where we were 14 adults and 2 kids was all screwed up by me who pushed my friends to skip italian and to do some Indian bread. HORRIBLE in all ways... I now know you get what you pay for, $6.95 buffet means they are giving garbage with no taste. BIG NOOOOO..!!

This is my second visit here. One tip, before you decide to come here make sure you give 1hr enough to get your food. Cart located near 20th and Ludlow st. There is no menu, serves only one meat that is chicken. You can tell him to make vegeterian if you want. Now the food, one of the best and juiciest chicken I have ever tasted. Everyday the menu is different. Gus the chef he prepares the chicken fresh in front of you. It's 10$ cash. Get a mix of all the flavour, with chicken, fruits and falafel. Totally Worth the wait.
Always great food, great service & inexpensive. Atmosphere is lovely. Never had a bad experience & have been coming here for years.

HoangTofu to be honest is a bit rough around the edges but the staff is cheerful and food is delicious. A diamond in the rough for banh mi sammys. I decided to explore the space a bit with the sardine sammy and honestly I was a little scared of what to expect...it was absolutely delicious. Sorta like a spicy tuna sandwich with traditional banh mi veg. It was so pleasing to my belly that I ordered another this time grilled pork...also delicious. (Besides for $3 how can you go wrong)The bread looks heavy and filling but upon first bite was pleasantly surprised at how airy and light it was. A great vehicle for the assorted filling inside. The food makes up for the very basic interior and I believe they have approx 12 varieties along with hot soups. Give them a try you won't be disappointed. For a tasty quick lunch for a insanely cheep price this is a fantastic little joint.

Absolutely the best Indian restaurant in the area. We've been many times now, usually eating in but we've had take out too. Always consistent and full of flavor. Can be a pricey night out but well worth it!!

I loved this place from the moment I walked in the enviornment and the service was delighting, The sushi was fantastic only thing I was not crazy about was the Pad Thai but the ladies are wonderful, the sushi is moderately priced and the portions are nice. Definitely my new fav sushi place

So I have never had Indian food before. My girlfriend and I are on vacation here in Clearwater and she said hey there is an Indian restaurant nearby that has a buffet we should go there and that way I can try out different Indian food items. Get a variety since I don't know what I like and don't like. So we drive to Deccan Spice. When we got inside it is very nicely decorated and the servers were very friendly. We sat down and the server pointed us towards the buffet. They had about 20 different items on the buffet. Each was in its own chafing dish. Nice hot and fresh. They very aware when items were low and brought out more of the items that were out very fast. The food was amazing. The stand out to me was a spicy fried fish and the curry goat. But everything else I had was delicious! I now know I like Indian food. Sadly I don't live in Clearwater otherwise this would be a place I would come to often.
A nice local coffee & eatery. Slightly price. Free Internet is a nice touch.

this is the best restaurant in all of carpinteria! this place isn't over priced and it's delicious! i love Thai food and this is my all time favorite place to go when i'm in carpinteria. I usually get the mixed vegetables with gyoza. the Gyoza (potstickers) are SO GOOD you have to get them if you go- there fried potstickers.

I had a serious gyro craving and decided to go here after reading good reviews on yelp. Well, I'm sorry to say I have to disagree with most of the reviews. Coming from Chicago, maybe I expected more. They don't use the typical lamb meat that's thinnly shreaded off a roast, it's more like big square chunks, it did not feel like a gyro. I'm used to tomatoes, onions & sauce on the side. This place only includes some watered down white stuff, so you'll have to ask for the extra goods. For me, when I want a gyro, it should be hot, thick & greasy meat with some zang at the end...this was the complete opposite. And so continues my search for a good gyro in Nashville.

Absolutely delicious, one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. The two biggest things to remember: bring cash and don't cross the lady at the register. She makes Sam the sushi guy look like Mr. Rogers.

Absolutely delicious. I had the onion naan with dipping sauces and the chicken biryani. The flavor of the food was very satisfactory and the chicken was cooked perfectly. Best quality Indian food that I've ever had. The servers were friendly and helpful as well, and made sure I never ran out of water to drink.
Excellent food! Would definitely be coming here again. It's a new restaurant, opened about 2 months ago. The service could be slightly better but overall 5 stars!

We got there at 9:25 pm and asked for a table. The server told us that they were closed and we could only have a takeout. Their clock showed 9:27 pm and they were closed? My husband got real mad and argued with them but they insisted that they were closed. My husband went on to say that they should just open for 2 hours and then go home since they didn't want to do business! Ridiculous! That actually gave us a chance to try another Indian restaurant nearby which turned out to be much better with more variety of food and with a more lively atmosphere.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant. Have been to fancier places; the food here wins, hands down! Tonight, had the 'Sweet & Spicy Duck'; now wondering why i never tried it before. The dish came out of the kitchen VERY quickly, the spicing was exactly to my taste (level 4, on a scale of 1-5), good size portion, and friendly service. Note: lychee juice is almost as good a fire extinguisher as Indian lassi or raita. Very glad to have a place like this so close to home.

I can't get past the red curry with shrimp. It's so crazy delicious. It has lots of good sized shrimp, fresh crispy vegetables (and lots of them), just the right balance of spicy and sweet. It's just to die for. This time I ordered the steamed dumplings as well, intending to share, but yeah, that didn't happen. They were also superb.

We just got take out tonight from Ekta, and I can't wait to eat the leftovers tomorrow. The tandoori chicken and shrimp were both excellent. The nan was right on the money and the rice was perfect. Good prices and great food is what I was hoping for and is what I got! will definitely go back.

A gem of a place with excellent food and customer service. I frequented this restaurant while in Tampa during my business trips and my experience was par excellence each time. The hot tea was amazing with all its aromas and hints of spices. For dinner, each time I ordered Queen's Eight Platter - sampling of different dishes (chef's choice). The owner chef is very accommodating to your requests for different food items and provides helpful suggestions regarding the same. The portions are generous and surprisingly, prices are not high, compared to other places I've been to in different locations. Also, each table has its own bottle of hand-sanitizer which you don't find in many place. I will definitely be going there during my next visit to Tampa.

Amazing dinner as usual...Francisco went out of his way to go to his other restaurant to ensure that my father got the dish of his request that was not on the menu tonight...the Hawaiian fish was amazing and so was my appetizer---the scallops in a lobster cream sauce This was a special on the menu.

Closest thing to home when it comes to food! Alcapurrias were fried to perfection and the beef seasoned very well, had the crab mofongo and it was splendid. What stood out the most was the phenomenal service, really felt at home here.
5 stars. 4 words. Foot.Long.Banh.Mi.

I happened to find this truck by accident and was drawn to it because of the lovely flowers and plants on display in front. I want to love this food truck because it has an air of mystery (no written menu!) and is run by a couple of fun characters, but the sauce was too spicy/garlicky and I did not care for the homemade pasta/spaghetti that came with my falafel. I asked for no chicken, so I only got the falafel, which was excellent (except it was doused in that overly spicy sauce that leaves a gasoline taste in your mouth for hours). And who serves pasta with falafel? The fresh greens served on top were delicious. I'm not sure what they were but they were yummy. Also, the red grapes sprinkled throughout were a great touch and added a succulent, sweet taste to the dish. The guys in the truck were so friendly and nice, and I know a lot of people love this truck, but I wish the food preparers gave you a little more control over what you want. They do seem a little Soup Nazi-esque in that regard.

Yummm. That's what I'm thinking as I write this review. Basil Spice is better, in my opinion, than King and I. I'm not usually the person to go to a place and repeatedly order the same dish, but I do here. Gang ga rhee is the jam. A yellow curry dish with onion, carrots and potatoes, your choice of spiciness. I eat this dish every time!! Order it and you too will be in love. A few honorable mentions: Thai tea, pad thai and summer rolls. I've tasted other things, but at this point, I have gang ga rhee on the brain.

My wife and I were recommended this restaurant by other puerto Ricans which live here in Tampa. We found the place to be very nice, we loved the Mofongo with skirt steak. I highly recommended to anyone visiting the area.
Great service! Great Food! Great Experience! The manager, Karim, is extremely attentive and friendly. Definitely worth trying and becoming a regular customer.

Yet another Viet restaurant in the area! In addition to the Lotus in Elmwood and Kim Ahn's further down Jeff Hwy and the Pho Orchid express down Airline. The prices are high. We went a few days after opening so the staff were just learning the ropes. The waitresses were very polite and helpful and very willing to get the answers to our questions. Having been back a couple of times now, the pho is good and they give a good amount of herbs to add. The Vietnamese crepe (not made with eggs-- it's made with rice flour and coconut milk and yellow from turmeric) was very tasty, but not as crispy as the superb one at pHo Nola and they don't provide enough lettuce and veggies to eat with it. The spring rolls don't have enough herbs in them to be really good. The big selling point is the really nice, bright welcoming, open renovated building. There are numerous tables outside for warmer weather, though being right on Clearview it might be a bit noisy.
Food was mediocre at best. Chicken piece in aloo tikki tray did not inspire confidence in anything being truly vegetarian. Bahtura was not warm.

While the staff was friendly and attentive, and the background music very nice (classical), we found the food to be mediocre. The Pho broth was not very flavorful and the bean sprouts were a bit past their prime. In the Mango Chicken and Shrimp, the shrimp were not very fresh, and the chicken was low quality (almost like processed chicken). The sauce was too salty yet not that flavorful, and I couldn't even really taste the mango. To top it off, they only offer white rice.
Extremely mediocre. Literally zero crab in the "crab" rangoon. Pineapple friend rice and red curry were just ok.
the spring rolls as well as the pho was amazing! the pho beef broth was made to perfection. we've been visiting out here in indiana, looking for the best pho, and so far this place has done it.

Yah Mon was absolutely delicious, they definitely deserve their rating! It's a bit hidden and in an awkward location, but so worth it. I had the oxtails and wasn't able to finish it was so filling. I was really upset that I forgot my leftovers in my hotel fridge. Both of my friends absolutely love their dishes as well. Good ambience, good service, good food, no complaints!
Delicious falafel! Really enjoyed our lunch here this afternoon. Very friendly and attentive service. Must try!
Ate here for lunch today ordered the Jungle pork it was amazing. Victoria was so nice I will definitely eat here again...
This place is a gem! They are super nice and the food is excellent. The interior of the restaurant has a lot of wood and the vibe is calm and warm. I will definitely be back.
Good Greek food. Tried it with my wife and son. I plan to go again whenever we want local Greek food.

Great atmosphere and nice staff, but don't come here if you want to leave with a full belly... or leave satisfied with your purchase. I ordered the quail ($29) and was very disgusted. The potatoes were undercooked and it just.... tasted bad. No other way to put it. The table also ordered the scallop pasta dish and the prosciutto chicken. Both were similarly bland and considerably small yet expensive. What a ripoff. The only yummy dish we had was the dessert: the tiramisu cheesecake was fantastic.

One of my go to places, especially for date night! Pro: - the food is delicious. You can't go wrong with the Lamb shank or seafood linguini - portions sizes are really great for the price - looks like they have a great happy hour with food and drinks Con: - snails appetizer was mushy and flavor left much to be desired for - service can be improved i.e. Our water glasses sat empty for a while each time before they were filled

I've never been a huge fan of thai food...meaning I tried it twice and wasn't happy. But then I I watch the Food Network...gosh darn it Bobby Flay I wanted some Pad Thai! I got it, and though my tummy filled fast, it was delicious. The atmosphere was cozy and the service was wonderful and understanding of my lack of "culture". I always appreciate when people accept my lack of anything.

Thai 5 is really really good. My favorite is the chicken pad Thai with medium spice. It's just the right amount of spice and it's even better the second day. I also recommend the steamed dumplings. The dipping sauce that comes with them is the perfect compliment.
Great food, deals, and service! The Pad Thai was delicious and at a reasonable price. I found my new favorite dinner place. Service was excellent and very hospitable. Live music was also very good.
Great food and friendly service! The spring rolls were a little bland and the rice paper was chewy. The dipping sauce was delicious! And the Pho Ga made up for it. Great flavor!
Some dishes are excellent such as the Vietnamese BBQ and some the chicken was dry. I've found the shrimp cooked to my satisfaction. The staff is friendly. I would recommend eating here.

This foodtruck is full of some authentic southern cooking! I tend to catch them at any festival that has food trucks...they will be there! Try to get to them early because they sell out of a lot of stuff. They don't have prices on the truck. I got a chicken breast small platter with mac n cheese and candied yams for $12. My boyfriend got the chicken sandwich for $8. They are cash only! It's definitely delicious! The mac n cheese is that perfect amount of creamy and the yams are perfectly sweet and sauced! I've also had their potato salad and it is bangin', but I'm not sure they sell it in the winter because they didn't have it at Bloktoberfest. The chicken sandwich is literally just a chicken breast between two pieces of white bread, so just get the breast.

Just moved to Carp. My wife and I love Thai food and after spending a month in Thailand we are always searching out great restaurants to go to. This is now on our regular list. The food is fresh and spices are perfect. Staff is very friendly and accommodating. Looking forward to going back.

All the food is good here and halal, which is a bonus! The ashak appetizer is delicious, the qurma chalaw with lamb has the lamb so tender that it just melts in your mouth, it feels like such comfort food. The lamb kabobs were also very good. All of this came with fresh salad, and afghan bread. The portion size is good, but one dish is definitely enough for one person and probably would not be enough to share. I have family members who are afghan and cook amazing food, so I had high standards, but this place is definitely one I can't wait to come back to!! The decor and atmosphere in the back is also clean and very well done and shows off the traditional afghan culture. If you like middle eastern food, go try this place out for yourselves!

We love it here! Whether it is the two of us, our whole family or business dinners we have never been disappointed by either the food or the service. The avgolemono soup is phenomenal although all the appetizers soups and salads are delicious! I enjoy their filet dinner and their veal to name a few dishes!

Dinner for 4 (2 adults and 2 kids -12 and 8)..we love eating here for the last 5 years when ever we are in Carpenteria...it has given us great memories and excellent food. This weekend we had the pumpkin curry, fresh spring roll, ginger chicken, shrimp tempura, and the pad see with steam rice..yes we had left overs! We were stuffed..the flavors were spot on and found our 8 year old daughter can handle the heat on the pumpkin curry. For desert the hubby picked mangoes with sticky rice..the rest of the family headed back for Smores'

Brought hubs here for an early Father's Day lunch after reading fabulous reviews. Loved the vibe and layout from the moment we entered. The playful black and white checkered ceiling tiles kept me smiling throughout the meal. The staff were friendly and attentive. I liked that the water automatically had lemon in it (hubs did not, oops). We opted to try the grilled lemongrass beef salad rolls to start - yum! I ordered the combo Bun Vermicelli bowl since I'm a vermicelli girl by nature. I really liked the fried onions sprinkles on top. Unfortunately I did not like the shrimp/fish cake. I'm a DIE HARD Golden Bird Vermicelli girl so it's hard to improve upon that. Hubs tried the Vietnamese Style Soup. The flavour was great - but admittedly we were a bit squeamish with the fat/tendons. Both of us thought the mains were lacking in meat considering the prices. I ordered a Vietnamese Iced Coffee to go that was perfect! All in all, really liked Thien An and will definitely be back and next time I'll ask the server for recommendations of what they're favourite dishes are. Clean, bright, and playful atmosphere - perfect for a Vietnamese Newbie that might be a bit shy in China Town. See you soon Thien An, see you soon!

I love this place. I tried the other Indian restaurants and I was not a fan, but this place..this place I love. the food, the lunch buffet was amazing. So many choices and all delicious. I ate too much. even with nascar playing on the tv, that could not make me lower my rating. wow wow wow great food. Only thing that could improve this place would be some Indian tapestries on the wall or a India mural. Great food, polite service, unpretentious atmosphere. I'm in love.

Go for the food, not the ambiance. My boyfriend and I went for dinner at around 6:00 p.m. on a Saturday. We were the only people there. To be honest the place looked pretty dirty and the seats were in need of repair, but since we were there to try Vietnamese food, it wasn't a huge concern. A baby mouse joined us when we sat down and was dancing around near us the entire time. I guess most people would leave a restaurant if they saw a rodent, but we just laughed it off and stayed. Neither of us got sick, so I guess we survived haha. Even though we were looking at it the entire time, the staff didn't seem to notice until I said "Excuse me, there is a baby mouse..." and the waitress was like "What? Oh my god!" but of course it disappeared conveniently when they went to see. Now for the food...neither of us had really had Vietnamese food before, but we are very adventurous and there are few things we won't eat (as long as it tastes good). We asked the waitress for suggestions, and she didn't seem to know much, and ended up mentioning that a couple of items seemed to be popular. Later we found out she was Chinese, which is maybe why she wasn't as familiar with the food. I ordered the "Bun Bo Hue" (Hue style beef and rice noodle soup), and my boyfriend got the "Com dac biet" (Grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, and steamed egg meat loaf). Both dishes were delicious. If you are a picky eater, you probably won't be thrilled with this place. My dish had congealed pig's blood, pig feet and beef tendon. But it was all very tasty so it was fine by me. The broth was truly amazing. We really enjoyed the food. At the end when we went up to the register, the waitress ignored us for a bit because she was chatting with the delivery guy (which is how we found out she was Chinese since he was asking her about that). We weren't in a hurry so it wasn't a big deal, but maybe other customers wouldn't take it so well. In the end, go for the food if you have good company and aren't in a hurry. But this place may have some issues with the health department.

I love Thai, but there is a dish that tops every dish anywhere. Panang Curry! Oh my, it can be good or it can be horrid. Not here though! It was spot on delicious. Along is Thai restaurant serve you half of what's served here or some business's get stingy on the rice. Not here! Portions we exceptional. And there was enough rice to complete the dish. This is a diamond in the ruff. The atmosphere was pleasant. The staff (family owned I assume) were friendly and attentive. They are a young business and I wish them good fortune and keep up the good work.
Excellent food, they are located in the old Kombo Kitchen truck in the same place on Dale Mabry. I had the pad thai, fried rice and chicken panang, all excellent (see photo). Really nice people also.

I was kind of disappointed in this place, I'm not going to lie. I stopped here with my fiancé for lunch so we were able to try the lunch special. It was pretty empty in there and there was only one waitress. She came over quickly and gave us waters and menus. The menus were only for the lunch special combos (with soup, salad, a spring roll). I'm not sure if that means you can't get anything else, but we're fans of chicken satay, so we ordered that, even though it wasn't on the menu. She never brought over a beer list my fiancé requested so water is what we stayed with. Everything came out really fast, likely because the combo items are already prepared. Unfortunately the downfall of ordering off a lunch special menu is if you don't dig the soup or salad (like I did), then you're just stuck with a smaller entree portion. Could be worse, though, since the portions were still plenty big. I got pad see ew, which was really good and my fiancé ordered pad kee mao, which came out as pad Thai... it didn't seem worth it to say anything, since it felt like she wanted us out of there (the whole lunch took 25 minutes. The price was great, but nothing about the experience made me excited to come back.
Super spicy (not hot) panjabi food. Didnt like it much. Service was good though & quick. Kinda expensive too.

Firstly, we live in Little Saigon in San Francisco, so for some white folks, our standards are pretty high. In the past 2 years NOLA has gone from NO Vietnamese places to such a glut I am worried that some of them won't stick around. Been to Magasin (upscale and weird to pay so much for food we pay like $4 at home), Lily's (love), and then we gave this place a try for the first time yesterday and I gotta say FAVORITE!! They do the grilled beef vermicelli rolls which we always had to go to the West Bank for (AND add avocado to anything for $1), the broth in even their basic wonton soup was really rich (I am not a Pho FREAK because its something we eat almost every day back home, its like maybe a Big Mac in terms of passion). The whole adding a fried egg to dishes is a NOLA thing, no one does that back in Cali. But i LOVE it. We had a rice dish, the crab rangoon (which EVERYBODY schmucks up for some reason but theirs was delicate and really good). So, yeah, pretty freakin wowed. Not like Tu Lan or Slanted Door in SF, but what is? For NOLA, this is definitely the favorite hands down.

Excellent peshwari naan! Soft and fluffy on the side with a crispy, flaky exterior layer. It wasn't greasy at all like some versions can be and was a great compliment and vehicle for the curry. I also loved the chicken kalburi, which is a variation of the traditional korma with a creamy cashew sauce and tender pieces of boneless chicken cutlets. The sauce was amazing and I will definitely return to try the chicken korma. The chicken coconut was also solid but it's not a cream-based sauce but rather one made with chili-oil and shredded coconut. It's a great dip for the naan and fantastic mixed with the basmati rice. I can't tolerate too much spice and they were great about making everything very mild. Service is very friendly but the food can take a long time to come out, although they do bring everything out at once. It came to about $45 for a naan and 2 entrees, which is slightly on the pricier end but the food is solid.

I live 5 minutes away from this place and for some reason I've never been there until the past Saturday. We had the crab dumplings, I ordered the green shrimp curry, the person I was with ordered the spicy chicken. The dumplings were absolutely delicious, so was the curry, I felt like it was missing some shrimp, but the flavor and the spiciness was excellent. The service was ok, the ambiance is nice. Excellent food for Lansdale, will definitely go again and maybe try something else. The presentation of the dishes was really appealing too.

The lady at the counter with the shotcut, glasses, and colored hair seems to never smile or give off positive energy. The food is awesome. But the vibe sucks. Even when your trying to be nice and smile at her, she keeps a straight face and just comes off mean. I stopped going just because of that. Im a very happy person. I md rather recieve service from a person with the most greeting spirit and the food is horrible, or maybe even just okay, than to get service from someone with a jacked up attitude and waste my hard earned money.

The combination sandwich was very good and not too spicey. The people working there especially the waitress that helped me was very nice they are definitely university students. Only thing bad was the slow service but with more experience they will get better. I would go back but when not so crowded.
great new restaurant Rings a lot of diversity for food options in the Ruskin area. The food is fresh and the ingredients are good

I had such high hopes for this place but did not enjoy the flavoring of the food. It all had a rather sweet taste, the stewed chicken, the curry chicken.. The roti seemed stale... I really wanted to go off the fact they had great reviews and them being the only real Trini restaurant here... But honestly. Because philly is deprived of good island food. The natives don't know any better. Coming from NY I had high expectations of authentic, highly spiced food. It was just all a sweet mess...

Really great coffee shop with a huge menu! They have quite a few locations all over Edmonton but this one is probably my favorite. It's spacious, good for studying (although loudness and outlets may be an issue) and for socializing. What I appreciate too is that they have a big food menu as well. I've had everything from their samosas to rice dishes to wraps and they're all very satisfying and filling. My only complaint is that it is a little pricey. Its not the most cash friendly but to be honest it's worth it as a once in a while splurg. Their cheesecake is also quite tasty as well as, of course, their drinks. I'm not the biggest fan of their coffee black but their Chai and other tea drinks are good. They have a lot of vegan and vegetarian options as well - for sweets and eats. There vegan cookies are certainly on the thin and hard kind of side but taste wise they don't fall short! Being in the university area there's quite a few students going there and usually it gets pretty crowded, it's rarely even half empty. Fun fact: there's a magician who shows up sometimes as well to entertain people which is pretty darn awesome. All in all I think remedy is a safe bet for a coffee shop and if you haven't checked it out yet you absolutely have to!

I really like Sofra. My last visit there was exceptional. My boyfriend and I went for our anniversary. We ordered the Sultan's four-course meal for two. It was incredible and a great way to sample the menu if you're not familiar with Turkish fare. It started with stuffed grape leaves, a duo of dips with Sofra's delicious handmade pita bread, then a platter of meats, bulgar and fresh greens. The dessert is perhaps the most amazing Baklava I've tried, and it was the perfect finish to the meal. The chef and owner of Sofra is Turkish and went back to his homeland to be trained as a chef. The food is always perfectly cooked and perfectly seasoned. If you go, be sure to try their pita and dips, washed down with a Turkish beer. Incredible. I've always had great service, and the restaurant is unique and cozy. I highly recommend Sofra.

Good coffee...complete with silly coffee sleeves (Twix ads?). They make a mean egg sandwich...it's an omelet folded up. Mmmm substantial. One time I ate there they used terribly out of season tomatoes...which is not okay, thus no 5 stars.

I was very disappointed . I got two noodle dishes to go, the pork and the chicken. Neither portion was very generous with the meat and neither had much flavor. And the meat was very dry. I asked the server about the brown noodles at $1 extra and she couldn't tell me much more than that they were brown.

An hour ride took us here to meet friends with friends for Ethiopian fare. I ordered the Yebege Tibs, described as "tender cubs (sic) of boneless lamb," etc. They were more akin to nuggets than cubes, but they were very tasty, despite not being seasoned extra spicy as requested. I would not describe the meat as being tender. Many pieces were chewy, and a few not even chewable. My companions had the Doro Wat and Keye Wot, which they described as falling off the bone. The service was friendly and efficient and the place looked nice. I'd give them another chance as maybe on my meal it was a s*** happens event.

If there is half star, I would give them half star. I waited 20 mins and have not get my orders which is "bun bo hue" and "bun thit nuong" ( "spicy beef noodle soup" and "pork with egg roll rice bun") I asked them how long I actually have to waited because it was already 15 mins and I am starving. Everyone who are after me, they all get their food even though they are behind. I cancelled the order but they said they can not because they have to wait for the batch to be closed (p/s: they use clover device which I also use at my work place) so they do it tomorrow. They can do it manually because every credit card machine all have that option or they can void the transaction through the order number. They just played around and don't want to do it because they are busy. I could understand the fact that they are busy but I don't like the way how they play around like that (if you have no idea about credit card machine)

If they had better hours, I would be there daily. Chicken Katsu with Thai Iced tea is my typical order but the short rib tacos are great as well. Compared to other food trucks the food here tastes clean and I don't feel gross afterwards. Always excited to go back!

Well worth the wait. There isn't a place in center city with more flavorful food. All of the ingredients are fresh and he takes pride in his product. My first time visiting was last week and I'm hooked. There's so much character to the meals and enough to go back for seconds or thirds.

WORST SERVICE EVER. WAITRESS WALKED PAST US 5 TIMES. Our first and last time ever going here. The waitress took our drink order and left. 20 minutes later still no waitress! Barely wanted to answer our questions. TERRIBLE SERVICE. I've worked in food industries and I would never treat the people who PAY ME TO FEED THEM the way this woman treated us or lack thereof.

Good solid Thai food in Calgary, and now in Edmonton? What's going on? I had the stir fried noodles, which came with thin egg noodles which was not too salty, and not too oily. It had a variety of veggies, including cauliflower, which was the first time I've had it in a stir-fried Thai dish. The chicken was nice and flavorful for breastmeat, and it smelled great. The restaurant, although empty when I picked up my to-go order, looked bright, cozy, and clean. Prices were average for Thai places, approximately $11-14 per entree. The negatives? Not too many! The meal itself wasn't as colorful as I'd expected from all those veggies, and they forgot shrimp in my shrimp fresh spring rolls...they almost forgot my Thai iced tea and I had to remind them. What saves it from becoming a 5 star is that the flavors are solid, but not unique or unforgettable like at some other places.

My first experience with this place was when they have just opened up. The food was amazing everything from the drinks to appz, to entrees. I would highly recommend tikki masala and the naan is a must! The prices are reasonable.

I love Greek food. Looooooove it. I don't love Momo's. I don't even like it. I really wanted to, too. (My best friend is Ruth "Momo" C., for goodness sake!) Dolmadakia are my favorite, and I think the ones here are some of the worst I've ever had. Oversized (go America!), and filled with salt. The grape leaves weren't tender at all, so it was like gnawing on undercooked, soggy-but-tough kale. Two stars because service was good. The food makes me shake my head.

I noticed this place while shopping at Target a few weeks before it opened, and looked forward to trying it because I LOVE middle eastern food. I walked in around dinner time on a Monday, and there were a couple people ahead of me. There were probably at least 6 people behind the counter, and only 1 or 2 who really knew what was going on. I get it, training people takes time, but it just didn't seem like a great system they had going. Service was SO incredibly slow, and the people putting together my veggie feast were so incredibly stingy. If I got a full tablespoon of hummus in my bowl, I'd be shocked. The food was good, but I really don't feel like it was worth what I paid.

We just finished our first meal at this welcome addition to the Vanderbilt area. The staff was friendly and helpful with the menu, and the food was fresh and tasty. My chicken gyro was a generous portion of grilled white meat folded into fresh, chewy pita bread. The accompanying tomato-cucumber salad was well dressed and enlivened by fresh basil, and the roasted potatoes (which I was allowed to substitute for chips) were garlicky and perfectly cooked. My companion had the lamb plate, which featured a mountainous Greek salad and a bed of flavorful basmati rice. Great service, great value. Highly recommended.

This has to be my all time favorite Turkish restaurant in Edmonton. The chicken was perfectly marinated and cooked to perfection. I even tried the lamb thanks to my friend A. Oh yes, its New Zealand lamb. I've never enjoyed New Zealand lamb because of the gamey taste. But Sofra got it right. Service was wonderful and it wasnt too busy but it could be that we went on a Sunday. I think Friday and Saturday could be their busier times. Children under 12 are not allowed. Im not sure when or if this rule has always applied but its good to be aware. Washrooms were clean. If you are looking for authentic turkish cuisine this is the place.

I have never had Ethiopian food but this place was so delicious! The menu gives new comers some background of the food and a little culture and it really gets you excited. They have vegan options! The best is the lentils but all the food is great! I can't wait to go back, so yummy!
Awesome place with great ambience. You can really enjoy the place when you are out with your gang. Food is great and hookah are heavenly.

Amazing meal. We had lunch menu and usually lunch menu are not great but here it was delicious. All ingredients were fresh and veg were crunchy. Great service. 5 star quality at 1 star price. I will go again soon.

Food is great, however service can use a bit more common sense. Server brought out food for whole table except my paratha. Come to find out he had dropped it on the kitchen floor. Things happen but for it to take another whole 20mins to remake a single paratha is not justifiable. Table had already completed eating their food by the time paratha was served to me. Please prioritize whats on the cook's to do list by using some more common sense.

Ah after a hard days work thought I would go for some mouth watering food. I had my reservation in going to Jaipur as my Indian colleagues did not recommend it but I wanted to see for myself. I was on assignment and was missing nice spicy Indian meal. What a disappointment. I am not going any further suffice to say out of 4 of us the person who enjoyed the most was a caucasian who never had Indian food and later told us he was just being polite. I will not say anything accept, thats my first and last trip. But some of you may like it.

We went here for dinner with a group of 7. We brought our own wine because they do not have their liquor license. We ordered so much food and entrees that its hard to separate one from the other (or maybe it was the wine). It doesn't really matter because all the plates were good (and we seriously shared about half of them). After all this the bill was a laughable $90.
5 stars!!!! Makes me want to fly back into NJ just to eat here because I can't find any other Caribbean restaurant here in Chicago! The oxtails and Jerk Chicken was perfect!!!

First, the good. We ate outside which was nice. The food we ordered was very good. The bad. You are given a tiny menu with food that states its to share and prices for sharing. We ordered the special which was a dinner (THERE ARE NO DINNER PRICES ON THE MENU) and there is a reason for this. I had sea bass to the tune of $38 my date had Veal $42. The portions were very small. We are not big people. Do not go here if you are hungry or on a budget. This restaurant is way, way, over priced. You can do alot better elsewhere. My biggest complaint though is they are not forthcoming with the prices. If you order dinner you better ask what it will cost or risk heart failure when you get the bill.

Stopped by for lunch. Didn't even know this place was here! It's a small space with a few tables. The lady there was friendly. She took my order and made my food. I ordered the banh mi special and an order of the eggrolls. Sandwich was good, the bread was soft and chewy and all of the ingredients in the sandwich were fresh and tasted good. The BBQ pork was meaty and not fatty which I prefer. The eggrolls on the other hand were not good. They were way too greasy, not crispy at all. I would pass on that next time. Will have to try their drinks next time. This place is pretty close to my work so when I am craving a banh mi, I will probably just swing by here.
Went there for lunch last weekend. The food and the service was great. Prices very well... definitely recommended.

Nom nom nom. So good! This is my go-to spot for Thai in South Tampa and it's the best Thai I have had in the area. It's pretty much the same as when Kombo Kitchen was there. The lady who takes the orders is so nice and friendly (I really should know her name...) and the food is consistently good and the portions are generous. I always get the Pad Woonsen - lots of good veggies, and my husband always gets the Chicken fried rice. One word of warning on the spice level - they will ask how spicy you want it - medium spice has a good kick to it, so depending on if you are spice-adverse, you may want to do no spice or mild spice.

I ordered takeout from Zorbas and it was so, so good! I had the Greek salad, spicy feta and pita, and fries. It came super fast (I ordered through Uber eats) and the food traveled super well. The fries in particular were still very crispy and absolutely delicious even after traveling. Only didn't give 5 because they forgot my side of tzatziki. Overall would definitely recommend.
Delicious and authentic. The fresh baked pita is to die for. The beef kafta? Fugetaboutit! So good!

Great Italian BYO, charming rooms, attentive staff, with the food very well prepared and reasonable prices.The Head waiter is a complete Pro, hard to find such competency these days, and I know I'm in the Biz. Do give them a try, you won't be disappointed.
Five for food. Just amazing. One .., one one one for service. These guys are just oblivious to the needs of clients. Management are you listening? Great food....add responsive help please

Today was my first time trying Tiffin Etc. I've eaten at Tiffin before and thought it was very good, not great but a solid 4 stars. My Murgh Tikka Kati Roll from Tiffin Etc, well I would have given it 6 stars if I could, that is how delicious it was! It may be a while before I go back to the original Tiffin because now I can't wait to try some of the other kati rolls and of course the Indian pizzas at Tiffin Etc. Damn, that was yummy - perfect lunch for a rainy day.

Came here for lunch with a $10/$20 Groupon. I expected to grab a sandwich and take home some goods from their market but I did a bad job of reading the fine print (menu items only). Anyway, I went with the Greek beef/lamb gyro which was very good. I also ordered a Wilson sandwich (chicken, falafel, lettuce, tomato, onion, olives, hummus, tahini and hot sauce), a side of pita and hummus and a couple pieces of walnut baklava to take home. The hummus is great. Creamy in texture with nutty notes. The Wilson special is sitting in the fridge until later but if the chicken/falafel platters that I saw coming out while I was there are any indication, I won't have disappoint. Fresh food at reasonable prices. If you're complaining about a lack of A/C or the staff's "attitude' (the latter of which I didn't experience at all) then you're paying attention to the wrong details. Will be returning.

I really wanted to like this place. It's the perfect mix for a cool chill restaurant: outdoors, live island music, Jamaican food and BYOB. In fact, I love that that they're winning the battle again the Symphony House's noise complaints. What I found instead was a BYOD that charges a corkage fee, has nearly non-existent service and phenomenal food poisoning the morning after. After not getting wine glasses for 20 minutes and having my waiter promise a couple times that someone would be by with glasses, I went inside to get my own glasses. I can't think of a better reason to have a corkage fee than to have customers retrieve their own glasses. I should have gathered my group and left after the scene I saw in the kitchen. The majority of servers were hanging around the kitchen eating plates of food, talking and generally seemed to be hiding from customers. Our glasses eventually came, as did the food. Silverware came along a little later. I wish the silverware never arrived. The food was epically bad. The goat roti was filled with meat still attached to bone pieces. The same goes for the jerk chicken. How lazy do you have to be to not butcher the bones out of goat? The whole experience was a little comical and and very gross but nothing compared to the amazing gift of food poisoning I had the next morning. It is such a shame because, with a little effort, the restaurant could be a really cool special place to enjoy good food and music in the open air.

We stopped by here with friends who live in the area. Very yum!!! The waiter was very helpful in helping us decide on our lunch choices. It was my husband's first time eating Vietnamese food, and although he was admittedly apprehensive, he loved it and definitely wants to return.

The chicken tikka masala was really good. It was my favourite type of indian food. My family really loved it. We took the chicken tikka masala with rice and butter naan. I rate it 5 because the food was very delicious and the service was great.

Boy am i glad they opened in Chinatown. I work a few blocks away and they are awesome. Their Drunken Noodles (order it spicy) are out of this world. I also had a spicy soup and that was really good too. I usually order Pad Thai, but I have been hooked on their Drunken Noodles w/ chicken for the past two months. BTW...if you do not like spicy food, do not order it spicy; it is extremely spicy!!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I love Indian food and especially love having it when I'm in new locations. I'm here on business and looked up this restaurant. When I got there there was a young girl to greet me and seat me. I ordered my meal and since I regularly eat Indian I knew what I wanted. My food came out with in a regular amount of time. What I received didn't seem like what I normally order and in fact looked completely different then any time I have ever ordered it anywhere else. I decided to keep it because I do like to try new things and to give it a whirl. What made it awkward for me was that even though I told her that it was fine and I would try it she still sent over the chef. I didn't want that bc I was still going to give it a whirl. I told him I was happy to try something new since I'm sure each family or interpretation of this dish can vary. I had my dinner which was good but not what I was craving. Nonetheless by this point I would have said 4 stars but then the server came over asked if I wanted a box. I told her no thank you bc I was from out of town and had no where for it. After that she left and never came back for a significant amount of time and not until after I asked a different girl for my check. Finally she came to the table and I paid for my meal. Her demeanor was just very dismissive. Upon leaving the restaurant the girls did say goodbye. I would grade the restaurant on a whole from beginning to end including service with C as average.

Food was great! Island shrimp pizza, chicken Philly wrap, and spicy chicken pita. The service was horrible from the moment we walked in the door!!! We were not greeted with a smile; we were spoken at and directed to our table. The restaurant was not properly staffed. People around us left and they had never even received drinks. The person who brings out the food, reached over me with a pizza and knocked a glass of water all over my son's lap. She got a napkin, but didn't bring an apology!! And she never told our server what happened!! They brought the wrong food to my husband and argued that it was right. Hmmmm...

I wandered in, as I am new to the area, and ordered take-out (a lunch special - came to 9.95 plus tax). Next time I will call ahead or maybe dine in. Took 11 minutes to get the food (was told 15 - so that was great!). Chicken pad thai was a tad greasy but good and a large portion. Standard American-Thai loaded with sugar, which I happen to like from time to time. Tulip dumplings were good but unremarkable. Thankfully they were steamed and not deep-fried. I would definitely come back for lunch, but this is still not the greatest Thai food. Pensylvania - even the great city of Philadelphia still has yet to find me a good thai place. The one in Bala is OK (Chang Mai?), and the one in University used to be good. The Little Thai Market in Reading terminal Market is the best I have gotten. The 2 pseudo-Thai places in Media both suck. Sorry, but they do. So for Suburban Thai? Thai Orchid is looking like my new place. The 2 ladies serving were lovely and courteous. Super easy parking (and you can head to Giant afterward to shop.) Next time I will do my litmus test of Tom Kha. See you in about a week!

Really good place with outstanding tasty food. A HUGE menu with good prices. They will alter the spice to your liking on any of their dishes. I found the service t o be very friendly and the overall prices are with the value of each dish. We defiantly will be going back

Ordered online and had a fabulous dinner! Crispy honey chicken was amazing and the chicken tikka was done to perfection! So happy to have such a fabulous restaurant close by. Perfect spice as ordered. Definitely ordering again. Can't wait to try something new.

My first Pho experience! I decided to give this place a try after driving past it for the last few months and always wondering. After initially embarrassing myself and ordering some Pho (Foe instead of Fuh), I received a plate with three egg rolls and dipping oil and a giant bowl of steaming Pho. I ordered the beef broth with round steak and beef brisket pieces. The giant bowl of Pho was accompanied by a plate of fresh veggies (basil, cilantro, jalapenos, lime wedge and bean sprouts) to add at my discretion Before digging in, I took a taste of just the broth. Amazing. I know this is going to sound silly, but it just tasted so complex, like a lot of time went into it. I started adding some of the herbs and veggies and a big squeeze of lime juice, then dug into the rice noodles. You can't be shy here, folks. You ARE going to slurp a lot and, if you're super unskilled with chopsticks like me, potentially get some broth on your shirt. It's totally worth it, though. Filling and delicious. Great first experience, will definitely be back.
Went here for the first time and was very pleased! Best Thai place hands down. Got the pad Thai and thai see ew and both were super delicious and fresh! This is a must if looking for great Thai food.

I've been meaning to try this spot for awhile now. I went yesterday for the first time and now I can say that the best tacos I have ever had were from a food truck on Drexel's campus. The best part is that it's cheap too!!!

Excellent authentic indian food ever !! Must visit if anyone craves for indian food .. Worth the visit and good service too .. Curries and biryani were excellent ! Mango custard dessert was a treat to taste buds !
Great Florida oysters at a great price, the local beer was cold and tasty and the waiter was funny and nice, plus you are right on the gulf, what's not to like!?

Good Indian food. We had the chicken Tika masala and the lamb vindaloo. We had the food "hot" and it was quite manageable. Also the garlic naan is covered in plenty of fresh garlic. Re service was good but then again it wasn't crowded. I would come again.

The food was excellent! We had squid salad, crab rolls, dumplings, pad Thai, and lad ma and every bite was delicious! While the outside of this restaurant doesn't look like much, the sit-down portion of the restaurant is beautifully decorated and comfortable. What struck me most about my visit there yesterday was how fantastic the staff was! I went with a group that included my mom, who sometimes has trouble seeing and getting around easily. The waitress took my mother's arm and led her to the table as if it were her own mother. The wait staff was attentive and kept our drinks full, and one waiter dropped by a couple times to make some jokes with us. What a fantastic restaurant!!
I was so surprised the line was short for me today to be able to get the food. You get so much food for 10 bucks and it's so delicious. You have to try it when you have time to wait in the line.

Not much verity . Bread was not avaiable . After calling many times it come after 5 min and again wait for 5 min for second time .. i think railway station tea is better .. do think twice before gonto that place .

Super friendly service. Amazingly diverse set of menu options. Grab a smoothie of your choice and a halal salad. All the smoothies and salads can be made vegan or non-vegan and they have regular meat options like chicken and beef. A great spot.

Its a new Indian restaurant which serves traditional as well as innovative attempts - silver chards in dosa!! The good news is that it actually tasted great! What we ate: We had Bollywood Masala Dosa which was basically your regular masala dosa, Farmers Market Dosa which had chards, bell peppers and onion and we also got Indian Railways cutlet which was a better tasting cousin of the original railways cutlet! The table next to us had the 3 foot paper dosa which sat along the length of their table. Ambience and Service: Definitely room for improvement. Price: Worth it. Overall, the place needs a revamp - in terms of decor (even though it looks like they just opened! ) and service needs to be organized and faster but their food makes up for any flaw in their setup.
Nice addition to the local dining scene. Good menu with seafood specials which we liked. Very good service and ambiance.

yelp book club ROCKS!! for one, it's introduced me to some great books (and yelp friends!) that i may not have otherwise been inspired to read on my own. and two, with our ever-changing location, i've had the opportunity to venture in to a couple places off my beaten path. last nite's meet-up to discuss 'a confederacy of dunces' landed our small group in graduate hospital's la va cafe. it's a neighborhood i don't often find myself in, but la va is reason enough to come back. to be fair, all that i sampled on this particular evening was a delicious peppermint latte. tho pricey ($4+), it is on par with the similar beverage at starbucks, only this one was served in a real mug (to-go cups are, of course, also available) with the added bonus of a lovely leaf design in the foam. little touches like that make me smile. some other book clubbers nibbled on tasty looking brownies and danishes, but i was, pathetically, so busy trying to finish up the last 20 pages that food wasn't exactly my priority. when i come back, i might just have to get myself a bowl of soup, which, according to their menu, varies daily but is ALWAYS VEGETARIAN. ooooo-weeee! whoa! the cafe is large (esp for a non-chain), well lit and conducive to most anything one would want to do in such a space. while our chatty book club dominated the couch corner on this winter wednesday nite, la va was boppin - with a menagerie of people (ie, no hipster haven here!) reading, studying, drawing, conversing, eating... this was not a library-esque setting where you felt like silence was golden. those who wanted their peace plugged in their headphones, and the rest of us enjoyed the good tunes playing in the background.

Wonderful experience and food. I discovered this restaurant on Yelp and it certainly lived up to the reviews! Although far from our neighborhood and usual hangouts in south Philly, I will definitely venture up there again. We went as a party of 6 at 8pm on a Friday night and although the restaurant was nearly empty there was good music and friendly staff that made the place feel lively. The restaurant is run and owned by a father and son team. We ate oxtail that the father told us he started preparing at 4 am that morning. And let me tell you, it was AMAZING -- as was the curry chicken, the traditional trini vegetables and the plantains. This is definitely a hidden gem that you'll want to get to before it gets too difficult to get a table!

I wish I'd known about this place a long time ago. It is unfortunately hidden in a strip center off Olive St. that cannot be seen from the road. And I guess no one generally just sees a place on the road and says that they have to try it. But it might have been on my radar earlier. As it is, I had a restaurant.com certificate that brought me here. So many of the Indian restaurants around me suffer from a sad inability to provide decent service, as you can see from reviews on Yelp. However, this place knows how to be attentive, provide help with picking dishes, and provide a pleasant experience. It also has a bit more refined interior that is just relaxing. We were very happy with the food, too. The wife and daughter order chai teas. Our waiter (the owner, I believe) told us it was being fresh brewed, so it took a bit to arrive. Good smooth taste, though, when it did come. Our waiter also asked if they wanted a refill, which my daughter did. I wasn't sure if that would be an additional charge, since I seemed to remember that other places only provided one cup. However, there was not, so that was good. Shoot, I'd have ordered it and drunk three or four cups if I'd known. I liked how the menu provided clear and detailed descriptions of the all the items. I know what my regular options comprise, but this really helps when a non-South Asian wants to try something different. Even with the (many) bread options there is quite a bit of difference that I wouldn't have known. Our order: Nan bread - good, standard, with a light oil coating Roti bread - whole wheat; was denser & dryer than the nan, but to be expected Chicken tikka masala - they did a good job, with a pleasant flavor, very tender & quality chicken, no heat at all Palak paneer - excellent pieces of cheese that were springy without being rubbery and were also savory, creamed spinach was fairly dense which I liked - don't want no runny stuff Lamb korma - the waiter helped me pick this (I wanted more lamb and not so much sauce); this had tender cubes, just as described on the menu, which were quite flavorful; the sauce and vegetables also were flavorful, with just a hint of spiciness for interest I know some people have complained on the reviews about the mildness of the dishes here, but I don't see the problem. The menu clearly describes which are mild and which are hot or very hot. Perhaps they wanted some of the mild dishes to be spicier. but I like flavor, not heat, and I thought there was a good balance here.

My boyfriend and I went there Saturday night for dinner. The restaurant is very clean and the service was excellent, the waiter being very attentive. I had the chicken pad thai and my boyfriend had the beef with black pepper sauce. The presentation of the meals was excellent and the food was of excellent quality. This place is definitely a keeper !!

I eat here probably about once a week (I live on the same block) and never get tired of it. I eat Vietnamese all over the city and this isn't far in terms of quality from what you can get at Pho Ha or Nam Phuong. They had a couple kinks in first couple months open but that should be expected for any new business and now I find them really consistent. I always order extra broth for takeout and am a big fan of the papaya salad with shrimp and pork. Great addition to the neighborhood!

Love the fresh food and pleasant service at Hummingbird. I was referred here for some good jerk chicken. I was not disappointed! I have also had the Jerk salmon salad which is delish and Oxtails which are my favorite. I believe they are now open on Saturdays. I have never eaten at the restaurant. I order to go. It's not a fancy place inside but has always been neat and clean when I was there. Can't wait to go back to Trenton again! I will definitely pay them a visit!
Best Indian food in west county! Great lunch time buffet with a variety of Indian favorites. Best tandoori chicken that I have ever had. The owner is supper friendly too.
we had the chicken souvlaki and the gyro for dinner - excellent food. Service was also excellent. We had a great dining experience.
Very good Authentic Puerto Rican food. The Mofongo was fresh to order and the Pernil was great my family enjoyed a great meal and awesome Prices

Quaint BYOB on the river. Dined there on numerous occasions and never been disappointed! Fabulous filet pasta Gorgonzola! Nice specials offer additions to the menu for frequent diners. Accept reservations.

Abundant portions of well-seasoned food in a lovely dining room. My husband and I have shared an appetizer sampler for dinner. We also have ordered separate meals and had enough leftovers for two more meals! The rose water and pistachio ice cream should not be missed. A welcome addition to the north side of town!

this is our go-to spot in philly when we've got a craving for simple vietnamese food. 1 order of pho, 1 order of the bun w/ pork/eggroll, 1 lemonade, 1 pink jelly drink. DIVINE!! cheap and delicious, that's how we like it. the grilled pork is super flavorful, i def recommend.

I've been coming here for years and I am still trying to find a better Indian restaurant- hasn't happened ! The Navratan Korma is an absolute delight !! POA is not as spicy as other Indian restaurants but they certainly make up for it in flavor. The staff is wonderful and the food is out of this world - even my one year old loves it !
Everything was amazing! Especially the naan bread was so fresh! My only complaint was that the samosas were not included on the $11 buffet.

The food is delicious. It's not fancy, it just tastes really good and isn't very expensive, either. The curry goat is delicious and has actually big pieces of goat (not lamb, goat). The food actually seems closer to Indo-Caribbean cuisine than traditional Indian... but what do I know about Indian food? Nothing, really. Except that I love it and I love it when they make it.

Viet Pho shares a dining area with Port O Subs in the run down Shoppers Square Mall. I had a couple vietnamese sandwiches with bbq pork....very fresh and tasty. Good value too compared to the hordes that kept going to Port O Subs. I didnt understand why people wouldnt try a local joint, especially when the sandwiches were much fresher and tastier. Owner was very friendly. Had a banana smoothie that was phenomenal. Not the best vietnamese I've had, but pretty good.
Food was great. We got the chicken vermicelli, shaken steak, and spring rolls. Very open and bright. Nice atmosphere and sweet staff.

Enjoy some really good food while it lasts! A city air quality inspector stopped by today while I was there and told Gus that there were numerous complaints about the smoke from his cart. She took down all his operator/cart license info and took lots of pictures of the smoke from all sides. Said she wasn't sure how they'd proceed, whether it would be forcing him to switch from charcoal to gas or shutting him down completely. Can't imagine the chicken without that smoky taste.

good food, good chai. Place is dirty, bathroom is disgusting.. try to avoid it if possible. prompt service but lady at the till seems to be cranky all the time. No smiles at all. Pretty much "just pay n get out" attitude. its not just one particular person, its pretty much whoever is on that till. This seems to be the issue only in this location. I have been to the one downtown and whyte ave n people there are very nice and polite.
Great Indian food! I have ordered take out several times and have never been disappointed! The portions are generous and well priced. I highly recommend the vegetable samosa and the Baingan Bharta!

PHOlicious. Love the chicken pho from Basil Fusion. I usually go here on my lunch break. Everyone is very attentive and nice. Food comes out quick, so you don't wait too long. Also the restaurant is really cute and cozy inside!
Always enjoy having lunch here! Staff is very attentive and friendly. Great selection of food and the naan is fresh.

We love it here. The food is excellent and the hospitality top notch. Tom is a super owner/host. We've brought everyone we know here and all have enjoyed it. We also really enjoy the atmosphere but also do frequent take out when a night in is call for.

What an utter disgrace! I had high hopes bc the great reviews.. But was I wrong, the curry was too soupy & tasted like sewer water.. YUM!! Won't be coming again, but on the plus side I'll be shitting out this food ASAP

I've been eating at this place for about 3 years now and I love it. Would give 4.5 stars if I could. Reasons I love it: The owners are sweet. I love the remodel they did awhile back! Their King's soup knocks my socks off. Their fresh and fried spring rolls are also really great (i've not tried the duck). Love their coconut soup. Love their tamarind wings. Love their pad se ew. The Thai cut fish is also delicious. Good atmosphere and they let you relax and hang out with your friends & enjoy your meal instead of rushing you out the door. Reasons I didn't give 5 stars: The last time I came in there was a strange smell in the dining room area. :/ I brought someone here after talking it up and everything he got truly wasn't great. The chicken satay was really small and tasted of fish. The service was very nice but we were seated way in the far back corner and there were long periods of time where no one checked on us. His food wasn't spicy at all and he asked for 4/5 spice level. I ate it and I was fine with it--normally a 4/5 spice level would kill me. He got a bad bite of something in his salad and these things combined ruined the dining experience for us both. Will judge on the whole and not this one time, but I hope that this was a one-off. Certainly hasn't been my experience previously. to note: Cash only, BYO

My seafood fettucini was excellent. The escarole and rice sides were bland--and this is coming from an Italian girl who loves escarole. I think my expectations were just really high because I've only heard amazing things about this place. I would be willing to give them another try, especially considering they're super close to me and a BYOB.
Really delicious and creative with their food! Great customer service and very friendly. The fish taco taste amazing.

TLDR: wouldn't recommend take out or the kabobs, not a great experience with either. I decided to try this place as take out after seeing that it fills up quick to dine-in. Just wanted something easy and requested the Greek salad with greens and grilled chicken. She told me they can't add grilled chicken to the salad (weird, but ok?) but she'd put on a side of kabobs. I showed up and found out my side of kabobs was $14 ($4 less than the platter, so I'm assuming they deducted for not including the sides?). I was surprised... I expected a side to be smaller and definitely less expensive. The kabobs weren't great (Not worth the $14+tax) but the salad was good. Ultimately I was most put off by the fact that my take out was not rung up anywhere but just told to another server who then pulled out a wad of cash and gave me incorrect change. I realized after having been home for an hour or so, she must've too, because when I called back she knew who I was and told me she'd be happy to give me my remaining change. She also apologized that I was confused about the way overpriced side of kabobs. It was nice that they fixed the mistake and gave me my correct change but overall that was enough of an unpleasant experience that I won't be back.

Been here on multiple occasions and love the food. The thought of a steaming hot bowl of delicious pho on a snowy day sounded perfect until we got there and the place has no HEAT! They have little space heaters around but every time the door opened, the whole place became a freezer. The door opens a lot due to more take out traffic than dine inners. It was just to frigid so we had to leave. I didn't want to due to wanting the food but there was no way we would have been able to comfortably enjoy our meals.

I love Thai food, so it is dangerous that Asian Chef is so close to my home. I've visited Asian Chef twice since the ownership change a couple months ago. The service is always excellent. I cannot eat gluten without being in a lot of pain and hating myself for a few days, and I am always a little afraid to eat out at Asian restaurants because my requests seem to get lost in translation. However, I can enjoy my meal without worrying when I eat here because the waiters are very attentive and willing to ask the chef any questions I have about what goes into each dish. My favorite dish here is red curry with tofu. It is very filling and always the perfect spice level for me. I've also tried several of their sushi options, which always taste fresh and look nice. I'll definitely keep coming back here, and maybe I'll branch out a little from my usual red curry.

We love this place! We've been fans for years. The ambiance is great and the service is excellent. They also accomodate take-out orders. Wetried another Thai Orchid in Devon (we thought maybe they were by the same owners?) but we strongly prefer the Blue Bell one. We love just about everything we've tried at this restaurant (except maybe the desserts...) I only knocked off a star because the last few times I've ordered the royal crabcakes they've had a bit of shell in them and the quality of the lump crab meat seems to have declined (more shredded bits of crab and fewer big, juicy lumps). I would have preferred they raise the price and not compromise the quality of my favorite dish.

My favorite BYOB in Philly! I must have eaten here 20 times now. It's unpretentious and just perfect. I hope they never change a thing. Favorites: grilled octopus, pil pil shrimp, soft shell crab, grilled whole fish, bluefish with pasta, almond cake, and really anything else on the menu.

Excellent Indian buffet. Not always 100% consistent so they get a 4 instead of 5 star but usually wonderful food. Today we had a cabbage dish, several other vegetarian, dishes such as spinach with paneer cheese, vegetable korma, chana masala, curried eggs and dal. Other dishes were lamb biriyani, goat, butter chicken and tandoori chicken. There was naan, papdam, rice, potato pakora and a lovely carrot dessert. All this with several sauces and condiments. The quality is very good. My only disappointment is they used to serve Chai with the buffet. I miss it as it was a wonderful accompaniment. I also like that they mix it up and don't always serve the same stuff. For all you spice lovers this is the place. Not too much not too little.

After coming here several times in the past week or two...I have gotta say that Bui's really does deserve 5 stars. You can text them your order and have it ready for pick-up . So convenient! Especially if there is a line.

Interesting menu. Fresh ingredients and preparation. Cakes were awesome. Like all good independent local joints, several special offerings not on menu. Quiet place for a light breakfast/lunch. I'll be back when I'm near Irvington.

this used to be our favorite vegan/Thai cafe when visiting Santa Barbara. this time we ordered tofu and veggie curry with rice. it was mostly tofu and just a couple bites of veggies and the curry was not rich but watery and not that good... won't be coming back

The exterior does not do justice for the interior nor the nice Pho inside. Decent interior of the restaurant and a nice older woman who does all the front work while the food is brought out by a gentleman manning the kitchen. I ordered the Pho for $9.50 that came with brisket, beef round, beef meatball and tendon. Came out in a HUGE bowl plus the accompaniment of bean sprouts, jalapeno sliced pepper, lime, and Asian basil (?). Everything was fresh. On each table/booth is your soy/hoisin/pepper sauces. Everything was really good except one of the meats, I think it might have been the brisket, seemed like it was overcooked as compared to the beef round which was that nice beefy taste and texture. The most important thing is the broth (I am no expert on Pho broth) but I thought it had some nice deep flavor. Overall very good, I rather enjoyed it and will most likely will be back.

Don't get me wrong. The food here is the best Vietnamese food you're gonna find in a Nashville restaurant. But hear me out. With an organization at my university we have spent THOUSANDS of dollars over the past few years ordering food for various events, enduring mediocre service. This year was the final straw. Is it too much to ask someone to be docile on the phone? I'm not asking for world class service, but when you snap at me "What do you want?" and treat me as if I'm inferior, I'll go ahead and take my business elsewhere. Eat at Kien Giang if you like rude people and good food, but that's just not for me. There are other options.

I've been wanting to try this spot out. An Indian restaurant in Mt. J.. I was a little unsure. Was really surprised at the reasonable prices on their lunch menu. For under $10 - you can get the soup of the day (man.. wanted to drink this stuff), an appetizer, an entree with rice and naan. The food was really flavorful and a nice large portion. The waiter helped me make a few selections, and I was really happy with the recommendations. He was really pleasant and never let my water get low. I was in and out in under 30 minutes, which makes this a great spot for lunch. Definitely excited to eat here again on my lunch break.

So far, this has been by far the best Asian food around. I have eaten there and gotten take out many times and have yet to be dissapointed. Whenever we go in, everybody working there are always friendly and happy to serve you. The best thing is that you can choose what type of food you want. Chinese, got it, Japanese, no problem, Thai, sure, Vietnamese, of course. Whatever you are in the mood for, they will make it. Whenever we are feeling lazy, we order delivery. They are always there in the time they say or earlier and the order is never messed up. They even are smart enough to not put the sushi with the hot food. Whether you go in and bring a bottle of wine, or stay at home and eat on the couch, you will not be disappointed.

Came by to try out the bun bo hue after reading lots of positive reviews. Yes, the decor and space is outdated, but it was clean to my eye, and apparently quite popular as it was pretty busy with both Asians and Caucasians over a recent weekday lunch hour. They only offer one size for the bun bo hue. A pot of tea came out right away, soon after followed by a plate of sprouts, Thai basil, and a lime wedge. The noodle soup didn't take too long to come out, piled high with purple and green cabbage, sliced onions, and green onions. Not too much spicy oil floating on the top. I ate about half of the bowl and then added more spicy oil from the jar at the table - unfortunately, it is NOT the same stuff so it ended up altering the taste in an unfavourable way :( Anyway, prior to that, the broth was pretty good, though not as lemongrass-y as I had been expecting. There is an excellent noodle to meat/broth ratio (whereas Xu Hue, my current favourite bun bo hue place, has too many noodles). The meats were mostly brisket-type beef, and a variety of homemade meatballs/meatloaf. Good, but I think I prefer the meats at Xu Hue better. All in all, it hasn't replaced Xu Hue as my favourite, but I would come back, and make sure to ask for extra spicy bun bo hue next time :)

After reading multiple good reviews about this truck and then seeing it constantly pop up in my Highest Rated list on Yelp, my brother and I decided to make our way out the Falafel Truck for lunch... Food: 4.5 stars Its a food truck, so how high quality can the food be?? This is why the truck is so unique. The ingredients are high quality, well prepared and served in generous portions. Word to the first timers about ordering... There are 2 plates on the menu. Falafel Platter or Falafel Platter with Chicken. There is no menu up or signs indicating what they serve. The chicken is really a home-run. Made with a great marinade, they shine. Service: 2.5 stars The owner of the truck and chef is a little different. He is very forward and loves to engage in conversation and banter. It can be a little excessive at times but its entertaining, too. His service was prompt and on point.
