Location: 3.0 stars 20th and Market St. on the North side of Market. You'll see the smoke billowing from the truck... Price: 4.0 stars $8 per platter and you only can get 1 per customer if its busy. Ambiance: 3.5 stars The truck itself is unique, covered in plants and garlic clovers. Its obviously a truck so its grab your food and go. If you aren't taking it back to work, I would recommend a walk to Rittenhouse Park for lunch outside. **Overall: 3.5 stars The food is delicious and its quick. Great for the work crowd and those that can get out to the truck for lunch. Will definitely go back again.

I feel very foolish for returning to the "Hut" for yet another disappointing dinner. I like to try a place at least twice before I completely write them off. This establishment tricked me three times. The first visit was for takeout jerk chicken that was actually semi frozen in the center, though cooked through. It had obviously been reheated perhaps from the day before. The second was a Sunday where we waited for over an hour for our appetizers of overly dressed BQ wings, soggy coconut shrimp, and an incompetent server. Entrees followed 30 min. later with bony chicken, hard, not-so-sweet-plaintains and tasteless rice. On our third visit, we went Labor day nite, after a great weekend at the beach. We enjoyed the music, but again waited for an hour for our appetizers. There were three servers running around like chickens with their heads cut off, inefficient to say the least. They were working too hard for the 30 guests or so in the outside area. Appetizers arrived of ceviche(almost completely devoid of seafood), soggy wings. Sir may we have some forks at the very least?? Napkins...please? Jerk chicken for dinner was just as disappointing as the other visits, lukewarm, very bony. The Hut chops up the chicken, bone and all, which causes the multiple bone fragments. I was seriously afraid of chomping/swallowing the splintery bones. We paid, after we finally were able to chase down our server, and left without finishing our meals. The server tried really hard to take care of everyone, but just didnt have the forethought to bring what was needed from the kitchen and save himself a trip before food is served. I attribute this to lack of experience and planning. Why not have utensils/napkins/water pitchers OUTSIDE where the guests are? I LOVE jerk chicken, and this is a far cry from what I have sampled in the Islands. We love the IDEA of the Jerk Hut,outside,live music,casual setting, bucket of beers shared with friends, but the food really is terrible, and overpriced for what it is, and the service needs some serious work.
Food is delicious but the service is super slow. Don't bother with the cocktails as they are overpriced and syrupy. This place gets crowded around 6pm so get there before then, if you can.

I've been here twice and was favorably impressed both times. Good service and excellent Tonkatsu (pork) ramen. So good, in fact, that I had it both times and was glad I did. Last night the charming bartender made lychee cocktails that were the perfect compliment. A friend who apparently knows her ramen recommended this place; both times I've been I met her here. She knows the aforementioned bartender and their friendly banter made dinner even more fun. Also, the decor is spot on.
My family and I have been regulars here for years, and the fact that we keep coming back and even had our Christmas dinner here is pretty much all I have to say. A+ mango lassis, too.

It's a total shame !!!!! I wanted to absolutely love this place since I'm a TOTAL pho addict!!!! I go to the wonderful Vietnam Palace in China Town a few times a week, so much so that they don't even give us a menu anymore. They just say hi & bring us our regular order. Regrettably iPho Fairmount couldn't hold a candle to Vietnam Palace... If it were as good I'd probably eat there daily since its around the corner & wouldn't have to deal with the nightmare of China Town parking. Despite the fact that our server was amazingly good looking the eye candy couldn't make up for the flavorless, bland food... If I had a dollar for the amount of times I've said "Fairmount needs a Pho place" I'd be retired, unfortunately this place was not what any of us have been hoping for in our neighborhood... The Pho broth tasted oily & the noodles mushy & had the consistency of a glue stick - just blaaaaaah!!!! They "forgot" to bring us bean sprouts, jalapeño, mint leaves, lime etc for our pho... Aaaaaawwww! I think the team from iPho needs to go eat at Vietnam Palace & take a "mint leave" outta their book!!!! I genuinely hope iPho gets it together it would be fantastic for Fairmount!!! I would have given my first visit one star but giving an extra star for our good looking waiter!

Adored this experience my first Ethiopian meal and I will be sure to try Zagol again the owner personally served us she was a delightful and cultured woman who even served us right before closing. We brought our 2 small children who adored the decor and friendly server. The food was delicious an awesome experience definitely Reno's hidden jewel.
I love this place. I always get the summer rolls and clay pot dinner. So good. I got the shrimp clay pot with veggies and rice.

Went here several weeks ago and loved everything. Fast friendly service. The beef patties and jerk chicken were excellent. We haven't had Jamaican food this good since the last time we were in negril. Will go back again soon .

I eat here for lunch almost every week, (Drexel Hill)., having the buffet. Always tasty, with plenty of selection. Food is a bit spicy, not just hot. Probably why I like it so much. Quite a bargain, with a free order of Nan included.
Good Greek. Not great, but decent. No atmosphere to speak of and probably used a lot for local take out!
Try everything on their menu! Food is great, has flavor and good presentation. The ambiance is nice. Will definitely be visiting this place again.

Tandoor India has a great Indian buffet with all the essentials at a great price. They're constantly bringing out fresh trays -- granted, they sort of have to, with the popularity of the buffet -- so you never have to worry about getting old, cold, or dried out dishes. My favorite dish is the saag paneer. I could just keep loading my plate up with the stuff for hours, honestly. But the naan -- I love exploring the great breads of the world -- the naan is deliciously oily, and it you can pile whatever you want on top; it won't get too soggy. At dinner, I believe the buffet is $9.95, and it includes a choice of desserts and coffee.

Love the AUTHENTIC eritrean food here (if you don't want to try that they also have frid chicken, chicken fingers, fries, fried fish etc.) the owner is always so nice and pleasant as well as the staff come for an afternoon CITY SPECIAL a shot of whiskey and a beer for four bucks!

This place is very small, but it's cute and really clean. They're located in IV, but surprisingly make a good bowl of pho! The pieces of beef are already cooked in the broth, which isn't how Pho Tai is supposed to be... but I'll let it slide because the beef is actually nice and tender. If you don't live in IV, it's kind of an inconvenience to eat here because there's no parking (it IS Isla Vista, after all).

I love Indian food and I found their food good especially the rice but the spice overwhelmed the dish. I couldn't taste anything else. Too many peas in the muttar paneer. But good other wise. I had the mild spice. I can't imagin the hot.

Great new find in St. Louis! The nihari and chicken briyani are excellent! This place is definitely geared more towards take-out than dine-in, but both options are available. This Mom and Pop shop is a hidden gem in St Louis, and deserves more attention. I'd have to give this and Lal Qila in Ballwin, MO to be the best Indian-Pakistani cuisine in the STL area.

We were not planning on going to Kabob and Grill tonight but we passed it on our way to our destination restaurant that ended up being closed for Labor Day, so we reluctantly gave it a try. We are SO HAPPY that we did!!! Best Indian food around! Tiffin and Ekta were our go to places for Indian when we lived in the city, but this place is WAY better!!! Service was friendly and fantastic, food was delicious, prices were unbelievably reasonable and it came out so quickly....which was great because we had a baby and toddler in tow :) Our waiter even surprised our daughter with a mango drink! You don't find too many restaurants like this one anymore. The only downside is that it's a very tiny place to eat-in, but I would suggest giving it a try because you won't understand how wonderfully nice the people are unless you do so! Also, it's cash only so be prepared. We can not wait to eat here again! One of our new favorite finds after moving to the burbs!

Never would have known about this place if I hadn't been looking for recently opened restaurants. It was nearly empty on a tuesday night, but the food was amazing. The fried calimari was some of the best I've ever had, and the sizzling sole fish entre was incredible. I would drink a glass of that basil sauce. One of my friends had the roast duck, which he rated excellent, and the other had the vegetarian pho, which he said was some of the best in town. The poke taco appetizers were good, but not in the same class as the rest of what we had.

It's worth it! Mazzah is not near as good as this place. Hummus authentic as you would get Israel. Chicken kabobs are seasoned so amazing that you could not recreate at home and the cilantro sauce on side will please foodies.
It's really one of my favorite places but you never answer the phone and you're losing a customer because of it

If wish I had an option to give more than 5 stars!! Best ever chaat and lassi!! The owner is a gem of a person and will talk you through the best combinations of food and will make your experience an unforgettable event. We were given extra lassi and sweets over and above what we ordered. I would love to come here again and again. I wish him all the success and more mint-lassi stories like the one he told us ;-)

Awesome new spot in the Upenn area. When you walk in, there's a nice bar with a good variety of drinks. To the right is the dining area which is nice and cozy which is where I sat. From there, there's also a karaoke room which had pretty up to date music when going through the music selection. The food variety is a lot of Chinese food you'd typically expect but they also have some more Americanized appetizers and they also have Sczaun and Dim Sum as well. The good thing about this Dim Sum menu is they have 4 variations of Soup Dumplings which is everyone's favorite. I ended up getting the Shanghai Steamed Pork Soup Dumplings and Shanghai Crabmeat and Pork Soup Dumplings with a friend. We ended up getting the Shrimp with Walnut and the Jumbo Shrimp with Chilli Pepper. The walnut shrimp is exactly what you'd expect which is one of my favorite things to order when available. The jumbo shrimps are pretty huge and are spicy but not to the point where you can't finish it because it's too hot. Food was presented well, tasted great and most importantly(for me) filled me up leaving me satisfied. I'll def be here again for Soup Dumplings and to try new things on the menu. Def worth coming through. Pics of the menu and the food I ordered posted in my pictures.

Sticky chicken wings is a must. Rice with crispy hen is recommended. Grilled pork bun worth trying. Do not understand why panda waffle is green, looks unsavory but tastes not bad. When you order rice, you can exchange white rice for fried rice, much more tasty.

A great find here in Tampa and located so close to Bushe Gardens. We came here after a full day in the amusement park at around 7pm. Plenty of seating at the time and we ordered our food right away. The interior look more like a fast food restaurant with pretty nice cushion seatings but they do bring out the orders to you once its ready.The food was levels above what you might find in a typical fastfood restaurant. Especially the rice and beans plate I felt was cooked so well that I wanted more. Even though I thought the Fried Fish was a little dry but everything else we've tried were really good. Unfortunately we didn't get to try their classic Gyro as that definitely seem to be one of the favorites. Even the baklava that was just sitting out in the fridge was really delicious I certainly think that was freshly made on the same day. The prices were reasonable and the portions generous. The food came out practically within minutes which was much appreciated since we were ravenous after a long day and dying for some sit down food. Overall a great place that I would recommend to anyone visiting Bushe Gardens if you want to give Greek food a try. Its definitely well worth a visit and the interiors are modern with really delicious food

I love this place. I've gone twice at lunch. The first time I stood in the loooooong line and saw an advertisement for online ordering. Best thing ever! Both times I got the chicken salad with tahini sauce. The pickles and cucumber/cilantro/tomatoes combo is a fresh yummy combo. And the baklava is magic. I prefer the original over the salted caramel. The pita is pure magic! The staff is friendly and everything was fresh and at the right temperature. I not a fan of the fries as they're more like Chips but great for dipping your hummus. The first time I went the music track was excellent. This last time I didn't hear any music. Bring back the contemporary r&b! I've planned to pop in once a month for lunch and I ALWAYS carry but, the food is just that yummy. I got my dressing on the side and had enough for a snack later as I'm not a big eater. Great concept! Only thing missing is shrimp!

There are no shortage of Indian restaurants on this stretch of Ridge Pike. Desi Spice was here first and it will probably survive longer than any of the others. Their food was always spectacular and it continues to be so. The Chicken Saag was wonderful, the Tikka Masala was delicious, and the decor and the service are wonderful. Granted, I'm not Indian - I'm a white guy from Collegeville. Maybe I don't know what I'm eating and can't tell the difference between dosas and biryanis. But I'm judging the entire package here - decor, service, food, quality. In my opinion, this place is top notch.

The restaurant upon entering has a strong stench of mold. Similar to what I have experienced in locations down at the shore after the effects of Sandy. The food was fair and so the service. Their strong suit is items ordered off the Mediterranean menu. But if you have allergies toward mold there are plenty of locations in the area.

Nice authentic Jamaican food right here in delaware county, an area flooded with nothing but pizza places and mediocre italian. even the authentic mexican place in the area serves pizza! lol. The owners here were super friendly and told me about all the different dishes and what went into them. We had the oxtail and the curry goat. both were pretty good with generous portions and it was pretty tasty although I will admit that it was a little hard on my stomach, but I'm gonna attribute that to the fact that I'm not really used to this type of cuisine. I will definitely be back to try some of the other dishes soon Oh, and the fried plantains were amazing. you gotta go if only to get some of these.
Horrible food. Very salty and full of sodium. The two dishes we ordered were straight out of microwave frozen dinner. Will not return
Will say was a pleasant find. Flavors were great and staff was very friendly and helpful. Tom Yum was one of the better I've had anywhere. Would recommend this without hesitation.

Note to self: when you enter restaurant and see harried, rushing, glum-faced waitstaff, turn around, walk away and eat elsewhere. Lesson learned! Two of us dining. We ordered two apps to share and an entree each. One app came soon, the other 20 minutes later. Barely minutes after the 2nd app arrived and we were still enjoying it (or trying to), one entree arrive, just one. A full five minutes later, as entree 1 gets cold (since my companion is gracious enough not to start without me), still no other entree. Waitress rushes by, we manage to catch her eye and ask where other entree is. She says she'll check, but after five minutes more hasn't come back. I get up from table and go to find out. Waitress sees me and look of "uh-oh" comes onto her face because she obviously forgot all about it. She gestures toward manager who starts to give me all sorts of excuses -- "we're so busy, kitchen got backed up, it will be out soon" -- and I say, well, yes, but my companion's dinner is now cold. So she says they'll bring him a new one along with mine. Which she herself does after a few more minutes but then slams it down onto our table, literally slams it down onto the table without a word of apology, no smile, no nothing -- and, by the way, no fork, since the waitress had cleared our forks with the apps. Meanwhile, our empty beer bottles sit on the table throughout the meal, as no staff have the sense to take them away, and a grimy, dirty candle-holder sits there, too, because, when we finally ask about a candle, we're told "we ran out." So, I figure you either walk a block to the dollar store nearby and buy some candles or you take the yucky candle holders off the tables. All in a lousy experience. When entrees finally came, they were adequate, nothing special, same for the apps. Never again. http://www.tripadvisor.com/ShowUserReviews-g60795-d893578-r323391251-Vientiane_Cafe-Philadelphia_Pennsylvania.html#

I ate here today for lunch although I ordered the entree plate of beef shawarma. It was good but unlike the other reviews it didn't rise to greatness. It was served on a medium sized round plate with a ring of hummus along the edge. Not much color or interesting to look at. One thing that I recommend diners to stay away from is the God awful Lebanese Iced Tea. I ordered it on a recommendation from a previous reviewer. It's iced tea with "Rose water". Its an unbelievably strong taste. As if you put very fragrant rose petals in your drink. It's so strong that it fills your nostrils with that fragrance thereby not allowing you to truly getting the flavor of the dish you're eating. I couldn't drink but about a few swallows with my meal. If you're with a group of people and you feel you want to try it....order only one glass and share it. You'll soon see what I'm talking about. The restaurant itself is okay. Nothing fancy but passable.

I had heard this place was pretty good from some friends of mine and being the yelper that I am read some mixed reviews. That being said I wanted to see for myself. Probably one of the worst Vietnemese restaurants I have ever ate in, for sure the worst in Reno. The spring rolls were horrible. Bean Sprouts were half rotten. Soup came out and it was zero flavor outside of all the fat that they never skimmed off the top of the soup. It was literally like a steaming vat of grease. Never going back again.

Rosemary's Grill is a diner which offers a small Mediterranean menu in addition to their diner options. Service was questionable as our waitress was very strange and only helped us now and again. The hostess assisted us most with our meal. I went for lunch and had the Gyro platter which was shredded lamb, tomato, lettuce, onion and tzaitziki with french fries on the side. The gyro was actually quite good and only $7.95.

Decent meal, but not what I expected. Started with Caesar salad that, while it was served with better than average dressing, still came up short because there was not even a hint of anchovy in it. My main dish was a special for tonight, Tilapia and crabmeat with an overbearing tomato sauce that pretty much ruined the subtle flavors I should have been able to taste. The sauce was so in-your-face that it might as well have been on a hot dog. Veggies and potatoes were very good. Our server was sweet and efficient, but her thick accent and limited command of English added annoyance to an already disappointing meal. Had I not gotten a good discount through Groupon, I'd have been pissed. This dinner was not worth the price on the menu, not at all.

Whether or not you've tried Middle Eastern food, definitely come check this place out. Gyro plate can't be beaten, and the falafel and hummus are awesome. Make sure to try their mint lemonade, which is also excellent. They have a hookah smoking section in the back, and have wonderful servers who replace charcoals frequently. When you're done eating and/or smoking, check out the grocery section, where you'll find a large variety of Middle Eastern spices, food products, and tobacco supplies.

I went to Macarons and Goodies a month ago. I mention this for two reasons. 1) If others are like me, they didn't notice the quirky combination of Macaron (French) plus Goodies (English). Although it is respectable use of our two official languages, it may make M&G hard for the unilingual to find on the Web. Secondly, my review being a month old, the store may now have evolved. I was slightly disappointed after my initial visit to M&G. Perhaps it was that I grew up in Montreal a block from Banville Bakery and that patisserie has been imprinted on my soul as the ideal. Perhaps it was the review M&G received in the Journal. That review stated that there is plenty of parking behind the store. That is only partly true. The parking has reserved signs and not for M&G customers. Furthermore, even if there were ample parking, the back door is locked, necessitating a long walk past the notorious Macdonald Lofts to get to the store. The day I visited, there was a snow ban, obliterating what little parking was available. I am disabled and needed to park in an expensive Impark lot where the machine was frozen and didn't work. Inconvenient and would have added to the expense of patronizing M&G. Yes, it is expensive to shop there. I spent $5.50 + GST for a mille feuille and a pistachio eclair, twice as much as at a grocery store near my home. Both were well done but I can't say that the mille feuille gave me twice as much joy as the ones I buy at Andy's IGA. Plus, Andy has plenty of free parking and Vallyview is definitely a cut above M&G's neighbourhood. I only bought the eclair because I wanted two mille feuilles, one for me and one for my wife. The server said that there were more in the freezer but emerged from the back to announce that the one in the display case was the entire inventory. Have you ever tried to cut a mille feuille in half? I want M&G to succeed because Edmonton has a shortage of quality French patisseries but I suggest that you wait a couple of months more and M&G may have their act together.

Dinner was a simple lamb, spicy tomato dish, basmati rice, a chicken samosa and a light, crisp naan. Yes the ambiance is a classic strip mall, a Pakistan/India store/meat counter/restaurant - but I'm not here to impress or be impressed by that . Bonus - a friendly conversation with a local resident, and the lights (and AC) go out toward the end. Woot! Authentic all the way!

We stopped by on Sunday night around 7 and were told that the kitchen was slammed so we'd have to wait 45 min for food. I had a major pho craving and was fine with hanging out. We ordered the summer rolls and two large chicken Phos. The summer rolls were great and tasted just like ones we had at Mekong River in South Philly. The server brought out two small chicken Phos because the kitchen didn't have enough chicken left for large bowls. The server was extremely nice about the issue and offered us a bubble tea and pork chops. The chicken pho was GREAT. I'd say it tastes better than a lot of the places we've tried on Washington. Very fresh and the broth had a lot of flavor. Don't leave without having the honeydew bubble tea. It. Was. Seriously. Amazing. So good. And finally, the porkchops. Very tasty! All in all, ipho was great and I'd definitely come back. I think they need a few weeks to get off their feet. They just opened on Tuesday. Great addition to the neighborhood.

The sandwiches (banh mi) are really good. We tried the combo (#1 on the menu) and the one with grilled sliced pork (#4). Everything - the bread, meat, veggies, and sauces - was done properly with nice proportions and great flavors. There's quite a few sandwiches to choose from, which is good because everyone likes to have options, right? I will start thinking of this place as "Subway in Vietnam". We also tried the steamed rice rolls filled with beef and veggies. For the sauce (comes on the side), you get to pick between fish sauce or soy sauce. We chose soy sauce and it was super tasty --- it was no ordinary soy sauce and had a lot of flavor and a well-balanced sweetness to it. There's also a veggie option (the rice rolls), and I'm looking fwd to trying that next time. Don't let the name fool you ... There's lots more to this place than just tofu! A great place to pickup some lunch to take back to the office.

Good food, but the atmosphere is dominated by loud house and techno music - which would be fine at a club, but it severely impairs the enjoyment of a weekend lunch. I've updated this review to reflect the fact that the atmosphere has improved of late. The music is at a much more comfortable volume.
Found this Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara looking for some good Thai soup. Not disappointed. Really good. Then we decided to have some drunken noodles. Highly recommend if you are in the area.

Second time was a charm. I was greeted with a smile and seated right away. The atmosphere was very peaceful with nice Decour throughout the restaurant. The owner came by several times to make sure everything was perfect, and let me tell you it was. I would rank this as some of the best Jamaican food that I've ever had. Cheers and much success to these guys!

Wish I could give this place more than 5 stars. EVERYTHING was delicious. Got the calamari and eggplant to start. Not usually an eggplant fan but could not stop eating it. I got the lamb gyro which was delicious! Something about their sauce was just perfecting. Can't wait to go back for more

This place is a diamond in the ruff. You could easily just drive right past but what a mistake that is. Everything we had was so fresh and prepared expertly. We started with a caprese salad. It was amazing, the tomatoes were so fresh and juicy and complemented with delicious mozzarella, red onions and roasted peppers with some mixed greens as well. This has to be the best caprese salad I've ever had. We also had the bruschetta, which was similar to the caprese salad but was also delicious. For entrees we had the penne alla vodka with chicken which again has to be the best I've ever tasted and shrimp scampi which had 6 large shrimp over risotto with a tasty lemon wine sauce. The shrimp were fresh and prepared perfectly. One of the people we were dining with had the stuffed veal chop which I tried and bet your bottom dollar I'll be ordering that next time. Ordinarily I wouldn't order dessert but we couldn't resist the cannoli, and you guessed it, hands down the best I've ever tasted and I've had more the my fair share of cannolis. The place is a byob so be prepared for that. All in all the price for the quality and quantity of food can't be beat, needless to say I can't wait to visit this place again. In a market so saturated with big corporate chains it's great to find a fantastic family run bistro with food that is more affordable and better quality.

This was such a weird experience. Because of Yelp, we l went to have their buffet lunch. The tandoori chicken was looking like baked chicken. The tikka masala was broken sauce and very little chicken. Like no other Indian I have ever seen/been to. We left. Not recommended!

I grubhub the *ish* out of this place! About once a week the delivery guy brings me happiness in the form of various dishes. He is always polite and gives me a little bow upon reaching the top of my stairs. I've also dined in-house a few times and am consistently very pleased. Erawan has my favorite chicken satay in the city, and their coconut soup is another solid starter. I've had numerous dishes, but my favorites are Yellow Curry, Rama Noodle, Pottery Shrimp and Pad Woon Sen. The portions are monstrous and reheat well. Big hearts for Erawan!

My husband and I love their food here and often get it. The only complaint that I have is that they have been making their portions smaller when you order it for pick up/to go. Very good food quality and service though. Everyone we know likes it, as do we.
Our family's most favorite spot for Indian. We love, love the dishes here. Flavorful and spicy as request and just tasty all around. Friendly and attentive server always, big plus!

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Slightly on the expensive side with a fairly limited menu But nice and friendly in a old converted house in downtown Reno Also it has no parking lot

Great environment and very friendly bartenders / wait staff. The food leaves a little to be desired, though. We had just eaten at Sang Kee a few days before, and by comparison all the food we ordered at Shanghai Station just didn't make the cut.
One of the better thai restaurants in the area. Nice atmosphere and delicious food. I usually get Pad Thai or Masaman Curry. Byob is a plus too.

I had the Pho with Brisket. As good a bowl of Pho as I have had, not greasy, not salty... spot on! I didn't taste the banh mi but my colleague raved about it. The bread looks spectacular. Great food in an upscale setting at not upscale prices. What's not to love?! Well now that I ask... the service wasn't bad but it was a little indifferent.
I went to Smiley's for falafel and they were out of falafel. At noon. On a weekday.

Stopped by for an early dinner after work. Service was nice and really fast. Got myself the wonton soup which was amazing ! Fanciest wonton soup I've ever had - had shrimp, chicken, beef, onions, and some greens plus the wontons which were very soft and has amazing filling. Shrimp and pork rolls were good too but I wish there was a little more meat and less noodles! Great price too - full dinner for one, plus a drink, for $16!
Typical beach bar food. Hit or miss quality. Drinks are good, the scenery is the best thing to recommend this place.

I finally tried this place after seeing many great reviews. I ordered the pad won sen and duck fried rice. The meals came in large portions and were very flavorful. We order everything in hot but it tastes like THAI HOT. It literally burned a hole in my stomach. I want to go back but order everything medium instead.

Best Thai restaurant in town! Food is delicious and service is outstanding. I had almost all of the menu items so far and the ones that are must try are: Duck Fried Rice, Beef Noodle Soup, Thai sausages, Panang Curry, Tom Yum soup and Ice Thai Coffee.

Much better price to value ratio. Service was excellent. I got in early and the place only got half full. The noise was better. I believe this is still an issue that corporate needs to address. Mongolian Beef was beautiful. Moo Goo Gui Pan had lots of shrimp.

I love this place. I've picked up lunch while at work, had intimate dinners, and frequent take out and I am never disappointed. The owners are this cute Thai couple who are as nice as ever. The food is delicious- I love the Paneng Curry! The restaurant itself is tiny (townhouse living room sized) and the tables are a bit close to eachother. That's probably the only thing that isn't my favorite, but stopping by when it isn't busy makes for a pleasant experience.

Ordered delivery through Yelp and was pleasantly surprised my order arrived in 20-30 minutes! The food was very tasty. We ordered lamb samosas, lamb Rogan josh, chicken shahi korma, and naan. All of the items had great flavor. The chicken was fairly spicy even though I ordered mild, but I enjoy heat so wasn't a problem. We will be ordering again and will definitely be trying the dining in option.

The only thing that made me smile was throwing away the food. Cold, 30 minutes late, and half my order was missing. Instead of offering a refund - they said next time the order would be on the house. Thanks but no thanks.

I had such a good memory of that place... and yes, I'm giving it 2-stars for the outdoor patio and the band (although they're charging $3.00/head for "entertainment") and the general fun atmosphere... But the rest... Seriously? We had a reservation for 10 people and the place was decently busy, but not to a craze... I've never experienced anything like that... We ordered a bunch a of appetizers to share, some bread and entrees for each one of us. Some appetizers came first (about an hour or so later) as well as 2 of the entrees, then (about another 1/2 hour later, when the first 2 people had finished their entrees) came a few more appetizers, and a few more entrees (but not all of them)... about over 2-hours into the meal, we decided to cancel the missing entrees... and that's when they brought the bread! Oh, and did I mention that we had to fight the check for items that were charged and never brought to the table... The waitress was nice, but totally clueless and ended-up dropping some jerk sauce all over my friend, with barely an apology. As for the food... It was merely ok. Nothing to rave about. One of the worst restaurant experience ever... And it's such a shame, because with a little bit of common sense, and restaurant management skills, this place could be a jewel.

I come here often to do work and it's easy to order something because they have juice, gf bagels, eggs, hummus, cucumber and tomato salad. Very easygoing atmosphere especially in the mornings. Includes couches and little sofa arrangements if you just feel like talking, not working. Sometimes they spray Windex on the tables while you're eating and that doesn't taste so great. Maybe they could spray the rags before coming out to the tables?

A friend and I went for the lunch buffet. It was wonderful. So many options for vegetarians and meat eaters but a little expensive for lunch. I think it was $12 then, even so, it's still a great deal for how many options there are and how tasty everything we tried was. The atmosphere is a little quiet and we couldn't hold our normal level of volume for our lunch but it was kind of nice to just focus on the food. I probably had 5 of the "injera" bread/utensils. Ethiopians don't eat with forks and use this spongy bread to eat with. It was delicious. My recommendation is to get the buffet for sure, it lets you try lots of freshly made Ethiopian foods.
Visited India Sizzling II for their vegan buffet. It was endless buffet with incredible food. Service was even great. Tasted just like the food I had during my travels in India.

I went to Zagol for lunch yesterday because I got a coupon from Living Social. When I informed the owner, she asked me if I had the coupon printed out. I politely informed her that I do not print the coupons because it is a mobile application and it says to show the coupon on the phone. I have never had to print a coupon from Living Social or Groupon. She then went on to say, in a very accusatory manner, "How do I know you won't go back and print the coupon and try to use it twice?" I explained to her the unique verification code can only be used once. She then got mad at ME saying how the coupon company didn't tell her when the coupon would be activated. I'm sorry, but how was this my fault and why must she yell at me for it?! SHE signed up for the deal and should have read the information prior to agreeing to do the deal! All this before I was even seated to eat. Grrr. I thought about flipping her the bird and leaving, but I held my composure. Another group of people came in immediately after me with the Living Social coupon on their phone, and she was sweet as cherry freaking pie to them. Whatever... The food had good flavor, but I will say that for $10, there should be MUCH larger portions. You eat with your hands which is fun, but the amount that was served looked like they portioned it with a single hand scoop as well. Since when did peas and carrots cost $10 for a single ladle? The lady was back in he kitchen for a long period of time, so I left my 50 cent tip plus 2 pennies for my "2 cents" and bailed. I have never left such a measly tip before, but this lady didn't deserve and ounce of my business to begin with. Hell no I'm not going back and I doubt anyone I talk to about Zagol will either.

Super restaurant! Great food, service is excellent too. Stopped here after a close up show at 930, they were still open! Ordered take out. They didn't have the Nan I wanted on the menu, so they made it special. Great to have a good Indian restaurant in the neighborhood.

So I usually go to Tiffin but I wanted to try something different. I started with the fish appetizer and the fried onion & spinach appetizer, I forget the names. They were just okay, not bad or really good. We ordered the lamb vindaloo (which didn't have potatoes. I love potatoes in my vindaloo), aloo means potatoes I thought, curry chicken and butter chicken and garlic naan which were all okay once again. Didn't blow my mind but it wasn't bad either.The mango lassi was really good. I I'm going to stick with Tiffin because for me the flavors were better. However this was good but based on the reviews and everyone saying it was competition for Tiffin, it was a let down. I was hoping to have another good Indian restaurant to go to because I love the cuisine but it was just okay. By no means am I saying it was bad because it was alright, but for me tiffin's food taste way better. The waiters are a bit awkward and quiet. I prefer attentive and friendly. I just found them distant and kind of quiet. When I asked a question they answered quickly and spoke in a low tone. This place is one of the better Indian restaurants, that I will say.
Wings are great. And I've been getting the roast pork and wonton noodle soup lately - good alternative to always getting pho.

Stumbled upon gem, which is located in a strip shopping center. Enter and be welcomed but what I presume is a family-comprised staff; very polite and accomodating. Sit down and open up your linen napkin which is folded into a pretty rose (how do they do that?) and then spend the first few minutes trying to try to refold it just like them. The food was all delicious! Tulip dumplings are pretty to look at and yummy to start with. The Tom Yum and Tom Kha soups were so flavorful - one with rich coconut flavor and the other with a perfect sweet/sour lemon grass base. The panang and massaman curries are both better than average - I only wished I had bread to sop up both broths. There is no alcohol, so BYOB. We didn't know that, so we were a tad bummed. Overall, a great meal out for anyone who lives remotely close by.

Everything from the meat to the noodles are very good. The soup though can be improve but other then that feels like a 626 bowl of pho. The only thing that I question is their Vietnamese culture value for they closed on American holiday such as the most recent Memorial Day. So idk restaurant like this back home don't close on holiday they get the busiest on holidays. So if you wonder if this place is truly Vietnamese you can use this to measure your standard typical Vietnamese restaurants.

Thai Country Cafe is one of my go-to restaurants and the best Thai on the loop, as a WashU student. I've been there maybe 15 times and every time get the same thing -- YELLOW CURRY. Theirs is fantastic, with just the right amount of heat for a midwestern white kid like myself. Add a little bit of peanut sauce for 50 cents more and it's one of the best meals out there -- I'm stuffed every time I leave. I can't speak for the rest of the menu, but the Yellow Curry is some bomb ish. Plus you can substitute Tofu for most of the entrees, which is great for vegetarians.

I used to live near here, which was just great because this place has some of the best bún in town. For the uninitiated, "bún" (pronounced similarly to BOON), is a rice noodle bowl topped with a variety of grilled meats (pork, beef, chicken), prawns, and spring rolls, then topped with chopped peanuts. There's usually some lettuce, cucumber, and carrot sliced at the bottom of the rice noodles, and you pour "nuoc mam" (flavoured fish sauce with a sweet tang) over top it all. You have your choice of bún where you can limit or add the types of meat you want on top, but why bother with anything but their most deluxe offering? All of the above, please! Honestly, I haven't tried anything else in the restaurant except for this dish, but Thanh Son does theirs wonderfully. It's very generous with its meat portion, and for the price and portion, it's a steal. Most bún in the city is generally tasty (it's hard to say no to grilled meat in some sweet marinade), but I have yet to find the same value for money and taste as the bún in Thanh Son.

Used to ride my bike to this place every weekend, one of the best buffets in town because they ALWAYS have Samosas and Pakora on the buffet, most other places in town do not. The Chicken Tikka Masala is always a crowd pleaser, if your lucky you can find AWESOME Malai Kofta on the buffet, my favorite vegie indian dish. Service is prompt and friendly and the atmosphere is pretty plain but the food makes up for it!
Great location by The High Watt. The dinner was a bit overpriced and the restaurant smelled bad.

Visit number 20. Still the best Thai food in the Tampa Bay area. Just amazing! We tried the Pla Koong salad this time, and it was a truly special dish. Tremendous flavors and presentation that would befit any of the top restaurants in Tampa. And I love the ladies who run this place. What are you waiting for? Try this place out. You're welcome.
Great Indian food at a great price. I have only had the lunch buffet, which has had a good variety each time. The garlic naan is so good! Also, the service is great.
its good food, not authentic jamaican food-- (= big portions
great lunch spot. the pork milenesas are fantastic. good service too

Nice little spot in Irvington. So i was in the area around lunch time and thought i would give this place a try. i was not disappointed. My review doesn't cover the breakfast items. Location is great on the south side of Washington with a shared parking lot so you don't have to try to find street parking. The inside was a lot bigger than i expcted. You can order to go at the counter or sit down and be waited on. The decor is simple and minimal but nice and open. The staff that waited on me were great! a young gentleman started out but as the place got busier a woman from the back came out to help him and they both did a great job. The menu is small but well done. Sandwiches, Soups, Salads, pretty much all you need for a good lunch/brunch. Drink menu is nice with teas and coffee, water to soda and sparkling water. I saw some wine bottles but didn't see it on the menu. I had the cuban sandwich that came with salt and pepper chips. I have to say that i have had some of the best cuban sandwiches ever and I'm pretty snobby when it comes to cubans. Theres isnt the best I've had BUT it was very good! and i do recommend it! the chips were great too, not sure who they get them from but yum! All in all i will definitely come back here for lunch again or maybe breakfast if I'm in the area that early. Good spot, good food, good service. try them out!!

This is the hands-down the BEST north-Indian restaurant in Indianapolis. Being a California transplant, I am snobbishly critical of any Indian restaurant. Finally finally an "authentic" North-Indian restaurant opened in Indy. Especially fell in love with the vegetarian version of chicken wings - Gobi Gopura (Cauliflower)... it was yum, yum, yum. And also fell in love with BAINGAN BAHAR & DHABEWALI DAL. Delicious food and great service. Just hope and wish they keep the taste and quality consistent.

The food was ok but the service at this restaurant is beyond terrible. The server dropped off my off and never came back to check up on me if I needed anything. I had to call another server and ask for a sauce for my meal. My server was standing on the side and just watching. The other server brought me the sauce and didn't mention to me about it being extra when I got my bill I saw extra two dollar charge on my bill for a small ramekin of white sauce it was beyond ridiculous and the server gave me such an attitude! He basically fat out told me why didn't you check our menu! Worst service ever!!
The food is tasty and reasonably-priced, and the country decor is well executed. This place deserves better than Penn students looking for a snack after a night of partying.
Wouldn't go back if it was free terrible service and food tasted pre cooked might as well go to wing house if you want crappy microwaved food save your cash folks

The gyro was amazing unfortunately I can't say the same about the service. After placing my order I was quickly told her they close in 30 minutes so what you're saying is if I'm not done eating I have to leave? Can't bring outside beverages in. the sign on the door says it's because of health code that's a lie. With just going to order water but my only option was for a bottle of water. Maybe a renewed focus on customer service and satisfaction would help this place be busier. Overall experience was poor due to customer service and because of that I will never go back

Awesome for Philly to have such a delicious and modern Lebanese spot! Restaurant and outdoor garden coming in March. We came from center city to check it out for sunday brunch. Such a warm, welcoming, authentic atmosphere. We sat at the bar and watched them make our food - mezze plate, lahm biajin (with egg and chili), and side of fries - which was all phenomenal. Fresh and beautifully prepared, you can tell the kitchen takes great pride in their work. My only hang up (I wanted to give 4 stars for this but the food and atmosphere is too food) is that you have to go back and wait in a long line to order a second round of drinks ! Wish that you could order from the bar instead. In any case, amazing experience, highly recommend !
The best ox tails & curry goat I've ever had! The cabbage at a lot of places is usually bland for my taste but not here, it's perfectly seasoned & cooked. Absolutely love this place.

It is so sad to see what the place has become! My husband and I have been coming here for years and I know there are different owners but I still can't believe how bad it has become. I mean if you want cheap sushi.. Then yeah this place is for you but if you are looking for good quality sushi.. Stay away. Even the chop sticks are cheap little balsa wood knockoffs. From the cheap looking decor to the cleaning supply smell, I am sorely disappointed.
When I worked on 19th I went here all the time to get my Quality. You dont go here for customer service so stop complaining people, its not that deep. Just go and get your fresh delicious food.

An amazing culinary experience in the midsts of pub food and bars. Ariana's provides patrons with a calm and homey ambiance, stellar service, and delicious, flavorful food. Fresh, vibrant tastes that are so different from the surrounding restaurants in the area. We are sure to be visiting again and bringing friends! A must go!

I'm taking one star off Pita Jungle... Don't get me a wrong. I loved this place. But the waitress this time was absolutely clueless. We asked her what was chicken del sol in the menu, and she had no idea. We asked her about the specials of today, and she answered, "I should have known this..." Urrr.... I will probably come back with friends soon, but hopefully the service can get better next time.

Absolutely delicious. Sometimes the service can be a bit on the slow side, but the wonderful attitudes of everyone in here as well as the effort put into the dishes makes it easy to swallow. I'm not a vegetarian but me and my wife are both addicted to the Navratan Korma.
Good gyro. Plus they have chicken gyro and other unique flavors. Drive thru only no seating. I like to order double meat for an extra dollar.
Always a favorite spot for some friends and I to eat. The pad thai and boba tea are so good

For a place within walking distance it took us a long time to finally get here. Unfortunately, we were there on Mother's Day evening when they weren't offering their traditional Sunday dinner or even a full menu really. The husband and I enjoyed 2 flights of wine (a great flight of Rose and he tried the reds) and we shared a cheese platter and charcuterie. Everything was great! Our service was on top of everything for the first 3/4 of the time we were there. We ordered desert and she vanished. I would like to go back and try more of the menu.

Some of my friends had been here and highly recommended it, so we went there for some food. The Mexicano dog had been one of the items they mentioned, so I got one. To be honest, I'm not a huge fan of hot dogs, but I do love things wrapped in bacon and covered in guacamole, so I gave it a shot. It looked pretty good, but upon picking it up to take a bite, the bun was already falling apart. Strike one- can't my bun be intact when it arrives in front of me, please? But, whatever, I figured I'd just cut it with a fork and eat it. This is difficult, though, with so many toppings. When I started cutting it, I realized that the bacon, well, was just raw and had no meat on it. Just a slimy pale white blob wrapped around the hot dog. The only thing I found myself saying was "this is a disaster". Strike two. I sent it back. I was still hungry, of course, and the bartender said I wouldn't be charged for it (awesome, thanks) so I split the pork tacos and chimichurri sliders with the aforementioned friends. The tacos, while being highly recommended by various people at the bar (we ate at the bar) were nothing special- pretty dry. The sliders, same thing. Dry, basic, and uninspiring. My friends, who've been gushing about this place, were also pretty unimpressed and apologized to me for the food. "It's usually better" they said. Strike three. Don't know if I'll be back, at least not for the food items I got this last time. That said, service was good, beers were good, atmosphere and decor is cool. But. I'd rather spend a little more next door at Delicia and absolutely love what I get. To be fair, I'm a late night sort and there is never a wait at Delicia when I head in after "normal"dinner time. Hopefully La Mulita gets its act together to consistently deliver the kind of food that made my friends rave in the first place.
Banh mi thit nuong aka BBQ pork my fav! Reminds me a place I used to go to in San Diego called K sandwiches!
The chef is a true genius when it comes to falafel, chicken and preparing food in the truck. The line is long but it is well worth the wait.
Very good Thai food, great atmosphere, and clean restrooms.

Everything we had for lunch today was excellent. We tried the Thai Fried Rice, the Orange Chicken and Red Curry. The rice was perfectly spiced; the Orange Chicken has a mild orange taste just the way I like, in fact, it was perfect; the curry was nice and creamy to my preference. This is a great place for lunch.

Friend told me about a new taco truck, and since it was only a few minutes from where we worked, I couldn't say no! While he raved about the chcken satay taco and the thai taco, I went with the chicken katsu. What a steal for $5! Lots of rice, and the chicken katsu has just enough of that famous brown sauce. Will definitely have to try the tacos next, and all their menu items. Yay for yummy food trucks! They have thai iced tea....which I absolutely love!

I got a groupon for this restaurant and took a like mined friend for dinner. If you can still get the groupon, Get it! This was some of the best Indian food I've had in quite some time! Nice atmosphere, very friendly staff and some innovative food at a very reasonable price. We had a a crispy avocado chat appetizer that was amazing followed by chicken korma and lamb makhani. We will definitely be back!

Ordered two sandwiches and a drink to go. Friendly service. Good toasty banh mi. Great variety of them too! I got the BBQ pork which was delish. The Korean beef BBQ was OK, just a touch dry on the meat part. Can't wait to try the other ones!

I always get a Mrs. Bui. Solid sandwich. This is the best place to go for breakfast or lunch. The sandwiches are fairly cheap, and the people are fast. There will most likely be a line, but it is definitely worth it.

Terrible, completely terrible quality. They are ripping off people with their takeout!!! My boyfriend came home with a mango bubble tea that tastes like chemicals and has excruciatingly hard boba. All for $4.50. Not the first time it happens! How on earth are these people still in business?

Great portions of gyro and chicken for the pita. For the price, you can't beat it. The ziki sauce was delicious. Having the ability to choose from pita, wrap, bowl or salad and chicken, steak, gyro or falafel - is a winning combination! Great choice!

This is a frequent place for us. We prefer to sit at the bar but their dining area and outdoor patio is also nice. The service always meets my expectations and so does the food. My go to dishes are the eggplant Anatolia and their Caesar salad. I also like their steak, lamb and salmon entrees. My husband loves their seafood linguini.

meh. It wasn't good but it wasn't bad. I had the tom kha gai which was good but I didn't like the broccoli in it. My chicken pad thai was bland but at least it was edible cause I was hungry after waiting 50 mins for my food to be delivered. I was quoted 30-35 minutes for delivery.

Overall,good place to go. My other half and I have been on several dates there. We had dinner and the lunch buffet. The lunch buffet is inexpensive and tasty. If you are worried about spice concerning the buffet don't be as it is mild. They have a good variety of food in their buffet. I would recommend their paneer and chicken curry. Also don't forget the dessert, keer. To drink, the mango Lassi is always a treat. This is a great place for groups or couples/families. The service in my experience is descent and attentive. On a random note, I must admit the music there is cheesy old stuff from the movies and the shrilly voices annoy me. Other than that, an inexpensive place especially for the buffet and delicious food.

I have always wanted to try Ethiopian cuisine, and tonight it finally happened, my belly is happy! This place is and the food is simply magical. It was 25 mile trip each way from where I live, was it worth it? Oh yea!

Love it. Love it, love it, love it, love it, love it. I'll give them a human 97% success rate-- once out of the 30+ times I've eaten there I had a dry falafel with not-so-good pita, but it's almost always absolutely excellent. My one recommendation would be to explore the menu-- there are a ton of different ways to have your falafel. As you go through the menu, you can find a number of interesting combinations. Three last points on Bitar's: (1) They do better with the pickled vegetables they put in the sandwiches than any of the other local joints I've seen. The genius of grilling the falafel patties goes without saying. (2) The halva is wonderful-- one of my favorite dessert treats. Just don't think about it or ever look at nutritional information. (3) Ajvar (pr: "eye-var"). Red peppers, eggplant, a little garlic and a little vinegar. It's the best thing to spread on anything-- sandwiches, crackers, vegetables, pasta . . . I actually go through about a 16-ounce jar every two weeks. I go with the mild and add my own spice.

Super good. I want some right now haha. The money you spend is worth it here. The gyro plate is amazing and you can choose your side and you get a drink. Very satisfied and super yummy. It is also quick.

We recently moved away from NJ and boy do we miss Asian Chef!!! The food is phenomenal. The staff courteous. The sushi and the green thai curry is out of this world! We have never had a bad meal here!

We went to India Sizzling II on Saturday night and had the buffet. My husband and I are both vegan and appreciated the time our waiter took to explain the dishes to us. There was a wide variety of options and the dosa were amazing! We tried the masala dosa and the onion dosa and they were both great. The flavor was great and the food wasn't too oily or salty (have had that problem at other local Indian places). In summary, great food, attentive service and a clean, pleasant dining room. We will definitely be returning!

I give them a 5 star because everything is such good quality it's worth the wait when they get slammed with orders. Chanel is very helpful & accommodating - she treats me like family since I'm a regular. They're very nice and work very hard. If you want a quick healthy but delicious meal you have to go here or call ahead.

Originally I thought this place was great, but based on my recent experience I will never be back. Service was terrible. Our server kept forgetting to put drink orders in, was not familiar with the menu at all and the chef refuses to make any modifications to menu items. For example, I had the shrimp and grits here previously, but it was no longer on the menu. However, shrimp is on the menu as well as grits. Just seperately. I asked if they could just put them together and the answer was no. Also, when you wait 20 minutes for a beverage and ask your server about it and her response is, I put the order in, let me check with the bar. Followed by "What did you order again?", it's never good. The location is great and has such potential but far too pretentious for me.

This place is great. So much flavor to everything and excellent hummus! The owner is really nice and wants to make sure everyone has a good experience. You get a pretty big portion for a good price and the food is filling but healthy. I'm so full right now I'm just gonna lay here for a bit, haha. Great place all around. I'd highly recommend!

Best pho in Reno/Carson City, hands down! Beef based broth with great flavor, Pho Ga came with a mound of chicken. Egg rolls were also very good but lack the usual accouterments of lettuce and pickled carrots and radish, and mint leaves. (Oddly, there was lettuce in the soup.) Asian Pho sets the bar for Reno. If they'd add the accouterments for the egg rolls, this would be five stars.

I love Thai food and this restaurant is in my neighborhood so I've eaten lunches and dinner there and have ordered take out. Every meal has been very good. I like spicy and they have spicy! When I have out of town guests, they always want to have dinner here. The curries are excellent, the restaurant is clean and comfortable, and the service is always good.

I go here all the time, and this place is really good for Reno. It shares it's space with a Port of Subs, and is in a small strip mall, but that is something that you'll get over quickly. From reading other reviews, I see that they do not have the authentic names up for the dishes, but they do have a large variety and a nice selection of real vegetarian dishes. I stick to the pho and vermicelli dishes. I have always put all the sauces and things that they provide for you to flavor your dish in, so I am not sure what the original broth tastes like. They are also willing to work with you if you have dietary restrictions (I'm allergic to cilantro). I think they are a little on the pricey side, especially for lunch (a regular meal with small sized soup, single spring roll and modest drink can run you over $14), but I like the owners and I always get a filling meal there.

Had the grilled chicken with rice, beans and plantains. The meal was okay, but I don't think it was worth the price. The portion was kinda small and the food was a bit bland. The rice and beans were good.

PLEASE RE-DESIGN THE INTERIOR AND OFFER AFFORDABLE COMBOS/SPECIALS. GOOD: -friendly staff (almost too friendly though - owner quizzes you about where you heard about them, and is overly chatty about how great they are) -fruit tea, smoothies, baklava, bubble tea - YUM -good authentic food and good variety - really liked the hummus and meats BAD: -would like to see more combos / coupons / specials (maybe a $5.99 lunch/dinner menu?) -the place is NOT inviting to dine-in. Had a very cold, empty feel. We sat in these cold metal chairs and there was no ambiance whatsoever. If it weren't for the good food, we may not have returned. The owner needs to invest a little money into an interior designer, some lighting and mood music, and an overall more inviting restaurant if he wants to increase future business

Small but comfortable dining room. Tasty Pad Thai, Green beans with garlic and Massaman Curry (though we'd ask for it spicier next time), Eggplant stir fry was OK. Service was great. Family of five. Kids loved it. Would like to see a longer beer selection although Santa Barbara Brewery is closeby...
Having just dined at another tai restaurant I can't wait to return to this spot to get good tai food. Siamese Princess is far superior in freshness and taste.

Overall, kind of meh. Been to this location twice. The caucasian waitstaff are kind of smarmy and make you feel rushed. Lunch special is very well priced, but the portions are TINY. Got the dumpling appetizer, it was literally two dumplings. Come on guys. Food is pretty tasty though. Work on your staff and portions and maybe I'll be back.
Closest thing I'll get to NY's signature chicken & rice. Don't get a gyro. Just get the lamb box. Fufill your protein requirements while skipping the soggey fries.

I love it here. I hate that I always go here because the food is so addicting and will most likely make me fat. The lunch special is great. The dinner is phenomenal and the portions are pretty big! They have some of the BEST tasting crab Rangoon I've ever had! This place is amazing and one of the best if not THE BEST Chinese restaurants in town. Try the General Tso's, you won't regret it!

Finally checked out Season's after so many people kept coming here. I was pretty satisfied. It is a cute little place with a menu for warm food, as well as a menu for drinks. They have boba tea, shaved ice drinks, and premium teas. They also have various snacks that are pre-packaged for your convenience, and they sell loose leaf tea. This place gets quite busy, but just stand in line, then order your food, and they will bring it to you. They have a nice outside area too, so you can sit outside, or being with your doggie. I will be back, and can't wait to try even more of what they have. I tried their shaved ice with fruit. It was good but seemed like more ice than fruit.
I love this place! The food is excellent, the restaurant is cozy and beautiful, and the staff are lovely.

Finally, a casual asian restaurant that does not just taste like every other homogulated tourist-friendly asian joint. The food is delicious, authentic and the flavors are excellent. I would venture to say that this is best Thai food in SB.

Authentic Jamaican food but a little pricey and it depends on who's at the register because the pricey slightly vary but I ordered the large oxtail and Mac and cheese and plantains it's always banging
Our first time here and we thoroughly enjoyed the kabob sandwiches! Everything tasted fresh and the seasoning was good. Friendly staff and clean restrooms! We will definitely come back!

Sunday Brunch The Good: Such a cool building, has that good modern rustic feel. The Bad: Way overpriced. I had the lamb, egg scramble for $14. The taste was there, but there was no more than about eight bites of food. Also there were several pieces of just fat which were very unappetizing. My girlfriend had the buttermilk pancakes which were nothing special. They had this pear and plum compote that was too sweet and extremely dry, it was more like a sugary dry jam and it would only cover about half of one pancake. They also came with a big glob of frozen butter on top and no syrup. When we asked the server if he could bring us syrup he looked confused and said he wasn't sure if there was any. Ten minutes later after munching on dry pancakes he brought the syrup. My sister ordered eggs and bacon, the bacon was nothing special and was $5 which was a little ridiculous. Kitchen Kulture has some bacon that is worth it, but this was not good. Also when my sister asked if she could also have a side of the brioche bread the server said there wasn't enough bread to make it a side -we ate brunch at noon and there was only 4 other people in the whole restaurant, so I don't know why the bread was such a big deal. Also our coffee was hardly refilled. They had some weird system of pouring the coffee out of a thermos and I saw no coffee maker in the back. Last complaint is our server said they are under a change in management, so I think they might have used that as an excuse to be so bad. I was so excited to try this, but it was just awful. So disappointed.

So, let me explain one more thing. I gave Zaika 5 stars before, and after visiting them again, I wish I could get them 5+. Here's my reason why: there is another take-out place in Bensalem that sells fantastic kebabs. I mean, I'm talking about a really good product here. I always thought to myself, "the one food that Zaika gets beat on is the kebab". I went to Zaika last week and ordered my regular chicken curry, rice, and pakora. It didn't feel right not to order some chicken kebabs, and I thought to myself, "well, I'm already here and I don't plan on going to the other place, so why not?". Lo' and behold, they were incredible. You can taste all of the ingredients and spices, and the execution of the food is phenomenal. I cannot wait to go again. TL;DR version: Everything is better than the other places you go to, including the kebabs. I'm hungry.
Almost once a week, my fiancee and I get a Gyro and a Shawarma, and two delicious fruit smoothies! Even if we just need a snack, we will swing by just to get some Hummus and Pita. Highly recommended!

I like this place. .. the owner is really nice and recognizes me .. I aways order the palak paneer and 2 Naan for take out... it doesn't taste as good as house of india. ..or this place in LA that I ordered like almost once a week. .. the restaurant in LA calls this dish saag paneer.. it was a lot more creamer and they delivered. ... the prices at spice n grill are high... but if you like a quick place to get Indian food. ..this is the place to go

Zayna Mediterranean is a nice little cafe on the NE side. You order at the front counter and then can either get take out or dine in (you can also bring your own beer or wine). The food was good and affordable. What a pleasant experience! I think this is a great place to go if you're craving Mediterranean food but don't want to trek all the way across town to the Greek places near U of A.

Worst first experience ever! We never even got our food because the service was so poor. I came in with my family today with high expectations but was thoroughly disappointed. We were seated in a cramped area and when we politely requested a different table we were rudely declined and then ignored by the server. She then proceeded to serve two other families that came after us, outwardly ignoring us. After 15-20 minutes of being neglected we just got up and left.

We are lucky in New Orleans to never worry about a shortage of Vietnamese joints to grab some food. Seems like just yesterday (or maybe five years ago), you had to journey all the way to the East or the Westbank to find anything decent. We truly live in amazing times. We wandered over to Pho Cam Ly last Thursday to grab dinner, and we were happy with the choice. We ordered two glasses of water, Gi Cun B (Fresh spring roll w/veggies & avocado), Bún Nem Nng (Vermicelli w/ grilled pork patties), and a large bowl of Ph Đc Bit (Beef soup w/eye of round, brisket, tendon & meatballs) Being able to cut and paste from their website made that a lot easier! The Avacado Spring Rolls were good, albeit a bit different than what we are used to. The peanut sauce of plentiful and exploited to the maximum extent. We may be slightly addicted to the stuff. The large bowl of Pho was definitely large, and very tasty. It came with the requisite basil, bean sprouts, and lime. The soup was hot, and the broth was fairly robust, with a good beef flavor. The noodles were definitely noodles - not much to right home about on this front. The Bun was also excellent, with the pork patties adding a nice flavor to the dish. This joint was pretty good, and we may return if we are rollin' through the Uptown 'hood. Fortunately, we are blessed with a great little Vietnamese joint close to us in the Channel/LGD. Good food, good service, and no way I'm ever going to try the Pho Challenge (two pounds of meat, two pounds of rice noodles, and what appeared to be gallons of broth). Only knock on this joint is having one just as good and touch better a few blocks from the homestead - sliding in at a solid FOUR STARS.

I thought I ate the best food in the world when I lived in Thailand for 3 years. I was wrong, Siamese Princess in Ardmore is just as GOOD and authentic! Great duck, pad Thai, drunken noodles, and lamb. Beautiful, friendly people. I'll be a regular now! :)
It is a good place .Hokkah is good ,lamb shisk kebab is avarage,other than atmosphere is good.

This review is for the vegetarian pho. I ordered the small vegetarian pho and it was yummy! It was pure vegetarian / vegan broth and there was broccoli, carrots, tofu and rice noodles in the vegetarian pho. The broth was slightly flavored which was good. There were only a few people in the restaurant which made service pretty quick. There are two other vegetarian / vegan items on the menu if you are not interested in pho.

Smiley's gave me a fresh new perspective on Manayunk. I used to feel like I have been to every restaurant on main street too many times, my friends and I would spend too long trying to think of where to go. But today my friend and I discovered an amazing mom and pop giro place after initially walking by, but smelling something delicious soon after. Smiley is a gregarious talented chef who makes everything from scratch, with love. You can taste it! My friend is the son of a well known chef and its so hard to find a place he likes. He is a relentless food snob but couldn't help in joining me in raving about smiley's. I have lived in three countries, two of which are littered with delicious giro shops (I was a regular), smiley's was the best and right here in 'merica! More than that, it is a charming venue, full of potential. He just moved in but he has big plans to offer hookah, belly dancers, and stay open until 3 am on weekend nights. Hope to see some of you there after the bars close! Places like these bring character to neighborhoods.

The quiche here is amazing, so if you stop by for anything, make it that. I enjoy La Va because it's in my neighborhood and it's a nice place to chill out and read for a few hours. Most of the time, people are doing the same - either reading/working and the place is generally quiet with some light background music. It's cash only, which I find somewhat annoying, especially when I just want to sit down and read with a coffee, but all I have is my debit card. However, most places in the area are cash only, so maybe I should just learn to carry a few bucks around.

I am so disappointed in my lunch takeout. I have been here twice for dinner when it first opened and loved it. I called in takeout today and when I arrived (weekday afternoon) the lights were off in dining room and kitchen and someone was sleeping with their shoes off in the first booth!! Seemingly surprised by my arrival (although obviously I called ahead), the sleeping shoeless man got up and someone else ushered me to the back to take my money. After I paid in the dark, as I turned to leave the man was horizontal again and I got a nice feet smell on my way out. If I had come to eat in there I would have been mortified. To make matters worse my food was dry chicken, greasy sauce, and my favorite rice that had cardamom and spices in it the last two times was just plain bland rice this time. My stomach hurts now. Will not be back, really is a shame how downhill this place went.

This place is awesome! I'm glad we gave it a try. Normally we don't like Asian fusion restaurants but this place is an exception. I had the tonkotsu ramen and the wife had the Thang Long sizzling sole fish dish. The ramen is the best ramen I've had in town. The broth and pork are so flavorful. I don't normally like cooked fish, but my wife had me try her sole fish and it was great as well. Very tasty. I definitely recommend giving this place a try. I don't think you will be disappointed.

Drove down from Atlanta for the weekend and to my delight..a Jamaican spot right by my hotel...my delight very quickly turned into disappointment and disbelief...how could they mess up Jamaican food this badly..smh.. 1. They started with a bad product..I had the stew chicken but I think they meant to say stew turkey because the meat was so big and tough. 2. When the person that works there tells u NOT to buy something they are not joking...RUN AWAY!!! 3. Food is really bad...not worth it even if free...

When I travel to St. Louis, I like to stop in and sit at the bar for a tasty well executed cocktail. Just ate a nice kale salad, octopus plate, and trout tartine. Perfect after being stuck on Southwest Airlines all day in the middle seat. Bartender and servers very friendly and fun to talk with! I wish I could go here when its warmer outside.

We tried the papaya salad, steamed dumplings, green curry and pad Thai--all were fresh, flavorful, and well prepared. We've tried a number of Thai restaurants here in Nashville and Bangkokville rises to the top. Great service; clean.

The food was good and we're heavy Thai food goers. we especially loved the asparagus and avocado salad which boasted a perfectly grilled asparagus (not to be taken for granted in a Thai restaurant... historically speaking) Service and ambience were awesome and friendly We debated if it's a 4 star or a 5 star. We would have put the 4 star but decided we wouldnt be the ones pulling the rating down (as of now it's slightly over 4). Will definitely come back
This place is amazing. The only thing better than the amazing service is the food. Everything we ordered was perfect. This is definitely my new spot on South Street.

Saw this place several times and decided to give it a try! Was not disappointed. Everything was so delicious and great portion sizes. Perfectly fried and accompanied by the guasaca( avocado) sauce. Definitely a hidden gem. We got the shrimp and beef arepas which were delicious! The plantains , empanadas and chapatas guava dessert. The owners were really nice and it was all fresh! The prices are VERY reasonable ( especially coming from uptown). Try this!

Oh my! I am blown away by the quality and taste of this food. The oxtail stew with jollof rice and steamed cabbage and carrots. We also got beef stew and rice and peas. Even though we got there at closing and they were out of quite a few things, we got a good portion of both entrees. (Pictured is about half of the oxtails). I will be back! #FoodCriticDaily #MeAndTheKid #TravelAdventuresDay2 #WasSkepticalButNowIGotANewSpot
Steak, egg & cheese. Every weekend for 4yrs to make the hungover happy.

I liked it but I think it was too hyped up for me. I like nice/romantic ambience, but it was a bit too dark.. felt like I was eating blind. The pastas were all very rich which I'm totally fine with (healthy people, beware). I loved their gnocchi (warning, it is VERY rich so healthy people shouldn't order it as a full plate). Also liked the Tagliatelli al Limone (another warning, it is VERY lemony, but again, I thought it was good/refreshing). Pesto Trapanese is also very good. Hubs ordered the Fisherman's stew which was ok, he said he wouldn't order it again though. My favorite was probably the antipasto siciliano. I realize it's a small, fancy restaurant and maybe I'm not refined enough to truly appreciate it. The flavors were excellent. Service was good. But I thought it was a bit pricey for what we got. Oh, and we did eat dessert there... just don't remember it much since it is a byo and probably had a bit too much to drink by the end of dinner. ;) But I do vaguely recall that being good too. Glad we tried it. Probably won't go back, but it was a good dinner with awesome company.

LOL! Used to a bottle mix? Seems like your go-to response for the other reviews pertaining to the same problem. I assure you I am not "used" to a bottle mix. I have had plenty of delicious from-scratch margaritas AND bottle mixed margaritas. The caliber of deliciousness of your restaurant's particular creation did not even come close to what I've experienced before. Actually, it didn't really even taste like a margarita. Just tequila, lime, and AND SELTZER. This could be a problem with that particular bartender, but I expected better from a restaurant named after this style of drink.

As a born & raised Baton Rougean I never thought that moving to the bright & shiny Nola where everything is bigger & better meant giving up my Greek food fix. It's now been 3 years & im sad to say I only JUST found out that there was an albasha here. I ate so much my fiancé had to roll me out the door like a grape leaf! I'm so excited to have FINALLY found a place that cooks the chicken on a skewer & I can ask for it "crispy" or "burnt" & not get a crazy look. Don't know what's with the lack of authentic Greek food in Nola but this is the ONLY place I will be returning to.
Very extensive menu, speedy service, very good food, authentic, good value.. my husband over ordered, but we managed to finish all, nothing left.. that says something..

Meat and beans are good and cheap. The oxtail had more bone than meat but the pork was better. Wish it were hot. They're super generous with the rice and beans but the rice is terribly salty so the whole meal begins to numb the tongue. Inside tables are sticky sticky sticky. I used to like going in for smoothies until one day, my blonde friend and Asian I walked in the young lady behind the counter took our order and then her male friend walked in and they started flirting and talking about how neither of us know Spanish. Didn't say one word to us after he walked in. We both speak Spanish. Comes with decades of classes and living in Southern California, I guess. Thought that was in poor taste. Just like some of the food.

WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! I have a dream that curry paste and coconut milk can combine harmoniously to create an unforgettable taste... I have a dream that rich and creamy crab rangoon are fried to perfection and melt in your mouth like cotton candy... I have a dream that I am treated like a human being when dining at a restaurant... I had that dream... I had that dream until the moment when the bitter thought of Jasmine Thai crossed my mind... and then I woke up... It was just a dream! Red curry with beef: The sauce was too thick and artificial. It was grainy and not fresh. The bell peppers were not cooked through all the way. There is al dente and then there is al dental visit.
