Lidocaine anyone? The beef was tough and old like a southern grandma who forced you off of her property by threatening to blow your head off with a side by side shotgun. Crab rangoon: Have you ever had stale tortilla chips? Multiply that experience by 10 and the product is the exterior of Jasmine Thai's crab rangoon. As if that's not bad enough, you are dishing our $6.95 for 5 of those little buggers. They must be out of their minds! Thai iced tea: Not bad... At least I had something decent to wash down all that garbage and mask the atrocious flavor of both of the aforementioned dishes. Service: You know how clowns have a permanent smile. Now imagine the opposite of that and you would have just imagined the wait staff at Jasmine Thai. Nothing more needs to be said but i'm so mad i'm saying it anyway... It was a complete and utter disappointment, and a perfect example of how not to treat customers. No smile, no emotion, but plenty of not giving a damn. HORRIBLE! RUDE! EXCRUCIATING! INEXCUSABLE! Aftermath: 10 minutes into my curry dish... NAUSEA! HEADACHE! STOMACH PAIN! It felt as though cement trucks and steamrollers were operating inside of my stomach. I am writing this review 5 hours after my meal and my stomach still hurts, except the pain has now traveled to my small intestine. I'm just one guy who had one meal at Jasmine Thai. Try it if you'd like, but at your own risk. As for me, i'm through with that place! Happy Dining!
Been here a few times - love the food!! My go-to for Pho. Spicy lemon grass broth is the best ever! Service is great too.
Very interesting original concept perfectly pairs Asian flavors with flavors of the South. Cool location and friendly casual atmosphere. Great for the meat eater or the vegetarian diner.

The restaurant is small yet quaint with some Indian decor scattered around. It is one of my favorite Indian restaurants to go to. Their chicken tikka masala is a classic. If this is your first time eating Indian food, I would definitely recommend getting this here. You can never go wrong with chicken. My personal favorite is the Palak lamb. The base is spinach with herbs, onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic. Their curry is just so savory with all of the fresh spices and ingredients they use. Im a little surprised that rice doesn't come with the curry and costs extra. Other than that, their naan is also very good especially since it always comes out hot and fresh.

Orchid Thai is my new favorite Thai restaurant! I've spent years patronizing an establishment in Odessa and honestly the food and the friendly owner absolutely blows my former place out of the water! Thank you Samantha for such wonderful food!
This is a hidden gem off of Broad street. The food is amazing and the owners are very friendly. I recommend that you stop by and give them a try. You will love it.

When there for the first time this week. Excellent food, authentic and fresh. Staff was also very nice and most of all the Buffett is great value for money! Highly recommend and will be back for sure...
The food was great. Would have given 5 stars but the noise level with a full house was equivalent to dining next a 747. The chairs were very uncomfortable also.

This place is a hidden gem of deliciousness! Went there with my family and was amazed by the whole experience. The service was prompt, friendly and very attentive. The ambiance was magical, spanish music played in the background and the decorations all around the restaurant were awesome. The food was simply amazing! I hate that it took me this long to discover the magic and wonder of Mofongo! Truly unreal how much flavor was in every bite. Would defintley reccomend to anyone!

I have only been here twice. 1st time, food was good but we waited forever to pay. 2nd, food was good but there were a couple of surprises in our food. Looked like bristles from a brush. Found one in our appetizer and didn't say anything and then found another in my soup near the end :( I mentioned it to the waitress who I assume is also the owner and she just looked at my hair and smiled. Seemed like she didn't believe me and thought I planted it. I mentioned this to her just so that they don't repeat that with other customers but she did deduct our appetizer from our bill which was $6. We will never be back, even if just for the 20 min wait for us to pay. (Reason being there was only one person working, she was taking the orders and making the food).
Amazing food! It looks like a gross run down place, I only went because they're open so late and I wanted to go back immediately. The food is crazy fresh and the staff made my day
Their lunch buffet is to die for. The naan is fantastic and the tikka masala is great. Would definitely recommend.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Excelent food. Food prepaired right. I had he curry salmon. It was amazing. So tasty. Service good, food came quick, quality of food excelent.
Great menu! The French dip was delicious and definitely recommend the side of fried rice! Super friendly and attentive service. Loved it!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We stayed one night in Boise and picked Taj Mahal for dinner, based on Yelp reviews. Turned out to taste more authentic than equivalent restaurants in San Francisco's Embarcadero or in Mountain View's Castro. The menu surprisingly had a couple of cider options, one from Spain. We very much enjoyed the food. The concept of building your own dish (pick curry, pick meat, pick spiciness level, etc.) seemed unusual but turned out to be convenient. The owner treated us to personal insights about Boise. We then forgot a couple of important items and only called back one hour after closing time - turns out they were waiting on us to call and pick them up. Taj Mahal restaurant has our heartfelt recommendation.
A very unique, yummy meal! Check out my full review with pictures below! :) http://goodyummyeats.wordpress.com/2013/08/18/mood-cafe-ecstasy-guaranteed/

I don't usually post reviews but I just wanted to say this place was absolutely amazing. We first ordered off of grubhub and the food was not as good as we expected. However, the Brian took care of the entire situation and made us go from never eating there again, to our future go to spot. He was very caring, professional, and handled a bad situation with absolute professionalism. It was everything you wanted to see out of an owner/manager. The food was absolutely amazing and so was the service. We really felt like royalty dining in there. I recommend everyone and anyone to try this place out!

My group of friends had a wonderful dinner experience here. I had the curried tofu and LOVED it. My friends had curried chicken and jerk chicken, which they describe as fantastic! Definitely recommend this place.

I love this restaurant! This restaurant was a Yelp recommendation. It turns out to be very convenient to where I live. The best thing about this restaurant is the staff. They are so nice and very accommodating. The first time we went, it was right before closing, but they took our order anyway. The second time, I went with a friend. We sat and talked until after closing. They never once asked us to leave. My favorite appetizers are the edamames and the eggplant tempura. I love eggplant and when it is done well, I'm a very happy camper! It has great flavor and really hits the spot. As an entree, I've had the yellow curry both times. I really like this dish. It has potatoes in it which I wasn't expecting. This is not a hot curry, so anyone should enjoy it. The curry fried rice was different. I enjoyed it as the curry flavor blends well with the rest of the ingredients. I like my curry dishes over rice, so this seemed like a natural fit. It worked for me! The next part may seem odd, but this restaurant has the cleanest restrooms I think I've ever seen. It seems like a natural connection to think if the bathrooms are this clean, then I would imagine the kitchen is spotless! When you go in, be sure to note the tabletops. They are hand carved and from Thailand. They are unique and beautiful. Swing by...and enjoy!

I'm a big fan of Zoe's: it's like the Panera of Medi food and I feel pretty good about feeding it to my kids - the tossed Greek salad is my favorite and the kabobs (steak in particular) are terrific as well (both paired well with their Hibiscus tea). I order a lot of catering for my company through Zoe's and they've always delivered (both literally and figuratively). It's a good, solid dinner option for families (and then just do a three-minute walk over to Kiwi for some fro-yo!).

Love this place. Once a staple of downtown Saint Petersburg, Tangelo's moved to Gulfport at just the right time. Several years later they are going strong. A testament to their quality meals. A cocktail of Cuban cuisine with Southern Hospitality and the flair of folk art makes Tangelo's a place worth visiting often. Prices are in the pocket. The charm of Gulfport is alive and well thanks to places like Tangelo's.

We get take out from here a couple times a month. The beef and flank pho is out of this world. DAT BROTH. My girlfriend and I usually get that and two chicken bahn mis. Our food is always ready on time and absolutely delicious. They never skimp on the veggies (jalapenos, sprouts, basil) which are always fresh, and the prices are completely reasonable. I've never eaten in the store, but it is always spotless when I go in to pick up my food, and the staff is always friendly. Couldn't ask for more when it comes to Vietnamese food!

I come to Sher E Punjab constantly. I love the food. We almost always order chicken tikka masala. I have eaten at 6 Indian restaurants in Tucson but none compare to the consistency and taste offered here. The one downside is the portion. They do not put enough of the chicken tikka masala, although the rice portion is fine. Other than that, it is worth every cent! I suggest going here esp if you're in a rush as they get my orders out in about 10-15 mns, or 20 if it's really hectic. They could do w some remodeling. The inside is old and dilapidated but I don't eat in here often.

Best bang for the buck in the area! The kids meal is huge & cheap, $6 gets you basic pad Thai (you can get rice instead), egg roll or 2 crab Rangoon & 2 chicken strips...nice! The pad Thai for adults is big & you get to choose your toppings, one protein is included in the price. With the weather nice, they have 2 patio tables although ours was a bit rickety. If you are in the Hills, it's Worth the trip.

This is my favorite Thai food place! I come here at least twice a week for the Pad Thai extra Thai hot! It come out fast and super hot! I love the owners, they are super nice and friendly. If you haven't tried this place I highly recommend you do!

Visited this restaurant for the first time last night. The food was very good and reasonably priced. The staff was friendly and helpful. So glad to have a good Indian restaurant nearby. Will definitely go back again

One of the best hidden restaurants in Tampa! Food is amazing!!!!! It's definitely one of the few restaurants where you can't go wrong with anything you order....everything here is very tasteful, and perfectly spiced. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who has adventurous taste buds!!!!!! The service is usually very laid back. Don't have expectations to get in and out quickly. Food is amazing and well worth the wait:)
We love this place! Been several times for the weekend lunch buffet, and twice for dinner, and each time the food was excellent!

Been here twice for lunch and I gotta say, this is probably the best Lansdale has to offer. Had the red curry first time and green curry second time. Both were excellent. The salad and soup accompanying the lunch special were just as sumptuous. Exactly what one would need during a windy cold weather where the moment you start gulping down the hot soup, you start watering from your eyes and nose and all you wanna do at the moment is crawl into your bed under the cover and sleep for just few more hours..... hmm... hmm... hmm... nough said.....

Great little hidden gem on the Delaware river. BYOB makes it even nicer. Their pasta's are great, but so is the very robust and moist grilled pork chop. Be sure to get the garlic bread too. Nice atmosphere in a cozy setting along the river, while the views are not great, the overall charm is very nice.

Even though I don't live anywhere near Mood Cafe, I regularly travel across the city for their chaat and lassis. The owner is sweet, funny and generous--I have seen him send an indecisive pregnant woman home with an extra chaat on the house, just in case she second-guessed her choice of flavor, and today when I asked him to explain a certain seasoning to me, he gave me a free second drink so that I could sample it. The food is always wildly flavorful and so, so satisfying, whether as a summer picnic meal or a light, spicy way to warm up in wintertime. If you have any questions or want a recommendation as to what to order, be sure to ask the owner! Hearing his explanations and having him customize your chaat and lassi is an important part of the Mood Cafe experience.
Nice little chicken joint staff of this again very nice friendly food always comes out in a timely manner it's good to have another option down the road

Value is great at lunch time! I got Drunken Noodles and the red curry. Its the staples I get to see if I like it better than...well the red curry was good not amazing but good. The drunken noodles were cooked well and I like the assortment of veggies etc but it lacked flavor. I would definitely give them another shot...but Thai Paradise and Siam still are my favorite Thai places in Indy.

Great lunch deal. I grab the chicken, rice, and planting for like $10. And that's a lot of damn food. Owner is big chills too. Loves to talk and the service here is good. Real Dominican food here if that's what you're looking for. Big selection too

Decent for Fairmount, but not as good as the places in China Town or on Washington Ave. Also - don't get take out.... I got raw steak in a plastic bag and had to re-heat the broth until it boiled and add the steak in. Sort of disgusting and not what I wanted to do before eating.

Best Vietnamese food I've ever had. They have a whole vegetarian section and everything on it is delicious. Their spring rolls are the best I've ever tasted. I go nutz for their vegetarian soup too. They are closed on Tuesdays, I think, which always throws me off and I've driven there sooooooo many times only to discover that they are closed. Worst.
Great service, friendly owner, awesome philly steak sandwiches, gyro's and the best hummus! Falafel is good too. This place is a diamond in a rough. I am addicted to it.

First time writing a review despite using Yelp for years, but how awful the food was here brings me to it. I'm not sure how this place has such high ratings but this was, beyond a doubt, the most bland, flavorless, and unseasoned pad Thai I have ever eaten in my entire life. To make matters worse, they charge $16 for it! Ridiculously overpriced and again, literally unseasoned clumped noodles and chicken with no peanut sauce visible anywhere. A complete disappointment to thai food as a cuisine, Philly and Rittenhouse Square.

Great place, great price, great people. This is my girlfriend and I's go to place when we are going out for dinner. We like to try new places but when we want something that we know will be a great choice, Zorba's fits the bill. Cool atmosphere. Small but open dining room and a very knowledgeable staff. The waiters all recognize us and remember us when we walk in and they always have something to recommend to us. Pricing on items outside of the platters is a bit on the high side but don't let that sway your decision. This is traditional greek. You will love it. If you don't know what to get, get the grill sampler platter. It is enough for 3 people to share or 2 people who are really hungry. I cannot recommend this place enough. Do yourself a favor and sit down and let the staff take you through athens on fairmont.

This place is awesome! My mom and I went for curry rotis and were in heaven. The ownership is so wonderful too- new restaurant started by a father and son who want to provide authentic Trinidadian food and vacation vibe. They're so sweet and gave us extra dish on the house so we could try something new! Plus, it's BYOB and they encouraged us to come anytime and hang out a long as we like- they play really good music! Definitely will come again !!

Great pho place. I was excited when I found out this existed. I ordered the large #17 Beef combination noodle soup (Pho Dac Biet) with an extra pork chop on the side. it is a great value and fills you up. The broth is rich. The pork chop is marinated deliciously and seared beautifully.

This place is my go to whenever I'm hungry. And don't want to cook. (Often) Their goat is to die for. The mongoo is also excellent. Ask for their smoothies. Owner and all workers are so nice. Pay them a visit. Will not be disappointed.

I LOVE this place. We are regulars here, and the waitresses always recognize us and say hello. Everyone is so friendly! Food comes out super fast in my experience, and we can be in and out in under 30 minutes if we are in a hurry. I always get the spicy pho, but I have tried my bf's bahn mis and vermicelli bowls. They are all great! It is one of his favorite places too. They have a small porch area outside which is nice when the weather is good for watching the activity on magazine, but bring mosquito spray because I have gotten eaten several times!
This is our neighborhood spot! The food is consistently great. The pho and banh mi are delish. We strongly recommend this place for a casual meal.

Best Thai in Doylestown. We go here at least once a month. There best deal is lunch. You get a choice of soup or salad and then your entree for a good price. I always get the Thai salad and shrimp or chicken pad Thai. My husband gets the Tom yum soup and the red curry chicken. All of their food we've had has been really good.

This place was amazing! I can't believe there weren't more people here. Ham and egg sandwich and fish tacos were amazing. Don't get me going on the dessert! Burke, our server was knowledgeable and a great server! I'll be back!

When a friend suggested celebrating her birthday at this restaurant, we all jumped on board. First off, I must say, this is a case of a fine restaurant being located in a rather tired-looking strip mall. Don't let the outside turn you away. It's a lovely little restaurant with a comfortable and relaxing atmosphere with friendly service. If I may, I'd like to quote some of my friends on their first meal here for we ordered a nice variety of dishes. I might add the menu was very extensive and offered good vegetarian choices as well. "The food was delicious and I found the service to be efficient and very friendly. I also liked the tasteful decor and ambiance. We tasted many items and I found them all to be very good." "The restaurant was clean and pleasant, not crowded but well frequented. The food was plentiful and interesting. My dish was more spicy than expected but had large pieces of chicken and rice that was aromatic and flavorful, although spicy." Chefs Special Combination Mixed Grill: "The service was excellent and very attentive. Though the dish had great flavor it was overcooked. The lamb was way over done and dry. I loved that they had real ice tea, and lots of lemon! The naan flat breads: we had onion, garlic and plain. They were tender, flavorful, and melt-in-the-mouth delicious. All the appetizers we tried were fantastic." I had the Vegetable Biryani with flavored basmati rice with veggies, nuts, and cashews. It was pretty bland as I ordered it. Should have spiced it up a bit more. Here's a link to their website with all the food they serve: http://sher-e-punjabtucson.com Several of us remarked upon leaving that it would wonderful to return for their famous lunch buffet. I look forward to that.

Lived here a year and finally tried Kalamata's today. Hummus is THE best I've had in Nashville!!! I am thoroughly impressed. Super clean inside and food was absolutely delicious!! I did the salad sampler and had the tuna salad (OMG amazing), pasta salad, and Greek salad. I am a very very picky person and my food blew me away it was so good!! I am more than stuffed for $9.75 with tax. Will be back soon!

What a great little place ! And how could you not love Smiley ! (The owner) I've been here a few times and the food is always delicious! A platter is plenty for one person and I usually get 2 meals out of it. They have a few little tables outside and some inside in the back as well. Smiley is super friendly and the others working there are nice as well. Definitely worth stopping in !

First of all, this place is so cute! The decor is very charming and makes you feel like you're in someone's home. We came here for easter dinner (a busy night) and were seated quickly. They have a large vegetarian menu, I had the papaya salad, pad Thai with tofu, and coconut rice. The papaya salad wasn't spicy (which is traditional) bit the flavors were very fresh and I enjoyed everything I ate. They also have a dinner combo plate which comes with soup/salad, appetizers, and rice and a main dish for a reasonable price. I would return here In a heartbeat!

My wife and I went to Miss Saigon the other day to try their pho. Situated in the old Mongolian Express location just across from the Strathcona Save-On, it retains the look and much of the feel of the previous tenants. Though we printed the coupon from the Valpak website which clearly stated we should have been able to use, they turned it down, insisting that they only accepted the coupon from their delivered flyer. What's the purpose of having your restaurant coupon available on-line if you can't use it? Luckily we did also have the flyer coupon which we were going to save for another occasion. My wife had the #2 Rare Beef Noodle soup and I the #5 Vietnamese Spicy Soup. Both came with the usual bean sprouts, slice of lime, basil leaves and a chili. Though my soup was reasonably spicy, it didn't have that nice pho broth flavour of the better pho places even though the #2 soup did. Disappointingly, I was told it was a different broth, and mine came with spaghetti noodles rather than the standard rice noodles that the # 2 did. Overall, it was okay, but for a much more flavourful experience, you can do better. I'd drive a few minutes down Whyte Ave to have the wonderful broth on 100th Street.

Came in for the March madness sweet 16 game. No CO2 meant no soda or beer. So I asked for a Thai Tea. They ran out of that too. Very disappointed that I am stuck with a water or hard liquor to drink. Restaurants should have CO2 at all times and never run out.

This is my very first time here. Just stopped by to pick up morning treats for me and my co-workers. A man greeted me when I walked in and made small talk...very nice. I didn't realize that he was the new owner (Mr. Bello). They sell the less than day old goods for a very reasonable price and I am here to say that if these taste so freaking good, I can't wait to see what the fresh ones taste like. All of my co-workers loved them. I will be back.

Went here on a Saturday night without a reservation and was seated within a few minutes - the space is much larger than it seems! We were served bread while waiting that was delicious with the oil/vinegar. The two of us ordered the charcoal grill sampler for 2 and it was brought out quite quickly. The platter had a variety of meats with some rice, beans, potatoes, and veggies as sides. The lamb chops and gyro meat were our favorites; both were very flavorful and the lamb chops were juicy! The sausage was also tasty. The other meats were not as good - the kebab chicken, marinated grilled chicken, and kebab pork were all quite dry and we had to eat it with a lot of lemon juice and tzatziki. The sides were all great and very flavorful. The platter was a good amount of food. Between the two of us, we finished everything and were very full. The service and atmosphere were great, overall enjoyed our experience. Would recommend the lamb dishes and gyros!

Pretty freakin' tasty for Thai in Columbia, IL. The bf and I ventured over the river because this place came highly recommended to us by a nice lady and her husband. Well, we were not disappointed. We did not order an appetizer but everything sounded tasty. For our main courses we had: Red Curry - fresh red chili, bamboo shoot, coconut milk, green pepper and basil with chicken. $9.95 & Vegetarian Green Curry - fresh green chili, bamboo shoot, coconut, milk, green pepper, mushroom, eggplant, broccoli, peas, baby corn and basil with tofu. $9.95 Both curries were flavorful and smelled amazing. The veggies were fresh and the food came out uber fast. The server was friendly and helpful. The ambiance was kind of whatever but it was clean. The spice level was LOW. I love spicy food and I ordered the highest level on the menu. Don't get me wrong, the food was good but it was not spicy. the bf doesn't like his food as spicy as I do and he said he could have handled the level of heat my curry was at. I chatted with the server a bit and next time we visit I will be ordering a level 10. I'm looking forward to our next trip out there.

Yah mon...The service was excellent and the food was amazing. I don't remember the servers name but I hope he and the restaurant does well. Very good food. Only reason why I didn't give it a 5 is because Food was pricey but that probably is a perspective thing. I would recommend them. reserve your table with the hearts and the rose pedals for that special someone in your life. I will be back.

Best Greek food I have ever found...and I've frequented many a gyro stand in my day! The greek salad dressing was outstanding - definitely not out of a bottle. And the gyro meat was not your typical stuff - very tender and flavorful. My non-foreign-food-eating son got the special of the day -- beef. We weren't expecting much....but were incredibly surprised. The meat was way above average. The service was good as well. We had to leave before the live music, but that would have been a nice bonus to the atmosphere.

Dined in a while back and forgot to write a review. I came here with my friend visiting from Nashville and i don't remember what she had, but I know she liked it. We came here when they were just opening so there were certainly kinks to work out, but aside from minor hiccups, the service was great and the food was equally satisfying. I remember ordering a Thai tea which they topped with whipped cream. It made for a nice garnish of sweetness to an already sweet drink, although I feel I get a little more Thai tea in a typical serving at most other places. I remember mine going rather quickly. The seasoned rice with beef was my choice. I also added an egg because, why not? They offered it, and I obliged. I've seen quite a bit of mixed reviews, some people calling the place downright terrible, which I would disagree with. The food here is good enough, like, if I was in the mood for Vietnamese and in the neighborhood, ok. If I'm planning on Vietnamese, this probably wouldn't be my first go-to. Although this review is from a visit close to a year ago, I will go back for another try and hopefully they can get an extra star or two out of the deal.

I always get disappointed when I go out to eat because I always think "I could've made this better at home for a fraction of the price". Not here! I love the chicken shawerma. I mean really, really love it. I crave their garlic sauce at least once a week. Definitely go there and order this dish. Their chicken shawarma wraps are yummy too for a great price. In the beginning the waitresses were not that great, but they're getting better.

I come from a big Italian family and this was where I decided to have my birthday celebrations this year. It was the BEST meal I've had in month!! Everything everyone had was DELICIOUS! Chicken Saltimbocca, calamari, veal francese, stuffed calamari, some penne with vocka sauce and scallops special... but the BEST, and I was surprised because my mommom usually makes this the best, was the stuffed artichoke- filled with chunks of bread and cheeses and gooey, this was AWESOME! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

Overall it was a decent experience as per usual. We have been together for 7+ years and have spent every anniversary there as well as a few other occasions in between. THe last two times (Oct 4th & last night) & they have been screwing around with some of their classic dishes. We get the same things (and have been) since we started going there. For example, they tried to add carrots & other random veggies to the Mongolian beef - WHY?! Now to their credit, they did ask folks to fill out a survey and rate the "new version" and which version we liked better. Pro tip: DONT MESS WITH A GOOD THING! Lol. But this time I noticed that my Shrimp in Lobster sauce was much less juicy & even though it was the dinner portion it still seems significantly less Shrimp, sauce and sprouts and more mushrooms. Again, if it ain't broke don't fix it. Also, the price went up. I get inflation and etc but our bill with 1 drink each and desert was over $100. Seems extremely high when we usually spend around $75-$85 with much more leftovers for the next day. If changes like this keep happening, we'll have to find a new anniversary spot. Oh & my "Great Wall of Chocolate Cake" was dry af. I ate it bc I paid $9 for it but it wasn't the quality that I come to expect from PF Chang. #MrProTip

Excellent Indian buffet with tons of flavor and a lot of choices to fill you up! Really loved how samosas were included and fell in love with the vegetable korma. I'm really big on chicken tikka and this wasn't the best but the tandoori chicken made up for it so tasty. Only $10 for a lunch buffet you can't beat it, amazing meal.

Picked up takeout......wow. Asian pickles are to die for, but the pork dumplings and the pad thai had no taste and no sauce on/with them. The pad thai was basically a bunch of noodles, a few shrimp, some slivered snow peas....no taste, no cilantro, no onions, no peanuts....just a soggy mess of nothing. And not cheap.

If you haven't had Jamaican food there's something wrong with you. Let this place be the entrance to a whole new world of flavors. Food 5/5 I can't stress how delicious the food is and it's always well prepared and always fresh. They don't skimp out on portions either, the small is basically a medium. The medium is really a large. The large should be labeled "Family of Four". I recommend the jerk chicken or curry chicken for starters and then make your way to goat or ox tail. The Mac and cheese is great as a side as well as the "hummingbird salad". It's a baked Mac and cheese by the way, not that watery Kraft bullshit excuse for Mac and cheese. Trust me, you want this. Service 3/5 You don't interact with anyone much. It's pretty straight forward. You go to the line, order, wait for your name to be called. There are no servers, you order and eat or order and leave. Ambience 4/5 This is what I'd expect from a mom and pop Jamaican restaurant. It screams Jamaican proud. It's clean throughout and bright. They have reggae playing as well. Nothing crazy but don't expect a 5 star steakhouse. Jamaican food is humble in its roots. Over all, amazing food amazing experience. For a place that serves exclusively in paper trays and utensils, it's definitely over priced. But it's a hidden gem and a must eat. Evolve your palate and check it out!

We ordered take out tonight from SEP. we only waited 10 min for the order to be prepared. Here's the chow rundown: #19. Palak chicken- chicken in puréed spinach, onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and spices. #25. Tikka Masala - chicken broiled in tandoor, cooked with masala sauce #70. Paneer Bhurji - cheese pureed with spinach onion chili and spices. #94. Garlic Naan. Naan bread with garlic. We had to order rice as well as take out even though it comes with these meals if eaten in. Why? We asked that it be prepared with medium spice. It was so mild that we agreed it was bland. All 3 meals were bland. The garlic Naan was delish.
Called 3 nights straight each time earlier then the other and they always say Kitchen is closed the website says open until 10pm sad because the food is great

Food is good. Just FYI- I've been twice and there was just one staff member there which was the same one both times. The first one was when I went to eat there at 9:40pm when they close at 10pm. He told me they close at 10pm and I said that I knew that, then he waited to see if I would change my mind and I did not. So I felt that I should say that I would promise to be done by 10pm. He reluctantly told me to take a seat. How crazy is that to treat a first time guest this way! I usually don't care as much about the quality of service as long as I like the food, but this was awkward!
love love lovethe best fresh puerto rican food!!!!! winderful staff especially jessica :)

Always try to get to this place when we are in town. Traditional criollo cooking, from mofongo, alcaparras to chillo! Great service, clean and fresh food moderately priced with even Boricua craft beer! A must try for all.

Let us, together, knit together the scattered fragments of all foodstuffs available to us (including but not limited to: milled and pounded grain products, the flesh of beasts of the land and sea, everything in the vegetable and fungus kingdom, and the horrifying mutants of the processed food tribe, belonging nowhere and owing allegiance to no one) into some Frankenstein-like embodiment of the ideal "drunk food." 1. Since coordination decreases in inverse proportion with one's alcohol consumption, the food must not require intense manual dexterity to eat. Anything that requires peeling, slicing, delicate dipping and/or saucing, or spearing with skewers or chopsticks is right out. Ideally, the food should be able to be maneuvered with only one hand or paw or whatever, enabling you to smoke or gesticulate wildly with the other. 2. The ideal food should essentially be a mash-up of carbohydrates, salts, and grease, to soak up all of the toxicity. This is desirable, though by no means a magic bullet-Pandora's box is irrevocably opened sometime following the fourth drink, of course, and nothing you consume after that will change that fact. However, let us at least remember the sayings of Hippocrates--if you can do no good, at least do no harm. So, best to stick with the simpler things--carbohydrates, proteins, simple veggies--rather than attempting to consume something hazardously spicy / creamy / soupy that'll create trouble for you later. 3. It should be cheap--odds are you aren't going to remember eating this thing, and you don't want to wake up the next morning with a bill for a $36 fish filet that you have no memory of on your credit card (though, if this is the worst of the embarrassments you suffer at the culmination of a drinking binge, sir or madam, I envy you). 4. It should be fast. Thirty minutes from now you could be passed out at the bottom of the ball pit at Chuck E. Cheese's, and you don't want to miss out on that, do you? The revelation of the ideal drunk food, of course, is not a revelation at all--unless two bare wires in your brain are perpetually crackling in outrage at never really touching each other, you've deduced from the context and the menu of Dööners what I'm going to say. Bit anticlimactic, really. It's not remarkable, but it's tasty, solid food, considering what you want and where you are.
Amazing food for a good price. My friends and I absolutely love it :)

I've always eaten in at this place and never had less than great food and good portions. Seems a little healthier than most Chinese American places but even tastier. The employees don't speak very good English but that's part of the charm.

I've dined here quite a few times.Quiet & pleasant ambiance, as well as friendly service.I didn't see a seafood pho on the menu, so the server said he'd make one up for me.It was delish, & the broth was even yummy.Spacious seating, private parking, and perfect date spot in my opinion.Don't sleep on this gem on the west side of Indy!

The owners and management of Aladdin's are rude a$$holes that don't care about their customers at all. Wouldn't recommend sticking around until the lights go up either, it's disgustingly dirty in there. It actually makes a lot of sense that they don't care about customers or cleanliness because the lounge is UNDOUBTEDLY a cover up for some super shady business dealings.

Pros: Open late on a Sunday (esp when orig dining plan fell through) The venue is nice for an intimate setting decor is somewhat modern Person who greeted us at the door was very friendly and gregarious, i do believe their shift finished while we were there THE BREAD- TDF. Cons: Rather plain flavours for mezze style plattering and the genre of the food (could be that American food doesn't use a lot of garlic). Not a busy night and the staff there unable to really cover the service. Meals took a while and we were forgotten about for 15-20 before our drinks order was taken. Couldn't be convinced on any of the 10 cocktail options, would have been nice to have two or three simpler, cleaner flavours. Neutral: Priced for the higher end of the St Louis market for a casual locale, the serving sizes were commensurate for the part of the market they are trying to feed, just be aware of this.

I've been the place twice since it opened and I can only give it 2 stars. Here are the critiques of the foods I have tried there: The taziki dip - good, the pitas are a bit chewy and not toasted well $6 The tirokafteri dip: way too salty, I took two bites and couldn't attempt to finish, again pitas too chewy $7 The Soulvaki Pork: good, the pork was well seasoned, only had like four cubes of pork in the pita, felt there could me more, nice array of veggies, pita was tough. $10 I felt was a bit pricey for the portion provided. The Athenian Half Chicken: good sauce, a bit dry, only served over fries, it was okay. $13 The Horta greens: did not like at all, cold greens slathered in olive oil $6 The Venue is nice and open. Customer service was great. Greek beverages were good and nice touch. The food is just okay to me and find it to be over priced for street food. I probably won't be back unless something changes.
I've eaten some so-so Indian food and decided I wasn't a fan. My lunch, today, at india Cafe changed my mind. Everything on the buffet was absolutely delicious. I'll be back.

It's a very small place but the owner is very nice. I ordered R1 the rice platter was nice. Coconut rice is vey flavourful. I especially like the fried fish on the side and very tasty. For Noodle N1 is also nice. It's kinda like ramen but they put the soup on the side. Some veggie, pickled egg, fried wonton in the noodle, all tasty. I think the flavour can be stronger and a bit different from what I had in Indonesia. It's cheap. Each dish is $5-8 range.

This is one of the best Thai restaurants I've experienced. It definitely compares with, if not beats, Thai food I've had in Boston and San Francisco. I came here with a group of friends at their suggestion - a few of them have become fanatical about this place. Two of them come here once a week during the workweek - apparently the luncheon specials are pretty good. We ordered 4 large Orions ($6/bottle). They give nifty frosted glasses for ice water, and oddly shaped (but usable) beer glasses. Adds to the fun. It is a family owned restaurant, according to one friend who knew the owner/waitress. The father cooks in the back, while the mother and daughter are waitresses/cashiers. Onto the food: we ordered family style. Pad Thai, Angry Shrimp, Basil Chicken, some kind of vegetable sautee, and Penang curry with shrimp. Prices of all those dishes ranged from $9-$13. We also got generous portions of white rice. In a word, all of the food was great. The Pad Thai was slightly saucier/oilier than I've had, but it was a pleasant surprise. All of the other The basil chicken, vegetable, and angry shrimp had similar brown sauces with varying degrees of spiciness. They were all well prepared (perhaps a bit too similar, but it was all great, so no complaints). I loved mixing the sauces with white rice. Each table is outfitted with a tiny carousel of 4 spices/sauces. My friends used these more than I did, but it's a great way to allow each person to customize to their own levels of spiciness/flavor. Incidentally, Sukho offers multiple levels of hotness for their dishes, including "Native Thai." I was curious to try this, but was warned by my friends that it was pretty insane. I'll save that for another date. A couple others have noted that it's not super authentic, which I disagree with. The restaurant does offer a mix of other cuisines (specifically Chinese and Japanese sushi). However, I don't fault them for this - after living in Nashville for a few months, I get the feeling that all Asian restaurants have to diversify a bit. Sukho definitely focuses on Thai. Overall, I'm definitely coming back here even though it's a bit out of the way. I highly recommend anyone go here, especially if you're going to be in the Grand Ole Opry/Opryland/Opry Mills area.

The food is ok But everything just fades away due to the horrible service The restaurant was empty yet the waitress was impatient, rushing, rude and just plain not nice I asked for wine and she just cut me off and said they don't have the kind i wanted without even offering a different option/ beverage. If you're hungry and crave thai food just pick up don't sit there.

First off, having come from a place where Vietnamese culture and food shops are saturated (OC, California), this place is not too shabby! I had the Pho Special aka Pho Dac Biet! While it was missing a few components such as tripe, rare beef, etc, (Yes, I know, it may not be easy to source certain ingredients around here, and yes, I know that every restaurant can do it differently...) the rest of the toppings were so good! The meat actually has flavor and the noodles have a nice al dente, chewy bite. The broth isn't too salty either! The vegetables that came with could be a bit more fresh, but it didn't matter since I put it into the soup anyway. I did have the cafe sua da... Or Vietnamese coffee... Iced and it was a little watered down from what I'm used to. Condensed milk, Viet coffee and ice is all I need on a hot day. It wasn't amazing but it wasn't bad. Plus, I liked how the staff remembered me after only one time and even remembered how I liked my Pho. Really friendly people and always down to talk. And the portions are deliciously huge. For having a lack of real competition, they put forth a really good and sturdy foot.
crab and mushroom omelet need i say more!!! oh yes, bloody mary Atmosphere was great. Staff delightful. Highly recommend

A Groupon brought us in, food will not bring us back. I do think some of the positive reviews on here are suspicious. I think they are fake. We had pad kra prow and green curry, ordered hot. Both were underwhelming in flavor and quality. Service was okay.

This is a place I've been dying to try for a long time & now regret I didn't get here before! IT'S AMAZING! The blends of spices and ingredients truly make it unique. I can't wait to go back and try some different stuff. You.owe it to yourselves to get out and support this place! Also a great place to take a date as it's special.
The food was very good. The chicken kabob was among the best I have had in America. Their "dogh", yoghurt, drink was excellent. I highly recommend this restaurant!

This was my first experience with Ethiopian food, but I have always heard from others that it is delicious, so I was quite excited to try something new. The service was OK but I thought it was a bit pricey for the portions. The food was incredibly bland. I was expecting something flavorful and delicious (I ordered Gored Gored) and it was just very spicy, no flavor at all. I felt a bit rude not finishing my food, but it was so flavorless, I was very put off. The friend I was with assured me that Ethiopian food can be better, so I will try it again, but probably not at Zagol. I am glad to see others have had better experiences.

This was our fave restaurant until yesterday when we came to have lunch all the way from DC. They had special of Nasi Padang that came with couple dishes: chicken curry, sambal ijo, sambel goreng udang, daun papaya, and rendang. The server asked whether we wanted breast or thigh for the chicken. We ordered thigh (since he asked). Long story short, we got chicken breast instead thigh. No problem. It tasted OK eventho I prefer thigh. All other dishes were good. When we were ready to pay, we told the server who took our order that we got chicken breast instead of thigh. Not complaining, just wanted to let him know (what was the purpose of him asking what chicken we wanted, right?!?). He replied while he's pointing on our almost empty plate; 'well, too late.. You finished it all!' I and my friends were speechless, didn't expect those kind of answer. Then we laughed, because again it wasn't a complain. But since he answered in that kind of attitude, I decided to leave a review. The restaurant is NOT clean. If you expect them to be like 'regular' restaurant, please set your expectations lower. Their food were great. The portions are smaller than before. The service was 2 out of 5. I put 3 because of their food. Would I come back? I think so. Well, I hope their portions won't be smaller than what we got yesterday .

Yah Mon, located next to Walgreens, is a hidden gem a half mile from the downtown Marriott. Andre promptly greeted and seated me tonight. The dining room is well appointed and lighted. I recommend the Jamaican sampler plate - excellent! The service was impeccable.
I love the Vietnamese beef noodle soup! Super nice customer service they always remember me when I come in.

Great lunch choice! I had the black bean burger and my buddy had the chicken shawarma. Enjoyed the signature mango iced tea while we waited, and refills before the meal was over. The black bean burger came with a side of roasted potatoes that had a unique flavor. Easy to overeat! The burger bun was a heavy duty roll and the dish came with enough sprouts, onions, and tomato to either have as a side salad or throw on the generous burger for a real treat. My buddy told the waitress "Fabulous" as he polished off the wrap. I'll be here for a week, so this will be a great place to take in again.
one of the Best Thai places in the Burbs. you easily forget that you are in a strip mall once inside. Green Curry rocks my world.

Hi, First of all i would like to start with that I used to love this restaurant. The food has always been amazing. Even today the food I ordered was great and it was takeaway order. However, the quantity was not sufficient for even a single person of Chicken Makhani. Along with that I ordered 4 garlic naans out of which 2 naans were plain. I was really disappointed with this service and so I am rating this as 1 star experience.
YUM I made that seafood combo (grilled) disappear. It was worth the traffic. Generous portions-I have leftovers for lunch tomorrow as I just could not eat all of the rice and beans provided.

I've been here twice for lunch and really like their rice vermicelli special w lemon grass. It's great summer fare at a good price for the area. Service was fine and they have a nice menu. I liked it better than other local Vietnamese restaurants.
Love the food here! They are fast with preparing everything and never disappoint with portions. Never had a problem with calling in orders for work
Absolutely love guru. Pria is amazing. And her husband is an amazing cook. The food is the best Indian around.

Rarely will you find a restaurant that would serve both an intimate date as well as a giant family affair - my visit was in the latter but it was easy to order a round of dishes family style and allow the entire 10 person party to enjoy everything this incredible restaurant has to offer. I hope to come back one day to enjoy their brunch as it seems everyone raves about it. Their front area with the pastries and cafe is adorable as well. Both a tasty dining experience, and a beautiful place to visit!
Good food, service with an awesome view. Highly recommended, although I'd pass on the deep fried pickles again.

This is a tiny thai joint tucked in amongst hotels, behind a McDonalds and a gas station. Though it's small and the decor is a little under-dressed, it's still a very tasty place! The milk tea is flavorful. The curry is spicy and delicious. Most of the dishes I've had are curries. All of which were unique and very good! The panang curry is my favorite. Nice big chunks of chicken, smooth creamy coconut-based sauce with delightfully al dente bell peppers and a hint of basil. The yellow curry is also quite good but I thought the sweet potatoes were fried in something that put off the flavor just a little. I've also had the spring rolls and crab rangoon. Standard fare to be expected from any decent place and served with really enjoyable sauces. All in all, Bhann Thai is a favorite lunch spot for me and my coworkers when we have the time for it. Very tasty! Try the milk tea and the panang curry!

Zeppoli is delicious Italian food- very heavy Mediterranean influence. My absolute favorite thing is the antipasto. And I always make sure to leave room for the Zeppoli dessert- Nutella donuts! Keep in mind, this is a very intimate dining area (which can get very loud) and in the winter it gets very chilly when the door opens since they lack a vestibule.

The ceviche is quite good and the guy taking the order was very nice. Unfortunately, they might have some communication issue with the kitchen: our two ceviches came out both with different ingredients than what asked.

We left Busch Gardens today, hungry. We had no idea where to eat so I looked on Yelp and the consensus from fellow yelpers was: fresh, quality, fast, inexpensive and pleasant staff. We decided to try it out...and I am SO, SO glad we did! It was absolutely all of these things! We were greeted by Helen when we arrived and she was very helpful when we ordered. My husband, Mom and I got the original gyro wrap with fries which happened to be the special. When it came out, it was surprisingly big (bigger than most gyros I've ordered at other restaurants) and very fresh. The meat was delicious and the sauce was divine. My children got the chicken gyro wrap and loved it. The steak fries were delicious and came out piping hot. My youngest daughter got the chicken tenders which she loved and my Dad got the steak sub--he said it was amazing. Everyone agreed that we'd be back when visiting Tampa and WISH we had a Zeko's in Richmond, VA so we could eat there way more often. Thank you so much for the Florida hospitality. If you're looking for good Greek/Mediterranean food, definitely give them a try!

Third time here. I ordered over the phone and was told 30 min wait, no problem...50 min later no food and informed I need to wait an additional 25 min. Unacceptable. I try to make my point that the delay should have been fully explained and to allow me to make the decision to wait or move on. Now I have no lunch and wasted an hour of my day and to insult to injury, I was treated poorly and the Muslim sister was rude and ignorant. Poor communication and a bad attitude, just lost my business for good.

I'll admit this place seemed a bit confused as to what exactly it wanted to be at first, so I can understand those initial customers' frustration. However, I've been here a few times now and they've really stepped up their game. The shop is quaint and cute, the food is good (coming from the same kitchen as Chabaa), and the to-go products are a nice touch. It's also cheaper than expected, as Thai cuisine is unnecessarily pricy for some reason. Overall, I hope Binto becomes the Thai version of Manayunk's Smiley's, as takeout places on Main Street are few and far between.

It was my first time. Have eaten Thai in various places places in the US, and was quite disappointing. The food lacked flavor, with poor consistency, for example the watered down curry dish for starters. They could not accommodate for our preference of flavors, "because the sauce is already made", is not good customer service. The waitress was very courteous and kind. Will not be returning there.

Always enjoy my meal here as eat in or takeout. Small casual place with just about 6 tables. I enjoy their selection of naan. Their raita is delicious. My girlfriend always orders samosas "to go" to stock up in her freezer as a snack.

We enjoyed the food (red curry and drunken noodles), really liked the thai iced teas, and the service was nice. The restaurant is clean and bright. There are lots of options and we liked it more than the other thai place we tried in Santa Barbara.
Update: Mediterranean plate and fried flounder are still amazing ! One of my favorite spots.

hassan now has dosa, an indian favorite similar to a crepe that is made of lentils and then stuffed with delicious things! such a great addition for the chilly weather as they are served piping hot and fresh... i think that hassan may be the only one making these in the philadelphia area so it's worth the trip. hassan the owner is one of the kindest people i know!
I was surprised to see that this place didn't have more 5 star reviews. Solid local joint. Nothing fancy but sometimes that's good. I come here to study a bunch. Always a solid choice.

First off, if you've ever been to Thai Orchid in Blue Bell this place will be a huge disappointment. It wasn't horrible, but it wasn't great either. If you want to order the lunch special, like I did, you better have cash on you because they won't accept cards unless you spend more than $15, therefore I was forced to spend more money because I almost never carry cash on me - was not a fan of that. I ordered the drunken noodles and asked for no onions (allergy) and they put them in anyway, so I had to send it back and wait for another to be made. I also ordered the spring rolls (again, because I was forced to if I wanted any food at all) As for taste, it was just okay - it was edible. No veggies in the drunken noodles. At Thai Orchid, there's green beans and zucchini (in place of onions) in the dish which makes it a more balanced meal. Overall, just a disappointing experience that I never intend to have again.
I wouldn't know if the food is any good. We sat there for ten minutes and no one even acknowledged us. They took the orders of people who sat there after us. First time last time for them.
Just FYI the pineapple fried rice comes with ONLY 2 Shrimp!!!! I asked the lady if really that's all it came with and she said yes. What a rip!!!

Only reason to be down in Chester PA, I had their jerk (can specify spicy or mild for you young'uns) in $7 small platter, the following week, tore up their Large $13 platter.. #FOODPORN, worth a trip, choice of white or rice with beans.. I split that latter with wife & somewhat picky daughter.. Finger wipe worthy! Just kidding

This is a great, locally owned place. The owners are wonderful! The bahn mi choices are great, but the pho is the way to go. I have also tried the egg roll vermicelli, and it was also really good. I really haven't tried anything I didn't like.

This place was amazing! We ordered a huge to go order to be picked up at 5:15 yesterday evening even when they open at 5. They were so accommodating and very personable. When we walked in to pick up the food it was almost all ready. Someone was there to greet us right away. The place looked very clean and put together. Staff was very friendly as well. The food was amazing! We had several dishes all spices to our liking. We will def be back

Just a mess... Food was horrible, and the service was really rude when we told them we didn't want the food. I only had a house wine so I don't know how the drinks are, but def not a good place for a good meal. Over priced and very poor taste.

I have eaten here on two different occasions . Both times I left feeling disappointed . The service was nice but the food is lacking in flavor . On one occasion I had the red curry( a Thai favorite of mine) with chicken as the meat. The chicken had no flavor at all. Every thing was just, a disappointing version of the real deal. The service was nice time. Nice/fancy atmosphere but the food just didn't taste as great.

I have had 2 experiences at Creazian. I figured i needed to give them a couple shots before i wrote my review. The first time we ordered Pho to-go. I was quite unimpressed. It had about half the meat I was expecting. I have had pho at a lot of different places and it was definitely much less than what I have experienced in the past. Flavors were nice, they didn't include the typical sides like the basil, jalapenos, bean sprouts, etc. Not sure if it was an oversight or just not apart of there menu. My second experience was another to go order (we ordered thru yelp). We decided to try some different items. We ordered the lo mein, the chicken ramen bowl, and the garlic beef plate. I was the most excited for the beef dish, and the traditional spring rolls. It was described as a garlic beef dish with heirloom tomatoes. NO tomatoes, no garlic, it tasted like beef simmered in soy sauce. Super salty. I was so sad. The spring rolls were fresh and tasty, and the peanut sauce was delicious. The ramen was good, but nothing extraordinary. I felt like for the price it was quite expensive and not special. All in all it was ok...but Im not sure I will be back.

We have a group of friends that goes to Zagol about once a month. We love it! Don't go if you're on a time crunch - this is not fast food. It is delicious, flavorful food prepared with great care by one woman. She's the hostess, chef and waiter and she's lovely. We love going with a group, taking our time catching up, sharing an amazing meal, and having a wonderful excuse to eat with your hands. The Zil Zil Tibs is a favorite - strips of beef and grilled onion that arrives sizzling on a cast iron platter. But really you can't go wrong. Give this spot a try!

Great improvement in customer service since last time! The buffet is great. The tandoori chicken at tandoor is the closest to the one back home in India. Chicken tikka was amazing. Will definitely visit again :) Thanks Brian!

I am visiting from California, and love Thai food and decided to check this place out. I ordered chicken pad Thai and spicy fried rice. Pros Bomb food, good size portions, and very good priced for lunch. I was seated right away even though the place was packed. They constantly filled my water which I think is a great plus when eating spicy food. Cons Ordered just chicken and it came with shrimp as well. Oh well it still was good and came with like 4 piece of shrimp each. I also asked for really spicy and was yet again let down. I usually am however at most Thai places. Overall I highly recommend this place for lunch or picking up to go. Very flavorful.

The food was amazing! I love Jamaican cuisine and this is one of the best in the area. I got the oxtails with rice and peas and side of cabbage. It was very flavorful and hardy portions. I called the order in and picked it up( quick service) I also tried a vegetable patty it was ok. Their beef patty was amazing. Flaky crust and moist meat. I wanted to get the jerk or fried wings but they didn't have them( hence the 4 stars otherwise I would have given them a 5. I would definitely be returning their when I get a taste for some yummy Jamaican food. Also, the restaurant is very unassuming and small.. Who knew such big flavor would be in this little gem.
Poor service, worse food, and there was a chunk of beef in my tofu dish.

Amazing food. I try new things every time I come here and it's always perfect. Definitely my favorite Indian place. Great relaxed atmosphere too. And it's BYOB! Favorites: Paneer Mangoli and Lamb Vindaloo

I drove in from Wilmington for this place. A friend of mine recommended it because I was looking for something different, but great. To say the least, I went away extremely satisfied and happy. I ordered 3 plates of food just to taste them and I was in foodie heaven. The price was inexpensive but the taste, my god the taste,...absolutely stunning! I Highly recommend! It is definitely worth the drive, but lock your car doors, not a great area. But under no condition let that stop you from going there. The food is worth it!
Has gone downhill. Doesn't even put spices on tables or soy sauce and fish sauce. Peanut chicle made totally different. Hey get more real Thai!!!!

Marjie's is delicious and the staff is great. Such a cute, casual new spot in an old house....we've sat inside but the back patio is our favorite. The ribs, fried chicken and tomato salad are must orders but everything is tasty!!

This place mediocre. The food had good flavor but they charged me 1.45 for a glass of ice water, really. Well that is it for me, I won't return and recommend walking past it because there are plenty of other establishments within walking distance.

Growing up in rural Indiana I had no access to Ethiopian food growing up. This was my first exposure to this cuisine and I loved it! We got the combination 1 for lunch. It was plenty of food to split between 2 people. A 3rd could probably join in if you weren't starving like us. The lamb, chicken, and beef dishes were amazing! The lentils and cabbage were also extremely flavorful. The bread was very satisfying with a nice sour tinge on the back taste. Wonderful restaurant. Will be back!

Simply Thai is "Simply Amazing"!!! Great food portions, great price, great location, GREAT service!!! My wife and I have our weekly date night at this Thai restaurant every single week. Best kept secret in NoCo!!!

First time I came here was yesterday based on the reviews and I was glad I went. The roti was great. Texture and freshness was the key and was even great heated up. My new spot for roti, definitely bc a lot of Jamaican or Caribbean spots in philly don't carry roti or they taste old. So again great spot, and they made me a new repeat customer.

Good food all organic and stuff for gluten free vegan hipsters but smaller portions and about 4 dollars more per dish than other places and expect to order extra rice if you get a curry dish. They have a limited simple menu which is smart for white ppl but as a thai person the dishes lack full flavor.

Fantastic! Groovy vibe, great service and food! The bacon phyllo tapas are worth going back for alone. I enjoyed the lamb chops...perfectly cooked and seasoned well. The cocktails we very good as well. We will definitely be back! If there was a down side, it was the on street parking, but since we got there early (5:30) on a weeknight, it was not a problem. Highly recommend this place!

**Disclaimer** I haven't actually been to the Jerk Hut for a number of years, but this was my absolute favorite restaurant when I was living in Philadelphia. Nice to know it's still open some 10 years after I moved out of Philly. For me the jerk chicken was the best thing going, followed by their "festival" and then the fresh juices. I was a poor student at the time, but I always managed to scrounge up the $$ to treat myself at the Jerk Hut. Back when I was a regular, the menu was pretty simple and I think that simplicity held the charm for me. Later I recall the expansion of the patio in the back and added selections to the menu. And I remember being really happy to see the place growing because by this point I had become friendly with the owner and her family. However sometimes expansion can be a bad thing especially *too much* expansion. So I am and I am not surprised to read the negative reviews. Hopefully they get things right soon.

What a great experience we had at Zoe's. The food is yummy and unique. I really like the Ham piadina. And the basil pesto hummus is awesome. But what was really special was the staff. My daughter has a peanut allergy and even though there are no actual peanuts in the restaurant, two of the servers went out of their way to tell me about a bean that's on one of their salads that have the same pheromone as a peanut. Just so we would feel safe. Wow!!! What a great establishment!!
I've been going here for 20 years and the quality of the food has never wavered. Every dish is prepared with care. The service is excellent, the prices are modest and it's quiet!

Wow, this place was really, really good! I found it by accident, and frankly had never heard of it. But it was excellent! You can smell the meat roasting on the fire from the parking lot, and it's the first thing you see when you step inside the door of this clean and neat dining room. (They also have bar and outdoor seating) The quality of the ingredients , and fresh herbs are such a welcome taste. Your choice of lamb chicken or pork , is made in pitas or along side of full plates. The salads are full of olives ,feta, leafy fresh greens, lemons( option of proteins on top as well) and sauces of your choice.You can choose Greek wine by the glass or bottle, as well as local craft beer. The staff was professional and welcoming. I will absolutely return, and tell anyone in my orbit about this true find!

Amazing Thai! Ordered delivery (all vegetarian) and it was "wow". Had Tom Yum Soup, Green Curry, Veg Duck Pennag Curry, Basil Fried Rice and Basil Tofu. Perfect spice level and flavorful. Best was Veg Duck Pennag Curry and Basil Fried Rice. I'll be back for more!

Like all Pho Hoa's, they all seem to be the same. I ordered the #15 pho with all the stuff in it and salad rolls. I still think that the Vancouver ones have a better soup broth but this is still decent. And for $5, 3 mini salad rolls is a good price. To be honest, walking up from 101 Street NW was an eye opener! I think coming on 97 Street NW would have been a better route from downtown. The staff were very friendly. It wasn't busy at all so what else were they to do? This place isn't overly fancy so maybe do your first date elsewhere. It was clean enough. I would suggest that they get proper soap dispensers in the washroom. I mean putting liquid soap in empty hot sauce bottles work....but come on?!? Go to Dollarama and spend the buck on a better bottle.

Really great find! The meals are so reasonably priced and the food was fresh. The peanut sauce was great and the sweet, almost pickled cucumber was wonderful. Also, the crab meat dish has real crab meat in it. Great value!

So I had some friends that have been nagging me for a long time to get me here. I wandered out and braved the freezing rain to go a kabob house. The place is sandwiched in the basement of a building on Samson between 15th and 16th and is frankly quite easy to miss if you aren't looking for their sign. The restaurant itself wasn't much to write home about either. The decor was just basic tables with a cloth of a map of Afghanistan with a glass slab on top , along with basic dining room chairs. It actually felt kind of homey, it was nice on a cold rainy night. So why does this place get 4 stars? The food. The food was absolutely fantastic. My friends I was with were vegetarians so we got mostly veggie food. I got just basic rice and lentils. The lentils were nice and buttery but not too much and seasoned very well. My friend got this cauliflower stew which was great as well. My only real complaint was that I felt it was a bit overpriced for the quantity of food. Overall, I really liked the kabob house and I will certainly be going back for their meat kabobs.
Tonight I had dinner buffet at tandoor food is excellent chutney chicken , butter chicken and veg gobhi mussalim I never had my life .food is to delicious I will back next time

I decided to take my family out for dinner, it was our first time eating at PF Changs. Everything was going great, I have ordered some appetizers and the waitress had brought out 4 small plates which I notice had food all over them. I told the waitress and she said "ugh" and apologize and got us more clean plates. Once our meals come out, I went to take the spoon out of my food to scoop some rice and it was hard food all over it. I alerted the waitress again and and told her I wasn't paying for the meal and me and my family was leaving. Since she was standing there in surprise I ask for her manager. The manager Evan come out and I let him know what happen. He took very good care of us and provided great service, he took care of the bill, give me a $30 gift card, and 4 cards for free appetizers, my son wanted a slice of the Great Wall of China cake to take home and he give us that. Evan also said when I come back ask for him and he would take care of me. Sorry, Evan....I don't think I will be returning, this was such a turn off and I can't get the pic of that spoon out of my mind.
Am still not sure what I ate here (chaat) but boy it was an explosion of all five senses. The Chaats are an explosion of flavors! Also try the lassis, can't go wrong!

This place, also called "Noodi", is BANGIN! I don't like the suburbs too much, but this is a reason to like Media, PA. I had to see a show that my friend was in at the Media Theater, and this Thai place is right there. So my Aunt Suzy and I go in and had the BEST dinner we've had in a long time. We ordered the appetizer sampler, which I believe is called the "Nadi Sampler", which was EXCELLENT. Then my aunt got Pad Thai and I got Woon Sen and everything was so delicious. They give you so much food, I had a gigantic lunch yesterday as well. I can't wait to go back! I have an audition at the theater in a few weeks, so maybe I'll catch the lunch special at this place. so good.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Went here for the lunch buffet which had delicious options at a great price. The service was incredible and we can't wait to go again! If you're trying to decide between Taj Mahal and another restaurant Taj Mahal is definitely worth it!

Alright, so, second party in the restaurant, two parties enter the restaurant after, and eat before. I ordered a dish, and was informed 20 min later that they didn't have the dish I ordered. My son ordered the duck soup.... Was... Very... Mediocre at best. Pho decent, prawns decent, ramen decent, tho the pork belly ROCKED. So far, best pork belly ever, sadly the rest of the experience was poor or mediocre.

I read a very recent review that said they have a new chef. May be the reason my experience this second time was bad. Waiter was overwhelmed. I ordered Thai basil chicken, but not too spicy. However I do like spice. The chef is screaming from the kitchen...."you no like spice, you don't get Thai". My dish was absolutely bland! I've had it before here and it was wonderful. Actually, I got beef not chicken as ordered! Mango salad is fabulous, but it took 25 minutes to get it. There was Only One other patron, who was served already, in the restaurant. May only go for take out. Service was Terrible. Waiter didn't care any more than chef did! Too bad, because food is good and fresh. Hope the manager reads these reviews!

Msg laden pho. Costs 4(?!?) extra dollars to upgrade the size of the bowl when the price of the pho is already higher than what it should be. Meat quality is terrible. And they nickel and dime you. Asked for a side of white onions and they said that it'll cost me. Never been charged for something as simple as a side of onions and I've been to my fair share of Vietnamese restaurants.

We came here late on a Sunday. We had been traveling all day and the gentleman on the phone suggested we could place an order and have it ready when we arrived. Brilliant! After eating we could continue our trip. I'm Indian and let me tell you these favors were authentic and delicious. We ordered the sag paneer, chicken tikka masala and malai kofta, as well as samosas. All dishes were served upon our arrival and they were very flavorful. The service was attentive and friendly. The restaurant itself is modern and immaculate. We had a great break from our journey. Oh, and we had gulab jaman for dessert and it was very good too. We wished we lived closer but we are hundreds of miles away.
SO YUMMY. Really you can't go wrong - snacks, dinner, brunch. The owners and staff are incredibly accommodating and kind. And you have to pick up some of the incredible desserts.

I go to this place often because of how friendly the owner guy is, and the fact that there aren't very many asian food places in IV in the first place. Overpriced compared to Noodle City and Saigon, but the proximity to campus is worth the money. Pho is pretty decent, not the best but definitely good enough. Egg rolls are amazing. Waiters often lack in service, like bringing water, but it won't be a problem once you go there enough and they recognize your face.

This place is fabulous! The menu, which had a mixture of Greek and authentic Italian cuisine, was quite extensive and everything looked awesome. I opted for a very tasty shrimp pasta dish. Most dishes were under $10; I think the most expensive item on the menu was a veal dish at just over $16. The food was homemade with fresh ingredients, and the portions are a healthy size. I've heard great things about the pizza, so I'm looking forward to going back and trying it soon! The owners have paid much attention to detail from the trendy atmosphere to the excellent service. This place turned out to be a great find in an unlikely location. I'm excited that this place opened - it could really help bring back the Bevo neighborhood. FYI - Laganini serves breakfast lunch and dinner, closing at 9 p.m. They are located at Gannett and Gravois, next to Bosna Gold.

The 4 star rating is soley based on the food. We ordered the shrimp pil pil and grilled octopus appetizers, then split the whole grilled sea bass. The shrimp pil pil is a dish of shrimp lightly dusted in flour then cooked in a cherry pepper and garlic paste. In general, I find it blasphemy to coat seafood and fry it, but this shrimp was an exception. It has a nice crispy crunch on the outside, perfectly cooked on the inside and smothered in a delicious, flavorful paste. This is not a dish for those who do not like garlic. The grilled octopus was exactly what you would imagine. Fresh octopus grilled and served in a lemony light sauce. Sauce might be stretching it, as it was more of a clear broth. Anyway, it was pretty good but I still preferred the shrimp pil pil. (Note: I recently had the octopus dish at LIttle FIsh so with such an outstanding dish in recent memory, it is not surprising that Dmitri's octopus would pale in comparison.) For the entree, we had the grilled sea bass. I love whole fish. The fish was cooked perfectly and presented beautifully. The rice and escarole sides were unmemorable, just as other reviewers commented. Finally, the pita bread they served was delicious. I loved the taste of the smoky grill on the bread, although I have to admit the interior tasted almost gummy like it was just a minute or 2 undercooked (underbaked?). The "baguette" should not even be served at all. It tasted like mediocre italiam bread in the shape of a baguette. Even though my review and rating was supposed to be solely based on the food, I feel I should comment on the atmosphere. My recommendation is to avoid this place on a busy night. You are crowded into tables so it feels like communal seating and it is so loud you can barely have a decent conversation without yelling. Despite the less than ideal atmosphere, the food is still worth it.
First time here. Food tasted great!!! Portions where just right. Not like other places where they serve you a couple of pieces of meat. Will return for sure!!! Service was excellent!

Most important trait of an indian place to me is that it appears clean when you go there, check the box on that one. Though service was kind of slow (I think they were unprepared for a Sunday evening surge) the wait staff was kind and attentive. I had spicy lamb rogan josh and the level of spice certainly cleared my sinuses. Honestly not the best Rogan Josh I've ever had but not bad. My date had Chicken Tikka Marsala and it was "the bomb.com" fantastic. The Naan was just out of the oven or wherever it comes, yum! We had Mango Lassis for dessert and they did not disappoint! I will come back, I think I've found my little indian joint.
It was great, totally reasonably priced and delicious. I will definitely be going back.
Best pho I've had in Indy! The ingredients are so fresh and delicious. I definitely recommend this to anyone wanting Vietnamese.

Went here last night on a saturday weekend of fourth of july. Arrived about 7pm place has about 16 tables and was about 1/2 full. The decor is awesome. Its like eating inside a big tent. There are drapes or tapestries on every inch of the walls. We had the 7 course feast and enjoyed it alot. Food came out at a great pace and service was excellent. We had the waiter laughing by the time we left. I especially liked the lamb with honey. This place would be awesome for a group of 4 or more.

You know that a Honduran restaurant is good when you sit down and the first thing that the waitress says is, "I don't speak English." Indeed, no one here spoke English except for me and my dining companion and that was just fine with me. We were given a menu, and although it is completely in Spanish, there are pictures of the food on the menu and some of the stuff is pretty easy to figure out, as it is basic Latin food. Everything in the menu sounded really good. I decided on the Honduran tacos. They were delicious hard tacos that were rolled and fried with chicken inside. They were topped with lettuce, tomato and huge slices of avocado. I posted a picture, if you want to check it out. It was so good! The tacos were huge and I finished two and took the rest home. They cost $8 and it was definitely a good meal for that amount of money. I will definitely be back. On my way out I noticed that someone had ordered something that looked like a quesadilla, so I will probably try that. Don't be put off that no one here speaks English or that it's in a shady looking strip mall. It's worth it.

This is a very good Indian restaurant with a charming owner who went out of her way to serve my six year old. The naan is outstanding as is the butter chicken and the saag paneer. Very highly recommended.

The tom yum soup is super yummy! I've tried a couple other noodle dishes here as well and they are a little too sweet for me. I had to add a lot of hot sauce. Service is good. I will definitely be coming back for more soup!

OMG!! It's a must-go to eat the food are excellent! Never pass this one or you'll regret it. My whole family had enjoyed are dinner here in The Pearl Restaurant.We all had different orders and all was excellent. We came home talking about this restaurant and we're coming back for another night.

One of my favorite places in Wilmington, also one of the few places open late! Excellent food with a unique variety. From burgers and fish to their asian fusion, I've enjoyed everything I've had here.
