First time here. Slow service. 40 minutes for 2 drinks and 1 shaved ice with less than half of the cafe occupied. Strawberry smoothie with boba tasted like sour strawberry ice cream....

If you want overpriced Thai food this is the place for you! The owner is not accommodating for what the customer wants. I asked for vegetables separate from the chicken fried rice. The owner said the cook could not do this because we are busy... I guess 4 people in the restaurant is too busy for them.. We had leftovers , asked for extra chutney.. waitress brings a thimble sized container..asked for more.. owner said we will need to charge you for more... Sorry but you lost our business!! You are a joke... 0 stars. Oops can't rate 0 stars...

I eat here probably at least 2x/ month so obviously I love it. The only reason I don't give them 5 stars is the variation in dishes from 1 visit to the next. Spice level differs depending on whose cooking. The people here are very friendly and usually understand enough English to answer basic questions. One of my favorites is kea mai noodles with tofu. Great flavor They have beer and wine. They also have a new back patio but I had never seen anyone out there.

If I'm going to eat out I definitely want to eat things I can't make at home. A decent curry is on the list of things I've tried and have failed miserably to prepare well! I've driven by this place more times than I can count on one hand, but never really knew what their deal was! I assumed, based on the name, that they sold bottled spices and sauces. I was wrong, and I'm glad I know now because I loved it and I will be back. Favorite tidbits: -This place was impeccably clean and inviting! The modern decor made it stand out quite a bit from other joints who serve similar food. -The opportunity to sample EvErYtHiNg. Definitely helpful when ordering new foods! -Incredibly kind, outgoing, inviting and helpful staff! -They've got BOGO coupons in a couple of local coupon books (Entertainment, etc.) -The takeout containers for the bowls are sturdy and are not going to leak! -The bowl is a great value: 1 rice, 1 curry and 1 chutney in a bowl. The portion was definitely very generous and could easily be shared. Least favorite tidbits: -I waited at the counter for about 30 seconds before anyone came out from the kitchen area to greet me. But, he came out and apologized profusely and welcomed me right away!

Crystal BBQ Noodle House used to be the Jasmine Noodle House - in fact, the original signage on the purple awning over the door remains, with a Crystal BBQ sign in the window. We were not sure at first we were even in the right place. Upon entering, our olfactory senses were filled with the smell of barbecue meat, and we saw a table of people cooking their own food on one of those little portable stoves. Were we in a noodle house or a barbecue restaurant? Our menus indicated noodle house. The majority of the menu were the typical dishes expected in a Vietnamese noodle house, especially pho (noodle soup) and vermicelli bowls. I opted for a rare beef pho, while my co-worker had a steamed chicken pho. For appetizers, she chose a half order of shrimp salad rolls while I had green onion cakes. Our appetizers were brought while I sipped my jasmine tea, rich in flavour. My onion cakes were crispy and delicious. My co-worker raved about her salad rolls. We both looked around and kept admiring the beautiful decor of the dining area. With anticipation, we looked forward to our soups arriving. After a short while, two steaming bowls of pho were placed before us. My bowl was big enough, but did not seem to have as much broth as I am used to. There were loads of noodles though, and I dipped my spoon in to taste the broth. Alas, there was not much flavour - the only seasoning I could really taste was salt. I would have put some of the herbs served typically served to the side, but all we were given was a tiny plate with a few sprouts, a lime wedge, and a leaf that I had never seen before when having pho. The meat tasted good enough - all six slices of it, which were already cooked through by the time the bowl arrived at the table (rare beef pho is supposed to be served rare). Colleen had a similar experience with her soup. Although she doused the broth with salt and soy sauce, she commented that it was flavourless. The tiny shreds of chicken tasted good - almost too good. We suspected they were processed or laden with MSG. Neither of us finished our soup, nor took home the leftovers. The prices are slightly higher than other noodle houses, so I could not understand why the portions of meat were so small. While paying the bill, our server explained that they had kept the lunch menu from the previous owners, and the evening menu was barbecue. Judging from the rich, meaty smells that greeted us, I am willing to bet the barbecue is not bad - however, given how bad our soups were, neither of us are willing to return to find out. Here is a suggestion: if you take over a restaurant, don't try to be all things to all people. Either change the menu to what you do best, or learn how to prepare the existing menu items properly. Any pho lover would have been disappointed by their meal - we sure were.
Ordered take out from here for lunch. The falafel was pretty good. Salad was meh, something you could probably make better at home.

This place is delicious, and I'm saying this as somebody who adores Thai cuisine and has tried a lot of it. The food is always fresh, prepared well and authentic. The owners are very nice and the staff is attentive and knowledgeable about the food. The only downfall would be the strip mall location and decor, but when it comes down to it the food is what really matters. Some favorites of mine (I am vegetarian) are the Tom Kha Gai soup, the crispy tarot root appetizer, the lettuce wrap appetizer, vegetarian green curry, and the vegetarian pad thai. I prefer this place to the other local Thai place, Thai L'elephant (even though this place is very good as well and the ambiance is definitely of a higher level. As are the prices). If you are going for the quality and flavor of the food, I recommend Thai Place.
One of the best restaurants in downtown Trenton. The jerk chicken with rice and cabbage was spectacular. Service was friendly. I can't wait to go there again.

I went there one afternoon to meet up with a friend. I have to say the latte I had was great..Soy chi. Really lovely tasting and the atmosphere was good. It was just really really crowded in there. That is my only criticism, we basically had people standing over us, hovering and waiting for our table. I think its the lay out..its not the greatest.
Good food and reasonable prices. A nice place to eat near the beach.

I love the atmosphere of this cafe. Very cozy and welcoming, amazing hummus and naan! The food is on the cheaper side and the portions are larger than average. I love how this cafe accommodates varying food preferences: vegan, vegetarian, and gluten free. Vegan cakes! Mmmm. Well known for their Chai, which you can get with whole, skim, almond, or soy milk. I definitely recommend the Vanilla Roobios Chai. You can't go here without trying it! Only recommendation would be to serve food instead of yelling out the order. It can get crowded at times with everyone ordering and picking up their orders at the till. Other than that, awesome!

This simple family restaurant, with its friendly and solicitous service, is a good place to satisfy one's hankering for Indonesian home-style food. The menu covers pretty much all the standard dishes subsumed under the catch-all term "Indonesian" and is broadly divided into noodle and rice plates, some organized in the fashion of a (modest) colonial Dutch rijstafel (a style of eating that allowed for sampling food from different areas). We started with the egg noodle dish Mie Komplit, a combination plate that included BBQ pork, shredded chicken, vegetables, and eggs (hard boiled). Rice platters we tried included the Rendang beef platter and a combination platter of various meats and vegetables. The noodles were nicely prepared, as was the rice, and the diverse accompaniments tasty, if of somewhat differing quality (the pork belly had been around for a while). The soups that came with these plates had a clean but thin chicken taste. One minor quibble I have is that the temperature of the food was not as hot as I would have liked it to be. All this delectable eating comes at astonishingly low prices. The tea served is hot and always quickly replenished with another pot, the ice coffee serviceable. The attentiveness and generosity of the service must be mentioned here again, maybe that is one of the reasons, besides the home-spun food, that so many Indonesian families eat at Sky Cafe.

For our first delivery in Indy, we decided to go all in and order Indian food. Haveli's serving size was quite generous for the price and both meat-eater and vegetarian agreed that it was some of the better Indian food we'd had. Delivery was quick but at some point I'd like to get the full experience and eat in the downtown location. Yum!
Matsaman curry was good. Very good deal, the portion was big enough ,interesting decoration in the restaurant! Satisfied with my meal:)
First off, Pho is fo loners. I ate my giant amazing pho by myself, alongside 3 other loners, it was great pho!!! I mean it guys... I'll be coming back again like tomorrow. #pholoners

We had been here for dinner last night and went with the Vegetarian feast option. The food was pretty decent, the only thing that's bugging me is that we were given pickles in the bowl and we felt it didn't go with the concept of Mediterranean cuisine. The Harissa sauce could definitely have been more spicier. P.S - love the pitas !
Thanks Kelly. Tried it today and had a great gyro. My friend didn't enjoy his falafel that much but he really liked the biryani.
Absolutely A-MA-ZING Vietnamese food! Spring rolls - wow. Pho (chicken rice noodle soup) is exquisite. Beef stew (with carrot) with bread is outstanding. Yellow bean coconut dessert is super yummy.

I AM IN HEAVEN. I am still eating this magical meal as you read this. The experience I am having prompted me to share right away so that you can have the same experience I am having now. First of all- I am here from out of town and for the past 4 days of trying different restaurants in this area: I have been physically sick, grossed out and flat out disappointed in the area's local selections. I am so glad I discovered this hidden gem! They delivered to my hotel within minutes, which is a relief as all the other places take at least 45min. This hot, new concept: Chinese- Indian fusion is so unique so hopefully it will make it's way to my area out in Arizona! One thing about the menu is that it is long, therefore it may be challenging or overwhelming to determine what is best to order.. But per the chef's recommendation, and now my recommendation... you MUST order: apps: 8. Gobi Manchurian ( crispy cauliflower in chili garlic sauce) 14. Chicken 65 soup: Tom Yam (chicken) Entree: 1. Shrimp Goan Curry Spread the word guys- I want this concept to expand in the U.S culinary world!

Completely authentic, the food has become a family favorite for us. We struggle with placing an order as the staff often doesn't speak English. We've never allowed that to bother us. They are kind and happy to help us place our orders! We often stick to the Spicy Pork, The BBQ Ribs and the Beef. We always get at least a double order of the dumplings. And all the side dishes are fantastic. You may think you can't do it - but you can and you'll be proud you did. It is really tough to tell you how much we love this place.

Great food...call ahead and place your order though cause the place is small. The oxtails are so tender they fall off the bone. Great find in the middle of chambersburg. If it's only for one, I recommend small order or large of you want left overs. Oh and bring cash because they charge you extra if you pay with a card.

I ordered the Southwest chop with gyro meat. The gyro meat was very dry and the lettuce was one second away from turning brown. And there was a bug leg or antenna on my tomato. I accidentally confused this place with Pita Pit which is right around the corner and with much better food. I will not be visiting again!
Try the fish with the rice & beans with fish gravy...YUM!!! Everything that I tasted from here was very good

I have tried here buffet for over 5 times and all the times its okay in taste, flavor, and presentation. Spice kitchen has good interiors and attracts lot of non Indians who want spice levels to be low. For a typical desi this would be okay place for buffet with low to medium spice levels, veg curries are good, chicken can better, biryani is okay overall some people might like it and some people don't. For me it lacks the taste, spice levels, and punch that I'm fond of so I would pass on this. I have not yet tried at Spice kitchen at Lansdale yet. It can be seen that Spice kitchen owners give a lot of attention to ambiance, waiters(all non indians), and cleanliness but food is average. This is not the typical desi restaurant, this has its own style statement. "Spice kitchen lacks spice but try once and decide for yourself"

Finally got around to trying Zaika today. Food was very good; however it was a bit difficult to tell initially as the spice level was definitely not even along the same scoville scale as I ordered. Way too hot for mild. That said the food was tasty and portions ample, more than enough for two or three or maybe four, which was really challenging for me as I'm the only Indian food lover in the house, so I will be eating vegetable Biryani for weeks. I got take out and the young woman who waited on me was helpful and absolutely delightful. I will definitely be going back, but will choice other less heat provoking options. Than you Yelpers of a good recommendation.

Delicious, authentic Indonesian food. We had the kwetiau goreng and lontong sayur. Both were generous portions and brought back memories of Indonesia. Having lived in Medan, Indonesia for 9 months, I was thrilled to discover that the owners are from Medan. Definitely trying the nasi campur Medan next time! I highly recommend this place to anyone who misses Indonesia or just wants some Indonesian food.

The food is just plain good. I dig the pho big time and it is a staple for me. The customer service is good. Seating is tight as there is always a crowd of patrons in this joint. Yep it is hooked on to a gas station with a Wendy's fast food joint on the other side; if you're too uppity for this type of setting you're selling yourself short on the best Vietnamese food in Reno (In my humble opinion).

Awesome authentic Thai food with fresh ingredients and of course, served with a smile. Preeda,the owner, was very friendly and helpful. We had the green papaya salad, Thai beef salad, pad Thai, and the red curry. The papaya salad was amazing and by far my favorite. We will go again and everything we ordered was a hit.

This place is great! The chicken tikka masala was delicious and spiced just right. The chicken biryani was also wonderful. Even better, the service was great! Have been to other restaurants where the people working weren't terribly friendly but the owner was just lovely.

Excellent jerk chicken. Flavorful with a good kick! Had sides of fried plantains and couscous. Everything was really good. Place was empty for a late Tuesday lunch (1:00), but service was still friendly and prompt. Several other menu items I look forward to trying on a future visit.

We wanted to try this place after seeing great reviews but were surprised it was empty at noon on a Thursday(day before 4th of July). This gave us reluctance but we tried it anyway. boy are we glad we did. The lunch was perfect and so was the service. We were amazed at the quality of the meats and my beef was like a very good steak. All of the food was exceptionally fresh and of high quality. Very good attention to detail. Now we can't wait to try them for dinner. We both had the lunch special which was very reasonably priced and cost about the same as the usual burger place but much healthier.

Summary: - Great Thai food with awesome flavours - Very good value for money - Quiet simple space with friendly service Detailed review: I've found my new favourite Thai place in Edmonton! My wife and I were here for dinner on a Tuesday and we had the following: - Som Tum mango salad -- primarily shredded green mango (not ripe and a bit sour) with shrimp in a spicy fish-sauce dressing; it's a party in your mouth! - Chu Chee shrimp curry -- shrimp in a very comforting red curry sauce; served on top of basil leaves with provides a nice flavour blast - Crispy chicken in garlic sauce -- fried half chicken that's topped with fried garlic and served with a garlic sauce; needless to say, perfect for garlic lovers - Veggie Pad Thai with tamarind sauce -- tasty and no ketchup, 'nuff said - Black sticky rice with mango (dessert) -- loved how the rice was both sweet and crunchy and it's perfect with very ripe mango We were stuffed after the meal and had some leftovers. I think there are some really good Thai places in Edmonton but find many of them pricey - couldn't say that about this meal as all the dishes were reasonably priced and delicious. Will definitely return!

I had a BUG in my soup. I reported to the server. Server took the food and after three minutes, brought a new soup. But seriously, no apologies? I NICELY told her that it might be a good idea to say sorry next time. She said " i didnt make the food and you got the food. Why do i have to say sorry?" Server should be responsible with the food they deliver to the customer. When we turned around to go out we could clearly hear her swearing. Such a bad service. Never going back again nonetheless of food quality. Waste of tip.

I have only eaten 1 item from here. I don't speak Thai, and that makes it tough for me to remember what it's called. It's a squid dish, with seaweed, cucumber and a couple other ingredients. When I order this item I don't ever remember what it's called so I end up with the wrong thing. THEY ALWAYS FIX IT FOR ME! The service is fantastic! My wife won't eat Thai food so I don't have this as an option very often at all. I give all 5 stars for the squid dish I order, and the service. The dining room is nice, and clean looking, as well as the kitchen and sushi area look well maintained, and clean as well.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: When the owner brought our food to us, he said, "you are about to have the best Indian food you have ever had." He was right. Great complex flavors, super fresh, delicious! The dishes are a bit pricey but the portions are generous.

My bf took me to Fez for my birthday last year. Not bad.... we had chicken with olives. (Very tender!!!! ) It was dark as I-don't-know-what, inside the restaurant and I could BARELY see my menu!!! I can tell you this, though.... I didn't eat everything that was brought out to me! I ate the bread and salad, but didn't care much for the vegetable cous-cous. I enjoyed my mint tea and pastries.... and loved that steamed towels were brought out to us in between each course to clean your hands. We also got a hookah. I took a few puffs and didn't think it was anything special, since I'm not a smoker. Would I go again? Not sure. The atmospohere was cool and fun, but the food was nothing special. Also the belly-dancer had clearly seen better days, and it was pretty annoying the way she lingered at my table until my bf tipped her. LOL

This place is a great find. It's tucked away in a little corner of a strip mall. the only reason i found it was because I went to a music shop next door. Anyhoo, the place is great. Good prices, great food!!

Coming from Vancouver I've experienced some amazing Vietnamese cuisine and I enjoy the variety it has to offer. I also like how clean and fresh the food normally is. I was hungry and just saw this place so I stopped for a quick bite. They had a sign outside advertising their Bun Bo Hue soup which I normally like. I decided to try it out. I received a pot of tea and a plate of fresh sprouts, Thai Basil, a wedge of lemon and a red chili pepper which is all standard. When I received the large bowl of soup I noticed something that I wasn't used to, a large pile of fresh cabbage right in the middle. I wasn't sure if I'd like that but I actually really enjoyed the addition. The soup broth was quite good, the noodles were exactly how it should be and there was a good amount of meats. All in all I would give the food a 4/5 stars but I would remove a 0.5 star if I could because the price was $10.25 which is around $3 more than I'm used to in Vancouver. I guess I'll just have to get used to paying more! PS. my waiter was a 10 year old boy which was the son of the owners. He did a good job but it was a little weird.

Oh my, I thought I knew good pho... I was wrong. Very wrong. I had the vegetarian pho. It was broth perfection. The perfect balance of veggies/tofu/noodles, and everything was cut to perfect size for easy-eating (a hard thing to find in pho dishes, it seems). The atmosphere isn't dynamite perfection, but what does that matter when you're hunkered down in a cozy booth with a steamy bowl of soul-warming pho in front of you?

This is the best Thai food in Goleta in my opinion. I always get the drunken noodle with tofu and it's SOOO good. The service is always great when I'm in and it's not too pricey for a sit in Thai place.

Ask the owner for suggestions! He's amazing. I had never had chaat before so he talked me through all the options and eventually just had him give me the most simple item- samosa chaat. Be sure to emphasize that vegan because yogurt sauce is a default ingredient.
Great place! The dumplings are a little salty but the Mapo tofu and the kung pao chicken are great.
Really enjoyed the pho. Service was a bit slow, but they were kind. Also really liked the tapioca smoothies!

Had a reservation on a Saturday night, was seated promptly and attended to soon after we sat down. The environment here is terrible. Awful lighting, furniture, carpet that looks like it belongs in someone's basement. I'd have thought they would have udpated the decor once it turned over from Nonni's to Avalon, but they didn't. It is very very loud, which doesn't really bother me. For the price point, I'd rather go to a nicer looking place. We got the "Meat and Cheese" board which was great, but overpriced (around $30) and 2 pasta dishes. It was just eh.

I saw yelp reviews for this newly opened Indian restaurant and decided to give it a chance. I am glad I did ! The food was delicious. I and my friends ordered chicken chilli, malai kabab, vindaloo chicken , garlic naam and Biryani. Everything was at a proper heat level we specified. The malai kabab especially were Soooo soft and melt in the mouth .. total wow! Every food items were well prepared , fresh and really tasty! Also a mention to the owners, they were really really sweet. I am going back to try their buffet next! Hope they don't dissappoint.

Visiting from out of town and actually planned to go to Stella's next door. We were able to get a seat outside with no wait on mother's day, the weather as great, the staff was super friendly and the food was delicious. Everything was reasonably priced too- fantastic experience, would definitely recommend and eat here again!
Last visit to Sam's for a party of 5 - every single serving of fish was over cooked. How can one claim to be a seafood restaurant and almost burn every dish served to iur table?

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Amazing food. We always stop at Indian restaurants when we are really hungry and tired. This one met all of our expectations and far surpass them. Delicious chai. Amazing food and extraordinary naan. Try the ginger and chili naan. Uhmmm... I already want more.

I have passed this restaurant a thousand times and have been curious about their food. To celebrate my birthday, my husband and I finally went! I'm so glad we did! It was everything I had hoped for. I'm no pho expert, but I savored every bite of the #51 pho beef and flank steak. The meat was a perfect rare and sliced perfectly thin so the hot broth cooked it....well, perfectly! My husband ordered the #56 Hu tieu/mi thap cam. He said he would definitely order that again. He's a very tough customer to please, so hearing him say that is amazing! We also went with the appetizer Sampler and fried tofu with sweet chili sauce. My favorite was the lemongrass beef! No room for anything sweet at the end though I really wanted to try the mango bubble tea. There's always next time!

I have been here a few times, but this is my first time reviewing. Everything is wonderful, esp. the Pho's. I have sent numerous friends here and they all come back saying they loved it as well. This is as authentic as you can get.

It's a very risky game to play when restaurants start down this path I call the "soup Nazi" path. It's when they start to act like you as the customer are just lucky that they feel like maybe making you something to eat today. And they're certain that the food is so good that no matter how they treat you, or how long it takes - they will still have a line out the door. This works for some places - but only if they truly do have something very special to offer. The food here is not on that level. It's fine, maybe even good - but nowhere near good enough for their level of arrogance. As I type this - I am sitting in their dining room at 2pm and there are maybe 12 people in here just waiting.. We all look lost and confused. No one has food and we've all been waiting 20 minutes or more. My wife and I don't even have our drinks. We may just walk out. I just saw a customer spray and wipe off her own table. This place will never get my business again and they don't deserve anyone's. Pride comes before the fall.

This is my first time eating here and was recommended by friends. The crab with house made cilantro and basil noodles was delicious! My wife said the toasted coconut creme brûlée was the best she has ever had.

Very rarely do I post a real bad review. But I want the manager of this place to know that something is wrong with the food. It was very "off" tasted odd I think that the broth was somehow burnt. Maybe the chef made a mistake. And please start offering new things. I'm sure your kitchen can go beyond the norm. thanks you

I really wanted to love 8th, but after multiple visits I'm just not incredibly impressed. I love the atmosphere, and their fried chicken sandwich is really good. However, service can be slow, the pho (both meat and veggie options) are very bland, and other meals have been off. My partner's sister got the cauliflower sandwich once, and it was just a soggy slice of cauliflower on a bun. I actually liked the taste, but she couldn't eat it. There is a good beer selection, which is why I'll continue to patronize this business. I'm hoping I'll be able to boost this review after a few more visits and some improvement!

Best lunch buffet, Indian or otherwise, in town! I have been a frequent guest of Shere Punjab since about 2004, and my lunch there today solidified its standing in my mind as the best Indian food in Tucson. Sure, Saffron is fancy and all, but its also kinda Americanized. This place is pure authentic, and the quality is outstanding. The lunch buffet is what its all about. Come here around noon on any given day, and the place is going to be packed. I was lucky to get a table today. Their selection is always great, and though it changes up from day to day, there is always something for everyone. One of my only gripes about the place is that they do not label their dishes on the buffet, but there are a few rules to the buffet that should help you along: at the start point is always the desserts, sauces, and salad, followed immediately by tandoori chicken and Naan (btw, this is the only indian buffet in tucson where the naan is actually ON the buffet line, so you have as much as you want--AWESOME!). After that, you will find two meat dishes; one is going to be chicken, the other will be either lamb or beef. Then you will find samosas (best samosas in tucson, imho) and basmati rice. Finally, there are 4 vegetarian dishes, 1 of which will always be Saag. The saag at shere punjab is a bit sweeter than most places, but its truly delicious. The buffet is always well stocked, all the way up to its closing time of 2:30. At times, they may run out of naan or samosas, but you can return to your seat assured that within 5 minutes, there will be plenty available again. Nothing is bland here. Everything is cooked to perfection and spiced magnificently. Just phenomenal. The buffet, after tax, comes to $8.50 even. That's really quite a good deal considering what you get, and the quality of everything involved. I never understand it, but every time I go for lunch, there are several people ordering off the menu. Look, any Indian food connoisseur knows not to order off the dinner menu! Indian restaurants are famous for nickle and diming on non-buffet items. Why would you pay the same amount for 1 very small plate of food with no rice or bread as you would for as much as youd like to eat of 10 different dishes plus sides and desserts? It just makes no sense to me. I always have a strong urge to get up and tell these people, "Hey! Youre doing it all wrong!!!" My only other minor grievance with the place is that if you go later in the buffet hours, theres almost always this older man wearing a turban who sits at the very last table and glares disapprovingly at all the clientele. I have no idea what he does for the restaurant, since Ive never seen him move. Whatever he does, its a little off-putting, but ultimately im usually way to romantically involved with my curry to be bothered. I just think they should set up a chair in the kitchen or something for the guy... Anyway, if you want really good Indian food in Tucson, this is the only place really worth your time (gandhi?...eh, maybe if youre short a buck or two). Just make sure you go for the buffet and dont be tempted by the menu!

My favorite Indian restaurant in Tucson. The ingredients are fresh, and the taste is flavorful without being heavily salted, something I have found in other Indian restaurants. The chili chicken and palak paneer are my fallbacks. The mango chutney has a wonderful ginger flavor.

Not an easy choice on South Grand, but we went here for lunch, and it was...odd. We stood for ten minutes as this woman kept sweeping by us nervously with her head down. We were confused, and finally asked for a table. She seemed bowled over by our request, and put us at a dingy table inside. Scary interior with some possibly authentic Thai trinkets, felt like a Thai haunted house that was serving mediocre lunch before they open. The food is listed as vegetarian, but it's not vegan. You can taste the butter, which is orally unnecessary in Thai food except to please white audiences. The same woman turned several people away after we sat, and she seemed to be struggling with service and sanity. She was sweeping, like a lot, and definitely paid more attention to the floor than to us as customers. The tea is gross, but good luck telling your server that. I tried - I think she thought I was complimenting it? I'm not sure. The food was equally off-putting. Spring rolls with lettuce in them? Seems A) super cheap, and B) not authentic at all. The sauces were okay, but you could easily do all of this at home and do it better than these struggling, geriatric custodians. And the curry dish we ordered, well, it just tasted like butter to me at first bite, so to me, that was also gross. My friend nominally said "it's not so bad," which means it was actually terrible. Go literally anywhere else on Grand, except maybe The King & I, which is just as bad but with worse ingredients. If you're craving Thai food in STL? Get out to Delmar Loop, or buy the ingredients at Jay's and get your lazy tuckus in the kitchen! Do not spend your money here, unless you are desperate/pathetic and/or a jolly white person on hir lunch break...

The half chicken, with rice and beans special incredibly good! for not much money. Seriously the chicken and beans are some of the best I've ever tasted. My gf and I walked from a nearby hotel but they actually have their own parking lot. The owner is great and Ms. Maria was very pleasant and took care of us. I hope they do well there and we'll be sure to visit again the next time we're in Philly,would love to try some of the other dishes on the menu. Salud!

Holy..... food is crazy different but so good. Everything is homemade even the cheese. The ingredients are very high quality. The chicken is free range, the beef is farmed raised. The beers are ok but they have non-ethopian ones you can have if you want. All in all it is great date cause they bring out the man courses on this dish u share and eat with your hands. Awesome!!

Excellent. Favorite place to get Indian food, and one of the best restaurants in general. Paneer tikka masala is amazing. They just need to offer more mint chutney. I would buy a pint off the menu. Its good

I had GiGi and Big R at the Made in America Festival. Whilst traveling from stage to stage you encounter your food trucks, your beer stands and promo booths. GiGi's truck stood out almost immediately. Aside from the crazy long line, there's the menu. Amongst a plethora of what I'll call carnival or boardwalk food.. The thought of big food platters of jerk chicken, oxtail and fried chicken was like a blessing! The prices were damn reasonable considering what other places charged. Servings are grandma sized, like how you'd expect your nana to throw down a plate for you, so it's a ton of food. The line was crazy, we sat on this line for near an hour and we fought and pushed out way to the front to get to this group of tired but smiling group of 4 women serving food. I had the oxtail, rice and beans, Mac and cheese. Hot damn. So good. I got transported back to the West Indies for a quick second. The sounds of the concert drowned out. The clouds stopped moving. Time stopped. All I was tasting was the delicious strewed meat, perfect rice and devilish mac and cheese. Right then and there it hit me. Only in America can we have these experiences. A Vietnamese dude with his British-Indian wife, sitting on the grass amongst a sea of people, listening to Meek Mill (R.I.P. btw #backtoback) and eating oxtail. Made in America.

I was a little confused about which door to walk into, but once I was in (front door :) ) there was authentic Italian music playing and the atmosphere couldnt be beat! Well,k maybe by the food, which was insanely awesome. Get the Zeppoli. Just do it, even though you will be tempted by the other brilliant dessertss, just steal tastes off your friends plates :)

The suitor and I eat here at least once a month and it's usually very good and VERY reasonably priced. The service is friendly, but not always the most attentive. We ate there last night and I ordered something new: a lightly battered spicy chicken dish with vegetables--or at least that is the way it was described on the menu. In actuality it turned out to be a very bland dish served alongside some sauteed onions and a few pieces of red bell pepper. There was absolutely no heat to the dish, despite the hot red pepper designation on the menu. I would have told our server this, but we never saw him again until he brought our check. I'll still eat here, but I think that I'll stick with pho and some of their noodle dishes.

We dined here on a wonderful evening and made resi through OT. Had a great table outside and food was alright ... Oysters, grilled octopus (ok sort of mushy), po boy,swordfish special (just ok), beet salad, tuna appetizer. All very decent. Service, disappointing. My husband did not get his meal until after everyone else ate. His salmon topper and salad dressing arrived 20! Min past the other 4 diners in our party , and they didn't even comp it. Hm. Would have given 4 stars , but More like 2.5. The 3 is generous.

This place is my absolute favorite restaurant in Nashville. Small and in a neighborhood that only attracts locals (thank goodness!!) it is the only place we will have thai curries in the city. Thai Taste is family owned and ran and on any given day you will find the owner and her teenage daughter at the helm. We absolutely love the casual conversations with Tina and her family. We are protective of this place and on a couple of occasions have let offenders know that this isnt a place for snobbery. You will wait for quality and every time we order we experience new flavors in our favorite dishes. We're not here for chain restaurant service, we come her for the best thai in town and to be treated like old family friends.

The antique garage interior is quaint and rustic feeling. However, it does little to retain heat. Conveniently, next to our table, there was an antique thermometer that consistently read at 65. We went in early December and I look forward to trying it again in a few months when the weather warms up a bit. This would have been a five for me if it wasn't so chilly. I'm sure it will be a phenomenal place for summer evenings if they open up the garage door. Our server was laid-back and proficient. It was very pleasant to have a waiter who wasn't overly intrusive nor unavailable. The three courses were served at good intervals and he was attentive to detail. He was able to give very good wine recommendations (which is fortunate because their wine menu can be daunting). I got the meatball marinara and braised lamb and hummus. They were fantastic choices. It had all the niceties of a fancy restaurant without the pretentiousness. Because of the rustic decor, you don't feel out of place in more casual clothing. Great place to go if you are looking for great food but not wanting to dress up-but I'd recommend a sweater if you are going in the wintertime.
Amazing food!!! Great service, owner was such a great host :) I recommend the pad see ew, papaya salad, pad thai and the chicken satay.

I didn't know there was good thai in brandon! the food was cooked perfectly, each ingredient fresh, and spices just right. they don't advertise and it's located in a strip mall but don't let that turn you off. inside is small, nicely decorated, and quiet. I am definitely coming back

This place is outstanding. The staff is so welcoming and always make sure your water glass is full and you have plenty of injera. The food is delicious. They have great vegan and gluten-free options. We always get the vegetarian platter and the lentil and cabbage sambusa. We also love the atmosphere. Watching the music videos they always have playing on the tv is one of my favorite reasons to eat here. Definitely a must try!

I love Dominican food and was excited to discover this affordable Dominican restaurant on 12th and Callowhill. Friendly staff made for a good start but the lack of air conditioning made for a stifling and uncomfortable meal. There were a variety of dishes to choose from. I had the tres gulpes and was underwhelmed. The fried cheese and salami were good but the base of the meal was mushy and not flavorful. My friend had the Tilapia which came out black. I did;t ask her how it tasted but it looked severely If I were to go back again I would order the chicken lunch special - half a chicken with rice and beans for $7.50. Also getting it to go would prevent from having to eat in an un-airconditioned room. This place has potential unfortunately I didn't feel like it was quite met.

To the super accommodating, super gracious, super nice guy who answered the phone, took our order, and delivered food to us last night, despite the fact that we're well out of Zaika's delivery zone: THANK YOU!! My boyfriend and I were craving Indian last night, and we live in the Mayfair section of Philly (read: Irish dive bars and pizza shops as far as the eyes can see, but not much else). After doing a Yelp search for Indian restaurants in the area, I decided to give Zaika a call since the ratings on here are great and I was taking a shot hoping they'd deliver. Not only did they agree to deliver out of their zone for us, and read parts of the menu off to us because there's not one online other than the small snapshots people have taken, AND let us order under their delivery minimum, they also came with TASTY FOOD. DELICIOUS. The Korma was creamy, had those delightful bits of cashews and raisins in it, just enough heat to it, and really tender chicken. I hate when Indian places throw huge, dry cubes of chicken in there. These bits were perfectly braised. My boyfriend also loved the Tikka Masala, and both dishes had the perfect ratio of meat to sauce so there was plenty there for the dipping. The rice was just plain beautiful, and the naan was great too. So, this experience sealed the deal for us, we'll now be regulars. In the future I plan to order and pick up on my way home from work in order to not send them out of their way again, as it's totally going to be worth it. Although, I do recommend that the owners consider extending their delivery range, and definitely get their menu up online (or even better, sign up with Grub Hub). They could probably make a killing, as not all of us in the Northeast are only interested in wings and cheap pizza. This gentleman was so appreciative for our business, and it was refreshing not only that they went out of their way for us, but that they also served up some really good quality food. 5++ stars. Try this place!
Wow, every dish was amazing! The gnocchi was so good we ordered another round for dessert! Thanks Zeppoli!
They did not give the 5 dollar off on 30 as they mention on Yelp Food was cold in buffet.

This place was a true surprise for me to find in Philly! I am not Dominican but I travel to the Dominican Republic often for work, so I'm pretty familiar with Dominican food and restaurants. This place felt exactly like being in the DR, in all the best ways! I will note that if you want a fancy restaurant with fancy food, this certainly is not it. But if you want authentic Dominican food, served the way that it is at little roadside restaurants throughout the DR in generous portions with a side of great hospitality, then you should definitely check it out at your first opportunity! The prices are very reasonable, the food is delicious, and the staff are friendly. Parada Maimon also exceeded my expectations for accommodating the big group that I reserved for when I went there. I didn't expect them to take reservations, but they did. The table was ready for us when we got there, and they were ready to serve us. They split the checks for each person at the end, and allowed us to pay with card or cash - once again, simply not expected and really felt to me that they went above and beyond to accommodate us and make sure that we enjoyed our experience. It's a great little place that I'll recommend to anyone interested in trying something new or reliving memories of the DR!

suraya. you have me for LIFE. i'm just gonna say it. this was better than my zahav experiences. don't get me wrong, zahav is amazing but damn this place is better. make a reservation way ahead. get all your baked goods before 10:30 am. i've eaten probably a little less than 2/3 of the items off of their menu and i have not one complaint! meats are fragrant and juicy pastries aren't bogged down with heavy syrups or sugar...like you know and feel like your eating quality ingredients in everything. just kidding i have one complaint. open your patio asap

Extremely disappointed in this place! Jamaican Jerk Hut use to be one of thee best Jamaican spots in Center City. However the quality of the food and service has changed drastically. My food seemed as if it was 3 days old and microwaved. The plantains weren't even soft because they were obviously old. I eventually threw the entire platter away, because it was so disgusting. For the price of their platters I would not recommend. I don't see this place lasting very long if they keep this service up.

I love their signature pretzel crusted fried chicken! Salty and sweet, and the dark meat is deliciously tender. I'm amazed at how well everything delivered too! Ordered delivery on a Friday night and everything arrived within 30 minutes. There are a variety of sauces depending on what you're in the mood for, but my two favorites are the pesto Parmesan and the honey mustard. The chicken is top notch in my opinion, albeit very expensive, however the mac and cheese was somewhat disappointing. It's packed with ingredients (sausage, peppers, herbs, cheese, etc) and almost has the consistency of stuffing. But all of the ingredients leave a mush of indistinguishable flavors. I prefer a crumbly mac and cheese instead of a mish mosh. Overall, great spot in U City to satisfying a fried chicken craving!

Great buffet for both vegetarians and meat eaters. Lots of dishes, I didn't count but there was plenty, everything you would expect at an Indian buffet. We came about 1pm, there was a good crowd there but we didn't have to wait to be seated and all the food was fresh. My favorite was the butter chicken, a close second was the vegetable biryani, and I think it was better than the chicken biryani For the biryani, I recommend scoop at the top of the container, because the food at the bottom may be dry or overcooked, they use flame underneath the warmer so it's constantly cooking. Interior is spacious and nicely decorated. Get 10% off with Yelp check-in, they do honor this. I will definitely come back. The plaza has a strange layout, to get there you have to drive through the Shell Gas Station parking lot.

Great atmosphere! Andre was a courteous server who explained the mission of the restaraunt. The jerk chicken is excellent! A bit spicy but I like spicy food. Fish are big specimens. The inside decor is excellent and up scale Do not be fooled by the outside appearance. I recomend this place!

Hands down the best Thai food I've ever had ..for now! It was a couple of months ago since my trip here, but everything was so wonderful that everything is still so vivid in my mind. I came here with a friend, she had a lemongrass soup, pineapple fried rice, and I had pad Thai for the first time.i fell in love with everything, and unfortunately since this place is far, I have not been able to come back. I've been trying the same entrees at other Thai restaurants but none have been able to compare. I thank Nadia for my high expectations in Thai food and hope I get a chance to come back soon! Btw, just to note: service was also amazing, and the atmosphere/environment made it a suitable place to have a date. Place looks a tad deceiving on the outside, but the interior is just absolutely gorgeous.

I love this place!!! The food is great and the service is amazing. Thank you for going above and beyond Greg (my mother in law was so happy). We will definitely be ordering here again. Thank you again. Go here if you want great Greek food!!
love the catfish, cheap, grilled fish, cheap,good service!!!!!!

We visited Jamaica about a month ago and I was introduced to beef patties. Holy Moley are they delicious. So two weeks after we visited I was looking up recipes to make them on my own. Ugh no! Not going to happen. To make them takes all day and like 30 ingredients. So I started googling Jamaican restaurants near McGuire AFB. And Hummingbird was the first to pop up and had great reviews. So I had to check it out. Me, my husband and two friends went with us. It's in the middle of downtown Trenton, which is a lovely area. It's a small hole-in-the-wall and it is absolutely delicious. My husband had the BBQ wings. They are spicy even for our Latin taste. But so tasty you keep eating despite your mouth being on fire. The rice and peas (which is rice and beans) was better than any I had in Jamaica. My friend had the BBQ jerk and it was also juicy, tasty, spicy and better than the jerk I had in Jamaica. I had two beef patties. They were a 7 compared to the ones I had in Jamaica but it did fix my craving for them. The dough was a little bit thicker and crispier than the ones I had in Jamaica, which were soft and flaky. Oh and they have fried plantains. These are the sweet ones that are known as Maduro in the Latin world. But boy are they just as good. The cook made them fresh for us so they were piping hot. But we didn't care. Yummy. Def a place we will go to get great Jamaican food!!! The only thing I was sad about was that they didn't have any Jamaican coffee. :-(

Solid spot with very good and reasonably priced food. We got here pretty much right when they opened so it wasn't busy which is always nice. Service was quick and with the prices we were able to try quite a few different things. To start we got chips and guac which was very fresh and a good way to start off our lunch. My wife and I followed that up by sharing and order of chilaquiles with eggs, on shrimp and one carne asada taco(2 for 7.50 if i remember correctly), and a Mexicano dog. All were excellent, the egg was a little too runny for my wife's liking. The Mexicano dog my have been the highlight to be but it is extremely messy so be prepared to ask for lots of extra napkins. We finished off our meal with some churros & chocolate. These were very good but the chocolate is basically just a warm chocolate milk so just know that going in.
Wanting to eat there but they had no authentic heat They had little Electric heaters and that was a major turn off ... the staff seemed nice the rest is on you
Maybe it was an off night! The service was terrible! The food was not good at all. Very disappointing!

Let me start by saying that I think it probably is closer to a 4 star establishment but I needed to over compensate for all the terrible yuppy-mainline reviewers. I will also say that any unpleasantries are more likely to be caused by the fact that restaurant is attached to the sad excuse for an irish bar, jack McShea's. I have been to this siamese princess multiple times and have always had a good experience. Good food for the price, nice cozy atmosphere and friendly staff. The service can be slow but it is clearly a mom and pop joint-- it seats like 30 people max-- what do you expect. Almost every time I have eaten in this place, get take out more often, I have heard atleast one table of snobby, over entitled main liners complain about something irrelevant. Recently had to listen to an ass hole loudly complain about how his bold and spicy shrimp was not hot enough. The waitress politely offered to make it more spicy for him and said they err on the side of their dishes being not spicy enough because they could always add... Then he cut her off, demanded a menu so he could point the dish out to her and that it said "bold and spicy" and he claimed it was neither. Listen jackass she said she would make it spicier so don't ram it down her throat, we get it your a lawyer. I am so tired of living on the mainline and dealing with such pricks. Never open a restaurant on the mainline, these savages will never be satisfied. In summary the food is good, waitstaff is very courteous - could be faster at times, and is a very enjoyable place to get a meal. The patrons are hit or miss... Mainly a miss.

My husband and I visited the restaurant today after reading the Yelp reviews and decided to try it as we had a craving for curry on such a cold day. The restaurant is small and quaint but do not be deceived as the food is amazing and does not disappoint. I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and my husband had the Chicken Curry and we both had Garlic Naan. All of it was phenomenal. The owner greeted us and was very kind and checked on us while we ate. We will definitely be coming back to this little gem and I would recommend it to anyone. Please check it out.

I had been to Mojitos during Mardi Gras, so my memory of the food, service, etc was a little "vague". We went for dinner last night because the weather was sitting-on-a-patio gorgeous & we were going to hit some bars nearby. We had no real expectations...and were really happy with our entire experience. The live music was great. We loved the fact that we could have a conversation. We also loved the fact the musicians were talented enough to make us want to stop talking & listen at times. Our server, Alexander, was fast and attentive. He knew when to check on us & when to let us relax...love that! The food was really good. We shared the Alligator Bites, my fiance had the Cuban sandwich, & I had the Mojitos House salad...which I LOVED! Everything was fresh & tasty. We will defintely be back to Mojitos again!

Thank you Yelp! Dinner was wonderful. Had Drunken Noodles with the Seafood medley. It was perfect. Not too spicy and just the slightest bit sweet. The seafood was plentiful and large pieces. From an out of towner to the locals... thanks for steering me right! Side note: there is a lovely Rita's Custer stand just around the corner *wink*
I love Thai food. This pace is small, very nice, the food is really good. They will make it as spicy as you like ..or as mild. Panang Curry Chicken, is great! The staff is very nice too.
I ordered pad see ew and sticky rice with mango. The food was REALLY tasty and the service was great as well. I highly recommend this restaurant!!

This is one of our favorite restaurants. Any time we suggest going to another Indian restaurant our kids protest. The staff is wonderful, they greet us like family at the door and the treatment continues throughout the meal. The food is excellent, I recommend asking if they have any specials as we have had many amazing dishes which were not on the menu. Go a few times, you too will become part of their family.

I've tried a few Indian buffets, most of which were okay. The staff here are super friendly and quick to refill drinks and remove dirty plates immediately. The selection of the buffet is decent and the food is really good. The garlic naan is awesome! Great Indian buffet for lunch!

I must have come on an off day. My expectations were a bit high. I had received great reviews and recommendations for this place; but at my visit all the hype came crashing down. When I walked in, there wasn't anyone else in the restaurant. I wondered if they were open. But nonetheless the young lady seated us and began to wait on our table. I assumed that since we were the only party in the restaurant we were get great service. The thing of it is it wasn't great, she was just a bit much. It seemed a little awkward. Just my opinion. I began to order some dishes and it felt like everything I asked for they were out of. No beef patties. No curry chicken. I can't remember the other thing, but there were at least two or three things that were not available that were on the menu. When the food did come, it was too spicy. And that could just be because of my meager American taste buds. I know in Caribbean cuisine things are usually a bit heated, but this was really unbearable. We couldn't really eat the food it was so spicy. We ended up bearing through it (didn't want to waste food and money) and eating it but it didn't even really taste good. The vegetables and rice were so bland; I guess they concentrated on seasoning the meat, they forgot the vegetables. When it came time to pay, the young lady was awkward there too. I'm not sure if she was trained as a waitress or what. Normally what happens is, they give you the check and then they walk away and come back a few minutes later. She was back no more than 60 seconds later. I just felt a bit rushed like, "nobody else is here what's the rush?!?". I feel like the awkwardness of the waitress turned me off a bit. Like I was being rushed, I don't know. Like I said at the beginning maybe it was just an off day.

We are locals and went there to fix a jerk chicken craving. We've had better jerk and never at those prices. They charged $12 for my husband's quarter chicken platter. He got one slice of a plantain, with rice and cabbage. It was a "slice" of a fricken banana - not even a serving slice scored lengthwise but less than a quarter inch garnish slice. For my half chicken platter, they charged $19 and I got two slices of the toothpick plantain, with rice and cabbage. A $7 price difference for a couple of extra chicken "pieces" filled with bones and another wheeny plantain slice... It wasn't worth telling the waitress she'd messed up my order to begin with. Add to that one soft drink and a $9 coconut shrimp appetizer that showed seven shrimp on the menu but was served as five, and a side of extra plantains. $45 for two before tip for a hut-style meal that was average.

I love Thai food, especially Pad Thai, so when we went here for Supper Club I was really excited. I enjoyed what I had for dinner (for the most part), but it ended up making me really sick. My friend was fine though. I might try it one more time to see if it was me or the place itself, but it definitely gave me a mixed first impression.
Been twice, both times it stunk of cigar smoke. Great décor, good atmosphere, better outside than inside.

I was lucky enough to attend my best friends mehndi at this location and it was gorgeous, well staffed and an amazingly fun time. The food though - my goodness the food was amazing! I don't often get to eat traditional Indian food so I indulged heavily in the meals. From the chicken to the lamb to the chai tea to the creamed spinach- it was all delicious. I hope I get to come back here for an event in the near future!

I've been going to this place says Iversen play for the 76ers. A friend and I were looking for somewhere to eat before a game and from that point I was hooked. The cooks there or just so consistent with the Dishes. The food still taste the same from the first time I went. Everyone I take here returns on their own. Great food, Ambience and staff

This place is by far the best restaurant in Avon and the best Vietnamese food in all of Indianapolis! What makes it even better is the fact that the management and entire staff are the nicest people you'll ever meet!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Very nice cozy place to go eat authentic indian food. Owner was very nice to talk to and thr ambiance was welcoming. The main thimg os the food was tasty. Def order goat biryani and the chiken korma and if you like spicy it was perfect.

A bit awkward having never been there before knowing just want to do. bit the entirely laid back nature makes you feel at home right away. I was surprised to walk up to the counter, order.. get the food.. eat.. and then pay. We weren't even provided with a ticket to say what we had ordered, we simply recited it from memory. The remarkable effect of this is, it makes you feel like family. Sure, you could probably go in there and order something, and then not pay for it, but what would be the point? Why reward courtesy with crime? The friendly nature of the restaurant is second to none. The food, as it is, was good. While I can't speak to the legitimacy or authenticity of this Greek food, but I quite enjoyed it. The beverages are mostly bottled with some "fountain" teas. If you are looking for free refills on your coke, you'll be disappointed. Overall I enjoyed my visit and I certainly plan on returning.
I really enjoy Thai food and this small place is one of my favorite. I really enjoy the vergetarian options such as spicy vegetable soup. i would recommend this place.

This place may not have the best pho, but you can't beat the price, especially in Philly, plus the restaurant environment is good. They also have bubble tea and smoothie with interesting flavor, e.g. durian

Went back to my favourite take out 4-08-2014 and sorry to say this will be the last time, portions have gotten even smaller and both dishes the sauces were very watered down. The garlic naan breads were definately not fresh and tasted and felt days old.

Wayyyyyy overrated. I drove pretty far out of the way to try this place, and it let me down. The atmosphere is fine enough. It's just what you'd imagine when you think of a fairly-fancy Indian place. The food was a let down, though. I had the mixed vegetable curry. (It was the non-creamy style, which I like.) I wish I had something enlightening to say, but I don't -- I just didn't think it was all that great. When I tasted my friend's meal, I knew my meal wasn't a lemon. In fact, the sample I had (sadly, I can't remember the name of the dish) was worse than my meal. I'd go to GtI if I lived nearby, but it's not worth traveling for.

Worth the drive. We drove from Bucks County for dinner here with friends. Needless to say, this is not your average Italian restaurant. This type of cuisine is what you expect in Italy--we almost forgot where we were, had we not looked out the windows onlooking Collingswood, NJ. With a Sicilian focus, the food is as fresh and gourmet as it gets. We were promptly greeted and seated. Like most classic, quality Italian restaurants, the wait staff moves to your speed. If you seem like you're in a rush, they'll move along to your pace. If you there for good food, drink and conversation with friends and want to take your time, they'll move along at your pace. We ordered so much food, I can hardly rate each dish. We enjoyed the uniqueness of each bite, and were pleased that we took our time over the multiple courses so that we could savor the flavors. Do not leave this restaurant without trying the Zeppole--to die for. The ambiance is average. The restaurant is small (so make a reso), the service is top notch (wait staff shares responsibility of all tables), and the food is out of this world. What's almost better than the best Italian food you can possibly find? ...BYOB. Bring you own and enjoy!

My husband, toddler, and I tried this restaurant for a weekday lunch. I was surprised that it never got busy, even around the Noon rush, but maybe others were simply as unimpressed as I was. The staff was friendly enough (though our cashier had no energy), the ambience was pleasant, and I do love the unique selections (a nice change from the standard burger joint); but the food was really just OK -- not bad at all, just mediocre. For Mediterranean food, it didn't "wow" me. Maybe it's what we got: I had the Quinoa Salad, my hubby got the Turkey Stack, and we got the Kids Roll-up for our little one. I also had the hibiscus green tea, which was decent. I will add that the portions and temperature were just right. I am willing to go back again and try a pita or kabob, but I don't have the highest expectations.

I think I would give 3.5 stars. The vermicelli bowl was really good. The pork was well cooked though could have used more char. The mint was a nice fresh element, but without cilantro made the dish lean toward being too sweet. The yum sauce was great. I would certainly return given the value. This place is cash only. Be warned.

Wonderful! Excited to find a great Thai restaurant while on vaca. Very clean, authentic looking, smelled good when walked in. Had Thai tea, chicken panang, chicken phad thai, beef red curry - all very tasty. Also had a custom phad thai for my picky eater with no sass and was perfect. Yum!
Compare to the other pho I have this place provides less food and same price. We decide to buy a slice of pizza after two bowel of pho
No complaints. Excellent food. Great service. We had a vermicelli bowl chicken and shrimp, pot stickers, spring rolls, and a bowl of rare steak phõ. Quick service. Hit the spot.

Drinks and Hookah well priced, but the service is SUPREMELY lacking. The waitress was unfriendly at best and rude at worst. It took forger to get her attention to refill water or clear plates. We watched her get into an argument with another table. snatch things from them and conduct herself in a rude manner. The music is random. Lots of good top 40 and rap songs, but then there was a gospel song?!?! And other random choices.

Aside from the fact that it is a kind of expensive, I do like PF Changs. I was there in time for happy hour so I had a glass of Riesling for $5 and I split the Pre-Fixe (2 4-course meals for $40) with a friend. We had the hot and sour soup which was not my favorite. It lacked heat and flavor compared to other hot and sour soups I've had. We had the chicken lettuce wraps which I love. The hot ground chicken with the cold lettuce is a great combination. I had the orange shrimp which was spicy and very tasty. For my mini dessert I had the lemon cream which was soo yummy. This place is nice for a treat but definitely not somewhere you would frequent. Their food is good but not outstanding and for the price, it doesn't really make the mark. Their servers are on top of their game and their staff is friendly.

Another after work dinner night with my kids. Sticky rice, sausage, bamboo soup, laad na and fried banana with chocolate drizzle. All of that food was all for me... lol. Thai ice tea to finish off my dinner. Got embarrassed that I was eating too much and had my food packed to go with extra sticky rice. Food was excellent. Service was great.
A super cool great place to enjoy brunch! I even rented the place out for,a special event! Support this neighborhood treasure!

I used to order from Little Kitchen fairly often. I always ordered take out since the ambiance of the restaurant isn't great and the place is usually empty. I would get the General Tso's and various kinds of sushi. The food was actually pretty good and for a while I was a loyal customer, but the last time I ordered from them, they gave me spoiled sushi. It smelled pretty bad and I really don't see how they could have missed that. It's really a shame - I haven't been back since.
Food is good, interior is a bore. Waitress was sweet. I like this place. The food is always hot and fresh. Delicious naans

the service was terrible. worst ever. our waiter barely even came to us twice and every time we needed something we tried to ask another waiter but they flat out ignored us and didn't even look. hate this place.

My goto chinese takeout. Its more then just chinese... its also japanese, and thai. Thier pad thai is good, and their sushi is tasty. i always order a ton of food and they do not disappoint. Try the kani salad amd chicken pad thai... yummm
Ordered takeout twice from uber eats, inconsistent and the last order was pretty terrible.

This is our fourth time here and it got better than it was the first time. Everybody loved their food. The waiter was great. Each dish was better than the next! Great location if you know where it is!!

Definitely some of the best Chinese in University city. General Tso's chicken was fantastic and so was the crispy duck. Server was nice and the place was busy, so it was excellent service considering that drinks were filled up and food was brought out promptly.

Had a meal here after I dropped by the local Starbucks, always loving Chinese food. I walked in, noting the $4 lunch buffet sign on the window, and was greeted by a woman that knows about as many words in English as there are on their menu. As it is a Chinese restaurant, this is forgivable. I sneaked a look at the buffet, and since it didnt look too appealing, I looked at the menu for a while and decided on the sesame chicken. I've been to many a happy dragon and various other Chinese restaurants, but none have matched the pure calorie packed goodness that lies in that sesame chicken. No joke, best Chinese food I've ever had. It kind of sucks that it's 40 minutes away or I would be back, and I don't know about anything else on the menu but the sesame chicken is awesome.

The food was good. My wife had the Pho with rare beef and meatballs. Not the best we have had, but not bad. I had the flame grilled pork, one of their lunch specials. It tasted old and reheated. The fish sauce was bland, lacking the carrots and peppers I have had elsewhere. The big disappointment was the service. Both of the ladies with whom we interacted appeared to be miserable. We were not acknowledged by the hostess the first several minutes that we stood by the cash register. The lady was too busy to even look up and smile. The waitress was equally abrupt and bland. When we paid our bill, the waitress never spoke to us or even looked at us. I felt like an inconvenience, not a guest.
I love the chicken gyro and hummus here. Consistently good food and service!

Worst service here ever! Waiter could not speak English, got our orders wrong multiple times, charge us wrong, had to rewrite the receipt 4 times before he and the manager got it right! I worked(bust my ass) as a waiter in the food industry before so I cannot stand terrible services. Never eating here again!

I was in town for the night thought I would give this place a shot. Hookah was great had mint and grape, ordered tea as well. Service was okay the person who took my order never checked on my not once, I was surprised when I got the check and they added 21% gratuity ! I would've tipped anyways however you should not add 21% for below average service. I gave 3 stars based on the hookah and the atmosphere.

This place is wonderful! The buffet had so many selections and everyday it is different! You can tell they use the freshest ingredients. Hands down this is the best Indian food I have had. Price is reasonable and the place is very clean. Location is different but well worth it when you find it!

Great take out food. Terrible take out service. I've never dined there. Only take out. Food is outstanding. Problem is with take out experience. They don't bother tracking your name or phone number. So if you are not the only take out order expect 20 questions. Did you order blah, blah, blah. What about blah, blah, blah. If you are the person picking up but say your spouse ordered, forget about it. If you can't identify the order, they resort to "is it the small order or big order". Lol. As if you are privy the size of your order relative to that of others! It's quirky once or twice. Aggregating the third or fourth time. After that, you'll just stop ordering from there. Good luck you kooky dudes! It's not that hard to track orders by name or telephone number!

When walking in, you notice the interior is a lot nicer than expected for the location. It's a mix of Caribbean and Indian influences, i guess it makes sense being west Indian? I ended up stopping in with a group of friends the night before diwali and ended up meeting the owner. He over heard is taking about family style and offered to do a pre fixed for us... But i think he was just trying to clear inventory before the holidays . Pricing was fair under $20 a head. We had the jerk wings, ox tail, some sort of chicken, fried rice, and white rice... Maybe something else i don't recall The jerk wings were the best and would definitely recommend that. It was done well with a good kick of spice if you like that. The ox tail was a close second and had great flavor too. The pieces of chicken were a little under cooked, but ok. Would not order that again. The fried rice was good, but don't recall it being anything super special. I didn't have any of the white rice. Either way, it was a good place and a friendly owner. Vibe was cool, would stop back again.

Thought I would give IV pho a try myself after hearing all the horrible things about it, and most definitely those things are true. The Vietnamese coffee is horrible, straight horrible. I was hoping for some authentic Vietnamese food, but I was very disappointed. The staff however are very nice. Restaurant itself is very small.

Wanted something quick and close to the water park. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Huge portions and the food was great. Tried the giro, Greek salad, wings, dolma, shrimp and falafel - all really good.

Ordered over phone, they said its going to take 20 mins. Went to get the order in 20 mins but they made me wait for another 30 mins and on top of that i got the wrong order. Customer service is the worst. The place was very noisy. The staff pretends as if you dont exist. Felt like a fool to wait for so long unattended. Heard so much about the place, but its not worth it. Horrible experience and awful place.
Restaurant was clean! The service was great! The food was AMAZING!! Omg, the crunch roll!!

Best Vietnamese restaurant in Indy (and this is coming from a Viet)! I've gone here for years, and grew up eating at this restaurant! I've tried several dishes and their all great! My favorites are the bun bo, goi cuon, and bun thit nuoung. It is definitely authentic and made fresh. They have other cuisine on the menu, but because it is a Vietnamese family, I would recommend sticking to the Vietnamese cuisine. If you're not familiar with Vietnamese food, starting off with pho or a rice dish is a great place to start, Vietnamese egg rolls for appetizers (they're the best!). Service is great and fast! You won't be disappointed whether this is your first time trying Vietnamese cuisine or if you're a seasoned pro.
I was pleasantly surprised by the comfort of this place. It's warmly lit, the tables and chairs are all in good condition, actually the chairs are very comfy.
Authentic Mediterranean food that always tastes fresh. You can't go wrong with a BYOB & great food. The place is tiny & doesn't take reservations but worth the wait if a wait happens.

Clean, delicious, low price. They also serve a free soup with bread and salad with meals. Not only but there is an available tea for free in the restaurant, all of of that for a meal price as low as $6.99

I've been here a half dozen times over the last 2 years and I love it for it's unpretentious feel. Some nights its more happening than others and some times it is full of the Geritol generation, but over all its just right if you wanna show up in a t-shirt and flip-flops and knock back a couple of buckets while enjoying some blackened fish and the salt air. Its about $11 bucks a plate average and can be a nice day or night out.

Not only does this place have amazing food and ambiance, but the staff is so friendly and willing to cater to any of your needs...Heidi was our server for Sunday brunch and was everything you could ask for in a server! They have half of Moët and Chandon bottles on Sunday's which is perfect for a brunch outside in their patio! We ordered the chicken panini, the biscuit sandwich (which is to die for...it's an open face biscuit with house made jam, over easy egg and thin sliced ham), and fries on the side. They have the best fries thin shoe string fries! Also the bloody Mary's are unreal! They have a burger stack on top with a pickle and veggies! So good!! Would definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting st Pete!

This place was an experience! I love different ethic foods and really did enjoy this. My wife also had such a nice experience here. We had the Queens Platter which was great for only $15 /person. Service was a little on the slow but oh well the food was good and the experience was great. Will check you guys out again in a few months.

This place was not good, I am so surprised to see all the good reviews. It was overpriced and under spiced. Also they jipped us out of samosas on a take out order. The makanhi was bland and the nann tasted like frozen pizza dough. Overall I was very disappointed, there are plenty of better places for indian food in lower bucks.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: They are back! This is my family's favorite place to go out. Birthdays, milestones, post-traumatic stress recovery - all are celebrated at the Taj. We were at a cultural loss as to where to go for the last year. There are some new items on the menu - chicken achar is an excellent new entry. Achar is tangy and is a nice complement to the creamy korma. palak subzi dal is a spinach dish with other veggies. The spinach was a little over cooked, and maybe from frozen spinach (yuk) but this might be the way the dish is normally prepared. I can't wait to go back and sample the channa and okra. There is also a beef tandori which sounds great. They have a lunch buffet which would be a good time to sample a lot of the staples. We also enjoyed the garlic naan which they dialed down a little for us. Nick, I think they have always had the extensive drinks menu. They have switched to a lot of regional brews. I'm a fan of the Rogue products. The nutbrown ale was nicely malty and combined well with the savory achar. At the old incarnation of the Taj, I experienced my first ever Tripel Karmaliet. It is really amazing to pair the sugars in beer with spicy food. The new space is cozier and probably more affordable to maintain. I hope this family business thrives so that I can grow old with it.

Friendly owner, bubble tea and delicious food make Blu Fig a hidden treasure diners need to discover. All the dishes are fresh, the falafel is the best we've had in Nashville and the prices are right. The restaurant is small, so arrive early. But if you are craving a little Middle Eastern flavor, you will find Blu Fig a pleasant surprise on Nolensville Rd in Nashville.
So happy they now have this great restaurant in Tucson. We would drive to Scottsdale for the original. The food is the same quality of ingredients and the ambiance is excellent. Love the Soltani.

Went there on a tuesday for dinner with 7 of my friends and the dishes were not great and the place just looked gloomy but the only good part about the whole experience was the music which was really good. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone who wants good moroccan food.

Came here with my mom and had the lunch special. The coconut soup and dumpling appetizers were delicious, as was the Pad Kee Mao noodles (like drunken noodles) that my mom ordered . I wasn't a huge fan of the chicken satay - it was cut differently from what I was expecting and was just okay. The Penang tofu curry that I ordered was a little too peanut-y. Overall yummy, but it depends on what you get.

I had read former reviews, especially about the small portions, so before we ordered, I politely asked about that, the owner got quite annoyed, and after that the service deteriorated. the food was average, I have had Ethiopian food beore and enjoyed it, this was ok but not great. the portions were small, we had 3 people and ordered 5 meals, and it was just enough, a bit overpriced for what we had I thought. But the worst thing was that at the end of the meal, we had been looking forward to eating the yeasty bread ( injera ) that had been sitting under the dishes on the large platter as it had sopped up all the juices and looked yummy, it was not ! It had a really weird chemical taste, very overpowering and we were concerned that it could be unsafe to eat, as the platter the food was served on was plastic and I have no idea if it was food grade plastic, especially with having acidic food on top which leaches stuff out. I would have told the owner, but she seemd very unreceptive to any input, as demonstrated earlier. I won't be returning to this restaurant, but I doubt it will remain open anyway, too many negatives, which is a bummer as it was nice to have something different.
