Very tasty Thai food! I mostly get take out from here, but i have eaten in there once or twice. Staff is always super friendly, my food is always ready when they say it will be and it's hot! The green curry and pad kee mow (sp?) are my favorite!!

Best Thai food I've had in the Bucks/Mont area. Spring rolls, soups, curry, and seafood dishes were all very good. Not sure why people talk about the portion sizes. True-the lunch portions are not huge, but they filled me up and I thought the dinner portions were substantial. Service is fast and friendly. BYOB

DO NOT GO HERE! Went in to try the pho. It started out well, but then, I saw that there was something black in my soup which is unusual. I fish it out, and it's a ROACH! I called the server over and she says, "Sorry! That happens sometimes." She then proceeds to give us the check WITH the roach infested pho on it. Don't go here. Not worth it.

I have only two requirements for food to be considered truly awesome: it has to be ridiculously delicious and not ridiculously expensive. Man, is this food awesome. Most dishes are $6.50 (including tax, cash only), and are quite unique. The blends of flavors and textures are just great. I had the house special noodles, which I really enjoyed. I also tried the flat noodles (kwetiaw, kind of like the drunken noodles that you get at Thai restaurants), and those were very flavorful and delicious as well. The crispy-skinned fried chicken (both spicy and non-spicy varieties) served with fragrant coconut rice looked great, as did a curry soup dish. It's difficult to beat the quality of food for the price here in Philly. The staff are busy but friendly, and kept our water glasses filled. We were the only non-Indonesians in the whole packed restaurant (that's how you know it's good). I'm positive that our favorite Indonesian-raised president would love this place. In fact, this place makes me wish I were Indonesian myself, so I would have an Indonesian grandmother to cook me these fantastic dishes. Do yourself a favor and visit Sky Cafe as soon as humanly possible. [The content of this message has not been approved or endorsed by President Barack Obama.]

Thai Orchid is a great choice for Thai food in the Blue Bell area. We have only taken out, never eaten in the restaurant. The Pad Thai is really good, many takeout places overcook it and it ends up being dry. Not here.

My wife and I had heard of the new Indian Restaurant in Newtown, and tonight we went there for the first time. It was a wonderful experience all around. We were greeted with warm friendly smiles as soon as we walked in, and were directed to our table. After reading about the specials, I decided on Lamb Curry, and my wife had some questions about the Biryani. You see we used to go to Harini's in Lawrenceville,NJ because my wife loved the Hyderabad style Biryani, but Harini's closed a few years ago. There are many ways to make Biryani and after asking the server at Guru's about Their style of Biryani my wife placed an order for it. We also ordered Chana Masala, and buttered naan. My wife was so very happy when the Biryani arrived and she could tell just by the wonderful aroma that she would love it. I found the Lamb curry very much to my liking and the sauce was excellent. In fact all of the food was above our expectations, and when the server came by to ask how our meals were, I told her how happy my wife was with the Biryani, and how much I loved the Lamb curry. Now that the food has passed our test, the next thing to do is to bring my Mother in law with us next time. It was a very nice gesture that we were served rice pudding without asking for it or being charged. I would highly recommend Guru's Indian Cuisine to anyone that enjoys Indian Food!
amazing indian pizzas tastey and fresh highly recommended

The place is decent. We may have just gone on an off night. We ordered drinks and food at the bar and the bartender just seemed distracted. We just had some small plates and the food was average. We will give it one more try, but so far they are not doing anything worth driving into town from N Wilmington.

$13 for 2 bland tacos? No thanks. My side of sweet potato fries was the highlight, they were quite tasty. Our server was super nice too. However, I got the fish tacos and they were rather disappointing. I'm not hard to impress, they just needed some flavor or an amazing sauce. Just meh
I love this place! The food is absolutely excellent. The service is wonderful as well. The salmon is cooked perfect and the tomato soup is delicious! Highly recommend!

I would give this place 3.5 if that were possible. I enjoyed the stir fried egg noodle dish (#104, I think), which came with a couple of nice big shrimp, chicken and beef, and lots of veggies. I would say it was moderately flavorful, but the veggies, noodles, and proteins were nicely cooked. I also had a cup of the won ton soup, which came loaded with won tons and was tongue scalding hot - just what I was looking for coming in out of the frigid night. My wife had the "grilled platter" which featured a variety of meats and veggies that you use to assemble your own spring rolls. This was a great dish and I think went more to the strength of the menu.

The food was great and the dancing was a blast, however the service is very very slow. I don't know if it's from a lack of efficiency or training or both. We came in early to get drinks and eats before the dancing at 9. Drinks took awhile to get at the bar, even longer to get from a table. It took about an hour to get our food. Once we got it though, it was delicious. No complaints on that. It's a fairly small space. They clear out all the tables to make a dance floor. It took a little while for the dancing to really pick up but once it did there was always a great showing on the dance floor. We'd go again for the dancing, but with more pre-gaming else where. We'd maybe order out for the food.
My favorite Indian restaurant in the Carmel, IN area. For some reason the food is better (ie, less salty) in the buffet than when you order off the menu. Love the Korma!
Wow, really bland Pho and powder milk tea. However, the service is really nice but I do not think I'll go again.

We didn't have a food here because we couldn't. It's an underground restaurant, dark and humid. You can't go with little kids, no strollers can go in because no accessible ramp or way to go. I don't know how the food is but the atmosphere is zero.

Awesome food made even more awesome by the family that owns it and the odd 80s pop music that they play. I got soup with chicken, mushrooms, vegetables, and dumplings and every part of it tasted perfect. Can't wait to go back and try lots of other things.
By far the best Indian food in Tucson! Everything is delicious. Their lunch buffet for $9 is a great deal for great food! If you haven't eaten here yet I would highly recommend doing so.

Nope. Fail. Never again ... the meat was so tough as I tried to bite and rip it off with my teeth it flew out of my mouth and hand onto my friends lap. Lucky we can laugh about it. Otherwise super embarrassing.

Went there as a party of five with 3 adults and two children (age 2 1/2 and 4 1/2). I wouldn't say this is a specifically "kid friendly" restaurant, but they were incredibly friendly to our kids (who aren't particularly civilized to fine dining). We arrived at 5pm and were seated without a reservation. I figured we would be out of there before the evening crowd showed up. I was pleased to see the seats begin to fill up before 6pm. The food was amazing! We started with the tangy eggplant appetizer and the mushrooms, the latter at the recommendation of the waiter. The portions were very good, the diversity of items on the menu great, and I will remember to wear elastic waistband pants next time I go because I just couldn't stop eating the fantastic food (all vegetarian). The kids who typically survive on fish sticks and pasta enjoyed the complementary pappadam served to us upon arrived and then the chana masala and veg jalfarezi. We brought the kids back to look through the window into the kitchen, which was some great entertainment when people got antsy!. This is our second time there, really enjoyed the lunch buffet at another time as well. Will certainly be back (and taking advantage of delivery!!!).
Pad Thai was okay. Very nice on the phone and in person and food was promptly ready for pickup. Unfortunately, it was a bit dry and needed more sauce.

What I expect when I go get Pho: 1) huge portions 2) fast service 3) lotsa noodles but also a good balance of other soup ingredients 4) ridiculous amount of choices 5) cheap Pho Hoa hits all these points. It took us a little long to actually get a waiter to come to us-- I think they were confused because our party staggered in at stages so I don't think they knew when everybody was there so giving them the benefit of the doubt. But they have an extensive menu and they let me order what I always like to order in my Pho-- shrimp and tofu and veggies. And it was delish. We were confused if this was a BYOB since they had drinks on their menu. So I don't think it is. I paid $10 for Pho and an appetizer. That's including tip. Life is good. Oh and there were huge flat screen TVs so we could eat silently and watch the game. Exactly how I like to spend time with my guy friends.

Small neighborhood restuarant. The food was good and tasty but not exceptional. Both entrees were served lukewarm and had to be sent back to be reheated. The service was good but a bit unpolished. We would try it again but it's not a place we would rush back to.

It's not the cleanliest place, but the food is really good and you can't beat the prices! We had the cha gio (spring rolls), banh mi thit hoac bi (not pictured), and this dish that i can't remember the name of but it's pictured. It's unfortunate I can't remember the name 'cuz it was the best thing we had. I also can't remember which pho we had but that's pictured too and was also really good! The service was fine - nothing to rave about, nothing to complain about. But for such a cheap, yet authentic Vietnamese meal, I'll definitely go back!
Simple delicious! Will be back! Suggestion the staff need to smile more! Love the tunes playing!

You know they are authentic when they only accept cash. Their lunch is always super busy. I love their pho and spring rolls. The service is ok( just like most Asian restaurants, the service is kinda disorganized) and they normally only have one waitress. Also their food is affordable. When we have cash on hand this is always the place for Asian food.

Great place! Except they were out of a few dishes. As usual little zak chowed down on the food despite his hunger strikes! Lol! They gave us some free baklava dessert. Food was e cellent. I definitely love coming here each time I come to boise and am so happy I got to bring little zak to share the experience.
Second time to eat here. The food has been GREAT both times! I recommend the Pita. The atmosphere is cool and trendy and the servers couldn't be nicer.
Great selection and diverse range of sushi. Love the sauce bar. Service took awhile during an evening when it wasn't very busy.

This place has changed hands and not for the better. It was a Japanese restaurant, but is now a Thai/Sushi place. The rice for the sushi is not made right. It tastes like overcooked cheap white rice. The shrimp tempura used to be large shrimp, but now they take small cheap shrimp and cut it so they can stretch it out long. Their chef and staff are Thai, so maybe the Thai food is good, but the Japanese food was awful. And don't get me started on the elevator musak (as opposed to music). They need to drop the Japanese food entirely rather than serve such poor quality. I won't be back.
My favorite Indian restaurant in the St. Louis area. They make the best chicken vindaloo and palak paneer, and their garlic naan is awesome. I've never had anything here that I didn't enjoy.

Unfortunately, I will not be able to review the food here. This was going to be my first order from here. I had several friends at my house and we were craving some food and decided to call Zorba's and get a bunch of appetizers and gyros delivered. The woman asked what I would like and I started by telling her two lamb gyros. No sooner than I said the word gyro I was told they don't make them after 4:00PM. It was about 8:00PM when I called. This was a major disappointment and I stopped my order right there as we all wanted gyros and apps. I don't understand how a place that specializes in Greek food can take gyros off the menu. I've been to a few greek restaurants and other than Zorba's they make gyros all day/night. Because Zorba's doesn't make gyros after 4pm they just lost our $60 order. This experience has soured me on this restaurant and I won't be trying again.

This place is a great. I had several different types of the Phó and I found it quite tasteful. The basil was fresh and the price was very fair . Come here to eat good food not worry about a fancy place .

This is the first time I've been back since they reopened and I really wish it was as good as when it first opened a long time ago. The Pho broth was super salty and the beef wrapped in grape leaves (bo nuong la) was super tough...probably because there was more grape leaves than meat. The only upside is that the place is nice and clean and the new decor is not bad. Staff is friendly and attentive. Just wished their food was just as good.
Went today and got the Red Quinoa salad special and added chicken. So much YUM!

Echoing the sentiments of poor, slow service. Really want this place to succeed as it's in my neighborhood but they seem like they have a long way to go. Also where are the vegetarian friendly items? Would be it be too much to ask adding on a tofu bahn mi or bun bowl?

pizza is great! I'm not a hamburger fan but they do have a great spicy one here, I loved it. I've gone several times and never leave disappointed. Pizza is a little bit small... but very good! and staff is amazing, once we did not know they were about to close, and they never rushed us or make us feel uncomfortable. I love this place

The food is very good here, and I love the flexibility of the menu. For a chicken kabob and 2 sides, it's $7.99. Add $2 for a 2nd kabob. Add 99 cents for a 3rd side (rice, beans, & salad). Add 50 cents for a side of tzatziki. I'm giving them only 4 stars, because they don't use basmati rice and it's hard to get the chicken off the stick with a flimsy plastic fork.

Disappointed!One star for the people there--friendly/welcoming. After reading reviews here I gave it a try.The place smells of rotting meat--literally.The smell was so obnoxious that we decided to do a takeout.While the food was getting prepared we chose to stand out in the cold.Ordered papri chat for starters and malai kofta/kashmiri chicken/naan for dinner.Papri chaat was average--not the best I have had in philly.makhni kofta and chicken were submerged in oil.We scraped off atleast 20 teaspoon of oil floating on top.plenty of artificial color in the curry--stuck to our fingers even long after finishing the meal/washing hands again and again.All in all a bad experience.There are better options around.Another point--not a single soul arrived there in the 30 odd minutes we stood outside--this was on a saturday evening 7 pm--speaks for itself! Not going back.

Went here for lunch. I was looking to get in and out in under an hour, but got out in 30 minutes. Although the place was small and crowded, there were a few open tables. The food came quickly, was hot and tasted great. Service was a bit spotty and slow, BUT it was the middle of lunch. I've also had better Thai tea in my day (theirs was much too sweet). Overall though, great value for the money. I've been before, and I'd go back.

Dark lighting, overly loud music, and straight up melted peanut butter on the peanut sauce dish. Waited forever for the last dish for our group of 4. I'm embarrassed to show how much I actually ate because I was so hungry by the time the food came.

Stopped in for lunch today! Everything was great and service was friendly and helpful. We don't know much about the cuisine so we had a billion questions and they never seemed upset by them. We are going to make it one of our frequently visited spots!

We ordered the family kabob meal. The veggies were delicious. Unfortunately the chicken was not fully cooked and the shrimp were not deveined. The Greek salad was ok, until we uncovered potato salad under all the lettuce (weird). I may give it another try only because my kids' wrap was really good and I've heard their lunch offerings are good as well. This place is fairly new, so I hope they're just working out the kinks.

The foods ok here. We tried the Burani appetizer, the Qablee Palaw and Qurma Chalaw lamb entrees, and the Firni dessert. All were decent enough. The service is fine too. But what was really cool is that somehow they designed this place to look just like my basement when I was growing up like 400 years ago with christmas lights and other knick knacks. Where are the scantily clad women posters though? Oh well...it's so dark at the Kabob House that they would be hard to see anyway.

We have eaten here a few times and it has always been very good. As another reviewer said, the "salt & pepper squid" (calamari) is especially good. The one problem with "Double Dragon" is that it is frequently closed, with no explanation. When available, the "two lobsters" dish is unique and very good. We have never had anything wrong with the food and feel that it is the best oriental place on the West Bank. Were it be open consistently, we'd go weekly.

I didn't even check yelp before going to Amber. I was staying in one of the local hotels and popped on google to see what restaurants were nearby. I was tired after a long day and a lot of driving and randomly decided on Indian. Boy was that a great choice! The dinner atmosphere was perfect, quiet, dim, and totally relaxing - just what I needed :) . The guys were incredibly polite. The food was superb and the quantities were massive compared to what I was expecting! The leftovers were great the next day and saved me from having to go out again the next day. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Great new fast casual place in the KOP town center. It's like a Chipotle style build your own shawarma bowl. Their meats and falafel are decent-- they could be more flavorful-- and their fries are really interesting, kind of like a thicker potato chip that's crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. But what brings me back time and time again is their pita bread. They advertise it as addicting, and it really is. It's so soft and pillowy and served warm. Definitely satisfies a carb craving on a cold day.

I like this place and would go back. I am a bit frustrated with their minimum credit card charge requirement. Fortunately, they have an ATM inside the restaurant and they don't charge a large fee. There are several great options. I would go back.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Indianapolis! The food is excellent as is the service! The vermicelli bowls are amazing and the spring rolls are the best! Everything tastes extremely fresh and has lots of flavor. The pho is very good and makes for a great meal! The only problem with this place is that once you go there you won't want Vietnamese from anywhere else. We moved out of state but Pho 36 is one of our must go places when we come back to visit. This place is a MUST!!

A pleasant traditional Greek restaurant serving all the standards at reasonable prices. There is nothing especially noteworthy about the food with the exception of the grilled octopus, which was perfectly done. The roasted lamb is overdone but tasty, no pink for this chef and accompanied by the traditional sides of roasted potato and rice. Why an ice-cream scooper's worth of rice is considered important with another starch on the plate is something I will leave for others to determine. The service was efficient and the Greek music apparently SOP for traditional tavernas. You won't break the bank here and you won't leave planning your next visit. You will have a pleasant experience.

This is a no nonsense local Vietnamese joint located in the most obscure location sharing a building with 7-11. Once you get passed the ambiance and the lack of service, the food speaks for itself. My pho was generous and delicious. The broth was tasty and their version of chili oil was unique and very good. I will definitely return!

Great food. Hadn't been there in a while but they recently began delivery so I ordered. Delivery was fast, friendly and food was just as my last visit in person, delicious. The Greek salad, gyros, rice, roasted potatoes and mixed vegetables were awesome. I'll be ordering again soon.

Stopped by here on our trip cross country and it turned out to be one of the best meals I had the entire way. We had the Chicken Tikka Masala, Naan and Lamb Kabob and all of it was amazing. What I nice little surprise in Boise. I would highly recommend this place!

I LOVE THIS PLACE. I went with a friend who claims it's the best thai food ever, and she was right. I just got home. I don't feel greasy and gross, just real full, because I couldn't stop eating it. I would go out of my way to go back here.

My first experience having Thai food. The food was very tasty, I'd give that 4.5 stars actually. The service left a bit to be desired. We ordered ice water when we ordered our appetizers but did not receive it until AFTER we were served, and we did ask for it again. There were only 2 other couples in the restaurant at the time. Was also surprised that our meals were served on chipped plates with only knives... I had to take silverware from the table across the aisle from our booth. I will have Thai again, I might even try this place again... could have just been a bad night ;)

Never eat at Sofra on Friday the 13th! (and certainly don't send anything back to the chef!) Normally a devout and 3-4X a year Sofra fan, I've always ordered the Sultan's Sofrasi, as mentioned in other reviews: a 4 course platter of appetizers, main course of meats and the almighty baklava finish. When eating the lamb portion of our dinner, the lamb was raw of both pieces of meat. Normally, I enjoy a medium or well done cutlet (and the chef/owner ALWAYS cooks it in this fashion without special request to the amazing and professional wait staff). Considering the potential for bacteria and food poison, my bff and I request that the meat be cooked thoroughly. It's returned in only slightly better condition. This game of ping pong is done 3 more times over 2 different selections of lamb (the owner refuses to swap out for other kind of meat such as hamburger patties, chicken or beef that is also served with the dish), before I'm vehemently told that "this is the way that it is always prepared" and that "You're stupid for not telling the wait staff how you want it done". Upon consultation with our two servers, this is apparently typical behaviour for the owner whenever food is deemed unsafe or undesirable by patrons. The owner smugly repeats his aforementionned comments when I pay for my meal with one of our servers for the evening. After 4 years of dining at Sofra, I think it's time to find a new Turkish place.
Excellent Chinese restaurant! Food is consistently delicious! They now also have Thai and Japanese cuisine. Sherry and Annie are wonderful hosts!
Great food for a reasonable price. I really enjoy the vegetarian plate and the med. salad.

Looks pretty ghetto from outside. But man is this food good. It's byob. The kabobs are delicious, the eggplant dish is amazing, the meatballs are so savory. For dessert they have baklava, it has a unique flavor, still really good. The server is a little bit awkward but a really nice guy. The music is nice, not so loud like many Americanized restaurants prefer, I've never seen it very full, I can always just walk in and get a table. Don't let the outside dissuade you from coming in!

I'm from Los Angeles and stopped by here on the way from the airport. Great Korean food and the Korean bbq was awesome! I'm sure this place will be discovered soon enough since they just opened a few months ago. I hope I'll be able to get a table the next time I visit. Reasonable prices and a must if you're wanting authentic Korean food. There's a Korean grocery store next door so we were delighted to get Korean vegetables and seaweed to take home as well!
The food is pretty good, but when you take price into account, you can do much better. I wouldn't go back here. It was better when they had a lunch buffet.

Opa! My wife's been here five times already and it's only been open six weeks. Love it! I've been here three times. Fantastic! Got to have the Korinthian lamb, the grilled octopus and the authentic lamb pita. They slow roast the lamb roast to medium rare and serve. Excellent!
I feel that chicken was not fresh. Probably stale. Food quantity is less. You can see that bowl is half empty. Not worth for the price they charge

Grabbed the Thai short rib and chicken stay tacos for lunch today. There were many layers of flavor and was over an enjoyable experience. Cucina Zapata gave large, no giant, portions for low prices. A few comments: The short rib and the chicken were both a bit dry, but given that this is a food truck, it was forgivable The tortillas could have been warmed for a more well rounded experience Everything seemed quite sweet Overall, it wasn't perfect, but definitely good for a lunch food truck stop.

Oh how I love this place. I don't know why I don't go more. That's a lie. I don't go more because every time I go I eat waaaayyyyyy to much. It's so good, I can't help myself. Bear in mind, one does not go here for the ambiance. It's in a strip mall next to a CVS and the decor is.....minimalist at best. It's my favorite kind of place: a little hole in the wall restaurant that you would drive by a hundred times without ever knowing it was there. One of those places that you only find out about because someone takes you there. The food is AMAZING. The menu offers a wide variety of items so there is something for everyone. You are able to pick the level of spice in your dishes, so you can customize the dishes to suit your taste. The naan is wonderful. And the palak pakor....oh, it's just delicious. I get it every time I go. Go for the food (not the atmosphere)...you won't be sorry.

While you wouldn't know it to look at it, this is the best Thai restaurant in Nashville. I can speak to the buffet- I've never had it. But, I love the service and food in the dining room. The dining room has sunken Thai seating with pillows and is very comfortable. My favorite dish hands down is the Masaman Curry with Tofu. I always ask for extra Thai basil to go with it. The fresh spring rolls are also very good, however I ask them to hold the shrimp. My boyfriend loves the spicy eggplant. Such a hidden gem.

The meat moussaka entrée and moussaka appetizer are my favorite items on the menu. I think they have the best moussaka in this area that I have tried. I also like the Albasha super salad, it has no meat but it filling. I always ask for the dressing on the side as they put too much on the salads for me. Lentil soup is good and hot. Any of the kabobs entrees are a good recommendation and I love the hummus. Everything is always fresh. Service is fast and efficient. A great place for lunch and easy for take out.
Fresh, authentic, high quality food. Awesome staff, family owned. The owners are so appreciative of your business. Honestly, though - this place is a gem

We shared the chicken biryani, chili paneer, Taj Indian beer and naan. It was different and wonderful. Come on Mt Juliet, support these eateries unless you just want fast and chain restaurant food in our backyard!
Cheap and delicious! Had the Captain Crunch, can't wait to go back for tacos!
The food was great and definitely be back. It was a bit slow getting my order but worth it. Had my order to go so I don't know about the service.

I wanted to love this place. We had actually driven out to visit King Wok, but decided to try here because we've been wanting Indian food. The garlic naan we had was great. The sauces for both the Saaglamb and the lamb vindaloo were both delicious. For me, the problem was that both dishes' lamb had shards of bone and were chewy with fatty or bad cuts in it. I ate around the meat, which is tragic to me when the lamb should be the best part. I'm not sure I'll come back. The photos of the buffet look great, and they probably do chicken just fine, but apparently not lamb, or at least not tonight.
We had an excellent meal - I had the trout and my husband had the lobster ravioli. Both were delicious. Make reservations, if possible, if you want the dining room, but the bar was very roomy, too.

More like 3.5 stars. I've always wanted to go to the Jerk Hut in the summer and sit outside and listen to reggae, but it turns out, I ended up going on a cold November night and sat inside. The inside is pretty small and crowded on a Saturday night. Our server was very friendly and attentive. Luckily we had some sort of Groupon or Living Social discount because the prices seemed a bit high for the type of food and restaurant. I got the pumpkin soup which was pretty good. It was definitely homemade with chunks of pumpkins and other vegetables. I felt like it was very healthy. After that I got the curry potato roti. I have had many rotis in the past, and in comparison, this one was VERY dry on the inside and the filling was not as spicy or flavorful as I would have liked. I could only eat about 1/3rd of it and didn't want to take the rest home. As much as I hate the service in the Mini Trini food truck, I much prefer their Caribbean food - it's 5 stars. I will probably come back here in the summer for the outside atmosphere and music. If you have a vegetarian in your life, the Jerk Hut has many options.

First off, what a charming place this is. I found it intriguing that one descends into this place, as it is below ground. It's nestled in between the many shops and restaurants on Sansom Street. My waitress this evening was a cute little girl of no more than ten, who took her job quite seriously! And to boot, she's a far better waitress than 90% of the other restaurants I've been to. It was amusing how serious she was at ringing up my bill. But on to the food. I have to say it's nice to have something other than banal Middle-Eastern food prepared with little to no imagination. SKH puts thought into their menu, though by no means was my experience a cerebral one. I ordered a lamb stew that was cooked in a sauce similar to a curry, though a bit sweeter and it had onions and pepper. It was served with a light salad with a yogurt dressing as a starter. Then came the brown rice and lamb dish with Afghan bread. The lamb was like butter in your mouth and the sauce was fantastic. All the food complemented itself. And they also brew a wonderful tea. My only negative detail was that I found the sauce to be a tad bit salty. As for one who likes to keep an eye on the salt consumption, this was a minor detail. I'll see if this was a fluke or a regular practice next time. If you find yourself in Center City, by all means, visit the Kabob House on Sansom Street.

This is our go to Indian restaurant in the area. We first went on the recommendation of an Indian friend, and I'm glad we did. The food is unique, well prepared, and the counter service is always nice. Pay with cash and get a free dessert - yum!

The Biryani is amazingly authentic. My water glass is always full. The servers are more than attentive and the manager is always available to help patrons navigate the well-crafted menu. He is polite and kind and great with our two kids that are quite a handful. They have a nice kids menu! They have pick-up or dine-in. They said they'll be starting delivery soon, too! The decor has a chic trendy vibe that reminds me of an inner city restaurant without having to drive into Philadelphia or NYC. I would highly recommend this restaurant and urge you to give it a try. Date night, family night, business meeting, groups or single dining. You won't be sad you did.
The service is excellent and the people are incredible. Extraordinary food in all aspects. Hands down the best local Indian restaurant in the surrounding area

I just cannot bring myself to find this place worth it. I've been here twice because of the ultra-convenient location (and, OK, the pretty cool equestrian stone leviathans flanking the front door). While the food was fine, I always have opportunity cost regret when I get the check--$50 for the two of us to eat food that I would have enjoyed more from my local chinese restaurant for half the price. So an all around meh experience--service, food, value. If you're hell bent on getting fancy-ish chinese good, I suggest going to this place's more casual little brother, Pei Wei, on City Ave. As for PF Chang's, I think that there's a high probability that those stone horses that lured me in could end up as equine Ozymandiases, telling the story of something that existed long ago.

Used takeout from EAT24. Ordered: Roti Canai: really enjoyed this, compared to places like Banana Leaf or Penang. It's much thicker, and the curry has bits of chicken and large chunks of potatoes. This for sure is a must order. Popia (Summer Rolls): never had this before. It's got a really light and gelatinous outside, and the inside tastes mostly of bean sprouts. Did not really like this. Sauce was tasty. Beef Chow Fun: good amount of spice and nice tasty slices of beef. Solid, and tasted better than most generic Chinese places. Green curry: I liked how many vegetables were crammed in this, it was chunky and less liquidy compared to most places. Good spice and good balance with coconut milk. Will definitely have to stop by in person.
Would highly recommend this place for delicious lunch! Shrimp vermicelli was very tasty. Check out my experience on Picdish: http://picdish.com/experience/16779-59533
Came back here for dinner tonight. Really good once again. B0 is the magic number. Chicken with lemon grass. SOOOOOO GOOOOOOD. Also get the fire "fried" ice cream for desert.

This is one of the best Thai places I've been to, which is impressive since I've lived in L.A. for a while. But seriously, although it's location is not ideal for the downtown Phoenixville traveller, as a local I highly recommend it. The curry is always consistent and delicious. The staff is always friendly and always remember us even when it's been a while since our last visit. Definitely check them out!

Oh man I don't even know how to describe Zorba's. I have literally never had a bad meal there - at least 20 times eating there between dining in and takeout - and everything I've had immediately becomes my favorite! BYOB (there's a liquor store just up Fairmount Ave).

Our first visit was amazing! There were seven of us and we had everything from roasted duck to BangBang Tofu. The tofu was devoured by teenage boys who never tasted it. The chili sauce made the difference; just not enough of it. The restaurant has an elegant ambiance with soft music, low lights, wood carved table decor, and stunning servers wearing authentic dress. The food was served in a timely manner on beautiful dishes. Everything was super delicious!!!!

Disastrous first experience and I will not be going back. First, they got my order completely wrong and then tried to blame me. I know damn well what I ordered. Secondly, my co-worker was over charged for her order. We went for lunch and should have had the lunch pricing. Instead, she was charged $10. Even the dinner prices are not that much! Finally, the lady "helping" us was very rude. As someone who deals with the public, I understand miscommunication and frustration, but that's no excuse. To top it off, the food wasn't even that great. This is one customer who was not impressed.
Love the Chicken Satay, Chicken Pad Thai and Massamun Curry; Thai rolls are good; thai tulip was okay. We drive 20 minutes to get it.

We went for a birthday and ordered the octopus, shrimp pil pil, tomato & mozzarella salad. They were all amazing. Honestly way more delightful then our main meal. Then we put in an order for the seafood combo - I was shocked that this was in broth and served with rice. No flavor to the broth. It was awful. I wish the servers would have actually told us how it was prepared or at least that it was in ... soup? Also, the seafood fettuccini.... we all had honestly thought it would be seafood in fettuccini Alfredo style sauce. Once again, not soup. It was gross. We both picked out the main fish and threw it out. However, the Appetizers were to die for. I will give this another shot and specify I would like to not have a fish with broth in it........

I guess this is a relatively new spot judging by the lack of reviews. Nothing really stood out about my dinner experience except that they had lamb samosas which were a real treat compared to the normal potato ones. Their chutneys were weak and they were missing the red onion so it was only the tamarind sauce and the green one. The entrees were good and came out "indian spicy" as request. I had the lam Karahi while my friend had paneer. He mentioned how it seemed to be higher quality but I saw it as on par with all the other local Indian spots.

This place was excellent! I got a make your own pad thai with beef and it was the best I've found in St. Louis so far. I'm eager to try everything else on the menu. The staff was friendly and laid back. Great experience overall.

The atmosphere is completely opposite of most Caribbean restaurants. It is the Perfect setting for a romantic dinner, wedding party, etc. The food is immaculate and had great presentation (I ordered the oxtail). The owners really catered to my experience and I will be revisiting this restaurant in the future.
The food is consistently fresh and flavorful. This is one of the best Indiana restaurants in Indianapolis.

Cozy new spot in South St! I love thai food and they are located just by my workplace, so they're perfect for me. I ordered drunken noodle and really enjoyed it. Excellent service and friendly waitress. Hope they stay busy so I can keep getting my thai fix from them!!

This was my second time having dinner at Guru. I really like the dish I get (malai kofta). Unfortunately this past experience was not as good as the first time. The people are very nice and attentive but there was a miscommunication last night regarding spicy levels. This isn't good if you ask for mild and get spicy. We were also surprised that the tandoori chicken was dry. We'll give it another try and hopefully the food will be better and more consistent with the first visit.
The food is full of flavor and quite delicious. It is a bit pricey but totally worth it!

We were underwhelmed. We came expecting a good range of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, as per the normal menu, but the Christmas even menu didn't have a single vegetarian main dish on it! I would then have expected the chef to be able to whip up something fairly easily, but my vegetarian pasta was very disappointing - it was essentially noodles in a soup of olive oil and white wine, and I could have made something better myself. The rest of the food my family got was tasty, but all overpriced for the quantity. The cheese board looked like leftovers thrown together.
Bulgogi - damn good! Dolsot Bibimbap - awesome!! There is a new sign outside Korea House, not sure where the Hangook Kwan sign went. But either way, I cannot wait to return!!!
I love tryst. Matty is a great bartender. I had the salmon crostini, goat cheese was really heavy, maybe half that. You really need to bring back the bar tater tots.

I placed my order with them through Eat24 on Yelp.. They said my order would take 1 hour to arrive, it was delivered 20 minutes earlier.. My food arrived Hot, Fresh and Exactly as I ordered it.. My food was absolutely delicious .. This was a completely easy way for me to get food Fast and Fresh brought right to my hotel door.. I will absolutely be ordering from them again and I love using Yelp services..

Amazing west side pho place. Can't go wrong with any of their soups. Ingredients are always fresh and very flavorful. Went in there the other night for take out and noticed a lot of chat between the owners and people walking in, so must have a lot of regulars and that says something. Just bring a jacket if going on a cold day because the swinging door and a small restaurant equals super chilly inside.

DOONERZ = SUCCESS I don't even know how to start this review. I've been to this place a number of times, but those number of times don't add up to many memories if you catch what I'm throwing at cha. All I know is that I walk in and literally say this, "give me the shit" which is usually followed by a confused stare, which is then followed with me reiterating "give me whatever's the shit" They usually finally understand what I'm babbling and respond with "I got you bro" What follows is amazingness. I couldn't tell you what the hell Im eating, but I will tell you it's definitely The Shit

This is a good option for Thai on the Mainline. It's small, quaint, and offers a nice selection of tasty dishes. I love the sauteed ginger flounder, which is a rich and delicious stew-like concoction. The mussels appetizer is tender, well-spiced and very flavorful. The curries can be made extremely spicy and the green curry, in particular, is excellent. The pad thai is also very good. Whenever I'm on the Mainline and in the mood for Thai, I come here. It's small but offers much better cuisine than the chains in the area for a good price. Our waitress was very pleasant and sweet. Definitely recommend. We also get take-out here quite often, and that has always been great.

The atmosphere and decor was very simple and beautiful, open and airy restaurant with a very nice outdoor setup. The food didn't take long, and the service was great. At one point we asked if we could get one of the wraps cut into several pieces and manager came to our table to suggest other options - we got a deconstructed beef kofta wrap and were able to make mini pitas ourselves. True to Lebanese culture, everything is sharing-style plates. Ordered the Lahim bi ajin man'oushe, beet salad, lamb hummus, shish tawook, baba ghanoush, and beef kofta wrap. All were good, but compared to their other restaurant (Cafe la Maude) it fell a little short. And.. The bakery section was basically out of everything BUT we got the last rose and pistachio cruller and it was insanely good
Delicious lunch! I had the coconut soup (veggie) and veggie drunken noodles. I wish I could have finished it all, but I was stuffed! Great service, friendly staff.

I have rarely had food this nasty. I mean--wow. I wanted to scrape my tongue off when I left this restaurant. They had this HORRIBLE eggplant soup. It was bitter and gritty. So nasty. I was actually amazed at how wretched it was. I had a small salad as well. I think it could have been good if I had gotten a different dressing. I had a meat entree as well. I want to say that it was lamb. It was tough and flavorless. Will never go here again.

Still a solid option for Ethiopian, wish there were more choices in Tampa, this food is full of bold addictive flavors. Gotta knock it one star because the service has gone down. The place is missing something, they now do buffet only on Thursday and Friday, we were the only ones in the restaurant and the place just felt dead. No real ambiance.

Nadia is a small BYOB, tucked away across from the Lansdale train station. I ordered take out. The order included the Nadia Treasure Platter, which came with a crab dumping , a fried wonton, 2 little shrimp corn cakes, a spring roll, triangle tofu, 2 skewers of chicken satay. Included 3 different sauces-peanut, soy, and sweet & tangy. I also ordered a salad with peanut dressing. There were varied textures and colors and everything was tasty and varied. Another time, I ordered the drunken noodles, and I have also ordered the Pad Thai on a different occasion. All dishes used fresh, varied ingredients. Next time I'll order the Bangkok Eggplant special with bell peppers, shrimp, and chicken stir fried in a spicy Thai basil sauce.

Overall, I can't complain about the place. The food hummus was good as well as the boneless chicken wings. I can't give it an AMAZING review but I was satisfied. Be aware, the boneless wings ARE BIG - I accidentally ordered 10 of them and felt like a glutton. Clean store, the drink options were lacking.

I apologize in advance for the lengthy review but when I give a low rating, I like to elaborate on the "why". My husband and I went to Momo's to use our Groupon that was set to expire. We had seen the place be busy before but had never been. I knew to call in a reservation the morning of. Service: We arrived right on time for our 6:15 reservation and were seated right away. It was super busy for a Tuesday and 10 minutes passed before we even met our waitress and got to view a menu. Our waitress was training someone so that led us to believe the restaurant was short staffed. 5 minutes later we ordered an appetizer. We needed additional time before ordering the main course so she said she'd come back. At 6:45 we still did not have our appetizer but had at least put in our main course order. Long story short, we finally got our appetizer at around 7:00 and our main meal nearly 1/2 hour later! Not just that, but: -- a couple who arrived after us and ordered just as much food had eaten, paid and left before we got our meal; and, -- a server kept running around the area attempting to deliver customers' orders to the wrong tables (this happened at minimum 4 times). Now, about the food. The Baked Feta was yummy. It was a 5x5inch square of warm feta topped with olives, onions, red peppers, and sun-dried tomatoes. It was served with lavosh (a cracker-like item). Our lamb gyros were so-so. There was meat somewhere under all that pesky lettuce. The tzaziki sauce and other toppings were in the right amount but there was way too much lettuce. I have actually bought comparable gyros in a kit in the frozen section at Shop N Save. The side of fries were listed as "Greek Fries" of some sort (truthfully, we only ordered them to max out our $30 Groupon). We thought we'd be getting regular fries with some sort of Greek seasoning. Nope. Just crinkle cut fries OreIda-style. Sad sad sad. About the atmosphere. The decor is exotic; warm colors and lanterns. At 6:15, it was buzzing, but not loud. By 7:15, there was loud Greek/Mediterranean music playing and a belly dancer perusing the aisles shaking it. It was kind of charming on one hand, and kind of not on the other as we finished our meal with a booty shaking right in our faces. The atmosphere is definitely what you're paying for. Overall, we won't be back. It was far too busy for a random TUESDAY - and they clearly couldn't handle their large customer base. There are other places in The Lou to get equally as tasty Greek food. PS - Parking is a NIGHTMARE. Only street parking near a residential area with no parking signs posted. Good luck.
Used to love going here but dj is awfulllllll. Service isn't bad when busy, yet when it's slow they take forever? hope they make some changes because the hookah is usually good.

Eh, not awful but not great, but for $6.50 it's ok. I ordered chicken casserole which was basically rice with a minimal amount of chicken pieces thrown in. The veggies were good. The waitress exhausted me just watching her - she was nonstop and on point with all her tables.
Awsome, waitist was very nice. clean and sooo delicious!!!!

Found this place during my lunch break from jury duty (I'm a sucks for Thai food), right around the corner from the court house. Staff friendly, Won - ton soup is a must have...totally different spin than anywhere else. Pad Thai was delicious, but I should have asked for the heat, but would definitely recommend and return to this restaurant.

Chipotle style Indian food. Service could have been a little faster. Rice was not hot. Chicken is chopped up. Overall the flavor was not bad. I got the chicken Tikki Masala sauce and Lamb with Korma sauce. I also got the chicken samosas. They were kind of dry and can use some sauce of some kind in it. However, 2 for $3.95 is kind of expensive. I think I will give them another shot.

As a regular customer of Pita Jungle on Broadway. I love the food and the variety of options on the menu. The service is by fare the best I have experienced while dinning out. My server Kirsten the other day was just awesome. I came in for lunch and didn't have a lot of time. She was fast to greet me and take my order. Even with all the customers she was taken care of. She suggested new items for me to try and made sure my allergies were noted. She asked how my day was and I could tell she was over all a genuine person. I will be back without a doubt and hope to have her as my server.
Love this place! Their tilapia burrito is amazingly delicious! They took orders pretty fast but there is always a long line there. I would suggest avoid the lunch break time - it gets way too packed.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Very vegan friendly! Love the vibe in here, as it's very bohemian & authentic. You see live music and get a delicious Indian meal. We enjoyed watching painters paint in the front entrance patio some beautiful portraits. I felt like it was in downtown California San Francisco area. I'm Punjabi and grew up eating Indian food, so I'm very critical with my favorite dish - bhindi masala. The dish was freshly made with the spice level customized to our request. Okra was very fresh, although I prefer a thicker sauce. The owner came by to check on our experience & we had a great chat. Service was excellent- we had a college student very eager to please. Highly recommend it!

This place is not the best, but not the worst. I've had their Thai Spicy Fried Rice, which is pretty good and big portioned. Their Pad Thai, however, is not very good. Definitely have had better elsewhere.

My wife and I eat here about once every month or two. The pad thai and spicy fried rice are our favorites. Tonight, we both ordered the spicy fried rice, and I guess they changed their recipe to be way hotter than it was before. I thought it was OK, but it was too spicy for my wife. The service was fantastic though, and they had no problem cooking up a new, milder plate quickly. It was a great experience.

That chicken lawd.... was seasoned to perfection the perfect amount of salt oregano lemon butter and whatever else they use...oh yea the fries just soak up that honey lemony goodness and the salad with chicken makes for a good lunch option.... fries by themselves were a tench salty for me but my friend loved them... I have finicky taste buds.... but back to that dang chicken it was so tender and juicy and just damn good... i also tried the Rosé wine which was a nice 8oz serving... Go here eat here please and thank you

Extremely underwhelmed is an understatement. Green curry was arguably the worst I've ever had--watery and extremely bland. Coconut soup was the same- not thick enough, diluted and no where close to being remotely authentic. I've been to Thailand several times therefore have a solid benchmark of real Thai cuisine. Only thing I tried that somewhat resembled real Thai was the Pad Thai. Best Thai in town is King and I without a doubt.

Flavors and low level of heat a bit Americanized for my tastes. Ordered food on way home from airport and was told it would be ready in 30 minutes, and it certainly took a bit longer. After a long day of travel I was starving--to have brought home this blander version of Thai food was disappointing. Perhaps owners could ask customers if they want bolder spicing and heat? This place was recommended to me as the best Thai in the city but I felt it didn't meet expectations.

I was heading from Orlando to Clearwater after work for a 200k bike ride the following day and passed this restaurant on my way to a hotel just down the street. When I checked Yelp and saw all of the positive reviews, I had to give it a try. I arrived around 7:15 on a Friday night and the dining room was fairly empty; a few couples and 1 large family. I was seated immediately and ordered shortly thereafter. Lamb Korma and Peshwari Naan. I asked the waiter for some papadam, and he brought over 2 halves with somovere sweet tamarind sauce and green chutney, but no spicy onion chutney. Oh well. My food took a while to arrive... about 35 minutes... but it was worth the wait! The lamb was tender and juicy, the sauce was thick with complex flavors and the naan was baked perfectly and had just the right amount of sweetness. The portion sizes were quite generous; if I wasn't doing an 8 hour bike ride the following day, it would have been enough for two. The service was good and similar to what I've experienced in other authentic Indian restaurants: the servers were unobtrusive; they didn't constantly check on me, but my water glass stayed full and they came over if I looked their way. Much nicer than being asked how everything is going every 5 minutes, usually when your mouth is full. All in all, a great dinner at a fair price. My only complaint is that like seemly every restaurant these days, there were several TV's the bar showing various sporting events (Little League World Series, NASCAR, etc). I can see that in a sports bar, but is it really necessary in a nice Indian restaurant?
Been going to Tony Express since medical school. The best breakfast and lunch in the area! The egg, cheese turkey bacon wraps are unmatched and the burgers are phenomenal. Lucky to have him here!
We just ate at the Persian room and I must say the food was wonderful. The inside of the restaurant was so beautiful the service was great. Dinner was a little expense but while worth it.

These guys really deserve the five stars. They work so hard. Even if they put avocado on something when I ask for it without avocado, or if my veggie burger is slightly crisper than I'd like, I have to remember that they have dozens of customers lining up to order at any given time of day, and only a few people working in the truck. Their food is consistently phenomenal, and they're such a friendly bunch of people! The food is delicious; the veggie burger is my favorite in the whole city, especially because they top it off with cabbage alongside the lettuce and tomato. It's a stroke of genius, in my opinion - the extra crunch elevates the whole burger. I enjoy their spicy mayo on everything. The vegetarian curry they occasionally have is pretty delicious; I love the flavor of the sweet potatoes. I'd like to try the tilapia over rice sometime, and my coworkers think that their breakfast specials are phenomenal (although I can't eat any of their current specials). I'd also like to reiterate how friendly the staff are at Cucina. Seriously nice folks. Be aware that there is a good chance that you'll be waiting for half an hour or longer for your food. If you don't have that kind of time for lunch, don't come here and feel insulted when your food takes longer than you intended to wait. They're working their butts off. Additionally, they DO NOT take cards. I mentioned this in the survey, but I think it's important to note here, too.

Came here for dinner for the first time. The servers were nice. Ordered hot tea, and it was good compared to other bland hot teas I've ordered in other Asian restaurants. Ordered Summer Rolls (with grilled pork) for appetizers. These were delicious. I liked these more than the Spring Rolls with Grilled Pork at 999 Pho. For our main dishes, we ordered Salt & Pepper Shrimp and Peking Pork Chop. Both tasted fine. Their hot chili oil was basic, I like Hong Kong Diner 2's more.

We were in town for a weekend at Sesame Place and decided to do take out from Guru's after our little one went to sleep (shhhhh!) Here are the details of our take out experience... Food: Delicious choices. Most of the dishes you would expect at a great Indian restaurant. We opted for one Chicken Makhani and one Paneer Makhani. They were absolutely delicious. Probably one of the best versions of each that we've ever had. We added an order of naan (the name escapes me) that had a chutney type mixture inside with a sweet sauce. It was like nothing we have ever had and it was amazing. Service: From placing our order on the phone to picking up the meal at the restaurant, they provided great service. They even gave each take out customer a mini-bottle of water (it was a really hot day) while we waited. It's apparent that the staff takes pride in their work and values their customers (locals and tourists alike). Bottom line: We absolutely would visit Guru's again the next time our travels bring us to the area as this goes down as our favorite Indian meal to date. Highly recommend you give them a try if you have not already!

I grew up eating Indian food -- so when I moved to the Main Line, I immediately started looking for a quality Indian restaurant. There's quite a few around the area, but truly, I haven't even tried the other ones yet because I love Ekta! Fresh and delicious food -- I've tried many of their non-veg main courses and I have no complaints so far! Can't go wrong with the naan, vindaloo, saagwala, kadai ...all very good! Next time, will try their tandoor and biryani dishes. I guess I wish they could adjust the spices on some of the dishes, but that's not too big of a deal. The service is great once you are seated, but I've been here a couple times when I've had to literally wait for over an hour on a weekday night (and there's not much room to begin with) -- so make a reservation even if you don't think you need one. Nice atmosphere and BYOB. Prices are reasonable (main courses $11-16ish).

What a cute restaurant but unfortunately the service and food brought the ratings down. I located this based on the yelp app. On Yelp app it has an average rating of four stars. Ambience: It reminded me of the restaurants seen on Hollywood movie sets. They have very dim but red lighting. Kind of cool and different from other Thai restaurants. It did distinctly remind of of Thailand evening district. Service: Service was poor. I waited 10 minutes before she came and took my drink order. Then I requested a glass of red wine. This took another 10 minutes. She finally took my order after 20 minutes of waiting. Yes the server was not in any hurry to wait on me. Lastly, it took her 10 minutes to bring my check and return my credit card. She definitely was not aware of my request. Not once did she ask how I was doing and if the food was ok. I might as well have served myself. Food: I ordered fresh spring rolls but our came the fried spring rolls. The fresh spring was not so fresh. The chicken tasted like cool presses chicken. Do not order unless you want slimy spring roll skin with compressed faux chickens. I ordered the Tofu with rice noodles and Vegetable soup. This was the beef noodle which she allowed me to sub the beef with the tofu. The broth was very good. But beware of the peanuts crumbs. The soup was so hot and spicy it made me sweat. Good flavors though. There was no vegetable just some cilantro and scallions. This was not the tofu with vegetable that I had really wanted. Overall, I have had great Thai food at other restaurants and this place was just ok not Great based on the price of what was received. My not so fresh spring rolls, tofu with some rice noodles, and one glass of wine total check came out to be $30.00. Pricey for mediocre food.

Yes, oh my, yes! After a heinous experience at a Thai spot on Delmar, I sort of fell off the Thai wagon--quite sad considering I ate it at least once a week while living in Chicago. Anyway, I had gone far too long without my green curry and decided to give Basil Spice a try this weekend. Hoo. Ray. Friendly, efficient service, relaxed atmosphere, reasonable prices and GOOOOOD food. Thank goodness. Justin enjoyed the tom yum, which nicely cleaned out his sinuses; we gobbled down the summer rolls which were fresh, fresh, fresh and came with two subtly spicy sauces (no overly sweet stuff here!); and the curries were great--just enough spice tingle, but no searing pain (although I'm sure they could up the ante if you asked). I docked a star because I'm fairly certain the peas and carrots in my curry were, um... frozen vegetable medley. Come on, guys, you can do better than that--you just proved it with your fresh veggie summer rolls! Still, if Basil Spice was in my 'hood, I'd be here all the time. I can't wait to head back and work my way through their menu. Yum!

I have lived in St. Albert for 8 years now and have enjoyed many a meal from here. One of my favorite menu items is the Bun 5 Mau. It is a Vermicelli bowl that has Julienne Pork, Meat Ball, Fried Roll, Grilled Pork, & Grilled Chicken. I find the service to be good here and prompt. My wife usually gets the chicken Pho and she really enjoys it. My kids get the brisket with noodles kids meal with no soup and they love it. We sometime also get the green onion cakes too and they are ok .. nothing to rave about. My family enjoys the food from here and we love to support local St. Albert business!

We enjoyed this place so much after the first time we visited that we came back within a few days to try the lunch buffet. What we loved: The decor is so absolutely beautiful. The restaurant is clean, and the service was spot-on. Our waiter (the first time) and our waitress (for the lunch buffet) were both very professional, very prompt, and seemed very eager to answer any questions we might have. The korma sauce is amazing, we couldn't get enough of the tandoori chicken, the sexy naan (yes, it's called that and it's deliciously spicy) and the chicken tikka masala. One thing I've personally never had before that I highly suggest giving a try is their vegetable pakora. We literally fought over it. With the lunch buffet came our own basket of hot and very fresh naan and it was delicious. What we would like to have experienced differently: While the chicken korma was delicious and used all white meat, the portion of chicken itself was a bit small compared to the amount of sauce. In the lunch buffet, the vegetable korma used standard mixed vegetables, but most importantly when we had dinner, our papadum was stale and therefore soft and not at all crisp. All in all, we loved the variety, and the quality of the food, service and over-all dining experience. We will be back.

This is a great place for Thai food. It is very clean and the staff are very friendly. We have gone here off and on over several years. When we were last there we noticed how many people were regular customers, having a good report with the staff. The food is well done and flavorful with multiple vegetarian options available.

Delicious and flavorful food. Their Ras Malai is A class!!! Ambience is professional and friendly. Seems like they have a new management now but I did not see a restroom or handwash place though inspite of being an Indian restaurant. Not very many silverware and napkins are served to customers either. But its definitely a place visiting more than once.

La Va is a pretty good place to hang out & possibly get some work done. There's a nice couch that's great to kick back on. The hours aren't that great, though -- they seem to close up for dinner pretty early. They serve substantial food, too, if you need sustenance. Good if you're in the area.

There's three things you need to know about why I like Land of Smile: 1) Thai food in St. Louis is generally poor. There's maybe three or four places in the metro area worth going to. Land of Smile gets bumped up largely out of frustration at the lack of viable alternatives. 2) The menu is a total minefield. If you order Calimari, Tom Ka Ga, and Pad Gra Pao or Pad Ginger and you're going to wonder how this place is in business because the first is from a freezer, the second is the most disgusting Tom Ka Ga imaginable (I hope they were just having a bad day that day, but the lemongrass was bad and the broth was just not good), and the third are just not memorable at all. Many of the entrees (ex. Lard Prig Sod) are horribly overpriced, and the salads are generally not well done at all. But 2/3 of the appetizers (crab rangoon, spring rolls, gui-chai, etc.) are delicious and definitely worth the money. Their Cashew Chicken is probably the best I've ever had, as they add a Thai flare to it. The real star here, however, and my favorite things on the menu, are the noodle dishes and curies. The masamun lacks any spice whatsoever (not necessarily bad, just different), but overall, I've always had good curry here. They seem to make it to American taste buds, so if you want it spicy in the thai sense, ask for it that way. Every noodle dish on the menu is good, with the Pad Sriracha, Pad Kee-Mao, and Bangkok Thai noodles being my favorite. Their rice noodles seem of better quality than most thai places (nothing from a Thai Kitchen box here). 3) I've found that the staff here is generally friendly and quick.

Stumble in here with a hangover; order a bowl of pho with rare steak; mix with hoisin sauce, sriracha, mint leaves, bean sprouts, a couple jalapenos, and a splash of fish sauce; eat; walk out of the restaurant a new person. It's always a good time for pho, but it's especially magical when hung over or on a rainy, gloomy day. Saigon is on par with the Vietnamese restaurants I frequent throughout LA and Southern California. Their vermicelli bowls are great as well. I recommend the grilled pork with egg roll (#91).

The food was amazing. We had the Bollywood biryani, Bollywood dosa, veg thali, and lamb curry. After the meal we couldn't decide which was our favorite, all of it was so good. The service was nice and very friendly. They kindly explained what we were eating and gave us recommendations when ordering, which turned out well. Over all a great spot for Indian food!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: I am a visitor of this area and not a resident. The sushi was good, just not the best I have ever had, which is why they get 3 stars. The service was great and next time I will just stick to the Chinese food which was pretty good!
First time trying this restaurant today. I had the crab fried rice and panang curry, both delicious. Fast, friendly service too. I will definitely be making this a regular stop for take out!

The food is amazing! My fiancee and I shared a vegetarian Queen's Eight platter and every single thing on it was delicious. The mushrooms were our favorite! Service was great as well, they are super friendly and the food came out very quickly. Their wine pours are generous as well :) As newer vegetarians, this will definitely be one of our go to places.

Wanting to try Rendang ever since It was on CNN's world's top 10 foods, husband & I found this little Indonesian place through Yelp. We travelled 30 miles to this restaurant and I was apprehensive when we stepped in but the food blowed me away. Definitely worth the drive. We ordered Chicken Satay, Fried wonton, coconut soup, Chicken Nasi Goreng and the Beef Rendang combo (I believe its R9 on the menu) & a coconut drink. Food came out pretty fast. Satay was good & Rendang was the best. It had the color, texture, flavor & the beef was perfectly cooked & tasted awesome too. just 2 pieces on the plate weren't enough. I was craving for more already. Would order it every time i go to this place again. They accept only cash but no worries there is an ATM right opposite to the restaurant.

I have never written a Yelp review, though I constantly read them in an effort to monitor and improve my own performance as a server. I know how devastating it can be to receive bad feedback, and I tend to give everyone in the service industry the absolute benefit of the doubt. However, after my experience at Pita Jungle this afternoon, I feel compelled--simply so that management is made aware of what happened. I walked in at around 4:00 and was promptly asked by someone at the host stand if I wanted to order food to go. I said no, and she told me (in a bit of an exasperated tone, but whatever) that I could sit wherever I wanted. I chose somewhere visible, near the patio doors. There was one server (maybe two?) on the floor, and she had, at most, three tables. She did not, at any point, acknowledge me or hand me a menu--instead, I watched her bus tables and enter orders in Aloha for approximately ten minutes before walking out and heading to Pei Wei. The girl who asked me if I wanted food to go was sitting at the bar when I left (maybe she wasn't actually on duty?) and didn't seem to care that I was leaving. I went to the Pita Jungle in Flagstaff for years, and was really looking forward to some hummus and a beer. Oh well.

Been coming here 2 weekends in a row, my husband, my son and I are very satisfied...we recently moved here from VA/DC area and craved for Viet dishes. I'm so glad we found this place...their summer rolls tastes fresh, combination rice platter is on point besides the rice isn't the authentic broken rice but it's still good. My husband got pho because that's all he ever crave. The staff/owner were friendly and very attentive. The price it is very affordable. Definitely coming back when I'm the area.
Used to be good. Now it blows. New owners are dropping the ball. Would never order a salad from here again and even the gyros are not as good.

Being fans of Thai food, my lovely date and myself decided to check out a local Thai place, and chose Erawan, as it received better than decent ratings on Yelp, and our choices were limited as Philadelphia is not known yet as the Thai Capital of America. Nonetheless, we both were excited to enjoy some Thai food in a Thai restaurant. I made reservations via phone on Friday, and spoke to a very polite person on the phone who was able to take me reservation with no isse, and was delighted to hear they were a BYOB (I have a bit of a wine cellar with a selection of somewhat unique wines) and did not charge an outrageous corking fee. The place itself was well put together; very clean, simply decorated without being boring, and quite spacious (long, but narrow). The service was quick and friendly as well. They made sure that there was always a full glass and no empty plates in front of you for very long at all, without making one feel rushed, a rarity indeed. The food was, I regret to say, a tad bland. We started with a chicken Satay that gave me high hopes - flavorful, moist poultry with a peanut sauce that wasn't overpowering. Following this for our main courses we ordered Drunken Noodles with a Massaman Curry, to share amongst ourselves. Both seemed, at least in my opinion, a bit lackluster. The noodles were overdone, and there was just a lack of punch that makes me enjoy that dish so very much. The curry was also bland; there was no discernable flavor that really jumped out for me. The portions were quite large, however. For dessert we had a mango sticky rice which was overly sweet (for me) but was still well done and beautifully presented with a fresh mango (yum!) flower atop the rice. I give this place 3 stars because of that blandness. I would really hope to come back here sometime soon and bump up the rating, because the rest of the dining experience was quite fantastic.
Best authentic pho in Indy. You should check out their Beef Stew. It is just so TASTY. Beef is tender and flavorful. The broth is unbeatable

I was hungry when I showed up just over an hour from closing time. They were inviting and pleasant and the food - calamari and the BBQ meat sampler for one - more than filled me up and was really delicious. I sat out on the walk on a nice night, not sure how big it is inside. Well done, glad I found the place.
In town for the evening and I was craving Indian food. Glad I found this place on Yelp. Delicious! Had the Chicken Tikka Masala w Garlic Naan.

Went recently with a group of friends on a Friday evening. It was novel, but I will not return. The waiters were friendly and attentive. The belly dancer was engaging and fun. However, for $25 per person including a 20% add-on gratuity, bringing the total to $30 a head in a group of ten; ($300), this does not include beverages. The value was horrible since the FOOD SUCKED! If this is AUTHENtic Moroccan food, then breadsticks are REAL Italian cuisine. Instead of nan, we were served wedges of french bread. The shishkabbobs were dry and over-cooked, the couscous was flavorless. The meat dish was uninspiring and tasted like they ordered a rotisserie chicken from the local Acme, then broiled it in water. Not bad, but, not worth the money. We do not recommend this place. There are other Moroccan restaurants that have higher recommendations; next time we will listen to the online reviews.

Since it's Santa Barbara, Pho Bistro is alright. I had the vermicelli a while back and I just had a bowl of Pho (Dac Biet, or means special) recently. I think I had the beef vermicelli. I was a bit disappointed. There were a good portion of beef and vermicelli but there wasn't a lot variety of veggies. They only had lettuce. I was hoping for bean sprouts, cucumbers and more. It came with one eggroll. It was good but it wasn't enough. I'm from the Bay Area where there's Pho restaurants every 3-5 miles. The pho from the Pho Bistro was alright. The soup was kind of bland and needed more flavor and a bit more salt. I was wondering if they had those small sauce dishes. There was a good amount of bean spouts but there wasn't enough herbs like basil. I had a Thai Tea along with my pho. The Thai tea was good. :) The prices are a bit high but it's Santa Barbara afterall. I didn't expect a lot from this bistro. I just wanted to try it out. Overall, like I said since it's Santa Barbara, Pho Bistro is alright. :)

In my opinion better than all other area Mediterranean restaurants. It was EXCELLENT! No wonder they have 5 Yelp stars. Great, fresh food, cosy place and the owners make you feel like family. We had a great meal and lots of fun! Highly recommended.

Center City has a dearth of good Thai food, but this place is the best I've eaten at so far. The decor is bright, upscale and nice. The service is good. Most importantly, the food is tasty. Philly has poor Thai food overall (except for Circles) but this place is by far the best in Center City. It just opened a couple months ago so give it a try.

Walked in for dinner last Friday for the first time. What a cute place! It had a great ambience and very clean. Not a lot of people sitting for dinner but a lot of people walking in and out with take-out. The place is BYOB. Food was pretty good. I ordered a dish I had never tried before called Three Friends. Everything was cooked well but didn't love the sauce. No fault of the cook, just not my thing. I will definitely order/go here again and try out their more classic dishes. Massaman curry here I come!
Wow ! I love this place ! It's clean, customer service is great and food was delicious . I will definitely bring my friends back next time when I'm in the area.
The food is ok..... Just wished they was portion was equivalent to the prices. U get here and most of the time they don't have the food u want available. Customer service could use some help.

I have no idea what I'm eating, but it's amazing. I put a layer of basmati on my plate and then the equal parts green, orange, and lightly redder orange. It was all so very good. Server offered me something I couldn't understand through his accent and when I asked if it was good he said yes so I agreed. It was like a savory crepe. Like I said, I'm very clueless to what I ate. Pretty sure there was chicken involved. The recognizable fried spinach was tasty and the naan was hour and cooked perfectly. Server guy was perfectly attentive, clearing plates each time we went to the buffet. Worth our thirty minute drive from the car east side.

My order took some time to make. I waited about half an hour. I got the pho special combo...lawdy lawd! It was tasty! A good variety of meat and veggies and the portions were generous as well. The mango bubble tea was great! Would definitely go back next time I'm in the area

This place is awsome, the best chinese/vietnamese food in reno. Have to try the potstickers, so good. And the thai tea is brewed to perfection. The pho is amazing the orange chicken is good i keep coming back cause the staff is friendly and the food is amazing. Definately recomend tgis place

I can't say enough about the superb and efficient service from Shannon, our server, as well as Alan, another employee. Grouper and mahi mahi were both fresh and perfectly cooked. We had shrimp appetizer and key lime pie for dessert- both terrific! The view is breathtaking. We will most definitely return!
Fantastic food! Fantastic & friendly service! Bartenders know what they are doing. Alexa, our server has been spot on and friendly. Shrimp po boy is perfect! I love this place! Thank you, Wassim!

We came up on this place in between classes one day and had a good sized line, so we had to try. We ordered the Cap N Crunch Tilapia Burrito and the Chicken Satay taco. The Tilapia was great. Crunchy and the sauce was very good. Good Combination and size. On the other side, the Chicken Satay was...not that great. I would not recommend that, but I would definitely recommend the Cap N Crunch Tilapia. Also the Thai Tea was good, but get less ice.

One of a kind Restaurant, I was very pleased from the chicken tenders, the sauce, biscuit, Mac & cheese ,pie and the watermelon cream soda! Everything was on point, I can't wait to make another visit to philly! I love wishbone!

I'm so glad I found this place, it's definitely gives Pho Cali and Pho Nu Vu competition in my favorite pho places. Alot of the same dishes are common Vietnamese food, but Pearl has quail and some other things Ive never seen on the others menus. I tried the brisket pho with tripe and cartilage, and vermicelli noodles with pork, both dishes were delicious. This place is also ten minutes from me. Even better. I'll be returning. 9/11/15 Check your CC/Debit account, I was charged $10 on a $6 tip, it could have been a mistake, but I'm always suspicious of that type of thing. And the manager never called me to remedy the error, I had to go through my bank. Not very good customer service.
Great good, awesome service We came late and they were nice to let us dine in and take our orders We had the Maqloba lamb and mixed grill Everything was tasty.
This was a great find for a late-nite family dinner. Staff was very friendly and accommodating. We had some sushi, Thai and Chinese food. Everything was excellent!

I frequent this cafe at least once a week. The staff and environment makes everyone feel comfortable. From the option of comfy chairs and couches, to tables to get work done at, it's the perfect cafe environment to chill out. I always get an iced soy latte, and it never disappoints. The food is always delicious and never takes too long to come out. I've had the shakshuka, hummus platter, hummus bagel, and Israeli salad. All of these dishes were very filling and very tasty.
