The food tasted amazing!! very authentic!! I ordered the green curry extra spicy, it was one of the best curry dishes I've had in awhile! The service was great. The waiters were very pleasant..
This is the best Thai food around. It is always specially made however you order it. They make you feel like they are cooking only for you. Fresh ingredients, perfect portions, and friendly staff.
A refreshing, modern take on Indian food. The samosas were light, and not greasy, as so many are. The Zaikka chicken was fantastic, spicy but flavorful.
For the price this place is decent. The guy at counter was very helpful since I am not familiar with this type of food.

Great food & cheap price. The only cons: they only accept cash so be prepared to bring cash. If you want to try some original authentic indonesian food, try their sop buntut (a little too much MSG for me) or mie medan (medan noodles). Recommended!

This unassuming treasure is tucked in a strip shopping center off US 19, so if you aren't looking for it you could drive on by, but don't make that mistake. The stuffed boneless chicken wings (stuffed with seasoned chicken and pork)were fried with the crispiest of batters and served with rice and veggies. I opted for the red chicken curry served with rice and fresh basil, and it did not let me down. Their menu was vast and had something for everyone. I heard from several people there that their Boba Tea is some of the best that you will have in Florida. This eatery was very clean and bright. They had an assortment of sauces to adorn your entree should you choose. The staff was friendly, helpful and extremely attentive. Didn't have the long wait time mentioned in other reviews, I am sure it is because it is a small restaurant and the food is prepared fresh and served hot. Thinking about going back later in the week for their Pad Thai (which I also heard rocked).

A friend of mine dropped in here for the lunch buffet, it was delicious and a great deal. I fell in love with their Chicken Tikka Masala, whenever we are looking for some unique takeout that is our first choice! Great food and the buffet is a great value.

To me this is the best stall in the Southgate Mall food court. A moderate selection of different dishes and naan bread made fresh by dudes in the back. So far I have tried; Both types of rice(saffron & steamed), saffron being by far the best of the two. Vegetable pakora, not bad, lots of fennel seed and sometimes too salty. Goes good with the green sauce Beef & Vegetable Samosas, beef was not the best. Vegetable was great with lots of potatoes. Saag Paneer, very good. It's like chili India style. Chunks of goat cheese with lots of peas in a great sauce. Chana Masala, great. Chickpeas in a masala sauce. Roasted Potatoes, not bad. Spiced up good, but not as good as the other items. The people that work here are really nice. They told me they couldn't make any specialty dishes from the larger restaurants, but they do change the buffet at times. You can also get mint and mango lassi drinks, I have not tried them yet.

The food is amazing. However, I recently arranged for take away, called in my order, told them I had one of their coupons from their website. They told me to bring it in and when I tried to redeem it, they said that they did not take them at that location. When I said that they told me to bring it, that it was from their website, they said that the coupon was for their other location. I explained that it was not indicated on the website or coupon. They went on to say that they were not really the same restaurant and that they'll be changing their name soon. Then they said, "It's confusing our customers". I said that it's especially confusing when it's your restaurant's name, number and location on the website with the coupon. Despite how good their food is, I doubt I'll return. I'll pay the delivery fee for another very good Thai place.

My wife and I come here regularly. Great vegetarian plate and their falafel is the best in the New Orleans area! Great menu selection and the grocery portion of the cafe is nice as well. Highly recommended!
I always have amazing experiences when I eat at Richards. The food is consistent and the atmosphere is great!

We have eaten from this Pollo Tropical a few times. We usually get the pork tropichop and enjoy it. The last time we ordered it, they forgot to give us the sauces. We just ordered it today and this was not the usual tasteful dish. It was cold and the pork was two very large chunks of fat. . I could not even cut it. Usually it is pieces of slow cooked pork over the top of it. Again, they did not give us the ordered sauces. I called, the manager and he did not make me bring it back. Although he should have looked at it to see how bad what was being served to me. He stated to come back to get a new order. Thankfully, I live close to the place but did have to go out of my way. I explained to the worker at the window and never received a "sorry for the trouble". Yes, the second order was better but still not as it used to be. Not sure if I will return to the place. If I do, I definitely will not order the pork again.

I have heard nothing but great things about this restaurant, however, when I entered in this beautifully layed out establishment I recieved awful service. The lady at the desk began to take my to-go order and walked away in the middle of it, cashed someone out from a table and entered my order after asking me again what I was. Then she was handed the payment and started cashing the person from behind me out while mine just rested on the counter. The number of completed transactions was more important than the quality of service. Not impressive.
Not so vegetarian friendly. Their cream cheese wontons has crab in it and they tried to give me fish sauce.
Got the Greek salad and hummus and it was delicious. Will definitely go there again when I'm in the area.

Such great Thai food! All of their plates are adorably plated! BUT... also quite tasty. I had the massaman curry with seafood- which was perfectly flavored! I also loved the seafood dumplings and the coconut soup which I got wth tofu! The staff were very friendly as well. The restaurant is in a cute little house.

I know that this is traditional Italian food, but they are so very limited on the vegetarian options, and I wish they would add at least one meatless entree. The ricotta tortelli with sage had a rich, but not-too-filling cream sauce. The white bean salad combined a good variety of flavors. We had good service tonight. Our waiter, Sean (Shawn?), was polite and attentive without being overbearing, which helped us enjoy a relaxing outing. I do think some of their items are overpriced. The salads and other small plates are tiny and would be more appropriate at about $6 instead of $9ish.
Great Thai food, but doesn't beat Sukoh Thai. The menu is simple along with the food. Still a great place for lunch for CBD workers.
Broth amazing. Eye round steak nice and soft/fresh. They have all the condiments and sauces. Largest portion of pho I've ever had, I had to pack the rest to go. Will be back for sure.
Best Vada Pao in DE!! I would say add PA too or maybe the east coast! All other items are good too but we stop at the farmers market specially for vada Pao, soooo worth it!

Went yesterday for the first time for BOTH lunch and dinner. Let me explain. We stopped for lunch and had the meat sampler for two + veggies. Everything was delicious, in particular the lamb, chicken, and sausage. My friend also had the rice pudding, which he loved. After paying, we felt so comfortable that we just sticked around chatting the afternoon away. We didn't decide to stay, it just sort of happened. Everyone was very nice and kept filling our water without sending us away. Dinner time came and I ordered the grilled octopus, which was very very good. Sidewalk seating was a plus. All in all, excellent food and comfortable, down to earth environment. Highly recommended.
The chaat was good, but the food was all cold. It seems like it all sits out for a long time. I would come back if the food was fresher since the flavor of everything was good.

This was my weekly to go place to get dinner for four but after today I'm not going back. I always order the same dishes and so know how much my bill should be but today it was $10 more. I took the to go menu did some math and sure I was overcharged. I asked to please check my bill again and the lady said she is charging for the to go containers...$10 for foam containers? She gave me $4 back and blamed calculator for not working. When I got home .... unbelievable.... I was missing spring rolls that I paid for. I'm not going back ever.

Food is good, healthy. I'm not a fan of their aggressive tip technique. When you pay they spin their screen around to give you the "opportunity" to auto-tip them 15% 20% or 25%. This is before you've experienced their food or their service. (Which is limited to running food). I'd give the food 4 stars but that pushiness made me lose my appetite for Taziki's.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I'm visiting family and friends for the week before heading back to Portland, Or. The Taj Mahal was first introduced to me at the beginning of my trip by friends, and it was such an amazing experience I had to go back once more before leaving. I haven't really delved into the world of Indian cuisine before- but am familiar with curries and what not. This restaurant has opened my eyes to all the spices, textures and flavor profile that is true Indian cuisine. This is not some chain that throws together food in 15mins.... This is made from scratch, using fresh, quality, authentic ingredients and a touch of amazingness. The prices average around $15-$25 an entree- but you will have plenty to take home! Or share (that's the best). The staff is mostly family that owns the restaurant- so they are attentive, efficient, kind and truly the best service you could ask for. The two times I have been to the Taj Mahal have been identical in incredible food quality, taste and service. The brood menu has something for everyone (I highly recommend the coconut curry with halibut) And I would suggest this restaurant to anyone in or visiting boise-whether your an Indian food fan or not- the sheer deliciousness will win you over. Very glad we found this little gem in the heart of downtown. My next trip to Boise- I will be sure to stop in. Probably twice.

Sad news: the Mrs. that used to run the front of the house passed away. Now the owner and chef's kids are running the show out on the floor. One little step-sister was there at lunch too. The other kid must be in kindergarten now. Good news: I forgot how good the pho can be here. I must have been there on an off day before. That dude sure knows how to simmer his stock. The thin sliced beef was so good. Lots of herbs. On my recent pho tour this is my 2nd favorite. Fusion Grill out in Meridian is numero uno.

This cozy spot in Center City offers some tasty Thai food at reasonable prices. The appetizers, like the spring rolls, can appear tiny when looked at. Probably because they are. The entrees, at lunch, at least, are not particularly large, but are a good size to fill you up but not stuff you. And more importantly, they are yummy. At least my chicken curry was. It was so good I wanted to lick the plate clean. The chicken meat had a good taste and texture, too. And there are many more entrees to try on the menu. Service was friendly and attentive, with a server never letting a water glass sit empty on the table.

Not your average Mexican restaurant-with some unique menu options, La Mulita provides you with a fun, "hole in the wall" type experience. Great beer options as well, which is always a plus! And the service was wonderful, attentive, knowledgeable and very personable.

i really dislike giving bad reviews and i'm quite surprised this place has such high ones at that. i rarely ever say that i don't enjoy a meal however this thai joint really disappointed me. the service was excellent, but i've honestly never had such bad pad thai in my entire life. maybe it was the day that i went? or perhaps the chef changed... i have no idea. but because of the high reviews i've decided to drop by and give it another try when i'm in the area.

I am so glad that Apollo Beach finally has a quality quick service restaurant. The food was very tasty. We ordered the veg platter, grilled platter, schwarma and spinach pie. Everything was hot and delicious. The falafels were freshly made not frozen.One of the best we have ever had. We will most certainly visit them often. If you live in the area please try them, you will not be disappointed.
I love this place. My dosas always meet my expectations. Their biryani is mouth melting. I eat here twice a week and I have not been disappointed yet.
This place was pretty good - I liked the spring rolls. The mango salad was much spicier than expected though - so watch out!

I was so disappointed by this place. I trusted the yelp ranking and we went out of our way to stop here to meet some friends on our way through Indy. No one liked their meal and the buffet was quite sad. Almost everything was gone and they never filled it back up and it was only 1pm! The rice was mushy and lukewarm. To top it off the bathrooms were in bad condition! I don't understand how this ranking is so high and would never recommend it to anyone.

Ordered by phone for pick up, staff were very friendly and courteous. There was a little delay, but they were very apologetic and made sure we were comfortable- offered us chairs and brought us water while we waited. Food was delicious, I rarely enjoy any Asian takeout, but this was probably the best take out I've had. Roti with curry appetizer was delicious!! Mango salad was so refreshing! Entres were excellent as well. Great place to try a different twist to Asian take out. Highly recommend.
I love this place is so Yummy I always make sure I stop by when I'm in the side the waitress is very friendly It's is a good wait because the food is fresh and it's not Premade

I love this place. My favorite dish is the grilled mahi with the cilantro jalapeño hummus and pita chips. It's incredibly flavorful and light, great for lunch. I strayed once and got their variety type plate with hummus, tabouleh, dolmas and some other stuff I can't remember. I was underwhelmed by that dish but continue to return for the mahi. The staff is very friendly as well. The female bartenders tend to be more chatty with the men but I guess that's just nature. Either way I really enjoy this place. My only qualm about this place is that it smells like sewage out front sometimes. I try not to hold it against them because that's an underground city issue that's tough to get fixed but it's a little bit of a turnoff.

In my younger, more reckless days, I used to drive a 198X (substitute the rational number of your choice for X) Mitsubishi Galant around. The windshield was so cracked that everything you saw through it looked like it was transpiring in a basement indie rock venue's bathroom mirror, it was entirely done up in hideous blue mouse fur, and the transmission had suffered such horrible travails in a previous life that when you attempted to downshift it sounded like an opera singer attempting to eat a live chicken. Something was always going wrong with that car, and my dad was always wrapping duct tape around some unidentifiable piece of the engine to keep it rolling with the punches. But, you know what? It was a great car. It got mileage better than any car I've owned since, it always started (sometimes with a little coaxing) and it had one of those plastic hula dancers on the dashboard whose mesmerizing hip-shaking more than once bore my mind off in dreams of tropical utopias whilst I steered the car into a cottonwood tree. Queen of Sheba is a bit like this--something always goes wrong. The injera is too cold, the doro wat has unexpected bone fragments emerging to lacerate your gums, the iced tea you ordered is actually hot tea or iced coffee or Diet Sprite or something, and at some point during the meal you're apt to hold up a dripping fragment of one of the sides and say "what is this? seriously, what is it?" If you demand your dining experience to be utterly identical each time, this is not the place for you. Might I suggest Cracker Barrel instead, where the biscuits are as round and normalized as the top of a Pringle's can? But the food is tasty. I get the same problem here as at virtually every other ethnic restaurant in the history of ethnic restaurants--to wit, the fact that they won't make anything spicy enough--but everything has the hallmarks of care and attention put into its preparation. Good injera (though always weirdly cold--not sure why), good lentils, good meat dishes, an excellent mushroom dish of some sort, etc. The Wat dishes are maybe the best--I would put them above the Tibs. All of the sides are good. Is it the best Ethiopian food I've ever had? Well, no, but that Galant wasn't the best car I've ever driven, either. And it stands alone as Tampa's Ethiopian offering. So either look into a really really fancy Zipcar or get yourself down to Queen of Sheba.

Cute location, cozy environment - doesn't have the usual Thai feel, but solid food. I've been here on two occasions. The first time, I already had dinner, so I tried their Thai iced tea and mango sticky rice dessert. Taste was as expected = good. Second time, I got the pad thai (I am so adventurous I know...), and again, it was solid. Portions were decently large, and I couldn't finish my portion. If you have a small appetite, you could probably split it into two meals. If you like your food spicy, you can ask for extra chili sauce on the side, and they bring you this fresh made chili sauce! I didn't try any, but it looked really good!

Not impressed. (Let me first say that I love Greek food and sometimes cook Greek food at home. No, I'm not Greek, but I feel like I know a thing or two about the cuisine. Opa!) Went here on a Saturday night and was surprised that it wasn't crowded. Was it a sign of the economy or the quality of the restaurant? The saganaki had the look and texture of fried mozzarella sticks. (When, I believe it should be more grilled than deep fried.) The cut-up vegetables on the plate (onions, tomatoes, cucumbers) seemed a little dried out. I ordered the gyro from the dinner menu and was confused to see a pile of meat with french fries --- that's it. Oh, sorry, a little tub of tzaziki. I asked about a pita. Was informed it was 75 cents extra. Um, isn't a gyro a pita sandwich? Oh, and for $15, I expected something more than meat and potatoes on a plate. The meat and the french fries seemed overly greasy, as I had quite bad indigestion later that night. My dinner companion had a vegetarian dish that was "OK" but this person also made the comment that it, too, seemed greasy. The servers were all pleasant and quick with water refills. The decor is cute and we joked with the waitress that we had a view of the Aegean from our table, based on how the wall was painted. I really hate to give them a bad review, as I really wanted to like this place. I've had gyros a million times better from little hole in the wall places for a fraction of the cost. I don't understand the high premium on pitas. I understand wheat prices have gone up, but that's kind of a staple of the cuisine. I could possibly be persuaded to go again, to be proven wrong, but for now my gastrointestinal system needs to cleanse.

This place has the best Thai food I ever had. The food is very authentic and flavorful. I tried many Thai restaurants but nothing like this one. It tastes like nice home cooked food. I love the Coconut custard here. I have never tried something like that before. Overall its a very good restaurant to go to for thai food. Love it!

We arrived not long after they opened and were seated right away. The water was never low and the bread was delicious. The calamari tasted like buffalo chicken but was still good. I had the pasticho (sp?) which was one of the best dishes I've ever had. My friend had a gyro which was good. The food was all great but toward the end our server got really snappy. Not sure why seeing as by the time we left there was only one other table. The food and experience was good overall. I will definitely go back.

Great new restaurant on the Northwest side of Tucson! Very elegant interior. I felt very under dresses walking in in cargo shorts and a button up shirt but receptionist said I was dressed fine. The food and service was good. The deserts were very tasty. Large selection of Persian food and the flat bread with onions, cilantro, basil and butter was awesome! I could have made a meal out of that alone. Definitely worth your tine to stop by and try out this new restaurant!

I have to strongly DISAGREE with the last few negative reviews of PF Changs. I think the food is FABULOUS. The Mongolian Beef, Hot Fish and Garlic noodles are SUBLIME and the Banana Eggrolls with Coconut and pineapple ice cream? Well let's just say that dish would included in my last meal ( along with roasted Veal Bones- 'cause I am a marrow freak). Service can be slow?? then don't go to the restaurant on a Friday or Saturday night when you know it's going to be packed. It is still crowded every night but go on a Tuesday or Wednesday. The decor is very nice- upscale. The one negative about the restaurant is the horrible music they play- like bad acid house music where all I hear is the booming mixed with the high volume noise of the restaurant. They need to either A) Play classical , new age music or B) nothing at all and possible re-vamp the restaurant since it is VERY noisy. By the way the appetizers are also excellent . Also the prices are much cheaper than Sang Kee Asian Bistro in Wynnewood, PA. For example- a noodle dish at Sang Kee is $10 versus the garlic noodles at PF Changs which is $6. We ate there ( 3 people)- had 3 appetizers, 3 main dishes, 4 drinks- 2-alcoholic and 2 non-alcoholic, a pot of tea and dessert and the bill was $90. So to sum it up- Great food- Very noisy- Crowded so go at an off -peak time. Cheaper than the upscale Chinese restaurants on the Mainline. Take my advice and order the dishes I mentioned.

My husband and me have yet to make it to the lunch buffet. I have read some reviews that said the service was not good for supper. That has not bee the case twice now. We love the service, prices, authentic food, and clean restaurant. What a treat to eat here.
This place is great! The food was awesome, the waiter was fabulous and the view is wonderful. I'll be back many times.

I am only giving it as much as 3 stars for the food. If you are willing to wait for it, the chicken is deliciously seasoned and grilled. The black beans were tasty and, I don't usually care for it, the fried sweet plantains were the best I ever had! I can't say anything about the rest of the food, but I had no problems with what I got. Now, on to the rest of my visit. The place was filthy. I can only imagine that they had a very busy lunch rush. Not one table was clean; I had to ask for someone to clean a table off for us. He was friendly, they all were, but he left a bottle of cleaning solution on the floor by our table when he accidentally knocked it off. The salsa bar looked...disgusting. I wasn't willing to get any closer to find out what was there. The floor was littered with napkins and food debris. They were out of some key foods too, like the red beans. So we could only try the black. Their soda fountain was out of at least two flavors, but I was happy with a coke. I honestly felt like they just lacked direction on how to keep things running in an orderly manner and the staff didn't seem to know how their job affected others. Things could be fixed with the right management, but not quite right yet. So if you're willing to wait and possibly have a coupon like we did, GET IT TO GO!

Best Thaï food I've ever had, Nelly is a amazing woman! You are treated like family here. I've tried just about everything on the menu! And I've not had a bad dish yet! The Pad Khing is my all time favorite!

We visited this establishment on a Friday around 7 pm. There were about 5 other tables occupied. We started our meal with the cashew naan, it was delicious! We then ordered an eggplant and chicken dish that comes with rice. Both were very good. The rice has great flavor on its own. You can customize the heat level for every dish. We ordered the rice pudding for dessert. It was creamy and better than the average rice pudding. I typically don't like rice pudding but this one was thicker than I have had in the past. The staff was very friendly and attentive. I feel like the decor could use some help though. The seat to our booth was ripped which isn't particularly attractive. We will definitely come back for more Indian food.

My gf and I love this place. It's a hole in the wall with amazing food! The gentlemen that run this place are fantastic and extremely friendly. I could eat here breakfast lunch and dinner! I will be supporting them on a weekly basis.
I can't tell you anything about the food but the Pumpkin Kiss drink is just awesome. I'd suggest coming in and ordering one before fall is over. It's a pumpkin beer with a special twist. Awesome.
Need a new Local Pho place to go to?! This is it! Food is delishhhh!!! Price is in everyone's budget!! Everything tastes sooo fresh and made to order! Great spot!

Order wrong after asking several times if my order was correct. Very poor customer service, Folks act is if they are doing me a favor. When I called to complain folks asking for a ticket number, I never received a ticket number, For sure I will not be back too many other options.

Indianapolis has it's fair share of Indian restaurants (not that I'm complaining). India Cafe is going the extra mile. Both the Baingan Bahar and Chicken Vindaloo were very good. In addition we got the spicy chicken appetizer. Very good as well...well worth experiencing the heat of the chili. The staff was very nice and tended to our needs very well. Also, the plates the food was served on were beautiful. Our host said they were imported from India. You have to love attention to detail.

I still find it strange that I somehow got an ROTD for my last review because I wasn't the biggest fan. However, I decided to give this place another chance because I was craving a little something reminiscent of home and am so glad I did! This second time around was MUCH better. I actually ordered two sandwiches, one for lunch and one for dinner, and was pretty happy with both. While nothing is going to compare to home, this satisfied my Vietnamese sandwich (YES, I called it a sandwich and not a hoagie) craving. I got #2 (Dac biet) and the #4 (Xiu Mai). Everything about both sandwiches were much improved! The baguette was much better this time (last time it was stale). There was more meat/pate and condiments as well. My only complaint, I still wish the pickled carrots/daikon was more thick (instead of shavings) and more sour. I'll be coming back :)

I hate to pile on but I have to be honest. The service, food and alcoholic drinks were very bad. Until management take their food and service seriously; I would recommend that you save yourself from this establishment and not spend a dime.

I stopped in for lunch yesterday and had a large #2 (brisket pho) and a Vietnamese-style iced coffee. Service was efficient, and the price seemed good at first: $7.45 for a large pho and $2.95 for the coffee. Pho has three basic components: the broth, the noodles, and the meat. The pho I had at Pho King was mediocre on all counts. The soup had generous amounts of lean, tight-grained brisket, but I was disappointed to discover that it had a leftover taste, as if it had been cooked two or three days prior and refrigerated. Bleh. The rice stick noodles were overcooked. They broke apart as I tried to pick them up with my chopsticks. The broth was weak; I had to add salt to it, and I've never had to do that at other pho restaurants! I know when pho broth is good when I want to keep eating it even after the meat and noodles are gone. I had no such desire at Pho King. The coffee was disappointing as well. It certainly tasted good, but the quantity served was remarkably small for what they were charging. I won't be going back to Pho King. For a good bowl of pho, I recommend Pho Binh off Stony Plain Road.

I frequently visit this restaurant and highly recommend it. It's tucked away off the street and looks old from the exterior but the staff is very friendly and the food is fantastic. The Pad See Ew and the Pineapple Fried Rice are excellent.

I love the food at other Zoës, but the Wayne restaurant keeps getting the order wrong, and the quality had gone down a lot! Pick up order was prepared too early and was cold. Also, the food is inconsistent. The last time we ordered the food was SWIMMING in oil. The Android app is useless.

Tandoor restaurant is one of my favorite indian restaurant! I love the food specially the chicken tika masala and fresh naan that is served on the buffet. Also i always eat kosher and halal which all of there food is which is a huge plus point for me. The wait staff is amazing! This is a go to lunch everyday place for me from now on. They also give 10% student discount too...it cant get any better..:)

I'm in town visiting family and we decide to try a new place, it's not much to look at from the outside... But looks can be deceiving. Inside is clean, the food is well priced... I travel to India on business ...so I can be a bit snobby on my Tandoori and Saag.... This place is great, fantastic and a treat!!!! The Chicken Dosas were heaven and gluten free....... U must have warm rice pudding for dessert........

For what it is, it's incredibly expensive. The chicken coating was nice and crispy (not greasy), but the chicken itself was dry. And overall it was very bland. The desserts sound amazing but really don't live up to it. My order (via UberEats) was also stone cold. Better off at KFC.

My gut instinct is to say that this place is pretty decent, sitting somewhere between 3 and 4 stars. I think the management's changed recently, based on the name change (formerly Hangook Kwon) and also some changes to the food. The food seems to have improved since before the change. Food overall seems better prepared. For lack of a better term at this time, it seems like it is more "fresh" and the flavors are cleaner and more distinct. They offer a pretty good variety on the menu of the traditional Korean fare. Lunch prices are pretty decent. Portions are nicely sized. All in all, not the best Korean I've had, but maybe one of the better ones I found in St. Louis. I'd say try it at least once.
Would recommend to try for a buffet: OK Went for buffet: $12.50 Vegetarian: good variety and tasty Non- veg: goat curry, 2 chicken varieties Desert: ok

Pho is alright. First pho place I've been to where green onions aren't in the pho. It came out totally white, without veggies. Maybe they forgot? Dunno.... spring rolls didn't have mint, just lettuce and meat.

It's a good spot for lunch when you don't want to wait for a table or service, meaning it's not crowded. Food is good quality and price reflects this. The salmon croissant sandwich is good, could use a little more sauce so the croissant doesn't seem so dry. Beer and wine is good, service is good overall (I never like it when a server says "it's all good here" or worse "gee I've never tried either of those" but overall it was a good experience each of the three times I've had lunch here. My friend has a burger every time he goes here so that says something about the burgers! They put fried egg on their burger, which I understand lots of people like. Not my thing but there are other choices for picky eaters. I've heard their brunch is good but I personally haven't tried it yet. Maybe this weekend?

Quite a simple place in a strip mall. Had dinner on a Friday night, and was pleasantly surprised to see a revised layout and decor. Not exactly to my tastes, but it is good that the owners are investing in the business. Pleasant greeting by a friendly woman with an ipad, and a decent enough table with ample room (ill mannered that I am, I often find my elbows on the table!). She opened the bottle of wine we had brought (The place is BYOB) quite competently, and the table was well set up (appropriate wine glasses, wine chiller bucket, water, tableware etc.). The orders were taken on the ipad ,and she showed us pictures of the food to make sure that is what we wanted. The obligatory choice of spice level (mild, medium, hot) was also captured in the order, and another server brought us a nice complementary tray with assorted pappad and chutneys (yummy). The chicken kababs we ordered came in short order and they were pretty good, as was the lamb vindaloo, naan and rice. Not the best I've eaten, but good enough that I will return. A decent ras malai for dessert wound up our meal. To sum up, service was excellent, food was acceptable, and overall, a decent experience. I will definitely be back.

Usually do takeout as I work closeby so its a good option when being too lazy to cook. Very friendly owners who usually offer samples if your food is not ready. I do not eat seafood so I tend to stick with the Charcoal Platters which are always spot on. Only negitive is I think the prices are a little high however you can always depend on a quality meal.

This is the worse service place! When you walk in you get seated wherever you want. But it's never a warm welcoming greet. They will come get your drink and food order, the food comes out and that's about it. You won't get a refill or service asking us if we need anything else. Food portion looks smaller then what it used to be. You basically have to wave them down for everything you need or get up and get it yourself. Food is mediocre. I will go else where. This must be like the 3rd new owners and their service sucks!

I tried this restaurant and I have to say it didn't impress me. Granted I didn't dine in and maybe that's the issue. I called in a pick order. Service was good, check out was quick and staff was nice. I got it home and it was just blah. Nothing special about it. I tried the Chicken lemon soup vegetable fried rice and beef salad. The price was a little more than what used to. I'm not used to paying 29 bucks. I will try again and perhaps dine in next time, to see if I get same results. Every restaurant deserves another chance....right? Sincerely Kat "Will travel for food"
The owner was a jokster. Funny gentleman. Made for a more enjoyable experience. Interior is simple but familiar. Food was very good. Stop by if you're looking for solid Indian food.

Really tiny gem in Media, now expanded coverage in Drexel Hill. I have been visiting this place since it opened. Our boys *only* have their Chicken Butter Masala. Undoubtedly the very best there is. Other items on their menu is good, but for some reason, the CBM is spectacular. Be reminded that it is a BYO. There is a PA wine store about 2-3 blocks down on Main Street. Their choice of [Hindi] words to describe their menu is quite cute/amusing. For instance "Shuruvat" which literally means the "start" or begining (as in an inning) for the Appetizer menu, "Samunder se" meaning from the sea! As for comments about the wait staff, while I whole heartedly agree with previous Yelpers, one must give them a little leeway as it is pretty typical (I personally think it is cultural, but happy to be corrected by fellow Yelpers). Why did it take me so long to write this review? Well just happened to do a pick up and realized I had not put in my good word ;-))

Stopped at Smiley's to grab lunch after buying books next door. No frills, delicious gyros. Since I just got back from Greece last week I had high standards...but the friendly service, and outstanding food was a great surprise. Definitely recommend!

I was excited for this addition to the dining options in the Providence area. The first thing you may notice when you go here is that the interior atmosphere is pleasantly sleek/modern and the host will greet you immediately. Everything on the menu can be ordered in three spice levels, appealing to a wide array of taste buds: mild, medium, or hot. So don't be afraid! The menu is standard Indian fare with some upgrades and fancy presentations. Both times I've been, my meal has been wonderful and served quickly. My friend ordered the goat dish and it had a lot of bones in it. He ate around it and said it was delicious but the bones were unexpected. The service is very friendly and helpful and you'll never have to ask for a refill. I will definitely be going back!

Little on the pricey side but food was excellent. The beef empanadas, ropa vieja y pernil were awesome; along with the tres leches dessert. Plenty of parking, no wait on Friday night, great service... We will be back!

After my last visit (where wine was spilled) I got a personal call from the chef, Joe B, apologizing and offering to pay my cleaning bill and to come back for another meal on him. WOW. No worries about cleaning the sweater but happy to come back for another meal. My friend and I returned this evening and it was great. We had the anti pasta, which as others have said, is delicious. Salad was also done right and not overdressed. My friend had the amazing gnocchi again and I ordered the spaghetti and clams. Simple and delicious with the pasta the right level of al dente. Nutella donuts were incredible. Service was attentive again (no spills!) Chef came out to apologize and ensure we were enjoying ourselves. Very impressed that the chef cares that much about each patron. Will definitely be back!

I've been here many times, but I have only had the beef patties and the jerk chicken. They are both fantastic, so much so that I have thus far neglected all the other menu items when I get there simply because I cannot imagine walking out without a beef patty or jerk chicken. The prices are very fair, and the staff are genuine!

I came in on a Thursday night and has the best customer service!! Van and Jocelyne the two waitresses were working and were very attentive and helpful. I ordered cream cheese wontons and wings which were both very delicious and fresh!

I don't know much about Pho, but since eating here I have gone out of my way to try different Pho restraunts, and this is still my favorite. It is a Owned/Operated by a local couple, and they are very pleasant & friendly! The Pho Portions are pretty big, and always extremely filling! I highly recommend the number 10, the Rare Beef pho, it is my absolute favorite! My wife loves it when I bring home the Spring Rolls, and their Pate Sandwiches. The Sandwiches are different, but wow, are they good! Great Food, Really Good Prices, and quick and friendly service. Family loves it, and I go out of my way to stop by at least ever week or two.

Atmosphere is so cute here! All the food and drinks are phenomenal. I debated between 4 and 5 stars. The first two times I went it was really a wonderful experience. The food was out of this world, it's gorgeous, and the staff was great. It's gotten insanely crowded and harder to get a table which is a bummer. Also when I've called to get tables, they've been surprisingly rude. But that could just be a fluke so I'm giving them a five because honestly every thing on the menu is amazing. Small parking lot (free) across the street. Update: apparently they're building something there now so no more lot.

Once upon a time, I had come to this cafe while visiting a friend. However, I forgot where it was and what it was called. This was a couple years ago. I had been woeful ever since, for every cafe I from then on stumbled across in Edmonton was not this one. Yesterday, before heading back to Calgary, I asked my friend, "Where can I get some delicious vegan food before I take off?" He replied, "Remedy. You have to." And so, I set off to Remedy. And upon walking in, I came to a startling realization... THIS WAS THE CAFE. THIS WAS IT! I was immediately charmed by this shop. It was so beautifully buzzy, and full of people doing their own thing. I had stopped in to grab some food to go, but quickly began to wish I had brought in my laptop to finish from projects for class. I was a little overwhelmed to see a section on the menu board labled VEGAN! I had a hard time deciding, but eventually settled on veggie samosas, one of their notorious chais, and a giantic vegan gluten free gingersnap. I took off with my delicious things and away I went. My good evolutionary theory, was that the best "chai" (the word chai admittedly kind of pisses me off, as it translates directly to tea) I have ever had. Next trip to Edmonton, I am eating here only.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Food was great, service was slooooow, but the people were really nice. I'm giving it 4/5 stars only because my dad asked for very mild curry and his was definitely more of a medium spice. We both agree we'd come here again!

I usually go to the 30th and Market location, but I have been to the University City location as well. 30th and Market usually gives me a larger portion but I got a generous sample of fried fish (really tasty!) at the University City location, so each location has won me over in their own way. I am a huge fan of jerk chicken, and this place comes pretty close to Negril. In a small platter, you get three large chicken drumsticks, cooked until it's falling off the bone. I don't mind that it's not grilled fresh, because the chicken sits in a hot dish of delicious peppery and spicy jerk gravy, so the flavors really penetrate the meat. If you choose rice and beans as one of the two sides in a platter, they'll ladle some extra gravy over the rice and beans. When you reheat the leftovers, the rice and beans will have soaked up that sauce, making it even better than the first time. I also love the collard greens at these trucks, which they drain after piling into the styrofoam container. This prevents the juices from contaminating the other foods, especially if you choose to get other distinct sides like sweet potato. I get the mac and cheese if I'm in the mood for a pick me up, because Gigi and Big R's mac has that thick, starchy, sticks together, made in a huge batch quality, that is so (wonderfully) different from the box variety. Freshness is not my top priority when eating comfort food. As other posters mentioned, the portions are big enough for 2 meals. At University City, a large platter ($9) more than does the trick, at the 30th and Market location, the small ($7) is sufficient. I can't imagine having a better home-cooked meal for less than $5. It's a Philly staple I will definitely miss.
Our go-to spot for pho uptown. Never disappoints. Huge bowl for a reasonable price. Clean.
Such delicious variety of food. Very pleasant service and i will be coming here more often. HIGHLY RECCOMEND THE NAAN BREAD!!! :)

I have to always order the Panang Curry with Beef, love the spiciness. The fresh rolls with shrimp are tasty and their peanut sauce is addictive! I love the tofu and carrots, the basil gives it a nice freshness. I usually end up getting some sort of fried rice and pad Thai, I recommend the sweet sticky rice it's delicious! I've had the yellow and red curry, both are great!

Ok so we are here on a Thursday and every drink we have ordered the female bartender Donna has said they don't have it and have not offered an option and quite honestly have been very rude..... Not happy and may not come back

I love the fresh and generously sized Papaya Salad. The Green Curry with Beef has a good flavor and assortment of vegetables, but is not very big. I like the Pad Thai with Chicken as well, although the chicken can be a little dry. My only complaint is that the free delivery within a limited area seems extremely limited as I live fairly close and yet have been charged the delivery fee a couple times. Double-check your bill before paying!
Love it, great flavors and portions, friendly staff and chill atmosphere. Been here many times and take-out is speedy and hot!
Excellent Greek food and fast. The octopus was succulent and so were the mixed wilted greens. Fresh, fast and yummy. So glad this option is in the neighborhood!

This would be a 3.5 for me. I want so badly to love this place but the food is average, so very average. The flavor profile is...bland. I got the fried papaya dish which I was told was going to come with a spicy sauce. The level of spice was 0 on a scale of 1 to 10. Go here because its unique and the outside is great and the food isn't terrible. But unfortunately its nothing more than that.

This is my second visit. Good food, good drinks, great place to hang out and relax. The guacamole and chips are on the salty side in a good way. The tacos are consistently good; make sure to hit them with the house sauce.

You need to eat here!! THE best Thai food we have ever had. We ordered the vegan pineapple fried rice, pork Thai Legacy Fried rice, & chicken Tom Kah soup. You need to order dessert because their mango sticky rice is SO GOOD. Absolutely loved our waitress and everyone we interacted with. We left feeling like family. Can't wait to eat here again the next time we are in town. They are very kid friendly as well, it was a great experience eating with our baby.

So I was super excited about this place because I've never had Vietnamese food before. I've been wanting to go for a while, and watching an episode of Bizarre Foods is what pushed me over the edge to try some non run-of-the mill common cuisine. The experience started off good. We were promptly seated and began to look through the menu, which is HUGE (I'm talking about 18 pages!) Our waiter came over and we ordered an appetizer to start-the #10 (can't remember the name) which was a pancake like option stuffed with shrimp and other goodies-very awesome and my favorite thing ordered. We told our server we still needed a few more minutes to look through the menu. However, for whatever reason, he did not come back to take our order. When our appetizer arrived, I asked if we could place our order. When the entrees arrived, we were still working on the appetizer. Not the hugest deal but a little annoying. My pork chops were flavorful, yet were very fatty and not that big (I walked away kind of hungry). The vegetables accompanying the entrees and the appetizer tasted a little funky. Unfortunately, we weren't checked on throughout the meal, nor were any plates cleared from our table once our appetizer was gone. Overall, I was not a huge fan of this place. Maybe I just ordered the wrong thing, but the mediocre food coupled with the poor service make for an "I've experienced better" review.
Best Indian food we've had, the samosas are perfect. Service was fast and the servers were very enthusiastic. We even got a free glass of wine!.

We went to Mirna's last week on the advice of friends. The food was outstanding, especially for the price. I had a the Meditteranean appetizer plate, which was huge, fresh and flavorful. The best dolmades I've had in this region! My greek salad was generous and tasty. Hubby had the grouper, which was out of this world delicious, with a complex, rich sauce. The only drawback was their pita bread, which I find dry and flatter than the average. Also, don't expect a private tete-a-tete with your date, since the tables are close together. But even though small, the decor is simple yet elegant. Mirna's is a definite keeper!

This is where I go when I want to reward myself. The staff knows me by name, and I love this! I usually order the TA2 with all chicken. Ethiopian is my favorite food, and I love the warm comfort I feel when eating it. To me, this is the southern comfort style, while Major Restaurant on the far Westside is the less heavy, but equally delicious option. It is hard to pick a favorite, but I love them both for their uniqueness.

I stopped into the Kabob House one day after school thinking it was a take out place. Nope, It's a sit down restaurant / Hooka Bar? We were the only customers at the time. It was very quiet and apparently it's a family owned and operated restaurant so we could hear the kids crying in the kitchen. I didn't let it bother me, but might of been a distraction if I was there for dinner instead of just a snack. The food was great and the owner was very pleasant.

A friend of mine and I tried this place on a whim and were very, very pleased. I've only had their lunch buffet but I'm sure it's indicative of their dinner menu. Great breadth of selections for lunch including all the usual suspects, plus fresh warm bread brought to the table. All the dishes appear and taste fresh and the quality of ingredients is apparent. Lovely decor that is a big step up from many similar places. Ample vegetarian options for the cruelty-free set but meated options as well. I've since been back a half-dozen times with different people and everyone has been delighted every time. if you're in Media you might want to hit up Trader Joe's (http://www.yelp.com/biz/trader-joes-media#hrid:Bn-FNdtsNuHjyRcU1XHLCA) as well and if you liked Shere-E-Punjab, check out Himalayan in Malvern (http://www.yelp.com/biz/himalayan-exotic-indian-cuisine-malvern#hrid:Ah0OAxmaZRNWNDg9JmY_fA) .

I am ashamed to say today was our first time eating here. I've driven by Persis Biryani Indian restaurant twice a day since it opened and never stopped by to eat. Well we did tonight and I have to say it's my new favorite restaurant in Mount Juliet. It was fabulous. I had the Aloo Palak medium spice, my hubby had chicken vindaloo spicy and the kiddos had noodles with chicken fry and fried rice. By the time I got home I was craving more. We will definitely go back again.

I went there yesterday based on the previous reviews, the food was amazing....especially the grilled chicken. But, the best part was the line......the people (who all seemed to be regulars) could not have been nicer. The man in front of me gave me his spot so that I could try and avoid a parking ticket. I should have paid for his lunch! Instead I made a donation to "Emily's Medical Costs and Funeral" on GoFundMe. People of Philly......the best.

I was excited by the reviews for this place because I love Asian fusion, but 8th and Union fell short of my expectations. The poke was artfully presented and tasty, though the plaintain chips it was topped with were barely crunchy. The pork belly sliders were okay - unlike the traditional burger buns you might expect, they put these little morsels in puffy bao buns. Unfortunately, I wish that the sauce had more kick to it (it was rather bland and milky) and that the pork belly had some crisp. I split the pad thai as a main with my boyfriend on our waitress' recommendation, and it was quite a substantial portion. However, I've had great pad thai, and this is not it. The noodles were soggy and sticky and the chicken (we got both chicken and shrimp) was overcooked and dry. For the quality of food we received, this place was pretty overpriced as we ended up paying over $40 for one main and two small dishes. If there's no other place nearby to get my fill of something on the menu (pho, pad thai, banh mi, etc.) then I would come here. Otherwise, I don't think it's worth it.

Thai Place is "Aroy Mak"! Thai food is incredibly difficult to get right in Pennsylvania because of the shortage of the same ingredients, so what you end up with is a really 'typical' Americanized version of Thai food in most restaurants here. Thai Place carries these staples for sure, BUT they do an amazing job at it! Which is why, I give it 5 stars. You just can't find Thai food around here that's this good at these prices. I have been eating homemade Thai food since I was a baby, and I know how difficult it is to get right. I even cook some of my mom's dishes now and then, but when I don't feel like cooking, I come here. Most Thai restaurants around the area can't get their Curries right, and I walk away wishing I ate at Thai Place instead. Thai Place does an excellent job. My favorite dishes are: Gang Pa (country Curry), Papaya Salad, Por Pia (Spring Rolls), and I LOVE Pad Wood Sen. Also, as a vegetarian, I am able to find plenty of options which offer mock dock, or mock chicken in it. We love coming here, and Eddie and Apple are fantastic welcoming owners who know us by name. The owners are real Thai people, and they do a fantastic job with the decor and ambiance of their restaurant. If you want straight up Thai food, this is where you go! Also, they can make food extra spicy if you request it, but if you can't handle the spice make sure you tell someone. Thai food has a natural kick to it.

Message to owners : Worst restaurant experience ever ! The owners or owners family had atleast 4 kids running all over the restaurant screaming their heads off continuously. You would think they would have controlled the situation considering they had customers , but nope they didn't do anything until I said I want the food to go and that's when they left . They never apologized or nothing so disrespectful! What a way to show new customers that you appreciate them ! The place is lame but the food is okay not bad at all. I suggest taking the food Togo, because the ambiance is depressing.

I happened to visit this resturants last week and I finally got to taste authentic south indian and north indian food. I happened to meet the chef, who happened to be from south india. This place is a must try for Indians and Americans

Don't be fooled by the name. The Shishkabob House offers a full menu of Mediterranean food from Shwarma to Baklava...plus the most delicious Hummus you ever tasted. This place is a relatively undiscovered food treasure.

Loved the food and the staff. We've eaten Ethiopian food before, but they explain what it is, how it's made and overall a friendly environment. We are visiting but we'd eat here often if we were ever stationed here. I'm leaving very full.

This was a great little Middle Eastern stop. I love that there is a market attached to the restraunt so I can buy my tahini and extras after I get my delicious falafel and fresh made bread. I really enjoyed the seasoned rice, the grilled vegetables and even the hot tea was aromatic and flavorful. I need my Middle Eastern foodie fixes and I'm extremely judgemental if it doesn't taste authentic. I loved every taste and bite in this very tiny but cozy atmosphere. This will be a place I'm going to frequent for lunch and for my market needs!

Reservations are accepted, but not required. We ate outside on the patio on Friday around 6:30 and were able to be seated right away. I felt semi-underdressed wearing jeans and a t-shirt, so maybe step up your game a bit when you come here for dinner. Ordered 4 small plates for 2 people to share. Perfect amount for us! Server was awesome- she brought out 2 plates first and then brought out the next 2 dishes once we were done. Great spacing it out so our table wouldn't be crowded. Everything is covered in dill- everything. Not just a little dill, but a lot. So keep that in mind if you hate dill (as I do) to just ask for less, or ask for it on the side, or not at all. There are plenty of other fresh herbs that also top each dish, they didn't need the abundance of dill. -King of Kings Hummus ($8) is served with both pita points and baguette slices. The portion is huge for 2 people and we did have leftover bread when the hummus was gone. Better than what you buy in the store, but not super fancy. Pass on this one and get something outside of the box instead. -Zucchini Carpaccio ($12) was my favorite dish! Served very thinly sliced, wrapped in little cone shapes, and with several sliced of preserved lemons. It's really the lemons that make this dish. Make sure you have a bite of lemon with each bite to really get the best experience. I need to learn how to make this at home- it was so good! -Mushroom flatbread ($14) was served hot and with fresh veggies and herbs. I would get again. -Beet salad ($12) was my least favorite. I am normally a big big fan of beets, but this salad was not my cup of tea. It was served with ricotta and not goat cheese as I traditionally get, so that alone made the dish less creamy and salty than I would have liked.

This restaurant opened up recently in the last year and thankfully serves a variety of banh mi sandwiches in addition to pho, vermicelli, and rice plates.+1 star for variety. Santa Barbara just doesn't have a good selection of Vietnamese restaurants so I was glad when Phamous Cafe opened up. We've enjoyed their Grilled Pork Banh Mi, Grilled Chicken Banh Mi, and Pork Cake Banh Mi (my favorite). I always request for more veggie toppings of the pickled daikon and carrots; this adds more flavor to the sandwiches. +1 for banh mi alone. The baguettes are good, but not your French warm-style bread you'd expect, but it's still good. For Santa Barbara, their pho noodle soup is definitely better than the Saigon Noodle next to KMart, but not better than ones served up by Noodle City. We usually go with Rare Beef Pho and Meatball Pho +1 star for pho noodle soup. Their staff is friendly and attentive. The food comes out pretty quick. + 1 star. I'd stay from ordering appetizers, generally their spring rolls and eggs rolls. They're a bit pricy, not the best-freshly made, especially the spring rolls with an imbalance of lettuce to rice noodles. Another thing is that they close on Tuesdays, and I keep forgetting it every time I go out there on a Tuesday.
Fantastic food, super friendly service...will go back in a heart beat. Can absolutely recommend the tulip dumplings and mango curry

I've been only once, but I was really impressed. I got the lamb shank plate, and my date got the mousaka, both from the "house specialties" section. My date grew up eating mousaka and enjoyed hers, but said it wasn't her best. My lamb shank was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. It was very flavorful, pretty spicy, but just perfect. And there was so much on the plate that I spent my next day really looking forward to my leftovers. I will be back. Oh, and a full bar and a workable beer selection. It matters.

Chaat is awesome, also ordered a avocado Christine chaat for appetizer, so Yum. And my tummy feels good after having these, which is usually not happen after eating outside. The owner is really nice, definitely will come back and try others again.

Seasons is located on the corner of a small plaza in St. Pete, so it can be hard to spot! Although the restaurant isn't large, there's plenty of seating and a small cafe area with snacks and other goods. I went with two friends, but we decided to order and take out because of a time crunch. We were very impressed with the prices; a banh mi costs around $4. I ordered a roast pork banh mi, which had the perfect amount of pork in vegetables on a toasty bun! Even though they had an arrangement of desserts, we just ordered a variety or bubble teas. I ordered the Thai tea with boba, which had a nice combination of tea and milk. It wasn't the best bubble tea, but I would still order it again! Their boba wasn't too mushy, and was very chewy, which is the best consistency. I was a little disappointed at the speed of Seasons, since their food is made to order. However, we waited about twenty minutes for three banh mi and two bubble teas. Despite this, the taste and cost makes the taste worth the wait!

Tagine is a fantastic experience all around. The food is amazing and the staff knows the details of every dish and which one to recommend for each person. The food was so fast coming out, there was barely any waiting time. Since it is a three or four-course meal, the different options come out one at a time. The soup and salads come out quickly, and by the time you're done with them the next course is brought out. I would recommend the lamb tagine, since it is brought out in a traditional tagine, a beautiful clay bowl that keeps the sauce bubbling and the meat tender. I could not recommend this place enough, a hot spot in Media which is saying a lot with all the amazing competition!

I went to jamaica in january so last week i decided to check out the jerk hut to recreate my adventures there. I phoned in an order for jerk chicken and a cohort ordered curry chicken. Both were delicious. The jerk was better than most i had in jamaica and it brought me back (it's a shame the Red Stripe isn't as fresh in PA). The chicken was cooked just right and had just the right amount of sweetness and spice. My only complaint is that i could have gone for more cabbage in my platter, but i can understand them wanting to get me to buy a side order. i can't fault them for trying to make more $. Also, i don't know if they still have it but when i went there a few years ago they had real heavy duty homemade ginger beer. i totally recommend this! it's like nothing i've had before or since.

Delicious!! This was my first time here and I'll definitely be going back in the near future! I got the spicy drunken noodles (hot) with chicken. It was pretty damn spicy and very delicious. Huge portion. Also got the steamed pork pot stickers. Best I've ever had. The lady at the front who took our order was nice and funny.

Literally the worst food I've had in IV the Gyros tasted like old Boloney, the French fries tasted not like French fries and the pita bread was just no good. I'd say 1/10 I'd much prefer Taco Bell to this place I just ate here couldn't even finish my plate and I'm feeling sick now probably food poisoning.
Best Indian food I've ever eaten. Very nice atmosphere and super friendly waiters. Really one of the best dining experiences. The food was so good! We had the Chicken Tikka Masala and Lamb Korma.

Stephani is the friendliest person that I have ever met at a drive-thru window. I knew she was friendly when she first started to talk. Every drive-thru should have a sweet friendly person like Stephani.

Owner needs a lesson in common sense. He/she needs to decide whether or not he/she wants to keep charging 2 bucks for about 6-8 oz of soda (literally). Not kidding. This is what they charge for a small soda (mostly ice), with no refills. Except when they do give out refills. Unless you're there on whatever day they decide to charge an extra dollar for a refill. Really, it's that inconsistent. The menu does not state "no refills"...? Not sure if they can't make up their mind or just recently decided that 3 bucks is the new going rate in west Boise for 16 oz of soda. Outside of their soda prices being higher than just about anywhere else in the world, Baguette Deli is decent. It's a basic hole in the wall sandwich shop with moderate cleanliness and less than moderate friendliness and personality. The only thing worth going there for is their banh mi. Everything else they have is better somewhere else like Pho Nouveau or Pho Tam. Their banh mi is pretty decent. Like everyone else says-the BBQ pork is the best item on the menu.

Was driving downtown and came across T.H.I.S Place, which I'm sad to report has closed. I hadn't been there in a while, but I always liked coming to T.H.I.S Place while I was studying at MacEwan. It was a simple little coffee shop that had expanded to a nice little lunch spot. The tea and coffee were good, and the staff were friendly. R.I.P T.H.I.S Place. Your coconut popsicles were amazing and I'll never forget your delicious teas and that spicy hot chocolate. For those looking check out Lan's Asian Grill up by Kingsway. The same owners of Lan's owned this place and if you're looking for some awesome Thai food it's a good spot.

The atmosphere is an absolute embarrassment. It's something straight out of the TV show Golden Girls. The food however is excellent. Order delivery or takeout so you're not subjected to the horrible time warp. PS, the entrance is actually on Park Ave. It's nearly impossible to find via 70.

My group and I stumbled upon this place when we were desperately trying to find a place to eat before crossing over to the Eastern Penitentiary for our haunted journey through the abandoned prison. Everything else nearby was either closed or too crowded, or was no longer serving food. If you ask me what types of cuisines I like, I probably would not mention Greek, which was why I was not too excited to come here for dinner. But we were all starving and out in the cold and just needed a place that can feed us as we waited. I know very little of Greek cuisine and I know for sure that they are famous for their gyros. I thought I'd just pick that but that night, we were told that they were not serving gyros. I was worried that I would not have any other interesting options to choose from. With the hunger and very little energy I had left, I just trusted my sister to pick the dish and my friend to pick the appetizers. We were all gonna share anyway. To start, we had the combination of hot appetizers that included fried calamari, mussels in red wine, and grilled octopus. Very good choice! No crumbs were left behind. The grilled octopus was tender and marinated humbly in some oil... For our main courses, we had the meatballs with rice, roasted potatoes, and grilled veggies. Originally, my friend wanted something from the vegetarian menu but our waiter told us almost everything vegetarian was out that night. Must be that good eh. So he recommended the meatballs. My sister and I ordered the Grilled Skewered Chicken Breast served with rice, roasted potatoes and mixed veggies or french fries and mixed veggies. The meatballs were nice and soft, but I was not too crazy with the sauce that it came with. I LOVE their grilled chicken breast skewers. So tender and juicy! The french fries were unlike others that I have ever tried before. They were flat like chips and well-seasoned. It helped that we were all starving. We devoured and savored every bite and did not leave anything behind. I'm a sauce girl but I did not even need sauce on my chicken! That says a lot! Where the waiter promised a delicious meal, Zorba's delivered it. If I am around the area again, I would not hesitate to come back. =)

Wonderful Thai food. There were 8 of us dining here. All of us with the exception of our friend Stan had the special combination. The Chicken Tom Yum Soup was exceptional. The best I have ever tasted, and I love Thai food, so know what good Thai is... We also had the Pad Thai, and the Pineapple Fried Rice. Both superb with a 5 star rating. The beer drinkers in the group liked that the beer came with the special. Service was really good, and attentive. Yes, it is GOOD......

Amazing authentic cuisine, and it's in Mount Juliet. The chicken tikka masala is very flavorful, and with naan there's no need for a fork. Lunch menu is very affordable but limited, however, they will make something off the dinner menu if you ask. It's as good as any restaurant in Nashville, and better than most.

This place is as good as it gets. My fourth time and it was probably better than ever. Don't worry about what to order it's all fantastic - the specials are wonderful, last night they sent over some pasta to taste and some dessert. I've only gone during the week. Service is unrushed and efficient. Room is plain but you'll be focussed on the food. BYOB. I wouldn't try without a reservation but getting one during the week hasn't been an issue.

Went there couple of times. They serve fusion foods. Tried short rib taco, chicken taco and tilapia burrito. Short rib taco is delicious, lots of colors and flavors. Chicken taco: average, tilapia burrito is kindda complicated. If you call it a wrap, it's good but if burrito then bad. They will always have lines because of the location and hype. Their ratings are more hyped based than food. If you like to try different foods in different locations then you will understand what I meant. Btw, Thai tea was good.
I come here for all my Asian grocery shopping! The owner Moon is super friendly! I enjoy the chicken & duck pho here. Nice to have a place like this available in Manayunk!

Good drinks. The service is a bit bizarre. The staff seems tone deaf on understanding customers personal space. They would yell across to each other about work related stuff to the point where you struggled to have a conversation. At one point, this blonde server was talking so loudly to another server my friend put her hands over her ears. It was surreal. I've never encountered anyone so jacked up waiting on us ever. We watched her take our 4 empty drink glasses in her arm, then go wait on other tables with dirty glasses still in her arm. Lol. Huh? At one point she walked up to the drink fruit tray and stated eating the cherries right out of the tray, then grabbed two straws for drinks but proceeded to cough into her hand still holding the straws and then right into the glasses. We pulled our straws out and tossed them on the table. There were only about 10 folks there but we were exhausted watching her tear through the place like she drank a VAT of Red Bull. Probably won't go back. Yeah...

Went to Sam's Beach Bar for lunch Tuesday 10/3/17. It was a very windy day but warm so we sat on the deck. Our server was very nice & patient with us. When our food was delivered, we asked to be moved. Our server didn't mind at all & allowed us to pick the table. Our food was great & we had generous portions! The atmosphere is great. Will visit again. I loved being by the water but it was just too windy. My only complaint was they want to make their already generous portions seem bigger by serving your food on very small plates! Our food was literally falling off & we didn't want to eat it off of a dirty pic-nic table. The bathrooms were absolutely filthy!!!!!!
The duck (any of the several) is my favorite. Good service, good soups good curries. Have never been let down. It's our 1st choice for Thai.
Best Thai food I've ever had, but they got a new waitress.....she does not relay orders correctly. Other than her it's a great place.

Vietnamese food is usually the healthy choice for Asian food because it is not fried in a wok with lots of oil. This place has one of the best Pho and the sandwiches are phenomenal. Also of note is that behind the scenes in the kitchen they have older ladies preparing the food that know what they are doing. So you're probably getting some of granny's special fish sauce in your Pho. This is another nice addition to Indys International Marketplace scene.

Average meal. I ordered the Sweet and Sour chicken and it overly sweet, and missing spice after taste even though I've tried 3 on their 5 star hot scale. The Thai Ice-Tea I've ordered with the meal was good, but over all the meal did not impress me to go above 3 stars. It's a decent option for lunch, the portions are big, and the place is clean and quite. They have a wide verity of lunch specials and good selection of dishes.

The smokey burger and aged cheddar burgers are really good, but the Tiki burger is a new burger deliciouseness. The plumb sauce with pineapple and over easy egg is so good with ground beef and bread. Never had a burger like it, like the Grateful Dead, "They are not the best at what they do, they are the only ones that do what they do." This burger will go down as one of my favorite burgers, and uniquely delicious. And the hand cut fries in the oriental food container did not go unnoticed. I assume they cut them, soak em for a day, pull em, then fry off at high temp, and toss is salt because they are crispy, soft, and delicious.

I really liked this place. We stumbled upon it for drinks and appetizers, and we were pleasantly surprised by the great musical trio playing in the BEAUTIFUL courtyard/patio area. It really is a magical ambience at night and the service was excellent. Highly recommend trying this place. I know I will go back again when visiting the area.

This is a small family(I think) owned restaurant. There are only about twelve tables caring from 4-8 seats. Try to ignore that you are right beside a go kart track and the experience can be nice. The restaurant is a bit run down but the food is very good. Service was quick and there are lots of vegetarian options. I had the Home Style Tofu with steamed rice and vegetables. The lunch portion was perfect. My friend had the Angry Beef and he liked his as well. The parking is limited so plan accordingly.

Get the naan bread with anything you order! It's an up charge but worth it! Made fresh in house. It's not the typical naan u get at an Indian restaurant but so good...almost similar to the doner kebab in Germany.

Some of the tastiest food you will ever eat. Similar to Greek fare, all dishes are unbelievably flavorful. Go as a group and order a bunch of appetizers to share. Just be sure you make a reservation. There's never an empty table.

The reviews are real. The food is amazing and portions are huge especially for lunch. Everyone should try it. I can't wait to go back often to try everything on the menu. They are very friendly, knowledgeable and the place is beautiful and spacious so you have some privacy dining.

This place is awesome! It's delicious, inexpensive, and offers great service. I ordered beef pho with lemongrass broth and banh xeo and my mom had the sol. Everything was perfect, especially the banh xeo - sooo good. There are both traditional and fusion dishes. My new favorite Vietnamese place in Reno!

I honestly can't say one negative thing about this place. We live nearby and I'm just sorry we didn't try it sooner. We ordered take out and it was ready when my husband got there. The Tom Kah soup was, hands down, the best I've ever had. I ordered a small and have more than half left over. For entrees we ordered the Chicken Pad Thai and the Chicken Green Curry. Both were outstanding and good size portions. We ordered the Pad Thai medium spicy and it packed some serious heat. I'd be careful ordering it hot. This will definitely be a regular takeout place for us.

For all you fellow foodies- If you have never tried Indian, the Amber Indian buffet is a perfect option for you to adventure out. The buffet is full of delicious options for meat lovers and vegetarians.
Thai iced tea! VERY TASTY! The captain crunch burrito -AMAZING! Curry chicken tacos -AMAZING! I brought my friend there and she went back there 3 times in the same week!
King wok and Saigon better family cook inside traditional Vietnamese food , they are nice to me , the food wasn't terrible

This was the best Indian food I have ever had! I got food to go today, and it was amazing. We ordered the butter chicken, samosas, and butter naan. The staff was very friendly as well, and the owner makes you feel very welcome!

I came here for lunch with my family today. The interior was nice and spacious. The fresh garlic Naan was the best I've had, and the food in the buffet was all tasty. Service was also good, the staff was very attentive.

I couldn't decide what to order and thank god the prices are reasonable enough that I was able to order everything I was considering. My instincts were correct everything was good. I was polite I did not stand up and scream DAMN! I told my food mate I may need to step outside and scream because my fish was so efn good! I want to do the dance that happens when food taste so good it tickles your bones. I can't give you an exact description of the style because it is southern ingredients and it is southern food but they gave it a Asian kiss but that description doesn't match the beauty of flavors. I don't want to paint a picture that can only be tasted. Just go you don't need a lot of $$ bring your appetite.
This is a very acceptable Thai food restaurant. The atmosphere is clean and the service is always pleasant.

One of the better falafel places in KOP area. The menu is somewhat like Chipotle. The thin fries are awesome and the concept of hummus bowl is too tempting to pass up on. Overall, I would recommend the place. The falafel are freshly fried and served hot. I have this place bookmarked for future visits.

The food is delicious, among the best places I've ordered Indian food from. I had some issues with their online ordering, but the owner has graciously apologized and offered compensation for my inconvenience. Try the chili chicken, it's the best I've had.

Gus is amazing. His food's amazing and he takes great pride in his bold, novel creations each day. His food explodes with flavor, and it's wrapped up in great care. He's also got a mind like a steel trap. I didn't go see him for easily over a year (I was traveling a lot), and when I went back, he asked me about my yoga classes that I teach. When I think about the thousands of plates he's served up to the often long line in the interim, I was amazed he remembered me instantly.
They have the best chicken Pad Thai and Panang chicken curry I have ever had!!! This is the best Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara by far!

My husband and I went for an early dinner on Monday. We absolutely loved the food! There are so many vegetarian options that we want to come back to try each and everyone of them. For the first time ever we ordered something different then red/green curry and Pad Sew ew. We got the bamboo salad, king's soup and one more thing that I cant recall right now. But everything was great, As I said, we are going back soon!
Closest thing to eating in Italy I have found. Love the antipasta and the gnocchi with BB sauce. YUMMMM. What a gem.

I met a literary friend for coffee here, to catch up. We haven't discussed books, etc. in a long time. It was a wintery afternoon, and after my long walk from the east side of South to the west, I was frickin' freezing and ready for something hot! On walking in, I couldn't find a seat, and people were crowded into every corner. It was a nice mix of conversationalists and people using computers and studying. You wouldn't get stared at for talking. Found a seat on the sofa by a nice guy who let me squeeze in, and soon after, we had a table. And soon after that, I had the most beautiful latte I've ever seen. It was really very pretty, and I wish I had a pic to share with you. Great afternoon! How charming!

Hard to find a parking spot. Food is mediocre at best and overpriced. Side salads are laughable, few shreds of lettuce from a bag a cherry tomato and a prepackaged kens dressing very tacky. If this restaurant was anywhere other than right on the water it would have gone under a long time ago if you absolutely have to eat on the water its your only option in pasco but be prepared for a meh experience. Its a snack bar at red lobster prices reminds me a lot of the tourist trap restaurants in st pete.

Honestly, there isn't much in Carp by way of "ethnic" eating, but Siam Thai isn't bad. The prices are relatively reasonable and they are able to accommodate gluten free diners (a friend is on a gluten free diet). The wait staff is friendly and the service is fast. I love that they have outdoor seating in the Thai-style "bungalows". Reminds me of when I went to the islands off of Thailand. Another reason I like them is that they don't treat Asian diners differently. I've found that some places treat you differently when you're asian, like you're expected to know something and/or that you get less courteous treatment. Overall, a yummy Thai place in Carp!
