Great local Thai place, clean, friendly and very tasty. Drunken noodles are very good as are the veggie spring rolls..

I liked the chicken patay with peanut sauce. It was delicious. I thought the chicken was well seasoned and moist. There were a lot of portions, enough for a meal. I wish I had ordered the beef to try out also. I would go back anytime.

My husband and I come here often for lunch, as it's an easy way to beat the crowds. Their food is absolutely phenomenal. We've had the bento, the katsu, and what we call KFC- the Korean fried chicken (wings). The taste is OUT OF THIS WORLD! I like the mild garlic, my husband usually goes for the spicy. They have my favorite miso soup in the city! I'm a miso fanatic, so I try it everywhere I go- it's truly the tastiest I've had. Their salad dressing tastes fresh without being overpowering. I never finish my salad at other restaurants but not the case here. My only problem is that everything tastes so good and I get too full before I can finish everything. But it's not the worst problem in the world to bring home leftovers from here. Now let's talk Service. Again, I have to give it 5 stars. EVERY TIME we've been in the owner has given friendly and fast service. She's helped us choose menu items based on what we like and she's really just a lovely and friendly person. We always feel genuinely welcome. If you want to try amazing food (I take my food seriously) with great service and good prices give Umami a try. I promise you won't be sorry!

My Yia Yia would approve. Momos is one of my favorite restaurants in St Louis, and since moving away from Detroit and its fabulous Greektown, I was so happy to discover wonderful and authentic Greek food. You really cant go wrong with this menu - very rarely have I been disappointed in anything I've eaten here. Personal favorites are the Tenderloin (a must-have!), the Greek Meatballs, Baked Feta, Saganaki (of course!), the Kebobs and Gyros and the Broccoli with Feta. YUM! The staff is pleasant and remembers us every time we come in. We have gone there for date nights, business dinners and family dinners (including taking our son with us, and they are always kid friendly!) The only drawback is the belly dancing - which I dont particularly mind, but they crank up the music to near-deafening volumes and the clanging finger cymbals make me want to use my fork to impale my ears. If they could just take down the volume, this restaurant would be near-perfect!

I got goat curry. Their spicy is real spicy. The portion was pretty big. I just think it is pricy and not worth spending on indian goat curry by paying 17.50 including tips and tax. I want to check their 7.99 lunch buffet though.

I have to admit: anyone who knows me knows that I have a Saigon addiction. Like, a really bad one. Hands down, this is my favorite restaurant. I eat here at least once a week (sometimes more...way more) and I get a variety of dishes, ex., pho, bun, lunch menu items, and the list goes on. The vegetarian spring rolls are just about the greatest thing ever in my opinion. They come with a tasty peanut dipping sauce. I also enjoy their bubble tea (Pineapple and Papaya are my favorite flavors, but many of my friends enjoy the Thai Spice flavor). If you are eating here for the first time, try one of the Bun's (#90-#99ish) with the eggroll and don't forget to dump the entire bowl of fish sauce on it. If you are feeling under the weather, and need a good pick me up dish, try one of the Pho soups or the Duck Soup with egg noodles (The duck soup is delicious on a cold winter day too...mmmmmm.....). Pho soups come with plate of freshness; bean sprouts, basil, limes, jalapenos. Duck soup has baby portabellas, some sort of greens (maybe Kale or something similar), and tasty deliciously prepared duck. You will dribble all of this wonderfulness down your chin and onto your shirt. The prices are good, the food is FRESH, the waiter (Peter) is awesome. They've moved to a new location and they easily accomodate some of our large lunch groups now (sometimes 12 or 13 people), which is terrific! Carry out is always super fast. Oh, and they are closed on Tuesdays (I actually have a note in my office to remind me).
I went to this place about 2 months ago . The food was amazing and the service was wonderful .

If you are anywhere near this restaurant make a bee line. Loved the atmosphere, music, vibe. We had the calamari starter - a must. I had the pad thai which was excellent. Heavy in the tamarind, but I personally love the flavor. Husband had the aged cheddar burger with a side of fried rice. Just delicious. They should be charging more.

I have to give this 3 star because of the wine. It was a amazing wine can't remember the name. Food was ok afterwards it gave me very bad heart burn. Service was pretty ok. Buy the time we got out of the restaurant it was full so this must be a good place to eat. I might try it again sometimes but not now.

Yikes! I was in love with the idea of going to the Park Allen Restaurant! Never been, driven past a million times and finally said I'm going! Made a res for the four of us and showed up on a Saturday night. The place is cute and quaint with a cool wine feature that had no wine in it. After sitting down and waiting for about 15 minutes for someone to come over and getting shot down on my first 3 wine selections due to them being out of stock we finally got a couple bottles to the table. And then the bomb from our waiter (actually really awesome waiter). No lamb no filet no salmon...hmmm not what I expected in a Mediterranean restaurant with almost no wine. So we got some calamari which was delish and a couple steaks (not filets) but ok also cooked well. Waiter was great and comped our desserts because of the lack of everything else. All in all tasty just wish I coulda got the wine and the food I was looking forward to. Maybe would return Andy

I've been here twice. Both times the service was a little slow even when it was not crowded- I think the bartender may get a little distracted- but don't let that keep you away. It's got an interesting atmosphere (I like the little cubbies on the walls with the Mexican tchotchkes) and will definitely go back for the drinks. Both times I've thought the speciality cocktails listed on the menu seemed too sweet for my liking, so I told the bartender/waiter what types of things I tend to like and not like (not sweet, dry, bitter or spicy is OK) and he's concocted delicious things to pair well with my food, which is also delicious. I think the portions are just right - not enough that I either feel too stuffed or have to take a box home, but even when I arrive hungry, I leave perfectly satisfied. The dish with the grilled eggplant (I can't remember the name) on a bun is a very tasty vegetarian option and I've heard others say they especially dig the fish tacos. Oh, also, parking never seems to be an issue. I'll definitely be back.

This is my favorite restaurant in Nashville. Not the fanciest, not the fastest, but you can not beat the food! Everything is so fresh and the flavor is on point. Got to go back and get a sandwich after talking about it now.

After Saffron's successful entrance into the Main Line, we were excited to get a place even closer to our home. After trying Ekta's food twice, we were somewhat disappointed. Perhaps it was because Saffron was our point of comparison, which is outstanding in our opinion.

Super delicious Thai food. A++ for the Yellow Curry. Tastes exactly like it was prepared in Thailand. Fast and friendly service. BYO is an added bonus. Great presentation on the fried banana treat (see pic with flowers)

Very disappointed. Lunch specials are only available for dine in so I paid $14 for takeout only to find that my chicken curry was made with tiny pieces of all dark meat and only a small amount of chicken was in the container. All of the curry pictures from the other location have white meat and I have never been served dark meat in a curry before. The curry flavor was good and there were a lot of vegetables, hence the two stars, but not worth the $14. Would try again if some changes are made.

All the food seemed to be very good. We had the Sampler for two, a lovely platter with two lamb chops, two chicken & two pork souvlaki sticks, chicken breast all perfectly charbroiled. These were placed on a plate of tasty rice and potatoes, greek style. It was one of the best Greek meals I've ever had.

Great food, the service is excellent. The flavor of the food is fresh and of quality. Compared to the tipical "caribbean foods of the area" this is the place to go to really have the complete experience. The price is great putting on a scale of quantity served and the deliciousness. Highly recommended!

I ordered take out for lunch today with my mom. We got the lasooni gobi, chicken jalfrezi and chicken saagwala. Everything was absolutely delicious. The chicken was very tender and flavorful. The rice served with it was light and fluffy. The service was fast and friendly. I would definitely recommend this place and will be going back to try more items.

Tourists on Bourbon will be happy (or not) to learn that their options for quick grab and go eats aren't limited to lucky dogs, as a tiny restaurant just off Bourbon offers similarly uninspired drunk food. It's maybe six feet wide and fifteen deep before the cash register, with booths on the sides and old boxing pictures along the walls. The Muslim owners and operators have placed a few religious decorations on the wall too, which provides an ironic contrast to the obviously drunk customers who stumble in and provide the bulk of their business. Ali Baba offers about ten different middle eastern themed items including chicken and beef gyros and shawarma, hummus, and baba ganouj. The gyros and shawarmas look like the usual stuff thrown onto the rotisserie, but taste like they've been constructed from poor quality ingredients. Dry meats and borderline stale pitas ruin the sandwiches I've had here. Much better late night drunk food can be found at Jimani, Alibi, Clover Grill, or Three Legged Dog. I honestly can't think of a reason for eating here other than being inebriated on Bourbon and not knowing any better. I find it hard to believe that someone would drive here for middle eastern. Lebanon's offers far superior gyros and shawarmas for reasonable prices if you're willing to trek uptown.
the food was ok for, the service was pleasant. but there is a very pungent odor, sort of musty or moldy. it's a bit distracting from the food
Rip off, small portions and expensive... Food is less than mediocre in a great day... Don't!!
Over-priced and bad service! Two person per hookah and added charge per added person to use the same hookah!!!

For our visit, we had no trouble finding a street parking right outside the restaurant. Staffs were friendly and inviting. All the dishes were soooooo good! We had: -Crabmeat and asparagus soup--this was a nice starter. Lightly flavored. Not bland and not salty. Perfectly made in the middle. -Bo Luc Lac--the meat was soft, tender and full of juice. Bite-sized potatoes complimented the dish. All sat on a bed of fresh vegetables. This was my fav dish to eat with rice. -Crab Rangoon--crispy with warm cream cheese and real crab. Hubby loved that the most! -Lemongrass shrimp--lightly flavored and so wonderful to my palate. -Fried Banana--this one is a must try. Just enough of the fried and the banana. It's even better with ice cream! Overall, I'm content with my experience and the delicious food. Will return soon ^_^
A French fry lovers paradise where your sandwich has fries packed inside and then served with another side of fires. Think a Lebanese Primanti Brothers.
Our new stop on our way to Nashville! We had grape leaves, falafel plate and gyro plate. It was all incredibly good! Very fresh and delicious. Super clean restrooms too.

Went there during the week at lunch time, there were probably 6 other people there. The decor was really nice, really Thai. First off we started with some appetizers: Spring Rolls and Satay Gai. The thing that impressed me the most about them was the peanut sauce. The best peanut sauce I have ever tasted! However, and this is the reason for three stars, upon eating one of the spring rolls my friend came across a piece of string, maybe half a foot long. The waitress was very nice about it and took it off our bill. I have no idea what it was doing in the spring roll but the group became very wary of the upcoming dishes. Next came the Pad Thai, Pad Khee-Mao, and the Tom Yum Goong. All of these dishes were hot hot hot! The dishes had plenty of vegetables and the soup had a decent amount of jumbo shrimp. Main dishes were delish, but the appetizers were a huge turnoff. Overall i give basil spice an "A OK"

After falling in love with local food while on vacation in Thailand, husband and I have been on a hunt for good authentic Thai restaurants in Edmonton. Numchok Wilai may just be the place. I wouldn't call the food mind-blowing but it is definitely tasty and authentic. We have tried spring rolls, tom yum, pa-nang shrimp and pad khing (with chicken). Everything was good: tasty and flavorful. Shrimp in pa-nang and chicken in pad khing were in abundance. Tom yum could have been better though. I felt that it lacked something - I can't quite put a finger on it. I could locate all usual ingredients that go into this magnificent soup: kaffir leaves, lemongrass, galangal...and yet, it lacked certain oomph. Tom yum served in Thailand spoiled me for life, I guess:) The hunt for perfect tom yum in Edmonton continues... I'll be back to Numchok Wilai to try more menu items, though. For sure! Service was excellent: timely and courteous.

Went to Magasin in the CBD tonight and while the food never disappoints, the service is horrible and the attitude of one of the employees tonight prompted me to write this. It was 915 pm and a couple walked in to be seated. The sign on their door clearly indicated that they closed at 10 pm on Saturdays. (Even their hours on Yelp indicate that). A male employee with a bad Justin Bieber hairdo walked up to them and told them they were closed. The couple looked surprised but were very mild mannered and polite. The woman even pointed out, almost apologetically, that the sign on the door said that they were open until 10. The employee rudely insisted they could not be served and that the restaurant was closed. As the couple turned to leave, he rolled his eyes and flipped his Bieber 'do ever so arrogantly. He then walked to our table and without a word handed us the bill and soon came to pick it up without saying anything-- not even a simple thank you. It was like he couldn't wait to get everyone out of there. He is a horrible representative of the business. I took his picture and plan on contacting the owner to let them know what kind of jerk they have working for them.

More like two and a half... I want to like this place, but overall it has been disappointing. First, Taj India is pretty much the only Indian restaurant I've ordered from where rice is not included with the curry dishes. Keep this in mind If you want rice since you will need to order it separately. Also, takeout arrived with just my small container of Chana masala and naan - no rice (as mentioned already, though luckily I remembered that from eating there several years ago), no napkins, and no utensils. Very no frills. The food is decent, I'd give it about three stars. It's not the best I've ever had but it's also not the worst.

I've been eager to experience Olio since I discovered how the former garage was transformed into this amazing restaurant. The decor did not disappoint; it's beautifully put together both inside as well as the outdoor garden area. Gretchen was nice; meek but nice. I mentioned I had an itching for hummus and she recommended I try the Eyal; it was delicious. The shrimp in the Eyal hummus was sauteed and seasoned to perfection it also came with plenty of dough; pita as well as ciabatta..but I truly felt like I probably could've dressed up a container of Trader Joe's Mediterranean Hummus and not known the difference. Don't kill the messenger I'm just being honest here. There was a lot more oil than I prefer and the serving size was quite small for $12 before tip. Next, I wanted to try the roasted cauliflower but Gretchen advised me they were out. Then, I wanted to try the Roasted Beets salad but Gretchen advised me they were out. Finally, I gave up ordering anything else however, Gretchen did advise me they were out of Romaine Hearts. I thought to myself, "Why are you guys open?" Maybe I picked a bad day; but in the restaurant business a bad day can cost you 2 stars on the Christy Scale.
We love going to this family owned small restaurant where the service is friendly and fast. Food is authentic Thai, very generous serving and at a great price

If you want good views of the sun setting, good beer, and music then you found it here at Sam's BEach Bar! The food is kind of a who is the cook. I"ve had good food, and I've had semi blah food. I can't complain about service. Every waitress has been attentive.

I was visiting Media from Philly and was looking for a quaint little spot for dinner, from the outside this place looks great. It was Friday evening and there were some open tables, so we were seated quickly. Service was not bad, although it took a while for someone to come to our table and food took a long time as well. Lots of take outs, so we figured it was good food so worth the while. Unfortunately, the Pad Thai and Massaman curry were a big disappointment, and I say this because I am a big of fan and get these dishes regularly. Overall, not impressed with quality of food. Other than that, it's a fine place for casual gatherings. Maybe there are other dishes that are better, we only had two!

The atmosphere was very nice and the service was excellent. I probably didn't make the best decision in ordering but I didn't want to be super full since we were going to a movie afterwards and I wanted popcorn. I ordered a wedge salad and a tomato, mozzarella and basil flatbread. The salad was great but I don't know how you could mess up a wedge salad. The flatbread was just okay as I felt like it was a little dry and they could have been more generous with the cheese. If I go back I will probably choose a pasta or fish entree next time.

it's weird. while waiting for the check, Sue & I were both assessing dinner. Massive disappointment. But, while going dish for dish, there was only one that let us down. Yet, for some reason we were still dissappointed. Like I said, weird. So, we had the: * MELITZANOSALATA - a lot easier to eat than it is to pronounce. I really liked this dish, Sue didn't. But, it's my review, so who cares. Tasted fresh and light. * GARLIC ROASTED BEETS - this was the letdown dish. I dunno, I hear Garlic Roasted Beets, I think savory, not sweet. It was basically diced beets underneath a giant slop of something called a Skordalia. Here's what wikipedia says about Skordalia: Skordalia or skordhalia/skorthalia ( [skora'a]; in Greek also called ) is a thick puree (or sauce/dip/spread/etc.) in Greek cuisine made by combining crushed garlic with a bulky base--which may be a purée of potatoes, walnuts, almonds, or liquid-soaked stale bread--and then beating in olive oil to make a smooth emulsion. Interesting, thanks Wikipedia. Too bad it still tasted like damp sock. SPANIKOPITA - Four small fantastic spinach pies covered in feta. It was so good that Sue knowingly ate my last piece after we had already unspokenly divided the dish in half. Bad wife! CHAR-GRILLED OCTOPUS - I dunno, these things were a little too real for me. You're not getting pieces of 'pus, you're getting whole baby 'pus. That being said, I'll eat anything if it's got a face, this face just happened to be a little too chewy for my face. And, last but not least... GRILLED LOKANEKO SAUSAGE - really flavorful sausage over roasted peppers. You know what I just realized, they don't make this crap, they probably got it from Trader Joe's or Whole Foods. What a letdown! The service was kinda slow too. I think our poor waitress had about 15 too many tables. You can barely enjoy your food over that wretched shit blaring out the speakers. So, that's us. Better selection that Olympia, but the eating just doesn't come close.
Very good pho, iced coffee, dumplings and spring rolls. An absolute must if you are in the area and are craving Vietnamese.

I love their cuban sandwich. They always cook their food fresh and its very tasty..its best to call in your order if you have s big order that way there is no long wait ..the servers are always nice and polite big plus for me and my family. My family and I will always go there

My favorite Thai place in the city. It's right off Nolensville Road right next to the aptly named "Latino Tire". The parking is tight, but the food inside is so good. Nice cute little dining area. Absolutely great Thai food. Of course I dont know the names of any of the dishes, but the chicken in coconut milk soup (tom cat ka?) is great. As is the chicken with cashew, and a number of other chicken dishes. Definitely not a boring thai place. And great service. Good prices. Really enjoying my culinary excursions up and down Nolensville Road.

Delicious!! I had the shredded beef empanadas. And they were freaking amazing. Family owned restaurant that you are sure to love. I'm not one for branching out on my food choices, but Tu Casa is making me rethink that. I'm ready to try everything on their menu!
Awesome authentic Vietnamese food! Yummy finally. Happy birthday honey.

This is our favorite indian place. I usually get the Chicken Tikka Masala and it never disappoints. Bonus points for being able to customize how spicy you want your dish. Pakoras and vegetable samosas are also first rate. Service can be slow if it's busy but nothing that you wouldn't normally expect. It can be expensive but so are the rest of the indian places in the area.

I am originally a customer of the Media restaurant, so you can imagine my shear joy in hearing one closer to home opened up. I usually get my food to go, but am really looking forward to checking out the lunch buffet. The food is ALWAYS consistently good, and the servers are well mannered. This is a must visit!

Was at the Opryland for a conference and wanted to have food outside of the resort. We were disappointed to say the least. The lady, which I assume is the owner, was not welcoming at all and simply glared at us. The pineapple fried rice was very oily and bland. The pad sa eww noodles were all clumped together. Dinner was very unsatisfying.

If I could give them NO stars, that's exactly what they would've gotten! The food here is soooooo nasty. I got a cassava leaf platter with rice and I hated it. Like seriously, the rice was nasty. Like how do you mess up white rice?! The cassava leaf was DISGUSTING! It tasted like pea flavored baby food! DONT COME HERE! Just take the ride up Southwest

This is a real hidden gem in Nashville. Wife and I used to eat here very often until we moved from Tennessee to Arizona. Even my mother, and two aunts (from India) called the food very good. This is a small, but nice restaurant. I wish this restaurant well. You can not go wrong with anything on the menu. NOTE: Call the restaurant if you can not find it. They are hidden very well. I had to call them maybe 3 times just to find them.
Looking for a quick bite? Do your waist line a favor and get a sandwich or a bowl of pho and skip the gut bomb burgers across the street. Service is very fast and the food is always tasty.
Always delicious! Service is great and pick up as well!!! I have been their costumer for the past 3 years and the food still great!!! My favorite is the Pad Thai very spicy!! With Tofu
Love the sega wett. Excellent sega wett as always.

I've been walking past Jasmine Rice for months and months, and always wondered about it, but was happy enough with Circles that I never gave it a chance. Finally, I tried it with a friend for dinner and we haven't gone back to Circles since! Jasmine Rice is a more affordable and, in my opinion, even better-quality Thai food option. It's also really convenient to pick up from there instead of having to order from Circles. We loved sitting in the restaurant - it has a very calm and laid-back ambiance. It's not pretentious, but still very classy. I loved the Chicken Massaman curry - my friend loved it so much that it's her new go-to. Their classic Chicken Pad Thai is my personal favorite, but I do like that they have a nice variety for when I'm feeling more adventurous. I always get a small Veggie Coconut Soup. The broth is really light, with a hint of lemon and has just the right amount of veggies. It's a nice way to start any meal. Their spring rolls are just average, I think I'd like to try their spicy Thai Basil Meatballs next time instead as they get really good reviews on Yelp - update to come! Their Thai Iced Tea is good, just a classic. I liked it to go and in the restaurant, so no difference there. Their Chicken Pad Thai is pretty huge - when I get it as take out, it usually lasts me two full meals, and by full, I mean that I'm really full after eating about half! It's just your typical Pad Thai - nice rice noodles, great sauce and some peanuts sprinkled on top. Mostly, I just find the quality to be really good - no MSG or any gross aftertaste that I've been fighting to avoid with take-out. My roommate still prefers Circles in this department because theirs is more garlicky and has more of a kick, but I prefer Jasmine Rice's milder take, so it all depends on your preferences. I think I get a bigger portion at Jasmine Rice too, so that makes a difference! The Chicken Massaman curry is a really tasty - it's has potatoes, carrots, chunks of onions and sprinkled with peanuts. The sauce is tasty, mild, although don't get it if you aren't a fan of coconut. I loved it because I can't handle anything very spicy, but do enjoy rich flavors. This was a great dish for someone who doesn't want to compromise on something bland, but isn't in the mood for something super spicy! FYI - Order it with rice - when my roommate ordered it as takeout it did not come with rice, so it wasn't something she had leftovers for the next day. But it's still worth it, delicious flavors that don't overpower the veggies and chicken. The Green Curry with Chicken was spicy, but not too spicy. It wasn't anything super exciting in my opinion, I much preferred the Massaman to it! The owners are also very nice - and the service is great. It takes 20-30 minutes for the food to be ready if you order for take-out. I've generally waited a few minutes when I got there right at 20 minutes during peak dinner hours, so I might give them five more minutes next time. But they're very friendly and make it easy to pay while you wait. Just FYI - it's BYOB if you go there, as their website suggests! So don't forget to bring your own wine!

The salmon and cabbage was excellent the first time I went but the the second time, the salmon taste more burnt than of a grilled taste and the cabbage was hard and not as seasoned as the first time...I will return and if it's not to my liking 9/10 I won't return. The customer service is outstanding might I add and the establishment has a friendly atmosphere. I hope they don't disappoint me because I really like the place

Delicious and fresh food. The tika misala is a must have, we also had the ground chicken kabobs for an appetizer. Very delicious, food is great and the service is just as good. I highly recommend trying

This is 138% the best food truck in Philadelphia. It is seriously worth the wait, and for those of you who work in center city--I'm incredibly jealous. I also had no idea it had a name until today! I usually just sniff it out. You seriously can smell it from like three blocks away. And that alone is impressive considering it cuts through the gross mashed potato smell of the city. This is one of those, hand over $10 and get whatever is given to you type places. It's never bad, portions are always huge and it's just perfection in a styrofoam container. You get rice, amazingly tasty grilled chicken, falafel and whatever side dish of the day is. The man serving the food will ramble to any guest that comes up, and sometimes will give soup out on a cold day to wet your appetite. I'm always so jealous of my boyfriend whenever he sends me pics of this delicious food. And most likely hold a grudge for about a day until he brings me leftovers. Only complaint is please be around on weekends!!! I need your delicious food.

While visiting NAS I cam across this place. If you haven't been here and you are in town you should go. Food was fresh, service was polite and restaurant was clean! Great value for your $$ with unique food you can't find everywhere. Unfortunately I was traveling alone and only wish my family was with me to enjoy. Truly a pleasure and worth the $$ spent.

Yummy and a little spicy gyro. Small dining area as another review mentioned. No need to repeat what others have said...good Gyro...tasty and served up fresh. I personally like more onion and tomato on my Gyro but this was very good.

We found this place thanks to Yelp and Boise Weekly, and make the trek from SE Boise a few times a month (it'd be twice a week if we lived/worked closer). Best sandwiches in Boise, hands down. The bread is light and chewy on the inside, crunchy on the outside. They offer both Vietnamese-type meat choices, as well as the normal, boring roast beef, tuna, etc. My typical order - #6 (grilled pork loaf), extra veggies, no jalapeno. And the prices! Love that you can get a sandwich this good for under $5. UPDATE: You MUST try the Pho. Freaking awesome.

A group of 12 came here on a Friday night and the staff was very friendly, welcoming, and attentive to us throughout the evening. If you have any questions, just ask and they love to help you! The restaurant is more spacious than I expected for a strip mall place. You're given a menu and an informational sheet that defines common words from the menu. Point of interest: they have 3 different kinds of imported Ethiopian beer to choose from. We tried a cabbage sambusa and a beef sambusa, which are similar to an Indian somosa (fried dough with a savory filling). Both were great but the cabbage had more flavor. All other dishes came on top of a circular piece of fermented sourdough that you are meant to eat the food with - you can request rice or French bread if you don't like it but it has a very mild flavor! The lamb was not de-boned so beware. I would recommend the "tibbs" - either chicken, beef, lamb, or goat meat fried with peppers and onion in a delicious sauce. The vegetarian sampler platter was a great variety of authentic spreads and the perfect appetizer. The baklava for dessert was the best I have ever had! So perfectly warm and sweet. There was a variety of other customers there, one family who brought their adopted Ethiopian son to eat there for the first time, it was awesome to witness! It seems good for takeout - I noticed quite a few people walk in and get their food for takeout within minutes of arriving.

This cart has been here for ages, and it's a shame that I hadn't checked it out until now! Super cheap breakfast and lunch food with a smile. Make sure you try the Bui sauce, it's some type of yummy spicy mayo. Not sure what kind of bread they use, but the other reviewer's comment about it being very fluffy and easy to fill up on, is spot on. Not a fan of the bread because there could be more meat on the sandwich. Can't really complain though cause it's so cheap and delicious!

3.5 stars The service was spectacular. Upon arrival, the girl at the counter was very nice and asked if it was my first time. When I replied yes, she asked if she could tell me what the have to offer. Why of course! So they offer pretzel crusted chicken tenders, dark meat and white meat, spicy vs mild. They also have some sweets that I didn't indulge in (but baked on premises!) I also got their mac and cheese, and jalapeno corn bread. So the way they price things here is based on weight. And if i remember correctly it's either $7.50 or $8.95/pound I can't remember.. I'll update when I check! But as you can see, it's kind of pricey. For my chicken, cornbread and mac n cheese it came to $15.46 (and I got 5 pieces of chicken tenders). I'll give it to them for the mac n cheese. It was awesome flavorful, with a good crust on the top! The chicken was A-OK. It was decently juicy, but not very flavorful! Kind of bland. But the crust was nice and crispy! They also have a handful of dipping flavors for 50 cents a piece. I opted for the pesto parmasean which was super awesome. The cornbread was pretty good. A ltitle on the dry side, but I really appreciated the amount of jalapenos in there! I love jalapenos :) I'm not sure I'd be back just due to the pricey-ness and OK value of food. Maybe if I'm in the area :)

This place offers a good alternative to burgers and fried chicken. So if we were in the mood for fast food, but wanted to avoid a trip to the usual chains, Dooners would do the trick. That said, the food was nothing to rave about. It was just different. We went on a Saturday night and the kids working the counter seemed a little "out of it". Didn't seem excited to be there. They were talking more to each other while preparing our food than they were to us. They were unenthusiastic about answering questions (maybe because they are always answering questions like, "what is dooner?"). Be careful to restrict their use of cabbage. It has a powerful flavor and they will literally smother your food in it. So... would we go back. Maybe. But we won't be craving it, and we won't go out of our way to eat there.

Andre and Janeice are the bomb.com! My sister and I visited their restaurant in November. We had jerk chicken, plantains, oxtails and rice and peas and took some beef patties home. The food was delicious. A couple walked out because it was A LITTLE BUSY, but they should have stayed because the food is absolutely delicious. The only thing they are missing is a grill with pimento wood. Our service was great as well! We will definitely come back while in Tampa.
Love Pita Jungle!!! Especially the hummus! Server was nice and friendly and efficient. Food was good but ordered too much of course. Nice place to go for a change. Will be back!

We had our Holiday party at Francisco's On The River. The restaurant was awesome and I am so glad we picked this restaurant! The service was excellent! And the food was delicious! I highly recommend Francisco's On The River! Not one person complained about the food or service. And Giselle was just wonderful to work with. We will be back again and again! Jim Nicoletti (Wyvern Ltd)
The lamb and rice were delicious and the fries were fabulous. Delicious gluten free pita bread. But the tatkoutki and the roasted eggplant need work. I will be back to try other dishes.

The service was very slow to greet our table. Had to walk up to desk and ask for menus. The food was surprisingly bland and all of it was heavily spiced with paprika and cumin. Everything on the Queens 8 tasted too similar. I enjoyed the atmosphere and the people refilling water and delivering food were very pleasant. There were only 6 items on our queens 8. Overall it is pricey for one shared entree one app and two drinks. Came to be $55.00 before tip.
I eat pho once a week and have been to most spots in the city. Love this place. No frills just solid food. Very nice staff always friendly! Take out is quick and easy. Love it here
Had the Chuleta with rice and beans and tostones of course mayoketchup all delicious. Chuelta was 3 times bigger then I thought made leftover so good!!
Love the food & bartender. Im really glad I stop in. A new Hot spot to come to. Luv it.

The food is sooo delicious! I love the hummus and gyro wraps. The pita bread is warm, and the meat is juicy. I wish I could eat here more often. The workers are kind as well. When I came here last Easter, I was on the verge of passing out due to being dehydrated and out in the heat. The woman working was very considerate and gave me a free bottle of water, which was great to see in comparison to street vendors demanding $5+ for a bottle of water. Sheesh.

I took my husband here and was very excited to try the Jerk Chicken. I love spice food and it was very spicy. I was burping Jerk Chicken for days. The boys got it mild and over all we enjoyed our meal. I just think it was way over priced and the staff was blah. Actively looking for another Jamaican spot.
The Bo 7 Mon (7 course of Beef) is very tasty and worth the trip even though they charge $2 for very little extra noodle is a bit too much. Bo Nhúng B is awesome too and you can't go wrong with it.

I love the tapas trios. I wish we could have that option throughout the dinner time. I dislike ordering a platter of tapas which is gigantic for me. The other thing I noticed, sometimes the happy hour tapas has different sizes. One day I came and the little plate was good size, another day was barely anything there. Why aren't the pita bread cut in small pieces everytime? It seems the chef at the moment may or may not cut the bread into pieces. If I wanted to cut my pita bread myself I would stay at home. It would b nice if the server asks me if I would like a glass of water as I am sitted not when I am leaving.
The best Gyro deluxe sandwich in the St. Louis area. The staff is always so friendly and the prices are reasonable and the portions are large.
Still beautiful sunsets and cocktails!! Pretty and cute waitresses!!! Had the fried green tomatoes, so good!!!

The gyro platter was delicious. Enjoyed every bite. The rice was a tad overseasoned but not enough to make me stop eating it. The meat was tender. The tzaziki was perfect. I'd definitely order it again but not before I sample other dishes.
I've only tried the falafel sandwich, which tastes good, but was a bit dry.

The tom yum soup was ok, wish it was a bit more sour and spicy. The larb gai was alright, I've had better in seattle so my personal preferences are high. The papaya salad was super spicy! Definitely got that thai kick. My mouth was burning! The red curry was yummy and the phad thai was ok. Ambiance and decor is really nice. The service was good too. Just have higher expectations on the food, but then again, its hard to find good asian food in FL.

It was my wife's birthday and we planned to go to an Indonesian restaurant in Phili that we read a very good review While driving on turnpike we changed our mind and decided to look for Mexican or Indian food in Lansdale. We took the Lansdale exit and checked on Yelp. Found Spice kitchen and decided to try it out. We were very impressed with the decor and the wait staff were very friendly Mary was very helpful and took good care of our food We ordered shrimp masala and Lamb rogan josh along with appetizer. All the items were real tasty. The menu has the right selection of items not overwhelming It is certainly a place you want to go with family and friends. Good value. Will certainly return

Finally came here for dinner. WOW is all I have to say. Service is speedy and food is amazing. I think I might be a green curry addict. That is one of the best things I've eaten in a loooooooooooong time.

I've only been here once specifically to try the pho, and I liked it. There was only one other table of people so their service was prompt. More importantly, the pho was DELICIOUS! Good pho is hit or miss, and theirs was definitely a hit. I will say the price was a bit more than I'm used to paying. While this wasn't bad, I'm gonna try out some other pho places to see if there are any better options.
I tried the location on Magazine in about 2013 and wasn't impressed. Decided to take another stab but this time at this one. Turned out much better than the first time. Would definitely recommend it.

I came here for dinner with a group of 7. We all seemed to like our food, as everyones plates were pretty clean. I got the oven roasted meatballs - Soutzoukakia. I was originally going to get fish but was told it would take 30 minutes (my only complaint). The food we did order was relatively fast though. The service is really good. They came frequently to refill water. It was also BYOB. The waiters were friendly even though we weren't the easiest group to deal with. As soon as we sat down, baskets of bread were brought over. The food was filling, so we didn't have room for dessert. They were also accommodating and let us pay with several credit cards. 3.5 stars for this place.

The poor customer service and cheap owner will make you think twice about eating here. They do have healthy options... but so does Lucky Dill. I recommend eating elsewhere - if they make your sandwich wrong, do not expect them to make you the correct one. Wrong sandwich twice. Promised a credit, so ordered again, and was going to pay for one and get the other free as promised. Got there. They "changed their minds" and never made the sandwiches.. said they would call to see if I still wanted it, but forgot - it got too busy. Really, Dooners? So I opted to pay since I was Already there - and they got the second sandwich wrong. A chicken souvlaki with bacon? This place is going downhill.
Very good in taste, friendly staff and a good bar counter.! Good place to hang out till late night.

The companies lawyer came by and said lets go to lunch. I knew where we were going because he has a serious like of Spiro's. So here we go. I wanted to order the Gyros but I can't spell tzatziki. I flipped the lunch menu to the back and saw what I wanted. The Lamb Shank. Since I am over 60 and there are rules about soup and 60 I started with the Greek lemon chicken soup. Then the lamb shank came out. It was not a shank it was darn near a whole leg of lamb. Served with rice and vegetables. I wish I did not get the soup because the shank was more than enough. Wonderful flavor cooked to beyond belief tenderness. Yes I ate it all and I am glad. I get to Spiro;s about once a year and I wanted to enjoy every last bit of the shank. The usual great service came with the usual great food. I think this place is every bit as good or better as any Greek place I have been to in Chicago.

On Whyte Avenue. Middle eastern food. Place was quiet. Ordered a donair and asked for onions, taziki sauce and peppers. To go. Had no onions and sweet sauce instead. A lot of lettuce filler and light. A donair should have some weight to it. Not happy.

Ugh. Let me share that I had high hopes for this visit. Moving to St. Louis nearly a year ago from Jersey where Cuban restaurants are plentiful, I've really missed the cuisine. Oh, and with a name like "Raul," it's not hard to guess that I know a thing or two about Cuban food. Hehe. When we walked in, around 6:10pm, only 1 other table was seated. We sat, looked at the menu and instantly knew what we wanted to order. Pollo a la plancha (grilled chicken) with white rice, black beans and tostones (fried green plantains)...and Bistec de Palomilla (grilled streak) with white rice, black beans and maduros (fried sweet plantains). After a short wait (around 15 minutes), our food arrived to the table. Instantly I knew this was going to be different. The Bistec de Palomilla was thick (not thin) and sorta curled on itself (as if it was fighting while cooked, LOL). Lots of greasy onions topped it and I'm guessing garlic with other seasoning was all around it. I didn't let the appearance bother me and cut a piece quickly as I was anxious to taste the familiar flavor...but that didn't happen. In addition to the ordered entree, a scoop of what I gathered must've been spinach was on the plate. I tried it and found it absolutely repulsive. I quickly scooped it off my plate and placed it into the empty bowl where my black beans were being housed (before I drenched them over my rice). The rice was barely warm and the beans were a massive disappointment. The maduros, eh. Not great either. The Pollo a la plancha also had onions...but they were pickled onions which was different but they didn't enhance the entree. The chicken was a split open chicken breast but rather small and lacked flavor. Another disappointment. By 6:30 I was asking for the check and we left the restaurant. I really expected the visit to be different and to be so much better (hoping it would knock my socks off)...but it simply wasn't. Reading some of the 5 star reviews here, I really thought I'd find my new weekly must-have. Damn. Oh...and near the end of our meal, a cook or possibly the owner came out of the kitchen, sipping water and staring directly at us. It was mad creepy. I'm only mentioning it here and not holding that against the overall rating... Hope your experience is better. I might try this place after a few months (if it's still in business). Shame.
Most likely the nicest owners of an establishment I've met. They are so caring and will go very much out of the way for you. I love the Pad See Ew, and my boss always has the roasted duck.

I like this place for lunch because it's fast and good and peaceful. I always order the green curry dish, and I always ask for it to be spicy. Hot really isn't very spicy but that's just me. Let's meet for lunch. :)
1st and second time awesome ...looking for authentic cuisine while in Indiana ... Can't wait for third visit hopefully tomorrow

If you're looking for standard Azn food then Vientiane Cafe is the place to rock out to. It's a quaint BYO with a menu customizable to any palate. Standard options such as noodles, rice, curries and vegetable stir fries accompanied by your choice of meat, tofu or more veggies abound. No one will leave disappointed...even if they only eat the sticky rice. Because everybody loves perfect sticky rice. The green papaya salad is scrumptious, even without peanuts. This is where Vientiane lays claim to other Asian establishments: peanut allergy? No worries. They'll make sure those little goobers don't infiltrate any part of your dish...even offering to box a separate papaya salad only after learning of a food allergy. Nice.

Delicious, flavorful, and incredibly fresh! The owners couldn't be nicer. Very friendly and truly passionate about serving their customers the very best. Best plantains around! I'd also recommend the shrimp arepaz with the guacamole salsa. Yum!

The food and service was fabulous ! My friend had the orange chicken and egg drop soup I had beef lo me in and the special flatbread they make fresh there. Absolutely one of a kind . Several patrons were locals so I knew we were in for a real treat !

This place might serve good Thai food by 1979 standards (although I'd disagree with that too), but it's not authentic. Having been to numerous excellent Thai restaurants in the US as well as in Thailand, the food I was served at Thailand Restaurant was not good. The best thing about the place was the decor, which was 1979 Thai appropriate. But the food -- no thank you. It has been horribly Americanized, but not in any sort of tasty way. The fried shrimp is wrapped in turkey bacon. Ew. Bacon makes everything better, but turkey bacon does not. The egg rolls are not delicate at all. Sauces were generic. The tom yum gai was lacking the usual bite, unless you count a metallic taste as bite. I asked for medium spiciness, but the food I received was bland. I didn't know how curry could be bland and salty at the same time. The best thing about this place is that they have Singha and Chang beer and come around frequently to offer another bottle.
Great addition to the neighborhood. Pork is awesome, get it anyway they serve it. Lamb Pita is phenomenal!

Food was fresh! Duck fried rice was so good. I usually order "thai hot" when I eat thai food but decided to go with just hot. Be careful when you order the hot as it is flaming hot. Probably hotter than thai hot at other places. Enjoy!

Horrible service avoid this place! We went on a Sunday night. They had 3 people working 1 bartender, 1 working the entire floor and 1 guy doing coals. We had one that was ok. They are very inconsistent with their mixes (too much mint not enough "insert flavor"). We ordered a second one, it came with 0 coals. We waited about 10 minutes, the server/manager on duty finally came over and she said it wouldn't be more than 5 minuets on the coals. Well 20 minuets later still nothing. So we decided to leave. They tried to charge us for the second one that we didn't smoke. The manager was very rude. Told us we had to pay for it. I told her no way. She took it off. Threw my change at me and then told the guy in the waiting area (yes waiting area) come with me want a free hookah. Never once explained why we never got coals, never apologized, never said why it took 30 minuets to get a drink. I'd venture a little further out and avoid this place.

Had the Pho without noodles because I'm off da flour stuff. The broth was delicious! I had Pho in Vancouver last and this was so much better! Bummed I couldn't eat the noodles but super happy with the broth. I do wish the had more vegies to throw in since I couldn't get noodles it would have helped round out the meal since there was not alot more I could order. However, I'm on a special food plan so I will suggest people go when they are not so they can have the full food experience!

You'll have to walk by all the other lunch trucks in Drexel's lunch truck alley to get to Cucina Zapata. Resist the temptation to go to the questionable chinese truck and even the awesome greek guys to try this place out! My favorite meal is the sweet potato curry which is so filling and only $5! You get huge chunks of potato and chicken on a bed of rice in a unbelievably sweet and savory curry sauce. The tacos are not to be missed either my favorite being the korean bbq. Another gem is the captain crunch crusted tilapia burrito. Amazing! I'm a messy eater so I steer clear of the burrito which I would make a complete mess of and stick with the curry that is eaten with a fork. Great guys run the truck. Just be ready to wait!

If, one day, you find yourself in the little hamlet known as Bryn Mawr, PA, and are looking to try something different, then I encourage you to stop where you are!! Then, pull out your phone and type "Ekta Indian Cuisine" in the search bar. Follow those directions, and before you know it, you will soon find yourself in India! Well, not really, but the food that they are serving up, will arguably have you feeling that you are. You might recall that I had recently discovered vegetarian cuisine, so as I sat down at Ekta, I began to ponder their veggie options. After, what felt like eons, I finally settled on the cashew rolls to start and the Kadai Paneer as an entree. Man, they were so dang good...just, WOW!!!

Absolutely awesome service! I am on crutches and had to wait for my ride to come get me so I stopped in this restaurant. He filled up my drink, brought my food, and gave me a refill all without me having to get up. He didn't even leave me an option to leave him a tip. I highly recommend this restaurant for the service and food. Try the hummus!
Amazing service!!! Food was really good, except the crab cakes... they used artificial crab meat which was disappointing.

Excellent. Had the fresh rolls. The sauce was just perfect with the rolls that included great lettuce. For an entree we had the chicken sizzling platter. The plate came out "sizzling". The peanut sauce was light and flavorful. The veggies included broccoli and spinach. A generous sprinkling of cashews added some crunch to the dish. Overall a tasty meal enjoyed with Thai iced coffee. Would definitely come here again.

This place is amazing. I came here on Saturday night with my boyfriend for the first time. The service was impeccable, we were seated within minutes. The food was delicious. They have a great dinner combination for a great price. The owners are very personable and welcoming. They both came up to us at the end of our meal and made sure we were completely satisfied with our meal. We will definitely be coming back here. Thanks Siam Elephant!
Great carry out. Hot, tasty, clean restaurant, pleasant staff.

Good food, family owned, we're regulars here and the owner always recognizes us. 2 things to keep in mind. 1. Be patient with the owner or wife when taking your order. 2. It takes a little while to get the food, (15-20minutes) but since he makes it from scratch it's worth it. I recommend the #35 Pad Thai and #13: spicy pho soup

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Great location. We arrived and were seated immediately -- there were only two other diners in the restaurant. The positive comments end there. We ordered drinks, an appetizer and entrees all at the same time. Drinks (beer) and appetizer arrived 5 minutes later -- pedestrian, but acceptable. We had to ask for silverware. 75 minutes later (yes, you read that correctly,) having never been visited by our hostess or waiter, our food still hadn't arrived, and we had to ask to have it packed up to go. When we arrived home, having spent $65 for the full meal, our food resembled nothing that we had ordered. The four tiny wedges of garlic naan (the menu listed it as "nawn", why I have no idea,) had no garlic, and looked as if it had been baked a week before; the tandoori chicken, which consisted of four dry drumsticks resting on a bed of charred but raw onions and peppers, was flavorless; the paneer biriyani had no paneer (3 pieces?) nor sauce, and lacked the add-on raisins and nuts that we had paid for. The experience was an absolute and utter fiasco. We will never EVER return, nor will we EVER recommend this establishment. Our disappointment is beyond words -- to the point that we are considering checking with the credit card company about withholding payment -- something that we have never done before. Just. Terrible.

Walked into an empty restaurant (red flag) and began looking at the menu. Excited to try some of the street food. Unfortunately this didn't happen. A dude came out to greet me and immediately made me feel uncomfortable. After he tried to flirt with me left and right I decided to leave. He pressured me to stay and continued to follow me outside and even watched me dive away!!! Totally unprofessional and I don't know if I'll come back here again. Cultural appreciation can be found through the joy of food and this behavior caused me to go somewhere else to eat.

Horrible service! I walked in w/ my kids. No one bother to welcome us. A moment later, the waitress just waved us down and pointed at any random table (or maybe she was just fanning herself to keep cool, who knows?). She handed us menus and walked away without offering any beverages. About 20+ minutes pass and none of the workers were on the floor for me to wave down to take my order. I don't know what was happening in the kitchen because there were only a couple customers who also seemed impatient themselves for their orders. I really wanted to try this place out, but my kids were too hungry to sit & wait that long to eat, so we left.

Best Mediterranean food in the area hands down! Too bad I have to drive all the way to Lenox Village to eat there. The place is a little odd inside. Only a few tables to sit at. It's never busy when we go, so we've always had a table. I've met the owner and he is from Jordan. His background is probably the reason this place is a little different than the usual Greek inspired Mediterranean establishments. Get the Plato's Delight appetizer, which is edamame, corn, garlic, and red pepper sautéed in white wine and spices, drizzled with tahini sauce. It's amazing! I usually get the duo plate with chicken and gyro meat. The gyro meat here always melts in your mouth. So good! We have begged for them to open up a second location in Cool Springs. We can dream, right? In the meantime, we'll make the drive every so often here because it's so worth it!

Momo's food is very good. However, the wait staff deserve maybe one star. This is my second experience with the same result, different waitress each time. On my most recent visit, the waitress threw things on the table to us, even when one of us was close to her. When she asked a question and didn't get an immediate answer, she stalked off. Too bad, because we like their food. Just don't want to tolerate that kind of behavior.

Stopped here for lunch on our way to Valley Forge. Food was really good - large portions. Everyone was super friendly except for the one gal actually making our bowls. Clearly we hadn't been there before and she seemed super impatient.

Been here three times now and the food is always great. Dinner service is prompt and reasonably attentive without being overbearing. Food quality is excellent with a nice mix of "americanized" Indian and more authentic dishes. Kitchen staff is willing to customize spiciness to individual tastes but tend to overstate the level of heat. Lunch buffet is OK but the quality is a bit lower than dinner but certainly priced right. Definitely a return customer.

The Subs are done well here, that also goes for the boba. As for the other items on the menu like Bo kho, pho and others they are not that great. Timing is also not that great. I ordered everything and sat there like an idiot while people who came after me got theirs and left. I tried the Bo kho and the soup was Luke warm. Took about 20+mins to het three subs made. Pick up the pace people!

We have been coming to Meun Fan for 5 years. I am not sure if the ownership has changed recently or if I have never met the owner before but I had a very unpleasant interaction with him last week. He was extremely rude and agitated, not only to myself but also to the staff. It was enough to make us not want to go back. It is too bad because everyone else that works there is very friendly and helpful, and the food is great.

Wait staff doesn't appear to have any interest in customer service. They communicate with a series of grunts or one word responses, and will not be there to check in on you. If you want a water refill, you'll need to go and wait at the front until somebody notices you to ask for it. Doesn't appear to be the most hygienic place either. That being said, the pho is always really tasty and the price is very decent for the portion size you get. Take out is a better option.

Horrible experience the first time. Ran out of chips for our spinach & artichoke dip and requested a few more. Server brought back a bowl full and we graciously accepted only to find out later he charged us $4 or $5 for it without telling us first. We felt very cheated. Our food was also made wrong (we requested our gyros without olives and onions). When our food finally came out, both were on our dishes. When I said something to our waiter, he picked them up without apologizing and took them to the kitchen. They were returned to us having looked like they'd been picked through and I still found a few straggler black olives. A few months later we decided to try again, our waitress ignored us, never asked us about our food, and never filled our drinks up. After these two experiences, my boyfriend and I will not return. The food is pretty good, but id rather go elsewhere for better service. If you go, look forward to crummy service.
Had dinner tonight. Great and delicious veggie bowl! And the fries are awesome! And the owner made a point to thank me for coming. I will be back!!

Found this rare gem on Yelp while visiting Tampa from NY, I must say when I saw a 4.5 star on Yelp for a Caribbean Restaurant l, I had to try it out. I was definitely blown away, the ambience was amazing, the decor was beautiful and elegant. The owner/waiter was courteous, friendly and was just an all around exceptional waiter. We had the beef patty to start off and it was delicious, then we had the taste of the Caribbean and bread pudding for dessert. Everything was just delicious and presentation was beautiful as well. I would definitely recommend this place.

So..a close friend of mine one day said "Hey paison, have a great time in Italy, maybe we're related" "What, why would you say that, where is your family from originally". Him: Sicily. Me: oh, like I said I'm Italian so probably not :). If you never make it to Sicily, or the less pretentious part of of the boot, a short trip from the city or Jersey burbs here is well worth it. Yes it's small, yes it's loud. Picture Sunday pasta at moms, crushing tomatoes, rolling dough and running it through the pasta maker, all while your great aunt is pinching your cheeks and screaming in your ear. All kidding aside, this remained one of the few spots in Collingswood I hadn't tried. (Best of Philly Italian In Collingswood?) (Vetri eyes rolls). A wise man once told me his best advice on Italy was the farther north, the more beautiful the women, and the lousier the food. The farther south, well...that's Zeppoli. What a great gem of a BYOB. Close to authentic cuisine from a clearly passionate well pedigreed kitchen delivering refined comfort food at great prices. There's been enough reviews of individual plates but be sure to hit up some pasta and seafood fare. Shout out to my brother for picking up the tab on our chefs tasting for eight. Go with a Sangiovese, Chianti Classico or my personal favorite that could touch every dish a nice Rosso Piceno (Total Wine has several 12-15$) Comparably, if your this side of the bridge and its a choice from the other Italian spots nearby, or what I will call Osteria -1 in Moorestown, do yourself a solid and let this serve as a measuring stick
For having a limited menu, the food was average at best. The mussels and clams were not tasty at all and did not taste fresh.

This is our favorite Thai place in Philly, and that's saying a lot because my husband is a huge green curry snob. :) Erawan is the only restaurant I've ever heard him say does green curry just like Thailand. Great service, large space. We've tried the pad thai, drunken noodle, green curry and red curry -- all very good. The thai ice tea and mango sticky rice dessert are also very good. We'll be back!

I got a Gyro here late Saturday night recently. Within an hour of eating it I was throwing up. Food poisoning completely ruined me for 2 full days. Had eaten here with no issues perhaps 10 times previously, but thats not a good enough ratio.

Good fast cheap authentic. I like everything I have tried on the menu. Having tried most of the other Viet place around there, and Kien Giang remains one of my favorites. While some will mention the service when reviewing, it as always been adequate for me. Remember they are closed on mondays, and they do not take plastic. Get the pancake, the ice coffee, or the Bánh mì. The bread is baked in house. And of course the Pho is better than any i have had in town.

My husband and I have been to this Thai restaurant many many times. Their food has been consistent in quality. Their attention to little details like fresh flower in a basin at the door and in the lady's room definitely is good sign. My favorite is their curry dishes. Very very authentic.

I pretty much always start with pho at any new Vietnamese restaurant I try to gauge what I should expect from the rest of the menu and I wasn't too impressed. However, I like the extensive drink/dessert menu, but I haven't tried desserts yet so I can't comment on that. I started with the spring roll appetizer, nothing extraordinary either, not something I would order again. I can make it better myself at home. I also ordered the banh mi and taro boba. I was pleasantly surprised that those two were amazing! Honestly, with the pho being a letdown I wasn't expecting much from the sandwich, but wow..banh mi and drinks are the way to go here! And it's a cute laidback little place.
Philly has amazed us with food, but scannicchios was food for the gods! Every plate within our party of six took us on a trip through Italy... We can't wait to go back!!!

Just as good as their original location down the street. Their penang curry is a bit runny. It should have a thicker consistency when cooled down, like a smooth bisque or tomato soup. But the flavor is delicious!
Ethiopian. Slow service, no one spoke English except our water spoke some. Food slightly over cooked Not too our taste.

Traveling through the midwest I thought I would checkout this Pho place based on its great reviews. I consider myself somewhat of a pho connessuer. This review is for the Pho Dac Biet. Overall I would give this bowl of pho a score of 5 out of 10 possible. Broth had decent flavor but did not last the duration of the meal. The noodles quickly absorbed the flavor. Noodles were too soft and absorbent. I prefer the noodles that do not continue to cook in the broth and get softer and absorb all the broth. Veggies were fresh and tasted good. Meat trimmings were ok. The flank had marbled cartilage which normally I like but this particular meat had an off flavor I didn't care for. Tripe was cooked just right. The meatballs were good flavor but too soft in texture. They should be very firm. There was NO tendon in my Dac Biet! Tendon is a MUST! Not sure why it was not offered in the dish. Lastly, the soup needs to be served HOT. No excuses. This was hot but not piping. Combine all these factors and you have a decent bowl of pho but not excellent. This is the only place within 15 miles of another pho place. Worth a try.

I'm not sure what happened to this restaurant since the other people here reviewed it, but my husband and I had an awful experience there today. The food was at best - fair, but the service was absolutely HORRENDOUS! We arrived at about 2pm for lunch. The place was freezing, I suspect they did not have their heat on at all. The place was practically empty. There were 3 other tables in use, one left as we sat down. Our server could not have been less busy. He sat us and gave us menus, but took at least 5 minutes to come back to us to even ask what we wanted to drink. When he did come back we'd already decided what to eat so we gave him our entire order. We came for lunch, but the menu was obviously a dinner menu. We asked if there was a lunch menu and he said no. Neither of us were hungry for an entire meal, so we each ordered 2 appetizers (spinach pie), and an Israeli salad to share. I ordered a cup of hot tea. TEN MINUTES LATER my tea came, and 2 glasses of tepid water. We asked then when our food was coming out and were told a couple minutes. 10 MINUTES LATER our food came. Our 2 plates of spinach pie came in 3 squares each. 2 of our 3 squares were lukewarm and obviously had been sitting for quite some time, with the crust being rather tough and chewy. The 3rd square appeared to have just come out of an oven. Let me repeat, we each had 3 squares, 2 of which were old and one was new-er. I have had and I have made an Israeli salad before, this was not one. It was mashed roasted eggplant with cucumber, tomato and onion chopped into it. The texture was odd. The spinach pie was as good as any you might buy frozen and put into the toaster oven. Almost 1/2 an hour waiting for appetizers and a salad in an empty restaurant. As we were finishing up, our server came by and asked if I wanted more tea. I said, just a little more hot water would be fine. He took my cup away and it was another 3 minutes before I got HOT WATER. While we were eating, a party of about 5 or 6 came in, sat down, got ignored for 5 minutes, said it was cold in there, and LEFT! Perhaps this place is going out of business, already had their heat shut off, their cooks quit, and they just don't give a sh-t anymore. I read other reviewers state the prices were good - maybe for New Hope, but I thought it was pricey. $16 for 2 plates of spinach pie, $10 for a salad, and $3 for a cup of tea. We could've had a couple of big sandwiches and a beer at Havana up the street for that price! We will never go back.

Yelp was down one night so my girlfriend and I decided to come here blindly. She went with the tonkatsu ramen, which was a very generous serving for 13 dollars. The egg and pork was amazing. In contention as the best ramen in town, up there with Kauboi Izakaya. I got sizzling sole fish, a dish I've never tried before. I expected something crunchy and salty, but instead I got a curry-like dish, served with rice. The flavors were really good. At 16 dollars, the portion was a good size, and I ate pretty much all of it. I also ordered some Thai ice tea, which is freshly made for every order. Very good, I would highly recommend it. Overall, good experience! Would've liked the atmosphere to be busier on a Friday night, but that's hardly the fault of the restaurant.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: This place is easy to miss. It's literally a hole in the wall place. However, they serve bold authentic food. My husband and I love the biryani and Lahori charga. But each and every item I have tried here was simply finger licking good. I did try the buffet once and wasn't very impressed, since they didn't have their famous biryani on the menu. The owner is super nice and makes you feel at home all the time. There is one staff member however who is rude and obnoxious, and seems like he would rather be doing something else than this. If he is taken out of the picture, the place is a must try!

I love this place. We've eaten here numerous times, both as a family and with out of town guests. The food is always amazing and getting to share dishes is always an added bonus. The service is always good and we've never had to wait to get a table. Hopefully my review won't make the place so busy that that becomes a problem! The place itself isn't much to look at from the outside which may concern some folks. Nothing to be concerned about though. The interior is lovely and the food is awesome!

i been to mint modern twice now and its pretty cool there. the atmosphere is nice, very modern-like decor. the lemongrass chicken with vermicelli was good. i've never had the pho yet, surprisingly, bc i always order pho, but my friend who had dinner recently with me said it was good. the porkbelly bun was good. nice and hot, pork belly was crispy and just melts in your mouth with every bite. it was an okay experience to be honest. shoutout to the chef, jason, coolest dude ever!

Ong is the latest fried chicken joint to open up in town. This one specializes in Hanoi style fried chicken and is owned by the same crew that runs Jack's Burger Shack and Cerdo Tacos. We came on a Wednesday for lunch and I was surprised to see it wasn't busy. A couple families and that was it. The murals on the wall are interesting; I liked the Vietnamese farmer working the field with his ox but the village behind the counter is also pretty. The menu is small with them focusing on half a dozen items. - Banh mi ($7.00) - decent and even had a nice kick to it; sadly, it's a small and average. Go to Chinatown and get one for $4.00 instead. - Pho sot vang ($9.00) - this was the best dish we ordered. Hearty, homemade, comforting broth that I imagine your Vietnamese mom/grandma would cook for you. The beef was tender, juicy and you get a plethora of noodles. Perfect to share; just ask for an extra bowl. - 2 piece chicken ($13.00) - the thigh was moist and flavourful but the breast was quite dry. We liked the sweet, sticky sauce but I thought they could have used more of a bread coating. The side of rice is tinnyyyyyyyy. For the price tag, you'd think they wouldn't be so stingy. It's plain rice...yeesh. Overall, decent but everything is a few dollars overpriced. At least St. Albert is slowly getting more ethnic restaurants so chalk that up in the plus column.
One of the best Thai food places in Nashville. Fresh vegetables and great curry. I have been back several times and love it every time.

My girlfriend and I have searched for a good thai food place in the city. So far this is the best one. The curry that I ordered came with fresh vegetables that were crunchy and sweet from the curry base. My girlfriend had the ginger fish which tasted tangy, spicy, and sweet. We both found the appetizer the best part: crunchy tofu sticks. I would definitely recommend this for the person looking for Thai food in uptown.

Went to Soco Gyros for the first time today. The staff was very friendly and professional. The menu was organized and simple. I had a blackened chicken wrap and it was delicious. I also had the red pepper hummus and pita, easily the best I have had! I was very pleased with this great little gem!

really like this place, we've eaten here a number of times and it is always good. We've tried the gyro, lamb and falafel sandwiches and recently I had the gyro salad. All of these are good. Get the fries with it, they are thin potato slices with great seasoning on them. I've seen dishes that other people have ordered and that all looked super tasty too! check this place out.

When Fulins first came to Mount Juliet, I was thrilled. Food was fresh, tasty and the lines on weekends were out the door. Over the past 10 years +\-, the food has gotten worse and worse. Tonight we visited again-one thing I ordered was seaweed salad. It tasted like dead, old fish. Used to be sweeter/fresher. My husband had pork lomein. He had about 1/4 of it. No so good. Not so much pork. We have tried to continue eating there, mostly because it's convenient. Tonight was our last visit. Prices were fine, service fine. Food pretty lousy.

Great Cuban food north of FL! The camarones al ajillo (shrimp in garlic sauce) is wonderful - soak some of that delicious golden bread with the sauce and you'll be in heaven. Fantastic ropa vieja, and the maduros are nice and sweet like they should be. Friendly service, good beer list if a bit uninspired, but more than enough. More than once I've found myself wanting to try a different place in New Hope but I pass by here and can't help myself.

I had some really good authentic falafel here and the guy fried it fresh from the batter for each order. You get to pick what toppings (salads) go in your pita and say how much and he puts them in. I re-heated my falafel pita later and it was still JUST as amazing, if not moreso! Definitely better than Maoz, where you make your own. The falafel tastes better and doesn't upset my stomach. Also, I can't put a pita together like the professionals here, with their fancy paring knives cutting the pita all fancy and neat and not making it overflow or rip. I just can't do that. So I get something yummy and stay neat too. Neat-o. (*sigh* how I love gratuitous-ness-ness). Anyway, It was very very yummy and authentic. This is now my go-to place on south street for hummus and falafel treats.

I'd give it at 3.5 if I could. I can count on one hand how many times I've given a place 5 stars. But since there are no halves, 3.5 rounds up to 4, hence the 4 stars. Anyhow. My husband and I arrived there just before noon on a Saturday. We were the only ones in the restaurant. There was only one person working at the time. A few min (maybe 10) later, another 2 people came in. The hostess/waitress/cook came over to take our order...but only to have us write down our own order on an envelope because she said something about having to be in the kitchen (very hard to understand her). She then went to the other table to have THEM write their order as well so she could hurry back to the kitchen. While we were waiting for our sampler appetizer another table came in and thankfully 2 more people came in to work. I always read reviews and noticed they were very slow and short-staffed. Once they arrived things started to get a little better. We got our appetizer but was told that it was missing an item and to just eat what they brought out and that they would bring out the other item later. Well we got our main course and half way through, I realized we never got the rest of our appetizer. I waved someone down to let them know and she eventually brought it out. After eating, we sat for about 10-15 min or so, waiting for our check. Like other reviews, we had to flag someone down for that as well, despite them walking by and us not eating. The food was excellent though, thankfully, as this was their saving grace. We ordered the appetizer sampler for 2, the Queen's Eight, and Ethiopia's main dish (I don't recall the name). It was all VERY good and I would def go back, now I know what to expect. Give it a chance, as long as you have ample time to do so!!

It wasn't a pleasant experience. We left even before we got our food, that's how bad it was. We decided to dine in and we were still choosing the food from the menu. The server gave our drinks which we haven't opened yet (they were Coke bottles). We went there because we remember going to our relatives house and they served fried chicken and Lo mein which they said they ordered from Bamboo House and we really liked it. That's why we wanted to order it but we couldn't find which chicken it was from the menu. So the server said she will ask because we remember it was fried chicken and it was all drumsticks but she said they do have it but they are all wings. So the manager went to our table to follow up on our order, she was kind of in a hurry and talks really rude. I was also making sure that the Lo Mein we were about to order does not have shrimps because I'm allergic to it. Then next thing we know, while we were giving our order, she just said, "Faster hurry up, we're busy!" But it was only us who were there! So my husband asked her, "why are you getting mad?" And she said, "we're busy on the phones!" But there was one person taking orders on the phone already. And the manager just left our table! How rude! So we just decided to leave and hand the drinks back to them. We got mad too! This is unbelievable. Horrible customer service. If there is -500 star rating, we will give it. It pains me to give them 1 star, they don't even deserve it. Stay away from this place.

Absolutely beautiful interior. I cannot wait for the outdoor patio to open in the nicer weather, which I heard would be a beer garden. I've only eaten the pastries and hummous but I'm looking forward to going back for the market items. While waiting on line, a nice woman in front of me recommended the chai latte and I can't imagine drinking anything else. It's a gorgeous drink with a lovely taste. The jalousie and cruller were gobbled up. We're really looking forward to when they extend hours

First step in the door and I knew this was the place!! It smelt so good. We had a happy welcome from the owner who was happy to see us. Wonderful costumer service. He suggested some things and we are so happy we tried them. I will be back!!

I would like to give them 3.5 stars, but I'll round it up to 4. I've wanted to go here for a long time, but just never made it. I went on a Wednesday night, and it was empty. I guess its probably more of a take out place during the week, but it was nice out and I wanted to sit outside. The waitress promptly offered ice water and a corkscrew for the wine I brought. We ordered a chicken patty, beef patty, and both got the jerk chicken breast. The patties were really good, and much bigger than I thought they would be. They were pretty promptly wrapped up to eat another day. The chicken platters were pretty large. I appreciated the quality of the chicken, lots of white meat, not a lot of mystery parts.
