I'm not a jerk spice expert, but I have had it in Jamaica and other areas of the Caribbean. I think this was a little spicier than I typically have had it, but it wasn't too spicy. I think there could have been a little more sweetness, but I was pleasantly surprised by the flavor as this place gets pretty middling reviews. The rice was good too, and I love the plantains. I think we probably had half a plantain each. Next time I would probably order a couple really well done ones on the side. The only thing I didn't like was the cabbage. I think a cold salad would be better given the heat of the chicken. The service was fine. We got there around 7:30, and left at 9. I did not feel like we were waiting a long time for the food, and our waitress occasionally stopped by to see if we needed anything. I definitely plan on returning on the weekend to check out the live music, and I'll probably be back for take out.
Could not be more pleased! The food was absolutely amazing and our waiter was the best!! We dined outside and had such a wonderful time! We will definitely make this a "go-to" when in town

I LOVE the sandwich here. The bread tastes like it just came from the oven. I think they make their own bread right there. And it's so reasonable, like $5, but it still fills your stomach well! Also Baba ghannouj is the most delicious one I ever had!

This restaurant was out of this world! Our waitress Dusty was fabulous and very friendly and prompt. The food, I cannot praise it enough. The rice was perfectly cooked and the pesto sauce was creamy and delightfully seasoned. The salad had the best dressing and I added shrimp which had been grilled to perfection! To say nothing of the margaritas! Would definitely come here again.

JUST OK.....Went in at 3:30 on a Saturday and literally everything I went to order they were out of. So that was frustrating. Foods average. Not really one of my go to places for Thai food in the area. Servers aren't the friendliest either. Just meh...
Tried them on South Grand Dine Around night. Rangoon was delicious. Wish they offered something else to get more of a taste. They were also very fast which was a big plus.

This slop is different and tasty, and the price is right! I'm a sauce guy and I was a big fan of the sauces that came on the appetizer (Ashak - scallion dumps with sauce) and the eggplant vegetarian entree. They aren't quite as rich, creamy, and spicy as Indian gravies, but they're good. The bread is excellent as well, almost as good as Indian naan. Don't get the special yogurt drink. In fairness, the server warned me, but it smacks of salty jizzum. Every item is under 10 bucks. Service was friendly.
GREAT Happy Hour! Super flatbreads at amazingly low prices and low wine and beer deals. We'll return!

Oh my! First time eating here. The food was absolutely delicious!! The name certainly fits the description of the food,"pleasant savory taste"! We will certainly be back!! Nice atmosphere and awesome service!
Long wait. Rude staff. Bad food that tastes worse than what you get from a halal food truck at twice the price. Will never come back.
I really like their Paneer appetizer. Customer service is excellent! They'll make sure you're satisfied with your food :)

Haven't eaten there. Prob won't either bc nothing on the menu looks like it wld appeal to me. Went for the drinks tho- and those were superb! I don't mind paying $8 and up for a mixed drink as long as you are going to make it a DRINK. I like alcohol--Don't judge me. My drinks were strong and the beers were cold. It's a visually appealing place w comfortable seating in and out. Great place for a date and enjoy some drinks which chatting on Beach Dr or a group of friends to drink and catch up. Drink up!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This is hands-down some of the best Indian food I have ever eaten. Every dish is prepared for you, fresh. You might be thinking "hey, aren't all dishes prepared for you after you order them?". This is different. They make the dishes from scratch when you order it. And you can tell. I have been here several times and every time it has been absolutely amazing. They have a wide variety of dishes from vegan, to vegetarian, to full of meats. I was able to get a curried goat dish here most recently and, while it was a bit boney, the flavor and texture (not the bones, of course) were incredible. They also have a very good wine and beer list which means you'll be able to find a beverage that perfectly complements whatever you have ordered. I would make some recommendations on what to order, but you're going to be pleased with whatever you get. Seriously. It is definitely worth visiting.

Excellent Indian fare, with a nice buffet of vegetarian and meat dishes, including curried goat, butter chicken, tandoori chicken, palak paneer, gobi aloo, dal, and pakoras, as well as several other less common dishes. I enjoyed the variety of desserts that went beyond gulab jamun and kheer to include mango custard, some sweet carrot dish I'd never seen before, and a round, white pastry that looked like a jamun, but wasn't. (I didn't care for it, but was glad for the opportunity to at least try it.) They also offered pani puri, a street food that was new to me, and masala tea included in the buffet. So, we experienced a wide variety of dishes, many of which were extraordinary--at least for me--and many that appealed to my vegetarian husband. Delicious naan. Excellent service; clean restroom. Lunch for two cost $24. Absolutely worth it.
Superb atmosphere, outstanding service, and great food. We live on the southside of Indy and this is well worth the drive to Avon for us. We will be back!
The best in town. I eat at this place 3 times a week and habe never had a problem. Try the number ten

After first enjoying Naf Naf while visiting Chicago, we had little hope that such awesome food would find its way to our area. Imagine how amazed we were to find this almost brand new location in KoP! An outstanding but simple menu, our favorite is the shawarma in a hummus bowl (with extra hummus). The additions, including purple cabbage, pickles and sumac onions are then improved with one of several fantastic sauces, with tahini our usual choice. Finally, we cannot say enough about the fresh baked pita!!!! A real treat.

Went for lunch. It is in walking distance of Touro. The Uptown location. Anyway, with the lunch special you get egg drop soup, fried rice, and egg roll, and then your main dish. I got sweet and sour chicken. Add a water, and with a $3 tip you can get the sweet and sour chicken lunch with a good tip for under $12. The service was good but you will need to ask for Chopsticks. They have TVs.

I love Simple Thai, always clean , servers are nice , food is Awesome! !! I love there tea so delicious! !! Building is smaller than most restaurants but who cares I have never had to wait. I suggest everyone go and try it out !!!

It's nice to have a good restaurant within walking distance of your home. It took too long for us to give Olio a try, but I'm glad we finally did. While they did not offer their usual menu, the service was pretty good and the location is great so we will be back. We went with a cheese and charcuterie plate to go along with a couple of flights of wine. The one real positive out of this dinner was I found out that I'm not a fan of Sherry after trying their Sherry flight with dessert. I am intrigued by their menu offerings and can't wait to come back.

Since we first moved to D-Hill in '07, we have been bemoaning the lack of dining variety. Unless we wanted pizza, cheesesteaks, or Chinese food, we had to venture to Media, Ardmore, or Philly for a nice dinner out. So we were THRILLED when Shere-E-Punjab showed up in our backyard. We took ourselves there for an end-of-summer dinner 2 weeks ago. Since it's a BYO, we picked up a bottle at the Township Line wine store beforehand. Wasn't crowded at all (I get the feeling they do a booming take-out service), and our waiter was quick and attentive. We started with Papdi Chat (kind of Indian nachos, for lack of better comparison), samosas, and naan bread. All yummy...but nothing compared to the Chicken Tikka Masala I got for my main course. Unbelievable. I actually ordered more naan to soak up the sauce when I was done. (I made sure to request "mild", which I think made a difference--I was actually able to taste the flavors rather than be scared off by the spiciness.) Everything was reasonably priced, and it really was a nice night out. Yum, yum, yum.

I've taken the special combination with Pad Thai Noodles and soup. The soup was great, slightly spicy and sour. The spring roll, wonton and fried shrimp were okay and the Pad Thai was just delicious. The staff was very friendly and the restaurant itself very nice. I would go there again.

I have been ot Momo's several times, and I have to say that it is easily my favorite place to get Greek with the (vegetarian) lady friend. I have experienced my fair share of Greek restaurants, but none of them have the variety that Momo's has, and none of them are quite as vegetarian-friendly as Momo's is. The atmosphere is pretty interesting, and you have to pass through tapestries/rugs that are hung around the main entrance, which gives it the feel of a Middle Eastern or Mediterranean hookah lounge. The food is delicious, and although I haven't ventured very far outside the standard gyro sandwich, I have had the opportunity to persue the menu, just in case I ever feel like getting something besides my standard choice. Last time we were there, I tried the fallafel, which was quite tasty. It wasn't the best I've ever had, for that honor goes to a little hole-in-the-wall, take-away place in Paris, but it was good. The pita is always soft, warm, and delicious, and the ingredients are always of the utmost freshness and quality. Their tzaziki, which we ordered last time we were there as a stand-alone appetizer, is delicious, and their fallafel itself was also very good. Crispy on the outside, warm and tasty on the inside, it is definitely a close second to my all-time favorite fallafel place in Paris. Their gyro meat and feta cheese will also keep me coming back for more, and their saginaki (flaming cheese), which we get pretty much every time we visit, is similarly delectable. Crispy on the outside, creamy, tangy and stretchy-melty on the inside, and served on fire in a bath of lemon juice, it is just about as good as it gets. The last time we were there, I remarked how if we could get other things that were presented in such a fashion (brought to the table and then lit on fire), I would enjoy that immensely. What a better way to start a meal than with a fire ball brought to your table and a resounding cry of "Opah!" Since we have at least one more groupon for this place (but even if we didn't), we will definitely be returning, and maybe one of the next times, I'll try one of the delicious pastas that caught my eye, or maybe the calimari, which a table next to us had ordered on our most recent visit, and which looked damned tasty. The only unfortunate part about this place is that their baklava, in my opinion, is just not as good as their asking price suggests. I know it's only $6 or so, but for that much money, I expect a little more. It's not bad, but most of the time, we will now forgo it, since we don't feel it's worth the extra money. Luckily, the Cheesecake Factory is close enough that we can stop by there for a piece of delicious cheesecake if our stomachs will allow it. The people who work there are always exceptionally friendly, and the prices are extremely reasonable. They have a full bar complete with a score of interesting-sounding cocktails that will set you back about $8 apeice. They also have capirinhas and mojitos, which I have yet to try, but in which I am extremely interested. The only reason I didn't give Momo's a 5-star rating, and I know some of you will call me a blasphemer, is that I really do not enjoy the belly dancers that seem to be present every time we visit. I know many of you think that they add to the Mediterranean vibe and contribute to the overall atmosphere, but I think they serve as little more than a noisy distraction to my otherwise enjoyable dining experience. I have never once tipped them, which thankfully will usually get them to stop with those god-awful finger cymbals and leave us alone. I prefer to eat without a bunch of noise, and I know I may be in the majority here, but I would like Momo's a lot better if the belly dancers were 86ed. That said, I really do enjoy the food at Momo's and will continue to eat there in the future. I suggest you give them a try, because it really is a unique experience, and the Greek and Mediterranean fare they have to offer make it well worth a visit. Opah!

I LOVE Indian food! This is pretty good and it would be a 4 star for the lunch special/buffet but out of all Indian food I have had it tastes average. BEST mango lassi and okra I have had thus far. Chicken is tender and food had spice. I recommend the chicken tandoor.
fantastic!! Perfect for romantic dinners or meals with family or friends. Delicious traditional Italian everything, a local fav.

I really really enjoy Ekta. I have been here quite a few times over the last few years, and the food never disappoints. The only reason this review is a 4 and not a 5 is the service. I have just been consistently disappointed in the staff, the speed of service, and the general treatment of customers. Most recently, I placed an order for pick-up on a Saturday evening around 6:00pm. I ordered lamb roganjosh and garlic naan. The roganjosh was SPICY, like very spicy; which I love and I really appreciated this day. The naan was fine, nothing special but good for take-out naan. I will be back to Ekta, especially with a smaller group of friends and for BYOB. Also, parking is VERY HARD in Bryn Mawr. Very, very hard. So just get ready to drive around a bit for parking.

I really have mixed feelings about this place. Looks very seedy from the outside but the view is nice. My wife and I got a sitter for our three kids and wanted to spend a quiet sit down dinner together. We went to this place and all our waiter was talking about was the buffet. We didn't really want to do buffet as that meant a quick dinner, which is not what we wanted. After attempting to order from the menu and the waiter saying "but that's on the buffet!!" we relented and got the buffet. The food was only mildly ok. Indian food is supposed to be full of subtle flavors and the heat/spice is supposed to be mixed in with good flavors so it's not just HOT/SPICY. Failed on all counts. The sauces were very thick and heavy and although some packed a punch, spice wise, that was all it was. OMG SPICY!! Not "Wow what a great taste and that heat hits you subtly...then OMG that's SPICY". THAT is really great Indian food. This is not. I've had every dish on the buffet but done MUCH better in other parts of the country. I'm still looking for some GOOD Indian around here. The search continues...
Yo they should change their name to "Straight Fire". Good stuff, IV needed a new joint that actually puts in work.

My husband and I frequent this restaurant I must admit they have good food but in my opinion that is ONLY half of your experience. This last weekend we went with several people and were treated by the MANAGER like we had the plague!!! She was rude and nasty. She ranted at our table for adding extra people to our party saying we "were inconveniencing her staff by having to move tables around!!!" REALLY?! She stormed off. We decided we would leave before we even place our order. BTW--when we left there were a whooping 2 tables that were being used. I felt sorry for the waiter who is actually pretty amazing but he lost close to $60 in tips because of the thoughtless, moronic manager who doesn't have any tact!!!

I live in the Nampa and Caldwell area but I work at the Boise airport. I go 3 or 4 times a week and get 2 of the #2 before I go all the way back home. I have to say this beats all the other sandwich shops. My wife got me into this place and at first I was like NO Way but she didn't eat it all, so i took a piece and was hooked. I hope they make one in the Canyon County Area so I wont have to drive all the way. I strongly recommend this place!
Worst Thai food I've had in the states. Food was sweet and had no authentic flavor to it. And it was completely over priced. Don't waste your time here.

I'm still stinging over my pick up order of almost $50.00 of Chinese Food on Sunday, August 13, 2017 around 5:20 p.m. (they closed at 10pm). When I placed my order, I was told it would be ready in 5 to 10 mins. That should have been my WARNING TO CANCEL. Only 2 entrees were edible: Sichuan Beef and Moo Goo Gai Pan. Every thing else had to have been cooked the day before and reheated or sat on a warming rack all day. Fried chicjen wings were dry. BBQ spare ribs were size of 3rd finger and tough as shoe leather drowned in too sweet sauce. Shrimp rubbery in dry Egg Foo Young. Sichian Wontons were twice cooked with the dough being dry, rubbery and filling tasteless. And, finally, the complimentary crab ragoon was a day old and crust tough. I called the restaurant and told them they just lost a customer. No apology, just "ok" and I wonder if he understood my English at all. 1 star rating is too high. I had to select a star in order to post my review. Go to China Taste on Gandy Blvd. for takeout if you want fresh Chinese food.

Very poor service i would say till date the worst experience i ever had....i called for a deliver and even after 2 and half hours they dint deliver my food and on top of that they charged me for the food and still dint deliver very pooor service
Fantastic! Ordered two veg dishes, naan, papadum, shrimp appetizer. Each dish was delicious. Can't wait to return.
Lunch buffet is baller. Freshest, lightest, most buttery naan. Ever. Rice pudding and mango pudding(?) is some of the best I've ever had.
Very prompt service and great food. haven been couple of time for lunches and its been really good.

Do not come to this place. It is a complete ripoff! It's not Thai food it's just Chinese take out food. Save yourself some time and money and just go to the China star. It took almost 10 minuets for someone to come to our table, and then another 5 minuets to get our drinks, which was just water. I then ordered Thai tea and that took another 10 minuets. It took about 30 minutes to get our food and on one ever brought us the spring rolls we ordered. I asked for a spice tray, I guess the only had one that someone else was using, so I had given a spice try that was for duck. Like I said save some time and money and just order Chinese take out because that's all this place is. The whole experience just left me angry, and disappointed.

omg, this place is fantastic. I got a lunch portion of chicken with rice and beans for $6 and it fed me and both of my kids. We try and stop in once a week and try something new each time and we haven't been disappointed yet. And you have to love free parking, given the location it's not always easy trying to find street parking!

My biggest peeve when I went there the other day was that I ordered a pita sandwich which said that it had roasted eggplant and feta on it. There was a small amount of baba ganoush and no discernible feta AND french fries - NOT on the side - in the sandwich. What the heck???? Nothing served during lunch came out on anything larger than an 8" plate including my brother's lamb dish. We ordered their sample of spreads which was delicious but there were only like 2 Tablespoons of each spread. A plate of pita bread triangles came out with everything - we had so much that we took home a large take out container of them. Our bill came out to $62 even after my sandwich was taken off the bill - this was for three people at lunchtime. My brother said they should change their name to Ex-Zorba-tant. There are definitely better Greek restaurants in the city.

I really appreciated that they squeezed us in the night before the marathon, but my search for great Thai continues. I went with Pad Thai with shrimp, at a 2 spice level. The spice was perfect, but the sauce was too sweet, and it seemed like they ran a knife a few time through the noodles. They were really short which made it hard to eat.

Wow! My lips just stop tingling from the spicy awesomeness that was the chili noodle. Delish! We also had the Panang Curry and the fried spring rolls. All the food was fresh and yummy. The atmosphere was really light, airy and open. I guess I haven't been inside this space since it was a coffee shop over a decade ago and it still had a house configuration back then. So the renovation may not be new to this restaurant but I really like it. The menu has a lot of variety without being too long. And they state that they will customize any dish even making stuff vegan. The Chili Noodles normally have chicken or beef, but I got them with fried tofu, but I also could have picked soft. It looks like they have a liquor license now since behind the bar they're was the biggest bottle of knob creek that I've ever seen. mmmm bourbon. Also, the name is really Singha Song Thai so I'm guessing they aren't affiliated with the Singha downtown. I submitted the change to our Yelp overlords so I guess it will changed eventually.
This placa is amazing. We eat Suya back home and i came for it. It tastes great!! We also got a jolleb rice and the shrim fried rice and both were great. Definitely i will come again.

I love these guys! Usually super fast (but I'm pretty close)! The soups are very good and I think the chicken dishes are delicious. Especially for the reasonable prices! I have it delivered as it is very near my house.

This place has made me love Thai food! Everything I've had has been great. My favorite is the pad see eew with tofu. The pad string beans, orange chicken and fried rice are also good. Try the Thai iced tea too. They make a great lunch deal too and they do carry out. If you're not into spicy tell them, their 4 was hot even to my spicy-food loving husband.

My favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Indianapolis, in part because it's quick and inexpensive. Very small, only a half dozen tables. Have had six or more different pho, all were delicious; I expected "rice paddy crab" to be crab, not crab dumpling things, but I don't know enough to know if that's standard. Smoothie flavors include avocado, durian, soursop. The only real complaint is that the parking lot is, like the restaurant, small, and it's really only accessible when going southbound (or when you get really, really lucky and can take what may be an illegal left turn into the lot if headed north).

I can't praise this place enough! First and most importantly, the gyros are incredible! It's a once and sometimes twice a week stop for me, and every time the food has been spot on. Second, the staff is the friendliest I've ever met. Good people, and very appreciative of our business. Make sure you try this hidden gem!

Mumbai knows what it's doing. It's going for wide appeal and succeeding. With vegan-friendly, buffet-style curry at $4.95/lb, you aren't going to hear any complaints from this guy. They avoid the potential pitfall of inadequate heating on the buffet line, and for an additional buck, you can add a side of naan. I have frequently pointed people in Mumbai's direction not only because of the food quality, but also because of the unbeatable prices. Not to be the eternal pessimist, but this is not the best Indian food in Philly. It's the best price, without question, and the service is always friendly; however, there are some other options worth considering if you want top-notch Tikka Masala and other Westernized curry dishes. Mumbai Bistro is definitely deserving of a 4-star review and while there may be nicer Indian restaurants in the city, few could compete with its accessibility. For those working in Center City, this is a staple.

Under a new ownership, it went good to great! I was just here for Lunch Buffet $9. It is amazingly good. They had everything from Lamb & Chicken curry, Butter chicken, Beef and Chicken Kabobs...etc. Even sweet dessert. House Chatni and Fresh Naan bread made to order was awesome. Just right amount of spice and great taste and smell! $9 lunch Buffett, you can't go wrong! I'll be back again with my family.

Just an FYI: This is the same Double Dragon that was opened a while back (then Double Dragon II). Not sure what the story behind it is, but Sake Sake and Tay Do couldn't hold down the fort. Also, they don't have their liquor license yet, so BYOB until they do, which should be soon. Call to check. Atmosphere: It's really not fine dining like it says on their business card. They do have quite a number of round tables that seat up to eight people with two TVs to keep a bored crowd entertained. The restaurant itself isn't as big as it used to be, but it still looks the same from when it was Double Dragon II. Food: I frequent Double Dragon with my family because of family-style dining where you can order some dishes, and it'll feed at least 6 people. Of all the items (there are a LOT) on the menu, I love the calamari (comes with diced bell peppers, ask for the lemon/pepper/salt sauce) because the calamari was crispy with just the right amount of seasoning, and the Chinese broccoli with oyster sauce because well... I really can't explain that one. However, since its "reopening," I'd say the overall taste went down. I was disappointed, especially with the Chinese broccoli. It looked like green beans in soy sauce diluted with water. Sigh. The beef teriyaki appetizer comes on a stick (the appetizer comes with about 4-5 if I remember correctly). The meat is a little tough, and it doesn't come with any type of sauce. I think it's just marinated then grilled to "perfection." I also had some type of beef noodle dish (man, I forgot the name, but I'll update when I find out). That was actually pretty decent, but I only ate the noodles, so I totally can't vouch for the beef or vegetables that was also in it lol. Service: Most do not speak fluent English, so if you're looking for someone without an accent, you're sh_t out of luck. The server I had was helpful but a little inattentive. Maybe that's because so many servers were already on the floor, they didn't know who already did what. I think one of them asked what chicken tenders were... oh my...

We've been to this location a few times but tonight was very disappointing. The evening started poorly when our server brought me the wrong beer, not that big of a deal and he promptly replaced it. I wouldn't even mention that fact, but unfortunately it was the first of several things that happened during our dining experience. There were 6 of us at the table. 3 people got their food 15 minutes before everyone else :/ that's always an awkward experience for everyone. After the last 3 meals came out the rice they served us had pockets of luke warm and parts that were ice cold, but my entree was boiling hot. They brought us new rice after we complained. Our server also didn't pre-bus any items. We had so many dishes on the table we could barely sit anything down. Granted they were busy, but if this was my first time eating here, I for sure would never come back. At this point still debating if we will return or not. It's never a good feeling to pay for bad food and poor service

I address this to all Philadelphians who enjoy authentic Sicilian/Italian cuisine--go to Zeppoli. I was intrigued when I heard about Zeppoli, as Sicily is one of our favorite places to travel and Zeppoli was promoted to be about as close as you can get to real Sicilian food in this area. It certainly lived up to its reputation. The Fisherman's stew rivals any couscous alla trapanese that we've had in Sicily, and I still think about their spaghetti and clams before bed every night. Not really, but it really was the best spaghetti and clams that I've ever had (they use cockle clams, which is what did it for me). It's a BYOB too so bring your favorite Sicilian wine to jazz up the experience (we brought an Etna Rosso (Nerello Mascalese)), but make sure you have a DD if necessary. I'm not sure what the public transportation option, if any, to Zeppoli is, but, if you live in Philadelphia, then chances are you or someone you know has a car so I encourage you to make the 10-15 minute drive for a great dining experience!

Made a detour on my way to a Sixers game because of the stellar reviews for this place. It wasn't quite as good as some of the other reviews make it out to be, but still very good. And, frankly, Indonesian restaurants are such a rarity and the prices so reasonable that I feel compelled to give this place five stars. It's small, unpretentious, with limited seating. Service was surprisingly fast. All five dishes we had (fried wontons, mie komplit, mie kepiting, nasi lemak rendang, chicken satay) were good, though I didn't see or taste any crabmeat in the mie kepiting. For me the surprise was the satay; I never had peanut sauce that good before. Would love to try the other dishes if we're ever back in the area. One nit as others have mentioned: Finding parking in this residential neighborhood is a challenge but not impossible.

Damn you Koba for closing! Rumor has it they couldn't keep their damned costs in line. Haven't we heard that before... -_- We were in a serious mood for grilled Korean stuff and couldn't think of any place that offered it besides here. I think JooJoo might have them grill plates on port-o-stoves but that isn't quite the same... So yeah we drop almost 50 bucks for ridiculously little amounts of meat that totally don't make up for the price, the dinginess, or the slow service. I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place as this is one of the first places in St. Louis that I became a regular at. Before, I'd stop by here for some of their other stuff but the poor experience is driving me more towards Seoul Garden and U City Grill. Alas.

Being from California where there is an abundance of good, authentic Asian restaurants, my expectations weren't super high. But I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed. I started with the veggie spring rolls, which were real fresh and the sauce was tasty. Then I had chicken drunken noodles... one of the best Thai dishes I've ever had, and I've had alot. I couldn't stop eating!!! I love the big picture windows so you can see all the folks walking by on the street as you're eating. Sen is doing it legit for sure, highly recommended!

First, I just want to say the owner is very attentive and kind. The food are very authentic. The steak is very tender and juicy. The Vietnamese ice coffee was ok because it was a bit too light but that doesn't matter as much as how I enjoy the food. The shrimp tempura was very crispy and the shrimp was made just right, not too cook nor too raw. The pork with vegetables and ban bao (not sure what that is in English) but it was delicious. I love the service by the owner who was very friendly and engage in conversation with the guests and always trying to find out how the guests are enjoying the food and finding ways to improved. I wouldn't hesitate to come here again. I wish they deliver and open up one near the hospital I am working in. Great job guys! Steve Z, I suggest you give it another try. The food there are as authentic as it can be.

Best pho ever anywhere. Make your way here past endless strip malls and car dealerships. A sweet oasis in the middle of an urban sprawl desert, though I came here on a frigid, colorless January day. Triapsed through the dirty slush to the very plain storefront, shivering in the dining room as I waited. Then the smiling woman behind the counter brought out a plate heaped with bean sprouts, fresh mint, jalapenos, lime, and dried? pickled? onions, followed by a big bowl of steaming broth, teeming with noodles, shrimp, some kind of reddish tofu-type substance, and strips of fried flattened fish, essence of the ocean. Pho is all about the broth, and this one was briny, salty, sweet, hot, and rich. The flavors develop as you eat, deepening as the bowl empties. I took a sardine banh-mi home for dinner and was not disappointed. I hope to return on a Sunday for the Duck Soup! This place is authentic and the absolute bomb!

I LOVE indian food. Finding a place that makes it well is not that easy. I stopped by this place for lunch. I had the malai kofta extra extra spicy. It was SOOO good. I get takeout of the same thing about once a week. I get the cravings for it and HAVE to buy it. As I am typing this the cravings are starting. Guess what's for dinner?!?! The people there are very nice. It seems to be a family that runs it. Anywho the food is great. Be sure to try!!!

My new favorite place in the Terminal. The sandwiches are a great size and delicious. Tried the bistek and tripleta, and both were outstanding. Lots of yummy appetizers, too. Definitely visiting again soon. My husband said the bistek is the best cheesesteak in Philly.

Such a cute place. We went here on a weekday night, so it wasn't crowded. A really relaxed ambiance and kind of romantic with it being a little dark. We ate outside where the restaurant faces the street so there was ample opportunity to people watch. We had the Saganaki, Chicken Kabobs, Spanakopita, and Bacon Wrapped Olives. We weren't really feelin' the olives, but everything else was great! And our waitress was really nice and had some good suggestions on what to get and what she liked. Although it wasn't crowded, parking was kind of challenging in that Momo's didn't have its own parking lot (that I noticed). There is a parking lot directly across the street, but I wasn't sure if we could park there after hours (it belonged to another establishment). In the end we just parked along the street and our cars we're fine.

I love this place! My Thai friend recommended it to me and we went together. She said it was really authentic to Thailand. It was a month or so ago so I don't remember what we had, but it was incredible! The place is run by real Thai people and they spoke Thai with my friend and brought her a big spoon so she could eat the way Thai people do traditionally. It definitely doesn't look very appealing from the outside, but this little place has fantastic food and was not very expensive!

The menu is pretty extensive for such a small place. We had the Vietnamese tacos, fried chicken and waffle, and New York strip steak pho. All were delicious, but the pho was the best. They had a good wine, cocktail, and beer list as well. I ordered the lush cocktail, and it was okay. The cocktail was a little pricey in comparison to the rest of the menu, but it was high in alcohol content. The only downside to this place is the noise level. It's REALLY loud when the restaurant is full, and the tables are really close together. We practically sat on top of a drunk table of six, which is unfortunate, even though there were other tables available.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Not that great, people are nice, interior is typical strip mall chinese food place. Sushi is small, I mean tiny!, the more expensive rolls are SO not worth it. Maybe this place in a pinch, but I would move on.

Amazing pho. You can order on a touch pad and customize your order any way you want. No more forgetting to ask without cilantro. Ordering for takeout is an option. Portions are huge, so come hungry. I think that's why prices are a bit higher than most typical pho places. Also the customer service is great and the place is very clean. There is also free WiFi. If you're a tofu lover, the tofu pho is so good. Nice and soft.
The buffet is such a great deal. The chicken tikka masala is one of the best I've had. I don't like my food too spicy and theirs is just right. Will definitely be back.

Trini transplant visiting from Michigan. OMG! This place had generous portions and lots of variety, including breakfast options. Actually took home some baked goods for family & friends. Oh! And some doubles - yes they travel well when you're desperate. lol! Their currants rolls are amazingly good! Can't say enough good things about this place. From Center City take the Market-Frankford Line (Blue Line) towards 69th street. Exit @ 52nd. From station head about 1/4 mile south on 52nd.

By far my favorite Thai place in the area! The restaurant is very warm and welcoming. Staff is wonderful. I always order the chicken pad Thai which is absolutely amazing! I will definitely be back! Keep up the good work!

I just left a Yelp Elite "Dia de los Muertos" themed party at La Mulita and am already planning when I can go back. Heads up, La Mulita; I will be asking for the custom Marigold Hotel cocktail every time I visit. Pure gold, that's what that is. Great job partnering with Yelp, La Mulita! What a great way to check out a new (to me) restaurant; cocktails, tapas, face paint, flowers, cake-- the whole enchilada, if you will!

We ordered the chicken chettinad and authentic hyderabadi chicken biryani..the chicken chettinad was simply awesome...the biryani was flavorful but a little dry, but was still pretty good..the rates are on the higher side..it was a good experience over all...

I have been here a number of times since my last review. Every experience has been as good or better than the last. My family and I try to order something new each time but we always get the staples, nasi goreng, Kewtiew (spelling), and the fried chicken dish. I love every single dish that comes out of kitchen. The service is great, the price is right, and I love how this is a family restaurant. The breath and soul of the food is from the mom (who cooks every dish). Weekends are busy so try to get here during the weekdays! Oh and I have had the beef rendang again. It's pretty amazing. The beef was tender and the sauce was very flavorful. You really can't go wrong with anything on this menu.

The decor is pretty nice, the staff wonderfully attentive without being intrusive. I had a delightful Tom Kah starter followed by the mango curry. Delicious! I finished up with the mango ice-cream in a chocolate cup, beautifully presented. This place rocks!

I was in the mood for a gyro/falafel type sandwich for lunch on a lazy Saturday so I decided to try this place for take-out on the recommendation of my fellow Yelpers. Needless to say, I was not disappointed. I went with a Wilson's sandwich, fries and an order of grape leaves. The Wilson's sandwich is genius. Why have two separate sandwiches of meat or falafel when you can combine them into one awesome one? The sanwich came with grilled chicken, falafel, veggies, tzaiki sauce, olives, hummus and special hot sauce all wrapped in a homemade pita. It was messy, but it was delicious. The fries tasted good, but were soft and soggy probably due to the stryofoam container they were transported in during my walk home. I could've done without them. I was going to get a piece of pistachio baklava ($1.25) but only had 50 cents left to my name. Next time you will be mine sweet baklava... On a side-note, besides the "Wilson's", they also have a sandwich called the "Angelo Cataldi" which I guess is a salute to the venerable figure of Philly sports radio and such notable events like Wing Bowl. Right on Bitar's, right on. .

New owner or management after the remodel. They still have the same chef apparently but I got the same dish as I always do (baby bok choi) it was subpar. It's more expensive and the decor is not great. There's just a bunch of Christmas lights. It has the atmosphere of a sorority girl's dorm room. I preferred the old zen yai.

Although the place is really nice, my experience wasn't what I was expecting. The appetizer we had was the scallop sashimi.... terrible.... and very expensive. The wine selection is good, and prices are ok. The service is very good, very helpful waiters. Maybe I just have to give this place another chance and see what happens.

Multiple times have called to place a to go order and the bartender takes the call, then sets phone down and FORGETS! Will wait on the phone 15+ minutes with no response. Even worse since the phone is off the hook and you can't even call back. HORRIBLE

This is our go-to place for pita. If you want fresh wonderful pita at home or at a meal away from home, go to Bitars. Yesterday, we needed to take something to a party, but wanted to take something that no one else would bring (the usual cookies and cakes). So, we stopped in at Bitars on our way out of the city, got pita, grape leaves, hummus and falafel. What a great treat. The other guests were very happy with our selection. I was most impressed with the falafel, which was not as dry as it is in some stores and restaurants. Now we have a new go-to place for falafel. Thanks to the Bitars!

Hands down THE best Thai place in Nashville. It looks like a bit of a hole in the wall from the outside so I was sceptical at first put I am so glad I got past that and went inside. The atmosphere is good and the seating includes some nice authentic Thai pillows that go behind your back as you sit the down. The service was very good, the people genuine and friendly, and the food was absolutely incredible!!

I had the lemongrass chicken vermicelli. Spicy and really perfectly seasoned. More fish sauce please! The chicken wasn't dry and rubbery as you typically find with this dish. I ordered the grilled pork rolls. They're fresh rolls with grilled pork and they come with fish sauce. Great! I tried a fried egg roll with pork. These were some of the best I have ever had. I also tried a fried chicken wing. These came with a couple sauces and were just plain unbelievable. Crispy and impossible to stop eating. The food here is creative and thoughtful even though sometimes uneven. Nice menu and good service.
The atmosphere was very nice. The staff was very welcoming and friendly. The food was delicious. I would highly recommend.

My boyfriend and I alllwaayyss order from here. The food is out of this world delicious. There is always so much food for a great price. No matter what mood I'm in for what to eat, I can't go wrong with shere e Punjab. A must try in media The service is not bad but not great. The staff seem like they're always hiding and take a long time to do one thing. The food is what brings me back and I order take out.
The food was fresh and delicious. The staff was friendly and polite. I highly recommend this place.
Consistently good food and service. We end up here often because my 5 yr old son loves the Mac n' Cheese and I love the many options, flavor, and good ingredients.

My co-workers and I are always ordering from Thailand as the food and service are great. My usual order consists of Chicken Mussamun Curry over rice which is just packed with flavor. I happen to love the double dipping of starches. I recently tried Pahd See Eiw which is just stir-friend noodles with broccoli and it was tasty. Their spring rolls are delicious as well. Every time I order from Thailand I am satisfied and full.

4.5/5 I have always called and ordered food to go, so I cannot speak for the sit-down experience. The food is always ready to be picked up and the staff are friendly. Great food - entrees, dessert, drinks. Menu shows which items are gluten free.

I am very new to Indian food and both of my experiences were with Shere-E-Punjab. The food is delicious! I love the chicken vindaloo. I've had both the standard naan and the garlic naan and they are both very good. I love the rice they give you as well. I also tried the Mango Lassi and was very happy I did! It was delicious. I will definitely be coming back! The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was because of the service. It could have been better.

The. Best. Scallops. EVER. The BF and I shared the Grilled Scallops entree, a side of grilled veggies, and a small plate of Grilled Octopus. The Grilled Scallops were AMAZING and the grilled veggies was really good too. I'm not sure why everyone's so excited over the Grilled Octopus. I've had octopus lots, but for some reason, the grilled octopus here just kind of taste like chicken. I heard the line gets long, so we got there at 5pm and people were already waiting outside!

Adore this place! Loved the service and the food was on point!! I walked a mile to eat here because the place in the loop was closed on Wednesdays. Upon walking up to the restaurant it looks a little sketchy but wow, oh wow, did this place blow me out of the water. I ordered the goat korma and my boyfriend got the chicken tikka. The naan bread was fresh and delicious. I have nothing but great things to say about this place other than I wish they were in my town!
We came on a Monday night, there were a few tables not crazy busy. I ordered the house special vermicelli which was delicious, good stuff. we also ordered the spring rolls and they came out alright.

We live nearby and have gone to Saigon Corner several times. The place is clean with soft music and a huge fish tank. The menu offers chinese and thai dishes. Don't get them. Too saucy and overbearingly sweet. Stick to the Pho, stock is very tasty and the chicken broth is actually better. The cucumber salad is very good.

Pros: conveniently located, next to lodging/major shopping center/star bucks, dish comes in huge portions Cons: extremely salty and sugary, poor customer service, expensive, too Americanized Thai cuisine

Meh. This place is OK. We go here often for lunch at work, and it's always just ok. We found out early on that if you want to get back to work within the hour, you need to get here between 11-11:30, after that you hit the lunch rush and you will wait a while for your food. The food is just OK. Several times I've ordered a dish with chicken and ended up not eating the meat because it tasted either old or cheap or both. They do give you a little spring roll, though, with every dish, and that's kind of a nice little treat. The best part about this place is that it is in an old Tomatillo Grill and they've taken down all the Tomatillo verbage on the signs, but left the decorations up. We call it Land of Tomatillo Smile and someone inevitably makes a joke about ordering chips and salsa. Har. Don't get me wrong, the food is good, but it's just not the best and service can be really iffy. I've seen the whole place full and two servers running around covering the entire dining room.

Not incredibly thrilled by the food from here. I ordered take out and service was incredibly fast and the staff was super nice. I ordered a gyro, spinach pie and hummus. It would have been great had they used homemade pitas and not pita pockets. The gyro meat was a bit institutionalized. I have had better from trucks in NYC

The service staff was terrible; it was hard to tell who was service staff and who wasn't. And, when you found service staff, they were very slow to get what needed. I had the lunch buffet. The buffet was sparse, bland and WAY overpriced.

I have only tried the lunch buffet so far ( vegetarian options) and it's fantastic enough that I will be back. The food is interesting, fresh and 'clean'. And really good! A lot of times buffet lunches seem to churn out the same old stuff. And sometimes things are spiced too closely that it all begins to meld into one common taste. Not at Nirvana! Good variety, good taste and very nice place. Try the Chai as well. Authentic and delicious!

Honestly, not the quality we're used to... Average price for an entrée here is about $12- not horrible for the beach- but just not worth the quality we received. We did enjoy the outdoor patio seating.

This restaurant is a special gem in Reno. The food is incredible. The owner is lovely. If you are not familiar with Ethiopian food, you should definitely branch out your culinary wings and give it a shot... You will not be disappointed. It's all true!!!

Let's face it people...we don't have a whole lot of choices for great Indian food. At Ekta you will find it fresh, hot and delicious. I don't think there is a buffet, so you will always know that it was cooked for you that day. As other reviewers have noted, the dishes are not very spicy. My American palate didn't mind. I'm sure if you asked the server, he would accommodate a request for more spice. I would highly recommend Ekta and will definitely plan to return.

Located on Grand (just south of Bates), the newly opened South Grand Gyro Express has become one of my favorite neighborhood eateries. From the outside, it looks like a typical Middle Eastern fast food restaurant (neon signs and photos of gyros/kebabs in the window). Inside, it is small and a little rough around the edges. It looks like they started to decorate and never finished the job. They do a great carry out business, but, it is also a great little dine in spot. Not because it's pretty, but because they have the other elements down. What I like most about Gyro Express is the food and price. Everything is priced under $10. Most items are under $7.50. The Owner (former Chef at Natasha's Kebab International), is a friendly bloke. He is very passionate about his food and it shows! The Gyro meat (typical American lamb/beef combo) is put through an extra step after it comes off of the spit and is sauteed with onions and special sauce. It is so tender and yummy and is the best gyro meat I have had in St. Louis ($4.99). They have an unbelievable warm eggplant puree appetizer served with pita that is similar to kashke badmen-jun ($2.99). I attempted to nail the chef down on a name for this scrumptious dip (I could live on this stuff). On the menu, it says "eggplant" appetizer and when asked, the chef kept calling it "Afghan eggplant dish." Low and behold, I Googled "Afghan eggplant dish" and came up with lots of hits. So, I humbly accept the name "eggplant dish" in lieu of something more exciting. Other excellent dishes include sambusas that are similar to samosas (2 for $4.50), and house-made ice cream with pistachios ($2.50). I have plans of returning to try other items, but I don't care much for the chicken biryani. It's a bit dry. Other menu items include kebabs, hummus, felafel, and the usual middle eastern fare. The owner stated that he is planning to expand on the menu.

I am would give 4 stars. Service was good, ambience was great and entire staff was full of energy. I tried Indo chinese and it was decent. Entire staff was accomodative inspite of being pretty full. The chef made one mistake when paneer was added to noodles but they were able to quickly rectify that and offered replacement. I will definitely go there again.

I've been to Cucina Zapata three different times now and each time I come away amazed! I've had the Cap'n Crunch Tilapia each time and it has been consistently delicious - well-cooked, enhanced just perfectly with Asian slaw and a mayo sauce with a ZING! After reading the reviews on this site, my next choice in the chicken satay taco. Well done, Cucina Zapata. You are a welcome addition to the Drexel 'Food Truck Row' and I will continue to frequent your business. HOW do they make such amazing food out of a TRUCK??? And - they are super-friendly to boot. I also caution readers to not wait until late in the day to grab your lunch - you may be disappointed as I have been a few times.

I am an asian food lover!!! And I admit that this PF Chang is ok! The service is very nice. Have to admit though that their food is very oily and as someone said before very loaded with sodium. Were not too happy about the cleanliness of their glasses. It has been the 2nd time today that the server had to go back several times to get us clean glasses. I do not mind water stains but smeary glasses are just gross......Seriously???? Several weeks ago this almost ended in a fiasco until the waiter hand washed them.... the glasses were ok but not great!! Altogether they are ok but not too great!

Usually this is my go to place when craving Jamaican food .... But today was very disappointing.... I ordered stewed chicken with rice & beans/cabbage there was absolutely no gravy (STEWED chicken?) the food also taste different ... From the looks of it they switched cooks ... I really hope the normal cook just had today off
Food is ok but the worst service ever. Especially, the lady boss doesn't know how to deal and talk with customers.
Nice atmosphere, ok food. Parking is awful for the area, so you might want to come during the week if you can. Fun when they have music going, and the weather is nice.
Order a falafel; sit on a stool to eat; Repeat.

Ugh. Sweet, watered-down pho, old and stale bbq pork and I'm sure the vegetables in my spring roll and for the pho were nowhere close to being fresh. But none of this even holds a candle to the poor service at this place. I've encountered the bad service here in the past and have found the wait staff to be inattentive and borderline rude, but kien giang managed to drumpf (I couldn't resist, sorry!) it all today. If you walk in at 8:30 pm or after, entire sections of their menu disappear, not because they run out of supplies for them, but because they close at 9 pm and don't want to put in the effort to make these items. The worst part is, the wait staff unabashedly told my group this as we tried ordering several of these items. Add to that the fact that they started closing up shop while we were still having our dinner, and you have a winner for the restaurant with the WORST service ever. Why did I come here you ask? Because my favorite Vietnamese place is closed today and I didn't remember the good here being this abysmal. Needless to say, I'm never coming here again and refuse to give my money to someone who doesn't deserve it. The best Vietnamese in town is across the street from here anyway and they treat their customers like family...

I went to Fez with some coworkers and it was my first time having Moroccan food. The atmosphere of the restaurant was pretty nice, really dark, but still fun and great for groups. The food was fantastic! The thing that will probably keep me from going again is the staff. I was there for 15 minutes before I was offered anything to drink and the waiter was disappointed when we all wanted water. Despite asking several times they did not split the check and not everybody brought cash. We only saw employees to bring us the water and 40 minutes later bring us food and then we had to go ask them to bring us the check. Of course they were more than willing to charge us the automatic 20% gratuity even though the most certainly didn't earn that.

I'm not a big fan of non-salmon colored fish, but when I feel a craving for something different, Dmitri's immediately comes to mind. This is probably the best place for Mediterranean seafood in all of Philadelphia, and perhaps an even better testament of their culinary prowess is that every time I go, I find myself downing their bluefish so fast that I feel like hurling. Yes, it's that good. Elbow room is a luxury here, but you'll deal with it. Service is pretty friendly, and you can choose between a normal table or a seat near the cooking action. Dmitri's does not take reservations, however, and the lines are always long, so it is best advised to go during non-peak hours (around 5 PM, or after 9 PM). My one major gripe is with the olive oil provided on the tables. There is a dish of olive oil on every table, and this same dish is used for different groups of patrons. Maybe I'm just being picky, but for food this good, I would expect them to be less tacky in this area, and a lot more hygienic. It was sooo good. Great service, very fresh food. I had the green curry w/chicken and I loved it.

A lot of people have called this great hangover food but my best friend introduced it to me as "Netflix food." She calls it the kind of guilty pleasure food you want to hold close to your chest and happily nibble on as you watch your favorite TV show and bum around on a weekend day (while procrastinating on homework, of course). I tried the turkey bacon, egg, cheese sandwich and was pretty blown away by how satisfying and tasty it was. Make sure to eat it while it's still warm. I was also so pleased to be able to choose turkey bacon (instead of regular bacon) as an option.Can't find that in most places! Additionally, the spicy Bui sauce definitely takes the sandwich to the next level. I expected it to be a red sauce but it turned out to be white -- interesting! Basically a spicy mayo. Can't wait to enjoy one of these when I visit Penn again!

If I could give stars just for food, it would be 5++. Unfortunately, the service only deserves 1 star. I am Puerto Rican and came specifically to this restaurant for mofongo, for which they are known. It came highly recommended. It took ten minutes before someone even passed by to take our drink order...this is after she sat us which was just as we walked in. After she took our drink AND food order, which we already knew since we were waiting so long with menus, she asked us if we wanted our drinks to come WITH the food!! I can honestly say, I was too shocked to even answer and my friend told her to bring the drinks now. They don't have fountain drinks, and to me this was weird because they had cloth napkins and real utensils and it was a nice looking restaurant. Also, they charged for a refill of brewed tea, cups were 12 oz mason jars; 2 bucks per glass! It took almost 45 mins for the food to come and people who had arrived at least 20 mins AFTER us were getting their food before us! The waitress noticed and went to the kitchen to check up and the food came. The food: I got classic mofongo and palomilla steak w pink beans and rice, my friend got the steak but his was breaded and fried (mine was sautéed in a pan; my other friend got the mofongo w beef stew, even though she ordered it with shrimp. The waitress argued that she wrote down my friend ordered stew, sighed and offered to take it back, but my friend was cool about it and stated she would eat what the lady brought since she was starving. The food was DELISH!!!! I would get food here again IF I ordered ahead and went in just to pay and leave then eat at home. Too bad service leaves a lot to be desired...

Bindi Masala with essence of pomegranate? Yes please! Under full disclosure, I've only ever ordered Bindi from Ekta, but that's because it has been so delightfully satisfying that I've never found the need to change dishes. Regardless of ordering carryout or eating in, the chefs are willing to accommodate "spiciness" requests. The rice is always fresh, and never greasy. As for dining in, Ekta offers a pleasant, quiet environment, which is surprisingly conducive to quiet conversation given how small the seating area is. And for carry out? Twice I've been the recipient of a complementary rice pudding dessert. Happy Munching!
If you don't mind sitting on top of one another, some of the best seafood in town

We found Zorba's through Yelp! when we wanted some good food near the Art Museum. The walk was pleasant and found Zorba's in the area between the Art Museum and the Eastern State Penitentiary, along with other small restaurants in the area. We found the homely run place welcoming, and were promptly sitted in a nicely decorated area. The menu was vast and they seem to have different portions for lunch and dinner. The hummus appetizer was delicious, and our meals were well portioned and tasty. We really enjoyed our lunch there and were chatting with the waiters. Highly recommended.

Seriously the best! I have only been for the lunch buffet but uh really cannot beat it. Great variety, nice atmosphere, consistent food. I could literally drink the Tikka Masala sauce like it was soup it is so good. Also, a great place to take first timers due to the variety and options at lunch.
Was a little disappointed that the chicken pho is made with beef broth, but really enjoyed the chicken fried rice.
Have been pleased on both visits. Attentive service and great food. Atmosphere is nice.

I agree with a lot of Yelpers, this food is bland, no spice like we've had at other Moroccan restaurants in other cities. The prices are a little too steep for the quality of the food. Lamb couscous was chewy, bland rice. Soup was tasteless. Chicken Tagine also lacked any spice. Just adding dates and apricots and a few olives doesn't make a dish taste Moroccan. The people were very nice, but wouldn't go back.
We were in the mood for some Indian food on our way West Virginia from New Jersey. It was a little off the highway but so worth it! The food and service were both amazing.

If you are tired of eating food at regular Indian restaurant (Naan, Butter Chickecn, Tandoori Chicken etc.) then Dosa Hut is a whiff of fresh air. I am from south India and have been longing for a good south Indian restaurant throughout mid-west and was lucky to find this tiny spot in Nashville. We tried a variety of foods including Dosa, Veg. Thali, Kotthu Parotta, Vadai etc. All the food tasted really good. The decor and the ambiance is not on par with the food. I visited them again the next day and the food was consistent. Overall good tasty south Indian food, friendly owner, piping hot food which makes Dosa Hut a must visit in Nashville if you love authentic Indian food.
Went for lunch buffet. Not the best Indian food I had but is good food. Top that with good ambience. Would be nice if they had more than just one desert.

My friend and I arrived about 10 min before opening on a weekday, and there was already a line of people pre-ordering. Then when the truck officially opened at noon, two lines formed: one receiving new orders and the other calling out names whose foods were ready. We ordered chicken satay tacos, cap'n crunch burrito, and mango tea. I would've loooooved to try the short ribs taco but they didn't serve them for that day for some reason. They were all delicious!! The foods all looked delectable too, with all the different colors. Honestly I have never seen so many people wait in line for food truck to open. Great food, fast service, friendly people, and affordable. Definitely recommend it

Horrible experience! Unfortunately it was my son's first experience with Indian food. We entered the restaurant today at 1:30 and a woman yells from across the restaurant, "here,here, you sit here." As we rushed over she says, "only water" as she pours water and walks away. The buffet had little to chose from and it was obviously sitting for awhile. My rice had hard burned pieces that were inedible. A man stood at the counter mean mugging the remaining customers. Shortly before 2 he rounded the 3 tables of customers telling all of us that they were closing in 15 minutes. He then went and put out the sterno burners, continuing to stare at everyone with his arm crossed. We finished, paid, and left before 2:15. The sign states that they close at 2:30. Not one ounce of good or appropriate customer service. There are far too many friendly Indian restaurants nearby to ever patronize this place again! Will never be back.
Not many places to get Vietnamese food let alone bahn mi (Vietnamese hoagies) plus bubble tea of all varieties. Hope they stick around for a long time! They do a good job, tasty good portions.
This place becoming my favorite spot. Son far I had curry chicken, jerk chicken, and oxtail. They are all great with wonderful flavors. The portion is great and can't bet the price for quality food.

Olga and I went there Saturday 19 Aug 2017 at around 1:30. Service by the owner was excellent. My bahn mi (#64) had several large pieces of gristle, and the meat was tough. The baguette was soft and chewy, not the crisp crackly kind one would expect. The shrimp spring rolls (#1) were very good and the peanut sauce was a very good complement. The pho had good flavor and the noodles were a perfect consistency--cooked just right. The restaurant was clean and light, and it was evident that a lot of the customers are regulars. If I were in the neighborhood I would try it again, but I would not make it a destination.

I love this place...Why one may ask does someone make a special trip to a rather questionable part of town...easy to answer...it's the Antithesis to the Dutchess. One review stated they shouldn't try to be Dutchess. Number one GOOD. I have supported Dutchess since they opened...I spent THOUSANDS yes thousands in Dutchess AND Provisions. They still treat me like a stranger. It's just NEXT...whose next. The staff rarely smile and almost seem like they are doing me a favour serving me. Don't get me wrong Dutchess has earned its stripes...however I am VERY happy they are no longer the only place in town. Having said that M&G is not TRYING to be Dutchess...or...anyone else other than themselves. They offer very good well priced treats. Try the Pear cinnamon pie if you want an authentic French delight. It's a recipe from the French Patisserie Paul, where Fadouah was Executive Chef. She and her husband are both Classically trained but that's not there idea at M&G. They are providing a service that is missing in that area...Good food, Good value, Friendly Service. Great Macarons. Unfortunately they had employed someone that did some serious damage to her. That person almost finished her...I'm grateful she did not. I love nothing more than a Saturday afternoon in a cozy chair...having a Chicken Mushroom crepe followed by some delight. IF you are looking for the Dutchess or ANY other iteration of it...keep on going. I and my Family and friends will continue our enjoyment of the place. Oh and as to the Kitsch someone referred to...it's there so poor people can afford things as well. Brava Macaron and Goodies! I can't wait to see what's next!

My favorite Indian food place in the St. Louis area! I usually come for the Saturday buffet which offers a great variety of curries and deserts, however I recently came and ordered a la carte. I got an order of aloo gohbi and it lasted me about 3 or 4 meals when I took home left overs. I am a vegetarian and have no trouble at all finding lots of options. The food is outstanding and the service is great as well!

Another great addition to Main Street and East Nashville in general. Had the best octopus I've ever had. Everything else we had for lunch was exceptional. The space is bright and cheery and there's also a great outdoor space in the back. The only changes that I would recommend is that they had fish to the menu and instead of being able substitute a side for an extra $2 instead of the fries that come with many of the dishes, I would just say you could add a side for two bucks and still give the customer the fries.

3.5 stars. Decent, pretty average thai food. Nothing spectacular, but still a satisfying meal. The prices are standard for the Rittenhouse area. All the waitresses were super friendly, and although our food took a while to come out...everything was super HOT. Overall, if you're on an expedition for the BEST thai food in Philly--look elsewhere. However, this is quite a charming restaurant...perfect for date night or a quiet meal with friends. Bonus point for BYO.

My husband and I stopped in for a quick dinner. I had the pork sandwich and he the Cuban burger. They were both amazing, flavorful and cooked to perfection!! Our waitress Catherine was a breath if fresh air! Friendly, informative and attentive!! And Margaritas delicious!!
This food is amazing very delicious only had a problem once with my gyro the meat wasn't to my expectations other than that very great place and sweet workers very friendly

My husband and I decided to give iPho another go because we had a less-than-stellar experience during their grand opening time. Definitely has made a 180 change from before. Normal to no-wait times, courteous staff. The food is as good as it always was :) We are very happy we tried it again. Looking forward to going back!

A good place for Indian food. The place is small and the ambience is moderate. They have many choices and varieties. The place is moderately priced, the food taste good. I would recommend this place for lunch. The service is mediocre.

No lie, I have probably eaten at Blue Plate 100 times... and I have never had a bad meal there. The food is amazing, the staff is awesome and I love that the owner/chef tries to cook with local ingredients whenever possible. Everything on the menu is delicious - breakfast or lunch. I will say that I don't go there for dinner only because we don't eat out at night much but I've heard that the dinners are wonderful as well. One tip, always order off the specials menu. Whatever they have cooked up for that day is guaranteed to be amazing! The atmosphere leaves a little to be desired, but the food makes up for it.

Thai hot at this place is no joke! The food is so delicious! This is the best Panang Curry I've had in Tampa, leaps and bounds better! I ordered the Panang Curry with chicken, and it had tons of broccoli, zucchini, and bell peppers, as well as heaping amounts of chicken. A perfect thick gravy bursting with flavor. They do it right here! The service was very friendly, and the food came out quick. They have seating outside with plenty of shade, or if you prefer A/C, they offer a small dining area inside. The price is not bad. The quantity is plentiful, and the quality is unmatched in this area. If you like Thai cuisine, I recommend trying this place out. If you are unsure if you like Thai cuisine or not, I recommend choosing this place to help you decide. I was not disappointed. This food is amazing!

If you've never been, its a great place to try out! Very unique and the food is good and well priced. In fact, I'm not even sure why I'm not giving them 5 stars other than I'm not a huge sandwich person normally!

Laganini is located in the former home of Captain D's behind Bevo Mill. The owners have clearly dumped lots of money into the building. It still has the Captain D's floor and okay lighting, but overall, they did a nice job redecorating the restaurant. The booths with granite tabletops are especially nice. The atmosphere is very quiet, with soft background music. The menu is American/Mediterranean/Bosnian, all with a clear Bosnian interpretation. Plenty of appetizers (spanikopita & toasted ravs), interesting pizzas ($8.50), calzones ($12), burgers (Greek burger - $12), sandwiches (Philly Cheese-steak $6.95), Bosnian sausages, meats, etc. The warm homemade crusty bread that they brought out first was to die for. I could live on that bread! The table next to us raved about the Tilapia. They said it was fantastic and that it was a great portion that they couldn't finish. We shared an order of spanikopita, which was a little different than the norm (cream of spinach filling, instead of spinach/feta). we also split the meat sampler entree ($15). It came with salad, roasted potatoes and a TON of meat (beef and pork sausage, steak, veal, burger, etc.). It was so much food, that we had leftovers after sharing the entree. it was tasty, but a little on the salty side. This platter was the most expensive thing on the menu. Most items were under $11. The dessert menu is a little pricey (average $6), for the area. You can get great crepes at any of the local Bosnian restaurants for under $2 and they are $6 here. Most of the desserts are ice cream sundaes. The owner/waiter was very nice. It's basic fare. Nothing fancy, but good, nonetheless. It's close to home. So, I'll be back.

Amazing food, great service, and a really neat atmosphere. They were super accommodating with my food allergies, which is hard to find in New Orleans. We got 6 or so plates to share amongst a few people and we loved everything. Definitely will be back soon!

This is day four of business and obviously still having a few growing pains. On the plus side the service was fast (buffet steam table), super friendly and helpful. I appreciated the option to sample an item before selecting. The servers are experienced but new to Indian food and eager to learn flavors and spices to better assist customers. Everything I ordered and sampled was very good and I loved the flavors and spices. The only negative that I experienced, and I pointed out, was the steam table wasn't keeping the food hot. Once I brought to their attention they immediately began attempting to correct and thanked me for bringing to their attention. Growing pains always exists with a new business. Hopefully adding a cover or lids will correct the problem. Apparently the game plan is changing the menu weekly for variety. I'm not sure if this is the entire steam table or just one or two items. Hopefully they'll keep a few items for consistency. I'll be back soon to try new selections and see how that stubborn steam table is working out.

Very good and super cheap. Yes the bahn mi is small but it's 4.50. So order 2 and it is still cheaper then anywhere else. Plus you can try 2. The spring rolls are great even though a egg roll inside sounds strange. Not the best peanut sauce but still tasty. However I was pleasantly surprised. Vietnamese coffee was wonderful. As strong as it should be and not to much condensed milk. The vermicelli noodles were great. Lots of carrots and great fish sauce. We had one vermicelli bowl. One bahn mi. 2 orders of egg rolls and 2 Vietnamese coffees for 28 bucks befor tip. That's cheap. And very good. I will be going back again and again

I have few negative things to say about this place. The food is Afghani, simple, and delicious. I've had several of the kabobs, some of the special lamb dishes, and several appetizers (with pumpkin). They are unique to my palate, so flavorful and satisfying. Most dishes come with flatbread, and the main dishes come with a salad or side of your choice. Most menu items are priced very reasonably, and the service is what it is-- they bring you the food you ask for in a reasonable time frame. The space is slightly cramped, and you might leave smelling like roasted meat, but it's worth it. I will definitely be back for lunch.

Poorly run. Sunday afternoon and they are out of rice for the black beans and fish for the fish tacos. Both popular items. I guess the manager was not smart enough to go to a store and buy more if the supplier could not deliver. They were out of a few other items also so we left and went to a restaurant across the street that knows how to stock the kitchen. Not worth going back to as the prices are hgh, the service was slow and they dont know how to run a business.
This place has the best pad Thai and curry I've ever had. Really nice place and really good food. My favorite Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara county and worth trying.

Olio is a unique place to grab a bite. First off, it's an old service station that serves up Mediterranean and North African cuisine. Second, it's also connected to a little bit classier of a restaurant, elaia. To me Olio seems more of a small plate and cocktail kind of place. The food was very good. We started with the torshi, a pumpkin spread with some bread. The main course we each had our own flatbread. I had the mushroom and my girlfriend had the lahmacun, Turkish seasoned beef with pine nuts and caramelized onions. Then for Dessert we split a pie in a jar. It seemed similar to chocolate pudding and whip cream. The whip cream was made in house and was delicious. Overall the food was great and they have a great cocktail menu. If the cocktail is not on the menu, you can ask for it and the bartender will make it. The staff was all very friendly and checked in on us frequently. Even though it was a small place (maybe sits 35 people at most). There was only 1 waitress for the whole place. Although the bartender did assist in waiting. I will for sure be back to Olio, it just didn't wow me enough to make it a must return right away kind of place.
Some of the most flavorful Indian food in Delaware at a low price! Lunch counter style eatery with elegant tasting food!

Just left Sam's. The food was excellent. I had the grilled tilapia. It was seasons perfectly and came with a side salad, veggies and red potatoes. My husband had the crab cake sliders which he said were delicious. And The best was our server, Angel, who was attentive and had a great sense of humor. We'll be going back again!

Okay, I gave it a try. Twice. I really wanted to like it because one of my friends loves this place. Mediocre experience was two for two though. First time there I ordered a pork banh mi, some egg rolls, and an iced coffee. The egg rolls were fine, the coffee was fine, but that banh mi was pathetic. It was about two thirds pork fat and didn't really taste like much of anything. I decided I would give it another try and see if it was just a one-time problem. Round number 2 I decided to try the pad Thai. I asked the girl working if it was more limey/tamarindy or peanutty and her response was "umm, I don't know".... I should have trusted my gut and passed. Well, when it came to my table, it was neither. I couldn't quite figure out what was off, but it was the worst pad Thai I've ever had. I think it might have had too much fish sauce in it based on the weird aftertaste. I wasn't going to stop for dinner somewhere else on my way home, so I just stomached what I could and passed on the rest. The girl came back over and asked how it was and I told her it had a strange taste. So, I guess the only thing here safe for me to consume is iced coffee, but even that is just kind of... generic. I'm not a boba person and I'm not going to try a third time for food that doesn't suck.

Super delicious, "non-traditional" Thai (which can get derailed occasionally - spiced eggplant with mozzarella?) that manages to turn out innovative dishes featuring the best of Thai cuisine (ingredients and flavors) in a casual, intimate and trendy-ish (but not too) environment. Must-have dishes include pumpkin curry, spinach with peanut sauce, smoked tofu salad with mango, and the mango with sticky rice for dessert. Decent selection of wines by the glass. Very reasonable prices.

This place is very popular in my area, though I've never had an experience that lived up to the hype. Most recently, I ordered a black milk tea with boba. It tasted like it was on the watery side, rather than a somewhat creamy consistency. The boba was an average texture, but I'm not really picky on the softness of my boba. The fruity bobas I've had always tasted powerdery to me, even though they advertise as fresh fruit drinks. I've had a few dishes in the past and nothing was really memorable or made me want to come back. There's a decent amount of table settings for mostly 2 people and small groups and it has a very clean and sleek feel. I've visited this place multiple times and I really wish I understood what everyone loves about it!

Orchid Thai is fantastic. The food is consistently delicious. Unassuming little place with small dining area and kitchen but wonderful staff. Definitely my go-to place for Thai food! I usually get the Tom Kha with chicken and Thai Fried Rice with chicken. My mother is extremely picky and even she loves it!

I really liked this place. We happened to pass by it after a tour of the penitentiary and decided to stop in for an early dinner. It is a small and quaint little place. The staff was very nice, attentive and knowledgeable. The prices are good as well. We got the pita and hummus, and i fell in love with it. The pita was so fresh.
