The artichokes constantinople was just delectable. The gyro were so delicious and juicy. Nothing was overdone or dry or undercooked for that matter. I definitely loved it!
The food is decent and prices are reasonable. Service was way too slow and inconsistent. The food came cold and flagged waiter seven times during dinner. Got annoying...

We go here a lot for boba and sometimes food, too. The employees are all very friendly and helpful if you're not sure what to order. It's more convenient than a full service restaurant when you just want to pick up a boba and they have tons of choices. I've only sampled the shaved ice, but I here such good things about it and plan to try it, especially this summer. The Brian's special and meatball sandwiches are good and the Nate boba ;-) is a good choice.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: My first time at South Ocean was a week ago. I've been back twice since then. First, their customer service is top notch. They are so friendly and welcoming. I felt at home...and I was taking mine to go. Their food is like a cloud wrapped in a rainbow dipped in angel tears. I can't even begin to say thank you enough to everyone at South Ocean. I prefer sushi rolls and did their lunch special today. The spicy salmon was a great balance of flavors. Miso soup wasn't too salty and the California roll was very fresh!! I highly recommend South Ocean to anyone interested in delicious sushi and Asian cuisine.
Pretty decent Thai food in Philly. We ordered the egg rolls, pineapple fried rice, pad prik khing and coconut rice pudding.

My first visit to Zeppoli and I will go back. It is small (12 tables) and fairly loud, but the staff is great and the food is outstanding! I do not agree with previous reviews stating that the portions are small. The course progression was very well done. I think that Zeppoli is suited for small groups of 4 or less. If you value quality, rustic Italian food without having to head into Philly, this place is for you.

Man, I wish we had one of these near my house. I can't fly all the way out to PA when the craving hits. My group ate here for dinner one night when we didn't get around to eating till pretty late. I wasn't sure what to expect because I'd never heard of Naf Naf Grill before but very glad we checked it out before heading home. The restaurant is CLEAN. That's the best word to describe it. Bright lights, bright colors, and everything looks brand new. The food is ordered over the counter and you see it prepared. The flavors are fantastic and the variety is great. Real shame I was only able to eat here once. The best part about my dinner here was how light the meal felt even though I was absolutely stuffed. The food is fresh, and the ingredients are so flavorful. Definitely something you'd expect from a restaurant in its location. Great job, Naf Naf Grill! Hopefully you open a location near Dallas some time in the future.

As many have already said, it's rare to find cheap food in the Quarters that is not a hot dog. Ali Baba's had really good gyros reasonably priced and definitely were a nice alternative for our wallets than paying another $11 for jambalaya or $4 for a slice of pizza. It's basically a hole in the wall, apparently started by a boxing trainer. The history of the place is probably more significant to the owners than tourists, the only thing that matters is...it's good food. it's reasonably priced. it's not pizza or hot dogs.

Amazing..I've been here on several occasions and the food has been phenomenal. Ambience was decorous and really felt that there was a lot of time and creativity into creating a high-end Thai experience. I'm not all that into ambience...the food is where it's at. i've had the Cuu Cee duck..delicious..the skin is grilled to perfection and the inside are tender and juicy. Topped with a delicious white sauce which i used sparingly to savor the flavor of the meat. Their curry dishes are good..spicy, hot, flavorful, creamy, no toning down of flavor here. The noodle dishes are spectacular..they are Americanized which i think is a good thing. (I've had my fair share of authentic thai dishes). There is a certain flavor to these noodle dishes, unique to Thai Orchid and not necessarily a bad thing at all...to be honest, i enjoy these noodles moreso than the 'authentic' noodles you'll find elsewhere..they really got Thai noodles down for the Blue bell area in my opinion. All in all, a gem of a restaurant serving great Thai food to the Blue Bell area.

Very professional on the phone. Understood me even though I didn't know what I wanted to ask. The gentleman was patient. They said my food would be ready in 30-45 mins. It was a little after that but we were in no huge rush. First time there we picked up our food and realized it's a really nice place to go eat. During or wait they offered us parties. The chicken patty was soooooo good. I haven't ever had one that good ever. And I'm 38 from NYC city of island food. Even heating it back up the next day it was soooo good. Curry chicken peas and rice. I didn't eat the salad though my partner had ox tails he said it was good just not enough meat. He said well do it again.

This place is amazing! The owners go above and beyond to make the customers happy! The food is perfect and the service is exquisite! Definitely a place everyone should visit! The ambiance of the restaurant is wonderful and the music rocks!

Fantastic Vietnamese food for Asian food lovers. Delicious and great value. Save the hassle driving downtown. Great location to eat for folks living in Delaware County. Try the Summer Roll or Spring Roll dipping in fish sauce! Mmmmhh Yummy!

Best Indian on the Main Line by a wide margin. Any review that is less than 4 stars is from one of those people that absolutely loves being unimpressed because it gives them the ability to write a pithy Yelp review. This place is incredible. Anyone who says otherwise is a pain in the ass.

There is nothing bad here. I've been here a couple times and their gyro, wings, fries, chicken kabob, and beef kabobs were top notch. The staff is extremely friendly and they make sure the food is to your liking. I will recommend anybody who goes to Busch Gardens to stop in.

Had a great dinner here with friends recently. First time here so didn't know what to expect. The menu is diverse. We started with pork belly lollipops (as delicious as they sound). Even better was the fried calamari appetizer. Spicy but slightly sweet and perfectly fried. Two of us had ramen that was delicious and a good size portion. Broth was flavorful and I am a stickler for a perfectly cooked egg (this one got close). My friend had the "Shaking Beef" with potatoes. I thought he was going to lick his plate. I managed to steal a bite and it was very good. Service was attentive at the beginning and thinned out a little as they got busy but overall very good. Parking is available in the garage next door and they validate.

Are you wondering what happened to Bitter Sweet? They may have closed their store but are on the dessert menu over at Steer Inn on 10th and Emerson. I tried the strawberry cake and it was the best I'd ever had...way better than the place on the A-list that sells for $13/slice in Broad Ripple and far less expensive!

After being spoiled by excellent Thai food in NY and NJ, I read the reviews to this place and thought I hit a jackpot. Unfortunately I didnt fall into pad thai heaven after my meal. I do think it has cute ambiance, service was friendly, my water glass was never empty and the bathroom was very clean. Sadly I dont go to a place to just sit there and use their toliet, I go to EAT! The food was just ok. We ordered the fresh spring rolls with shrimp as an appetizer and they were more carrots and wrap and one tiny shrimp. Anything that I have to bathe in sauce to eat, I dont think is worth it. I ordered the Kings Pad Thai with chicken and it was very good, a nice large portion and thank goodness bc my bf ordered the mango chicken and he hated it. There was nothing particularly special about the pad Thai besides the portion size. The mango chicken was just tons of over cooked veggies, barely any mango taste, and it wasnt even ripe mango, it was green mango which made the plate a bit bitter. I think the prices are a bit high for a Thai place, I guess they figured since its BYOB, they can inflate the price of chicken a little.....

I guess I was really expecting an amazing experience because my friends eat here all the time and have hyped it up so much. I wasn't really super thrilled with Pho Hoa any more than I was let down. I ordered a big bowl of the chicken noodle Pho (which for those not in the know is a noodle soup.) I guess what let me down the most was how SPARSE the dish was: literally just some sliced chicken, noodles, scallions and broth. They do provide a plate of bean sprouts and basil for the table to break up and add to their dishes, but I guess I was just hoping for more. It was tasty but kind of boring. Ironically my biggest gripe is the small selection of choices, especially starters; but my favourite part of the meal was my own starter, a fried tofu encrusted with cheese. Totally delish!

What a charming place with nice staff and delicious food. Went here Friday night for the first time with a friend. We both wanted to go somewhere neither of us had been. Seating and bar seats were immediately available at 7pm, which was nice. We sat at the bar. It would be a great date place, the area with tables was dimly lit and more intimate. The bar was lit more brightly but it didn't hinder the experience. Jose, our bartender, had perfect recommendations for food and wine/cocktails. I enjoyed everything i drank/ate. My friend and I shared a few things, since we really didn't know the portions. We started with the "famous" egg salad. It was 3 bread slices, like French bread. Egg Salad was on top and a whole anchovy. I was afraid. I said give me the smallest fish and I'll be brave. I tried without the fish and with the fish. The anchovy actually enhanced the taste, added a nice fresh ocean kinda fish taste and the right amount of saltiness. Next was the tuna melt and the peppers. The tuna melt wasn't mayo-ey at all and a fresh approach. It was really yummy. I can't remember what the pepper dish was actually called but it was highly recommended and my favorite of all 3 dishes. It came out red & thinly sliced with capers & bread slices and other things. It was sooooo good. Putting the peppers on bread, loved it. I'll go back just to taste that again. Anywho, give it a shot. I've only been once and tried 3 things. But I'll be back to try more. :)

If you aren't familiar with Ethiopian food. Basically they put a bunch of different foods on top of a big piece of injera which is a spongy bread. You tear off pieces of the injera and use it to scoop up the food. There is something really fun about the communal experience of eating this way. Although I cant speak to the authenticity of the food, I can say that I do enjoy it. The food is well seasoned and spicy. Major plus: The staff is extremely friendly and welcoming.

Zeppoli: currently my favorite restaurant in Collingswood and my go to dinner spot on Mondays (when the other restaurants in Collingswood are not open). This is some of the best Italian food I have ever had - it's important to note that this is a Sicilian Italian restaurant and very authentic to the type of cuisine you would experience in Sicily. (Not the typical type of Italian restaurant I've frequented in the past- as I'm definitely a chicken Parm kind of girl- but despite this it is some of the best food I've had and keeps me coming back again and again). I've been lucky enough by this point in time to have tried the majority of the items on the menu and I can honestly say everything I've had has been phenomenal. They have incredible pastas which you can get in half portions as appetizers or as entrees. My favorite by far is the traditional gnocchi on their menu which is served in a brown butter sage sauce and is unlike traditional gnocchi; instead of being made with potato it is made from ricotta cheese and spinach. Don't come here without trying it, it's incredible! Another favorite of mine is the ribeye- it has been cooked perfectly to my preference each time I've ordered it and is some of the most tender and deliciously seasoned steak I have ever had! Zeppoli is truly a gem in this area and as a foodie I couldn't be happier to live in the area and experience this incredible cuisine!

Everything we've had had been delicious! Spinach and egg sandwich, fruit, Mediterranean pita, potato and gram bean salad, strawberry cake, mini cheesecake, snicker doodle maple cream Whoopi pie, and chocolate chip cookie. Next visit we will try the turkey Ruben. The staff has been very pleasant. My only issue is with the hours. Earlier hours would be more conducive to a breakfast crowd.

SO GOOD!! I had Ekta twice before, the first was for my first date with my now wife! I didn't remember how delicious it is!! I liked this location--the staff is friendly and prompt & the decor is really pretty. They give you wafers and sauce to munch on--so good!! We ordered vegetable samosa to start--crispy, flaky & flavorful. For our main course we shared tandoori chicken and saag aur paneer with rice. Everything was really flavorful. The chicken was tender and the cheese in the saag paneer was soft, but not too soft. I literally cannot wait to go back!

Best Pho broth in Nashville, star anise shines through. The broth is comparable to what I have had in DC and San Fran. Terrible service, cash only. Affordable and consistently what we expect. We drive 20 miles to go here, mostly because the place we used to go to on Nolensville burned down.

Definitely extremely over rated. Was told they we're featuring eggplant, which we love so we we're cool with that. But it was very mushy and just kinda amateur. For the prices and and portions they should be on point. It seemed a bit chaotic and disorganized. After we placed wine order, we then had two other servers come and introduce themselves and try to take an order. I appreciate a staff that is eager to wait on people, but it was really strange. The place itself is cute but I think we'll stick to Blood and Sand from now on. Bummer we wanted to like it since it is so close to our house.

Went with a few people for a dinner of appetizers, and I ate veggie-only ones. The papaya salad and the mango sticky rice in particular were tasty. Fantastic service, nice ambience, reasonable prices!

The menu includes typical Latin dishes like arroz con pollo, carne asada, ropa vieja, etc. We were there at 6pm on a Thursday and there were only 4 other people in the restaurant. We started with empanadas. The chicken was a little dry but the filling was flavorful. I had the ropa vieja, which was delicious! The stew was so flavorful with olives, onions, cilantro. The maduros (fried sweet plantains) were mushy, a little too ripe or overlooked. My friend had a steak that was cooked perfectly. The black beans have a nice hint of citrus. The service was great.

My girlfriend and I moved into the Grad Hospital area several months ago and LaVa immediately became our new coffee shop. What we didn't expect was for it to also become one of our favorite lunch and dinner spots too! To start with, the coffee is fantastic (La Colombe) and the service is great. I particularly enjoy the iced coffee and more often than not, the iced red-eye, as it isn't bitter and tastes great! I also really like that you can order larger sizes and the prices are reasonable. As far as the food goes - it's fantastic! Israeli influenced and consistently great! My favorite dish is the Pargiyot, which is grilled chicken that just tastes great with rice, hummus, and a little salad of cucumbers. My girlfriend and I often say we are just so happy to have LaVa in our neighborhood!

I've been waiting to try Go! Gyro! Go! for some time and finally got to experience their yummy food yesterday at ArtFeast at Crestwood Court. I was looking forward to their food so much that I waited for them to open and I it was worth it! I ordered the Chicken Tahini Gyro ($7.50) which comes with roasted potatoes, however they were not yet ready yet so they took $1 off my order. I was kind of dissapointed with no potatoes but the gyro was so filling and delicious, that I didn't miss them. Not to mention, Go! Gyro! Go! was very apologetic about the potatoes. I will be back to try the roasted potatoes - I've heard they are a great compliment to the gyro's.

Kind of a down, as in depressing, atmosphere. Okay service, no music outside, and the food was pretty ordinary at best. Pretty disappointed. Don't see ourselves coming back. Nothing compares to Thai Spicy in Greenwood. Thought of this place because it's closer to home and it was a new experience. Just not good. Too sad.

The food is always delicious when I come, but the service is not that great. Sadly, I don't come here as often as I used to or want to because I know other places with the same quality of food and much BETTER service. It's fine when there are one or two tables filled, but once it gets busy, you will be waiting a very, very long time to order food and be served.

First time here. Very impressed with the food. Had the jerk chicken, rice and plantains. Very flavorful. Jerk spice was on point...wish I had more though. Enough food for me to have for lunch tomorrow. Will definitely go back because I love plantains.
Good basic Viet with no frills and priced right for the nearby Colleges. Nothing over the top but a good vibe and energy. Crowds come quick.

This is my favorite market to stop in. The new bakery is amazing with fresh bread, hand pies, cookies, and other delectable desserts. They have a great selection of olives, cheese, spices, Turkish meats, and pantry staples. You have to stop in to see all of the offerings. I always leave buying more than I intended to!

My husband and I decided to go to this buffet after finding out that the one we really wanted to go to was closing at 3:00 and it was 2:45 p.m. I called to make sure that this eatery was opened and they were going to be opened until 3:30 p.m. When we arrived we were shown to a table and then left to our own devices. I had to go to the cashier to find out how the process worked. After we had gotten our food we realized that we had nothing to drink or was anything offered. I spotted some pitchers of water and went over to get water. The lady apologized for not giving us water. No offer or mention of other drinks was made. The sweet and sour chicken was salty and didn't taste good. All the breads kind of tasted the same....while there was a wide variety the flavors were very similar and there was a commonality of extra salt. When we were leaving the cashier told us to come earlier next time and I was left wondering whether the subpar service had been an effort to get us to leave. I will not be returning.

Being in town from Houston for mini vaca, my hubby went on yelp to look for a Vietnamese restaurant and he tried to convince me to come here since I wanted to go to another one. As usual, he is right. We ordered 2 bowls of beef noodle soup and they were delicious. I'm really impressed by the egg rolls . They were so so good compare to most of the Viet restaurants I've been in Houston. The spring rolls menu looks yummy too but we were so full so sadly we had to save them for next trip when we're back in town. And the girl who took the order was so kind and friendly . I give it 4 stars bc I think it's just lil pricey. Otherwise, a must try place folks.
Solid bowl of pho and great restaurant atmosphere. Nothing that blew me away but it had a fair mix of noodles and meats

I feel bad writing this review. The people serving the food were so very very nice. The food is so heavy in grease and oil, everyone felt so sick and had stomach pain after. Even felt the food coming back up. I can't come back.

The lady at the register was very nice and also inquired about how me and my girlfriends day was going! The food was brought to us in less than 10 minutes, and everything tasted wonderful! They have so many different dishes with a variety of different flavors so no matter what kind of food you are in the mood for, you can pretty much find that flavor of noodle (or a noodle inspired version of that dish) on the menu! They have many gluten free and vegan options as well for those who can only have those! The food was delicious! For such a low key and causal feel, the quality of the meal was like something you would expect to find in a fancy "date night" restaurant! Noodles and company is a gem!

Thai Place is my favorite...well...Thai place, in the suburbs. It's almost as good as some of the spots in Philly. The pad Thai is amongst the best I've had, mainly because there's a Smokey flavor to it, and I love burnt food. I usually get takeout, but the dine-in experience was good from what I can remember...except the one time when one of the chefs must have called out, because I saw the waitresses cooking in the back. Hence, service was unusually slow that day. Overall, I highly recommend this place, and I'm already a regular here.

This place is my new favorite spot for authentic Jamaican food in Nashville! The restaurant is inviting and well-decorated, our server was attentive and friendly. We went for a late lunch on a Sunday and it was not very busy at all. I ordered the curry goat, and my friend got the curry chicken. Both dishes come with rice and peas or coconut white rice, cabbage, carrots and plantain. The curry got was so delicious I forgot to offer some to my friend, or ask to sample her curry chicken. It was well seasoned, not too spicy (I got the lowest heat level and it was perfect for me) and the meat was so tender. My only complaint was they only gave me 2 pieces of plantain, but my guess is if I'd asked for more they would have been nice enough to give me some. I also ordered the pina colada smoothie which was yummy. We had a great experience here and will be back very soon. Next time I'm going to try the Jamaica pea soup and the rum cake!

Wow. I am so glad I stopped here. I grew up eating this food almost every night. I'm way away from home...sometimes I crave my aunts cooking but I don't bother going to any places that serve it cause it just isn't the same as what I'm used to. This was the best meal I've had in a long time. The curry goat was amazing. Honestly, thats not even a good enough word to describe it. Not one bad thing about the oxtail and the rice and peas were perfect. The food was still hot when I got home I didn't even have to heat it up. This is now my favorite comfort food spot. Also, everyone was SO so friendly and polite on the phone and when I got there to pick up my food. Not the cheesy friendly either. That's rare!

LOVE this place. You will definitely need a reservation. Seasonal menu, and the flavors are amazing. We've dined here about 3 times. As you can see from other reviews, the place is worth it! Besides the food...one thing we tried was the Sicilian Lemonade...WOW! Very unique drink and extremely refreshing.

I signed up for yelp just to review, and after seeing the nasty comment that is clearly from a would-be rival coffee shop owner --- smileys is about so much more than coffee! The word 'cafe' is used in Mediterranean / Middle East to refer to any small wondrous place that serves food but does not have a huge kitchen / servicing staff / etc. Yes, they do have coffee. No, I haven't tried it. But to critique smileys for the coffee without trying the food is like lambasting the opening act to a show without bothering to stay for the main event. The best food i have had in manayunk (handy nasty is also amazing) - fresh, healthy, delicious, reasonably priced, smiley service. I go there at least 2x/week, and find myself inviting people over just so I have another excuse to eat there again. The baba ganouj is amazing, the Greek salad is uber tasty (you get a side of it with the platters, along with hummus), and I've enjoyed the falafel, beef gyro, and chicken gyro. And the hummus! Owners are super friendly, offer free tastings of baklava. Phone number: 267 323 2098

I dined here in early January 2016. The quality of the food was sub-par in every way. My husband had to return his dish because it was flavorless, and was supposed to be spicy. I will not return. The server was pleasant and smiling, which I appreciated.

After a weekend of having burgers and fries, I was like I need some rice!! We were staying at the Holiday Inn in Carpinteria so the restaurant was in close proximity. I ordered the food to go since we had dogs with us but while I waited I had some time to observe the dining area. Waitresses were nice and friendly. I asked for some water while I waited and they offered for me to sit in their back patio. The inside decor was quaint and dark. It seemed to have pretty good business inside. The outside had authentic looking Thai patios. I wish I had taken a picture to show you - but it looks cool. I wanted to eat in there. We ordered pad kee mao, curry chicken panang, spicy beef fried rice, pad thai and three orders of white rice. Total bill came out to $44.92. Not too shabby. Food breakdown: Pad kee mao - looked different from all the other times we've ordered the same dish at other Thai resturants. However, still was good and spicy. I didn't really eat too much of it since this was my bf's pick. But he said it was two thumbs up. Spicy beef fried rice - N/A I didn't try it at all. Pad thai - tastes the same as anywhere else. So I guess that must be a good thing? Totally got what I expected. Not too much sauce but still had enough seasoning. Semi sweet. Chicken curry panang - mmmmmm delicious! My favorite part of the meal. Did not expect it to be as spicy as it was! So incase you can't handle the heat, make sure to ask them to make it mild. The curry was slightly sweet and extra spicy. I kept coming for more. Definitely a good choice at this place. It sure doesn't compare to Thai town in LA, but I think this restaurant is definitely great for Carpinteria. It's a place I'd definitely stop by again if I'm ever in the area.

Great food and great staff. The food is always consistent when I come into this restaurant of Middle Eastern goodness. I mean my goodness people, are we in Beirut or something!?! You won't find any mediterranean food like this in all of Nashville. Their food is delicious and always consistent, their service is always spot on, and they are always friendly. Look for the bald guy with glasses, he will make make you laugh. I will always come back for my gyro fix.

I was taken here by a buddy of mine. I ordered a Ban Mi, Vietnamese Iced Coffee, and spring rolls. The Ban Mi was delicious! I gave it four stars because I am a bigger fan of the Vietnamese restaurant named Ban Mi off of Waters Ave and Dale Mabry. I would definitely go back here if I am in the area. It is tucked into a shopping block and you could pass it or may have passed by it without noticing. Stop in and try some of the good food they offer!

Absolutely the worst service ever . Walked in thinking everything would be great. The 2 girls working here can't even get the drinks straight let alone food . We ordered a Cuban apparently the local favorite and ceviche got charged an arm and a leg for it and had maybe 4 shrimp cut up and some hunks of tilapia not near worth the price( taste was good ) and then the Cuban which we split had mangled pork with tendons and fat all over it and maybe one slice of ham and the thinnest piece of cheese my half was nothing but pickles and fat . Worst ever !!!! To boot it was put on garlic bread !!! I'm a chef and I feel bad for the owners of this place . The bartenders made the same drinks 2 times in a row !!! HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE!!! Also the server was in pajamas and when she came to our table told us it's not her fault she's just passing they and decided to help !!! Wow that's all I can say !! Stay away from here

Kalamata's is without a doubt one of my FAVORITE places in Nashville. Their food is made fresh every day and they deliver incredible/consistent food every time. I would have their $10.75 salmon special over ANY other salmon at any fancy restaurant any day of the week. A true mediterranean experience to the T. I can't say enough, incredible-always!
Great food and service. Must visit if your in the Tampa area. Real Jamaica food and drinks

Great food! I've never had anything here that I didn't like. Their naan is EXCEPTIONAL! I will say that I prefer Ghandi's for a couple of reasons. 1. Ghandi's has better customer service by far. 2. Ghandi's food is just slightly better (except for the naan). But Sher-e-Punjab is very close to my house, so I usually just go there and I've always been very happy with the food. I highly recommend it!

A Groupon first lured us here (make sure you mention it prior to seating--they'll love you more) and the food will lure us back. FOOD Sounds crazy, but the food tasted like some Thai Grandma was in the kitchen cooking it specifically for me (while her son makes the plate look pretty) The proteins were cooked well and not overwhelmed by any of the seasoning. Vegetables tasted fresh. Thai food done wrong can easily get drowned in strong spices, but this place keeps afloat. SERVICE What? An Asian restaurant with Asian servers who actually show personality? There was a lot of smiles... however... THEY ARE SO SO SO SLOW. Timing was totally off despite having all servers' hands on deck. It was slow service before a server initially helped us, slow to filling water glasses, slow to bringing food out and getting the bill. ATMOSPHERE Prices are similar to other Thai restaurants. While decorated, this place doesn't look like an elaborate Thai temple... so you don't have to whisper all night and doesn't have a very "date night" atmosphere (at least during busy nights)

Probably the best place to eat on campus. I always got the chicken pita meal for lunch while attending UCSB. It was so delicious and all for a reasonable price. I'd highly recommend. Now that I've graduated I miss eating here.
This is the best breakfast I have had in years. Hash browns are excellent. Say yes to onions in your hash browns. Corn beef hash was perfect with 2 eggs over easy. It will be hard to beat this meal.

I suppose the food here deserves four stars, but the service was subpar and the restaurant smelled like a cat litter box. Ordered fresh veggie spring rolls as an appetizer and rice noodle soup with meatballs. Both were great. I frequently order chicken pad Thai as takeout from this restaurant and it is wonderful, as well. Not sure if they actually have a cat litter box behind the corner booth or what, but the table I was sitting at was so unpleasant that I asked the server to move me somewhere else. I try to not be picky about things but this was ridiculous. After my inquiry, I was relocated to another table that wasn't anywhere near as bad as my first one. Unfortunately, the server was rude after that and I had to ask for water twice before she brought me one. Will revisit Thailand Restaurant and update my review in a few weeks. Hopefully that was a one-time bad experience. Always willing to give them another chance since the food never disappoints.

Finally stopped by on my way home last night and glad I did. They have a thorough but not too huge menu of gyros. I had the Delux Gyro and house salad. Loads of good food. They meat was plentiful and hearty. The pita was just perfect--soft but not so squishy that it fell apart. Don't expect fries with your sandwich--the owner (?) is proud to say that they don't offer anything that had to be cooked in oil.
Everything from the service to the food was excellent. The Pad Thai I had was really good and a huge amount for the price. Lunch prices are awsome. Will be coming back.

In a nut shell..bad food, bad service and extremely slow. It used to be better but since the change of management things have spiraled down. Although some of my friends love this place and the service too. I will give it one more shot, although I highly doubt it will change my opinion.

This place is AMAZING! My girlfriend and I stopped by for a quick lunch on a weekday. They are located right on Main Street. He woman behind the counter was so friendly and kind! We got the beef gyros and split a small Greek salad. If you're a light eater the small salad alone would be enough. Or split the gyro with someone else. That being said everything was so delicious and it's the kind of food that doesn't leave you feeling grossly full. The gyro was on fresh pita with a garlicy tzatsiki. So good. Definitely will return!
Tom Kha & Larb --- really good.
Lesson to self. Never ever try small town chinese food again! Everything tastes diff. from what i ordered.
The food is so delicious! You can't go wrong with the Shrimps and Chicken wings combo with French fries.

awesome dive bar!!!! $3 citywides here! LOOOOOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE. also $9 pitchers (like real actual large pitchers, not the lame ones with a big hollowed out area in the middle for ice but it means it's actually only half a pitcher). SO MUCH CHEAP ALCOHOL.

We had dinner at Guru's tonight because I couldn't take the same boring dining choices! The staff was so kind & patient. They helped us pick vegan dishes for our daughter that were not too spicy. She loved everything! I definitely recommend the sweet corn soup, aloo jeera, tandoori & tikka chicken, but everything we had was delicious & fresh. I'm originally from New York & frequently dismayed by the dining choices in the area. I'm so happy we found this gem!

True to what ha been said this food has some heat. So I ordered mild and it stil gave me hot flashes. When I walked in the place had a variety of "personalities" present (only two tables had patrons and one person at the sushi bar). I don't think I will be brave enough to eat the sushi. Doesn't seem the place gets enough business to do fresh sushi (as fresh as it can be for Nashville). I was ordering to go. I ordered some dumplings made with chicken and shrimp. They were overcooked, the wrapping was soggy and the filling was a little to firm. I also ordered the red noodles at the bottom of the list of noodles on the menu. I was exited about the cakes that were supposed be be in this dish but when I got home there were none. It didn't take long for my food to be prepared but my food was over cooked which maybe me wonder if I just got some reheated fair. My noodles were falling apart and my seafood was tough. Maybe it was an off day but I don't think this is going to get a second try from me. I will stick with king market further down the road, ginger off Thompson lane.

I am dropping my rating from 4 to 2 stars. Food was horrible last two visits. Dosa was not cooked properly, Coconut chutney was like water. The lady at the counter didn't care for our business. It' s like there are two sets of people that manage the restaurant on a day to day basis. When there is a college kid/white lady at the counter and the mexican cook the food turns out to be good and service is great. But when there is someone else, the food is horrible. Hope the owner fixes these issues soon.
Fast, friendly, delicious, and affordable! Best place to eat in Manayunk!
Surprisingly good for a strip mall sushi place. Cute interior, clean updated bathrooms, good service. Sushi was very good

Okay... a bit pricey - they sell you the bowl as of it is the same cost... a bit of false push marketing going on at the point of sale. Pita is cheaper, in reality Decent food... not bad, but not amazing Might be better to look elsewhere

If I could give no stars and still leave a review I would. Their food is way over priced and not worth it. I would have been happier next door at Steak and Shake to be honest, and they're trash. The only thing I enjoyed was the sweet tea. I got a cup of soup and a "half salad" and payed over $20 for it. The soup broth had OK flavor but was stone cold when I got it. The chicken is frozen, pre sliced, and pre cooked, tasted like rubber. You only get one ramekin of dressing and they charge for an extra one, when it clearly isn't enough. Absolutely unacceptable. Their menu is misleading and they are also confused about it. I will NOT be returning.

I was hoping this place would be on point because I really wanted a go-to Mediterranean spot near work. Nothing was particularly terrible, but nothing was that good either. The hummus tasted like nothing and looks like thick mashed potatoes with chalk dust mixed in. It's like mortar. And the pita bread looked good on the outside but has a super soft, elastic, squishy inside (like a bagel) with a slight sweetness and a hint of sourness like sourdough bread. Sounds as if it might be good but it didn't go with the rest of the food very well (or even by itself to be honest). I didn't even finish the bread (and I LOVE bread! I bake all kinds of stuff at home and go to certain restaurants just for the bread!). Because I feel that bread and hummus are staples to any middle eastern dish, I have to give this place a low rating. I would give it a 2.5 if I could. It wasn't so bad that I would necessarily steer people away from here, because they might have different standards, but I was disappointed enough that I won't be back. For $10 a dish, there are other options in the area that don't disappoint as much.
Very good green curry and the price is great too. It's a small restaurant with a family - run feel

It sadden me to give this place this review. But they really upset me December 12, 2015 in the morning. My coworker and me came in at 11:15 am, they were suppose to be open at 11:00 am. My dad owns a Thai Restaurant too and he's always there 2-3 hours before opening to prep all the vegetables, meats, and noodle. So I had a feeling already it would be bad since they came in late. We decided to order, fresh shrimp rolls and medium beef pho. I love the fresh roll there, it's the best of all the places I have been to in TN. When the pho came out, I took my chopstick to stir up the bundle of noodle only to find the noodles where tiny little 3-4 inch strands chunks and not bundle. My coworker got the same thing. Not only where they short but they were super soggy. The new rice noodle usually have to be submerge in water to for about 30-45min to soften them up. And they just opened not 15 minutes ago. So it led me to think these are probably old strands from leftovers from yesterday night. I would be able to accept if they told us the truth and offer us alternatives for their lack of responsibility for opening late, but instead they gave us half-assed pho and expect us to eat it. Really disappointed me because I really liked their pho. But what disappointed me the most was the fact they try to sell that to their customers. Which makes me wonder what else have they doing to cut corners? Overall I won't be eating there again. I am too paranoid on what else they are doing to cut down cost. And the fact they have the moral and ethnics to serve that to customers kills me.

This place was a decent Indian buffet, having a pretty good choice of foods. I decided to try this out with some friends on a Tuesday when sitar (our fave Indian buffet in Ucity). Their chutneys were not as flavorful as others I have tried, but i definitely was able to still enjoy my meal. I had their paneer tikka masala which was pretty good. Their butter chicken was very very sweet. Would recommend this place over New Delhi for sure.
Very upset this place has changed hands. Was a really great authentic sushi restaurant. Now, just like everywhere else in Florida.

Yesterday me and the hub decided we wanted some Caribbean food for dinner so i found this lovley place on here which is up the st from where i live.. yes yes yes is all i can say the food..the music and the owner and his son was wonderful... My hub had the oxtails and rice which was to die for he loved it..i had the curry shrimp and rice it was a bit spicy but delicious..this place is mades u feel like your at home i will be going back soon

After not having middle eastern food in a year, I decided to try this place on Busch. The decor is nothing to write home about, but they have nice music. I ordered the Petra Mixed grill and lentil soup. Lentil soup was decent. Ive had better in the UAE and Michigan. The Mixed grill was great, lots of food. Pita and hummus, Tomato/Onion Salad, 2-or 3 kabobs That was the highlight of the meal. They have the great Toum, white garlic sauce which was very yummy! My 2 main problems that kept it from getting a 4 stars are: 1) The server while nice seemed to only check on me sporadically. Im pretty low maintenance on service,(just bring the correct food, hot and dont mess up the bill)Even after I finished , it took something like 25 min to get the bill. I waved my hands frantically in the air, but it seemed for naught. 2) The white sauce is good,,but its kind of a low blow to charge 75 cents for a tiny smidge of it DURING the meal. In my favorite Michigan restaurant, La Marsa, pita and garlic sauce are complimentary during your meal. Only if you order it to go is there a charge. If the sauce was made of Uranium-238 or Monica Bellucci's toenails , I could understand. Its just garlic, olive oil, and spices lol. Maybe one should consider carryout for this place.

This place is surprising good. I've had just about everything on the menu. Good hummus and chicken, average falafel. Sea food is very good. Most stuff is fried but you get baked fish. Service is a little slow but its good food for the price. When they 1st opened they had really good fries but seemed to have changed to frozen stake fries in reason months. I wish they would go back to the old fries.

We had a party this past weekend of about 40 people and had dinner catered by Nirvana. We ordered Samosa Chat and Chili chicken for apps and for dinner we had paneer kalimirchi and chicken tikka masala. Everyone loved the food and there was plenty of it. Thank you Nirvana.
Incredible selection!! The staff asked me multiple times if I needed any help and offered help if I had any questions if I didn't know what I was looking at. The food is delicious!
Really good and the price is right. I wish I lived within 10 miles so I could get delivery!!

Nestled in a small farmers market sits this Indian restaurant .food is made with fresh ingredients and very delicious ..we had the best vada Pav, misal, Pav Bhajee..With traditional Indian fare, a very affordable food..highly recommended

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Excellent food!! Professional, friendly staff! This restaurant is beyond 5 stars. Perfect downtown location too

I am Indian and trust me I know Indian food. My other reviews can show how harsh I can be about some places but this place is special. Put it this way, I have introduced over thirty people between my brother and myself to this restaurant and everyone has raved about how amazing it is. It is so amazing that I order there once a week and when I get carry out the waiters know my voice and what I would like. There are two waiters who simply do not get enough credit. They are the sweetest men I know and my brother and I have already decided when we get married we not only want POA to cater but those specific waiters to attend our wedding. There food is not only fantastic for how it tastes but it goes to show they don't cheapen out and water down the food like many buffets. During buffet they have 6 entrees!!! Three veg and three non veg and delicious appetizers! I literally cannot recommend a better Indian restaurant in the Philadelphia/south jersey region. I wrote a little tip for people that love spicy food. And I'm one of their regulars for ordering their spiciest meals so check it out if you're interested.

The storefront is basic, but the flavors that come out if this place are incredible!!!! Cooked to order. Nothing pre-made. I bought the Dibi Chicken and Plantains .... OMG! So fresh. Plantains are so delicious. A MUST is the Ginger Punch!!! Friendly people too. The cook, Halona is so nice and happy to share his cuisine. They work very hard and it shows in results.

Walking in we were greeted with smiles and the service continued to be great throughout our stay! We had Paneer Tikka Masala with garlic & cheese naan which was absolutely delicious! Can't wait to come back! Oh and the decor and cleanness was on point, very clean and tastefully decorated!

I have had this place bookmarked for quite some time now and could not wait to check it out! I am of Jamaican descent, so this food is what I grew up eating - yah mon! :-) I called in and ordered my oxtails and rice and peas dinner with a side of plantains. Yummm after reading some Yelp reviews, I decided it would be a good idea to also add the coconut cake to my order. Yes! The minute I walked in, I was greeted by a sweet lady hostess with a welcoming smile and then the owner Andre(?) came out with an equally warm smile to say hello and that my food would be ready shortly. How sweet! It was a comfy wait with wonderful slow reggae tunes playing and the dark ceilings and floors with the bright white booths and seating was so divine! It was inviting. I got my food and was sincerely thanked by Andre and was on my merry way. I got home and dug right in and the flavors of home hit my palate! The oxtail fell right off that bone and the rice was cooked to perfection. The plantains were also sweet and delicious. Even though my meal was for take out, the presentation of the food was top notch! The coconut cake was the perfect finish to my trip to Jamaica :-) it was moist and delicious and drizzled with caramel and accented with fresh blackberries & strawberry. I would highly recommend Yah Mon for takeout and can't wait to head back to dine in!

Great sunset and atmosphere. Had the ultimate bucket and oyster basket. Loved the fries. Hostess forgot to assign us a server so after awhile we alerted the manager who immediately got a great server for us. The hostess even came back to apologize. Will go again.

Zen Yai is one of the best Thai restaurants I have ever been to. The decor is fun and very different from any other Thai restaurant I've been to. It's small and dark, which gives an intimate feel. Also, since it's so small it never gets obnoxiously loud and the service is great. I love the food. It's spicy but not overly so, you can still taste the food. This seems to be very hard to master in Thai cooking. It is overpriced but what else can you expect with its State Street location?

Yo people you wanna go to the best BYOB restaurant in the city? Then this is the place. Come hungry and ready to have a great time. Ive had everything there and its always been 5 star. Its great for all occasions. You gotta try it if you're in the area. You wont be disappointed. Enjoy!!!

OPA!!! If you are looking for a Greek food fix in a pinch...Zeko's is your place. Great prices, amazing food and friendly people. I had the basic Gyro from here and it was great. The menu offers a lot of other options for people who may not want have authentic Greek. They had a chicken strip meal for kids and a nice salad selection. The indoor dining area was spacious and clean. My meal was $6.99 and it was a very hefty Gyro! Happy eating!

Saturday night with friends! Truly the best way to enjoy an evening out! My hubby and his friend have a thing for Gyros. We have eaten Gyros where ever we go, trying to find the elusive taste of the Tito's Gyro they first fell in love with. While the Gyro here was decent, it was NOT what they were looking for. Luckily for them this was not the night of the Gyro, this was a night of Mezes. This is a Greek Tavern. The best food in a tavern is ALWAYS the 'appetizers'. It also gives you the best chance at having various flavors and enjoying small bits of wonder. The evening started with drinks - I have read the other reviews and I am not certain what they are talking about -- the "Poseidon" was quite strong and the beer was exactly what they ordered. The soda and tea were refilled many times over for free, so . . . I will let you decide for yourselves about this. Tonight seemed to have been the 'bacon' night. The bacon wrapped olives, the bacon phyllo, etc. Needless to say these dishes were the hit of the evening. The scallops were perfect and the crab cakes were delicious. The eggplant fries were soft inside, crispy outside and the perfect accompaniment to the marinara sauce. Of course, after these spectacular dishes, the gyro was obviously nothing to write home about. The meat was good but it was just average when compared to the other mezes. Everyone raves over the flambé cheese (Saganaki) so it should be tried. Other things not to be missed - desserts! The size of the desserts make them perfect for sharing. And, while the Baklava is absolutely a dream when heated and served with a fresh drizzle of honey syrup, you absolutely MUST try the chocolate phyllo! This treat of crisp, flaky phyllo encasing a decadent chocolate filling served with a scoop of ice cream is simply something you should not miss out on. Several of my dining companions said that it was worth coming back just for this dish! The peach bread pudding was also very good but it just couldn't compare with the chocolate phyllo. Belly dancing is always fun to watch and it added that 'spark' to the evening that gave us something else to talk about. All in all, it was a wonderful experience. It's fun to enjoy an evening with my foodies and this was a great place to do just that!

I had one of those days where you have an emergency need for Indian food - you know, one of those days. I needed to bring it to an event at a certain time, but the first two places I called couldn't accommodate me. New Delhi (4004 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia), in fact, was particularly difficult to deal with. They were absolutely unwilling to help me get the food even while I tried to be flexible. Tandoor India came to save the day! PICK TANDOOR INDIA OVER NEW DELHI! They were helpful, courteous, nice, eager to help, quick, friendly, all around a life-saver. I said, "can you do this for me within 30 minutes?" and they said "absolutely" and it happened! And the food was great also. I'm not a great judge of Indian food because I haven't had a lot of Indian food, but I really enjoyed it.
A little expensive but it was a lot of fun and the atmosphere was great for a Wednesday night!

If I could give this ZERO STARS, I would. We ordered 3 orders of French Toast, and ALL of them had MOLD on the bread. It was absolutely disgusting. Now we're all sitting here feeling like we need to vomit. Don't order breakfast from here. I personally won't be ordering anything else either.

Great chicken korma, naan, samosa had pine nuts-one of the best I've had. Staff was incredibly nice. It is truly like eating in a store but it allows the owners to function in multiple ways ethnic store/restaurant/catering. Worth the trip if you are ok w zero ambience but food made w love.
Perfect blend of flavor. I ordered the Kufta lunch portion which is generous. The salad mixed with the hummus, rice and kebobs do the taste buds good. Will return for sure.

If you're craving Turkish cuisine which includes delicious grilled meats/ veggies/seafood and pita with various dips, then look no further. Sofra is probably the best choice in the city for well-prepared food. I highly recommend the pita with hummus, the grape-leave appetizers and the garlic shrimp as appetizers. You can't go wrong with any of the entree selections - there's something for everyone. I've also tried one of their Turkish pizzas, although prepared well - I found a hair in it so needless to say returned the dish but they made me a new one and by that point I was a bit turned off by eating it so it was just okay to me. The interior decor is kitschy but cozy. They are usually quite busy so be prepared to make reso's or try arriving early or later in the evening.

The first time I went I hadn't had Korean food in a long long time and I loved it. The second time was soon after and I went from loving it to just liking it. By the third time, I realized that it is good enough to satisfy a Korean food craving. Some of the previous Yelpers touched on this, it's good for St. Louis, but if you have had Korean food in a major city, like LA, you are probably going to be slightly disappointed. Stick with the basics and you will enjoy yourself. The atmosphere is old, but didn't appear too dirty. The service was friendly too.

From first glance it is easy to tell that this isn't your average food truck. The seasonal flowers and fresh fruit and produce are not traditional food truck decor, but the charcoal grill is the best marketing tool he has. You can smell the grill from blocks away. It was the grill smoke that first brought me to this food truck. There menu is made up of one option... The lunch always includes grilled chicken and falafel. Both are cooked very well but you must LOVE garlic to eat here. The chicken is sprinkled with dry garlic and the falafel has garlic inside of it. There is usually some sort of salad or rice that accompanies the falafel and chicken. The menu changes constantly but if you look at the ingredients he has on display you can sometimes predict what will be on the menu in the coming days. Overall the food is very good and you would never guess it was whipped up in a food truck. As you may of heard, the food is only half the experience. The cook is quite the character and has many pet peeves. He doesn't like too many questions, special orders, or people circling or investigating the truck. It's best to get in line, pay, and say thank you and leave. No questions no fuss! Any question can quickly lead to a lecture on the quality of what he is preparing. Some people don't know how to handle his enthusiasm and appear to be annoyed or offended when he goes off on a tangent. Simply agree, smile, pay, and enjoy!

This is easily one of my favorite Indian restaurants. All of their food is exceptional but their biryani is out of this world. I am also a huge fan of their paneer tikka masala which is the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and spice. Their rice a little less buttery/oily than some places and is seasoned with cumin and a touch of clove - amazing! They are a bit pricy, but not significantly moreso than any other Indian restaurant in the area.

We are traveling in our motorhome and this place was really convenient to our park. The fresh spring rolls were so good (and fresh). Shared Drunken noodles and there was plenty and really good. Only draw back was go cart track outside . Still would go back.

At first I wasn't sure if I would like La Va. But it has definitely won me over with its eclectic charm, friendly staff and most of all its consistently good coffee, chai tea and tasty food. I especially love the spiced chai and much to my surprise so does my "I don't like coffee or coffee shops" fiance. It's just that good. They also have great breakfast treats, like chocolate croissants and cream cheese pumpkin muffins and those super yummy spinach bureka's. This is especially nice since the Graduate Hospital 'hood doesn't have a lot of decent breakfast spots. The only thing I will say is that they should ask repeat customers to use the little La Va card they have on the counter. If you have one, they don't ask you for it and they don't offer it regularly to new people. I guess it's up to us to get our own discounts! Besides that La Va rocks.
Awesome chat! I've never had an iced chai that I've liked but the one I had here was great. Just the right strength and amount of spice. I just wish their menu was a little bigger.

The timings posted here and on the front door of the business are wrong. I showed up at 4 PM on a Sunday and they were closed. That is pretty unacceptable for a business that claims to be open throughout the day. Poor.

Moving from San Jose to Nashville meant sacrificing the standard of Vietnamese food, especially pho, that i was able to find, then i heard about Kien Giang. It is waaaaay cheaper than Miss Saigon, right across the asphalt, and waaaay better. Do not let the unassuming exterior and minimally decorated interior drive you away. The food is amazing. chicken soup has nothing on their Pho; it has a depth of flavor that penetrates to your very core. And at the price of $5 for a HUGE bowl it leaves you stuffed to the gills and still wanting more. other items of note include the bahn mi, which is an explosion of different tastes, textures, and temperatures for ONLY $2 for a whole sandwich. And everything on the menu is under $7. Literally everything.
BYOB and the best Indian food I've had in Philly to date! The Naan -- we tried 3 types -- was spot-on. As was the chicken Saag and chicken Marsala. Can't wait to revisit Zaika!

Great service. Cute restaurant and nice patio. They quickly made us a vegetarian version of the Tom Kha soup that was delicious. The Eggplant with Thai Basil was delicious and so fresh. The sticky coconut rice was perfect.

Whoa! I went here around 5:30 - right before they close, and the owner and I had a fabulous little chat. He let me sample so many of their drinks. Their lemongrass tea is quite refreshing. However, my favorite is definitely the mango milk tea. OMG. Best mango milk tea EVER!!! I decided to go the "healthy" route and have the Cap'n crunch crusted tilapia over salad, and I didn't even realize I was eating salad. It was delicious and filling. Though I'm sure it wasn't as healthy as I would like to believe. But shhh! Let me live in denial. :P This is one of those spots that you have to visit if you're ever in Philadelphia. Though if I were you, I'd go for lunch rather. They get sold out of most of their menu offerings by 5-ish.

Very neat place. The food was amazing. I would recommend going here with some friends and just shearing all the apps they are delicious. So is the rest of the menu. Very friendly and knowledgeable staff.
Tried veg and non veg thali here. Filter coffee is awesome. Felt like home food. Will come back for sure.

I was on this side of St. Pete doing some errands and decided to give this place a try based on the reviews. I'm so glad I did. I called to place an order for take out and the hostess was extremely helpful and polite. Once I stopped in to pick up my food, I noticed the cozy but stylish ambiance and all the employees seemed genuinely friendly. Most importantly, the mango lassi, garlic naan and chicken masala I ordered was amazing. I even had enough leftovers for lunch the next day. Although it isn't cheap, you get what you pay for. This is the best Indian food in the area. I actually live almost next door to another Indian restaurant (which isn't bad just not nearly as good as this one) but will drive an extra 15-20 minutes each way just to go here again. I will definitely be back.

This was a pleasant surprise! The food is tasty, servings generous and the calm ambience friendly for children. The bubbly wall and twirly lights were delightful. (We thought the 5-star ratings were staff-generated, but this is the real deal. A low cost 5-star experience).
Most awful Indian food. 16$ dollar curry without taste, thick uncooked nan, dry lamb, and fried rice in the name of biryani. Will never order from this place
Authentic Lao Food, Outstanding service, and Reasonable prices. What else can you ask for??

We ordered a variety of egg rolls and all were delicious. Of the ones I had, Korean Beef was my favorite, but all were really good. Baked not fried. There are some tables inside, but I'll do take out instead. Great and different idea for lunch or dinner!

Queen Vs. Fitler Though Dmitri's Fitler Square location is much more spacious and inviting, I think the Queen Village digs are the way to go. First of all, they give you bread AND grilled pita when you arrive. Fitler Square just offers bread. Second, their rice is NOTICEABLY less mushy and more flavorful. I actually wanted to eat it this time. I thought it was odd that there was one less scallop on my plate than when I ordered the same entree at Fitler Square, but it's alright. For a date- go to Queen Village. For a family gathering- take it to the Square.

I was extremely surprised how good the chicharones were, not too salty or oily but perfectly seasoned and fried. It is great addition to south st for a Latin/caribbean non Mexican restaurant to offer a variety of dishes. I would suggest the Cuban sandwich which was a delight. The services was acceptable for opening night. Our waitress was very nice and offered my son sample dishes but still learning the ropes.
I have had lunch at the Kabob house many times. The food has been consistent and very good. Love the rice even though I am not a rice fan. Priced very reasonable. Definitely recommend trying it!

Awesome food! Everything we had was amazing and was big on flavor. Mango Lassi, Chicken Tikka Masala, Garlic Naan, Coconut Soup. All yum. We will be back. Cant wait to try their buffet to sample other Indian foods.

By far the best Caribbean food in all of Tampa. The service and quality are top notch and the owners are very personable. The food is made fresh to order, so do not expect to be in and out in a short time. However, that's what makes the quality premium level. I recommend the Oxtails... Been eating Jamaican/West Indian food all my life, and Janise makes the best Oxtails ever! Jerk wings are also amazing, and my wife's preference is the stew chicken and the bread pudding for dessert. For authentic and delicious Caribbean food, Yah Mon is the place!

Great place! The food is so good! highly recommend!!!and definitely will be back! It is a new place in the same building where sushi house used to be. The place is very clean and beautifully decorated. I just came back from Thailand a couple of months ago, and I think this is the best place in town to get the best yummy Thai food:)

The food and service at Flambo was excellent! The server was very knowledgeable about the cuisine & took her time to explain what she recommended based off of our experience with Trinidadian food. We had the oxtails & curry chicken roti. Highly recommended. The food was flavorful and plentiful. I will be returning again!
Best Indian food I've had. We order from here a few times a month. Consistently good and we have never had an issue with service.

Went there on a whim this evening after downing a few delicious pints at a nearby brewery. Had a chance to meet the owner whom was awesome! But I must say the food is excellent! Some of the best in the entire area. Had the general tso shrimp and it was terrific. Highly recommend this to place. I'll be back!!!
Great buffet. This is a small family run place. The ambiance is shabby chic. Love the chicken tikka masala and the gulab jamun.

One of my favourite noodle soups is the Vietnamese bun bo hue. Everyone always talks about pho, but I like bun bo hue better. This spicy Vietnamese speciality originated in Central Vietnam, and features pork, beef, and thick rice noodles. Lemongrass is the predominant flavour in the broth and the heat from the chillies just opens up the sinuses when the cold weather hits. My go-to spot for bun bo hue in Edmonton is Trang Tien. This little family-run restaurant claims to have the best bun bo hue in the city - and I won't argue with that claim. The location is a bit sketchy with a hole-in-the-wall feel to it, but I love it. The restaurant has never been full on any of my visits, but there's always a smiling little boy that takes my order and serves me my food. This massive bowl of Hue's Beef Noodle Soup (#22, $10.25) always arrives steaming at the table with a plate of basil and bean sprouts to add into the bowl. Not that it needs any, though - the bowl is filled to the brim with noodles, beef, pork balls, fish cake, raw onions, green onions and shaved red cabbage. The soup has an amazing aroma and the depth of flavour in the broth comes through with every bite. The rice noodles are a great al dente texture and I like the contrasting crunch you get with the vegetables. Seriously, it is such a great bowl of noodles to warm the soul on a cold winter day.

I don't know that I have a whole lot to say about India's Kitchen, except that it was a decent dinner. Now don't take it to mean that I'm not giving praise. After all, 3 stars does mean "A-OK." But at the same time, I've eaten at a number of other Indian food restaurants that are as good or better. For our visit, we shared a vegetable appetizer. That was pretty good. A nice variety of breaded & fried vegetable-based items, all ot and with generous ingredient quantity. The rice for our entrees was good - delicate flavor and not sticky - like it should be. My wife enjoyed here chicken tikka masala, and my daughter enjoyed her chicken mango. I will shout out that the chicken in the chicken mango was extremely tender - but still firm and flavorful. My goat curry had a good, typical flavor. However, the volume of goat seemed a little skimpy when it arrived. And it was more than 50% bone, meaning that I was left a little hungry. That shouldn't happen. The final item we ordered was naan for each of us. The naan was excellent (I really like naan bread in general), but that is the case at most places. the visit was enjoyable. I'd go back again. But I'm not of the opinion that this is the Indian restaurant that has to be near the top of my list.

Ambience nice, clean and well maintained, although too dark for my taste. Service was friendly and attentive, but a bit slow and not knowledgeable about the menu or wines. Food was good, but not great. My La Zuppa (seafood, tomatoes, garlic, & liguini ) contained very little seafood and was almost tasteless. While not bad, certainly not worth the price charged. Left the restaurant feeling like I had been conned.

I ordered the beef tenderloin gyro. It is by far the worst gyro I have ever eaten in my life. The entire meal tasted like eating a lemon. The rice was equally as disgusting. Surprisingly the meal came with CHIPS. Very unauthentic, but it was the only good part of the meal. All in all, I wasted $12. This was my first and last time coming here. Very disappointing.

Decided to try this restaurant on a Saturday afternoon. A few of us ate from the buffet while others ordered off the menu. Everyone was very happy with the food from both! The buffet offered good selection of different dishes and the menu was extensive. I personally had the Dal Makhani along with Paneer Pakora and onion kulcha (bread)... everything was delicious and abundant. The Dal had a little bit of heat which was perfect for me, but if your not used to spicy food, you might ask to lower the heat level. The Pakora was by far my favorite. The folks who ate from the buffet were huge fans of the chicken tikka and the chicken tikka masala. We will definitely be back!

La Va is a great little neighborhood spot with comfy couches and lots of tables to sit at. The couches have large tables with magazines on them. Decor is pretty in that old world kinda way. I have been here several times for coffee, they have La Colombe so I know what to expect. Today I tried the Mexican Spiced Mocha, which is still to this day one of my favorite froo-froo coffee drinks. I tried it over ice and it was delicious. When I was a kid visiting Germany, I used to order the Wienersnitzel even though I didn't even really know what it was. All I knew is it was tasty and had a cool name. For my first time since Germany (like 15 years!) I saw Snitzel in the States, at La Va. They had two options, a platter or a sandwich. I opted for the sandwich, which had garlic ranch, feta, spinach and the beloved breaded chicken from my childhood. It was pressed on a paninni grill and served with a mediterranean salad of cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce, olives, and a light vinaigrette. Perfect lunch and a relaxing atmosphere to enjoy it in.

If the young girl isn't working, don't eat here! This place was our go to pho place. The soups came out fast, and food was always good. Here's why we won't be back. My husband, son & I went it on a Tuesday, and it wasn't busy. The mom took our order which was 2 soups. We watched two tables who came in after us get our food when we realized it was already 40 minutes and no soups we decided to wait another 5 minutes, but still no soup. We ended up leaving and told them they took to long. There's so many other better pho restaurants around, they need to step it up

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: I decided to come here because of the pictures of the entrees. The pad thai looked really great. I ordered mine to take out. I opened the box and was very disappointed. My chicken pad thai was noodles, noodles, noodles and about four little bites of chicken. The chicken seemed to be from the leg or thigh. I just wanted to let other Yelpees know. UPDATE: I received a humble apology from the owner. I have been cordially invited to their new location to give them another chance and it is uncharacteristic of their their food to have this lack of quality. I will take them up on their offer and they deserve a better rating due to their kind gesture and customer service.
All I can say is wow! Great food and great service. For a grab n' go place they have more food options than some of the big buffet places.

Coke to go, $1.99, 12 oz. You're kidding me, right? Ordered the Mulligatawny soup, paid for it, then they tell me they're out Got the sour chicken soup and a vegetarian appetizer, waited for almost half an hour, paid $20 before tip at lunch and barely received enough food to get me to an afternoon snack Food good and I very much liked it, but terrible value for the money

This was the second time I've been to BluePlate. The first time was for lunch and I wasn't impressed at all. I had a sandwich with roast beef and it wasn't very good. But friends kept telling us to try their breakfast so my husband and I went today. Again, we weren't impressed. The service was slow. My husband ordered creamed chipped beef and it was runny and didn't have much flavor. He said any diner he's ever been to does it better and cheaper. I had sausage gravy with eggs in the hole. It was ok. The worst part were the flies. We had to keep shooing them off our food. They were everywhere. The people behind us even complained to the waitress. The wall by our booth was dirty too. We won't be back.

A very nice place for authentic Indian Street Food. Vadapav and decontructed samosa chat are a must have on the menu. We had ordered a bunch of items on the menu and all were very good. Fresh Sugarcane juice is a big plus!!

Food was great, but had to ask someone to take our order. Then our food came out at all different times, and we had to check twice on remaining orders. Also out of plum wine. Appetizer came out with my meal as well. I would go back because I loved the soup but would try to go on a less busy night.

My favorite place in Nashville. Best Vietnamese. Nicest people. Everything I've tried has been absolutely delicious- pho, bahn mi (my favorite is lemongrass tofu), and the bahn cuon (rice rolls) are amazing. And their drinks are bomb too, especially the nuoc rau ma and the nuoc sam. Can't say enough good things about this place!

The last time my husband and I ate here (about 5 years ago) we were not impressed. Decided to give it a try, tonight, and WOW! What a difference a few years (and, apparently, a new owner) makes. It was excellent. I had the chicken satay combination dinner which came with yummy coconut soup, spring roll, white rice, a fried prawn and won ton chips. I practically licked the plate. Hubby had the Pad Thai combo with the sweet/sour soup. He loved all of it. Very gracious server and warm, inviting atmosphere. We are so happy that good food quality and value has been restored to the Siam Elephant!
I only had their lunch buffet. The food is excellent and the spices will make your pallets dance bravo to the chef and I can't wait to try their dinner menu.

Almost every time I get a to go order they completely forget about me then after I remind them the food has been sitting there in the box for 20 minutes. Great food but you need to watch for that. I will just go to another restaurant instead.

I stopped in for lunch the other day and enjoyed the meal but wasn't blown away. The lemon rice soup was good although quite bland and star hire than I am used to tasting with this soup. I did appreciate the slice of lemon that they added on the side. The stuffed grape leaves were quite good but the saganaki was bland and undercooked despite the rave reviews from so many others. Unfortunately, it was also what I had been looking forward to the most but the cheese wasn't particularly cooked and was rubbery without any of the gooeyness one expects. On a side note and not the reason for the rating but I was disappointed to not even get a single O-pah when it was lit on fire. Either way, the meal was decent. I have heard great things about Spiro's and would definitely return to try their entrees in hopes of a better experience next time. If I do and have a better experience then I will certainly add an updated score and review.

We decided to come here since it was one of the closest Indian restaurants to the KOP mall, and I wish we traveled a few more minutes to go elsewhere. The two stars is only because the food was half decent. We had the chana saag and paneer makhani with plain naan. We asked for medium spiciness, but it was actually not that spicy at all. Overall the food was sub-par. The service we had was quite horrible, most likely because they had two parties going on, but still, it was a nightmare. We walked in and waited about 5 minutes at the counter until we even saw someone who worked at the restaurant. They seated us with menus and no one came back over for about 10 minutes. We ordered our food and they gave us some water. Another person comes over and repeats our order, to make sure the other person got it right, I guess. The food comes out 20 minutes later and somehow it was the wrong food! They gave us lamb saag instead of chana saag. They took it back and left the paneer makhani and rice. At this point we were not given silverware or serving utensils yet so we couldn't even begin eating. They came out with the chana saag 5 minutes later... and we had to ask for silverware. At this point the paneer was room temperature. Another waiter came over and asked us is everything was okay and filled our waters. We asked for the check and it came 10 minutes later. Overall, really bad service and no apologizes were really given. Will we be coming back? No.

I'm a huge fan of this place! I've been here about 15 times over the past couple of years and really love it. Good atmosphere and the food is great. One of the best chicken vindaloo's I've had anywhere. Really looking forward to trying the new one opening in Glen Mills. Oh and do yourself a favor and get a King Fisher beer...its solid and an underrated beer.

Just for the amazing customer service alone I would go back, you feel like old friends the minute you walk through the door. It is just an added bonus that their food is also really good. My roomates and I are going to make going here a weekly thing.

I'm not that difficult to please when it comes to Thai food, but I can certainly appreciate when it's taken to a higher level. The dishes here are traditional, but have a refinement and clarity of flavor that I have not previously experienced. The service could have been a bit more coordinated, but given the price point and quality of food, I didn't have much trouble overlooking this.

I would like to recommend this Indian restaurant for mouth watering South Indian food.I don't want to say about biryani's here because it's already popular and many people suggested me to have biryani and I do agree now,It's very good than many Indian restaurants.We tried Mysore Masala Dosa,Egg Dosa,Chicken Fried Rice,Butter Chicken.Proper Tamil Nadu style Egg Dosa don't miss it.Mysore Masala dosa is delicious, Chutney and Sambar is as good as home food.Fried rice and Butter Chicken must give a try. Its compact restaurant but they are hygienic and very patient.Many To Go Orders. You missed 5/5 only because restaurant is compact else you people deserve the best

My wife and I had eaten around the corner at the old China Express many times. When they announced they were opening back up as Rice Box, I was very happy. We went in and had the Family Styled Vegetables with Bean Curd along with sides of the vegetarian egg rolls. Excellent service as it has always been. We will return!

I love love Remedy! I always get a Pomegranate Ginger Ale and a Butterchicken Wrap when I go. However I recently have gone and they seem to be changing the Butterchicken wrap. It's significantly inferior than what I have had before. Worse, today it was completely different, with a multi grain wrap and not containing all the ingredients. Not sure what's up with that but it was underwhelming.

Dear, Mr. Smiley. Please please please consider opening another location in Abington. Everything you make is delicious and so fresh! Your staff is so friendly and the place is so cute. We need more places like this!

Hands down the best pho in Philly. I find myself making excuses to come back days in a row, sometimes meals. The staff is no nonsense, you order soup, you get soup in less than 5 minutes. The broth is rich, soulful, and exotic. Every part of their pho, unlike its competition, is perfect, and most importantly, consistent. Fully recommend going out of your way to get down on this pho.

This is the best Indian food I've ever had and some of the best food I've ever had! Everything is delicious. The service is amazing. The owner helps us pick what we order and is just the most lovely woman! She is so friendly and welcoming. It's a huge menu and she's introduced us to some great new dishes. My fiancée and I eat there at least once a week! He loves it just as much and he used to live in India. It's clean and pretty and a place everyone should try! Oh and did I say how delicious the food is???

It is easier to reach being closer to 86th St than Major. My wife didn't like that she got a fixed veggie platter whereas at Major she could pick and choose what she wanted. Service wasn't very slow and the day we were there the credit cards were not working (at least not for the woman who was trying to pay and leave). So we paid cash to avoid the issue. I'll go back but only if I'm too lazy to drive the extra distance to Major.
Consistently very good food, great small plate choices. Parking in the area is a pain, but worth it.

Was a little bit skeptical at first because pho in Avon just sounds scary but this place is a little piece of Asian paradise in suburbia. The spring rolls are so fresh and delicious not to mention the pho is amazing. I think it might be better than my favorite pho place in West Lafayette on Purdue's Campus. Oh! And the boba tea is to die for

The two times I have given this restaurant a chance, I have had a bad experience. The food is undercooked and doesn't taste all that great. I would much rather spend my money elsewhere, even if it means less convenience and more money. The dim sum was bad and the boba has a weird consistency and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
