Great Paella. Have been here twice. Huge portions. All fresh tasting. Great value too.

Good lunch option in Downtown! Anyone who has been to Wilmington knows there aren't many options for a quick, tasty, affordable meal. This place rocks! You choose your protein, carb, and sauce. Add on as many fixings as you'd like and you have a tasty, quick, and filling meal. For those who have never had true "Indian" food this is a good way to see if you like curry or not. If you enjoyed your dish here it is time to visit one of the many full service Indian restaurants in Delaware Also, the staff here are so friendly!

Great place on Alberta Avenue for Vietnamese Food. Under new ownership and they have elevated their customer service and food is great. Always a friendly smile when you enter and I never have had a bad meal!

Best falafel sandwich I've had in franklin. It was amazing. I was expecting mediocre but was blown away. My husband was peeved about the plastic silverware, and always is when we're at a restaurant without real silverware, but other than that it was SO GOOD! Haha
Had dinner at this place first night in St. Pete. Great food and service. Will definitely come back.

My husband and I stopped by for a morning coffee with our dog. We both had iced coffee (standard taste). We shared a savory crepe that was a bit over priced. The bacon was over cooked too. You can choose to sit inside (the decor is quite nice) or you can sit outside (but beware-it sits next to an abandoned house.) Overall, I will go back for some coffee early in the AM. I may try a sweet crepe next time we visit. The cashier bussed our table, gave our dog a water bowl, and was pleasant enough for me to give this place another try :)

Like the food n convenient location... But expensive specially since the food isn't anything "to die for"...is thai...I've had better and I've had worse... it does come in generous helpings and all come with crab rangoons incl.

After a very long time I decided to go back to this place and boy was I glad I did. I reached the place at 9 pm hoping they were still open, but they were more than welcoming. The guy serving us suggest that they had dinner thali and I was instantly thrilled. It started with idli, vada, coconut chutney, sambar, masala dosa, pakoda, rice papad, sweet, aalu mutter, batura, and some other curries.. After which he asked us if we wanted more dosa, and we said yes! He got us 3 extra dosa and extra batura.. Best thali I've had in Nashville area.. Guys make some time and go to dosa Hut for dinner and you can have the complete north and south Indian cuisine in one plate for just $15 bucks.. Worth every penny you pay..!

This is my favorite restaurant. The food is amazing and the customer service is phenomenal. The service is very quick and the restaurant is very unique compared to chains. I always get the Pad See Ew with chicken and I would highly recommend it. Watch out though, they mean it when they say an item on the menu is spicy.

Despite favouring Indian food over almost any other cuisine, you might notice that I'm severely lacking in Indian restaurant reviews. In spite of my Indian fondness for butter chicken, saffron rice, every kind of curry EVER and of course, naan bread. There is a special place in my heart (and in my belly) for naan bread. So why don't I eat it more? Don't look at me. My darling husband wouldn't put it very high up on his list of favourite cuisines...so I either go at it alone or don't eat it at all. And I have this weird thing about eating at restaurants alone, so...I don't eat it at all, for the most part. That was a very long introduction to explain why I'm so thrilled about New Asian Village Express at Southgate Mall. There's no shame in eating at a food court by yourself, so I'm totally fine with dining here. The combo includes one of two kinds of rice (steamed or saffron), one of six curries (including my fav, butter chicken), potatoes (they're amazing), plus one of two salads (I go with caesar, a weird choice, but it's delicious). I haven't tried the samosas, but they're next on my hit list. I always order garlic naan bread with my meal, too. Last time, it came out a little crispy, but it was still full of the most perfect and delicious salty, garlicy, bready flavours. Perfect for scooping up that leftover curry! For $10-12 you'll go from very hungry to very full. Lots of hot, fresh food from a local joint for a great price!

I had the pleasure of being introduced to this place the other day. A nice, clean place with a pretty good selection of offerings on a chalkboard. There is plenty of seating upstairs. The staff is also friendly. Anyways, I ordered the falafel platter and it tasted great. The platter consisted of a bunch of fixings in addition to the bar of other fixings you can put in your falafel. With the platter, one also receives fries which were great! Not greasy but were full of flavor. A lot of the people there were ordering kabobs so they must be doing something right with those. I have love for food cart falafels, but these hit the spot.

I'm not an expert on Thai, but I enjoyed many meals at Nadias' during the six years that I lived in the Lansdale area. My usual meal would be the Lemon Grass soup, the Massaman curry with chicken and a Thai iced tea. Its' location, on the south side of the tracks at the Lansdale SEPTA station, makes it easy to get to even if you are limited to public transportation. I've never been there when it was more than half-full and it's generally quiet.

I come here pretty regularly for something cheap and quick. The food isn't the most flavorsome around, but it's worth the money for sure. The servers are all very nice and the service is usually pretty fast. I've been working my way through the vegetarian menu for some time now, and most entrees have been pretty good.

I love phoooo. I almost try every pho place around indianapolis area but this place pho was mediocre. I didn't like summer roll. Spring roll (fried one) was okay..... Also I have something to say about bubble tea... The person who was at the casher/ server made it in the kitchen, who knows if she washed hands after done with casher job. The tabiyocur didn't taste fresh and she put such a little amount of it that it barely filled the bottom. Of all, I will never have bubble tea again and maybe I'll have pho only when I'm really hungry.

This place is just okay. The menu is a little expensive for the quality of food you're getting. The dining room is more formal than a family-owned Italian restaurant, but the food is just the same. We had great service by Sonya, and the Groupon made it worth coming here. However, without a Groupon, I probably would not come back. The caprese salad was good, but the chicken was tough, and the tilapia and shrimp special was covered in tomato sauce. There were only two shrimp. Cheesecake was okay. Nothing noteworthy about this place, but it wasn't bad by any means.

They are one of the only places that will give you real heat if you ask for it. They don't go overboard on the fish sauce and their portions are bigger than most. The only drawback is that there is no tv and the beers aren't always available. But, the food is great, given in large portions, and it comes out quickly.

During the 2 weeks of xmas break, I vowed to not just stay home and try some of Tampa's diverse restaurants. I have no experience with Viet food, but the restaurant was clean and simple. There were some Asian families dining there the day I went, so it probably was authentic. I ordered number 20, since some people on yelp had recommended it. Rare steak pho. It was pretty good.vermicelli noodles with steak and some cilantro and other herb. I usually only eat soup on cold days. However it was 75 F on the day I went. It was a good meal, but not world-changing for me. The server didnt tell me, but I added the red hot sauce which made it 10 percent better.. There were some jalapenos and bean sprouts on a plate which came with it. The price on the menu said 7 bucks, but it was actually 8. slightly annoying. I ordered the Vietnamese Coffee, which IMO should be classified as a dessert more than a beverage. Very sweet. I like seet stuff, but this was a bit much. OVerall, a nice place with decent food at fair prices.

This place is awesome! I came here with my boyfriend to see and film our friend Dave Smolen's performance. Parking was street but easy to find (it was on a week night). I love how those at the bar were able to tune out (or at least ignore) the experimental music being blasted unbearably loudly in that tiny space. The drinks were cheap and REALLY strong. I felt really comfortable there. Great atmosphere. I don't venture into West Philly too often for leisure but if I did, I'd love to check this place out again on the weekends.
Very good Szechuan cuisine, the chef is from Chongqing area. Service is always good the staff are nice too.

This is NOT what I expected to find in a mall. Holy Cow is this a fantastic place if you are wanting authentic S E Asian food! Everything is made to order, I DO recomend the Spring Rolls, one bite and you will never want to eat anyplace else! This is not a chain place, the owner is the cook, and she is GOOD! Portions are good and the variety of different dishes is great considering the size of the restaurant. I found this place and I am going to be a regular from now on!

The food was decent and the pho is one of the better ones in the city. I am never really harsh with my reviews, but this place deserves it. The customer service is so unbelievably terrible I never want to go back there. I am not familiar with all Vietnamese dishes so when I asked the young man behind the counter about certain dishes he replied either rudely or sarcastically. There was a dish on their menu which I know is usually made in Chinese restaurants, when I asked him if it was Chinese or Vietnamese, he rolled his eyes and said well this is a Vietnamese restaurant. I have never been treated so rudely at a restaurant. Geez, maybe they should get real waitstaff instead of employing their angst teenage son. He seemed bothered I interrupted his Pokemon game. Anyways, if you want terrible service, dirty restaurant surroundings and okay food. It's fine. But there are WAY better Vietnamese restaurants in Edmonton.
I got the meifun Stir Fry with beef was flavourful.Beef was tender.My husband got Soup with Roat Duck with Ho Fun.Delicious Broth.Drinks Thai Iced Tea and Oishi Green Tea the Bomb.
Went here and was pleasantly surprised by their food. It's in a strip mall so if you blink you'll pass it. Everything was delicious.

Had a great late lunch when meeting up with friends. Beachy atmosphere, lovely breezes, and live music makes for an entertaining afternoon. My group ordered peel and eat shrimp (chilled) - probably the cleanest peel and eat shrimp I've ever had. The fish tacos were a rave at the table along with the seafood salad wrap - all fresh and tasty. The original nachos came with queso blanco and very fresh guacamole with lots of black olives and jalapeños - a good choice. Kids meal came served on a souvenir frisbee and teddy grahams.

I must admit, I was skeptical at first that a group of hipsters in Wilmington could cook Vietnamese food. They have managed to improve upon classic southeast Asian dishes that have already been perfected by centuries of cooks. They have taken pho and banh mi to the next level. I also like what they did with the Thai salad... It's nice to see some greens there for a change. Not sure what the obsession with cauliflower is... Must be a hipster thing
Authentic Ethiopian food served with love. Only authentic Ethiopian restaurant in tampa (that I know of) luckily is a very good one.

Probably the best Indian food in the suburbs (along with Aman's in Chalfont, which is northern Indian, while this place is southern Indian). The dosa (filled with potato and onion) was excellent as was my chicken chettinad and son's mixed grill of tandoori cooked chicken. Glad I found this place, about 20 min from my house but very worth the trip!

I was expecting a lot more. I came here early evening on a Saturday. It is BYO which is good. We started with the cold appetizer sampler -- wouldn't have been my first choice but my girlfriend wanted it, so okay. I was very disappointed immediately by the solitary dolmades on the plate. The various dips were nothing special at all. The hummus was very lackluster, and to be honest I'm suspicious that it came from a large store bought tub. I followed with the roast lamb. Again, disappointing. It was well seasoned, sure, but so dry and overcooked, which is a sin with roast lamb. I am actually wondering if it was tossed into the microwave given that it came so fast and it was early in the evening. The server was quite nice but the food was disappointing so I wouldn't recommend.

Interesting place with enough that made it "interesting" that I can't see a four star rating. No bathroom for customers. None of the variety of Thai pepper offerings (typically dried, ground, in oil and as a sauce) but they did offer a homemade version that was pretty good. No limes available with their Thai dishes. I had the Pad Thai and thought it was a bit strange. I opted for the vege option and it came out with a visible amount of broth on the plate...thus making me nervous that I would wear some spatter. The flavor was good but not what I was expecting from a Pad Thai and I just could not get over the amount of liquid on the plate which made me incredibly nervous about wearing the dish. I am glad I tried the place but really can't see myself going back there anytime soon.

Awful awful awful. I've been here multiple times and I've always had bad service, bad drinks, and bad food. My last experience capped them all. When I came in with a friend the host looked as though she would have rather of been chewing glass than doing her job. When being seated at the booth I noticing that the cushion part was broken and that the back rest was broken as well, I was actually able to feel the people behind me rocking back and forth causing me to be pushed forward. When I addressed this with the server his response was "I know it's broken." Which led me to ask why I was sat there if they knew it was broken. His response? "It's not that big of a deal." I should have left right then and there, but decided to move to another table. Drinks took about 15 minutes to get and the food was subpar and lukewarm. I will never be back, and advise everyone to not support this place.

I gave this place a try today while I was at work. I ordered online for delivery, and it took quite a bit longer to deliver than what they stated. It was about 20 minutes late. I got an order of fried pakora, and a vegetable mixed appetizer. Once we received them it was barely warm. It still tasted good though. My bad on ordering something fried for delivery. We also got an order of regular naan - also barely warm. For our meal we shared an order of chicken makhani, and it was delicious and piping hot! The chicken in it was delicious and tender, but there were a couple pieces that had little pieces of bone in them. I wasn't expecting that, but it was still really good. One thing I wasn't too fond of was that they didn't give us any utensils or napkins. I had to hunt down a spoon just to eat. Next time I will probably just dine in to insure everything is fresh and hot. I would order again, but forget the fried foods and just stick with the meals.

Came here one night to eat Ethiopian food me and my friend ordered the Beef tibs and gored gored it was flavorful and real quality Ethiopian food! Definitely give this place a try if your in West philly!

Good inexpensive restaurant I had dinner with friends on Saturday night. This restaurant does not look interesting from the outside but inside is very nice! The food was tasty, large portions, good prices. I had the Pad Thai and it was very good. The service was quick, good and pleasant.

We had the early bird special(s) tonight. The service was excellent, and the food portions on the early menu are big enough for two guests that are over 6" tall! I NEVER go to early bird special offerings....except tonight...and I am glad I did. I have been to The Pearl for the regular menu a few times...its great too. I had the sirloin steak 8 oz. cooked perfectly, and a nice size helping of steamed mixed vegetables. My friend had calfs liver and onions, and she said it was very good. She had split pea soup instead of the salad that I has as a starter. We will be back. BTW the waiter told us that on Monday nights, they have 1/2 off bottles of wine.

Great service! Sukho Thai's lunch dishes are very large in portion. This is conveniently located by the Opry Mills Mall. I recommend this place if you're not feeling like cafeteria food. I always order the chicken drunken noodles or laht Na which is consistently delish!

A solid representation of Thai food in Santa Barbara. The place is clean and I like the home-made feel to the interior design. The servers seem a little punch-drunk, but I didn't get any negative vibe from them. And we got the items that we ordered, even if we were a little worried based on how confused the waitress was by our orders. We started with CHICKEN SATAY and DUMPLINGS. All agreed that the satay was delicious--a good marinade and delicious peanut sauce. But I can't recommend the dumplings. They were bland and the sauce didn't help. Between the three of us, we split a PINEAPPLE CURRY, SPICY GROUND CHICKEN WITH BASIL, and EGGPLANT-TOFU. The spicy chicken took first place with a great balance of spicy, savory, and herbs. It hit the nail on the head. The pineapple curry missed the mark, but only by a little. The chef went overboard with the pineapple, in my opinion, so the dish took on a cloying sweetness. Either upping the ante with more chili or cutting back the fruit would have fixed this. The runt of the litter was the eggplant-tofu which lacked any direction. My first thought was: Thai hospital food. There were leftovers of all three dishes. Good deal.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: A great place for lunch with stylish dishes served fresh. Very comfortable environment. The staff are great.

I tried this spot last night and was disappointed. There are some good things about this spot: Takes online ordering Prepares the food fresh Smells amazing Good presentation The only thing missing.....taste! The yogurt saved my meal. The salad was fine and I don't like falafels but the chicken tasted like ....nothing. It was seasoned and smelled awesome but no taste. Hopefully they see this and will improve the flavor. I would try them again. They had my food ready on time and the worker was nice. Sn: I threw my leftovers in some shrimp bisque, delish!

I've only eaten here for dinner. Great food in a seemingly out of the way, hole in the wall type of a restaurant. Enter into a basement lunch-style restaurant, walk past the lunch-order counter and up to a nice little seating area in the back of the restaurant. Very tasty middle-eastern food. It's a BYOB, which is obviously nice. Great food for the price. My wife and I often go here before shows on Broad street. Never too busy, and sort of feels like a IYDKYDG place to ourselves when eating there.

The location is not that great. But, this restaurant is a fine vienamese one for me. Whenever I visit to Indy, I visit to this restaurant for their delicious food because I could not get good Vietnamese dishes in West Lafayette. Their "fish in the clay pot" is a hit for me. Their prices are very good too. I have never received a bad food there.

My friend invited me here, saying she had the best lamb curry here ever. I bought a red chicken curry, which was spicy and sweet. It was really good. They have really great service. The waitress was super nice. When restaurant was closing, my friend had been taking her precious time, but they did not hurry us at all. Instead they gave us more rice and water. I will definitely go again. Oh and it's really cute how they make rice pyramids!

I'm writing my feedback as I'm waiting for my food I've been here before they have good food but customer service suck I hate the blond one that works here she never smiles. This place is not cheap I want better service when I pay over $100 when I come here.

I've been ordering from Ninja Noodle for close to four years now and it has never disappointed me. I had some last night but realized I've never left a review. Their service is amazing and really fast. I was especially impressed last night cause it was steaming hot when it arrived. Super fresh! My absolute favorite dish that I can never get enough of is their szechuan beef. It's a really good balance of crispy and chewy. The flavor is mild, it could be a bit spicier, but it's still so satisfying to me. Their chicken fried rice is amazing as well compared to a lot of other places. What I love about this place is that they give you a lot for what you're paying for. I always have leftovers. Thank you Ninja Noodle for giving me great comfort food for the last few years!

Yet another good find in the state of PA. Service is great here, which surprises me. Appetizers are expensive but food is paid special attention. I'd say its worth it. Had the summer rolls. Very good. Banh beo hue style was rreeallly good. Had the bun Rieu. (Crab meat noodle soup) Also the bun bo hue. Bun bo hue was soso Bun Rieu was pretty good. Fried banana can't go wrong. A+ would return

Split an appetizer w some friends. The sampler is great. Food made w care. Takes a bit but well worth it. Also had the afghan style ice cream. Omg indescribable. W the red velvet hookah, the tastes were divine. Lots of louder, afghani and Turkish hip hop playing- it seemed to get louder as the night went on. Great service

Ok, I admit it - Indian is low on my ethnic food totem pole. Not completely at the bottom, that space is reserved for Ethiopian (too mushy for me - like eating a meal of different flavored baby food) but it's down there. HOWEVER, there are certain Indian dishes that I really really enjoy and India Palace does them the best. In particular, the Chicken Tikka Masala is excellent, I think it has a really good balance of creamy and spicy. I've only come at lunch time - coworkers love to go to the buffet.

I love the food, and it seems home made since it tastes a bit different every time. Love the colorful, pleasant décor and anticipation of new and exotic foods and tastes I am allergic to wheat and love that I can eat the Injera since it is made of teff flower. Not only are the prices and food amazing, but the owner comes by the table to say hello almost every time i've been there. Even occasionally offering free tastes of new wine and once a free container of their special tea blend when my friend asked about it. Great setting and it's great to go to a place that appreciates its patrons. The only down side is the service is almost always slow, but I think that is really more a matter of a slower paced atmosphere than inattentiveness. I've suggested Queen of Sheba to dozens of people, and no one who has gone has ever had anything negative to say.

Someone better call the cops because Bui's deals drugs. Don't believe me? Have any of their breakfast sandwiches and you will be a believer. They must lace every breakfast sandwich with crack because I get all itchy when I can't get one. On second thought, don't call the cops. I want this truck to stick around (:

My fiancé and I decided to come here one night because we had a Groupon. The food was great. The quality of the sushi was good and fresh. The service was attentive and friendly. I would be willing to go back again. Some of the prices are a little on the higher end compared to places where I've had the same sushi rolls, but this place does it well.

I ordered a gyro and it was absolutely delicious, lots of flavor. The service was quick and good customer service. We wanted to go somewhere that wasn't fast food, but not a restaurant, and this was the perfect in between.
Awesome Dishes and me and my wife liked the Apollo Fish

5 stars for the curry dish, 3 stars for the fried rice dish, and 2 stars for the noodle dish. The curry was delicious, good amount of spice and great price for the amount you get. It is all a great price, especially since they don't up the price for dinner time. The noodles were like a solid block, I didn't like the taste of them either. The rice was ok but I wouldn't order it again. I have definitely been back just for the tofu curries and recommend that. The meals are a good size, they are two meals for me when I get take out.
Try the pork chop rice and their vietnamesse coffee...the pho hoa are hands up!

Growing up in Hawaii I am very cultured when it comes to Asian food. Thai food is by far my favorite of all. After moving to Delco the only quality Thai food was found in the city. I don't have time to drive to the city every time I get a craving. Green Herb came and brought a smile to my face. I saw them while driving home one day and decided to give them a shot. Their food is amazing. It's not 5 star amazing, but more than satisfies my love for good Thai food. They are even available on Uber eats!!! Definitely check them out if you want some good Thai food.

I have been here 3 times a do not understand the managements stict policy of not allowing subsititutions. I was raised eating caribbean food so I find it very dissapointing that they cannot be flexible to their target clients requests. We had the bandeja paisa and they refused to substitue the ripe plantain for green plantain. Yet when the plate came in, the plantains sere not ripe but cooked as if the were. The sausage was way overcooked. The food generally lacked flavor. Giving 3 stars bc we had a large crowd and generally treated us right.

So I've been to Siam Cafe around 6-7 times now and I've been waiting to write a review. Last night I took my wife there for Valentines Day and it really served to seal the deal. So I'll start by telling you what we ordered because every single thing was delicious and the price is spot on. I recommend anyone new to thai or this restaurant, if you don't know what you like, try the following items. We had: Starters: Fried Spring Rolls, Steamed Dumplings, and a large pot of Tom Ka Kai Main Course - Red Curry Beef(spicy red curry with an assortment of mixed vegetables) Desert - Fried Bananas(bananas wrapped in won-ton skins deep fried soooo crispy and laced with honey and sesame seeds) We shared everything(which is the only way to do Chinese and Thai imo). Warning: DO NOT SKIP THE TOM KA KAI. I've had it at so many places but never as good as this. Its probably one of the best soups I've ever tasted in general. Try a little chili oil in it! I've also had Green Curry Chicken, Panang Beef, and the Disco Chicken all of which were very good, but the curries are my favorite for sure and they do them right. What did all this food come out to? 26 bucks! Atmosphere: Call me wierd but this place looks like a converted laundromat and I LOVE IT. Its homey and not trying to be something its not like your typical asian restaurant. I've seen staff family members running around the place on numerous occasions. Call me crazy, but at night time its well lit and comfortable. Great place to share dishes with whomever you are with. Finally, the lady up front and who serves sometimes is fricking hilarious. She might catch you off guard joking around but she's really funny. I could complain about the parking, but its a small family owned Thai place. Cmon, its about the food!
Awesome Pho, great ground pork rolls, and the Vietnamese curry chicken was delightful. They use bone-in drumsticks and thighs in the dish, and the meat just falls off. Great food and a decent value.

This is absolutely wonderful, authentic Jamaican food, period. The jerk chicken is amazing; be sure to order it "spicy" for an authentic experience. The ox tail is equally amazing. Our debate is always which one of these should we order, along with something new. And the rice and beans are perfectly flavored. For desert - if you like bread pudding, this is the best! With a real kick of rum too, and a side of blackberries. A completely satisfying dinner - we can't wait to come back!

Cool little place. Vibrant and hip on the inside. I'd say ideal for lunch not so much for dinner. Menu is rather small which I guess it should be since it is "street food". I didn't know it was only a street food Greek restaurant but that shouldn't keep you from going. I was just excited for mousakka and stuffed cabbage rolls. It's very good. We had pork souvlaki and octopus skewers and they were good. Octopus really good. Souvlaki to me had a little too much charred taste and not enough spice. Kinda blah. I would go back and try more items. Staff very nice.

Suraya is a beautiful space and has an incredibly delicious menu. I have come here so many times and found it suitable for a gorgeous brunch spot on weekends, casual work & coffee nook, quick lunch break, and a sophisticated dinner location. Not only is the interior beautiful, but the food is amazing! I especially love their weekend brunch menu! Some of their must-try's are the lebanese chai latte, FRENCH FRIES, the slow-roasted lamb hummus, za'atar/onion/tomato, cheese/tomato/long hot,the manoushea, and the shish taouk. do yourself a favor and add an egg to the flatbreads! Honestly, I could live off their Lebanese chai latte. It's so beautiful to look at and also so deliciously warm and soothing. Everything at Suraya is perfectly balanced with warm and fresh flavors...and the spices are to die for!

I really can't think of a bad thing to say about Dmitri's. We had the Spinach Pie, Bluefish Greek Style, and the Steamed Seafood Combo. The pita was fresh and light and the oil was flavorful. The bread was dense and chewy. The spinach pie was delicious, though I am not crazy about the bit of dill they had in there...but that's just personal taste. My boyfriend's blue fish..I would describe as a robust flavor with those green peppers and onions. My seafood combo was awesomely delicious. The fish was perfectly cooked and firm, I thought the squid was super, and there were plenty of clams, mussels, and shrimp floating around in a light, spicy tomato broth. I didn't care for the rice side dish but the greens were fantastic and really complimented the seafood well. What else is there to say? Well, the water was cold and wet and was refilled frequently, and the portions were generous. The small corner restaurant has large windows facing 3rd street and is full of tiny marble tables, well suited for 2 or 4 diners. There is a grill with a bar right in the front, though we sat in the back. A more satisfying meal would be hard to find, and at 8pm on a Sunday night, the restaurant was a couple tables short of full and we were seated right away. You must go here!

Just stopped in to give this place a try. GF got the veggie bowl with the falafel and I got the bowl with steak. I have to say this was more like a bowl of salt with sides of other things. The bowl is way to salty. I'm not a health freak but this has got to be extremely bad for you. Almost inedible only plus is the fries were ok.

Wondering around looking for a quick bite, Yelp suggested we eat here. Well, it was not quick, but the food was really good. The lamb kabob was tasty and we really enjoyed the green sauce for the bread. And, the LevelUp rewards / discount means the nicely priced place is that much more affordable.

TLDR; Fresh food made to order in a little strip mall. The staff was friendly and accommodating. I had the chicken gyro, my husband had the philly gyro, and we shared the appetizer sampler. Everything was hot and fresh and delicious. Will definitely return next time I make my way over to this side of the state.

I had dinner here recently and enjoyed it. That said, I think the ratings for this place are a bit inflated. It's cheapish, somewhat greasy, and hits the spot when you're looking for some tasty noodles. It's not especially quick or memorable, at least based on my experience. The broth for the mie komplit was the highlight of our meal and epitomized how deep and flavorful a simple broth can be. The homemade egg noodles were pretty good, but sadly the rest of the dish was just average. Second star of the meal would have to be the flat fried noodles in the Kwetiaw Goreng. Like I mentioned at the top, they're a bit greasy, but that doesn't take away too much from their chewy goodness. I'd probably recommend this dish over the komplit, honestly. The sausage in the Kwetiaw was quite flavorful, there just wasn't much of it to enjoy. Don't get me wrong -- I had a decent meal here and I would recommend eating here if you're in the area and not looking to spend too much cash -- just don't expect this to be that incredible hole-in-the-wall place you can't wait to come back to.

We haven't dined in yet but have taken out several times now and never been disappointed. The menu has a great variety including the standard dishes you would find at most other Indian restaurants but also includes some delicious surprises like keema naan. The service is professional and friendly. This is a new local favorite of ours.

Minor updates: -why haven't I taken advantage of their $5.99 lunch specials before today? What a steal. Thai curry with rice, soup (crab or mushroom, upcharge for wonton) and a spring roll = mmm. -new sleek booths, feels less Little Richards and more sexy Thai now

It appears that Inchin's Bamboo Garden is a chain, and one opened about two blocks from me. I popped in for dinner one night. I'm a vegetarian, and was glad to see that vegetarian items were listed first and clearly on the menu. There is a LOT to choose from. I had some sort of paneer appetizer, and it was out of this world delicious. I will go back just for that! I can't even tell you what I had for dinner -- I forget! -- but it was also good. The waiter brought the check before he asked if we wanted desert, which is a pet peeve of mine. We DID want desert, and got some sort of fried noodles with ice cream. We probably should have skipped it: the noodles were fairly flavorless, and the ice cream was nothing special. I wouldn't order that again. I didn't love the decor. It feels like the tables were just dropped into the room with no regard for the layout of the space, and in an odd relation to the windows. The windows were floor to ceiling, yet the back of the benches butted up against them, which makes no sense. The room just didn't feel comfortable to me. I doubt many people would even notice, but I used to design retail spaces, and I notice things like that. They could have done a much better job on design. That said, the food is excellent, and I plan on heading back again, and soon.

Weeeeee hhhaaavvvveee aaa wiinnneerr!!! I am a 100% Thai food elitist. Having traveled through Thailand, I have had a lot of Thai food. Nothing in New Orleans has been able to fit the bill. Basil Leaf is terrible, Bangkok is so-so, Singha downtown is pretty good but never open. The place on Magazine is up and down. Singha Song is a beacon of light in the New Orleans well of Thai food. I had the two things I judge Thai places on: Green Curry and Tom Yum. The Tom Yum blew my mind. It was perfect, sweet, sour, with equal flavorings of lime, fish sauce and chili. I could live off of their Tom Yum. The Green Curry was perfect and served with some creative flair. I had leftovers. The wife had Pad Thai. It is the first time she's eaten Pad Thai in the US and not had to seriously alter the dish. It's also solid eating the next day. Their prices are average for NOLA Thai $10-$12 an entree. Other positives are that it's a beautiful restaurant. The server was extremely attentive and had a terrific Thai accent. The only negs: no liquor liscense, the menu was fairly small (no som tam, or grilled Thai fish except for Tilapia), and the neighborhood. We were forced to listen to a good number of loud students, while trying to enjoy a romantic dinner. Ahhh well, I guess that's what happens when you eat on Maple Street.
One of the best vietnamese restaurants in indiana- hands down! Service is always great and the food comes quick! Nothing beats a cheap home made meal.

This is one of my favorite lunch destinations. I always call in my order ahead of time to avoid the wait typical of the establishment. On the occasions I eat in with friends we plan to wait 15 minutes for sandwiches and up to 30 for pho or noodles. I've had their pad Thai and was really impressed- I forgot to order it hot and really should have. Their sandwiches always go over well, although the bread is sometimes too hard. If you're a newbie to Vietnamese food these are a safe bet. Be mindful of the hot peppers, though. They have a large pitcher of water with styrofoam cups available in the restaurant and a million different types of teas and boba. My coworker swears their boba is some of the best. Prices are beyond fair and my lunch is always under $5 and dinner under $10. They don't mind having patrons pay with a card most of the time but on occasion I've been asked to pay cash if possible. Friendly staff, great food, good location... I highly recommend.

I've always passed by here, finally went in for some take out! Wow! I was not disappointed! Everything was delicious and the staff was very friendly. I had the chicken Tikka masala and my husband had the tandoori chicken. Both were really flavorful and fresh. Would order both again. Will definitely recommend! Can't wait to go back!

I love this place! Although the pho was a bit watery, everything else is top notch! I'm completely addicted to the fried rice cakes with egg, and the banana coconut dessert is to die for. Service is super nice, and you can get a Vietnamese sub for $3.50. You just can't beat the place for price and convenience.

Lunch buffet is amazing. The chicken tiki masala will blow your mind. Be sure to loosen your belt before you come here for the lunch buffet. I went out at least two notches. The prices are great. The service is wonderful. The decor is OK but who cares if it doesn't look great when the food is throwdown quality!

I have honestly never been a fan of this place, but recently visited again with a co-worker. I do have to say that I was pleasantly surprised with my meal (lunch). My co-worker has several severe food allergies, so I always leave the restaurant choice up to her. They seem to have plenty of options to meet her restrictions, and are willing to prepare the food properly for her to enjoy. While I don't require the same restrictions I can appreciate their attention to the situation. The lunch menu was decent, and relatively new from what I heard. I ordered the Asian Grilled Salmon with fried rice and a cup of Egg Drop Soup. The salmon was absolutely delicious - I loved it. Like I said, I was pleasantly surprised at how delicious it was. The service was okay.. I felt bombarded by the numerous servers coming to the table (one brought drinks, one took the order, one brought food, another cleared the food, etc). I appreciate their work ethic, but it almost felt rushed. The food also took a while to come out, but that may be due in part to the dietary restrictions/prep of my coworkers meal. All in all it was okay. I probably won't go back (unless dining with her again) but it was a good lunch.
Went after seeing4.5 stars. Ordered 2 dishes. Both flavorless. Pad Thai was under cooked as a matter of fact. Didn't enjoy the meal at all.

I got the fish platter w/ Mac n cabbage. The fish was good I just thought it needed a little more flavor, Mac was excellent but the cabbage I did not like I just thought it didn't taste like cabbage I don't want seasonings they use for the cabbage but I didn't like it. I gave them 3 stars because of the cabbage and the younger lady at the front gave me slight attitude when I asked her how long would my food be, but that didn't bother so I would go again just to try different items this was actually my first time trying this place.

I went there with my family and I had guests with me, the service was terrible and the food quality was very bad and appetizers came out so late and when the entree came out it was so cold and disgusting, I will never step a foot in that place ever again, the waitress kept on apologizing but the damage was done , when my wife went home she had a bad stomach ache and one of my kids were feeling very sick, stay away from that restaurant.

This place was okay. I went during lunch, had the buffet. The selection wasn't as big as I thought it was going to be. There was a lamb dish that was pretty good along with a chicken tikki marsala that was yum. The wings weren't that good. They had about 5 different chutneys which were all good but the mango one was yum! I would give this place another shot!

I was here on Friday and I left my food on the table - it was that bad. I started with the spring rolls, they smelled fishy from the get go, but I decided to give them a try- i opened the plastic wrap around them and it fell apart- i couldn't even eat it like a spring roll. The peanut sauce was nothing more than just cold runny peanut butter. I ordered the soft noodle with beef dish and it too was very fishy, tasted almost rancid... not to mention the noodles used were basically top ramen. We also ordered the bbq pork vermicelli... which was very thinly sliced pork (?) and had no flavor. I might as well have thrown $22 in the trash... We ended up at panda express for lunch... Very disappointed... Maybe the pho is the way to go with this place, but i don't dare come back to try...

Stopped by Dosa Hut on a whim while we were in Norristown, and were glad we did. The food was exceptional. It's hard to get good authentic South Indian flavors outside of South India, but we were impressed with the food, the service, and the reasonable prices. We had the cutlet chat, onion masala dosa and Hyderabadi biryani. Everything was very good, and the biryani was the best we've had outside of Hyderabad. Good sambar is a challenge anywhere, and the sambar was the only disappointment on our table. Highly recommended!

Unimpressed! My coworkers and I spotted this place on the way to have lunch at the Couch Tomato one day. We made a special trip the next week just to try Smileys Cafe. First of all the food is expensive for what it is. Most people ended up spending $15 on a platter and a soda. For not being a sit down restaurant- this price point is a little too high for lunch hour. Now, you can get a gyro for about $10 with no drink. This is the way to go. The gyro was plenty of food to fill me up. It just wasn't amazing. The chicken in the platters were dry and needed lots of the in-house made garlic sauce to moisten it up. The service was surprisingly fast for only having one girl working. Smileys doesn't have bad food.. I just wouldn't go out of my way to come back again. Just being honest!

I only ever go to this place on special occasions with co-workers - when I'm not hungry. I've been here 4 times and have only eaten here once. The other three occasions my order was either lost or forgotten about. Once I'd even had to hike it next door to Sub-Way and bring it back to eat with everyone else. The one time that I'd actually gotten my order? Meh, kinda wish they lost that one too.

We went for dinner at 9:00 on a Friday night and didn't leave until 11:30. Service, in the (dark) backyard, was painfully slow. The stray cats were sharking around our table, unknowing that we didn't have anything to eat. Fortunately, we took advantage of the BYO policy and made a little concoction of rum and their tasty juices. Food, when it finally arrived an hour+ later, was good, not great. The rice and plantains were delish. I'd return on a warmer night, earlier in the evening, or for takeout.

Place is 40 Mins from me and I would even justify driving 20+ miles to this place Pho -HUGE bowl for the price $8-8.50 (12-12-17) -One of the best broths I've ever had. Flavorful, yet not tainted by memories of excessive msg. It'll smack your tastebuds without warning. -meat is fresh, not too fatty/tough even when soaked in broth for a while -noodles are prepped perfectly -all veggies like the bean sprouts are fresh Spring rolls -exactly what a spring roll should be. No disappointment -Authentic family run business -Nice looking booths, good change from traditional cheap looking chairs. Abundant choices of beverages in the fridges -they even have fish sauce along with the condiments -Plenty of street parking
Zoe's is our go to place for a quick healthy dinner out. Our favorite is the salmon kabobs. Hummus is delicious. The Greek dressing for the salad is really good, too.

Saw this place by accident driving down the road. Turned out to be an excellent random stop for Indian lunch buffet. They had more variety for meat eaters and vegetarians compared to other places Ive been. Really great flavor.

I really wanted to like this place. I dragged my husband a friend one Friday night across town because of the great reviews but it just didn't deliver. Cheap banh mi? Yes please! It was cheap but lacked flavor. Seemed like a lot of meat, a few carrots and not much else. No mayo, no sauce, no cilantro. I was greatly disappointed. I would have happily paid more for a real sandwich. The pho? Just ok. I've had great pho at Vinh-Long and Far East and I was hoping this would be on par. The broth was good, but not memorable. My husband got the seafood pho and all it had was imitation crab meat and some veggies. We looked around and saw some great other dishes coming out which is why I'll give this place 2 stars. I'd like to think I'll go back and try something else, but it won't be anytime soon and I won't make a special trip for it. Go else where for pho and banh mi.

What a great find! It's in a bit of a sketchy neighborhood, but no one seems to mind. The cocktails were fantastic with interesting combinations and the wine list was really fun. Their house red is Turkish if I remember right, don't see that very often! The food was great and in very generous portions. I can only imagine how great their fancy sister restaurant must be, but it was closed on the day we were in town. We were staying by the ballpark in St Louis and the only options were pubs or breweries, this place was much more up our alley!

Good stuff. Everything was really good. They have both meat and vegetarian options. The meat is only chicken which was OK I felt. There is a little dessert section but I didn't try it. Nice clean place and very nice staff.
New owners since the last 3 months Went for lunch and it was mediocre at best The waitress / manager was great Service was great and would go back only because she was a delight

This is a great place. Yes get past the strip mall thing. The inside is well decorated and the Moroccan them is beautiful. The chef here is outstanding. Service was great. Will definitely go back here next time we are in the area. Best sea bass done the Moroccan way. I had the mussel appetizer for $10. They were great and a big portion. House salad is delicious with a homemade Asian vinaigrette. The braised short ribs are to die for.

Whenever it's a nice day in University City and I'm going for a walk there is a magnetic pull that draws me to this place. One of the main reasons that must be is how much value you get for your dollar, especially when you order the larger sized meal. I'd say that you get so much value for the large size that you should just get that even if you want small (no one says you have to eat it in one sitting like I do). My problem is completely a personal failing. I want to try something different when I go there, but the jerk chicken, yams, and collard greens have been so good to me that I don't want to try anything else. One day I'll find that courage, but not just yet. I've seen some complaints about the speed of service, but I've never had a problem showing patience for food. I know how they operate and if I really wanted something faster I could have just as easily gone some place else. The food is definitely worth the wait. Just make sure to stay active after eating this or else you'll find yourself falling into one of those food comas.
Good decor and presentation. We ordered coconut soup, pad Thai and cashew nut with beef. The soup was delicious but the rest of food was average.

We visited last night. Hadn't been there in a while, and it's really crazy to have a gem of a restaurant like this so close to home and not go frequently. We often miss the window because we eat dinner late on weekends, and Sky closes earlier than most. The entire experience here is wonderful. The dishes and sauces are unique, and the dude who waits on us always frets over our order, afraid that we might order something we will not enjoy. That has never happened! We had forgotten the amazing Sky Salad with tofu. Immense flavor with hot spices...could probably eat it every night and not need much else. We hesitate to tell people about this place, but at the same time we want them to do enough business to stay in business. Go there...you will ooh and ahh at the food, and you will certainly know that you have found one of the great food values in the city.

While on vacation we decided to come and have lunch/early dinner here. This location is in a mall that's currently under renovations(the mall). This place was nice an clean and the staff was super friendly and helpful. I was really surprised to see a Manager actually being hands on. This manager...his name was Kevin Benzel...was very helpful and patient. He helped us by making some suggestions and took our order. Once you order at this franchise, you take a seat and they bring the food to your table. That was cool! We ordered rice, black beans, corn soufflé, balsamic tomatoes, 1 whole chicken, maduros (sweet plantains) and a chicken quesadilla to see what the rave was about. Oh and they have come garlic cilantro sauce and a mango BBQ sauce at this "sauce station" those are great!!!! The chicken is really good for being a franchise restaurant, not dry and flavorful. The quesadilla was Blah! I've had better. The rice was OK, the beans were good. The corn soufflé was DELICIOUS!! I couldn't get enough! The tomatoes were good. I even decided to try their flan which i truly enjoyed. Throughout our time here that manager always made sure the customers eating were happy and walked around to interact with them. I mean I usually see this at Mom-N-Pop spots, not a franchise so this really surprised me. We really liked the food and the staff at this location. When we return on vacation we will be coming back and will suggest this place to our friends. Its not everyday you get great food and great service at the same time.

I love this place. I used to come here when it was a hole in a wall, then they had new management and remodeled and it's so cute now. I've been coming here for lunch for about 5 years now. The food is great, price is good, servers are soo sweet. Great for lunch.

Wow! Let me just say this place is phenomenal! My husband is Puerto Rican and I have had some Spanish food and this did not disappoint. The less than wonderful service is EASILY overlooked due to the amazing food! Never had better tostones in my life! So glad we stumbled upon this place!

This is my favorite Indian restaurant in Indianapolis. I am very happy that they will prepare their dishes "extra, extra hot." Bland Indian food isn't worth eating. My favorite thing about this restaurant is the fact that they have a Sunday night dinner buffet. Yes, the food is mild for the American tongue, but is still delicious. My favorite dish is the chicken tikka masala--extra hot, of course. One of the most positive aspects of this place is the staff. They are VERY friendly--and usually remember what I want (and how I like it) from the second I walk in the door.

Lovely service, amazing food. It's very easy to overcook meat, especially when it's not in a sauce. In fact, overcooking meat is kind of standard in many Boise restaurants. Not so at Kabob House, where food is delicately cooked and deliciously marinated. Dipping sauces are bright and lovely. Even the rice was lightly seasoned and perfectly cooked (too often it's over- or undercooked as well). I had the mixed kabob--lamb and a beef, both perfect and tender. My dad had curry, which was a different kind of curry as I've had elsewhere. More like a curry gravy. Not as good as the kabobs, but still tasty. Atmosphere is tasteful and evokes the middle east. You barely remember you're in a strip mall. Our server was very attentive and sweet without being overbearing. I'll be back!

Wow! Despite the casual simplicity of the atmosphere, the good was over the top delicious and the service percent. I had a drink called Isabelle's Sour to start. So good! The jumbo gulf shrimp with garlicky chili-lime sauce was impeccably cooked and we LOVED the whole fried specked trout. It came with a salad that was interesting tasty fresh. I'd like to buy some of the watermelon radishes and winter melon for use at home, as they made it extra special and beautiful.

Service was alright, ambience was ok. I felt like it was kind of dead for it being around dinner time. My husband had the teriyaki chicken with rice but it was pretty salty. My sushi was great though so I can't complain. Probably wouldn't go back there if I was in the area.

I'm middle eastern and I must say their food is amazing the service is great and u get a lot for the price very nice and clean always fresh iv never been disappointed anytime I have family in town this is the place I bring them to love this place

It's a decent Indian cuisine with good western ambience. Main course order took bit late, you can dine n booze. Menu was pretty decent n taste was ok but I felt bit expensive compared to taste n quality quantity..

This is an excellent restaurant in the Metairie area both for lunch and dinner. Food was so fresh and tasty, with huge portions. Service is great. It is probably going to be my go to location for Mediterranean cuisine.

I FINALLY got to try Thai 5 after it sat in my bookmarks for far too long. We ordered through Postmates because yes, we are that lazy even though it is right down the street. After reading all the Yelp reviews, we went with the Crab Rangoons, Banana Coins, Drunken Noodles (medium), and Duck Fried Rice (medium). All were amazing!! The Crab Rangoons were delicious and the Sweet Chili Sauce that came with it was surprisingly really good. The Drunken Noodles were very spicy even after asking for it medium, but so full of flavor with lots of fresh vegetables. The Duck Fried rice was topped with crispy fried duck that melted in your mouth. To end the meal, the Banana Coins were the perfect compliment to the spicy Thai food. They're basically fried bananas with honey but they were amazing, I've never had anything like them before. Portion sizes were huge, the two of us definitely could have split one entree. Prices were very reasonable as well. If they offered their own delivery service, this would be my go-to. I'll be back to try the Crab Fried Rice and the Pad Thai!
One of my favorites in the city. Great food. Quick. I love the korma and kaboob. Great service. Definitely recommend for a great home cooked meal! Hookah is some of the best in the city.

4 stars for being open on July 4!! Enjoyed my second visit and had pretty much what I always have, a beef (bit fatty) Pho and my grilled pork vermicelli...shrimp BAHN to go. Busy corner but easy parking...lively street scene.

We've been here 2-3 now and the food has been quick and tasty both times. When you come in, your order from the counter and pay, they'll get your drinks for you, and then you get your forks, napkins, etc. and sit down. Sometimes they bring the food out to you, sometimes the lady hollers "Pad Thai!" from the counter and you come and get it. The food is good, but you should probably order one spice level down from what you usually get at other places. We had a 3 on a scale of 1-5 because we like our food a bit spicy and both of us had eyes filled with tears and had to blow our noses a bunch. My lips and gums were burning too. We'll get 2s next time or maybe even 1s...I feel like such a wuss! I have yet to try anything that hasn't been Pad See Ewe or Drunken Noodles because I love those big fat noodles! Veggies have been nicely cooked, fresh, and cut into nice-sized pieces. Each time I've been in there have been the same 3-4 people there...an older Asian lady, a younger Asian lady, a white man, and an African-American man. The guys are a bit rough around the edges but not unfriendly...I think they do dishes and prep work and the deliveries. I've only seen the ladies in the kitchen. The do deliver! Who would have thought you could have THAI food delivered in AVON, of all places?

Awesome! If you've been wondering where to get real, honest-to-goodness Moroccan food, come here. Mmmm-mmm good. He even has real mint tea! One piece of advice: Ask Brahim (the owner) for the tagine with french fries on top. Trust me. It's better. Do not eat it with a fork. Dip the bread in the sauce, grab the french fry with it, and enjoy the carbtastic meaty goodness.
Great food but the service was horrendous. We came in on a sunday night of a holiday weekend and we were rushed by the wait staff to sit down and order about an hour before they closed (9pm).

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: The Taj Mahal is another superior restaurant burdened with a little known and poor location. It has managed to survive though, despite the recent economic troubles, and I believe it's do to the consistently high quality of the food and the friendly service. Like others have said before, don't expect your food to be rushed out to you. My Mango Lassi didn't appear until near the end of our meal, for which the owner himself apologized and gave to me for free. We ordered several dishes, with the chicken tikka masala and Beef Korma appearing as the favorites of the evening. The decor is varied and colorful. The restaurant itself is a treat to sit in and gaze at. With Indian love stories playing on the television in the corner, it really sets the mood for the evening. It's a wonderful dining experience! P.S. Since Yelp has been so freakin slow to update business info for us Boise yelpers, here's their website if you'd like to gander at the menu: www.tajmahalofboise.com Enjoy!

This place is definitely worth all the hype. The atmosphere and decor is beautiful. We had a reservation but still had to wait a bit, however they have a really nice "lounge" waiting area where you can order drinks while you wait. Our waitress gave us great advice for what and how much to order (there were 4 of us so we did 6 Mezze and 2 entrees and it was plenty). Everything we ordered was amazing. My favorites were the hummus, baba ganoush, raw veggie salad, and the braised lamb. We couldn't resist dessert so we got the Kanafeh which is a traditional Lebanese dessert and the chocolate coffee ice cream. Both were delicious but the Kanafeh was very unique and stuffed with cheese so I'll let that speak for itself. I'm excited to come back here to try the brunch or lunch!!
I love ordering from here, some of the best Mediterranean/Greek in Philadelphia. The soutzoukakia is fantastic.
Great flavor in the food. The atmosphere was very nice. I also got the opportunity to meet the owner...very pleasant individual.

Small restaurant with an at home feel. Took a minute to seat us. We did not have a reservation. Not very big inside at all. One server for the entire restaurant so the bar tender helped serve. Appetizer was a little cold but all the food was seasoned well. It's a little pricey. Parking was free. Saturday night in Nashville.

This was not a good place to eat. The pork Cuban sandwich was dry, the jerk pork sandwich was horrible. The staff was not friendly at all. Katie Lee from Beach Bites recommended this place, but I don't think she should recommend anything else. So I suggest that if you want bad food go there.
The food quality was really bad. We ordered lo mein and it came out very mushy and clumpy. The chocolate cake was a huge disappointment.
Quite good. The young man tending bar was very knowledgable in Mezcal. Nothing beats a smokey cocktail. Ask for the Oaxacan campfire.

I started to write an in-depth review of this place's food, but instead I'll just say this: everything I've had was great. My personal favorite is the basic "yee-ro" plate. I'm not sure what they do to the rice, but I could eat it by the pound. A few people have said their staff/management is a little too gung-ho in the friendliness department. I disagree; they're friendly but not annoyingly so. (It's not like balloons and confetti drop from the ceiling when you walk through the door). This is called good customer service and job engagement. They're just trying to connect with clientele and sell their stuff. The food is a bit pricey. But if you live in the Lenox area, you'll spend the difference in gas/time cost to get an equally tasty gyro.
Worker making my food had toothpick in his mouth the whole time. Only had one glove on. Food was okay, not big portions.

We called before coming and when we got there the door was locked but we saw him through the window and he opened the door promptly. Service was amazing. He was super attentive and kept replacing our coals. You can tell the product was great quality too. Loved our white grape (my usual go to flavor) and the coals burned smoothly with replacement before we even complained of any harshness. Our cheap coals at home from our Saudi friend definitely don't burn the same. Love the menu too and got some great mint tea in a cutely presented tray. We snacked on some awesome fries as well. Amazing friendly, kind and attentive service, good product, and nice ambiance made for a perfect date for 2. We would definitely come back with friends.

Food review: both my husband and I are huge greek food fans and seek out new places in the st louis area.... the traditional lamb gyro is fantastic and huge in size !!!! the meat is tender and tasty, the pita is soft and fresh, the tzatziki sauce is really fresh and excellent flavor as well. the baked feta meze is fantastic as well !!! also there was a chocolate dessert we had as well which was super yummmy (i forgot name of it) the decor is nice, fun & comfortable the service is kinda slow and not the friendliest but we go back because the food is excellent
A bit overpriced and the ordered stew had less meat than rice. The staff was slow during pick up and in the restaurant.

I'm not a Hookah smoker. In fact, before last night I had never been to a Hookah bar. I like new experiences, so when someone suggested Hookah as something different, I said "Why the heck not!" Aladdin's was pretty cool. It was clean and the customer service was great. Even though it was crowded, someone was always checking on us to make sure that we were ok. I wasn't really hungry, so I didn't order a meal there. I had a chance to sample the Aladdin fries with lamb meat and they were delicious. The drinks were on point as well. What I enjoyed best about Aladdin's was the atmosphere. The music and belly dancing were a nice way to enhance the experience. I really liked the crowd as well. I don't know if it was because it was a Saturday night or what, but there was a great mix of people there. It was extremely diverse & that was cool :-)
Very good. Great choices. Great prices. I will definitely be returning. Don't let the location fool you. This is authentic and very good. Excellent service.
Some of the best food ever! Treat yourself, family and friends to this great cuisine. The Salmon Hoagie is my favorite.

Odd experience. Listed open until 8PM, but at 6:30PM, other patrons and I were requested to do only take out. Don't know what that was about. Initially told me they couldn't substitute tofu for beef in their salad, but then said substitution was okay, but salad would stay at same price, then knocked two dollars off, which was very appreciated. Mentioned I was vegetarian and ordered spring rolls that didn't list chicken. Ordered arrived with chicken, very little vegetable, and mostly noodles. Salad listed with carrots and cucumber. Ended up being 95% iceberg lettuce and 4% onion and 1% everything else. Not sure if I ever found cucumber. Ended up eating on the sidewalk outside the restaurant, as I was visiting the city and arrived at the restaurant on foot. Overall, disappointed in service and food. The whole experience with hostess was harried and stressy... Not great value for what was produced.

Went there last night and it was crowded. Ordered food-to-go instead. Just two items: Thai Bar-b-Que chicken and beef Pad Thai. We were told it was going to take 10-15 minutes. Indeed, they delivered on their promise and we were delighted. However, the chicken, as one of the reviewers stated was dry. The noodles had a little left to be desired in presentation; no tomatoes or parsley or peanuts as we're accustomed and expecting to see.

the restaurant has good interior but it wasn't very clean and the food was cold and tasteless. It felt like there was a mix of stale and freshly cooked food. There were used tissue papers and plastic glass/spoons under my chair and the carpet looked very dirty. while the buffet was on, the guy was moping floor with a strong smelling chemical, which kind of spoiled the environment too.

We just got delivery through GrubHub. Very disappointed with the quality and value of food: * Salad was watery * Hummus was bitter and not creamy * Meatball entree was a joke with 3 meatballs for $17!!! * Sambosa was soggy and oily * Bulani was okay but at $5, it was expensive for 3 small pieces. * Chicken and Lamb kababs had 4 pieces each- $7 for each skewer- very bland and expensive * Mantu was okay- a bit salty but the only saving grace for this disastrous meal. For $80, we can get better meals at so many restaurants in the city! NEVER AGAIN!!!
This place is fantastic!!! Mom and pop shops are the best and this is by far the best Mediterranean food in the area. I ate everything before I could take a picture... Sorry
Excellent authentic, homemade chicken & beef patties

Walking into Suraya, you are instantly welcomed to a spacious environment filled with modern decor, grandiose lighting, open kitchen design that is bustling with energy. From the outside looking in you would never expect such a huge setting inside! You really feel like you've walked into a new city. We were quickly seated for Sunday Brunch and was floored by how clean and new everything looked. From the tables to floors to ceilings and walls, everything looked immaculate. Navigating through the Lebanese cuisine was a daunting, yet fun task. As we were perusing the menu trying to figure out what we were in the mood for, we kept our eyes peeled on the open kitchen to see what was coming out. This is definitely a place where it is strongly encouraged to share your plates. We settled for a flatbread (manousche) that was very similar to a flat bread pizza, an order of lamb hummus with fresh pita, and a sharable plate also topped with pita. Our only regret was that we did not realize how carb-heavy the meal was, but nevertheless we dug in. The food itself was very fresh. I am used to middle eastern cuisine, so the flavors itself were not very bold or aromatic, something I felt could have made the dishes stand out. Pitas came out piping fresh from the steel oven and the spreads were all made on the spot. I really enjoyed getting my hands into the food and tasting it. My only qualm was that I got bored of the flavors quickly (as-in it didn't make me want to go dig in for more) and after a while it was just a chore trying to finish the pita breads. I will definitely come back again to try out more things, definitely need to get more meat and vegetable options! The good thing is that it is very reasonably priced compared to other Fishtown alternatives.

Excellent quality chicken. Good and cheap patties. I like this place a lot. Downside is you have to wait outside and it seems to be one at a time sort of slow service most of the time. Who cares, gimme that chicken.
I love Thai, it's my treat to myself. Spice Thai is spot on. Exactly what I'd expect from a restaurant on the strip in Doylestown.

Mint Modern is my go-to place for Vietnamese lunches near campus. I love the ambiance of the restaurant and although the restaurant is small, it never feels too crowded. That staff are also so friendly and service is fairly fast. Our server was exceptional today. Although it was super packed when we arrived, our service was quick and he took he time to get to know us. I've tried a few of their dishes before and they're usually pretty great. Today I wasn't all that hungry so I got the fried tofu steamed buns and the grilled shrimp steamed buns. The tofu buns were average, the sauce gave it some flavor but it was simple and pretty filling. My favorite has to be the shrimp buns. The butterflied shrimp was coated in the perfect amount of flavor. Both of the buns had a very light sweetness that complimented the fillings. I was extremely happy to see that they did not skip out on the carrots and cilantro that were in the buns. I'll probably get the shrimp ones again as an appetizer and I'm definitely excited to try other kinds. For dessert, I decided to get a scoop of red bean ice cream. I was skeptical at first because I don't always like bean type of flavors but I really wanted to push myself to try them regardless of my preference. I was honestly surprised by how much I like it. There was a light aroma to it, which I absolutely loved.

Went there with friends from Collingswood and loved it! We shared the antipasto which was unique, plentiful and exceptional. The men had the rib eye which they both loved. I had the gnocchi and my friend the tagliatelli, both of us were more than pleased. The pasta was fresh and melted in your mouth. The zeppoli and cannoli were the perfect ending to the meal. Space is tight and the room is small but that didn't take away from our experience at all.

I love the concept of freshly prepared foods and menu sounds amazing,but... I've ordered chicken Kebob with Greek salad in side. 1. Chicken was cooked tiny bit too dry, yet not hot -rather hardly warm. 2. Rice overcooked and tasted little salty and a bit mushy. Cooked too long? Or too greasy? 3. Greek salad was good 4. Staff friendly and nice. 5. Nice happy decor I will be back to try other meals. Prices seem to be really good comparing to other restaurants nearby

the food is fantastic. The gnocchi were beyond great - I'm not sure that I would even call them gnocchi. They were light as air. The other homemade pasta was a sublime Pesto Trapenese. Again extremely light. There was a special - whole fish - perfectly cooked and better perfectly sauced. The sauce was infused in the fish not ladled on top of it. There a large kitchen staff for a small restaurant - probably why the food is so good. I should add that the courses are sized so that you can actually eat a starter, pasta and main. The room is loud - I would call it fun rather than romantic. It may be attributed to the large table seated in the middle but I think its loud. Wait staff was friendly and attentive but busy. All in all a great place for dinner.

I never thought that a cafe could offer such delicious meals , omg i loved their chorizo & egg burrito "Perfect" one i've tried yet ... If you love strawberries you have to try their strawberry cake it's like having a foodgasm lol so all in all i loved it here and definitly will go back soon
The "Old Fashioned" donuts are the best around. Absolutely incredible and especially when they are warm still. Fried and crunchy on the outside and warm and moist on the inside. They are fantastic!

Great! They fill a noticeable void in the West Philly scene, and they fill it well. The soup dumplings are amazing (they're close enough to the the city's best-- the consensus is that Dim Sum Garden has the best-- to justify NOT spending train fare to Chinatown), plus they serve reasonably priced draft beer and cocktails. Alelujah, good Chinese food AND I don't have to remember either a token or to hit up the beer store.
Went with a groupon. Enjoyed the dishes we ordered. Food and service was good. We were put at a tiny table with no room for food. That is only complaint.

Hands down the best pho in the city. Hands. Down. I love this place. Everything on the Vietnamese portion of the menu is fantastic; so if you're not going for the pho, just pick anything and it's bound to knock your socks off. Don't expect to be coddled by the waitstaff. That may be a culture shock for us Americans, but so be it. This gem is WORTH IT.

Every time I get to enjoy the Brown Stew from Yah Mon I am taken away. That special brown sauce that goes with the chicken can be used universally. The place has a nice romantic feel to it. The service is excellent and personal and not to mention the food is so flavorful. To be in Tampa and be able to recreate flavorful island food there is no better place than Yah Mon :)
Decent food, but very very very slow service. Place is noisy, and there are much better Greek places around to go to.
This place is not worth going to. The lunch buffet is terrible. You get 1 plate, fill it up, and then they weigh it. Then on top of that, the food was cold and bland.

Love the ambiance. Excellent specialty cocktails. I tried the Crown Jewel infused with Lavender and my husbands drink had real rose petals in it. Really cool. The meal was most enjoyable... Singapore noodles were yummy!!
Very excellent food. A lot of delicious flavor and mix of different food and texture. I was thrilled with excitement the first time coming here and it wont be my last time.

Not terribly impressed. Ordered the steak salad, and the service was great, but the food was just so-so. Overcooked steak (some of which needed to be trimmed better), and a TON of raw onions, along with a bit of iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, and cucumber. The dressing was tasty, though, and if raw onions are your thing, the portion would've made more sense.

I got the food to go so perhaps that's why my experience was not as positive as others. I ordered tofu bibimbap with NO egg and extra chili paste. Well, the vegetables were anemic and wilted and sparse, the tofu was mushy with absolutely no seasoning, there was no extra chili paste, and there was half (so weird) a fried egg thrown on top. Also, it was supposed to come with miso soup and sides, of which I got none. I am so disappointed because I love Korean food and I was looking forward to having a Korean restaurant nearby. I will never eat food from there again.

Great service and had a good experience. Never had pho so really an overall great time. We ordered incorrectly and they still offered to remake it due to an allergy. Will definitely come back and try it again. Keep in mind the portions are huge so it's awesome.
Great foods but service is not that great. Slow and rude server, especially the older male. But the foods is very good, would come back to order togo.

I don't know why it's taken me so long to review this restaurant. My sister is Vegan so there are only a couple of restaurants in Tampa we can enjoy a meal together. We love this place. We always get the veggie platter and it is always yummy. Yes it takes a while sometimes for the food to come out, but it is well worth the wait. The staff is friendly and warm and always a pleasure. We love the Injera bread, a sourdough and somewhat "spongy" texture flat bread, you use it to scoop up your meal. They have veggie or meat platters; you can order for however many people in your party. They have individual meals too, with beef, chicken, lamb and seafood, but we always go for the platters. Love the variety. Most Ethiopian dishes consist of stewed meats and veggies with distinct Ethiopian spices. If you have sensitivities to spicy foods, be sure to ask your server so they can control the "heat" like they do for my daughter. My faves are the yellow lentils (Ye Kik Alecha), the stewed mushrooms (Mushroom Wot) and the cabbage (Tikil Gomen). The owner always comes out to ask us how our meal was and we love the ambience. We Americans are always in a hurry! This is a place to come and relax, enjoy the sights, aromas and sounds of people having good conversation and sharing a meal. What I especially like is that if we want more of a particular dish on our platter (and we always do!!) they are quick to accommodate. The owner even "tweaked" a meal for my daughter when it was a bit too spicy for her taste. Always a good experience here. And yes, you eat with your hands! Be sure they are clean...

This is the most bi-polar restaurant I've ever tried. The food is either very well prepared and flavorful, or it's borderline inedible. I'm talking things as simple as fried rice, lo mein, etc. I suspect that much of the problem can be attributed to the expansive menu that seems to cover so many different kinds of Asian cuisine. If the offerings were a bit fewer and better attention paid to doing those items well, I think it would improve. But obviously this a restaurant chain, targeting the widest possible demographic and committed to providing "something for everyone" but nothing exceptional.
Best pad thai and fresh spring rolls I've ever had in my life! And they deliver. The only issue I've had is not being able to get the phone call to go through to order. Try them!

We recently had a small family dinner party and we decided to give Guru a try. My wife spoke with the Guru team, and they were very nice and helpful with decisions. They also were kind to to customize the cuisine to fit our child's allergies. The food was excellent. My family is South Indian and are really picky when it comes to catered Indian food. Everyone enjoyed the food and wanted to know where it was ordered from. ( If the ask from where, they want to go there themselves, which is key that they loved it!). We ordered: Chicken Makhani, Goat Curry, Navratan Korma, Raita, Rice and Naan. All the dishes came out great to my tasting. Thank you Guru! We will be back soon!!
I went two days in a row! Great good, kind staff, and beautiful experience! Even great for families as my friend's picky eating son (age 7) enjoyed it and asked to go back!

Came here on a Thursday night around 8 pm. When I was walking towards the restaurant I see a worker (probably the manager) looking out the door, hoping to get some customers. Walking in, there were only 2 other occupied tables who were just about to be done (although to be fare, it might've been empty due to it being summer and their huge customer base left campus). The style of the resturant is nothing to rave about. The lighting was dimmed significantly. The buffet was in the middle of the restaurant, which felt kind of like a long hallway. Meat options are pretty standard for an Indian buffet, with choices of goat curry, chicken misala, chicken curry, and tandoori chicken. None of those left me with an impression that I had to get more. On top of that, the rice was a bit hard (either they undercooked their rice or used old rice cuz they didn't have a lot of customers recently). The only side I went up to get again was the naan.
