Lastly, the chai tea tastes really watered down. If you want a better Indian buffet experience and a good chai tea at it, then I would recommend heading to Sitar which is just a few streets down from Tandoor.

Let's be realistic here. P.F. Changs is a CHAIN. As long as you get that you will be okay. The décor is made to be smooth, cool, sophisticated and duplicated to some degree. If you have been in one Chang you can pretty much feel you've been in another. This one just happens to be new, so they were able to build the outside area onto it. I have been going to the one down Route 1 and 202, but this one is now closer to home. I like to go every once in a while. NOT every month. Just got back from a dinner there, so I thought I'd write while everything is still fresh in my memory. If you think you can walk into this place on a weekend evening, I hope you do not come hungry. You will give your name at the desk and be given one of those beeper thingy's. Then you will wait. And wait. We had a reservation and we waited close to 30minutes. NOT HAPPY. The host/ess were fine and busy. We were finally shown to our table, brought our drinks, our order taken and then we waited. My Gawd, what fools we be. We had ordered everything that they considered an entrée. No appetizers. Our fault. The wait seemed unbearable. We eat family style so the table was covered with no room to spare. Snap peas, cucumbers and a noodle dish from the Gluten free menu. NOTE for you people with Gluten intolerance. The owner of the Chain himself I've hear has this condition. We had the chicken dish that is quick stir fried, the special salmon in soy sauce over rice, and the grilled shrimp in lemon grass. Brown rice for the table. The snap peas were just okay. Nothing special. The cucumber w/ sauce was better. The noodle dish was very flavorful. The chicken dish was light and moist and came with broccoli. The salmon was just a smidge dry from the grill, but if you put the rice and sauce over it, mmmmmmmm, it was great. The open grilled shrimp with lemongrass still w/ shell add a little extra lemon sprinkled over - nice and I have to say everyone at our table just had a cup of coffee and that was enough. The noise level in this place is about a 7-8 on a scale of 10. There is very little romance here. If you like soup get the wonton soup, but don't expect to eat it yourself, it can feed 4 people easily unless you are ordering nothing else. The chocolate cake----some people say they die for. After having it 3 or 4 times, I'm ready to move onto something else. I don't know what these dessert shots are, but I saw them as I passed on my way to the table. Looked interesting. 3 dessert choices in a somewhat large shot glass on a white plate. Hmmm wonder what is in them. Maybe next time. There is a new Redstone restaurant directly opposite P.F. Chang's that opened last week. Ah the competition. Dave and Buster's opens in a little bit. The whole mall is changing. Chang's is located in between Boscov's and Macy's on the outside of the Mall. Oh yes - I wanted to tell you about the Host on our way out. Our friend went to get the car and I glanced around the restaurant and noticed the guy behind the front podium. Boy was he in Zombie land. A little freakie. They wear headphone gear and black outfits. He's just staring out the front door totally zonked. It was 10:15 PM, so he must have been tired. But it was like a scene from a movie. Imagine Will Smith from Men in Black just standing there as a room full of people are eating, running food to tables and the world turns. I wanted to run my hand up and down in front of his face and see if there was anything working behind his eyes. But then I had to leave. Oooooh I hate to leave in the middle of a movie.

One of the cleanest restaurants I've ever seen. The food is consistently good (the won ton is super yummy) Service is consistently good. One of my favorite restaurants in New Orleans. Freshest spring rolls in town!

Showed up here with a friend at 5:45 (fairly early in the evening, no?) only to be told that there was no jerk chicken left. Or jerk anything-else for that matter. We placed our order and proceeded to sit for 50 minutes waiting for our food. No one ever stopped by the table, offered to take a drink order or drop a glass of water in front of us. When the food finally showed up we sent it back immediately to get it 'to go' as we had 10 minutes to get to sound-check. Only reason I'm not giving it one star is that the food, when finally consumed, was pretty good (a stew with goat and lamb, if I remember correctly).

I ordered the Falafel Pita Sandwich with chicken, which also came with fries. I don't have much experience with Mediterranean food, but I liked it. The boyfriend thought it lacked flavor and was missing something, whereas I thought it very flavorful. He also felt that the yogurt sauce was overpowering, but I thought it added to the flavor. Decor seemed a bit tacky to me, but that doesn't stop me if the food is good. Service was fine. One gripe I had was that the added chicken was an extra $2 instead of $1 as advertised on their website. I also gave their Mango smoothie a try, but did not care for it at all. I took a few sips and didn't want to finish it as it had a weird taste to it and it left an aftertaste that lingered. My boyfriend thinks the taste was due to fake sugar being used, but either way I'm never ordering a smoothie from there again.

I'm from Los Angeles area visiting Nashville. I was near the Gaylord hotel and looking for a Thai restaurant near the hotel and I found this restaurant. The food is very good, service is good, the older woman was really nice. I think it's a great place to eat. I recommend it.
Stopped by for a late lunch of pho. Good service and food. Nice atmosphere. Next time I will try the oxtail pho, but what I had, the #4, was very tasty and substantial.
Great vermicelli bowls!!!! Good Spring rolls and nice small patio along Magazine Street to people watch. Friendly and prompt service! Will be back!
Excellent Indian food. Extensive menu, owners take pride in this place. I always seem to need help ordering at Indian places and they were very accommodating. A good value as well.

I visited both the downtown YEG and St. Albert location of Macaron & Goodies today. A group of coworkers and myself popped into the downtown location today on our way back to the office. It's a couple blocks north and east of Rogers Place - located on 105th and & 101st street. We all got the feeling that this isn't much of a walk up shopping area and maybe used more so for the catering side of the business. Everything looked absolutely scrumptious inside from the 21 flavors of Macarons to the spiced pear tart! Between the lot of us we ordered about a dozen flavors a Macarons and a couple pastry treats. My favorite macaron by a landslide was the lavender vanilla. The mango was okay and the salted caramel... well, both my coworkers salted caramel Macarons were crumbly and crunchy - not fresh or soft or chewy. And mine had an oopsy - a hair in it. I emailed the store a picture of it and a note when I got back to the office. They responded quickly within the hour inviting me to come back for a replacement (and that's what brought me to the St. Albert location later in the evening... but I digress...) This location offers lunch and French breakfasts but the ambiance and seating didn't really make us want to stay. Again, we felt the vibe was more order to go and catering here (St. Albert is larger and felt more inviting to stay for a cup of tea or coffee). Unfortunately the consensus in my group was that these were okay but not amazing - and also not consistent. One coworker has been to France and lived there for several years so she loooooves her French pastries and she was disappointed in both her macaron and chocolate au pain. So I'm left up in the air about the downtown location. I'll be much more likely to pop into the St. Albert one as a mom daughter treat. * Also they still had candy canes and Xmas decor up in February - odd, but okay. Valentines Day is next week ;-)

Thai 5 is my new go-to place for delicious, fresh, and satisfying Thai food! Their soups are delicious and very good portion. The spring rolls are so good and the sauce is to die for! The staff is very friendly, too!

I really enjoyed my meal here. The food was good, I ordered the lunch special which came with soup in addition to the grilled beef over rice. For appetizer the Eggs rolls were very tasty and I enjoyed that it came with lettuce. Overall, the customer service was great and they paid close attention to our table, our water cups were never empty. I plan to come back and try a noodle dish next time!
Good Pho and classic southeast asian salads. Will definitely go again.

I will say the main reason I visited this place was because of their decor And their hookah is pretty good and smooth , didn't get harsh Keep in mind they charge $25 plus 20%fee For someone who hasn't tried Moroccan or Arabic food they will find the food amazing I'm not from Philly , but in Kentucky even the most flavorless and cheap of Arabic food (not even morrocan) has more flavor than the food in this place They have a dish called the "feast" ..only thing is they require (when 2 people or more ) the order one per person ? So if I was to come alone that means I could not order this dish ? Customer service interaction was a little bit awkward but we were not treated bad or anything like that but worth it for the hookah and the decor inside

Delicious small plates - Mediterranean-style tapas. Staff was friendly, engaging, helpful; atmosphere hipster (former gas station, revamped into restaurant). Hummus is to die for, unusual salad combinations and yummy Middle Eastern larger plates. Fresh hot bread (!) was great. We took our time, did not feel rushed, and enjoyed the wine selection. Will be back for sure!

My monthly dinner party group went here for dinner last night. We all really enjoyed it. Yes, as other reviewers stated it is a bit on the noisy side, but no big deal to us. We were a group of 8 at 6:30 pm on a Thursday, so it wasn't too busy. It did fill up later on. We had good service, the bartender was very friendly, the food was great. We never felt rushed to leave. Here's what we had: Cocktails: Zu Orleans Punch--my friends liked it. Refreshing, not sweet, a bit bitter for me. Lychee Mojito--I had two of these. Lovely lychee flavor, a tad sweet, but good. Other cocktails were had, but I didn't try them. Fairly well stocked bar and lots of wine choices. My only wish was for them to carry Hendrick's gin. Apps: Avocado rolls and pork/shrimp roll--these were fine, not super special, but nice. Bacon and Crab Rangoon--really good, esp liked the sauce. Vietnamese Pork Tacos--FABULOUS, spicy sauce on the pork served on the soft puffy taco "bun?" (does anyone know what that taco bun thing is--I loved it and want lots more!)--This was by far our favorite app and I would order it as an entree with sides in the future. Entrees: I had the Crispy Hen Rice. I thought this would be a bowl of rice with pieces or slices of chicken, but it is a plate with a large serving of steamed white rice and half of a small hen, with pickled cabbage and carrots on the side. This was seriously good. I loved the cabbage and carrots (light and refreshing--perfect for summer). The chicken was excellent--super crispy very light coating on the skin and great flavor. They should serve this with a knife to start with, but I was quickly brought one on request. All the other entrees looked great, good portion sizes and everyone was very happy with their meals. The Crispy Hen Rice is a good bit larger in serving size than the Shrimp Rice, so if you are hungry go for the Hen. Afters: Earl Grey Lavender tea and little ice cream filled mochi balls (no idea what they were called on the menu, never saw the dessert options. These were good, three flavors to a plate. Everyone enjoyed them and we all had a favorite flavor. Perfect for sharing and just having a little bite of dessert rather than a big heavy something. The damage: Eight of us ordered cocktails, a total of 7 app plates, 8 entree plates, 2 cups of tea, and 3 dessert plates for a grand total of--wait for it---$200 (not including tip). That is awesome for that amount of food and drink. We frequently eat at more upscale restaurants and those have all been fantastic, but it was great to have excellent food, good service, and not have to balance my checkbook afterwards.

My favorite place to be on a Tuesday night! The empanadillas, carne frita, and pastelón are all great. Stay for a free salsa/bachata lesson from 8-9, followed by some fun social dance, especially when it is nice enough to be out on the patio! And having free parking in the Gulch is such a nice plus.
Empty for weekday lunch. Lamb chetinad with coconut was a bit bland. Kadai lamb was fantastic with tomatoes and ginger. Basmati rice. Saag aur paneer. All delicious.

I am a Mullica Hill native and I was eating at this little cozy spot when it was still Hill Top. They had thee best chocolate milkshakes then and they still have the best chocolate milkshakes now. And let me tell you, the BEST cheesecake within a 5 mile radius of my house (I added peppers and onions, its making my mouth water just thinking about it) and I ordered a chef special another time, the eggplant reuben-- thinly sliced eggplant crispy and fried and DIVINE. Their homemade potato chips really are a homerun, as well. I know a lot of people were miffed when this changed management and name and upped the prices (granted I do wish they would go back down to more diner appropriate pricing) but I say to still give Blueplate a chance. I'm impressed with the quality of their food. And its just one of those places where you can get to know all the staff by name and become a regular and feel good about it. And they do those special date night options where they serve you a couple courses for a set price, I'd recommend that. My aunt and uncle always love going to those. The only downfall is when they are busy, they are slooooww. But if you go in there when its dead, boom, immediate service, hot food, happy tummy.

It's sad for me that the reviews on this place could not have been more wrong because I trusted them and ended up with a dismal dinner. This place is barely edible. I ordered chicken pad thai and it was pretty much paprika and noodles with very dry chicken. It was bland and unimaginative. If this was my first experience with Thai food, I would never try it again. Luckily, I have had amazing thai at other restaurants before and know that this isn't what it should taste like. If you want a true Thai experience, I would strongly recommend making the trip to Tampa to have a more authentic dinner

Had dine-in falafel and lentil soup with kids. The interior is humble and it probably makes sense to order take-out instead. The food quality was almost average for North American Middle Eastern, 2.2 out of 5 perhaps. The soup was ok. The guys working that night (4/21/2018) were courteous. While I was glad to have Falafel in NOL, this was not a special experience.

WE'RE TAKING OUR USUAL SUNDAY DRIVE. SUDDENLY, I EXCLAIM, "WHOOOA, STOP THE CAR!". What's that intoxicating smell? Do detect a cacophony of spices like cumin, coriander, and cardamon wafting from that unassuming roadside Indian restaurant known to locals simply as Nirvana? I pull the car over and slide into one of the few parking spaces that seem to be placed precariously on the edge of the roadway. Am I sticking out, asks the wife? No, I reply, and quite frankly, I don't care because I wanted to get inside this establishment as fast as possible to gorge on what smelled like gorgeous Indian food from a well stocked buffet. We enter and are immediately greeted by a smiling and friendly waitperson (whose name I would later discover is, Raj) who motions for us to take a just set table. After requesting some ubiquitous ice water with lemon, we drop our things on the tabletop, and waste no time hustling to where the real action is: The buffet area. We are presented with two main stations: Veg and Non-Veg. Since, I'm a big time non-veg person, I can only speak to that portion of the buffet. First up is the Tikka Masala. Very tasty with a nice dark color, and deep well developed flavor. As I would later find out, this is the hallmark of all the dishes. Each item had a distinct flavor and you could tell the chef knew what he was doing. The Northern Punjabi style of preparation dominated the cuisine, which was to my liking. The tandoori chicken tray seem low and none of the scant few remaining pieces were unappetizing, so I asked Raj for a refill. He informed me there would be a short wait as the chicken had to be cooked in the tandoori oven, a piece of information which I welcomed, knowing it would be come out piping hot and infused with flavor, rather than a quick 2 minute re-heat in a microwave, like some lesser Indian restaurants tend to do, in order to save time. After a short wait, I was suddenly presented with my own platter of tandoori chicken, before they put it out for general consumption. I appreciated this personal touch. Let me just say, that the tandoori chicken was the best I've ever had. Even better than Gaylord's in San Francisco, which is considered by some to be the pinnacle of Northern Indian tandoori cusine. Needless to say, the rest of the meal was equally superb, and rather than to bore you with the details, I would like to simply ask that pull the car over when you pass by Nirvana and go in and experience it for yourself. You will not regret it, nor will you mind sticking out a little from your storefront parking space.
Best Thai food in town. Hands down. Me and my best friend from Orlando can't stop coming here: my entire family is hooked too! All thanks to my sister recommending the place!
Great little Thai spot hidden behind Broad Ripple's main strip. The cashew pork was excellent and just the right amount of spicy. I will definitely be returning.

I took my wife here for her birthday, and we REALLY enjoyed our experience: comfortable ambience, excellent food with freshly prepared ingredients, and a very clean and well kept place! The owners, Hollis and Rojana, greeted us at the door, and provided excellent service. For my wife's bday, they recommend their made-in-Thailand coconut ice cream- delicious! Anytime we are in Santa Barbara we will be going back for some more of their delicious food and genuine hospitality.
We have ordered food delivery from Nirvana about 5 times now, every time it is hot and delicious! Can't wait for tonight's dinner.

Good food, good service, fair prices. Just what a guy likes! They are about a block off Main Street, but hey if you prefer to pay for over priced food, stay on Main Street! They also have a good vegetarian selection with ethnic flavors. What else can I say ... give them a try!
Fun take on traditional Indian flavors. Cool new spot to have lunch and feel a bit of India in Indy. Also naan is made in house!!!

Absolutely amazing experiential dining. As soon as I walked in I felt like I had been transported to another city. The staff is very kind and attentive, and really did an excellent job. The food was delicious and interesting. I was able to share two appetizers, an entree, and dessert with one other person and we had plenty of leftovers.
Was not busy for weekday lunch, they were able to quickly accommodate our group of 10 on 2 tables though. Food was ok, there are better thai food options in Goleta. Service was ok, we felt rushed.

The quality of amber was much better when the opened. However, their quality dropped significantly. We used to go tp their buffet lunch at least 3 times and regular dinner 4-5 times a month. Unfortunately, the quality and portions both went down gradually. In addition, the behavior of the servers and not good at all. They behave like they are doing a big favor to you.
This tiny place makes such a delicious hoagie for only $3.50. It's one of my favorite sandwhiches in Philadelphia.

The food is good, and its pretty fast if you're looking to eat quickly. The restaurant itself is plain, and the service is impersonal. I ordered the chicken biriyani and it was good, but I ordered it at a spicy level medium, and was definitely expecting more spice.

We went to Tandoor India in University City for dinner on Saturday, so glad we did. We've eaten at New Dehli and Sitar, before, but were never impressed. The new owners are extremely friendly and shared that they have been retooling the Tandoor India brand. Apparently, Tandoor has been there for more than 25 years, so it was in need of updating, which they are doing. So far, the bathrooms are done and if they are any indication of what is to come in the dining room, it will be a beautiful restaurant when they are done. More importantly, about the food. I usually order chicken korma at Indian, but they suggested lamb korma, it was fantastic. They assured me that all of their meat is Halal and fresh. After eating the lamb I'm certain it was fresh. I've never had anything like this dish, the lamb was tender in a rich cashew based sauce, but it didn't taste like it was full of heavy cream, it was rich with spices, not cream. Truly a wonderful indulgence. The owner also recommended a pumpkin masala dish. I had read great reviews about it before going, so we quickly agreed, glad we did. The dish healthy (by Indian restaurant standards) since there is no cream and minimal oil, but it has wonderful spices. I highly recommend it! The owner said they brought on a new chef who is highly trained in both North Indian and South Indian dishes. The chef will be putting one South Indian dish on their buffet every day (we didn't have the buffet, but next time we will). I'm looking forward to trying South Indian flavors since all the other restaurants I know of cook Northern Indian. Good luck to the new owners, they are doing great things.

Found within a crowded shopping complex and sandwiched between two popular national chain stores is this delightful find for good Indian cuisine in the KOP area. Typically I prefer to order a la carte when in an Indian restaurant, but today I was forced to go buffet during lunch. There was no option for a la carte, which is reason for 1-star reduction. In retrospect, I'm glad the buffet was the only option because of the chance to try a wide assortment of dishes and flavors. For hot dishes, they featured 10-12 choices including the typical tikka masala, saag paneer, biryani and curries. Their rice and naan were on par or better than most I've had at other sites. The salad bar was about as extensive as I've seen in an Indian restaurant. They had mulligatawny, a rare find in many buffets. And they even feature a dessert station that included 5 choices - three of which were new to me - including a fan fave in gulab jaman. All of this allowed me to choose broadly... leave just as broadly after clearly overeating. But when the food is that tasty, can you blame a guy?? The service was attentive, albeit limited to quick empty plate removal and refills of water. I'd definitely recommend this spot for a quick lunch. Hopefully, I'll be able to try their dinner (and go a la carte) on my next excursion.

Was in Tampa after visiting Busch Gardens so it was pretty late looking for a place to eat. Noticed this place was open till 4am so why not? My fam and I absolutely loved it! The atmosphere was great and the workers had amazing attitudes. On top of it all everything is halal! Nothing to complain about here :)

I feel so sooo happy that me and my husband checked this place out tonight. The food here totally blew my mind!! First of all, while we walked in the restaurant, the cute and beautiful decorations made us WOWed...we felt very welcomed and peaceful. Those hand drawings on the wall are so well done and i cannot keep my eyes away from them. Alright...about the FOOD now. I ordered beef short rib paratha bread "taco" and my hubby ordered somasa chaat. They both are amazing. Paratha bread is my favorite and I love how they use pulled beef instead of beef chunks. I feel so satisfying eating them. Finish all my tacos within 10 mins;) My husband's chaat is delicious too. The mango is fresh mixed with some spicy sauce...and the somosa is soft and flavorful. They just did everything right!! Totally recommend people who love Indian food and I bet you will find this place so authentic and unique at the same time. I will definitely go back again and try other food on their menu.

I'd heard so many rave reviews about Bitar's that I thought it was going to blow my mind. I ordered a falafel sandwich and waited, my mouth salivating. The first bite was devastating, but I was hungry so I finished the sandwich slowly with generous amounts of liquid to help it go down. So dry, so crumbly, so sad. Falafel is best when it's fresh and warm and crispy on the outside. It shouldn't sit around waiting for someone to take pity on it. I would have gladly waited 5 or 10 minutes for it to come out fresh. The people working there seemed nice. There's a small grocery selection, so I have a place not too far away that sells tahini when I need some. The pistachio baklava is otherworldly. So, I can't hate this place. I am just going to avoid that falafel from now on.

If you haven't been here yet GO! Sen redefines my perception of Thai cusine. As part of a larger group I was able to sample several dishes. We started with the Spicy Calamari and Coconut Shrimp both take what you thought you knew about these dishes and turns it upside down! The shrimp were pefectly cooked and NOT sickly sweet like the other restaurants serve you; the calamari were amazing as well, spicy, crunchy. Perfect. My favorite main dish was the Drunken Noodles. They were prepared well with the beef very tender, with a perfectly spicy sauce. .just amazing. The pineapple fried rice and the sushi are both must haves as well. And, just when you think it can't get any better, they break out the coconut ice cream.. OH MY GOODNESS! Go check it out you will not be disappointed. Oh, and last but not least, the owners and the staff were fantastic, warn friendly and attentive. Just a great experience, we will be back!

I can't believe I'm even giving this such a bad review because I used to love coming here.. The food and service and overall experience use to be so much better.. Now prices went up a lot compared to the old prices.. I wouldn't mind paying the prices now if the food was as good as it used to be with the previous chef lady ..because her food was seriously that good. pho broth now is dark.. And murky and meh. Service is ok but not as great anymore. What happened !? I was so thrilled to find really good vietnamese food in the suburbs. I don't come here as much anymore and after the previous visit I just don't think I'll be coming back.. Not for awhile. It really pains me to say that ! I really hope the best for this restaurant.. But it's gonna need some serious improvements.. (Hopefully the previous cook returns! Her cooking was really spectacular. )

I went with a large group (15 people)- they easily accommodated us. It is BOYB and service was polite. Only about half of the people at our table enjoyed their meal. I got the salad, Yum Nau Yang, and almost broke my tooth on several bites. I ended eating only a few bites and just going hungry. However- the prices were good! Not the best place if you're gluten free either.

Went with my wife and daughter on a Groupon. The room was fairly empty when we arrived but by the time we left it was completely full. Nice to see this restaurant succeed--and it succeeds on the merits of the food. We ordered four main courses, and the flavors were completely varies from dish to dish. All were fully seasoned and nicely spicy, as we requested. The Indian food just blows Tiffan out of the water. We also had Hakka noodles which were excellent. There was a lot of food to take home, so I look forward to eating it again. We will definitely be returning.

Small and friendly Indian eatery. Good lunch buffet. Healthy share of salads and grilled meats. Location could be tricky as it doesn't face a main street. In case you miss it, it's right in front of Ace Hardware.
Everything here was absolutely amazing. A nice quiet atmosphere, good food, and attentive service! Highly recommended
Food, service and ambiance are all super good. Chicken Lo Mien and Vegetarian Hong Kong Lo Mien that we ordered are excellent and I am a Chinese. Outdoor seating. seasonal
Great food! I had the a gyro and a falafel plater for take out. My wife and I loved it and there was plenty of food to have for another meal the next day.
My notes: Small portions coke pricey ($1.75 for a can! It was wayyyy cheaper at the gas station next door) fried rice bland

I like the set-up: it's basically a chipotle but for Indian food. You get to pick your base, protein, and toppings. I opted for a lamb curry with rice. I also got two samosas. The curry had some SPICE to it. Not enough to scare the basic folks but enough for flavor. Much better than the bland nearby Indian buffet if you want indian for lunch. The samosas were...not good. To be fair, I came for a late lunch at 1:30 and these are not prepared fresh, so they were sitting in the warming tray for a while. But still. This kind of ruined the experience a bit. Service was very nice; likely because it's still rather new. An older woman (owner? Manager?) went around and asked everyone how their meals were. When I said I was curious why my one samosa was so black inside but the other was green, she said it was because different spices were used in some of them. Hmm, ok. Maybe it's a different style than what I am used to? The seating is adorable - definitely sit in some of the special booths The employees are also nice because a young girl came in with her guardian just straight up sitting down with customers and asking if they wanted to buy chocolate bars from her, and they asked the employee as well. Some places might be mean and tell the kid and guardian that no soliciting is allowed, but they did not. I'll definitely go back again

Update We have dropped-by numerous times since my last note. We live here and are very familiar with all of the places in the area, know the owners / staff, etc. The owners here are always here and are extremely attentive, almost to a fault. Bar & wait staff are stable. Food is eclectic; adaptations of Island styles to local ingredients and tastes. It has to be better to satisfy the many locals who are the backbone of business. In this, or any other locally-owned establishment, speak up (politely) if there is a problem. Your concerns will be addressed promptly. The live music is typical of the area, with occasional Caribbean Bands. Daytimes, it is typically local easy-listening jazz. If you desire a "disco", this is not it. Remember, you are about 100' from the French Quarter, not in LasVegas. The tropical theme patio is a cool & comfortable place to people-watch as the streetlife of the Quarter and Marigny flows by. Yes, try the "house mojito", but be careful, as I have watched them made; they are more than full-strength. Try the "calamari" appetizer. Ask your server's suggestions. Mojito's is a clean, comfortable, honest, & welcoming retreat in a very convenient location. A great "base" for on-foot expeditions into Marigny's music venues, the nearby French Market, RiverWalk, Museums, & French Quarter attractions. Rick

Their tacos and curry don are really nice and offered at good price. Really like their green curry, yellow curry, veggie curry and occasionally offered Thai noodles. Try the fried chili when they have it - delicious and interesting is what I would say.

The chicken shawarma was a bit dry not that flavorful. I expected a decent middle eastern culinary experience. Yet, with the commercialization of food ex. fast food already prepared you lose the cultural flavor of the cuisine. The falafel was decent, however over all was not impressed with the food.

First off, the food was really good. We ordered panang curry and pad thai. Both amazing. I will definitely be back, BUT doing carry out, not eating in, which brings me to while I am only giving three stars. The service was awful. And not awful in the 'busy and overwhelmed' kind of way, which I can understand. There were only two other customers in the entire restaurant when we were there. We entered, the one woman working up front, walked past us twice never saying hi, but instead acting like we were in the way. We went up to order right after entering, she stood back in the kitchen chit-chatting with the chef about her personal life (we could hear and see her). When she did return to the register after 5 minutes, she didn't greet us, didn't smile, just waited for us to place our order. It was extremely uncomfortable and awkward for us, almost as though this woman did not want my husband and I there. We remained polite the entire time, but days like the experience has really stuck with me. So bad front staff. But an amazing chef, I believe the owner works the kitchen. Yes, go there. Just pickup and leave, and I guess don't take it personally if they are extremely unpleasant.

This place exceeded my expectations. I was a bit skeptical at first cuz I love indian food and this one is almost like a chipotle set up (while I enjoy chipotle, I wasn't sure what to expect). This place is yummy. A little bit different than your typical/traditional Indian tastes, but the blend of flavors and the options allows you to mix and match things. Chaat flavors are yummy, and the potato somasa . It's a place I'd stop by for a quick bite and a little extra to take home. It's like a modern fast-food Indian place....don't come here expecting to blow your mind with indian flavors, but it's perfect for a quick bite to satisfy your indian craving....and the spice is on point

Nice family restaurant. You can eating and enjoy your time with family. Absolutely, the food is outstanding. I am Asian, but I still very enjoy this kinds of food. Next time I will try the honey wine.

Happy it's a halal restaurant Masha'allah but I waited almost an hour for one small chicken and broccoli, I watched them cooked the food and noticed everything went into the deep fryer before the saucepan #notgood when I got home everything taste fried I really wasn't impressed and I won't be going back. May Allah preserve them all for there good efforts Ameen

I sent a delivery order to my son in Levittown and he reported back to me that the food was AMAZING! He had curried pork, veggie lo mein, pork noodle soup, and a tuna roll (raw) and a crab roll (cooked). Im sorry that I wasnt there to enjoy this feast. Looking forward to going there when I get down to Levittown. (I live in Philly)

Food great. Service terrible. Turns out our server was the bartender, as the night picked up she became solely bartender and we literally never saw her again. When she took our order she didn't write anything down...not a good sign...20 minutes later she informed us that they didn't have one thing we ordered...I asked why it took so long to find out, they just got to our ticket! Still no fried chicken...I eventually asked the hostess...was never ordered because first server forgot because she didn't write anything down. They did comp the chicken to make it right. Will never go to the restaurant to eat again...would order food to go.

this is your typical but nicer thai restaurant in the Rittenhouse area. It's small but clean everywhere including the bathroom. the price is reasonable and the food was pretty good. not loving their thai tea though it might be premade and not thick enough. the spice level can be up if you want to. would come back if i'm craving for thai food around the area.

Excellent $9 all you can eat buffet. I've been here 4 times for their buffet. Naan and samosas are always fresh. Chicken and spinach curry tastes good, and the cool Indian guy at the reception is always nice. Tandoori chicken can be more fresh, they are typically a little dry.
Very, very tasty. Served hot. Nice mix of vegetables and spices. Generous portions. Not much atmosphere but very well maintained and clean. Definitely worth it.

This is my family's favorite place to get Vietnamese food. It really does have some good food. When my friend's and I eat here, we usually do family style, and the food that we usually get is so yummy. Like the sauteed ribs and some kind of sauteed fish -- full of flavor. So yummy with rice. We also get some kind of slightly sour soup that has fish in it and a ton of vegetables. I don't know the names of these dishes, obviously. Also, cash only.
First time eating pad Thai and I loved it! While I don't have anything to compare it to I still thing it was spectacular.

A friend took me to Kien Giang today because he had a craving for the Vietnamese/French iced coffee. I wasn't all that excited because I had made up my mind on the totally flawed assumption that because I hadn't liked Miss Saigon all that much, I would not like Vietnamese Food in general. My friend said, on the way there that there are people (in Nashville) who like Miss Saigon and people who like Kien Giang, but very few who like both. After eating there today, I can see why he made that statement. I liked the atmosphere as soon as I walked in. It looked less grungy than Miss Saigon and it smelled better - less greasy. We only ordered coffees and spring rolls, but both were incredible. The coffee, which you can have hot or cold, is a strong brewed French press variety and comes to the table in its own mini-press. There's condensed milk in the bottom of the coffee and you stir it up and pour it over the ice in the '50s diner ice cream glasses they give you. It's perfect and I think I'm now hooked. The spring rolls were also delicious. I think I will try the vegetarian version the next time I go because I found the meat in them distracting from all the other wonderful flavors like mint and basil and cucumber. While we were there, bowls of hot aromatic Pho kept passing our table and I wished I were hungrier because they looked and smelled delicious. I can't wait to go back with a growling empty stomach!

My family and I dined in on a Saturday around 4:30. It was our first time eating here, and I must say, it was delicious. The server was attentive and the staff was very friendly. We had a party of 8, three of which were young kids. We each ordered something different, but two of the items that I would highly recommend are the Korean chicken tacos and of course, Korean fried chicken. The chicken in the tacos was perfectly marinaded and tender. Very flavorful. It was my first time having Korean fried chicken, and now I am hooked. I loved the crispiness of it, and the sweetness of the sauce was just perfect. I would definitely come back for it. I liked the vibe of the restaurant, as well, and can always appreciate a clean bathroom.

Tried this place on a friend of a friend recommendation and it was awesome! Not the place to impress a date for its ambience but for its unexpected delights. For most this might well be a roll-by given the outside drab and seeming lack of depth. It is an oasis of eastern Mediterranean cuisine from egg salad to egg plant and hummus to hand shaped bread hot from the oven. We had several small and large plates but for me the egg salad was the best. Service was very good and the noise level was moderate. After dinner I love a good coffee and hoped for something rich and strong but it was not to be. Coffee was average. Wine selection was good and the server was helpful in picking out a great compliment to the food we had. Will I go back? Yes! Can't wait to go back when the weather warms and sit outside. I recommend this for a first date or an outing with friends. Non appetite!

I feel like Dmitri's doesn't get nearly enough props. Back in the late 90s when Philly was a relative food wasteland, Dmitri's was the hot young thing. But now that the city has exploded with BYOBs, Dmitri's doesn't seem to turn as many heads. But do not overlook this reliable little gem. I love so many things on the menu, it's hard to pick what to rave about. The grilled octopus, the sautéed mussels, the seafood combo, and so on and so on. The shrimp pil pil is probably one of my favorite things I have ever tasted. It's vegetarian-friendly, too! There are plenty of options from hummus and baba ghanoush to grilled vegetables, snap peas with feta, and escarole pasta. I was marveling with a friend of mine who is a chef how they do so much here with a few ingredients: olive oil, lemon, parsley, garlic. And everything is delightful. Even the sides that come with each entrée, rice and escarole, which used to seem sort of boring to me, have this homey vibe to them that's like eating your mother's cooking after a long absence. The other thing is how reasonably priced it is. You feel like you're on a nice date, but you could afford to eat here every week (or multiple times, really). My only complaint about this place is it can get super loud when it's crowded. But don't let that deter you. You'll be too busy enjoying your food to notice. Tips: Get there early--or late--to avoid the dinner rush.
Everyone that works there is very nice and respectful. The food is delicious and for a good price. No complains so far.

I just spent a half hour waiting for an order of lobster mac. After going up to the truck and asking how much longer, I was told 5-10 minutes, at which point I asked for my money back. No apologies were given and it seemed like they couldn't care less that they had an unhappy customer on their hands. They mentioned something about problems with their truck, but it certainly would have been nice if they had mentioned that ahead of time, or at any time during my long wait. I've had the food here before, and it's pretty decent, but the customer service is just non-existent and it takes forever to get served.

I waited 10 mins in line because the person in front of us was charged incorrectly and the person at the register couldn't figure it out. We finally are free to start ordering and the same person who couldn't figure out the incorrect transaction.. Nodded out while taking my order... She was out more than 30 seconds!!! She woke up and said wow I'm really tired.. Sorry. NO YOU ARE HIGH AND YOU ARE LITERALLY NODDING OUT IN FRONT OF YOUR CUSTOMERS WHILE TAKING THEIR ORDER. #SICK #DELAWARESFINEST #OURHEROINPROBLEMISREAL

Food is ok. I have gotten meals there twice both take out for lunch. First time i ordered online picked it up got it back from the office and we were missing a couple items. Second time ordered in the restaurant waited half an hour for soup and hummas. The food is good for soup and hummas but be wary if you are going at any rush time. Make sure you give yourself enough time and get all the food you ordered. Staff needs to get it togeather. Several other customers were waiting in excess of half an hour and complaining as well. I wish the girl taking the orders wouldve told me there was a long wait and the kitchen was backed. 6/14/13 Edit, just finished my hummas left over form yesterday. Large peiece of plastic film in the bottom of the container. WOW

Music every night. Directly on the beach. Food is alright. On Friday, Saturday, and Sunday they have live music and karaoke, too. Can get a bit noisy so if you're not into that, check this place out for lunch. This is located on the small Hudson beach that has its perks. Take a stroll along the water, but don't go in.

changing to 2 stars...I gave it a 1 star and have reconsidered and want to be fair. Not real happy with my last experience here so its 1 to 2 stars . PF changs has always been spotty and this particular location always having worse food than changs in Lawrenceville NJ or other locations I have been to. the appetizer lettuce wraps are always a mostly flavorless pork filling but this time we had the added benefit of the lettuce pieces being solid white pieces of iceberg lettuce that had zero flavor and made the whole dish a pain in the ass to eat. the ginger chicker was ok....sort of food court quality but not horrible - but not good. the dan dan noodles were the lowlight of a bad meal...can PF changs go to an authentic Chinese place and see what this dish is supposed to be. (han dynasty, some other Szechuan place, etc) It was poorly designed and I'm sure poorly executed.....flavorless, mushy noodles, overcooked, the server stirs the noodles for 60 seconds before serving a giant bowl of mush (I give this a dish 1 on a scale of 1 to 10 on quality) anyway we won't be back unless we have another gift card but I'm not ordering any of the stuff I got this time......too many other places to spend my time and money.

I was hoping that after being persuaded by Stephen S. to give Sansom Kabob House another try yesterday that I could boost their rating. But, alas, I will not. Although yesterday the food was substantially more delicious, having gone with the stewed pumpkin dish, rather than the yellow dal, the service was crummy. Crumby? Crummy. One server was friendly but couldn't remember who ordered what. I'd make some excuse like, oh yeah, it's hard to remember. But come on. It's your job. The other server was not so friendly, quiet as a mouse, and also couldn't remember squat. You can read Alex W.'s review for additional details. The chalaw kadu (a delicious pumpkin stew topped with yogurt over basmati rice) was delicious. Filling but not garbagey. A unique and delicious dish. So, while the food is now alright in my book, the service was on the low end of mediocre. I would consider eating the pumpkin again, perhaps for take out, but with Su Xing House on the same block it's got some tough competition.

This is basically a coffeehouse because their food selection wasn't as great, especially since Honey's is right across the street from this place. I tried their Spanish omelet over a bagel, which is decent, not the greatest I've had. Surprisingly I had not had their coffee yet, because I actually stopped at a Starbucks before the drive. But they have a good selection to choose from and I have heard/read many good reviews about their coffee. Their service and hospitality were not the greatest but they are very quick with sending out the food. It definitely looks like a place you can sit down to read a book while sipping on a cup of coffee. I would come back to try an item from their coffee selection. I would suggest to go elsewhere for food, probably across the street to Honey's.

I like it here, but cash only and meager protein servings take a few stars away. My seafood pho only had one or two tiny shrimp. I guess you get what you paid for, that huge bowl of pho was only $6! I definitely don't think it's the best Vietnamese in the world, but I will be back to satisfy my pho and bahn mi cravings while I'm in Nashville.

The best pho around!! This is run by 2 people. The grandmom lady in the front. And the guy running around like crazy in the back. The broth they make is heavenly. The pork belly bowl will melt in your mouth. The vermicelli spring rolls are so flavorful. And the crab rangoons are so light and puffy. I eat here often for either work lunches or dinners. The neighborhood isn't the best but there is parking close and it's well lit with the hospital being across the street. It's well worth the venture!

Until last night I lived secure in the thought that I had seen it all by now, when it comes to the (rather dismal) restaurant scene in Santa Barbara. But I was wrong: I had not yet experienced a meal in this place. There weren't many diners when we arrived, as dinnertime for the locals in rustic Santa Barbara is so early, even on Saturday, that it could pass for lunchtime in many other parts of the world. We were shown to our table and handed a promising-looking menu listing many standard Thai-American items. We ordered, and while waiting enjoyed drinking glasses of filtered water (a definite plus). Then things went downhill quickly.The soup was served in an angel food cake baking pan, which could have been put to far better use elsewhere. The tasteless seafood appearing in it, and in later dishes, likely came from Smart and Final's freezer section, though the prices would have led one to believe that it was caught just offshore on hook-and-line earlier in the day. The vegetables were also out of a freezer bag, alas, and--perhaps fortunately--were served in miniscule quantities. We ordered some plain white rice as a side dish, and a small bowl of gelatinous and nearly inedible goop was brought to us. No chopsticks were offered, BTW. All in all, for this writer it was a simply abominable parody of a restaurant meal, even by our local (low) standards. Reading the reviews on Yelp of this place is bewildering: are all these good people talking about this same unfortunate place? You can eat better at Denny's.

I get this five stars all day every day. Is it a five-star restaurant? No it is not. Is it five star cuisine for what you pay? Yes, by all means give it a try if you don't like it maybe I'll just give you your money back. But then again I'm pretty confident you'll be very happy. Actually start off with the combination platter if I've got a big group extra crab Rangoon or whatever else someone really likes, and are usually go with the pho or the Vietnamese stirfry combination. The hot and sour soup is to die for! I really don't think I've ever had anything bad here and I may go in here for a very long time. Enjoy

Update: talked with manager & they will honor YELP coupon with purchase of food, not just liquor. Despite poor reviews we enjoyed our experience. Walking down the street we heard the live music & were just looking for a place to have a cold drink. Monday at 5pm got 2 seats at the bar, beer was chilled and service was good. NO draft beer though. Other patrons seemed to enjoy giving the musician their music requests & we left happy. Large space and I would give it a second chance for sure.

I gave it 2 stars because the food was reasonably tasty, but the portions were way too small, it was quite pricey, $60 for 3 at lunchtime, and only1 person ordered a drink ( tea). The service was atrocious, the woman was unfriendly, and seemed to resent any questions about the food. Before we ordered I mentioned that reviews had commented about small serving size, (the owner was annoyed by that,) so we ordered 5 dishes for 3 people, just enough and there were no leftovers, usually I have leftovers just ordering 1 dish anywhere else. I definitely will not return.
Really good food, friendly staff and didn't wait long at all for the food. You should definitely try this place. Nice job blueplate!

Barely mediocre. There was absolutely no love in this food. And it showed. I wanted Mamas Vegetarian but they closed 10 min before I had gotten there. The Bitar's falafel is dry, crumbly and tasteless. Majorly majorly disappointing. The gyro Greek salad was ok. I've made better myself and really should have this time. I'm sad. I was just getting take out but the dark and gloomy ambiance and barely sanitary appearance made me think twice about even paying for and eating my meal. Maybe having grown up with access to the finest Greek and Mediterranean food outside of Greece/the Mediterranean has spoiled me, but I will NOT be back. EPIC fail.

I ate at the lunch buffet for my second time yesterday. The taste of the food really has the strong spice flavors that I have come to enjoy with Indian food. This restaurant has not dulled down the flavors like some of the other Indian restaurants in Indianapolis have done. The buffet itself is moderate sized but contains many of the standard Indian dishes. The only issue I have with the food is that the buffet could be kept a little warmer than it was the 2 times I was there. Also, even though they list 11:30 am as the opening time, the food was still being brought out at 11:45 on my previous trip. I do wish this restaurant would invest in new carpet and close off the door to the kitchen area with maybe a partition.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I will never return to this place again, which is a shame since it's close to my house and i love some good Indian food. It is hard to say which was worse, the food or the service. We were told to have a seat anywhere so we sat outside and that was the first time that we were forgot about. Maybe 15 minutes later we were brought menus and water. Much later she returned to take our order and THEN brought the drink menu. Our server said the we could order mild, medium, hot or extra hot. I ordered extra hot but when my dish arrived it had no spice or flavor at all. The server never once came to check on us, bring us water or anything. The owner finally did come to see how everything was and I told him about my problem. He said that they don't normally make hot food unless they know you and took it back to have it fixed. It was much better after that but my husband and I both sat with empty water for most of our meal and finally gave up on anyone bringing us a check.

Not being a coffee drinker, I tend not to frequent coffee shops for anything other than the atmosphere, and the atmosphere at La Va is spot on. It's cozy and welcoming but still slightly swanky (for a coffee shop anyway). The staff is just hip enough to still provide good service and my hot chocolate was delish. It was a good place to study on my way from a film fest flick to a party in the G Ho area. If I lived in this neck of the woods I'd probably spend a fair amount of time here.

Amazing food. I met my husband for a quick lunch since he is working in Phoenixville for a project and doesn't get much time. I normally hit Aman's (which is awesome) but wanted something different. The restaurant is cute, small and cozy and the wait staff very warm. We ordered the fried taro app and both got lunch specials. I opted for the satay, Thai salad and drunken noodles. My husband got some ground chicken patty app, cucumber salad and cashew chicken. Everything was truly great. I was also pleasantly surprised at the portion sizes. Normally when they offer a lunch special where you choose app, salad or soup and entree they are all tiny. Not so here, I had to box up what was left and trust me, I'm no petite little flower eater. Like most of the gem restaurants you'd walk or drive right by because it's jammed in a strip mall, which is a shame. Stop by, trust me, even if you've never had Thai food, you will love it!

The broth of the pho needs some improvement, it is different from what I am used to in california. In my view, it lacks a bit of umami taste that is the signature of Pho. I almost feel the broth was diluted after it was done. In any case, a welcome addition to the Indianapolis restaurant scene.

This place was AMAZING. The food was excellent and we even came back the next day. Our server was such a doll. And the over all place looks gorgeous, very nice and clean. Me and my families new favorite restaurant in Nashville.
The pad Thai jay was good and the Thai tea was great! However they had the same song playing on repeat for the entirety of our meal (45 minutes) Would eat again, but perhaps to-go.
This is great pho. The location isn't that great, but who cares?! The pho is great, meat is good flavored, the veggies are fresh, definitely a must try place!

Was expecting an OK meal as I have eaten at the King and I on several occasions but the experience at The Queen and I exceeded my expectations. Sushi was plentiful, the peanut sauce for the house salad was wonderful and the pad thai much better that others on Central and a decent glass of wine was available :-)
Ordered delivery and got the cubano. It was really good but didn't arrive as freshly hot as I wanted it to be. If I ever get food from here again I'll have to have it in house.
I had the garlic shrimp with yellow rice and tostones. It was so delicious. Everything is fairly priced as well! I also had a chicken patty that was awesome!

Eh. I don't really care for this place. I've tried this place probably about 3-4 times. And all the times that I've been here, it wasn't the greatest.... Mainly due to the food. If you know Vietnamese food, then you'll know that this place isn't the greatest. They also don't have the best variety on their menu and the most recent time I went, there were so many things crossed out so I was very limited on the stuff I could order. I think I'm done trying this place...
Great store, gives excellent customer service! Authentic food, if you're in the Carrollwood area please stop in and give them a shot.

best thai food i've had in the main line area. the food is super fresh, the service is great and the place is adorable. it's also a byob with wine and beer shops right nearby. definitely check this place out!

So I had been wondering about the semi-brand change from New Asian Village to The Great Indian Factory, and well I wonder no more as the buffet here is really quite good. Now, I will say that as a cilantro-hater, I did have to play the cilantro avoidance game a bit, but that is only to be expected at an Indian buffet. I really liked the butter chicken, the cheese, the cinnamon naan, and the fresh naan and sauces! I also rather enjoyed the half pot of chai tea I ordered and drank throughout the meal. Yes I overate a bit due to it being a buffet but I so enjoyed my food! The kabob of the evening was delivered directly to our table which was a good touch. As was the naan and beverages. The buffet was well lit and each dish was labeled with the ingredients including whether it was vegan friendly or nut-free. This seemed nice although the grammar was occasionally poor on signage throughout the restaurant. The food quality was good and staff were really helpful and welcoming. I would be happy to return here if my experiences continue to be this good!
The Caesar salad is terrific and the lemon-flavored rice is the best I've ever had. A popular place with great food.

I'm so glad that this is in my neighborhood. Definitely one of the best Indonesian food I have ever had. I have never dined in mostly because I haven't had the time but they are super friendly with their delivery service. The staff is wonderful over the phone, you never feel rushed and they really take the time to listen to make sure your order is accurate. The combination pan fried flat noodle is so yummy. The spring rolls are always fresh, hot and crispy. The wonton soup is so meaty and the wrapper is so thin that you don't feel so guilty about the carbs. Not only is the food phenomenal, the price is AMAZING! I look forward to having time to actually dine in but if you can't definitely give this place a chance to deliver you some authentic Indonesian cuisine.

Went to Momo's last night with a Groupon, and there was no problem using it, #1. Great! #2. Food was delicious. It was a warm evening, so we each got a cold drink. I got a nice glass of Argentine white and the hubby, a cold beer on draught. We ordered: the garlic roasted beets which came with a cold potato mash, and the dish was refreshing. Also had the meatballs, pan seared scallops, and one order of chicken kabob. Meatballs were slightly salty, but both them and the scallops were cooked to perfection. Very tender, and their sauces were very tasty. The chicken was a little on the dry side, but again, its sauce was good, and the potatoes it came with were also cooked well and delicious on their own. #3. Service was excellent. We were promptly seated and tended to. As the evening brought more and more diners, the attention to us did not subside. All in all, a great dining experience, a neighborhood gem, and I look forward to trying more of their food. I did miss the sign about their happy hour drink specials...next time.

I had the vanilla boba tea, it was great! My first boba tea and a the ultimate mango shaved ice was good too. The menu for the drinks and shaved ice was a good selection! I couldn't choose what to get.

Nice addition to the neighborhood! The cubano sandwich here was done just right, the bread was crunchy, the cheese melted together with the meat for a nice decadent blend of flavors, and the crisp pickle cut the grease nicely. I got the sandwich with a side of sweet plantains, which were gooey and delicious. The empanadas were also done well, light crunchy shells and flavorful meat fillings. The arroz con pollo was less exciting -- fairly traditional style, served in a perfectly round mound, I just thought it could have had a bit more flavor, and the side of tostones was just a couple pieces, not a large serving like the sweet plantains. It wasn't bad, but it's not something I'd go back for. All in all, the dishes we tried were faithful versions of some classics -- nothing bold or adventurous, but a solid performance. I'd be happy to see a little more variety in presentation, or different sauces with different dishes, but if you want classic Caribbean food, I think they do a good job, and the servers were polite and welcoming. The outside patio also seems like a great place for a late afternoon margarita (and they just opened the bar), so I can imagine this place filling up when SLU students get back in the fall.

Food is good to excellent, prices Fair considering you're at a somewhat tourist kind of beach bar, the staff have always been excellent in my experience. Great local go to place to enjoy Sunset some music some good food and drink

I've been to Naf Naf twice so far and I loved it both times. The employees knew everything about the food like what is in it and if it's vegan. They were also the nicest people to talk to. The food is really good and there are quite a few choices. I will return here in the future for a night of really good food.

We ordered chicken chettinad and chicken biryani, tandoori roti and garlic naan. The ingredients were fresh, the taste was on point. As others have stated, what they serve is perhaps the closest to proper biryani. The quality of basmati rice used in the biryani was very good too. The quantity was on the smaller side, so if you have a medium or greater sized appetite, one entree won't be sufficient. The Chicken chettinad was excellent too. They know how to cook for sure...no cheating on this aspect. Good quality ingredients, well cooked and quite close to authentic food, a bit pricey for the quantity but they don't compromise on taste and quality. The place is quite clean as well. No wonder people started arriving at 4:30 pm, as soon as they opened.

I posted my last review of this restaurant right after a horrible "run in" with the delivery guy. I have since received another phone call from the owner. He apologized for the incident and seemed very sincere. All in all, the restaurant shouldn't be held responsible for something they had no control over. It just so happens that they gave the guy an opportunity to work and had no idea he had anger issues. I would still recommend this place to anyone looking for a good meal. They have plenty of flavorful options. My favorite is the rotisserie chicken, beef patties and smoothies.

My new favorite restaurant! Had I just heard of it and its been open for 4 or 5 months! They are very cheap price wise but big on taste and portions. I went Friday and then I was back again on Sunday!! The have a lot of good stuff in the store as well. When my husband picked up his food today, the owner said that they were going to have a new menu next week and one of the new things would include some fish among other items! So check it out next week! I had the falafel plate both times. And it was wonderful! I plan on trying everything on the menu!

I had no idea PF Chang's was so hip. First we tried going to the one in Glen Mills - at 4:30 on a Saturday afternoon, we were told there was already a TWO HOUR wait and that we should have made reservations up to a month in advance. Are you kidding? For a chain restaurant serving faux-Chinese? I was flabbergasted. Anyway, a few weeks after that, we tried out the Plymouth Meeting restaurant (with reservations made far in advance). They were even flexible when we had to change things up at the last minute. Ordinarily I wouldn't go for this place but here's the thing: PF Chang's is heaven on earth for gluten-free people, with something like 10-15 entrees to choose from. They even serve GF beer (Red Bridge, made from sorghum). The egg drop soup & chicken/lettuce wrap appetizers are also GF, and there's an uber-rich flourless chocolate dome for dessert. Since I hadn't been able to eat Chinese food in ages and was jonesing like a fiend, my delicious GF beef w/ broccoli was a chorus of angels singing Bach cantatas. In any case, we were all very pleasantly surprised. Sure it's inauthentic, but it was damn tasty. Thank you, PF (or should I say GF) Chang's from the bottom of my stomach for your concern for the celiac nation.

Fantastic food in a nice, calm, cool building. Food is excellent, and has a dedicated vegetarian menu. I had the chicken green curry mild and it was extremely well prepared. She will not let you order spice level "hot" until you visit a couple of times. Next I get to have medium, and it is really a good idea to take her advice. My mother had Pad Thai and also really enjoyed it. Really felt welcoming and authentic.
Fez Moroccan was absolutely delicious. The eight course meal is shared among everyone sitting at the table and you eat with your hands. The chicken was so tender it literally fell off the bones.

Excellent BYO, I recommend coming in really hungry, food is delicious and spicy. I had the green curry rice dish and it was very tasty. Good atmosphere to come in with a few friends and have drinks while you eat.
Love the chicken! The food for $8 is great...only problem is you need a nap after eating the food here. Just take your boss with you and it'll be alright.

Probably more of a 3.5. They have great naan, and the samosas are pretty good, with good prices as well. However, the buffet line isn't that great. The curries, particularly the chicken ones, are rather watery. The lentil ones are pretty tasty though, and the rice is fine. They have a minimum card order of $10, which is a bit of a bummer if you just want a light lunch. At least everyone's been pretty nice when I'm there. Overall though, I'd recommend it if you want something quick in the area (but wouldn't go out of my way to come here).

Can't say enough good things about this place. I went here for the first time with a friend who thought very highly of the place. I was in the mood for a good gyro and had no idea this place even existed. I recommend the gyro with hummus and a side of greek olives.

Avoid "hibachi" dinners. Nothing hibachi about them. Looks more like pepper steak with miscellaneous veggies but the whole thing is drowning in beef gravy. Disgusting. Literally threw it directly into the trash. What a waste.

my friends and i agree: best pho in tampa. the broth's got the right amount of fat and thus, great flavor. they don't skimp on the meats/tripe/noodle either. and when we asked for steamed bean sprouts, they came back with portions for everyone. that's what i'm talkin' about :) as for decor.. yeah, there's none. also another negative: salted lemonade's not as good as at song huong's. that said, the service was great. the location wasn't bad either. and the main attraction is, well, "best pho" in tampa. order the 'xe lua' size.. you'll have a blast :P

I have been to Pita Kebob numerous times and each time it is delicious! Gyro meat is quite good. Falafels are of good texture. Could have a bit more flavor. Baba Ganoush and hummus are tasty. The baklava is very sweet and nutty, buttery flaky pastry. The customer service is very good and the owner is always nice and smiles. I highly recommend.

Great tasting Thai food from a standard menu of options. Food is made fast and staff is friendly. Wonderful place to sit and eat with plants all over the restaurant. It is higher priced than typical Thai food.

One of the best viet noodle bowls I've tried ! And a very good price, I had chicken and prawns which tasted very fresh and not greasy at all,I intend to go back, they also have western options and a great breakfast menu

Horrible experience! We were a party of four super hungry when we visited the place. Ordered veg and non veg appetizers, main course, but everything was salty. The service is also very bad . When one of us told them about the food, they don't even have the courtesy to listen to the feedback. Got a reply that no one complained about the food. Will never ever visit again.

Went here for dinner with my wife. The food was impressive-the Kim chi burger was incredible-perfectly cooked with the right amount of spice, and the spring rolls were spot on! The modern look of the restaurant gave a nice atmosphere as well.The only reason I am not giving Modern Mint a five star rating is because of the slow service. They seemed to only have three people working-one behind the bar and two on the floor in an absolutely packed restaurant. We will be back to give them another try.
Wonderful. been here about thirty times. Great food and nice people.

Oh my gosh, their FISH CURRY! One of the best foods I've ever eaten in my life!! The spice level was medium-high, and it was perfect. Unfortunately it was pretty expensive --- $12. Although I can't wait to try more items on their menu, I won't be going there often because it's a bit pricey for a casual place.

Just ordered delivery from here for dinner tonight... got the chicken vindaloo and lamb bryani. Thoughts: 1) The delivery service was very quick 2) The food was good, right level of spice, and really cheap... One thing to note was that the food wasn't super hot so it warranted a quick nuke in the microwave but not a big deal 3) We also ordered garlic naan which they forgot in the delivery. I called and the guys were super apologetic and nice about it. They took it off the bill (which was all I expected/wanted). They took it a step further and called Grub Hub to let them know what happened and Grub Hub took care of the situation by giving us a $5 credit. Overall, I was happy with the food and especially pleased with the customer service. Will definitely order from there again.

This is our go to date place. A place we just feel comfortable and don't have to worry about what we're getting because it's all good. I've been here so many times I can't count it and I've never had something I didn't like. The staff leaves something to be desired but the food is so good that doesn't matter.
Pad Thai very good. Service a little slow. The tam ka Kai soup was good but a little salty. Not sure if that is how it is supposed to be, my first time trying it.

There is a lot to love about Bitar's. A cute little sandwich/Mediterranean grocery shop tucked away right outside of the Italian Market, Bitar's has been an institution in the neighborhood for well over 20 years. Let's be honest here: South Philly is a mecca for a lot of different cuisines, but finding a good gyro isnt the easiest thing to do. Even Mazzo's which has my favorite hummus in the world, falls a little short. Bitar's however, is fabulous. Oh, I could just swoon for their fresh, tasty tzatziki sauce. I can feel it on my tongue now. The dancing combination of creamy yogurt, smooth dill and sweet mint is almost too much to bear. The lamb meat is so thin, cook perfectly. All piled high inside of a pita and stuffed into a handheld aluminum wrapper. Forget the overrated, over-indulged cheesesteak, Bitar's Greek gyro is a far superior sandwich within a stone's throw of those true South Philly dumps.
Food was delicious and the personnel very friendly. It is very clean and fresh made food. The owner was super friendly. Red chicken curry was delicious. Posted appetizer sampler picture.

Wow!!! Excellent food!!! I'm Puertorrican and it can't get better than this. Order the "Pechuga Rellena de amarillos" (Chicken Breast stuffed with sweet plantains) and it was delicious. The mofongo was also excellent which was made with "chicharrones". I now live in Texas but if I ever go back near Nashville, this restaurant is a must! By the way... If you like rum, they have the BEST Puertorrican Rum which is Don Q (not Bacardi as many of you would think).
All around amazing place. Superb food and service. Don't miss the orange kulfi dessert.

The very best that the Loop Thai scene has to offer. As others have mentioned, all of the Loop thai restaurants are owned by the same family. They are all great, but Thai Country Cafe stands out for it's delicious, affordable food and excellent customer service. I have probably eaten here over fifteen times and I have yet to have a bad experience. It was my go-to spot during college to eat in or take out, and was one of the places I had to stop back into during my trip back to St. Louis this weekend. It will never take more than 15 minutes from the time you arrive to get your food, whether you are placing an order for take out or having a sit down meal. Some favorite dishes include: 10. Tom Yum - hot and sour soup (I go for chicken but you can also choose tofu or shrimp) mushrooms, galangal, lemon grass, lime leaves, and green onions. 11. Thai beef salad with cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes, mixed with lime juice and spicy sauce. 36. Pad Thai- Rice noodle stir fried with bean sprouts, green onions, egg, and ground peanuts. 37. Pad Nam Prik Paow Sen Mee - rice vermicelli stir fried with chili paste, broccoli, green onions, bamboo shoots, bell peppers, and basil leaves. 50. Pad See Ew Sen Sod - flat rice noodle stir fried with broccoli, bean sprouts, soy sauce, and egg. The Thai iced tea and iced coffee are both great. Very, very sweet, but undeniably delicious. Be forewarned that they are closed Tuesdays! Nothing is worse than getting your hopes up for Thai and being disappointed. Luckily there are no fewer than three other Thai options, owned by Pat, in walking distance.
Pork belly melts in your mouth!! I had the brisket pho and the broth is sublime. Definitely best pho I've ever had. Service was fast and friendly. I'll come back for sure!

Zeko's has great service, great food, and a friendly feel... Not to mention they're also open really late, which makes coming here at all times of the night a joyful experience. This restaurant really is awesome, and it's cost efficient too. Definitely would reccomend to anyone who likes food! Haha

Between Miss Saigon and Kien Giang, I go here for my Pho needs. In my experience, the more it looks like a HS cafeteria, the better the pho tastes, and this place fits te bill. Not the best I've had, but the best I've had in Nashville. Definitely worth checking out.

Yum yum yum!! I'd never been here before, so I decided to give it a shot. The Gyro Shack did not disappoint! I took one reviewer's advice and got the double meat...it was a little too much for me, so next time I'll just get the regular amount of meat. Yes...I'm definitely coming here again!

Good food, terrible service. I was running errands and stopped by for a quick bite by myself. I sat at a 2 top next to the window and then moved over to a 4 top because the table was in direct sun and really warm. The entire restaurant was 25% full at best with 6-8 vacant tables and the owner came and told me I couldn't sit there because it was just me. Rude. Moving on, my spring rolls were awesome and my stir fried chicken bowl was ok, a little too much gravy on the chicken. I waited a good 10-15 minutes after I was done for the server and owner to notice I was still waiting for a box. I asked for the check and she never returned. I finally waited in line at the counter and paid . For what should have been a very quick lunch turned into more waiting than anything else on what was not a busy time. Perhaps take out is a better option here.
My "go to" for an Indian Buffett. Food and price point can simply not be beat. The renovations to this place were well done.

Went, again, Pan D'Olive on McCausland just South of I-64. Amazing! If you don't have any dinner plans - you need to go to Pan D'Olive tonight for dinner. Get the pork chops and mashed potatoes . . . you will be e-mailing me from your table to thank me for your delicious Saturday evening meal. Please tell Sam the owner and Angela the restaurant manager hello! Enjoy your night!

My girlfriends and I had SUCH an amazing experience at Phamous Cafe today! The service was friendly and attentive. Dan (the manager) is so sweet and knowledgable about the cooking methods and ingredients which was very helpful because our friends is allergic to so many things common in Vietnamese cooking. He was able to make suggestions based on her allergies and she had a great time and loved all of the food! We all enjoyed everything we ordered (the pho (P.2, P.4, P.12) eggrolls, the combination bahn mi, and Thai Iced Tea) so much! Thank you Phamous Cafe! I'll be ordering some food to go on my way back home!

To be clear, I'd give this place 2.8 stars. Staff was friendly and we got seated quickly despite that the place was full. Oh, it's CASH ONLY. We ordered the Vegetarian Naam Salad. The texture was good (good, as in "expected, because I've eaten this before" good). The flavor was...actually, unremarkable (but not bad at all, to be clear). To be fair, naam khao is normally a favored dish for me and my friends...so an unexpected unremarkable flavor also means a heightened sense of disappointment. If you have had really good naam khao, this dish is like naam khao that your cousin makes when they're lazy...because it's crunchy and chewy and tart, but missing the salty and sweet flavors. You will need more lettuce too. We also ordered the homemade jerky; it was fine. Fine as in, it's not bad at all, tasted like soy sauce...but it's not ::shrugs:: good like the jerky that you get at the Lao temple during the New Year's good. Last, we got the pork laab (instead of beef laab since we didn't bring a lot of cash, we thought we'd save $1 with this option). We ordered medium spicy (I think) and I thought it was definitely "butt burn" spicy level. Actually, I think we ordered medium spicy and then asked for chilly on the sides...whatever, it wasn't the complex type of flavor that you normally get with laab anyway. It was just spicy (as my friend said, "one note"). We got a teeny tiny, looks like kid-sized portion of sticky rice to share among three adults with the laab. Well, dang, we had to take really small bites of our sticky rice to make it last...but the proportion of sticky rice to laab wasn't really appropriate. Oh, all the herbs and greens and stuff tasted fresh. That's all I can remember. Now...with all that said, I feel like this is a good place to eat if you haven't really eaten all that much Lao or Thai food and would like a tidy introduction to basic flavors of the dishes I have mentioned above. There are a lot of other things to try on the menu too.
Tried this place last night. Great service, the Shisha was top notch, and got a free mint tea as well. The prices were good for the area and the Chicken Shish Kabob was delicious.

Gobi Manchurian in Amans is wayyyy better than here. The atmosphere sucks and I have the pleasure of waiting 50 minutes for my dosa's.
