Seems to be a hit and miss lately with their biryani that burned my tongue. Looks on Photos are deceiving. I rather travel another 25 minutes to Devis or 10 minutes to mmmAmans.

I sampled the new menu with my wife this evening and was extremely satisfied. The same high quality, bright flavored Asian influenced dishes are served within a very unique establishment. I enjoy the atmosphere as much as the cuisine .

The food is amazing--I would give 6 stars if I could base just off that. I've had their pho as well as the pad thai--perfect balance of sweet and spicy, and the meat cuts are good as well. HOWEVER, they have a lot to work on in terms of customer service and health standards. They answer their phone with spotty regularity. The first time I tried to order, one gentleman told me they delivered and another said they do not (they do not deliver). This I could deal with, but what is completely unacceptable is the hair I found in my recent order. Absolutely disgusting and unsanitary.
Chicken kabob is the best in Philly! Their bread is out of this world! Friendly staff that knows what their doing... Thank you for your awesome food!
Oh no, the pad thai is the best I've ever had and I just moved pretty much across the street from this place..... I'm going to go broke trying all the yummy menu options!!!
Great food! Great service, very hospitable staff. Very helpful. Received complimentary dessert samples that were very flavorful. Will definitely go back.

I came here with work people who eat here for dinner almost every other night. The waitress knows one of the guys so well that she brings him his beer of choice without even asking what he wants. It is slammed at lunchtime, so get there early if you don't want to wait (even the carryout wait was 20 minutes when I tried in vain the week before for lunch). Our dinner was good - I enjoyed the duck dish that I ordered, but I should also say that most people at the table were surprised by the spiciness/lack of spiciness of their respective dishes, based on the separate descriptions they had received for their entrees from the menu and the waitress. A minor detail, and shouldn't stop you from checking Singha out.

Falafel is such a cool food. It's one of those tastes that I crave at least once a week, but the falafel joints that crowd center city are either fake falafel (ie. maoz), or not good and too expensive (ie. Sahara Grill) as compared to Bitar's on 10th and Federal. My favorite thing about this place (besides the price of $2.50 for a huge falafel sandwich) is that the falafel is grilled instead of fried making it not as heavy, greasy and unhealthy as the fried variety. I love their falafel there so much i never order anything else off of the menu, although they do have an assortment of chicken, lamb, and beef pita sandwiches. They also have a case of excellent filo deserts that all pretty much taste the same but are delicious and highly addictive. With prices ranging from 75 cents to $1.25 go for it! My old standby is the pistachio baklava . If you plan to sit and eat, there are only 3 small bar-height tables, or some seats outside now that the weather is nicer. Sometimes it can get a little smoky in there from the grill -- its only a few feet from the seating area. Overall, delish - I love it and I'm glad to be so close! The people who work there are very friendly as well.
Always amazing service and food! We feel so welcomed there and leave with full bellies and big smiles :)
I'd understand the place getting an order wrong, but they just falsely advertised what is in their food. Tofu pad Thai came with 0 pieces of tofu. Coconut rice was just plain white rice. Not flavor.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: AMAZING food the FRIENDLEST service If yer in Boise andnyern in the mood for spectacular Indian food, you can do no better than Taj Mahal. I'm currently on the road with my band and to come accross a treasure like this is one of ny favirite parts about touring. Seriously, hit em up. Regret it you wont.

Came for one quick lunch to go. One banh mi (traditional) and a fried cheesecake. The banh mi was nothing to write home about - a typical banh mi. The cheesecake however was absolutely wonderful. It has a crisp outer layer and a creamy center that has little shreds of what seems to be mango. This, served with vanilla ice cream was very delicious and I would strongly recommend it.
One of the best restaurants around! I would recommend their "Spicy Basil" dish with a Thai tea.

Best Indian Buffet I've ever been to. Hands down. It's hard to rate a buffet without writing 10 pages on it. I could easily, but I won't. This places crushes every Indian place that I've ever been to, and I've been to ALOT. This is my absolute favorite. It's very rare that I give place 5 stars, but I'd give six if I could. Stop reading now and go!

I have heard so many great things and my fiance raved about it. Met some friends here for dinner. It is a very small and intimate place. Nice in the winter, I don't know about the summer. When it cleared out later in the evening I found I rather liked the interior, simple, dark wood tables, candles, and a clean modern open kitchen. The dinner was terrific. The variety of breads and olives provided were delicious. The antipasto is highly recommended and has a delicious variety of special Italian treats, not run of the mill. The tomato, bread and anchovy salad was simple but tasty also. The shrimp appetizer was good but nothing special and the white beans with it were a bit mushy. The entrees were delicious. I loved the tagliatelle with prosciutto and the veal looked awesome although I didn't try it. The Zeppoli dessert should not be missed and should be shared. Generous portions of food despite what the waiter suggested. The only downside was the service. It was attentive and not poor but unrefined and seemed not to fit the restaurant. It felt like a high school football player's first night on the job, although a very nice football player. Overall a great experience, if it is a hassle for you to get to Collingswood though, there are plenty of equal and better places in Philadelphia. Not necessarily worth a trek.

This place is an old, long-term hidden Millwoods gem! Best jerk chicken in town; always amazing and so full of flavor. The staff are friendly and efficient, never a long wait. And you can even take it to go and expect the taste to still be fresh when you get home.

I came here for dinner by myself on a Thursday and it wasn't too crowded. It's more on the casual side. I had the tofu bowl (under the ball section on the menu). It had tofu that was very well cooked (not always the case as tofu is hard to cook!) The rice noodles were great and the vegetables (carrots, cucumber, lettuce) were fresh and crisp. The service was fast and the prices were very reasonable. I would love to return!

The hot and sour soup is delicious! Best hangover soup! Full of meat and flavor. I also had the butter chicken, which was so rich and had a smooth taste. The only downside was that it was a little on the watery side. I would've liked the sauce to be a bit thicker. But that's me just being picky. The garlic naan was alright. It was a bit oily but had a decent garlic taste. The only truly negative party of my experience was the long wait. It look over an hour for me to get my food. And the restaurant wasn't even crowded. But overall, it was tasty and the best Indian food I've had in the Nashville area so far.
My wife and I were hankering for some great indian food and we found it here! You have to try the sticky rice and mangos. So delicious

business_name: OPA! of Greece West Edmonton Mall - A
text: Yet again (I really feel like I'm repeating myself), ethinic cuisine has made it's way into fast food, and this time it's Greek. I was feeling adventurous, when I was in the smaller food court at West Edmonton Mall this past weekend, and I decided to try Opa! The people that worked here were super nice. They asked me and my friend if it was the first time we had eaten there. Since we hadn't, she explained the menu to us, which was actually pretty helpful. I got the Souvlaki Pita with fava. This was topped with tzatziki, lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. I could have added feta for 50 cents, but I passed. My pita came with a choice of either Greek or caesar salad; I chose the latter, but I kind of regret it. The Greek salad looked so delicious, but the caesar was very mediore. The pita was yummy. The bread was soft and the toppings were very fresh, but I wasn't crazy about the fava. It was actually a falafel--it was very strong and not the best I've tried. I tried a bit of my friend's food too. He had the Spanakopita, which is a pasty filled with spinach and feta. The taste was rather disappointing--I would not recommend ordering this. This platter also came with rice and potatoes, and these were very tasty. Opa! isn't bad. I know what to avoid now and what is good, so I'll probably get it again one day, when I am in the mood for something different.
Delicious little place! Didn't think much from the outside but the food is sooo good! Big proportions too!

This is the place I first tried Indian food 7 years ago and it is where I compare all of my other Indian experiences. Their lunch buffet is huge including a desert buffet. They even have a Sunday night dinner buffet which is a great end to the weekend. I always get their Chicken Tikka Masala and the Saag Paneer which are staples for me but I also try some of their other dishes as well but always go back to CTM & SP. My mouth is watering just writing about this! Looks like Sunday night we are going back to the buffet! It's worth the 30 minute drive for us every time.

One of the best Thai restaurants in Hillsborough county. The sushi is very good too with a varied menu for both. Service and wait staff are always available and helpful. The restaurant is very clean and nicely decorated/updated. Check it out if you are hungry for some sushi and Thai.

( lunch buffet review ) Wonderful food. Definitely northern inspired. Korma was much more coconut than spice :). Naan was buttery and delicious delivered to the table. Had a few chutney to choose from, as well as a pickle. Many vegetarian dishes, many chicken for us omnivores. I only wished for a lamb or beef keema on the buffet. Pakora was flavorful, not too spicy-hot. We will be back!

After a long day, I got back to my weekend rental in Washington Park, exhausted, hungry and no clue what I wanted. I searched right here on Yelp for options nearby and topping the list was Mumbai Bistro. Indian food...yes!!!! When in doubt, Indian food is always the answer and with a 4-star average review, how could you go wrong? I can never seem to pick just a single item or two, so I ordered a trio, chicken vindaloo, channa masala and saag paneer with a side of rice. All of that for less than $20. I ordered online and my food arrived within 35 minutes. Side note: my delivery driver was cute. :-) The food was fantastic. The channa masala was definitely among the best I've ever had. I'm already thinking about the leftovers I'll polish off tonight.

Highly Recommended I visited here from California seeing family one night we planed to go and eat outside and we found out about this Ariana resturant to be honest We really liked this place very nice people the owner I met Mr Sultani was very nice and very friendly guy with two other boys they served us the food it was so yammy We liked the Qabili rice the Kobida grilled chicken everything was awesome 5 stars

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Definitely among the best Thai food I've ever had, and living in Asia, we do have access to great authentic Thai food. Great ambiance, and impeccable presentation. Lanna's owner is a true representation of the sweetness and kindness of all Thai people. Amazing experience!

Nice atmosphere walking in. Overall good look and feel. I am normally pretty easy to please, especially with food. Unfortunately, the food was not at all impressive. Ordered the calamari and it was soggy, rubbery, and undercooked. Ordered the Brisket and Steak Pho - broth had zero flavor. Girlfriend ordered the Mushroom Pho, which was actually pretty good and had a better broth. Waiter and staff were polite and friendly. Live music was also a plus.

This is great place to hang out and be seen but not seen. There are a lot of different flavors of hookah and I enjoy the music and live shows. The drinks are moderately priced. I've only noshed on others food so In not sure if it's great or not. Good place to go late night for a little fun.

I came here on Saturday night with my mother and experienced "Amber" for the first time. I have to say I was very impressed. My only other exposure to Indian food was a few years back at a place in Broad Ripple that I thought was lousy. We each had the lamb curry and asked for spicy. It was definitely spicy and was a good value for the price. We ordered the garlic Naan and my mom thought it was as good as she had previously experienced in India. My only minor suggestion for improvement would be to include a small side dish to refresh the palate. Rice and curry can get a little tedious even if it's great.
Different than I was expecting, you don't use silverware! I am glad I tried it, thought it was too expensive and won't go back unless someone else is paying.

We were very excited to be trying this Thai restaurant that had a good number of reviews and 4 stars. So......I'm not sure what part of Thailand the owners are from but there is NO love in there food. We ordered Tom Yum and it was bland so much so that we needed to add salt.....yuck!! I've traveled all over Thailand and this restaurant has dumbed down the true essence of real Thai food. The soup was lacking Tamarind and Fish Sauce. We then ordered Panang Curry with pork. It came to us and at first I thought we ordered vegetarian Panang because except for the 6 pieces of pork the entire dish was filled with green beans. Come on.....you are using this vegetable as a filler!!! Give me pork!!!! The sauce also was lacking so much flavor. If we did not order to go I would have returned everything. Not so Thai!!

Good service, great location, even better food. We started off on the right note with the chicken curry and bread for an appetizer. The curry was excellent. For an entree, I strongly recommend the Shakin New York strip. The steak was seasoned beautifully, and so juicy and tender. Their fried tofu was also executed perfectly.

Always enjoy the food here. Taro app is excellent and so are the veg spring rolls. Great vegetarian choices and friendly service. One of the few places where take out is as good as eating there and that is no easy task to achieve..

I really like this place....being an South indian, who was born and raised in north India, I get to taste the best of both worlds. Whenever we get a craving for the chats, its probably as good as it gets in this area. The south Indian food is great, the dosa's, Utthappams and combo thalis are pretty good and reasonable priced. Would definitely go there as often as we can
Food was good but expect small portions & its pricey for the stuff. I like their concept being similar to chipotle.
Very tasty chicken vindaloo on naan sandwich. Very kind and attentive service. Keep up the great work T&T.

How nice to have some true diversity in Reno. I'm guessing by the owner that this accurately represents Ethiopian cuisine, though I'm no expert. I can say, though, that I enjoyed the food and atmosphere, and the owner/ server was very nice. Pack your patience, however, and possibly eat a snack before coming if you are super hungry and need food -now-, because this is not necessarily quick-prep food. Also, they appear to operate on very limited staff. The spice blends were teriffic (I had the one chicken dish, my boyfriend had the lamb). We eyeballed a few dishes at other tables we will try on future visits. Try the Ethiopian beers. Skip the baklava. Traditionally you eat this cuisine with your hands, but a fork was offered in case we weren't feeling adventurous. One cool thing I found out from the owner is that she buys local ingredients. The teff grain for all her bread is purchased from a farm in Fallon. A suggestion to the owners: Please offer a sample platter (smaller and cheaper than the huge $40 ones for a large party) that includes both meat and vegetable dishes, or even better, allow customers to 'build' a sampler by selecting a meat dish and vegetable dish of their choice. I like to have a little of both, and was bummed not to have any vegetables in my diet that evening. Please support this small business owner and the Reno food scene, and give Zagol a try!

After trying a multiple amount of Vietnamese restaurants throughout Indianapolis, (Saigon, Pho 54, Pho Tasty) I must say Sizzling Wok has the best Pho bo vein. Though our table was quite sticky...The meatballs are more tasteful and the amount of bean sprouts served was delicious. Our server was distant but the food made up for it

Food: One word: "Delicious!" The aroma: as soon as you open the door you are hit with an alluring aroma that increase your hunger ten fold. It is something about the smell of the spices that will surely make you over indulge. Ambiance: cozy, warm and inviting. The service is impeccable. This place is a definite must!

Very fortunate to have them open new location next door to us in Colmar ! Our staff takes turns ordering the jerk chichen, ox tail and curried goat. The food is great and the people there are very friendly.

Cute little cafe with really good food & drinks; prices are very reasonable. I'm so glad that we stopped by here before heading back to Atlanta. We got the banh mi thit nuong op la (grilled pork & fried egg sandwich), summer roll (avocado, shrimp, rice vermicelli, & herbs wrapped in rice paper), spicy Thai papaya salad, sugar cane drink, & thai tea. Everything was really good. Service was friendly & attentive. We'll stop by again for sure next time we're in the area. Free wi-fi available. Shared parking lot with other businesses.

We ate lunch at an outside table yesterday. This was about the fourth time we had lunch here and it has been consistently excellent. This time I had wide rice noodles with duck and washed down it with a Father Hennepin Ale from the local craft beer store, which is two doors down. My wife had Coco Thai Basil with chicken. Our daughter had turkey dumplings and spicy edamame. The food was outstanding.
This place has a nice ambiance. I had high expectations. Food was just okay. Maybe it deserves another chance. My lunch was $30. I had salad, sandwich and a Moscow mule.

The staff was so good! Super friendly and charming. The food was good but I've definitely paid less for comparable food in philly. Pet peeve: why are the bathrooms, with fully enclosed individual stalls, gendered? It's 2018, this is fishtown, there's no reason to have gendered bathrooms.

If all it takes to win stars is the location, then this place would definitely be top notch. Loved this feel of this little place! Cute little brick 2 story makes me excited to see what lies in store... Loved how intimate the setting is...Wood floors, white walls, filled with white draped tables intermingled with white-washed wooden posts. Makes everything seem like a blank canvas awaiting the colors and flavors of Thailand to grace the stage. Colorful Thai fare, yes! Flavorful Thai fare, not so much. Ordered a few of the staples I typically prefer on a first visit: Pad Kee Mao and Papaya Salad. Ordered both Medium heat since I'm fairly comfortable with Thai spice. Unfortunately, they either forgot to spice or they just went waaaayyyyyyy too easy on me. The colorful dishes left me yearning for missing flavors and spice. Lunch portions may be a bit smaller than Dinner. Maybe not...but come to think of it, having a larger portion of bland Thai leftovers might have been a bad thing to bring back to the hotel room. Guess my venture into the Philly Thai Cuisine scene just didn't work out. :(

Food was great! Very quick service! Great place for a quick and tasty lunch! I had the lamb gyro which was very good and we had the hummus platter also very good. Small outdoor seating area was a bonus.
Great drinks and service at the bar! Guacamole was delicious (small portion but delicious). It's a fun little spot for cocktails before dinner.

Long over due review. I have been on this place before it changed ownership (more than 2 years ago). And yes, food and service have gotten better. They used to be open 7 days a week, now they're closed on Mondays. It felt like it came without any warning. Mondays are a tough place to be in Carpinteria if you are hungry. This is not a fancy place; it's more like your hole in the wall place. But, the environment is really cozy and homelike (like if it was your grandma's place). I have to say that I had better Thai food, but this is the best Asian food place to eat in Carpinteria. But to be fair, it might be the region of Thai food that is not one of my favorites. Needles to say, the reason for my 4 star rating is that I have a few favorites. Recently discovered the Chow Mein (not your typical Thai plate, but it was really good!). The Massaman Curry and Pineapple fried rice. The Pad Thai and coconut soup need work. The menu has added recently Salmon to the meat alternative (a plus and a mmm), and a thumbs up for gluten free soy sauce option (great for those of us that are sensitive to the wheat in the sauce). And, the spice levels accommodates me (zero tolerance) to my husband (high tolerance). The staff is good at knowing who you are (and I wouldn't call me a regular), and that is one of the reasons I keep on coming. This is also one of the restaurants closes to the camp grounds, so there are lot of tourist. Most locals might avoid.

Ok so now there is serious contention for my favorite pho place. I've been to Pho Hoa (note the extra o) a couple times in the past two weeks. This spot is very large, and very clean. They have a very extensive menu and their service is spot on. I know it's a chain, but I think it's every bit as good as Pho Ha. The pho selections are very similar and they serve beer and wine. We've eaten and taken out from this spot and been very happy with the prices, service and quality of the food. Aces.

While the interior decor and outside may not be most appealing, Hangook Kwan makes up for with amicable service and great and authentic Korean food. They don't have an extremely large menu, somewhere on the average scale with maybe 50-60 unique items, but they have the classics of course, with popular items such as Bul Gol Gi and Be Bim Bop. They also have a number of tables with the wonderful Korean BBQ accessible and it is most delightful! Recommended for Korean food lovers and those interested in trying. The servers, while they will have a medium to heavy Korean accent, are very friendly and will do their best to answer and recommend good and authentic food to you. I've even had servers who recommend us to not try particular menu items because they are only for people with certain tastes. Great service, great food, and a very quaint and homey feel to the restaurant. Look past the heavy accents and it's all there!
Great new BYOB Thai food in the neighborhood! The lemongrass soup and the pad Thai were both delicious. I've only been here once but I will be back!

Just few minutes ago, I just finished eating at this restaurant and customer service SUCKS! Waitress are only nice to those American or like-American people and we are one of them and they don't even smile or greet. Food is not that great at all. I should've take pictures of those grumpy looking waitress. Never return and will tell everyone about it.
The breakfast food is excellent the service good The served vegetarian Omelet with middle eastern flavor that very tasty
NO MSG!! I had the duck noodle Soup and it was amazing. This is the best Laos/Thai restaurant in Rutherford county! I highly recommend trying it out!!

Cute little spot. The menu is easy.to follow with just enough options in each category. ( seafood,poulty,beef and vegetarian) Food was presented well and had great flavor and texture. Those are all of the positive things. We were a party of 5. Once seated we waited more than 20 minutes before we had to approach a waitress about getting some service. The waitress that was helping us was interrupted by the man who seated us. He angrily tossed and kicked the wine menu, the waitress provided across the floor. Once our order was taken the food arrived in a timely manner. The angry man also provided us with a complimentary plate of food for being patient. The food was overshadowed by the angry man, confused staff and lack of timely professional service

In my opinion, it is the best pho along with V and V, and Kings Market. Theirs is the cheapest too. However, their service has to pick it up several notches! The workers are just too complacent and do not seem to care about anyone. .

We have become The Christmas Story family and enjoy eating our Christmas Eve meal at an Asian restaurant. Our usual go-to was closed, so we ended up here. Turned out to be a more-than-nice alternative. Everyone loved the veggie app platter. My massaman curry and Tom yum were the best I've had. Staff were pleasant and attentive. Plan B was A-Ok!

Outstanding! Very warm and friendly-they can't do enough for you! Lunch buffet was incredible! Great variety of food-all of it delicious! Atmosphere is authentic and makes you feel like you've opened the door and landed in India!

I'll give it 5 stars for delivery. 2 families ordered red curry, dragon roll, rainbow roll spicy salmon roll California roll miso soup salad and edamame. Everything was spot on ... The red curry was wonderful and everyone loved it... Should have ordered extra rice... The rolls were better than average and I'd even say on par with the best around. Again I give it 5 stars because they are nearby and deliver, they have no competition for that combo.

Wasn't the best or the worst. Between three people we ordered sesame chicken, both a Philadelphia and unagi roll, and a sauteed mixed vegetable roll. The mixed vegetables and Philly roll we're good, but the unagi tasted a little off compared to other unagi I've had in the past. The sesame chicken was basic - a little to sweet for my taste. The service otherwise was good, and I'd go back - maybe just order something different.

My taste buds are happy, my mouth is on fire...this sums up the food that Chef K whips up in about 4 minutes for you. Expect to wait 30min, that's what it was for me, having 9 people in front. The food is amazing, the flavors will explode in your mouth and your belly will instantaneously thank you. What you get depends on the day, today the Chef made a plate of about a pound of food, comprised of pearl couscous, grilled peaches, cooked cactus (don't eat the skin, tastes like and looks like pomegranate), grilled chicken tikka, fried falafel (I think best I have had so far), and round noodles, all that wrapped up in spicy sauce. You don't get to choose so if you don't like surprises and spicy food, this might not be for you to try. I thought it was delicious.

Absolutely the best Caribbean food in the area. The chef has gathered a tasty collection of recipes from around the Caribbean and is presenting them to you, masterfully, in a relaxed sophisticated environment. Feel confident in choosing this place to have dinner. The only negative is that they don't open for lunch! I can't get enough of this place. Try the Curry Chicken, the Ox Tail was magnificent! The rice and peas (Chick Peas) tastes like someone's Grandma was back there cooking it. Very well done.

Others here have done a great job describing the style of the food and particular dishes. I'd just like to add that about a year ago we ate twice at an Ethiopian restaurant in Washington, DC. DC has the largest Ethiopian population outside of Ethiopia and the restaurant is generally regarded as one of the top one or two in the city. I think Zagol is just as good. We've been twice and thought the service was perfect Used credit card both times with no angst so not sure what that was all about. I recommend Zagol to people all the time. Just love it.

I was pretty underwhelmed with this place unfortunately. I heard good things and brought my family here and we all agreed it was not great thai food. I had pad see ew which was tasty but not the best I've had. My mom's massaman curry was pretty delicious as always but the big offense...the pad thai was terrible. You cant mess up pad thai at a thai place, I'm sorry. It usually has that odd stench to it, but this one was just pretty gross to get a whiff of. There was hardly any peanut, egg, or bean sprouts either. A hint of them but it was really just noodles and chicken. We got an app sampler that had some tasty treats and the environment is pretty clean, but I would definitely choose another thai place over this one.

Great Indian restaurant! I arrived just before closing and was able to order chicken saag with garlic naan. The food is delicious! The restaurant is owned by a husband and wife - the husband was working the front counter and the wife was in the kitchen cooking. Great spot for carry out or a quick bite. It's about the food and not the decor.

The owners of Spice-n-Grill used to own an Indian joint down the street near the Olive/I170 intersection called simply "Indian Food". I was terribly heartbroken when it decided to close up and subsequently elated when they decided to open up a primarily take-out operation north of the Loop area (right next to Schnucks). This place caters more towards a "native" palate than other Indian restaurants in STL. For one, they don't use as much cream in their sauces as other places and offer spicier options. The real difference between this place and other is their selection of unique dishes. They have unique dishes like the Beef Nihari, Lamb Nihari, and Goat Pishwari. These dishes are not often found in other Indian joints in STL. I'd suggest going for one of these. It's their specialty. I would also recommend their plain roti/chappati. These are Indian bread items that resemble Mexican tortillas than naan. I find them to be a better vessel to scoop up curries than naan, since they're not as filling. Go forth and explore this really cool mom and pop place in U City!
i dont think they are opened for business anymore... we went there about 2 weeks ago and there was no sign of anybody, so... it is probably a loss for the locals...

This place is amazing. The food is very clean and cheap. The owner and staff are very friendly and remember customers. I used to eat here all the time when I lived in University City, but recently moved. When I returned, the owner asked where I'd been and offered to deliver to me, even though I technically live outside of the immediate area. I can't say anything about the meat, but I love the Tunisian Tuna sandwich and the Lentil Soup. This is definitely a great, healthy, and affordable place to dine.

The environment is surprisingly amazing. It looks like a little whole in the wall restaurant but when you walk in you really feel like you're in Thailand. The decor is beautiful, it's quiet and peaceful, and the staff is friendly and attentive. Most importantly, the food is delicious.

I was pleasantly surprised with the quality. We ordered the green curry with chicken - good balance of spice and coconut flavor. The sweet and sour chicken was too tangy (2.5 out of 5). Thai iced tea was too sweet, but hey who doesn't like sugar :) Service was okay, they were busy so I can understand them not being as attentive as they could be. Overall, not too bad for a strip mall place in the suburbs.

One of my favorite go-to dinner spots! I've been slowly introducing all of my friends to basil and now we order on a weekly basis. With the friendliest staff, speedy service, and relaxed atmosphere, I couldn't ask for a better place to frequent. I typically order the vegetarian pad see-iew and my only complaint is that the entrees could use more protein (my friends and I find ourselves wanting more beef, tofu, etc.. on our entrees) and I wouldn't mind getting a little more on the plate for the price point. Love it!

So, I am trying to diet and I had only been here for dinner --i stopped for lunch and damn it! They had a buffet my fat ass could not resist. Delicious food. Good service. Lovely atmosphere. Food is piping hot off the buffet line. Definitely recommend.

This was my first Indian food experience. Incredible! $7.99 lunch buffet. Very fulfilling, very flavorful. Goat curry might be my new favorite dish. The garlic naan was great. Honestly, I know next to nothing about what I had, but I loved it all. My friends and I went back for supper the next day. No buffet. We waited quite a while, an hour, before we got our food. Served family style, very friendly staff. Just overwhelmed that night. 5 stars otherwise. Definitely going back next year.
Great little thai place. Small but plenty to choose from. The staff is very friendly. I had the pad thai it was great.

Some of the best Indian food I've had. I work a couple minutes down the road and was craving an Indian food buffet. This place did not disappoint. Everything from the buffet was delicious and they even brought me out an order of fresh garlic naan and didn't charge me. I will definitely be going back!

Dislike dislike dislike. Sweet & sour chicken: the sauce was runny and underwhelming and the chicken bits were hard. General tso: the chicken was kinda missing, the spiciness wasn't noticeable, and the pork fried rice was bland with a refrigerator taste to it. Both were the dinner orders which should have included egg rolls; they were not. Not even utensils were included. We called back to ask about the missing egg rolls and the lady who picked up gave us a hard time but agreed we could go back to pick them up. When we picked up the egg rolls, the lady scolded us because we didn't call ahead of time despite her saying we could just go pick them up. When we got home they were SO GREASY! Like they were sitting in oil instead of being drained. I'll never order from here again.

Went there on August 29th. I had gyro, rice with a chopped salad. I had also ordered hummus. The food was very good and plentiful. I would recommend the restaurant to people who like middle eastern food.

My husband loves Afghan food and we have been to Ariana a few times. In the past, we have always liked the meals and service here, but this time around, it has gone downhill. The food was ok and the service was not great. We were seated at the same time with another couple who walked in just before us. We ordered at the same time. Yet, it took at least 50 minutes before our meal came out. 30 minutes after ordering our entrees, the lady server came to us to ask if we wanted our meal to be spicy! What took so long? Meanwhile, the other couple already had got their meal and was eating. My husband ordered the Lamb Kabob entree ($16.50). The lamb was nicely charred but quite tough and overdone. I ordered the Chicken Kabob ($15.50), which also was nicely charred also, but not bad, it was actually good. The dishes came with onions and pieces of peppers and tomatoes in addition to the meat. The meat portions seem to have shrunk. All food came with a salad with dill/ranch like dressing. It was tasty. The entrées came with what they called basmati rice (but seemed more like long grain rice to me. I am Indian, I know my basmati rice) and Afghan bread. No one came neither to refill our water, nor ask how our meal was. If we wanted service, we had to raise our hand for it. We used the entertainment book discount, which clearly said buy one entrée and get one free (up to $15). Since our lowest price meal was $15.50, we should have got $15 off, but they honored only $13. This to us is misleading the customer. Overall the food was not awful, but I feel it was overpriced for what we got, and the service is not at all great. We will not be returning. Rather go next door to Kabul!

Been wanting to go here for a few weeks now and it surely did not disappoint! This used to be Thai Boat and numerous other things in the past...but I think and hope these new owners are here to stay! They give you Rice chips with Prawn chill sauce as soon as you sit down. Never had these at a thai place before but it was very enticing. We got the Drunken Noodles with Pork in Medium and Vegan Red curry with Tofu in Hot. Both very delicious- the drunken noodles had all the flavors I was looking for (with a hint of whiskey) and they def didn't skimp out on the meat. The Red curry had the perfect mix of coconut milk and basil with a big serving of tofu sided with Jasmine sticky rice. For dessert we had the Thai Fruit Parfait -it's with sliced jackfruit, coconut jelly, in an aromatic jasmine syrup. I personally didn't think it was sweet enough but that's just me. Oh, I also ordered a Thai Iced Tea- taste was standard that you get at every thai place, can't complain. They have a full regular menu and also a separate Vegan menu...and even have vegan dessert options! The menu is as catering as the staff. The woman owner of the restaurant served us and had the cutest smile on her face the entire time. The food came out super fast and the restaurant is very spacious and clean. Not to mention, both the entrees were under $10! Def enjoyed our experience here and will be back to try more menu items...like the stuffed chicken wings and Panang Curry!!
Best dinner!! We didn't know what to expect but wanted to do a BYO and something other than pizza so this was great. Portions were huge and delicious.

Excellent food. We had the buffet. Chicken tikka, vegetable curry. Tandoori chicken. They brought naan to the table and had delicious onion chutney and tamarind chutney. Service was fast, efficient and attentive. We will be back! Ticket was $23 good value. We recommend gateway to India to those who love good Indian cuisine!

Best tacos in Philadelphia! Best workers in Philadelphia! I just want them to open up a restaurant already or a truck on Penn's campus. I'm sure they make enough money to do both haha P.S. have to be patient with the "sometime" long wait BUT IT IS WORTH IT!
Amber is addictive!!! Our office does delivery every 2 wks and we gorge on all our favorites. Worth every penny and the leftovers are better than anything else I ever bring home!

Went for happy hour on a weekday with few people there. It was two of my friends and I and we sat at the bar. It took over a half hour to get fried spring rolls and over 45 minutes to get our pho and fried rice. The food was very very good, but the service was extremely slow for the amount of people in the restaurant at the time. Perhaps they are understaffed? Regardless, I'll try it again soon.

Was glad to see they were open late on a Friday night - open til 10, we got there about 9:20. We had the larb gai, the green curry with chicken and the duck fried rice. Sounds like a very similar menu to what lived in this spot before. The food was good, the staff was very friendly. We sat outside at a picnic table in front of the truck next to a small water fountain/feature that helped with the Dale Mabry road traffic noise. I need another visit and try another dish to make another assessment. But so far, it's a quick, good Thai fix.

After finding this place on yelp and seeing that all 266 reviews gave it 5 stars, I was excited to try it out yet skeptical. All of my skepticism melted away as soon as I walked in with my wife. We were graciously greeted by the owner, Andre, who seated us and helped us through the menu options. Andre and the rest of his staff were extremely polite and attentive. He waited tables along with the other waiters, which was refreshing to see out of an owner. As for ambience, this place is perfect for date night or a night out with friends. It's neither pretentious nor a hole in the wall. The place has a very good vibe, playing chill Jamaican/Caribbean music at just the right volume. Not to mention that the restaurant is extremely clean. Now the best for last, the food! Andre's wife is the cook and what a cook she is! They start you off with some melt in your mouth bread. There's two kinds, both great, but the cheese filled one was the best. My wife and I ordered a beef filled patty for appetizer and it was delicious. So delicious that my wife ordered another one towards the end of our meal when it was already clear that we were going to be taking food home. For our entree, we had a hard time choosing between the jerk chicken, oxtail and goat curry. Andre made the decision easy for us by suggesting the combination platter which allowed us to try all three. The jerk chicken was perfectly spiced fall off the bone chicken. A little spicy but I love spicy food. The oxtail was also fall off the bone and bathed in a delicious gravy that goes perfect with the rice. No complaints about the goat curry either. You can't go wrong with any of these as an entree. In addition, we also ordered the spicy Caribbean jerk chicken wings as an entree. It was flavorful and spicy by itself, but I would recommend trying their hot sauces with the wings (Only if you really like spicy food). This restaurant will definitely be a place that I go to time and time again and I highly recommend that you try it at least once. I will definitely be telling all my friends about it.
Very friendly and attentive staff who gave excellent service. The food was amongst the best Thai cuisine that I have experienced. Would definitely come back again.

This place is absolutely worth a stop if you're in Arabi, or generally looking for Middle Eastern food. I believe the place is Lebanese, for people who can tell the difference in Middle Eastern food styles. They have all the things you expect to find at a Middle Eastern restaurant in the U.S. (falafel, gyro, lentil soup, etc.). They also have excellent baklava. The restaurant is attached to a grocery store, with mostly Middle Eastern ingredients, mostly canned or packaged goods.

My favorite place in Broad Ripple has been the best Indian restaurant in Indianapolis for years. However, that just changed. Amber Indian is a notch above. First thing, this place charges more. It was $10.00 for the buffet, but I would spend $10 any day to eat here. I will always pay more for quality food made with standards. I will not pay high prices for average to below average gimmicky food that seems to be the trend these days. Why people waste their hard earned money on those places when there is a bunch of places like this around, I don't know......... They have the largest Indian Buffet in Indianapolis that I have been too. To me it seemed close to double the amount of items at a typical Indian Buffet. They also have a selection of what I believe is Pakistan dishes. Everything that I had was cooked perfectly and seasoned well. Large staff which a lot of other places don't have. This results in everything is taken care of quickly, buffet are is clean and is stocked at all times. (This is a problem at several other places I have been where it takes 5-10 minutes for more to come out when they run out.) I didn't have a dish I didn't like. The best thing for me was a spicy chicken dish that I have never had before. It wasn't Chile Chicken which I have ate many times, but it was similar but much better. Everything that I ate would get a 9 or higher rating with the Chicken getting a 10.

I love Thai food and I have one (count 'em, one) friend who loves Thai food too, so when we get together, we eat Thai food. He lives in Carp, so when I visited, we ate here. We ordered off the specialty menu, so soup or salad, and appetizers came with the meal--spring rolls, fried shrimp and a couple sort-of chow mein noodle chips. The appetizers were a little old-tasting, like they had been sitting under a heat lamp, certainly not fresh out of the fryer. Also, although the soup was good (chicken in a coconut milk base), it was not very hot (temp.) as if they had already turned off the burner under the soup in preparation for closing. Like I said, it was very good....even fantastic, but I am always surprised when I don't burn myself on the first spoonful. The entrees were also very good --I had the basil chicken and my companion had a chicken curry (panang, I think). They weren't terribly spicy at all, and, perhaps even a little bland in the flavor department. Nothing distinctive to speak of, but yummy nonetheless. We didn't have dessert, as we were full, but I was also surprised to note that the portions were small enough that we had no leftovers. With oriental food, I always expect to end up with leftovers...but I even finished my rice here. Service was fast, and courteous, as we were there near closing on a slow night, I chalked it up to them trying to hustle us out of there. On the other hand, since other reviewers report fast service, maybe they're always like that.
I ordered Thai vegetables with chicken "Thai Hot". The dish was below average and had zero heat. I would not recommend this place to a friend nor an enemy. Go elsewhere & have a great meal.
Threw up after eating here. Absolutely disgusting Not good at all I was excited to try, not authentic, too much food coloring . Everything tastes fake

The food truck finally came back. I'm so excited!! The food is good as always!! It's a platter with chicken, falafel, hummus and other yummy stuff I don't really know what they are called. You really don't have to ask him what he has, cz the platter is really the only thing they sell. It is 10 dollars but huge portion. I always get deathly full. But it's really really good!!!! I waited like half an hour in line but it's totally worth it!! The truck is now located across the street from the original location, by the Starbucks, due to the construction.

Went and tried their lunch buffet today and let me tell you! This is the quickest, the best and most welcoming establishment I've been to in the Manchester/ballwin area. Since moving from the east coast I've been looking for great ethnic food and did I find it!

After finding a sign posted on the door at Buttercup and a line nearly out the door at Ants Pants, La Va looked especially welcoming following our trek through the snowy (read: ice-covered and sometimes treacherous) streets. Finding an empty table at 11:30 on a Saturday and breakfast for two served within minutes for under $15? Awesome when you're starving. Right on the cusp between Rittenhouse and Graduate Hospital, this place is just hipster/yuppified enough, both cozy and cool. We settled on bagel breakfast sandwiches and coffee and were happy with the results-- doughy everything bagels with plenty of onion and sesame seeds, melty cheese and omelette-style eggs. They offer plenty of variety at La Va, with options like turkey bacon and greek-style eggs with spinach and feta. My boyfriend went for the pesto. The regular coffee was good, but I was super-psyched for my mochacchino, rich and chocolatey with a swirly heart on top. I was surprised to see that at least half of the people taking up tables were hard at work, but most seemed respectful of the carefully scotch-taped signs on every table, asking patrons to kindly vacate their tables after half an hour of "studying" during peak hours. Though my laptop and I don't generally take part in cafe business ventures, La Va seems like a great place to get some writing done, and the music was chill. As far as art and atmosphere go,I want to use the word "urban-outfitters-esque"... I hear there's also a well-stocked book and game shelf near the back. I'm still thinking about that chocolate croissant that i was eyeballing, so I'm sure I'll be back...

Just flew in from New York tired and hungry. Treated super nice by Caroline and Mike as they arranged and rearranged tables for our large party. The food was innovative and flavorful. All was really excellent but the sriracha wings, sweet potato fries, curry and chicken mojo were exceptional. Service was great and ambience was relaxing. Wish the cappuccino machine was on during week days...but this place is an excellent choice!

Food was very good, unfortunately service was very slow. Many waiters and waitresses standing around . We ordered truffle fries but they did not come out until the end of the meal. Overall good food poor service

I love the Quality of the food they provide and the Taste is Awesome. Best indian Restaurant in Nashville Metro area i can think of in 2016. Everything i ate at Parsis is just awesome. My Fav's All Biryani's Paneer Butter Masala Chicken Tikka All Naan's

Interesting place - this is mainly a takeout place. If you eat in, you use plastic ware - plates, forks and cups. They have a small buffet which is priced on weight and then you can order from the menu. I chose to do both. I ordered the veg curry, naan, and veg samosa. The food was good. From the buffet I had some basmati rice and aloo gobi - I'm a little disappointed in the buffet because the food was not hot, not even warm. That was a damper. It was very inexpensive and tasted authentic. I would have liked the buffet food to be served hot and fresh!!

Huge menu so if you aren't really sure what you like, there is bound to be something you will enjoy. Service is friendly and the portions are a good size for a great overall value. I love Thai food and thought everything was good but not great. My group tried a variety of things and were all satisfied but not knocked out. I will go back again if I feel the Thai craving.
Gotta say: wasn't impressed. I went for the lunch special and the price was great, but the food was pretty bland, and I couldn't help the feeling the kitchen wasn't very clean.

I was skeptical. Ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala. Was a bit spicy for my wimpy taste buds. But it was manageable. Thought it was so yummy until I tried my friends chicken korma. Wow!!!! That was my favorite. Great, rich flavor! The garlic naan went well with our meal. Good flavor and nice, soft, chewy texture. I preferred the steamed basmati over the rice pilau.

The first time I tried the southern sandwich. The chicken was so deliciously breaded and everything in it was so good I had to try another sandwich the next day. I got the buffalo and it was amazing. The chicken did not disappoint, the buffalo sauce was not like anything I've had, and they used real blue cheese chunks (not the liquid, ranch-like form). The sandwiches taste good even as heated leftovers. The sandwich size is between a shorti and classic from wawa, but the chicken pieces are large so it's filling. I definitely want to try their entire menu.

The inside was very clean looking better than most Chinese places I've been. I got the hot and sour soup it was only $3 and there is a minimum of $5 on the card. He was nice enough to give me $2 back in cash. The soup was delicious and I will definitely be returning!

4.5 stars, technically. First off, came in late, just before closing and were still served with a smile! that goes a long way for me. there were also still a lot of cupcakes available (except chocolate which is apparently really amazing. will have to try next time). Amanda helped us, and she was super pleasant and friendly. If she could get a rating on her own it would be a 5!!! now, to the cupcakes! they were large, and moist, with a LOT of frosting. the one i had did have some kind of filling (i had PB cup, which is chocolate with PB frosting and a Reese cup on top). i prefer less frosting to cake ratio. i dont really like eating just frosting and no cake. and it really didnt need the filling for my preference. The PB frosting was light and fluffy- it may have had a trace of cream cheese which i normally dont like, but i thought it was subtle enough and i enjoyed it. The cupcakes are baked in a paper wrap and they reallllly stick to the wrap. i had to eat with a fork (not that bad) but i kept thinking i wish i had more cake and it wasnt all stuck to the wrapper! flavor overall was delicious, very sweet. i also tried the orange spice sorbetto, which was amazing!!! it was a perfect fall flavor, if you are into cold treats in the fall. I would go back but i would try the mini cupcakes, hoping that i would have a better cake:frosting ratio.

Ordered in from GrubHub last night and thought it was excellent. The chicken biryani (mild) was delicious and spicy, with smooth raita and good not. Lamb Rogan Josh was tender and rich. Highly recommended--this is our new go-to for Indian Food on the north side of Indianapolis.

The food is solid Indian fare. One of the two best in the Philly area. The staff is just the rudest staff I have ever seen. I really couldn't fathom it. It was as if we had offended someone by simply coming here to eat. That having been said, the Na'an is excellent; the Lamb Rogan Josh is great; every plate the 4 of us had was delicious. Perhaps if we come again we'll bring out own wine (it's a BYOB) so if the help continues to be surly we can give them a little 'tude back and whip them into shape.

After a long client meeting, I came to Pho Hoa for a late lunch -- we wanted something quick and something deliciously Vietnamese. The place was packed with lunchtime eaters, and people from call walks of life enjoying delicious noodles and pho. I ordered a vermicelli bowl with BBQed beef and spring rolls. Everything came out really quickly, and was delicious. The service was OK, but we could have used some quick tea refills. I'll definitely stop by here the next time I'm in Chinatown. Good, quick food. And next time, I'll try the Pho!

While the outside seating area is nice and the walk up bar is convenient, the music was terrible. I saw the "DJ" playing more on his phone then he tended to the music. Drinks were also ridiculously expensive. Don't know that I'd give this place another try.

Favorite Chinese restaurant on this side of town. The service is always very fast and the staff is friendly. The crab Rangoon is DELICIOUS! also the chicken lo-mein is a must have. If you are looking for something sweet the sugar biscuits are yummy as well. Definitely recommend ordering from here for lunch or dinner.

How are the reviews so high for this place? Seems like a glorified take out joint to me. Came here on Wednesday to see what the hype was about and left mildly disappointed. You walk in and order at the counter. You can sit outside out front where they have two or three tables, or inside down the steps where there is a TV and some chains on the wall for I guess when they want to get all 50 Shades of Grey. My girl had the garlic chicken wrap, way to much lettuce and dry as hell. It was a decent size however for the price. I went with the Chicken shawarma platter, and a side of BABA with with extra pita. Baba was just okay, hummus was okay, my chicken was dry as well. Once again portions for the price were pretty good and the food wasn't bland. But 5 stars though? You yelpers getting soft man. This place is a 3 for sure. Bonus: They were playing hip hop audible when I was eating, 5 star music selection, NAS, Biggie, Jay. They was killin it!

We dined here for the first time tonight and it was phenomenal. I'm vegan but the rest of my family isn't, so normally eating out together is a struggle. The owner was soooo friendly and he went over the menu to help me figure out what I could eat. There are a lot of vegan options and everything we got was amazing. My two year old is pretty picky and even she was happy with the food. You just can't beat a good Mom and Pop restaurant with great food and friendly service. This place is a new favorite and we can't wait to go back! I will be sure to update my review with pictures, the next time we go back.

Updating my review. Since close to my work I came again for lunch. I put in my order but then decided to order some egg rolls after my food had already came out. The waitress was very pleasant and smiled and said of course. I ordered the flame broil beef and rice this time. Came out quick and was very tasty. I've been here a few times now. Each time has gotten better. It's a little different. This place is connected to 7'11. You seat yourself and they will come and bring you a menu and drink order. They don't really say a whole lot to you though. First time I came I wasn't sure if I seated myself or if they do (you just pick a table). Today I got the rare steak Pho. Broth was tasty and it came out quick. When done eating you have to go to register to pay (or so far from my experience).

A friend told me about Petra and we tried it tonight. It is a wonderful restaurant. We are both vegetarians. The food is so tasty and fresh. We ordered the veggie platter with the bonus as a starter. It was relish. The service is also great. Friendly staff and fast. I was impressed. Will return for sure.
Yum!!! So glad I found this place. So cheap and such lovely staff. I'll defo be back.
Great food, could have better customer service and make me feel as if they appreciate the money you are paying.

Well seriously, who doesn't love Remedy. It's the perfect place to go on a date or meet up with your girl friends for coffee chats that last hours. I've had some great drinks and food at this location and some even better heart to hearts with great friends. The staff are wonderful people, it's close to campus making it an ideal off campus, but still kinda close venue to get away and study. I find this location is quite busy so you may have to wait a little while to find a table. Over all though I would never pass on an opportunity to hit up remedy, it's pretty rad!

My husband and I have been here a number of times, and basically we have been pleased. Chicken Biryani tastes wonderful. I always get it mild and it doesn't disappoint. Temperature of the food could be a little hotter. Garlic naan is always excellent. We have always had friendly, attentive staff. We have ordered the Kulfi for dessert a few times. One time it looked, and had a consistency of something that had been around too long. Overall though, we are pleased and eat there once every week and a half or so. We hope they're here for a long time!
Never got to try it. 99% sure the place is shut down. Empty inside and phone is disconnected. Too bad, looked good!

This was a very cool and tasty dining experience. This was my first time trying Ethiopian food, but I know when something tastes good, and this was great. We shared the Queens Eight Platter for 2 (more than enough for you and another person) and dipped the Injera in all the awesome meat and vegetable choices. I've never had bread like the Injera before, and I loved the consistency and how it was all rolled up. Apparently it's a great gluten-free option because it is made out of some flower or something. Most of the dishes on our sampler were stewed meats of various kinds and seasoned veggies and lentils. In the middle was a traditional drumstick and soft boiled hen egg - very good! For my beverage I tried the Queen's Secret Recipe Honey Drink (recommended by the server) and it somehow tasted a lot like honey without being overly sweet. I think they use green tea as the base. The server explained everything on the plate very well, and was such a nice guy! We really enjoyed talking to him and hearing about the traditional Ethiopian cuisine. I also felt like his suggestions were very good, as we were pretty much lost without his assistance!

Wish I could eat here every day and give this place 10 stars!! The decorations are amazing and the food is as well!!! Everything I tried was better than expected! The only strange thing is there is no table service. You order at the bar and grab a number. Then they bring the food to where-ever you choose to sit. Excited to see the back garden area in the spring! Don't forget to try the drink specials they have!!

The food was good but very salty. I hear that they are closed right now for remodeling. It's a family owned restaurant and the kids are allowed to walk in and our as they please, no problem with that, but keep the back door closed so we don't have to see the family room. I hope that they add a bathroom for customers.

This place really is as good as the reviews say it is. We had: Ox tail: Done perfectly. If you undercook ox tail, it's chewy. This was done right. Ribs: Tender and well flavored. Pork chops: Excellent. What makes it even better but may be strange for the well-heeled crowd is the skin is still on the meat. Yes, pigs actually have skin! And it's tasty. Rice with beans (which came with the dishes): I'm usually not a huge fan of rice with beans, but this is very good, especially with the juices of the above dishes. We got there at around 6:15pm on a Wednesday evening and they had already run out of most dishes, so you want to get there early. The area is as bad - or at least it feels as bad - as many reviews say it is. The situation sets up for the perfect marketing tagline - "Food so good you'd risk your life to get it!" I live in Carmel where the exact opposite is usually the case: boring food and safe locales. Too bad...

Meh. That's the best word I can use to describe this place. I would give the food itself 4 stars. It was actually my first brush with Thai food and I did enjoy it. My husband's food was so hot it was miserable in my opinion! He liked it, but had to eat it very slowly to even get it down, with lots of iced tea. I do understand Thai is spicy but it was specifically recommended by the server as "Not too spicy" so they may be a little out of touch. But my dish was rather good, I had the Chicken Noodles. The thick flat noodles seemed to be house made and they worked well all together as a dish with the chicken. The mark down here goes for the service which I would give 2 stars to. I felt uncomfortable and little unwelcome here. Several times we were passed over with no word as to how things were going, this being our first time having Thai food we wanted a suggestion from the server but by the time she got over to us, I had decided on what I wanted already while my husband used the server's suggestion. I can't explain the feeling of discomfort here other than to say, it seems like they cared very little whether or not we (or their other customers) were there. We also were a little cramped with the table arrangement. It felt a little pricey for what we got, but in all fairness this is centrally located so that can usually bump up prices. My official thoughts: I can't recommend this place based on the service. Based on my limited experience with Thai I can't speak to the authenticity but as food in general it was pretty good.

Lemme just start off by saying, I grew up in Iran and I know my kebabs. When it comes to chicken, lamb, and beef kebabs on skewers, it's really easy for a Persian to tell if they know what they're doing or not. And Ariana offers SUCH an exquisite experience. The basmati rice is fantasticly cooked. The bread is fresh, homemade, and DELICIOUS. And not only have they mastered the art of making kebabs, but they give you ONE skewer with THREE different meats on it. How the hell?? Each meat cooks differently... Some cray ish!! I'm giving this place 5 starts for 4 reasons: 1. The staff is friendly and really helpful. Ask for a glass of water, and they'll run for it. 2. They know how to make, HANDS DOWN, the tastiest kebabs. (At least in the Philadelphia area.) 3. Their hookah is ON point! Wide variety of flavors, and they surprised us once with a pineapple on top (where you put the tobacco.) Which was SO cool. Never tried that one before. 4. And lastly, the flavors from spices take me back to when I used to eat kebabs with my family in Iran. After living outside Iran for quite some time, I've been in the haunt for some legit kebabs in Philadelphia and it's been extremely disappointed. Then I gave this place a try. The first bite of their chicken kebab delightfully reminded me of what middle eastern kebab's ALL about!! My dad came to Philly from Iran for the first time, and he thought this place was the bomb too. And my dad's NEVER wrong. EVER.

A hole in the wall place...was here one Thu night when one of our friend recommended this place for good grill food and they had BYOB. A small restaurant with few tables does not look lavish or onset but the food blew out our expectations. We ordered the tandoori platter and Lamb Bihari Kabob, Malai Kofta and few breads. The Lamb Bihari Kabob was tender and melting in the mouth. One of the finest tandoori I have eaten so far and make me to go again there. The Breads were fresh and did not feel like store purchased and reheated one. The Malai Kofta was not like the regular one or the ones that I have eaten in other Indian restaurants elsewhere..very different and delicious. I have not tried their rice items and will go there again to taste it out. Heard they are opening one more in Montgomery Ave....Way to go!

1 star is too much for this place. If you want to eat horrible food that not only tastes very bad but also doesn't resemble anything Thai then this is the place for you. I didn't like the food but it straight up gave my partner food poisoning. We tried alerting the owner that the food tastes strange, we wanted to return a dish that tasted completely off but the owner said that he won't return the dish or exchange it and that he will call the cops if we don't pay for the dish, even though there was clearly something wrong with it.
This place was amazing. The food was great.The owner was super nice and welcoming. We will DEFINITELY be back!!!

Very clean and recently opened restaurant. Inside they have about 10 wooden glossy tables. There is also outdoor seating, about 3-4 tables. The decor is a nice wooden floor, white/blue themed painted walls and the ordering counter is made out of small tiled stones. The staff is friendly and ambience is not loud, background music in greek or some shit similar. In the kitchen, the cooks are Mexican and very friendly and polite. The food is very good here! I recommend you come here for lunch or dinner. A chicken pita for example is $7.27. Bathrooms are very clean too.

The new location on Washington at 10th is easily accessible, the food remains exceptional and reasonably priced. The menu has also expanded to include sushi and Japanese dishes. We loved everything we tried.
Great food. Pork Jowl was awesome! Eat it like a taco wrapped in herbs. Fried chicken was also great.
Small,cozy place. Authentic south Indian dishes. Rates are also pretty cheap. Good food.

Went here last night with family and I can't believe I have never been here before. I can only describe this great South Philly BYOB as: If I were on death row and was being asked for my last meal, this is where I would want it to come from. The best Caesar Salad in the city. My main course was a huge seafood Fra Diavlo with clams, muscles, shrimp, lobster, crab, and calamari in a great spicy red sauce. The fried romaine lettuce special was very tasty and not a combination that you would think would go well together. Our group also had the filet, pork chop special, and the shrimp scampi which were generous in size and delicious. We were not hungry for desert, however our server treated us to an after dinner pineapple shot. Can't wait until my next visit.
Some of the best Indian food my wife and have ever had, and we eat a lot of Indian food. The Saag Paneer is amazing.

I've gone to this place 2 times and both times I have been completely satisfied. I gave it only 4 stars bc I've only had the falafel sandwich and the greek salad. It is hard to find a good falafel sandwich in the area but look no further. Love this tiny gem.

The Captain Crunch Tilapia Burrito and the veggie burger are AMAZING. I've pretty much tried everything on their menu, and everything is delicious. You can't go wrong ordering anything on there. The bubble teas are really good too, and the flavors of the tea change from time to time. Service is extremely friendly and efficient. I wish I was back in Philly again just for this place.
Great little place for lunch or dinner or grabbing a bubble tea treat. They have quite the selection of boba options and tea flavors. If I was in the area again I would stop in for another boba.

Another lunch with Natdogg, another new restaurant to try along 97 Street. Next on the list, Filipino and Pho 97 Restaurant, a Vietnamese and Filipino spot if you couldn't guess from the name. Menu is insanely long. They have a couple combo specials (only available weekdays) advertised behind the counter. There's also a buffet every Sunday (from 11:00am to 3:00pm). Can't believe they have to explicitly state no take out or leftovers are allowed... - Banh bot loc (#4) ($6.50) - started with their tapioca dumpling. These were baaaaaaaad. If you're expecting banh bot loc, think again. The dumplings were soggy and filled with mushy shrimp. We weren't impressed. - Combo 3 ($10.99) - I decided to try one of their special combo deals. Figured it would be smartest to stick with their Filipino dishes. You get a plate of white rice, ginisang, toge and adobo pork ribs. The adobo pork was tender and meaty. The rest was unmemorable. - Pansit canton (#109) ($10.99) - Natdogg went with a typical Filipino/Chinese noodle dish. Fried noodles with pork, chicken, prawns and vegetables. It was okay; again, pretty bland. We wanted to like this place (the server was very sweet) but unfortunately, the food didn't impress. Running out of new places to try on 97.

I got the Pad Thai combo special and it was delicious. The coconut "chiller" (kinda like a boba tea smoothie) and it was straight up delicious. Good service and fairly price. Great, simple location. I'll be back.
Simply put......The best Thai in town. Actually the only true Thai in town. I lived in Thailand for a year and I have been lost to try and find authentic Thai. Thank You Bangkokville!!!

Go to this place! It's easily my favorite place to grab some Thai food. The fresh rolls are awesooommeee... green, spicy, crunchy heaven. The soups are hot and delicious, and the curries are tasty as hell. The food is consistently good, and the staff are all friendly. The restaurant is spotlessly clean and well lit. If you want a satisfying, reasonably priced meal, this is the place to go.
Had lunch here today for the first time. Chicken roll ups were very good as well as the Greek salad. Staff friendly and quick service. Everything tasted very fresh! Will be back!!

Wish i could give zero star but i can't. The service was just terrible! This young lady server kept rolling her eyes and it seems like she doesn't want to serve tables. Shen she gave us waters, it almost spilled on our table. The milkteas that my friends had were not closed right. She even knew it. It was really an awful experience. I just hope the management would do something about it. I also had another friend who dined there and told me the same thing. It's the same lady too.

We were staying the night in Reno and had a hankering for some good Asian food....and we were not disappointed. I don't give 5 stars often but they definitely deserve it. We were there about 5:30 and not many patrons were there....but they started packing in the place after 6pm. You know the food is good when 70% of the clientele is of some Asian descent. My only regret is that we were passing through and will not have the opportunity to eat here again. Superior food....excellent service and friendliness....cute decor and impeccably clean. If you are in the area....STOP and eat here, you will not regret it.

Indian cuisine is hard to find in Florida. I am from New York and have been spoiled with amazing Indian food. I have tasted great Indian food in Boston and Chicago. Now let's get on with the review of the food. I ordered chicken tikka masala which is my favorite dish. I lose respect for restaurants that can not make a good tikka masala. This place had the best chicken tikka masala I have ever had, in Florida . I had ask for it to be spicy and they didn't just dump the whole spice seasoning in there. It was spicy enough to give a good kick but not to spicy that it burn going down. The location could be better because it is very hard to get into the place off Tyrone blvd. if that was different I be in haven. I am a very happy costumer. I will continue tongi there again.

We ordered from this restaurant because we both love Chinese food. After a long days work we were looking forward to our meal. However we were very disappointed. The food was tasteless. It's almost like they forgot to season the food. Then the sauces were bitter instead of sweet. I wish I could find something positive to say. Considering how expensive our food was, we won't be ordering from there again.

Wow! First time here; certainly not our last. Food, service, atmosphere - all great. The restaurant seems to be run beautifully - from the moment the reservation is made. My husband and I were greeted and seated upon arrival. Courses were not rushed, and the menu was explained beautifully. Amazing how well orchestrated everything is in such tight quarters. Tables are tended to by all waitstaff, yet there are no miscommunications - no dropped balls. Our meals were delicious. I won't detail what we had, because the menu changes. Let me just say, I can't imagine anything being any less delicious. The only "negatives" I can share are our entrees were both a little on the salty side. Not awful by any means, but we're just more sensitive to salt. Also, my husband's ribeye was much flatter than the ones we saw at other tables - and it had no bone. Tasty, but slightly disappointing to my husband since he based his selection on what he saw. Regardless, we look forward to our next dinner at Zeppoli and highly recommend it.

Such amazing food in this little hideaway restaurant. Just behind Busch Gardens is Zeko's. Tasty Greek food. We had the gyro with their crispy steakfries. Also the 5 wings with 1/2 fried shrimp was so tasty! Such a good find, and friendly staff!

The best Indian food around, for sure! I have been going to Shere e Punjab in Media for three years now since I moved to PA, and I always have a fantastic experience. The naan is perfection, and the palak paneer at spice level 4 knocks my socks off. I go there with friends for the buffet on a regular basis, and we always leave content. The new bar area looks nice, but I do miss being able to bring in my own bottle of wine or six-pack of beer to share.
whoooaaaa! great indian food...very clean... very professional

Blu Fig is a very tasty spot to check out if you're driving down Nolensville road. The tahini sauce is just about one of the best I've ever had (I usually ask for some extra), and the gyros are great. The staff is extremely friendly, and welcoming. The decor may take some people by surprise, and perhaps the blue walls may be a bit much for some people, but I don't mind it - I'm there for the food!

My husband and I were regulars here when it first opened. It was a quick, delicious lunch after grocery shopping. However, we were incredibly disappointed by our last meal. The portions appear to be reduced by half. We were left hungry after quickly finishing our salad and rice bowls. We were also disappointed to learn that adding a small amount of rice to a salad bowl would be an up charge. Sad to say it is no longer worth the money and we will not be returning.

My rule of thumb is eat here twice before I judge a restaurant. First time, was pretty good. Can't say so for the second. My real problem was my fried rice veggies and pork. It really was just fried rice with a garish on the top. Second, everything tasted the same no matter the dish. Skip this place, save your $$$.

Visiting Indiana and my best friend and her husband brought me here! I had the pan fried egg noddles with chicken and vegetables... I finished it ALL! It was perfect along with my slushy green tea bubble tea! Delicious!

for $5/lb you get amazing, fresh indian food, to-go or sit-n-eat. they give you free water and hot sauce. 2x samosas for $2. and with your frequent flier card you get 10% off basically (every 10th LB free). i'm not a vegetarian but their veg dishes are so good, i almost never go with 'curry chicken,' just seems boring (if you are, bring your dates/sig other here). delivery is not as good a deal as the buffet but still fair, and same delicious food. agree w/other that service is top notch, very friendly and accommodating. my roomie is indian, we go here 2-3x/week, and he's picky.

Some English is spoken here. There were some tables to eat at, but we didn't. I wish we had, because the sweet sour sauce would probably have made it into the order for sweet sour chicken. The family is nice. Food....eh. Even without the mistake that left my daughter eating chicken nuggets is was only so so. Spice it baby, spice it. Please!

Food is always delicious and is better than any Indian food I have had in Philly!! Service is always great and on time when I order out. As good as home made Indian (I've had some so believe it!). Saag paneer is awesome and flavorful. Samosas are mouth watering. LOVE this place. It's become a staple for my husband and I!!

The lunch special was tasty and reasonable. It consists of 3 courses: I had a nicely seasoned small bowl of Lemongrass Soup, the crispy and flavorful Thai dumplings and the Evil Jungle Princess which was not as spicy as I expected but good nevertheless. My lunch partner had the Lemongrass Soup, the Thai dumplings which she rated good. For her entree she had the Pad Thai which was ok but she felt the flavors of the different components of the dish didn't stand out as they should have. The waitstaff was very friendly and attentive. The decor is very Thai and tasteful without being overwhelming. All in all, a good place to enjoy Thai food.

My favorite coffee spot! You can tell by the way this place is always packed that they must be doing something right. The staff is very friendly, the food is delicious, and the coffee is great. One thing to note is that this is a "cozy" corner cafe... Tables will fill up so get there early if you are looking to sit down.
Horrible clientele, great beer selection and very knowledgeable bar staff. Will probably come back just for St.Bernard's Triple but beyond that very boushchwa crowd.

I highly highly recommend this place. The hummus is silky and well flavored. The rice is buttery and has a beautiful flowery spice I can't put my finger on. I got a lamb kabob and a chicken kabob. The meats were tender and excellently spiced. The dishes reminded me of my grandmother's cooking and I felt happy. They decorated the restaurant well and created a pleasant atmosphere. It was clean and our waiter was a gentleman. I am so glad to have found this place. I am going to be their new regular.

I came here with a friend with my Groupon deal. The food is absolutely terrible and the service was just as bad. I ordered my regular order I would usually get at any Vietnamese restaurant, which is their special pho with everything in it. We tried two phos total and egg rolls for appetizer. We waited for about 25 minutes until our food came and it wasn't even very crowded. There is only one server, and he did not know much about the menu, and did not bother to really "serve" us.
