When the egg rolls came (finally), they were "okay" at best. It isn't the best but it isn't the worst thing ever. They were warm temperature, almost cold. I like my food hot. I think the server left all of our orders in the kitchen for a while because both our pho and egg rolls were almost cold. When our pho came, it was absolutely terrible. The broth was practically like water. It had no beef flavor at all. The portion of a large was pretty small, and the rice noodles were in one big clump as if, they hardly even boiled it long enough. The beef wasn't very great either. The seating at this place isn't very cozy. The tables are pretty close to each other, so it seems like the table next to us were on top of us. The parking wasn't that great either since there was a limited amount in this "little" shopping area (very hard to miss!). Overall, I was not pleased one bit. I wouldn't come here again if I did not have a Groupon deal. The food needs more work, along with the service.

Came here with my girls the other day and we were pretty much the only ones in the restaurant. I ordered #39 and it was DELICIOUS. It was some type of yellow curry with chicken, and while it said spicy it really wasn't and all. That would be my only complaint about the food. Then again I'm pretty sure I have a leather tongue. The service was meh. Meh only because the waiter was a bit rude. Well more like a lot rude. He did bring our food out really quickly though which was nice. Oh and then he awkwardly placed the only other patrons right next to us. Thankfully we were about to leave but jeez that was unnecessarily uncomfortable. It was far too quiet! But overall a really delicious place to eat. I would definitely recommend it to anyone.
Awesome food! Well seasoned and true to the Puerto Ricans .. Will come back for sure ! And the mojitos are amazing

We had the food delivered (free delivery for a close radius) and was very impressed. Grubhub kept you apprised of the delivery time via email, and the food actually arrived early. Limited menu, but it is after all a small business. Saag Paneer and Chicken Korma were excellent, and you can't beat the price. I'm a fan...

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I believe the best food I ever had it my take long time but I know I have to eat fresh food some food can take time to prepare some not .so don't be mad if you have to wait longer than other people just come in , when the owner told me that I have to wait 30 mt I thought will as long the food is good thats all I care about price is right the food is best I will come back every time I have time family owned nice people good service I will come back with my friends again best Indian food at least in Idaho. Thanks taj mahal thank you sohayil see you soon

This place is aptly named, because, whoever is the Chef here, could or should be the Guru to other Indian chefs. I am a vegetarian who adores Indian food. I've been eating it for about 15 years now, any chance I have gotten, all over the US, and this is the absolute best Indian food I have had anywhere. On my last count, I've been to about 25 Indian restaurants one or more (some many, many, more) times. Not only does Guru's Indian Cuisine offer quality food, they also offer quantity, with the largest menu I have seen anywhere. An absolute must try is the Avocado Chaat, which I have never seen or had anywhere else. It's absolutely delicious. And on the night we visited, Methi Paratha was on the Chef's special menu and it was absolutely delicious. The service was very friendly, and the meal ended with a small, complimentary serving of cardamom rice pudding (kheer), which was the perfect little bit of sweetness to finish the meal. The restaurant very clean, and nicely decorated. Take a look at the extensive menu and go and try it for yourself. You will not be disappointed!
Excellent shrimp spring rolls and pho ga. Definitely will return on our next trip. It's a good respite from heavy creole/Cajun food. Family run and many Vietnamese eat here.

Terrible service. Waited forever and am still sitting here waiting for my waitress so I can just get a check. Have my table away multiple times and food for a few apps took forever. This place can't handle any sort of volume of customers. Also menu is very limited.

We had a great family dinner at Guru's celebrating my father in law's birthday! Our waitress Priya was great and attentive. The food was good and prices reasonable. They are also BYOB. We will definitely return in the future!
Everything was so incredibly over salted, they should install a saltlick at every table and save some money. I've literally drank a half gallon of water today. I'd pass. PS-parking was ample.

I really liked the empanadas but unless you get them when they have a special they are too expensive. I didn't really care for the sandwiches or anything else. The staff is amazing though. Very friendly and the owner is great as well. I've referred them to people but I will not be making this a place I go to eat all the time.

I've enjoyed Pollo Tropical over the years, but lately it seems like the food has become less tasty & the service has become a struggle. In regard to the service, the past 3 times I've been there, including today, the order that came to the table was incorrect. I looked at my receipt & it was correct there, so the servers or cooks are perhaps assembling too fast & overlooking details of the order. They kindly fixed the order though when I said something. Also, today I tried a Tropichop Bowl. It came with chicken. The seasoning that used to be on the chicken is what always drew me back for return visits. The last 2 times I could barely discern much seasoning. The added toppings they offer include sautéed onions. The onions I received were a little nasty. They were stringy & oily & not cooked all the way. I'm thinking they threw some onions into oil on the griddle & the griddle wasn't heated up yet. So instead of the onions cooking, they merely sat in the oil & absorbed it. There were however some highlights to the meal. The sweet plantains were spot on delicious & the sauce bar is always tasty.

Searched for a yummy Puerto Rican restaurant to celebrate my birthday and stumbled upon this delicious find! I was thoroughly impressed with the food. This menu is the bomb! I had the Tazon with some delicious maduros (fried sweet plantains). So good! And there was so much food, this was dinner for another day too. I would definitely recommend. The only reason this is 4 instead of 5 stars is because I think the wait staff could have attended to us more often to check on us and refill water while we were waiting. Otherwise, very good!

Best Thai food in NOLA - hands down. I've eaten at just about every Thai restaurant in the city up to now and have been woefully unimpressed. Again, I realize that with ethnic food there are 2 challenges: (1) american tastebuds and (2) regional differences in how the food is prepared. That said my assessment isn't an indictment on how good the other places are (except that place on Magazine street which is waaaaay too expensive considering the quality of the food; you're really just paying for the swank ambiance). Rather, I just think this place is a cut above the rest. When eating here, for me, everything just tasted right. I strayed from getting the usual Pad Thai. My general reasoning is that if you can't get the national dish right why would I bother eating anything else??? However, on this occasion the deviation was well worth it. I had one of the specials and it was rolling!!! I felt like a kid returning home with my spoils on halloween. I can't remember what I had but it was delicious -- well seasoned. The Thai tea was excellent. The decor was calming and spacious -- no cramming to fit everyone in and maximize profit. Overall, just a good place. Also, I have no idea whether they include MSG in the food or not, but it just tasted like Thai food should taste.
Very good food and service. Clean. Fun atmosphere. Have not tried the sushi but love every Thai dish I have ordered.
I got the roasted chicken dish. Very tasty. It came with rice and beans, also very good. A huge portion as well. Good place.
I love the Thai food! Tasted really good . And the restaurant looks clean and comfortable! I like Thai tea too
Super nice employees and the food is great. The food tastes fresh and the bread was good. We had the Mac and Cheese, Tai pan and Korean BBQ and all were top notch!

My wife and I have traveled throughout the Middle East and enjoyed food along the way. This local Brandon restaurant's food is authentic as it gets. We ordered the mixed grill and mixed salad that my wife and I shared. Both were excellent choices and there was plenty food for both of us to share. The food was bursting with flavor! We talked to the couple that own the restaurant and found out the husband only wanted to use their current location to open a catering business. His wife convinced him to open the doors so they could operate a restaurant/takeaway business too. Lucky for us she did. The food was very delicious. I would have given a 5 star but the restaurant appears to be in the middle of renovation.

Second time coming here and it was just as delicious as the first time! I had the Black Pepper entree with chicken and it was perfect! Servers are kind and attentive. This is a great little spot if you enjoy Thai food and I really hope they are around for a while!

I was looking to try a new Thai restaurant and stumbled upon Jasmine Rice. Apparently they've been here for 5 years. Based on reviews I was expecting really good food. I ordered the massaman curry with chicken. First impression, too sweet. Second, first bite of chicken was tough as rubber. And for them to charge $16, I thought it was entirely too overpriced for the quality.

Easily one of my new favorite spots to go to!!! Chipotle used to be my go to, but not anymore... I can't stop recommending it. I try not to eat there every other day, but it happens. The steak rollups are perfect. The portion of sides are slightly small, but the meal as a whole is filling. The best part is that after every meal, you can fill out a 3 question survey on their mobile app & they'll send you a Rewards (Goodie) 2 days later. Customer service is top notch. Very clean & quiet
Attentive servers. Plenty of free parking and seating. Food and portions were average but prices were on the higher side for dinner at least.

My husband and I used to go alot and would always get a bowl of the lemon chicken soup. Our last visit was very disappointing because a bowl of soup is now the size of a cup. We questioned the manager and said the home office made the change. He told us to order take out and we would get more. So we did at our next visit but that was also a cup size. We won't go back. Don't lie to your customers.
In the burbs of Philly this is as good as you can get to a cross between Vietnam and France. Their tofu eggplant is the best in the area.

Pho is good. Ambiance is decent in relation to other pho places.. Located near an asian grocery store, so you can get your asian food fix in one stop. Bun Thit Nuong Cha Gio- add some fish sauce, mix up and enjoy.. really good. Ban Mi vietnamese sandwiches are good Cash only.
Chicken shwarma is delicious, but the potatoes can't be missed. Excellent small cafe with flavor filled Mediterranean treats.

Taziki West End ave. I work in the area and this is a great place to have healthy food (if you so choose). We (ppl I work with) get whatever daily special and it's be pleasurable each time. Beware of the chocolate cake. The only problem I have is PARKING.. UGH. I almost cancelled my order several time b/c of parking issues. Be on the look out for the small guy in the gray care that will boot your car if you park at Panera parking lot. He will help you in the door and boot your car. Just kidding but for real...Please put a sign up to remind people of this guy even for to-go orders. We spent $100 bucks on lunch $50 of it was to get the lunch time boot off the car. LOVE the food guys.

My husband and his work colleague often go here for lunch (often enough that the employees greet him by name, which is charming), and they have been raving about it, so I had to try it myself. Apparently, the restaurant gets fresh bread for bahn mi every Tuesday, so we went on a Tuesday. My husband and I shared a papaya salad, pork bahn mi, beef Pho, and I got a taro bubble tea. Everything was great. Everything was cheap. Now I'm obsessed with Saigon Restaurant. Note: When we were there, the building was in the process of being painted. It looked a little iffy from the outside before, so the paint was much needed. The outside should match how perfect the food was. Now it does.

The green curry here is amazing. I can't speak about any of the other food, since that is all I ever get, it is so good. I will say that everyone i have been here with has always enjoyed their food as well. Service is friendly, though it can be a little slow sometimes. One of the better Thai places around, I think.

I have been to Tandoor India countless times over the last 10 years. The food is not the fanciest, but it is plentiful, tasty, and, best of all, the price is right. We always get the buffet so we have a little of all the flavors. I have always found the foods to taste fresh and homecooked (although I did not grow up on Indian food, so it may differ from your grandmother's recipe). The decor has been the same for at least the decade that I have been going there. It looks like a hole-in-the-wall type place, but the owners are present and very friendly. To be fair, I have been to better, fancier Indian restaurants, so if you are looking for the high class, gourmet, impress-your-date experience, this may not be it. But if you are looking for satisfying, tasty food at a great price this is a great choice.
The happy hour was excellent. The house mojito was sub par. But they had good happy hour food. The outdoor seating area was beautiful and they had great live music.

I've been hear about 5 or 6 times. I've not really tried their food, but their mixed drinks are creative and spectacular. My favorite is the cucumber drink (forget what it is called). The atmosphere is chic-casual. Indoor and outdoor seating. Great location on beautiful Beach Drive.

A great addition to Brentwood! Godavari has a great selection of food for those familiar with Indian food and those who aren't! The dosas are great and are something you can't get at other places in town. We also had the chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and chicken biryani -- all were SO GOOD! The service was fast and friendly and the place was very clean. I heard they also have a great buffet for lunch. Can't wait to be back!

Decor: 4/5 Service: 3/5 Food: 1/5 I got the special and had them get me one of each fried chicken. Props for trying to be unique but I wasn't impressed with the texture or taste. The only thing that I liked was the locally brewed soda

The other day was the first time I've ate at this place. My husbands family are from India; and they are always cooking Indian style food around the holidays and special occasions. Anyway, the womAn at the counter wS very friendly and nice. She allowed us to taste test the food before we purchased. The restaurant was clean and welcoming. I gave it two stars bc the food was terrible. It was not authentic Indian food, they didn't have white rice, anything curry, no roti and their dal(pronounced doll) was disgusting. I was very disappointed and their prices were expensive!!!!! When thinking of authentic Indian food you would assume they would WHITE rice and curry. Their version of "white rice" was actually yellow rice that was over spiced and nasty.

Pretty good. Okay service. Great Venetian Aperol spritz - actually tastes just like the ones you get on the street in Venice. I ordered a creamed root vegetable soup, egg salad toast, and Israeli bruschetta toast. The bread is fantastic. The soup was good and beautifully presented. The bruschetta was tasty, but had made the bread really soggy, boo. I was not a fan of the egg salad, at all. I scraped it off and ate the delicious, crispy bread underneath. Id definitely come back. If/when I do, I'm going to give the brussel sprouts a go. The bagel with lebneh piques my interest too.

There is a lot of great food in the french quarter, even when you're sober, but I end up at this place multiple times on my Nola trips. Always on a mission to find the best middle eastern food on US soil, I first tried this place back in 2002 during my first trip to new orleans. I got a chicken shawarma and it's so good and perfect I've never wanted to try anything else. Of course I've gotten the baba and hummous and they are also stellar. Big portions too. The guy who currently works there is extremely friendly and appreciated greatly my attempts to converse in Arabic with him. I was staying in a hotel at the end of the French market last trip and I trecked it all the was to st peters street for a shawarma meal once a day. If like like good Arabic food GO HERE MULTIPLE TIMES DURING YOUR NEW ORLEANS STAY. Also, as a sidenote plus: they have an ATM that charges a lower fee than all the other ATMs on Bourbon, so get your cash while here.

Unfortunately, it's taken me nearly a full year to come to Meun Fan! The ambiance is nice, food is tasty and service is fast and courteous. I am a fan! Ambiance - the restaurant was decorated nicely with nice tables and dim lights. Great for romantic dinners. :) We ordered one chicken satay, red curry and a ginger pork, total was $34.00. all the dishes tasted good and fresh. Price was average and I think one of THE best Thai places in town. yum!

I've been here twice now for lunch. There seems to be a slow lunch crowd, sometimes I'm all by myself, but that has no relation to the food. I've had noodle soups both times. #22 and #30. Condiments were fresh and taste was awesome. I'll keep coming back as long as they keep serving it up.

I don't know why this place has these many good reviews . I have been to many states in US and this place serve the worst Indian food. We had the lunch buffet and everything was cold and not at all reached the standard of Indian food. The place has a weird smell .

I live in Bala Cynwyd, so this is one of my go-to-take out spots. The other day, though, I went for lunch with my daughter and was very surprised on a Saturday ay noon to see the place so empty. Actually, unless you are heading east on City Ave, and know the shortcut through the Muffler place parking lot, it is nearly IMPOSSIBLE to find the ample parking lot in back. Otherwise you really need to know your back roads. Anyway, about the food. My daughter is not really adventuresome. The menu is actually HUGE and spans classic Cantonese/Szechuan, Japanese (Sushi/Hibachi/Teriyaki/Bento etc.) and some classic Thai (like Pad Thai.) This is one of the few places who keep their $5.50 lunch specials (inlcudes a soda) running on a Saturday instead of jacking you $13 bucks for exactly the same food. A shared order of steamed dumplings (thicker skinned than I like, but my girl loves them that way) came with the traditional soy-based dipping sauce with a surprise touch of some fresh-chopped cilantro tossed in. Six for less than 5 bucks was a good deal for an app. This is the kind of stuff that differentiates Little Kitchen from your typical 'hood Chinese. Wonton soup was darker than average with a richer flavor then typical. Entrees (girl had sweet and sour chicken, I ordered Hot and Spicy Beef) came with heaps of fresh fried rice. Onions and other vegetable matter were very fresh. Hot Spicy beef had a very unique sweet sauce that left a nice after burn on the tongue. Service was polite and friendly, and food came out QUICK and too hot to eat immediately. I am wary of sushi in a place that is not hopping busy, but I suspect they must do a lot of takeout. In any event, you cannot go wrong for the lunch specials, but I will absolutely return to try some of their more ambitious fare (Japanese and Thai.)

So glad to have found this very fresh and inexpensive Greek/Lebanese place close to home. To start we had the Baba Ganush and it was perfect...not too bitter and very creamy. There were three of us and we had two kabobs (one beef and one shrimp) and they were seasoned perfectly...we also had one steak wrap. Next time I go back I am going with the Baba Ganush and the steak wrap.

Definitely a great spot to eat in Hatboro. There name is accurate for what they offer. We had the crispy lamb and crispy chicken for an appetizer and they were excellent. If you ever had Han Dynasty in Philadelphia, these two appetizers were were similar to that szechuan style. The chicken tiki masala was very good. Not oily like other Indian restaurants. Chicken and Shrimp biryani was very good, get the hot spicy if you love spicy food. Met the owner very nice person, staff was great.
Tasty food and great prices. The service was also very pleasant. It's not a large place, and it isn't fancy, but it is perfect for casual nights out.

Yesterday was our second time visit The Palace Of Indian , oh my god it was full of customers and we didn't reserved the table before any way They were able to give us seats, food was awesome as same my first visit . This place is so popular and busy so we can't expect like home service, restaurant was full and whatever they gave us service it was more than enough of our expectations, we visited so many restaurants and somewhere we have to wait outside fo long time for seating, so definitely we got the good service, and they have lot of delivery from Grubhub, Definitely come back again,

Every positive review was 100% true! Nice comfortable atmosphere. Walking In on a chilly day, the fireplace was very inviting. Immediately greeted with a very warm and friendly smile and hello. First time here so decided to try a few things. The chicken and sausage skewers were my fave of the items I ordered. Accented with a nice sauce and roared pirates, the dish was tummy. The lamb chops swing a good second. The grilled octopus was very delicious too. It is an aquifer taste, not for everyone. Warning- it is the entire octopus that is grilled. If you're not into that, don't order it. Portion size isn't much for the cost, this would be the only thing that keeps me from giving 5 stars. Every staff member was friendly. The restroom is clean, small Sink area, but clean. I will be back when I'm craving good Greek food.

This is the best Thai place near me. I fell in love with Thai food in Boston and was extremely disappointed by the quality of Thai food in PA, and then I found this place. (I have since found others, but this is the best one closest to me) Their Tom Yum is on par with what you'd find in Thailand. Flavors are authentic and we've always had wonderful service.
Really Good Food and Service! Sea food , drinks And more!!! Love the place infront the water like a real Floridian life!

This is a great place if you want a quick taste of asian (Thai) quisine. I always order their Spring Rolls with my dad. Cheap by very tasty; only $2.50 per order. They also have a delicious plate of fried rice although I have to admit I am a little biased towards fried rice haha. I definitely loved their desserts, especially their coconut ice-cream. It is actually served inside a tiny coconut. It's delicious. The place is very friendly since it is mainly run by people from Thailand. The atmosphere is very calm as well so it's just a nice place to grab a bite of your favourite Thai food. :) What I did not like was the prices. Yes, the Spring rolls are $2.50 and it is genuine Thai food but 7 bucks for a noodle soup? Definitely recommend it for the taste alone though.

We visited Saigon today for lunch. I've been wanting to try it for some time now and am glad I did. We started with the appetizer platter. It include crab rangoon, spring rolls, firecracker shrimp and two other tasty treats that I don't remember. All the apps were really good. Especially the shrimp. Next we both had the Pho. I had the special beef pho which included tripe, fatty brisket, meatballs & thin pieces of beef. It was good but I felt like the both could of had more flavor. My bf had the shrimp & pork pho & said it was really delicious. We wanted to try the pork bahn mi but they were out of sandwiches today. Oh well, next time. We'll definitely be back as there are tons of items on the menu that I want to try.

i'm so glad my man found this gem of a restaurant for us to check out last week! i'm a twerp though and can't remember what i had to eat (it's not shown on the online menu) but whatever, go there and be dazzled. i'm sure you can find SOMETHING - the menu is flippin huge. also huge is the owner's personality which was charming, sweet and attentive as all get out. i hope that despite people's comments on the location that folks will go. there are FAR WORSE neighborhoods in our fair city, it was about as sketchy as anywhere if you ask me. plus, takeout is boring. sure it's small seating but we had no problem getting a table and i'm sure the wait there is never going to be as annoying as the one that you might be given at the cheesecake factory. i will go back again and again.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: Their sushi is better than their Thai food. Service was lacking with only 3 wait staff managing the entire restaurant. I ordered the Amazing Land Chicken, its also called Amazing Chicken, which is basically stir fried vegetables drenched in peanut sauce. Their peanut sauce was watered down and the stir fried veggies had no flavor. This is my second time there and I was disappointed before, I try to give places a second chance, but they don't get a third try. BottomLine: not recommended.

I have been a regular here for the past two years and love it! The staff is excellent and speedy! I like to switch up between different Pho dishes. Usually end up with Pho do bien (seafood and noodles) or with pho tai gau (steak, flank, and noodle). All the pho dishes come out piping hot and taste delicious. For the rice dishes, I choose something with com tam (broken rice) paired with various meats. I love how they serve a quite large portion for such little money. I usually end up taking some home and eating them the next day. In addition to my hot tea I always treat myself to sinh to b (avocado shake) or sometimes just stop in to get one to go. I highly recommend Pho 38 for Vietnamese food any day of the week.

I've been here twice, once with my husband for dinner and once alone for the lunch buffet. Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be back. First off, when my husband and I ordered dinner, I ordered the lamb curry. I was told "no no no" by the waiter and that "it was too spicy for me" and that I should order "butter chicken." I was honestly insulted. My husband is Indian and I've eaten at countless indian restaurants. When the lamb came out, it wasn't too spicy for me, so there's that. We were instructed to order the vegetable korma as well. The vegetables in there didn't seem fresh, as if they were frozen or something of that nature. I decided to give it another try for the buffet. I found that the buffet was overtly spicy. I was told that it was "Southern Indian cuisine" which is spicier. I've travelled allover the world and come from a city that has hundreds of Indian/Pakistani restaurants, I've NEVER eaten at a buffet with so many items that were beyond spicy. Unfortunately, we won't be back.

Love their pho. I've only ordered take-out and get the same thing (no. 9 with extra meat), but it is so awesome! I like how they put everything (even the plastic tub/lid) in a tied bag so it won't spill out in the car or the way home. And they are fast! Healthier then chinese take-out. It is a fun project to create your own version of pho. You get enough soup, meat, veg and basil to fill one of my big baking bowls. The things I would recommend is that they don't have the workers all up in the front of the restaurant near the door (never seen anyone sitting at these tables) making basil bundles. Well, that is why I wash them really well when I get home.
This is an amazingly good and reasonably priced bakery. Gooey butter cake is great here but the paradise cake is addicting.
If I'm ever in the mood for vietnamese. This is my go to spot! Delicious! I always get the egg rolls (of course) and depending on the weather either the pho or pork chop.

When a new Latin restaurant opens up I feel the obligation to come by and support the establishment and make sure it gets noticed on Yelp! Sadly my high aspirations for Mojito were short lived. We came in and sat in a beautiful table in the middle of a room lit up through sky lights and surrounded by palm trees. The decor is very inviting and despite the odd picture of two white guys smoking cigars behind us, we were very pleased. Our food took a little long to make, which I assumed was because I ordered the steak sandwich. When it arrived at the table, I immediately knew I was going to hate it. It was huge chunks of bland looking meat lined up in my plate. Every bite I grew more and more frustrated as they fell out of the bread and made a bigger mess. If it wasn't that the meat was so poorly seasoned, I think I would've dealt with it better. Thank god for the the delicious yuca fries and aioli it came with. My hubby's sandwich was much more appealing, he ordered a Cuban which came out with great flavor and zero hassle to eat. Our yelp check-ins gave us coupons for free dessert so I ordered the warm Cuban butter cake which made me forget all my issues with the chunks of meat. My hubby ordered the tres leches and it lacked wetness, and it came with chocolate all over the bottom which really ruined it for me because the two did not go together at all. The thing that actually bothered me the MOST is that they were playing soft rock as background music in a place full of palm trees and margaritas; I mean come on, at least get the ambiance right. I don't know if we will return, the prices are kind of high for Spanish food, a steak sandwich was $12 and an extra $2 for fries. Plus with our meal literally being 50/50 good and bad, and mediocre service from the waitress, this place is easy to walk past in comparison to others in the area.

Food is fresh and simple, but personally I would never wait to be seated. It's average good. It's a cute and convenient neighborhood spot, but the servers need an etiquette lesson. Lots of reaching over you and clumsy handling of plates, I was envisioning oil spilling all over us as they cleared the plates. They are not attentive at all, it's not deliberate, I just don't think they've been trained properly. For instance, they bring 3 napkins when there are 4 of you. They clear the plates and place your cutlery on the dirty table instead of asking if you'd like a clean set, they'll ask if you'd like dessert, but they don't offer you coffee. They do the minimum required in a clumsy fashion and it's rather disappointing. Owners/Managers - a little training goes a long way. This is basic restaurant protocol that enhances the dining experience and brings back business.

My wife and I love Thai style cooking and we generally do take-out at the Thai Cafe because the atmosphere is nothing special. However, the food is of very good quality and we have never been disappointed. The only inconsistency I have found is with the degree of "heat". I usually ask for "Thai hot" and it can vary depending on the cook.

Pretty decent Vietnamese food. I like that they have a huge condiment tray to adjust your liking if it is more sweet, savory and spicy. Their soups are good and the broth for pho has good flavor. I was a little disappointed with the Banh Mi that it didn't have enough pickled vegetables on it. Very skimpy and they do not put enough meat in their spring rolls. Good taste but they could amp up their Banh mi and spring rolls by adding more meat and veggies. The soups are always delicious and served with the proper herbs, lime and bean sprouts.

I was impressed by the food served here. I got a mango lassi, vegetable samosa, and tandoori chicken. For the price, you really get a lot of food, like two peoples worth! My friend also liked this place as well.
new to Indonesian so may not be best person to judge. Tested like Thai - ordered only one entree for lunch.

We go for lunch regularly. Food is always fresh and delicious. They usually have an interesting special that someone in my party will order. Their menu is varied and their food is consistent. It's a hometown gem!
Great quality. Love this spot. Pita sandwiches w/ chicken gyro are great. Portions a little small but overall great. Been here twice in the past month.
Great experience, service was good, and food was flavorful and had plenty to go home. We ordered medium spice and they brought extra spices for us to add, perfect.
Nice food. Serve in decent amount. Waiters are helpful. Love their durian shake and papaya salad.

Ran across the place online and decided to give it a try. I was introduced to Doner Kebobs while living in Germany and had a taste for some. Showed up about 7:30 and was greeted by the two ladies working. They were very friendly and gave me a run down of what they had to offer. I ordered the mix of chicken and lamb beef. Everything was delicious and exceeded my expectations. I'll definitely go back again.

We went here a while ago on a whim. We were starving, so we ordered a bunch of different goodies. We started with barbecued pork steamed buns and they were so good that I wished I had just gotten like five orders of those. But then the pho came out. I got chicken pho, my boyfriend got beef. It came out with the typical fixings, plus a homemade chili paste/oil. The broth was delicious and rich and the chili made it really special. You get a huge serving of meat, as well, so even with the smaller sized pho, you will leave full. The ingredients, as with the steamed buns, were fresh and high quality. The service was a little slow which I actually like because I don't like my dining experience to be rushed. But something to keep in mind for those that prefer a faster experience.

First time here- the decor and ambiance was very clean, nice, modern, and sleek (even the bathrooms were very clean)! Had a great impression of this place since I noticed a lot of young Indian people were also dining there. We had the mango lassi drink (a yogurt based mango sweet drink), garlic naan bread (cooked perfectly) & cheese appetizer. We didn't realize it would come out on a sizzling pan and it made the dish taste surprisingly different but delicious. It was perfectly seasoned with spices. We also ordered the tandoori shrimp (medium), the curry chicken (medium), and okra veggie (medium) and they were all too die for! My husband thought the medium was a bit to spicy for him but it was just right for me (I usually eat mild spicy types of foods). The wait staff was pleasant and we enjoyed our meal very much and totally recommend this to anyone! We had totally forgotten to take photos of our meal but next time when we return, I'll post some pix's then.
I really enjoyed this place! The spicy noodles were incredible and the tofu was cooked well. I would highly recommend this place and I'd say it's the best Thai place in the region thus far.

Delicious food and great prices! When you walk in the market, you'll feel like you're in another country. Lots of authentic ingredients for purchase in the market. The restaurant is adjacent to the market. We tried the lamb kebab. The food had great proportions and we still couldn't get enough! It is a must stop location!
Bar none the best Pho in Reno. Don't let the gas station location fool you this place is the real deal.

We have been going there for 15 years. The sushi chefs are still the same, as is some of the staff. Very friendly and humble people. The food is consistently good, and reasonably priced. Highly recommended.

It was bad. Somehow they managed to serve tom yum soup that wasn't good, a salad that was mediocre, and pad thai ($20 for shrimp pad thai WTF!) that was bad. It seemed like it was noodles tossed in a tamarind sauce and had shrimp added. I mean, how do you mess up pad thai in a Thai restaurant? My wife's curry dish was good. The atmosphere was very nice. But the food overall was expensive and bad.

An explosion of flavors cooked into the chicken fried rice, with the perfect amount of spicy kick. You can tell everything is fresh and made to order and that the crew knows how to cook Thai food the right way. Definitely worth a stop to try!

This place is amazing! I went last night with my family around 7PM and the place was already swarming with people. We were a party of 7 and they seated us promptly and got our drinks in right away. Because they were so busy, we got our drinks, but had to wait a bit before putting in our order. We ordered the crab rangoon, sticky wings, chicken and green waffles, kimchi burger on French bread with sweet potato fries, lemongrass chicken on steamed bun, bun rieu, and bun bo hue (spicy beef noodle soup). Everything was soooo amazing! I don't have much to say about the crab Rangoon, because I can't stand cream cheese. It did have a strong bacon flavor which made it bearable and the sauce was very good. Everyone at my table loved it. The sticky wings came out nice and hot and the flavor was phenomenal. All of the entrees were delicious. Especially the chicken and green waffles. Definitely something different. The bun rieu and bun bo hue tasted homemade, like my mom was cooking in the back! If it's on their menu when you come in (they're specials), you have GOT to try it! The specialty drinks do need a little work. I had a perfect strawberry mojito and the second one I ordered was 10x stronger, which is not a bad thing, but not consistent. On to decor. This place is decorated very beautifully. Very modern, which fits its name! I will be coming back for more!

I finally branched out and tried another Vietnamese restaurant in the Tampa Bay Area. The restaurant was clean and the staff was very friendly. We started with the fresh rolls and those were very good. I ordered the large bowl of beef pho, which wasn't too bad. The broth was ok too, still not as tasty as my favorite, Saigon Deli, just down the road. I was disappointed with the portion of beef and noodles in pho. Usually, I end up taking home leftovers from most Vietnamese restaurants but there seemed to be more broth than anything in this pho. My friend's Bún looked good, but once again, the portions of pork and eggrolls were very small. I would probably go back and maybe try other dishes but I prefer bigger portions from the other Vietnamese restaurants.

First time trying Indian food, and I can't complain! The buttered chicken and cheese naan were delicious. I had the mild, as I don't do really spicy food, and it was enough for flavor. I'm looking forward to going back!

Best thai food in st louis, hands down, especially when i'm needing my pad see-ew or pad thai fix. I have a fondness for the owners as well - friendly and accommodating. The downside: portions are small for what you pay (compared to places like King&I), and there have been times when ive ordered take-out that they forget to include utensils! which is more of an inconvenience than a real problem.

This place was delicious and extremely authentic Thai Cuisine! The service was great and the staff there are so helpful! I always ask what the waitress recommends because they know what is good, and what is GREAT! She did not disappoint! I am VEGAN and it is so comforting when the waitress knows what is and what is not vegan on the menu! She also gave us great recommendations of what to order and was honest about what are the best choices! We did not get the curry this time, but they are all Vegan too! Must haves: - Tom Yum Soup - Vegan, Spicy and Delicious! be sure to add the veggies! - Pad Med Mamuang Hamapran Dinner- Vegan, delicious, not to spicy, and very flavorful! - Duck Panang - Not Vegan, and big enough to share - Sweet Rice Mango - Vegan, sweet, light and fresh! Yummyy Be sure to ask for the spicy sauce tray to add some heat to your dishes! I can't wait to go back to this place!

what a wonderful surprise. Really good food, the two of us ordered several dishes, veggie and seafood and loved each one. Everything was so well seasoned and the service was very good. Looking forward to a return visit.

I was really impressed by the delivery service. My food came promptly, far before Grub Hub estimated, and they threw in some free egg rolls. The sushi was very good- better than many sit-down restaurants I've been to. I'll definitely be trying Little Kitchen again.

Nice place, byob and cash only. I took advantage of being in the area for the Baltimore Dollar Stroll to finally have a sit down dinner here. I'm not well versed in Laos cuisine so I tried to pick anything that didn't seem obviously Thai or explicitly said Laos. That turned out to be homemade Laos sausage which came with a spicy pepper sauce and sweet chili. It was delicious! There was also a side of veggies and sticky rice that was served in a cute wooden container. I also tried the chicken skewers and the yellow curry with grilled salmon. For those, they were just meh and would recommend picking something else.
Food is too plain. I wouldn't recommend the place of you want authentic Thai. My husband had the Chu Chee duck which he liked but too dry.. however pad Thai was so bland no favor at all

Always gotta get the Korean fried chicken when coming here. The texture and juiciness of it makes it special compared to other places. The taste is nice and delicious as well. I always get the fried rice and some entree. If you like raw fish I suggest the hoedeopbap it's once of my favorite dishes there. But sometimes I get the bimbimbap with the hot bowl. Gotta love the crunchy rice at the bottom.

Olio is my favorite restaurant in St Louis right now. I have been here on numerous occasions and it has yet to disappoint me. All of the dishes are made with tasteful, fresh ingredients. All of the flavors are amazing! What I ordered: we started off with the king of kings hummus. I cannot go here without getting this hummus. It is amazing!!!! I'll go out on a limb and say it's the best hummus I've ever had. For my meal, my boyfriend and I split the egg salad and the broccoli pita sandwich. The egg salad was so fresh and light-tasting. The broccoli pita was good (there is lemon that really balances out with the slight bitterness of the broccoli), but I remember it being better the last time I had it. I love this restaurant! One of the best things is how affordable it is! Our whole bill was only $28 (since we didn't get drinks). I would gladly pay $28 again and again for this amazing food! It's a steal!

Hmm...this is probably not the place for you if you are new to Indian as we were. Their "mild" killed out mouths and had us all practically crying. The flavor was good, however it was just very spicy. They are very cheap though. We fed 5 people for less than $30 with tip including drinks. It's nothing fancy, just a little hole in the wall, but if you got a thing for not feeling your tongue and are trying to save money, I would totally recommend this place. The owner was super nice and had a good giggle at our lack of being able to handle spice.

Fantastic dinning experience ALL DAY LONG!!! We have enjoyed lunch, cocktail at this beautiful restaurants with amazing ,unique ,tasty selections of Lebanese middle eastern cuisine, served by incredibly professional wait staff in a Beautiful setting!! Stopped in for a quick light dinner ~ Place was rockin on a Thursday evening ~ We enjoyed amazing grilled mushrooms, with pine nuts, as well as huge Pillowy pita. The meatballs, of some type ,were fragrant + light ~ wish we ordered another order! You will not be disappointed! Food is priced right for the exotic ingredience, attention to detail of the service + the interior design. Outdoor dinning option looked beautiful. We found parking spots on the street as well!! Our fav in Philly!!

We already knew we loved Delicia, but who knew they had such a cool little sister? Excellent tacos, the BEST guac, brunch on Saturday, and a stellar Bloody Mary or margarita. I couldn't love this place more. Our favorite bartender is Will, who puts up with my chatty ways and is always on top of things!

I was appalled by the lack of customer service and rudeness from the staff. I had eaten at Asian Pho before and, at the time, thought they had decent food but were lacking in customer service. You could hear the staff arguing with each other. Today, my BF and I decided to make a visit and thinking that because their sign glowed "open" we were about to enjoy a nice meal. We walked in and no one greeted us or directed us to a table. Instead, we were approached by one of the staff who rudely told us that they were closing at 7:30 and we had arrived at 7:00. Another member of the staff approached us and asked if we would like take out. I think she was trying to smooth the situation over but my BF and I decided to leave instead along with our money. I completely understand when it's so close to closing but rudeness is unacceptable when you are in the business of hospitality.

Very authentic taste. The meat was seasoned perfectly. I've had the lamb kebab platter, the dolmas and the gyro, all were fantastic. I've had a lot of Mediterranean food in my life, these bad reviews tell me that people around here have not ever had good authentic cuisine and it's not over seasoned or salty. I'm excited to try their breakfast!
Fez feast is the best. Go for the lamb and the lemon chicken. Great hookah, fun atmosphere and good times.
Went first time had a good meal. Liked pineapple fried rice and pork with garlic would definitely come again

Newly opened restaurant in my neighborhood! Food freshly prepared. I ordered 3 gyros fries and onion rings. My only complaint is that my gyro was messy to eat. Wished the package was wrapped tightly so the inside ingredients would not have fallen apart when I opened the foil. I will try something different next time. Nice Family run business.

I thought this place was okaaaaay... I've had a lot of good pho in my life, and I wouldn't put this in that category. On the other hand, it's apparently better than most other pho places around here, soo if you're *really* craving pho this is the place to go. They have great TVs if you like to watch TV while you eat. There was something off about the flavor of the broth, but I couldn't put my finger on it... but like I said, still better than other places around.
Great place. I have been here three or four times over the last five years and have never been disappointed. Service is wonderful and they don't rush you out.
I love this adorable little gem!!! Admittedly the store front could use a little updating, but the food and service more than make up for it!!!!
A bit dark in the restaurant but the food makes up for it!! Highly recommend & come hungry bc you get tons of food!!

Hello delicious! Kien Giang has two limitations that had not allowed me to visit in the past: - Cash only - Closed on Mondays But alas... I had a $10 bill in my pocket and it was a Wednesday so I planned accordingly and picked out my to-go order. I had the spring rolls and chicken pho. I was a bit puzzled when I looked in the bag because the broth did not have anything in it. But I was relieved to discover they had FILLED a take out box with meat, noodles, and additions. Whew! I was worried for a second! The spring rolls were hands down the best I've ever had. Their peanut sauce was simply unreal and the soup was filled with flavor. Outstanding. I didn't even add any hot sauce to my dish since it was so good! I'm anxiously awaiting my next non-Monday, non-card visit!
Awful experience. Ordered happy hour appetizers, which came out cold, bland and appeared manufactured.

The food is great, except the fish. Don't order the fish. But the classic curries are fabulous, and if you order meat you get vegetables with it. Incredibly good value and flavors are spot on. Ambiance is a little lacking- but it's a bar with a restaurant side so for what it is it's great. We also bring our toddler, there are booths. I recommend to try this one- it's the best one for Ethiopian food in the area if you aren't worried about having a huge menu or the fancy ambiance.

Smiley's has been great to have in Manayunk. Delivery around here tends to be mostly fried foods and pizza so it's nice to have an option that is fresh and healthy. Nothing here has disappointed us yet and today I discovered 2 new favorites. The falafel here is awesome and the iced coffee is BY FAR the best I've ever had! Also the delivery through Grubhub took 30 minutes-- unheard of around here! Definitely try this place out, you won't regret it!
This place is great. Michelle is the best hostess. What I really love is all the food combos. It's amazing!

I would've had a picture of my food i ordered but it was so good that it was too late.. Yes it was that good, I specially requested a duck fried rice which was not even in the menu but they happily made it for me, that's a + in my book. I came from california north cali, i would say that i'm a good judge when it comes to real authentic thai cuisine and i would like to say it's the best in nashville. Give it a try and you might feel the same way, i will be going back to siam since going somewhere else is cutting urself short. Love the service.
Best Banh Mi in Philly, hands down.

I love this place! Not only does it have great food but it is also conviently located near target, another one of my loves. The staff here is great and they carry a wide array of Thai noddle and curry dishes as well as appetizers and desserts. I have had the pad thai and the yellow curry, both of which were great! I also highly recommend the crab ran-goons as appetizers!

I don't understand why this place gets such great reviews. If I were to review the smell alone as you walk by I would have to give it five stars. After moving to Philly and walking by it on several occasions I really looked forward to eating there. Unfortunately that is where the good things i have to say about it end. I ordered a jerk chicken plate and a fanta which I figured had to be safe. It came to just under $20!!! for chicken. On top of that it was awful. So over-cooked and dry it was almost inedible.

Delicious and cheap. I have yet to try a sandwich I did not love. (Yes, I love you #1, and you too #3). The bread is great and everything between the bread is great. I enjoy trying the drinks from the cooler but I like the coffee best. As far as I know this is the only place in Boise to get beignets, and if I that is true, then they are definitely the best in town.

Great Thai BYO! The owner is very friendly and accommodating. Make sure you have a reservation, since the place is quite small. Portion sizes are a little small, so consider getting an appetizer to go with your entree.
Very yummy!!! It was my first time eating thai food so I stuck with what I knew, fried rice. I had the beef fried rice and it was so good. My hubby had duck and it too was great. Overall great

I have heard great reviews from my friends. I finally tried it. First impression: Signage was bland on the side of the restaurant but attractive on the front. Inside was nicely decorated and clean. As for the food, I ordered a $10 duck glass noodle soup (I questioned where are the mushrooms). The duck was not roasted but alright. It was a huge bowl of soup. Unfortunately, I was expected to be overstuffed instead of understuffed. I needed more food. My friend said that she would share an egg roll appetizer; there were 3 small, crispy vegetable rolls (I would say spring rolls) and fish oil for dipping at the cost of $3.95. They were good but seemed overpriced. I was still hungry. No fortune cookie to end my meal -- maybe that is just at Chinese restaurants.

Lemme start this off by saying I'm Black with a southern mama. Went in here with my mom one day. The staff was nice and helpful, but the menu was limited and disappointing. The macaroni and cheese is not mac n cheese. More like some kind of macaroni casserole. Not bad, but not mac n cheese. The chicken was flavorless. I hated it. I threw it out. Breaded with bread crumbs I think? Hated it.

I was so excited to get some Indian buffet, only to realize that they don't serve buffet at dinnertime during the week. Lame! Oh well. They serve some chutney with that crunchy delicious flat bread (papadum?) as appetizers. I got the chicken tikka masala which was good and came with rice. Also tried saag with mushrooms, but wouldn't go for that again. Will have to come back for lunch buffet sometime though!

Quite a good Indian restaurant. They do have good biryanis, a dish that every Indian restaurant serves but only a few have mastered the recipe. Atleast no one in Silicon Valley. I am a stickler for authentic biryanis, and this place gets a 5/5 from me just based on that. I tried the Persis Goat Biryani, the tandoori shrimp and they were good, real good !!

order anything on the specials menu: notably hangover special, mrs bui, veggie special get all sandwiches with bui sauce. bui sauce is free. prices have gotten more expensive over the years. sandwiches went from $5-$6.50 and the sandwiches have been the same, maybe slightly less food

The food was ok in my opinion I ordered pad thai with tofu the tufo was over cooked. The reason I rated it so low was it's costumer service. I waited a while for my menu, after I got my food no one came over to ask if I needed anything I had to keep calling them back even to get a water refill. Poor service low rating!
Excellent food and nice atmosphere Services is awesome , we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala , veggie samosa and Garlic & cheese Naan , it was delicious and flavorful Definitely we will be back

I was really pleased at The concept of a fast food Indian restaurant, so I was disposed to be positive when I went here. Reality bites. For positives, the server at the counter was friendly and efficient, the decor was nice, and the place was very clean. I ordered the platter, which is one rice and two (out of four choices) curries. There were two vegetarian and two chicken curries available. I had both chicken ones, and they were not very different in flavor, and a little skimpy on meat. They were also only lukewarm. On the good side, they were nicely spicy. The rice was fine, but the flatbread (I expected naan) was awful, funny tasting, tough, and elastic as a rubber band. There may be better choices on the steam table on other days, but I doubt I will be back.

Delicious! I ordered the chicken, beef, and lamb kabobs. Everything was spiced perfectly, my husband wanted to order more! The meat portions are a bit small, but you can always order an extra a la carte skewer after you've ordered a meal for half the price. The lentil soup has some pasta in it, I had never tries that before and it was amazing. Going back! Don't let the stairs deter you if you have a stroller, one of the workers came up and helped me down and then back up after I was done. Really nice people! Going back soon.

Awesome breakfast sandwich! My sandwich: I get egg, cheese, and turkey bacon (or sausage). This comes on a toasted Amoroso roll. I always order Bui's special sauce, which adds a delicious siracha-based kick (i.e. this is a MUST to add). I also say yes to salt, pepper, and ketchup. A nice perk: Although I rarely do this, but you can also get all egg white if you want to make it healthier. Bui's serves hungry college students at Penn. This popular food cart is known as the place to go when you're hung-over, and it really hits the spot when you want a hangover cure. But it also makes a cheap, yummy, and filling breakfast when you're completely sober and are on a tight budget. When I lived near campus, I would come here several times a month for breakfast. Not the healthiest breakfast on the planet, but absolutely delicious.... This is the best egg sandwich I've had in Philly!

Food was very fresh, very good. I could have eaten the gyro meat all day. Rice, sauce, meat, salad. All some of the best I've had. I wish portions were bigger, but that may just have been me wishing for more of the tastiness. Highly recommended.

Wow, this place is delicious! My mom and I are visiting from D.C. And we saw this small and unassuming place. My mom got the chicken gizzards (fried) and I ordered the "Zeafood" (fish, calamari, and shrimp with sides). The gizzards were a little tough but tasted fresh and flavorful. All of the seafood was perfectly cooked and seasoned (no small feat). The service was warm and welcoming. Fast and efficient. The manager was gregarious, engaging, charismatic, and knew his food well. We will definitely be coming back here when we visit Tampa again!
My favorite in Santa Barbara. Great flavor and when you ask for spicy they don't hold back! Great menu and friendly far service.

Has anyone ever noticed the owner (large man) treat his staff very rudely? I have never seen anything like it and especially in front of customers (YELLING from the kitchen and in the dining area, pointing, ordering them around, degrading them). Our bill also had 18% gratuity already added for 5 people. I hope this tip goes towards the staff in the kitchen who are doing a fine job of cooking meals and cleaning our tables - they deserve all the credit (notice the only work the owner will do is bring out your entree so you can praise him). I'll sadly never forget this experience.

I loooove Northern Chinese food. It's the only time you'll see me recommending a Chinese restaurant, at least when it comes to Edmonton's options. Okay fine, Shanghai 456 would make the cut but technically, that's Shanghainese food. Either way, Wheat Garden Noodle & Dumpling Bazaar quietly opened up last month, taking over the old red house from Old Szechuan, which moved it's digs to Whyte Ave. Anyways, I was stoked to hear about a second Northern Chinese restaurant opening in town! Finally, an alternative to driving all the way to Noodle Feast. The interior received a much needed face lift. The walls are freshly painted white and gives the place a much friendlier vibe. Don't expect too much though, there's still plastic mats covering the tables. Typical Chinese décor. There's also a small TV set up playing random Chinese shows that you can only chuckle at. Who cares though. Most importantly, would it live up to the glory of Noodle Feast? The menu consists of noodles, dumplings and snacks. What I like is that for the noodle section, there's four different styles for you to choose from. Just tell them what type you want when you order them. Don't forget. Go with the wide, flat ones, those are my fav (the third one). Service is very friendly. The couple (I believe) working are a bit shy but they are quite attentive. Nice that their hours changed since my original visit - they're open for lunch now. Trip #1 - Beef noodle soup ((#101) ($11.99) - beef with green onion, leak and daikon. The broth is simple and to me, it tastes herbal/medicinal/healthy. You won't be blown away but if you're looking for a bit more kick, add some of their chili oil to your bowl. - Wide noodles (#109) ($11.99) - wide noodles mixed with Northwest Chinese style spicy chicken, potato, green pepper and onions. This is one of their specialty dishes and have to say this was my favourite dish of the night. Nice bit of heat to the dish, super flavourful and the noodles had a great bite/toothsomeness to them. -Lamb rice pilaf (#303) ($12.99) - with lamb, carrot and onion. Think biryani but replace with Northern Chinese style spices. Again, another of their specialties and it delivered. Lamb was nicely spiced and flavours were just umami. - Dumplings all in one ($13.99) - you can either pick one type of dumpling (six types to choose from) or if you want an assortment, you can go with the all in one option. We choose the latter and you get a colorful platter of dumplings, 15 to be exact. The dumplings were pretty good - moist, tender, and juicy. My friends liked it so much we ordered another round. Trip #2 - I had to come back a second time to try a couple more of their dishes before making a verdict. Bbop and I checked them out Friday for lunch. - Cold steamed noodles (#301) ($5.99) - comes with cucumber, bean sprouts and gluten. I wanted to try this on my first visit but they don't enjoy cold dishes. Their loss, this dish was doooooooope. So many great things coming from this little dish - the noodles are perfect with a great bite and texture to them that's different than their other hand-made noodles. Tantalizing, prepare for a bit of numbness to reach your lips. The cucumbers and bean sprouts help to cool things off a bit. - Ground beef noodles (#110) ($10.99) - comes with bok choy, peas and chicken broth. This noodle soup was BOMB. Our favourite dish for sure. The broth was heavenly - almost peanut like but quite light and again, the slightest level of numbness. I was pleasantly surprised as I wasn't expecting this to even have a soup base. What I've learned so far - order their noodle soups with the "hot" icons beside it. - Lamb noodle soup (#102) ($12.99) - with black fungus, kelp, dried lily and goji berries. I thought this one might be different than the beef noodle soup we originally tried but the broth was identical. Bbop wasn't a fan but at least it gave us a contrasting flavour. For what it's worth, he kept on going back to the other bowl. I really like the black fungus and kelp in the dish. Fungus is just texturally pleasant. Kelp was new to me - it's a seaweed, which reminded me a bit of Hawaii and their numerous algae/seaweeds that they throw into their cuisine. - Jelly noodle (#302) ($5.99) - stir fried jelly noodle with bean sprouts and vegetables. Thought they might have forgot about this one but they brought out it out piping hot. Poor Bbop, what a rookie, didn't wait and burnt his tongue. I'm not kidding when I say it came out hot.This was my first time having this type of jelly cubes - it was more like a starch jelly. If you've had lo bac go (turnip cake) before, it has that same mushy consistency. Surprisingly good with the chili flakes but a half size would have been more than enough to share. Oh well, nothing wrong with leftovers. Wheat Garden has "hidden gem" written all over it. Hope the word gets out soon and that more specialized Chinese cuisine gems starts to pop up in the future!

Delicious. We were going to Delicia, but found this right next door and it was already opened - we had to wait for Delicia. We also weren't dressed very nice and didn't want to spend too much, so it was a better choice between the two, though we still want to go to Delicia for the Ribeye. Had the Tlayuda de Chorizo and pork carnitas tacos and they were delicious. Bought the salsa fresca appetizer - wish a basket was free with the meal. And had the margharitas, which were good, but smaller than Delicia - a tad cheeper. But i wanted it to be a little bigger. Overall delicious and we'd go back. Very friendly! If I went back, I would go for lunch instead - the menu has more options that I wanted to try.

I often stop in here while waiting for Sprint (right next door) They have a nice little outside area and the food has always been very good. Their cocktails are fairly good as well, but a little on the high side. I have had the pad ke mow (probably spelling that wrong!) - It rocks! The Tom Yum soup is just the right blend of spicy and limey The apps were good I tried one of their salads but do not remember what it was, however, it was *very* good. About a 25 min. drive for me but well worth it!

Had family visiting from Maine and after the long winter they have had, they deserved dinner on the water and the beautiful sunset. We got there and had an hour wait. They took our cell number to text us when our table was ready. While we waited we got ourselves refreshing and pretty cocktails and sat on the deck and savored the beauty of the water. It was actually very entertaining watching the boats and all coming back in. When we received our text we got a great table with a nice view of the sunset. We ordered steamers and calamari for apps. The men ordered the fish tacos, my sister a salad and I got the crab ball sliders...yes imagine the jokes from the men! My meal was good, but I did end of eating some of hubby's tacos and they were DELISH. Will definitely order them next time! Finally we got phenomenal service our waitress was attentive and worked very well with the personalities and humor at our table. Definitely will return for more sunsets!
Great service! I had the falafel pita and they threw in a small container of babaganoush to try as they were low. I will definitely return.

Visit here several times yearly and pick up occasional take-out. We love the food and the ambiance. It's very relaxed and informal but not noisy. Service is excellent and prices are reasonable. Highly recommend, especially the seafood.

I'm from PR and this is by far my favorite place in Tampa. The food has never disappointed, exactly like what I would find back home. I recommend the mofongo with crab meat or the asopao. It's small and quaint which ads to the charm. I've taken several coworkers here and they're addicted now.

I saw this place on Triple D so I always wanted to try it out. Despite the low reviews, I still have it a try. It's a small restaurant with cute decoration inside. The tables are kinda cheap looking but I didn't care much since I ordered to take out. The menu is a bit confusing and somewhat messy. I ordered the beef patty and Jerk chicken quarter platter that comes with rice & beans, cabbage, and plantains. The patty was recommended but it was dry and the dough was thick with little stuffing. So I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THE PATTY. On the other hand, the chicken was tender and well seasoned. It tasted great with the sides and the sauce. The sauce was a bit spicy but it worked so well with the chicken. I would love to come back for more chicken when I come back to Philly.

Wow might be the best broth of pho I've had. Great pieces of meat and the noodles are cooked well. If you're looking for a bowl of pho with a very rich flavor, this is one to check out. Friendly service too

My gentleman friend and I came on a Sunday evening, around 7:45pm. The restaurant was not crowded, and clean. We were greeted and immediately seated. I ordered the butter chicken (mild) and he ordered the chicken tikka masala (spicy) and two orders of the butter naan (because the first round was so good). We loved our dishes. Mine was the perfect amount of kick, and his was super spicy, but he loved it. We will definitely be back!

Let me start this review by saying that we did not go into the restaurant. Please be careful when making plans to come to this establishment. We planned to celebrate my milestone birthday here last Saturday (Jan. 13). I called in advance to se if we could make a reservation but was told that they do not take reservations. I then asked the person on the phone what the wait time would be if we came on a Saturday night. He told me that there would likely be no wait and if there was one it would only be about 10 minutes. Now, while I had never been to this place before, I've been to several other hookah places. I thought it was odd that there wouldn't be a wait so I asked him again, the man assured me that there would be a 10 minute wait tops. We get to the restaurant around 11:30pm and walk to the door and the bouncer tells us that there is a wait and he is not sure how long it would be before we could go in - imagine my surprise. Another woman walks up and is told the same thing. We started talking and found out that she frequently comes there and the wait is at least an hour. And to top it off they do not have anywhere you can wait inside the restaurant! The bouncer basically said we could hang around outside and he would remember our faces when a table opened up. Seriously?? It was a cold January evening, of course we didn't hang around outside hoping for a table. And they can't come up with a better system? I'm supposed stand around and hope the bouncer remembers my face? How about taking down a phone nunber and texting when a spot opens up. We went to Reef Caribbean lounge instead. I wouldn't have minded waiting had I known in advance and been able plan accordingly. But instead we were lied to by this establishment.

Catherine, her amazing chef and wait staff welcomed my group of 50 and handled it with ease and professionalism. The appetizers and main course were simply delicious! I couldn't have asked for a better experience! I recommend you call ahead for a reservation as they do get busy!

It could probably get 5 stars, but I have only been there one time (thank you Groupon). Big on roasted red peppers. I saw it in soup but didn't have any. They were in the Htipiti spread (w/feta) for the warm pita wedges, and in the Horiatike salad - Greek salad made with pieces of tomatoes, sliced cucumbers, onion, feta cheese, and olives, typically seasoned with salt and oregano, and dressed with olive oil, and green bell peppers; and roasted red peppers were also on the excellent lamb kabob. It was nice to get a big bowl of salad without any lettuce or fancy leafy greens. I'll go again and see if it gets 5 stars. Next time I will go later so I can see the belly dancers.

Came by with my friend, Fred, on a Saturday afternoon to check out these banh mi sandwiches. We stopped in at around 4 and there was no line. We each got 2 - the pork and the tofu - and were pretty pleased with how filling they were. There are a couple seats in this hole in the wall, but we decided to walk over to the park at 8th/Fitzwater and eat on a park bench.
Great Gyros!.. this restaurant is authentic Greek. I will come back to try other dishes. Staff was friendly and attentive

The Mezza dishes were great! We had the fattoush salad, hummus and grape leaves. Incredible!! The warm pita served with it was so fresh. The dinner however was very very small. For the price, I at least thought it would be a normal size portion. All in all it was a great experience and I would definitely go back.

I am here because of Johnathan review that they really put out a good Thai Hot restaurant. There is no hold back. So if you ask for spicy, watch out. There is no American Hot. The restaurant has good ratings. The interior is open seating hall that most efficiently for maximum seats. The owner pay attention to the customers. And the wait staff is alert enough. They have extensive menu for your choice. We got the Drunken Noodle and the Lad Na Noodle. The drunken noodle is a bit wet. I like it dryer. But they did a Thai Hot for me. The spicy of the chili extended to my throats. The spiciness stay at my mount at least good 7 minutes. The Lad Na noodle is crispy noodle with beef. Food is good. We also got the stuff chicken wing. This is a dish that not normally serve. This actually the best dish. Like the staffing with pork.

I love coming to Sam's whenever I'm in town visiting friends and family. Great beach bar vibe with an amazing view and friendly staff. Pros: 1) Friendly staff. The busboys were great, (Johnny from Brooklyn) very friendly and nice to have them constantly clearing tables as servers are taking orders and dishing out food. 2) Great seafood and $2 house beer! 3) Amazing view and outdoor atmosphere. 4) Saw a manager (with a polo labeling him as the manager) active on the floor with a smile on his face and working....always a plus. Cons: 1) Hostess wasn't around so we sat ourselves and then went to notify her that we did so. 2) Side salad needs improvement to compliment such great entrees. 3) Menu is a bit cluttered and busy. We wanted to order crab legs but didn't notice them on the menu so went with other choices. Suggest the servers announcing their best sellers with current market price, would have sold us right then.

My husband and I went here on a Monday night, only because the place we really wanted to try (L'Angolo) was closed. The atmosphere was okay, the wait staff average and the food nothing to write home about. If that is authentic Italian, then I don't know why anyone would like the food in general. My meal was very bland and I did not enjoy it very much; ended up taking it home for the dog. The next night we tried L'Angolo, and the experience was 1000x better, along with the food. Save yourself time and money, go a half block down to L'Angolo's!!!

My iPhone told me to eat here, so I did. I pretty much do whatever it says. Wife and I decided to try this place out, at the suggestion of Urban Spoon, and we were not disappointed. In fact, we were quite pleased. We cannot speak to the spicy curry dishes since we're not curry fans, so keep that in mind with this review also. They could be excellent or crappy for all I know. Immediately upon entering said Smiley establishment, we were greeted and invited to sit. It was close to 1pm, so it was practically empty. Needless to say, we got great attention. Looking around, I could tell it was clean and step above your typical strip-center Asian eatery. For starters we ordered Bangkok Spring Rolls, which were delicious with their dipping sauce that had just a nice little kick. The 2 spring rolls were a little expensive, at about $5, though. The crab rangoon (they called it something with "Delight"), on the other hand, was tops! Not all 'goon is created equal, you see. It may not have crab in it, but it was done up just right. Highly recommend. $5 appropriately spent. I washed the apps down with a Thai Iced Tea that was one of the tastiest treats I've ever had. I loved the milky orange color (think creamsicle), and that perfect mix of of a solid-tasting tea coupled with a milky sweetness that was spot-on. Didn't need any extra sugar, but wasn't sickly sweet like some I've tried. For main courses, we had Cashew Chicken and Phad Thai with chicken. Neither blew us away, but they were still good dishes. They were cooked perfectly with fresh-tasting ingredients. The Cashew dish had lots of great, crisp veggies, tender mushrooms, and a fairly thin (and just slightly spicy - for a 1 star) sauce. Portions were reasonable, and I'm looking forward to the leftovers! I'm being picky about handing out more stars than this because the meal was a shade more expensive than it probably should have been, and because I hoped for more from the main dishes. However, take this to be a hearty recommendation to try this place. Lots of great choices, and overall a darn good experience.

Wow! Wow. Still, wow! This place is really impressive. You don't feel like you're in St. Louis when you are in Olio. By this I mean that you could be in any major cosmopolitan city, anywhere. I feel like I'm in New York or San Francisco when I'm in this restaurant. Unlike many of the best local restaurants/empires in St. Louis, this place has a totally unique feel. It is a converted gas station or garage that carries so much charm in its original brick and mortar. We sat at the bar, which I highly recommend. We ordered several drinks. I stuck to wine and vermouth (on the rocks). My boyfriend chose mostly beer and pastis. I fell in love with their stemware. They have a different (delicate) glass for every drink. The care and attention that went into the details are obvious and exceedingly successful. The menu looks amazing. We ordered the kale salad which was especially savory. The warm bread from the oven was an added bonus!

This place is awesome! (Definitely didn't even know it was there.) Went in with my girlfriend and my little sister on a rainy Saturday afternoon for some drinks. After flipping through their extensive drink menu we all decided what we would like, and decided to order some veggie spring rolls and a shaved ice in addition to a boba tea and some sort of sweet tea with fruit in it. It wasn't that busy when we ordered, but once we sat down it got swamped! The spring rolls and shaved ice were so yummy, and the boba tea my sister got was the best I have ever had, hands down. I don't usually like boba tea at all, especially the little bubbles, but this one was so good I made my girlfriend go back up and order me my own! The boba was perfectly sweetened and didn't just get mushy and gross. Loved it. The only two complaints I have is that this place has too many fluorescent lights. Since it was so dark, the lights were on, and I think the ambiance could be improved with some more mood lighting! Also, this place is pretty slow. Like, don't come in here on your lunch break because you might be waiting the entire time for your drink slow. Unfortunately. But other than that, so good! So, so good! Open another one up in downtown St. Pete and I think it'd be amazing!
I was checking my yelp yesterday and notice that a new thai restaurant opened up. I just had to give it a try, the food was good. The place is small and very clean and the owner is very friendly.

Here is a restaurant that deserves every bit of success that it receives. I am a frequent visitor to Florida and lucky-stumbled into Lisa's downtown location after having spent a month in Bocas, Panama in December 2009. WoW! mucho gusto! The food, the tropical colors, the friendly welcome-backs, the banter among regulars ;o wink, Tangelo's Grille has it all! Go There! Sip a cold one. Pay attention! You'll have a great time!
Does anyone have any idea where Chistos went? The felafel truck has been MIA for the last month +.

It must have been a good sign when all of the other tables were Indian in an Indian restaurant. I dined there last night for a quick meal with the wife after a long day at KOP. The staff was very attentive and accommodating. I just recently had Indian at another restaurant maybe 2 weeks ago and was very underwhelmed. The meal here was one of the better ones I've had in a while. Now, on to the food... I ordered a Mysore Masala Dosa (crepe with a layer of spicy sauce, potatoes, and onions), Paneer Butter Masala (pieces of homemade cheese cooked in a rich, creamy tomato sauce), and a Garlic Chili Naan (fresh garlic, green chilies, and coriander seasoned bread). The dosa was maybe a little thicker than a French crepe, but had a crisp, cracker-like exterior and was very large. Although the dosa hung way over the edge of the serving plate, it held its form throughout the meal without getting limp onto the table. It was folded into a triangle with a mound of spiced potatoes in the center and accompanied by a red sauce, a green sauce, and a soup. I emerald enjoyed this dish. The paneer dish was seasoned very well. I asked them to make it very spicy and they were hesitant at first, but complied. My spice tolerance is very high. It came out with a nice kick, but not anywhere near a ghost pepper or even a habanero level. The paneer was nice and firm and the sauce was thick and flavorful. Also comes with a bowl of white rice. The naan was freshly made as expected and had some heat due to the green chili. It was almost like a green Thai chili. This is the first time I've seen chili on a naan and think I will be having it this was from now on. The portions were generous and two hungry adults failed to finish the meal.
