We left with more than half the paneer and half the naan. I would come back.
Ordered takeout last night. Very good food for a much better price point than the other Mediterranean restaurants in Brandon. Well done!

HK BULGOGI!!!!! Wow, for years I only thought the thing to do at a Korean restaurant was the BBQ (sit at the table and grill your own stuff). I have been out to LA a few times and there was a fantastic Korean BBQ out there and I thought there was no way St. Louis would have anything as good. I literally work minutes from Hangook Kwan and decided to give it a try as I always wanted to taste Bulgogi, one of the most delicious dishes in the world! Typically we would do the cook it yourself version since it's way more fun than just ordering and eating. After ordering and trying the Bulgogi at HK I don't think I will ever do the BBQ thing again... Why? Because their Bulgogi is friggin great! If you are thinking of trying Korean for the first time then I: A. Highly suggest Bulgogi (its the safety net of Korean) B. Highly suggest Hangook Kwan My only complaint is that maybe this isn't the place to grill your own because they don't have the variety of meats/veggies or DIY dinners. At least nothing like the one I had in LA. Great place for lunch too! Affordable and delicious with great service, and no wait! No frills decor, looks like they might do Karaoke or something on the weekends. The staff is very friendly! One cool thing about this place is that they grow all their own veggies right out front which is unique, and they are also right next to an Asian market which is a great! You can get items like sesame oil at a lower price than you would a chain grocer.

Love the place sooooo much! I love Thai food and I think this place is the most authentic one I've ever been to. For appetizer, definitely try the Thai spring rolls here, they will be different with what you eat in other Chinese restaurants, the spring rolls here are crispy but also juicy. I'm also a fan of the Tom Yum, though many of my friends cannot bear the taste. Honestly saying, the main dishes are ALL really yummy! I will recommend Seafood Lover, which contains many sorts of seafood. The sauce for this dish is amazing, removing the stinky taste of seafood.

Le Gourmet is a great little cafe my husband and I visit on the weekends. It's true the menu has a Mediterranean flare and coinciding with that is their service which is more of a European style. We've had breakfast and lunch on a few separate occasions and have not been disappointed yet. The space is also great for events like bridal showers, baby showers, birthday dinners and more.
The service was great, I had two people who helped me and they both made me feel very welcome. The food was delicious!

I had Kimchi Ramen Soup, it was okay but I wasn't blown away by it. All in all, I think broth was spicy but lacked flavour, would have liked more veggie toppings and meat. I feel that I need to try the other Ramen soups to compare, I will return to try Miso and Tan Tan.
Incredible food. Excellent decor. Adorable store front. Very spacious. Have yet to try a cocktail but i look forward to going back.

Pork Banh mi was amazing! My husband said it was the best sandwich he'd ever had! The pickled carrots and light crusty bread made it over-the-top good. Chicken pho was very good (but I'd prefer dark meat) and beef pho was excellent. Huge servings of pho. Bang mi was smaller. Lots of fresh Thai basil and bean sprouts for garnish on the pho Good iced Vietnamese coffee. Nice and strong.

This is a nice change to the indian buffets you usually find for lunch. Here, you order from the menu. The lunch menu only has a few items, but it's delicious, quick, and you can get it spicy if you want. I'm going to try dinner here tonight.
Great for lunch! You walk up to the shack on the side of a liquor store and they take your order. Awesome authentic food!

We eat Vietnamese ALL the time in NYC so it was a pleasant surprise to run into this restaurant. We usually have tendons and tripe in our pho but this establishment does not have that. My husband and I ordered the Pho Combo. The bowl was pretty large and enough to keep you full without ordering sides or appetizers.

Have you heard of a Dooner? The owners are from Germany and the Dooner sales beat out MC Donald's and Burger King by double. Similar to a Gyro but on steroids. The bread is better, the stuffing is better and don't forget to ask for the home made hot sauce. If you never had one of these it's a most have at least once in your life. It's a great tasty treat!

Went on a Friday and were able to be seated right away. The atmosphere is great for either a happy hour or a date night. Our server was very attentive but not annoyingly so. The flat bread we got was a little bland but everything else was really good and well priced.

The restaurant gets 5 full stars for taste of food so if you are looking for somewhere that blows your taste buds away this is it. The only reason I dock them a star is because of this: The price is a little bit high for me, but I am in my early 30s and I truly appreciate great food for reasonable;e prices. I will say that the pricing is somewhat level with other similar establishments of this kind in this area. We really enjoyed the scallop appetizer but for $13 you would think there would be more than 3 of them on the plate (but they tasted fantastic). The goat cheese and walnut salad was plentiful (for two people) and it tasted very fresh. I had the lobster ravioli which was very good. If you want a good pasta dish this is it. the honest best part was the tomato-based sauce it was in. The sauce was so far away from a traditional red "tomatoey" commercialized sauce and was so much more tasteful, and buttery. My wife even used the homemade wheat garlic bread (very good) to mop it up off my plate! My wife had the dish called "Bob's plate" which was a about $30 and consisted of fettuccine covered with a red, light sauce and two of the following: shrimp, scallops, and salmon pieces. All in all, the food tasted great, as stated at the beginning, but I would have appriciated just a slightly lower cost for the meal...maybe I'm cheap! It is definitely worth trying if you have not been and you live within 10-12 miles. Note - It has evening hours during week and weekend that I can tell and it IS BYOB.

Good takeout service! I work nearby, and my order is always right and ready in 15 minutes. I really like their sandwiches, of all things! So good, the grilled pork sandwich is nicely marinated on a soft bun with fermented vegetables and sliced peppers for a little kick. (It's not too hot, unless they miss a seed!) It's a good sized sandwich, and only $4. The soft spring rolls don't look very appetizing, but are very tasty. They have a nicely priced lunch special menu, but the one time I ventured away from my standard I regretted my decision. I think the lunch special is about $6 and a huge portion. I've heard great things about their pho, but I never want to try to transport soup when I'm picking up orders for the office.

The best place to get a quick cheese steak and some fries with garlic sauce, don't forget to ask for the garlic sauce. I don't know why people are salty, the owner is super humble and very welcoming. The food is good and not expensive. I never had a bad experience at this joint. you just have to tell them exactly what you want, for instance - every time I order wings I ask them to cook them well and put just little bit of hot sauce. They always accommodate. I really like this place, it has been in the Overbrook area for awhile now, and after reading about some bad experiences here I wanted to share my experience and show some appreciation.

Grabbed brunch here on a Sunday. Indoor space is small, but if you can grab a spot at the bar or adjacent, you'll be rewarded with one of the most creative spaces in Saint Louis. It's an old gas station with modern conveniences and tons of charm. The patio can get warm if it's in direct sunlight, but great for a cooler day or the afternoon. The drink menu is extensive and unique. For brunch, we grabbed the pancakes, which are small, but filling with 3 different types of jam. I've never had Shakshuka, basted eggs in a spicy stewed tomato base accompanied by bread, but I plan on getting it again because it was amazing. And we rounded it out with a buffalo mozzarella with seasonal summer fruits. The place feels like it could easily be somewhere on either coast in a New York of LA. The benefit of finding it in Saint Louis is that you can probably get it. The staff was incredibly friendly and took us up to check out Elia, which is the find dining version attached to Olio. We'll be back soon.

I was so impressed with this place! It was a little pricey but it was worth it. Atmosphere was nice, even a little romantic. We were sat right next to the fire place. Our waiter went above and beyond. Cant wait to return.
We come here every weekend. I love everything here and have really missed this restaurant since moving to California. Say hi to Peter for me!
Great lunch option. real quick, lots of tasty options. all in all it was some good flavor-packed Indian food.

Went to Zeppoli for another epic meal in the harsh dead of this never ending winter, and for at least a few hours, i was transported. The chef really outdid himself on this particular night with such dazzlers as a blue crab crostini off the menu which was outrageous and whole mackerel on special served whole and grilled were just mind blowing. My guest and I were treated to their array of amazing pastas including a couple special bites including a lovely baccalao filled ravioli and a sample size of their beautiful and ethereal spinach gnocchi. For mains we ordered the rabbit and the seafood stew, both standouts and both leading to dreams for days to come of those flavors and impeccable mouthfuls. For desert a wonderful rose water panna cotta with an almond crumble which was great and their famous namesake which were particularly on point this bitter night. Some of the best treatment and service ive ever had. We will be returning again soon.

Like to sit at the bar for a beer and appetizers. The potstickers- panfried and the tuna appetizer are personal favorites. Clean atmosphere and friendly bartenders. Not big on Chinese food but the fact that this place serves alcohol is great.

This is a decent, all around Vietnamese restaurant. I feel as if the more run down places are the more authentic places. The menu itself has a wide range of foods to choose from. I just don't like how they used white out to write new prices.. just print a new menu. I ordered Pho Tai and it was pretty good and had a lot of meat. Only thing is I asked for no onions but they gave me absolutely no veggies like cilantro, which I asked for. Checking out was weird too since she pulled out a calculator and added up all the food. Other than that, good food!

We had the board room that was very nice. They didn't have wine for the entire dinner. Had to change. Service was excellent! Food was disappointing from appetizers to main courses. Prices were reasonable. Not Cafe Vicino. Terrible drop off in quality. 3 stars is being charitable
It was ok. A bit lack luster. Food was alright, nothing for me to wanting to come back.

the lemongrass tofu bahn mi is delicious. we ordered the deal of 6 for the price of 5. looking forward to heating the rest of them up in the oven tomorrow. the jasmine green tea in the french press was nice and strong. the plastic soda cups that were provided to drink it in are part of the umm, charm :)

Because of how good it was the first time I dined in there, I wanted to wait and try it a few more times before writing a review. I can now say, after another 3 trips there, that Zaika is one of the best features of Northeast Philadelphia. It's right behind Nifty Fifties, so look for the neon lights, and then park your car in the strip mall. They ask you how spicy you want the food, and will prepare it to that level of heat. So, don't feel intimidated about trying Indo-Pak food for the first time. It won't overwhelm you. The leftovers somehow taste even better. The staff is friendly. It's a pretty quiet dining room, although the dining room is not much to look at. There's no soda fountain, so you have to buy cans or bottles of soda/water/vitamin water from a cooler next to the counter. And I don't think they have a restroom for customers. Maybe it's in the back, but there aren't any signs for it. But frankly, all of the dining room features are unimportant because the food is just so very good. I would recommend this 10 out of 10 times to friends and family. Northeast Philly has a surplus of pizza/cheese-steak/wing places. Zaika is a fresh change of pace from the usual take-out places around us. Forget about some of the best Indo-Pak food you'll ever have (which it is!), this is some of the best food you'll ever have in Philadelphia.

On a rate of 0-5 Customer Service: 4 Environment: 4 The food: 3.5 Overall everything was content especially the pork belly baco, according to my lovely boyfriend. However the BBH (spicy beef soup) from which I had chosen to be my main course was a disappointment. The soup was lacking the aroma of lemongrass and the kick of spices. ( I had to request for extra chili). It came with about 3-4 pieces of brisket chunks which I found applaud of because it was so tender and succulent every time I bit into it. Therefore,I'll probably go back and try the pho along with the brisket chunks. As for lovely boyfriend, he got the combination pho which was also lacking the aroma of ginger, onions and star anise, however he ended up finishing it because of their meats which came plentiful in his bowl. In the end, we ended up leaving no evidence behind except empty bowls and used utensils.

Grabbed a quick dinner here before seeing the Phila Orchestra. We had a reservation but it wasn't too crowded so we were seated right away. Brought our own bottle of wine which was awesome! Service was very prompt and very friendly. The atmosphere was good, small place but it has character and with the many conversations, it gave the place a comfortable feel. Food came quickly as well because we let them know we had a show to go to.

I have actually been meaning to check out Cucina Zapata since it won the People's Choice at the 2011 Vendy Awards...I really have no good excuse for why it took me so long, but I'm glad I finally made it! Inventive dishes, fresh ingredients, great prices. These people love their food and care about the entire culinary experience that goes along with it. I got there at around 1:20pm on a Wednesday, and the wait for my food was about ten minutes, which was not as bad as I was expecting from what people had warned me. I ordered one short rib taco and one chicken satay taco along with a Thai iced tea. I was absolutely delighted when I cracked open my styrofoam box: two pretty sizeable tacos with giant slices of fresh avocado smiling up at me! Aesthetically beautiful and delicious too. I found the short rib taco to be better than the chicken satay, which was a little on the dry side. The Thai iced tea was also a little too sweet, so I would recommend specifically asking for it to be made less sweet. However, the short rib taco was incredibly juicy, tender, and well-seasoned. And of course, it came with wonderfully friendly service. Cucina Zapata really delivers the full package. I'm looking forward to trying the burrito next! Oozing with jealousy this truck isn't on Penn's campus!

My husband and I wanted to try it, we heard it was great, it's right in town and we're always looking for a "go to place". Unfortunately, for some reason, they are only open a few hours a day and a few days a week. It says they are open between 5:30 and 10. Ok. I attempted to call to make a reservation one Friday evening (around 6pm) for a little later that night. No one picked up, I attempted 3 times, and each time, they said to leave a message. We thought it was strange, on a Friday night, no one would pick up the phone? We cut our losses and decided to go to another restaurant in town instead. It's a shame, we pass by the place all the time, and we never have a problem with other restaurants with making reservations. Its such a small place, and on a Friday night, we're not ones to sit and wait for a table, we like to be proactive and call ahead, we just couldn't with this one.

This is the third Korean restaurant that I have dined at in the STL, the first being Koba (which is sadly now closed) and the second being Joo Joo. Honestly, I would rank the three in this same order if Koba were still open. Ate here for dinner on a weekday night with a party of 5 others and there were several other tables so it seemed like it had a decent following of customers. The service was super friendly and the fried dumplings we ordered were also delicious, but it didn't get much better beyond this. The side dishes were on par with other Korean restaurants' and they brought out two of each for our larger party. We also ordered both the steamed dumplings and fried dumplings. The fried dumplings were great; crispy, but not burnt. The steamed dumplings were not as good, had less filling in it and seemed to be a bit undercooked. Everyone at our table either had the Dol Sot Bibimbap (rice with assorted veggies cooked in a stone pot) or the Soon Doo Boo (spicy soft tofu stew with beef and assorted seafood). The Bibimbap was a bit bland and only tasted slightly better with the sauce that you add to spice it up. The portion of rice also seemed ridiculously small considering how expensive it was (over $11!!!) The Soon Doo Boo didn't earn rave reviews from our table either; it was skimpy on the beef and seafood (a few pieces of beef and one shrimp) and lots of tofu that did not fit the "soft tofu" billing. Overall, we were disappointed with the food and everyone went out for dessert elsewhere afterwards. While the service was great and the restaurant had a nice environment, I would opt for Joo Joo next time just because the food was significantly better and I think slightly cheaper.

Have only visited for the lunch buffet. Probably at least 10-12 different selections and all were very good. Fresh naan brought to your table. Food was fresh every time we visited. Will be coming back.

Our first visit today was great! We've been wanting to visit and now they're open for lunch! The interior has been updated and is more modern. The service was great and the food was good. I have food allergies so have to order simple rolls with fish and veggies only... the Alaska was great as well as the spicy Tuna. My friend ordered the Pokémon Go roll (how funny) which the server told us was the most popular... she loved it. Their miso soup is good as well... some places are not. We will be back for lunch often! They could use some music though.. it's a little too quiet.
Not a bad little place to eat, but was a little let down by the portion sizes. Ordered grilled chicken and I got such a small portion.

It has reasonably lunch prices for considerable portions. I really enjoyed the rice that came with gyro and chicken Schwarma combo. We had great service. Glasses never empty constantly being checked on. The food was good but not great I found the chicken to be a tad dry. Do not get me wrong I ate every bite and would eat it again. It was just missing flavor. One of my favorite parts was the salad which was a tad disappointing because I was just craving juicy gyro meat. I still enjoyed myself enough to want to go back.

Only ok. Had the grilled pork rolls, spicy beef pho, and meat lover baguette. The nuoc cham for the rolls was too fishy for my taste. Yes, I know there's fish sauce in it but it was too much. The broth for the pho needed more depth of flavor but the spicy sauce was good and meat portion was generous. Baguette was just ok, nothing special.

OMG indian buffet that's actually amazing?! Crazy right? This place is flat out fantastic! Went here twice for lunch with co-workers. Now I did judge when we arrived bc I saw this place attached to a motel...yes a motel. Don't be alarmed! Restaurant was pretty, employees friendly and attentive. I'm drooling just thinking of the delishiousness food! *they bring fresh nan to your table :) I can not wait to go back! This is my place to go for lunch! Go here you will not be disappointed!

The flaming cheese is a must have! Not only for the "show" and cries of "Opa!" when it's afire, but because of the crusty outside and molten inside. A squeeze of lemon and a bite on top of a soft triangle of pita sent me over the edge of cheese bliss! I devoured a nicely portioned salad that consisted of earthy beets, sliced almonds, creamy feta (versus the dry, firmer type I've typically encountered), delicate greens and a delicious vinaigrette. I was running out of room, likely also due to the Guinness I'd been sipping, but ordered a traditional lamb gyro. The meat was nicely cooked and more tender than I've had at other restaurants - or from street vendors in NYC. I would've preferred longer, thicker slices to their bite-sized pieces, though that's minor. I prefer a thicker tzatziki sauce - this one was quite thinned out. It tasted house made and had a lot of herbs and cucumber bits, but was on the less flavorful side. On a high note, the service was impeccable! Ambient music played in the background and was at just the right volume to create a relaxing atmosphere. The decor was lovely and there was a cozy fireplace in the dining room. Though I visited on a Saturday afternoon, I'd go again during the week for the belly dancing. A downside is their policy of not splitting checks, so if you go with a group, be forewarned. A definite must visit for authentic Greek cuisine!

This might have been a fun place if we were slurping hurricane drinks or ordering "buckets" of longnecks like half the crowd on this enclosed-deck, picnic-table style beach place. Jet lag left us looking a lot more like the other half of the patronage - namely the geritol generation. Mostly, you're looking at deep fried stuff, burgers, etc. But they do have a fresh fish special. Tonight's was grilled mahi-mahi with a mango chutney, served with your choice of sides: rice and beans (yum), spiced apples, sweet potato fries, slaw, or many other options. We rather enjoyed the mahi-mahi, and there was a nice view, but not nice enough to justify a $50 tab (after tip) for 2 adults, 1 kid, plasticware, paper plates, no appetizers, no alcohol, and no dessert. Acceptable, but not great.
Out of all the three Indian eateries in University City, I would rank Tandoor as #3. The food was OK (could use more variety), but it was just the atmosphere that did not quite sell to me.

Yum - this is a delicious shop to grab a quick bite to eat in downtown St. Pete. I love that there are so many options for what you can add to your sandwich. I always go with the chicken and lamb combo. I've always had phenomenal service. They go above and beyond to be patient with me as I meticulously choose the perfect topping combination.

Great food, interesting atmosphere. Later in the night they play fun music so people can salsa dance. Everyone in my party was very satisfied with their food! The service was slow and didn't seem like they were prepared for the large party regardless of our reservation made far in advance. I would also say that the drinks are not worth the steep price. I payed $10 for a margarita that tasted like grocery store sweet and sour mix.

UPDATE: I understand the management has changed since my negative food event and 3 day intestinal roller coaster ride. In all fairness to them, and in the spirit of generosity, I will up my rating to middle of the road. You challenged me to try again Desi, so I will. OLD review: Food poisoning. I'm pretty sure it was the mint chutney, which in years past would sit out on the buffet line. It wasn't there...so I asked for some, and out comes a cold, half empty, open container. That little voice in my head tried to warn me. Two days later...If I had only listened. Besides that it was a letdown! Cold tandoori chicken and dried out tikka masala. Done w Desi V.

Friendly staff. Decent drinks. Have not had their food. The atmosphere to me feels a bit snobbish. I prefer to sit outside with the dog patrons. Just be wary of Gary who is sweet but always there. He's harmless yet intrusive. Good ladies night specials. It would be a fun date night place. Very dark inside at night, but great decor. I like this place!

I only started to patronize this place after my father-in-law suffered a heart attack five years ago. The owner's wife is the coronary nutritionist at the hospital where he was a patient. I sat in on her training session for the heart attack and bypass surgery survivors, and I was quite impressed with her teachings. So, I decided to try Greek food for the first time a couple of days later. I was an immediate fan of this place upon my first visit. I frequently get a Greek Salad and Lamb cigars with Whole Wheat Pita to go on the way home from the office. It is delicious, quite filling, healthy, and not too expensive. The owner, his wife, and his daughter are all quite friendly, and they get to know the regulars.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: Good but not great. Service could be faster. I thought 9 Bangkok Restaurant (nearby) was better.

Refreshing see to a nice small restaurant here seemingly in the middle of nowhere in Norristown. Taste of the Island brought me back when I lived in the Bay Area and was able to sample to delicious tastes of the Caribbean, namely Haitian, DR, and Jamaican foods. This place has a small and large portioned plates, both for a little under (small) and over (large) $10. I got the jerk chicken plate with Mac and Cheese and rice with gravy. I was in the middle of working so I just took it to go. These portions are serious, I think I had like 4 pieces of chicken in this 10 dollar meal. The flavor was really good, and even though we weren't in the Caribbean, I could feel the Caribbean emanating through the food. I could feel the love put into the food. Come check it out!
Got the order wrong. No bread.I called and instead of making it correct they blew it off.

Delish! The very best Indian cuisine in town. The staff is very friendly. The scene is quiet and elegant. And the price is excellent. The Sunday all you can eat, is amazing. I recommend the chicken masala.

My husband and I used a coupon while on vacation in St. Louis and we loved it so much we bought another coupon online and returned later that same week. It was over $50 both times, which is really expensive for us, but the food was so good we didn't mind. We usually only eat gyros and I cannot remember what exactly we ate here, but I just know that it was unlike anything we have ever had. We adored everything from the appetizer (hummus) to the dessert. The seats are comfortable and intimate. We sat in a booth both times. The first time it was rather empty so we got a large booth all to ourselves. It was a lot of fun. One of the times we went they had a belly-dancer dance through the restaurant, which I felt was a really cool touch.

I am very critical of Indian food and I think this is the best Indian food in the area!! It's a family run restaurant. I can see that they put a lot of effort on providing quality food and customer service. As its owned by a Nepali couple, they also have some Nepali dishes on the menu! I would really recommend trying their momo's which is a authentic Nepali cuisine.

Amazingly hot and spicy! When you ask for extra spicy at some places you don't get it. They didn't flinch and brought us pure awesome spice. The garlic naan was a good size but not too garlic flavored. A little bland but I live everything over the top. The chicken tikka masala which is a staple if what I get at Indian restaurants was fantastic. So smooth and creamy yet spicy. We also had lamb biryani which was packed with goodies. It wasn't quite as hot but super tasty. The rice was perfect. Can't complain. They didn't overdo the raisins or whatever it is they put in biryani. Lastly, the best water service I have ever had. When my water was even slightly empty they came by to check and refill. That's something I appreciate. I hate waiting for water especially with spicy food.
The best Dorato fish I have ever eaten!! Actually everything we ordered we loved!! Going again tonight!! A must go to restaurant!! Best chef ever!!!

I'm sure there's far worse but I was unimpressed with my first visit to Saigon today. Got the grilled pork spring rolls which, honestly was my favorite part of the meal. Husband got the stir fried noodles with meat and seafood...i had several tastes and "meh" sorta bland. i got the lemongrass tofu and it was just so-so. I could have been much more flavorful IMO. Made me long for the old stand by I used to visit weekly in Dallas. I truly much prefer two other vietnamese restaurants in the area. I'll give them one more try for some PHO!!!

This place is awesome. I've never eaten there, but the take out is always consistently delicious. I get #12 Pho (rare beef), shrimp and pork lotus salad, Apollo shrimp wrapped in springroll wrapper for the kids, shrimp paste on sugar cane, mixed grill sampler, some of the best tempura I've ever had, PORK TACOS ARE TO DIE FOR !!! ( on special menu) . I love turning my friends on to this place !

Visiting friends and wanted something I could eat (vegan) and spotted the restaurant on yelp near. Warm welcome to nice clean dining room. There is a small vegan menu (ask for it) with some favorite dishes tailored to vegan eaters! They make their own spice and it is Hot....but found med little to mellow for me but I love heat! Added a little sprinkle and kicked up the heat and flavor a bit! Yum! Portions for lunch were large for even a dinner menu! Can't wait till I'm back in Brandon, if not anything else,to come back here!

Wow, Indonesian food is amazing and has a totally different spice palate than other Southeast Asian cuisines! This place is a hole-in-the-wall but one of the best super-cheap Asian meals I've had all year.

Large portions and low prices make this a good restaurant if you are interested in basic Vietnamese food. We have been there a number of times and found good food - the sandwiches are very tasty, the Pho soups are very good and the other items were also good. The problem is service! It is slow and at times weak. Not everything comes out at the same time, Supporting item, greens and peppers for he soup, silverware etc. are missing at times. With the university out, business is slow and the kitchen reorders food when it runs out. This Saturday night we ordered sandwiches but they had run out of rolls, we ordered another dish that had egg rolls but they were out of egg rolls! It would be easy to forget about this eatery BUT the food and prices are so good.! try them when time permits, enjoy the food and complain about what you are not happy with

India Palace rocks. They have a great lunch buffet which I like to frequent on the weekends. However, it's OK to go here at other times too! The tandoori chicken is amazing. And honestly, who doesn't like chowing on Naan? Service is fairly good, with a slight, but consistent, tendency to slam glasses down on the table a little drastically. I've never had a complaint. A nice place for anyone who likes Indian. Keep in mind, though, this place isn't very spicy, if that's the taste that you prefer.

I haven't written a review in quite sometime. I also haven't found any hidden jems until today either. This place is awesome. I ordered red curry with pork and had a mango bubble tea... let me tell you; this hit the spot and the void of a great place since I moved here. Very kind staff and the food had great flavor. I don't take left overs home.. had to convince myself in case I craved it later lol.

This place has incredible Indian/Pakistani food, it's more of a take out place so don't judge it for its grocery store appearance. Very friendly owners and great fresh food. Priced fairly A total gem in NE Philly

Don't let the location or lack of patrons concern you - they do a large amount of takeout. The food is fresh, made with loving hands and the owner even comes to talk with you about life. I love different and engaging experiences with good food and this didn't disappoint!

This is our classic go to restaurant for lunch and an afternoon snack. This time it was less than satisfactory due to the service. The greeter/waitress sat us and never came back after we told her that one of menus was splattered with food and the table required cleaning. The experience was only saved when a waiter who had just come to work recognized that we hadn't been serviced and asked us if we were ready to order. The food was good as usual, but poor service drives away customers.

Schannicchio's is great! The service was really good and everyone was friendly. On top of that, they have a very authentic Italian menu. Everything was cooked perfectly and the specials were excellent. Would highly recommend the bruschetta as well as anything fradiavolo (the sauce has a decent kick). It's BYOB too, so stop by a liquor store and pick up a bottle of wine before heading over.
This is the best curry chicken I have ever had. Prompt service and kind employees. A must experience.
My husband brought me food from the place a few times and it is always great. I would strongly recommend giving them a try if your looking for authentic great quality Puerto Rian food.

The pho was awesome. Good sized portion for pretty cheap, tons of flavor! Like other reviews have said, the service could be better, and the cash only thing is a little absurd in 2012, but it's right up the street from my house and I would still eat there again in a heartbeat.
Ewww!!! I got attitude as soon as i placed my order. Let's see if the food was worth the grief.

This place is nothing special. I had the greek salad with chick peas and my wife had the taziki dip. Both were good enough but nothing to write much home about. If you have a craving for some decent mediterranean food and thi sis the closest or you are new to this type of food, it is a good blander choice.

A great place to get fresh #veggie juice in west Philadelphia! Please read more below. A great mix of West Indian/Trinidadian food. Get there quick because the fish runs out early. Platters are plentiful and reasonably priced. Authentic food. I recommend the "King Fish" with macaroni & cheesecake.

Excellent restaurant right next door to the Springhill Suites and Residence Inn. Delicious and unique cocktails, great ambience and very tasty pan Asian cuisine. Our server Prakash was polite and very helpful and made great recommendations about the food and drink all of which which we enjoyed thoroughly. The manager Pratik stopped by each table to greet the guests and inquire about the food and service. If you are in the Nashville area or visiting, definitely make a stop here.

Finally found great Thai in the New Tampa area! Lunch special was delicious, hubby had salad and spicy chicken pad Thai. I had spring roll-nice and crispy and the beef pad Thai. Portions were generous and everything was freshly cooked. We will be back!

Great Vietnamese spot on Magazine St. The food is consistently great. A go to spot in the neighborhood! Convenient spot for take out! If you stay to eat, it's fun to dine on the front porch while watching all the passers-by on Magazine Street.
Great food, great service. Lovely family owned restaurant. There are so many options: Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, and a bit of Japanese.

Been looking for a thai food restaurant that delivers since ive been in NJ on business, after yelping I located Asian fusion and decide to give it a try. I ordered the red curry chicken dish and enjoyed it for the most part the only disappointment was that it was too watery . However the flavor and heat was great with this dish.

Update: The restaurant is under new management and although the food seems to be the same, the service has taken a nosedive. I am between a rock and a hard place because the last time we went (December 2014) the treatment was absolutely sub-par. Were it not for the years of good experiences, I'd have written it off on that experience alone. I called on a Friday night and was told the restaurant was open until 9:30pm. I arrived at 8pm with a group of 5. At the time there was one large party and 2 other tables. I was told by the waiter (the same one who had answered the phone and told me 9:30pm) that after I called they decided business was slow and they wanted to close early. I offered to order for takeout but the waiter seated us instead. After seating us, he mentioned that it would have been easier if we sat on the other side of the room-- but he chose the table, not us?! We ordered and waited. Food was thrown rudely on the table. The waiter never checked in to see how things were. As has been my experience, the food was terrific. At the end of the meal, we flagged the waiter down and asked for the check. When he brought it, we gave a credit card which he took. He then come back and announced matter-of-factly that we had to leave the tip in cash. I was honestly flabbergasted that the waiter would (1) be do bizarre to start; (2) give poor service during the meal; (3) and then demand a cash tip. I was embarrassed in front of the friends I brought (I recommended we go to Palace of Asia) and left. I don't know WHAT to say?! I really don't. The food is a 5 star review for me. The service would be a 0 and I wouldn't go back. So my previously 5 star review is going down to 2 stars. I am very disappointed. *******PRIOR REVIEW BELOW******* I've eaten Indian food all over the US and in the UK (where it's very popular). Palace of Asia is authentic, delicious, and the same good consistent service every time. It is located in a very seedy motel, but inside the restaurant it's nicely decorated (white tablecloths, traditional decor). The food is excellent and perfectly cooked. Not overly spicy but appropriately spiced. I particularly enjoy their Malai Kofta and pakoras. Everything is cooked traditionally and well. I have not had one bad dish! Overall, it's the best Indian I've had in the US and always a good experience. Recommended!

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: I went back after a break for over a year. I definitely liked the food well enough the last few times I went, but sort of forgot about it. Then I remembered, and read up on recent reviews. Seemed to me that it must have improved even from when I used to go. So I decided to stop in recently (still has that hole-in-the-wall feel I remembered), and the owners seem to be different. Even more friendly... And they had beef nihari on the specials board, so I was all IN for that (I'm a fiend for nihari). Once I got the dish, it was just sublime, with fresh ginger and cilantro punctuating the deep savory flavor of the sauce. They warned me it would be hot, and it was indeed quite warm. Not intolerably so, but just right to the point I got a mild sweat going on my brow. Perfect. The dish was so delicious I keep thinking about it, and wondering how I can figure out whenever they will offer it. If the rest of the menu is as good, it's most certainly a hidden gem. Very highly recommended (not 5 stars because for me it takes the highest of perfection to earn that distinction).

We travel a good bit, and generally have at least one Thai meal in every city we visit. This was our last full day in Nashville, and after eating some terrific southern food, we decided to try a highly rated (Yelp) Thai restaurant. It was a cold rainy day, on some warm comfort food (read - soup and noodles) sounded perfect. Did I mention we eat a lot of Thai food? Yes I did. So when I say this was one of our best Thai meals, it carries a lot of weight. I love the foods of Nashville, bbq, hot chicken, fried green tomatoes, etc. But when we come back, Bankokville Thai will be on my list as a 'must visit"

I have never been a huge fan of Indian food, until I came to Persis. This place has never failed to provide fresh, delicious food and I have yet to have a bad experience. The butter chicken, garlic naan and spring rolls are to die for! When you eat at a restaurant that serves foreign food and you always see many people of that nationality there, that is usually a pretty good sign that it's good food. This Indian restaurant always has many people from Indian descent filling it's tables. Here today and trying the Biryani chicken for the first time. Can't wait! Update- Biryani is frikkin awesome as well.

For the food specifically, in light of others of its ilk, fantastic. Their chutney (sp; difference for Persian/Afghani here) is the very best I've ever had, super tangy and a bit hot. Strange as it's standard fare and not a main entree. So be it. Had the beef kebob and it was solid, very dependable and very generous in portion. Afghani salad was not my bag, but my date assured me it was good despite the difference in palate. The neighborhood is densely urban, so parking can be harrowing, but this is not a reflection on the eatery so much as the poor urban planning of Philly. Ambiance is clearly Middle Eastern as Hell, tasteful, not over-the-top. Price was better than anticipated in light of the inflated finances of Philly, too. Staff was prompt, friendly, and very accountable.

I'd really like to give it 3.5 stars. I also reserve the right to re-rank after a few more visits (thinking it could bump to 4)...and yes I plan on returning. I've eaten here twice and the food was good. The portions were a really good size and everything was very fresh. Service was a little slower than I would've liked the one time but overall great place. They have outside seating which is a plus I've only eaten outside or done takeout so I can't really speak for the interior beyond the ordering counter.

Holy good Thai. Finally found the one Thai restaurant in Florida that's worth traveling to. It's taken three years. Read reviews and gave it a try. Had pot stickers red curry and drunken noodles. Just so delicious with enough left over for tomorrow. Just give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

This place is AMAZING! The noodles are made in-house and the food is incredible. The service is great. The price was reasonable. Convenient location with plenty of parking spots. Totally recommend the food here.

I came here the other day with a group of folks, so we got to try lots of stuff. We had the lamb special, tabouli salad, fried cheese, the mixed grill, Turkish coffee, and vegetarian platter. The lamb special was super tender, and the smoked rice added a nice flavor to round out the dish. The tabouli was very fresh and really helped to balance out some of the heavier dishes. It was especially good as a counterpoint to the fried cheese. I have a meze addiction, so the vegetarian platter was superb. It really comes with everything you might want to smear onto pita. The Turkish coffee was super tasty as well. The taste of cardamom was robust yet not overpowering. I didn't dip into the mixed grill till near the end. I recommend eating it hot, as I think all the time I spent waiting for the other layers of food to digest made the lamb tough.
Great food; consistent. Long waits during busy times. Love the "house" dishes, popular versions that include shrimp. Chicken and pork.
Every time I'm in town this is the only spot I go to for banh mi sandwiches! I think best in the Bay Area. However the service is slow sometimes but the staff is friendly.

Pho Orchid Uptown is one of the best pho restaurant in New Orleans. Their foods are to die for especially their spicy beef noodles. Their happy hours are also incredible from 3pm-6pm and 9pm-12am. The staff and service was amazing, everyone is extremely nice and funny. This place is cleanest pho restaurant I ever been to. It's a very causal and chill place to have lunch or dine. I 100% recommend to try this place out if your in New Orleans!!!

This is the best Italian in the area. My family of 3 went tonight for dinner and came away thoroughly impressed. For appetizers to split we ordered the antipasto plate for two, the shrimp with fava beans, and the sausage with broccoli rabe. The antipasto plate was the star of the meal--there were about 14 or 15 different items on the plate, including some fresh vegetables and my favorite, a salad of fava beans and Italian tuna. The mortadella with pistachios was great as well. The fresh-ground sausage was also excellent, as was the rabe. The shrimp was excellent as well. For entrees, two of us ordered the swordfish and one ordered the spaghetti with clams. The portion of swordfish was massive, probably around 12 ounces, and the fresh fennel salad that came with it was a perfect complement. The clams on the spaghetti were great, and the spaghetti wasn't completely coated in oil. We didn't plan on ordering dessert, but the chef sent over 3 zeppoles on the house. The zeppoles, served with Nutella, were sweet and had a bite from the cinnamon sugar coating. They even sent over another without the Nutella to accommodate a nut allergy. Our servers, Jessi, Vinny, and Kris were all excellent and knew the menu front to back. All were able to explain various menu items and preparations, and the pacing of the courses was perfect. We'll definitely be coming back.

I live in Queen Village- just down the street from this hidden gem. I am so happy that Golden Triangle is now a part of our neighborhood. Cute place, excellent food and service. You can't beat the price either. I hope that Golden Triangle continues to be successful. It's a great neighborhood staple!

I didn't try the pho because I can't eat raw meat right now. I had the shrimp and scallops with vegetables and it wasn't too fresh. My husband had the tofu with curry and it was just ok. We also had the crispy spring vegetables which again were not that impressive.

This place is not bad, but it's not particularly good either. I've had several things off the menu, green curry, pad thai, thai fried rice, and some kind of soup, and everything was just so-so. On one occasion the lady asked me on a scale of 1 to 5 how spicy I wanted my food, I told her a 5, and she all but refused to make it that spicy.

Ordered level 3 spiciness of the green curry and it was truly spicy which was greatly appreciated! Food was fresh and tasted great. Large portions and kid friendly. Didn't have to wait for a table and the food came out in a timely manner.

After long gours of shopping, we decided to stop by dosa hut to grab some chicken kuthu parota.. as my friends said it was amazingly done. Loved the taste and we also called in couple of other friends to join us. Pros: Good food Cons: Tiny space, need to create better vibe.
Excellent Food! Great service. Drunken noodle did not disappoint. Also, really good steamed dumplings.
The best Indian food in all of Tampa Bay. Love the buffet options and amazing menu options.

First time here today. We picked up lunch. I had the lamb shish-kabob. Very tasty. They certainly didn't skimp on the meat. Everything was cooked perfectly. And wen it comes to lamb you have got to cook that perfectly. I'll be back.

I'm not sure if they changes ownership or what, but the food is very different than it was a year or so ago. The tzatziki had a pinkish tint and OK flavor, the chicken was passable, but the gyro meat was sliced so thin that it had the texture of notebook paper. It was like ribbons of meat instead of slices. Also, I don't know what spice they're using in the grape leaves, but it had a strong licorice flavor. Not great at all.

Stopped in last Thursday night with the fiancée. Had a groupon. Upon walking in, the first thing you notice is the size of the place, it's BIG. The decor is definitely dated and in need of repair (our seats had lime green duct tape on it), but it did appear to be clean. We were immediately welcomed with water and our orders taken promptly. We started with gobi manchurian, which is a spicy cauliflower appetizer. It is lightly fried and comes with a spicy sauce. I would highly recommend it. My fiancée ordered a bowl of mulligatawny soup. This Classic Indian soup was made with lentils here, which seemed highly unusual to me, though I'm no expert. It was however fresh and hit the spot on a frigid night. For our entrees, we ordered the chana masala and chicken tikka masala, with some garlic naan. SO GOOD! The entrees were so delicious, you could tell the food was made fresh. When you order tikka masala at a lot of restaurants, sadly, what comes out is overlooked chicken, covered in a thin pink sauce, lacking in flavor. Here, the chicken was tender, the sauce flavorful, with lots of veggies visible. Overall good meal. I will return, though I'll wait until I get another groupon.

Ive been searching for Thai place like this since I've moved to Pennsylvania. We took the suggestion to try the lunch special. It was soo good. We had my favorites, panang and tom ka kai. You have to eat here. The other places we tried in Philly have been good but totally fell short. Im am drooling jus thinking of it. okay gotta stop writing or i wont eat dinner tonite!!! later....

As a pho connoisseur of sorts (my parents are from Vietnam), I have to say that Pho Bistro has the best pho in the Santa Barbara area. I was pleasantly surprised when I got a huge steaming bowl with all the appropriate cuts of meat in it. The broth has a deep beefy flavor (unlike all the other Vietnamese places in town that give you a bland broth) and will definitely quell any pho cravings you may have. My only issue is that it was pretty pricey for a bowl of pho. I think I paid about $8 for my bowl, which is way overpriced. It should be under 6 bucks in my opinion, but then again I come from the Bay Area where prices for great Asian food are way lower.

Had a nice lunch here today. The fries were wonderful and the roasted veggie pita was well seasoned and filled with vegetables. The pita was soft and very fresh. The quality of the ingredients made it worth the price. Fun space, friendly staff. Will definitely go back.

I walked in there on my first day of moving in to Franklin. I've been back many times since July. I love their food, my family does too. It's always fresh, tasty, plentiful and well-priced. Apart from the gyros and the salads, I love their spanakopita. Their humus is excellent and so are their desserts!

I've wanted to try this out for months but never could since he's always closed on weekends. But having taken off a few days for July 4th was able to come out here that Monday. I walked up a little after 12:30pm and there were maybe 8/9 ppl ahead of me. The pace of the line was a standstill as this isn't fast food. I said hello when it was my turn and didn't get a response, but maybe cos I was new or cos he was focused on putting the meal together though he talked to a few of the other ppl who were ahead of me. He wished me a nice day when handing me the $10 mystery box and I was on my way to find utensils and napkins as this is not provided with the meal. Unsure what was in the box, it had chicken, sausage, tomatoes, rice I think, falafel ball, maybe a bean sprout? Doesn't matter cos the shit is delicious and filling and for me worth the wait. I came back up 7/5 but later around 1:20 and was told that he didn't have enough for me, only enough for the guy ahead of me who was like 4 ppl in. Ugh what a bummer lol. While I haven't tried Mamas Vegetarian, that is real close by should anyone not want to wait or should he run out of food before getting to you. I should of tried this spot when he ran out my 2nd here but didn't have time. I would say this deserves the 4.5 overall rating. And I like the idea of a delicious $10 mystery box. Hell im debating calling out this Monday now lol

Walking into the space was breathtaking. Light, airy, inviting. Yelpers pointed me in the direction of the mushroom hummus and they were spot-on! The shiitakes were scrumptious and seasoned/cooked beautifully and went so so well with the creamy hummus. This dish, including the pita, definitely gives Dizengoff stiff competition! My table mates also got the baba ganoush and it was equally scrumptious. To complete this lovely lunch was the clementine/ginger soda ... refreshing, with a great kick! The servers were warm, gregarious and genuinely were pleased to ensure you had what you needed. They were as excited for you to taste the plates as they brought them to the table. Can't wait to return for dinner!

Yummmmmm. So many authentic flavors. Been in several times and the food is consistently delicious. Family run. I love working my way through the menu. My favorites are the Lar Nah and Mee Shan. Never had any dishes quite like them before. Seriously good. This is a staple for the neighborhood.

We made a reservation for 23 and Priya accommodates us with 100% satisfaction. We orders both non-veg and veg and all the dishes were absolutely amazing. Customer services was 10 out of 10 and food 10 out of 10. Beats Indian Garden which appeared to be super rude. Highly recommended. I just Prefer talk to Priya she is amazing
Outstanding Indian cuisine! Excellent weekday lunch buffet. A wonderful dining experience right here in Newtown.

Husband and I came here for a late lunch. He ordered the coconut shrimp for his appetizer which were good but slightly over fried. He had the Mahi Mahi Mango which was really good but a bit on the greasy side and we were expecting fresh mango but instead got some kind of mango sauce which was reminiscent of baby food. I ordered the fish tacos, also good but the slaw was a bit heavy on the mayo side. Most disappointing was when we went to redeem our free dessert coupon, they "didn't have" the dessert we wanted, the Helado del dia (fresh tropical ice cream). Better for our waste lines I guess? Overall service was fast and friendly but the food could use a little less grease.

This is one of our favorite places to go for banh mi and for iced Vietnamese coffee. Prices are reasonable and the decor is inviting. However, don't get the pad thai. For some odd reason they load it up with paprika, which doesn't belong in the dish. Everyone at our table agreed the pad thai was really bad. But oh, the banh mi! served with the bread freshly toasted, still warm and crispy on the outside, the banh mi's the bomb!
New owners. The buffet is the same food, but not kept up to the proper temperature. The soup was ice cold, and could not be eaten. Would not repeat.

I'm genuinely mystified as to why everyone's so mad about this place. Based on the over-the-top reviews, I gave it two tries over three days: once dining-in on a Wed night; once carry-out Fri night. Neither time blew my mind, and I did get the much-praised King Soup. It was fine, but I literally had a better version of it last spring in a middling Thai place in Lincoln Nebraska, so that's kind of telling. 1) The food seems v. fresh, so that's great. It's also on the pricey side, so I would actually expect it to be more mind-blowing. 2) WAY TOO LOUD. Be prepared to face a Wall Of Noise when eating at Vientiane, and to shout at your dining companions - there is no other way. 3) They're understaffed: service is friendly enough, but very haphazard (it took multiple tries to get anyone's attention for things like extra napkins or a wine glass). On the rare occasion that we saw an employee, they seemed feverishly consumed with what they were doing - to the point that they expressly avoided looking around at any surrounding tables to check if they might need anything. Food is pretty slow -- again, this would be fine if I thought it were really spectacular - I just don't think it is. Def. won't be hurrying back, and will actively avoid the dinner rush. Chaotic dining environment = super stressful.

I've been going to Coco regularly for dinner since they opened. The food is tremendous, the value for the price is outstanding, and the service is kind. The chef/owner is genuine and has come out each time I've been there to check on the diners and make sure everything is good. The decor has been upgraded over time, and if it were slightly more comfortable I would give it 5 stars. The pad thai (regular and the style they serve that is lower in fat and calories) is as authentic as it gets. The appetizer sampler is fantastic and the other dishes I've had there are perfect.

If you're looking for an amazing breakfast joint and you are around the Cheery Hill area, do yourself a favor and stop by Zac's Pancake House. The staff was friendly and the food was phenomenal. I can't say enough great things about this place. Keep up The good work!

A pretty small place right around the corner of 16th and spruce. It's a good place to get Thai take out. I forget what I got exactly, but it was damn good. 14 bucks was worth the meal and a half that I received. Very satisfied. The owner/manager was very nice too.

Amazing. I've been searching SB for good kabob and I found it! Super good food, big portions, and very friendly staff. My bf is a picky eater and he cleaned his whole plate. LOL The chicken and beef kafta are on point!

I've had dinner there twice so far. The first time, my boyfriend and I were one of the only people there since we went for an early dinner and the service was fast and wonderful. The second we went the place was packed and the service was a bit slower which is the only reason I'm giving 4 stars, not 5. The food is absolutely amazing though!! The naan is fresh, fluffy and hot and they will give you as much rice as you need with your dish. I've tried two of the lamb dished, the roganjosh and the korma, both of which were delicious! My boyfriend has had the chicken korma twice and loves it. Prices are quite reasonable, too.
Best Mofongo in Tampa, hands down. Had the seafood mofongo with lobster, clams, crab, in a creole sauce. Excellent. Great service too, and nice ambience. Well done.
What a great find for a couple of visitors demonstrated wonderful use of spices. Very nice and attentive

Really great chicken, but you have to eat it with sauce. The chipotle lime mayo sauce is amazing. Mac and cheese is quite good too, but a little bit greasy. Solid place for comfort food. I went back on the second day and got the salad---SOOO good!!! Love it. Definitely try.

Pleasantly surprised! We have ordered takeout from here twice now. The second time was far superior to the first. I ordered the beef pad Thai the first time and it was tasty, but a bit dry. However I am glad that we went back! I had the shrimp pad Thai the second time and it was so good! The summer rolls with the peanut sauce are excellent and huge! I think next time we will try eating in and see how that is. **Update** We went into the restaurant to eat and man, I am changing my review to 5 stars. We walked about 15 min before closing (which we felt terrible about) but they happily sat us. The food was wonderful and they were so kind. Even got some free spring rolls. Love this place!
Seriously good food and excellent service. Great Thai. Small restaurant space but sometime the best places are hidden gems this is one of them.

I was so excited to find my fave Thai joint after passing the old empty trailer this week. A little research and here I am! Everything about this gem is authentic and wonderful. You can never go wrong with the specials. And while I can go gonzo on the spice I always get great advice on treating the delights with just enough fire. I am giddy awaiting the highlight of my Friday! SKÅL!

Very cool, eclectic small out of the way place a local friend took us to. We shared several plates, all of which were excellent in both concept and execution. Among our dishes were riblets, fried chicken, grilled shrimp, grilled swordfish, broccoli salad, wintermelon, and shishito peppers. All were fantastic - great blending/layering of flavors in each dish. I highly recommend this little gem.

Had the clay pot today and the food was delicious with a lot of heat. I'm glad our waiter asked more than once how spicy I wanted my dish. It came out exactly as I prefer, with kick but not so hatefully hot it can't be enjoyed. My cousin had pork wonton soup and he said it was great. He burned through his spring rolls pretty quickly so I'm going to assume they were good too. Will definitely come back. Wasn't busy at noon when we arrived but I think more people should come. The food is great and I'm happy that I don't need to drive into Philly you get good Thai food.

Phenomenal place. Food seems different than your average Thai place, but that's because it's authentic home style (as we were told). Different is good, really good. Do yourself a favor and have dinner here. Owned and operated by an adorable couple. I vouch for the legacy fried rice and thom yum seafood mix!
The Ariana kabob is bangn! Best afgani/ hookah spot in Philly. And you know its good when the chef actually joins you for dinner! Def will recommend to friends.
Eat at the bar so you can have Kristie wait on you and have her make you one of the best martinis ever. The rigatoni is super light with leeks and amazing meatballs. Wonderful service.

Once again the food was delicious. The service was great which seems to be the norm. Got my usual the chicken kabobs and spinach roll-ups. Oh yea before I forget I was helped by Nicole and she did a great job providing excellent service. Love this place!

Such a great find! The staff could not have been nicer - especially Kayla behind the bar! Such a sweet, smart lady who made drinks and dinner a memorable experience. I will be sure to visit again next time in Boise. Cheers to you all!

What a sweet little restaurant! Everything has such thoughtful detail, even the straw wrappers are twisted into roses. We started with the chicken satay and spring rolls I also had the coconut soup which was warm, sweet and frothy. My husband and I both had the Pad Thai, perfection! My kids both had the Kao Mun Kai and both cleaned their plates! We finished with the warm mango sticky rice which I highly recommend!
This restaurant is so good! Great food, great atmosphere and much less wait compared to other local Thai places.

Love this place. My go to for good Thai and sushi restaurant. And the ambiance is one of the reasons to come here! It is cozy and very Thai, with the fabrics, lighting, and elaborate wall art and sculptures will bring you to another place. The first time I came here I was amazed, no other Thai restaurant features elaborate interior design as theirs! Female servers wear traditional Thai clothing and are warm and friendly. It's one of those places to take a visiting friend or family to and amaze them with the ambiance and the food!

This is my favorite restaurant for lunch and dinner. Consistently delicious every time my wife and I come, which is often. Love the interior decore and the owner is super kind and hospitable. The is very flavorful and the ingredients taste of good quality. Good verity of dishes makes this a great place to brings family and friends.

The Malai Kafta is the best I have ever had! The vegetable biryani is amazing too. They are very consistent, always the same quality food- never disappointed. Super fast service too! This is my go to for carry out, delicious comfort food and they will make it as mild or as spicy as you want. Sooooooo good!!!!!!! I order double just to freeze some for later. Some people talk down on the atmosphere- it's not uptight, fancy, shwanky. It's not one of those places where your waiter will not hound you for updates or engage in overly enthusiastic, useless conversation for bigger tips. It's a super easy going place that I highly recommend.

Sleek, modern and brand new adding one more type of cuisine to the food boom happening on Freret Street. I have eaten there twice and been happy with my pho and spring rolls. The staff seemed very friendly and competent and that's not always a given. It's Vietnamese food if I haven't mentioned it.

Good bang for the lunch buck. Mussels were a little overcooked, chicken & green beans entree made up for it. Thai spicy wan't insane heat, so kick it up if you need to. Very friendly wait staff a plus.

Ethiopian, African, and Jamaican fusion. Excellent food! I've been twice, and this new location really adds to the experience of their food. I hope more people in the area expand their horizons and drop in, it will not be their last.

Loved it here. The staff are incredibly gracious and attentive. I had the Jerk chicken and it is no joke, lots of flavor, but even more heat. My wife had a wonderful Snapper dish. Both came with rice and salad. Just delicious. I can't leave out the Virgin Island Sunset. A really nice daiquiri that feels like you're on a beach somewhere. Loved everything.

So I'm in the middle of a five day trip down to this part of the country visiting family and hanging out. On the way back from a visit to some Dupont estate turned into a museum/horticultural center, I somehow wandered off course route 1 and end up in Media. I cruise around the block and stumble into this spot. Having not eaten really anything all day, I ordered the appetizer platter and my sister orders the Chicken Red Curry or something like that. I also ordered the fried squid. I always tend to order only appetizers at restaurants that I have never eaten before. Its a good way to gauge the food without taking too much of a chance. The chicken on a stick was ok, the fried spring rolls was'nt too bad and the couple of other items were all pretty good. The fried squid was somewhat above average, my sister was'nt too happy with her dish, I tasted it and it did seem a bit bland. The service was however very good, decor very soothing and it is nice and cozy.
We LOVE this place. We live 40 minutes away, but try to get here at least twice a year. Excellent food. Good service.

amazing. I got the vegetarian eggplant entree and my boyfriend got the lamb. I would eat this eggplant every night if I could. Very affordable and all entrees come with a delicious salad. Service is a little slow and bland but I don't mind slow service when it is BYOB!
This is our local go-to Vietnamese place. Delicious food and reasonably priced! Very friendly staff. If you check in, they give you a discount on the total bill.
The Creamiest Mango Lassi in town! Love it! I would give 5 Stars if they had Samosas, which they do have on the lunch buffet in Shalimar.

Looking at this place from the outside you wouldn't think much of it, but I'm sure glad I decided to give it a try. Their potstickers come in a pork or chicken and steamed or pan fried option. They're flavorful and a plentiful appetizer option. I decided to also try the spicy drunken noodles with chicken and it was also a massive portion for the price. The quality of the food was excellent and I think I found my new quick, go to place for my future Thai cravings.

Overall, this was a disappointment. The menu online indicated some items were gluten free which the menu on site did not. There were very few choices left which were gluten free and those I chose were very salty or underdone. I like Puerto Rican food but this was not somewhere I would go again.
The food is delicious. I would recommend the seafood linguini or the lamb shank. Everything was fresh and the staff was super attentive.

Everyone knows this place. No one knows its actual name, which is probably why I'm writing the first review for it. I guess everyone just calls it that "Vietnamese hoagie deli on Christian." The sandwiches here are absolutely delicious, and on one hand, I hope that lots of people go here so that the friendly owners can get rich, franchise out their place, and buy a nice set of rims. But at the same time, I hope they don't charge more than the $2.60 they currently charge, and I hope it never gets so popular that I have to wait in line to get my food. Can't have it both ways I guess.
I have eaten at baguette deli to many times to count. They are always fast, consistent, and the pho is delicious! My favorites are the beef/ shrimp spring rolls and the beef pho. You can't go wrong

the food is delicious! tastes fresh and perfectly spiced. nice owners, very friendly and accommodating. mostly takeout, but there are a few tables inside. the lamb special is very tender and the curry sauce is incredible! the palak paneer is very milky, creamy. you can taste the freshness of the spinach. not overcooked. fluffy rice. the flat bread (#1) is served hot.

This is my favorite place in Nashville to get the best Pho, Barbecue sandwiches and lemon soda. It is the cheapest and best tasting. Always helpful if you are not sure what to get, and I never have been disappointed in the quality of food. Love it!!
Love Zoe's! Everything always tastes amazing. Shout out to Bri who is always smiling and awesome at the Collegeville location!
Not suitable for vegetarians. Broth is either beef or chicken. They have a tofu stir fry and a few veggie appetizers, but the stir fry was bland and soggy. Good appetizers, though.

Came here several months ago on a Saturday for another restaurant in the area, but was attracted to the live music in the grassy area. Decided to eat at this place to enjoy the outdoor live music, even though it was a chilly night. First time eating jerk and loved that they had a number of options on their menu. Amount of food in the portion size was just right. Food was decent and a new flavor and experience for me. Juice was one of the best part of the meal, I think--absolutely fresh and real. Service was friendly and fast. Wasn't the cheapest place, even though everything felt like the neigborhood cheap eats for university student. Atmosphere was definitely more casual than what you paid for in food. Live music was great. The atmosphere really was alive because of it. I only wished that we were warned that the band had only 30 minutes left of their gig. Advice is to come earlier and try to make it for the outdoor live music. I think there was a small cover for BYOB, so I think I'll do that next time and enjoy the music of the talented band.

This place is delicious, affordable, (especially for the type of cuisine), and a really great new addition to this neighborhood. The people that work there are friendly and I would strongly recommend it. The Tikka Masala (both spice levels) and samosa's are tasty. The paneer pakora and naan (plain and the mozzarella) were also really good. Check it out and support local business!

If you want to broaden your dining experiences... Try something new.. This is the place!! The food is amazing.. The owner is so nice and will be glad to help you navigate an entirely new experience.. And!! The prices are sooo reasonable... Do your self a favor.. Give it a try

LOVE it. Reasonable prices, very friendly service, clean, beautiful atmosphere and the food is great! I get cravings for Thai food and Erawan has become my "go to place". I usually go by myself but I always think that Erawan would be a great place for larger group dining (I've seen bigger parties there and it seems like they're taken care of very well). The menu is big and definitely has something for everyone....vegetarians, meat lovers...whatever. I was also intrigued by the fact that they include a little survey to complete when presenting the bill. I get the sense that this isn't just lip service, but that they actually care about your satisfaction with your experience. I took the time to complete the survey, and upon returning with my change, the server very nicely thanked me for doing so and for the nice comments. I'm hooked! ...and BYOB!

This spot is right down the street from my house. We are talking walking distance here, and is my number one go to Pho in the city for taste and convenience. The quality is good and fresh. I usually take my chicken pho to go on rainy days for some home comfort. We get a lot of rain in the south so it happens frequently enough. The broth is good and not too salty which is easy to oversalt this dish, but not here.

Pho was delivered in locally-crafted ceramic bowls with generous fixings. The "fish and chips"-fried catfish, plantain chips, and green papaya salad was very good. There was homemade fish sauce on the table. Nice ambiance and great service.
I'm just passing through Indiana but I'm so happy I made time to stop here. I got the vegetarian pho and the tofu steak and it was absolutely delicious.
The food here is excellent and delivery is always prompt. They beat their time estimates by a lot most of the time. They have a lot of dishes you won't find elsewhere.

This is by far the best Indian restaurant I've ever been. They have a large variety of food and it all taste amazing. Highly recommend this place! This will be the only Indian food place in the area I will go for lunch!

Me and my boyfriend were here yesterday (Saturday) night, we had to wait about an hour. The staff were very nice, professional and courteous as thy checked us in and with others as what I observed during my hour wait. I even witnessed the manager help seat people and clean tables to help seat people faster. (Next time we will Make reservations we can make the same day and as little as an hour ahead). The manager sat us, told us she was the manager and if we had any problems to let her know. Our waitress was very very nice. It was very busy so the food did take a little long to come and I was a bit disappointed that my food was just warm and not hot but it was sooooo delicious and it was very busy so I over looked that. The waitress made suggestions on how to order the pepper steak as the one on the menu is spicy due to the pepper and it came out perfect and she was very pleasant to my request for more peppers. She suggested the fried banana appetizer with the pineapple coconut ice cream which my boyfriend loved! I had their cheesecake which was good but not as delicious as their food. Wish their was a pf Chang closer to me. Can't wait to go back again next month!
So yummy and fresh! Beautiful restaurant and decor. Quick and courteous staff. Our 10 year old picky eater loves it too. Best Thai I've had outside nyc

Wonderful food and you can beat the prices. My favorites are the spring rolls, banh mi (BBQ pork sandwich), and pho tia bo vien (rare steak and beef balls). Love that two people can feast like royalty for under $20.

We usually come here for the Pad Thai and Chicken wings, but today we came for dessert. It was our first try at their specialty shaved ice, typically we just order honeydew shaved ice no toppings, but today we were feeling adventurous. Kid #1 ordered the Romeo and Juliet which is milk shaved ice, Oreos, strawberries, chocolate syrup, strawberry syrup, and condensed milk. Kid #1's rating was a 4.5. Kid #2 ordered a custom shaved mango shaved ice with mango bursting boba. Kid #2's rating was a 5. So overall we give it a 4 star rating. This place is good and clean, but prepared when it gets busy it gets busy.
This place was good for what it is: cheap, ready to go Indian food. However still not the best and I prefer takeout from other places nearby.
I love this place! I moved her on July 1st 2015 and have been to Sam's five times already! Family came down to help with the move and they enjoyed the food, drink, people and atmosphere.

Good stuff!! I though NY (53rd and 6th) had the most amazing chicken/lamb rice, but after a recent trip, I think this Philly one is a close or even better one! I really appreciate the bigger chunks of lamb and chicken (as opposed to the minced up pieces in NY). And at $5 a plate (including a soda) you can't get a better deal than this. The food quantity is enough for more than a meal, that is if you can keep your hands off eating all of it at once!

Been here a couple of times. I like it. It's owned by a Pakistani fellow. So I suggested some south Indian type dishes every now and then (I'm a big Dosa, idli and Sambhar) fan and the clientele (both Indians and Westerners) will like it. Lets see if it works. For now, it's a great place for buffet.

Since we both commute to the Main Line, the manpiece and I meet up here after work sometimes to grab a quick bite to eat and evade particularly horrendous rush hour traffic on Rte. 76. So far, everything we have ordered has been incredible--especially Paneer Chilly and Chicken Chennai. And it doesn't get any better than sopping up the savory sauces with Pudina Paratha (whole wheat griddle bread stuffed with mint). I also highly recommend Rasmalai, a custardy rosewater-flavored treat, for dessert. Other reviewers commented about the prices being a bit steep, but it was only 30 for two people for the dinner menu. Plus, there's always plenty of leftovers for a second meal as well. You totally get your money's worth in terms of quality and quantity. A legitimate complaint, and the reason a star fell off of my review, is that the service could be better. The hostess/waitress isn't very attentive and at one point actually refilled our water while talking on the phone. At least we weren't parched? I don't know. It was very odd. The busboys keep you happy though. We don't live around there, but if you do, take advantage of the BYOB sitch and bring along some yummy wine.
Great food, indifferent service. Typically get the Babaganoush, hummus and shwarma. Had the fallafel recently - it was great too. The homemade pita bread is amazing. All the desserts are fresh.

Saw that new Vietnamese restaurant on Yelp so we decided to go try it on Sunday afternoon. There was no wait and we were seated right away. We order two pho, the portions was small for a bowl of pho that cost $10. Soup was lacked much flavor. It took about 10 minutes to bring one pho and took another 10 minutes to bring another pho to the table. Our witness was friendly. However, we were asked "how is everything" about ten times while we were eating there.

Queen of Sheba is a great place to go if you're looking for unique food. Ethiopian food is a mixture between Mediterranean food and Indian food - very flavorful - without being too spicy. What you should know before coming here. Sometimes a section of the restaurant is devoted to music and dancing. It's fun to watch. You can ask for a fork, but traditionally, you eat Ethiopian food with your hands. You are given injera - that tastes a lot like sourdough bread, and you pick up the food with the injera. (It looks like an ace bandage, but it tastes delicious). I have always gotten the Queens plate which is a mixture of the most common dishes. The more people you go with, the larger the selection, so I recommend a group. Check it out if you're looking for something outside of the ordinary.

Unfortunately I have to agree with many of the reviews posted here. I love pho and was hoping this could be my hometown go to. I actually thought the pho was decent, not great and not awful... but the level of cleanliness (or lack thereof) in this establishment made my fiancé finally say we were done here after a few visits. The service is bad, and our final visit saw every unoccupied table in the place full of dirty dishes. There was food on the floor, and the owner (who was obviously sick with a cold) sat behind the cash register loudly hacking, coughing and sucking snot as we ate. As stated before, were done here and won't return.
