Tiffin quietly expanded their menu a few weeks ago. This excellent Indian take out spot added a few new item, the most exciting being an arsenal of Indian inspired pizzas. Rachel and I ordered a few pies last night to try out the new offerings. The first pizza was topped with tandoori chicken, crushed red peppers and mozzarella. After a few bites, the spices and heat really kick in. This is a great pie. But I liked the second one even better. It was topped with grilled lamb and little cherry tomatoes. Again, the subtle spices on the meat really make this pizza shine. We also ordered two stuffed parathas. It's like a gourmet pancake filled with different vegetables. Although these were decent, they pailed next to the pizza. The only other part of the new menu includes wraps, and these don't seem too exciting. The pizzas are excellent, and with six different options, there's bound to be one to please almost everyone. We ordered more than a enough food and the total was $17 for the two of us. Seriously? These pizzas are awesome and $5? You have no reason to avoid Tiffin's new pizza. The worst part about all of this new stuff is finding the menu. Tiffin is great at Indian food, terrible at web design. Go on a scavenger hunt on their page to find the pizzas, or use this direct link for the menu :http://media.philly.com/documents/ETCMenu+v33-2.pdf. Essentials: 712 W. Girard (215) 925-0770 Avg Ent: 5-6 Cash only: No Reservations: No BYOB: Yes
I drive out of my way for this place. Great price, super value. I get the deluxe Gyro with avocado. Better in the summer as eating in the car is the only option when it is cold/raining!!

There's no denying that this restaurant's food is very good but the service is appalling. A colleague placed an order by phone. When we arrived to pick it up, the order was wrong. We asked if we could place an order for the item that was missed, the women simply told us that she would not cook for us and we could order that item next time. She also threatened to not let us buy the food we ordered. She repeatedly yelled at us that she would not cook for us and to order the dish next time. There will not be a next time.

CUSTOMER SEVICE IS HORRIBLE! I'm giving this place a 1 star...it actually deserves no stars but that's obviously not an option. We walked in, a waiter says "2? You can sit there or there" just pointing in two different directions with dirty tables. I asked if we could sit outside and all he did was point outside in a rude way. We sat outside for a good 5 mins until he came with silverware and menus. He just threw the menus and silverware at us and took off! We were under the impression that he didn't want to serve us so we got up and left. After that experience, I will never return there ever again! I would much rather go to zap noodle or thong phon. At least they're very friendly at both places.

a cup of coffee was $3.50! I ordered a cup some time ago and they put too much condensed milk and made it way too sweet. i ordered a small special order of pho and the price alone was $8.00. The broth was overly sweet and too salty. The owner inside is a nice man.
My boyfriend and i eat here 2-3 times a week! Service was great plus the ambience.. we love the food and me personally i love the shrimp tempura!
I'm not a pho expert but the food here is tasty.I have to have it at least once a week.

Came here for the first when I visited Carpinteria beach. About 4minutes walk from the beach. Ambiance- cute casual place. They have a nice little patio and indoor seating as well Parking-street parking Service- welcoming and was seated fast. waiter was very nice and wait was not too long. They did check on me few times to make sure I was satisfied and had everything I ordered :) overall quick and polite Food- 10/10 I ordered the spicy egg noodle combo meal which comes with choice of side soup or salad. Plate includes appetizer one spring roll, two wontons, and one shrimp egg roll, rice and choice of entree(chicken/beef/pork/tofu/vegetable) . I love Thai food and this place was traditional and pretty authentic Price-reasonable and believe we'll worth it for portion and quality of what you get Overall was very pleased. Good service,environment, food. Will definitely come back again!

Say what you will, but every time I leave this place, I dream about it until my next visit. The food is some of the most delectable morsels I have ever tasted in my life. I recommend the lentil sambusa for an appetizer. Trust me, you can't go wrong! Just be careful because they are always piping hot! As far as a main dish goes, order anything, anything at all because it is all good! The price is very reasonable. Two people can get super full for less than fourty bucks. The service is sometimes not the best, and that's why I'm only giving four stars. The servers are always friendly, just not always fast. If you have never been to Abyssinia or an Ethiopian restaurant, this is the perfect place to try something new and delicious!

Yah mon I cannot undersell this couple! They went above stellar in service. From the moment we walked in my friends were enamored with the place.I'm easy to please my friends are absolutely not. The yah mom "team" worked to present a fabulous array of Caribbean dishes that a novice like me appreciated. The place is white tablecloth, black and white decor, and cozy. I suggest you try the taste of the island, curry goat, and jerk wings!!! The moment you see the color of the wings you will know you are experiencing a great part of the "island." Wine and beer only and honestly would be the only reason I would give a 4.5. However, a 5 more than distinguishes them from the mundane comparisons out there.
This was my first visit to Etheopian restaurant. I ordered platter of 8 items. I liked each one of those. The bread was really good, too. If visit Tampa, I would definitely go here.

We were hesitant after reading some reviews. It was WONDERFUL from the service to the AMAZING food. The Bread was to die for and they kept refilling our basket. I requested a dish different than what was on the menu and they created it especially for me. It was unbelievably good. The service Superb and the Manager John came bu and checked our table twice to see if all was OK. We sat in the wine cellar and it was much more quiet than the 2 upper rooms. We will keep going back to this FINE establishment.

I live in downtown St Pete and I drive out of downtown area past all the restaraunts to eat here at Gateway. The quality of food you get here is off the charts. Everytime I went here the service has been incredible and I have tried something new to eat each time. Each time was better than the next!

Lovely open space with an enticing pastry cooler right up front. While I was super tempted by the caprese grilled cheese, a salad was in order that day. I chose the chicken chop salad w no chicken. (side rant: when you order salad with the most expensive ingredient removed, should you be charged the full price? No option of a non meat salad. Rant over) Dish was full of tomato, egg, bacon, blue cheese, olives and fried onions. It was well mixed and dressed in a tangy creamy dressing. I love when a salad is manageable with no huge lettuce pieces and this one was indeed that. Cute idea alert! Bittersweet offers a decorate your own cupcake option. They provide cupcake, sprinkles and pastry bag of icing for $5

Best Hyderabadi Biryani in the Western Phllly Suburbs. Indian Chinese is pretty decent, but more on the sweeter side than "Hyderabadi" spicy. Traditional South Indian fares like Dosas, Uthappas are pretty good. We go to the place at least once a week for the Hyderabadi Biryani. Decor has been updated in the last couple of months and looks pretty nice. Try it - you cannot go wrong with this place. Update 03/2013: Not the best biryani anymore. It's been more than 6 months since I even stepped inside. There is absolutely no consistency with their Chicken Biryani and their prices slowly started creeping up. Last I went there, I paid about $36 for 2 mediocre Chicken Biryanis. Yes, for TWO. They also charge 3% service fee on ALL orders. My new favorite is Biryani King down the road.

I give them two stars for the sandwichs. I ordered a couple and noticed they were a little thinned out. My coworkers joked with me and asked me if I was picking on the sandwichs bringing the order back. Wish I can tell them I was but I wasn't. The space is tiny. So be ready to order as soon as you step in the door.
Love this place!! Everything is delicious and fresh. Everything from pho to vermicelli to rolls! Amazing!!

This truck was like my gateway drug to all food trucks. I never knew how good food truck food could be until I had a bite of their Tilapia Burrito. I've tried all of their other tacos which are all delicious in their own way but I keep coming back to the Capn Crunch Tilapia. They will put this into two tacos if you ask them because the burrito can be unwieldy. Occasionally I will get the One and One if I'm looking for some variety. It's one of each of their other tacos. (Short rib and chicken satay if I'm not mistaken) The curry is okay too but I come for the tacos! The staff is friendly and willing to customize your order if you ask. The price point is pretty reasonable, on the low side if you compare it to some of the new gourmet food trucks. $6 gets you two tacos. Most dishes are $5-$7. The only cons are that the wait can be really long now that they're so popular, the location isn't great and they only accept cash. But these are minor details compared to the great food!

We celebrated my husband's birthday here. It's our third time and is a favorite! Everything is so flavorful and delicious. This is not your run of the mill Indian food. You must come and taste the difference. Everything is fresh and cooked to order. It was quite busy for a Tuesday evening yet the chef made his rounds to check on his dinner guests. Great ambiance and loved that it's a byob. We brought our margaritas and they provided margarita glasses- love it! Check it out, you will be delighted!

Amazing chai and amazing food. Definitely a must-try if you're in the area. There's ample seating for lots of people and I loved their robust tea offering. Food includes meat and vegan options so there's something for everyone!

The food was great and the staff was amazing. I had the Drunkin Noodle with chicken and my wife had the Pad Thai with pork. Both dishes were huge portions and delicious. The owner came out and talked to us about the different dishes they offer and made sure we were enjoying everything we ordered. Definitely coming back soon!

The hubs and I wandered in for dinner this past Friday, not sure if we were dressed appropriately in jeans and t-shirts but the friendly waitstaff didn't bat an eye. The atmosphere was calm and relaxing, with dim but not-too-dark-to-see lighting and soft love jazz.. The server was friendly and funny. For drinks, we decided on martinis with their house-stuffed blue cheese olives - omg, soooo good! We'd never had blue cheese paired with martinis before and I think we may now both be hooked. For dinner, we ordered the orange-glazed duck and the fish-of-the-day (Chilean sea bass) prepared tagine-style. Before it arrived, we enjoyed their complimentary garlic-and-herb olive oil and fresh bread, plus their salad with a sweet vinaigrette. Mmm! They brought more bread when we polished it off since the actual meal was still coming, so the wait was very comfortable and enjoyable. The entrees were delicious - both items tender and well-seasoned. We were very happy to take the leftovers back to our hotel!
Great food, and friendly service. Try the goat curry. It's so good. As are the homemade beef patties. I haven't had anything there that was not delicious.

Inside the decor is spartan, at best. I ordered the Clay Pot Fish, which sounded awesome. Instead I got about five pieces of fish floating around in a pool of straight oil, served of course in a metal bowl. No chilies or anything else, just oil. I couldn't even get to the minuscule amount of "sauce" for it was smothered 'neath the fish oil. My friend ordered the pho, which had to be sent back because it was cold. Apparently, we came in near closing time and they had shut the heater off that kept the broth hot. If that sounds delicious to you, this is your place. They serve Tsing Tao, and the waitress was friendly. That is what merits the second star.

It takes talent to make a concept like this work. A tiny converted gas station that's close enough to other trendy places, but really off on its own in a pretty bare area. Olio is dreamy. Like stepping into the Narnia of wine bars. We visited for happy hour on Valentine's Day and it was spot on with what I was looking for that night. We were lucky and snagged the last two bar seats. It gets cramped in the bar, but I found it to feel communal and not off-putting. Though that's a possible side effect of booze on an empty stomach. Our bartender was friendly, attentive despite the crowd, and extremely pretty (just telling it like it is). Fantastic beer, wine and cocktail selections. The menu looked great. We just did cheese, which was perfect, but I can't wait to try more. A couple of really nice touches: we ordered a bottle of Cantillon, and they let us know how long it had been chilling and to what temperature. Also, the Valentine's soundtrack was all 69 love songs by the Magnetic Fields. Huge win. It's clear that the owners know what they're doing. The whole staff was hospitable and knowledgeable. Thanks for a great start to Valentine's night, Olio!

Great pho but WORST SERVICE EVER. The waitress actually came and took my food before I was done, with about 1/3rd left. Didn't ask, just took our dishes. My friend tried to call her back but she ignored us and just kept walking. She was pretty cold and unfriendly before that, and didn't check with us at all while we ate, but that was the weirdest thing I have ever had happen at a restaurant. The pho was so good, great flavorful broth, but I won't be back. There are plenty of other places without rude staff. To the owner if you are reading this, it happened 6/26 at about 5:30. You may want to do something about her before she drives all your customers away.

The Husband and I went in around 1:30 for lunch, and we were the only people in the restaurant. That made sense since it was off-peak lunch rush and the place is still fairly knew. We were pretty impressed with the prices on the special lunch menu, which ranged from $5.95 to $8.95 for soup, salad and an entree. We did not get to choose the soup or salad. I don't know what the soup was called, since I couldn't find it on the menu. But it was like PA Dutch ham and green bean soup with spice, and tiny bits of pork instead of ham. It also had cabbage. I grew up in PA Dutch country, so I liked it. The Husband didn't. The salad was a rather bland pile of iceberg lettuce, a slice of cucumber and a slice of tomato - topped with ranch dressing, which we thought was a weird choice for a Thai restaurant. To drink, I ordered a Thai iced tea. It was perfect. (And yes, a restaurant can mess up Thai tea - just try the stuff at Tamarind on South Street in Philly.) The Husband ordered unsweetened iced tea to drink. And when he asked for sweetener, the waitress doled out a single packet of sugar. (He prefers the fake stuff.) When the waitress brought our drinks, I accidentally knocked my knife on the floor. I picked it up. But she did not offer or bring a replacement. For an appetizer, The Husband and I ordered the Mee Krob. We'd never had Mee Krob before, so we didn't know what to expect. (We had just watched the old "South Park" curse words episode, in which "Mee Krob" is a dirty word, and we were fascinated by the dish.) The appetizer wasn't the most visually appealing - a pile of crunchy noodles, soft chicken bits and a single shrimp covered in an orangey-pink sauce. We enjoyed our first few bites, but ultimately agreed it was way too sweet. For my entree, I ordered the Three Flavor Catfish. The menu describes it as "lightly floured, crisp fried, and served dancing in a three-flavor sauce." I think at least two of the three flavors were curry. It was hot! If you like curry, you'll love the catfish. I don't, but it was still pretty good. The Husband ordered the Pad Thai, since we evaluate all Thai restaurants on their Pad Thai. It was not the best Pad Thai ever (that award goes to Bangkok Wok in Mechanicsburg, with a second place to Chabaa Thai Bistro in Manayunk), nor was it the worst Pad Thai ever (that award goes to Nadia Thai in Lansdale - awful, awful stuff). It was just different. It was covered in an orangey-pink sauce that was a little spicier than what The Husband and I are used to having on Pad Thai. After we finished the entrees, the waitress brought our check without offering dessert. That's a big no-no. I always eat dessert. And any restaurant that fails to offer me one automatically loses a star. The menu didn't have any desserts listed, so we thought there might not be any. But we asked the waitress and they had only two. Thank goodness one was my favorite - mangoes with sticky rice. She came back a few minutes later with a big white plate of sticky rice shaped into a large flat heart and two big slices of mango cut into bite-sized bits. Mmmm... delicious. So, the meal was... you know... OK... not great... not awful... I might go there again, but it's not going to be my first choice.

This place has good food. But it's mass chaos everytime I'm in there. If you can deal with no order to anything happening, poor service, zero waiting area for pickup, and orders consistently being 15 minutes later than expected, this is the place for you. However with several other wonderful Vietnamese restaurants in the city, you don't have to subject yourself to the madness. UPDATED REVIEW: went from 2 to 1 stars. Ordered delivery through postmates. Driver showed up and had the wrong food. Not even close. The driver told me he double checked with the restaurant and they told him that was correct. I couldn't even follow my own advice and not order from here. Even though it's a Sunday and most other Vietnamese places are closed, do. not. do. it. I know you're thinking, "well if the food is good I can deal with crap service." No. I'm that person and even I can't deal with this level of consistent incompetence.

This is a pretty classic pho house. I wish it was located closer to me. (Why are all the good ones near Lafayette Square?) Pho is all about the broth. And the broth here has that nice savory richness without crossing over into the 'too salty' territory.

Being a creature of habit, I most often order the same thing at Thai restaurants, however, after doing some research, I decided I wanted to try some Issan-style Thai so I asked the lovely lady who seated us if they had a special "Thai" menu. She enthusiastically pointed to the menu on the table. I think she misunderstood and I said, "what I mean is a special menu from which Thais order" and she again pointed to the same menu. So, I further asked her if they did any Issan specialties that are not on the menu. She said "Laab" so that is what I ordered. "Laab" (sometimes "Larb") is an Issan-style meat salad, very pungent, usually spicy. My dining companion and I ordered the Tom Yum Kai (not on the menu), Laab (not on the menu), Som Tum, Pad See Ew (not on the menu) and Red Curry with Chicken, all ordered at native Thai spice level. I explained that we like our Thai really hot (native Thai hot). It was very, very hot and lovely, but not the incendiary spice-level for which we were looking. The Tom Yum Kai was exquisite and redolent with lemongrass and Kaffir lime leaf; the Som Tum, pungently sour with fish sauce, lime juice and dried Shrimp, and shredded green papaya. It was the perfect foil for the blazing Laab (ground chicken, lime juice, Thai bird chiles, red onions, cilantro on a bed of lettuce). The Pad See Ew was quite delicious, as was the Red Curry. Unfortunately, the red curry came topped with some of the ground chile powder instead of chopped Thai Bird chiles (which are truly incendiary). The taste, though, was fantastic. This is, without a doubt, the best Thai in Nashville.
Really great food! They are really helpful for first time visitors. They helped me choose a rice bowl that was delicious! We will be back. This is a great addition to the food options near IUPUI.

Best restaurant in Zephyrhills! The service is outstanding and the food divine. They spice their curry hot, so spicy means spicy - yum! A large selection of vegetarian options as well. Highly recommend you give it a try. My fiancé who doesn't normally like Indian even found something to enjoy.

Nice place. The restaurant is hidden a little bit, tucked away on a side street. It is worth searching out though. Chicken tikka masala was delicious. We went on my son's birthday and the owner/cook was nice enough to bring out a piece of cake for us. We did appreciate it. My wife had the lunch buffet and enjoyed it fully. Service was fast and friendly.
For me, the best restaurant in the area, best Indian food ever !!! Today the lemon rice was absolutely delicious !!!

I had never eaten at this place before, but I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone interested in getting some fantastic, authentic Caribbean food. The plantains were the best I have ever had including all my trips to many of the Caribbean islands. Andre, the host and server was terrific. He was the most friendly, nice and genuine people I have met in quite some time. I would come back just for the conversation and friendliness of Andre and his wife who are the owners. I HIGHLY recommend Yah Man!!!

I really enjoy this place! Small and cute. Everyone is always very helpful and friendly. I have personally only had their Pho which is very very good! I think I get a different kind every time. It is the perfect thing to get it you are feeling under the weather especially

Hunan chicken and/or beef with veggies were delicious. It's perfectly spiced. Szechuan and bourbon are also in our favorites. Their egg rolls are crispy and fried to perfection. Their pork fried rice is also very good.

The food was not very good. The Service was terrible! No extra service on water or tea. We told the server to separate the bill. We never received a bill for the dinner. We had to pay at the cashier. The cashier was rude toward us about the bill. We told her we didn't receive a bill and the bill was suppose to be separated. They didn't take credit cards or debit cards. So one of us had to go to a ATM machine to get cash. We paid our bill and the cashier yelled at us when we left in a very hostile tone in non English. Want be back ever. Terrible food and service and treated rudely!

The food was good and the waiter very friendly. For the money I'd prefer the first plate of rice to be free. My mango lassi was given to me warm on ice and it look a bit of stirring to chill it but once chilled it was my favorite mango lassi :) It's costs a dollar more to go from naan to garlic naan and it wasn't very garlicy. I was happy and would go back though.

My first time eating pho in Indiana and I'm very impressed. Service was fast and friendly. The waiter was always asking us if we needed anything. Food came out very quick and the pho and spring rolls were very fresh and delicious. Highly recommend, if I'm in the area will definitely stop again.

A friend and I went here and loved the sushi roll, chicken curry, and pad thai. I personally craved the chicken curry days after having it. The only issue was the service. I think they were short staffed, but we sat there for a while before someone came over. They also forgot to bring an appetizer.
Great ambience, ecclectic food selections, great service. Live music is the icing on the cake.
I signed up for yelp just to say how disappointed I was in this establishment. Thumbs down.

I had the PLEASURE of going there this evening for the first time with some family members. The food was excellent, they were ready to make changes to items so we got exactly what we wanted The food was supurb, the staff was very friendly and attentive. This was the 3rd dinner we'd gone out for this week and the most pleasant of the 3
Omg! Delish! Had to wait 30 minutes to be seated. Luckily, there was a bar across the street. Though tiny & crowded, very good food. Can't wait to return.
Love this place! The crispy duck is incredible! The service is a little slow, but definitely worth the wait!
Went for lunch yesterday. Nice selection. Good service. I would love to go back for breakfast !

Have been wanted to try this cute place since we moved here. We went last night for our 34th anniversary. Not a pleasant experience. Our waiter acted like he didn't want to be there, the food was super salty and it was expensive for the quality of food. Will not be going back...

I'm a vegetarian and Thai is always a good bet. The food was really good, though not cheap. I ordered the apple somtum salad and green curry with tofu. both very good. the atmosphere is lovely. I'm sorry we waited so long to try it, thanks to the middling reviews here. if you don't mind paying for it, you'll enjoy your meal. I'll go back soon!
I think Basil Spice is the best Thai in STL, this is our go to spot for Thai. We usually get the Pad Thai. All the vegetables and meats are fresh.

Are you in the mood for good food? Really awesome place, I like the the atmosphere, tastefully decorated interior, great choice of authentic Lebanese food, vines and beer. I was introduced to this place by my friend who happens to work there and would definitely recommend Soho Oasis for anyone as I know for a fact that the staff is very friendly :-)))

Solidly meh. The noodles were decent. The 'steak' seemed like the meat from a can of Dinty Moore beef stew. They also have one of those touch screen soda machines which means waiting in line behind technologically illiterate people who can't make up their mind and push a button properly. On a positive note, the staff were extremely friendly. I don't fault them for the food at all because I'm sure they prepared it exactly how their company wants them to, and I could tell by the great service and lovely presentation that they put work into it. It isn't their fault if their company hands them substandard ingredients to work with. I'd probably give this place three stars if it cost half as much, but for the $11 I spent on my bowl of noodles and 'steak' I'd honestly expect a bit better.

This is a zero rate restaurant. I went to this place on Sunday May 29 with my family. We had a big disappointment. The food is really gross. My husband had rice and ribs wich the meat turn to be at least 2 days old. I saw a octopus salad in the display that had bacteria grow in it( I know what I saw I wok in the lab). In top of that my husband got a piece of cake and it had mold. Authority of Philadelphia please check this place for the benefits of the community.

I happened to walk in without a reservation and was seated right away at one of the best tables, in a windowed corner overlooking the Delaware river. I wouldn't recommend this walk-in method, though. Most people I overheard talk say it gets busy and the owner said several times to callers that reservations were recommended. This place is BYOB if you want wine, which I didn't know, and was sorely missing from my meal. Certainly not their fault, nor mine since I'm not from around this area. I had an arugula and radicchio salad with shaved Parmesan and a lime vinaigrette. Beautiful presentation. I little heavy on the citrus, but otherwise a great tasting salad. For my main course, I had a med-rare Ahi over a bed capellini. There were sauteed grape tomatoes, green and black olives, pine nuts, and capers. Essentially, a slightly stepped up version of a picatta pasta dish. The Ahi was a perfect medium rare, although, for some reason the flavor was very flat; not the typically fresh and bright flavor of you tend to get with Ahi. This dish was rather disappointing. The portion was good and the dish was filling and ok, but far from impressive. For dessert I had chocolate mousse pie and a latte. The chocolate mousse was sublime! The chocolate was perfectly light and airy in both flavor and texture. It had a very atypical oreo cookie crust where the oreo was not the usual compressed crumbs, but rather like a thin, moist dough. The only complaint about the latte was that it was served in a stemmed glass which made it tough to hold, although it was a great compliment to the mousse. I would say that the waitress/owner needs to do a better job describing their menu, and more so with the specials. I overheard too many other tables ask about something and it was described as 'great' or 'really good.' A fish should be described by the firmness and flavor of it's flesh, the soup by what kind of base it is and what other flavors are pronounced or blended with other flavors or components. Other than that, the service was quite good; friendly and well timed.

place is shared with the subs place, inside the same mall area as cvs, convenient that you can buy something to drink at cvs and just drink it in the food court. Overpriced, smaller portions, cannot possibly be the best pho in reno. My pho was okay, a little bland but they advertise to be MSG free, so i can't complain too much if they were trying to be healthy. HORRIBLE service. I asked for an extra bowl and they said it might take awhile because they are so busy...........you can't take 10 seconds to bring out a bowl for me?? My friend got the chicken curry, no idea why he would get curry at a pho place, but it was the worse curry i have ever tasted, bland, watered down, rice tasted like it was out for 5 days. Extra star for them actually changing his dish after he complained... too expensive for what it is, if it was cheaper, i'd give it like 3 and half stars no doubt.

Delivery time was great! I would rather you have taken your time and packed my order correctly. Called the restaurant, did not want to bring the food they forgot. It was easier just to give credit for the missing food. Ok. Grubhub charges 5.99 for the incorrect delivery and you have to tip the driver. Grubhub- shame on you for the 5.99 you do not give to your driver's. Do not offer delivery if you cannot get that right. The food: Too much oil people! The oil is separating in the chicken tikka masala like crazy. This is supposed to be a creamy, tomato and onion gravy, not a container full of oil. The lamb biryani is soft and mushy. Again- too much oil. All the rice is clumping together like mush. Flavors just aren't there. A million Indian places a and I decided to give this place a chance. $60.00 is such a waste of MO eye for the food and service. Cross Culture is still the best for flavor, freshness and quality.

I gotta give my usual intro about having recently moved from Philly and really trying to find some reliable international food that doesn't cost twice what I'm used to paying. This place says it's Vietnamese and Chinese, but I ordered Thai. I'm usually wary of places that specialize in too many cuisines. I made a good choice, though. I had the panang curry. It was exactly what I wanted. It could have been a little spicier, but the sauce was good, the chicken was tender, the veggies were fresh, the rice was even exceptional compared to some Asian places I've tried in this town. I knocked off a star for price. $13 for chicken curry is just too much for me. But it's also less than I've seen on the menus of places I just refuse to go into, so I guess this is my spot for Thai at the moment.

Classy, cozy restaurant with EXCELLENT food and fast service! Try the coconut water served in an actual coconut. The jerk chicken and curried chicken was tender and juicy - fell right off the bone! We can't wait to visit this establishment again soon.

Curry chicken was delicious & the small platter was a huge portion! Was glad I went with small...it came with rice and choice of two sides. Very affordable. Everything was fresh and flavorful. Nice Jamaican spot with some unique beverages & bakery items too. Coworkers have raved about the bakery, I'll have to go for breakfast or dessert next time.
Had dinner with a group of 34 and the food was excellent and service was very good Did a real nice job with our large group. We would definitely return

We love this place! We do delivery from here a lot! Great service. Food, we think, best Chinese food around here. They always say 30-45 minutes. They are always here before the 30 minute mark. Just all around great place!!

I recently got to try Tryst for Sunday Brunch. I'll say if the review was solely on service it would definitely be 5 stars, but my food choice only rated at a 3 star so my overall review meets in the middle. We were planning to do a ferry ride over to St. Pete and tried to get a reservation for our group of 15 at various places around St. Pete to no avail. Tryst was the only place that returned my call when reaching out to make a reservation and was actually very accommodating to our request for such a large party on a Sunday afternoon. When we arrived we were promptly shown our entire reserved area out front and the staff was kind enough to even get the umbrellas set up so we would be shaded from the sun. Our server worked diligently to get our drink, food, and miscellaneous requests taken care of in a prompt and efficient manner throughout our entire 3 hour Sunday Funday outing. The 1/2 off bottles of Moet until 3pm were a huge hit for our group, especially with such a large crowd we were with. I ended up ordering the Chicken Panini off the menu and felt it was only decent for the price and how it was prepared. It felt more like a Starbucks ready made sandwich that was just reheated rather than a freshly made item. Next time I'd try something different as those who ordered burgers and various other brunch items were quite pleased with their selections. Overall, hats off to the Tryst staff for making this a pleasant group outing and being so accommodating.
The balls and the crabs are amazing! And the service! Amazing cocktails. Superb. Fabulous. Swell. All the rage, etc etc.
Grilled eggplant salad was very good. I certainly recomend the noodle dishes. Atmosphere is good, overall a nice place.
hands down- best place in the city! delicious! affordable! friendly service! I can't say enough good things about this place.

Half a block away from "Hatch and Coop," (see last review), but 50% more expensive. $6 fried chicken sandwich at Hatch and Coop. $9 fried chicken sandwich at Wishbone. Though Wishbone's sandwich was definitely worth $3 more, I could do with the cheaper version. Do NOT get the overpriced chicken wings. $8.95/lb...we bought 2 wings to try them out and the total cost of the wings themselves were $3.00. Bland wings are not worth $1.50 each.

I visited this place after getting off work. I stopped for gas at the 7-11 located next to the restaurant. I went in to get a to-go pho. I wanted to get #18, the seafood egg noodle soup, something I usually order at a Vietnamese restaurant. Unfortunately, they were missing an important ingredient or something because they couldn't serve it. I was fine with that because I didn't mind trying something new. The lady behind the counter suggested #1, Rare steak, Well-done flank, Fat brisket. I'm not picky so I went for it. Delicious. Flavor was great, meat was a little dry, but I usually don't order anything with steak in it, so don't take my opinion on that and try it yourself.. I was quite satisfied with it anyway :) I will definitely come again and possibly order to-go during my lunch breaks from work.

I loved the pahd see-ew, shaped linen napkins for lunch service, and lovely long-stemmed water glasses. I went here for lunch yesterday on the recommendation of a friend for good thai. I always order pahd see-ew everywhere I go, so the comparison between restaurants is of a comparable dish. The portion was very good; excellent meat to noodle and veg ratio. Nicely platted. Good sauce, well-matched spicy level as per my request. The ambiance is nice too. Very good stemware and plates. Excellent service. Nice touches abound in the service such as a cloth napkin tied around the water carafe to prevent drips. Good tasting tap ice water too, which is always nice.

I frequently order takeout from Simply Thai. I was craving a Drunken Noodle dish and was absolutely disappointed. They got my order wrong, initially they did not offer the large egg noodles and put the wrong meat in it. When I returned to get the dish I originally ordered, the noodles and meat were overcooked. This isn't the norm. Hope they figure out the problem.

Well decided to try this place again. Big disappointment. We ordered hummus and it tastes like Mexican bean dip. No flavor, no garlic-you can certainly get better tasting hummus at the grocery store. The calamari and spanakopita were good. When asked if we wanted more bread, we agreed but then found $2 extra charge in the bill. When I asked about the server said that's what it costed and I told him we should have been told. The service was poor beyond just this. I wanted a drink but the meal came before anyone came around to ask. I almost got up and went to the bar myself to get the drink. The server didn't bring the food out, never refilled the water we had. It was barely worth any tip but I left him something. Won't be back.

Really excited to see this restaurant join some of our other favorites in the 86th/Ditch corridor. We ordered the chicken makhanwala and palak paneer with regular naan. The portions were generous and we had plenty leftover to take home for lunch. We like spicy so we asked for it extra hot and it was just about right. The service was attentive. I really hope this place does well. I'm looking forward to trying some other dishes on subsequent visits.

BANH MI: FOUR STARS. Like I've mentioned in my previous review, I don't recommend getting anything with broth here unless you want to go into an MSG coma. I do, however, still highly suggest getting the banh mis to-go (well, you can only get them to-go anyway, sadly)! My boyfriend and I were close to the area again and got our banh mi fix. This time, we ordered the banh mi thit nguoi (regular banh mi with cold-cut deli meats), banh mi nem nuong (grilled pork patties banh mi), and of course the banh mi bi (shredded pork banh mi). The banh mi thit nguoi isn't all that great, but banh mi nem nuong and banh bi mi were good! Om nom nom nom. Bottom line: cheap and convenient banh mi in South Jersey!
Pad thai was delicious and service was excellent =)

Pretty good thai - only had the takeout on a busy week night. Pretty good though- curry is thick and they can make it really spicy. The serve a good dipping sauce with their spring rolls which are always hot and crunchy!

This is my go to Thai place and favorite comfort food. Nothing fancy. Just basic delicious ingredients and flavors. Crispy spring rolls and pad Thai are my kids favorite meal ever! Usually carry out, but dining in is always pleasant and there's never a wait. Owned by a very sweet family.
The gyro was delicious! Service was so great! The decor in the restaurant really makes it feel like you're at someone's house! So homey! Will definitely be back!

I had the chicken panang with Thai iced tea and boba. the Thai tea with boba was pretty good! chicken panang was okay, not quite as flavorful as I'd like (but I'm a salty eater). tried my cousins pad thai and didn't care for it. my other cousins said the banh mi was good so I got one to go. I'll update with banh mi later ^^

One of my favorite places to come for lunch. Food is prepared fresh to order, the restaurant is always clean and staff is always friendly and knowledgeable. We drive from Wesley Chapel at least twice a month if not more to eat lunch here. The menu has a wide variety of foods, from burgers to seafood. I absolutely love this place!

I have been to the lunch buffet several times and it certainly plentiful! I like the food but the service is lacking. We had a wait to be seated both visit and had to ask for our drinks to be refilled. Would have given it four stars if not for the empty glasses!

Went to Sam's on Friday 7/1 at sunset and the place was packed. I was pleasantly surprised to be told the wait would only be a few minutes. Under 5 minutes later we were sitting on the deck with a great view of the sun setting over the gulf! I enjoy a good Cuban and was shocked to find how amazing Sam's Cubans are! Also the pulled pork nachos were loaded with delicious smoked pulled pork, awesome!The thing that impressed most was how terrific the service was! All the servers were in top form for the holiday weekend crowd, a breath of fresh air in comparison to other nearby establishments. This is my first time back to Sam's in 2 years due to that experience being horrible. Thank you for turning things around Sam's!

I love this place and it ain't no lie. The pho mint combo is insane. The broth is sooo tasty. The banh mis are SO good with great crunchy veggies and crusty bread and the chargrilled pork MMMMMMMMM. even the kim chi burger surprises you with goodness. I am SO HAPPY you can get this deliciousness in a nice place, for not expensive prices. THANK YOU MINT my only maybe concern is that it cannnnn be inconsistent on a slow afternoon. I need y'all to be always consistent! Maybe once out of 12 visits I will get a stale bread or not-that-seasoned vermicelli.

What a suprise. I was pleasantly suprised by the quality of Jasmine Thai. Hidden away in a drab shopping plaza you would guess it was a shithole. The staff was quick and polite and the dining area was very clean and quiet. I had the green curry grouper and it will be a challenge not to order it again the next time i visit. I will definately be back.

This is my favorite restaurant so I'm kind of bias...I'm not sure how great the wait staff is because I always sit at the bar but the bartender Joseph is amazing! Mint has the best food and the best drinks...sticky chicken wings pork tacos pho banh mi burger rice dishes it's all great! So great I go on solo dates here...it's my go to place!

The food here is phenomenal. It's exciting, flavorful and quality. The service experience is strange. The waitress, while very polite, is over-eager to take your plates from you, despite many times being in a nearly empty restaurant. As another reviewer noted, they make you keep your silverware between courses. I've found over the years that most upscale restaurants will refresh your silverware. I don't know why other restaurants haven't caught onto this, because it indicates a higher level of service that people appreciate. I probably never will. I mostly get takeout from here. Despite going in once a week over the past 3 months, the woman there looks at me as if she's never seen me before. Again, very polite, but there might be a cultural nuance here I don't understand. Despite the bizarre attitude of the staff, I'll continue eating here because the food is out of this world.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Tired of pizza, pasta, or burgers? Try something different! Taj Mahal is one of those gems in the City of Boise that everyone needs to try. The owner was friendly and personable and the food was absolutely amazing. For the timid, try the buffet during the week. It'll give you a chance to sample the different cuisine they offer. For you curry lovers out there, try the buffet during the week. It'll give you a chance to pig out on all the amazing food they got without breaking the bank.

We used our groupon over the weekend and tried a bunch of dishes. We would definitely go back. It is a large restaurant that can accommodate big parties. Service was attentive and food came out at the right times. Apps - we had the duck rolls and coconut soup. The duck roll was wrapped in lettuce and then rice paper, it was not fried, and served with a dipping sauce. It was good. The coconut soup was good, what you would expect - sweet, coconut milk, mushrooms. For entrees we got the drunken noodles with veggie and tofu and the Holy Basil with beef. Both were very good. The drunken noodles had a medium spice. We had mango ice cream for dessert = yum! They are on opentable - yay. And they accept credit cards, except when you use groupon. And they are byo!
My favorite part of my dinner was definetely the home made mango juice. It was so delicious and fresh. The food was good, nice size portion. I bought a Groupon for $19 for $30 worth of food

This place rocks if you live in west Philly and want to casually amble across the street to get wasted cheaply and un-ignominiously. Bartenders are amicable and relatable. Citywide special is available and recommended. Late-night, bar is usually full of African people eating special food from the kitchen that others can't readily partake it. I was okay with this and enjoyed the jovial atmosphere of this sort-of-seedy bar.

So glad I tried this food truck out finally! I live right around the corner and decided to try this place today. Cheap and good sandwiches?? AND fast service? All possible thanks to Bui's. Sandwiches range from $4-$6. They have a menu, but really, you can just tell them what you'd like in a sandwich, and they would make it for you. I ordered the steak and eggs sandwich today with onions. My boyfriend got the pork roll, eggs, and cheese sandwich. The sandwiches are pretty big and filling. You can order with ketchup, salt, pepper, or Bui's sauce. Bui's sauce is a mixture of probably sirarcha and mayo. Tastes like spicy mayo really. Good stuff to top your sandwich with! The steak and eggs sandwich was great for what it is. Basic sandwich and simply delicious! Wish I added mushrooms to it! That would've made it a whole lot better. The pork roll and egg sandwich was probably my favorite from today though. We got Bui's sauce to go with it, and it complimented it pretty well. If you're in the area and want to grab something quick, cheap and good, definitely come to Bui's!
Best hidden secret in Nashville. This place has everything. Great food and great service. We probably eat here too much but we can't help ourselves!

I've had Naf Naf Grill multiple times, in Philly and even Chicago. I have always loved their food. I came here on a 3 pm and first used the bathroom, which was absolutely filthy. It almost made me want to leave, but I got food because I love it so much. This is a really dirty location, I saw flies buzzing around. The employees looked like they didn't care. The woman behind the counter could not care about cleanliness or presentation. I got the chicken salad bowl, and the chicken was overdone. I felt almost sick eating the meal. Super disappointed.

I'm not a big fan of mint but I still enjoyed the spring rolls. And the pho was a tad too spicy for me. BUT I recognize tasty food, and great customer service. They're definitely doing it right at Pho 36!

I was super excited to finally try Dmitri's-- we had the hummus to start and I have to say it was very lack luster and I thought it would have been great. The greek salad was great as well as my shrimp scampi, but everyone else's entrees left something to be desired . I will definitely give it another try, but we were certainly disappointed after hearing so many wonderful things.
We were in Jamaica a yr ago so have a little idea of good jerk, this was top notch jerk! Very simple setup but the spicy chicken made up for that.

Got some delivery it was pretty good and only took about 35 minutes which was 10 minutes faster than they said. I will order here again. Had the Shrimp pad Thai , crispy shrimp rolls, chicken skewers, and panang curry beef with white rice all were good.

Food was fresh. Huge menu. Very authentic. Some things were a little too authentic for us. We were able to try several dishes because we had a family of five. The girls were a little less enchanted by the food than the rest of us. Surprisingly large building. I think it used to be a Bob Evans. Kind of strange.
Very good vegetarian options. Very generous host. Well priced .have a nice gift shop too :)

Just had an excellent very late lunch here. Ordered the combo hot pot and it was delicious. Had plenty of pork, chicken, shrimp, and tofu. Even the tofu was very tasty. Vegetables, a plenty, even enough to satisfy me. The only thing that could've made it any better would have been brown rice instead of white, there was no choice and a warm plate that the rice came on. The hot pot itself was still bubbling as it was put on the table and I really appreciated that. It was in a heavy ceramic dish that stayed hot throughout the meal. I would definitely come back here to try a different selection. Today, seven months after my original review, I tried San Francisco kitchen again. It is still good, possibly great! This time I was there again in the late afternoon and they were much more busy than they were the last time I was there. Today I tried one of their lunch specials which is a hot dish paired with either white rice or fried rice and it includes a couple of the daily soup. Today's soup was hot and sour and it was full of goodies, Bean sprouts, tofu and something crunchy that I did not recognize. The soup was served so hot that I set it aside and begin immediately on my main dish and rice. I had mixed vegetables with shrimp and there was a good mixture of vegetables including fresh carrots and fresh Broccoli. The fried rice was somewhat mundane and I am still waiting for them to add brown rice to their menu. I had the Thai iced tea but I will try not to order that again as I felt like if it was not a caned mix it was too similar to some that I have had in the past. This place remain safe favorite Chinese-Vietnamese restaurant for me. See my empty plate photo elsewhere on yelp.

This is my utmost favorite spot for Pho! I've been too many times to count. I love the manager and her staff. I've gone so much they know my entire family even when I don't go with them. The manager knows my order when ever I get there. I just love the customer service. They really cater to our needs. Now for the food....DELISH!!!! The spring rolls are bomb and the fried egg rolls are great too. I've had The vermicelli lemon chicken bowl and it was very fresh. The Pho is phenomenal! Great taste and the fixings are always fresh. I usually get the #60 in Pho. I think it's brisket and eye of round. Sometimes I add grilled shrimp to it. Add grill shrimp to anything here only makes it better. The jasmine tea is amazing. I have yet to try the Pho Challenge, it looks fun. I've actually seen someone try to eat a large bowl, but I don't think they succeeded. It was very entertaining.

Great food, great service, great price! Amazing quality and it is fast food. I had a falafel wrap with a side of chop salad instead of the fries. I wish they had one of these in Miami, I would be a frequent customer! Loved the baklava too!
Recommend. We showed up late and they were having a private party. The owners made us welcome, sat us and fed us well. Even though I think they were closed:) Enjoyed the food. Recommend

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: I am a nut for Thai cuisine, and I have tried every one in Reno. This is hands down the #1 Thai restaurant in Reno for flavor, ambiance, and staff. What more can I say? If you are in Reno and want a wonderful Thai dinner in a lovely environment, this is the place.

This Resturant was one of my favorites. It has so many veggie options that I love. I am not a big meat eater but my favorite thing here (besides the lentil soup) is the chicken kabob. The chutney and dressing for the salad is amazing. And the bread comes out warm and is worth every carb. Highly recommend. Can't wait to come back.

This place was really good. Calamari was spicy, but perfectly spicy. My wife and I got the pork banh mi and pad thai - both were delicious. The fries are killer, and I'd definitely get them again. Great drinks too! Loved the smoked manhattan.

I like coming here for lunch because it isn't as busy in the afternoon. Love the coconuts, decent price too. Can't say much about the pho, I don't eat that much, but the fried rice is good, and the servers are always friendly.
Wonderful Middle Eastern food, worth the trip! Great Middle Eastern grocery as well, all authentic. Fresh meat to take home too.

First time here. Visiting Nola! Service was pretty spotty. We had to ask the server for our iced coffee like 4 times and they kept saying it was still dripping? I'm sure we waited about 15-20 minutes. I wish I had something more exciting to say. The pho was pretty average. Tasty but not the best I've ever had. If I lived in Nola I would definitely come back. Just had the pho and a few appetizers. The egg rolls were good. They shrimp and avocado fresh rolls were tasty and fresh. The pho was actually a pretty nice portion. I wish I would had more room to try their dessert
Awesome food and awesome service! It's like going to place where everyone knows your name! Cheers!
Amazing Indian buffet -- tasty, fresh, healthy, and affordable. Plus, everyone's really nice and the food is incredibly consistent. Don't miss it!

Lena was a wonderful host during the whole meal. She gave helpful advice about which meal i should order. The appetizers were absolutely delicious, hot, and came out super fast! We tried the crab rangoons, sticky chicken, and beef tacos. I would definitely order everything again. For my meal i got the steak and eggs which was the perfect amount of food and was delicious. I would def come here again!

Way too expensive for cart food, the guy is sometimes annoying and hard to understand, it stinks the whole block up with garlic smell, you have no idea what he's putting in your platter or sandwich, the line moves slower than a glacier, and it's the best food in the city. Someone once asked me since I love it so much if it would be my death row meal and my reply was if I'm on death row it's probably because I killed someone for standing between me and this falafel.

Let me start by saying that I don't know much about Indian Food or it's authenticity. Just going strictly by taste. Food tasted great. Plenty of variety. Restaurant was nice and clean. A little on the pricey side for a buffet, but I guess that's to be expected for a non-Chinese buffet. Also, it's BYOB. What's even better is that there is a liquor store right next store.
Food doesn't seem to be on par with the ones out in AZ, but between grief and nothing...

We stumbled upon this restaurant in its new location on Gay Street right after it opened. The menu, service, and food was just about as perfect as it could be. The mussels in red sauce were unforgettable. The decor creates a fresh, lovely atmosphere. I love having a good Italian alternative to the sardine-can crowded atmosphere at Limoncello's.

I had never eaten Indonesian food before coming to Sky Cafe for the first time a couple years ago. Check it out. Delicious, fresh food and quick, friendly service. Hands down, my favorite thing to eat here is the house salad (lettuce, cucumber, bean sprouts, fried tofu w/ peanut dressing). Other favorites include the coconut rice with a tea egg and the fried wontons. Iced coffee is also perfect. Great little BYOB and worth the trek from N. Philly every time. Love you forever, Sky Cafe.
What stood out in the pho for me was the firmness/texture of the noodles, I felt like I was eating high quality ramen something I have never experience in a bowl of pho before!

Delicious Jamaican jerk chicken and curry goat! The stir fry vegetables, however, were overdone. This is one of the places in the Farmers' Market next to Mom's in the Rosemont shopping center. It is a nice selection of restaurants, including Margaret Kuo's. After your jerk chicken, checkout Le Bus, Bella Oliva for quality olive oils and vinegars, and the cheese shop with its excellent selections across the aisle. And the sushi place nearby is very nice too. Admittedly, there is little or no ambiance. The market needs to make the eating area less stark. But this is an upscale food court that is worth exploring.
Exceptional service, terrible food. Sodium loaded, not "grilled to perfection". Even the naan tasted like I was licking a salt block.

So I've never been a major fan of Indian food as I'm not a big curry fan, I was convinced by family and friends to try it and was pleasantly surprised. I even took my daughters left overs to work the next day

I thought I was going to a nice restaurant for a fine dining experience. I was sooooo wrong. The waiter who also seemed to be the bartender would be better suited in a sports bar, he was loud and abrupt. He kept interrupting me after he would ask me a question and then he just walked away in the middle of me talking to him. I had the pork chop which was blah and the mashed potatoes tasted like they were made with water rather than cream or milk. I was there two years ago and it was an amazing experience but after this, I will never go back.
The food was great. However, the drinks are watered down. Must try the Deluxe hummus platter, it was simply amazing.

Great pho, TERRIBLE service. If you're busy, respond by being nice, not acting like a surly douchebag. My partner and my son had been here before and thought it was pretty good. The last time, it was a bit busy so we decided to try to seat ourselves. We were told by some angry guy that the area we were going to was closed. That's fine. We walked back to the bar to wait and we were utterly ignored for 15 minutes. I finally mentioned to Mr. Angry that we could go somewhere else, and that seemed to please him a great deal. And so we will, always, given that there are three other fantastic--and friendly--pho places within walking distance. Update: +2 for the manager taking the time to contact me and apologize for his employee's appallingly inappropriate behavior. He was even nice enough to offer me a gift certificate, but I have a job and I'm not looking for free food--I'm specifically looking for a positive experience in a restaurant, particularly when I'm starving, have already dealt with parking, and have my young son in tow.

More vegetarian / vegan options than any other Vietnamese restaurant I've been to in Tucson. AND, they have veg. ban mai! The prices are reasonable. The seating area is clean. I always get my food to go because the atmosphere is pretty dull in there but the food is good :)

I had almost given up on this place. I've driven by it, I've stopped on days I thought it would be open - but it must have been closed for a holiday, For what ever reason, I've had a horrible time getting in to the Little Thai Cafe. Tonight, though, we saw that it was open, so after the last push of Christmas shopping, we decided TONIGHT's the NIGHT! I'm glad we were able to get in, while the decor is not at all like the other Thai places in the area - no rich woods, not many statues, no familiar altar- it was comfortable. The place smelled AMAZING. We were seated almost immediately and offered drinks. I chose my favorite, Jasmine hot tea and it was -the absolute best- hot jasmine tea I've ever drank, it smelled of pikake blossom. We ordered the fresh spring rolls and chicken satay for starters and they were both the epitome of fresh. The flavours of the herbs and the curry just jumped out on the tongue. Our mains were a Amazing Thai Chicken for me and the husbeast got a Thai Noodle soup with beef - thai hot. (He always does that, and I always laugh because he ends up crying and sweating, it's SO very funny to watch. ;) The flavours were both bright with garlic and cilantro, mine was light and crispy, the chicken was especially delicate. It is certainly a place that we will want to visit again.
This Indian place was good. The food was good the service was good. I would say the portions could be bigger. Be careful you are going to the right location. I think they moved recently.
Nice and clean Vietnamese restaurant. The staff was friendly. I ordered the Pho #2. The meat was nice and tender. I really enjoyed the Iced Coffee!

The food is usually pretty good. I love the chana batura and dosas but everything else is just okay. My biggest gripe is the recent price increase. A onion rava masala dosa is $10.99. That is absurd. On top of that it's a 12% service fee. Chana batura was $8.95 and an extra batura was $4.00. I guess go if you must but be prepared to pay through the nose.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia. The food comes out fast, it is inexpensive, and I like the diversity of the cuisines they offer. At this point I have eaten about eight different dishes here, and nothing was bad. The roti canai appetizer is absolutely delicious and can actually serve as an entree for those who are not big eaters. I also really like the Malaysian and Indian chili chicken, as well as most of the Burmese options.
Great Vietnamese with great ingredients. The service team is really in tune to their regular clientele.

Tryst is a hidden gem in DTSP. It is a great place to have a drink and enjoy great food. The outdoor sitting is always happening. You can see interesting characters walking by or just simply enjoy sitting inside at the bar. The inside decorations overwhelmed me, but if you get past that, you can find a great selection of craft beers, full liquor bar and great food. What is else can you ask for? If you go, ask for a Logan special...

I really hope that the other people who left good reviews for this place were paid to, because this was literally the worst meal I have ever had in my life. That is not an exaggeration, and I've been to more than one third world country. I ordered the duck noodle soup, which is a pretty difficult thing to ruin. Yet, it was bad enough that I ended up taking the noodles out of the soup, putting them on my plate, and drowning them with sriracha. They were still disgusting. I've had ramen noodles with Frank's hot sauce on them that tasted better. Legally, I don't think I can or should say that what was labeled as duck was cat. However, when I smelled the meat in my duck soup it smelled suspicously like what my cat smells like. Sadly, the "duck" was still the best component of the dish. If you want vietnamese food, I implore you to take the extra half hour drive into Philadelphia's Chinatown where you will find several excellent establishments. Seriously, don't eat here.

The Pho (with chicken) was delicious and fresh with sides of cilantro, mint and sprouts. We also had a spicy clay bowl, scrumptious spring rolls and Duong Chau Fried Rice. The service was friendly and quick and the prices were good. We can't wait to go back again (Westtown Location).

Don't be scared of the market set up - EAT HERE! It's worth the 40 minute drive for us...so that's sayin something! You really should order the lamb gorma and the onion naan and DIP it! So good! The sauces they served with our fried vegetable appetizer were also really great. Very nicely seasoned. The gulab jamun was cool because it was unlike any dessert we've ever had and it was a nice light way to end the meal, plus it left us with fresh breath! Next time we'll try more food - and there WILL be a next time! Yum! PS: We were the 1st ones in there and the server was very attentive. Then the place filled up and people started ordering at the counter and seating themselves....so just go with the flow. If it's busy - grab a table and send someone to the counter with your order. Otherwise, sit down, relax and enjoy!

Thai Country Cafe is definitely a great place for Thai food. As a tourist I was a little bit confused as to which Thai food restaurant was better on Delmar but since they are all owned by the same family you can't go wrong. I ordered the chicken fried rice (Number 19) to go and it was good. I wish that they had given me some extra soy sauce to go but it was still yummy. With tax it was $9.80 and the portion size was great! Overall it's a quality place.

Horrible horrible horrible food. So I chose to order from the menu than to do the buffet. $15 later I was horribly disappointed. The tandoori chicken was fried, tasted stale and nothing like tandoori chicken. The lamb vindaloo was just as horrible. Tasted like steamed beef in some nasty sauce. Total waste of money. Crap. Will never go back. Oh you have to pay $2 extra for rice that goes with the vindaloo. Couldn't eat more than a bite.

I'm very picky when it comes to Greek food since I've been and had the real thing in Greece. But i must say this place is pretty close to the flavor I've been craving. Fresh and made to order. Friendly staff. The environment is relaxing.

Outstanding pho at a great price. What more can you ask for? I will say the cocktail menu could use some modernizing - the drink options seemed kind of cheesy. But I know this is not a "mixology bar," and that's cool. Note they do have two large TVs at the bar, and show sports. That's a plus in my book, but not everyone is looking for that in their fine dining experience.

Sooooooooooo good. I can't imagine anything more comforting than sitting in PJs after work eating take out Indian food. Chicken curry & malai kofta were delicious, flavorful, and appropriately spicy! They had the orders ready in like 15 min. I'm usually a woman of too many words, but there's not much else to say on this one. Delicious.

I'm sure someone likes it... But not me! I spent $13 on a dinner and didn't even finish it - that's saying something because I love food, I love eating and I don't like wasting food. They seem to be trying too hard to have unique recipes. I did not enjoy their tough fried chicken and the mac and cheese was just disgusting. Also, I was put off by the fact that rap music was playing so loud that you couldn't have a conversation about their somewhat confusing ordering system.

This place is improving. Came back for another try. This time I dined in instead and ordered the bo ne, pho, and torpedo shrimp. The pho and bo ne was delicious. Their homemade bread was to die for! Torpedo shrimp was alright. I just wish they add a little bit more cream cheese to it. Overall, I was happy with my visit.

Best dinner we have had in a long, long time. Very attentive wait staff, lovely ambiance, and it was an overall outstanding birthday dinner for my husband! We started with the fried calamari. They were crisp with delicious breading and wonderful sauce....they were not rubbery at all!!! My husband ordered the Caesar salad, which he enjoyed, and I ordered the spinach salad with dried cranberries, candied walnuts, and gorgonzola cheese.....wonderful! My husband enjoyed his New York strip steak, which was cooked to his specifications and the perfect temperature ( it was served with some yummy mashed potatoes). I ordered Veal Picatta, which came with some flavorful sauteed zucchini, and I have to say the sauce was so good I could have eaten it with a spoon!!! The veal was so tender that I could cut it with my fork....just perfect! Even the bread they served was tasty ( I think it had olives in it, like the restaurant's name). Al in all, we could not have had a better dining experience. I bought a Groupon so we could try this place, and we will go back soon!

We love Bangkokville! My husband lived in Thailand during his high school years, and he is very picky about Thai food. He loves their curry, and especially the sticky rice and mango. I love the Thai noodle soup, which is basically like pho without a strong anise flavor - loaded with beef, unlike what you sometimes get at other pho restaurants. Yumm!

Damm good Indian food. IMHO, far better than the Indian places around downtown & University City Philly, which are the places I'm used to in the last 13 years or so(Minar Palace, Passage to India, Karma, Tandoor India, New Delhi.) The only thing I didn't like was the price was $13.95 pp for lunch on Saturday, instead of $8.95 as during the week, which we didn't know until we stood at the cashier reviewing the bill, when we noticed the price in very small fine print below the main price listing.

I also tried Pho King on the strength of yelp reviews, because I do love Vietnamese food but I've had definite mixed results trying restaurants in the area. Very happy with the food, very happy with the price, very happy with the service. My boyfriend enjoyed his lesson in how to drink Vietnamese Coffee, and we both really enjoyed the relaxed, genuine friendliness that can be a hall mark of area businesses (yeah, that's hit and miss too, but when you find it it's pretty sweet). Point deducted because they could swing the mop a bit harder, but eh, I have an old place myself and know full well how you can spend a day sterilizing the place and have it still look grungy and smell old, so if I could do half stars I might have been more generous with that benefit of the doubt in mind. The food was fresh and the plates were clean, after all - I wasn't eating on the floor anyway.
Amazing crispy duck! Great service, perfect environment. This is the best Thai spot in the area. Byob and for a bottle charge they will chill and serve.
Since this was the first Korean restaurant I have tried I have nothing to compare it too. I like the beef and the chicken and there is an appetizer that is like a sushi roll that I like.

Alicia F loves this place. I adore Alicia F. Therefore, I was destined to like this place even before I ate here. And luckily, it was pretty damn good. We lunched it up here and started with the crab wontons - uhhh, amazing! My bff then sold me on the Singapore Street noodles (as did the waiter, who was super sweet and said "gracias" every time he put something on the table). Those noodles were yummy, and I have enough leftovers for two more meals. I'm not the world's biggest fan of Chinese food but this place might make a believer out of me. Who would have thought that my life would be altered forever at the Plymouth Meeting Mall (not me, that's for damn sure!)?

Amazing amazing food! I have been here twice and every time I have seen variety of food. The most famous stuff is THE BIRYANI - out of this world, slow cooked, with lot of flavors infused, and perfect. I love their Appam's with coconut milk. Never found these in US before. They also have indo-chinise options. Service is great too. I highly recommend this restaurant and weekends/Fridays are the best days to get most varieties.
This place is so incredibly good!! The owners are great and the food is amazing!!! Just go! Dinner is the best time to go! Well priced and byob. Perfect!!

Really delicious food, glad I was able to give it a try! My only concern was with the waiter we had.. I had just spent roughly 13 hours at the hospital with my mother, so afterwards my boyfriend & I wanted something besides fast food. We landed here around 9:10p. I understand coming in just after 9 when you're closing at 10 isn't ideal but it's part of the job. I just expected to be seated at an already set table, not one by the bathroom with nothing on it, waiting for the waiter to bring things over and half-a** set up with us already sitting down. This looked like a classier place than that. Throughout the night he just seemed more annoyed with having to serve us than anything. Then he argued with the table next to us because the guy wanted iced tea but the waiter claimed he just asked for regular tea. Eventually the woman who was working had to take over because it was clear he wasn't doing well. She was incredibly pleasant and attentive, and the main reason why I'm giving 4 instead of 3 stars. Give this place a try. It's a beautiful restaurant with wonderful food. Just don't come in too late.

This was an excellent place for pho and the prices were great. I got a huge bowl of broth, and all the trimmings for $7. The restaurant is very out dated with old metal chairs and plastic tables and the parking area is pretty dirty. The service is also slow, as it took over 20 min to get the check.would recommend for cost effective authentic pho but not for ambience.

Upon walking into Shere Punjab, you get hit with the wonderful aromas of Indian spices, and if you're an Indian food fan, your stomach is going to start rumbling. Prepare to get your eatin' on. As for what dishes to choose, I have to say my top dish is Tikka Masala...and I believe all of Great Britain can also agree. Apparently it's the national dish of England, and it very well deserves to be. The sauce is a creamy tomato-based curry that also has bits of coriander (aka cilantro) in it. I like it with chicken or lamb. This was my gateway drug to Indian food, and I've never gotten over it. Eat it with some garlic naan (fluffy Indian flatbread); you won't be disappointed. For those of you who are a bit hesitant about diving right into Indian food, I suggest trying out their lunch buffet. For $9 or so, you can try 5-6 different dishes with rice, naan, vegetables, and yummy appetizers such as samosas. PLUS, it's all-you-can-eat. Go back for seconds...thirds...fourths... Also, don't forget to try their desserts: sweet, syrupy doughnut holes called gulab jamun and their rice pudding called kheer. I eat them together in the same dish. The sweetness of the gulab jamun is tempered by the light flavors of the kheer. Absolutely delightful! The best way to eat at Shere Punjab? With friends/family and eat your dishes family-style. You can have some of my Tikka Masala...because I want some of your Korma. Food always tastes better when you're eating in good company. Shere Punjab is my favorite Indian food place here in town. I went there tonight for some take-out and their dining hall was almost full...on a Monday night! It warms my heart when I see our local gems staying busy.

The chai was absolute perfection, and this place is great to grab a beverage to go. I do like that there are options for every diet type. We ended up waiting literally a full twenty minutes for a bagel with cream cheese. Many people who came after us got their food first. When I approached a staff member, she assured me that the bagels are made authentically (aka, toasted) so they take longer than the regular dishes, which are merely microwaved (gross). I mentioned to her that I understood, but that I thought 15-20 minutes was a little excessive to wait for a bagel. She said it was because there was a rush. I feel like a plain bagel with cream cheese should not take more than 10 minutes (max) so I was disappointed. After asking her to look into it, it still took an additional 10 minutes. I was already finished my chai by the time the bagel came. Not wowed.
This place was fantastic! LOVE the low-fi, authentic ambiance, the terrific Dominican food, and the very friendly staff. We will return when we go back to Philly!

We went last night for UC Dining Days and Vientiane was terrific. A lot of restaurants slack off for Dining Days, which I always think is a big mistake. It's a great opportunity for restaurants to lure you in, which Vientiane did! They had great choices on the pre-fixe menu. The food was terrific and the service was very good. Great local byob. Can't wait to go back!

Can't believe I lived so close to this place and never went there. Ordered the special with the gizzards and fries combo. Was the bomb will be coming back just for that and the drive through is super convenient.

omg! I found this amazing restaurant on google when I was craving Thai food! Boyyy do I love google! My favorite restaurant! It's perfect! I usually always get the green or yellow curry with salmon or tofu or both. So delicious. The best coconut soup is made here! I haven't ordered a dish here that I would rate less than 5 stars. Only downside is that I've gained 10 pounds because I just can't stay away!
MY favorite place for India cuisine. I love love love lamb korma and the curry pumpkin is a great side dish for sure! I have never had anything here I did not like.

I was pleasantly surprised that Reno had Indian restaurants when I moved here 11 years ago. Discovered A Taste of India six or seven years ago and it has become my favorite of the two others (that I know of June 2010). Not because the food is any better as it is on par with the other two however it is easier to get to as it is on Moana and not buried down somewhere on South Virginia. A Taste of India has been through three different owners since I've been going. While Indian and Thai are my favorite cuisines and I will sample them at almost any opportunity, I've stopped eating Indian in Reno. I've just been unimpressed. Seems as all three serve "diner' Indian - it just lacks pizazz. None of the flavors stand out except for the salt. :-( I thought A Taste of India was good Indian until I had some truly amazing Indian at two different locations in New Haven, CT. On the bright side, the lunch buffet with a soda comes out to $9.00 which includes hot/warm, if not fresh, naan. Limited soups at the buffet. For better or for worse, the same dishes are prepared by the day. Chicken Tikka Masala appears to be a Wednesday hit. It has been six months since I've been to A Taste of India before going in today. The good news is that it seems as though the various tastes were beginning to stand out. Not enough to warrant four stars but more than three stars. If I need an Indian fix while in Reno, I will go back to A Taste of India again someday. Meanwhile, I'll cook Indian at home.

Really nice place! I got a living social offer... I was a little sceptical because the place was almost empty when we came in, though it started to fill in very quick. It's a really nice place, quiet atmosphere, the food was amazing! I ordered Indian food because I never tried it before, and I was NOT disappointed, everything was simply delicious. Also a big plus is that it is BYOB!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I never miss a chance to visit this restaurant when I travel to Boise. I do not eat a wide variety of Indian food, but the Chicken Tikka Masala and butter naan is usually great. The owner is friendly and kind. It seems as though the food and friendly service has earned them repeat customers (from the conversations I overhear). I would give five stars, but I think they have changed a number of recipes and not for the better. Their naan used to be thick and soft. Now I t is quite thin and crunchy, to the point of being like a saltine cracker. The chicken tikka masala was not as good as the last half dozen times. It seemed to rely more heavily on chili powder to add spice (I asked for it to be "medium"). It lost the creaminess that I enjoy. Nonetheless, I will continue to eat here.
I havent quite decided where my favorite Banh Mi spot is just yet in the city but Nhu Y is definitely my fave for their vegetarian one.

I was in Nashville for the Eclipse and decide to explore the popular area of Broadway St. I wanted something different from the Southern food and quiet, also the waiting for the other restaurants was an hour minimum. So when I saw this place I was excited because the middle eastern food is one of my favorites. There were a couple in the front with hookah and another inside dinning. This would be a warning for me but I didn't care because I was tired and hungry. The bottom line for this place is that they include in the check 20% of gratuity.
