I wouldn't care but the food is with no flavor at all. The check came with a line for the tip, if I hadn't pay attention I'd finished paying 40% of gratuity.

It's been awhile since I've been to a Thai restaurant, the last being my visit to Boualouang over a year ago. So when Jessica mentioned that we should go eat Thai at Numchok Wilai on 124 St, I was pretty excited for our dinner date! I blame Joe for his "peanut allergy" and my fear that even a little could kill him, even though in reality it's just a sensitivity. I'm just making excuses really... I don't know why I haven't been to a Thai restaurant in so long. I didn't dwell too much on interior this time, it was more about the company and the massive amounts of food I was about to eat. But the restaurant was pretty filled when we ate on a Thursday night. By the time we ended dinner, the restaurant had completely cleared which left me with (attached) photo. My boss mentioned that he loved Whyte Ave's King & I spring rolls and wondered how Numchok Wilai compared. I had never been to either, so I couldn't really do so but I convinced Jessica to try it with me. I use the word "convinced" because I think it's rare that Asians (which the both of us are) do not order spring rolls when we go out to eat. I was raised to order things on the menu that my mother could not make better in her kitchen. Fair enough rationale, no? We ordered the pork spring rolls though just for funsies. I liked them! They were mostly filled with vegetables but hints of pork were there. Fried correctly to develop a crispy exterior without being greasy or soggy over a short time period. Wrapped loosely so that the density of the rolls were just right. Were they better than my mom's? Heck no. Did I tell my boss that? Yes, of course. But an excellent dish to order if that's what you're in the mood for and the sweet dipping sauce was a refreshing take on the traditional Vietnamese fish sauce in my household. The benefit of dining with Jessica is that her eyes are a billion times larger than her stomach. As a second appetizer, we ordered the Som Tum Mango, a Thai style spicy mango salad with shrimp. Funny that I'm afraid of Joe dying, but not so much Jessica... who actually has a true allergy to peanuts. She's a pharmacist, she can deal! The dish did call for ground peanut, which I can only assume they replaced with cashew nuts like the mango salad, a different item on the menu. What we actually got seemed to better describe that dish, so I'm not even sure if we actually received the Som Tum Mango. The salad had a nice heat to it, cooled nicely with mint leaves and the sweetness of the mango. Shrimps were cooked perfectly making the dish a stellar choice. Much like how every cuisine has a signature dish, the pad thai clearly comes to mind the Thai food. The rice noodles at Numchok Wilai are thinner width wise than Boualouang, which I liked preferred to the wider variety. We chose the house tamarind sauce rather than a tomato sauce, a more traditional route. Not even sure how a tomato based sauce came into play. The sauce was not overly sweet and not overly thick which I find can sometimes ruin a pad thai really quickly. Combined with egg, shrimp, chicken, beansprouts, and green onions, I loved it! The green curry chicken came out with its own tea candle heat source, a cute presentation. Creamy, spicy (!), and loaded with bamboo shoots which covered tender chicken pieces underneath. We had ordered it moderately spicy, can't even imagine how the highest spice would fare. It's nice that they let you choose that option for all spicy dishes! Loved the mixture of coconut curry and thai basil! Lastly, dessert! Four dishes later and we were still holding on. We decided to try a dish called "Kow Neaw Sung Kaya", a coconut black sticky rice topped with a Thai style baked custard. The custard is more of a bread pudding texture, sweet and slightly sticky. The black sticky rice was also sweetened but surprisingly the overall dish wasn't overwhelming. Perfect way to end the meal! The meal left both of us satisfied and full! For a fraction of what a fancier meal would cost us but for the same amount of happiness. Wiiiiiin. Absolutely loved our meal at Numchok Wilai and would definitely come back. There's parking in the back of the restaurant, as well as street parking if you can find it! It made Avenue Edmonton's Best Restaurant 2014 as honorable mention in "Best Thai". I'd have to go to Bua Thai again to compare, as it's been over a year and a half since I've been there. With restaurants like these in town, my standard "sushi or..." can now be "sushi, Thai, or..." Where's the best Thai restaurant you've been to?

Love. Love. Love. Best swordfish I've ever had. Too many menu favorites to name them all. Save room for dessert if you can. My single wish: that they would add something new/different to the menu offerings from time to time.

Excellent service! Wonderful location/atmosphere! Delicious food! BUT...$8 hummus or baba ganouj with NO pita bread? (They charge $1.50 per basket and you probably need 3 baskets to finish the plate of hummus.) Seems like a pretty silly policy, to me...am I really going to eat a plate of hummus with a spoon and no bread?
Food was amazing and different. A new take on traditional Mediterranean food. All the food was fresh and the wait staff was helpful in explaining everything. I would highly recommend!
EXCELLENT food!!!! Just don't ask him any questions!!! I've never been disappointed. Get there early. The line is long but well worth the wait.

It was about time! Saigon had been on our list of restaurants to visit for way too long and we finally dined there last night. Simply said, we loved everything about this place. From it's quaint, old-timey, sit-down Asian restaurant atmosphere, the polite and competent service, the excellent food and beverages offered and the prices that were so reasonable that you almost feel guilty when paying. We began our dinner with 2 bottled beers - 33 Export and Saigon Export. Both beers were what we expected, pale lagers with a slightly sweet & malty taste that perfectly complimented all of the cuisine. For an appetizer we had the Lemongrass Beef which was an absolute hit with us. Thin slices of beef steak rolled up with lemongrass and cheese inside then pan-seared nicely. A dipping sauce, similar to a sweet & sour, was served on the side but was completely unnecessary. Being our first time at Saigon I decided to go with their signature meal of Pho, which is a rice noodle soup, and ordered the Pho Special. A large steaming bowl of a delightful broth with slices of flank steak & beef eye of round, tripe and meatballs. And oodles of noodles. It was also served with a side plate of basil leaves, bean sprouts and a wedge of lime. Don't forget the bottle of Sriracha sauce on the table in case you want some additional heat! Seriously, Pho has got to be the most delicious, comforting meal you can possibly have. The tender meat, the noodles and the broth that has so many hidden flavors in it - a perfect dish. We loved Saigon and if we don't go back soon then we are huge losers. With a capital L.

Nice atmosphere, but it's expensive. There are more reasonable places just a few blocks away. I support time limits on patrons who might be camping out with paperwork or a laptop (don't get me started on that!), but 30 minutes is a bit strict. When I go for coffee with a friend, we usually sit for longer than that.
The food is outstanding! The best Pad Thai I've ever had. Everything we have ordered has been great.

One of the most popular food trucks in Philly, and the one on the top of my list for a while now. Mexican? Thai? These are all things I like! Shared a Chicken Katsu platter, Captain Crunch Burrito, and Chicken Satay taco(they were out of short rib tacos for the day). The chicken satay taco was basically instagrammable it looked that picture-esque with its heaps of lettuce, avocado, chicken, and sauce, and had a fresh flavor that was both surprising and delicious. The Chicken Katsu plate was also quite delicious as the little salad/slaw that came with it complemented the crunchy chicken quite well, though the sauces really made the dish. Surprisingly though there was less food in the plate than I thought there would be; chicken portion was fine though I expected them to fill it up more with veggies and rice. Oh well...portion control. I actually thought the captain crunch burrito was the weakest link as the fish that was fried and placed inside the burrito was nothing all too special, though as stated earlier the sauces and fresh avocado and other toppings kept the burrito tasty anyhow. At $8 for 3 tacos(you can mix and match), I'm coming back soon to both try the short ribs and get some more chicken satay tacos. Along with a side of Chicken Katsu platter. Yeah I'm fat.

The food was fine for a buffet. I loved that the tikka masala was spicy. However the staff is RUDE. They barely look in your direction and certainly don't smile or say anything. I was utterly shocked the restaurant had so many people with that odd atmosphere. Trust me, you can do better and the owner should be ashamed!

a little pricier than most for thai food but they are probably passing along their cost for rent. they have a small menu for those of you who are indecisive. the interior is very eclectic which is a plus compared to other restaurants with the same fare. you cannot go wrong with the curries and expect to pay a little more for anything that was pulled out of the sea, despite it being 3 blocks away
Worst boba tea and bahn me I have ever tried. Pho was pretty good. not going back...ever
This food is amazing, freshly made, hearty amounts, and delicious. The owners are great. A MUST TRY in Brandon.

Updating my review based on the recent visit to this establishment. The food is still good but has become a costly affair. 20$+ for lamb kabob which is enough for one person for lunch is not something one will call for. Apart from that no issues with service or quality of food. Veggie options are also priced almost 17$ which I feel is on higher side cost wise

The banh mi here is very good, especially the house special, which is filled with veggies and sliced, cured meats. The daikon/carrot mix is more finely shredded than that at the other cafes, which I'm not sure if I like; the flavor is good, though, but it is sweeter than Ba Le's or Cafe Huong Lan's. They use a seasoned butter spread on the Sarcone's rolls rather than plain mayo, so that gives the hoagie an extra flavor boost. The sardines in tomato sauce banh mi is also pretty good, if you are: a)vegetarian or b)want a hoagie but not the usual banh mi. The vegegie banh mi is probably the best option here; it is stuffed with plenty of jicama, tofu, potato, daikon, cilantro, peppers, and cucumber on a crusty, buttered roll. Yes, it's slightly more expensive at $5 but it is a fantastic sandwich and a great veggie option that has all of the delicious flavors that a proper banh mi is known for. The special and sardine are $3.50, and the other varieties are $4.00; it's also buy 10, get 1 free. I would call in your order since it gets very busy and there is barely any standing room; the cafe is tiny with no air conditioning (there is a tiny table with 2 stools max). Overall, a good pick for banh mi but I still like my banh mi ga from Cafe Huong Lan slightly more (and the seating a WHOLE lot more!). Would def recommend the special and vegetarian here, though.

I don't know how you can give this food anything less than 5 stars. Sure he can be grumpy, sure he changes the price all the time, sure its a serious wait sometimes, but the food comes from this passion. I like Gus, and I like his food.

Situated right next to one of my other favorite little restaurants in Indy this place is fantastic,,,mofingo ,tostones, chicharon, great rice and beans and wonderful service,,, my Spanish is not spectacular I could get by if I had to, but nice to know that they speak English as well . Well worth the trip not very expensive just excellent Latino , Caribbean food at very affordable prices I will definitely be back

Went here with my family and everyone loved the kabobs. I tried the chicken and lamb, and also had the ground beef. All excellent. A bowl of lentil soup is not only delicious, but the portion was huge! And only $4.50 for it. The atmosphere is really nice and authentic feeling. Definitely look forward to coming back!

Great food great experience. The service was excellent. All types of dishes were on the menu. The waiter suggested that I wait for fresh nanan ( bread) which was hot and taste great. And a plus is that they serve mango Lassi( mango drink like Rita mango misto which come with the meal or buffet. Other restaurants charge for the drink. Great place to eat lunch.

This is a great place. Decided to stop in during the Baltimore Ave Dollar Stroll as they had $1 PBR's advertised....and I'm glad the rain made me stick around. Especially in time for Quizzo...which I kind bombed at, but, I guess it's okay. Food and service is excellent. I got some kind of spicy lamb dish with peppers and sauce over rice. So bangin! And a portion big enough to serve 2-3 for $10+tip. Ethiopian food is definitely a favorite from here on out. Drinks were cheap as well 2 mixed drinks and a beer came to $11, one of which was Miller Fortune for $3. A nearly 7% ABV beverage, I mind you. You're lucky if the closest watering hole to you has High Life for that price. My only complaint is the $10 minimum for cards. Combatted that by ordering in bulk, though, that isn't always feasible. Will return.

The florescent lights kind of make things look a little dingy, but the food is worth it! I ordered the Tamales Cubanos as an appetizer and the Pan con Bistec (steak sandwich). Both items were much larger than expected. The sandwich was probably a foot long and very wide. Half of the sandwich was probably enough food (and the other half was a great second meal later). Everything tasted absolutely wonderful and I've been craving it ever since. I went with four other people who each ordered something different and everyone loved it. There weren't any other customers the the whole time we were there (granted it was late), so I hope they are able to stay in business so we can all enjoy their wonderful food!

This was my first time ordering from here. The food was delivered super fast, well before the 30-40 minutes. Delivery guy was very friendly. The food was great. I really enjoyed the chicken tenders matched with the Modern BBQ sauce. The legendary Mac and cheese was ok. I think it was the chicken sausage that threw it off. Topped off with the buttermilk biscuit. Great job!

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: This is a cute little Thai/Japanese place. The portions are generous, the quality is high and everything is tasty. There is sushi, curries, and other typical things you would expect, all in a cozy, attractive atmosphere and with reasonable prices. The timing of our entrees was way off: things were coming out one-at-a-time. Otherwise, no complaints.

I want my time back!. We were looking forward to trying this place because if all the great reviews and our love of Korean food. Our first impression coming through the door was one of an old neglected Asian restaurant complete with the red stained red carpeting and 1980's karaoke machine in the corner. This reminded me of some of the Asian dives that serve some of the best food. There were a few tables of Chinese speaking dinners that seemed to be enjoying themselves. Being Chinese ourselves, we were surprised that not many Korean ppl were there. The waitress sat us at a table in the corner and preceded to tend her 2-3 tables. We read through the menu as the waitress sat and served other tables that came after us. After waiting a while the waitress was nowhere to be found. Finally after about 20min as she was serving another table that came after us, we were able to flag her down. She acknowledged us! but then went back to the kitchen. After about 5 mins she came to our table with our silver wear and said in broken English if you order now then you need to wait 30 min for your food. This complete neglect and disregard of customers time was incredibly insulting. Needless to say we left and am currently enjoying Korean BBQ across the street. This place is not worth one star. I would comment on the food but we never got that far.

Small place and no online menu but Yelpers said it was the best place around for take out. Husband and wife owners were pleasant and made sure we had our food cooked the way we wanted it. Got take out kung pao chicken, teriyaki, and a beef, chicken, and shrimp dish with vietnamese spring rolls. All were good and portions were plenty.

A new place that we just discovered! Great food and very reasonable place. I enjoyed their service and food. I love their Thai tea! Also, I like their dishes because they don't use excess salt. Definately recommend this place.

As many others have stated the service is meh! But the Pho was great! Mild spice and rich broth.Bring CASH. Portions are large. This might be my favorite Pho in Nashville! The three stars are based only on service,the food is a four star!
The breakfast prices here are out of sight. With tax, over $8 for two eggs, bacon and toast, no potatoes? Why bother when there are great breakfast places in Tucson for half the price?

Everything tasted great. Servings were a good size for two. Service quick. We had chicken satay, pad Thai and panong (sp) curry and no drinks $40. Clean and friendly. We are traveling and found them through yelp for a quick meal before we checked in to our room. Good choice!

This place is amazing!!! It was our 33rd Wedding anniversary and my husband chose this restaurant based in some recommendations. Thank you to everyone that recommended it! We were warmly greeted at the door, Mark our server was fun and inviting and we knew we made the right choice. Eggplant tower of Pisa was amazing... Then Mark our server, sent over a plate of homemade meatballs with sauce and ricotta and bruschetta as an anniversary gift to us... Seriously... If you are looking for authentic Italian food and the love to go with it...you have to have dinner with the Scannicchio family. Delizioso

Really enjoy the banh mi options. Love the shrimp spring rolls. Overall pretty inexpensive. Have yet to try the Pho, but perhaps someday. Contrary to some reviews, the service has always been friendly and the eating area in such a small space is generally clean.

Olio is delicious and offers many unique menu choices. This was our third visit to Olio and each time we ordered something new. The beet salad is delicious! The egg salad was awesome! The carrot salad was different. The hot ham and cheese was really really good. Not a fan of the cauliflower dish but it was removed from our bill.
OMG I am addicted to their Grilled Octopus appetizer!!!! And the tomato mozz salad AND the shrimp pil pil! So incredible. Minus one point bc it's cash only - but five stars otherwise.

This place has spoiled me with their buffet-styled dining. There were so many new things to try, such as, idly, dose, & murgh makhani, but also had some favorites, like butter chicken and chicken biryani. All food consumed was flavorful and perfect temperature. I only drank water with my meal, but they do have a full bar. Four desserts were available. I tried a bit of three and enjoyed the carrot halal that had a hint of cardamom, the fruit custard, and the sugar dough balls. Not only was the food amazing, the staff was top notch. We were seated right away, they were friendly, helpful and always kept our table clear and cups filled. We are definitely recommending and returning.

This place was exceptionally awful. I'd give it no stars if I could, and the only reason I'm writing this review is as a warning to other unsuspecting hungry people. Walked in, both employees looked at my friend and I without even a greeting. (We were the only two in the store). Strike 1 fools. I got the $11.00 special (1/2 lb chicken, mac n cheese and a soda). The white meat tenders were just ok, crispy but absolutely no flavor to the crust or the meat. (Strike 2) The leg/wing were horrid. Again, no seasoning and the meat had an awful aftertaste as if it was spoiled before they fried it. (I would know, I cook chicken all of the time.) (Strike 3) The mac n cheese was more like spicy cajun pasta, but still nothing exceptional. On top of this crap, they got my friend's order wrong after acting funny about letting him use the bathroom--you speak English so why are you acting so confused about a simple question? DO YOU OR DON'T YOU HAVE A BATHROOM THAT PATRONS CAN USE? (Strikes 4 aNd 5). SMDH The icing on the cake was the fact that they didn't even give me the cup for my soda, so I left without it rather than waste my breath. (Strike 6) Needless to say I walk past this crap store every day to and from school, and will continue to do so. I'd advise you to do the same.

Food OK. Service, wanting. Atmosphere is all right -- if you like dining on an airport tarmac. (Noise level would deafen the deaf!). Prices just about right. Though I didn't appreciate the sparkling water scam: Small bottles ONLY, so you have to buy multiple bottles so as to jack up the overall price. Go late when the crowds thing. Jeez, we were there for 5:30 opening (our dinner companions are Americans transplanted from the Midwest, you see), and the place was already jammed. -- Hotspur for The PJ.
Have eaten here several times and gotten take out. Food is good quality and delicious! For your local asian go-to you could not find better.

I've been to this location a handful of times - both dine in and takeout- the wait is usually minimal, and the restaurant is on the cleaner side. Service can be a tad slow, even when they aren't busy. The cocktails aren't the best I've ever had, and I personally don't think they are worth the price tag. The food is decent, it's slightly above average in flavor. The portions are decent. I make sure to know what I can and can't eat with my allergy and there have been times my food has the allergen in it. Even when I request a menu item that isn't made with that allergen. I'm not trying to be an inconvenience to the kitchen which is why I always ordered from the allergy list the hostess stand has on hand. Oh well - I still prefer to eat the Mongolian beef I make at home. Unless I'm in the area I don't think I'll be returning again.
Stopped here on our drive to Kansas...had Thai fried rice & massaman Curry. Food was great, service was great...nice little place with a hard to open front door

Hands down, THE WORST Thai food in Philly, and possibly the worst that i've EVER had. We eat Thai food a lot. Love it. This place was recommended to us by friends, for some odd reason. We usually have the same taste in food. Not this time! The food here was appallingly BAD! The place itself was icy cold on a damp, rainy day. No heat. We started off with the dumplings, which were tough and chewy and rather tasteless. Then, we tried the meatballs, which were grisly. The pad thai, usually a big fave of all of ours, was sickeningly sweet. But, the biggest annoyance was that they never brought one of us their entree. Totally FORGOT IT! The waiter never WROTE down our order. ALWAYS a bad sign. There are at least THREE OTHER THAI places in Philly that are far SUPERIOR and much less pricey! AVOID THIS ONE!!

I love this place...when its not busy and I'm only with 1 other person...and its lunch time... I've been disappointed on more than one occasion when I've gone for dinner. They are considerably busier but they make you wait a lot. The staff are really nice but aren't honest about wait times. I waited out front at 9:30 on a saturday night for 45 minutes (when they said it would be a 20 minute wait) before I left to go somewhere else - they never gave us an update or checked in or said anything. I cant really comment on the food because I'm addicted to pad thai and tom yum soup so i always get that. But both are delicious and you cant beat the lunch special prices and bang for your buck.

I tried this place for the first time and I am extremely glad I did! I got the Kabuli Palow was incredibly flavorful and filling. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the rice was nice and tender. They also delivered it very fast and the delivery man was quite nice. I am making this one of my usual places!

Review is 2 part, the first time we went as well as the 2nd & 3rd time: Just moved to the area and was told Blueplate is a great breakfast spot from a few friends who frequented the area. The first time we went, we accidentally parked in their overflow parking lot which is about a block down (don't do that, check the first lot first, it looks like it was recently expanded. Coming in the front door is kind of awkward, no one is there to greet you really until you turn the corner and its typically a gaggle of servers chatting and ready to help a customer. Kind of weird, especially since they mostly block the thru-way to the bathroom, but not a huge deal. The first time we visited, the service wasn't good. The person who helped us acted like they didn't want to be there, we had to repeat our order 3-5 times and had no expectation of it coming out right. Luckily our food did come out right in a fair amount of time, but our waitress didn't come back to check on us. My wife and son ordered traditional breakfast food, I ordered pork belly with some sort of berry sauce. It sounded great but really didn't work together. Not that it was bad, just adventurous and needed something. My wife didn't want to go back because we felt is was just like a more expensive diner, and we'd rather just stay closer to home. We just happened to be in the area a few weeks later and tried the place again hoping for a better experience. This time, however was MUCH better than our first. We were greeted and sat quickly (by either a great manager, or an owner) and she made sure she had a sizeable booth because we had a baby carrier with us. We had a great server who was very attentive, sociable and did an overall great job. The food was fast and hot, and the service was much improved. We went back the next day (and got the same server again!) because we were in the area again. 4/5 stars only because the service was lacking the first time we were there. I can deal with a clunker on an adventurous dish (every chef has them sometimes), but can't deal with unattentive service. Will definitely return.

Good food, terrible service. Specially the young guy who always looks so confused. He is so rude and always seems like he's having a bad day! Dont come here if you dont want to be treated like trash!!!
Excellent Thai! Very generous portion sizes with flavorful dishes along with incredible side sauces.. extremely friendly service. Highly recommended!

Can two places hold the Gold Standard for Indian lunch buffets? In this case the answer is yes as these folks have two locations; Media and Drexel Hill. The lovely wife and I have enjoyed lunch at the Drexel Hill location many many times and visited this location a few times including once for dinner. The lunch buffet is absolutely amazing. When many many folks of Indian decent, or who have Indian spouses, or who have lived in India all say this is the real deal you know it's something special. During the week it's 10 bucks and on the weekend it goes up a buck or two. It doesn't get much better than that. If you are a vegetarian you will be in heaven. If you are a flesh eater you'll find chicken and lamb choices. There is no Naan on the buffet here. They automatically bring you a basket of hot, fresh, fluffy, deliciousness. The wife thinks the Korma sauce is to die for and I agree. We have always found everything appropriately spiced. Both locations have great Yelp reviews but the Drexel Hill locations are a little higher. For me it's not the food it's the seating. This location can be a little tight. The Drexel Hill location gives you a little more room. If you are in town around lunch time any day of the week these folks are a must try.
Nice friendly family run restaurant. One of the best soup bowls I've had in Nola. Highly recommend.

This is the second Indian restaurant I have ever been to, and I really enjoyed the lunch buffet. I haven't had Indian food very much, so I can't really say what exactly I had. I just know that I really enjoyed it, and I will be back for more.
This place is a must!!! My husband and I were looking for a good gyro and we ended up getting a perfect, fresh experience with courteous staff

Friendly spot in the heart of downtown. Small intimate place. Their house rum is Don Q, so right away the place feels legit. Lunch menu and dinner menu had selections that made me homesick. The portions were spot on. I went with the jueyes empanadillas and the mofongo. The taste was authentic Puertorrican and it was so nice having a bit of home in Tennessee. This is a kind of place you visit several times to deplete the menu. Simpler is to have 3 or 4 guests to sample each other's plates. The coconut flan had it going on for dessert. Next time I'm in town, this will be my stop.

Let me preface this review by saying we visited Cumin Cafe on an evening when a new waitress was working her first night, was responsible for the entire dining room and was clearly overwhelmed by the number of tables occupied. We attempted to calm this poor young woman and recruit some help from the kitchen for her. Once the owner was made aware of the situation, he addressed it and found a solution that satisfied our table, along with other guests. We will have to visit again to post a more fair review. Formerly Annapurna, Cumin Cafe has the same owner (the owner of Lambertville's fine Marhaba middle eastern restaurant). No longer featuring an exclusively Indian menu, Cumin Cafe now features Moroccan specialties, including couscous and tagines. There are also a wide variety of starters and sides that might better be termed pan-Meditteranean cooking. Cumin Cafe is located in the rear of the Four Seasons mall, a tacky, tourist-driven arcade of useless shops that are almost always empty or nearly empty. An almost equally tacky, flashing LED sign reading "OPEN" adorns to front window of Cumin Cafe. The dining room is large, with several picture windows overlooking the Delaware River and providing a view of Lambertville. Seating is comfortable, the restaurant and rest rooms are clean. Noise level is relatively low. The restaurant is, like most other Lambertville and New Hope restaurants, BYO. As I have noted, we visited on an evening when a young woman received her baptism by fire, so service was poor. I certainly hope she sticks with the job, as she was pleasant and well-meaning, but she will require some training and support, particularly when the dining room is busy, such as the evening we visited. The food is fresh and tasty. Is this the best Indian or Moroccan restaurant I've visited? Not by a long shot. Nevertheless, it is an good alternative to the expensive and often noisy dining scene in downtown New Hope and will satisfy your craving for ethnic cuisine. A return visit is in order, along with an updated review.

This is probably the worst Thai meal I've had in Santa Barbara. Stopped by with a friend to branch out for our regular Thai spots. I ordered the yellow curry with beef. If you want to mix veggies or tofo with beef is an extra $1.50. The curry had long pieces of beef with a few carrots floating around with little to no flavor. My friend ordered gluten free spicy noodles with chicken and tofu. Warning it's extremely bland. They remove all the sauces. Which is fine but definitely let the customer know beforehand. Thai ice tea was delicious with a good ratio of tea and condense milk.

This place deserves more than 5 stars! We were dining on a Wednesday night, walking into a beautiful restaurant, great ambiance, and reggae music...we had the best service in Tampa. Andre and his wife, both owners of the restaurant greeted us and were very attentive. And the FOOD was delicious! Chicken curry was hearty and the chicken was incredibly tender, and it was Organic! The ribeye plate my husband had was very tasty as well, a great Caribbean twist. It is definitely a place I will return to !

Solid. But there is no need to write a two page review. Simple menu, good sandwiches, nice owner, quick service. BTW if you are not too particular about your hair cut, there is a lady next door who cut hair for eight bucks does a pretty decent job. You order, go get your hair cut, come back and sandwich is ready.

Amazing food! The pork tacos are amazing and are my favorite every time. They are covered in delicious sauce and have the best fluffy rice buns. I also recommend the bahn mi burger. My friend gets the pho here and also loves it. It's great for creative Vietnamese recipes.

Delicious!! I found out abouut Guru's through Groupon. We ordered almost double what my discount was, but it was worth it. The prices are fair, so you don't feel ripped off and the quality is still just as good. Anyway, we ordered everything medium spice level, and we broke a sweat with pleasure :) They told us they opened 4 months ago. They brought out complimentary pappadam, which tasted better with the tamarind and mint dipping sauces also free. We got the vegetable something appetizer, half tandoori chick to share, chick tikki masala, and lamb josh rosh and roti bread. They gave us seconds of rice and free rice pudding, and then boxes for the leftovers. So great! I've missed an Indian restaurant since the one closed and became Flap Jakes.

I've been to Nadia three times now, and have always left impressed. I love their curries to pieces! The portions could be a little bigger for the price (but I could very well be a pig, haha), but I just eat slower and savour more, so it's not a big deal. I wasn't a fan of their drunken noodles. For such a popular dish, you'd think they could make it less salty and oily. I was literally having to drain off the oil when I got towards the bottom of my plate. Their mango sticky rice is TO DIE FOR. The last time I went, I was afraid we weren't going to get any, because the waiter had to check and see if the mangoes were ripe/sweet enough. Luckily they were, and I got my rice, and he left me impressed that he was unwilling to serve something that wasn't up to their standards. So many restaurants just don't care. I am also consistently impressed with the fact that they understand what "vegan" means, and even if my dining companions and I don't mention the V-word, they ask us if we're okay with eggs and dairy in our food if we order a dish with tofu in place of meat. I'll keep coming back again and again. Also, BYOB!
Basically all I can say is it's delicious. From the mango lassi to the food. All around yum.
I tend to get the rice noodle combination. if you like rice noodles, it's the way t go. Also their egg rolls are simply delicious

I was passing through the town and this is one place you should avoid at all costs. The food was just plain Nasty. There was a couple that walked out as I was walking in and the man made a statement that the food was nasty, but I was trying to give them the benefit of the doubt. My daughter took one swallow of the wonton soup and spit it out, and then I tried it and had a hard time swallowing and had to take a drink of soda immediately to get rid of the taste. I spent $35 and I am still shaking my head.

Excellent food and service!! So happy we found this spot!! The pad Thai was fantastic and perfect amount of heat. The Thai hot had my husband happily sweating! We got take out and it was fast and fresh! We can't wait to eat inside! Staff was very friendly and faculty was super clean.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: What a disappointment. First off, how are they 2 dollar signs when a lunch item of purée spinach and cheese is $16. Palak paneer should be $8-9 for lunch. What about people who don't want a buffet that's been sitting out for hours. The owner or man that sat me was horribly rude. I got the feeling it was because I was a woman. He was talking with a friend and pretended I wasn't there even. Will not go back.

Looking for new lunch truck and found this gem. When I arrived around there was a long line so I decided to try it. I had the tilapia burrito and it was crunchy and delicious. Very flavorful not spicy at all. I also had their satay chicken tacos and short rib taco. These were good too but not as memorable as the tilapia burrito. There teas are very good too. I had the Thai tea and I'm going to try jasmine green tea next time. I will definitely return here. I went earlier this week but it wasn't open :(

I was here on opening night. I loved the music, the service was great, and the lamb was like butter. The Greek salad I got had ripe tomatoes and yummy feta. The pork souvlaki was delicious too. I got a glass of rose which worked with everything. My friend got the greens as a side and they were delicious. The fries were a little too salty for my taste. I'll probably be back.

Pleasantly surprised by this place! First time at this or any location. The staff was super friendly and greeted me when I walked in. They were also very accommodating of any questions I had. I ordered the hummus bowl with falafel. Honestly, I feel like there should be 1) more hummus and 2) more falafel (at least 1 if not 2 more pieces). Other than that it was delicious! Pita comes with it and it was fluffy and warm. Overall, good experience! I'd come back again.

I was hoping for a bit more but all in all this little place was pretty good. The coconut chicken soup had a great taste but I found it odd that it had lots of onions and green and red peppers. I'm not used to that when I order this at other Thai restaurants. Entrée: I had the Panang Chicken. Again, there was an excessive amount of green and red peppers. I suspect it was to make the plate look like it had more food. I had to pick half of them out because there were so many. The taste was excellent but I would have liked the Panang Curry to be less watery and more creamy. I found myself not liking it until I got about half way through. At that point it tasted better to me, I'm not sure why! The wait staff was very friendly, and they never let my drink glass go empty. Also, they didn't charge me for tap water like Thai Nana did! I will return here to try another dish very soon. I use Panang as my main dish when comparing Thai restaurants so it's what I get my first time. Why only 3 stars? The amount of green and red peppers in the soup and the Panang Curry. If they improve on my next visit I will change my rating.
Just got delivery from here, spring rolls, pad Thai, and chicken cashew. They were all without a doubt best delivery Thai I've ever gotten!!! Pad Thai was perfect ratio and plenty of flavor!

I usually go to this place and I like it. But today I ordered rice bowl, chickpea, vindaloo and I asked the lady to put minty cilantro sauce instead she served tomato ketchup. It was a take out order so I noticed it when I got back home. Secondly it had a hair in it too. I would highly recommend the owner to ensure that the servers dont mess up the orders and also to maintain the food standards.

Living and growing up in Southern California, I had the privilege of having all kinds of ethnic foods at my fingertips and one of them being Thai food. I moved to Nashville and stumbled upon this restaurant. At first, I was a little scared to go inside because the place looked really weird outside, but decided WTH. I had no expectations, but that's a good thing. I ordered my favorite dishes (panang curry, tam yum, and pad thai) and to my surprise I was impressed! Their food was delicious! My husband who is a picky eater enjoyed this place too! Their staff was very nice. I will definitely come back here again. It looks a little sketchy outside, but the inside isn't bad at all plus the food is great!

Great fusion food! I would't necessarily categorize this place as a modern Vietnamese bistro just bistro with an Asian twist. The beef steak and eggs are good but not much beef to make a meal. The chicken and green waffles was good but the waffles are heavy. The chicken was good and the sauce for the waffles made the dish. The pho was good not great but good. The kimchi burger was great and the fries was fantastic. It's worth the effort to come out here for dinner.

This is a real hidden gem. The menu is limited and based on the day of the week. That's why it tastes so fresh and homemade. It's very pleasant inside. If you go for the lunch special, make sure to ask what's included. Some menu items are pricier. This is my new go-to lunch spot.

Sunday evening a double date brought us to Taziki's. For $32 we all walked away satisfied. I love going Greek! There were hardly any patrons in the cafe and so we had the pick of the place. That is also concerning because I'm not sure if they have picked up enough buzz over the last few months. I don't know what I will do if they shut down.... Regardless it is still my favorite place so I'll operate under the "more for me" notion. Medi-salad + scoop of humus = Happy Sarah P. What can I say? I'm easy to please.

I wish there were a no star rating. After eating here several times, decided to do take out. Easy, two apps & two noodle dishes. Was told 25 minutes, knowing what 25 minutes generally means, arrived 35 minutes later. Took my money, then said 'sorry, need another 10minutes'. I waited, went back in after 10, stood at the counter for another 5...so sorry, we messed up your noodle order and it will be another 10minutes. Took my money in a heartbeat, hope they enjoy it, it will be the last they see from me. Learn how to run a kitchen.
We have been multiple times and are never disappointed. Definitely my favorite Indian restaurant. No complaints and such a great addition to the Newtown restaurant scene

This place isn't too bad. The spring roles were pretty good, but the dipping sauce didn't have enough peanut flavor for our tastes...there also wasn't much of it. As far as the pho, I found the broth to be a little tomatoey and greasy. The other issue we had was that the noodles stuck together in a big clump in the bottom. It was tough to get them pulled apart.

This is the best indian buffet in town, hands down. I love the huge variety of things to choose from but usually I go for the same dish... the chicken tikki masala. I drive from the east side to the west side every time I want indian food. Other buffets don't even come close. Great food, great service. Ask for the frequent diner stamp card and after 10 visits/dinners, you get a freebie!

When I first walked in and looked at the menu, I didn't think I was going to enjoy the food. To my surprise I really enjoyed it and will be going back again. I had the flat bread with cheese and I had the pita with hummus and they were amazing. I recommend that you give them a try.
Very unexpectedly good. Had the gyro platter. And the walnut baklava was perfect - had the right blend of crispness and chewiness.
The portions are very large and prices excellent. Try their fataya and fresh baked bread from their bakery menu. I will definitely continue going back.
If you haven't eaten here you should! The food is really good and it's fast too. It's very clean inside, and the staff, especially the owner/manager is very polite and friendly. Keep it up Zaikka!

Good food, but be prepared to wait- sometimes MUCH longer than they tell you. My wife and I enjoy the food from Thai 5 and typically patronize the place once or twice a month. We've been customers ever since they took over the space from Kombo Kitchen. The food is good, but the personnel's estimates of wait times are severely lacking. The past several times that we've called in to order food, we've shown up at the time that the food was supposed to be ready ("30 minutes", "45 minutes", etc.), but have had to wait another 15 minutes, 30 minutes, or more before the food was actually ready. Most recently, we ordered our food (two entrees and an order of spring rolls) at 6:30pm and were told that it would be ready 45 minutes later. Upon our arrival at the trailer at 7:15pm, we were told "Your food is almost ready. Please wait in your car and we'll bring it out to you". After waiting for 25 minutes, then walking back to the window to inquire about the status of our order, we were told "I'm sorry, but look at all of the orders we have" (while pointing to tickets hanging from the rack). The food was finally ready a few minutes before 8:00pm (almost 90 minutes after we ordered it- double the time that we were quoted). Upon asking why there was such a discrepancy between the estimated time and the actual time of the food being ready, we were told "I'm sorry, but I wasn't the person that took your order". Because of the prices that they charge and the long wait that's required to actually get the food, you're better off patronizing other places nearby that offer better value and more timely service: Chef Thai & Sushi, Thailand Restaurant, Royal Palace, etc.

The first time I had Momo's it was great, and I thought I had found a gem. We went that first time early-dinner and sat near the kitchen. Our waiter wast attentive and knowledgable. So as soon as I saw the groupon I was esctatic! We usually love their saganaki--last nigts experience was awful. They are getting sloppy. The alochol they burn it in--there was too much, or they didn't let it burn all the way through. it was seriosly gross and hard to eat cheese swimming in alcohol. Very disappointing scallops--not cooked correctly. Our server was frazzled and had like 3 tables. And I was shocked at how they brought out our food in such an odd manner---would bring one persons dish and then 7 minutes later another dish. I got my meatballs and then14 minutes later I was like---did you forget my salad? Nobody could eat together and enjoy it, like dinner out with friends should be. It was all just very unorganized and they were not even busy at all! Very, very disappointing. I'll be going to Olympa from now on.

there are at least 4 or 5 Indian buffets in the KOP area, but this one is consistently my favorite. it's also offers the biggest variety. my coworkers and i come here at least once a month and have never left hungry (my personal record is 5 plates). it's a great place for someone who has never tried Indian before because you can try so many different things. the fact that there is usually a large and diverse crowd at lunch is a testament to how good this place is.
Excellent! Super fresh and high quality ingredients. Maybe the best pho I've had in many major cities in the USA.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Good Indian food. As usual, got the lamb vindaloo with a side of rice and naan. Vindaloo was a little "greasy", if that makes any sense, but good nonetheless. Naan a bit crispy and heavy on the pre-dosed butter, but again, still good. One of the coolest things is the beer selection. I had Cave Creek chili beer, which went good with dinner (for $2). Overall, would recommend and will be back again!

3.5 stars: I tried the lunch combination which included the satay tofu, coconut soup and red curry dish. The tofu was awful; half of the tofu was overlooked (like burnt) and it was very salty. The coconut soup was okay; a little bit runny and sweet. The red curry was good but I think it was lacking ingredients (a bit runny). Customer service was great.

Although this is an Indian-Chinese-Thai restaurant, I only tried the Indian food so this review is based on that. I had the vegetable samosas, chicken biryani rice, and garlic naan. I didn't thoroughly enjoy the samosas or rice. Something about the spices were really off to me - I've had some really good indian food before and this didn't cut it. I can say that the garlic naan was VERY tasty. If I ever came back, I'd probably get a few orders of the garlic naan and I'd be happy. Priced very reasonably.

Amazing good - get the lasagna- get the lasagna! The plantains are awesome. Cesar the bar tender is very cool. All the pork is soo good. We live Cuban and S American food - and this was great. Coming back soon!

I've been to Remedy several times over the last few years, and while this location is certainly a step up from the previous, it also lost its small coffee shop charm. As a coffee drinker the new $3.50 price tag on regular coffee (a large is maybe 12oz) is very steep. The taste and size being comparable to a McDonalds coffee, which rings in at half the cost. I won't be back.

OMG!! I'm from Rolla and I've eaten here three times in the past month because I love it that much! A transcendent eating experience!! The charred cherry tomato bruschetta was just incredible. The zucchini carpaccio with preserved lemon was out of this world! Don't miss the egg salad either! Each meal made me soooo happy!

Ordered take out. The egg rolls were good but very small and it much substance to them. Spring rolls were not what I expected at all. I had to through them away. Soup was very tasty. Service was acceptable. I was told 15- 20 minutes for my order. When I arrived 25 minutes later they quickly aged up everything for me with little to no wait. However, at the end of it all, I spent 27.59 and was still hungry.

The hookah flavors are abundant and there are cool mixes like Passion Kiss or Wildberry Mint. Tonight I'm enjoying strawberry with friends. This place has plenty of street parking nearby and an extensive menu. The ambiance is comfy cool with booths and dark lighting. The only issue with this place is the music could be more current then folks would be able to dance and hookah. The music selection is traditional middle eastern which is okay but on a late night sometimes you want to level up and get lit.

Beautiful jewel located on Lancaster Avenue in Bryn Mawr. I thought their lunch buffet was incredible for $9.99. Included many chutneys and several desserts and salad. They brought warm nan bread to my table. The mango lassi I ordered was great- very fruity. Lovely decor with Indian paintings and murals line the walls. Great tranquil atmosphere. Perfect!

This is the second time I have been to this restaurant for the lunch buffet and I am very impressed with the food! The service is friendly and fast and they have a great variety of food. Everything that I had to eat was exceptional! I would highly recommend this place to anyone. It is a real hidden gem!

The service was very friendly and the food exceeded my expectations. I had the spicy basil fried rice with chicken and the mango sticky rice was a great choice for dessert. Would definitely come back!

A good noodle house. Tried the staple steak Pho. I recommend getting the sprouts steamed so it doesn't make your soup cold when you throw them in. The basil and limes were fresh, and the 33 beer was just what I needed after walking down on a hot day. The staff was friendly, I was lucky that I went with two native speakers so I'm not sure if my experience would have been different but I doubt it. P.S. I didn't see any mice.

As pho goes, the stuff at this place is pretty darn good. I admit, I'm a bit of a picky eater so I ordered mine dressed down, but the broth was still warm and flavorful and the thinly-sliced steak perfectly pink in the center when the huge bowl arrived at our table. My girlfriend ordered shrimp and crab rolls that looked so good I helped myself to one. Packed with seafood and few pesky veggies (I hate the green stuff) and fried to a golden crisp, they were the perfect accompaniment to the slithery rice noodles. The hostess saw I was struggling to eat the noodles with chopsticks and hurried over with a fork, saving me the embarrassment of asking for one. (I do know how to use chopsticks, but just can't seem to master the art of eating slippery pho noodles with 'em.) My favorite part of the meal was the mango bubble tea. At least, I ordered mango bubble tea. What I got was more like a smoothie, thick and creamy and obviously freshly made. Though it had chewy tapioca balls in the bottom, I wouldn't call this bubble tea. I would, however, call it delicious. If Pho Hoa was open in the morning, I'd get one on the way to work for breakfast every day.

The service was excellent. I'm pretty open to eating ethnic foods but for some reason I wasn't impressed with this style of cuisine. I felt that a lot of the dishes tasted the same and was very bland. It was tasty enough for me to finish but not impressed.

This place is basically a stationary food truck but they actually have a decent sized menu. I've only had two different items because I usually go for the Tom yum soup when I'm in the mood. For this it hasn't disappointed me yet. The service is friendly and the food is spicy if that's what you want. I would caution against eating outside in the summertime. There isn't too much shaded seating. I believe there's inside seating but I always take mine to go.

Best thai food in south Tampa, I go at least once a week and bring everyone I know here! Everything is fantastic, and I highly recommend the duck fried rice and phad woonsin with seafood. The portions are huge and they are able to accommodate everyone's heat preferences!

I purchased a Groupon for $30 that had a value of $60. My husband and I drove 45 minutes to celebrate our anniversary. We had both already eaten and I was about to order dessert. I mentioned to the waiter that I had a groupon. When I mentioned that I had the $60 version he said that is only good if you have 5 people in the party. I asked to see the manager. I was willing to take the $30 value that I had paid for the Groupon. He tried to blame it on Groupon and say there was nothing he could do. My husband is a business owner that uses Groupon. You can always give the value that the customer paid. I was so upset it really ruined my anniversary. I will never go back.

Very clean interior with a bar. The lady that served us had a neat accent and was very polite. I ordered the curry chicken with rice, cabbage, and plantains. It came out very quickly and was portioned just right. The chicken could have used a but more curry flavor but was still delicious. It was very tender, and falling off the bone. I did get some broken pieces of bone every now and then but it's probably due to how they cut up the chicken.

My high rating is based only on their bahn mi sandwiches. Their menu is quite overpriced as compared to Noodle City, but the best kept secret of this restaurant are their sandwiches. Such a great value! $4 for something that can fill me up in Isla Vista.
Fresh, reasonably priced, good variety, friendly service are all some of the reasons we think taste of India has the best Indian food in the area.

This used to be such a great place before they changed ownership. The butter chicken tastes like it was covered in ketchup; no warm spices at all. The only redeeming quality was the fresh naan. Everything else was just bad. Will not return.

Not the best Indian buffet. Surprised at the other ratings. The goat (curry) was swimming in the excess water rendering it to be absolutely flavorless. The only reason this place gets 2 stars is the price for the buffet and thanks for not blaring sad desi music and good garlic naan..

It's 3:00 in the afternoon and my daughter wants crab pad Tai. I call once no answer. I call ten minutes later and the owner answers and says they are closed but he would take care of me. Told me to come in thru the side door. Great service is hard to find. You'll find in here along with outstanding food.

Very authentic Laotian and Thai food. As good as it gets. Ordered the Naam rice salad, sate and fresh spring roll. Light dinner for 2. Flavors were great, food was fresh. Ordered via Uber Eats as we were staying at a hotel.

Tons of people in this parking lot, and it was fairly busy when I went in. Lots of empty plates - I did not even get a chance to see the food. I came for the boba - the bubble tea - yep, with that huge straw that you can suck up those black tapioca pearls. They are like gummy bears and should never be wrinkly. It takes a specific science of soaking them in the right sugary syrup and not keeping them in there for days either. I thought the Boba tea here was gross, but it actually got better after I waited an hour. I got the green milk tea and it tasted like super strong green tea powder. I also got the taro smoothie with jelly - yellow cubes of squishy jelly - kind of gross. It was alright. I don't think these Bobas are the best, but if you don't mind a super concentrated flavored milk powder taste, it's not bad. I definitely want to come back for the Pho!

Probably the worst restaurant that I've been in Center City. First the service was horrendous, it took them forever to change the plate and sometimes we have to tell them to change the plates. The food was really poorly made and extremely simply prepared. The belly dancer was not so good and people were putting money in the skirt as if she was a stripper. The decoration of the restaurant is trying to be a tent environment, but it just looks dirty with all the dust accumulated in the fabrics on the walls. Other than that, there is nothing much more to say but an awful restaurant. I do not usually give bad reviews but this place is just one of a kind.
Food is amazing and the female employees are very friendly, but the older male owner is extremely rude

Good service in a cozy setting located on Central Ave in St. Pete. Try the pad thai, any of the curries, or the tom kha gai for a delicious sample of what they have to offer. Only gave it 4 out of 5 since every time we visit on a busy night, they never seem to have enough servers, so you may feel like your table's not getting enough attention from the wait staff. However, the kitchen never lets us wait for too long (15-30 mins) before we forget about the busy service and happily stuff ourselves in our delicious "Thai spicy" dishes. Give em a try!

This is a hidden gem! We are staying in St Pete Beach on vacation and came across this place and decided to try it. I'm extremely happy we Did! I had the sea bass tagine which was phenomenal. All the food was excellent. We planned on having food at a different place everyday on vacation but this restaurant is definitely worth another trip!

The food was pretty good, but the atmosphere was awful (it was dead quiet in a bad way). There were about 6 tables of people all seated right on top of each other, so it was really awkward because you could hear everything people were saying so everyone stopped talking. I really don't think I've ever felt so uncomfortable at a restaurant in my entire life. Beside that, though, the food was good (we had the hara bhara kabob, lamb chettinad, and garlic naan) but not the best I've had either. Next time I'd probably get the chicken tikka masala (as so many other reviews have mentioned was really good) TO GO!

Delicious, authentic and quickly made Thai food, from a Family owned and operated restaurant! Providing a comfortable and inviting atmosphere, coupled with their great prices, makes this a definite go to for me. They also have authentic Thai Redbull and other hard to find local drinks!

This is easily the best food truck in the city. Take it from a local. The man always Cooks chicken platters, they're always $10, he doesn't have a menu, and he doesn't have utensils. His food truck is a work of art. You can stand in line (and you will unless you're very early). And in that line you can appreciate his fresh fruits, his fresh flowers and how the trend is the color purple, for example. The man is an artist. And on top of that his food is incredibly delicious and oh so filling. Sure you can find something cheaper for $10 but this is really the size of two meals. Something you should understand is that he opens up around 11:30 and sometimes the line will form even before he starts. You want to get in line early because people will usually spend an hour waiting for his food. The reason for the long lines is that the nine-to-five workers along Market Street come out at the same time and sometimes are in groups of four or five or seven people. So you could end up first or you could end up eighth and depending on how fast you walk haha. Really check this place out. An example of what I got in the past is grilled marinated chicken with blueberries, plums, noodles and some really hot peppers. Be careful. Those Peppers killed me. But now I'm back and I'm eating more octopus falafel.
Poor chicken for a chicken place. Sandwiches overly greasy, panko on chicken soggy. Can get better fried chicken at the grocery store.
the only vegetarian item on the menu is soup, well, that's of course if you like chicken broth. they would have gotten 1 star, if a solution wasn't thought of. we got steamed vegetables.
From the freshly made pita to the mezze plates, and the beautiful layouts inside, they really want to make you satisfy when you get in there! I love going to this place! Highly recommended~

The food is decent and it offers authentic flavours, but it's not over-the-top good. That being said, what the kitchen at Golden Szechuan pumps out should keep you happy enough. The service was very good on the night that I visited as well and that's always welcome. All-in-all, Golden Szechuan deserves a look in by those who enjoy spicy Chinese food.

For reasonably priced, fresh, and delicious Vietnamese food with some flair, Mint can't be beat. I haven't tasted but am curious to try their house cocktails, including a Sriracha Bloody Mary. I love the kimchee burger. Their pork, on any dish, is always amazing (and I'm not usually a big fan of pork), and my mouth is watering just thinking about the sauce that comes with their vermicelli bowls. The menu is compact but everything on it looks appetizing, and I'm curious to go back and taste more. Their service is also consistently good and crazy fast. This is my go-to spot if I'm in a rush or in the mood for some light, fresh Vietnamese.

My order from yelp didn't get to their system. They still made my food quickly. The food was okay, but I still had a slight allergic reaction. It's very hard to find restaurants that cater to my allergy.

This place is really great. I think their original recipe was better than the Thai Curry. The Thai Curry didn't have a lot of flavor. I haven't tried the pies but they look very good too. It's a little pricey compared to a typical fast food place, but it's pretty hard to spend a lot here because they sell chicken by the pound. I had eight pieces and it still only came out to 5 dollars. The honey mustard was great, it's got a little kick which I liked. Will definitely be back.

This review will be updated as Taziki's continues to approve but they were definitely working out bugs about 10 days ago when I visited. I have been a Taziki's fan for 15 months. When they came to Nashville, I thought I had struck gold. Ordered the pasta special with an extra side of pita chips on Friday night. It was pretty dead as the ENTIRE kitchen staff stood around waiting for new orders to come in. After a mere 7 minutes, I had my order. Noticed it appeared to be missing a box. After bringing this to the cashier's attention, the shift leader/asst mgr quickly jumped in and rectified my order. Got home - the quality of food was decent. The only problem - it was ice cold within 10 min of leaving the store. Thankfully I was home and able to heat it in the microwave. Overall, I wonder how much attention they will get with their location behind Which Wich which already competes with Panera Bread and Chipotle on West End.
Beverages on point.... Great food and ambiance!! AWESOME deserts!!! Excellent service by Erica

Service was great, however place needs a GOOD clean. Almost walked out, but based on reviews thought we would still give it a go. Had fried tofu for the first time (not bad) and. Chicken satay to start which was good. I got the pumpkin curry which was very nice and also the pineapple fried rice with vegetables, however the vegetables overpowered the little rice that there was so that was a little disappointing. Waitress was very nice.

It was Just OK. Took us over 30 minutes to find a parking spot. Once we had a spot( our friends already found one and got a beeper) we had an hour and half wait to eat. Drinks on the tiki bar were kinda $$.. $11.50 for 2 drinks. Food was mediocre. I got fish and chips. Fish was heavily breaded and greasy. Hubby had lobster mac and cheese. He said was good but extremely rich. Would I go back? Maybe.. The music in the tiki area was good.

The crab, cucumber salad was light and fresh. The fried catfish over rice was good. The yams on the side were delicious. The staff was courteous and very helpful. I wasn't too into plastic plates and it really smelled of smoke from cooker.

Given all the other reviews, I was expecting to have trouble finding the place, but with GPS, it was actually incredibly easy to find. And parking (in back) was good too. Certainly much easier to enter and exit than many other places around town. I actually thought the interior decor was quite nice with several large modern flat-screen TVs. The tables, chairs and other interior decor looked new and in good shape. The food was quite good! My dining companion and I had the following dishes: - Spinach burek - huge, flaky, light, delicious, much bigger than it looks in the menu picture, great deal for $4 - Chevapi - The menu says 'minced meat', but it's actually a bunch of little sausages in between two pitas. I thought it was quite tasty. The waitress recommended it as an authentic Bosnian dish. This is also quite a large dish of food. I ate 3/4, was stuffed, and took the rest home for tomorrow's lunch. Also, be sure to ask for the roasted pepper sauce/spread. The waitress brought me some half way through the meal and I thought it definitely complemented the meat nicely. By the way, I wasn't at all sure how to eat this dish - cut it? pick it up? I ended up eating pieces by hand, cutting some and finally rolling up some of the sausages in the pita bread. Improvise! - Pljeskavica - Like an enormous thin hamburger patty. The menus says beef or lamb. My companion did not specify and I think she got lamb. I'd say that's the better choice. Very tasty and different than a standard burger. Wanted to try the baklava, especially given the quality of the dough used in the burek and the chevapi dishes, but they were sold out! :( I'll call ahead next time to make sure it's available before I come. In fact, they were sold out of all their desserts. There must have been a hungry mob of sweet-toothed bandits that came through and cleaned them out. A number of the other customers were speaking what I assume is Bosnian, which I'd say (as other Yelpers have pointed out) probably speaks well for the authenticity of the place. Incidentally, Euro Grill is very authentically European in the sense that you are expected to order a beverage. Asking for water in most Nashville restaurants will get you a glass of tap water. Asking for water here will get you a little bottle of water that you will be expected to pay for. Personally I ordered an Orangina (http://www.orangina.com/ -- when's the last time you saw that on a restaurant menu!) and it was delicious, but I think it was probably almost as expensive as the burek. Overall, it's a bit more pricey than a meat-and-three or some of the Asian and Latin restaurants around town. My meal was $16+ including tax and tip. But I still thought it was a really good meal and a lot of fresh, high-quality food for the money. Lunch and dinner menu prices are the same, so while it might be a little expensive for lunch, it's actually rather affordable for dinner. I hope Nashvillians will support Euro Grill. I know I'll be back to try the greek salad, maybe some soup and that elusive baklava.
The Grilled Salmon Feast is just that!! Explosive taste with a large portion of salmon. The wait time was minimal with good atmosphere. I'll definitely be back to try the remaining dishes

Finally made it to dinner here at the Drexel Hill location...so happy we did! The food is delish! Everything we had was so good. The atmosphere was warm and quiet and service was friendly and quick. We ordered two appetizers; Reshmi Kabab and Gobhi Pakora...both were beautifully plated and arrived to the table hot! We shared both and not a piece of anything was left on the plates! For our entrees we had the Chilly Chicken and Punjabi Tikka served with rice...so good!!! The heat from the spice in the Chilly Chicken made my husband sweat, but he asked for it since he told the server he wanted it very spicy! He shared it with me, it had so much flavor and so much heat, but it was wonderful. The Punjabi Tikka was very flavorful and it was so much food, I took half home. Lunch tomorrow! Our server was so sweet, i asked for the dessert to go...Kheer, a rice pudding with spices, nuts and raisins...he put it in my bag complimentary. I cant wait to go back again for lunch! Oh! Get the Garlic Naan!!! Oh as for some of the negative reviews, i have a hard time believing them because we had such a nice experience!

Despite the cold rainy night that my boyfriend and I decided to try this place, we were welcomed by happy faces and the promise of a really great meal. We decided to try this place based on everyone else's comments here on Yelp so thanks! As we arrived we watched someone finishing off a place of heaped steamy aromatic rice. We could barely decide what to eat because I'd read so many of your recommendations and everything sounded great. We finally settled on the chicken shawarma platter and it was just as good as I hoped it would be. The chicken was seasoned nicely, the rice was amazing and the hummus and salad really fresh. We ordered an extra side of rice so enjoyed some leftovers the next day. The price was really reasonable for the amount of food and the staff were super friendly. We were offered some mint tea after dinner on the house which was excellent and I'm not a tea drinker. Overall - really excellent meal. I can't wait to go back and try something different.

Came here because I was dying for a bahn mi, I got a pretty basic sandwich with no sauce on it, the veggies weren't pickled, and the meat was a joke. I also got service with attitude and the bare minimum interaction. Guess my search for a good bahn mi goes on.
Total rip off. Paid 10 dollars for a Greek salad that was all lettuce. Disappointing.

The very best gyro I ever had very good quality meat and the pita was overloaded with gyro meat. The wings were also very good. We went very late so I want to say thanks for late hours. We will be back

Very ordinary food at extraordinary price in a horrible atmosphere. Extremely noisy, very little space, continuously bumped by the waters, slow service, pompous waiters, marginal menu items, very overpriced, small food portions. Eat a snack (or a Subway sandwich) before you go there. Not a pleasant place to be for a quite dinner or a dinner date. It is BYOB. So you can bring your own and booze up. You do not go there to eat; you go there to booze up surrounded by other drunks. Do not expect to have any kind of conversation. For that privilege, you will get a big bill at the end. But you are boozed up so you wouldn't even know.

Rather surprised by all the negative comments. I consider myself a bit of a gourmand, and, yes, Chinatown is better, but PF Chang's is what it is - solid Americanized Chinese food done well. I am not a fan of chain restaurants by a long shot but find that PF Chang's is consistently good (I've been to four locations now) with fresh food, overall great service (just ONCE I had a bad experience with service), a nice atmosphere and fair prices. Lunch, in particular, is decently priced. I can feed myself and my two daughters for less than $40. What other reviewers didn't mention - it's a good spot for vegetarians. Personal favorites: the spinach with garlic, the spicy tofu, the chicken lettuce wraps, the lo mein, good dumplings, great salads, awesome drinks. Forget the naysayers and give it a whirl!

I literally live 7 minutes away from here and it took me 2 years to come. King Doc came before I moved to the area and said his portion was really small for the price so i stayed away. But soOOOO glad i finally stopped in. First Mr. Spice-n-Grill was a breath of fresh air, super nice and funny. I got the Chicken Biryani, i choose a medium spice which was perfect, i choose the garlic naan because i was really hungry at the time. The Goat Though. Now you will get to know I am a huge fan and boy did they deliver. I don't know what happened when King Doc went but i had sooo much food I ate it for 2 days and shared some with him and Chef Veto. Yes I will be back. Keep in Mind I do not eat in because I live nearby but there are a couple of tables if you want to eat in.

some of the best Dosa you can find anywhere. the dosa itself is cooked perfectly, the potato masala is super flavorful and delicious as is the sambar. i highly recommend the Mysore Masala Dosa, Paper Masala Dosa, and Onion Rava Masala Dosa. the owner, kitchen and wait staff are absolute sweethearts. not listed on the menu but equally delicious is the Idli Manchurian. the Bhel Puri is also worth ordering as an appetizer as well. this place is a gem and definitely worth keeping in heavy rotation.

They have the best red velvet cake in town abd there beef party's are amazing there always nice hot Nd I like them spicy there always busy long lines but that's good because that means it's great food

I love these sandwiches. Best in the city. I live within minutes of a hive of bahn mi shops, but I will drive across town to get the bbq pork or tofu specials offered by Nhu Y. Perfectly flaky french rolls, (that WILL explode all over you when you bite them -- best eaten standing up), delicious and zingy sauce, great all around.

Delightful service and authentic and delicious Caribbean food. It is off the beaten path for sure, but a very nicely designed place, gracious service and really well made food. Jerk chicken had nice heat, complex flavor, crispy skin and fall off the bone tenderness. Have a red stripe and enjoy!!!!
Four stars because the food is incredible! The staff on the other hand is enough to make you not want to eat there. The attitudes are outrageous and customer service skills are lacking.

First time to try out the evening menu and we were delighted with the meal we got. We'd tried the lunch buffet several times and were pleased with that, so the evening sit down meal was a new thing for us. Worked out great, good food, good prices, and nice place to enjoy our meal in! Try it, you'll like it!
Very nice restaurant. Good food. Great service. Wonderful views. We even saw dolphins.

Great modern setting. The service is great. From the entrance to exit we received exceptional service. We ordered the spring rolls which were good. For entrees we got the jungle fever with tofu which was good but had a little bit of extra salt. He got the Pad Ka Paw which was good as well. As it goes for any Thai place food is a bit on the spicy side. We like it that way but if u like your food on the milder side please inform them.
This is my favorite restaurant hands down. The food is extremely flavorful and they actually listen when you tell them to make it spicy. You haven't lived until you've been here!

I wanted to like this place a lot more than I did. We love Greek food and especially gyros - we were so excited to have a great place in East Nashville. After growing up in Chicago, we've been missing a truly authentic gyro (aka not served with ranch dressing or rice). Unfortunately Greko doesn't fit the bill and we'll stick to Cizar's even though it's also not very authentic. Positives: - Staff. They were so nice and they had tons of people working so everything was moving quickly - Fries. Crispy and seasoned well. Negatives: - Lamb pita. Instead of tender meat shaved and served in a pita like you'd expect, it was pieces of lamb chopped up. Super tough and "crunchy" when I bit into the pita with lots of fat chunks. Not appetizing at all! - Prices. We had 2 pitas, a soda, tea and the feta cheese appetizer which was very small and our total was almost $40. Not exactly street food prices. -Loud. There were barely any people in there and we had to shout to hear each other between the music and the way voices carried with the design. I'm sure this place will improve over time so we'll try again in a few months and see if anything has changed.

I am a picky Cuban-American and my friend is an even pickier Puerto Rican. We were driving by and decided to stop and try Mi Caribe since St. Louis's selection of Latino restaurants leaves something to be desired. What a find! The owner helped us and was very friendly. He took a lot of pride in the restaurant and told us where each piece of art work came from. He informed us that the chef was Dominican and that many of the dishes were prepared Dominican style. My friend wanted the mofongo but was on the fence because she doesn't like Dominican mofongo. The owner assured us that that all of the Puerto Rican customers seemed very pleased with the dish. She ordered one for herself and we both loved it. We were so impressed that we ordered 4 to go to feed our families for dinner. I ordered the vaca con tostones and was equally impressed. The skirt steak was very well seasoned. Even though the steak was on top of the tostones, the tostones were crispy and delicious. I recommend this place to anyone who misses or likes authentic Dominican, Puerto Rican or Cuban food. We'll definitely be returning. UPDATE: After having such a positive experience, my friend and I returned yesterday. Wow, what a change. The service was terrible. We ordered a pork mofongo and a shrimp mofongo. 1+1=2, right? Well, the waitress didn't think so. She only brought the pork mofongo. She argued with my friend about what was ordered, which was very unprofessional. Not to mention the fact that she was flat-out wrong. She said she would bring out the shrimp mofongo in 20 minutes. Instead, she brought a plate of shrimp. Again, she argued about what we ordered and tried to charge us for the plate of shrimp! The owner was sitting nearby and heard the whole ordeal. He never intervened or apologized. Again, very unprofessional and overall terrible, especially for a new restaurant trying to build its reputation. On the upside, the pork mofongo was delicious so props to the chef. I just wish the rest of the experience had been more positive.

I'm from northeast and I have only been to one other vietnamese restaurant in the area where I was underwhelmed by the Pho. This place had good size pho with healthy dose of meats, tripes, meat balls, and other goodies. I still prefer any pho place in northwest though, but for this area it's 4 star in my book.

Good food, very fresh, spicy if you want it to be. Fresh spring rolls, Panang Curry, Pad Ginger are among our favorites. Atmosphere is a bit sterile but the service is good and the people are very friendly. BYOB, plus delivery and take-out.

This review is for delivery only...never ate at the restaurant. Food came lightening fast...I was starving so the promptness made me instantly happy!
