Food was above your standard Chinese delivery fare. The sauces and vegetables were fresh tasting, not frozeny and/or bottled. The hubby even said, "this is good," which, for him, is a lot. I'm a vegetarian, and I had plenty of options. Awesome - definitely recommend!

I was a bit nervous about trying a new cuisine and I absolutely loved it! The owner/manager was helpful in selecting the right dish to start off with and the pho was fabulous! Prices were right, service was terrific, and the ingredients were fresh and expertly prepared. A long drive out there from Carmel, but we will definitely be making the trip out to Avon for Pho 36 again soon!

One of the top spots in Philly for Indonesian food. It is cash only but it's BYOB and the prices are super cheap. Recommendations: - Mie Komplit - Nasi Lemak Rendang - Nasi Goreng Special - Kwetiaw Goreng Service is great -- feel free to ask them for suggestions as well.
This is our "go to" spot..Dine in or carry out the food is always good...the pho is delicious-my husbands favorite is the deluxe. The service is always great and the staff is very friendly

Stopped in for take out. First time trying it. Has a charming but cramped dining room. Signs say BYOB. Looks like a nice place to have dinner. I ordered shrimp coconut soup; small Pineapple fried rice; and Chicken Pad Thai. I was taken back at the $26+ price. Overall, I was not impressed with the food: the broth of coconut soup was very tasty but it was just broth with a few sparse, coarsely chopped, large chunks of red pepper, onions and grocery store, bland pre-sliced mushrooms. The pineapple fried rice was a good portion but just fried rice with 4-5 chunks of pineapple mixed in. The Chicken Pad Thai was very disappointing - the noodles were overcooked, there were no peanuts at all (Pad Thai should have peanuts! for crunch and flavor!!) and there was more Tofu mixed in than chicken in my "Chicken Pad Thai", lame to substitute tofu for meat. Just not that flavorful for Pad Thai. Not sure if I would try again, especially at those prices. Dissapointing because I have heard such good things about them. Was really hoping for a flavorful exotic treat, didn't get it. Nice little place though and the staff was very friendly and helpful when ordering. If you go, bring quarters, parking is primarily street meters. Hard to find parking during peak times.
Went here for the first time about a month ago, I've been back about a dozen times since. Amazing food, amazing prices, great customer service, best water in town.

If you work in or around Cool Springs and want a good lunch spot, Noodles & Company is a really good spot. There's a lot of variety - from Italian, to Japan, to Thai - as well as sandwich and salad options too. Perhaps a bit on the pricier side, it's well worth it when you consider the fresh ingredients, and that everything is made to order - so much so that you can customize any dish - add or remove ingredients as you see fit. Also their website/app make it super easy to order, so you can do a quick pickup if you're in a rush.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Owner is warm, welcoming, and helpful. A husband and wife own this place and my girlfriend and I have never had better Indian food. The husband works the front of the house and they wife prepares the meals in the traditional fashion she learned from her mother. In addition to being the best Indian food in Boise it is also the most vegan friendly establishment we have found in Idaho. Even if you still eat meat I would recommend trying some of the dishes listed as vegan on the menu. With all the delicious flavors you won't miss the meat. You won't regret it and you'll make your cardiologist happt too. :^)

I really like the vibe of the place. It does always appear to be a bit dingy and needs dusting (though maybe that's just the theme). I really enjoy the eclectic furniture. However, the fact that the baristas are never quite friendly and make you feel like an inconvenience more than anything makes me drop the stars. It's a quaint place that could be really warm and welcoming, but it's hard to get past the cold demeanor of some of the workers.

Beautiful, clean restaurant with good food. Friendly waitress and promptly delivered food. What would make my review 5 stars?: 1. Better attention to asking if I wanted another glass of wine. I did but she never came to ask, we had to wave her over after 10 minutes even though there were very few other diners (before 5 pm). 2. HATED the canned tinkly music playing (not Asian) sounded like xylophone or harp in high key that went plink-plink-PLINK and was very annoying. Better choice would be New Age Zen that soothes. 3. They should put fresh rolls on the menu. We asked and they made them (thanks). Also the fried rolls were in egg roll wrappers not rice wrappers. Rice wrappers are better and expected. I had green curry chicken medium hot and it was perfect. Husband to yellow curry beef and he liked it a lot. Large servings which we took home due to over-ordering on purpose. Dumpling appetizers were good not great. Fried rolls good not great (see item 3 above). Coconut soup (not the sour kind) was GREAT! and I ordered an extra to take home. maybe the best I've had anywhere.

I've heard all the hype about this place and can't help but feel like I got gypped. I went on a Thursday around Noon and ordered 3 shortrib tacos for $8. The line was not that long, probably a 15 minute wait. I came back to my desk, sat down, opened the box and my first thought was wow these are pretty. 5 star presentation for a boxed food truck lunch. My tacos had heaping mounds of avocado, fresh cabbage, and all the other veggies. However, I had a hard time locating the short rib. I wondered at first if I was accidentally given a veggie tacos. I dug around and found two quarter sized pieces of short rib in each taco. What gives? Did they run out of meat? Take a look at the photos, there was barely any meat! I'm giving 3 stars because the flavors of the sauce and the veggies were quite good but I was highly disappointed with the lack of short rib.

The food was timely and delicious. We ordered a variety of vegetarian options, including their vegetarian appetizer sampler. Their selection of chutneys was exquisite and the portions of the two entrees we ordered were more than enough for three people. Service was courteous and the Bollywood playing in the background was highly entertaining. I'll definitely be coming back if I'm ever craving Indian food in Norristown. I'd like to check out their lunch buffet!

Sooooo good! They set up at the Penn Relays in Downtown Philly this weekend and I had to try it because the smell was amazing. I travel the entire eastern part of the country and this is some of the best jerk chicken and mac n cheese I have ever had. The owners are so nice. You have to keep an eye out for their truck and give it a try. ~Alexis
Have tried all the Pho's in the vicinity of IV and it's by far the best Pho!!! Try the wontons, your taste buds will love you.

4 1/2 stars. Fresh, tasty, well-balanced healthy salads, sandwiches and soup. Fast, friendly counter service. Clean, airy space. Good value. Lots of variety -- love the chicken and fruit salad; tabouli salad. Could be marginally improved, but it'd be difficult to achieve. Parking can be challenging at lunch time.

had a small pho and some tofu summer rolls. the summer rolls were fine, the soup was not - the broth was mediocre and the meat tasted as bad as it looked (and it looked pretty bad). I spent the next six hours or so feeling like total crap from the megadose of msg, something I have never experienced before as a frequent pho eater. Ive been there before and had a perfectly fine meal, but after this I wont risk a repeat experience.

Delicious indonesian food Must try...mostly all of the food taste so so good, always come back again n again If u r an Indonesian n especially from jakarta or medan, Sky Cafe is the right choice Nothing compares so far

This Indian cuisine is Quick accessible from my work, had a lunch Buffett with colleagues. Overall test is OK, I felt some of the items on the Buffett menu are not authentic in taste. Nice deserts though taste really good n authentic. I advice to give it a try but not up to the authentic mark for some of the non vegetarian curries. Hope this will leave you a good choice.

This place only gets better when ordering from the menu, as do many Indian restaurants. The spice levels at Persis will satisfy most palates, and traditional Indian spice levels are quite good. The regular menu offerings are more generous in portion size than the lunch menu, so be careful not to over order if you're used to their midday meals. All in all, this is one of my favorite Indian spots in the Nashville area, and it is well worth your drive to Mt. Juliet.

Hi Melissa, I never thought of posting comments on yelp until I read your comment about racial discrimination that you claimed is prevalent at Sky Café. Your feedback was amusing. I literally laughed and disgusted at the same time reading your comment below. Mind you when you and I dined in (yes, you read that right) yesterday, it was Columbus Day. The restaurant was so packed and they were short of staff. (I sat at a table a few feet away from you.) Yes, I agree at times the owner could come across as feisty and annoyed. I can attest that her reactions towards the patrons were not based on one's race or ethnicity but towards their rudeness and low mannerisms and behaviors. Have you witnessed and seen some of the requests many of them have asked on that day? This is a restaurant business that caters mostly to Indonesians. The fact that you brought racial discrimination disgust me. As a fellow Indonesian, you need to know that racial discrimination and racial segregation are two sensitive subjects that should be brought up carefully among and with your fellow Indonesians because those touchy subjects can bring back the awful memories of the tragedy of 1998 that many of us had carried and wish to never happen again, ever. Perhaps you need to ask your parents about the root cause of the 1998 Riot that happened in Jakarta and also in many big cities in Indonesia. Many of us have left our beloved country so that we could be safe. Many of us have sacrificed being away from family and children for so long to only start from scratch in America, the land of opportunity -- as long one is willing to work hard and sacrifice A LOT to achieve his or her goals. You should feel fortunate to be having the opportunity to live your life freely in a country where diversity is valued, and good moral is acknowledged. So next time, before you leave a very obtrusive feedback, please be factual. Oh, I hope you are reading this, Melissa.
I absolutely love this place! The food is great, the owners/workers are really nice, and the turnaround time is unparalleled. The spicy drunken noodles w tofu is amazing

The food is good. The people working there are horribly unfriendly and cold. No hello, thank you, good bye, have a nice day, anything. The old lady who works at the counter is especially cold. So next time if I need some pho "to go" I think I will go else where. I hate places that make me feel this way. If you do place an order to go, check your bag to make sure that you have everything...sauce, fork/spoon, napkins.

Don't let the look of this place fool you. From the outside it looks like some kind of hole in the wall place and the inside isn't much better to look at with a handful of tables and chairs and not the cleanest looking environment but the food makes up for any lack of ambiance. I had the grilled pork chop with rice and it was fantastic. Pork chop was cooked beautiful, well portioned, moist on the inside and seasoned beautiful, easily one of the best pork chops I have ever had. Rice was also well cooked and they throw some fresh lettuce and tomato on top just for a little greenery. Great spot to grab a cheap lunch option that will really surprise you once you get past the look.

These kinds of places are really hard to rate because it is all so subjective. I suppose in a smaller town without the excellent Thai places Santa Barbara offers, Meunfan would have scored higher. But the bar has been set high, and so 3 stars is the best I can give. Why? Because it's average. Which isn't to say it's bad, quite the contrary, but if given the option of Meunfan and "Your" other choices (see what I did there?), I'd go to one of them. I ordered the Drunken Noodles, and it was good. But the problem here is that I was pretty hungry, and the portions were on the smaller side of average. So I am leaving hungry, which is not a good thing when one has just eaten. But the food is solid, and tasty. It just wasn't enough given the price. And noodles are cheap, so I don't understand why this is the case. Final thoughts: it's the only Thai place in Goleta on this side of the freeway, so it's convenient. But if you don't mind driving to mid town or lower Milpas, the food is better as well as the value.

For all the Non-Indians. Enjoy the food there but don't call it Indian food. On a rainy Saturday evening and the last weekend alone with wife before the baby enters the outside world. We thought would go on a date night and ended up here. When first walked in I was surprised to see no Indians at the table but all non-Indians. The server takes our order for Kadai Paneer, Roti & naan. We were hungry and waited anxiously for our order. After 15 minutes and our order arrived. While we quickly grabbed the bread and served ourself some curry. The first bite into it and went into future on how good would taste when our kids cook it for the first time @ age of 3. I tried to tell the server that Kadai Paneer doesn't have ketchup on it as I have had it zillion times and he just wouldn't accept. I wish I had printer to print him the recepie. No wonder why it's hidden in the corner and all non-indian customer base. My advice drive few miles around and find a place that serves Indian food Quantity is OK and Rotis are good ( not from clay pot) straight from stove top I don't think I will ever go again even if I am starving. If you like the food enjoy. But please don't bring a shame to Indian food by calling this Indian Hopefully the owner and chef will sit down one day. Get the recipes from YouTube atleast and learn to cook authentic Indian
Great atmosphere and friendly service. Their food is outstanding. As a Shanghainese, I would recommend this place for dining in.

Decent hookah, decent atmosphere, shady location, crappy service, and felt dirty. I came here when I first moved to Philadelphia 4 years ago thinking it was the best place in Philly, but there are many many better places in town with much better/smoother hookah. The location makes it a popular place to be on a Friday night (because it's right next to Penn's Landing on South St.), but if you're looking for good hooks, try University City instead. After trying the other places, definitely would not come back here.

Pretty large buffet for lunch, dinner and weekends. A larger dessert selection than many Indian buffets. The preparation of the food is typical of other area Indian buffets -- lots of stuff in sauces, though. We were not offered menus, so I don't know if they serve more than just the buffet.

Ordered pick up here last night. It was ready promptly and the food was SO good. My boyfriend was craving Indian food and I'm glad he was. We got the garlic naan and a few other things. One of them was very spicy, and it was mild. The other was just perfect. I think I found my go-to place for when I want some comforting take out while I drink wine and binge on Netflix.

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE Jasmine Rice! The layout is slightly better than Sawatdee on South Street, but still tight. I was happy to see that they were busy though since they've just recently opened. The food is incredible! I cannot pronounce what I had, but it was spicy and delicious. Everything is delicious. My husband had the Pad Thai and it was citrusy which was interesting. The waitress asked if it was our first time, we said it was and she said "It won't be your last..." at the time I thought that was rather presumptuous of her, but damn, she was right! I can't wait to go back!!

Okay so I will start by saying that I have never had Jamaican food before, so I have nothing to compare this to! The adventurous palate of my brother in law brought us here. I am not a big fan of spicy, so I was apprehensive. For those of you who don't like spicy, here's what I found: the curry isn't spicy, the ox tail isn't spicy. They both still have TONS of delicious flavor, just nothing to burn your poor delicate throat, like the jerk chicken does (if you like spice, it's apparently excellent...I just don't tolerate spice). The five layer dip, the mango salsa, and the beef patty and coco bread were delicious!! The atmosphere was AWESOME!! Elegant, clean, inviting. The only reason for 4 stars instead of 5? Slow service. I was HUNGRY when I got there, and unfortunately it took quite some time to even place our order, then to begin to receive our appetizers. That said, I found out after we ate that this is a small business run by a husband and wife and their son. She is in the kitchen doing all the cooking, and the husband and the son are doing the rest. I LOVE supporting a small business as they are growing, I just wish I had been prepared- I wouldn't have arrived over-hungry! Perhaps they should give some rolls or something right away to get you started. Just a thought. The food is truly worth the wait, and it was a great experience!! I look forward to going back.

I keep coming back to this place, and am always happy. Their take-out portions are very very generous, and a great value. I almost always end up ordering the Navratan Korma, which they make very spicy on request. It has all the vegetables I crave, and even sometimes comes with paneer cheese, which is a nice surprise. The raita sauce cools down the heat and balances the flavors. The take-out portion makes two good meals for me. The buffet is good too when I'm in the mood for something quick, although I usually prefer to have leftovers. Although I found I prefer the chicken dishes on the buffet at Sitar, Tandoor's samosas and desserts are much better. I would say for the buffet I would switch between Sitar and Tandoor. I enjoyed my meal at New Dehli as well, but in the end I always end up back at Tandoor.

I've been here three times. They're slow. Everytime I've come we waited a long time for food. You just get the impression that they don't know what they're doing. The menu items sound fancy but fall short each time. Additionally, the inside needs renovation. This last time, I ordered the tuna melt special, crab soup and 2 orders of chicken fingers for my family. The food is fresh. The fries that came with the chicken fingers are way over cooked. Some are almost black...all of them fries are floppy, not crispy at all. I can't fathom why this would be ok to serve to someone. The chicken fingers are breaded and cooked well but have no absolutely no seasoning. My wife and daughter wouldn't eat them so that was wasted money. The tuna melt was just ok. The salad that came with it was the best part, with fresh veggies and fresh vinaigrette. The crab soup was good though. It had good flavor. I'm just disappointed each time. If you like good food, go elsewhere...which would be outside the area because we have nothing in Harrison Township.

We were told 45 mins for delivery of pad Thai and curry and it took 1 hour 45 mins to arrive. We had to call the restaurant 4 times and the driver 5 times. They told us 10 mins every time we called. Incredibly frustrating experience. The manager gave a refund on the final call. Somehow the food was still warm.

This is a a great place to try some Ethiopian food! The service is good and the food is amazing. I split the meat combo platter for 2, and it was a lot of food. But all the meats are tender and flavorful, and the vegetables are delicious! My favorite was the lamb and the greens, but my boyfriend loved the chicken and lentils. And the best part is the bread they serve with it. It seems like a cross between a pancake and a crepe, but very sour. It goes perfectly with their food, and since you eat with your hands, it makes eating much easier. We also tried their hot tea and honey wine. The tea was yummy. The honey wine had bits of wax in it (beeswax?) and was really strong but delicious! If you're driving, don't down the whole thing by yourself. I can't wait to come back and try more food.

Belly dancing like, all the time, man. That's kinda weird, but also kinda cool. And a little unnerving when the gyrating hips of a pretty woman are coming between me and a plate of gyros. Get back, Dancing Woman! But yeah, aside from that, Momo's is a pretty cool place! It's walking distance from our house, so whenever I feel a gyros craving wash over me (which is surprisingly more often than most would assume), we head over to Momo's. I'll be honest--I haven't tried too much on the menu because I really do just stick to the gyros and tzatziki. Last time, Justin had the falafel, which I thought was interesting with its smooth interior. Not your usual falafel and personally, not my favorite. The gyros is my favorite, but you've probably gathered that by now. I love the outdoor seating on nice evenings and I haven't actually ever eaten inside, but I love the decor and it looks like a comfortable, stylish, inviting space. Not so sure about the Greek (?) techno, but whatev. Service is pleasant, prices are fair and sharing means caring, so get yourself some mezes. (I should talk; I hog all that gyros to myself!)

First off - looks can be deceiving. The interior of this place is like a tricked out 70's den that the owners have spruced up with asian restaurant fare. You can sit on little pillows at your table at some seats, but thats about it for ambiance. Do NOT let that sad looking mostly typical chinese buffet up front upset you - do not order from it. Order from the menu. I am an omnivore through and through, but I like to get classic thai dishes here (curries and yummy gingery or peanut-y noodles) made with the tofu, they do tofu right here! Crispy and soft on the inside, not too greasy either. The Thai tea is pretty standard and they could work on getting things out a little quicker when you eat in-house, but other than that my neighborhood joint will keep getting my thai food craving love.

The menu was inventive and fun - totally unexpected! They also have almost everything available gluten free. Definitely one of my new favorites. Had the Pad Thai and it was yummy and authentic; the server was great and even brought some extra chili dipping sauce of his own suggestion! Would definitely, and will, go back.
Tried the lunch buffet today and it was delicious! As expected - lots of options, hot, fresh, tasty. We will be back!

This place may be overlooked because of the location. Parking is challenging and limited, but if you find a place to park, go for it. It is a small place and the wait time takes awhile for your food to arrive, even if you get it to go. I ordered combination(house) fried rice. The rice wasn't mushy or hard. The beef and shrimp weren't overcooked. Very enjoyable meal. The portions are also a generous size.
First real lounge I've been to in Tennessee. Everything is wonderful with this place. Wish I could live closer

Great customer service Waiters visit frequently Water is refilled Clean Decorations aesthetically pleasing Food is warm and fresh You can control the level of spicy you want On time service (not much of a wait time) Waiters/waitresses are friendly and considerate

It doesn't look like much from the outside. And, in fact, it doesn't look like much from the inside. But I'll be damned if the food isn't good and the price is nice... real nice. We've only recently expanded into Thai and Siamese Princess is now our lock-down restaurant of choice.

God, the problem with this place is the SERVICE is so hit or miss. The FOOD can alternate between good and great too. Lately it has been CRAP. I have been going here for over three years and I noticed that at times they can care LESS if you are served or attended to. The younger servers, when they are working that night, are great. They are efficient, polite, and get your check for you reasonably on time. The other servers? HORRIBLE. You may sit there an HOUR before you get your check served, and almost as LONG waiting for it to get back to you. I flagged down the lady, made eye contact, asked politely, and was ignored. She was NOT even BUSY! Am I a second class citizen? it is so odd that you can have such polarized service at this establishment. What a shame! I can't believe I went nearly 8 months without crappy service here. Wishful thinking that it would always have good service. TIP #1: Just walk up to the counter and ask for the damn check. TIP #2: If it isn't the younger servers overall working that day, good luck to you. You have to be proactive for service during your stay more likely then not. p.s. Don't leave GRATUITY or TIP if they treat you like dirt. why reward crappy service? Some days the food is tasty, cooked fresh! Other days, its just downright soggy. It should be sizzling if it is served on the skillet and hot, not luke warm, cold, and boggy. Its almost like there are days the cook is there and other days he pre-cooks that food at an earlier time and then it is reheated. Who knows. TIP #3: Don't have high expectations for your grilled meat from the kitchen, unless you are grilling the food yourselves at the tabletop grill. People crap on the new competitior Joo Joo's Korean restaurant next door. I admit that Hangook Kwan restaurant can have better food.. the keyword is "can". hangook usually cooks their food better than Joo Joo's while Joo Joo's undercooks their food. However, keep in mind this: Joo Joo's has: 1. Much, MUCH better customer service. 2. Cheaper dish prices. 3. More side dishes included in the meal. Now if only I can combine the best qualities of both these restaurants into one... In conclusion, there are few Korean restaurants in the St. Louis region.. so I may .. let me rephrase, " i have no choice" but to be back at one of these restaurants int he next few months.... just not for awhile now. I need a break from the crappy customer service here at Hangook Kwan restaurant. they make me so angry.

We've been going here for years. It's so good that I get angry if anyone eats my leftovers. This is one of the places where the items we ordered are so good, we rarely get anything else off the menu. Lamb korma, shahi paneer and basmati rice with naan. Even our kids now eat it!

Undoubtedly one of the best Vietnamese restaurants in Indy. This place lacks true true authenticity but it makes up for it by being very flavorful. The egg rolls had a traditional filling which was tasty but the ratio of filling to crust was waay off, it was difficult to cut the roll because the shell was soo thick. They also should have been served with enough lettuce to wrap each egg roll individually instead of the single leaf they give you. Each roll (of 3) was also the size of an average index finger so really it's only enough to whet your appetite but it was cheap and tasty so w/e. The fish sauce was one of the best in the midwest, maybe needs a hint more tang to be perfect. I think the problem is that their pickling sauce for the carrots & turnip aren't tangy enough and they also don't include it in their fish sauce like many other restaurants. The rice dish was the best part of the meal, it had one of the most tender pork chops I've had, seared in a soy sauce marinade. They didn't have shredded pork skin which was a bummer and the egg loaf had a seafood-y taste which is unconventional but it was still very delectable. The side-cup of broth had good color and decent body but really lacked the deep savory salty flavor of a great broth, the heavy peppering draws your attention from this fact though. The least likeable thing was the special sandwich which came out a little burnt an was way too skimpy on the meat and lacked jalapeños. They did, however, have pate (ground liver) and the traditional mayo which are absolutely required in this French-inspired sandwich. The coffee was perfect although I was sad they didn't let it drip at the table side in a French press like the picture showed; it's part of the unique experience you only get at vietnamese restaurants. Overall this place was great despite all my quibbles. I enjoyed my meal thoroughly with the excellent fish sauce, tender pork chop, and delicious coffee. There is certainly room to improve but this place is one of the best I've had in the Midwest.
Fresh, spicy and delicious. Well worth the wait. Flavorful and exotic. Will return...and return.

Brought the family for dinner on Thursday evening. Francisco's was packed but we had a lovely table for 6 reserved in the fireplace room. Everyone loved their good. Delicious! Our waitress, Sonia, was wonderful! Efficient, attentive and very sweet. Great experience!!

First things first, let's not call this place an Indian Chipotle equivalent. There are many differences and most of those make this s terrible place to eat at: 1. What's up with the tiny portion sizes - you start to doubt the intentions of the restaurant when they serve you four chickpeas (from chickpea curry), 3 pieces of paneer, half a spoonful of curry (in such small quantity they should call it sauce instead), and half a bite of everything else. Their bowl may give you the impression of a chipotle bowl but it is quite shallow and only half filled with food. Chipotle, a place I frequent enough to know this, fills you up with food for 8-9 bucks. Zaika's bowl costs around the same and is only about half the food. Their margins must be astronomically high. I'd be an investor but not s customer. 2. Indian food is flavorful and tastier than what they serve here. Maybe it's because of only half a spoonful of curry that I don't taste the Indian spices/flavors. Nah, I'm kidding, everything here is very bland and lacking in flavor. Chipotle's food is much more flavorful by comparison. 3. Serving a side of $1.75 naan bread on the side of a $9 rice bowl makes little sense unless you want more bland to go on the side of bland mess that is the rice bowl. All things said, I'm not coming back here unless they increase their portion sizes. When I go to a restaurant, I want to taste the food and I want to feel that they want me to enjoy their food. When they serve me in a stingy fashion (read 4 chickpeas, 3 paneer cubes), I doubt their intentions. Let's see how long they can keep in business like this. On second thoughts, I wouldn't be an investor here either.
Service was great. Food was average, but the Thai iced tea was pretty great. Prices were reasonable.

Seasons has really good Banh Mi, Boba, Bun Bo Hue, and shaved ice. Every time I had a visitor, this was the first place I would take them to. This is like the only place in Saint Petersburg that serves that type of desserts/food well. the only thing I don't like about this place is how pricey it is. A cup of boba costs up to 4$, like come on, I can easily get that for a cheaper price in a bigger city.
I'd say the best fried rice in North County. I love the other sides they have as well.

Lived across the street from here for a year and always meant to try it. Finally made it in about 6 months ago and my wife and I have been back at least 5 times since. Outstanding food(not as spicy as a lot of indian places you encounter),great service,and a very relaxed atmosphere. Have not made it in for the buffet yet but i hear its top notch.
My favorite thai in Tampa. The Tom yum soup is out of this world. Also recommend the Panang curry. Service is great. Excellent for lunch as well.

How have I not reviewed you yet, Remedy Cafe? This is the perfect place for those who want Indian food at a great price,dessert or a snack. They have a deal with samosas ans chai for two for 12$. I go for the Kashmir chai - it different from usual chai (which they also have) because it's caffeine-free and green in color and has pistachios in it. So delicious and I've never seen it anywhere else. As well, they always have a ton of dessert choices (pies, cakes, etc.) in the cooler and the selection seems to change quite a bit so you can try something new. They seem to have lots of vegan & vegetarian options for food and desserts, so if I was a vegan, I'd go there even more. If you're lucky, one of the armchair pairs in the front window will be free. It's pretty uncommon, though - this place seems to be busy every day at any time. And rightly so.

I used to love them - I even voted for them at the Vendy Awards last year. Now the thought of them just irritates me. Why are they are SO slow now? Why?? One time I ordered the jerk chicken (which is normally pre-stewed) w/ greens and cabbage - it took over 20 minutes and I was the only one there at the time. My next most recent experience was even worse. Went during lunch - ordered the jerk chicken w/ greens and french fries. 25 min passes... no food. A guy walks up to order and gets his food in less than 5 minutes. So after he pays, I ask the staff what the deal was? I ordered forever ago and still no food. He says, the fryer is frying really slowly so if you still want the fries, it will take a long time. What?!?! How can a fryer fly slowly!? Does it mean the oil frying food at a super low temp, therefore causing you to have the oiliest fries ever bc it just soaks?! Why didnt they tell me 25 min ago?! And why didn't they put the fries in the fryer 25 min ago?! Totally inexcusable. Definitely never returning.

I've been eating here for the past year... The service is always fast and friendly. The food is always hot and tasty... While I like pho, here I mostly have the grilled pork chops and broken rice with a bubble tea to go... I might need a remedial chopstick eating class....lol.. I usually wind up with a messy shirt while eating pho with those plastic type of chopsticks
Really great food with a great staff. We always enjoy going. We try to eat here first before seeing a movie in the same plaza.

First thought: wow, this place has 5 stars...After eating: Wow, this place deserves all 5 stars and more! Everything about this place is rockstar. The ambiance is adorable, I feel like I'm eating in the owners' very own dining room. The food is made fresh and is delicious! We ordered the spicy beef patty and chicken curry patty, both were awesome appetizers. Spicy beef was not too spicy, just the perfect amount of kick. We ordered the tilapia and jerk chicken. The tilapia was flavorful, perfectly buttered, and texture was as good as any. The jerk chicken packed a spicy punch, which if you are looking for good jerk chocked - that's what you mean. Owners were so pleasant and both stopped by our table to chat. We had an unbelievable experience and will tell anyone we know that visits Tampa they need to stop at Yah Mon!

Haveli got the price point working for them. At $6.99 (after coupon), the lunch buffet is fulfilling and alleviates your Indian fix. There were about 8-10 entrees to choose from plus a salad bar, par for the course for an Indian buffet. The goat curry and chicken curry were solid, while most of the other items were decent. The chicken masala and paneer masala tasted a little too milky for me. The naan (plain or garlic) was quite good and was brought to the table by the server. Don't be shy about using the coupon. You will need that dollar back for parking if you are not within walking distance.

This is one of our favorites in Pasco County. Truly fresh, truly wonderful, truly amazing all around. You will not leave disappointed by anything. The menu offers many vegetarian, macro/micro biotic, and gluten free options- more than any other Thai or Asian restaurant we have been too. The staff are genuinely friendly and care about their clientele. This is our "go to" spot and it has never, ever let us down. We love you Orchids Thai!

Thai 5 is awesome. We had visited the Kombo Kitchen truck back in the day and had only been back once since it turned into Thai 5. We definitely won't be staying away in the future - it's definitely the best Thai we have found in South Tampa, and some of the best in the Tampa Bay area! My favorite is definitely the Thai sausage. We got the drunken noodles last night and they were good, but not as good as the other dishes we have had from there (my old favorites were crab fried rice and padwoonsen). Their fresh rolls are delicious, especially the peanut sauce which tastes homemade. I know others have complained about pick-up times, but we were quoted 25-30 minutes and I'm pretty sure it was done quicker than that (it was ready when we arrived to pick it up). Love me some Thai 5!
This place is great! My daughter that is not vegetarian and is very picky enjoys dining here. Everything I have tried has been excellent. Highly recommended.

P.F. Chang's, what happened to you? We went with friends of ours, one of whom is allergic to mushrooms. Bad decision. The allergen menu had somewhere in the neighborhood of three items for him. Amy the waitress was extremely rude to our table, including making a disparaging comment about the fact that our other friend was allergic to tree nuts. We ordered two appetizers - Lettuce Wraps and string beans. The appetizers that came out? Lettuce Wraps and Calamari. The waitress was rude about this as well, saying "I guess I'll let you keep it without charging you for it." Dessert was not even safe from them. Our friend had the mini dessert, thinking it would be something normal sized. Her tiramisu was served in a shot glass.

I come here often for their sweet treats. The cakes are stacked high and super moist and fresh. They change everyday. The owner is the baker and chef and she is always up front and visible. They also have heathy options and a nice wine selection.
Great food and atmosphere. We sat in front of the wood burning fireplace, had a belly dancer stop by, and dined on greek tapas. It doesn't get any better.
Wonderful atmosphere with delicious food. The group platters come with plenty of eats--enough for leftovers--and you get your money's worth. Must try.

Before our experience last night, I would have definitely placed this restaurant at 4 stars, for the take-out alone. However, our experience at their Valentine's Buffet was so terrible, that I hesitate to even go for the three. Know this- almost everyone can agree that the food here is on point. I only wish I had been able to sample more of it at their advertised Valentine's special. They ran out of food; they ran out of plates. Some foods were hastily refilled using large salad bowls and adding to the leftover sauce that had been sitting under the lamps, while others were never seen again (or in the first place) Dinner plates were replaced with salad plates, and with sauce heavy food, it made eating awkward. The staff was obviously overwhelmed. From other reviews, perhaps having a full restaurant is unusual for this location. They were snipping at each other, and at us, as we had to ask for our check 3 different times. I ate a fraction of a dinner, and was charged $20 (per person) - more than twice the cost of their normal lunch buffet, which sounds far more efficient and with actual food. Despite feeling very upset about our experience, I did feel bad for the staff, as we were not the only ones unhappy, but were far more quiet than other patrons. I am sure it was a frustrating evening for everyone involved. Take-out from here is delicious, but I would not come here for a holiday special (and they have several more advertised) again.

This place is so so so good! I love caribbean food, and jerk hut doesn't quite cut it for me. I went to Yah Mon a few weeks ago, and I can not wait to go back. The food tastes extremely authentic, and the service was amazing. There was only one person running the show out on the floor, and between all the people there, he did a great job checking up on everyone. The inside is very well put together and is perfect for catching up with a friend, or going solo after work on a weekday. If you're considering Caribbean food, consider Yah Mon. I promise it won't disappoint!!!

This place is AWESOME! If you want to treat your taste buds come here! We had the duck w/ asparagus & mushroom, the pork w/ vegetables .. Both were incredible! The soup and appetizers were tasty. Be sure to try the papaya salad - delicious!!

I've been here a few times, and they are often busy but once your order is in, the chefs are fast! Sometimes the service is slow, and I've noticed multiple times that they seemed understaffed which is why it may have taken a while to seat us. Though the food here is pretty good! I've had better around New Orleans, but this place always seems a little more convenient, and when delivered through post-mates it maintains its quality! I love the green tea boba drink here, it's not too sweet like a lot of places. I also always get the lemongrass chicken vermicelli, with light noodles and extra veggies. One time I got it with "very light noodles, extra extra veggies" and they even added some carrots, broccoli and onions, which aren't normally included in the vermicelli dish, but were surprisingly tasty! Overall it always satisfies my craving for noodles and boba tea, and it's in a lovely location, so I'll continue to come here!
Excellent food and service. Great dishes and a well run family restaurant. Can't beat their lunch buffet.

Wowza! This place rocks and the staff is so cool. This was my first time dining at an Indian restaurant and between our friends (been before) and the owner, we got to try some awesome dishes ranging from mild to spicy. The cheese naan is to die for (had to order a double batch) and is perfect for dipping in all the amazing sauces. Atmosphere is cozy and intimate and drink prices are reasonable. I highly recommend if you're an experienced cultural eater or someone wanting to spread your taste bud wings!

Beer, a well-packed hookah that burned for 3 hours and falafels for 20 bucks. A little run-down inside but exactly what we wanted. It turned into a bit of a sports bar too, with the playoffs on, and a hookah. Great place.

This restaurant never ceases to amaze me. Everything I have gotten here has been fresh and made to order. The hummus is out of this world. The chicken Greek salad is from another planet. The gyros are delish! The beef kabobs are cooked to perfection. The shish kabob has flavors of the Mediterranean. Just everything is damn good ok! Except....unfortunately the hot wings. The locals who live around that area buy them because this is like the only place where you get get fresh food at 2-4am in the morning. But they are lackluster to say the least. But go for all of the Mediterranean dishes and you are sure to have a great experience. If you dine in, they even bring your plate to you. That was a surprise being that it does appear to be a fast food like restaurant.

The food and service was excellent. My wife and I visited the restaurant for a date night. We really enjoyed the atmosphere and the food. The curry patties were excellent but I recommend ordering the curry chicken or the browns stew chicken. Great flavors. Would definitely go back to this restaurant.
Great taste and very fresh. I got the Pad Thai lunch special - great quantity/quality for the price. I would definitely recommend it.

As far as the food goes, this place is good. As far as the service goes, this place is great! The prices, the delicious dishes, and the stellar location make this place a no brainer for any local or tourist. What makes this place special though is the staff. I can honestly say I have eaten here monthly for the past three years and have never had a bad experience.

Absolutely delicious! We LOVE Indian food, and have tried tons of restaurants in the area, but were very, VERY underwhelmed each one of them. Thank goodness we found Guru's last night! We were delighted to discover that this little restaurant in Newtown is on par with some of the best Indian restaurants we've visited in New York City (not even joking). The staff is attentive, friendly, and generous (they brought out complimentary appetizers while our dinner was being prepared, and a complimentary dessert afterward). After suffering through bland, uninspired Indian in the area, Guru's is a breath of fresh air. Our dishes were beautifully spiced (the chicken tikka masala and the shrimp nawabi korma were exquisite), the prices were very reasonable, and we loved the family atmosphere. Guru's is exactly what Newtown needed to spice up its restaurant scene!

I really like this place. I've bought their groupons twice. The salad (first one on the menu, I don't remember name) is really good, with some crunchy bread inside and olive oil dressing. Super fresh. I also like to order their catch of the day with Libanese rice. Tried their falafels as well, I liked them. With groupon the restaurant wouldn't be too expensive. The groupon is $27.5 towards $50, so end of the day for two people you would probably spend $40-$50 for totally. Reasonable price.

Their Tapas are pretty good size and delicious! We tried the falafel plate and the gyro plate. They were both good. The roasted red pepper soup was the best roasted red pepper soup I ever had. They also have happy hour with $2 Sangrias, beer and wine. The service at this place was good as well. I will be back here.
Excellent amber house beer, similar to Kilian s. Excellent blackened mahi tacos. I will be back.

If you told me there's a cart that doesn't have any menu, doesn't sell any drinks, and has a bunch of plants, garlic hanging all over, I'd say where is it?! You really can't miss this truck because there's always smoke coming out and a bunch of plants. The line can get quite long so make sure you come here before noon to beat the rush. You could wait until 20-30 minutes easy. You don't even need to say anything when you get up to order, you just pay the man - sorta like the soup nazi. The ingredients are fresh and there's tons of flavor into the food. For $7-8 bucks, you will always get a lot of charcoal grilled chicken with two falafel balls, pita, salad. He mixes up the sides between rice, champagne grapes, corn on the cob, apples, etc. It's a really big meal and quite filling. I've gotten some chicken that was very burnt so it wasn't that great. But when it's grilled right, it's banging. The falafel isn't the best - I'd probably go to Mama's right up the street. But the mystique of what you're going to get is amazing and keeps me coming back.

The one and only place I will go for pho. We have tried other places and their broth does not even come close to the flavor Pho an Hoa has. Whether we have dined in or had take-out, we have never had a bad experience! Everything has been made of the freshest ingredients. The spring rolls are also delicious!!

The reviews for Sofra don't lie! When you walk in, the decor is welcoming and themed very tastefully, even equipped with a large trojan horse. Perhaps its casual fine dining. Its classy but not stuffy. There are two menus - meze/tapas downstairs and fine dining upstairs. The waitress was super friendly and let us review both menus before we decided where to sit. We opted for the dining room although I encourage anyone to try the meze's because their appetizers are amazing! The chef prepared, seasoned, and grilled all our food to perfection. Everything is so fresh. I have never been to Turkey so I can't speak for authenticity, but they chefs here take their food seriously! It's like, Food Network worthy! So far, I've been so lucky to have tried the stuffed apricots, stuffed grape leaves, the meat platter, the veggie plate, hummus and baklava. Everything was shockingly delicious. The baklava is homemade and fresh. I don't even like baklava but this baklava is amazing!

The food is terrific - every dish we had was wonderful. Chicken Tikka Masala was excellent, as was the onion kulcha. The Butter sauce was delicious - a mild, creamy, tomato-based sauce that is great for first timers. Amit is an amazing waiter who even entertained our group (of 13 in the small private room) with some pretty awesome magic tricks. Excellent food and great value!

We've been coming to this restaurant for years (almost 7 years) and we've been ordering the same menu over and over again everytime we come here for dinner or just carryout. The food that we ordered always between pad see eew, menu no 35, menu no 35 A, tom yum dried noodle without the soup, or choo chee with fish. Most of the time we come on saturday evening, rarely we come here on sunday because the food always "taste different". From our experience, everytime we come here on saturday evening the food always EXCELLENT but if we come here at different day like thursday or sunday evening, i would say the food always awfully oily and bland (not good and disappointed). We asked the staff about the chef, maybe they change the cook and they said no, they have regular cook in the kitchen. But again your tounge never lies when it comes to good food, if you've been coming and eating the same food here for years, 1000000% you'll notice it right away different chef must be cooking your food. Which is okay, as long the taste is good and everything still the same. So today, i gave it a try again ordered the same menu with super thai spicy means really spicy (they failed me more than 4times if i come at different day but saturday), the food says "stir fried with red curry paste, eggplant, green beans", once i get inside the car and opened my food "THey Failed me AGAIN" i was so upset seeing my food with tons of oil (half of big plastic cup), no sign of red curry paste, no taste of salt at all, no green beans, and not spicy at all not even little bit!!!! And for sure, wrong menu!! Aarrrgghhh huge disappointment thai country restaurant!! Please fix the food and tell the chef to follow what is the ingredients on the menu booklet.

Not a place I would visit if I didn't know any better. The food here is excellent. I was first introduced to Palace of Asia in Lawrenceville. You would never think the two are related. The restaurant in Lawrenceville is opulent, polished and beautifully decorated, and the exterior is welcoming to by passers. Definitely come here for their lunch buffet. There is a vast variety of Indian curry and chutneys, as well as tandoori roasts. This is probably the best Indian food I've tasted in this area, and I would put it up next to any restaurant in London. My only complaint is the Curry's are not spicy enough.

Many better options out there, here's why: Portion sizes unsuitable for anyone other than an adolescent female, we had to ask for utensils, we then had to ask for napkins, no one asked "how's your food" or ever came to check on us, water was not offered... Although prices were not touristy/high, I would not return. Choose another restaurant on this strip.

Tried the Bun (Vermicelli). It's not bad. Solid. But I prefer thicker noodles -- they use thinner vermicelli, and I'm not impressed with the iceberg lettuce they throw in there. Even green leaf or romaine, maybe, but iceberg? More herbs would have been nice. Beef wrapped in grape leaves was interesting -- first time I've had Vietnamese grape leaves! Tasty but they don't fit into my Bun experience that well. Pork and Shrimp were nicely chargrilled with that chargrilled flavour, but the pork seemed a bit overcooked. They have 2 hot chili sauces on the table (besides Srirachi). One is roasted, the other is fresh. The fresh red one is really nice, flavourful, and has a lot of kick -- if I needed chili sauce with my food, I'd definitely come here for that. (I don't really need it for Bun.) 3+ stars

Would have loved to try it! We walked in at 8:15, they close at 9. We were waiting on friends and were confused about the locations, so asked an employee about it, who told us there were multiple locations, and added 'you better decide soon because we close at 9.' That could have been 5 paying customers who ordered Pho. Shrug.

Stopped here for lunch today after driving to the St Louis airport on a practice run. Good find! Relaxing atmosphere with amber glass chandeliers, soft Rat Pack music. I'm finding more and more that the dining experience l really enjoy is one that can help me forget all the trouble in the world if but for an hour. This place did that for me. I had the special, chicken stuffed with spinach with a lemon wine sauce came with rice and broccoli. Great value at $10 especially since l took half home for dinner. It was excellent. My husband enjoyed his gyro and Greek beer. Lovely lunch!

We were greeted by very friendly waitresses in authentic dress and sat at a table with intricately carved scenes of Thailand beneath the glass. Service was efficient, helpful, and citrus, and the food was the best Thai food we have had in Florida. My wife ordered the pineapple chicken curry. Jasmine added a hint of peanut sauce that gave it an excellent flavor. I had the beef basil, which was not too spicy at there starts but very flavorful. The Thai iced tea was very creamy. The prices were very reasonable. Highly recommended.

This is my Indian/Pakistani restaurant. I love this place. Just got back from an Express Lunch where they treated me to a wonderful chicken kardhi, fluffy rice and perfect naan. There are two more Indian restaurants in the area and I've been to both. After I tried Tandoor India I can no longer visit those places. Sorry, but I found my Indian/Pakistani niche.
Good food. Good price. Can't complain. Went there twice when I stay in tampa. Friend recommend it. It's a nice little family own restaurant. But the side is good and price is right.

Had a great meal here. Plentiful choices for vegetarians. Four of us shared all dishes and everything was spiced really well, with no overpowering heat. BYO. Owners/Chefs were super nice. Its a small space, so good to call ahead to check on table availability.
Cat can cook !!!!!.... And the sushi is fresh and delightful.... We eat here once a week for years......It has always been very very good.... VERY RECOMMENDED
We got here for lunch. We was happy for the service- waitress were friendly and helpful, foods came out a bit slow but it was good and tasty. Highly recommend their papaya salad and seafood tom yum.
Awesome food. Awesome service. Awesome freshly squeezed fruit juices. Just all around awesome. And it's a byob.

I arrived with the highest of expectations and everything about this place exceeded them. The atmosphere and decor, the waitstaff and their dress code, and the cuisine and culinary genius. The food was fresh and inspired. Unique flavors and textures. The cocktails were incredible. I went with my two kids for Mother's Day. It was just perfect. Thank you for creating this space of delight, abundance and joy that feeds both body and soul. Highest Praise for Suraya.

*** vegan review *** i got probably the worst tofu dish i've ever had at pho hoa. it was basically fried salty spicy tofu and some green peppers, no other veggies. really bad. look elsewhere in this hood for vegan fare.

Just disappointed. I love a good gyro and had high hopes. Ordered the super chicken gyro and the thing was a huge mess. Way too much hummus and the flavors didn't mesh well at all. After a while just found it impossible to eat.

This is my favorite Thai spot in Santa Barbara. Amazing food. We have travelled all over the US trying different Thai resturants, and only one Thai place ( In Flagstaff, AZ), was as good as Muen Fan. I usually eat lunch there, and the usually get served by the owner. Usually order the Pad Thai (amazing), but have been branching out to the Fried eggplant with chicken- sounds horrible but its the yummiest thing I have ever eaten, and now I get it regularly.
Very bad taste for a vegetarian person from Indian subcontinent, quality of raw ingredients is rotten. Avoid if you understand and appreciate Indian vegetarian food.
This place a bit pricier than your average fair, but well worth the experience. Great food with original flavor combinations. Good date spot.

This is a cute little place. I am boring and unadventurous so I ordered pad thai with tofu and it was excellent. The portions could be a little larger for the price, but that's just me wishing I had been able to have leftovers. I would go here more often if they weren't cash only. I don't always have time to run to the ATM.

Eat Well is a small convenience store in Mid City, that happens to also have a food counter. The Good: Their banh mi is hands down the best banh mi that I've had without having to travel to the Westbank, or New Orleans East. It's big, and it's reasonably priced. The So So: The service can be slow, and isn't exactly personable. But I honestly don't care. Just give me mah banh mi. The Bad: It's in sketch area, and there's no parking.

going here on a triple dinner date was quite nice on this nice spring-like night and i believe we got the only large table that could fit us all! it is a small place, so come early. it gets crowded fast due to the good food and cheap prices. there are plenty of veggie options and they do offer fish and meat for us carnivores like myself. yay! but bring cash! cash only here. also, this place is byob. i started out with the thai tea. yums. the fresh spring rolls were just that, fresh! the veggie dumplings are delicious. whether you get sticky rice with sauteed lemongrass, shallots, and chicken or if you get curry soup and jasmine rice, there is sure to be something on this menu to please every mouth! the meal ended with fried banana with honey. of course, i was the only one that got dessert. the smallest girl at the table, but i always leave room for dessert! it's how i roll.

Extremely disappointing. Invited my friend and family for dinner. There were eight of us and we ordered variety of dishes. Every single dish including the appetizers were loaded with salt. If a restaurant cares for the customers, they should not put so much salt in the food.

I have been there several times. Food is very average and pretty bland. Service is really bad and slow. Very difficult to even get salt and pepper. They did not even have ketchup for burger and fries. Good atmosphere and great location. Food has really gone down hill

Abyssinia is a fantastic place to eat! It's great for groups, and everyone I've ever dined with there immediately becomes a fan. All the vegetarian options, so far as I know, are also vegan. The carnivores I go with can attest to how delicious the vegan options are. I ate here twice last week and am contemplating going next week. The service is attentive, & their accents are amazingly beautiful.
Absolutely amazing food! Great for vegetarians and omnivorous alike. I highly recommend the spicy awaze lamb tibbs.

This is my very favorite Thai restaurant and I have tried many. Relaxed atmosphere , friendly prompt service and delicious Thai food. I am a sweet tooth and someone gave me a taste of their sticky black rice dessert and I was hooked, sounded odd but tasted divine. If you enjoy Thai food you can't go wrong at this place.

I have gotten dinner from here a few times since it first opened and both the food and service have gone downhill. My husband got a babaganoush bowl and they barely put enough to cover the bottom of the bowl. They also skimped when it came to the protein and toppings. I witnessed a lady asking for more tahini sauce and there was a lot of back and forth between 2 employees about whether or not they could provide it - she even said she would pay extra for it and they responded by saying that they can't charge for it so eventually they unwillingly gave her one additional little dollop of it. It just seems like they're trying to skimp all around to save themselves a few bucks. The employees seem like they don't want to be there and can't even bring themselves to appear friendly to customers.
So good! Got the Caribbean Chicken Platter and was 3 home runs! Knocked it out of the park on all 3 dishes!!

Amazing! I was hesitant to try this place because I live close by and didn't want to get addicted.....but I went and I am. I had both dinner last night and breakfast today. Everything is awesome and we will be back....probably tomorrow.

I had a very pleasant 4 star experience an Nooddi - but it is really a 3 star kinda place (needs a makeover!). But - I happened to get there before 6 PM and got the early dinner special which is a great value. A cup of Tom Kha soup. 2 steamed crab dumplings (delish!) and a generous portion of Chicken or Tofu Pad-See-Yu. Loved every bite. And my wallet thanked me. Great service - place was empty on a Thursday at 5:40 PM. No, it's not the best Thai ever - but it'll do and I will be back - and likely soon.

I'm in a love-hate relationship with Fulin's. They have good chinese food, and their singapore noodles are excellent; however, their sushi is sub-par at best. If they concentrated on purely on one form of cuisine I'm sure they would be great, but the mix of branded "Chinese-Japanese" is just not a win for them. The atmosphere, seating, and service are average and what I would expect from a restaurant; however, the bartender's service when I come in after work for a drink and quick meal is above average and more than I would expect. The sushi is a mix. The rice has the nice sweet, soft flavor I would expect; however, the fish normally has that distinct fishy smell and taste that let's me know it is past it's prime. The nigiri shows that this is yet another restaurant with sushi where the chef does not know how to properly apply the wasabi; however, at least they don't over do it like some other places. Dollar-for-dollar, this is an average restaurant, and I make sure that I come here every now and again for the singapore noodles and a scotch.

Ate there for the first time tonight & we'll definitely go back! I ordered the chicken Udon and it was fabulous. My husband had the teriyaki chicken and said it was delicious. Everything was fresh and authentic. The service was excellent and the staff was friendly.

I want to be honest about this post: I am comparing this to my amazing meals and experiences I have had at Masala Café. Reading the varied reviews I was eager to try this restaurant, which is quiet close to the motel where we are staying during our home renovation. Strike One: did not have cabernet, although it is on the menu. (Really, no one could make a run to Sam's club or even across the street to Publix, so that the customer could enjoy their meal?) On the other hand, Masala Café had excellent wines at good prices and with a generous pour. Strike Two: brought my husband's rum and diet coke in a tall glass, instead of the requested small glass. (Masala Café has only beer and wine - a hit against them.) Strike Three: Failed to bring me the dreaded merlot, which I settled for. Since these issues are really just management things, I prepared for what I assumed was the best of the Indian food in the bay area. We started with soups. I had the Hot and Sour and my husband had thee Mulligatawny. He liked his and I REALLY liked mine. It was quite hot (like in to the touch) which is a departure from how soup usually comes. It was also spicy and tasty. Another management issue: the chili naan should have arrived by now (how long does it take to toast bread) and would have been good with the soup, but it did not come until after our entrées arrived. So maybe the soup dulled my spice tastes because the Chicken Tikki Masala I ordered (so I could do a fair comparison to Masala Café) was pretty dull. Not much taste or heat. Masala Café really has them beat on this dish. They provided a generous amount of rice and there was plenty of the Chicken Tikki Masala. While the atmosphere was nice and the place seemed clean, I much preferred the homey and more elegant atmosphere at Masala Café, which also has a bathroom so clean you could eat off the floor I am not an Indian food expert, but between these two, Café Masala is the best.

There are some tasty and interesting choices on the menu here, BUT every time I've been (3 total) I've ordered something different each visit---something has been wrong with my order AND it's luke warm to cold. Very disappointing. Usually I get it to go I'll eat a few bites there go back to work and microwave it. Once it is HOT it is so GOOD. Wrong orders: BBQ chicken mac----there was mac and BBQ sauce NO CHICKEN! Had to wait 10 minutes for that. Pad Thai with peanut sauce and chicken---NO PEANUT SAUCE!!!!!!!!!! Truffle Mac----suppose to be mac and cheese with mushrooms and truffle oil---NO MUSHROOMS. and 2 out of the 3 times I've been the ice machine has been broken. they have ice out for you to scoop but it's not covered and it is placed right by the trash can.

There really wasn't anything terribly bad about this place, but nothing that made me jump for joy. Off the bat, I thought there was a buffet option (which I choose so I get some variety0. There wasn't. I opted for the lamb tekka kabob lunch special (roasted lamb bits, rice, salad...). I've had arab / indian / mediterranean salads like this before, so nothing too special. The lamb was nicely done, but kind of boring. Rice is rice. As for service, I had a young guy who was pretty attentive at first, but sort of didn't care to give me any more water. In the end, a nice, polite older gentleman did refill my water, but it was as I was leaving. If you're staring at this restaurant, just look around for Maru Sushi or Saladman, which are mind-blowingly awesome by comparison.

I recommend this to all people who want to try delicious Hispanic food, that is a different taste than Mexican food. They have South American dishes and it does not disappoint! It's definitely authentic. I drive over an hour just to get here, but it's worth it. I'm South American myself and the food here makes me feel at home. I'm picky when it comes to seasonings, and this food is not only well made, but the seasonings are spot on! I recommend this place to all my family and friends, and recommend it to you too. I try to come at least 2-3 times a month because of how much I love this place!

I love boba tea, so when I found a place that has AMAZING, customizable boba tea and slushes I knew I had found a winner. I went and ordered the melon lovers boba slush, which was perfectly blended and tasted very fresh. This is the best boba I have found in the Tampa Bay area. I also ordered the spring rolls without the shrimp, and the peanut sauce that came with them was AMAZING. My friend ordered the pad thai and it was a HUGE portion for the price. My friend said the pad thai was some of the best they've ever had. The service was quick and great, and the workers answered all my questions and were super helpful. When school starts back up I think I am going to come here to study because it is a cute little place, with awesome boba tea, food and decor and I really recommend it to EVERYONE who loves authentic food.
Just moved to the area, found this gem. Pho was great summer rolls were great, the guy at the front (the owner) was hilarious. Very friendly
the food is pretty good. but the roach on the wall will prevent me from eating there again.

The apps we ordered were okay and my meal and dessert were very good. We were the only table in the place, I think it was a Thursday night and we had the whole restaurant to ourselves, which I thought was strange, especially for a Thursday when many people are ready for the weekend to begin. Anyway, I can't give Le Gourmet more than three stars because I might have gotten food poisoning after eating here or it was a poorly timed stomach bug.

West Philly is likely one of the few places in the states where you can legitimately claim the Ethiopian restaurant market is saturated, thus places need to be on their top game. Queen of Sheba has been around as long as I can remember, but for some reason I always thought is was just a bar. This misunderstanding had me missing out on one of the best vegetarian combos around. Sorry Abyssinia, but I think I've found a new place. That said, it's more of a sit at the bar and order kind of place, the restaurant section was desolate the two times I've gone, but the bartenders are friendly, and the beer is pretty reasonable, the food takes a little time, but then any good Ethiopian food I've had does.

Found this place after the demise of my former love, o sandwiches. At least once a week I stop in and grab a number 5 (tofu) and/or an 8 (veg special) with a chrysanthamum tea. Hey, don't judge me for getting 2, one's for dinner. I swear. Although it is really hard to wait that long. All I can say is that these sandwiches are absolute heaven. The bread can make a bit of a mess but they are among the best veg Bahn mi I've ever had. Make sure you have a little time to wait, it takes the guy a little while to throw yours together, but the shop is always toasty this time of year and the food is worth the wait. The only downside is they don't offer boba tea like o sandwiches, but then there's always the ba le bakery on 6th n Washington (good Bahn mi there too). Oh and heads up, they appear to be closed on Thursday, at least around 2 when I tend to pop in before work.

I too am a Pho-oholic. 4 of us stopped into Asian Pho. 2 ordered pho one noodle salad bowl and one orange chicken and chow mein. The pho is pretty good. I don't know that I would say the best in Reno but is right up there. The chinese food was average. Service was good. We ordered Egg Roles and they were barely warm. Let's face it though it is connected to a 7/11 and Wendy's. It is what it is. It's a good place to stop in for a bowl of pho and I will return.

I have had a very different experience from the other reviewers. I've eaten at this restaurant four or five times and the food and service are very, very good. I am a vegetarian and have frequently made special requests to get a vegetarian version of something I see on the menu and it's no problem at all. The owner is as personable as can be and even remembered what I ate from one visit to the next so he could make suggestions for ordering. One of the really stand out things about this restaurant is the presentation of the food. Not only does the food taste great, it looks great too. Everything is artfully arranged on the plate and you can tell that it tastes good just by the way it looks. Sure, you can find Thai food for a couple of bucks less at other restaurants but this is a much nicer space and you get what you pay for here. I heartily recommend this restaurant. It's an undiscovered gem in Olivette.

Place was awful. Went in and my party was the only customers. Place smelled like moth balls. Portions were especially small, overpriced by 3-4$, and didn't taste all that great. The waiter was playing games on his I-touch the entire time and we had to go up to the counter to ask him for the checks. Will not ever go back.

We orded the antipasto for two which truly was a sampler with a wide variety of food. Nice. The Housemade pasta with lemon topped with prosciutto was too lemony. The Ribeye was undercooked and grisly and the organic chicken was undercooked as well and very . Service was excellent though. Very good wait staff.

This is a nice new addition to Doylestown. I have been 3 times and the first 2 times the service was good this last time it was so so. We waited about 10 min to get anyone to our table to take our drink and food order and there was only 2 other tables that had people at them. Started with the hummus and pita and a Greek salad. The hummus was good and I loved the Greek salad. The salad was very fresh and the dressing is really good. For our entrees I had the lamb gyro and my husband had the steak kabob. Both were very good and I loved the flavor/marinade on the steak kabob. The lamb gyro was very good and the lamb had a nice mild flavor to it. The French fries were great too very crunchy. Definitely will be back.

I didn't eat Oxtails until I found Ron's. They're food is consistent ( I get this food often) and they give you more than enough. Sometimes the line comes out of the door, but it's worth the wait. They have seating but there's something that says "to go" about the place. I recommend.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: We headed downtown with an idea of going to Daughters Cafe on the day before Thanksgiving. If we had memories we would have remembered we did this same thing last year. And we would have remembered that they close for the week. Drats...another missed opportunity. Or is it an opportunity gained? We had to wait a bit before we went in so we took a side trip down to the Powning district. After stops at the Hub and Dorinda's Chocolate we headed back to Lanna Thai Cafe. We went right in as soon as they opened so the place was empty and they were still getting ready for the day. The place was quiet, but as soon as they turned on the Asian sounding music all was good. The sound of eating in silence is murder to my ears. The place is obviously a renovated home and it feels that way. The windows let the light pour in lighting the light woods. I think I noticed that they have a more private room that could probably accommodate maybe 8 or more. We started with Green Papaya Salad also called SomTom. It was good. This is a standard menu item I order every time I hit a new Thai place. This wasn't the best I've had..but it may be more authentic because it reminded me of the SomTom I had in San Francisco a few years back. My wife ordered the Green Curry and I ordered Pad Thai. Again, nothing like Reno Thai I have had. Very light and not heavy at all. Everything seemed fresh and subtle in flavor. My wife felt it was a little too subtle but I liked the change of pace from the Reno Thai places. The service was "mom and pop" level, friendly, warm and human. The prices were right in line with a normal Thai place. Right around $10 for each item. We will return to try the other curries and dishes. And we already are planning our own class.

I go to Pho 36 when I'm feeling drained and depleted. I order a large bowl of Pho, and I come out feeling slightly better about life. As others have mentioned, the owner is incredibly friendly, and the service has generally been quite good. Expect a longer wait during lunch rush, since the owner has to do quite a bit of multitasking. The spring rolls and the fried rice cakes are fantastic. The boba tea is a little bit expensive for what it is (the norm, I guess, for a somewhat gimmicky drink) -- I recommend getting it simply over ice instead of the default "smoothie" style.

Been here three times in the last few weeks after discovering this place recently. We've been to Berlin where they have have Turkish kabob stands everywhere, and they are DELISH! Dooners is the closest we've found anywhere to the ones we love so much in Berlin. The food here is absolutely wonderful! And had been consistently delicious each and every time. Just had one for lunch and already contemplating when I can have my next Dooners! Don't miss this fabulous place!!

We went for lunch and was not impressed at all. Seen it on food paradise and now wondering why it wasn't really good at all. We had the half chicken with the rice. Beef pita. Pork kabobs and the street salad. The best part of it all was the feta after I wiped all the olive oil off. They drown every thing in olive oil. And was extremely expensive.will not be back

Food trucks are an essential part of the West Philadelphia diet. They're everywhere: up and down Spruce Street, with a bunch on 38th and 40th. They're inexpensive, convenient, and many of them serve food that's surprisingly good. But Bui's Lunch Truck manages to stand out amidst all the rest. Maybe it's the charming Vietnamese family that runs the joint, or maybe it's those perfect egg & cheese sandwiches that they put together in no time, but people form long, long lines on the weekend to land one of Bui's famous concoctions. Penn kids will tell you it's the perfect hangover cure. If you make it there, definitely go with tradition: bacon, egg & cheese; sausage, egg & cheese; or just egg & cheese --- these sandwiches, on fresh Amoroso long rolls, are always your best bet. Ask for it with Sriracha-brand hot sauce, salt and pepper. Also, if you're watching your cholesterol, the Bui family can assemble a lovely egg white and tomato sandwich for you. Any of the above should run you about $1.50.

worst service, ever! went there and my dinner and table of 6 was rushed, the appetizer, soup and dinner came out all at once. the waitress was so darn rude. our orders were all messed up, if they didn't rush us so darn much maybe they could have gotten our order correct. My friend asked for her noodle dish not to be so spicy, and of course they made it extra spicy, no, not spicy, but piping hot! I came all the way from NYC to go meet with friends at this place and was not worth the trip at all, the food wasn't horrible, but it def wasn't good. I'm from Thailand, and the food was bland, not much flavor. Thai food is known around the world for it's abundant flavor and spices in which this establishment clearly lacked. Never will I ever eat at this place ever again, worst service ever.

Authentic Thai cuisine. The food is very good with nice sized portions. Everything we tried was fantastic. Standouts are: any of the crispy duck dishes, Pad Woo Sen, any of the curries, and save room for their seasonal dessert Sticky Rice with Mango.

I enjoy coming here it's the chipotle of Indian fast food. The place is very clean and modern with plenty of seating area. I enjoy coming here to pick up samosa and a mango lassie. The food is good quality. The owner is very friendly. The staff is always super friendly as well. I think this place is a wonderful addition to downtown Wilmington. The last thing we need is another donut shop or hoagie place.

I always like to be fair. I had visited this restaurant the second day it was open, and I did not have the greatest experience. Well, I went back last night. The stuffed grape leaves were fantastic. Probably some of the best I've ever had. I also had the Pho, medium size. It was delicious. Although, I thought it was still a little "light" on the meat. I ordered mine with tendons and tripe. I was a little hard-pressed to find the tendons and the tripe. But overall, it was a great experience and yes, I will become a regular.

great service. great pho. clean facilities. quick service. No complaints here! All the people that work here are very nice. Their product is solid and very healthy portions. No way I was able to finish the small pho in one sitting. Will definitely be coming back!

7:50pm on a Saturday. Terrible service. Been here 30mins so far and no food, our order was just taken. Took almost 20 mins to get a glass of wine. The wine selection is really small and I would not say good. The wine we picked it terrible. It seems like everyone in here is waiting for something. The food was good, however no one ever came to check on us. Like at all. We are still currently waiting for the waitress to come out.
