It is very awkward in here, considering my table and 1 other table of 2 are left. Watching everyone clean and prepare to close is not an ideal dinner settting
Excellent food. I had the Pad Prik King with pork. Very good hot tea made from loose leaf. Great atmosphere.
Ate here for the first time today. The beef nihari was fabulous! I'll definitely be back!!!

This is a great place to get donuts and pastries but last Saturday I bought one of their cakes and a box of cookies for a party. The cake had an almond flavor and was delicious. The cookies were a variety of types and all good.

What a wonderful Thai restaurant to randomly try on a beautiful Sunday afternoon! Walking around Broad Ripple, we wanted something light, but tasty, and after hitting the end of East Westfield, Chiang Mai stood out to us! We of course sat outside; they have a really great, spacious outdoor seating area, with plants and fountains galore. It was very peaceful for being in Broad Ripple's main area. I ordered the orange chicken, which was some of the best orange chicken I've ever eaten. Orange chicken is a favorite of mine and they did not disappoint. The vibrant crispy chicken was mixed with orange sauce topped with green onion and orange peel. It was beautiful and tasted amazing! My girlfriend was craving seafood, so she ordered the seafood madness, made of stir-fried shrimp, scallops, mussels, calamari, asparagus, bell pepper, carrot, and basil in a hot chili paste. This plate came out steaming and sizzling! Chiang Mai is definitely a great place to try and dine if you haven't already.

Blu Fig - Short name, short menu. When I think of Mediterranean food, I think of Falafel, Moosaka, and Baba Gahannouj. Foods that are as much fun to say as they are to eat. Blu Fig however, misses on all of those. They started in the right direction, with an appetizer menu that contains Dolma, Tabouli, and Hummus, but once you get past the appetizers, you get 4 options - gyro, grilled chicken, salmon, or shrimp. The first 3 can be served in a pita, all 4 are available as a salad or on a bed of rice. So I was disappointed. I didn't get to order something funny, like shawarma or matbucha. The Blu Fig didn't even have Figs on the menu. If I opened MJ's house of pasta, you can bet I would serve pasta. Then the food came. It started with a smoothie. It was very good. Fresh fruit, yogurt, and locally produced honey. If this place was next to a gym, I could burn off 400 calories and put them right back on all within an hour. Then my gyro came. It was good. The meat wasn't greasy, but fat equals flavor, so the meat was a little sad. Healthy, but bland. The laban & tahini sauce made up for it though, so they hit their mark. Where they excelled was with their basmati rice. Very tasty, despite the fact that they jazzed it up with a bag of mixed frozen vegetables. Almost floral tasting. I really want to support local eateries, especially ethnic ones. But the Blu Fig dumbed down their menu too much. They don't even have "Gyro" on the menu, they call it a Yee-Ro. As if to say; "Hey you redneck hick, this is how it's pronounced." Well you Mediterranean Bluneck, Salmon isn't native to the Mediterranean, and that's a quarter of your menu. Tip: Be ready for takeout. Despite the size of the establishment, there are only 4 tables here. Three of them are 4-tops, and one only seats 2. Also be aware, that it runs kind of pricey, a lunch for 2 (one plate, one pita wrap, a side of tabouli(so I could order something funny), a diet coke, and a smoothie) ran us $28 not counting tip. 2 1/2 stars, rounded up to 3 because of the rice.
This place is amazing! The owner and his wife are awesome people and dedicated to providing restaurant goers with a quality experience. Food is 10/10 Service 10/10 Go there!

my favorite thai places in Tampa!! It use to be a truck however expanded into a restaurant. Still as a restaurant they provide a home-y feel and welcome you with open arms! Everything on the menu has been full of flavor and they definitely do not skimp on the portions! I highly recommend any of the entrees but my favorites include the steam Potstickers, eggplant basil stir fry, pad won sen. Everything is amazing!! So glad this is a short 10 min drive form me

Not a big fan of Chinese food unless it's done well, but Mizu had me coming back only a few days after I first tried it. General Tsos, chicken + broccoli, and lo mein were all delicious! My fiancé got the sushi and said it was fresh and tasty.

Flambo is truly a gem. Delicious food, super awesome juices, BYOB, amazing service, very reasonable prices, and a wacky atmosphere that you can't help but fall in love with. My monthly dining club likes under the radar, off the beaten path, authentic restaurants serving food we've never tried from countries we've never been. We've gone all over the city and suburbs for 3 years and this was one of our favorites! The decor is amazing- giant chandeliers, colored lights, giant paintings, flamingo figurines, mannequins decked out in carnivale garb. You'll fewl like you stepped into a different world (Trinidad, perhaps?) We had the place nearly to ourselves on a Sunday night, and there's a whole upstairs private seating area. Would be a great place for a private party. The service is exceptional- we forgot to BYO and the owner and his son brought us a complimentary champagne toast to start (and then left the rest of the bottle!), explained the menu in detail, gave great recommendations, told us the history of the restaurant and really achieved their goal to make people feel like they just stepped into Trinidad and were welcomed into someone's home. They even sent out some plantain cinnamon bites to start! The drinks- we tried all 5 and loved the passionfruit juice, the soursop and condensed milk juice, and the hibiscus punch. The peanut butter drink was like a peanut butter milkshake and delicious. The Mauby (licorice flavor) drink was interestingbut not my favorite (but my friend loved it). Some of these juices would pair well with liquor so keep that in mind when you BYOB! Last but not least the FOOD- the mix of indian, African, Chinese, and Carribean spices is super interesting and flavorful. You MUST get the curry goat and the curry mussels you will not regret it. We got the bussa roti (easier to share) with the curry goat and basically licked the plate clean. We also loved the escabiche fish (whole fried fish) and the pelau (like a chicken biryani). The only thing that was a bit of a letdown was the pepper shrimp chow mein (too spicy for us and overall just an odd combo, but I have no doubt this is authentic). The side of veggies were nothing special, but again, I'm sure they're authentic so more of a personal preference. They served everything family style for us which was great. 5 dishes was plenty for 5 people and 3 of us had leftovers. There are also lots of vegetarian options- we loved the side of pumpkin. We were bummed they were out of oxtail and will have to come back! The owner told us they like to do special events with live music so look out for their Christmas and Carnival parties! Highly recommend!
Such a disappointment. Food seemed to have way too much sodium as I felt so sick afterwards. Price too high for the lame quality of food.
Seriously the calamari was so dry n full of breading .... which says on menu slightly .. never again will go there .the worse calamari I ever got ...

This is one of my favorite Mediterranean restuarants. The food here is always good, well presented and the service is excellent. I'm gonna go with 4 stars based on strength of service staff...they deserve it. Pan d'Olive has a very relaxing atmosphere whether dining inside or Al fresco. The whether was wonderful tonight and we were seated on side patio with misting stations in full bloom! The menu is not extensive but all selections are quality offerings. This is a great date night location or a lovely spot to dine with friends. We'll keep coming back.....you should too!

This Indian restaurant is amazing. I have been to this place many times. The food and the variety that they offer is really great. The choices from South India ( Wada ,Idli ,Sambahar , Dosa, Pongal ,Upma) and varitey of chatnis in itself is worth the money they charge. The choice of Veg and Non Veg selections are perfect . Chicken Biryani and all the curries are perfectly spicy and creamy. palak paneer has unique taste...All of the food perfectly matches my taste buds. Love this place
Looking for a good pho place a little closer to home, I gave this place two tries. Both times, the broth brought to mind the word "dishwater". Needless to say, I will not be returning.

I love Mumbai Bistro! I work a few blocks away and their super fast, free delivery is a Godsend on those days I accidentally leave my lunch at home; I will admit that I sometimes accidentally-on-purpose leave my lunch at home these days just so I have an excuse to call the guys at Mumbai. The food is crazy cheap for Indian, even the worst things on the menu are still decently good, and the small portions keep my pigginess in check. The restaurant itself is reminiscent of a generic chain, but I actually think the food is quite good. Others have mentioned the nan and veggie samosas could be improved. I agree (and will add the tandoori chicken to that list), but they're still yummy. Their chicken biryani, chicken vindaloo, paneer masala, channa masala, tikka masala, mixed veg curry, and basmati are all delicious. I've probably been in or ordered delivery a dozen times since discovering them about 6 months ago and I have never had a disappointing meal. Contrary to some other reviews, I think the food is aromatic and overall very good - some dishes are lacking in heat, but it's nothing a little hot sauce can't remedy. The place is clean, the service is quick and friendly, the food rocks, it's cheap...what more could I ask for?

This is the second Thai food restaurant that I've been to in PA and by far my favorite. It's a bit out of reach but will manage to take a trip there. I came here on a weekend and it was hardly busy. They had more take-out customers than sit down. The atmosphere is nice (dimmed lights, casual environment, friendly staff) To start I ordered the spring rolls ($4.95) "Cabbage, carrots, mushrooms, silver noodles, and deep fried tofu, served with a sweet and sour sauce" which are the best I've had in awhile. I recommend you to get this while you wait for your food. As the main course I had Drunken Noodles ($10.95) "Jumbo noodles, bell peppers, Thai basil, and onions stir fried in wine with a spicy sweet basil sauce". Everything was good but the spring rolls stood out.
I love this place. Been here 20 times. Haven't been disappointed yet. Food is amazing. Customer service is always friendly.

Best food Wife and I have consumed in Carpinteria. Started with our go to Gyoza(steamed instead). Soups and how do I say other than, OMG! The rich flavors. Her creamy Tom Kha was sweet and spicy and ohh so good. My Poh Tak was a very clean tasting seafood soup yum. We shared the main dishes and got out go to Pad Thai. Some of the best ever. The Pineapple Fried Rice was a perfect ending to change for a well rounded meal. Service was perfect and helpful from all staff. Seating inside was perfect but the outside looked even better. Thank you!

Nice place give the the impress of home. Hopeful nice friendly and welcoming workers. Great food especially Falafel, Showrma, And all types of juice. Best hookah with multiple choices of flavors. Strongly Recommended.
Beware do not eat there my boyfriend bought a cuban and in that a bone which was stuck in my throat! Awful awful place to serve a cuban w a bone in it!

Wow. You wouldn't necessarily know it from the outside, but this place is BOMB. My boyfriend, his family, my mother and I came here with short-notice reservations on a Thursday evening after an afternoon of sightseeing, and it was truly amazing. The setting, given that this restaurant used to be a row home, is super adorable. Quaint, romantic, yet trendy and fun - it really has everything. Except a liquor license. But that's okay, because it's BYOB! And they don't charge you something ridiculous for "corking" and "pouring" and "lifting" and all that other crap that typical BYOB restaurants charge you. The food, including the antipasto, was to die for. We all loved our appetizers and entrees, and the desserts were just as delicious - the perfect finish to a perfect meal. I can see why it's so popular, especially for concert -goers. Our server was excellent, too, even if his Italian was a little rusty. We couldn't remember how to say "you're welcome," and neither could he. I can't say enough good things about this place. Just go here, and ask for the limon after dinner. Trust me.

Good masaman curry...the peanut buttery savory broth that you really crave when thinking masaman. Good mix of veggies and textural bliss in the curry as well. Also ordered some fried tofu and it was pretty decent, but the curry certainly trumped it. My friend got drunken noodles and they were pretty decent, but again, the curry was the winner -- excellent umami flavor in the curry . It is a bit pricy but curries usually are about 10-12 since they're pretty well portioned. The place itself was nice -- a good date atmosphere or just a casual hang out with a friend. The service was a bit unfriendly, but they were astounding at water-filling. It was like someone was hired just to watch surveillance of customers drinking water...the moment I emptied my glass and put it down, it was filled. If you are a Thai fanatic, it would be worth trying Circle in S. Philly as well, though Erawan is certainly in a much better location for walking around with a date before or after eating.

It is truly one of the best food trucks in University City area! I had the short rib tacos which were really delicious and all the flavors with the sauces, avocado, toppings, Siracha, and short ribs all complimented each other very well. Plus $7 for 3 tacos is a really good deal! Not only were the tacos amazing, but the service here was super fast and friendly as well. 5 stars for their great food and superb service!

My family and I tried this restaurant on opening night, eager to enjoy fresh Indian cuisine so close to home, and thrilled to have a good Indian restaurant right in the city. We ordered takeout and were completely disappointed. It felt and tasted like we were at fast food joint, choosing our own toppings and nothing tasted authentic, There was, in fact, nothing at all authentic about our meals. I have no idea what that rice was, but it wasn't basmati. The sauce on my chicken zaikka was WAY too spicy, and I LOVE spicy. My daughter's chicken tikka was awful. There was corn in on of our toppings - I have never seen corn in a chicken tikka. None of us ate much that evening. I will not go back.
We like this place. We stumbled upon this place Sunday night. We ordered pineapple fried rice, Tom yum soup, satay like. Everything is fantastic. Definitely check out this place.

Following up my previous review, I've made a point to try Remedy's chai tea and can finally understand what all the fuss is about. Warm and creamy with a thick velvet foam sprinkled with spices, the chai is a world away from the syrup concoction served at Starbucks and its ilk. I've gone back again and again for this tea delight, and Remedy provides the perfect compromise - chai for me, beer for my companion. I've also finally tried their samosas, which rate similarly rave reviews - they're spicy, served with a thin, sweet cinnamon-y sauce on the side. Remedy's only downside is that it's usually impossible to find a seat.

Taking parents to Indy 500 means I will get to try most of the Indian buffets around the state! This was our second buffet out of the 3 we had all weekend and can't say I was a fan, but it wasn't too bad. Compared to Indian food in Chicago, I'd give it a 2-star maybe, but compared to other Indian food experiences in Indiana, it probably earns 3 of them.
Some of the best Vietnamese food we have had! The crab ra goons and duck tacos are a must! Fast and friendly service!!

I love chaats. Being from India, it is very difficult to find the kind of quality I am used to back in India.. Most indian restaurants in Delaware region serve stale or food which just does not make my stomach happy. Then I heard of masala kitchen, I just had to try this restaurant. The chaats we get here are awesome and quite delicious and the staff are friendly as well. Only down point I see is the location, but frankly I do not mind that as well, as I am getting good authentic gujju food!! Loved it They also provide fresh chapathis in bulk. They are open only on Friday sat and Sunday.

I ordered takeout from here (they use a third-party delivery service). It was nothing short of amazing! I first had this place when a coworker ordered it a few weekends ago. I don't remember the names of exactly everything I have but I can say that it was spiced amazingly. Prices were fair and portions were generous. I will definitely order again.The garlic naan bread was perfectly spice with cilantro. I then got another appetizer call Delhi something.i'm not exactly sure what that one was but it was really good. I have an eggplant dish for my main dish. They offer different levels of spiciness I went with the medium. I'll try the hot next time but medium is very spicy. I'll be back.I will say that Indian food usually doesn't look the most appealing but that's OK. It's all about the spice.

Love this place. The food is authentic, the atmosphere is great and it's in a good location. Plus the service is nice too. I will definitely continue to be a regular here when I want some Thai food and I'm downtown. I've tried salmon teriyaki and there Curry's are amazing. The specialty one is my favorite. And don't forget the Thai iced tea !

Visited this place for lunch today. I ordered the arroz con pollo y tostones and the meal was delicious. Also a good portion size. I had to take half home with me. The food was fresh and there's wasn't a long wait for it. The service was awesome and the staff there made me feel so comfortable. Prices were good as well and it's in a nice location nearby the SLU campus off Lindell blvd. Theres a nice patio outside also. I will definitely be returning to this place again soon.
There is a full bar here. Great happy hour specials from 4-6 daily

Yes, the food is cheap but I found it to be somewhat lacking in flavor or actually, richness. When I want Indian, I expect my dishes to be prepared with a small amount of ghee to give it that rich taste, which was lacking in the entrees here. I suppose my heart should thank me? Anyhow, the chicken tandoori was a bit disappointing, as was the chicken tikka masala; both were a bit on the bland side. While I have yet to find the perfect chicken tikka masala in the tri-state vicinity, the tandoori chicken at Mehek in Princeton remains to be surpassed. The naan here was not that fantastic but still edible; it wasn't as crispy as i would have liked. Overall, the place is a very clean, organized restaurant to grab an inexpensive meal that is pretty healthy. Maybe a bit too healthy for my personal taste but it is cheap and fast. Kind of like cafeteria-style Indian food.

I love the food here most of the time but today, it was disgusting. I ordered a pad Thai to go and it's usually great, but they've changed the recipe. My container was more than a quarter full of red onions. It was a lot more oily than usual too. Don't get the pad Thai if you usually do because it's very distasteful now. I've attached a picture of the amount of onions they are now putting in one dish of pad Thai.
Yum Woon Sen (glass noodle salad) is my comfort food here. Never fails to get me through a tough day. I also love Pad Thai, Pad Chan and Tom Kha Gai here. Very tasty!

Please Please...... if you want some good chicken to eat... stay faaaaaaaaar away from this joint..... this was the WORST chicken I EVER had and some of it was PINK INSIDE........ oh God was it TERRIBLE..... Now if you want to go there for the hand made little pies they were GLORIOUS... I had the Lemon, and the Banana Foster... both VERY GOOD but STAY AWAY FROM THIS CHICKEN!

My husband and I dined in for an early Sunday afternoon dinner. We ordered sampler combo #2 (lamb, chicken, beef, chick peas, yellow peas and other veggies). This along with the injera bread was delicious!!!! Be ware, the bread is filling! We had to get a takeout box for leftovers. The restaurant was clean and inviting.... The waitress was excellent!!! This restaurant is an Indy must try!

I was excited to see this place pop up recently as I am a fan of noodles of all types... Italian, Thai, American, etc. I've been twice with my husband, and I've been pleased. The food is pretty good... not amazing, but for a quick inexpensive lunch or dinner, it does the trick. The variety of the menu is a plus. I like that there are regular and small portions, so that I don't walk out of there uncomfortably full. If I were comparing the food to nice restaurants with authentic food/menus, I'd give this place 3 stars... but for the type of 'fast food" restaurant it is, it's a very solid choice! I even thought the soup was pretty good that I had. Oh, and the staff there is VERY nice! Usually a manager or owner comes by to ask how everything is, and staff checks on you for drink refills and take your plates. That's a plus for a fast food joint. My only complaint is the fancy soda machine with the touch screen. I'm a straight up Coca Cola chic, and both times, the coke was way off. However, if you'd like diet vanilla grape coke with lime, you can get it! This place will definitely be on our rotation of quick dinners during the week.
Loved it! Atmosphere, food, service. Ceviche, fish tacos and paella. All was good. Def come here again.

Terrrrible!! We are used to such fantastic Greek food at 3 AM in San Diego.. went here after party as no other places around were open.. terrible sandwiches with some chicken not cooked properly and leaking roofs and terrible service

I've come here several times over the past year and won't be back after my last experience. I try not to judge upon first visit, but when I have bad experiences time and time again, it's time to let others know so they can avoid it as well. You know how you want to keep giving something another chance, because you know that it has good potential? That's how I used to feel about Momo's. Now, I've just given up. The food here is mediocre at best. I've had numerous entrees burned. The dolmades come out greasy and there's way too much lemon juice in them. I think way put me over the edge is the TERRIBLE service. Our waitress was so beyond rude. We opened a tab at the bar rather than add it onto our bill directly, and when she served us our ouzo she slammed the glasses onto the table so hard that some of the liquor spilled. Anger management, anyone? Here's a tip. If you actually want good tapas check out Barcelona in Clayton, Boogaloo in Maplewood, or even Roxanne. And if you're in the mood for Greek try Aya Sofia (I know that it's supposed to be Turkish, but they do have amazing Greek dishes). All of listed above are much better choices.

This is a small family owned restaurant-daughers and son working the steam table, and mama cooking in the back! One daughter sat in a corner peeling a yucca. Can I say that I was immediately transported to Dominican Republic when I walked through the doors! My family and I have traveled there often and we all agree that this is definitely authentic. Everything was delicious! We will be back!
Friendly staff and great legit Dominican food. Really reasonable prices, too. We'll definitely be back.

This place has a lot of potential. The food was great. The waiter we got was very bad. He was kind of nice but he has very bad etiquette when it comes to waitering. I don't like that they have the glasses sitting at the table and when they give you water, its not in a new glass. Dust and crap get into the glasses when it sits on the table like that. We had to ask for new waters. Than the waiter gives us straws, which is good but the straws were not covered. He carried our straws in both hands and put it in our waters. It sounds like i'm nit picking but its the little things that you don't think you have to worry about when spending a decent amount of money to eat out. Maybe thats why we saw a lot of take out at this place.

Food and ambiance was great. We got the jerk wings and jerk chicken. Only negative thing was they didn't have the jerk sauce, only dry seasoning. The night we went in they had few big parties so was a little slow in service but the server was still very nice.
This was so good. Everyone loved what they had. I had the pork with eggrolls and it was so good that I didn't say a word until my bowl was gone! We will definitely be back!

New favorite restaurant in the area. There was not one bad thing on the menu. The food is creative and classic all at the same time. Suraya is a must try. I cannot wait to return in warmer months so I can sit on the gorgeous patio.

We were really excited to try this place out after reading (most of) the Yelp reviews. Maybe we should give it one more shot, but we weren't that impressed by our dinner. It's definitely cheap and service was slow, but we're all about the food when visiting family-run, small places like this. If the food was great, we'd gladly overlook slow service - and actually, what they lacked in speed, they made up for in friendliness. They started us with a nice small salad with a delicious sweet dressing. That was kind of the highlight - unexpected and really good. The fried calamari was also good, with a crisp breading and sweet/spicy sauce. It was the entrees that were ho-hum. I had paht mee mao, medium spice - a noodle dish with beef and veggies. Despite the other reviews warning about the spice level, I was really underwhelmed by the spice in this one. Had to doctor it with the spices at the table. The beef/veggies were fine, but not too exciting. My wife had the shrimp pot, one of the more expensive items on the menu at $13.50. It was fine, with lots of ginger, large shrimp and some veggies, but there wasn't a lot of flavor to the sauce. She didn't want it spicy (as in hot-spicy) but it seemed to be lacking a little flavor-spice. Overall, a fine dinner and we may go again since it's close to home for us, but I wouldn't go out of my way to go there again.

I came at an oddball time, 3 pm on a tuesday. I was the only customer dining in. I ordered chicken curry (gaeng) and asked for spicy. Waitress was very nice and the food was great...Just like it tastes back in Thailand.

It's really unfortunate that the service is poor because the food is always great. Greek food is my favorite and I absolutely love their fatoush salad with feta added. However, the staff is less than enthused and not friendly at all. The guy that greeted us and the waitor looked like they were about to fall asleep standing up and could care less that we were there. I didn't feel appreciated at all. I've been to several other albasha locations and had a great experience. This location's staff is not pleasant at all.

Loved it. I ate here for the first time and just loved the place. The staff is extremely friendly as well. They helped me choose a lovely combination of falafel bowl. Just loved the mango amba sauce. Wish i could take all of it

Very disappointing experience from a restaurant we used to love. Even though the menu still includes a beer/cocktail menu, they no longer serve alcohol - which the waitress informed us after we had lingered over the menu and were ready to order. We got an appetizer and 3 entrees. Our daughter's arrived first, and then ours over 5 MINUTES LATER. Even after we pointed out to the waitress that we hadn't gotten our dishes, it was still a while until they arrived. Keep in mind, we were eating early and there were only 2 other tables in the restaurant at this point, both of whom had arrived after us. No apologies or even acknowledgement that there was anything wrong. We ate quickly, paid our check, and got out of there -- probably never to return. 2 stars because the food was still pretty good, but not any better than you can get on SGrand or at other Thai places on Delmar. Sad.

Though I've only had two dishes here I quite liked them a lot and plan on coming back. Firstly I had the goat Keema Naan which was fabulous. The goat was perfectly seasoned and the bread was baked very well. I then had the chicken tikka biryani, and despite the red food coloring, I really liked it. I got mild spice not knowing what to expect and it was on par with what I expected (as in, my nose only ran a little and I didn't break out in a sweat). Be forewarned this is a take out place, though I ate in. There's not much to see and I was a little disappointed in their drink selection (no lassi, really?). Also their dessert selection (only two options?). However, I feel their good food more than makes up for it. Friday night take out, here I come!

Oh I definitely feel like a lumbering oaf within the tiny confines of Cafe Nhu Y! It's so small that I feel like I might break it... and great, juuuust great! Then there goes my most precious place to get bahn mi in Philadelphia. NoooOoo! Monster don't know monster's own strength. . We've been enjoying the bahn mi from Nhu Y for years and they are our ever-crusty, enduring freshy favorites.

Good drinks, great area to kill time. I had the trust cocktail and liked how it went down smooth. It was fruit but the fruit was strained out. We tried the Tuna appetizer, it was ok. I also got the maji tacos appetizer. That was really good. It had guacamole in it and the fish was seasons lightly and fresh. I also had the shrimp poboy. I like that the shrimp aren't fried but grilled and the bread want a hard but instead flaky. Another dish done well done. Also, do yourself a favor and upgrade to the truffle fries. We ain't them and then licked our fingers clean. Overall a good spot to hang out. I like the trendy decor too. The wait staff is also friendly and well trained.

Pho Hoa is my default place for pho, bubble tea, spring rolls, etc. Pho Hoa successfully expands beyond the pho horizons to offer a delicious, and at times overwhelming, choice of Vietnamese food. When I stray from my normal Pho Tai, I like to sample their variety of rice and vermicelli bowls. Should I get grilled pork? Maybe spring rolls? Or how about beef wrapped in grape leaves? No matter which one you decide on, they will all leave you with a smile on your face. The bubble tea selection is ridiculous, and they have a flavor for everyone! I am currently obsessed with the Iced Thai Tea, which is almost like a dessert! It's sweet and refreshing, and cuts through the saltiness of the pho. My only complaint is that sometimes the meat in the pho is sometimes a little "off", in the chewy sense. But it's still good!

This is a cool place. Food was average and took too long to come out, also the lemonade tastes like lemon water instead so becareful. The staf was very friendly with the patrons who were obviously regulars so don't expect special treatment. Seems like a lot of Veteran's go here for drinks and food so be prepared for that. Awesome view of the water and sunset and little beach. Probably won't go back cuz we just went because we were in town on business but its cute and beachy and VERRRRYYYYY relaxed.

Would recommend Olio restaurant to anyone who's in the Tower Grove area! Best St. Louis-Mediterranean foods even healthy options! Great wine selection and not only great but the most delicious I've tried as a first timer! You'll be seeing me coming back, very soon!
This place legit has the best Mediterranean food in the city. It's prepared so well, and the portions are hefty. The sides are delicious!!!!! I highly recommend the kafta!!!!

The atmosphere is great. The service is good. The tom yum EVERYTHING is spicy and delicious. You can get it as a soup or noodles. The chicken pad thai, panang curry, and fried rice were just ok. I live downtown and really want to find THAT dish so I keep trying...

This is absolutely amazing !!! Everything we ordered were so delicious and I definitely recommend this place for dinner. Great atmosphere, nice staff,and underrated food!! It's definitely a five star restaurant for me. Thanks for providing us with such amazing food!
The service was very good. It does get busy with lots of locals. The meal we had needed more spice. Temp was good.

Outstanding. Excellent food and great service. The young woman helping us gave great recommendations and told us all the recipes come from her grandmother. Healthy potions, good prices, perfect decor and atmosphere, and fantastic service. Family dinner out did not disappoint!

This is the first time I ordered from this place. I'm sure it will be my last. I ordered a pepper steak platter, which cost originally 18 dollars and some change. Luckily I had a 5 dollar discount from goggle pay. Their portions are horrible. I will never order from them again.

Falafel in a tortilla? Online menu says pita, I get a tasteless falafel burrito..this is suppose to be Mediterranean? Gave it a try..disgusting. never again. Go to a mom and pops instead of this franchise.
Food and service is great. Definitely will return, however this place needs to work on keeping the floors, and bathrooms tiddy. Especially if they want to be viewed as a clean restaurant in Seminole.

A hole in the wall decor, but maybe that's the vibe of this restaurant where the focus is on the food. And what excellent food it was. The wintermelon salad was a yuge surprise. As a true blue Viet I'm used to eating it cooked in a soup or as candied "mut." This version is fire! The beef tongue, grilled catfish and Thai grilled chicken rounded out the meal. I'm not usually a fan of the "Asian fusion" joints because I'm a snooty Saigon born and bred Vietnamese, but somehow this place works for me. Definitely would be back.

Hands down the best falafel in the city. Not only is it amazingly good but you get enough food for almost 2 meals and it's all for just $10.(this price has been stable for some time but it can vary. Safe bet would be to hand him a $20) There's no ordering so you line up, receive your container, and pay but I've never had a bad experience from whatever he decided to dish up for the day. However, be warned, you will smell like char grilled chicken and garlic for the rest of the day. It's a small price to pay for this awesome food. The only negative thing I'll say about this truck is that you should expect to wait. He does not rush his food and if there are 10 people in line a 30+ minute wait is not out of the question. I've timed him at about 3-4 minutes an order.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We went to Taj Mahal because it ranked alright on Yelp. It was our first experience with Indian food, and we were disappointed. Our food took a realllllly long time, which we expected since it was made fresh, and we would have been okay with that - until we saw people that came in after us getting their food before us. Then the food itself was really bland which was quite surprising. Service was friendly, but probably wouldn't go back.

YUM! The saying "big things come in small packages" applies to Thai 5, though they are a food truck their food is extremely fresh and delicious. I got the roasted salmon box with fresh veggies, jasmine rice, an egg roll and a crab rangoon and it was really good. My boyfriend order spicy (medium) fried rice, and it changed our lives forever. We took awhile to pick what we wanted so we waited for some time for our food but it was well worth it. Places like this remind me why I love yelp, because without I would be without delicious Thai food.
It's as middle eastern as McDonalds is Irish. Onions are overly pungent and the taste remains in your mouth - and on your breath - for hours. Not good value for the price.

I'm giving it 5 stars not because I loved everything I ordered, but because the server was great describing the food to the best of her ability. We ordered the Isi-ewu (Goat meat in a spicy sauce). Sauce was spicy and yummy the meat is fatty, but if you pick around it very tasty. For dinner I ordered the Vegetarian Dish (Jollof Rice, plantain & mixed vegetables, spinach & beans). All very good except I didn't care for plantains. The spinach is a must to try. My husband order the Suya beef with the Jollof Rice. He liked it. We both said we would go back and try something else on the menu.

Mixed reviews for my new neighbor. I have to say I am FAN because of the ridiculously close location and the fact that the few things I have ordered here have been deeeelicious. I am fully obsessed with the Pad Thai and the Pad See Ew both with tofu (and I am SO not a vegetarian in any way!). I have also gotten the satay chicken and the Thai basil meatballs - both tasty with a nice amount of spice. I had one disappointment in my several visits - Chao Phraya Express - and I won't blame them because I don't think I would have liked this appetizer no matter where I went. As mentioned, they are a bit on the slow side with service. I don't know why I am not bothered by this as I normally would be but for some reason, I am not. I get the sense that they don't have many people in the kitchen and they are making the entrees one at a time. Maybe the best advice would be to bring your wine and settle in, knowing that you will have a bit of a wait but it will be worth it. FYI - they do takeout. Its a dangerous thing especially when its just a few doors down!!

I love the concept of this place - am always a fan of bringing ethnic cuisine to the fast casual sphere and executing it without sacrificing quality. I came here over the weekend, and clearly many others are in the same boat. It was packed but the line moved quickly. On top of that, our food arrived quickly and seating was still ample since the restaurant space is surprisingly large. As for what we actually ate there, we split: + Hummus w/ slow-roasted lamb - The meat & toppings mix was kind of funky and gamey tasting for some reason. Not as big of a fan as I am for Dizengoff's hummus & toppings. Suraya's hummus is also more neutral-tasting. + Shish taouk sandwich - stuffed with chicken, french fries, and some other stuff. Not bad, but wasn't super impressed compared to other Middle Eastern fare I've had in Philly. + Turmeric tea - very nice and liked the spices The baked goods counter looked incredible, and I wanted to just sample a little of everything. In fact, I came close it and got a huge bag of pastries to go: + Cruller - one of the best I've had! + Flan patissier - this had Meyer lemon in it. Wasn't a huge fan, and comparable to other egg tarts I've had + Jalousie - not bad. Not as buttery or flavorful as I'd hoped + Chocolate pistachio (financier?) - same as above. Again, I love the concept, the incredible design of the interior, etc. However when it came down to the food, I wasn't super impressed. In an area with tons of good restaurants, I still might take my friends to give this place another spin and because it's such an interesting space/food.

Very disappointed in all 3 dishes we ordered. We regularly order pad se ew, pinnacle fried rice, and a pork dish from several thai places. All three had an off putting taste and smell. Will not order from here again. Three stars because service was fast and very nice people.

Our friend recommended olio as a "must-do" while in st louis, visiting from chicago. The cocktails, food, and ambiance were all amazing. Everyone was friendly and unpretentious. The prices were great for the quality and quantity of food. We will definitely be back when in St Louis.

Ordered TOGO! I ordered TOGO for lunch one afternoon. I was greeted and my order was taken promptly. The food came out very fast and was extremely hot! I ordered the Pad Thai Chicken. It was a good Pad Thai but not the best I have had. It was a little dry and not as flavorful as I am used to. Still was a good Pad Thai!

I really enjoyed my food here, as it was hearty, homey, and not too complicated. It was a bit pricey for the lack of complexity of the dish and there wasn't *that* much meat, so I'm not sure why my cauliflower chicken was like $15. Anyway I couldn't help but eat all the rice and felt very satiated upon completing my meal. All food comes with a salad and also Afghan bread. The salad has a very strange dressing that is not quite like ranch, but if pressed, you'd call it ranch. The bread is pretty interesting, it's like a milder focaccia. My main concern is that our waiter was almost completely unintelligible. I couldn't hear a WORD out of his mouth. He was speaking so softly and just mumbled all of his words. I mean, he wasn't rude, in fact he was very polite in his demeanor. I think he just needs to energize and project his voice. Overall you get a very homey vibe from this place and none of the food is very offensive in taste so I think it's a great chance to try out Afghan food if you're feeling adventurous.

My husband and I decided to go to this restaurant to celebrate completing a home renovation project. We stood inside the door for approximately 15 minutes while being completely ignored. We tried to amuse ourselves by looking at the wines. Servers and other people buzzed past us without so much as giving us the finger. Finally we gave up and left. We went instead to Earls, a much better-run restaurant. Since I have learned that Parkallen clients apparently are invisible for the first fifteen minutes after they enter the door to this restaurant, I recommend that you use this facility as a washroom rest stop. However, if you want to dine or have a little wine or a celebration, go elsewhere. Cross-posted from Parkallen Restaurant.

We had a group of 10 with reservations. Service was horrible. 1 hr to get entree which was only warm because they heated the plates next to table. Couldn't get checks or pay bill. 4 hr to eat is too long. I had forgotten how good it tasted by the time we left.
Food is so delicious! Fresh ingredients! Gus is an experience. The aroma makes you salivate. Worth the wait in line & when he calls out "No 1" & your up be ready to be falafel'ed.

WOW!!! Where do I start... Everything exceeded our expectations! From the chic decor and the Bob Marley in the background (which definitely sets the mood!) to Andre and his wife Jenise who made us feel like family ( I hope I spelled her name correct :) And the best part ... the food!! Authentic, flavorful, delicious all come to mind...everything on the menu sounded so good and the prices were reasonable. It was difficult to make a decision on one meal so I ordered Taste Of The Islands (comes with a salad): oxtail, curry goat, jerk chicken, and rice & peas. The salad has strawberries and apples that taste amazing with the vinaigrette dressing. The oxtails were extremely tender falling off the bone! The curry goat was scrumptious! The jerk chicken! OMG lol...the best I've had...EVER lol. So juicy...tender, just the right amount of spicey...better than the jerk chicken I've tried im Jamaica! We will definitely be back! If you are looking for authentic Caribbean food...great portions... appropriately priced...look no further...you will not be disappointed! If I could rate more than five stars I would! We also found out the 2nd and 4th weekend they cater and rent the restaurant for events. A beautiful clean venue with phenomenal food...we will be planning our next event at Yah Mon!
The best food!!!! And most items are GLUTEN free!!! So hard to find good food without GLUTEN.

OMG. This place was awesome. it was a $10.99/person buffet. YUM!! I couldn't get enough of the veggie samosas and the spinach/mushroom dish. and to die for = the dessert. deep fried balls where you can taste the CONDENSED MILK upon consumption. yeah, this is not a vegan item. but it took me by shock when i ate it. yes, it was amazing. it's like crack! plus their naan was yummy too. i coulda ate here all day... it was so good, it forced me to pull up a spinach/mushroom recipe dish online and make it when i got home. YUMMY!!!

Today I had another great meal at Singha. We went for 11 and were seated immediately in the front room. The front room is a very nice spot to eat lunch. We had a table right next to a window that looked out to Carondelet St. A server immediately took our drink orders and another server took our food order. Today we ordered Cashew Chicken and Pad Son Woo. I ordered the Cashew Chicken thai hot. Although the server gave me an odd look, they prepared it that way. It was incredible. If I had been at home I would have licked the plate clean. It was that good. I tried a bite of the Pad Son Woo and it was also very good. I really like Singha. The prices are very reasonable and food is great. Note: I noticed a Yelp sticker on their door. It read "people love us on Yelp".

Momo's is quickly becoming one of my favorite Greek restaurants. The menu is great. Everything I have tried I have enjoyed. The atmosphere is great - kitchie and fun. The servers are good and the girls are very easy on the eyes. Outdoor seating great in this weather. Prices are good for the quantity of food. They call it Tapa's but the portions are not small. (Comparatively, I think Olympia has turned into small plates at high prices). At lunch try the tenderloin sandwich - a great value at $9. The greek spinach side was great and plentiful. The scallops delicious. Mussels were unlike any I've had before but delicious and not a small plate. Wine selection is good. I've been twice on cash and twice on Groupon and found no difference in service or quality. Go to Momo's for a change of pace. You will enjoy the evening.

Biggest Thai teas ever!! Pad Thai is always my go to and it does not disappoint. The Pineapple Fried Rice is so delicious, I would recommend ordering one with the rest of your food even if you aren't that hungry.

Fun times last week with the STL International Supper Club. I wanna give 5 stars cause i had so much fun with this crazy group of people. But i am not here to review the Yelpers! I thought the service was pretty spotty. There was a very large group so i get the challenge, but dang it was hard getting a refill on my water...and getting a box for my food (thanks to Stephen for finding our waitress and asking for one for me!). Okay, now on to the food. It was okay. I had #43 Pad Thai Woon Sen which was Glass noodle stir fried with green onions, bean sprouts, ground peanuts, and egg which would have been really good i would have ordered a side of vegetables to mix in. I also ordered the Fried Corn Cakes as a appetizer. There were okay, but the corn inside was a bit chewy or something...i don't know something was off (these have potential to be amazing, the sauce that came with was killer). The real shocker came when i got my bill...it was more than $20! I know they added gratuity, but i didn't even order a drink. They didn't give each of us itemized bills, so its possible i paid for someone elses dinner...not really sure but i didn't want to mess with it cause it was getting late and i was anxious to get the heck outta there! So, to sum it up. My food was pretty good, but i would not come back here with a big group. Not even sure if i would suggest this place as there are many more Thai places to chose from. But i would not resist if someone wanted to go back.

Food was great as it was my first time eating at an Indian Restaurant. My friend and I went during lunch hour where there was a buffet. The buffet had many options that tasted great. It was indeed a refreshing experience. However, one small qualm is the change in price. We arrived during lunch hour which the waiter explained. Now we did leave after lunch hour was over and was charged the dinner hour's price. I don't know if there was some discrepancy since you'd think my friend and I should've paid the lunch hour's price. We should've paid first. They need to have the hours of lunch and dinner printed to see so there isn't a feeling of perceived unfairness. Would go back for the food on one condition that I am sure to pay the appropriate price during the appropriate hour.

This little place is amazing. I walked in one day a bit too late for lunch (It was 2:59 and they close at 3:00pm) and the waiter insisted that I get food to go. I am so glad he did. The food was amazing. Apparently I caught the tail end of their lunch buffet. All of the food was fresh and vibrant. I had to wait a bit because they made me fresh naan. *swoon* I had the Chicken Tikka Masala, which is my personal favorite. I have eaten at many Indian restaurants, but this Chicken Tikka Masala was, by far, the best. The coloring was perfect. The flavors were spot on. It was divine. I can't wait to go back to experience the best of their service and food selection, but from what I did have (a huge takeout tray with fresh naan for $10.55) I can easily recommend it.

Atmosphere & the company get 5 stars!After that, well it went downhill. We sat outside and our waitress came by and took our order. She mentioned she had a large party, but said not to worry. She brought our drinks and it started to rain. We moved to a table she said to move to. Our appetizer came, and we never saw her again. Never asked if we needed more drinks, never brought our food. Never brought our bill. Even after we alerted another employee that we had to leave. We had been there over an hour and a half! We saw her assist another table near ours, but she pretended not to see us. Very disappointing.

Great food. I'm a big fan of pho and this place delivers very authentic Saigon style pho. I also absolutely love the spring rolls. Vietnamese spring rolls are wrapped in a kind of rice wrap and served cold, and these were done perfectly. The only concern I have is the price. $8 for a bowl of basically noodles is too much although I'd say it's standard price in the US. When I lived in Vietnam, I paid less than 50 cents a bowl for the same meal. Staff would very nice.

Two words: macaron Monday. They're not laduree, but they're the best I have had outside of manhattan. They're light and fluffy and the flavors are changed up every week which keeps it interesting. My boyfriend has off every Monday morning and runs to Ndulge pretty early for macarons. A few weeks ago he arrived just before noon on a Monday and they were already sold out! I would recommend going as early as possible if you're trying to buy these cookies.
Roti, yes! Beef patties! Yes. Call first, sometimes hours are erratic.
Very bad experience. So much for a buffet. The worst place I've ever been. No food, no service, no washroom.

I love that there's finally a Middle Eastern Store/restaurant in the parish. I cook lots of Arab dishes (I'm Arab so go figure) and here I can find the spices and ingredients I need for most of my dishes. The food here is excellent especially during Ramadan. Overall I love it and hope they remain open for a very long time.

My new favorite restaurant in Indy. Ordered vulavacharu Biryani at closing time for a family pack and the person took the order was so patient in answering all my questions and did delivery for free. Food was so tasty felt like visiting my home town. Love this place.
Great fast healthy food option. Everything is fresh. You leave feeling good about what you ate.

Me and my girlfriend went on a whim the other night and were a little confused as to what to expect due to the fact this is a mish-mosh of Chinese/Indian/Thai cuisine. Maybe that's the fusion part?;-) We are both into very flavorful foods but not fans of hot spices. They did accommodate different levels of spice on dishes. We ordered Tom Yam w/ chicken and Sweet Corn w/ veggies soups. Didn't finish the Tom Yam as it wasn't that tasty and the Sweet Corn was so-so. For appetizer we ordered the Sambosa which is medium heat and it was very tasty. The one criticism was that the outside appeared to be over cooked in my opinion but it didn't take away from the wonderful flavors. Now the entree which was the Lamb Korma was unreal. The flavors were so well balanced and the lamb was tender with zero fat. I was full but kept eating cause it was so tasty. Their basmati rice is also lightly seasoned and went so well with the lamb dish. The naan was also well prepared. Staff was very friendly and took good care of us while we were dining. There are not may tables in there so I am not sure how busy they get on weekends but I can see it filling up quickly. Check this place out, it'll be worth your while, I think.

Portions were small relative to other Vietnamese restaurants, but it should be noted that a "super bowl" size is offered for ~$4 more. Flavor was good and on par with many others. A bit on the pricey side though for the portion size. Not the kind of place you go to for ambience or decor It was likely previously a Bob Evans and Saigon has done little to change that appearance. Menu does offer many items that are not standard on other Vietnamese places which seems to make this a good place for the adventurous palette.

Food: -Disappointment. -Sea bass roasted in grape leaves with lemon oregano vinaigrette and tomato orzo: sounded pretty legit, came out as a sad piece of fried fish on top of bland tasting orzo grains. -Baklava: I love sweets and I almost never complain about something (especially baklava) for being too sweet, but freakin zeus, all the sugar in their baklava almost melted my teeth. It did not need to be drenched in honey. I am NOT Winnie the Pooh. Overall, I was fed but derived no pleasure from being fed. I could've just saved myself the money and cooked myself a bucket of plain white rice for the same effect. Service: -Spotty. Our waitress brought our lukewarm pita bread (for extra charges) AFTER we were almost done with the Saganaki. Belly dancer: -Very awkward belly dancer getting too close for everyone's comfort (like guys on dates, my gay friend, and 12 year old boys who were probably popping boner under the family dinner table) -I'm sure she's a nice girl... and kudos for being able to balance a giant machete on her head. Overall, Momos=Nonos. (Also, $7 for a piece of baklava in St. Louis, are you shitting me?)

Sprios used to be one of my favorite places. We were there Friday night and...meh. First, we received apologies for long wait for food, an offer to refill beverages while we waited, but yet charged for them in the end. Then, the food came. My lamb shank was in a dish of grease. Literally at least 1/4 inch of grease. And the side of veggies I ordered were entirely & overly coated with oil. I moved my food to my bread plate to drain. The waiter brought me a clean dish & showed the grease dish to the manager. Manager never came to the table. More apologies from the waiter. That was probably our last visit to Sprios, which is really too bad because they used to treat their patrons well and I don't think I've EVER sent anything back or been unhappy. Oh, and by the way, we were charged for everything. How simple it would have been for management to correct this situation and have happy, returning customers.

Didn't want to give it any stars. Had been here before and much has changed. Always crowded. That's ok. Knew we would have to wait. Drinks were mostly juice, waitress came and took our order, came back a half hour later and said she lost our order, little laughter like it was a joke. Then asked us to remind her what we ordered. By the time raw burger was delivered, we were no longer hungry. She did, however, take it off our bill. Still. A burger should not take 2 hours, especially since it was not even cooked! Never going back.
Very nice ambiance. Nice wait staff. Shrimp ya ya, cuban castillo were excellent.
Seriously this place was amazing. Went for the lunch buffet and had garlic naan with my meal. I am in love and want to go back immediately. I hate that I live in Texas...

This was our first visit here, & I was quite impressed. The first thing that stands out was the timing. We ordered our drinks & kid dinner first, and they were all brought out almost immediately. The soups & salad were just as quick. Almost the instant the soups were finished & set aside, our entrees arrived. It really was all excellently timed with very little lag. The hot & sour soup was fantastic, spicy enough to meet expectations but not too much. The pad Thai was also tasty, and the portion was big enough for leftovers. Also had the seaweed salad, one of the best I've had.

Go to spot for (super) quick lunch during work hours. FOOD: I've tried pork, grilled pork, grilled beef sammies, and pho. My favorite that I've been sticking with is the grilled beef. It's sweet and savory at the same time. I love the pickles in their sandwich! However, I now stay away from the pork sandwich because the meat looked and tasted like something regular deli meat you get at grocery store. The pho is average at best. They only have 1 option for pho (beef) and it's nothing to write home about. Finally, I have to tell you that their avocado smoothie is the bomb! I love it! PLACE/AMBIANCE: The place can be pretty busy during lunch time. They have limited seating so I almost always get my sandwich for to go. Not the best place for a large group (I'd say max is 4 people). But parking lot is huge because it's located in the Fred Meyer complex. SERVICE: It's a "walk in-get your order at the counter-your number is called-sit down&eat" type of place. So you'd expect to get limited service here. If you decide to dine in, they take care of your dishes at the end of the meal. One of the most amazing thing about this place is how fast they make the sandwich. I've counted when there's NO line and I can be in-and-out in 3 mins.

I came here for the latest installment of the International Supper Club. The company was fabulous, and the food was even better! I ordered #24, the Khao Pad Sriracha. Hello -- anything with Sriracha in its name HAS to be a winner, right? It consisted of fried rice, green onions, broccoli, onions, egg, and thai hot chili sauce. It was very heavy on the onions (I'd ask for no onions next time), but other than that, it was DELICIOUS. The whole time I was eating, I kept saying "this is so STINKIN good!" over and over in my head. Wow. And it definitely had a kick. Sriracha is no joke! My nose was running like crazy. Sexy. Service was a little crazy, but I won't judge since there were about 30 of us. :) The only thing I wasn't a fan of? The thai iced tea. The first few sips were good, but I couldn't down much more than that -- it's SUPER rich. It felt like I was drinking a glass of half and half! I will definitely be back to try other things on the menu.
Seafood noodle soup lacked seafood. Fake crab and fish loaf. Yuck. Curry chicken was greasy, bones and skin, no vegetables. Not greatest curry sauce I ever had. Restaurant needs TLC.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: So good! Friendliest people and the food is super tasty. The naan bread is money.

Update: I never understood all the poor reviews here but after dining on a Thursday night around 7pm .. I totally get it. The service was AWFUL. Our server never brought us bread or refills on most drinks until we asked for it. It took forever to get anything. When we wanted to order more drinks it took ages for her to mosey on back to our table. I still think the food is great. I had the ravioli which was good but it doesn't compare to other menu items so I wouldn't order it again. My friend had the pasta carbonara and everyone at our table was tasting it and raving over it. I'm only gonna downgrade them to a 4 (from a previous 5) but they are really pricey so I will only go back on a Monday or Tuesday early dinner to get the prefix. -------------------------------- This is one of the best meals I've had in Downtown St Pete!! Disclaimer: We went for an early dinner (5:30) on a Tuesday. So that may be why our experience was way more positive than some others on here. First impression - the inside is absolutely gorgeous. Fresh flowers on the tables. Beautiful couches comprise part of their table seating. Even the bathroom was spotlessly clean and smelled of fragrant eucalyptus. Service: Our server was extremely attentive (but again it was early and only a few ppl there), seemed very passionate about the food, and was very personable and funny. Price: Yes it's pretty pricey but it's quite the classy place. But they offer a prefix menu from 5-7pm for 25$ that includes full size portions of appetizer, entree, and dessert. INCREDIBLE deal. The portions were definitely full size. Many entrees are $25 so it's like getting an appetizer and dessert for free. FOOD!! AMAZING!! Appetizers: I had the baba ganoush.. extremely flavorful, though I was not a fan of the deep fried chickpeas scattered throughout. My girlfriend got the sweet corn chowder.. it was a HUGE bowl and she was blown away by it. Entrees: I had the chicken roulade which was so moist and juicy. The veggies were cooked to perfection, still a little crisp. The mushrooms were so meaty.. they seemed like some wild variety that you don't see everyday. My gf had the filet mignon brochette.. the steak melted in your mouth, didn't even need a knife. It came with the most amazing garlic butter mashed potatoes we'd ever had. Dessert: Chunky monkey (banana nut) cheesecake. I thought it was good, though my gf was again blown away, best cheesecake she ever had. So based on other reviews, perhaps your best bet is to go for an early dinner when you know service will be better. Seriously amazing food! And the happy hour specials (from 5-7) were also pretty great. Only $3 for wells. and some beers and wines were half off. Definitely recommending this place to others.

Staying at the opal sands and wanted something other than seafood after a week. We went looking for Indian and although it was 11 miles away it was totally worth the drive. The samosas were piping hot, moderately spicy (to me), very large and were a delicious start to our dinner. We had the butter chicken and chicken tikka and both were very good with generous portions. I don't know what dessert was called, it was like a donut hole that had been soaked completely through with a spiced, sweet syrup. It was served warm and melted in our mouths, it was really good but one tiny donut was enough to satisfy as they were so rich. I would definitely go here again.

So apparently Zagol has received notice the restaurant must vacate the premises in 30 days (5really, is a 30 day notice even legal?). I love this place and they need a place to relocate. If you can help, please contact the owner. This is a great place to bring friends and relatives for an interesting and delicious meal.
My boss recommended the chicken tekka masala. I was not disappointed. The atmosphere is pleasant and the chicken was perfectly tender.

Pretty reasonable prices...and food were pretty good, the only complaint I have is the potatoes in the dishes I got were too big and not really that much seasoned. But all and all I would still go back and order again from them.
This place sucks!!! They plays no music! she gave me only two options NASCAR and Soccer! I'm not here for either soccer or NASCAR!!!!

Short Rib Tacos - Thai sauce was delicious and veggies were fresh! Actual ribs were marinated well but tough.. almost like jerky.. not cool... Tilapia Burrito - mayo based sauce not quite as good as Thai sauce but very filling.. apparently the tilapia is fried in CTCruch crumbs... couldn't even tell. Had to wait 35 minutes after ordering at 1pm. That may have been why it was tasty... cause they make you smell food for half an hour while you're hungry... Pro tip: Penn Park has some nice scenic benched 10 minutes away

I'm sorry but this place is AWFUL. Somehow it is crowded at lunch with people who, I presume, have never had other Thai food (or really any quality ethnic food, for that matter). The prices are lower for the New Orleans market, but the food is just nasty. Nothing fresh, nothing particularly flavorful, the only benefit this food has is staving off hunger for a couple hours. It's not that I want them to fail, just the opposite- I really would like them to try harder!

The Chef here is such a Star that I had to trek a little further than my immediate area to try this restaurant of his. Though not a fan of "fusion" food, I find his combinations to be delightfully refreshing. The Chinese Appetizer, Crispy Chicken with Honey was light, delicate and scrumptious. I could easily eat this dish every time. My party shared our selections of Eggplant with Hot Garlic Sauce, Coriander Garlic Chicken & Pineapple Fried Rice with Chicken, so we could each offer our opinion. The Eggplant was mashed for a perfect smooth texture. And the tangy heat was welcome. The Pineapple Fried Rice was a favorite of my mate. I LOVE the Coriander Garlic Chicken. They will adjust their recipe to your desired taste for mild to 5 alarm heat. Dhaba Dal is a yellow lentil dish that is a staple for me. I loved sopping it all up with the Kulcha Onion Bread. Any of their Naan will do. But I enjoy the ones with veggies or garlic, onion or other stuffing baked right into it the most. The space is modest but beautiful. Very warming for a cold winter's night. The Rasmalai was one of the best I've ever tasted - delicate, rose-flavored, mmmm. I noticed some Take Out action during our visit. This is probably a great take out place. This place is Highly Recommended!

This'll be short and sweet. As many others have posted, the chai and some of the desserts are delicious. However, I find none of the Indian food tastes like Indian food. I went there shortly after a trip from India, and have been back a time or two with a friend that really loves the place - but it doesn't stack up to other places boasting authentic Indian fare. It is full of uni-hipsters, some incredible artwork, and some snazzy tunes, which sets a real cool vibe in the place. Something I give a big thumbs up for. Cafe - Yay. Resto-bar - meh.

This may have been the worst Thai food I've had - and I love good Thai food, and will go out of my way to find it. We ordered appetizers, two red curries, a vegetable dish (Chili Yam if I recall correctly), and I ordered wide Spicy Noodles, asking them to be "very spicy, Thai spicy." Probably the best dish was the chicken satay appetizer. It was sweet, but the chicken was tender. The other appetizer, fried tofu, was well made but both appetizers came with sweet peanut sauce, so we were already getting a little tired of "sweet." EVERYTHING else was pretty horrible. The Spicy Noodles were just plain sweet, and, unlike the description, came with just a couple token slices of vegetables. To spice it up, the kitchen just dumped powdered chili on top of the dish, but it was a mild powder so not actually spicy, so I basically had a wad of sweet noodles covered in powder. Yuck. Both of the red curries where overpoweringly sweet, although the curry flavor hiding under all that sugar would have otherwise been nice. The Chili Yam vegetable dish was basically vegetables swimming in sweet duck sauce - none of us wanted more than a bite before abandoning it. As for service we sat for about 20 minutes before even water was served. Nearly 45 minutes had passed before the appetizers showed up, and almost an hour before the first main arrived. We were getting pretty tired of waiting by then... All five of us agreed, pretty terrible Thai food, very slow service (and only two other tables occupied!). We will not be going back here.
Great place! The owner was so sweet and attentive to everything we needed! Chill place, definitely will return again and again! (:

Was visiting Philly and wanted a snack at 3pm. This was the highest rated food truck in Philly on Yelp so I had to check it out. It's located in somewhat of a back alley on the Drexel campus where there are literally a dozen food trucks lined up. It's the last one at the end. The guys running this truck are super energetic and upbeat. It's obvious they love what they do. short rib tacos ($3 each) - thai-mexican fusion with peanuts, crunchy onions and cabbage, marinated chunks of short rib, avocado, and tomatoes with a spicy sauce over everything. It's good, I'm not gonna lie. The combination of flavors and textures works, but if I had to be nitpicky, the short ribs were a bit too chewy and there was a bit too much sauce which masked the flavor of certain ingredients, like the avocado. Overall, the food didn't surpass my expectations. The food itself deserves 4 stars-excellent but not out of this world. I actually think Jolly Pig in Baltimore makes better fusion tacos. However, I've never been to a food truck where I could so easily tell that the owner (Mr. Zapata) was sincerely trying to make people's days better in the short interactions he has with each customer and in the food he sells to them. For that, this place gets 5 stars.

I like this place a lot. The beers are huge (and I mean like a half liter huge) so make sure youre prepared when you order a large. They come out with this cool cracker bread thing which you can top with salsas on the table. Then, with the order comes a fresh naan bread, which is huge by the way, and some rice. I do think that they cut back a little on the rice but thats okay I guess. I've had both the lamb curry and special lamb dish and both were pretty good. My friend got the chili chicken, which is a HUGE dish, and it also is something I would recommend.

If you are trapped in Brentwood at lunch time everyday, you likely have been longing for something different. Something better. Something outside the ordinary. Me too and our wish has come true. Not only is this newly opened Indian restaurant immediately one of the best places to eat around here, it stacks up very well against other Indian restaurants in the greater Nashville area. For quality, flavor, and variety, the buffet is probably about the best Indian buffet I've had anywhere. They don't cheat you on flavor. Get there early. It's kind of like Disneyland in there now. Five stars are definitely in order relative to the other forgettable places in the Brentwood area.

This place wasn't very good. The food tasted very bland, and the quantities were small for the prices charged. In Santa Barbara you expect tourist trap over-priced food, but I also expect that food to be at least somewhat good. I recommend to try a different place in town or a completely different cuisine.

This eatery was worth the drive to Trenton NJ. The jerk chicken was tender and full- flavored. My tongue still waters when i think about that gravy on the rice and peas. Shall we talk about the escovich fish: scrumcious, finger-licking, to-die-for, I-just-can't-wait-to-go-back, and delicious. You must go if you're in Trenton.
Best Jamaican food in Nashville! Excellent service ! Our waiter was pleasant and polite. The restaurant was so clean and had peaceful ambience

This is a newer fast casual Indian restaurant that has won over my heart with their delicious mango lassi, chicken tikka bowls, and samosa chat. You order at the front and build your meal, whether it's a bowl, pizza, or sandwich. You get to pick your ingredients and customize your meal all the way down to the sauce and toppings. I think this place is wonderful for someone who is looking for a quick, tasty, and affordable Indian meal for sit down or to go, as well as someone who is looking to explore something new and unique. There is a decent amount of seating and I've seen this place pretty full. Some of the seats are 2 rickshas put together. While a neat concept, not ideal for eating as the table is narrow and the seat is leaned back further than comfortable. (But for those who enjoy a very casual seat at the dinner table.. maybe you'll love it !)
Beignets are out of this world! Try the Pho on Saturday...it is to die for. Friendly service, new location downtown as well!

This place is my favorite in the whole city. Always amazing food, and my friends who visit insist that we go here. Try the Naam salad, you will not be disappointed by the crispy, crunchy goodness - not really sure why it's called a salad. My family begs me to bring it to them to MI! The satay is delish too. Try the triple flavored duck with the sauce on the side so it stays crispy. The pad thai is not like other pad thai, but it's amazing. It actually has veggies in it too! Maybe avoid the casserole thing. The curries are great, yellow one isn't spicy. The yum salad is pretty awesome too! You gotta try this place!

Been meaning to go forever, finally made it for an early dinner on New Year's Eve. What a great little find. We shared the Tom Kha Gai soup which was an amazing blend of coconut milk and spicy broth with chicken and mushroom pieces. Then onto the Pad Thai which was more about the vegetables, than other local versions which seem to be mostly about the noodles. This was subtle, but tasty version. Our final dish was a rice and green mix that wonderfully spicy, but so balanced. Dinner for two was under $40. Amazing price for the quality of the food. Can't wait to return.
Great little spot. We stopped for breakfast on the way to Jean Lafitte park and it hit the spot. Baleadas. Yum.

Amazing concept, extremely poorly executed. The Mac and cheese was terrible, dry with a strange taste. The chicken was overcooked, under seasoned, and not worth eating. My advice, don't waste your time or money on this fake out of a great idea.

Only 2 stars for the Pho which always makes me come back. But as soon as I do, I get reminded why I stopped coming. Service - Only the owner is attentive and that's when we catch his attention. Every one just stands inside and talks when customers have their hands raised forever. Literally raised my hand for a good 8 minutes while the waitresses just stayed on their phones and talked to one another. Seriously? Every. Single. Time. Food - Besides the pho and rare steak, everything else is pretty mediocre for the prices they charge. Came in here wanting spring rolls and 4 different times of a day, they said they didn't have them. Spring rolls are not hard to make in stores, doesn't have to be done elsewhere and transported here. Makes no sense. And the egg rolls are completely tasteless. Pho and meat are delicious, but not worth when portions are small and service sucks so bad. Having pho restaurants myself, it's really hard to stand horrible food and small portions with 1-star quality service.

This is by far the best Ethiopian restaurant in the area!!! I highly recommend the buffet, which is from Monday-Friday starting at 11AM-2PM. By the way, the traditional way of eating Ethiopian food is without utensils. So get ready!

I tried to love this place but their vegetarian dishes are TERRIBLE. I've tried the ital stew and the spinach and groundnut stew so far. They are both incredibly bland. The veggies in the ital stew were mushy and overdone. When I told the waitress that the ital stew was bland, she said that it was because it's vegetarian. *pause* what? I've had plenty of vegetarian Jamaican food that was flavorful. Avoid this place if you're looking for vegetarian dishes and walk down to Caribbean Delight. They do a much better job.

Ate there today but I was surprised that the food wasn't as good as the other times I've been there. The good thing about the place is at least the waiters try to get the food orders right. I've had Pho there a couple times, but today it just looked and tasted as if well, it wasn't to good today. The Pho soup was very dark brown and it just didn't taste as good as my regular visits. I also ordered the broken rice with pork chop special to share and usually the pork chops are really flavorful with lemongrass but it was dry and there was no flavor. Overall, If your ready for a quick bite and hate waiting, its a OK place to go. They have TVs for you to watch and its a pretty casual place to eat. The servers are good because at least, they do try and get the order right.
One of my fav hookah spots in Philly. The Moroccan style setting just gives it a vibe that u can't get anywhere else in Philly.

Conveniently located in the Dilworthtown Shopping center, Wasabi2 offers a very cozy atmosphere for your dining pleasure. The owner of the restaurant, along with our waiter were both extremely attentive and engaging, but not over bearing. Our waiter was very good at offering some sushi suggestions while we were looking over the menu. My partner was very excited to see that they offered Sea Urchin Uni on their menu but was told that it is only available on Friday's and Saturday's. We sampled the seaweed salad and spicy tuna tar tar as appetizers and were absolutely blown away by both. The seaweed salad was served on a bed of julienned cucumber and was some of the freshest we ever tasted. The tuna tar tar was at first glance not what we expected. It resembled a spicy tuna filling with avocado on top, but again were pleasantly surprised by how delicious it was. For our sushi entrees we ordered a classic Rainbow Roll and a Fancy Lobster Roll. The Rainbow Roll practically melted in your mouth and had some of the freshest fish I have ever tasted. The Lobster Roll was absolutely out of this world and the creamy lobster meat was superb. To finish off our meal we had the Japanese Mochi Ice Cream in a tangerine/orange flavor. Being that neither one of us had ever had it we were both excited to give it a try and again we were blown away. The ice cream was rich and creamy and the rice paper that it was wrapped in also had a strong, but fresh orange flavor. It was the perfect ending to a delicious lunch. The prices are very reasonable for both the sushi and Chinese offerings. I think Wasabi2 is quickly working it's way to being "the place" for sushi and Chinese food. If you are in or around the West Chester area this is definitely a place to visit.

As a lover of "In Her Shoes" I had to try this place out. Friends of mine invited us to meet them there for dinner, I don't like "jerk" so I was reluctant to go, but then I remembered the delicious patties we had in Jamaica and we headed over. We forgot to BYO so there was a 6 pack to split between the 4 of us. Not well planned. The service was less then mediocre, but the food was delicious! We ordered the patties, and although they weren't as good as Jamaica they sure beat the hell out of the store bought poisonous frozen ones. The Dunns BBQ Chicken was finger lickin' good, albeit a little too much bbq sauce, but mmmmmmmmmmM! My friend ordered the Ox Tail Stew, which was my second choice. The gooey deliciousness fell off the bone and made me wish I got that. A "d" rated movie was playing in the background, the grassy area made it more authentic rather then a slab on concrete. I would go back in a minute for those aforementioned items, but this time with some margaritas!

We went here on a Monday night as New Delhi was closed. We would have been better off picking another cuisine instead of substituting with Tandoor India. The staff were so dour that they would have been better suited for working for a funeral home than a restaurant. All the food was mediocre at best and the selection on the buffet was very small compared to ND. We finished our pitcher of water and were not provided a refill.
