The rice in the rice pudding was overcooked.... and I got very bloated after eating here - a reaction I have never had in the past to eating anything. My fiance had the same outcome.

The food was amazing. I had the chicken tiki marsala. The décor was lovely and modern, not your typical Indian restaurant. The staff was great and one of the owners talked with us. Great place and great people.

Although I did not eat inside, I definitely want to after I picked up my food and saw how adorable the place is inside. Since I usually can't pick what to have for dinner, I decided to go with the vegetable combination plate #8. This combination plate included the Ye Misr Wot, Mushroom Wot, Shero, Ye Kik Alecha, Gomen, Atkilt Alecha, Tikil Gomen, and Keiy Sire. Everything was served on a large, airy, and poreus sourdough pancake. I personally didn't mind the pancake but its strong flavor kept me from pairing it with the dishes after a while. The Ye Misr Wot has a strong smoky flavor: the same thing goes for the Mushroom Wot, but in this dish the moisture-content of the mushroom slightly mellows out the intensity of the spices. The Shero had little texture but compromised with flavor: it tasted smoky like the two dishes mentioned above, but it also had a very strong cumin flavor to me (which is not a part of the berbere spice mix that they use). To compare, the Ye Kik Alecha has a mild but very delicious flavor with a starchy consistency. The Gomen (collard greens), one of the mild vegetable dishes on their menu, tasted pleasant and light without the starchiness. The Atkilt Alecha was also very delicious and mild, and probably my favorite if it would come to ordering a single meal: since it has the different textures of the potato, bean, and carrot. If you are fine with having less vegetables on your plate (I like variety), you shouldn't hestitate to order single meals of any vegetarian dish on the menu. Okay, saying it's my favorite might be a lie, because the Tikil Gomen has a very unique, mildly sweet taste that I just can't put my finger on. However, it only gets its texture from carrots and cabbage, so personally I probably wouldn't order it as a single meal unless I'd eat it over rice. Then finally, the Keiy Sire also has a very interesting flavor that I can't explain very well. The sweetness of the beets is there, but it's not overwhelming and it blends in nicely with the tomato sauce. Overall, I ordered the combo plate to nail down my favorite dishes, but I think I might keep ordering the combination plate since it includes many different textures and a good variety of flavors!

This is our favorite Indian restaurant in town - delicious food and pretty good service. All of the dishes are delicious and made to perfection. The only deterrent for me is that, when ordering takeout, they short you a bit on the portions (the rice was about half the size of the in-house portions). This was disappointing when getting home and expecting the awesome portions they give you there. In short, it just means make sure you eat there!

This place is one of my favorite restaurants hand down! Great food and BYOB! Can't go wrong with that! Makes the bill so much cheaper! I love everything on the menu! It's kind of small in there so groups of 6 or more will definitely be cramped! The only reason why I didn't give this place 6 stars is because the parking SUCKS, which I understand is out of their control but I also think the waitresses could be nicer

Staff was friendly upon arrival but I have to say it is WAY over priced an NOT authentic at all. My salad was $15 and came with 1/2 cup of diced up very chewy lamb. My salad was to go and the usual protocol for salads to go is dressing comes on the side but this one had left my salad soggy by the time I got home.

I wish Jamaican Jerk Hut evoked images of kids chasing fireflies with mason jars and friends laughing and clinking beers. After all, they have giant yard with picnic tables and lawn chairs, a homemade stage that features Caribbean bands, and a BYOB policy that helps create the ideal setting for a backyard BBQ. It could easily assume a G Love vibe, but my friend, this place falls way short. Meredith's review is exactly on point. After the astounding "corkage and entertainment fees," which can get up to $20, you're fighting other tables to win the server's attention and before you know it, everyone's throwing food, flipping tables, and trashing the stage (joke). What I'm trying to say is, there's a lot of wait and trouble for food that's blandness personified. Points for concept, not for execution.
Good food - friendly service - not the best of neighborhoods - But...I always leave with a smile and full belly - yum!

My wife & I made our first trip to this restaurant and the exterior of the restaurant initially caused s some concern. However, when we stepped inside, we were pleasantly surprised. Unfortunately, the steaks we ordered we some of the toughest we ave ever tried to chew and unattractively plated. We will definitely not be returning!

I have been to more Thai restaurants than I can count, and have never found a bad one. This one is special, I went for lunch and was pleasantly surprised from the moment I walked in. The place is comfortable and the tables are spaced far enough apart so that I don't have to listen to someone else's conversation. I split an order of Tom Yum soup with my lovely lunch date. It is a Thai version of hot and sour soup and was a unique combination of subtle flavors that made each mouthful an event. The entree was Padthai and was every bit as good as the King and I. The one complaint i had was that it could have been hotter but since I was given the choice of hotness, I only have my self to blame. I don't normally consider "service" that big of a part of my restaurant experience unless it is so bad that it was insulting but this was different. I felt that the owner and the waiter considered us guests in their home. All in all this was a most enjoyable experience. I will make the half hour trip to visit this place so evening to savor their dinner menu.

What can I say, this is certainly my favourite stop for Vietnamese subs in downtown Edmonton. I've stopped by twice since they reopened in this location and I've thoroughly enjoyed the chicken sate subs that I've eaten. This location is pretty unassuming, but I'm happy that they have their expansive menu. I'm not terribly fond of their bubble tea (but that's not the focus of this place anyway) instead, it's their subs that I adore and will continue to eat every so often.
They have a quality (ie cheap) city-wide special and a legit dive bar experience. If you like dives this is one of the many Baltimore Avenue gems.

This little hole in the wall has pretty good pho and it is of decent serving size. However, the service was slow and bland. The waitress looked uninterested/annoyed when we waved for her attention. When I asked if I could substitute spring rolls for egg rolls for my combo, the answer was an absolute 'no' accompanied with an almost impatient eye-roll. Our drinks never came. Be ready to go up to the counter and ask for what you need or self-serve. Might opt for take-out next time around.
Great pad Thai & very affordable. Friendly & polite server. The owner brought us a free plate of summer rolls (non-fried spring rolls) during our meal, too.

I love Thai...but this was just..MEH..We stopped in on a Friday evening about 8 and it was busy but not "crowded". They service was ridiculously slow. It was 15 minutes before i got a cup of tea. The calamari was good, as was the dipping sauce. I ordered my pad thai "medium hot", as I always have in every other Thai joint from NY to FL. It was bland and unimpressive. I also feel that the portions were on the small side for the price. I might stop in for lunch, but I wouldn't bother for dinner. There are better choices in the area.

Stopped by for a late lunch/happy hour to try out their menu. I always eat Vietnamese food so I went with Japanese, I think. The pork belly pops weren't on the menu but the gentleman was happy to serve them up. I also ordered a pork ramen (tankatsu). Pork belly pops were delicious, tender, sweet and salty. Then came my ramen. I have mixed feelings about this dish. It wasn't smooth tasting like other ramens I've had but it was good none the less. Possibly too much wood ear? Eggs were perfectly soft boiled. Presentation could of been better but I guess it didn't matter as I just dug in. I probably could deduct this place a star but since they are new, I'll let them work out the kinks. Some examples would be, they brought me "pho" condiments for my ramen... That's just weird. I'm all for fusion but ugh no. Being the only person in here, service should of been top notch. The server was nice but he forgot my setting before he gave me my appetizer. It also looked inexperienced carrying out my ramen bowl without a serving tray. Sure it's convenient but it's just not professional. Then Wassup with the music? I think the DJ went through three genres. I'll be back and hopefully the staff gets training on basic restaurant equiette.

Great place for those who get the culture. I am from Tajikistan so I spoke the language the personnel did. They place special requested music for us. Food was simple yet very good. We had a great time. One only thing is that this place needs a good manager who will renovate the place and will emprove the appearance of the food....make it more esthetic

Excellent!! Service can be slow but food is worth waiting for. I had the fish cakes with cucumber sauce as an appetizer and the shrimp and veggies with red curry paste as a main, along with rice and a Thai iced tea. It took a while for the waiter to take my to order, but after that the food came right away and the taste was superb! Veggies were fresh, and seafood succulent and yummy! I would certainly go again at the next opportunity! Recommended.

Nothing special here. Don't order the crab soup. There is very little crab...and zero white asparagus, they substituted it with canned baby corn. If you are looking for contemporary Vietnamese, MOPHO is way better. The only thing Magasin has going for it is just cute wallpaper on a trendy street.

This place is soooo delicious!! My boyfriend and I have ordered from here twice. Tonight being the second time. We have gotten the fish hoagies and mac and chz and omg so good. I feel like the food is cooked perfectly and super tasty. Also tonight, they forgot the 2 sides of mac and chz with our order, I was so bummed out Bc I've been craving it, so I called and the woman I spoke to on the phone was really sweet and accommodating!!! She immediately sent out the order without any hesitations or difficulties. And the mac and chz was hot and delicious when it got here :-)

Fantastic Indian food in an unlikely, intimate location. Menu items were super diverse and well representative of what Greater India has to offer. One of Tampa Bay's better restaurants - we will definitely be back.

The food is legit here! I've tried about 1/2 of their menu by now and I can certainly say they know how to Season their dishes. The menu is pretty diverse as it offers both Carribean food & West african dishes. The Oxtail & Jerk Chicken are my go to dishes. Today I had the grilled goat and it's divine!

Delicious food, and the BEST Spring rolls ever! We take-out from here a lot, it's all good. I love the Hue noodle soup with veggies and the lemongrass chicken with rice noodles. The Banh Mi is very good, but on the smaller side. Portion sizes are generally a bit smaller but it's never enough to prevent us from going there often.

Ordered the appetizer platter which was a lot more food than I thought. Definitely worth it. We also got the coconut soup. It was ok. Not a lot of flavor. We also got the drunken noodles which were very good, but we ordered it the spiciest you could get it on the Yelp app and it still was only moderately spicy. Luckily we had also asked for extra spicy sauce on the side. I'd order from them again.

It's hard to imagine this truck slipping through my fingers for so long but I've finally been filled in on what I've been missing out over at the Drexel campus food truck scene! I was lucky enough to have a friend deliver it to me at work as it's slightly far from the hospital that I work at. BUT OH MY GOODNESS! If this truck was 6 blocks closer I'd be 6 times heavier. I got to try the seemingly yelp famous tilapia burrito and it was worth every part of the $6. Man I will definitely find my way back to try the rest of the menu soon!

Definitely a place we need in KOP, much better than The Halal Guys. The steak shawarma is excellent. Only two complains. 1) there should be morr hummus in the shawarma and 2) they don't have lamb as well. But this is authentic Israeli/Middle Eastern quality food.

The food is great, service is good and the prices are reasonable. I would recommend the Antoinette. It is great!!! The only reason I did not give it a five star is because they should really think about remodeling. I do like the hometown feel but would not mind it being a little cleaner. I like it better than a busy diner.

Update: Recently, I've had some not-so-great meals from here. My last one was particularly disappointing. We ordered the Pad Thai, which was nothing special, and several appetizers (tapas style.) They were flavorless and cheap. I won't be ordering from here again. They're very friendly, but the food just isn't great. -----(original post)----- I've only had take out from here, so I can't speak to the restaurant's service/atmosphere. However, the food is very good. Creative dishes, super reasonable prices, and flavorful, hearty proportions make this my go-to Asian place. I've had a couple of chicken dishes which were very good and included fresh veggies and a shrimp dish which was surprisingly good. The shrimp was not overcooked (amazingly!) and the sauce was tasty but light. If you're in the mood for Asian takeout, Jasmine Rice is a wonderful option.

Oh gosh, while I miss the restaurant that used to be in this location, I really was wowed by my experience here tonight. Not only did my group have some great food (the appetizers were wonderful especially the enoki mushrooms!!), but the beverages were wonderful as well! Next time I may just come here for the bubble tea in a lightbulb glass that really does light up. I mean where else can you get such a thing?? My pho was good and flavourful (and I got a regular -- there's no way that I'd be able to have finished anything larger!!). I wasn't actually a huge fan of the mochi ice -- I liked the green tea one but the other two flavours weren't my style of mochi ice cream dessert. The service was pretty great as well. I rather liked the presentation: we got all of our bills split and brought to the table in a pretty awesome way. I look forward to returning to this location as the food was great, the presentation was unique and I do want to try a lightbulb bubble tea drink at some point!

I went here with my mother, a native Jamaican. She ordered fish, the snapper I believe. I ordered the jerk chicken, my favorite food on the planet. Her fish came out completely dried out. They didn't have any more fish (???) so they brought her curry chicken. It was also dry and flavorless. She was very disappointed. The jerk chicken was fine. Pretty spicy and not too dry. The rice could have been a little softer. Overall, it was an okay meal. Nothing special. Not worth a return visit when there are food carts that are much better.

So good. Their roasted chicken sandwich is delicious. The combination of cilantro and the flavor of the chicken along with the jalepenos. So good. Their Pho is really good too. Also, very affordable which is always a plus.

Great food. I always want to try this place and I finally did it thanks to groupon. Food is great. I wish it's spicier. I used to live in Thailand and honestly some food here taste just like food in Thailand and some are too Americanize but still good. I have been here three times and will go back again for sure. BYOB and very friendly service.

Delicious! Best Indian food in Indianapolis. I would recommend the Chole and Tanduri Chicken. Great vegetarian and vegan dishes, even at the buffet. Finally, somewhere we can go for great Indian food.

I gotta say, this place has certainly had its ups and downs over the years. I've been a customer here on-and-off for 7 years, and while it hasn't been the most consistent place, right now it's very good. The new owner is trying REALLY hard to make it work, and is (mostly) succeeding. The food is spicy and tasty, and the service is prompt and friendly. We ordered the usual: Chicken Tikka Masala, Baingan Bhartha, Saag Paneer, an order of plain Naan, and Tandoori Chicken. Everything was delicious and tasted fresh and spicy. After a long hiatus away, we were pleasantly surprised! My only gripe with Desi is that they no longer take Restaurant.com gift cards, or coupons from the Entertainment book. This is a bit annoying because it is misleading. Why advertise in a coupon book if you won't even take them?! Overall however, this is definitely a place to try!! Come here if you want great Indian food and awesome service :)

first off, we didn't eat here, but we did drink and smoke... a lot. The flavors were so cool, you get to mix and match and you found out quickly which ones you enjoy the most. (Mine was a combo of orange and vanilla for an Orange Julius flavor) it was the weekend, so they had a belly dancer, who was pretty good and did a great job of embarrassing some of our male friends. Over all a great time, but you have to be open to a lot of smoke and like to people watch and be entertained.

Stopped by to try the lunch special as this spot was recommended by a coworker. Extremely good yellow curry. Spicier than usual but I love spicy. Portions and service was decent but nothing exceptional. I will give them another shot.

i visited al's fingerling good bbq in ybor city it was great experience i will come back again, in my book it was a ten, i did'nt have to many sides i tried the mac n cheese and okra n tomatoe i was very satisfied, i give them five stars thanks, see you soon

This little cafe is a heaven on earth. Extremely friendly staff. Food was authentic and amazing. We ordered jungle curry and noodle soup. Very fresh, light and flavorful. But if you are looking for a fine dining experience, this is not the place for you

I keep coming back quite often. However after my last visit which was in 2014 I didn't come back since during that visit I had a live cockroach crawling on my table. So much for authentic experience ;). Apart from Mumbai grille in greenwood this is the other place which offers authentic Indian food. So today I came back again! Note that all buffet items were not ready at 12:06. However they had enough items to complete a meal nonetheless. Some highlights of today's visit: 1. Sambar was awesome 2. Medu vada good 3. Server promptly came and took order of masala dosa. Unlike most of the time the server was actually seen socializing with others and offering suggestions. The biriyani and mutton rogan josh were good as usual. Will come here again.
I was not very impressed with the food at this location. Everything was very very bland. Not very authentic......
After a recent visit to P.F. Chang's, I should add that the crispy fried green beans with spicy wasabi sauce should be a staple for anyone visiting this place!

I was over charged by a few dollars and the woman behind the counter was completely out of it. She put my order in a to go box when I told her it was for here, then over charged me when the price should have been around $7.49. I probably won't go back here for a while. The salad was off today. Not memorable.

Food is delicious and reasonably priced. Service is very friendly but they could use an extra person.. Tends to be slow. Even so the kitchen seems quick if it's an empty night. It's your average, solid Thai place. Good for dropping in with no reservation or take out. Parking is the usual in Media.. There's a lot just east of here off of state street... Otherwise it's street parking. It is usually kind of loud with conversation.. No booths or dividers just a room full of tables.

When there was no other restaurant open in the area this Sunday, we decided to try out the $6.99 lunch buffet. It was completely dead in there, maybe because we were close to the transition between lunch and dinner. Our server was completely attentive and really polite. He made sure that we had endless amounts of water and naan. The food was pretty good, but because we were the only ones in there, I'm not really sure how fresh it really was. I did like the veggie pakora and the spinach and cheese, and I love the veggie tots that they had, so good. Something about the presentation was a little off putting. It just wasn't visually the best looking buffet that I've ever been to, which is important to me when the point is to eat a mass quantity. I would go back and try their menu items, I just don't know if I'd be up for buffet again.

Poor customer service, but good usually. Went for lunch and was served something in edible after many wonderful breakfasts and much money spent. I sent it back after one bite and was told I had to pay for it. I never send food back, nor was I really upset about the money, it was the rude way I was treated. I have never been back and never will go back.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: This Thai food is by far the most authentic and delicious Thai food I have tried. I had the yellow curry, which was full of flavor, and had chicken, potatoes and chickpeas. It was really good. My boyfriend had the Tom Yum Gai, which is a sour soup with chicken, and it was very spicy but really good. My friend had the pad see ew(noodle dish), and she was also very pleased. Each entree was $10, so it is very reasonably priced. Overall, this food was amazing and we will be back. The chef, Pim, also came out and talked with us for awhile. She genuinely cared about our opinions, and when we mentioned it was a little spicy she said to tell the waiter next time to go easy on it! My one complaint would be the portion of rice they give you is very small, but that's nothing to complain about, as asking for more rice is easy!

They have some of the best food I ever tasted !! And that's saying a lot coming from a foodie! YOU HAVE to try the fried fish Mac n cheese with yams or oxtails rice n peas with cabbage !! only downside is it STAYS PACKED, long lines ALLL the time

A friend and I were wanting something "different" and we came across this restaurant. After reading all the positive reviews here, we decided to try it. I was excited to try something new and walked into the place with high hopes. The place was absolutely empty despite another couple; the only lady working sat us right next to the couple already there (which was awkward because it was dead silent except for our conversation with our respective company). The lady didn't seemed too thrilled to be there and gave us our menus and walked away. After looking through the menu, we picked what we wanted and waited to be tended to. After what seemed like a long time the lady finally came back and took our order. I can't remember the name of what the dish was but in the menu it said it would only come raw or medium-well - so I told her I wanted it medium-well. She quickly shot back at me, telling me she would not cook it that way, but instead rare and huffed off to the kitchen to make it. The food was alright the first few bites... then it just became overwhelming. Not in a good way. When we asked for more of the bread, the lady seemed annoyed we bothered her. Overall, it wasn't a pleasant experience. Maybe it was just a bad day or a fluke, but I still probably won't be going back anytime soon.

I used to love this place, but the last handful of visits, food has been consistently different than before. With new faces in the restaurant working, I assume there is new ownership or new chefs or both. They used to make some of the best tom yum noodle soup I have had but not any longer. The soup used to contain ground and sliced meat both along with chicken balls and wonton to accompany the crushed peanut, noodles, beansprouts and bok choy. Portions were larger and spice levels higher. Dish has totally changed in all of those regards but also broth is different. I feel most of the dishes taste different now such as larb, kao soi, and pad ka pao to name a few. They are not bad, but not as stellar as previously were. It's a bit disappointing for me as well as some friends who feel similarly. Still recommend, as food is good, but does taste different!

I haven't been back in two years but I wanted to have a dosa so I came back. Big disappointment. New ownership brought a lot higher prices and a lower quality of food. My fav chicken makhani was too tomatoey and the lamb curry was runny. I think that's it for this place. Dosa quality is the same but not worth the price.

Me and my wife went there and it has been a long time since we had Indian cuisine. The server was great. She explained most of the dinners on the menu, a great help. The food was excellent. We will be going back again. I had the lamb naag and really enjoyed it while my wife had the butter chicken. Lots of food. The only draw back was the server asked if we wanted bread and we said yes but we were not aware of the charges for the bread, which came with a mango spread and a third charge we were not expecting. These three items jumped up the bill over ten dollars. Other than that, we both enjoyed the atmosphere of the restaurant and the food was great. We will be back!
Great curry house experience outside of the UK.

Experience Brain: We have been coming here for 3 years now, and I want to make one thing perfectly clear about this particular Zeko's. We have not been able to figure out who the owner may be on any particular visit because every person on staff here is just so phenomenal! On our first visit, a gentleman greeted us right away and made us feel so at home we thought it was his place and came back looking for him only to receive the same treatment from a young lady in his place. Then so on and so on with every visit. This place is service perfection! We have never once had issues ordering our food. The cashiers are always quick to help out with suggestions based on our favorites. They even point out what's on promotion that day! Most people these days could not care less whether you order or not, are happy or not, call their office to complain or not. This place is the perfect opposite, as we cannot tell who the owner or manager must be based on attitude because every person there is so happy and helpful. We make regular trips here from Orlando for the entire experience, and I am proud to say that we are constantly telling others to make a stop on their next trip to Tampa. They are constantly cleaning too. I have yet to sit through a single meal without every empty table around me being scrubbed within an inch of its life. A funny little thing though. We never plan this, but we always end up sitting in the exact same booth every single time! :) Chef Brain: I will say here and now that the food is delivered to the table straight from the kitchen screaming hot, so do not come here starving or you will have no tongue or roof of your mouth left. The gyros are my go-to here, because they are just the right size to fill me up, and are seasoned so perfectly that I have trouble ordering my way through the rest of the menu. The fries are always the best bet if you want the freshest fries you've ever eaten straight from the fryer. They serve steak fries here, so they can hold up under the hardcore dunkers who, like myself, dig into the gyro with a fry to get at that amazing tzatziki sauce hidden inside. The falafel is another favorite with my little group. None of them knows what falafel is, but they know it is good and that is clearly all it takes for this normally picky crowd.
Mmmm! Recommend Samosa Chaat, chicken curry, beef short ribs, pakora, paneer...and of course dessert sampler. The iced chai was sweetened perfectly.

Really great restaurant. Nice atmosphere. Tables well placed (not sitting in your neighbors lap). Staff willing to please. We had two chicken dishes and a vegetarian entre along with garlic naan. Everything delicious and the meal was well timed. Would definitely return.

Yah Mon is an exquisite Caribbean restaurant that tends to all dietary needs. My friend and I were served by Andre, the chefs wife, and they did an excellent job at accommodating our time and dietary restrictions. Their dedication ti customer service, detail and original cuisine is amazing! Thank you for being great.

New Review: Food was pretty good overall and the menu had a bunch of interesting selections. I was pleasantly surprised. I will definitely go back and give it one more go-around. Old Review: I don't understand the fuss over this place. The food is not particularly good and is dramatically over-salted. They seem more interested in having interesting cocktails than in focusing on the cooking. To top it off, it's kind of expensive. The only really fun and enjoyable part of the meal was dessert. It's nice to be able to order a shot glass taste of a few different desserts. We ordered 10 for the table and shared tastes of them all. They were good and the perfect size.

It's been awhile since I've been back to Numchok Wilai but I was finally able to try their lunch deal ($12). Heard good previously and it definitely is a good deal. They have 12 options to choose from and I went with the pad thai. Lunch deal comes with lemon grass soup (had a nice bit of heat to it and a couple pieces of mushrooms in it), two spring rolls (light, crunchy) and the main of your choice. My pad thai was pretty good - really liked how it wasn't overly sweet and had the essential elements of what makes a solid pad thai good. Came with a couple shrimps and chicken. Winner winner - now if only they would move closer to my work so I could go there more often...

Excellent Gyros....I would have to say one of the best I've ever had! Instead of just onions and sauce and tomatoes, they put a really good dark leafy lettuce as well. Excellent taste...and friendly service. I will definitely be back!

Visited this restaurant for dinner Friday night and was pleasantly surprised to arrive to live latin music. The food was very good, as were the drinks. The service was a little bit slow but only one waiter was working the entire restaurant. Overall great experience and lively ambiance. Will definitely return.
By far my favorite place to go for a quick bite. The choclatey turtle cheesecake changed my life. The girl who helped me was very friendly despite the place being packed.

Definitely going back! We were going to try out Hostaria down the block but it was closed for some reason so we took our two bottles of wine here. They only take cash, which is annoying, but the food is DELICIOUS and you get a huge portion. Well done!

Oh Dmitris, how I love you. Let me count the ways. There are so many. You are amazing. Dmitris is a SMALL BYOB that does not take reservations or credit cards, so be warned. As one of those annoying people who never has cash (Why yes, I would like to pay for this 99 cent pack of gum with my card!) I'm not thrilled with this policy, but remembering to hit up the ATM is a price I'm willing to pay if it means I get to eat at Dmitris. And there's no corkage fee or judgement when you roll up with a group and each of you has their own bottle of wine. Cheers! The restaurant is small but never really feels super tight or crowded, even if it is a packed house, and there's always an interesting mix of people here - couples on first dates, kids, people dressed up, people wearing gym clothes...no matter what the occasion, Dmitris can handle it - Let's celebrate Tuesday! The kitchen is open, which I always think is a cool touch, and it's always nice to see how fresh your food is. Because, it's like, super fresh. I basically get the same thing every time I come here - spanikopita, hummus and the tomato and mozzarella salad (which, for some reason, is always called a Special, yet they always offer it. Strange). My boyfriend is a loyal devotee - ok, obssessive fan - of the baba, hummus, and shrimp scampi. All the dishes are just fabulous, and huge portions. We always end up packing up leftovers, although depending on how much damage we've done on our wine, sometimes we forget to actually take them home with us. The pita here is amazing, and they make this awesome olive oil/herby dipping stuff that I could drink. That would be inappropriate, but it is just that good. The waitresses kind of work as a team, which sometimes I don't love, but they manage to pull it off here. They are all incredibly nice and never seem to be flustered or overwhelmed, even though there's always a lot going on. It should be noted that it's 10:00am and I'm ready to go get some hummus! Ugh, thanks Dmitris.

While I can only vouch for their take out Thai Iced Teas, I can tell you they are fantastic! Walked in here the other day & loved the atmosphere. Reminds me of all the authentic Thai places I used to frequent back home. A very friendly woman was up at front, greeted me really kindly, and had my drink ready really fast! I can't wait to come back and eat here, because I have heard over and over again this place is a must for Thai!

The food is delicious but the customer service sucks. They make you feel like your bothering them by being there. The guy at the counter has no personality unless you have a flat tummy and big breasts. And the waitress isn't much better. I was sitting at the table waiting to place order and the waitress walks up. Puts the order book in one hand and has a pen in the other and just stares at the table. She doesn't say a word, just stares at the table. I order and she writes somthing down and walks away without a word. So now I'm irratated and hungry. I start looking around and think they did what they could with decorating this place, and it seemed dirtier than my last visit. My food came and was great, the portions were large. I finished and sat there full and happy waiting for a bill. Nothing. I got up went to the counter and after several minutes the guy come out of the back, stops at the counter and stares at me. I tell him I need to pay my bill, he looks around and picks up a bill a tells me the amount. I hand him my card and thank him, still not a word. He hands me back my card and the receipt to sign. Finally he speaks! You, copy? I said yes and he printed me a copy, set it on the counter in front of me and walked away. As a rule I don't put up with this kind of behavior, good food aside. I'm in the area every so often, but unless I'm craving Vietnamese food with a side of dismissive disrespect I'll pass on eating here
Don't eat here, ate there last night my wife and I got food poisioning! the food tasted ok, but the hidden illness caught up to the both of us. If you don't mind getting violently sick eat there.

First off I can't believe I have to rate these guys with atleast one star. They don't deserve a single one this place had the Worst food. We paid 35$ for nothing this place is an epic fail...if you like throwing your money away for free be my guest. I have never ever wasted money for food like this.Don't waste your money here.the service is run by a bunch of dumb-asses who don't know what the hell they are doing and they force you to pay tip and the tip is insane these dudes are crazy... Thank you

A better than average, gut busting lunch buffet! Be warned that this place gets packed during lunch hour. The ding space is tight, noisy and the pace seems to be hurried. Combine that with the equally crowded shopping strip it sits in and may have a slight case of indigestion when it's all said and done. Either way, the buffet is worth checking. Bring your appetite and your patience.

You know the soup guy from Seinfeld? Well, imagine the same experience, but with falafels and meat instead. What you need to know: $10 per dish, cash only, one dish person, the line is long, you have to ask for veg option early! The owner of this food truck has been doing this for years, and it shows because he absolutely loves his job. His cart is decorated with fresh fruits and vegetables, and he'll dance around in his cart, take small bites from his own creation from time to time, and create a concoction that is different every day of the week, with a particular protein du-jour and seasonal vegetables. Is the line worth it? Absolutely, but will your colleagues be upset when you promised them a plate, but then realized that you had to go to the back of the line to get a second plate - YES! I recommend going early, because despite what yelp says, he runs out of his ingredients early, and there's nothing you can do about that! And he doesn't give you utensils, or napkins...be prepared.

I should state that my stomach has always been considered weak. I've been getting better with my exploration of food and culture. With that said, Jamaican food is spicy. My mouth was on fire. Fortunately, the restaurant is BYOB so I was able to down a lot of wine with my meal. The atmosphere is not my style of a restaurant. It had a stage with an i-Pod playing music. Luckily, the restaurant had a setup outside and the weather was nice as the inside of this place was disgusting looking. And, for those of you who enjoy the partaking of illegal activities that are stereotypical of Jamaican people, you are in luck. At least on that night, I was able to enjoy secondhand smoke from it.

I have been a big fan of this restaurant for a long time until today when I saw they reduced the portion on the biriyani. Not as good as they were earlier on the food portion. The food quality and consistancy remained the same but portion is simply not enough.
Great service, great food, and reasonable prices. We were super happy with our visit! Get the beef kafta, chicken kabob, or steak kabob!! So gooooood!

Pho-king pho-nomenal pho. Now that I've gotten all those pho-nny puns out of the way, let's talk soup. Finding Saigon was a godsend. After moving to Indy and leaving behind my favorite pho spot, I was desperate to find some brothy, noodley goodness in my new home. It took some trial and error (serious error), but I was finally pointed in Saigon's direction. The broth is absolutely delicious, and that's the most important fact of any pho worth it's weight in rice noodles. Other establishments come close, but Saigon is my clear favorite. Also notable are their spring rolls and vermicelli bowls. Be it order in or take out, service is expedient. I live about 15 minutes away, and my call-in order is always ready by the time I arrive. Next time you need some pho (which is all the time if we're being honest), look up Saigon.

I had my aunt take us here because I wanted to try the Crab Fried Rice, and I'm glad I got to try it. The Crab Fried Rice was very tasty and had good texture. And there were plenty of crab meat in the rice, which seems way more than the amount other restaurants use in theirs. It is only $10, which is a very great deal. I've never seen crab fried rice at any other restaurant for less than $12.95. My family ordered Pineapple Fried Rice, Spicy Fried Rice, Phad Kee Mao, and a duck bento box. They weren't too bad, but I don't think as great as my Crab Fried Rice. Service was excellent. Our waitress was very friendly and personable.

This is as good as it gets. Fresh, quality ingredients, which he claims to get from Whole Foods (meats/cheeses) and farmer's markets (produce/herbs). Completely outstanding flavors and variety. When a man puts chicken on the grill for you, and then splashes it with white wine, and throws a bundle of fresh thyme into the flames beneath the grill so that it smokes the flavor into your chicken, you have to know you're in for a treat. Nothing lets me down on a given day as much as heading all the way to this street corner, only to find that Quality Man is not there that day. (We call him Quality Man mostly for his enthusiastic lectures on how important it is to put quality things into your body, which you will listen to for as long as it takes you to get your food and leave. Soak it up, people. He's both amusingly bombastic and dead right.)

As a rule I never eat food from the street but rules are meant to be the broken and the Falafel Truck at 20th and Market promised a good time. This Falafel Truck has been well documented in local magazines and papers for years. Complete with the ornery owner and sole chef that's a "Soup Nazi"-quality character, he serves up the most buttery falafel I have ever had, fresh to order each and every time. This means a long line and long life stories of his as you anticipate the mulititude of veggies, sauces, and love he will put into your sandwich once it's your turn. Only open from 11am-2pm.

This place was good. Service was excellent. I think they're better known for their happy hour. As we sat down for dinner, it sounded like there was a large crowd in the bar. We had reservations at 6:30 on a Friday for dinner. As we sat down, there was only one other table, but the place filled up very quickly. They only have a handful of dining room tables. However, about a third of them are quaint private booths. The appetizers were good. The lamb sliders (gunless) stood out. The meat was seasoned, and not greasy at all. For dinner I tried the sea bass that was on special. It was broiled with simple seasoning served as a full fish... head and all. It was good... just watch out for the bones. My fiance tried the canneloni. This too was good. Again, the meat stuffed inside was flavored very well. All in all, this is a great place. However, I'd suggest trying the happy hour before jumping both feet in with a full dinner. The dinner was good, but not nearly as good as Harvest or a few other upscale places in the area.

Might be the best Thai food we've ever had, and we've had a lot... Great gem in a wonderful little town. Dishes were all fantastic beyond compare. Highly recommended. Visually, aromatically and taste-wise wins on every angle.

The best Indian food I've found in St. Louis since I moved here last fall. Everything that I have tried from here is been very good. The nan is very good, the sauces are thick and flavorful. and you get plenty of rice with each dish. I would highly recommend going to Flavor of India.
This place makes my favorite gyro in Saint Louis. The Gyro with hummus is to die for. The only downside is that they close early! Excellent and friendly service.

After trying the other 2 Indian Restaurants on Rt. 202 / Concord Pike, Bawarchi definitely takes 1st place for food and price. I now get take-out here almost every Friday night and have become a 'regular' at this place. In terms of atmosphere inside the actual restaurant, you don't get much, but for what they lack in that department, they sure do make up for it with their food. As I previously stated, I get take-out , so I'm not judging them on the dining atmosphere, I'm strictly judging them on their food and price. Items to note: 1. Their Raita is the best in Delaware , 2. Service can be a bit slow sometimes, but only because they make every single item fresh and made to order, 3. Their Chicken Biryani is the best in Delaware and 4. In my opinion, you get the best bang for your buck here.

I absolutely love this place! From the ambience and the decor, to the AMAZING food...I would come back time and time again! The owner is super accommodating and the staff exemplifies some of the best customer service I've ever experienced! From beginning to end, it was clear that the owner and staff here want each patron to have a nice time! This place is truly a gem! Make sure you try the half chicken and rice, you will not be let down!

This was just an awful experience. Food was good not great but for the price it was good. My wife and I ordered fried chicken and kimchi fries to start around 4:15. Our server came back a few minutes later and we ordered two sushi rolls. About 10 minutes later our sushi rolls came out but still no starter. We went ahead and ate our sushi not really worried about what came out first. After we finished our sushi we continued waiting for our starters. Our kimchi fries arrived about 10 minutes after we finished the sushi. We ate those and continued waiting for the fried chicken. Finally at about 5 our server let us know the chicken was almost ready. At 5:10 i had to ask the server to make it to go. At 5:15 he brought us the food and gave us a light apology for the wait. It took an hour for our starter with no explanation. There were 7 people in the restaurant when we arrived and only 4 people came in while we were there. I was so disappointed. Other reviews suggest this is a good place. Maybe I just caught them on a bad day. However based on my experience i would not recommend Umami and i will not be back.

Visited the Slidell location roughly 8x. The food is mediocre compared to other Greek restaurants I've visited. The baba and vegetarian grape leaves are the best items in the menu. I once had overly greasy falafels.

First time here and definitely a great spot! Outside Bartender Amanda is awesome! Food comes in huge portions and is so good. Had a grouper sandwich and crab leg bucket. The drinks are amazing as well. Live music and dancing on the water. We will definitely be coming back!

Frustrated! Worked on a reservation for 22: planned meal, set time, added to itinerary for my group traveling to Boise. Today, we got a call only 24 hours from reservation and they cancelled on us without any sort of options until I called and emailed. Their option was to come three hours earlier; however, we have a strict schedule that cannot be changed. I am now looking for dinner option for 22 - less than 24 hours to book. Lot's of frustrated people. I don't trust these guys - so, if you plan on going - maybe just show up and hope for the best, as they don't accommodate you and allow a last minute, new party to bump you out of your time slot.

Can I get a no-star review?? Went the last night of my son's military leave. Were quickly greeted and seated. The waiter quickly pushed the beer's on us, but would not show us the beer menu. Said that we could see what they had by looking up by the wall. Then left us to think about it while he promptly seated a couple next to us and gave them a beer menu!!!! Came back to take our drink order and we put in an appetizer order. Meanwhile, the table behind us was seated,their drinks brought and their appetizers brought. The table next to us had their appetizers brought out. Our waiter still had not come back. The table behind us got their entrees. Still no waiter. Finally we had to tap him on the arm on the way by as he delivered the entree's to the table next to us. He seemed "shocked" that the appetizers were not out yet. Which I had to point out to him, even though he could clearly see that from the table. I pointedly asked him if he had put the order in and he stated that he had. We put our entree order in at 7:30. Thirty minutes after our arrival. 7:45 still no food, including appetizers. One person in our party asked for the manager, who never came out. Three of us left to go next door to get a table. One stayed behind to talk to the owner, who tried to convince him that we should stay for our food. He declined stating that we had waited 45 minutes and no food. He offered a 10% discount on our meal. No thank you. He then offered the food that was made for free to go along with a coupon of 10% off for the next time. That was agreed to and the food was received, which was 2 of the 4 orders at almost an hour later. The coupon was inquired about and the owner stated they "did not have coupons" but wrote 10% off on a piece of paper. We will not be back and will never recommend this restaurant.
Best samosas on earth. Including India. That alone deems it worthy of 5 stars. Yes, the other stuff is good too!

Food excellent, service a bit lacking. I had the green curry and loved it....it had an herbiness that I've never tasted but I normally get red curry so that may be why. My husband had the beef larb which had steak not ground beef and he really enjoyed it. The papaya salad was extremely flavorful but quite spicy. Perfect for my husband, a little too spicy for me. The fresh spring rolls were made to order and contained lots of lettuce. The freshness of the ingredients was obvious and they were excellent. So, we will be back for the food. A few negative notes: The TV was blaring a TNT movie and that was distracting and annoying. The person who took our order might have been the owner, not sure about that. We found his customer service skills extremely lacking. This being said, the food was good enough for us to plan a return visit.

My first pho experience and I was not disappointed! The shrimp spring rolls were deliciously paired with a peanut sipping sauce. The big bowl of pho was served with so any fresh veggies I nearly lost my mind, and it was piping hot. The tofu crepe was equality delicious with the sweet chili sauce. The service was great and the atmosphere is a great and minimal. Will definitely return here for a meal next time I'm in Indy

I moved to Boothwyn from New York City (Manhattan). If you've been to Oriental Pearl, I'd advise you not to go looking for good Vietnamese in NYC afterward. You will find that nothing there measures up to Oriental Pearl. My personal favorites at Oriental Pearl are the Pho, Vermicelli with BBQ Pork and Spring Roll, and the green papaya salad.
Really good food! Ordered the combo with jerk chicken and stew chicken. Both were very juicy and flavorful. Highly recommend.

Great food at a fun, friendly, unique atmosphere. I had the lamb gyro, it was pretty good and the Greek street fries were really good. It had a clean and cool atmosphere with a spacious outside area in the back. Lots of interesting choices on the menu and it makes me want to come back and try some other menu items. Highly recommend.

Went to the smaller Dmitri's in Queen's village with my boyfriend for his birthday. It was still early, and there were plenty of seats, but the waitress tried to sit us elbow to elbow at some table where other people were already sitting. Mind you, the bar area was completely EMPTY! So, we told her we didn't wanna sit next to people and were finally able to get a seat at the bar. Waitress was kind of snoody as well, which kind of ruined our initial vibe. Oysters were WAAAYY too salty and they didn't even offer the spicy shrimp special! I recommend the Dmitri's on 23rd and Pine 100x over this little craphole!!!

Somewhat happy to report that most of their flaws have been corrected. Friends have seen great improvement. Not charging extra for the sauce now, and not overcharging the bill (still, please double-check your bill). Food is good. Pad Thai needs to improve (buy new better pan that does not transfer the old metallic taste to noodles). The decor and overall look of the restaurant do not match the waitresses (have them dress better particularly in the evenings, no tight shorts). Also instruct them not to pick the food with their own bare hands when making the take-out bags! Also, update listing online which is misleading customers regarding hours/days of operation. Hope this feedback helps to make it better.

Excellent fried chicken with very tasty dipping sauces. The chicken has a perfect crispy pretzel crust. My favorites were the honey mustard and the green goddess. I highly recommend! They also have delicious hand pies, with great flaky crust, particularly liked the pumpkin. There is plenty of seating inside and the place has been beautifully remodeled.

During the last ten days of August, I went on a trip to DC, Philadelphia and NYC with girlfriends. We tried a lot of different places based on Yelp reviews, even to Morimoto's in NYC, and this falafel was BY FAR the best meal I'd had. We waited in line for about 10-15 minutes, and the aromas that came from the truck made my stomach growl horribly. The cook seemed quiet - made the dish, handed it over the first person in line and accepted his $10 accordingly. Quick transaction. We attempted to talk to him, and that's when the floodgates opened. This guy has been in business for 20 years, and he's still going strong. There's obviously a reason for that, and when we tore into our meal, we understood why. The salad was light and contained bits of marinated peaches and grapes, and it was the perfect compliment to the juicy grilled chicken. The outside of the falafel was a bit overdone, but the inside was moist and delicately spiced. The pita bread and another piece of bread he served allowed us to mop up every last bit of the hummus - and believe me, you want to eat and savor every last bit. It was absolutely delicious and such a deal for only $10. We were so pleased with our meal that we had to come back to the truck to tell him and to take a photo with him. If I worked in Philly's financial district, I have a feeling I'd be down at the falafel truck at least once a week. It's two weeks later, and I am still craving another helping.

Let me also caveat that I went on Open Mic night. That was my first mistake, although I really like the decor and the general feel of the place Open Mic night ruined that because all of the people who stayed for Open Mic night were no longer eating chicken or never ordered chicken to begin with were taking up the seats. Meanwhile my group of 6 was there having ordered 3 lbs of chicken and Mac and Cheese. So we start eating and talking about our meal and then we get shushed. That is right we got shushed by the manager or greeter when I am pretty sure out of the 20 other people there, we were the only ones actually eating chicken. We were forced to sit directly in front of the players because all of the non-chicken eating customers were in the booths. This is the main reason I am giving this place 1 star. That was a pretty crappy way to alienate your only customers eating chicken. Aside from that, the front counter service was friendly and courteous. That one experience just poisoned my overall opinion of this place. I thought the chicken was pretty alright with the sauces being the best part of the meal. The Mac and Cheese was breaded but was bland and needed a bit more flavor and probably less breading. The food on its own and overall restaurant feel would have rated a 2 stars. They have a cool drink selection including cock cola (named after the rooster) and some hip natural colas. This place is worth a try but I would recommend a lunch time trip to avoid any Open Mic night concerns and you can make your own judgement. They just started up so maybe they are still working out recipes and what the final food will be.

Seriously one of the worst Indian buffets I have had in Metro St.Louis. None of the dishes had a flavor of there own. The floors were muddled if they existed at all. The tandoori chicken, typically a highlight for me on any Indian Buffet, was dry, overcomes and flavorless. The kitchen or whatever was behind those doors was extremely loud especially since the rest of the restaurant was quiet. I don't know if they we killing chickens for dinner service or just throwing the pans around for fun but either way it was loud. On the plus side the restaurant was clean, tastefully decorated, well themed, and generally comfortable. It really is a shame the food was so bad.

If you are into serious flavor, then this is your place. The Chicken Wett is awesome and spicy, and the lentils are super yummy!! I had a lamb dish with collard greens that was fantastic as well! The staff are very friendly and make you feel more than welcome! I think that we are lucky to have a place like this in Indiana. Highly recommended!!

I knew about this place because we went here (it was close) with church friends who said that this place is really good. They used to have a buffet during lunch but we never get to do it. Now all they have are lunch specials which goes around $7. I've been here twice, first with the hubs (can't remember what we had but I'm guessing it's kabobs & they were great). Second was with with a friend. I ordered Qabuli Palow (not a lunch special) it's basically rice with raisins carrot strips in it & there's a lamb thigh inside. The lamb was ok, I want more someting on it I guess, more spice or more taste. It seems bland. And I think it would be nice if they will add something on the side coz it's pretty much all rice, the raisins & carrots adds taste but it looks like it's all rice lol. The beef kabob on the other hand tasted great & I like that it has a side of salad on it. Oh and I tried the Turkish coffee, it was yummy! I will come back to try the other choices they have!

Just had a delicious lunch! The roasted potatoes are wonderfully flavorful and crispy. My husband's souvlaki (chicken) was perfectly juicy. Grilled cheese pita a big hit with our 9 year old. I loved my gyro platter and stuffed grape leaves. Sometimes I have found stuffed grape leaves a little bitter, these weren't at all. Very friendly employees and owner!

Very good Thai food. Saw this place in St Louis Magazine "best Of" article. They are lauded for the BEST Masaman Curry in STL area. The curry was VERY good. We have been back several times since and always get the curry and another dish. The place is a hole in the wall but worth checking out.
Some of the best gluten free bread I have ever had! Always a great meal every time we go.
Excellent food and amazing service. Very fresh and authentic. Very nice owner and staff members too!!

This may possibly be the very best Tikka Masala on the face of the entire earth. Not a light statement, to be sure. This sauce is exquisite. The Onion Kulcha is the real deal too. This place just set the bar on both of those dishes. If you are a fan of this cuisine, you must stop here. I can't think of anything else relevant. Atmosphere, service, facilities are on point.
Third class food! Period. They tried to sell Indian food chipotle style but is a complete flop in terms of pricing and espetially the food taste which sucks.

It's been 2 years since I've been back to Philly. I have since tried to find the perfect coffeeshop since I arrived last week. After trying out a few and almost puked because of their substandard espresso, I stumbled upon La Va, which was recommended by a friend. I love the atmosphere and the friendly baristas. I would definitely come back!

My first thought when I walked up to this place was to turn around and find someplace else to have lunch. I just didn't have a good feeling about the tacky way the place looked from the outside... The second hint to leave was the handwritten note placed in the entrance stating that if it took longer than one minute to be seated, you should forward a message about it to the email address on the note.. But since I saw a party of about 12 people seated having lunch, I figured that it was an ok meal to have... I couldn't have been more wrong. The food that I recieved was served barely warm, and looked as if it was premade.. If I thought that they were just having an off day, I would have asked to see the manager.. But since there were only a few people working inside, I probably had already seen or had been served by the so-called manager... If you're tempted to stop in one of the few restaurants they own under the same name, remember that yelp's lowest rating is one star... That's what you'll likely be giving them after they serve another disgusting meal..

Loved the food! Had their artichoke special as an appetizer, the pasta with pistachio pesto as second course (this was awesome!). Then the rabbit as my main course, delicious! Finally the cannoli for desert. The food was as expected, very very good. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because the restaurant is very small and the tables are crammed in together. Where I was sitting, the staff had to walk by my chair to the kitchen and almost every time they bumped my chair ( very annoying ).

Have dined here 3 times and every time I've said we should come here more often. The place is empty or maybe has another table filled all 3 times I have been there, not sure why. I eat Thai quite often and this place is one of my favorites. The quality and quantity of the food is on point. They get their spice levels right which is highly important to me when choosing Thai. Service is great and prices are reasonable. They also have a happy hour menu with $5 sushi rolls and apps such as exam ma and spring rolls. Update: apparently we come too early. Ate here again around 7pm and place was packed

I really enjoyed this place! I went for a lunch buffet and had a positive experience. The service here is great - the servers were very attentive and the manager was very friendly. He even helped to point out which specific dishes would be safe for my food allergies, and he offered me a free sample of their mango lassi. The ambiance was cozy and the food was delicious. I loved the complimentary chai tea at the buffet! I decided to try this place out instead of opting for any other place in University City where I would have spent the same amount of money, if not more, for less food and mediocre service/ambiance. I look forward to coming back to this place soon!

The food was outstanding as it has been for around 20 years. The seafood was perfect tender and fresh. The lamb Delicious, tender and cooked to perfection. Same for the deserts and appetizers! But the service unfortunately doesn't hold the same magical appeal. It was a special occasion and the servers ruined it!!! They're rude, and have a air as though your doing them a favor by coming in!!!! Heaven forbid you try to strike up a short conversation they just stare at you!! Is this the new of in the Queens village area? Serving style aka alien abducted style!! Ohhhh wait it just hit me it's the hipster style/cool to be rude and stand offish. At least the food rocked and my families Italian so not much can ruin a night out for us!

The pho here is really good! Better than what I usually have back at home in MD. Their spring roll was also delicious - my husband almost ordered a second one. I'm giving it four stars b/c our table didn't seem all that clean, service was just ok, and my husband ordered the mango chicken & shrimp and that was ok.

"Above Par" is the best way to sum this place up. They are consistent. The food - whether it be eggs and pancakes with home fries for breakfast, tabouli with dolmas for lunch, or gyro for dinner - is always tasty and fresh. I believe they make the BEST tzatziki in town. The service isn't always the cheeriest, but they are always helpful, prompt, and precise. If they smiled and showed a little more personality, it would be easy to bump them up to 5 stars. The other way they could bump up to 5 stars would be to lower EVERYTHING on the menu by about 50 to 75 cents (everything - the cans of V8, the coffee beverages, the side items). For how limited in space they are, the dining area is still accommodating and spacious. It is also kept cleanly and I like the array of reading materials they provide. Though it is tucked in the NE corner of town - if you are ever near, and enjoy good food, this is a must try.

I was a little sad when Shinju decided to re-locate and move on to bigger and better things (Fat Salmon). But, Mumbai Bistro doesn't make me miss that restaurant at all, it is that good!! Food is delicious. Prices are really good/cheap and the people that work there are so nice and friendly. I prefer to go on Tuesday or Saturday as I love their menu options on those days. I also like the Mango lassi they sell too and it seems to be a popular item..they've run out of a few times. This place is the whole package.

My BF and I were hungry after all the drinking we have done and walking up and down Bourbon St. We didn't want anything fried so we kept looking until we stumbled upon this place. Really good Beef Shawarma. Affordable and good service. The pita bread was really warm and good and the meat was tender and flavorful. It definitely HIT OUR SPOT that night! I recommend this place for late night snacking/dinner.

This was a regular go-to spot when I worked in the area, and even though it would get very hot/crowded inside, it never kept us away. The buffet offered plenty of variety, and was not the same few dishes every single time like other spots in the area. Loooove the chili chicken. While I hear they have raised their prices, I would still stop by as you typically would not need to eat dinner afterwards...so its still a value.

Excellent and healthy for a great price! They have a lot of options with some very healthy choices. The prices are very reasonable with good portion sizes. The basil pesto hummus was amazing!!! The Greek chicken pita was also very good but a bit messy to eat. It also has a choice of sides which I got the roasted veggies. The side could have been a bit nicer on the presentation but the taste was good. We also tried the chicken kabobs and chicken orzo soup both of which were a hit. Overall this place is a great choice and one I will be returning to again!

Phenomenal restaurant! Tried it for the first time with a friend because of a promotion they were running. It was crowded but the quality of food and service was worth the wait! Portions were nice size for sharing at the table. Everything tasted fresh and well prepared! I had the honey shrimp and my friend had the Mongolian beef. Both delicious. Coconut Mojitos and Banana Spring rolls are a must when you come here!!

I had the worst chicken 65 ever here.....I ordered chicken 65 and asked them if it was dry and they said yes.....I got a take out and checked it once I got back ...it was semi-gravy....and the chicken was horrible.....they were frozen pieces and warmed up or something....it was so dry and hard and chewy....I was thinking of a negative review but there is no option for that in Yelp
pretty good! great service. very attentive. just a sucker fish in the fish tank.
Service was a little slow, but staff is friendly, and food is good, not great

Came by for dinner on a Tuesday. We had a great time. We were able to talk and laugh all evening. The drinks and small plates just kept coming at a good pace. I love Mediterranean food, and everything was great.
Everything's pretty average - food, prices, ambience, service.

1st time eating here. I am soo happy to find another Indian restaurant so close too where I live. It is located in a strip mall. Once you walk into the place, your eyes will relax and your heart take a sigh of relief. The decor is great as you look around you will find more things too look at. Btw the men's restroom is huge. Now the food. We had the buffet. Which I have too say was top notch. There is a 6 meat option and tons of veg options. The rice pudding is nice and thick, I love it that way.
Some of the best food overall I've had. I do either the garlic beef, curry shrimp or penang curry. All 3 are stellar and bursting with flavor.

Simply put...this place has amazing food. My wife and I went there on a Friday evening and had a wonderful time. Everything from the location of the restaurant to the decor does not do justice to how great the food really is. I would best describe this place as a diamond in the rough. For the appetizer we got ground chicken wrapped in egg roll wrapper, deep fried and served with sweet chilli sauce. For dinner I was craving something really spicy and so I went with drunken noodles and my wife opted for rice with vegetables. The drunken noodles were just the thing I was craving...and the spicyness too. But beware the spice is not for the light hearted nor is it too hot if that's your thing. My wife's dish was pretty good as well. For dessert we got the mango ice cream and the only thing it had going for it was that it's homemade. I would have liked it to a creamy and it was more crystalized. Enjoy and happy eating!
Everyone working at this fantastic restaurant couldn't have made you feel more welcome, part of their extended family. And the food - fantastic The tres leches cake, to kill for, seriously!!!

The pho here was delicious, just like I remember back home in San Diego! I also ordered the sweet onion and cheese appetizer wrapped in beef & lemongrass, along with egg rolls. Both were very flavorful & I enjoyed it all!

This unique pita place has never let me down, the food is delicious such as the kebabs and natural cut fries. The owner is very kind and friendly. I would recommend this place to my friends and peers. The price is very good as well. I found this restaurant to be one of my top 3 medditereanen restaurants in tampa and is a must visit
We went last night and THEY HAVE VEGGIE PHO. It is now "as good as it gets".

I didn't eat at this place for too long, but I tried their Roti Canai. As a Malaysian, I can say will much pride that this is one of the only places that makes Roti Canai the way Malaysians make it. Other restaurants tend to make it overly crispy, and in much smaller servings. Golden Triangle has a better sense of how it's originally made, and has a much larger serving, well worth the price!
The buffet is amazing! I think all the food was very good and the price was actually very reasonable.

So Shere-E-Punjab may be a staple for Swarthmore students venturing out for more exciting fare than Renato's and Cheng Hing's, and the food is pretty decent, but as previous reviews have intimated, they have some serious service issues. When they started offering delivery, my friends and I rejoiced - finally, decent food that didn't require a car for pickup! We ordered $40+ worth of different dishes, including several orders of naan (their naan is admittedly v. good, if overpriced). That was only the beginning of our adventure. Well over an hour later, we called, desperate, plaintive, begging for our food. They assured us that no, they had not forgotten, and yes, it would be coming. When? we asked. Soon, they replied. We could extract no further details. It was a full thirty minutes more before the delivery guy finally limped onto campus (understand that the restaurant is a ten minute drive away, fifteen max). After bestowing a generous tip on the good man who finally alleviated our starvation, we headed inside for a feast. We soon discovered that we had only received one order of naan, but been charged for everything we ordered. I don't know about the rest of you, but I pretty much hate eating Indian food if I can't scoop my food with bread. We called the restaurant, and they said they were sorry, all of their people had left and they could not come bring us the naan we were missing, but they would write down our names and info, and the next time we ordered they would give us the bread we paid for for free and a discount on the meal to repay us for the trouble. Well, maybe I'm an idiot for not getting something in writing, but I think you can guess what happened the next time I called and asked for my already-paid-for naan and discount. Not only did they not make good on the deal, they were nothing short of rude in responding to the suggestion that anyone at their establishment might ever have made such a promise. Now, their eggplant is amazing, their mango lassies are good and their chickpeas are extremely tasty in all forms. But they are unquestionably overpriced and poorly organized. I, for one, am not going back for a repeat performance.

Thai Taste is a delightful little GEM! The food is delicious. The service is prompt, accurate and incredibly friendly. There's a vibe at Thai Taste of eating at the family table. It's obviously family owned. And moreover, family LOVED. The decor is simple, but the emphasis is on the food and service. The folks here love what they do and want their patrons to walk away not just content, but truly happy. From the creatively woven straw wrappers, to the star-shaped rice, there's a true emphasis here on the details. As an avid patron of restaurants, I find these little details go a very long way. Personally, I recommend the Peanut Chicken. It's a lightly creamy, somewhat spicy, complex dish of flavors. All served with a generous portion of rice. After writing this (and, consequently, conjuring up my fond memories of how good it is,) I may have to order some take out.
Love this place! The food is always hot and delicious. Since I've eaten here several times, I can highly recommend them...try the avocado spring rolls or the Pho Chay...you won't be dissapointed.

Siam is my absolute favorite restaurant in Carp. I don't usually eat out, but for Siam I will definitely bend my "no eating out" rule! The food is Great, the customer service is ALWAYS fantastic, the decor is nice, and the wait is always reasonable for how busy they always are. Busy restaurant means great food, and it's always worth it!

IPho has decent pho, but we haven't enjoyed the other dishes like the spicy beef noodle soup we've gotten there; it contained ingredients not listed in the menu description, a huge amount of oil, and it looked nothing like the image on the menu. The duck on their duck and cabbage salad is more bone and gristle than meat. While we'd likely return when we're not in the mood to cook, we wouldn't stray too far from the pho menu.

Food was basic, taste was alright but was like food you'd rather cook at home. Came in on a Sunday buffet, expected at least something special but unfortunately disappointed. No daal, basic sabzis like aloo baingan, cabbage etc. just one edible dessert(not even gulab jambun) Long story short. It could be better, the menu and quality and presentation.

I went with my wife for the first time. The staff is friendly without being intrusive. Pearson went through the menu with us. We recommend the "Trip Through Puerto Rico". We will definitely be returning.
Always like the chai tea! Home made and one of the best in the city. You can also get take out indian food to go as well :)

Random dinner with two other people and hour before they close - sorry! but oh was it so good! From the no wait time till the great service! Hard to believe this small BYOB can deliver such flavorful food! :) Not sure why the AC was on which made it slightly colder. Pros: Grilled octopus was delicious! tender and zesty with powerful flavors. Shrimp Pil Pil was awesome - my favorite small dish that night! its cooled with some garlic and pepper flakes but it doesn't taste spicy at all Baked fish of the day was delicious. I also ordered the baked talapia but that wasn't nearly as good. There really wasn't a horrible dish though, so this is definitely on my list to come back and try some more entrees. The place has a old diner type feel too it, so it's a bit cozy. You can actually see the chefs work their magic behind the counter right out front, which is always a plus. It's not a really big place, so parties of 6 or more be warned!

Great ambiance, great food, great service- what else could you want? I come here often for lunch and for Happy Hour. The Pho is hard to resist, but the lunch specials are a great deal, and sometimes they tempt me. The Papaya salad has a very spicy, flavorful sauce. The pork belly is the best I've ever had - perfect mix of melty-soft and chewy-meaty. The Tacos are wonderful little pastry cups filled with appetizer sized veggies & seafood. Everything is attractive, tastes great, and the service is exceptional.

Some people will eat burgers and fries their whole life, never try new things, or venture ouside their home state. Ethiopian food is probably not for them, and Zagol's demands that you live outside your comfort zone. Zagol's owner is from Ethiopia, and she operates her restaurant in traditional fashion: you eat with your hands (so wash them). The food is very delicious, and we had the Zilzil Tibs (steak strips) with Bozena Shiro (a thick beef/peas sauce) and Doro Wat (thick spicy chicken sauce with chicken leg and whole boiled egg). You eat with pieces of Injera (soft thin bread). I recommend having their spicy Ethiopian tea with dinner, along with fresh Baklava and Ethiopian coffee (they roast their own beans on-site!) for desert. I admit that Zagol is not a place you'll eat every night, but every few months this could be the place to energize a meeting with friends. If you LOVE good coffee and have four or more people interested, request their Ethiopian coffee ceremony, where the roast the beans and make the drink right in front of you. The restaurant is very clean and seldom crowded, the owner is almost always your host, and everyone seems to have a very happy attitude. Vegetarian's are welcome, and have a few options to themselves on the menu. Overall I had a great time, enjoyed the food, and found the owner to be extremely friendly. Hopefully Reno will reward her hard work and dedication with tradition with frequent visits, because if you don't patronize the businesses you like they won't be around when you want them. I rate Zagol with: food = 4.5 stars selection = 4.5 stars service = 4.5 stars atmosphere = 4.5 stars price = 4.0 stars I'm happy to give Zagol 5 stars because Yelp! lacks a closer rating! FOLLOW-UP EDIT: we have visited Zagol's a second time, and it was even better than the first! So far, so very good. Don't be afraid to give it a try, you'll really like it!
Mmmm love the food here! Highly recommend this place for lunch, you get a great deal! Order the saganaki (awesome flaming cheese dish!)

Walking around chinatown I stumbled upon Erawan. The bf and I ordered the Wonton Soup (chicken and shrimp) and the calamari to start. The soup was delicious, but not enough for two. I've had better calamari, they serve the large calamari rings that look a lot like onion rings, they just weird me out, but drown them in the dipping sauce and they are quite alright. For our entree we ordered shrimp pad thai and yellow curry with chicken. We were both pretty satisfied with the portion and the quality of the food. The only minor thing I was not a fan of was the rice, it was really mushy, not like normal sticky rice, just mushy, like water had been added to it. The service was great, we were the only guests, so maybe we just got lucky. Will have to test that out. Prices are reasonable, all that food and paid around $40, Pretty awesome! This has been the best Thai food I've had in Philadelphia, so ERAWAN, I will be BACK.

I stopped in with four friends, we had the Family Feast. I enjoy trying new things...but this experience was better than I imagined. I enjoyed the egg plant salad and the Chicken Bastille...... But the chicken with the Harisa Sauce, was truly my favorite. They have a full bar, good service, and great food... I would definitely return....

Amazing food. The lunch deal is also pretty incredible, and a fantastic meal for an equally fantastic price. They also will tailor the foods to your desired spice level on a scale of 1-7, which is great. You can ask them to take the Pad Thai (which is a 1) to whatever number on the scale you want. The Thai Basil with Chicken is great at a 5. It's great at all the other levels too, but 5 is my personal favorite. The staff have always been friendly and efficient, and the restaurant has always been clean in my experience. Absolutely my favorite place for takeout.
