On a whim we tried someplace new for dinner. I have now found my favorite Indian restaurant. The menu is extensive and the dishes we had were well seasoned and flavorful. The waitstaff were attentive and helpful. I had the saag special with chicken and it was delightful. The medium level of spicy was perfect for me but most non-Indians would prefer the mild spice. We look forward to coming back and exploring more items on the menu.

Absolutely amazing food. I tried both the Tandoori Chicken and the Chicken Tikki Masala and they were both extremely flavorful and delicious. I've been to many Indian places and I can sincerely say that this is likely the best that I've been to.

Amazing dining, highly recommend the oxtails, chicken patty appetizer, mango juice! Service and ambiance was amazing, glad we stumbled upon this gem! Check it out, you will not be disappointed, or hungry!

Ok, right up front the 1 star is only because I can't rate it any lower. Avoid this place. I have been to many, many beach bars all around Florida and frankly cannot think of any that are worse! The drinks we had were horrible, weak, small, tasteless and too expensive for what they serve. As we were about to eat the people next to us sent all their food back complaining it tasted horrible. This was very bad considering we were trying not to get angry at how crappy the two bartenders taking care of 6 people were. They left plastic cups full of water and old cigarettes on the bar well after people who we never saw had left, stood in front of us with their back to us, never asked how anything was or if we wanted a menu. Frankly these bartenders would do much better serving Kool AId to kindergarten children cause this job is not for them.

I'm a fan...and one that plans to return to this yummy place. Really good Thai food!! Has the reputation for being the best Thai place in SB. Very friendly service. Very Small and intimate with lots of character in their decor style. Because it's small you need to go during an off-time because there's really no place to wait for a table. I recommend calling for a reservation even though it looks like a place that doesn't take reservations.

Had the garlic and black pepper chicken dish and ordered it Thai Hot. No I must confess that you cannot make food hot enough for me, the more my nose runs the better. The dish was fantastic, with just the right amount of peppers mixed in. The spice was perfect, allowing me to taste the black pepper and garlic but feel that strong heat.

So, my first visit to Olio was interesting, the food tasted good but that is the only thing that did.... Service was slow, waitress was a soft talker and my party of 3 had no clue what was being said, plastic chairs that felt like it circumcision in progress. Again food tasted good but very small portions.... Won't be going there ever again
Good service but the food was nothing great. It looked like they used frozen vegetables in the dishes and the portions were very small. Good flavor to the food but nothing else spectacular.

What? Food this good from a truck? YES! Everything is excellent here. My personal favorites are the Thai short Rib Tacos with the Chicken Satay Taco. If you get the Chicken Katsu, please the fried egg on it. That extra flavor just pushes it over the edge. The Sweet Potato Chicken Curry is spiced just right, and the Cap'n Crunch Tilapia Burrito is a wonderful creation. The Mexican Veggie Burger is so substantial, you won't miss the meat. The Thai Tea and Coffee beverages are delicious and a great 'pick me up'. The food is quality, and is good enough to be served at a sit down restaurant. I am usually sad when my food is gone and my belly is full, because the experience is over. :-) Keep up the good work!

This place rocks! My sister and I were strolling through New Hope for the first time looking for a place to eat. We decided on Mojito and I'm so glad we did! The staff was exceptionally friendly and the food was outstanding. During happy hour (unsure of when it starts, but it goes until 7) most of the appetizers are $5 which is pretty unbeatable. Recommend the classic mojito and the maple jalepeno bacon slab. Will definitely be returning!

Been to Mumbai countless times... Its great food at a cheap price. Cant beat it!... In all the times I've eaten here I've only had one complaint where my garlic naan was overcooked and hard. Other than that I have not one complaint. The food in the buffet is always fresh, the place is super clean, and the guys who work there are really nice. They have the best basmati rice I've ever tasted and the chicken tikka masala and chicken vindaloo never disappoint

What a discovery! Absolutely LOVE this place; from its delicious (and authentic!) Thai dishes, to its classy-yet-cozy ambiance, to its fantastic waiting staff - Ploy Thai is an absolute gem. We were looking for a good Thai restaurant and while some were pretty yummy, nowhere really knocked our socks off...until we found this place. Hidden in a busy shopping plaza, it's almost easy to miss altogether, but the moment you walk in, you know you've entered somewhere special. The entire atmosphere is so well-done, so genuinely Thai (the owners brought back one-of-a-kind pieces from Thailand and designed the interior of the restaurant with tons of unique touches), that you can't help but be transported. Even the smallest touches make the biggest difference (the salt and pepper shakers on each table, even the restrooms are impeccably done!) As for the food, one word: spectacular. We've traveled a lot, and authentic Thai that really shines is hard to find in Tampa. But here, the dishes were amazing; pad thai, green curry beef, spicy noodles and the tom kha gai soup, all magnificent (with the right combination of spices and herbs). This place packs just the right amount of heat into any spicy dish (their Thai Spicy Beef Salad is to die for!) and upon our fifth visit, we still have yet to find another place that can compete; talk about consistency! They even have sushi, and it is some of the freshest I've had anywhere in Tampa. Try the Volcano roll, the Dancing Eel roll and the Spicy Conch roll for some serious yumminess. Their wakami (seaweed) salad is also so fresh, I couldn't remember the last time I had any that good. Meal after meal, each time we've come, we have never been disappointed :)
Great customer service! Roy was awesome! The broiled tilapia was amazing!

Food quality has gone down tremendously under new management. The service here was always bad but food prices have gone up yet the taste has plummeted. Gone are the days when Palace of Asia used to be full. Now it feels like you are in a haunted house; sooooo eerie that you have to whisper your conversations. The menu has remained the same since last 5 years. Plenty of better restaurants around the area!

This place is lacklustre, ashamed, had high hopes for it, especially when it was in the movie, In her shoes! Went with a friend avid Jamaican cuisine connoisseur, like I. Wow..were we disappointed or what? Took 35-40 minutes for the food to come out, mix up in ordering Are you kidding me, you had to go up to window order, no one one came out to the dingy , very small store front, patio area wasn't open, since it was winter time. Wow, I got jerk chicken, he got ox tail meal, It wasn't cooked long enough, the ox -tail was hard, not falling off bone, seasoning was just Ehh..ok..my Jerk chicken was dry..seasoning OK, Hell, I make better jerk chicken at home then they do and their prices are not reasonable, high for dingy , small place, but I guess the hype from being in movie, not too many Jamaican restaurant s around. Just so sad, very disappointed. After hearing about corkage fee, etc, Wow-where do they come up with this stuff. Ridiculous!!!??

Ate at the restaurant once and grabbed take out another time. Have to say I am disappointed in their execution of pad thai, pad see ew, and appetizers (the spring rolls & dumplings are too fried and greasy, not enough filling). The one good thing was the curry dish. Fantastic service and a cute, small dining room but the food isn't up to par.

I've been here a few times for the weekend buffet but it's quite a steal at $10.99. Loads of different entrees, sides, appetizers, and desserts to choose from. My favorite is the fresh garlic naan they bring to each table that makes the meal even more delicious.
Great Thai, maybe the best in SB. The ground chicken with basil is amazing!
Stay away. Not the best hookah place, and talk about overly priced. One hookah is gonna run you $28...that's ridiculous! The mood is very unwelcoming and the service is beyond horrible.

Note before you read: I ordered a standard sandwich, not Vietnamese. Pros: Bread was good, very good price, fast service Cons: There was just nothing outstanding about the sandwich, processed turkey on a white baguette. Both me and my colleague had pretty good stomach aches after eating this. I might come back after my stomach has settled for a Vietnamese sandwich.

after a talk thread about gyros, i decided to try soco gryos and deli. i got the stuffed chicken combo, it included a can of soda and a side. it was very good and filling. i think next time i will tget the regular chicken gyro. i don't care for peppers or artichokes. so it is not that it was not good but that it was not worth it for me to pick it off. the seaoned fries were hot and crisp. the other sides looked good too. i will keep them in mind next time i am looking for something different in soco.

Dinner there last night with friends. Very comfortable restaurant (most places in So. Philly pack you in like sardines). Good service, staff was very friendly. Appy's were delicious. Most entrees were very good to excellent. One was just OK. I would go back, but try something different.

I used to go here when I lived close to 38th street a couple years ago and then I moved away. Once I came back I found that they'd moved to a new location in what seems to be an old Bob Evans. Thankfully, the food seems to have survived the move without incident. The Banh Mi sandwiches are still great according to my wife who can never seem to resist ordering one if it is on the menu. I like the Pho with meatballs, but my true love here is the Bun Bo Hue. They have my favourite that I've found in the city thus far. Fantastic spicy rich broth, chewy chunks of fat and what I believe to be tendon. Rich tasty beef. I love it all. The cha gio here are delicious, enough so that I usually order two orders. The service can be a little slow in the off hours, but I don't really mind that.
First time ordering food from here. Food was great! Easy online ordering and payment. I recommend this to anyone in the area to check out!

This is literally my favorite food truck to eat at on campus. 100% my go to for lunch, and even sometimes an early dinner. Everyone inside the truck is always SO nice to all of their customers. Rob and Gabe, the brothers who usually work the window have great customer service, and Nico and Peter are the chefs working behind the scenes prepping and making most of the food. If you're ever in the area, I highly suggest eating at this food truck.
On time delivery, food in general was delish, friendly service; truly no negatives other than I've had more flavorful sushi from my hometown, and that's the only reason it got a 4 star rating.

I go to Bryn Mawr College and I frequently order take away from Ekta. They used to have the most horrible delivery man, but they fired him and his replacement is very friendly. The butter chicken is my go to, and it's quite flavorful and creamy. You can really taste the butter and the other spices they use. The vegetable samosas are nothing to brag about, they're merely okay. There's no pop of flavor and the pastry is occasionally soggy, but generally they're fine. The chicken korma is also delicious. The sauce is a good mixture of being nice and thick and flavorful. I am partial to the peshwari naan, which is much better than their regular naan which is dry, flavorless, and not worth the calories. The peshwari naan, however, is softer in texture, and sweet, but not too sweet. Like most restaurants on the Main Line, it's BYOB, but luckily there is a liquor store across the street. The butter chicken tastes even better with a Kingfisher. Service in the restaurant is mediocre. It's family run, so the servers aren't trained and or particularly friendly. I'd recommend take away or delivery rather than eating in the restaurant. It's reasonably priced as well. Take away takes usually 45 minutes, but I've had cases where it's arrived in 30 minutes. Overall, this Indian restaurant is pretty good. The town where I'm from has one of the top-rated Indian restaurants on the East Coast, so I'm used to a very high level of quality Indian food, but this restaurant on Lancaster Ave delivers (no pun intended).
Had my Birthday party here in February definitely would come back here the drinks are good and the atmosphere was awesome,pricey but good

Yum...Yum...Yum...Ok, so it's not quite as good as Oak of Mamre was (I could cry since that place is gone...my mouth is watering just thinking about it), but Abyssinia is a decent substitute. The service has been excellent every time I've been too. Oh, and the homemade ethiopian honey wine...well, pace yourself. I have loved everything I have ordered from meat to chick peas to whatever other slop is placed on the injera. A friend of mine even ordered the raw beef dish (the waitress questioned us :)) and that was very good too...a little chewier than I would have preferred for raw beef, but grow a pair and try it out. I love that there is no silverware (thank you for being authentic), so if you struggle with people's hands touching everything then you probably wouldn't care for ethiopian in general. This place does have hand sanitizer on every table though:) I always feel like ethiopian is a great place for kids because they can use their hands. There are tons of "puree'd" veggies to pick up with the injera. And actually, I do think I've seen kids in there every time I have eaten there. They seem to really enjoy it. I have never sat at the more traditional communal seats that they have. A friend of mine did recently and she said they are super uncomfortable unless you are actually eating. So, if you have a bad back, you might want to stick with the regular tables :)

Food and table service was very good. Reception almost had us walking out. We had a reservation for four and were offered a table in the bar. When we said we did not want to sit in the bar we were subjected to a tutorial about reservations and busy restaurants. After several minutes of waiting and a battle of logic, we got a perfect table. Wonderful experience, but I'm not sure it was worth the hassle.

I used a Scoutmob deal yesterday at Salsa, and was completely blown away by how wonderful the food was. I ordered the Pastelon de Amarillos, which is sweet plantains with ground beef "lasagna" (no noodles), with a side of Mofongo de Yuca. I almost made myself sick trying to finish it, because it was so flavorful and different. The plantains made it just a little sweet, and combined with the delicious ground beef, I just couldn't stop myself from eating until I could pop! My friend ordered the Pechuga de Pollo Rellena de Amarillos, which is chicken breast stuffed with sweet plantains. I tried it, and couldn't believe how much flavor they packed into that chicken. We had the Limocillo drinks, which were pretty good, it's rum with lemon juice. They have a happy hour with food specials and some of the drinks are 2 for 1. It's in a semi-hidden spot, just past Cummins Station almost to Mercy Lounge. I hope the location doesn't prevent it from taking off, because there is plenty of free parking and it's so close to downtown, if people know about it, I'm sure it will be quite popular. I would definitely recommend Salsa!
This place is great! Swing by for dinner all the time. Summer rolls, bamboo pho, and bamboo special always delicious.

First Impressions: Stopped by here on our way home to Milwaukee from Cincinatti. It's conveniently located off the highway so a good pitstop for those on a road trip for sure! It looks like they took over a building that was once a diner or something of that sort as most pho places are pretty small. This place was definitely very spacious and open. Service: Service was quick and flawless. Food: We got the pho special (you know, the one with everything basically!) and the vermicelli dish with egg rolls and pork. Both were alright. The beef in the pho was a little tough.

My first time here was delish! We had pho all around (chicken) and I was not let down! The fresh pho additives were so scrumptious, and a small portion left me just enough to have a bowl full for work the next day. To start: we did the sampler app, spring rolls...TO DIE FOR. LOVE. But everything else was super tasty as well. For my first Vietnamese place, I was definitely not dismayed!

Well what can I say. I have a love/hate relationship with the place but for the most part, I love the pad woon sen and there are new dishes on the specials board. Check it out. Although the softshell crab is a bit overpriced because the portion is just not justifying. If you work in the CBD nearby, get there before the line starts forming, but make sure you understand that if you come in during the height of lunch hour and you have to sit at a tiny table, apologies because that's alll they have left, it's a popular spot and if you have to wait they usually comp you with the veggie crispy spring rolls or some shrimp and pork dumplings. YUMSSSSS Everything is homemade and the staff is harried during lunch but otherwise if you are not happy----u know what you need to do. They usually accomadate you if you have special request for veggie dishes too! Please understand that they have to tone down the spice(ALOT) because most of the customers who do frequent the joint cannot take real Thai style. However, if you think you can take it--ask the person waiting on you to make the dish THAI SPICY. Full bar and accepts cash, credit--no checks yo.

We arrived there for dinner around 8:30 PM. It was a cold night so we decided to get soup. They took our order and as we sat down, we heard the table next to us complain that one of them asked for a large order, but got the same bowl size as his companion. They explained that they put more noodles in his bowl. Not good start... We were sitting on a table that faced the hallway going to CVS, and unfortunately it smelled strongly Lysol cleaner, perhaps because the bathroom door was close by (not their fault though). We got our soup, I got the spicy one, and my companion got the pho. Both were salty, and the broth tasted like made from a powder, with typical aftertaste that you get after eating ramen package. The portion also is half what you get in the Bay area. Very disappointing, we will not come back.

One of the best restaurants I have ever been to. The food is to die for & the owner is nice too! He really knows how to take care of the customers. The Chicken Sahara is my favorite. I really wish the restaurant would open up again :(

Stopped in for lunch while I was at a conference downtown, and I'm glad I did! As a practice, I avoid buffets and was planning to order off the menu in lieu of the lunch buffet. But I took a look at the food and decided the buffet was clean, well-stocked and piping hot (not one of those gross someone-stuck-their-finger-in-the-pudding places). The chicken tikka masala wasn't as flavorful as others I've had, but overall the food is good quality and tasty. Plus a big, sit-down meal for $8? I'll take it.

Great Indian take-out! I typically order from their a la carte menu rather than the buffet and have zero complaints so far on all the different dishes I've tried. Standouts are the saag paneer, samosas, chicken vindaloo and chicken tikka masala. The food always tastes fresh, has lots of flavor and just enough spiciness. Wish I had discovered this place sooner.

They close at 3 PM, to me that means if I walk in there any time before 3 PM you serve me. Me and two friends got their at 2:30 today, they served us but then proceeded to rush us out so they can close the place down and leave. If you want to close it down at 3 PM then put closing time as 2 PM so that customers that walk in closer to that time can actually eat. Secondly, can I get some ice with my water? This is the only place I have ever been to that treat ice like it's a precious metal. Just overall poor customer service!! Now on to the food, their dosas and chicken 65 are very good. The rest of the stuff is mediocre at best.

When I first saw the signs for Mumbai Bistro before it opened, I admit that I was slightly skeptical. One day while passing by I decided to stop in for a veggie samosa and recognized one of the staff from New Delhi in University City. I was happy to learn that in fact, Mumbai Bistro was affiliated with New Delhi. Hearing this, I decided I had to return for dinner. Since that brief visit, I have been back numerous times - so very happy to have another quick, inexpensive dinner option in my neighborhood & another good Indian option at that! The menu lists the schedule of what is going to be served in the buffet each night, so I know what to expect and the food has been fresh and delicious every time we have stopped in. The dishes rotate every day- a few meat dishes and mostly veggie dishes here. If you have been to New Delhi then you know what to expect in terms of the food. As the dishes in the buffet aren't super spicy, they will also throw in extra hot sauce if you ask. The only problem we had with the food here is the Nan- it reminded us of the store bought kind you can get at whole foods and it usually ends up soggy by the time we arrive at home. Because good Nan is such an essential element of Indian food, I have to deduct a start for that. However, if the Nan improved, I would definitely rate Mumbai Bistro 4 stars. Also of note- the staff here is always very friendly and helpful, and the restaurant is always clean. The majority of customers here opt for takeout, however, there are a few tables in the restaurant so there is the option of eating in. Overall, a welcome addition to the neighborhood!
Phenomenal food and service! Highly recommend. I'm visiting for work, I wish this restaurant was in my backyard.
Very affordable & delicious buffet. Great for those who are not very familiar with Indian food and want to sample Indian cuisine.

I fell in love with this cafe immediately :D Their interior is cute and very clean environment! Cleanliness is very important especially it is a rare thing to see in Chinese or Vietnamese owned places. Their drinks are just great....boba is so soft and chewy. They have variety of drink flavors and toppings. My favorite is peach boba. It is a thicker type of drink...almost like fruit smoothie. I also had shredded pork sandwich, meatball sandwich and summer roll. Yummm. I want to try their roast pork sandwich and Pat Thai next time. They have cute little area where they sell Asian snacks, candies, tea etc. For dessert, try their Romeo and Juliet shaved ice! Don't bother trying their cookies and macarons. P.S. Their service is very friendly...however if you don't step in the restaurant at a right time...you might be waiting for your food for a little while since the place can get crowded in a minute. So if you don't know what to order, try hurrying up your decision making process. Next thing you know there are millions of people are in line ordering before you.

Love this place for pho, fresh and delicious. Service is friendly. I usually take my orders to go and I like that bowl they provide, the portions for meat and noodles are more than enough. There is outside seating a plus for since I bring my pup everywhere.

What can I say? The food here is excellent and service is likewise. I had Amazing Tofu, my favorite Thai dish. They make the best I've ever had. I've been away from the area for a while and the food was even better than I remembered. Nice relaxing atmosphere. Great food.

My favorite noodle house. Sky's homemade egg noodle soup is a must to try. My partner loves his Combination Pork platter. The Indonesian style Chow kwe tiaw is delicious. The Medan Lontong sayur was very coconuty delicious .. Heck, all their foods are insanely delicious. Brought our friend from backwoods West Virginia and they kept on wanting me to bring them back here again ...:)) Appetizer, try Gado gado (house salad) & Tempe Goreng Writing this makes me hungry *sigh* enjoy it guys ! This is well deserved your trip.

My wife and I just had dinner here on a sunday night. We have eaten at other Ethiopian resturants in the area. This one has a limited menu, but the food was very good. The service was also extremely attentive. Compared to other Ethiopian restuarants in the area I would say this one gives bigger portions (particularly of meat) for the money. We were stuffed for a total of $19 for the 2 of us. As they do not serve dessert and we wanted a little something to cleanse the palate after dinner, we went to a nearby cafe for dessert and tea and spent almost as much there as we had on our entire dinner at Queen of Sheba. This is also a really interesting and diverse neighborhood.

Such a fun, yet relaxing atmosphere. I ate outside, could watch the water. There's a bar with an area for dancing. The good was also really good as was the service. You have to get there at the right time. We got a table right away, but when we were leaving the dinner line fire takes was really long.
Delicious authentic Jamaican cuisine. Love the whole fried fish. Great sides. Byob with a wine shop downstairs.
Olio is consistently on point each time we visit. Great service, drinks, food, and daily specials. I highly recommend this place.

A last minute change of dinner plans lead me to Abyssinia, and am I glad I went. Located in a strip mall along 38th st, it is a very unassuming place. If I didn't know it was there, I would have probably missed it. Wasn't too packed at 7pm on a Wed. evening, so I had no problem getting seated and having my order taken right away. Very typical menu, meat and veg options with the always pleasing combination platters...my personal choice. I opted for the "Taste of Abyssinia" veg combo...I noticed that it did not include shirro, which I must always have when dining on Ethiopian...so I asked the owner (who took my order) if I could get shirro added on, and he did so with no extra charge. I also ordered a glass of tej wine, a brand of which I had never had before...and would honestly not like again. It wasn't bad or anything, just not the usual tej wine I am use to...it tasted like brandy...of which I am not a fan. The food was great, good spice to the shirro, and good use of the berberre. The injera was fresh, not soggy and not dry...just right, and you could tell they make it in house. Not sure if this is the only Ethiopian game in town, but if your looking for authentic fare, this is it.

Went here due to the high reviews and this place did not disappoint. Got the short rib tacos and a taro bubble tea. The tea was a bit too sweet for my taste but you can always ask them to hold back on the sugar. The tacos were phenomenal! Wish I had some more right now. Make sure you ask for the spicy mayo on top.

One of the best banh mi that I've ever had. I like it ten times better than the Hong Kong Market's banh mi. It's not super heavy or greasy, the bread is great, and it's just perfectly delicious and filling. And they're HUGE. I feel lucky to have this place super close to home.

I have been to this restaurant 3 times and I am not overly impressed .When they first opened I was told to come back later because they were going to go on lunch break in 20 minutes and this was right after they first opened.there doors . How Weird to turn away guests. One would think a new restaurant would be anxious to get customers. This one not so much. The food is average in taste on all visits. We found portions to be small and my main complaint is with the overwhelming smell of mildew that hits me in the face as soon as I walk in. The decor is pretty, exotic and the place seems to be clean. The service has been spotty. The parking lot was a pain to get into from the direction we came from. I would say if you are not bothered by mildew try a lunch special to get a feel of the place before you spring for dinner.

The space is very nice and I enjoy the semi private booths. Short but good draft list, I especially enjoy the Murphy's Irish Stout. The wine list left a lot to be desired, short but adequate size glass list but the choices were mostly big name brands. We tried a white and a red, the red seemed to have been opened a bit too long, or just not good. Lamb sliders - good and much better with the sauce, my only complaint is that the bun was a bit too big for the filling and therefore a little difficult to eat. Carpaccio - fairly good for American carpaccio and loaded with capers and parmesan so it felt a bit more substantial. Lobster ravioli was a little fishy and the edges of the ravioli were a little thick and therefore undercooked. Overall flavor was quite nice though. Veal, unfortunately I can't remember if we got the cutlet or the marsala - it was a thin cutlet with what seemed to be a red pepper mushroom sauce. This was the least favorite of the night, the sauce tasted a bit like sweet and sour sauce. I will definitely return to try more dishes or just to have a nice Murphy's draft.

Not bad. Ordered kabuli but got rice with half a handful of raisins and carrots dropped on top. Lamb was good but not enough. The pregnant hostess was super nice but the waitress was a bit curt and rude. Could've been a good experience but wasn't. Probably won't be going back. Philly just doesn't seem the place for good afghan food. Northern VA is still the best area for afghan cuisine.

My girlfriend and I enjoy Thai food, so we were anxious to try the newest Thai restaurant Uptown. They've only been open a month or less, and some of that showed. The waiter seemed inexperienced, but the Singha owner was helping him out and giving us great service the whole time. So it wasn't a big deal. The menu was your typical set of Thai fare. We ordered a few standards -- the pad kee mow and the combination fried rice -- and they got the food out to us within eight minutes. We weren't blown away, however, with the food's flavor. It wasn't awful. The meat was bland. The vegetables weren't great. it wasn't extremely spicy. Overall, it was just very average, and I think there are much better Thai options in the area, such as Sukho Thai and Bangkok Thai. It wasn't an extremely great value either The service seemed very nice, and I am definitely rooting for them to succeed. I would even consider going back. I just think there are much better places around that give you more bang for your buck.

I ate here a couple years ago and the food was quite good and the service standard. Last year we tried to go here with a friend and her children. There was no one in the restaurant and when we arrived the lady said they were fully booked and that they could not fit us in. She was quite abrupt and not very friendly. We were surprised since it was empty aside from maybe one or two customers. So we called when we got to our car to see if we could come in then and the lady on the phone said it was no problem because they weren't busy. Yet we had just been turned away a couple minutes ago. So obviously they are not kid friendly at this restaurant. I would not return here simply for this reason. The food may be ok but the service and staff are not.

Tried this restaurant for the first time and it was delicious. I loved everything I ate. The food was fresh and flavorful, and the selection on the buffet was perfect. There was an equal sampling of meat and vegetarian dishes and I was able to fill my plate with fragrant and savory vegetable creations. The service was very good and the staff friendly and accommodating. The pricing was incredibly reasonable, too. I am looking forward to going again very soon!
We get delivery from here all the time & it is incredible. They have some of the best Indian food in the city, especially the chicken curry. They are affordable & have exceptional service.
Everything I have been getting here lately has been excellent. I tried the grilled pork Banh Mi hoagie and the beef Pho. Both very good

Ok..I ate my food before I could take a picture of it. I had to laugh because the thought really did escape me. No exaggeration. I'm new at this. Forgive me. Masala Kitchen is hands down one of my all time favorite places for authentic, Indian street/vendor food and snacks. Some quality can't-put-the-fork-or-food-down-between-bites type of food. For those who like to skim, the food is superb, staff is friendly and the place is only open on the weekend. I frequent just about every weekend and at $3 - $8 per food item (with most being $5) you're getting a clichéd big bang for your buck (I'd pay more for sure). Yes, the place sits in the New Castle Farmers market. That said, while many frequent the market for their staple stores - the BBQ ribs, fresh produce, Amish meat and food stations, seafood or that grill where I see everyone walk away eating monster sausage with giant fried onions hanging out the side of the bun (I digress), I lean towards the almost hidden, all vegetarian Indian food take out/dine in restaurant. You could miss this place is you walked fast enough, which is almost impossible to do at the farmers market. The decor is mixed with mainly heavy square wooden tables and what I would consider traditional hand crafted India-inspired, wooden backed chairs. There's a subtle splash of modern in the lit food wall display and you're also almost guaranteed a Bollywood style movie to keep you entertained while you wait...and wait you will, so hang tight and be patient while your masterpiece is crafted in the back. I prefer it this way - made just for me. When I'm in a hurry I call the order in while in route and it's hot and ready when I arrive (suggested). The vada pav is a must try here. A perfect ball of potato spicy goodness in a warm, soft, fluffy bun. On this visit, I had the deconstructed aloo tikki. Deconstructed? YESS!! Who does that to Indian food in Delaware?! I also ordered a mango lassi, and a few pretzel shaped jalebi (Indian funnel cake). And a pair of samosa. And walked away with only handing a lonely $13 for huge bag of food. Spices in the deconstructed aloo tikki were on point, showcasing the hot and sweet chutney mixed throughout. The jalebi was so sweet and the mango lassi, while I hear is an acquired taste for some, was just as good, if not better than a mango smoothie. I bit off the top of one of my samosa but that is a guaranteed treat for me to enjoy later in the evening. If you're in the area and in the mood for a true taste of Indian "nummy nummy street food" and an insane tastegasam, stop by and try a few items. Almost forgot to mention they are opening a new location in Newark, DE. Grand opening is April 11th. You're welcome in advance...

Oh man...I keep seeing places on here that I have never reviewed yet come to all the time. Forgive me Amber Indian!!! On a side note, I can only rate this place for the Lunch Buffet as I have never come here for dinner. The buffet is outstanding! So many choices and variety from vegetarian options to some with meat. 3 different kinds of rice and all the naan you can possibly stomach without exploding....and explode you will...because you will easily over-indulge here on the choices and deliciousness of them all. Is this the BEST Indian food I've had? no....but it sure is the best Indian Buffet I've had. if half stars were possible, I'd give this place a 4.5 honestly. Amazing, but not perfect
Favorite, Favorite spot for Real Jamaican food. It's always fresh, the owners treat you like family. I'm a regular at least once a week sometimes twice. I have my coworkers hooked! ~Emilia

Absolutely AMAZING eastern European cousine. THIS place is the real deal. When you think of Nashville, you think country music, Hot fried chicken, barbeque, various middle eastern/Mediterranean foods. But authentic Bosnian cousine? This I gotta see for myself. First on that list was Café Bosna, surpassed all expectations (already reviewed). Then I hear of Euro Grill and I'm like hummm....Antioch? Really? Let's go! I drove past this place three times when I was looking for it. Finally got my bearings and pulled in. Upon entering you feel that rustic European ambience; it's a mixture of southern France/Tuscan dive and not quite eastern. But once you order than fresh-baked spinach bürek and chase it with a Chevapi, you know this place means business. The bürek is a nice healthy portion, I'd recommend sharing one as an appetizer. Keep in mind it's got strong feta cheese in there so it's rich! Now, the Chevapi. What a frigging sandwich! The lapenja bread is baked fresh everyday, buttered, and stuffed with these mini Bosnian sausages and fresh diced onions. Simple, fragrant, delicious, filling. Those little sausages are so packed with flavor they literally kick you square in the jaw upon first bite. It's like nothing you have ever tasted before. Order it. Seriously. The owner is super awesome, very friendly and won't mind chatting with you about the mother-land and hearing about his past is fascinating. So my fellow Nashvillians, head on over to Euro Grill, share a bürek, toss back a lager and chow down on a chevap. It is a meal worth driving out to Antioch for on a daily.

Came for the Bahn MI and was not disappointed! I got the #55 Grilled Pork. The Bread is FRESH BAKED there at the restaurant!!!! The pork was flavorful and tender. My only complaint is that the cilantro was not chopped at all. A small complaint in an overall excellent sandwich! I will be back for the Noodle Soups!!!
Their vegetarian hoagies have been a staple of my diet for several years now. I've never had a better one from any other place. Everyone who I have introduced to the cafe is hooked.

The Good: - Huge Portions at Dinner - Food Taste Good - Friendly Waitress - The Spring Rolls are Tasty The Bad: - Slow Service - Drinks Empty A Lot - Very Bright Light From Go Cart Track Shines in Dining Room The Ugly: - I'd Avoid if Vegan (I'm not sure what I got was 100% animal free - she had a hard time understanding what vegan is) - Go Cart Track Next Door is Noisy To sum it up. I won't go back because they don't really know what vegan means.

Went there twice for lunch buffet. Barely 5 dishes looks to be the usual offering. The lamb is cooked very weird. Mostly undercooked and tastes unhealthy. Chicken is standard fare. The vegetarian dishes (sabji's) are ok. Less variety, only 1 sweet dish. The ONLY saving grace is nowdays, the naan comes hot to your table. But still, only 5 mediocre dishes for a total of $9.50 (after taxes) is NOT WORTH IT! Specially when you get more bang for the buck at other Indian restaurants around the area. Not coming back till I hear changes in dish quality and quantity.

My food took too long. I think I waited about 45 minutes to an hour. I ordered 3 different orders. 2 general tso chicken and a sesame chicken. Let's just say it wasn't appetizing. It doesn't taste like typical chinese food. There was no air condition inside. The guy who I think owns it or runs it was nice, and offered a cold drink free of charge.

Went to this restaurant with my boyfriend after a job interview because it was at a convenient location for us. We love Indian so it was perfect. The prices were great and you get a lot of food with your order. We both got the chicken tikka masala and garlic naan and it was better than we expected. The chicken was very good and the sauce was thick and spicy. On the way out we picked up a couple cakes from the bakery which were fantastic. Would defiantly recommend this place to lovers of Indian and anyone with a sweet tooth.

This is the type of place I love to see doing so well. The owner truly cares for the customers and his restaurant. The food was tasty. They have an extensive menu including breakfast! It's a BYOB which is also a plus. This is a neighborhood gem and highly recommend to anyone.

Im only giving 3 stars because I didn't have nothing but 2 things on the menu. Ive had the Jerk Chicken with Ricw and Beans. I LOOOOOVE me some Jerk Chicken with rice and beans :). It was good. The gravy was verrrrry Spicy. I Love spicy but not to the point where I have to stop eating it :/ The Fish is just DELICIOUS. LOVE LOVE IT!!!

If I had to choose one perfect food in this world it would be the grilled octopus at the original location on 3rd St. The texture of the octopus, the smokiness from the grill, the good olive oil, red wine vinagar, and a bit of parsley... Go there, bring cash and wine, eat lots of octopus, some salad and a whole grilled fish.
Got the Qabli pulaw. It is pretty good!!

I've gotten delivery from Nirvana several times in the past few months and each time, the food has been consistently delicious and the delivery service has been very fast. You do have to create a separate account with the delivery service (I forget the name) which was a little annoying the first time, but certainly worth it and I'm still giving this review 5 stars because the food is that good.

The food is wonderful here! My husband had the basil chicken and I had the orange chicken. I loved the basil chicken. It has lots of veggies and great flavor! They also give huge portions. I would definitely recommend!

So excited to have this restaurant in the neighborhood. I did both takeout and have eaten-in, and the food has been consistently fresh + tasty. Service has also been good. I recommend it and can't wait to try more on the menu.

Amazing food! The Korean Fried Chicken is an absolute must have! The bento boxes are huge with large servings of a great variety of food! Full bar.... Ohhh....and the beer selection of 90 different beers plus a rotating 6 tap draft is quite impressive. A family favorite!!!!

I used to really like this place. Nothing irks me more than a restaurant who skimps on quality for carryout orders. I guess they assume once you pay for it and leave with it they don't need to worry about it. I spent $30 on my carryout order only to find myself hungry afterward due to the fact that it was just plain awful. The only thing in my order that was worth eating was the cheese sampler, hard to mess up putting cheese in a go box. I ordered the vegetable cakes and the spinach salad. The "cakes" were actually a pile of crumbles. I could have even overlooked that had there actually been any flavor to them. The spinach salad was exactly that, all spinach with barely a hint of the blue cheese and figs. The salad dressing had a very odd flavor to it. After a couple of bites of each of these dishes, I ended up throwing it all in the garbage. Such a shame, this place used to be very good and I would often recommend it. I feel like I may as well have just thrown $30 straight in the trash and saved myself the trouble of going to get it.

We went here for dinner on a quiet night (Sunday) and service was great, as was the food: chicken tikka and bhindi masala. We asked for mild, and it arrived as ordered, very fresh. I'd definitely go back.
Loved it! Food was great, authentic. Everything was perfect. Super friendly accommodating staff. Can't wait to go back!

Some of the dishes that were recommended were the General Tso chicken, the salt and pepper chicken, and the Beef Pho. I have to say that the General Tso was the best and definitely a must-order. The sauce was frankly one of the best sauces I've ever tasted, and the chicken was covered in a perfect crispy shell that was absolutely delightful. Some other things that I want to comment about is the friendly and family environment of the restaurant. Overall, it was a delicious and relaxing environment.

Had dinner here last night with a friend. It's a small, quaint place. It wasn't too crowded last night around 7. My friend got the chicken satay skewers and I got the ginger dumplings. The dumplings were delicious and crunchy. The sauce for the satay skewers was also very tasty. For our entrees we both go Chicken Pad Thai. It was ok. The portion was a little on the smaller side and it didn't have as much peanut flavor as I prefer. My friend had been there before and got the Duck dish and said it was amazing. The service was good and prompt. I would try Jasmine Rice again and try a different entree.

Disappointed. I just moved to this area and the Zoe's by my old house in NJ was sooooo good. I had high hopes for this one but was disappointed. I ordered a tossed Greek salad with extra grilled onions and a cup of chicken orzo soup to go. I got home and the salad did not have the extra grilled onions, and all the other ingredients in the salad were skimpy. They didn't shake the Greek dressing before filling the togo dressing cups, so mine was straight oil. The worst part was my soup (which mind you is usually my favorite). There was not ONE piece of orzo in it. It was an entire container of shredded chicken and a small amount of broth. You could hardly see the broth because there was so much chicken. It was definitely the bottom of the soup pot. I wish they would have told me they were running out of soup and I wouldn't have ordered it. Biggest disappointment as a nurse that just wanted a quick, nice meal after a 13 hour shifthave been a frequent customer of a few Zoës Kitchens over the past few years and I will definitely not be returning. I'm
a great Kabsa and Mandi , love it , nice service . the place can use some renovation

The name says it all. This place is for Dosa, which is a south Indian crepe. If you are looking for meat over rice, look for something else. Best dosa in the whole Philly area. I had a onion rava dosa, Pesarattu and Veggie hakka noodles. And my friend had a Mysore Masala dosa and Samosas. The chutneys were good and Sambhar was average. I agree that the service can be improved. They are a bit under staffed. Other wise, good food. I recommend to dine in for hot dosas. Because, if you get a take out dosa, they become soggy.

I'm no Vietnamese food expert, but I love it. Tried this place for the first time the other day - ordered a combo pork Banh mi and Thai tea. Bread was fresh light and flakey, similar to what I have had in Santa Ana. Good size, tangy with the right amount of heat; maybe a tad heavy/chunky on the carrots and light on the coriander for my taste. To-go service was quick and I didn't find $6 to be bad at all for "imported" ingredients in a sandwich that is generally hard to find elsewhere around here. I'll update after I try the Pho and some of their other items, but so far, so good!

After hearing all the rave about Philly food trucks, I was heavily disappointed until I found this truck. Short rib tacos were not as good as advertised but the tilapia burrito and chicken Katsu were even better than hyped up to be! Yum, yum.

It's really great that MJ has a non-chain, decent version of Indian food. We have been twice, and both times, the food has been hot, fresh and decent in quality and preparation. From experiences at other Indian restaurants, it seems that they could offer a few more "standards," then they do. The menu is a bit limited here. Also, yes, Indian food is supposed to be spiced and fragrant, but this is quite heavy on the spices (not the hot spices, just the heartburn heavy spices.) We would go a bit more often, if there were a few more choices, and a bit less spice.

Eating at Olio was a complete pleasure. It's a sweet little place with an open air feeling. I had the smoked trout sandwich which was topped with crunchy cucumber slices and pickled onions. Absolutely delicious. Also had the hummus with the shredded lamb and their warm, freshly made, pita bread. We ordered the roasted cauliflower as well, which was also totally tasty! We ate every crumb on our plates and later in the day told at least 5 other people how incredible the food is here. Besides great food, we had the nicest waiter ever. I do hope I get to eat here again while I'm visiting St. Louis.

I'm not sure how this place has such great reviews. Maybe the night I ate there they were just having an off-day? I was with a party of four for dinner. All four meals came out at different times. The naan we ordered was cold. The meal I got was completely flavorless. The wait staff took ages to get our order and never bothered to ask how we were enjoying our food. The restaurant really wasn't that busy either, so it wasn't a case of them being overwhelmed on a Friday night.

This is easily the best Korean restaurant in St. Louis. That's not just my personal opinion. I asked Koreans: Me: I heard Hangook Kwan has really good Korean food! Korean friend: ehhhhh.... Me: Good for for St. Louis? KF: Yes, yes! Best in St. Louis! There you go. They do dolsot bibimbap, which is great. It's what I expect from most Asian food in St. Louis. It's not that they don't try, it's just that they start with ingredients that can't compare with elsewhere. Pricey for Korean food on the whole, not pricey considering how much decent food costs in St. Louis. Definitely try for some of the most authentic-tasting Korean food in the midwest!

Great beach restaurant......we had a pound of shrimp which were very good.... But the dish that took it over the top for us was the Creole Shrimp N' Grits or as I like to call it the Southern Budda Bowl! You know it's gotta be a great place when you see so many locals hanging out there!

Wow! Really amazing food. Something special for the city. Creative approach to interesting cuts of meat. Asian flavors, touching on Vietnam and Thailand. Smoked mushroom salad, fried pig tails (like pork belly), coal charred sweet potato...damn! Can't wait to come back, and hope the city doesn't sleep on this joint. One of my new favorite places! Can't wait to hit the lunch.

I honestly have tried their Pho before, so this will be a two-item review. Part one: The Pho - The Pho was decent, it wasn't what you would expect. The meat seemed a little rubbery, they put way too much MSG in the soup so much so that I literally had to chug ice water. The customer service was stellar, seeing as college students work here. In all, I was sort of disappointed at the quality of the meal. Part two: The Bun Bo Hue - The Bun Bo Hue DEFINITELY does not look like your standard one. For one thing, they use Thin vermicelli, instead of the big, thick Vermicelli. Second, the meat looked like it came from a Pho bowl, lighter than what you would expect. Thirdly, the greens looked a little old, especially the lemon slice I was provided with. Fourth, the slices of peppered... I don't know what they are... they are like pieces of rubber. I do have to give them chops for the soup. The soup is very authentic, typical to what you get in Little Saigon. Overall: I'm not going to recommend this place, but I'm not going to encourage people to stay away from this place. For some things, it does better, but for these types of main cuisine. They could improve. Sure, the 10% off with cash is nice, but I would not mind a modest price increase to be served what I expect, with better ingredients. I'm part Vietnamese, so I grew up eating this, so it's not quite up to par as I hoped it to be.

Went to the lunch buffet. Food was very good. I sampled some of everything and nothing was too spicy. Welcoming atmosphere. Half the restaurant was being painting and there were not many tables in the section that was open so the hostess made small talk with us until a table was available, everyone was very nice. I went on the weekend and it was still only 10.99 a person which included soup, salad, large selection of dinner food, and sweet cream with rice for dessert. Great bank for your buck! Will defiantly return.
I really enjoyed the Banh Mi sandwich, it was delicious! The price point was also good especially for the quality.

Disappointed! The food had no spice and no flavor. My whole meal was one big plate of rice with a few pieces of chicken. If you are in the mood to eat 2 pounds of white rice, this is the place for you!! Cute restaurant but the food was dull and boring and tons of white rice:(
Dosas are good, but place is stinky and unkept. Their ventilation is worse. Not a bad place for price but they can definitely improve.
Good food! Pad Thai plate was really good. The Yellow Curry was a little watery for me. The waitress was very nice too.

This is more than the usual meatsicle gyro meat that you get at most places. The bread is thicker, so it is definitely a sandwich. I always come here when I want a sandwich, but I want something different. Their green hot sauce is really good, and I also enjoy their spicy tzatziki sauce. On a lighter note, the ice dispenser has a picture of the rapper Ice Cube on it. It makes me smile each time I see it.

I am, as of this writing, the reigning Duchess of Tryst Gastro Lounge, a bar/restaurant/lounge in downtown St. Petersburg. I went four nights in a row while in town for a conference, with a group of drunk crime writers who had to stay out after the hotel bar closed at midnight. I'm still not entirely clear on what time Tryst closes. We definitely stayed past closing time, though, until around 3:00 or 3:30 every night. We sat on the sidewalk patio, where there was always an open table with wicker outdoor furniture, and around 1:30 or 2 or whenever, someone would come out to announce last call and then politely bring in the cushions and swap out our glassware for disposable cups. The staff was patient with us and prepared our many massive drink orders in a timely and competent manner (there was no table service late at night, but it was easy to get our drinks at the bar). The space was nice, though the interior was kind of weird and flashy. I'm guessing Tryst is about as close you might get to a club in St. Pete, but it really wasn't that bad, especially on the patio. The only night it was sort of crowded was Saturday, and even then, it cleared out by like 1:30. The patio furniture was super comfortable, and after our first night, it got replaced with even nicer furniture. I hope it's not because we somehow ruined the first set. We're not that nasty, I don't think. Drinks were solid enough, an above basic bar selection with some local/regional draft beers and a broad choice of liquors. I had a number of 3 Daughters beers on tap and like, a mojito, whiskey gingers, some bourbon on the rocks. I mixed my alcohol a bit my first night and got dreadfully sick. Still came back every night for the rest of my stay. Tryst is not a perfect bar, and it probably isn't even a bar I'd visit in my hometown. But as a late night bar in St. Petersburg, it was an absolute boon. My trip wouldn't have been the same without it.

I was really excited about ordering from Bitar's based on the mostly good reviews posted but the meal did not live up to expectations. I ordered the rice combo with chicken. They give you plenty of food but the chicken was overcooked, the tahini had congealed on the chicken and the dressing for the cucumber salad was overpowering making it almost inedible. I will say the hummus and pita were quite good but everything else I could have skiped. Also, I wasn't the only one who wasn't enamored with the food as my mother also stated her meal want that good.
Hands down the best food we had while visiting Philadelphia. The restaurant was beautiful, the service was warm welcome as well as friendly and the food was incredible.
Great atmosphere and cozy place to share a cup of mud and a tasty treat. The staff are very cool.

Very friendly staff. The guy who works there is really nice. Oh and the food... The food makes me cry from how good it is. The chicken tikka masala is my favorite. It's really really good. Don't get ask for it spicy though unless you are ready for it. They are really generous with their spiciness!

A friend recommended this place to me yesterday and I just had to check it out today. It's a little hole in the wall in a small plaza. They serve hot food that is ready for easy order and pickup but they also have a menu which you order and wait for and either eat in or take out. Keep in mind if you plan on eating in that it is a small place. 1 merengue (drink), 1 chicken empanadilla, 1 plate of mofongo with shrimp, black beans and white rice -- all for $16.15 (after tax)

Nice decor. Good prices. Hospitable wait staff. Decent food. I recommend the lettuce wraps and the honey shrimp. Everything looked good as well. I too was skeptical of a Chinese Food Chain, but I can't wait to go back.

Good food, reasonably priced beers, and a nice waterfront atmosphere. Fried pickles, calamari, and Fish tacos are all good. Kind of a fun little place where you can go and not break the bank for dinner.

I didn't see any basis for complaint. The jerked chicken dinner with rice, cabbage and plantain was delicious. The saltfish fritter appetizer was very good. The freshly made corn bread was excellent. The portions were more than ample and the service was all you could hope for.
The food is great! Of coarse like most of us, I tend to eat the same thing every time I go! I love their salad! We were glad to see them come to Apollo Beach!

First time at the new location on South St, but worth the extra half-mile hike. I agree that this place can be slow and no one's gonna accuse the wait staff of being too attentive, but they serve a good meal. I recommend the Sansom kabob, sort of a mixed grill of grilled lamb, grilled chicken, and the star of the show: the Chablee kabob (ground beef mixed with onions, garlic and spices formed into a long kabob -- delicious!) -- comes with grilled onion and tomato which are very good compliments, as well as brown rice with a nice topping that's sorta like a thick hummus (plus afghan bread and a little salad). Went on a Wednesday evening and there was barely anyone in there, so I got my food quickly. My sambosa appetizer (not quite as good as an Indian samosa, but still good) arrived in just a few minutes. I always leave sated and happy and feeling like I had a refreshing and balanced meal -- it's not cheap (Sansom kabob is $18 for dinner), but well worth it!
The pho, honestly, is my favorite in town. We walk in and they put our order in, even if we haven't been in months. Delicious.

The overall experience was mediocre. The waiter seemed very apathetic and was almost rude. He interrupted me in the middle of my order and tried to push my boyfriend to order salad. We didn't order drinks and in response he said nothing and walked away. The bread came with olive oil, and was pretty normal. But ten minutes later some other waitress appears with butter when were on our last piece of bread and sets it down without saying a word. Confusing... We ordered chicken & rice soup (which could have been less oily) and calamari (which could have been more crispy) for apps. The entrees were just okay as well. Shrimp scampi pasta had a funky aftertaste and the shrimp was slightly over cooked and burnt. The veal was also too oily. Overall the food was underwhelming. Seems like the place could've been more popular a few years ago but never kept up with the times. The food was meh and the waiter made us feel uncomfortable, so overall not an experience I would return to.

The warm weather inspired a byob food adventure into an array of flavors and ingredients, familiar and foreign. It was my first time eating Laotian food, but it resembles Thai, so we were able to work out tasty dishes to try with the help of our super helpful and friendly server! We had six dishes and two desserts among us and rolled out satisfied and stuffed!! **Cash only
Lovely little Thai restaurant in Brandon Fl. The food was amazing, and they are also veggie/vegan friendly. Nothing seemed overpriced. Good service and will definitely eat there again soon.
I haven't been there for a while and the foods gotten better. Maybe my tastes have changed, but the end result is the same.
From start to finish, one of the best meals I've experienced. The aesthetics, staff, and food were out of this world...2 weeks serving dinner and they didn't miss a beat!

My son was doing a project on Jamaica for a school project. I called Island Vybez to get an authentic Jamaican dessert for the class. Kevin went above and beyond to make a delicious Jamaican banana bread . Everyone loved it ! Kevin and Island Vybez went out of their way for us and what they delivered was enjoyed by all.

This place rocks. I always drove by with curiosity but never stopped in, but I am glad I finally did. I was greeted as soon as I walked in, and the staff was very friendly. The hummus is so creamy and delicious. And the pita bread is always nice and warm. I wish I had the recipe. I ordered The Duo and it was fabulous. There was just enough meat, and rice to balance out, along with a small salad. I love the meat here because it is not too greasy, and I don't feel guilty when I leave. And don't you dare leave without trying the Pb&J smoothie, I think it's called. Wow, this drink is so underrated. It is not too sweet, and is just so heavenly. I really urge anyone to give this place a try.

I really am in love with this coffee shop. Not only do they make a good cup of coffee but they have excellent tea too. Love my chai and London fog! If you like good deals, grab a chai tea and 2 samosas for a light snack before going to the movies. Their dessert options are excellent too. In general this is a great place to meet for a quick get together or have a large group at the family tables. I have to say an additional awesomeness of this place is their set up for those that are physically limited. There's a ramp and stairs on the side or you can access the cafe directly from 109 st door. Seating is limited but if you're able, go hang out upstairs. Also, good tip to know is that there's free parking if you sign in to the iPad when you walk into the cafe. Staff is always friendly here and today I greatly appreciate the extra kindness extended to me. The cashier made sure to bring my tea over as I'm currently on crutches and well, life's a bit difficult when you don't have hands free to hold that precious hot liquid you've been looking forward to all day. Thank you.
I have been there twice so far, it actually pretty decent food .... but way too over priced for Indian food.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Best sushi ever (although I am vegetarian and do not eat any fish. But vegetarian sushi is still called sushi, right?) I always get the avocado roll, sweet potato roll, and inari (bean curd) roll. And it fills me up everytime! I'm still trying to figure out how they cut the oranges the way they do at the end!

I come here whenever I can for their Drunken Noodles. It's pretty good but still a little salty. I cannot say its the best I ever had....but it's the best in the PA/NJ area that I can find so far. They'll make it spicier for you if you want and will use actually thai chillies not like some places where they just added dried red pepper flakes. I'm not impress with their Tom Yum soups or the other appetizers on the menu. Once we ordered their dumplings and it came out smelling sour. We told our waitress and she said that's normal. I'm not sure that's right. Nothing should smell sour unless it's bad or pickled. In any case, instead of taking it away immediately she tried to dispute it. I wasn't very please with that type of approach. I didn't want to start a scene just wanted the appetizer to be remove. We still come here...because I do enjoy their drunken noodles but that's all we ordered.
Good strong drinks although mojito is not my favorite. Fajitas are great and served piping hot. Very friendly and prompt service. We like coming here before a play at the Bucks County Playhouse.

Ordered a catered lunch for my office from Bitar's through ezcater.com. The order was supposed to arrive at 11:45 for a 12 o clock meeting. The order arrived almost 2 HOURS late after I'd already cancelled and been refunded for the order. When ezcater was trying to find out the ETA of the order for me (while I had a whole meeting full of hungry people) they relayed someone at Bitar's would scream at them that the food was on the way and then hang up the phone. Bitar's lack of transparency ended up causing a major headache for both parties, as I had to go out and get a different lunch for 20 people and Bitar's delivery driver had to return hundreds of dollars worth of food.
Food was cold and the absolute worst service I have ever had my son asked for soda several times and we got the check and he still never received his soda. If I could give it negative stars I would.

We were excited to try this place, but left disappointed and hungry. Its Memorial Day weekend at roughly 3pm and the place was practically empty..really, maybe six other patrons, yet we waited nearly 40 minutes for our food??? While we waited we ordered drinks and appetizer. Shouldn't have bothered. The guacamole plate is delivered with a high-end price tag of $14, but plays like low-end $1 menu. Guaca was not fresh and had layers of lemon juice throughout the tub it was served in laying atop the avocado like a slick oil spill. Floating on top were the wilty vegetables and to the side a handful of ordinary tortilla chips. You can get some fresh guacamole with homemade chips and oh, flavor just down the street at El Torro for $3.50. I ordered the Vesper Rose cocktail $11 which was described as gin, vodka, rose, rose water, and lemon. It tasted only of gin. now gin is not an aged alcohol, so therefore you will not hear the mixologist terminology "smooth" preceding the word "gin" ever, no 'Sloe" is the only word you hear before "gin, and honestly I'm convinced its because drinking straight gin is like a slow death, but this wasn't even the sickly, rosy red kind that you got drunk off ..sugar high drunk, that is... in high school, this is the plain old taste like watered down bleach brand. There wasn't even a hint of the other flavor notes hanging around in there. A cocktail should be sipped with anticipation of meeting delicate burst of flavor, not like chlorine tea. and to add insult to injury it was barren from even a stitch of dressing, not even a slice of lemon. Apparently, presentation took the holiday off. I wanted to send it back, but our disinterested waiter never floated past our table in order for me to do so. As a matter of fact, there didn't seem to be any other staff in site. Was this a culinary rapture? Helloooo We had made the decision to just leave at this point when our food appears. The only surviving waiter slides a jumbled plate in front of me with fries spilling out of a cardboard box next to my $16 White Castle sized crab cake sandwich. I can't critique the crab cake or the mango slaw because I didn't get past the Sunbeam, American white bread bun, and again not a stitch of garnish on the plate. Oh presentation where, oh where did you go? $14 appetizer, $11 cocktail, $16 entree, walking out priceless. I paid for the guacamole food...you know, like cheese food... and the liquid formerly known as cocktails & ale, but left the rest in hopes it would go the way of wait staff.

This is one of my favorite places to go to during a lunch break from work. Their wait staff is super friendly, and they have you in and out pretty quickly. The happy prawns and fried bananas are a must, and the curries are great. They can be a little bland sometimes, so I'd order one of the spicier versions
Cheap and delicious. Bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich hits the spot every time.
Awsome food! We go there a few times a month. The staff is always friendly and the chef is a genius! Best Asian style food in the area! And very reasonably priced!
Word to the wise, don't come here... We reserved a reservation for 15 3 weeks ahead of time and got there and there was, first off, No air conditioning, it was 99 degrees out...

I got a flyer in the mail at my house and immediately knew I had to take it to work, as my co-workers and I love chinese food. My favourite dish ever is peaches and cream, so I get it everywhere I. Best Peaches and Cream Shrimp that I have ever had. Their hot and sour soup is up there with the best as well. Totally recommend them, their delivery service is fantastic!
3. 5 stars... The Pad Thai is really good and so is the barbeque pork. However, the yellow curry was very watery and didn't really have much of a taste.

I like this place for it's unique food and atmosphere, but I wasn't blown away by the flavor of the food. I had never had Ethiopian before and wanted to try it. I sampled several different options and nothing was gross or bad, but nothing blew me away either. I wouldn't protest if friends wanted to head here, but I wouldn't be the one suggesting it.
Tried our friends new restaurant, wow, everything was great from the atmosphere to the food. Wishing him the best of luck on this new venture
Excellent food! Very professional staff! Buffet is a great way to sample various dishes. Will definitely return!

Pretty chill atmosphere with good coffee. La Colombe coffee and an array of seating options make it a good place to chat with friends or read. Not as inviting as La Citadelle, but is way less crowded than Good Karma.
The gilled beef bo nuong was really tasty, the pho was the best we've had in Boise so far, good thai tea too. Food came out fast.

Probably the most disgusting food I have put in my mouth. The miso soup was powder chicken bouillon that reminded me of wet socks. The sesame chicken, what can I say? "Chicken" reminiscent of pineapple. Not even close to sesame chicken. I was sick for 3 days after eating here. Customer beware. Run!!!

This was the perfect breakfast with colleagues on the first day of our conference at Loews Resort. I ordered the vegetarian Mediterranean Omelet with no cheese + Turkish Coffee. I added the hot sauce to the omelet. Both tasted excellent with just the right portion size. We enjoyed eating outside on a beautiful sunny morning.

We stopped in Carpinteria for lunch on our drive back down the coast. We found this little gem along the main drag and after perusing the menu, thought it would be a good spot. All three of us ordered off the lunch specials menu. The portions were the perfect size, not too big or too small. The server was able to accommodate our vegetarian needs and swap out the appetizers for veggie options. The yellow curry with tofu was delicious and a tad on the spicy side - which I was not expecting but found wonderful. We ate inside, but if we went back, we would definitely want to eat out on the patio in one of the cool wood booths. If you are stopping for lunch or dinner in Carpinteria, I would highly recommend this restaurant. Very affordable and yummy.

This place is consistently delicious. The pad thai is seriously yum, and the sesame chicken is wonderful. One thing I like about Chopstix (as a spicy food lover) is that if you ask for it extra-spicy, that's the way it arrives, without questioning you with "are you sure about that?" I'm always sure. The food here tastes fresh and healthy, and the portion sizes are very generous--I always end up with a full dinner of leftovers, more to enjoy later! The atmosphere is relaxed, clean, and well-decorated, and the service is A+, friendly and non-intrusive. It makes me happy that the closest Asian restaurant to my house is also one of the better ones.

Balle Balle! A little bit of Punjab in Arizona. Do not leave this restaurant without trying their Mango Lassi (sorta like mango smoothie). Tandoori chicken is amazing but I like the Palak Paneer (Spinach and Cheese cubes) dish the most.

Had the chicken pho - it was good, my husband enjoyed that way more than i did. Smelled really good though, and had some light spices we couldn't quite figure out. I had the chicken fried rice (I'm so adventurous!). It was probably the best chicken fried rice I've had in quite a while. It's worth a trip.

This is a small restaurant and was hard to locate for the first time. I visited here on new year day evening with not many people around and they still took long time to serve my kothu paratha dish but its very delicious. Though service and ambience is average, food is top notch. I highly recommend if you love south Indian dishes
My wife and I ate here based on what we read in Yelp. Excellent service from the minute we walked in. Our meal was cooked perfectly and prices reasonable. We would definitely go back again!!

We decided to try someplace new for lunch one Sunday, I looked at some of the different places on Yelp and we decided on Zagol Ethiopian cuisine, partly because of their advertised Sunday lunch specials. When we got there, the place was dead. There was one other table in the whole restaurant and one employee. She had been in the back, and we waited a good three minutes before she came out and realized we were standing there waiting. She sat us at one of the dirty tables and we waited while she wiped it, which was necessary because not one table was clean. The other table paid and left, and at least five minutes later she came back for our drink order. We decided to try the Ethiopian honey wine, or Emat. This stuff tasted just like honey, but easily drinkable. Yummy. Finally, she came back for our food order. When we asked about the advertised lunch specials, she simply said "no" and looked at me like I was ridiculous. When we asked if one was enough to share, she replied that if that was what we wanted, we could finish our wine and leave. So we decided to order two, despite our stronger urgings to leave. We tried to play it off like she was joking, but she wasn't. We tried a vegetarian Kik Alicha (a pea based mush that tasted somewhat like hummus) for around $9 something, and the Key Wat (a beef stew/mush made with what tasted like low grade meat and some spice) for over $10. Our food arrived quickly after overhearing a dramatic phone conversation in the kitchen. It came with a small salad on the pan of bread, and it was good thing we ordered two, but it might've been better if we'd left at the moment she suggested it. We left unsatisfied from the small portions and disappointed by the service.

One of the few Indian places I have been too, but that being said, I love it. The service is always quick and friendly, their prices are good, and the food is yummy. This is one of the mainstays for take-out in our household and it never disappoints. The lunch buffet is a good option for those that arent sure what they like. It gives you a good chance to try a bunch of different items for not a lot of money. Highly recommend giving India Palace a try if you are in the mood for Indian!
It doesn't matter what you get off the menu. Everything is really good. The lunch specials run through Saturday so the prices are even better. The service is fast.

Right across from the New Wave Cafe, you would never expect this small little place to dish out their accolade-ridden dishes. It is simply, though. If you like fish, you will love Dimitri's. Do not miss their calamari. Oh, and because it's a small place with the kitchen right next to you, I would recommend not taking a first (or romantic) date here.

Wait was a little longer for the food, but came out super fresh so I am ok with the wait! The Greek salad was delicious!! My boyfriend got the gyro and it was delicious! Their fries are super fresh and tasty.

When I sat down here, Pat Bentar's "Love is a Battlefield" started playing, and that's how I feel about Viet Pho. The atmosphere is pretty much zero in that it shares seating with a strip mall and some sandwich shop. It's not gonna be an authentic feeling experience. HOWEVER, one thing this place has got right is the flavor. I'm not gonna claim expert on Vietnamese food, but I have been known to eat Pho on the side of the road in Nha Trang. Viet Pho does have it where it counts: flavor country. Conclusion: if you're into flavor, Vietnamese, and don't care about atmosphere, Viet Pho is a good choice. If you're trying to impress a date, I'd look at another place before heading here. Also kinda expensive compared to other Vietnamese restaurants I've been to before. 1 large bowl $9.39 including the $0.50 cc surcharge

I agree with others on here who have commented on inconsistencies and bad service. I overlooked the service on my initial visit because the restaurant was brand new and it always takes time to get service up to par, but it has been shoddy on two subsequent visits. The service seems insincere -- if I ask you if something is good, be honest, don't just say everything's good. You have favorites, tell me -- and seems to have no clue about the food, almost as if they've never had it. They also are TERRIBLE at clearing plates, and every single course that required a new plate did not come with one. I had to ask twice for a plate to eat my food. Also, the food just wasn't as good as the first time I went. You would think the food would improve over time, but it has become blander and greasier. I live a few blocks from here and could, conceivably, come here all the time, so I hope they get their ducks in a row and improve. I might try it again, then again I might not.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Loved our meal there last night. The four of us had a late night reservation and the owners were so accommodating. The meal was fabulous. I'm visiting from San Francisco and wanted to take my friends out for dinner. A true foodie, and a vegan, I needed a spot that knew how to prepare foods for my lifestyle while my friends who eat meat were also able to enjoy their choices. Food is prepared to order in any way you like it. Accommodating for all dietary restrictions. Organic. Fresh. Go! Enjoy yourself!!

The only reason I'm giving this place a single star is because of the service. Food was great. My wife ordered a veggie gyro with no sauce or sides and I ordered a chicken gyro. We also ordered the hummus appetizer. The nonsense started when my wife saw there was pesto on her gyro and she requested no sides. The young lady that brought it out to us was new and very nice about the order and tried to explain that sides came with it. Fine. No problem. Then another young lady walks up with a very nasty attitude and appeared to be frustrated that we asked for no sauce or sides for my wife's order. After we acquiesced and said no big deal, the one with the attitude snatched the number from our table and walked off muttering something. I was obviously pissed but decided that it wasn't worth it. I took my wife's order back up and the manager redid the order with no problem. Then she brought it back out to us and really made it worth staying to finish our meal. I didn't mention the experience with the employee with the attitude. I'll let Yelp do the talking for me. The food here is actually great. My wife and I try eating healthy so this place fits the bill. But after this experience I won't be going back. We visit Nashville a couple of times a year but I refuse to patronize an establishment that has rude workers. I think some of the grace and kindness that the manager showed to us should be passed down to the employees.
