If you can't handle dealing with customers then don't apply for a job where you deal with customers! I added a tip as I paid prior to getting our meal. It's on their checkout screen. Maybe that should have been an indication of what was in store.

I've been to a lot of Thai places in Philly and the red curry here is the best! I could and do drink the coconut red curry sauce. Pad thai, pad see ew, and penang curry are aso delicious. Green curry mussels were soo good as well. Sirracha calamari is so-so. BYOB. Extremely friendly service and very attentive. Gets a little noisy if the place is crowded.

We went for the lunch buffet. It seemed like a one man show, with the same guy seating everyone, filling water glasses, taking orders, etc. The poor guy seemed a little overwhelmed... but there I go being all sympathetic when my water glass is empty. There was a woman who came out to fill the buffet from time to time. The buffet's size was a bit of a disappointment. I'm used to being able to try a wide range of dishes but for the price I guess it was alright. There were beef dishes, which was surprising but maybe a regional thing. Chutneys and sauces were quite good. I think I'll see what else Tucson has to offer before making another trip.

My BF and I go to jamaica a couple of times a year and I swear, the jerk chicken at Taste of the Island is better than some places in Negril! Perfectly seasoned, tender and delicious. Excellent sized portions as well. I've also had the curried chicken (also delicious) and the brown stew chicken (so so). Patties are delicious -- flaky and just a bit spicy. They're baked not fried which is also a plus. Now one thing to mention...this is definitely a Jamaican joint. Once they run out of food, there's no more, so get there early. And service is slow, but you'll forgive them because everybody is so friendly and it's all part of the restaurant's charm and atmosphere. This is a hidden gem in Norristown; I'm so glad we can enjoy a taste of jamaica all year round!

Just had lunch at this location. I typically choose Masala dishes. But the owner was super helpful in helping me select something just as tasty. I had a jumbo shrimp dish that was awesome! They have lunch specials until 3. Dinner starts at 4. Definitely a neighborhood gem!

Across the street from Busch Gardens. Dropped by on our way out because of the Yelp ratings. What a great meal: lamb Gryos, Greek salad (complete with Dolmades), falafel sandwich, saffron rice and beans, baklava, sweet potato pie. Delightful surprise! And the owner is a hoot. Noticed they even have a drive through.

Just had brunch here, always have a good meal but today was phenomenallll. Cheddar pancakes stuffed with pulled pork with a side of chipotle maple pork belly. Pulled pork for brunch you say?!?! Hear me out. Easily one of the top 5 best meals I've ever had. The absolute perfect balance of savory and sweet. Huge portion and pork belly was cooked perfectly. Our waitress Madison was sweet as pie and absolutely awesome. Blue Plate for the win!
Sesame chicken had no flavor and the meat was too tough. Friendly staff but definitely do not recommend

I came here for the first time about a week ago and the food was phenomenal - I got the jerk chicken with rice and cabbage. I was worried that it might be too spicy for me but it wasn't! Will be coming back again. My only suggestion is if you work in the area, call in your order, the wait can be a little while.

Great food. I was in the area working for a week and ate here twice. The goat curry was fantastic, my favorite. I love the sweet Nan bread! Ground lamb kabob was also good, as was the chicken tika masala. I also had the garlic Nan but prefered the sweet Nan, it is so good. Almost like a sweet desert bread.

Came here for the live music one night. The service was slow. We had ordered a bottle of white wine, a beer, and two mixed drinks. The waiter brought out the beer and glasses for the wine (mismatched). We asked about getting another glass that matched the other one and he said he'd go look for another one. He finally found another white wine glass, but then brought out an already opened bottle of wine. We pointed that out to him and then had to go back for a full bottle. In the mean time the mixed drinks were taking their sweet time getting to our table. They finally came to our table about 10-15 minutes later. I'm guessing it that it had to have been either a nre waiter or just an off night for the place. Other than that, the restaurant looked nice and was comfortable. Came on another night and service was more attentive, but so busy because of the live music. Enjoyed the drinks and the latin jazz music on that second evening.

I'm no expert in Indian food, but I'm definitely a fan of the buffet here. Great variety and flavors. I rarely get to eat Indian, but I'm happy to get my fix here. There are times that meat is sometimes cooked or heating for too long though. The curry sauces are the best... love soaking the naan and rice in all that saucy yumminess!

One of my favorite places in STL. Converted gas station, small and intimate. Great food. I like the sandwiches and salads. Great drinks. Limited but thoughtful selection of beers. Nice wine selections. Great for a quick bite or longer chat.

The best green curry in philadelphia hands down. The shrimp are huge and there's so much of the bamboo shoots it will blow your mind. I love how they let you upgrade the spice level. The papaya salad was said to be award winning and I can see why. It's so fresh, tang, and tart. The tom yum soup was also very good they gave me more oil so I could control exactly how sour it was. The rolls were a little on the small side but tasty none the less~ I will forever be a loyal customer and fan of Jasmine Rice. I wanted to try they green curry rice dish and pad thai but the green curry is so good I just can't not order it!!!!!!!

Plus three for the excellent quality Tzatziki, the delicious chicken wrap meal (a more than worthy replacement for Cizar's wrap & fries if you need it) and it's layout as a very family friendly place to dine. Minus one for our take out order that featured under-cooked chicken and minus another for some of the peripheral issues - parking (no spaces even without line going out the door) and staff not answering the phone for take-out orders when there were open seats in the restaurant. Also: Greek place without Mythos Beer?
The food here is absolutely amazing. I have yet to find something on the menu I didn't love. Will continue to go back for the food and the great people.
Awesome food and a really good ambience. Close to the cooper river park. Their curries are to die for. This place is also a byob.

Good Americanized Chinese food. A good lobster combo value... 34.95 for two lobster with sides. The portions are massive, and tasty. They have ice cream, vanilla and chocolate, nice finish on a meal. Cocktails are pricey tho. My waiter was very distracted and had to be reminded frequently however. (One star down).

This is a small place but the food is good. Not a lot of seating but people seem to eat and get out. The service is friendly and fast. They make your food fresh and the Greek Salad is so good with the Gyro for Lunch. And the price isn't bad for the amount of food you get. If you haven't tried this place yet you should put it on your list.

Found this little gem today. Let me start by saying, don't let the location or appearance fool you. It's a little hole in the wall place in an older strip mall area. The decor is nothing special, but it IS clean and the food...Lets talk about the food. I ordered a deluxe gyro, meaning it has feta on it. Wow! Flavorful and huge!! I can say it's the best gyro I've ever had, hands down. The spanakopita...large portion (enough to share with another person). I shared with my hubby. Greek salad light and delicious and the hummus was good too with enough hummus and pita bread for four people. The line to order was nonstop for the lunch hour. Folks just kept coming in! If you haven't been here, I'd highly recommend you give it a try. Like I said, it's nothing fancy but the food is delicious!

After driving by the place a million times and already trying all the Thai places south of Kennedy we finally decided to give the place a try. My wife and I started with the BBQ chicken appetizer which comes with a little fire pot to heat them up. For the meal we split the pork thai pad and sweat and sour chicken. The thai pad was some of the best we've had. With good service and reasonable prices we'll be back for more.

I had dinner here yesterday as part of a large group. I ordered the Vegetarian Gheimeh Bademjan, which the menu describes as "Sauteed eggplant, onions, yellow split peas simmered in our special fresh tomato sauce and Persian spices, served with basmati rice." I ate half of it and took the rest home. Price: $14.95. Service was good, the food was good and plentiful, and I enjoyed the flatbread with basil, cilantro and onion, which is their alternative to free chips and salsa. Prices are pretty high for meat and seafood dishes, but it's a good restaurant.

Came here on a Monday night when it was practically empty... Wish I knew about this place sooner! My bf and I had curry and drunken noodles and they were both delish. We will be returning again to satisfy our Thai cravings. Try their fried bananas for dessert as well.

Great tofu sandwiches here. Everytime I try to order the sandwhiches anywhere else, they don't quite get it right. Tey're not bad, but it's not something they're used to making. I might be a little spoiled and too picky from my experience with great Vietnamese food in SJ. Anyways, this place does an excellent job with that dish in particular. Everything else I've tried has been good too. I'm impressed that there's finally a restaurant that seems to work in this location. They're always busy and the staff is friendly.

Servers are very attentive and friendly. The food is good. I had chicken tikka masala and a mango lassi. I thought the lassi was a bit sweet and the chicken tikka masala was not the best I have had, but overall, a good Indian dinner.

The atmosphere is nice, somewhat cozy. The greeter was very friendly and sat us promptly. Our server was at out table in minutes with water, asking us what we might like to eat and offering us me us and daily specials. I order the Bacon Wrapped Filet, and it was lovely. I ordered it Medium-Rare and I could literally cut it with a fork! It was tender and juicy. The accompanying salad was good and the veggies were a nice change from zucchini and cauliflower. We really enjoyed it.

Finally, after being bookmarked forEVER, I was ready to check out Palace of Asia. The restaurant is connected to a sketchy looking hotel and its even sketchier if you enter the back door. Once inside it transitions into fine dining though. There was a chandelier hanging above with fully plated tables. I ordered a large rice and shrimp dish with onions and peppers in a red sauce, which was full of flavor. It was served mild in spice and had generous amounts of shrimp. It didn't 'wow' me but was just standard taste. My date had a yogurt based sauce and was accompanied by chicken. His dish was a very large portion. Our naan was potato stuffed but was by far not something I would order again. Even the bread itself was floppy and the potato was mush mash....no flavor. The service is where Palace missed the mark the most. Our waiter didn't seem to really care about our visit....he was a little pushy to get us in and out. Overall, the meal wasn't bad and the staff clearly, were over working their shift.

When you go out to a restaurant, do you liked being DECEIVED or LIED to? I don't and I'd assume most of you don't either. It started out harmlessly enough. Our friends were moving to Tennessee and we wanted to have a special dinner. We made reservations for seven guests, but unfortunately, one of friends had to emergently go to the hospital for a surgery and was unable to attend. We went from seven guests to six guests. The restaurant never said this was an issue and made no mention of how this would affect the menu or the price... Everyone in attendance was very pleased with the meal until the bill arrived. Management decided to charge us for the seventh guest. Now if we were informed at the beginning of the meal, it would not have been a big deal. However, imagine the expression on our face when we had been charged an extra $65...not good. When asked why we were charged for the absent guest, we were told it was because they had prepared food for seven people. This would have made sense; however, they gave us six shrimp, six sausages, six zeppoli, etc...clearly not the amount of food for seven people. Do they think we can't count? It was a complete SLAP IN THE FACE and an affront to our intelligence. We had previously been to Zeppoli about five or six times and have recommended it to many of our friends. Unfortunately, after this DEBACLE, we will never go there again, nor will we ever recommend it to any of our friends. Buyer Be Ware

We came here for dinner and I loved it. The sushi was perfect. I ordered the spicy Hulk roll and the spicy tuna roll. The spicy Hulk roll really surprised me. It comes topped with crab and they piled it sooo high that I could barely get the pieces into my mouth (that sounds so bad lol). I'm not complaining though because I was full by the end of our meal. Everything was super fresh. My friend had never had sushi before and he liked the roll that I suggested for him. The only thing that concerned me was that they only had one waitress working at one point and she was also the bartender, so the service was a little slow.
Absolutely amazing meal! The best pasta/food/service we've had in a long time! Can't go wrong with any of it! Highlights: antipasto, pesto pasta, rabbit entree, chocolate chili gelato.

Come hungry! Enjoy the view! Anything with Paneer. Naan is perfect.... chutneys are decent. This is where native-born and speaking Indian-Ameicans in the area eat. Which tells you a lot. Weekdays buffet is hugely popular. Service is prompt and efficient. I've eaten were dozes of times and only had one less-than-four star experience.

My boyfriend and I frequently patronize this restaurant... It is in Chinatown, and it is SO GOOD! My favorite is the Drunken Noodles, because I like spicy food, but my boyfriend and I agree that all of their curries are very delicious. It's also a BYO, which is a good thing to keep in mind when you want to go out to dinner but are trying to save some $$$. This place is always empty, and I have no idea why. Do yourselves a favor and make Erawan less empty. I promise you won't be dissapointed.

My brother and I are huge fans of Indian food, but it took us a while for us to try this place! Now that we have, I can say I'm glad we finally did! The place itself is nothing special. Pretty small with run down decor (the place used to be a Fingers Wings and Other Things) and their dinnerware is simple, if those things even matter to anyone, hah. I guess the food is what counts! They have a variety of dishes to choose from served "family style" where they put everything in the middle and you take your portion on individual plates. The food can be spicey so be careful if you're not a fan, but they do warn you and ask your spiciness preference. In my opinion, I think they're a little on the pricier side compared to other Indian restaurants I've eaten at, but I guess you can say it's worth it since the food is good!
Amazing food, great service! It is a BYOB, and we didn't know, so our server (I guess it was the owner) brought us some wine from his private stash :-) Sooooo amazingly nice!

We happened upon this place because they were open on Monday evening, and because of the positive Yelp reviews. We were very pleasantly surprised to find Aroma Indian Bistro to be really first rate. All of the dishes we ordered were well prepared, well balanced and cooked and served with pride and care. We had vegetable samosas for a starter. There were plenty for three adults, and they were beautifully prepared, not at all greasy, and very tasty. For entrees, we had chicken makhani and chicken saagwala. Both were first rate, well prepared, perfectly cooked and spiced, and served with an excellent dish of basmati rice. Service was attentive, prices were reasonable, and the ambiance, while not special, was pleasant and clean. Although we discovered Aroma by chance, we are delighted with our find, and will definitely return.

Awesome food, awesome ambiance, and top-notch staff!! The place is gorgeous and every time I have been in, the staff has been warm and welcoming. I have had two sandwiches, the BLT and Sloppy Dave, and they were both perfect. Also had two cookies, the chocolate chip and Belgian chocolate chip and they were really tasty. I also had the privilege of checking-out the kitchen and it is the cleanest I have seen anywhere in the city, and trust me, I have seen a lot. They also carry New Hope Fountain Sodas which are so yummy! I cannot wait to return and try more menu options. I highly recommend this place.

This place is amazing. I am so happy they've been in business so long - I think I had my first Bui's in the 90's when my sister was at Penn, and can't wait until my next one. The sausage and bacon are equally good. If you're in the mood to treat yourself at the expense of your health, get extra bacon. Mmmmm. Love it. The egg sandwich standard. "Bakea-egga-cheee!"

Love it here. Come often with my grandson. It is his favorite Chinese restaurant. Had won ton soup. It has shrimp and chicken in it. Also had sweet and sour chicken with fried rice. It was an excellent choice. Server was friendly and quick.

I spent a weekend in Columbia, IL and ate here twice. We discovered it out first night in and liked it so much we ended our weekend with lunch there. The only reason I did not give it 5 stars because there were some inconsistencies but minor and still tasty food. Value. Well priced with good sized portions. I had a large bowl of Tom Yum soup for dinner and it was so satisfying. The flavor was diving, it was served piping hot and had a good amount of chicken in it. The same held true for my second dinning experience even though I tried a different entree. Fast. Our food came out of the kitchen quickly and as mention before, it was fresh off the stove. Taste. All that we sampled was delicious. Cucumber salad- yum. Tom Yum soup- rich and tasty. Green curry- creamy with a nice spice level. I am not sure I will ever return to Columbia but if I do, I know where I am eating!

We ordered takeout pad Thai , coconut soup, and mango sticky rice. The soup was excellent, very authentic but not very spicy, the pad Thai was as good as some we had back in Thailand. The mango sticky rice was also good although the sticky rice was not the real deal. Overall, pretty good based on our limited selection. Will definitely try more.
This restaurant never lets me down. Lately, I have been going there about once a month and have always come back a satisfied customer.

This is likely not authentic Indian. What it is, however, is very good. My favorite is the Chicken Tikka Masala. I ordered it once in preparation for an all-day-and-all-night-huge-paper-researching-and-writing-cram-fest. The portions are so nicely (hugely) sized that this delicious chicken was literally all I ate for lunch, dinner, and then breakfast. Whenever I was hungry and needed a break, I just broke out the containers of rice and chicken and chowed down. Ekta propelled me through my terrible procrastination and into a A on the paper. Oh, and they threw in a complimentary dessert! Wasn't exactly sure what it was and I didn't eat too much of it (by the time I remembered it, it had been stowed in the back of my fridge for a week...) but it was a nice gesture. Doesn't deliver for lunch though. Pity.

I ordered Cuban tamales and a Batido de Pina to start and both were delicious. With that said, it took about 30 mins to get the tamales and they weren't busy at all. I ordered Picadillo as my entree and that took another 20 mins to come out. The waitress laid down Palomilla in front of me. I explained that is not what I ordered, thought it looked tasty. She went back to the kitchen and 5 mins later came back with the same food telling me this IS what I ordered. This didn't make me happy at all, and especially after the wait. I got a menu and pointed to Picadillo. About 10 mins later I finally got this pitiful excuse for the classic Cuban comfort food. There was not ONE single olive or raisin to be found, or even a note of sweet/sour that should be. It tasted like a reeeeaallly greasy bowl of Taco Bell taco meat. The plantains were good but too ripe. My husband's Cubano was decent, it had roast pork on it, but it wasn't too bad. I would defiantly go back for the tamales and to give them another try...that's how good the tamales were.

Wish I could say more positive things about this place. Their shawarma is good. However, I ordered a schwarma sandwich and wound up with a salmon shawarma. Honestly, if you know shawarma, they will give you salmon instead of beef or lamb and expect you to pay for a replacement. Will not go to again.

I definitely won't be returning to Tin's House in the future. I was so excited to try another Thai restaurant in the area. (There are at least five within a ten mile radius). We ordered the yellow curry with chicken, the teriyaki salmon roll, and the crab magic roll. The sushi rolls were rather boring and they both were absolutely drowned in specialty sauces. The yellow curry is the real reason for the low rating. The container that held the yellow curry had at least an inch and a half of oil sitting at the top of the entree. My family orders yellow curry takeout often and I have never seen such a sight. It smelled off-putting and was very thin compared to a typical yellow curry. I felt as though I had wasted money that evening. I now know that there are much better options to choose from the next time around.

I have been coming to Petra with friends and family for as long as I can remember. The food is delicious and comes in large portions. I highly recommend this restaurant if you are looking for some great middle eastern food.

Whoever has seen me in the last two days has had to deal with my hyperbolic talk of this place, like "THIS IS THE BEST MEAT ON THE PLANET." I'm not kidding. I have traveled far & wide, partly to have and to hold, to find and to experience places like this. There are hundreds of restaurants, bars and stands that I've had a perfect experience. Think of it like movies: there are hundreds upon dozens more movies that I walk away feeling: "that was a perfect movie." But then... there are some that live in my fistful of favorites and get the title: best ever. I've eaten $80 dry aged steaks. "Best Burger in The World." Michelin Starred Chef's five course dinners. Indy's finest dining spots. And street food from San Francisco to Mexico City to Jamaica, and this street food / liquor store stand... is the best food on the planet. I traveled the streets of Jamaica a few years ago... ate at every stand, and yes it was remarkable... but this is, this is Jamaican food / all meats perfected. And I'm talking about their ribs. I have no idea why it took me 18 months to return. A half slab of their pork ribs is more than enough for one. They're served with sauce on their side. I really have no idea what to say at this point other than... you have $9 somewhere... save up for it... and go. I arrived at 1145 and the ribs were ready -- straight from the parking lot smoker.

Extremely slow delivery and dishonest on the phone. Stated that the driver got lost on a delivery of 2 miles away. It's difficult to see how a 40 minute delivery delay be attributed to getting lost when we have a gps in each of our phones. Once the food arrived it was decent with a decent price however the trip it had made certainly spoiled it. There are plenty of other options in the area.
Nothing special. I liked my egg roll vermicelli but I get more egg rolls in it at other restaurants. My mom didn't like her crepe. She said it's much better at one of the places uptown

Good food and friendly service. Just a regular Thai place, nothing fancy and food is excellent. They also have vegetarian items on their menu. On our request they were able to make all our dishes without eggs and meat. Tom yum soup was perfect blend of spicy and sour and amount of vegetables weren't overwhelming. Green curry is a must along with Thai basil fried rice. That combination is just perfect. Drunken noodles were also good and the spice level was as desired.
Without reservation we waited 20 mins to get a table. But for the quality it was really ok. I recommend to reservate.
Love this restaurant.. even Indians love it..nearest I've come to a good curry in Indiana ...
Some kind of Persian-Indian fusion that does neither very well. Tried dishes from both sides and found them average to mediocre.
authentic Chinese street food! 煎饼果子加酥脆，鸡蛋灌饼加午餐肉，羊肉串，羊腰子。水煎包，金针菇超辣。肉筋也比较辣，面筋是提前腌过的。很正，好吃

Greeted with smiles and they were happy to accommodate our party of 7 on short notice! The food was perfectly balanced and they even asked the level of spicy that we would like to have! Kind staff, amazing service and Excellent food!! We will be back!

This place is amazing! I've eaten here throughout the years when I'm in philly and even after moving locations I was pleased to see that the quality of the food is as great as ever. I always get the Sansom Kebob which is my go to dish. Definitely check it out if your in the area.
Food was great. The jerk chicken platters are amazing. It was a small spot but there is a spring garden next to it where you can sit and eat if you would like. The wings were really good as well.

Normally a nice beach bar to watch the sunset or enjoy a meal. Last night however they left us waiting for over an hour for a table and then another hour for dinner. Did tell the manager and he said he was sorry, would check out ticket times and come back to our table. He never came back however. Very disappointing. Heard another table complaining to the manager as well about same issue.

Amazing food, amazing service. I ordered Thai green curry and beef skewers. Green or Red curries are my usual "test" when trying out new Thai restaurants. I was really satisfied. The beef skewers were a pleasant surprise and I ended up ordering one more round. Service is extra friendly. We had a toddler with us and the staff were very courteous and attentive. Definitely coming back again!

I've only been here once since I do live out of town. They had a variety of snacks and sandwiches (Banh Mi). However, I was at Seasons cafe for their shaved ice. Supposedly its a lesser calorie version of the fro-yo. In a way, it has the same concept of fro-yo but with an Asian twist. It kind of reminds me of the fruit dishes I had in Vietnam. Basically the shaved ice had like a milk flavoring to it and you can add toppings. Seasons cafe offered fresh fruits, canned fruits, jelly and other varieties. I must say it is quite tasty and can get addicting. Luckily I live far enough away where I can control my cravings for them. Definitely visiting this place again next time I'm in the Tampa/St.Pete area.

Had a lovely dinner here during a college visit trip with my daughter . There were plenty of vegetarian options for her. The food was delicious, and it's obvious that the owners have put their hearts into this place. Beautiful decor, great music, friendly owners, amazing food lovingly prepared - our favorite meal by far during our visit to Tampa.

It's not as good as it used to be. I only recognized one sushi chef that has been there for a long time. Everyone else looked new. That could be the reason for the poor quality of food and service. I was very disappointed that what was once a favorite restaurant of mine is now one that I will not be back to. The sushi did not taste fresh and we did not finish any of the rolls. Don't waste your money on the Groupons. They have a lot of restrictions on what you can order and they are not friendly when you present them.

Amazing food. They have dry vegetarian Manchurian! I was so happy to see it on the menu and it's delicious. Their methi mutter malai is tasty too and layered wheat paratha is so soft, crispy and freshly made I guess this is one of the best Indian restaurants in US ! Great service too!

Everytime I'm out in Green Hills, I end up stopping in here. I like that they have small portions and you can customize your protein choices. The price for what you get is just right. I was especially stoked to discover on my last visit that they offer more gluten-free options for pasta.
Second year in a row at the Phoenixville food truck festival, jerk chicken is the bomb and the mac is amazing! I'm going to look for this place when I'm downtown next.

It's a really charming place! The service was quick and gracoius, and everyone's food was great! I got the spinach egg sandwich. The sour dough bread was a bit texas-toasty, and the filling was a good balance with layers of egg, spinach, and cheese. My friend got the chile relleno tart, which was really good! If you've had chiles rellenos before, it had the same classic flavor and cheese, but it's in a quiche-like form with a cornmeal crust. I also got a gingerale, which was a bottled cane-sugar gingerale that was pleasant. For a pricing frame, I think all the entres were $8, the gingerale was $2, and we shared a $5 slice of strawberry cake. The cakes are 3 layers, so sharing 1 piece between the three of us was perfect. Also, one review from 6 months ago noted missing ceiling tiles and lights--it looks fixed up now. Still mostly bare walls, I guess, but it was charming.

We stopped in to try some Afghan food on a whim. The restaurant drew us in due to the beautiful flower display outside and the promise of a new delight for our taste buds. Sweetheart ordered the bean soup, and we shared a chicken kabob dinner. The meal was okay, but quite bland. The kabob dinner was served with a salad topped with yogurt dressing and a side of aromatic rice. Nothing that I could not prepare better myself. Is this REAL Afghan food? I am not likely to travel there, and definitely not for the food!
A new favorite. I love the spinakopita and the fava bean hummus. Really, everything we try here is delicious. Staff is friendly and helpful!

I don't usually write reviews of established businesses with ratings that I already agree with, but I'm writing one here because they're so awesome. These guys should write the manual for running a food truck. First, the food is amazing. But you already knew that from all the other reviews. So I won't waste your time here. Second, the price point is, well, on point. There are lots of ways to combine things to get very full on less than $8. Actually, better than on point if you know how to order off the written menu. (Ask some locals if you wanna know.) Which brings me to the third, and arguably most important point. The guys running the truck are simply amazing people. I know this review is supposed to be about the food, but the quality of the place is totally reflected in the attitude of the guys running it. Even if you're having a bad day and order rudely with a resting b* face frown, just talking to these guys will make you feel better. You can tell these guys really love to get to know their customers, and its not a show. I'll end with a story. One day they had red vegetable curry as their special, and I asked if there was any meat in it, which obviously there wasn't. So I decided to go with the chicken satay over salad (there's an off menu item!). But seeing I was interested in the curry, Robert asked me if I wanted to try some of it - he would put some on the side for free! I was expecting a tiny sample, but it was a sizable scoop, and it made the chicken over salad amazing. For $6! Definitely one of the most memorable food truck meals I've ever had.

Decent indian food. Lots of choices on the menu and ive never seen goat on an indian menu. They pump lots of air in the restaurant so it doesnt smell like curry. The food is overpriced though and i would like to see the restaurant a little bit cleaner. Lots of advertisements and brochures in the restaurant, it feels like a flea market.

Excellent authentic Puerto Rican cuisine. We tried the "trip thru Puerto Rico". We loved all three dishes. The Pastelon was amazing along with the Carne Frita. The ropa vieja was best I have had but it's not my favorite dish in general. Side dishes of manposteo and mofungo de yuca was delicious. We tried the sampler dessert tres leche was best I have ever had!! Coconut flan amazing. This restaurant is extremely traditional but only serving the best of Puerto Rico. What a great island!!

Cheap, delicious, and healthy! You can't beat the price-to-quality ratio here. Sometimes I feel a bit guilty eating Indian food when it's really oily, but Mumbai Bistro doesn't include butter or ghee and it doesn't taste too oily. I love the freedom of being able to choose exactly what you want, on your plate. (Sometimes I want naan, not rice.) Only thing is, it's so cheap and delicious, you might want to go back for seconds. $3 for two pieces of tandoori chicken and $1 naans are a steal compared to other places. First time trying malai kofta curry, loved it! Who knew little balls of spinach and potato could be so good. The chicken in the chicken tikka masala was still juicy and tender, and the actual curry broth was addictive. If you like cheese, the paneer masala was excellent, as well. The mumbai dal was probably the blandest out of the curries I had, but it tasted like exactly what it was supposed to: lentil bean curry. It's pretty small, though, so either plan for takeout or don't bring too many people. The guy working the counter was really friendly. Don't forget to grab a frequent-eater card; if you try it once, you'll definitely be coming back.

I really, really like this place. It is what it is...a simple water front bar, with outstanding sunsets and a healthy diet of Jimmy Buffett playing in the background (and for a very good reason). I've always found the service is always friendly, even when swamped; the beer is always cold and I do like the fish tacos (did I mention the sunsets?). See? Nice and simple... Bring the kids, your family, round up some good friends or go alone, you'll have a great time.

My third Thai meal in CA and I have been consistently blown away! Thai food in London just doesn't compare. Or maybe I'm just in love with those freaky thick flat squashy noodles.... mmm... God they are awesome! And the sauce I had with the flat noodles was just fricking amazing, lovely and garlicky with just a hint of sweet. And when I ordered coconut juice they brought me an ENTIRE fresh coconut, with the white fleshy bits that peeled off and made my day :D

Different, flavorful, and did I mention different? My wife begged me to go here with her one Saturday and because I'm a pushover with her... She eats here about once a week for lunch and brought home leftovers for me to try. Even nuked in a microwave I was intrigued, and I usually dislike almost everything microwaved or warmed up. With that said: Enter Noodles stage right. I really liked the look of the restaurant, and I'm not a decorations type guy but man did it look and feel clean. So plus one on cleanliness. The menu is simple, sampling noodles across Europe and Asia alike but I'm not a fan of the Far East Noodle so someone should try those and let me know. I instead chose the Alfredo Mont Amore. A large bowl arrived to the rim with a mixture of ingredients that mend well with each other. Visually appealing, fogging my glasses I dove in unexpectedly and came out pleasantly surprised. Delicious Alfredo, not your out of a jar and slow heated type but an original product, think Olive Garden but add way more flavor. The trio of tomatoes, mushrooms and spinach along with four types of cheese... need I say more? Then the main ingredient in the name: Chicken. I get scared with chicken, undercooked = a trip to the hospital or a bad night with the porcelain. Over cooked = inedible sand paper. Then there's the choice and cut of chicken which could be full of grade A white meat or it could be budget chicken with fat and gristle. For me a bite of gristle will end my meal in a hurry. To my surprise each bite was as the first, delicious. Overall, I put my seal of approval on Noodles 'N Company and will be back. The only drawback here that prevents to grand five star would be the lack of bread. If I held even a simple piece of wheat bread this would have been perfect. How else do you sop up all the alfredo? Otherwise, a great lunch spot that leaves you satisfied.
Great combination Banh Mi sandwich. Not he cleanest location but I would definitely order more sandwiches to go. Didn't try anything else on the menu.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: I used to work in Thailand and had high hopes. Sadly my hopes were dashed on the rocks of reality. Lunch was mediocre at best. The cafe is in a cute old style house and the staff were very nice people. However, no one at the table was able to rave about their meal. There other Thai resturants in Reno I would head to before Lana Thai.
Good, fresh Thai place. Small seating area s d no alcohol but tasty. Service is quick and friendly. Had the Joes spicy noodle and it was yum

Two friends and I were in the shopping center and noticed that this restaurant had opened and decided to try it out. The food was amazing. We had chicken lo mien, crispy prawn with walnuts and a chicken hibachi plate, plus soups and a vegetable egg roll type thing (pictured- all plates were beautifully presented with flowers and garnish). The atmosphere is nice, the staff was attentive and the prices are good, especially for the amount of food you get. We were all pleased with our experiences and will definitely be going back!

Not sure if it's "authentic" but I do know it's clean, great portion sizes, friendly staff and tasty food. No there are no belly dancers or broken plates (they don't use glass) but it's consistently good. We eat here regularly and have never had a bad meal. Can I get better Greek someplace else, I'm sure but in Carrollwood, I know I can't. I have been to all the other Greek places in Carrollwood and there is no comparison. Is it fast food, yes but it's very good fast food prepared fresh and worth every penny.
Taste was good but man I wish I took a picture of the amount of food that was in my $10 plate. My 7yr old brother wouldn't be full off of that. Better off getting a combo at Taco Bell!

We stopped here while passing through Trenton and I'm so glad we picked this place out of everything else! Stew chicken and jerk chicken were fall off the bone juicy and flavorful, a good bite of spice without being too overwhelming. Rice and beans sound simple but were so delicious here. Also got the pineapple lemonade, which was a little on the sweeter side, but very refreshing and tasted like real pineapple!

I am so bummed that this was a huge disappointment. I've had Ethiopian food many times and it's always delicious. With the ratings being so good I took my friend here for his first experience. After, I just had to keep reminding him that it was not a good representation of everything I have raved about. We ordered The Queens eight platter because I wanted to make sure he got to sample several items. They were all tasteless bland overcooked or undercooked with not a hint of seasoning...even salt and pepper. Where is the berbere? The cardamom garlic fenugreek paprika cayenne?? Everything tasted like it came right out of the can. Disgusting really.

I don't even want to tell you about this place. I don't want to tell you, because I don't want it to get crowded. I want to walk in the door and get my delicious double, or pattie, veggie roti, or coconut cake. But I'm going to tell you, because good people run this joint, and good people deserve good business. 52nd St. is dotted with Caribbean joints - this one is Trinidad/Tobago. The food is authentic, down to the "roots" and Ting beverages in the cold case, is made quickly, and is inexpensive. Because a decent number of their customers are Rastafari, there are also tons of vegetarian options, which make me happy. If you want hot food, order at the window at the back, and for bakery items, order at the case. Watch out for the Black Cake, a specialty soaked in rum, that is only available during the Holidays. This is a real neighborhood joint run be real folks celebrating their culture and their customers. Photos Calypso and Soca musicians line the walls, and you can pick up cds here, or informational publications about Haile Selassie, or a flyer for all the crazy Reggae shows you didn't know were going on in West Philly.

We've been to Spice Thai several times and have thoroughtly enjoyed it every time. Great food, byob, and place you can go to as a date night or to have a dinner out with friends. The pineapple fried rice is awesome. Great find in Doylestown when you feel like doing something different than Italian.

I ordered and my husband picked up our to go order tonight and so far, I am impressed. I told the lady who answered for to go orders that it was our first time trying the restaurant and she was happy to help with suggestions. We got red curry with chicken, spicy noodles with chicken and a simple Mexican sushi roll (my usual sushi go to is spicy tuna but I am pregnant so went with cooked). Portions were definitely big! Two entrees could definitely feed four and I am happy to have the left overs. :) Spicy Noodles had amazing flavors and were not overly spicy but had a small after bite kick. I ordered them medium spice as well as the red curry. I was very pleased with the red curry and my husband, who is not usually a curry fan, enjoyed it as well. I love how many bamboo shoots were in it and the pineapple was a nice touch - I have only had pineapple in my red curry at a few places. The Mexican wasn't the greatest but it was bad either. I just am spoiled with sushi further south on Seminole Blvd at Jimmy's. Overall, this will be our go to for Thai food, which is exactly what I was looking for!!

Momo's, a small Greek restaurant located just a little off the intersection of North South and Delmar in University City, is almost a wonderful little secret. I say almost because each time that I have been there, it has always had a crowd. So far, I have been there twice, and I plan on returning as soon as I can. The ambiance is truly inviting, the wait staff, extremely polite and as accommodating as possible. What sets Momo's apart from most other restaurants is the fact that they have belly dancing, yes, belly dancing. While at first when you think of a belly dancer making her way through the restaurant and past your table, you might not know what to think. But, the belly dancer is a rather enjoyable and entertaining aspect of Momo's. Belly dancers aside, the food that Momo's has to offer also are quite delectable. The tapas Momo's has available is a teat in their own. The way to start any meal is with a small flavorful delight ready to wet the taste buds for anticipation of what is to come next. Momo's offers many of the traditional Greek foods found here and everyone that has eaten with me at Momo's has all agreed that the food is always superb.

Friendly, knowledgeable staff, comfortable atmosphere, and amazing, authentic dishes! I have been to many Indian restaurants, but nothing beats the Chana Masala and Baingan Barta at Spice Kitchen. I ate here last night with two friends, we are all vegan and the staff was very helpful and knowledgeable to help us all pick dairy free dishes. The manager, Sharma, even went as far as bringing us a complimentary dish of Vegetable Korma made vegan. The dish is traditionally made with cream, but he asked the chef to use coconut milk as an alternative. It was amazing! We will be coming back often!

Finally found decent Thai! Since moving to the area a couple of years ago I've been in a serious Thai drought. Thankfully I discovered Nooddi. Thai basil chicken was excellent. Steamed chicken dumplings were similarly good. And while the beef panang was unlike any other I have had (less creamy, more brothy) it was delicious. Only knock is that ordering it "Thai hot" did not result in a spicy enough dish for my palate. Looking forward to trying the West Chester location that is closer to my home.

Such a great addition to Newtown. We went for the weekend buffet and all the food was delicious and very authentic; you can really taste all the spices. The naan was made fresh and brought to the table. The service was great as well. Everyone was extremely friendly and attentive. They even asked if I wanted a side of hot sauce, which was spicy and tasty. I also purchased their groupon so I look forward to trying some menu items as well. I really hope this place is here to stay!

Don't let the location or the exterior appearance fool you. There is Jerk goodness being served here. I stopped in for lunch before leaving town and I was glad I did. The good- Jerk Chicken was fabulous, portion size was adequate and price was reasonable. The bad- there was standing water under one of the tables where I tried to sit. Next table almost fell over when I put the weight of my elbows on the table. The awesome- waitress named Crystal was beautiful and very pleasant. This place would have earned 4 stars if the location and decor had been better.

Upon my most recent visit to Seasons Cafe to show my friend the local offerings, I was able to get takeout so I could try the peanut chicken curry entree. As always, the staff at Seasons were pleasant, helpful, and patient during my visit. Our shaved ice, boba, and take out were delivered to our table in a few short minutes The next day when I had the generous portion of chicken curry for lunch, it was delicious and pleasantly spicy. In addition, the price was very reasonable for the quality and amount at $7.25 (I believe). I will definitely return to try more of the entrees. Thank you, Seasons, for always delivering a positive dining experience.

This is the only Ethiopian restaurant in the Tampa Bay Area, and having had a lot of delicious Ethiopian cuisine in Seattle and New York, Queen of Sheeba certainly fulfilled my hunger for Ethiopian food. I've read many reviews about this place, and I ran across one that sums it all up, this was a negative review about how you have to eat with your hands, really you eat with the anjera using your hands, but most Floridians are ten plus years behind and they are incredibly ignorant and plainly stupid. Please don't attempt to be open minded to new food and then arrogantly ask for your little american utensils, instead wash your hands and embrace different cultures, do not continue to terrorize others with your pig headed American ignorance. Again, this wasn't my favorite Ethiopian, because every place is a little different, but is was still good food, and a great environment to eat it, as far as good environments go in Florida where burgers and fries are not on the menu.

The food is so good. We love the shawarma and the falafel. We live nearby and eat here way too often. The pastry case in the market section is also to die for. If you love middle eastern food, this place is amazing. And if you've never tried middle eastern food, then you need to get to Ishtar ASAP. You won't be disappointed. Bring warm clothes in the winter because it's a bit cold, but that doesn't reportedly take away from the incredible food.

Great for lunch specials and large takeout orders. Love the fact that they don't have a lunch buffet instead they cook a dish for you from scratch as part of their lunch special and serve it with freshly made naan and some rice. Try their butter chicken, chicken biryani and goat biryani.

Wonderful atmosphere, and excellent food! We ordered the lump crab, artichoke dip, but unfortunately they sold out of it, so we ordered the crab cakes and they were so delicious! My fiance ordered the AM burger and I ordered the shrimp po boy, neither of us were left disappointed with this trip. I would highly recommend! Service was great, drinks were awesome!

Good food. Atmosphere was horrible. I just order Togo instead. Staff was very friendly they don't take tips!! Not even when you insisted. Deluxe Gyros was perfect every time. I've noticed that I drank lots of water after I finish my food !! Talking about gallons of water. I guess water is always good for you. Will be back again and again.

It doesn't look like much, but this tiny place is the cat's meow! We have tried several of the appetizers and sandwiches and have enjoyed everything immensely. The pickled vegetables are homemade by the owner and taste like nothing I've ever tried- sooo spicy and delicious. We've tried a few of the pureed dips (hummus, baba ghanouj, muamarra) and were very impressed. We took our friends who lived in Egypt and even they thought the food was incredible. We love the lamb sauce on the gyros! Even their fries are good (and in my husband's opinion, it's tough to make good fries)... It's difficult to spend more than $10 a person here as they have no liquor license (at least the last time we went) and the prices are very reasonable. Once my husband left his hat and the owner came running out to our car with it. You will not be sorry you drove all the way down south for the So. Grand Gyro Express. Meow!
Excellent thai. Pad thai and panang curry were the bomb.. Almost forgot Tom Yum also rocked.

Never failed to satisfy all my guests from far away land as Jakarta, Indonesia ; Paris, France ; Calgary Canada ...just to mention a few. These people kept on coming back for the Noodle soup ( Mie Komplit ) . Sky cafe has some new offerings but my palate still wanting more of the noodle soup over and over again. The only downside : They close on Thursday :( Wish they could open 7 days a week. Thanks for having such a great place to eat and to bring out of town guests for a good delicious indonesian comfort foods !

Terrible place to study!!! Trust me do not attempt! If you're a loud abnoxious 16 year old girl this is deffently the place for you. Noise levels ; never ending (open-close) any given day! If you want good, cheap indian food or just chill out with friends to drinks, deffently nice joint to check out. Studying = not possible

Ignore everyone who gave this less than 5 stars. They must hate great food. This is by far some of the best food I've had in Philadelphia, let alone Greek food. Every place you thought was a 10, well they go to 11. It's now our favorite place. Hummus is spectacular, shrimp pil pil was just flavorful and tender, pan fried scallops cooked to perfection, meatballs just delicious beyond belief and rice pudding to die for. Better yet, it's a BYOB that doesn't break the bank. Friendly staff as well. Update - went there a second time and just as delicious as the first. Our only regret is that we waited this long to try. 11 stars

Ever since I found this Thai food truck I try and get there once a week. Their food is authentic and always made fresh. My favorites here are the duck fried rice, green curry, beef short rib soup and the crab rangoon. Go see their friendly staff, you won't be disappointed!

Went here for dinner last night. Food was very delicious. I ordered the drunken noodles which were delicious and my girlfriend got the pad Thai which was also really good. For an appetizer, we got the crab dumplings. They were delicious, but for $7, I would've liked a bigger portion. Parking for this place was not a problem this time, but as other Yelpers mentioned, parking is limited and I could see it being a problem on busier nights. Overall good experience.

Came a few times and basically always the same experience over and over. Slow service and food is never consistant. One time, I ordered chicken curry. The chicken curry was on the extremely salty side but the rice and beans balanced it out. Next time...ordered the oxtail. Oxtail flavor was delicious, but not cooked long enough, so it was knawing to try and get the meat off. The rice was way way way beyond peppery. Third and final time was jerk chicken. Jerk chicken was ok. Needed a lil more flavor. But the sides were HORRIBLE! Mac n cheese was not cheesy and bland. The rice was actually really good this time. If you want good carribean food..just go about two trucks down! :-)
I love this place! I definitely recommend their buffet but if not some of my favorite dishes include their: tandoori chicken, chicken tikka masala, and vindaloo.

Have not had a disappointing meal here. My all-time favorite is the Turkey Waldorf sandwich, but today I went for the lobster reuben (with those highly-addicting homemade chips subbed for the fries) and have to give it a solid two thumbs up. Service is friendly and capable. But I'm withholding a star because today there were a number of pesky flies that we had to swat away constantly.

My family has been going to this restaurant for years and I still love it. This is not your typical Chinese restraunt. The food tastes better and seems like fresher ingredients are used. For example, rice is actually a natural fried brown color (not dyed yellow like at other Chinese restaurants). The atmosphere is also a lot nicer and it is decorated tastefully. They also have a variety of awards displayed on the wall and don't fall short of their reputation. My favorite dishes are the Soft Noodle Cantonese, the Vietnamese rice noodle lo mein, and the sweet and sour chicken.

Good ambiance & great Indian/Bangladeshi food. The owner is an awesome gentleman. Try the buffet, many items & they constantly serve fresh food. If you like less spicy food, eat here. Ate here many times. One of my fav places.
A waiter was very friendly. I liked the relaxing atmosphere. Green curry was excellent.

We tried half the menu here! The staff was so friendly and accommodating. The food was good, but only one "wow" dish in our opinion. The winner was the Soto Medan, which had a great unique combination of flavors! We also tried the fried dough, the pork platter (2nd fav of the night), and the Mie Komplit. We didn't love one of the overwhelming flavors of the mie komplit and wouldn't order it again. Our food came with rice and two soups as well. The restroom was a major issue for my boyfriend. You could barely sit without your knees touching the wall and the sink was only like 10-12" We'd come back for the soto medan and pork platter and maybe check out what other yelpers liked best (we've found that yelpers know what's up!), but it won't be one of our frequent stops.

The best Vietnamese hoagies around. There are some others that are close. But these are my favorites. The pork and chicken are great. The tofu is also really good. I even order TOFU. So that is saying something. The little couple that work there are adorable, and the place is the size of a juicebox. They are not super fast, but they are certainly delicious! I can eat one as an appetizer or put down two if I am feeling no shame. Hey, if 2 sandwiches only cost $7 total, they are considered one lunch in my book.

I like this place much better than Heng's Thai down the pike because of the fact that I'm not paying exorbitant amounts of money for the same quality food. Their lunch special is extremely cheap, and though your two appetizers are small, your entree more than makes up for that. The last time that I went I received drunken noodles instead of what I ordered, but hey, their drunken noodles were delicious so I wasn't complaining. The waitresses are extremely polite and attentive, so that my glass was never empty either. I'll lean 4 on this one given how few other Thai options there are around here.
Went their during lunch.food was better than average.alittle salty but thats something i have to compromise when go out to eat.
Great Thai restaurant, heavy on the flavor and the heat. I had the panaang curry while passing through STL and have no complaints.

I love Philly's food carts and this one definitely makes my list of favorites. I've been there several times and have enjoyed my experience every time. Their chicken wings are to die for. Fried to crispy perfection and juicy and meaty in the middle. Best combo ever. Also having just come back from a vacation in Jamaica, I can tell you their jerk chicken is fairly authentic flavoring, on top of being a fiery delicious treat. And their sides cannot be beat. Their mac and cheese, while not as "cheesy" as expected, is soooo tasty. I always contemplate skipping the meal and just eating a huge side of the stuff. Yams and collard greens are also pretty solid. Unfortunately, they're a little pricey, with $8 being on the low end for the their dishes. However, expect to have leftovers! I usually make two meals of their large size. If you're just looking for a quick lunch and go, this is not your place. But if you're looking for a unique double lunch, stop on by! Pros: authentic flavors, huge portions Cons: price, wait time (sometimes) Dishes to try: Chicken Wings, Jerk Chicken, MAC AND CHEESE Dishes to skip: None

I hate that I enjoy their food so much. It is always so hard to order and get the right things. I try to order the dinner special of sesame chicken without the rice, though apparently that's not possible. I asked if I could have the rice on the side and that's not an option either. Instead I had to pay $10+ for what I thought was only chicken. Fine. They delivered and it was half full with broccoli, when I said I just wanted chicken. There was the same amount of chicken as my husband got in his dinner special. I called to try to replace it and had to argue with 4 people about it. I eventually had to drive it back there and demanded my money back. Great food if you can take it the way it comes.

My husband ordered the chicken pita and I tried the pork pita. We were both very disappointed in the quality of the meat--old-tasting and chewy-- and no flavor at all. We both experienced stomach issues later this evening.

I love Thai food. Enjoyed Thai 5 very much. Love the pad Thai and fresh rolls. Shrimp were plentiful and the peanut sauce delicious. Staff is very friendly. Would definitely recommend this food truck.

The Best Soup and Egg rolls, I have to stop in every time I am in town......SO GOOD. Definitely worth the trip. Don't be alarmed it isn't a dead mall but the food is extraordinary, not to mention it is family owned and operated. I like to support local company and not a chain

It was suggested that I try this place for the Bahn Mi. What a great suggestion. The rolls are made to the owners specs at a local bakery and this is the only place you can get them. Once you have this roll, all others will pale in comparison. Great flavor, texture and structure. The meats and veggies were great too, I had the roast pork.

Not wanting Japanese, Italian, Mexican, good old Yelp lead us to this Afghani restaurant. The layout is a little strange - the front is more for take out but up the stairs in the back, is a small, cozy restaurant. Sansom is obviously a very popular eatery for the locals and after a few bites of our meals, we could tell why! The Afghani bread was so addictive, we asked for another basket and they had no problem accommodating us fatties. The menu is very vegetarian friendly, which was fortunate for my girlfriends. Being the carnivore, I couldn't help myself go with a lamb curry-like dish. The lamb melted in my mouth, it was very aromatic and I nearly died of a food coma at the end. You will leave this place feeling very full and happy. Do your belly a favor and eat here!

India Palace is far from authentic, but overall ordinary Indian Americanized-dishes that we all love. Their buffet is pretty good with 6 vegetarian options and 6 non-veg options. They have a salad and dessert bar. If you frequent regularly don't forget the frequent eater card that they stamp, fill the card and get a free lunch. Food: 3/5 Location: 3/5 Service: 3/5

There weren't many reviews for this restaurant but I wanted to give it a try. I only ordered steamed brown rice and wonton soup. The wonton soup was not good at all. The wontons were hard around the edges and the broth lacked flavor. The rice was good but then again it's brown rice. Service was good. Lots of vegetarian options that are Asian inspired. Overall, not a good choice for a simple meal but maybe other dishes are good.

Tangelo's Grille is located in the quaint little town of Gulfport. They are a block away from the water. The restaurant is clean and the atmosphere is soothing. The service is great but the main event, the food was not so great. Their pulled pork was tasty but some of the pieces were burnt. They should pull the burnt parts off the meat before serving it to their customers. Now to the rice and beans; I think I should have left them my recipe for black beans under the candle that was on our table. Maybe I just should have had a Cuban. I would not recommend this restaurant for the true lovers of authentic Spanish cuisine.

Great! Our waiter was super nice -- I forgot to tell him I had a peanut allergy before he brought out our food and he brought us out new food without us even asking. It made my night. The meatball pho is great - try the avocado bubble tea!

Is hard-to-find if you don't look for it. It's in the corner by a tire place. It is well worth it to find this place. I went because of the Yelp good reviews. I was not disappointed. I took two buddies and they also had a great experience. I ordered a Boba Ice-T for the very first time and relished in the taro and boba balls in my drink. The drinks were a little pricey @ 3.50. The dishes were hot tasty and plentiful for lunch. My friends had a pho dish and another had a Thai curry, both were extremely delicious and very satisfied. They adjust the spice level. The place was well attended but had seating for the lunch crowd as they have inside and outside seating. I would come back and try and another dish at this place. They can make any dish with tofu.

My favorite Indian food in Tucson! I can't believe I drove past this place for three years without knowing what I was missing. But thanks to yelp I tried it out and loved it. Their chicken tikka masala is creamy and delicious and their beef vindaloo is so tender. I recommend both. The sauce is so good I could just eat that with rice. Their garlic naan is also very good.
A wonderful family owned restaurant. Delicious and nutritious food that's good for the soul. Great service as well!
The food is good but this restaurant doesn't seem clean. I saw some kind of animal droppings staining the bathroom and hallway to the bathroom.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: My husband and i enjoy having lunch here. One of our favorite places in Reno. Paul is a very creative chef and the food is always fresh.

I've only been here once and there is a reason why. I like all kinds of international food, especially Indian and Vietnamese, so I was excited to give this place a try, but disappointed shortly after arriving. Perhaps I just don't care for Ethiopian cuisine, but it definitely left something to be desired. My guest and I ordered the sampler plate, which came out with 8 different piles of various stews and injera. The tastes of the stew were quite odd and not something I wanted to keep eating. The service was fairly slow. Food was pretty expensive, probably because they are one of the only Ethiopian places around. If you're feeling extremely adventurous, give it a try, but I likely won't be back again.

I thought I wrote a review for this awhile ago, but apparently not. In my walking around, stopped by this spot numerous occasions, they serve La Columbe coffee-that is a Plus!!! Lots nice little tables, people on their laptops, newspapers. Nice & quaint. Usually have nice variety of pastries, sandwiches & light fare!!! Stopped by again Sunday, but it was late, majority of items were pretty much sold out. But I will be back!! Yum!!!

Small, a bit dusty a good selection of sweets and pastries and a reasonable array of spices & sauces. Some homemade stuff and single-serving foods and snacks. I'm not much of an expert on Indonesian food but I like that there's something more interesting available than your average corner store. Cosigning that the owner (or older guy working there) is honest - he caught an expired package I brought up.

Sorry Spiro's I didn't want to say anything bad but I had to speak up so hopefully you can get back to business. I guess the owner has been absent the last few times and the food was great and bad. The special was great Sea Bass and the Greek food but the lamb chops portions was so small it was like not ever a bite (two). The apps were terrible and the cheese was so overdone it was like a brick. The waitress was horrible and spent more time talking to friends and forgot the service. Not only did she forget us and ruined the food, I could get her attention to pay the bill. I love to see the ownership there to correct the ship!

This place sucks. We ordered food for delivery. While it showed up faster than the time quoted the food was ice cold. We had to reheat it ourselves. I had maybe 3 pieces of chicken in my kung pao chicken. There was no crab to be found in the crab rangoon. My bf got chicken and hot garlic sauce which had abt 4 pieces of chicken in it. They charged us 3 extra dollars each for egg drop soup which is high since most other places charge 1.00. It was so tasteless and gross that we tried to give it to our dogs who refused to eat it as well. Will never go here again
Was excited to try the Korean fried Chicken. It was just ok. I think they put too much sesame oil on it. Would have been way better otherwise.
The food is excellent! I usually go with the $5 special, the brown stew chicken is outstanding, jerk chicken is tasty. So far it's been a hit, so much I go every Friday

My favorite place for Thai food in Tampa! Originally a food truck, Thai 5 has only gotten better. The restaurant is small but always busy with people eating or picking up to-go. The staff is always welcoming and remembers returning customers. Food wise, everything I've had has been amazing! Some of my favorites include the green curry with crispy tofu, tom yum soup, drunken noodles and panang curry. They also adjust the heat to your interest.

Overpriced place. The new management includes a sneaky 3% "service charge". It's ok to charge a tip..but the way they behave when asked is a little shady. Food's alright but not worth the price at all Dissappointment.

My first and still favorite vietnamese hoagie. I interned right around the corner from here and it was definitely the best eats around for someone on a tight budget. I always got it with chicken and was amazed at the harmony of textures and flavors- crispy bread, tender carrots, and some delicious sauce (no idea what it is, but I don't question). Still wish I was close enough to eat here all the time!

RIPOFF I should have listened to the review here from a year ago when it said that the seafood dish had very little seafood. That was extremely accurate. I ordered the sizzling seafood @ $18.95, with mild spiciness. I received an extremely bland, flavorless dish consisting of one small, overcooked lobster tail, two small shrimp, one piece of calamari and 6 tiny fingernail size scallops. You've GOT to be kidding me. Part two of the ripoff occurred when I presented my Groupon (expired, but the base amount is still supposed to be accepted by the merchant since it was hard money and not the promotional amount) and the restaurant refused to accept it, saying they had severed their ties to Groupon. Doesn't matter, they had agreed to ALWAYS accept the base amount of the coupon. The restaurant was a major disappointment on many levels. Needless to say, I won't be back and I will warn my friends. You can find much better Thai at honest restaurants within a couple of miles of this place.
I like their Gang Dang chicken . Their mild is spicy enough for me. This is our place for Thai food.
Very interesting place to bring the kids for dinner. You eat strange foods with your hands in a very friendly comfortable atmosphere. We love adventures in dining so this would be great if do too!
This is hands down the best Italian restaurant I have ever eaten at !! Everything is homemade, service was wonderful , and I can hardly wait to go back!

My fiancé and I love this place. The food is delicious with very generous portions..we always have to take some home. The service is great. The owner, Nick, is extremely accommodating and very helpful. It is also nice that it's a byob. We will absolutely continue to come back for the excellent food, service, and atmosphere!

This is so hard ! I have been in the area and saw this tiny little shop with Vietnamese hoagies. Great, I stopped by to get one on Saturday. I was greeted by a smiling man who opened the door for me. Polite right? I said I was hungry and he pointed to the sign on the wall. I think they were all under $5. I picked the pork. He made my sandwich. Crispy chewy bread, crunchy veggies and sweet pork. The problem? I KNOW he did not wash his hands when he made my sandwich. The place is small. You can see everything they do! Oh Man! I didn't complain because I'm tired of complaining and that might have made it worse, you never know with people. Do I want to go back for the veggie? Um, yes and no. Food safety is a must in my book. Therefore, buyer beware. Its yummy, but is it worth it? Three stars for EH-OK.

Zaikka is in one of the rows of stores in Center Pointe Plaza. This restaurant is rather like an Indian version of Chipotle. Their main offering is a choice of rice or bread, a choice of meat/tofu, a choice of curry, and any number of toppings you like. Put the four together and you have a meal. They also have a few side items and a separate "street food" menu, which I didn't try this time. All in all, it's a good variety. I thought the spicy toppings and curries were decently spicy, while the mild items were less spicy but still had flavor. I would not expect authentic Indian food here but I'd take it for what it is: a clean, fast, and no-fuss place to get something a lot more interesting than the usual fast food.

Good grief...this man is not a falafel nazi, he is a falafel god! Finally made it here the other day (birthday falafels, holla!) and I was not at all disappointed. I waited in line (hubby and 3 yr old in tow) for about 15 minutes. When we got up to the cart, falafel man was very engaging and chatted it up with my little guy (who just stared and smiled, as I'm pretty sure he had no idea what he was saying). So, about 2 minutes later, we had 2 platters (1 vegetarian) and were excited to dig in. The veg platter had about 8 falafel balls, some sort of amazing greens, a rice/chick pea/curry mix, fruit (yes! diced apples, blackberries, and grapes), grilled peppers, a generous dousing of hummus all over, a giant hunk of multigrain bread, and a roll. Did I mention it was only $8??? Hubby's had a ton of chicken and 4 falafel balls as well as everything I had, minus the fruit. Guess he doesn't look like a fruit guy. Everything was gobbled up (even my 3 yr old enjoyed the fruit, falafel and bread) and thoroughly enjoyed! Amazing. Can't wait to go back.
Unbelievable food. Plenty of gluten free options. Can't recommend it enough.

Usually I don't stray far from Pho when I find a good one and Asian Pho has good enough pho. The broth is ok but I wouldn't say it's my favorite...yet it's their lunch special that's outstanding and has my hubby and I repeating our business there! Whether or not you're getting it to go or eating in, or even actually during their lunch special or not, their "Traditional Vietnamese Charbroiled Dishes, specifically the Flame broiled Shrimp and Pork is something everyone has got to try at least once! Now, as I have said before, I feared to stray from the pho, but my hubby told me I had to try it so I decided to roll with the punches and order what he was ordering! A heaping bowl of Vermicelli noodles, piled high with flame broiled pork and shrimp, veggies like cucumbers, carrots and beans sprouts, with crushed peanuts and a "special" sauce... this is crisp, refreshing and down right tasty! I wish I could replicate their special sauce... The fresh vegetables pair well with the savory meats and the way it's all put together is unique and playful. Definitely something different to try than the usual pho! It is a good thing, However, that the food is so good because as mentioned before customer service is hit and miss. They always seem like they're un-interested or maybe even annoyed by the patronage which is off putting. I suggest ordering over the phone and getting it to go.

Wow great gyro's. They fill them soo big that you have to take some home. They even told me if I wanted to make one later they would put all the fixings on the side. Super nice. They do catering too. They will sell just the meat. They have other deli items, too. I have been to others but they were over the top nice. I will definitely be back and soon. I saved part of mine and had it for breakfast.

I have to admit, I was a bit skeptical trying this place. I don't live too far from the restaurant and noticed it was always empty. However, my partner had been really wanting to try it - so we went. I must admit, I was wrong! This place was delicious! The service was fast, our waitress was polite and the food was amazing. I went on a Wednesday night, and there was only one other table there. Check this place out if you are looking for something different.

La Va has some good selections of pastries and stuff. Apparently the cheesecake is banging. The coffee isn't bad either, although it ain't cheap. The sandwiches are really good and they have some Israeli specialties, including Israeli coffee, which are not to be found everywhere. My problem with ths place is similar to Jake's-- they offer wi-fi but kick you out after a half hour. I understand the logic of this to some degree...I know the old milk a cup of joe for hours routine, but it doesn't lend itself to a comfortable place to work. Which is what I'm looking for in a coffeeshop. I WILL spend cash (I figure overall, it works out to be cheaper than renting an office) but I don't like being rushed.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We've tried two of the Indian restaurants in town now (Taj Mahal and Madhuban) - and Taj Majal wins our vote, hands down. First off - the decor and customer service is second to none. We've only been here a few times (twice for dinner and once for lunch), and the owner already recognizes us. The dining room has a living-room quality to it - super comfortable and inviting. The menu is big, but does a great job of explaining each dish - I always have a tough time deciding what to order. There's a decent beer selection, and the hot herbal tea is awesome, a great accompaniment to the food. Ah...the food. If they're busy, it does take a while to prepare, but it's worth the wait. Order naan as an appetizer so you have something to nibble on while you're waiting for your entrees. We've tried the plain, garlic, and chili naans, and love them all (though I wish they'd try using roasted garlic, rather than chopped). The chutney variety provided for dipping is excellent as well. The main entrees can be a little on the oily side, which is something that I've noticed at every Indian restaurant I've visited - 2 in Boise, 1 in San Francisco - so it might be a normal thing...? Regardless, they taste amazing. The levels of spice are exactly to my liking (hot but not too hot), and the basmati rice is good enough to stand on its own!! I always make sure to leave enough for a lunch the next day - the flavors are even better then. If you love spice, or are even remotely curious about Indian food - please stop by. You won't regret it!

I have been to this restaurant twice (once for lunch, once for dinner) and both times I experienced horrible service. At lunch, they only had one waitress for the entire place. For dinner, the waiter forgot to bring us things that we ordered. The only reason I'm giving this place two stars is that it's cute and the food is decent...but it's not enough to get me to go back again.

Went to Scannicchio's with my dad for dinner this summer. I grew up as part of a large italian family with lots of good cooks, so I definitely have a preconceived notion of what my typical traditional meal should be like. This place is exactly what I am looking for in a real south Philly italian restaurant. We came early (5:30) on a week night, and the only other customer was an old italian man who looked to be about 85. The host greeted us warmly and even got our names as we were seated. We opened a nice bottle of red (byo) and settled in for a great meal. We started out with the fresh bread, some broccoli rabe, and my dad had the stuffed artichoke (excellent and very traditional) and I had the special: tower of grilled eggplant, tomatoes, fresh mozzarella with balsalmic- amazingly good. Being a huge eggplant fan I tried the eggplant parm for dinner which was also delicious, but my dad's meal was truly the standout: stuffed calamari in a red sauce. The calamar tasted exactly the way that my grandmother used to make it for the holidays, it really brought my dad back to his childhood. The flavors were great, the sauce very rich with the flavors of the seafood. It was a treat eating this meal that we usually reserve for Christmas eve. After finishing our wine, the manager brought out some of his homemade pineapple-cello which i could not get enough of. So delicious. I was happy that I didn't have to drive us home. I would definitely recommend this place for a great traditional italian meal. I was hoping to eat here on New Year's eve but they are completely booked- will just have to come back another night...

Oh gosh, I adore this little place, especially for lunch. Their lunch menu is a steal of a deal with every option being about $13 and which includes lemongrass soup, spring rolls, one entree and rice. My go-to option here is the green curry with bamboo shoots (I've tried both beef and chicken) but all of the options are great! Additionally they have quite extensive vegetarian options on the menu which is great! You can tell that it is a family owned restaurant by the care that it put into setting the tables and otherwise working at all sorts of tasks. A child was helping with some of these tasks and she seemed to be doing a rather good job while we were there during my last visit. I don't go here nearly often enough. I really ought to visit more frequently.

We've been here a few time in a month. .food is good and decent price BUT SERVICE IS TERRIBLE. .especially the kid who works here....never seen him smile. .we always order the lunch special. .BUT NEVER once automatically bring us the soda that comes with it ..we've we ask about it..it's like seriously look on their face.....luv the food ..but service SUCK!!!
Everything my table ordered was spectacular! The spring rolls, calamari and pork belly lollipops were amazing!
