One of the best places to eat at UCSB but still not that good.. don't get the falafel, nobody likes it. I recommend the chicken; most people like the gyros but I'm not a fan. Good prices.

Came here for birthday dinner and was pleasantly surprised by the food and the ambience. Unfortunately, service was nice but extremely slow due to just one poor waiter running around the whole restaurant.

My wife and I paid a visit to this place because we were looking for something close by. To me sushi is sushi just like a burger is a burger. While the food, drink and ambiance was nothing really noteworthy, what was great was the service. They were attentive, courteous and timely.
I love this place. The staff is friendly. The sambussa was amazing. The honey wine was delicious. Everything was wonderful. I highly recommend this restaurant.

The Lunch menu is a super Value plus the quality makes it even better.The chicken parmigiana perfect mix with the sauce and the mozzarella cheese awesome with a side of linguine perfecto.Ive never had a bad meal. Parking is the only issue definitely give it a shot you will not be disappointed.

Being an Indian I am extra critical about Indian food..came here based on reviews and did not leave disappointed! Warm friendly greeting upon entering..deep rich Indian flavor aromas...fast and friendly service! Ordered chai , chicken tikka masala and the Thai fish curry all of which was extremely flavorful to my surprise!!! An overall affordable and pleasant experience! One of the staff also showed us the banquet hall which was also quite nice despite the unusual path we took to get there! Great for Indian parties for sure! I would definitely come back for more!!!

Addictingly decadent lehmajun. I've had both fresh and frozen and they're both perfect after 45 seconds in the toaster oven. Each pita is the perfect serving size for a snack or a part of a meal. With ten at a time, the price is right, too.

A very good North Indian restaurant. I took one star off because (a) the bathroom has somewhat dirty and (b) one of the chutneys was in the beginning stages of becoming spoiled. Other than that, the food and service was excellent. This is based on a dinner experience.

This restaurant deserves an award for the top notch Middle Eastern food they serve all year round. This has been my GO TO spot for years now and they never fail to put a smile on my face. I can never get enough of their Friday specials and their MEAT STEW is to DIE FOR. Nothing makes me happier then when i know they made a fresh plate of KNAFA with exxxxxtra syrup . If you ever need to grab a delicious plate of food on the go they'll have it ready for you in no time. FRESH FAST FOOD can not get better than this. Gordon Ramsey aint got nothing on this restaurant !!!
Excellent place! Great food & flavors. They weren't too busy when we went..but the kitchen was backed up...seems strange but it was worth the wait!

After we parked around South Grand, my crew decided to go to here instead of King of I because it was a block closer, but I don't think we'll be lazy bums again after learning our lessons from Basil Spice. Food: A few hits and a lot of misses -Appetizers: the Satay Gai was good -My friends ordered the generic stuff like simple Pad Thai/Curry/Stir Fry and they weren't pleased. I tasted one of their noodles dish and it completely lacked flavor as well as moisture. I can usually tolerate a lot of food but that was just gross. -I decided to venture out of my comfort zone (aka ordering Pad Thai at every Thai place I go to). I got the Rahd Na (stir fried baby corns, broccoli, and carrots in soybean gravy sauce. Served over stir fried rice noodles with black soy sauce), and the flavor was just right and made my daily intake of veggies go down easy. -Desserts: SKIP THE DESSERTS. Seriously, SKIP THE DESSERTS! I was looking forward to my Khao-Nuea Sunka-Ya (steamed sweet sticky rice with coconut milk topped with Thai egg custard) and Glua Hom Sa-Bai (fried banana crepe) because they sounded really good in descriptions and I usually have good experiences with Thai desserts. However, I was super disappointed when my dessert plates came up. I felt like a kid who was expecting a giant/delicious black forest cake but got a tiny gross muffin instead. The fried banana crepe was literally just banana in egg roll wrap with some honey on top, nothing special at all. The steamed sweet sticky rice dish was sweet in a disgusting way, and the egg custard on the side looked like a pile of poo and tasted like play-do. Service: -Nice people, but also VERY SLOW people. Our server was also a bit forgetful and forgot about the chicken dumplings we ordered so now we'll never know what they taste like since we don't plan on going back again.

Super tasty. The broth was flavorful and I'm happy that such a good spot is so close and to me. I don't have to drive all the way to Philly for good pho anymore! I had #16 pho, and the tendon was flavorful as were the brisket and steak.

Meh.... We ordered delivery and it took a very long time. Apparently, they had "driver issues". The gal who delivered the food was very nice and apologetic. The food was just OK. It wasn't awful except the fresh rolls which were anything but. The lettuce inside looked and tasted like it belonged in the garbage. It was sloppy and wilted. Just nasty. The Pad Thai was dry, but in their defense, most of the sauce had sunk to the bottom. However the beef in peanut sauce was very good tasting even if the sauce could use a bit of thickening. Overall, not good nor bad.

I've only been here once. Got a couple breakfast sandwiches that were pretty good. The bread was fresh, but they add a spicy mayo sauce that I didn't know about and that completely ruined my egg & cheese sandwich :( other than that it was pretty standard breakfast.

Decor atmosphere and condiments not at level they should be. Please don't bring me a condiment bottle with s&@; all over the top. Service was decent, pretty well versed on menu. Main reason to go out. FOOD. It was above average. I am know oriental expert. But I would give it 2 fingers up. Ingredients were fresh. Cooked well good portions and tasty. Def return spot

My niece went to college in st pete so when i come to town i always go to Dooners..(it was also my niece's go-to in college). I was starving today and went 20 minutes out of my way to have lunch here. I ordered a falafel bowl (i usually order the falafel sandwich). This was the worst falafel i have EVER had. Hell, it wasn't even a falafel. It was some flat orangish color patty..it almost tasted like breaded deep fried egg. This is not at all a falafel. I brought it back in and asked about it and they said they would make me the usual sandwich that i get if i was unhappy with it. I explained that i was puzzled by the falafel. The sandwich they made for me came and it was the same. Really bazaar. You cannot asvertise falafel and gove something tjat does not even resemble a falafel and has no texture or even the dame ingredients of a falafel. I am not sure why they have changed this food staple but never again will i come here. So disappointed and nausea after that weird dining experience.

I really love this place. This is the place I take newcomers to when we eat out in Media. It has reasonable prices (the lunch option is a bargain!) and great service. The food is delicious. It is not the best Thai I've ever had (Circles Contemporary downtown is my favorite!), but it is really good. The noodles are delicious. Thy also have LOTS of vegetarian options which is great! Definitely try Noddi Thai if you're in Media!

This restaurant is incredible. The owner is a sweet man who genuinely remembers customers and the food is far superior to most local Indian places. The lunch special is out of this world! Less than $15 per person for a huge amount of food - I had a samosa, rice, goat curry, a small bowl of delicious spicy lentils that reminded me of chili, a small sweet ball that I didn't know what it was, and a yogurt desert. The goat curry is creamy and delicious, and whatever those lentils were - sign me up for more! All in all, even coming very hungry I left with a little doggie bag and a happy stomach. I definitely will be coming back for lunch more and more often!

Buel puri was not fresh, medu vada was ok but sambar had no flavor and was very watery, chutney was not good. A blind man could have made a better chutney and sambar, chicken tikka was also average. Save your time and money. Try another place

THIS IS MY GO TO SPOT!!!! I go here all the time and that's no exaggeration!!! I love the staff and the locals that have become friends and/or family. When u go there u get that lounging cooling vibe along with a lil club scene from time to time!!!! AIMEE is the bestest bartender in the Bills. Mess with her u may lose some friends...lol Nah but Aimees my girl and the loves everyone and is the coolest. She's been there since I started going there and 1 of the main reasons I go and also to talk about her lol monkey. But the rest of the crew and staff Yunis, See, Jay, Soapy, Elece, Tanya, Kelly, Ginny (prolly spelled that wrong) r amazeballs and are some of the coolest people you'll meet!!!

It has been years since I've had a chance to go to a Vietnamese restaurant (since we left Chicago back in 2005). Saigon here in Indy does not disappoint. Only 15 min drive from our house too. For our first trip we tried (based off the previous yelp reviews) the Vegetable egg rolls (good) the grilled pork rolls (delicious++) my wife had the tofu curry (delicious) and I got the super bowl pho special (really really good and tons of food for $4 more). It was too much food and we had to bring the leftovers home. I also had the coconut bubble tea. I will most definitely be trying out the different flavor bubble teas on subsequent revisits (yes we WILL be back). Service was quick and efficient. They even provided a plastic bag which he placed my pho container into. They do not take Amex so paid w/ Visa. We were there for exactly an hour. Could've spent less time had the wife brought her reading glasses for the menu. They do have a menu online (see their Web site link above) so next time we're going to go in prepared with our order so we don't have to waste time w/ the menu.

Horrible food! The service was very slow even though we were the only ones there. Came here because we heard the good reviews. Wouldn't ever come back again!!! The bhel was too sweet, the samosa chat tasted weird and the dhaba chicken should be called spineless chicken.

So glad there's a place on this side of the bay that has good banh mi. Whenever I craved for banh mi in the past, I had to drive to Tampa for one, but now I go to Seasons, a cute and clean little deli in Pinellas Park. Aside from the banh mi, I also like the milk tea here. It's not as good as ones I've had in Atlanta, but definitely the best around here. The chicken curry noodle soup is very good. I definitely recommend this item. I've also had the quail and they're quite good. Unfortunately, the pad thai and pho leaves little to be desired. The pad thai has too much pad thai sauce and the pho is pretty bland. I'm very picky about my pho and this does not pass the test. Keep in mind before you go here that the menu is quite limited. But if you love banh mi, I know you'll love it here.
The food was just as tasty this time around, and the staff was much more welcoming. I do like it here. I'll keep coming back :)

The food was really good. What won me over was their friendly service. We visited the restaurant on a weekend evening, and were happy to have thought ahead for a change and made a reservation as it was packed! We entered with 3 kids - 2 in strollers and they didn't make a face and ask us to put the strollers away as it was a full house. They were really friendly and didn't mind the commotion the kids were creating. They also brought out the cake (we arranged for it before hand) and were happy and smiling while doing it! The food was good. Large portions, reasonably priced and well presented and full of flavour. Their menu looked real good, and will definitely be going back to try more!
Good Jamaican food. Lived in Jamaica for 2+ years and this is close to what would get there. Great outside space during the summer.

I wish I didn't even have to give a star service was absolutely terrible due to the long waiting time , the sumbusa with beef had an awful taste as though the meat was old. The injera has a strong vinegar smell it has my stomach in a knot , the only thing that tasted fair was the eggs and chicken & lentils. The cabbage made my daughter throw up due to the fermented buttery flavor , it was an experience for sure . Extremely overpriced it should be $15-20 for the entire plate for the party to share not per person it was small portions of samples . Proceed with caution good luck.

After hearing raves about Tangelo's Cuban Sandwiches I stopped in. I was not impressed as it was mediocre and over pressed. I might go back and try something else, but with other great restaurants in Gulfport, I might not.

This is a small storefront restaurant in River Ridge near Manguno. It was difficult to find in the dark. I wasn't sure what to do when we walked in. There were about a dozen tables and a bar, two couples at tables and a single waiting at the bar. Cheerful upbeat Latin music was playing. There were half a dozen TV screens or monitors on the walls cycling through pictures of New Orleans, beach, mountain and city scenes from, I assume, Trinidad and Venezuela. Along the left wall was a buffet. It looks like they have a liquor license since they sell rum drinks. We sat down and waited for several minutes before the woman behind the buffet came over and explained the menu, which was pretty limited. Apparently they always have the buffet, at lunch and dinner. The buffet contents were some small cornbread griddle cakes, that they melt cheese on top of if you ask, chicken soup, marinated beef brisket and paella. They were out of the beans at 6 on a Saturday night, but fried up some plantains in place of the beans. The beef was very tasty, one of the owners said they marinate it and slow cook it until it's very tender. The paella had mussels, sausage and chicken, that I could see, but not much else in the way of seafood or meat, and a bit too salty as well as the rice being dried out. I really liked the idea of a Venezuelan restaurant and wanted to like it, but for me to enjoy it I want to know more about the food of the country, what the typical dishes are and how they are cooked. The menu needs a much wider selection of dishes, explanation of what they are, and a Saturday night buffet should be a showcase for the cuisine, rather than a way to cut down on staff and make customers serve themselves. $17 for a very limited menu of soup, beef, rice and plantains isn't interesting enough to hold my interest.

I wasn't too impressed with this place. I ordere the Jerk chicken with rice and pea, and I will say the chicken was cooked perfectly, however, not what I would call jerk sauce. It was more of a spicy BBQ sauce. My boyfriend ordered the same with mac and cheese as a side. The mac and cheese has no cheese. Just some dried chesse on top and they rest seemed like butter noodles. I probably won't go back. Its good if you want a break from pizza and chinese and want a good meal, but def won't go if i'm in the mood for Jamaican. I would rather take the drive to People's Choice in west Trenton.

Love, love, love this little gem. My family and I always bring visitors from out of town to this restaurant. The food never disappoints. If you are lucky enough to go and find a patio table overlooking the water it is so sweet. The only complaint I would have is the music played on the weekends distracts people from the scenery and the delicious food. It is too loud. I have eaten here and watched dolphin play in the water next to the patio. Check this place out!
Picked up take out about a week ago. We opted for the drunken noodles with chicken, pineapple fried rice and crab puffs.

I'd give a 3.5 if I could . The food were definitely tasty but not worth waiting in the line tasty. Here is why: Tilapia burrito : the first time we went they were half hour away from closing time, so the only thing that were left was the burrito and chicken katsu. We ordered two burritos , one spicy and the other one non spicy. The spicy one was really tasty with the spicy mayo sauce and the portion is quiet large. But the non spicy ones were tasteless. Short rib taco: since we didnt get to try the tacos , we returned the second day for lunch. Again it was really tasty with the spicy mayo , i really like all the cabbage and avocado they put inside. However, the short rib was kind tough, by the end it was kind like eating beef jerky. Satay chicken : this one we did not enjoy it at all, it was a curry chicken that had too much curry flavor which over powered the spicy mayo sauce, we really didn't like this one. i'd like to try again their short rib taco someday when there isnt a line of people waiting.
Fantastic food and friendly staff. Loved the chicken kabobs.

I love food trucks and I love when they are awesome to scream about. When I was pregnant and too lazy to cook, this was my go to place to feed my starving hubby. Oh the jerk chicken is amazing as well as the oxtail. The collard greens are fresh and it is not can greens. The fried fish and chicken are delish. Fried and season to perfection. Perfect crunch when you bite into it. I love the rice and beans with a little gravy from the oxtail. Let's say I have tried almost everything and would recommend the this place.

We found this place via Groupon and we're definitely going back again. The prices were so low, we had to order the next day's lunch to take home to make it easier to use our whole Groupon. I had the Angry Bird St. Paul Sandwich. This is my first time having any sort of St. Paul sandwich. I would have tried the regular St Paul, but the photo on their web site of this sandwich really caught my attention. Not as spicy as the name suggests, but the flavor of the patty was just what I wanted. I should have looked for some Sriracha to top that. I have to believe that these sandwiches are their specialty - it really shows in the flavor. The crab rangoon is a triangle fold with only a moderate amount of filling, so you have to be careful how you eat it so you're not eating straight fried wonton. I do prefer star folded, just because it holds more filling, but these were decent. They also had some varieties I've never seen that I wanted to try - philly steak rangoon and that day's special was a pizza rangoon. The pork egg rolls had a very good amount of pork. Not too much, but more than I've seen anywhere before. The rice was just right. The stir fry dishes were sauced and seasoned well. I have not eaten mine yet, but my wife's sesame chicken was very good. Overall, it was a good amount of food for not a lot of money. They have a surprisingly large, but bottled/canned only, beverage selection. Everything from Jolly Rancher Soda to Chrysanthemum tea. The dining area does have tables now (as opposed to earlier reviews I'm seeing).

I've been to this restaurant over 5 times in the last 2 months. Food is freshly cooked, and the waiting may take 10-20 minutes depending on your order. But I tell you what, it was all worth it at the end.
Loved the shrimp red curry. It's BYOB! Great food great service. Cute spot for a date night

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: Not the best, not the worst either. I had some house special that was fried snapper filets or if you want the whole thing, you can just get the entire fish, in a chili-garlic sauce. Pretty good but not that spicy, but you can always get the spice tray. The other person had the red curry and it was really fresh. The past few times I was a bit let down but this visit was a lot better.

Really great, I hate to admit it as it is hard to get into as it is but to be fair I thought I would post. Nice variation of menu from the other Italian restaurants in Collingswood. Bring a nice bottle

The food is really good. Went there once and had the pad thai and thought it was delicious. I called ahead and took my order to go and it tasted fresh. The only reason I wouldn't give this restaurant 4 stars is because the second time I went, I ordered the same thing...and they told me they were out of pad thai. How do you run out of a staple at your new restaurant? Puzzling to me. The server offered me curry...which I don't eat so I just got up and left. When I go back next time I'm hoping they have s full stock of rice noodles. Returned a bunch of times and this place impresses me each time! Love thai legacy

We took our twin boys to Rosemary's on Friday after reading an article about it in a local paper. The boys LOVED the garlic bread and Mac and Cheese. My wife and I choose entrees from and Mediterranean Menu and really enjoyed it. We will be back!

I've been a quite a few times, used to be awesome! But now it's always just packed and loud, with slow service and cold food. Usually 1 person per 4 top table with their laptop trying to be hip and study, not sure how they can concentrate with the noise lol. Since the reno this place has gone down hill in my opinion. My last visit I waited about 30min for my drink that was actually not even made till i said something as it was lost in the frey... Little too big for your britches sorry to say! Think I'll try a different location!?

The fact that it says "craft fried chicken" should have clued me in. It's sad, because I wanted to enjoy this place. It looked very nice inside and out, and the staff was excellent. Unfortunately, that's the only reason I am giving it two stars. We shouldn't have ordered anything after tasting the mac and cheese - it was a very unexpected flavor that added nothing good to traditional mac and cheese. And this comes from someone who likes to experiment with flavors. But we wanted to give the place a chance. We ordered a pound of dark chicken tenders, fries, and a biscuit. The chicken was bland, the fries were salty enough to gargle with, and the biscuit was disappointing. The ketchup you get with the fries had a metallic flavor only. We couldn't finish our meal and will never return.

Decent gyros; super friendly owner. The lamb/beef shawarma slices are perfectly spiced and very tender. The portions of fries that come with the meals are fresh, hot and huge! We stop whenever we are in the neighborhood. And don't forget to grab a bite of their delicious baklava.
Love the food and the owners are delightful. Chicken Vindaloo and the Peshwari Salmon are our favorites!

A solid little Indian restaurant in Media. I've been twice and the food was good both times. My wife and I recently went for a lunch buffet special which was more expensive than most Indian restaurants' dinner buffets, so that was a little disappointing. If you don't feel like heading into Philadelphia and since there isn't an overabundance of Indian food in the area, this place is the best option I've found so far which may be why they can get away with charging a little bit more. The place was pretty crowded both times I've been.
This is my favourite Thai restaurant in Edmonton. The stir fry garlic pork is as addictive as crack. I would highly recommend.

The food here was gross. Just don't eat Southeast Asian cuisine in Indiana, especially if you have had the real thing. It's just disappointing. They did not even try with my noodle dish. The noodles I ordered were hard and fried. It was not supposed to be fried. It was also swimming in grease. I felt bad for recommending this place. I also came here due to the Yelp reviews, but I should know better from now on.
It's as good as it gets. I'm a pain to make soup for and they get it right every time. It is always full for a reason.
The owner is very interesting to talk to, and the food is great! The restaurant is very small and slightly cramped. Definitely will be back!

"The food is terrible and the portions are small." I don't remember what comedian said this but it is true of Vientiane. I hate dissing a small, locally owned place, but I've eaten here four times and the food just sucks. I can only figure that the people who have eaten here and like it have never had much Thai or Laotian food before. I always swear off this place but friends want to go and I don't want to be a pain in the ass. The last time I got carry out I had two bites and threw the rest away. Life is too short to eat Thai food that is this bad. The dishes are either flavorless or off flavor. All that and it is so overpriced.

Awesome Thai food. Their tofu is perfect - not fried to carbon, and not raw. I had an eggplant dish with red curry paste - bangin'. The only part of the meal that wasn't excellent was the veggie spring rolls appetizer. They reminded me of something you'd get in a subpar Chinese restaurant.
My go to place I always go here. Honestly the best Pho I've found in Goleta in comparison to the ones in LA.

I love this place!!!!!!! We were at Busch Gardens and wanted good food and we got it. The people were incredibly nice, best service ever for fast food. Then the good was amazingly delicious. Greek salad, gyro, chicken kabobs, chop chop salad, the French fries, and the shakes. All amazing. Whenever I'm in Tampa we will be stopping here!

I heard about this bakery but walked right by it as I was going to meet a friend. I'm glad that after our lunch she wanted to bring me here! The bakery was empty when we arrived and no one behind the counter but a woman popped head out from the doorway towards the back. I don't recall her saying anything and we browsed the baked goods as we waited for someone to help us. The young woman who helped us with helpful and gave us her recommendations. She also told us there was parking behind the building. There was also a free sample and it was yummy! I can't recall the exact name but it was like an apple torte. Next time I will buy that. My friend tried the almond croissant and recommended it. There were 3 so I bought one and she bought the other 2. I also bought macarons to share with others but I should have gotten other sweet treats as they were not my favourite. I ate half of the croissant the next morning but I didn't warm it up. It was a heavy instead of light and flaky and later that day I warmed it up and it tasted better and not so heavy. They also have ice cream that looked yummy too! There are two tables with chairs and reading materials. I likely wouldn't sit and eat but I'm often in the area for work so I'll definitely be back to get other sweet treats!

Good Mojitos and very good service....just didn't think the food was all that great. The Baked bread appetizer was cold and the fried avocado was not that good. The fish tacos were pretty bland. Compared to the competition this place doesn't stack up. A lot of other restaurants in the area to choose from.

This is a Gem of a place for "American Thai" Yea it isn't the authentic stuff but its VERY good and very well priced. My wife and I have came here for YEARS and honestly never had a bad time.. they play the same music OVER and OVER though lol but it is calming and sounds Thai. Small place but dont pass on it! We now moved to St Pete and STILL make the drive across Gandy bridge for this place sometimes..

First time trying Indian food, and this place didn't disappoint. I came here shortly after they opened for lunch. The place was nice, clean and tastefully/subtly decorated. As soon as I walked in, the aroma from the buffet made me even more hungrier than I was. The people were friendly and attentive. The buffet wasn't as large as some "typical" buffets, but it contained so many items that it didn't matter. I had Lemon Rice, Chili Goby Manchurian (stir fried cauliflower in a garlic ginger sauce), Chloe (chickpeas in North-Indian spices), Chicken Tikka Masala( which was moist and not dry) and Saag Paneer (homemade cottage cheese in a creamy spinach sauce). Everything was delicious, especially the Chloe. Let me just mention that I hated cauliflower as a kid and wouldn't touch it from my pre-teen years on. However, the Chili Gobi Manchurian looked so good, I had to try it. If my mom cooked cauliflower like this, it would have been one of my favorite vegetables. Trust me on that! If you've never experienced Indian food before or if you are a lover of it, give this place a try. The dishes I tried had just the right amount of spice and a ton of flavor.

Delicious, simple egg sandwiches with fresh bread. Fast service, cheap prices. What more could you ask for? Service isn't stellar and it sometimes is hard to hear and understand the people from the truck, but it doesn't faze me too much.
Amazing!! Consistently great food! Must try the chicken 65 and kabobs! Always on point! Great customer service and food!

I want to like this place but it's just too damn expensive for no reason. Came here with my sister ordered a yuenling lager $5 she ordered a mango juice $3.50, hookah $25, chicken skewers $14, and $9.50 for gratitude the bill came back $60.80 I didn't even eat. Hookah should never cost $25 period! And the food was small portions good but small, total rip off. I'll go somewhere else next time. Everything is just overpriced.

The location and appearance of the place are seriously lacking. Its basically part of a gas station with a few picnic tables. However looks can be deceiving. The food is great and the portions are huge! Half a chicken, rice, bean, and plantains for around $10. Easily one of the best place around Indy to get jerk chicken.

What a lucky stop. After spending the day (4 unexpected hours) in Nogales, we knew we needed to stop before heading back to the Phoenix area. I remember a busy shopping area north of Ina Rd in Marana. Trying a hunch we drived through and saw many of the typical chain places. I had mentioned Asian food to all four of the passengers and they didn't object and we landed, unexpectedly on a Monday evening at Chopstix in Marana. The place was mostly calm except there were a some tables in the process of being bussed as we arrived around 8p. Our party of 5 had to wait a bit before sitting, as it appeared they had a big crowd who had just exited before we got there. So, we sit and look at menus and don't know what to expect. I have had Asian food from great to terrible and I didn't know where this place was going to land on the chart. I should say, our group are all foodies and one is chef/owner of a great Tempe bistro. So, we can be snobs about our food. We ordered some appetizers and soups to try...lettuce wraps, egg rolls, wonton and hot and sour soup. A beer, some waters and some hot tea. For dinner, we ordered Kung Pao Chicken, Lo Mein, Orange Chicken and Sesame Chicken as we all plan to sample a little of everything. Our waitperson comes singing to our table and is the most happiest restaurant worker I have ever met. The manager also establishes a very cool vibe so things feel like this could turn out ok. Well, the appetizers come and as I say...the first bite in a restaurant on your first visit is the most important bite of all. And they were all very special bites. Everything was terrific, the lettuce and vegetables crisp, the frying oil...fresh, the appetizers were consumed quickly. We passed around the hot and sour soup with big chunks of mushroom and a wonderful warm, sour taste...perfect and enjoyed by all. I admit...I was very greedy with my wonton soup with the mini bok choy and the flavorful meatballs in the most delicate duplings...well seasoned and very chickeny. Wonderful. Since the business of the earlier evening had subsided, our main course offerings came quickly. Some of the best Asian food I can remember. The Sesame Chicken was lightly dusted and fried perfectly. The sauce was spot on...hot enough...but not overpowering. Rich without being over salty. I hear raves from the Kung Pao contingent and the orange chicken and lo mein is gobbled up gleefully as well. And all accompanied by an occassional tuneful classic rock song blasted out by our wait person and her lovely soprano voice. Again...happy people work here. We have no room for afters and we still have to box some of the portions as we need to get back home...but we do ask to speak to the manager to tell him what a wonderful experience he and his staff gave us at Chopstix. The place is a great step up from the normal asian inspired places that dot many a shopping area. This place cannot be missed. Go...as soon as you can....drive the 80+ miles that we will drive again to taste more from the Chopstix menu. Hint...we got a sneak peek at the new menu coming next week. Think Korean BBQ added to an already outstanding menu. I am now trying to figure out how to move these folks north or me to go south toward Tucson more often. Chopstix...you sold us on asian deliciousness.

It took my husband and I a bit too long to finally try this place out. It's located in a little strip mall right off of US 36 in Avon. This was actually my first experience at Vietnamese food altogether. The owner was there to guide us through our choices, and he exceeded my expectations. He explained that he lists the menu according to his favorites. The top choice in each category was how he recommended to us. We went with the pho and the spring rolls to-go. This place is very small inside and doesn't have a ton of seating. It gets pretty busy during the prime times, so be prepared if you are planning to eat it there. We took ours to go and it was just as delicious as the next time when we ate inside.

We ordered take out. Order not right, chicken way over cooked and tough to eat, fried rice~ so-so. Not impressed, and pretty expensive. Is there good chinese take out in the Mount Juliet area? My fear is there isn't~ at least that I've tried.

In an attempt to find a thai restaurant that was open on a random sunday evening, we found ourselves at Thai Orchid. Yes, I thought that was strange too that we ran into three others that were closed for no apparent reason. The only reason we didn't try this first was mainly for distance, nothing philosophical. Anyway. Upon arrival, we were lucky enough to get seated immediately. As had been in a previous experience, there was a bit of a wait. Considering how packed the place was, the two servers did their best to accommodate everyone diligently. And, the place seems to be too small to have more than two servers as well. So we had to wait few extra minutes for our orders, but no biggie. The food took care of it all - Lemongrass soup, Chicken Coconut soup, Pad Thai Duck, Evil Jungle Princess, and 2 sensational banana (or something to that nature). The lemongrass soup didn't have any lemongrass in it. But, it was spicy and had three GIANT shrimp floating in it that made me forget all about the lemongrass. Soup wasn't too spicy or too bland. Just perfect and tasty. Chicken Coconut Soup was sensational. Some places make it really sweet that just takes the thrill away. We did wish there were few pieces of carrots in there. Pad Thai Duck was the special of the day. The duck was dipped in batter and deep fried. Although it was crispy on the outside, the meat seemed a bit too dry. But, I forgot all about that as I dug into the pad thai. Every bite of the tender noodle was balanced off with peanut garnish and crunchy lemongrass. I got mine to be extra extra spicy even though it wasn't indicated on the menu of being a spicy dish. The portion was just perfect to stem off a hungry stomach, but not so much so that there were no room left for desert. Evil Jungle Princess is a medley of vegetables and chicken cooked in a spicy sauce. Again, we got ours to be extra extra spicy. The dish was filled with sauce and fresh vegetables with a scoop of rice at a corner. Nothing bad or sub par can be said about this dish. Then came the desert. Oh Boy. Sensation Banana (or something to that nature) - basically, its their fried desert dish topped off with a scoop of a variety of their ice cream. We went with mango ice cream with mango sauce. The fried banana was brilliant - crispy on the outside, firm on the inside. Some places, the banana is overcooked and ends up smushy. Which was what I was expecting here as well. But, I was thoroughly surprised. The mango ice cream and the mango sauce was a pretty good complement to the banana. Their silverware was actually from thailand and made of brass. Found that to be an impressive feature. The decor of elephants plastered all over the walls was quite pleasing to the ambiance as well. The only down point of our visit this time was how long we had to wait to give our order and again for the food to arrive. But, can't fault them much for it. The place literally packed. And they tried their best to tend to everyone. Will definitely return again soon during a weekday or something when its less noisy/crowded.

A great restaurant on a great road in Nashville. The dosa is great, sambar is unusually good, and the parotta is a different kind of Indian veg option in this town. The service was very polite and happy we were there--even though we came in close to closing time. We're happy to have the south Indian coffee and chai as well.

What a nice surprise when I walked in here for lunch. A Taste of India is tucked in a run-down looking strip mall off of Olive Blvd. It has a nice clean and modern looking decor and the lunch buffet here was pretty good. They had some of the basic Indian staples on the buffet as well as a full menu available at lunch time. I enjoyed the Chicken Tikka Masala and Fried Vegetables. They also had these cheese balls soaked in syrup that were just delightful. (For dessert) However, the service here left a lot to be desired as our server seemed to be the only one there during lunch and he disappeared from time to time. Overall I liked this place and would definitely go back. I would just like to see the service improve a bit.....

Got the navrattan korma to go. It was ok, slightly less than average portion, and could have been much more flavorful. Planning to go back to try other entrees as I've heard this restaurant can be promising!

Again if you have not tried Sabor Del Caribe you do not know what you a missing. The food and service is top notch and very very affordable. The empanadas are the be I have ever had and the pork tips and fried chicken are to die for. I can't believe all this comes from a food truck. The chef should have his own restaurant. Go and check them out you will be glad you did.

I decided to go to Umami because I wanted to branch out and try to find more good sushi places in Nashville. Everyone knows about the higher end places like Wild Ginger and Virago, but I want to find more mid-level places to grab sushi in town. Overall, I'd say Umami was pretty good. Umami isn't just a sushi place. They pride themselves in having dishes from many different Asian countries. There were a number of dishes that looked really good. My wife and I decided to split some sushi and Thai to try to get some variety in our experience. On the sushi side we split the Umami roll. I have to say that this roll was really good! I'd love to try some of their other rolls, especially their standard $5-$7 rolls. There were a bunch of specialty rolls that looked really good as well. I think if I go back we'll try a few different rolls. I ordered the Pad Kee Mao. It was tasty and a really great size. At $10 I'd say that's a pretty good deal. It's very flavorful and I really liked the rice noodles. Like I said, I'd like to go back and try some more of their sushi rolls. The vibe is a little off to me - lots of neon going on. Also there is a hand washing station outside the bathrooms but in the eating area. We happened to be sitting right next to this and couldn't help but laughing at how odd it wa a Giving this place 3 stars: solid food, nice service, ok vibe.

This place was a good find. The food was full of wonderful spices. My friend had the Bollywood chicken, the rice was flavored well, but did not have much meat and I had the lamb curry was a little greasy but full of bold flavors. The one thing this place could do would be to bring all the food together or maybe write the items ordered down. All in all good service, friendly. I would come again.

It looks like it's all been said, but yeah, this place was wonderful! It was a perfect meal for me and my party. I was treating my mom and cousin to dinner and also a friend joined us. The four of us shared everything and absolutely EVERY bite of this varied meal was deliciously flavorful with every mouthful fulfilling. We were all impressed they weren't afraid to use flavor; not a bite was bland. The lamb kabab was so damn juicy and flavorful I'm still thinking of it. Both our fish dishes were heavenly. All salads were on point. Im so glad this place was as good as I hoped; it's rare a restaurant meets the hype and lives up to all the anticipation of their obviously wise choice to open slowly; so worth the wait.
Oxtail was excellent , very rich. Enjoyed the Sorrel drink. Met the owner/chef and his son..very nice people. I recommend. It's a BYOB, too btw.

Wow, this was so good. I really didn't know what to order, so I looked up some pictures on yelp and asked him to bring me this -- which turned out to be the stir fried pork noodles. Also got the shrimp spring rolls. Both were excellent -- and the soup that came with it was so flavorful!

The pork Ramen was great.... duck one not so much as it tasted bland but I am certain that it is GF (don't quote me on that). Service was a little slower than I would have liked (hence the 4), but overall I would say that this restaurant is a must if you like ramen. Cocktails were superb as well as the decor. Check it out if you haven't. Definitely a nicer and elevated experience in Reno as seen by a California girl.

I ordered a whole Jerk Chicken with a side of peas and rice. The flavor was decent. Honestly, not the best Jerk chicken I've tasted, but this is Indiana, not Florida. I digress. The deal breaker was that the chicken was as dry as the Sahara. The rice, peas and plantains were good, except that for a family of 4 (which is what this was advertised to serve), I don't feel that 1/2 a plantain is adequate. I won't be back, not because it was oh so terrible, moreso because I know that better exists, so I can't bring myself to settle. Now, if I would just apply this same principle to my love life, alas... Once again, I digress.
Went there Friday night with a group and had a good meal and a nice time. The staff was great and my Pad Thai was really good. Definitely worth going too if you are in the neighborhood.
Perfect for a group or unique date night! Excellent food and love the belly dancer! Guaranteed a memorable fun night!! highly recommend
one of the best pad thai I have had recently. Nice, low key neighborhood place, byob, good value.
Friendly staff. Good size portions. The Falafel was exceptionally good. The chicken sandwich was also very good

I am from Wisconsin and I visit New Orleans very often. I have to come to Shishkabob House every time I come down here. This is the best place to eat if you are looking for authentic, clean, and tasty food. On top of all that the service is just exceptional. Highly recommend

Trendy, downtown place. Came for drinks with a group and would have stayed longer because I loved the vibe, but there was no air since all the doors are open. Would definitely come back here when it is cooler. Club-like feel with young professional crowd. Great for drinks at night. Bartender was friendly and made strong drinks!

I showed up at this quaint little establishment that was enclosed inside the South County shopping mall looking for the perfect mac & cheese. I think I have found it here at this chain restaurant. I walked in and asked for nutritional information, because I am a weight watchers user. They had a laminated sheet with a lot of their dishes and I was surprised they did not have a pamphlet or a smaller piece of paper they can hand out to people. No matter, the dish I chose fit perfectly with my points. What was also amazing was that when I asked for a military discount, the server took off the price of my drink as the discount, so I ended up paying more than $2 less for my meal. I ended up getting a small order of the Wisconsin Mac & Cheese. Sweetie pie's, you guys should notice this, this place is in huge competition with you for the best mac & cheese. They had plenty of montery chedder on top which made the dish ever more flavorful. I was very please with my visit and I recommend Noodles & Company to anyone who wants a cheap and easy place to get some very awesome food. The only negatives that I experienced was that this location was inside the mall, but there was no enterance and exit to go inside the building, like most other places. It was very cold outside and walking down the sidewalk to a nextdoor store was rather inconvenient.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in St. Louis. From the home made warm and fluffy pita to the hummus to the short ribs to the trout tartine... it's hard to choose a stand out because they are all so delicious. It's a great take on the food I have had in Israel. Do not forget to get sangria!

I don't live in St Louis, found this place 3 or 4 years ago when my son's were playing baseball in Affton. Deluxe Gyro is awesome!!!! (even though is has lettuce, I know its not supposed to, but I don't care its still awesome) whenever I'm in South County I consider it a treat to stop and get a Gyro...

Okay I'm repeating myself here, but again nobody has Yelped this and is instead writing about Applebees or other lame chain restaurants you could find in any city?! Anyhow, I had my birthday dinner at Zagol with a friend and we loved it. It's been a couple of years since I've had Ethiopian food, but we split an order the Abesha Selata (mixed salad/greens with homemade dressing) and the Beg Alicha (mild lamb stew flavored with onion, green pepper, ginger, garlic and Ethiopian spice). The procedure is to use the injera as the utencil for your food - we were both full about half way through the meal and had enough for leftovers. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED and the main owner/cook will come out to talk to you about the meal and its background.

Coworker and I decided to order some tenders for lunch. They offer delivery and we went with that. It was a bit strange ordering since it's by weight and we wanted two separate orders but it was going to the same place. I wanted three pieces but I got four (one was a smaller size) and that was around $4.50. I got the Pommery Honey mustard. That sauce took me by surprise; I didn't think it would have that much kick. I was hoping for more honey than tear inducing. I'd probably stick with the Chipotle Lime mayo. Chicken was still great as before. The white meat is very juicy and the breading was still crispy. Delivery charge is $2.00.

I haven't had a lot of Thai food, but since I love Chinese, Korean and Vietnamese, I figured this place would probably be up my alley. I was right. The dining room at Siam Cafe is pretty sizable, and there are several neat little booths with pillows and cushions perfect for lounging during a casual meal. Our server was quite a character, and she checked on us and made small talk regularly. I ordered the Pad Thai, which my friend informed me is a relatively simple, traditional dish. It was quite delicious, and the portions are pretty huge, especially considering the less exotic entrees only cost around $7-$10. Fancier items (especially anything containing squid) are quite a bit pricier. My dish had chicken and shrimp (though the shrimp-to-chicken ratio was a little weak) seasoned with a really tasty peanut oil. The atmosphere and staff at Siam Cafe are very friendly and informal. It's a nice spot to go with a friend or two, though I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for large parties. As far as Thai goes, it's probably the best I've had. I'll definitely go back, and I recommend it to anyone with a penchant for Asian food.

I really love this place. The food is very good and the decor is quite nice. We are always greeted quickly and warmly. Servers are knowledgeable and attentive. We typically always start with Po Tak soup, a hot and spicy seafood soup that would clear up any sinus problems if I had them. My wife typically gets the red dragon sushi, and I usually get their panang curry chicken, both of which are delicious. I've tried their Pad Thai, which was very good but not the best I've ever had. Reasonably priced and a good value. A good little quiet spot that's on our "go to" list.

I ordered an iced mocha with skim milk. I got what tasted like a scoop of dirt stirred into milk with ice. I'm not even kidding. I let the drink sit in my mouth for a moment ot properly identify the flavor. It was dirt. Fail.

Ordered the regular plate. They didn't have rice available. What kind kabob place doesn't have rice? Rice is half of the main items in the meal. The pita bread was half cooked, still doughy. The meat was ok. Will never come back. The hummus was salty. The owner was nice enough to come outside and smoker where we were eating. Not exaggerating how horrible the food was here. Such a disappointment for students. Don't waste your money or your taste buds.

We absolutely LOVE this Thai treat! We've traveled the world, only to find this amazing restaurant in our own back yard of Spring Hill, Florida. Our faves - Crab Rangoon's, Amazing Chicken & Green Curry. Can't lose when you come here, never disappointed. Good service, clean & exceptionally delicious food.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: We met a native Thai lady at the bank. We asked what restaurant she'd recommend for authentic Thai food and she suggested Lanna and so we gave it a try. We had the Somtom salad and the Pad Kee Maow. They were spicy but excellent. Everything was fresh and cooked at the time of ordering. The food came up quickly and was very reasonably priced. It also had good service, they were very friendly. The owners took time to chat to each table and welcome their customers. Will definitely come here again. It seems like a good place to go have dinner with some friends and we are eager to try the cookery classes. Definitely a must for Thai food lovers!!!

Come here regularly for lunch - their lunch specials are limited, but usually pretty tasty. The vegetable soup as an option (basically cabbage vegetable water) is pretty sad, but their main dishes more than make up for the lack of flavor in the soup. I usually order the eggplant tofu - super tender eggplant with a hint of caramelization on the edges and crispy fried tofu, or the phad thai - great because it's not as fish-saucy as some other places I've tried, and the curries are great. Service is also very friendly, but can sometimes get backed up. Overall, a fan of Meun Fan since their prices are very reasonable and the portions are great.

The food here was good. They were very accommodating and the server was nice. The server was wearing an old tshirt which felt out of place since it's a nicer restaurant (cloth napkins & tablecloths and such.) I got the linguine with clams in white sauce, my boyfriend got the baked gnocchi. Our friends got a pork chop rack special and lobster ravioli, they were very happy with their meals. We got calamari and brussel sprouts as appetizers, which were good as well. The olive oil for the bread basket was not good. I did feel sort of rushed, which I understand because it's Saturday although the restaurant itself was slow. Also, very fairly priced which was great.

this random Indian restaurant set in the back of shady looking hotel... turned out to be a good find! Great flavorful food and great service! :) Mango Lassy drink was tasty! :) Garlic Naan was fresh and tasty! I'm not even a vegetarian but we had the Mutter Panir, which is homemade cheese in a curry like sauce and that was delicious! The cheese cubes look like tofu, but def. try it.... it was actually very tasty! Who would have thought cheese in a curry like sauce would go well together...
Love this place! There is always a line to get in during the week at lunch time. I always get the pork noodle. It's the best dish here if you like noodles and BBQ pork.

I'd been craving good Ethiopian food, and stumbled upon this place a few months ago. The food is fantastic! I highly recommend trying the vegetarian combo (TA3) if you don't know what to order. It's a good blend of several dishes. The portions are quite large, so an order for two will likely be plenty for a party of 3-4. One word of warning, they don't generally provide silverware, so this place isn't for those who are huge germ-phobes, especially since most dishes are served family style. Each table has hand sanitizer, however. I've also ordered take-out several times, and service has been quick. Enjoy!

Best Indonesian food in Philly, hands down. I'm very satisfied with the quality of Indonesian food at Sky. Typical Indonesian food outside Indonesia are far than the real thing, but Sky definitely beats that prototype. My favorite is their Emie, and anything available on their snack counter (if you've never had Spekoek/thousand layer cake, you're missing out a lot). When I'm broke, I usually get their nasi uduk (coconut rice), which I claim to be the most satisfying meal you can ever get for $4 anywhere in US. I'm Downsides: closes early on Saturday nights, space is too tight.

We were in route home from Orlando to Venice and had a craving for Thai, most of the other places were closed on Sunday so I was happy to find this place. Nice decorations, very clean, love that the wait staff wear Thai clothing. The tables are so neat as they are carved wood art. It is a very calming space. Husband got the chicken pad Thai which was very reasonably priced at $9.95 and he has enough for a second meal. Spice range is 1-5 and he ordered at a 3 which was pretty spot on to medium spice. I ordered the yellow curry chicken it was very good. The sauce was thicker than I'm used to but great flavor. The dishes were nicely presented with carrot origami. Overall I would come back.

I had never tried Ethiopian food prior to my first visit to Zagol about a year ago. You pick a few different main dishes and they are all brought out on a large platter that everyone shares. Its quite tasty and hearty! The fact that one amazing lady basically runs the restaurant herself makes it even more impressive. From making the bread to taking orders, cooking the meals, even roasting her own coffee beans (!), Shita has her hands full but pulls it off well. It can take a bit to get food if a few groups show up at once. They have a couple decent wines, but the beer menu is a bit lacking. There are two Ethiopian alcohol options, a wine and a beer, but they have not had either any time I've been. Looking forward to trying them someday. The lamb dish is my favorite, followed closely by everything else. Haven't tasted anything that I didn't like. The injera bread (made of teff, which is gluten free) has a very nice sourdough flavor and goes great with the richness of the dishes. Just make sure you order enough for everyone!

We've continued dining and ordering take out from here since my previous review. We visited tonight with a friend, three of us total. I'd seen previous reviews about poor service and rude staff, but had truly never experienced it. We were seated and the vibe from the mature, gentleman server was surly from the beginning. The table had been set for two and he, literally, threw a napkin and silverware in from of me. The silverware bounced. I ordered apps for the table and then he walked off without asking about drinks. We continued to be kind to him and he addresses my dining partners as "sir," but was dismissive of me and generally inattentive. I ordered my entree and he said "mild or medium?" The other two at the table were offered "medium or hot." Women can't have it hot? I was scared into ordering medium because I'm not sure what would have happened had I said hot. The food was delicious and fairly priced. Lets get that out of the way. They make pretty darn tasty food. Eventually, he gave up on us altogether and someone else was checking on us here and there. It came time to pay and the amount charged to our credit card was incorrect in our favor. It was $23 instead of $57. My husband pointed this out to him and purposely said, "While you haven't treated us very well, I want to be fair and let you know our bill isn't correct." He said, "Oh, I'm sorry," and whisked the card away to fix it. Nothing else. No thanks for our honesty. No apology for the rude service. Really disappointing experience. The parking lot was full, but the place was empty. I imagine that Spice Nation is pulling away a lot of their business and this level of service isn't going to keep existing customers.

Be prepared to spend about 2 hours in there if you go on Saturday night, they have two waitresses who also double as hostesses and dispatch take out orders. They need to hire more help because the food is decent. It took about 20 minutes for the soups to be brought to our table, others had similar experience. A couple of parties showed up early for their reservations and were told to wait outside because the tables were not set. Instead of setting and cleaning the tables right away they wait until the party shows up. The take out customers have no place to wait except to perhaps sit down at I e of the tables with dishes left from the previous party.

I feel really bad writing this review since I come from this culture... I feel like the atmosphere is not welcoming, the service is very bad, and the food is poorly made. Three times I had to call for a waiter and tell him to please change my plate. The intervals between courses were extremely long and I also had to inform the waiter that I am finished and he could take my plate. I came with a group of people and every single one of them was disappointed. The belly dancer was wearing a yellow costume and had shoulder length light hair. Her dancing skills are awful, she definitely is very far from being professional. The way she moves is ridiculous, she doesn't know how to dance at all. This is the first time I am writing a review in my entire life and trust me I am not a mean person. I wanted to show my friends my culture and the food we eat ... But it turned out into an awful embarrassment. I will never come back here. 1 star.

Clean, and the service is friendly with reggae music playing in the background. Can eat-in at the counter with bar stools. Veggie special, which consisted of rice and peas, cabbage and kallaloo, was on par with other Jamaican spots in the area. The veggie patties, which appear baked, not fried, are delicious. I get 2 b/c they're so dang tasty.

Came back to the gem for excellent pho. This time also tried Grilled Pork and Shrimp with vermicelli noodles, veges and dipping sauce. Omg, so delicious, loved every bite! Grilled pork sauce was so good, and balance of all the fresh, zingy flavors. Pho is excellent. Tried green apple bubble tea, but too sweet for my liking, even with reduced sugar. Bright, clean place, friendly service. We've making it our fave Indy Vietnamese haunt.

This is my boyfriend and my go-to Thai when we feel like splurging on take out. We get the Pad Thai and the Crab Rangoon every time and it is always delicious. We ordered take out tonight and Grubhub delivered it. The taste was a little off so we called them and told them about our experience. The woman that answered the phone told us she was so sorry and told us to come down to the store immediately and she would take care of us. We drove down to the restaurant and were greeted by one of the owners (I assume) - the lady we talked to on the phone. She ushered us to a table while we waited and cooked some fresh Pad Thai for us to try. She made sure we approved of it before remaking our to go orders (which we did - It was amazing!). 2 of her servers came and asked us if we wanted water and we both said we were okay, but while we were waiting they delivered us some water anyway. The woman owner also said we had to try their curry because it was amazing, so she brought out some curry and rice packaged to go for us to take home and try. We just got home and tried it and she was definitely right!!! They knocked it out of the park with the curry. What started out as a bummer turned into an awesome experience. If all business owners acted as professional, kind and accommodating as they did there would never be a bad review on Yelp.
Very tasty and flavorful. Relaxing and quiet atmosphere. I am not an expert on Thai food but I like everything on their menu.

It's hard for me to judge this place because I grew up eating McDonalds and my taste preferences aren't the most culturally diverse. I tried the curried goat. I liked it. It was good. I liked the rice as well. My wife and son shared the lamb shanks and they tore them up. They really liked them and wouldn't even share a bite with me. That's high praise. The chicken tenders my other son ordered were so surprisingly good...quite possibly the best tenders I have ever eaten, but who goes to an African/Caribbean restaurant for chicken tenders? The dinners were priced high, but the portions were enormous and can easily be split or shared. My West African friend who joined us told me the African food they serve is mostly East African, if that helps you at all. I'd say this place is worth trying out before it goes out of business (the owner and staff were very nice and I hope they prove my prediction wrong). This place doesn't have it all together, but can easily correct the problems I'll point out. I've come to this place twice now, but have only eaten here once. The first time I came here they were having problems with their credit card machine and I wasn't carrying any cash. There almost wasn't a second time either when I tried opening the front door an hour after the restaurant was supposed to open and it was still locked. The hostess chased us down in the parking lot as we were getting ready to leave. We ate together with friends and tried ordering several items which they said they were out of. I'm thinking, how could you be out when we're the first customers you've served today? Next, you'll find an unpleasant aroma of mildew or something funky as you approach the bathrooms, which were actually very clean. This location has never done well. It's in the International Marketplace area on 38th, but there isn't any direct turn into it. You have to turn at the Meijer sign and cut thru the Planet Fitness parking lot to get to it. I almost never see more than a couple cars right outside the restaurant, but I wouldn't let that deter you from checking this place out...at least once.

Best thai place in st louis! I order the same thing every time because it's that good. Number 45 with chicken: it's a spicier dish which is right down my alley! Comes with thin, glass noodles, yummy veggies, the meat of your choice, all soaked in the tastiest sauce. Also, the crab rangoon here is a must!

Hands down, Cucina Zapata is the best food truck I have ever been to. Every dish on the menu is delicious, and always fresh. The Mexican Veggie burger is my favorite: its brimming with lettuce, tomato, red onion, avocado, and a spicy sauce that gives it a kick.

My friend and I decided to come to this place for pizza takeout. We met up just before the Eskimo game oct 3, 2:00 pm. We both had groupons and once our female server heard that her whole demeanor changed. Well you can only use one at a time she says in a rebuking manner. I'm not supposed to do this but I'll let it slide this time acting as if she was doing us a big favor. I disagreed with her but she insisted she was right and said if you just read the fine print you would see that. So we ordered and she placed it. I stewed for a few minutes. Her behavior just rubbed me the wrong way. I decided to look at the fine print. It says specifically. One per person. Per visit. So if we had come in a minute apart it wouldn't have been a problem. I pointed this out to her and she wouldn't hear it. She got all huffy and self indignant. Well if your going to be rude to me I'm just going to cancel your order. She storms off and as we're leaving I can hear her say to the cook. They cancelled the order!! Unbelievable!! Will not be back here again. Heard they had great takeout pizza. Ps: I usually tip 10 bucks on groupons. X2 she would have had 20 bucks tip for placing an order. Her loss.

Vientiane Cafe is a great spot for dinner, but even better for lunch. The dinner crowd is often a big one with long wait times, but lunch is usually quieter & you get your pick of tables. When it's nice out, sitting at one of the outside tables is lovely. Their dinner prices are a bit high, though the food is good quality. Also, their crispy noodle salad is *technically* a salad because it has a sprinkling of scallions and a sprig of greenery, but mostly it's tasty sauce and little fried noodles. Not something to order if you're trying to be health-conscious. Their lunch special is a moderately-priced three course meal, consisting of a soup, an appetizer, and the main course. Each category has several options. I prefer the coconut soup, which is creamy and tangy, with a nice assortment of veggies, though I'm not a fan of the peppers. The dumpling appetizer is not very good. Although the dipping sauce is just right, the dumplings are kind of chalky and bland. I suggest the fresh spring roll with strips of fried tofu and two dipping sauces instead. The entrees offered are mainly curry variants, as well as pad thai and a few other things. I enjoy their pad thai a lot, and it's good with beef and great with chicken. I'm giving them three stars due to a few unpleasant incidents, one opf which I'll detail. We were waiting to have dinner for a while, and we'd left and come back to kill some time. The waitress had said 20-ish minutes, so we were back in that time. We waited some more, and then we got seated by one waitress. Unfortunately, a moment later, another waitress unseated us and told us we'd have to wait at least another 20 minutes, if not more. Needless to say, we were rather disgruntled. The waitstaff should really be more coordinated and communicative on busy nights. And long story short, we went home and got delivery.

One of South Philadelphia's finest! I recently was in the area and asked a local if she could recommend an Italian place for Dinner her eyes lit up and without hesitation she says Scannichio's! I wasn't going to question her. She is a local and she is Italian so I took her at her word. Let me say that there is something special about family owned and operated places. It's either "special" because its disorganized and under budgeted,or in this case its special because of supreme personal service, atmosphere, and quality of product. Very pleased with appetizers. I had the bruschetta not the most difficult thing but all fresh flavors and seasonings. Their is a distinct taste in there Parmesan cheese very good. For dinner I had the best meal I've ever had. "Death sentence last meal good". Had the chicken Saltimbocca with asparagus and pasta (oil and garlic ) Guys I'm not kidding best meal ever. All fresh herbs and seasoning. Distinct taste in the sauces and pasta was perfect. Finished with cannoli and Capp. Will be back soon and often. Strongly recommend.
With family.... great 5 stars service great people delicious food specially dosa chicken lollipops Lassi. Was very busy. Place .drove 40 min to get here Thank you

Great dining experience! It's tiny, it's crowded and it's a little loud. But the food this place is shelling out, is top notch. I was really impressed with the quality of food and the knowledge of the servers that we had. They recommended the perfect dishes and it was just the right amount of food/was exactly what we were looking for. I'm really glad we stopped in and will be stopping back! The other reviews are spot on. The spinach gnocchi was great, as was the antipasti plate.
Yummy pho tai and iced coffee. Quick and friendly service. Spotless interior. Just a couple blocks from Bookhaven :)

We had been looking for a good indian resturant for a while in the area... The chicken was incredibly tender, the sauces were all very flavorful, and the staff was very friendly. I will be coming back often, and would highly recommend trying this.

My boyfriend and I tried this place before we went to a show at Mercy Lounge and we were very impressed! The margaritas are some of the best we've had - only fresh ingredients - very well done!! I had the yellow chicken with rice and it was to die for! The chicken was so juicy and very flavorful and paired so nice with rice. My boyfriend got the plantain stuffed chicken and it was delicious as well! For dessert, we ordered the tres leche cake, and oh my goodness we were in heaven. The meal was perfect from start to finish. It is a bit pricey but I say it's totally worth it!! Also you should be prepared for the service to be a little slow... It's a very laid back atmosphere but we didn't mind because we had time to kill before the show. So, don't expect quick, but, again, totally worth it! The atmosphere is awesome as well... The back porch has a great view of some of Nashville's skyscrapers and the inside is very modern and chic. We will definitely be going back!

I just spent 6 months living in Thailand so when I got back to Nashville I was desperate for a good, authentic thai place. After trying nearly every thai restaurant in town I feel confident saying that this is the best thai restaurant in town. And the staff is so friendly, I go here now just to keep my Thai sharp. Definitely go here if you like Thai food because if you haven't been here you haven't really had it.
This is my first time here and I had take-out. It takes just like all the other restaurants I've been too and I luv it!! It's a good thing!! I will be going back again!

This place is amazing! The food is authentic, the service is first-rate, and the environment in the restaurant is perfect for everything from work lunches, to family dinners, to private events. Easy parking.

In my quest for the perfect Pho that I had in Asia I gave Sizzing Wok a try. The Pho is ok, although lacking in all the necessary accompaniments. However on my first trip is was overshadowed by the yelling, laughing and loud banter coming from the kitchen. Our server was not friendly in the least and spent more time in the kitchen carrying on with the rest of the staff than in the actual dining area. I decided to give it another try and the service was more of the same. There is an overall feeling of disconnect, for lack of a better word. It was busier in the dining room than on my previous visit but I noticed that it was also visibly dirty; even as I peered into the kitchen when paying the bill. I think I will continue on my quest for better or for worse.

Little Thai is great! I've eaten at several thai restaurants throughout Pinellas and this is the best. The priority of some thai places seems to be the interior decorating at little thai that is not the case their energy goes into consistently producing quality food. The wait staff are friendly and the service is great. The food comes out quick and your cup is always full. They have an unbeatable lunch special, I forget the exact price but it's something like 7 dollars for a thai meal such as pad thai, param, panang etcetera and two sides. The sides are soup, salad or egg rolls. Most all of the meals can be vegan by choosing steamed tofu instead of meat or by just getting vegetables. I do believe that some of the entrees may use a fish sauce base so if you live a plant strong life make sure to ask. They are very helpful and veg aware.

Ploy Thai is a smallish restaurant lavishly decorated yet casual. Service was very good- there must have been 3-4 people helping me. Silly me didn't realize that the pot of hot tea they brought to me had the mug on the bottom. How would you know?? It's hidden well! I had the spring rolls ($3.5)which were good but the serving was small- it amounted to one roll cut into quarters. I wish they would do half orders as I was visiting from out of town and could take home leftovers. I ordered the Pad Thai ($10.95) for an entree. It came with shrimp, chicken, sprouts, scallions and ground peanuts. It had a very good flavor but I wish it had had more peanuts. Prices are a little steep, especially if you are going for the take-out. I'd called several times before I drove down to make sure they were open but no one answered the phone. I noticed when I got there they were taking to-go orders on the phone and that I had the correct number. Strange.
I loved this place! They have an extensive menu and the prices are super reasonable. The remodel that they did looks very good. I hope everybody gives this place a try.

this cart turns out some pretty tasty eats for cheap. 5 usd will get you a no-frills lunch (including a drink.) since i'm sans-gluten, i get the lamb salad with the white sauce and a decent pour of their hot sauce. the vendor has been nothing but nice each time i've gone. he's been very polite and provides efficient service. so don't be discouraged by the (often) long line...it moves quickly. nota bene: this cart likely moves around but the times i've visited have been on wednesdays when the cart is at 36th and market.

Hiding in a strip mall with an unassuming storefront, Thai Place (unassuming name!) has food you might not guess is as good as it is. "What's that Thai place you were talking about?" "You mean Thai Place?" "Yes, the Thai place, what is the name????" Argh! Cheap too. We split a cucumber salad and each had a curry dish, and it was $27. We love BYOBs too, because we always know the wine will be good, and affordable. We chose a New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, which is great with Thai, but another great one would be Verdejo from Rueda, Spain, yum yum yum, perfect if you love Sauv Blanc. What made us drive straight there a few nights ago was seeing that they have mock duck and mock chicken made of seitan, and it is tender and delicious. (I am a vegetarian-trying-to-be-vegan but am not supposed to have soy, which is a total pain, but I am finding my way around this, thanks to seitan and Thai restaurants.) I have never seen more than 3 curries on a Thai menu, usually red, green, and mussaman, but there were more here, including one made without coconut milk, which was delicious, but man, that was a hot one. We did not make any heat requests, but I would say that one dish was mild and the other was medium, fine with us. We loved the beautiful celery green plates and the elephant decor and were geekily taking lots of pictures. The only other things I would advise is to turn the lights down a little and add candles to the tables. Service was friendly and well-paced, and people were constantly coming in to pick up their takeout. I can't tell which is better, this place or Thai L'Elephant -- I am just jealous that Phoenixville has two Thai restaurants that are this good.

Am I missing something? Look... I'm all about kitschy-but-classic, and after a few friends told us how "awesome" this place was we finally broke down and went. Our reaction was basically: "Huh?". Food was... okay... service was... okay... atmosphere was campy but without anything like charm... just tasteless. And the prices were way higher than the quality of the food permits.
Really enjoyed the deep fried tilapia. We ordered lemongrass beef and green curry chicken as well, I would have rated these items 5 if only they had added some more salt!

Do not get catering from Tandoor with its new management. We ordered chai tea and samosas and they brought our chai tea in a plastic gallon milk bottle (one bottle was $50, ridiculous). The tea itself is now awful too, completely bland. We even saw traces of dried milk on the bottles, made us wonder if they even cleaned them. Also those bottles have very soft plastics that nearly melted with the hot chai. Previously, they brought a proper plastic container and for $50 we could serve 45+ people with no problem and it tasted great. The samosas are now also more expensive, we only got 33 with $50. I haven't been to the buffet since the new management, so this review is strictly for their catering practices.
Pho was used with beef bone instead of beef bouillon ( which is key) and a plus that I can order a small, large or xtra large bowl of soup!

After reading some of the great reviews I decided to give it a try tonight and I'm not impress. The flavor of the food was either too salty or overly sweet. I ordered the stuff tofu sizzler and vegatable phai thai and I didn't like either one. Even my tea got no flavor. As for the service, I got service period.

There should be a requirement that ALL places serving food after midnight should be this good! While there are no problems finding alcohol at 1am, decent eating is slim picking. Hot dogs from carts at corners, rubber looking pizzas from those daiquiri places, fried chicken that have been sitting under heat lamps for too long...and there's Ali Baba. Truth be told, we didn't have high hope. The menu didn't look especially attractive or promising but we needed food. We ordered the lamb/lamb gyro and OMG, it was SO GOOD! The pita bread was warm and soft and filled with a very generous portion of delicious juicy tasty meat. Every bite was heaven and we weren't even buzz. Only if we didn't waste stomach space from another spot eating dry chicken...we would have ordered another. It's a small place with some counter seatings. There are a lot of photos on the wall of this man with many celebrities and it sure looked like the person preparing the food...when hubby asked, the man proudly said the person in the pictures is his cousin. When we thanked him for one of the best gyro we've had, he was so happy...we were simply telling the truth. If this place is closed to home, we would be in big troubles..

I agree with the other yelpers on the unimpressive look from the outside of this place and the inside although seemed very clean and tidy was not very restaurant like. A half dozen tables at most. BUT, the deluxe gyros we ordered and the side of pasta salad were excellent. The olive salad was pretty tasty as well. I would like to warn you this place closes very early,why i dont know but we arrived around 15 minutes $before closing . Thing is we werent the last ones to walk in that late and the more people that did come in the more aggravated the what i assumed was the manager seemed to get. I understand a little of what he was feeling because when you work all day and its that close to close all you wanna do is Go HOME ! I just thought to myself, i dont mind him being frustrated but as a professional he should have put on that fake smile and at least tried to hide his emotions from the customers. That being said dont let it keep you from going there and trying the gyros ! They were overstuffed with meat and veggies and delicious! Im giving it 4 stars and not 5 for the simple fact i expect perfection in all aspects of my dining experience and they failed on the making us feel we were valued as customers. I will be back again and hoping for a smile next time!
