So so good. We husband and I came for dinner with our kids and we all loved it. The owner was warm and welcoming. The dining area was clean and comfortable. All of our entrees were rich and flavorful. My butter chicken was incredibly tasty, as were the goat curry and Thai fish curry. My 6-year-old enjoyed her Chinese chicken and broccoli. We definitely want to come back on a Sunday night when they serve Nepalese food.

This is a nice restaurant near UCSB usually packed with college students. They served good pho. I tried one of their rice plates. That was good too. Service can be a tad slow during busy hours. Very good value for money.

Amazing... had the sausage with rabe.... so perfect. Followed up by pasta with clams... asked for extra bread to finish up the sauce. Steak was as good as a steak can be... Waiting on dessert and cannot wait to come back!

Ordered from here due to many rave reviews. Kang Massaman Curry, Crab Rangoon, and Duck Panang. None of it was bad, just meh. All the dishes were just a bit bland. I won't say I regret ordering from here, but I likely won't order from here again. There are just many Thai choices available in town that are much much better.
Best Pho in town! Affordable and great food on the bench. It's a great alternative if you're looking for something different and flavorful.
Great food, awesome view of the water, good service. Fun to sit and listen to the music or dance on the weekends. Really good ice-cream. Good food portions. Favorite is the Taco plate.

meh...its just ok. its pretty obvious he reads the reviews and trys to give his customers the full show. Falafel was average, the vegetables were tasty but very oily. in the 20 minutes I was in line he asked some very important questions....like why do black people block the sidewalk? and telling chinese customers "you wont find this in china town!" I made the mistake of ordering 2 sandwiches...hey you! tell your friend to get her own! one per customer! what a wanker.
Very good food, curry shrimp is sooooo good! Nice and clean restaurant,i will be back to try other dishes on the menu.

Just ate here yesterday and the food was excellent! Authentic Thai food. We tried pineapple fried rice and pad Thai and we loved them. The frozen watermelon drink is a must try. A lot of vegetarian options. Just wish they have couple more tables. It's very small but nicely decorated. We're a party of 6 so they have to put 2 tables together. They only have 1 small table for 2 and 1 table for 4, then 3-4 bar chairs. Will definitely come back to try their soup.

This place is amazing. It is run by a husband and wife. We love it for lunch or dinner. Basil Chicken and Chicken with Mixed Vegetables are two of our favorites. Hot or Thai Hot are a must!! You won't be disappointed!!!

Dal Mahkni was tasty prepared medium hot and Raita was just right. Rice was great. We were told we could have as much as we liked. Ended up finishing two plates full. Aloo Palak (Sag Aloo) was bland. Lamb Korma was sheep in brown gravy - tasty not not at all exotic. We were the only ones there on a Sunday at 6:30. Buffet is lunch and Friday and Saturday nights only. Waiter/Manager was very nice. Price was fair. Everything clean. Music at a good level for conversation.
Intimate atmosphere, delicious food. The freshly baked pita (clay oven!) and hummus are a must try. My favourite little gem in Edmonton
This man is the FOOD DOCTOR!!!.. I had a pasta dish with a half of grilled pear and it was absolutely delightful. Thank you Sir!

With all the competition from Indian and other cuisines I've thought for a while that the neighborhood Chinese Restaurants would have to up their games to thrive. Well this one has and then some. They feature Thai, Chinese and Japanese food. The Penang Curry I had was simply outstanding, and the table next to us was raving about the sushi. Come here and decide for yourself. You will not be dissapointed.

The food was "passable" and the service was troubling. The food was a mixture of Moroccan and Tunisian food that looked promising, yet the flavour on other side needed improvements. The price tag for you what you are served is extremely contradictory. By all means, I would pay more if it was worth it. For the décor and the food, I would go somewhere else.

I was craving Pho yesterday due to the beautiful weather and my go to place is closed on Sundays. Thanks to Yelp I know that Pho An Hoa was close and that other Yelpers enjoyed it so I decided to give it a try. Upon entering, I was impressed with how nice and clean it was. We asked if we could put in a take out order and upon ordering were told it would be ready in 5 minutes and it WAS. Let me tell ya, the Pho was delicious. It was the perfect spicy meal for a chilly day. We were given a very hearty portion for $8 a piece, which is insane. I look forward to coming back and trying some of the other dishes.

The $10.99 weekend lunch buffet is a good deal. There was a pretty good variety of food and most of it was very tasty. I especially enjoyed the chicken tikka masala, saag paneer and navratan korma. I was a little disappointed by the naan which was dry and kind of burnt. Service could have been a bit more attentive. My husband liked the naan more than I did and wanted a refill, but we weren't able to get one.
Take out was delicious and well cooked. Portions a bit small. Yellow curry is great with lots of veggies.

There is a new saying in the land of elephants, Hinduism and where more people have cell phones than shoes: "But of course, Americans like buffets. But of course!" I can't conceptualize how in the sh*t they make so many varying dishes that may lead to choice fatigue, yes; yet, the pantheon of palette-pleasing choices creates an opportunity for everyone to sizzle their own core tandoori (that's your stomach by the way in yelp-speak). And, how exactly they have every dish under the big red one, matters not. What matters is that I'm an American and I have options, dammit. Now... I didn't get to slowly cruise the buffet like a good American should... but we rode those randy coattails of choice for a Sunday dinner takeout. *Tandoori Chicken (I can't speak for the taste as I've hung up my meat boots). Appearance: rich & served with onions, peppers and lemon. 5 baseball sized pieces -- one on the bone. *Vegetable Samosas served with mint chutney, and tomato chutney. (The spices involved and chickpea to potato ratio makes this triangle of joy more complex than other samosas). *Chana Masala: an Indian staple that is a foundation of comparing restaurant to restaurant. This was medium spiced and super dense and was a perfect compliment to the extra spicy dish. *That extra spicy dish: "Punjabi Bhaji Vegetable fritters, shredded onions, and bell peppers cooked in tomato and butter sauce." Yes, super buttery -- however ordering it at the absolute spiciest level ("extra spicy") makes it very doable. *Dal Makhani: "Lentils flavored with freshly ground spices and sautéed in cream." It's a bowl of mehhhhhhhhhhhh. This is my first stop on the tour of Indian in Indianapolis (yeah, I know, it's taken a while), so I don't have anything to compare it to in this city. As I've had some serious Indian in San Francisco... it's just about par and par in Punjabi means "better than the rest of you!" I will be back for the buffet. Hot damn, I'm a happy man Alexander The (Not So) Great's campaign ended at the Beas River & allowed for the Hindu / Punjab / Indian culture to flourish. Their campaign... a successful thrust of flavor through the Americas and Indiana. Curry On!
The food was fantastic. Full of flavor. Lots of vegetarian choices. Hot and fresh. Staff very attentive. Will be going back and brining friends.

Food: This was, some years ago, my first experience with Ethiopian food, and I loved it. However, now that I've had plenty of time to try other Ethiopian restaurants, I can safely say that the food here is average. Unfortunately for Reno, this is the only Ethiopian place in town -- so if you've never tried it, this is as good a place as any to give a try and see if it's for you or not. Price: The price for the meat dishes is average, but the price for the vegetarian dishes is exorbitant. At every other Ethiopian place I've gone to -- these located in Portland and Seattle -- the vegetarian dishes are an excellent value for the amount (often ~$11 or less for two or three generous portions of vegetarian dishes, whereas Zagol charges more than twice that for a combo platter of vegetarian dishes, never mind how much a meat dish combo platter costs). They are pretty free with giving tables extra injera ("utensil bread", as we like to call it), although it could take a long time to get the next basket to the table so that you can start eating again. Service: Average to below average. I tried to allow some leeway because the owner is the main and usually only server, and I know she does her best; delays in service are not generally purposeful or because they're lazy, etc. An Odd Incident: The last time I was there, the owner got angry and yelled at our table for not tipping her enough, and one of my nicer friends sitting at the table gave her an extra $20 in cash. The friend who had paid for the dinner tipped something like 20% (I bought a bottle of wine for the table, and I tipped 20% on that because we used to visit this place regularly). I imagine it was a misunderstanding of some kind, but even after my too-nice friend was bullied into ponying up extra cash, she told us that our table would also be charged an automatic 15% gratuity in the future (I believe we had six people at our table). It was a strange and infuriating incident; we used to go here a lot and most of us were recognized by her on sight, so I feel if she thought we had stiffed her, the incident could have been resolved in a myriad of better and more affable ways. I have not seen this happen to anyone else so it is likely an outlying incident, but it will leave a sour taste in your mouth. For my part, I have not returned to Zagol since this happened.

It's not just dinner, it's an intimate meal and BYOB setting that isn't only for romantics. I would definitely say this is a place to bring your inner circle for great food and conversation. The lighting is dim, the room is small and a reservation is a must. The tea light lit tables aren't fancy and it has plain wooden tables that are generic but done on purpose. Servers (2-3) understand their menu and since they aren't overworked as you would see in a crowded noisy place they are much more in tune with patrons. For starters the complimentary bread is every bit of delicious. The focaccia has a contradictory texture of crispness on top but moist the on the bottom. It is served with olives and an olive oil. Our special appetizer was one of the anchovy starters that was served with roasted red peppers. My husband was a bigger fan of this dish than I was but still, it met my expectations. Drinks can be BYOB but since it skipped our minds to bring wine we ordered the lemon aid that is for 2 people. It was served in a pitcher and was tangy and less sour than I would have expected. It was refreshing and a pitcher carried us on throughout the course of our meal. The salad we had was light: giant juicy red tomatoes, a bread that was soaked with flavor-fulness and cucumber on top of arugula. It was our pre-game before the entree. For our next course, I had the fusilli pasta in a pesto pistachio sauce. My husband had the rabbit with rosemary oven roasted potatoes. The rabbit was moist and it fell off like silk away from the bone. Dessert was three Zeppoli doughnuts and a rich milk chocolate sauce. The inner dough wasn't too dense and had outside crust that was cinnamon-sugary and sweet.

In the University city area at 4034 walnut street there was a hoagie place. "Lee's hoagies" is a familiar name to many student as a cheap,close place for reasonable food. You would never love what you got at their University city location, but you would eat and it never cost too much. No longer though, Lee's is no more and it within a month of it closing a different kind of restaurant opened. Enter "Wishbone," a fried chicken place hoping to ride the recent culinary craze in Philadelphia to great heights and hopefully even greater profits. The decor inside one of my favorites for this new wave of restaurants hitting our fair city. It combines the new and the old through the use of wood and steel. Table tops and chair backs are made of thick old grain wood. This can come in a couple forms from jagged hunks for tables looking like they had just been pulled off the beach before being polished and mounted. To wide flat sheets that can come from a variety of sources. The "Shake Shack" in University City recovered theirs from an old bowling alley. The only thing they all have in common is that the wood is or at least looks old. The new comes from normally mat black or muted red steel used for the rest of the construction. This includes the legs of the tables and chairs as well as exposed girders on the walls and ceilings. The ceilings themselves are generally high and show exposed ducts and lighting. These elements create a strange juxtapose between the old and the new.With the almost clinical approach we have in modern architecture off set by the old world feel that real wood brings things. I would like to dwell more on the subject, but I need to stop and actually talk about the food. Its bad, all they have is fried chicken and they messed it up somehow. It's not greasy, their pretzel based fry dough has an odd taste to it and for a place calling itself "wishbone" I was shocked to see that all they have is boneless white and dark meat chicken. The only other flavor of breading is some coconut Thai monstrosity and I wish many horrible things to whoever thought marinating the dark meat chicken in something sweet was a good idea. For the life of me I don't know why they opened in the first place, but it will appeal to the more hipster yuppie crowd and at the very least it is cheap. At under ten dollars a pound you can get a lot of chicken. Overall (), it wasn't terrible its cheap and the decor inside looks nice. The wait staff was also friendly. Though they should have two cash registers instead of one. Having four people give out chicken and only person collect money makes the line start looking like an indecisive inch-worm if more then three people are ordering. I'll finish with a cultured debate I was having with a buddy of mine about our local "Crown Fried Chicken" . I was shocked to see how low his jaw dropped when I suggested that I enjoy going their for fried chicken. I don't consider myself to be so stuck up as to not see good product at low prices and when I pressed him he admitted himself that he could and I'm quoting here "pack away a metric ton of it". It just shows that some days you want grade A meat some days your happy with grade C. What keeps me happy is variety, so do yourself a favor and try some of the other chicken places in your area before going to "Wishbone".

We LOVE eating at Dmitiri's. We ALWAYS go early & get a seat at the open kitchen bar... otherwise it gets REALLY crowded & you get stuck sitting close to "strangers"! When you sit at the bar you get a meal AND a show. The guys cooking are fun to watch. We LOVE the grilled ocotpus & the new shrimp dish on the menu. Also a fan of the grilled veggies 7 hummus with fresh grilled pita bread. We rarely order entrees b/c it is just way too much food. We usually order 3 or 4 appetizers between the 2 of us & always have leftovers. We also LOVE that it is BYOB. The servers are always super cool.
Eating here is an amazing culinary experience. It is definitely not a falafel truck more like a Michelin star restaurant. Trust me it will be one of the best meals you will ever have.
I can't recommend this place enough. The service is always good. The owners know me by name and they take the time to educate you about the food. I have never had a bad meal.
One of the most authentic south Asian food in center city.. Love their Ashak Bulani and Sansom kabob.
Very good and fast sandwiches. Just had sausage and egg on a large roll for only $3.75. Always gets you the sandwich quickly. Open 7 days during College school year.
This is a great little place with lots of vegan options. The prices are very reasonable, and it's clean with friendly staff. I would definitely go again.

I love their Bahn Mi sandwiches. The veggies in the sandwich can be a little more pickled but I think they use a better meat then most Vietnamese places. Also, I highly recommend their thai iced tea. They don't use the nasty powder stuff and instead they freshly brew the tea.

Just had a great experience here! Easy to get a super satisfying, affordable vegan meal here. I ordered veggie feast bowls, fries, and baklava for my husband and I. The employee had to make fresh falafel and fries for me, but I didn't mind the short wait at all and he went above and beyond to make up for it anyway. Everything is delicious and definitely a feast! My new favorite fast casual chain. Will definitely be back!
I went here with a group of about 12 of us & we took up half of the place because it's really small! The food was OK but overpriced & portions were small.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Wow. All I can say is, despite my tendency towards hyperbole, this place made me want to write yelp and ask them to loan me a 6th star. Seriously (and perhaps strangely enough) this is the BEST Indian food I've ever had. Period. You're reading this thinking, 'Boise the best Indian food?!' Yes. The service was top notch and the food even better. The proprietor and his wife are Indian and know what they're doing. He does the front of the house while she cooks up her mom's mom's recipes to perfection. Order the vegetarian kadi, some naan and a beer off the incredible beer list and just enjoy.

Good music, not big but not too small inside. They have really good happy hours. Must try the mofongo! Never too crowded but I do recommend making reservations and checking out the website for live performances. Also Salsa lessons on Tuesday nights.

This place is OUTSTANDING. It is a bit of a dive, but it was clean. Whoever was in the kitchen today was FRICKIN AMAZING! After a horrible experience at some Ventura Thai place I reluctantly tried some cocoanut milk based soup and I swear I couldn't stop eating it... it was heaven in a bowl. I HIGHLY recommend this place but hope it doesn't become too trendy and crowded.

Do you want variety? Then COME HERE! The buffet, which is available every day at lunch, as well as lunch and dinner on weekends. I think they also do a buffet on Friday evenings which is awesome. I can't go any further without saying the garlic naan is awesome. I eat myself into delirium and still want more. The buffet itself has 25 items to chose from (ranging from the chutneys/salad/cold items to main dishes) I love the saag, chicken tikka masala ... pretty much everything. They do have goat curry which tastes good but watch out - can get some gristle sometimes. The vegetable samosas are always good too! I love that they have a variety of dessert options - its something I have yet to see anywhere else. Gajar Halwa (shredded carrots, ghee, milk, sugar, cashews, cardamom) is my happy place. I'd never seen this dessert before coming to India Palace. I love it!! Tip: add a bit of ice cream on top and its even better :) If thats not up your alley then the Gulab jamun (cheese solids made into a dough and deep fried) and ice cream will likely do the trick. The staff are all so friendly and they go out of their way to make you comfortable. Get their frequent customer card and every time you go in - get a stamp and you'll be on your way to some free meals!
Amazing food and in deserts, my fav is the chocolate phyllos. It is out of this world. They have a huge selection of tapas/mezes kinda dishes. I like the ones with feta cheese.

For Wilmington, Delaware this is hands down one of the best restaurants where one could dine. Even in a larger urban context I would rate 8th & Union as a 4 Star restaurant. Their Tiki Burger will knock your damn socks off! And that's saying something coming from a Texan who knows a thing or two 'bout burgers! No better option than Monday Night Happy Hour where you'll have a Smoked Manhattan for $5 and a burger for $6 (Monday, burger night). Do yourself a favor and eat at this awesome Union St establishment!
Very enjoyable dinner. The vegetable samosa was delicious as was the lamb tikka masala and garlic naan. Will be back.

Weak. The food was somewhat seasoned, but you can't really tell the difference between curry chicken and tikka masala. Saag paneer was pureed. Chana masala was ok, but watery. Curry was very oily. The worst was the naan. Inedible. Tough on the edges dry in the middle, rock hard in several places. Veg samosas were good. Mango lassi was bottled, not fresh. Definitely wouldn't do it again

Rain during our Florida vacation meant Plan B. We went to Pinellas Park to see a movie and found a great place for pho and boba! The pho broth was clean with plenty of noodles, fresh basil and bean sprouts. My only suggestion would be to include limes and sliced jalapenos. Those might be available upon request, but we ordered carry-out so we didn't discover this until we got to our hotel. The boba (we had lychee, strawberry-banana, and mango in our group) was perfect. The sweetness was just right, and the boba was the perfect texture - not over-cooked or too chewy. The pad thai was OK, and the Korean short ribs were OK as well. We thought the flavors were just a bit off - a little too peanut in the pad thai and not enough garlic in the beef. Service was a little slow for a place with such high ratings, but the young man who was at the registered apologized and mentioned hiring a third person to help with the dinner shift. We leave in a few days but we may have to make stop for more boba and try the bahn mi!

My wife and I came to grab a late dinner and could not have been more impressed with our experience. The staff was exceptionally kind and helpful with our questions about the menu and made us feel comfortable and welcome. Genuine people. As for the menu, there's a lot to look over but literally (I NEVER eat Thai) every descriptor for every dish looked delicious. We started with the Thai dumplings which were gone in about a minute they were so good. Like really good...get them. I went with the Tom Yum noodle soup and my wife got the Pad See Ew (flat noodles with egg and vegetables) - both fantastic. Flavors were exploratory but familiar providing a refreshing and satisfying meal. Portions are plentiful so I'm pumped to warm up my noodle soup leftovers, and my wife pretty much has a second meal with hers...which is a nod to the value you're getting with entrees ranging from $10-15 per person. You won't leave hungry. Thoughtfully decorated, clean, humble energy with a staff that didn't miss a mark, along with warm delicious food, we scored tonight. Living in the neighborhood, this is the kind of place I want to thrive here. Check 'em out.

I'm so glad this place was open on Thanksgiving! I was visiting Mom, and neither of us wanted to cook. All the food was fresh and prepared with skill; service was also kind! There was enough food left for lunch the next day. I've had a lot of baklava, and I'll for sure be back for the baklava at Euro Grill....or maybe one of the other awesome-looking deserts!
I came here only for events. The food is really great. Service is outstanding. Always enjoyable experience. Highly recommend for special events. And their room is private and just perfect.

Best Greek food in the city, hands down. This place prides itself on simply prepared but fresh dishes. My boyfriend and I normally get a bunch of their appetizers and share them. Our favorites are the grilled octopus, grilled veggies, spanakopita, and the baba ghanoush. Four appetizers is usually more than enough to feed both of us (and we're hungry people). We did end up getting entrees once, and they were also delicious. The seafood stew had more sea life than I've ever seen in a single dish: mussels, clams, scallops, shrimp, and squid in a nice tomato broth. If you're on the fence about this one, just try it. It's small and cramped but that adds to the intimacy of it all. Plus, you can watch the cooks making everything right there in the heart of the restaurant.

This was my first experience with Vietnamese cuisine. I was always curious since it is similar to Thai food but never took the opportunity. I was at autozone and the cashier had a beautiful sandwich and he suggested Saigon. The decor was trendy with calming earth tones. I sat in the booth. The menu is a bit over whelming but it is well organized. The staff was friendly and the service was prompt. I ordered the Saigon Sampler for an appetizer. The crab rangoon was excellent. All of the samplers were delicious. For my meal, I had the #94, the Noodle soup with shrimp. I will definitely be back to try more of the menu. I would recommend this place.

The spice levels listed on the menu are * (low spice), ** (mildly spicy), *** (spicy) and ***** (super spicy). Or something very close to that. I am a huge fan of very spicy Thai curry dishes with a delicious Thai iced tea to cut through the heat. Vientiane will NOT sell me the super spicy. I don't know why. I've tried ordering the spiciesy. They will give me mild. I've tried convincing the waitstaff that indeed they cannot make it hot enough. I've received mild food. I've even then pointed out a lack of heat in the dish and the crappy side of spicy red pepper flakes in oil. My wife has had the exact same problem. I gave up going here because it would appear they do not make anything spicy. Then, my friend Mike assured me he was actually served spicy food here. It was renovated so I gave it another chance. Both my wife and I ordered 5 stars. Our waiter looked surprised with my wife's order and checked with her to confirm that she REALLY did want 5 stars. She said yes, that she wants it as hot as possible. 5 stars. MAKE IT HOT. I then proceeded to order 5 stars as well. She received mildly spicy. I received zero spice. When the check arrived we were shocked. Her order was written down with 5 stars next to it and TWO of the stars were whited out. Yes, they changed her order. Mine? Well it had one star written next to it. I have no idea why. But they will not sell us spicy food. This is not just once, it is endemic. Fans of spicy food, do not frequent this place. I know I will not.

Honestly, it is as good as it gets! The P3 is perfect--the brisket is very tender, and on top of that, the customer service was fantastic! The waiter was very kind and willing to make us feel comfortable and have a good meal.

OK, I'm a huge fan of Ethiopian. I have eaten it in many cities around the country and now, I have even been to Ethiopia. Abay was one of my first experiences so it's near and dear to my heart. The food hear is great! It is very consistent as we tend to order some of the same combos every time. I have my favorite Ethiopian in town now, but if I am on this side of town I will hit Abay too. Word of caution about Ethiopian restaurants; be patient. The culture is not in a hurry which is different for us. Take your time, and enjoy some yummy food. I recommend the Samosas.

If a place can cook chicken correctly, then I'm almost willing to forgive anything. But in this case, Blue Fig, had exceptional service. Really attentive and helpful. Chicken is almost always overcooked at any other place. I only had it once, so I have to try it again just to make sure it wasn't a fluke. Price is reasonable, comparable to Zoe's.

Came here on a Saturday evening and the place was empty. Found everything quite expensive, especially the drinks ($7.25 for a 1 oz. high ball). We ordered chicken tandoori and lamb biryani and it was quite delicious. The service could have been better though considering only two other tables were filled. The waitress wasn't that friendly and we got a dirty plate.

Hmmmm. The decor here was somewhere between Cracker Barrel, Country Bear Jamboree, and... thrift store? I have to guess this is the only place Thai meets country in the entire universe, and walking into this place I realized why that is. Food would have to save the day here, and it surely did. Ordered the Tom Kha with tofu to start off, and it was a great choice on a chilly day. Really tasty broth, and the tofu was perfect. Followed up that with the old thai standby, yellow curry with vegetables. It was great. Nothing out of the ordinary, but still mighty tasty. Seriously, the vibe here kind of sucks, but if you aren't trying to impress someone on a date this is a good place to get some thai food in the area.

I love asian food, and I love how Saigon makes asian food. I started my lunch with fried dumplings. They seemed fresh and the sauce they were served with added to the experience. I followed the fried dumplings with combo rice and pho special. Combo rice is fried rice with chicken, shrimp, and chunks of some kind of sausage. Delicious. Pho special is one of my favorite Vietnamese foods and I order it pretty regularly so my expectations are pretty high. Saigon did not disappoint. The food is good, and the prices are competitive. The only weird thing about Saigon is that it is closed on Tuesday.
Very Good Yummy Vietnamese food. this is the real deal. its a small deli...nothing fancy here but if you want good Viet food.....this is the place.

This was our first time eating at this restaurant. We were greeted and seated at a window seat over looking the singing fountain square in Passyunk. The food was consistently delicious for the four diners. The vegetarian appetizer offer a mixed pakora. The entries were as familiar as chicken korma to more complex lamb dishes. There is the option to select how much heat your taste buds can handle. Service was very good and friendly. Will definitely return to this restaurant.
Great food. Green and Red curry. Excellent flavors. Great prices and tons of food for lunch. Will definitely return.

Great choice before going to the Kimmel Center. My husband and I had a delightful dinner before hearing the Fabulous Philadelphians.The service was friendly and efficient. The flavors were fresh and fun. The fried items were not greasy. Our favorite items were the chicken coconut soup, Sriracha calamari, crispy duck fried rice, and white elephant dessert.

Amazing food, the only way the meal could get better is if they upgraded their wine list. SAMKE NAYYEH: raw yellowtail, seasoned with chives, parsley, garlic, lemon, jalapeño & labne - 9/10 FATTEH: warm chickpeas, eggplant, crispy pita & tehina yogurt * finished with almonds, cashews & brown butter - 10/10 KAWARMA: baharat rubbed lamb, grilled & slow roasted * served with a pomegranate-cucumber salad & dill yogurt - 10/10 KARUS BALADI tilefish filet marinated in parsley, cilantro &cumin, wrapped in a banana leaf & grilled * served with turmeric rice - 8/10

I've eaten here three times: twice for dinner and once for the buffet. I totally don't agree that this is the "best in Indy." I think it's fairly similar to other Northern Indian restaurants like Shalimar or India Garden--but with a fatal flaw. Read on. THE GOOD For dinner, they bring out tasty papad and chutney. For dinner and lunch, they bring out a generous basket of piping hot nan. It's A- nan in my book, but it's fresh (unlike the nan of many other establishments who leave the bread to languish on the buffet). The food is of pretty good quality. The staff is cheery and attentive. So what's not to dig? THE BAD The food is SALTY, man! It just destroys me. My girlfriend and I split a fish pakora and a goat curry for dinner recently, and I think we lowered the water table because we were drinking so much. Crying out for ¡EL AGUA! Yes, Indian food is not usually your first choice for low-sodium fare. But having half an appetizer and entree and feeling that bad is unacceptable. It's a shame, as their food is pretty well-prepared, otherwise. For example, the ajwain seeds in the fish pakora were a nice touch (by the way, I think the majority of the saltitude was in the curry, not the pakora). THE BUFFET People have given the lunch buffet high marks. I had it today and was unimpressed. There was no more variety than at your typical Indian joint in town. There were no dishes that really blew me away. It was just average--except SALTIER than average. (In fact, I tested out the buffet today even after my previous, salty experiences precisely because so many people were lauding it.) For Indian food in Indy, I recommend Passage to India (my favorite--vegetarian with lots of Southern food, great soups), India Palace (huge lunch buffet with substantial meat dishes), Taj of India (simple but good quality for lunch or dinner), and Shalimar (decent lunch buffet, nice dinner service with good thali).

I really love this place. I love the size of the restaurant (small but in a way that feels cozy,) the parking (FREE,) and the atmosphere. The food is delicious; definitely NOT Mexican. I don't usually go to eat but the few things I have had there have all been good. The soups are hearty enough to be a meal and any of the appetizers are delicious. The braised beef is also quite nice. One word to know before you go: coquito - Coquito - COQUITO. My new favorite cocktail and, at only $5, you'll have to be careful not to drink yourself under the table. I've been informed by a reputable source this is the Puerto Rican equivalent of spiked eggnog. If that's true, we are doing eggnog very, very wrong. Coquito is a creamy, sweet coconut/cinnamon/rum drink with a flavor similar to horchata ... with rum. Reminds me of ice cream. It's heavenly. Three things that will keep me coming back: the coquito, the band (El Movimiento & Marcela Pinilla salsa/jazz it up every Wednesday), and the vibe. The food is great, don't get me wrong, but I like to go to Salsa just to pretend I'm vacationing somewhere south of the States. The music, the drinks, and the people make it so fun - you'll feel like your somewhere else. Staycation anyone? PS. They do not accept AMEX!

Wasn't extremely impressed. When I stopped in during brunch time there were no customers and very little food. The food was just so so. I got what food I could get and left. On the plus side; the place was clean, service was friendly and the prices were average..

Delicious food. Formally was known as Just Jerk, but new owners have come and bought it and changed name and place. Food is authentic, and delicious. Jerk Chicken is the best! Great little spot for good food in Norristown!
Generally I think Indian is expensive, but Mumbai Bistro offers affordable, delicious food. I always go buffet, and they're always clean and courteous.

The food here was excellent - absolutely delicious. The waitstaff were also wonderful. The place is small and intimate. Not fancy. BYOB. My only complaint, and the reason I gave it one less star, was that the restaurant was so loud, my friend and I had to shout to hear each other. We went on a Friday night during dinner hours. I think it may be best to go for as early a dinner as possible before the place fills up.

This is by far the best and most authentic Indian/Pakistani food I've had in St. Louis area- and this is coming from a person who grew up in India! Poori, chole (Chana masala) halwa on the weekends is my favorite part about this restaurant. Growing up that's what my mom cooked every Sunday morning and the Chana masala tastes exactly like my mom's. Highly recommend this restaurant!

We ate at Tryst and got a table right out in front on the patio of downtown St. Pete. The wait staff was very attentive and the place was lively. I had the special of some pork belly sliders that were delicious and a skirt steak with chimichurri for my main entree. We even had the pleasure of the head chef come out to our table, to ask how the food was. It was reasonable priced for the quality of food, service, and ambiance. This restaurant reminded me of something you would find in NYC or Las Vegas. Quaint, but really well laid out and tons of options for food, drinks, or if you wanted to catch a game at the bar.

Yum!!! Went here last week with a few friends, 5 of us total. I wasn't really sure how we were supposed to go about ordering, since in front they have a type of cafeteria set up. We were greeted by Jose and the very pleasant woman working the counter. They were great about accommodating us as "sit down" diners even though I don't think this is the general premise of the restaurant (my friend who picked the restaurant didn't do their research as to what type of set up it was). Anyway, onto the food... We ordered a bunch of different things to share and I can honestly say that everything was great- from the ceviche, to the plantains, to the grilled pork. The chicken and rice was my favorite- so flavorful and moist, unlike some other rice dishes I've tried. I was pretty bummed they didn't have the fried pork chunks- I haven't been able to find good ones since moving back from Miami. I was salivating at the thought of them...I guess I have to go back! Prices are super reasonable as mentioned. Oh, and the tres leches cake...nom nom nom nom! In the midst of all our gorging, we got to talk a little bit with Jose, who turned out to be the owner. He told us that he had had a restaurant in New York but had moved it to Philly. I'm so glad he did. I cannot say enough how gracious he and what appeared to be his only other staff member were at accommodating our awkwardness. I hope Parada Maimon has a bright and prosperous future in our city and look forward to visiting again. If you haven't yet, definitely check them out!

(vegetarian / vegan review) My wife and I eat here regularly. Very regularly. Embarrassingly regularly. If it's been more than a week since the last time we were there, they ask us if everything is okay. Of course everything is okay - we're about to have great Indian food! The service is attentive and polite. The food is very, very good, although it often leaves me feeling a bit heavy. But hey, I can hardly blame them for making food so delicious that I feel compelled to stuff myself silly. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because it's a bit pricey - after adding a tip, one order of appetizer and two main dishes add up to around $30. This isn't terrible, since (a) the food is very good, and (b) we usually have enough leftovers for another serving and a half, but still, it would've been nice if prices were a bit lower. None of this changes the fact that this is one of our favorite places in the world. Proof: We had them cater our wedding. Which, since You ask, was a smash hit. :-)
Amazing Italian food, so fresh and incredible taste. The gnocchi melts in your month, the antipasto plate is to die for and the desert was unbelievable. I will def be going back again and again!
My family and I like the food. Everything seems freshly cooked. Two of us are vegetarians, and they have plenty of dishes to accommodate us.

Who in their right mind argues with a customer??!!HORRIBLE customer service. I got the Pad See Ew. I've had it MANY times from other places. I've never had it spicy before from anywhere except here and the waitress wants to argue with me and try to get me to PAY for it??!!! Who argues with a customer??!! The hell is the matter with these people??!! Needless to say I'm never coming here again

PSA: The week of 8/14/2017 is his 'last week' before he goes on hiatus for renovations to bring on a helper and hopefully shorten the wait time. He'll be out for a couple weeks but will be back very soon with a slightly bigger space. Today's was as amazing as always. I didn't want anything to go to waste and took a bite of the orange pepper after I ate everything else and drank all my water.. it hurts but it hurts so good

The best Thai around period! The food and service are top notch. The food comes out very quickly and always tastes fresh. You must order the crab delights as an appetizer, they are AMAZING! I usually order the garlic and pepper with beef, FANTASTIC! If you go for lunch they give you a free egg drop soup that is fantastic. Portions are quite generous. This place has fair prices and is just hard to beat. Been here many, many times. YUMMY!!!

The dish I had was jerk chicken it was really good !!! Not to spicy with an undertone of sweetness . The plantain were cooked to perfect ! An awesome complement to the chicken . And the cabbage was a wonder array of crux my veggies just the way I like it . I will be back to try more dishes . My only issue is was that the young lady at the desk was slightly rude . But hey maybe she was having a bad day

Shanghai Station is a popular University City Chinese restaurant. It is located right off of the Penn campus in Spruce Hill. I occasionally use it for a quick meal. I don't love this place but it is decent enough. Last evening I had a function at International House and stopped in here beforehand for the Shanghai beef fried noodles. (This is a Shanghai food eatery!) The dish was tasty if a slightly bit oilier than I like. There are no condiments on the table so I had to ask for hot chili sauce which I always use with Shanghai noodles. Also I was never offered tea here as in many Chinese restaurants and my water glass was not refilled. It's a college Chinese restaurant.
I love their Vegetarian sandwich (special #4). the bread is toasted to perfection and the combination of spinach and eggs is mouth-watering. Overall it is very tasty.

It's Nhu Y, not Nhuy. Sorry, I'm being a Vietnamese sandwich snob. Being born and raised in CA, I've had my fair share of Vietnamese sandwiches or "hoagies" and can say this compares to the places that I would not not return to if I were back home. With it's high rating, I was just hoping for something more I guess. This place is definitely meant to be for take out as it is quite small. The couple that owns the place is super nice and friendly. I ordered the Thit Nguoi Dac Biet ($3.00), which includes Cha Lua. Meat was good, pate was good, bread sucked, pickled veggies big time sucked. I guess I'm used to having my sandwich served on a French baguette but what I got instead was more of a hoagie. Not only that but the bread tasted crunchy in the way that it's been left out for too long. As for the pickled carrots and daikon... well, it wasn't pickled. It was completely tasteless and rather than having nice thin slices/strips, they were tiny shavings. Because the veggies were so tasteless and small, it could not balance out the saltiness of the pate and meat. It's just too bad because this is an easy mistake to fix.

Food is ok. Customer service is horrendous. Waited 45 mins for an order that they said would take 20 mins. Place your order at least an hour before picking it up. Do not trust their time judgement. They will come up with lame excuses for the delay in your order. Never coming back here again.

The food we ordered was pretty good here. The veggie pakora was a great deal ($3).... the plate was piled high with deep fried veggies (mostly spinach). The chicken korma and the lamb korma was very flavorful and yummy. My son loved it! My hubby liked it (but said he's had better). We also ordered the sag paneer which was decent. I didn't realize that chicken sagwala was basically identical except had chicken. Still I like it, so I'll be happy to have it for lunch this week. The portions were large enough to share & yet still have leftovers. The service was pretty good and not overbearing. We got refills on drinks when the glasses weren't quite empty which is always nice. The lemonade and soft drinks were only a buck with free refills so it was a bargain! I'll be back. Maybe for lunch buffet!

I have only had drinks here a few times but I love the creative cocktails and the SOBE vibe. Reminds me of back in the day living in Miami. I am very picky about my dining out experiences so based on the other reviews here I think I'll pass. Besides, I found my fave in that area and I'm sticking with it! So, for a creative, lovely cocktail, Tryst gets my vote!

I was really craving some Ethiopian food, and this place totally hit the spot. We went there for lunch on a Friday, and it was pretty empty, but the service was nonetheless pretty slow. Luckily, we were not in a rush, but I wouldn't recommend it for a lunch break during a work week. I also didn't mind the wait that much, since the food wass great, and the server was very friendly and nice. We ordered five different vegetarian dishes to split, and all of them were very good. Most of them were more mildly spiced than I remembered Ethipian food to be (except for the lentil dish), so much so that even my picky 12 year old nephew ended up eating them and thinking the potatoes were delicious. My favorites were the atkil wett, the collard greens and the spinach. I'll definitely be back!

Queen of Sheba is the only Ethiopian food option in Tampa to my knowledge unless of course you are privileged to have a skilled person make it for you at their house or yours. The food at Queen of Sheba has a rich complex flavor profile and is oh-so-tasty. Despite the Mr. proclaiming to not like anything that stewed or cooked hours upon end, he gobbles this food up without hesitation (which leads me to believe its pretense in his part). There you go--Queen of Sheeba is game-changing! We visited on a particular Friday afternoon for their excellent lunch buffer with my vegetarian sister who was visiting. Because Indian food has many vegetarian options it seemed like the easy choice but we wanted her to try something different and outside her comfort zone. There were many options for her who was interested to try this style of cuisine. I found the vegetarian options to be extremely tasty myself. You are provided with copious of injera--a spongey, sourdough-risen flatbread made out of tuff flour--to consume with the entrees which is unique and different. It is very tasty this way but I even love just eating the food as is. There is angled parking outside of the restaurant but it can be limited so get there early for lunch or get creative. I believe the lunch buffet occurs Fridays and Saturdays but I would call to confirm. I look forward to trying more of their menu on subsequent visits. Enjoy!!!

I'm hesitant to 4 star the restaurant after 2 visits....but both visits were stellar! I would actually call it "Asian Fusion". Clean, nice decor, super friendly and attentive service. First time I had honey walnut shrimp and that it was the perfect amount of sweet, not overly. The spring rolls were so good, and the peanut sauce was great. I tried my friends general chicken, and it was crispy, not to saucy, and while not spicy enough for me, it was excellent. The prices are very reasonable, the menu is extensive, and not your run of the mill Chinese at all. Definitely recommend.

Probably the worst tom kha soup I have ever had, and I eat at a thai place almost every other day! The soup was so milky, almost tasted like you are drinking whole milk, no coconut flavor, no lemongrass or ginger flavor. The spicy flat noodles was good. The portions are small for the price. Nothing out of the ordinary.
I am not a big fan of leaving five stars on any of my reviews, but this place is the definitely the best, from their Nan to their Tika Masala , every single dish is just exquisite!
This place was amazingly delicious for a great price. We all tried something different and loved it. If were ever in Tampa again, we'll be definitely coming back!

My girlfriend and I ordered take out from Erawan on a friends recommendation. She got the red curry chicken and I had the pad tai. We ended up sharing both. Both dishes were Very good and the red curry had a nice smooth heat. The chicken pad tai was great with Perfectly thin Noodles and a decent amount of crushed peanuts to provide a nice texture. We will definitely order from here again/have dinner here for a date night or group dinner. The Dining room looks nice.

After having an awesome experience at Chiangmai, T and I wanted to try Thai Orchid as well to see if it could hold up. It did! We had the Tom Yum soup, Fortune Bags, Drunken Noodles and Bold & Spicy Shrimp. Everything was just amazing but seriously, I can't get enough of the drunken noodles. T was the one who ordered the dish but I think I'm going to be forced to get my own next time. And I'd like to try it with shrimp instead of chicken just to change things up. Don't get me wrong, my bold and spicy shrimp were fantastic. Just enough heat to keep things interesting but not completely kill your taste buds. Fresh veggies and rice. Very tasty. But the noodles? There are no comparisons. I will say I thought Chiangmai had a BIT of an edge but that's just personal preference. I'm becoming a VERY big fan of the Thai food ...

I visited this location and we were the only people eating in, the food was absolutely delicious, i was a bit disappointed that you didn't have a choice of what you had as a side with the plates . It's default rice and peas with cabbage. I think they should give the option being as though the price is a bit more expensive then my local Jamaican spots which are just as good. But the curry goat was definitely tender and flavorful. The cabbage was made great , not too cooked down , just right . The only think I can say is that the waitress could've been a bit more up beat since we were the only people in the place. That's why I have put only 3 stars . I would maybe gone back , but for take out only .

Great ambiance!!! Good service with yummy authentic Indian food!! One of my favorite Indian restaurant in town,I'm a vegetarian,but surprisingly this place has lot of options to satisfy my taste buds ,I highly recommend this place to everyone, don't forget to try the panneer tikka masala ,navaratna korma!!and the gulab jamoon!!! Its the best. Stop in,try the delicious food, I promise you will not be disappointed!!

These people are fast! Even better the food is excellent. Our business orders from them at least once if not 3 times a week and we have never been disappointed. The quantity is good and the prices more than reasonable. Personal favorite it the drunken noodle, and make it spicey! A pretty different egg role than I am use to but delicious all the same. Any one want to go?

3.5 stars! MMM Great hummus. Kabobs are tasty. Chicken is tender. I love the pumpkin spiced entree. the rice is great too. Good service. It's not hip and fancy inside, but you come for the food! So much flavor!

I would try again just because I'm not sure where else to get this type of food in Newtown, but we were not impressed. We had a combo platter with chicken and falafel. Meh. And the pita did not seem fresh. I did try a piece of baklava that was very good, but then again, anything doused in honey should be pretty good.
The tofu hoagie is great and an awesome deal, what a delicious treat! Not much else to say but if this was closer to my house I'd eat it every day and look like a balloon!

Bought a Dealchicken Cert for this businesses other location... same Owner... They closed that location before I the coupon expireed.. I went to thier main location adn they refused ot honor the COupon... told me that was for other locationa and essentially left me hanging.. Never mind its same owneres and same name.. SCREW THIS PLACE... Idont care if the food is the best in Reno I will never eat there.. would have cost them $10 to cover cost of coupon and I would have taken it in food and spent another $10 on the spot.. Remmber.. 2 fat people = lots of $$ next time... Now to complain to the BBB , Deal chicken and Mastercard about them
This place is pretty close to our house and always hits the spot when a Thai craving hits! It's well priced and we've never been disappointed.

I dropped by this café by chance without any expectations. For a place in Philadelphia I got impressed by the worn out, old style furniture which adds to a casual but personal atmosphere. I ordered a mushroom quiche which was heated up and to my surprise served with a fresh but sinple green salad on the side. Real olives were tasty as were the pickles too. All of this for just about 6$! Great place for having a light lunch or just a coffee. I spent my time reading a book while other customers on their tables seemed to be working on their laptops meaning it's a great place to concentrate on own thing without noise or interruptions.

Ever since moving from Baton Rouge, I have been hoping Albasha would open in the NOLA area.... as you can imagine, THIS EXCITES ME. Besides Lebanon, this whole area lacks delisciousMediterranean food. This is the best. The best gyro, chicken shawarma, hummus, everything. This IS the only place to go for Greek/Lebanese. Gyro is still heavenly as ever. To go plates are still plenty for next day lunch leftovers. Plenty of parking in this shopping center. It is BYOB
Great food great people! The food blew my mind when i tried it. Now I'm here Every weekend ordering something to eat

Love this place! It's cozy and comfy and had so many different things besides coffee. It's a cute neighborhood spot to sit with friends or get some work done. I often get their bagels and lavender iced tea when I'm on the run. They have a lot of fresh baked goods and now soup for fall. Whenever I'm working from home I find myself coming here to get the hummus platter. The pita and hummus are both so fresh and tasty. If you haven't been here yet, check it out !

In the mood for something different, we decided to try a spot we've never been to. I debated the baked chicken platter with mac and cheese and veggies, but then decided to try the fish hoagie. $9.50? I was concerned that it would be a little fish filet on a sub roll. However, it was amazing! The fish was perfectly seasoned and fried. And they provided so much fish that I could only eat half. I enjoyed the atmosphere and friendly service! I definitely recommend this place and can't wait to go back.

Update: Have been here three times in the past year. The food remains outstanding and the price and quantity extremely satisfying to both wallet and stomach! What I truly appreciate as a parent about this place is they really are good with kids!! Each time they have very graciously accommodate our needs with regards to strollers and meal times messes or meltdowns! They don't ignore your child at all and bring crackers/cookies and chat with him in a fun and friendly and genuinely interested manner! This is our sure shot place to take people for dinner when we have our little guy with us as we know we will enjoy the food and the service both!
Wonderful food great staff, try to get here whenever we ar e in Tucson. We are always made to feel welcome, even when we arrives just as they are closing. Always a great experience.
Pretty amazing chicken fingers and Mac n cheese, the dessert pies are also definitely worth trying

Just a straightforward great neighborhood place to check out. No frills, tight, often busy BYO. Nothing wrong with any of this. Pil pil shrimp are awesome - spicy, garlicky, addicting. Octopus is served as heaps of tentacles rather than the sparse portion you get elsewhere (for more money, too) and fried smelts are a great dish to share along with everything else. Not much else to say except...go!
This place is a hidden gem! Homemade quality that far exceeds every other Thai restaurant in Tampa.

Wow, really great dinner!! Great service, friendly staff! Flavourful food! My first time eating Indian food, so I have nothing to compare it to. It was delicious. Goat curry, flavours of lamb. Wonderful. Peas and potatoes in a gravy all warm in spices! Ordered medium on the spice level. It started very hot, but simmered as we continued enjoying. Rice included with dinner and rice pudding/soup served for dessert. The two of use ate for under 50.00 with a healthy tip!! Great meal!!!

We went to Island Breeze Cafe for takeout a few weeks ago, and our experience was less amazing than the first. We ordered jerk chicken; they were out of jerk chicken. It wasn't even 6pm, so that was kind of a shock. So we ordered curried chicken. I asked if there were any desserts available, and the woman that works there said that they wouldn't have desserts until a couple of days from then. (Huh?) We get our food home and start chowing down. Only...what we received was not chicken. The carton I grabbed had a mix of meats. Some was clearly chicken, and some clearly was not. My boyfriend's carton contained only the "clearly was not." The mystery meat was full of little bones and proved to be a little more difficult to eat. I Googled and ruled out ox tail. It would seem that we were served goat. The fact that I received a mix of meat in my carton indicates to me that it wasn't just a mistake. I think they probably ran out of curried chicken in addition to the jerk chicken and, instead of letting us know, just threw whatever was available into our bag. Everything tasted good, but I love goats. I would've preferred to live my life without eating one. :( If it was an instance in which we just got whatever was left, I would have appreciated it if the kitchen had let us know. We would've ordered something else or taken our business elsewhere. Also -- The restaurant was affected by the floods of August 8, 2013. Island Breeze is closed at present.

I could literally eat here every day for lunch if I lived in this area. The falafel and the fresh baked pitas are second to none. Amazing fresh flavors. I will come back the next time I have work in this area.

Food is average. I went on a night that the chef was at their other location so even though we had asked for indian spicey the food came out sweet. When we asked why we were told that the chef was at the other place. Call ahead and check if chef is at this location prior to going...they charge the same inflated price even though the food is pre cooked and just reheated.

I've been twice so far, only living in Valrico for a month, and I'm proud to say I'll be coming back. Being a native to Clearwater, it was not difficult for me to travel to Pinellas Park for delicious, authentic pho and banh mi. Ever since I moved to Gainesville, I dread how boring Pho is up there. Now being in Valrico for 10 weeks, Pinellas Park is still a drive but Saigon Corner has made my cravings easier. I've gotten the combo pho and meatballs and sliced beef pho. When I ordered the combo, the lady had trouble understanding my English so she forgot that I requested no tripe...not a big deal, I'm not a big fan but I'll eat it. There was lots of tendon, but it was really more like just fat. I prefer my tendon to have a little beef on it for extra flavor instead of just chewing into fat so I did not like the tendon in my soup. Second time, I brought my friend and we both enjoyed our #8 pho with meatballs and sliced beef. The broth is very flavorful and concentrated, not watered down like some places. We both got decent amount of meatballs and beef so I'm not sure if previous reviewers had gone in on bad days?? Their summer rolls are OK, I like mine to be with shrimp, pork and thai basil; these seemed to have grass(?)/lettuce and shrimp. The thai tea is very very sweet! But very good. The Banh Mi was so good! What a secret! For $4, you are getting a steal: lot's of pickled veggies, pate, and roughly 7"-8" of crunchy bread filled with greatness (I got the grilled pork one but I bet the cold cuts is just as good). I went to Saigon Deli on 60 and was not too happy about how overpriced and not-as-good their banh mi was. I do agree, they had a lot of NY styled Chinese and Thai dishes. I don't really mind though, I always order pho when I get Vietnamese anyways.

Excellent service and the dining room is very nice. Good selection of wines. Food was interesting. I had a combo plate of lamb chicken and beef. Rich and mild would be how I would describe the flavor. Might have enjoyed it more with a sauce but it was good. My companion had the lamb shanks (2) and he like them. The portions are large- good place to split a single dinner.

An awesome experience in New Hope's Ferry Market. Super flavorful delicious food. Knowledgeable, friendly, caring and passionate team! My husband and I eat a vegan / plant-based diet and loved their vegan options. We had the veggie empanadas (wow, yum), a bit of one of the vegan friendly soups (again wow!) as well as a Lima salad (hearty, nutritious and delicious). We arrived for dinner just before closing on a Friday night and the team was still welcoming, extremely informative, and to be honest made our stop one of the most awesome experiences we've ever had. Major kudos again on the veggie food and caring team!! They could offer courses on how to welcome and care for customers. :)
Can't help but love this place. Their duck curry is amazing and the service is always fast.

One of my favorite places to eat in IV during my undergrad! The pho is always good and their customer service is excellent. The lady who works there is friendly and even remembered my usual order. I will definitely be stopping by the next time I'm in the Santa Barbara area.

If one has been to regions where "real" Indian food is served, e.g. the UK where there is a huge Indian population and/or in NYC, one will realize this food doesn't come near what good Indian food is. It's bearable, but I wouldn't waste time and money on it again. This was the second time there and I would say there had been no change from the first visit. The staff were very pleasant. Sadly, that doesn't improve the quality of the food.

Just had Sunday buffet with family of ten! Very nice food Great hosts! Ample food selection Perhaps needs a little more timely and prompt desert refill Maybe a foyer to be added to the entrance to ensure a more hygienic and temperature wise conducive exclusivity of the eating area Overalls great eating experience

I would hate to work in the convenience store across the parking lot from the Latin Twist Food truck. It would be hell constantly breathing in the smoke from the grilled meats on the barbecue without being able to partake. Latin Twist has a permanent station at the corner of Boise Avenue and Beacon Street, at the bottom of Protest Hill. It's a good spot, close to the Boise State University campus and plenty of drive-by traffic. I tried a rib plate and it was fantastic. The meat was tender and falling off the bone and no would complain if you ate it with your fingers. It was served with a salad topped with chimichurri dressing that was also good and a tropical fruit salsa that was very tasty. And the yellow Columbian rice and Cuban black beans were also delicious. The truck has an extensive menu, including Jamaica jerk, Cuban sandwiches, pibil from the Yucatan and even burritos. Latin Twist makes a great addition to Boise's food scene.

It is the only Ethiopian that I know of in the Reno area. I have eaten at several other Ethiopian restaurants in the past and indeed Ethiopian food is my favorite next to Chinese and Indian. The lentil and the Doro Wat was fair to slightly above average but the Collard green and the Cabbage was not so. The owner was personable and friendly which makes up for the points I give this restaurant.
Best Puerto Rican food in Tampa! Food is always fresh and prices are good for the amount of food you get. Nothing fancy just a good old food truck with friendly service and great food.

I ordered food for delivery for my family. We were told it would take 45min for delivery. 2.5 hours later food wasn't delivered and the restaurant didn't pick up my calls. I will never order from them again.

My wife and both I love Thai food and we were taken here by a friend a few years ago. This is one of the best I've ever experienced and "checking" it last night, it was again superb for us and our guest. The service is charming and fast, the food unbeatable. In spite of being on State Street, the restaurant is not noisy, probably because of the size of the room. A very enjoyable evening for dinner.

I had the TropiChop & side of plantains. Everything was over cooked and tasted like crap! I may just continue going to your Pinellas Park location. The workers need to be properly trained on how to cook the food.
Great spot! Family owned; excellent curried chicken and lovely service. Definitely worth a visit.

I have been to dosa hut quite a few times in the past month. This is the only restaurant in the area which serves south indian. As the name suggests, this place is mainly to satisfy your dosa craving . The dosas and the sambar served very hot and tasted nice. The chutneys are also pretty good. The place is clean and the parking is also pretty sufficient. The service was also very friendly. The appetizers were also good. The one gripe i have about this place is the time it takes to get service when because of the number of people who take orders are less. So we have to wait long time before person comes to take our order.

I almost feel bad about giving Taj 3 stars. It's definitely some of the best Indian food I've had, and if it were served in center city I'm sure it would be a hit. Unfortunately, it's in the northeast and not very many people frequent it. I'm also afraid my review won't be very specific... Indian food has an inventive and unique flavor combination that requires the use of spices that I'm sure I haven't even heard of before. And the names of the dishes are too difficult for me to remember if I've only had them once. As I said, the food is great. We started with the vegetable appetizer platter, which had four different types of appetizers on it. But the amount of each type was so awkwardly decided: four of the onion fritter things, two of these other things, and just one of the spring roll and the giant other thing. For the entree, I had a lentil dish with a tomato-onion-spice sauce. This was delicous! But I was a bit put-off because they don't give you rice with your meal unless you buy two entrees. Since we were a party of two, we got the free rice but it was a small amount for two people. Not enough for the portion size of the entree, but just enough for the amount I actually ate in the restaurant. The service and atmosphere are very meh. But I think that's okay for the northeast. In center city it definitely wouldn't fly. I would definitely consider this place if I were in the NE, but it's not worth a drive from CC just for it.
My favorite Thai food restaurant! Love their dishes like the poor man noodles and chili basil chicken!

This is my 2nd visit to this restaurant. First time was average, would give it 3.5/5 stars because food was decent but service was awful. After this 2nd visit I will NEVER come back. Place was half empty and took 10 minutes til we were Seated (no one came to greet us). Then took another 15 minutes til a waiter took our order and they said they were OUT OF PHO! How do you run out of pho by 730 on a Friday night? That's like an Italian restaurant running out of noodles. Between the poor service and average food look elsewhere. Best to drive to the city or go a few extra miles elsewhere for a better experience.

My Saturday night 7-course "feast" at Fez provided a fun distraction from the din of the holiday season. I was glad I was there with good company because the night stretched out longer than anyone could have anticipated. Most of the food has been adequately and accurately covered in other reviews, so I won't go into too much detail. I will echo that the style of bread they hand out is not well-suited to use as a scooping, eating utensil; pitas would be MUCH better. The food was, overall, forgettable with the exceptions of the delicious pickled carrots that came with the salad and the truly excellent whole chicken that we tore into like savages. The meal was a decent value for the $25 price tag. The belly dancer brought her A-game, dancing at least four sets of 15-20 minutes apiece, with ~30 minute breaks in between. The crowd really got into it, and many people got up to dance with and tip her. Now, if you do the math on the time-frames that I listed, you will see that we were at Fez for a LONG TIME. In fact, we were there for well over 4 hours. We enjoyed the pace of the first half of our meal, and were pleased that we were not being overly rushed. However, following our fourth course, our table became like the forgotten step-child of the restaurant. We sat for at least half an hour following the completion of each course, and could not catch the attention of any of the waiters. We had also run out of wine and water during some of these stretches, which made them seem even longer. We ordered a "Tangerine Dream" hookah, which ended up being a surprise highlight of the night since we had ordered it primarily for the novelty. The smoke was very smooth, and the flavor was pleasantly reminiscent of Tang, leading to amused speculation that perhaps it is what the astronauts smoke. Overall, I do not regret my trip to Fez but am not in a hurry to go back. If I did return, it would more likely be a late-night stop for some hookah and a cocktail or wine rather than a repeat of the glacially paced "feast".

The old patriarch who sits in the corner, shoes off, and stares at me is the best part of the decor. Also, when "Mr. Bean's" doppleganger is working I feel happy. He is nice. I love this place. It has never let me down. Their lunch buffet is really good, too. Tucson is lucky to have this restaurant. It is my favorite Indian restaurant in Tucson. It is one of my favorites ANYWHERE! As a side note: Shere Punjab gets extra bonus points for having Guinness Extra Stout. I hardly ever drink, but having this specific option is great.

To start I have been here a few times and India sizzling keeps me returning. The north Indian food is standard with a small selection of south Indian food available. The masala dosas are delicious and come highly recommended. A nice, neat restaurant comes with the family vibe. Would recommend it for someone wanting to experience the differences in Indian cuisine while on a budget. Thumbs up in my book!

Best chai lattes in the city (but I get them half sweet). This location, especially, is always busy as many university students study there. There is some parking along the side of the building which makes it very convenient in this area. Otherwise, there is some street parking nearby. I am a big fan of their butter chicken wrap and samosas. They have a combo for two samosas and a chai latte!

Cash only. You never know what you are going to get for the day. No sign or anything. Rain, snow or sun which never forbid us to wait for at least 40 mins to get this delicious food. Oh, how much I have missed the college days and good old Philly. You have to be prepared for the surprise and not make any adjustments to the food. People who are in the line already are the usual customers and know what they are getting and boy, Am I proud of say that I am a loyal one since this food truck is on the top of my food priority list for my annual Philly trip. Try it and you won't regret it. Food is full of flavor and it also comes with seasonal fruits. Falafel is the best from this food truck since it's fried fresh for each order.
I like this place. it's very clean and inviting with great food. I really love their "Beef Salad". It was tasty, and spicy that I'd want to come back for more!!!!
The restaurant is above average , its more like a Mediterranean fast food. I expected more from gyro than flavored rice , plain cooked meat and sour cream.

I would not recommend this to anyone. We went despite the negative reviews because of the menu options and the pictures of the plates, showing what seemed to be delicious food options and savory drinks. Should have listened to yelp!! Service took FOREVER. First round of drinks were too sweet but at least refreshing, ordering another round was a horrible decision as they both tasted like straight soda with gin and mint thrown in at the end (an attempted mojito, cmon.. That's the name of your restaurant). Food was bland, ceviche came with literally 5 chips and the tres leche cake (thank goodness it was free from the yelp check in) was frosted with what seemed to be shop rite brand birthday cake frosting... Not satisfied.

This is one of my favorite restaurants not only in West Philly but in all of Philly. They have a great lunch special where you get soup, an appetizer, and an entree for about $9. The Pad Thai and fresh spring rolls are excellent. I also recommend any of the curry dishes with tofu. The pho was a little lackluster but I chalk that up to the vegetarian broth. Portions are large, so I normally have to bring half home. They have nice outdoor seating in the summer. There's also a free city parking lot right around the corner if you can't take Septa. (The 34 trolley line runs right in front of the cafe).

This is truly outstandingly good Mediterranean food. So glad I found this place on my last day of a business trip in St. Louis before flying out of town. I had the Egg Salad with white anchovy and the Speck sandwich. The subtle hints of lemon in both were amazing. I walked all the way here from Park Plaza Hotel 40+ minujust to take a nice long walk only to find they were closed between shifts, but will he came to the rescue.
Fantastic place. We have been going there for years and the quality is always excellent. My favorite is the two friends panang. Highly recommend it.
Waited 10 min and didn't get served at all. The host is just on her phone and when she finished she walked off. Hmmm...what can I say?

YOU MUST EAT HERE! My husband and I were wow'ed by the food and service here! It's a tiny yet charming BYO restaurant with amazing food! We had reservations at 6pm on a Wednesday and it was PACKED. Reservations are a must as we have seen people get turned away. Our favorites of the night were the antipasto siciliano, gnocchi alla argentiera, tagliatelle al limone (get it with bottarga), and the special which was orata, quite possibly the best fish dish I have ever had. IMO it's better than Osteria or Vetri in Philly and the service is always spot on. Will definitely be coming here many times :) Edit: It's unfortunate that people give this place a 1 star just because they couldn't secure a seat. Make reservations ahead of time, even for a weeknight!

Oh my goodness this place is AMAZING!! We live in Miami area so there are Caribbean places everywhere but none that compare to Yah Mon. The ambiance is nice. Love the live plants on the tables and the booth seating. I ordered the Caribbean Chicken Sampler Platter and I am so glad that I did. It by far was the best Caribbean food I've tasted and I've been to the islands several times. I also had the bread pudding which was very tasty! The owner was so nice and gracious and truly cares about his customers. We hope they will open in Miami! And if not, we will definitely be coming back to Tampa just to come eat there again.

Went there yesterday with seven of us, four who were new to Indian food. The service was very good, and the restaurant seemed to be very empty. All the dishes were acceptable. i didn't care for the bindi (okra) but the lamb and chicken dishes were excellent. All in all a good experience

It's not often you find a buffet place with consistent quality control, but you do here. I've been here a dozen times, and each time the food was tasty. They also have quite a bit of variety in their selections.

The servers work in sync and are very nice, the food is always delicious. The Honey drink and honey chips are superb, this is my second time getting the chicken tibs and we got the sample for two people, we killed it . thank you ladies for the nice ambiance.

Guru's is the absolute best Indian around. Every single dish we've had has been outstanding. The lunch buffet is extensive and it's impossible not to overeat. We have a toddler and the staff is super friendly and accommodating. Gurus is, easily, our favorite restaurant around.

A decent place to grab lunch or an easy casual dinner. Very fresh and favorable for chain restaurant fare. A nice break from burgers, pizza and more typical lunch choices. A somewhat strange mix of food items, but it works and tastes good.

OK, I''m doin' it. I am giving this mom 'n pop, cash only BYO the full 5 stars - based on that 5 star food. Simple, fresh flavors - like a party in your mouth. Yes - it's cramped and close quarters. And there's a sign on the back kitchen door that says, "Beware Attack Waitress" and they are not kidding - those ladies can work it! Yes - there are 3 terrific Laotian cooks, grilling up greek fish. And it somehow all just works. Perfectly. A close friend and I (tip - do not come with an odd number of people - a single gets stuck at the counter, and a 3 will be forced to do a deuce with an extra chair) ate dinner here. We split everything and ordered just right. Mozzarella & Tomato salad was delicious, fresh, easy to eat and cut up home-style. Perfectly seasoned. Baba (no Ghanoush - ha, ha!) was some of the BEST I've ever had, bursting with charred eggplant flavor, olive-y richness and fresh garlic zing. Not too oily. Just AWE inspiring. (Great with that char-grilled pita.) Next came a perfect Scampi (or Gambas if you were in Spain) with an abundance of fruity olive oil, garlic and paprika. Delish. (Dip some of that pita in the oil when nobody is looking!) And they are not skimpy with the shrimpies. We had at least a dozen. And a platter of grilled veggies - mostly Zucchini and Green Bell Peppers, but also a few red onions, pepperocini & olives. It also had 2 BIG hunks of fresh (bulgarian or greek??) feta. I would have liked to see some RED peppers and EGGPLANT in there. Drinks & Desserts are mothing to speak of here - and I coulda used a nice Lemonade - but the house brewed iced tea (in a teeny tiny glass) was good. I had 2 of 'em. I can easily seeing just giving this place 4 stars - it is NOT fine dining and there were a few service related flaws, but for pure, simple Greek/Med cuisine (and perhaps the East Coast's BEST BABA) I give them 5. And I can't wait to go back. And I kinda want to try the other location on 22nd Street, too.

Best Indian food we've had in Nashville. This mom and pop hidden gem is worth the drive to nolensville. Highly recommend the veg kottu. We also loved the Bollywood dosa, coriander naan, lentil patties and chicken biryani. Can't wait to go back!
We order carry out often and it's always hot and fresh. Our order is always correct even when we make specifications. Portions are large, expect to have leftovers!

2nd time here, and the food is great! This little shop does a perfect job at authenticity with the seasoning, and ingredients. The blend of flavors is outstanding, and the portions are plentiful! Highly recommended!

Amazing food, Great staff, at a great price. The food was so exceptional! My husband is Vietnamese, so he knows his pho. We usually have to go to Philadelphia to get good Vietnamese food, so i am beyond excited we found this place rite around the corner! If I could give more stars I would, it is definitely a must try!!!!

Leaning more towards 3.5 stars if Yelp had half star ratings. This place is alright. It's the only game in this part of town for Viet (Viet fusion?) food.
