Kinda pricey, but I guess they can charge that for being the only Viet restaurant in downtown Clearwater. $5.50 for a regular banh mi?! I have only ordered take out from here and taken it back to work. The restaurant is nice though, modern and cute. I have tried their Korean short rib banh mi, egg rolls, lemongrass pork spring rolls and basil beef noodles. Oh and the Vietnamese iced coffee. Coffee was not as strong as it should have been, tasted watered down. Sandwich, egg rolls, and spring rolls are good-- would definitely recommend ordering. The basil beef noodles were bland and all of my rice noodles were clumped together-- would not order again. Service was very prompt and friendly and I never had to wait long for my orders.

I've been to Ekta a couple of times and really enjoyed it. The first time was a year or so ago - that time, we all had the buffet which was a great way for me to try out Indian food for the first time. Apparently they were losing money on it though, so they recently shut it down. Went again last week and had the Vegetable Biryani which was just outstanding. Also tried a couple of appetizers - Vegetable Samosa, Onion Bhaji, and the Cashew Rolls. We declared the Onion Bhaji (little fritters of onions, spinach, and potatoes) the winner. The Samosa was pretty good too, but the Cashew Rolls were really gummy and we just didn't really care for them. Guess I'd have to say that Ekta is now my go-to Indian food place. Couldn't eat Indian food every day, but once in a while, it's a nice treat!
They have an entire vegan/vegetarian menu which is really nice. I got curry and it was really good! The spicy was extremely spicy so next time I'll just get medium.

This review lands between 3&4. As mentioned this place opened up within the last 6 months or so and so deserved our attention! Just inside one of the busiest intersections in the Reno area it offered a delightful quite place for lunch. There were just a few seated but to be fair we were there late for lunch but early for diner. Being new it still had the "new" crisp qualities. Surroundings were good not overly done. The staff was very attentive through the entire seating. We each had single entree selections as no combination plate was offered for under 10 dollars. There were three of us and my wife and I picked the same meal, a rare occurance! So it was snow pee and chicken X2 and sesame chicken for one with all three served with hot and soar soup and fried rice all three for 8.50 each. With the single entree there were about 12 or so offered at three price tiers- 7.50/8.50/9.50. Rice came either plain or traditionally fried, mine was a bit on the dry side and had a few dozen raw kernels of rice mixed in- I have never experienced that even at home! It was disconcerting to say the least. Taste of both the entree and soup was very good (it is hard to mess up either) with portion size adaquate. I will probably go back on occasion but not for the single entree which I felt was slightly overpriced. An oriental restaurant on this corner is a welcomed addition!

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Went to lunch with my wife and family today, and I absolutely fell in love with this place! The food is out of this world. It really really exceeded my expectations! I had the orange chicken which was very light, it was the best I have had anywhere around. My wife had the pad thai, with chicken. The freshness and all white meat was wonderful. The spring rolls with peanut sauce were also amazing. Our meals came with salad and for $10, it was incredible. I highly highly recommended this place and can't wait to go back! I really want to try the mango and sweet rice dessert. You will not be disappointed!

Had two meals from here. The pho soup was inedible - huge drops of fat and no flavor. Chicken felt like rubber. Really bad. The noodle dish was okay - not gross, but not good. Need to revisit their recipes. I

Ordered: Combination Fried Rice (Beef, Chicken , Shrimp) - Cleaned the plate, good flavor for fried rice dish, good meat portion Vegetarian Lo Mein - Substantial amount of vegetables, slightly oily but tasty and satisfying Ambiance: -Warm, noise level average Service: -Super fast, got food within 10 minutes

Just had a great experience at this new place. The staff was very friendly and attentive. The manager introduced himself right away and our main waiter gave great recommendations and was very considerate. The drinks that we tried were good (our favorites were the tropical mojito and ruby dragon). For food we tried pork and crabmeat dumplings, dan dan noodles, and walnut shrimp. All were delicious and came out quickly. We will definitely be coming back!

Wow, after eating at Jaipur last night and being very impressed with the food I was shocked at the negative reviews I read on Yelp. Now everyplace can have and off night but the food we had last night was superb, authentic, just about perfect. The service and cordial treatment we got was clearly at odds with the other reports. As to cost comparisons, the very best does cost more and these folks do it correctly. We will return often.

Came here to celebrate a friends birthday. There were 6 of us, so we got a booth with curtains that you can close and we felt like we were in our own little world. Not having Greek food before, I didn't know what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised. Being the beer girl that I am, I decided to try something different for a change (plus no Sam Adams). I went with Athena which is Creamy chocolate martini blended with Godiva Liqueur (more like an after dinner beverage) and also Sappho Absolut vodka, Apple Liqueur and lemonade (what can I say, I like to drink). We ordered the Momos Spread Sampler to get the party started. You get your choice of three spreads and they are all served with pita. We ended up ordering 2 of them so that we could sample all of the yummy goodness. I love humus and pita, and just eating all these spreads was like heaven. We tried Baked Brie Cheese, Crab Cakes, Steak Kabob Salad, Gyro and all sorts of other goodness. The best part is that it is tapas so that we were able to share them all. Great evening with good food, friends and beverages. My kind of evening!

I decided to give this place a shot based on the Yelp reviews and am definitely pleased with the result. We came on an evening for some appetizers and beer. The gorgonzola salad and shrimp flatbread were amazing. The server was very friendly and attentive too. The front patio was a little chilly at first but they turned on the heaters shortly after we sat down and it made for an enjoyable fall evening. The prices are a little steep but given the location and service, I think it was worth it.

Amazing fun place to dine and drink until 2am in St. Pete! Awesome atmosphere, great music, sports TVs, and great food!! I absolutely loved their Mediterranean dip platter (their hummus and tzaziki sauce iS incredible!!) Service is top notch and they even keep the kitchen open late to feed us! Love this place!!! Definitely going back!!!

I'm always suspicious of negative reviews, especially about a place that has so many glowingly good ones. I always think.. this is just an overly critical person with unrealistic expectations. Well, I can only speak from personal experience, but the food that I ATE here sucked. First of all, they brought me garlic sauce chicken when I had ordered the shrimp. Ok fine, human error. I'll eat it anyway. Sadly, it tasted like the worst airport Panda Express faux 'Chinese Food' that I've ever had. I just wish I could stop burping so I wouldn't have to keep tasting it over, and over, and over again.
Seriously delicious food for a great price. I usually add a little lettuce on my gyro and it's wonderful & cheap lunch.
The tandoori was fantastic! Service was good. Very pleasant atmosphere. Wife and I will definitely become regulars.

Good food get the chicken or lamb curry it's amazing. The jerk is fantastic. I like the oxtail but nothing compares to their curry dishes. The fish was so so. I am looking forward to trying the rib eye. Wine doesn't meet the same standard the food does but is workable. Not sure why they don't seat people in the booths?
Great food and customer service! Absolutely recommend for a quick, healthy, and delicious meal.

Wow, I was shocked and awed. I can be pretty critical of restaurants, but this place exactly delivers what it should, for what it is. I really enjoy a good gyro, and there aren't many places in the bay area that can deliver on that, and not even in Tarpon Springs. We thought we'd try this, but were hesitant because it's kind of in a bad area by Busch Gardens, and it's set up as a fast-food dine-in and drive through format. The menu is pretty limited, but that's okay. And it's open late. I got the gyro and Greek salad, and it was the best I've had in years anywhere in the bay area. I just wish I could have gotten a separate order of their very nice grape leaves, which only comes with the Greek salad. The Greek salad and dressing was very nice and fresh, with nice tomatoes, cucumber slices and pitted black olives with feta cheese. The mashed potato salad in the Greek salad wasn't so great, but that didn't matter to me with everything else being so good. The gyro meat was great, not too salty or too greasy, moist and just right, and cooked perfectly on their rotisserie. The pita was fresh, excellent. The tzatziki sauce was thick and tasty with cucumber and garlic. The portion size is generous, too, I made two meals out of it so it was quite a bargain. I also got an order of their smooth hummus with olive oil, just great for dipping in their excellent bread. (I took most of the hummus home and added my own salmon roe to make the perfect Greek caviar). I really wish they had Greek caviar (Taramasalata) there, then this place would be utterly perfect (hint, hint) I highly recommend this if you like gyros done right! But, although the previous items were spectacular, their "chop chop salad" is a big nothing, just bland diced tomatoes and cucumbers, and their chicken wings are terrible, way overcooked and dry. We ordered wings on two different occasions and they were so bad and petrified we had to throw them out without more than a few nibbles. So, skip the wings, definitely.

I was excited to see an Indian restaurant open up in East Passyunk. We ordered the chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, and the garlic naan to go. (We were in the neighborhood and didn't feel like dining in that night) I'd say the food isn't as authentic as other Indian places I have tried. However, I do think it's a good place for those who never tried Indian food before and would not get too overwhelmed by their strong flavors. Would I come back? It would depend if I'm going with friends who hasn't tried Indian cuisine before.
Aways delicious. Pop in weekly and have a great meal with friendly waitresses.

Walked out after waiting over 45 minutes for appetizer. Despite our servers insistence that our food was coming right up, all the tables seated after us started receiving their food. It also took them over 5 minutes to acknowledge our existence upon arrival even though they seemed to be well staffed and the restaurant was mostly empty. Should have taken that as a sign...
Best Asian restaurant we've found in Mt. Laurel... and we tried a lot of em! Great food, staff and prices!

Delicious! It's about time Madison, TN gets a decent, affordable, authentic place! The staff (shout out to our waiter, Frank) are extremely friendly and the food is incredible!! The phone number is now programmed in my phone...We go every week and if we don't make it, we call in! I highly recommend this place!!

Terrible. Terrible. Worst Thai food I have ever eaten. Very small quantities for the money. But looking back on it - that is the best part of the experience. Frozen veggies, greasy sauce and cardboard-like meat. Could not have told the difference between the beef and chicken. Same color, same taste, same texture. Terrible.
This place has some of the best Chinese food I've ever had. Everything taste fresh ,the prices aren't bad, and the portion size is nice. This place is a definite repeat.
So good! Love everything on the menu here! I'd love to see a little more rice with the curry dishes but other than that we love the food!
Food is delicious and a great value! I wish it was closer so I could get dinner from here too!

Went to this spot on Thursday evening around 11pm. I had been searching Yelp for places to eat at that hour besides fast food and found 8th & Union with great reviews. Place was pretty much empty besides some of the staff at the bar having a bite to eat and a drink! I don't blame them after being told how hectic it was earlier in the day. Took a seat at the rustic looking bar adorned with 2 big screen tv's and was greeted immediately! Ordered a Moscow mule (my absolute favorite) and received it quickly. The drink was good but there is nothing like drinking a Moscow mule in an actual bronze mule. But the taste of the drink more than made up for it! Food was delicious and I didn't wait long for it to be prepared and bought to me... Even at 11pm!! I ordered Pot of Mussels with french fries and guacamole with crab meat. Both were equally satisfying!! I wanted to drink the broth the mussels were in and immediately regret getting fries instead of bread to sop it up with. I certainly visit again and recommend this place to anyone wanting good food, good drinks & 80's tunes playing in the background.

Always a good experience, and when it wasn't 100% the staff made sure we didn't leave without it being just that. There is rarely a wait for the food and quality is consistent. Management is always visible. There are many regulars here and it is obvious why. The staff truly makes this place which is why we come so often.

Been there four times. The first time was not a great experience and is documented in a separate review from my friend. Chalk it up to a new restaurant getting into the swing of things. Since then have dined in the restaurant twice and had take-out. The experiences have been superb. The staff is terrific (special call outs to the bartender Mike and the waitress Chrissie). The owner Anthony checks in regularly and is very down to earth and open to feedback. The food is outstanding and is served tapas style (small portions) and they explain that from the outset. Lots of great food we had from the tuna ceviche, beef tartare (I would add an actual egg yolk though), perfectly cooked scallops, pasta and sausage, cheese & meat board, deconstructed cannoli, and caramel & pretzel budino (although it could be bigger). It is also well decorated and has a great atmosphere! We loved it there and will definitely be going back!!

Now this place was certainly a pleasant surprise! Great Cuban sandwich, very nice little egg dish and good burger (though really over cooked). If I had pick a negative, it would be that they don't really have many good non-alcoholic drinks, and the waitress came over to our table like five times to ask us if everything was ok. It got a little annoying. Solid place!

Delicious food! Friendly staff! Clean restaurant! The gyro was so good and the sauce was perfect! Pits great soft but crunchy and the hummus was delightful! Support this local business with great service and food!

Not only do you have a pretty stellar restaurant here (though not a fast one) with some very excellent shawarma, which not only satiated my fix but was one of the better versions I've had of this, but there is a very cool grocery store to wander through while you wait. If you're like me and love trying new stuff, this is a gold mine and I had to intentionally limit myself, particularly on the sweets side, so I didn't wind up buying a small tonnage of the stuff. If I lived in the area, I'd probably be hitting up regularly for figs and dates or some of their desserts. As to the shawarma, it came with a couple different versions of hummus, one a very strong and coarser garlic-heavy version and the other a much smoother and enjoyable version, more like a tahini sauce that is a staple of any good shawarma plate. Pita bread was likewise excellent and the jasmine rice that came with it, of which there was much more beyond my ability to eat, was also excellent. If there is one minor complaint, it's that there are not pickles or olives or something along those lines included to kind of temper the meat/rice/hummus aspect of this, but this is not enough to deduct. Fantastic showing here.

Wanting a change from the Thai Places on Grand we came to The Loop for some Thai. I started off with a potent Thai Iced Tea. Still pretty good. As an appetizer we ordered the Chicken Satay. It looked fried and seemed dry. I reminded me of eating a fish stick. My salad came out right away. I ordered the Yum Beef Salad, number 11. The "salad" did not have any type of leafage. The beef was some sort of beef jerky that got soft from the juices of the salad. Loved the cucumbers, cilantro, tomato mixture with the lime juice. We also ordered the Tom Yum Noodle Soup. That was the best. Although our server didn't ask us how spicy we wanted it. I had to go to an empty table and grab the hot sauce since our table didn't have one. Once I added the hot sauce it was nice and spicy. The broth of the soup was delicious. Over all I would try this place again. I do have to add that our server did not check up on us once. Until next time.
Great grilled garlicky chicken, falafel, a veggie, rice, noodles or grain, some fruit... 10 bucks... No menu, no choices, different every day. Best lunch in center city!

Okay. if you are looking for noodle soups, THIS is where you should go :) Following dissappointments in my search to quench my noodle fever, I stumbled into Bamboo with a friend, hoping for the best. It probably also helped that it's BYOB, so I already was fully loaded with a bottle of wine in hand when I walked in the door. (P.S. dont be scared that from the outside it looks more like a cig outlet than a restaurant.) Both my friend and I ordered the crab vermicelli with the spicy chicken broth and shared a side of summer rolls. That, with the white wine and fabulous girl talk, was the perfect combo. The spicy broths have a zing, but wont leave you tasteless. Also, they bring out a quartet of sauces for you to sprinkle into your soup for flavor. I loved all sauces--they made everything so interesting. I will say that I stayed away from the spiciest of the four, but if you like the spice you'll have to let me know if it was good. To accompany your soup, they bring out a plate of greens, lime, and jalepenos, which I think is brilliant. The other places I've been just dumped them all into the soups, but since you can add them at your own pace here, the herbs and sprouts are never wilted :) When we went it was pretty dead... More people should visit this place A) because it's worth it B) so that when my friends and I tell salacious stories, they won't echo into the cavernous void of an empty restaurant (sorry to our server!! ;) ) CONCLUSION: sluuuuurrrrp! :D Quality: Best so far in the West Chester area for noodle soups! Price: A soup dinner plus a split order of summer rolls came to $15 per person. A little more than chipotle, but less than your standard eating out fare in WC.

Price is great. I had the beef pho and my boyfriend had the bah mi. We both agreed that the pho was better. It's not the greatest pho but this place is so close to home and it can satisfy my craving in a pinch.

Incredibly friendly service and owners, homemade authentic food, and a warm interior make for an excellent experience! I love everything about this place! They also are very conscious of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free needs

The restaurant is very nice inside and the staff is friendly but I wasn't impressed with the food. My chicken, rice and peas, and plantains were dry and although my jerk chicken was spicy it wasn't flavorful. There were a few hits in my meal: the corn bread, callaloo, and the mango drinks were tasty but overall it a few side dishes aren't enough for me to frequent this restaurant.

I just drove from Philly on my way to New Jersey. I thought my family and I would stop in and grab a bite because this website posted open until 10:00 pm. That was wrong. The restaurant was closed. I saw a man opening the restaurant with a young woman with him. I started to question why he was not open, but did not feel it was worth my time. I should have stopped in Philly for a taste of Jamaica. Update your operating hours so you don't waste people time, gas and make a bad first impression.

Very good food, but pretty bad service. A young lady served us both times we came here and she's very unfriendly and not very helpful when it comes to explaining the menu. The menu is very confusing if you've never been to An Indian place before. However the food is very good! It's really spicy and they give you a ton of food.
Stopped here today for lunch. Hamburgers were definitely disappointing. Ordered mine medium and it arrived well done with no flavor at all. Would not return here for a meal.

They gave us an extra roll along with our Coconut soup (a.k.a. Tom Yum). The sweet and sour and curry dishes were awesome. Service was prompt and efficient. Decor is very good as well. The only odd thing we noticed was that it was very easy to hear people in the booths near us. Perhaps it was a side effect of very few people since we stopped in pretty late for a normal lunch time. If you haven't had much Thai, do yourself a favor and go to Jasmine Thai!

Came here for lunch and dinner. Excellent meals at both. At lunch I sat in the dining room, dinner was over in the bar....I actually preferred the bar area. Lunch was the pasta with clams, perfectly al dente and the clams weren't overly cooked. Dinner started with an excellent classic Negroni, then the monkfish with couscous, pickled fennel, Romesco sauce, and Castelvetrano olives. Perfectly seasoned all around, and the monkfish was seared on the outside and tender and juicy inside. My husband had the braised lamb shank which fell off the bone. We the blood orange and sage panna cotta for dessert, beautiful combination and texture, as well as the pistachio gelato, followed with a great Amaro digestivo. Service was polite and friendly.

For me, nothing exciting here. The guy that took our order was spaced out/ asleep at the wheel. When asked the difference in sizes between large and small he went ahead and rang in a large. Turns out we wanted a small. Food was just ok, it was edible. Seat on the bench was all ripped up, bathroom was dirty and the floor sticky.

THE FOOD IS AMAZING!!! Jeniece is a wonderful chef! Andre her her husband is a wonderful host and took care of us! His music playlist is awesome! Everything was so good. We started off with the wings - Delicious. My hubby had chicken curry. I ordered the special platter with chicken curry, Jamaican Jerk chicken, and Brown Stew. ORDER THE BROWN STEW!!! IT WAS EXCELLENT! I even ordered another Brown Stew to take home to my daughter. IT TASTED JUST LIKE GRANDMA'S STEW!!! My hubby & I had very happy stomachs!

Salsa is a great addition to nashville! It is a great place to go out to eat for dinner as a family or if you want to go as a group with friends or coworkers. I had the grouper sandwich when I went there and it was superb. I am a florida girl and I take my grouper sandwiches seriously and salsa delivered. There are so many things I want to try, I can't wait to go back!

The food was delicious. Good portions and very reasonable. A nice cocktail menu, too. We ordered four dishes and two appetizers for four people and had leftovers. I ordered extra empanadas to take home! Service was friendly. The only reason I am not giving 5 stars is they were out of a few items we wanted and it was only 730 on a Saturday night, that was a little disappointing. But overall it was a fun experience and we will go back.

New favorite place for a weeknight drink or 3. Knowldegable staff. If you get them talking about wine and its history/processes, they may even get you a glass to try for free :) Sit at the bar if you can - makes talking to the staff easier. Better for small groups. Perfect for a date.
went there for dinner w/ my girlfriend Saturday night. I wish they weren't out of spring rolls, but the egg rolls were a good substitute. good Chang beer. nice dinner
Good gyro, sarcastic service (unless it's the daughter). Ignore the uncle. Chalk it up to the clientele.. No bathroom, open til' 3am. Bread is better than the meat.
Best Thai in the area. No delivery. But just started "Uber eats" green curry, drunken noodles, amazing taste, potions. I've only done take out but looks nice to sit. Highly recommended!

The food, the service, and the ambiance were all excellent. (assuming you like a modern street ambiance) Big portions, great flavor, quick service and very friendly staff. You better make a reservation, because it gets really busy. The decoration of the place is very interesting and the waitress told me that the owner made the ornaments that are on the walls himself! Pretty impressive and beautiful. We ordered the vegetable fried rice, the chicken noodles, and two salads. The duck salad with wine dressing was absolutely delicious. The only problem was that the duck had a lot of fat. But other than that, the dinner was perfect! We loved the coconut drink. Fresh coconut water from the real coconut. It was the sweetest one we have ever tried!
The food is delicious! I got the garlic naan and paneer masala... Such a comforting dish. I'm craving it now!
Will only sell you bottled water with your food and cocktails. Poor business practice. The only reason anyone goes there is location.

Really good food. Our table had the Shanghai noodles, Singapore noodles and chicken curry soup. We all loved each dish. Pleasant service. Our food arrived in good time. The prices are good - for a large portion.

I'm a big fan of Sam's. It's a great place to watch the sunset for everyone, and it's also nice for people like me who don't have much experience around oceans. Great atmosphere to just relax with friends and have a nice meal. I'm had quite a bit of their menu. The only thing that fell flat for me was the chicken and waffles. They need to leave that to Roscoe's and stick with the other things they do so well. I can't recommend anything in particular because most everything is of such high quality. I plan on returning to Sam's whenever I find myself in Tampa area.

Amazing, amazing, amazing! Had deluxe gyro and words can't describe. I think it was the seasoning of the meat and the feta. Hummus was also delicious as was the olive salad. Will be back here as soon as I can.

I am on business travel, so just trying to find restaurant close by. 8 mins from Courtyard Marriot, maybe less. I got Deccan special briyanni, hot. It was really good I like it. It has chunk chicken meat, boiled egg, briyanni, served with 2 different kind of curries on the side. I close it with dirty mango coctail. It took a while to prepare the food, but it is worth it

Delicious! I loved my pananag curry, so sweet and fruity. Also the presentation is awesome, i love their plates and serving dishes. The pad seew was also really good as well as the oriental salmon. Portions are nice and filling but not too huge which is great. This place filed up fast so make reservations if you're coming for a later dinner! Plus I loved the chocolate mints at the end!
What a wonderful surprise. The staff was incredibly helpful with outstanding suggestions. The food is freshly made and delicious! We hope to become regulars at this delightful restaurant.

Long overdue review. I fly into Indy for work and get take out a lot. I have eaten at Haveli or gotten take out here at least 15 times. The food is always great and I have never had a problem with delays or order mix ups. I frequently order through Yelp's Eat24 app. Haveli handles orders that come through this app very well. The lamb tikka masala, vegetable samosas and lamb korma are among my favorites.

Enjoyed my lunch! While I tend to fumble with chopsticks, I managed to make a huge dent in my chicken vermicelli! The chicken was seasoned perfectly, and I'll definitely get this dish again. I did notice most of the other diners eating Pho (soup). I skipped it due to the summer temps, but, now know it is a must at Pho Cam Ly. I will get this next time. We also had the fried pork egg rolls which I was mildly disappointed in (odd flavor), but, the beef spring roll I had a bite of (with peanut sauce) was very good. Clean establishment, friendly staff and great prices make Pho Cam Ly a very smart choice for lunch!

Tonight a Monday night, I placed an order at 7:02 P.M. It is now 8:30 P.M. and still no food has been delivered. I've called an all they can say is the food out..I just hope it tasted good and it's hot. To be continued....

Walking in I was already skeptical. It was HOT and seemed kind of dingy in a not so charming way. I went to wash my hands and their bathroom was more reminiscent of a gas station than a restaurant. We were told we could sit anywhere so we did. Service and waters came quickly. The server was friendly and she kept our waters filled. Her menu knowledge was a little scant which is forgivable in a place like this. However, when asked a specific question about the menu and you don't know the answer you should go find out not just say it could be this or that. That being said I really did like our server and the family that owns the place is friendly and seems to care about what is going on in their restaurant. I did want to like it more but I just didn't. We all ordered the vegetarian summer rolls @ $3.95 - Fresh spring rolls filled with noodles, bean sprouts, carrots, romaine lettuce, and cilantro. served with sweet & sour sauce and peanut sauce. They were ok but didn't blow my mind. However they were the hi light of my meal. I ordered the Vegetarian Gang Dang at heat level hot @ $8.95 - Tofu with carrots, sweet peas, bamboo slices, bell peppers, green beans, and sweet basil, cooked in red curry paste and coconut milk. served with steamed rice. I was underwhelmed to say the least. The veggie that appeared the most in my dish was bamboo shoots and the rest, other than the peppers, the rest of the veggies had the texture of pre frozen vegetables. My rice was mushy and flavorless. The heat level might as well have been zero and the flavor lacked the beautiful brightness and aromatic quality that I love with most Thai food. My dining partners ordered: Vegetarian Pad Thai @ $8.95 - Thai stir fried rice noodles with tofu, bean sprouts, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, baby corn, green onions, roasted peanuts and egg. Sen-lek Hang with tofu @ $8.95 - Rice noodles with bean sprouts, and topped with crispy wontons, green onions and cilantro (with/without crushed roasted peanuts). They both reported their dinners as good and tasty. The prices were very reasonable but I am definitely willing to pay more for quality. I won't be running back here. However, I wouldn't avoid it if my friends wanted to come back.

Hands down, one of my favorite places to eat in West Philly, and beyond. I've lived in the neighborhood for almost five years, and have been here several times. The service: Very friendly, thorough, and fast. The prices: Reasonable, though it has increased a little over the years. They also offer a lunch special - which includes an appetizer (love the fresh spring rolls), soup (LOVE the coconut soup), and entree (I frequent the curries with vegetables or shrimp) for a set price (comparable to the cost of just an entree at dinner) depending on your choice protein (tofu, chicken, shrimp, duck, and more). Other things to keep in mind: BYOB, cash only, they close between 3-5pm, and very allergy-friendly. Gluten-free folks, you will have many options and the servers know what's up. Great dishes: Yum Salad (a little spicy), Penang Curry (nice and peanut-y), Sweet Basil or Ginger Sauce entrees (really fresh flavors). Also, of note, they serve the most delicious coconut ice cream in a coconut shell. with strawberries.

I visited again recently. I couldn't be more happy. I ordered some dish with a kebab and shawarma. I think that's how you spell it; I just adored how the waiter said it. "Shawarma." Anyway, I fell more in love with Ishtar because the waiter came back out with lentil soup. I have never had such good soup on a miserably warm day. It has this spice in it and I don't know what it is, but it just gives it this very distinct taste. I would say that the food here is better than the competitor up the street. The restaurant is a nice and quiet environment that you can have a nice conversation in. You can also purchase some baklava for desert.
Amazing. Had the butter chicken; spicy of course. I enjoyed the service an the quality if food. I would highly recommend if you are in the area to stop by.

Yummy food, quick service, clean environment. Super classy! Love this place. The staff is super friendly and the soups amazing. Really good if you want something filling but not too filling. Overall nice place thats quiet and peaceful

Ekta is fantastic. They do everything right. The vegetarian dishes are fresh and flavorful, especially the cashew dish with their homemade cheese. The naan is wonderful, chewy, and comes in many varieties. The rice pudding is delicious, too. Yum! One of the best places to eat in Bryn Mawr. Very sad that the buffet is gone, though :( Bring it back, please!!
We love it here. Green curry is my favorite, and they gave great boba teas. Everyone is always so friendly too!

In what seems to be a theme in this area, Blue Plate the building is a bit beat up. It's old wood, covered in worn carpet, dings and scratches, etc. Maybe I'm spoiled from my highfalutin', trendy, Old City life, but this country mouse charm stuff does nothing for me. The good news is the food doesn't seem to have suffered. I've only been here twice (so far) but both times I was happy with my meal. (First time turkey club, second time chicken cheese steak, both served with fries and a pickle.) The portions are great, (even though the drinks are served in like baby sized shot glasses, causing multiple refills), and the people seem really nice. Blue Plate also ups the ante with their catering menu, which has a lot of swanky options and custom sandwiches, like the Turkey Waldorf and like a goat cheese and fig pizza. Basically, they have more than just "diner food." Bonus points; you get 10% off with a Yelp check in!
My favorite pho place in town. Consistently excellent food. It's one guy running the whole show, so give him a break if it takes him a little longer. He's sweet.
Very good Rangoon. Exceptional waiter. Many choices to select from. Highly recommended!

I just wasn't impressed. When this place caught my eye, I couldn't wait to try the food. I love Indian, and had tried several of the local Indian spots in the area. I was really hoping to add this to my list of favorites, but after trying here, I think I'll stick to what I know. I came in not long before closing (maybe why I got *meh* food) but was assured it wasn't too late for carryout, and also there was a table of 3 finishing up. The man behind the counter was very friendly and attentive and more than happy to explain the menu. After he finished with the table, he took my order to go. I ordered the chicken biryani and the veggie samosa, to-go. When it came time to pay, the man (owner?) strongly encouraged I pay with cash, even though they had a credit card machine. Hmm. Anyhow, I paid with my card and was given a paper menu with my food. I got home less than 10 minutes later, and was underwhelmed by my order. The chicken biryani was not what I expected. The rice tasted like Minute rice and was an even brown all the way through, not like the white-and-orange basmati servings I'd had elsewhere. Plus, it seemed to have been simmered in a broth or some kind of spicy, overly salted sauce. The chicken carried the same flavor, which made the dish seem bland. The samosas were soggy and cold. I may or may not try this place again.

Zen Yai is my favorite thai restaurant in Santa Barbara. As some others have pointed out, there are only a few other thai places here, so claiming it's the best might not be saying much. Though Santa Barbara has great restaurants in general, this isn't LA or San Francisco and so I don't know why people expect SB to be on the same level as those metropolises. Anyhow. Call ahead to make reservations and also to make sure they're open, as I've gone by a few times and found them closed (usually on weekend afternoons). The som tum (papaya salad) is always great, I love that dressing! Soups are yummy, curries are solid, desserts are a treat. If you love thai food, go check it out!

I've been working in the Town Center for a year and a half. I remember eating at Zoe's for my first lunch break ever working in the center. I instantly fell in love. That was then and things have definitely changed. The food use to be amazing I've sent a lot of people, my customers, my family here to eat while they visit the center. But now the service is horrible. I've called in orders 4 different times just to pick up the wrong order. My receipt will say exactly what I called in and my order will be completely wrong. So disappointing because I truly loved this place but now I refuse to go back and spend any more money here. I don't know if it's training or the new staff just don't care but it's a huge NEGATIVE CHANGE. Looks like I have to find a new lunch place in the center. It's sad.

My homegrl got fried rice, and to her eye rolling, I just went for much-ballyhooed pad thai--I eat plenty of Thai food in quality, quantity, and diversity, I just had a craving for it, k? Anywayz, both were bland and disappointing, and cost twice what they should have. They get one point for decor, which is nice enough, but it was a real bummer to be out nearly $20 for pad thai, tip, and a glass of water when so thoroughly mediocre. As with pizza and Mexican in this town, you're probably better off making your own.
The chicken tikka masala is amazing here. Beware though, if you say spicy... It's going to make you sweat. The takeout service is great at lunch time, and the portions could be shared.

I have two pieces of advice when it comes to the Jamaican Jerk Hut: 1. Do not come with people who are starving and grumpy. They will become a huge annoyance to you and everyone else in your party if you come here. The thing about JJH is that the service is slooowww. It's no secret. You will be here for a very, very long time. You will feel ignored. You will be on the verge of tears by the time you order. Bring a snack. Or eat before you come and then by the time your food has actually arrived you won't be tearing out your hair in hunger and confusion. Trust me, I've been there. 2. Expect to spend a lot more money than you think. When I first walked by this place I thought it would be a great spot to host the birthday dinner of one of my friends. We could sit outside, listen to free live music and eat some good, cheap Jamaican food. The only true thing about that previous statement was the eating al fresco. Because there was music we had to pay an entertainment fee even though the band played for a very small portion of the time we were there (which was a pretty long time). There's also a corkage fee if you bring your own alcohol. Uhh...what? And the food...it ain't cheap. It was good though. I got the classic chicken curry and it was seriously phenomenal. And there was some spicy salad my friend ordered and that was bangin, too. I wish I had known these things before I went, I would have enjoyed my time there soo much more. I'll probably go again but I definitely will eat something beforehand.

My fiance and I went to dinner there last night and were really excited to try a new Thai place close to home for his Birthday. When we arrived there were about 8 people in the whole restaurant and 1 server. We just assumed they served alcohol and went to order a birthday drink not knowing that they had recently lost their liquor/beer/wine license. So....needless to say that was a bit of a bummer but not a total deal breaker. We ordered the Lemongrass soup which was really good and the crab rangoon which was really just cream cheese and no crab. My fiance ordered the pad thai HOT which was subpar and not what I think of HOT being...it was missing something (cilantro?). I don't know but it was just not the best I've had. I ordered the beef and broccoli and the beef was so chewy I could barely eat it. The sauce and veggies were good. Not a great experience, likely won't go back anytime soon :-/ Also way overpriced.

One of my favorite places in South Tampa! Always fresh, hot, seasoned well and with a smile :) Yes it's a food truck with some picnic tables but it's the best 'fast food' you'll have on Dale Mabry. Parking can be tight but it moves quick so it's 5 stars for this Tampa gem!
The kabab is more than perfect, real iraqi kabab. Very lovely stuff . I love the chicken also. Big size portion, And very affordable prices.
By far my favorite Thai restaurant in Santa Barbara. I could live off the coconut shrimp soup.

If you have had good pho and summer rolls before don't come here. I was so disappointed in both. I honestly had such high hopes because other people gave it good reviews but clearly they don't know what good pho is. Also I came because they had boba tea but even that was bad and flavorless.

I really want to like this place more as its the only gyro/Mediterranean place around - outside of the great vegetarian falafel place in newtown. So when I want a Gyro this is the place that has it anywhere close to Newtown. There is absolutely nothing bad about any of their food - but it is nothing special. Last time I had a gyro they microwaved it from a frozen state I think. Still was Ok and they have a decent pita and vegs with it. But its nothing different then you might get at a pizza joint in NJ that also has gyros. Same with the falafel and some of the other sandwiches I've had. They are really friendly, prices are good, and all in all the food is "fine". However I can't give it more stars given its just ok...

I had to stop and review this spot! The individuals who serve us at this place are very kind, and their food is always amazing! Most recently, I had the jerk chicken, dark, with rice and peas. Portions are nice, and it was Sooooo Bomb! I don't live in Indy anymore, and I make it a point to eat here when I visit. 55555 stars!!!!!
The line is long at Noon but it is worth the wait! Everything is fresh and made to order. The cookies were not available but if you check in they give you one for free. Good food.

How have I been around the corner from this spot for so long without stopping in? Inconvenient parking. That's how. And the only reason I made it in this time was a fortuitous spot near the corner. If I walked this neighborhood more often I'd be a regular, no doubt about it. This is a regular lil corner store spot... Cold drinks and wine and chips. And a deli counter in the back. The store was empty when I arrived, which made me nervous about my dinner choice, but soon after I ordered others came in and did the same. Felt much better. I wasn't alone. I had the pho ga, and it's prettttttttttyyyyyyyy good. A little heavy on the onion, but the broth is somehow both light and satisfying. Chicken is well seasoned. Service is quick. Maybe 10 minutes from order to exit. I am pleased. And eating pho.

This is my favorite place for Thai, hands down. I think it was the first Thai restaurant and I think the best. The place has real character and the staff is fun and know ther regulars and that makes a real difference. I've tried a lot of things here and never had a bad dish. Pad Thai, Soy Sauce Noodles, Lad Nah, Fresh Sprng Rolls, Mee Krob, Tom Yum Koong, Spicy Noodles, Noodle Soup w/Beef & meatballs - it's all good. I've never eaten off the buffet on the 'other' side of the wall though at lunch I see plenty of people that do. The biggest draw back to this place is the parking - it's tight to say the least. But this old hole in the wall is the best and most fun.

This was my first visit to any P.F. Chang's and I really don't understand the hype. There was a wait so I was expecting some good eats, but I was not impressed by any means. The fried calamari was average. The mongolian beef was comparable to any americanized chinese takeout place. The sweet and sour chicken was neither sweet nor sour. Service wasn't great. At least they give you fortune cookies at the end... I heart fortune cookies.

India Palace is my favorite Indian food of all time. Their paneer masala is some of the best I've ever had. The nav ratan shashi korma is also quite tasty! Also, don't miss a perfect vegetable pakora with delightfully spicy onion chutney. They have a really great lunch buffet with several good vegetarian choices. This is a great place to come and try Indian food for the first time. During Dinner hours, there's a small basket of papadam on the table to start things off. These are always perfectly cooked without being greasy. Dinner is nice with very generous portions. We usually get one entree per person, and have lunch the next day as well.

Yum! Everything that I have tried here is so good. I always get a taro boba tea..I really need to try some other flavors..but it's really good! The boba is soft and chewy and the taro is blended just right. Papaya salad and sticky rice, quail, chicken wings- two thumbs up! Pad Thai is kinda too sweet, not how I like it. Their banh mi are good too. I like the Brian's special and the pork roll/pate sandwiches. Interior is clean and nicely decorated. There are a couple of tables if you want to sit outside. The staff are normally very friendly and helpful. Service can be a bit slow when they are busy, but worth the wait. I love Seasons Cafe!

We have a steady stream of food trucks at work and my lunch crew decided to try the Gyro truck. I've been to a handful of other Greek restaurants in town so I was skeptical that the price/quantity would measure up to the others. Boy was I wrong. The gyro is packed, and their tzakiki sauce is tops. Plenty of meat, plenty of "fixins"; this thing was amazing. (Which was probably why the line was so freakin' long) They don't seem to have a regular day so I'll just keep my eyes open because I'll definitely be eating here again.

I went to this extremely crowded place on a Wednesday night and still had to wait 30 mins for a table. I will just summarize now unless you want the gory details below. My expectations were high and the food was bad. I have heard good things about PF Changes, great things in fact about the food and the quality etc. I went in and was just disappointed after every moment i was there. I had requested a booth to sit in for me and my wife. We get there, and after our beeper beeps we are seated in....a small table against the wall...i inquired about where my booth was they said that none are available and it'd be another 20 min wait. (sign of things to come?) So we sit down and our waiter asks us for our drink order, we order and brings over a thing of sauces but doesn't say what they are or why they are there.... We order egg rolls, dumplings, a Changs spicy chicken and double pan fried noodles. The dumplings were good, but the presentation was key, the dumplings were 4 to an order for 5 bux....high in my opinion. Egg rolls were two per order and were bland and very mediocre and again for 5 bucks....kinda steep. We finally inquire about the sauce after our apps and the waiter was like OMG totally forgot about that! And mixed stuff...i wasn't impressed and basically ignored the stuff there. Entrees. I was expecting great things but again was highly disappointed. The chicken tasted like McDonald's chicken nuggets with some duck sauce and some hot pepper mixed in. This is their "addicting" dish? It sucked! The pan fried noodles were good, i enjoyed them but they were odd. To summarize, this place was OK, but not worth the price nor the wait. I kept saying the entire meal I'd rather have gone to yangmings in bryn mawr or San Kee in wynwood which is never a good sign when i go into a place with high expectations. I know that alot of people are giving this good reviews but i just can't as it wasn't good. A very disappointing experience.

Combination Banh Mi was delicious! Loved the heat from the jalapeños and the combination of meats and pâté were scrumptious. Of course it's not a decent banh mi without good bread with a nice crunch and this one delivered with a very fresh roll.

This tiny spot is hidden in the same building with Delicia, but it has an approachable, affordable street food focus. We tried and shared several items from the menu -- including the guacamole, the chilaquiles (with egg! and chicken), and several tacos. I appreciate that the server was nice enough to warn us from overordering. We each had a cocktail and the prices were extremely fair ($7-$9). I feel good about coming here any day, wearing even a ratty T shirt. Delicia, we'll save for date night. Parking can be tricky, but there is a lot around the back of the building!

BIGGEST MISTAKE! Prior to eating here, I made an attempt to research the raving reviews regarding this restaurant. I happened to be in the area one day and decided to stop in an grab takeout. Long story short, afterwards, I ended up sick for almost 3 days. I hardly ever become sick after eating out and boy did this place throw me for a loop. I later asked around about this place and 2 out of maybe 10 people revealed they had friends who were sick after eating here. Wish I would've known prior to trying it out. Overall the restaurant appears clean and staff was extremely pleasant, but after three days of nausea and diarrhea I could never recommend this place to anyone.

The restaurant itself is very good. I really like the variety of north and south Indian dishes on the menu as well as the indochinese selection. Food is well spiced and authentic in taste. A good selection of Indian snacks such as Bhel puri, papdi chaat, and pani puri which is a big plus. I do, however, have some reservations with this restaurant. First, on numerous occasions here, I have noticed service is slow and not all that accommodating. The wait staff always seems a little bit, how should I say this..grumpy? Secondly, the food on the buffet is very good, but that is only while busy. If one goes to this buffet in non peak hours, the food is not ever recycled and could be somewhat of a health hazard and gamble to consume. The buffet, tho one of my favorites when there is a good crowd present, can really swing the other way on the pendulum when slow. Lastly, the chicken is not the greatest quality in some of the dishes. The tikka masala, the chicken is fine (as it is marinated white meat). But in other dishes, such as vindaloo, the chicken is much more fatty and rubbery in texture, and mixed between white and dark meat which leads me to avoid chicken curries here for the most part. Veg dishes and lamb dishes here are heads and tails better. So in summary, go to this joint if you are craving Indian street snacks, indochinese, or vegetarian/lamb curries. Be ready for subpar, not so welcoming service, and sort of a dingy environment.

Had the Panang. Was empty when we got there at 7:30 on a Sat night. Was honestly pretty bad but we are from Seattle where great Thai food is the norm. Didn't ask how spicy to make it. Sauce thin and one-dimensional. Peas may have been canned. Server was friendly. I wish them the best but the panang was not good on this night. The music stopped and we spent most of the meal in silence which was also pretty bizarre.

SAVE YOUR MONEY!!! Okay, I saw a sign that says it is under new management so that may be the problem. Fresh rolls were good! So, I loved the dipping sauce and I asked for the ingredients. They would not tell me. I'm not sure if that is even legal!!!??? IT WAS A DIPPING SAUCE! WOW!! Top secret I guess! Okay fine. But their pad thai is AWFUL! Unless you are a very, very fat person who likes a pound of sugar at a meal! They have no clue how to make pad thai sauce. I would say they are using a ratio of tamarind : fish sauce: sugar of 1:1:6. It should be about equal. Could not taste tamarind or fish sauce JUST SUGAR. The noodles were coated in a syrup. Gross!! We ate about 1/5 and asked for to go boxes. We would have left it but after spending the money we figured we would pick at it over a couple of days and treat it like candy. One of the worst I have ever had, and I have eaten in at least 200 thai places from the Keys to Alaska, and I make my own all of the time. Pass on this one!!!! And how rude to keep the ingredients of a dipping sauce!!

Fish burrito= amazing and filling. Huge crispy pieces of fish, some lettuce, tomato, avocado and spicy mayo, all for $6? Such a great deal. The avocado did get a bit lost in the rest of the ingredients though but I can forgive that. Chicken satay tacos (3 for $8) were also good with an interesting fusion of flavors- sweet&savory. Thai iced tea ($2) was a tad too sweet but overall, tasty food at a good price!
Nice little spot, although it's in an unassuming strip mall behind Psghettis! I had the Deluxe Gyro and it was delicious! Very generous portions and fast friendly service.

Disclaimer: I got their Autumn Salad with Fried Chicken to-go. Disclaimer Part 2: It was delicious. The salad was a great mix of quinoa, sweet potatoes, and leafy greens, and was topped with a healthy dose of fried chicken. I was a little hesitant about my choice initially, but I loved it. It was filling, lasting me two whole meals, and made me feel like I didn't completely wreck my new years diet.
The Cuban sandwich was great as well as the empanada picadillo and the relleno de papa. Will definitely be back for lunch.

It took 50 MINUTES to get my to-go order which was only two items!! And I was watching them in the kitchen & the waitstaff was touching the food with their bare hands. Never once did I see them wash their hands. Some waitstaff were back there eating. Horrible experience, won't be coming back.
Good food and amazing ambiance. Servers could be more polite. But overall a good place to chill out.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in St. Louis! Hands down. There's nothing here that I dislike. I recently tried the Tom- Yum Ramen, it so flavorful and smooth. It does have a spicy kick to it so if you can't handle spicy this isn't the ramen for you. Eve was my waitress and she was so sweet and amazing. She's only been in the U.S. for a month so her English isn't perfect but she communicates very well. I'll definitely be asking for her next time I go.

You know, it's really too bad that I have to give the Hookah House a three-start review. The place is beautiful, and I've often said that it seems like a place that James Bond would have visited. If Bond were to have visited the Hookah House, he'd have enjoyed a seat in one of the establishment's dark corners--quietly discussing espionage while sipping Turkish tea and enjoying water-cooled hookah smoke. He'd also enjoy the excellent Middle-Eastern fare, although I'm sure that in his travels (even in the Indianapolis area), he'd had better. However, James Bond is a character of fiction. I'm a real customer, and I have to admit that I was a mite dissatisfied with many aspects of the Hookah House. My biggest complaints are with the staff. During my last visit, I had a wonderful server. She was quick with our orders, was friendly, and if it wasn't for her, I would have left. On my first trip to the Hookah House, a friend of mine, not used to high levels of nicotine, vomited on the floor. Of course, no one was happy about this. To make matters worse, a young man, who I later learned was the owner's son, began screaming, "FML! FML!!" (although he didn't speak in abbreviations). He then told us that we would have to pay for his cushions to be laundered in the event that they were soiled (which they were not). Come on, man. You sell a stimulant drug (nicotine)--accidents are bound to happen. On my second trip to the Hookah House, the establishment's owner would just not leave us alone. When we asked for a few moments to look over the menu, he huffed away. When we finally ordered, he did not seem to like our selections. For the next 30 minutes, he swore that he was eavesdropping on our conversation. Was it espionage? I couldn't tell. He also did not mention that he charged us for refills on our Diet Coke. I believe that I spent $16 just on diet soda (out of a fountain). Ripoff. Get your act together, Hookah House.

Looks like nothing on the outside, but really nice on the inside and the food is terrific. I like that they aren't shy about making the curry spicy -- highly recommend Panang Curry or drunken noodles -- appetizers all very tasty too!

Ordered the Orange Chicken and Singapore noodles to takeout on a weekend night, the chicken was an undifferentiated slop of fried batter crumbs and tiny shredded fragments of chicken and the sauce was super sweet. The noodles looked like half of them had dried out a little bit.

I hate giving negative comments. Wish the pho was as good as the service. The pho is very bland it's like eating pho noodles and plain water. It lacked flavor from the broth. I would highly recommend eating pho somewhere else. Sorry I'm just being honest.

Eggroll Queen is already a family Favorite. We can each get something different...buffalo chicken, cheesesteak, mac and cheese and bbq pork are a few of our favorites and there are more to try. The Eggrolls are delicious and the owner and her staff are so nice. We always call ahead and it works out great for a quick dinner.

This place is amazing! My friends and I bought 5 different bahn mis so we could try them all out. The Lemongrass Tofu bahn mi is my favorite: crusty bread, warm fried tofu with a spicy sauce, and of course plenty of cilantro, shredded carrots and cucumber. They have a bunch of pastries too: egg custard tarts, meat pies, and this crazy sweet cake and onion roll. The lady that works there is very kind and will educate you on what everything is. Also it is very affordable. Not all of the prices are listed but the bahn mis are like $3.50.

always get the same thing-- im a creature of habit if you ever look at my other reviews, tandoori chicken chicken vindaloo (comes with perfectly cooked basmati rice !! its so good) vegetable samosa ( so good, although i should probably stay away from anything fried) mango lassi-- yogurt drink with fresh mango and a tad of sugar so good!! og and the garlic naan is awesome they deliver.. sort of expensiveee? sort of,.but for 2, its around 50

Good Food. Great Service. Friendly Faces. I've been a repeat customer for over a year now and can confirm that each order is made fresh and consistently tastes good. The staff are extremely friendly and are always so appreciative of the repeat business. This is a best-in-class restaurant and gets my highest rating.

Best Thai food I've ever had the food is so fresh and delicious and omg the presentation of the food is out of this world it's not only presented to you in the most beautiful way it is pretty and good where some miss the mark but you will not be disappointed

We drove an hour. We went inside to ask if there are any ramp since we had a wheelchair with us. She said we are booked instead of helping or providing assistances. I would of understood if the restaurant was full. It was empty. She didn't even bother to help or say it nicely. I've never been so disrespected. I'm disgusted.

So glad I got to try their food during the Baltimore dollar stroll! I got their tofu summer roll and the nam salad - both were really yummy! The only thing was I got the salad thinking I needed to get my daily need of veggies, but the summer roll ended up being more veggie heavy..the salad was still good! Just lots of fried things so it didn't feel as healthy as expected

The Panang salmon was phenomenal. The flavor was absolutely perfect! The papaya salad was, for the first time with such a salad, something of which I could enjoy the complexities of the flavoring without setting my mouth ablaze in mild discomfort. Not that I mind such things: it was just nice to feel balanced with the spice, the fresh lime juice, the peanuts, the tomatoes, etc. The hot tea was a perfect compliment for a chilly night. And I met my soulmate* at the next table over. Didn't even order him: he just appeared! Appropriately random for February 29th. I went to SB from LA on a whim: my friend was doing a beer promotion at a couple bars, and had a free hotel room for the night. She invited me along, and I figured "what the hell." Little did I know (that one's for you, Stranger Than Fiction fans!), I would end up being the one to find a hot guy to make out with, which is what she had wanted to do. I figured I'd just kinda enjoy some alone time and just relax. I must admit I enjoyed my non-alone time, and though I felt a little guilty, hey, it's not like I was looking: it just happened. She was very gracious about it, though. :} So I'd spotted the other Thai place down the street when we first got to town, and that's where we headed after parking. Even though I was looking, we blew by it. But hey there was another one, so OK. They had no tables for me (she was getting hers to go) so I just hung out till she got her order, and planned to proceed to the other place. Well, I'm glad I didn't have to leave: a table opened up. I was very happy with my meal, and was given a happy excuse to exchange looks, comments, and smiles with a lovely gentleman when I had trouble getting the attention of the lady serving me (she was a good server, just a little hard of hearing) for a hot water refill. This gentleman happened to be dining alone also, at the table next to mine, facing me, wondering like I was, "What is this sexy person doing here alone?" He had been seated a good while after I had, so I was finished before he was, and offered him company. We ended up hitting it off. I mean, sparks flying everywhere, like damn I finally remember what this feeling is, and as much as I would have liked to feel it, and admittedly force it, for many years, it just happened right before my very eyes and heart. Bam! I don't know what Zen Yai puts in their food, but it tastes incredible, and seems to have some magical qualities as well! ~~~~~~ *UPDATE: definitely not my soulmate. But a fantastic story nonetheless, so I'll keep it up. Hope is good, right?

Omg, so good! My noodle chicken fish soup bowl was HUGE for $9 and the spring rolls were so fresh. I'm still eating soup left overs the next day! I told server I had to catch up with old friend that was arriving and she left us alone for very long time, and the exact second I was ready to pay and looked up she was ready to bring me check. PERFECT.

Mofongo was awesome. It was garlicky and very good. I felt like I was in Puerto Rico. The staff was friendly and helpful. Its a small place but they make you feel like you are family. Wife is Puerto Rican and she agrees La Casona is worth the trip. We visit as many PR restaurants while we travel and this was one of the best in Tampa.
Amazing assortment of food for lunch. Quante atmosphere and easy to locate. I will definitely come back here. Great place to have a lunch date, we had a Valentine's date today...

Dined in because the reviews were so positive. Was greeted by a young man who didn't really listen to what we said. Asked us questions over and over again about our order and drinks. Water and tea seem pretty standard. Then we were informed that they were out of gyro meat. Chicken was good. Overcharged on both meals and drinks, which was supposed to come with meal. Not sure why this place has so many great reviews. Must have caught them on a coast day. Wasn't an outrageous price, so give them a try. Maybe you'll have a better experience.

AMAZING. Not only is the food excellent but the service is too! I've ate from here plenty of times but never actually came to the truck myself (thanks for the deliveries mom) until today. We pulled up and one of the guys immediately recognized my mother and gave her a warm welcome. The guy taking the orders was very polite, funny (and handsome). Do I really have to explain how great the captn crunch tilapia is? Don't be scared to try it, it's sooooo good. I'll be back for the food, and possibly the guy taking orders lol
Love this place. Drunken noodles are fantastic. Curries are tasty too. One of the only places that if you tell them "make it REALLY spicy" they will actually do it.
Best Asian food in Hernando County. Dependable lunch and dinner spot for over a decade. Always leaves me full and happy.

Went for lunch and boy what a lunch. The service was outstanding. I ordered a gyro with a small Greek salad. The food was out quickly. The salad was crisp and cold and the server added the perfect amount of cracked pepper. As soon as the salad was finished whoosh away goes the plate a new drink hit the table next to me before I was 1/2 finished. Away the server goes and bam here comes the gyro. It was warm and full of delicious beef and lamb slices and a huge amount of sour cream uh err tzatziki I was just teasing about the sour cream..... It was delicious. I was a clean plater. Have you ever been sad when you have finished your meal and wish it would have lasted longer? This was my meal today. pk

A long time favorite of mine I have been going there for years and years now and never a bad experience yet. They have simply prepared great Greek fish and seafood. If you can brave the noise from the other customers and the open kitchen you will enjoy a great meal. I love the fried Calamari - the best I've had ever. Grilled octopus is very good also. Blue fish Greek style is nice and very moist, I always try to go for the specials which are fresh and tasty - when the flounder is on the menu get it - same for the soft shell crabs and any kind of grilled whole fish. I like the smaller dishes too - the peas are very refreshing, the humus and baba are great - I usually ask them to make a dish of half and half. If you have room at the end of the meal - try the rice pudding. It's a fairly small place - there are no reservations. There is often a wait - but you can go across the street and have a drink after you put your name on the list and they will call you. I try to get there towards the end of the evening - it gets more quiet and there is less of a wait.

I think the place is pretty good. I got the lamb gyro sandwich, and it came in a fresh pita pocket that was puffy and lightly toasted. The lamb strips was plentiful and juicy, while there was an abundance of lettuce, tomatoes and cucumbers. They added a good amount of sauce, enough that it definitely added a good flavor to the ingredients, but not too much that it was drowning the gyro. The sandwiches are pretty affordable for the quality they provide, around $6, but I do wish they were bigger. The plates are up at around $10, but they look well presented. Everything is made pretty quickly. If I find myself in the area again and need a quick lunch, I would consider returning.

This is a real, real good restaurant! My husband and I had the feast for two. The lentil soup with little crunchy bits of cilantro had real, savory taste. The nan bread was soft and yummy. The rice had tiny slivers of orange peel and cardomon in it. The red lamb curry had a real depth of flavor. The orange chicken and vegetable curry was well seasoned, the vegetables cooked just right. We had a beverage called masala chai. It could have used a little more chai as it was just a little weak, but the spices in it were right on. We had a Tandoori platter with roasted, seasoned meats and vegetables. We also had a very nice rice desert. All of this only cost us $40.00! We left with three boxes of food to take home! The inside of the building was nice. It was hard to find. The wait staff were quick and clean in all that they did while looking great. I would eat here again and bring the rest of my family.

Good for vegans by design, don't miss this one. The lunch buffet is so indulgent that it will make you cry. It is magnificent. Baby angels riding unicorns give you your plates and it feels like you're full of rainbows inside. Okay, not really, but it is that good. Dinner is cheap, good, but not great.

Was a waste of time and money. They are one of the worst Jamaican food I ever had other than Jamaica Ds. I don't understand why they have awards for this place. Maybe they use to be good. I order oxtail, jerk shrimp,Mac and cheese, and jerk chicken. The oxtail were very hard and the flavor was bad it probably was old the sauce was not fresh and it was sleep up on the plate. The plantains was the worst I had in my entire life it was not sweet it was hard and over cooked like they didn't use a ripened plantain. The jerk chicken tasted old the jerk sauce was pure pepper. It's nothing wrong with spice but damn they over did it. The Mac and cheese was so so nasty. First of all it was like they used the cheap blue box of Mac and cheese and than it must have been old because the noodles were all broken up like it was giving trouble coming out the pot. I even saw the lady scraping up something when the curtain blocking the kitchen from the counter was drawn away for a brief moment. My daughter did not even want it after she had her first taste. I wish I didn't eat I already had a bad feeling about it when I saw it. The jerk shrimp was not jumbo as stated and it was just drowning in jerk sauce that was overly spicy and they were very small like they were over cooked or just very small shrimp on white bread. We needed a lot of water and overall I think we had left overs and or maybe they just had a bad cook. I will never return to this place.

This is the best new restaurant in town. Friendly, Courteous, Flavorful, Filling. Free Samples. Many choices, many flavors. I see every review talking about slow service, its not slow, its helpful. If the person in front of you is there for the first time and needs to sample all 16 things then so be it. If your in that big of a hurry White Castle is down the road. Everything I have had in my 6 visits had been a perfect eating temperature. They do check food temps often and have it under control. Are you going there to eat or nit pick a new place? When you complain water is too wet that's not a complaint that's just being stupid. Go there and talk with Sujata the owner and cook, everything is made FRESH all day long. And she is a delight to speak with.

Jasmine Rice is the 7th Thai BYOB restaurant I've been to in Philly. Jasmine Rice exceeded expectations; the service was friendly & well paced (on a Saturday night when the majority of the restaurant was full), and the food was tasty. I had the Beef Thani which was really flavorful (it had a TON of garlic, which I love, but a warning to those on a date night!). My friends are all vegetarians and got various noodle & veggie dishes- everyone cleared their plate and was really satisfied. I'm giving -1 star for the portion size/price ratio. When I get Thai I'm used to being able to take home half my dinner & still feel full, for the same price. However, Jasmine Rice puts out great tasting food and is so close to my house, it will probably become a new go-to place for me.
Most of the food I've had here is pretty good, sometimes dishes are a bit bland, but overall a pretty good vietnamese spot.

We are so grateful for the new great find we discovered in Boise! The food was fantastic and the two working the counter were so friendly!! We had the Kebab sandwich and the Felafal sandwich with a side of fries. They were seasoned beautifully and cooked to perfection. Hot, fresh sandwiches right off the grill! So tasty and what a GREAT price!!! We'll be back soon!

The food is good but far more bland than it should be, and the prices are higher than you'd expect. Don't waste your time eating in; takeout diners get FAR better and faster service than those who choose to dine on site and be ignored by the waitstaff. We waited almost two hours for our Jerk Chicken, and it was very clear that the kitchen was giving first priority to those waiting for takeout. We asked for more tortilla chips to tide us over, and were told we'd have to pay extra for them. Not worth the hassle, and we won't be back.

I've been to two Indian restaurants in town and this one I would not return to... nothing was horrible except the salty lassi which tasted like some sort rotten diary. The service was not special or nice in anyway - they forgot two things we ordered, then later remembered one of them. I think it was pretty timely though. The atmosphere - same. The plain na'an was good. - no complaints there. The tikka masala was the only dish I somewhat enjoyed. I didn't thoroughly enjoy it because I've had better. We did the 4 people meal option with meat to try several different things. This may be purely personal preference, but the lamb in this meal was pretty difficult to get through the taste. The yogurt chutney didn't have much taste, the green chile /mint chutney was nice! It had a southwestern twist to it. I got addicted to Indian food for their immense and different seasonings and tastes. I wasn't excited about that here. I went to New Delhi restaurant 3 times in one week after having it. I want that type of pleasure/excitement when I eat Indian.
Buen servicio, buen ambiente es como volver a sentirme en casa. Me encanto venir aquí y seguiré viniendo.

FINALLY! I have been wanting to go here for at least a year! My husband and I went one afternoon after church. This place is great! While the portions are small compared to Indian buffets (which is what we are use to), the food is delicious! The owner was our waiter and he was very friendly and enjoyed his job! We ordered the Chicken Curry and Palak Alu (spinach and potatoes). You can choose how spicy you want your dish, and it comes with rice. Add some Naan and you have a great meal! We will definitely try again, and the new location on Delmar!

We went to dine in on a Saturday and had a fantastic meal! Guru's had items I've never seen on an Indian menu before (like an appetizer dish with avocado which was great!) and everything was outstanding. Most notable was the exceptional service which I'm not used to at Indian restaurants. There must have been 5 staff members serving us and making sure everything was okay. So glad this place opened - will be back :)

Pleasantly surprised. Kim chi fried rice was really good and they make their Kim chi in-house. Service was not bad but lacked in knowledge of the menu and food genre overall, but food came out good and will go back.

I haven't had Indian in a while, so maybe I'm out of practice. But the hot -actually- made me sweat. The very nice mango lassi cooled me right down. The portions were plentiful and flavorful. We had, seemingly, a fleet of very attentive staff and were well looked after.

Just got home from a Sunday brunch and I am sad to say that we are very disappointed. We have been to the Blue Plate several times. We were seated in the basement (apparently new seating). It took 10 minutes for someone to come take our order and we then sat there for 40 minutes before our food came out. The server never once apologized for the delay and everyone around us who was seated after us, we served within 10 minutes of ordering. It will be a while before we return if at all.

This supposed to be hummus bow. But most of the time I only have falafel. And I notice most the time when Busy they don't give my hummus bowl proper. Ok quality, but I still go because it is close to my office . BusinessOwner pls change you hummus bowl picture with this because it not what we get.

I've been here a couple times, last time I brought my sales team to eat lunch here. Everyone liked it. It wasn't too busy and the food was pretty good according to everybody. My garlic shrimp actually was just okay, but everyone else (there were 8 of us) liked their food. Someone had the red curry duck and I tried it, it was delicious, I should've gotten that dish. The 2 times I've been here it seems I keep ordering the mediocre dishes while everyone else ordered the right ones. Ohh well, I wouldn't knock it, if you want decent authentic thai food. Eat in the restaurant part and order from the menu. I still prefer Thai Taste on Haywood, but this would be 2nd choice of the 2 for lunch near my office. The lady servers are very nice and accommodating.

WOW. I am in awe of Zeppoli right now. I honestly cannot say I have been more emotionally attached to any meal in a long long while. Is 6 stars possible? You know how some places do get that 5 star rating in your mind, but it's like a "you-barely-made-it-to-five-stars" kind of thing? Well from the moment I stepped into the door, I already KNEW it was going to be a 100% 5 star kind of evening. Everything they said, did, and served just blew me out of the water. It all began when I read Michelle C's review. She had me at Sicilian fisherman's stew, and tagliatelle al limone with prosciutto. I called the restaurant the same day and made a reservation for a few weeks later. They only have 12 tables and that was the earliest weekend they had available. I live roughly 45 mins away, and more with traffic. Since I'm pretty noob at navigating in NJ, I naturally got lost on the way to the restaurant, and was 20 mins late for my reservation. I wanted to call to warn them and apologize as I normally do when I am late, but did not have the number and the combination of being lost and not being able to call just made me feel annoyed at myself. By the time I got the restaurant, I was frazzled and also extremely pissed that the bottle of wine (this is a BYOB) I had gotten for the occasion was sitting on the kitchen table...at my house. The server was all smiles when I walked in, and the restaurant was already in full swing with almost every table full except one. Each table had a bottle of wine, which only made me sadder. When I profusely apologized to the waiter about not being prompt and then jokingly mentioned something about being the only one without wine in the whole place due to my idiot self, he just smiled and said, " Sounds like quite a mess coming here! I want you to relax while I get you some nice wine pairings for your meal from my private stash, and also please take your time and enjoy the meal, dont worry about rushing because you were late". It was as if an angel with a Golden Harp was playing music in my ears! I instantly relaxed and the wine parings were amazing! A white for the apps I got, and a light red for the main course. All on the house! I didn't know service existed like that anymore. That one comment and 2 glasses of wine earned them a big. fat. tip. which more than covered what 2 glasses of wine would even cost if it were on the menu. Money knows no bounds with kindness. On to the food. Amazing. I think you will drool when looking at the pictures. I would try to describe the things I ordered but I know I could not do it justice. Homemade pasta.
