Luxurious olive oil drizzled on our bread. Rosemary. Perfectly ripe and flavorful red tomatoes. Anchovies, Lemon! A tastful and rich balsamic. Tender chunks of fish, melts in your mouth lamb. Perfectly salted prosciutto. Tangy dried orange on creamy cannoli. Lightly whipped pineapple sorbet. Let's just say for me this meal was pure heaven sent. My bf and I both enjoyed all the things we ordered so so much. I would love to come back SOON!!!!!! Just know that this experience is so much more than just eating. It is the pure enjoyment of flavors, essence, company, homecooking, traditional Italian fare, and a wait staff that you'd like to take home with you...or party with. Absolutely Outstanding. Bravo, Zeppoli, Bravo! Mi Amour!

Came late for drinks and appetizers with a few friends. The wine list is excellent and the manager on duty was super-attentive and helped us order exactly what we would be happy with. The beer list is short and to-the-point--a few excellent choices in bottles and nothing else. The cocktails obviously had a lot of time and thought put into them, and were absolutely excellent. A note on decor: This place is absolutely beautiful. Hip, cool, clean. Incredibly well designed with a lot of ephemera and interesting furniture and accents. The chandelier up the stairs is seriously like the most beautiful thing I've seen in a restaurant.. It's a tight fit, though, so keep that in mind if you need a lot of space when you're out dining.

Excellent service and food. We had a 5pm reservation. Ashley explained the menu and specials clearly. All the wait staff were first rate. My wife got the rub, one friend ordered the salad with anchovies, the pasta with clams and the sausage. I ordered the green salad and the lemon pasta with prosciutto. My wife ordered a size grilled zucchini and I got her arugula which was perfect with the pasta. From the bread to the salad to the pasta to the entree, it was so delicious, fresh and flavorful! My only complaint was loud. Highly recommended!

We really enjoyed this place. The food is good, and the service is good. This review is for the restaurant that's located in Drexel Hill, at the Drexel Line Shopping center. The items we ordered were Chicken Madras, Chicken Tikka masala, Shrimp Karahi, Baigan Bhartha. Every single dish was delicious. We also ordered tandoori roti, which was very good, and we like the fact that they don't add butter on it until you ask (we eat ours without). At the end of the meal, we had a Groupon, which they graciously accepted and we left with a happy tummy and left overs for the next day. I would go back any time! Really like this place.

We came in a little late so I will give this place another try earlier in the day. We stopped by after getting takeout from india palace and hating the taste test we took; when we saw this place driving home I begged my boyfriend to stop and get something small after such a rough day (I had a rough day and knew when I got home to bland indian food that was supposed to be comforting, I would feel miserable!) When we walked in, the man at the counter grimaced like he was upset there was a customer. I asked him if they were still open and he just stared at me. I checked on the tiny door sign and the hours said they were open til 10 and it was 9. I walked back in and he had disappeared into the back, probably thinking I had left (although my boyfriend had remained at the counter) It took him probably 5 minutes to make his way back to the counter. I was very excited to see bubble tea and pho on the menu. However, there was a man eating pho at a table and it seemed to be 99% noodles. I decided since we did spend so much on indian I would only get two apps and a bubble tea. I ordered taro bubble tea, with beef spring rolls and a Vietnamese pancake. The bubble tea was terrible. It was ground up ice with a little taro flavoring (i suspect they use a powder mix) And some tough, half-frozen bubbles. It made me sad to drink. It might be the worst bubble tea I have had in my life. The beef spring rolls were bland and poorly constructed; they were falling apart when I got home. The sauce with them was watery and bland as well. The pancake was about 80% bean sprouts. There was one or two shrimp pieces, a few bits of veggies, and i think something like a few slices of beef or pork it was honestly hard to tell. It tasted mostly like egg and bean sprouts. Again this was a limited taste of what was offered, and I might come back and try the pho, but what i did sample did not make me want to come back.

Kalamatas is great Greek food, and the price is right. I got a gyro and hummus for $9. The gyro was the best I've had in a long time. Very tender meat and seasoned perfectly. Fresh lettuce, chopped cucumber, and ripe tomato. They do it up right at Kalamatas. And their hummus is the best I've had. So fresh. Kalamatas is all about quality. The menu is basic Greek food. Other than beef/lamb and chicken gyros they have a good selection of salads, kabobs, saffron rice with chicken, fattoush, tuna salad nicoise, tabouleh, and falafel. Hear the falafel is amazing. The dessert case looked divine! The tiramisu was calling my name, but I resisted. I will have to try it next time. I know I'll be back soon!
What an awesome new spot in Nashville with authentic Greek cuisine! Fun, modern atmosphere with excellent cuisine. Highly recommend Tzatziki and Tirokafteri for side items.

I had a great experience at this restaurant. It doesn't look like much from the outside being located in a small shopping district, but the inside is actually very nice. I ordered the Palak Chicken and it was delicious! I also ordered the cheese naan and was slightly disappointed. I was expecting it to been cheese-filled naan and it was just naan with a little cheese sprinkled on top. Other than that, everything was great. The wait staff were very attentive with drinks and everything else. If I lived closer, I would go there quite often.

My friends and I got the rice combinations and while the meat was tasty, the rice was an odd cheddar yellow color that (surprisingly due to it's outstanding color) tasted like normal white rice. So odd.

I wouldn't quite call this place Greek or Mediterranean. They serve hummus and falafel, and their "chop chop" salad is a variation on a Greek salad, but a good chunk of the menu is fried fish or chicken and french fries. However, the food is fairly solid. I had the falafel "sandwich." Basically, it was falafel with their Greek salad wrapped in a pita. For $4.99, it was a good deal. Additionally, the service was great. The person behind the counter clearly had familiarity with his customers, which was nice. And when he saw that I was a new customer, he introduced himself to me with a handshake, gave me iced tea for free, and also brought me a sample of the black beans and jasmine rice as well as some chop chop salad.

Honestly, I have only had Indian food in South Jersey and have yet to make it to Edison or anywhere with supposedly super authentic Indian food (India, for example ;) ...) so I may be going overboard here with 5 stars, but I will change it if need be in the future. I've been to Palace of Asia twice, once for dinner and once for the lunch buffet. Needless to say, I had a better, more fulFILLING time at the buffet - $10 for all you can eat AND naan?! Come on.. you can't find that anymore. Maybe $7 for lunch at the Chinese buffet, but what is in that stuff, anyway? I tried almost everything there, and I wish I could remember all of the names. I tried paneer for the first time, and although it was a bit too spongey to be cheese for me, I really enjoyed the spices and broth that it was stewing in. Also had saag something or other with chickpeas in it. I love anything with chickpeas and spinach, so this was also very good. I tried the Lamb Rogan Josh - EXCELLENT! With a bit of rice, I ate all of this up! My favorite Indian food, though, is still chicken tikka masala, I feel like I am cheating when I say that, but my boyfriend is Indian and it is his favorite, too, so maybe I am not. At Palace of Asia it is a very thick sauce, but the chicken is cooked well, and when mixed with rice and eaten in the naan, it is delightful. Not too spicy either ;) I tried the gulab jamun, not a fan. Definitely too sweet for me, and I have a hard time with fried food. Bad enough Indian food is made with so much oil! It's ok every now and then, perhaps I should try more vegetarian options next buffet.
Wonderful find off the beaten track! A terrific take on the southern meat and three where local food and Southeast Asian flavors blend for a fabulous, well-priced meal. The banh mi was delicious!
Too many unmarked items- no price on them then when they ring you up it's ridiculous! Nice people but they need to mark prices on all their products.

Went here tonight with colleagues. Rating consistently showed 3 stars. Since it specifically mentioned Pakistani food, we decided to give it a try. Ambiance - not bad. Staff is courteous as well. We went early in evening so maybe that's why there weren't many people yet?!? Food ordered - Pakora - they were ok. I would give it 3/5 Daal tadka - it was ok as well. Nothing exceptional but not bad. A big spicy. Rating 3/5 Kadahi chicken - it is definitely not Pakistani style. Didn't taste bad but Kadahi chicken is not suppose to have curry. Rating 2/5 Naan - bread was decent. Rating 4/5 Grilled platter - Appearance gets 4/5. Taste wise 2/5. It was undercooked. Shrimp and fish tasted good else everything else was undercooked Rice - two bowls. Tasted good. Rating 3/5 Overall gets 2.85 rating. This place definitely doesn't have any Pakistani flavor. Looks like it was made by East Pakistani aka Bangladeshi

Can't say enough how DELICIOUS this place was. We were on a business trip and then a family vacation & absolutely did not want anything we could get here in California. We wanted Caribbean food!!! Well, La Casona delivered. The wait time for the food was a bit longer than usually but it is worth it. The food was fresh. I've only tried Mofongo a few times but this was hands down the best. Even my one-year old loved it! She was loving the alcapurrias also. Will definitely be back when we are in the Tampa area for more of this place! This is a MUST if you want good, genuine Caribbean good.

After 3 days of trying several of the local dishes at various restaurants/bars on and around bourbon street with mixed results I randomly came across this place and wanted a break from all the seafood dishes I had been eating..I stopped in around 8pm on a Monday night to check out the menu...it is small place just off bourbon street and so very easy to walk by and miss....once inside to the left there is a bar high table with 6-8 tall seats and then straight ahead a small counter were you order from...I ordered the combination platter and it was ready in less than 10 mins...the food and salad was fresh and flavour full and the pitta bread was possibly the best I've ever had...from my personal experience for $12 you will do well to find food this good on or near bourbon street!!
highly recommend the pad thai noodles, green curry and thai iced tea...

Everyone was Nice, but the place lacked Spice! Sorry, It's cheesy but I just had to. It's the simple version of the truth. This restaurant used to be Mai Thai in Eagle, but recently the ownership changed, and they tried to run it under the same name but with new owners for awhile. Evidently that was to confusing so they opted for a name change . This news was from the waiter so if its incorrect, I apologize in advance. We were also told the cooks were the same, and they had free reign to make the new menu "authentic". The hubby and I always order 2 control items when dining in a new Thai restaurant. 1) Chicken Pad Thai, 2) Chicken Curry. Since this was the Grand Opening the restaurant was giving away one free glass of wine to each patron, and a free appetizer to every table. We ordered white wine and Chicken Satay. This was the best part of the meal. The Curry and the Pad Thai looked and tasted exactly the same. The color was the same, the seasoning was the same, the taste was the same. And my biggest compliant was how BLAND everything was. Maybe the most bland Thai food ever! Everything seemed as though it was cooked properly, the rice, the noodles, the chicken, and the rest, but there was NO SPICE at all, NONE. My Minnesota born and raised Grandma who is scared of spice on a cheese pizza would have eaten here!!! I don't think I will go back. There is much better curry around town, closer to me, and with some authentic flavor, and spice/seasoning. Give me something more than bland please. To end this review, I will say again, everyone who worked here was very, very nice. But nice isn't something you really eat for dinner.
Presentation was spectacular! Warm and inviting lighting and dining area. Hostess, waiter and serve staff impeccable! What can I say but give it a try and you'll see and taste the sensation!

Had yet another wonderful meal at Jasmine Rice last Saturday with my boyfriend and our friends. This time I had the pad Thai with salmon.... Amazingness!! Other dishes enjoyed by our party were the crispy duck over rice (delicious! and I'm typically not a duck fan), Talay Thai, and the king and I. Everyone left feeling satisfied and impressed. I also must say the atmosphere at Jasmine Rice is so much more comfortable and relaxed than some of the other byobs. I can't say enough about the staff here - everyone is so helpful and very attentive. We will be back again soon!

A very cool spot! It was my first time trying pho and shaved milk ice. Both had great flavor and all the ingredients were fresh. Would definitely return again and bring family or friends who come visit.
The pineapple shrimp curry tastes very good, I ordered Thai hot, but still hope it could get more spicier though.
The atmosphere is all beach, the food is all fun. Don't change your clothes, you're already over dressed. The food is Carribbean, off-beat and very good.

I LOVE this restaurant. My husband and I love to try new places, but Ekta is one of our frequent neighborhood go-to's. Honestly, we'd drive a long way just to go to this restaurant too. The atmosphere inside is great--quiet, cute and a BYOB. The prices here are incredibly reasonable (I might even venture to say cheap) and we love that we can bring our own wine or beer. My favorites appetizers are the samosa chat and cashew roll-both equally delicious and different. I am obsessed with their paneer tikka masala (rich, delicious and addicting) and the lamb vindaloo main courses (a bit spicy and the lamb is awesome). The portions are huge and three of us have shared these dishes before with plenty to spare. They will continue to bring you basmati rice as you run out, so eat up! Also not to be missed-the paneer naan (I love paneer!) and garlic naan--neither are particularly unique Indian dishes but they sure are good!

My aunt lives in the area and has always wanted to try the food at Nadia's. We brought a bottle if white wine (it's a BYO restaurant!) and started with the Shrimp & Corn Fritter as an appetizer. I should have known better given the "fritter" name but it came out a little to greasy for my liking. The flavor was enjoyable, but not worth the calories - I'd skip this one in the future. Now onto the entrees, which were delicious! I ordered the green curry with tofu and brown rice (available upon request for an upcharge) and my aunt had the yellow curry with scallops. The scallops were cooked perfectly! I was able to sample one of her scallops and while the tofu was really good, I wished I had ordered them with my green curry.

When you ask what is a great food truck in University City, Cucina Zapata is one you'll often hear. Situated in the back of the food truck line on Drexel's campus, Cucina Zapata is a Thai-Mexican fusion food truck that you'll often have to wait half an hour or more for. After three previous failed attempts to taste its goods (due to rain, closure, and poor timing), this Spring Break day I finally got the opportunity to try the famed Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito. Going for a late lunch on a Friday may not have been the best time (the usual tip is to go between 11:30 and 12 to put in a preorder), but I got my burrito in around 40 minutes. The fish was nicely breaded and crunchy at certain parts. There were only hints of the Cap'n Crunch, but probably for the best since it would've made it too sweet. The amount of fish was more than it needed, taking away from the other flavors, but you can easily just take some out. The sauce was very good and adding sriracha would do wonders for those who like the spicy. The burrito also had avocado but I didn't get to thoroughly enjoy it since it was left to one side, not evenly distributed. I would definitely come back. At $6, the burrito is definitely well worth. With a drink, it will keep you full until your next meal. I've heard good things about the tacos, so I'll probably get those next time.

Had dinner with a couple friends here. Yummy food! Service was great. Flavorful and well spiced, not overly greasy or creamy. Naan was good but a little dry. Paneer butter masala was great, saag paneer was good, and our friends liked their chicken korma and chicken vindaloo. Will come back!

First of all, some people might think of this restaurant as Mexican, but it's not! I found this gem as I was walking from the Music City Center for the Wizard World Comic Con. The restaurant is somewhat small, but it's delicious food makes up for it. As some people (mostly my family and few friends) know, I LOVE calamari! So when I saw it on the menu, I had to get it. It came out crispy, not rubbery (like I've had it at other locations), encrusted with herbs and cilantro! Yummy! I then went on to have the Ropa Vieja, which is cuban-styled {very well seasoned} pork flank steak. I loved this item. I Had a pina colda (of course with rum....they have a "virgin" style, good for kids). There were some many good items on the menu that the next time I go down, I'm going to have to bring a few friends to sample different food items. Any volunteers.

I didn't get anything here, but this place was awesome! Prices were so reasonable, and the atmosphere was wonderful! Nice 'market' section, cookbooks, spices, drinks, a limited selection of packaged goods, excellent intro into Levantine cuisine, although I'd definitely do my shopping for these items at a place like Makkah Market since they likely have better prices on the market items. I will definitely be back here for coffee, tea, pastries, or food!

Now called Zoes at the NW location. The best Mideast food I've had in any restaurant ever. For example, the baba ghanouj was light and fluffy with a delicate flavor and the dolmas (one of my fave dishes) were lightly seasoned and lemony with creamy rice filling -- just as they should be. Perfect preparation, very appealing, healthful, utterly delicious. The people who work there are knowledgeable, friendly and helpful. I've been there 3 times in 3 months. Its one of my favorite meals in Tucson! Tiny place but clean and pleasant. If the ambiance was better, it would be 5 stars. As it is, it deserves 4.5

Little hidden gem in Haverford area. Find it by chance and already planning the next trip. The service was fast and very friendly. The food came quick and in the order we asked. I have to said it was exquisite the chicken was soft and buttery we had the Vandaloo sauce and the currry. You have to order a naan with it go for the garlic one you won't regret it. Overall a great fantastic little restaurant. Tip: plenty of parking in a Sunday afternoon.

Right up there with Thai phooket for my favorite Thai food in Nashville. This place gets added points for ambiance & solitude even though its just 100 feet off the busy nolensville rd. Low light & nice table settings make this a great date night location without traveling towards the more tightly packed downtown area. Complementary pork rinds are melt in your mouth delicious & appreciated. The rice based dishes here are huge & full of flavor, I usually opt for the combination rice plate with three kinds of meat because meat sweats are the best kind of sweat.....
This place might get missed by some in the area... but you shouldn't. If you like good authentic Thai this is absolutely one of the best options for that in Nashville

Pho dac biet was really oily and the flavor profile was pretty flat. The grilled pork vermicelli was ok but really not flavorful at all--the meat or the fish sauce. Noodles in both dishes were overcooked and mushy. The service is really great though. Nice and helpful workers
The chicken pad Thai is heavenly. Good prices. We frequently get our take-out there and we love it.
I always get the Red curry. Very delicious!!! The restaurant is not as good as it use to be. I have been going there for the last 25years. Over all it's still good!

When you step inside and make your order, sit back and get ready for your tastebuds to take a trip! The food is simple but delicious and layered with flavour. If your not sure what to order the helpful staff will make sure you get just the right meal. Hit this place up on your next trip downtown

Great food. Service is so so, but it is a mom and pop shop. Can't say much for decor,but that adds to the charm. This ain't no high end white table cloth place so don't expect that type of service or vibe. It's literally a hut building. Go and support them!

What a great gem! My family and I just ate there and loved it. Perfect for a family with kids (kids 7 and older)or a romantic dinner for a couple. The restaurant is so clean and beautifully decorated. The food was outstanding. We will definitely go back.

It's good Indian food. I can recommend Taste of India. But I guess I haven't found anything special they do that rates four stars. The food is good and so is the service. I used to eat at their former restaurant at what is now Thai Chili. I've only been to this location a few times.

First time dining at this establishment. Ordered the combination rice and sampler platter. Food was very GOOD! My faves???? The fircracker shrimp and these little steak appetizers (with cheese and onion on the inside). The combination rice (shrimp, chicken and pork) was fire! Will have to try the Souper Bowls the next time.
I went to the restaurant Last Tuesday after 11:00 am only to find it was not open, even though posted per the website it was open. HMMMMMM!

They say it closes at 9PM. We went at 8:15pm and they did not allow us for dine-in. They say the kitchen closes at 8:45, so we cannot allow you at 8:15 which I felt was ridiculous. It seems they only take togo's after 8.

My friend took me here, and I'm sure she will be checking to see my review. First of all, thank goodness for amazing service. Finally, some place where the people are actually nice to you in Philly! (Please don't kill me Philadelphians...) My friend and I both had two short rib tacos. Meat was a little chewy, but the flavor was all there. Slightly spicy, tangy, and overall amazing. A bit pricey for tacos, but two each was enough to fill up our beliies.

There aren't many restaurants we choose to return to, but this one we will.Great food, charming service, appropriate prices, authentic food according to the Ethiopian person with us. The lamb dishes and lentil dishes were superb as were the greens and injera bread. The honey wine is well worth a try, though it was a bit different.
Tom yum soup... am not sure if this is tom yum soup... totally different from what I had in Bangkok

Everything was delicious. Try the tom ka gai. It's this spicy- chicken-coconut-yummy-goodness all in one soup. I also loved the chicken pad se ew really good flavor and not greasy. Thai iced tea was also refreshing and not too sweet. Which is what I hate in thai teas. As far as service, it's hard to tell, our group came early afternoon, it wasn't crowded at all so we got great service. I will definitely come back the next time I'm in SB!

I must have ordered the wrong dish (and my sis in law must have, too) because I did not enjoy my meal at all. I ordered beef thai basil. My experience with thai basil dishes is that they, at the very least, have some miggyfiggy thai basil in them. This bowl of soupy veggies did not have a hint or trace of anything resembling thai basil. Literally. None. Not like, "oh man, i love thai basil i sure wish they put more of it in here!" It was just completely absent from the dish. This place also doesn't take cards. I totally get that lots of little cafes in West Philly don't take cards. It's inconvenient and I hate it but I get that when most of your transactions are $1.75 cups of coffee, accepting debit and credit is not a necessity. But when the average dish on your menu is $10+ being cash only is ridiculous to me. I just don't see why I'd ever return. meh

Nice patio and music but the food is not all that me and friend had some kind shrimp and grits and other entree with shrimp but it wasn't fresh ,the heads were all black and dry really disappointment .

By all means-GO! I took DM the vegetarian here last night for dinner. We'd spent the afternoon in New Hope and since she drove and gassed up, it was the least I could do. Parking was a breeze and this little place is not at all hard to find. We got there right around 5 p.m. and were graciously greeted by Colleen and told to pick any table. This is a really attractive space-great murals, lots of color, mismatched, brightly painted chairs. Made me feel good just to walk in. Colleen gave us a good tour of the menu, the specials and the drinks, all in great detail. It was a lot of information all at once, but she was patient and kind and seemed very willing to answer questions and tell us what her personal favorites were. We both ordered a lemonade with rosewater and cardamon; good enough to be sold by the pitcher! Pulpy, not too sweet and hell-who can't get behind an exotic lemonade when it's in the 80s in South Philly? If you are considering a visit, keep in mind that this is not your typical all you can eat Indian buffet joint with lots of murky, heavily sauced mystery meat dishes on a long steam table. If that is what you want and expect when you think of dining out for Indian-you need to reset your expectations or go elsewhere. There is a beef short rib dish on the menu; that alone should alert you to the fact that your experience here will be something different. We choose the bhel puri as a starter along with an order of the Indian bread basket, which is an assortment of their breads. Colleen asked in what order we wanted our food to come out and was really helpful and solicitous throughout our stay without being obsequious or annoying. The appetizer was a good start-cool, creamy, crunchy, summery and tasty. The young lady who brought out the bread assortment took the time to point out what each piece was and how it was made. It was nice to get the overview of what we would be eating. I had the summer/seasonal version of chicken tikka chaat (refreshing, crunchy and savory protein packed, too) and DM had kala chana curry. DM's came with a side of a garlic pickle which she didn't care for-but I thought it was quite good. We had both eaten a very large brunch at Cafe la Maude earlier and had ice cream in New Hope so our eyes were bigger than our stomachs. Colleen was great about packing up what we could not eat-even to dividing up the bread assortment for us and the barely touched garlic pickle. Colleen explained the dessert menu (wow-they have jelabi!) and we choose gulab jamun which came with cubed mango and a pomegranate mango sauce. This is not one of my favorite Indian desserts and the pastry balls had an "off" fried taste, so we didn't finish it. I'd love to see kulfi on the menu or better yet, rasmali, but I wouldn't diss this place just for a not so great dessert. I mean-really-who goes to an Indian restaurant just for the afters?! The same young lady who served our bread brought us our leftovers and they were packed in the nicest way. Everything here, from start to finish, showed a great deal of care, concern and thought. I had my leftover warmed up garlic naan and cold chicken tikka chaat for breakfast this morning, and immediately wanted to go back to Chaat and Chai for another meal. This is very good food, served with care and attention, in an upbeat space. Open your mind, free it of food bias and get to 15th & Snyder for a dose of chaat. You'll be glad you did!

This is my favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Indy. Though, they need to improve their service. It has not changed since I started coming here in 2010. Well food is great, worth the try, just don't expect good service.

We stopped in for lunch at 1:45... The sign on the door said they were open until 2:00 for lunch... Three of us sat down and the woman told us that they were closed...The woman threw the menus on the table and seemed to be upset that we were patronizing her restaurant. We got up and walked out... We will never come back again... Rude!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Oh my god, the food was delecioussssss and very authentic Indian food!!!! The service was top notch. Suhail the owner made my companion and I feel very welcomed. I was there on 10/14/15 and wanted to go back on Thursday for lunch before flying back home to Seattle but was not able to get in before 2:30 p.m. They are closed from 2:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. I was so disappointed as I was looking forward to eating some more of that home cooking that Mrs Farah cooks with love. Thank you so much for the delecious Karahi dish we had with rice and Nan. I highly recommend it to folks who know what good authentic Indian food taste like. Can't wait to come back for more yummy food. Thank You Again, Ahlam
I have been here a couple times so far. The food is great and the staff is friendly. I will be back soon!

What a nice find! When strolling on South St., be sure to keep going all the way to the end toward Penn's Landing. Your palate will love you forever. Green Basil is a quaint & unique authentic Thai restaurant that won't disappoint. It's super affordable, meticulously clean, & serves the absolute freshest food. It's just delicious!!! And oh yeah, fantabulous service!

I come and get the war wonton soup every Friday. The soup is my favorite off the menu, the food here is great, but they can use some help on some customer service. They never smile nor greet, and I'm not sure if they know how to be polite.

One word: yum! I arrived at Zeppoli right on time for my reservation. What started off the meal perfectly was the fact that the reservation was for 3 and my lame friends were not there yet. Nobody made me wait, they just sat me right down. There's nothing I hate more than restaurants stipulating my reservation! I know it sounds awful but I absolutely judge a restaurant based upon in exterior. I loved the "old timey" sign in the front, the adorable little nook it sat in and the twinkly light still around for effect. It definitely set the mood for a great dinner with friends before even walking through the door. This place is TINY. 12 table tops and three servers/helpers who kind of rotate around the room. This is not a formal setting but you don't feel like you are in your typical South Jersey Italian joint. We did not think the atmosphere was noticeably loud or uncomfortable. The staff was friendly and informative and even offered us a free shot of limoncello on the chef. Awesome! To start I had the Antipasto which was excellent. The waiter told me about the billion different items on my plate but I barely listened and just dove right in. There was nothing on there that wasn't scrumptious and interesting. I would recommend this to share with a friend or the significant other to share if you didn't want to get two appetizers. If you're on a date, I would have found this to be a fun conversation piece to laugh about figuring out what you're eating. My favorite dish that I got because of the reviews on here was the tagliatelli at limone. IT WAS SO GOOD. The flavor was so spot on and it was not drowning in sauce which is always a turnoff. The pasta tasted (and is) homemade and the prosciutto pieces were the perfect size to not overtake the dish. Why not five stars? I also got the gnocchi and was not wowed. They were slightly too soft for my liking and didn't have the spinach flavor I was expecting. I definitely didn't dislike it just would probably not order again. Go if you can! I will be back.

*This review is for Bitar's market-side of groceries and prepared foods, not the lunch counter/sandwich side* I never really appreciated proper Middle Eastern fare until I started dating a good-looking half-Lebanese fellow whose family members are all superior cooks -- coincidentally also named Bitar! Though his mom's baba ganouj is tasty, even she admits it's not as good as Bitar's smoky, creamy eggplant mash. Scooped up with their housemade pita and studded with bits of Bulgarian feta (so cheap at only $6/lb.), or rolled into a wrap with tons of arugula, their baba is one of the most satisfying vegetarian items in existence. Bitar's also prepares huge party trays of baba, hummous, grape leaves, tabbouleh salad, spanikopita and other hand-made edibles for catering purposes. We also pick up grocery items like tahini, chickpeas and rice here at very competitive prices.

Being a military pilot I have been all around the world. One of my first missions took me into northern Thailand where we had local family cook us meals at a remote location while we operated out of their base. I have yet to find original Thai Basil type dish that I came to fall in love with in Udon Thani, Thailand. Today I have found its perfect doppelganger. The dish is aromatic, plenty of veggies (onion, bamboo, and peppers), and the finely diced chicken gives it that authentic texture. After your first bite the slow heat of the (Thai hot = just say "pet, pet, pet" which means spicy) and you will get the authentic heat of the thai basil, with the fish sauce, and peppers crushed with a mortar and pestal which dulls the burn and just leaves a nice heat on the tongue. I will be back, but I will have a hard time ordering anything else. The family is so nice, that when I greeted them with a Thai hello (Saa-waa-dee-krap) they let me know they had just caught a red snapper that day and wanted to share their new snapper larb (cold salad) recipe. Ok, enough already....

YUM! Way better than pattaya thai in goleta! I love their pineapple fried rice, so good! ALSO their pad thai is good but it is a little bit on the wetter side. If you don't mind that then you should be okay! :) The fried bananas were pretttty awesome. Tiny restaurant but very good.

They are located inside farmers market and initially we thought they won't impress us too much but I was wrong .. I have not reviewed a 5 star so easily .. But this one deserved every bit of it .. What amazzzzing food yummylicious took us back home .. specially the vada's (mumbai style ) lovely cholle bhature .. dabeli, (no pics we were so busy finishing it ) .. Thank you masala kitchen .. keep up the yummy work..
Really good pho. Finally a pho place close to home. Affordable and gives a lot of meat

Noodles & Company is a great place to go for lunch or even dinner, it is filling and the food is amazing, it is one of my all time favorite places to eat. Other than the food, the service is quite friendly and respectable, wait times are not too shabby at all, never had a bad experience there, would most definitely reccomend!
This a great place to go for a gyro sandwich or a nice Mediterranean omelet. It's not slick, flashy or trendy; just tasty food made to order
If you're looking to stop by for a quick lunch you're better off going someplace else.. Service is good but can be slow. Be sure to expect a good 20 mins before your meal comes out.

It wasn't awful, but it definitely wasn't good. The chicken gyro had very little meat, no sides, and the meat that was on it was hard from sitting out on the cutting station. As usual, Florida disappoints in the food department.

Excellent Gyros! The mixed olives are delicious, just watch the pits (which is why they are so good). The place is difficult to get to if heading in a certain direction but it's worth driving around a block Can't imagine life before some fine Yelper sent me there for lunch one day. Small area to sit being a deli, great take out and they offer catering.
Best Indian I've ever had and the owner was so sweet. Definitely adding to the rotation of go to places.

PF Chang's provides you with average Americanized Chinese food for a higher price than your average Chinese joint. I've been to this location a couple of times. The service is good and the atmosphere is fine but both times I've been relatively unimpressed by the food. It's not bad, it's just not that good. I prefer to go to my neighborhood Chinese take-out place instead. Try the Mai Tai.

JoTo is tucked back in the corner of the Shopping center behind the Subway, so you might miss it if you didn't know where it was. Entrance is around by the water, not facing the parking lot in case you wondered. Service was excellent and the sushi was very good

I love everything about Olio: the decor, the staff, the food, the selection, the expertise, the ambiance, the booze; I could go on. If you haven't been here yet, you should check it out. It's best for parties of 2-6. Personally, I love the hummus with braised lamb and the pâté best, but everything I've ordered has been fabulous. The cocktails are incredible, always new and rotating so even the regular never gets bored. Ask the servers about the different flavors and spirits inside your cocktail of choice--they're knowledgable, excited to share, and then you learn things!!

Best pho in the city. You go for the food. There are some minor issues - the service isn't great and it's really sunny with the west facing windows at sunset. But, who cares. You're there for the pho, which is on point.

I love sky cafe, their noodles are amazing, the value is just about unmatched in the city, and I'm a big fan of the spice level. I do have one complaint though. Don't talk your customers out of trying new things on your menu! You guys have loyal customers who won't stop patronizing your business if they try something that's a little funkier than they're used to. On multiple occasions I've tried to order something only to be told "you won't like that" or "that's not popular." Well your customers won't know if they like it or not if we can't taste it! I wouldn't even bring this up if I didn't see other people who have had the same experience. If it's on the menu, let us order it. Otherwise I can't recommend Sky Cafe highly enough!

This place is among my favorite Thai restaurants. The food is delicious. I recommend the summer rolls and kao pad with shrimp. The service is quick and the atmosphere is laid back. I've always been in and out in under an hour here. The prices are good. The only thing is, prepare to drink water as they do not ask for drink orders unless you specifically request a drink.

Just happened on Kebab Erbil on Sunday afternoon. I got a kebab and hummus. They were both delicious. My husband got the lamb and rice and enjoyed every bite. We also both got a salad and lentil soup, both of which were great. I can't say enough about our server, Ayas, I'm sure I didn't spell that correctly . He was so kind and helpful when we were trying to decide what to get. He shared a bit about his life when we asked and was so friendly. We will definitely be back!!

This was my first time back since it was Cafe Marcello. Food was very good, I had the Frutta di Mare, with arugula and radicchio salad. Prepared well, and the service was excellent- I will return again!!!

Atmosphere: dark, behind a (abandoned??) go kart rink. Kind of awkwardly placed, but near the Grand Ole Opry, if you want to pop out for Thai! Food: Is what brings it up to a solid 3. I can forgo the environment for the food (sketchy place but decent food? That's fine with me.) Pad Thai is good, Curry is not too watery. Service: Not the best... there were open tables but we waited 15 minutes to be seated (4 of us). I think they were very seriously understaffed for dinner. Generally inattentive.

This is one of my favorite lunch trucks and there are not many! Get a few tacos 2/$6 or 3/$8 The Chicken Satay is my favorite out of the tacos but I usually mix it up with two satay and one short rib. The Cap'n Crunch Burrito is a must have on your first visit! Then get some bubble tea while you are at it. I have been meaning to try the Veggie Burger because I have heard nothing but good things even from my non-vegetarian friends! The truck is hard to miss among the many many trucks on Ludlow. It is at the end closest to 30th Street Station. If you go during prime lunch time you are going to have to wait, but the line and service is definitely quick!

This place though small packs quite the punch when it comes to authentic Thai food. We ordered some of the classics like Pad Thai and Green curry, and they were probably some of the best I have tasted in the Tampa Bay Area so far. The Khao Soi is another dish I'd really recommend and if you can handle spice ask for the special in-house chili sauce that the extremely pleasant lady who runs Orchid Thai makes herself. The lady (we sadly didn't get her name because we were too busy devouring our dinner) is extremely sweet and local patrons that walked in seemed to love engaging in a light hearted conversation with her. I will definitely be coming back here as the food, the manager and the dining experience were incredibly gratifying! Totally worth the hour drive ... So much so that we packed a Ginger Curry to treat ourselves to once we get home!

Suraya is a glorious and much-anticipated addition the the neighborhood. Wonderful ingredients, fresh-baked bread, good coffee, and courteous, professional service (not to mention an exquisitely designed interior). At first glance, it seems like a place that will be both a destination for people from around the city as well as a popular neighborhood spot. As they develop and continue to build their menu, I really hope they keep a selection of items at a variety of prices so that this can be a place I come often, and not just for special occasions. I absolutely adore their brunch spot in NoLibs (Cafe La Maude), but $18.25 for an omelette puts it in the "it's someone's birthday" category. rather than the "it's Saturday" category. Additionally - we go to La Colombe often because it's such a relaxed place to bring our infant daughter. I'm really hoping this place turns out to be similarly family-friendly though, of course, it's totally reasonable if they're going for a different vibe.
BYOB and so so good, I so enjoy going to this place, the people are friendly the people that eat here are friendly, and the food is good and the spices are hot hot hot. Come and enjoy
Just delicious. My new favorite Indian restaurant in Tucson. Be sure you really like spicy if you ask for extra spicy because they don't need around.

This is my local Thai place and I think they do a great job. Favour is authentic and if you like spice then ask them to bump it up to "Thai spicy". I usually do take out but the decor inside looks really well done

As fabulous, delicious and artfully presented as the food options are here, it is truly the service that shines. Visited the place twice while on a trip to check on Mom. Having just returned from France and Spain my foodie sensibilities / expectations were still on high. This place, I dare say could easily be competitive in the food meccas of Barcelona or Paris. Firstly, every single member of the staff was 'extremely' attentive, professional and well informed as to the specific details of food and drink options. As sensible as it might be to assume that this practice should be a 'given' at every restaurant truly committed to delivering an exemplary experience, we know all too well that this is not the case. World class here! Secondly and arguably most importantly, my experience with the food was quite exceptional. I had the fennel salad w/ extra fennel and chicken panini. Friend had niçoise salad and mushroom ravioli, all superb! Mixup with order was profusely apologized for, handled quickly and without an iota of drama. Added perk is that hours of operation extend to 3am on most nights. For a chronically nocturnal foodie wine snob. I'm in heaven

In my last review, I knocked off a star for there not being any Pad Kee Mao (aka drunken noodles) on the menu. Well, the menu has been updated, and now this option is available. I could be totally wrong, but I am pretty sure the rice noodles are house made (at least they taste that way to me). Also, if you loved to get punched in the face with (spicy) heat, then you should order the Beef Yum (Native Thai). It is absolutely one of the most delicious dishes I have ever had! I also think the Thai Tea is on point here and not watered down like it is at many places.
Tried four different dishes including standard chicken pad Thai . Both me and my wife were very disappointed

Decent Vietnamese-style sandwiches, but very slow service. Came in the other day to order the sandwiches to-go. It took at least twenty minutes to get four simple sandwiches (from ordering to payment). I would recommend #1-the special and #9-meatball. The bread toasted is absolutely delicious. I was bit disappointed we received a tiny bag of veggie sans sliced cucumbers, which are a must for banh mi. Maybe it's because I eat a lot, but I find a person would need two sandwiches to be satisfied. Don't get the fruit smoothies, they're bland and the bubbles are too soft/mushy. At least there's a Vietnamese deli in Indy now.

Some of the food on the menu , I found a bit heavy lots of fried stuff . I had the peel and eat shrimp , they were incredible. It was a long wait , but the atmosphere was fun and relaxed . Our server was pleasant and got our order right even though I asked for it to be served differently than how the menu says . One thing I found odd was people were smoking at the bar a few feet away from our table. It didn't really bother me . Honestly I thought it was illegal . Overall we had a had a good experience .

It was my first time going to Guru's Indian Cuisine, and I had a great experience there! The setting is intimate, very laid back. The food is delicious and reasonably priced! Loved the garlic shrimp appetizer and Naan bread! It's BYOB, which is nice as well. Looking forward to going back!

Wonderful staff and service and "crazy delicious" food. Thanks again, guys, for letting us stay late until we had eaten every last bite! Major highlight of my trip to Tampa. Wishing you the best of luck with your business!

Got to be customer # 1! Just went there for lunch, they opened today. They had a choice of two different lunch specials, #1 being a Indo-Chinese-Thai combo, and #2 being a traditional Indian combo. We had a party of three, two ordered the Indian Combo and 1 ordered Combo #1. Everything we very fresh and very delicious. The Naan was insane, straight out of the the oven. Although at first I thought the portions looked small, the bowls they came in were very deep, we couldn't eat everything. The decor is beautiful, all dark wood floors and paneling with nice photos on the walls. The owner used to be the chef at Amans, which was our favorite Indian restaurant until he left. I'm glad to say the food is actually better than it was at Amans. Highly recommended.

Food great. Service was slow to start with beverage order. Beer was forgotten until asked for with meal. No huge issue until 18% gratuity was automatically added to the bill. 20% would be our average for good service , but AUTO tip applied to a table of 3 adults and 2 children - without a word mentioned??? Apologies if menu states 18% gratuity added on parties of 4 or more, but that would not be norm.

It's not my favorite Indian in the area, but it's definitely good. I am concerned that they lack of business is effecting the quality of the food. Too many times I've been here at 6:3007:00 during the week for dinner and been the only person in the restaurant. I hope they can turn it around. The service is friendly and accommodating.

Went to Kabsa for the first time tonight. I had the Lamb Kabsa and it was absolutely delicious. The lamb was cooked to perfection, very tender. It came with rice and a soup to die for. This will become my go to place for nights I don't want to cook at home!

Their tag line is "Curry in a Hurry," but it's nowhere near that. The filthy dining area leaves one to wonder how bad the kitchen is. My flip flops nearly came off my feet from the sticky floor. Dining table tops were not cleaned, and the high chair was nasty. All this was before the dinner "rush" just before 5pm on a Saturday. Plenty of time to clean up the lunch mess--but it seems the dirt is more of a fixture there than something leftover from lunch. Back to the wait... my wife and I were the only ones in the restaurant and ordered some standard fare. Another couple came in and ordered after us, got their food, and I was still waiting at the counter asking the man working if that was my food in boxes in the window. He said yes. I asked if I could have it, and he chuckled and asked me to help interpret for a man who was ordering by phone. The man wanted raita, but the Bawarchi dude couldn't understand. We left empty handed after over 30 minutes of waiting with no food from our to-go order. Curry in a hurry? Puhhh-lease!!!

I walk in here and the first thing that comes to my mind is Wow, this place is cramped up AND so beautifully interior decorated! - Yummy Thai food but nothing different from the other Thai places nearby. - Tried the drunken noodles, Masaman curry, Red curry, Basil Fried Rice & Chicken Satay. - Friendly staff and very well interior designed place! - BYOB PS: Just wished the table seatings were more spaciously arranged. You can literally bump into someone's soup while admiring the wall paintings & showpieces! Will I visit again?
Great lunch buffet. Dinner is good but overpriced for simple things like rice.
Very authentic Vietnamese food! Banh Mi is great! Don't forget to try Sugar Cane juice, Vietnamese egg tarts (this one is crazily good), and Pho!! And their roasted duck is out of this world!

Worst Service I've had in a very long time at any restaurant. Took 10 minutes to even get water. Was before peak time. Yes our server was new but there were several people standing around doing nothing while he was working. They made it a priority to clean all the empty tables before they waited on new customers. Overall food was good but service is where it's lacking.

I walked past Ariana on a beautiful Sunday evening and i couldn't resist going in for dinner. I started with the yogurt drink which I picked salty over sweet. It was very fresh and tasty and especially after a long day at the game. Then I had three sides mix which was the spinach, cauliflower and the lentil, with a side of bread. Everything was absolutely delicious and the service was excellent.

This became one of our default go-to places as soon as we tried it. There are some dishes that we love so much (starting with the Tom Kai Gai Coconut Soup for her and the Tom Yum Lemongrass Soup for me) that we get them every time. Beyond that we've loved everything we've tried but tend to over order just because there are so many things that tempt us.
Food was absolutely phenomenal but here's a word to the wise. Take it easy if you are not used to eating food with these types of spices. Four of us were affected the next day. Bummer.

Great food. Comfortable atmosphere. The tacos are great and they change up the flavors often. The taco that I think is going to be good is always good but the one that is usually my second choice based on its description is often my favorite. Also they may have the best sweet potatoes fries in Indy. Crispy, flavorful, just the right size and perfectly cooked. They lose one star because the lemonade is subpar and more fresh lime would be appreciated with the food.

I've eaten at at least 10 pho restaurants in town and this is one is probably my favorite. It doesn't hurt that it's also in my area. Good service, good prices and good food. It's connected to a gas station but don't let that fool you.

My husband and I have been here twice, there will be many more visits to come! Their calamari is the best I have ever had. We have had the chicken satay, dumplings and the pretzel plate...YUMMMM! I had the mushroom pho and my hubs had the salmon on our first visit...it was scrumptious!! We took our sons with us today and we all had a different burger...all were delish!! Our servers were so attentive and made excellent recomondations!! Looking forward to our next visit!!

It was fantastic as always great people Tony is the chef he is awesome always helping you try different things my lady doesn't try some stuff but he got her trying stuff. You won't regret eating here.

You pretty much have to know you are going here to find it. It's hidden in a side-facing strip mall of Lindbergh that you won't see just driving by. But it's good enough that word-of-mouth should keep it busy. A very simple place that basically just focuses of excellent gyros. The pitas were fresh, not dry. The meat was well seasoned and juicy, again not dry like some places' meat can get. It seemed to be cut just a tad thicker too. Splurge and get the deluxe for ~50 cents more. The crumbled feta cheese adds that extra that makes a difference. Pita and hummus side was pretty good, but really not needed with how well-stuffed the gyros were. Again, the pita triangles were fresh and the hummus had a richness that was enjoyed. Baklava, of course, for dessert. These things were big and dense! And I especially liked the light touch for the honey. Just enough to enjoy without making a big mess of it.

Descent food with quiet a bit of options to choose from during weekend buffet. Good for a change in taste with limited Indian cuisine in the neighborhood. Weekend price is bumped up to $15 from $10.99 on weekday which they justify by saying they present more options for customers on Weekend. Try it out!

8th & Union is by far the best restaurant in Wilmington, DE. Service is superb. Highly recommend the buffalo cauliflower, calamari. All the burgers are amazing, cooked to perfection and to order. The Gouda burger is to die for.

I really enjoy this place, the atmosphere is great and we always have a great, relaxing time. However, we have been overcharged anywhere between $2-$8 every time we've been here. There's no arguing, you'll always be wrong no matter how right you are, and I think today was our last straw. As much as we love the place we will not be going back, the business practices have proven to be dishonest time and time again.
This place is way over priced and is a joke .... i wouldnt come back here id rather go up the road to the gyro place next to papa johns and have same quality for 5 dollars cheaper for a gyro plate
Excellent. The lamb is to die for, the gyros terrific, and everything is fresh. A definite keeper. Do yourself a favor and go here. You won't be disappointed.

charming locale, badass food! Appetizers: *Sticky Tamarind - strips of fried tofu, plated on a bed of mixed greens with a tamarind dipping sauce - fabulous! *Shredded Green Papaya salad - crisp, fresh - delicious. Entrees: * Panaeng Curry with shrimp, 4 star heat - a spiciness that blended perfectly with the sweetness of the peanut sauce - declared the biggest winner by all present, *Green Curry with tofu, 3 star heat - slightly sweet with basil & perhaps annise - fantastic flavor! *Yellow Curry with tofu, 4 star heat - this is my friend's go-to dish, he orders it on nearly every visit! thoroughly enjoyable!

Food is amazing! Had the mojo chicken cuban and it was bursting with flavor! A bit spicy as well. The bread is toasted to perfection. Sweet potato fries are also delicious and come with a very flavorful dipping sauce. This is in downtown Gulfport where there are tons of cute shops and bars, and right across the street is a beautiful waterfront so after you eat, be sure to take a stroll! Also worth mentioning is the lady running the place is full of personality and extremely friendly. She remembered us even though it had been close to a year since we last ate there. And finally, the colored lights in the bathroom were awesome! Be sure to stop in.

Stopped in for a quick lunch and got the brisket and round large pho. The pho was light but flavorful! The service was super friendly and l loved sitting out on the porch on a super nice NOLA afternoon. The veggies to add to the pho were fresh and the service was really friendly and fast. Def stop in if you are craving some pho and are in the area!

Best value I have ever gotten on Groupon! We started with the hummus and the eggplant, then on to the main course! Lobster Ravioli for my wife and the Turkish Ribeye for myself! All amazing! Then, she got Creme Brûlée for dessert and I tried the Baklava. Both very good as well! Service was excellent, and we would have been happy to pay full menu price if we hadn't found the great deal on Groupon!

Since I think this is the only Ethiopian restaurant in Indy, I'll just have to live with it. Everything is good, but I was expecting a lot more spicy! To be fair, I was with a large group and the waiter may have dumbed it down a bit for the group. The enjera is a lot less sour than other places I've had it, but was still spongy and delicious. The waiter (owner?) even brewed some Ethiopian coffee for our group. Overall, we had a great time and the price is very reasonable.

It was late we were hungry and a local said this is the best falafel place in town. Nope. I mean it could be the best one in town but it was not good in any way. Not even decent. Maybe bc I am used to New York halal carts and this was no where similar. Idk but I really would have preferred to have just ate some cheese itz and gone to bed.

The menu was smaller then i expected. I had the lamb ketban platter and amazing i must say!! This was my first experience with morrocan food and I will hopefully be back for more! The lamb was well seasoned and juicy the rice was a well balanced accompaniment. The cucumber salad was soo refreshing and there was coriander in it which I didn't expect. I had the hummus as my appetizer and it was alot more mellow then I am use to. The whole meal was a well balance example of simple but great cooking and doing a couple things really well. I just wish I lived around the corner so I could try the entire menu. Whole meal with a interesting all nature soda was only 12.65. Great deal.

Anyone who knows me knows that I am a freak for Pho. It's probably the most perfect food ever and Pho Orchid is one of the few Pho places I had never been until recently. Pho Orchid is a pretty laid back place and I was excited to see what they had to offer. I got my usual pork spring rolls appetizer and eye round steak and brisket Pho. The spring rolls were really good. The pork was flavorful and the rolls were a good size. The Pho was okay- it was nothing overly spectacular but I definitely enjoyed it enough to return next time I am looking for lunch in the area. I think this spot is probably best for "to go" food pick up, because the tables are pretty small and I felt a little cramped. It wasn't a huge issue, just an observation.

The food here is just so good. Have eaten her several times and it's definitely one of my favorite lunch spots. I've tried a couple of different things but the Grilled Chicken Mediterranean Salad is my favorite! I recommend this place when your looking for good, quick bite to eat.

This was possibly the best Indian lunch buffet we've had in the Indy area. Fo starters, the naan was fresh and delicious, and the mint chutney was definitely homemade. They also had the best selection we have seen, with several vegetarian and vegan dishes as well. The saag was creamy and delicious, and the goat curry was tasty as well. They had a great dessert selection, too, with mango yogurt, gulab jamun, rice pudding, etc. Finally, we received the best service we've experienced at an Indian buffet, and our server was super accommodating of our toddler.
This place is awesome "mom-pop" restaurant with really tasty buffet. Highly recommend! (I am Indian too) :)

I gave four stars( more like a 3.5 star) because I think the food is really a bomb, especially the vermicelli and Pho noodle soup( such as # 15, 17 and 24). The only downside is that the place is too small, and compact. There is not that much room for people to come in and sit.
Food is outstanding! The owner's son came out and took time to explain the food and how they got started. Very pleasant guys, awesome experience.

Although this place is a chain, the service is exceptional, and the food is amazing! I always start off with the Changs spare ribs (hint of star anise), and always share a meal with my boyfriend b/c theres so much food (we even have leftovers for the next day). Save room for dessert. The banana spring rolls are the best thing ive ever ate. Give it a try!
first time eating here and it didn't disappoint the place is clean great service family oriented atmosphere food is HELLA good its worth coming back for.

Finally was able to try him out today and might buy a lottery ticket because there was only one person in line. Gus takes pride in the quality of his ingredients and the food backs it up. Looking forward to more trips here, with or without a (deservedly) long line.

Pho Hoa is a block away from my house so I find myself eating here pretty often. The offerings are pretty good, with the Pho being good but not quite as good as Pho Ha down the street. The steak and broth were noticeably better there. I do like that their menu is pretty extensive, so you can have something other than pho, vermicelli, or broken rice dishes. I also love the smoothies! A must try is the avocado- delicious!! Sometimes I'll stop by just to get one to-go. The service is pretty good here- actually friendly and attentive, unlike a lot of places on Washington... Overall, as the stars suggest, I'm a fan!

Went for lunch yesterday- second visit. Lucked out with a spot in front. Got the hummus and Greek salad platter. Loved it! The hummus was so smooth and yummy! Also really enjoyed the cucumber salad with yogurt and dill that came with it. Will go back as often as I can!

Thai Place is probably one of the best authentic Thai restaurant in the area. One can tell if there is a 30-minute wait on a weeknight, it is worth trying. We were politely and promptly taken care of for our refreshment, order taking, dish delivery, and drink refills. The food was absolutely spot on and made to appropriate portions. Be sure to save room for their desserts.

Per the recommendation of River Front Times best of 2008, gave this one a shot while in STL. Buffet was above average in terms of food, above average selection in the veggie realm, stuffed nana, unlimited mango lassi! Good times, overall quality could have been better, clearly not Bay Area like, but hey.. when in St. Louis not too shabby.

Not sure how my GPS got me here but it worked and sent me through the back. I was almost frightened since the rear entrance was nestled in a hotel of some kind. Yelp has steered me correctly once more, this time in my quest for some tasty Indian food. We only got take out but everything was well prepared, properly spiced and well served. They did give me chicken vindaloo instead of lamb but I was not about to hike back down Marlton Pike to have it corrected, talk about a jacked up road. Car suspension preservation is greater than lamb cravings. The chicken makhani, garlic naan, rice, samosas and accompanying sauces were all on point. I look forward to the dining in version for sho! Hands down the best take out I have had since moving here 2 weeks ago.

such a quaint little place. their bread is to die for. their meat portions are smaller than most places but definitely delicious. and their baklava is way over priced for the little piece they give you. our waiter was very nice and helpful in picking our meals. i enjoyed this place because it was not super crowded, due to the fact it is perfectly hidden under the sushi place.

Establishments like this add to my increasing wariness of Main Line restaurants, no matter how good the reviews. The food here is almost insultingly bland and insipid, drowning in a goopy excess of cashew cream and salt. It is also extremely overpriced for what you get. ($26 for two vegetarian entrees? WTF?) And beware: their website advertises 25% off entrees at lunch time, but when you go to pick up your food, they'll tell you that deal only applies to dine-in orders and refuse to honor what's printed on the website. No thanks.

I recently moved to the neighborhood and always wanted to try this restaurant since I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE Thai food. it was last Friday, I was soooooooooo tired and drained from my hectic-crazy work week. Glad I went early,so, i could soak up the intimate atmosphere, sipping Jasmine tea while listening to the traditional Laotian-Thai music. first, I ordered an appetizer: I was channeling my favorite Thai restaurant in Chicago (Joys) and thought I should try the fresh, vegetarian spring rolls. I had one before from Vientiane, as I did the Baltimore Ave stroll in August. Yum! It was light and tasted nice with the sauces it comes with. Then, my entree: I have always LOVED Thai noodle dishes. Nice fragrance and spices. Yum! The Vegetarian Pad See Eiu is chocked with veggies and Tofu. It has a nice flavor too. I am glad the restaurant is a mere couple of blocks from my apartment. It was very good. PS when I walked by after my coffeehouse visit to Satellite Cafe, I saw the cafe was filled to capacity later that evening. Awwwww, come early, come often!

Fez only even gets stars because the food is delicious but here's the catch- it's probably the worst service you'll ever have. Atmosphere: Awesome. The windows are all blocked out (we had no idea it was torrential downpouring) and there are awesome tapestries all over the walls and ceilings. There is cozy seating and awesome gold tables. Great decor. Three of us went here for a celebration dinner with a groupon. We each decided to do the 7 course vegetarian feast. Everything was very fresh and delicious. I liked the second course best although I had no idea what it was. So an hour or so later once we've gotten through all of them we get the bill. Here's where things go south. The first bill had no gratuity added to it as there were only three of us, not five. Once we gave the waitor the groupon he came back with a $19 tip added AND more tax on there. How does that happen?? We read the fine print on the groupon and menu neither of which allowed this. We approached the waitor about it and he wasn't helpful. One of the more bold people I was with then went to the manager with it and he would not even look her in the eye and said they added gratuity for 'more than two.' Shady business. We even told them we were going to tip them- and in cash not on our cards. If it weren't for the whole tax/gratuity debacle I'd go back in a minute. But, they were so rude about the whole situation that it left a bad taste in my mouth (not to mention my friends as well). So, if you want good Moroccan food and a cool atmosphere and don't mind getting ripped off and having terrible service- go here. Oh- and I didn't get my opentable points even though we filled our reservation. And we got bread that looked like it was from Amoroso's instead of pita? Strange behavior all around...

Reading the other reviews, there must have been something wrong tonight. It took 1 hour to get our food and the restaurant was not even very busy. You would think that waiting for an hour would make everything taste better on account of us being hungry, but it did not. The food was serviceable, but it was not worth waiting for an hour and definitely not worth going back for. I will definitely look for a different place next time I am in the mood for southeast asian food.
best lunch spot in university city. Thai Tacos are mouth watering and worth the wait in the long lines. I highly recommend this place.

This was our first experience at this brand new restaurant. My husband and I are great fans of Indian food and we've been looking for a great local place. I hope this continues to be a go to spot. Food was outstanding. Service was impeccable with the server asking the chef to make is something that wasn't on the menu. They also gave us a lovely complementary dessert which we will have again. Good job to the owners and staff and we look forward to going again.

I went to Fez one night for my friends birthday. We ate, hookah-ed and watched the belly dancing. I don't smoke so I can't comment on the hookah but the food was pretty good and the belly dancing inspired me to take classes. This is a pretty cool out-of-the ordinary place to visit.
Dropped in to get some halavah to bring back to SoCal. The halavah was very bitter and not very fresh. We were very disappointed and will not go back.

Had Thai Ice Tea it was very very sweet. could drink even quater of thr drink. Ordered Penang curry and Yellow curry, they serve it with rice which server in the same dish as rice. Both curries were good.

Great find en route from Maryland to NYC. Brunch menu is interesting and the $4 make your own Bloody Mary is awesome. A duo is playing blues so a really nice atmosphere for a Sunday brunch and worth the detour - back to the Delaware Memorial Bridge to get north.

I like the food but the rest is a bit quirky. Parking can be a problem with Lazy Acers providing overflow While the food is good, there's very little embeance. It looks like a strip center eatery but at least there's beer and wine. Red curry with chicken $9.95. Not on the lunch specials @ $8.95. Odd that I was charged $10.95. Looked again and the menu was clearly marked at $9.95 for all curries and $2 up charge for shrimp. Where did the buck come from? Asked for brown rice and the waiter came back a few minutes later and confirmed I wanted white rice. It's only him on the floor servicing 15 people (about 1/3 full) so maybe he's in the weeds. Friendly service bit a little scatter brained. I'll be back but it will be tough to try dinner here. Solid lunch destination.

Wow! This place was outstanding! We had just arrived in Tampa, after a very long car ride. We decided to give this a try, based on the reviews, proximity to the hotel and it being touted as something quick. I had absolutely no reason to suspect that it wouldn't be good, but it far exceeded my expectations. I wish that I would have gotten the name of the employee acting as cashier. I'm not sure if he was an owner/manager/or just exceptionally good at his job. He was so friendly and personable. He took the time to offer us a sample of the delicious beans, rice, and chop chop, while explaining that they are made fresh. He checked in with us to see how we were enjoying our food. He made sure to thank us & wish us a good evening on the way out. Seriously, exemplary customer service! The food- DELICIOUS! Everything tasted fresh & flavorful. The toughest critic in our group, my ridiculously picky 9 year old, said that she was going to "call the Mayor of our Hometown & tell him that he needs to put a Zeko's in" haha. She asked if we could come back for every meal during our trip! Everything was wonderful, but I will say that the Beef Kebabs truly stand out. They were incredible! This is not at all what I was expecting from a "fast food/quick service" style restaurant. I frequently order similar at table service restaurants, which aren't nearly as good. These were cooked perfectly at the requested temperature. They were so tender and juicy! I HIGHLY recommended them!
Best kept Bahn Mi/Bubble tea spot there is. They also offer bubble tea made without creamer which is a lifesaver.

This is my 3rd time here and I can't believe I have never written a review. This place has changed hands since I have been here last, but the food is just as good as I remember. My husband and I went in yesterday for lunch and had the lunch buffet I can't remember the names of everything,but I can tell you you need to try the chicken meatballs they where spicy, but super good. My husband had 2 helpings. Service was good also, we where greeted by a man and sat, a lady came by and cleared out empty plates and then the man always kept our drinks full. Just can't say enough good things about this place!

Carry out- Lamb Curry. Ok...I'll admit the flavor of the Lamb curry was really really good. And the meat incredibly tender (although at least one of the chunks tasted like beef...which seems to be a common practice at some lower end Indian joints even when you order what you think is 100% lamb). Probably the biggest shocker was that I don't think any actual"cooking" happened. The woman in back pulled a large vat from a cooler. Nowwhere was there the sound or smell of cooking. Yes...I think they just heated up some premade curry in the microwave. Again...incredible tasty. And the naan...I literally think it was the same stuff you buy in the freezer or in the bread aisle at some grocery stores. You know...that sort of longish triangle with rounded corners? Sure it was warm but not at all crispy...again, I think it was just microwaved. I do a better job at home with the store bought in my toaster oven. Lastly...not a lot of food for $15. I had to buy the one lame piece of naan. And he said he put some rice in the bag as if it didn't come with that. Lol. So...again, it was some very very good lamb curry. (I just finished it. Too bad there wasn't a lot more). And I guess curry gets better after a few days in the fridge like chili...but I won't be going back. Not the least of which reason was the general weird "non restaurant" feel of the place and that they were cutting up raw chicken right behind the counter...practically right next to the cash register. So one minute he's cutting up chicken, then taking my order, then cutting up chicken again, then putting my order in a bag and ringing me out. Maybe there was a sink right there and some hand washing? I don't know. Just odd. Again...good, albeit small amount of food. But im just hoping to god I don't come down with salmonella.

Great food, great service, welcoming owners...Great prices too. We have plenty of leftovers for another full meal for the two of us. Great center city location with a small customer parking. my only complaint is the nats. they're all over, i think due to the numerous plants in the restaurant. my suggestion - sit in the middle area away from all the greenery and you should be ok.

The food was delicious . I order the coconut shrimp and avocado salad and the cheese steak egg roll. I love them both, but I would suggest the dipping sauce for the cheese steak egg roll to be something other than hot sauce. My fiancé got the BBQ chicken I tasted it but it was nothing special. I did love the dressing for my salad, it was sweet but not too sweet. For a drink, I tried the coconut juice... Yum. When they bring your drink to the table, the straw will have a paper heart on the top (so sweet). The coconut juice had slices of coconut and coconut ice cubes inside the drink.I was impressed. What made me go inside was the pictures of the food on the outside of the restaurant and the food is exactly as pictured.

We have been to Blu Fig twice and have been served fresh, healthy food that tasted amazing. We had a great conversation with one of the owners and they use ZERO processed ingredients! Everything is made in house from scratch from the hummus to the gyro meat and even the fresh smoothies! We have had the hummus, tabouli, gyro pocket, rice, grilled chicken, house chips, bubble tea and even the salmon....All outstanding. Can't say enough great things about this place and the people that serve here are awesome. We don't even live in Nolensville but drive here for an awesome quick dinner or even lunch. They even make their own tahini and serve gluten free, vegetarian, dairy free and even vegan options... We'll be back to try more of the menu for sure. Can you tell I was impressed? I haven't done many reviews but our experience was so great both times, I had to share.

Tandoor did not live up to expectations. The food was bland and oily. I highly question the palettes of people that are giving this place anything higher than 2 stars. My roommate and I had take out from this place a little while ago. We both agreed that the food was mediocre at best. The next day, we were both sick from it. They did throw in free desert, which was nice. Perhaps they do this to win over customers who otherwise would not be satisfied. I'm never going back again.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Was surprised that this place was now a Thai restaurant. It was very fresh, authentic, great flavors. Nothing dressy about this place but some of the best Thai we have had in Reno. The spring rolls were very fresh and loose wrap with large shrimp. I love the Thai tea. They also will refill Thai tea for 1.50 when everyone else makes me buy another full price. The yellow curry had so much flavor instead of just pure heat that many places serve. I want to try one of there classes. You cook in groups and then eat all the if all dishes. With wine the price looks reasonable but have tried it yet. Don't miss the mango and sweet rice desert. Best I harbor ever tried.

Amazing food. Entertaining and engaging staff. They do treat you like family. My wife had a huge Gyro salad that they call regular. The "large" is enough for a small diner party. They have fabulous gyros, and they customized mine to order. We had a nice piña colada shake and tried their falafel. Everything was great. The portions are huge. The prices are a bit more than average for lunch , but you can't argue with the serving sizes. You can watch the prices and still come out with an affordable lunch with great quality and quantity. We were hungry so we went a bit overboard. Be ready to ask for to-go containers for the leftovers. The place is clean, with nice tables, beautiful tile work and they even have nice outside seating for a day like we had today. Enjoy! We did!

Have you ever visited a place with high hopes, had those mostly met, and then had those dashed all in one visit? That was my experience here. I love Greek food and was pleased to find this place on Yelp. I visited around lunch time during the middle of the week. I was slightly confused as to how to order since there isn't really a clear routine to how to do that. I ordered my chicken gyro plate, though, and payed. As I was sitting down, I noticed that most people were receiving their food rather quickly - usually in less than 5 minutes. I received my salad very quickly. After that, though, things went downhill. It took 40 minutes for me to receive the rest of my food and this happened only after I went up to the counter to ask where my food was. (You might ask why I waited so long, but I assumed that maybe my food was taking an extended period to cook. That, and I gave the benefit of the doubt.)
