It took less than 2 minutes for my food to come out after that. Needless to say, I was not happy. The manager apologized and blamed it on a "mixup," but why did no one notice when they walked by my table several times? Not pleased. The food itself was pretty good, although i thought $10 for that amount of food seemed like a bit much. I might try a different location, but I highly doubt I'll be returning to this one.

Very good thai food. Nice little classy sitting area. Kinda small and long, narrow. I. Don't suggest you take a bunch of people. You can... Only when it's not busy though. Wait staff is great. Prices are good. And they do take out. Call ahead and normally always ready within 15 minutes.

Incredibly delicious and awesome prices! - great service every time I've been - love the kibby, falafel, and yogurt salad appetizers! - We always get the gyro sandwich - can't beat the ingredients and price. Super delicious. - Yummy beverages too! Mint lemonade! Lebanese tea! Turkish coffee! Scrumptious!!

After a few times seeing their truck parked on Passyunk Ave and 24th I decided to give them a try. At first I was concerned that there were no prices listed but what the heck, I wanted Curry chicken and nothing was going to stop me. I tried the small curry chicken platter with two sides (yams and Mac and cheese) and an additional side if cabbage. The chicken had little flavor, was mushy...the texture really turned me off. The yams weren't sweet, just taste like cinnamon and/or nutmeg, couldn't really tell. The Mac and cheese was a crime...tasteless, separated and eggy. The cabbage was ok. All in all I wouldn't go there again, of all the things I purchased, had I found anything that was some what good I'd be willing to give it another shot. Also, I paid $16 bucks, according to my brother I may have overpaid but how could I know since there's no price list.

A wonderful little gem in an unexpected location. Love the little record player on the bar. Extensive wine and drink menu; I believe the food menu changes. I've tried a few of the dips (za'atar yogurt dip - YUM) and sandwiches - all were excellent. I cannot wait to come here in the summer and sip wine on the patio. I've been here twice, once on a weeknight and also on a Saturday. The Saturday was very crowded and the service was not so great, but the food and wine made up for it. The experience during the week was exceptional. We were given a tour of the space and an unexpected lesson in wine.

Spice-N-Grill has become one of my favorite Indian restaurants in the St. Louis area. Run by a friendly husband and wife team a couple miles from the loop, this place consistently delivers some of the most flavorful Indian food around. Food is made to order, and you can also customize the spiciness of your dish. I opt for medium which is fairly spicy, so if you don't like a lot of heat you may want to let them know. I highly recommend the insanely delicious Chicken Tikka Masala and the unique Goat Pishwari. The Aloo Gobi is an excellent vegetarian option, and the chapati bread is a nice alternative to naan. I should disclose, however, that this place is small, brightly lit, and lacks the ambiance of some of the larger Indian restaurants in town. Nevertheless, if you're looking for incredible food with bold flavors I'd strongly suggest giving Spice-N-Grill a try.

We stopped in before a ball game at CBP. It's a cute little corner Italian restaurant with very friendly staff. BYOB is a huge plus. Unfortunately the food is so so. Our party had the lobster ravioli, breaded chicken, spaghetti and meatballs, beat salad and artichoke. The lobster ravioli was fishy tasting. I don't think they were fresh or homemade. The chicken was decent. The meatballs were ok, but tasted more like sausage. The beat salad was extremely salty, which we had to send back.

Great place to go for a water view while you eat. Had the crab cakes and a fruit cup. Angel our server was spot on the whole time. Very informative and quick with answers about the oysters from where they come from and why the prices are higher. Live music while you dine and relax. Would like to go back in the evening time to see a sunset and the ambience.

When Kombo closed, I was so sad. When Thai 5 opened, I was hesitant to check it out, worried that nothing would compare to my beloved Kombo. When we walked up and saw familiar faces in the kitchen, I let out a small cheer. Sure enough, the menu was nearly identical and so was the quality of food. Pineapple fried rice is still my favorite, but I also love the amazing Thai, pad Thai, and pad see ew. If they have banana coins, you must order them! I'm so thankful to have amazing Thai food back in the neighborhood!

The food is and service is great. Just watch out for the to try and sneak on automatic tip for a party of 5 which was put on the total bill including tax (ended up being 21.5% tip). tom yum soup is very good.
Decent food and quick service. We had fried wontons, General chicken, fried rice, chow mien and honey shrimp. Nice clean restaurant.

Picked up takeout. Staff was nice. Fast cooking, but food was mediocre. Lacking strong flavours, rice a little overcooked, Thai iced tea was overly sweet and served with whipped cream, odd for Thai iced tea. It was disappointing and I found much better authentic Thai food at Orchid Thai.

Great spot to watch the sunset. I've been coming here for years on my trips to Florida. Service is good although you need to double check the check they seem try to up charge people often. Food is delicious, I recommend the grilled fish sandwich and tacos. Hush puppies are always great. The sweet potato fries with apple butter are a good change of pace. All in all a great low-key pace place to relax and take it all in.

Nothing bad at all to say about the food! Excellent food, excellent portions, decent service, but the reason for the three stars... the smell! They burned the most noxious incense the whole time we were there. It was a bit overwhelming to walk into a cloud of stinky smoke especially in a restaurant. We both thought that the food was a bit bland but honestly it may have just been that our senses were overwhelmed. I know that Indian food is strongly scented to begin with so I get what they were trying to do, but it is OK to walk into a restaurant and smell good food. it is not OK for me to walk out of a restaurant and have to go home to shower and change my clothes.

I really enjoyed this new pho spot on Fairmount. It's walking distance to bars, ice cream parlors and the Eastern State Penitentiary. It is a friendly and quaint neighborhood spot to meet friends or family for a filling lunch or dinner. I loved the 2 walls that had Vietnamese hats and the other wall had a painting mural of a bamboo forest. The prices are so reasonable and the pho bowls range from Small-Large ($7-10). I got the large but should have gotten a small or medium because it's SO MUCH food! ONE Large bowl is good enough for 2 people to share. This pho is way better than spots in DC because it flavorful and not just a bland chicken or beef broth that was poured into a bowl with noodles and meats. I ordered the #32. I will definitely try it again on my next visit to Philly.

Very clean environment , lot of parking . Nice authentic decor . Friendly staff . Variety of options . Good quality food with diversity in flavors . Nice combination of caribean and African cuisine . I recommend the lunch menus
I am happy to report that the owner contacted me to say that they are revamping the grocery area and will be glad to offer my preferred tahini again. That's service!

I've been here twice now and the owner is very nice!!! It's a small family owned place. The food is good, the service is GREAT!!! The pho is not as awesome as it could be, but for Avon, it's fantastic. They use hu tieu broth, not pho broth. The sandwhiches are great. The grilled pork chop had a little too much five spice - type seasoning on it. We have not tried the bubble tea yet, but that's next. Overall definitely a good addition to Avon's 'restaurant strip'.
Nothing special. Tried a few different dishes with some friends, none of them were unique or interesting. Very average in every way.

What a gem of a restaurant! Delicious, fresh middle eastern cuisine in Arabi at very reasonable prices. I've had their appetizers, gyro plates and more, and am never disappointed. The staff is friendly, and it's great take-out or dining in.

Extremely dishonest and poor service. One of the worst dining experiences I've had. Double check your receipt! I ate dinner at this restaurant with 1 other person. When I received the check, I used a groupon and credit card to pay. When I got the receipt page to sign I noticed they charged an automatic 20% "service charge"!?!?. They didn't even point it out to me when they gave me the receipt. I understand this charge if you have a larger party but there were only two people eating. There was no mention of this automatic charge in the groupon terms and conditions. When I asked them what the charge was for, the man at the counter told me it was their own rules that they applied for people from out of town? What does that even mean? I live 5 minutes down the road! When I explained this was wrong for them to automatically add this service charge the man again said it was their own rules. I would have probably left a 20% tip anyway but now I have to make a dispute through my credit card and dispute with groupon as I feel I was scammed by this restaurant. The food is not good, and the service poor. Very shady and dishonest business, would not recommend to anyone, and check your receipt!

This place is always packed at lunch time - perhaps because it is a new place in an area with not a lot of lunch options. Or maybe because it really is good. I have mixed feelings on the place. Like I said it is always busy - they do have some great dishes, and the lunch specials are fantastic for the price - plus you get enough for 2 meals! It's a take out place - with a few stools to sit - but those are mostly used for people waiting to receive their food. Everything is cooked to order which is nice to see as well. The only thing I don't like is the soup combo is extremely small for a lunch combo, oh and if your going to visit the green curry is a preferred choice over the red! Enjoy!

The currys here are A+. Very flavorful, spicy (if you so please), and delicious. I got the biryani and it was OK- a little less flavorful and definitely less spicy than I would have liked. The meat included is always delicious. Garlic naan was amazing as well. The owner of this place is also super nice, remembers us and is always so helpful when providing service. I disagree with the majority about this place being cheap- I don't find it particularly cheap, but rather on par for Indian/Pakistani food in the area.

My first impression: I'm the only person to walk into a small dining area and literally every single table is littered with used dishes from the dinner crowd. It looks like they only have one lady working the front of the store, and a cook in the back. My rating is strictly on the food itself, and not the service. But if I'm being completely honest the service made me feel uncomfortable. At some point there were 3 diners and the lady had a hard time keeping up with cleaning the tables, attending to the customers, and pushing out orders. It wasn't pleasant. I also wasn't a fan of the chunky reusable plastic chop sticks. It was more difficult to keep food from falling out compared to the one-time use wooden chopsticks. I ordered the fried egg rolls, the #12 pho (eyeround + brisket), and bubble tea. Fried pork rolls: These were tasty. The filling itself had a very bold flavor, I'm guessing from a generous amount of black pepper. I enjoyed it these, though I have definitely had better. You get a small amount of dipping sauce, and wilted shredded lettuce for garnish. I'm not sure what purpose the shredded lettuce serves. Personally I like fresh crisp lettuce to wrap around my rolls. So although these were tasty, I've definitely had better. I would probably repurchase these again. 3/5 Pho: I had pretty high hopes for this pho considering all of the reviews. However, the pho had an overwhelming cinnamon and clove aroma. It's the one thing I couldn't get over while eating it. The pho came with a very generous amount of sliced onion, scallions, and cilantro which I loved. You get an average amount of meat and noodle. I think the broth would have been perfect if it had more of a beefy aroma. This specific broth simply overdid it on the cinnamon/clove spices ratio. I don't want my pho smelling like a Christmas candle. Though I will note that my leftovers tasted more like traditional pho after the bean sprouts, basil, green peppers, hoisen sauce, and sriracha were added into the broth and refrigerated for a day. The cinnamon-clove aroma was no longer overwhelming and the broth was very very tasty. I think if they tweak the spices ratio a bit then this broth has potential to be exceptional. 3.5/5 Bubble tea: Too sweet for my personal liking, and the boba was frozen. I think she used too much ice and there were chunks that weren't crushed when she blended it. Will not repurchase bubble tea here again. 2/5 I drove the 30min out of my way to try out this place. I personally do not feel that it's worth it and I do not see myself going out of my way to come here again. The pho has so much potential because it is definitely good quality broth, but the clove aroma is a complete turn off. It might be someone's cup of tea, but it's not mine.
Tried to stop by while on a business trip to the area, only to find out that both the restaurant's website and Yelp were wrong - they are not open on Sundays

Grand opening. Grand closing. Order there the other day off of another website. Went to pick it up only to find that the place was closed. I went into the grocery store next-door to ask what the deal was and they were real shady about it. Bottom line is I think the people of Collegeville and trappe need to look elsewhere for their Indian food.

Newtown needed this restaurant. The food is fantastic. They cater to gluten free and are aware of avoiding cross contamination. Try the gluten free naan with just about anything on the menu and you'll be happy. I frequent this place more than I should, and am never disappointed. If what you're looking for is simply great Indian cuisine, without any of the fluff, you can't go wrong here.

My daughter and I went here for lunch and were not disappointed. Her chicken shawarma plate was exceptionally good. My gyro sandwich was overwhelmed with lettuce leaves, but tasted great. (I ate half or more of the lettuce separately.) Grape leaves are served cold. Pita bread is soft and delicious. Hummus is excellent. Reasonable prices. We'll go back!
No fries!? Really? This is Idaho! Fries go so well with a gyro! gyros are great. didn't really want to giv e one star but needed to address this egrigous omission.lol
Best gyro I've had in franklin. The location isn't great and either is the inside, but my review is for the gyro. I'll be back for sure to have another.

Thai food is my absolute favorite, and Siam Cafe is definitely the best I have ever had in all of the many places I have lived. There are several thai restaurants within a couple miles of my apartment, but the 20 minute drive to Siam Cafe is worth it!!! The place itself is quaint and comfortable, always with friendly service. I always order the chicken satay and I am amazed every time at the peanut sauce. I don't know what they put in it (maybe applesauce?) but it is addictive. I also love their Massaman Curry...definitely the best ever. It is the perfect combination of creamy and spicy, with tender chicken and perfectly cooked potatoes. I am salivating just thinking about it. Though this place is kind of out of the way, and not in the best part of town, I wind up there at least once a month.

I took my wife and kids here, and I ordered a meal with hummus substituted for another item. The waitress brought my order out without the substitution, saying her boss instructed her to do this. Well, if she'd informed me at the time I'd ordered, I could have chosen something else. But to tell me after the food arrived, with my family ready to eat after a long wait, what was I supposed to do? Also significantly better Mediterranean food in town (e.g., Zayna). Haven't been back.

I went to Palace of Asia for a lunch buffet. They offer satisfying Indian entrees and the price is moderate for what they serve. Delicious food but I took off one star because they didn't offer many options for desert and the desert options they had were dull and unsatisfying; they only had the cheese balls cooked in some sort of syrup (which tasted like a munchkin from Dunkin Donuts drowned in high fructose corn syrup), and a "fruit blend" featuring some honeydew melon and grapes (which looked like it had been sitting out for a while). I've been to other Indian restaurants that offer a wider and better desert selection. However if you steer clear of the desert table, the rest of the food is quite tasty. The location is a bit awkward (connected to a motel?), but inside the place is roomy and well-decorated.

Great little Thai place tucked away on a side street right near the train tracks. If you are eating in, street parking might me tricky and the dining area seemed to be a little tight. I ordered takeout and food was ready to go when I got there. Drunken noodles and the red curry were great! Pad Thai was good. Everything looked, tasted fresh and had great flavor. Prices are a bit on the higher side. My only regret is not ordering my dishes spicy or at least leaving with a side of hot oil. No worries as I'll make sure to ask for it next time I order.

I like the food, but I am also spoiled because I can walk here. 10% cash discount. I'm writing this review because I could not find a menu online anywhere. I typed out the basics here: APPETIZERS Steamed dumplings, $6 Buddha dumpling, $7 Thai spring rolls, $6 Fresh summer rolls, $7 Taro & tofu todds, $7 SOUPS Mushroom soup, $5 House soup, $6 Tom ka gai, $6 Tom yum, $6 SALADS Salad kag, $7 Som tum, $9 Rainbow salad, $8 Beef salad / duck salad, $9 Larb kai, $12 NOODLE & CURRY DISHES * tofu, chicken pork $13 * shrimp, duck, seafood $15 Pai thai Pad see eaw Drunken noodles Pad woon sen Massaman curry Red curry Green curry Yellow curry FRIED RICE Basil fried rice, $12 Pineapple fried rice, $13 Crab meat fried rice, $13 TRADITIONAL THAI DISHES Bold spicy shrimp, $16 Jungle princess, $14-16 Thai eggplant, $14-16 Three friends, $15 The basil, $15 Chu chee duck, $18 Thai's lamb $20 Seafood lover, $17 Salmon apricot, $17 Heavenly fish, $18 Love & passion, $16

I went out on a second date to Jasmine Rice because I looove Thai food, even though I can't name most of the dishes. It was Saturday night, so the place was packed and there was only one table available RIGHT next to kitchen-Yikes! But they quickly made up for this inconvenience with excellent service. They were on! If they saw I was done with my appetizer silverware, they promptly replaced it with our entree cutlery. They saw my water running low...seconds later, it was filled. It was like watching a well orchestrated waiter ballet. I started to sway in my seat. Then came the choreographer of this perfect dance. I believe his name was Bob. He created the menu and he took the time to explain it and suggested something that was...mmmm! I wish I remembered the name of it, but it was duck and sweet and spicy and exactly what I wanted. Aside from the food, I believe that Bob was the best part of the experience. He was informative, jovial and really was the icing of an already wonderful dining experience. If I had to complain about anything it would be the size. Intimacy is one thing, but at one point I felt like I could reach over and have some of our neighbor's appetizers and they would be none the wiser. But if they continue with their top-notch service, expansion should be inevitable. Loved it!
This is the best Jamaican food I've ever eaten in my life! I'm pullin up everytime I'm in philly from now on! The jerk wings alone should get an award! I'll be back probably every week until I leave!

Giving iLuv Pho 2 stars for 2 reasons: 1. The soup was actually pretty good 2. The guy working at the counter was sort of friendly. Will I go back? Most likely not. We went on a Tuesday afternoon around 2. The place had about 2 or 3 tables already eating, and the rest were empty. We stood at the counter for about ten minutes as the server walked back and forth occasionally glancing in our direction and seated us, perhaps after realizing that we were actually intending on eating there. She pointed at the room and said to sit wherever. The menu did not arrive until we had waited another ten minutes. We both ordered the vegetarian pho, a couple waters, and a green tea boba for me. about 45 minutes passed. My drink did not come. When the soup came out, the server didn't bring any napkins or utensils. She ignored us for another 10 or 15 minutes and when I got up to ask her, she seemed very annoyed by the request but finally brought some napkins and spoons. No sprouts or basil came, I again got up to ask her and could tell that she was getting more and more irritated at these requests. "they have to wash them." she said as she was walking away. Ten minutes later they came and we ate them in our cold soup. Last thing I asked for was my green tea boba. Not wanting to be rude, I said "I forgot, did I order a green tea boba?" "uh-huh" she said, but the request seemed to irk her yet again. The drink never came. As I was paying I asked the man at the counter whether or not it had been made but perhaps looked over by mistake. Nope, not the case. The order was never placed. I understand having a new business and the stress that can come with it...but really, people! To sum it up: Food is ok, but this place had the worst service that I have ever experienced. You will feel unwelcome by hoping for the most basic accommodations like napkins and spoons. Go to Pho 88 down the road. Super sweet people, wonderful service and better soup.
I eat here often. I am obsessed with paneer masala and I always ask for it spicy and they deliver!

Excellent food. Atmosphere isn't much, but who cares when you can get such great tasting, authentic food that is fresh and made to order without driving into Philly? We will definitely be back, and soon. Pho was excellent, BBQ pork summer rolls were top notch, and the Bun with BBQ pork and a spring roll was amazing (lots of fresh veggies, which was great).

Very poor service and poor quality of food. The pap di chaat was substandard. The oil in the cauliflower pakora was old and so we returned. Goat curry was average and the Punjabi Chanda was old. Dessert of mothers Kulfi was good and do was the mango ice cream.

Great food but the cook times are all over the place often erring on the side of long. I would avoid this place if you have anywhere you have to be soon after as you will surely be late, even if you order ahead for take out.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Wonderful food, amazingly delightful and I'll be back without fail. The owner is a kind man and cares for his customers unlike you see it today's typical restaurants. Their beer selection has anything you like to include some rare opportunities for Belgian beers that aren't available everywhere. The atmosphere is comfortable and has soft tones of music from India/Pakistan. The seating is comfortable and perfect for having an intimate night in trying excellent food or a business dinner with colleagues.

Went here with a group last weekend, which was great as we got to share each others dishes and taste a lot of the menu. We started with some Chaat's to share which we're really nice, and unlike any Indian food I've had before. The Chana Chat was my favorite. For my entree I had the lamb curry which was quite delicious with just the right amount of spice. My friend had the beef short ribs, which were served as 3 tacos and we're amazing. The beef was incredibly tender and delicious. The restaurant is well decorated with a really bright Indian motif. It's a small restaurant with minimal seating (maybe 20 seats) it was pretty much full the Saturday that we we're there. I'd definitely recommend this place and hope to go back soon.

Had been driving past this place so many times and wanted to give it a try. Heard good things about the pizza, but went to eat Lebanese food. We were very disappointed. Maybe we expected too much, but the food was not impressive at all. It was also too expensive given its quality. If I was to ever go back it would be to try the pizza.

Awesome Indian takeout! Can't really comment on the atmosphere because my husband picked up our dinner, but from what he said, it's more of a takeout place. We had the chicken tikka masala, the curry chicken and naan. Everything was so good, I can't wait to order from here again!
This is good place! Food is fresh and taste so good! Professional waiter consider every need you probably have! Defiantly recommend!

While I cannot say that any of the cupcakes at *Ndulge are groundbreaking in their preparation, flavor pairings, or presentation, there are a few factors that make this shop deserving of praise. 1. The hours of operation are impressive for a purveyor of baked goods. I love that I can have a few beers at Lucky's and roll over to *Ndulge around 9 and snag a cupcake to enjoy at home. I do not expect a bakery to be open late under any circumstances so this is a nice perk. 2. The employees are always friendly, effervescent, and greet you promptly. They describe their products well and maintain a pleasant demeanor. I will always give my money to businesses that provide great service. 3. The dining space is kept clean at all times. Nary a crumb to be seen. Can I, and my fellow baked good aficionados make cupcakes of equal or better quality at home? Yes. But I am a graduate student so I am lazy and usually fatigued. Sugary treats and stellar service from *Ndulge brighten my week.

Absolutely love this place. The food is delicious and affordable. It just like having a home cook meal by your grandmother. I would recommend this place to everyone. Also, the restaurant is family owned and the staff are super nice.

Its actually a Turkish joint not Greek like Yelp says in the description. The last time I had a Dooner Kabob was in Germany in Cologne & Berlin. Its a common fast food in Eastern Europe where you have large Turkish populations. Its like what a Burger joint is here in USA, you see Dooner joints on every corner as a fast food option. I had the Dooner Mina which was very good with Lamb, vegetables, and tzaziki sauce. Very light healthy not heavy and greasy. The chips (fries) were very good & seasoned well! Plus they got beers there you can choose from. The staff was very friendly and quick in service. Overall a must if you in St Pete and want a quick more healthy light option for a sandwich. All served on Naan bread not pita, big differance. Naan holds better as a sandwich. Also you have free WIFI a big plus!!
Singha Song Thai has a great new location near Tulane. The food is great and I had very good service. Best Thai in the city!
The food and service was wonderful. The pad thai was just the right amount of spices . Chicken rice and a spring roll come wirh your lunch. Will be back the next time I am in town.

Great Pakistani food. Delicious and simple. Fair price. Highly recommend going on Saturday or Sunday for "Halwa Puri" lunch. This includes famous fried bread, chickpeas (chana masala) and potatoes with sweet halwa. You won't regret. The owner and his wife work tirelessly to make sure you are happy. At the end, if you like, try mango lassi made fresh.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: I love love this place ! Always delicious and I haven't had such a great Indo-Pakistaní food in years !! The owner and his staff are so sweet !

I love the concept, but having recently visited Berlin, it just misses the mark when it comes to authenticity. I want that variety of sauces in my doner. That's the key that was missing. That's just me being picky though. If I lived in the area, I'd probably return pretty frequently. However, it's not worth a drive from Tampa.

Very good Thai food provided by the same people who run Thips. I went with my family of 5 and every dish was excellent. It is a bit small and can be a bit cramped when full, but the food makes up for it.
Best Thai food in the area Mitt is an excellent sushi and sashimi chef family owned and operated bathrooms are clean and nice you must try the Thai Chi tea it's to die for

Land of Smile is my favorite Thai restaurant in the St. Louis area. I've tried them all, and keep coming back, even though I live much closer to a couple other highly rated Thai places. I have two friends who grew up in Thailand, and they both prefer Land of Smile for the quality and authenticity of the food. The food is great, the service is great, and the price is very reasonable.

It's been all amazing.. My food was beyond great, everything was done to perfection. I have had my fair share of Indian in the last few months.wonderful atmosphere with attentive and personal staff!! Food is delectable

If you have had authentic Thai food in Thailand (like we have), you will be sorely disappointed. Even I can make better Thai food. We found the Pad Siew and Pad Thai to be terrible. Not even close to authentic and even other Thai places do it better. The Chicken Satay wasn't too bad.
Awesome Happy Hour with great service. Haven't tried the regular dinner so I can't give it 5 stars yet but I have a good feeling it's coming!

This place is cheap cheap cheap and surprisingly GOOD! I followed the suggestion of past reviewers and got the chicken shawerma with lentil rice pilaf...it was awesome. The chicken shawerma was very curry-ish and was all white meat which was nice. It easily was enough for two meals. The gyro meat was also really good although I'll say the biggest dissapointment I had was the tahini sauce (tasted like pure sour cream) and the hummus (yuck). Please Zayna's...go to Costco and just buy their big jars of hummus because what you serve isn't very edible. $1.00 Baklava...WIN

Glad to see they got a bigger venue, which is spacious and usually clean. It's a casual dining place and a family setting restaurant. Maybe because I'm Vietnamese but i find myself going here when in need of comfort food. The pho is good and so are the fried egg rolls, banh uot, fresh spring rolls, bun thit nuong cha gio, and pork chop rice dish with egg (my favorite here). They also have bubble tea slushies and taro is my favorite. Prices have sadly risen over the years but it's not too terribly high yet. Service is decent and there's not usually a wait. If you never had Vietnamese food before, this place is legit :)

Somebody else said that this place doesn't feel like St. Louis at all and I agree. It has a very laid back Northern California feel to it. Excellent Mediterranean food, many delicious vegetarian options, friendly but descrete servers. Beautiful space with gorgeous light in the lunchroom around noon. Truly a treat. The only reason I am giving it four stars and not five is that we had to wait quite a bit for our food because the kitchen got too busy. We weren't in a hurry so it was ok but it could be an issue if you are trying to grab lunch on your lunchbreak. There is a separate dinner space upstairs that is even more beautifully designed: cork floors AND chairs. Very tasteful and simply stunning! The owners are really cute! Support them!!!

I can't believe I haven't made a point to review Remedy yet! I come here on a fairly regular basis and don't see that changing any time soon. When I first moved to Edmonton a year and a half ago, I was told by countless people that I "needed" to try the chai at Remedy. Once I finally made a point to check it out, I completely understood the enthusiasm. It's absolutely fantastic. I especially enjoy the Kashmiri chai which is flavoured with pistachios and rose petals. Divine! Plus it's decaf so you don't need to worry about grabbing one before bed. As for the food, I find Remedy to be hit or miss. You can order the same dish two days in a row and end up eating something that tastes completely different. Sometimes it's fantastic and sometimes it's nothing particularly special. It's never been very bad though. I do love how vegan/vegetarian friendly the menu is. I tend to order the vegan butter chicken whenever I go here for food. Yummy! My biggest issue is how slow the service can be. I honestly don't really blame the staff for this one. I don't know how the managers can justify having one person on the counter on a Friday night. It's ALWAYS busy at Remedy so this shouldn't be a surprise. Don't go here if you're in a hurry at all.

I ate here over this past weekend. First impression: very trendy and decor is on point. Loved the aesthetic. You can see into the kitchen as they make your food. There is also a bar if you want to grab a quick bite alone. The food: I got the filet mignon pho. Sooo good. The meat is marinated and super tender. The broth is really flavored and the size is a large portion. I also had the grilled shrimp spring rolls which I loved. I definitely recommend getting the grilled shrimp over the traditional fresh shrimp. I've never had grilled shrimp in my spring rolls before but I wish I could find it back in Houston now that I've tried these. The waitress that was working was attentive and sweet as was the rest of the staff. Coming from Houston I'm definitely picky about my pho and know quality when I taste it. I'll be back here next time in NO for my pho fix.

I came here randomly after looking for a place for a quick drink. My boyfriend and I were happily surprised with their drink menu as it looked extensive and delicious! We wanted something refreshing since it was a hot day and settled for the iced lemonade and limeade. Both were made with real lemons/limes and super refreshing! I personally preferred the limeade better =) I'm interested in trying their food options as they sound delicious - they have a selection of curry bowls, vietnamese pho noodle bowls, and asian-style appetizers.

I was really looking forward to trying this place but didn't love their gyros. I appreciated the fact that they griddled their pita but I found several issues with the sandwich overall: 1. Their interpretation of tzatziki was a bit on the bland side and appeared devoid of cucumber...a signature component of a good tzatziki. Also, they went a bit light on the sauce. 2. The meat was carved from a spit (big plus!) but was one of the off-brands that come out of the Chicago restaurant supply houses. If you're charging eight bucks for a gyros it should damn well be Kronos or Olympia supplying your cones. Also, the slices of meat would have benefitted from having spent a little more time on the cone or run over the flat top to give them the sear that really brings out the flavors. 3. Red onions instead of white seemed a little out of place. Service was good. Folks, there really are some good places to get gyros in the STL but unfortunately this doesn't turn out to be among the best.

Great food and Great People We were passing by from Lansdale area and tried this restaurant. This place is hidden gem. They great menu and buffet items. You must try their Mix Veg Soup, Kadai chicken, Mix Veg Pakoda, Rava Halwa. We met owner and chef- they were great and really nice. We will definitely come back and recommend this place to our friends.

This place is amazing! The flavors are amazing and it's perfect for a cold, winters night. We had chicken xacuti and tiki marsla- both were so delicious. The bread is perfect for dipping. The service is attentive and friendly. Perfect neighborhood spot. We will be back!

I come here often out of desperation for some Asian food but if you can, I suggest you go to Noodle City or Pattaya. Don't Togo. You'll get more dining in. Food is overpriced and check the bill often before paying. Don't buy the drinks unless it's Thai tea. You'll just be paying a lot for disappointment. Chow fun dishes are no fun. Pho is decent. Pad Thai is eh. Service is nice by the student workers but not from the owner.

The location of this establishment is the best in the area. And as any realtor will tell you -"you can change the house but you can't change the location". This is true of Sam's. The food is sub-par and the staff is not at all accommodating or attentive. They know they have the best location with a steady stream of customers..so they care very little if they retain YOUR business.. I gave it 2 stars strictly because the location is beyond equal in the area..grab a beer.. But for food cross the street and enjoy good food and a family that appreciates your business.

Came here today with some friends to get lunch and was not disappointed! From the start the servers were very attentive and our drink orders were taken right away. I had the P4 and it was delicious, the meat was very tender and the broth was very flavorful! The egg rolls were also super delicious! The entire staff was super friendly and even though it got fairly busy they made sure to come back and check on us to make sure everything was still going well. Definitely somewhere we would all gladly come back to!!! A big plus goes to the manager Dan who was super helpful and knowledgable about the menu because my friend had some severe allergies and she was able to enjoy her food 100% worry free!

This was my first time here since having moved to the city. The dining room seats about 40 , there also an outdoor patio. We say in the dining room, which has a more intimate feel. The weight staff was attentive, and polite making sure we were taken care of, but, not overbearing in any way. The food was AMAZING, I had the shrimp appetizer, half portion of gnocchi, and chicken. I don't know how, but we're made room for dessert afterwards. Overall I had a great time there and rang enjoyed the food and staff. GO THERE NOW!!!!

I stopped in for lunch with a friend, and was greeted with the aromatic waft of delicious Thai food, a friendly welcome and quick seating. The restaurant was clean, well lit, and quiet for a weekday meal. We ordered Crispy Spring Rolls to share, two orders of the lemon grass soup, a Pad See Ew and a Panaeng Curry. The spring rolls and soups came quickly, and the rolls were beautifully golden and crispy and the soups fragrant and tangy with just the right amount of lemon grass and lime. My order of pad see ew was appropriately sweet and garlic savory, the curry spicy with crisp carrots, string beans and peppers. Overall, service was good and the food delicious. Would definitely dine at Jasmine Rice again.

The food aims to please everyone. The menu is more of an Asian inspired than a true Vietnamese menu. There was also Chinese, Singaporean and Korean (ie kimchi) inspired items. The pho lacked many of the ingredients I find at other restaurants such as tripe or tendon. I was not that hungry so I ordered a cup size wonton. The wonton consisted of pork and some water chestnut. It tasted okay. I did try a couple pieces of spring roll. The filling was nicely seasoned. However, I prefer the rice flour wrapper (the traditional way of making Vietnamese spring rolls) over the wheat flour/wonton wrappers. Service was good. There was an automatic 18% gratuity as we were a large group.

No complaints, praise for the staff, draft beer selection and hummus. Live acoustic music on Tue and Wed nights was nice. Jesse and Will get high marks for excellent bar service and welcoming demeanor. You had me at Stone IPA on tap... Thank you!

A weekly favorite for my wife and I, and it is very easy on the wallet! Friendly staff. I have eaten at many Indian restuarants, and this is one of my favorites. The vegetarian options are great, including Kadai Paneer, Shabnam Curry, and Mutter Paneer.

We were disappointed when we went last weekend. At the old location the place was so great. This was our first time at the new location for dinner. We had only had drinks at the Gay St. location before. We had a reservation made weeks in advance, but waited for over half an hour for our table. Then when we were finally seated, the service was not good. Drinks took a while, and the entrees took forever. Good thing the group had a lot to catch up on. And when trying to order, they were out of items that were regulars on the menu. It seemed everywhere we turned we were met with things being sold out - mussels, wine, entrees. The food was good. Just the overall experience tarnished our impression.
The gyro is fantastic! Kabob (chicken) looked great, but brother in law would let me try!

So yummy and really cool atmosphere. They have genuine home made grapeleaves and hookahs! The hummus is really delicious... I find in many restaurants it is too salty, but this was perfect. The service was fantastic, but it wasn;t very busy... so I don't know about on a crazy night because the location would lead one to believe it gets hectic in there! I really cannot wait to come back and try their kufta wraps they looked huge... Way more than a single serving! Very cozy environment.... Wine selection seems unique. This would be perfect for date night.

Best Greek food in town. Quik and easy to grab and go. I have had the spicy bacon avacado and it is always dripping with goodness. I am so happy this place is right down the street from where we live. My hubby gets the Philly and that has so much filling in the sandwhich that its hard to keep from getting all over. We love this place. I have had the hummis and pita on the side which was a great choice over chips. The backlava was the only thing I was not a huge fan of but it could have just been a bad batch. We have made this our special lunch run many times. :)
Personal-size murgh makhani pizza for $5. Get it! The drinks are an acquired taste. Great, unique lunch spot on Girard.
Very average Indian fare - if you've been to Artesia or the Bay Area, you know this is ridiculous. It earns one star for still being an accessible Indian food option for students

grilled pork: not bad, not really good. would be amazing if it were half the cost. no need to ask for extra carrots. ordered spicy, but wasn't spicy at all. no more free drinks with sandwich. nice staff.

This review is more for the service than the food since I never got to try any. I went Sunday, July 23 at 9:30. When I got to the cashier and ordered, he said there was no white meat. I couldn't believe a chicken place would run out of chicken. I really think they just wanted to serve what was already cooked even though they were open until 11:00. The guy who waited on us seemed like a good kid, but it would have been nice for the manager, who stood in back talking and giggling with her friend, to come talk to us. She just shouted, "I got ribs!" from the back. We left unimpressed.
Outstanding. Great food. Fast service. Warm friendly staff. Tons of meat on the sandwich. Fresh sides. Hard to find good fast Greek god, but this place knocks it out of the park.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I love the food here. And the owner... he is so friendly. It is a fantastic experience just being here.
The pho was very tasty, service was fast and friendly. Most delicious was the fresh-squeezed lemonade.
This place is sooooooooo amazing!!! Highly recommended!! The food is very authentic, get the cauiflower.....

I've been here for brunch and dinner. The brunch was good but over priced. We also had horrendous service. The table next to us had to tell the waiters on 3 separate occasions not to bring the dishes out all at once because the table was too small. We had the same issue and it seemed like we were also forgotten about. After being finished eating for 15 minutes we called over the waiter so I could hand them my card to pay. I may go back for brunch at some point but why bother when their dinner is amazing? We had an excellent server that provided phenomenal recommendations and ensured our glasses were always filled. We started with the Croquettes and they were perfectly crispy on the outside. The inside was a little too runny for me. The stuffed grape leaves were beautifully presented and I loved how the apricot balanced out the bitterness of the grape leave. The Baked Cheese was one of my favorite dishes of the night. It comes out on a cast iron skillet sizzling hot. It's ricotta and mozzarella based and has a hint of sweetness to it. We moved onto roasted cauliflower which was nicely cooked. The coriander cashew butter was perfect for dipping. The Berbere carrots had a nice hint of the berbere seasoning coming through and didn't overwhelm the dish. I couldn't stop sopping up the sauce with flatbread for Peri-Peri shrimp. The harissa provided a nice heat to the sauce. The Octopus Escabeche was SO tender. We also had the Lamb Ribs which fell off the bone. The pickled radishes were a nice edition to cut the fat. The main courses were everyone's favorite. The Dry Rub Chicken fell off the bone and had excellent seasoning. We couldn't get enough of the muhumara sauce (walnut and pepper based) to dip the chicken in. My favorite of the main course was the Date Braised Lamb Shank which was beautifully presented surround by vegetables. The meat fell of the bone and had a deliciously crispy outside. We ended with dessert. I could have done without the Chocolate Tahini Cake. The cake was a little dry. It's pretty difficult to get the right balance of ingredients for chocolate cake since it has more ingredients than most cakes that dry it out. I had a bite of the shredded wheat and it had a filling similar to baklava that was delicious. My fiance had the Sundae and he devoured it even after he claimed he was full. I highly recommend dinner at Spice Finch but would skip brunch until they work out the kinks of opening a new restaurant.

Been to a lot of Vietnamese places. I didn't really like this one to much. I felt the flavoring was a bit on the bland side. The portions are generous and the service was great. Food just didn't have that wow factor for me. I was disappointed. Would not repeat.
In the land of chain restaurants, Pho 36 is a hidden gem in Avon. We've been there many times, and have always had good food and even better service. I will return time and time again.
In town for work and found this on yelp. Came in during lunch and had one of their beef soups, it was good. Had a grilled pork sandwich to go, also yummy. I plan to return before I leave the area.

This place needs a lot of attention!! The man at front desk needs to learn how to treat customers! Upon my visit, I checked the buffet and while I was at door to call my other friends the front desk guy asked us to go and check the food in New Delhi restaurant next door!! I was surprised as hell we often dine in there and love the food but this guy made the night , A nightmare! Very disappointed and couldn't understand why was he referring us to the other restaurant?!!

Everything about this restaurant was great! It was small and quiet which is great for a relaxing dinner. It is BYOB and the atmosphere was romantic with candles. Our waiter was awesome, I think his name was Thomas and the owner came out to our table. He thanked us for coming out on a Monday night and gave us a complimentary dessert. Everything was amazing, and they were so nice! We go the antipasto appetizer, the lasagna, and the gnocchi. Definitely a great experience and I would love to go back!

Just recently visited this place after driving by it many times since it is right around the corner from our house. It is a small quaint coffee/sandwich shop near the graduate hospital area. My friend and I had the chicken panini which had a great taste. We were actually working on our laptops from the shop since they had the free wireless internet. The restaurant was clean and inviting. The only issue we had is when the 2nd shift worker came onto his shift. He seemed dis-interested in what the guest preference were as to music and air conditioning. I understand it isn't always our choice but he turned off the air ( which made it incredibly hot) in the restaurant and then turned up the music which made it entirely too difficult to concentrate on my work I was performing on my laptop. I would definitely give this place another try but if it is steaming hot and loud again at 2p.m. in the afternoon I would have to give it up.

Best Thai we have ever had anywhere. The food is unbelievably delicious and the presentation is lovely. The Panaeng curry chicken is to die for... simply amazing. This GEM deserves your business. Give it a try!!
Great spot! Drinks and food are awesome! Staff is kind and attentive. You have to try the Les Leches and the key lime pie ad desserts!

Delicious!!! Went there twice and is in love with the food especially the beef kababs, fetteh, and fresh warm pitas! Food the second time was a bit dry, but the flavor and spices still tasted the same. Love how they take late reservations up until 11:30pm! Can't wait to try breakfast where many are raving about the rose pistachio cruellers. Will definitely eat back!
The combination sandwich is great. I highly recommend Phamous Cafe for a quick lunch.

Relative to other ethiopian places in the area (none), unparalleled. Still, doesn't coast- great food. The service was nice, and helpful. I experienced my first Ethiopian food in a place with a large Ethiopian community (israel), and this doesn't compare. But I'd go back again!

The food was delicious and the service was excellent. I had the spinach gnocchi as an appetizer, which was amazing, and the stewed rabbit as a main. The rabbit was so tender no fork was required. I can't give it 5 stars because the tables were so tight it was uncomfortable. I had a corner table and it required gymnastics to sit down and once the other tables were full, it was quite difficult to get out.
Small but very comfy place, you won't regret. Food is delicious, and so is the hookah! I definitely recommend!

My family and I came here for a nice lunch before we headed back home. There are 5 of us here. I'm the only one who doesn't speak Spanish at our table and the waitress refused to speak English to me. She knew how because she was speaking it with the other waitress. The manager just sits at the bar and stares at people. We have been here almost 2 hours and have not received our food. The waitress is being very rude to my in laws and myself. So we will not be coming back here. I have never been in such a hateful restaurant.

This place was wonderful and family friendly. We came on Friday for happy hour and really got to try a wide selection of food. From appetizers, to entrees (lamb shank), and dessert everything was spot on. Happy hour wine by the glass was great too.
Love this place. We order take-out from here all the time and it's always delicious! Our favorites are the chicken korma and the vegetable samosas.

We arrived in town at that least fortunate time of day - when some restaurants close up between lunch and dinner. We had intended to go to a different Indian restaurant closer to The Loop (if that is what it is called) but it was closed. However, we had cultivated a serious yen for Indian food - and living in Rolla, where there are literally hundreds (if not thousands) of Indian students, but not a single Indian *restaurant,* we needed a back-up plan. We pulled up yelp as we stood outside in the freezing cold (this was back in February 2015) and found this place. We walked in that direction - it was not the most scenic of routes, but Missouri in winter is not that picturesque to begin with. We ended up ordering I think we got chicken Makhani, lamb palak and a biriani. And shared a mango lassi too - we had worked up an appetite both while deciding what to do and walking over! The food was really excellent - the meat was all very tender, and the spices were spot-on. I would definitely eat here again, although it seems like they mostly do take-out: the restaurant has maybe 4 tables, and is in a weird parking lot they share with a barbershop full of unfriendly-looking youths. The owner, like everyone has said, was personable and attentive - although I have NEVER had a server at a restaurant - owner or not - demand that we "finish that last bit" of a dish. It was just weird to be scolded like a child because we were full. He also insisted that we write a yelp review for the place - I guess it worked in the end, but again was just kind of weird for an owner to say. But, when the food is really good, one can overlook a lot. Give it a try!
Absolutely one of my favorite places to eat! The atmosphere is so inviting and friendly! The sushi is amazing!

Went there last eve with a friend...hadn't been to Dosa Chaat House since they renovated, always thought the food was top-notch, but the ambiance left something to be desired...WELL, that is all corrected now...everything we had was amazing, the vegetable cutlets (appetizer), the chicken 65, just thinking of it makes me sorta drool, the paper dosa, oh yum, and the uthappam, we ordered way too much since the portions are generous but once we started eating we wanted to taste everything. Our waiter was knowledgeable & very pleasant, he gave us great suggestions & warned us that we were over-ordering... btw, my friend is what i call white bread, not terribly adventurous when it comes to food, and she was scarfing the food in as fast as she could...she loved it... It's byob, and they give you wind glasses as needed. I'm trying to decide what I'll try next time I go...

First time here and my guy really enjoyed The Trio although it was supposed to come with ribs, chicken and pulled pork (he had two pieces of chicken and no pulled pork). The sauces are really tasty also, especially the pineapple rum. I had the chicken Caesar salad which had a huge piece of chicken. I won't get this again - chicken was dry, salad dressing pre-packaged; Nothing special. But I will try the chicken wrap and soup next time. It looked really good. The establishment is clean, the staff is friendly, and the manager checked in with us after we finished our dinner. And the table is bussed for you! If looking for an inexpensive lunch or dinner, give the store in Seminole Town Center a chance. I know we'll be back.
Food was amazingly good. Fresh, wonderfully flavored . Best Indian cuisine I've had in a long, long time. Worth the drive!!

First time at the new location. First time was unsatisfactory. It got worse. The only plus? .. I got to write chalk on the wall in the bathroom. The hookah was so weak it felt like I was inhaling air. The guy never ever came around to change our coal and the service in general was very poor. I ordered hookah for 5 people but they only gave me four. When I asked for another tip, a clerk gave me a bit of an attitude before giving me one. The pink grapefruit had no flavor; overall I felt like this was a waste of money. I was excited for a hookah bar in west county but I think it's back to Nara downtown for me. I will never come back again.

I really wanted to love this place, alas I can't do it. I ordered chicken biryani with medium spice. There was no spice even leading up to that level. I would say it was mild at best. The biryani itself tasted very good, but I was so disappointed in the lack of spice. The chicken was very tender and moist. I feel like they could have done a much better job of layering flavors. The vegetable samosas were good, but not the best. I've had better.
This place is ok. I'd never had Pho before so that through me off a bit, and I had to add quite a bit of sauces to spice it up, but not bad.

Momo's is an amazing restaurant that is top notch in both decor and in food. Doing both right is a rare feat, and really there is nothing lacking in this establishment. The staff is very friendly and is outgoing, and they really make you feel at home here. The different styles of seating is fun, as is picking from the menu due to all of the choices. The mezes [tapas] here are fantastic! I love Momo's. I have loved everything that I have tried here, The dolmades are superb, and anyone who has never had them before should try them here. I've had a gyro here, and it was just as great as anywhere else. That fact plus with this place is option of getting the mezes and the decor makes it a great time. Now, there are things on the menu that I am not so sure are Greek, such as pasta, but the vast majority seems to hold true to the food my old Greek friend often ate. I've been here a bunch of times, and have never had a bad experience.
It's good. Really nice clean inside and it was packed inside I loved that you could see the cooking area. The food was really good to

I have eaten here at least a dozen times in the past 4 years. Their food is delicious, fresh, and perfectly spiced. The service is warm and attentive. My kids often choose to go here for their birthday dinner. It looks very unassuming, being in a strip mall, but the food is so worth it! My favorite Thai in Chester County!
The service was good and the kebabs were nice. I did like the atmosphere because it was a bit exotic. Off the beaten path for some good food. Salad was nice too.

We went for an anniversary dinner on a Thursday night. We were happy that the restaurant was full and just loud enough that we could have our own conversation without others being able to eavesdrop despite the small dining room. The service was attentive, which is a huge factor in the overall enjoyment of a meal out. The wait staff was personal and informative. We ordered two of the special small plates, sardines and calamari with gnocchi. The sardines had a bit of the flavor of the gas grill, but the calarmari was unbelievable as were our other dishes. The sausage was excellent with a lot of flavor and a huge portion. The pasta was cooked to perfection and the pesto had just the right amount of texture. We also loved out whole fish. Delicious! While we are not generally dessert eaters, the waiter brought over some zeppolis on the house. They were hot, vanilla flavored and delicisous. As a matter of fact, all of our food was piping hot, which is another key factor to an excellent meal. One cannot get food like this anywhere else in South Jersey. Zeppoli is a treasure!

I love love love Laziza. We come here often, and love how friendly the owners and workers are, and the food. They have delicious, fresh, food for good prices. I usually get the "steak sandwich" which consists of steak, fries or rice, veggies, and garlic toast. my mom gets the spaghetti and steak (I forget the exact name), which also comes with garlic toast. We've also tried their shrimp basket, hummus, pizza, lasagne, cheese burger, chicken burger, and other dishes. Everything tastes so delicious, and fresh, with the exception of their pizza. Its a hit or miss. My mom ordered it once, and it was absolutely delicious. Nice crust, and nice amount of cheese and toppings. However, the second time around when I ordered, the pizza was so soggy we couldn't eat it. We threw out the entire thing. Not sure what they did to make it soggy... but oh well. The chicken burger I once ordered was also very very soggy. I had to eat the piece of chicken and throw the rest away. I should also mention the portion sizes are HUGE. You won't feel like you've been ripped off. I would definitely recommend trying this place out if you're looking for some yummy food, and a great place to socialize with your buddies/family/whoever.

I came for their Sunday buffet for the first time for brunch. Brian, the owner was so gracious and attentive to our large group! We were a party of 8 with a few vegans included. Brian and the rest of the employees at Tandoor went out of their way to provide more vegan options for our group. The food is absolutely delicious!! I really had to resist the urge to make my 3rd trip up to the buffet. We will be back again and again!

Hi To all the Middle Eastern food lovers . We have visited Naf Naf in KofP Probably 7 times . Chris has always taken good care of us and remembering who we were from every visit was such a surprise We don't live close by so we don't get there often (Hope they open in the Princeton area sometime soon ) The MOST Delicious Everything on the menu Authentic, Cooked From scratch at the location Clean Very professional We have visited Israel and if I would close my eyes and eat Naf Naf I would think I was in The Middle East On leaving our visit today we spoke with Stephan another very impressive employee who gave us a history lesson about Naf Naf I could go on But you all have to visit Naf Naf to ENJOY a delicious meal and pleasant environment

The only point being taken off is for the decor which honestly did not impact our experience. It was a mix of country America decor meets Thai. That said... the food was excellent. As you will see from the pictures I will attach, we had eaten about a third before thinking of even taking a picture. Everything we ate was really good and the service was just fine. It wasn't overpriced and it was a nice walking distance from the moonrise hotel. Overall impressed and will be back.

We were in the mood for good thai food and picked this place. Load and behold, their food was delish. I will definitely be baxk for some pork steam dumplings. I ate a salad with peanut sauce, steamed pork dumplings, chicken pad thai for $8 bucks. Service was excellent.

I first met Rabia and Muhammad at a volunteer event where they exclusively catered over 150 members of the Camden, NJ community free of charge as part of a Christmas Celebration. Needless to say, you could taste their passion in their food. Zaika continues to exceed expectations in quality, consistency, and price. If you are in the area, go here not only for delicious food but for the great People as well.

I have been here many many times and i have never been disappointed!!! Food is always fresh made to order with good quality customer service. Zekos is located on Busch blvd directly across from Busch Gardens. Zekos opens early and stays open late. Prices a good with weekly specials which i highly recommend you ask before you order. You will be surprised by the great deals. I highly recommend you try there wings(OMG). They come in different flavors but i always get the mild wings. There are a good size not to small and to big. And also please get the steak fries to go along with the wings!!! You will not be disappointed

I haven't eaten heat in a few years. I was craving Ethiopian and Zagol is the only game in town. I ordered Doro Wat and asked if I could have a thigh instead of the leg. The server/cook said that they had no thighs. Why advertise the choice then. I asked if it was possible to get an extra leg. She made the comment "for the same price?" Of course not, I would pay for the extra leg. She made some lame ass comment about the option not being available on their Point of Sale system. I also asked for a side order of Gomen (collard greens). I also asked for a normal iced tea. She brought me my iced tea and it ended up being the Ethiopian sliced ice tea. She clearly heard what I said but was too lazy to comply From the time I ordered the food, it came out in half an hour. There was one small chicken leg and one egg exactly, 6 small pieces of Injera and the side order of Gomen. The chicken was good and spicy with Berbere flavor. However no Ethiopian cheese as expected. The colllard greens had no flavor and were really bland. I mixed the greens with the sauce from the Doro Wat. I'm glad I asked for the greens as the portions are skimpy compared to bigger portions that other Ethiopian restaurants I've eaten at in Washington DC (which has a high population of Ethiopians), the Bay Area and SoCal. I finished my meal and she brought out my bill. To my surprise, she charged me for 2 entrees. The Doro Wat and then the Gomen as a veggie entree. A meal which would normally cost me $18 at the most cost me $28 here. I left a tip which brought the total to $34 for an Ethiopian lunch. This restaurants business practices is short of highway robbery. I will never be a patron of this restaurant again. Although the flavor of some of the food was good, I would skip coming here an go to a Middle Eastern Restaurant instead. This restaurant is a bad representation of a welcoming Ethiopian restaurant. By the sheer emptiness of the Restaurant, I was the only customer, this place should be going out of business soon

After a long hiatus from my regular dining at Nadia, I returned! Puffed up with courage, I ordered my standard Pad Kee Mao with tofu, later digesting with ease and no sign of illness. I hereby retract my 2-star rating and issue a 4-star rating. I can afford a personal favorite the space for an occasional slip-up, right? :) Especially since Nadia is STILL the best Thai place in the area code-- despite the recent advent of a couple contenders. No contest.

Can't get enough of this place. A little on the pricey side; however, the food is 110% worth it. We have yet to eat in here but when we're looking for take-out it's by far and away our first choice. We live in Chalfont but have no problem making the 15/20 minute drive to get some of the best Thai in the area. Our favs are the Pad Thai, Pad See You and you have to try the Drunken Noodles.

Veggie rolls are great!! I was impressed by the overall ambience here, i thought the decor was tasteful and creative. Server was very friendly and the food was great. I had the Salmon with apricot sauce, a combo i had not had before and I loved it. very yummy! I'd definitely go back if i lived in the area.

I got peanut sauce beef. Awesome! I am not a fan of Asian food but always loved Thai. Does not disappoint. Bad reviews are wrong except carpet could be replaced. Attentive servers. Ornate silver covered cups for rice. Feel like a Queen.

I was so pleasantly surprised at my first visit to this authentic Greek restaurant. A casual and clean atmosphere set the stage. Enter the most amazing Greek salad with chicken on top! Delicious dressing, heirloom tomatoes, and crunchy chickpeas make this salad a reason to return! Friendly staff and owners are a bonus. Give it a try! You won't be disappointed.

Fun place for dinner with friends. The ambience is very nice, creative bartender, friendly staff and fantastic Vietnamese food. Pork belly pops are wonderful. We also loved the pho with lemon grass broth and bun. Great value for the price too. Next time we're in Reno, will definitely be back.
The food is consistently good. My husband and I order delivery from here very often. They are one of the only places that actually deliver! It's priced decently too

Bowls are great! Flavorful and spicyyyy sauces! I don't eat pita but I will here! Warm and fresh! Mainly writing this review to recognize Tanisha for being so friendly! It seems so hard to find good customer service anymore when you realize a simple "how is your day" catches you off guard!

On a breezy autumn evening of enjoying outdoor music & pumpkin beers at Philly's Blocktober Fest, I ordered the Jamaican Jerk chicken platter and a chicken patty. The order was incorrect, so not a great sign from the start. I was given a vegatable patty. The frozen vegetables inside the patty were bland and had an awkward sweetness to them. I had been craving the savory curry of the chicken patty, but it was not meant to be. The Jamaica Jerk platter was atomic. It was so spicy that you could hardly distinguish any flavor. The rice, beans, and lettuce were standard. All in all, I was not impressed.

Makes us sad. My husband and I visited Nashville for the evening and came across this place. The reviews sounded wonderful. Visited the website and tried to make a reservation but said nothing was available until after the New Year. Tried calling with no answer and NO answering machine/voicemail available, "the mailbox is full. Please hang up", I heard . Finally, husband found a closed message on Facebook. It would have been more effective if they had let guests know on their website, at the very least. Hope no one else has to go through this for dinner before they are back in action. Maybe next time.

More like.. chicken tender spot. Nothing that special about it. A little disappointed though -because it's chicken tender. Not chicken wing. Not that cheap. Not that expensive. Street parking. Friendly staff. Fall short of my expectation. I thought it's wings.
Very good Indian food. Service was good and the food was amazing, especially the garlic naan. Definitely recommend!
Excellent food, great prices. The French fry medley is some of the best fries I have ever had. The Mediterranean platter is big enough for two and has lots of delicious variety. Definitely recommend!

Our experience kind of mirrors that of Liz F. who reviewed on 8/21/11. The food and atmosphere were all relatively good. There was a Belly Dancer and hookahs were freely available and Customers appeared to enjoy them immensely. There is a flip side to our experience which strongly outweighs the positives listed above. First off, I had to ask the waiter 3 times for a fork because I don't enjoy eating with my hands. He told me that very few people asked for forks. Being that it was the weekend we were limited to the 7 course price fixed dinners at $25 per person. A Gentleman of Middle Eastern descent and his wife sat next to us and were immediately served enormous salads and flatbreads and automatically given forks (yes, forks and they didn't have to ask for them). The salads were not offered to anyone else. The real kicker is this: We paid for part of our bill using an "Eversave Coupon." When they presented us with the bill there was a gratuity on it for about 20%! Now I don't mind being hit up for a gratuity if the party is greater than 6 people, but for only 2 people this is highly unethical. IN THIS COUNTRY WE HAVE THE INALIENABLE RIGHT TO BE THE JUDGE OF OUR OWN GRATUITY, NOT THE OTHER WAY AROUND!!! (In most other countries there is no gratuity). Secondly, the wine my wife ordered was only $7 per glass of which she had 2. They charged us $8 per glass. The final insult was a charge for tiny glasses mint tea. They charged us $2 (x's 3) for tiny glasses of mint tea and it was listed on the menu as being part of the 7 course meal! I have been in Morocco and never have I been charged for mint tea. Where ever you go, mint tea is pushed on you as a sign of hospitality from the local pharmacy to rug shops and every place in between. Our final bill which included two $25 dollar price fixed dinners and 2 glasses of wine cost over $92.00. If you choose to eat at this place, Caveat Emptor! (let the buyer beware)! We will never return.

A few Saturday mornings ago, after walking around the city for a few hours in beautiful weather, my friend and I basically knocked the door down to eat here at exactly 11am. We were greeted cheerfully by the super nice woman working there and placed our orders for 2 platters- jerk chicken and chicken curry. Both were very tasty although not the amazingness that I expected. What was amazing though was the fresh juice- the orange/mango was the perfect combo....perfectly cut the thickness of straight up mango juice. Besides 2 teenagers snuggling up over a shared jerk platter, we were the only ones in the place and thus free to enjoy our meal to the sweet sweet sounds of reggae music on the radio and CNN on the television.

This place is AMAZING! Exactly what Reno needs broadening the palate. I went with a group of 8 people and all of us were enjoying every bite of our meal! Chef Justin is great, we must have ordered what seemed like everything from the menu and my fiance and I are already making plans to come back.
Great place to eat, excellent lunch specials.....Friday lamb shank special is AMAZING!!!! (I always take home two or three!!!) Every dish I have tried here has been good, well seasoned and delicious.

I do not recommend this place at all. The drinks are a little rich in a bad way, but there are worse problems than that. What earned this place the two stars is how incredibly terrible the food is. Ever heard of seasoning, people? Add a bit of spice once in a while. The food is inedibly bland. From what I could tell, they seemed pretty used to people handing back barely-touched plates of food, because the fellow who took it from me didn't even try that "Is there any way we can make it better or improve your experience?" damage control that most restaurants and coffee shops practice.

I would recommend Chicken Dum Biryani and Lamb Biryani .It comes with Raita and gravy. As my search for Biryani continues in Delware,this place scores better than most of them. Food taste is very nice.

I ordered take out here right before they were about to close and they were still happy to serve me. I had a $17 chicken tikka masala which was very well portioned but still overpriced in my opinion. The sauce was delicious and very tomatoey but chicken was extremely dry.

I adore this place! Service can be spotty but that's not what I come in for. I will tell you I've been several times and have had nothing but the pho so I can't review any other dishes. I can't rave enough about the pho. I always leave feeling like I'm going to burst! I always have to ask for extra live wedges but that's no deal breaker. Perhaps if I keep visiting, one day they'll recongnize my overwhelming need to limes :)
I am so happy to have a good sushi restaurant in this shopping center! We got takeout and mainly just sushi rolls. Everything was great. I'm sure this has become our new sushi spot.

Excellent food! Lamb chops were tender and tasty. The appetizer (Ashak) was seasoned perfectly and yummy! It's funny because they are right next door to another Afghan restaurant, which might be tough for patrons to choose between. It was for me lol........but I highly recommend this place. YUMMY!

What a lovely experience! They have sidewalk seating, great for enjoying a lovely night's weather and people watching. The menu was a fun blend of French specialties and Moroccan. I loved the escargot appetizer. Dinner was a seafood bouillabaisse and the lamb targine. Our server went above and beyond to make sure we had a unique, pleasant dining experience. As an added bonus, the cocktails were delicious - not too sticky sweet. Please take your special someone out for dinner here soon!

So first I want to start by saying, this is your typical sushi takeout restaurant. Beautifully decorated inside but rather small, definitely seeming like they cater towards more takeout orders. The sushi is your typical: fresh, tasty and definitely does not disappoint. But the reason I went for the 5 stars was the service. My friend and I ordered takeout off of yelp and when we arrived at the time it was supposed to be ready, the lady at the front apologized and said that the order had just been sent through to them a couple minutes ago. At first I was a little mad because we were picking it up during our break and we only had so much time. HOWEVER, the lady was very apologetic and put my order in right away and within 5 minutes she brought it out! That to me was extremely important because she wanted to make sure we were taken care off, so if anything it's a 5 star to me because the sushi was good and the service was even better.

Def a FALAFEL NAZI... - No Menus, No (set) Prices, No Common Sense... But Food is Delicious! I got volunteered to pay for my friend when he asked guy about the price, but at-least he was nice about it : ) tip: don't pull out your money before he calls the price...
First time here. We all tried something different. Very good atmosphere, good fresh food. The dinning area is very small. The service was awesome.

Love love love it here we are total regulars. I get the Novrattan Korma, great vegetarian options. Service is great. Food is always very tasty and plentiful, enough to take some home for the next day. The samosas are killer. Great delivery service too.

OP is my #1 Vietnamese restaurant! I don't have to drive all the way down to South Philly, and get stuck in traffic anymore. The food is excellent. The Vietnamese spring rolls and summer rolls is on point! It's always fresh when I get it! I would recommend their pho (it's simple and filling), because the broth is the best I have ever tasted. I also love their grilled pork. It's very tasteful. The shrimp is a decent size (it's not the small, cheap ones). If you enjoy spicy food I would recommend the Bun Bo Hue. This dish is delightful noodle dish with a little kick to it! I tried a lot if dishes and I am very satisfied, customer and NOTHING is disappointing to me. The service is wonderful, and the music is classy. It's a nice restaurant, and PLUS it's BYOB. :)

Great place food and service top notch we just moved to largo and couldn't find an India food But we did last night Great testing food and the young woman that took care of us was a real go getter Blonde hair Our go to place for good India food

I be eaten about for five times and always found the food to be one of the better Thai restaurants here. The last two times I've eaten here the food had been very mediocre. Something changed. They need to get back on track.

So I have to say that the location of this place isn't the best and the service, while, friendly, is not super attentive. BUT the food is super tasty! I get the vegetarian platter every time (although I do move meat) because I love it so much! It has a variety of different vegetable dishes, each with a unique seasoning....so good! I had one of the lamb dishes once and while very good, it was VERY spicy! Event so, the flavor was great. I will continue to dine here because the flavors and seasons are spot on!
Decent. I had the chicken salad and it was not skimpy by any means and it had a lot of chicken in it. I would not be jumping out of my seat to go back but I enjoyed my meal.
Amazing and authentic Lebanese food, highly recommend the baba ghannoush and manoushe for brunch.
Fresh food. Place looks clean and staff is friendly. Chicken is delicious with peanut sauce.

Walked in on a typical weekday afternoon, the place is reasonably clean with 4 customers already in it. Ordered the special pho, what I always order when I first go to a new pho place. The price was very reasonable, sub $10 for a large bowl of pho. The condiment choices were good, nice amount of basil, sprouts and chilli. Sate and other sauces were all present. The complimentary tea has a very unique flavour to it, I am not sure what it is but I did not enjoy it. The pho came fast, hot and fresh, a good thing. The toppings look good, the portion was generous but the broth was very dark. On first taste, the taste of soya sauce in the broth was overwhelming. During the whole meal, I just couldnt get over how overpowering the taste of soya sauce and how salty the broth was. I went there on the strength of the reviews here, it may be just a bad day for the chef but based on the bowl of pho I had, it only deserved a "Meh" rating.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: You're not going to get a better curry in Boise! The owners are attentive and caring, and you will feel part of the family.
