The food is cooked to order from scratch so please don't arrive in a rush! You can't rush perfection! I would highly recommend the lamb biriyani, absolutely divine! Also, the naan breads and made and cooked traditionally! Try one... You won't regret! Three years we have been in the area and the taj is our absolute favorite place to eat!! :)

This is the best Indian restaurant I've ever been to. Granted, I've only been to ones in the southeast US, but I was very impressed. Also, I left my Amex there for two days and they didn't go on a shopping spree, so they're decent people!!

12/05/10 what a tasty dinner. We had a cabbage salad which came with luscious spring rolls. Our thai basil had a wonderful fragrance with an abundance of fresh veggies. We picked this wide noodle dish, I can't remember the name,but the flavor was memorable. The hostess was even hospitable. The place is a little hole in the wall on Lancaster Ave in Ardmore, with authentic food.

I so wanted to love and rave about this place but unfortunately I can't. Service was great - friendly - attentive - and enthusiastic. The antipasto was creative and delicious as were the pasta small portions we shared (3 of them). The entrees however were way over salted. While they were tasty I felt as though I couldn't fully enjoy them or "get" the flavors as the sodium was really overwhelming. Ambience was nice but as others have noted very noisy. Not that it was uncomfortable but just be prepared. All in all I don't think I'd return. Nothing was so delicious that I feel like I have to rush back. I think it's more hype than quality taste.
Pho is pho. There was nothing different. But the staff were very friendly. The atmosphere is great and the neighborhood is nice too.

We saw this place on Guy Fieri's "Diners, Drive-ins, & Dives", so when we came to Nashville for a visit, we wanted to check it out. My husband ordered the Athenian chicken with rice and I ordered the Lamb pita with fries. The woman who took our orders was rushing us a bit upon ordering, which we thought was slightly rude as there was no one on line behind us and it was our first time there. She also spoke very quickly so when confirming our order, her "rice" sounded like "fries", so I asked her to repeat that it was in fact rice my husband was getting, to avoid any confusion. She seemed a little annoyed by that. Sorry! We sat down at a table and waited for our food. The girl that brought our meals was much more friendly. My husband loved his chicken but wished the lemon oil that came on top of it was warm. He devoured it. The Lamb in my pita was so fatty that I spent most of the time awkwardly pulling fat chunks out of my mouth. It was quite a turn off. My fries were very good though. If it were just a review for my food, I'd give it two stars, but my husband loved his so much, I gave it three. Don't think I'd go back.
Really good food and the best Naan we ever had. Go there all the time and the service and quality are always Consistent.

Great food. Awesome service. Went here one night after realizing my usual place was closed. The owner was super friendly and helpful even though it was close to closing for them too. The food was great too and there was plenty of it.

We were told the food would be done in 5 minutes. It's been over 20 minutes so far. We should have known better from the dozen people all waiting around and no one was leaving with food. I will update the review if we ever get our meals but don't tell people 5 minutes when the wait is 20 or 30 minutes. There's plenty of chinese places around here to choose from we chose this place because it looked nice. Big mistake. UPDATE: it took 27 minutes. Food isn't even cheap for two meals and 4 egg rolls (egg rolls were not included with the meals) it was $25. The rice portions were small too. We ran out of rice before we ran out of the food. The food was really good so I'm giving it 2 stars I'm just disappointed about the time and rice portion. If it's 30 minutes tell me so I can run errands and come back. There's actually a place across the street we will try next time since they did not look busy.

We went here because of the yelp reviews. But was disappointed. We had the fried wantons and chicken wings to start. Both were very good. I had the bbq pork soup - that was ok. My husband got the spicy beef. He couldn't eat it. Two big chunks of beef. I will say this was the first time we had Indonesian food. So we didn't really know what to get or to expect. But the reason why I am giving two stars is because of the staff. When they asked if we wanted a box and I replied no and that my husband didn't like it, the waiter just shrugged his shoulders. He said he thought my husband was Indonesian. I was kinda taken back by this response. Most restaurants would ask if you would like something else or take it off the bill. He just said you order you pay. I am not upset that we had to pay but more of how they went about it and the comments from the staff. i would want to make sure everyone to eat at my place was leaving happy. they seemed not to care if we enjoyed the food or had a nice time at their place. the only reason why they i even gave them was because of the chicken wing

I've eaten here a few times this year. It has become my favorite restaurant. The food is heavenly...always fresh and perfectly seasoned. The environment is authentic, warm and comfortable. And they play authentic middle eastern music which adds to the experience.
Great food. Friendly owners! We always get the tikka masala and garlic naan (typical beginner food) but it is absolutely delicious

Service great. Place is very LOUD and full off drunks. We showed up at 6:30 on a Sunday evening for dinner and everyone in the bar was wasted. Really wasted. Food was good. Great beer menu. A little over priced. I won't come back. It's not my style.

I was looking for something new in town. Something tasty and reasonable in a normal price range 20.00 or so per person. Voila, SEE magazine had a review of this restaurant. I was surprised to hear that it had also been selected for the Where to Eat in Canada review guide. The food is remarkable, of course the satay is delicious, the two soups we ordered, one a coconut, the other a seafood hot and sour were also very spicy and full of complex flavours, The green curry was superb as was the mango salad. Just thinking back on the meal makes me want to run over and pick up something to snack on. Highly recommended, a big yum in my books, the bill for four with two drinks each was just under 30 per person.

Incredibly cozy, wonderful decor, and that fantastic smell. The rosemary naan was great (not the best, but good), the lamb dishes were very tasty, and the desserts were fine. Only gripes is that the dishes were VERY small for the price and they gave us one bowl of rice to share between two people (definitely not enough). The finishing touch was adorable: little bags of a sample of Lindt chocolates (random but still cute). Don't ask for tea though, unless you know what Indian tea is. Other notes: bathrooms are very clean and nice. Cheap metered parking is across the street. BYOB!
Ok finally went here based on reviews. Soooo worth it. My son and I loved the pho! Alot for the price.

I finally got around to eating here after talking about doing so since they opened. I had never had Ethiopian food prior to this, and neither had my date, so we didn't know what to expect. The restaurant was empty aside from one large group and us. Service was friendly and helpful. We opted for two meat dishes, and one veggie dish. One of the meat dishes being a lamb dish, the other a beef "stew" dish, and the veggie dish of split yellow peas. Food took about 20 minutes to arrive, but from the sounds in the kitchen, it was made to order. The injera was totally different than anything else I've eaten, and I can only compare it to a mouse-pad, but in a good way. The entrees each had very distinct and full flavors. The vegetable "slaw" that they come with is a very nice addition to the spicy meats! This is a great place for a first or second date, as the food is "fun" and can break any tension that might be. Also would be fun with a large group! I look forward to going back and trying some of the other dishes out, as well as the beers and wines they offer.

Pros: Fairly good food, reasonable prices, and a moderately large menu. Cons: They RAN OUT of steamed rice, the service was slow, and I had to remind them to bring me part of my order. I gave Siam Thai a try while in Boise for work, and I am mostly glad I chose to eat there. The food was tasty and plentiful, the servers were very friendly, and the restaurant was clean and very busy. However, I was disappointed by a few things. To begin with, the menu had a LOT of dishes that are would be considered more Chinese or American-inspired Asian rather than "authentic Thai." The service was very slow (40 minutes from the time I sat down to the time I got my food), and the server forgot to bring my soup until I reminded her. And finally, I asked for steamed rice with my meal, but when it came, there was friend rice in it's place. I was told that they had "ran out" of steamed rice. For any Asian restaurant, running out of steamed rice is definitely breaking a cardinal rule. So, by all means, give Siam a try, but be wary.

My family had been many times prior and we recently hosted a family gathering in their private room space. The manager was very easy to work with, the service was great during the party (and after) and the food was delicious as always! Will always be our go to spot for Indian cuisine!
This place was amazing! I highly recommend it. It is a tiny hole in the wall place but the food is great. I had the tacos Honduras. I cant wait to go back.

Had a great meal really enjoyed the plantains (first time trying those out). I tried the beef patties and my wife had the oxtails. She enjoyed her order but I was pleasantly surprised. Will be coming back.

Absolutely delicious and cheap food. I came here for a birthday with a party of about 14 people. Service was noted to be excellent. There was so many known Thai places in the city, and I never heard about Vientiane Cafe so I was a bit skeptical to think that it would be any good. But I was proven wrong. Thai tea was delicious and on point, although I have never tried bad Thai tea at any restaurants yet. I was debating over coconut or tom yum soup and I gave their coconut soup a go, and it was delicious. Chicken was perfectly cooked and the flavor of the broth was full of flavor. P.S: DON'T MISS OUT ON THE NAAM SALAD FOR APPETIZER. It's like Thai version of lettuce wrap but the stuffing is so crunchy and flavorful with a bit tangy and spicy kick. I'm obsessed! For dinner, I got the green curry with chicken and it was divine. Texture of the chicken was prefect and the flavor was just amazing. I just wish that their sauce was a little creamier than watery, that's all. I'm already craving to come back here again, and I'll be sure to try their drunken noodles next time. Update after few more visit: I returned back and tried their drunken noodles and they're literally the best drunken noddles I ever had. It's called pad kee mao.

Overpriced, subpar, bland food that is not authentic at all. No flavor! Meat portion was so small, not characteristic of Arab food. Sampler appetizer was decent but we have had better. Also service is slow and inconsistent. We do not recommend.
Indian food is my favorite, and this place makes incredible food. I was very happy with everything I had. Chicken tikka masala, yellow Dahl,channa masala, beghan bartha. Total and complete yum!!!

Everyone loves this place. The food is amazing and very accessible for college students. Although, I would recommend not coming during 11:30am - 1:30pm. It's very packed during that time and you might end up waiting more than an hour. It would be awesome if they expanded into another location near campus though!
Extensive menu + fresh ingredients= many visits to this establishment.

Stopped in for a late Sunday lunch on a road trip. We ordered the lamb shank and jerk chicken and were not disappointed. The chicken was fantastically seasoned and juicy, the lamb was tender and delicious and the fried plantains were sweet enough to be dessert. If we are back in the area, we would absolutely come again!
The gym of Philly. Best tasting breakfast at very reasonable prices. Nice portion too. You can't find better value anywhere else. Make sure you get "mr. Bui's sauce" on it.

Excellent food and very friendly and considerate service. We ordered several items, and everything was fresh and delicious. Highly recommend the Lebanese tea! This restaurant is a great find. We will definitely be back next time we're in NOLA!

Fez is a nice place to go to once for the novelty, but the food is not so great. As others have described, the tent-like decor, cushiony seating, traditional music, and ritual handwashing make for a fun and unusual atmosphere, and the belly dancing is terrific. The food just isn't up to the same standard, especially if you get the vegetarian stuff. We ate there on a recent Friday. On weekends you have to get the $25 per person "Fez Feast," which is fun to order. Try telling a waiter "I'll have the feast, please" without grinning. In deference to gender stereotypes (not to mention our dietary preferences), I ordered the vegetarian feast and my boyfriend got the one with animals in it. Despite its warm and cozy appearance, the restaurant was very cold, so we ordered the Burgundy wine to try to warm up; the wine was excellent, but we were still chilly throughout the meal. Instead of napkins we were given big fluffy hand towels, which was a little disconcerting. When you're eating without utensils you need a whole lotta napkin, but white terrycloth is a peculiar choice. My boyfriend felt like he was eating a big messy piece of chicken in a spa, while I had flashbacks to covert cookie-smuggling missions in the bathroom with my little sister (you had to catch all the crumbs in the bathmat so my mom wouldn't see them). Miscellaneous notes that don't fit anywhere in particular: The vegetarian meal is not a good value at all. They must make a killing on it (so to speak). Pita and hummus are not equivalent to chicken. The bread is disguised as something exotic and triangular, but it tastes like supermarket hot dog buns. The service was attentive, although the waiter seemed incredulous each time we were ready for the next course without having eaten all the food on our plates. We were saving room! Seven is a lot of courses! If you like to smoke hookah, then this might be a nice place to go to regularly to smoke and drink and watch the dancer. Just don't go for the food.

I was in St. Louis for 3 days and happened to visit this place when flying back home as this is close to Airport. This place deserves more than 5 rating. The owner is extremely hospitable and though it was his break time he welcomed us to the restaurant. It's a small place to sit in but the food is amazingly delicious.I ordered Chicken chole ,chapati and kheer (all highly recommended) and the taste and spicy level were perfect..Being from India and having tried indian food in different cities , I will say this place is the best indian / Pakistani food I have ever had..Looking forward to another St Louis trip just to go back to this place..The owner and his wife personally cook the food , the food is not oily and spice level is just perfect..If you want to try some great authentic Indian/Pakistani food do visit this place..

I have been to Basil Spice a few times over the last couple of years. I am a tad surprised I never wrote a review for them before, but here goes... Latest visit was last night with Jason and our friend Rhoda. Faithfully, every time, I seem to get the exact same server, the exact same man comes around to each table to refill waters, and another elderly woman always brings out the food. This is definitely a family owned place with great quality food. I usually get the Pad Thai and fresh spring rolls simply because I think it is the best in the city, but last night I tried to go out of my comfort zone. Since realistically this will be my last visit to Basil Spice for a long while (we're moving Monday to Washington DC), I thought I would give my beloved Thai place one last visit. I had to get something different. So, this time I decided on getting their #32, Sen-lek Haeng. Sen-lek Haeng comes with rice noodles, bean sprouts, crispy wantons, green onions, cilantro, and crushed roasted peanuts. You can have them remove any items you may not want in there -- peanuts if you are allergic, or for me, green onions because I don't like them. I asked them to bring me extra crispy wantons also. You can choose which meat you want it to come with. They can bring it with chicken, select seafood, beef, or vegetarian. I opted for chicken for $8.95 for the entree. You can have it as spicy or not spicy as you like. They ask you with a 0-5 scale. I told them 0, but turns out, I actually wanted it spicy. Go figure. I added some spice from the brown sauce that was already on the table. They have certain additives on the table already before you get there along with the chop sticks and extra napkins. Jason ordered something sweeter than what he typically does. He loves spicy anything. Pad See-iew with beef. It's stir fried rice noodles with eggs, carrots, and broccoli in a sweet soy sauce. He rated it on the 4 for spicy. Turns out it was not spicy at all, but more sweet and very tasty. I told him I wanted to trade plates. lol This was before I had asked for the extra wantons and added the spicy brown sauce from the table. Once I did all that, I really liked mine the way it was. If I were to come here next time, I would want to order his dish. I think the only mistake of this meal was Jason ordered some sticky rice. He saw that Rhonda had some rice on her plate, but was unaware that it was simply white rice and not sticky rice. The white rice on her plate had been overcooked and could easily be misunderstood as sticky rice instead of plain white rice. Honest mistake. He got the sticky rice which was only an extra $1. Turns out the stuff is really bland and not that good in my opinion for the one bite I had and could barely swallow. I never thought that I would not like taking a bite of rice. He added some spicy chili sauce to make it more flavorful. He thought it was alright after that, but next time he will know to just ask for plain white rice. I enjoyed our visit. 2 entrees for $8.95, the sticky rice for $1, and no drinks totaling out to be $20 without tip. Not bad, especially with the portions. Oh how I will miss you my Basil Spice! You have always been good to me and I shall always remember you.

Gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because it was good food but not the best I have ever had...but don't misunderstand, it is very good. Although the prices and food quality are very reasonable, My Pad Thai was a little bland but the fresh rolls were some of the best I have ever had...we got Vegetarian. We ordered on a Saturday night at 9 pm and the food arrived within the time specified ....hot, which is usually not the case with other delivery we have ordered from different restaurants. We are in Fishtown and Erawan is down in China Town so it is a little bit out of the area and we were pleased when the owner told us it was no problem to deliver to us. I believe her name is Lodi (not sure if I spelled it correctly) and she was super, super nice on the phone! I will recommend this to others and we will for sure order again! I think next time I will ask for a little more spice in the Pad Thai as I like it spicy!!!

This was hands down the worst place ever. The food was tasteless, not authentic or fresh and just downright disgusting. Service was okay, but overall, I felt like I wasted money on food that made me sick to my stomach. I thought I was going to vomit on the way ride home because I could still taste the grossness in my mouth. I thought this would be my go-to place for Vietnamese good but definitely NOT. No thanks ever again!

Tonight was our first time eating here and my family and I really enjoyed everything! The customer service was Outstanding. We are new to Tampa/Brandon area and wanted to try something new and this place did not disappoint. We will definitely be dining here again.
Great ambiance. The masaman curry was delicious but I left still hungry. I probably won't try this place again.

i loved this place! when i used to live in philly i came here all the time. it's a little hard to find and isn't much for ambiance but the food is great. whenever i go to visit, i make sure to visit and eat there

If you are looking for great AA soul food, healthy fast food alternatives and cooked corner store food in place with a touch of love, look no further. My favorite item on their menu unique to them is their fish cheese steak. Its a regular philly cheesesteak, but instead of steak slices, they fry and chop fish! Simply Genius.

This is one of my wifes favorite resturants in Philly. when it comes to resturants, the hardest thing might be finding one that serves food simply, allowing the natural flavors of the food to come out. I believe that Dimitri's has managed to do this well. My favorite is the grilled octopus. It can get crouded, and tight. Bring a bottle of wine (or two) and get your name on the list. This place is about quality food, cooked simply. A great summer resturant. P.S. don't forget to bring cash.

The service here is top notch! I always feel like I am entering into Happy's home when I visit Desi Spice! I am immediately treated like family and seated at a nicely prepared table! The food is expertly prepared and allows time for conversation and relaxation. You leave feeling like you were treated like a VIP! You definitely need to visit ASAP and enjoy your meal!

Absolutely love it here! I've only been twice but both experiences were top notch. The service is great and the chef was super accommodating of my vegan restrictions. The food is so flavorful and the menu variety is very nice. Great value also!!

It gets 5 stars, b/c for BOI, this is as good as it gets. The sandwiches are light, and tasty. The pho is my favorite. I always get the big bowl, never thinking I can finish it. It is gone by the end. The prices are excellent. I wish it was easier to get to. It is off the beaten path for me. I live out of town, and it is not near any errands I run. But way worth it.

We went to Godavari for the first time this past weekend. Reviews which I had read beforehand cautioned about how spicy the food is. I asked the waiter to explain which chicken dishes were "less spicy" and he suggested one I might prefer. The 3 guests with us also noted they wanted less spicy items. Everyone got something different, but they all had in common being overly spicy. We quickly asked for Yogurt to cool us down and drank lots of water. When we got home I took 3 tums!!! I hope that management will recognize that they are losing customers (see a few other reviews) due to the food being too spicy for at least some people's taste. The owners should consider including on the menu items that are prepared with no hot spices, where the customer can personally season their food with spices in side dishes, or a side menu with items having no or minimal hot spices. We liked our waiter and the ambience was ok---the food,unfortunately, is just too spicy for our tastes. It may simply be that South Indian food is not for me. However, if you are concerned about the spiciness of what you are going to order, this place may not be the right one to choose.

Such a cute little place, the staff is very friendly, the food is good and I love the fact that they have a vegetarian section on the menu. They also have some great hookha flavor, it's great for an intimate dinner where you can actually have a conversation without loud music.

This was my first experience trying Indian food and I went with the classic - chicken tikka masala with rice. Umm.... YUM. I get that every time now because I just crave it. The chicken is so tender and everything is just so flavorful and filling, I always leave super stuffed. We also get the naan, which is perfect to dip. Cannot recommend this place enough. Amazing service and the complimentary little rice pudding for dessert is the PERFECT cap to the meal. Definitely go here if you have the opportunity.

I used to love this place. A year ago it was my favorite and I would drive thirty minutes to and from the place just for carry out a couple times a month! About five - six months ago this changed. The chicken Tikka Masala that I had come to love was barely edible. For $20 for my meal, you would think that the chicken would be good and tender. Instead it was fatty and grisly... In fact the last three times I have gone back, hoping that the last time was a fluke, it was the same poor quality chicken. Also the service is horrid here. That's always been the case but I could overlook it because of the food quality. When the quality also waned, I could overlook it no longer. The servers are rude (period).
The chicken pita is to die for! Crispy and soft with soooooo much flavor. Made my belly smile!

Good Indian food at a reasonable price, I enjoy the fussion of various cuisines together. We purchased the rice bowl and sandwich version, and suprisingly with our combination, it tasted great. Now, I'm quite harsh with Indian cuisine here in the US since I've worked in an Indian restaurant before and give this place a thumbs up for fresh food with awesome taste. However, they may want to lower the glass screen a bit - I get the fact of ensuring food quality but it almost feels like playing peekaboo with the staff.

Absolutely excellent Duck soup. I've sampled a few dishes from Creazian and they've always impressed. I've had the shaking beef (5/5) and quite enjoy their fried rice, but today I had their duck soup and I must say I was very impressed. The duck was tender, not overcooked; the noodles were soft but not gummy; the spice was on key. The ambiance is quite lovely despite a somewhat concealed (though easily accessible) location on South Virginia Street, the price is reasonable, and the staff is courteous and helpful. Will certainly be returning. Shout out to my server Geri, she was exceptional

Wonderfully innovative Thai food! My husband had a Pad Pumpkin dish that was fabulous; a friend had a sushi plate that was beautifully presented and very tasty. The Tom kha gai soup I had as an appetizer was authentic and wonderfully seasoned. Be careful of asking for more spice, though. I asked for 6-7/10 and was served the hottest pad Thai I've ever eaten. This was our 3rd visit.

Great food and service. We had a party of 10 and everyone was served at the same time. Quick turnaround for credit card payment as well. Was a little noisy...but given food quality, portion sizes and service...all in a great experience.

I LOVE Taziki's and this restaurant is GREAT. Things are always fresh, tasty, and cooked and seasoned to perfection. The staff is friendly and courteous. Service is always prompt. They will even pay for an hour of parking in a lot they don't own behind the West End location. BUT Premier Parking watches that lot like a hawk. They will be upon your vehicle within minutes to boot your car if you even as much as hesitate to stop by the parking kiosk. Their practices are predatory, and the parking that should cost you nothing will all of a sudden cost you $95 plus the lost time and hassle of having to wait to get your car unbooted. AND THAT'S NOT ALL. Parking is enforced by a third party contractor who reports NOTHING to Premier Parking. You WILL have to pay the citation to get your car unbooted, and then to close the violation, Premier will require YOU to prove that you paid your ticket because THEY are too lazy to track their own receivables. (This is particularly disturbing because Premier has reportedly been caught charging credit cards two years after the fact and has major data security issues with their systems.) So to conclude, I give the Taziki's 5* and Premier Parking who manages the lot a negative star for an average of two stars.

I visited Thai Basil Spice the other day in an attempt to check out some more restaurants before ending my vacation here in St. Louis. The spring rolls were decent, and the yellow curry was ok. Not particularly great, but not horrible. The ambience was a bit weird as I could not put my finger on what type of crowd it attracts either which slightly confused me. Worth a visit, but do not expect to be blown away.

Upon all of the recommendations from other comments, I got the roti canai and it was definitely good! The pad thai was also great! The Thai iced coffee was good, but just a bit too sweet and creamy for my taste. Its a nice little place on South Street. I would definitely go back!

This review is a few weeks overdue but I thought of Dosa Hut and I remembered I had to make a review. I wouldn't have done this if it wasn't so good that I felt the need to spread the word! This place is amazing. I did not know Indian food like this could exist in Nashville! I grew up in Los Angeles where there are dozens of Indian restaurants even in the suburbs where I lived and I have eaten at almost all of them. I would rank this place among the best I've had anywhere in my life. What an incredible surprise. The food: One word. Tiffin. From my understanding, they always have a tiffin (at least for dinner) on the menu and the dishes it comes with change on a weekly basis. For those who don't know, you get a an appam (unsure of spelling), like a thin pancake made of rice flour and coconut milk in the middle of a big tray and then they surround it with different curries and side dishes. There were like eight dishes and we found every single one to be flavorful. The best part? You get up to three appam (get them one at a time so they are fresh and hot) and then unlimited amounts of all the dishes! The tiffin made my girlfriend's and my decision easy. Before we saw it, we were looking through the rest of the menu and wanted to try something in every type of food on the menu. We love to share and sample a wide variety of things, so the tiffin allowed us to do that. We also got a chicken tikka masala and chicken biryani to sample some go-to dishes. The curry was on point and the biryani was good, though not the best. It was definitely still good enough that I would order it again, though there are about a dozen other items on the menu I want to try in addition to the current tiffin so it'll make its way back in the rotation eventually lol. Lastly, we got a dosa and I forget which one it was. It had potatoes in it, and honestly it was nothing special. There was a potato dish on the tiffin and we wished that was inside the dosa. However, I still plan to try several more dosas because I'm sure they are as good as the rest of the food and we just didn't get the right one. Pros/Cons (or Summary): This place is the perfect hole in the wall spot. The service is good and everybody that works there is extremely nice, the food comes out in a very timely manner, and of course it is delicious. Don't expect it to be fancy. It isn't important. If you are looking for good food with tons of flavor, which you should be if you are on the hunt for ethnic food in this cultural wasteland of ethnic restaurants of a city, you should definitely check this place out and expect to eat a lot of food.
We come here all the time for the clay pot. Always the best. Good service & the owner is so friendly.

Ordering is always solid. I've had like 5 different dishes . All good spice and flavor. Had the buffet inside once. Maybe we didnt come at the most opportune time because meat was scarce, but I can imagine it's good if u get there on time.

This is a welcome option on St Charles Ave. Hop off the streetcar at Jackson and grab a bowl of pho, or their Spicy Beef Soup (Bun Bo Hue) or their Vietnamese Crepe (Banh Xeo). Everything is good. Really. Full bar and attentive service round out this great new place!

Olio is my favorite spot in St. Louis. There is no other place like it. Everything on their Mediterranean menu is so delicious that I always know I can't go wrong. The music on their patio on a summer night is perfection. It's always light, romantic, and not too loud. Sitting at the bar and having a perfectly made craft cocktail while chatting with their fun bartenders is always fun too. Great wine selection, fair prices, good service and the place just reeks of charisma. I come back again and again, love it!!!

this is not a fancy looking place...reminds me of an old Shoneys converted into a Viet restuarant....but if you can get past that, you will find that this place is pretty good. great menu...lots of choices, food and service were good great Pho, Fairly good spring rolls, excellent Boba Tea....best I've had in this town so far

Not authentic Indian cuisine -- it tasted like the Indian version of a kraft dinner. No music, a place for lonely people to eat lunch alone, plastic chicken, and microwaved naan. Make sure you don't need to use the bathroom while you are there. It is disgusting! Redeeming qualities are decent dessert and cheap?

Found this place by accident. Pulled into St. Pete by boat @ 10 p.m on a Thursday night with 5 friends. This place stays open serving food and drinks past midnight. The staff was very accommodating and the food was very good. Prices were reasonable . We will definitely go again.

I moved to Boise on August 2014 and since then I went to kabob house at least 4 times a month. I'd give them more than 5 stars if I could. The servant is nice, food is delicious, and I like the floor coaches they have. The restaurant is high in price, but it deserve the money for what you get. I can compare the food here with the food from my country in Middle East. Meaning that in my country the original kabobs are there, but kabob house made it to the top. I'd prefer their rips with the best rips we have in my country. Food suggestions -Qabuli pillow (rice with lamp chunk) -lamp rips ( it's the best of the grill) -tikka lamp kabob -Tikka chicken kabob I prefer (mantoo) as the side order.
The pho broth and banh mi are delicious. Customer service is average, depending on how busy they are. They're always out of bread, so go early if you want your banh mi!

Back when we lived it Lenox Village & it was always great. The place was never packed but the stuff was attentive & friendly. The portions were large & the place was clean. It kind of got a little odd at the end because they wouldn't be open on certain days or open for lunch one day & not the next. I've now just realized that Thai Taste has closed down & it's now called Thai Ville. If you're looking for Thai in the area you'll want to search for that one & not this one as its now CLOSED.
1st time, delivery took 2 hrs. 2nd time, 2.5 hrs, and food was cold/congealed. Delivery driver called me a d*ck when I wouldn't sign (I had paid in full online, he slowly realized his mistake)
This place is amazing - stopped here on a road trip and are reviewing this in part so we can find it again to go back every time we pass through!
Pho didn't taste like pho Dirty,there a beach chair kids sleeping next To bathroom ,real dirty,$9.50 for a bowl of pho soup Too expensive health department needs to check this place out
Amazing place for breakfast!!! Loved everything, especially the peach crumb pancakes! Wonderful ice tea!

The service, food, and aesthetics were all great! The popcorn appetizer is a nice touch. I enjoyed a great bowl of steak pho, and passionfruit cocktail, and my friend enjoyed the pad thai. I'd highly recommend this restaurant!

Just got to go food- prepares well- labeled all the boxes- very good variety and tastes- atmosphere really nice inside- recommend appetizer sampler or crab Rangoon! Also had a Thai iced tea while I was waiting so cool and refreshing! Very good food for the Spring Hill Area, good portions and nice and hot! Be adventurous! Yum! Have Left overs for days

Their olive bread is tasty. We tried several of their entries and were never disappointed, although I wish they would extend their menu to include more variety of items. Dining atmosphere and service are nice too. They offer different seating options, and provide party and gathering space upstairs.

First off, the smell is amazing when you first walk in the door. The staff is very friendly and always making sure that everything is okay. This food is traditionally eaten with your hands and the injeera bread. The time I was there, utensils were offered, though optional. It does take a bit of a wait for your food since everything is prepared from scratch. However, the wait is worth it. They also give you a choice of mild or spicy for all entrées. The food we had was absolutely amazing. I got the Queen's tibs. They serve most of the entrées on a large shareable platter with Ethiopian style veggies. Everything was delicious!
This place is a gem. The lamb Qozi is the best meal on the menu. Qozi is a popular Iraqi and Arabic gulf region food and it was very authentic! Their bamyia saloona is a close second. Thank you guys.

My local friends brought me here and I absolutely loved it. The staff are incredibly polite and thoughtful - full of smiles and kindness. The food was excellent; just the right amount of spices with good flavor. Will come back when am in town

Great indian food. I didnt give five stars cuz food was too hot and they have the same level of spicy. Other indian places let decide what level of spicy you prefer. I asked them to make the baryani with no spicy, but they told me that baryani is made already and not upon request. I like their food and plan to visit them again. The place was perfect and friendly staff

I don't know where the positive reviews come from. Our experience was horrible. The serving sizes are very small. Our server would place plates and food on our table as if throwing it at us. Not only that she touched her nose while serving us. The food was mediocre at best

Just ate here for the first time with my wife and 2 young kids. My wife who is gluten intolerant had the steak kabobs and was surprised they were tender and flavored well. I had the Mediterranean chicken platter. The chicken was tender and the caramelized onions were good considering this is a quick service restaurant. The white beans suffer dish was very good and had a nice creamy texture and subtle flavor. The hummus trio was homemade and you can taste the difference from store bought. It came with soft and crisp pita wedges as well as cucumber slices and bell peppers. An employee brought more cucumber slices for my wife so she could enjoy the hummus. Even my 7 year old son enjoyed the grilled chicken fingers. He didn't mind the fact that they were not deep fried and not accompanied by French fries. I only wish they served Falafel which I love.

First time at Blue Plate this morning for breakfast.... Banana pancakes with a carmel sauce were great and the vanilla praline butter was a perfect addition. The bananas were cooked right into the large fluffy pancakes which was nice compared to some places that just plop the bananas on top. We also had blueberry pancakes which were equally as good. The prices were reasonable, there was only a very short wait on a Sunday morning, the staff of mostly young kids were friendly with good teamwork with one seating us and taking drink orders, another taking the food order and another offering a coffee refill. I know it's ONLY breakfast, and yes there are lots of diners to get breakfast, but this was a nice change. I'm wondering when we can make it back to try thier dinner menu.

In really enjoyed the food, but there were some things that prevented me from giving it a five star review: 1. The amount of hummus in the hummus bowl is a joke. There was so little hummus that there was none at the bottom of the bowl. I had to order a side of hummus which made the meal not worth the money. The hummus is excellent, mind you, but they need to rethink their portions. 2. They should cut the chicken for the shawarma on order. I can understand pre-cutting the chicken to faster serve customers during the lunchtime rush but I was there in the evening on July 4th, and there were only a handful of patrons there. Hope these things, especially item one, can be addressed.
Very good Thai food. One of our favorite neighborhood spots. Love that it is a BYOB.
Please PAY your taxes and reopen ...our favorite restaurant in EAGLE

Five stars for the food. One star for the service. Absolutely do not ever, ever go to this restaurant if you have a larger party than 4. Six people and four people all get the same space arrangement: two small tables pushed together. They will refuse to allow three tables to be put together and they will insist that 3 people sit on each side and not allow two people to sit at the ends. They will not seat you if you don't have everyone ready. They don't split checks and they only accept cash.They don't let you order in stages and will force you to pile all 14 plates onto the small space they have condescended to give you. But once you start eating, you want to forgive them for every service sin. The food here is absolutely amazing. It's simple but everything has an incredibly bold, vivid flavor profile. The portions are more than generous and I strongly advise against ordering one dish per person because there will be too much food left over. We had two orders of the hummus, it's a very creamy, nutty texture. They serve it cold, it was obviously pre-plated and kept in the fridge, but still went wonderfully with the warm house pita bread. Between six carb-loving girls, we emptied the single basket of pita triangles 3 times and had to ask each and every time for a refill. I had a plate of the grilled octopus which was amazingly tender and not at all fishy. The texture was unlike any other seafood, it was more like chicken. I would strongly recommend this for those that generally avoid fish dishes. A few pieces were charred and crispy which I personally enjoyed. My friends had a variety of salads including the Avocado citrus salad, as well as an order of the scallops and spinach pie. I shamelessly stole bites across the table. The avocado citrus salad is gorgeous with glistening slices of peeled grapefruit and orange. I really enjoyed the spinach pie because it was composed almost entirely of spinach with a flaky crust and the cheese was only sprinkled throughout. It didn't feel heavy or greasy at all. But the scallops. The scallops were king. They come in a thin coating of breadcrumbs and melt on your tongue. You barely have to touch your fork to them before they flake off into succulent bites. I would do a lot of things to eat those scallops again. We ordered such a huge variety of dishes that the waitress actually missed one, a small plate of the beets. It never came out which was probably a good thing for our stomachs but when the bill came, they didn't include an item-by-item list so we had no way of checking if they charged us for the beets or not. Of course, it took us a long time to work through the meal and we tipped over the mandatory 18% they already charged us on the bill but we were still standing around the table and pulling our coats on when they started clearing our dishes away. Even before that, a series of 3 different waitresses came by to ask us if we wanted things to go. I've never been so torn about a restaurant before. I loved the food but is it worth the experience? If you factor in the price point, I think my answer is going to have to be no.
The fresh and warm Amoroso bread was clutch, but too little egg and too little ham for a hearty breakfast sandwich.
My favorite place in town to get great Tabbouleh. Worth checking out!
Very tasty and affordable Greek food. Try Beef Kabob, it's very tasty. Drink selection isn't wide, however they have root beer. They also have desserts.

Great food and relatively inexpensive for the quality. My husband and I wandered in one evening and were delightfully surprised by the romantic ambiance and classy appeal. We tried several of the appetizers and had a few cocktails. Since we had ordered so much I was pleasantly surprised when the check came because without keeping a cost tally, I had expected it to be much more compared to other places we have been. We will definitely be back soon!

I don't know what the previous reviewers are talking about when they talk about the low health inspection score... I'm not even sure if they know what they are talking about. Our friend who lives in Reno took us here, and I'm glad they did. I'm from San Jose and the Pho here was surprisingly very good for Reno. I was shocked that I could get a bowl this good out here. The broth was a bit oily but the quality of the meat and flavor was definitely on point! It's next to a 7-11 store! Never seen a Pho restaurant next to a gas station and 7-11 at the same time. The service wasn't super fast but I didn't mind it too much if the food was good. My friend ordered a side of egg rolls were were definitely underwhelming but you don't come to a Pho restaurant and order egg rolls... spring rolls maybe but not fried egg rolls. Anyhow, I got a large bowl with almost everything in it except beef balls. Never get beef balls in pho cause its just overly processed meat. Try this place if you are in Reno! There are a number of other Vietnamese and Pho restaurants I noticed in Reno but I don't know how they stack up. This is a safe choice I think. :) I felt perfectly fine after, so there are probably good on their health inspection now. Nothing like a hot bowl of Pho in freezing cold temps!

Loved this place, although it is probably one of the most cramped seating arrangement ever. Get the grilled octopus, fantastic, along with the warm pitas, with hummus. The wait is long, but there is a nice bar across the street you can wait in, and the hostess will come and get you. Miss this place a lot

Food was good. The service was abysmal. Waitress had no personality what so ever, messed our order up, and we had to get up and ask for a refill! Not many restaurants will lose my business over a day of poor service, but I will not be returning to Beryani.

I usually don't like Indian food, too spicy, too much curry, but I like this one. I love their curry & naans. The only thing is the waitress, sometimes she looks like she doesn't understand or speak no english, but she seem nice. This is the only Indian food that I like for now. I like this place!
Thoroughly enjoyed the Drunken Noodles, the Panang curry was OK but would avoid the Crying Tiger salad. It is authentic thai mostly and the staff were really pleasant. I would recommend it.

The BBQ Pork sandwich is a now my favorite thing is this town to eat paired with a steaming bowl of Pho next to it. I love the way the do it the right way, by serving you bowl of broth with the meat and all of the condiments on the side. They even give you the raw beef to add you self and just barely cook in the warm broth. Hate to say it but deli George is now a close second to this place for sandwiches.

Oh dear. Was so looking forward to my Friday night Bun. Sadly, it was not to be. iPho, we were so pleased to see you land in our neighborhood. Vietnamese food! In Fairmount! We wanted to support your arrival in Fairmount. But we were so disappointed by the reception on our first visit, we decided to leave before ordering. Basic customer service was seriously lacking. 101 for a restaurant host is to smile, greet the customer warmly and provide them with some helpful info (or better yet, a table!). Do not leave them flailing by the door, and then shove them on the window counter, when there is space for at least another 8 people at tables (because you haven't figured out how to separate two tables for 2). The hostess was neither friendly, nor did she seem to have a clue. Once seated at the window, we were told that it would be a 30 min wait to throw together a bun. It was 9pm, so hardly dining rush hour. And it's bun, so most of the ingredients are cold! We cut our losses and went to the fun Japanese BBQ place on Callowhill instead. Ok, we get that it was opening week. Mistakes get made. It's busy. But employ staff who have basic customer service skills and treat local customers with some courtesy, otherwise they won't come back. We're going to give the delivery / takeout service a go this evening. But if that fails, we won't be returning. Customer service really matters in a big city like Philly. There are heaps of other great places to eat that have customer service down, so if you want to compete, let alone be a loved neighborhood eatery, fix this, and quick! UPDATE on takeout - Zero customer service on the phone either. We're going to Pho Cali in Chinatown instead - ten mins wait for takeout bun and noodle soup (they know how to run a takeout business). We might try iPho again in a few weeks, if reviews suggest they've got their act together.
What a find! haha. Instant smell of a lemongrass and cappuccino. Clean, modern, if your looking for a tastey snack downtown -THIS is the place :P
Bring a friend. Get a foot long banh mi sans butter ($6.99). Jalepenos are darn spicy, but delish. Drink a Big Shot soda. Thank me later. This is some good stuff people!
Pho Cam Ly is THE BEST Vietnamese food I've ever had! Please go and try my favorites: Spring Rolls with pork sausage and a wonton strip Lemon Grass Banh Mi Curry (when its available)

One of the most consistent restaurants I know of. - for both food and service. Always a notch above ordinary. I don't hesitate for a minute to bring friends or recommend Spiro's. I tend to order Greek specialties but the steaks and pasta are wonderful as well.

First time here. It is a hole in the wall but that doesn't matter. I ordered curried goat and oxtails with rice and peas, delicious plantains, and cabbage. My daughter's oxtail are a cut above these, but these were very good. A few pieces of the oxtail were dried out but dipping the in the sauce rejuvenated them to their tender deliciousness. I savored the flavor and texture of the perfectly cooked gelatinous cartilage. The curried goat was delicious as well and I especially enjoyed sucking the delicious gravy off the bones. The sweet crispness of the plantains was a perfect addition to the savory flavors of the meats. I'll return to try some if the other offerings.

Food was very pathetic. NO taste and chicken was literally hard like rubber. Non cooperative staff. Seriously, if you are looking for Indian food, please do not waste your money and time going here. Highly disappointed. ZERO STAR.

I haven't had food here but their hookahs are excellent and their drinks are delicious. It's not fancy but they go around changing coals and have many options, such as ice hoses, mixed flavors and many many more. Waitresses are sweet and attentive.
My husband and I love bringing a bottle of wine in and enjoying the vegetarian food. We always get an app, 2 entrees, and naan and are never let down. We always have leftovers to bring home.

Since moving here in June, I have come here for the lunch buffet at least once a week (literally...). The service is always impeccable, the naan is fresh, there are at least 10 different entree choices and there is always rice pudding. I mean what more can you ask for from a lunch buffet that's ~10/~13 (weekday/weekend).
This is my family's favorite Thai restaurant. Food is so fresh and tasty. Staff is very welcoming and attentive. They also have the BEST peanut sauce!!!

My husband and I decided to try something new a couple weeks ago. We can't stop talking about how good Pho36 is!! We loved the Spring Rolls so much we had two orders. They were all fresh ingredients and not fried. Oh, so good! Then, our entrees were both great to. We will be back on that side of town nov 1st and will be eating there again! We can't wait! The decor is not much, but it does not matter, because the food is so good!

We were in town for a conference and looking for a local place to eat. We saw that they were brand new and we were craving Indian food and decided to dropped in. It's a fun, fast, inexpensive and easy spot. Enjoyable for lovers of Indian food and for those new to it. Great lunch spot!!

My boyfriend and I got delivery from here, and it was pretty good. We shared the drunken noodles with shrimp and the vegetarian golden spring rolls. The sauce flavor for the noodle dish was delicious and spicy, but the noodles were all stuck together, so it was a little hard to eat. The spring rolls were pretty good but nothing special. Also, we were kind of annoyed by their delivery rule that they charge $3 when they deliver more than 4 blocks away. That just seems a little silly. Overall, it is a solid Thai restaurant, but I don't think we'll be making this one our go-to place.

Quite yummy, big portions, reasonable prices, sweet staff, nice décor, easy parking. What more could you want? Other than silver ware maybe... Yes we had a few folks ask for it... I lived dangerously and got my hands dirty, burned them too on some hot dish, dove right in there, lost half my food on the way from plate to mouth, but hey it's the experience that counts. Having no idea what anything is I just ordered one of the combination plates and I likes most everything on there... now I just hope I can remember next time which one was my favorite and order a whole serving of that one, cause it was really delicious. I really wish I could describe things in more detail for you but I would first have to know what it is that I ate, which I don't. Let's just say it was all very flavorful and obviously made with great care. The chef even came out to inquire what we thought about the dishes, which I thought was a nice touch. Oh I did have the beef sambusa (I do know what that is) as an appetizer and it was awesome. Light flaky crust, hot as heck and obviously freshly deep fried, with a savory filing of ground beef with herbs and spices. Highly recommend.

Everything I ever wanted from a Vietnamese restaurant. So glad they are here! Touchscreen experience isn't the -most- intuitive but that's hardly worth docking a star. Multiple visits show the food is fantastic and fast and perfectly priced. What's not to love.

Great service. The chutneys were a little lacking in complexity though. The salads come with fenugreek all over them, are delicious, and serve two per order. I told them I wanted it extremely spicy and they still babied me. Overall I'm a fan.

Took the #1 bus from WEM alllllll the way to the end almost and found this place.The big giant noodle sign drew me in like a magnet. Mmmmmmmm.....noodles....mmmmm. Not terribly fancy inside but nice and homey. Good service and good prices . The bun bo hue is indeed very good . The broth was really spicy for a change so no condiments were necessary. I'll be back for more.
My favorite restaurant ever!!! I have gone here for years and the quality has always been outstanding. The staff is wonderful and tremendously kind. A Phoenixville gem!!

I gave this place 3 stars because I think the price is a little steep for what you get. My boyfriend got the Jungle King curry. It was really good, spicy and tasty. I had the Drunken Noodle. I didn't have a problem with the portion sizes; they weren't huge, but they were reasonable. My biggest problem was with the Drunken Noodle being too oily. I noticed it more as it cooled down, but it really was too greasy for me. I will definitely be back to try a few more things. My co-workers rave about this place. I thought it was good, but I wasn't crazy impressed or anything. Worth checking out if you are in the area. I also want to try their lunch special which looks pretty good.

Food and service were terrific. My friend and I had the cauliflower and carrots to start, then the clams and octopus. Split the sundae for dessert. Everything was fresh and well prepared. Yummy! Will definitely come back.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Best Biryani in st.louis. Hyderabadi style which is very different from North Indian or Lahore Biryani. Meaning no tomatoes, rose water and apricot in it. Once you eat Hyderabadi Biryani and compare with other styles you can tell the difference. Biryani comes from Persia (Iran) Brunj Biryan in Iranian language (Farsi) means fried rice.

Love this new neighborhood spot! We came for the lunch buffet and were very impressed. Excellent variety of dishes, all of them very tasty. We loved the flavors and spice in each dish. We'll definitely be back!
Friendly service. But Pad Thai was still disappointing. Dry (and too much tomato taste). Best pad thai we've had is on Dale Mabry (Thailand restaurant)
I used to be a regular customer to this place but in last few months quality of the food is worse..

{ International Wednesday Post } Checked out this adorable little BYOB for international Wednesday, and found it to be just alright. The 2 person tables in the windows are way to close together, there is no privacy. The service was a bit awkward and although the food was alright, I have had WAY better Thai for much less money.

The price for the portions was excellent! I had never had Dominican food before and a co-worker of mine is Dominican and told me that this place was good so I took my wife. The food was good and the price was amazing. We also had left overs. We definitely will be going back.

What happened here? There was a friendly atmosphere, friendly servers, charming lady making the drinks. The staff would actually recognize us and say hello Now, the Vietmamese equivalent of Sgt. Joe Friday has taken over. He scowls around the place, sometimes takes orders without looking at anyone, looking away even, while chewing gum. He is a hospitality fail. This place still has the Vietnamese clientele, still has the tasty dishes, but the welcoming ambiance is gone.

This is a go-to spot when I want good and fresh comfort food. The food has always been prepared to order. I've had the fried whiting and fried chicken wings. Both are very tasty. My only minor complaint is that the meats are cooked with very little seasoning. This is their process in order to keep the grease clean. The solution is just to ask for your meat to be seasoned after it's cooked and viola issue solved. The mac and cheese tastes just like home and the candied carrots (no yams) are delicious. I've tried the cabbage and string beans and both are just okay. All in all I would definitely recommend Sister Muhammad's if you are looking for soul food. I would also suggest calling ahead they can get pretty busy.

This place is good if you need to have your pho explained, or if you want to get vegetarian pho (why is this so hard to find?), or if you want to order sides of vietnamese food that are not pho in addition to your soup, a luxury for some reason not afforded at other pho places in the area. I do love their extensive drink menu of various bubble teas and smoothies, but I think the food itself is only OK.
We make the drive from Riverview all the way into Tampa for this place! Mainly for the Thai sausages! My fiancé loves them, he's thai and finds they are the most authentic!

Still a 5 star food experience. You are MISSING OUT if you have not been here. I seriously think this is some of the best food in Tampa. In my top 3 of Tampa restaurants. Get the chicken kebab with rice and salad, extra garlic sauce. Have someone else order the hummus so you can try that. And ask for boxes, because the portions are ENORMOUS. Don't complain to me or to Yelp about the decor, the location, the prices, or the service here, the food is SO GOOD it doesn't matter. Sometimes the service is perfection, other times it's barely decent. I could eat here once a week and be in heaven. I CRAVE that chicken and that garlic sauce. (See photo Number 4 above.) JUST GO.
Your Mediterranean Chipotle! The bowl is a good quantity and definitely value for money. The naf fries are mediocre. Not much of an ambience or dine in place. More of a take out.

This was the place that made me start really liking food. This was the place that also makes all other thai places stand no chance of getting 5 stars. The owner, Wes, is a really nice guy, makes a lot of the decorations himself, has some pink floyd tattoos and likes his customers. Yes, you, he likes you. The rose potatoes are cooked to a perfect, buttery consistency--The curries are thick and filled with a cornucopia of delicious, seasonal, and cooked just right veggies. The masaman curry is perfect. I used to get teased for ordering it over and over again, but it was just that good. I had tried every vegetarian option on the menu and most were on the excellent side, but the masaman was just exactly what I loved. I'd say 3 out of 10 of my top meals ever were here--maybe more. After about 4 years of living in Santa Barbara, I had easily gone here over 100 times and was not ever disappointed--even on their worst day, they were still the best thai food in town.
Food was very delicious and fresh great service, the BBQ pork was one of our favorites

This is a very good lunch spot in general. Some of the soups are hit or miss, but generally it's a lot of bang for your buck. The service is fast and friendly but not always very attentive. Overall it's a good experience.

My girlfriend picked up takeout from this place. She ordered two chicken dishes with garlic nan and rice. The chicken vindaloo and chicken makhanwala were seasoned perfectly with perfectly cooked chicken and potatoes, and plenty of sauce to dip the nan in. The rice was perfectly cooked and tasted great. Very impressed.

this was my 2nd & last time here/ food is overpriced & has no taste to it. naan -$4.95 - no wonder this place was empty. asked for onion chatney-$3.95 for very small portion - was in there by my self- the owner waited 15 minutes before taking an order --i'm sorry i went in there.

I went here in the mood for udon noodle soup. Ended up with the vegetarian noodle soup. It was pretty good , nice medley of flavors. It looks like they have a healthy amount of vegetarian options. I'll probably come back just to try the rest of the menu. But only if I'm in the area.
Must Try:Pork Chop..,One in a while, I went to Philadelphia and a friend of mine recommend to try for Pork Chop. The best Pork Chop every I had.

Happy Hours here are great, and a good value. Staff is always friendly. But...Had dinner here for the first time in a long while and the Lobster Ravioli tasted like a reheated sugar bomb. Also really pricey for what you get. I'll stick to the Happy Hours.
I loved this place but I just went recently and the menu stated they were not doing the coconut shaved ice any more. I am so sad :(
Best Shusi & Thai by far. We have been to all most every Shusi bar in the Tampa area and Ploy Thai has them beat hands down.

Dosa Hut & Chat House is a bit of a conundrum. On one hand the food is excellent. Supremely fresh and with a variety of Indian dishes that you may not find elsewhere. If you grow tired of chicken tikka, butter chicken, and other items you'll find en masse at other Indian restaurants, Dosa Hut is a great place to visit. Given the name, you'd expect that the dosas, utappams, and chats are prepared quite well and indeed they are. You really won't go wrong with any of them. The curries are also consistently tasty, but not the best I've ever had. For what you get, I think the pricing is a tad high but is not unreasonable. Where I have trouble giving DH&CH 5 stars is the service and environment. On a Friday, during lunch--which you'd imagine is the busiest period during the entire week--they had ONE employee staffing the entire dining room of 40 or so patrons. With the entire dining room filled up (so much so that we actually shared a table with other people) and other patrons waiting outside for a seat to open up, with one guy waiting on the entire room made it difficult to get any service. Speaking of the dining room, it consists of high stainless steel tables, swivel chairs probably from a discount hotel furniture store, and styrofoam/plastic dining ware. I think I'd peg DH&CH at 3.5 stars.... the food really is excellent and I have no reservations about heading back frequently, but they really need to bring the other aspects of the experience up to the same level as the cuisine. That being said, my official Yelp ranking will be 4 because it's great to have tasty and different Indian food in the area.

Seriously delicious! Everything tasted authentic and service was great. This place was is a bit far for us but it was so good that I will be back! I will be dreaming about their palak paneer, lamb vindaloo and garlic naan until I return.

This was my first time going to La Mulita and I'm unsure why I haven't been before. Sooooo delicious!! I am a vegetarian and loved having options! I ordered the Tacos De Rajas with Herb Green Rice and it was absolutely amazing! 2 tacos and a side for $13. Can't beat that! We did order Guacamole and Ceviche but they were gone before I could snap a photo! And....how could I forget- the margaritas were really good. I'm really particular about not having too much lime juice in mine and they were outstanding! Try this place out- you won't be mad you did!!
Very flavorful gyros for $6. It was also kind of cool that the guy making my meal looked like he came straight out of the movie 300. The place is well hidden. It's right next to Mr B's.

Went today for the first time. I am not overly familiar with Indian food, so my opinion on the food may not mean much but I really enjoyed what I got. I got a rice bowl with tandoori chicken. The spiciest of the sauces (sorry forgot the name) but it was just the right amount of spice with yogurt chutney. It was delicious. I will definitely be trying that dish again. But, I feel that the atmosphere and kindness are more important to mention. Every person working there greeted me with a smile. With this being more of a fast food feel and less like a traditional Indian restaurant, I was worried that I wouldn't have an authentic experience, and that was not the case. When paying, the woman who was behind the register asked if it was my first time because she didn't recognize me and also asked me where I heard about them. She told me thank you for coming in and to please come back. Will do!

Our favorite Pho place....I've disregarded that this is a chain....it's the only one in Philly, and for this type of food, it's okay.... Great Spring Rolls, Fresh ingredients, clean, attentive service, a great price for the quality and quantity.

Had good reviews thought I give this place a try. Started off with no service attentive to seat us. They weren't busy. We sat ourselves. They have a nice outside patio seating. A great location that's across from the cannery ballroom. Free parking. Ordered drinks all drinks came in small little glass after one sip it was gone. So annoying they could of given us a taller glass so the waiter wouldn't have to keep coming to refill your glass. Started off trying the appetizer empanadas which were good. The prices for the entree meals were a bit expensive. I tried the Specialty mofongo Pollo $16. Came out in a silver bowl. The mofongo is fried plantains mashed down with seasonings and tasted over cook or fried and very SALTY. With sliced up plain chicken breast like they just brought it out of the freezer. Was not impressed with the meal. It was disappointing cause this place had good reviews and their pictures does not look nothing like what they posted. I would not be looking forward to coming back to this place.

Service here is very good and Apollo Beach needed a Mediterranean restaurant. I have been there probably 4 to 5 times and I get the Greek salad with Gyro and the meat pie. The salad is very good. It has plenty of veggies and it's really fresh and green. I know that sounds odd, but I really hate when restaurants bring me a salad with white or wilted lettuce. I really like how the gyro is grilled and crispy. The meat pie is served hot and has just the right curried spices. Very delicious. Six months ago I would have given them 4 stars. I know this may be petty, but I don't like bottled or canned soda and they got rid of their fountain drinks. Since I only have soda in the middle of the day, I would rather go someplace where they have it. If they change that I would certainly give them more stars.

We went here on a whim after seeing the previous Yelp reviews. The place is tiny---in an outdoor shopping center without even a sign on the building except for a little stand on the ground in front. When my girlfriend (who has lived nearby her entire life) asked how long they had been here and we were told "eight years", she was shocked---no idea this place was even here. I got a standard beef gyro and my girlfriend the chicken gyro. Top notch---easily the best gyros we've had in Tucson. She paired hers with the mint tea, and after tasting hers I wished I'd gotten one, too. I ordered an Arabic coffee (mind you, I'd never had one of these before) and had that after dinner. Delicious. Afterwards, the manager (?) brought out an entire iced coffee (I did not order this nor pay for it), said I'd probably enjoy it if I liked the hot Arabic coffee but that it was a bit different, and just left it there (it was also delicious). Only downsides: their kitchen seemed a little off, and it wasn't exactly busy. A "no tomatoes" request was ignored (not that that's a big deal but still would be nice) and the Arabic coffee didn't come out until about ten minutes after we were finished eating. I wouldn't even hesitate to return, though!
The food is great and as a Malaysian, I can vouch for the authentic tasty nasi lemak. Service is prompt and attentive. I enjoyed my experience here.

Bahn mi -- so hot right now. Fact: before I took the bar exam this summer, I bought 6 sandwiches to eat for every meal so i didn't have to leave the hotel and waste study time. After spending the first 10 years of my life one block away from what I still consider the best bahn mi I've ever had (shout out to the Berryessa King Egg Roll!), the next 17 years driving 15 minutes to get said best bahn mi, and the past few years trying out assorted other sandwich shops, I feel like I have the wherewithal to sort out meh bahn mi from awesome bahn mi. And Baguette Deli has some pretty awesome bahn mi -- ingredients are fresh, bbq pork is tasty, and that bread! The bread is really what sets this sandwich apart from the others I've tried. It's an actual baguette, which is different from the more oblong, shorter sandwich rolls that I've experience. 12 inches! Never a bad thing. I went for lunch on Columbus Day, but there was still quite a crowd and it took a little for the order to come out. But while I was waiting I noticed that they also serve pho at certain times; I'll have to check it out.
Went for lunch. Ordered the vermicelli noodles with grilled pork. Pork was delicious. Reminded me of back home in Bay area. Will return again during my stay in PA.
Absolutely amazing. Best stew chicken ever. Unreal. This is the real deal. Almost forgot we are in the states.

Excellent Food Truck! Loved the Egg Rolls 3 for $5. Totally get what you pay for! The Pad Thai with Beef or Chicken were both off the charts!! Great flavor and nice portion sizes!!! Both times I have ordered the person was friendly and brought the order to my car within 10-12 minutes. Will return for sure!

3 stars because the food is excellent. no complaints there. Hopefully you don't try to have a late lunch there because they don't have listed that they close down from 2-4 in the afternoon. As a hungry patron and employee of a nearby business, i was very sad to discover this when i tried to go during those closing hours.

I have to say I'm surprised that there are not more reviews for this restaurant on the board, but then most people seem to go to Philly for their food. Hmmmm? I guess you might say this is a little hidden spot in the shopping center and easily missed if you do not know it is there. (Near Einstein Bagels, Bravo Pizza. In front of the Acme grocery store in the Paoli shopping center. To the far right of Boston Chicken). I like it here very much as it is QUIET, the food is good, the people are nice and so is the clientele. Bring your own bottle. They have lots of rice dishes that you can have with chicken, shrimp or beef. The same with noodles and the above C, S or B. Then you pour a sauce over it. The grilled shrimp are great. The Pad Thai my daughter tells me is nothing special here. It is a little dull and I'm getting tired of it- it could use more citric juice or something, a few more nuts on top, etc. (I had Pad Thai at the place on the corner in Media and I can now tell the difference. If I remembered the name of the place in Media I would recommend their Pad Thai much more.) But I do enjoy their deep fried sea bass with sauce on the side. It is one of their more expensive dishes at about $27? So compared to that the other dishes running about $15 and up are middle of the road I'd say. Lunch totals about $10-$15 a person. The dishes on special here tend to be just that. Special and prepared fresh. The people in the neighborhood all know about this restaurant and I find that we consider this place to be on our list of "make us feel right at home". You do not need to get dressed UP to go here. I would not consider this a place to bring the kiddies though you could I guess. I come here when I want to meet a friend for lunch or go out with another couple for dinner. In comparison I consider Nectar's to have good food on the whole (pick and chooses), but is extremely noisy, over crowded, overpriced and snobby. They think they are a city restaurant in the burbs. I can go to Philly for that. Hey you might like that? And besides, I remember when it was Pizza Hut.

Best place to eat in Narberth! Coco was recommended to us when we first moved in the neighborhood and I was hesitant because I never eat Thai food. We decided to try takeout and have ordered once a week ever since. Their Coco fried rice with Beef skewers is phenomenal! I've never had better rice- so light yet so flavorful. Everything we tried was very good and nothing is greasy at all!! We love this place!

Stopped in for lunch and decided to go with the buffet. Although they were busy, it was not packed. There were a lot of empty tables. The buffet, however, was like out of everything. They have weird little plastic sheets hovering over the containers in the steam table with just dabs of food in them. The chicken tikki masala had no chicken - just the sauce left, and they never did refill it. The naan was good - and useful for soaking up all that sauce. Waters did not get refilled unless we asked. With all the other great Indian restaurants I have tried in the past couple of weeks here, I don't think I will be back.

WOW! my mouth is on fire! Korean Beef Noodles is very good. We also tried the Potstickers & Korean BBQ Meatballs. Very good. Gavin is the best. He let us sample Spicy Chipotle Adobo & Japan Pan Noodles. We are definitely returning. Recommended
Very sweet service. Home style cooking. Delicious food. Authentic experience with care. enjoyed a lovely experience.
Absolutely delicious. Great food, great service and great find! Will definitely come back again or order takeout!
Had shrimp fried rice that was absolutely perfect. This place is so good and extremely reasonably priced for Thai food. So glad we found this spot right around the corner!

Not sure why previous reviewer said for vegans and vegetarians to be aware, as Momo's has the best veg selection I've found in St. Louis. Most of their tapas is meat-free, and the two times I've been here I've been more than satisfied with the offerings. Now, the vegetarian entrees are sparse, but with so many tapas choices I didn't need an entree. Dolmades, feta, hummus, falafel...all are wonderful and will bring me back again and again. Service is courteous and super fast, no issues whatsoever. This has quickly become a favorite of mine!

Wow! We had the chicken platter with brown chicken stew, curry chicken, and jerked chicken. It also came with a small side salad and rice. It's a big plate, so plan on splitting it. Of the 3, brown chicken stew was my favorite. I wouldn't have ordered it otherwise, but man, I would have missed out. We followed the meal with coconut cake. It was very warm, so the icing just started to melt and ooze between the layers. What a great cake! Soooooooo good. Just wish we lived closer to here so we could visit again. Andre was our waiter, super nice guy and very attentive. Anybody else traveling to Tampa needs to come here and see the envy of the locals.

Nice staff, relaxing dining room on a quiet late afternoon,and BYOB makes it nice for a group. Food was so-so and we'd try someplace else the next time we're in south Philly. Fried calamari looked like we were served the last portion in the place, small portion and small little pieces. Veal saltimbocca had a flavorful sauce but was dry and overcooked; broccoli rabe so overcooked it was unrecognizable, fettuccini Alfredo tough and congealed......all this on a quiet sunday. Can't imagine what they're serving on a chaotic Saturday night. Better dishes were the tender gnocchi with Gorgonzola , and the stuffed artichoke appetizer. Desserts were uneven, with a mud pie frozen dessert being great, but a chocolate cake with peanut butter mousse being dry and tasteless. Would have like cannoli instead of either .... But we're told they ran out of shells the day before.

Just started going to the Blueplate even though I do not live very far from the restaurant. I give high marks to everything about the place. The service is excellent, the food is very good, and the prices are very reasonable. I go for the breakfast. I am a big eater and when I leave food on the plate I know when I am getting my money's worth. High marks all around for this place. Highly recommended if you want to start off your morning with a filling meal.

Someone told me of this place and I went the same day. So glad I did. I thought I would enjoy the meat more, but instantly became a fan of the beans. Price is inexpensive. I will definately visit again.

These folk have the hands of home helping them to create authentic middle eastern specialties as well as all-American wraps, wings, salads and things. From lamb to chicken, beef and salmon, this place serves up generous platters or less. And dang! The best, sizable piece of baklava a being could want. The dining area has a TV that, while muted, detracts from the eat-in atmosphere, though many a student waiting for food will instinctively divert the eyes toward the telly. They're very efficient if you want to bring it home or have it delivered too.

The food was meh. I got one of the taco options and was really disappointed about how bland they were. The same is true of the service; friendly but just meh. The killer for me was the price; for a group of 5 our total came to a whopping $125. Talk about sticker shock. Don't expect chips and salsa for free, it's not. Womp womp all around. Won't be going back.
Don't be scared just because of the location. You'll be greatly rewarded when you order the oxtail and plantains.
