Have been here a couple times at the end of GenCon. This is a good place to come with a large group, since you can easily share dishes. The food was fine, the decor is a bit shabby. But the waiters are very nice!

Food was decent but not as good as Saffron in Ambler or Tiffin. The corn soup was quite good. We ordered a lamb dish and shrimp dish medium hot. The lamb dish had too much flour and was thus too thick but medium hot and the small 8 shrimp Shrimp Tandoor had NO heat despite ordering the same spice level . It was a good groupon deal. Service was very poor. I had to repeat my four letter first name 4 times when I called to make the reservation and she could not describe the dishes well at all. She left the dirty dishes on our table and then when she showed up with the entrees expected us to be the Busboys and hold the dirty dishes up as she handed us the entrees. Once she told me to pass her a dish even though there was plenty of room behind the table for her to get it herself. Bindi, you have no business being a waitress and should maybe wash dishes or be a hostess. The waiter with her seemed to communicate better and genuinely seemed nicer. Food B- Service D.....but good deal with Groupon. Will not return unless there is a coupon with it
Very very poor taste. Rama Rama. Bad biryani. Old food. Bad taste. Not clean place. Poor service.
I really like this place! It's always very easy to get into. The food is delicious, veggies cooked just right and the sauce is always super flavorful. Try it out so it doesn't go out of business!
Veggie feast was awesome, super quick service and really good food. The falafel was cooked exactly how I like it and the tahini sauce on top was a nice finishing touch.

This place is FANTASTIC. I've been here twice, one of the times being a busy Valentine's Day and received awesome service and amazing food. I recommend the trout, but everything I've tried (and sampled from my friend's plates) has been excellent. It is a little pricey, but the ambiance is worth it, especially if you get a booth.
If you want thai food go here. Staff even knows my name and my order (wife and I) and are always super welcoming! Really like their food
Best Thai food I've EVER had including in Thailand!!! Unbelievable. Everything is amazing!!!

Had an amazing dinner here, great new spot! Very cool, trendy vibe, drinks to match. The stuffed grape leaves were delicious, the shrimp were awesome, head-on and super flavorful, very good octopus. Every menu item is packed with tons of layers of flavor, packs a punch. Loved the shredded wheat as a light, perfectly small dessert to finish it off. Highly recommend!

We've been to almost every greek restaurant in NOLA area and this is the BEST GREEK FOOD in town. The gyro platter is my favorite and what i like the most is that the portions are so good that i always take the leftovers home. The falafel is so delicious too. I can eat here everyday :)
Good place to get some rice in St. Louis, affordable and filling, stop by here whenever I'm in town, service always great

I went to the Sansom Kabob House on Saturday night before going out for drinks at Nodding Head. (next door) The place doesn't look like much from the outside but that's the kind of places where you get great and inexpensive food. The inside is fairly simple but inviting and comfortable. I got the lamb kabob and my girlfriend got the Sansom kabob, both were very good. The meat was properly marinated and cooked. You can see the skewered meats cooking when you walk into the place. The rice and salad were also quite good. The only bad thing I could say about this place is that the service was bit slow but they only had 2 people working the whole place. (including the cook, waiter, etc) Food = 4.5 Service = 3.5 Decor = 4 I wanted to comment at some other reviews for this place. In no way does this place deserve a 1 star. If it's busy and there's only 1 waiter working, relax and give them a damn break. It's obviously a small probably family owned operation. For those who thought the food was worth 1 or 2 stars... I'm not sure what you all tasted. My food was fresh and well prepared. As yes there are kabobs that are made out of ground meat...it's not f%cking hamburger meat. If you confusing well seasoned lamb/beef ground meat kabobs with hamburger meat you should probably just go eat at McDonald's.
Great food. Wonderful service. Always have the vegetarian platter with an extra order of salad. Brought the family for my birthday meal once and meat-eaters and not all enjoyed!
Delicious! Mom's Country Fried Beef - is the best.

Hands down, the best egg sandwich in West Philly, maybe even in the city. Only Bui makes it just the way I like it whole wheat + egg whites (spelled "eggs white" on the sign) + sriracha so fast, so cheap, so delicious, I can't get enough, and I rarely order anything else. Spinach is a nice addition, though, if you need some more vegis in your day.

Went there with some friends while in town. It's a unique use of the space, and their selection of shareable apps were great (tried the kale, olives, tzatziki/pita), and the speck sandwich was great (bread and melted cheese was done perfectly). The signature drinks were solid. Only reason for less than 5 stars was service was a little lacking...too suuuuper long time to get our drinks (was 4 of us, and didn't seem overwhelmingly busy), but other than that was good experience.

Is this the best Pho place in the city? I'm not sure but it's darn tasty. I really enjoyed their soup and noodle. Good price as well. Great green onion cakes (tip dip it in the broth) The salad rolls we got (beef and shrimp) were only so so. My favorite part is the name ....heh pho king. heh.

Don't let the rather uninspiring outside fool you. Sitting next to the Go--Kart track it is hard to even find the entrance. But the interior is warm and inviting. The food is more Americanized Asian-Fusion than pure, traditional Thai Cuisine. But it was fresh, served piping hot right from the wok. They seasoned it to the requested heat, which is more than I can say for many establishments. We had the Vegetarian Spring Rolls (good, if uninspired), the Rangoon Crab Appetizer (crab & onion in melted cream cheese stuffed inside a won ton skin and deep fried (YUMMY!) The Thom Yung Kung soup was pleasantly hot without searing the mouth and had plenty of shrimp! The Seafood Combo Pacific Noodles were a bit oily, but, indeed, had plenty of scallops, octopus and shrimp. Overall, a pleasant place. Good value! We'd go back anytime!
Ordered take out from this restaurants and the food was good. Typical South Indian style curry food... good food, good portions... relatively expensive.

Saw the good reviews and thought I would give this place a try. Ordered my favorite Chinese food take out dish, General Tso's chicken. Was not disappointed, absolutely delicious. Will most definitely be back for more.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in town. They have really good lunch prices with most dishes being around $8. I love their pad Thai and panang curry. The tofu and bok choy dish is also REALLY REALLY good. I like really spicy food and they are usually really good at making it the right level of spiciness. Plus their rice comes in triangular pyramids which is a cool touch. They do have weird hours so make sure you check if they are open before you go!

Tried Richards after going to Morrison. Bar was pretty,short pours on scotch and small glasses on martini Hubby ordered lamb and liked It. My short ribs were fatty. The coconut brûlée was good. Caesar salad average. Beet salad was lacking beets. Not on our list to revisit.

Love this place. BYOB. Lao and Thai food. You can get things spicy 1-5 stars. Fair warning, five stars will make you cry. Lots of vegan, vegetarian and gluten free options. This place is great for adventurous eaters. Vietiene has several authentic options that some americans might cringe at; like papaya salad with soft shell crab. That being said they also serve the typical food you would expect to see on a thai menu like green curry or Tom yum soup. I've been going here for years and it's consistently yummy food that anyone could love. Never had a complaint about the service.

My bf and I went on a Wednesday afternoon for lunch. The atmosphere is fun and comfortable. There is in door and out door seeting with large open windows that afternoon. The cuisine is Greek. I am hot and cold on Greek food. I hate olives so that kind of eliminates a lot of the Greek flavors. None the less there were enough items on the menu to satisfy my hunger. As an appetizer we ordered BEEF DOLMADES (ground beef with jasmine rise topped with a saffron aioli in greape leaves). I would not order this again, because I don't typically like grape leaves, and the filling was incredibly salty. I'm not a salt eater. I had the curry chicken salad wrap as my entree and my bf had the gyro omelet. Both were delicious. His omelet was light and fluffy. Filled with gyro meat and cheese, topped with lettuce and sauce. My wrap was filled with a spiced, but not too much, chicken salad which included raisins. Very delicious. After the presentation of the appetizer, I was a bit let down by the presentation of my chicken salad wrap. Just a wrap on the a plate. We had both ordered fries and they came out with the appetizer in a bowl. Nothing fancy. We had a restaurant.com certficate and since we were under the minimum, we opted for dessert. I have the chocolate phillo and he had the peach bread pudding. Let me say...these were both amazing. The chocolate phillo is phillo dough baked with a rich chocolate filling. Services with ice cream, whipped cream, and fruit, all drizzled with chocolate sauce. The peach bread pudding was drizzled in caramel sauce with fruit and whipped cream. I, personally, am not a fan of bread pudding due to texture and consistency, but this was firm and warm. The caramel sauce was a perfect mix with the sweetness of the peaches. When i cut into the chocolate pastry the inner sauce was warm and rich. The entire dish was heavenly. I must say that the presentation was amazing. So very worth every calorie and fat gram. Over all, I would like to return and try some of the dinner items. There was not a belly dancer at lunch, nor was there a need for one. Maybe next time just appetizers and dessert. Mmmm.
The legendary Mac and cheese was some of the tastiest I've had in a while. The chicken tenders were huge and juicy!

Honestly the food here is so good that I would rather not leave. Ever. It's light (even the curries amazingly), the flavors are perfect every time. The spice level is great, too many places are afraid of being too spicy. There is a spicy thai basil dish that you should really try. You can get fresh young coconuts opened and you can drink them with dinner. That is one of my favorite parts about this place honestly. The ONLY problem I have had here is the size of the restaurant (but that really isn't a negative, it never gets loud).

Petra is your local middle eastern hang out with no frills. Menu choices offer regular fare of wraps, kebabs, and salads. The meal came with a starter of marinated veggies and pitta, both of which were good. And then the wait began... Wait staff appeared very relax and hardly moving, it took almost 25 minutes to get the food, although the restaurant didn't look busy at all. I was pleasantly surprised by the shawarma, it actually resembled what I had tasted while traveling in the Middle East, even tahini was used instead of yogurt sauce. My friend had a kebab, which I tasted, it was just ok, nothing to be extra happy about. At the end of the meal I found myself trying to find the waitress again, which was not an easy task to do. The restaurant can benefit from better customer service.

Delicious, full of flavor and the price is comparable to other restaurants in the area. The lady who runs it is an absolute joy & I look forward to my bi-monthly trips here. The saag paneer, bhindi masala and the chana masala are all I order. Along with naan and vegetable samosas. My mouth is just watering thinking about that yummy goodness.
Gus makes great, quality food. His menu changes every day, and come early so he doesn't run out before you. Also, love the tunes.

The pho flavor is great! I wish they added a couple more steak strips though. The spring rolls are delish. I've been to 4 Vietnamese restaurants in the East, West, an Noblesville and this is so far the best I've tried since we move here from Cali.

I went for dinner with 10 people and the food was OK.. but would advice EVERYONE to keep an eye for food prices.. when I received the bill and verified the price against the menu - they overcharged me $3 for every single (6) dish - totaling of almost $20 bucks. When I spoke to the Manager (Owner) - his answer, and I quote "We didn't change the prices on the menu so I am not going to refund you the money back' -- if the owner has to be that rude and not honest about the business - then I am sorry but you are going to loose customers.

my neighbors to the right and left in LA were Indian so every single day the entire hallway smelled like home cooked Indian food straight from their kitchen...and I loved it! this is the 1st Indian joint I hit up since moving to STL cuz once in a while I get these crazy cravings for this stuff. Been here twice, buffet both times. One lunch, one weekend dinner. The flavors were authentic and satisfied my cravings. I think the curries were a bit on the mild side for the buffet in order to cater to the Midwestern taste but everything was tasty and I have been recommending this spot to others. comfortable seating and easy location. come hungry and tear up that buffet and disrespect your toilet in the evening.

This place is awesome! Ive been there twice and both times were for the Early Bird. If you get ther before 6 you can get a great meal for 10 to 12 bucks. The ambiance is great, not by the water but it is very relaxed. The Crem bru le cheesecake dessert there is phenominal!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This was absolutely fantastic!! A huge Vegan menu and plenty to choose from for those meat eaters. Everything is cooked fresh and to order and you can tell. The service was friendly and on point. The food came out quickly. Highly recommend.

My wife and I were vacationing in St Petersburg and were attracted by this restaurant's high rating and rave reviews. I mean to reinforce all of the superlatives. The food was spectacular. My wife had pasta with a rich lobster sauce and I had a dish called La Zuppa, pasta with a pot pouri of seafood. The freshness of the seafood and powerful flavors were unique. No appetizers or dessert. We both ordered a glass (rather generous pour) of Cabernet. Our bill with 20% tip was $95. It was a memorable evening. Very busy on a Monday night. Waitress was busy but still made time to talk to us. Highly recommended.
We just discovered this place and love it! The food is authentic. The value is great.

i ADMIT, I COME OFTEN: because all the food here is wonderful, prices very reasonable and the Owner, Brahim, and his wife, are very lovely people, as is the rest of the staff. Since my first review, I have had the Tagines - The other night the Chicken Tagine with Veggies on top over rice. The rice has a nice fragrance and the sauce/seasoning of chicken is really tender and delectable. I have also had the Chicken Shawarma sandwich before. The pita is light and all the spices are really nice. I love both the soups they offer: The Lentil is nice, but the traditional Harrira is out of this world. MY ADVICE: Come early so you can try the soup. The Mint tea is wonderful after having a nice meal. For Morroccan, I come to Marrakesh. I like to support small businesses where you are like part of the family....and it's great because I live in University City so I can walk home....

The vermicelli bun was alright, but the dish did not have many ingredients. Most noodle bowls I have had at other restaurants are full of a variety of veggies, garlic, etc. I also do not feel the staff was very attentive.
Love this restaurant.. even Indians love it..nearest I've come to a good curry in Indiana ... great service .. great food..?what more does an English girl want

Cool hangout, wings are great and the hookah is even better! The music is loud and not really my style, but the belly dancer was cool. My main complaint is that friends meeting us later arrived around the time the belly dancer was due to perform and couldn't sit in the only available seats I guess they would be "in the way" of the dancer. Understandable, but no other seating was given or suggested. My guests left (along with more money for the business).

Terrible service. I've come here about 15 times and ordered drinks, and I've been frustrated with the service almost every time. The only reason I come here is for the salsa dancing, otherwise I would have never returned. The problem is that it takes them forever to get your drink, even if you're the only person at the whole bar. They just don't care. First, when you go to the bar to order something, they ignore you. Once you order a drink, they just stand around staring for a couple of minutes. Last night I ordered a vodka and pineapple, and I waited about 7 minutes for her to start on my drink. They were busy last night, but there were three bartenders, and they were all moving slowly or just standing around. Before she started on my drink, she took orders from several other people and took care of some bar chores that didn't seem crucial. I tried to get the attention of one of the other bartenders. I told her about the situation and she did not acknowledge that there was a problem or anything. I will say that I have had the coquitos twice, and it was pretty good. It was really good the first time, but too sweet the second.

The two stars are for the ambiance and the fact that my dinner guest's meal was good (I tasted some of her rice, it was really well seasoned). However, I ordered the Bamia (tomatoes and okra) and it was really bland (both the rice and the sauce). I politely asked the waitress for hot sauce and she seemed reluctant to give it to me and then asked if I thought it was bland. I tried to politely tell her it was and she seemed shocked and said no one had ever said that about the dish. When she came back with the hot sauce she said that the chef was fasting for Ramadan and perhaps that was the reason (I assume this means he isn't tasting the food). The hot sauce did what hot sauce does and I ate the meal. I would have given three stars if the service was better but it wasn't great (think kids working for their parents). I'm disappointed because this is close and the ambiance is great but this will probably be a pass in the future.
I will no stars for this place,there is no flavor in gyro plate and the rice is way undercooked I had to throw out 2 gyro plates I bought Fries are soggy as well I would not recommended this place

Kalamatas has outstanding food. Every Greek place that I go to, I immediately compare it to Kalamatas. It sets the standard as far as I'm concerned. The gyro plate (or pocket) is outstanding, and the Greek salad is very, very tasty. Fresh ingredients, friendly staff. I like both the Green Hills and Brentwood locations.

My first venture into PHO. Yelped this place after an airport run with my daughter. Basic chairs and tables, no biggie. very casual. Friendly service. Awesome Pho. Yeah it's my first bowl ever, but boy was it good. THe broth is awesome and the various meats are tender and delicious. Very cheap considering the quality.
Warm and inviting-- the space and the people. The food was eclectic and the flavor combinations intriguing. Quite vegetarian friendly as well. We'll definitely return.

My Cucina Zapata withdraw was severe after they closed for the winter break. I was so stoked to go back and get my favorite Sweet Potato Curry. I wanted to prepare the cash payment AFTER ordering. Then I came to realize that MY WALLET WAS LEFT AT HOME. The embarrassment to tell them that to hold off my order because that situation was real!! The master cook Nico of the truck said that "no worries, just pay us back next time". As they knew that I was a regular and loyal customer. This is the exceptional service that keeps bringing their customers back!!

Glad I actually got to sit down and have a meal here finally. Staff was very friendly greeted you as soon as you walked in. Atmosphere is relaxed good place a group of friends can go and get some good food at a decent price. I had the Pad Thai mild with steak and shrimp very good and fresh. I also had the fried egg roll which were great! Loved these sweet and sour dipping sauce. Fresh, hot and full of yummy veggies. I also tried the Thai Sweet Tea, def. a new fave. I do want to go back and tried the desserts though. The of Thai was big around $9.95 I believe, i took home another portion so def. a two meal deal really. Egg rolls $3.95 also took one home. Place was clean and low lighting. I'll def. be going back, right down the street from my house I believe I found my NO cook nights place to go

I love this place..I cant seen to stay away from my Indian cuisine. I was in Media for court and I was hungry for something yummy. They I all of a sudden i had Indian in my mind. The small amount of items in the buffet lunch is great. The have some of my favorite items such as Chicken masala, tandori chicken and acouple more. I could not leave with out having a mango lassi. I cant wait to go back.
Fantastic, quaint, and welcoming! Most things can be made vegetarian, which means many options to choose from. I especially enjoyed the banana chocolate spring rolls.
Olio was awesome! The decor, the staff, and food were great! I would highly recommend

Quite simply, this food truck is amazeballs. Yes, this is a Thai Mexican fusion truck. An undeniable awesome marriage between two of my most favorite cuisines. I swung by to try their famous Cap'n Crunch crusted tilapia burrito but I ended up ordering their entire menu. And I wasn't even hungry! THAI SHORT RIBS TACOS (1 for $3)- Tender yet perfectly chewy. The flavors literally burst in your mouth letting you know these meats were given a good marinade bath before it was cooked. Generous slices of avocado canopying the filling of veggies like shredded cabbage and cubed tomatoes. And oh my, that green sauce.....creamy, yet light and refreshing. CHICKEN KATSU W/ AN EGG ($5.50) Extremely crispy, thin flat cutlet of well-cooked chicken served with a bed of slaw, a fried egg, rice, and spicy mayo drizzle. Ask for extra sauces! CAP'N CRUNCH CRUSTED TILAPIA TACOS (2 for $6)- The disadvantage of coming here late to avoid the long lines was that they ran out of burritos' ingredients. However, they accommodated us by making us a taco instead! Made with the same love as the ribs tacos, except with the crunchy, slightly sweet breading, and delicious flaky fish inside! I don't generally expect good service from a food truck. But the people who work here go above and beyond with their genuine helpfulness and friendliness. I was super impressed with my entire experience. I only spent $15 for all of that deliciousness and I was 100% satisfied.

This has been my favorite restaurant in Indianapolis for four years now, and I will tell you why: SOUR SOUP WITH SHRIMP. I will start by saying that I have never had any of their Chinese food. I've eaten here with people who have ordered fried rice or sesame chicken or what have you, and it never looked all that impressive. But the Vietnamese food, you guys, oh my GOD. I have had Vietnamese food at Saigon, King Wok, Viet Bistro, Sandra Rice and Noodle, and four or five other places, and I don't like any of them as much as I like this place. I do usually order the goi cuon, which are always fresh and accompanied by a little peanut-topped brown sauce that I end up eating with a spoon (I have low blood pressure, okay? Yeah. That.), but my favorite thing (even more than the delicious, delicious, delicious pho) is the sour soup with shrimp. If you order it, trust me, get a small. I haven't ever seen the large size, but it must come in a bucket. The small comes in this hot pot thing with Sterno smoldering underneath, and it makes a very satisfying crackling sound as you eat it. The soup contains tomato, pineapple, some kind of vegetable that kind of reminds me of celery if it was made of sponge, tomato, herby leafy bits, and the shrimp. It's a little sour, a little spicy, and it is so freaking good. I actually want to eat it right now. Too bad they aren't open at 5 am. I will warn you, the ambiance is...not awesome. It's kind of a seat-yourself place, and there are no tablecloths or anything. But! The food is TOTALLY worth it. I love the waitstaff and the cooks in the kitchen, who always wave hello to me. And by the way, I'm MSG sensitive, and maybe it's because I love this place so much, but I've never had a headache or anything after eating here. Very glad this place is in Indy. Love it!
Yes it is ironic sir that i opened a yelp account to rate the bad customer service of your restaurant.
I find the food great. Large portions (not that this is a plus, just a fact). Nice staff. They put a lot of effort into the food.

Since the remodel, the food isn't as carefully prepared. The drink glasses are too small for iced tea. The decaf tea is gone. All the friendly people have disappeared. We went once a week but will probably not go anymore. Too bad.

The best service I have ever had by far, and I have been to countless restaurants over the last 5 years. I consider myself a foodie and the food was impressive. Higher quality Jamaican food. The atmosphere and ambience was upscale, clean, and great background music. Great food, excellent service, and all around top notch experience. I'm happy to support a great small business that deserves these accolades. I don't like writing reviews but I was compelled to write after the experience we just had. Enjoy!!

I was absolutely taken aback by the price you pay for the amount of food that you get. $12 for a gyro? 4 ounces of meat piled with lettuce, and scant amount of feta that had no flavor. For 7 dollars in Chicago you can get a gyro piled high with meat. I will say that the collared were outstanding. You get four of them for $8 and they were filled with meat and nicely seasoned. Aside from the value, the worst experience was my service. I got a waitress named Tina who couldn't wait to get me out of the restaurant. She didn't ask me how my meal was, she didn't ask me if I wanted dessert. I needed an extra napkin, and she was nowhere to be found until my meal was finished . The minute I had finished my gyro, with 2 appetizers left on my table she brought my check over. I told her I would like to order a salad to go. She looked at me like I was from another planet. I had to repeat it a couple of times. I have gotten friendlier service from a body search at the airport. I would never come back to this restaurant. I was traveling out of town and this was my first time at this place. Cannot recommend it at all. Overpriced not flavorful, terrible service. I watched other waitresses behaving similarly and people were paying these prices for crappy service. Your mileage may vary
one of our favorite places in media- casual BYOB with great food- never need reservations- service is great. Perfect date night spot.

I mean, I knew it was going to be good. I had seen the glowing reviews, I've met Anney on a number of occasions because I work nearby, so I was aware of her dedication to the craft. What I didn't know was how much Id like it...all of it; visually aurally, olfactory and most importantly gastronomical. Chaat and Chai is an amusement park for your senses. Previously, I've had an aversion to most Indian food. I just never took to the taste of curry. Turns out, I've only been exposed to generic curry because what Anney is creating is sublime. My first impression of C&C was awe and wonder. Bright colors, umbrellas and murals just jump out at you, the music is inviting and sets the mood for the experience to come. (Forgive me here because I don't remember the names and descriptions of all of the food I ate. I'll do my best.) We started with the Samosas and the Lentils with roti. We had a vegetarian in our party so this worked for everyone. I just was surprised at how much I liked it especially the bread (we ended up ordering more). I was just going to politely try the lentils (I've never been a huge fan) but I found myself going back for more and more and was disappointed when it was gone. We all made quick work of the samosas as well. For my entree, I ordered the city famous short ribs. I was not at all disappointed by the meal that Craig Leban said is one of the best in the city. Short ribs in curry with onions and other spices, in sort of a roti wrap. Honestly, I don't have much idea what was in there , I just know it was fantastic. I did sample some of my friend's Lamb dish. The heat profile was through the roof , which I quite enjoyed. I might try that one next time. I didn't try my other friends vegetarian meal but she seemed to enjoy it immensely. I should point out that the young lady that served us and the rest of the small spot was efficient and lovely. Overall this was one of the best dining experiences I've had in Philly. Definitely don't pass up a chance to check it out.
Best Asian-Fusion food in Washoe County. I have to get lunch here every time I'm in town. Keep it up SF Kitchen your rocking it !!!!
Great Pakistani restaurant. Food taste amazing. I tried almost half of his menu so far and not disappointed. I wish there is more seating. But still great new addition.

UPDATE 04/22/16: Still amazed with quality and taste! You can't go wrong with Indian food, but here you also get warming atmosphere and shining and welcoming smile of the owner's wife. You're greeted like a special guest every time, and that's exactly what makes us and our friends coming back here again and again. They did a great job and they still doing this -- they keep improving and improving. Well, full Friday nights will say better that me! For those who don't know where to start: start with garlic shrimps. They. Are. Amazing!

Wow, I dreamed that I reviewed this place. Since ya'll aren't in my dreams, I'll recap here. Once I found out that Jamaican Style Jerk was otherwise known as 'the carryout place on 34th and Keystone attached to the liquor store that used to be a Shell' I knew I had to stop there. I picked up some curried goat, rice and peas and plantains (I asked specifically about them), plus a ginger beer. I was on my way to work, and didn't sample it until I got there, and it was on and popping after that. Super awesome curry, perfectly cooked meat, and I couldn't stop eating. Oh goodness, I couldn't stop! My mom stopped through randomly and I gave her my plate, with the exhortation to get it out of my sight so I could stop eating and start working. She did- and that was the last I saw of my curry, sniff. She said the rice was calling to her. All I know is, it's calling to me, and I want to answer! The only reason that a 5 star wasn't given is that their hours are short, but that's a minor pick. Go! Eat! Love!

Traveled to Tampa for work the other day and stumbled upon this hidden gem. From the moment you walk in, you immediately are taken back from its great ambiance and decor. The team there is extremely friendly and courteous. They make you feel like family. The food is A1! Everything I tried was perfectly seasoned and tasted amazing. I wish I lived here as I'd stop to have a meal every week!
I love this place and getting the nadia duck definitely reminded me of what I missed . The drunken noodles are fantastic and great with almost every main entree. The best Thai in the area, for sure.

Had the jerk chicken, and it was fantastic! Great flavor! The service was quite good. It's a family owned restaurant, so the dad seated us, the son was our waiter, and the mom's cooking was delicious! I recommend this place, and I'll be going back next time I am in town.

The food was fabulous and flavorful! There aren't many places in Boise I can eat out because of food restrictions, but Ishtar I can. The service was good when we were there....I'll be happy to go back. Interesting market too!
Above average Pho, just never enough meat in my opinion. Always have had good service there and it's a clean, professional place. Lunch special is a great go-to if you're uptown.

As far as a breakfast sandwich at a food truck can go, this is the best it could get in my opinion. I had turkey bacon with egg and cheese on their longer rolls with some creamy sriracha sauce. First of all, the fillings were incredible, but its hard to mess up egg and cheese. The bread was what really set Bui's apart. I've yet to have another breakfast sandwich with such delicious and fresh bread. Will go back for sure.

We stopped in the other night, and had some of the best Indian food ever! This place had been completely redone since it was Lucky Dog. The tables had clean white tablecloths and were set apart so there was plenty of space to get around. The Chili Chicken appetizer was unique and delicious. The crispy garlic naan, mixed pickles, and mango lassi were all excellent. The vegetarian dish of cauliflower, peas, and other vegetables, without cream was very tasty and had some of the freshest vegetables ever. The tandoori lamb chops were very tender and flavorful. Even the dessert, gulab jamin, was a cut above the usual. Our server, Raziv (spelling?) could not have been more friendly or accommodating. The owner/chef Nabim came out to greet us enthusiastically. Even the prices were more reasonable than we were used to elsewhere. We had a most pleasant and tasty experience.
Worst food I have ever had in an Indian restaurant. The food over here seems to be a nightmare for vegetarians. I strongly suggest to skip this.

This place is right down the street from my job and occasionally I get their lunch special. The food is really good, but pricey. I would only ever get the lunch special because it's such a good deal (and I don't have tons of money to splurge on eating out). Their chicken pad thai and jasmine rice soup are delicious! The food is ready quickly and the staff is very friendly. I would definitely recommend tier lunch special--you get a soup or salad with entree for $13.

This really is the best Gyro in New Orleans, and probably the best I have had in my life! I do not gush about stuff that is not good, or that is good but not great. this is great. You would not think it when entering this hole in the wall. I have not had the chicken gyro or any of the other dishes, so I cannot attest to their quality. But I have had the Gyro twice and it rocks. Grab one and go to the divey bar across the street for a 2 buck beer. You will not be sorry.

Wonderful place for authentic Mediterranean food! The owners are super sweet and personable, the menu accommodates both vegetarian and gluten-free diets, the portions are generous, and the prices are very reasonable. While you can dine in with your meal, it's probably better to do delivery or carry out, since the space is rather small. Hopefully the owners will expand soon, because this is food worthy of a proper sit-down meal.

I have never had pho so subpar. I think the broth was just not very good. I hear it's a chain restaurant and they have a very extensive menu, but no one in our party enjoyed our meal here. Save your money and go to Pho ha a few blocks away.
Best place to have lunch on a weekday in Creve Coeur. Good food, good service. This place deserves to be packed at lunch. Very very tasty

This place rocks. Hope you go!! Newly opened right in town. My new fave place for Vietnamese Spring rolls; more than excellent: delicate wrap, fried to perfection, filling was fabulous, with wood ear mushrooms. Garlic Shrimp noodles were fabulous. Shrimps huge and meaty and tasty. Took most of it home and it was even better heated up two days later!! Wow. Will definitely be back to try more.

A real neat spot with a beautiful interior. This is a review for brunch. I have no idea about the dinner service but I have to believe it is comparable. A few thoughts - 1. This place gets VERY busy on the weekend. We just beat the rush, and you might want to consider eating early. 2. Do not miss the cruller. I repeat, DO NOT MISS THE CRULLER. it is light, airy and delicious. Rose pistachio. Must have, worth the trip alone. 3. The coffee is excellent. I often judge a brunch location based on the quality of their bottomless cup of coffee. it tells you if they are cutting corners or how much pride they are taking in the program. The Stumptown roast they use is of high quality and is an excellent compliment to the food. 4. All of the food we had was delicious and everything around us looked delicious as well. Add an egg to your manoushe. 5. Those bowls. They are beautiful, but unfortunately everything in my house has to be able to go in the dishwasher. No handwash only items for me. That being said they are worth taking a look at.

We loved this great new concept area near the IUPUI campus! We walked in an ordered the rice bowl which is what I always get at chipotle and Qdoba. The chicken and lamb were amazing and the they let us get half sag and Tikka Marsala. We loaded it up with toppings and also some interesting sauces. I would definitely recommend!

I love Ethiopian food, so I try to find one in the cities I travel to. I took some coworkers here for lunch and was a bit dissapointed. The Injera was dry and a bit unappealing. The lentils were very dry and lacked flavor. The buffet they had out seemed like it was not very fresh. I usually wouldn't get the buffet but if you ordered off the menu, I'm pretty sure you would have just gotten what was on the buffet anyways. I am a bit spoiled because of the amazing Ethiopian restaraunt I am used to in Raleigh, but I would not go back to this restaraunt.

Had this just now at a Philly Food Truck Festival. As I wait for the wife to finish eating just thought I'd drop a wore of praise for this amazing jerk chicken. Had it with the rice & beans plus the yams. All of it was great, thanks guys. I've been on a search for decent jerk since my trip to Jamaica and I never found any in Chicago. This food truck definitely delivered, I don't even mind that the spices are making me sweat even more in this 95 degree heat. Cheers.

Great Caribbean cuisine and good customer service brings us back to this West Philly nstitution everytime. We like the baker Joseph Clarke especially, he is the best and Reynaldo is great. Good food with a Trinidadian vibe and a West Indian irie !!!

Found about them today, saw great pics on IG and was convinced! Sent my boyfriend to pick us up a few things since he works in the area (he was less than convinced to say the least... Lol! it is a truck after all)..... He had a little trouble finding it because he went down Chestnut instead of Market but said the guy on the truck was really cool and said they could also make any dish over rice as opposed to a taco. He calls me 5 mins after getting our food (2 fish burritos and one veggie burger) and says please get online right now and write a review saying this is the best fish taco I have ever had in my life... He meant burrito but was obviously have a foodgasm.... Now I am praying mine makes it back and looking forward to writing another glowing review when I have had a chance to taste... PS. I was shocked by his enthusiasm because he is not easy to please when it comes to trying new places!! This was a total success!!

I got this as delivery to my hotel through the DIningin website. The delivery was prompt and pleasant. Of the food I got, the saag paneer was definitely my favorite--it was perfectly seasoned and just the right texture. The Lamb Korma was very tasty, too, but the sauce was a little watery.

How this place stays in business is baffling, even with its location. The food was disgusting and way overpriced. I managed a few bites before throwing it away and just writing off my $10. Spend your money elsewhere.

I ordered chicken wings, chicken fried rice, and crab rangoon to go. It was a bit pricey for just these 3 items. The rice tasted fishy and the veggies were a little raw for my taste. Chicken wings were spot on without being greasy. The crab rangoon was by far the best tasting ones I've ever had. Service was courteous and quick. I may try something else if I order again.

What a fantastic experience! We had the #3 under the lamb options (although a little drier than I expected) and we had queen of 8 (I can't remember the exact name but it's the sampler option for $15 per person), which comes with 2 chicken portions, 2 need portions and 4 of their vegetable portions, all the chef's choice. The food is eaten with their bread, although they give you a fork if you feel more comfortable eating with a fork instead of your hands. This place has a nice small ambiance with soft music playing in the background. The servers wear typical attire and are all very kind and helpful. Our server, Claris was extra great! She was so patient with us and made sure we got an array of food choices. She was willing to ask the chef what would come with our sampler dish to make sure we weren't ordering double of anything. We really appreciated her hospitality. They made sure our water glasses were always filled and she was still quick even when the place started to pick up in business. I would love to come back. It's a great place for those looking for responsible priced vegetarian and vegan dishes. All the plates have excellent taste and flavor. I was pleasantly surprised.

You know when the Pho craze started a few years ago you always heard about those "meh" places that were riding on the coattails of the pho hype? Yes, this feels like it was one of them. I went with a large satay soup. The broth was overly salted and uninspiring, the size was medium at best and amount of toppings left me disappointed. I think I will skip this place next time.
What a surprise! From the exterior I expected a very casual noodle take out place. It's a lovely full service cafe, mostly Thai and lots of Asian noodle and rice dishes. Lunch special is a deal!
Started coming here 3-4 months ago. Wife and I are addicted to the Pho and Spring Rolls. If you are looking for something a little different to than the normal fair. Give it a try!!

I'm very happily surprised by Santorini's! This restaurant is in the UCEN of UCSB and unique as there aren't many Mediterranean cuisines in this area. I wasn't going in expecting much since it is a restaurant on campus but it exceeded my expectations! I got the gyro plate and it includes the meat, 2 sides (I chose veggies and salad) there is also rice and fries, and a pita bread cut into 4 pieces. Please look at the images as they have photos of this meal. The meat is VERY tender and well flavored. It tastes as it has been marinated for a long while and care was put into this dish. The side salad was delicious and I'm a huge fan of the grilled veggies that holds a lot of flavor as well. the plate is very filling and all this for $8.07 including tax! As this is located in the UCEN where there is a lot of traffic during the lunch hour, the service is very fast and efficient. Overall I'll definitely be back and I want to try their $1 Wednesday breakfast special from 7-9!

We came on a busy Sunday and had a decent meal, mixed reviews of the food across the dinner. We loved the appetizers, great calamari, decent escargot and an amazing salad special of grilled romaine with strawberries balsamic, pine nuts and blue cheese. Entrees - I tried 2 of the specials. The veal shank (Osso boucco) in red sauce that was quite disappointing. The red sauce drowned the veal and the risotto and was not powerful enough for the meat. The shank itself had great flavor and texture. The risotto was completely drenched in sauce so I could not really taste it as such. The other entree I tried was a crusted salmon that was just OK. Presentation was nice. We had 4 deserts a great bread pudding and Tartoufoo, a bad cheese cake and an a decent chocolate cake. Service was OK - not bad not great - again you can do much better in Philly. I am a little bummed because the good dishes were really good. For the price I think you can do much better in Philly. I would try this place again in the hopes I was there on an off night.

Small casual dining place not too far from Washington Univeristy. Really good Indian-Pakistani food. Fresh chapatee. Loved it. Great service. We had a couple of hours to kill before catching our connecting flight at STL so decided to go for lunch - well worth the effort.

We enjoyed a late lunch here. Our order consisted of: 2 pieces of the white meat breast 4 wings 1 biscuit A sample of the Mac and cheese 2 sodas 1 chocolate peanut butter hand pie The chicken was slightly tough and was not freshly prepared. But the buttermilk pretzel coating was still very good. I think the chicken would have been better if it was cooked per order. The biscuit was really good, but again could have been fresher. The Mac and cheese was some of the best I have ever had. I will definitely order some when I go back. The unique selection of sodas were very good. We tried the cola, watermelon cream soda, the birch bear and the huckleberry. They also had a nice selection of bottled soft drinks. The selection of desserts was amazing including a variety of baked hand pies, cookies, and brownies. I don't think you could go wrong with any of the dessert selections. If the chicken was cooked fresh to order this place would be unbeatable!

The other day, I got the hankerin' at lunch for some good Asian. Did a little investigating and the Sizzling Wok came up highly recommended. Took the short drive over and didn't know what to think going in... but, was pleasantly surprised. Let's dive in. First, the restaurant is very clean; I really like when a restaurant goes the extra mile to keep the place looking good. And for the typical Chinese/Asian restaurant, Sizzling Wok is ahead of the pack. Sat down and the server was very prompt, friendly, and communicated very clearly. I ordered some pork egg rolls to start and the duck soup with egg noodles (pho). The egg rolls were tightly packed and perfectly breaded, served with a nice red pepper sauce, these might be the best egg rolls I've ever had. The Duck Soup came out and was steaming with the savory smells of duck. This is served in a deep bowl with chop sticks and a nice serving spoon for finding those nice chunks of duck on the bone. The duck cuts are the cuts you would use for a stew; a bit tough on the bone, but packed with flavor. The mushrooms and noodles were very tasty, as well. Although I did not go with any of the lunch specials, it was a little pricier than I would have liked, but I did go with a hearty entree (the lunch specials are very reasonable, $5-$7). I might have those hankerin's for good Asian more often.

Blu Fig may be a smaller establishment tucked away in the middle of nowhere, but for those of us living on the outskirts of Nashville, it's an amazing option. I was hesitant to try it because I can be a picky eater and it's not much to look at from the outside, but one bite of the hummus had me intrigued and the falafel pocket made me a convert. My mother and I love to go together or just order two falafel pockets to go - I'm sure the other menu items are phenomenal, but I can't pass up the falafel to try them! We're also huge fans of the bubble tea, which is an atypical, smoothie-like beverage with either traditional or bursting boba. There are quite a few different flavors and they will even let you mix them together - I had the pineapple-coconut blend on my last visit and it was to die for. The prices are fantastic, the service is quick and friendly, and the food is far better than I would have expected. Also, to my great surprise, they have one of the nicest bathrooms I've ever seen! It's definitely worth a visit, even if you have to drive a while.

Delicious food, great service, and amazing menu pages long, couldn't complain about anything. Very many varieties with different levels of spice for you to try. Great atmosphere, comfy tables. Great place to bring family or friends for something new and exciting!

I come for shaved ice . Variety flavor of it makes me happy. I once was very addicted to green tea shaved ice. Best food they have is chicken wings with sticky rice and papaya salad Laos style but it will kill u lol I love it
Cheap and very good phad thai. Very cute and quiet restaurant.

Thai Taste is in a typical location: Strip mall. The decor is minimal and predictable, the lighting a bit dark. The service is absolutely fantastic - A+. I ordered the Yum Woon Sen salad - a mix of thin glass noodles, cilantro, crushed peanuts, red onions, chili paste and lime juice, served on a bed of lettuce. For degree of hotness I specified medium - which was actually quite spicy. Our waitress also brought us out an assortment of three medleys of spices (all hot) The dish itself was fairly tasty and came with a simple Thai salad of iceberg lettuce, cucumber and a thin, sweet dressing. ***WARNING: For those of you with tender tastebuds intolerant of high degrees of heat, stay within the "Mild" range of spiciness. Do not... DO NOT order the "Native Thai. In fact, don't even order Medium. I would only come here again because my best friend swears by this place - and as I mentioned, the service was genuine and prompt.

Had breakfast on a Saturday, busy but no wait. Interesting specials and regular standards available. The omelet was a little overcooked for my taste (crispy) but the Apple sausage was great. Good potatoes and toast. Coffee was ok. My friend had the bread pudding and it was amazing.

Don't be fooled buying a Groupon voucher for $60, me and my husband bought a voucher towards $60 and said we couldn't use it for the $40 since there was only 2 of us. No where on Groupon did it say it we had to have 4 people. Food is way over priced for what it is. Nothing special. Wish Yelp allowed us to give no stars.
Loved the place! Service and food were great! Very clean and cozy! Comfortable location. For sure coming back!!

My first experience here was ordering take out with a friend. The person taking the order on the phone was apparently kind of rude, but honestly the food was really good. I have since eaten in the restaurant two more times and have actually had very good service. The pho is done well and is fairly priced averaging $6.50 to $8 per bowl. And surprisingly the Vietnamese taco (I know the name is weird) is very good. It has super tasty marinated barbecue meat with veggies in a soft rice bun served with plum and siracha sauce on the side. I highly recommend the taco.

Super amazing Korean food and sushi! The owner was super nice and friendly! They even made an authentic Korean sushi roll for my husband that was not even on the menu. We will definitely be return customers!

After going to the one on 2nd and finding the air conditioning was broke and it smelled like a fish market we located this one assuming the food would be the same. WRONG! Service was unfriendly and nearly threw the hummus on the table at us. While sitting outside around 9:30 at night I was told I couldn't smoke however had to eat among peoples dogs sitting around me. The hummus was the most bland Ive ever had and we added salt, pepper and even hot sauce to try and make it better. My SO had linguine with fresh plum tomato sauce again lacked any spice or flavor. The only reason this place gets 2 stars is for the shrimp pil pil and the lamb meatballs which were both done very well. No sides come with the shrimp or pasta, everything is a la carte. Rude service, less then average food for over an hour wait. I would never come back.

Let me preface this review by saying, Basil Spice used to be the go-to restaurant on south Grand for my husband and I. This used to be our number one pick to eat out together for about 7 years. However, I have been significantly disappointed when eating there in the last 6 months. We had not eaten there in a while when we invited my in-laws to dinner at Basil Spice. We recommended sharing 3 plates or so with the table (since portions used to be quite generous), but they preferred to each get a meal. Thank-goodness, because somehow, although prices had not decreased, the portions on the plates had shrunk to about 1/2-2/3 the size they used to be. We continued to patronize the restaurant, although the decreased meal portions happily encouraged us to explore some of the other Thai/Vietnamese options around (and we found some other restaurants we now prefer). Then in February 2015, we invited a couple to dinner. My husband left a 15% tip (we were paying for both couples, so the check was more than usual). Sadly, when I reconciled our bills (I keep all receipts), my records for that meal didn't match with our credit card statement. Instead of the 15% we put down, we were charged a 20% tip! (I looked back and found the receipt to verify this.) I'm afraid we will not continue to eat at Basil Spice unless there is some extraordinary circumstance or gathering... nor can I now recommend it to my friends. :-(

Wow, was in St Pete Beach for a week and this was by far the best meal I had. Very good wine selection. The tuna martini was an excellent appetizer. The salad included with the entree was amazing, and I'm not a big salad fan. For my entree, had the fish of the day, Chilean sea bass, prepared in the Tangine style, the house specialty. Wow is all I can say. Another person in my group had the lamb shank prepared Tangine style as well. The meat was falling off the bone, it was amazingly tender. The creme brulee and profiterole were outstanding.

The food was soo good; interesting & unique marriage of southeast Asian with contemporary southern. Everything was fresh with lots of local & seasonal ingredients; the flavor profiles of dishes was well-balanced and perfectly executed. Casual atmosphere. Went with a group of friends and enjoyed how easy it was for "family-style" dining (sharing the portions around). Will definitely return!
The perfect meal: saag panner, cheese naan, falooda, and orange delight! Absolutely amazing!

This place is a diamond in the ruff. The food was amazing and the owners were friendly. I will definitely come back. We had the brown stew chicken, fried chicken wings, short ribs, jerk chicken wings and Lima bean soup. There was silence in the house while everybody are and enjoyed. Portions were generous and you will enjoy. So GOOD!!!

We've been looking for good Arabic food in Tampa, so when I Yelp'ed restaurants nearby when leaving Busch Gardens we decided to give it a try. We ordered a hummus appetizer and 2 lamb gyros. Each were OK, but we basically concluded we are unlikely to come again. The hummus had way too much tahini which overwhelmed the chick pea taste and the oil poured on top was quite mediocre. The gyro meat appeared to be hand sliced, but very bland.

Man, I hate having to leave less-than-positive reviews but I gotta be honest, this was some of the weakest Thai food I've ever had. I am baffled by its 4-star rating. My husband ordered the BBQ lamb and tom yum soup, and I got the Chu Chee Duck. The lamb: cooked well, but a very small portion for the price. And the sauce seemed like a bottled bbq sauce. The noodles were ok -- I mean, hard to screw up plain noodles -- but the veggies were boring beyond measure. The soup: basic tom yum. Not bad but also not memorable. The duck: honestly? Kinda lousy. EXTREMELY overcooked, at turns tough and stringy or dry and mealy. The red curry was extremely weak... The menu indicated a spicy dish but man, it was definitely not. It tasted like someone took a proper red curry and then mixed a bunch of milk in. Not much flavor at all. And beneath the poor, ruined duck, swimming in the so-called curry were the same uninspired and slightly overcooked veg my husband had. For a $60 meal it was overall very underwhelming. I'm leaving a 3-star rather than 2-star review because at least the service was good. I'd put the food at 2 and the service at 4, if we could rate them separately.

Food wise, my meal here last night ranks in top 5 worst restaurant dishes of my life. Tuna tacos that were tasteless, mushy, and cold. The textures of the tuna and mango within the tacos were identical. The dish needed crunch, acid, heat, salt...anything! Also, the tuna had so much connective string that I couldn't even bite through it. It was absolutely disgusting. My friend had the mussels which I didn't try. She said that they were just ok. We sat on the patio and were packed in so tightly to the table behind us that I was jostled throughout the entire meal. The table was incredible wobbly. On the plus side, the drinks were good. Service was fine. I will not be returning here for food!

Visiting St. Louis for work, and being from San Francisco was skeptical about getting good Thai food in middle america. I stand corrected, Thai Country Cafe was delicious from the crabmeat ragoons (OK, those are midwestern) to the chicken satay. I had the cashew sauce rice plate with chicken that was so good I couldn't stop eating it. Great little spot, I loved the whacky decor too. It's sort of Bonanza meets your grammar school best friends refinished basement.

Everything was delicious, from the salad to the finger lickin pork baby back ribs. I have been to this restaurant when it was scampis, It's not the best location, so I hope it is a success. Liam the owner and chef came to our table and introduced himself, he is very nice. I wish him all the luck in the world!

Get Vietnamese Coffee with grass jelly Or try the Green Tea with honey & basil seeds with lychee jelly!!!!! Their Thai Salad is good & sandwiches too... they no longer have shave ice - if your in a hurry call the order in or call Togo

The sushi was great very fresh, and the plum wine was good. In enjoyed the atmosphere. I also had the orange chicken. Overall good experience, and will be returning (especially since they are always on Groupon)

First visit I had the drunken noodle, last visit I tried the pad ginger. Thai spring tools and edamame for appetizers. Went with a group of friends both times and everyone loved their meals. Always pleased with the food here!
Chicken Carma is bomb! You have to pay for extra rice though. Tiki masala was delicious and had a smoked flavor. Overall great service and food. Order a mango lassi!

The Jerk Chichen was AMAZING!! I ordered a large with mac'n'cheese and candied yams. The whole thing was fantastic and was a TON of food. Definitely a good bang for your buck. The chicken was extremely supple and fell off the bone. The spices were fantastic and multiple people in my office came up and commented on how delicious it smelled. Be warned though... the Jerk Chicken isn't for the feint of heart. It packs a mighty punch and leaves your mouth with a strong burn. But its sooo worth it. Definitely check this place out!
Delicious and very fresh Pho! I'm tried many pho spots in Jersey but this may be a new favorite! Great and attentive service as well. Will definitely come back.
Pad Thai was horrible. Too sweet for my taste. I had way better Thai food. Service was good though.

Nice people. Knowledgeable waitstaff, good service coordination Made for a pleasant experience..Menu varied but not large. Preparation was spot on. BYOB handled seamlessly.. Party of four seated quickly. Prime time on a Friday seems to be after seven. Got a bit loud with a full house but dining rooms are small. Will make a second visit.
Best Gyro's I've ever had. Also, I don' t think you can go wrong with the desserts. Everyone at our table also raved about the various ones they ordered.

Food was very good, place is neat and clean but not the friendliest or most knowledgeable staff. The young waiter was very friendly but clueless about the menu. I asked a few questions about the food and he didn't know nor seeked the answer elsewhere. The lady in the front didn't say hello when I entered or thanks for coming as I exited. But the food was very good so I'd give them another try.
Absolutely delicious! Best Jamaican place in all of Tampa. Family owned and awesome. Easy to locate. Adequate parking. Did I mention the food amazing. Whole family enjoyed it.

Fantastic food. They make authentic South Indian food. I had the egg dosa and it was really good. Just the right balance of spices. They also have a full "thali" which has a fair number items. Highly recommend it. We will be coming back here again soon.
Delicious Thai food, with fast and friendly service. Great option for my sister who is vegan. We got panag curry and supreme tofu.

Reservation would be good. We didn't make reservation on busy Friday evening, but the host asked us to wait for 10 minutes and were seated. I had seafood pasta and snails. The portion was generous and the service was friendly. But I would pick Pesto over this place.

So I've been here twice now, and I have to say it is really just OK. Positives include the service and a great guy who may or may not be an owner. Also, the veggie dumplings were really very good. On the other hand, both entrees I have had were mediocre. Most recently I tried "The King and I"--"Jumbo shrimp & chicken sautéed in prik khing coconut curry paste with fresh string beans and bell peppers." The shrimp were anything but jumbo, and the coconut curry paste was bland, lacking any distinguishable flavor. Veggies were fine. Asked for 4/5 spicy and didn't receive (a recurring problem in Philadelphia Thai restaurants it seems). Before that, I had the Jatujak Stir-fried with chicken--also bland-ish and not very different even though this was a thai basil paste. Will probably go back because of the area, and hopeful for an improvement.
5 stars on all 3 attributes: ambiance, food, and service. Very cozy setting, extremely friendly service and excellent food. What more can I add?

I saw some poor reviews regarding the prices but tell me where you can get freshly made delicious Indian food in Philly where it's not overly spiced to the point that you can no longer distinguish the flavor of each ingredients? Yes, the portions are not astronomical but this isn't an Indian buffet. I feel that an appetizer with an entrée is plentiful at this establishment. I love the decor, colorful, vibrant, cozy and offers a fresh take on Indian cuisine in the West Passyunk neighborhood. The staff are always so sweet and wonderful. The food selections varies from mild to strong in terms of flavor and spice. It definitely can appease a variety of taste buds from a newbie to an expert. I look forward to many more visits. Those paneer sandwiches are to die for!!!

Omg the tofu pad see ew is amazing - so many vegetables and they actually managed to make it spicy enough for my taste. The massaman curry was also nice and flavorful - and had papaya, so interesting! but could have maybe used a little more coconut milk. Nice staff too. Glad to have found this place on our long drive through the South.

Love this place! I've never dined in or gotten the lunch buffet which sounds like a great deal but this is my favorite place to get take out from. The lamb korma is amazing and the veggie samosas are honestly the best samosas I have ever had. Plus it's dinner for two for under $20 every time, can't beat that!

Zen Yai is an interesting place. The inside is a small and intimate experience. The walls are a dark maroon red with a large John Lennon painting on the wall. We had a reservation for 5, and they already had the table blocked off for us and gave us a choice. I decided on the table away from the table that would have lots of foot traffic. The table we were seated at had a cool ream of paper attached to the wall with specials written on it. The menu itself was rather large. I would say a little bit larger than a ledger sized paper. Perhaps they could make them a bit smaller. Menu wise there are a variety of choices and each section had about 6-10 dishes to choose from. I went with the Pineapple curry. Our wait time was reasonable 20 minutes and an older lady came out with our food. The plating was pretty good and because of the small tables it took up a bunch of space. The food was basically family style where you place everything in the middle and grab what you wanted. Now to my dish. Well lets just say it was disappointing and lackluster. The curry was basically a soup and barely that much chicken with it. The rice was cooked pretty good. For what I got I don't think it was worth $12. My friends shared me the fried vegetarian dish with cashews and that tasted substantially better than my dish. Overall I was disappointed with the food, but without having tried everything else, I'll give it an average rating. Service was good and the atmosphere was good.

The quintessential old world bakery. One of the last bakeries in St. Louis to do 20th century fine bakery goods.trust me, you will not find unique, exquisite bakery items like this in most places in St. Louis.
We stopped in while in Reno due to having good reviews. Our meal was very lack luster and wasn't anything special. I don't understand why this place has such good reviews.

After walking around Doylestown for a little while looking for somewhere to have lunch, we ended up at BLU. The space was small, like most place in Doylestown, but not cramped. The atmosphere was very pretty with blue lights and blue walls similar to something you would see in Greece. We started with an order of hummus and fried calamari. The hummus was good but I've had better. There was a flavor in it that I couldn't name but I wasn't a huge fan. The pita was average, it tasted like all other pita I've ever had. The calamari had a really flavorful garlic sauce on it which added a lot to the dish. The portion was small but all the pieces were meaty. For my main dish I had a lamb gyro. The meat was deliciously marinated and wasn't too tough or chewy. It really was one of the best gyros that I have ever had! The pita was different than the pita given with the hummus and was much better. It was crispy and held everything together nicely. Inside there was a cucumber tomato salad which was really tangy and flavorful. Instead of french fries I got the Blu salad which was just average. We also ordered marinated tomatoes with potatoes. I can't remember the name of the dish but it was good! The tomatoes were firm and not too mushy. Overall, I enjoyed this restaurant. The prices for lunch were fair. Looking at the dinner menu, I noticed that the prices were hiked up a little for the same dishes which would make me not want to go back for dinner. For lunch, it was fine and if I'm back in Doylestown I will go back!

We tried to get in at Delicia, but the wait was longer than we could manage (45 minutes) since we had tickets for a show later that evening and so the hostess suggested we try their sister restaurant next door. The food was good, but the menu available at dinnertime is very limited. The lunch menu (served until 3PM) offers a variety of tacos, but at dinner, only the fried fish tacos are available. There are soups at lunchtime, but not at dinner. My best guess regarding the reason for this is that the food is coming out of the same kitchen as Delicia, and so they pare down the menu at LaMulita so they can devote the bulk of the kitchen resources to Delicia. We has the guacamole which was really tasty; fresh avocado, with a nice little kick. The chips were fresh and tasty as well. All food is served in plastic baskets, so presentation was nothing remarkable (clear plastic cup for the guacamole with chips loaded in the basket. Salsa is in a squeeze ketchup bottle on the table which didn't seem terribly promising, so I stuck with the guacamole. I had the pork cemitas, which were basically tasty pulled pork sliders with black beans and avocados. We also ordered sides of plantain chips and sweet potato wedges which were both good. The cocktails are only $6 and they do offer a decent variety, but they do not serve the fire and ice cocktail over here in LaMulita. I'm really not sure what the rationale is for that. If they manage to figure out a way to serve the lunch menu at dinner, I'd add an extra star here, because the food is good, but it seems they haven't figured out yet how to manage the dinner crowd at Delicia and still serve more than a few options next door.

The food here is so good and the portions are huge for what you pay at a Thai restaurant- but the hours are so wonky it's impossible to tell when they're going to be open. The service staff at the register isn't ever very friendly either. I would stop going here all together if it weren't one of the only Thai places near Clermont.

As someone who has never tried Indian food before, this is certainly the best way to try it! There are so many popular dishes to try, and they keep the spice levels at a mild level. I tried just about all of the 18 or so offerings. Some I enjoyed, some were just not my cup of tea. I also tried the after dinner mouth freshener or Mukhwas as it's called. It's definitely a taste that will stay with you for a while. It was good to try, but once is good enough. Lunch crowd fills up quick, but they do a great job keeping things moving and replenishing the dishes. I would definitely return and indulge in some more of my favorite Indian dishes like the butter chicken.

The spicy beef noodle soup is SO flavorful and had the perfect amount of spice. I got it to go and the broth came in a good pint sized container with the noodles, beef, bean sprouts, and jalapeños on the side. The portion was HUGE and lasted me 3 meals. I will always come here as my Vietnamese go to.

The food here is great but the service was not very good at all. I asked the waitress twice for more water (my mouth was on fire at that) and then I asked for a box and the check and she only brought the box and walked away tending to other guests (it was not busy at all btw). We waited for awhile and then walked up and paid at the front- I don't know if that's how they operate but she was rude and so was the girl at the counter. Stars are only for food.
I was thinking of jerk chicken for a while. Heard of this location and ordered the large with their signature salad, rice and beans. I was so happy! Enough for 3-4 helping. Thank you!

The food was good, but the portions were really small and for the prices, it was not at all what I expected. I ordered the shrimp skewers which were $19.50. I got 6 shrimp, some cabbage, rice, and 2 plaintains. For 19.50 in a place like this I would expect at least 2 skewers. I mean, this is a tiny, no frills place, we even had plastic cups. It was really good, very spicy! But for the price I would never go back or recommend to anyone else. Sorry!

We were very pleasantly surprised with our first visit to Pho Vorhees. The space is large and modern with high ceilings. It also has a more modern vibe going then most of the other Pho places we have visited. We ordered two staples we usually order at Vietnamese restaurants. The Pho with beef brisket and vermicelli noodles with spring rolls. The pho here was really good and the broth was well developed. The brisket was also well seasoned and tasty. The vermicelli noodles were also very good and the ingredients, such as the chicken and shrimp, seemed a little higher quality then some of the other local Pho shops. Very happy to have this new addition and option locally. We look forward to returning and trying out some more of the menu. This was a really great first visit. 4.5 Yelp stars

This was interesting...I had the short rib tacos and although it was good, it didn't really wow me. The salsa on top of it was really strange; I didn't like how it fit in with the other flavors. The tea was solid, albeit a tad expensive. I expect good food and cheap prices at food trucks, particularly in this area (just because there are so many food trucks that do well), but this isn't somewhere I'd trek more than 4 blocks for.
Great food, fast service for lunch or dinner, evenings are often busy. Never have had to wait for a table.

We've been to Elaia but have been wanting to try Olio for a long time. We went for dinner on a Saturday evening and were seated right away. We ordered the Hummus with braised lamb, the Chicken Tagine and the Kale salad special. The kale salad was mixed lightly with chile flakes, tossed with a umami packed anchovy dressing, and served with shavings of pecorino romano. The hummus with lamb was a generous serving, it could have easily been an appetizer for 5 or an entree for 3 or 4. The lamb was absolutely delicious (think pulled pork of the great BBQ houses here in STL...but lamb!). Served with thick pita wedges and thin-crusted, warm farm bread. The hummus was topped olive oil, parsley and pine nuts. Lastly, the chicken tagine was divine! Two tender chicken thighs were perfectly seasoned, savory and subtly sweet. Served on a bed of saffron rice. This was a sumptious dish. Overall, all great hits! We'll be back again!

Loved everything about this cozy little Italian restaurant. Must make appointment in advance for the weekend nights since they only have 30 tables. I had the Shrimp with white beans, gnocchi for an appetizer (all pasta can be ordered in small or large portions) and the swordfish for my entree - excellent!! Went with two other couples and had a great time. Looking forward to returning.

As our waiter noted, this place has excellent food but the service is horrible! But really, this place has great food, great service, a very nice atmosphere, and is very accommodating to dietary needs. After a rather unpleasant experience at Crabby Bill's for lunch, this was a welcome treat for dinner. Ask for Nick, he'll show you a good time.

As I've mentioned in my first review that we'll be back for another night and we did. We want our last dinner to be memorable as we heading home in Virginia. My family of six has voted to come back to The Pearl as our last dinner. We all went home with happy tummy!
Delicious!!! All around incredible food. I've been to India and this was my favorite meal by far. We've eaten here a couple of times already!

This is one of my favorite local Indian places. Ekta in Bryn Mawr is probably my favorite, but I love that I can order online here. I always get something different and almost everything has been fantastic. My standout favorites were the lamb banjara and lamb kadai for entrees, and I love the special chaat appetizers. My husband always orders the chicken tikka masala (yawn!) but he loves it. I've tried it, and it is tasty. The naan is great too! The only ones I haven't really enjoyed as much were the shrimp coconut curry and chicken korma. They were kind of bland. It's a little expensive but it IS the Main Line. The takeout portion sizes are large! I just recently saw they're opening a new location in Bala Cynwyd.

This review is based on the service only and not the food. Came to Nola for Halloween! Following day, I had a craving for pho. I checked around on yelp to see any place close by was open and this one fit our bill. Paid 11 dollars to taxi from my hotel. I arrived at 8:10 and noticed there was a closed sign on the door despite their business hours stating that they open until 9pm. Walked inside and was promptly shooed out. The staffs explanation was that it is a full house and we cannot accommodate Anymore people, even though there was about 5 empty tables and I can see more in the back. Pho is supposed to be quick service so I don't understand why we couldn't be served. Waste of my time and money. TLDR: came in 50 min before closing and wasn't allowed to dine in regardless of there being a bunch of empty tables. 20 bucks for a round trip taxi for nothing.

Finally went here, and I am so happy that I finally had a chance to try it. I went with a large group so there was lots of opportunity to try a bunch of things. The summer rolls were phenomenal - holy cow, so good. I had the combo bun, which was perfectly sized and very flavorful. Not quite as good as some of the more serious sit down Vietnamese places, but very good for a quick casual type place. I also appreciated the good selection of bubble drinks that they give to you in takeout cups (that way you can take them home). Overall, a very good spot.

The portion sizes are great, the Angostura Lemon & Lime Bitters soda is amazing, but the goat curry wasn't my favorite. The meat is plenty tender, but I'm not sure about the seasoning. Still, it's solid portions and they take credit cards with no minimum. I'll experiment with the menu and see if the next dish I try is tastier.

Home style dominican food at its finest! Their Mangu with Salami and queso frito (Smashed green plantain, salami chunks, and fried cheese) is one of a a kind! Makes me feel like I'm back home in D.R. The perfect spot for wether on the go or to sit and dine!
Rice and Chicken Korma was dry. They don't serve any beer - let alone Indian beer. Not that great a place eat.

The best thing I've had here is the Black Bean Chicken. It is DELICIOUS, and comes with all kinds of vegetables! I usually just stick to broccoli, carrots, onions, peppers, and mushrooms. They offer a lot of atypical chinese entrees.
See check in comments as they are very detailed as to why i rated this a one star. wish half a star was an option. And to top it off they just ran out of milk.

Yum! What a great new addition to the ever-expanding Reno food scene, and while it's tough to compete with the already-great Asian joints in town, Creazian does a commendable job at elevating familiar grub. We came for a late lunch during a weekday. Since I had already heard great things about this place, I was disappointed with how empty it was. I hope they are busier for dinner. In any case, the location is gorgeous and feels extra fancy, yet accessible. I would love to do a Happy Hour or romantic dinner here some night. Parking is pretty simple: access the parking garage on Sierra street, same one for Peg's. They will validate. We started with drinks: a glass of Cabernet for him and a Vietnamese coffee for me. The wine pour was generous and a pretty good value. The coffee was a bit sweeter than I'm used to, but the quality was still excellent. I enjoyed every sip. For an appetizer, we decided to try the pork belly buns - tender pork belly, sauce, and a variety of veggies in a fresh steamed bun. The bun itself was fluffy and warm, a tad bit sweet and so much fun to eat. Unfortunately, there was not enough pork belly inside so it did leave me wanting more. The flavor was still outstanding. For a main course, I opted for the lunch special: a "smaller" portion of the Lo Mein, also served with 2 crab rangoons. The rangoons were just ok and fit the standard expectation. The Lo Mein, however, was a huge portion, even as just the lunch size, and tasted just delicious. There was a variety of meat including shrimp, chicken, and pork, along with perfectly cooked veggies and big fat noodles. I ate every bit of it and was absolutely stuffed. It was a steal at $9 for the combo. My lunch date got the Shrimp Garlic Noodle: a simple dish with noodles and shrimp tossed in a light (but strong) garlic sauce.
