The garlic was almost too overwhelming for me, but my date adored it and ate every last bit. Overall, while I am missing the part of Creazian that is supposed to be "fusion", it doesn't take away from the quality of food or the experience you get when you dine here. They've got ramen, bun bowls, poke, pho... so much to try, so we will definitely be back!
My favourite Thai restaurant, ever. Best Pad Thai I've ever had. Spring rolls delicious!!!

I'm no Pho expert, though I do know how to pronounce it properly. But this place seemed pretty good to me. Lots of fresh veggies and noodles with their Pho and their non-pho entrees. Eggrolls were good. Would have easily made 4 starts but I am dinging them a bit for the following reasons: 1. Their potstickers are pretty bready. Like, buying potstickers from Trader Joes and cooking them yourself results in a tighter, crispier skin. 2. My shrimp and pork Vietnamese entree was good, but it was 95.7% pork. The shrimp part consisted of three small tail on shrimp. Both the shrimp and pork were very good though.

Stopped in for a look-see upon recommendation from a family member. Very attractive space, friendly staff. Did not stay to eat but got two amazing containers of hummus (beet and squash) to take home. Plan to go back & eat more delicious food!

We come here frequently for the pho and are never disappointed. They seem to be getting more business and it is certainly well deserved! We start off with spring rolls which are simple and fresh served with a peanut sauce which makes the dish. The pho is an ample portion, filled with meat and always delicious. The broth is fragrant and served with plenty of bean sprouts, jalapeños and Thai basil. We also get the boba teas which I must say are much better than those the old owners would make. The boba are chewy unlike the old version which would occasionally still be frozen. I'm glad for these new owners and will make sure to keep coming back.

We went for an early dinner on a Saturday night and were pleasantly surprised at what we found at Abyssinia. This is a fantastic little gem of a place tucked in an unassuming strip mall. Both meat-eaters and vegetarians will find plenty of tasty options to suit their tastes at Abyssinia. We had the vegetarian taster, as well as one of the meat tasting menu. The food was all delicious! Most of the dishes weren't very spicy but some had a bit of kick to them. There was plenty of food for the two of us, we didn't finish everything either. The waiter was really pleasant and attentive. The decor of the restaurant is really nice, with warm tones of color on the walls. There are some traditional tables with the basket and stools, as well as Western tables for those who want a back to their seats. My only complaint is that there are two flat screen tv's at either end of the restaurant and they were at full volume when we got there. Who on earth wants to go to a decent restaurant and watch tv? You can sit at home and watch tv while you eat. The annoying thing is that with all the pretty, moving colors, it's hard to not watch while you eat. I really think the tv killed the atmosphere of the place. How about shutting them off and playing some music? That would be killer, to go hand-in-hand with the killer food. Well, the food still far too good to pass up due to the inconvenience of a little modern technology. I highly recommend giving this place a shot.
Loved the food here. Bahrain being a big part of me, for a while it took me back to Bahrain

Very very good. I really liked the sampler appetizer platter for the main course. Has hummus, baba ganoush, and really awesome tabouleh. I swapped out the grape leaves for felafel. Yum. The fatouch salad is really good also. And I've tried the pizza there too. Mushroom and black olive. Very good. Plus the staff are great, friendly and quick. They remember me whenever I go and ask about my family. Great place to frequent, you won't be disappointed.

If you're a picky eater, avoid this...you pay $10 and you get what he gives you. The meal always includes his delicious falafels, flavorful chargrilled chicken, artisan bread, and a mix of whatever he made fresh. Its well worth the money and I dont think I've ever disliked a side (some were just ok).
Not only has their grandma voted their bathroom "the best in TN" .....their BIG SALATA with gyro meat & tahini is amazing!!!

My husband and I have not ever been to Fulin before 7/18/2018 we were going to a concert in Nashville that evening and we decided to stop in Mt Juliet on our way into town for dinner. The hostess seemed dismissive and not very happy to see us. We got seated at a booth and the table top and menus both were grime caked. Our waiter was prompt and courteous and the only really pleasant part of the whole trip. The shashimi plate arrived in a timely manner, but it was not presented well. For a $23 plate of shashimi I expect presentation not just chunks of fish that are haphazardly cut into large irregular pieces just lopped on a plate. It also didn't seem very fresh with a particular cut or two being extra fishy. We both left super disappointed and feeling ill. We ended up missing our concert due to illness and headaches. I wouldn't recommend this location.

Having had a week trip to Thailand (Chiang-Mai), and been a frequent Thai afficionado in California, I've seen my share of really good and really bad Thai restaurants. coming to Nashville, I actually didn't expect very much, but was quite surprised at how good the food turned out. The thai food was not quite as spicy as I would have liked (they served me the white man's version unfortunately), but the taste was fairly authentic and well made. The service was also fast.

Absolute joy to visit this place. The owner is super attentive and friendly which made the experience that much better. Our coals were replenished and ashes cleaned on a regular basis by the attentive owner and his staff. We also ordered food and it was tasty as well. At the end of the night, we were given fruit smoothies, on the house! I would go again and recommend it to my friends. Thanks Sherif!
This was not good at all. Maybe it was a bad night. I don't plannto return. The staff were friendly. I always get Pad Thai and this was one of the worst.
This shit is legit. Don't listen to anyone who says it's too salty; it's supposed to be, and its flame. You won't find better french fries in the area, and the gyros sandwiches really turn me on.

Maybe take out is just not the same as dining in? The search for the best thai continues! We Moved from D.C. and miss our go to thai places but this is the third place we've tried and unfortunately didn't hit the mark. As a caveat: the food itself was very delicious, my bf and I shared, pad thai, the thai basil stir fry and coconut soup all with chicken and the coco turkey dumplings. Everything was fresh, spiced well, but there was one common problem: ALL the dishes were small and had so little meat I forgot I even ordered my entree with chicken! The $7 soup was literally the size of a small mug with maybe 2 pieces of chicken, the thai basil was also very small with a few pieces of chicken. The pad thai looked vegetarian as well. Don't get me wrong, I love veggies, but when i pay $15 for a dish with meat, I expect meat. The dumplings were great so no complaints there. Normally when we order $50 of food we have a ton of leftovers but not after this meal. We may try again and dine in instead. When I picked up the place was packed and the decor was gorgeous.

great food and great service! i have hosted many parties with them and they have been very accommodating. the manager named Mo is also very accommodating. the only drawback is that the food portions (specifically meat) are typically on the smaller side and tends to be a little bit overpriced.

At last we've made it into this curiously named spot. The service was nearly spot on and the food was delicious. I'm not sure if they gave us the right salad, we ordered the Som Tum Mango (Thai Style Spicy Mango Salad). It wasn't medium spice as ordered, but perhaps we should have ordered hot spicy. Regardless, it was very good and was a nice balance to our curries. The red curry and massaman were very similar, I loved the high bamboo to chicken ratio in the red, and peanuty cream in the massaman. The stir-fried eggplant was good, but the sauce overpowered these delicate little veggies. Not sure that I'd order that dish again, and it wouldn't win over any newcomers to eggplant. The coconut rice was yummy and the perfect base for the curries. Our group paired the meal with Singha and Chang Thai beer and the meal came in at a very reasonable price with a couple bevies each. Our server was very welcoming and friendly, it felt like being welcomed into the family with gentle recommendations and timely service. We'll be back. UPDATE: We took our leftovers home and they were delicious. The only caveat is they didn't send home the left over mango salad or one of the curries. I know there was leftover sauce with a few bamboo shoots that weren't in our doggie bag, and darn it, I loved the sauce and those crispy tidbits. I'd take away a star if I didn't enjoy the food that much!

I love this restaurant. The atmosphere is intimate and the service is great. The cocktails are inventive and the food is amazing. I definitely recommend trying the egg salad, the beet salad, and the octopus. Highly recommend!!
Go for the mediocre food. Stay because the service is so horrible that you literally have to wait hours for your mediocre food.
Amazing authentic food and great customer service! It seems to be locally owned. To-Go takes awhile but when you eat in everything is super snappy.

I love to eat here when I am in the area, especially lunch time. The price is right for lunch and the food is good. I especially love the Panang Curry and the Pad Thai. Pad Thai is not always good at many Thai restaurants I have been to because they get the ratios wrong on the fish sauce. Orchid Thai does it right. The establishment is small and the atmosphere feels more like a lunch place than a dinner. Be careful when you order spicy, medium is even VERY spicy. I recommend spice just be careful how you order it.

Me : "I'll have the number ____" Viet Pho "umm we don't have that" Me" It's on the menu" Viet Pho " we forgot it's there" so I order a boba tea, the powered mix they used wasn't even stirred, also the boba was cooked too long, it wouldn't go up the straw. $4.95 is a lot for such a mediocre drink and service. The table I sat while waited was really really sticky. and the sauce bottles were oozing out of their containers. yuck :p

Steve was very informative & a pleasure to talk with. Beautiful decor that we learned was all imported to furnish the restaurant as if it where in their homeland. The food was fantastic and plenty of it!! Will definitely be one of my new regular places to eat.

Since I moved to 107st I've been going to thanh Son for two years and their service is always fast and their food always comes out no more then 8 mins after ordering. My favourite is their Bun Rieu which is a big bowl of soup with rice noodles, tomato, shrimp, and pork with a side plate of beansprouts. My personal favorite Vietnamese dish. What I find stands out from a lot of Vietnamese places is their Shrimp Rolls. Not their shrimp rolls per say but the home made peanut sauce that comes with it is the best in town in my opinion. The only reason why I wouldn't rate this place a 5 star is because of their parking lot. Nothing to do with their food and service at all but the parking lot is so tiny and the area of which it is located makes me think twice as to going back sometimes...but I've always went back for more...

I haven't had a chance to try any other good Thai places but by this is the best one yet..definitely better than "I and King" which is on the same block. Any who, I had the shrimp pad thai and it was pretty good..I think the reason why I gave 4 stars is the service was horrible, our waitress barely came back to check on us or even ask if we needed anything. But the food is good, and reasonably priced. I will probably go there again when I have another Thai craving! but nothing like the bay area (San Francisco) with Asian foods...or any type of food for that matter :)

One of my favorite places to eat. Great place to take a vegetarian friend too, because any of their dishes can be made without meat. Don't forget, they are cash only, and BYO. Not open on Sundays. Everything on the menu is amazing. My favorite is the Panang Curry dish. With shrimp or chicken. When I was looking for a new apartment, this restaurant was one of my top reasons not to leave West Philly. I left anyways, but there is a great sadness in my heart when I remember that Vientiane is no longer the closest restaurant to my house. They do take out orders too.

i love that there is an Indian place less than 15 minutes from my place ! however, every time I have been here , the biryani has been different - the spice levels vary , the dish itself is different at times. with that being said - their chicken biryani is great ! chicken chettinad is great . avoid the chicken vindaloo! but the apollo fish is a must must have ! B.E.S.T. appetizer ever !!! the place is BYOB so don't forget to bring your own favorite bottle
BEST. FOOD. EVER!!! I especially love the chop chop salad with the rice, so delicious!!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Great service at this BYOB place. In a strip mall and exactly like other Chinese/Sushi places in this area of PA. I really liked the food. Only ordered off the sushi menu and was truly delighted with food quality and presentation. One criticism: Their website is truly amazing and over-represents the actual restaurant.

Simple and sweet. Family ran and local; located right off 38th on the same strip as Planet Fitness. The service is excellent although I wish she would've told me how strong the ginger drink is, think twice if you're not use to it. I got the bbq jerk ribs with rice and plantain. I was a bit surprised by the texture and coating of the plantain. Definitely had better, but theirs might be unique to the region. The meat was tender and flavorful there wasn't major heat, but just right. Rice was fresh and so were the fries. Definitely coming back for oxtail. Best thing is they're halal with the highest quality meats.
Absolutely perfect. Friendly employees, who serve top notch Puerto Rican food. Love these guys. Recommend to anyone who wants good Puerto Rican food to come here.

I tried this food via a pop up menu by the airport and it was delicious! The rosemary chicken was the juiciest chicken I've ever had - and it was seasoned perfectly. Never would have tried the food without Fooda's pop up menu. So glad I did. Didn't give 5 stars only because I didn't experience the physical location. Very pleased with the food though!

We went to this restaurant last Sunday after church and it was pretty good. I had Island Jerk Chicken wings and fries and my fiancé had chicken curry plantains and mixed vegetables the chicken Curry which was good and it's not spicy at all. my friend had Jerk Chicken and rice and the jerk chicken was really good. There Chicken is amazing but hey you can't go wrong with chicken

This place was great. We stopped in after a long day at Busch Gardens with our two boys. The place is nothing fancy but the food was quick and very tasty. The service was super friendly, too. We would definitely go back!

First time here tonight. Everyone was delicious. The gyro meat was perfectly seasoned. The hummus was flavorful. They are also very nice, I will tell more people about this place. My best friend told me to go here, his friend is food critic for the times picayune and said this place is superb. If a food critic says so, then you best believe.

Food is good but the service needs improvement. You often have to wait for someone to acknowledge you. My last experience here the two waitresses argued with me in front of the other patrons about what I ordered and then blamed me for ordering the wrong item and insisted that I pay for it. I will not be back.
FOOD IS FABULOUS..service at times stinks!.... fair pricing...worth trying!

I went to Fez for my friend's birthday. If you're trying to accomodate a large party, I'd highly recommend this place. It's especially great if you're trying to accomodate vegetarians within a big group. Also good to note - we had absolutely no trouble booking a table for nine on a Saturday night two days in advance. On the weekends, they have a fixed price ($25) eight-course menu that you eat with your hands. It was so dark I could barely see what I was eating, but it was fantastic, even for a fussy gal like myself - the lentil soup was delicious, the chicken was especially moist, and the hummus was top notch. I would have given it five stars, but the service slowed down significantly after the first five courses. After dinner, definitely indulge in the hookah -- they have a myriad of flavors; I'd recommend mango or mixed fruit.
Superb quality food and customer service! Great teamwork among the staff. The finest of Boughasha!

Went to Philly for a Christmas party, but i reside in NY. First thing i saw was how clean and well kept it was. I had a bit of everything from fried fish,salmon,mac&cheese, potatoes salad, candy carrots and squash pie. Yup all that :), best part was everything was amazing!!! had my taste buds on another level!!! I wish they had one in NY

This is a really good place. Unassuming, so don't expect much in the way of decor. It's a few tables in a white room with a counter and some pictures on the wall. That said, i go for the food and good service. I don't eat meat and there are quite a few veggie options here. They also will make spring rolls with out shrimp or pork upon request. I have been to places that will not do that and it's always disappointing. Of the Asian places I've been to , this is tied for top spot. Never mind - I just decided- this is my top go-to spot.
This food was so good and a reasonable price. We got the eggplant with steamed rice and the miso salmon and both were amazing!

My parents and I just enjoyed the first of many wonderful meals at this great restaurant. Fantastic lamb korma, chicken biryani, fish curry, and garlic naan. More importantly, the staff was extremely warm and thoughtful - we felt extremely well cared for and had a thoroughly enjoyable night. We will definitely be returning to this hidden gem of Newtown.

I have been here twice and both times the food was excellent. Began with a perfect French 75 cocktail along with the bruschetta and lemony egg salad which were both wonderful. We are every last bite of the zucchini carpaccio and I had the smoked trout on toast as my entree which was my favorite. The interior atmosphere is uniquely charming as it is located in a refurbished gas station. The lighting on the patio is quite dim in places and there are a few spots where hot air from an air conditioner blows making some spots less desirable. Overall a place I will definitely return. I would only suggest a bit of help for the bartender on busy weekends, since the drink service is rather slow.

I've tried to give this place a shot but they're way too rude. I went there many times for bagels, iced tea, coffees, sandwiches, etc. Everything is relatively average and the fact that the employees are rude kind of negates the whole experience.

I was excited to finally try this new location because of it being closer to my house than the uptown location. I love the food as well as the ambiance at the other location so I expected the same coming into this one. I knew once I walked in this was going to be the "touristy" version which I can understand due to it's location. Looking at the menu I was confused why the prices were significantly higher as well as the dishes having different ingredients. I asked the waiter why the change and she said "they wanted this location to be a different concept from the other one". I ordered what i usually ordered at the other one and changed the ingredients to match what I appreciate most in Vietnamese food. The food was very flavorless so I took to the condiments to hopefully make it better. I'm not sure why but they don't offer anything in its original bottles and they all seemed like watered down versions of what they are supposed to be. The Sriracha had little to no kick or spice to it which I don't understand how that happened at all. I didn't even bother to try the hoisin at that point and went straight for the sambal oelek sauce. I will continue to frequent the other location

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Excellent! My girlfriend and I split an order of chicken madras with a side of gluten free naan. We are both full and satisfied! The owner is very nice as well. It did take awhile since all dishes are prepared individually but we were warned and not disappointed with the food.

Great gyros! You won't find a better gyro anywhere nearby for sure. Reasonably priced for how big the gyros are. Its nothing fancy inside, and I always get mine to go, but they do what they do very well. The baklava is amazing and fresh daily. The hummus and pita bread is always good as well. I am here at least once a week!
I didn't like the taste. It's more of an Indian food suited for Americans. Though the ambience was good but food lacked indianality.
Great cubans and daily specials... Also have a nice collection of imported beer with a seasonal beer or two on tap.
I had the beef Kafka, it was delicious with rice, salad & pita bread. I will definitely be back. The staff was great and the service was fast. I recommend this place to locals & visitors.

Since Momo's is within a short walk from our house, we've eaten there a number of times. This is some good solid food with a high variety on the menu with some more-creative-than-usual choices than other Greek or Mediterranean restaurants. Considering that their menu format is basically large and small plates meant for sharing, the price/value equation gets a bit dicey. If you are going to really fill up on the typical large portions, you'll be paying for it. But frankly, that is the problem with our dining out today anyway. Too much friggin' food. If I weren't trying to eat very healthy (as a vegan), I'd give a better rating since the food has been quite good and consistent. However, I'm rating Momo's (and other eateries) based on how they measure up against healthy eating. Went there for lunch today and I selected from a very abbreviated lunch menu an eggplant sandwich. Normally served with mozzarella and feta cheese, I opted to leave those off to keep it vegan. Considering the high-fry of the breaded eggplant, I could fear that they used the traditional flour, egg, breadcrumb technqiue, but what I don't know about, I can't care too much about. It was a delicious sandwich even without the cheeses, though likely a bit higher on the caloric scale than desired. They also offered a grilled vegetable pita that I'd have ask to skip on the feta and tzatziki sauce as well and may try that one in the future. If I were ovo-lacto vegetarian, I'd probably take some point deductions from Momo's as they absolutely drowned one of our other diner's gyro in sauce. Unnecessary. One of Momo's competitors, Olympia has some good vegetarian options as well and should be considered if you are really seeking out the heralded "Mediterranean Diet."

Went there with three generations, the youngest being five, during a recent baseball visit to St. Louis. The food was very good and the service as well. Place is a bit quirky, the reviewer who mentioned that it lacked the bathroom was more or less correct, although there is one in a pinch, as we found out when all of our kids needed to go at once. Unfortunately I didn't take photos or write a review at the time so I can't remember exactly what dishes we had, but I would definitely recommend this if you're looking for good Indian food at a reasonable price.

I love my Pho, and for me, this is the best Pho in town. This location is just a few months old, but it's the cleanest, friendliest and tastiest spot for Pho and Cafe Sua Da!! The Rainbow Ice and Bubble Tea are all good as well. The broth here is the key - it has the most flavor with very little oil/fat. Portions are typical for Pho spots along Washington, so you won't be disappointed. With several places to grab a decent bowl of Pho along Washington, it's the service, cleanliness, and of course food quality that puts this restaurant a step above the rest. Due to being fairly new to the neighborhood, this place is never packed and the restaurant itself is very large for a Pho house. Please support this restaurant to make sure it sticks around for a long time!! They also accept credit cards with no minimum limit, which some of the smaller joints do not and they are open everyday till Midnight!!!!
All I can say is this: my favorite local snack is a chicken patty from Brown Sugar. It's $1.50. Delicious value. Go for it.

My 3rd visit to Pho Orchid in a week because they are close to my house. I really wanted to like this place. i ordered the Korean Beef to go and had the same experience as the first visit. 3 very small slices of fatty beef. I complained to the gentleman at the bar and was told the amounts used are prepackaged. He walked off and didn't look back. I din't get upset but I won't go back.

This was my first time trying pho so I admit that I don't know if I just don't like pho or if it was just this particular dish I had - but I would first off say that I had no idea there would be raw beef in it. I feel like this is something you would usually tell a person when they order a meal. I ordered the food to go. As others have said, the broth was really good and the noodles too - so that's all that I ate. I've been wanting to try pho for awhile - I have now, and I don't think I'm likely to try it again any time soon.

We recently moved to the area and we're looking for a new local Thai restaurant. We stumbled upon this place on yelp and are so happy we did! Great service, delicious food, and reasonable prices. So happy to have a new go-to Thai place close to home!

They just opened and I've tried them twice now. First time, they overcharged for an extra drink I didn't order. I waited to address it with the guy taking orders, was asked to wait until his next 3 customer orders were taken. Asked to speak to manager, was corrected. Our food came out & was sitting there getting cold. Had to ask waitress to bring it to the table. Tables dirty also., Second time last night. Heard other customers complaining about wait time of 30 minutes on the food ordered. One got a refund & future gift certificates for food complaints. Another party complained it took 30 minutes to get their food. After 25 minutes, we asked about our order, was told it'd be another 10 minutes. Orders taken after ours were being served first. We asked for a refund & were about to leave. Manager comped the meal & asked us to stay. Brought wrong order. Just not acceptable for mediocre food that's supposed to be fast food. Nice restaurants get the food out faster than 40 minutes & manage to get the order right! Not returning!!!! Big mistake allowing this one to come into the new Seminole City Center!!!

This is one of my go to resteraunts! I love their pho the broth is amazing and flavorful! Prices are very reasonable a big bowl is between $8-8.50. The staff is super friendly and quick. Area isn't the best but I will continue to come back
treat yourself to this wonderful family owned restaurant, your taste buds will thank you! great staff, atmosphere, and in my own opinion, the best veggie thai food around

This is a great Indian restaurants in the area. Came here for the lunch buffet with colleagues and it was awesome! They had goat on the buffet which was amazing because usually you can't get that in a buffet. All the rice items/biriyanis, meat, breads were good as well. It was nice and clean inside and the seating arrangement was good too. Very spacious inside. I will come back soon.

Stopped by for a late lunch/happy hour to try out their menu. I always eat Vietnamese food so I went with Japanese, I think. The pork belly pops weren't on the menu but the gentleman was happy to serve them up. I also ordered a pork ramen (tankatsu). Pork belly pops were decent, tender, sweet and salty. There was a hint though as if they dish was just reheated. Hot on the outside and lukewarm on the inside. Then came my ramen. I have mixed feelings about this dish. It wasn't smooth tasting like other ramens I've had but it was good none the less. Possibly too much wood ear? Eggs were perfectly soft boiled. Presentation could of been better but I guess it didn't matter as I just dug in. That's where I found the random scattered pieces of pork in no particular shape. I probably could deduct this place more stars but since they are new, I'll let them work out the kinks. Some examples would be, they brought me "pho" condiments for my ramen... That's just weird. I'm all for fusion but ugh no. Being the only person in here, service should of been top notch. The server was nice but he forgot my setting before he gave me my appetizer. He also looked inexperienced carrying out my ramen bowl without a serving tray. Sure it's convenient but it's just not professional. Then Wassup with the music? I think the DJ went through three genres. I'll be back to give them another shot and hopefully the staff gets training on basic restaurant equiette.

I would say they have absolutely the best Chai Latte in the city! I quite like the atmosphere very trendy and always busy often with university students and also often Remedy has some great art work from local artists on their wall to check out or purchase. I have eaten a few times and have yet to have something bad, mind you I haven't been too adventurous. I did try their Masala Dhosa and it was delicious, I had the veggie one and am glad I opted for it as my friend had the chicken and found it to be too filling with the meat. But I guess if you have a large appetite that would be perfect. I have also had their breakfast sandwiches a few times and love them, I don't know what sauce they use but it is very tasty! I don't think a lot of people think of desert when they go to remedy but I have to say they have some of the best cakes and pies I've had and it is always a plus when you can order by the slice. A personal favorite is the Kitty Lime Pie, I'm not sure why Kitty is in the name but it's what drew me to it and holy pie batman it was amazing!!!
Food is not authentic. You have fewer options on a weekday buffet. Ambience is good because this is a newer restaurant. However, the food is cheap and the service is ok.

The 5 stars caught your attention, didn't it?! I'll start by saying I was compelled to write this review for various reasons to which I'll get into. First impression walking through the door friendly and welcoming. The staff actually look you in the eye as they greet you. They encourage you wait to be seated but if you have a preference they'll grant the request happily. With a smile. The restaurant it's self is spotless. Not one dusty old fake plant in sight! That is an automatic WIN in my books. You'll notice quickly the sriracha sauce, hoison, etc... Are placed on a CLEAN tray WITHOUT a trace of old crusties along the spout. The menu is simple and to the point. Be it your first time eating Vietnamese food or your 1 millionth, there's something on there for everyone. The price, THE PRICE! As someone who has been using pho as a hangover cure for 8+yrs and eating it before I was legal, I was over joyed at the menus pricing. It was like a throwback. So much so I had to double check my calendar to make sure it wasn't Thursday. Soup used to be under $10 and had my 'go to' places to enjoy it. Over the years the price has gone up and the food quality and taste has gone down. I understand ingredients, minimum wage, etc increase over the years. But why sacrifice the quality of your product. Wouldn't one pay more to ensure quality stays the same? No dice. The freshness of the salad rolls blew my mind. The size was long and girth was satisfying (). The dough from the green onion cakes was soft and crispy. The rare beef pho was flavorful. I gotta say what stood out was the beef. The thinly sliced melt in your mouth beef. For a regular bowl there was lots, to the point I couldn't eat it all. Blown away by the ingredients and quality of the food for the price I was paying. Unreal. I discovered this place because I've been unsatisfied with some of my 'go to' places. Be it the price hike, poor food quality or simply because I no longer wanna feel like an inconvenience walking through the door. So I've been rolling the dice by trying new spots all over the city. I took note of this one when it came up on my FB feed. I will not be venturing any further than Miss Saigon to satisfy the craving for Vietnamese food. Nor should you!

Everyone time we are in Reno, we stop by. It's a small family owned business with great customer service. They are always accommodating and kind. It is hard to feel welcome when you have 3 little ones that is why this place deserves 5 stars. Their food is delicious and very reasonably priced.
This place has some AMAZING Indian cuisine!!! Their buffet is delicious and they are also very hospitable!!! They introduced me to their culture with style and grace. I absolutely love this place!!!

I always order the green curry with either shrimp or chicken, but my husband is much more adventurous. One time we got a whole fish- eyeballs an everything!- it was baked with a clear sauce and vegetables on top. It was pretty good though for something that looked so scary, that thing had teeth! It was very large, I believe it could feed 3-4 people. When my husband isn't deployed, this is one of our top places to get Thai food, they not only have the traditional dishes but also some unique and very different entrees; if you want to try something new, this is the place for you!

An amazing experience of authentic Ethiopian food. I love the quality of the service and decor of the restaurant. There aren't that many African restaurants in Tampa, FL so I was nervous to eat at Sheba's. Immediately Ms. Seble removed my fears and made me and my friends feel at home. I ordered the Shrimp Wot that came on a beautiful plate that allowed us to share and enjoy each the night together. The stew for the shrimp was spicy with a great heartiness to it. I recommend this for all true adventurous foodies

I have been trying a few Thai restaurants lately and this was definitely one of my least favorite. They didn't even ask or put ANY spicy flavor on my 3 dishes I ordered. This was the first Thai restaurant that didn't ask to put any spicy flavor and just left it bland. I even tried the pineapple fried rice that seemed to get good reviews, but it was simply fried rices with chunks of pineapple. I was going to give it 1 star but it did seem like they were short staffed. However, it was not busy and our food did not take very long to come out. Our server seemed to be stressed out and gave us zero acknowledgement. Not one smile was shown to me even when the bill came out. This was a Sunday at around 7:00pm.

This is some of the best Indian food I've had in the US. Additionally, some of the menu items are unique to the US, but are more available on UK menus. We had take out, so I can't comment on the restaurant itself. Also, I see they have a buffet, I don't eat buffets and you shouldn't either. Samosa's were delish. Really big and plump. Full of warm smashy veggie filling. Chicken Pakoras were 5 stars with a flavorful chickpea breading and really moist, juicy chicken. Chicken Tikka Masala was thick and rich. It was so thick, creamy and full of flavor. I want to do the back stroke in their Masala sauce. Chicken Manchurian was really good, but kind of reminded me of buffalo wings. I love buffalo wings, but it was an unexpected flavor. Chicken Jalfrezi was spicy and full of chunky meat and veggies. Really good, tradish Jalfrezi. Chicken Patia was a really good dish that I've never seen on an Indian menu in the US. Very reminiscent of UK Indian take aways. An Indian sweet 'n sour, if you will. Yummo. Veggie Biryani was so good and had a lot of unexpected veggies in it - like broccoli, bu it was delish and hearty. Flavor was tremendous. Bread was all good. Order was correct. The only thing I didn't love was the mint and tamarind chutneys. These were watered down and oddly flavored (flavorless). Mango Chutney is good if you like that.

I came the other night with a large group of friends. It was our monthly International Supper Club gathering. We were seated at two large tables, since there was about 14-16 of us in attendance. I wasn't that hungry, so I ordered two appetizers as my entree; Fried Spring Rolls and Crab Rangoon. The spring rolls came with 4 to the order and the rangoon had 5. The Crab Rangoon's were larger then most and the pocket was full of creamy cheese and a fair amount of crab. For the price, I couldn't expect a full crab leg in each rangoon. They were better then any carry-out Chinese. The Fried Spring Rolls were a major disappointment. They basically were nothing more then a rolled pastry shell. The inside was filled with air and the vegetables inside could not even cover my thumb nail. We had two servers and they were like the stereotypical cops, one playing good server and the other playing bad server. When one of our guest questioned the preparation of her favorite Thai dish, the one almost became argumentative. When they spoke in their native language (which is fine), about the situation, you could tell the one was trying to make the situation right. Once my friend got her right entree, I think she had the best dish of the night. It looked so good, I'd like to return and enjoy it. Dealing with a large group, the kitchen had a good flow of the food to our table so I give them around of applause for that. When: March 13, 2016 Why: International Super Club
So yummy. While the menu isn't huge, it has a lot of variety. The Yukon gold potato chips were amazing. Service was quick (but not rushed) & friendly.
I love their boba and shaved ice. Chicken Panang and banh mi are my all time favorite. Staffs are friendly too. Fast service.

Amazing hash browns.. good coffee.. I ordered whole wheat French toast which in it self was delicious. I was however, extremely disappointed in the corn syrup masked as maple syrup in a plastic single serving cup. Guys, you have to work on making the food healthier. Corn syrup is a killer. It's a gmo. It's fake! Help us be healthier!!!
Momos is a great place for greek tapas. The atmosphere is very fun especially with the belly dancers. Groups can sit in there own private booth in the back. I recommend the Mythos beer.
The samosa tasted so good! It's a must try here! Btw, the buffet price is not expensive which in sensible price. Try it!

My husband and I are regulars at Phamous and for good reason- this place is amazing!! It is without a doubt the cleanest and best pho/bun/bahn mi in town, and the egg rolls are equally phenomenal! If you needed any more evidence for Phamous's commitment to quality Vietnamese food, the owner (Dan) can be seen working basically every day they're open, alongside his typically cheery staff. If you even remotely appreciate Vietnamese food, you must try it out!

Tried this new place for lunch today (got it to go). I went around opening so it wasn't busy, and the place was immaculate. I ordered the falafel bowl with baba ganoush and rice, onion, chopped salad, and 2 different sauces. I also ordered their fries, not realizing my bowl came with a pita. It was a lot of food, but it was SO yummy! The fries are more like chips, though some are on the soft side. They were warm and lightly salted. I just had to try them, though I probably won't get them again simply because the rest of the food is filling enough. The pita is perfectly soft and fresh, and was a delightful surprise in my bag when I got home! The main thing I cared about was the falafel. It did not disappoint, and I cannot wait to eat it again and again. There were 5 in my bowl, nicely seasoned and not overly greasy despite the fact that they're fried. All the stuff it came with was delicious, too. I liked the spicy green sauce (s'khug). I thought the tahini sauce was too watery. My hubby had the chicken shawarma in a pita, and couldn't stop raving about it. He got the chopped salad, hummus, and garlic sauce with his. The service was great. There's no signage on the food line so I wasn't sure what some items were (namely the sauces), but all of the servers were patient and friendly. One of them was a bit difficult to understand, as he kinda mumbled a lot, but he was still very nice. Parking is a bit confusing right now, but will hopefully improve as the shopping center gets completed. I just parked inside the edge of the Wegmans lot and crossed the street in the crosswalk -- no problem. I will most definitely be back!
Very good. I was impressed. Hummus and pita were amazing. Didn't love their fries but there was a ton in the bucket I got with my combo. Will be back.

The Thai basil is still as good as ever, but the Grand Palace Vegetable with chicken, veggies, and glass noodles was a bit on the bland side. I had to mix the basil sauce in, which was actually really good. The portions are still very generous, and our food was served very quickly. A solid option for Thai but I would stick to the standard entrees.

I love this restaurant, truly!! The new owners are terrific. The food is so delicious and they are very friendly and accommodating. My favorite foods here are the homemade chilli chicken meatballs, the tandoori chicken, and the vegetable pakora which I especially love dipped in the sambar! They have the best chicken tikka masala too! The weekday lunch buffet is a great bargain at $8.95. When you order from the menu, they will adjust the spice to your taste. Just go...you will love it!! :)

Grilled Octopus is a must and keeps me coming back to Dmitri's. It's tender, has that grilled flavor with a light dressing and fresh herbs, and the portions is generous. The atmosphere is intimate, a hidden jewel tucked away in queen village. You can't go wrong with any of appetizers: hummus, meatballs, olives and feta are my favorites. The Whole Fish entree is a must.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Taj Mahal has been my favorite Indian food for six years. I started going when they were in west Boise and was impressed with the quality of the food, the atmosphere, and the extremely courteous service. The Naan bread is excellent, the vindaloos are spicy, and the tandoori chicken haunts my dreams. The new location downtown is convenient for those going to clubs and so forth, and I am happy to report that the food is as good as ever.

The sandwiches and boba teas are delicious. The only reason I don't give them 5 stars is because they seem to always get the boba tea order wrong and they have to make it again. If you go there and order boba tea or boba milk tea, keep your receipt.

Looks like they either moved or closed down. We drove 18 miles wanting to try this place and saw a paper on the window saying they moved on October 3rd, however location of their new place (where they moved) was not posted :-/ disappointed that this info was not posted on their website, which I checked before we decided to drive there. Unfortunately no other decent alternative choice around here

Love Santorini's! I get lunch here every week because it's the best place to eat on campus. I grew up on mediterranean food and this place is legit. The Baklava tastes just like my aunt's! Also, the price is great for the amount of food you get. One thing that really stands out to me is the meat. Meat at other places around IV can be kinda sketchy and have grizzle or taste a bit funny. The chicken and the gyro meat here are always fresh though! Santorini also catered all the food for my club's free CPR/AED certification course in Corwin, and it was a hit! The trainers were thrilled and everyone was all smiles while eating it. Even my vegetarian friends were happy. The service is great, the workers are very friendly and nice, and the helpings are generous. I'm gonna miss this place when I graduate!

We loved it! We went at an odd time (3 pm on a Thursday afternoon) so we had the run of the place... Everything we ate was delicious. The margarita may be the best I've ever had! Our server was awesome and made sure to bring our son's food first without our asking, which was really thoughtful. My only complaint was that they switch to the dinner menu at 3... I would have liked the "pick 2" on the lunch menu to try more Looking forward to trying Delicia even more now that we've tried the "little sister".

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: I was one of their first customers and I was so thrilled to find good sushi practically around the corner from me. We've been patronizing them since they opened and have sadly watched the gradual deterioration of the quality of their food. Their first sushi chef was an absolute genius. The current one is no better than one found in your basic supermarket. Tonight I gave them one more chance....ordered the Floujrtown Roll and my husband ordered the tofu dinner bento box. Up front, I have to admit that I cannot tolerate any kind of spicy food, which is why I ordered the Flourtown Roll. Unfortunately the sushi chef of the day likes to add that spicy Japanese mayo to his dishes and I had to cut off the top of each piece of my roll. Meanwhile, the California roll in my husband's bento box could not be picked up with chopsticks because they were not properly rolled. I could have done better, and I've made sushi just twice in my life. I'm so sad to see the deterioration of what was once a promising restaurant. We won't be coming back.

I recently came here for dinner with friends. Because I had previously never tried Thai food I was a little nervous. A friend recommended I try the "Pad See Ew" so I did, not knowing what anything on the menu really was. The dish was so tasty, and so was everything else I tried off of friends plates. The prices were affordable and it's a BYOB! I will definitely be back. Also- if you have a large group definitely make a reservation (or a small group for that matter) because the room is small and it's often packed.
Amazing Pad Thai. I have only done carry out orders but the service was very fast and friendly. Very large portions with fair prices.

Excellent service and food. Table of 8 was there for the Sunday lunch buffet which ran until 2:30pm. Had been to lunch buffet weekdays but never on weekend because we didn't know they did it on Sundays. Very clean. We will be back!

Come here for lunch whenever I can. Great sandwiches. Had fish tacos last time and they were perfect. Today's special was beef sliders and they were awesome. I also recommend the Damon bow tie pasta. Service is excellent.

Delicious!! The service can be hit or miss which is why they lost a star, but the food is excellent. Very flavorful and fresh! A great place for date night, a family with young children, or groups. Plus it's BYOB!!

Ordered curry goat and it was absolutely disgusting!! I am Jamaican born and bred but you don't have to be from Jamaica to know good curry goat. I paid for the meal which she asked me how it was , I replied disgusting , no flavor and she said well people cook curry different. Well I have no problem with Indian ,Trini curry and I know what Jamaican curry is suppose to taste like. If your starving for Jamaican good ,cook your own .... It's that bad!

I like the food. It's very yummy and the people are nice, however I showed up at 2:50 and they were closing at 3, they turned me away because chef has left. :-( This has never happened to me at a restaurant. If you say you're open until 3, you're telling your customers they can walk in at 2:59 and place an order. If you want to leave at 3, then close at 2:30. It's never a good choice to turn away customers and leave a bad experience.

I have always been a fan of Taziki's. I was happy to see MJ finally get one. I'll say that this Taziki's was hit or miss for a while, but lately they have been consistently good. Thursday's is my new favorite day because of the Taziki's Tilapia Taco. I've tried to get fish tacos around here before and eventually just stopped trying. You just can't get good fish tacos unless you are on the coast it seems. The Taziki's Taco sure comes close. The harmony of flavors is very nice and tastes so good with that pasta salad. The only way I would be happier is if that taco was a regular menu item!

My friends and I wandered into Samson Kabob House not knowing what to expect. Wow! Am I glad we did. The restaurant is beautiful, the service excellent and the food was out of this world. We had several vegetarian dishes and found them to be outstanding. I highly recommend the following appetizers: kadu (pumpkin), burani (eggplant) and ashak (dumplings). There were leftovers and I enjoyed them the next day just as much. This is my new favorite restaurant in the area.

In addition to Hummus grill, I never tasted an authentic middle eastern Falafel like Naf Naf make. Pita bread is fresh and amazing. I would recommend the place for any one who likes middle eastern food.
Great food, great service. I have been here six times and enjoyed it everytime. The staff is super - friendly and goes out of its way to make you feel special.

The best bánh mì in the city. The fillings are generous - tofu, pork, and chicken, etc. along with the usual pickled carrots, daikon, and hot peppers. The real clincher for me is that they use the crusty and delicious Sarcones baguettes. I feel like a crusty baguette really allows this sandwich to realize it's full potential. One star off because on a hot day last summer, the gruff dude behind the counter made me a sandwich while not wearing a shirt. Awesome.
Decent South Indian cuisine , had masala dosa and chicken kuthu paratha along with chicken lollipop and mango lassi!, kuthu paratha was spicy and dosa wasn't crispy, taste can be improved !
Excellent buffet, to-go option, amazing staff. Cannot say enough good things. Best Indian in this whole area.
Ughhhhhhhh. SO GOOD! I'm so happy there's finally a legit Dominican spot close by. Now if you'll excuse me, I need to weep over my lunch special from home sickness and then fall into a food coma.

Love all of the vegan, gluten free options! Vegetarian pho with mushrooms and sweet corn soup are my favorites. I always sit in the bar area, there's occasional live music and comfy booths with an inviting atmosphere!

I really liked the atmosphere and design of the restaurant. Beautiful paintings on the wall and cute small area reminding of special areas traditions. I ordered Qablee Palaw. It came with hot bread, house fresh salad and a vegetable dressing. I really liked the food, although I expexted a larger portion. It tasted so good and it was my first time eating at an Afghan restaurant. I did not like the service that much. Although, I recommend checking in this place because of its variety of food, kabobs and pelows and the beautiful design of this restaurant. Give it a shot!!
I had their fish sandwich, falafel, shawarma, gyro at different visits at both Tampa and st Pete locations; delicious food, efficient service, very well taken care of.

We tried this noodle house last weekend and couldn't wait to return this weekend, it was just that delicious! The noodles and dumplings are all handmade and so unbelievably tender. The sauces and broths are filled with layers of flavour that make every bite a heavenly experience. This location has been around for a long time on 107th and it's age shows but it's quaint and the food is all important here! We tried number 111 and it was terrific. The sauce and chilies are not burn your mouth hot, but again each toothsome bite of noodle is coated with the layered complex ground meat chili, peanut, bean vinegar and garlic sauce. The cold cabbage salad disappeared in a flash as did the tender handmade dumplings. Friendly prompt service. Try this place, you'll love it!

Dinner was wonderful. My bf, my friends and I arrived about 15 minutes before they closed. We were the only ones in the restaurant. Needless to say, the staff were very helpful & wonderful. The pad see ew was a larger portion than the lunch size. In any case, it was good! I only wished they used wider rice noodles. The masamun curry was close the authentic version. The fried tofu & sticky rice with custard were really delish as well. My only problem with the sticky rice with custard was the extra coconut cream added on. The selection of teas were great, but I wished they had chrysanthemum tea.
Absolutely love this place. Have been there once a month since I discovered it. The goat and lentil dishes are the best. The service is wonderful.

I LOVE indian food, but there were no nearby options for me until this place opened up! It's a very modern-looking and stylish place. Great location in the Providence area. Wait staff is attentive. Reasonable prices. Decent portion sizes. Gobi Manchurian....I can't say enough about this appetizer. It's so flavorful...spicy and a bit of sweetness. Who knew cauliflower could be so good? Like, I would eat this every day if I could. Chicken Tikka Masala, Paneer Kadai, Goat Biryani, Goat Curry...those are the dishes I've had here so far. Everything has been delicious. And I have to say they have some of the most flavorful goat here that I've ever eaten. Can't wait to come back and explore the menu more!

Nothing exciting to say about this small ordinary Thai restaurant. I had a craving for pad thai and thought of this place for the location. This is near Menards and since I needed to pickup an item, I decided Aroy would be convenient for dinner take out. I wish I had a craving for something else cause the pad thai was not to my liking. The flavor was not bad. I just think it does not compare to most pad thai in other restaurants. The spice was very weak and more on the sweet side than anything. The amount is decent for the price but did not matter since I could not finish all of it. The cucumber salad was so sad. However, the crab rangoon was best I've had in metro east. I would not say this will be my only visit. I tend to give restaurants several try cause one menu item does not spoil the bunch. Until my next visit, two stars is the best I can do.
BYOB and come early or wait. this place is very small and always packed. our service was excellent and my grilled octopus was amazing. i had no complaint and will be back soon.

We grabbed food from Sansom Kabob House twice during our short visit in Philly. After eating at some overhyped & overpriced places in the city, we wanted something reasonable yet satisfying. We love Afghan food (there are some great ones in Fremont, CA), so we had to give this place a shot. I ordered the Sansom kabob & my husband the chablee, and we had no complaints whatsoever. The food was delicious (though not as perfect as what we've had at our favorite kabob place). We went back for another meal on a different day & had the qablee palaw and kabobs (again)... it's a kabob house so one must definitely have these tender, tasty morsels of meat! There was only one server when we had dinner there and a party of 10 or so was dining as well... so service was very slow. We didn't mind, though. We were on vacation & weren't in a rush.

Great Indian food at a very reasonable price. I came here with my wife yesterday and we liked it so much we came back again tonight. The buffet gives a large assortment of dishes (including desserts), all delicious, for under $12.

Buffet here has small variety(very few). Items dont taste well at all!. I also felt there was not even an effort to make them taste well. Only bright side was the nan's. For the same price, next day we had far better indian food in downtown area.

The cuisine is authentic and delicious. The staff are so prompt and kind whether I am dining with family, business, or getting take out. The Saag (spinach), daal (lentils), and Naan (bread) are my favorite, though you can't go wrong with any of it. I suggest the lunch buffet if you wish to try a little bit of everything...great selection!

I was walking home in the cold of night when I suddenly had the craving for hot, delicious samosas. I Yelped around for a bit and found this place, which was nearby. Even though I popped in fifteen minutes before closing, they served me my heart's desire (hot and fresh samosas)-- and I didn't intend to, but the prices were so inexpensive that I ended up ordering a meal and chai along with it. I had gobi masala with garlic naan and mint chutney. The mint chutney was not as savory as I would've liked and I prefer it room temperature rather than cold, but these aren't really things to argue about. I came again with my Grandma and ordered the vegetables Malai Kofta and was similarly impressed. I want to try the buffet next. The impression I'm given is that while their food is pretty good (excellent even, considering the price range and neighborhood) their samosas are the real kings of the menu to me. A great go-to.

I love this place and I used to be a regular except that they do not take children under 12 (tip!). I finally starting coming by again, and I must say it is a great place with amazing meats and the bread is a fresh as it gets. I normally order the Sultan Platter (2 people but you can maybe feed 3). It comes with a variety of meats, salad, humus and bulgur. Baklava is also included. I am not gonna lie to you. It is pricy! And their current list of wines is even more so! I also wish they had better dessert selections. But overall this is among the best Turkish restaurants I have visited across Canada.

I've read great reviews for this restaurant and decided to drop by for a try since I was in the neighbourhood. I'm impressed! Lots of parking in the front, easy access and close to downtown. I have to admit this place is my new Pho heaven. It has lots of room for large groups. Surprisingly, the washroom is very clean. Don't expect 5-star service. When I was there the owner/waiter took my order and I was eating in less than five minutes. Stellar! If you are looking for awesome Pho, check this place out.

Heard about this truck from a couple friends recently so definitely had to try it as soon as I could. I couldn't believe I haven't heard of them earlier being that I'm a Drexel student, but then again, I'm barely on campus! I got the chicken katsu over rice. The katsu was pretty good and they give you a LOT of rice. Overall though, I thought that particular dish was mediocre, maybe 6.5/10. On the other hand, the thai tea was great though, not too much cream like many other places do it, which overpowers the tea. I'd like to try the satay tacos next time, or the Captain Crunch burrito. I'd definitely give this place another try, especially because it's a different style of lunch truck food on campus.

After finishing law school I ate a lot of Chinese food. It was cheap, usually good, and great leftovers. During one of my visits at the hospital I was on a clear liquid diet. I read that this place also served pho and I convinced my friend to go grab some and he could eat the good stuff and I would drink the broth. I an currently on another clear liquid diet, I would rather drink the chicken broth then going back to this place. The pho was bland and so ridiculously priced, and I imagine they are pricing their food knowing that stressed out doctor or an exhausted intern would go there and spend the money. Not me, says I.
Best sloppy joe I've ever had. "Turkish pizza" or Lahmacun. Questionably. Everything else we had was food.

I just went here an hour ago after many years. OMG things haven't changed expect for the renovations. Everything was top notch. Jerk Chicken, Rice and Peas, Cabbage, Oxtails, Beef Patties & Ginger Beer to wash it down. Only thing missing was the Coco Bread :-) Friendly Staff and well worth the wait.
Fish Hoagie, Yum. Food is made to order so prepare to wait or be smart and call it in.

So when I first heard about Zeppoli, I was like " great just what Collingswood needs, another Italian Restaurant '. But then I read the Chefs bio and I was intrigued, I love Vetri and am a fan of Osteria....so I have been waiting rather impatiently to try Collingswoods newest italian addition. My partner and I went tonight, we were lucky to get a reservation as they are booking up fast. First we were treated to a basket of house made breads, semolina , focaccia and a savory zeppoli , YUM ! Then we both had the Insalata verde, market fresh with romaine radicchio and shaved endive delicious. Then we shared a couple of pasta dishes, the spinach gnocchi , one of the best I have ever had, light as a feather, and a cavatelli with a pistachio pesto Awesome ! I had the rib eye cooked to perfection and perfectly seasoned and he had the sword fish and I quote " fracking awesome". For desert I had the chocolate almond torte, which was much lighter than you would expect but just a chocolatey as you would hope, he had the lemon tart, which was divine! Both complimented by a delightful espresso. This delicious meal was made even better by the comfortable room, and the superb service. Our waiter Tom was terrific, attentive without being intrusive. Overall a very positive experience and we look forward to going back. Welcome to the west side we wish you the best of luck ! Nice job chef Joey.

This establishment is a bane to the otherwise QUIET neighborhood in which I live. It was a sad, sad day when they were allowed to continue to play their horrendous "music" at a volume that must wake the American patriots who have been dead for 200 years.

I've been going to Blue Plate since it was called Hill Top for Sunday brunch. My go to dish that I get everytime is the crab bisque. It's amazing! I would go back for that alone. I also get a side of their homemade chips; which are the best homemade chips I've found in the south jersey area. Also, for all the bacon lovers, they actually cook your bacon how you request it. My family only eats crispy crispy bacon and they get it right everytime. It is a small place, so Sunday brunch can get crowded. I've never been there for dinner but I have heard that it's very good.

We found this restaurant by chance when bicycling in Santa Barbara on vacation from the Greater San Francisco Bay Area in July 2011. We were pleasantly surprised by the quality and taste of the entrees; they could easily compete with the Thai restaurants we have up here, and that says much. If in the area again, we will certainly dine there again and again. Their service was equally commendable..

Is this the best Indian/Thai/fusion food I've ever had? No. Is it acceptable enough for me to go back more than once? Yes. Sure, the setup is a little weird and the prices aren't really advertised, but a full take-away box for me is always around $10 and I get two meals out of that. The food is not as spicy as I would like, but I'm okay with that. This place is on the way home, and the food is pretty decent, so for those reasons I'm not picky about it. They usually have a few veggie dishes (some lentil-based, some broccoli-based) and Thai and Indian curries done with lamb or chicken. The taste of the food is good, but a little bland. It does kinda irk me that they charge for naan bread...who charges for naan bread? NOT YOU, NAAN BREAD. Anyway, as an after-work, on-the-way-home, Jesus-I-do-NOT-want-to-cook-tonight place, it's not bad.

I really, really wanted to like this place because 1) it is close to home and 2) they serve 12" Vietnamese sandwiches. When I saw this I immediately began to have fantasies about being able to pop over at any time to pick up a quick banh mi. And since they share a space with a Port o' Subs, it would be like a one-stop shop. "Who wants sandwiches?!" So I brought home a 12" BBQ pork sandwich for Husband and I to share, along with an order of spring rolls and pot stickers (totaling over $20--ouch!) What a disappointment! The sandwich had good bread--fluffy on the inside, crispy on the outside--and the pork had decent flavor, but that is where the flavor ended...the cilantro was wilted and flavorless, and all of the other layers of flavor that make banh mi so delectable were missing. And even though I specifically said that I wanted EVERYTHING on it ("Jalapenos, too?" "Oh yes, definitely jalapenos"), they left off the jalapenos. It basically tasted like meat on bread. The spring rolls weren't much better. They were overstuffed with way too much rice noodles, which overpowered the other flavors in the roll and made the whole thing taste starchy. The pot stickers weren't bad, but not good enough to make up for the rest of the meal. I might be back to try their pho--Husband really wants a shot at the duck pho--but overall I don't think Viet Pho will be getting much more of our business. Which is really too bad, because we could have had a great thing going.

This place is a hidden gem. It is right behind Patel Brothers on Nolensville Pike and the neighborhood isn't what you would call great, but don't be deterred by any of that! My girlfriend and I were here for dinner recently and absolutely loved the food. Given that most Indian restaurants here in Nashville use the same old "meat and curry sauce" formula, Dosa Hut's menu was quite a refreshing change. The menu is limited (and I say this as a good thing!) and has items you'll never find in any other Indian restaurant. As another reviewer pointed out, this place has the BEST dosa in Nashville. We first tried the "Bollywood Masala Dosa", a rice crepe filled with spiced potato hash and smeared on the inside with a spicy chilli chutney. Not only that, the chutneys (coconut and tomato) and sambar (a lentil-based thick soup) commonly served with the dosa were ON POINT, with very authentic flavors. In south India, you always judge the quality of a restaurant by how good their chutney and sambar is and this place's were on par with any good restaurant in south India. We next tried the sambar vada (a thick black gram batter seasoned with spices and deep fried, with the vada dipped in sambar) which was also very good. The freshly chopped onions on top is something I've only seen back home in India, and was a nice addition. We also tried a couple of their chicken dishes - the chicken lollypop and the chicken kothu parota. Both dishes are akin to street food and were so good that they transported us to the streets and alleys back home! The chicken lollypop (drumsticks with a sweet and spicy garlic/honey glaze) was tender on the inside and crispy on the outside. The chicken kothu parota (chopped pieces of flakey bread with chicken, egg and spices) had the perfect amount of heat and depth in flavor. My only minor disappointment was that this was served with raitha (a yogurt sauce) and not the kurma made from chicken bones and left overs (as I've been accustomed to having where I'm from). The waiting staff was really friendly (albeit a little slow, but these dishes seem made to order and do take time) and the prices were reasonable. I'm looking forward to trying the other dishes on the menu and I wish everybody reading this would too!

This place probably has one of the best boba in Florida. The boba is cooked just right - chewy and not hard or soggy. I tried the avocado coconut last time I came and I was actually pleasantly surprised. I also had the pad Thai here. Also very delicious and on par. I think I will come back. 4 stars overall.

I came to this place as I am a lover of pho and it's close to my work. Ordered the Shrimp Salad rolls. Asked for a half order which they offer, however he bought me a full order and when I pointed it out he said "too late now I can pack it to go for you"! I should have to pay for something I didn't order. I was not a fan of these rolls, they weren't put together well and fell apart once picked up. The peanut sauce that accompanies them I bought seems think rather thick and tasted more like peanut butter, again not a fan. I also order the Beef Satay Pho, I was a little disappointed with this also! The soup was almost sweet, I think that was due to there being cucumbers and tomatoes in it. First time I've had this in my Satay. Again not a fan, next time I'll try the beef Pho and if that's no good I won't be returning.

Chiang Mai is one of my very favorite restaurants in Indy, but I was disappointed to learn that they are under new ownership, and that a number of my favorite menu items will be discontinued. I cannot fathom why the new owners would want to drastically alter the menu so far as the remove the entire noodle section. This used to be my go-to restaurant, but that will probably be changing.

Damn this was fresh. I love our immigrant brothers and sisters runnin' gryo shops all over the city, but this was fresh, next level. $13 for lamb gyro and fries (no drink) so just fyi. But it's worth it. Parmesan on the fries was tasty too; exceeded my expectations.

One of my two favorite Thai places in Brandon. I love the Mussaman and Panang. And the Thai Salad is almost a meal by itself. The staff is incredibly friendly and service has always been really really good.

Another new Indonesian store.... great place to practice your indonesian or just grab a bite to eat. has groceries, soda and other stuff like: coco juice, rice, sugar, cooking supplies. they also have a rack that has only sweets and pastries that are brought in from chinatown every day (they told me mayflower bakery) that's not bad, and only 10 cents more than chinatown, but without driving there. they also sell all kinds of phonecards, they are posted all over the wall of the place. they have a glass enclosure there too. it is okay, but still safety first.

I went there today with three of my friends. The food was not horrible, although my "mild" entree was spicy, and my friend's "medium" wasn't spicy at all. We ordered a sampler of four types of naan. One was bad. The other three were mediocre. The quality of chicken used in my Chicken Biryani was not great. Overall, this place wouldn't be awful if not for the horrendous service. Our waiter was Martin. Martin ignored our table. When the time came for us to pay, we had to wait twenty minutes for them to take our check. Slow, poor service brings this restaurant down to one I will not visit again.

We are not from here, but we love Thai food. This is by far the best Thai food experience we have ever had. This place is phenomenal and the food is amazing. I would highly recommend the pad Thai and the chicken masaman. The staff is extremely friendly and super efficient. This place is super relaxing and extremely clean. We will definitely be back to this amazing establishment. Thank you!!

This place is great ! The decor is stunning , service is good and food is delicious !we went there for brunch and everything was very delicious ! I grew up on Arabic food, so I know how it's supposed to be, and their food is the real thing ! It is a little pricey tho, and the portions are a little small . But i would still back there for the great food !

Visiting from California, I didn't expect much. Just wanted to have some asian fare far from home. For a Thai restaurant, food quality was below average and I was prepared for that. What irritated me was how poor their service was. Servers were never around except when they took orders and delivered food. I actually had to call the restaurant from my table to grab their attention. They also misdelivered my food to another table. Then they charged over 20 percent gratuity for a group of 7. One star because i cannot give a zero.

Just had an excellent very late lunch here. Ordered the combo hot pot and it was delicious. Had plenty of pork, chicken, shrimp, and tofu. Even the tofu was very tasty. Vegetables, a plenty, even enough to satisfy me. The only thing that could've made it any better would have been brown rice instead of white, there was no choice and a warm plate that the rice came on. The hot pot itself was still bubbling as it was put on the table and I really appreciated that. It was in a heavy ceramic dish that stayed hot throughout the meal. I would definitely come back here to try a different selection.

We went for happy hour, expecting wonderfulness. What we got was ONE drink (bartenders choice) and one that I detest, expensive, stupid "small plates", one of which was ONE scallop in a cream sauce. Why bother. We won't be returning any time soon

The picture of the bldg in some of the reviews must be the old address. They have expanded into new space, still on Lancaster Ave. ordered beef satay, beef yum yum salad, red curry chicken, chicked pad thai and silver noodles with shrimp. Everything flavorful and distinct. Good service, looks like a BYO
This place is awesome. Service is stupendous, food is top notch. A definite go-to. Even if you don't care for spicy Thai, the other menu items are so well-prepared and delicious.

I grew up in St. Pete and return about once a year to see family . . . one of my "must stops" is Tangelo's Grill. I love the Cuban Sandwich - Ybor Style with some Calypso Sauce added, plantains and their refreshing sangria. The atmosphere is very relaxed and the owners are wonderful and friendly. A TRUE GEM! - Tad

I went to Fez, never having been before, and had an awesome experience. The decor is set up to give the feel of being in a tent. Low lighting, beautiful belly dancer, the round table/couch seating was excellent for group conversation and for leaning back comfortably when smoking hookah and after 7 rounds of delicious, Moroccan food. All the food was very tasty. This is no in and out restaurant, our group was there for about 2.5 hours lounging, conversing, hookah-ing, and eating. I loved that. I didn't feel rushed to get out, and our server was friendly and did a great job getting us what we needed. 9 of us got the 7 course meal, and though eating everything with your hands was something I wasn't use to, I feel it brought the group closer together. $5 bottled beers, not a bad price for that part of the city. All in all a wonderful dining experience.

We ordered Tom Yum which was great. The rest of the food we ordered was not. The Shrimp Pad Thai was dry and flavorless. The green curry was tasty but soooo watery that it should have been under the soup section. I will not order from here again. Unfortunately, can't find good Thai food in philly. I guess I'll have to keep looking.
The buffet is meh. The selection is reasonable but the food is not exciting. Given that the buffet is all you can eat, however, you will not leave hungry.

Really great staff but very basic chicken. There really isn't anything craft about it. Chicken tenders fried in a pretzel batter is hardly craft. I guess I was expecting a little more variety. On the up side, the dark chicken tenders were pretty tender.The white tenders lacked flavor. Additionally the avocado on the mixed green salad is actually guacamole. I was excited to try this place but can't say I'll be back.

LOVE this spot. Everything on their menu is amazing. Love their Mac and cheese, jerk chicken wings, rice and peas, oxtail and curried goat. Be sure to ask for some oxtail gravy on your rice and peas mmmmm

This is a good find on the Westside. Great ambiance. A family owned venture with excellent Vietmanese and Chinese food. A small, but romantic hole in the wall. In a small strip mall on the corner of Georgetown and Lafayette Roads--easy to pass by, but don't.

I am not a falafel fan, but I am a huge fan of this shop's fresh whole wheat pita, zataar bread, tabouli, olives, and spices. This is one of the few places where I can find the proper kind of bagged zataar (a Middle Eastern spice mix with thyme, sumac, sesame seeds, and salt) which is a necessary ingredient for Fatoosh and makes a delicious grilled, herbed chicken (marinate the chicken overnight in lemon juice, olive oil and a copious amount of zataar). Their zataar bread (which are flat disks like pizza) is praiseworthy. The bread is thin, crusted and chewy with just the right amount of baked in zataar and olive oil, Delicious hot or cold, and zataar bread is a perfect dipper for hummus or baba ghanoush.

3.5 stars because they were out of both of our first food choices (Zucchini Carpaccio & Coca Cola Beef Brisket) and a couple of others on a Tuesday night. Really nice atmosphere, service and food was good. Hummus "King of Kings" was good. Meet and Cheese Plate you can't go wrong Pizza with meat on top (name?), not good, even with hummus on top Would go back...:) Recommend for something a little different, this is a couples restaurant per my single friend. ;)

I love Indian food. Very good food, tasty and probably the better quality Indian food I've ever had. The restaurant was full of Indians, which to me is always a good sign. I had the lamb saag and some mango lassi. Yummy. Service was real slow. Our waiter had an iPad to take orders which is cool, but it obviously doesn't track food. He came by with our meals a good 35-45 minutes in, and thought we already had our appetizers. He comped my soda for the mess up. The twenty minute ride back to my hotel was too long. I felt every bump and prayed things would hold together. I was cross legged in the elevator as I rose to the 7th floor. I darted to my room just in time to make it to the bathroom as my lamb saag exited with fury.

Fun spot with great Afro-Carribean music, delicious food and urban vibe. We ordered the byssop and the ginger drinks and they were interesting and tasty. I had the vegetarian entree and the servings were huge! You could definitely get the entree, a couple of extra sides and share it all with a friend. We ended up with lots of leftovers. Service was a bit slow, but super-nice. I got the sense that this is a family-owned restaurant, and the family was working the service. I like that this place is international and gives us a slice of another continent. Definitely worth the stop!

Finally, a restaurant in Wilmington that gets it. If the city wants to revamp its food/bar scene they should use the blueprint from this place. We sampled a bit of everything during our visit. Speciality cocktails, the appetizer sampler (pork dumplings are top notch). I had the pork pho (with an egg) and my wife had the shrimp pad tai both were very tasty and fresh. Service was good and the restaurant itself was modern and tastefully decorated. Anyone who has been to a decent restaurant will know this place is a winner the minute they walk in. I'll be a regular at this joint!
Excellent food with great customer service. The owners are great and will go beyond to earn customer value. Will highly recommend for anyone in Newtown looking for great Indian food
Fun little bar with great drinks! Jessie the bartender is amazing and so cute! Indoor and outdoor bar area.

When we really need a fix of authentic Vietnamese (or Thai) food, we head for Oriental Pearl in Upper Chichester. I love the fresh herbs.
