I have had so many dishes there that I can't even enumerate, but I have never had a bad one--except that we learned we dont want to eat tripe. But every dish is masterfully created and filled with flavor. Latest discovery was Basil beef with a nice mix of basil, beef and nice veggies. I'd tell you about hte mango salad, but if I EVER got there and found they didn't have the ingredients for MINE, I'd never forgive you. so I'm not going to tell you about it.
Just ok... This was much better in the past. It is not bad but not up to what I would consider good Thai food
Would give no stars if I could. Ordered delivery on 6/14/2018. This place gave me food poisoning that's lasted for 24 hours so far. Eat at your own risk.

Pho Cam Ly always hits the spot if you are looking for fresh and filling Vietnamese food. The prices are great also. Along this stretch of Magazine Street, it is difficult to find anywhere with as good of prices. I usually get the Grilled Pork Vermicelli or the Tofu Pho. BYOB if you are looking to drink. They charge a $5 corkage fee for wine, not exactly sure how much for beer.
I like this place a lot and order from them frequently. Their food is very very good and their service is great. Would 10/10 recommend.
Our appetizer and our meals were delicious, prepared from scratch in a timely manner. The service was personable and excellent.

We come here almost every Sunday for breakfast and it never disappoints. The "special menu" is based off what's in season and is always delicious. The stuffed French toast and pancakes are unbeatable. If you like a more savory breakfast the eggs Normandy are also a personal favorite. The staff is extremely friendly and even when the place is packed they still greet you with a smile and a calm disposition. Their dinner and lunch menu are also extremely good but the breakfast is the BEST!

I used to live in Edmonton, and recently I paid Remedy another visit after two years of being a part. We were in Edmonton for a week, I was at Remedy on three occasions, that should be telling. I like the place. Once upon a time it had delicious vegan cheesecake, that time appears to be no more. However they still have lots of other vegan or gluten free and/or other treats that look delicious but I've never eaten. They have an amazing selection of teas, I've never counted, but it looks like at least 30? Parking is terrible, take the bus, or park on the street. The lot beside Remedy is usually full, and has always been. They are generally catering to the campus/pedestrian crowd, and you can tell with the random music playlist and the general ambiance of the place. You'll notice some exhausted academics plodding along on their laptops because hey - free wifi with power outlets makes for a good nerdy time. There is also alcohol if that's what you're looking for, and dinner options (for nearly anyone, omnivores and vegans). I wish Remedy was in Toronto, because it would be appreciated, and I'd probably go there at least once a week. I miss you Remedy. For additional amusement, please note the delightful graffiti in the bathrooms. It's kind of awesome and/or silly.
Delivery is great, but the customer service is bad. I called to place an order for takeout sushi and the guy first placed me on hold then hung up on me. Lol Pretty bad service.

This is basically Indian food for white people. It is NOT spicy whatsoever, it is extremely mild. I don't doubt that the owners know how to cook, but I suspect that they're catering the food to whatthey think most of the public would want. The restaurant serves an Indian buffet which is charged for by the pound. They also serve some breakfast dishes. I'm not sure how much they charge per pound but a full plate was about $10. The buffet offered a variety of chickpea dishes and lentils - there were about four vegetarian options total. The meat section had some chicken, beef, and fish options. There were also samosas. They naans they give are not the nice ones that they have in other places, these ones are the kind they just heat up in a pan. I don't think they have the right oven for the real naans. I'm only giving this place 2 stars but don't let that stop you from trying it out if you've never had Indian food before or if you can't take spicy foods. You'd probably like it if it's your first time to try Indian. It's also better than Nirvana and Taj Mahal (which are the only other two indian buffets I know about and which I'd give about a half a star each). New Orleans desperately needs some good Indian/Paki food.

Great BYOB in South Philly. Informal casual atmosphere. Good menu selection: pasta, seafood and meat all have great choices. Seafood alla scannicchio is my personal favorite. Portion sizes are large and you should have enough to take home for lunch the following day. Complimentary limoncello is a great way to end the evening.

So glad we have this restaurant in Apollo Beach! Everything I've tried has been delicious, and the service is quick and friendly. I am especially fond of their rice. Not sure how they spice it, but it's wonderful.

"Good option in buffet..." I went there for the buffet so this is a review for that. I did not try ala carte yet. A buffet is $15 on Friday, nearby restaurants charge $10 so compared to that, expensive. Courteous staff, good ambience... mirror on the whole wall makes u feel like this is a big restaurant. There was 4 option in Nonveg starters (i like malai kabab and chapali kabab) and as a usual poor option for veg fellas. 2-3 option in both veg and nonveg entree. Mango juice (too much sugar) along with gulab jamun very good) and gajar ka halwa (just ok). I liked the food but $15 is a bit more for the buffet.

Best Carribean food I've had. It gets extremely packed, so I'd strongly advise calling in your order. Then you can walk to the front of the long lines. I've had the curry chicken, and their ox tails, both are great. Beef patties are really good too, and so is the fried fish. It isnt too expensive. I'd highly recommend this place. Dont let the area scare u away!

We love Coco Thai. The food is tasty and the waitstaff is friendly and helpful. The owner remembers our name from our first visit. This is our weekly go-to place, and by far the best ambiance in town. I especially like the Masaman curry and also the Penang Curry. I hope that An, the owner, will market their homemade thai tea ice cream more, because it is heavenly and I wish she sold it by the pint.

Briefly: Very good food with a diverse menu including dosa in a nice space. Cash only. Quick and friendly service. Default spiciness is not very spicy. Very good food, with a larger and more diverse menu than Shere-E-Punjab. We got takeout, but the restaurant looked casual, pleasant and bright, though it's certainly not fancy and is small, with just a few tables. Two groups were eating in and seemed to be having a good time. The menu seems to have all the standard Indian restaurant dishes plus dosa and other less familiar (and I think southern Indian) dishes. The selection of vegetarian dishes is large and diverse. We got masala dosa and aloo mutter with samosas and sesame naan. Everything was very good. I'd never had sesame nan before and enjoyed it. The takeout containers were neatly labeled with printed stickers, which is a nice touch. Service was fast, with my order ready in 15 minutes as promised. I was told on the phone that cash was strongly preferred, but a sign in the restaurant said cash only. The food isn't cheap, but I was satisfied with both quantity and value. It's great to have another good option for Indian food in the area, and though I like Shere-E-Punjab, this place may be my new default takeout (even though it's farther away) because they have dosa and a broader selection of dishes.

Tried the JAS Himalayan. Indian Restaurant. We had Chicken and Lamb Tika Masala. Ask for mild and it was very nice. The garlic Naan was wonderful. Prices were reasonable and service was friendly and attentive.

This is one of the few eateries in Delaware that I truly enjoyed. It's the perfect spot for a quick bite of Indian food. Other reviewers are certainly correct in comparing it to Chipotle. Like Chipotle, I often found that I could never finish one portion. With guaranteed leftovers, I always felt like I got my money's worth. I pretty much ate everything here, and I always topped with the spiciest sauce. Yum! And I loved the ginormous samosas. I also appreciated the alway-friendly staff. No, this Indian food might not be particularly "authentic", but it's quick, cheap, and tasty.

I've got to go back, after reading some of the reviews. I should give this place another shot. I love Ethiopian food. I lived in New York for awhile and with all the selection there - it was my favorite cuisine. I didn't like the food at Queen of Sheba. It didn't taste fresh. One of the dishes on our combination plate was way too bitter. I didn't eat more than one bite. The waitress wasn't very nice. We brought in a restaurant.com coupon and she wasn't very accommodating. I should give it another shot because I really want to like this place. I hesitate, though, because really my meal was just gross.

We ordered Basil Spice delivery through the Postmates app on Sunday around 7:00 pm. It came in a reasonable time.The chicken pot stickers were pretty good and the crunchy chicken spring rolls were decent. My 16 year old stepson said the chicken pad Thai was pretty good and he ate all of it. We also ordered red curry chicken and green curry pork, paying over $3 for extra pork. The meats in the curry dishes were switched, that was the first problem. So we had red curry pork and green curry chicken instead of what we ordered. Then, there was barely any meat in either dish, like 5 bites of pork! The veggies looked like they were from a frozen $1 bag from the grocery store. All around the curry was tasteless and then we barely got enough rice for both entrees. Including the Postmates delivery fees, it was a $60 meal for 3 ppl and wasn't worth it. Probably won't order again.

To keep my review short and sweet... Went here for drinks with my friend on a Friday night- everywhere else we tried was packed. Ended up being able to get seating by the bar and then had a BLAST- cheap drinks, an interesting/eclectic group of people to talk to, and the best part was that my line of sight was douche-free all night. They had a jukebox- one of my favorite things when inebriated. The stools were a bit uncomfortable, though, although maybe it's just because I'm getting OLD. We stayed til the bar closed. Next time I'm in West Philly on a Friday or Saturday night, I'll be here, rocking out with my friend to "Kiss From a Rose" and ordering PBRs and shots for everyone in sight.

I was pleasantly surprised when I dined here last night. It was a quiet evening and the dining area is pretty small. However, I loved everything I ordered--Garlic Naan, Chicken Tikka Masala, Shrimp Pakor, and a shrimp dish (I forget the name). I had no issues with service either. I usually go to Tiffins for my go-to spot but I think this place will replace it since it is closer to home. I'll be back to try more dishes and even try the lunch buffet.

Had lunch today with family from out of town which I haven't seen in three years. This was also my first time here. Everything was great. Our server Ashley was amazing. We ordered apps and there was enough time in btwn apps and entrees to enjoy both of them. Always had refills and dirty dishes taken away immediately. She knew we were in no rush and let us enjoy our company without trying to rush us out. The food was great! The melon shrimp was awesome along with the crispy green beans which my dad loved. Thanks for a great experience. Will return!

The atmosphere of the restaurant is nice. The service is ok. Good selection of beer and wine. I was a little disappointed by the food though. It must be northern Thai style. I had a boat style noodle. It has a strong smell compared to other Thai food soup noodles I normally have. The taste was ok but the strong smell restricted me from enjoying the food.

my husband and i always get the groupon for fulins when it comes up. it's one of our favorite places to go for a "nicer" dinning experience. the steamed chicken dumplings appetizer is one of our favorites, and the egg flower soup is pretty splendid as well...i will actually go to fulin's just because i'm craving egg drop/flower soup. we've always had great service here too. the servers have a professional manner, which my husband and i appreciate for a calm, nice dinning experience. reading through some of the other reviews, the chicken i've gotten has always been cooked perfectly, the california roll is pretty yummy, and i think they do nice job of serving delicious food from several ethnic cuisines. awesome: steamed chicken dumplings; egg flower soup, general tsu's chicken, mongolian beef, kung pao chicken, and spicy sesame beef.

The only Ethiopian restaurant in Tampa so it's safe to call it the best! The food is very good and you can tell it's made fresh. I usually order the sample platter so I can try a little bit of everything. The menu has a lot of options though, and it can be hard to choose just one dish. The atmosphere is very ethnic, and the staff are very nice and attentive. It's one of my favorite places to eat in South Tampa. Delicious and affordable!

We had lunch here on a Saturday - the food was delicious! I had three vegetarian sides - pumpkin, Dahl and cauliflower - with rice. Superb, especially the Dahl. My friend had the chicken kebab and a dumpling dish and said both were excellent.
The food it on point with Dominican food. Only downside it the hours of operation. The yucca is delicious. He mango wings are tasty and the soup is ohhh so good. You can't go wrong with their menu
Mediocre main dishes. Very cheerful staff, tasty cauliflower curry soup! Will not stop again when on next road trip.
It's all about the curry here! Their soups aren't the best, but as far as spicy Thai deilciousness goes...possibly the BEST I've ever had!!! I'm pretty obsessed with this place!

Extremely poor managed. We waited and already signed in only for the wait staff to tell us later after 30 minute wait that there would be another 30-40 minute wait. The entire time we were waiting we had thought they were setting up our tables, but the wait staff couldn't tell one Asian group from another so they supposedly miscommunicated the information to us. Ridiculous, outrageous and offensive. We left.

I love this place! The service is always prompt and the food is always fresh. Never a problem with customer service or the food. They are always there to accommodate your needs are a reasonable price. Their lunch specials are awesome and the drinks.. even better!

My son and I had dinner here last night. All the food we ordered was very nicely prepared and presented. The flavors were exquisite and well balanced. The wait staff was attentive and efficient as well. Overall, a very good experience and I will definitely add this place into my rotation.

My wife and I have come to enjoy Thai food within the last year-and-a-half and have explored several Thai restaurants. Siam Cafe is pretty good for service and friendliness. The menu is fairly good for non-vegetarians. For us vegetarians, the selection is limited to about 5 items. My wife had the stir fried vegetables with tofu and I had the green curry with tofu. Both were excellent with copious amounts of food. The fried spring rolls were light and delicately delicious. Refills on our iced tea were attended to quickly. Parking looks to be limited to about 11 spaces unless there's more that I didn't see.

It seems like this place has had a gradual decline in service and quality. The first few times I dined there, I had a decent experience. However, this past Saturday left me wanting for more. :( We sat at the bar and it was a fun environment. The servers were chatting us up, everyone was wearing Halloween costumes. We ordered two beers and two entrees, as we were in a hurry. I finished my beer and sat there with an empty glass for awhile. Meanwhile, the bartender sat down to have a smoke and eat a bagel.... uh, wtf? I understand if you want a smoke break, but I want a beer! I can understand coursing the meal so things come out at different times. I enjoy it. It is very nice to get the chance to try everything without feeling rushed. However, when two people order two entrees, they should come out at the same time, right? My salad (my sad little salad) came out a solid ten minutes before my date's gyro. The bizarre thing about it, is that essentially, we ordered the same thing. The only difference was that his food had a pita underneath it! I suppose we ordered the wrong things... but our food was definitely lacking. I am sure it's fun to dine at Momo's when the belly dancers are out... but I really thought the food was lame o. Booo.

I'm so happy more Vietnamese restaurants are popping up in center city! This place is a great addition to the neighborhood. It's conveniently located within walking distance of my apartment and similar in taste to the other places I like to go to in South Philly. Staff is super friendly and prepare your order quickly. The restaurant itself is very large and clean. Its turning into one of my favorite spots to get Pho. It's a little on the pricey side compared to other Vietnamese restaurants. However, that's true for all center city restaurants and the serving size is large. I'll need to come back for bahn mi and coffee!

I do have to start by saying that the delivery guy was very nice. However, the food itself was not really good. My boyfriend ordered the salmon platter which was good overall. But, we didn't really like the hummus that he chose as a side. In fact, it actually brought the flavored of everything waaaay down. I ordered a Greek salad with a side of falafel (which was also not brought with the original food...had to wait about 20 more minutes). The falafel ended up coming in a wrap/pita, which was not expected. The falafel had ZERO flavor and was covered in the equally flavorless hummus. I was pretty disappointed cause the only thing that gave me any flavor were the vegetables (onions, peppers) from the salad. Oh also, the tzatziki sauce tasted good at first. But then halfway through, it tasted like mayo. Womp.
Did a ToGo and really liked the food. Pad Thai, Pad Ki Mao, Vegetable Rolls were all nice. Will definitely go back if I am in that area.

Though I've still enjoyed some of the vegetarian dishes here, the quality has declined somewhat. (I never found the meat dishes good here before, so that hasn't changed.) Meanwhile, catering prices have gone up. 1. Saag paneer had much less cheese, was greasier & not as flavourful. Cheese cubes hadn't softened & absorbed flavour. 2. Aloo gobi (cauliflower & potato) seemed undercooked such that the flavours hadn't developed. The cauliflower was too raw & hadn't softened up sufficiently to absorb the flavours. The veggies either need to be cooked longer or cut into smaller pieces so they cook faster. 3. Navratan Korma had a similar problem: vegetables are undercooked & lacking in flavour. 4. Veg kofta was still tasty, but also a little undercooked (in the middle). 5. Baigan bharta seemed greasier and not as tasty as before.

I flew into town and heard about Marjie's Grill. WOW !!! I came for dinner and am back two days later to try lunch. I love southern food but this chef takes it to a new level, bringing tastes from Southeast Asia to the southern meats and greens. The porkbelly with herbs and a dipping sauce was my personal fav the first time but the grilled sheephead today is just delicious. Try it. This place is good-- very good!

Writing an update ! After work in evening we were looking for places to eat around Allentown, PA. My colleague was craving for Dosas then we decided to drive to this place instead to NJ. We ordered drumsticks, chilli chicken, onion dosa and Pesarattu with upma and tea. The food was really disgusting, bland and have no flavor !! Both of us had stomach upset for next 2 days. Strongly feel like punishing these people. I rather travel another 30 mins more to NJ. I don't recommend this place and we are never going back. Wish I could give them zero.
I had the squid lunch special. Two problems: 1) Virtually no squid. 2) Virtually no taste, despite a few hot peppers. All for a mere $14 with tip.

The Banh Mi sandwiches and Pho are both really good. The bread was nice and soft and the veggies really fresh and crisp, no greasy spoon feeling here. The price of the Pho is too high so I won't be eating that often. Service is really good, always plenty of people available if you need help. If you're in a hurry you can order & pay at the counter. The place (and employees) are very clean. My favorite thing in Vietnam is the coffee (they roast their beans in cocoa & butter oil) so I must review that as well. The Viet iced coffee with sweetened condensed milk was pretty decent and had a unique taste, I detect Cafe Due Monde with a shot of Mocha Mix (no condensed milk?) but I could be wrong. CDM is basically strong New Orleans coffee mixed with chicory and is commonly used by Viet-Americans. I can buy a can of it for $8.00 and it would last me weeks so charging $4.25 for one serving is a rip. Peets and Starbucks can get away with charging that price because you're getting premium beans and a cup crafted by a trained barista from an espresso machine that costs thousands of dollars. Here you're getting cheap, pre-ground coffee brewed in a large batch so they should ease up on the price. In summary I want sandwich, coffee and tip to total $10.00 or less. 5 stars if they can make it happen.

I have a long standing preference for this restaurant! I have known the owner since he was a waiter in another restaurant on 2nd and Chestnut. The buffet always has several dishes that I want to eat and the desserts are always delightful. I enjoy the take out as well, if I am feeling virtuous I can turn them into 2 meals, but sometimes they are so tasty I eat the whole thing!

MK's has a friendly relaxed atmosphere. Their menu is simple and small but the food was tasty. Service was prompt and courteous. One thing I would recommend is obtaining their liquor license... Multiple patrons asked if they had wine or beer while we were eating our meal. They have a rather large bar that is unused and therefore makes the restaurant look a bit unfinished.

We visited tonight using a Groupon, having never visited before. We ordered Saganaki, Spanikopita, vegetarian dolmades, calamari, and the lamb empanadas. Everything was excellent and fresh. Kayla was a great server and the bill, even without the Groupon, was quite reasonable. Beer selection was adequate and baklava was delish! Our kids (10 and 14) felt right at home, even on a Friday night, but the atmosphere was nice enough for a date, as well. We will return!

I eat here regularly (three times a week)! I love it! I enjoy the choices of Indian food and the casualness of the restaurant. Its clean and very efficient! The prices are under 10$ for almost everything and you get alot of food. The style of the restaurant is basically an Indian MOEs, you select everything from sauce to meats to toppings and build your meal.

I've been to Mizu several times and am never disappointed. The service is wonderful the food is delicious and plated beautifully. The staff is so friendly and always leaves us with a wonderful experience!

Ordered from UberEATS. My main complaint is that their meals do not come with rice. I obviously ordered from my phone and it could been the app but it was not clear, that their 16 oz did not include rice. It just initially looked like the difference was in in size. After I further invested a realized the difference Once again possibly an issue to take up with app. But it did not take away from the fact that I ordered my food, and I had tikka masala naan and no rice. So that was an instant bummer. It could've been more clear, or just charge me 2 dollars more and include rice with every meal. Also it is kinda expensive. The food isn't bad, but it is not anything spectacular.

I have ordered from here a few nights ago and let me tell you, you will not be disappointed with their authentic Indian cuisine. I have ordered the vegetable samosas. It's very huge and flavorful. The sauces that came with it, a perfect combo for a mouthgasm. The chicken tikka masala and chicken markhani (butter chicken) was light, creamy, and had a tint of sweetness. They both have very distinctive flavors with the right amount of spices. It will leave you craving for more after every bite. The goat curry was on the gamy side. The curry sauce helped keep the balance in the flavors. Would I order this again? No, but it definitely worth a try. Yes, I would highly recommend this Indian restaurant to those who enjoys flavorful spices that is incorporated into a mouth watering experience.

Very disappointed. Poor service and it was not crowded. Had flaming cheese and had to pay extra for the Pita otherwise there would be nothing to put the cheese on! The Pita was paste-like and floury. Our entrees were very good, but sized small at best. Refills on drinks came slow. No belly dancers...a Jazz band played instead. In the past, the food was delish and the belly dancers made it an event. Used my Groupon, but sadly...we wont be going back. Michael's had much better food....and service.
wonderful food, great service, and a lovely location! food was a bit more expensive than we anticipated, but incredible quality!

Our go to Indian take out restaurant. Everything we get is great, you really can't go wrong. And the staff is always pleasant and accommodating. Staples for us are spinach chaat and chicken kadai made the traditional way.

I really hope this place maintains their quality of Indian food. I would have to agree with the rest of the reviewers and say that this definitely my go to Indian place anywhere within 15 miles of this area. The authenticity and quality of this food was made reaffirmed after seeing the head chef was an elderly Indian gentleman. It truly feels like home cooked Indian food and is among the best I've had period. Get some grub here, i definitely am tonight.

One of the better restaurants in Brandon. I don't get here as often as I like but every time I go the food is fresh and served quick. The servers are helpful and attentive. Prices are in line with other Thai restaurants around but I think this food is better. Usual selection with some wonderful chef specials.
This place never lets me down. Great indian, very knowledgable staff regarding gluten free, and there are lots of gluten free and vegan options. They even made GF naan for me. Great all around

3.5 - 4 stars - never actually ate in the restaurant but I get takeout here all the time. I tried almost all the Kabob meals and they range from good to very good In my opinion. You get your choice of kabob (or combo of kabob's), Afghan rice, salad and Afghan bread (very thick pita). Warning - the Chutney sauce is very spicy so be careful. My preference is the chicken or beef but the lamb is also good. The beef option is marinated / spiced ground beef and definately a highlight on the menu. The kabobs are always cooked perfectly and never dried out. If you want a lighter meal, get the kabob salad and skip the rice. I'm certainly not a rice connoisseur but Afghan rice has a different texture, a larger grain and most importantly delicious. I love this rice. Kabob main courses are in the $20 range and portion size is above average. Recommended BK

Four stars because of there coffee and there assorted la bus bakery items.The ambience is nice one star for the bitches that work there.The other reviews are spot on withe the rude clientele. Wake up a@#holes you still open because we spend our cash there.
Delicious! The jerk sauce is perfect and the festival dumplings amazing! Polite service. Couldn't ask for more.

This review is not very fair to the truck owners. They offer great food and very pleasant service. However, it is NOT worth braving the elements for a 30-40 minute wait just to get a food truck lunch. Food truck lunches are about convenience and value. The heat stroke at the end sort of takes away your appetite for enjoying the food, and the unpredictably long waits disrupt your whole schedule. So this review mainly reflects the perils of their success. If you can catch them at an off-peak hour, I'm sure it will be worth it. The food is significantly better than the average food truck, but they are also slightly pricier. Got the short rib tacos and a tilapia burrito (both pretty good).

I like this place.. quite and good service.. but don't like the music.. looks like the CD has scratches and it repeats over and over one song.. I wanted to eat really fast and get out.. Taste: alright (I ordered pho for safe..I might try 'real dish' later..)
Happened to come across this place due to hurricane Mathew, best Puerto Rican food I have had in the whole state of Florida and I have tried a few

MM MM I'm a faithful patron. Great food, awesome price, very convienient! The bathroom could use sprucing up but the owner's wife standing to greet & bid us farewell was a homey remedy of kindness to make up for it. I loved it and plan to visit again soon. :)

Decent Pho. Had the steak, flank and tendon. Generous portion of meat. Meat oddly flavourless as if it had been boiled. Broth decent but not fabulous. Green onion cakes were good. The service was quick and very friendly. We will stop by again if we are in the area but are unlikely to make a special trip to eat here. It's a place that could grow on you.
Best Indian food I've ever had. I got take out...the chicken curry. It was SO good! The garlic naan was amazing too. I'll definitely be back!
Such fun! We have been listening the big band during our tuesday night from 8-9 pm. Prices are really good. Food was amazing.
This place is a hidden gem. Food is delicious and their homemade fruit teas are second to none. Atmosphere is kind of lame but highly recommend grabbing some for take out.

Found this restaurant through Groupon. From my understand typically, lunch is buffet style and in the evening was the traditional order off the menu. My husband and I went for dinner. We were greeted at the door and taken to our table but not offered a menu. There was only one other table in the restaurant at the time but it took probably about 5mins before the server realized we needed menus and water. For appetizers, we got the samosa chat and another "street food", both recommended by the server. Dinner was goat korma, chicken korma, garlic naan, and tandoori chicken. We were both very satisfied with our dinner. Flavoring was amazing and portions was filing. The server was nice and personable. We can't wait to come back!

Really good food. Have had some issues with consistency of quality and order completeness. But they are really working hard to deliver a high-quality product. Love their Big Salad and Duo most of all. Chicken and Gyro meat are really juicy. Overall i love this place. Order there once a week. I like that they offer delivery on most days.
Great food, so so service, small portions, overall overpriced and sandwiched between two really sketchy motels.

Have taken out many times and have eaten there once. The food continues to be fantastic (best chicken I've ever had at an Indian restaurant), and the people there are fantastic. Wishing these folks all the success in the world and looking forward to continuing to frequent them for years to come!

I made reservations here for my birthday by a friend's recommendation. The service was TERRIBLE! The majority of my guests were running late because of the crazy traffic around Providence Marketplace on a Friday night, and the manager was very rude and started taking my tables away without asking! This caused three of my guests to have NO WHERE to sit! (We ended up squeezing into the booths together... since the workers didn't really care.) The tables were dirty, one of the booth's chair my friend was sitting on was caving in, and the table decorations were very cheap!!! We also one had ONE waitress working our party, which is pretty ridiculous. She mixed our orders up with other people's and took over an hour to even bring change back. I myself ordered the sesame chicken, and it was overly sweet. I've never experienced service this bad. Also, I will never come back to this restaurant again!!

Sadly, I must downgrade my prior enthusiastic evaluations of Mojito's Rum Bar & Grill. Stopped-in Saturday, mid-afternoon, for a respite from our weekly bicycle tour of the area, as usual. WHAT, you have no Coors Light ? You say you don't carry it now ? Barmaid, did Carla quit ordering MY Coors Light ? What's that: "Who's Carla?" You must be really new here ! Twenty points-off penalty right there. So, If I want a "cold-one", this favorite oasis is now off my list ! Hmmm. . . . LSU pre-game party was in full-swing, live band and crowd. We had to wait for bar seats. Carla & Bruce have worked so hard to make this great place a success; why diss over 1/4 of beer-drinkers ? This may "work" with tourist one-timers; but your local regulars, like me, surely don't like it ! Please give me back my ice-cold "Silver Bullets"; cans or draft would be A-OK ! Sadly, Rick
A little pricey, but ree-lee effin' good.

The down stairs was intimate and clean and friendly. The lamb was exquisite salad was awesome and the cheese platter was amazing these folks deserve to be busy. Get there as soon as possible you will love it!

Soon after posting this review, the owner of the restaurant contacted me, apologizing. His attention to detail and good intentions shouldn't go unnoticed, especially since he informed me that he has addressed this issue with his staff. Of course, I can't speak for those that have read about my latest experience, but I do like their pho so I'll be back to give Sizzling Wok another chance.
I am usually not the picky. But the food here is terribly bad. I have never had this bad Aloo Tikki Chat ever in my life. Their curry and protein was equally bad :( Very disappointed!
Always very tasty food. A good variety is available, served on top of fermented bread. Great atmosphere with typical Ethiopian decor. Service is fast and friendly.

This is the best food truck in the city that I ever seen. The food is awesome and different everyday. You never know what you'll get until you order- This is the mystery that makes this truck special. After being a frequent customer it was much easier to have a conversation with the man. You just had to get to know him. 5 hour he spend just to clean his food truck... I can never eat again at another food truck- It's like having your own chef. Have I mentioned that beverage was part of the menu this week? Hey! Don't expect it at your next visit.... It's just mysteriously delicious... Lol..

We were blown away by this place. Honestly, we never have high expectations for Asian places in the burbs. We eat a lot of Asian food... and were after something lighter between meetings. The lunch special they offer is great, and it seemed like everyone in the place was ordering it. There are plenty of options, and the special comes with salad and soup... which is fantastic. I am not usually in Blue Bell for lunch, but this is certainly going to remain at the top of my list for the days when I am. Definitely worth checking out if in the area!
good for quick pit stop on a short lunch break unless there is a line. the have limited offerings of pho and rice and vermiclli plates. But what they offer is good. not DIVINE but pretty good.

Queen of Sheba is the best Ethiopian Cuisine I've ever had! You can taste the quality and authenticity in the amazing flavors! They have gluten free injera if you ask for it! It is my favorite restaurant in the area and me and my partner drive 75 minutes to get there. It's THAT good! We always get the Queens 8 platter. Yum! The owner is a lovely person with a warm heart and beautiful smile! I plan to dine there on my birthday this year.

While having dined many Indian restaurants, AMBER INDIAN's buffet rivals most entrees served à la carte elsewhere. 3 times the choices and offering Pakistani cuisine in addition. Broad Ripple's Indian Garden is decent however, once you come here for their $8.99 lunch buffet ($9.80 w tax) to SEE their selections, TASTE the quality... and DISCOVER the difference, you'll then KNOW why this place is such a success! If you have any other Indian restaurants 'bookmarked', you'll be 'unmarking' it and 'bookmarking' AMBER INDIAN RESTAURANT!

Their portions is HUGE. I usually eat a lot but i have to control myself not to over order the food here because they have big portion with very decent prices. They have an great out door seating and a live band every Saturday night. Their services is slow so face with the fact that you will wait for your food at least 15 minutes.
Awesome. I am a chef. I have worked in the islands. This food makes me so very happy. First time customer. Instant addition

Just got back from our first trip to this fantastic place. You don't need to go here for the decor (lacking), ambiance (barren) location (less than ideal), or even for the service (great). You need to go here for the food. Traditional and authentic Cuban fare made from scratch and to order. We had Tomales Cubanos and Mariquitos con Mojo as appetizers simply because of a Yelp review. They were both as advertised...delicious. The Mariquitos are long strips of flash fried plantains. They are great by themselves or with the fabulous olive oil/garlic sauce. Neither of us were big Tamales fans...until tonight. Just excellent. Not too wet or too dry. The consistency is reminiscent of a really good cornbread dressing. Great flavor. We ate all of it. She had the Original Cubano sandwich. Very traditional and tasty and large.. I got the Masitas de Cerdo Fritas. Chunks of some of the most tender and flavorful pork I have ever had the good fortune to consume. The Tostones (fried flattened plantain slices) and Congris Cubano (rice and black beans cooked together) that came as sides were perfect for the dish. Since we ate every morsel of both appetizers we each brought half of our dinners home. The total including tax for two apps, two entrees, two beers and a Cafe con leche was $33. Tremendous value. We will be back often and I'd be willing to bet you'll return regularly if you give this true gem a try.
Love their Pad Thai. Super friendly staff. My children love the flowers on the tops of the straws. The waiter even took the time to show them how to make one.

This restaurant was great. My wife and I ate here on a rainy Saturday for lunch. She got the Wonton Soup and Coconut Fried Rice. I got the Orange Chicken Lunch which comes with an Egg Roll and a side of Fried Rice. The food was fantastic! I would highly recommend this place and we will definitely be back. Wonton Soup - very light and flavorful. Comes with a side of crunchy strips of something that are Fried and very good. Wife loved this soup! Coconut Fried Rice - Wife had order this before on a previous visit and loved it so much we came back the same week to get it again. Orange Chicken - This was great! Very flavorful with just the right amount of spiciness. Had bits of orange peel to really cook in the orange flavor. I ate around these. I'm not sure they should be eaten, lol. Nevertheless, it was very good! We're excited to come back and try more dishes!
Fantastic Vietnamese food. Very friendly staff. My new favorite restaurant. The lemongrass pork was very tasty.

Been to Dosa hut many times, had veg thali, non-veg thali(on weekdays only), dosa, masala dosa, idily, wada etc. Forget about the service, ambiance, cleanliness, this place is for just eating. Food is okay not bad, especially south indian food is good. Dont order biryani or any north Indian food they are not good at making them. Just stick to south indian food and you will get your moneys worth. "Best for South Indian but still can improve"

Now that I am starting to go to coffeeshops to get work done, (I have found that I am doing much better being in a coffeeshop than in lab)...and La Va is the primary reason why. Being here on a weekend is great as they usually have a rocking sound track going in the background (Depeche Mode, Cure, etc), tasty drinks and free wifi. Works for me as a place to get work done.

The vegetarian combo plate at Abyssinia is one of my top choices for eating out in all of Indianapolis. I honestly must slow myself down while eating here or I wind up feeling (pleasantly!) gluttonous. The owner and staff are very nice and attentive!

Been coming here irregularly for the past 6 years and this place is mediocre and inconsistent at best. On some rare occasions, the food has been great. Most of the time however, I'm shooting myself in the foot. Like last night, I got the peanut curry noodles and it was inedible. I was starving, too! The noodles were soggy and overcooked. I had to take the rest to go and stir fry the crap out of it at home. Decently flavorful and a bit crunchy, but helluvalot better than soggy wet noodles. I wish I could sent it back, but me thinks thats asking to have food spit on.
Food was phenomenal and I love how they break down Vegetarian vs non vegetarian options. Spices are too notch. Bummer it's a chain but it's damned good for one.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Four of us went on a Saturday evening. The food was outstanding. We started with Tom Ga Kai soup, some of the best we've had. We shared two salmon dishes and chicken Pad Thai, again some of the best in Reno. Chef Pim, the owner came to our table and visited. Although the name of this place is Fresh Creations it serves only Thai food. We will be back!

This is my favorite Greek restaurant I've been too. The setting and food is classy enough to be a nice date night but casual enough to just go after work or on the weekends with no frills. We have had beyond friendly and accommodating service every time we've been. They have a nice drink selection with a few local choices, and the food - OH man the food. Excellent choices from top to bottom of the menu. I've not been able to find something that we don't like and we have never ordered the same thing twice. Food on, good MoMo's. We will keep coming back.

I had some time to waste before a class. so, i decided to stop at Arroy Thai. I walked in and saw that the interior is very nice. All dark wood tables and chairs. I ordered the springrolls as an appetizer, and the curry chicken fried rice as an entree. the spring rolls came out almost immediately. i said "wow that was fast." the waitress said well they are premade. The sweet chili peanut sauce was good, but i think it may have been out of a jar. it tasted like the sauce we have at work. the spring rolls were large and i got 4 of them for $5. I would have liked it better to get 2 and had shrimp in them. i barely ate one roll and here came my entree. at this point i am mildly perturbed. The curry fried rice was good also, but everything tasted premade.As if you order, and then they take a cup of this and a smidge of that. I spent $24 on one meal. i want it made fresh from start to end. the tea was ok but had an they need to clean the nozzles taste to it. i expected more and got disappointed a bit. i don't know if i'd go back, they are pricey for premade food. the service was just ok. but there were only 3 people dining that night. several people came saw and left.

This was our very first time at any Indian restaurant and we loved it. The food smelled and tasted delicious. We stumbled upon this place from Groupon as it has been there for only 8 months. Your server will ask you what level of hot/spicy you want in your dish. You can order mild in any dish. They are very accommodating for any dietary restriictions, just let them know in advance or when you order. My best friend and I preferred dishes with the sauce as the dry dishes do not come with sauce and are not very moist, but that is how it is supposed to be. The dishes were all full of flavor and all tasted differently, so read the descriptions to explain if it will be a sweeter or more flavored by a multitude of spices so you know what to expect when you dish arrives. Mamfa, our server was superb and very nice, always kept our water glasses full without asking and offered us boxes and bags to take the leftovers home. Mamfa was very helpful and made great suggestions. This is a BYOB restaurant and they encourage you to bring it. We had a dessert that looked like a munchkin, didn't taste like it, but warm and delicious sweetened by honey. Definitely get the mango drink, but ask for ice on the side, as they serve it room temp, but would be more refreshing if colder. Beautiful atmosphere, clean and excellent service. They didn't rush you out and loved engaging in conversation with you if you are open to it. The Naan bread is great to dip in the dishes with the sauce. Had a great time and would go back. It is within a shopping center, so plenty of free parking. We were told they have a lunch buffet all week, but better on the weekends, I guess for more selections. Thank you for the great night and we will be back..

I recently dined-in at Jasmine Rice and it was so-so. The spring rolls were really tasty, but probably the best part of the night. I ordered the Pad Thai because it is one of my favorite dishes and a pretty good indicator of a good Thai restaurant. The dish was overly sweet and just not a good Pad Thai, with almost no sprouts and no peanuts-- I would not order this again. My boyfriend had the Crying Tiger salad which he thought was ok because it was spicy but a little on the vinegar-y side. The service was very good in this tiny place, with the server regularly checking on us and refilling our water. We'll probably return because of proximity to try a few more things, but not dying to go back.

I went for lunch and I was really pleased with their lunch specials! I got the pad thai and dumplings for an appetizer, and then we got coconut sticky rice for dessert, which I never thought I would like, but it's definitely turned me on to getting this dessert whenever I get thai.

One of the best Indian Restaurant I have been to in recent times!! I have been travelling from Maine to Florida on road and this restaurant is really amazing!! if you really want to taste some traditional South Indian curries then I would say this is the best!! (especially Lamb Rogan Ghosh and LAMB KADAI and Biryani). Not to mention Staff are so polite and friendly and the place is very clean and hygiene!! Especially Manager (Tejas) was so friendly and caring!! This is my go-to place for food when I visit Florida again!!

I pretty much eat here everyday since I operate the business next door, Aristocat Salon + Nail Spa. The staff is super nice and the place is always clean. Favorites on the menu (in no particular order): 1.) Banh Mi (I always ask for extra carrots). If you like your food spicy, ask for Extra Spicy. 2.) Pho Beef - So good! 3.) Tuna Salad Sandwich on Wheat toast 4.) Grilled Shrimp Wrap 5.) Omlet Combo - Sausage + Bacon 6.) Grilled Shrimp Vermicelli They also carry a wide range of juices and drinks to go with your meal. You can dine in for lunch or take out. Make sure to call in advance to avoid long lunch lines!

4 years ago, Abyssinia was my first experience with Ethiopian food. I have had many since then (here and elsewhere) - and while I can now say I am a huge fan of the cuisine - none compare with Abyssinia! Not only is the food outstanding, but its relatively cheap and the service the friendliest you will find. I recommend the all-vegan, 3-day a week lunch buffet. It is a great way to get your feet wet in this under-appreciated cuisine!

Amazing food, Average service, Cramped ambiance. We had the Veg Thali and 3 feet butter dosa. The food was as authentic as it can get. So far this is the only Indian restaurant in the U.S. whose food reminds me of the food you get in the streets of Tamil Nadu. Even the Saravana Bhavans in the U.S. don't serve such authentic South Indian food. If you have had real Indian food and crave for some, this is the place to go. The only dish that wasn't upto the mark was the chilli gobi that came in the Veg Thali. It was a bit hard. But i am willing to ignore that considering all the other perfect accompaniments. Prices are nominal. And oh! I almost forgot to mention the fresh filter coffee you get for just $2. Will definitely visit next time when we are in Nashville.

My fiance is from Miami so I wanted him to have a food experience that made him feel at home. He felt right at home. The food was magnificent. When you come tell them you want an authentic food experience. You will not be disappointed
Have you had Banh mi? If not, this is a good spot to try it out. Many flavors, consistent quality. Great prices, of course. Its creepy. Its sort of dingy, maybe even dirty. But it is kinda awesome.

I've only had Thai at a few places in Philly, and this was definitely up there as one of the better places I've tried. I usually judge a Thai place on the Pad Kra Pao (basil chicken), and this place was better than average. It wasn't as spicy as I would have liked or expected, given the chili pepper designation on the menu, but then again, I didn't specify a level of spiciness so they probably decided to take it easy on me. My bf got something that involved "wild boar"-- he loved it and i liked it a lot (I think he's more easily wooed by novelty than I am). The thing that really set this place apart was the service. This is by far the best service I've had in Chinatown and one of the best places I've been to in Philly. The servers were really friendly and helpful without being overwhelming, and they were super sweet even though we had changed our reservation several times. Plus, it's BYO! I'm sure that the next time a craving for Thai hits, we'll be back.

This was something else. Came here for dessert and brunch. At dessert had the kunafa and banana (can't remember the full name) dishes. If you're used to overly sweet kunafa then this isn't for you. It was lightly sweet with an addition of rose syrup, absolutely great. The banana dish had a complex taste that was awesome. Capped it with a Lebanese chai, great pairing. For brunch had the pastry basket which had 5 amazing pastries in it. The hummus too was great along with the manoushe. The vibe inside is impressive and all the servers were wonderful. Looking forward to returning to try out some more items here.

We decided to try Haveli Indian Cuisine as take out. We got the Tiki Marsala, Bengan Bhurtha, and Lamb Bhuna. We also got two different kinds of Naan - plain and Garlic. We picked the mild to medium seasoning on the food. The Tiki Marsala was outstanding - very creamy and delicious. The Bengan Bhurtha was just spicy enough for me and very filling. The Lamb Bhuna was very good and flavorful. We really enjoyed the food.

This review for mojitos only. We came in for drinks and the bartender, Jamie, was excellent. He was attentive, sociable, and made a mean mojito. We tried every flavor, and all were exceptional. My favorite was coconut. At $10each, they are worth it, as they are strong. We will definitely be back and will try some apps with our mojitos

Oh Seasons café, let me count the ways I like you. I love that you are different and you bring more culture to the St. Petersburg area. Papaya salad and Chicken wing YUM, but a little pricey? Couldn't we have a combo of a little bit of papaya salad and some chicken for a more decent price? I would be there every day if you did! The Hulu skirt to die for, my fav! Only place that you can get shaved ice, great for summer days. So refreshing and not too sweet! Its Fresh fruit meets snow cones! Very popular in Hawaii! Grilled pork banh mi can be a little fatty at times, which kinda grosses me out, but I love grilled pork banh mi, so im torned! STOP the decorations, you guys are going overboard. I feel like it's too much right now and my eyes are everywhere when I enter the café, it's too busy for me. Keep it simple and clean. You had it right when you first got there, no more decorations please! Cool place, you should give it a try!

This place gets an extra star for being able to get Med. food in this location. The Lentil soup is wonderful, Falafal is great too. I also enjoyed my smoothie very much. The salmon is really good, over their rice. The appetizer plate was ok, and gyro just ok for me. Salad and tabouli were good. I think if you live in, or pass by this area, it is definitely worth a stop.

Love this place. A regular stop for us when ever we are in the area and have a hammering fkr spme high quality Mediterranean food. The owner is proud to serve you and takes great pride in what he provides. Excellent value and quality.

After my last trip to Singha, I am compelled to raise my rating to five stars. What a wonderful experience. Our service was wonderful and the food was incredible. The Cashew chicken made Thai hot is now one of my favorite dishes. Singha at lunch is truly a five star Thai experience.
Good plate presentations. Cordial and fast service. Great tasting food!

This place looked like a tattoo parlor. It had neon lights on the windows and looked really dark and dingy. I almost walked away if it were not for good Yelp reviews. Instead I walked down the steps into a dark space to find no one there but me. Reluctantly, I ordered a chicken kabob dish to-go. I was only in Philly for an interview and it was getting dark so I wanted to get back to my hotel ASAP. The food was ready in about 10 mins. It smelled fantastic. It tasted fantastic. I loved the grilled taste of the chicken and subtle hints of mediterranean spices. The plate also came with rice, salad and some pita. It turned out to be such a satisfying meal that I'm glad it's scary exterior didn't scare me away.

Looking for something different, both food and experience? Definitely check this place out! This restaurant is one of my favorite international / ethnic in the city! It brings a variety of flavors, textures, and new tastes all at once. The bread is amazing, spongy, and gluten free for all of you that need that accommodation! I usually get the veggie sampler platter. It comes with a variety of the vegetarian entrees and allows you to try all sorts of options in one dish. I always have leftovers cause they give you so much food! They have carry-out and dining in. Be sure to wash your hands!
Haveli is my favorite place to grab lunch. Not only is the price great, they have the most delicious chicken chili and chana masala. I would swim in the chana if they'd let me

Food is always good, but the last time we were there our waitress Megan rushed us the ENTIRE evening... I had my dessert on the table before my husband finished his meal. We tipped her 20% which I regret later on as she asked again if 'we were doing alright' because we were just sitting there talking after we payed the bill. She seemed very annoyed and frustrated that we were still there. Disappointing... Other locations have much better service.

Definitely not the best Chinese food but far from the worst. Relatively well priced and the food was pretty good. Ordered a bunch of apps including Cho Cho, Beef Teriyaki and Egg rolls and tried the combination lo mein and rice. All really good!

Good food for the right price, I have been here twice in 2 weeks. They don't have just curries and don't have a intimidating menu, a good variety of South Indian food. The place is hard to locate, and needs more visibility. But if they keep up the quality of the food they will have customer loyalty like me. I will be back.
Love this place, good prices and lots in your portion... My favorite when it's cold, the rare steak large soup bowl!

Really loved this place and would come back for authentic idli sambhar; mint chutney and papad; rasam and vada; I've named all the items I loved here. I had an extremely hard time eating the paneer tikka in tandoor items, I understood it was very tasty, but the spice level was so high it was just impossible to eat. Also the Mysore masala dosa special delite is unbelievably spicy; I gave a rating of 3 as no warning whatsoever was given for this level of highly spicy food; not sure if it was based on the assumption that all Indians can handle it. The paper dosa was good. I would say if they can tone down very much on their spice level, this place is a real gem. Will definitely go again, and next time beg them to mention the dishes they consider extra spicy.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: When traveling, my husband and I try enjoy Indian cuisine. Tan Mahal did not disappoint. The food was delicious and the service was great. We will return when in Boise again.
A great value. I'm a novice as it pertains to Indian food, but their offerings are very yummy.

Perfect in every way. As soon as we walked in we were greeted warmly by the staff behind the counter. Started with the Cruller with rose and pistachio. One of the best fried dough experiences I've had. I then had the Man'oushe with cheese, tomato, onion, long hot, and parsley with an egg on top. I watched as this was prepared in the wood fired oven. Absolute perfection! Wonderfully warm decor. Even the men's room was immaculate and smelled like rose water. Gregory Root really knows how to do it!

My favorite spot in Indy for smoking. The owner knows me by name and knows what I like. Doesn't bother us unless we need something which I like. Turkish pipes are the best in my opinion. Go here and enjoy yourself.

I love this restaurant. It is small, family owned. Kahled is a sweetheart and easy to work with. A friend arranged a birthday party that Kahled basically catered there. We filled up the restaurant and had a wonderful evening. (It is small and not fancy.) A lot of people come in for take-out. The gyro special ($4.99) can't be beat. Huge pile of tasty meat and excellent sauce. The eggplant appetizer is awesome. Check it out and the prices are right.
This place is terrific you shouldn't let the mystery of difference deter you. Stop in you won't be disappointed

My first time here. On a Vegetarian diet for 30 days so tried their Veggie Pita but added Falafel to it. So Bomb!!! :) I will definitely come back here again. It was a big portion and I needed no other food. Their sweet tea is not all that though... so get water or lemonade. Overall really liked this place and it was very clean too.

Their food is yummy for my tummy. We ordered the salmon with Greek salad. Eating the couscous was like exploding a large stick of delicious dynamite inside my mouth. OMG. We highly recommend this restaurant to anyone wanting to eat a memorable meal!!! Go Vols!

Food was great, but customer service was a little iffy. Two delicious experiences here. All was very very good food. All items were made per instructions, ready on time, hot and well-packaged for takeout. They used quality ingredients, fresh vegetables, and the presentation was artfully done, and very colorful. Even in our takeout containers, the food came out beautifully. The chef knew how to put flavors together, and put out the (albeit Americanized) Asian taste craved and expected of a good Vietnamese/Thai/Chinese restaurant. We were drawn in by the great reviews and a certificate they offered on a discount site. Our visit was a little while back, so I don't know what their current offers are. But for us, before purchasing the coupon, I called to make sure I understood the terms. They are over 30miles roundtrip, so I did not want to waste anyone's time buying something we couldn't use. When I called, I spoke to the manager, and he was very friendly. He made it sound like he was happy for the business these certificates were bringing him. He said it was fine to use on takeout, and when I asked about the number allowed, he said I could buy one for myself and give one as a "gift" to my husband, so we could both use them. I asked if hubs could pick up each time, and again, that was all fine. After the conversation, I bought and printed the certs and wrote his name and notes of the conversation directly on each one. The first coupon was used just fine, no problems. The second one, which we used about a month later, was when the story changed. The second certificate had the same notes on it as the first. The conversation I'd had with the manager was right there for him to read, as he himself was the one taking it when my husband went it. He didn't refuse it, but he acted like it was making an exception to take it when he had given his word that it would all be fine. Having used these kinds of offers in the past, it is sadly kind of common for business owners to go back on promises, and sometimes to refuse to honor their own terms. In this case, I went out of my way to speak to the person to prevent problems and was given a hassle anyway. Long story short, it wasn't the worst experience ever, and he did finally honor it, but when someone has a log of their call to you written on the coupon, with your name there, don't you think you should recognize that in a professional way?

These guys have a buffet for lunch and dinner. It's somewhat reasonably priced and offers your typical Indian fare. The first time I came here, I had only eaten Indian food once or twice. I'm happy to say that I liked it! However, I quickly found out that the food from this place empties my intestinal tract. So I thought to myself, "maybe it's just me." I found out the next 3-5 times I visited Amber that, no, in fact, this place destroys my insides. It's like eating an entire bag of Sun Chips. It sounds like a great idea, but a few hours later, you and your colon regret it. If you can stomach Indian food, this place is great. The flavors of all the glops are great... Seriously! Just remember you'll be crapping it out soon after.

This is a pretty solid place to get Thai food. I recommend their crab Rangoon and vegetable spring rolls. All of the food that I've ever had from here had been very fresh and the dining room is always clean. Their lunch special is a pretty good deal.

What a pleasant surprise! I'd been craving a banh mi (vietnamese sandwich) for a while, so I was super happy to discover this deli. The staff are very friendly and welcoming. The menu had a fair selection of sandwiches and beverages, even for someone who isn't feeling adventurous and simply wants a roast beef sandwich and a Coke. I ordered the special sandwich, which had ham and pate, jalapenos, mayo, and cilantro. It was wonderfully crisp yet chewy, tasty, and filling. I wish they had put in larger slices of jalapeno, but I guess I could have simply asked. The thai tea with boba was pretty good as well. I was tempted to try their pate chaud (a delicious flaky pastry filled with ground meat) but I will save that for a future visit!

This is one if my favorite restaurants to eat. On the corner of Mill and Kietzke, you will find plenty of parking. The food is delicious. My favorites are Salt and Pepper Shrimp Chef Dish that comes with a serving of steamed rice and the Flamed broiled pork and steamed rice. Who am I kidding, almost everything i have ordered as been delicious, I've had their Spring Rolls, Vermicelli noodles, Pork Fried Rice and Walnut Shrimp and have never been disappointed. It's a family owned business, Fiona and her husband run the restaurant and are such friendly people. Call your order for take out or dine inside, you won't be disappointed!

I gave Flambo 5 stars because as a trini, I appreciate the food, ambience and good vibes. Best Roti I've had in Philadelphia. The goat and chicken curry was well seasoned and flavorful additionally, the roti skin is made fresh when ordered. I like how the owners mixed authentic Trinidadian cuisine with a very elegant ambience. Will definitely be back for doubles on the weekend.

This place is awesome. Found some spices I use for a great price and the food at the cafe was delicious. My daughter and I had a nice quiet lunch and tried new food in a lovely environment with good service.

The lady taking orders is very rude. I simply asked for dark fried rice and was rudely denied it. I know this is not St. Louis city rice but I didn't ask for a miracle just dark fried rice. Their prices are overly high too.

The food here is consistently good. My GF and I go here together, and we often meet friends for a foursome. The service is also very good. We have always enjoyed the place, never a bad experience. We have only had the dinner service. We'll try the lunch one of these days. When we want Thai this is first place we think of and we would dine there more often but it's a bit of a drive for us.
Loved it! My boyfriend and I have been a few times and always delish!! The location is terrible, but worth finding!!
Very delicious. Saganaki good. Gyro large and open face
Love love love this place! Great for a quick dinner or a Thai iced tea. My personal fav is papaya salad with grilled shrimp. Jungle curry is also a must try!

When my boss offered to pick up the dinner tab for my mate and I, we called Zen Yai for reservations. This little place has been in town for as long as I can remember and never disappoints. Last night we had the Tofu Sate, Red Curried veggies and Tofu and Tofu Fried rice. We are not vegetarians or vegans but, we both enjoy the tofu especially when prepared well. The sate is served with spicy peanut sauce and cucumber salad, great way to start a meal. The Curry was sweet and spicy, veggies were fresh and crisp, with perfectly fried tofu. The Pineapple fried rice is surprisingly great. The rice was perfectly balanced with raisins, onions and cashews and it was not greasy or heavy. Desert: I'm a big fan of desert. They had a special mango and rice dish that sounded peculiar and worth a try. The rice was a sweet brown rice cooked in a very sweet coconut milk, served warm. The rice is plated with sliced ripe perfect mango. Strange combo delivering delicious results, it was heavenly. We had an appetizer, to main dishes, desert and 2 beers for about $60. Only negatives are that the place is noisy and hard to get into without a reservation, so call ahead or it's worth the wait.

This was my first Pho experience, and I was honestly underwhelmed. We got the veggie spring rolls to start with and they were delicious!! Then for the Pho, I got the chicken pho, which was dry and tough. The broth was really enjoyable though. My boyfriend got the tofu pho and I liked his a lot better. He got a ton of veggies that were super fresh. We also got the smoothies! I got taro and he got honeydew, and they both were really good. I'm not writing this off my list, I will definitely go back and try it again. If anyone has any pho tips or suggestions, please let me know!

I wanted to have a nice brunch with my girlfriend who lives in Delaware. Using Yelp was a very helpful and important tool when it comes to choosing or finding restaurants to fit your needs. This restaurant on the surface fits everything that I needed. It has brunch, drink specials and live music. So I made a reservation and took the 30 minute drive. Upon arrival I gave my name, I was promptly seated and greeted shortly by the server. I was impressed by the brunch options and I had to take extra time to choose my entree, but I was clear on the Bloody Mary buffet! We started with coffee, on to Bloody Mary's, for my meal I ordered the Brioche French Toast which I enjoyed and pork belly that was tasty but not worth $5.00! The live music was mellow and entertaining. As a whole my sever was attentive and pleasant however I was a little taken aback by my bill. First, when I ordered the Bloody Mary it's listed at $6.00 I didn't know adding the vodka was an additional cost. Unless you order a 'virgin' drink in my mind the alcohol is implied! It is very important to have utensils at the Bloody Mary Bar. It is not unlike folk to use the toilet, not wash their hands and dive into the condiments such as olives and pickles with their fingers. YIKES!!! Finally, if coffee refills are not free as they are in most places in the free world please inform your customer!
Get the spinach ravioli. It is excellent!! Service is great, nice place. House is very old, but that adds to the ambiance.
Superb. My wife had veggies with shrimp and I had the Pho bowl. We also had egg rolls. All excellent.
Excellent service, delicious food, and pleasant atmosphere! Who could ask for anything more?

Love Zagol for lunch. They have even started to offer lunch specials, while not scrimping on the taste. The owner is always available during lunch, and it seems like she is also in the kitchen, since lunch is a little quieter than dinner. The Ethiopian coffee is fabulous, if you can handle a strong shot of caffeine late in the day. Have only had the veggie options, which are great. The owner implied that all of the veggie dishes are actually vegan, which makes this place a minority in meat-loving Reno. Other than requesting a little more spice in their spicy dishes, I have no qualms with Zagol. If you can get seat at one of the authentic Ethiopian tables, it makes the meal even more fun. I'll return again!

My husband and I have stopped in twice so far and I know we'll be back regularly. So far we've tried the chicken satay appetizer and the Pad Thai and Spicy Drunken Noodles entrees. All have been were delicious. Beware the spicy markings, Pikpon means it! The staff is very friendly and really makes you feel welcome. They even have a rewards program which I know I'll be enjoying. You can get a free soup, appetizer, then entree after every 5 purchases or so. There are a handful of chairs and tables but I'd suggest getting food to go if you're visiting with more than 2-3 people. They also offer delivery if you don't need it to go too far. Overall, very satisfied and looking forward to exploring more of the menu.

While giving my Urban Spoon app a shake one night, this restaurant popped up. My fiancé and I were contemplating on where to eat that night, (hence the app shaking...) I suggested, how about Ethiopian? His attention perked when he heard it, "Sure!" We were on our way to discover new cultures through food, which I love to do. I had no idea what to expect when arriving to this place, which is on 4th...and anyone local knows 4th street isn't the best area of town, however houses some of the best places to eat, (Louis Basque Corner for instance.) We walked in and were instantly transported to another place! We left that night happy as could be and I hadn't returned until a homework assignment, a presentation on our favorite local businesses in which used local products or gave back to the community somehow, required a trip to Zagol. I did my presentation on Zagol for my English 101 class last semester and was honored to be able to interview the owner! She brought the decorations for her restaurant, along with all the Ethiopian spices she uses in her restaurant, in a suit case from Ethiopia, and keeps her spices filled by her continued trips back home. The bread she serves her food on is called Injera, which is a traditional Ethiopian flatbread made from LOCALLY grown Teff!! A type of flour used to make the bread, and it is Gluten free. She has Honey Wine, which is a ceremonial wine traditionally served at weddings and special events in her homeland. She also offers a traditional coffee bean roasting ceremony, in which coffee beans from Ethiopia are roasted table side, then the beans ground and the coffee prepared, all at your table, the ceremony is even performed in a traditional Ethiopian dress. Reservations are required, but the ceremony is well worth it! Truly a unique experience! Be prepared to eat with your hands as well as share your food! Each table's entrees, for everyone, are served on a large piece of Injera on a huge plate, with baskets of extra bread for eating with your hands! This way of eating is communal and reminds me of eating with family. The food was delicious and the bread was so good when it was being eaten with all the meat and sauce...hmmm, have some honey wine and enjoy being transported to another country when you come here, because her food will move you, her story will move you. She is an amazing person and it shows through her food.
Nicely redesigned atmosphere - looks like a palace ! Food was excellent and service friendly. Portions were more than ample and we ended up taking some home. Highly recommended.
Great food, incredibly friendly staff. Everything I have had here has been fresh and tasty !

What can I say that hasn't already been said? The place is great. Cute interior, the rickshaws are whimsical, the rope lights quite dramatic and rustic as is the rest of the place. Nicely done and very clean. And it smells soooo good in here. And here comes the reason why I didn't give 5 stars: not accommodating to fat and/or old people like me... The stools are bar height and therefore hard to get on and into the right position, plus depending on your girth, the butt won't all fit on that tiny seat. And the rickshaws, while very cute, are difficult to get in and out of if you are of size, or rather tall, or old and so on. I also don't see a way that this place would be wheelchair friendly. Then there is the location of the solitary trash can, off to the farthest corner of the restaurant. Sure I don't really want to eat sitting next to a trash can, but this is so far out of the way, that you can hardly find it. Maybe put one by the door, so you can throw away your trash on the way out. As far as the food goes, this place is great. The sauces all looked alike to me, but they allowed me to taste all of the sauces prior to making a decision. All of them are delicious btw. I decided on the rice bowl with chicken and Korma sauce. We topped it off with cucumbers, ,sprouts, onion, tomatoes and cilantro. Drizzled some yogurt and mint-cilantro sauce over it, sprinkled with lime and my dish was ready to be devoured. Absolutely delicious, fresh, light yet filling. A great value for the money. I also sampled the chicken samosa which was quite yummy and came with mint-cilantro and also tamarind sauce for dipping. And may I follow suit and recommend the mango lassi...

Best place in town for drinks! Great bartenders. I would recommend a drink but they are all my favorite. In fact, forget the drink menu or your favorite drink. Allow the bartender mix up a new concoction based on your favorite type of alcohol. I've yet to be disappointed. The decor is spectacular and fun! Great place for friends to hang out. You'll feel at home.

The delivery is unbelievably slow. We ordered 1 hr and 45 mins ago and the driver is still not here despite the owner's insistence that the order is "on the way". It's past 9pm and our exhaustion outweighs our hunger. It's a Tuesday night so even if they really are busy like they say, they should really apologize for their tardiness or do something so that their customers are not kept waiting. We will definitely not be ordering here ever again!

Nice setting located in strip mall. Good food overall. Very authentic Indian food! Ordered the chicken curry with medium hotness and was excellent! Also tried the butter chicken which also delicious! Price was reasonable for 4 people. Would definitely go again soon!

Still one of my favorite places to eat. Everything I've eaten has been delicious, the staff are friendly, and the atmosphere is quiet and homey. Every person I've taken there to eat has enjoyed the experience and asks to go back. Would definitely recommend!

This is by far one of my favorite lunch trucks in Philadelphia. They serve fusion Thai and Mexican food. My favorite dish is the captain crunch breaded tilapia in a burrito or on rice. The line can get very long because they are so popular on Drexel's campus so prepare for a wait. I also would recommend the bubble teas that they have in assorted flavors, the bubbles are fresh and chewy and not stale like some places I have gone to.

A couple weeks ago we tried to get pho at a couple other locations, but they were closed on a Tuesday night?!?! SF Kitchen was close to the second location we tried, so we decided to come here. The staff seemed pleasant and attentive. When ordering pho, there was no option of small or large, it was a single bowl for all. In our group, one person ordered the chicken pho and another ordered the rare steak pho. Both of them said that there was nothing that stood out to make it better or worse than any other pho place, but they both indicated they liked the pho at the other places we go to more. I ordered the grilled pork over vermicelli noodles. The waitress brought out the fish sauce prior to my dish coming to the table. The color was more red than any other place I have been to, and my wife sitting to my right indicated that she could smell the sauce from across the table (to my left). It didn't smell bad, it just had a strong smell. The portion of my dish was fine, and the addition of the fish sauce, made the flavor that much better. I agree with the others, there was nothing that I tried that made me want to come here over the other locations we enjoy.

This was my first and last time coming to this place there is no seasoning are flavor to the chicken the rice was are looked like regular brown rice with 2 peas in it luke warm i thought it was supposed to be fried rice worst experience of a fine dining Chinese spot
I went to this restaurant with groupon deal and the food was nasty and made me sick. Also the place and silverware and table cloth wasn't clean. So disappointing

So good. Being from Florida, I've had my share of Hispanic food so I was very hopeful when a restaurant opened in StL. The dishes are delicious at Mi Caribe. The dishes are prepared a little different from their traditional style, but they are still amazing and flavorful. You NEED to try the mofongo. It is amazing. I've been twice and have had good service both times. The portions are big so you'll have enough for a great meal the next day. Also, the owner is very nice and has clearly worked hard to make the place what it is.

We sat down to eat here, but it's more of a take out place. Amazing authentic flavors. Would definitely order take out or delivery next time. Their seafood isn't the freshest, bit they make up for it in fresh vegetables.
The food was good but the service is horrible. We were there tonight and waited for an hour to get our food.

Consider the Vietnamese. What's the first thing that comes to mind? There's a very good chance that because of their willingness to welcome us to their dinner table that they've changed your perception entirely. There was a time where "war torn nation that helped catapult America into two decades (if not more) of unrest," was the leading charge and definition of Vietnam. We're moving further and further away from that era. We're moving to a place where when we here "Vietnamese" the first thoughts that *bubble* to the top are on food: from pho to bubble tea to banh mi to those hard-working, kind smiles we find when we enter a Vietnamese store front. The spirit of Vietnamese business owners have finally -- over the past handful of years -- really shined in Indy. I found my kinship with their craft sandies -- the banh mi -- by traveling on a budget in America.
