Downtown San Francisco, fringes of San Jose and San Bernadino to Denver to Indy... there was always somewhere to eat a remarkable sandwich for $4 or less. And now with K&T there is a place to eat $3.50 banh mi -- and there's an entire sandwich board of them: 10 choices (including a vegetarian option). With its spartan setting of scattered tables, Viet action movies on TV running roughshod on your ears, a deli counter and a simple menu of what you need -- banh mi and vietnamese coffee -- I feel right at home. And then... they have a full Viet menu, including pho. Then, I look over and they have American staples... of sub sandwiches and fried okra. Don't let those bizarrely placed choices steer you away from the classic french roll of pork pate, jalapenos, carrots, onions cilantro and *insert meat of choice.* For me, pork belly is where the journey begins (and ends). The warmness of that pork belly. The warmness of an exchange of what yelper Benjamin H would call: "I give them money, they give me [insert smile-inducing item]." The warmness of the thought that here I am in our -- Indy's -- "Little U.N." ordering banh mi. The warmness of a peaceful marketplace. The warmness of how vital this exchange is to us as a community, as a culture. The warmness has me all warm & fuzzy & bright-eyed & in love with this city. Something's going on here. (This is that moment just after the bridge in a song where the bar raises; or that moment in the movie where everything comes together and the music crescendos. So turn it up). This is a remarkable redefining of how we look at a culture once burdened with the past. For the future, the Vietnamese Community, the City of Indianapolis, you have unleashed a new sense of peace via the banh mi. With that there is only one thing to do... let's have another banh mi, Bon ami.

I came here with some friends and we threw down. The more people you have in your party, the more incredibly delicious things you can try at Abyssinia. They offer a large variety of both meaty and vegetarian dishes. The bread... it makes you never want to use a spoon and fork again. I love the potatoes. Yum.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We visited the Taj Mahal for the first time last Saturday. We booked reservations online for 5:30, but probably didn't need them. There were only a few occupied tables when we arrived, and quite a few empty tables when we left. The restaurant itself is wonderfully tacky with crazy 1970s Indian movies playing on a big screen hanging on a wall above a haphazard selection of statues and musical instruments. The service was personable and attentive, to the point where you feel like you are eating in someone's home rather than a restaurant. Our beers were delivered quickly. My wife ordered a chili beer that was pretty spicy (a whole chili is bottled in the beer), and mine was nice and cold. They have a decent selection of imported beer, a smaller selection of wine (I watched a glass being poured from the box of wine stored in the beer fridge, next to the lunch buffet station) as well as a nice selection of sake. I previewed the menu online and I must say it is much easier to follow than the menu you are handed at the restaurant. We had the eggplant apps and the potato with peas apps and they were both good. Will probably skip them next time as they were deep fried and pretty heavy. The three sauces that accompanied them were tasty. For our entrees we shared the Babajan Biryani which was huge (everything is served family style) and wonderfully flavored. We ordered mild spicy and it had just the right amount of heat. We also had the Baba Ji Fish which also had a little kick to it and a fairly small dish compared to the Biryani. The fish was crispy on the outside, but a bit dry inside. Still very good, we just used a bit of the yogurt sauce on the side for dipping. The warm Onion Kulcha bread was a perfect accompaniment: crisp, filled with moist onions. We left happy, full and carrying half of our Babajan in a to go container. Overall, the service and the food were very good. My wife and I have already booked a return visit this week. I wouldn't consider us highly educated in Indian cuisine, but we have had wonderful meals in Fez and Marrakech, and Boise's Taj Mahal is a pretty good substitute if you can't get to Morocco for the night.

I have been to 3 Indian restaurants in Indianapolis, and this is my favorite so far. Palak Paneer, chicken tikka masala, and lamb vindaloo were all very good. The naan was a little on the thin side for my preference.

First off let me say that the other four times I have been to PF Changs (Atlantic city) it was delicious. This is the reason we decided to dine here for valentines day. Horrible idea. We were sat Within 10 minutes of our reservation which is great considering it's a holiday. We got drinks and food but my martini didn't come until our second course. Also, it wasn't until after our second course that we received silverware and napkins...which we had to flag someone down for. The plate we received with our appetizer was blatantly dirty, we had to request another one. My soup had a small black hair on the dish. Then when our dinners arrived the shrimp we ordered was so salty it was unbearable. Another server, who served my second drink halfway through dinner, brought out another dish for us instead which was less salty but not good at all. Not once did a manager stop by the table..I don't even think our server had any idea about our first dish. The experience was horrible. I will most likely never dine at PF Changs again even with my past good experiences in Atlantic city. I wish I could go back in time and dine at Red Stone which is located right next door. Never again.

I'm a fan. And I'm a fan of pastries. This beautiful space has excellent ones, and they serve Stumptown, which makes me happy. Please, take note, Philly restaurants, and offer something other than burnt, burnt, burnt La Colombe Corsica- that black, oily, charcoal tasting coffee of the early aughts. Anyway, get the cruller. It's an expensive donut, but man, do I want more of this particular expensive donut.

FIY: Bui's sauce is a must Breakfast sandwich trucks are a staple around Philly, especially in the University City area where poor college students are always hungry for cheap and fast food. WHAT I GOT: Ham, egg, and cheese with pepper, ketchup, and Bui's sauce PROS: Extremely filling!! These sandwiches are a bit longer than your average breakfast sandwich, though to me, the taste is pretty much the same. The Bui's sauce, which is literally just spicy mayo, adds a nice kick and flavor. CONS: I wanna say about 1/3 of this sandwich is bread. Bui's uses different rolls from other food trucks I've been to (Lyn's, Happy Sunshine, and Pete's Little Lunch Box) in that the rolls are THICK. Like we're talking at least an inch in width if you measure it after they cut it in half. I'm pretty sure the full feeling you get isn't necessarily from the fillings, but it's mostly from the ridiculous thickness of those rolls. It's also makes it hard to actually taste anything but the bread and sauces and maybe the egg. Their prices are also a bit higher than other lunch trucks I've been too. Probably because of the size of their sandwiches but seriously though, if I'm going to shell out a couple extra dollars for this sandwich, I kind of want to taste something other than bread, ketchup, and egg. Like where the frick did my ham even go?

Ohh, new favorite place for Indian/Pakistani takeout!!! The owners are sooo adorable and welcoming, and the food is amazing. I ordered the lamb nihari ("as spicy as you'll make it"-- packed some heat but not so much as to detract from the delicious curry flavor) and daal masar, along with a side of mixed pickles--that stuff is POTENT and not for the faint of heart! Went great with the daal. The garlic naan wasn't anything to write home about, and mostly served as a vessel to sop up delicious curry sauce and daal. I'm hooked. Must. Have. More.

Thank God For This Place!!!! As a vegetarian, eating in the French Quarter can be greasy, fattening and just down right unsatisfying. How many 'slices' of cheese pizza with PAM sprayed garlic butter can one eat before having a heart attack? My friends went to Yo-Mama's which looked DELICIOUS.... except..... No Veggie Burgers! NOTHING! Ice Berg Salad and a Stuffed potato. That's your option. PA-THE-TIC! I glance across the street and a halo of veggie salvation emerges.... GYRO'S & FALAFEL. THERE IS A GOD!!!! {well, I knew that anyways} I was worried.... will this turn into a nasty slider? Well the answer was no. This was a fantastic, fresh falafel sandwich. It was DELICIOUS and CHEAP! A couple different veggie options too as well as chicken shwarma for those that eat meat. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Reasonably priced, nice sized portions. We shared the tom kah & red curry with chicken. Staff was friendly & service was quick. But if you want to cut straight to the chase, get the sticky rice with mango slices. They shape the the rice into a cute little pyramid. The mango was fresh & the rice was the right stickiness.

This place needs to be closer to Philly. It should probably just be in my backyard so I can go every day. It really is that good. Get the Antipasto Siciliano. Seriously. It is HUGE and is filled with so many delicious cheeses, vegetables and meats. It is really fun to eat with someone. Also, if you go here, you have to get the Gnocchi alla' Argentiera. If you don't, you should be ashamed. No seriously, it is THAT good. big pillows of heaven. UGH. I want them right now and it is only 9:30am. It is realllllly tiny inside, so plan on making reservations if you can and bring your reading glasses because it is a little dark. BYOB also- so you really can't go wrong.. actually...we brought champagne that may or may not have busted everyone's ear drums when it popped. You won't be disappointed.

To be honest, the combination pho at this restaurant is not spectacular but I am giving this review 4 stars because the rice w/ grilled beef plate was absolutely BREATHTAKING!! My boyfriend and I ordered the combination pho ($10.95 for a large bowl) and the rice with grilled beef ($8.95). The combination noodle soup consisted of rare meat on top, Vietnamese style meatballs, tripe, tendon, and all the other goodies. The rice plate had a good amount of rice, a good amount of grilled beef on top of a bed of lettuce and cucumbers; there was also pickled carrots on the side. ALSO, the rice plate came with soup, which was basically the pho broth. The pho was alright, I am usually very picky about the broth and the broth today was a little watered down (probably because its nearing the end of the night). There was a decent amount of meat in the pho but I wish they would add more tendon (my favorite!!). The rice plate was delicious and I really enjoyed it!! I had the option to add a fried egg to my plate but that would be an additional $1.50 and tbh, dass essspensive for one egg?!? WTF! The grilled beef was grilled to perfection and wow my mouth is watering just thinking about it. ALMOST FORGOT! We ordered the Thai Milk tea as well and the drink came with boba! The boba was a little hard but the thai iced tea was good, I liked it :) Overall, I would definitely come back to this place. I am glad I came tonight!

A little hole in the wall place on South Grand. I stopped in today while my car was down the street being inspected at Doc Holloway's. I had never been to SGGE, but had passed it a bunch of times so it was time to try it out. Wasn't too busy which was more than OK by me. It was REALLY hot in the restaurant which wasn't helped by the fact it was hot outside. I had two of the "special" gyros....other than I wasn't expecting them to be so spicy, they were great. The meat (beef & lamb combo) was soft, tender, and VERY good. The gyros were huge as Deborah M. had stated, I indeed needed to use a fork. I will be returning and recommending them to my friends & family. Great gyros and decently priced.

They have the best iced chais in the city, in my opinion. I recommend them spiced. Only once have I had a negative experience with drinks, and that was this past week where I ordered my usual chai but ended up with basically a cup of milk. It's pretty difficult to find a place to sit inside. It's always full of ppl on laptops whenever I go. Also, a dislike... their large sizes are probably similar to a medium in other coffeeshops. not cool. makes me want to order 2 instead, espeically considering the amount of ice inside anyway, but then it's pricey.

Perfectly grilled chicken, deliciously fresh falafel, and tasty garlic hummus are staples of the fixed single menu item at Konstantinos 'Gus' Falafel Truck. The falafel is crispy on the outside and the perfect texture on the inside... never doughy like you get everywhere else. Added to this are ever changing seasonal ingredients that perfectly compliment each other, including some sort of incredibly prepared veggie, fruit, and pasta combination.
A gem. Yes an overused term, but it applies here. Great, local food at a very good price Congrats Jim on a perfect meal and perfect evening.

I came here two weeks ago for the first time and I have to say i was pretty impressed. The food here is on point, there wasn't anything that was bad about. It's a nice small restaurant and you do wait a little bit for the food to come out after you placed your order. But don't get to mad that the food you got came to late as you won't be disappointed. I suggest getting the chicken red curry really nice and although even though the spice level was at a two it def seemed hotter than two l think it was either level 4 or their hottest Thai hot. Do come here as this is a very good restaurant for family outings

Ron's is a great place for Caribbean style cuisine! Their food is to die for! I normally get the ox tails with mac & cheese and their sweet potatoes (yams) are wonderful! i.e: you now have to pay $1.00 extra for the yams but they are worth the price believe me! They are yum & melt in your mouth. I would recommend this place to anyone. Ron's is located right on Broad Street so it is easy to find and get to from anywhere in the city. The trip to this place is worth the commute. Pros: Wonderful food! Cons: Be wary of the staff, most just take your order & they lack friendly customer service. Don't worry though, you won't have to put up with their behavior for long, it is a take-out place so it won't take more than 5-10min to receive your food & you are good to go!
I Love this place. Great food. Cold beer. This is their 3rd location in 30 years, and I can't get enough. My fav is their Drunken Chicken Sandwich. Great people, that shine with smiles.
Just felt like Chinese at the moment and decided to try it out. They have the best lomein I've ever had in my life. Just needed to add a little siracha.

I'm torn with how to rate this place. The food is in fact very good, (minus the biryani) but the service is lacking terribly. They're completely unable to keep a water cup full. In fact when they do refill the water, they fill it only 2/3 full. Granted, I drink a lot of water, they're rather un-attentive. My absolute biggest complaint is the Naan situation. I understand that they think they must make fresh naan for every customer, well today I sat there for 24 minutes waiting for the naan. I go to this buffet for lunch because the food is ready when you get there, i can get in, get out, devour my food quickly and go. Today I found myself waiting, waiting waiting.. with an empty water glass and no Naan. I left $10 on the table and walked out. I've gone out of my way to bring friends and family there but unless the service changes, and they start wrapping the naan in foil and or bring out small portions at different increments to be left on the buffet I will not be back. Cold naan, or hard naan is better then NO NAAN! There were many mistakes their first week, the place was new, I understand growing pains in a restaurant but these are careless mistakes that really affect the dining experience.

On our way to the zoo and in need of a bite to eat. We happened upon this place and were not disappointed. Kind staff and generous portions. We had the lamb shank and combo kabob platters. The Lentil soup was excellent. A hidden gem.

This place is great. It is definitely no frills inside and I will admit to being a bit nervous about what was going to be put on my plate after receiving a half-hearted salad that likely came from a bag. Everything else is great. I have tried many dishes and never been disappointed. I am particularly a fan of their lamb and eggplant dishes. Service is good and goes with the laid back atmosphere. The food is consistent and great. I've eaten here close to 30 times in 5 years. My dad still talks about the kabobs. Do your self a favor and try it.

Good food but service was incredibly slow. There were only two waitresses for the entire place (about 8-10 tables??). Saw them doing everything from taking orders to bringing out food to bringing glasses to bussing the tables after patrons leave. Can't speak to whether it's inefficiency or they need more staff. Byob. Come if you don't mind the pace, else keep eyeing the staff and maybe they will bring urgency

This is one of the most elaborately decorated thai restaurants I've been in. It's obvious that they are trying REALLY hard with all the details. It's very clean inside as well. It was quite empty when we were there so it's hard to speak about the ambiance. The service was very efficient. A touch cold, but nice people. The food was good...not exceptional but good! I will definitely go back, hopefully when it's a little more crowded, but it's a big space and probably hard to fill.
I went in there for lunch because I had heard good things about this place. I was disappointed when the pineapple curry I ordered was as runny and tasteless as water.
Traditional food, relax environment, excellent service. First time here and we love it. Amazing food!

Speedy and amazing service, delicious food. I had the egg roll bun and Vietnamese iced coffee. I think they know that many of their customers are there during a work lunch break so they brought everything out quickly and checked on us often enough. We didn't have to wait but it was definitely busy!

As a strict vegetarian, it is kind of difficult to go downtown all the time for great vegetarian cuisine. I come from the Northeast part of Philadelphia where the only thing vegetarian seems to be pizza fries. Along comes one of the greatest surprises to come along in quite some time, Taj India. Taj India is without a doubt the best restaurant I have been to. The food is ALWAYS AMAZING! The samosas are the best I have ever had from any Indian restaurant and the people at Taj India are always courteous and pleasant. This is a restaurant both vegetarians and non-vegetarians can enjoy, the food is so good. If you are looking for amazing Indian food or just amazing food in general, look no further than Taj India. I guarantee you will love it and come back again and again!

A Vietnamese banh mi place charges 25 cents for sriracha? Lol... No thanks. And please clean your restaurant. Maybe I caught this place on a bad day, but it's beyond selfish and foolish to charge for Vietnamese hot sauce for my banh mi !!!

Great food and attentive service! We were a tad bit tentative given some reviews but it just goes to show, some times you have to try it out for yourself. We had vegetarian gyro wrap and pork tenderloin sandwich. Sat in the patio. The servers were so attentive and our sodas were refilled several times. Food was very good and we will be coming back.

I found this place on Yelp and suggested to my co-workers that we take a trip here for lunch. When we walked in, it was nothing like what I had expected. The restaurant is set up in a very upscale looking manner. Clean well-organized, and looking downright fancy. We were greeted by a waiter who came by and took our drink orders. After a few minutes he came back we asked a few questions about the menu and each of us ordered one of the lunch specials. The lunch specials are price right and provide plenty of food. We also ordered a couple of hand appetizers, that I only can only describe as "empanada like." I had the curry chicken over brown rice and it was out of this world. The Empanada like item, was filled with some type of beef, and that too was exceptional. I don't have enough words to describe how good this food tasted to me. My colleagues had the same impressions of their meals, and I was lucky enough to take a taste of each of theirs, and I have to agree that every morsel provided to us was nothing short of delicious. The owner came by and chatted with us for a few, he was very nice, very genuine, and seem to be very concerned about everybody's opinion. This was nice and refreshing. The only drawback to this establishment, which we did share with the owner, is that if you order refills for tea or soda you will be charged for each refill. This is explained to us and it is due to the sodas and teas are single serve rather than from the fountain. I'm not sure this is actually a drawback, it just is uncommon and was a bit of a shocker when the bill came. I will say that the owner removed the charges for the additional drinks, although we did not ask or expect for that to happen. If you like this type of food you have got to try this place. The lunch is exceptional, and on the day we went it wasn't that busy. Get here soon, before this place becomes packed every day, as this is a lunch time gem.
Amazing food! Fantastic atmosphere and Swift's service! I selected the jumbo shrimp with coconut curry sauce with curry leaves over the rice with naan. It was so good

We tried out Rangoli tonight and it was STELLAR. Plenty of vegan dishes to choose from, and the staff knew exactly what was in each dish. I had the Bhindi Masala and the Paratha, and I almost placed a second order to take Home for tomorrow...it was that good. We will be back!
I love this restaurant. The Italian food is so old school. Nice portions and great service.

I really liked this place. It's pretty new, but super clean, and the food was pretty good for Vietnamese. I got the vermicelli with pork and egg rolls, and it was pretty delicious. The food was ready pretty quickly as well. My only complaint is the Thai iced tea. I'm used to traditional thai tea that is less sweet and has that hint of earthy flavor, and this one was way too sweet and had whipped cream on top. Totally not my thing, but I'm sure some people will like it.

Great date spot that gets you out of center city. Authentic, no frills cuisine. BYOB. It's not the best meal Italian meal I've eaten in my life, but it was a nice place and it's popular with the South Philly crowd.
Traveling through Nashville & craving Thai food we were delighted to find this restaurant. The food was delicious, service impeccable, & conveniently located near I/24. We plan to return.
Terrible service, lady that helped us was rude and disrespectful. Food was decent, very oily and no fresh veggies

Tried Viet Pho a couple of times. Food is good- especially if you consider that it is "fast food" I have had the beef spicy noodle soup which was very flavorful and had some punch. Could have been spicier but added some sriracha hot sauce. Also had the chicken pho. Points for using breast meat, but it was a bit dry. Wife had BBQ beef bun- she thought it was just fine. The ambiance is nil, but the food makes up for it. If you want a quick meal, beats fast food burger easily. Easy top five for Reno, but a little below my Bay area favs.

Delicious. A healthy fast food choice. Had the chicken doner mina sandwich. Chicken and salad consisting of white and red cabbage, tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion and tzatziki sauce in a toasted bread resembling a pita. The server told me it was naan bread. I can't wait to try the beef next time.

I could basically copy/paste Jason F's review into the box I'm currently typing in. I too went to Bitar's in search of that perfect falafel sandwich. What did I find? Bland falafel balls overly drenched in hummus and tahini. Talk about a messy sandwich! I actually had to change my pants from all dripping that went down. I still look to Maoz as my favorite falafel sandwich. Perheps Bitar's can satisfy on the meat end of things? What say you Philadelphia?

This was my first time at Goree, and they definitely did not disappoint. This was also my first encounter with traditional African cuisine, and I am now hooked! I had the Mafe which comes with white rice. And I ordered a side of plantains. Large portions, for a great price!!! Lovely spot.

Remedy was one of the first cafe's I found when I first moved to Edmonton, that actually felt like a cafe to me. It's one of a few cafe's in Edmonton where you can feel a real sense of community inside. I have noticed it's popularity grow within the last few years, which makes it a little harder to find a spot to sit during the evenings, but if anything that's just a testament to how great the place is. The food is great for the price in my opinion, and the chai is something I always look forward to. They have a variety of coffee drinks (their brewed coffee is quite a good brew imo), iced drinks (and chai milkshakes :D) , and a pretty good selection of beers. The food is mainly a selection of indian food and deserts (cakes and pies) with fun names. Overall it's a great place to go to kill a hour or two, read a book, bring a friend for conversation, and enjoy some good food and drink.

I ordered the Falafel Pita to go, but there is bistro seating available. It was excellent. The place is clean, didn't have to wait too long, lots of people working on the orders to make the food fresh. I will be returning.

Ambience - 3/5, scope of lots of improvement. Correspondence - 3/5, people need to listen, understand and respond to the customers. Cleanliness- 3/5 Food - 3.5/5, I think this is the only one area where I can give a little higher score. Not much choice but what ever there is chef seems to know them well. Overall - 3/5 One incident, may be lack of knowledge, customer asked for butter paneer masala which is not in menu but was given paneer tikka masala and was told that they both are same. In reality they both are completely different.

We had an excellent dinner last night. We ordered an asparagus / snow peas with chicken and steamed rice and Kai Kua with chicken. Both dishes were excellent. The asparagus and snow peas were cooked perfect. The dishes were nice and hot when they arrived and very tasty. Not too salty, not too spicy although they will spice it up to your preference. The inside of the restaurant is comfortable and quiet. The servers were polite and timely without be intrusive. A definite MUST for SB locals. Try it, you will return. We will.
Tried Nirvana for the first time last night. Will definitely be back. Food was delicious! Best vegetable spring rolls I've ever had.
My new go to spot for fresh, healthy, non meat options. Today I had the Veggie Feast. Hummus, cabbage, pickles, onions, falafel, cucumber with jalapeños sauce YUM!

Ate here while attending conference at Opryland. We waited at least 15-20 minutes to be seated despite there being a couple open tables. Seemed to be extremely understaffed with only one person in charge of all front of the house activities. Felt bad for the lady but nonetheless this led to less than ideal dining experience - very slow to take our order, get drinks, pay, etc. The food was inconsistent. The spring rolls were good, however the pad thai was inedible - swimming in fish sauce. So bad I ordered veggie fried rice because I couldn't eat it. This dish was better but still not great - too dry and a little spicy for fried rice. The other food our party got was good though. Overall I wouldn't return.
Under new ownership! Very personable family sharing "mom's favorite recipes". Limited menu when I visited. But very good.

My husband and I found this new restaurant this afternoon. We really enjoy trying new places, especially family owned. We were immediately greeted and seated by a friendly man, not just polite, but friendly. The restaurant was clean and decorated with an island feel and we listened to island music playing on the speakers. We ordered and briefly waited. As we waited, I read over some of the other Yelp reviews. Based on what I read, I thought we'd be waiting a while for our food. We didn't! Our food was delivered a lot quicker than expected. I had the Spanish pulled pork and plantains. Delicious! The pork was full of flavor and so juicy. The plantains were fantastic. My husband had the jerk burger and fries. He was very pleased as well. We had several sauces with our meal, one of which reminded him of his time in Costa Rica. We shared the Tostones which were wonderful. We were so full, we had leftovers. We asked for a recommendation when we ordered our drinks. It was suggested we try the managers favorite. I forget the name but it was a whole lot of delicious! The atmosphere is great for families, couples, ladies night out. Friday nights-Couples share a free dessert. Saturday is ladies night. Other nights have live music, open mic, jazz, and Latin dance. The prices are average, maybe a touch below average. The portions were average. The service and food were far above average. Add to that, a clean restaurant with an island feel and you get 5 stars.

One of the worst salad I have ever had at Hungry Greek today. Romaine lettuce.... no feta, no beets, 2 tomatoes and 2 cucumbers. Potato salad was a joke. Very disappointing! Use to be my favorite and I will not visit again if this is the new standard.

3.5 stars. Haven't been back in a couple of years even though I work a couple of blocks away, because I don't want to pay for a salad and get iceberg lettuce (see my previous review from 2011. I didn't realize it has been that long) Friday lunch. Great staff. Great food. Romaine lettuce is back. Chicken on the pit was okay. Love the yogurt dressing. $9.51 Sunday late lunch. Okay staff. Okay food. Out of Soulavki chicken/grilled chicken breast. Out of yogurt dressing. Tzatziki was a good replacement. Very good gyro meat/lamb. The cabbage, which is slightly pickled, tasted old. $9.51 Will be back to give it another try.

This place is great. The owner is very customer focused. I have had hookah in Kansas, Wisconsin, Georgia, California, Washington, Virginia, Alabama, DC, Rhode Island, Illinois, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania, Morocco, Spain, Italy, Kuwait, Italy, and Austria. You will find it near impossible to find a better host than what you get here. Layalena ranks in the top 2 of my experiences. If you like hookah this is the place to be in Philly. They are a small location and it is byob. But if you didn't bring any and you really need a drink there are 2 bars next door that also stay open till 2. My only complaint would be that they don't open till after 6 pm. When you visit you can expect a somewhat small place seating about 30. They have 2 tvs, great mint tea, and Free wifi. I did not try any of the food so I can not comment on that. They are stocked with both al fakher and star buzz plus coconaras. Thanks for a great time Sharif.

This place has top notch Indian cuisine. I have only been for dinner, and have been impressed with all of the vegetarian options I have tried. Great naan, and they will crank up the heat in the dish if you ask for it!

Hummus, Lamb kabobs very tasty and Greek salad very good as well. Great relaxed atmosphere. Was out of my usual places to eat but worth trying something new. Prices are responsible and there was a live belly dancer!
Delicious food and very polite people working there. Highly recommend for lunch buffet and dinner!
Had the gyro ...just like I get up north. Hard to find good middleastern food in florida. Fresh cut fries and a great lunch special price.

Don't come here for the service. But every thing that leaves this kitchen is astounding. The baba ganouj is the literal best I've ever had, and the kibby and falafel we're crisp on the outside and juicy on the inside. Good for kids, the meza plate for two was generous enough for leftovers.

There's nothing that really redeems this place. The service is a nightmare - like you go in and it seems no one even notices you and even when they finally do, you go 20 minutes without a water refill although you're 1 of 3 people in the restaurant. The pho was extremely EXTREMELY bland. This place has some tough competition in Tucson (with Miss Saigon and Ha Long Bay). Just being cheaper than the others won't get you where you need to be. Will not go back!

I am so sad to give this place 2 stars. The decor was very fresh and clean, none of that tackiness I find a lot of time in Thai places. To be fair I have to say that the food was very good as well. However, the poor service is what brought what would have been a 5 down to a 2. We headed over here on late on Saturday night. The place was pretty full, but we had great timing because a few tables got up at once. All we had to wait was 5 minutes or so. It started going downhill when the waitress took our order and seemed very indifferent. In fact my friend tried to order a drink and she walked away! We called her back and all saw her do a very loud annoyed sigh at him! Geez, I didn't think taking an order was that much of an inconvenience! Three of us got our food together, but the fourth person had to ask after 5 more minutes of waiting. Once she got her dish and I was able to start mine, I was pleasantly surprised by how good it was (I had the Pad Prik-Khing)! We all tried a bit of everyone else's dish and they were all delicious. After we all ate we sat and waited...... and waited some more. We waited for I'd say about 30 minutes after we were done eating just to get the check---and the only reason we got it was because we asked another waitress. I know you might read this and think we must have done something to offend her, but I promise you we were nothing but nice people. I was completely baffled by her behavior. Perhaps you'll get lucky and get a different waitress!

The ONLY reason I'm giving this review 5 stars is because of our waitress, Amanda. My boyfriend and I went there for date night and it wasn't our first time so we knew the food was going to be satisfying. We got seated and it took quite a bit of time for a server to approach us. Amanda noticed, came over and offered us drinks. Turns out there was a mixup with servers and she ended up waiting on us anyway. Our food took an extremely long time to come out, which at that point they remade it fresh and the manager delivered it to us (I cannot remember her name though) and apologized. So thank you to management and especially Amanda. She was extremely accommodating and made our date night enjoyable. I'm not one to write reviews but both my boyfriend I felt it was necessary to give proper recognition.

I come here since the opening. The staffs are very friendly. Over all, food is little better than average Thai food. They are using canned mushrooms in Tom yum soup, that is very disappointing. Green Curry's flavor is good, but slightly watery here. The menu pricing is right. Mainly this place is a takeout place, but the dining area is neat. The biggest complain I have is not their fault. The neighbor store people are smoking right outside of the restaurant. You can smell the cigarette when the door opens each time. If you are looking for casual inexpensive Thai food for takeout or delivery, this is the place!!

We went for the first time last night and loved it. It's a bit hard to find, tucked back inside Lenox Village but right next to the parking garage which was convenient. We had spam musubi to start, and even my wife liked it even thought she can't stand spam. Followed that up with kimchi cheese fries, also awesome. My wife had Korean beef tacos and I had hoedeopbap, which is a cold salad entrée and a hot paste which was actually mildly spicy. Both entrees were excellent, as was the service. We will definitely go back and try more of their dishes.

I went to this restaurant twice, but only ended up eating the second time. The first run with Meun Fan was a complete disaster. My party was lazily motioned over to an empty table, where we sat at and went unattended to for the next 10 minutes. My party wasn't given a waiter and even when we tried to initiate some kind of reaction from the staff ourselves, we remained ignored. This was perplexing to us, especially since the place was not very busy, so we simply got up and left the restaurant. My second time with the same group of people was a far better experience. This time we prepared a little more by calling in a reservation. Upon arrival we were seated in an already set up table and promptly received a waitress. The waitress was just fine and from the last experience it was almost just a relief to be talked to at all by the staff. The food turned out to be excellent. All of my party was happy with a mixture of dishes ordered; curries, noodle plates, chow mien. The Thai iced tea was also refreshing and slightly above average portion sizes of the food were provided. The prices were competitive, if not some of the cheaper Thai food you'll find in the area. I would be happy to give this restaurant higher than 3 stars had it not been for the very poor service that we received on our first trip to Meun Fan.

Terrible location. Barely made it a year! Went in once to grab a take out menu and they didn't have any??!! What restaurant doesn't have a takeout menu? That combined with the scrappy location is reaon why they closed.

Went to a birthday party with 25+ people here. Really great outdoor space in the summer, I mean there aren't many better in philly methinks. But corkage fees? Mediocre food? I used to live in the Crown Heights area of NYC, so while I'm not expert I've had my fair share of great caribbean food. This stuff... meh seems about right.

I went here with a friend for University City Dining Days recently and got the naam salad, panang curry, and mango sticky rice. I was really excited because of the average rating of 4 stars on yelp, but I wasn't really a fan of Vientiane by the end. Food: The naam salad was delicious, and the panang curry was pretty good, but they used a little too much oil -- I could see the oil separating from the curry on my plate. As for the mango sticky rice, they used a little too much coconut milk. The small mound of sticky rice was completely covered in the milk, rather than being well-balanced. Overall, I would give the food 3.5 stars. Service: This was where I detracted 1 star because I was pretty ok with the food at all, but the service was extremely slow. In addition, they messed up the dessert orders for both my friend and me, so I had to go to the front desk and wait for a waiter to come out to tell him of the mistake. In addition, the service didn't seem well-organized, as there were long periods of time in the back of the restaurant where a waiter did not even check in on the tables. I would be ok with this, except that the waiting time was inordinately long and that this was during Dining Days, where the restaurant should at least try to be at their best. Overall, go for a nice long (like 1.5 hour long or more) dinner, but if you're in a rush, skip.

Amazing. Couldn't stop eating it was so good! Smoked fish fritters, broccoli salad, sweet potatoes= damn. Fish entree was fab especially the SAUCES!!! I sampled my parents shrimp and steak and they were also great! Finished it off with the key lime pie and pecan pie to share. Side dishes are easy to share with 3 people. So get a few! Highly recommended! I will be back!
Flavors are very authentic Thai and service is fast and friendly.

This has been my family's go-to place for Indian takeout for years. I can't vouch for its authenticity, but the food is so rich and flavorful, I couldn't really care whether it is Americanized or not. Our typical order is malai kofta, vegetable korma, saag paneer, and garlic naan. I'm still not sick of it after ordering pretty much the same thing all these years. The layers of flavors are complex and keep me coming back for bite after bite even after I'm stuffed. It's the kind of thing that makes me say "yum" aloud after eating. The chutneys and yogurt they give you with your order add even more vibrancy to the dishes. Keep a big cup of water next to you though- their food IS on the salty side!

I (like others) am hoping that this place is just in their "getting our feet wet" stage. I REALLY hope this place gets better. I enjoyed the potato Dosa. Prior to cooking it, they asked my spice level liking which I said was a 3-5. Well, their definition of 3-5 is much higher than mine (in other words my Dosa was SUPER spicy. Great but almost TOO spicy). I will adjust accordinlgy next time. I hope they learn to keep more options available later in the night in the future. Alot of the food seemed to be gone at about 8:00pm and they stated that what they had was what they had (in other words they were not cooking any thing additional to choose from). I ordered a few curries and apps (basically I took one of everything they had left). mothing stood out except the Dosa.
Whoa! Great tasting gyros on the go! Love the avocado-lime tsziki and their hummus is fabulous!!

I came here with my siblings (brother's treat, yay), and was a little nervous since we just picked this restaurant randomly while walking by the piazza. But I'm glad we stopped by here. It seems like a really cute BYOB place. The shrimp pil pil was great, and the mussels was out of this world.. I sopped up all the jus with the bread they gave me and drank it down. Service was good, I had no problems, and they didn't seem bothered when I asked them to redo the grilled octopus. Which brings me to the things I didn't like about Dmitri's. The grilled octopus was so chewy and gross, I couldn't get past the texture, and neither could my siblings. I thought it was overpriced for the shrimp pil pil for the amount they gave as well. Overall, it was a great meal. I'd just avoid the grilled octopus and bring a bottle of wine next time.

I have been to this location about three times total, so far. Here are my thoughts on the restaurant and my last outing there: Overall: Each time, the dining room and the bathrooms have been clean and acceptable. (I don't understand the absence of a urinal in the men's bathroom.) The food has been good, not great. Something is not exactly right with the tofu. Perhaps it gets old quickly, but generally, the tofu I get here is tougher than I think it should be. The Food: On this most recent visit, I ordered the Bangkok Curry with beef. The meat was good, but just didn't seem right; a little too soft and odd shaped. I found the dish to be filled with vegetable, black sesame, and noodles (go figure). I would certainly get this again. The Service: I think I primarily dealt with the manager on this last visit, and he was quite accommodating. He provided my friends and I a complimentary rice krispies treat for dessert. That was appreciated. I always like a dessert to settle my meal. Hehe.

Don't mind all the haters who complain about the service...you're here for a good bowl of pho, and not to make lifelong friends of the proprietors, right? Well then, you're in the right place! Very good pho - not too salty, tons of meat in the combo (loved the tendon!), and a fair price of $9 - make this my new goto spot when that pho craving hits. And quite frankly, I found the service to be fine. I'll totally be back!

I really enjoyed the Spice Kitchen in Trooper. The food was excellent, the location was nice, and the wait staff were always incredibly nice. I just received an email the other day however that they have closed the Trooper location, but still have the Lansdale location.

The food is above par, which should be enough to keep you going back. Unfortunately, the service is terrible. Ordered the crab ravioli from the specials for $22.00, but ended up getting a plate of dough with shrimp on top. The cheese filling was nowhere to be found. Three ravioli into my dinner, I was told that my dinner was lobster ravioli and not the crab. Instead of profusely apologizing for the mistake, the waiter just flung up his hands in disgust and walked away. He was upset that my plate was for another table. I'm not a complainer, so I finished my mediocre dinner without saying a word. To add insult to injury, when I received my bill, the waiter crossed off the crab special and wrote in lobster, which was now $2.00 more. Needless to say, I deducted the two bucks off my tip to the waiter. The food is above par, which offsets paying the slightly higher prices. However, my family and I have decided that after two trips in, the wait staff is horrible enough to keep us from coming back.

This is our go to vietnamese restaurant for lunch (from work)... so needless to say, my coworkers and I go there often. This place has always had super friendly and accommodating service when we have gone in. Their prices are pretty average but the quality of food is better than a lot of other places in the area or even in the city. They have a fairly typical menu with all the normal tasty vietnamese dishes (soups rice noodle bowls, stirfries, grilled meat salads, salad rolls, etc) and a decently large vegetarian selection. I would definitely recommend the sate peanut soup - delicious with a little bit of spicy. So perfect for a cold day or if maybe you have had a bit too much to drink the night before. I wish this place was actually closer to my home cause I would probably make it one of my go to Vietnamese places but I will settle for it being a nice treat on a work day.
good coffee, friendly staff. does get crowded though, i worked remotely one day and had a stare down with other computer users over the outlets.

Tonight I was in the mood for some Chinese food. So I found this quiet small restaurant tucked away in a strip mall, next to another place I will try another time. I ordered General Tso's chicken & sesame chicken (for the wife) from the cashier who appeared to be slightly distracted with other duties. The place smelled good until another employee decided to mop with a heavy bleach solution. When I returned with the takeout, everything was prepared exactly as requested, the food was still very hot (temperature) and the Tso chicken had more heat (spice) than I last remembered. Still everything was very tasty and I would definitely order again from the Bamboo house the next time I am craving Chinese.
Buena comida y excelente servicio! Good food and excellent service! It's good for groups and walk-in dine in.

Excellent service and food. I am glad to have a good Place to go to for Indian food just 15 minutes from me. My hubby and I went here for an early dinner around 5. He got the lamb saag, I got chicken tikka masala, and we shared samosa chat for appetizer. We also got a side of garlic naan and raita to have with our meals (definitely worth getting!) We ended our meal with some yummy gulab jamun. The meal portions were perfect, we had to take some to go because we were pretty full halfway through our meal. We enjoyed everything we ordered and definitely will come back to try their lunch buffet!
This place was amazing!!! Fresh authentic food. Hummus and baba ganoush were fresh and super tasty! Gyro sandwich was really yummy as well! 10/10 recommendation!!

First perplexed thoughts upon unexpectedly running across Singha Song with no knowledge of it: "What? They're really going with that name? Wait, where are we? Did Chill Out Cafe redesign itself?" It's bizarrely positioned a whopping block from another long standing thai place-Chill Out Cafe. My impressions so far are positive, but I can't say it does anything special relative to its thai brethren. I've ordered the pad thai and the pad woon sen. Pad woon sen is my default thai dish because 1) I love it 2) it's a good way to compare restaurants based on the same dish. It was mostly as expected. Flavors were pretty on point. However, I would have liked a lot more egg in it. My fellow attendee had the same meal and was equally pleased. The prices fall somewhere in between Chill Out and Sukho Thai with decent portions. Note that when I have gone, they give you bottles of soda instead fountain refills. It's well decorated, if a bit of a hodgepodge. The place gives off a very clean and slightly upscale feel. You wouldn't feel uncomfortable in a decent pair of jeans, though. The staff has been very welcoming and generally attentive. They actually don't have miserable, dead shark eyes from working there it seems. If you're in the area, I'd check out Chill Out first but Singha Song is a perfectly fine choice if you are looking for something a smidge more upscale. Side note: I thought it was funny they bill themselves as "authentic thai" when everything I've tasted is nearly identical to the Chill Out version. Either they're both authentic or somebody be lyin, yall!

I go to new hope all the time we have eaten almost everywhere. We saw this place recently this summer and tried it with some friends. The food was very good, we had the nachos and they were delish! I had the fish tacos and they were also amazing. It's a very cute place I enjoyed sitting outside on the patio. I would definitely return and try other dishes.

Best (but only) Indian food I've had in the Northeast! Like many reviews say, the interior isn't anything special or fancy. Basically tables in the middle of a little grocery shop. BUT the food is damn good. I mostly order one of their 3 lunch specials, usually a meat curry with rice (or naan), tandoori chicken and a can of soda for about $7. The portions aren't overbearing, just right for my appetite but it can get messy if you're not properly stationed at a table (as I learned when I ordered the chicken tikka masala and spilled it in my car). They are located in the plaza with Nifty Fifties so there is parking in the lot. Fast and friendly service. Cash and credit accepted.

Mom and pop Mediterranean. This place may be a small spot but don't let it fool you. I had the baba ganoush and falafel wrap. Both excellent. My wife liked the chop salad, she thought it was ok. We also had spanokopita, very good .

If you like authentic Indian food, this is the not the place for you. That said, if you are not a very adventurous eater and prefer more Americanized cuisine (nothing wrong with that!), I think you would enjoy this place. The food is mediocre at best (I think I'm being kind). I'm Indian and perhaps have a higher standard for Indian food but this food is barely edible. Before I discovered Coriander and Indiya, this was one of my few choices when I was craving Indian food. I gave it maaaany chances, trying the buffet and also ordering ala carte. The food was either consistently bland or tasted of one particular spice, as if they only grabbed the cumin or turmeric etc that day. If you asked for spicy food, all you could taste was the cayenne. Add the fact that the servers are very creepy (they would ask odd personal questions) and I just couldn't keep returning.

People raved about this place. Built it up and got me giddy to give it a try. I was a bit skeptical considering this was a small town Thai restaurant. I met a friend there for dinner on a Wednesday night at around 6pm. The place was buzzing. Actually, the whole street was alive and parking was at a premium. We walked in out of the cold and into the tight waiting area to be seated. After a few minutes we were greeted and sat at a table nestled in a corner. It was a cute place with Polaroids of customers lining the walls and a few Asian trinkets here and there. Our waitress arrived and we were handed 2 incredibly odd menus that were almost like looking at an order form for car parts. We ordered a couple of waters and they were promptly placed in front of us and we were asked if we were ready to order. Not quite ready, we sent her away and studied our menus. There was a fair amount to choose from, and a group of duck specialty items I would have normally gunned for if not for the whole one I roasted the night before. Things started to pick up in the place and it was getting busy. I could tell our server was in the weeds, and it took her a good while to get back to us for our order. We did have our chance early, but wasted it catching up. This wasn't the server's fault, but it looks as if they were caught a little off guard. She returned, and we ordered a Dumpling Soup, Panang Curry, and some Crab Rangoon. The Rangoon came out swiftly and was served with a light sweet and sour sauce with an yellow tinge. These were pretty good, and much better than the frozen varieties that you get at those cookie cutter Chinese restaurants. 15 minutes after we finished our appetizer, the entrees arrived. A large bowl of broth with sprouts and dumplings and a plate with chicken and veggies covered in a red sauce arrived at our table. The panang had a nice aroma and thick slices of green and red peppers. I stirred it around and found a few leaves of really dark, wilted basil. I took my first bite, which contained one of these leaves and there was something off. The panang lacked kick, and that basil had an incredibly bitter flavor to it. I took a few more bites and picked around the last few bits of basil. It wasn't bad, but I've had much better in the freezer section of Trader Joe's. My companion thought the dumpling soup was good, and allowed me to have a few bites. The broth was heavy in garlic, which I liked, with little hints of cilantro and green onion. I snagged another bite with a dumpling which was heavy on garlic as well and some crisp sprouts that added some texture. It reminded me of Pho and I was craving some fresh herbs and rice noodles to go with it. Overall, this place wasn't bad. It doesn't live up to any of the places over on S. Grand or even Sen Thai downtown. However, if you're in the boondocks of Metro East, you'll be hard pressed to find anything better.
Oh Zoe's! You never disappoint! LOVE everything I've ever tried on the menu! I wish there was one here in Downingtown PA!

Wow St Louis! Where'd you pull this one from?? When I think small trendy bars I think Seattle, San Fran, NYC, Melbourne, St Louis is no where near this list. Olio is definitely an oddity in that respect! Super trendy little space with great drinks and food! The staff are super friendly and always willing to help, as well as join in with a bit of banter when they're not busy making their next concoction! If you're looking for a low key place to enjoy some quality drinks with friends this is definitely the place to head! Great ambience, but not super crowded or loud. They offer a "tapas" style menu so you can enjoy some delicious food with your meals too! PS Have to send some kudos to my wife for finding this little gem on Yelp.

I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at Tagine. The food was delicious - a four course prix fixe menu. My boyfriend and I had the soup du jour and the waiter brought out a small bowl of the house soup so we could also try that as an added bonus. The staff was very friendly and attentive. The food was great and the atmosphere was very cool. I would highly recommend.
The gazpacho was astonishingly good, the rice and salad were tasty, and the lamb gyro was meh. Would definitely make the trip back on a warm day for the gazpacho.

I'm going to say this with all seriousness: Marjie's Grill is serving the best, most interesting food in NOLA right now. I eat there a lot, 3-6 times/month. I've had every dish on the menu and so many specials. I've taken almost every visitor and local friend. All agree.

The food here was delicious. I had the kebab platter. It is a good amount of food for a fair price. I was stuffed when I was finished, but I had to clean my plate because it was just that good. They have a big menu with photos. The dinner plate I ordered had chicken, kofta, and I think lamb. All of them were moist, juicy, and tasty. There was bread and hummus and pickled okra, some olives and a few grilled veggies. Oh man, the pickled okra was DELICIOUS! I'm not normally a huge fan of okra, but this was so good. I liked the bread a lot, almost perhaps more than pita. The woman who took the order and cooked the food was nice. It is a small place, but it's clean and bright. I think it is attached to a grocery store and I wish I had more time to check and see if they sold that okra there. I will definitely come back here!!!

I love this restaurant! First time here. Upscale Greek "street food". All the "Greek" places I go to are really "Mediterranean" this is truly Greek. It's a simple atmosphere but the food is what I would expect at a fancy place. I ordered the beef souvlaki - excellent! Spicy feta dip was really great as well. Definitely coming back.

Soco is arguably one of the better restaurant in South County (no offense soco...) Their gyros are consistently delicious and quick. They don't do anything earth-shattering, but they just do gyros really, really well. You get a ton of food for your money too. The service isn't anything spectacular, but I've never had an unsatisfactory experience, and I've been there many times. That being said, I prefer to get takeout because the restaurant offers zero ambiance. Oh and check the hours before you go because they're weird hours. My only complaint is that they're not open for dinner :)

WORSE service ever! The waitress we had was completely incompetent. I saw a few other waitresses who were attentive but we got stuck with a terrible one. Took 2 and a half hours to receive food, they said they were busy but if you looked around they were not. It was quicker to go to the bar and get a drink then to ask the waitress. I will never go back to this place, ohh on top of all of terrible service, the waitress automatically drops in 20% on the bill even though there were three of us. I complained that we did not receive our food, the order was incorrect, and it took almost 3 hours and she basically looked at me and was like you still have to pay it.

This is a hard decision to make, but I think this is my favorite Banh-mi in the city. The bread is perfect, nice and crispy without being stale - I'm pretty sure it's from Dong Phuong, but I've been wrong before. I get the grilled pork, which is just the right amount of crispy, tender, and sweet. The fruits/veggies include carmelized onions, carrots, cilantro, jalapenos, and cucumber. Ask for spicy, unless you're some kind of wimp. Just walk to the back of the store and wait for your sammich, or call ahead and pick it up. There is seating available.

This is not the same Nirvana from Conshohocken. The food is sub par. The service is very good, but we don't go to restaurant just to have good service. I tried the buffet and dinner. Both very disappointing. I guess all the 5 stars must be from friends and family.

I've eaten here nearly ten times. The chicken satay with peanut sauce is always a winner. And I love the coconut rice. The place gets packed with real indos during the weekend at lunch. But I've been lucky to always get a table within a few minutes.

From the moment of walking in Yah Mon is a warm and welcoming establishment. The ambiance and tasteful decor are refreshing to experience. You feel the pride of ownership. Promptly we were greeted with a glass of water while we reviewed the menu. Wonderful selections of the Caribbean are offered. For me the food was deliciously fragrant, getting whims of herbs and spiciness that danced on my tongue. Presentation is everything and my plate was delightful. Thank you for a beautiful dining experience.

Ultimate mango shaved milk ice is out of this world. If you are a mango lover then this will be your favorite desert. I also wanted to mention that they have a pokestop. Because of the many people that frequent this cafe, you will almost always find that a "pokestop lure" has been enabled. There are also two gyms less about a block away in case you need to catch up on some training. The gyms near by at this time are team Mystic but that can be changed! ;)

I do like Sukho Thai. I have been coming here for a few years and this is just a good simple Thai joint that serves decent Thai at a decent price. Sukho Thai is a little slower than some other restaurants, but they are consistent and the atmosphere is relaxed. The food tastes the same today as it did almost eight years again when I started coming here. The same family owns and operates the place, the service has remained the same since day one. I know walking through the door what to expect, and am never disappointed. My go to dishes are the curry, house spring rolls, and the hot and sour soup. Whether eating here or getting it to go, it's good food.

Amazing food! I'm from India, and I can comfortably say that the food here is amazing. Price is decent, not too expensive, but the serving size is huge! They also deliver for free! They've got a regular customer in me for sure!

This restaurant has seating for no more than 15 people and has a carry out feel; however, don't let that atmosphere fool you. Hands down the best Thai restaurant I've been to in Tampa. This Northern Thai restaurant's menu goes beyond the usual green curry and pad thai menu see at many places. Pla Koong: 4 stars. Shrimp salad. Very good. Khao Soi with chicken: 4.5 stars. The coconut milk based broth was amazing. The chicken was not that great. I'll try with beef or shrimp next time. Panang Curry with duck: 5 stars. Excellent flavor. The duck was very tender. Pad see ew: 5 stars. Really good

STAY AWAY! Everything about the visit was horrible. The food was so bad it literally made me throw up. The poster who described the broth as tasting like "dirty dishwater" got it spot on. The service wasn't much better. It took forever to have our order taken and to get our food. One couple actually got tired of waiting and left (I was quite envious of them after the food arrived).

They make vietnamese food to go from a small kitchen. It's not quite as good as restaurants in Nola-East or West Bank, but it's right there in mid-city instead of 20 min drive. Their Banh Mi (vietnamese poboy) is really good!

I was at Olio on fairly early on Saturday evening. My boyfriend and I were out for dinner. Olio is a cute place and the wine list is very nice and very long. The menu was a little disappointing to us. Olio is a great place if you want to drink and have a snack along with your drinks but it's a little disappointing if you are there to eat. The plates are small and you would most likely need to order about 3 of them to end up eating an adequate amount of dinner. This would mean you would have spent about $40 on dinner alone and if you are going to do that you can basically eat at any of the city's most expensive restaurants. The food we did eat was all very tasty though. In summary really nice place to hang with friends and drink all night but not the best choice if you are looking to eat!
Why do restaurants after being open for a few years feels it's okay to cut back on the quality? When this placed first opened and was very good, but now it's just average.

Highly recommend the superb brunch at Suraya! A group of 7 of us tasted almost everything on the menu, and it was all incredible. The chai latte...the brunch cocktails....the labne and babaganoush! Heavenly. My favorite dishes were the gravlax flatbread and the pastry basket, which included an unbelievable assortment of baked goods. This is my favorite spot in Philly hands down.
Staff was kind and the food was amazing, I recommend the beef pho and the KRAB RAGOON WHICH WAS DELICIOUS. Casual place with good prices.

I was excited to see a new African spot open up. Unfortunately my experience was just ho-hum... nothing to write home about. The food was ho hum, service sketchy at best. I had teh oxtail which was so chewy that I left most of it behind, despite being hungry like a wolf.

Absolutely the best Thai food I've had since I've moved down to the area. I've had multiple attempts at getting quality Thai food (especially at a heat level I wanted - for me, if it doesn't make me tear up, we have a problem.) Here, you have the perfect balance of all Thai flavors, and despite the heat level you specify, they allow you a wide range of condiments to elevate the heat. Side note: the first time I ate here, a man tried to bust in and steal all of the change from the fountain from the inside of the door. A man (who seemed to be the owner) burst forward and told the man it was bad luck. From what I could tell, that was enough for the man to put the change back. Long story short: if you want great Thai food, come here. If you want to steal change, try elsewhere... the Taco Bus, maybe?
EXPENSIVE...WORST PHO IN RENO. stay away people. Don't fall for the sign outside .."Reno's best pho" what a joke.

They have really good sandwiches and they have really good iced coffee. whenever I need a quick bite to eat this is always a first place I go to also if you have a big appetite get some spring rolls their peanut sauce is amazing! I would choose this over Jimmy Johns or subway any day of the week. I would definitely recommend the pulled pork with the baguette bread.

My wife and I stooped at this place on our way from Philly to NY. I called the place prior to arrival at 330pm and asked if they are open and serve lunch. Their first response is that Indian buffet is closed. I never cared about that in the first place. Looks like buffet is their large crowd puller. We reached there and found that they are attached to a motel. I didn't like the fact hat it is attached to a motel. The place was empty at this time. The waiters were busy folding napkins and cleaning the bar when we stepped in. The waiter came to us with an unwelcoming look; he just didn't want us there. Anyhow, he got us seated. The ambiance is good and they had good tables/chairs and has a decent view. We ordered veg samosa, paneer tikka masala, poori, roti and chicken Shahi kulcha. Paneer tikka masala was a wrong choice in the first place. It was filled with cream and tons of color. Overall its a 2.5/5
I have been going to this restaurant for 4 years now. The food with the old owners and the new owners is the same. Pretty good. Its a bit expensive for what you get tho!
Best Thai in Santa Barbara. They have a great lunch menu for $9 each. Be sure to try the Phad Prik King or the Panang Curry.

The food is ok and their lunches are pretty cheap for understandably smaller portions. I do enjoy the chicken pad thai with extra egg for less than 8 bucks. Unfortunately the portions are so small it's getting harder and harder to convince the coworkers to come here! Gah! It'll have to be one of those "I haven't had thai in months and I'm not that hungry so let's go here."
It's nice place to get lunch only, because you have to look at the food in the buffet before get it coz I'm sure you'll be surprised with the food that you order from the menu.

I came here in search of some good Pad Thai. I hail originally from Philadelphia, and we have some great Thai spots. This place has filled my void since I moved from Philly. The Pad Thai was amazing, my brother had the spicy noodle which he claimed was unreal. Service was on-point to top everything off. My good friend had his first Thai food experience here and said the stir fry was sublime.

We stopped in for a very late dinner after catching Godzilla and the service and food were great. Our server, in particular, was attentive, helpful, and very friendly, even at 10 pm! The moo goo gai pan was good and the buddha's feast had a great source and tender five spice tofu. Plus, having a brown rice option is always a plus. 3 stars for the food but an extra star for the service.

I really wanted to give this place a good review, but dang it wasn't living up to my expectations. Got there at 8:00 PM on a Saturday night, and didn't have to wait to eat - wonderful. Just going to eat at the outdoor bar. Ordered a black&gold mojito and a pulled pork sandwich. As a restaurant with the Caribbean vibe going, I was hoping the sandwich would be awesome. Also, spicy slaw sounded yum. The sandwich was cold when I got it, and the bun it was served on was probably a Wonder bread bun. Un-impressive. The pork tasted like it had been part of a meat sauce, like the pasta sauce my mother used to make as left overs. Got some pork? Sure, lemme throw that in the Prego. Well, that's what this pork tasted like...yet it was still somehow dry. And if you are going to taste tomato-ey instead of roasted or BBQ, why put mangos on top? It was odd. Not happy with it. The slaw was normal, not spicey, not 'inventive' - boring. French fries were skinnier and less crisy than McDonalds fries. To be fair, my friends loved their shrimp & grits taster plates. For reals, this place was not what I expected. I was bummed out . My mojito was never cold enough and I don't know if they make their simple syrup correctly, because the sweetness wasn't there. Come on! You are named Mojitos! I should be all like, WHOA, rockin' drank lady. Pros: Outdoor seating, live music.

Amazing!!!! My favorite Thai Food Place in the Indy area....The Padd Thai is superb & the Beef Larb leaves you thinking about it until you have it again. The egg rolls are wonderful & my son loved them too!

This food was good but I will NEVER go back there again. It was around 8pm on a Sunday and we were the only people there and there was no music. They charged us for every little thing. We ordered Samosas which average tasting and not hot enough. and they gave us the smallest amount of chutney that would fit into a thimble. Maybe 2 spoons full. We asked for more and they gave us another tiny amount and charged us. We ordered garlic and plain naan, but they only gave one large piece. The portions were less than most restaurants I have been to in the area, but the prices are the same or higher. The naan was served very warm and greasy but delicious and the garlic was the prefect amount of garlicky goodness. I ordered Saag Paneer and it was very good. It wasn't any better than any other that I have had in my life. I was very uncomfortable there. The male server would not speak to me ( I am a woman). if I addressed him, he would shake his head but only speak to my boyfriend. Perhaps they were trying to be courteous but it was awkward. The bill was so expensive. They charged us gratuity which is noted in the back of the menu. I stupidly forgot this and tipped on top of this. They didn't mention anything. But there were only 2 of us, why the need for mandatory gratuity. The interior was nice and the wall art was really pretty.
Wow! Tonight had the burger, beet platter, Brussels sprounts small plate. All incredible. Heidi was a fantastic waitress. Update 4/1/18. Still 5 star brunch. Trust is always amaxing

Super clean & super friendly. We mentioned it was our first time to a Zoe's & the employee/manager (if she's not a manager or owner she should be) was super kind about answering questions. We had hummus app, shrimp kabobs & steak kabobs. These were better than the ones I had in Greece! The food was cooked to order & the veggies tasted like they just picked them outside. We were pleasantly surprised by both the food & service!
This restaurant was excellent! The service was great and our food came piping hot. The serving sizes are big, which allows you to have leftovers. We will definitely be back!

First time in. Nice clean restaurant. The spring rolls were fresh and tasty. I planned on getting Pho but ended up getting one of the weekly specials which was the scallops with veggies. $9.95. The food came out hot and there were good sized scallops and the dark sauce had a fantastic taste with hints of garlic and ginger. This is a great little restaurant and very reasonably priced for a restaurant on St Charles. The staff was friendly, prompt and knowledgeable. We will be back for sure.
Have never had a bad meal here. The food is tasty, generously portioned (so much so that one meal feeds me three times), and the staff is very nice! You feel welcomed like family here.

You need to make a reservation or eat at the spacious bar. That is because in the suburbs any place worth going to will always be busy. Food was tasty, and the special sauce isn't necessary and not mixed well, but the star for me was my mai tai. Towering over the table, I can down 'em all night long! I also enjoy how they don't cut the calamari into rings. That is so 2001! :) Service was also superior juxtaposed by havingbeen ignored by THREE bartenders downstairs at Dave & Buster's across the street a week earlier.

Mai Thai is a really cozy place to enjoy some good Thai food in Tampa. The restaurant itself is a bit small and dark, but the decorations are nice and very Thai. We ordered Pad Sea Ew and Green Curry. Both dishes came out fast and very tasty. Lunch prices were very affordable and the staff was very friendly!

I got the beef pho. The broth is a little different. I can't pin point what's different, but it's pretty tasty! I can taste the flavor and the seasoning. It was delicious. I got a large for 7.99. You can't go wrong with that at all! Next time I try this place out, I want to dine in. I got their egg roll appetizer. It was good, but not the best, but good. I definitely want to try their bubble tea and dessert! Until next time pho 36! I'll be back.

Vientiane Cafe is a terrific neighborhood gem gently nestled along a string of dive bars and fellow ethnic joints on Baltimore Ave. We came here on the recommendation of a friend of mine while entertaining out of town guests in search of the classic Philadelphia BYO experience. Armed with two bottles of wine, the six of us enjoyed a filling dinner of delicious and cheap Thai and Laotian food that satisfied our hunger and kept our wallet light. I enjoyed the Lad Na with Beef, which is sort of like a Pad See Ew except with a slightly thinner sauce and more vegetables. The broccoli was crisp, the beef was flavorful and juicy, and the noodles were done just right. Everything in the dish worked perfectly together. The BF and I also split a Nam Salad; some sort of lettuce wrap thing that tasted pretty good although I have no idea what the filling was (kind of reminded me of Bac-os?). Not as good as the noodles in my opinion. The service could have been slightly better (it took them forever to get us the wine glasses, although to their credit we were a large party and it was very crowded for the later side of a Friday night), but I was still very pleased with the food, ambiance, and overall value. Definitely a place I would be happy to return to for a low-key dinner or even take out. Also, at just under $20 per person with tax and tip included, it's extremely reasonable. Do make sure you bring cash though.
The service here was nice. The food was freshly prepared and refilled promptly. The workers were very nice to us. I would definetly come here again in the future!

It's good, but overpriced. Not enough to blow you away for the price. Zahav is amazing and is worth the money. This place is okay, but not worth it. The place is gorgeous and the prophet cocktail is very good! But I don't think I'll be back for dinner I'll come back In the future for coffee and pastries during the morning. Or just to sit at the bar for cocktails

We used a groupon.... that's what got us in the door. We were excited to try some real authentic Greek food. The food was Ok.... not the best I've ever had. The thing that I have to complain about is the service. The bar took forever with our drinks, and we didn't order anything crazy. Then two of our plates were served to another table- by the hostess who didn't know what was going on. I tried to tell her that the plates were ours- but was ignored. Our server didn't even know that the table next to us (that arrived only a few minutes before) received our fried octopus. My husband then had to wait another 30 minutes to get the food. We spent over 2 hours to receive only 4 dishes, which were minimally good at that. The atmosphere was just not welcoming and we most likely will not be back. Too bad.

I really enjoyed the atmosphere. It made me feel like I was in Italy eating at a restaurant. The service was impeccable and the food was amazing. I'll definitely go back to try other food on the menu.

Good western style Chinese food place. Fresh ingredients and lots of veggies in everything. Would go back. I say western style because the menu is in English only and the appetizer section includes buffalo wings...
Love to go for lunch buffet. Items don't change often. Tandoori chicken is always moist and paneer is my favorite. Excellent value for very good food. Excellent service
Excellent Thai food, had the seafood combo lots of shrimp, scallops,oysters ! Highly recommend this place!

The food of the main dish was not bad, basic. Though, the dessert (jelabbi) and the lassi mango were awful, especially the mango lassi that was like a mango white yogurt. I ordered a peach mint hookah that looked more like a mint than a peach mint one, but still the price is of 18 what I consider fair. To sum up, nothing extraordinary in this restaurant for the food, it is not a place I would come back to.

I have been going to Dosa Hut & Chaat House on & off for over 3 years. I was in Allentown, PA for work which is about 35 miles, I drove to this place with friends to have dinner. We waited at front desk to be seated and menus were given. We ordered Chicken lollipop, Chicken 65, Samosa chat, 3-different Dosas, Uthappams and Andhra Chicken Biryani. Took more than 30 mins to get Dosas, Uthappams & Biryani. (Place was not busy while we were there except 2 other families in restaurant) Chicken lollipop, Chat and 65 was served 20 mins after the order was placed. Place is under staffed and service was not attentive. Place is good for Dosas, Uthappams and Idlis but not for chats. Chicken lollipop was lick smacking. 65 was ok. Place is absolutely no no for Biryani's, I am Hyderabadi and I could cook Biryani for 50-100 members at home. Their Biryani is more like a fried rice with low-quality basmati rice, when complained they were rude and in turn showed attitude ! The quality of this place has been consistently going downhill and prices are going up ! The new management includes a sneaky 3% "service charge" and rude. It's ok to charge a tip..but the way they behave when asked is a little shady. Overpriced place, Food's alright but not worth the price at all. If at all close by in area will only go for Dosas and Chicken lollipop.

I really enjoy the use of spices in everything, and the chicken is really special. The flavors are most unique for Boise. I'm sure some people will not enjoy the food as much as I do, but it is always a pleasure to eat here. I agree with others the ambiance and service could be improved. But I go there for the food and the rest doesn't bother me.

Excellent lentil soup, oh!! I fogot to mention the veggie pickles,fresh and crispy.the chicken with garlic sauce...OMG from heaven,what a gem in temple terrace. The ambiance needs some improvement,but the food i love it. I do not like to watch tv here with jerry springer show,they have to work on ambiance.
