Flavor Flave Chicken Tikka Masala is now having not as good chicken chunks in it. What happened dear one? On more juicy notes, a new dessert was found today instead of rice pudding. My Indian cohorts have only learned me the name of Udupi, which was not this. We settled on the Joosey Donut. Please see picture.

Nothing like being scolded by the waitress after waiting for 20 minutes after being seated with not even a "be right there" from any waitress. When we asked the busboy which one was our waitress (he didn't know), she announces across the room "There are other people who were here before you! I'll be over there soon!" No apologies. By minute 45 we had our breakfast, which was fine. Same older waitress's attitude is why I have not been there for a couple of years even though the restaurant is one of only a couple in our town. Not sure I will be convinced to go back again.

Out of the 3 indian buffets in the Area (New Dehli, Sitar & Tandoor), I must say Tandoor is my personal fave. The food is the most fresh, and the staff is super friendly. Plus they remodeled the place which was a plus. I wish they had bigger dessert options on the buffet but overall I'm definitely going there again.
Really great menu! I ordered the jerk chickan with Jialo Rice and Plantains. It was excellent comfort food. The Jerk seasoning was very flavorful and the rice was great! Can't wait to go back!
Fantastic variety of dishes. If going for gluten free njira order ahead of time. The best way to wrap up the meal is with the Ethiopian coffee.
Completely unremarkable Pad Thai. Food very slow to be prepared. Nice venue and friendly waitstaff. Tap beer selection quite pedestrian. Not worth a return visit.

This is my second review of THIS Place. A little gem right in my neighbourhood and across the street from MacEwan. My boyfriend and I received very friendly service again and this time, decide to try their selection of food because delicious bowls of Thai curry and Vietnamese Pho are perfect in this cold, wintery weather. My boyfriend tried the beef pho with a veggie stock (they ran out of the beef stock) which was full of flavor and very yummy. I on the other hand tried the green curry bowl which was a bit too spicy for my palette, but full of flavour nonetheless. The side of rice could've been warmer but once you mixed it in with the curry, it seemed to be better. We both ordered the limenade (they ran out of the lemonade) and it was perfectly tangy for me. Come check out this hidden spot downtown, they have a wide arrange of hot drinks too that look wonderful.

3.5 Stars So I went back for a second time today. There were a lot of changes made to this cart which I thought all dramatically helped the experience. For one he had a helper, so instead of just him serving and cooking there were two of them popping out orders. It still took some time, about 1-2 minutes a person, but it was much improved over the last time. I also received more food then I did the first time. I was actually content at the end of my meal. And lastly I thought the food was just plain better. It wasn't slopped around all over the place and the chicken while still kinda burnt was softer then the last time and much more flavorful. It was a great plate of food. This man has passion for his food, and almost runs a great business. He still needs to be quicker, cheaper ($10 is a lot for a food cart lunch w/ no drink) and have some sort of customer service. If he improved all of those just a little bit, he could get the 5 stars his food deserves.

The food is great. Staff is very efficient and friendly. They do very well with lunch time rushes and normal dinner time traffic. The eggplant and Thai basil was AMAZING!!! Best Thai food ever. I don't say that easily. This restaurant can accommodate large parties if needed as they have plenty of tables and a specious enough dining room to rearrange for it. The ambiance is very nice and calm.
Great service. Great environment. Food is pretty good. Sushi didn't taste too fresh. Menu was a little confusing, Kind of all over the place. Overall a good place

Food is good but not worth the price and customer service they have. They take forever to serve food. I have had bad customer service experience twice. They don't even look at you while taking order, there is no management of handling in house customers or taking orders on phone. Sometimes they forget to give you water eve after asking twice. And about food it is not that great. Samosa are hot from out side and you can still feel cold frozen masala inside.

Zagol appeared pretty austere. It's a large space so the emptiness is amplified when only a few customers are present. It also dilutes the attempts to establish an ethnic decor. The food seemed on par with other Ethiopian restaurant I have visited in other cities. The communal Ethiopian dining experience is always fun; particularly for those who are new to it.

We just picked up lunch here for the first time. Drive by this food truck every day on the way to work. So glad we finally stopped in...excellent!!! The jerk seasoning is TO DIE FOR and everything else we ordered is exceptional too. I'm still in nirvana :-D This saves a special foodie trip to the Caribbean...for now at least ;-)

Expansion Ruins a Favorite We and one or two couples have eaten here regularly over the years. Great food, BYOB, with a pleasant, busy, bistro feel on a Saturday night. In expanding into the building next door, we think they have misjudged, and ruined the place. Other than the low lighting and claret walls, the dining area could be any mid-range restaurant serving any type of food in any part of America. Add to that, $18 for what seems like a smaller portion, and waiters stopping by at the table every five minutes to where we just wanted to ask them 'Please, leave us alone, stop asking if we need anything!', we left disappointed. I wish them all the best, and perhaps others will like it, but we are now looking for an authentic Indian to visit.

This is one of the best Thai places I have ever been to. The food was INCREDIBLY fresh, and the drunken noodles were the best I have ever had, and the coconut ice cream was out of this world. Portion sizes were very large. The atmosphere was beautiful, and very relaxed. The staff was very helpful, and willing to offer advice as to what to order - in addition to telling some people what was in their order. They even have some less exotic options for the little ones. The prices were outstanding as well - a great bang for your buck.

I must admit, i have driven by here dozens of times but i never knew about this spot, until I was exploring yelp for new finds. For those in the know about banh mi and boba tea, this is the cleanest and most modern spot to get these awesome, insanely cheap delicacies in the entire Tampa/Clearwater/St Pete area. It is well lit, full of enthusiastic people and families, and plays a great assortment of modern electronic dance music. Even better, the Jalapeño and pickled vegetables on the banh mi were super flavorful. Don't miss it! We'll be back!

THIS PLACE IS THE BEST. I dont really get where all these reviews about poor customer service are coming from. I mean at most Pho places i've never had stellar customer service, but its never mean yelp worthy about. As long as your pho is good, I dont really care. And this place is GOOD. Always really fresh ingredients and its very well priced. Just a heads up, if you come during the lunch hour you might be waiting a little bit due to it being so popular. I just call mine in with ease and pick it up for a little work pho. I highly recommend coming here!

Highly recommended. Great food, reasonable priced. I really enjoyed the Panang Curry. Very nice atmosphere and clean as well. At times you can hear go-karts outside but the windows are frosted so you don't have to watch them.

For a cute little town like Media, I'm really disappointed there isn't a better Vietnamese place. This place is the closest thing we have and their pho has been a bit hit or miss. Once it was extremely salty as if they spilled soy sauce in it. More likely it was just not fresh and have been cooked down too much though. The other two times they were decent, not quite what I was hoping for but got me through as I just needed some broth-y comfort food. The Thai options here are good, and I like their spring rolls. They get extra credit for plating also. All in all a solid restaurant within walking distance of my humble abode. Definitely room for improvement to go from "eh" to "wow" though. I hope they can step up to the plate.
The atmosphere is unique and the food was amazing! Def try this place. The food can be mild or spicy. My fried rice had a hint of coconut sweetness. The green curry was spicy but not too much!

We had the Chicken Tikka Masala, chicken vindaloo, and garlic naan. Everything was great. The garlic naan was fluffy and garlicky, best we had in St. Louis so far. Our entrees had the perfect level spice and heat. The flavors were well balanced. We loved how spicy it was. They definitely aren't afraid of adding to heat to the food. We can't wait to go back and try their goat dishes.

Awesome service and ambiance. Incredible food. Try the stuffed peppers for an appetizer. We had the surf and turf last night and was not disappointed. Sit at the bar and chat with Todd...try the Metaxa cognac for an after dinner drink. A great dining experience.

My family and I went for the first time last night (there was 5 of us) and we loved it. The owners were so nice and the staff was super attentive. The food was amazing and we would definitely be back. We had leftovers that were delicious for breakfast this morning (lamb with rice and naan)....yummy

If you at all a fan of good Indian food, please do not even try to eat here. Just had some made-to-order dishes along with food from the buffet (was eating with friends), and it was all pretty terrible. Then again, you get what you pay for, and the food here is incredibly cheap. It also tastes cheap. If you want quality Indian, try Ekta, which offers the best Indian food in the city. You'll get twice as much food at twice the price, but the quality is incredible. All the curries I tried here were watery and oily and pretty much inedible. The naan was disgusting and tasted like it was made days ago prior to being blasted in a microwave and served. It's really terrible. I couldn't even finish what I ordered. If you aren't that familiar with what great Indian food could taste like and are on a budget, perhaps you should give it a shot. If you want the real thing, try a better spot. Ekta is still my #1 in the city,

We tried several dishes, sweet & sour chicken & shrimp tempura and honestly the taste was quite bland but it was warm when served and the prices were a bit high but on the plus side if you have issues with spices in food his place uses very little so you'll be safe eating here.
Not a Thai food regular but loved this place. Had the chicken basil. Others had spicy noodles and they were fabulous! Staff were friendly.

Came in for lunch, and appreciated their lunch menu! Ordered Panang Curry, asked for 4 star spicy. It was delicious! Very flavorful and good-size portion for a value lunch item. Will definitely go back!
Love the concept and the food was good. Really loved being able to sit in rickshaw to eat. They also have beer and wine. Will eat there again.

Okay this is my first time trying this bc Gigi & big r sucks lmao! But man oh man the oxtail w the rice & peas along w the cabbage goes hard! Shits so good! The mac n cheese could use some work tho. My moms is much better , but hey everyone can't be like her. I was sick as shit y'all didn't have doubles or buss up shot but it's cool, the oxtails sufficed. Over all good, just try new mac recipes!
the food here was very good. The staff was very helpful, nice and all worked together as a team. I would eat here again.
Great food. Unique ingredients. Great quality. Full bar. Awesome, casual spot for tacos and drinks. Highly recommend
First time eating Thai and I was pleasantly surprised. I got the drunken noodles with beef. The beef was a little overcooked for my liking but in general it was a good dish overall.

The food is good and they give you generous portions. It's usually pretty easy to get seating. The only issue is the last time I went they brought my food out significantly before my friend's, almost 10 minutes before. This made it a little awkward as we were eating at different times.

Just what you want for fast tasty fresh food at a great price...and much more ...today running in not realizing there were just closed for Thanksgiving..we were served with a smile AND told not to worry we could sit and eat while they cleaned up...when was the last time someone welcomed you when they were closing....great staff . Thank you. chicken tikka bowl was excellent.
Very solid option for dinner. I like the ambience, the staff and the food is great. Prices are reasonable making this a high value draft pick in a world of busts. I will be back for sure.
Gone for lunch a few times. It's a great deal and everything has been very good. I esp liked the green curry. I usually get something to go as well, it's that good.
Great service and many choices on the menu. I have been here 3 times but have only ever ordered the curry chicken (it's too good not to eat while I'm here)

The gyros are where it is at. Baklava so light and flakey, don't miss it either. Friendly service. Outdoor seating (it's a strip mall but at least it's an option!). Pita is not the best (seemed a day old almost) but I also can't really complain about it either. Definitely worth the trip when in the mood for some Greek.

I went to P.F. Chang's yesterday for the first time and I had a great experience! First and foremost, our server, Michi (Michelle) was the best! She is so pleasant, patient and friendly -- you should definitely ask for her. The drinks and the food were all delicious. I will be going back soon!

DO YOURSELF A FAVOR GO HERE NOW. HURRY! Stumbled across this lovely place as a six party refugee group from an unnamed popular place acrossed the street refused to accept my guests government issued picture IDs from England. Fabulous food, great drinks, lovely accommodating bar tender and staff. Cannot rave enough! Thank you. SEE YOU SOON.

Have loved this place for several years. Stopped by today (first time in a couple months) to find it closed with a sign on the door! Devastated, and my 6 YO daughter was crying (she loves Blue Fig). I hope for the best for the ownership, and we will miss you!

I've been coming to Mesa Thai for years (that's what us locals call this place). The service is good and food is excellent! My favorite dish is the spicy Thai basil chicken-unbelievably good! Definitely worth a visit or just get it to go :)

Interesting interior with drapery all around. NOT EVEN a crack of window. I am a hookah & belly dancer EXPERT. Trust me when I say this. This place knows neither. Hookah - uses cheap coals that burns out too quickly, too tightly packed shisha that doesn't pull any smoke, small head basin (i'm used to grape or orange base) Maybe I'm just too used to NY quality vs. Philly? Just saying.
Delicious pizza! Great crust, zesty sauce, fresh ingredients and professional service.
HIgh quality italian food with a great ambiance. One of my favorite local restaurants
Used.to be good for Ethiopian good, but no longer serving Ethiopian food. They might still serve bar fare though .

Definitely a fan of both the quality and service here! We have now been twice for a quick bite pre-Regals and have always been pleased with the speed of service and the quality of our food. I've tried both the chicken gyro and the traditional and every time am in shock at how much meat is in a $5.95 gyro. It definitely looks fresh and tastes amazing. The pita is always soft and fluffy and the veggies always crisp. Great for quick bite without sacrificing quality!

This is restaurant quality food served out of a food truck. I would have paid $20 for half of the food, it was that delicious. The "interesting" conversation with the cook was just icing on the cake. You HAVE to try this food if you live or work in the area. It doesn't disappoint!

After reading reviews for Olio in basically every newspaper and magazine in St. Louis over the last month I decided that it was time to give this place a try. In advance of my first trip, I extensively researched the menu, wine, and spirit options of both Olio and Elaia via their websites (honestly, if it is your first time going I would suggest doing this. There are SO many drink options that it can get over whelming if you don't know what you are walking into). I came to Olio the first time with VERY high expectations, and I was blown away by every aspect of the experience! I am hooked... Olio is set in a vintage gas station is McRee Town just south of The Grove and north of the Botanical Gardens. The other half of the experience (Elaia) is positioned in the adjoining townhouse next door, both restaurants are attached by terrace and covered walkway. The ownership group has done a phenomenal job restoring the gas station. There is a good mix of antique influence and modern flair, not to mention a phonograph sitting on the bar to set the musical mood for the space. When you walk in there is a bar area and window seats for about 20 people. In the old service bay to the right is a small dinning room with about the same capacity. While yes Olio is a wine bar, don't let the small food menu fool you. The dishes that this little gas station puts out are exquisite! There is a nice range of european cheese offerings, Salume Beddu charcuterie options (go figure...), some small plate/salad dishes and then the nightly rotisserie feature. The cheese and charcuterie blow away everywhere else in town, then again this is what the ownership group is known for. While I have only had a limited number of the salads at Olio, I can tell you from experiencing Ben's coking elsewhere that every item is well balanced. Ben's cuisine always tends to be light, fresh, and pack a lot of flavor. Olio does a great job of showcasing simple ingredients in an almost out of this world way... very inspirational stuff! If you are in the mood for more of a "meal" or would like to try something a little bit more filling, go with the nightly rotisserie options. Porchetta, Lamb, Guine Hen, ect... Each night one protein is featured, as a result all of the staffs effort is into perfecting that one dish, none of these will disappoint. I would be remiss if I did not mention the wine and spirit program and Olio (after all this is a wine bar!!). Olio employees an Advanced Sommelier and also an assistant sommelier. I was told that the wine list features over 600 unique offerings. You can do wine by the glass, the bottle, of the flight. For me there was too many options, I always suggest talking it over with the staff and working with them to pour the perfect glass for your palate. If you have been thinking about going to Olio, what are you waiting for!?!?! Olio should be near the top of everyone list. (Side note - Olio is a home run, can't wait to try Elaia!)
Very relaxed environment, awesome vibes. Good hookah. Tea was alright. Didn't try the food but will next time! Looks great.

Nice place to go for a quick and very reasonable lunch. $10 for the buffet and bread (sort of a puri but deflated). It is a good way to introduce new comers. None of the food was very spicy, even the vindaloos which in other places can burn the hair off of your head. If you want something convenient and different in DelCo, try it. They also have a place on State Street in Media, as well. The decor is quite nice for being in a strip mall across from Fisher's hardware.
I don't know how the food is because they close after lunch (whatever time that is) and reopen at 5pm. Very small seating area. No restroom.

I love this place! This is the first place I discovered bubble tea! The curries are wonderful and authentic. I am glad this restaurant is conveniently located on the south side of town and close to my house. I hope to visit this place many times in the future!

First time here, it was a fine experience. I like how the food is spicy but they give you the option to lower the heat, since everything is made to order. The service was really good. I will definitely come back again and would recommend to people who are looking for something different.

I know, I was hesitant too at first. I mean, Mexican and Thai... but but I when I asked where there was anything good around where my work was, I got pointed to CZ. The first thing I noticed was the line. At 2 pm, considerably outside of the normal lunch rush, there was one crowd that easily beat all the other stands on the street. There was a bit of a wait, but it was worth it for one thing: the short rib taco. Short rib is a wonderful thing, and I've actually had a similar version back home in Buffalo. The difference was, the cost of one there was the cost of three here and they tasted just as good if not better. The beef was well seasoned and had a great mouth feel, the avocado was rich and creamy and the spicy sauce (supplemented with sriracha) left a wonderful burn in my mouth. I went back later that week and got a Chicken Satay taco as well, which was alright but not as good, but that short rib taco was still just as good. The last time I was there I got a chicken katsu (which can be served on its own, put into a burrito to on a roll) which was crispy, not greasy and served with a wonderful katsu sauce. They do a rotating curry special, which I have a fondness for and I think is worth checking out. Feel free to ask about getting any of the dishes changed to a platter or one big burrito as an off menu substitution, as they generally are very flexible. Probably the biggest down side is the wait. They tend to get very busy, and I've waited as long as 20 minutes to be served (the chicken katsu). If you're looking for something quick to grab before running back to the office, this isn't it. However, the prices are reasonable and the wait typically translates into your food arriving hot, perfectly cooked and correctly seasoned. If you can put up with standing outside that long, you'll be good.

Great BYOB spot with authentic Dominican food. It is my go to spot before seeing a show at Union Transfer or Underground Arts. We always get the half chicken which comes with beans an rice, plantains, and empanadas. This is all under $20 total for the both of us. Can't go wrong with this authentic and affordable Dominican restaurant. Friendly staff as well.

I can think of nothing wrong with this restaurant. It has incredible food, authentic to a T. The service is... beautiful. They had a band playing chill tango music one time I went here, and another night had a salsa dancing night. I love the vibe, the drinks are great. I just love this place.

I absolutely love Vietnamese food and I'm envious of the array available in Philadelphia. That said, as a restaurant in the West Chester area, this is about as good as it gets for Vietnamese. Of course, with the suburbs comes an increased (but still reasonable) price and a less diverse menu. Servers are generally very nice and attentive and I can satisfy my bun (vermicelli rice noodle salad) craving easily with the bamboo special. Plus, they bring out a condiment caddy that has a special place in my heart. Now if they only can add some bahn mi I might loose my Philly Vietnamese envy.
Pho Broth is pretty damm good. Meat is pretty tough, service is ugh, and you only get one napkin. But like i said the pho broth is pretty damm good. 4 stars
Friendly staff. Great fast service. Clean. Not busy on a Tuesday night. Only drawback was there are no changing tables in bathrooms for babies. Food was good.

I ordered takeout on Christmas Day and was impressed. The food was ready in 15 minutes, piping hot, and very tasty. Bonus: they gave me a discount for paying in cash! I ordered Channa Masala (chick peas), Bhindi Masala (okra) and Pepper Chicken. All three were very good. The spices were legit; curry leaves, coriander seeds, and cardamom were beautifully balanced. I love that no pre-ground blends were being used; it definitely impacted the flavors. I plan on going back and trying more from their menu.

No wonder there was a small crowd of people waiting by this truck: the food is fresh and delicious, and the portions are generous. We got a fish platter with collard greens and candied yams, plus a four-sides combo platter with mac and cheese, rice and beans, cabbage, and (more) candied yams. The owner was friendly and chatty. Looking forward to our next visit!

Nice location, nice atmosphere, bit I've no idea where all the 5-star reviews came from. Having grown up on Italian, can safely say that while the food is very good, it is NOT great or excellent, and certainly not exceptional. You likely won't de disappointed, understand; just understand it's not excellent food. The other turn-off was the prices; they're somewhat high for a place of this nature... $19 for linguine and meatballs? $21 for linguine and clam sauce? Sorry, that's simply too much for a place like this.
Yummy lunch special..had noodles with pork and fried wonton. Iced coffee​ was smooth! My 2nd time here.
New Fave!! The Umami roll is to die for. Definitely going to be a regular spot from now on. Nice array of drinks to choose from as well. Very clean. Very modern. Convenient location.

Highly recommended *Gem*. Very welcoming, locally owned small restaurant that prides itself in unique and seasonal menu items. Mushroom chicken risotto was superb! Rich and flavorful with the natural flavors of the risotto, hand-pulled chicken and fresh mushrooms. Thankfully they had a lunch and dinner portion (the lunch is plenty). The service was very attentive and authentically kind. I am in town for business, so not sure when I would be able to return, but it's a great spot! I didn't have room, but the desserts looked delectable!
I didn't really like pho here but I have a lot to say about bahnmi. They were awesome. Bread was soft and the meat inside was super delicious. I would go for bahnmi alone next time.
We had another delicious dinner here tonight. The staff is very friendly too! This place is consistently good.

Food tasted great as always. But customer service is severely lacking. I believe they have new personnel on staff that lack common decency and are rude to customers. My dad ordered takeout from here yesterday and the person at the cashier was incredibly rude to him and seemed bothered to ring us up. Even though you are not expected to tip on takeout orders, my dad perhaps thinking the cashier was expecting a tip (and hence was throwing a hissy fit) reached out to him and attempted to hand him couple of dollars. To our surprise he very rudely refused without maintaining eye contact and handed us our receipt. I have been regularly visiting this restaurant since 2009 and even booked a hall here for an engagement party with catering but ever since this sour experience we will NOT be returning here or recommending friend's & family to come here either. For the management, this discourteous staff member was working on July 19 10:30pm on Saturday. ..... For customers that eat Halal food, note that employee's wrongly claim that meat is halal. In the above mentioned transaction, the waiter told us that the food is indeed halal but the manager immediately corrected him saying that the meat is NOT halal. Again, Muslim customers should know that meat is not halal. The fact that waiters are misrepresenting this sensitive religious issue shows their lack of professionalism and respect for their customers religious beliefs. Long story short: avoid this place if you value honest customer service.
This place is under new ownership (3months old). The owner was very welcoming and the food delicious!! Give it a try!
Such a wonderful place. Fantastic food and lovely owner. Will definitely be back!

Excellent, excellent, excellent! Party of 3 dined in on a rainy Monday evening and we were provided excellent service. We ordered the samosa chaat, garlic naan, chicken tikka masala, lamb korma, rice pudding, pistachio ice cream, and 3 cokes. Everything had such depth of favor - almost beyond comprehension. Naan was sooooo super thin and crispy but soft. Tikka masala (ordered as "very hot") had a wonderful backend heat without the feeling of being scorched. The lamb korma was succulent and complex. Everything was just great. I can't wait to go back!!!!!

The bread is extra crunchy- after eating this meal- still feeling hungry - only giving the stars for the building its self- we ordered three things on bread? Bruschetta was the best in my eyes- 45 dollar bill-also had added one beer on the nothing stood out to me- the food wasn't bad- but the food is overpriced - our server did a great job- considering she could had told us everything would of been on bread-

I was shopping at Target for some Halloween decorations for my yard and saw a sign for the new Naf Naf Grill. Since, I needed a bite to eat, I decided to stop off. I came in and was greeted by the site of interesting seating options. However, I pretty much forget about that thought after seeing a staff member dancing around. I guess it shows she is excited about her job, but it just seemed unprofessional. Still, I stayed and ordered. I decided to order the chicken schwarma hummus bowl. I got it with the chicken schwarma topped off with peppers salad, hummus and one of their sauces. I also got a container of fries on the side. My food came out very fast and was pretty hot. I got and seat in one of their booths and began to eat. While the food looked very good and healthy, it just wasn't great. I felt as if the chicken really lacked flavor, which threw everything else off. The pita bread, which came on the side was immaculate, but it wasn't enough to make up for my bad experience with the chicken schwarma. Altogether, I had a pretty average experience at Naf Naf Grill. When on City Line Avenue again, I might stop off.

The food is a 5 star experience...best falafel sandwich in the city. But then there's Cristo, the owner/ cook. This man refuses to post his menu, or prices. Sometimes you show up and the sandwich is $8 and the next week it's $10....Steep in my opinion for a cart. The experience of standing in line is tortuous. You have to listen to the egotistical Cristo tell how his food anywhere else would cost $100...yada yada yada. Same story EVERY time. The last straw for me was when I waited for 20 minutes and through numerous of his rants to be told that I could get only one sandwich at a time as the person who would eat the other was not in line. Needless to say, my wife was quite disappointed when I returned home empty handed. If you can tolerate a long wait, not knowing how much you'll pay that day and listening to the same rants over and over, you'll definitely enjoy the food

My sister, niece, and I tried out Guru's on a whim last night and we couldn't be more pleased with the food, the atmosphere, and the service we received. We were sat immediately and were treated to a plate of bread (more of a cracker-like consistency) with a couple of dipping sauces - one green and one tamarind, both were yummy. After ordering our entrees, we were treated to a bowl of Spinach Chaat - a chickpea breaded, fried spinach salad with a sweet tomato and onion salsa on top. It was fresh, bright, crunchy, and a delicious way to start the meal. I could have eaten that as my meal by itself. As for the entrees - We tried the Chicken Korma, Chicken Makhani, and Lamb Rogan Josh. All three of us shared so we could all try everything. Every single dish was perfect - we asked for them all to be mild (they offer to make each dish more mild or spicy depending on your own taste). The Chicken Korma was creamy with thick, tender chunks of chicken. The Lamb Rogan Josh was hearty and juicy like a stew. And the Chicken Makhani - my go-to at any Indian restaurant - was just perfect. All were so different but each so flavorful, seasoned with various spices and herbs and the meat cooked just perfectly - so tender, you can cut with a fork. None were "hot spicy," but all were full of spices and flavor. (Again, you can increase the heat if you want!) We shared garlic naan and dipped our bread into each of the sauces. There were three of us sharing three dishes and we had plenty to take home afterwards. Once we finished eating, we were treated to little dishes of creamy, delicious rice pudding (it's not actually rice pudding but I didn't get the name), just a couple spoonfuls, enough to satisfy that sweet craving after a good meal. The husband and wife team that own this restaurant are incredible - he was knowledgeable and thorough, she was prompt and so friendly! They obviously have a passion for what they do and it comes through in their food and service. The prices were totally reasonable, especially considering the amount of food you get and the obvious care involved in making the dishes. My family and I will be back, for sure! So glad we tried something new :)

Yummiest food platter I've had in a while. Everything tasted fresh and delicious. I ordered the rice with beans and the chicken skewers and man did it hit the spot. The restaurant was clean and airy and had a patio that we enjoyed. Also the main guy behind the counter was so sweet and hilarious. Overall o had a pleasant experience and the food hit the spot.

Not traditional Thai, felt more Americanized and devoid of spice/flavor. We went on a weekday for lunch and asked for wide noodles, and got thin noodles. Asked for spicy and got what i would consider mild. I prefer the places in uptown or metaire if you want the traditional spicy flavor.

Situated in the small borough of Glenolden, Pennsylvania, just southwest of Philadelphia, Everything Jamaican seemed like an improbable fit in this community rife with crappy corner pizza shops and Chinese take-out. The tiny boroughs just outside of Philadelphia in Delaware County aren't much known for their "cuisine," in fact the nicest place in Glenolden I can think of may be a Ruby Tuesday (yikes!). As for all other cuisine, I have never seen so many roadside weenie huts and burger joints in my life. The day I noticed a new authentic Jamaican restaurant was opening on Glenolden Avenue, just down from the SEPTA R2 station, I was extremely skeptical. Not that the food would be good (okay, I did have my doubts about that too), but that such a niche restaurant could do well in such a town. I gave it a try today for lunch, and despite my poor experience with Jamaican food in the past (I ate at the Jerk Hut on South Broad and South street in Philly, and I thought the food was awful), I was very satisfied with Everything Jamaican. The lady behind the counter was very nice, and the food was fresh. I ordered the Jerk Chicken with the rice and peas, which also comes with a side of fried plantains. The rice was seasoned perfectly, full of flavor, and not too spicy. The chicken had a wonderful barbecue flavor, was tender as could be, and fell right off the bone. The portion was generous and the service was homey and welcoming. What a gem for Glenolden, I just hope it is able to catch on in the community, it would do people good to put down their slice of greasy, stale pizza, and treat their taste-buds to something new for a change.
Amazing place to hang out with your friends specially if you like to hear music and smoke hookah

As one of the only Ethiopian restaurants in Florida, Queen of Sheba is a must when in the area. We have eaten here over a dozen times and every time we leave happier than the time before. As with most Ethiopian restaurants, I recommend trying the large platters (to be shared within the group) as it gives everyone an opportunity to taste the variety of dishes. My favorite dish is their tibs but I've never had one I didn't like (even the lentils and I usually hate lentils) so I always hope to try something new. With a home made flavor and great service, I highly recommend Queen of Sheba!

Best Indian food in the neighborhood! My favorites are their Chicken Tikka Masala and their Saag Paneer. Their dinner entrees are a little pricier than I would like to see, but their lunch buffet is a great deal!

This is an authentic Korean restaurant that offers solid selections. Good tasting food. Decent size portions. We got seafood pancake, soon dobu and Jap Jae. They are all fairly standard and definitely above average Korean food. Appetizer small dishes are average. They also have all you can eat Korean BBQ. I will come back and give it a try.

I ordered a Saturday to-go lunch via the Yelp app. The place seemed nice during my minute inside picking up the food. For an appetizer I got the Gobi Manchurian. Deep fried cauliflower never disappoints. For my meal I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala with a spicy spice level. You can choose mild, medium, spicy, or very spicy. Unfortunately it was not spicy at all. I'd say a 1/5. For my wife, who cannot eat spicy food, I ordered the Chicken Biryani with spicy level mild. I found it delicious, but the spice level was about a 3/5 which was hot for her. It was upsetting she got the spice and didn't want it and I asked for the spice and didn't get it. Had the spice levels been correct, it would have been a fantastic lunch I'm sure. It was still ok overall, but they had to have got the order wrong. I

This place has the best Bombay street food around. It is reasonably priced and simple. The owner is a very sweet and friendly guy and will patiently explain the menu to those who do not know this type of food. I also love the fact that this place is all vegetarian.

Wow this place is great! The soup part of the pho is the best I've had, large generous portions. There is absolutely NO service, you don't even order from a person, so know what you're getting into here. Also, there's no hand holding, so I feel sorry for anyone attempting to navigate Vietnamese food for the first time. BUT, if you know what you're getting and you don't need a human cashier you are in luck. Beautiful spring rolls, tons of side garnish, and incredibly flavorful soup. I'll definitely be making this a regular lunch stop. I can't wait to try their Vietnamese Iced Coffee! --EDIT-- Tried the iced coffee: YUM!
Excellent falafel pita sandwiches. The fried potato is so good. The portions are big enough to share.

Finally, I found the best Indian restaurant in St Petersburg after coming here for a year on work trips. The ambiance is great, big wide​ open spaces, colorful lights, a bar area as well as outdoor seating. I'm from Hyderabad, the Deccan area, and the food is quite authentic and definitely has some spices to kick it. The service guys are nice and friendly and the food portions are good at a decent price.
Very good food, don't let the location fool you...this is authentic Thai cuisine, very well done...

I went to Flambo for lunch and i did not leave disappointed. Started off with the jerk chicken which fell off the bone and was delicious. I then ordered the stew chicken with some buss-up-shot on the side with rice and beans. Amazing flavor on all items. The owner was very gracious and gave us good insight into meals we had questions about. I would definitely come back here again and recommend it to anyone who has a taste for Caribbean food.

-Atmosphere- Crowded This is a really small place with room for about 30 patrons, so you definitely need a reservation. The place is just a little cramped and noisy, which I find to be a bit of an issue when in a place with low lighting and candles on the table. I was hoping for a bit more of an intimate setting as my Wife and I dined here on Valentine's Day. It didn't help either that we probably sat at the worst table in the place as we were right next to the entrance and with no foyer or waiting area every new customer that walked in stood and waiting pretty much right next to our table. I would definitely suggest you ask not be sat at that table. -Service- Excellent. Everyone was friendly and very knowledgeable of the menu. The entire wait staff works as one big team so even if your server is busy someone is always nearby to help out. Our drinks were never empty and our finished plates didn't sit around long at all. -Food- Phenomenal. This is some of the best food I've ever tasted. My wife and I started with the Antipasto Siciliano which was a variety of meats, cheeses and vegetables, all of which were full of flavor and tasted fresh. It was so good, I would recommend it to anyone. Next we shared the Rigatoni alla Disgraziata, a pasta dish with eggplant. Again fresh and full of flavor. For the main entrees, I went with the Bistecca Enna, which is a Ribeye served with an arugula and tomato salad. This was one of the best pieces of steak I have ever had and I have eaten at my fair share of top of the line steak houses. My wife went with the Coniglio Pizzaiola (the Rabbit), while she said she enjoyed the taste, she did not however enjoy all the little bones in the rabbit (but that's just how rabbit is). We finished our meal with the Gelati, which I have no complaints about, but after reading some of the other reviews I look forward to trying all their other desserts. -Value- Spot on. While it's a bit on the expensive side, I feel the price is just right for the quality of food you get. Plus it's BYOB so you're not paying for overpriced cocktails. -Overall- My wife and I will definitely be returning as this was some of the best food we ever tasted. The only knock I have on Zeppoli is how cramped it feels inside. The service is great, the food is delicious, and the price is just right. I would definitely recommend Zeppoli to anybody.
Coconut chicken always great. But whenever i order seasame. Its very soupy (liquidy) I like the thicker, sticky icky sauce!

Nicest patio in the area. Great drinks that are well poured, if you know what I mean. We had one appetizer while here and it was delicious. Like 5 star restaurant delicious. They also had a talented guitarist playing in the courtyard that was just right for the time of day, not to loud but loud enough. Go and enjoy.
Good little joint in this lovely neighborhood in Indi.. Spice level is appropriate for American standards ..

Third visit here. The first two were great! Third time was not a charm. The service was terrible. Three of us dining, and we all got our food at different times. (Like ten minutes apart.) When we asked why, they blew us off. I had the red curry and something was definitely off about it. The others liked their food, but service counts and it didn't exist.

Oh man...we've eaten here twice and both times it was amazing African food! I got the lamb BEWARE there are LOTS of bones. Pretty annoying but that's the normal. Next time will order something else but their flavor are insanely divine.

Very charmimg atmosphere. Staff very friendly and attentive. Food rich with flavor and good quality. Everything was very satisfying. -only thing is they need to get rid of the lap napkins. They look like raggedy dish rags and left lint all over our clothes.
The best afghani restaurant in Philly with afghani style and they have perfect foods & services and the staff is super friendly.

Love the Chaat items /Indian snack items available. The staff are very courteous and friendly, and super attentive. The vada-pav, dabeli and usual pav are exactly like the ones I've eaten in Mumbai and Pune, so definitely recommend the food. Other items to try: samosa Chaat, dhoklas, sevpuri.

We order pad thai with shrimp, papaya salad, green curry with chicken and Thai ice tea. Love papaya salad since it's sour and crunchy. Green curry is creamy and spicy. Pad thai and ice tea are okay. Highly recommend. We'll back again for sure. It's a family restaurant giving us fell like at home.

This place serves up good pho food. not great, but very good. the price is good and you get a lot of food! The restaurant is clean and the staff are usually very friendly. Just dont go there half an hour before closing. They say they will serve you, but 10 mins before closing time they started bleaching the whole place and we about died from the fumes and had to leave. Not too cool. Other than that its a good inexpensive place to grab a quick meal.

I was surprised at how nice Mirna's was. I was expecting another Jenkintown casual place, and though there is nothing wrong with that, Mirna's was much nicer. Service was excellent (almost too good, until more people showed up to distract the hordes of servers). Food was very good, and the portions were gigantic. BYOB.

Some pressed garlic bread was brought to the table to start. You can easily use this place for take out, but sit down service is available and friendly. I ordered yuca fries, that came with two zesty dipping sauces. For something less traditional- fries, cheese with bacon. This was as good as you might expect, as in, very very good. It also had a zesty sauce on it, making it a little more interesting; you can feel less bad for ordering fries at a Caribbean restaurant. If you order the papas rellenas, and you should because fried potato balls stuffed with meat are always awesome, make sure they remember to bring the rich, meat gravy. Ours came after we had mostly finished ours, and our last bites with the rich, meat sauce on it were most magnificent. We dabbled in to entrees; they come with your choice of rice and a small salad and plantains and are all under $12. The yellow rice and sweet plantains are both excellent. I was not great about sharing the plantains. The beef stew was flavorful, but a bit dry, though not to the point of making it unenjoyable. The roast pork was chopped in to glistening chunks. Some of the skin was a little too chewy to swallow, but the rest of the meat was shreds of soft, prime swine. While the pork was not quite as good as what they serve up North (as in, North Philly) or down South (as in, the islands of the Caribbean) it is a worthy stop that is much more accessible for Center City people. Great for lunch, or a BYO dinner, and if only they stayed open late... it would be most perfect for a weekend late night snack. Drunk pork is always a win.
Been there for lunch buffet. Very good number of items. Matches the price. Found a rare gem Rasmalai in buffet. Enjoyed the wide range of buffet. Quality should be improved, though!

Absolutely one of my favorite restaurants anywhere! It's byob which makes it great to start... they don't take reservations but you can put your name down and go over to the New Wave Cafe across the street and grab a drink and someone will come over and get you which is also awesome! The food is delicious and fairly priced. The grilled octopus is amazing! I'm one of those people who don't like my octopus real chewy and natural like some seafood lovers do so the grilled octopus here works great for me! The mussels in the white sauce are also amongst the best I've had anywhere. I'd probably say that Melograno does it better than they do but other than that, I can't really think of another place I've had better at in Philly. The Hummus here is great and also amongst the best I've had in Philly. The food is just really done well... nothing really fancy, just simple cooking that hits the spot!

Great food, great service and great price. I've been coming here for a while now and never bothered to write a review until now. My family ALWAYS gets the chicken tikkah masala, its that good, trust me. Their naan is also good however I have had better naan's before. Chicken 65 is good as well but the recipe is def. a bit different. Their chicken kabobs are on par with any kabobs you might have. Overall, this place is top notch and can go head to head with any other indo-pak food in the area.

My wife and I both had wonderful meals served by Kelly at the Pearl. Both means were superbly cooked and very delicious. Love the eclectic menu choices. If we ever return to Treasure Island, the Pearl will be on our to do list.

What a find! Not a fancy place, but boy the food is good- my favorites are the penang chicken and the red curry chicken. The veggies in the entre are always super fresh & crunchy. I try to get here at least once per week. Employees seem nice, and prices are reasonable ($10 for my entree with rice).
I must say, this place is delish. Have ordered via delivery services twice and it's been great! Can't wait to go in person :)

The best Indian food in the area, and I've tried them all. Great service although at peak times it does get busy so wait times increase, but no worries enjoy a cold Kingfisher Beer while you wait. My favorite dish is the chicken Kadai although everything I have tried has been excellent. Samosas pakoras Bhajis are all fantastic appetisers Don't forget a garlic Naan with your entree The spice levels are on the truly Indian style so start with mild. I typically get "Hot" at most Indian restaurants but the "Medium" suits me better here.
OMG so good !! Chicken pita meal is delicious !! So fulfilling and it doesn't make you feel bad about eating out haha . Definitely recommend (:

Indian food has been missing from Newtown for several years. It was worth the wait because now we have the best Indian food in Bucks County, located at the site of the former "Mamitas". Perfectly prepared dishes served by delightful staff that, like the chef/owner, are most eager to please. All the usual Indian standard dishes are here and many unusual ones as well. Prices are lower than the competition in Doylestown and Yardley. The level of spice can be personalized and should not deter anyone. There is something for everyone here. The wife and I plan to be back real soon and, likely, real often. It is BYOB! Buffet is available for lunch, with choices that vary from day-to-day.
I am so disappointed by the food that came. We spent a decent amount of money and received a terrible meal. I am sorely disappointed.

Food is definitely reasonably priced and pretty tasty. Glad it is only two blocks away from me. Check out their website. Did anybody else notice the pictures of the army guys that pops up for two seconds when you click on the homepage? Trippy and subliminal.
Nice little Thai place with some decent dishes. They have sushi on the menu, however it is never available when ever I go.

Best Mediterranean food in town (grouping Greek, Lebanese and Turkish together). My only complaint is that the baklava isn't very authentic. It seems like something from a package. The fig feta dip is unreal. And they (I think) make their pita bread in house! A very nice dining experience.
Pho king is always reliable. Broth of soup is the best. Owners friendly. Food is cheap but quality is there.
The lamb Karachi dish was good. Ambience is so-so. Service is excellent. It's pretty good for lunch buffet with more variety but since the food is rich plan on a siesta afterwards!

4.5 stars. I don't plan to give many 5 stars, so out of principle I am leaving this out as it is not favorite of the favorites - - but certainly a destination I would be excited to return to. The venue catered to our 14 person easy going albeit anal academically grad student party wonderfully. They did separate checks and did not add a mandatory gratuity - which in hindsight I realize may be one of only a few restaurants to do that. And the food! Delicious. I got the ribeye which was delicious. Subbed the rice pilaf for a side of spinach and really enjoyed the meal - cooked perfectly. I tasted the lamb kabob and it was delicious - for next time?! The flatbreads also looked delicious although I did not taste. Enough reading - anyone thinking about going should get the car started, pump up their tires, or put on their running shoes. Get there, sit down, relax, and enjoy!

We come here often and are usually completely satisfied; however, this time was different. My husband ordered the 14.95 volcano roll. Six small to average size pieces! Ridiculous for the price. Mentioned it to server and he was indifferent..... A little surprising since he knows we are regulars. Lost my faith and business for now! (I forgot to mention my sesame chicken was barely warm.)

I love this Indian restaurant! Their buffet is really good for a very good price: the curries, the side dishes and the tea is what I go for in this restaurant. The service is good too, and the people who work there are very friendly. I would definitely recommend anyone in Philly to try this place at least once.

My family and I eat hear at least once per week. It is probably our second favorite Asian restaurant. The food is always top flight, served quickly, hot, and delicious. We have never had a bad mealtime Fulins. As far as the service goes, the staff is always friendly and helpful. We have not once ever had to wait to be seated more than a couple of minutes. The staff and service are quick without any rushing. Fulins is a great place for a nice dinner and a movie night.

So happy that Tucson now has a Persian Restaurant! Bonus - It is Very good and has some of my favorite Persian dishes. 1.Location - Seems to be a strange location, Far NW Tucson (dare I say Marana), empty strip mall, across from Mt View High School and Crooked Tree Golf Course. But don't let that put you off it will surprise you walking inside 2. Decor - Gorgeous and very decadent and Fancy, but this is Tucson, so it is okay to be in shorts, but this is something I would expect to see in upscale resort in LA. Very Instagram worthy. 3. Service - Outstanding, we arrived on Sunday evening and Friendly greeted at the door and shown our table. Service was friendly and happy to help us with our choices. Very knowledgeable about menu and options. They did not linger over us, but made sure we were happy with our choices and checked on us off and on during the meal. promptly getting refills. As we left the restaurant, every thanked us for coming. 4. Cocktails Full bar and even has a Bar area, that was empty on Sunday evening. Drinks were strong and very good. Seems like it would be a good place to hang after a round of golf, if you wanted something more than the golf course bar 4. Food. They excel here. Lots of choices and as I mentioned many of my favorites. Many of the options are Gluten free. They did bring out a Warm Flat bread which was very tasty (Don't think that was Gluten free) We started with Tah Dig & Ghormeh Sabzy. It was the first time that I had those 2 combined, Generally we would have Tah Dig (Crusty, buttery Rice) alone almost like our Bread for the meal. Ghormeh Sabzy was as good as I have had in the past. Beef was very tender and the "gravy" was flavorful. We each had a entree, Koohidah, Lamb Shanks and Lamb Shish kebabs, which was way too much food and Rice for 3 people, Each dish is served with Basamati Rice (which you could ask for Half Rice and Half Salad, but we forgot to do that. Everything was very good and the lamb they said was very tender. We had a lot of food to take home and enjoy the next day 5. Price On par with most upscale restaurants you have in the Foothills. But well worth the price of what we got and the service. You could probably order fewer dishes and split with multiple people, I will come back and try out their Lunch menu. Hoping it is not as much food as the dinner menu, but who cares if it is good tasting. Hurray for Persian food in Tucson.
Excellent Persian food! So glad they opened a Tucson location. We have eaten here numerous times, and loved it each time. We will be back!

Great food and service and bar. My boyfriend and I went there today for his birthday. I like how it's decorated and the waiters and waitress are helpful. The food and the environment are both very Asian fusion, you can find the hint of Chinese but it incorporates with those modern and American elements so well. Our favorite dish is the appetizer tuna takaki, it's seared tuna but still raw in the middle, it's tender and fresh, definitely try it if you are a tuna person. And our fav entree is the hunan-style hot fish, it's not authentic but the sauce and the tenderness of fish really make it a great one. For desert, try the mandarin key lime bar, the sourness of fruit compliments the cheese so well and it's a great wrap up for the meal. Again, we like this place a lot. ^_^
I love it here. I've come twice on lunch work break. You get a lot of food for your money and always leave satisfied. So delicious.
Perfect late night falafel and hummus wrap! Nothing better after a long night out on Bourbon St. Not the most friendly staff, but it's still worth it for some solid Mediterranean food. Cash only!

Can't believe I didn't try this restaurant sooner! Beef tibs is hands down best of any Ethiopian I've had in MY, DC or Boston. And everything else was delicious too. Finally, restaurant managed by a very friendly, smart woman. Admirable, I can't wait to eat here again.

These guys are great!! If you're traveling though 30th Street Station, taking a break from class, or just visiting Drexel, they are the perfect lunch / dinner truck. Be aware that they open at 12 noon until around 6pm. There's usually a huge lunch crowd, which is pretty normal for any of the trucks. There's a lull from 2pm-4pm, so that's when I try to go. I like that they have a limited menu that they do very well. It's a great strategy - every dish is something interesting and tasty, and I haven't found one that I didn't like. Of course, if you ask, they will try and make whatever you want! And of course, say "yes" when they ask you if you want it spicy. Totally worth it!

I recently ate here with my wife and another couple. My wife and I split the Caprese Salad. The plum tomatoes were not ripe but the mozzarello was very good. I thought there was a little too much pesto on the mozzarello and tomatoes. The Farfalle con Salsiccia e Aglio was delicious, and the sausage was cooked to perfection. My wife had the Chicken Porccini which I didn't get a chance to taste but she was pleased with the dish and the portion. Our only complaint with Francisco's is the portion size - it's too small for what they charge. Regardless, because of the flavors and textures we will return. This is a BYOB.
Best Thai food you can find! I moved to Chicago years ago, but every time I come back to St.louis, I still have to make at least one stop here! Unpretentious and so legit.

I've visited this place several times, even grabbing carry out just to see if the quality was the same. Though I wasn't a fan of the carry out, Every time I've dined in, the service and quality of food was good. I've tried many things on their menu, not showing favoritism to any one entre, as everything I've tried has been great. Their prices are reasonable, the establishment is nice and clean, and the staff is always quite friendly. My visits have always been during down time, so I can't say what their service and quality is like during rush hour. The only reason I couldn't give them 5 stars? You have to go through the kitchen to get to the restroom. (weird, I know) If you're ever in the U-City Loop, I'd say give them a try.

On a Wednesday afternoon, one of my dearest hometown friends took me here instead of my usual pho go-to, Golden Flower. My goodness I was impressed as soon as I walked in the door! The atmosphere is very elegant- tastefully decorated with a high-class feel, something I expected would reflect in the pricing on the menu. It comes to no surprise I was shocked at how reasonable the dishes were priced- which prompted me to ask for a wine pairing along with my meal. The server was very pleasant, accommodating, and even provided recommendations on which wine would go best with my order. It was to my delightful surprise that the man serving me, was also the Chef! The woman who brought me my wine offered me the choice of something different should the wine not be to my satisfaction, which is always appreciated as not many establishments that serve alcohol are so quick to toss an order for sake of customer satisfaction. Then our appetizer arrived- and boy was it delicious! We ordered the calamari- which was served drizzled with a slightly spicy cream sauce over a bed of lettuce. The calamari was perfectly crispy, with just the right hint of spice on top. Honestly it's probably the best calamari I've ever had, and trust, I've had many a variation and it's a really hard dish to nail. Creazian does just that. When my pho arrived, it was hot, flavorful, and left enough for take-home! Overall my experience was lovely. There's a fountain in the middle that provides a pleasant ambience, a warmth about the place that feels very welcoming, not to mention the view of South Virginia. A first thought I had once (slightly drunkenly) venturing to the bathroom was, "boy I hope they rent this place out for private events because my parents' 50th would be perfectly hosted here!" I am thoroughly impressed by Creazian, and having moved to Bay Area, I've become very picky about my pho. Creazian has left such a good impression on me I'm afraid I can no longer eat anywhere else for pho in my hometown of Reno, Nevada. Having grown up here, that says something.
Every time we come here they are out of something. Then the food is cold. Employees seriously just standing around.

Excellent find. I had no idea this place exsisted because it is relatively hidden from the main road. The service is excellent! My glass was never empty and food arrived in a timely manner. Very polite and good recommendations. I have become a big fan of the walnut shrimp and the lo mein. Generous portions and skillfully plated. Flavors are seperate and distinct, not like everything was cooked in the same pot. They offer carryout, but you miss out on great service. I traded Panda Express for Chopstix even though the latter is a little more expensive. Well worth the extra cash. Don't hesitate. Very good.

I came here during a conference with some friends and the wait was sooo long.... this place is understaffed and for ~30 people there was one guy cooking, one women serving, and one dishwasher. So it took ~40 min to get seated, 1 hour to get our tea and food. One regular customer was really nice and helped seat people, take orders, and get water... the food was okay... most of the dishes were chinese and not really thai, but you have to adjust your menu for the people in the area so its not really surprising... Overall the food was okay, but not great Thai food, but I have high standards being Thai and all...

Sooooooo goood! I haven't had pho since moving to NOLA and this place hit the spot! The food was prepared quickly and the waitress really sweet and attentive. Cool, Hip, calming atmosphere, reasonable prices and the steak pho was the bomb!! Perfectly cooked with just the right amount of noodles. May have to visit once a week.
Great ambience, great food, but a bit too pricey. We were there late on a Weds night, and I wished it was a little quieter, hard to have a conversation with my sweetie.
A treasure among the chains of restaurants that make up green hills. Order whatever the special is and enjoy.

I went to this spot one night for a couple drinks and snacks one night. Loved it so much that I took my husband two nights later! The second time was wonderful. We had the croquettes again and they were just as delicious as the first time I had them. We also had the carrots, cauliflower, baked cheese, shakshouka, samosa, broccoli tabbouleh, chicken kabobs, sundae and chocolate cake. Everything was really good. I think next time I would pass on the shakshouka and samosa. Shakshouka was for sure my least fav. Service was great and drinks were as well!!

I am so sad to say that we are very disappointed with our meal. We ordered delivery. Pad Thai and Red Chicken Curry. The pad thai was flavorless, and the red curry was so thin and runny and again, not a lot of flavor. The Tom Kha soup decent. We were so disappointed that we threw it out and ordered from another place.

Never disappoints. I love the service here - attentive and they seem to remember their regulars. Pho is always a classic choice but the hot and sour soup, clay pot pork, beef stew are a few other great choices!!! Also must cap off your dinner with the corn coconut cream dessert! And the Vietnamese iced coffee! Basically, everything is great.

Franciscos almost always has a full room, mostly locals, amazing location/view and the food is good. Didn't get the name of our server, Spanish accent, covered a lot of tables...she's a real pro. Not her fault that food comes out slow. The table next to us suffered...had to take their entrees to go...maybe they were being punished for the dude wearing a tee shirt and a baseball hat in the dining room. Garlic bread was very good...not as good as Revere's across the river, but what is? Apps: mussels in red sauce was good, garlic, seasoned right, canned tomato chunks. Mediterranean salad was quite good, dressed perfect, avocado, olives, mozzarella, artichokes, etc. It was tiny for 12 $bones. The kid's lamb rack was reported as "above average"...and he is one of New Hope's most renowned lamb connoisseurs. Wife's spinach ravioli was standard fare. My butterfish was a bit dry with overdone pistachio crust...had about half a teaspoon of pan sauce on the plate. The sautéed spinach and smashed potatoes that came with it were woefully under seasoned.

We are vegan and just love this place. Food is delicious. Vegetarians and omnivores alike will enjoy this restaurant. No alcohol is available however they welcome BYOB and there is no corkage fee. (Great selection of wine in liquor store below the restaurant. ) Free live jazz every Thursday in the indoor courtyard. We will be back regularly.
Awesome, this place does Not disappoint they know Exactly what they are doing and they do it Very well Food is superb decor is warm, if you love Indian cuisine this is the spot!!

I went here for lunch. The lunch menus is very tricky. It isn't explained what come with and if added chicken and seafoods, the price is same as regular menu. I ordered a Kao Soi Noodles but unfortunately it's not spicy and noodle was too boiled and absorbed with curry soup. I tasted this meal around world including Thailand, Singapore, Tokyo, Vietnam, HK and some in USA. Looks fancy but the taste is 2 stars :p

This place is great for casual lunches, for which they have special pricing, even on weekends. The ambiance is cute and cozy, the food is tasty and affordable. And we never had a problem with service, though perhaps it is only because we come during off-peak hours.
Food was fine, ample, and a good value in every way. The dining room is musty. Service was good. Disappointed by the use of canned mushrooms and dried thai bird chilies in my soup.
Friendly staff and quick service. The crispy spring rolls and pad see ew were tasty and perfectly spiced. Large space makes it great for groups. Tasty grub makes it great for carry out!
Very Decent food... Fast and speedy. Very Tasty Deff one of my favourites
Mac n cheese was burned. Disappointed! ;-(

This was my first visit here since I was in the area. The place is on the smaller side but there are a lot of tables. I will say that it was pretty chilly in there....but maybe I'm getting old. We started off with the summer rolls and the shrimp rolls ....which are both the same only one has a TINY bit of shrimp. They were pretty good but VERY sticky. I ordered the Tom kha goong - ( coconut milk, lime, button mushrooms, chili paste, chicken soup) only they were out of mushrooms so it was mostly just a very yummy, creamy broth with chicken. My friends got the Pad Thai which I tried and it was really good.....and a large amount. I took home the Cashew Nut ( sautéed with cashews , bell peppers veggies, mushrooms and chili paste) for hubby and he really enjoyed it.

Honestly, this restaurant needs an update to it. It is very 80's in decoration and food preparations. The sauces are very heavy and are poured over the dishes. The service is excellent. My mom likes to come here so we brought her for dinner. The best thing off the menu is the fried cheese, one of the BEST dishes I have ever have. We shared it, I'm going back for my own portion. Each bite was magical in taste, indescribable how good it was. I had a fresh fish, it was good not great. The baklava was very good, almost as good as what I make. We have since been back a few times. The service is excellent. My favorite dish, which is an appetizer, is there stuffed baby red peppers. The cheese is also from their cheese appetizer with 2 more cheeses are added. This dish is delicious. The restaurant is not as dark looking so they have made improvements. I just order sauces on the side now. I wanted to also comment on some visits. The lamb chops or might be called rack of lamb is excellent. I'd still order your sauce on the side for any dishes.

ditto on what alexis d. said. I really think this is one of the better Thai places in St. Louis. Update April 2008 - Just ate here during our college reunion. My palate and experience with thai food must have expanded a bit, because it was not nearly as good as I remember. I guess for a thai place in the Lou, though, it was still very good.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Visiting St. Louis on a business trip, and was glad to found this little gem. Excellent Pakistani food! the buffet was top notch! Owner is a nice person too.

So I went to Dosa Hut today. If your expecting some pretty little restaurant this is not your place. This is a small little dive hidden behind a Subways which is hidden behind an auto parts store.. but this dive's food is fantastic. I had the Lamb Sukka, and some Garlic Naan. It was extremely flavorful and absolutely worth the wait. I went with a group of friends from work and all left happy. I will say they are a bit slow, but to me it is the type of place you go when you want something different. It makes its merits on the food. So if you have time and want some great tasting food this is your place. If you want pretty napkins and table cloths I would look elsewhere.

Loved loved LOVED it! The staff was welcoming and kind, offering recommendations and instructions on how to eat the food. The dinner (lamb with collard greens and a spicy chicken- wett, I believe) was amazingly delicious. My companion and I barely spoke as we wolfed down the entire platter. I have told all my friends about this place and you should too! In fact, we're gathering a group to return next week!

Moved into the neighborhood and was excited to have some pho nearby. Nope. Dirty, poor service, and the pho was bland and the meat was almost inedible. I feel sorry for the fish in the dirty fish tank.

I dont eat indian food very often, so i dont have much to compare to, but that being said this food was just good in general! I was craving something warm and ethnic, needed something spicy so i yelped restaurants around where we live in U City and came across Spice-n-Grill. It had very good reviews and i trust other yelpers even if the restaurant is in a tiny strip mall! Dont let the appearance fool you, its a great mom and pop shop, i felt like i was coming into their house for dinner. We ordered it togo and i could see them in the kitchen making the food while we were there. I had the Chicken Tikka Masala (again i dont each indian much so i stuck to something i knew) and my boyfriend had their specialty Beef Nihari. The seasoning was great just enough spice and lots of flavor. The chicken and beef were large pieces, tender and fresh, it was good quality not just small random pieces of meat. Sometimes i have found the tikka masala has a lot of spice but no flavor but this has both, it was awesome. It really hit the spot on a cold fall night! We also had the veggie samosas and naan which were traditional and yummy, again both fresh and cooked in front of us. We will definitely be back when we need a spicy warm meal.

I have visited Jasmine Thai on two occasions, ordering Beef thai fried rice, Red curry with Beef, and Hot pepper basil chicken. This saga is about the BEEF thai fried rice and BEEF red curry experience. The journey to Jasmine Thai began on a sunny Tampa afternoon where clouds cease to exist. A thai restaurant next to an Aldis had caught my Wife and I's eyes, and we were destined to test the cuisine. We entered the restaurant and laid our eyes upon a beautiful interior set-up and a table that tells about the Tale of Thailand. All was well and calm as the waitress came to take our order. The waitress was a nice and pleasant person who wrote down our order of beef thai fried rice and beef red curry. The world around us was beautiful and calm, but it did not prepare us for what we would encounter next! Our food arrived in a timely fashion. The colors and aroma of the food appealed greatly to our senses. We could not wait to taste the food and then.... We took our first bite of the beef from the beef fried rice... Then we took a bite of the beef from the curry... I realized that we lost the battle for middle-earth. We gagged from tasting the beef both times and realized the truth about Jasmine Thai's beef. It was spoiled beef. In fact, it was so spoiled, it seemed to have thoughts and a life of its own as it stared into our souls. The world around us changed with the onset of the spoiled beef taste. It was as if the beautiful atmosphere turned into a field suffering from the barrage of Lighting arrows and Firewalls. Our HP drained to 0, and so we paid and left without making the issue known. We already knew that they know about the beef; spoiled beef is not hard to detect and we were utterly defeated and left quietly. The second time around, we ordered chicken and it was ok, but we will never forget the beef.
Great atmosphere for enjoying cocktails. I didn't have dinner there, but I'd certainly return for drinks and appetizers. The dinner menu seems a bit pricey.
Always a good meal at PF Changs! Went in for a quick bite/cocktail. The pan fried shrimp dumplings and chicken lettuce wraps were really good! Great ambiance as well.

I bought a Groupon for this establishment and called in my order for take-out. The lady on the phone said the Groupon was for dine-in only (she was very polite) I asked to speak with the manager. He was very rude and said that it was in fact dine-in only. I told him that I had read all the details and fine print and that was never mentioned. He would still not allow me to make a take-out order so I just took my business elsewhere. The manager was very rude and I would never recommend this place to ANYONE!

My parents are from Kerala and my whole family loves dosa, my kids especially. We'd circled the place a few times but were hesitant to go in. The recent review by the Tennesean made us drop everything and head there for dinner tonight. As we seated ourselves in a corner booth, I saw movement along the wall and was quickly repulsed by a clutch of at least 12 roaches scampering around. We told the server who waved us into an interior room littered with dead roaches under the tables. I honestly couldn't believe my eyes because people were eating there and I didn't understand how they didn't notice. If the dining area was this neglected, I can't imagine the kitchen. We love divey places but expect them to be sanitary. Sorely disappointed - wanted this place to be our new favorite

I have had great food and service here in the past. Today, being Labor Day, I was expecting a brunch Menu. I was surprised to have no Brunch. We were going to just have a drink and find a brunch spot. The waitress was rude when we asked about Labor Day specials, poured one glass of water and walked off. The best part was she proceeded from our booth to go talk about us asking about Brunch on a Monday with the bar help! I could here the conversation and their mocking us. So no drink just up and left off to Kid Shelleen's they understood it's a Brunch Holiday served brunch had water for two and a full brunch menu.... also Labor Day specials .

Updated Review: I'm bumping up the stars for this review as I've had a chance to eat here a second time and this experience was great! I ordered the Pad Thai and Red Curry, both with shrimp and spice level 3. The Pad Thai was delicious and carried a really good heat. I've never had curry before, but it's not bad. Not my favorite as it's too sweet for me. I will provide another update when I have a chance to try the hibachi, and retry the Pho.
Amazing decor and music. Ginger chai was great. The food, however, is below par and quantity or taste does not reflect the price.

I didn't exactly care for this place...we went around brunch one weekend. There was no wait and everyone was friendly, but the place was infested with houseflies. Plus, the actual food was not very delicious. Although there was plenty on the menu i was excited about, the way a simple soup and sandwich was executed, I don't think it's worth going back. And the food made me a little nauseous afterward. Definitely a no-go...which is unfortunate. I really wanted to like it here, as it came highly recommended.

I had the Thai rice noodle soup with beef and meatballs. It was very good. It is a necessity to add the jalapeno vinegar to the soup. I was introduced to homemade Guay Tiew and have been looking for an authentic place ever since. It is hard to find in Thai restaurants. This wasn't exactly what I had but it was still good and full of flavor. Good prices, very friendly service and good food.
I have only had a breakfast sandwich from Bui's and frankly, I am not impressed. The sausage, egg and cheese is way better at Hemo's.

Went to this Restaurant for the first time for dinner the other night with friends and I was impressed!! The decor is beautiful even down to the wood carvings on the tables! The staff were dressed culturally and looked amazing! We were seated immediately and waited on promptly. I ordered Combination Fried Rice which was fried rice with chicken, shrimp, beef, and pork. Food was delicious and portion was enought to fill me up and take some home for another meal the next day! Prices were very reasonable! I think my dish was $11.95, can't beat it! The staff even brought everyone at our table individual checks without even having to be asked! Great food, great service, and great atmosphere will definitly bring me back to this restaurant!

​When my friend and I walked into the local Ethiopian restaurant in town, Zagol, we found that the restaurant was empty. We were greeted by a friendly woman, which we then noticed that she may have been the only worker there for the night. All around the room the restaurant displayed cultural art from Ethiopia. There was a large area in the corner they dedicated to showcase tradition Ethiopian culture. When we sat down the first thing I noticed besides the nice table setting was a sheet of paper that taught their guests some facts about Ethiopia. ​The menu that the waitress provided was listed in two pages, and predominantly divided into three sections-beef dishes, lamb dishes, and vegetarian. My friend and I opted for the vegetarian combination plate which came with three different types of vegetarian dishes.
