While we waited for the food to come out, I noticed that they played a lot of music videos from their native country, and the aroma around the room smelled like spices that were not familiar to my senses. ​When the food arrived, it was not really what I expected, because the consistency seemed mushy, and I expected food that would have some sort of shape. What threw me off was the Injera, the bread that held the food and served on the side. It had a very strong sour taste, which was something I was not used to. Overall the taste of the food was sort of bland to me, or just foreign to me. I can definitely say that I have not tasted dishes like these in my life. ​Since walking in I could tell from my short experience that they take pride in their heritage and culture from the display of all the artwork around the restaurant. I could tell from the slip of paper containing Ethiopian facts that they wanted us to learn some things and explain about their culture since Ethiopian culture is not as strong in Reno compared to other places. I noticed that the entire place, including all the lights and even the display candle holders on the tables were warm toned colors. I interpreted this to either be just the design scheme they went with, or related to their culture in some way. I looked up the nation's flag, and the colors around the room actually went along with the flag's green, yellow, and red colors. I also observed that there was only one worker for the night, working the front as well as in the kitchen, so I can see that they are probably very hard working in their culture, or prefer to not hire helpers. I too can relate to this, because my parents own a restaurant in town, and currently it is just my parents operating the restaurant. I did some prior research and I was also interested in the reason why they close their restaurant midday, between 3pm and 5pm. Maybe it's related to their culture and it is a period of time where they don't eat, or it could possibly be related to religion. Overall what I drew from my experience is that they are rich in culture and tradition, and they take pride in it as well. ​As for the food, I concluded that it was not a typical dish that I have ever had. I can tell that Ethiopia is probably rich in beans and grain. The majority of our meal was the Ethiopian bread they served, Injera, which is made from teff flour and gluten free. This bread tasted very foreign to me, because it had a tart taste. The rest of the food was bland to me, but I could taste some spices that were foreign to me as well. I could tell that they eat a lot of beans and veggies, and they have a special type of Ethiopian coffee that was well advertised. Overall this was a good experience due to the hospitality of the people and the rich culture they displayed, however the food is probably just not for me

This place has the best f-ing Vietnamese hoagies in all of philly. I am Vietnamese and tried all those places, Cafe Cuong, Ba le, Q, all those place on Adams. No bueno. Nhu Y does it right. Light, crispy bread, the right amount of filling. Amazing. I love their vegetarian hoagies.

First time we tried Rosemary's and we really enjoyed it. As my wife said "its a keeper". We went there for the Turkish menu and we weren't disappointed. Mediterranean food is hard to find in Lower Bucks so we really enjoyed it. As we were leaving we noticed someone carrying a bottle of wine as they arrived and the management told us that we were welcome to bring our wine. And we will as we plan to return.
Excellent food and very good service. My wife and I have the no. 1 meat combo platter. Everything on it was very tasty and had a nice balance. Well seasoned but not overly spicy. Will come back.

We ate here yesterday for brunch. I've been before, but today just really hit the spot. First, the restaurant is so cozy on a cold day and they also have outdoor seating on a nice day. Next,The coffee was on point. It was Irish potato flavored, which was cinnamon and sweet but without sugar or cream. I am so glad our server talked us into getting it. The food was just overall awesome! I had a quiche that was so delicious! It came with soup and a Cesar salad. Both of these were fantastic too. My husband loved his potato and chive omelet and my girls loved the Mac and cheese. We promised each other to come back sooner rather than later!

I don't even want to write a review of this place, because I'm scared it will be invaded, but it is the best secret in PHL. Best roti canai of my life, excellent tom yum, perfect spice on the noodle dishes. Everything is prepared with care.

After passing by the ZK numerous times and having heard great things he about it, I finally had an opportunity to have lunch at the Collegeville, PA location. I had the lamb pita sandwich with a side of rice and I'm afraid to say, it was edible, but forgettable. The service was first rate. Store was clean and atmosphere -all quite agreeable. However, I didn't go there to socialize or inspect the place. I went there to eat a hot meal, people. The ground lamb was luke warm, the rice was luke warm, portions were frugal. The pita wasn't warm or fresh and I was, sorry to say... unimpressed. Will I give it a second chance? Probably not. I really like the mom and pop type Gyro places where they carve the meat like shawarma from a hot spit and serve it on warm, fresh pita bread with a heaping side of rice side and veggies. This was definitely not that.

THE BEST PHO IN TAMPA BAY!!!! Extremely affordable, extremely delish, and man you get your moneys worth!!! I love the Vietnamese Ice Coffee, with the the fresh rolls too. The only place here in Tampa I will go since The Bamboo Flute closed.

Food is good, standard Thai. However the service was a huge bummer, even on a non busy night. No customer service skills. They don't notify you when your to go order is ready despite sitting right there in the restaurant. Also didn't give us any silverware or napkins for out to go order. Overall just didn't come across friendly. Will pick a different Thai restaurant in the area next time just to try for better customer service.

Ordered lunch for delivery today. Must have repeated myself three times. I ordered a pint of shrimp fried rice and a lunch special with a Pepsi. We asked that the lunch special get beef fried rice instead of pork fried rice. When the receptionist repeated the order, she left out the shrimp fried rice. I repeated the order again. When it arrived it was wrong. There was no shrimp fried rice; instead it was pork fried rice. Called back to have them fix it and still had to repeat myself three times. Allegedly it will take another 30 minutes to get my lunch. She originally offered to have the shrimp fried rice free for next time. I asked what I was supposed to have for lunch today then. Awful, simply awful, way to conduct business. If you don't understand the language, get someone who does. Will not be ordering from there again.
Love this Thai spot, I always get the papaya salad extra spicy. The staff is always friendly. They are very busy during lunch/dinner time so keep that in mind.
Great location, very nice staff... Very limited menu and the one thing the irks me the most is they nickel and dime you to no end. Compared with other places, they are just ok, not great.

Everything about this spot is genius... The people, the staff, the owners, the drinks, the food.... No mistakes were made! I am a true fan.... I will be here often!!! Thanks Tryst for a fabulous spot in Dtsp!!! You have elevated Beach Drive:-)

I went here with a groupon. the banh mi was decent but not great. the pho was pretty bad. it was salty and not very flavorful. they provided no thai basil with the pho. the vietnamese springroll was sticky and bland. FYI, the bathroom is on the other side of the stripmall.

Dropped by while looking for a new go to place for pho. Their pho was tasty, I wanted to try something else but their menu is confusing and the person attending me behind the counter was too busy to tend to my questions. Would I return? Sure.. but not on the regular. Food: 4/5 Location: 4/5 Service: 2/5

Avalon has made a smooth transition from BYOB on S. High St. to a full service bar and restaurant on main drag of the Boro. Been there a number of times, we always eat at the bar. Bryce is very friendly, excellent happy hour, reasonable prices, outstanding entertainment and food.

I love the Panang Curry with Basa fish. All of their dishes are very good. The ambiance is relaxing. You don't hear a noisy kitchen as you eat. You can carry on a conversation without straining to hear. The servers have on traditional dress and are lovely. They have a section that has a bar and can be used for special occasions.

Food was average - which may deserve a rating 3 out of 5, but bad service. I ordered a pho with 2 types of meat and tripe.(pho #2 ) I started eating the food, and I realized there was no tripe. I asked the waiter why there was no tripe in my food, (I specifically ordered the pho with tripe). He then talked to someone in the kitchen and told me they are out of tripe. That's it as if I am just supposed to accept what they gave me. They didn't bother to tell me when I ordered the dish, didn't bother to apologize, didn't give me any discount. I didn't make a scene out of this because I was with my wife, but I at least had to give the lowest rating here. If you go to this place, you better ask all the ingredients are available for your dish because they won't tell you even if they don't have it. Visited November 2016
OMG! What a find! I looooved the food here. Reminded me of the food back home. The spices were spot on! Great variety!!

Not good. I would make more authentic Thai food at home and I have no knowledge/experience in doing so. I ordered my Pad Kee Mao very spicy and they straight up dumped crushed red pepper on the center on it. Like half a normal sized bottle of crushed red pepper! Also, they used frozen vegetables which results in a mushy, non-restaurant quality texture. Sadly, S. Grand does not have a good Thai place to add to its mecca.

Not so great. The inside atmosphere is less nice than the outside suggests, tables and chairs were sticky and beat up. My meal (shrimp with lobster sauce lunch) was tasty but lukewarm. The place was really understaffed, we had to eat our whole meal without drinks as it took close to ten minutes to get a refill. Our waitress was nice and we felt bad she had so little help! Overall this experience was underwhelming and we won't come again.

Love this place. Hands down the best Indian take away that I've had in the area. I really like that they offer a scale of spice unlike other places. The gentleman who rang up my order was really nice and when I went to grab a take away menu for later, he stopped me so that he could give me one with coupons. Its about a ~20-30 min roundtrip drive to pick it up, but totally worth it. Eating in is also an options and nice - BYOB.

Pad see ew was ok but lacking in spice. Tom kha was extremely bland- just tasted like coconut milk. Beyond that, it was expensive for what you get! Service was great and the guy was really friendly, and atmosphere seemed nice though we got takeout.
The best food! The lobster & garlic noodles out of this world! Poke tacos! Great price for amazing food!

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in the Tampa Bay Area!!!! It's is delicious! I recently moved to Brandon and I have busted this place 6 times already... That's how good it is!!! It's a small restaurant maybe 65 seating, the service is great and the food is very fresh and tasty! They have great sushi variety which I always enjoy and their Thai curries are made to perfection!!! Definitely worth a visit!!!!

This is the second time that I have eaten here. I loved it both times. Their food is delicious, and I like the fact that the menu isn't overloaded with an abundance of dishes. This makes it easier to order if one is not familiar with Indian food. Everything from the appetizers to the desserts are all well prepared and seasoned perfectly. The only reason for my three star rating is because the service is lacking. Don't get me wrong, the owners and their staff are extremely nice people and friendly, but they have no sense of urgency. I was seated for a bit of time before anyone came over. They also need to do a better job checking in on their guests to see if refills are needed, etc. And I do think the prices are decent. Not too expensive at all for the quality of food that you receive. Overall, I would go back. Service is always something that can be corrected.

Missing some great puertorrican food while in Tampa I've heard good things about this place and wasn't a disappointment! Started with the jueyes empanadas and yumminess! Then, my favorite mofongo stuffed with carrucho and pulpo. They served it as a salad which I preferred in a red salsa but the mixed octopus and carrucho salad was delicious. Perfectly cooked, food arrived fast, decent portions and service was excellent! Five Stars, my favorite puertorrican place in Tampa!!!

This was my first experience with Caribbean/Jamaican cuisine and I can't wait to go back! It was one of the most delicious culinary experiences I've ever had. Everything tasted like a home cooked meal it just had that certain something to every dish that really made it stand out. The service was fabulous and the restaurant is beautiful. I really felt like it was a gem of a find and I can't wait to go back! We had the goat curry and jerk chicken with Mac and cheese and the corn bread everything was incredible! The plantains were also the best I've ever had! So happy to find this place.

I ordered takeout from here tonight (Sunday) and thought it was only okay. I opted for the pho ga (chicken) in the small size since I was not super hungry. It turned out to be the right amount of food, but had I been hungrier, I certainly would have wanted to size up or add on an appetizer. The pho was a 6/10. I've never before thought that any Asian soup needed more noodles, but I did find myself thinking that when I somehow had at least a third of the broth remaining but no more noodles or chicken. Although I found the chicken portion generous, it was very dry and I therefore wasn't crazy about it. The broth was fine but nothing special. The toppings, which were fresh and flavorful, were probably my favorite part of the dish. Regarding mechanics, I found online ordering easy and convenient. I was given a pickup time estimate that was about 20-30 mins after I placed the order, and then I received notice via the order tracker that it became ready for pickup about 5 mins earlier than the 20 min estimate (i.e., approximately 15 mins after I placed the order). The food was packaged up tightly, so it would've been hard to make a mess out of it, even with a bit of a distance to travel. This packaging also helped keep the broth warm, though I imagine it would've needed a tiny reheat had it been a cooler evening. Given this neighborhood's relative proximity to a couple excellent Vietnamese places in Chinatown, I probably wouldn't choose iPho as a destination. That notwithstanding, it's nice to have an easy takeout option right down the street that's a step up from greasy Chinese or pizza.
Will work in a pinch, but not my first choice when I want Thai, which is often. Mostly run of the mill. Pad Thai is too sweet in sticky sauce.

Delicious food served with kindness in a pleasant atmosphere. The flavors are expert. Wonderful chat and malai kofta. My son had a curry with a mango-tomato sauce - sounded awful to me but it was fabulous. Don't miss the masala tea.

Picked this restaurant using a "Local Restaurant" Yelp search. Reviews were pretty good so we gave it a try. Our experience was similar to what was shared in each review; the food was good, menu selection good, service GREAT. BTW...their fountain cokes are up there with the best ever- perfect mix of coke syrup and soda water!!!

Excellent customer service and excellent taste of Indian food, specially South Indian. My husband and I love that restaurant and anytime we are in Indy, we will definitely find ourselves going there. Being a South Indian restaurant, they make THE best Paneer Tikka Masala. No one can beat them. Overall, great place !

We has the lunch buffet and the food was great! Plenty of different dishes. Want to do there for dinner and would definitely recommend this place. We did wish the food was a little spicier but it was a buffet.

This is absolutely my favorite place to eat in Nashville. In fact, I've only ever ordered one thing - the falafel pita, which is pretty much heaven. It's a great little place; the staff have a good sense of humor and like to joke around, and the food is quick, fresh, cheap, and very good. Also, if you come on Saturday night you can listen to live music. Always a fun time!

At last, a Thai restaurant that actually believes me when I ask for my meal, "Thai hot" That is a rare occasion in the Tampa Bay area! What a neat little place this is! Staffed by Owner Bualin (Lynn) and I am guessing her daughter, the feeling is quite welcoming, and the service is swift and attentive. Today I had the Panang Curry for lunch, and I don't believe a left a single morsel of food on my plate. It was just that good! Now I am going to have to find more reasons to be in the Brandon area at mealtime, so I can work my way through the entire menu! Look for me there again and again. If you don't see me, give my warm regards to Lynn!

The main reason I won't go back here again is because of one reason - they served everything on disposable tableware. Plastic forks, spoons, styrafoam plates and plastic cups. I am not a big fan of any place, for any reason, that serves food suchly. The Perch in Brentwood was one other place. Barring that, the food was good, but not great. I had the spinach pie and I don't know if it's the spinach or the recipe, it was bland. I also had the filafel pita pocket and left unimpressed.

Don't be put off by the entrance to this delightful restaurant. The food is excellent and the staff helpful and friendly. We shared the fresh spring roll which was perfect for two, a Thai salad, the Pad Thai and the 3-Flavored Shrimp, all of which were excellent. The food came out before we were finished with the salad which was a little annoying but other than that I would say it was a wonderfully satisfying dining experience that was reasonably priced They should have a separate entrance to the dining room so diners don't have to go past the take out area.

The best Vietnamese restaurant in the area, eaten here since they opened a few years back. The crispy spring rolls are a must try and everything on the menu is delicious :) The staff is great and the service is amazing.

Horrible service last night. Osama Bin Laden was easier to find than our waiter. After being seated and waiting for 10,minutes with no waiter in sight,, I went to the bar to order a round of drinks for the four of us. Five minutes after that... the mystery waiter showed up. He must be "Wanted" somewhere as he never told us his name. We ordered entrees right away, not taking a chance of not seeing him for another 15 minutes. Well sure enough, another period of time passed, we had finished our drinks and no sign of Osama, I mean our nameless waiter. So once again I got up from our table and order another round of drinks for the table. Once they arrived, so did the waiter with salads. Nothing special about the spinach or wedge salads, standard fare you can get at franchise restaurants . Finally the entrées arrived and nothing special to talk about here either. Pork chops were greasy, eggplant with onions and a pasta Steak entree that was bland. No one at our table finished their entrée. After the poor service, I would have thought at least one round of drinks would have been comped or perhaps a dessert, since I did the majority of the waiting on our table, but other than an apology from the bartender for lack of service.. Nothing.. Needless to say we won't return.

i got 2 appetizers and 2 entrees. i paid $40. for chinese food carry-out. i thought "well it must be amazing...." so i gave it a try. yes, the food was good but the portions were so small! usually when i've gotten chinese food, I have left overs for lunch. not here. there was barely enough as a dinner entree. it was too little for that much money.
Was in town from the Pittsburgh area and looked this Restaurant up on Yelp. Reviews were good so I tried it. Was not disappointed. Peanut Chicken was great. Would go back in a heartbeat.

This five star rating is for the only dish I have ever eaten here: the salted caramel fish hot pot. It is truly phenomenal. I just never try anything else on the menu because if it ain't broke, don't fix it. I find the downtown location better than the Whyte Ave location.

With so many Thai places in SB, it's nice that Meun Fan is conveniently located in Goleta at Calle Real! So happy that there are more Asian food options popping up in the area. My friend and I started off with drinks. She got regular Thai tea, and I decided to try the Thai green tea. Thought this was unique because I normally don't see this option anywhere else. It was good, but nothing too special. However, the crab cheese wontons were SO good. Super crispy and fresh!! Could probably eat the whole plate by myself if I didn't have self control. The curry, fried rice, and pad see ew were all really good as well! Not the best I've ever had but definitely still quality. We came during a lunch rush but still got all our food out pretty fast. If you're craving Thai food and don't want to drive out all the way to SB, you should give this place a try!

This was our first time at a Noodles and company- and we loved the concept and the food! However the service here was terrible. It was the end of the night, so I understand that workers are tired, but they were hours away from closing time. The workers were rude, and annoyed that I had never been there before when I admitted this and asked for help with the menu. The two ladies that served me were really rude. There was one manager there that showed us kindness when he noticed this. They were 100% out of all soft drinks. They refused to let us use real silverware (which was sitting clean behind them on the counter) they were out of several types of noodles, they were out of potstickers, and the bathrooms were completely our of toilet paper - paper towels, and very dirty. I was not impressed and will be seeking other locations next time I'm craving some noodles.

Good Indian food in East Philly? What? Yeahh, its true. This restaurant is right behind a motel (America's best something), so don't blink or you'll miss out. I went with a Desi (Indian-American) friend who said this place was great -which it was. It's a big place, very well decorated, with dimly lit lights and indian music in the background. The service is very good, waiters very friendly. Since my friend recommeded the place and i'm sure had a lot more experience with indian food than i did - i let him order. We had: Masala Paneer (Cheese in Tomato sauce) - The sauce on this platter was awesome... I'm not a big cheese eater but this plate was soo flavorful. He ordered the spicy which I was like - SPicy? What does spicy mean - because my level of spice tolerance and indian level are very different. It actually was a tolerable spicy though. Aloo Gobi (Potatoes and Cauliflower) - Another great amazing dish - the sauce was incredible - the plate all together was very flavorful.. Garlic Naan - Mmm.. Also, this was my first time drinking King Fisher beer (lager). It was really good and ice cold! These two dishes, naan and rice were more than enough food for two people. Definitely recommended if your in the area or not. FYI - It's not cheap - it came out to like $50 for two people.

I love pho, yes I do. But iLuv Pho does not meet expectations. There is something odd about the way the space is designed -- when my partner and I went into the place, we were the only customers in the joint -- the register counter was situated in the corner in a weirdly Orwellian way such that we did not feel free to converse because of the employees looming there. The dudebro at the counter was friendly but not knowledgeable about the content or the preparation of the dishes and the pho broth was bland and greasy and the meat was sparse. The only thing iLuv Pho really has going for it are the cheap prices that compete with prices for pho in LA, but dude, we're in the desert and I'm okay with paying a little more for you to make pho the right way + shipping.

I came here for lunch with co-workers. Wasn't my choice. I was thinking "how bad can it really be?" The answer to that thought...really really bad. We started with wonton soup, which you can probably find in any american chinese restaurant anywhere. I had their singapore noodle. It did not have the right kind of noodle. It didn't have curry flavor. Everything was very far off from what I know this dish should taste like. It's like the chef never had this dish from an actual Chinese restaurant. So I immediately try to forget my association with this dish and try to judge the dish on its own. The flavor it did have was single profile. It felt like they mixed ginger, soy sauce and suger and poured it over. The noodles didn't have any bounce to it and broke too easily as I was picking them up. Also among the food we ordered there was some chicken dish that resembled Wendy's asian chicken. It probably was my mistake that I came here. I would never come back to P.F.Chang's ever again. I would gladly order americanize chinese food anywhere in any suburb than come here. Maybe I will go to Wendy's and get their chicken dish before even dreaming of coming here.

Being in the area for St. Vincent Carmel Hospital, this was a quick drive to satisfy my Indian food craving. The Indian Masala Tea was hot and good. The Chicken Curry was delicious and had just the right amount of spice. I upgraded to the Kashmiri Naan to offset the heat and to satisfy my sweet tooth at the end of the meal. A perfect dinner for me!

$35 including tip for 2 appetizers and 2 entrees so price wise pretty good. Appetizers: the fried shrimp was awful! The veggie spring rolls were yummy. The broken rice with pork chops was yummy! Loved the pork! The vermicelli with grilled chicken was alright.. the spring roll (it wasn't the veg one but not sure what it was made of) was really yummy!!! Overall, decent food!

Totally different mix of people. Average age looks in there mid-30's to early 40's and it's a Thursday evening close to 7p with temps at a scorching 63 degrees [lol!-]. The vibe is very chilled amongst the chatter of multiple conversations, slightly heavy bass from the sound system playing Hall & Oats - Maneater :-) and the excessive clinking from the kitchen. [I'm sitting at the furthest end of the bar.] Ordered 2 Spring Rolls that were tasteless. You need the sauces they offer. Bartenders are friendly. It's been at least two years since I've been here and this place STILL has not grown on me. :-( Stop in and form your own opinion. Enjoy!

Called to order lunch for delivery; I'm staying in town without a car. At first, they said delivery orders had to be $25 or more. Then called me right back to say they'd make an exception. Delivered my food quickly afterward. Awesome service. Delicious shrimp pad thai, too!

The food at this restaurant was pretty good! While the flavors of the dishes we got didn't taste as good as they would have homemade, they were still good representations of the dishes. My only complaint about this restaurant is the location. It's pretty tucked away inside Lenox Village and you honestly wouldn't see it if you were driving down the main road. I think this location would hurt their business as well. We came during the 6pm hour and it was pretty dead inside the restaurant, which was a shame because the food and service were pretty good. I'd go there again, but I definitely wish they did a little more advertising or were closer to the main road and not tucked away behind the apartment complexes in that area.
I have been ordering from them for over a year and have to say their food is absolutely delicious. Too bad they moved away form Whyte avenue!
Worst restaurant I have ever eaten at. wife & I suffered from old poisoning. Service was poor & mixed up our orders. 20minutes to get the new check Absolutely horrible.
I am only giving this place 3 Stars the prices are high they charge 9.00 for four wing pieces that seems like a rip off to me. The other food was simply okay. I will not be coming back

WOW!! This place is AMAZING! I met some gals there for lunch and we all ordered something different, and we all LOVED everything! I had the lamb pita and the lamb was soft and juicy and perfect. The french fries are to DIE for! Perfectly seasoned and sprinkled with feta cheese. The wait staff was on top of it and the patio was really nice - beautiful artwork! I will definitely visit again soon!
They have cheap beer and nice people. I don't get to West Philly much, but when I'm in the area, I go there. The food is weird. I like it.

My daughters wants to eat pho, so we found this place on Yelp. We got there and found that they don't have Pho, but there are lots of other options. We ordered traditional hoagies, bubble tea, and summer roll. Waited for a while ( I think the cashier is not very experienced, so she's not aware when orders came out). Anyway, it totally worth it! Best Vietnamese hoagie I ever had, and we'll come back:)

i dined here with the ISC. First, i got the Persephone martini. It is a pomegranate martini. It was good. second, i got the small size spinach salad. the spinach salad is spinach, feta cheese, walnuts, and figs. The vinaigrette dressing lightly covers the salad. I liked this because i do not need a lot of dressing on my salads. I not only love figs but also salty feta cheese. The service is fast and friendly. I did not like that with a big group, they did not do separate checks. We had to figure out our totals with tax and tip. Good thing big j stl's wife is good at math. i probably would have figured i owed $80. this is why they lost half a star from me. the belly dancer only made one circle around the restaurant and was done. now the reason i had to take away another half star. i ordered the Greek version of fettuccine Alfredo. it was chicken, i substituted shrimp, feta cheese, mushrooms, and sun dried tomatoes. I ask the waitress where the mushrooms were, THEY WERE OUT! GGGGRRRRRRRRRRRRR!! The mushrooms are the main reason i wanted the dish. I had a major sad face for a good 60 seconds. as i was walking out, Mr. sheinider, my high school history teacher was sitting at the bar and remembered me from high school. Matter of fact, i think i had him sophomore year for home room. I was like wow!! overall, i will go back. the food is good and the service was good. I will just bring some mushrooms just in case.
Good food,Huge portion I just wish they have a server to assist everyone in their orders.

We went last night and the food was great! My husband and I shared 2 vegetarian dishes which were incredibly tasty and our friends had a meat combo which they also loved. We shared a bottle of Tej which is an Ethiopian honey wine and is very sweet, goes great with the food. The service was great, very friendly and accomodating. Thank you for a wonderful meal!
Quality of the buffet food has seemed to decline a bit (kinda lacking in flavor in some foods). This appears to be an epidemic Philly but I'm still a loyal customer.

The Lava, a great coffee shop by day just decided to become a BYOB by night, so I went to check it out. Food and service were great. I had the Rib Eye steak with home made chimichurri which was done exactly right and was delicious. For starters, I recommand the MAZOT, which is basicaly a selection of home made salads and pickles served with Pita bread. All in all, a great experiance, looking forward to going back and check out the other items on the menu.

I stopped by this restaurant on a rainy wed night for dinner. I entered the place and at the counter, there were 3 people making a line. I stood around for about 2 minutes not being acknowledged by anybody, so I decided to sit and wait. I noticed two people were there trying to pick up their meals and another one was lining up to pay for dinner. An older gentleman came out from the back and took care of the pick up orders; as that was happening 2 more people entered the place to pick up the orders; by then about 6 min had gone by and I was yet to be acknowledged; at that point I decided maybe it was best to leave, but since there was quite a traffic of people getting their pick up orders, I figured the food must be good so I decided to stay. Finally, 12 min after I had entered the place, the older gentleman asked, 'how can i help you,' and I told him I was there to dine in. I waited another 3 min to have the table ready, and I sat. The menu had a lot of choices and yes, plates start at around 10.95 (only saw one dish with that price though) for vegetarian selections and higher for meat dishes. While I was deciding on what to have I observed the same ritual that happened to me---couple of people entered to dine in, but others also entered to pick up their orders, and between the older gentleman and the waiter, they couldn't efficiently handle the traffic of people. I ordered mattar paneer, since I have had that at many other restaurants, and that's a good dish to compare how good an indian restaurant is. The food arrived and the dish did look good; the consistence of the gravy/sauce looked thick enough, and there were enough chunks of paneer on the dish. The meal did come with a serving of rice that could be easily serve 2 people. Unfortunately, I was highly disappointed with my dish; the flavoring was somewhat bland, and definitely I have had tons better at other indian restaurants. If you have never had Indian food, this might be a good place to get introduced to the many dishes they have; you might even like the food cause it does smell good; however, if you're an experienced indian diner, you might be highly disappointed with the food as it lacked the proper taste of what an indian dish should taste like. If i were to go back again, I would go for the buffet to try the other dishes, but definitely wouldn't pay 12 dollars for a plate of indian food that is as bland as they are at this locale. What I liked about the place though, is that they do give a large serving of the meal; I had to get a to go box because I could only eat half of what they brought out; I've been at other restaurants where the taste of the dish was a million times better, but there was enough food for one serving. However, i would rather enjoy a good meal than being given a large serving of a meal.

The food is pretty good here, but the profanity-laced shouting experience I had here tonight was embarrassing and should never be tolerated at any dining establishment. I guess I came in about 20 minutes before close and they were getting in produce for tomorrow. Literally as soon as I walked in the woman working behind the assembly line had a meltdown, cursing at the delivery boy whose boxers and underwear I could clearly see because he wasn't wearing a belt. I ordered my food, and that much went alright, until I asked for regular tzatziki on my bowl and then asked for spicy tzatziki on the side. The same woman who was cursing at the delivery boy told me she was just going to put both sauces on the side, which wasn't what I asked. So I just got the regular tzatziki. I paid for my food and sat down to eat, and the shouting and cursing continued. I was the only person in the restaurant at this point, which all of these people recognized. Three of the workers here apologized for their language and then carried on shouting and cursing about the produce. I left before even finishing my food because I was so appalled. Save the drama for when the doors are closed and you don't have customers coming into your restaurant. And put a belt on so I don't have to see your underwear. It was just trashy, honestly, and signified a severe lack of respect for customers. If you're having a bad day, I get it. We all have our setbacks and personal issues. I'm not immune to that. I actually came here BECAUSE I was having a bad day and just wanted a nice casual meal. And then I had this experience. I'm only getting to go from now on.
Very good food. I live down the street so I take out at least 2 to 3 times a week.

Some of the best Indian fare we've had, ANYWHERE! And we have some pretty great Indian and tandoori food in the Bay Area in CA. I liked the thin bubbled naan that was crispy on the bottom. It was chewy but not tough and doughy as it is in some places. Garlic naan was not too garlicky but we could have requested that if we wanted. We ordered medium spicy and it was perfect, and so so good. We had chicken tikka masala and lamb curry. I can't wait to get back there to try more! We should have ordered more rice instead of splitting one order... But then again I would have over-eaten! It's BYOB so bring your own Indian beer-- we saw some at the Weis market. Or try a wine with some power to it like a dry Zin or a dry Sauvignon blanc. Loved meeting the owner too. Really nice guy.

Great (and probably only) restaurant in the newtown area. The family who runs the place is very nice and the food portions are large, always very good and a good price for Indian. Anyone who is looking for Indian and hasn't tried Guru yet should DEFINITELY try here!

One my favorite restaurants in all of Philadelphia. They always have plenty of customers and for good reason. Their food is authentic and addictive. The vegetarian papaya salad is just perfection(warning can get extremely spicy so tell them to keep it at 2 out of 5 spice level). Their curries, from red to panang, are all excellent. The flavors are not to be beaten. I also love their homemade stuffed Lao sausages. I dont even live in Philadelphia and have eaten here about 4 times in the past two months. Go here.

I've tried to give this place two opportunities and both times they said they were closing an hour before the posted and advertised time. Also today the owner even said that I couldn't eat in and that their seeks kebabs are 80% chicken and 20% lamb, even though the menu only says lamb.

i always ge the same thing-- Spicy Noodle with tofu (or chicken) Larb Kai Salad (awesome spicy salad with lime served under a bed of ground chicken) their coconut soup is good, and in the winter i love the mushroom soup- it needs a bit of saly but theres none on the table though =\ byob they deliver now too!!! good prices, good service awesome lunch time special-- cheap $7.95 app soup entree iced tap water and they dont cheat you on the sizes either- its just right for me (too big for others) haha
Tasty, creative dishes. Small well-chosen wine list at fair prices. Top notch service and atmosphere. A fine restaurant which we look forward to enjoying again.

Great authentic halal and soul food restaurant. They have great service and a clean environment. They take cash and credit. The parking is limited but the food is worth looking around for a spot. My fav is the chicken or lamb brochette. Though it takes a little longer to prepare its amazing. The kassava is also amazing and all the food is fresh. I will definitely come back. This is my third time here. Love it.

Okay, first of all, I love that Greko sells a nice choice of craft beers as well as three different kinds of Greek wine. I joined a couple of gals for lunch yesterday, and upon arrival, it was decently full. There's a little bit of bar seating available, a window sill facing out the front window where you can eat, a couple of couples tables inside and three larger picnic type tables in the middle. Of course, there's the backyard patio area to eat as well. If it was so hot rn that would've been an awesome choice! I opted for the Greko salad with dressing on the side, which was a smart choice. Even with the little bit of dressing I drizzled on there, it was plenty. So so good! This salad is not just a salad. While the portion is a bit small for $9, I didn't regret it. I did leave a little hungry though. Probably should've added protein, but that bumped the salad up at least a few bucks. No thanks. Nearly $15 at that point. I will say, the ingredients they use are wonderful. Fresh made everything! The two girls I was with ordered the lamb pita and said it was delicious! Everything served around us looked good as well. Can't say enough good things about the staff either. There was always someone coming to make sure everything was alright, and the gentlemen placing my order was really friendly in a genuine way. I also like how you order, they give you a number, and then bring it to your table. Really convenient and quick dining! Great for lunch! Also some a couple of people doing takeout..so that's an option as well. Pickup at bar looks like. Will be returning when I can manage to eat one of those massive gyros!

Everything I had was fantastic. Went with two other guy friends that can eat. We ended with the slow roasted turkey thigh and were stuffed. Recommend the turkey thigh, zucchini, smoked trout, and ham and brie tartine.

Cute little Vietnamese spot with Chinese selection available. Ordering was very confusing and difficult. Lady who took our order spoke almost no English and when we asked her questions about the menu we got a blank stare. Only one type of phò was available, which was what I got. Fiancé got a dinner combo with chicken curry, sweet and sour pork, and pork fried rice. Our meal took 40 minutes to get out to us. Which is quite a long time time considering that there was only 10 people in there including us. The meat used in my phò was very low quality, and the chicken curry didn't taste like chicken curry. But the sweet and sour pork was actually pretty good, but was so hot it burned his mouth. I don't think we will be returning.

This place serves fantastic food. My personal favorite is the Grilled Pork Sandwich, coupled with my favorite Boba Tea - Thai Tea. Side note; their Pho is pretty good - the broth could be a little better but I'm just being nit-picky now. Conclusion; if you're interested in a nice Vietnamese lunch, this is the place to go!
First meal in Philly in a long time and it was great. I know we ate late before closing but we were well served. The place was very clean and pleasing for our first night.

This unassuming Thai restaurant lays nestled within a row of low-key Americana pub in the heart of downtown Narberth. The location alone might lead one to temper their expectations but if you take the time to step inside you will be more than pleasantly surprised. If you're not afraid of spicy food then the green curry is a must as it provides a hearty kick without leaving you gasping for water. Furthermore, the Pad Thai is one of the best I've had outside west coast enclaves. If it's available, the meal should be ended with the mango sticky rice, incredible. I can understand some of the complaints regarding portions for the price as you will not likely leave with a bag full of leftovers; however, those complaining about taste simply have not experienced good Thai food. Can't wait to go back and try out other items on the menu.

Mediocre at best. Arrived pre lunch rush and felt rushed to order and we weren't asked if we wanted something to drink. My friend and I ordered salad rolls. Hers to start, mine as my meal. Hers arrived early(within one minute of ordering) so she had to eat alone. They don't put basil or mint in the salad rolls either, I asked for basil on the sides which they brought with bean sprouts too and I was charged $4 for the basil! The rolls are pre made because I didn't get the basil in the rolls like I originally inquired about. The Kim chi was a little too sweet and the rolls were bland bland bland. That pork inside had a weird taste. No one came and asked us about water refills of anything during lunch. We then had to wait in a line to pay despite them having one portable debit machine. I wouldn't recommend this place in the future, nor will I be back soon. I will much much more willing to cross the river for Phobulous next time as their salad rolls have basil and their peanut sauce has some oomph. I wish the service was better and that the bill was correctly printed out instead of a bunch of random values punched in.

I am definitely a fan of dosa hut- the food is delicious. Beware the spiciness of the Mysore Masala Dosa...:-)... While the food is certainly very tasty, the decor leaves much to be desired. My lassi came in a styrofoam cup. Nuff said. There is ample parking in the back parking lot. Definitely a good restaurant for an authentic dosa experience.

Yes! This is a great little Haven away from burgers and fries (ok not fries, they serve them here) in Boise. There are five or six booths in the restaurant and a couple of TV's streaming Muslim TV channels. Adjacent to the market, which has a great supply of Middle Eastern Staples, including French nicotine gum in a variety of fun flavors (fun in the types, not in that I've tried them). The menu is guaranteed to have something for everyone and fill you up! Check with the staff on what type of iced tea they have that day (we ordered the green and it was a peach flavor). It's a great deal for excellent food that is abundant.

It is indeed possible to fall in love with the owners of a restaurant you love. This is the case with Parisa's, owned by a Persian couple who are the very definition of hospitality. Once a week on Saturdays Parisas serves a buffet between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. Krista and I had planned to get there by 1:30 p.m., but each of us being the less than perfect time managers that we are, it was clear we weren't going to get there until 2:15 p.m. I called the restaurant to ask if it would be alright for us to arrive this late and was told, "Yeeeasss, shhhhuuuuure," by Parisa who then said, "I will make fresh kabobs for you!" Wow. That made me feel special and we hadn't even left the house. We were greated with hugs and excitement, as if we'd come for a visit. There were four other parties seated and we were told to choose any table we liked and then to help ourselves when ready. Krista gushed about being new to Persian food and both Mr. and Mrs. Parisa took her under their wing, but Mr. Parisa made Krista his special project, explaining the food and the sauces to her in some detail, and even dishing up combinations of sauces and foods he thought she might like. There are no strange organ meats here, no odd body parts such as hooves.... no no no!!! Everything is quite amenable to the American palate. Everything we wanted was our's for the asking and Krista couldn't be more correct that the Parisas make you feel both like family and royalty. Who wouldn't want to come here as often as they could afford it. You leave feeling pampered, satisfied, and dare I say loved? Yes -- love is the word.

Rearn Thai was recommended by two friends whose opinions I highly trust. I went there for lunch today because I have been on a pad thai kick (3 times in the last week!). I was surprised to see that there was not a pad thai on their lunch menu, only on the regular menu. I ordered it anyways, remembering the recommendations of my friends, and was brought out a lunch-sized portion of the dish. For the price, $10.95, the portion was very small. I would say I eat more than the average person but I don't eat an abnormal amount. The flavor was pretty good, but it seemed very "one-note". The chicken was dry and the three shrimp in my dish were small and a little under-cooked. The environment was fine and my glass was never empty of water, I just expected a little more after the recommendations. I am still on the search for a great pad thai spot in STL...

After watching the movie Kong I strolled by this quaint little restaurant. First of all king was good, but don't go to theaters... stream it. Anywho I was walking by and something smelled fantastic... what was it you ask, wishbone! So I walk in to this rustic little space and order from the wide variety of comfort food! So what do I do, I get the mac and cheese, as well as a tasty sandwich, the tasty dirty bird sandwich... and might I say this shit was nuckin futs! I mean perfect seasoning, chicken must've been Kobe beef or something but everything 10/10 would deff recommend!

The Samosa Chaat was delicious and beautifully presented. Also excellent and unique to me was the Pachadi - a side dish of beets, yogurt, shredded coconut, toasted onions, mustard seed and a bit of chili pepper. So good on Indian breads. The flavors of everything were just right which must be tricky with so many exotic ingredients. The colorful decor is wonderful too. It was a cold, gray day and the surroundings were a real mood lifter.

Erm, I'm not quite sure why there are two pages for this place but whatever... This place is a great find tucked away from Walnut Street! It's great for a casual bite of food and their free salad bar options are quite interesting: pickled eggplant, pickles, tabbouleh, carrots, spicy mango chutney! The falafel is pretty good, the shish kabobs have so tender meat, and the portions are so big! Awesome deal!

We've been wanting to try this place after driving by it numerous times and we finally made our way here this afternoon for lunch. We went around 11:15 on Sunday and we were the only people but I figured that was because we were eating lunch so early. The staff was extremely nice and did a good job of answering any questions we had about the menu. To start off we had the Kanom Jeab (Chicken/Shrimp Steamed Dumplings), which were absolutely delicious! My fiancé had the Pad See Ew and I had the Pad Kee Mao. We both loved our food although we weren't too much of a fan of the others meal so I guess we ordered the right ones for ourselves! The ingredients seemed to be very healthy and fresh, which made the food seem even better when we were eating it. I would definitely recommend coming here and we will be back again!

One of those things that makes me feel like an "in-the-know" Philadelphian! I've been passing this cart for over a year intrigued by the constant line of people as 70s and 80s jams blare out of this cart that always looks like it's on fire. Pack your patience. This guy is making food with love and it takes time. He talks up his regulars and gives you the speech about why his food is so awesome and why he doesn't have a menu. The deal is you stand in line - he makes some kind of chicken and falafel over a little rice with heap of fruits and/or veggies and then hands it to you for $10. You don't know what it is and it doesn't come with modification. You can only get one per person. Today it had a very bright sauce with grapes, sliced apples, and some little citrus guy. It was delicious and fed me for two meals and cleared out my sinuses in the midst of allergy season. My ONLY sadness is that it takes so long - we waited over a half hour in the line which is my entire lunch break. If you have a slow day, can take a friend, or see the cart with less than 9 people in line it's worth the wait though!

Food: 4 Decor: 3 Ambiance: 3 Service: 4 Value: 4 I'm learning that my interest in Thai restaurants is directly correlated to whether or not they serve "Evil Jungle Princess". This restaurant does, they make it well, and I like them for it. I'm sure it isn't a particularly authentic dish or anything, but man, I love the spice and flavor of it. This may be the best rendition I've had.
This is my favorite lunch spot in Nashville. The food is healthy and fresh. Simply the best!
The food was pretty salty and the service wasn't great. The bathroom was good though. So, ya know, there's that.

This is an amazing restaurant. I was skeptical about Indian food before but this place really changed my mind. I got the fish Marsala (salmon) and it was fantastic! The manager was so friendly and recommended some great appetizers. AND ITS BYOB!
The food is good but service seems spotty. Been there several times and sometimes things are perfect and other times they give you the wrong meal.

Has read about the spread of this chain so when I heard it was coming to the KOP area, had to try it. I had the falafel on a pita. Have to say, falafal can be crunch and full of flavor or, if done badly, it is like eating a fried golf ball. For a fast food sort of place, I was very impressed by their falafel. It was hot, crunchy, and tasty. Next time, I'll ask for more sauce -- it was a bit skimpy. The greatest disappointment was the pita. It was soft and fell apart. I dispise Wonder Bread and the consistency this reminded me of it vacuous taste and empty calories. I will go back and give it another try -- perhaps the shawarma next time, but in a bowl.

I love this place. I love Ethiopian food, and I love Almaz specifically. I usually hit the Rittenhouse location, but I was in Norristown for an event and couldn't resist. In addition to our zilzil tibs (delicious, perfectly spiced, perfectly cooked), we also got an order of yegebe (lamb) tibs that was juicy, flavorful, and rich with peppers and onions. The chef brought out our platter and injera and told us what the sides were - heaping portions of red lentils, yellow lentils, tikil gomen, shiro, and some sort of beet dish that was sooo good. The staff here are just as friendly and welcoming as the Rittenhouse location, and they serve beer! I'm told that the location puts some people off, but ignore them - it's worth the trip.
Healthy food, clean flavors and a casual hip atmosphere - solid service.
Paneer tikka rice bowl aka the chipotle burrito bowl with an Indian twist! Amazing concept and amazing food at tandoor and tikka!

They must have lost their chef.....the last two times we were disappointed in the quality of their dishes.......likely not go back. Do not let the name nor the location fool you. Its doesn't have great curb appeal. However, the food is EXCELLENT! its the best we have ever tasted, even better than the San Francisco Bay Area Thai restaurants. I highly recommend this place. We have been there three times and tried six different plates....all impressed us! Nice wait staff and a real Thai woman cooks the food! Awesome!

It was my first experience at 8th and union and it was very pleasing! Started the night off with the pork dumplings and snapper ceviche which were both executed very well! Ceviche was VeRY fresh, and had nice heat and citrus flavor which paired nicely. For dinner went with the green curry, which was fantastic. I'm a big fan of curry's and this didn't disappoint, I highly recommend it! The owner, Brian, came over twice during our meal to make sure everything came out as expected, which was a nice touch. I will be back in the future for sure!

Love getting their chicken kabob plate. Everything that comes with the plate is so good. Their steak kabob is also a great choice. Meat melts in your mouth. The place is always packed, for good reason. I've had their Greek salad once and it was really good as well. I've tried two of their soups (tortellini and a beef stew). Tortellini was better than the stew. If you like Mediterranean food, this is a good stop

This is our go to restaurant prior to the movies at green hills. However, it had been awhile since we visited and tonight it was an incredibly pleasant surprise. Grilled shrimp salad delish. The lettuce extremely crisp and fresh and the salad dressing was the perfect compliment. My hubby had the other special which was a lamb Kebob. Surprisingly, it was so much thicker than the typical kebob, making it cooked to perfection. A solid medium rare and amazingly tender. Forgot to order the garlic knots - that is the best way to go with the bread.
Food was fine ,would have liked it a bit spicy(personal preference). Service is good. Got hot food even past the buffet time. Ambience is ok.

I love Pita's Republic. Whenever I see one, I get excited. It's all about that thickand chewy pita, the tender and juicy meat, and that fabulous yogurt sauce. No matter the location, I will always come back for more.

Stopped by for lunch with a co- worker on a Tuesday. This small place was very busy with the business lunch crowd. I ordered the Pad Thai, which just wasn't up to snuff. The shrimp weren't cleaned, and the sauce tasted like it was bottled, not fresh. Overall, not bad, but not impressed either.

Great interior very cute place. I did takeout, lamb vindaloo was very tasty but not enough lamb too much rice, the yellow dahl while tasty was too watery almost like soup & too mild for my taste. Overall I'd say it was good & I'd definitely return & dine there next time

I have been dying to try out this restaurant for the longest (seriously, nonstop insta-stalking). What really caught my attention was the flavor combination that they were working with, Southeast Asian and Southern spices, and I definitely wanted to see how it will be executed. First off, the atmosphere of the restaurant is so lax and you can immediately sense that your meal is going to be prepared with some TLC! And honestly, that's what I felt when I ate my meal. I had the gulf fish over popcorn rice with two sides, the spring green salad and the the vinagery root vegetable side (I can't remember the name of it). My friend had the pork and grilled cabbage. Both were delicious because the flavors reminded me of my mom's cooking. The spring green salad was delicious. There was a mix of bitter greens, thin sliced watermelon radishes, and (I think) a light fish sauce dressing. The protein on both plates were seasoned well, however, I think the overall saltiness of both dishes with sides over powered everythinggggg. I wanted more rice to balance out the flavors on my plate, and more water. The spicy sauce drizzled over the pork could be reduced by a tad because the rice became soaked in it also, which just made everything salty and you had nothing neutral to balance out any of the flavors. I finished my entire plate anyways since everything was pretty good. Other than my own saltiness, I enjoyed my experience here and will definitely come back to try other dishes!
This is the best Thai food I've had in Boise. In Seattle or Portland, it would be 4/5, but by Boise standards, it's the best there is.

This is my favorite Indian spot in Philadelphia. I used to order from Indian restaurant on south street, but I am now loyal to this place. I always get some naan and the paneer masala which is amazing. They don't use butter so it's much healthier than any other Indian restaurant I have eaten at in the city. It is also significantly cheaper than any other Indian restaurant in the city. The paneer masala is $4.50 rather than $10-15 at other places. Affordable, quick delivery, and healthy options!

Food = A Service = F Personally I think they do not want to serve Asians in the nearby communities. It feels like we owed them money when they served us. My observations in multiple occasions were when they served non Asians, services were excellent. Maybe they don't care. Sad!!!

I came here on a whim hoping for some delicious curry, and boy did I find it. I was treating my boyfriend to dinner here, and after a little confusion in finding the place, we finally arrived. I was kind of glad it was quiet inside. The weather was yucky, so it was very quiet for a Sunday evening. Good for me, but bad for business. The inside is decorated with a comfortable vibe. It strives to look high class, but falls a little short with some tacky decorations. Either way, it looks nice enough inside and the staff had a huge smile the entire time. That's pretty charming. :) Our server took our order promptly. We already knew what we wanted, so that part wasn't hard at all. Gotta love people who know what they want, right? I ordered the yellow curry with tofu. My boyfriend ordered jungle curry with chicken. We waited awhile for our order, but they kept refilling our water glasses while we waited. I hate not getting enough water at a restaurant, but they kept me pretty hydrated. Bonus points. When the food came, I was surprised by how much you actually get. Not only do you get a generous side of delicious rice, but you also get a huge bowl of vegetables and curry sauce. Delicious. My curry wasn't spicy, but I wasn't expecting it to be. It was a mild and creamy taste with plenty of vegetables. I think next time I will request a spicier version and the vegetables to be cooked a little longer. I like my curried potatoes soft, but mine felt barely cooked. A kind male server stopped to talk to us for a few moments, and he learned that it was our first time here. My boyfriend passed on some compliments to the chef, and the chef sent out a free mini dessert for us. How sweet was that? The fried bananas were delicious, and I thought that this was a thoughtful gesture. I've never been treated so kindly just because it was my first time at a restaurant. Maybe I should tell more servers that it's my first time at X dining establishment. Overall the curry was pretty good, and I left with a full belly. It didn't upset my stomach, it tasted good and I didn't feel weighed down after eating it. I look forward to returning and trying the other curries and dishes that are offered here. If you're vegetarian/vegan, then this is a great place to go!
Great egg rolls Moo Shu yummy, pork fried rice good, basically everything I have had there is good, hole in the wall Chinese, good eats.

Had this recently at their food truck during Roots picnic and was charged $30 for two (less than generous) plates of oxtails, rice/greens and mac and cheese. Total rip off! Let's get to the food. The oxtails were good and so was the rice but the greens lacked flavor and so did the "famous mac and cheese" they both needed some salt if you ask me....very bland. Conclusion: This soul food has no soul and will leave your stomach and your wallet empty.

FYI: They charge certain items by weight in a way that's sorta similar to Kiwi. I live literally 2 blocks away but this was the first time I've ever even been inside of this place. I don't really walk past 40th a lot so there wasn't exactly a motive to go and try this place out, but I mean the bright orange, mural of a giant chicken does sorta call your name as you walk by it. WHAT WE GOT: Classic white & dark meat chicken tenders + Wishbone mac and cheese PROS: Really cute and homey decor that gave off a really inviting vibe. The meat in the chicken tenders was cooked beautifully with none of them being dry or hard to bite off and eat. You could literally pull the chicken tenders apart with your hands without them putting up a fight. They have a pretty nice variety of sauces on display, with the new addition of a citrus honey butter. That honey butter is literally gold. It know it's probably suppose to go on the biscuits but I ate some with the chicken and fell in love with the combination. I legit took the rest of it home with me. But I gotta say, the mac and cheese was definitely the star for me. Tasted awesome with just a bit of heat at the end though the presentation could use a bit of work. The noodles were sorta falling apart but I still enjoyed it. CONS: The coating on the chicken didn't really taste like much to me. It got a lot of it's flavor from the sauces you dip them in. We got the chipotle lime mayo and the pommery honey mustard, both of which should be renamed. The chipotle mayo was like 99% chipotle and 1% mayo. There was no creaminess to it and had absolutely no lime flavor. The honey mustard was also lacking the "honey". Also, for how much food you get, Wishbone definitely fares on the overpriced side. This isn't really something you'd eat to get full but probably as a snack if you don't want to spend a butt ton of money.

Going to Ali Baba's has become a NO tradition. Originally stumbled on during a late night food run, it's become our regular grab a bite place when in NO. Basically for the price of a street dog, you can have a tasty gyro with a squeeze of rooster sauce if you please.

I was curious to try this place since I have not had a lot of Mediterranean food; it ended up being decent. My friend and I came here for dinner and some after work drinks. They had quite the selections of interesting beers and cocktails (there was also wine too). I tried a Dark Room Bloom which was very tasty and came in a fancy glass! We ordered the King of Kings Humus which was delicious. They handmade the roll of pita bread, which was very good. The downside is, they only give you one and there is no way you can use up all the humus with one pita; ordering an extra one will cost you $2. I ordered the charred broccoli sandwich which was very tasty indeed! I love the fresh baked bread and the meltiness of the cheese paired with the charred broccoli. The food here was delicious as were the cocktails, the reason I only gave it three stars is because I do not feel the price justifies the food. The sandwiches do not come with a side so if you eat a bigger dinner, I would not recommend this place. This place is for getting a good quality drink and a lite dinner.

Lots of food, no menu. You get what's being made because Kostontinos wanted to buy those ingredients today! Today, grill chicken with salad, fruit rice and beans. The chicken is absolutely bringing the heat!!

Place is pretty decent. I got the bento lunch box for $12.99 it came with miso soup, seaweed cucumber salad, 1 roll, tempura, and choice of another sushi. It was overall delicious and tasteful. If your in the area and not looking for anything to expensive, check this place out.

I was pleasantly surprised by Taziki's! We've had quite a varied reaction to the Mediterranean places around Nashville, with some places offering us uncooked meat in our gyros. For this reason, I wasn't really sure what to expect with Taziki's. However, I tend to use lamb gyros as my standard test at Mediterranean places, and Taziki's was pretty amazing. For $8.25, you got a pretty big gyro wrap that was completely stuffed with lamb, and accompanied by the usual lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. It was also filled with their own tzatziki sauce. The gyro came with regular ruffled chips, with the choice of one "healthy side," for which I chose roasted potatoes. We were also given a free order of hummus and pita chips, and then given an extra coupon for free hummus on our next visit! First of all, I was super impressed with the generous amount of lamb you were given in this email. But best of all, even compared to our usual favorites in town, Athens on 8th, the lamb was so, so, so tender and flavorful. It was delicious! My only criticism for the grilled lamb gyro was that their tzatziki sauce was a little too salty. As for the hummus and pita chips, the hummus was pretty good - nothing that blew me away, but still tasty. However, I wasn't the biggest fan of the pita chips - they were not bite-sized, and a little too crispy for me ... but that's a personal taste, as I like my pita chips to be in the middle of soft and crispy. The roasted potatoes were pretty tasty and had a nice garlic taste - great for a big garlic lover like me! Next time, I will probably ask to sub out the ruffle potato chips for something healthier, like their tomato-cucumber salad, pasta salad or fresh fruit. All in all, I really enjoyed Taziki's, and was pretty pumped to find a place close to campus that actually serves great Mediterranean food! It may not have the ultimate lamb burger like Athens on 8th, but I think at least their lamb gyro beat out the same meal we usually have at Kalamata's (crazy to think, I know). I would highly recommend this place for a try - it's pretty healthy, inexpensive (nothing on the menu over $10), and quite tasty! WINNING.

My husband and I had a rehearsal dinner for 60 people at Erawan Thai, on a Friday night in March 2012. Our experience could not have been better! It is a cute very spacious venue. The venue was fine for 60 and probably could have accommodated more. The food is delicious. We originally asked to serve appetizers at the table. and then three entrees buffet style. The appetizers were amazing. Laddie helped us craft a varied menu and even threw in an extra entree. The place is BYOB, which meant we saved a lot of money and could bring exactly what we wanted to drink. Also, Earwan has a sound system that is ipod compatible. We were able to play a playlist we created for the event for our guests. Erawan's staff decorated the restaurant for the event. It was soo cute! They put out different linens, covered the chairs and even hung small vases with flowers. Laddie, the manager, was on hand during the event to help host and organize our guests. We love Erawan generally, but I highly recommend considering Erawan for private events. We had a terrific experience. Laddie is the best!

I wasn't expecting much because of the secluded location,but boy was I wrong. I ordered the famous Fish Hoagie,and it was worth the wait. Fresh bread,fresh fish,homemade mayo,and fresh veggies!! Delicious and worth the brief wait. Give Sis Muhammad's a chance,even the stereotypical prepared desserts were great and fresh!

Yay! Vandy finally has a vendor for Asian food! They sell Pho soup and Bahn mi, which is limited but its a great start!!! And if you're a student, this counts as a meal on the commodore card or if you're visiting, they take credit cards but not cash. It's located on the Vanderbilt campus in Alumni Hall. And they now have bubble tea :)

Always a great experience. Always great food. I have to admit, I order the CRAB RAGOONS at least once a month, if not four times. The PHO, can be in HALF or FULL portions. Great for someone like me who can't ever finish pho in one sitting. Tina, the manager, is very sweet, pays attention to detail, and always greats me as a loyal customer. Thank you for your time and service.
Yummy Indian!! Vegetable samosas were my husband's favorite. The portions were generous and delicious. We're moving to the area soon, and will absolutely be back.
Avoid not good on all levels. Food is not good bad service not clean not in a nice area

Went here for a late lunch. Pho was great- yummy broth with plenty of noodles and meat. I heard positive things from my friends about the other dishes but think pho would be thing to get here. The green tea boba smoothie was enjoyable as well. Service was friendly (but a little slow- not that it mattered for my very casual lunch). Would definitely recommend. 4.4
It was okay. My noodles came out very chewy but the Mac and cheese is good. Nothing to be too excited about.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in Tampa. As someone who absolutely loves Thai curry and ventures out to find the best, this place has some of the best red curry I've ever had. It is creamy, delicious, and they give you a perfect ratio of rice to curry. The food is ready in a timely manner and the staff is friendly. Highly recommend for Thai food lovers!

This is one of my absolute favorite restaurants in St. Louis. The food is awesome, the ambience is cool, and the belly dancers are fun. A lot of reviews here are saying how the dishes are not authentic Greek food, which they might not be. But it is absolutely delicious. I've been here many, many times and recommend everything on the menu. Here are some of my favorites: Hummus- My boyfriend says it's the best he's ever tasted. Fava- Tangy and rich spread Gyro- Can't go wrong here Falafel- Again, can't go wrong. Lamb Kabobs- They are served over these lemon roasted potatoes and it's the perfect size. You won't be stuffed, but you won't be hungry when you're finished Lamb with Fig Sauce- OMG. So good. Greek Medallions- One of the best things on the menu. Its beef tenderloin with blue cheese mashed potatoes and a raspberry wine sauce that you will want to drink right from the cup. Again, I'm not sure how authentically Greek it is but it's delicious. Baklava- Best I've ever tasted. This place can get rather packed on a weekend night, so call ahead for reservations. Bring a group of friend, share some small plates, have some wine, and you'll have a great time. Trust me!

I just went here for a group birthday dinner. I was pretty nervous since I am a picky eater and assumed I would be eating food strait out of an Indian Jones movie. The meal consisted of a 9 small courses and the meal lasted over 5 hours. The atmosphere was great but I the food was below average. I only enjoyed 2 or 3 courses and I passed on a few. They really gouge you on the drinks so be careful. Bottom line. If you are looking to try something different (with a group of friends), give it a whirl.

This place is wonderful. We tried mostly vegetarian dishes and all were stellar. We also had the chicken tikka masala which was delicious. The spice levels offered are mild, medium, and hot. The "medium" spice was just right for most of us, about equivalent to hot Mexican food. Perfect for sharing and trying new flavors! The samosas were an ideal appetizer. We also had the masala spiced naan. Great service and BYOB. Wonderful place on a freezing night!
Food: 3.5 Decor: 4 Ambiance: 4 Service: 3.5 Value: 3.5 This felt like the coffee shop from Friends or something. I enjoyed the experience, and the food was decent as well.

Shocked this place doesn't have a higher rating. This is hands down the best Thai food I've had. At a lot of Thai places the flavors run together and it's hard to distinguish between sauces, but every dish here shines and you can really taste the different ingredients. The chef takes a lot of pride in her work. Can't miss: coconut soup, vegetable dumplings, panang, curry asparagus. The cabbage salad is also great. Two downsides: 1. Some items can be a bit expensive (the dumplings are like $2 each for example). 2. I wish they did a tofu satay with peanut sauce or something similar! They only have a chicken version. Still gets five stars because the food is outstanding.

I loooooove the chicken shawarma salad from Shishkabob House. It's more of a chopped salad style than the typical "greek salad" that other restaurants place under the meat, and I appreciate that there are plenty of cucumbers to go around. I've also had the dinner plate with salad and hummus. It was yummus! (sorry, had to). For me, it's conveniently located in a small North Kenner strip mall, perfect for takeout after work. Friendly staff, great portions, and delicious!
Great food and service. Our waitress Ryan was outstanding and made the experience even more enjoyable. Potstickers were fabulous. If you are looking for somewhere to eat, don't pass this place up.
Is M. Express closed now? Went today and there was a shwarma place opening up at their address. did they move? i am dying to eat at this place after reading the reviews and looking at the menu!
Very friendly staff, great atmosphere and EXCELLENT FOOD! Please come it's a hidden GEM.
Walked into Delicia and was under-dressed so opted for La Mulita. I was impressed! Very small menu but delicious. Great service!!!
Very good, like a little oasis amidst half-weight eateries... Banh Mi sandwiches rule, awesome flavor and low prices - thanks for a great dinner! :)
Closed about 2-3 months ago to make room for a Gino's Chicken Franchise. Don't know why.

Referred by a friend and what great food it is at this BYOB I had the pollo cacciatore my date had veal parmesan and pasta. Tomato sauce was really great. We had fennel with oil & bread. A fried meatball appetizer made out of three meats. Service was real good as well.

OMG - Lunch buffet was great!!! Had a groupon - had great service - Wonderful Naan, can't say more. Ill be back!! Nice decor! Hot food- all around a good place for lunch with friends who enjoy Indian food.

The food was absolutely delicious! I have no idea what I ate because my friend ordered all of the food for our table. She had been there many times and we put ourselves in her hands. We had about 5 different vegetarian platters and 4 different meat dishes. Everything was served on large platters on top of the bread that's used to eat the food. In addition to extra rolls of the bread, which is like a spongy crepe, everything was serves with some kind of cabbage slaw. We also enjoyed honey wine with our meal, which was slightly effervescent and quite good, but I'm not sure I could drink a whole lot of it because of its sweetness. I look forward to going back again!

Been a couple of times. Great waitstaff there...very helpful. Great food and the atmosphere is really nice as well. It is a byob, and is just a few doors away from the county theatre and also near spas, bookstores, boutiques...easily a nice way to end a few hours in doylestown. Does not disappoint!

The grilled steak was great. Very tender and flavorful. I wish I could say the same for the salad, lemon chicken soup, and grape leaves but they were all horrible! Waste of money so I will never go back. The restaurant was clean and the people were friendly. I've had really good Lebanese food but this was not it!

One of the few places that I would give 5 stars. I have made it a tradition to celebrate my birthday at Dmitri's. Pick up a nice bottle of wine, get the grilled octopus and oysters. All the fish on the menu that we have tried are superirro. The pan-fried flounder -- I swear they put the breading on with a laser beam; it's so thin and perfect. Noisy, boisterous and cramped -- I wouldn't have it any other way. What always amazes me that the chef staff is all asian, cooking Mediterranean food.

Their grilled Fish and shrimp is good especially for a post work out meal . It's a clean place and the people there are so nice! They do not get annoyed if you adjust orders and have no problems accommodating to what you want. Chicken salad is ok, kind of have to drench it to be able to get through all the big amount of dry lettuce , more chicken added would be nice as well. Ultimately This is more of a place to eat fatty foods and be satisfied .
Food was really good! It's a really cute small restaurant and the service is superb!! The lady that works there is so sweet which makes me want to keep coming back.

On the heels of being overstuffed, I thought I'd right a fresh review. I've wanted to try this place since it opened about a month ago. It didn't disappoint. This is buffet style and it looks like they slightly change up their offerings from day to day - but only by an item or so. Today, I tried the chicken tikka masala, vegetables malai kofta, and the mixed veg curry. I thought the chicken and veg. malai kofta were really good but the veg curry was just so-so. I'm not a fan of spicy food so if I go back I'll have to ease up on the sauces. However, if you like spicy food, they do offer free hot sauce. If you're in the mood for quick, cheap Indian food, Mumbai will hit the spot.

Quaint breakfast spot. I've only ever passed by on the weekends, when there is always a line. I got in line over the last weekend. It was worth the wait. Great staff. Delicious food. I got a buttermilk breakfast sandwich with home fries. Yum! Can't wait to go again.
Delicious. Wonderful, fresh ingredients, cooked to perfection. The restaurant is clean, quiet, and inviting. The staff are friendly and provided great service.
