Having been to many mojito bars in the South America, Miami & NYC metro area - this was a watered down version of the decent ones. Here's the good: the decor is really cute, you can bring your dog in, they have a band playing and the Mojitos don't have too much mint, that way your not picking it out of your teeth the rest of the day. The not so good: we ordered food and it was served on a tiny desert plate but cost a full meal's price. The band that plays there plays Jazz, yes I know it's New Orleans but this is a MOJITO bar! I would not return.

I got my first taste of Wishbone last night and I was pretty happy with it. Yeah, a lot of people will say that you can get more or less the same thing (chicken tenders) at places like KFC or Popeyes, but Wishbone certainly seems to have the one thing that those chains don't have: consistency. Anybody who frequents fried chicken chains will speak of those times that they had perfectly fried and seasoned juicy chicken tenders...but ask them about the bad experiences and they'll have just as many. That's the true value in a place like Wishbone, you can expect some level of consistency. That said, the chicken was extremely juicy and tender and the fried surface is as good as the best days of KFC and Popeyes. The one big downside of Wishbone is the flavor in the breading. Unless you get the special (eh), it doesn't have exactly blast you with favor. However, they have a lot of really great sauces on hand for 50 cents each (maybe overpriced), I sprung for the lime chipotle and the BBQ. I recommend both! While very yummy, I'd pass on the pies. They're good, but maybe not four dollar good.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: General Tso's is super crispy and delicious every time. Sushi is great. Won-ton is also fantastic. Food is always super hot and delicious and on-time.

One word - yum! Not a five star environment, but a great place to grab lunch or a quick bite for dinner on the cheap. Good variety on the menu, service is good, and the food is better than what I expected for the area, a small strip center on a quiet freeway ramp. Based on the food alone it would be a 5-star rating, but taking the whole experience into account, it's a solid 4. Enjoy!

Really good servers and food. Enjoyed myself thoroughly. Food came out pretty quick and was delicious. We went in really near the closing time, but they still served us with a smile and didn't complain about it at all. Will definitely visit the restaurant again.

I went for the lunch buffet. Plenty to choose from, but, the food was mediocre. The chicken chili and goat curry were over seasoned with a particular spice. The 'butter chicken' and dal lentils were both very bland. All the way around my plate, the experience was one dimensional and didn't have balance.

It's been over a year since my first visit to Thai Orchid. Looooooong overdue as I've been wanting to come back here to try a couple more of their dishes. Well, L and J both had somehow never experienced good Thai eats in town so I decided that needed to be remedied immediately. We came on a Friday evening without reservations but luckily arrived just before the dinner rush began. Hello perfect timing. If you want to be safe, it'd be wise to make a reservation otherwise you'll be waiting awhile for a table. Service here is friendly but sloooooooooooow. There's only two waiters manning the whole room so keep that in mind. I was actually surprised how busy they were as I didn't think that many people knew about them. I like their menus that they bring to the table. Fits all on one fold out page. - 2x Thai iced tea ($4.00 each) - this one was quite satisfying although I thought there was a bit too much ice in it for my liking. -Tom yum goong (#10) ($14.50 for 4) - hot and sour soup with shrimp, mushrooms, tomato, spices, galangal and lemongrass. Woaaaaah, their tom yum soup had my taste buds tantalizing. Sour? Check. Spicy? You bet ya. An explosion of flavour. We probably only needed to order the small tom yum ($9.50 for 2) as J and I ended up having to eat a couple more bowls to finish everything off. Poor L, the heat was a bit too much for her although she loved it. - 2x Kao mun (#11) ($4.00 each) - Thai Orchid's signature coconut rice. Fragrant, light and delicious. You'll definitely need at least two of their bowls to soap up all the curry sauce. - Pad chan (#13) ($13.50) - a version of pad thai, originating from the Chantaburi province, that is lightly spiced with a homemade sauce. We opted for chicken with our pad chan and just like their pad thai, it was tasty. Love the bite of the noodles and sweetness was well balanced. I didn't taste any spice but that helped to counteract the other dishes. - Lad nha mhee krob talay (#17) ($15.50) - crispy noodle topped with seafood, vegetables and tasty brown sauce. Don't you just love that description? All in the "details" eh? All kidding aside, our second noodle dish was tasty but I wanted the noodles to be a bit more crispier. At least there was a good amount of seafood (shrimp and squid). - Geang khao whan (#27) ($13.50) - green curry with bamboo shoots, green and red peppers, basil and coconut milk. We opted for beef but I thought they skimped on the meat. The green curry I had to order for my friends as they've never tried it. Just as good the first time I ordered it. The spice level is perfect, it's rich and creamy, what more do you want in a curry? Portions are on the slightly smaller side of things but the quality more than makes up for it. I'll be back for more the next time Thai cravings hit.

Food was excellent. Same with the service. Clean place and quaint. In the back of a shopping center so I'm not sure if people know about it. They rate their dishes so you know how spicy it is. I got the Level 4 of 5 and it was delicious but I like things hot. I'd go back.

Go! Gyro! Go! is a every week must have! Each time they are at Wells Fargo Advisors the line just grows. At least 3-5 of us from dept have it each week. We'be even converted the pickiest of eaters into trying it! Each of the dishes have been great but I am partial to the classic gyro (beef & lamb). The salads are also very popular amongst the crowd. The crew inside the truck is always smiling and moving as fast as possible. If you see this truck parked near you....there is a reason for the long line! You won't be disappointed!
Only one guy to take the order, Serve and billing. They will make you wait until you lost the interest on food. Not hygiene and not worth.

No real decor / Not inexpensive / but the food's tasty and they'll adjust the spice tolerance to your preference - It's the Indian restaurant I always come back to... Favorites- Chicken Makhani - Vegetable Samosa - Lamb Sagwalla --

Great indian buffet place if you want some decent indian food. They have a wide variety of their specialties, so there is always something to cater to your taste. Whether you're trying out Indian food for the first time or you are a long time veteran, you can't go wrong with this place. My only gripe is that they raised the price a number of times... used to be 8 dollars for a lunch buffet. Now it's up to 10.
Definitely worth trying. An almost Chipotle-style approach to Indian food. The chicken was delicious, the atmosphere was comfortable, and the service was very friendly and helpful.

I walked into Wishbone because my friend who I cosplay with told me that they do breakfast. So, I guess the chefs are fancy because they had this thing called Muesli. never heard of it before. SUPER TASTY. Makes me forget that I stuffed my face with 2 beef 'n cheddars last night at arbys! (felt sick afterwards) Anyway, this muesli had some fresh fruits, honey, yogurt and oatmeal. They weigh it for you too, so you can get as much or as little as you like. Also got a breakfast sandwich. I got their chicken apple sausage deal with cheese on a croissant. HOLY SITHHHHH. I think they also had a muffin version. Downed it all with one of their fresh squeezed juicesssssss. Honestly, I would get this 3 part breakfast every day if I could. It also helps that the staff was super nice especially since it was early on a Monday morning. It def helped me start my week off right. I just thought... It would be totally awesome if I could have some of this breakfast stuff late at night when I'm watching clone wars on my computerrrrr. uggggh a sith lord can dream thoughhhh

Worth the trip to Arabi! Falafel with tahini was the best ever and spinach pie fresh and delicious ! Awesome service, soothing music. The desserts look yummy but no room. Very reasonable too! What a find! Oh, and there's a grocery inside the restaurant (or maybe the other way around?) Lots of Mideastern goodies to choose from !
This is the best Dabeli i ever had outside of Bombay. Whatever we ate was very tasty. Love it!!
Few items were good but most were average. The wait time to get in was 25 minutes and the long buffet queues didnt help either.

We have eaten here twice now and both times were excellent! I ordered steak dishes both times and they were were both super flavorful and tender. The first time I got the Bistec de Palomilla and the second time I got the Carne Asada. Their chimichurri sauce is stellar and I highly recommend trying a dish that includes it. The people I went with tried a variety of other things and everyone loved their dishes. I don't think you can go wrong anywhere! Also, make sure you try one of their cocktails. They are tasty and strong. :-)

Our area really has needed to kick it up a notch over the past few years. Downtown Yardley, while having some staples that are just plain good, has really gotten away from exciting and excellent dinner options. Enter Francisco's on the River. My husband and I found this gem on a hectic night and, thankfully, they had ONE table open for two. Reservations highly recommended. The waitstaff was awesome, the food exceptional, and the experience top notch. One recommendation: If it's a chilly night out, and the restaurant seems to be booked, make sure to bring a coat. There is no vestibule to shield you from a gusty cold draft every time the door opens, so Husband and I froze every time a new party came in.
Great place with delish food. Potions are big, and not overpriced. naan is tasty, and coconut rice is to die for.samosas and sauce pairing are great as well. I Highly recommend this place.

Francisco's On the River is one of my favorite local restaurants in Washington Crossing. The food is simply outstanding, some of the best meals that I ever had. A little pricy but the food is delicious, creative and appropriately proportioned. There is not one course I would not happily eat again. With reservations made we never have to wait for our table. Service was impeccable. The atmosphere is cozy with a nice view of the river. It is BYOB. Highly suggest it to anyone.

So it's pretty regular as pho goes. I enjoyed the spring rolls cuz it had a lot of mushroom in it. I had the well done beef pho and the meat was a bit thick. otherwise, the broth was on the bland side, but the meal wasn't offensive.

I was really looking forward to coming here for my birthday brunch after reading such great reviews. I was disappointed to say the very least. We waited 30 mins just to get our drink order (by drinks I mean water and coffee) and over an hour to get our food. My dad received his food 25 mins before the rest of our table and had finished his meal by the time we could even get our server's attention. Once we could ask her if our food would be ready soon she responded by saying that some things just take longer to prepare- meanwhile the tables next to us (who had arrived after us) had been served their meals and signed their checks and we, a party of 3, were still waiting to eat. Once our food came I was extremely upset to see a giant hair cooked into my shakshuka. I wasn't going to say anything but my mom insisted that she tell the server and ended up doing so. The server apologized and then the manager came over. He was extremely kind and comped our entire meal and offered to make another dish for us. However, we were not willing to wait another hour and a half to be fed and were ready to go. I gave this 2 stars for the manager being so great, but I will sadly not be coming here again.

Had lunch buffet. Dont know everything about indian food but i do love the food culture they bring here, All the different spices and taste. Most underrated food out there. For this place. Everything was hot and well made. I like how they change up the buffet every time I go in. You will enjoy it here..not a huge selection but enough. Service is a bit slow but I feel they are under staffed. Give them a try.

What an amazingly charming piece of heaven in the middle of the city! We had been drinking wine with dinner and wanted to continue on with the theme for the last bit of our evening. Upon pulling up I was immediately charmed by the lively patron filled restaurant. The menus are unique and inviting. While somewhat giant, there is a table of contents to keep your head from spinning. :-). We enjoyed a glass of Syrah from Walla Walla while Our Companions drank a European cider which they raved about. Service was impeccable and the family feel of the seating layout sparked a sense of community. On our next visit to the city we will be sure to visit Olio for both wine and food. In mad love with it.

Came here a few weeks ago on a Friday night, and the service was pretty awful. They confused our reservations for the night before, and then told us they could only seat us in the elevated section of the restaurant. When we got there, they sat us at an empty table instead, and we waited about 20 minutes for a server to come by. We were in a rush so we quickly ordered and awaited our food. It took quite some time. The dishes were flavorful, but very similar in appearance and taste. Fortunately, this place is BYO so our time waiting was time well spent drinking. Not sure if I would come back - I miss their more casual location on Sansom Street.

At a small retirement luncheon, I ordered the Thai crab salad expecting something ... well tasty with a little heat. The dish is bland in appearance as well as flavor. Everything was white, except the julienned carrots and served on a white plate. The pieces of crab were minuscule, the shreds of carrot too thick compared to the size of the noodles, flecks of cilantro but not enough to provide flavor. Once in awhile I found a sprout. Overall there was not much flavor to any part of the meal. When I find myself shaking bottles of sauce haphazardly I know the dish is off. The worst for me is that I splurged thinking this would be dinner and left the table still hungry. Our server was nice but they kitchen sort of messed up some of our orders so they didn't seem very efficient. Coffee was good but, in general you can do better elsewhere.

Foods good here. The crispy orange chicken was tasty and plentiful. The Mongolian Beef was pretty much 8-10 pieces of beef and the rest green onions smothered on top. Beef very tender had good flavor. Service was rather slow. Not many people in my section, it took about 10 minutes to get my tab, and another 10 for her to pick up my card. *** If you are allergic to shell fish do NOT come here. My friend is allergic, and they gave him a photocopy stapled menu with like 5 options.****

Outrageous. Total auteur cuisine. You feel humbled to order and eat food by someone so clearly devoted and passionate about his craft practicing it in such a novel way. Feels like a secret right out in the open. Can't wait to see what he serves up on my next visit.

I found myself here for lunch and dinner one day last week due to a long court appearance. I have no complaints about the kitchen, nor the service of Spice Thai Cuisine. The space is all cool dark wood and deep red texture that took me far away from the courthouse for a peaceful interlude. The young server was gracious, engaging and had a high watt smile that made ordering a pleasure. I asked if this was truly a Thai house, and she assured me the owner and chef were legit. For lunch I had the Hot Jungle Special at heat level 4 (out of 7). The plate arrived loaded with fresh veggies and a mildly pepper/curry sauce that brought everything together nicely, but wasn't quite the inferno I was looking for. Still, it was totally enjoyable, and I used it as a measure should I chose to return for another round. That I returned for dinner was totally unexpected, unless you consider leaving a briefcase behind as an act of kismet. I had to return that evening to get it, and while there decided to sit for dinner. I supped on Pad Thai with Calamari and heat level 5. This was more like it! The meal arrived in a large ceramic plate with a built in pedestal. It looked beautiful. The spice level was excellent, and the Calamari was fresh and scored in a crosshatch pattern to expose max surface area. It was soft and pliant. The overall experience was delicious. I took enough home for another dinner. Spice Thai Cuisine is a very good restaurant, if not quite at the level of Aroi Thai or some of the other specialty houses in the area. No doubt, it could reach that apex with a little more time and imagination.

I went to Fez last night with eight of my galpals. The decor and ambience is very nice and the music was pleasant. I had high hopes for a good time out! I had been to other hookah restaurants (one in D.C whose name escapes me was top-notch, it was a real-live affair--with singers, belly dancers, and the patrons dancing in betxixt smoking hookahs) so my hopes were high. Service was attentive and on point. Our servers made sure our waters were never low, our alcohol was flowing (their wine selection was very small but nice), and that we were happy throughout our meal. We were one of the few patrons dining as others were just there for the hookah (it was about 9pm on a Friday night). The eight course meal was delicious (and a great deal at $25 pp plus tax and gratuities) while some courses were better than others. However, the time in between courses seemed to drag. My personal favorites were the whole chicken dish and the lamb and almonds dish. The chicken was flavorful and juicy and fell off the bones. For the eight of us, they gave us two chickens which was more than plenty! My vegetarian friend had the vegetarian courses different dishes like a falafal and a hummus dish in lieu of the meat dishes. I tasted the hummus and it was delish. There was a fruit course (just bananas, oranges, and apples) and a couscous dish that was unremarkable. I wore a borrowed Fez the whole evening after asking if it was culturally acceptable for me to wear it. Yup, I am a hot mess and I do things like that. So the Fez and hookah and chicken made my night. And of course, having a ridic time with my ladies. The bellydancer had "called out" so there was no live entertainment. Boo to that. The hookah was great and reasonably priced ($20 for hookah for three hours for four people). Definitely go for the experience...would have been 4 stars if there was a bellydancer as advertised.

I'm sure that this place is considered halfway decent by some people who have experienced fantastic bbq, but not authentic Thai food. The Pad Thai was extremely boring, with little or no taste. While I didn't have anything else off the menu, considering my review only as it pertains to Thai food, the rest of the noodles offered might be great.
Probably the best bahm mi I have ever had. Many snacks sold in the store as well (egg tarts, sugar cane drink etc). Highly recommend!

Back again for Numchok because it's my favourite and it's that good. Was going to try another place but decided not to because when you love something why change!! Ordered the salad rolls (vegan style), coconut soup, Tom yum soup, red tofu curry, jasmine and coconut rice and my guest ordered a spicy chicken dish. Incredible !! They keep their curries on a lamp to keep them warm. So appreciated. My guest loved their vegan beer also.

Good, somewhat spicy, filling, quick Indian food. We love coming here on weekends for the buffet (the tikka masala and the saag paneer will cure what ails you, whether it be a hangover or a cold). Lots of good veggie stuff, especially the potatoes and the chickpea curry. It's a little different each time we go, but if they have the deep-fried potatoes dipped in chickpea flour--yum! Sometimes the food is a bit cold, but always tasty.

Excellent Mediterranean restaurant in Ruskin. Owner was courteous and friendly. I had the chicken platter. The food was delicious. I will definitely come back and try other menu options in the future.

Wide variety of sweet and savoury items, which is a plus. Unfortunately the space is small as there's only about 3 tables, better to get your goodies to go as this cafe fills up quickly. The pastries are all beautiful and the ones we ordered tasted good. My group and I also tried some of the savoury items, they were just okay. Overall, if I'm in the area I might stop by to get some goodies to go but would not go out of my way to get some. The area can be pretty sketchy at times.

Cozy little BYOB with limited seating, so get there early. The food was great, I had the penang(sp?) curry and everyone else got the pad thai. The curry was the best I've ever had, the pad thai was excellent, but I've had better. We visited for dining days so we all got a desert too, all of them were excellent, especially the banana and chocolate spring roll. The prices on the menu were very cheap considering the portion size and quality. Would definitely recommend if you're in the area and you can go to dock street first and grab some beer for your meal.
Ya gotta check this place out!!! Awesome service and great food. Started with Arancini that was fabolous and moved on to the steak burger. I shall be back....
The duck noodle soup is oh so good. The Queen and I has absolutely the best Thai food in town.
I come here whenever I'm craving take-out Thai. I think it's better than some of the other options in the area. I've had a few of their noodles and entrees, and have no complaints about anything.

Best pho I have ever had. Just saying. I used to live In Manhattan.. And now I live in LA.. But this little pho place in Reno beats all the big name Vietnamese restaurants I have been to in both of those cities. And that's HUGE because pho is my favorite food so I have been to them all. I ate here so many times that the guy remembered my order and he'd always be like.. Same thing?! When I walk in. It's awesome. I approve.

Called ahead for carry out. Very nice place. Food was ready on time and was packed well. I had vegan spring rolls with vegan pad thai. Both were excellent. My dad had the chicken pad thai and was also excellent. He also tried a vegan spring roll and loved it. Will definitely be coming back! Highly recommended.

Thanks yelpers for introducing this vietnamese restaurant to us. I would never discover this place and from the outside appearance, it didn't look very appealing as it's located nearby other shops, I think like nail salons... I order broken rice with grilled pork chop, meat patty and shredded pork, fried egg, and pickled carrots and veggies. It was yummy! The service was nice. We went on Sunday for 7pm dinner and soon after arrival, the place got packed so I suggest come on early if you want a table. Otherwise, order for take out.

Horrible Customer Service .. Placed an online order and after we placed the order,we called an was told 20 min.. Oh and no soup because the cook had not come yet ( it was 1pm) when we got there was told oh it will be 45 min to an HOUR because there were several other orders that he did not know about. He said he canceled our orders but still charged our card!
One of the best Carribean place in town. Great and friendly staff, and more importantly, delicious food. Jerk chicken is my favorite, but everything else is delicious
Great ph, good egg rolls, and awesome service. I'll definitely be back - recommended for anyone who likes ph.

So I lost count on how many times I have been to this place.Everytime I have came here I've always had a great experience.The food is freakin' delicious!! Also, at a decent price compared to other places in town.A must try!!!

I tried this restaurant twice. Once for lunch, once for dinner. The lunch special was a good price, but the soup included wasn't Tom Yum Soup. The soup included was gross. It looked like broth with some green leefy vegetable floating in it. And the table cloth was stained and dirty. That should have been our first indication. For dinner, we ordered a few dishes. A red curry, a beef salad, and a squid dish, along with Tom Yum Soup. The soup was ok, but not the exact right flavor it's supposed to be, and the pieces of lemongrass in the soup were inedible. The other dishes were ok, but again not the exact taste that I have come to love at Thai restaurants. If you live in the area, I would say stick with Nadia Thai or Thai Orchid. Don't even bother with this restaurant, it's not worth it.
I went down a wrong street and found it.. It's kinda hidden I thought it was a karate school lol.. The food was really good.. Roti was awesome and tom yom noodle soup was also really good

Quite simply, the middle eastern gyro with feta and tabouli is the best gyro I've ever had in my entire life and it takes every ounce of my being not to order it every time. Bonus points because the chef is always pleasant and you can tell he takes great pride in his cookie. Always have to get the pistachio baklava as well

After reading the glowing reviews, I came here for a late lunch with a co-worker while we were in Wilmington for a meeting. I ordered French Onion soup ( standard pub fare right?) and a Beet and Goat Cheese Salad. The onion soup had absolutely no flavor at all, and it looked like they took a pearl onion and a piece of bread, covered it with broth, and then microwaved a piece of cheese across the top. Awful. But it gets worse. The salad looked like wilted lettuce and orange sections on a plate smeared with pink frosting! The beets were yellow and unrecognizable. The pink stuff turned out to be the dressing, made with what tasted like rancid goat cheese. It was so gross I had to spit it out! The only reason I am giving this place two stars is because the waitress was pleasant enough and my co-worker didn't spit out his burger. No more lunches in Wilmington for me

Orginally my first visit did not go so smooth and I wrote a review regarding that but since every time I've gone its been great. I try to go once a week now. Took the whole family for dinner one saturday evening. My 4 year old got the chicken fingers and loved them and its the first time ive seen him eat unbreaded chicken. My steak kabobs were better than most steaks Ive gotten in steak houses. Everything is great here. I thinks its much better than most of the restaurants in the complex. No alcohol here though and cafeteria style but its ten times better than PF changs and olive garden.

I love their fried avocado appetizers, so amazing. For the entree, I had the Cuban bowl which was average. My friends enjoyed their entrees as well. The portions are good sizes. I'm not crazy about the decor or the vibe here, but maybe because we were seated in the back near the kitchen. It also gets quite loud. However, the food and service was very nice.

After seeing all the good reviews I thought this would be a good place to go. There was no sign out front I thought it was closed down. They were open, the place is ripped up, the walls have half the paper ripped off and just glue on the wall exposed. Now let's get to the food. The chicken was dry like jerky. The rice had no flavor. This was not what expected. The steak was cooked fine but lacking in flavor. It was overall a disappointment. Drinks were in a can and not very cold. They would be better being in a food truck I would not have been so disappointed. They get two stars because the lady was very nice in there. Would not recommend.
Very good dinner.. The restaurant is beautifully decorated and has a quiet atmosphere. The food was delicious, I loved the Crab Ragoon. The pad thai and fried rice were also very good.

Super good Greek/ Leb .An insane amount of food for the money on the Combo Schwarma and chicken platter. Babaganou was perfect. We ordered food for four but ended up with enough for six. We were worried that dining at An odd time would yield bad service of subpar food BUT that was not the case. We will be back!

I came here when traveling for work. I'm a big fan of Mediterranean food and I've been to a few other places like this, so I decided to give it a shot. You get to choose between a bowl and a pita, pick a base, meat, and toppings. I got a hummus bowl without chicken shawarma, all of the toppings (cucumber salad, onions, pickles, and cabbage), and amba sauce. I enjoyed it, but the chicken was lacking flavor compared to other chicken shawarma I've had. I really liked the addition of the sauce. I thought the food was good overall, but compared to other build your own Mediterranean places, the selection was very limited. There were only two protein choices (chicken and falafel) and 4 toppings. Usually there are at least 4-5 protein choices and 10-15 toppings. I would consider coming back here again next time I'm in the area, but I would really like to see them expand their selection.

I love Bamboo House. I always get the vegetarian options (which they have a lot of compared to other restaurants) which come with yummy spicy or tangy sauces. The only reason I docked them a star is because of inconsistencies in their vegetables. some days they seem less fresh than others. But overall, very good.

This is an amazing little place located inside of the New Castle Farmers market. After walking the whole circle around the market and finally locating the store, i would like to help fellow yelpers by informing them to enter at the entrance #4 to reach this joint. We entered from entrance #6 but went left towards the other side instead of taking right towards the shop! To tell you frankly, we were hungry already and the detour did not help, lol! So we ordered dahi puri, papri chaat, mix fresh lime soda, uttapam, vada pav, pav bhaji and usal pav. The dahi puris were pretty delicious for Delaware standards! I have had some incredible chaat in Dallas, NJ, NY and the bay area but had no expectations to find this yummy chat here in Delaware.. oh I am so happy they opened shop! The papri chaat was also very delicious, made with good amount of papri, chutneys and onions. They did not skimp on the ingredients and the dish was the best i have had in US! Many places mess up papri chaat by pouring too much yogurt or too much chutneys, but they did no such thing. The usal pav was very spicy, but i loved it. The uttapam was also well made and filling. The mix fresh lime soda was made well and delicious. The vada pav was also very delicious, with the right amount of spices. Pav bhaji was not too great but just decent - more like a 3/5 dish. We also had a pista kulfi - which was okay... nothing exclusive. Will definitely repeat and try other items.

The Donner box ;) french fries child with lamb and chicken tzatziki sauce and I always add feta cheese to the top. filling!!! This place is downtown during the day it's kid friendly but at night it's a great place to go grab something to eat specially if you're hanging out by the bar scene...
Tom Yum soup horrible and from can concentrate. Thai curry is acceptable with fresh vegetables.

Today was our first time here ,we were greeted right away very nice man named Steven the restaurant is bigger than it looks and it absolutely beautiful in there , food was super ,super good I had the chicken curry my hubby had beef Vanderloo, the chips and dips we got we incredible melt in mouth wake your taste buds up,the garlic bread was to die for , it's really good food, it's very filling , it's served in a way that you can share your food with everyone at the table or keep it to yourself, it's nice, Steve was an excellent host /server he was great at answering our questions , he kept our cups full and made us feel very welcomed, will be going back again for sure , we heard the buffet on Sunday might not be big but extremely good food ,
When inside of your samosas are frozen and the crust is warm in more than 1 visits, u should say goodbye to such a place. Just sharing my experience
Went here on a Saturday night and the restaurant was about half full. Service was friendly and pretty quick. Prices were reasonable and food was good. Would definitely go back!
Drunken noodles and pad cashew are awesome. Really enjoyed it a lot. Dining at Erawan for lunch was a great feeling because they have this combo offer.
place was half full, ordered Pad Thai and Red Curry. food arrived quick and was very good. However, service was terrible. Had to go to ask for tea refills..twice. Place is clean and inviting.
Grilled stuffed grape leaves and fried spring rolls are excellent. Pho Tai is as good as any restaurant in Philadelphia. Give it a try yourself..very affordable.
Excellent food. Very nice, friendly staff. The red curry chicken was delicious. The orange chicken had a fresh citrus taste with just the right amount of sweet and savory.

I went for lunch with a friend and plan to go back with my husband for dinner.... We shared an array of appetizers that were some of the best I have ever had. The menu is HUGE and the noodle dishes were tried were fantastic! It is BYOB and they offer take out as well!

The food was fantastic! We will go back again for the food alone. We split a salad and each had a gyro. Again food we top notch! The people working there?? Ummmm do you like zombies or anti social people? Then this is your place. We had never been there. The counter girl never greeted us nor did anyone in the shop. I was expecting, Hi how are you, have you ever been here before? No, well here is our menu glued to the counter. The people who made the food, you think they would have walked it the 10 feet to the table we were at? Nope shouted #28. No thanks enjoy your food nothing! The ambiance is a hole in the wall but fun! You clearly go here for the food!

Misleading a bit, it is not a tapas bar. But great food non the less. Pretty loud so don't bring the hard of hearing. The fish tacos were delicious as well as the cheese platter. I suggest going all out on appetizers cause it's a great variety. Good selection if drinks and the cocktails I did see looked great although that's not really my thing. Live music thurs-sat I believe. All in all cool spot, great food, good drinks and perfect location.

This tiny BYO is worth the trek over the Walt Whit. The service is astounding and the food leaves you wanting more the minute you leave the restaurant. The menu is divided into the traditional three courses - salad, appetizer, entree (of course, all of this is in proper Italian on the menu). While they recommend that you order one item from each section, you can do whatever pleases you. We ordered a variety of dishes and all were amazing. However, do yourself a favor and definitely order the gnocchi. It melted in my mouth and made me sad I had only ordered a half portion. Each course was paced nicely and the bread they give the table is to die for. I could have made a meal on that alone. Bring a few friends, a few bottles of wine and be prepared to put this restaurant on your list of favorites. Can't wait to go back!

What a delightful discovery right in our backyard! This Thai food is some of the best that we have ever had! Everything is fresh with minimal overpowering sauces, crisp veggies, tender chicken and all spiced just right. Their Tom Ka Gai soup is a celebration of tangy and sweet flavors with just the right amount of heat. Pad Thai is another favorite and it was perfect. Portions are generous and the service was prompt and friendly. We will be returning often.

I am sorry, I am a HUGE fan of the original India Sizzling, but its sequel was a tremendous disappointment. Their Chicken 65 was mostly bone, it contained virtually no edible meat. I ordered their Tandoori Mixed Grill as well and, due to my own restrictions, I emphasized that it be all chicken. My server said it would be 100% chicken with no other meat. When I received it, one of the items had a funny flavor and texture, and I later was eventually told after the waiter tried to deny it that it was fish. He refused to do anything about it until I demanded at least a discount for the trouble and the inedible Chicken 65 at which he took 10% off the bill. I will say though that the Chicken Malai Kebab was delicious, which is why I am allowing for 2 stars instead of 1, but given that they cannot get orders correct and one of my dishes was entirely inedible, this is not enough to return. I am hugely disappointed, and there certainly are far better Indian restaurants to be enjoyed in Indianapolis. Check out Mumbai Grill instead.

I have eaten Thai food in big cities around the world, and Phoenixville's Thai Place measures up shockingly well. The location is an unassuming strip mall, and the interior is a little kitschy, but the service is excellent, and the food is amazing. I'm not usually one to go for boring old Pad Thai, but it is divine here. I often get duck panang, or the peanut-y Praram Rong Song, but you can pretty much choose something randomly and get a delicious result. Great choice for take-out as well. Not as dirt-cheap as some thai places can be, but that's probably a good sign.

Ignore the outdated decor, the large tacky statue outside, and the servers who are all texting during their downtime, and the pack of cigarettes hidden behind a potted plant. The food and friendly service carry The Pearl a long way. My husband and I got to the restaurant just after 4pm (strange time, I know) when the doors first opened, and to our surprise, there's an early bird menu, which offers about 5 different dishes, which rotate week-to-week, and a soup or salad for just $10! You have to be seated before 5:45 in order to order from this menu. Our server, who was Moroccan himself recommended the chicken tagine, (which was on the early bird) and the lamb tagine, which was not. (Note: On it's own, the tagines cost about $20, so obviously the early bird special is the way to go!) We weren't disappointed with the tagines. Both came with nicely cooked couscous and veggies, and the meats were tender and well seasoned, but not overly salty or oil-laden. We left feeling satisfied and happy. Can't wait to try this place out again!
My absolute fave Indian restaurant! There Goan Curry shrimp is ALWAYS delicious! Their Butter chicken is quite good as well. I love their rosemary naan. It is BYOB.

I would say this could be the best new restaurant addition to downtown saint petersburgs growing treasure of eateries. Our server was excellent and our foods was even better. That along with great company made for a great experience and evening. Also the decor really enhanced the atmosphere.

This place has been cited for lots of health code violations. The Health Department found hundreds of live roaches here in December 2017. Not sure if it's been shut down yet or not. If not, please be aware of the health code issues.

Had the crab rangoon appetizer, which I have never had before and they were very good. For dinner, I had the Pad Eee Eew with chicken. Got it Hot (NOT Thai hot, thank goodness). I love hot food, and the Hot was just right. Noodles were great, the brocolli was fresh and crispy and cooked perfectly.

Impressed! First time here. Loved the ambiance, the wine pours :), the vast menu, delicious meals (red curry, Tom yum, and crab fried rice). All were delicious. A great experience and we will be back soon!

Pretty good hole in the wall, tried the lunch biryani after I stumbled upon the place. Seems authentic not sure if they are South Indian...interesting specials mention "Ceylon Parotta" Lots of interesting menu items too...will have to come back for more. Liked the lamb biryani.

Grabbed dinner here recently with my sister. Pretty decent pho place in the Fairmount area. We ordered the fresh vegetarian spring rolls for appetizer. For the pho we both got medium sizes and it was just the right amount and left us full! It had plenty of noodles and tasty broth. I got the vegetarian pho and it had a generous amount of veggies and tofu. Great bang for your buck here. Definitely worth a stop here for some pho on a cold night.

First, if you are expecting regular Phooket menu, don't. This place is not owned by the same people as Nashville and Madison. Similar but different menu items. No lemongrass chicken . Which is why I went last night. I did have the basil with beef and chicken. I ordered a 7 spicy to let them know I'm serious about spice. They obliged! Nice and ! Also had the garden rolls. Absence of cilantro was noticeable but the peanut sauce was . Food was good. Service was excellent and friendly. Go... Eat and tell others. They were not busy at all for a Sat night and could use a boost.

I LOVE THIS PLACE. I know the family who owns it. The husband gets up at 5:30 every morning to go bake the bread fresh. Yes, there are flies. Yes, they get busy. Yes, it's a little different. But, if you take this place for what it's worth it's a gem in the rough. The Phuh (f-UH) soup is the most delicious, I also recommend the bbq beef, teriyaki chicken or bbq chicken baguette sandwiches. DO NOT TRY THE SANDWICHES IF YOU DO NOT LIKE CILANTRO. Trust. My very favorite thing on the menu is their smoothies/frappacinos. They are all available to have boba (tapioca pearls) added. My FAV is the mocha with boba, but the strawberry banana and tarot (tare-oh) smoothies with boba are also absolutely delicious. This place is a must-try!
Amazing service. I believe he was the owner but he's so kind and quick. Really enjoyed my lunch today. The food is big portions.
Try the Saturday buffet....it costs one more dollar but there are some premiere options like the lavish paneer masala.
Cute & quaint! Don't underestimate the place by the location. The food is amazing. Chicken with peanut sauce is the best. Hidden gem in Spring Hill! Ask for thai spicy for an extra authentic taste.

My fiancè and i eat here at least once a week but usually twice, we eat in and get it delivered. The food and service is always great when we eat in, never have any complaints. Delivery is hit and miss food wise. The actual delivery its self is always very unorganized if you pay with a card the delivery person has to call in and give your card number over the phone to someone at the restaurant. If you pay cash and need change i would make sure they know you will need change when you order it because the delivery driver doesnt carry it with them. overall we love this place even with its quirks.

Not tooo bad! I came here with my dad yesterday & was surprised on how great the food was. The cheesesteak sandwich was a bit tooo salty for me, but the bread was delish! The staff were very accommodating to my weird dietary needs. Initially, I ordered a chicken noodle soup with my sandwich, but was informed by one of the employees that the soup had dairy in it. So, I switched to a cucumber & carrot salad with an Asian vinaigrette. Yummy! I was happy that they could make a "salad" without the usual leafy greens. My dad ordered a pad thai & looked partly authentic. Where's the crushed peanuts & sides of sugar & crushed dried chillies? The only problem is that I wished I could enter this place from inside the mall in addition to entering from outside like Qdoba. It is a bit pricey as previous reviews stated. But, the taste & service is worth the money. I like how they offer 2 different meal sizes (small & large).

I've been a regular at Jasmine Thai Restaurant in Brandon, Fl for several years. Although located in a strip mall, this restaurant is charming, beautifully decorated and very clean. It's a nice quiet atmosphere where you can actually have a conversation without the need to yell over background music or noise. Over the years, I've tried many menu items and liked just about everything. I really recommend their WonTon soup and Thai Steamed Dumplings. I've enjoy their Pad Thai, fish dishes, and other rice and noodle dishes. Everything is fresh, made to order and prepared as requested. If something isn't right, they make it right - this is a family running this restaurant and they care about their customers and their business. The waitresses, dressed in traditional Thai garments are professional, friendly and efficient and knowledgeable about menu items. .

First off all let me start with that it took forever for a server to come take out drink orders & food! We waited there for almost half an hour. Had to get up and get someone's attention. Second our food took forever to get out the other customers that got there after us got their food way before our and their drinks too. Server wasn't that attentive. Other then that food was delicious. I would go there on a not so busy day.
Love the pho here!!! Fast service and larger then normal pho servings. I ordered take out from them once, it was okay. I would recommend eating in!

Decent Middle Eastern food located in a strip mall in a former Chinese restaurant. The chicken shawarma and lamb were good for the entree plates. The menu specifically makes note that all of their meats are halal and there is also a nearby halal meat shop. Overall it is a decent spot for a quick meal but it isn't my favorite Middle Eastern place in the area and I find for a similar price I get a bit more food at other places.

Wow.. Let me start off by saying that this restaurant is entirely different than the old "Al-Sham" that used to be here pre July 2017. It just kept the name. This new restaurant cook everything like they did in the middle east over thousands of years ago. Over open charcoal grill. I've been to fine dining Mediterranean restaurants across the United States and nothing has flavor like this. This place could be in downtown New York at 5x the price and it would be justifiable. I've eaten here many times now and I had to leave a review. If anyone reading this likes Mediterranean food, you won't find a dish served better than this nationwide. I am very critical when I go out and eat as you can see from over a hundred reviews I've left on restaurants, only a handful get 5-stars. This one deserves 6.
Kodos to a great staff and a fabulous meal. Sea bass was perfection and my other tastings were all above expectation. Kristin was great. Appreciated the welcome feeling as a business traveler.

Thai and tacos are my two favorite things in the world. Finding good Thai and tacos on the east coast is much harder than most think. Thank you China town for this gem. + never usually busy + great for groups + excellent coconut milk soup + amazing curries + amazing avocado duck dish + decent service + byob (can't remember if any 'bottle open' fee) + usually have groupon deals + not cash only! My only downside is, more than once, we have made reservations for larger parties that they didn't have scheduled. But, within usually minutes a table is set up/combined to accommodate us. However, just kind of annoying to make reservations to walk in staring at confused servers.

It it wasn't for a good friend who grew up in the area, I probably would have kept driving by the this place. It's definitely nothing special on the outside, but as I've learned time and time again, you should never judge a book by its cover. Inside this was probably some of the best food I've had in Tampa. The owners barely speak english, but I'll take that as a good sign this place is as authentic as you can get. I highly recommend the spring rolls, coconut soup, red curry, and the pad thai. The pad thai was amazing - not too peanut buttery, with just the right around of fried egg and chicken. Order it Thai hot, trust me.

I ordered pernil and arroz con abichuelas- now there, I'm Hispanic and have eaten this countless times before so I can say while it was tasty, it still wasn't quite all that. The rice and beans was a bit to plain for me and a bit overcooked. The pernil was decent. Now what did make me a happy guest was the coquito- ordered two. I was in love; it was too yummy! I tried my friend's mofongo and it was moist and flavorful, had I known, I would have ordered this instead.

Went here for lunch and for dinner, and I think it's a winner. Ok, bad rhyme aside, the first thing that jumped out, even as they were working on getting this place ready for business, was how much effort they put into decorating. It really looks nice. The waitstaff was very friendly and went out of their way to serve us. As far as food, the lunch menu is a bit different from the dinner menu. I went with one of the kebab plates, all of which are listed at around $10. It came with 4 pieces of meat, of varying sizes, along with Afghan rice, and was pretty good. Lunch reminded me a little of Sahara Grill, which is my go-to Middle Eastern restaurant. The dinner menu is more varied and elaborate... and more expensive. I got the Qablee Palaw (also on lunch menu for a bit cheaper, and not much smaller, if at all), which consists of cubes of meat, usually lamb, along with shaved carrots and raisins, on a bed of Afghan rice. I've had this dish at a couple other Afghan restaurants, one in Philly and another elsewhere, and I must say this was the best of the three. Not too oily, and the ingredients tasted fresh (the opposite was my complaint about the other two places I tried). Both meals were accompanied by a small salad and a basket of bread. For dinner we also ordered the kidney beans with Afghan rice, and an eggplant based appetizer. The small samples I tried of both were very good. The food didn't necessarily come out fast either time, but was certainly within the realm of what I would consider acceptable. Subsequent visits have varied as far as speed of service. It seems like they tend to forget about you if it's a slow day. This place is definitely worth trying, as long as you aren't in a hurry. I wish them well, and hope they stick around at that corner.
There's little more satisfying than finding a little hole-in-the-wall where the food is outstanding. This is that place. Greart Pakistani/Indian food made to order...hidden behind Nifty Fifty.

I always feel so conflicted when I write a review for a place with a really friendly waiter. The guy that I have often seen working here is very friendly and very attentive. The food quality here is what cause my internal conflict. I ordered the ban mi sandwich combo (it comes with any drink on their milk tea menu or a fountain drink). They offer chicken, pork, and beef. I opted for the chicken. One of the parts of a ban mi that can make or break it the most if the french roll; in this case they used day-old bread (at least a day, probably more) it was hard from age, not from being toasted. The chicken was really (visibly) dry and probably reheated. The toppings were on the older side, with the jalapeño being visibly dry from being sliced likely days ahead of time. I ended up having to bathe the meat in sriracha, hoisin, and chili paste since it didn't have much of a flavor of its own. I got the taro milk tea; it was decent but grainy at the end. They finally got better lychee jelly with a more pleasant texture than what they used to sell so I was glad about that. My partner got the pho and it contained an assortment of noticeably bad cuts of meat (when was served the tough, inedible type of tendons that showed their meat was clearly not trimmed). They also served her basil that was soggy and brown, literally expired already. On top of it all, their pho is overpriced, a small bowl, and the broth is very bland. The broth should be the most important focus and they neglected making it taste like something. You can get a larger bowl of better pho at any of the pho restaurants in the goleta area (I've tried them all multiple times each to make sure) Overall don't recommend this place.
My go-to Pho place. Just sat down and said "water and a large #60." So tasty and a casual enough place that I don't feel weird sitting by myself for lunch/dinner.

This is my go-to spot to meet up with one of my closest friends. I never feel rushed. Most recently, my friend and I met up on a Friday night and meandered over a meal for an hour and a half. The food is quite reasonable and even the less spicy options are very flavorful. I've had the pad thai here which is excellent, but my normal order is the vegetarian lover. That dish is packed with vegetables, fried tofu and comes with a very tasty sauce and a side of Thai white rice. My friend ordered the Buddha dumplings to start and a noodle dish for her main entree. Her father owned a Chinese restaurant for years, and he still cooks for her at home, so she's very picky when it comes to Asian dishes. She's always happy to meet me at Thai Orchid which speaks highly of the food here.

This is one of my favorite downtown lunch spots, especially if I'm looking for something quick and easy. It's not much for decor or ambience, that's for sure, but they have a great Meditteranean Chop Salad for lunch that's delicious and a great deal. For about $7 you get the salad with gyro meat and hummus and pita bread. All the food I've had here is consistently good which is probably why I'm in here so often. If you like pitas this is the place for you.

Easily one of the best Mediterranean restaurants in the south Davidson/Williamson county area. We moved to Nashville about two years ago and have been looking for a good Mediterranean restaurant. We have found plenty of restaurants that pile on the food but the quality is average as the food does not feel fresh. Gave this place a try on a whim while driving down Nolensville Road and have been back at least once a month since. You can tell they take great of ownership in their food quality and service. From what I understand, they make many items from scratch including the hummus and some of the desserts. We have had the gyro, chicken and falafel and it is the freshest we have had in some time. With the gyro pockets, the meat in tender and flavorful and melts in your mouth. In many Mediterranean places, it feels like the gyro meat has been sitting under a heat lamp for days. In the past, I was indifferent about falafel but I have grown to love falafel because of how the Blue Fig makes their falafel. The falafel pockets are enough for a meat lover, like myself, to bypass meat for at least one meal. Our service experience has never been anything short of great. We have eaten in the restaurant and done carryout over the past couple of months. They are appreciative of their customers and take great pride in making sure your order is correct and to your liking. We have been there with small children and they will bend over backward to make sure the picky little ones are doing okay. I have given up going to any of the other Mediterranean places in the area and will drive a little farther when needed to get the food here.

This was the worst Jamaican food I've ever had, start to finish! The plantain were thin and bone dry. The peas and rice had almost no peas (actually, just a few kidney beans). The rice was taste-less and bland. The jerk chicken was over-cooked and dry. The food tasted as thouh it had been sitting in those warming pans for more than a few days. After reading other reviews, I was stunned at how bad the for was.
Clean, cute and friendly! Bahn mi was large, tasty and reasonably priced. Thai tea was brewed fresh and VERY good! So glad to have a place like this not far from us. We'll be back!

Lunch takes four hours here -- 30 minutes to eat, three hours and 30 minutes to recover from the food coma. But, if you are looking for a classic American Indian lunch buffet near Penn, this is the place to go. While not inspired, the food is tasty and plentiful. I will be back.

You need to get in here. Lamb was cooked perfectly. Everything is really good. Should be packed on a Friday night and we were the only ones here. Get in and enjoy before they can't make it. Bed let M E in town!
I've been waiting for a Bambu to come to South Jersey. The bubble tea was very good. My favorite is the #6 Vietnamese Che.

This is the best Indian food I've had so far in Tampa Bay. The ambiance is nice and clean. I've dined here several times and each time the waitstaff are friendly and efficient. They have a buffet during lunchtime which is excellent and all the menu entrees I've had here are also delicious. Highly recommend.

This is a great place to study, read, drink, relax or catch up with a friend. There's plenty of comfortable seating, and it never gets too loud or too quiet here. While you're here, I would highly recommend the Ginger Chai Latte for a warm, spicy treat. They also have a gorgeous display of decadent cakes, including gluten free options. I had a slice of the Red Velvet Cake, and I felt complete.

This was our first time at Zoe's kitchen. I have to say we were all impressed. I had driven by a few times and didn't know what to expect. We are restaurant owners ourselves so we tend to be more observant of all the details. I got the steak kabobs and they were cooked perfectly. My wife got the chicken kabobs and they were equally as good. We each get tsaziki and greek salad for our sides. Again, all was very good. We finished off with a big chocolate chip cookie that was excellent. The service was friendly, the restaurant was clean and the food was good. We will be back Mike

I really want to like this restaurant - I really, really do. I've ate here many times, however I get really mad sometimes because they screw up my order or give me rice instead of fried noodles. I don't think I've ever gotten my chow mien the right order. This is a family run chinese fast food place, it's really cheap and they give great discounts on bulk orders. It's great for fast family dining and lots of other options. I don't have an issue with the taste, or portion sizes. I honestly really want to like this restaurant, but they've screwed up my order 3 times in a row. Not kidding! I even ask to not skip the noodles but they give me rice instead, I ask why? and they say "it's what we have" despite the description says fried noodles. I would give this place 4 stars if I didn't have issues with my ordering. Tampa doesn't really have many options for Asian food, maybe Pei Wei down the street. Overall if you want decent chinese food, Top China is good.

Went to lunch for this place, a bit to hard to see this place from the road. We had veggie lunch thali and the Bollywood dosa. The food tasted great. Rasam, sambar and the curries in the thali tasted just home like. Dosa was also good, will visit this place again.
This restaurant simply blew me away. Amazing service, AMAZING food, very great price, and the vibe is great!!! Thanks so much!

Bryce is EVERYTHING! I had the best wine experience in my life. Based on the highly informed recommendations from Bryce, I tried the PlumpJack cab and it literally changed my life. Enjoying his company is worth every cent. The food was also fantastic. Did I mention the apple wood smoked Manhattan?

Excellent food. The fish is seasoned and fried to perfection. They give you generous portions. The greens are awesome. The mac and cheese is awesome as well and the cabbage. The hot sauce is almost made for the greens and fish not too hot just right . This is my go to food truck. I usually get a large fish platter that my fiance and I share. There is enough for the both of us to be satisfied and stuffed and always food left over to where we can both eat from it again!

Putting food aside, I think an important distinction to make is that Shere-E-Punjab has introduced Indian food to many people in Drexel Hill (or has at least made it something that they eat more often). Before it opened in Drexel Hill, the closest Indian restaurants were in Media and University City. Given this exposure to people generally unfamiliar with Indian food, I am happy to say that Shere-E-Punjab's food is very good. Some Indian people I know have said the food is not the best. I think the main reason for this sentiment is that many recipes are Americanized. The samosas, while good, are seasoned on the outside the same way a curly fry would be. I had dum aloo (potatoes in tomato sauce) here for the first time and really liked it. When I told some of my Indian friends about it, they were surprised to find out that the potatoes were stuffed with cheese, saying that this was an Americanized version. In this case, I actually don't think that's a bad thing. Considering most people in this area aren't hardcore Indian food eaters, it's fine to make dishes slightly different so that people will enjoy it. It's better than making completely authentic dishes and reducing the amount of people who are exposed to Indian food! Most dishes come with rice, and Shere-E-Punjab rice is some of the best I have ever had. Whatever seasoning they use, it's great! The lunch buffet is also great. Occasionally they even have dinner buffets. Last Christmas Eve they had a special dinner buffet and it was delicious. It was nice to see the place packed, as most of the time it's relatively empty. In terms of pricing, Shere-E-Punjab is pretty average for comparable Indian restaurants. I've been to cheaper ones, but I've also been to more expensive ones. The interior is beautiful, the service is friendly, and the food is very good, so there really isn't anything to complain about. I'm glad that Drexel Hill is diversifying its restaurant scene!
Great food. The buffet has good fresh choices. It's authentic and affordable. A must try.

Ordered carry out this afternoon and the order was promptly ready within 10 minutes. They have a really broad menu and finally settled on Yum salad with beef and Pad See Ewe with pork - both medium high heat. The Yum salad had a very tasty refreshing dressing with subtle heat. The Pad See Ewe was one of the best Thai noodle dishes we've had. The noodles were perfectly cooked and the sauce was the right combo of sweet and spicy. Portions were large and prices reasonable. Will definitely add this place to our carry out rotation and explore more of the menu!

Now that we have moved here and found an apartment just a couple of blocks away, d'Mitris is our default go to place for dinner. Food is consistently good. Service is friendly and efficient. It can get crowded and loud on the weekends. Solid four star for sure.

I had high expectations for Cucina Zapata given the stellar Yelp reviews as well as the recommendations I've gotten from my friends. I feel weird being the odd one out with an average rating, but I really can't give it anything more. I came here at about 1 pm, and apparently the line was much shorter than usual. Even though we were at the front of the line, it was hard to get the dude to take my order, which was annoying. Eventually, he took my order, and I decided to get the Cap'n Crunch Tilapia Burrito, since i have heard good things. Honestly, I wasn't raving about the burrito. It was pretty good, but I wasn't like DAMNNNN, ya know? It just seemed like a fish burrito with sriracha and some vegetables in it to me. Maybe they had a bad day or something with my burrito. I don't know. I will probably try this again soon, and maybe I'll try the tea and the tacos next time. Maybe I'll feel it next time!

Poor quality food. The pizza was too doughy, I think mine was actually slightly raw. Not fun too eat. The tabouleh was way too lemony. The fries were pre-made freezer fries, i.e. not from freshly cut potatoes. I've been here three times now and it is always a disappointment. They are pretending to be a slightly fancy restaurant, but the quality of the food does not support this. The staff is great though.

I live far away from Bitar's in West Philadelphia, but I have to come here every so often because they have the best price on the best feta cheese. They sell the Bulgarian kind in two- and three-pound lots for something like $6 a pound. Then I always pick up a bag of pita, which is baked fresh every day. My favorite menu item is no longer there: it's a little snack called a bitza, which is a round flat bread grilled with little bits of tomato, cheese, and sumac on it. The chicken sandwich is good though. And if aliens landed and demanded that I bring them seven different varieties of mamool (Lebanese filled cookies) I would not know where else to go. Update 2009-09-01: Went by there last Saturday. Here are some other things they carry: Dried fava beans. Tahini. Fig marmalade. Bulgur wheat in three different sizes. Lebanese pastry. Olives. Update 2016-11-30: Bitar's is still great, but I don't visit as often as I used to because I'm not nearby and because I learned that Makkah Market in West Philadelphia is an equally good source of feta and pita.

I'm a man who likes spice. Whether it be spice in food, in a beer, in coffee, or in life. I like spice. Whether it be from a red chile, or in the simple form of salt and pepper. Being quite a spicy person, Pho is a natural gravitation for me. In my small hometown of Columbus, IN there is no Vietnamese food to be had. When I moved to Indy, Vietnamese was among one of the first ethnic foods I longed to enjoy. I tried one or two and settled on Sizzling Wok as my go-to spot. First off, it's really close to me which is an enormous plus. Second, the food and atmosphere are really nice. When you walk in you'll realize it's not tackily decorated and there are a few articles posted along the wall near the register which are praising the food served here. The first time I went there I ordered the Goi Cuon (Vietnamese spring rolls) and the rare pho. Both were very good. Spring rolls were nicely rolled, filled with fresh bean sprouts, and were served with a nice spicy plum peanut sauce. Pho was excellent. I've had some Pho which was obviously laced with a ton of MSG which I am very sensitive to. This Pho was laced with lovely spices, plenty of noodles and beef. Served with the obligatory "salad" which I added throughout the bowl. Overall this place rocks. After going there 2 or 3 times, the waitress already new my order by heart. I'd walk in, she'd come over and recite my order and I would nod enthusiastically, and minutes later I'd be downing spring rolls and slurping pho. Needless to say, my order hasn't changed much since the first time I went there. Goi Cuon and Rare Pho, some hoisin sauce and plenty of Sriracha with a generous spoonful of red chile sauce will satisfy the urges of any spice fiend like myself.

To start off, we had shrimp springrolls. YUM! The dipping sauce was good too! The Pho is your average Pho. It isn't anything spectacular, but it is tastes good when you are having a craving. The other dish we ordered was lemon grass chicken. This was not what I am used to. It was heavy on the red and green bell peppers and not heavy on the lemon grass flavor. I was a little let down by that dish, but am willing to go back and try another dish sometime. The interior of the restaurant is nothing fancy but it is relaxing and quiet. All that is needed, right?!

Came for dinner twice. The server is very friendly though could use another when it gets a little busier. Food was great on both occasions. I recommend the appetizer sampler, queen's honey drink, and the Ethiopian. Dining area and bathrooms are clean.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Excellent place to have a wonderful indian meal. Beer selection is solid; however, the beer menu is generally not accurate, so ask the staff. Food is delicious. Nann is so delicious. I typically get a curry. The food is cooked on order, so sit back, relax, enjoy the bollywood flick playing and chill. If in a hurry, go elsewhere. Good place for vegan and/or vegetarian folk.

So we went to Jamaican Jerk Hut last night. Now, this place has gotten some hype from my friends so I went in with some high expectations... First things first: It took a good while for the waiter to come and take our order. When he got there though, he was really attentive and quite friendly. We all liked him. Second: Orders taken and we are chillin. The outdoor grassy seating was tops. We had a big table full of people, something like 10 or 13 heads or something. Waiter dude comes out with two heaping plates of awesome veggie, chicken, and beef patties. ON THE HOUSE!!!1111!1 Rock. So Rock. Third: The foods come out. It took a while, but we totally didn't mind. This place oozes ambiance and the Jamaican patties certainly pacified us. Anyway, back to the food. Things I tried - Jerk Chicken Roti - Delicious. Seriously, this thing is HUGE. Tasted great. A challenge to eat without getting your hands dirty so get over it. Jerk Red Snapper - A little bit dry, a lot a bit flavorful. Seriously, I wish it were a little "juicier", but it came on a bed of snauce and there was so much flavor in it I got over it. Spicy Jerk Chicken Salad - WOWOWOWOWOW!!! This is a cold salad that has enough heat in it to melt an ice cap. It was amazing. Veggie Pattie - Yum. Reminded me of a pikora Chicken Pattie - Yum again. Beef Pattie - Yum. Less greasy than the ones you get from the chicken shops around the city, and the dough taste fresh. Now, my experience here was great. I loved the service, even if it was a tad slow. I enjoyed everything I tried too. BUT. Yes, there is a but.... A Roti is basically a Jamaican burrito. Why, oh why, would you put meat still on the bone in a burrito? I must of crunched 1000 little shards of chicken bone. I got over it because of the whole Jamaican authenticoness thing. But I almost didn't enjoy my food because of it. Jerk Hut folks. Take the meat off the bone. Just do it. Lastly: Price. Over-priced. Also, a cork fee for beer? C'mon now. That shart is wak. The food was great, the ambiance was awesome, our waiter rocked, but I cant get behind how expensive this restaurant is. Cheers*

Kind of your typical Greek gyro place, but it doesn't disappoint if that is what you are looking for. The guy that runs it always seems to be there, and he is a nice guy. Good prices. All of the food seems very fresh. I especially like their hummus and tabouli, which I believe the make in house daily.

Ordered take out marinated pork entree. Pork was good. Has baked sweet potato "fries" which weren't crunchy by any means not flavored. They were just baked sweet Potato slices and there was literally about 6 skinny pieces. The beans were just okay. The atmosphere looked nice so will try them again for a dine in experience.

The wait staff is extremely friendly, and the atmosphere is colorful and cute! The food was very good We had the spring rolls which were great. I had the mee goreng which was delicious. It was spicy but not overly spicy. Definitely recommend that you go here!

Dinner buffet was a huge let-down. The restaurant was shabby looking and completely empty, which should've been a sign to turn right back around. Food was clearly out all day and not flavored well. Naan was hard and cold. Appetizers and deserts were ok, but still not hot or delicious. Definitely won't be returning.

The customer service was awful. I placed an order for takeout and ended up with sauce all over my car seat. I called to complain and was told I should not have tilted the bag and this is why they warn people not to tilt the bag. A) I did not tilt the bag. B) I was not warned against this. I told the lady I didn't tilt it and she told me that wasn't possible. She told me they do this all the time and there is no way it would spill if I didn't tilt it and then she hung up on me!! I am appalled that she would assume 100% that there wasn't an error with the packaging and hang up the phone on me. I am never returning. Do not waste your money here.
My husband and I were here on a date....Highly recommend! We loved the Queen's platter!

Why do I feel like I am alone in leaving a poor review on this place???? I think I had a bad experience in St. Pete overall and I really hoped every time I sat down to a meal it would be the saving grace.... Stumbled upon this place while walking around downtown. It was raining so ducking into Tryst without having to wait for a table was a quick plus. We were seated at a table where the air was blowing very heavily, we quickly moved to the bar. The bar is outstandingly beautiful both in the tiles that were selected and the beautiful selections of beers on tap and the bottles winking at you from the cooler. WE asked the bartender if they had a tasting menu for the beers, why wouldn't you have a beer flight with over 25 beers on tap? It was such an ordeal that we quickly just asked for water. I ordered carrot and ginger soup, a salad and a few other apps. I watched the wait staff goof off with each other and pick up and study a salad that was in the window at least 3 times and put it back in the window. The soup just didn't hit it for me, I don't often order soup out as they are over flavored with salt or oil. I took a few bites and pushed it away. The pita bread that came with it was slightly stale but I dipped it in my soup because I was bored as I waited to take some bites of my mother's salad. It's just got to a point in our meal that we were not satisfied and wanted to leave. My mom went to use the restroom and left me with her credit card to pay the bill...but wait our bartender was in the corner chatting with his buddy and I sat and waited, and continued to wait, then finally asked someone else for the bill. This place, I agree with other Yelpers, has a South Beach feel and does tend to feel pretentious but I can't understand why, the service sucks and the food is lame. I don't know how or why they use the term gastro lounge, this leads me to believe the food will be delicious and like nothing I have had before, as well as enjoying some yummy beer or wine. (Another Yelper mentioned the list was overwhelming, and in fact they are and the service doesn't seem to know how to guide you through it).

The order came in 16 minutes late. I did not mention this to the manager when I called him. I had called him to complain that my order of Shrimp Ceviche had only one shrimp but that the Beef Kabab was good. He did not offer a refund or an offer to give me a new order of Shrimp Ceviche. I think he was also the cook, because, he didn't give a damn.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant! They have a wonderful range of vegetarian and pescatarian options. I had the masaman curry with shrimp, curry samosa, chocolate cake, and Thai coffee. Plain and simply the most delicious food I've had in a long time with great presentation and great service. I will definitely be coming again!

Absolutely love this place. The food and staff are wonderful and never disappoint. I've bn coming to this location for years eat in or take out. After a horrible and very disappointing experience at the 2nd st location, Danielle was very accommodating and took the time apologize for the experience (despite it not being her fault or same location). Nikki our waitress was also awesome in the service she provided. This places never disappoints

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Awesome food :) Halwa puri is great Goat Keema ( ground goat meat dish) never disappoints Biryani (Hyderabad Style ) never disappoints

This place is made for cool summer nights. If you don't (like going when it's raining or wintertime) it really sort of ruins the whole experience. The small, very hot or very cold front room doesn't really make for a pleasant time. Maybe it would if the food was something to bring you out for. The only thing here really worth coming for is the coconut shrimp which although pricey, are the best I've had. The breading is fluffy, full of coconut pieces and it comes with a delicious coconut cream sauce for dipping. The other highlight of my trips was their killer home brewed ginger beer - perfect for a byo-dark rum, dark & stormy Everything else - the greens, coco bread, vegetarian stew, fish, etc., is really nothing to make the trip for and is overpriced. (If i was a meat-eater, this review might be different - i didn't try their namesake chicken.)

Nothing to complain about here. We only got the pancakes and a veg omelette. Everything was tasty and prompt. There was only one other couple in there. The chef brought our food out with a smile and we enjoyed the unique decor.

The food here is great! I tried the Chicken Kabob lunch special, which came with rice, a salad and flat bread. Everything was flavorful and very tasty, and I even got some hot sauce on the side which had a crazy crazy kick, It was delicious! I will definitely be back to try the lamb.
I had a lunch with my friend. We truly enjoyed the food. The restaurant was very clean, nice and fancy. The personals were very welcoming, and friendly. We met the owner. It's an amazing experience.

I recently visited Queen of Sheba Ethiopian Restaurant. I have visited QoS since it opened in Tampa. I have visited when the experience was superb but ,most often, the visit is lackluster to say the least. The people who own it and work there are always very friendly. However when it comes to portion sizes and service i am usually disappointed. We ordered two vegetarian platters. They asked if we wanted them together, we said no because the last time it was not enough for two people. Be that as it may, they still were light regarding each dish that they served; like two table spoons of yesmissr wat etc. It is disappointing to be served two bites of each thing and be charged so much. They are always really spare on the injeera. In fact, our injera came with forks! Perhaps, people always ask for silver ware so they included them in the basket. I know tef isn't the most inexpensive grain but the injera batter is made in 5gallon buckets and this is an ETHIOPIAN restaurant! Injera should be plentiful. The last thing is the service. Every time we go i end up having to get up and find the server to ask for water or injera. I think the next time we am wanting Ethiopian food We will drive to Orlando for it. The food does taste good, even delicious but its like winning the lottery in this place regarding serving size, food temperature, service etc. i am not sure i will be back.
Never been upset with the quality here. Always consistent and awesome. My favorite is the shrimp curry( Thai hot!) with the crab rangoon appetizer.

It was my first time here and I was pleasantly surprised how good it was! The employees were super helpful and friendly. The food was delicious and fresh! What more can you ask for? I will definitely be back soon

I've been to this place a couple of times as it is not too far from my work. The eggrolls are really good and I like that they are baked and not deep fried. The buffalo chicken is my favorite as well as the pepperoni pizza. I'm not a fan of the dessert rolls but would be willing to give them a try again with a dipping sauce. Great concept!

I don't no where to begin..... FIRST of all we waited 45 minutes to be seated, once we were seated then waited another 25 minutes for the waiter to come over to take our table. Not to mention it was my BIRTHDAY celebration weekend and I had to experience such horrible service here at this hookah spot.
