Second, as we were trying to get the waiters attention he walked by several times before stopping over to attend to our needs. And third, may I add to this they had the nerve to add gratuity to our bill after their shitty services that they performed. So let me say this if I could rate this place a -5 I would because that's what this place deserves. As a manager myself this is not how you display customer service to your guest/customers.

Went here for a quick takeout. I don't typically tip for takeout or fast food. No waitress = no tip. As they were empty I told her to round it up. She noticeable swiped an extra $1. I don't care about the cash but it just bought her a nice Yelp review. Hope she enjoys the cash.

I didn't expect any good vietnamese restaurant in center city since so many good one located in north & south philly. Therefore, I picked this place on a cold day just for the experience & to satisfy my pho craving but I was surprised with the Pho. It was so good. The meat, the broth, the flavor were great. After the good experience there, I returned the next day along with my coworkers this time. They tried pho & liked it a lot. I tried the broke rice with pork chop & egg quiches this time. It was not as great as other viet restaurants, so I will stick with pho next time. This is really a great place. Definitely coming back more often for my pho fix.

Went for lunch yesterday. DevourIndy brought us. We had chips and salsa, fish, chicken and meat tacos, ice tea, coffee, and a margarita. Taste: delicious. We all agreed the chips and salsa were excellent. The tacos were fresh and two were more than enough with a side. Everything tasted freshly cooked and not steam table or reheated. The green rice was spicy and the cowboy potatoes were demolished. More like a square of scalloped potatoes with cheese. My ice tea was different and I would order again. Not a lipton or a fruit flavor but a very good unusual tea flavor. Server excellent. Very informative, knew the menu, and checked on us for refills. Atmosphere fun. Not crowded with tables set apart for conversation. Variety of seats from wood benches to wire chairs or bar seating. Light and modern. Price on the high side. But we liked everything and plan on returning so it was acceptable.

I adore this place. I've never had a bad meal here and think the people who work here are so nice. We've had nearly everything on the menu! Recommend: (we always get tofu and love how it's prepared) Gang (Red Curry, green is good but I prefer red) or Panang Pad See-iew Pad Khee-Mao Pad Wuhn-Sen also like to get these stir-fry entrées with tofu... Pad Med Ma-Muang Pad Khing or Pad Basil oh, and can't forget! Veggie Spring Rolls and Thai Iced tea Get your dish a little spicy and get a thai tea to cool the spice... oh so good! And in my opinion is much better than any other Thai place in St. Louis. We've recently moved to Chicago and haven't found a Basil Spice replacement! I miss you!!!
A good, no frills pho place in my neighborhood. Good atmosphere and has a nice little bar. Excellent service. I'm here a lot. 5 stars why not.

Fantastic, fresh, flavorful Vietnamese hoagies--vegetarian and non--on a scrumptiously crunchy roll, with lip-smacking sweet Cafe du Monde iced coffee. In a place no larger than your walk-in closet. Exceptionally air-conditioned on this steamy May afternoon.
terrible food cooked without love! same quality as hooters, but much more expensive!
Had the panang. Was very good. Not the best, but it was certainly worth the $11 for a very generous portion considering the prices in the area.

Recently had dinner and it was a great experience.... food was all great highly recommend the fried rice dish. My daughter ordered a grilled cheese and the entire table bugged her for a bite bc how good it was . Service spot on . We will be back !
Meh - indifferent service and food. Some items better than others but at $80 plus for the two us, I'll be heading other places before I repeat. Olympia in dog town comes to mind.

I was in the mood for a Cuba sandwich and happened to be in New Hope, so thought "why not?". Overall, it wasn't terrible, but it wasn't great either. We ordered the guacamole for an appetizer, a bowl of black bean soup (it was a very cold day) for me, a cup of tortilla soup for my friend and we both had the Cuban sandwiches. The guacamole wasn't bad, just didn't have much taste. More concerning was the acidic taste it left in your mouth, not the kind from lime juice, but the kind when food is starting to go bad. It wasn't a meal-killer, but it didn't leave us wanting to finish the whole portion, by any means. The tortilla chips served with the dish were super greasy, again not a complete miss, but it didn't want you yearning to reach back into the plate for more. The soups were sadly a let down too. My black bean, which should be a stand-out at any Cuban restaurant was just so-so, It wasn't very hot, and coupled with the dollop of sour cream, just cooled it to barely warm. Of course, it was a real cold day and hot soup would have hit the spot, but after the guacamole we weren't expecting a great meal anyway. Again, there's just no flavor in either soup. My friend liked his a little better, but there's just no seasoning in either dish. The sandwiches were okay, and I mean just okay. The bread wasn't authentic Cuban bread and although the rest was pretty typical, we had to ask for pickles, because mine had none and my friends had one small pickle slice for the whole sandwich. My friend opted for the french fries which he described as "okay" and I had the side salad (which you should not request) which had that same acidic taste in the dressing that made me immediately stop eating for fear of the unknown. The salad dressing was definitely past it's sell by date; I believe it was a homemade dressing, but not sure when that batch was made. Maybe a daily "test" of the food that's been kept awhile isn't a bed idea here? My friend was on his last 1/2 of sandwich and the waitress said "Do you want your check now?" which really confused us. I asked him to look at the front door to see if there was line or something, but that was not the case. Including us, there were three other tables occupied in the whole place, which should have told volumes at lunchtime on a sunny Saturday. Lastly, it occurred to me after we left, that the fruit flies (they're pretty big here!) we saw hovering around the tables were most likely being fed on rotten fruit/food in the restaurant. It would explain the acid off-taste of a few items and thought if the food were fresher, would the flies go away? I'm not accusing them of unsanitary conditions, but I can't think of another restaurant I've been to that had fruit flies hovering around. I've only encountered them around rotten food, and I do have my suspicions about two parts of our meal. There are so many great places to eat in New Hope and this one just doesn't seem to be one of them. Although the name suggests Latin flavors, aside from the music, you'll find little else here.

The Abyssinian Ethiopian restaurant is an authentic Ethiopian restaurant. The entire restaurant does a great job of really making you truly feel like you are dinning in Ethiopia. This restaurant tells the story of what a true Ethiopian life is like. When I ordered Ethiopian coffee my waitress also brought over incense and lit them for me at my table. The smell of both the coffee and incense really enhanced the atmosphere. From the beverages to the deserts, this menu is strictly Ethiopian. The Ethiopian menu consists of different sections labeled lamb, fish, chicken, beef, and vegetarian. The Ethiopian assets that are displayed throughout the restaurants consist of Ethiopian music and dancers displayed on the flat screens in the back of the restaurant, an Ethiopian hut, and an Ethiopian store. Displayed in the Ethiopian hut is true authentic Ethiopian artifacts. The Ethiopian store attached to the restaurant displays Ethiopian clothing, foods, and other items. The participatory elements that are in this restaurant is the ability to go in the hut and experience what it is like to dine like a true Ethiopian and the ability to view all the assets up close. People cannot dine in the hut because it is only a walk through display that houses numerous Ethiopian artifacts. This is reverent to tourists who want to experience who want to interact in a true Ethiopian setting. And above all that, the service was amazing. Our waiter was extremely attentive, happy, and engaging. She did a great job of explaining the history of the restaurant, the menu, and a few of the items showcased in the restaurant. Though the menu was a lot different than what is typically expected in America, there was still something for everyone since the menu is made to appeal to a wide variety of people.

"Meh. I've experience better." That's what Yelp says represents two stars, and I'd have to agree with that about this place. I think that many people would agree that an integral part of what makes pho good pho, is the broth. The broth here was exceptionally weak and flavorless. As a matter of fact, I am certain that what they use for pho "broth" is none other than the clear simple broth they use for American style wonton soup in Chinese-American restaurants. I know this because my family has been in that business my entire life. Now that we established that, the portions are small. I asked for a large bowl of pho and what came out was what many places I've been to serve as a small or regular bowl. Authentic Asian food is never much for presentation, but they never hesitate to fill you up. Not here. To top it off, the bowls are pricier than usual. Next, the plate of greens/vegetables that accompany the pho was sparse. All it had was two sprigs of cilantro, a small clump of lemongrass, two lemon wedges, and jalapeno slices sliced so thin (slivers) you couldn't even taste them. No basil or Thai basil, and no thick cut jalapenos. Decor/layout isn't much of a factor for me but I must say this place is tiny, and you have to go outside, walk around the corner, and go through the back door like a burglar to use the bathroom. It's not far, and I'm not lazy but you shouldn't have to do this at a restaurant. I guess all this is fine since I can't imagine this place ever being packed with weak pho. I am surprised at the four star reviews. I know I won't be coming back here to get pho when I'm in Tucson. The one good thing I will say about it is that at least the meat was fresh. A good bowl of pho should leave your belly FULL and your brow SWEATY from the hot steaminess mixed with the natural kick you get from the added jalapeno SLICES. YMMV
Fun little spot if you want a quick bite to eat. I'm a fan of the vegetarian ham baguette and spring rolls. I do have a soft spot for the Cajun shrimp sandwich. Beef soup ain't that bad either.

I'm so happy that South Grand Gyro Express has reopened. The mother (Marena) of the former owner took it over after being closed for many months. They have skimmed the menu down and added a few American fast food items. They've also painted the place with a more sterile color, to promote that it's a fast food restaurant, I guess. And truth be told, it's not that fast. But, the food is very tasty. You MUST get the eggplant puree from the appetizer menu. It is UNBELIEVABLE and would surely be a hit if you bought two orders and offered it as a party dip. Seriously, this stuff is good! The gyro meat is another standout item on their menu and they have some great specials. If you can handle a small wait, stop by. They have a few tables, but carry out is their main businesses. Most items are under $6 bucks. Great value!

This place is pretty good. The jerk chicken is decent. The chicken itself is flavorful, and the sauce they put on the side has a decent kick. I would not rank it in the top 10 places for jerk chicken, but it is good. Platters come with this cabbage mix, which is really good, and rice, which is dry but tasty. Prices are not awful, though more than what is expected. Per person, you are usually looking at about $15.

Came here for a friend's birthday dinner with a large party of 12, and the service was friendly and attentive throughout. We made reservations and were promptly seated when we arrived, and they were super accommodating when we had 2 more people than originally reserved. I got the Pad Woon Sen (stir-fried cellophane noodles) - it was pretty good and portions were generous. Overall, a good place to dine at (with a large menu of the standard thai items as well as more exotic ones like alligator!), food was pretty good, and service made the experience very pleasant. Also a BYO!
in two words: THE BEST in a few more words: this place is an egg-and-cheese mecca. nothing beats spending pocket change on one of these heavenly sandwiches.

My favorite Thai spot in Philly so far. Too bad they don't deliver to my current address, but I'll be moving soon (primarily because of work, not food, I swear...) We started with the Crispy Spring Rolls, which were lightly friend and VERY hot (beware, eager eaters). The Chicken Pad Thai had the perfect peanut-lime combination with tender meat. The Beef Green Curry had a nice portion of vegetables to balance out the protein and a fantastic kick. And, it must be mentioned that the bathroom was kind of heavenly. A heater warmed the spacious room, the scented candle smelled divine, and it was very clean...extra points!

Okay been to this place 11 Times had family and friends come from N.Y. and all over the world enjoyed the food and the service was perfect but this time went for my birthday with more than 9 people from N.Y. and Florida and just because I had a tank top this old man did not want 2 make money at a place that I wanted to spend my birthday at my day was just crap thanks Casona restaurant

If I could give this place a lower rating, I would. The last time I was there, I ordered soup. I could see towards the back as they reached in with their bare hands and grab noodles to put in the soup container. Never went back.

The truth is that I have no real complaints. This is NOT haute cuisine. It is NOT fine dining. It doesn't pretend to be. It is simply excellent ethnic food. It is really a mix of Greek and Kurdish. I'd say the flavor a are more Kurdish. Everything was very fresh and flavorful. We started with a delicious saganaki (brandy flamed hard cheese) served with wedges of pita bread. It was quite a soft pita, rather than the 'tougher' pita you see in Greece. We also had a dish of hummus, which had a lovely silky texture and an honest chick pea flavor that wasn't overwhelmed by gobs of oil and lemon. We both opted for the Shawarma platter with delicious beef/lamb gyros meat, saffron rice and a salad of tomatoes and cubes of cucumber delicately flavored with a mild vinegar. The portions were large and we ended up taking quite a bit of food home. We had ordered baklava but had to take it home. It was, by the way, perfect. Not the sickeningly sweet sticky mess served by many other Mediterranean restaurants. The earthy flavor of the ground nuts was perfectly offset by just enough syrup to hold it all together without being at all runny. Despite some complaints by other reviewers, we didn't think the prices were at all unreasonable. If you want cheap food, go to Macdonalds! As my mother always said, "you get what you pay for." At Sunrise you pay for delicious, fresh, rustic food and that is what you get.

You have got to try the flaming cheese! It is amazing. The pita is fresh and the service is always outstanding. My family eats here at least once a month. The authentic Greek gyros with lamb are melt-in-your-mouth tender. You can often enjoy live music and belly dancing in the evenings. This locally owned business delivers in atmosphere, taste, and service.

We got take out one night and really enjoyed everything so we followed it up with a weekend visit for the lunch buffet. Parking wise, it might be easier to find a spot in the Lafayette Eye Associates parking lot, but there are a few spaces in front of the restaurant. The buffet had a fair number of options. I know chicken tikka masala is a staple at all buffets, but this ctm was REALLY good, probably the best I've ever had. In many other places, the chicken is dry, bland, but Nirvana's version is tender, flavorful, and has just a tiny bit of kick. One unique thing here that I haven't had at other buffets was a mango pudding. That was YUMMY! Consistency was thinner than most puddings, but had the flavor of a mango lassi, definitely on the sweeter side. The gentleman waiting on the tables was also thoughtful to step in to warn me that the gulab jamun did contain flour (I had previously asked about the mango and rice puddings). I couldn't taste the actual balls (which were comically half the size that I typically see) b/c of that, but the syrup was good. They offered masala tea as well, and I had the kooky idea (hopefully not offensive) to use the gulab jamun syrup to sweeten it instead of plain sugar. It was so good that when my husband mentioned we really liked it while he was paying the bill, the man let us know a fresh batch was coming out if we wanted to wait a few minutes to have some more. So nice of him! I definitely want to come here again!

To be fair, this restaurant really deserves somewhere between 2 and 3 stars. There is nothing special about this restaurant, unless you count the loud music and belly dancers as special. Mildly amusing at best. The restaurant is divided into small nook-like rooms where tables are crammed together, surrounded by cheap, dark decorum. I think that the wait for our food was most likely caused by belly dancer traffic jams, as servers and dancers must share the small spaces between tables. The food was marginal, but nothing to freak out over. I imagine, unless you really need a pseudo-Greek fix or you happen to live in walking distance, this place is really not worth the drive. Sorry Momos, but I probably won't be back :(

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Finally got a chance to go back, I didn't order the curry this time, but the pad see ew, which was fantastic!!!! The staff and owner were awesome! This is the place for Thai noodles...If you are looking for curry, of all Reno Thai, Bangkok cuisine south has the best IMHO....

The well-priced $10 lunch special included an appetizer, soup and entrée, but know the portions are sized smaller for lunch. The soup was served in a really small cup, only one spring roll was included for the app, and the yellow curry was served on a pretty small dish. However, everything tasted very good! The flavor of the chicken yellow curry was perfect, and the only negative thing I could say was that the potatoes were ever so slightly under cooked. I got the curry with 2 stars hot, and it was comfortably hot, without ruining the good flavor of the dish. Eating every bite on my plate, including all the rice, I can say that I am full enough as far as lunch goes. One other thing worth mentioning is they also serve dishes from other cuisines, including Vietnamese, Korean and Malaysian. I will definitely come back!

I would definitely go back and or recommend to a friend. Food was delicious, service was fast and friendly. I thought the a la carte dish portions could have been a little larger but it wasn't a deal breaker.
I am updating because we eat to go from Asian Pho every Tuesday night. My usual order is #38 and it's amazing! All for $7.95!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This is a great place for both newbies and Indian food connoisseurs to experience the best of Indian cuisine. For those afraid of Indian food's reputation for spiciness, they can tone it down for those who don't like it hot. The lunch buffet is outstanding and a great way for the inexperienced to get a feel for the menu. They have a nice representative sampling of many dishes and their delicious "naan" flat-bread. The chicken tikka masala is always a great Indian "gateway" food and one of their best dishes. The bright orange dish is unbelievably good -- chicken in a creamy tomato/curry sauce. WARNING: IT IS HIGHLY ADDICTIVE! Be sure to try the Naan. I initially resisted because it looked simply like a tortilla, but now it's a favorite. The garlic naan (flat-bread slathered in butter and garlic) is out of this world. For dinner, I recommend ordering a bunch of different dishes and eating them family style. I have really enjoyed the Onion Bhaji as an appetizer (think onion rings in a hummus batter with a variety of chutney dipping sauces). The roasted lamb shank was fantastic last time; it was glazed with a fruity sauce. Since it's Indian, of course they have some great vegetarian choices: both the Palak Paneer (Indian cheese in a creamed spinach sauce) and the Palak Subzi Daal (lentils cooked with cauliflower, tomatoes, eggplant, and potatoes) are so good. Most dishes come with Basmati Rice, a long grained rice with a mixture of spices. Be prepared for a little wait for your meal. The owner (a really cool guy) and his wife make everything from scratch, so it takes some time. However, it is worth the wait while you enjoy some Bollywood videos on the flat screen TV.

No luck. Went for the lunch buffet, it was complete chaos there were like 10 people waiting to pay, the food selection was barely there, some things didn't even look hot and there was clearly no idea what they were doing. After standing waiting for 9 minutes I gave up and walked out. Perhaps I'll try another day.
Very, very clean place. Shocked me but I also wasn't expecting it to be dirty either. Great food as well.

Ohhhh babyyyy Bui's breakfast sandwich is trucky food at its finest. None of this $8 gourmet nonsense. If I'm going to a food truck I want fast, good food but most importantly, I'm looking for something cheap! There's a place in the world for the lobster roll truck... there's also a place in the world for Bui's! I'd be lying if I said I've never had a Bui's hangover special (ham, bacon, sausage, eggs, and cheese- comes with a gatorade, awesome) but typically I go for a #3 (tomato, mushroom, spinach, eggs, cheese). The secret here is to order the Bui's sauce. It's not really anything too special- I think Bui's sauce is a mix of hot sauce, ketchup, and mayo... given that I like all three on my eggs it's the perfect addition to my breakfast sandwich! The line is always long but thankfully you can text Mrs. Bui (856.630.7269) and she has it ready when you get to the front. Keep food trucks cheap! Support Bui's!!!

Went here because Ian Freobe (moron) reviewed it in RFT recently (I wanted to take a friend for gyros and now could kick myself for not sticking with St Louis Gyro Company). Anyway, Freobe or whatever that dorks name is, does not mention that the gyro meat has it's own "Special lamb sauce" which is totally unnecessary and totally defeats the purpose of rotating it on a spit in it's own juice. Guess what? The special process means that when they bring the gyro to your table it is ICE FRIGGING COLD!!!!! Totally unacceptable. Totally poor spin. You morons who state this is the best have got to be kidding me. Get back on your meds! The falafel was good, if bland. Where are your sauces (hot/med/mild) to pour on? Anyone who has enjoyed a good street falafel in the middle east would know what I am talking about. Freobe, once again you have proved that you are a jackass. Gyro Express...try microwaving your meat after your special applique'...if I wanted a cold meal I'd go to Ted Drewe's.

This is one of my two favorite Thai places in Brandon. I eat there at least a couple of times a month if not more. The seafood Panang with the lightly breaded and fried Basa is to die for and the peanut sauce which they call Amazing is just that. My wife and I never tire of eating here. The staff is as friendly as you can possibly imagine. Come early though, as it can fill up quickly at lunch time.

iPho has become my favorite lunch spot. Their food is delicious, fresh, and always great! There is nothing as comforting as Pho on a cold day, it's like a warm hug, that leaves you feeling full, but not miserable like you just ate too many french fries. Their portions are generous and very fairly priced. The staff is polite and attentive, delivering just the right amount of service! This is a huge compliment from me, as I'm usually annoyed by servers that feel the need to articulate every thought and upcoming action out loud, which of course, is not necessary. Clean and consistent, I LOVE this restaurant... and if that's not enough, they even have bubble tea, yay!

WoW! I had the opportunity to order from this food truck today and you can believe the reviews and the awards! Awesome Gryo! I hope to catch them again and try the Greek salad next time. If you see this truck out DO not pass it up.

The food is so good. Staff is friendly. They have a lunch buffet, regular menu, and a bar for date nights. There are vegetarian options on the buffet and menu. I love their mango drink (non alcoholic)

The atmosphere is excellent and very inviting. The group I was with unfortunately all chose pastas for dinner and most of us left still hungry. What we did have was tasty, just over priced for what it was. Their other entree's looked more substantial so I guess maybe we just chose poorly. I would go back and give it another try however.

Not worth the wait. If you are looking for falafel, head on over to mama's. You can get the falafel platter there for $9. For $1 more, the portion is larger, tastes 10 times better and you save a bunch of time :) it's not a bad cart, but i won't be returning.

Got a chance to check out Zagol recently, as I was in the mood for some different cuisine, and only had Ethiopian food on one previous occasion several years ago. I went with the Bozena Shiro (pea pods with spiced beef,) and it was great. It appears that most of their entrees are served with Injera (flatbread - not too sour or rubbery here at all,) which made things interesting as no silverware was needed. Fortunately, I didn't get too much on me. The little wicker tables and stools really added to the experience. There was a sign posted inside the restaurant advertising high tea every Sunday, which is apparently pretty popular. Give it a try. A unique dining experience for sure, and not too pricey.

Very authentic with a smaller menu but overall good dishes. The decor is pretty cool, which makes it unique from other restaurants. They bring out some side sauces which is very accommodating to the dishes you order. You can change the flavor or spice levels as you wish. I have really enjoyed it. Interesting enoigh they sold hot sake here but i wont ask questions. Good service with polite attitude. The prices a bit pricey but well worth it.

Three of us came here for Friday night dinner after reading positive reviews and a trusted friend said this was authentic Greek food. One of our party is a Greek native. Also, we liked the BYOB idea. Disappointing experience overall. From the rude staff, to the impossibly noisy space to the inauthentic 'Greek' food, we were sorry we came. We ordered multiple plates of starters to share. The avocado citrus salad was romaine lettuce smothered in slivered almonds atop five grapefruit slices with 2 tiny mushy avocado slices hidden underneath. No flavor dressing, no hint of lime,

I am working in KOP as a consultant for the time being and tried this place the other night. You will be pleasantly surprised by this diamond in the rough. As an indian from NY, I am very critical of Indian restaurants but this place did not dissappoint. I had the lamb biryani. The portion was huge and the flavor was great - I asked for the "American spicy" version. KOP is full of big name restaurants, but this is a hidden gem!

Note: this is specifically a review for the PF Chang's To Go service. If you're looking for the restaurant, try my restaurant review at: http://www.yelp.com/biz/p-f-changs-china-bistro-plymouth-meeting-3#hrid:jtuIKB6X2h6qrVgkEcwfxA, or any other review from all the other Yelpers! Having worked in Malvern for a while, I pass by Plymouth Meeting on my drive back into my apartment in Philly every day, but the traffic going that way usually looks pretty foreboding. Finally, I gave in and ended up at PF Chang's, since I was desperate for some Asian goodness, but decided to give their To Go curbside service a try, since I wanted to grab the food and head back home. So I tried ordering from their mobile app... and it is SUPER easy. I'm really impressed with how well designed the app is, and thankfully, even with my recent switch to Android from iOS, the app is still pretty much the same. So I placed my order, and they can have it ready within 15 mins (or so the app seems to allow). In any case, I got there, and I wanted to try the curbside delivery, since the order had already been charged to my card. And that was the first (but only) hiccup. I called the number for the restaurant to say that I was there, but it kept ringing and nobody picked up. I know that there's even a camera for them to see the folks parking in the curbside pick-up spots, but no dice. No worries, I went in, and then suddenly realized why nobody was picking up. Kind of hard to pick up the phone if nobody's manning it. :) It seemed like it was super busy, so no harm done, and I grabbed my order and headed home. Everything was amazing, as usual, and was packed very well. My only tip would be to avoid the crispy green beans, since they don't stay crispy that long due to the humidity in the container. If you really must have them, try to vent them by opening the container lid a bit to prevent the steam build-up, but then beware of the fact that they may smell wayyy too good and you may finish them before you get home. Just a heads up, since I've gone through that experience first hand. I've been back for several other times, and the curb-side pickup really doesn't seem to work for me, but that could just be my bad luck. Bar that one aspect, their To Go service is just as awesome as the place itself! TLDR: Great service, but be wary of the curbside delivery claims! Might be faster to just go in!

My first visit (a Tuesday night at 6pm). Order taker greeted me when I walked in and was helpful in going over the menu with me. I ordered the 'Whole Grain Tuscan Linguine", small, with a grilled chicken breast. I don't always go the healthy route, but this item sounded tasty, and the two customers ahead of both ordered it, so I figured "when in Rome..." Despite being 'healthy', the dish had a lot of flavor. The noodles and veggies were NOT overcooked, but had just the right amount of firmness to provide different textures. The grilled chicken had been squeezed completely flat, but still had a touch of good flavor from seasonings. It still tasted fine, especially when cut and mixed with the noodles. I just tend to prefer chicken that tastes and looks more fresh [natural plump?] Overall, the restaurant was clean, the staff friendly and the food good.

As a big fan of Vietnamese and Chinese food, in addition to the restaurant coming highly recommended, I had expected my experience at Sizzling Wok to be extraordinary. It simply was not. As I walked through the door, the first thing I heard was rap music. When I am dining out, I expect there to be a certain relaxing ambiance. The rap music destroyed that. I could also sense a very angry vibe from our server. We were never welcomed to the restaurant, which I felt was uncouth. Much to my chagrin, I was informed that I would only be granted only one drink refill. Knowing how inexpensive fountain sodas are to serve, this further led to my distasteful view of the restaurant. We started with pork spring rolls. They were satisfactory and were generously portioned. However, they were crudely assembled and the ingredients of the sauce had not been completely mixed. For my main course, I ordered the Lemongrass Chicken. As I normally do, I asked that the dish be prepared with as little oil as possible. While the Leomongrass Chicken was tasty and large, it still contained too much oil and was overly salty. My brother ordered the Cashew Chicken. It was basically a large pile of fried chicken with some sauce on it. We had to hunt-and-peck to find an actual cashew. He was likewise "2-star dissatisfied." This establishment is clearly not as health conscious as its area competitors. Sizzling Wok is not a terrible restaurant. It is reasonably priced and the portions are large. However, it is merely mediocre. If you're in the mood for Asian cuisine on Indianapolis' West Side, you have many, truly outstanding options. I suggest skipping Sizzling Wok entirely.

Wonderful, not-too-expensive seafood. Delicious, actually. It's BYOB, so you should have some expectations about atmosphere - knowing also that it's a small space. Staff was excellent. I noticed that whenever our waitress checked on us, she quickly mopped up my clumsy wine pours. It's the subtle things that set great service apart. Shrimp Scampi might have been the best shrimp I've ever tasted.

This small BYO's full name is Spice Thai Cuisine, so don't confuse it with the same-named place in Bloomfield NJ. Located near the art-deco County Theater, it offers easily the best Thai food we've found in Bucks County and almost ranks with top Thai eateries in major urban areas. Crying Tiger salad is delicious, with a fine balance of flavors and spices. Curried Chu Chee duck is delightfully flavored, crisp with no fattiness -- a textbook example of how this should be prepared. However, salmon supreme is relatively bland (ginger fish is much better), and default-level spices can overwhelm calamari taste in curried fish offerings (best to ask for mild spiciness with light-fish curry dishes). If you insist on mild spiciness in other dishes, specify when ordering, although recently the default spiciness may have been reduced, so taste and experiment. Polite prompt service most weekdays, although it can get moderately slow during crowded weekend evenings. The setting is modest and tiny but pleasant, with a large window for sidewalk people-watching, but tops of chair backs dig into your spine if you're tall. On frigid evenings try to avoid the rearmost tables, which like the bathrooms can be chilly. When calling last Friday evening we were told we wouldn't need reservations, only to be nearly turned away because we didn't have reservations. After us, most were being turned away, with some leaving and others waiting patiently for an opening. Alas, one waiting foursome leaned themselves next to our table near the front, something even a diner shouldn't allow, and carried on a shouting conversation practically in our ears. So reserve ahead Fridays and Saturdays to be safe, but even better is to try for weekdays.

O.K. I am very pleased with this place. it is great to have another Indian option in downtown Indianapolis for lunch. The buffet isn't huge but it is more than adequate for its choices and I've read it changes from time to time. I would much rather have a limited number of choices each of which has a discrete spicing and taste profile than a bunch of things which all taste very similar. The changing buffet is a big plus. India Garden is an "American tastes" Indian restaurant. I don't particularly care for it, so its really wonderful to have this new option. Haveli is a bit of a walk from where I work but it can be done in about 10 minutes or so, and the walk back to the office helps settle things so I don't fall asleep in the afternoon. I would have given it 4 stars, but the price is inexpensive and so that bumps it to five.

Fabulous food. My husband and I come here often. We enjoy the food, especially all the vegan choices. Everything is fresh and delicious. The owners also take the time to explain how the different dishes should be eaten. We truly love the food and the charming and kind service offered by the owners and their staff.

Okay, I'm not one to eat fast food style, but this place is the fair exception. The staff alone is a 5 star team, with some of the best quality service I have seen. They talk to you, explain their menu and gave us samples. We have Gyros, wings and fried mushrooms. Skip the mushrooms (giant white mushrooms, fried and unseasoned). The gyro and fries were good, and the wings were really tasty. Fair enough to say, I wasn't expecting much, but the staff and menu diversity is good for a quick bite on the fly. Good for the locals, but not a stop for a visitors who's in town for a few days, unless they are into this kinda menu.
Excellent food!. Quaint place, quiet atmosphere, outstanding and friendly service. We'll be back! Highly recommend!

My husband and I enjoyed ourselves at Umami. We started with the Hulk roll, which was delicious. I ordered the Chicken Pad Thai (medium heat) and he ordered the Seafood Ramen. Both of our meals were great and very flavorful! Service was wonderful as well! We will definitely be back.

This Jamaican restaurant is located in downtown Trenton and has been there since at least 2010 because they had food reviews on the wall from 2010. Nice place for Trenton, the interior looked nice and you get your food from ordering at the counter and then seat yourselves. Got the brown stew chicken with peas and brown rice and plantains and the jerk chicken with brown rice and peas and mac and cheese. They have small/medium/large portions, got the medium for $10 which just means extra chicken, small is two pieces, medium is four pieces and you get two sides. They normally serve with white rice, the brown rice and beans are $1 extra. Mac and cheese ($1.50) and plantains ($1) were a little extra too which I didn't know but not big deal, plenty of food. Was quite good and tasty. They also have goat and oxtails which I will try next time. Big fan of goat and oxtails. I was able to walk there from work, I have to imagine parking might be an issue.
Good food, pleasant atmosphere. I always get the chicken dishes. The naan breads are tasty. The food comes out pretty quickly. Service is friendly, and the Guru's has been here for a while.

Last I checked, Seth Wahlman was heading things up here. Seth Wahlman is, in my opinion, the best mixologist in the city of St. Louis. And it's not just my opinion. He's won about as many local awards and honors as one could hope for. He's an institution. That said, I don't know if he's mixing any cocktails here. When I visited, I saw him, but he wasn't doing any drink mixing, and I've heard he's managing the restaurant. Well, the cocktail list certainly bears his mark, and the food is excellent. I had the best hummus of my life here. The pitas are warm, soft, and pillowy. I'm vegetarian, and the menu was a delight. The food isn't cheap, but the booze is extremely reasonable. You can get a bottle of wine for the table for under $40, and what I assume are Seth's house cocktail creations for $12--not exactly cheap, but compare those prices to Planter's House.

Excellent! The food is perfectly cooked, the staff really knows their stuff and makes great recommendations. The space is small and causal, but personally, I like this as I don't feel I need to behave for my waiter. The food is Sicilian, so not your typical Ameri-Talian red sauce joint. You really can't go wrong here, but reservations aren't always easy to come by. We will definitely be back

The ambiance is really neat. I've been to India about a dozen times and when I walked into Fez I felt like I was in the middle of the Rajasthan desert. The walls are decked out with these different tapestries and their cushy couches come fully equipped with bucket seating and low tables. I highly recommend the cherry mango hookah. This is also a great place for cheap drinks and large groups. Not the best for wait service though. He wasn't very courteous and we had to remind him a dozen times to bring more water.

I haven't eaten Thai food in Philly too much so I can't compare them to some of the other places, but the food was amazing! I got the red curry and the wifey got the Penang curry. Each dish was absolutely delicious. The restaurant is very small and clean. The service was good and prices were fair. The place is BYOB so you can't go wrong here. I would highly recommend trying anyone of the curries.

ignore the morons, THIS PLACE IS A GEM. It's an authentic northeast-style Mediterranean eatery- plastic cups & utensils, bare bones space, and an owner that knows what he's doing- the food is excellent. If you want decor, go suffer the Cheesecake Factory- if you want fresh handmade med food, stay here. The special is ALWAYS great. The falafel are excellent, the tabbouleh is all freshly made as are the salad dressings, the flavors are bright, clean and authentic. BYOB- I suggest a Pinot or a nice Sancerre. Easily my favorite fresh eats in Nashville along with Kien Giang. Is it perfect- no. Pitas are frequently meh. It can get crowded. It's old school- ORDER, SIT, EAT, PAY. Parking is tough sometimes but there's a garage under the strip mall with stairs in the corner. All in all, one of my fav med eats, when it's on it's killin', when it's not it's merely very very good.

We had an early Valentine's dinner date here over the weekend and felt it was a big miss, given the hype. Beautiful decoration and ambiance. We walked in through the hotel and interior door was opened for us with a greeter to show us the way. That was over-the-top fancy! We were sat next to the floor-to-ceiling windows and, on a 30-degree night, that chill came inside and by end of meal, I was left wishing I had kept my coat, rather than take hostess up on her offer to hang in closet. Wine selection good. As another Yelper reviewed, we had the Gorgonzola-stuffed figs and it was all bacon. Didn't even taste Gorgonzola in the first one... the bacon overwhelmed everything. Hubs ordered tomato basil soup and that was good. Most soups are served piping hot, but this wasn't and ready to enjoy right away. I ordered a butter leaf salad with chick peas, but the name should've been reversed... I had 200 crunchy chickpeas on my plate, again, overwhelming other ingredients. My entree was the sea bass, cooked beautifully, high could've benefited from a sauce. Served atop a cauliflower purée and arugula. Hubs had quail. The bird was cooked to perfection, but the plate experience was odd... very large cold pickled chili peppers atop a warm meat with bulky potato fingerlings. With this much hype, you expect some pop and the pairings and balance of ingredients was off for us. Hazelnut pot de creme was amazing so we finished on a high note. I'd go back for that, as a post-movie dessert. Service was a bit slow, considering the restaurant wasn't full. We were waiting awhile to order to the point another server noticed and asked us to confirm we were being attended to. And, it took 3 trips to serve coffee, one each for brew, then cream and sugar, and a few minutes later, a spoon finally arrived to stir it together. So a few kinks to work out there. Glad we gave it a go, but not in a rush to return.

As a resident of Delaware I have rode past this establishment many times but never stopped in because parking was always an issue in the area. My girlfriend called me on Saturday from out of town and invited me to Sunday brunch at this very same place, parking shouldn't be an issue and I didn't know they were open on Sundays. When I arrived there wasn't anyone at the door to greet you so I walked in and located my friend who was already seated. Their was live music and the atmosphere was very pleasant. I love the rustic chic decor! The brunch menu was composed of some good stuff and they were offering a Bloody Mary Bar . So far so good. The server was very attentive and shared his take on the Brunch options. I had the vegetable omelet and it came with potatoes, grilled tomatoes and salad greens. The omelet was tasty but small and the vegetable assortment was very pleasing to my palate. It was not your tradtional omelet veggies . The coffee was strong but good , so I had 2 cups not realizing not being informed that they CHARGE for refills!!!The breakfast potatoes reminded me of a smashed baked potatoe , unimpressive. They had a very nice set up for the Make your own Bloody Mary with many options to choose from. What they failed to do was have utensils or napkins available to retrieve the drink fixings and share that the VODKA was a separate charge! I had to ask for these items and the staff seemed perturbed about me asking . Safe food handling is important and this should have been considered.

Came on a Friday night and the place was full. we had spring rolls, which were small but tightly rolled and tasty. The service was very friendly and the food was very good. We tried a pumpkin dish and a ground chicken dish. Both were excellent. We had a bit of a wait for things but I think it was because they were at capacity. My friend goes there for lunch and says it's quick. I'll be back!

Came here for happy hour and was really excited to see all the drink and appetizer choices. Got the poke, which was good. Service was good, especially considering we had a large group that kept growing as the night went on.

Ordered a fish hoagie (Muslim). First time ordering from here, it was a mess, there was sauce everywhere, too much fish in a very little bread loaf.. Too be honest I couldn't even taste the fish, it was just sauce and more sauce, too messy. However it was decently flavored and even tho I looked like a fool eating it, I did it anyway. Only if they can get the ratio of fish and bread right, it might actually be ok. Not to mention everyone doesn't like a hoagie loaded with sauce...

Since this place has been getting overwhelmingly great reviews on here, I decided to invite my girlfriend's parents out with us for dinner. That can be nerve racking, because they have very high expectations of what a nice restaurant should be. When we arrive, they were a bit worried since we were the only car in the parking lot. I explained that one it is very new, open for only about 6 weeks they said, but also because it was at 6 o'clock on a saturday and most people eat later. We go in to be greeted warmly by what I believe to be the owner, or at least manager. My first impression of this place was very good. The layout was fun, and the bar was very neat looking. We then get sat in the back dining room in a booth. I loved the booth layout. It was encased in glass, and very private. It helped keep the noise level down too, once everyone else showed up later in the evening. We brought in our own wine, and there was a 12 dollar corkage fee. That is pretty standard it seems. We decided to order the Arancini. I didn't really know what that was, but the incredients sounded good. It was kind of like a weird hush puppy. Not my favorite thing, but it wasn't necessarily bad. Just not at all what I was expecting. I ordered the Cannelloni, which was just great. It was a big portion too, especially for the price! The two ladies both got seafood linguini, and they really both enjoyed it, and they both had enough to take home for a second meal. Now onto Mr. tough to please... He ordered the Filet Mignon. He opted to get the sauce on the side, which they did perfectly. It wasn't even touching the steak, so you only had to use it if you wanted. He also orders his steaks rare. A lot of places never really cook it rare, because they are afraid it seems like, which I don't blame them. However, his steak came out, cooked to absolute perfection. He was so excited. I imagine that he will be back here a lot, because once he finds something that he likes, he really goes on a kick! All in all, it was a wonderful dinner, with great food and service. We will definitely be back!

I've been a few times, trying both brunch and dinner. Brunch was fair but nothing outstanding. I'll give it another try to see if it was an off day. We shared several dishes for dinner and really enjoyed the burrata, Crab Louie and a fava bean pea puree. Crab Louie was quite good and a big portion. Our other dish was octopus salad, but it was really chickpeas with small pieces of octopus. It was good, but just all chickpeas. The atmosphere is hip and always packed. The food is very good. They'll open nearly any wine you want it seems, but be careful letting them direct you toward a glass of wine not listed because they have good wines and can be $15-16/glass. If you order off the menu you can get glasses of wine for under $10. good cocktails too.

I stopped in here on a sunday for a quick brunch with my boyfriend since Honey Sit n Eat across the street was busy as usual. Upon walking in, the room was filled with students doing work on their computers. There are two couch lounging sections towards the front and back of the room. They offer cafe style brunch, so basically sandwiches, bagels. The menu also seems to have some kitchen prepared meals; however, seems though it's a difficult place to dine in with students sitting at the table for hours. Anyway, I ordered the caramel latte (iced) and my boyfriend had the mocha latte. Both were delicious and being lattes are mostly milk, it's nice to be able to taste the coffee in there. For quick bite, I had a bagel with their house made pesto cream cheese. The cream cheese was on point. Other than that, nothing really to brag about here food wise. I would come back for coffee and bagel.

Still great food, some cosmetic updates in the dining room make it a little less butcher shop and grocery store-esque. Chef and owner are still the same and thankfully so is the food! Hands down the best Pakistani food, and will even give Indian restaurants a run for their money!

Look out other Vietnamese restaurants (u know who u r) there's a new sheriff in town!! I just had their Pho, but that's enough to let me know these guys are the real deal. I haven't had Viet food this good since my Seattle days. Aaaahh sweet memories. The flavors were all there with lots of onions and rice noodles and those little globules of flavorful oil on top. Can't wait to try their sandwiches and other dishes! Lovely owners too! This place is gonna be hella busy for a while since it just opened, so go at off peak hours. Enjoy!

Bubble Shack sure had some great-tasting mango bubble tea. I enjoyed it, just wish it would have been a bit sweeter! Other than that, friendly service and a menu with plenty of tasty options, so plenty of reasons to come back!

I love Remedy Cafe! There's no other coffee shop like it in the city. This place is always busy with all types of people--mostly bohemians and University students, but this place is very welcoming to all types of people. The tables, chairs, and couches in this place are ecclectic--making each area of this coffee shop interesting and different. Remedy has an inspiring atmosphere, so this is the place to have great conversations or to write (as long as you don't mind noise). The music they play is cool--usually a lot of indie ranging from rock to electro. I don't drink caffeine, but there are a lot of other choices like interesting cans or bottles of juices or carbonated beverages, Italian sodas, and alcoholic drinks. They also serve Indian food, delicious cakes, and other baked goodies. Remedy is a lively, interesting place--much better than any bar I've been to.

Huge dishes for extremely reasonable prices. I got the curry and received a huge bowl full of a mild curry, noodles, and all manner of interesting inclusions (whole hardboiled eggs, fishballs, scallops, etc.). It was awesome, and only $6.50. I was hard pressed to finish it. Between 2 entrees and a split appetizer, we grabbed the bill at 15.50 before tip. Unbelievable. The only thing that keeps the rating from being 5 stars (and this may be my fault for what I ordered) is that there were absolutely zero vegetables in my dish or my girlfriend's dish. I'm a big veggie guy, so who knows if you can ask for them as extras, but that'll be something for a later visit, maybe once the know me :)

A great family owned business that delivers on customer service, and most importantly, great food. I regularly come to have their rice vermicelli bowls. While it gets extremely busy during the lunch rush, I find myself coming back for more!

If you're a fan of Caribbean food, they cook up a mean chicken curry and Ital roti here. Ital is vegetarian, and the cook changes the recipe up each time, depending on which veggies she's got in her fridge. The shop's small and simple, with a counter, kitchen and drink case. Nothing special, really. It's all about the food here - and what they do, they do well! The roti shells are fantastic - full of delicious dhal puri - and I love the Champagne cola. It's the perfect bevy for a hot and spicy roti if you're not into mango juice or ginger beer. I've driven all the way across town through rush hour just to sate my craving. I haven't tasted a roti anywhere in Canada this good since I lived in Toronto and ate at Bacchus Roti Shop at Queen & Dufferin. They've mastered the roti - but this is as close as I've gotten, here in E-town.

Please do yourself a favor and stay away. I went here for lunch and couldn't have been more disappointed. I waited over 15 mins for anyone to take my order. Multiple guests walked in after and received drinks and had food orders taken. I understand you might be busy, but the professionalism of your staff leaves much to be desired. Service like that won't keep a restaurant in business.

Not that great. The toro was hard to consume, really not pleasant--especially for what supposedly most special, and the last hand roll I had was nearly unpalatable. The tamago was alright, though definitely not the best I have had. The service was kind, however, and the quail egg on roe was delightful.
Great customer service. Delicious food and good prices. I am not an expert at Pho (my second time) but it was tasty and the place was packed, so it must be good right :)

I'm a Newtown local, but have never before Sunday night "eaten in" at Guru's - we've always ordered home and had it delivered or picked it up. An unexpected visitor was the occasion for us to see Priya, and the experience was a very nice one. She was very happy to have us as personal guests instead of the usual routine of ordering over-the-phone and a resulting quick chit-chat at pick-up time. Arriving at 5PM (opening time) with the place not yet populated allowed us to have a more substantial dialogue with Priya. She introduced us to our very earnest waiter, a young guy who seemed to be very happy to have us there in general, but was even happier to tell us about all the dishes he felt we should try since he liked them so much! Rita (my wife) ordered a vegetarian dish, our guest selected some Tandoori, and I opted for Lamb Vindaloo, prepared "Indian hot". The main courses and the samosa/breads that we also chose were all quite good (tastier than our take-out experiences, since we were able to have the food almost immediately as opposed to somewhat cooled after a short drive home). While I'm no "expert" on Indian cuisine, in my earlier years I spent nearly a half-year total working in various Indian cities, where I sampled all sorts of different regional Indian foods, and Guru's is exceptional, Also, as prior Northern-NJ-ites before residing in PA, we've also had many meals in the "India" of NJ, the Metuchen/Edison area (with friends of families of some of those restaurants) - and Guru's favorably compares to nearly all of them. Visit some time soon and you'll be pleased with the food AND the hospitality.
An amazing food experience which lives upto the name. It's a fixed platter which costs 10 bucks and it's different everytime

Went twice for lunch., both times on a Saturday.BOTH times, was told by an apparently hung-over waiter, (who was nice, however) that there wouldn't be ANY jerk available for at least 3-4 hours! The wait for food was close to 45 minutes, and the food we did order was good, but being a jerk place, we wanted jerk. The prices were kind of high for the atmosphere and slow service. Doubt I'll evergo back and really cannot recommend it.

I am so glad I stopped to try this place. I really enjoyed the food. I had the chicken with humus and veggies my friend had the steak pita with all the trimmings. The Pitas are soft and fresh. It's like chipotle of middle eastern food. I wish there was one in my area. The service was great everyone was friendly.

In St. Louis, Olio is in a league of its own. This is my go-to for out of town guests and when someone else is paying. The chef Ben is a great host along with cook and the dishes rarely fall short of impressive. Service has almost always been excellent and the staff is very knowledgeable about wine parings, cocktails, etc.

Had a wonderful brunch. Reasonably priced, especially for the portions. We had the chicken and waffles, French toast and crab cake Benedict. Also a side of scrapple and pork belly. The pork belly was very well done, not what we are used to in Texas, but it was good... basically thick cut bacon. The hollandaise was a bit too acidic for me. Just a tad too much lemon. Overall, great brunch spot. Would come again when we come back in town.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Fantastic food offered in a small space with a very basic decor. Had the most incredible chicken curry! Many goat options. The goat korma is very delicious. The bread is fluffy and super fresh. Nice staff. Most people order to go.

Came here tonight with my sister. Like the other reviews say, do not judge this place by its appearances. When you first walk in it seems like it could Definately use a little redecoration. But with the good reviews I had to try it! We ordered the garlic naan, chicken biryani, Butter chicken and chicken 65. The do not have fountain soda, they're beverages are all bottles you get from a fridge. The food was awesome! Loved the garlic naan which came with a cucumber yogurt sauce. We got mild spiced butter chicken and chicken 65, both delicious. The chicken biryani was bone in chicken, and awesome. The waitress was suppper friendly. I would absolutely recommend for a takeout place..

I'm nine months pregnant, and I was in deperate need of a bathroom. I completely understand business' protecting their bathrooms, but I offered to buy something - but I didn't have time to wait to be waited on, review the menu and buy first - before I used the bathroom. Apparently, that's a no go. Luckliy, Ten Stone across the street is much more understanding of a desperate pregnant woman's bathroom needs. If you are looking for a place that has no tolerance for pregnant bathroom seekers, this is probably the type of community removed place that you are looking for.

Definitely give this small business a chance. This place is tucked away in a strip mall, so it's easy to miss. The owner is super friendly, the food is delicious and reasonably priced. They also have great smoothies and daily specials.

I really like this place. I'm Puerto Rican and of course I was so exited to try it. The only thing I did not like is the miss understood about Calling "Mofongo" as a Dominican dish. No people "Mofongo" is a Puerto Rican dish and "Mangu" is a Dominican dish. I will be very happy if they change that on the Menu.
Always amazing! Never had a bad meal. . We bring friends so we can boast best italian food outside of Italy...yeah! Been there too!

I ordered a jerked whole chicken before opening time and went to pick it up shortly after they opened. I got two small lunch boxes of chicken costing $33.00 It was very very dry inside and out; I couldn't eat it. I've been eating jerked chicken for about 25 years so I know what it's supposed to taste like. I'm not one to complain about food then re-order. So I just left it at that.
Not bad, but very generic Punjabi food, wait staff does not acknowledge questions, but they do the requested task :)

Lunch for two. We started with saganaki (kasseri goat cheese heated in olive oil and flamed with brandy) I had the lamb gyros. Absolutely delicious. My partner had the greek salad - fabulous. A great lunch and excellent service from Michael.
Best Gyros in town! I've had my share of Greek food and this has by far the best tasting pita bread, meat and sauce! Wish I lived closer!

Can't wait to go back It was my first time there, but my wife's second so she had an idea of what the place was like. I ordered the steak shawarma bowl with baba ganoush and all the toppings with the tangy sauce and I really enjoyed it. My wife got the chicken shawarma bowl with the hummus and all the toppings as well, but got the tahini sauce. I actually thought her's had more flavor and she thought her's was better than mine. The place was clean and the workers had a good attitude along with patience in asking our questions. Definitely look forward to going back to this place.

I was a bit dissapointed with this Restaurant. I order the chicken swarma. Even though It looks really delicious the chicken was too salty. The fresh pita bread and the hummus was so tasty. If I come back will have the hummus and some falafel. The service was excellent.

We come here every week for our dose of pho. It's not that great when compared to what you'll find in LA, but for Tampa, it's the best you'll get. I always get their summer rolls and jalapeno steak. Yum!!

Been here plenty of time and its a hit or miss with the service and food. I wanted pho and crawfish. So I ordered an order a crawfish and it wasn't as flavorful as it use to be. It wasn't really warm either more on the cool side. I probably should of sent it back but I hate sending food backm then I got the pho mi krob which was really good. Eating the two together was good. Our service was good as well. We'll be back.
I was severely disappointed by this restaurant. I had a breakfast gyro, my fiance had an omelette. Both were very bland and overpriced. It's not worth it to go here again.

Possibly the best meal I've had this year was at this little gem. Our party of four accidentally arrived before the restaurant opened, but when they did there were already enough people waiting outside to fill every seat. We wanted to try almost everything, so ordered several apps and entrees to share. Our food came out at a good rate, we were never waiting between courses or had more plates than could fit on the table. And the food. Was. Just. Wow. Pita bread, shrimp pil-pil, and soft shell crab were the stars of the evening, but everything was good. My only regret was being too full for dessert. The place got a bit loud and they don't encourage lounging around with a line out the door, but if you come with an appetite, a couple bottles of wine, and talkative company you'll be sure to have a great time!

Our waitress decided that it was her lunch break right after she brought our drinks. She's the only thing one working and she's sitting at the bar eating her lunch as we wait for her to take our. She glances over once in awhile letting us know that she knows we're ready.

It's hard to find a decent cheesesteak around u-city. Well I just found one. By far one of the best cheesesteaks I've had around here. Better then Abners!! Worked in u-city for almost 3 years and see this truck everyday, never even crossed my mind to stop. Came here based solely on yelp reviews. So grateful that I did. I got a cheesesteak with hot peppers and their special bui sauce which is some kinda like spicy mayo. And it hit the spot. Definitely will go back...maybe even tomorrow!!

While visiting Tampa for the day, we were on the search for middle eastern food. We had stopped at a few places included one Indian restaurant (which will remain un identified) which looked like world war 3 in the kitchen. So we gave up our search and started heading back to our hotel when we saw Petra from a distance next to a barber shop. We decided to take a chance and check out the menu and alas we decided to give it a try. We ended up ordering chicken schwarma sandwich and a chicken schwarma dinner with hummus. I must say it was so delicious, I wish I lived in Tampa as my mouth is still watering from the taste. They have this garlic sauce that makes me all warm inside! I knocked one star off because when we sat at a booth, they had little ants crawling around on the wall.

My friends come to this place so much. This has got to be their go to spot after work. I'm not a big fan of hookah but they do have a lot of flavor choices and very affordable. Whenever I come here, I do see some students studying as well so it's really for everyone. The ambiance is nice and dark and even though I always think they don't have enough chairs, they somehow manage to fit all of us all the time. The servers are always nice and attentive. Their cocktails are just your regular mixed drinks. They're strong! and cheap! Very cheap. So if you're looking for a cheap place to drink and smoke, I recommend coming here. Parking is a little bit hard to find around this area though. You would have to park on the street since they don't have their own parking lot.

Best sushi I have had when it comes to presentation and taste! Peters sushi in Brentwood gives them a run for their money taste wise, but wow the rolls look incredible. Highly recommend either the umami, mango tango, or spicy hulk. Service was quick and non-intrusive.
Great food, good service and exciting stuff - I absolutely love it! The pad thai (wet noodles) with shrimp were SICK good!!! wowowowo oh and the pink sake (dont remember the name) was fun and nice!

Upon entry I was really confused and thought this restaurant was really big because of the wall of mirrors but it wasn't lol. The waitress was kind of slow getting to our table and taking our order but I will let that slide on account that they have a really great lunch deal which includes apps, soup, and then an entree for like $10-$12 if I remember correctly. I would definitely come here again if I'm ever in the area.
this is just simple, very delicious thai food. the staples (pad thai and pad see-ew) never fail, and the curries are some of the best i've had. good place to go if you're on the main line.

This is a tiny place which is very inexpensive and serve below average food.There is only one lady who cleans,serves and takes orders.She is very rude and loud and behaves as if she doesn't give a damn about her customers ! I have ordered a fried rice plate and it tasted like a Chinese fast food junkie place dish!

I visited Zaika for the first time last night and was so amazed by my meal and experience that I felt compelled to give them a review...they more than deserve it. First off, you are greeted by a most gracious and knowledgeable staff. Our waiter was patient while my party of 3 decided what to order, and gave us recommendations based on our personal likes and dislikes. We felt like welcomed guests in his home, and you could tell that he enjoyed his job. Our appetizers, Garlic Naan and Chicken Pakora came out quickly and piping hot. The Garlic Naan was no doubt delicious, it was topped with fresh garlic and fresh herbs, and was perfect by itself or dipped into the sauces of our main dishes. The Chicken Pakora was my favorite. It was flavorful, slightly spicy, crispy and especially wonderful when dipped in either the yogurt or tamarind sauces. We ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala, Lamb Korma, and I got the Chicken Tandoori. The Chicken Tandoori was a recommendation from our waiter and I am SO glad I ordered it. It was succulent, juicy, smoky from the coals/clay oven, spicy, and had a vibrant red color. TRULY SCRUMPTIOUS! Both the Chicken Tikka Masala and the Lamb Korma were complex, wonderfully seasoned, each had large pieces of chicken or lamb. Our only complaint was that there wasn't more of it for leftovers, but we did take home sauce and rice. In conclusion, when the waiter asked how our food was I jokingly asked him if the owners were looking to adopt a daughter. Yes, it is THAT good...go now!!

So happy to find out such a gem of Vietnamese food in this whole area. One of the best healthy Pho I have had in the whole US so far. The portion is much bigger than NYC Chinatown or even in Philadelphia (where Pho is also very good but seem low positive energy from the tourist service). Especially Thai Tea which is cooked by the owner, not made by industrial packages, is also a perfect healthy drink to kill. Yummy and much less sweet than I afraid and I love it. Please give this place a try and support for healthy foods and the only truly Vietnamese restaurants so far in the area. With a very reasonable price. We have lunch and to go for dinner and even breakfast for next day with only less than $50 (including tips ) and important thing is you feel amazing light and healthy after the food. I'm sure will come back and wishing they will keep doing their good job.

My friends and I (5 of us) had the pleasure of dining here last night. There were only a few tables occupied, and we decided to sit outside...it was great for people watching. The food was fantastic! We tried the ropa vieja, pork pressed sandwich, oxtail, and fried pork. We all agreed that this was a warm welcome to the area. We've all enjoyed the Cuban/Caribbean food from south Florida, and this was as close as we've come to that. The only reason they lost a star was the bill. We did not receive an itemized bill, which would have shown the auto gratuity. We had no problem with the grat, but we think the server was going for a double grat (thinking we wouldn't notice).

Don't know why we haven't been here before. Very good meal! My wife had the mussels as her entry and loved them. She even asked for a spoon to finish the broth. The salad she had (house) was lovely and the philo cigars as appetizer were very good and unusual. I had the Caesar salad and rigatoni amatriciana. Both were perfect to my taste. We will be back.

My first time in Philly and this place was a hit with my group! We came late (around 10pm) and the food was great! We loved that it was BYOB, since those are hard to come by in Cali. It was a Wednesday night in the early spring, so the outdoor area wasn't opened yet. The server was very nice and personable, she suggested a few places for us to go get a drink afterwards. I ordered the jerk chicken platter, and it was really good! It was spicy, for sure, but I also ordered cornbread to help cool my mouth down! The rest of my group ordered things like coconut shrimp, BBQ chicken, curry goat...and everything I tried was delicious! If I'm ever in Philly again, I'm going back! Hopefully for some live music as well! The inside dining area is small, but seems authentic to me! It was overall, a great experience!

There are a few places where you go and feel you have left your home country and dropped into another world. Sky Cafe feels like one of those places. You are no longer in Philly, you are in dropped into Medan, Indonesia. Your speciality is noodles (Mie Komplit) and also there rice dishes as well (Nasi Goreng /Fried Rice & Beef Rendang w/rice). The sauces and side dishes are typically spicy but they don't overwhelm the palette. Also there meat on a stick are great appetizers as well (Bebe/Pork Satay, Ayam/Chicken Satay). I typically get the beef Rendang (spicy dry beef with white rice) or the Nasi Pandang (a mix of beef Rendang and other small dishes of chicken and veggies). If you are not in the mood for a spicy dish, try the Oxtail Soup which will be perfect for a cold evening. If you trying to mix things up for your lunch/dinner plans, stop by and dig in at Sky Cafe. I promise you will keep coming back for more. P. S. They only accept cash.

My husband and I were looking for a local Thai place. We have been searching for good Thai and most places were fails or just okay. I saw the great reviews on this place and gave it a try. It's located in the giant shopping center, which made me think it would not be so good, but I was wrong. We ordered take out from here 3 nights in a row! Their food is amazing. We tried the Thai crepe, pad Thai and the drunken noodles. We were impressed! The food was fresh, tasted authentic, the spices were not overpowering, and just enough on the hotness level. We re glad to find our go to take out for Thai. Hopefully we can try dining in next time.

There are a few Vietnamese restaurants in Goleta but this is the one that stands out the most to me. As soon as you walk into the room with it's colorful walls and pop radio station give it a playful casual atmosphere. I have never been here while it has been too busy which is great because that means less wait time for your food and more attention from the waiter/waitress. There are a ton of tiny little tables scattered around which are perfect for you and one other but they are also capable of holding a large group. The workers here are all very kind and nice but I want to mention Jennie. She has been our waitress most times that we've eaten here and she now recognizes us and knows what to bring us before we even ask her. Definitely the perfect balance between attentive and overbearing. As for the food, I am not a fan of pho so I have not tried that dish here but I love their rice places and most of all their vermicelli. I love the way they introduce mint leaves here, it is not something I have seen at other restaurants. Also the beef cuts are great, marinated to perfection and thinly cut for small bites with the rest of your food. The vermicelli noodles are the perfect texture, not hard and not too soft. Would recommend to 7 out of 7 friends.

fastest, most delicious pho i've had in a long time. super great service, the waiter even explained the differences on the menu to us and offered his recommendations. The milk tea was really good too! They even came by halfway through our email and gave us more broth for our pho. Ramen was good, but i'd recommend the spicy soup. Great place to go on a rainy day :)
Stopped in for a drink and appetizer... maple hot wings very mild but yummy. Served with pickled veggies, also yummy. Attentive staff and nice outdoor location!

Fantastic breakfast sandwiches! Egg and sausage on a soft and fresh hoagie roll cures everything. Don't forget the salt, pepper, and ketchup, and the hot sauce if you are in the mood for something spicy. It's delicious.
great food good service must try food so good don't eat goat but gonna try it because of great seasoning and food just good
This is the best Indian Food! The chicken tikka masala has wonderful flavor! Love it

I sampled mumbai bistro for lunch today and i was pleased. small, bright, clean space. I agree with the reviewer who mentioned that the flavors are a bit muted in the cuisine, arguably to be palatable to a wider audience, but the food is tasty nonetheless. I opted for the $4.95/lb buffet bar, which changes daily. the chicken in the tikka masala was a bit dry. my favorite was the navratan masala. i've never had this dish before, but it is mixed veggies with onions and peppers in tomato sauce. yum! and mildly spicy. one plus with regard to the buffet is that you can take-out, which i do not believe you can do at the palace at the ben. all in all, mumbai bistro is a pleasant alternative if you are not in the mood for your usual fare. the prices are reasonable, the service friendly and fast, and the food decent. I will definitely return.

I'm kind of surprising myself by doling out five starts to Momo's, but when I can't stop saying "oh, this is so good" constantly throughout the meal I guess they deserve it. I've been a couple times and both times have been amazed by the food. Greek is never the first (or second, third, fourth..) thought that comes to mind when deciding where to go for dinner and except for the random Greek food I've had at various festivals, Momo's is actually the only Greek restaurant I've been to. But I definitely need to remember to come back more often. Everything I've had has been delicious. Thus far I've skipped over the spreads and salads and went straight for the cheeses. The baked goat cheese and saganaki are both good (I prefer the goat cheese). Eggplant fries, falafel, gyros all good. Actually the gyros are delicious! The lamb is so tender and yummy. Of course I had to try the baklava, which was not my favorite. But the peach bread pudding is amazing!!!! Definitely try this! They have happy hour as well as daily specials. And don't forget the belly dancers!! The only negative is that they allow smoking on the patio. I'm not going to rant about this again (see Mud House review), but what are restaurants thinking that allow this?!?!

In all fairness, we went back and tried this place again and I would like to say that we all had a marvellous time ! Everybody was very attentive and helpful including the very attractive blonde bartender. We loved everything...I am revising my previous review and we are going back tomorrow night !

I stopped by here today while I was waiting for my clothes to be processed at Plato's Closet and I am really glad that I did. The workers were very friendly and the place was decorated all out as usual. When I was seated I put my order in right away, a Pad Thai with Chicken and Thai Tea, my usual when I eat Thai. I was surprise when they brought me a chicken soup and eggroll because the order was $6.95. It turned out to be part of their lunch special! How awesome. Both tasted very good and the Pad Thai came out quickly as well. The Thai Tea was made very well and I think they put more than other restaurants because it lasted my whole meal and they already brought it out with water so I could sip on when I was trying to cleanse. Anyway good experience, loved it, will be back.

Absolutely delicious. I came here twice for dinner and loved it both times. The chicken tikka masala is especially delightful. The owner is a kind and jovial guy, an absolute pleasure to be around. This place really cares about their customers and their food.

I kind of held off on this place because I used to live 3 blocks away from Fu Wah in West Philly and figured that was the apex of tofu hoagie-dom. Fu Wah is its own amazing thing, but these tofu banh mi are much more similar to conventional Vietnamese sandwiches, which is to say GOOD. On beautiful, slim, crusty baguette, with tons of fresh veggies (cuke, scallion, lettuce, cilantro, jalapeno) and thin slices of spiced tofu rather than the steak-like deal on the other side of the river. Not better or worse than Fu Wah-- just a different animal (same price though --$3.50). And hey, there is definitely room for more than one tofu banh mi in this town.
Great! Their delivery is pretty quick, food is the bomb. Great selection too.

This place is perfect! all the way from the built in hide-a-way floor seating and no air conditioning to the lunch time buffet line and a plate full of the best duck you didnt order! The English can be rough and in the summer its more a sweat lodge than a dinner on the town but all of this and more is worth the last little dribble down your chopstick! Ive been eating at Siam since the early 90's and the food has been heavenly every single time. Favorites: Nam Sod, Mee Krab and the Pla Lard Prig is devine!
