Great food which is comparable to the flagship restaurant in Scottsdale, as they have brought over some of their kitchen staff. Good service, adequately staffed. Dining room is clean, bright and airy, with more booth seating compared to the Scottsdale location. We will definitely be back.
A go-to standard for take-out/delivery Indian food. Does the job to handle any cravings you get.
Chicken was crisp, seasoned and tasty. Mac and cheese will leave you coming back for more. Worth every dollar!

My first visit was dinner and the ambiance was great if you like loud Greek music and belly dancers. Today we went for lunch and it sucked. Waited five minutes for a menu that she tossed on our table as she walked by. Five minutes later we gave our drink order. Apparently they have a well outback and must manually fetch this water. Otherwise why would it take 5 minutes to make a glass of water? FYI they were not busy...maybe 3 tables taken. After my chicken gyro arrived I wished I'd asked them to put the head of lettuce on the side. That would have made the search & rescue attempt to find the teeny, tiny pieces of meat easier. I say meat cause I ordered chicken and it was so dry and chewy I thought it was jerky...but jerky has more flavor! The menu stated olives on the gyro..olives means more than one right? They should have just kept the soggy, wrinkly olive off my gyro...it was gross. If you want great, consistent Greek food eat elsewhere. If you want a loud, party atmosphere with a half naked woman dancing than this is your place. I refuse to go again unless a visiting friend really, really wants to see a belly dancer. I'd probably tell them they'd be better off going to Larry Flints!

I went to this restaurant because it was right across the street from the hotel I was staying at. I looked at the menu and saw the different options between the chicken, sandwiches, wraps, and salads. Since I read this was a soul food type restaurant, I decided to try the dark meat chicken tenders and the mac and cheese. The server explained to me that the chicken and the mac and cheese were sold by the pound. Two pieces of chicken tenders were $4.50 and the mac and cheese was $6.26. I had also requested a biscuit but I did not realize it was an additional $2.25 so I asked her to take it out. I simply thought that $2.25 for a biscuit was excessive. The chicken was okay but you do need to dip it into the dip to have some flavor. The mac and cheese was pretty good, no complaints there. I also got a Peppermint Patty cookie to try something new and it was also ok. I definitely would not return to Wishbone. For the amount of money I paid at Wishbone I'd rather go to BBP where I can get a delicious burger and a milkshake for about the same price.

Pretty solid breakfast / lunch food truck. Lady serving was courteous and recommended I get the hangover. It was 11am and I was pretty sober but what the heck. She runs an efficient shop as I got the goods in less than 2 mins. Couldn't even fumble my cash (ONLY FORM OF CURRENCY THEY ACCEPT) quick enough to pay before she handed me my goodness in tinfoil wrap -The Hangover Breakfast sandwich ($6 cash money): would highly recommend you get it with the bui sauce, their homemade version of spicy mayo. White bread sub with egg, bacon, ham and sausage inside. Pretty standard breakfast sub but the sauce gives it that zing Overall, good food truck. Would come back again. Only improvement areas for me would be offering whole wheat sub and accepting credit cards

Went here last week because where i was originally going was closed. Ordered the chicken red curry given it's a thai place. If i had 10 small pieces of chicken ill be exaggerating.. I basically got a bowl of vegetables. My friend had the green curry, same thing. My other friend got the panang curry he asked thai spicy, it wasn't very spicy. Aside from this, we all got sick from the food. One of them actually got nauseous on the way home. I just got a bad stomach ache. Personally wouldn't recommend it as a good thai place but the lunch price was pretty cheap.

Good cuisine, particularly the appetizer salads,but what happened to the soothing, relaxing Mediterranean music the owner would have during dining? All of a sudden he decided to say the hell with it and put on an fm radio station with rock or pop or whatever that garbage is and commercials to go with it? Nuts.

Pathetic service. I never ever wrote reviews online in my whole life but this restaurants poor service encourage me to share my worst experience there .i went to PF changes to celebrate birthday with another 12 people. First they took 1 hr to serve our starter then they took another 1 hr to serve our main course and we had to tell them again and again to serve us. They embarrassed me front of my guests for being a bad host.

Come here whenever I'm visiting from NYC the bartenders are always extremely friendly. The clientele is a huge range from mid 20s-30s late night to an older crowd earlier. Cocktails and food are always on point. Always meet great people here and unlike a lot of bars nearby excluding canopy has a great upscale atmosphere where everyone feels welcome. Great outdoor seating as well

The level of service is a reflection on ownership and this place really drops the ball. Do not expect much from this restaurant. The prices on the website are not the prices they charge you. I've even found a metal screw in my food before and I'm not sure why I gave it another chance today. The only reason why I'm being petty and leaving a 2-star review is because I believe in great customer service and today was a HUGE disappointment. It's a shame - the business is in a prime location in Downtown St. Pete. It should be busier than what it is, but ownership doesn't seem to know how to run a business for this city.

I definitely have to give this place 5 stars for 3 reasons! 1) The spring rolls were perfection 2) The Pho was also just so yummy & delic! 3) The food came out so freaking fast Yay Yay Yay, I'm going back tomorrow with a friend because now I'm craving their awesome food!

I love Mediterranean food, but among standard fare, even the best rarely surprises. This is where Suraya stands out. Even staples like babaganoush and hummus are elevated here, offering nuanced layers of flavor incomparable to what I've found elsewhere. I'll be dreaming of this spot as I try to reverse engineer these items from home. Also: the cruller is as good as they say -- don't miss it.
brought the parents, food is too good to miss out. What a great place!

First impressions are lasting ones. The hostess automatically said he didn't have our reservation and we had to show him the email stating we had one. Then all of a sudden it popped up. He seemed very standoffish and unhelpful. Definitely won't be back. I'm not sure what his deal was.
Great customer service! The servers were very nice and made me feel comfortable. Prices are a fair deal, and the grilled chicken sandwich was very tasty. Highly recommend the Thai tea as well!!

When I ordered the tofu pad Thai today, the woman asked if egg was okay in the food. I thought that was awesome! By asking that simple question, she made sure she wasn't giving egg to a strict vegetarian/vegan. Though I'm a meat-atarian anyway so it doesn't matter to me. But I thought it was kind and good customer service! I love it here.

I have been to this place a few times and every time I am reminded of why I like it so much. I have eaten in the restaurant for dinner and the lunch buffet and have also had take out. The restaurant itself is a decent size with table and booth seating. Service each time has been up to pare, they keep you filled on water and make sure to check on you throughout your meal. The lunch buffet had a pretty good spread of options. I always like trying the lunch buffet because its a great way to try things that you might not want to order a whole dish of at dinner in case you might not like it. Everything I tried was really good and fresh. Nothing looked like it had been sitting for hours. (Lunch buffet hours are 11:30-3pm - i think everyday but double check). For dinner/take out we have tried the Punjabi Tikka Masala, Palak Paneer (my fav), Lamb Korma and of course you have to get some Garlic Naan! Dishes are served family style, you get a serving of rice with your order and they ask you what you want as far as the spice level. I love it and will continue to partake in the delicious-ness! Note: I have also been to the Media location - check that location for a review.
I love the pineapple fried rice with chicken or shrimp... I call ahead and pick it up; never dined in. Place could use a spruce up, add some color. Prices are fair- portions are huge!

Screw these people complaining about the service... it's like a chinese take out place but with Jamaican food!!! Been here a few times and loved it every time. I get the Jerk chicken platter, damn I'm so full after each time. I always want to try something different, but can't resist the jerk chicken when I smell it!! I'm definitely a noob when it comes to Jamaican food, but their jerk sauce is close to my Jamaican friend's jerk sauce.

Consistently delivers well-executed Thai dishes. Right in the middle of town, this small BYOB restaurant boasts a lovely ambiance, particularly because it is full of exotic potted plants. They also accommodate take out and delivery, something I would guess people often do!

My group at work goes here for lunch so often we've taken to calling it our Manchester office. Terrific buffet for lunch. The staff are friendly and attentive, the restaurant is clean, the atmosphere is casual. A great choice for lunch, and I've heard that dinner is excellent there as well (although I've never been there for dinner myself). Fairly easy to find, and check out the Indian/Pakistani grocery (Seema Enterprises) in the same lot if you want to try some of that cooking yourself.

My boyfriend and I stopped here for some boba. We ordered together but got separate tabs because they didn't hear me when I said it was going to be on the same tab. It was whatever, so we paid and waited. I ordered a taro smoothie and my bf ordered a regular Thai tea w/boba. After waiting for a good 10 mins, they came out with a Taro tea instead of smoothie. I went back inside and told them I ordered a smoothie and the employee in the front gave me a confused face. Another employee came, I think it was the owner, I told him and he said they will make it after showing him the receipt. 5 mins it came out, it was half smoothie and half tea, and it was so powdery! I could taste and see the clumps of taro powder and cream. So freaken disappointed. Everything is overpriced too. Horrible service. Don't ever eat here!

Great food and wonderful employees. I go in with my daughter every couple weeks to get takeout and they will often give her small mango lassie while we wait. She loves it. We've tried several different dishes and are never disappointed!
Stopped by last minute this past Thursday night. Once again, another spectacular meal. The service and quality of the meal never ceases to amaze me. Going back next week!

Ordered from this place multiple times and each time i get delivery it stinks. I ordered the chicken broccoli and the beef broccoli lunch special for myself and my wife. Took 1hr 15 minuets for delivery from their location to my office, a 6 minute drive. Beef was over cooked and their was literally 5 pieces of beef and 3 pieces of broccoli, majority of the dish was rice. I called on 2 occasion to check on the delivery, 1st at 50 minuets and again at 1hr 10minutes. Both times the restaurant told me the delivery guy was 5 minuets away. Blacklist these jokers from your Chinese food restaurant if you're smart.

Solid Greek food and relaxed atmosphere. There's brick arches bisecting the dining area for a Mediterranean feel, good ventilation to keep the place cool, floor to ceiling windows plus skylights on one side to keep the place well lit, and tasteful Greek-themed art. Service was speedy, and there's WiFi available for guests. Oh, the food? My wife and I both had different gyros, and both were excellent and reasonably priced. I've had gyros off the street in Athens, and the gyros here were at least that good. Mine was grilled chicken and pesto, which is a fun twist on the lamb and taziki original. I'll definitely keep this place in mind next time I'm in the area!

I don't know how anyone could not enjoy this place if you enjoy Indian food. Every time I go I end up ordering more and more dinners just to take home and eat a day or so later. Yes it takes time for the food to be made, but they clearly tell you before you order that everything is made to order fresh! I wouldn't mind waiting a whole hour for one dish from this restaurant because the food is so excellent. If you are impatient or shopping with little ones you can go for a walk around the market and return for your food. I only wish they were open all week! My fellow vegans & vegetarians, this place will leave you well fed!!!!!

This is located next to an Army Surplus store. Great spot to pick up lunch meat, milk, fruit and veggies. Prices are good. Owned by a very nice Turkish couple, and they are always happy to answer a question. Try the round Turkish bread with sesame seeds. Get some Merve white cheese, roma tomatoes, green onions and olives here. Makes a great lunch. Baklava is good as are the home made salads such as hummus, potato, macaroni etc. They have a butcher who is very accommodating. He will double grind your ground beef to order. Good soups. Marinated chicken kabobs are delicious. Haven't tried the lamb & beef kabobs yet. Next on my list.

I love the veggie burgers here. It's literally everything I could possibly want on a veggie burger, tons of avocados, pico de gallo, lettuce, purple cabbage, red pepper flakes and siracha. I mean what more could you ask for for $4. It's really a steal. I think they make the burger patties fresh too? I'm not sure but they taste like it. This place is always packed at lunch with a huge line but they somehow manage to prepare the food so quick. I've also tried the chicken satay tacos and chicken and sweet potato curry.It was my first time trying curry so I don't really have any others to compare it to, but I definately liked it. My favorite here is veggie, it just can't be beat. The man who runs the truck is always really friendly too. My only critque is I wish they took credits cards because I rarely carry cash, but then I would be there everyday so I guess its best the way it is.

If it weren't for the bubble tea, I probably wouldn't come back. Every time I come here it's so smokey, like they just had a fire or something. And the same girl at the counter gives me the same grumpy/bored service, every single time. None of the employees seem bothered with speed and they all look annoyed at me for having ordered something.

If Thai Country Cafe had a better, cozier atmosphere, I'd bump this up to 5 stars. We've been here a few times- both eating in and also take out- the food is always excellent and the service is flawless. Dimmer lighting, a little less of the same light colored wood, and softer chairs would do this place wonders. The pagnag curry with tofu and fried corn cakes are fantastic. The corn cakes are sweet though, so keep that in mind when ordering them as an appetizer. I could even do them for desert. My husband loves their pad thai with chicken and crab rangoon.

Living in LA, I have some pretty great choices for creative, tasty and well presented food. Olio is a serious great spot when in the Luu. Always fresh quality and a super good vibe. Sit at the family style table and meet some new friends while enjoying great food.

First time at Francisco on the River today. It was easy to get to. We arrived at our reserved time and were seated immediately. There restaurant is small, but nicely laid out. We were seated at a table in the main entrance dining area with a great view of the river. I enjoyed the whole wheat garlic bread...hot out of the oven...so hot we couldn't pull it apart for a few minutes! It was crunchy and delicious. I had the Pistachio Crusted Hawaiian Butterfish, red skinned mashed potatoes and spinach. The fish was delicious. The pistachio crust and tender fish were a great combination. The butterfish alone is very rich and tasty, the pistachio crust makes it divine. This is a very hearty fish so come hungry if you order it. The mashed potatoes were nicely seasoned, as was the spinach. My son had the Porcini Chicken with red skinned mashed potatoes and a vegetable medley. He enjoyed his meal as well. After dinner, the coffee took a little longer than usual to arrive, but the dinner crowd had picked up by then and everyone was busy tending to the tables. The staff was very friendly and attentive, even with the wait. This was definitely a good place to eat and will be on our list of places to visit again.

This is one of the more convenient venues for snacking on nibbly little things and getting slightly drunk with friends. The decor is mildly funny, the waitstaff is friendly, and its location on beach drive means that it's a great place for people watching. While there are better dinner options nearby, it's good to make this a stop before dinner to check out some cocktails and appetizers - generally I've gone for oysters and flatbreads.

Nice neighborhood cafe. Very cozy and airy. Excellent place to come and do homework. Amazing food, though I would eat in rather than take out. They do not provide the side salads and such when you order the sandwiches to go. Coffee is average, but the service is always excellent, even though it can be a bit slow.
First time eating Indian food my boyfriend and I now have a new favorite place to eat! Was absolutely delicious!! Thank you Persis!!
AWESOME!!! had the pepper shrimp appetizer... so so good! excellent service and the food was Great!!. Going to try to get back on a Sunday for the Buffet.

When I was first moving to St. Louis, a distant relative who was showing me the ropes took us to Olio. I had expectations of an Italian place from the name, but what I've found in that first time and on a number of repeat visits in the few months I've lived here has defied all expectations. It is easily the best restaurant I've eaten at in St. Louis. Olio charms from the first glance to the first bite. It's built inside of a converted oil filling station from the 1930's (hence the name). Touches of its past life are lovingly preserved, including spark plugs used as coat hangers and an old register sitting prominently near the front door. Overall though, it doesn't feel like a dusty relic but a hip, vibrant spot. When it's warm enough, the patio makes for a lovely evening, but the cozy modern interior is a perfectly fine setting in and of itself. But of course, it wouldn't get the crown as my favorite STL restaurant if the food didn't deliver. Plates are served in a shareable way, making it all too easy to try a wide range of tastes. In four visits, I've tried at least a dozen different dishes ranging from great to amazing. Overall, the food is fresh, flavorful and anything but standard. The most consistent highlight has been the Jerusalem Bagel, a must order. Served hot and fresh, this oversized oblong sesame-covered treat comes with labneh, olive oil, za'atar and pomegranate molasses... a perfect spread for all of that doughy goodness. In general, their bread is ridiculously tasty. While I tend to be a meat fan, the vegetarian-friendly dishes at Olio are what often shine the most. The Zucchini Carpaccio and Tuscan Kale both have sharp flavors balanced well by pita but delicious enough to stand on their own. Unexpected pairing decisions on many of these plates prove fruitful. The Sheep's Milk Feta plate is refreshing, balancing the saltiness of the cheese with sweet watermelon and bright mint, while keeping things grounded with shishito peppers. Olio isn't a place for those with a sweet tooth (I've been too full for dessert every time) and the pricing puts it out of reach of being an everyday dining spot (at least for me). But if you're looking to be blown away by a meal or looking to impress the foodie in your life, this place is off the charts good and well worth paying a little more. In Summary - Retro setting, modern feel - Incredibly flavorful Israeli food - Shareable, unique plates - Plenty of mind-blowing vegetarian options - Get the Jerusalem Bagel!!
Closed! Used to be my goto place for Thai takeout. It's closed now. Have to start looking now...

The food was really good, and the staff was *incredibly* friendly and helpful. It has a family friendly, pleasant atmosphere with enough variety for everyone. The kids loved the soda machine, and my only complaint was that the water out of the machine tasted really bad--not sure why. We will definitely come here again, though!

This place is great! Friendly staff and great food! Did you know that noodles and co uses all fresh items? In fact they don't even have a microwave or freezer in the building! They also give back to the community and support local schools! What's not to love? Give them a try, you will be surprised, I know I was!
Went there today with my friends, we had the mie komplit, curry noodle and fried wonton. Food is superb and price is very reasonable

Sad, sad to update so soon, to report that it looks like Latin Flavor has left the building. After a couple of attempts to return for some of that good cookin and finding the place dark and locked up during business hours, I'd hoped that it just due to the Wintery weather- remember that Spring snow? Yeah, but no. Last night we saw a, "For Sale By Owner," sign up in the window. Bad news!
Fantastic food! If you want something light get the Greko Salad. Don't miss the octopus or the Greek fries and Greko dressing.

Really great, authentic food, especially for a chain. I ordered the chicken shawarma pita sandwich, which was totally amazing. They have a good selection of menu items, with toppings that compliment the dishes perfectly. (By the way, if you're getting a pita sandwich, try the garlic mayo sauce!) They also have lighter options if you're not as hungry. Overall, it is really great Middle-Eastern food. If you are driving by, it is definitely worth going to.

A new place to the back of Chinatown, still a lovely portion and quick to serve. While it has less meat than some places, everything was piping hot, as opposed to only regular hot compared to some other places. And my table also enjoyed the spring rolls, and the place was cleaner than most in the area, which is a definite point in their favor.

This restaurant wins two awards, most expensive Thai food, and worst Panang Curry ever. This review is based on food, service, cleanliness, and overall atmosphere (food being most important). The food was below average compared to other Thai restaurants in the Bay area. I started with the Crab Rangoon and Mon Tod (spicy fish cake). The Crab Rangoon was mostly air, with about a quarter tsp of cream cheese. There was not a hint of crab in there anywhere. The Mon Tod was the only thing I enjoyed about the meal. I ordered the Panang Curry, but wasn't asked how (if any) spicy I wanted it. I didn't think about it until the food arrived. The curry gravy was very thin, almost watery, and lukewarm. It came with chicken and an assortment of vegetables, which ranged from lukewarm to warm. The kicker that made this dish the worst Panang Curry I've ever had was the seasoning. I didn't even know a curry could be make bland. I guess because I'm "Farang" they assumed I don't like spicy. They should have asked, because I always order Thai Hot! I like my food spicy. This Panang Curry had zero. The service was okay. Just a few small things like not asking the level of spice, asking for things multiple times, etc. The dining area was clean, and the atmosphere made me want to like this place. Unfortunately, the food just wasn't up to par. Due to the lacking quality food, low caliber staff, and overly priced menu, I don't see any reason to come back to this establishment. Another bummer: They have two frog leg dishes on the menu. We were there about 6:00pm on Saturday night, but they said they were out of frog legs. This is a planning issue. If it's not popular, take it off the menu, because all you're doing is serving up a big dish of disappointment.

The combination of pita and fresh french bread was wonderful, but the real stat was the hummus with lamb. Amazing! Its listed as a appetizer but its a meal. Very awesome. Great wine, fabulous cocktails. I can' t wait to go back and try something new!

My husband and I came for the first time based on the positive feedback on Yelp. We are native New Yorkers and are very well accustomed to authentic Dominican/Cuban food. Mi Caribe DID NOT DISSAPPOINT one bit. The food was EXCELLENT!!! We just hope the staff gets it together with their servicing the customers...slow and trying to find their way. But hopefully they will improve. They were very polite though.

Met with a friend who works at Jefferson's Hosptial and he recommended this place for my fiancée birthday. First and foremost, parking was a bitch. Took us about 25 minutes to find a parking spot, very typical for this area of Philadelphia. So plan ahead. While speaking of plan ahead, it's a cash only venue. The restaurant itself is very small and intimate. We had high table in front for 3 people. It was a small table and with a few condiments on there, it took up a majority of the space. I really enjoyed the complimentary grilled pita bread and oil. I ordered the Shrimp Pil Pil ($17), it's lightly breaded shrimp with a garlic and chili sauce on top. It's very garlicky with a kick! The portion came very generously with about a dozen shrimp . It was overly salty for my taste bud. The shrimp was crunchy and hard, each was a little inconsistent. For my main course, I had a the steam seafood which I was told that it's just a bouillabaisse with mussels, clams, tilapia, scallop, and shrimp. The portion is huge and it comes with a side of rice and steam escarole. The food reminds me someone little grandma cooking's. It was okay, the flavor was good but again a little heavy on the salt.
Good food and a nice place for dinner. I'm not a huge fried rice fan at Chinese restaurants, but Thai fried rice is one of my faves. Spicy and delicious.

Best pho and 7 dishes of beef in town. I've been coming here since I was a little girl. The restaurant may not be the best looking one but at least the pho is great. I wouldn't recommend any other dishes

I went there with the expectation of great pancakes, as it is calls itself a pancake house. However, the pancakes were just fair and it was not like you had a tremendous amount of choices on the menu. Our server took a while to get to us and when our food came, my side was missing. She was slow to come for a coffee refill for my breakfast companion and slow to check if we needed anything else. There are too many great breakfast options in the area. I will not return to Zacs, but I do wish them luck.

Great service. Great food. Great drinks. Exceeded my expectations. The empanadas were perfect and the dipping sauce was good. The Tripleta sandwich was delicious. Perfect place for lunch. We enjoyed it very much!

I've been here many many times, but have neglected to write a review. I've eaten in the restaurant and I've had take-out. The owner is incredibly helpful and attentive. With my most recent visit I noticed that they have hired a server. She was nice enough, but doesn't know the menu and was somewhat flaky. I will let that go though. She is new and the owner was double checking and ensuring everything was enjoyable. The Pho is phenomenal. I've had it a couple other places and by far this was the best of the bunch. I personally like the chicken pho, but have had the meatball and the beef brisket. The broth is so flavorful. If you are going for the first time, get the Pho. Their Bahn mi sandwiches are also very good. The owner recommended getting one as a appetizer to share. Yes please! As previous reviewers have stated, the spring rolls and egg appetizer are also really fresh and delicious.
Went in today and I must say they have good food but the customer service...SUCKS! They don't speak, throw the menu on the table and they don't smile. I won't return.

Alright lets start this out by stating I work for one of the best rated, high end, italian restaurants in St. Louis... This place is pretty good!!! I was surprisingly pleased with everything! The prices of the starters are super low, so i was assuming they would be bite sized portions, not true! The goat cheese, and red pepper bruschetta were amazing. The wine prices are decent as well, their selection isn't that amazing, but I wasn't expecting it to be. The Nero D'avola was nice. Our entrees were nice, but everything had a semi sweet taste to it which i wasn't too excited about but it worked. My boyfriend got the lobster ravs and i got the veal cutlets. We saw someones entree sat down next to us and the mashed potatoes looked amazing so we got a side of those too. The service was interesting lol. Our server was goofy, but so goofy that i found it entertaining. Coming from the industry side of things, the man was an upselling machine!!!! Genuine and nice i appreciated him greatly. The busser was polite and discrete. The hostess stopped by several times to make sure we were enjoying everything which was nice as well. I keep hearing about their happy hour so I will be back to try that out :)
Very tasty. Maybe a bit pricey for portions but good, fresh food. Easily taken as to go order if staying at local hotels.

This place was surprisingly good. I had the gyro combo with fries and a drink for 6.50. The gyro meat was tasty and moist, and fries seasoned. My hubby got the falafel wrap and it was delicious too! My pita chips were a little stale but still tasty. The tabouli was great! My friend ordered the pk salad with grilled chicken and it would have been a good light option. If on a diet, choose this! I will be back if I am near by, the owner seemed like a really kind person.

Nice ambiance and great quality food. The menu is a little limited. I expected more middle eastern options but overall a great experience. The cigar boregi was a really good. Flat breads are delicious too.

Stopped in tonight for a gyro plate because I haven't had one in a couple of months and the girl behind the counter remembered my order like I had been there yesterday. Awesome customer service and great food!

I agree with the reviewers that referred to this place as the Indian food equivalent to Chipotle. This restaurant is a nice addition to Wilmington's Loma section. The first step in ordering is deciding if you want a rice bowl, naan roll, or salad greens. I always go with the rice bowl. Next, you have to choose a protein. I won't bore you with the various protein options they have, but I do want to point out that there are a couple of vegan protein options. I usually order the Zaikka chicken, which the server said is spicy, but I didn't find it spicy. There are several Indian inspired sauces to choose as your condiments. The last things to decide on are the toppings: masala chickpea, cilantro, red onions, etc. I was glad to see that they have mango lassie. It's a little small for the price. The place is very clean, and the food along with service is good. Parking at times can be a little tricky. I'm glad to put this place into my lunch/dinner rotation.

Food is good, service is wonderful, but the atmosphere is lacking. The ladies there were very nice. I was just a little disappointed to see folding chairs at the tables. My first thought was that they would be uncomfortable. They weren't, but still... it doesn't look great.

Where can you go to get authentic Borek? Turkey, Yugoslavia, Slovenia, Israel, anywhere in the former Ottoman Empire, and Dooners in downtown St Pete! This casual spot, with outdoor sidewalk seating, is conveniently next to Empouria in case you'd like to try a unique brew. The food is savory/crunchy/tasty, potentially healthy depending on what you order, and quite filling, especially for the price. We had a nice relaxing meal, once we got past the perfunctory service, except when an aggressive bee decided it wanted to share. Me - 1, Bee - 0.

The chicken here is, well, just OK. They have buttermilk battered chicken pieces and several different dipping sauces. I tried the plain chicken and BBQ sauce. There really wasn't much BBQ to the BBQ though. It was also too thin. I also found the menu lacking in side dishes. I've heard the mac and cheese is really good, but I was looking for a lower cal option. I wanted something like string beans or collard greens, or even corn. The restaurant itself is very nicely decorated, and the service was great. I will definitely give it another try sometime. They had some awesome looking pies too, and my friend recommends their sandwiches over the plain chicken.

My sister was in town a few weeks ago and wanted to try a thai place around the area. We found this place and saw the great reviews and decided to try it ourselves. It is a very traditional place and the food is very authentic, if you are into curry and egg plant, you should definitely check this place out if you are in the area!
Was craving for dosa so went here. Place is decent nothing special. Dosa and another items are just about average.

Love Dooners! The portions are huge, the staff are friendly, and the restaurant is clean. I fell in love with the food truck before coming to the restaurant itself, and I'm in heaven ever time I take a bite!

Siam cafe has the best red curry in Nashville. The prices are very reasonable and the environment is very cozy and even though I showed up 40 minutes before closing the staff was still nice and did not rush my meal. It may not have the greatest location in town but it's definitely worth the drive.
Great food. The people who work here are nice. Must try the pho special, it's delicious. I can eat it every day of the week. Good prices on their food. Highly recommended.

OK - It's realy a 3 star place but our food and service were so nice on a frigid January night that I will round up to 4 stars. The place is, indeed, a "hut" - you have to walk around outside to get to the bathrooms and the decor is sparse - but Nikita - our server/cashier - saved the day with her congenial manner. To top it off my friend and I both loved our huge platters of Oxtail Stews in a rich brown saucewith plantains (not dry - very nice) and rice - fragrant with allspice and studded with beans. A $5 (ouch) side of roti bread was the perfect accompaniment. I loved my meal - and will return.

Went to Queen of Sheba based on Yelp reviews and extreme craving for veg-friendly Ethiopian food on business trip. Nice atmosphere, vegetarian/vegan options clearly marked with lots of options for non-vegans as well. Wine selection goes beyond the usual and Ethiopian beer a terrific option with everything. Seble (owner) was charming and delightful and, after having a cup of her amazing coffee (with her special spices), we bought some for the suitcase. Food was wonderful, including delicious injera. Patronize this restaurant! It is a Tampa gem.

At 6.95 for a lunch buffet, Taste of India offers one of the best valued meals in Reno. On the weekends, you have your standard spread - Tandoori Chicken, Chicken Tikka Masala, Vegetable Korma, your choice of chutneys, etc - AND goat! Compared to the lunch buffet at the 'nicer' place on Virginia, the food here has deeper flavor and more soul. The naan is consistently soft and excellent as you have the option between plain or garlic. Dessert offerings include rice pudding and the Gulab balls of dough in the cardamom sugar syrup. I look forward to exploring their other menu options...

I thoroughly enjoyed my vegetarian Chalaw Sabzi dish ($9.99), which came with flat bread and a salad with yogurt dressing. This place is a hidden gem and is much cheaper than Kabul Afghan Cuisine (2nd and Chestnut St.). My girlfriend had the Ashtu (sp?) and said she liked the Kabul's better. She also ordered the yogurt drink and found it more bitter than she expected. However, her experience did not deduct too much from my review. We both agreed that Kabul had a slight edge in taste quality but the Sansom Kebob's pricing makes the place a strong competitor for my business. On a Tuesday night, the place was empty. The waiter was nice. All I know is that I'm coming back to this place.

I have been going to Remedy Cafe for over 15 years - at the various locations. I have been really happy with them until today. I ordered my favourite, palak paneer with rice. Remedy has always done a great job with it but today, it fell short, very short. They used to use flavourful, real spinach, with a great mix of spices. Now it seems like it's bland, canned spinach, and the paneer just disintegrated. I am so disappointed. I won't be ordering that again, and I'm leery now of ordering anything other than their drinks. I do enjoy their great drinks (Kashmiri chai, lattes, etc) so I have given some stars. Please go back to your old recipe for palak paneer. Remedy was one of my favourite places to go!
Pad Thai was alright, however it was a very small portion which wasn't worth it for the price.

Amazing and authentic Indian food....Dosa and Biryani are best in town...Me and my family are regular here since they have started and have only seen improvement in quality with every passing day...Service can be little improved but food is awesome!!

Been here on 14th Oct 2016. Had Buffet. The place is crowded. The food overall is good but it seemed a little pricey at 13.99($14) for buffet. There are couple of chicken appetizers which are good. And the two kinds of biryani i.e., Aavakai Biryani and ulavacharu biryani are just OK. Beetroot Halwa for Dessert is good. Giving only 3 stars because of being pricey.

A poor experience turned around! The owner contacted me and was very understanding of my previous experience. I am pleased to say that I will continue to enjoy soco! Tom was caring enough to come out and apologize and welcome myself and coworkers back. Given that level of costumer care, I highly recommend this place again. They really do have the best gyros around! Thanks again.

I braved the cold today to try out this food stand, thinking that the weather might deter some folks. I was wrong because even the bitter cold couldn't dampen the loyalty of the followers of this stand! After over a 30 minute long wait, during which the owner was nice enough to serve us hot spinach and chickpea soup, I finally got my platter which had grilled chicken, falafel, hummus, a chickpea salad, a rice and lentil dish, a fruit salad, pita and bread..oh and he also gave me a small bottle of Perrier. All for $10. Everything was really delicious - the hummus and falafel in particular. In the end the wait, as well as the eccentric cook, are truly worth it. Will be back soon.

Had to keep getting to look around for the waitress (co owner). Each time I looked in the kitchen it was full of busy looking guys but no patrons seated. Finally got food. Great 'Israeli salad' but the Moroccan chicken dish was just clumsy and tasteless.

Where to begin? This place is pretty fancy. Interior was small but easy on the eyes. The staff is very good and so is the service. The prices are pretty ridiculous as well as the portions, but the food was good. Wish they had mor hot and spicy-ness in it but it was good nonetheless. The sam savera was delicious, and the chicken tikki marsala. Curry chicken was a tad bit bland but still savory. I have to say there aren't that many food options either compared to other places. Disappointed that the lunch buffet is no longer there. Service - 5 stars Food - 4 stars Prices - 3 stars Other - 3 stars

Fantastic! I felt like I wasn't in St. Louis... It was a chic, hip place that exuded fun and vibrant life that you don't always see in the Lou. I was happy to be seated on Valentine's Day without a wait or a bad seat. Olio is very small with lots of wooden high tops that create a rustic feeling. The large garage doors add such a wonderful atmosphere and effect on the whole wine bar. The menu is small-ish but wonderful at that. I had a great glass of Red and the fiance had a beer. Both were excellent and we ordered a few glasses. We split: - The Hummus - The Salume Beddu Plate - Kale Salad - Scallop Ceviche - Egg salad open faced The hummus was to die for. Very interesting and unique, wonderful. The bread that came with was soft and delicious. The Salume Beddu plate was a treat with 4 different meats. Everything was fabulous... I love Salami though. The kale salad was topped with a light anchovy creamy dressing and a few pine nuts for taste. The Ceviche was delicious, small but the perfect size for a few bites with a citrus-lime kick. The open faced egg was three slices of sourdough with the heavenly egg salad on top. I will be back for girls nights, more date nights and just an evening that I want to grab a quick delicious bite to eat paired with a savory glass of vino. Love!

I was really disappointed in this place. I'll admit, I only went because of the movie In Her Shoes. I've been meaning to go ever since I saw it a few years ago. I guess I hyped it up in my mind too much. I expected it to be a little more ... I don't know ... jamaica-ey. Not that I've ever been to Jamaica, but I was hoping the atmosphere there would make me feel like I had. The Veranda was bland. It didn't feel like a permanent space; more like someone's enclosed back porch decorated for a summer luau. I got bit by two mosquitoes and spent the entire meal scratching my foot and I was cold. I'm tempted to knock off a star for that, but I guess its my own fault for wearing sandals and going on a chilly evening. The food was great though! I got the jerk chicken, which was a good amount of spice (I could have stood a little more) and my roommate who is Jamaican swore that the oxtail tasted just like his mamas. I would probably give it another try with a warmer evening and a bottle of rum.

I like to consider myself a fried chicken connoisseur. I have gone great extremities to find the best fried chicken on campus. With that said, it would have to be Wishbone. Not only is it appropriately priced for the quality that you get, but the quaint establishment also provides one of the most ample varieties of sauces and extras to add to your fried chicken order. I drop like 15$ every time I go cause it's so freakin good. My favorites are the dark meat chicken, the corn bread, and the spiciest grade sauce (which strikes a harmonic balance between the spicy kick and the soothing aftertaste). Also, snag a rewards card on your way out. I thought I wasn't gonna use mine very much, but by the end of the next day I was 40% on my way to a discounted pound.

I just tried this place and my experience was a true mix of good and bad. The owner and staff greeted us enthusiastically and showered us with attention when we first arrived, and we like feeling welcome in a place, so that was nice, but once we sat down it was a little weird. We had so many different people waiting on us that it was a little confusing trying to figure out who our actual wait person was, so we never knew who to ask when we needed something. The actual meal itself was good. I had a nicely prepared filet that was less tender than I expected for $32, but it was still tasty. My husband had the lobster ravioli, which he thoroughly enjoyed. Both items were presented beautifully. They also had live music that added an additional relaxing and classy touch, and we loved that! After the meal was over, it seemed like they totally forgot about us, and then we ended up sitting so long that we just didn't feel like waiting anymore when they finally came back to our table, so we did not order dessert, but the desserts looked delicious in the case, so we might have to visit them again in the future so we can try one of those! All in all, we felt like the food was good, but slightly overpriced, and the atmosphere was nice, yet chaotic at the same time. No place is perfect, and it was good, but I think it has the potential to be even better with a little fine tuning.
Top notch hummus, lamb and swordfish. The steaks bomb diggity too

Recently ordered takeout dinner. Ordered Naman, appetizer and chicken Tika masala. Got home and opened up and prepared on my dish and what a disappointment. Nice container of rice but the similar size container with the chicken was in was mostly sauce with very little chicken. Very disappointed. Love the food and have been there many times before but not going to pay that kind of money for mostly sauce. Tried to squeeze 2 meals out of it but the leftovers only yielded about 3 pieces of chicken. Very bad. Will have to reconsider future visits.

We walked in and were the only non-Indian people in the place, which is generally a good sign. And so it was here. I've had a difficult time finding South Indian food in the Philadelphia area, so I was pleased to hear about this place. The menu is extensive, featuring lots of dishes from both the north and south. All the food I tried was excellent (and I tried a lot). My lassi was very good, too; I think many restaurants tend to oversweeten them, but mine was nice and tangy. The prices were also cheaper than just about every other Indian restaurant I've tried in the area. I can't help but feel guilty eating here, though, as it has to be the least environmentally friendly restaurant I've ever been to. Plastic utensils, styrofoam cups, styrofoam plates...and an Indian meal typically uses a lot of dishes, so those add up quickly. I'm surprised the tables aren't styrofoam, too, so they can just throw them away after every meal instead of wiping them down. Overall, it was a great meal, and I'll be back, though I might bring my own silverware next time.

Underwhelming is how I'd describe this unfortunate find. My husband and I have had Thai food, authentic Thai food in NYC and this place doesn't hold a candle. After reading the reviews and making a special trip to this restaurant, we were sorely disappointed in their soups and thai basil entree. The restaurant also charges extra for brown rice. The service was lacking--because water glasses were not refilled and they could not deliver two dishes at the same time. The only time service came quickly was when they thought the payment was ready. Needless to say, we will never return to this underwhelimg place that has the nerve to call itself a Thai restaurant.

We give the service 5 stars. They definitely tried really hard. Almost too hard. Which can be concerning or a red flag for food quality. We give the Food a half of a star. The food was not good. So I'm giving them an average of 2 stars. We had the fried rice (with choice of shrimp) per the chef's and waiters recommendation. The oil tasted burned. Or maybe the rice was fried in a pan that was burned. The vegetables (peas and carrots) both tasted and looked like they were cheap frozen vegetable. Why not use fresh and local seasonal vegetables? We also went with the waiter's recommendation of the green papaya salad which had a Vietnamese "jerky" that we were curious to try. The green papaya was sliced WAY too thick, and since green papaya - if not prepared well, is already a rather a 'hard' food to chew, then the thick slices of hard green papaya and with the addition of the ROCK hard jerky - this meal was almost impossible to chew. The jerky was truly harder than boiled leather. Little rocky bits of leather. Lastly, I'd like to mention that we had spring rolls for our appetizer and while these tasted ok, the amount of dipping sauce that came with them was so tiny. Like maybe enough for 1/4 of the spring rolls. My gut feeling is that the positive reviews on this place are written by the owners and their biased helpful friends. I wish this place the best. Hopefully they can adapt and serve better quality.
Great Happy Hour! The prices are very reasonable. The mussels are very good. I would recommend the shrimp scampi with Alfredo pasta.

Amber Indian is simply amazing! My boyfriend and I either eat in or carry out once a week. The ambiance and service inside the restaurant is wonderful. I always leave feeling refreshed from the conversation had because there are no distractions. Let's get to the food. Every. Single. Time. It is perfect. We find ourselves loving every bite. I highly highly highly recommend Amber Indian! You MUST try it!

I just came home from a wonderful dining experience at Sansom Kabob. The food was so delicious. The flavors were artful. I am definitely going back to try the lamb kabobs. The Baklava is heavenly and their coffee is a wonderful closer to a great meal. Our server was so sweet and pleasant. Excellent dining experience.

Disappointing to see this establishment started cheapening out. Used to come here a lot but now I'm having second thoughts. At the start they used to have good portions on meat and sides. Most of the orders with rice came with soup. Now the portions are disappointing and no soup in most of my orders. The food is decent but for the price and meager portions you're better off going somewhere else.

This place is definitely not fit for large groups. A total of maybe 6 small tables and only one employee on a Monday night. You walk in to the aroma of greasy fries, and the chirping of birds. A small fuzzy TV teeters above the front door catering to those who don't want to miss tonight's episode of Wheel of Fortune. I'd give the atmosphere a 3 or 4, because in some ways a small divey Gyro stop is endearing. As for the food I thought the Gyros were quite good, and definately a bang for your buck! $4.99 for a Gryo that is larger than your typical Greek Cafe at least. Great Yogurt sauce with a smack in the face garlic twist. We had a couple orders of greasy fries to share between our group of 5, mostly because we couldn't resist the stuffy aroma that lingered and lured us in. There was a little confusion surrounding the check, so if any advice I'd say check the math. I find it comforting when I'm at an "ethnic" food place and get someone who clearly knows there way around the kitchen...even if they may not completely have the currency system down. Our waiter (and chef) quickly resolved the slightly inflated billed. Overall I'd recommend it for a good dive Gyro place for a weeknight when you don't want to cook.

The service is impeccable. The menu is a direct representation of having specialty items and doing them well. I eat and could eat one or more everyday. I love the Sweet potato currry and the veggie curry. I have half of my work going here. It's by far the best truck on the strip. It's always jumpin, and the prices are fair.

Best Thai food in town...in fact...in the Tampa Bay Area. Sushi is also fresh and delicious. I have recommended so many friends to come eat here. None of them has ever been disappointed. We used to eat here once a week when we lived in Brandon. The restaurant is beautiful, traditional, and clean. The service is always friendly and excellent.

WOW! Delish! The Friday buffet was hopping, lots of guests and lots of choices. Easily one of the largest lunch buffets I've exprienced in Indy. It was diverse (lots of veggie and meat options) and included a lot of freebiees: naan, soda, and a dessert-type bread who's name escapes me. The staff were friendly and quick to refill our waters. Price point was comparable to other area buffets. The food was wonderfully spiced, rich and flavorful. There were so many option in the buffet I didn't come close to trying them all--guess I'll just have to go back!

I used to love Bahnn Thai, and have eaten there on many, many occasions as I have worked in the area for several years now. However, my last trip there will be my last ever. In fact, I am sitting here hungry writing this after receiving an order where the meat tasted, let's say, less than fresh. OK, the meat tasted like it was rotten. It was so disgusting, I could not eat it. I will never eat there again.

There was a time not too long ago where I said the F. Nazi served the best falafel in the city. However, the last couple of times left me disappointed and confused. Before, I didn't mind paying $10, sitting thru his bragadocious behavior, and waiting in line for half an hour since his food was so delicious. Instead of getting tender grilled chicken with rosemary and perfectly fried falafel, I've been getting dry chicken and burnt falafel with purple goop sauce over withered lettuce. Instead, head over to Mama's for a better foodie experience.

Last night was the first time we tried Yia Yia's and it was so good that we had to have it again tonight. We dined in yesterday and tonite we had it delivered. The service last night was impeccable and the food is better than anything I have tried in Tarpon Springs. Every day from 3-8 they have BOGO specials (dine in only) which makes their already reasonable prices even more affordable. We are so happy to find a place that is not only delicious but also delivers. The delivery tonite was fast and the food was beautifully boxed. They even threw in an extra baklava. We love this place!

This place is GREAT! Really delicious food, large portion sizes, and low prices! Ordered the philly cheese steak with fries for $6.99...soooo good! So flavorful and so filling. Really kind and welcoming staff, place is nice and clean for a fast food joint!

I drove by this place at least 5 times before finally trying it out. And I am sure glad I did! The food here is amazing. I recommend the chicken kabob meal. The food is cooked to order, genuine and full of great Mediterranean flavor. Its not in the best of the best neighborhoods, but its worth going to. One of the few ethnic restaurants in tampa that still have quality and true food in mind. If your ever in the busch gardens area, stop by this place. You will be glad you did.

This standard metal cart is covered in potted plants and copper pots. Steam billows up into the air. A pungent aroma of garlic and grilled meat extends over the entire corner of the street. No doubt the most attractive cart in the city. Order one of two things: sandwich or platter. What you will get is grilled chicken, falafel, and whatever else he has in the cart that day. He dances, sings, hums, tells stories. It's like dinner and a show, and you can expect to get a couple of acts because you WILL wait to get your food. You can ask for vegetarian (no chicken), and I believe you can request hot sauce. Ask for any other variation, and I hear he'll throw you out of the line. Only open from 11-2 on weekdays.

Can't say enough about this place. Food is creative and delicious. I always Look forward to Sunday mornings to see the rotating specials. Wife swears by the bacon egg and cheese quesadilla I love the seasonal pancakes. Favorite are the peach pancakes available in summer. Most of the dishes are made with local produce. Lunch is also stellar the fries are amazing and so is the Mediterranean wrap. Staff is always so pleasant. Really good food in a comfortable setting give blue plate a try you won't regret it!
I always get a fish platter from here on weekends and its the best fried fish EVER! The sides are so so... not great but edible.

I had a savory crepe and it was yummy. I had one sweet item and it was just ok. Also, the teapot stream was messy, spilling water all over the table as I tried to pour into my cup. I want this place to do well, but I have to say though, from the look of the goods, it does not appear that they are made from scratch in-house. For a place that isn't that busy, they have too much variety for sale, and this makes me wonder about freshness. My recommendation for them as a new place: cut down on the selection and just make a few high quality in-house items from scratch. People are looking for food with integrity (home-made, from scratch, no preservatives just all natural like real butter etc.), and will go out of their way to buy it. As people come to trust your shop, you'll sell more and be able to expand. But trying to be Duchess right away won't work. Duchess worked hard to establish the integrity of their food. Get rid of the gimmicky extras like chocolates and candies that look like they were picked up from bulk barn.

Pass.... The food quality was not what I expected. For what they were charging, i was expecting superb food. I ordered the shrimp with broken rice. What i got was 4 grilled shrimp on a bed of rice for $12. Been to better Vietnamese restaurant in Philly

Great middle eastern food! So nice to have this locally to go to! Friendly service, they make you feel at home, very casual facility. Very authentic food! So glad my family and I got to come here to try the food and celebrate my uncle's birthday!

Where has this place been?? 10 out of Tin. Found this place on Yelp and wanted to try Thai for the first time, and boy was I surprised. Clean environment, great service and the food is very high quality. Food comes out very quick. Tried the fried rice basil and the tempura crunch sushi and I will be back. I repeat, I will be back. You can make the food as spicy as you are comfortable with. OMG so many Snapchats with my friends to tell them to come here. Sorry China Bistro - there's a new Sheriff in town...and his name is Tin.
The food is very fresh and tasty! The price is reasonable. Their carrot juice is a must try!!!! Yummmmm

Mumbai Bistro Ordered On Dec 8 2013 at 1:05 PM 1 Saag Paneer $ 6.20 1 Chicken Tikka Masala $ 5.25 3 Tandoori Naan $ 3.75 1 Paneer Masala $ 4.25 The curries were watery and didn't have an even consistency. I don't think I've had a Saag that has literally been served with a layer of liquid on top. The Masalas were like indian soups. The flavor was pretty good, but the chicken was dry and the paneer wasn't very soft. Delivery was speedy. You get a lot of Curry for the price. So if you are new to Indian food you probably won't mind the lack of quality. However, if you are quite experienced with the cuisine as I am then I suggest trying another restaurant in the city. I give the taste 1 star, but because it was very very affordable. I gave them another star. I don't ever award stars for service (but the delivery was fast and the driver was pleasant), so the rating stays at 2 stars.

Went there twice. The food is average. To me and my boyfriend, who always go vietnamese restaurant, this place is not as genuine as some others. First, it serves too many kinds of food and have a long menu, looks like it really tries its best to carter all kinds of customers (which is not necessarily a bad thing, just me I don't find it too nice). Second, it doesn't serve tea but iced water, which I found weird. I think a vietnamese restaurant should charge people for tea! Overally the food is not bad, service is not bad, just don't feel like it's a vietnamese restaurant.

i dine at banana leaf probably an unhealthy amount. last week we decided to try something new -- erawan -- and loved it! its just as inexpensive, byob, right around the corner, and the food is awesome! we tried the drunken noodles with beef, tom yum soup (the best!), pad prik king (a spicy string bean dish), and masaman chicken curry. everything was fabulous and although they somehow forgot about our reservation, we were seated quickly and the waitstaff was more attentive than expected. we will be back!

Ya done messed up tonight Umami. First you tell me 30 minutes for pickup when in reality the food took over and hour. You ran out of rice?? That's like an Italian place running out of spaghetti! Sushi rolls were not wrapped well and practically every piece fell apart. I've give high recommendations in years passed, but tonight was not your night.

Wow! The vegetarian platter I had here was amazing. Right after I ate it I couldn't stop craving it and dreamt of coming back for more. Big servings, a littleeeee pricey but I feel like I got what I paid for. Overall, I had a really great lunch with my friend and was impressed by the food. Bonus: you get to choose what goes on the plate which I loved.

Jasmine Thai is a small business that strives to make diners feel at home. The ambiance is relaxed and waitresses wear traditional Thai clothing. Two recommended dishes are the red curry and spicy noodles. The red curry tastes fresh and has the right balance of coconut and spice. The spicy noodles are an interesting alternative to Pad Thai. Instead of stringy noodles theses noodles are wide and the sauce is spicy rather than sweet. Most importantly the service was kind and attentive. We felt welcomed and valued as customers.

My wife and I had our date night let night and decided to try something out that we normally can't with our boy... he doesn't eat anything except popcorn and milk. :) Anyway, We very much enjoyed our night out. The food was so very good. I don't know about all these poor service reviews... maybe they've taken heed to the reviews and changed it up a bit? Our service was fantastic and prompt. I love that this place has made it for so very long. I hope that many will frequent this place. I like that we have a diverse selection of restaurants here in Reno. I had the beef combo so I could try a bunch of stuff, my wife had the veggie combo. Everything was awesome, it was a great experience for sure. I personally have nothing bad to say about this place and we plan on going back again and again.
Absolutely amazing buffet! Almost everything available. I already want to come back and regret getting full so fast. I'll be back.

I always go on Yelp to find a yummy place to eat and once again it pays off. There is not a lot to eat in Zephyrhills but this place is a diamond in the rough. The place has amazing decor and the curry chicken was amazing. You don't want to miss this place.

Decent food for the price and normally an enjoyable experience. The service is always friendly and they do a great job recommending dishes that you might like. The food is decent, but nothing out of the ordinary. I almost always end up getting a rice dish, although I have tried a couple of the noodle ones. My friends love the pad Thai (I have never had it, so can't say much besides it looks and smells delicious). I like the Khao Lard Kee Mao, personally. It's really filling and flavorful, but has no heat to it. The service is great if you're in a small group. But come here with more than five people, and it turns into a little Armageddon. When I came here for dinner, we were a little crammed in together. Our server was super nice and attentive. However, when the food came out, very few people remembered what they ordered. (Most couldn't remember the names of their dishes, but knew some of the key ingredients). Our waiter didn't write down the orders by seat specifically, so it got a little confusing. Somehow, everybody got a dish they were pleased with though. The other interesting concept this restaurant does for split checks took me by surprise. They come with a tray that has little stickers on it and you need to our the appropriate one on your card. The stickers are small and have the price of each dish ordered, but they don't have any names. Helpful for the staff? Sure... But it gets really confusing for us customers. We all just grabbed a sticker hoping it was ours and just went with it at that point. All in all, great food, fun experience, but they just need to iron out a few little kinks.
Greeeeeaaat brunch. Greeeat drinks. The service was good also. Not very expensive. The atmosphere is also very nice. Oh! and if you are not hungry, this place is good for going drinking and dancing.

The return of (IMHO) 1 of the top chefs in the country is an absolute triumph! Justin's passion and innovative desire to stretch the limits are now housed in a vision-fueled Vietnamese Bistro aptly named CreAzian. The initial offerings, while currently not entirely exotic, contain subtle surprises which allude to more palette-expanding dishes on the horizon. The interior appealingly screams of stripped down circa Moulin Rouge Paris bistro with accents of Southeast Asia. The walls are tastefully minimalist and your eyes are immediately drawn to the gorgeous, warmly-lit bar inviting you to sit down for a beer or 1 of their refreshing cocktails. The center floor tables feel like they're best suited for drinks and snacks while stepping up to the cushier elevated booths convey a more intimate, formal stage awaiting a show. And what a show. The pork belly lollipops are even better (and larger) than I remember them if that's possible. Meaty cubes of pork barely clinging to a glistening half of fat edged by an amazing char reminiscent of BBQ burnt ends. All of this richness is perfectly off-set with a sweet and savory maple glaze and chopped green onion. This precedes eye-opening (in both presentation and flavor) calamari and a "banh xeo" which (for the initiated) is not quite what you'd expect. The calamari arrives adorned with scallions in a thin, ribbon-like crater of wonton. The batter is light and crispy, containing tender slivers of squid. Like the pork belly, the game-changer is the glaze. Both citrusy and spicy, this sauce elevates the dish to a level untouchable by any calamari I'd ever eaten (and I've certainly done my part in decimating the world squid population). I've only previously experienced banh xeo once before, and it was the conventional thin egg crepe with a crisp and oily texture. This iteration was more of an omelette/quiche hybrid, filled with savory pork and shrimp. Wrapping up portions of this in the accompanying fresh jicama and greens resulted in a layered explosion of complex flavors including a "mintiness" I was not prepared for. You know when you eat a touch too much wasabi and it fills your nasal cavity? Well, I had a similar but nowhere near as unpleasant experience with the tiny mint leaves which came with the dish. Justin said that they're 1 of the strongest mint varieties in the world and I didn't doubt him having tried it. We finished an incredible (and surprisingly wallet-friendly) meal with the Creazian fried rice and tonkatsu ramen. The fried rice is definitely in the upper echelons of comfort food for most ppl who enjoy the occasional late-night Chinese take-out, and it would be perfect for soaking up lots of beer. The ramen is nearly the same as the legendary version offered by the chef at his previous restaurant. I'd go into describing it but I'd easily reach my character limit. Just get it. I can't wait to sample more items (including their papaya salad) from the menu. Word on the street is there will be a porchetta banh mi (vietnamese sandwich) as well as other never before tasted creazians (pun intended) from Justin's evil genius of a brain. I guess a follow-up review is in order.

I've had Albasha three times in the past few months. Today was my first visit during lunchtime. It's been solid every visit. My favorite is the veggie plate. You get 'a little bit of everything' it seems. Lots of food for a decent price. I will definitely be going back.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: This place is outstanding! My only problem is I always spend quite a bit more than I intend because I order 3x as much food after I walk in and the incredible smell hits me... On the plus side, I usually have leftovers for days.

If you love tasty noodles cooked with plenty of sauce, then this is the place for you. I'm writing this review as I use chopsticks my chopsticks like a dumbass to eat the noodles I ordered over the phone. I'm eating inside and the first thing I want to say about this place is that it is a little dirty but smelled like ginseng which is one of my favorite sscents. Wouldnt have known if someone was making ginseng tea back in the kitchen, but I did wish that they sold it. If you want to delight your taste buds then would recommend Top China for you. I was not even in the mood for Chinese!
Great food and great service. Nice little wine list too. Very comfortable to dine alone in this place too. Cozy and comfortable.

So came here with a group after a long weekend looking for pho after partying, sadly it was not the pho we needed. Compared to other pho spots the bowls were small, prices high, broth bland, tendon undercooked, no fish sauce, tea was an extra fee, the combo came with 1/2 a beef ball!!!! Add to this it took about 30 minutes to get all this to arrive at our table.

Finally got to go to this restaurant!!! I am a Cuban transplant from Florida and I really miss my Latino food. So we were very excited to try Mojito's food. First let me say that our waiter Lou made our visit perfect...he answered all our drink and food questions, made informed suggestions and made sure we had the perfect Mojito experience! I had the Lechon Asado and my husband had his favorite, Ropa Vieja! Both meals were cooked to perfection. The sauces provided to us were delicious. And the dessert of Flan and Tres Leches was to die for!! We were not disappointed (as I usually am when eating Cuban food at a restaurant). We will return and hope we always get Lou for a waiter...he made our day out to lunch a memorable!!

This is my favorite Indian place in Indiana! I always go for the lunch buffet, because honestly while I love Indian food, I don't know much about it and I just love to try some of everything. The naan is good, especially the garlic. I love the korma here, which is one of my favorite Indian dishes. The pakora is also good, as well as when they have aloo gobi or other cauliflower dishes. One time they had this picked potato dish that was just lovely. I used to always come on Thursdays for lunch, then when I mixed it up a bit I found they have other dishes depending on the day of the week. On Saturdays they also had chai tea. I love the galub jamun (sp? they are the honey balls for dessert). My grandma really loves the mango pudding. If you are vegetarian, there are plenty of options here (I'm not vegetarian, but I love vegetarian food and I'm not a huge meat-eater). There are also plenty of options for meat-lovers such as chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, and chicken vindaloo (depending on the day). The buffet is pretty economical (I think it was $9.99 or $8.99) and if you go on coupons 4 indy, you can get a dollar off the buffet. The servers are attentive and always keep your water full. I could honestly eat at this place every week. I would also say their food tastes better than India Palace on Lafayette.

Like the name, this place sucks! We waited near 5 minutes at the front entry and no one came to seat us. After a while we had to go get someone from the back room. There was only one server for 9 tables which normally wouldn't be bad but the service was awful. She was grumpy and nearly ignored us the entire time. The food was overpriced and NOT GOOD WHATSOEVER. Whoever gave this place 4 stars has never had good Thai food. We ordered some spring rolls that were pretty slim and were 3 for $3.99 (not a great deal at all). The Tom Kha (which took nearly 30 minutes to come out) was horrible, salty, and stunk. We also ordered green curry (which came at least 20 minutes later) that was the closest thing to a good dish that this place could serve. Additionally, everything was overpriced. Would NEVER recommend this to anyone looking for a decent meal.

For your money, the best Thai restaurant in the area. The family that bought the restaurant sold their other restaurant in Clarksville and moved to this location to be closer to their home. They have very consistent and tasty food. The service is personable and friendly, we've gotten to know the family that owns and operates the restaurant. For dessert, don't miss the coconut ice cream. It is imported and is served in a real coconut shell! It is a delicious way to cool down after a meal of spicy Thai food!
Really nice restaurant with good food and good prices, I went twice and I loved the felafel plate and the vegtarian plate that I ordered. As dessert I would suggest the walnut one!

A good all-around place to go for Indian food. Prices could be more reasonable and quality could be better. I never feel like the food is super fresh there. But there is a lot of variety and food is reliable and service decent

Question for all those who recommended this restaurant... why? Why did you like this place? Was it the burnt oil used to mix the stir fry? The chewy, unpleasant chunks of mystery seafood? Or perhaps the stale dry rice? I will never understand why anyone likes this place. I joked about it being unsafe to eat chicken out of a stir fry with raw mushrooms and onions. Just cause the vegetables are raw doesn't mean the meat would be undercooked, right? Wrong! Three hours later and I cannot be more than a few feet from a washroom. I will never go back. This was my experience here: We sat down. We ordered our food. Our food arrived. Naturally we started to dish it out onto our plates. As we were eating the server came along, said one of our plates was the wrong dish and removed it from our table. The dish that was removed was still pretty full and didn't really look 'touched.' I saw her walk into the kitchen with it and less than 30 seconds later walk back out to drop an identical dish onto another table. Now, maybe that was enough time to throw our plate away and pick up another one? Or maybe it was enough time to throw some garnish onto our place and take it back out to another? I am not sure and will never know. Every dish we had was terrible. The seafood in the noodles was very chewy and tasted old. The rice was not fresh. The stir fry was unevenly cooked. The only edible dish we were served was the tom yum soup. This was by far the absolute worst Thai food I have eaten in my life. I have never been to Thailand but, I have eaten at dozens of places across the Canada and this was nothing short of awful.
7:30PM, says they are open until 9PM and turn away patrons only accepting a take away. Lazy.... You lost my business for good before even tasting anything. Way to go people, way to go!

This is a snappy cafe to eat quick or hoard food in take-out containers and eat it at home. The food is good and so cheap. The guy who works there is also very friendly. If this was close to me I would pop in for lunch all the time.
GREAT food!!!! Try the plantains and yams. Lucious.

I came in last night right before their closing hours with two other adults and two little ones. The entire staff was very hospitable and kind. All of the food was amazing. Two apps bruschetta and an artichoke were unbelievable! One had the eggplant parmigiana, the special steak filet topped with crab meat, and I had the pollo alla bianco. Everything was exactly on cue and beyond our expectations. Great job to the entire staff at this fine establishment.

In a funny little backstreet just before Mercy Lounge and just off Cummings St. Ample parking, set up is a cross between warehouse/office basically garage dining. Nicely decorated, has a central bar with booths and some high tops around it. Patio outside. We split the slow cooked pork - Pernil, PR speciality $18 and Mofungo$5. Whilst tasty enough, the pork was dry and lacked any flavor other than pork, Mofungo (plantain with garlic) was tasty also - however both dishes felt that they had been made a few days ago. The portion was tiny more of an appetizer size for 2. Mojito was $10 in a small glass but quite strong, we also had a chicaito shot for $6 - Don Q rum with anise, the anise of course took over but it was tasty, I am a sucker for anything anise. Finished up with tres leches cake which was flipping amazing and I could have savaged the kitchen for its stash of this - pure crack. So upshot is - go with a group and split the dishes as its a little pricey for two peeps. Cocktails nice but again a little pricey.
The food here is so-so, but unfortunately the prices here are so high, that I won't give it another try.

Another great breakfeast at the Blue Plate .Great staff fast service only a 15 minute wait which is well worth it.Eggs normandy was very tasty .The pancake wrap was also very good ty blue plate .great place to eat .

Since it has been a few years since I first reviewed Pho 36, I thought I would do an update. Pho 36 is now my FAVORITE location for pho in the Indianapolis area. It is a great restaurant that is locally owned and operated by a Great family. Pho 36 would be the perfect location for someone new to Vietnamese cuisine & pho to take their first "test drive" of the options. I also think this restaurant would be a good choice for someone new to any kind of "non-American" cuisine to try to broaden their palates to something different than burgers and chicken fingers. The owner will take his time to explain menu items, answer questions you have, make recommendations, and even offer suggestions on how to eat trickier/more complex items like pho (especially in the case of pho. My husband & I both learned how to eat pho by basically spying on other people in other restaurants or by watching Anthony Bourdain eat it on TV, lol. We would have loved a real in-person explanation when starting-out). When we are in there, I love hearing him take his time to explain items, even when the place is packed. He is the waiter, server, busboy & cashier simultaneously, WORKS HIS REAR OFF, and still takes the time to educate his customers & offer suggestions if needed. The owners are also great about recognizing their regular customers. Case in point, when we were in last evening, after a 2-3 month hiatus (sorry :-(), he brought 2 iced teas to our table without us even asking. He knows us. Speaking of their iced tea, it is jasmine tea that is unsweetened (sweeteners are available) and it is OUTSTANDING. I feel like I probably drink a gallon of it when we're in there, and sometimes I feel guilty about that, but it's delicious. Another perk about this restaurant, It. Is. CLEAN! The dining room is kept in great condition and from the peeks I have seen back into the kitchen from the dining area (through the door or window), and it looks impeccable compared to some other restaurants in town I have had Pho in... Some people might complain about slow service, but this is a truly family run business with a small crew who all have to multi-task to the extreme. We don't mind that it might be a while until we get our check on a busy weekend night...because we know the owner is off providing excellent customer service at another table and will get to us when he can, and it gives my husband & I a chance to slow-down & just enjoy being present. A few of our favorite dishes at Pho 36: *Appetizer- Fried Rice Cakes with Egg-- This is our favorite appetizer and it is what we tend to start our meal off with each time (I think the owner has it written down on the pad before we even open our mouths to order now...lol). The rice cakes are kind of the consistency of little dumplings, that have a lovely pan sear on them. They are then sauteed with eggs & green onions. Then topped with a lovely pickled carrot/daikon garnish & black pepper. It is then served with an amazing dipping sauce that is so yummy I could drink it with a straw...but no worries, I restrain myself. *Appetizer- Spring Rolls-- I'm not normally a fan of the soft/cold type of spring rolls, but I like them here.
