The couple times we have had them they have been freshly made & delicious. * The Pho--- They offer several variations of pho, with most of the variations being what type of meat is served in it. There's no mystery meat at this Pho Shop!! (some would be sad by the lack of mystery meat...but I like easily recognizable cuts of meat). I typically get the rare beef with meatballs. My husband normally gets a combo with brisket & rare beef (I think). I love to super-spice mine with the hot sauce, especially in the fall when my sinuses start rebelling. I am always impressed with the quality & quantity of the garnishes that are served here (typically includes cilantro, basil, bean sprouts, jalopeno & lime...and a heaping pile of it). *The Vermicelli- it's outstanding here, and they offer several varieties of this too. My personal preference is for the grilled pork with eggrolls option...because it is like getting your entree with a bonus appetizer surprise in it. I love the delicious complexity of their vermicelli sauce here. For those that aren't aware, the noodles in vermicelli are served cold. This was a shock to me the first time when I didn't know, but it's delicious. *I forget the name, but they have a "pork in a clay pot" dish that is Delicious. It's served to you in a clay pot, with tender, delicious slices of pork that are in a bubbling-it's-so-hot sauce that is delicious (but very salty, be sure to drink lots of that delicious tea, as mentioned above). It's served with a side of rice. You can get it with catfish too, but I can't attest to how that version is, since I don't eat catfish. *Boba Tea--it's ok here. It's served smoothie style & it fills a boba tea craving for me (why aren't there more boba tea places in Indy?!)

My first time eating here and it was delicious! There was bit of a wait and it was cold that night, so that was not fun! We decided to order a few appetizers and entrees to share for the four of us. There are lot of suggestions to try the octopus. It was very tender and we gobbled it up. The sautéed mussels were also a favorite. Everything else was pretty good except for the chicken kabobs, they were really dry. Def a plus because its a BYOB. I wish they had more space but regardless I would def come back.

Always had a great meal here. Small but cozy, the staff is very friendly. The food is Puerto Rican Latino. I never heard of this cuisine until my friend tony b. of the travel channel had recommended it to me. I am now a big fan of the shrimp mofungo (mashed plantains with a savory red sauce with shrimps). The empanadas are flavorful too. Stop by for a great meal. Oh yes, the prices are great. Went back a few days ago, still excellent. My wife had the paella, it was great! I will be ordering that for myself too, packed with sea food, rice cooked perfectly. I was so happy when my wife took half her paella home. I enjoyed it at midnight!

Was going to Underground Arts for a show and this place was a block away. Decided to give it a go and very glad we did. Wife had rice and beans, I had goat stew with rice and beans and flan. Was 22 bucks with tip. Food was very tasty and the owner was very gracious. Highly recommend!

Pho Hoa is the place that got me hooked on pho -- Vietnamese soup filled with meat and rice noodles. The soup base is chicken or beef, with a load of rice noodle, some vegetables, and the customer's choice of meat such as chicken, brisket, or meat balls, as well as the choice to create one's own custom bowl from a variety of ingredients ranging from the basic to the exotic: fatty flank, tendon, and tripe, to name a few. My favourite is the chicken pho. You can also get vermicelli bowls, which are almost like Pho without the broth. The grilled chicken bowl is a portion of seasoned, grilled chicken, noodles, raw vegetables, and preserved carrots, garnished with peanuts and served with fish sauce to the side. I always order an iced Vietnamese coffee to drink. Pho Hoa has another Edmonton location in West Edmonton Mall.

I love this place. Great thai food and a wonderful staff. Always very welcoming. I've never had a wait but it is good to see this place is filling up on weekends. BYOB is added plus. I love their thai curry - it isn't as spicy as all that! Their tofu options are also excellent. Prices are just right for thai food. Far better food than the others in the neighborhood.

I come here on my lunch break at least once a week. The jerk chicken is amazing. The fried plantains are to die for. The beef patties are fantastic. I can't say enough good things about this place. I'm very happy I found them. You will not regret checking them out.

A very fine Indian Restaurant.The best part about it is the consistency in the quality of food; perfect every time. I've been here quite a few times now and have had 5 star experience each time. Paneer, channa and Biryani are my favorite and I cannot forget the thick kheer. The owner is a nice person to talk to and the hospitality is pretty good too. If you like or wanna try Indian food 'Spice N Grill' is the place!! I love this place.A+++++

I'll start this by saying that I love sweets and I was craving something a little different tonight. After reviewing the menu, I decided to try carrot cake, redneck pecan pie, as well as the mac and cheese. I decided to have it delivered and was pleased with the speedy delivery. I started with the mac and cheese, which I would give three stars alone. It was hot, deliciously creamy and cheesy. There's a good bit of spice but it's not overpowering. I don't think I'll order again soon, but if I'm out and looking for something interesting and filling I'd order it. Now to the more disappointing part of the meal. I realize that Wishbone isn't a full-fledged bakery, but I think if you offer a product you should be good at it. I can't speak on the carrot cake as I didn't receive that. What I got was a red velvet cupcake with icing that tasted and smelled vaguely of peppermint. It wasn't great, and the worst part--there was a hair in it. The pecan pie was a little better in comparison. The crust was soft, flakey, and wonderfully golden brown. The filling wasn't overly sweet and did remind me of pecan pie, though it could have been smoother. The whiskey, however, peaches threw it off. Not the worst I've had, but it could use some work. Maybe I'll try the chicken next time, but that won't be in the near future.

I look for diamonds in the rough, and this place was exactly that. Thank you, Yelp! I walked into this small Kurdish spot and was met by a nice gentleman who welcomed me to the establishment. I was completely open to ideas for lunch, so I asked him what their specialty was. It ended up being lamb shank (#1)! The shank was cooked perfectly - tender, moist, falling off the bone (yet not mush). It was served on a bed of yellow rice and included a small chopped salad and a soup. I went with the lentil and was happy with my choice. At the end of the meal I was asked if I wanted tea (um, yeah!), and gladly enjoyed the conclusion to my meal (with a ton of sugar, thank you very much). Long story short, this is the kind of establishment that I wish I could support more often if I lived in the area. They serve great food, check them out!

This is the first place I've been to since moving to St. Louis where I've actually said "OMG THAI FOODS". When I lived in So. Cal there was this great place less than a mile from my place that delivered, and was amazing, and I've tried a few places out here only to be disappointed by blandness. I ordered for pick-up, they were polite over the phone, the service was speedy, and most importantly it was delicious.

This place has great food at a fair price! Definitely recommend it to anyone. IV needed a new place and they are killing it! Also, the customer service is great! They are really nice and accommodating. The food may take a while but it is totally worth it! Best middle eastern food I have had in a while!

The vegetable samosa was exactly what I had been craving! Perfect. We ordered the lamb vindaloo spicy and holy moly was ever, but still super flavorful. This location has transformed into an Indian spot I could easily crave regularly.

This place is ok, but it ain't all that. This is a fine place to go if you are mildly hungry, but if you are looking to get your grub on, this is not the place. To be fair, I am not a fan of Vietnamese food so their asian fusion sandwiches miss the mark.

We got our order to go so not sure how the service and whatnot is, but the food was absolutely fantastic. Both got the chicken curry, with mine being a bit more spicy, and also got naan and paneer kulcha, just absolutely fantastic. Will definitely be coming back here very soon, hopefully to try the buffet.

I've been going to Spiros for years. Have always enjoyed it. My husband and I went and we had the exact same meal(Greek salad and Chicken Parmesan). We both woke up a couple hours later and we were both very sick from food poisoning. We were sick for days. Called Spiros to let them know and they were very rude and stated we could never have become ill from eating there. I will never go back and eat there again because they did not care even that we were very ill.

Came here for brunch. The place looks great and the decor and vibe is really nice. The water is straight tap and gross. Couldn't drink it and it smelled funny. I ordered brioche French toast (listed on the menu with whipped cream and berries) and it did not come out as expected (see photo). Instead of berries it came with a slice of honey dew and potatoes on the side. Overall rating the food as a 2 based on this experience but the venue is beautiful and the server was nice. Prices are very affordable. My French toast was only $10.

Just went here today and my goodness! It's amazing! I've had my fair share of pho and this is top 3 for me. You can taste the hard work that went in to making the broth. The brisket, meatballs and eye round were perfectly tender. This was my first and definitely not last time here. The location isn't ideal but that doesn't take away from the fantastic food they serve!!

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Small cottage house restaurant that is so good. Never would know driving by this is a authentic Thai restaurant. All fresh ingredients. Very friendly and reasonably priced. 1 appetizer of spring rolls, pad Thai, red curry with shrimp, 1 beer, two Thai teas, 1 desert of sweet rice with mangos only $44 including tax. I love how they will refill Thai tea for $1.50. Every other Thai restaurant charges full price per glass. This is a new owner so the previous menus of salads and vegan are changed. Sorry I never met the pass owners but this new restaurant is worth the time to try. Everything was made fresh to order. The young girl who served us was smiling and very delightful. Casual place, not dressy or fussy.

Salsa, so good! Found this place via Yelp and it did not disappoint. As a full blood Puerto Rican from New York I had high expectations and they succeed at every turn. Came in a group of four and there was something for everyone. We started with the beef empanadas and crab empanadas. I highly recommend the arroz con pollo...so so yummy! Server was super sweet and attentive and made the experience even better. Bonus was free parking which is alongside the restaurant.

I normally take pictures but guess we were so hungry, completely forgot about it though not a bad thing. Decided to pop in for dinner because didn't feel like cooking. Going to keep this real simple and brief. First place I tried in Lafayette hill so far, I like it. Definitely will be a go to Indian food spot for us. -chicken tikka masala (mild, I'd like it more spicy but the bf can't handle it). Dish was tasty with just enough flavor and sauce was perfect for dipping the naan. -tangy eggplant - I'm usually not an eggplant fan because of mushy texture. This one is lightly covered with tempura batter along with a light tangy sauce. Well done. -chili chicken - slightly disappointed at this dish, kind of reminded me of general Tso chicken, it was a little too tangy maybe. Overall, enjoyable spot, probably coming back for June 12 anniversary half off deal :)

Delish!! Great find!! I had their steamed dumplings and chicken pad thai. Dumplings were delish. Pad Thai had promise... but the woman did not ask me how i wanted it cooked... so it came out bland.... because i like mine spicy. So next time I'll know. Lunch comes with soup and salad for $8.00. Well worth! Great service too! I look forward to trying their curries.

GOOD STUFF! I had lentil soup (which was good but I wish they were not out of the traditional Moroccan soup called harrira) and I had a chicken shawarma which was pretty good. The food tasted like home-made stuff. Plus if you want to try authentic Morroccan mint tea, this place if for you. The owner was very friendly as well.
Fantastic food and with Happy there it could not be better!!! Awesome!!! We will definitely be back!! Thanks!! ------------------------ Went back again last night and once again it was fantastic!!
A GREAT option for late night food, possibly the best. My only gripe is quality tends to fluctuate depending on what time you visit.

The food was good and so was the service but it was GREATLY over priced. Do your self a favor and just drive to the center of collingswood and you will have food that is just as good or better for half the price. Tbere were 6 of us for diner each couple paid 93.00 which included a 20% tip. And no dessert. 2 couples ordered the antipasta so the waitress said she would bring 1 dish for tbe 4 of us. The menu says its for 1to2 people at 11.00. They charged us 44.00 should have been 22.00 they way i figure it. Rip off. One person had the special for 38.00 the others had regular menu items. Pasta portions were the size of a small house salad definately not worth 19.00 guests should not have to pay 93.00 a couple for an over priced antipasta and and a childs portion of pasta. Never again. Go to the center of collingswood for less money better food and you won't leave hungry

Came in with a friend and ordered two deluxe pho. Broth and meats were great but the noodles were on the cheap side. Came here wanting to order bun no hue but they don't serve the soup with all the proper meats so that was a blow. Still I was happy about the broth in the pho.

Pretty much echoing everyone else, I realize: - The grilled octopus rules - Whatever variant on "mixed grilled vegetables" is on the menu that day must be ordered - Cash only - Enjoy your wait for a table across the street at New Wave Cafe.

The expansion of Tiffin into the airy, bright Tiffin Etc. (same entrance) is a welcome development. The separate, easy to navigate menu, consisting of four equal parts (Signature Pizza, Stuffed Parathas, Kati Rolls, and Beverages) offers distinctly different options from its sibling next door. While I understand the restaurant's eagerness to include the ubiquitous pizza option, I liked the parathas and kati rolls better. The spices and herbs in the Masala Aloo made the freshly fried potatoes come alive Stuffed wheatbreads (parathas) were distinctive depending on the filling - we liked lamb with cilantro and chilies and the marinated onion and herbs versions). What is really unique are the beverages. For the less adventurous, Thandai (almond flavored milk with fennel and rose) and the Nimbu Pani lemonade will make addictive companions to the food, the Jal Jeera, a drink described as "Cumin,lemon, and black salt infused cooler" will, admittedly, take a bit to get used to (I began to really like it about half-way through). With the intensity of what seemed to be freshly pureed seaweed (earthy and very salty), this drink is really a very different beverage. As for the pizzas: I have no complaints except that boredom creeps in when the hunger pangs are satisfied, I preferred eating the whole wheat flatbread parathas. The bill is easy on the wallet, the people at Tiffin could not be nicer, a really tasty and excellent lunch experience.
Fun specialty drinks, good comfort food, and great service. We enjoyed the drink specials too. I will be back for sure!
Very small, casual, paper table tops with crayons to draw-- good for kids. Jerk chicken was very spicy!! Collards were sweet, plantains were undercooked, curried goat was really good.

Heard good things about this place so I decided to try them out! Got the fried chicken wing platter with double Mac ($1 charge for double sides) .. The macaroni... Oh the macaroni! So effin' good. I could eat tubs of the macaroni alone. On to the wings. They were nice and crispy but they desperately need SALT, SALT and more SALT. They are also juicy but once the salt or seasoning is on there, heaven. 4 stars because the price.. I could buy the ingredients of this meal twice for the price of this platter. $13 is ridiculous but overall, I would be back for the luscious desserts and cheesy macaroni and cheese!

Hands down the best Indian restaurant in the Western Suburbs that I have tried. Our go to place for Indian food ever since they opened in Bryn Mawr. I'm a big fan of the lamb dishes, especially the Malai Methi, Tikka Masala, and Chettinad, but so far nobody with us has gone wrong with any of the other menu items. Prices are at least as good as any of the other suburban Indian restaurants, and mostly a bit lower.

I decided to try this place cause it was new and the menu sounded good. I ordered pick up for the grilled beef salad. It was $8.64 and it was one of the most disappointing salads I've had. Because it was so small. Like a side salad portion. It was good but it's sad that I payed that much for a little salad.

I never found in New Orleans a very good Greek Lebanese restaurant until I went to Albasha. I have been there 3 times and the quality has been consistently excellent, and so has the service. I can recommend the rack of lamb. It really is lamb and not mutton. Many restaurants say they serve lamb, but you end up with mutton, not here.
WOW I was sort of sad the curry goat was boneless, but once I started eating I forgot that I was missing the bones. Thank you so much just what I needed.

This is an update to my 5/13/2009 review of Coco Thai. After writing the restaurant off many months ago, my friends convinced me to give it another shot. They assured me that the snarky British lady hadn't been sighted in quite some time and that the service had improved. Honestly, there aren't many places to eat in Narberth, and I like Thai food, so I allowed myself to be persuaded into going to Coco Thai one more time. I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised. The seating and decor is pretty much the same as last time, but it's a little place in downtown Narberth and not in Center City, so it's hard to expect a business like Coco Thai to be able to afford major renovations to make the interior really cool. My fiance and I sat outside for dinner because it was a nice evening, and Narberth was having its annual sidewalk sale, so there was music down the street that we could hear. It was nice, although the outdoor seating is a little awkward - I sat on the metal park bench that's in front of the place, while he sat in a chair opposite me. Our table was about 5 inches from the one next to us (because the park bench seats both sets of tables out front), so we heard much more of the conversation of the ladies next to us than I would have liked. But still, it was a nice evening to sit outside. Our waitress was a very pleasant young woman who was very punctual with her service. So got our orders right, and the food came out really quickly (unlike last time). I got duck pad thai, and it was so good that I ate it all. My fiance got the Thai basil with tofu, which was also really good. I'm still a little confused by their "spiciness" rating on the menu. Most things have four designations: no stars = no spicy heat; one star = mild; two stars = medium; and three stars = hot. The pad thai had no stars, so it was without spicy heat, as it should have been. The Thai basil, however, has 2 stars on the menu, but it barely had any spicy heat to it at all. There was just a tiniest hint of heat as sort of an aftertaste to that dish. To me, that would have been a 1-star dish. I mean, it was good, but I still think they should try to get their spicy designations more consistent so they don't end up with problems like I had last time (and I've heard my friends saying they've gotten dishes that were either unexpectedly too spicy or not spicy enough because they thought the star-system on the menu was accurate, like most other Thai restaurants). In all, though, I liked the food. And the best part of the evening was still to come. The chef makes her own ice cream! She personally came out and asked us how our meal was and then asked if we'd like any ice cream. Now, homemade ice cream is hard to pass up. It's even harder to pass up when it's available in unusual flavors. She presented us with several very yummy sounding options. I ended up getting green tea and white chocolate ice cream in a waffle cone, and my fiance got cantaloupe and honeydew ice cream in a waffle cone. Their best is apparently the coconut ice cream, but I don't particularly care for coconut, so that's why I didn't order it. When my ice cream came out, it wasn't all the way set, so it was a bit messy to eat. But I didn't care. It was REALLY good. It was smooth and had little bits of white chocolate in it, which actually gave the green tea a bit of a hint of coconut for some reason. It was delicious. My fiance's was also very good, and his was properly frozen. Plus, the waffle cones are awesome. So if you go, get the ice cream. You can also get the ice cream to go - just go in and order it, and in a minute you'll be strolling down the street in Narberth attracting envious looks from passersby. In short, I like this place better now. The food is decent, the ice cream fantastic, and the staff and chef very nice. So I'll definitely go there again at some point to make sure that the service stays punctual and pleasant and the food stays good. As long as that British lady doesn't make an appearance again, I think all will be well.
This place is great. The biscuits are perfect and the chicken is crispy without being greasy. I'm just a few visits away from a free sandwich on my bonus card. Surprised there are only two locations!

Hand's down Nadias is some of the best thai food I have had and definitively one of the better places to eat in Lansdale. Their lunch special is the best value, soup, appetizer and entree for around $11.. can't beat that! As a patron here for the past 4 years, they have become a bit short staffed lately so the wait time has been a bit longer, but it is well worth it!

This is an awesome dive bar slash Ethiopian food joint. I've never been there during live music though, too bad. Good things: - Amazing, cheap Ethiopian food--my introduction to the stuff. - Cheap drinks. Rarely any beer better than Yeungling though. - Good jukebox. - Interesting crowd--it's easy to find a friendly, semi-wasted new best-friend-for-a-night. - The space is really cool and relaxed, though sadly I've never sat anywhere besides the bar. There are low tables with patterned cushions that are pretty awesome. Bad things: - .....hmmm. The bathroom is kind of weird? - Drinks served in plastic cups. Eh. That settles it! Five stars! Wish I hadn't moved away from Baltimore Ave!
I went in a while ago for lunch, and was incredibly surprised. I had a fresh, tasty Massaman Beef curry and will certainly return!

The nicest people own this wonderful restaurant. The setting is fabulous. The food is indescribably good. We had the Strawberry Pecan Salad with Jerk Chicken and the Curried Chicken Lunch Plate. As an appetizer we devoured a Jamaican Beef Patty and it was to die for! For dessert we had the banana pudding and it's the best in town. They guarantee its the best or they'll buy you a free one. Oh, and where else can you get peach tea with real, fresh peaches in it ?! Do yourself a favor and pay them a visit! You will be hooked!

Food is always delicious each and everytime. The oxtail, and jerk are amazing. Still havent tried the curry goat or chicken but will do soon. Thurs - Sat the lines are long and sometimes out the door/corner after 6pm but worth the wait. They also have all kinds of sodas that are hard to find. Will be back.

Delicious and affordable are the fastest way to my heart and Golden Triangle is both. A friend and I stopped in a little after 6pm on a Tuesday. We had our pick of seats and got to ordering. We split the Roti Canai (which I had never had before, but will surely eat again) the veggie spring rolls (standard crispy rolls), and pan fried dumplings. Each of the starters were delicious and left me wishing I ordered more. My entree of the chicken pad thai was delicious and the portion was large enough for leftover lunch the next day. The servers were nice and kept our waters full. Can't wait to eat here again!

The area is pretty saturated with Thai options, but Thai Fusion is by far our favorite! Very spicy, so whereas I'd normally order a "medium" elsewhere, I stick to a "one" here. My husband has ordered "three" and we could barely eat it. Highly recommend menu staples: pad Thai, fried rice, any curry dish. The owner is a true delight. I hope someday they improve the dining experience so it feels like a nice dinner out, rather than a carry-out joint.

I had a very good grren curry, and the Tom Yum soup was marvelous. I do not know how this place stays open. I never see anyone eating hear or going through the drive through. The food is always very good ot excellent here.

Well that was quick... was with a friend from out of town and we often get pho. The first 3-4 times here was good food, good service. The last 3 times cold soup and little flavor, tasted like day old meat (dry) for bahn mi sandwich. They actually spilled soup in my lap once, a lot! I was cool about it but they didn't say sorry or offer anything. I was worried they were going to fire waitress. So today I suggested going back friend said not interested, we went anyway. Sat there for maybe 8-10 minutes and not a single person came to the table or addressed us. We bound. Inphamous Cafe...

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Excellent Chinese, Japanese, sushi and pad Thai. Very clean facility, good service. This will be a regular go to place for us.

We had a table of 5, and everyone loved the food! We ordered several small plates which were all delicious. The burrata, mushrooms, duck, and octopus were especially good. Also, Chrissy took great care of us! The drinks were great as well. The Negroni was top notch!

I'm rating this restaurant a well deserving 5 because of the overall professionalism and hospitality, being a very proud African Woman. I already knew what to expect as far as food, flavor, and spices. However, the Owner Sahmed and his wonderful staff has definitely stepped it up a couple of notches in overall dinning experience. I was greeted like a Queen from the door and before seated I was already descriptively told what was the special of the day and recommended a couple of different options off the menu. If I wasn't african and oblivious to african food, confining here would've definitely put me at ease everything was particularly understood! I already had my heart set out on their mouth watering Appetizers cassava fries and sautéed onions with my main dish, the Talapia fish with their very sweet but spicy pepper sauces alongside with the atcheke and fish my cousin had their seafood restaurant potatoe greens. This is a BYOB so it went really well with some wine from the local wine and spirits not too far from the shop. We both had great amount of food in portions with plenty for left overs. Which I was even more excited about! I will definitely be back here and I look forward to trying their cocktails as well next time. This is what black excellence in the making looks like to me! This Restaurant makes me proud to support the Culture!

Went here and ordered the basil fried rice with chicken, and the roast pork. The fried rice was awesome - I made sure to order mild and thank goodness because it was still pretty spicy. The roast pork is where I dinged them a bit on the stars. It clearly wasn't fresh; in fact, it tasted microwaved. I know some places prepare it in the morning then slice it up fresh, but at least that way it tastes pretty fresh. This just didn't meet my standards for roast pork and I wouldn't order it again. I would return to order more of the fried rice and to try the other dishes, though, as the prices were reasonable.

Basil Spice is one of my favorite restaurants in St. Louis. The food is consistently amazing. I too, start off with the Pad Thai when I first visit a Thai restaurant, and it is simply filling and good. In other visits, I have tried their different curries and panang, and they are really simple, fresh, and tasteful. Their appetizers are always piping hot, and the spiciness of their food is always tempered to your taste buds. I always feel like I can order any random dish off the menu and really will enjoy it. Make sure you try the gang dang and the panang aside from the noodles. Some cons to make it a four star rather than a five star: Servings can be small. They can also be a little stingy with rice on the curry dishes. During the summer, it is always warm inside, even with the overhead fans.
First time here. Had 2 chicken swarma's--(I liked how you could customized them, I'm picky and he's not) Great prices, friendly staff an super clean. I will return!

Remedy Café can easily position itself as a place for total free spirits. What an interesting place and what a unique crowd! I came in knowing that Remedy café serves best chai in town, and that Indian food here is worth a try. As soon as I stepped in, I made a mental note to myself that this place looks like a garage of a hippie dude in the 60s. The furniture is worn down and the walls are covered with posters and ads. Nearly every sit was occupied by cool looking young people who intently stared at their laptops. The girl at the counter greeted me with the big smile, and as she began preparing my order of tandoori chicken bowl and a cup of chai, I took a sit in the corner at the back of the café. It wasn't long before my food arrived. Tandoori chicken was perfectly marinated and a bit spicy. The hot cup of chai was sweet and comforting, and every bit as good as they promised. As an added bonus to all the great food and fun people watching experience, Remedy café is open till 2am every day (the kitchen closes at 11pm). Arm yourself with a laptop and come here on an empty stomach and with an open mind.

I love being adventurous with food, so when friends invited us to lunch at Queen of Sheba, we jumped at the opportunity. Having only ever had Ethiopian food once, it was great to have someone knowledgeable​​ with us. The place is really cute and decorated with interesting artwork and images. We got there just after opening, so we had our​ pick of tables. We all started with sweet Ethiopian iced tea, it wasn't very sweet but had a wonderful​ cinnamon flavor. Being new to Ethiopian​​n food, we followed our friend's suggestion to have The Queen's Eight Platter ($15.00pp). It comes with four chicken or beef options and four vegetarian options. As one of our friends doesn't eat beef we went with just one beef. Queen's Beef Tibs -beef sauteed with onions, jalapeno peppers, Ethiopian spices, rosemary, along with a special savory sauce) I found this to be a little bland and didn't see any jalapenos. The three chicken options were Doro​ Wot -free range chicken and hard boiled egg stew seasoned with Ethiopian spices and berbere. Chicken Dullet -marinated pulled chicken sauteed with kebe and mitmita. And, Chicken with Gomen - Seasoned chicken with mild seasoning, mixed with steamed collard greens. All had great flavor, and the chicken was really tender. With that,​ we still had four vegetarian​​ options too!e Misr Wot - Red split lentils simmered in finely chopped onion, garlic, ginger and seasoned with berbere. Ye Kik Alecha - Yellow split peas simmered in finely chopped onions, garlic, ginger and turmeric powder. Tikil Gomen - Chopped cabbage and carrots in a mild sauce. Atkilt Alecha - Carrots, potatoes, and string beans in a mild sauce. Everything was good​ and well prepared, but nothing was really flavorful. The platter was lined with light, spongy injera with another platter of rolled injera on the side. The staff was friendly and attentive; the food was good but not great. I'll probably give it another try and get an individual plate where I​ can request a little more spice.

We are visiting & read the other reviews, so we tried it. My husband & I both thought our meal was delicious ( he had chicken basil, I had drunken noodles). Unusual for us was asking h.ow mild or spicy we wanted it. The restaurant was nicely done, prices were normal, but the best part was the service!!! We will go back every time we come down here

So good! Always get my brisket and raw steak pho and it never disappoints :) the bowl sizes are huge! I recommend the small if you don't want to drown hahaha! Love the extra sprouts, lime, Vietnamese leaves they give! I always add them to my soup. all the apps are so good. Great service! I always come here for bite

I don't leave many reviews, but I was so happy to find this authentic Thai, family owned restaurant I decided to write this as we drive home so I would not forget. We ordered three starters. Steamed dumplings aka Dim Sum, which may have been the best I have tasted. After traveling in SE Asia several times this is a real compliment. The steamed rice rolls aka summer rolls, were excellent as well as the chicken satay. The father came out and explained how to properly use the four sauces served in special jars. (Their sauces are authentic.) we told him we loved the Steamed dumplings and he proudly told us he was the cook but his wife made the starters. We ordered the Penang Chicken Curry hot. My friend was a raving fan! For me, I do like spicy, but this was a bit too hot. Although it is about twenty miles from where we live, we are planning to be back with friends to share our new find!

I enjoyed my visit to Phan's Kitchen for lunch on a weekday. The restaurant is tucked away inside Washington Square Mall on the wing nearest to Target. There are a few decorations on the wall, but the general condition of the dining room was a bit worn. (Hopefully the place will be successful and can invest in new chairs.) There is a row of four-top tables on the left side of the dining room as I entered. The order counter/grill are on the right. I asked about seating/ordering and was told I could grab a menu and have a seat while I decided and then should return to the counter to place the order and pay. During my visit, there was one guy handling the phones, the grill, and the cashier's duties. So, even though I was the third customer, the order for my appetizer still took about 20 minutes (the entree came out much quicker as the boss arrived to help pick up the tasks.) I started with the suggested Lao Beef Jerky. Served on two green leaves, the jerky was tasty and had a nice chew, without being dry and tough. Not exactly a Wow! moment, but still quite good. I also ordered Pad See Ew which I've had many places that serve southeast Asian food. I had read that this place can really crank the heat, so I played it a bit too safe and asked for it mild. I think that robbed the dish of the fullness of flavor that I might have had if I had cranked it up just a bit more. It was okay, just a little bland. They do carry three sauces on each table, but I was afraid I would mess up what was a perfectly fine meal if I tinkered with it. The only real negative about my meal was that most places I've had this dish use the wide noodles that are a bit thicker and shorter. I checked and even the menu called for wide noodles. But my plate arrived with what looked like very long egg noodles (maybe a half inch wide and much too long for my limited chopstick skills to securely tug out from under the beef, onions, and broccoli.) The noodles just didn't have that texture and taste that I've enjoyed elsewhere. Overall, the staff was pleasant and took care of my requests for a fork, more water, and even a to go box since the portion was huge! I hope they continue to do well. Review #701

I think the reason they call place a jerk hut is because the people who work here are jerks. I didn't enjoy the service at all. And I didn't enjoy the food enough to make up for it. It's not a cool place to go. It should be. It looks cool. It's filmed in the movie In Her Shoes. Which I love. Oh well. The food I got was tasty which is why I'm giving it two stars. But come on. Anyone can make tasty food I'm not that hard to please. I'm not a food critic. But don't ignore me and my friends while we are sitting there waiting. It took so long for everything. And not in the polite hey sorry we are really busy way. In the hey we are fully staffed and there is nobody here to eat except you but we are taking forever because we just don't care way.

I absolutely love this bakery! I have been coming here since I was a child (back when it was Schmiemeier's, then Clayton). Thank goodness Bello's has retained their original sugar cookie recipe, they are the best I've ever had. My husband custom ordered "Grumpy Cat" cookies for my birthday this month, and they were able to do it! I can't speak highly enough about this local bakery. Way to go!

The food is absolutely fantastic, staff are very friendly and décor is nice and clean. We have been dining here since we moved here 2006. Appetizers we love are the Thai spring rolls with peanut dipping sauce and egg rolls with swet Thai chili sauce. The Duck Panang is my favorite. Duck Siam is my wife's favorite. Other excellent dishes are the Green Curry Duck and the very interesting Tropical Duck. Kids love the Pineapple Fried Rice w Shrimp, Pad Thai and Chicken Panang. Nice size portions made with very fresh ingredients, many of which are grown fresh in their own garden.

Geez!! This is the first restaurant I visited after me and my husband officially moved to south Philly, which is last Saturday!! It is a cute little family store which you know it is authentic right after you walk in. Based on some pictures shared by other Yelpers,I ordered Gyro Combo. It is very interesting that they mix beef and lamb together and make it flat. My favorite is their desert - baklava is always my favorite ;) I also tired Burma,the pistachio filling baklava. Yum yum! Definitelly will go back try other dishes on their menu next time since it is only 5 min walk from my house ! Another hidden gem found!!!
Wow! Affordable, AMAZING Thai food!! We love this place and our neighbors are totally addicted, haha! They just started offering lunch specials from $6.95. Amazeballs!

Pretty slow, prices been changing for the last month and so. I ordered over the phone today, and they told me it would take 10 minutes. I came in 11 minute later and had to wait 25 more minutes. The food is fine, not the best. And the portion is small. They should work on customer service!

There is a line everyday. I have walked by later in the day and there is no line, but it's past lunchtime. It's quite the testimony to how good this is. The cart is always decorated nicely. There is no menu. It's $10 and you choose a protein that is offered. You walk away with a delicious huge portion of the day's offerings.
Really good coconut soup and dumpling soup. Very clean. Very traditional tai. Very good food.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: I've been searching for a great sushi place in the area and this place is it! Great sushi for reasonable price and it's BYOB! It's a nice place if you want to grab a quick meal and not have to worry about over crowding or loud guests. The staff are nice and friendly, and the sushi is freshly made to order. You can even sit at the small bar and watch it be made. Overall I'm very pleased and will be back to my new found sushi place
A truly unique experience. The food was outstanding, décor was artistic, and the wait staff extremely pleasant.

Ok..., that's it, it's amazing. I've come here a hundred times, most recently being last week, and it's always always always the best Thai food I've had in the states. Pad Thai, Thai Basil, Cury soup are awesome!!! and great quality of vegetable.

I'm not sure how this restaurant got such great reviews. I've ordered take out 2 times and ate at the buffet twice and was disappointed every time. I've eaten at many great Indian restaurants in India, the UK, and North Jersey and unfortunately not only is this place not authentic, it really is not very good at all. Sauces were weak and not flavorful, the chicken was thin sliced breasts cut up and thrown into the ketchup/tomato sauce, desserts were unimpressive. Indian Garden isn't authentic either but at least their food tastes pretty good. I'm not trying to be mean, but can't believe all of the 5 star reviews.

When everything is closed so early around here and you start feeling hungry Zeko's is the place to GO! The food is Amazing! Love how they're open late ! Fast service ! People there are pretty cool. The wings omg so good! I'm hungry just talking about it best spot to feel your hungry need!

Wonderful food! Ordered Lunch Chicken Teriyaki Bento Box for Mom and 2 Sushi Rolls for me. Mom is a picky eater, I figured I'd get to eat most of what she didn't eat, but she ate it ALL. You could tell the Sushi Rolls were freshly made and had not been sitting around for an hour or more. We will be returning

Went there for dinner around 7pm with my wife on a Wednesday night. The restaurant was pretty empty with the exception of the bar. We ordered the Chicken Tostadas to start and every component of the dish was bland from the dry shredded chicken to the sad excuse for a citrus slaw. For our entrees I had the Ropa Vieja with white rice and maduros and my wife ordered the Pollo a la Plancha with white rice, black beans, and tostones. The Ropa Vieja was absolutely flavorless and tasted like it was boiled in tomato sauce, the rice tasted like boil in a bag rice, and the beans tasted old and microwaved. The maduros and tostones were greasy and cold. I could barely eat the Ropa Vieja and our waitress graciously removed it from our bill. The most flavorful and enjoyable part of the meal was the cilantro mayo that accompanied the tostones, but that was about it. Overall it was a really sad excuse for a Cuban restaurant. I went there a couple months ago and the quality was much better, but I think it has fallen victim to the New Hope restaurant scene; just another crappy bar with overpriced awful food. It's really a shame bc I was really excited about a Cuban restaurant in the area, but I rather take the trip to Asbury and go to Cubacan if I need my rice and beans fix.
Fast, friendly service, and consistently delicious, healthy food. I have been going here almost every week for years, and that probably won't change.

I went with my office colleagues for lunch. The waiter was really rude. They bought my friend burnt fried rice. When she asked it to be replaced the waiter said we will only remove the burnt parts and not remake the food and that he dint care about bad review. He then went into the kitchen and came back saying the cook won't remake the food. Very bad experience. Been loyal customers of this restaurant for 4 years. Will never go back now.

Not impressed/ went to website ordered by phone when I got to restaurant order amount was different from what internet menu by several dollars//also was supposed to receive a knot with my chicken salad and only received a rolled up pita bread. Thanks but no thanks
I'm very satisfied. The service was quick, the food was delicious, and I left full. Will definitely be back.

Consistently great food. Good for vegetarians and vegans (not a ton of options, but what they have is SO good). The hummus is my favorite in the city and the beets are amazing. There's a great snap pea dish with tomato sauce that can be vegan-ized by getting it without feta. Also a really good citrus salad with grapefruit & avocado. Yum!

I was visiting Edmonton from Miami and a friend suggested we go to Sofra. Best decision ever! Our waiter, Winston was amazing. He went above and beyond for us. The food was amazing. The meat was tender. The baklava was a bit too soggy for my taste but over all great food. He also made great recommendations as to where we should go for dancing.

My husband and I were pleased with our experience here. I had beef with broccoli and it was TERRIFIC. Tasty and filling, and not over cooked. My husband loved the beef with broccoli as well as the Hot and Sour soup. He is very picky about Hot and Sour soup, so this really means a lot! What I really appreciated is when you sit down, they immediately ask you if you have any dietary restrictions. I think this is great, because personally I cannot eat dairy, so they gave me a listing of entrees without dairy to choose from right from the start. The staff was nice and the price was not bad! Loved the dimly-lit ambiance as well.

Try the laab. It's not on the menu, but it is amazing! It is a minced chicken dish, very spicy (I warned ya). We also like the green curry, super coconutty & creamy! The service is fast & one of the waitresses here is off the chain, she's hilarious. Definitely an iffy area, but don't judge a book by it's cover this restaurant is a diamond in the rough.

Haven't been here for a while but going to check it out again soon. I LOVE this place. The Thai food is fantastic. My father in law used to live there and he said it is great as well. Love the satay, Thai rolls, both great appetizers. Love their curries, the Masaman curry is my favorite but my brother and wife love the red curry as well. Comes with lots of great veg in there too. I have had the duck a couple of times and it is always very good too, as is the whole fish if they happen to have it that day and a few of you want to share. Very friendly staff, ice cold Singha, what is not to like?

It was really good service. Food was tasty but I didn't like the rice (but that's just me--I hate parboiled rice.) I had the Kibby and that was delicious! The rice threw it off though--it threw off the whole meal for me. I'm used to jasmine rice with my Greek food. The Lebanese tea is different from what I'm used to from other Mediterranean restaurants....good but not the same. My boss really loves this place. I'll have to come back and try something else.
Wow! What a find. The sandwiches are epic and the bread alone is sensational. Highly recommend. I also have had the rolls which are a nice addition to your sandwich as a meal. Check this place out!

Given the inordinately large number of iced americanos I have purchased, I should probably write a review. La Va is great. It's a fantastic little neighborhood coffee shop. The beverage menu is pretty standard, and all the baristas do a pretty good job. I'm in here a few times a week, and I almost always order an iced americano. Occasionally someone lets a shot sit too long, but on the whole, it's pretty good, and I'm picky, so I won't hold that against the nice baristas. :) If you want to stay and sit, the seating situation can be a bit crowded, especially considering that there are way too many people sitting at a table for four with all their belongings strewn about like they're the only ones who need a table that day. If it's nice, I'll sit outside. I bring my one year old daughter here from time to time, and they're always really nice about holding the door for a stroller or binging my sandwich outside when I'm there with her. Their breakfast sandwiches are some of the best I've ever had. The pesto breakfast sandwich is my go to and it is fantastic. I always get it on a croissant. Highly recommend. Good coffee, good food. There is a $10 minimum on card, which is pretty standard for places in Grad hospital, but they will always let you put the difference on a gift card to use later.

Yes yes yes! Give me more! Once again I have found another Thai BYOB that has delivered. Seriously folks don't pass this place by. I came here with the lovely Teresa L. for a Groupon dinner and I am sold on both this place and Groupon. We had a diet coke each, delicious entrees, and a dessert for $10 bucks. TEN BUCKS. Dear Groupon, Thank you for giving me a new gem to spend my hard earned cash for delicious and filling food. I bow down to the awesomeness that is Groupon. Erawan, you have a new fan. I will be back and bringing my friends with me. This place is a big bowl of awesomeness paired with a glass of delicious. The decor is warm and romantic. The place is clean and well spaced. Don't be frightened if you see little white flecks floating in your water. The waitress informed us that they squeeze lime into the water. I really couldn't taste the lime, but I was also drinking beer/liquor. But the glass and water are clean. The service is spectacular. We had everyone but the chefs come by and ask if we needed anything. They were all very personable and wanted us to have the best experience possible. This place is perfect for any type of outing. Intimacy for dates, hanging out with the yelp ladies and gents, a birthday party (byob boozing), getting tipsy before a night of bar hopping, or a family outing. On to the scrumptious food. We shared the massaman curry and the drunken noodle. Both had the perfect blend of spices and I scraped my bowl of curry clean. The drunken noodle were also delicious. You could really taste the basil, but it wasn't off-putting. So so so good. And reasonably priced with large portion sizes. When you get the plates the portions don't look that big, but once you dig in the food is so filling that the portions are the perfect size. For dessert and a birthday treat we shared the Fire Ice Cream. We thought the had misspelled it, but no, the plate comes out on fire. I've had better fried ice cream, but it was good and hit the spot. So in summation: Why aren't you there yet?
Got to-go food. Very tasty. Will go back for sure. I had the jerked chicken. My wife had the curried chicken. We were both very happy.

Don't order from this place. I JUST got my delivery and it was close to horrible. But there are some good things that I can note. The food was ok and the packaging was great. I bought the traditional curry chicken and garlic naan (both were ok). But I ordered a masala chai and a mango lassi which was about 5 dollars, not much. When the guy came, I thought the bag was a little empty but I didn't know how big the dish was, so I said nothing, and I didn't look in the bag until I got to the kitchen. My order totalled 22 dollars and I have the man a 5 dollar tip. When he left and I got to my kitchen, both drinks were missing. I called the man again to ask if he had forgotten the drinks, and he said "no the restaurant didn't have them." If they didn't have them why did he take all MY MONEY without question. I'm pissed. Ughhhh. Anyway, if you're going to eat from here, go inside, it's better.
Food was good and better then I expected but the only thing that is gonna stop me from coming back is the price. Crazy prices. No thanks.

Every dish we tried was absolutely delicious. Me and my husband love indian food, we tried many other places in NY and Delaware but this one is a little different. Very flavorful, not greasy and good portions. We really like this place and continue coming back to try something new on the menu.

The waiters are inexperienced and can't handle customers during peak time. Had to wait for 20 mins to get their attention for a glass of water. After waiting for 45 minutes got two appetizers under cooked. Food quality used to be good when they started new. Taj is better any day when compared them. They need to manage things better. Their high price is justifiable only when they provide consistent quality food and service. Hope to see some improvement in the service, else this one is off my list..

All my friends love Vientiane but I just can't bring myself to like it very much. All the food I've had from here has been mediocre and the layout of the restaurant is a little weird so when you are stuck on the narrow side they sometimes forget about you and the service gets slowed down a lot. It is a BYO which is nice and my friends always like their dishes but I am just never overly impressed. I had the cornish hen this time and the meat was very dry and the vegetables weren't cooked much at all. The one detail I do like is that they put their rice in little baskets that make me happy to look at.

I had the Gruben yesterday - a turkey Reuben - that was curiously "grilled" with fresh cabbage slaw inside that was uncooked. Little did I know that the slaw side dish was the same slaw in the sandwich or I would have opted for something else. Bread was toasted on the outside but nothing melted or warm on the dry inside. We have some back-of-house instruction needed here. Iced tea was good and peeps were nice. The Bento box at the local Japanese place offers much better value for the same price.

First off, I want say that we grew up eating Vietnamese food at home and at the many Vietnamese restaurants in San Jose, CA. But now we live in Ohio and this is our best option. Okay, so we stocked up on the food! 1) We ordered 6 banh mi (ga, thit nuong, cha-bi, thit nguio), all were very good but the thit nuong was my least favorite. We had one there and the rest to go. The one we ate there was warm and toasty. For the rest, they packaged the veggies separately in a small bag (standard practice to keep the bread from getting soggy). They were very generous with the veggies. 2) We also ordered bun bo hue (spicy beef noodle soup), which was VERY good! I often judge the authenticity of a Vietnamese restaurant by this one item, and I can say it was indeed authentic! 3) We ordered to go: com tam suong (rice with pork chop). The rice was the right kind (broken rice), but the pork was way too salty, it overwhelmed all other flavors. But for those who ever tried to make their own nuoc mum (fish sauce), you know this is a learned skill, and they make a good one here. 4) Desert and other stuff: we tried two types of che, both very very good. We also bought to go Cha siu bao or (barbecue-pork-filled bun) and taho (sweet tofu dessert), all of which was very authentic and delicious! The service was friendly and fast. The prices were reasonable by CA standard, but cheap by Midwest standards.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: The Taj Mahal Boise is by far the best Food I have ever had! I have been coming here for years every time I visit Boise. I travel between Scottsdale, New York City, San Francisco, and Los Angeles all the time and have never found a place that even competes. The food is cooked from scratch freshly every day! Every single dish is extremely well engineered and Tailored for a dynamic family dining experience. If there was only one restaurant I could recommend, this would be it. Enjoy your meal!!

This is one of my favorite restaurants. A wonderful Thai owner & cook is the reason you will have a great experience. Lin has been cooking since she was a child. Her Bean Thread soup is so good, I order it every visit. Another favorite dish of mine is Pad Thai, again, always top quality!

OMG. I had the red coconut Veggie curry. It was soooooo good. My husband had the same but with Chicken on top, he loved it. We enjoyed our dinner so much we went back two days later. Really nice clean casual place with lovely staff. Just found our new favorite restaurant.

First time trying Ethiopian cuisine so I wasn't sure what to expect, but I loved the experience of eating with the injera (bread) from a family-style platter. I'm a meat lover but the veggie sambussa appetizer (lentils with spices and veggies in a flatbread crust) was awesome. My friends and I ordered the queen's eight dinner: chef's choice of 4 veggie and 4 beef/chicken samplers. Can request all veggie and mild vs. spicy. It's $15/person and the cooks prepare each platter based on how many people are sharing. Ours included the gomen with beef, tibs wot (beef in a stew with veggies), doro wot (chicken with hard boiled egg), ye kik alecha (yellow split peas), ye misr wat (red lentils), atkilt alecha (carrots, potatoes, string beans), and a couple of other yummy dishes. Though the platter didn't look like a ton of food, it was extremely flavorful and filling and we had quite a heavy take-out container of leftovers. Traditionally they don't use utensils but instead the injera, and the restaurant does offer silverware if you prefer. They also serve beer and wine; the Ethiopian amber was delicious. Docked a star as the server knew we weren't familiar with the restaurant or Ethiopian food in general but didn't bother to explain what any of the items on the platter was when he brought it out. Just placed it on the table and left. We later asked and another server helped us. There were only 3 other tables of patrons by the time we finished but they took over 25 minutes to get our check, and even by then were confused on what exactly was ordered/owed. Unique dining experience. Overall the staff was nice and the food was amazing. Kudos to the kitchen.
I've eaten here a few times. Really like the curry. Tonight I got takeout and was disappointed with the cashew nut entree - it had zero cashews in it. Will stick with curry next time.

My wife and I went to meet a work colleague, and her husband, here for dinner. She failed to tell me it was very very casual. Needless to say, my wife and I were a little overdressed. Nevertheless, the food and service was amazing. I had the lobster ravioli, fried meatballs, escargot, and beet salad. It was delicious. I'd have given 5 stars but my wife didn't like her filet, it was a little overcooked. Lol, I told her that's what she gets for ordering a filet in an Italian joint. Otherwise, everything else was great.

The first time that I went here, it was for a friends birthday. I was so amazed!! First, the restaurant is very clean and the staff are very friendly and helpful. They helped those of us who had never been there what to eat but to be honest, there are no wrong choices. EVERYTHING on their menu is delicious!! There is a great variety and it's all very flavorful and tasty!! After going here once, I have been back several times. If you download their app (which is a GREAT app, very user friendly, easy and informational and bright!) you get goodies when you eat there by saving your receipts! This place is AWESOME!

Its no wonder this place has such good ratings.. its hands down busting of yumminess at the seams... lucky for me, its right here in our hometown, but for most of you its probably not... and for those of you who love Thai food, or just food in general, I suggest getting your butts over the bridge, PRONTO! The crab rangoon is some of the best in Illinois, the thai food = above par... they offer beer (always a plus)- and i mean, it really just doesnt get much better than this... I am a lover of Chicken Pad Thai, and theres is the BEST I've had... and you get to choose your level of spicyness.There is a bit of a language barrier, but they normall get it right. and there is even a takeout counter if you're in a hurry.!

The food is delicious, owner is very friendly, service is excellent. We had the green chai tea, lentil soup and kabob platter (4 different kabobs) for two. Rarely do we finish our food at any restaurant but we left our platter (which is huge) completely empty. I could eat this good every day. Yum!!!!

Finally found a good ramen place!! had the tonkastu ramen here and it was great. Not too salty with good body and richness. Springy noodles and tasty toppings. The egg was not overcooked at all. Better than the other places in town. Also tried the oxtail pho. Good mixture of spices, however, a bit bland and the oxtail needs to be softer. Not bad overall. Also tried the pork belly pops. They were soft but a bit on the sweet side. Good meat to fat ratio (1 to 1). Ordered drinks from the bartender, good presentation and strong!!! Need to come back for the ramen!!

I have never ordered from the menu inside but I have experienced the restaurant's catered food items at two parties and the quality is excellent. It's authentic Afghan food. And the owner really takes pride in preparing the food with high quality ingredients and preparing it flavorfully, even if the meat has to slow cook overnight, as happened to be the case with a pot of veal stew ordered for a party of about 80 people. It was so delicious! The sauce was flavorfully rich and the veal was so soft and tender. Everything was great. He arrived on time and he made more food then expected. Check out posted pictures of a few of the items catered at the last party I attended. Price is pretty average but can get high if you order more variable items. With the last event, he gave the clients a low cost option (with average quality ingredients) and a higher cost option (with high quality ingredients). They choose the latter and it was worth it. Awesome catered food!!

when in st louis, it's hard to get authentic stuff, and most places try to cater to mainstream. anyways, this place was always more about the ambiance than about the food. belly dancer: mon., wed. & fri. lunches and mon.-sat. dinners
Went here last month and ordered drunken noodles at lunch time. The portion for lunch was perfect! The spices on it were amazing! Would definitely recommend it to anyone.

I've been eating here for years, and it never disappoints. They are the best Thai on the Main Line, and probably the region. The restaurant is a small storefront across from the LM police station. There is parking at several municipal lots within a block or so. I've had many dishes, but my favorites are Drunken Noodles, Choo Chi Duck, Red Curry, and the Rainbow salad. ITs BYO, so bring a nice bottle. Prices are reasonable, with most entrees under $16. The staff is very nice, but can sometimes get backed up when it is full on a Friday or Saturday night (reservations suggested those nights). Some dishes can be spicy, but for those that don't like spice, there are lots of good options too.

Solid vermicelli with a decent price. The staff is always friendly and when I've ordered to go I'm Not waiting longer than they say. Haven't tried anything else on the menu but I'll definitely be going back!
Best place to go and just point at an item on menu. Just go for it breakfast,lunch,dinner or a snack. I love this place. There deserts are even amazing.

A great middle eastern restaurant conveniently located near USF and Busch Gardens. At 5:30 pm on a Saturday night there were already a few groups of people inside, and by the time we finished eating, the restaurant was probably 75% full. After taking our order, the friendly waitress brought I over fluffy fresh pita, and some delicious homemade pickled vegetables. Yum! For my entree, I had the veggie appetizer platter since the waitress kindly let me substitute the baba ghanouj for extra falafel, and it was perfect. The platter consisted of hummus (heavy on the tahini), Israeli salad, some of the best grape leaves I have ever had, and perfectly cooked, crunchy, flavorful falafel balls. My companion raved about his huge shish kabob platter, and the chicken I tried from that was moist with great seasoning. No room for dessert, but maybe next time, because there will definitely be more meals here in my future!
La Ban recently reviewed this and hit it spot-on. It's a no-frills, affordable, delicious Indonesian meal. The chicken soup is my favorite.
Good renovation, inside-out of the dining area. Feel cozy, ambient good feel. Both Thai and sushi are delish. Friendly staffs

Food was okay, what was HORRIBLE was the man behind the counter, older guy, compared to all of the younger people there, hovering over the younger cashier (who was nice/pleasant). Went there for the first time with my mother. We ordered two different things, but were served the same thing. I asked older man behind the counter which was which was chicken, which was pork - he was rude. Took one of them back to fix/replace and, I kid you not, shooed me away with a hand gesture. It's funny, but that was RUDE. Rude enough to make me not go back or recommend that place to anyone. By the way, when my food went back to the kitchen, I saw two women picking off the chicken off of my meal and put it back in with the other not-yet-served chicken. The two women looked up and saw me watching them do that and then the rest of the chicken was thrown away - which I believe is the food safety law. Gross.

Yes, it's tiny, cramped, and noisy. Yes, *some* of the waitresses make you feel like you're an inconvenience. Yes, you may wait 2 hours to be seated. But going to this place, you should know what you're in for as far as that's concerned, and just be ready to enjoy some killer seafood, simple and fast, without the fluff. They love their grill here, and that starts right off with the bread basket. Skip the uninventive white loaf and go straight for the pita with olive oil (which could use a little seasoning, but I just add s & p to the little dish and it's fine by me). The grilled octopus is also a standby appy. Some might find it lacking in seasoning, but, like most of the seafood here, I find it to be so fresh and high in quality that I prefer them to let the natural flavors speak for themselves. Also as a starter, the avocado citrus salad is out of this world, with huge gorgeous slices of avocado, fresh fruits, and a light vinaigrette. The grilled scallops are so succulent and sweet that, once again, they need little more accompaniment than some lemon. The entree sides are the same across the board, escarole and rice, which are pretty ho-hum, but are really just plate decoration anyway if you truly came there for the seafood. They also serve an impressive seasonal whole fish, which you can have delivered to your table either pre-dismantled or, for the more adventurous, looking like it just came out of the water. To quell the waiting time, I've had the most success getting seated when arriving just as they open their doors. Get in and out before the place gets crazy packed, and snicker at the latecomers trying in vain to secure a table while you're enjoying your seafood. Failing that, chill at New Wave across the street - really reasonable drink prices, and you can pick up a 6-pack on the cheap if you forgot that Dmitri's was BYOB. Not that that's happened to me...
Solid quality of food comes in very generous portion. I have tried pho, banh mi and vermicelli. All good experience. I am glad this opened up in city!
Food was great. For the fried food they did over cook it a bit. The stir fried pork noodle was good. Perfect spice.

I'm probably not the best person to review a place like this because I'm not a fan of tapas restaurants, especially ones with a hipster flare, I find a lot of them to be pretentious. This place wasn't terrible, the environment was very pleasant, the service was great, and the food wasn't bad. I just can't get over the prices. I know you're paying for atmosphere and probably higher quality ingredients, but customers still want a value for their money. $10 a cocktail? I don't know, maybe it's worth it for some people but not me.

My parents and I came here during happy hour and were pleasantly surprised. The place is very clean and inviting. Their appetizers are amazing! We hade the chicken sake and egg rolls. So delicious! The food presentation was very pretty too. Our waitress was very friendly and helpful. I ordered the pad thai and didn't like it very much and they were very accommodating and offered us a free appetizer the next time we come it. The service was excellent and can't wait to go back soon.

Came here a few weeks ago because I was definitely in need of some thai boat noodle and saw they had this on their menu. Boat noodle is definitely a popular thai dish back in the homeland, but a bit overlooked here in the states. There was no one here around 5 pm on a sunday except another couple dining out, so it makes you wonder if this place is any good. It seems Indy has quite a few thai restaurants sprouting! I must admit walking in there was no one in sight so it is confusing whether to seat yourself or just wait, We waited and the hostess/waiter stated we can seat anywhere. We immediately were given our menus and water in some fancy glasses. Menu is overwhelming if you never had thai food, but since we have had it numerous times we kind knew what to order. We didnt feel like getting appetizers that day so we went straight to our entrees. We ordered pad ke mao - beef (med. spicy) and I ordered my boat noodle with beef (spicy). The boat noodle is very thick brothy noodle soup dish that doesnt need all the fancy sauce condiments like vietnamese pho. Just eat it as it is and I suggest going spicy because this dish is not great when mild. Be careful with those spice levels! I cant stress this out enough that that thai level spiciness is much different than regular spicy. We got our food quick and fast in less than 15 mins. Both dishes came out super hot! We both enjoyed our food and the portions was huge. It was a bit pricy but it being broad ripple things tend to be a little more for the area. I really liked the boat noodle and hope this place stays open because I would not be able to find this dish anywhere in indianapolis. We definitely be back because fall and winter will call for cold days so definitely I am going to need me some thai boat noodle!

Schlepped the family into Socos last Friday night to give it a try. We were very impressed with the quality. Every little thing was done right here, and for a fair price. Now as far as ambience goes, Araka it ain't. It's pretty much like a little corner deli - a little kitchen, counter, a few tables...and a beautiful mural that is very well done (and I'm not easily impressed). The AC seemed unable to cope with the heat on this particular day, but since it was probably 100 plus, I'll cut them some slack. We got the gyro deluxe (includes feta), gyro salad and hummus appetizer. All of it was very good, but I'm pretty sure this was the best hummus I've had, and it's a rare day we don't have some in the fridge. Give this little joint a try. They're putting out a good product at a good price. Greek food works pretty good for carryout, too.

$14.99 Saturday lunch buffet Although it is a few dollars more than its competitors, it's worth it. Very clean interior, large and spacious, with nice music (chillstep fyi), and a wide selection of food to choose from. Seriously, I've been to a lot of Indian buffets and when I say wide selection I mean it. There were at least 20 dishes and they were all kept very warm (they're individually heated with a fire underneath). We've had an issue with other places where the food just gets cold. Its mostly vegetarian options but there were a handful of chicken, as well as one goat curry, entree to choose from. We usually don't like vegetarian dishes but the ones here were seriously great and very flavorful. Also the goat curry had a good amount of goat meat in it as well and not overloaded with bones. Finally, there were two desserts to choose from and they were both great to cut through all the heavy spices. Five stars!!!

This place is amazing!!! Delicious cocktails, delicious food, and a great staff! My husband and I always stop by this place whenever we are on this side of Reno. The lychee martini and the ginger mule are two of our favorite cocktails. The BBQ pork vermicelli is my favorite dish.

Stopped in for lunch, got the Duo (gyro meat and chicken) plate with a side of hummus and fruit tea. Food was hot fresh and quick. Everything tasted great! The gyro meat was on the lighter side with spices which to me was the best I'd had.
Gyro was great. Perfect little stop for lunch. Great food and not expensive. It's hard to find a good gyro in St Louis and this is only the second place I've found with solid gyros

My husband and I were recently in Puerto Rico and fell in love with Mofongo. When we returned home, we were craving this delicious dish. We used Yelp to help us find a few places in town that serve Mofongo. This place's chicken Mofongo was very close to the one we had in Puerto Rico. It wasn't as good but it was really delicious. Their yuca is pretty good. It had a nice amount of mojo and was cooked until tender. Tres leches is one of my husband's favorite desserts. Theirs was a bit sweet for me. He liked it but didn't love it. The piece they served was huge...perfect for sharing. The service was fine and fast. The waiters weren't overly friendly but they weren't rude or anything like that. They were busy and focused on getting the food out to the customers. As soon as I left this place I already wanted to go back for their chicken Mofongo. Can't wait to do so again soon.

I actually really like this quick spot... Prices are not bad, food is tasty, fast to-go. You have to go buy some Jamaican food from here! And another plus, it's right around the corner from where I live.

Wow! Worth the wait in line. No need to order. You will get whatever is cooking that day. I was treated to an amazing, flavorful combination of rice with cabbage, falafel, grilled chicken, green apple and grapes with a spicy, sweet sauce. All for $10!!! I highly recommend this stand!

My husband & I are new to the area, and stumbled across this place. The food was delicious, although some dishes are little overpriced (compared to south philly) but definitely worth it! The staff were great, very friendly and attentive. The place was very clean and quiet. We've only lived in this area for a month, and have already eaten here 3 times! Also, our 2 year old son loved the food & our waitress was great with him. Side note: our son has a very serious nut allergy, which we informed our waitress about. She was great and very accommodating.

What a lovely restaurant for our office celebration. The adjacent parking lot makes it a breeze to pull right in, instead of having to scout for street parking. The bar is large with comfortable seating, a nice bar area with televisions and a loft. We sat in a cozy booth. Service was great and attentive, and our server was quite knowledgeable of the menu items. The house-made breads and olive oil were tantalizing and were on the verge of filling us up. We shared an order or arancini: gorgonzola, steak and potato balls served with a roasted tomato marinara ($5) -- it was two large balls . . . lovely and luxurious with a little piece of delicious steak in the middle. Entrees were: grilled pork chop ($9) and I got the grilled salmon with lemon and capers ($10) . . . I forgot what our other diner got. The pork chop and the salmon came with a lovely serving of spinach, accompanied by tomato and chunks of garlic. It was delicious. And the salmon was beautifully covered with a generous serving of capers . . . which was wonderful. After appetizer and salad . . . not to mention the fabulous bread . . . I took more than half of my entree home for another meal. Lucious!

I'm a big fan of Remedy. I've only ever had the Chai, but I know that is one of their specialties, and it is excellent. I'm sure the coffee is good too, but i always judge a coffee shop more on the overall vibe than the drink. I mean, let's be honest, you go to places like this to meet friends and have conversations, first and foremost. Remedy has a relaxed, cool, accepting feel to it. You'd feel comfortable wearing business casual, or hippie clothes, or workout gear, or just about anything else. I've also had some of the food, and it's great too. Try the dal. Also, I really like the recent renovation. Even with 50% more space they still manage to be full every time I stop by.

Truth be told, I created a yelp account so I could give this place five stars. It was a little busy but the staff was working like an oiled machine and I got my food in a cinch. The people working there are VERY eager to make you happy. You can tell they legitimately do care, as they do everything they can to accommodate you. The food was the stuff of the gods. The gyro I had was delicious, the sauce was perfect for the fries, and the portions were MASSIVE, whilst the prices were seven to ten dollars per combo meal. Everything in this place has "perfect for families" oozing out of it. Come here and I promise the only disappointment you'll be feeling is from eating too much.

Wanted to update my review to reflect my recent visits. I've noticed recently the owners (older couple) no longer there. It appears their daughter is now running he restaurant full time. While the food is still good (no longer great) I've noticed the service has went downhill. It seems like they just don't have enough staff to handle the large amount of patrons. Still a great friendly Thai spot!

My boyfriend and I love this place so much we eat here at least 1x a week whether it be take out or dine in. I'm vegetarian so I order the Paneer Tikka Masala with 1/2 potatoes because I got sick of so much cheese. I love that they made this accommodations for me. I have been to other Indian restaurants that simply responded "no" when I asked if they could do this. There are so many vegetarian options, but I get the same thing every time. My boyfriend always orders a dish with lamb and we've been coming to this place for about 5 months it's our obsession. Take out tip: You do need to ask for extras such as utensils, napkins, and plates. I don't know why they don't just put them in or at least ask. So remember to check your bag before you leave. I haven't been to the buffet, but for no specific reason.

Nice suprise in the heart of Trenton, NJ. Walkable from the Wyndam. Nice light Hummingbird Salad (more of a fresh light slaw very homemade and fine cut) with cucumbers and peppers. Rice and beans nothing special and properly cooked and spiced, the wild salmon jerk with onions and peppers was very very nice and of course the jerk sauce was so authentic and good with the rife and beans...or was it the Bob Marley in the background music???? This place must be rocking at lunch, prices are not bad and reasonable.
Food was excellent! Valentine's day special 2 for $55 everything was great! Customer service like always perfect.. Don't mind coming back here again!

How this place escaped my notice for so long I'm not sure. "Friends" of mine knew about it, and yet they didn't tell me! Some friends... Went here for the lunch buffet and found it much better than Indian lunch buffet experience of yesterday (different place). $10 a head and fear not when you don't see naan on the buffet, they bring it to the table. I'm going to guess there were six entree choices, two or three sides, vegetable samosas, some other fried ball of veggie bits. I should really carry a pad and paper to these kinds of things. Like James mentioned there are lots of veggie friendly choices so it's a good place for meat/veggie discordant groups to go.
