I remember reading in a review of the place I tried yesterday that they played a muzak version of "The Final Countdown" and it must be something common amongst Indian restaurants because we were treated to a listening while we were here. Great service, good food, looking forward to going back.

We were visiting from out of state and was excited to find this on yelp. After reading all the reviews, we couldn't wait to check it out. We went there on Monday only to find out they were close. We decided to come back on Tuesday. We ordered some padthai, fried rice (for the kids), satay, stuffed chicken wing, tempura chicken, fried eggplant and Panang curry. We were so disappointed, the padthai was too sweet and had too much liquid (def. American style padthai) the chicken fried rice lacked flavor, the chicken tempura appetizer was just slicked chicken lightly dipped in flour and fried. Looked liked something you would try to cook at home (so plain). The fried eggplant was $7 and it was tiny and just basically fried with tempura batter no seasoning or anything. I love eggplant and I can make better fried eggplant. Really simple and plain. stuffed chicken wings and satay was only thing that was decent. The curry was decent too. We eat a lot of Thai food and we were just quite disappointed with the food here. The service was not too friendly either.

Horrible.....The service is just plain horrible. They have no clue what is happening. I ordered online, they never got the order but charged my card. Then when my husband talked with the manager magically the order showed up. Brought it to my work, and food was missing. The girls at the drive thru have no idea what is going on. This location is going to lose customers fast. When we went back to get the food they telling us that we lied and that we got the food......calling corporate about the situation!!!

I didn't care for the Thai basil. 2x trying. Both times green pepper flavor overwhelmed the dish. 2x even ordered without green pepper 2nd time. Still found Green peppers and again flavor overwhelmed dish. Basil should be the main ingredient couldn't even find and i order extra bail. How many leaves of basil did i find...you guessed it none. Ooops I'm sorry a piece of a leaf haha not a place ill be going back again. 1st time forgiveness 2nd time even knowing what went wrong 1st time they still had same mistakes. Nice indoor outdoor ambience. Staff was friendly and courteous. Never saw chef.

We had a rehearsal dinner for about 30 for our son and now wife's wedding. Details were settled in advance.While Avalon would like to sell their package, they were flexible in regard to servicing our requests. The room was great. Felt like we had the restaurant to ourselves. None of our guests looked like they were waiting for a drink at any time. Service was attentive not intrusive. Courses were well paced. The food was delish. We had several 30ish guests who wanted to go to Avalon and now were ready to return. Great planning, coordination and execution. It was a memorable night.

I Really enjoyed dinner here with my wife and daughter. We arrived fairly on a Friday evening, so the place was still pretty empty - and we were able to grab a seat by the (gas) fireplace. It's very cozy inside, and pretty small overall, but I think that actually enhances the experience - kinda like eating at someone's home. Our server was pretty good. While she didn't really want to give much of an opinion on which spread to order, she was always attentive to us, checking on us after each new dish arrived to make sure everything was good. We went tapas style, and the dishes arrived pretty quickly (probably because it was still early), but one at a time. That was good because it let us get started on each dish one at a time. We ordered the htipiti hummus spread, vegetarian dolmades, falafel, lamb gyro, and baklava for dessert. Htipiti hummus had a nice flavor with all the spices well blended in. Dolmades were good. Falafel was probably the best I have ever had. I normally don't care much for them, but these really appealed to me. Perhaps because they were good and fried, and still warm. Gyro was actually an entree, and I'm not sure how one could eat it as a sandwich, since it was open face and piled high. But we cut it into quarters and just knife & forked it. Nice big hunks of tender, tasty lamb; perhaps too much other lettuce, etc. topping, though. The hummus spread, falafel, and dolmades all came with cucumber, onion, and olives on the side, so there was no need to order any extra olives, in my opinion. And the falafel was served on a pita, so there was plenty extra for the spread - again, no need to order extra. Baklava was simply excellent - highly spiced, warm, and warm honey too.

I've been seeing this place opened less than 2 weeks and I have been skeptical to see what this place is about. AND I was amazed by their food quality and how fresh it is! No other vietnamese place is as good as this one! The staff are friendly and wow I'm glad this place opened up!
Loved everything here. Beautiful decor, white linen tablecloths, fresh-cut flowers, personable service, and fresh, vibrant ingredients. Prices are reasonable and the portions generous.

The only decent Thai place I've experienced in the area. The pad thai and crispy rolls were very tasty. Portions generous, price right. The service was just OK, but they don't pretend to be a fancy place. Definitely recommend over any other Asian place that happens to have Thai on the menu.

Desi village has changed quite a bit recently - i think they had new ownership. The food quality has gone up. Wide variety of Indian options, a lot you don't see at other places. Lunch buffet has good options. Food is quite spicy - spicier than other Indian joints. Inside is nicer than other Indian places too.

Delicious and cheap. I had a lamb gyro and an order of hummus and pita for $9. Everything was extremely fresh. Food was finished quickly. My friend had the greek salad with steak - the meat was excellent: tender and grilled medium, and the house dressing was fantastic. The falafel is also very good. The falafel salad is a better option than the "sandwich" if you're really hungry - it's a lot of food. I would highly recommend as a quick and easy lunch option.

Don't let the lackluster decor put you off, my wife and I had a very pleasant meal here. She had the Fish ( mahi) Tika Masala and I had the lamb Biryani. Both were good size portions and were very tasty and the garlic naan was also very good. The service was quick and polite.

Not sure where to start from. Went to buffet with my family and it was the worst Indian buffet so far. The food was crappy and the owner, this big guy right in the middle of the buffet tables was having lunch. Buffet was expensive for a weekday lunch. Don't even think about going to bathroom. I wonder if it woud even pass the food and clensiness inspection. I was very hungry and would have least bothered about the customer service, but the customer service was worst than the food. The owner in the middle of the buffet area was having this weird look which kind of felt as if we are have done somthing terribly wrong walking in. The place was almost empty with just one more customer while I was there. In summary, I would rather starve instead of going to this place and pay to eat some crappie food and the worst customer service experience.
Fast and courteous service. Had the Salmon Lover Roll and Miso Soup which were both very good. Menu has many options.

One of a kind...Olio breaks the mold in St. Louis. My wife and I tried the kale salad...which was refreshing and tasty. Then we ventured out and tried the game hens. Wow! Talk about impressive!! We sat right at the bar and never felt overcrowded...it was surprisingly cozy. The bartender was engaging, yet tremendously busy. Cocktails and wine were delicious. My wife couldn't quite get over the fact that the place used to be a gas station...but I found the garage door frontage charming. I think it's a winner.

My first experience with Indian food, and I have to say I'm a fan. I fell in love with the butter chicken. It was too bad that we were in a rush so we couldn't fully enjoy our meal, but the waitstaff seemed to be alright with us rushing them. We managed to get our food and then have to pack it up right away, but it was still delicious later!

What a pleasant surprise! This was my first Ethiopian restaurant, and it did not disappoint. Don't be turned off by the less-than-enticing decor outside. We were fortunate enough to have the manager (possibly also the owner) take our order, and his suggestion that we order the sampler for 2 was perfect. The kitchen was very accommodating of our preference for chicken. I had qualms about eating with my hands, but the injera (bread) ultimately seemed more sanitary than sharing a dish using a knife and fork. And it was fun! The spices were well-balanced, and I actually loved the cabbage dish. The nicest touch was the birthday surprise they brought out for my boyfriend. I had made last-minute reservations with a special request to acknowledge his birthday, and the kitchen sent out a dessert hot from the oven. They really went the extra mile.

My friend was in town visiting from NYC and we wanted to find some Indian Food near the gayborhood. After checking yelp we found great reviews for the Mumbai Bistro. We then invited our friends to drive from Germantown to meet up with us for dinner. When we arrived it was A LOT smaller and more casual than we were expecting. Essentially it is Indian fast-food. There are only about 6 small tables and a buffet of about 6 options. We called in advance to make sure that it was BYOB and they assured us that it was, however, I think we may have been the only people in Mumbai Bistro history to take them up on that. We felt a little silly downing our two bottles of wine in plastic cups while the only other patrons (a couple with two young children) eyed us suspiciously. With that being said, the food was incredibly tasty and cheap. My entire meal including Nan and drink was around $5. It's neat the way they set it up where you weigh out your food from the buffet. That way you get a range of options to choose from but don't have to pay a hefty buffet cost. The saag paneeer was my favorite of the buffet dishes. If there is something specific you like, the a la carte prices were also incredibly reasonable. This place is truly awesome! I wish they had one in my neighborhood!!

MoMos is a neighborhood Restraunt that offers authentic Greek food. I have lived in the UCity area for last 16years and the greatest complement I can say is that after all these years it remains a regular dining stop. The staff are friendly and I would strongly suggest trying MoMos, A true neighborhood gem of a dining experience. Kirk Wittner of StL Law Group

They're having a rough time. My fiance and I stopped in to try it out and they took forever to give us our order, and when they did it was wrong. We were kind of in a hurry and thought we could stop in and get a quick dinner. WRONG. For starters, there were about 12 people working that night, and no one knew what to do. There were 3 people cutting a pita wrap for the person in front of us. WHY? Two of them could have been starting orders from the quickly forming line in back of us. At the second station, there were about 3 people putting the fixins inside of the pita. Again, too many people at one station, confusing each other. There were 3 more people at the last station, bagging orders and then the manager rang up the order. Soooo... with all of these PEOPLE, why is it that when I got home, my chicken shawarma pita wasn't even in the bag??? So, we had to go allll the way back. My fiance thought that maybe they just forgot it to put it in the bag, and it would be at the counter, but noooo, they actually stuck it in someone else's bag! We had to wait AGAIN for the sandwich to be made all over again. Did I mention we were in a hurry? Overall, the food was ok. The sauces were pretty spicy, but that was a good thing. Double check your order before you leave, though.

A solid three star restaurant, which means I would go back if nearby. I went cause it came up in the vegan search but didn't have much variety of food in this type. It is really a big Thai beef place. The friendliest and nicest staff ever. Very sweet people. Great service.
Excellent Indian cuisine and very nice staff here. Definitely a nice addition to Merchantville!

I have had Khao Soi at some other Thai restaurants in Tampa before but let me tell you this place has the BEST Khao Soi. Tips: 1. make sure you ask for oil chili on the side for your spiciness. It's so good with the dish. 2. If you order it togo, make sure you heat it up very hot. It will make the dish taste really good.

Went to Delicia, the associated restaurant next door but the wait was long, so the staff said this place had seating. We ordered a bunch of appetizers like guacamole and the chicken croquettes. All of them were good particularly the latter. Portion size on the guacamole was a bit disappointing. The entrees were more sized as expected. Fish tacos were decent and I also got the Mexicano dog, which was good too. The lunch menu is far more extensive. I would be inclined to try La Mulita again for lunch. All in all it was appetizing and enjoyable.

I love this place and often meet my sister here for pho lunch. Whenever we get there, we're immediately greeted and asked if we'd like 'the same thing'. The owner has memorized our order and it's just a treat to have her stop by and chat. She is wonderfully warm. We should probably get past the rare beef pho, and amazing spring rolls, but we just can't. Whenever we bring friends, they love this place too. The food is always fresh and prepared well.

We've been wanting to try this place for awhile, but there's sooo many in Indy to try! We went last Sat. afternoon & wondered if it would be crowded. We were surprised to find only 2 other people there. We stayed anyway to give it our shot-- Here's the info-- Food: Calamari - didn't smell as fresh as I'd like, an added feature on the plate was broccoli tempura which was nice Spring rolls-crispy w/all veggies, nice portion (5) but was $4.99, but good Tom yum noodle soup w/pork-broth had OK flavor but wasn't as rich as I'd like. I didn't like the meat balls in it & it didn't mention them, but I just set aside. It was a nice portion. Massamen curry w/chicken was very rich. The portion was small but w/richness was enough. It had too many large potato chunks. There was quite a pile when hubster pulled them out. Service: She started to seat us in the corner but since no one was there we asked for the table by the window to watch the BR crowd go by. The table was very dirty with magazines spread over. She removed them but we had to ask for her to clean it. All in all she was a good server keeping my water filled which is a big job. Décor: -very nice, I don't know if it's the same as former Mediterra because we never tried, there's plenty of seating Con's: Parking is really tight & I'm glad it wasn't full or would be impossible. -but better than most in BR. Also Hubster mentioned something when we left that maybe people don't wander in to eat because the sign is a strip mall kinda sign & only says Thai Noodle. It would be so much more inviting as Chiang Mai Thai. We might go back--

I walked in an hour after they had opened and found I was the only person in the restaurant. Almost made me want to walk back out, but glad I didn't. For $7.50 the lunch portions were huge, it could have easily fed two people. Beef and mixed vegetables was delicious, and the egg drop soup had a great twist with mushrooms and bits of chicken. My only complaint was that the owner ordered my waitress to go in the back and wash mushrooms. Afterwards she was told to go outside and bring in the fresh produce that arrived. I'm not a health inspector, but I question having waitresses handle raw food while they are serving customers.

I've passed this place several times and never stopped despite the aroma calling my name. But today we decided to try something different and I was not disappointed! To be honest I thought I didn't like Thai food but I've been converted, even my kids liked it and they don't like much! Very good flavor and great customer service. Yes, I will be back for sure!
Fast service, delicious authentic middle eastern food, reasonable prices and quantity was OK

I had a delicious dish with Thai Basil in it -- I can't recall the exact name on the menu, but veggies with meat and steamed rice. They were willing to alter the contents for my needs, and the sauce was very very good. Excellent service, pleasant environment, I will go back.

If you're looking for something quick but healthy, there are few choices around. Thankfully there's Zoës Kitchen. I always have a good meal here and have trouble making myself try something different. I just love the Spinach Roll-ups with a side of Braised White Beans! Sometimes I'll get the Greek Salad, or get it on the side, and they have the best Greek salad around. Their housemade dressing, a bottle found on every table, rocks, and makes that salad outstanding! I normally don't like tomato soup, but Zoës' tomato basil soup is so delicious, it is more like a pasta sauce. The fresh basil gives it zing and the melting mozzarella they put on top is gooey, like eating pizza fresh out of the oven. It's served with warm, freshly baked pita pieces. Yum! There are plenty of vegetarian choices as well as chicken, turkey and seafood. Anyone who likes good food will like this place.
Amazing middle eastern food with a down home feel. The service is great and the food is an amazing price. Also, for any Muslims all of their food is halal.

I have to admit that I was not a fan of Indian food before I came here! The buffet is a great option, and so cheap. It's a great way to try out new items. Always fresh and the people are really nice. I will always come here when I have an Indian craving!

This was my first visit to Pan D'olive and it will not be my last! I had a very satisfying meal. It started off with a free glass of wine, thanks to my Yelp check-in, and improved as I enjoyed a very fresh tasting wedge salad topped with bacon, tomato, and blue cheese crumbles. My entree selection was tougher as their menu offered a number of mouth-watering choices for a first timer. I chose one of the Turkish Specialties: Izgara, a marinated ribeye steak covered cremini mushrooms with rice pilaf. While ribeye is not my favorite cut of meat, the waiter's description of spices used in the marinade sounded too good to pass up. It was very flavorful. I expected some fat in the steak (usually comes with any ribeye) but the spices made every bite taste good. The rice pilaf was especially good and complimented the steak and mushrooms extremely well. I topped off the night with a freshly brewed cup of decaf and chocolate mousse. I'm rather easy to please when it comes to mousse and while this was a heavy version of mousse (meaning less whipped and dense) it was very good. The service was excellent (thanks Mark) and added to a very enjoyable experience. The weather was great so we also ate outside on their patio. The restaurant as a whole has very accommodating feel. The bar is fun and I could easily go back just for drinks with friends. I look forward to going back...soon!

Take Out / Eat In Food: Out of this Middle Eastern World. My husband has been gloating about this hole in the wall corner store for months as his new go to spot for middle eastern cuisine. Saturday was a snow day in the city. We banged out our grocery shopping on 9th street and were hangry for something hearty and healthy and FRESH! Boom! Bitars I never have compared any Lentil soup to my mama doos, don't tell, but yours was out of this world! Fresh, hearty and the aromatics heightened my senses. I love that the food is the starlight. Served on paper plates and bowls. And service. Service served with a grateful smile. The best.

Had very good salmon wrapped in a grape leaf in my last visit and tonight my wife and I ordered the fix price menu. She had Pad Thai with chicken and I had Thai Basil with meat. I had Thai Ravioli Soup and Thai Dumpling. As usual all of the food was excellent but not too filling.

I've gone passed this place a lot (mostly on my way to Duchess) and after hearing some great things, I went for dinner there with my aunt. We got our standard "starving student" order, which means we order a giant pile of things so we can try a bunch of different dishes, and then I get a couple days of leftovers. We started with the chicken satay, which was really nice, and then got crispy chicken with garlic sauce, a seafood curry, tofu red curry, and coconut rice. Everything was absolutely delicious, although at the upper bound of what my northern Alberta palette can handle for spiciness. We end up at Thai restaurants a fair bit, and while they're mostly pretty good, this place won hands down for the best Thai we've had in Edmonton so far. Our bill was about $50 for two dinners (and two lunches....) and I saw a menu up for a $10 lunch special, so the prices here are pretty reasonable. There were two servers working that evening, and they were both very friendly and very helpful. Service was fast and my water was refilled every time before it made it past half full. The only thing I found surprising was how quiet it was. They've been in that spot for 3 years, and have got great reviews (which they deserve), but there were only a couple other tables in there that night. Come on Edmonton....

I loved my experience at The Cafe DbyD. My boyfriend and I went here for my birthday. We were met at the entrance by Ben, a delightful, friendly, courteous man who enriched our dining experience (I mentioned that our dining satisfaction would likely lead to a positive yelp review and he told me that his mother would be happy as she checks yelp for reviews - so, hello Ben's mother! He's great!). Anyway, we shared mac'n cheese balls and the dumpling soup for appetizers and both were very, very good! For the main dishes, I ordered the goat curry (pretty good) with plantains (the plantains were very, very delicious)!!! My boyfriend had the short ribs for his main dish - GOODNESS. GET THE SHORT RIBS. Tender, mouth watering, flavorful, wonderful. Easily the best food item I've had in a long time. :) For dessert we shared the mini trio which was also good. They even gave me candles and a complementary coffee for my birthday!! Yay! One of the managers also introduced herself and made sure that we had everything we needed for a nice dining experience. The restaurant itself is beautiful, elegant, and welcoming. I love the wood flooring, the atrium, the chairs, and the color choices. The prices are reasonable. The service is exceptional and the food is amazing. Highly recommended. Go there! Order the plantains and the short ribs and say hello to Ben!

Saw this gem was close to home and they made Puerto Rican cuisine so I had to go and try it. The food was amazing and felt like a home cooked meal.... not to mention the prices are great. We ate two plates of arroz con gandules, pernil, and Maduros for less than 20, including our drinks. The decor was cultural and quaint, reminiscent of the island. Definitely going back!

We just heard about Flambo recently and after some friends recommended it, we went last night. What a treasure! Our server was welcoming, friendly and helpful. We had a lot of questions and he explained the menu and helped us make our choices. The owner, Anthony also greeted us and talked with us for a while. We took their recommendations and went with the Roti. I had the curried goat and she had the curried chicken; then we shared. Wow! Both were great dishes. As promised, the goat was flavorful but not the least bit gamey. The chicken was tender and tasty. We'll be back and bringing friends. It's great to have this cool place in our neighborhood.

I can't even justify giving one star because of how blatantly rude their staff are at this location. Not much else to explain. Normally they're fine but now I'm definitely not coming back here. Girl makes my drink without all the toppings. No biggie, I always get the vegan hot chocolate and they always make it with nuts and coconut on top. My drink is overflowing on the counter and I can't drink any of it because it's so hot. There is literally milk pouring everywhere. I ask another girl kindly if she can put it in a different mug and she was like "Oh yeah of course, no problem, sometimes the whip cream just makes it overflow." I'm studying upstairs and would rather not get everything sticky and covered in chocolate. Then I asked if I could get the toppings, like the nuts and coconut. She says of course, hands it off to the other girl to make (short, blonde hair, glasses) who proceeds to slam the pitchers down on the counter, make a big scene, and angrily top my drink with the wrong toppings, making it overflow, again. Nice. Thanks a lot. To top it all off, I get a few eye rolls and snarky comments made about me to her coworker while I'm in clear earshot. Disgusting, catty behavior. I don't even have the energy to talk to some of the people here, because when I politely ask for a modification I get treated like garbage. Next time I'll just go to transcend across the street because I'd rather not be treated like I'm useless, incompetent, and annoying when I'm nothing but nice to people working there. In short; Drinks are fine (when they're made right), food is decent, but customer service is lacking and staff are beyond rude. Will definitely be following up with management as it's more than unacceptable.

I love it here! This is my second time here and enjoying even more than the first! The atmosphere is great with the Spanish music playing in the background! This is my go-to spot for Puerto Rican food
Best location, best food, very profesional service i took my bf for his first visit and he loved the lo mein :-)
Food is always fresh and prepared / delivered quickly. They've got a nice variety of different Asian cuisine like Thai, Chinese, Schezuan, Cantonese style and Japanese without sacrificing quality.

The food was excellent! I love how they did the chicken and the lamb it was very tender and melted in your mouth. The rice was delicious. Service was good. Next time I plan to try the buffet. Try seemed a little high for a lunch but not that unreasonable.
Went to lunch there today food was fantastic nice and spicy. The names of their sushi quite humurous. Staff was great all around a great experience.

The owner is terrific and so is the food. Better than any other Mediterranean food I have had in Boise. A real cultural treat. We took the family there on Sunday and had a great time. The kids enjoyed themselves and it was very reasonable priced. Try the grilled plate. Also, the bread is wonderful. Highly recommended.

Wife and I went there for lunch on Sunday, it was the buffet. We paid about $35-$40 for both of us after tip. There was a lot of vegetarian options, everything was pretty fresh, and everything tasted really good. We will definitely be back, But next time order off the menu because we walked out of there like stuffed pigs. (Wife said she thought it was a bunch of slop. But I guess this piggy likes slop.)

LaVa is conveniently located on the corner of 21st and South, just a few blocks from my place. Over the past few months it has been my go-to for quick and easy lunches when I'm on the run. I'm a big fan of their hummus platter, paninis, and oversized salads. Staff is friendly and attentive, atmosphere is pleasant. The only downside is that it is usually pretty crowded, so if you can't get a table or you're waiting to take out, it's a little awkward standing around.

I like their fried rice and sushi. The kimchi fries tasted burnt. My husband said they were probably cooked in burnt oil so that wasn't very pleasant. I heard they got a bad inspection score so haven't been since then but I'd be willing to go back. The menu is just a little awkward.
My First time here. There is always a long line. One hour's waiting normally. But worth it. High quality food. So yummy. Will come back again.

Great Vietnamese food on one of America's most beautiful streets! The pho here is a bit different; one reviewer was caught off guard by the savory-sweet broth. There's just a hint of anise in their broth that gives it a welcome individuality. Try the Bun Bo Hue on a cool day to warm you up; split an Orchid Pizza (Banh Xeo) with a few people for a different appetizer, and try your hand at rolling lettuce wraps. Oh-and finish off with some delicious Vietnamese coffee! All in all, a welcome addition to St. Charles Avenue!

BYO, and abosolute high quality food and preparation. Dinner only and make reservations for Fri/Sat. A charming atmosphere with the river across the road. Service is always attentive. I generally do not like salads, but anything they prepare is delicious. All foods have the perfect balance of spices, which is not the norm even for touted restaurants. The most impressive aspect of Francisco's Restuarants (Florentino's in Newtown) is the amazing consistency of perfectly cooked product. Both places offer a good selection of fish and meat, but while the appetizer selection is somewhat limited, this is only due to the fact that both places have very small kitchens. These two restuarants are about 10 miles apart, but there is simply no other places worth going to in my humble opinion. There are a fair amount of choices of course, but the all lack consistency, service, or quality.
I had to come back to see if I was right. I was and it is. The Curry is as good as any Thai curry that I've had. Please come and support this fine restaurant.
Very small place, and the decoration looks cheap. Food wasn't bad nor amazing. Belly dancers are nice and engaging at times. Overall, it is an ok Morrocan restaurant.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Amazing food! I never have been a fan of Thai food it seems to be to sweet and soggy but not here love the coconut soup and I never though I would say that, and the family who owns it is so sweet and helpful it is really an enjoyable place to be.

There are lots of good Thai restaurants in Pinellas County. So there is no need to go to a mediocre Thai restaurant. And that is what we have here. The Tom Kha soup was lightly flavored and a bit on the thin side. The Veggie Soup was just bland. In the entrees, the Ginger Stir-Fry was pleasant and probably the most successful dish. The good old Thai standard of Pad Thai was just all right, again with a thin flavor. The fried banana dessert used over-ripe bananas and, again, was a bit bland. The coffee (at $3/cup) tasted odd and, upon asking, I discovered that it was instant--what a shame. The service was scatter-shot and confused. The décor is basic and, like the food, a bit boring. Too many other Thai restaurants get it right to bother returning here.

Have been going here for years. Staff and owner have always been very pleasant. One of my favorite desi restaurant if not the best. The chicken tikka Biryani is my favorite along with first khadi. Recently been ordering the chili chicken and that's been great. Definitely would recommend this spot to ask if my friends.

Ariana was absolutely terrible! One of the worst experiences I've had. A friend of mine reserved the restaurant for his birthday (starting at 9:30 p.m.). They didn't clear out customers in time and the last people didn't leave until 11. A little awkward when clearly there are 50 other people there for a private party. Ambiance: we had an ipod of playlists set for the event but they kept changing it to Afghani and Middle-Eastern Music videos... Fodd: I can forgive all the other stuff IF the food ended up being good because that's really all that matters at the end. Sadly, it makes me never want to try Afghan food again. There was a rice/Palow plate paired with a plain spinach dish (Chalow Sabzi ) but the rice was WAY too sweet and the Spinach had no pepper or spice. My friend also ordered Lamb and Chicken which came in curry and were decent but also lacked flavor and appropriate spices. We had preordered to have enough as a buffet style or enough for each of us but they came out in small bowls and hardly filled anyone up. We had to keep asking for more servings! We had the restaurant reserved until 2 a.m. but they started ushering us to leave at 1. Do not accept a party to reserve a venue that late if you cannot hold good service until they have had time to finish celebrating and clear out. Especially when you are paid a fair amount of money upfront. Overall- not a great experience, especially for a friend's birthday. You may like this cuisine if you like sweet, plain Middle Eastern food.

Posted on my blog on 3/27/2009: "I guess you can say food carts are the best example of an American dream comes true, low budget and as long as you have solid good food people will come. You can make as much money as the effort you put in. There are many a street food carts in Philly with interesting ethnic foods, especially around University of Pennsylvania, Thai, Chinese, Mexican, even Ethiopian. Ever since the soul food place around my former job had closed, I haven't had any good oxtail stew on rice and there are at least 3 soul food carts around that area that advertised for them, too bad it's so far away. The weather was a bit dreary and the line wasn't as long as we've expected. The cart itself is a bit odd. Instead of carrying drinks, cookies, candies and gums, the outside compartment of the cart was decorated with rows and rows or garlic, potted plants and some decorative bottles of olive oil. The owner Gus must be making a pretty good living not having to figure how he'd make more money. Also, there's no menu or prices anywhere. It's a good thing that we've seen the video in advance and know that he only sells falafel and chicken as platters or as sandwiches. In the drizzling rain, the guy in front of us ordered 5 platters, but Gus wouldn't do it because he doesn't make mass orders and would only make him 2. Strange. Not only that, Gus then ask if it's the guy's first time buying food from him because all regulars would know. Exactly what's the difference between 5 guys waiting in line and each order a platter or one guy buying 5? After waiting around 15 minutes, we got our platter for $10. The platter consisted a layer of shredded lettuce at the bottom, some hummus on the corner, a cucumber tomato salad, some pasta bits, some grape-banana salad, 4 fried falafel nuggets, a good amount of charcoal-grilled chicken, a pita bread, two kinds of sauce and a good sprinkle of oregano/parsley. I liked the platter a lot, the hummus is mild and pleasant, the falafel is chunky and satisfying, the chicken is well-spiced and crispy from the grill and the fruit salad is quite the perfect touch. I'm scratching my head over the pasta bits though, it's not bad but not quite necessary. We can see that Gus takes a lot of pride in his food. He has certain standards for his customers to follow and he has to prepare his food just the way he wants. Gus reminded us of Seinfeld's soup Nazy, maybe he is the one who inspired the skit. His food was pricey but worth it, although I didn't care for him not selling drinks or the fact that he doesn't have a price menu so at the end when his customers find out the price it might be too late for them to turn down the prepared food. It's almost an arrogance or his way to tell his customers that you can't assign a price to his art or don't patronize him if you don't think you can afford it. But eccentricity is not a bad thing especially when it benefits the customers that he has a higher standards for his food. If I'm in the area and hungry, I'll definitely seek him out again."

I and friends 8 members went to this place recently on weekend. It was a bad experience. This is not at all a proper indian food. There is no proper quality for the price we pay. The food doesn't taste like indian preparation. The service is not good as well.

We visited late in the evening, after the crowds are gone. It was intimate. I love the decor. The tables were all set in an elegant manner, and we were seated next to the fireplace. Our waiter made a big deal and show out of the dishes, which added to the fun. We tried new things and really enjoyed it. We will definitely be back!

This is by far one of our favorites for pho in the city. We've been here many times and they are quite accommodating to my family. And on the offbeat chance the kids are not up for pho, they do appreciate the western menu.

The best Vietnamese pork and fresh spring rolls in Tucson. The meat was lean and tender and marinated perfectly. I've had so many bad pork experiences at other Vietnamese places in Tucson - where anywhere from 20-40% of the meat was too gristly to chew. The quality at I love Pho was very superior to its competitors and I've tried them all - numerous times. Wonderful fresh spring rolls too. Their milk tea with boba is good but not great -seemed like the drink wasn't blended all the way or something but I would order it again. The atmosphere is a little fast-foodish, which may explain why it always seems to be empty. Highly recommend!

I love Indian Lunch Buffets. This one was ok, not fantastic but not horrible either. I would definitely eat here again. The buffet food was on the warm side not hot but the food was good. I love good tandoori chicken that's full of flavor and tenderness. The tandoori was on the bland side but that could be just the day. All in all a good reasonable lunch stop.

My girlfriend and I saw all of the good reviews and decided to give it a try and got two beef kabobs. We get kabobs all of the time from other restaurants and are not very picky. Needless to say these were the worst kabobs we have ever eaten. They were nearly inedible. They looked and tasted like overcooked hamburgers cut up in small pieces. We will never be eating here again.

Definitely the worst Thai food I've had in Philadelphia. The chicken was bone dry and the pad thai had too much tamarind (it was all tamarind and not much of any other flavor) and no veggies! Also, they give you a small bowl of rice and charge you $1 if you want more! Rice should be free yo! The only reason why I'm not giving it just one star is because the waiter was very nice (even though he got my order wrong).

This is the third time we have eaten here. The service is always great and friendly. The first two visits we had the Pho with brisket. I will definitely keep coming back here for this dish. This time we had the Smokey Burger (minus the ham). The Gouda and BBQ sauce made it salty and delicious! Satisfied my appetite If you're a couple and split your meals this is your spot! They don't mind at all, and even serve our food pre-split on separate plates. Although we don't mind the same plate . This includes the Pho dish as well. They even brought out a second small dish of garnish

I love Green Basil! Their food is amazing and their service is wonderful. The manager knows I am vegan and always takes care of my order perfectly. They have the best tofu pad tai! I order from Green Basil at least once a week and I highly recommend that you check them out!

Won't come back due to the horrible service from the lady bartender. Many times I came in to pick up my carry out, she always forget my sauce for my vermicelli bowls and rice platter. I have to consume my food plain. If I can give 0 stars I would.

Grand opening of a new branch of the best Thai food in Nashville! They had a great special, 50% off the bill for the first two days they were open, which includes tomorrow! The Pho came in two sizes. The regular size is enough for most people; get the large if you are starving. The Pad Kee Mao, Tiger Tear salad, Pad Thai, red and green curries, they are all there, being cooked by the owner, who is here from the main restaurant to get things going. Not sure how long she is staying or if they are training a cook, but the food right now is fabulous. I will definitely be a regular here! This restaurant should easily have received 4 stars but they got 3 from me for tonight's service. The hiccup came towards the end when they forgot about the dessert we ordered and brought the bill. This was after a 15-minute wait and the dessert was not comped, nor was an apology forthcoming.

We came here for a friend's birthday. There were around 15 of us so I think that's why the wait for food was so slow. It took a really long time for the food to come out and it came out in sections so not all of us got our food at the same time. I got the Sriracha Calamari and Crispy Duck Fried Rice. The portions are really small and I wasn't full at all. The calamari was average, nothing special. The duck was really dry and dissatisfying. The service was friendly and it's BYOB but besides that I'm not a fan of the food at all.
Superrrrrrrr, good service and amazing food!
This place is absolutely amazing! I ordered a hibachi shrimp plate that came with egg rolls, and a garden salad. The service and atmosphere is great, but the food is A1.

The food is excellent. The BF says "I could eat this every day for lunch" when speaking about the brisket pho. I, however, should have known better than to order a Thai dish in a Vietnamese restaurant. There were marked differences with this pad Thai than others, but the flavor of it was very delicious. Anyway, has anyone mentioned the cute little boy that helps his father and grandmother? He must be eight years old and is working for his money. Finally, I ordered a limeade, but the grandmother forgot it. Other than that, all good. I would recommend this place for a quick meal.

Thank you, YELP! I was extremely hungry and this is exactly what I was looking for. I had the lamb kabob and it was really tender and juicy. The kabob portion isn't really big, but it comes with vegetables and rice. The combination of everything smells and tastes warm and delicious. I came on a poopy rainy day, and this food made the day suck way less. The music is pretty cool too. The food was prepared really quickly - you can be in and out well under an hour during lunchtime. They take credit cards. Yes, even Discover!
Decided to try a Thai Place near home and after reading reviews on Yelp this was the best place nearby. The place is decorated beautifully, food was great, service was awesome.

I've been looking for good falafel around IV/Goleta for awhile. I've tried Santorini Grill on campus, Aladdin Cafe and even tried the falafel at IV Deli and none of those places had anything special. Then, 805 Kebab opened & I decided to try it. Best decision ever. Not only is the falafel super delicious, but the portions are HUGE! You get a really good amount of food for a fair price. I've tried the falafel, hummus, pita bread and fries and everything has been pretty good. This is definitely my go-to place for yummy falafel! Btw, the wait is pretty long, but worth it IMO.

Stayed in Edmonton for a few days; ate at this restaurant 3 times; we got the same happy-face results all three times. We ordered the cold cut sandwich (the meat inside was standard but the bread was so crunchy and toasty; the filling was of the generous-side portion), the spicy beef soup (which had the best flavor that I have never had), the rice vermicelli bowls was tasty (i particularly like the fresh veggies in it; the egg-roll side order was a good compliment to go with this dish). We didn't try their bubble tea; we had the soda and the vietnamese coffee. It appeared to be clean and organized during our visit; the decoration was young and urban-fitting; the ambiance was good for a sit down meal; the staff was friendly; our wait time for the food was OK, I have no comment of the menu prices because I did not eat at others vendors around to be able to compare; however, I thought they are fairly priced for the food I ordered. If I am ever in Edmonton area again, I will eat there.
Great food and service. Price is reasonable and the atmosphere is good. I have been here several times and would recommend it to anyone that likes good Indian food.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: Go for lunch! Maybe the food will arrive by dinner. Awful timing from the kitchen and awful service and food isn't great. There are definitely better restaurants in the area!

We went to Parkallen recently with a group of ten so right off I expect a little chaos when ordering for a group of that size. The servers were great except for one who when I ordered and mentioned I need gluten free options, brought out regular bread, my salad had crushed pita on it and when mentioned to her she brought me tabbouleh as a replacement which contains bugler wheat. I actually requested the Greek salad and she just never bothered to bring it. Besides that... at least I am attentive to what in eating so not to accidentally have an allergic reaction, the food was good. I had the steak in skewers which was great grilled beef and the little measly Greek salad was nice. Portions are small for what you pay, but the atmosphere and wines are great as well as the other servers we encountered.

Been there twice now and will keep coming back! Food really good, presentation excellent, vibe really great- friendly, accommodating, plus the wall art is cool. Behl Puri- fascinating combo of flavors and textures with sense of freshness. Ginger Beet Salad- a fave (but I'm sucker for beets). Kala Chana Curry- perfectly spiced, right proportion of chick peas to rice, took some home and had it 4 days later and it held up, was sooo good! Butternut Squash Curry- hit the spot, right texture and flavor, finished entire bowl. People I went with also loved the place!

August Moon, while not the best Chinese in New Orleans, is certainly above average and the Vietnamese dishes are great. Super Pho and Gua Cuo. Don't bother dining in, as the delivery guys for this place are not only quick but fun people to meet. Make sure to ask for chopsticks if you want them.

Chill spot for groups and individuals if you're looking for mixed music, hookah, drinks, & Moroccan food. I love their chicken and couscous vegetables style. It has just about enough season so it's not under properly seasoned. The chicken is very tender, comes apart with a fork or spoon. My only thing is that it's a bit more expensive for a relaxing spot. I love the music because they play a lil bit of everything. It was a Monday and I thought it would be empty but it wasn't!lol there was no charge fee at the door. No need for heels or whatnot. Just put on deodorant lmao. Anyways, if you're in the mood to chill smoke hookah and drink, that's one of the places to hit up. Also, the inside is like a Arabian tent, that's the closest I can put it

They are currently a catering company and soon to be a restaurant mid July 2015. They have catered the office several times now and every single time it just gets better and better. The food is always fresh and blended well. The owners are amazing too. You can just tell that they are passionate about their food. i have the brisket empanadas, black bean and cheese empanadas, and the fried plantains and all of it was just amazing! I absolutely love the food and customer service and can't wait for the restaurant to open!
About average Thai food. Hole in the wall. Looked like an old donut shop converted. Everything is plastic wear. Nothing to get too excited about.

My husband and I have been driving by this place since it opened and finally decided to stop in for lunch. So gald we did! The decor is very pleasant and the place seemed very clean. The woman behind the counter was super helpful (I wish I had asked for her name). Although we are fairly familiar with Indian food, it was nice having her so clearly explain the food that was offered. She was very specific about the dishes and the chutneys. I had a bowl and my husband had the platter. I don't know how much the other reviewers eat (must be a lot!), but I thought the servings were generous for the price. The mint rice is yummy and the ginger chutney was awesome! The only thing I missed was naan and I wish they had an onion chutney. Next time we are going to try a Dosa--we saw one brought out to another customer and it looked amazing! We will definitely be back to try some of what we saw but didn't have, and also see what different dishes will be offered next time. I love that this isn't a chain--it is a "mom and pop"!

Fantastic food, awesome staff, always try go or get takeout when in the area, been twice this week & the portions are so big that meant 4 nights food. Met the owner/manager when I was here a few months ago, the place was full & I was alone so she asked if I'd mind sitting at the bar. It was crazy busy & felt like I was in the way a little bit but I really enjoyed it. She was even asking me to try some wine she, ended up giving me 2 free glasses & the food was great. The staff all work so well together & have fun while giving great service. Cannot recommend this place highly enough!!
Service weak. coconut soup watery and lacking. some items over spiced, others under spiced. i've had better thai food at almost every other thai restaurant i've been to. Meh.

Terrible experience here on 4/1/2017 Peppers and bread where nasty. Peppers looked like they'd been left out for days and bread was dry. French onion soup tasted like chicken broth. Reuben sandwich was burnt and dry. Risotto and scallops was not good. Scallops burnt and risotto was undercooked. Will never go here again.

Jasmine is in my top picks for Thai in Brandon/Riverview. I almost feel like this is a hidden gem made just for me since it's always mostly empty everytime I visit. The green and yellow curry is always delish and full of veggies. Plenty of different options for vegans & meat eaters alike! Tom yum soup is a great starter. Crab rangoon are okay, nothing spectacular, but still tasty. The pad se-yew is perfect with a bit of kick. If you like to sweat while you eat, just ask for it to be medium or hot. Extra sweaty= ask for thai hot. A sweet thai tea will put the fire out. Love that the servers wear traditional Thai apparel and are always so nice. Portions are enough for leftovers and are served family style. Great date place. Quiet and nice lighting and ambiance. If you run out of things to talk about, don't worry-the tables are full of traditional carvings in wood with glass laid over. Plenty to look at and keep your eyes and mind busy and off your bomb of a dinner date.

The buffet options taste pretty good and the price is right ($8 lunch, $12 dinner), but the food is *very* oily. I've eaten here three times, and all three times I've ended up with a grease-induced stomachache. Given the choice, I'll take New Dehli every time.

Food 5/5 Atmosphere 5/5 Prices 5/5 Went here for lunch while on the South Side of town. Excellent serving size of Edamame -- not too much, not too little. Hot and well salted. Had the Money Train roll. So good. Plenty of food for 1 with a salad or app. I also tried the salad just to make sure it was the good ginger dressing, and it is. Also $5 house wine = great pinot grigio at least for 5 bucks. TOTES REC. So good. Wish it were closer to downtown so I could go more often!
Great food and ample portions. I can't believe I'm just finding them--you might easily drive down Trigo and miss the sign, even though the restaurant is large enough. Worth a trip to IV.
A family of 4 took 30 minutes to prepare 2 gyros to go when the place was almost empty...The flavor was average but they need to take "Express" out of their company name. Waist of time!!
Counter-service Greek food that has friendly staff and yummy food. I recommend getting the Greko Bowl and a side of Pita!

I can't believe I never reviewed Bitars. I've been going here for 30 plus years. It certainly has changed a lot and not so much in a way I like. When I first started they were the place to go for pita. I think the actual factory was next door. They had the best selection of middle eastern food products. Bread, olives, homemade labni , 5 kinds of feta including Bulgarian . They had all kinds of cool stuff, even pomegranate molasses ! But over the years they have become a restaurant. They still sell a few things I like but the restaurant is usually disappointing. I make better . I'm not kidding. Oh well.
Gyros are to die for. I have fallen for their tatziki and I do not want to get up ;) the pita tastes fresh as well, most places it tastes stale.

Second time ever to one of these restaurants. Did not disappoint. Had a spinach wrap.... Delicious and a bowl of some kind of Caribbean soup with plantains in it. Yummy. Will come back again. These restaurants are not located where I live up north. Try this for a healthy choice and a different taste sensation.
Good food, I got the mix platter which comes with the lamb cubes, minced lamb and chicken. Falafel was good too, the pita bread with the garlic sauce was great! And so were the french fries
Absolutely my favorite Thai place. Small, humble location on Lancaster Ave, family run sort of vibe, reasonable prices.

Got take out again this weekend... I make better green curry at home. The food was definitely spicy and lived up to the "4" level but not worth ordering food from here. I think the only thing worth getting is the Tofu Sog Kreg.

Phenomenal dining experience. This is what I miss about Jersey. Our server was so accomodating with my change in reservation and then went above and beyond during dinner service to make it a special meal. The ambiance is very cozy and intimate. I really enjoy when restaurants have a smaller menu and smaller feel. The kitchen puts out fantastic food as opposed to a ton of options executed poorly. We shared the antipasti, shrimp and sausage appetizer. Everything was a flavor explosion but the antipasti was unmatched to any I have ever had. I don't remember all of the nuiances since it's been over a month since my visit. However, you should order this. We also had the eggplant rigatoni, taggliatelli al limone, and the spaghetti and clams. Again, we were blown away but the taggliatelli was my personal favorite. I have never had anything like this. Finally, we shared the panna cotta and it was the perfect way to finish our meal. It was rich but felt light. Accompanied by homemade caramel, the panna cotta had complex flavors of cream and anise. I honestly can't describe how this tasted...it looks very simple and very vanilla, but it is much more. Make a reservation and go to Zeppoli. This will forever be on my itinerary when I come back to Jersey.
The service is very good! and the lamb is just right! I think it is fairly new, the decoration is very nice -- traditional, modern and clean.

Came here twice since their opening. Our first visit we ordered the Shanghai Soup Dumplings / Xiao Long bao which were very good, no worse or better than the ones in Chinatown so it's kind of nice to be able to get this type of food without traveling all the way to C-town! I also got the crispy fried noodles with seafood which were good, very similar to how my dad used to make it. I ordered delivery the other day, and the delivery was timely, faster than Grubhub had anticipated -- but there was a minor error with my order. I had requested ho fun specifically and I got meifun -- I didn't receive a call or any info that it would be substituted. Outside of that issue, so far I've been enjoying the food items I've tried.

Just got home after picking up egg biryani. The biryani is yellowish white in color, 3 pieces of egg and 2 piece of carrot n 1 bean n cilantro . Not only this is worst biryani order ever , this is pure rip off. People with intentions of business like this wouldn't stay long!! Not only u lost one customer for good, I'll make sure u won't get referral from me. Buyer beware especially to go!!
A perfect taste of India fast food and cheaper than other local chains. I tried vadapau, dabeli, tea, 7 thalli, cut mirchi, etc everything was at a satisfying point the only vote for no is Khaman

This was the worst "indian" food I've ever eaten. The rice was overcooked and room temperature. The butter chicken tasted worse than a frozen dinner. The only redeeming factor was the fact that the staff was incredibly kind and friendly.

Yummy! Fantastic addition to KOP! Food is delicious, great service, clean environment. We had a chicken pita sandwich and a chicken hummus bowl and thought both were fantastic. Also tried the lentil soup and it was tasty. Highly recommend for a quick inexpensive fresh meal.

The food here was decent...The whole wheat garlic bread was delicious and the meal kind of went down from there. It's a very nice setting, and the service was adiquate but I dont think the food lived up to my expectations. I would try it again, but overall was not thrilled.

I've been to other Taziki restaurants outside of Nashville, and they don't come close. Not sure what's different about the one in Cool Springs, but the service is excellent and the food always tastes fresh, well-seasoned and cooked perfectly. Love their Hummus with soft pita, their Lamb Gyro and Village Veggie. Been there numerous times and never been disappointed. A comfortable atmosphere, clean and great with kids.
Best place to dine afghani or Bar BQ. Must try . I loved it. Must try their ( green spices).

Suraya is, beyond a reasonable doubt, the best restaurant experience in Philadelphia and soon to become the next Zahav! Everything from management to the wait staff to the food (especially arak cocktails) and ambiance was top notch and I strongly recommend coming here before the waitlist starts to grow in respect to its popularity. Must get: literally every mezza, specifically kibbeh, samke, sawdat, strawberry cake Meh: fatteh, Missed: larger meats/fish and brunch? First of all, I am incredibly impressed by the entire staff at Suraya. At the moment we arrived, we were greeted by Gregory (the manager) to cater to our seating requests in the most courteous and accommodating manner. Our waitress, Siobhan was also very helpful and replaced our water and utensils at a frequent interval. Furthermore, she allowed the food to come out at a slow but deliberately paced manner that allowed us to recover from each culinary experience. The entire ambiance reminded me of a lounge from the movie Casablanca, albeit, a bit loud depending on the number of patrons. In terms of the food, my wife and I elected to do the Mezza tasting and only try one main meal. This is one of the only time in which I think less food would have been more preferable. This is crazy, but we definitely ordered enough food for 3-4 people, whereas the same menu at other expensive joints would have barely sufficed for 1-2. Our favorites were the sawdat djej (sauteed chicken liver) and the kibbeh nayyeh. The raw lamb, mixed and mashed with onion, basil and marjoram blew us out of the water with this unique mouthfeel and scintillating aroma. Personally, I absolutely loved the sawdat, particularly because I was astounded on how the chefs were able to take something as strong and fatty as liver, and deliver it in a manner that made me question the very food I was eating. It felt like eating a liver-roe that exploded into a burst of rich umami flavors that was immediately cut down with the strong acidity from the pomegranate and lemon juice. To be honest, our dish had 6-7 pieces when all we needed was...I don't know, 1 or 2. Don't forget, you can get fresh pita from the oven at any point, and I love how they sprinkle just hints of salt and spices to keep you coming back. I didn't like the Fatteh such much, as it felt more like a messy, rich tortilla salad, and that just felt too much after the heavy dishes like lamb and chicken liver. As for the drinks, I strongly recommend the arak cocktails as the anise flavor is definitely helpful and provides the needed break from the heavy dishes. Overall, I strongly recommend Suraya for any foodies and definitely call early to set a reservation. I have also heard great things about brunch here, and that may lead to a revisit. Food: 5 stars Service: 5 stars Price: 4-5 stars Ambiance: 4-5 stars

FOOD : This is where Phamous Cafe seems to get it right, for the most part. The food is decent, and certainly much better than all the other offerings in the Santa Barbara and Goleta area. The prices are reasonable but the value is moderately low for what you pay for. It would be nice to see upsell options for more noodles, vegetables, etc... At this time, they only offer extra meat options on the menu and the price for it is quite high. SERVICE : Overall, the service was quite good. Our drinks were always filled up, plates were taken shortly after we finished our meals. Server knowledge seems to be quite good given that the restaurant has been open for only four days. AMBIANCE : The restaurant was moderately full for a Monday night and there were a lot of what seemed to be happy diners at the restaurant. The overall noise level quiet which means you could pick out every conversation being made around you. It may be best for there restaurant to consider music to help drown out some of the other conversations going on as to reduce unintentional eavesdropping.

being new to the area, i checked my yelp android phone app to see "what's hot" near me, and i found this restaurant close to where i was staying. i loove thai food, and they had a killer lunch special, so i dropped in one day for lunch. i ordered the coconut soup, dumplings (i know, not very thai, but i can never resist dumplings), and pad thai (my usual go-to when trying out a new thai place). - coconut soup: yum. normal. as expected. downed the broth, left the veggies. - dumplings: soggy, mushy, fell apart. disappointed. my bad for ordering chinese at a thai place. - pad thai: from the first bite it just tasted too soy saucy. it didn't taste like pad thai to me. very, very disappointing. i might try this place out again to give it another shot, but if a thai restaurant can't get pad thai right each time they make it (in my opinion), then i'm not sure it's worth trying out a second time :T
We recently had a party at Ariana. Staff is really nice and accommodating, they gladly explain all the different food they have. Very very good food, more meet would not hurt!
Just your average gyro place, nothing to write home about compared to all the other food in New Orleans. However, the person behind the counter was friendly and attentive.

It was a Sunday and after finding out Thai Esane was closed I set out for Royal Thai in midtown. Also closed on Sunday. Frantically flailing about for Asian in proximity I decided it'd be a good time to try Inchin's Bamboo Garden. I started with the Manchow Soup, vegetable stock thickened with corn starch and flavored with soy sauce. It had chopped garlic, onion and cilantro. Very nice, although I was warned about how spicy it was and for me it was not spicy at all. The same for the Szechwan Dumplings. A little more spicy than the soup, very tender dumplings. I would order this again. Next came the Drums of Heaven. The menu calls them wings but as the name implies, they are drum sticks. The meat is pulled down to the end. Szechwan flavored drumstick popsicles with bell pepper & onion. It really doesn't matter how hot the dishes are or are not. There are four bottled sauces on the table of varying degrees of heat. I never tried the hottest one as the dishes were just hot enough on their own. I liked the sweet chili sauce the best then the garlic chili. The green chili sauce was seriously salty. There was also a small dish of spicy vinegar. The wait staff were nice but five or six check-ins are too much. They brought me a little scoop of ice cream at the end with a drizzle of chocolate which was a nice touch. I enjoyed my meal and there plenty other interesting looking dishes to try. More dumplings! Who knows what hidden gems await? I'll be back.

While I've never we had a single complaint about the food, the service is getting ridiculous. The wait staff all but ignores the customers as they sit and enjoy their own food, or socialize with friends.

This place is magical. I will start with what is important. THE FOOD. Excellent. Curry spices, well prepared. Stews, sauces, really excellent. The decor is wacky. Chandeliers, mannequins in headdresses, tropical music. But, it's kookiness made me love it even more. Do yourself a favor and go here. You won't be sad.
Very friendly. Got the lunch box which is a great deal. Prices are very reasonable and food tasted fresh. Garlic naan could use a bit more garlic.

There are several restaurants in this area that offer Indian cuisine, and I don't want Desi Spice to fall through the cracks! There is a lot that I cannot eat because of my many food allergies, and also my sensitivity to spicy food. So, I have mild tandoori dishes. Wonderful! Tasty! I wish I were a professional restaurant reviewer so that I could think of more creative ways to describe the food. This is my husband's favorite restaurant. He's more daring than I, and with his iron system, he enjoys the spiciest dishes! I have to stay away from sugar and dairy, but sometimes I can't help myself and order Ras Malai for dessert. What a treat for the taste buds! Now for the staff. Mamta and her husband, Vishnu, are the owners, and they are so friendly and accommodating. As a matter of fact, my brother and his wife were visiting and we took them to Desi Spice. My brother, having lived in Nepal for three years, was able to carry on a conversation with Mamta. I loved watching the two of them talk and bond. I feel like one of the family! I've seen their son grow to be a man, helpful and wonderful with customers. Back when I could eat what I wanted, I used to order Chicken Korma. Mamta said that this is the most popular order. At your first taste of it, it's quite easy to see why it's so popular. Oh my, it's good!!!! Lunch, at least on weekdays (not sure about weekends), they have a buffet with lots of variety.

I have been going here with the work crowd for lunch for years. I find myself comparing all Thai restaurants to Siam. You just can't beat the value, the food, and the service. My favorites: Pad Prik King, and the Green Curry. Writing this is making my mouth water!
So i finally made time to visit the sister site to Pearl Café and im so happy i did! The service was perfect, the food was even better. Definitely worth the extra 5 mins on the commute here

This is the buffet we talk about. I live in Seattle and every time we go to a different/new Indian buffet locally we always compare it to Amber. You absolutely cannot beat this place. The price is reasonable and on-par with other Indian buffets. The selection and flavor is where they win though. There are just so many different options and they are all so delicious. It's tough to choose. We've been to Indian buffets where everything tastes very similar... this is not the case at all. If you are a fan of Indian food then you need to make it a point to stop by Amber for their lunch buffet. You will make it a point to come back and thank this Yelp review for the recommendation because you will be so grateful... that's how good it is.

My husband and I did a cycling trip in Philly where we decided to ride and then eat like Fat Clemenza. We logged a lot of miles in 2 days and tried as many food trucks as we could. Now this was no willy nilly ride-stop eat at any truck-type excursion. I did weeks of Yelp research and narrowed it down to six places and we achieved our gastronomic goal. Well, as much as I really liked every other place, and even gave some of them 5 stars.... this place was mind-blowing!!! How do these 3 guys manage to make this food so damn flavorful and fresh and exciting in that little space?! No clue but I'm beyond impressed. We had the short rib taco, the Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito and the chicken satay taco. ALL were special: they had what tasted like a sriracha/mayo drizzle and all had beautiful fresh perfect pieces of avocado on them. The short ribs was husband's favorite, followed by the tilapia burrito, but he loved them all. I loved the satay chicken taco. Now have never been a meat eater. I've been to steak houses around the US as well as abroad...Butcher & Singer, Palm, DelFriscos, Peter Lugers ..and I have left each one without being convinced to taste one bite of steak/pork/veal/foie gras/etc. Well not sure what got into me but the short rib taco smelled so otherworldly that I took a bite. One word- PHENOMENAL!!! I cannot wait to go back. In fact, we live an hour away and we have planned a repeat trip on Friday!!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We traveled in and out of Boise in September 2017. During our first visit, the owner talked with us when he seated us, when he brought our food, and again at the end of our meal. He was friendly--asked if we were from Boise or visiting, how we knew about the restaurant, etc. He told us his emigration story, how he came to live in Boise. We sat on the patio and enjoyed korma paneer and alu paratha. They were delicious. We returned two weeks later. The owner's son was our server this time. He was pleasant but not as chatty as his dad. We tried palak paneer, peshawri nawn, wheat roti, and lassi. We were not disappointed. If we lived in Boise, we'd be regulars. It's on the second floor, so don't think you missed it when you drive on 8th street
very bad customer service and super disappointed in the way employees spoke to customers
Great food, great service and Depesh actually escorted us in the pouring rain under his umbrella to our next destination a few doors down. Now that's going above and beyond our expectations!!!

I went there for a Saturday brunch. Food looked amazing. However didn't taste good and took a long time to come out. The food was overcooked and under seasoned. They seem to have live music pretty often and when I walked by later in the evening it seemed to be a more exciting place. Not worth going to as the food just was not good and kinda pricy.

Quality = SUPERB Amount = GREAT Price = $8 (you can't beat that...you just can't!) I was across the street at the Kinko's, hadn't had lunch yet, looked on Yelp...said to look for a non-descript food truck with a long line and smoke piping out of the truck. Stood about 30 minutes in line. It was a windy day, so smoke was blowing directly into everyone in line. I was about to suggest that we move the line to the upwind side of the truck, but the two guys that I was sandwiched between (they were regulars) advised against it. "You watch Seinfeld? Soup Nazi? This is the Falafel Nazi. He will kick you out of line if you upset him." No menu. No drinks (instead, potted plants and pieces of fruit adorn the truck). You get what he serves you. No questions asked. Usually, it's some falafel, some chicken, rice, delicious sauces/hummus, and a plum. $8 cash. It's worth it. At least once in your life. People risk parking tickets (there's nowhere to park around there) just to eat there. That speaks volumes. Only open for lunch hours, btw.

Went for brunch and had a spectacular time. Food was extraordinary, service was friendly and quick, decor was beautiful. The pastries were incredible, I've never seen lamination that perfect. Went back for dinner and it was a complete disappointment. The price was ridiculous. I ate at Vedge two days before and spent almost twice as much at Suraya. Overly salted mushrooms, it's almost impossible to mess up hummus so that's not impressive, my husband had the liver, it smelled like cat food. I wanted to love this place and I didn't. Dessert came out and it all became very clear. The pastry chef is the star of the show. Everything James Beard nominee James Matty touches is spectacular. My satisfaction with Suraya depended on Matty's attention, if he didn't make it, I didn't like it. Save yourself the money and go for the pastries and desserts only. There is plenty of other James Beard talent in philly who can skillfully make you a dinner you'll love.

I came here with a friend for the University City Dining Days thing ($15 for 3-course meal). Do know this is cash only, BYOB. When I first arrived, the staff seemed to make a big deal that they couldn't find our reservation (though my friend said she had made one), despite the number of empty tables. She finally seated us at a table near the door. At no point was there a line of awaiting diners so it seemed like they made a big deal out of it for no reason. The food wasn't bad but the portions were a bit on the small side. Maybe this was due to the Dining Days deal. The curry entree I got was an OK size but the appetizer and dessert were tiny. The banana-chocolate spring roll was almost dwarf-sized and definitely small enough to rule out any sort of sharing. Maybe I'll come back here and try the non-Dining Days dishes to see if the portion size will impress but my experience here was just OK.
Very good food. I always get the Gyro Sandwich. My husband loved his too which was the vegetarian platter. It included stuffed grape leaves. Yummy! Our server was very attentive.
Was in the mood for pho food while on the road, found Pho 36 and based on the reviews decided to give it a try. Well worth the drive off highway 70 Good food for the money

I ordered the Mango Lassi and the Vegetable Biryani (and wanted NO spiciness to it). The service was good and the mango lassi was delicious, but I still found the food spicy. I am not the biggest fan of Indian food, and I am very sensitive to any type of spice, so this isn't really the place for me. However if you love Indian food the prices are great and the staff is attentive so you should have a good time.

The taste of everything we had in the buffet was good, but they were very lax in keeping the containers full. One of the items I would have liked to taste more of never reappeared at all. They were quite busy so I was perplexed by their lack of planning for refills. I would go there again but maybe need to go at 11 or 12, as opposed to 1.

I ordered salmon, peas and rice and cabbage today. I've always been a fan of Ron's but haven't been there in years since I've moved. I was very disappointed in the seasonings and flavors of the food. I was used to the food at Ron's being seasoned well with all of the authentic Jamaican spices and flavors. What I received today was a watered down version of Jamaican cuisine. The salmon portion was huge but lacked flavor. The rice was bland and the cabbage tasted waterlogged. I was beyond disappointed. The best thing about my meal was the prepackaged cornbread. I don't know if they reduced their seasonings to appeal to a broader base or if the cook was inexperienced but when people order Jamaican food they want all the flavors and spices that come along with it.

Probably the worst service I have ever had in my life. Everyone in there waited at least 30 minutes for their food. Woman behind counter never apologized or gave explaination for the long wait. It was a mistake visoting this spot.

CLOSED! DO NOT ORDER! Ordered food one week, took 90 minutes to show up. Ordered food this week online (thanks Yelp!), and it turns out Asian Star has closed. Not picking up their phone, food never showed.

I know the owner personally and his restaurant turned it so much more than I already imagined it would! It makes it even more special when you see that it's managed by him and his family. They are the sweetest. The location and food is filled with elegance and flavor, in addition to that red chili sauce, that I am obsessed with. I had the pineapple rice with chicken, while my friend got the coconut soup. I don't even think I tasted my food because it looked and tasted so delicious. The egg rolls, which the owner had made me for me way before he opened the restaurant, are still amazing. The dessert couldn't have been better - the sticky rice was the right consistency and the mango combination to die for. We absolutely loved it. You won't regret it

I'm originally from Dominican Republic, which is just next door to Puerto Rico. So, I consider myself somewhat of a connoisseur of Latin American cuisine and this place was right on! Had the churrasco with yuca mash, which was seasoned and cooked to perfection. The hub had the churrasco and mofongo and he loved it too. We later enjoyed a Tres Leches, which was also delicious. My hub is a sucker for it, he says it's the best perk of having married a Latina. He has become somewhat of a Tres Leches snob and he approved of the one at Salsa.
Best breakfast in the area. The blue plate out does any and all traditional jersey diners. They have all the traditional menu options, however their specials help to separate them from the rest.

I will never understand the love for this place. A co-worker recommended Nadia Thai to me when I first moved to the area in 2006. So The Husband and I gave it a try. It was awful. The first time we went, we were approached by a panhandler as soon as we parked our car. We should have taken that as a bad omen. But we went in anyway. I forget what The Husband ordered. But I ordered the chicken pad thai. What I got was a big plate of brown stuff that smelled like fried eggs. Brown noodles, brown sprouts, brown chicken, peanuts. Only the carrots offered some color. The Husband and I gave it another try a few weeks later; we thought maybe we just went on a bad night the first time. The second time, the food was about the same. The Husband got pad thai (a big plate of brown stuff that smelled like fried eggs). And I ordered the Fantasy Duck (fried duck with raspberry-Chambord sauce). The sauce was delicious, but duck is fatty enough that it doesn't need to be/shouldn't be fried. We haven't gone back. If you want good Thai food in the area, try Chabaa Thai Bistro in Manayunk.

Food is honestly fantastic - and we almost didn't go into the building, as it's attached to a very sketchy motel (and hidden from the highway). So glad we did! Unexpectedly nice ambiance inside and the most flavorful Indian food I've had since I move to this area a few years ago!
Great music great food! This guy is phenomenal. Love it so much. You have to go here for a wonderful experience and lunch.

It was so delicious!! We wanted to go to King and I, but they are closed on Monday so I decided to look up different Thai places. This one seemed just as close and people liked it. It was so good. It wasn't extremely spicy, but that changed once we added the chili pepper spice to it. They also did not have egg plant in any of their dishes, which we were not used to, but it was still amazing. The reason I gave it 4 stars was because the sign said it was closed when it was actually open (causing us to drive back and forth on Grand) and it was kind of cold, although the server turned a space heater towards us which was nice of her. I will definitely be back though!
Very expensive. 2 entries and 2 soups were $45 dollars. The containers weren't even filled all the way. Very, very disappointed and not coming back. Soup was also quite terrible.
