Got the curry chicken, mixed rice, jerk wings, and snapper. I was craving hard for Caribbean food, tried it here, satisfied the craving but was not great. The servers are nice. But the food was mediocre for the high price they charge. Prob won't be back.

Impressed with the customer service here, everyone is very helpful and friendly. They put together my 6 entree to-go order in less than 5 minutes flat and I was out the door. As an added bonus, upon arriving home I discovered a few "extra" treats! we will definitely return.
Just had delivery, took 30 min, had duck fresh rolls and Pad Thai, a bit expensive but tasty for delivery. Tons of food enough for 2-3 people.
Can't get enough of this place! Usually get the sandwiches and haven't found a bad one on the menu. Affordable and a great meal

Great experience here!! My husband and I went for dinner here on a week night. We had Indian food before so we stuck to what we knew. Chicken Tikka Masala for me and Chicken Tikka for him. Our server was very nice and pushed my limits insisting that I have regular spicy instead of mild. He was right and joked with us about it later. I really enjoyed the interaction but others may think it's intrusive. Our food came out so fast and it was hot. It didn't taste like something that had been sitting around all day. We had garlic naan also and our bill was around $30. There was still enough food left over for lunch the next day and we left stuffed. This is a new favorite. Update: I had my birthday dinner here (party of ten). It seemed very reasonable on the wallet for all but something out of norm. The service was impeccable. I had two friends that got lost and didn't come in until an hour after we had finished. The staff acted like it was no problem. The were promptly given water and their food came out in like 15 minutes. We closed the place down!! It was about 10pm (dinner started at 6:30) and they handed us the check. We didn't get the condescending "you need coffee dessert? no! then go home!" treatment.

So im not from the area but took a trip to Trenton for a training class. I yelped near by places in the area and came across this place. Im always skeptical of jamaican food because i make it myself and places can be a hit or miss. So i drove to this place and parked near the street light (not much parking). Upon entering, the place is bright yellow so you cant miss it. I saw 2 people in the restaurant. I was looking around for a menu but could not find one. I saw a paper taped on the counter which was the menu. It was worn and washed out. I ordered the bbq herk chicken with rice and peas and cabbage. First i thought to run because the server said "rice and beans" to me and all Jamaicans know its "rice and peas". I guess its because of the area but still, thats a no no. I waited about 25 min for my order and left. When i went back to my class the smell filled the room. One of the best bbq jerk chicken i ever had. It was a bit dry but the sauce was bomb. It was spicy just how i like it. Some places dont make jerk spicy, but this one stayed to its roots. It was an abundance dance of food with so much flavor. And the hot sauce is soo good and spicy. I live and hour away but next time im in Trenton for training, i will defiantly go to this spots

This place is da bomb. Seriously though, I get down to Indian food. I've tried a lot of places around Indy and this is definitely my favorite. The only bummer is I really don't find myself in the Georgetown area that often (since we moved to Plainfield) but it is STILL worth the special trip when I need curry in a hurry (ha)! The lunch buffet is definitely where the value is at (at a $7.99 cost). They consistently have over 25 dishes available that are always hot, fresh and delicious. Holy cow, I dream about that Paneer Tikka Masala poured over rice. Plus the Palak Paneer (pureed spinach thing) is always a favorite. Naan is hot, puffy and overabundant. Also, service has always been polite and efficient. If you like Indian food, check this place out! Also, for a bonus round, check out the grocery store next door. It's not as giant as Pagoda International Market, but still has some interesting items.

Love the food here. The samosas were so good (why are samosas so hard to find around tampa bay?) and the Queens eight is always a good choice as you get to sample a bit of everything. They make sure to tell you what dishes are spicy so whimps can avoid it (which I tend to be on occasion) . The teas here are delicious too. When we came they were nice enough to let us bring in a bottle of wine. Terrific service, very unique atmosphere and delicious food

La Va is an awesome neighborhood coffee shop. They're pretty sizeable with lots of indoor seating, and a few outdoor seats. The coffee is great and they offer a lot of food items as well. I had the burekos which were fantastic. It looks like a pretzel, but it's flakey like a pastry and stuffed with feta- delish! It also looks like they turn into a BYOB for dinner in Thursday-Saturday evenings, so I'm interested in checking that out as well. The only downside is that it gets pretty crowded on the weekends and there isn't a whole lot of space in between the counter and the tables so you constantly feel like you're in the way when you're waiting for your drink/food.

Went here today to pick up some lamb kebabs for the grill. Emily offered some advice on how to prepare an authentic Turkish yogurt sauce to accompany the lamb. Picked up some cucumbers, fresh herbs, and peeled garlic as well. Very nice kebabs, had a nice spice to them.

This is the best pho place in the area having tried to find a good one the past 4 years. The key of course is the broth, which as I write this now, am already picturing me going there tomorrow! The restaurant is not in a particularly nice area, and one also wonders where one could park. But if you go during the day, all is fine and street parking would suffice.

We were so excited to eat here. The restaurant that was here before this place was Sushi Me, and that was our favorite spot. We were welcomed right away by the new owner when we arrived. She was very kind and informed us that they still have the same sushi chef that Sushi Me had. Greatest news ever to us! I will say, everything we ordered was amazing! Some of the greatest sushi in Nashville, in our opinion. However, the waitress we were given is one of the worst waitresses we have ever had in our lives. By checking in there for the first time on Yelp, you can claim a free egg roll. So we ordered that soon after arriving. And then we placed our drink orders and sushi order. We had to repeat the sushi order 3 times. She wasn't even familiar with the menu. I ordered moscato. I had to show it to her on the menu because she didn't know what that was! Same with the beer order. It wasn't a lack of understanding us at all, it's like she has never heard of any item from their menu. We sat there for at least 30 minutes with no drinks and no egg roll. I noticed that our drinks had been sitting up on the bar ready for her to bring to us. This waitress was running around appearing to be messing up other customers' tickets and orders. She kept having to get the manager. Her other tables (maybe 2 other tables) looked very aggravated, as we did. I was almost to the point of going up to the bar and getting our drinks. We finally caught her attention and asked about our drinks. She had definitely forgot and went to go get them. I asked about the egg roll. She forgot about that too, and never put the order in. She assured it would be out soon. The place was busy so we had to wait longer than usual for our sushi, but that was understandable. Finally, our sushi arrived. But no egg roll. I asked if we could have that too. She forgot. She assured it would be out soon. I will say again, the sushi was delicious! We finished all 4 rolls and finished our drinks. The waitress never once came to check on us and see if we needed anything. We finally caught her attention after sitting there for quite awhile with our empty plates and glasses, and we told her we were ready for the check and that egg roll. She forgot. She asked if maybe we could just get our egg roll next time. Are you kidding me?! I said, no we ordered it over an hour ago. We want it now. We actually wanted it before our meal. She just walked away. About another 10 minutes later she comes out with the ticket and the egg roll. In the meantime, one of her other 2 tables was getting irritated and went up to owner asking for their ticket. She never said thank you to us or sorry for our long wait or anything. In conclusion, this waitress made our experience here terrible. We wasted a lot of our Friday night sitting and waiting to be served. It was ridiculous. We definitely want to come back here because we are in love with the quality of the food. And we liked the atmosphere. But if we are ever given this waitress again we will demand a different one. All of the other waiters and waitresses seemed to be doing an excellent job. But this place is going to continue to have angry customers if they don't do something about this horrible waitress. We weren't the only ones unhappy last night.

I had the cold steamed noodle which was delicious. I also had the beef soup noodle which was OK. My main problem with the beef noodle is that the noodle is not what I expected for Northern Chinese style. The noodle is run of the mill noodle that is typically served in Cantonese restaurant as Shanghai noodle. Have not try their dumplings, may be next time.

Pretty sure they do this truck for the love of the game: At the end of a day, all the leftover food needs to go somewhere, and they let generosity take over. Me: 'can I get the three sides plate?' 'Do you like fish'? Me: 'ummm.. yes?' And thus, I ended up with three meal's worth of food: side of Collard Greens, side of Cabbage slaw, side of Rice n Beans with jerk sauce added, two servings of tasty fried fish, side of mac n cheese (and I didn't even order fish or mac n cheese!). Thank you Soul Food Truck. May your generosity never run out, though the candied yams might.

What a disappointment! I'm not exactly sure how this place shows up on so many "Best of Philly" lists (I guess they must pay their PR people quite well). But there's no excuse for the inflated ratings on this website... I expect better from you, Yelp Community!! The food: The grilled squid was heavily charred - completely overcooked and DRENCHED in lemon juice... some of the worst I've had. The "Shrimp Sauté" came out on a gigantic plate loaded up with about 2 pounds of bland rice and escarole, but only 8 tiny shrimp. It reminded me of Chinese takeout (no disrespect to Chinese restaurants, who in general do this type of dish so much better). The escarole pasta was just odd (it sounded odd on the menu, so I guess partly my fault for ordering it). 80% escarole to 20% anything else... I don't know how else to describe it other than a warm salad with pasta mixed in, very weird. The Branzino was incredibly dry and flavorless - completely overcooked. I actually liked the Spinach Pie, but I was the only one that did. Now, If the issues with our meal were merely technical, I'd maybe just assume the cook was having a really bad night. But this menu lacked any hint of creativity or complexity, and was generally unimpressive in every way. As for the service: Very poor. We waited outside for nearly an hour for our table after being told that it would be a short wait. Once we were seated the waitress was inattentive and noticeably distracted. It was very loud in the restaurant... not uncommon for tiny BYOs, but here it just made a miserable situation even worse. Basically one of the worst restaurant experiences I've had in a while...
Very good food! Will definitely be back for sure! Even though the restaurant was small the menu has a good variety and value.

When we arrived the restaurant was almost empty with only one table occupied. Hostess tried to sit us right next to that table. When I asked to be seated pointing at another table a little away from people, the hostess gave me an attitude. Food was decent but nothing special. Won't be back.
Best Indian food in st.louis . I hv been almost all Indian Restaurants In St.louis area but This one has Real Indian Taste .!! actually Perfect service and Great Price too ..!! Friendly Staff .

Cannot... bring myself... to like... Siam. Sigh. I've tried. Really. My friends love it here and I'm not a picky eater, so I tag along. Maybe it's because I usually go at lunch and we usually end up getting something from the buffet. In which case, I feel like a two-star "meh" says it all. On the whole, I love Thai food, but this buffet is your standard Asian fare per mall food courts. You know the kind: glazey, breaded chicken... sometimes sprinkled with sesame seeds; fried rice; soupy broccoli with chunks of beef; chewy eggrolls. It's not the kind of food one should necessarily be excited about. Perhaps ordering from the menu is different. I'm kind of hoping it is. Also, lesson learned. No matter how delicious your friends tell you the Thai tea is, do not order it unless you can handle the sweetness in a 5lb bag of sugar. I couldn't finish mine and ended up wasting the $2.50. Free refills on soda though! There's a plus. As others have mentioned, the parking situation is EXTREMELY limited. In the case you can't find a spot, take this as a sign from the universe and park across the street for lunch at the blue-roofed Kebab Gyro instead.

If you have ever tasted any kind of Asian cuisine before, stay away from this PF Changs. They cannot say that this is any sort of asian/chinese restaurant. I have never been so unsatisfied with a meal before. I had heard that they had tasty lettuce wraps, so we were very excited to try it. Disappointing. Singapore noodles were hard, some parts seemed undercooked, and the taste wasn't just bland...it was bad. Salt and pepper calamari - *sigh* Another bland, tasteless, soft, mushy small pieces of a baby squid. I expect calamari to have flavor, texture, ... at least some sort of BITE. They gave us a cup of salt and pepper. ????? were we supposed to dip it in that? Well, we tried and almost died from the salt. Beef and broccoli lunch order with fried rice was another disappointment. The taste was tangy and sour but not the right flavor. It was just a brown saucy tang. The fried rice looked more like brown rice with some raw carrots tossed in. Did not seem fried or seasoned. Every bite had a rock hard piece of rice that seemed frozen or had been sitting out for days. Shrimp with lobster sauce was the wrong smell, wrong taste and how do you undercook mushrooms??? The white rice that came with that was almost inedible. It was so hard and dry that I wasn't comfortable giving any to my child. Something is very wrong if you can't get simple white rice correct. I am angry at myself for having wasted so much money on terrible, bland food. I would have rather spent the same amount of money from a corner chinese store in the ghetto. At least then we would have known what to expect. If you have thoughts of going to this place, DON'T. Hop onto 476, 76 then get off Broad st and go to chinatown. Anything and everything is better there and worth the extra drive. Heck, drive around plymouth meeting and go to the first chinese restaurant you see. That surprise place is guaranteed to be better than this place. The service does not reflect on my poor review. She was attentive, friendly, and always smiling. The entire staff seemed nice and professional, but that's not enough for me to ever return here again.
Good food and great atmosphere! I've been here twice! Will return! Service was good! Food hot and tasty!!! Will return for my pasta dish that's for sure!!

Dont let the 4 stars throw you off. This place is worth making your new go to for asian food, and that's my opinion after 2 visits. Everything ive had is pretty damn good. Think standard Chinese slightly elevated with a slightly more diverse menu. The price isnt steep and i wouldnt describe it as "pricey" but i keep ending up spending a decent amount more than i would if i got it from panda pavilion a min away in audubon. The chicken and broc, rock shrimp, wonton soup, lo mein all sit around 8/10. The walnut "prawns" are just big shrimp with candied walnuts, actually really good, but not what i expected for the price 6.8/10. I also got a rainbow roll..... not so great kinda meh but the gf really enjoyed the crunchy salmon roll so im undecided at this point on their sushi game. I dont want to say wegmans rainbow roll is better but....wegmans rainbow roll was better. Wasabi isnt burn your nose off either, i like burn your nose off heat. So a 6/10 on the sushi. Either way i look forward to trying more!
Really good, simple chaat items. Authentic North Indian style. Pav bhaji was really good. Vada Pav was ok. The owner of the restaurant was helpful. Farmers market was quite a experience in itself.

We went here on a weeknight and had the curry shrimp with sticky rice and chicken pho. The food was excellent, everything arrived in a timely manner and the portions were generous. If you're wondering the food keeps well for leftovers. I highly recommend the restaurant if you've got a hankering for Asian food and are in the area.

I went with two of my friends for their lunch buffet one of which is a vegetarian. There are PLENTY of vegetarian options with clear labels as to which are not. They give you the option of plain or garlic naan to accompany your meal. We chose garlic naan and I thought it was fantastic and a great vehicle to dip into the various curries they offer. The butter chicken curry was the absolute best! The dessert options were kind of lacking; they only offered two, neither of which I cared for. Other than that, we were very satisfied with our meal. The service, however, could have been better.

I am new to Philly and was looking for a good, solid, Indian place to be my go-to. Unfortunately Mumbai Bistro will not be it. The prices were good but the portions small. My Saag Paneer was very oily and the Chicken Tikka Masala was bland. We also had Garlic Naan which seemed to have been made looong before it ever made its way to us. Indian food is nothing if not flavorful, and I was disappointed. The search continues.
Whether you're there for the buffet or ordering out, definitely get the lamb chops. They may call it something else, but they're divine.
Love love Momo's ! The beef dolmades are delicious! Every time we go we get saganaki (flaming cheese!), beef dolmades, lamb gyro - all are fantastic! Definitely don't skip their house made mojitos!

My sister and I are both regulars here! Dosa Hut has the best dosa in town. It's a total whole in the wall but in terms of food, this place is amazing. As a South Indian it's so difficult to find a place with food like this. Wait time can be long but it's worth it. I always have a hard time deciding which dosa to go for because they're all so good :) I'm vegan but I've heard great things about the chicken curries and garlic naan.

The food is great! My usual order would be the duck fried rice and white elephant for dessert. The owner and his wife are sweet and easy going. With the many times my boyfriend and I have been to this place, the owner already knows our orders! We love it here!

Jamaican Style Jerk will always be in my top favorite places of Indianapolis. The ribs are the best and certainly a must have. The chicken, a close second, but don't look past things like ox-tail. Demand the hot-sauce for your ribs. It's unique, full of flavors and is one of the few food items I've actually had dreams about. Rice and "Peas?" Yes Please. (actually, they are beans) Plantains, if no - then what the hell are you doing there? A few of my friends are intimidated by this neighborhood, don't be. This is authentic street-food, uncompromised by faux-ambience, at it's best. You could lift Jamaican Style Jerk with helicopters and ship it back to Jamaica, set it down in a randomly location and it wouldn't change it a bit. And that's what you want, isn't it?

This place sucks!!! The staff forced me Andy wife out due to a game. They rushed everything our entree came about 5 minutes after we got our appetizers. The team they were cheering lost!!! Lol! I will never go back. Thanks Scannichio for ruining our dinner!!
Ambiance was good. Service was good. We ordered Biryani which was the worst I ever ate in my life. Hara Bara Kabab was good. May not visit again.

Ok, so this was my first time eating an Indian meal. The moment I took my first bite, I thought I had died and went to heaven! Every item on my plate was packed with love, flavor, and freshness! The Chicken Makhana is to die for! The buffet gives you a nice variety, and if you've never had Indian food, I'd highly recommend this place! I went with my boyfriend for lunch and our bill was only $17.99!

We drive at least 1 hour 23 mins ONE way to come eat here!! No joke, we would come more often if we had free gas or a helicopter. This has to be the BEST Thai restaurant EVER! Not just 'cause they have a vegan menu either. It's definitely family owned and operated and the attention to detail on every menu item is startling. I usually get a large soup to go so I have leftys for a while. They even humor me with my insane requests for more Thai chilies after ordering it extra Thai hot. I ruined myself. I know. Nevertheless they make stuff mild too and everyone we have taken loves it. Cant go wrong with green curry and thai tea. Don't let the tofu app go un-ordered its a treat. Only warning is sometimes food is served PIPING hot... like blow on that spoon for a long while.

Hands down best pho on this side of the river (Mopho you're good too but this is ). It's very flavorful and quick. They have great banh mi too. P They have a pho-rito that I haven't tried yet, but my friends love it! This place is a wonderful gem in midcity and it makes me so happy

The chicken wrap was pretty good but could use some more flavor. The combination platter was delicious and flavorful and you could tell all of the ingredients were fresh. It's a shame the place is so hard to find. I never would've known it was there without yelp. There's no sign outside with the place's name on it.
It was nice friendly place. Look plain outside but inside is simple elegance. Food was fresh, great flavors. Really good. In the summer I am sure view is lovely loved this place. I will be back

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Our go-to for Asian takeout. Consistent quality. Their Thai Curry is outstanding. Sushi is also decent.

As Indian restaurants go, this is the bottom of the list for me. I try to give every India restaurant a chance, and when I heard this place had a buffet for DINNER, that clinched it. Unfortunately, everything I had lacked the taste I've come to expect. The chicken Makni tasted like it was made with spaghetti sauce, the shrimp masala was very fishy, and the naan bread looked and tasted like it had been on the steam table all night. For Indian in Philadelphia, the best so far is the Indian Restaurant, you'll see it under my other reviews. I should have known what I was in for in terms of service when the person who showed me to my table left the pitcher of water behind. No offer for anything else, I was on my own.

This is our favorite Spanish Restarant in Tampa. Some of our favorite dishes are shrimp mofongo, as well as churasco steak with rice & beans. Spanish decor with friendly & pleasant staff has always greeted us and helped us enjoy the experience.

First impression was favorable. The waitress was quick, and was helpful in recommending dishes to try. We ordered the simosa, dal mahkani, and palak paneer. All were amazingly good. The food came out very fast, and was very delicious, and fresh tasting. Spiciness level of the food will be more than you are expecting--I recommend going with mild if you are not sure. The prices are very reasonable for the portion you get (a lot). If you are ordering 2 or more entrees the rice is included. Taj-India is a very good value and the food is amazing.

The service is great. The entrees are terrific, anything freshly made. The place is not busy. We really loved the Palak and the Tikka Marsala. The breads were very stale, which was quite disappointing. I'll go back but I'll see if I can find their busiest night and go again, hoping they freshly make poppadom and naan if there is a crowd.

Ate here with 6 friends on a Saturday nite. Waited almost an hour for drinks and even longer for food. Never got drink refills and had to get my own menu and flatware. If it is busy run away. If not slammed hang in cause the food is sometimes well worth it. They were so overwhelmed and then on a single person ticket added and automatic tip. Which really made me angry for such poor service that was not the waitresses fault but the dishwasher and kitchen staffs mess up. Grrrr. I hate to have to post such a poor review.

Decided to pick a random place to have dinner one night; Mojito had good service and great food. I had the ropa vieja and the meat was tender and flavorful... crispy yuca fries and guacamole with nachos were fresh and spot on as well. I got a beer and my GF had a drink she enjoyed, but both weren't enough to comment on the bar really. They should really play Cuban, or at least Latin, music... but otherwise it's a cool restaurant with good food.

Wonderful Ethiopian food here. Very nice, clean eating establishment. Nice service and very good deal for generous amount good quality food. Try the vegetarian platter with 7 separate dishes served with lovely injera bread (serves 2 people)! If you want the fried fish you have to call a day ahead and request it. OR if you want half meat, half vege, try the #1 and the #3, for the best of BOTH worlds. The prices are very cheap and quantities ample!! A side note, this place is in a strip mall, back behind on the side, it's hard to see and it almost looks as if it's closed down...but wait!! It's not! Go on in and enjoy! They also seem to accommodate large parties well as almost every time I go they have tables pushed together for such. NOTE: Abay is now closed on TUESDAYS.

Disappointed, as either this was an off night, or they have gone downhill. Two of the four meals were served almost ten minutes before the other two. One of the meals was actually cold and had to be sent back to be warmed up. One item was requested to be left off of one of the meals and it was served with it on it. The food itself was greasy and heavy. One of the items charged an extra $2.00 for shrimp, but there were only two small shrimp included. Unless they improve, we will not return
This place is always great ! Very friendly staff,delicious food,We love this place cannot wait to go back again.

The menu selection here is mediocre but the decor and atmosphere are perfect. Most of the hookah joints I find are party places with blaring music and sports on the tv. This place is quiet and comfortable. If they got some Fumari or similar on the menu it'd be perfect.

My most favorite place for a Greek salad is Kalamata's. Surprisingly, this is the only thing I have ever eaten here. Minus the occasional tomato basil soup if they have it. BUT, the salad is good enough to keep me coming back time and time again. I think it is the combination of the dressing and the garlic knot that comes with it. It's simply just fantastic. Yum. My boyfriend usually orders the combo kabob Greek salad, and he swears that the meat is some of the best cooked beef he's ever had in Nashville. I don't like meat on my salad, but I have gotten the chicken in the past, and it was really good. OH, and you can not leave without trying a baklava. Kalamata's is right in the heart of Green Hills right across the street from the mall. It's convenient and quick, unless you go at lunch and have to wait in a long line out the door. My one complaint is that the prices are a little high, but I gladly will pay a little more for food that is amazing every time.
Went last night before Amy Schumer, the service was great but the food was awesome! My husband had the filet with crab and I had the rack of veal....YUM Thank you and we'll be back!!

I came here expecting just to try something new. The food was amazing but even more than that, I really felt like a guest here, just an amazing sense of hospitality is how I would describe it. Attached photo is a screenshot of my sister posting on fb about the meal.

Spinach & mushroom piadina was flavorful and I was a big fan of the feta/parsley spread, but this was not filling at all for me. I finished my lunch and was still hungry. I get that they charge higher prices for quality ingredients, just wish the higher price tag also meant a more filling meal. The braised white beans are very hearty and delicious.

Food decent. Service horrible. Went here with a large church group of about 20 on Sunday around noon. My expectations were that it would take longer to get our lunch served - but it was ridiculous. Our order was 2x Pad Thai and 1x pho plus 3 bubble teas. The noodle dishes came out after maybe 25. But the pho took at least 45 minutes to show up. Everyone else was done with their lunch by the time she got her pho - which sadly it's just soup and really should have been one of the first things out. The bubble teas we ordered never even made it out. There were a number of workers milling about and not doing anything and laughing at the waiter that we had to keep flagging down to get water refills. I'm not sure if these are the same owners as the one in Rivergate - but honestly just go to the one over there. Much much better.
Best falafel yet! It was light and fluffy like a hush puppy! I was impressed. Great options for vegetarians! The lentil soup was delish and the mo jadara v was awesome! Will be back.

We showed up for lunch on a weekday in Feb this year. Took my mom (who'd never eaten Ethiopian before) and we totally relied on my fellow Yelper's reviews. OMG am I glad I did!!! Although the S.O. and I have eaten Ethiopian in a lot of different cities, this one was one of the best. And who'da thunk it would be on the strip in Reno? (I'm a native...I can poke fun at my home town) Seriously, the food was just awesome, the housemade cheese was divine, the ambiance was perfect, Server/owner was kind and accommodating. We took plenty of leftovers. S.O. Had the Lamb. Mom and I shared the Beef Strips. We all loved the Enjera bread and the cheese. The chopped spicy salad was THE BOMB. I could have eaten bowls of just that! There's something about the tactile element of eating with your hands and eating smaller bites that fills you up quickly. I realized eating with a fork is overrated and just shovels it in quicker.....you don't realize you're full until you're stuffed. Back to Zagol.....I'm happy as a clam this place is in Reno and I hope it becomes a mainstay!! Good Food, Good Prices, Good Location, and an Owner that cares and is AUTHENTIC! Will post pics also!!!!

This place is off the charts. My wife ordered from a flyer that was on our door 2 years ago and it has been a staple ever since. The Chicken shisih tawook is off the hook, so is the pizza and anything else on the menu.

Gave this place two chances. They won't get a third. The chicken in the Pho is not fresh and is over cooked. Their service is poor and the sauces on the tables are gross on the outside. You'd think they could clean them off once in a while.

Haven't been to hometown favorite spot in a bit and needed to check in.... well.... they have never disappointed me before and they still haven't. I think this creeping up on double digit dining experiences with Chef Joey Baldino and staff... (ooofa). Anyway, had the grilled Octopus special which was absolutely perfectly cooked, tender, just singed on the grill with some lemony potatoes and herb salad, a perfect way to start a meal. Had the famous Gambos., (head on Shrimp that honestly may have been the best i've ever had their, and that's truly saying something, maybe is was just because i was dining solo and got to have it all to myself, hee hee). Then things got serious... I really upped the anti by ordering two full main courses, the first the Disgraziata which is rigatoni with eggplant and ricotta salata that would make you faint, and the second was another special, the sepia pasta, (which is my all time fave) and boy you better believe i did not think twice about ordering both mains and two huge pastas and sitting there and devouring both of them consecutively. Also got a nice bite sent out from the kitchen as well as a beautiful Pistachio and Hazelnut gelato concoction that was mindbending... Bravo Zeppoli, you never let me down, ever. Best in The Whole REGION for the price point and the quality. If you have never been go, if you have go back..

its a very hole in the wall place about a 5min Uber ride from The Grand Sierra Resort. they close at 9p. limited parking. the first thing i noticed when we waljed in was the yummy aroma of some good cuisine. ...and the cuisine is delicious!!!! i was skeptic because i was going by 5 star yelp reviews alone ...and the location is hole in the wall .. in a random area near car sales spot ...BUT....the restaurant inside is well decorated, has a large dining space, the waitress at the time we went in was nice and friendly and offered suggestions and attentive. ...and the food we ordered tasted awesome...impressive even! im no chinese food guru but i know what i like and i will honestly tell the world if a place sucks ...and this restaurant didnt. i recommend that you go here for inexpensive chinese eating rather than that shi shi resort bistro wannabee ish.

I knew Doan's when they were in Chinatown and the place was flaming! Not with vibrant colors and men looking more prettier than me! I mean flaming as in fire fighters and smoke and crispiness! Two locations: Southside off Whyte and Downtown on 107 Street. Great food, little pricey when you are looking for Vietnamese food compared to other restaurants however cleaner, fast service, great looking dishes and over all good food. I love, love, love their Satay soup! They put cilantro in it and I am huge fan of cilantro!

I used to dine at Shere-E-Punjab when I lived in Media, but hadn't been there in maybe 5 years. We returned to try out the carefully-labeled gluten-free options on their menu, and we were NOT disappointed. I ate until it HURT. We started with the aloo tiki chaat - a recipe that we have vowed to try to re-create at home. It was truly excellent, and so large it could be an entree on its own. We made up the rest of our meal with our favorites (chana masala, dahl mahkani, and aloo gobi) which left us with plenty of leftovers. We were somewhat confused about their BYO status, since they have a wine menu, but other seemed to be carrying-in. Would save ourselves some money & BYO the next time. Taking a nice walk around Media to work off some of that delicious food is a must. ;)

One of the better Indian places in the city. Food looks and tastes fresh. Easy on the stomach and on the pocket. The number of dishes may be less, but whatever is on the menu is cooked nicely. Nothing is overly done with cream or spices. Perfectly cooked. Today was my first time here, and I am definitely going to frequent this place. Also, Mumbai Bistro is located on the intersection of DELHI street and Locust st. (between 9th and10th), which is kind of ironic :)

I had the veggie egg rolls, shrimp Tom Yum soup and a side of steamed rice. The soup was tasty and a huge portion for $6.00 with shrimp in it. It had a little bit more kick than usual (without asking for it) which I dig. Not the biggest fan of the egg rolls. They could have cooked them a little longer to get a golden crispy outside. Part of the inner wrapping was soft and the insides were mushy. The rice was mushy as well which is not my fave. But I eat it with the soup so not that big of a deal. Probably won't be back just because there are some really good other Thai restaurants in this area.

Nice place to go for a very interesting taste of the Middle East. We caught a nice day and were able to sit outside. It is a neat atmosphere. The food was interestingly good. We had baba ganoque (spelling?) and a hummus spread with really fresh breads. Also shared the lamb wrap and chicken wrap. A baklava and a Ishmaerala (spelling?) were absolutely wonderful desserts. A few glitches were that the crepe maker was broken and that the machine to make a special drink was broken. Reasonable price, nice waitress and very good food give this a 4 out of 5 star rating.

Easily my new favorite for Indian food in STL (2nd only to Bombay Food Junkies, which is more casual Indian street food). Tried the lunch buffet and was pleasantly surprised. Each dish was flavored independently (some Indian places try to get away with sharing their gravy bases - but not this one!). They had lots of vegetarian dishes, multiple dessert options, and even masala chai included as a part of the buffet. I loved the fried pakoras, which were cooked perfectly. The naan was freshly prepared, and the kheer (sweet rice pudding) was divine. The spice level was mild, as you'd expect for a buffet, but the food was still flavored well. There was some dry vegetable pickle on the side, if you wanted to add heat, but would've loved some traditional Indian pickle as well. The waitress did say they offer an extended buffet on the weekends, with Dosa, Chana Bhatura, Pani Puri, and other delicacies. Visit Fri-Sun if you want to try something different than the usual buffet items. Service was outstanding, as was the decor. We especially loved the Bollywood music and the Indian food channel that was playing on the TVs, as it added to the experience of traditional Indian cuisine!

I live in Hamilton NJ I've been in search of a PHO spot that's local and found this Gem Came across my yelp account and I couldn't help but take a look at what they have to offer came here was there every surprise on how good the food was I will be returning and I will be back with more friends and family
Little gem of a place with an amazing 9.99 lunch special. Had the chicken korma and paneer curry, which comes with generous serving of naan.

I am truly amazed by the food and atmosphere here, I had the shrimp and grits and my wife had the shrimp Po boy. The service was great and the food was very timely. We will definitely be back here when we return to the St. Pete.Awesome and filling

I stopped by here for some jerk chicken to compare it with Jamaican Jerk hut. I think they are pretty similar, and at $7 for a small platter with a ton of chicken this is a great deal. The jerk sauce is really good, being in the take out container though it gets all over everything, which is not great when you need a reprieve from the spiciness. I got the mac and cheese and the string beans as sides, and they were both good. The mac and cheese wasn't the best I ever had, but there was a lot of it. The chicken was very tender and very moist, and there it was mostly white meat. There also weren't really any gross chicken parts, just bones and meat. There are so many great food trucks be Penn, but this one is definitely worth a stop.

I have been wanting to try Suraya out for awhile. Made reservations on opentable for a Friday night. It was pretty busy when we got there so make sure you have reservations on the weekend. It's such a pretty restaurant with a great atmosphere. Perfect for a date night. The food was delicious especially the hummus and grilled prawn dish. Honestly the grilled prawn dish was one of the best dish I had in awhile. It was grilled with the head still on and the head of the prawn is my favorite part to eat. It has so much flavor. I'm so glad there's a restaurant that isn't afraid to cook the entire shrimp! The sauce that was drizzle on it gave it so much more flavor. All the dish is made to share and we ordered 3 different dishes on the menu to share and it was enough for both of us. All the dish comes with fresh pita bread. I also ordered a few cocktails and it just made my meal even more complete. Thanks for a nice date night!

During my last visit I tried to discuss how the steak is sometimes tough and ordered a brisket to be more tender. I think there was a language barrier and they gave me all fat. Literally the type of meat you trim off when you prepare your meat. I know this is an option to order on the menu, so some people must like it. But this is not what I ordered and I couldn't stomach to eat it. I just ate the noodles and broth. This happened twice at this restaurant when I felt I was explaining myself pretty well.

WOW, this place is great. I'm guilty of being a super picky eater, so trying new places can be scary; this hole-in-the-wall has made me a believer. Their lunch special is dynamite, taste- and cost-wise, and they happily subbed my tom yum soup for one without mushrooms. The food is just delicious. The woman who works the counter is very friendly. It's definitely the best place close to my work and I am so happy that they exist. Seriously-- try this place out! I don't think you'll be disappointed.

Best Dominican food and service I have had to date. They gave large portions and I couldn't finish all of it. My preteen son could, of course. And I saw a lot of Non-Latinos coming in to buy food. The only thing they are missing is a bar and a night club. That would be crazy hot!

Good Thai food for a VERY good price. The selection here is huge, and includes one of my Thai faves: beef salad, which is sauteed beef, onions, cilantro (and other veggies), chilled and served over hot steamed rice. It's spicy and wonderful, but the last time I was there it was offered as an appetizer when I asked for it. My portion was perfect. I really like their spring rolls, and they offer a fish cake appetizer that goes well with rice. Additionally, their summer rolls are fantastic (and huge!). It's a low-key atmosphere, and you're not going to get ridiculously great service, but you definitely won't get bad service. I got everything on time and the right order. That's all you could ask for when there's a table full of great food right in front of you.

Awesome food - this is our go to takeout place. Ordering online is super quick and the food is consistently great. We make a lot of our own Indian fare and have had trouble duplicating the quality of the dishes on the menu.
Delightful people and incredible food. If you live anywhere in the central FL area I highly recommend this treat!

Update! Appropriate amount of chutney if you ask with your takeaway (a couple of times, lol) huge plus! Nothing worse than 3 entrees with a tiny chutney Gets extra star Great service, our server was very nice and accommodating (I wish I got her name, but forgot to ask). We always order a lot when we go out for Indian so we have leftovers - and we're kind of picky (one meat eater, one vegetarian) so I wouldn't say we are the easiest table for a server. We're kind of needy and annoying. But she was very sweet and patient. We had our 7 month old baby with us who is new(ish) to food and I was looking forward to her trying a bit of yellow dal. The server let us order kind of a "side portion" (which isn't on the menu) and made sure the kitchen knew it was for a baby. I, of course, know it's something she's allowed to eat and would have made been cautious of any unpredictable spices or large pieces, but it was so nice for the server to do that for me without my even asking. The food is fine. We ordered several entrees to share and the table all enjoyed the shrimp biryani the most. They also serve onion chutney (generally a hit or miss). I like it and was glad to have it!

This man makes an amazing falafel with only the barest of essentials in his lil falafel truck. He's lost a star since he keeps upping the prices, and also runs out of food crazy fast, and the line is the bane of my existence (often taking up a good - but worth it - 1/2 hour of my lunch). But I am happy to keep going back and greatful he's always there.

Soup....vietnamese noodle soup...ok they do have more than just soup. They have sald rolls and spring rolls and other vietnamese dishes. Now i haven't really sat in this restaurant as i always order out during my lunch breaks at work. i just preorder with the take home menus and pick it up at a set time... I really enjoy the soup, but I'm more of the adventurous type, the type meat toppings they offer is not as exquisite as you find in other "Hole in the wall" venues whcih i thoroughly enjoy. I would consider DOAN's a more high end Vietnamese restaurant. It has a pretty good location. But I like having my food to be original and diverse. Unfortunately they don't go that route, they are kinda the conservative type with their dishes.

This place has some good Pad Thai but the servers could use some more serving lessons. The first time we went, I had ordered my Pad Thai WITHOUT peanuts and it came with peanuts. Lucky for them, I wasn't allergic but our server came over and was very sorry and replaced it with another one -- not for free, sadly. The beef was spoiled and it was a very bad first experience but we gave it another shot last night and it wasn't too bad. My husband thinks that their Pad Thai smells like a farm but I don't really smell it and it was good enough for me. This is a once every six months kind of place.

Great Indian Food! Best part, the only Indian restaurant in STL that has a Dinner Buffet on Fridays! Service is great! Looks cleverly clean and nicely decorated! Prices are very reasonable, you definitely get your money's worth. Really enjoyed the mango lassi!
For a small strip-mall restaurant they do Indian food very well. A nice find, recommended by Indian friends. We've been back a few times, so it's worth trying.

Best Caribbean/Jamaican in Indy, hands down. The jerk chicken was great and an even better deal. Got a whole bird with rice and peas for $16. Enough to feed 4 people. You can't beat that. The ribs were really good. I don't know how I have passed this place so often without trying them. Don't make the same mistake.

I've been walking past this place for months waiting for them to open, and was finally able to check them out on their second day. The other reviews that mention that it's cheap and fresh with somewhat muted flavors are accurate. The samosas were awesome; really fresh and only $2 for 2 of them. That is insane. It'd be cheaper and more delicious for me to eat these samosas than cook any meals, so there's a good chance that that's what I'll do.

These gyros are amazing! I have never had a pita that was so soft and delicious. Ok, so maybe we'd had a few drinks before we shoveled this ethnic delight into our mouths but I like to think I still had my discerning tastes about me. Hubs agreed so two people can't be wrong. If you're in the mood for eating on the cheap and something other than the typical NOLA fare, I highly recommend this establishment- conveniently located in the French Quarter!

We enjoyed our food. I had the saag lamb full of tender and delicious lamb and my husband had the Biryani special which was also delicious.The food was well prepared and spiced perfectly to our liking! The drinks at the bar were great with magnificent mojitos. The restaurant was busy because of Dining under the stars and service was a bit slow due to the high volume of patrons. It likely would be five stars on a quieter night in Media.

So glad we made the last minute decision to come here. It's a very intimate setting and quiet (which I like). The cocktails were fabulous. I'm sorry to say I can't remember the name of mine but I took a picture. The Israeli bruschetta, cauliflower and zucchini has amazing flavors. I highly recommend. Can't wait to try the restaurant upstairs!

I've never seen a place have more than 5 reviews and none of them were less than 3 stars. That should speak for itself. This place is fantastic, and I'm lucky to have it in my 'hood, as I hear folks bike from all over town to sate their cravings for awesome West Indian food.

This is my favorite pho restaurant after Pho 777. I was really surprised the first time we ate here, since this is simply the place closest to us, bu really no other place is better. Except maybe 777, to which I have a long standing loyalty.

Finally made it here post Midtown Village Festival. Our posse rolls deep i mean like 12 or more so that fact that they could seat us right away when i called was awesome. We had to split into 3 groups of 4 but that was not an issue for us as we were famished and needing to continue to drink. My one beef with this place is that everything took soooooooooo lonngggggggg (maybe it was just that i was slightly drunk and very hungry). We waited for what felt like an eternity to place our orders,to get our starters and entrees. Since Jasmine is known for their curries I decided on the panaeng curry for its coconut base. Jasmine offers multiple levels of heat for all tastes so you can customize your food to your liking.When our food finally arrived i dived right into to the curry and was pretty impressed with the depth of flavor. The curry had a slight sweetness to it from the coconut base but i opted for level 3 heat and that kick balanced out the dish quite nicely. The portion size was right on point for the price. This is a great option for anyone that maybe doesn't want to make the trek to NoLibs or South Philly to order Circles. Its a BYOB and they accept cards. The only reason I cant rate it higher was the slow service. I must make a return visit to try some of the other curries.

It's my mission to eat at every thai restaurant in Indy! Found this place thanks to yelp. We came here for take out. Took a while to flag the dude at the counter but finally got his attention. (They should really invest in a service bell!) love that there post pictures of there food, I know most of all the thai dishes but it's always good to know what to expect. Love that the prices is very reasonable. Orders pad thai level 2 spicy and pad seew level 5 (the spiciest of them all!!!) the pad thai was not so great, it was bland. It was missing flavor. But they give you so much noodles!! It was enough to feed 3 people. My pad seew was so yummy!!! The spiciness and veggies with noodles really hits the spot. Also asked for dry chili peppers on the side and made it even better. I really love spicy food and I can take the heat! I would come here again but it's a little far from home, just won't be ordering the pad Thai again. But definitely the pad seew is a must! And the food is cheap!

Oh goodness, I'm following around Emily Y. Wait... I went here with Emily Y. :) Rustic Thai, home styled cooking with decorations laden with country style thai accents. The obligate portrait of the King is present, as well as bamboo structures recalling another time and place. The food that we enjoyed on our visit were competently executed, but without any striking highlights. I fear that my palate is becoming increasingly jaded... and nowadays, I'm still looking for that epicurean epiphany of flavour. None here... but I left sated nonetheless. 4/5 particularly with attention to context.

This was the best bowl of pho I've ever had. After reading the 4 & 5 star reviews and ignoring the one 3 star review my wife and I decided to give Pho Friendly a try. We had the eggs rolls, the pork bowl, a bowl of rare eye round pho, and Vietnamese coffee. All were outstanding! While talking up their food the owner prided herself in her coffee, saying she owned a coffee shop in her country. It was the best for sure. We also got a chance to talk to a regular. It was a pleasure to exchange pleasantries and rave about how much we enjoyed the food. He'd been eating there since 2016. This place is a hidden gem and worth the trek off the beaten path!!!

The place is really clean, food looks and tastes great until I realized there was a long hair in my soup. I used to work for restaurants, I know things like that happen. It was kinda uncomfortable because the place was really nice and cozy.

Basil Spice really takes on the presentation game. Especially in comparison to 99% of the other Thai restaurants in the area. So you get a wonderful presentation of delicious Thai food, set to as spicy as you would like it to be, and have a little room for the sticky rice dessert, which is simple, yet indulgent. I like the pad thai, of course, but definitely try the pad see iw. Noms. If you like spicy, they can certainly make it spicy for you. Try it, if you can! If you want huge portions, go to a buffet. Sometimes the "Wow" factor in American dining has people so wound up in huge portion sizes that they forget that food is something more than just filler for your stomach. It's about flavor and culture.
the best place on earth, try the naked gyro, all meat. large gyros, very tasty, fresh, fast service , sit down or take out. I love this place. located by 21 & lindberg, in south county.
Awesome chicharrones, and the shrimp with cabbage were outstanding. If you come to NOLA to eat, step off the beaten path and come here!

I was so glad to have a pho place in the neighborhood, so I'm rooting for these guys! They just need to work out some of the details. Decor - clean, tasteful, Asian-inspired but contemporary. Food - I ordered the pork spring rolls and a bowl of pho with rare flank steak and brisket. Spring rolls were crispy, not oily, and tasty. The pho had fresh ingredients (Thai basil, sprouts, lime, good quality, tender meat). Alas, the broth was not very flavorful compared with some of the places down on Wash. Ave. It's lacking that "stewed for hours", hearty beef flavor I've come to love at places like Pho Ha or Pho 75. That's a big one they'll need to work on. Service - started out strong, then fell off a cliff. I was seated quickly, ordered quickly, food arrived quickly, then....hey, where'd everybody go? No one checked in to see how everything was, my water glass was empty, I had to wait for my check (after I waved down the hostess, who was very friendly), then I had to wait for them to pick up the check when I was ready to pay. Someone who appeared to be a manager was futzing with the lighting and the thermostat (we'll get back to the temperature in a second), but no one seemed to be paying much attention to the dining room, and not for lack of staffing. One more thing - there's a blast of cold air every time the door opens, and the dining room was freezing. They need to put a heavy drape or something between the door and the dining room in the winter. I'll be back to iPho to give them another try because I love a good, hot bowl of pho. I'm hoping the next time will be a little bit better.

While my photo doesn't look the most appealing the food here is delicious, easy and cheap. I got the tilapia burrito (extra spicy) for 6$! The truck is always very busy but luckily I made it 5 minutes before closing. They said they had run out of the chicken and short ribs but had there vegetarian options and fish left. While I had gotten the tilapia burrito I'm sure if I had gotten the veggie burger it would have still been delicious!

Good Thai restaurants are hard to find in Bucks County. This one is one of the best we found. The pad kai Mao with chicken was delicious and spiced as requested at a 5. Thee beef with red curry level 7 was a warm glow over the tongue and we'll prepared. We will be back.

It seems like every article I've read about new restaurants keeps mentioning Marjie's Grill, so I had it on my list. When Chef Goodenough from Carrollton Market mentioned how good the Cubanh Mi special is, I moved it to the top of my list and made a point of getting over there. I stopped in for lunch and it was perfect timing because the crowd was thinning out. Of course, I knew what I wanted so I ordered the Cubanh Mi and eagerly waited for my mind to be blown- and blown it was. If you're a fan, in any capacity, of Cuban sandwiches, this sandwich is a must. It's braised smokey rib meat on a pressed Ideal Market roll, with mozzarella, herbs, chilis and hot mustard. It was delcious! The rib meat was tender, juicy and flavorful, the chillis added the perfect amount of kick and the cheese brought the whole thing together. It was like an Asian Cuban sandwich and they NEED to make this a regular part of their menu. The sandwich is $12 and I ate half for lunch and had the rest for dinner. The staff here is friendly and the decor is adorable. They have a patio outside, but it was in the 30s on the day I was here, so that will have to wait for another time. They have a very eclectic menu, and check out their Instagram because they're always posting yummy food pics.

This place serves exceptional Dominican food and drinks. Everything Caribbean from chimichurris to country club drinks, they even make delicious shakes from all kinds of fruit. This is my favorite Dominican spot in Tampa

My boyfriend picks up tacos for me weekly from here! He went to Drexel and has been coming here, years later, religiously. Their spicy mayo is the best I've had! The tacos are always good, the short rib is a must try if you ever get it before it sells out. The chicken satay is never a bad choice, it's just good tacos. When everything melds together perfectly. We tried the tilapia burrito yesterday, uhm yeah, instant favorite. With sriracha and spicy mayo, that crunch is bomb. Also have tried the katsu, not bad at all, but I didn't enjoy it as much as the tacos.
Really nice patio, good happy hour menu. Service was a little slow but the Aruba Scallops were amazeballs.

I had dinner here after a friend's reccommendation. It absolutely exceeded my expectations! I had the palak paneer and samosas and they were fantastic! The palak paneer was creamy with slight heat and the samosas were very sizable, I had to save the second one for lunch! I will definitely be returning! (*Note - I had to change my review to 4 stars, the last time I ate here it really wasn't as great and they forgot to include my samosas and even the rice! I couldn't go back for it because I live pretty far away (about 45 minutes) and it just wasn't worth it. I will still go back but not as frequently as other Indian restaurants.)

Great addition to Harleysville for Indian food and this complements the top notch Butcher and Bar Keep in the same shopping center. Service is excellent and they have started a buffet recently with good spread and very well priced at $8.98. Mango lassi would be better if they take out the additional spice flavor and just keep it pure. Goat curry and chicken tikka were highlights along with Gulab Jamun in a light syrup that's perfect and not too sweet.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in town. I have been here no less than 10 times. The service is always attentive and the waitstaff is well versed in their fare. Favorites are: Tomato Bruschetta, Lamb flatbread, octopus when they have it (I think its seasonal). Drinks are delicious. Food is always fresh and of excellent quality. They don't take reservations for parties of less than 6.

Crazy falafel dude! Nomnomnom... nom. nom. How does a food cart take at minimum 5 minutes per person, have no menu, show up whenever he wants, and still have 30 person lines in both freezing and boiling hot weather?? Last time I went, it was 38F with 18mph winds constantly, yet the line was still wrapped around the corner. He did give out some free creamy tomato soup to warm everyone up, which was nice of him. The menu is whatever he feels like giving you and it'll always be $10. You tend not to ask for special orders because he just sorta stares at you, incredulous, and you feel like he's going to Soup Nazi you out of line forever. You'll generally receive a plate which contains freshly charcoal grilled chicken, three falafels, hummus, a starchy product, a salad product, and maybe a drink whenever he feels like giving you one. There's no avoiding the line so hopefully you get a long lunch break. Sadly, he's unavailable on the weekends so I can't gorge myself full-time. Obviously, this 5 star review is so much different than the other hundred 5 star reviews this guy gets so that means his cart isn't good at all. That's how this works, right? Don't go to this cart, because I don't want to line up behind even more people :) Cheers.

I went with my colleagues to try this restaurant as we were looking for a great Thai restaurant to try. We arrived before noon to ensure we could get a table for 5 and were promptly seated. There is a lunch special for $9.95 for soup, spring rolls, rice, and a dish. I ordered the pad thai which did not come with rice but a healthy serving of noodle, bean sprouts, 2 large shrimp, and chicken. The soup was a little too spicy for my liking but was a hit with my colleagues. The 2 vegetable spring rolls came with a sauce and were a nice appetizer before the main meal. I sampled the chicken, beef, and pork dishes my colleagues ordered and was impressed by the heat, sauce, and amount of food. No surprise the restaurant gets busy at lunch so best to go early and don't be too rushed as the service isn't the quickest either. But for the value and food, I will definitely be back.

What can I say about this place? This cafe is in Irvington Park and is a little hidden gem. They serve breakfast and lunch, but you can get the breakfast selections all day. Love the bow tie pasta with smoked salmon. It's a side, but a great light lunch option. Everything is wonderful on the menu, but the desserts cannot be missed! I am from the south and love caramel cake -- Laura's caramel cake is the best I have ever had. A slice of cake and a French press coffee -- you are in heaven!

I was in Boise this week from Seattle. I was looking for Middle Eastern food and came across Kabob house which was recommended by a friend. I must say I am very pleased with the delicious flavors of the food and the awesome service Mr Fraidon (the owner) gave us. I loved the food so much I went back again yesterday for a late lunch before flying back home to Seattle. I will definitly be back when I am in Boise. I would like to thank the cooks in the kitchen as well because they are the ones putting the love into the food. Thanks you guys!

Been there twice, always clean and bright inside, the staff are friendly. They have frequent visitor reward program, pick up a card and they will punch every time you visit, you earn a free dish every 5 visits. It's easy to order from the online menu. The food is good and tastes fresh, specially the appetizers. So far, have tried lobster fried rice, calamari, chicken and shrimp Shu Mai, vegetable dumplings, chive pancake, pumpkin custard but the best and the most unexpected in the Thai iced coffee and the fried bananas with honey. Both were amazing, this might be the new go to place for coffee and dessert.
Unable to understand what Thai Hot means. At least they know what sticky rice is. When a customer asks for Thai hot don't bring them a plate that taste like sugar.

Its definitely an upgraded version of your local chinese food spot minus all the grease! The food is clean, fresh and falvorful. The vegetarian lettuce wraps are great, but for the size of the dish they need to serve it with more than 4 lettuce leaves...lol The pear mojito was strong too! :)
Good family place if you like to enjoy the put side sitting and view of the noises of running cars.. Good are delicious..
Super cute atmosphere and a great cup Of coffee. The platter with chicken, hummus, rice and salad was really fresh and tasty. Will go here again when in the area.

The food was excellent and I really enjoyed dinner. We had the channa masala with rice and a Mysore dosa which was delicious but a large amount of food (I was happy to take home what I couldn't finish). It was quite busy on a Saturday which I expected; however, the server was polite and came by regularly to check on us. I would gladly go to dinner again at this restaurant.
They're not real gyros :( it's more like fast food and not authentic what-so-ever. Def will not be returning. Chick at window had zero personality either:[
Yum yum! Great Greek food right in the Quarter. Small restaurant with barely any chairs. I think a lot of people get their food to go. However, there is room to eat there unless it is really crowded.

Bread service was excellent. Both a fluffy sourdough and olive loaf. Olive oil was a decent flavor too. Parm from a shaker bottle so not freshly shaved. Arancini was cooked great and 2 big balls, but the gorgonzola was too prevalent and ruined the flavor for me. Spinach salad was excellent. Good blend of sweet with the mandarin orange and cranberry with the bitter feta cheese. House oil dressing was a good balance. Caesar salad was good. Would be better served cold. Dressing was flavorful. Cannelloni was very unique. Not your typical italian style. This one was super spiced with black pepper and other Turkish seasonings. A rich pink sauce smothered it. I will get this again. So many other things on the menu I want to try. Will have to come back soon.

An example of perfection! Simply perfect. The Vibe, the space, the music, every aspect lent itself to another wise perfect meal. Every flavor was enhanced by the last and made more enjoyable by the next. For a moment it tasted as though I was back in the Middle East, it looked like I was in LA or NY, areal gem in the hart of South Saint Louis. Willie, Nick and of course Ben. Very well done I will see you soon and often.

been eyeing Suraya for so long and finally had the chance to check it out. came here during a wednesday noon and there was already a big line when we went in. It is such a cute restaurant with a great atmosphere. when you first walk in you order at the counter and take your number sign to find a seat. water and utensils are self served. we ordered the traditional hummus(comes with two pitas), two extra pitas and the Lebanese chai latte. the Lebanese chai latte came in the cutest mugs and was good but the main star for us was def the hummus and pitas. they were are absolutely delicious!!! could have it all day if i can, no joke! cannot wait to come back and try all the other amazing foods they have.

Okay. If you are in the neighborhood and craving Thai, this will do for a Rittenhouse square price. And, I can't recommend the Tom Yum, small and too sweet. If you want real, awesome Thai for a way better price, head down to Circles in South Philly. Miles better food. Circles all the way!

I had this truck for the first time last night at the symphony in Forest Park. I admittedly waited too long to get food, but this truck stayed until the very end. Like I was in line when the fireworks were finished and still got served very end. Before even eating their food I was very impressed that they seemed to be prepared to serve a large crowd when none of the other trucks there were. Now, on to the food. It was WONDERFUL. I have never had a traditional gyro before, but that is all they had left so I didn't have a ton of choice. Literally this was one of the best sandwich-type things I have ever had, and sandwiches are my favorite food. The serving size was large, the pita was fresh and chewy, the meat was delicious, and all the toppings were perfectly portioned. I hope the Go! Gyro! Go! truck is near me again soon!!!

For $10, you are treated to a culinary delight. This is not standard cart food. The falafel is magic. Look over other reviews. He has rules. Don't stand too close. Don't cut. No subs. Just nod and smile when he speaks to you and enjoy

So this was by no means the best indian food I have ever had, probably was not even in the to 50% BUT they have a cheap all you can eat dinner buffet (even cheaper if your a student), and it has samosas! I showed up right at the end of the dinner rush, so most of the food had just turned over, and was fresh, and the service was fine. I would skip the sambar though, it was just not good, but everything else I tried was.

I'm not a pho snob, nor a Vietnamese snob, but I've eaten plenty of Vietnamese in Vietnam and all around the world. So, how well do I know Vietnamese food? Let's just say it's like my second language! They ran out of basil or didn't receive it and they thought I was crazy when I cancelled my order. Sorry, I've eaten plenty of Pho in Vietnam and without basil, it's just soup! So I tried the vermicelli bowl with BBQ and egg rolls. Yikes! It was one of the worst I've ever had! There are lots of Chinese in the Cho lon part of Sai gon, and they cook both Chinese and Vietnamese. I wish this was the case, it's more of Chinese in America trying to do Vietnamese food which just doesn't make my grade! Will I be back? NO!
Waaaay better than Jose Garce's overpriced taco truck. Next time I will ask for siracha on my taco. I hear that's the best way to eat the short rib taco.

My girls and I finally made it in to experience our first pho. The location is very convenient and there is a decent amount of searing inside. The menu pricing was very reasonable and they had quite a busy to go service. The menu had a really good selection and a large vegetarian section. The girls tried the chicken and noodle pho and the rare beef pho. It was loaded with noodles and ginger flavor. I ordered the crispy noodle stir fry with chicken, squid and shrimp. It was loaded with vegetables and the spicy pepper sauce was amazing. We were all fans of the egg rolls. It's worth a trip to beautiful Avon!

Pretty much the worst Chinese food I have ever had, and that's really saying something. I must admit I hate leaving a simple bare-bones bad review, but other then lacking in sanitation (if the bathroom is an indication of the kitchen it's real bad) and bad food there is nothing else really to say. Rude, bland, under/over cooked,**consistently bad and with apparently **no desire to improve one must avoid at all costs. If you look at the other reviews there is one '4-star' by "M.A.Y." that appears to my decently trained eye to be fake. It praises (advertises) two local Chinese places and then gives some weird (plagiarized?) reviews in all different grammar from random local places with weird syntax, worth looking at for a laugh. Anyway this place is pretty uncool. Pass on it. **=these thoughts are based on my "co-Yelpers" reviews as well.
Food is pretty decent and good price.. the service however SUCKED.

Yay! Great Pad Thai!!!!!!! Stopped here after a day at Opry Mills, so glad we did! I think the owner was our server, she was super, food was faaaaast & perfectly spicy but not too hot & they serve wine (much needed after a hard day bargain hunting!) Can't wait to go back!

Definitely one of the best food trucks on Penn's campus. The breakfast sandwiches are an absolute staple and a must after a night out. The bread is crispy and toasted before being layered with eggs, bacon and cheese. The cheese steaks are also some of the best and the city and one of the best deals around at under $5.

Elegant dining at its best. Atmosphere is upscale, service is excellent, and the food is wonderful. This is a place you go for a dining experience. The octopus and braised pork belly is worth the trip!

This place was rly good. Def one of the better places in Wilmington The menu was HUGE. After some indecision I had the andhra chicken and garlic naan for takeout. Yummy all the way down to the little pieces of garlic on my naan. And it's right next door to a Rita's! Mango lassi looked really good so I want to try that next time.

I went with my family to this restaurant on Mother's Day. We were unsure about the quality of the food, and our suspicions turned out to be accurate. Both the chicken tikka and goat curry's meat seemed to be made out of rubber. Also, the dosas served at the buffet lacked the homey steam it usually has. Topping it off, there were limited, mediocre selections in the entire buffet itself. We left the restaurant completely unsatisfied. Personally, I would not recommend this place to other hungry eaters, as there are several other nearby areas where you can enjoy Indian cuisine for its full quality.

Hubby and I dined here with a Groupon and were very pleased with our meal. Rainbow roll was very good and robust. I enjoyed the mushroom fried rice with chicken and hubby liked his masaman curry with chicken. We will definately be back soon!

My monthly girl's BYO get-together was held here on Wednesday night. This place is small, yet spacious enough to handle several large groups at a time. In fact, we were seated next to a table of 12 or so elderly gentlemen who were clearly having a fabulous time of it. Our table of eight started out with a selection of appetizers. We ordered the mussels, stuffed mushrooms, fig and sausage and the grilled romaine salad. I samples the mushrooms and plowed through the fig and sausage appetizer - I almost licked the plate. Portions were large, so once I filled up on the appetizers, I had barely enough room to take a stab at my linguini with clams in a white sauce, but I made a valiant attempt. The dish was good, not the best I've had, but definitely more than serviceable. I also snuck a bite of my friend's baked gnocchi, which was a lovely in its cheesy gooeyness. I think I was the only one not to make a considerable dent in my entree. We ordered desserts for the table - two orders of the chocolate peanut butter cake and one of the oreo cheesecake - and all were demolished in short order. This place is easy to get to, right on Broad street so accessible from Center City via the subway. My friend and I drove down and we got a kick (as always) out of the oh-so-unique parking rules, or lack thereof, in South Philly. We decided to to join 'em and parked in the middle of Broad Street, but were confused by the cars double-parked on Porter. How does one get one's car out? Really?!? The bill for the 8 of us divided out to around $40 a person. Not too bad for appetizer, entree and dessert with enough of my entree left-over to cover at least two more meals! All in all, Scannicchio's is a great South Philly Italian BYO that I wouldn't mind checking out again.

I don't usually write reviews but Kalamatas really earned it. There are plunty of food options for mediteranian or gyro style food. Kalamatas is really over priced, the portion sizes are small, and they nickle and dime you for every little thing. Don't be surprised to come in next time and be charged for napkins! The food is just okay, I have been to both locations and the owners are complete jerks, my food came out burnt and they told me they didn't see anything wrong with it. Furthermore, from a customer service or satisfaction stand point at either their greenhills or brentwood location they don't care if you are happy with your food or experience, the response that I received was "you have choices go somewhere else, we have plunty of customers". They clearly do not care about customers, so SAVE YOURSELF TIME AND MONEY and go to any other gyro place. I recommend mediteranian cuisine in brentwood or Tazikies in greenhills, they take care of you and make sure you have a great dining experience.

Finally made it to K&T Deli! The menu is full of savory noodle soups, meat-filled Banh-Mi sandwiches, and desert drinks like bubble tea, sweet Vietnamese coffee, and even bean-based Asian deserts. Almost everything on the menu has a photo, which is helpful if you want to try something new. I ordered the regular Beef Noodles, iced coffee, and pork belly banh-mi as takeout, which was enough for 2 people and cost just $16. If you're looking for just a snack, you can grab a sandwich for about $4.25. I think $3 for the coffee is a bit steep, but the low food prices make up for that. The restaurant packed the soup broth separate from the noodles, beef, and condiments (jalapeño pepper, lime, green onions, bean sprouts, etc) so that the soup would still be good when I got home. I appreciate that dedication to freshness! The restaurant also has tables to dine-in, so it would be fun to get a group of people together, order a bunch of items off the menu, and share!

Best indian food in the northeast! Very friendly service. Everything on the menu is delicious from beginning to end. Please support this place so they can continue to make delicious food for everyone :)

Loved this place! Nice atmosphere inside, no frills but that's ok cause the food is awesome. Had the thai iced tea, it was right on. Ordered the papaya salad and duck spring rolls for apps. So good, I could have made a meal out of those two dishes alone. For dinner I got the Holy Basil something or other and it was pretty awesome. I will definitely be heading back to Erawan again.

I should start by disclosing the fact that I am a novice to Thai cuisine. With that said, this place was amazing, even when compared to my handful of other Thai meals that I had previously considered "good", the food and dinning experience was exceptional at Jasmine Thai. A colleague and I came here after locating it on Yelp and taking a gamble. It is very nondescript and subdued from the outside, located in a strip mall with very little signage, and absolutely zero curb appeal. However, inside the restaurant was very nice, and had a lot of decorations that were actually pretty cool, especially in the tables. Our server was exceptional. She was very patient and accommodating to our naïveté of what everything was, and what to order. She had a very nice personality and made you feel very welcome. We ordered the "two friend panang" and the "green curry with beef" and decided to split them. When all was said and done, neither of us could decide which we enjoyed more, as they were both delicious in their own rights. Each dish featured a plethora of well-balanced flavors, as well as ingredients that tasted very fresh. The Panang was the spicier of the two, but not overpowering, and very well balanced. The green curry was slightly creamier and sweeter, and the flavors definitely held true to the descriptions I had read of green curry. If you do go, do not skip dessert. The Jasmine Banana dish was incredible! Homemade coconut ice cream that was delectable with bananas hand cut and perfectly wrapped like a present of flavor in a light dough and flash fried, all drizzled with honey. Everything had just the right amount of flavor to compliment the other ingredients. The juxtaposition of warm to cold, and the sweetness of the bananas and honey to the coconut were perfect. It was also a great way to offer your palette some closure after the bombardment of flavors in the curry. I full heartedly give this restaurant 5 stars, as the food and experience were exceptional!

I can't write a review that tells you how much I love this place. The service is amazing, the food is some of the best at a good price, and the restaurant is always so clean. I love this place and I've gotten many family members to become addicted as well. Definitely the best Vietnamese food in Reno.

Was happy to see this still open. Ordered Doner Box which was on their sidewalk price board as $9. Got it with a Coke and comes to $14? Told ye cashier and she insisted several times she was right as she rambled on about her boyfriend not bringing her Starbucks. Food was still good but they need to hire better.

Newer Indian restaurant in the area, and the service was quite good. I ordered Malai Kebabs for takeaway and was quite pleased.
