Even though it was closing time, they took an extra minute to prep up some chutneys to accompany my order. Their online order system was efficient and easy. I will certainly return for dine-in.

Went here earlier for family dinner I bought $25 voucher from restaurant.com for $50 purchase We ordered *Shrimp tom yam soup just okay *thai fried rice which is not bad-you can go to Penang or sky Cafe and get 2 order and tasty and more flavorful rice *Pineapple Duck curry not bad..but you can count the tiny pieces of the duck---for the same price you can get 1/2 duck at sang ke *Crab meat Pad thai was disaster! sorry i have to say this but it was super sweet like the cook gave box of syrup or candy out of it I can't even eat it...i love thai food...i'm asian even when i'm in asia or here in US i know which is authentic good thai or not I just waste $15 order for nothing I like to eat in NY and Chicago most of thai restaurant is very decent flavor But for Erawan i have to give you 1 star...clearly the cook/the chefs just learned how to cook! And the food came out too long we have to wait 1 hours...arrrghhhh Spend $35 and not satisfied at all Don't worry we still tip 25% because the server got nothing todo with the food! Little tips : Quality authenticity

It's good. Clean place. Prompt service. I had the fried rice with chicken ...the food isn't amazing but the portion sizes are great and the price is right.. Trying the fried banana now . Yeah, it's pretty good.

First time here - really great food and experience! We got some appetizers and two small bowls of noodle soup. The small bowls are plenty of food for one person. After a summer roll appetizer, I couldn't even finish the small bowl. The serving sizes are really great for the prices. I'll definitely be coming here again with friends and family.
Thrilled! Gluten free Indian food!! YES!!! The food is awesome, I can eat without worries, its affordable AND they deliver. This place is one of the greatest places on town!

I came at opening time and was generally impressed by the atmosphere. I ordered the spring rolls and the number 1 pho on the menu. The spring rolls were great and the broth of the pho was light and refreshing. The noodles were tender and chewy, great consistency and the there was plenty of meat to go along with it. The waitress and kind and she often refilled my water without asking. I thoroughly enjoyed my meal and will be coming back here again.

I finally got around to trying Thai House and I was really impressed. My only complaint is the lack of parking. The beef and broccoli was really good, but small portions. I had the beef noodle soup and was in heaven! It was so good. I will be coming back again. Thank you!

Very good Pho, I love coming here it's close to the mall and come here for lunch there prices are very reasonable and good portions. They employees don't speak much English but I'm not worried about that I am just happy for the food that they serve.

This place is pretty decent as far as Thai food in Philadelphia goes. Prices are average and the food is pretty tasty. The restaurant is actually quite large inside, and the decor is unique: kind of like modern reductionist Thai, with their tables nestled among white geometric indoor archways. The beef in yellow curry really brought me back to Thailand, the only thing it was missing was the melt-your-face-off burn. Otherwise, it was right on target. The Thai fried rice with crabmeat was good, but not totally authentic. They should lay off the frozen peas and carrots and add in more tomatoes, a lime wedge and maybe some bean sprouts or something if they're itching to add more veggies. Also, the flavor was a bit lacking, but overall it was fine and they were pretty generous with the crab. The fried tofu appetizer was tasty, though the sauce it was served with could have been a little better. This place probably deserves 3.5 stars, but I'm rounding up to 4 for the trip back to Thailand from the curry.

Anyone who's spent time in major cities with their fast-and-cheap curry restaurants and come back to St. Louis feeling a little sad that our only options for Indian food are white-tablecloth "fine dining" style Indian restaurants. Spice-n-Grill changes the game with affordable, take-away style curry. What's confusing is the multiple items on the menu that's obviously taking a stab at the "local palate" - Philly cheese steaks, chicken wings, fries, etc. Not necessary. Just focus on good Indo-Pak food, please! The Indian-Pakistani food here is really, really good; it's ran by the same people that ran Indian Food down at 170 and Olive a few years ago. The food is really good quality and doesn't take long to come out. On a recent visit, Chicken Tikka Masala was great (if not just slightly salty, needing just a touch more cream to balance it out). Chicken Biryani - advertised as the Student Biryani brand, a popular fast food franchise in Pakistan - was spicy with fantastic chunks of chicken on the bone. I'm sure their other dishes, brought over from the previous restaurant, such as Beef Nihari, are as good as they were when RFT reviewed them (an enlargement of that review hangs in Spice-n-Grill). I'm deducting one whole star - if not a star and a half - for the naan. One of the best parts of any Indian restaurant is the naan - the fresh-baked bread slathered in ghee. Spice-n-Grill's naan was the pre-made, frozen variety that reminds me of a pita. It was warmed in the oven, not freshly baked. One of the most outstanding disappointments of all time, not having edible naan for that amazing chicken tikka masala. They're also open until 9 PM almost every night - but despite advertising opening hours on Mondays, a recent attempt to visit on a Monday was met with the restaurant being closed. Try this place - you'll be surprised. Two of us feasted on curry and biryani and had leftovers today for lunch for $30. Not bad at all.
The service is great, had a hard time finding a time to make my reservation because they are always packed, food was great, elegant and detailed oriented

It has a nice dining area and the lady in the front, who took our order, was very kind. But the food lacked flavor. The jerk chicken was just ok, nothing special. Needed more of a kick to it. I asked for gravy and was given very little. The rice and peas were bland. And the mac and cheese was the worst. I can't compare it to anything. It looked and tasted like plain cook noddles with a little cheese melted on top. I wanted to try cabbage instead of mac and cheese but I knew we weren't eating for a couple of hours and I hate soggy cabbage. They have 3 sizes and what we expected for the price. Also, we were 2nd in line but it took 20 minutes. She kept going to the back to get food. Which seemed odd because there was a steam table in the front close to the register. We paid cash but FYI there is a $15 minimum for a card. We don't plan on going back.
We get here a few times a year; it's been my wife's favorite place for ages. We've never had a bad experience, although the other reviews here sound completely accurate.

We have been to India Sizzling in Fishers several times and enjoyed it so we decided to try India Sizzling II while in the area. Wow! Definitely the best Indian buffet in Indy. Great selection and everything was fresh and tasty. Drinks included as well as custom-made dosas for the table. I had my three children with me and our waiter was very nice to them. We will definitely be back!
The Cuisine awesome I just didn't like the seating I moved myself the waiter moved me again but ok whatever I settled in and started enjoying my food with my husband.

This is my absolute favorite Indian restaurant! With all this rainy weather, I find myself craving Amber Indian more than anything. I enjoyed their lunch buffet yesterday and was happily surprised to see 2 new vegetarian dishes added to the already wide selection of choices. This is what I love about this place :) not only is their staff friendly and provide great service - but they're always changing up the buffet menu so customers can try new dishes. The lunch buffet is a great price for all that's included, and of course I highly recommend ordering the garlic naan bread!

Tried Spiro's for the first time. Had the Saganaki. It was good but different then and I have had before. For dinner I had one of the specials, $19.99. Recommend was the chicken parm. Included salad, desert, and drink. The food was great. I could not finish it all. The baklava was wonderful, not too sweet. I will definitely come back in my return trips to the Creve Coeur area. The service was top notch.

We made a special trip to Baguette after reading a few reviews in Boise Weekly. We won't be making a special trip to go back. The bread they use is wonderful. I would go there just to buy bread... (do they sell it?) It's a sub shop with a twist. I ordered the rotisserie chicken and my husband ordered the beef. I inquired if the chicken was breast meat (I don't like dark meat) They chatted and told me yes it was all white meat. I get the sandwich and honestly thought it was wrong. A foot long sandwich with Fresh cucumber,cilantro, too much jalepeno and where is the chicken? The mystery dry, brown, beyond shredded, minute amount of ???? Stopped me from my first bite. She saw the shock on my face and told me to try it and if I did not like it she would get me something else. I was nice and ate half and ended up throwing other half away. :( My other choices would have been turkey/pesto or the cajun shrimp. My husband thought his beef sandwich was ok. We both agreed that there was too much bread and light on ingredients on the inside. We also tried shrimp spring rolls. I was uneasy ordering because they were premade , wrapped and no refrigeration.... Just sitting on front counter. There was also mystery meat in shrimp spring roll. Ordered beignets, they were cold amd premade. Would be better if made per order and hot. We might try again but is no longer on list of must try or lets go across town because it's so darn good.

My favorite hookah bar in Nashville!! Service is fantastic! They are very attentive and nice. Hookah smoked smooth and tasted amazing. We got flower power with mint! Also we got a fruit top/bowl as well. I will definitely be back when I'm in town! Edit: as of yesterday, I brought it down from 5 to 3 stars. I have always suggested this place to my friends, and I took my friends there yesterday for the first time, only to leave very disappointed by the rudeness of an employee at this hookah bar. Really sucks because I do like this place, but if you anger my friends, then who will I go with now to your establishment?

The chicken curry here is absolutely great. It's a convenient location in Green Hills, just near Whole Foods and the prices are reasonable. It's a nice neighborhood restaurant for us that is always reliably good. The service is great. I've been here about 6 times in the last year. Definitely recommended.

Absolutely fantastic curry. After moving to Brandon I had tried serval different places and all seemed to miss the mark one way or another. Tonight we happened on Ploy Thai and man was I impressed. The food was good, portions large and the service prompt.

This place was good! I thought that the taste was on par with what I was expecting, a little more mild than I like. Prices were cheap, but I thought that portion sizes were a little small... kind of reminded me of the small space of the restaurant. However, that being said, I didn't feel ripped off. Prices were adjusted for the smaller portion sizes. A friend and I split the Panang Curry with just veggies (unless tofu is fried I don't want it) and the drunken noodles (Pad Khimao) with chicken. I was happy to split two dishes so I could try two of my favorite staples at any run-of-the-mill Thai place, but I was just coming off of post workout and the hunger was real (talking borderline hangry) and I just wanted more food than what was in front of me. Thank god it was a BYOB and we had ample wine to deal with that issue. I think they way they served the curry at this place was super strange though! It was served on a flat plate. Makes it a little difficult to eat curry. I had a spoon and I couldn't ladle any of the delicious-ness on to my plate, which made me sad. The only other thing that was weird was that our food was brought out at different times. We had all ordered dinner portions and for whatever reason, they brought out one person's much earlier than the other dishes. The service was very friendly though and pretty attentive to filling our water glasses and clearing dishes from the table. Like I said the food was good, but this is too far away to become my new staple Thai restaurant so I'll stick to the other one's close by!

I love that there is a grocery side and a restaurant/take out side to the store. Grocery side : delicious hummus, babaghanuj, tatziki, falafel, pita bread, olives, and baklava. Can't say I ever picked up something and didnt like it. All was obviously high quality and better than any junk you would pick up at your grocery store. Restaurant side: the bitizza is delicious! I usually get the greek which is feta, olives, tomatoes and onions on zaatar bread. Different but delicious. Kabobs and gyros were flavorful and delicious.

Still have the taste of Banh Mi in my mouth as I write this short review. For 4.99 I got the Banh Mi and a can of soda. Banh Mi wasn't that spicy though, would have like it spicier, and filled with more cilantro. But it was delicious none the less and a great alternative to what I usually eat for lunch. Plus they replaced mayo with butter. I hate mayo.

Very generic, chain Asian food. I had lunch with a group and the consequences was it was nothing special and rather flavorless as far as the food goes. I could imagine them dumping pre-made soup by the gallons into a pot to heat it up. There are sauces on the table which we used to add some flavor but they are generic as well, full of preservatives. If you want good Asian head around the corner to Royal Thai on 19th. Much better food.

Came here on a beautiful Sunday night. Sat at a window seat and had a great view of the river. The whole wheat garlic bread is really good, save some for your sauce if you have the will power. We had the eggplant parmigiana, simply the best-just like Florentino's (Newtown)-anywhere and a delicious seafood fra diavlo. Limoncello sorbet was a nice way to end the meal. Service was excellent all around.

Nooddi is our "go-to" spot for dinner. We end up here at least twice each week. Being vegan, there aren't many great spots for us to visit locally, but Nooddi always provides fantastic options. Our favorites include Drunken Noodle (tofu, no egg), Massaman Curry, Pineapple Fried Rice and Tofu Eggplant. The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. Both service and food are always consistent. If you are in Delco, put Nooddi on your list to try if you haven't done so already!

Five stars isn't enough! I've been coming here for at least 15 years and it's never been less than amazing. Always worth the wait and I love the fact that there's no menu and you never no exactly what you're going to get besides the fantastic grilled chicken and falafel. He's an artist and a true original.

Ordered takeout/delivery. Reasonably priced, appropriate for the quantity. The delivery menu is very limited compared to the regular menu. Threre is a 5.99 delivery charge and a $15 minimum, and you still have to tip the driver. Potato samosas: good. Chicken Curry: ok - very oily which is surprising as this is supposed to be "healthy". Chicken Biryani: good. Garlic Nan - ok, nothing great. Tandoori chicken - ok, a little dry. Lamb curry: good quality lamb chucks but very few pieces. Overall, not bad but nothing great.
Mofongo was ok, service has a lot to be desired. Waitress took our order after waiting for 25 minutes. Didn't see her till we ordered the check. Not cool, you need to work on it.
Too American style and soup is just chicken base and little missing Vietnam species. It was just ok but little pricey.

Do NOT order Pad Thai, it was the worst I've had ever, by far. So overly sweet, I'm feeling sick now. The noodles needed to be bitten with force. I like al dente, but this was ridiculous. I thought I would like this place because the thai fish cakes were good. The salad was standard. Again, stay away from the pad thai. There are too many restaurants to give this place another chance.

This Indian restaurant was okay. I'm a little surprised by the high ratings but the food was the best part of my visit. The restaurant overall has a nice ambiance, plenty of seating and the staff was pretty attentive. Although difficult to understand at times, they did seem genuinely helpful. My biggest thing about eating here was the bathroom seemed quite dirty and not too nice, no toilet paper, toilet didn't flush and the second time I needed to use the bathroom before we left, a little kid stopped me to tell me the restroom wasn't working. Other than that, I would definitely give the food a try! Not the best I've had but worth trying again.

Hands down best Pad Thai I've ever had in my life. We ordered take out but decided to dine in (we were starving) and they let us take a table and without even asking the waitress came over and gave us water and checked on us periodically (which she didn't have to do since we did take out). 10/10 I would recommend this place to anyone and everyone!!

I heard so much about this place, I had to try it out. I had the chicken satay taco and the veggie burger. The chicken satay tacos are delicious, I would highly recommend. I decided to have my veggie burger spicy, that was not a good idea. It was too spicy for me. so they next time I try it, I will avoid the heat. Service is pretty good for a lunch truck and the wait was about 10 mins. The prices are very good and affordable.

My previous review was a 3-star rating. For some reason, the owner (maybe manager, dishwasher or who know what - certainly not chief proofreader) decided to attack me through the compliment system so I'm dropping them to 1-star. Check out the screen capture of consecutive pearls sent to me for proof. Now if I could just remember how to report a fake profile...

It's a shame that I have to give this place two stars. I order from here quite often and I'm usually pretty satisfied. They have a variety of foods to chose from which is why I'd often order lunch... Let's talk about today....I received HORRIBLE SERVICE! Absolutely HORRIBLE! Long story short, the delivery guy was having a bad day, spilled the smoothies in the bag with my baked fish, smoothies were dripping from the bag, I noticed it right away and the delivery guy immediately became upset when I pointed it out. He told me he was on a bike and said the owner isn't very smart and he's constantly requesting "stuff" from the owner to make the customers happy and continued on with the rant about the owner. I asked him to calm down. I stepped outside and called the owner who apologized. I went back into the building. The delivery guy had spilled smoothie all over the lobby floor. I asked him to keep it down and he became very loud and AGGRESSIVE! I'm so thankful for the security desk at my job as the security guards immediately sprung into action when this awful guy stepped closer towards me. I work in center city in a very busy office building. Needless to say, not only had I become afraid but I was also very embarrassed in front of my colleagues. Security advised me that it was standard procedure to take my name and they also needed the name of the restaurant. I returned to my desk...visibly shaken from the whole incident. The restaurant owner called my cell, I assumed he was calling to apologize... No, he was actually calling to complain to me about giving his number to my security desk because he told me he would handle the situation and he said the security lady wasn't very nice. He wasn't mean on the phone but I could tell he was irritated and he actually told me that this situation hurts him (from a business perspective I guess) more than it hurts me. I just couldn't believe it. Meanwhile I'm still shaking over the fact that I was just yelled at by HIS delivery guy. This isn't the first time I had to call the restaurant about an order "mix up". The owner has been very nice in the past and very quick to make corrections. This however, takes the cake. The owner did not show any empathy towards me whatsoever and I actually felt threatened by HIS delivery guy. I still can't believe the whole incident even happened. I don't think the owner realizes how bad the incident really was..His delivery guy actually became very irate in my place of business and the bottom line is I became concerned about my safety. The guy seemed like he would even get physical. Food is not worth that kind of inconvenience!
Stopped by after Christmas shopping, grabbed crab fried rice and chicken drunken noodles. The wife and I love id, so glad the deliver ;). Will have to order lunch sooner than later! Thank you

I love Ruchi! Most Indian restaurants have a lunch buffet - Ruchi is the only one I know of in St Louis that has a dinner buffet as well. And it's huge - easily two or three times the size of the buffet at House of India in University City (which is also recommended). Ruchi is casual. Friendly service. Lots of Indian people seem to be eating there so they must be doing something right! Note - dinner buffet is Fri and Sat only.

The atmosphere is classy and clean. The food is fresh and flavorful - cooked traditionally and full of incredible richness. The staff could be slightly more friendly and the layout for greeting and payment is a little backwards, but all in all the place is a must go. A little more pricey than its competitor Biryani Bowl and not as tasty, but definately delicious.

The place is never very busy but the food is excellent. My wife is not as open to different food as I am, but she loves this place. It's one of the few places outside normal american cuisine she will go to. Wonton soup is always great and the cha gio is awesome, best in town that I have had.

This place is legit! Every time I've gone, I've received great service. The owner and staff are incredibly friendly. The food is fantastic (you have to get the namsod salad)! Highly recommend if you're into delicious, hole-in-the-wall venues.

This place is great. I have been there twice and I plan on going back soon. Both times I have been there we had Lamb Samosa which was delicious. The first time I went my main course was the Mixed Grill and I really enjoyed it. My girlfriend had the Chicken Tikka Masala and she says it might be one of the best dishes she has ever had. Second time going there I had the Chicken Tikka Masala and I loved it. The Naan was amazing and perfect for dipping into the sauce. This time we both tried the Rasavat Lemonade and let me tell you, its the bomb, its a fizzy type of lemonade and they serve it in a tall glass with a little umbrella. The service was great, they really make sure you have everything you need and they really do their best to give you a great experience. The place has been nearly empty both times I have been there but I am sure it is because of the location, the neighborhood is safe and pretty nice but it is not really a booming place for restaurants. If you are looking for Indian food go check this place out, I know you wont be disappointed.
Best food on campus. Loaded fries are the best. 8 bucks for fries sounds expensive, but they put so much chicken and gyro in there it is well worth it.

Nice food....If you are looking for authentic Indian food then Zaikka is not a place. But I am an Indian and I like their concept. The Rice with Tofu, curries and all the toppings taste awesome. I am Veg. so I am not sure about Non-Veg entrees. But once I went with my colleagues who are not fan of Indian food but still they liked non-veg entrees. I would surely recommend if you want to try something new.

I think it's decent Thai food....However, their food has declined in taste and presentation over the last year. If you need a Thai fix this is not a bad choice for the area. My last two visits for dinner was at best disappointing.

Was this the worst pad Thai I've ever had? Yes. Soupy and with zero fresh ingredients. Visiting from out of town and this was near the hotel. It was busy and service was slow. And to top it off - there was a large, live roach in the bathroom. Maybe we caught it on a bad day.
A fantastic buffet for lunch. All the food was hot and delicious. Well worth coming in to check out. Will come again.

I frequent Brown Sugar too many times to count. I usually get Cassave Pone, Currants Roll, Roti, Doubles, or Patties. The roti is great and I've had the freshest Roti on a Saturday morning. The doubles bara is a hit or miss sometimes but generally very good. The actual restaurant is a bit small with the bakery counter and juice bar taking up much of the space. There are two booths that you can sit at if you want to eat your food there. Then there are two windows. You order from the window on the right and pay at the window on left. The roti prices are really good considering the amount of work that goes into preparing a roti. I highly recommend this place for take out roti or a quick snack on some doubles or patties. Oh and they have a Mauby and Sorrel fountain. Call ahead to order on busy days!

So the Chicken Pho. Perfect. Sweet, Spicy, Salty...Ohh let me count the ways I love you. This place is totally amazing! The staff is very friendly service is quick for carry out as well. Love the cabbage salad with pork as well. We eat here at least 3 times per month and it's always on point.
Awesome food. Went for lunch buffet the other day and food was really tasty. Good luck guys !!

Stopped here after church today. Had only eaten Indian food a couple times until now, so I really wasn't sure what to expect. So glad we did! The food was fresh, tasty and I was very happy with my menu selection. Our server helped me decide-chana masala, spicy, served with pan. (chickpeas and spinach with sauce over rice) I found the service to be very good, everything was clean, the atmosphere was comfortable and the food was delicious. I'm not an expert on Indian Food, but I would bet this is the most authentic Indian restaurant you will find in the Nashville area. Welcome to Mount Juliet! We'll be back!!!!!

I've come here for lunch and dinner many times. I love food! But, with having many food allergies there's not many restaurants I love going to. Since I'm allergic to wheat, gluten, dairy and the night shade family ... I order their Duck dish and their Pad Thai which are both excellent! They've also got great lunch deals with great homemade soups.

Delicious, fresh food, lovely ambience, and smiling great service. The best Indian food we've had in the US and absolutely the best dining in Zephyrhills. Surprised the place wasn't packed and a line out the door. Treat yourself to a wonderful meal at Mayoor!
The atmosphere is great. Fun for a date night. I had the vegetable pad Thai and it had just the right amount of spice to it. Price was spot on.

We weren't sure what to expect but were intrigued by the menu. We even popped in to have a look a few days before coming in. It's beautiful inside with interesting and elaborate decorating. The staff were all friendly and attentive. We even were given some special treatment by the manager in regards to where we sat. After seeing the size of plates going by we knew we wouldn't be able to eat an appetizer although I was curious about some of the menu items. I guess we will have to visit again. You are served lavash which is a thin flatbread. They literally make it right in the restaurant and bring it warm to the table with fresh cilantro, basil and onion. The waitress explained how to eat it by folding the herbs and onion inside with some butter. I went to the area they made the bread and the woman explained how they make it. Since I'm a food blogger I'm always curious about new foods. We shared a Greek salad which was very fresh. The tomato wasn't the ripest but they aren't in season right now so they won't be great anywhere. The dressing was different than the typical Greek oil and vinegar type, but was instead a creamy yogurt based. Very good actually. We had the Koobideh and Gyro plates. Both were delicious and served with rice. We both thought everything was cooked perfectly and seasoned appropriately. The portions were HUGE. We took home more than half our dinners. The waitress even brought us fresh bread to take home with us. The wine list was decent too. I just can't think of anything negative about our experience here! Well done.
Food was delicious! Staff was very friendly, and the chef came out to see how we liked our meal. Will definitely be back again!

Very nice, helpful staff. The fountain sodas were good. I had white and dark meat tenders with honey mustard -- very good. The mac and cheese was absolutely delicious. I tried the peanut butter pie and the s'mores donut, and those were just okay. It ran about $30 for two people, with dessert. This place has a very cool vibe and very cute decor. If I didn't dine in, I might have just given 4 stars.

Best Indian Food in Indy! Try it? Unbelievable They even have the tasty birdseed candy and every possible Indian dish. The place is full of families from India here for dinner. It is awesome! ALSO they provide butter/garlic flatbread that is heavenly.

Great food! Jerk sauce was off-the-hook, but beware, sauce is created by different people and sometimes can be spicier than others. BYOB so no complaints there but they ran out of ginger beer last time I was there.

What a wonderful find ! I stopped in for lunch the other day, which is a steal of a buffet at $7.99. The selection was tasty, hot and fresh. The 'server' was a nice as could be, and just overall a terrific deal. Definitely worth a return trip, again and again.
Best Food in NOLA. Alway my husband and I are going there. Cheap food but very yummy

Whoa, why did this place get so few stars?? The food here is delicious. I recently had a vegetable stew here and it was out of this world. My friends shared a veggie stir-fry, which they raved about. They said they'd never had such delicious peppers! They did, however, have a big problem with paying $15 for vegetables and rice. My one friend also got the chicken wings and she devoured them. Sure, the meat patties don't have that much meat in them, but if you are after quality, not quantity, you will love this place. The fruit juices are also really good. Indoor seating is minimal, but there is a big yard with lots of outdoor seating, and, sometimes, live music! I recommend Jamaican Jerk Hut!
Literally THE best lunch in Carmel! It is always fresh and delicious. Staff is extremely attentive. It is the perfect place to test the Indian cuisine waters.
The smell alone will make you salivate. It's an experience that everyone needs to have in there life. Can't recommend enough

Terrible service by who seemed to be the owner... He was dismissive and barely interacted with me, seemed annoyed to be hosting me... I ordered the chicken rice vermicelli soup, it was okay at best... The broth was sort of bland and there were no herbs or anything fresh to make the soup pop... I will not be back and I would not recommend

Tried this place last night for dinner as a 2nd option. Our intended destination, Flatwater, had a 30 minute wait still at 8pm for the patio, so we looked across the street and decided to give this place a try. They have an outdoor patio with maybe 8-10 tables, which is nice. There was absolutely NO ONE inside, which was off-putting, but we went for it anyway. It was delicious. We (2 of us) split the Pad Thai with Tofu, medium spicy, which was a good idea because the portion size is absolutely massive. We took the leftovers home and I actually brought HALF of those leftovers to work for lunch today. So, basically, they give you four servings of Pad Thai. Great value and the spice level was right on. We also split the Thai Dumpling appetizer, which I believe was six large dumplings. Again, we had leftovers. The interior decor is typical for a Thai restaurant. Nothing spectacular. Strange ambiance because, as I said, there was no one inside. Including us, there were four tables occupied out on the patio. Maybe it was just an off night because the weather was so amazing? Who knows, but I hope it stays busy because I'd hate to see it go. Nothing really seems to survive in that location though, for some reason. If you enjoy Thai food, give it a try! You won't be disappointed with the food.

I used to love this place but we just had bland food and terrible service. Our waitress never checked on us, even though were out of water and wanted to order more food. Right now I'm trying to flag her down for the check. Too bad, on to the next!

My absolute FAVORITE place for lunch by Jefferson. Food is fantastic, service is fast and friendly. Has great gluten free and vegan options. I probably eat here about 1-2 times per week. And you truly can't beat the prices anywhere around here. 10 stars for Mumbai Bistro.

Holy cow is all I can say. I've been to the falafel guy a few times now and it has always been out of this world! His food is insanely delicious and you can smell it a few blocks away! He maybe a little like the soup nazi but he's a one man show making magic inside that little silver cart! I don't know how he does it but I highly recommend checking him out at least once in your life. It's absolutely worth the wait and you get so much food for $10!!! You won't be disappointed!
Disgustingly rude. They got my take out order wrong, then accused me of being at the wrong restaurant.
It's ok for the price. I like that I can manage my calories but the taste is pretty bland.

Tiny hole-in-the-wall venue, but the food was terrific. A really great find in Nashville. The curry chicken and jerk chicken were well spiced and flavorful, the sautéed cabbage, rice with spinach and fried plantains worked well to balance the spice. Try the special lemonaide and flower infused soft drink too. A welcome change of cuisine from the usual suspects.

Family owned and food made with a soul...oh how I adore you original you...in the middle of the green hills food desert...Fernando tony Lorena eric ... today's team that made the magic happen .... just thank you for every single delicious bite...

This place use to be my favourite for donair on whyte ave but I had the worse experience last night. Did ask what I wanted in my donair. Waited forever to make fries which is fine, but when they were ready the guy scooped up fries for two boxes before me and I ended up with some cold fries that were already siting there when I had been waiting there the longest. The kids running this place now are gonna run it out of business, I will be taking my business to the other 5 donair places down the street

One of my favorite neighborhood places. You absolutely must try the couscous when it's on special! Other standouts are the lamb ketban -- always tender and juicy -- and any of the tagines. Side-dish-wise I especially recommend the string beans. Brahim never fails to greet you with a friendly smile and greeting, making you feel like you've just walked into the kitchen of a friend. And if you're really lucky, you might just get offered a cup of warm mint tea... I love this place. You will too. Go!

My wife and I had a vegetable seekh kabob, chicken Malabar, naan bread basket, lamb tikka masala, and chana masala. The seekh kabob was tasty and appeared to be freshly prepared. The chicken Malabar was dry, but the breading had good flavor. It was served with sweet and spicy sauces that tasted freshly prepared. The lamb tikka masala was flavorful but a bit salty. The chana masala tasted almost out of a can. The naan was not cooked to the right temperature--it seemed like some sort of strange pita. Service was friendly and the small eat-in area was clean. We changed our appetizer order because we were warned that some of the appetizers had a 30-minute prep time. We have eaten at many Indian places and our overall sense was, this is good in a pinch, but the flavor development and ingredient quality really wasn't there. We saw many boxes of dry mail-order ingredients on the floor and we would not be surprised if someone told us that the curry paste was out of powder mix and some of the ingredients, like the chicken in the appetizer mix, was previously frozen. I came away feeling like I could have had a tastier, more cost-effective meal by heating up some Trader Joe's frozen Indian dinners. When reading over the other reviews, think for a minute--this is not in a high-foot-traffic area for restaurants, so the reviews are going to be skewed. It's certainly just fine if you live nearby and need a quick Indian meal. But if you really want good Indian food, head to King of Tandoor in Fairmount or New Delhi Buffet in University City. If you must have Indian food in South Philly, the Palace of Indian near the Passyunk Fountain is a notch better.

The food is passable for Indian take out. Better options are certainly out there as far as quality of food goes in the immediate area. The real problem was the poor customer service. When attempting to use a Groupon for the restaurant I was denied saying they were under new management and stopped taking them. At least I should have been able to use the price I paid for it. No indication that the restaurant changed hands same name, same address. Staff was unhelpful as pointed out in previous reviews, but I don't think you get Indian take out for the smiles.
I normally get my Jamaican food in the Bronx and in other parts of NYC. This food was delicious and the service was good. Not bad for Indy.

I like Juan Reyes hanging fixtures. A nice couple of dangling gold ones over the bar remind me of ~ Holiday decorations. Most of the light fixtures are festive varied-shaped glass ones with squiggly flourescent bulbs. Reyes and Marcos Cruz restaurant specializes in cuisine from the island of Puerto Rico, perhaps our 51st state. Most of the decor is minimalist but the food sublime. I recommend the spicely-sauced Arroz Con Pollo chicken over rice. Also delectable are the Sorullos De Maiz corn fritters. An available side is a yuca dish worth trying.The Tres Leches dessert found in many hispanic restaurants is above average here, a good end. Salsa Puerto Rican restaurant is more upscale with a higher price point than another favorite commensurate carribean restaurant, Back to Cuba in south Nashville.

Delicious, authentic, fresh. Nooddi is our comfortable Thai stand-by. You can even score a great coupon (buy one entree, get one half off) in the Clipper magazine and get out of there for $30 for a couple! That being said, you won't have to compromise on great Thai flavor. I had the Bangkok Garlic Chicken last night. The chicken was not fried and in a savory garlic sauce with broccoli, mini corn, and carrots with a side of white rice. Just a simple, delicious and comforting meal that would've been great as a beef dish as well.

Amazing spin on a gyro. I picked the chicken sandwich with the spicy slaw. My girlfriend had to talk my into going, well because I'm not a huge fan of gyro's. I eat them, because I'm a guy and eat almost anything. YOU MUST TRY THIS SANDWICH SHOP IT'S CRAZY GOOD!

Short and sweet! All the good things said about this chain is spot on. In fact, I think it is the best of show for all fast food places. I would kill for the yucca alone. the black beans and yellow rice are tasty and good for you! The pork was so moist and yummy! Their bowl dishes are more than enough for me...and I used to chow down big time. Obviously, I've been lucky as I have never had bad service at this location.
The shrimp briyani was horrible. Rice was uncooked and raw masala in it. No consistency

Amazing lamb gyros! Pictures of old school Bill Clinton on the walls. If you're sick of the fried foods, definitely give this place a try. It's a perfect to-go spot to grab food before the concerts at Preservation Hall.

I've been here a few times since I moved to Abington and it's been great every time. In December, I went there for my birthday with my girlfriend and parents. My parents had never been to an indian restaurant before and our waiter (who, I believe is also the owner) took the time to explain what everything was and how to pronounce things. We all got something different (I can't remember what because it was 8 months ago) but everything was so good. The restaurant wasn't super busy (maybe half full) and the owner (who's name I always forget to get) made it a point to come out and take minute and take a picture of us for me. I got some takeout chicken tikka & naan tonight and it was fantastic. The tikka sauce was super creamy and had lots of peppers & onions along with a ton of chicken in it. And it comes with a whole pint of rice. And the naan bread...a little charred and chewy...pretty much perfect. I'm someone who can put away a decent amount of food, and I couldn't finish it. I have to remember to get it spicier next time though. If you like Indian food, or have never had it and would like to try it, you need to check this place out.

Food was horrible. Service was horrible. Price menu wasn't updated. They only have two choice of sides for your order, plantain and mix veggies. If you want any other side, you've to pay more. I ask why, they stated this is real Jamaican restaurant. They ran out plantain. Oxtail taste like soda. Horrible experience. Stay away. They are other Jamaican cuisine restaurants in the area with the same price range that are much better.

After visiting the Eastern State Penitentiary, my boyfriend and I were a little hungry so we decided to stop by here for lunch. We each got a small pho and it filled us up just enough until dinner time! I got rare steak with tripe and he got rare steak with meatballs. Overall we paid $18 pre-tip, not too bad for pho! However, if we weren't planning on eating dinner 4 hours later, it would not have been a big enough portion at all. The restaurant itself is very clean and the staff are friendly and attentive. I only took one star off because I found the broth to be on the salty side.
Really good. Nice menu with good descriptions . They leave the heat to you. My Lamb Vindaloo "extra spicy" was delicious. The Garlic Nan was hot when served and was great. I will be back!

I'm a huge fan of Palace of Asia in general and definitely rank it up there in terms of my top five Indian Restaurant Favorties. It's by far, hands down, the BEST Indian restaurant in the area. I was thrilled when they opened in Cherry Hill and now in Philly (their sister restaurant is called Palace at the Ben) because before I would travel all the way to Princeton for their good eats! The decor is royal. You feel like a Rani (Princess) eating here and they make sure that the service follows suite. They go out of their way to ensure a pleasent, satisfying dining experience that will make you come back again and again. You may go on a whim, but this intrigue will soon turn into a love affair with their creamy, flavorful, robust culinary concoctions. Their lamb chops are succulent and moist, full of flavor, and cooked to perfection. The chicken makhni is rich and the sauce punctures the chicken just right to bring out its flavor. Their white chicken will leave you craving for more. The naan is toasted to perfection. Writing this is making me crave palace of asia for dinner tonight! Above all else, they really cater to your needs. They want your opinions and will always remember what you like! The service brings you back to the way customer service is in India - where the sayings, "That's not my job!", "That's not possible, Sir." , and "We don't offer that on this menu." simply don't exist. This is a restaurant where they will make your request happen and will find a way to ensure that you walk away a happy customer. Definitely give it a try because it runs circles around Coriender Bistro, Gagan Palace, and Tandoor Palace!
Some of THE best food I have ever had in my life.... Service is impeccable and the food is diificult to top... As a buddakhan junkie this foood is nothing short of superb

Second time here and want to come more and more! It's nice to come to place when you feel the atmosphere and professionalism. Was expected a lot and didn't get disappointed - and it's very important for us. High quality of ingredients, welcoming staff, amazing decor of the place. Me and my husband definitely will be coming here often, luckily we live in the neighborhood:)

Thai meets Mexican? Fusion of two flavors that are ridiculously good together. All wrapped up in one graffiti covered red food truck. I wish I could tell you the exact name of what we ate, but I want paying attention to names because I was afraid we'd lose our place in the long line. This was easily the busiest food truck in the long line of trucks curbside... And none had a line waiting for food like this one. No, they weren't slow, they were THAT GOOD! I'd wait again in the cold air for their short rib tacos... And, whatever their special was (we ordered "the special") was amazing. It came in a milky broth or gravy, with chicken and little bits of pickled something in it. We would drive 5 hours back to Philly for this... You should too!

A date night I'll never forget. I feel like I've walk past this place at least a dozen times and not once did it give away that it was this palace on the inside. If you come here please do yourself a favor and check out the garden out back it's an experience, the seating choices range from cushiony to hard bottom all options are giving you an opportunity to take in its splendor view. Even still it feels naturally connected to the rest of the restaurant. The food was delicious vegetarian options were plenty, I felt like I died and went to spice heaven. My partner had the Lamb I enjoyed the Bass and we both had nothing to say the entire meal because we were too busy stuffing our faces lol. Needless to say my date was magical and delicious and if your looking for a place to blow her mind without blowing your wallet, take her here!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We were really excited about finding an Indian restaurant as out-of-towners, but were very disappointed with the service. The first sign of trouble came when we ordered two glasses of the house white wine and a different server returned with two glasses of red. We decided to roll with it as we like red wine too... this turned out to be a mistake as the house red tasted more like sour apple juice. We ordered the butter chicken curry, palak curry with lamb, and the onion bahji for an appetizer. A few minutes later, the waitress returned to double check that we wanted lamb. The restaurant was not very busy, but it took about 45 minutes for food to come, with no servers checking on us during that time. We wondered where our appetizer might be. The food finally came. We love great Indian food and were definitely hungry (so might have loved anything), but felt that the flavors here were just okay, and the palak was way too salty. We also never received the appetizer. We were disappointed. After a little while, we let the waiter know he forgot the appetizer and gave us the wrong wine. He apologized, but then left with no further discussion or options for us. As we were eating dinner, one of the servers (who appears to be the owner's relative, maybe son) began arguing loudly with the owner about a phone call he had just received from a customer. I could not quite make out the details of the conversation, but felt it was a disrespectful and inappropriate display; they could have had this conversation in the back or kitchen easily. We were very uncomfortable and wanted to leave. We decided to get up and ask for our check. The appetizer that had not been provided was included on the bill; I had to ask for it to be taken off. Again, I really wanted to like this place. I'm a big fan of Indian food and supporter of family-run businesses. However, our overall experience here was very poor and we spent over $50 for two people. I hope we just caught them on an off-night.

I was staying at the Wyndham for work when I came across the Yelp review of this restaurant and then subsequently saw a pamphlet on it in the lobby. The hotel staff did not know where it was even though it was only 2 miles away! Well, thanks to my friends at Yelp, I had a great dinner at a great price. The food was much better than the much more expensive and not as tasty Capital Grille where I had dinner the night prior. I will admit that I have had Ethiopian food before, in Los Angeles, Berkeley and San Diego, which have a good variety of Ethiopian restaurants. I will have to say that this restaurant has the best that I have tasted. The service was great and started with a nice cinnamon tea. I ordered a sampler and it was served family style with a basket of injera bread to use (yes, you use your hands and the bread to scoop up the food!). No utensils, so its also a fun second date place. Although it is in a small strip mall, the interior is lit well with mood lighting and the ambiance was very nice. The waitress may have been the owner, and she was truly very nice and down to earth. She appreciated that
Very good service and the food was excellent. Very generous portions. And my children, who are picky eaters, want to go back.

Love the food but the lady who frequently answers the phone is not very fluent in English. Our order is often wrong and then we have to wait to get our correct order. They are always kind and apologetic but you know, it is a little irritating. We never have this issue if we come in person. I'm a regular and pretty much order the same thing every time. I highly recommend the crispy spring rolls but discourage the fresh rolls. The crab Rangoon is in an egg roll shape but is so amazing.
Wonderful! The lamb was tender and the tzatziki sauce was tasty. This food truck was at Twilight Tuesday the past few weeks and always had a line so I'm glad I could try it out today.
So delicious! I had the Aged Cheddar Burger and my fiance had the Brisket & Steak Pho... both were great. We had a friendly server and I love the décor. We will definitely be back!

Loved this place when I stopped in a couple of months ago!!! The jerk chicken was pretty darn spicy (as it should be) and delicious. The combo came with two sides so I picked the (incredibly delicious!) Island Slaw, and since I wasn't sure which kind of rice I wanted, one of the girls was nice enough to give me half coconut rice and half rice and beans. The meal also came with some nice plantains. Overall it was just wonderful. And the two ladies that run the place were super nice and helpful and had the biggest smiles around! Can't beat that :)

Why am I just finding out about this place? And who would have ever thought you could find good quality pho at a corner store? Their pork buns are are also very delicious. The staff is also very nice to me also. The woman always thanks me profusely for ordering and even helped to walk my order out to the car. Unlike most pho restaurants hey give you a to-go bowl and soup spoon. They also separate the broth from the meat and the veggies. That's a big deal because most restaurants just put everything in a styrofoam cup and give you regular silverware or they only separate the noodles. I love this place! I'll definitely be back!

Slightly above average Thai cuisine. I wouldn't go out of my way to go here for the food compared to other options in the area. The environment is a cut above, however. And the prices reflect that. This would be a good place for a 40th birthday party. You may have been here when it was the flashy Mai Thai. It has the same modern decor with the fancy bar and the rectangular fountain. The Baan Thai Noodle was spicy enough, especially with the Prik Nam Pla added at the table.

It really is as the reviews state - Indian Chipotle. The flavors are decent but not the greatest I've had. It's quick, cheap and does the job if your hankering Indian food. I would go again just because it's a quick bite to eat and fairly close to where I work.

Used a scoutmob today and food was delicious! Coquito drink is great too and reasonably priced. Authentic Puerto Rican rum too. New place working hard to take off. Definitely worth a try. Somewhat pricey is the only issue.

The food is great, period. Honestly, I travel all around the world for work and this is some of the best Pakistani/Indian food that I've had. The place is small, but that just means we had very nice personal service by the owner himself, and his wife is an excellent cook. Favorite meat dishes were the Lamb Curry, the Chicken Vindaloo, and the Beef... oh how tender and melt in your mouth. On the vegetarian side, we had the Alu Gobi and the Samosa, which had great flavor and spice; we did medium spice, which is as much as my wife could handle and is slightly spicier than their "regular." We had a group of four, but you could probably fit up to 8 people if you wanted a larger party, but larger than that would probably suggest take out. The mix of spices are flavorful, even with dishes of potato and cauliflower, and the heat is never burn your mouth but rather a warmth that adds to the flavor. We will definitely be returning.
Great happy hour. Bartender always forgets my drinks when he has 3-5 guests at a time. Food is meh

Stopped by here for a late lunch on New Year's Eve on our drive back to the Bay Area. It was the first time I had Thai iced green tea. Wow! It was unusual and delicious! The Penang curry was the best we have ever had and the drunken noodles were excellent too. Our server was super friendly. All in all, an excellent find in Santa Barbara.

La Va is is kind of blah. There is nothing about this benign corner coffee shop that is particularly good or bad. The service is a blend of comatose and apathetic. No smile/greeting during any of my three visits there, and when I ordered a cookie, and paid for my extremely expensive beverage- was not included or given to me. Seven dollars for a texturally uninspired/too sweet/flavorless cookie and a mediocre mocha? I'm not expecting a red carpet experience when I frequent any establishment, but give me a reason to stop in aside from "it's on the way between points a-b". I like the thrift store couch and tables, the exposes brick and local artists featured in the shop... Just try a little harder to be awesome, apathy is so 1996.

I used to like this place, until the lady at the cash register knowingly and willingly gave me a torn $10 as change. The bill is technically not legal tender, and unfortunately I found out only after leaving the store. I guess la va cafe showed the true face of "getting to know your neighbor". However, I recognize that that is a personal gripe I have, and probably should not have a great impact on the place. Their carrot ginger juice, though pricey as hell, is pretty good, I guess. I wish I could get two more if they accepted the illegal $10 tender they offered me in change. :/

Went there for lunch with friends today. Had the Bahamas Crab Burger ($7.50) with lettuce, tomato, and garlic mayo on a fresh Cuban kaiser roll. It was a pretty large sized crab cake burger and tasted delicious! For a nice kick, add some Matouk's Hot Calypso Salsa Sauce. The french fries with special jerk sauce is also a treat. I highly recommend this restaurant for lunch.
Although Blue Bell isn't exactly a hot spot for thai food, this place is amazing. Pretty much every dish on the menu is consistently fantastic. Personal favorite is the massaman curry
Excellent service. Food was outstanding . Lamb appetizer , Chicken Curry , rice pudding and a couple of kingfisher's , it doesn't get much better.

Worst food and services ever received from a Pollo Tropical. The outside of the chicken was hot but when I bit into it, inside was cold with icy water coming out of it. When I report it to the manager , Roger, his attitude was that there is nothing wrong.

Looks like Simply Thai got an fresh coat of paint and some new decorations since the last time I was here! Looks a lot better. My first visit was about seven years ago or so. I can't remember what I ordered but my dinning partner had the spicy green beans with beef and it was delicious! I can't recall too many details because that was a long time ago. My most recent visit I was please to see some updates and a giant menu! We split the fresh spring rolls and they were nice and fresh. The sauce was pretty sweet, but offered a nice flavor to the rolls. I ordered the stir fried cashew with chicken for my meal. This is my go to dish and it was good , but I would have liked more spice. Noted, next time I'll ask. Mike O. ordered the chili stir fry with pork and once again I had food envy. This dish had tons of flavor and was so tasty! Next time I am going with the chili stir fry. There are 8 tables or so. Or you can drive thru! Awesome! I wish I still lived in North County so I could come here more often. The service was good. They weren't busy so we got our food pretty quickly. FYI: Simply Thai has a sister restaurant up the street called Pearl Cafe which is also yummy!
Excellent Thai food! Pad Thai is amazing! Khao Soi is a very well balanced and flavorful dish! Really good Pad Thai too!

I was in the area and searched Yelp for a dinner spot on Sunday night. I was surprised this Caribbean restaurant was listed as an option because I had no idea this type of Cuisine was available in St Louis. The food was beyond tasty. I can't wait to go back. I ordered the Bandeja Paisa, it's a Sunday only platter with skirt steak, beans and rice, picadillo, fried egg, chorizo, avocado & one arepa." There was an addition of carnitas on my plate that were so good. The delicious picadillo was like a tropical sloppt joe filling. They weren't getting good avocados in so it wasn't included. :( I didn't care for the chorizo but I've never been a fan of chorizo. I also loved my friend's LaBandera Dominica as did he. This was way to much food for me but i was able to sample a lot in this selection. The sweet fried plantains were so good. I probably asked them to be Friday just a little bit longer which is a personal preference. When I was done, i felt like i should be heading to the beach at my resort with some rum punch or a mojito. The outdoor patio was nice with day's beaitful weather. Not busy and service was good. It's on SLUs campus so i can see it packed with college students during hh and weekend nights. I've already told several friends about this place. My leftovers reheated beautifully and I was sad when it was all finished.

Sister Muhammad's Kitchen gets ***** because they continue to maintain the original taste since they first opened in 1999, Sister Muhammad's Kitchen doors were closed for a while as they did a revitalization of the neighborhood, however they are open and still serving their signature Nation of Islam flavors. Sisters Muhammad's Kitchen is known throughout the city for their Muslim Fish Hoagie, but they are making a lot of noise with the new Salmon Cheese Steak. The Bean Pies are CLASSIC and the Navy Bean Soup is MAGNIFICENT... Friendly Staff and Clean Environment.... HURRY UP!!!!
Just had a fantastic meal. Good flavours, nice mix of spices and fresh vegetables, topped with coconut rice and the banana desert. Now my favourite Thai restaurant !

Damn, I really wanted to give up a 4 here, but keeping it real is what I do and if not, I'm cheating you all and myself, so they don't quite make the 4 nut. It's probably a strong 3.5, though. I'll say straightaway that these guys are dynamos at presentation, as in damn near untouchable. I have yet to see anyone in the area - area? Hell, the whole damn state - come anywhere near what these guys do and a lot of it is just fluff plate decoration with no intention given to the idea that anyone is going to consume it, though it's edible, of course. Décor inside is nice; it feels partially like an Asian place and partially like a tasteful speakeasy. I back that, bigtime. Where it falls apart a bit is in the actual food itself. Chicken Satay was done well here, but the sauce that came with was kind of glutinous and flabby and sort of gel-like. It tasted mostly average. I've had it at a number of Thai places, so I suppose it's becoming the standard now. The green tea was acceptable, but a bit on the weaker side. At least it was free of flowery elements. The Pad Prik Khing had mostly the right taste, but lots and lots of gristle in the meat (thanks?), what little of it there was and the presentation here worked against things as it was a bit cumbersome to eat. Rice was also so-so, which I really find puzzling at Asian places (go ahead, call me racist - I'll wait. Back? Good). None of that would prevent me from returning, yet I have pause due to the incredible, nearly unnatural slowness. I get that food is cooked to order, but when the entire place, including staff, is pushing half a dozen people, dragging ass that bad is interminable. And inexcusable. The food was partially worth the wait, but their slowness left reasonable back there in the dust, with the slow, plodding march for everything, including drinks and the check itself. I know the city is laid back, but I'm not trying to move in when I slide into that booth to eat...I'll probably go again to explore more of the menu as there was a lot of cuisines packed into that menu, but if it's anywhere near that slow again, that will be the final time.

This place gets 5 stars for a food truck! Holy smokes the food is wonderful and the staff is very nice. Everything we've eaten has been wonderful from the potstickers to the duck to the fried rice. We eat from here at least twice weekly. Sofia & Don

I've been here several times. Pho and rolls were very good. Service is great. I recommend this restaurant. However six big screen tvs really tacky down ambience. I suggest to sit where there isn't one in your face. Just me.

Tried the cheesesteak, Korean beef and Chinese vegetable. Cheesesteak and Korean beef were good but the Chinese vegetable was terrible. Would try again but it was a very underwhelming first experience

I tried this place about four years ago and was not impressed. I was in the mood for some bubble tea so I checked Yelp to see if it was sold close to where I work. I have only experienced bubble tea at The Doughnut Shop on Keystone Ave, not realizing I have been spoiled. I also has the spring rolls, egg drop soup, garlic chicken and egg roll. The spring rolls were not bad, the egg roll was good, the garlic chicken was just okay and the egg drop soup was no to my liking at all. The bubble tea came in about a 12 ounce cup with only a half dozen tapioca pearls and chunky ice. The Doughnut Shop gives you a cup twice as big with easily five times as many tapioca pearls, completely blended ice and is less $$. The only other complaint that I have about most of the ethnic restaurants in the Lafayette Square area is that they do not have a website, you cannot view the menu anywhere online, they don't have a fax in order to fax you a menu and cannot e-mail a menu to you.
This place is good for quick fix pho. They have several chains in North America.
Delicious lamb kabob for lunch! Tender, juicy, and just the right spices. I will be back.

As another reviewer said your experience there could go either way. The Jerk chicken was wayy to spicy where the spice over powered the flavor of the chicken. the cabbage was cold but the rice and plantains were okay. Kind of odd that the prices were so high to be served water in paper cups. The service was kinds crappy the young lady seemed rude and inexperienced. All of the shakes and homemade drinks they were out off. My son wanted to try the ice cream and I wanted rum cake & they were out of that as well. Oh yea! and the "weekend specials" they didn't have any on a Friday night. Overall I WOULDN'T recommend nor return.
Just left African Palace the rating I gave should have been - the food was the worse. The service was great, but sorry that's not good enough they need a NEW COOK

This place is walkable from me and after nearly 2 years of living here, I finally came! It's on the corner of Raceway and 10th with that Family Video Store next to it. You wouldn't have expected this place to be here as it is pretty tucked away in this plaza. Definitely more of a take out place than sit down - most people we encountered were doing take out, so I would recommend calling ahead and picking it up. There's a little window you order at, almost like a food court of sorts. However, it's definitely decent Thai (other Thai places I been to in Indy: Siam Square which I enjoy very much in Fountain Square and Bangkok Thai more in downtown which was okay; good ambiance but slightly overpriced I think). My family and I had #19, 20, 21, and 38. Portions are definitely generous! I had half of my plate left for another meal :) although I "tasted" everyone else's dishes too. 19 Pad Thai: yum! Although the lime slices were not very juicey :( 20 Pad See Ew: yum! Although a tad on the salty side 21 Pad Kee Mao: Super yum!! My brother had a little trouble with the spice (#3) so I got to have a lot more of this -- aside: spice range 1-5, it was great for me but those who aren't spice adventurers, would caution to do either 1 or 2. For reference I grew up eating spicy and enjoy it. I think I could handle 4 but would be drinking lots of water and probably wouldn't venture to 5. 38: Yellow curry - was pretty yummy too! They have a good amount of choices and I do plan to return with it being so close to me. Entrees are just about $10. For me, with one order being 2 meals, it's a decent deal!

The food at this place is really really really good. The service is also good. That being said the seating is very limited, and because the door is open quite frequently, in the warmer weather, you get a fair amount of flies buzzing around in there. I have eaten there several times. It is a real find.If you want a beautiful dining room, or people that are amazingly fluent in English this place isn't for you.
The food here is amazing! Love the Thai iced tea too. Peter the owner came to make sure we enjoyed the food and our server was wonderful too . You'll enjoy it here so come check it out!

I thought the service was sweet & attentive. The food was fresh and very reasonably priced! I eat Vietnamese regularly in New Orleans and think that this spot brings a unique family atmosphere that many of the others lack. The round-eye pho was flavorful with excellent rice noodles. I can't wait to make it there again!

The lunch service was pretty quick, the food was filling and tasty, but the atmosphere could use a little more warmth and cleanliness. Also, I had to go to the bar to ask for my bill, kind of was forgot about at the end.

Biggest rip off I've ever experience. The sandwich was 2 buns and 3 tiny pieces of chicken. By tiny, I mean less chicken then what you can hold between your thumb and your index finger. Feel free to eat here but don't be suprised when you walk out angry.

We tried this place tonight. If you like Mediterranean food, it's okay but not spectacular. I had a gyro plate, which included some tasty pita bread. My husband had a grilled chicken plate, and he said it was so-so. The rice was flavorful, the meat wasn't greasy, and the salad was filled with a variety of flavors. While I waited, I was offered a sample of their fruit tea. Good stuff. They also carry baklava and cheesecake if you're interested in dessert. I'd like to try one of their smoothies since they offer a variety of flavors. Customer service was friendly and attentive, which is a major plus. Overall, it deserves 3.5 stars, but since Yelp doesn't offer that, I have to settle for 3.

I'm not a Philly local, but I come here every time I'm in town, and everything I've had has been great. The restaurant is solely vegetarian, but meat lovers won't notice anything missing. The food is excellent; it's incredibly flavorful, well spiced, and just plain delicious. Every dish I've had here has been excellent, but the Navaratna Korma is stunning.

My wife and I have gone to Nadia about every other month since we moved into the area four years ago. The food is well priced and portioned. I love the pad thai and my wife loves the curry, so we get to share when we go:) I've had some of the more expensive dinners (duck) and really enjoyed. The only reason I did not give five stars is because the appetizers are not the best. If you do get an app, go with the chicken Satay. Also BYOB.

So, I'm a little disappointed in this place. First, it has a weird setup. The storefront used to be the natural foods/vitamin store/vegan restaurant on Narberth's main strip, but now it's a thai restaurant/vitamin store. Apparently, one person owns and operates the vitamin shoppe by day, while another person owns and operates the thai restaurant in the evenings, all within the same space. Second, restaurant is only open until 8 p.m. during the week, and from what I've seen of the turnaround time for tables there, it averages one sitting per night. Not good if they wants to turn a profit. Okay, so here's the meat of my review. I've been to this restaurant twice. The first time was with my boyfriend and another couple on a weekend evening. The place is tiny, and only the front is used for seating (the back half of the store is for the vitamin shoppe), so we were squeezed into the tables like sardines because the restaurant was busy. My friends and I were lucky enough to snag a table, but it apparently was right in the way of the servers, so they had to keep squeezing behind and around us, which made us nervous that we'd accidentally end up with hot curry on our laps. The food was decent. I got a thai coconut soup that was good and a salad with granny smith apples and a peanut dressing, which was tasty. Everyone's curry was also good - flavorful with heat, but not too spicy. All in all, I thought, I enjoyed the meal, despite the crowded conditions. Last week during Narberth's annual Sidewalk Festival, my boyfriend and I decided to stop in for dinner. First, I got a jasmine rice soup that was tasty, and I ordered a duck curry off the menu that was supposed to be mildly hot (spice-wise), as indicated by the single pepper next to it on the menu (one pepper = mild spice; two peppers = moderate spice; three peppers = very hot). My boyfriend ordered a curry with tofu that was rated two peppers. Now, I enjoy some heat in my meals, but I don't like it when my mouth burns and when the heat is so intense that it's impossible to taste the other ingredients in the dish. Well, after quite a while waiting for our food, despite the fact the place wasn't busy, the owner (who was also the server that evening) brought us our curries. As she went to place mine in front of me, she said, "Red curry?" Now, the red curry is rated 2 peppers on the menu, and it has red bell peppers in it, which I detest, so I know that wasn't what I ordered. So I said that I had not ordered red curry, I had ordered the other one (I forget what it was exactly - panang, I think). She looked confused and said she'd be back. 10 minutes later, she returned with the same dish and said that the dish was, in fact, panang and not red curry. So I said okay and dug in. After only about two bites, however, I realized that something was amiss. There were red bell peppers in the curry, and it was so spicy that I literally could not eat it. Just to check, I tried my boyfriend's curry, which was supposed to be spicier than mine, and it had no heat to it whatsoever. He and I concluded that the dish in front of me was not what I had ordered. Now, I never, ever complain at restaurants, even when my order gets mixed up because I don't like to make trouble. Usually, it's no big deal, but I literally could not eat what I was served this time, and I was hungry. So I decided to speak up. After several minutes, I finally managed to flag down the owner and explained the situation to her. She said I could order something else. So I ordered the curry that my boyfriend had because his was not spicy at all. Then she came back 10 minutes later again (by now, my boyfriend had finished his meal and we'd been there 1.5 hours) and said, very patronizingly, that the chef said that I probably couldn't handle the spice in ANY curry on the menu, implying that I'm just a wuss who can't handle spicy food. That is not true - I've eaten spicy Thai, Indian, Mexican, etc. before and have always liked it. They simply gave me the wrong meal. I was miffed, to say the least, and said that I would like the bill and would just eat something at home. Then the owner said, no, to get something, so she gave me the apple peanut salad to mollify me. It's good, but it wasn't dinner, and I had really wanted duck. Frankly, I was seething as I ate it because I felt that I had been insulted, and I think that the chef probably just didn't feel like cooking another curry because it was now almost 8:30 and they stop seating at 8 o'clock (my boyfriend and I sat down to eat at 6 p.m.!). Rather than admit that they gave me the wrong dish, they blamed me for the mistake. Needless to say, I'm probably not going back there again. The food is decent but is not the best Thai food I've had by far, and the atmosphere is certainly not welcoming. I'd only recommend this place for those who like a surprise when their food comes out and some condescension from the staff.

Kinda cheap, and not in the good way. No rice with delivery orders. Be warned. Employee at restaurant was not helpful when I called to ask where is the rice. Only Indian restaurant I've ever seen do this... And again,, not a good thing.

Superb is the best way to describe this restaurant and the waitstaff. The decor is beautiful (wood carvings), food (yummy, plentiful and fresh), waitstaff (attentive and pleasant), waitstaff's attire (appropriate and in sync with the decor), service (the waitstaff and greeter ensure that we didn't want for anything - drinks replenished, water without asking, etc.) and price (a lot of food for the price). Note -- the restaurant uses a chain on the doors when it's closed, so don't think they are out of business. The first time we went by it was during their 'unopened' times and we thought they were out of business. Today we visited during their business hours as noted on Yelp and the chain was not there and the "open" light was on. :)

This is a good new Thai place in the site of the old Warsaw Cafe. My wife and I have been three times since it opened about a week ago, and each of the six dishes we've tried has been great. My favorite so far is the Pad Khimao, which was nice and spicy. If you're not into spicy food, most of the other dishes are mild (the menu alerts you to the spicier ones, and you can also specify your preferred spiciness on a 1-5 scale). The service has been good, both for take-out and dining in. And the space has been decorated very tastefully. Since it's on a residential part of 16th St., just south of Spruce, there's a very nice neighborhood-treasure-to-be feeling to the restaurant. The slightly out-of-the-way location seems to have limited their business so far, but hopefully the crowds will start coming once the word of mouth advertising spreads about their good food. Jasmine Rice is worth a try. Good food, friendly service, and a nicely decorated space.

Very very tasty even as takeout. Worth the wait, which was not very long anyway. We will most definitely be returning next time we are in town. We like businesses that find a way to make it work in odd circumstances and this counts. Amazing.

Aweful service and food....its the management writing good reviews...dont fall for these cheap tricks! Portion size...I have bigger amts of leftovers at many places than what was served here... They take buffet leftovers and put it dinner curries.... Dear management...rather than writing these reviews....spend more time in preparing and serving good food

Wonderful place for lunch or dinner! It's a casual vibe with solid food! The lunch time is an "order at the counter, and they deliver to your table", but dinner is a slightly more formal "please wait to be seated at a table" affair. Flavors of the locally sourced seafood are varied but with lots of Asian influence and super yummy! Fresh produce and herbs (some grown on site) accompany most food items, which come in small and large plates at dinner. Lunchtime is simpler: just pick a protein and 2 or 3 sides and is so affordable. At night, the bar is fairly robust and there are some unique cocktail options to share at the table! I've gotten the fish everytime I've been for whatever meal and I LOVE it! The papaya salad is also the bomb! The back patio dining is precious and sweet and you pass by their grill and smoker as you go back there. (It's very clean, too!) Idk what else to tell you except that this place is a hidden gem for locals and local chefs! Bon appetit!

I've been to there many times, and of course for several family birthdays. The food is excellent!!! I love the Chicken Parm, can not figure out they make it so amazing. Even for a marathon runner, that dish fills me up. I know the night before every big race in Philadelphia this establishment is packed solid. If you are around south philadelphia or want to have a great meal, you must call up and make a reservation.

Dosas are just ok..Nothing special But if you are a tamilian or an telugu person or love spicy chicken curry,do try chicken chettinadu curry! Its sooo authentic and is served with hot flavoured basmati rice (ask for ghee if u cant take spice) !!! U are insane if you crave homemade chicken curry in the US and still dont want to try it!
ate there yesterday based on all the great reviews and i was not disappointed. the reviews were on the mark. in summary "delicious"
it was very good and very nice decor, impressed on my first trip. would def go back

Well established Trini spot on 52nd & Chancellor... half-way between the El and Malcolm X Park. The food is solid and consistent. I usually stick to the oxtails or curry goat & doubles, but I've also had their snapper, jerk & various roti's as well. Everything is decent. Portions vs. price vs. quality make this place a win-win-win situation.

This is a good run-of-the-mill Thai place. All the classic favourites are available - red/green curry, pad thai etc. But they also have some lesser seen options like yellow and massaman curry. All the food was delicious, generous and fairly priced. Service was a bit spotty. e.g. some getting their food a while before others, removing some plates while others were still eating, but generally competent. Much better value for money than many close-by overpriced alternatives.

This place is excellent to start off , my girlfriend and I came for brunch and were highly impressed by the freshness and quality of our meals , we got the Huevos Rancheros and breakfast tacos with added chorizo and both were absolutely delicious , this little restaurant had a great staff and great food we highly recommend this hole in the wall.
