Love it. The Roti Canai is some of the best I've had in the US, must try. Satay beef skewers have always been perfectly cooked, and I order delivery exclusively. Tom yum soup is a winner if you're in to spicy and the crispy basil duck is great. Don't forget to order a Mango Iced tea, it's kind of sweet for those who care but I could drink a 2 liter of it and want more. Great work, Golden Triangle.

Just tried Blu Fig for the first time. Very impressive - the falafel is made in house as are many of the specialties & the hummus is to die for! The owners are also very nice & Blu Fig is locally owned which is always a plus in my book. I'll be back and recommend it as one of the few healthy AND tasty places to eat in Nashville. A+

Best Thai food in Nashville. Coming from NYC I wanted good Thai food and I got it! I especially like the Pad See Ew with beef. Only wish the Thai iced tea was less sweet and I would get it every time.

They have vegan pho! Satisfies your 'fix', but tastes okay. I've had much better. Broth is too sweet. The veggies include fried tofu & shitake shrooms (both yummy), as well as radish & carrots (both soggy, so not good). I included a pic. Other good things tho - they have 3 sizes for pho, small medium and large. And overall the food is typical vietnamese. Great go-to place in Fairmount if you need your pho fix.

Sansom Kabob House has picked right up where it left off in its move to its new digs on South Street. The food is still very tasty and nicely presented. However now the food is served in beautiful surroundings. This is the best-looking Afghan restaurant in Philly. Oh yes, it is still as friendly as ever too! Among the dishes enjoyed here was the bulani. These paper-thin pockets with potato and onions are on the addictive side of the food index. The tasty ashak (scallion dumpling) is right behind them ... and it also provides a dip for the fresh Afghan bread served here. For a main course, I went with the eponymous Sansom kabob platter and wasn't at all disappointed...especially as the brown rice was cooked so perfectly. Tip - Don't forget to ask for their homemade Chatni hot sauce! Welcome Sansom Kabob House to South Street!

So glad a bubble tea and banh mi place opened nearby! The first time I was here, we had our nephew and he was throwing a fit. He was upset when I told him the drinks were all teas so he couldn't have one. As we were waiting for our food, the owner came and gave us a drink she made herself without any tea! What wonderful customer service! The banh mi's are really good as well. I love the black tea with boba and the cold meat banh mi!

This cafe has recently been renovated, and looks amazing. It's a modern, bright, open space with tons of windows, and also tons of people. Try and avoid getting there right at lunch time when the line can get long. This is one of my favorite spots for lunch in the university area. The chana masala and palak paneer wraps are excellent - warm, full of flavor, and wrapped in grilled, soft white pita bread. They are priced around $8 to $8.50, and are very filling (sometimes I take half to go). They are served with a raisin soup/sauce... not exactly sure what it is, but it is so delicious. I have never had it anywhere else. People love the chai here, but I find it a bit sweet. Last time that I was in I ordered a regular coffee. I think that they made the coffee to order. I was a bit taken aback at the price ~$3.75, although it was a fairly large cup, freshly made, with excellent flavor. A minor note that they only have cream out to put in your coffee... I prefer milk. I assume they would have given me some had I asked.

A solid 3 stars, maybe even 4 - food is very basic (possibly a little bland) but the spring rolls and bun were tasty and the traditional Vietnamese Coffee hit the spot on a cold day. grilled Lamb over bun was succulent and tasty - albeit a small portion and $12.95. Quick service got me in & out even on a busy Thursday lunch rush. Nearly every table was full - and this after years of being open is a great sign. Prices are higher than in Philly (Chinatown, Vietnam,m Vietnam Palace, Pho Cali) but considering where we are - I am beyond thrilled to have a non-pizza lunch alternative. Can't wait to go back and try the sumer rolls.

Walk end this place, I really didn't think it was going to be about anything........ after getting my food and tasted it...... I was like damn. This shit it good........ after that throughout my stay I ate a gyro every night after walking up and down Burbon St....... now this will be one of my favorite spots when I visit the BIG EASY. LOVE IT

Possibly the best Puerto Rican food in Florida, and better than most places in Puerto Rico too. (I'm from PR.) The mofongo is excellent, I had it with the fried pork chunks and they were a bit salty but crunchy, moist, and delicious. Sangria is great too.

Came here for lunch. The decir is kitchy Mumbai style. The lines move quick. You pick your base, a protein, a sauce, toppings and then a chutney. I ordered the rice bowl with lamb and saag. The food is really good and everything tastes fresh. The price can be lower by $1-2 for the office crowd. The chicken samosas are 2 for $4 and smaller in size than regular. Overall a good experience.

Horribly detoriated the standard of food and service. They served water after half an hour in styrofoam glasses when the restaurant was not even full. The food is so spicy and hot that we Indians also failed to digest them. The waiter does not have any courtesy and banged the water pitcher on the table and walked off. We visited this place so many times but got very disappointed to see the decline.

We popped in before our run to Trader Joe's (we have a rule to always eat before Trader Joe's-- or else it gets bad), and we were more than pleasantly surprised! The food is SO good, and the portion sizes are HUGE. When we got our pho, I legitimately was in awe. We got the pho, a vermicelli noodle dish with pork and egg roll, and a "hoagie" with pork- which was essentially a bahn mi. The food tasted fresh and the service was great! I 100% am glad to find a pho place in the city so I don't always have to make the trek to Chinatown! Will be back again and again!!
Great quality comes with a hefty price for soup! BUTTTT, its darn good and worth the price. Anything to cure some cold weather or a cold!

This is a good neighborhood BYOB. Seating is limited for large groups so I would recommend a reservation and still possibly expect a wait, it is a great fit for two people though (they have a lot of two person tables). Food is decent but I still haven't found my "go-to" dish. $$$ Cash Only

My family comes from Xingjiang and this is the first place in Edmonton I've found that serves dishes from our home province!! They even made their liangfen, dumplings and noodles from scratch. The prices are very reasonable. everything is under $15. They had a lot of traditional comfort food and large portions. Sure it's not as good as moms cooking, but it beats waiting for the holidays for a taste of home. However, this is not the place you take your unadventurous friends. You know who I mean, that one person that thinks lemon chicken is the height of Chinese cuisine. They would not find anything familiar here.

This is the best priced, best tasting Indian buffet I've been to. ~$10 buffet, and it is real quality! I can name 10 or 15 local Indian restaurants that don't come close to the food preparation and service of Nirvana, but why would I? Our server engaged us in conversation after we arrived while waiting for our 3rd party member. Very friendly! Thanks again

I always hear great Things about Ethiopian food - finally decided to give a try. Don't get turned off by the small location etc. Ambietis great and it gives you very different feel - could be real Ethiopian setting. Music was great, already bought few tracks from Amazon. Try sveral different items - I liked it.

I had been looking forward to dining at Zeppoli since it received rave reviews in Philadelphia magazine. However I found the experience could not possible live up to the reviews. I went with two friends, so there was a total of 3 of us. I made reservations far in advance, yet upon arriving it was like the Spanish inquisition, I was bombarded with such questions as: When did you make your reservations? Who did you speak with? This did not set a great tone, but I shrugged it off and attempted to enjoy the evening. The atmosphere is small and quaint, and I do mean SMALL. For me it was like being seating in a middle seat in coach on an airplane. I found myself using the restroom to stretch. I personally think they should remove one table and spread the extra room around, but this could just be my hang up. We ordered the Antipasto appetizer, which was a decent portion for three people. The waitress asked how many people it was for, which explains the proper portioning. However when the check arrived, we discovered that the price is $11 per person. FOR ANTIPASTO, INSANE!!! We could have ordered a steak for less money for the three of us to split. The three of us ordered entrées, which were also a good size, I had the gnocchi, which was out of this world. For desert we ordered the zeppolis which were un-remarkable (I personally prefer the beignets at Grand Lux). Overall, the attitude doesn't justify the price and sacrifice of space. Considering there are so many other wonderful Italian places nearby, it is amazing that this place is so crowed. I think the best thing to do would be either order take away or visit another establishment.

This is without a doubt, the best Thai restaurant I have eaten at yet! The service, the beautiful interior, and the food exceeded all my expectations. They also serve Sushi! But, the owner Bryan is the sweetest person by giving back to the GLBT community, and he deserves a round of kudos.
One of the best Thai places around. The Hawaiian fried rice is too die for. Freshest Vegis in their dishes. Great service great food
This is a delicious Asian restaurant! I've never been disappointed here, regardless of what I ordered. That makes be feel comfortable enough to always try new things. Friendly service too!

First time at pollo tropical had the shrimp platter with yellow rice and black beans. Where should I start. The shrimps were not hot but just warm when I started the second pike with the shrimp they were cold. Didn't even start the back beans. They looked more than shredded beans than whole black beans. They taste of the yellow rice was not nearly my taste. Not tasty at all. Only one star also because of food spots on the floor. I defo not coming back

Wow! This place is AMAZING!!!! The restaurant is super clean and has an impeccable ambiance. The server was very friendly and completely competent of the whole menu. The food.......was INCREDIBLE!!!!! Even the people at the table behind me were moaning because the food was that good!!!! I ordered the curry goat and had a pineapple passion smoothie to drink. Everything was seasoned to perfection and simple delicious! You're really missing out if you don't eat here at least once!

Jeffersonville is lucky to have Desi Spice: the food is wonderful and tailored to you own level of spice love. More importantly, the family that runs it is both generous and kind: if you come more than once, they treat you like a friend rather than just a customer. I have gone to places with equally good food and terrible service; I've gone to places with lackluster food because the service was so good. At Desi Spice, we get both, which is why they will always have us as customers for life.

Off top: a star is removed for the price. Super expensive pad Thai and pho $40 and it's not even a real dine in restaurant, seating is very limited. We had to ask for water as we weren't sure if dinner came with water. You are able to purchase Asian groceries to make your own meal which is interesting. Pad Thai was edible but didn't have that Asian flair. I wouldn't go back but if your desperate for Asian food bc it's Monday, go. But no, instead go across the street to Han Dynasty. Or just stop in to say you Been To (Binto) It...get it. Okay cheesy but seriously you can skip the place and save your money.
Since its the only pho place in iv..might as well..pretty good for a rainy evening..cmon, experiment a lil!! enuff with the burritos!!

Wow, I'm so excited! This is my first yelp review and it feels awesome to write a positive one at that as a new yelper (after my friends kept convincing to sign-up since I am a Culinary Arts major~ok, you guys win.) I have never heard of Wishbone before until I stumbled upon it after going to the movies with the beau (Godzilla anyone?). Honestly, I didn't know what to expect from Wishbone when I first entered the restaurant. I was a little confused with how to place my order, but I got the hang of it once a fellow staff gave me a spiel about how things worked. Wishbone was described as a craft-fried chicken joint and indeed the chicken were craft alright! Although I didn't particularly enjoy the dark chicken tenders, the white chicken tenders were pretty tasty. I also had the chicken with a couple of sauces which were Chipotle Lime Mayo, Parmesan Pesto, and Madras Curry. Can I just say that I'm a big fan of pesto, but damn...that Madras Curry was good! I also had their biscuit and celery snap drink which the beau thought was ok. I found the food and decor above average, but I was most impressed with the staff. They were very knowledgeable about their products and sincere in helping an indecisive girl pick which chicken she wanted to devour. The verdict, food is 4 stars, however the service is absolutely 5 stars. It's not the food that makes the business great, it's the people. Great job Wishbone...I will definitely be back in the future! My next stop...Chocolate Con Cafe!

The food here reminds me of the many pho places in Houston Chinatown. The service isn't fantastic, but I am willing to overlook it for the food quality. Their pho, broken rice dishes, and grilled pork are all really good.

The staff were adorable and sweet! We enjoyed the vegetarian platter, the two hummus were delicious and fresh and the falafel was cooked perfectly. I would definitely go again, also if you are vegetarian they have a nice variety of options on their menu.. will be back soon!
Absolutely the best sushi we have ever had. Service was outstanding. Everything was perfect. We live in Orlando and have not had any sushi that comes close to theirs. Keep up the great job.

Really great hole in the wall place! The food was very good and the hostess was very nice and helpful in explaining what to order. Had the butter chicken and naan. Both were the best I've had in the US.

Have only tried once. Got drunken noodles. They were extremely oily and not especially flavorful. The vegetable prep was pretty rough and uneven. For the money, I would expect more care in preparation. I waver between 2 & 3 stars. The service was adequate. Based on the one meal I had, I would not be quick to return.
Service is FAST. Food is perfectly seasoned, prices are very reasonable for the portions and the quality. Next time I'll try something much spicier.

Such a beautiful art ambience, make me feel like I'm in Thailand. Waitress asked about allergies after ordering food, so nice of them. Service was fast. Sexy lady was too good, panang curry was so tasty .

Stopped by on my way home from the humane society. I live 5 miles up mt. rose highway so I'm not very close to this area. Ordered a stir fry chicken dish and when I returned home it was not only a beef dish, but looked as though someone through a bunch of mud over rice and lots of onions. My husband tasted it thinking he might eat it and it was so disgusting I decided to drive ALL the way back down to get the correct order. Not only did they seem indignant and pissed, but they never even apologized for the incorrect food order. When I returned home to eat it, it was so terrible, I gave the chicken to my dogs......they didn't even want it.

Great atmosphere - down to traditional attire worn by waitresses. Food delicious! Pineapple curry with shrimp & clear noodle dish with chicken were outstanding! Love the Thai tea & coconut icecream to finish off a wonderful meal.

I was in the mood for thai tonight and checked out this resturant. It was fantastic food with unbelievable flavor and the presentation was absolutley beautiful also! I will be going back again soon! Thank you.

Just average...I had the chicken tikka masala... ordered it at a "4"spice level out of 5... tasted like most tikka I have had without the bumped up spice level. Garlic naan was good... aloo chat was uneven. They scooped two scoops of garbanzo beans causing a big lump in the middle. Some "bits" were cold. Service was apathetic at best. I arrived at 4pm for a late lunch, early dinner and woke up the staff from a nap. Being the only patron in the place, one would think that the service would be attentive and efficient. I felt as the staff almost could not be bothered or if I was an inconvenience. There are too many Indian restaurants with better service and similar food to consider going back.
Great jerk chicken and awesome prices. Very laid back. Woman working the counter is super sweet.
Absolutely perfect, even got a recipe for the delicious shahi paneer.
Great experience! Wonderfully nice staff and amazing food. Hot fresh and ready for takeout in under 20 mins. I ordered the red curry and fresh rolls with chicken, must try this place!!

I wish I could give Avalon 10 stars! We just had my son's graduation/going away party at Avalon. John (the owner) and the entire staff bent over backwards to accommodate us. Everything was top notch! The food, the décor, and the staff were all excellent! The antipasto was fresh, plentiful with a wide assortment of choices. The pizzas were hot out of the oven and to die for. We chose a buffet option with mixed green salad, chicken saltimbocca (the best I have ever had), pasta bolognese, and penne alfredo. Everyone raved about the food. We have received so many compliments about the party from family and friends. Thank you so much for a wonderful day that my family will remember for years to come!

Have to say I'm not that impressed. Figured it was worth ordering after looking at reviews. Ordered take out and It took an hour and a half. Peanut sauce smelled a bit like stinky feet but the rice vermicelli was alright. Nothing worth more then 1 star!! Its a shame since I LOVE Vietnamese food! Yuck!

Had lunch there today and the gyro was dry and did not taste like it did a few months ago. Also the cheese on the pasta sides smelled and tasted off maybe bad. Bathroom had three live roaches. Me and my team used to once a week but we all agree since under new management this place has taken a turn to just ok/bad.

We ordered several items off the vegan menu. Yes. They have an entire menu that is vegan!! All of it was delicious, and the service was great. Kind, friendly, and aware staff! We can't wait to go back!
My favorite bahn mi in the city! Super easily accessible location with parking in the rear. Friendly staff, good prices. what more do you need?

This P.F. Chang's location is probably the best I have been to - service was great, food was good and came out quickly, and the restaurant was very clean. They have a nice outdoor seating area for the summertime, and a good bar as well. If you are looking for a consistent and reliable restaurant in Plymouth Meeting, P.F. Chang's fits the bill.

I seriously don't understand why this place only has a 3 star. Well, the only reason would be the communication barrier between the server and the customer. But I don't think their amazing restaurant should be ranked only with a 3 stars. It's their second language! Don't expect them to be like a natural born citizen, ha even natural born citizens have grammatical errors all the time. This restaurant works so hard to ensure that their customers leave happy every time! My roommates and I are avid foodies. We seek hidden gems and always find leaders of the different ethnic foods. The four of us agreed that this is our favorite Indian restaurant in Indy. The atmosphere of the restaurant is similar to any other ethnic restaurant, basic decorations with elevator music playing in the background. It's casual and easy to serve any size group. I enjoy the food at the restaurant but I also love taking home to my own comfort. My favorite dish is the butter chicken and I always get the garlic Naan. Best Indian restaurant I've found in Indy! Try it out and help their ratings. They deserve more than a 3 star!

Kalamata is a small casual café with a great selection of fresh, reasonably priced Mediterranean food. The extensive menu includes stuffed grape leaves, gyros, savory pies, baklava, rolls, fattoush, and much more. Their tabouli salad is delicious, and the various homemade baked goods looked amazing, but I managed to use some restraint, and save them for another day. The painted concrete floors and simple, clean dining area give Kalamata a rustic, authentic feel, which I especially appreciate considering their suburban strip mall location on Hillsboro Rd., diagonally across from the Mall at Green Hills. The staff here is friendly, and if you're having trouble deciding what to try, they're happy to give you a free sample. They have live music on Fri. and Sat. nights, and although they don't serve alcohol, the menu invites customers to BYOB. There's plenty of seating, so Kalamata is a good place to come for lunch or a quick, informal dinner.

After a whole lifetime of being warned that food cooked in a truck would kill me, this past year I decided to take my chances and see what this mysterious genre of cuisine has to offer. For the most part, I have not been disappointed. Philly does food cart pretty well. And my absolute favorite is Cucina Zapata. I've tried just about everything on their menu: short rib taco, thai chicken taco, cap'n crunch coated tilapia burrito, chicken katsu, sweet potato & chicken curry...each so wonderfully delicious and packed with flavor. The portions are also pretty large- I've never finished a meal for Cucina Zapata without feeling completely stuffed. It's no surprise then, that this place is so popular. I'd avoid going right at 12pm, seeing as you'll be looking at a good 15-20 minute wait.
No frills but great food. I stopped by for bahn mi three times on my three day trip. For a professional food person that says something.

I am sipping away on an almond hot chocolate reading about activity based costing and a funny thought comes into my head. Would I kill for this drink? And after much contemplation (more than I thought it would take to come to a resolution) I decided no, because that would be crazy, but I might nudge an old lady out the way to get it! Kidding aside, the drinks here are good. And not like 2006 Oilers good, closer to 1984 Oilers good. This is not a place that automates drinks, they craft them. So expect to wait longer than usually to receive your order. It's worth the wait. The almond hot chocolate was a reasonable $4 (for 473ml). That price is amazing given that I have paid more for comparable quality drinks elsewhere. Free WiFi available. Through a UYE held by Karlie "the rambler" M., I did get to meet the owners of this place. Trudy and Tom are pretty passionate about their products. I have been back a few times since and the quality has not declined. If I were to make a suggestion, a few hooks to put jackets on would be nice. Also a larger tea menu wouldn't be bad either. But what can I say, there is quality here in a wonderful atmosphere. We need more places like this in Edmonton.

Went for lunch with 2 other friends. Waitress was outstanding, great service with lots of attention. The food was we expected. Tasty, hot and well seasoned. For lunch it had a very decent crowd. Not too noisy but enough people there to make the place alive.
Great sushi. Service is good staff is friendly. Similar to pf changs.

Everything was excellent. We had the Bucatini pesto; the rigatoni with chicken meatballs; and clam linguini. All were super tasty with the bucatini just edging out the chic meatballs. The linguini had too much chorizo for me. We also had Caesar salads. The dressing was fabulous but the whole sardines were the stars! It's served as a romaine head quartered so you had to use a knife and fork on it. It was kind of annoying--would have preferred just the typical chopped version. Our waitress was spot on. The decor was so cool. I'm totally ripping off the wine barrel stave ceiling. Loved this place and will be back often.

This is a great cozy spot. Inside doesn't seat more than 12 people so if you have a large group you should get it to go. The food was fantastic and the portion size was perfect for a big guy like me. I got the pad Thai with pork and destroyed it. If I wasn't visiting from out of town, I'd definitely make this a regular dinner or lunch spot!
Fast service and tasty food. The spicy eggplant was super flavorful and the tofu crispy. Great experience. Their drunken noodles are always great, as well.
Great food. We had the falafel wrap and the chicken shawarma. The place has a quick bar seating type situation so while you are walking around you can sit, get a quick bite and leave. Recommended!

I just went there to get a drink and they completely ignored me, to the point i was embarrassed to stay waiting at the bar and was forced to leave! The bartender was talking to mildly attractive girls and saw me sit down and chose to ignore me. The other bartender ran by me holding up a finger as I rushed just to ask for a drink menu and didn't come back. The only time I get good service here is when the bartender with the manbun is on, needless to say, if you don't see a manbun you had better run! Horrible service, actually second time I've been unimpressed with the service here, don't know why I keep coming back. My advice, don't waste your time. Britt
Awesome! The staff was friendly, service was fast and the Shrimp Kebabs were fantastic!! This place is highly recommended!!
Came for Bahn Mi, had pork parties, they were alright, baguette could be better. Wife ordered crap Rangoon and the lemongrass chicken Bahn Mi, and she enjoyed hers more.

Found myself near Northgate around lunch time today and spotted Nam express from the parking lot. I believe the only other food outlet in that strip was Edo so we decided to try this instead and hopefully get something more unique. The space was bigger than I expected and they have seating for a couple dozen people (7-8 tables). The server was super nice and acknowledged us as soon as we walked in even though the place was fairly busy. There is a lot on the menu but it is mostly types of pho, vermicelli bowls, stir frys, salad rolls and a few other items. We tried the kung pao chicken with rice, the dry pork ribs and the chicken pho. All the items were delicious and the portions were generous, we had to pack it for home. The prices as reasonable for the pho, I found the ribs and kung pao to be a little expensive compared to other places but the portions arebalso bigger, so it is fair. I am not sure when I will be in Northgate again, but this place is a good bet for a filling meal.

I checked out the lunch buffet looking for a comparison to my normal haunt- Amber in Carmel. Needless to say it didn't measure up, not even close. Service was sorely lacking as was the food. Much fewer options & less flavorful food overall. Ex. the saag paneer was very runny with hardly any actual paneer in it. Food wasn't being refreshed, less veggie options especially, only saw a waiter once during my entire meal. They did offer an option on naan, garlic or plain, which I appreciate. But i will stick with Amber and skip this restaurant in the future.

Went here because it was well reviewed, and it was the worst hookah experience we've ever had! We all had one mediocre drink we didn't even finish (since it's a one-drink minimum per person) and we weren't even able to finish the house special hookah as two of us started to feel extremely sick. Ruined our nights.... It was not a great atmosphere- almost no space between tables, uncomfortable for any intimate conversation, strangers kept jumping into our conversation. But it might have been worth it for the affordable hookah had we not gotten sick. First time in several years of going to hookah bars any of us has had a bad experience. Don't know why this place is so well-reviewed.

We will return (might increase stars) to this just opened restaurant. The atmosphere and staff were very pleasant; open thru afternoon, so a leisurely late lunch was not a problem. We had and recommend Arancini, eggplant mezze (fried with tomato sauce), cannelloni and mushroom risotto.
This is the place serving best Flavorful Indian food in US. This is the 1st place everyone loved and finished their food in my family. Can't wait to go back and enjoy their food again.

Went there for lunch today. It was a cute little establishment. I ordered Pho Ga.. The food was very fresh and it was delicious.. The service and the food was superb. We will definitely back. I strongly recommend this establishment.

A really nice change from the usual, and is it tasty! I've been there a few times, and I'm always quite happy with what I've gotten. The creamiest, most tasty hummus I've ever had. One time the falafel was a bit overdone (but not horribly so), and there is one lamb dish that doesn't specify that the lamb is pre-ground before cooking which was a different texture than I was looking for that night. And while I'm a huge fan of baklava, every time I ask for some they're already out. Which I suppose means on the plus side it's fresh, but I couldn't tell you first hand. Plus, the servers are very pleasant and warm.
Get the mofongo! Delicious! Definitely bring a jacket because it gets a bit chilly inside.

Finally got to try this place (with a living social deal) Parked right out front and had a nice pre theatre dinner, We had attentive service (contrary to the other reviewers) and the food arrived quickly. Other diners and take out customers were also served promptly. Tried the barbecue chicken ( I was too chicken to go for the jerk) and the curried goat roti - good but sloppy. we will definitely go back- hubby wants to work his way through the menu.
By far the best gyros in town. Worth the drive from Columbia. This is not a chain restaurant. Friendly workers and the taziki sauce tastes like it was a grandma recipe.

I love this place so so much. This is by far my favorite food truck. Its so creative and delicious and the owners are so nice. They give my friend and I free thai tea all the time just because. Thai Mexican? So delicious. When I lived by here, I would beg my roommate to go every week. We both craved it constantly. any taco is fantastic there. chicken satay or short rib? yum! They have a captain crunch burrito that is huge and tasty. I'm mad I don't have one right now while I'm writing this. Even the veggie burger is fantastic there. No body whose been here has ever been disappointed. The spicy sauce and toppings just make it.

I stopped here after hiking one day, and thought I'd try a gyro salad. The employee behind the counter seemed a little less than enthusiastic about being there, but I figured on a nice day, why would anyone want to be stuck at work? So I tried to engage him. It it just didn't really work. That's ok, I figured I'd enjoy the salad at least. The patio is outside, facing the parking lot, and it's as nice as a patio facing a parking lot can be, actually a little removed from the frat of traffic, etcetera. My gyro meat, however, was a tiny bit on the dry side and I just didn't get that amazing flavor that a gyro should have. The rest of the salad was fine, fresh, and pretty much what you'd expect. Between the lack of flavor and the lack of fun from the service, I'm not likely to return.

Just enjoyed a great dinner with my daughter. If you're looking for ambiance you may be disappointed. However, if you're looking for good Indian cuisine at prices where you can afford to experiment drive straight to Zaika's NOW!!! The place was empty except for 2 women waiting for take out. Apparently they do a great take out business but I'd rather eat in and enjoy the food straight from the kitchen. The server was helpful with questions...I think she is the owner's daughter. My daughter and I indulged in aloo tikki, garlic naan, beef & chicken kebabs, shrimp biryani, tandoori chicken and chicken tikki masala. Hopefully I spelled everything correctly!! Everything had great flavors and was just as we ordered...medium spicy. The next time and there will be a next time we will experiment a little more and try the next heat level up!!
I love this place. The food is outstanding as well as the service. It's a nice quiet laid back place. It's a great place for a romantic date. I love the decor.
Delicious food, excellent chef, and May is awesome. Delicious shrimp in blankets and pad thao.

Hard working family has made this a popular dining spot in the Park for almost 20 years. Simple decor but great food and excellent value. Chinese dishes are great and the staff will go out of their way to accommodate your needs.

I ordered take out from here, staff was friendly and I did not have to wait too long. The mango lassi and mixed pakoras were fresh and definitely better than most indian restaurants in the NE area. However, the lamb samosas were not what I expected. You could barely tell that it was a lamb samosa as it was minimal amount of lamb and more potatoes. I will definitely not be getting that again. Also the wait staff could have been a little bit more clean between cleaning off tables from a large party and handling money and then wiping his hand on a table cloth to deal with checking my order and preparing the lassi.

Too, too great. Their lunch buffet can't be beat, and dinner is decently priced. Had the chicken vindaloo and it's pretty damn sweet. Service is impeccable there. The location is a bit unexpected, it's attached to a hotel. Can be missed if you're not looking out for it. I am going to ask my partner to take me there again.

I've been here twice now- I really like the atmosphere here. Apparently everything is imported from Turkey. The hookah was nicer than some I've had in Indy-better quality and smoother. We came here on a Sunday evening, so it wasn't very busy, but we'll be back on a weekend to check it out. They also have a hookah garden- cool place right next to Bosphorus. Service can be slow but that just adds to the European authenticity ha!

Delicious food, friendly staff, nice ambience. We had the Lamb Saag and the Chicken Korma, both with just the right amount of spiciness. The two entrees gave the two of us plenty to take home for another meal. We shall return!

Just had the Sushi Sashimi combo. Not only pretty to look at but absolutely delicious. My husband had the Seafood Teriyaki which he sad was very good. Second time we had dinner here and we will be back for more.
Fantastic authentic Thai! Super happy they opened up. I've been three times in one week! Highly recommended. Staff is friendly and the food is fresh, flavorful and ready very quickly.

I personally like my Thai a bit hotter than this place tends to make it, but the food is still excellent regardless of what I order. I return here all the time because the service is excellent and the atmosphere is perfect. 4 out of 5 for great food less hot than I'd like, plus 1 for all the other awesome stuff about this place.
Best fish marsala I've ever had. We tend to visit this restaurant once a month and always pleased with our meals.
We have been back to this place a few times since our initial visit. It's awesome. The food is good. Place is clean. Service is personable. Try everything on the menu, you won't regret it.

My review is solely based on thier Happy Hour, so if you're looking for a lunch/dinner/full dining experience, move on to the next review. I live close by and come here more often than I should, but not as much as often I should... Sounds a little confusing, but when I say "$3 WINE" it should all make sense?!?! Can't beat it! They have a great menu of Happy Hour specials filled with drinks and food! Lots of wine & cocktail specials for under $5, which is a great deal, espcially that $3 wine! The food I've had has only been off of the Happy Hour menu, but it has been delicious! Flatbreads are pretty good, on par with other Happy Hour flatbreads, nothing spectacular though. Pita & Hummus is my go-to... always good & refreshing, never a disappointment! The fish tacos are pretty good. The shell is almost deep-fried, not my cup of tea, so I just eat the fish and toppings with a fork, but oh my they are delicious! Patio area is small, but great when you get a seat! Service is so-so, but when you're there for Happy Hour, you shouldn't expect the best service. Overall, it is definitely something for everyone to try out... I mean this should have captivated you after I said "$3 wine!" ENJOY!

fast casual upscale Mediterranean, plus smoothies and bubble tea. free (and really fast) wifi. small owner run business in a new strip mall off Nolensville Road. This is south of Old Hickory Blvd just inside the Davidson County line. Bricks restaurant is in the same plaza, Kroger & Publix are just down the street. Brand new space, very clean. Kitchen is open in the space, nothing to hide here. Serving a variety of normal Mediterranean foods - gyro, chicken, dolmas, hummous, tabouli - plus some other more creative options. Variety of salads (including one with salmon) available. Basic gyro (lamb/beef or chicken) comes with homemade potato chips instead of fries -- didn't actually see any fries on the menu. That probably tells you something about the place. I'm a big fan of Mediterranean food & know a lot of places that serve the $4 or $5 gyro/fries combo - it's almost just a greek style McD's combo meal. This is not that place. Gyro sandwiches are made with higher quality (less greasy) meat, lettuce is romaine instead of iceberg lettuce, etc. Prices are a little higher but you're seeing better quality, too. On my 2nd visit I asked to sub tabouli for the chips. Tabouli had lots of bulgar and even chunks of cucumber mixed in - good stuff. In the top 5 of tabouli/tabbouleh that I've tried around Nashville. Stop by, give it a try, support your local business!

The food was great, but the servings were slightly small. The spot was kind of hidden from the street. You'd have to go underground to find the place. But the food here definitely worth trying! Xiaolongbao are great :)

I've been there several times. I think the place has gone downhill a lot. The buffet is okay. None of the items is exceptional, but you can take a much as you want for a reasonable price. I find the food a bit blend though, and often to cold. The a la carte items are wat overpriced in my opinion. The first time I came here, the restaurant still had the old interior. It gave the place a warmer atmosphere. Many people visited the place. One day, the owner decides to upgrade his interior to something with blue and white light. These colors probably work well in India, but in the West these are considered cold colors. It makes the place look like a butcher. Ever since, I have rarely seen more than two occupied tables here. My recommendation to the owner would therefore be that he restores the old interior.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Awesome food! The chefs are actually from India. Authentic naan, tandoori, tikka dishes, etc. The rice pudding is fantastic as a dessert. The service has always been a little slow, but the food is worth it.
Very good Carne Frita! Went there a couple a days ago and loved it. Good service, food was delicious. I had the Carne Frita with Mofongo and OMG I felt right at home. Great place to visit.

Big fan of this spot. The lunch specials are out of this world, for real. for $10, I got a super authentic, amazing tamarind juice, homemade (too good, too fresh), a fat fat plate of red beans and yellow rice, and two big pieces of marinated, tender, sauced up chicken breast. Service was fast, and the dude who runs the place was super nice. I'm a super white dude, and my girlfriend is spanish, and fluent, so he was loving how much of a gringo I was. I don't blame him, lol. He was a good guy. Overall, nice ambiance, great location, great service, and super good food. Will for sure, 100%, no doubt be back.

I stopped by Remedy Cafe for a late-night snack and coffee with a friend. The crowd is hip and young - a lot of university students finishing papers (free wi-fi!) and chatting philosophy. It's a great place to do some people watching. I tried a vegan coconut chicken dish, which I wouldn't order again (points lost for its weird veggie texture), but the desserts here are to-die-for. Each cake and pie gets its own clever name, such as "Fudge Judy." I would recommend Remedy for its lattes and atmosphere, but I would stick to desserts only next time.

Taziki's catered my wedding on June 10, 2017 and the food was nothing short of amazing! The staff were so polite and did a fantastic job. Olivia and Renae were in charge of the everything and they are the best people to work with! They were so helpful and sweet, and did exactly what I wanted for my wedding. I highly recommend them for catering services.
yeah, this spot is legit. Go there and feed your kabob cravin' the staff is friendly and nice. Its not a quick in-out place. Give yourself 30-45min if you wanna sit down..

This restaurant is a hidden gem. Boyfriend and I went for dinner tonight, he had Jerk Chicken, I had Curry Chicken and they were both tender and very tasty. His cabbage side dish was really good, cooked cabbage but with a hint of vinegar. I had the plantains which were insanely sweet and we both enjoyed the beans and rice that came with. I will be going back for their Puri on Friday and Saturday which they have with Channa and potatoes, another favorite of mine.
Good Indian food steps away, small place but good food. The biryanis, malai kofta and kerela chicken were good spicy flavor. Quick to serve

Came here for lunch on a weekend, they have a lunch special that cost just under $10 with your choice of soup, appetizer, and main course. I had their Tom Yum Soup - it was spicy with a lot of veges which I liked. My friend had their coconut soup which I felt was a little on the sweet side. I had steamed vegetable dumplings - nothing special there. My friend had chicken skewers and we both really enjoyed their peanut sauce. Our main lunch meal was pad thai. I had leftovers after, it has a lot more vegetables than most chicken pad thai places I've had before. Small, quiet and cute. A little pricey but portions were definitely worth the price.

It's pretty good I thought my food tasted like onions and my boyfriends did too if u don't want to spend your whole check on Chinese food I would suggest goin to Lisa's great food great customer service I just didn't like it

Pretty good, especially for vegetarians; most of the meat dishes are chicken and lamb. Spicing is medium-medium hot. Flavors are especially good. Drinks are somewhat limited; no de-chai, as an example. I've eaten from the menu, but was also surprised today at the buffet, which was very good with lots of variety, and also quite flavorful. The downside: the basmati rice was hard, and might break a filling if they don't do something about changing it out. Too bad about that, because the rest of the food in the buffet was superlative today-- hot, flavorful, and just very, very good with good variety. Too bad it the rice was so uneven. They might do better with more desserts, but we were truly full before the desserts were even thought of. The buffet also comes with naan, and we chose garlic naan that's also heavily spiced with cilantro. In all, nothing to apologize for save limited drink selection and occasionally hard buffet rice. Good for a large party, as well.

I'm all for forgiving small, quirky restaurants for poor service or unpleasant environments as long as the food is really special. It's the reason a lot of "hole-in-the-wall" places stay in business, because you don't go there for anything but amazing, unique food. Basil Spice Thai... is not that kind of place. Don't get me wrong, the food (or at least some of it) was pretty good, but not good enough to make up for the terrible service we got. The first warning sign came when we sat down and were (after a longer-than-usual wait) given our menus. They had wooden covers with Thai images (like an elephant or a shiva) on them. Maybe these covers were once pretty or interesting, but at a table of six only one of us had an intact menu. My image was completely gone, with only a glue stump left - others just had limbs, heads, and tusks broken off. It was actually pretty impressively bad. I will say that the food on the menu looked interesting, with a lot beyond the standard Pad Thai fare. After that, we spend a long time looking around waiting for our server to show up. Eventually we had to go to the desk to ask where our server was. When we finally got a server we ordered a bottle of wine for the table, which also took way too long to arrive. Our food also arrived in a bizarre manner. I have no idea why, but our server kept bringing each dish to me first, actually placing on the table in front of me, then asking who had ordered it. This happened at least twice. I ordered a vegetarian dish, and I repeatedly had to point away meat dishes. It was bizarre and off-putting. Our food also came out oddly paced, so that those who got their food had to sit for several minutes while everyone else's came out too. It all just seemed sloppy and hectic, really poorly done. I actually enjoyed my food, a vegetarian special, because it was different from most other Thai I've had. It was also just the right level of spicy for me (a 2 on a 1-5 spicy scale, per the waiter). Unfortunately one of my friends also ordered a level 2 spicy dish, but hers was waaaay too spicy. So much so that she had trouble eating it. Really a disappointment. Rinse and repeat the slow service when it came time for our check. Maybe try take out next time? At least that'd help the service. Not sure what to do about the spicy problem though. Overall, a very underwhelming experience.

After waiting over a hour and a half for my food, the chicken in my pad Thai was raw! I called and spoke with the "manager" who told me the food is good. Umm no sir the food is not good, you served me raw meat! I asked for my money back and he said "you didn't pay me, you paid yelp online. Call them". Never again!!

Staff is super nice and genuinely care about their customers. I've had their Plato's delight (amazing), Lentil bisque (very good but I like my soups with more of a chunky fill then blended but still tasty), delicious and light falafels with yummy Laban sauce and their marinated chicken is so tender and flavorful! I've had several smoothies and they're all good as well as their bubble teas. I highly recommend trying this place if you're anywhere near it. Always fresh and reasonably priced
Found some tasty Pho and will return to try other menu items. The restaurant is very clean and staff very friendly.

This is especially hard for me to say as a Jamaican American. I've been to this place a number of times and each time they seem to disappoint in a new way. During my most recent visit, I hoped to satisfy my urge for a Beef Patty and Coco Bread in timely manner. But that was not to be the case. It took 30 minutes for my order to get to me. 30 MINUTES!!!! I can understand if the place was packed but it wasn't. 30 minutes is far too long for an entree to reach the table let alone an appetizer of this small size. As, I said before Im a Jamaican American who has been eating Patty's and Coco Bread since I can remember, about the same time most people here in America remember eating there 1st chicken nugget from Mc Donalds. Never have I eaten a Beef Patty and Coco bread sliced into thirds. When we questioned the server about the way the meal was presented to us, he nervously explained that is the manner in which the cook "makes" it. In the back of my mind makes beans taken out of the Tower Isle box from the frozen food section placed in an oven and then on to a plate. I get the sneaking suspicion that this cook sliced the patties to avoid from giving me the correct amount of patties I had asked for. This was the case for my friend who happened to order more patties than I did. This was the last time I will give the Jerk Hut my business.

This was the only Thai place on EatGrubGo.com for delivery. My office (10 people total) were all looking forward to Thai food! However, most of us were more than a little disappointed. I ordered the Crab Rangoon and the Curry Noodle. The Crab Rangoon had very little stuffing in it and was essentially tasteless. Most restaurants have a 1/2 to 1/2 ratio of wanton to stuffing, this didn't even come close. The Curry Noodle dish would have been decent, however, the noodles were terribly overcooked. I absolutely love rice noodle dishes, but these were so limp and tasteless I ended up throwing away most of the meal. No one in my office would recommend Rearn Thai.

On the week I moved into my place, I went to La Va and grabbed a cup of coffee. I then proceeded to reach into my pocket and realized I had forgotten my wallet at home while unpacking. Looking really stupid, I apologized and said I would run home and get the money and return right away. The response was a relaxed 'Welcome to the neighborhood, you can get us next time'. Having grown up in a very small town in Vermont, this is something that was common to my youth but nothing like my experiences in Philadelphia. I knew that I had moved to the right location and that I was going to be a regular at La Va. I've now lived in the area for over 6 years and I've been to La Va a few hundred times I guess. The people are great and I've had some great random experiences while getting coffee. One day I walked in to get a coffee and just as I was about to walk out the skies opened up and it started pouring. I decided to just relax and sit down for a minute. I ended up meeting a great couple and we talked for almost an hour. La Va is a place that feels comfortable, so talking to a complete stranger doesn't really seem all that odd. It's not a feeling you get going into a Starbucks or other mainstream coffee shops and besides the great coffee, is another reason I choose to support my local coffee shop. Look forward to trying out the dinner menu soon, lots of great reviews here so I'm sure I will not be disappointed. Thanks for all the caffeine La Va!
Ordered a smoothie and it had huge chunks of ice in it making it almost un drinkable, would not recommend
There's a pretty good quizzo here Thursday nights at 8:30, which takes over the entire back booth area and can get pretty packed. The beers remain welcomingly inexpensive (like $3 Yuenglings).

I judge Vietnamese restaurants by their Bun Thit Nuong and not their Pho--and Pho 79 has the best Bun Thit Nuong in Boise. I've certainly had better, but not here and when I'm craving it this is where i go. I'm not sure what to say about all these 1 star reviews, but if you know the difference between Bun and Pho then this place is probably worth checking out.

Wow. It was my first time here and I'm so impressed. A lot of the Thai restaurants are chain like in the Indy area and basically the food tastes the same no matter what Thai restaurant you go to. This is not the case here at all. Food tasted fresh and delicious. Service was also pretty good and the waitress was nice. The ambience was excellent as well, nice seating. I very much so enjoyed myself here and will definitely be back. I recommend this to anyone in the mood for Thai food!
Website and yelp both say the restaurant delivers. I called to order and they do not. Update your information please
Best puertorican restaurant in the west side of Florida. Great service and good music.

Love this place! Not reallly sure how long I've been coming to this place but I really like their chicken shawrma and gyros. It's another alternative to late night food besides Lucky dogs, Krystal burger or pizza and I'm pretty sure it's probably better for you. I ran into this place randomly one night years ago and haven't stopped coming since. I've converted several of my late night pizza eating friends into gyro eaters. The owners are always really nice and your food is fresh and is usually ready pretty quick.
Been here several times and is always tasty! The staff is friendly and the buffet is reasonably priced. I especially like the Naan and samosas.

My friend and I went there on 3/21/2014. I gave one star because the food was good but the service sucked. The waitress was incredibly rude through out the entire time we were there. We were sitting in the booth shortly after we paid, she came to us and said " I need the table" while there were plenty of empty seats in the restaurant and kicked us out of the restaurant.
Drunken noodles were delicious and the staff was very friendly. It was my first time there and will be going back.

Never in my life did I think I would enjoy Thai food, but I am so glad I gave it a shot. I am never disappointed with the food here. Maybe it's because I always get the same dish (Pad Thai), but maybe because the food is just that good?!?! I have only dined in once for lunch, but the other visits typically require picking up food to go so I can get back to the office in time for more work. I am not one to enjoy spicy food and so I always order non-spicy and every time I get it just that way. No Spice at all. Just the way I like it. Usually when I go out to eat I say not spicy and I still get some spice, but the kitchen actually listens here and I appreciate that! I will continue to go back again and again.
This place has been around for many years and has always been absolutely superb. Try everything on the menu!

I guarantee you will not have eaten falafels like this. The food is VERY unique. The guy uses a variety of different vegetables and sure knows how to blend the taste with these unique ingredients. For $10 you get a HUGE amount of food. I eat a lot but still couldn't finish it. It's definitely enough food for 2 people.
Pad thai had strong ketchup taste, roti was ok, and thai tea was a little too sweet. Read the reviews and expected alot more.

I could barely contain my excitement on my way to Greko Greek Street Food. Walking into the restaurant I was faced with a menu on the wall full of wonderful choices from Athenian lamb to octopus skewers. Being someone who just had to try everything I ordered a good amount of food. I was let down to the highest degree. I got 2 different pitas, chicken and lamb. They were okay, run of the the mill pitas that I could anywhere. Nothing special that blew my underpants away. I also got the half chicken. If anything this was the best bite of the night. The chicken was incredibly tender while the glaze complemented it nicely, only complaint would be the skin was too flabby. Finally the octopus skewer and the fries. To say underwhelming would be an understatement. The fries couldn't of been more disappointing, just nothing really much standing out here. As a side that goes with everything at least make it enjoyable. I would say the octopus was my least favorite. It came out Luke warm and the texture and flavor was not very good. I have had octopus over a dozen times and this was the worst I've tasted. All in all I would say I was disappointed with experience with Greko Greek Street Food.

I love this place. They have a limited menu of about 8 sandwiches but they are delicious. My favorite is the vegetarian hoagie for $4. The sandwiches are on a crunchy roll that will leave a mess if you try eating it in your car but is well worth the mess. The veggies and whatever they season them with are so yummy and different than anything you would find in an American deli or hoagie shop. The sandwiches aren't that big but then again they are only about $4. This is a total hole in the wall and there are a couple of cramped tables and chairs in the corners when you walk in so I always order and then take it home or walk to the park and eat it. And I love that this is a family shop and the older couple with broken English that owns it are so cute. This is one of my favorite hidden gems in the Italian Market area. The only thing I would change is the hours. They have some strange hours that change throughout the week but close around 6pm give or take an hour or so. I often crave a Vietnamese hoagie for dinner but don't get home in time to grab one before they close. And they closed for about a month or more over the spring/ summer.

We live in Mammoth Lakes and travel to Reno somewhat frequently for shopping trips. We've been to a few of the other highly rated restaurants for Pho, but SF Kitchen has to be our favorite! The Bun bo Hue is to die for! The Pho broth is just amazing. Simple and aromatic. We also really enjoyed their spring rolls. We've resisted this restaurant a few times, and always intend to try something new but one of us always ends up ordering Bun Bo Hue :) If you need a great soup fix, try this place!
We ordered Pad Thai, shrimp rolls, fried dumplings and fried pork chops. It was staggeringly good. I would not hesitate to order, nor would I hesitate to recommend it to others.

Terrible. I ordered an oxtail, and it only came with 3 pieces (barley any meat on the bone) - when I asked for more, considering I paid $15 for the meal, the lady added 1 small piece to my plate. The food tasted cold, and old. I will never come back to this restaurant again. Plenty of alternatives in the area, don't waste your money!!

Have been here at least 6 times since opening. Food remains consistently good. Our only complaint in the past has been lighting so dim that we needed the Flashlight app on our phones to read the menu. The room has been brightened a bit, so that problem is resolved. We love the food and will be back many times again. We are not alone in our love for this place: even midweek finds the place quite busy at dinner.

Made reservations for dinner Lundi Gras about two weeks prior and was not told they had a limited menu. Showed up and had small plates instead. Crab cakes and jerk beef skewers were our choices. The crab cakes were pretty good but they were served on a smear of what tasted like stale mayo. This kind of ruined it for me. The jerk skewer meat was good as well and the smear of sauce underneath was a raspberry BBQ sauce which also was pretty good. Staff was nice but then again we were pretty much the only people in the dining section. Music was very enjoyable. As another reviewer pointed out you would think they would make good mojitos but the one I ordered was BAD. The worse I ever had. A skinny glass halfway filled with whole mint leaves with the liquor on top. YECH, With so many wonderful places in the Marigny to eat I would recommend you go somewhere else for dinner and just buy a couple of beers and listen to the music here.
My favorite local Thai restaurant. The flavors are excellent, the traditional Thai decor makes for a great dining experience and service has always been quick & friendly.

Ordered takeout from inside - asked the guys up front for a their recommendations. They were nice and hooked me up, sent with the chicken curry (medium). Loved the food, and service. PS medium was really spicy, and I like spicy, hot may be hard to enjoy.

My fascination is over. They no longer make my favorite drink, the Vesper Rose. My favorite bartenders were not there, in fact, it seemed like all new staff. I haven't been in a few months so it could very well be. Don't get me wrong everyone was pleasant but, the experience wasn't the same and the food wasn't quite as good. I'll probably go back again but it will no longer be the only stop when I'm in town for work.

I love this place. The soup is my favorite. Everything thing we've tried we've loved. Family owned, not a chain. Great food and service. We keep coming back again and again. The spring rolls are also a must have.

Moving to this neighborhood from our old Kensington wasteland has led to almost daily "wow, this is great" moments. Having Coffee shop(s) is one that lands in my top ten. La. Va is the closest and thus the first one I've really felt a connection to. It's a cozy place, La Colombe coffee gets a huge thumbs up from me and the breakfast sandwiches are the best I've had, bar none. Good pasty assortment as well. I really want to get in there to try some of the lunch or dinner offerings.

Clean decor, tasty pho, delicious mung bean smoothies, reasonable pricetag for two -------- Now don't take this the wrong way, but I wonder how this place is a franchise? I mean, do they license out their own brand of nuoc nom (fish sauce), or their specific brand of Monosodium glutamate for the soup base? They have franchises as far away as Canada and Alabama. No matter, the decor was nice and clean (as was the bathroom, A+!), and their beef meatballs had a good amount of "snap". Not bad for Philly Pho. Worth coming back.
Best Thai in Nash! Incredibly friendly service and always delicious meals. The kind of restaurant you put in your regular rotation.

The atmosphere is amazing! I love the decor. And the food is even better. I had the gin cider cocktail (amazing)! white pizza to start, it's a wood burning oven, my fav. The calamari and seared brussel sprouts... all highly recommended! The service was excellent, the owner Anthony came to check on us and was very friendly.

Pros: Fast servce Wide vareity Decent tableware Cons: Bland, Americanized renditions of Vietnamese food Bland, bland, bland I miss really good pho. And spring rolls. I'm guessing the clientele that frequents this place are people who don't like spicy, or spices that would be used in any decent Vietnamese restaurant. Or, they live/work nearby. In either case, I was really sad after my meal, especially because we went to see 'The Blind Side' afterward. Dammit - that's just money lost to mediocre all the way around.

I have frequented this location many times with co-workers, and have always enjoyed what I ordered. The service is good and food is usually served fairy quickly. The times I have been have usually been with a party of 7 or more, so there have been a few times where the wait was a little bit longer than desired, and checking out this many individual checks can be agonizing...but still it was worth it. I have never had their sushi, but I have had, and enjoyed, the Red Curry, Green Curry, Pineapple Curry, Spicy Noodles, Fried Rice, and the Spring Rolls.

What is up with this place???? One day I was charged one price, which according to their menu is the correct price. The next day the EXACT same order is higher and when pointed out to staff, they have no explanation AND DO NOTHING about it. Oh, and what is up with the guy who works in the afternoon, he wears the same clothes day after day and can barely mumble a word. Save the time and annoyance, go elsewhere.
Great restaurant, was just passing by going to get gas and saw this restaurant with 5 stars reviews so decided to try it and were amazed how good the food was...highly recommend this place to anyone

It's funny, this has been a favorite lunch spot for years (like 8 or 9), and I never reviewed it. Taste of India has one of the better Indian buffets in the area. It has a number of vegan and/or vegetarian dishes, a nice selection of Indian salad options, and at least 4-5 dishes containing meat (most likely chicken, goat and fish sometimes). The buffet is kept well and it's rare to see an empty or almost empty tray. I wish the naan was a bit better, but otherwise I have few complaints with the buffet. Mango lassi is complimentary with buffet, but I'm not one for that. They have always been more expensive compared to other Indian buffets nearby, maybe by a dollar or two. But they just recently upped the buffet price to $14.95 on a weekday ($15.95 on weekends). Personally I think that is too much to routinely to dole out for lunch, and I'm not one who is able take advantage of a buffet. I'm done after one go. But I'll still go occasionally as a special treat.
We've been here a few times for their lunch buffet, dine-in, and take outs. Food is consistently good every time and service is always great!

I've only visited for the lunch buffet but I was pleasantly surprised by the large selection and so many vegetarian choices. The salad portion was somewhat limited but I don't imagine that is a huge priority for most folks when it comes to an Indian buffet. I've seen others mention the palak paneer and it was definitely tasty and smooth. Items did seem to be on the spicy side so this might be a concern if you don't prefer your Indian food to have a lot of spice but I prefer bold flavors. The restaurant itself was clean, big enough for a group, and the staff was friendly enough. I didn't want for anything. I think the choice of plain vs garlic naan that is brought to your table is also a really nice touch. I'll definitely be back and am thinking about bringing a group from work since they had such a good varied selection.

My oh my what a surprisingly wonderful place. The service was excellent the food amazing and the ambiance took me back to my favorite place in the world my little nook In a crook PR. We started off with the alcapurrias and ahrip de Casona was excellent. My husband and his uncle had a mofongo de camarones they said it was the best they ever had. My son had a shrip in garlic sauce and I had the chxn in garlic sauce simply amazing. The toatones were fresh everything was truly out of this world. This place is one of those places when in florida you have to come to visit. 15 Stars we will be back soon!

The seasonings were impeccable, the flavors divine. If somebody is reading this and thinking 'oh, i'd like to go there!' message me and we can just jet off and go. It's that good. I've only had better Ethiopian in Boston, but come on, I can't just hop over to Boston for some Ethiopian grub. DONT BE RIDICULOUS! Some of my former co-workers were Ethiopian and they would bring in food to share. This place and their cooking tasted so similar that it left me nostalgic for hospital breakrooms. Plus, eating with your hands is fun. That makes everything more fun.

Gyros Deluxe, with a Greek salad...OMG(oodness). Fresh food, which taste great, at a good price. Don't let the external appearance of the business deceive you, cause you will miss out on some fabulous Greek food.

I went to Ottolenghi not that long ago and if I could only return to one, I think I might pick Suraya. The cocktails and grape leaves were merely good, otherwise the food is beyond excellent. Particular favorites include the muhammara, fried mushrooms, and chickpea and eggplant. The fresh pita that come with everything is a perfect vehicle for corralling the multitudinous meze you will order here. The interior is very well designed and seems like it would be a comfortable place to enjoy a meal at any time of day.

This was a perfectly fine, but not stellar thai meal. I have heard their spring rolls are delicious but sell out quickly. Since we arrived at 2:30, however, we just had the regular fare. It was pretty tasty and a good lunch. I like the NO twist of crawfish in the curry thai vermicelli.
The best Caribbean food in Delaware everything is amazing!!! Can't go wrong with anything on the menu!!!

Beware--if you put this into your Garmin or Tom Tom it will take you to Singha Thai, which is a completely different location. I have eaten in once and ordered out once from this location. It always appears very slow and it makes me sad that they don't have many customers. When I ask "how is business?" they always give me depressing looks and responses like "could be better". Do not hold the emptiness of their dining room against them. The food here is delicious. It is on par with LA Thai for sure--I think the stupid name may be hurting business here. This is located on a street with many other restaurants and it is hard to lure people into a Thai place when it sounds like the staff will sing you a song instead of take your order. I ask for my food spicy at Thai restaurants and this one, along with LA Thai obliges. My server laughed when my face was red and refilled my water two or three times. I don't know why I always do that. I feel more alive when my food fights back. It's a primal thing. The decor is really nice and everything is very clean. It is a beautiful building that probably made someone a gorgeous home at one point. I really hope these folks can stay in business. Go support them!
One of the best gyros I've had. I love the Philly style gyro. They have a bunch of different types of gyros too. Very filling with lots of meat and cheese and veggies.

My family and I are vegetarian and always on the hunt for different, more exotic vegetarian cuisine. We pass the Queen of Sheba restaurant on a regular basis and, after checking the menu on-line, decided to go for a rare evening out. The restaurant is in a small plaza on the West side of Henderson and does not have a very impressive entrance. The small, older strip plaza looks like it's seen better days and parking was a little confusing. Once inside though, we were constantly entertained! This is genuinely an Ethiopian family restaurant. There were children who obviously belonged to the waitress or one of the owners running back and forth and playing out in the dining room - they were adorable. The artwork is all Ethiopian as well. The colors and symbolism may remind you of a Jamaican place, or maybe a Bob Marley album, but that's just because Ethiopia is the homeland of the Rastafari, but that is the only similarity. The food was definitely different, reminiscent of Indian food more than anything else I've had. It was just okay, but the novelty of the atmosphere and the people make it worth the visit.

I was excited to try the lunch buffet. The atmosphere was really nice and the food was great. There were many vegetarian/vegan options. I do wish there would have been labels on the food so I could remember whats what. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask the staff. They're really nice and will give you any information you need. I thought it was interesting that they had forks out at the buffet, I had never seen this before at an Ethiopian restaurant. Most people there were using forks, but I think the traditional way to eat Ethiopian cuisine is by using your hands to scoop food into the bread (injera). So that's what I did :) I'd suggest getting a couple of different plates of food and eating this way instead of trying to put everything on one plate. I also ordered coffee which was served in the cutest little cup/saucer. It was good, strong. All you can eat for $10 isn't bad at all, but if you don't eat a lot you might be ok with something from the menu or a combo platter.

Bad experience. Dosa Hut was my favorite Indian place, but I am sorry to day that the food quality and service had declined considerably. I went along with 5 friends, and they all felt the same way. Food arrived after 1 hour and the main course was served along with the appetizer for the entire table. On the top of that the egg biryani was cold and tasteless. The only savior was gobi manchurian, but even that was soggy and below par. Regarding the service, the server bluntly blamed the crowd. When I asked him how the table that came after us got their food before us he ignored us. When we mentioned that the biryani is cold he offered to heat it up in the microwave.
Fantastic authentic Cuban cuisine. Service was fast and very friendly. Menu was diverse and reasonably priced. Will definitely go back!

For a $9 buffet lunch, Tandoor is pretty good. I really like palak and it was pretty decent here. Their samosas weren't bad either. Fellow diner enjoyed the chicken. She had been a frequent customer a number of years ago and everybody working remembered her and was extremely friendly. The actual restaurant and buffet display leaves a lot to be desired. I felt a little gnarly all day after eating here. BUT, for a once a year cheap indian buffet lunch, I'd go back for the annual visit.

Nice food, but not the best I've ever had in terms of Ethiopian cuisine. The flavors were nice, the bread just a bit too dry for me. The placed was almost full of ppl which is a good sign. The service was nice. The ppl working here are very sweet bringing big smiles with them to each customer.
I called at 5:30 on a Saturday and was told they were open until 8. I showed up at 7 and the place was totally locked up!

Finally!!! A good middle eastern restaurant in Boise. Yeepee. OK. So the "menu" (Laminated paper with 4 pictures), is simple: Chicken Shawarma, Falafel, Lamb Kebab, Beef Kebab, but the food is exactly the opposite, rich and wonderful. Tender meat, spices and flavors in the perfect combination. The flat bread and the Pita and a cause for celebration by their own account. Each meal comes with Hummus, Baba Ganush and Eggplant salad. For drink, grab what you desire from the fridge next to the door. I'm taking one star because the place still doesn't have the restaurant feel, but the food is nothing but AWESOME! You crave for a testy, zesty, crafty meal, head over. Make sure you're hungry!

We've actually been to Thailand, and this tastes just like home. I'm so glad we found this place. The people are super friendly too. We will be back! Thank youuuu! FYI: they offer indoor and outdoor seating.
A little pricey for lunch, but the Bamboo Special was delicious and certainly healthier than most alternatives. Will visit again.

delicious food! I live in media and this is a great, low key spot to go. It fills up on the weekends but definitely worth the wait. the servers are usually pretty attentive but sometimes they take a little long to get your wine open/place order. I always order the spicy noodle with shrimp and get extra veggies - best entree!! It's a BYOB, so that's always great. I would recommend them over other places in town.

We went with a decent size party and we're able to try a few different dishes they had to offer. Ever single one of them was unbelievably good. I highly recommend this place and we will definitely be back!

One of the most authentic Thai places I've been to here in Nashville. Their food is delicious, their customer service is great, and the prices are affordable. My family and I tried a little bit of everything because we were excited to see just how good this place was. We got the shrimp green curry, Pad Thai, fried calamari, Tom yum, Tom kha, and their shrimp fried rice. All of these dishes were up to par in comparison to California where we are from. The Tom yum and Tom kha was served in a small bowl instead of that pot with fire that they usually come with. It was perfect for us though because we got to try them both for only $3.95 each instead of the usual $10+. We also got Thai iced tea and Thai iced green tea. The drinks were good but a little on the sweeter than what we're used to. With all of that said, I love this place so I'm giving it 5 stars!

Very good spicy noodles and green curry! I have eaten here for lunch and dinner in the same week. The food is always fresh, hot and delicious. The service is friendly and always filling up our water glass. So glad they open a second location in Goleta now we won't have to travel to the mesa for good Thai food. We will be back!

Very disappointing. I ordered an eggplant dish that I have eaten at other Indian restaurants with nice sized pieces of eggplant. Only, palace of asia's version had the eggplant mushed up like baby food. The description of the dish was misleading. Very disappointing. I will be sticking to cross culture in haddonfield from now on.

Take your girlfriend here. She will love you forever. Try the stuffed talapia. Or the Panang. Or the pineapple fried rice. Great menu, plenty of vegetarian options, and plenty of spice! Good prices too. Take your date here. She'll be impressed and you wont break the bank.

Ordered the beef krapao and the papaya salad and I have to say it was the worst I've ever had. I ate a lot of Thai food but this was by far the worst. The jasmine rice was dry and hard. The papaya salad had no flavor at all. Definitely not order from here again.

This was pretty great. Not fancy decor at all. The food was good. They made me vegetarian spring rolls. I could have eaten these forever. I also had some vegetarian pho. This too was good. Very refreshing on a cold day. Every table in the restaurant was full so this is a popular place. We will return.

We met a couple of friends here and had drinks and snacks. It's a pretty cool looking restaurant with the glazed brick and garage door of the old service station as well as industrial-looking fixtures and seating. My husband. The mixed drinks were good as were the Mediterranean tapas. We had a hummus plate, some spicy carrots, a dish with seasoned ground beef on a pita (my husband's favorite), and smoked trout on toast (probably my favorite). Oh, and their "famous" egg salad which had a lemony flavor to it that I liked quite a bit. They don't have a lot of large plate options, so I wouldn't recommend it for dinner if you're very hungry, but it would be a good lunch spot if you work in the area.

This place is the real deal! Such a fun atmosphere! As soon as you walk in you're greeted with the very energetic and welcoming staff. We got our food which was rather quickly, Especially since it was packed! Food was amazing! The fries are perfectly fried, and the meats are all cooked to perfection and filled with flavor! Pita is freshly made everyday and is off the charts! You can really tell the owners put some thought and hard work into this... would recommend to anyone, I've been back myself twice already!

I have to start this review with an Apology. Few days back I left a negative review by mistake :( I am so sorry once again. I finally got to try Thai5 today. After reading the great reviews on Yelp, I was dying to try this place. I picked up Pad Thai($10) for lunch today and by the time I got home, I was expecting oil all over the plastic bag (Thats what usually happens when I order Pad Thai from other Thai places.) When I got home, there was not a single drop of grease or oil, Nothing at all. This already was a 5 star for me. When i opened the box, the pad thai was enough for 3 people, so huge. Like all other places, they do not just pack your food on the foam container. They place a foil on the container before they pack your food, which I think is great. Pad Thai tasted very different and so much tastier than any other Thai places around. Thai being my favorite, I have tried it a lot. This Pad Thai is by far the best Pad Thai, I have ever had. Location wise, its a food truck and they do have seatings outside. I am not very sure about the inside seating. The staff were friendly and nice. I feel like 5 start is not enough for this place. If I had to break it down and rate separately, I would give Thai5 5 star on everything I have mentioned above. I am so glad to find a good Thai place nearby.
