So less oil and such great taste, AMAZING. I tried medium spicy, which was a little too spicy for me so next time I may go for Mild. I cannot wait to try everything else from Thai5. I hope the delivery service starts soon. I am one happy customer :)

Delicious banh mi sandwiches and pastries. Will return for lunch. We ate in the restaurant, but next to us was a TV showing cockfights, which was not only offensive but annoying, since it was a steady stream of Vietnamese men yelling. Would recommend that the owners change the channel, or they will lose customers.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: By far one of the friendliest and tastiest restaurants in Boise. Great atmosphere, authentic fresh food, and just a fun place to eat. Hope this place is open for decades! Best curry in town hands down.

Zagol was a wonderful discovery for our out-of-town group of five (including one teen). The food is delicious and it was served by the warm and friendly family proprietors. We chose a meat-and-vegetarian combo and enjoyed Doro Wat (spicy spicy chicken!), Bozena Shiro (tender beef stew), and the delightful vegetarian dishes of Kik Alicha and Kilkil. All were served on a "platter" of injera bread with two extra injera bread baskets on the side. The decor is colorful and lovely as well. It was great to explore this unique restaurant -- a great addition to Reno!

I'm not the one to venture to the food trucks out here in the city, but this one caught my attention. The great aroma coming from the cart just draws you in with the curiosity of no menu and many people chattering boasting how great the food is and also the man himself is unique! So i had to try it and boy I have been hooked ever since, I go two to three times a week! Also, its not really a falafel truck - you are getting mainly grilled chicken, hummas and veggies/fruits with two small falafel balls. His lines are ridiculous. The wait on average is 15 mins or so per person! He's been missing since the beginning of December, so hopefully he'll return! Anyone know where is these days?

I've been salivating over the lovely photos and reviews on Yelp, and I can say that they didn't disappoint. We've been craving this kind of food for a while, since there aren't that many offerings in NJ; I personally haven't had as satisfying food as this since I was last in the Middle East. The grilled meats were delicious, the hummus and string beans was good -- lots of cumin and veggies mixed in -- as was the rice. We ordered the mixed grill platter and the shawarma platter, and belatedly realized the shawarma would have worked better as a sandwich, but we rectified that oversight by ordering sandwiches as takeout. We were supposed to save our sandwiches for leftover lunch the next day, but on the drive back, someone couldn't help himself and ate half of his lamb shawarma sandwich. I managed to get a few bites edgewise while we were stalled in traffic, and it was great :) Can't wait to eat my sandwich today. The atmosphere was friendly with a casual college feel to it, and the owner was hospitable, offering us sweet mint tea after our meal. We've yet to try the much-lauded tagine, so we hope to be back again soon!

Great find!! The food was really good and fresh! The sweet and sour fish soup reminded me of mom's :) the green papaya salad was to die for! Hubby loved the lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowl! Can't wait to try the dessert!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: I was walking around downtown Boise and noticed Taj Mahal in big letters and decided to go try some Indian/Pakistani food. Taj Mahal didn't disappoint. They have a large list of foreign beers and a large menu. The lamb biryani I ordered was even bigger than both! And just as tasty! I recommend trying this if you're around downtown Boise.
Great food, legit Indian cuisine! Will definitely be returning often. And they take credit cards now!
Green curry is my favorite! Finally found an authentic Thai restaurant. The owner is a sweet woman as well!

What an unmitigated disaster. Went here for lunch the other day and we were not impressed, to say the least. Between two sandwiches, an iced coffee, and a hot chocolate ordered, only one item was delivered as expected, and that was the pre-made sandwich. The iced coffee was hot and then the wrong size, they forgot to put chocolate in the hot chocolate, and the BYO sandwich was missing half of the requested ingredients. The dude behind the counter was all kinds of overwhelmed despite it not being busy. The girl who joined him eventually righted most of the wrongs, but even then it took some doing. That aside, the menu is pretty good and the atmosphere is decent, apart from all the passive-aggressive little bitchy notes taped all over everything. Oh, and the pre-made sandwich was pretty lousy.

We tried take-out two nights ago from Blue Fig for the first time and everything was really good. It did feel more like a place I'd rather have take-out from rather than eating there. We had the Mezza Appetizer, Falafel Pocket, and Kid Super Bowl with Chicken The Falafel was so good and I really liked the Laban sauce. The thing I liked about the Mezza Sampler is it allows you to try several of the things from the menu. The Dolmas tasted like the ones my dad makes minus the meat and I really liked them. The hummus was good too. You can never go wrong with a little Baklava to satisfy a sweet tooth at the end of a meal. I'd definitely get takeout from Blue Fig again.
I was thinking of jerk chicken for a while. Heard of this location and ordered the large with their signature salad, rice and beans. I was so happy! Enough for 3-4 helpings. Thank you!

Great lunch here! It must be the best buy in this town. The place is elegant and comfortable. The food is excellent. The service is, I don't have the words to tell you how well the owner and staff treat you. I thoroughly agree with reviewer Antonio M.

I have been eating at Tangelo's since 2000 when they were located in Downtown St. Petersburg. Their new location in Gulf Port is a little less convenient for me, but the quality of the food is the same if not better than it was at their other location. Make no mistake, this is casual dining. But it is one of my favorite casual dining experiences. The gems on the menu are the mojo pork and mojo chicken Cubans. You may think, Cubans? Really? Trust me on this. You will find no better. And if you like it a little spicy then ask for some Matouk's hot sauce. Also, you cannot go wrong with their sweet potato fries and their (unsweetened) cinnamon iced tea. The service is generally good, but sometimes it can be slow. The people who work there are very nice though and usually have a very casual Caribbean-style attitude. If they have a pork special then you should probably try it. Pork is kind of their thing and they do it better than most. I had a pork loin topped with roasted peppers, goat cheese and some kind of reduction there once that was nothing short of incredible (unfortunately, that is not a regular menu item). In short, I love this place and every time I am in Gulf Port I make it a priority to eat here.

I just came here for the first time and I did the lunch buffet. The food was flavorful and there were plenty of options! I was very satisfied, especially because I had a lot of great food for a low price. I will definitely come back for a dinner service so I can try their prime entrees. Overall, I have nothing bad to say at all. They do Indian food the right way here.

I tried to order a gyro here and received the most disgusting sandwich I've ever tasted. This place should be ashamed to call them selves Mediterranean. I hope they go out of business befor they have a chance to continue to serve such garbage to unsuspecting people

I have to update and bump up my rating because the quality, service and yum factor is consistently great at Pho 36. I find myself craving the grilled pork banh mi, the veggie pho and the shrimp spring rolls. All ingredients are always fresh, and the employees are charming and friendly. My one complaint is that the restaurant is not big enough, but we have never had an issue with finding a table. It just seems a little cramped at times, especially on weekend nights. However, this never deters my family from visiting.

My daughter is a patient at St. Joseph's Children's Hospital and wanted some Pho' so she search Yelp for Help. Pho' An Hoa is only 3 miles away and on the same street. The Pho' had a nice flavor, and the Wonton soup was nice as well. We will keep this place in mind in the future.
Hummus and yogurt was outta the world. Meat was just so-so, though.

I am in Thai love. The hubs and I (after always talking about it) finally tried this place out about 3 weeks ago. Since then we've been back 3 more times. Not only is the restaurant beautiful and clean inside; the staff, service and food are spectacular. Our latest visit was a week ago to celebrate the hubs birthday. We had a reservation for 15. Traffic didn't suck (shocker for Brandon) so we arrived kinda early. To our surprise...the table was set up and ready for us. I wanted a snack and a drink and we had about 30 mins to kill...we didn't want to sit at the table yet so we sat at the sushi bar that's off to the side and in the back of the restaurant. I ordered some yellow tail and smoked salmon sashimi and my husband ordered the steak roll. He had a beer and I enjoyed a glass of wine. The sushi maker dude was so nice and funny and the sushi was fresh and so fricken good (note...not only have I found my new favorite place for Thai food but I think I also found my new sushi place as well) OK..so once the rest of our party started to arrive we transitioned to the table. SERVICE WAS PHENOMENAL. Drinks initially came out slow but that was to be expected with such a large party. We ordered apps for the table which came out quick. The apps were the spring rolls- crispy, hot and delicious and curry puffs- tender, hot, and filled with meaty goodness. For my entree I ordered the Emperial duck. The portion was huge and consisted of a very large, perfectly cooked duck breast smothered with the most delicious curry sauce and vegetables. The side of rice was cooked just right and was perfect for soaking up the sauce. Every one in our party, including some folks that had never tried Thai food before loved everything they ate. I'm already thinking about what I am going to order next but I have to pace myself cuz I don't want to look like a Thai food obsessed stalker or something! :-)

The atmosphere is very nice and very family oriented/ accommodating. Once we parked the aroma of the food was the first thing that got our attention. Then friendly staff and wonderful food makes this place a go to spot for me and my significant other for a long time coming.

I like it as a little place in college town to get Asian food, but I still have a hard time giving this place more than three stars. My latest rant is that it lacks class. For example, tables are taped with packing tape, and the chairs in the place don't match. If they class it up, I could bump this up to 4 stars.

Sadly, Florida is a massive wasteland when it comes to offering culinary variety (unless you like everything fried and full of hormone-laden meat). However, this place is a shining example of delicious, freshly prepared food that offers health benefits not rivaled by much else. The vegetarian and vegan preparations are outstanding, and the injera is fresh and perfectly formed. The setting is peacefully arranged with traditional Ethio seating options as well as standard "American slopping tables." The owner is warm and delightful; and enjoys notoriety amongst a large group of loyal customers (it's nice to know there are actually people in Tampa who have an ability to appreciate good food when they encounter it).
Food was good and price was a little high but it's worth the taste. Paneer tikka is very good

Very pleasant family style restaurant. Service was good and the food very tasty. Tons of vegan options. I would recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic Indian food is a basic setting. $28 all in for 2 adults for Saturday lunch
Cute little place where you can linger over late lunch with a friend without being interrupted. Pleasant dining room, interesting food and friendly non-obtrusive service. I loved everything about it.
Naan is amazing! Order the aloo ... Chat from the appetizer section, it's cold and refreshing.

Overall, the food was just OK. I have been to many Thai places, and the taste of the food was very watery. We ordered coconut soup, red curry beef and duck with drunken noodles. The meet was not good quality, and the duck was served with the bone. The latter resulted in small bones in the noodles, which was not good for the teeth and the feeling. However, I have to admit that the service was really nice and polite, and generally the place was clean, and the environment warm. The prices normal for center city Philadelphia.

Had a great lunch at Magasin Kitchen !!!! Kids loved the Banh mi , And the beef fried rice was delicious . My wife is a vegetarian and they had great options for her ! A great change of pace from the fried and fatty . A must try place !!!!!
Worst food. Worst service. Stale items in Buffet. Ordered fish Tikka....tastes like a chewing a rubber piece. No taste no flavor. Very rude server.

Food was fine, nothing too exciting. Service was very poor. Called in for pickup and they got our order wrong. We waited about 30 minutes for the dish they got wrong, while the other food from our order sat cooling by the register. Had to reheat the food in the microwave when we finally got home. Very poor experience, not even an apology for the mistake or the wait. I won't be returning.

I think all the of the people who have posted reviews complaining about this place didn't get enough hugs as children. Whomp whomp. It's fine. It is exactly what you would expect. It is not the restaurants fault if you have weird expectations. Seriously. It isn't. I am sorry your dad was so mean.

We've been on mission to try all of the Indian food in our area. But we're stuck on Desi Spice. It's so incredibly good we don't want to keep trying other places. Delicious free papadams and dip to start with. The alu tikki appetizer is amazing. And the tandoori salmon is the best thing we've ever eaten.

Honestly, this restaurant needs an update to it. It is very 80's in decoration and food preparations. The sauces are very heavy and are poured over the dishes. The service is excellent. My mom likes to come here so we brought her for dinner. The best thing off the menu is the fried cheese, one of the BEST dishes I have ever have. We shared it, I'm going back for my own portion. Each bite was magical in taste, indescribable how good it was. I had a fresh fish, it was good not great. The baklava was very good, almost as good as what I make.

Came here a while back and just chose a random spot to eat. Okay Im in a foreign country...Belly dancer entertainment in a private tent in Arabia (just make believe with me). I liked it! I was on a date with an engineer who claimed to be african and it was funny because he was starving and whining like a little kid that night. So he ordered...and ordered he did the multiple course meals where you can try anything: everything. Yummy. I have no idea what I ate. I guess it was Moroccan food. I was too busy watching the belly dancer! haha. I dont think Morrocan food was my thing or else I would remembered what I had. But hey I like trying new flavors of the east. :) I found out later my date never eat moroccan food before. Great...Lol. I would do it again. Bring on the belly dancing!

I don't know why people are so hard on Pho Bistro. I have eaten here probably 10 times and never gotten food poisoning or diarrhea (which is more than I can say for Caje). I alway get the raw beef and meatballs (which admittedly look a little grey but they are delicious). If you are recalling craving hot beef soup, look no further than Pho Bistro.

This place used to be a standby for our family. We could count on them for cheap, healthy, consistently delicious eats. They changed their name, but management & staff were supposed to be the same, so we didn't think twice about hitting them up for dinner the other night. Sadly, the food was terrible the night we went. My vermicelli bowl was full of limp, way past edible green onions & iceberg lettuce that was brown & tasteless like it was from a plastic package the was past its "sell by" date. The broth just tasted like salt & they didn't bring fish sauce until I found a server to ask. But the biggest disappointment was the vermicelli. It seemed like spaghetti instead of rice noodles. Maybe we just caught them on an off night, but I'm in no rush to go back.
Absolutely one of my favorite places to eat. I always get the Queens platter and it never disappoints.

I have been frequenting this place for few months here. I admit i am hooked to the mouth watering taste of their kabobs. The place is v small and not much for dine in but I am willing to compromise on that for their succulent kabobs. I don't like the biryani much. The curries are good, nothing to complain but they could do better.

Disgusting. Made the mistake of visiting the Brentwood location today and was completely disappointed. I ordered a gyro pocket with chicken and the chicken was disgusting. Also there was zero tahini in it. What is a gyro without tahini??

Recently went back after many years. I don't know why it took us so long. Everything was so good and the service was outstanding! My husband had biryani and I had a saag dish. Can't wait to go back and try something new.

Delicious! It's a small take-out place with a few tables. I had the palak paneer and samosa chaat. The palak paneer was just creamy enough. I think the preparation of this dish by many other places in Delaware is a bit mediocre - usually too dry. I loved the flavor and texture of the dish from this place. The samosa chaat was filling and flavorful. Highly recommended!
Terrasse tres sympa pour prendre un verre , manger un petit snack et ecouter de la musique, service agreable

Although there are a few different locations we keep coming back to the original. Where else can you put your name in with the hostess and drop off your wine , cross the street to the New Wave Cafe for a few drinks and the hostess will come for you when your table is ready. We have been here MANY times over the years and the food has NEVER disappointed. We came here once with a party of six and the wait was very long so usually we keep it to a party of two. Its also easier to snag a table the earlier in the evening that you arrive. The menu is mostly seafood and is some of the freshest and tastiest around. We always order the octopus and ave sampled everything on the menu. Every couple of months one of us gets the hankering and we are off to 3rd & Catherine. Can't wait until our next visit.

Each wait will be at least 30 minutes. You'll realize the time spend is well worth it. There is absolutely nothing like this food You stand in line, no need to order because he only make 1 item each day and it's $10. You're arms will hurt from the weight of it. Be prepared. Best cart food I've ever tried.

a hidden gem, refereed to us by a friend and to then get a Yelp deal on top of it , outstanding. The PHO was wonderful and a specialty dish delish. Dont judge from the outside, this place is legit the real deal.
I recommend the hummus as an appetizer and the Pasa Kebab (Lamb and Shrimp) as the entre

This place is by far the best Mediterranean Cafe I have ever dined at in Tucson or anywhere else. The shawarma is incredible, their green beans and hummus is some of the best I've had and the salad comes with a tangy twist. I don't do Pita Bread but the folks are always gracious to let me sub in some grape leaves instead for no extra charge. I've had several of the other plates but the chicken shawarma plate is my go to option time and time again. It is that good. The only drawback is the distance from the City Center but perhaps that is what makes this place great. While this is a drawback, it is worth the drive out (or bike ride out!). Can't say enough about Zayna's.

Their crab delight (crab rangoon) is the best I've ever had! I had the cashew chicken for as an entree and it was delicious; perfect amount of spicy for myself. Great, helpful server who delivered the meal fast!

Really authentic Jamaican food. I have eaten Jamaican ate dozens of spots all around the east coast. So this spot in Chester county is a gem and has the best Jamaican food in the area. The food is really well seasoned, the plaintains taste crisp and amazing. I always order the jerk chicken and like it with Jamaican hot pepper sauce. The management here is very friendly.

I've seen this place on Instagram a lot so I'm here. At first we were very excited to try until our orders were taken. My order was taken at 10:22 pm and currently it is 10:59pm and still no food yet. (Currently waiting in the store) it's not as busy as I would have assumed. As I sit and wait I can over here the ladies in back saying that my order is messed up and I only order beef and broccoli a shrimp roll... Regardless on if the food was worth it or not I would never give a place my money with POOR CUSTOMERS SERVICE. 100% totally horrible... the food is overrated very small portions for an high price... the employees in the front just sit and watch and gossip when your waiting an hour for a lunch size dinner for 15 bucks ... Business rule number #1 great customer service #2 treat all customers equally... it was all of me and my friends first and last time... and we drove 1 hour for this experience..

The service was great. Super friendly and fast. I even showed up only about 10 minutes before they close and not only did they serve me but they were really nice. I'm a pretty tough critic on Thai food. I had the panang curry. It was pretty good but not amazing. Felt like they Canadian-ized the dish a little.

DISGUSTING food and bad service. 4 of us walked in around 10pm on cinco de mayo, and despite open tables, were not greeted or seated for about 10 minutes. There were only 3 employees circulating the floor; which you would think they would staff more heavily considering they are a latin restaurant in a trendy neighborhood during a Latin holiday- and it's a sizable dining area to begin with. They were only serving their small plates, half of which they were out of, and it took over 30 minutes for 4 appetizers to come out. They ran out of margaritas (no patron, no citronage/grand marnier)- at 10pm on cinco- I can forgive all of this, but the food was THE WORST. I have had better deviled eggs from my local grocery store's deli counter. They had a musty, stale taste and a "skin" on top as if they'd been sitting out for a while. The grits were the instant "just add water and microwave" kind, with only 6 (yes, we counted) small (51-60 size, yes baby I make my own groceries and I only buy that exact size to put into my gumbo); and some weren't deveined. I had to send the calamari back. I never send food back, I used to wait tables and I'm really lenient and sympathetic about minor flaws with my food. The calamari were a purplish-brown color and heavily crusted with course white grainy stuff (my guess would have been either those insta-grits or wheat germ). Incredibly shriveled and overcooked and inedibly chewy (the two of us brave enough to try it spat it out after chewing and chewing and chewing). I had to politely send it back; our waitress apologized and told me that the kitchen had ran out of flour and that I wasn't the first to send it back. Now, as a former waitress myself, I would have warned my tables that ordered the calamari of this huge issue and saved everybody (myself, my guest, and the fry chef) the trouble. And the pork picadillo plate was a fried corn tortilla spread with bland black beans, pork braised in a sweet enchilada sauce, and wayyyyyy to much salty salty cotija/queso fresco cheese. Once you scraped off the thick cap of cheese, it was edible but still had a slightly "canned" flavor to it. I will never go back and eat there, it was the most disgraceful food I've ever had in my 25 years of living in New Orleans. I may, however, get a mojito from there and hang out on the patio and roll with the great live music.
I love the food here. I always get the crab fried rice, and I CRAVE it all the time.

My friend and I had been wanting to try Suraya and were pleasantly surprised to score a reservation on a Saturday night. After checking in we did have to wait a few minutes for our table which was a small two top in the very back. The patio was closed but looked like an awesome place to dine. The best dish we had all night was the fatteh, a warm brown butter chickpea dip served with pita. The batata harra (crispy potatoes), fried kibbeh (ground beef dumplings), and turmeric rice were all delicious as well. I personally would not order the muhammara (red pepper and walnut dip) or the ground lamb kabob again. The kabobs were served with a side of charred tomatoes, onions, and peppers which were perfect on top of the rice. I wish I could make vegetables that taste that good at home. By the end of the meal we were both completely stuffed. I am anxious to come back and try brunch at Suraya, which I heard is their specialty!

Gus is back today from taking a few weeks off. He got all new equipment and a fryer for his cart and he now has an assistant to help him out. I got there at 11:35 today with one person in front of me and had my food within a couple of minutes. Its definitely a lot faster now with the assistant.

From the photos, the food looks so fresh and amazing, which is what drew me here. I ordered the roka salad with lamb since I was craving a fresh salad. The lamb was cooked well and chopped in smaller pieces for the salad. However, the meat came out colder than I expected, but maybe that's because I got it on a salad. Some of the chopped pieces were pure fat, which were chewy and tough to eat. The meat pieces were nice and tender, but I wasn't blown away. I enjoyed the sweet dressing and ended up eating the whole bowl. My boyfriend got the pork souvlaki, and he said it was good, but I thought the meal looked dry. It was just grilled meat skewers with fries. If you want sauce, it costs extra. I kind of feel like a plate like that should come with sauce. Overall it wasn't bad, but I was kind of let down. I feel like the ~$15 I paid for the salad wasn't quite worth it (the lamb costs extra). Also parking is scarce, so we had to park down the street and around the corner. Wasn't a total miss--I was just a bit disappointed!

Located in front of the Kmart store on Rt. 1 in Langhorne. As mentioned before it is easy to miss if you are not looking for their sign, as the back of the restaurant faces the highway and is hard to tell it even is there. We visited right after a small snowfall, so it was not busy at all. We were immediately greeted and asked if we had a preference in seating and were seated at a booth immediately. They had several specials and a decent sized menu from sandwiches to steaks and seafood. They also offer quite a few Mediterranean dishes as well. Our waiter Seth was very friendly and entertaining and wasted no time introducing himself, telling us about the restaurant and answering any questions we had and making recommendations. I had a gyro platter which was a bed of rice piled high with gyro meat, a large side of chopped cucumber, red onion and tomatoes, a pita sliced into wedges, tzatziki sauce and roasted tomato and a big roasted hot pepper. My husband had the chicken chesapeake ( breast stuffed with spinach, ham, Swiss cheese, roasted red pepper with crabmeat and a parmesan cream sauce) a side of broccoli, mashed potatoes and the salad bar. Everything was very fresh and while mine was really good, my husband said he may never order anything other than the chicken Chesapeake ever again because it was sooooooo good. We will definitely be back soon.
The General Manager, Joey Ka messaged me about my experience, first thing then next morning. He moved expeditiously to get the matter handled, and for that I am appreciative!

The food here is decent, even if it is 30% or so more expensive than it should be. I suppose those Whyte Avenue rents must put some awful pressure on the bottom line. Check out Kabsa if you can snag a Groupon deal.

I had an amazing experience at Suraya. This restaurant offers incredible brunch options. I ordered a mimosa and a chai latter. Both were exceptional. Highly recommend everyone to give it a try. Place is not romantic but great for groups and friends.
Excellent food. Friendly staff. Good to eat in or take out. Lots of veggie options. Great small plates and entrees. I have never been disappointed.

Over all nice looking place but does show some age. For the price of the food VS the flavors, quality and portion size I just don't see the justification. I definitly would not go out of my way for the place. If I was close buy and I was hankering for Mediterranean food, I might stop in and give them another try.

Had the falafel wrap. very delicious not oily. with tomato and onions / lettuce of course all the good stuff. As a vegetarian and craving mediterranean food more than normal this is a great place to go with many options. don't have any pictures because of how fast i ate it and if the owner is reading this the potato's you also made me to try were delicious you need to sell them!! 5/5* will go back in in the area!!! - a guy from srq

I had the Wishboner sandwich and was made a fan. It had beautiful artisan bread on the outside, and what's inside was such a treat. Below is my rating on the interior of the sandwich. - the fried chicken 4/5: The protein was well-seasoned, savory, not too salty, and crunchy. The portion was sizeable and I caught myself enjoying it after the buns were gone. One big plus was that it did not have the bitter after taste from used oil that a lot of fried chicken franchises unfortunately cannot get rid of. One point minus because the inside was not juicy. It wasn't dry, but just okay. - the pickled cucumbers 5/5: must be the best pickled cucumbers I've ever had. It's not straight-up briney or sour. The flavor was subtle, but really savory. I'd never thought I'd label pickles gourmet, crafty, and artisan. But here they are. - the tomatoes 5/5: not your average sandwich slices that come from beefsteak tomatoes that are plain and sad. The sandwich came with grilled halves that I suspect are of the tomatoes on the vine variety. It elevated the whole meal to be wholesome and satisfying. The sandwich can easily be marketed at $10+ at trendy bars, but I paid $7.19 after tax. I found it to be fair and a good deal for lunch. Other things of notice are the cute design of the store, and their New Hope fountain drinks that are made in small-batches. Although I did not try one, but the free water that came out of the machine was carbonated with just the right amount of bubbles and crisp. One minor rant is they don't have bottled sauces on the counter you can put on your burger, e.g. hot sauce, but you can purchase a variety of dipping sauces for 50 cents each. I'll come back to try their fried chickens and desserts next time.

I hav recently moved to KOP so was on a hunt for places of indian food and this came up. So first impressions : Good place arnd for chaats and snacks . Not much on the Dosas they were ok !! Sambar didnt taste good .. Chickn 65 was very much desi style so was the samosa ... Pani poori not tht grt.. Dahi poori was better ... The desserts were good ... Ras malai was yummy but the rose flavor was bit overwhelming and the gajar halwa was worth a shot.. But a bit pricey for 6$ each ... Overall a nice place to snack out . Desi style in both food and service .. If u knw what i mean .. Dont expect nrml hi .. Hellos of US nor the service nor the courtesy so dont bother abt the tip either .. Its desi after all !!!!
I will say the drive was worth it. The place is a little easy to miss, and I suppose at peak business hours, this place would be hard to get to, but I will say the pho is worth the trouble.

My friend and I decided to stop by Jiallo's after the Ethiopian restaurant we wanted to go to was closed. I had heard good things about this place, so we decided to give it a whirl. I ordered the yassa chicken with jollof rice. One of my friends from Senegal has made jollof rice for me before, and from what I know, every country (and every person) has their own version of what is deemed to be best. The jollof rice I had here tasted as if it had been sitting out all day and was extremely hard and crunchy. The chicken yassa was very salty and one dimensional. I think it needed some lemon juice to break up the saltiness, however, I thought the caramelized onions were good. I would definitely be willing to give Jiallo's another try, but not order this dish again.

Location near the hotel makes it harder to find than I thought it would be but once inside I liked the place. The chicken tikki masala was tasty and service was friendly. Next time I am down in the area working I may stop back.

Pretty darned tasty. But why only 3 stars? The Greek salad - tasty and fresh lettuce and veggies, solid feta - but waaaaaaay too much dressing. And a little lacking on the olives, but that might have been the luck of the draw. The lamb gyro sandwich was pretty bomb. Again - fresh ingredients. The lamb seemed really, really processed. Still tasty though. For what I got, I think it's a little pricey, but if you're going for some fresh food with a nice Mediterranean kick, this is definitely a decent place.

The drive-thru is always quick and easy. I really enjoy the tropichop when they get my order right, which they do 9 times out of 10. On this particular occasion, I asked for a side of the spicy poyo poyo sauce and was disappointed when I got home and it was not in the bag. The food is pretty good, but not as flavorful as a real sit down restaurant (not like a fast food chain). For the price, it's a pretty good value.

Probably the best thai food in the area, but that comes with a price. Heavy wait times during rush hour and even worse for pick up. The staff there try the best they can. My rec, try off hours and you wont go wrong here.

This place is one of the best for great Greek food for low prices in the downtown area. Not only do they give you a load of food, but it's fresh and delicious. I went there today and ordered the vegetarian combo. For 8.95 I got a giant scoop of hummus, babaghannoush, two BAKED falafel (which I love that), grape leaves, and tabbouleh with salad. A warm pita comes on the side and it was all delicious. Though not the best hummus or babaghannoush I've had, it was all really good. This is one of those places which is a hidden gem, homey atmosphere, and friendly staff. HIGHLY recommended!

The name of this place sounds a lot like "shoe kitchen" in some combination of romance languages, which would not seem super appetizing. However, the food they serve up here is quite the opposite. We tried the short rib tacos and the Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito. AMAZING. Both were filled with delicious, fresh, and healthy-tasting ingredients. The green sauce on the tacos was awesome, and the avocado slices were a bonus. The breading on the fried tilapia wasn't so Cap'n Crunch tasting (I could be wrong, It's probably been about two decades since I've had Cap'n Crunch, and never in fried form), but it was still fantastic. The burrito is filling and a nice size for $6. They don't open until noon, and I think they're usually swamped. Go on a cold day like we did, and the weather will hopefully keep the crowd (and the wait) under control. It's located at the very end of the hidden food truck alley at Drexel. Totally worth the trek, even from Penn. Also, the guy that takes orders is super friendly and tries to remember everyone's name. Very impressive. Cucina Zapata is hands-down the best food truck I've tried in West Philly. Possibly all of Philadelphia. Possibly ever.
I had the duck and it was incredible. The rice and vegetables are fresh and flavorful. The atmosphere in the restaurant is very pleasant as well. I love this place for dinner.
Mediterranean version of Chipotle. Delicious flavours, kinda heavy on the salty. Still love! Had half falafel, half chicken. Pita is one of best I've ever had, tbh.

If you don't try their lunch buffet something is wrong with you. This is NOT your standard buffet. The food is amazing. It also looks too good to eat. What lunch buffet do you know that has food that looks too pretty to eat? None that I know, except Shere-E-Punjab. Fabulous value. a Ten spot gets you all-you-can-eat Indian food. The atmosphere is peaceful, quiet, especially considering it is in a shopping center. Service is very good. Even the free bread they bring you is amazing. Easily my favorite lunch spot.

I was in the neighborhood for a lunch meeting and upon learning of my love of sushi suggested this place. It was perfect. The hostess was pleasant and the waitress was quick, knowledgeable, friendly and eager to help. But that's not why you go to Fulin's. I had one of the lunch plate specials, sashimi I think. I upgraded to the seaweed salad which was fabulous-perhaps the best I've ever had. The miso was good, and the plate of sashimi was outstanding. This is authentic, Japanese style sashimi. It's not the thin slice of fish on a big lump of rice like most round-eyes associate with sushi. This is a plate of thick slices of various fish. I ate every piece, even the ones I couldn't identify. They were all good. The wasabi was great. Everything was great, except that I wanted to order three more servings of the plate, and that would have embarrassed my colleagues. Go to Fulin's if you like sushi.

This is one of my favorite places to eat and one of the things I look forward to most when in Langhorne for work. Every time I eat at Rosemary's they treat me like family and the food never disappoints. The place is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner and has one of the most extensive menus I've encountered in my travel so far. They even have authentic Mediterranean cuisine which is highly underrated. It is AMAZING! Basically if you can't find something you love on the menu it's your own damn fault.

Honestly, the worst hookah bar in St Louis...I have been puzzles, h2, ranoush and double apple and this one has absolute worst service ever! You walk in and you immediately notice the employees hanging out with their friends, playing cards and smoking....the employees are not welcoming and are not helpful. When we went up to the cash register, the guy didn't even look up from his phone to give us a recommendation. After we sat ourselves (someone was playing their personal video game on the projector and an employee was sleeping on the couch) and recieved our hookahs, it was not made very well...barely any smoke but the flavor did last about 45 min. After it died, we asked for more coals (no one came around to ask us if we needed more coals, they were just having a nice little social gathering) and instead of giving us the amount of coals we recieved originally, he gave us 2 halves. It didn't work and when I went up to the guy he said that he would put another coal on but it's probably done...(WELL MADE HOOKAHS last usually about 1.5-2 hours) it took him 30 min to give us new coals and didn't even bother to try and help us start it or fix the problem....and I tried to get on the website to write a review or to talk to someone about this and their website wasn't even working....it looks like that the move to the new location was not a very good move

Queen of Sheba has become my local watering hole. It's perfect for a group, with generous portions of Ethiopian food and pitchers of beer. Twenty years ago I was a regular at another bar at this location - Off the Wagon - and I can detect the structure of the old bar - the booths and brown decor. I like this incarnation much better because the food is delicious and perfect for sharing. I stumbled in a Quizzo night there. The questions were fairly easy, but there were sharks among the crowd. A near perfect score is the only way to win the top prizes - and several groups vied for the top spots. I think it was a Wednesday night. The food service was especially slow and that had been the first time I experienced that. i won't take marks off on the restaurant, but I thought I'd mention it.

whoa! i had the whole red snapper with thai chili sauce. FAR EXCEEDED MY EXPECTATIONS! they let us order off of the dinner menu, during lunch hours, AND they made it for me to-go!!! EXQUISITE presentation (i eat with my eye, first). the flavorS that followed...well, i licked my fingers! i know, right?

Excellent food and friendly staff. My daughter and I ate there tonight. We had an appetizer of spring rolls, we each had a soup, and I ordered a fried rice dish which was great and my daughter ordered a noodle dish that was great. Several other guests came in while we were there and were greeted very warmly and their dishes looked good too.

The food here is great - authentic, good variety and decent prices (a little higher than the vietnamese places downtown). It's close to my house, so we visit often. I would give them more stars for the food, but the service can be really rough. When we take out and ask for sauce containers, they are very hesitant to give us more than one tiny container for condiments. It can be very frustrating arguing back and forth as to why we would go through more than one or two little cups of condiments (hoisin, sriracha, etc.). Just be prepared! 4 stars for the food, 2 stars for the service. PS - steer clear of the spring rolls here - very bland with not much in them. Pho is awesome though!
I had the red curry with beef today. Very flavorful and delucuous. The people working here are all friendly and take the time to answer questions about their menu.

What a wonderful place! I've been struggling since my office moved to the north side. It seems that all I can find are chain restaurants and the occasional local diner/Americana place (which aren't bad. I do love buffalo chicken.). However, every once in a while I have a craving for Indian food and Amber Indian Restaurant is great place to sate that craving. I went for their lunch buffet and, to be honest, wasn't expecting much. To my surprise, the food was rich and flavorful, true to the more authentic Indian I have in the past. I tried a bits of a lot of things, but the ones that stood out for me were the daal, the aloo gobi, and the goat curry. All three had a rich spice profile, with lots of layers and textures. The goat was a little fatty, but it usually is, and the meat was tender and delicious. Another bonus of this place is the fresh naan that comes out when you are seated. They make it to order so it basically melts in your mouth. I am excited to have discovered Amber Indian and I look forward to many spicy lunches there in the future!

Coming from the SF Bay Area, we have had our share of excellent Pho and Vietnamese food. Our dinner at Pho Orchid was easily as good, if not the best we have had. I had the rare steak Pho and my wife had curry. Superb!Excellent drinks from the full bar. This place appears to be a bit of a sleeper. Not to be missed!
Excellent food that reminds me of Vancouver. Always fast and delicious, and reasonably priced. The restaurant itself is quaint and clean, we will definitely come here on the regular.
Nice BYOB find. Menu had a good amount of variety and authentic Italian dishes. A little pricey but portions were nice sized. Service was very good as well.
Worst Indian restaurant ever I visited.they serve you stale chicken .too much oil in the food .never ever go this restaurant

I was in Wilmington downtown 2 weeks back and tried their Paneer Tikka platter and it was just grilled to perfection. Very authentic flavors with all freshness. I tried their Mango lassi and it was very tasty. I will definitely go back there on my next visit.

I was so happy to become reunited with the Sansom Kabob House. Today, I realized that they had relocated to South St., so my good friend and I decided to go find them this afternoon. We were not disappointed in the least. The sauteed pumpkin dish(w/ yogurt) and my lamb dish(w/ carrots, almonds, and raisins) was simply divine, well-prepared. The staff continues to be quite approachable and inviting. I was so happy for the welcoming atmosphere, that I spoke to one of the owners about my impeccable experience at their establishment in the past. This impressive occurrence will keep me coming back in the future. This Afghani restaurant is worth your time and money. Seek this establishment out, for you deserve to experience its magnificent cuisine personally.

I have been to lunch at Erawan a handful of times, and all of my experiences have been great. The food was delicious, and the service very attentive and quick. The lunch special is the best I have seen in the area- 2 appetizers and a main dish for about 10 bucks. The interior of the restaurant is clean and neat, unlike a lot of other places in Chinatown. I'm hoping to make it here for dinner sometime, it is a BYOB which is right up my alley.

Love the food here. I work next door , not only its convenient but the food is good. I love their beef pho! I thinks it's better then a lot of places. I'm Asian so I eat a lot of pho and it's even better then my moms. They have a good banh mi (Vietnamese po-boy) there also.

i'm sorry. i want to like this place, i really do. the servers are awesome and so is the decor, especially on a summer night. but the food...meh, not so hot. the only thing i've ever found good was the veggie stew wrapped in bread-ish goodness. the meat is always fatty and a little. though i could live on plantains. but the forays out of veggie/fruit world here have left me leaving a full plate to give to my housemates.

Someone did their home work before taking me to lunch. Great service. Cozy atmosphere. Delicious food. Can not wait to come back! Pineapple fried rice with shrimp and khao-nuea sunka for dessert are my favorites.

Went with my husband on Saturday night. Food tasted extremely good and fresh. Two starters, two mains, a dessert to share with four drinks (beer and wine) came in at under $60. We thought this was great value considering the quality of the food. The restaurant is very nicely decorated inside. Along with the friendly welcome the service wasn't rushed, felt nicely paced and we could have lingered for a while longer. I'm definitely going back.
Great food .Please be careful selecting how Spivey you want your food .I chose level 4 and it was okay for me

So far this is the best banh mi I've found in New Orleans without having to drive to the West Bank or out to the east and I literally could not stop myself from taking bites on my way home. I got the mixed cold cuts with pate as a large, 12'' po'boy. It was huge and packed full of delicious pickled carrots and daikon. My total came to just a little over $7.00, which I found to be an awesome price for a 12'' banh mi. My car is currently destroyed by flaky bread crumbs since I could not make it home without tearing into my sandwich. One bite led to another and I almost plowed my car several times into a number of potholes on Bienville all while sending more shattering bread crumbs down my shirt and throughout the interior of my car. Eating a po'boy while driving is by far more dangerous than texting while driving. They also have regular po'boys on the menu as well as yaka-mein which I'm going to have to come back for! I don't know if you're supposed to use the parking lot behind the building, but I did and it made coming here accessible and easy.

Awesome place to eat..I visit at least twice a week..have not had anything was not absolutely delicious..the owners are very friendly..a very good family owned restaurant to support in the Indy area close to Avon.

Finally made it here today. It's been a handful of hours and i'm still stuffed from lunch! It was peak lunch time when we arrived at the truck so we expected to wait a bit for our orders to come out. But no worries the guys work very quickly to get your orders so you can stuff the goodness in your belly. I came specifically for the cap'n crunch tilapia and it was great. It had two fried tilapia fillets, avocados, salad mix, and awesome sauce. They asked if i liked spicy so they added extra sauce to my order. I also got the jasmine green tea with boba topped with whip. It was a nice sweet treat. I would definitely order both again. The guy devoured his two braised short rib taco with extra spicy sauce. They hooked it up with some garlic fried peanuts with fried red hot peppers. I love fried garlic so this was a hit to me, the peppers definitely adds a nice spicy kick. The prices are very reasonable, you won't get ripped off with quantity and quality. Not only was the food great but the guys were very friendly and nice. Overheard a girl asking if they accept cc and unfortunately they don't but they offered for her to just get them back the next day. Just be careful with the PPA, they almost got us today. I'll be sure to come back for more!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: This place is great for takeout sushi. I used to like dining there before the fire. Unfortunately, after the fire the smell of the charred residue still remains and makes for an uncomfortable dining experience. The staff is super hospitable, it's just the smell.

Oh so good! We ordered a ton of food: 2 orders of egg rolls, 2 small beef pho, 1 large beef pho, 3 small beef pho to-go, iced coffee, and green tea bubble tea. All together the price was around $60. Wow! That is a great price. The eggs rolls were good. Yum yum. I wish the pho had more meat. I'm not a huge meat eater but even for me it was lacking. A small pho is 6.99, the large is 7.99; pho really doesn't cost a lot of money to make. A few extra pieces of meat would make a lot of difference. The bubble tea was the most amazing bubble tea ever. I've never had bubble tea that's a slushy. I was taken aback how good it was!

One of the best dining experiences I have had in Nashville. The thought and care behind each dish showed and the food was DELICIOUS. I can't wait to go back and try more items. The staff is so welcoming and warm. Above and beyond the best Thai food in Nashville.

Ordered takeout from this place last week. Empanadas were outstanding. Ordered a couple of the pork dishes - they were a bit mild for my taste. The torta was excellent. Portions were generous. We ordered a bunch since we wanted to try out stuff - and had enough leftover for another meal Overall - very nice place and we will definitely be going back
Delicious authentic Vietnamese banh mi. Hits the spot! The bubble tea is great and the added jellys and pearls are fun.

Cute looking spot with great outdoor seating so we had some high expectations. Their holoumi cheese was fantastic but the calamari was so so and the lamb my husband ordered was inconsistent, 3/4 were cooked properly but the 4th was under cooked. My salmon was crispy on the outside but dry on the inside. Also the drink specials seemed good but expectations just not met, they brought out a carafe of wine to pour over two wine glasses with ice and a few dismal chunks of apple. Perhaps their take on a sangria just not something we're accustomed to.

I'm seriously surprised by the poor reviews. This is a brand new location located in the old Seminole Mall. Clearly they needed time to work out the kinks. I went through the drive-thru last evening at dinner time and was greeted by a super friendly order taker. My food was delivered quickly and we couldn't have been more pleased with the taste. We tried the chicken quesadilla wrap (chicken, black beans, yummy sauce, etc. in a tortilla-like wrap). It was served with one side, and I opted for the corn soufflé (spoon cornbread-type). Both were delicious! I also tried the mashed potatoes and gravy which were a fantastic surprise coming from a fast food place. The plantains were absolutely delicious, too! I will totally be back to try other items.
Columbia is lucky to have Thai house they have excellent food blasting with flavor. Always a great option for dinner.

I have had the broken rice, vermicelli, and pho dishes here on many occasions. Oriental Pearl has proven to be very consistent with the food they put out. Thumbs up for that. Service is not the best. They're not rude or anything, just slightly awkward and maybe a bit inattentive. I would say the broken rice and vermicelli dishes are absolutely wonderful. My most preferred meat of choice would be the BBQ pork. The lunch special L-7 offers broken rice with 2 pork chops, a side of pickled veggies, an egg roll, and a little cup of fish sauce. The two pork chops makes this an awesome deal for $8. The pho here is not particularly great. The broth is okay, the portions are okay, the meat is fine. The portions are in line with a typical small size pho for places that offer small and large sizes. I may just have very high standards for pho, and it's not actually that bad? Try it for yourself. They also offer some thai stuff, but I have yet to try any of those. In summary, broken rice and vermicelli dishes are awesome. Service is not great, but that can be easily overlooked for the delicious food.
This was an interesting place. On the expensive side, while the food was good, but not great. Enjoyed the tableside cooking

Best Thai on South Grand (north of Chippewa at least). I've tried a bunch of the vegetarian options and they're all good but they have the best pad see-iew and panang curry. Their chicken satay (I think it's called satay gai) is good too, it comes with an awesome cucumber dipping sauce that I can't get enough of. I don't get their dishes with meat besides the chicken satay so I don't know how that compares to everything else. As another reviewer mentioned, the veggies don't always seem super-fresh but this seems to vary from visit to visit, I've had some excellent broccoli and peppers in the noodle dishes so I don't think they only use frozen vegetables. Service is always excellent and they're always so friendly. We live close by and they're always happy to deliver but I don't think this is something they usually do.

My husband I love this place. I was born and raised in India so my standards for Indian food are pretty high. This restaurant has met those standards every consistently in the past year. They catered my pre-wedding events and the wedding and impressed my family from India. We get Indian food from them once a month to celebrate our wedding date and are never disappointed. We have also visited the lunch buffet multiple times and that also is wonderful with the food items variety and taste. When anyone asks me about about eating good Indian food in the area I always recommend them because they truly are the closest to what legitimate Indian food tastes like. Many restaurants in the area cater to the American taste buds regarding spice level and often end up compromising with the food flavor. I think Deccan Spice has found that balance and their food is delightful for when you truly do want the authentic Indian taste. While their service in the restaurant might not be the best but the servers are nice and the food definitely makes up for it. In conclusion, I highly recommend this restaurant to everyone.

Delicious little thai restaurant off in a random strip mall. This is the best Thai place I found so far in the more rural areas of Southern Illinois/Missouri. The restaurant is clean and quaint. The service was awesome. Very nice and eager to help. Each dish was authentic and wonderful. The tom yum had a great balance of sweet to sour. There was depth of flavor to it. The pad see ewe was perfectly cooked and well seasoned. The curry fried rice was just that. I could taste more curry flavor than other curry fried rices I've tried. My only gripe is that after a while, you get the feeling that there is just too much salt because everything builds up after a while. Prices are good! No complaints in that department

I've not had too much Vietnamese food, so maybe I'm not the best judge here, but their food is pretty tasty. Unfortunately there is only one veggie dish on the menu: rice noodle veggie stir fry with mushrooms, chopped up spring rolls and tofu, but it is really good. They also give you a ton of food and are always super nice. Like I said, I wish they had more veggie options, but I do enjoy what I've had!
The pot stickers have chicken, which is a nice change from the standard pork variety. Some of the best Pad See Ew.
Gyro wrap is as good as you can get in the big apple. Delicious and right next to bourbon!!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Everything was delicious and fresh. Staff very friendly. From Las Vegas where we frequently eat at indian restaurants, this is one of the best. Will definitely come back next time we are in Boise. Prices are very reasonable, $50 for the both of us and left full. We ordered spinach cheese curry (saag paneer), samosas, rice, muliganti soup and mango lassie drink.

Uptown location is excellent. The pho was outstanding. The best broth in town! Also great was the Vietnamese crepe. The tacos were okay. Service was good. It seems they do a brisk business with tourists from nearby hotels, but the quality of the food is not compromised one bit! Very reasonably priced, too. A great meal and my new favorite Vietnamese restaurant!

Don't be thrown off by the basement level and "rustic" ambiance because this place rules. Freshly cooked kabobs (I've only tried the chicken platter which is a home run) served with a fresh salad and rice. The hot sauce adds for that nice extra kick. Go here now.

Sukho Thai is OK and unremarkable in every way, except for the fact that it shares its lot with a go-cart track. The decorations inside are OK. They are sufficiently "exotic" enough for people not to feel cheated, but without actually being beautiful or impressive. The food is OK. You can eat it (except the miso soup, which is frankly, downright BAD) but you won't be missing it afterwards. I can't even remember what I had. The selection is OK. You see the things you expect, like pad thai or tom kha gai, but nothing that might be surprising or out of the ordinary. The prices are OK... see where I'm going with this? The whole visit was just OK. Next time I go to Nashville, I'll try something new.

Our first visit here was shortly after the place opened and we liked it so much we recommended it to friends. It took me this long to write a review because there are some restaurants I enjoy so much that I wait for a second visit so I can try more dishes. The staff here is very welcoming and friendly. They are happy to answer any and all questions you may have about the menu. My husband and I shared the sampler on our first visit which I would highly recommend to all first timers. You can choose three of their most popular meats and two sides. Everything we choose was great. On our next visit we started with Relleno de Papa de Carne which was a ground beef stuffed potato puff. Great start to our meal. I ordered the Carne Frita with Majado de Yucca for my entree. Carne Frita is pan fried pork with a demi glazed onions. Majado de Yucca is mashed yucca. It was very similar to mashed potatoes. Since I like to try as many foods as possible I took a bite of my husband's Pernil which is Puerto Rican style seasoned pork. The pork dishes had a bit more fat than I expected but everything was good.

I ordered the lunch special and requested them to add broccoli to my order and they did. The food was good and extra hot. Have returned on several occasions. Always do takeout, so I don't care how small or cheesy the interior looks. The people working there are always super nice and friendly.

Just moved from NJ and stopped here for dinner on our first night in the area. After living in a town with four middle eastern restaurants I wasn't sure what to expect in TN, but we were pleasantly surprised. The food was delicious! Portions good for the price and everything made fresh. Manager was super nice too. Highly recommend.
Ackee/Saltfish and rice awesome! The meal was very flavorful and yummy! I couldn't put the fork down
I was there the old woman who is working in the back she was playing with her noose and handling the bread without gloves .I will never come back
Great menu, excellent Caribbean food that's made just right. We were seated immediately and our server was very nice. The quality of our meals was high and the prices were very reasonable. Yummy!

Pho is perfect....service is amazing....and all very affordable. Yum Yum. I eat here often the food is fresh and always plated well. The restaurant is spotless and the severs are extremely nice. It's great to go out to an affordable dinner where your money seems appreciated and you not just another reservation. PS the fresh spring rolls are to die for...jus saying.
Here at Indianapolis for a conference and wanted some Indian cuisine. Food was excellent! Service was great. Ambience could have been better.

What a great find. First of all, it was one of the only highly rated restaurants in the STL area that would take a reservation. I understand why it doesn't work for certain trendy joints that have constant traffic, but when you're planning for a special night out, it's imperative. We had a group of 6 for a family celebration and 2 of the guests were a surprise for my sister-in-law. They were seated first at a great table toward the back so the surprise was a success. The waitress was AWESOME! She had a great sense of humor and gave us just enough space to catch up with our guests while still being very prompt. The food was DE-LISH! Oh my goodness was it good. We started with Phyllo Cigars which were awesome little feta-stuffed noms. But enough about that...let me explain to you how divine the lobster ravioli was...you know how you order lobster ravioli and then never taste lobster? WELL...I couldn't STOP tasting lobster. Holy hell, it was perfect. My husband had the chicken tortellini and I have NO idea how they made that cream sauce but I couldn't keep my hands off his plate. I'd like to see this place stay successful. The owner answered all my calls, was patient through all my questions about the reservation/surprise, and made it happen. The decor is super chic and almost lounge-y but with proper tables so you're not trying to cut your meat on a pleather couch...I sure hope that makes sense outside of my mind :) We'll be back!

Don't let the location fool you. This BYO restaurant may be located in a strip mall but once inside, the place is very clean, the decor and ambiance is tasteful and the food is great. I haven't found a thai restaurant in Philly that I like better. The Shrimp Pad Thai is awesome as is the BBQ Squid and Crispy Taro Root Apps. I also love the Cripsy Tamarind Duck and Garlic Squid entrees. Don't forget to try their homemade coconut cream -- the only thing that would improve it would be a sprinkling of toasted coconut on top. I've been going here since it opened and the owners never disappoint with great, friendly service -- and they always remember us.
Great food! Quick delivery! Savory taste and I keep getting the same thing, give or take a couple of things.

The wife and I just visited today for a late lunch buffet (1:30). The place was busy but we only had to wait a minute or two. We have visited their media location before so we know what to expect and we were not disappointed. The 7 day a week lunch buffet is a great way to have some excellent food without burning a lot of time or $$. The weekend buffet is $11.95 and during the week it's a bit cheaper. All the basic dishes are here and they are cooked appropriately and kept filled. The wait staff was excellent. Very friendly and always kept our drinks filled. This restaurant is a nice addition to the Drexel Hill area!
Great atmosphere. Stuck on their Pork Chop entrée. Love this place.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Yet another well reviewed Indian joint by my fellow Boisans who know nothing about Indian food. Grease and salt. That is all.

I think I am on a Vietnamese kick lately, so I wanted to try someplace new. I got take out yesterday for lunch. I called in my order before going and the man I spoke with on the phone sounded so bored, disinterested, and depressed. I honestly felt that he had somehow drained my energy after speaking with him. When I went to go pick up, the same man I spoke with on the phone rang me up and handed me my meal. Again, how bored he looked made me want to crack up. I don't think I have ever spoken to a more indifferent and stoic person. Anyway, I got the #50 Broiled pork and imperial egg rolls. It was pretty good. Not the best I've had, but among the better. Good flavors, just nothing outstanding. I will probably return as it's close to the office and I really want to see if I can catch that guy with the slightest amount of interest. Maybe I could get a rise with a good joke?

Good food, great service. Some people may consider it expensive, ( for example $25 for lasagna) but very generous portions and it's a BYOB so prices always are always higher. I am not a complainer but I really think the owner should do something about the sun in the back room. The very nice waitress kept telling everyone, "the sun goes down fast", well for 25 minutes my elderly uncle had to sit with the sun directly in his eyes. He kept saying it was OK but honestly that it NOT ok. We fixed that problem at our house one week after we moved in with a $150 solar shade!! Maybe someone should let the owners know about them. Anyway, the cooks really do a nice job. You will not be disappointed.

Returned 3 days later and had the same meal. Kebob sandwich was a little better and the fries were still unbelievable. I also tried the salad, which was great in itself, though the chips were not a favorite of mine. Favorite restaurant in the Apollo Beach area. Fast, affordable, delicious, and great service!

Been here a few times. Really enjoyed it every time. Make sure to grab one of their "rose/pistachio" donuts if they aren't already sold out! Staff is phenomenal. Would love to hire any and all of them for my business!

They serve Middle Eastern food. I have to be honest-- the food is so-so. It wasn't great but not bad either. However, we won't be going back to eat here. The customer service was fine, which was greatly appreciated! The prices were a bit on the expensive side for my taste. Their outdoor seating area is really nice during this perfect time of the year in Tucson. Overall an OK experience.

I enjoyed the chicken with coconut rice, both times I was here. The flavor is great, but the chicken portion is not enough to fill me up, so I had to order an appetizer. I've been here twice and will definitely return. Low Prices, so with the app, I spent $11 plus tip. Also, the food is very spicy if you order anything with hot pepper on it. I love hot and spicy foods, but if you can't handle tobasco, you won't be able to handle their spice, as it is a little hotter than that.
This is hands down my favorite restaurant. They are clean, polite and the atmosphere is cozy and the food is pretty fantastic. I highly recommend this place

I love this place. Tonight I did take out for the first time (I usually dine in) and it was just as delicious. The staff are friendly and the food is tasty. My boyfriend who hates everything and never compliments anything said he loved his steak. My jaw dropped. That alone should tell you how yummy this place is.
This place is absolutely authentic and amazing . The flavors are so nice and we ordered lots of different dishes and loved all of them. (Definitely be getting the egg rolls ). Fantastic experience !
Love this place. Food, staff & environment both in and outside are super awesome. Very cozy and intimate.
Good renovation, inside-out of the dining area. Feel cozy, ambient good feel. Both Thai and sushi are delish. Friendly staffs.

I was excited to try a new Lebanese/Mediterranean place in the city as I'm Lebanese but I was so disappointed. The food isn't authentic, it's Americanized. The service was fine, but due to the underwhelming food, and overpriced menu I won't be back. Also, they don't have traditional Lebanese coffee, or baklawa, but they have peanut butter hot chocolate?! I don't get it.

Note their sign does not light up so it was a challenge to find. They are in a parking lot with a liquor store. My family of 10 came in Christmas Day. Thankfully they were one of very few that actually opened. We arrived around 5:30 and there was 3 large groups ahead of us. We got seated about an hour later. Thing we're hectic and I don't think they were prepared for the heavy crowds as they were running out of utensils and cups. They finally take our order which took a really long time and the food came out a lot later. Although the food took a long time and they seemed unprepared, I think they still handled it well. (Maybe they will take this as a lesson for next year) Everyone was friendly and by the end of the night it seemed they had called in more people to help. I ordered the Bun Bo Hue and it was flavorful. The spring rolls & spring salad were ask very delicious. This is the longest time I've ever had to wait for pho or Vietnamese dishes but can't complain too much about the wait cuz it's Christmas. They are open New Year's Day also!

Aw man, I really wanted to like this place. I love Vietnamese food and felt stoked about the possibility of being able to get my fix within walking distance of my apartment. Unfortunately, the food is god awful. For reference, my dining partner and I tried the pork summer roll, bun bo hue, and bun cha gio. I'm not really sure what was inside the roll's rice paper but the shredded "pork" tasted like cardboard and I had to restrain myself from spitting it out. The broth of the bun bo hue had heat but lacked any flavor (not even a hint of lemongrass; womp, womp) and the noodles were way overcooked. The bun cha gio was semi-edible. Noodles, herbs, and fish sauce were all fine but the mini fried spring rolls were oil soaked pieces of garbage and I am positive you can find better spring rolls in the frozen section at Walgreens. This place does not do Vietnamese food justice at all. If you're in the mood for Vietnamese, save yourself the heartache -- gtfo of Fairmount and head to Washington Ave.

Great place! Very cordial waitresses. Food tastes amazing. Unfortunately no diaper changing station is there. But still a beautiful ambience prevails. The usual red, green curries, curry fried rice tasted brilliant.
The Pho is one of the best in town. To get things going, my lovely wife and I had an egg roll before the Pho and it was delicious. Great meal. Thus will be our new restaurant to go to.

Very tasty. The Chicken Tikka Masala was glorious and creamy. Definitely try the vegetable pakora. They do theirs a bit more like tempura with individual veggies. The spinach in there, woo boy. One thing to note, if you like spicy ask for hot. The medium was only slightly spicy. I will be returning to check out the lunch buffet.

The first time we at here, my husband and I declared it to be our favorite Thai in St. Louis (though, that's not saving much considering I've been hard pressed to find anything rivaling even what I've eaten in Oklahoma City). We visited for the second time, though, and will NEVER be returning. When we came in, we waited a FULL five minutes before being seated. Another five passed before our waitress appeared with menus. We already knew what we wanted, but she ran away so fast, we couldn't put in our order. When she came back 10 minutes later to get our drinks order, she refused to even TAKE our food order saying she'd "be right back." While we waited on our Thai Iced Teas and waters, another party arrived. They were greeted and seated and provided their drinks and appetizers all BEFORE our waters ever arrived at our table. By the time we placed our food orders, these people were being brought their main dishes and chatting happily with another member of the waitstaff. When our food FINALLY came, it was terrible. My husband's curry was not only runny and bland, it had a slick of oil on top. My panang curry was also bland as well as being GRITTY. The food was unpalatable, but we were sick of being there so we flagged the waitress to get our check. I will NEVER return to this place and will warn others not to come here. I would have given only 1 star, but the first time we came, the food was fantastic.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Went there for lunch buffet and found it be only a few items. Very limited selections. Food is good though but wished there was more. Give 3 stars for limited items.

Not an authentic Indian restaurant plus it has just gotten worse esp in terms of customer service. The owner who know works as a waiter as well is quite annoying. Can't sit and eat there as he keeps coming to ask how is everything about 100 times and would not let eat. Always lies esp on take outs says he would be giving fresh made food but does not. Recently gave me naans that we're two days old. Previously gave me biryani with breast pieces when he promised to give me leg pieces. On confronting would be so defensive like a kid!! Would never go there again rather would be reporting him to business bureau.

This place is great because it is the only (Lebanese?) restaurant on Frankfurt Ave. I don't like to walk that far from my apartment because I was born with an inherent laziness I have yet to learn how to shake, and this place is pretty "in the thick of it" in Fishtown. Suraya stops serving food at 330pm, which I cannot rationalize, as they have an enormous, dining-oriented space. I spent a good 15 minutes zoned out at my table mulling over their business model and how it doesn't financially pan out. The prices are high, but the food is pretty unique and includes fresh ingredients. Though when you order the "Mezze plate" be aware that is comes with a bowl of chopped vegetables that are secretly resting on ice cubes. I found it fascinating that while I drank my glass of red wine (+1 star for their liquor license), my small salad sunk into what I thought was maybe a pool of succulent middle eastern dressing, but was really just melted ice. Please note they charge an additional 1 dollar for chili oil, which my family found blasphemous. My father has, "worked hard for a dollar every day of his damn life and will be f****** struck down by God's own light if he's going to spend that money on a tiny bowl of spicy indian oil." Though archaic in delivery, I can see his point. When I suggested that maybe we should "just go to Applebee's," my hipster brother pitched a fit and my dad responded with, "Oh why don't you go spin your vinyl soundtrack of Dallas Buyers Club in your room;" so here we are, silently eating foods we cannot pronounce. Overall 7.5/10 experience, subtractions for the high prices and limited hours, additions for the liquor license and Counter Girl patience regarding my verbally unbridled PáPa.

Although the place was crowded, we were seated quickly. The lighting is low and the interior is nice. The booths look great but they were all taken. The crowd seemed mostly to be of middle-age and older, and almost all seemed upper-middle class, kind of rich. People were dressed up. First, the service was excellent and attentive and knew how to talk up the menu items and push the drinks and desserts. The menu is a little high priced for me personally, but offered a lot of variety, all manner of mediterranean; Italian, Turkish, Greek, etc. I ordered an eggplant dish and my boyfriend ordered a shrimp dish. We got a mixed bread basket and the table olive oil standard. Our food was delicious, well-seasoned and prepared. Also, the server pronounced it "Pan Dah-LEE-vay"

Beware of what you eat!! This is one of the most unpleasant thai restaurant I ever been. I was petrified from this and have gotten sick for the rest of the day. I came with my boyfriend to eat lunch, and obtained noodles from the food stand. Unknowingly, I heard a loud CRUNCH when I was chewing on it, and revealed that it was a cockroach. I alarmed the manager about this and she was apologetic. Then she offered me a second plate of noodles, and this time, I discovered a tangled piece of hair in it. The lady apologize again and offered to give our money back, however, I was nice enough to let them keep it. As a result, I and my boyfriend left and never coming back again.
Stopped by for lunch. Had ginger scallion beef. It was great, long thin strips of ginger in the dish. Lunch menu is only $6 or $7 a dish. Decor was clean and modern.

Good fg pita with felafel. Much better place to stop and eat off I-75 than a chain restaurant. Handmade quickly and we ate outside on a beautiful afternoon. Too full but we are saving the baklava for later. My sons enjoyed gyros and kabob wraps. Not a huge fan of the tabouli with green peppers but nicely dressed. Wish it had more tomatoes. Thanks for a great experience.

Great, friendly service, great food! Get to build your own dish, whether it's a salad, pita, or bowl- like at qdoba/Moe's/chipotle, they walk you down the line to make your dish. Very clean place. Only complaint is that the music was too loud to hold a conversation with those you are sitting across from at the same table.

I went here with two of my friends just last night. First, the security guard outside was rude as I don't know what. He asked for IDs and our bags, but no one heard him the first time and I let him know. Unbelievably rude and unprofessional. Once inside, it was dark and not too comfy. The server gave us (3 people) one menu. I noticed that they put 20% gratuity for 3-4 people and I was over it by that time. One of my friends told me that he (the server) asked if we were with the other minorities there and I don't know if that was because we are minorities or not. I decided to leave because I thought the prices were high and it wasn't a great atmosphere. I gave it 2 stars because it could've been a good place, but the set up and the encounters before we were served just didn't rub me right.
The smells were intoxicating right when I went inside. Really delicious and hearty chicken and rice. The gravy really makes it! The beef patties were crispy and flakey outside and tasty inside.

business_name: Ratchada Thai Restaurant and Sushi Bar
text: This is fine for lunch, reasonable portions for reasonable price, and reasonably authentic. After 4 or 5 visits, I have yet to have a dish spicy enough for even me - and I always order something with the spicy symbol. Asking for high levels of spice seems to help, but also seems to just result in sri racha sauce being added and nothing more. No chili oil to help you 'spice to taste' so I'm always a little disappointed. That being said, there should be something for everyone here, vegetarian or not, very hungry or just looking for a snack. Makes for a good quick working lunch with a small group.
