The folks at SoBro Cafe apparently decided to take an extended holiday vacation, so my friend and I opted for La Mulita instead - best fate-driven decision ever. Situated to the left of Delicia, this is a great little spot with a bar, variety of wooden tables for small groups, and some booth seating for a few pairs of couples in the back. Decor is a touch industrial, but unique and fun, with big string lights hanging across the ceiling. Bit more of an intimate atmosphere - nothing wild and crazy...or at least, not on a Wednesday night. Food-wise, my friend and I opted for a cocktail each (about $6-7 each), split an order of guac ($5 - delicious!) and ordered our own cemitas (a.k.a. slider sandwiches). I ordered the veggie and I'm pretty sure I could live off these things - breaded eggplant as the "burger," topped with roasted red peppers, cheese, and chipotle mayo on a bun (recommend removing the nob on the bun and eating that separate, btw). We also split an order of churros ($3.50) and while good, I'd prefer a thicker, chocolate-ier sauce. This was more like dipping it in hot chocolate, which wasn't quite substantial enough in the presence of all that fried doughy goodness! Overall, though, very pleased with the food. Service was fantastic - very attentive and helpful in explaining drinks, entrees, and portion sizes. Will definitely be returning - chilaquiles are calling my name!
The first time having Indian Food and i was impressed.. Naan is amazing ... We loved it ..I ll be back again
You're not gonna find a better place to eat Greek food. It's delicious the sizes of the dishes are perfectly portioned and seasoned extremely well.

I've come here for breakfast/brunch a few times. Always a good meal and service. A couple times the wait was longer than they predicted, but it's a small place and one of the only good options in the area (sorry Harrison house). Will be back again!

It's rare to go to a buffet and say that everything you try is amazing, but that's what I do every time I'm here. Hands down the best Indian food I've had anywhere. And besides the buffet being awesome, they will bring MORE delights to your table! Bring your appetite. Great value for the money!

I live in the Bay Area now but my parents are still in Santa Barbara. We always go to Meun Fan when we come to town for a visit. I am so happy Meun Fan opened a Goleta branch. I love their drunken noodles and Thai iced tea. I could live on that stuff. The staff is always fast and friendly and this new location is awesome!

Flambo was EXCELLENT from the service to the food and everything in between. I had the escovitch (spell check?) fish with a side of the macaroni & cheese. It was delicious! A friend ordered the plantains and they were to die for! During dinner the restaurant played my favorite reggae and soca hits. The owner came out to check on us multiple times and even let us sample a dish he was considering adding to the menu. Kevin was awesome, too! We'll definitely be back.

I have gotten pho to-go a few times here, as it's an easy stop on my way home from work. I have thought the pho was fine. Not amazing, not memorable, but it hit the spot when the pho craving grabbed me. We ate in the restaurant on Saturday night, and again, it was just fine. We tried the Bò 7 món (7 Course of Beef Dinner). I have had this at a restaurant in Pinellas County, and while that experience was definitely a 5/5 Star experience, this was only a 3/5 Star. When we arrived, we were the only people in the place, but service was still slow. They also forgot a drink we ordered, but we just ended up cancelling it. To start with, they brought out our burner of oil, the first course of beef, and the wraps - but not the vegetables to put into the wrap. That took a good five more minutes to come out. Things did progress pretty quickly after that, though, with the other courses coming in a timely manner. We did the meal for "3", and some of the courses I thought they were pretty skimpy for 3 people. Of all the courses, I would say my favorites were the grilled beef wrapped like a sausage, and the beef congee at the end of the meal. They also screwed up my credit card payment at the end of the meal (and ended up hand-writing it in, which is sketchy at best). I'm sure I'll be back for some to-go pho, but I'm still on my quest for a good Bò 7 món in the Tampa area.

I ordered takeout one evening on my way home from class and we enjoyed everything we got. A couple notes - this location has a very small dining room, though it is tastefully done. Also - you get 10% off for takeout orders. Makes this a nice way to go. My order was ready in about 20 minutes and included a complimenatary rice pudding desert. What I ordered - for an appetizer, Gulistani Kabob from their special menu - 5 round fritters. Real tasty in the mint chutney and tamarind chutney. For breads, the Paneer Naan stuffed with cheese - very nice - and the Peshawari Naan with dry fruit and nuts, bringing a sweet flavor for a change of pace. For our main course I got the Ekta Dal with yellow lentils - a bit watery perhaps but still tasty - and the Lamb Rogan Josh, a traditional lamb curry, which had a dark color and was very satisfying. A couple of mango lassis rounded things out - they have other favors as well, I think they mentioned pomagranate - those would be fun to try. Overall I had a good experience, and saving 10% plus not having to tip makes takeout here tempting. I will return to sample more of their menu.

Veggie Szechuan dumplings are delicious! Burnt garlic rice and the General Tso was also delicious. We ordered delivery and the containers were perfect, not cheap or allows spills. Can't wait to try more!

This place gets busy fairly early in the evening. I love the Greek Salad (skip the Greek with Greens - the plate is to large for the tiny tables), Baba ganouch, and their Pita - right from the stove and crispy around the edges. The appetizer size of the Calamari is out of this world. Ask for a side of red sauce for this. The scallops are incredible. If you can't get a table.. sitting at the counter is a really cool experience. You get to watch this asembly line of wait staff manage all these moving parts of the restaurant. You'll also get an ear shot of some of the wait staff bashing the customers. While the restaurant runs very efficiently, there is this air of arrogance from the wait staff that can be diasppointing. They are not there to speak to you, only to take your order, serve you food, and impatiently wait for you to leave so the next in line can have a seat. They use very little spice in all their meals. It's basic, satisfying, with no frills. Bring a bottle of white, and enjoy.

I rarely give 1 star reviews, but I will definitely not be coming back, even for a the Halal dinner menu. Taste of India is basically the Mc D's of Indian food. It's edible, but it's definitely a $8 meal. I decided to try it because, and only because, it was $1 cheaper than the other indian places. Honestly, I suck at cooking and I would have preferred staying at home andeating my own leftovers. I'd stick with India Garden or Kabab and Curry, whichever people seem to prefer. India garden tends on the sweet-savory side and Kabab and Curry tends to be on the spicey-savory side. Very disappointed at the salty-sweet everything at Taste of India. I came in here with pretty low standards as most of the Indian places in Reno have a buffet that, while tasty, isn't made to order and is thus kind of lacking. Plus the reviews trend was bottoming out. Yes, I am one of those people that's willing to give a place with awful reviews a shot. This place literally tastes like leftovers from home. Indian food is not one of the things that only gets better as leftovers, like my husbands homemade chili, or cold pizza for a hangover. The place was totally empty when we came in, one of the workers were eating and watching tv and we bummed around in the front for a while before we were greeted and seated. Being the only person in my party who is used to broken english, I was the only one who could communicate that, yes, we wanted water and yes, we wanted garlic naan --which was more like roti. I am not usually concerned about folks speaking broken english, but it's impractical to have the host be the person in the place whom speaks the least english. We saw there was coke, but she could only understand pepsi and mango lassi. Half of the hot plates were empty on the buffet, and they had NO chutneys. Very disappointing. They had maybe 8 pans of food and 2 of them were meat. One had, strangely, ground beef. That was incredibly weird to me, but I shrugged it off because this place serves Islam-appropriate meat products, so I figured it might be some kind of middle-eastern fusion deal. The basmati rice was crunchy? How the hell does that happen? If even one of the dishes were hot spicy and not salty or salty sweet, I might have given this place two stars because it's quaint and cozy inside and the staff was nice, dispute because sparse.. The previous reviewers spoke the truth and the downward trend spells disaster for this place. Someone get this place on Kitchen Nightmares before it goes totally under. I have a feeling their "amazing deals" and limited selection is because they're having a hard time keeping patrons coming back. I hate to give a one star review, but, there it is.

Awesome Greek food at such a low price! Extremely friendly staff and quick service. I had a chicken gyro and hummus, and my husband had a plate meal. Both were fantastic, and we were so glad to find such a great lunch spot when we were passing through Franklin.

My family and I have been regular customers since they opened and previously would have always given Fulin's four stars or so. But the menu has recently changed. Specifically, we're vegetarians and just about all those options went away with the new menu, replaced by some vegetable "casserole" that is actually a soup. It's very disappointing since before the menu change they were one of the best vegetarian friendly restaurants in the area. I hope they eventually find their way back to better rounded options.

We had a wonderful experience at Siamese Princess. The soup appetizers were delicious - I had the clear vegetable soup, and my wife had the coconut soup. We followed by splitting the orange chicken. Our waiter was friendly & attentive. We'll return!

This is my italian-got-a-toddler-and-families-in-town GO TO. The service is great, the food is VERY satisfying, and the place is always full of old-fashioned italian families on a Sunday night (yes that counts for something in my book). My only problem? Parking.

You know, when your server greets you with a smile and goes about her job with a positive attitude, it can make your whole meal experience go well. And when you top it off with a delicious sandwich and side, you earn a 5-star rating. So it was with La Mulita. I grabbed a spot in the lot behind the building and when I entered the restaurant, the sign directed me to seat myself, so I grabbed a spot outside the "bar rail" and sat in the dining area. My server was busy delivering someone else's order and I soon realized she was not only doing the waiting, but running the bar too! She went by dropping off a glass of ice water, apologized for the wait and said she would be back in a minute as soon as she delivered the drinks to the couple by the window. She immediately returned and took my order. Efficient and friendly. In relatively no time, she brought out my Cubano and my side of sweet potato wedges served with a serrano aioli. The first bite of the sandwich let me know the bolillo (bread) had been toasted with the crispness of the bite. Then Wow! The flavor of the combo was great! There was a delicious grilled flavor in the ham & pork. There was also a pickled tomatillo and Chihuahua cheese adding to the blend. I then tried a sweet potato wedge which was lightly crisped and salted. The sweet/salt combo was good. Then I dipped one in the savory serrano aioli and that punch of flavor was all it needed to take the flavor to the next level. Simple flavors, but in the right combination, can make for a nice surprise. All too soon, the meal was devoured and I thanked the server for a great experience. Review #682

My boyfriend and I finally tried this place after hearing good things about it from his roommate. I myself was skeptical, but I was eventually persuaded. However, I was right about being skeptical. The place seemed dirty, and since there was only one worker when we came, it took a REALLY long time for our order to come out. The chicken we ordered was bland, even with sauce. Not worth it at all. Definitely not coming back here.
The food wasn't fresh, it was served immediately after we placed our order! And be aware that medium spicy means very spicy!!

One day I was desperately craving falafel but knew Mama's was closed for a Jewish holiday. So I searched "falafel" on yelp and this truck came up. It's only a few blocks from my work so I was excited. When I got there the line was about 6 deep. The falafel guy was ranting on and on about prices of running a cart and purchasing quality food. The people in line just looked around helplessly, occasionally nodding in his direction when they were unfortunate enough to make eye contact. There was no menu and I didn't actually hear anyone order (regulars?) until the guy standing in front of me got up to bat (he ordered two sandwiches and got a 20 minute lecture about ordering more than one sandwich). Once he'd scurried away, I ordered mine. It was 8 bucks and gigantic. I eagerly unwrapped it and took a bite. I gotta say, I was disapointed. The chicken was a little dry and unseasoned. The falafel was charred. The flavors were strange. And the hot sauce was non-existent. All in all it was...okay. But considering I stood in line for 35 minutes and listened to the same story told over and over (and over), it just wasn't worth it. Based on the other reviews, I might have gone on an off-day but Mama's will always have my heart.

This is a terrific place. We've had great times here with friends and family. Excellent food, atmosphere, & service. Dishes are unique. Definitely try the specials. They change frequently depending on the availability of fresh ingredients (so we were told by the chef). Desserts were great. This is a hidden treasure in downtown N. Wales.
Excellent happy hour prices for both drinks and snacks. I haven't been for dinner but HH is great!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Order the Naan as soon as you sit down. It's the best compliment to all the scrumptious offerings on the buffet tables. I can't tell you what I just ate by name, but it was all delicious and obviously made with love and served with pride. Oh, and order the mango Lassi!

Right now I am thinking, how to write up a great review then I realized that I can simply say that the Oriental Pearl Restaurant is great restaurant, but they deserve better from me. Located in Chi-Chester Pennsylvania is The Oriental Pearl. This is my go to restaurant for Pho, but before we dive into The Oriental Pearl let's briefly talk about Pho itself. Pho is a Vietnamese beef based soup dish made with thin cuts of beef (Ex. brisket/steak/round cuts), beef bone broth cooking for almost 8 to sometimes 24 hours, rice noodles, onions, scallions, and spices (ex. star anise, cinnamon). Another ingredient is tripe which can be omitted when ordering Pho if you're not yet ready to take the next step. When you're served Pho it is generally accompanied with sweet basil, sprouts, limes, and jalapeños on a separate plate. Sriracha, Hoisin sauce, and other hot pepper combinations are offered as well. I generally order Pho with extra onions, and sometimes with tripe if I need a self humbling session. When the Pho is placed on the table I begin to move the rice noodles around to separate them as the noodles swim in the broth absorbing the flavorful elixir. Next I begin eating without incorporating any additional ingredients or condiments. Near the mid-point I then begin to add the basil (tear it up with your hands), and a small squeeze of lime juice. Pho can differ in terms of taste depending on on where you go. It can be very beefy, very herbal, or balanced. I enjoy all variations as I appreciate each dish equally. The service, and most importantly the food at Oriental Pearl is amazing. You are greeted with hot tea, and do yourself a favor by ordering the spring rolls and summer rolls for your appetizers. What impresses me the most is their consistency. I am never disappointed when I leave, and when I arrive I feel like I am right at home. If you are looking to take a step into Vietnamese food cuisine, and you live in the Tri-State area give the Oriental Pearl a shot, you will not regret it.

If you are looking for good sushi, this is not the place. I've eaten there many times and the sashimi / nigiri is just consistently below quality. I'm finally writing this review because maybe the restaurant will read this and try to provide a more quality product. YUCK. The fish never seems fresh enough. I"m a purist when it comes to sushi. However, if you like your rolls fried and dunked in sauce so heavy you can't recognize what you're eating, you might like this place. Sakura in hermitage is better by far! The cooked food is good though. My husband gets the sesame chicken. That's why I'm giving this place a 2 star rating.

This place may be a little out of the way but it is well worth it. It is reasonably priced and a well kept secret. The lunch and dinner portions are a lot for what you pay for. They have great kabobs. My favorite is the goat. The kibbeh and grape leaves are yummy! I highly recommend this to any one that is a fan of middle eastern food. So much better than Mona's and such.
Best Thai I've had! Don't let the lonely atmosphere deter you! Very authentic cuisine. The staff was also greatly amiable and even allowed me to sample a dish!
Cost for food just doesn't live up to expectations at all. 5 dollars for fist size portion of broccolini??? Pass.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: This is back to back nights for me. This place is a gem. Service is friendly and very hospitable. The soups are a must try. I guarantee you will be dreaming of this place after your first go round.

So... I have frequented this particular Hookah bar numerous times. I've spent an insurmountable amount of money here. Tonight, forced my decision to NEVER, ever return. My cousin and I usually go every other Sunday to have a few drinks and smoke hookah. We generally know exactly what we're ordering, and how much we will spend. Brugada advertised $10.99 hookah on Sundays. Tonight, we decide to patronize the bar, on a very rainy, and cold evening. We order our hookah and the waitress brings it out. The issue came when it was time to pay. When the waitress brought our check out, I had to question the total that she charged to my card, because I honestly was uncertain of the amount. After respectfully approaching the waitress about my ticket, she became a bit attitudinal. I gave myself the opportunity to process what she said to me and how she approached my inquiries, and hen realized that her justification of what she charged me was still incorrect. I explained to the young lady that our total for ONE hookah (two guests) was supposed to be $10.99 (excluding taxes), and that my total should NOT have been $22.28. The waitress' disposition became aggressive, as she snatched the ticket from the bartop, exclaiming "I'm gonna go get my manager." She, the waitress later came out and informed us that they were unable to refund what was charged in error, but we could "come back on a SUNDAY" and they would take care of the hookah. THIS. DID. NOT. SIT. WELL. IN. MY. SPIRIT. Like, how do you tell me in one breath "there's is no way I can refund what I have charged you, IN ERROR," then, in the same breath offer complimentary service WITH STIPULATIONS. I respectfully asked to speak with the "manager." She comes out and I explain to her what had transpired, further expressing my concerns for her resolution. The manager then explains to me that they recently received a new POS system, and that she wasn't privy to processing refunds. To me, she was dishonest when she informed the waitress that "they couldn't do it." It wasn't that they couldn't, she lacked the proper training, as a manager. The manager, again reiterated that we could come back and receive complimentary service WITH STIPULATIONS... at this point, I informed her that I would NOT be returning and that I would be disputing the charge. I will continue to be a loyal patron to Arabian Palace in Antioch, TN.

What a gem and how is it that I've not had the pleasure of this establishment in the past? Do yourself and favor and give it a try! We hosted our Fine Dining Meetup here on 11.21.15. And while the price point was below what I would normally consider "fine dining" the food and service fit the classification. Our group of eight were all first-timers to Pan D'Olive. We had a reservation which was difficult to make - you leave a voicemail and are told someone will get back to you, but I had to make several more calls to finally speak with someone to confirm our date/time. But we were seated promptly! We were at a long table to the side of the bar area. I would normally say this is a great location for a group, but on this night there was a wedding just down a flight of stairs and the music from the wedding made it very difficult for our group to converse. We asked if there was anything that could be done, but were told unfortunately, no. We survived; it wasn't the end of the world. Around the table we all had drinks. Some mixed, some wine, some beer. The Belgium Ranger IPA ($6) and the French Martini were the favorites. For starters, we had calamari (roasted tomato marinara & caper aioli $7), spinach salad (candied walnuts, cranberries, gorgonzola, pomegranate vinaigrette $6), and mussels (garlic, tomato, clam jus $8). Both reasonably priced and flavorful. The calamari was a bit tough, but not terribly so. Our entrees were Pan D'olive flatbread (x2) (chicken, mushroom, olive, gorgonzola, caramlized onions $12), Shrimp Scampi (Eagean style with lemon, butter, garlic $22), Lamb Shank (asparagus, lamb jus, rice pilaf $25), Branzini (charbroiled, lemon $25), Lobster Ravioli (rock shrimp, spinach, tomato, sherry cream $17) and the Filet ($24). The filet, Lamb Shank and Branzini are all gluten free, and the Lamb and Branzini are available only in limited quantities. So, our group assessment? The Pan D'Olive Flatbread, Shrimp Scampi and Branzini...all heavenly! The other dishes were good as well, but these seemed to be the stars of the show. The prices and service were great! I couldn't believe the size and quality of my scampi for $22. The flatbreads are large enough to share. The lamb shank got an "ok" rating. Certainly not terrible, just not the best lamb he'd ever had. Our service was excellent! Seated quickly, coat check, drinks always filled, gracious server, food served hot. Slight language barrier, but nothing we all couldn't work with. A couple of hints: The Branzini is served whole. I mean head on, folks! They will remove it for you in the kitchen if you ask. So, be prepared. Also, parking is a bear! Guys, if you're on a first date, you may want to offer to drop your date at the door to save her walking in those high heels she's wearing to look great for you. And although we had a party of eight, they split the checks info four for us and didn't add required gratuity. So tip your server well! And lastly, if you're going with a large group, try to ensure you get in the main dining area if there is a function downstairs. I'd say give it a try! We will definitely go back!

Solid Thai food in the heart of the CBD. The service can be sketchy, but the food comes out ridiculously fast. I tend to favor the pad thai or the pad won sen, both of which are consistent every time. If you like them, the fresh spring rolls are extremely well done. I've had the chicken curry dish before and its pretty good, but be careful in ordering "Extra Spicy" as it'll make you sweat, even if you're used to hot food.
Amazing food, great service, not super roomy, but enough space for big families. Authentic taste and feel.

3 stars for the service, 4 for the food. This new pho place is right down the street from me. I make a point to try out all the new places in my neighborhood, so I stopped in here on a busy Wednesday night. The interior is simple, with coffee shop-style seating with two-tops and no elbow room. The menu, conversely, is expansive, with over 60 menu items including appetizers and entrees. I had the pho with brisket and flank and tripe and it was delicious. The meat was cooked perfectly and the broth was flavorful. I will be coming back here to try the rest of the menu.
Not the best, but also not the worst Pho that I've had. The broth really lacked flavor. Very friend staff on the other hand.

I stumbled upon this place and am REALLY glad I did! It's a nice bright place on the main road of Irvington with friendly, attentive service. I ordered the Chopped Salad and a glass of Sauvignon Blanc. The salad was fresh, very large and the basil dressing was wonderful. Wine was inexpensive yet good quality. I would definitely come back again!

OMG one of the best fish tacos I ever had. Fried just right a great amount of dressing and very heavy in your hand. My daughter had a cheese quesadilla and I have never heard her say she loved a food but she finished it along with the pico de gallo she never eats all her food. Even tho it wasn't on the menu they made it for her cause she was sad Lol thanks Guys!!!

I went in with mixed expectations looking out for all the things that previous reviewers had mentioned. The place was small, but it was just two of us and we happened to go slightly early for dinner so we got a table near the kitchen. (It appeared that the back had all been reserved) Service was just fine. I'm not a big fan of extra chattiness and we got just the right amount of attention..nothing more and nothing less. The food portions appeared to be a bit small so I was slightly disappointed...but the dishes we ordered the chicken kabob, chawla kadu and burani were delightful. The chicken was tender, the slow cooked eggplant (burani) was delicious and the chawla kadu had the enhanced flavor of the sweet pumpkin. Overall a satisfactory experience...but it is not a $ sign place. I would say $$.

Sunrise is a breakfast and lunch place, but I can't figure out why they are open for dinner. Nobody was in the restaurant when we arrived, and a trickle of mostly take-out customers came through during the excessive amount of time we spent there. Kids wanted gyros. Two stars because the pita was soft and warm, which did me no good because I don't eat bread (great for bread eaters though). The shish kebob took half an hour, and then was chewy and really not worth the wait - I can make much better fare at home. Unfortunately they have no clue about kids, and didn't offer to bring out the kids' food early; when we asked about the delay, they did bring it out, but it still took a while. The had 2 people working and they said that they weren't used to being so busy at night. As stated above, skip it for dinner, unless you call in and pick it up 45 mins later to take home!

Favorite Carmel Indian restaurant. Buffet is always great. Fridays are especially great for the buffet since they have the vegetable majestic in the selection. Dinner menu is priced well. Alot of vegetarian options which is superb.

Just left this great place. Early dinner for the kids and me. We started out with the asian fries which is new to the menu for happy hour I think. They were delicious. The service was great also. We'll definitely go back.
Great value for the portions of your food. Quick service and seating. It's super casual and a quick bite!

I had dinner at this restaurant last night with a couple of friends. The restaurant truly lived up to all of the wonderful reviews on Yelp. I just ate leftovers from #32 (a vegetable curry dish) and enjoyed it even more the "second time" around. Really wonderful restaurant!

After reading several good reviews, I was looking forward to trying Thai 5. However, I was disappointed. The portion sizes were too small; I was still hungry after dinner. I also think the dishes lacked spice and depth. This place seems way overrated. I may give it another try, and if I do, I will update my review.

Yummy, great quality falafel. The turkey schwarma and fries are not great, way too oily, but everything else is pretty damn good. The service is always friendly, love the bald guy pushing the salad bar like my mama would would be! I have been put off by the buddies of staff that at times take over the joint and the outdoor tables, but over all I always recommend the place.
Fast and efficient service...good food...clean atmosphere...authentic Indian as well...will be back when in the area again.

Maybe a 4.5. Note- this review is specifically based on the buffet. 400- BOOM. Thought I'd mark this milestone with one of my favorite places in Indy. A friend (yes, he happens to be Indian) recommended this place to me. He claimed this to be the best Indian in the naptown area. I had to examine the claim. AMBIANCE- The place is in a strip mall, but when you walk in, the place is bright and open (unlike many Indian restaurants I've been to). Seating is probably about 50-60ish, though they may have a backroom (I cant' recall). SERVICE- for a buffet, I didn't really expect much service. The servers were friendly though, and were very quick to replenish the naan (more on that later). MENU- this place has to have one of the more exhaustive selections as far as a buffet goes. Many of your favorites can be found here- palak paneer, rav korma, pakora, tikka masala, goat curry, tandoori chicken etc.... They have an interesting "Chicken 65" which in my opinion is like boneless buffalo wings Indian style. Standard desserts such as mango pudding and kheer (rice pudding) can be found, as well as chai to finish up the meal. Oh yeah, the naan. They bring out fresh orders of naan (either garlic or regular) with the buffet as well. FOOD- most everything is delicious. I must say I was a little disappointed with the palak paneer as it seemed to be a little too pureed in my opinion, and it being a buffet, the food tends to lack a little heat, but you can always add some spice if you need to. The garlic naan is really strong, but very good as well. The kheer has raisins, but you can pick them out if that ain't your thang. OVERALL- come hungry, leave happy. This place rocks. $9 for lunch (plus you can get a $1 off coupon at indycoupons.com) is money well spent. If you've been wanting to try Indian food, or are just looking for some good Indian food, this is your best bet. Do it up. Celebrity Rating- DJ Khaled

We really enjoyed the food here but were not fans of the pacing. We ordered 5 smaller plates and they started arriving before drinks hit the table and within five or so minutes of the first small dish appearing, our table was full (so full I was nervous I'd knock something over) of food. I understand often times dishes come out when they are ready, but your entire meal should not come out at once like that. Not sure if it was a kitchen issue, a service issue, or what, but hopefully it was just an off night. If I return, I would probably make sure to let them know I'd prefer slightly more time between dishes. As for food, we got the octopus, lamb ribs, merguez kabob, cauliflower and berbere carrots as well as an addition of the garlic yogurt. The vegetable dishes were the standouts, but everything was tasty. Presentation was also beautiful.
Went for brunch and was very pleased with everything! I got the Migas which were delicious. Exactly what I remember from my time in TX!

This is one of the best Vietnamese restaurants in Indy. It is one of a handful on Lafayette Road, but this is the best in my opinion. Please do not go here and get Chinese food, it is good, but you can pretty much get the same thing anywhere else. Most of the Vietnamese food that I have had is very good. My favorite is the spicy beef noodle soup called Bom Bu Hue. All of the fish dishes are tremendous too, very flavorful. Get the shrimp rolls as an appetizer you will not be disappointed. The Pho, which is the traditional vietnamese dish, is good, but I have had better but it is definitely worth a try. It is a small cozy little restaurant with usually just one server, but works hard and is very friendly. So go try something new, you will love it.
The food is ok but it is the slowest restaurant in town!!! Never come here with rush!

We've been searching for a good Thai restaurant in Edmonton since we left the Bay Area (California). Even though we tried all the ones our friends recommended (Syphay, Bua Thai, Viphalay, Boualouang, King and I), Numchok Wilai is the best. Just when I was loosing hope that we would ever find a good one. The seafood soup was really flavourful, not just spicy. The mango salad was delicious, reminded me of how a Thai friend use to make it. The curry and pad tai were also really good. I usually use the pad tai as my benchmark at every Thai restaurant. All the other restaurants make it too sweet and saucy, which may appeal to some folks, but is not really authentic. This place makes it with tamarind flavour...as it should be. So if you like the pad tai at the other restaurants I listed above you may not like this place, but this is the real deal.

From the creators of Delicia, La Mulita is a new casual and cheap lunch and dinner option location in SoBro. La Mulita is in the same building as Delicia and located right off of College and 52nd. One of the downsides that I can see to this location is parking. Yes, it is great that there is small lot in front and back, but if both restaurants are busy, I could see having to hunt for street parking. The restaurant is on the smaller side, having a mix of lower level tables and high top tables, with additional sitting at the bar. There are three tvs that allow you to watch a game while you dine. It's decor is that of a very polished cantina. The little extra touches, such as the brick wall, decorative tin on the under bar, and the light shades made of cans on the wall, shouldn't go unnoticed. The ceilings are on the high side, so it will most likely get loud at times. The menu has a nice variety of choices. If your looking to find the same food as Delicia, you will not see it on the menu. The only things in common between these two restaurants are the guacamole, sangria, and margarita. The menu does note which items are vegetarian. While there is no gluten free menu, the salads, soups, and tacos are either gf or can be altered to be gf. Starting off the meal with a Rum Punch, which packed punch, I felt the need to offset all of that sweetness with something a little bit salty and on the healthier side. The side of kale chips fit the bill perfectly. Looking over the taco choices, it was hard to decide which one to chose, luckily there is a combo in which you can choose two for $7. I opted for the grilled shrimp taco and carne asada taco. The tacos are on the smaller side, but do not let that fool you. They were packed full and extremely filling. The carne asada taco was good. The skirt steak had a nice marinate to it, but it was the grilled shrimp taco that stole the show for me. It was amazing. The pickled slaw and honey chipotle sauce complemented each other very well. I will definitely be back for some more shrimp tacos, and would recommend anyone looking for a cheap and filling meal, with great service to try La Mulita.

The food is quite tasty, and the service was attentive, friendly and informative. And it's not exactly a "hole-in-the-wall" as someone else stated -- although it's simple, it's somewhat charmingly decorated. The pastry appetizers (whatever they're called) were actually our favorite part of the meal. The main part of the meal is served on injera on a large round platter. The injera on the platter is suffused with the juices from the food resting on it, which makes it delicious but difficult to eat with. Fortunately, they provide a basket with additional injera. The injera is, well, weird. It has a really strange consistency which I could never get accustomed to, but it is fun to eat the food with it. Seems like this would be a fun place to go with a small group, as long as no one was too squeamish about everyone's hands all over the food.
Two of us had the veal marsala. Meat was tough. Hard to cut and chew. Salads were ok. Pleasant atmosphere and service. No reaon to go back.

I was in there last Thursday and food was utterly delicious. The service was quick with good quality of food. I even got free desert from the manager would definitely recommend people to try this place.

Delicious schwarma, huge portions, had enough for another meal. My dinner partner had gyro sandwich. Salad dressing was very good also. Also huge portions. Wine by the glass was ok. Service good. Prices reasonable. Will return.

Supposedly this place used to be good, and i ate here a few years ago and it was great, tonight my fish was overcooked- burnt in fact, the sides were bland- nothing i couldn't have made better and cheaper myself.
Way too expensive. I like tale atmosphere, but the cost is just too high in comparison to neighboring coffee shops.
The Pork Souvlaki is on point. Add some lemon to it for the right taste. GreKo salad is phenomenal and don't forget to add some chicken to the salad as well.

Visited St. Louis for the first time in 5 years this past April for my college reunion, and of course I had to return to my beloved Thai Country Cafe. I thought that my love was simply based on nostalgia, but I was pleasantly surprised with how good everything was. I went back with a big group of Wash U alumni; the one disappointment was that I guess the spring rolls weren't what they used to be. I think that the Thai Iced Tea was probably the best I've ever had. Oh yea, and the boyfriend I mentioned in the previous review who took me on our first date here is now my husband so cheers to you, Thai Country Cafe!
It was good and fast delivery but the gyro had literally 2 slices of lamb and the onions had suffered from freezer burn. The upside, best tzatziki ever!!!

Love me some Greko! The staff is super friendly and the atmosphere is makes you feel like you are eating with the locals in Greece! Try the half chicken. It's awesome! What a great addition to East Nashville!

First of all, we walked in knowing what we wanted to order based on the menu online. However, once we got in, we noticed their in-store menu was different. I asked if they served an appetizer we were interested in. He stared at me like I had two heads and said it was not on the menu. I said I had seen it online and asked when the menu was changed, and said they should update it when they get a chance. The guy was very rude, and said if you look at this menu it is obvious the menu was changed which didnt answer my question at all. We ordered chicken curry, lamb saag, and some naan. I asked if they served mango lassi, since that is common at a lot of indian places. He said they have mango milkshakes. I asked what the difference was and he just said well its a milkshake. I asked if it was made with ice cream or what and he laughed and said no, then turned on his heel and disappeared in the kitchen with our order. When we got the order the "milkshake" appeared to be mango juice mixed with milk and watered down. It was purely liquid with no thickness, and was unpleasant to drink. The curry was watery and had a bland lavor, though the meat and vegetables were cooked through. There was no onion chutney like the menu claimed, unless it was pre-mixed in. The lamb saag had a better flavor, though the lamb was oddly rubbery. It was cold on the inside as if it had been frozen and then re-heated. The naan was not very good either. It also seemed microwaved. It was rubbery and tough. I probably will not be back.

Absolutely LOVE everything at Phan's. From the fresh, crispy, piping hot egg rolls to the perfectly cooked potatoes in the yellow curry. The pork and brown eggs wasn't to my taste (it's very sweet, but it's supposed to be just not my style), but literally every other bite I've had there has been phenomenal. The spicy basil chicken, the pad kee mao, and most especially the beef pad ped. Do yourself a favor and go see Phan.

Been here two times: Very good Indian food with a variety of sauces and crispy dosas. The most recent time I went was a little off as there was a lot of oil in the dosa, everything else was good. The first time was great, I got their vegetarian taster menu which I recommend. I also highly recommend the chai tea, freshly brewed with their blend of spices and fresh ginger, better than anywhere else I've had it. Great friendly staff.

Finally, a Latin restaurant that is true to its roots. This Puerto Rican restaurant is right down the road from The Cannery near the new convention center. Even though it only opened a week ago, everything went very smoothly. I was greeted by the friendly, attractive hostess and seated at a table. This atmosphere is simple, modern, and comfortable with 2 TV's if you wish to catch a game. The menu is extensive but I would suggest sticking to the Latin dishes. I had the lunch special which was a lunch sized portion of the Carne Frita which was very similar to the Cuban Masitas de Puerco (fried pork chunks). It was moist, tender, and delicious. It was served with a very tasty rice that had beans and peas in it. I can't wait to try the Fricase de Pollo, the Grouper Ajillo, the Chicaronnes de Pollo, and the Mofongo. There are other mainstream dishes available for the less adventurous. I look forward to coming in the evening and trying the passion fruit sangria.

I wanted Greek food but didn't want to travel to Tarpon. So I stopped here based on the reviews. The staff is rude, and do not know the menu. Then blamed the owner stating they were changing the menu. The food is not authentic Greek food and over priced. Don't visit. Drive to Tarpon.
Great gem for Thai food in Spring Hill. Friendly owner-staff and excellent menu of outstanding Thai cuisine. You will not be disappointed.

This review is based mainly on the Pho, I haven't really tried the other items on the menu. Having grown up around a lot of Pho restaurants back in Orange County I think I am pretty picky when it comes to Pho, but Pho Bistro really satisfies my cravings. This place has a bunch of lower reviews, but most of those are from '09. This place has really improved from when it tried it back then too. The noodles used to have a stale taste to me and the soup seemed bland in the past, however this year I have gone so many times, and none have failed to disappoint. Most of the newer reviews seem be positive, except for a few that don't make sense to me. Pros: Taste- After trying Saigon Noodle and Noodle City, I think Pho Bistro has the best broth of the 3. This to me is a pretty big deal, since Pho is all about the broth. It's much heartier then the other restaurants and you can see it for yourself, the soup just looks dense and taste heartier while the other places broths are just clear and much lighter tasting. When it comes to taste, this place beats out the others easily. Location - It's right in "The Loop", so if you live in the Isla Vista area you can just bike/walk/skate there in a matter of minutes. Great for college students in the area. Setting- The people working here are always nice. Usually it's just one person working, but every time I've eaten there I've had good service. It's a small place with a few tables, but it's always clean. Takeout - Since it's a small place I usually prefer to just go pick up some food and eat in the comfort of my house. They always package everything really nice so it doesn't fall out or spill everywhere, and I've never had to wait more then 10 minutes to get my order, if anything it's usually around 5 minutes. Tase - Tastiest PHO in Goleta. Cons: Price - It's IV so you can't expect too much of a good deal I suppose. It's rather pricey compared to the cheaper prices/larger portions you get at the other pho restaurants in the area (definitely doesn't compare to the $3.00 bowls you can get in Westminster). Portion Size - There's only one size and I find it pretty small. The bowls could have more noodles and meat. I can take down the whole bowl including all the soup pretty easily. I really think they should consider offering a larger size,. No Tripe - I know it's catered to a broader crowd, but I feel as though there are enough people in the community in Isla Vista that would appreciate tripe with their Pho and wouldn't be grossed out by it. I feel as though Tripe and Pho kind of belong together. Don't really know many Vietnamese restaurants that don't have tripe at all. Setting- I wouldn't come here with a party greater then 4, it's going to get cramped real quick. It wont be fun for your party or the people working.
Yellow Curry at Aroy is like crack. Once you try it, you will do whatever it takes to "get u some." Seriously, the best in the region.

Attending UCSB Spring Insight on the SB campus this weekend. Stopped in to Santarini's Island Grill. I have to tell you the food was so much better then anticipated and the service was even better. I ordered the chicken pita special which came with a salad, feta fries, and a whole chicken breast grilled to perfection. Truly out of this world. My wife had the gyros very fresh and tender. Delicious ! An extra shout out to Zack, only the best cashier of the UCSB campus. So if you have the pleasure of dropping one of your children off on the UCSB campus for the next four years, make a detour to Santarini's it will make those students loans easier to swallow.

Wife and I were looking for a great place for dinner our last night in St Pete beach. Wife was craving a steak and they certainly did not disappoint. I had the Rib Tips which I would recommend. Dark, nice and quiet. Great date place.
The food was excellent and authentic . The service was nice and polite but very slow. We waited one hour to get our dinner.

So excited we now have this place in Apollo beach. I've eaten a lot of falafel in my days, and this is one of the best I've had. Everything is extremely fresh, very well spiced (tabbouleh is one of those that I'm often "eh" about. This was delicious and fresh. Even "just" the rice was flavored beautifully.) I hope they stay on the right track and people continue to support this new establishment!

We love going to Avalon at Happy Hour. The atmosphere is relaxing, sometimes there is live music, and the bartenders are knowledgeable and friendly. The small plates are delicious- we really enjoy the meatballs and fried mozzarella. Wednesday's are wonderful excuse to grab a few friends/loved ones and enjoy all you can eat mussels. Red or white mussels all depends on what kind of wine you feel like drinking that night :) Always an enjoyable experience at Avalon!

Don't even go here. They have an extremely disrespectful bartender that will tell you your money isn't enough and will threaten you and disrespect you. And then talk shit about you in front of your face... even though you tipped them. Then threatened us physically and kept making phone calls to "get his brother on us." Then 2 of his female friends tried to start a physical fight and pursued us for a block as we attempted to leave the situation, as they kept egging on my bf to fight them. Very sad and unfortunate. Can't support a business that allows this kind of behavior. The owner shrugged it off as well. Very gross and it was very unnecessary. I have never been treated this way in my entire life. Not sure if the bartender was drunk, but that doesn't excuse this behavior. He was passing out free drinks to EVERYone in the bar right in front of us but had the audacity to be upset we didn't tip him more than a dollar for ONE drink and then try to get all patrons (his family and friends) to fight us while the owner hid somewhere (he didn't speak good english and seemed scared to intervene). It was pretty unbelievable.

HOLY GYRO! This place is amazing. Driving up all you see is a little trailer looking place with a small sign on the outside reading "Euro Grill". It's the type of place where everyone not in the know drives past. As you approach the door an aroma of deliciously cooking meat takes over the air. My mouth began to water. Walking in I felt like I stepped into the wrong place. I wasn't sure if I could order food or find Grizzly Adams in the corner drinking a beer. A man at a table said hi (the owner) and my first question was "are you open?" The inside has the feel of an empty dive bar that doesn't open before 9 PM. Chairs were strewn about, TVs powered off, and the general atmosphere is best described as a hole in the wall. But let me be clear, those aren't bad things. To put it plainly, Euro Grill knows what it does best and focuses efforts on the food. All of a sudden I felt like I was in Europe. The owner, his wife, and two female customers began speaking another language - Bosnian. It was wonderful to hear and I knew I was in for a fantastic lunch. I went with the Greek Pljeskavica with feta cheese and was reassured that I would not be disappointed by a fellow customer. It took 10 minutes as they prepared my sandwich to order. I walked around admiring the 1980's style swivel bar chairs and the faux brick on the walls. I couldn't help but smile at the decor; it was so plain and boring that I was in awe. I paid for my food and went back to work, styrofoam box in hand. I opened the container to find a steak looking cut with melted feta cheese laying on 2 halves of flat bread. The smell punched me in the face and I grabbed my knife and fork. I devoured everything in record time. The smell, the flavor, it was perfect. Greasy...but perfect. Euro Grill is the exact place I was looking for in Nashville. It's friendly, it has flair, and the owners are charming in a way that's hard to find these days. I'll be back tomorrow for a lighter "trip" to Bosnia.

First visit to Pita Kebabs, and it won't be my last! Ordered gyro, and stuffed grape leaves. Both were excellent. The gyro was loaded! And the meat was nicely roasted (not microwaved like the only other place in this area that serves gyros)! Stuffed grape leaves on point. And bonus...every gyro comes with order of fresh cut french fries! Yum! Even though I picked up my order just a couple of minutes before closing time... I was greeted with a smile and hot food ready to go. Sometimes these little places are the best choice. P.s. those fries did not make it home ;)
All food delicious!!! The mint chutney was the best I've had in recent memory, awesome house-made chapati too. Extremely friendly service.

Small. Friendly staff that was eager to serve. Had a great lunch. We started with very tasty hummus and pita bread. The staff quickly brought more bread as the first serving ran low. My wife had the Yee-Ro plate. She loved it. Serving was large, so we brought half of it home. I had the salmon pocket. Salmon tasted fresh and was cooked well. This was our first visit, but we'll derfnitely go back.

Thankfully there are now other coffee options in Southwest Center City (the former Graduate Hospital). LaVa often crowded + with folks almost exclusively on laptops. Good for folks looking for an office outside the office, but not a fun, convivial vibe + a bit stuffy without the level of coffee to back it. And can't say much for the eats.

Met up with several yelpers for a UYE this past weekend. Thanks to Tiffany H for introducing me to this Mid Eastern restaurant, located within view of Busch Gardens. The ambiance isn't the best but the Mediterranean food speaks volumes and is deserving of all five stars! The food is served with pickled veggies (not my thing). And the freshest tasting pita bread I've ever had the pleasure of tasting. Not the cardboard type prepackaged stuff you get at supermarket. I ordered the veggie platter which came with a fantastic hummus, crunchy on the outside falafals (yum!) stuffed grape leaves, baba ganoush and a tomato and onion salad. All this for only $13?! Nice! I also tried the fried cheese as I thought this was gonna be another fantastic explosion in my mouth but found it too salty for my taste. Was way too stuffed to even think about dessert. So many wonderful and pocket friendly choices here! Do yourself a favor and try it, you'll like it!

Smelled like sweat at the counter. Horrible rumbling sound coming from the back. There was hair in my hummus. Chicken fingers were cold and the pita bread was stale. The workers were just standing around socializing with customers who didn't want to be bothered and were trying to end the conversation. Flies were EVERYWHERE. We were asked by a worker if everything was fine. We told her that the pita bread was stale, and she offered us more. She brought it back, and inside the tin foil were 3 pieces of pita. Great. This location was amazing when it first opened, now I'd advise anyone to drive to the Bryn Mawr location instead.

I think it's just the area--but this place is pricey too. We showed up for their lunch specials and they were quick to take our orders and serve us. They move like a well oiled machine and never let a glass be less than half full. The food was quite tasty and very flavorful. We will have to stop by again soon to see how it has changed.

This place is great! Quaint and enjoyable. We hosted a small family function here. The room was perfect. Jennifer was extremely helpful and the owner even came over to chat. Food and drinks were delish. I highly recommend.

Very authentic. New to the Westbank, we were searching for a replacement to Taqueria Guerrro (Mid City - Awesome) for our quick go-to baleada needs. Super nice staff, though it helps if you speak a bit of Spanish. Nice smiles from the woman behind the counter helped me muddle through it. The menu has translations on it, so you can probably point and smile if you need to. Baleada was very good. The eggs may have been a bit dryish, but otherwise it was quality and cheap. The man-half had the Tacos Hondurenos, which were very tasty. We'll be back and you should definitely try it.
Tom yum with noodles. AMAZING!!!!! This place always exceeds my expectations. I have tried nearly everything on the menu. 100% Amazing!!!!
Don't go for a buffet. Their menu is pretty bad for buffet. Chicken manchuria, Pakora and aloo dry items are oily and tasteless. Tandoori chicken is basically rubber. A STRICT NO!!

I came here for the tofu bahn mi. I was sadly not too impressed. I liked the bread and the presentation. And it was cheap, which is a good thing. But... the tofu itself felt bland and flavorless after the marinated goodness of Fuh-Wah tofu hoagies. It tasted like they just put a chopped-up block of plain tofu there without any sort of preparation on it. It wasn't bad it just... wasn't good. I'll stick to Fuh-Wah or Ba Le. Maybe the meat offerings are better?

This was one of the best experiences I've had in a long time. The food was excellent and customer service was at its best. Anthony went out of his way to make us feel welcome and at home. Our food was brought out in a timely manner and it was finger licking good. My co-workers and I drove from MD which was a 2 hour ride, and it was worth every min of it. Anthony is a genuine person with a good heart and good spirit. I am so grateful to have met him. If you are ever in Philly, make Flambo a must have. Ceronne
Best pho I have ever had! I'm addicted to this place, as I'm there once a week! The house coffee is delicious and the service is quick and friendly. I recommend it!

Came by for dinner with friends. 730p Sat reservation. Parking is ample the lot was close to full. We sat at a corner table by the window facing the river. It is a bit tight but not uncomfortable. Quite loud. This is a byob. Our server came by, Sonia. Pleasant and informative. We each ordered starters and mains. My caprese salad was good but the tomatoes seemed a bit out of season. It had a very nice flavor. For my main I was torn between the black bass and eggplant and finally went with the eggplant. It was very good. While the portion seemed large I actually had no trouble finishing it. My wife and our friends got different dishes all were pleased. The whole wheat garlic bread is wonderful we ordered two baskets. Each had five pieces and there was a bit of angling for the last piece. The ambiance is plain, nothing special. We enjoyed our meal and the whole experience. A nice place for a good classic Italian meal. We say, Food "b", Service "a", Ambiance "c", Value "c". Mark.

Not impressed! Went here on a recommendation from a gentleman from India. Tried the buffet lunch. Firstly, almost all food was cold that is supposed to be hot or even warm. Naan bread was not served fresh to order like most Indian restaurants. Instead it was on the buffet and tasted like rubber. This is one of my favorite items at an Indian restaurant as well as onion chutney, which they had none on the buffet. First time encountering this at an Indian restaurant. Chicken Tikka had no chicken at all nor was it replenished for the entire hour that I was there. And it was only twelve thirty when I arrived. Why? This is one of your most popular dishes. The cantelope melon was good and that was about it. Not as clean as it should be. Absolutely puzzled at all the five star ratings.
Absolutely fantastic. Like the Chipotle/Qdoba of Indian food. Fresh ingredients, helpful staff, great decor and amazing food that is fast, tasty, and healthy.

I am so sorry to do this but the place actually deserve 3 plus stars but the dishonest server led me to give one star, details are as followed! We went for an early dinner around 6PM. The place is mediocre, nothing fancy but the hotel where we were staying had given a good feedback about this place. So we went in, the place was pretty empty at this time, there were may be two other tables with customers. We ordered the mix grill as an appetizer. Usually, grilled appetizers such as theses come out piping hot and you usually have to wait a few minutes before you can even touch it. But our mixed grill came out just a bit warm, like it was cooked earlier (most likely, I am pretty sure, left over from lunch buffet (take a look at the picture)) So with my over communicating personality, I politely asked the server lady if the mixed grill was left over from lunch buffet? Obviously, she wasn't going to tell me the truth... But instead of lying straight out, she could have just blamed it on the kitchen & bring me freshly grilled mixed grill.. Update: changing to 3 stars, went back for lunch buffet before leaving town. The food was good quality & did receive better service today.

We came here for a work luncheon. Since we were busy discussing work, life, and everything under the sun, our waiter/host was very patient with us. He checked on us a few times and when we sent him away again, he told us to just flag him and let us know when we were ready to order. He was so polite and accommodating! One of our party ordered the lunch special of lamb kebob, another the chicken kebob lunch special, and I ordered the Mantoo. We each tasted all the plates that came to the table, and let me tell you something: it was all delicious. The lunch kebob plates were reasonably priced (under 10.00) and the Mantoo was out of this world. My husband also had lentil soup (which he said was fantastic) and an amazing Persian tea. On the menu, Mantoo is described as ground beef and onion raviolis topped with a special yogurt and lentil sauce. The presentation is beautiful and the ravioli filling is savory, fatty goodness. You can taste the fat in the meat, and the yogurt and lentil sauces on top compliment it and cut the richness of it so that it doesn't get overwhelming. I do wish that the Mantoo came with something like rice or a salad, because all you get is the raviolis, but next time I know to order a side. We finished by sharing a baklava and Shir-Berenj (rice pudding). My friend asked us to take the baklava away from her because she was afraid she would inhale the entire thing. The rice pudding was less wet than others I've tasted, and I liked that. If you want to save a little, go for the tasty lunch specials. However, if you want to go all out, ask to sit at one of the low tables decorated with Persian rugs and hookahs, and order as many yummy dishes as you can! This would make a great spot for a special dinner with a sizeable group.

Came here with a large group after a night of drinking. Service was okay at first but when I asked for extra herbs and sprouts we were told "sharing is caring" ??? Garnish plates were small to begin with and we had a big group so I'm not sure what the problem was. The place is decent and clean and definitely used to be a Quizno's. Soup itself was fairly bland. The broth was clear and not too oily but had do depth or layers of flavor. Meat quality was good, especially the brisket. Given the lack of good Vietnamese food in the area, this could be your best option.

I went to the Pho 38 that just opened on Tabor and Adams in Northwest Philadelphia, the food is great but the service is the complete opposite! They brought out our food in a order I've never experience before. We ordered drinks, appetizers, and 3 entrees. The order came out entrees, appetizer, and maybe 20 minutes later our drinks came out. We damn there finish our course and was super thirsty at the end. On top of this awful experience we were the only table in there, a 2nd table came in but they left before we did! This is a last resort restaurant for me as far as I'm concerned.

This place has the best Middle Eastern food in town. It's a Jordanian restaurant and I'm telling you, I haven't had better shawarma anywhere this side of Jordan! Well, maybe New York, but this little Tampa gem is on the level. The food is bright, colorful, flavorful, and always consistent. I also recommend the foule; it's sooo good! I've been to 3 locations and I've found the Busch Blvd. one is larger and has the most extensive menu. The portions are large, pretty much family-style. The prices are surprisingly cheaper than I'd expect, and the people are so sweet and helpful. Sometimes they close early to host an event so call ahead to make sure they're open. Highly recommended.

Went today for the first time, read reviews first and was pleasantly surprised. Easy to understand menu, and fair price overall. The food was hot and fresh(falafel and Yee-Ro) pockets. Plus the tea was good. Will return and try dinner. Clean and nice staff as well.

Best African Food in Philly hands down no debate. Gorees food is not only halal, but also fresh, I always order cassava leaf which is amazing. Chicken dibi with extra onion sauce and make sure you get the brown rice im addicted to it.

Has dinner here last night, the place is nice, the food was very good. I ordered a souvlaki in a pita and my only problem is that it was cold We also orsered a lamb and it was overcooked and cokd, if you eat lamb you know lamb should be medium But in general the flavours were there would definitely go back

Great Food, Unpredictable Service. This is about the 8 th time at this restaurant. We ordered the fish kabob which is salmon and delicious. It took one hour to receive the meal. The waitress abandoned us and never returned. We had to go looking for her. My water glass remained empty. When we complained to the hostess, she shrugged and implied that that's life. Most good restaurants would have apologized profusely and possibly offered a gift of some kind....VERY DISAPPOINTED, especially because they recognized us as they usually do as regular customers.
Eat Well has, in my opinion, the best banh mi in the city. Perfectly spicy, cheap and delicious. Decent yakamein too.
The food is amazing and the spring rolls are a must...great service and calm atmosphere

Food in this place is good. Waiter in this place is extremely friendly. Room design is good, but too much hidden steps(drops)..... I tripped twice. But...... when we walked in there were nobody to greet and seat us, had to to walk to the almost back kitchen to ask people to get seated. Will come back again. Foods to try: The duck; the beef; fried rice.

Went around 8pm on a Saturday night. Sadly the place was mostly empty but I'm not sure why. We had garlic naan, saag paneer, chicken korma, and chicken makhani (aka butter chicken). If you want the traditional Americanized Indian cuisine, this is it. Everything we had was delicious! The bowls they serve the entrees in were deceiving because we actually got more than expected. We ended up with left overs because we ordered too much for a group of 3 ladies. I found out the weekday lunch buffets are $9.99 and on Saturdays $10.99. They also gave us a loyalty card when you get 10 stamps you get a free lunch buffet or dinner entree. The card also mentioned the restaurant was under new management. Place was clean, service was adequate, I'll definitely be a returning customer.

My review is very optimistic at this point, as I've only had food from here once so far. But I was a huge, huge fan. We ordered some takeout, using the ordering system available on Yelp. We actually got our takeout for Yelp's 2016 White Night. The food arrived ahead of schedule, and when I dared to ask for a little extra onion chutney (for a meal that included chutney), they obliged my request. We were able to get free delivery based on our location and order. Indian dishes with creme-based sauces are my personal favorite, and historically, I've used Malai Kofta as a deciding dish to determine whether I like an Indian restaurant. I took a chance, however, to try a new dish, Matar Panir, a dish I don't believe I've ever tried before at an Indian restaurant, despite my many years of going to Indian restaurants. I was blissfully happy with my selection. My boyfriend is a lover of goat curries but decided to go with Lamb Vindaloo. I sampled from his as well and was surprised how much I enjoyed it. I was one of the most delicious vindaloo dishes I've ever had. Because we were sharing food with others, we decided to get something shareable, but because an appetizer was a little too predictable, we ordered the Haveli Special Mix Grill. It was perfect for our event since we could get some extra naan and get some chutney. I thought it was pretty good, and enjoyed everything I tried, but to be honest, I'm not a tandoori type of girl. I really look forward to eventually trying out the Malai Kofta here. It really is my favorite, when it's done well.
I'm extremely picky about Indian restaurants and I would rate this great. I would give a 2.5stars if possivle. Cutlet & lassi were good. Good service Dosa was decent.

Best Thai Ive ever had! Nice music a fountain and beautiful decorations ! Curry puff appetizer is amazing . I had drunken noodke with shrimp. Everything I tasted waa fantastic and friendly service. I dont come to this area often but I will be back!

Drink was decent, atmosphere was cool, but the honey mustard wings were terrible. Initially went to discuss having any event there. I asked for event planner/manager I had emailed earlier as soon as I entered establishment. Asked again during my dinner, stayed for over a hour and no one ever never came out to talk to me!!!! Will not be spending another dime here.

Good atmosphere with booths which provide a decent sense of privacy. $5 for three filo appetizer rolls was about right. They know how to make a chocolate martini. They provided bread and olive oil and parmesan cheese as soon as we sat down. Spinich salad, filet mignon, and lobster ravioli were excellent. The attentive staff checked in with us often enough. So, five stars for this one.

We usually stick to two dishes that we know are good: green curry + veggies or chicken and panang curry. We tried to branch out on the menu once and honestly, we weren't impressed. King Market (see my review) is our first love so it's tough competition. We live super close to this place, the owners/staff are always more than friendly & it's a great default for something quick with more flexible hours than KM. Therefore, Salmon Panang, Level 4. That's really all you need to know. K, bye.

Another Great meal. Everyone cleaned their plates, even the kids. Where did we put all the food because the servings were huge. The 3 Hot was perfect. Tom Yum with shrimp was so tasty. Fresh made for sure. If you enjoy Thai then you have to visit the Thai House.

The food at Pan D'olive has been great on several occasions. The main dining area is a little tight, but has nice ambiance. The noise level is fine. The basement wine cellar is a nice place for large parties to hear each other and have a private dining experience. The service has not been very good. At least one server was very neglectful. Another server with our large party tried too hard and was just weird. Our large party had people coming and going and switching seats, and he just couldn't keep up at all. Because of the uncertainty of the service I don't think I want to risk recommending this place to out of town guests or my boss.
Mom and pop shop. This was on a weeknight. The lamb kebab was quite good as well as the Afghan bread. Service is very good. Price very reasonable. Would definitely come back.

The food was very good and I love that they have gluten free items on the menu. I was less than impressed with the waitress. She made a point to tell us that she was the only one on Tuesday's and also that if we wanted to sit in the dining room "at the other end of the restaurant" she hoped we didn't mind that everything would take a while....and it did. We went DQ

Although normally this place is very friendly and always good with their customers, today I came in to order food for myself and my kid sister .. my sister doesn't drink apple juice at all so I asked if i can replace the apple juice for a drink she would like .. they flat out told me No and that kids meal ONLY comes with apple juice ..

We have been waiting for months to get to Zeppoli. We came here last night for our wedding anniversary. It is very small and crowded so if you are a big person or panic in small spaces, get there early. We arrived at five O'clock and was greeted by a nice looking waiter who got us some bottled water and an ice bucket for our wine right away. The bread and olives were a nice treat to munch on while studying the menu. This is not your typical dipping oil. It had some olives swimming about with a wedge of lemon which gave it a nice refreshing hint of citrus. We decided to get the Antipasto Siciliano for two. It had a little bit of everything including marinated eggplant, veggies, tuna and bean salad, an array of meats and cheeses and sardines. To my pleasant surprise my husband tried everything on the plate and liked it! We ordered a small gnocchi with spinach and ricotta as our pasta course. This is not your momma's gnocchi. This bad boy is on Silcilian steroids or something because it was a big gooey ball of spinach and cheesy heaven that swam in a yummy sage and brown butter sauce. If I had this at home, I would have licked the plate clean. The gnocchi is large so get a small plate if ordering a main entree as well. There is a small selection of entrees and I was not ready to be too daring yet so I went with the rib eye. This piece of meat was probably one of the best I have ever eaten. It was marinated and crusted in a nice herb mixture which made it just melt in your mouth. It was accompanied by a nice light arugala and tomato salad. For dessert, they brought us out a plate of cinnamon sugar dusted zeppolies that were fresh and hot and sat atop a nice thick layer of chocolate or hazelnut sauce. Remembering that it was our anniversary, the very nice to look at waitstaff placed a candle in one of the zeppolies which was a very nice touch. While we waited for our check, we were given a cute little cup of almond cello. Just a sip of that made me all warm and fuzzy! This was hands down the best dinner we have had out in years. It is Silcilian so do not come here looking for meatballs and heavy pasta with sauce. Everything was perfect. I cannot wait to come back again and try something new. It is pricey but well worth it, especially if you are coming here for a celebration of some sort. By the end of our dinner, it was quite noisy but not annoyingly noisy. Everyone was laughing and drinking with their company. There was a lot of oohing and ahhhing over the food. Like I mentioned before, if you are not into a crowded little place, come early. It was small but very cute and cozy. I felt like I was eating in someone's home. Well done Zeppoli. We will be back. Thank you for making our anniversary dinner a memorable one.
This is an exceptional Ethiopian restaurant, very authentic and excellent service, it is a real treasure to Reno.

Indy is always full of surprises! La Mulita. Before I praise this place. Let me say this first - this place is pricey for tacos. So lets begin. The ambiance is quite nice and romantic. The AC is adjusted to the 'Arctic' setting, so bring a fur jacket. I ordered a campechanos taco, while it was delicious! It was $13 for two tacos and exactly one scoop of rice. Were the food worth the $13.... ehh... but it is definitely above average. 7/10 would come back for more

7:10pm: Ordered food for delivery. Was told it has to be at least $20 after placing a $15 ordered. Ok. Ordered some cake to bring the total to an acceptable level. I was told that the food will be there in 45min to 1hr. 8:20pm: Still no delivery and I'm starving. Call them up and the girl says that the delivery guy just left and I should have my food in a couple minutes. 9:20pm: Still no delivery and I get a call from an unknown number. Yes! It's the delivery guy. I'm more hungry than angry so I'm just happy that it's here. I answer and it's the girl from the restaurant. womp-womp. She asked me if I received my food. I told her, "ah... no" and she proceeds to tell me that she can't get the "delivery service guy" on the phone and doesn't know where he's at. Really? I kindly told her that I have to order from somewhere else because its been over 2hrs already. She apologized, however the tone in her voice and her lack of reconciliation made it all seem disingenuous. I guess first and foremost; Why don't you have a dedicated delivery staff? I find it outright incompetent that you can't make a delivery 4 blocks away from you (FYI: I injured my foot and couldn't walk). The fact that you rely on someone else to handle a job you, as a business, should and could handle in-house is just perplexing. Not only do you have to raise the minimum order amount to cover the service, you also have to deal with, Yelpers like me, telling the world how bad an experience I had with your with your business. Maybe in like 5 or 10 years, if this business is still around, I'll stop in and let you know how the food was. Until then, the "Jerk", in their name, has nothing to with the sauce and everything to do with their way of treating customers.

Just awesome - been here dozens and dozens of times. Tried almost everything on the menu and its universally superb. Ekta is also ranked as the 8th best Indian restaurant in the USA by Travel & Leisure magazine. And it is well deserved.

Was excited to try this place as I have been wanting a replacement for my usual House of India. This is not the place. We were not greeted upon entry. There were many choices on the buffet, but not one really stuck out. A few chicken dishes had many small bones mixed in so be careful. The guy told us there was no naan because machine was broken. They offered us a fried/greasy bread which was terrible. I found the food "mediocre" at best. Still on my search for great Indian cuisine.

I came in to order a to go Chicken Panang Curry and some crab ragoon. As I was waiting on my order I was reading the reviews. Not sure if some of the ones for bad service was an off night, or the owner was actually there greeting and helping out. Looked like everyone got seated quickly and waiters were taking orders pretty quick. Got my order and left. When I opened it I saw that I didn't receive any sauce for my Crab Ragoon...was a little disappointed until I tried them. Def did not need any sauce with these. They were great without them. The Chicken Panang was very good as well with no shortage of chicken. I highly recommend.

I visited for lunch today. Arrived at 12 with two of my friends. One girl ordered and then they ran out of chicken, that's fine it happens. She told us two minute wait cool. We waited about five because more people came in and staff was limited. We finally were paying after about 15 mins total unfortunately our friend who had ordered ahead was already done eating so that kind of sucked! We ordered a side of naan at the register and we didn't get it u til we were packing up our leftovers :(. The food was good. I wish the chicken had been chunked instead of grated but that's personal preference I guess. The price was fair for what we got. The staff is what really made my visit. They were all so nice and patient. The group that we had allowed ahead of us due to chicken wait was asking s lot of questions as they were unfamiliar w the cuisine and the staff answered all questions and let them try sauces before committing to something g that might've been too hot. I am going to chalk up the slowness we experienced to growing pains as this is a new business and they do have hiring all position signs up. I will go back in a few months.

Thai Country Cafe is a staple in the loop. I've ordered carry-out multiple times from them. Carry-outs are always on time and the staff are friendly. The food can be a little too oily for me sometimes but perhaps that's not much of a concern to others. The menu is pretty extensive and you can request a spice level that you prefer. I've also dined in a number of times with friends and it's always been a good experience.

The food is good but it's the delivery service that's to good to walk your food up to you. In my apartment building they have a place for them to park, but the lazy unprofessional delivery guy refuse to bring my food up to my apartment. I was very sick so I didn't want to spread my cold around . There's a reason it's called delivery and this was the second time this delivery guy refuse to come. I won't be ordering from them this place again.

Worst service ever. Not enough staff food was good well the items that came out which were ordered correctly and of course they were not. Took 30 minutes waiting on checks that were incorrect. Management didn't jump in to help and seemed lost and a little rude himself. If a downtown restaurant can't handle a crowd especially when a reservation was made and they knee we were coming then they should not be in the downtown area!

This place is under-rated. The food was great. My friend got the pad-see-ew and it was one of the best, rich without being too oily.
