I asked for a recommendation and got the pineapple duck curry which I had never tried before. I was apprehensive at first because sometimes with duck it can taste real nasty if not made right. It was done right and was heavenly. It was savory and tangy and spicy but not overboard. All and all it was an excellent meal.

Best Thai in the world ! When I first moved to Nashville six years ago , my best friend introduced me to this place . I always get Tiger Tear and chai Tea . You simply can't imagine how good this beautiful food is ! The atmosphere is amazing . It really feels like you're in the culture. Owners are amazing & it's simply a five star for me :)

The staff here is super friendly, and helpful. I've always been wary of Indian food and wanted to give it an honest shot, and was very impressed. They're also very proficient in delivery. Highly recommend

Absolutely amazing service and food is absolutely breathtaking and delicious and the service was amazing on top of that the restaurant itself is very quiet nice music and the food is absolutely worth the money absolutely listen to the waitresses recommendations
My wife and I eat here regularly. We enjoy the menu as well as the great service. Highly recommended!

I love this place! It's a small little restaurant with delicious food! My sister recently moved to this area & took me here for their lunch buffet! A great price for great food. Their naan is so good plus they give it to you in a little basket, how cute! Great service, nice place, decent size & good food!

Zeppoli is absolutely delicious and one of the best 'non-chain' restaurants in South Jersey. We took the waitresses recommendation and ordered off the menu in the 3- course style. Panzanella was very flavorful with delicious crusty bread and fresh tomatoes, the ricotta gnocchi were like eating fluffy clouds and the rib-eye and fishermans stew were both delicious. I would not recommend Zeppoli if you are looking for a quiet night out as there are only about 10 tables and it gets pretty loud, but I like the environment of a busy cafe style restaurant.

This place is in a friendly neighborhood. The place is very small but it feels very homey, if that makes sense. I went there with a friend because we heard great things about the place from few of our mutual friends. Here is what we ended up ordering: Beef seikh kabobs - cooked perfectly, juicy and not over cooked. Chicken tikkah botis - very tender Nihari - it was good but not great Naan - The naan here is amazing! Probably the best thing we ordered, I would recommend the garlic naan, better than regular naan. The owners were nice enough to let us try one of their desserts, kheer, it was really good and very authentic. I plan on going back to this place with my family. Food is very authentic and the owners are friendly. The only complaint I have is that the spice level was a little lacking but I also didn't specify that I wanted everything spicy when ordering.

Just being introduced to Thai food, my friend convinced me to try it and we came to Ploy Thai. So glad we did. The food was fresh,elegantly plated and so delicious. The restaurant is quaint,beautifully decorated and the employees even dress the part. Can't wait to eat there again!

We ordered food to go. I am only giving 3 stars because they were out of several things we ordered. I was "upgraded" to the creazian salad because they did not have the salad I asked for. It seemed like mostly just lettuce and dressing, I expected more for $7. The pho was very flavorful. We also had the shaking beef and it was good, just a little salty.

Food is good but the worst service. No wonder it closed the owner has no knowledge of how to run a food business. I once called 7 times in one day and they didn't pick up, i go in the shop and they asked me "why didn't you call us to order". SMFH, glad it's closed

I like this place. Good food whether on the buffet or off the menu. Authentic and tasty. All the favorites (Chicken Tikka Masala, Lamb Vindaloo, Basmati Rice, Saag, etc) are SUPERB. Next time in, try a new dish. I'm sure they will pleasantly surprise you.

Stopped by for the 1st time & scored some of the best Tom Ka Gai soup ever. Expertly seasoned, plenty of chicken, loved it. However, I also ordered the Pad Thai with pork & am sorry to report it was dry, gritty and fairly flavorless.
The Malai Kofta and Indian tea are really, really good. Also, the prices are quite reasonable and the portion sizes are ample. This is a solid Indian restaurant and I'd recommend it.
Not authetic Indian food! Chat served is very cold. Ideally chat should be eaten hot. Worst indian food

I was pleasantly surprised at how delicious Naf Naf was. I had seen them popping up in recent months and wanted to try it for a while. Finally had an oops to stop during work. I ordered the Chicken Shwarma pita with rice, Chicken, lettuce, onion, pickles, garlic sauce and hot sauce. The pita was soft and delicious. The chicken was tender and tasty. I was disappointed they the "fries" are really chips and not fries. Other than that, I was incredibly impressed. I will definitely come back for another try!

I came here yesterday for lunch. I was just stopping by right before shopping. I never had Afghani food and I kept hearing from everyone how good Afghani food is and I wanted to give it a try. So I ordered the Sansom Kabob dinner which was really good. It came in with one piece of ground beef kabob, two pieces of chicken, and one piece of beef as well as a side of brown rice with a stripe of lentil sauce on it. This entree was delicious- I cannot describe the way it tasted, very spicy (but not hot) and sweet. It was amazing- especially the ground beef kabob. The rice with the sauce was really good- I finished all of it. For appetizer, I got the Burani, which is eggplant sauteed with tomatoes and onion- very delicious. I dipped the fresh-made bread with it. I also sat right in front and I got to see the chef make the bread- really awesome. I also ordered Kadu (pumpkin pieces in a sweet sauce) as a side. The Kadu was very different and delicious. The waitress was very friendly and I received my food very fast, despite the fact that it was only the chef and waitress working. The only criticism I have was the lack of meat they put on the entree, I guess I'm just used to other places. But overall, I would highly recommend this place if you are looking for exotic, delicious food- definitely bringing my friends next time.

Cool little food truck on the UPenn campus. They have the two staples of any successful college business down pat: they are quick and cheap. There are dozens of sandiwch options, from breakfast staples, lunch staples, and an array of cheese steak themed options. We had a cheese steak with onions and peppers as well as a steak and eggs. Each was $6. It isn't exactly Jims Steaks quality, but it is pretty tasty, filling, and served on a soft, warm roll. Good stuff.

Very good and authentic Puerto Rican restaurant. The mofongo (plantains) with camarones (shrimp) is delicious; accompanied by medalla beer or sangria. The tres leches for dessert one of the best I tried. Service is good.and prices are reasonable.Will come back.

Ordered Masala Dosa and Pau Bhaji.... Good! Topped it with Chai... And I am happy :-) The place is clean, I used the bathroom and it's clean as well..... You can tell a lot about the cleanliness of a place by quick visit to the bathroom. Good service with a smile face as well. Will visit again

The food was ok I got no complaints , but was greeting and waiting by unfriendly lady server. She didn't actually do much just taking orders with attitude . It is unprofessional if you want to work in service industry and especially work for tip , why would I want to tip you!!! By the way those $9 tip we left ,we want to tip the male server not you. He was always polite and friendly every single time we there.

Amazing Ethiopian food. This is their second location. The original is in Rittenhouse Square. The menu at this location also has some American fare if the kids are with you. Full bar, amazing Ethiopian food, coffee bar, smoothies and ice cream!

The first time I came here I was not impressed (it was shortly after they first opened ) however I have returned and food this time around was great! Pho has great flavor , spring rolls were amazing! Service is good and the place is always clean.

Being sooooooo close, as in NEXT DOOR close, to my most frequented nail salon; of course I've visited this eatery/quickie mart on several occasions. With each visit, I find the same level of customer service & product delivery... Yay!!!! #consistencyiskey I've eaten the Yetcamein here, French fries & the banh mi. Fair pricing. Food delivery is a little slow, but food is made to order & with one or two fry cooks, the lunch rush may not be a rush at all. Parking can be found in the rear of the building or on the street; you pick your poison, red or blue pill. I like that there are a variety of items for sale inclusive of but not limited to ICE CUPS!!!! Location is key & this place gets its right; corner of Broad & Canal, this is such a busy, busy spot. Way to go.

When I saw the pic in the restaurant that they had the best crab rangoons in town...I though...we'll see. OMG! They have THE BEST IN INDY!! Their Pad Thai, and shrimp spring rolls are delicious, too! Not to mention, they're close to my house!! I'll be back again, SOON!

My favorite food truck on campus. You know its good when there is a huge line waiting for the truck to open at 12. Fusion of thai and mexican. I always end up getting the chicken katsu. The burrito and the fish tacos I have to say are pretty great as well. Good portion size. Lots of flavors. Worth the wait. Check it out.

Definitely one of the better Indian buffets that I've tried in Indianapolis. Lots of veg options and aloo chana and a few other dishes I don't see as often on some buffets. The servers also offered made to order dosas as part of the buffet and brought them to the table which was nice. The nice thing with this location in the International Markeplace is that they honor the International Marketplace 10% discount card along with many other restaurants in that area. The building interior is a bit older and could use a few touch ups, but the ambience overall was fairly good especially with upbeat Indian music playing. It's nice to pop into the Patel Brothers grocery next door after eating here too.

Delicious lunch! Tried many items which were all great. My top favorites were the Cubano sandwich and Relleno De Papa. The Cuban was definitely the best I've had- perfect bread, juicy meat. Paella was also super tasty. Certainly will be back!!

Color me impressed! I've had the pleasure of eating here twice, both times I ordered the 2-piece chicken meal. They were in the middle of revamping the menu on my second visit and had to break the news to me that the 2 piece meal was no longer offered. The gentleman I spoke to on the phone, however, made a substitution for me and told me I could have chicken wings instead. Sure! Why not? I opened my takeout box to discover 5 or 6 massive chicken wings alongside the rice and homemade pickles that it usually comes with. I was super surprised to see the sheer amount of food I got for $11.50 (seemingly reduced cost). I had enough food to last me for two meals. The customer service has always been phenomenal on top of this, which just makes for an overall awesome experience! This has become my go-to chicken restaurant in St. Albert.
The food was amazing, it tasted fresh and the portions were just enough. They also have the best sweet tea!! Staff was super friendly, and the restaurant very clean. I will definitely stop by again.

I have tried their food twice now and I find them so-so; I have had better Vietnamese food than what I had here. Their prices are a bit lower than other Vietnamese restaurants around the area but that is because their portion sizes are so small (except the Pho dishes). I won't be coming back to this place for a meal, even if my co-workers are going.

We have never seen this good hospitality and customer care at any restaurant any place in United States. My husband and I walked in on Christmas night, as we were visiting the town and every restaurant was closed. We were greeted very warmly, even though the staff was in the middle of taking care of a wedding party. We ordered carry out for Karahi Chicken, the owner was so nice to offer us free appetizers, while we were eating delicious snacks, our carry out was ready, he insisted that we take our time to finish, he realized without us even telling him that we were staying a hotel and packed plates and silverware. Food was absolutely delicious! We will recommend Desi Kitchen to all.

La Va Cafe is a good deal--I had a yummy steamed spinach bureka for just $4.25, not bad. It really is a nice place to get a laid-back breakfast on a Saturday morning. The reasonably priced breakfast sandwiches and dishes, not to mention the La Va specialties such as the bureka, are high-quality, distinctive and tasty. The staff is friendly and the atmosphere is homey. Your cappuccino will come in a large bowl-like mug with a generously thick layer of foam, just the way it's supposed to be =)

Food was ok...too Smokey no air circulation. We got the 7 course meal for 2 pricey and you don't get much food. It came out very very slow we had to leave bc other half had irritated asthma bc of lack of any air in there. They still charged us for the whole 7 course...smh which we didn't get. Really had it came out faster instead of a 25 min wait in between smal courses well we probably would of made it all the way through. The appetizer was awful...salad was delicious and so was the bread. Chicken not cooked enough for my liking. I will not return here....yuk
Decent coffee, drinks, shakes and ethnic food. But in my opinion, over-priced for the portion.

I usually don't eat Asian when I'm traveling as it can be so variable. I was in Nashville on business and saw this place near my hotel. As lots of people mentioned, the little racetrack didn't inspire me - but I love Thai food. I looked it up here and the reviews convinced me to go ahead and give it a try. I was tired and it was late. The lady working there didn't smile but later warmed up and was very sweet. The place was clean and nicely decorated. The fresh spring rolls were gie-normous and quite good. The red chicken curry was very good too. I got it medium and it was western medium - not Thai medium, but it was good. All in all, a pleasant experience. If I were local, I would eat here regularly.
Not a fan of this place. I absolutely love pho but the kitchen is far from quality/fresh ingredients. I happened to see the lack of quality and I was so taken back that I refuse to go back.

Went in to grab a quick pita at 4:40pm. Sign said open, door was unlocked, no hours posted that were readily visible. I was told by the employee that they were done for the day. The website states they are open until 6pm. I have been to a number of other locations and never had this problem. May want to clearly post the hours or change the website.

Have been here several times for both the lunch buffet and dinner. Everytime, the food has been delicious and good portioned. The service has been excellent. My husband raves about their goat curry and tandoori chicken.
Amazing and fresh food. The pesto hummus is to die for and the kebabs are incredible. If you need a place to cater call them! They're efficient and the food is just top notch.

Suprisingly enough there are numerous Thai restaurants here in Nashville, however the quality and value of these joints is all over the place. I am always a little nervous when I try a new Thai place because they tend to hit my wallet harder than most "ethnic" cuisine in town, but Siam Cafe proved to be good food for a good value. I ordered the Tom Kha Gai soup and the Beef Panaeng which were both awesome. I like my food hot and this place definitely didn't dissapoint. At other Thai and Indian places I think the servers fear that "the gringa" can't handle spicy and when I say hot I often get medium instead. The dishes here definitely had some yummy burn and tingle. My bf ordered the Pad Thai which was not so good and drenched in mysterious red oil. I think their dishes are hit or miss, so maybe go first with a big group to try it all? Overall the food was good, the prices were very reasonable, and we had attentive, polite service. I won't say this is the best Thai in the world, but pretty good quality for Nashville. If they could get all their dishes on point and be less "hit-or-miss" then they would definitely bump up a star in my book.

OPA!!!!! I can taste the fried Kasseri cheese made tableside right now. I could eat this every day of the week. In fact I should go there now. The greek salad is my fav. I usually get a steak so i cannot comment on the other greek dishes. It is truly one of my most favorites restaurants of all time. Other things you should know, they have an outdoor heater so if you have to wait outside you will stay nice and toasty. Get there when they open or call for reservations. See you there.

I ordered form this place online via campusfood.com and the service was horrible! First, when I called to confirm my order, the person who answered was very rude stated that he never received it and refused to confirm with campusfood. He wanted me to call their customer service on a Sunday night! Luckily campusfood.com has a 24 hour customer service line for situations such as this. When I spoke to them, they told me they were trying to send me order to the restaurant, but the fax did not go through. Once they called the restaurant and confirmed my order, campusfood.com called e back to confirm (great service!). But that is only where the trouble began. I ordered a flounder hoagie with lettuce, tomato, provolone and mayo with a side of onion rings. In my order, I specified that I was in an apartment building, and to ring the bell, get buzzed in and take the elevator to the 4th floor (this is delivery service, right??). After that, it took over an hour to get my food and they delivered it well after closing. I had to call campusfood.com back to get them to call the restaurant & find out where my food was because no one was answering their phone. Campusfood.com finally reached them and told me they were nearby. When the delivery guy got there, he called me demanding that I come downstairs, he was not coming up. By this time I was reconsidering my tip. When I met him at the front door, he shoved the food in my hand and literally rant to his car...didn't even wait for a tip! When I got back to the apartment, I learned why. In the bag was a completely different meal that what I ordered. I wish that I could upload the photos to show you what I got! It was not the flounder hoagie I ordered, but two thin, cold pieces of fried fish laid atop a bed of soggy fries. Also in the bag was a bout a half pound of warm coleslaw and a side of soggy onion rings! Now I know why the delivery guy ran away! Of course, when I tried to call, the restaurant was already closed and no one answered. So I called campusfood.com back, told them what happened and asked about a refund. Unfortunately, they can't issue one unless the owner agrees, but they promised to call him and tell him my story. A little while later, they called me back saying they could not reach the owner, but promised to keep trying. I will also continue trying to reach the owner until I get my money back. So because of their shady customer service, I would advice not going there at all, but if you must, go there in person so you can be sure to get what you ordered and by all means, don;t pay in advance!
I've taken food out from Dosa Hut a couple of times and was very pleased with my food. The Samosa's are fresh and flavorful and my Biryani has very good levels of spice and taste fantastic.

Great Vietnamese restaurant in New Orleans. The kids were a bit tired of Cajun food (been in Louisiana for a week now) and wanted to eat fried rice and noodles. This place was the closest one to our hotel and had good reviews on yelp. When you enter the place you'll see its filled with Asian customers (which is a good sign). The portions were huge and the kids also got a chicken soup made especially for them for free.

I bookmarked this place immediately after reading Kevin F's review many months ago. If it was that good, then I had to get some of that. The problem is that I don't often have much reason to head up to Spring Hill. Who does? ;-) Then I get a call from a woman who wants to sell her house in Spring Hill, so off I go to take the listing. When we're done with the paperwork she remarks, "If you like Thai food, there is a good place around the corner." Goodness! It's Thai Cuisine! Kevin F. was right! It has to be one of the best meals I have had this side of Loei Province. In fact, it was so good that I think I'll schlep up to Spring Hill for lunch tomorrow....

I will update this review after I have tried a few more items, but the red curry was tasteless and watery. Maybe Thai Town Cuisine has spoiled me? If I were to rate on the red curry alone I would give one star, but the establishment was clean, and the staff was attentive. One of my lunch companions really liked his fried rice, and my other friend said his massaman curry was on par with Thai Town, and I am taking their opinions into consideration. As for now, I am not that impressed. Update coming soon!h Update: My fellow coworkers and I tried Tin's House again, and we all agree that the food had more flavor this time. I had the drunken noodles, and they were very delicious, and I would say they are comparable to the drunken noodles at Thai Town. My buddy that never has a bad thing to say liked his fried rice, but then he likes everything (except Dickies BBQ - long story). My other friends had a mixture of different curry and noodle dishes, and all agree that the food was way better this time around. I'm going to keep the score at 3 stars for now until I try a few more items.

Overall great experience. Food was delicious and the portions were very large for the price. Service was good. I had no complaints. The firecracker chicken and brown rice and honey walnut shrimp were all great.
One of my favorite Thai restaurants in the area. Service varies but the food makes up for it, when its bad. FIVE star hot baby!

Best Vietnamese food in Reno! I've been eating at Pho 777 since I moved to reno 2 years ago and just decided to try my luck here a few days ago. My husband had pho and I had the pork and vermicelli noodles. Both were delicious! I grew up eating viet food and my husband cooks pho so we know our way around Viet cooking. Staff was kind, restaurant was clean and we got our food in a timely manner. I am definitely coming back.

Great concept! Poor execution. 2.5 really. An "Indian Chipotle" is a great idea and certainly something I could see being very successful. This place just needs to get their act together. I came here for lunch recently. They were not too busy and had three people working at the front counter. For some reason instead of working in an assembly line, the staff was totally uncoordinated. There were only a few customers and I waited and watched as the staff one at a time kept going to the kitchen, putting on gloves, removing gloves, taking orders, checking out, etc. A little training - and having a runner - would help here. On to the food. The meat and sauce was actually quite tasty. I really enjoyed that part. The toppings were scant and need more variety. How about more fresh veggies, more chutneys, and more grilled or fried items like okra or eggplant. Also how about a nice scoop of chilled yogurt on top? So many possibilities! I look forward to coming back when they've made a few improvements.
Confused by all the great reviews. The crab papaya salad had chunks of frozen crab (still actually frozen) and tasted like fermented gym sock. The main entrees were okay, nothing special.
Best Hookah this side of the Mason Dixon line ! Amy is the best ! Nice atmosphere . Plenty of hookah flavors . Get the spicy chicken Philly!

This Place is the WORST thai i have ever had, and the worst experience we have ever had. It is family owned and operated for the most part. The People that run it are not friendly at all. If they mess your order up, they are so cheap they will expect you to eat it anyways. Or if they fix it because you complain enough they may end up charging you for two plates like they did me. And then at the register when i mentioned it he said "well we broght you out your order then you sent it back and wanted another so we charge for two!" What an unprofessional cheapskate move. Ridiculous! And its not about the extra 12 bucks its the principal of the matter. Terrible service i will never go back and tell EVERYONE i know to never go there.

Small family restaurant in strip shopping center with great food and service. Large selection on menu. Artfully decorated. I had the Panang Chicken and my wife had another panang chicken dish with prawns that was huge. Leftover will be lunch for a lucky person tomorrow. We spent $30 before the tip. Both my wife and I will be back.

Can't believe I never ate here before. Had excellent Massaman curry and Pad Thai. Rainbow salad very refreshing. I'll be back. Waitress was VERY nice. Unusually, got here in time for "early bird." Pad thai, but not with shrimp, was on the early bird, so she gave us the early bird salad and dumplings with the regularly priced dish for no extra.

I've been eating here for a couple years now and the food is always good and very reasonably priced. Occasionally its inconsistent, but usually not in a bad way. I assume it's a different cook on different days, as they add a slightly different level of spice or add extra meat, etc. Wait staff is friendly, but you often have to flag them down if you need something after your food is delivered to your table or when you're ready for the check. However, when you get your check, you're always pleasantly surprised at how cheap it is! They have decent vegetarian options, and my favorite thing here is the vegetarian summer rolls. I'm also a huge fan of their shakes, with or without bubbles. The avocado, mango, or pineapple are my favorites. They are all made with fresh ingredients - not the powder crap you find in many restaurants. My biggest complaint about this restaurant is that the condiments on the table are often messy looking. It would be great if they wiped down the bottles of sauces each night so they looked and felt clean instead of being greasy or gooey.

Yummy. Not the best Ethiopian food that I've ever had, but quite yummy nonetheless. Ethiopian is one of my favorite cuisines, hence the four stars. My party of two were the only guests in the dining room on a Wednesday night. The owner (and our server) Shita Yenenh provided prompt, friendly service. There is live music on the weekends. I don't remember the names of the dishes, but the vegetarian lentils were yummy. Next time I would skip the green beans & carrots.

Still great food and the best family people you will meet. Great job Tony and put living keep doing it every day and make it happen if you see this you know you will see me soon . Give this place a try and you will be back pig belly raps great and pho is real no base flavor cooking real flavor not base
My wife and I get the same thing every time - 2 summer rolls and the beef pho noodle soup (#38 I think) and it's good every time.

I still dream of my meal here. The shrimp pil pil was to die for. The seasonal soft shell crab was perfect. The mussels were amazing. I loved the charm of this place, just remember to bring your own wine.

Awful! Lots of waiting time. The woman at the counter was the only person doing everything. Feel for her, but she was overwhelmed and unresponsive with just 3 parties at her place when we went for a pick up. The chai was terrible.

This USED to be my favorite hookah bar in Nashville. Ever since they hired security I've had an issue. I keep giving this establishment chance after chance but the security/door person is horrible. I've left twice without being seated due to my frustration. Tonight, my girlfriend and I were seated at the bar even though I expressed we wanted a table. We were told to sit at the bar until a table became available. Three tables became available at the same time. My girlfriend and I sat at one of the tables. One of the waitresses went and brought the security/door man. He told us we had to get up because there were several people in front of us. I said fine we will cash out our check and leave. He then replied that he had our table ready. I asked him where the table was, his reply was that it didn't matter. Did we want the table or not. I'm not into "bargaining" with someone about a table at any establishment. Needless to say, my girlfriend and I cashed our bill out and left. I would like the readers to know that I have had several bad experiences here. ALL of them directly related to security. I've given this establishment more chances than a normal business because it is one of the few places to smoke hookah and drink in Nashville. I have decided to buy a personal hookah tomorrow.

SERVED RAW UNCOOKED FOOD x2 Tried this place from a suggestion from a friend a month ago, ordered Shrimp pad Thai and the shrimp were not cooked. I told the server, who said "oh I'll be right back," and rushed off to the kitchen- only to never come back! I removed the shrimp from my plate and ate the noodles because I was hungry. When I asked her what she did about it, she said she removed the shrimp from the check - $3. No real apology or concern that they served me raw shrimp. We gave them a second chance tonight only to have my husbands salmon come out completely raw and cold in the center. Again, no real apology or concern. Told the waitress to have it cooked well-done. They brought back out and it was still questionable. Nothing taken off the check. We paid and will never return to this restaurant again.

Got a southern sandwich and was felt very medium about my sandwich. The chicken was nice and crispy, but seemed slightly undercooked. Also, the combination of the pretzel crust and tomato marmalade made for a very sweet sandwich. A little too much for me. I had to put some hot sauce on it to balance it out. Good things were the coleslaw. They used kale as well as cabbage. Made me feel healthy. Also, it was a well built sandwich. It didn't slide apart at all and everything was in good proportions. Also, the bun was fantastic!! But all in all, I feel like I should stick with fried chicken here.

Breakfast is fantastic. Can't go wrong. Dinner is elegant. Expect to pay a pretty penny for the dinner but also expect some fresh ass food. The staff is nice and timely. The space is a little small but I think that's part of the experience. Feels like a small town go to restaurant.

I noticed that they didn't have any condiment bottle on the table and that got me a little worried. All decent pho places I had been to have condiment bottles on the table. We placed our order and our server came out with a condiment tray. Phew. I had the bamboo pho ($9) and it was pretty good.
Food was great. Quick service and happy with pricing. Did takeout, next time may try eating in. Sushi wash good and meals were delicious.. No complaints.

This is a really tasty Middle Eastern restaurant specializing in Greek and Lebanese cuisine. They have some very generous helpings on their entree plates and they have some nice combinations not offered by similar restaurants in the area. The food is delicious and the service is excellent. On my last visit my drink was kept full even though the restaurant was packed to capacity and there was a line of people placing take out orders so that says a lot! Keeping my drink full doesn't seem like a big deal but some restaurants really seem to have service problems with waitstaff just doing that basic task to actually earn their tips but Albasha took excellent care of me in that regard and these days that impresses me. I was also asked multiple times how my food was and my order was delivered very rapidly. This is a thoroughly experienced and professionally run restaurant that does good quality so even though they are a local chain they perform where it matters.

Casual setting, friendly service, delicious food. Half the building is a market with middle-eastern products for a fun adventure after we ate. Started with a lemonade-mint slushi, fried cheese (awesome!) and falafel. Ordered the gyro plate which had lovely presentation with delicious tender meat, home-made tomato/cucumber salad and creamy hummus. After lunch our server informed us that a tray of knafeh desert had just come out of the oven so we order a piece each and Turkish coffee to complete a wonderful meal.

I am from Bangkok Thailand and in St. Louis visiting my daughter at WASHU, the food at Thai Country Cafe is authentic and incredibly delicious. We had the Tod Mun, fried fish cake, which were scrumptious. The Ke Moa noodles and Green Curry noodles both with chicken were authentic in taste as they were so flavorful.

These guys are fantastic. I'm always greeted with a smile, and the lamb is always cooked amazingly. I literally get lunch here three times a week. The prices are incredible for the amount of food you get, + a free soda. So. Freaking. Good. Oh, and DON'T support their competition on 13th and Chestnut. Their stupid bright lights and flashy marquee to attract business doesn't cover up their attitude and lacking meat portions. The competition reminds me of exploited advertising methods while the Halal Gyro King cart reminds me of good, honest business :)

most love it, some hate it; i love it. simple ingredients, fast service, great citrus salad, good escarole. bad: uncle bens rice, not a fan... oh yea, this is another one on my list for 'write a real review'....

Not the best food we've had. Our first time there. Avgolemono soup had no hint of lemon at all, yet we were told it was freshly made. Spinach pie tasted thawed. Greek burgers were way undercooked. Almost raw. The place was empty, no one came in but us. That's a bad sign. But the worst of all I was asked if I wanted my half eaten raw burger put back on the grill. Not knowing me would you eat food cooked after my tainted half eaten back washed food was put back on the grill. Not me. The thought of who was before me turns my stomach. Anyway our first time is our last time. Good luck.

I always get the green chicken curry and I haven't been disappointed yet. It is pretty spicy so that is a perk! I have been searching Boise for green curry that I love and this is the best I have found yet. I will continue to search, finding several great curry spots can't hurt. Service is usually pretty quick, price is reasonable, and at lunch I always get a bowl of soup with my meal. Perfect! Great place!

The food is as good or slightly better than what is offered at their flagship location uptown, but the service here is TERRIBLE. The other location has set high expectations for an efficient restaurant machine, but at the South Market location, they are very disorganized, there's no host or any sign to let you know to seat yourself. I've been 3 times since they opened and it's been worse service every time. The last time, I waited at the bar for 15 minutes after seating myself, and no one ever spoke to me, but then two men sat a few seats down the bar from me and were helped almost immediately, so I left. They clearly did not want my business that day. I will go back and revise my review if the service improves, because I am definitely a fan of the food. I'm just really surprised about the great disparity in service between the two locations.

I've eaten here many times over the years and have never been disappointed. It is not the best buffet around, but it's still quite delicous. I'm amazed at how negative most of the reviews are. Perhaps I should make another visit...since it's been awhile. I just hope that the quality hasn't gone down since my last visit, because I really liked this place.
Delicious as always! Drunken noodles are da bomb! Great service and friendly people!
Attentive staff, amazing authentic Spanish food, generous portions! Will definitely be going again & again!
Love me Spanish food & Not just because I'm Puerto Rican either. Come here for a tasty meal for lunch or dit

I will say that this place is very friendly and very accommodating. Perhaps I'm not a fan of Thai food, however, the food is enough to fill you however, I would not choose to go here unless invited. Their lunch specials are reasonably priced and come with rice and soup. That in and of itself is a plus in case you don't like the food. The interior is tastefully decorated in the theme of the country it originated. The food is quickly served with a smile and pleasant conversation. I see it as a mixture of Chinese food with large fresh vegetables. It seems to be frequented by many customers at lunch when I have been there, so it must be pretty popular with the locals. Even though I give it four stars, it seems to be pleasing to some folks. I understand that they're hot and spicy entrées are just that, hot and spicy. So be careful what you order and make sure you clarify with the server if you have any questions.

Disclaimer: I grew up in Egypt, and have a high standard for middle-eastern food. This place greets you with an expansive space thats beautifully decorated. There is an open kitchen, a bakery and gift shop in the front, with seating in the middle and back, including an outdoor seating area. The staff are all very knowledgeable. I came for brunch after several friends recommended it. My girlfriend and I split the baba ganoush to start - creamy, eggplant coming through clearly, well balanced by the sweetness of the pomegranate seeds. I had the shish tawaook as my main course, a wrap filled with seasoned chicken, fries, toum (a garlic sauce), and coriander. This reminded me of home more than any other middle-eastern dish I've had in years. I highly recommend it, the balance of flavors and different textures is on point. My girlfriend had zaatar with egg, tomatoes, and onions, and it was equally delicious. Their oven makes all their breads on the spot so the bread is just as appreciated in each dish. We finished with a rose water and pistachio crueller - fluffy, not overly sweet, and a perfect finish to a perfect meal. Don't sleep on their espresso drinks either - their baristas are top notch. Well done, Suraya. Shokran, we will be back!

We ate dinner here yesterday, which was a Saturday night. We arrived around 6:30 to avoid any potential wait (sorry, no reservations for small parties). This place is not in my favorite area, so we also wanted to allow some time to troll for a safe spot to park. That being said, Fharmacy Nola is right around the corner, and I'll park wherever to get at that burger. The food was killer. I had no idea what to expect, but everything we ate, we loved. For the record, the food here is 5/5 IMHO. We had grilled shishito peppers, grilled okra salad, pig knuckles, shrimp, pork jowls and the chicken. So many good bites, it's overwhelming. All of our dishes were served family style, so everyone tried everything. But when it came to the entrees, much less sharing was happening. My favorite and my entree were the pork jowls. Excellent! Nice rim of marbling with tons of seasoning. The meet was served with some lettuce wraps and some kind of sauce. The lettuce wraps were a nice way to take a heavy and fatty meat and lighten it up. Angelo Brocato's is fairly close, maybe a mile or so away. There was discussion as to whether we should partake in Marjie's dessert vs 2nd location. The nuclear option of course is to eat two desserts which I supported. At any rate, we had the chess pie and galette from Marjie's. Both very tasty. Dessert was the weak link in the dinner, but that's not because the pie or galette weren't tasty. The main fare was just so damn good. The restaurant itself is quaint. Tables are close together and they keep it just a few degrees too warm for me. That may have something to do with yesterday's weather that topped out at around 90. Our server was Polli. She was enthusiastic and attentive. This place is really casual. The service was solid and friendly. Overall, we will definitely repeat Marjie's Grill. Excellent food in a tough location with limited parking. Still...worth it.

What a find... If you take a look at their website you will be swept away - - - they truly achieve the same ambience in person. Do not let their location deceive you. Fresh delicious curry and sushi was pleasing to the pallette. Brandon, Fl seems to be lacking in craftsmanship when in comes to culinary delights, however, Ploy Thai definitely delivers. Thank you for the experience.

The buffet was not all that great. 1) because the wait line was long. We had to wait 30 mins every time we wanted to get food and the layout did not make it easy to stand. 2) It felt like it was very expensive for the quality of the food. Uttapam was great but rest of them was average or worse. Sorry I have tried better Indian restaurants.

I've eaten THAI in Boston, Atlanta, Denver, Vegas, Portland, etc, and this was the best I've ever had. I had a sauté of shrimp, tomato, cucumber, veggies with a sweet, sour, spicy sauce. They make their own hot sauce. Lunch was served with Thai peppers sitting in fish sauce, peppers sitting in vinegar, house siracha, and ground chili power of some sort all on the side. I ordered 'Thai hot' and it was spicy, but not over the top. They have perfected the hot, sour, sweet flavor profile. Affordable too! What a great experience.

Would suit Non- Indians. Food is ok, less spicy and extremely costly. The price is more aligned to costlier cities like New York. Probably since this is only Indian restaurant in Mount Juliet, they are taking good advantage.
Definitely a fan! This is where I get my fix for Indian food! Best around- and their lunch special is definitely a good value, but I prefer to order from the menu when someone else is buying. ;)
4 sars fot wifi, unwaveringly above average (nut not incredible) coffee, and nice staff. ...its a laptop coffee shop; dont go unless you've got work to do.

I love La Va. It's honestly one of my most favorite places in the city. I had been a few times before, but my La Va love affair really began when we moved into Grad Hospital. My gf and I are here almost every single day. The coffee is great (the soy latte is soooo good!), but the food is downright fantastic. The hummus platter is so, so good, and if you haven't tried the Israeli hot sauce you must. Must. And for whatever reason, the rice with peas and carrots is so comforting I actually crave it. The nearly always vegan soup of the day is also a great option. And the cinnamon raisin bagel is probably the best I've ever had. Before I went vegan, I also loved the burekas (especially with the aforementioned hot sauce). I also have to mention the La Va staff. They are awesome. It's so nice to have a place nearby where not only is the food and drink great, but so are the people. I really couldn't adore this place more -- the well-loved furniture, the cute paper liners on the tables, the always-interesting rotating art. A great neighborhood place with a great feel. La Va, I heart you.

This is my first visit to this place and I'm really surprised to see how good ambience and the decoration inside the restaurant. Place is very neat and clean and decorated and I really liked it. We came here to dine in but there were no seats available for us as it was crowded that night. We have ordered to go and then waited for 30 mins. The main reason for giving two stars are as below. The lady in the reception was not really courteous and she was rude on us when we have asked for a table to dine in after 30 mins ( Initially we have ordered to go but we were hungry and asked for a table). Her tone was really not so good and she kinda annoyed us twice in that passion. The food was good but not great. Should've added more spices in the chats. I may visit this place again but I was upset on my first visit itself.

Singha was my first encounter with Thai food, and I was not impressed. I was there with a fairly large group, but we were the only ones in the place and our server was friendly enough, but none of us thought the food was anything to rave about. I ordered something that was suppose to be just chicken and rice, but I found pieces of shrimp AND beef mixed in- and not enough to make it look intentional. That concerns me for people with seafood allergies, but luckily I'm just picky, not allergic. My friends all thought their food was ok, but not great. It took awhile to get refills on our drinks, and when the bill came it was WAY more than any of us were expecting. Since we had such a fun time we didn't spend too much time analyzing it and just paid. There was an 18% gratuity automatically added in which I understand, but I feel like for 18% she should have offered to at least split the bill up for us.

We loved Jasmine Thai. The waitresses were friendly and very efficient. They looked lovely in their Thai dresses. The restaurant is immaculate and beautifully decorated. Everything we ordered was delicious. The steamed dumplings were very tasty. The Tom Yum soup was also very good. I noticed on the bill it said 'mild', so next time I will ask for hotter. Same for the Shrimp in Green Curry Sauce. And the fried banana 'coins' over coconut ice cream was a yummy dessert! Definitely will go back.

I love Vietnamese food and Pho An Hoa is pretty good. The food is good, place is clean, prices are pretty low, and service is generally fast. We ordered 2 entrees for less than $20 and it was very filling.

Amazing deal! Best falafel I've ever had. Labneh, hummus and combo platter were all very good. Portions are huge. The bill was so low I thought the server made a mistake----nope--this is just the best deal in NOLA. I've been to most of the other Middle eastern restaurants in the area but this one takes the cake (or falafel?).

We are new to the area and I was looking forward to trying this place. The decor is nice and we were seated right away. The flys are an issue since we were swatting them away the whole time. I was really disappointed in the food. My son got chicken tenders which he didn't eat, I tasted a piece and it had no flavor whatsoever. My other son had pasta and that wasn't good. My son other had grilled cheese which he ate. I had a burger and it was just ok. The cheese on the french onion soup is entirely overcooked. Just one big crispy, burnt piece of cheese. At this point, I don't think we'll return, but maybe if they changed the menu. The food seemed a little overpriced as well. So disappointing since they offer outside seating.

Excellent little place! I stopped here for lunch and was glad that I did! I had the crab & asparagus soup, tofu verimicelli. Both were excellent and fresh. We were served quckly and food was prompt and hot. Would definitely come back when in the area.

Definitely the best pho noodle I've ever had. 100% recommended. Clean and modern restaurant, very nice staff!! We both ordered large rare beef noodle soup, tasty soup and a LOT OF BEEF. Worth the money!!

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: Sorry to hear Paul has sold this restaurant. I wish he and Pam all the best with their future endeavors! Really going to miss lunching here.

We had a feast today of chicken curry, jerk chicken, plantains, festival (fried dough perfect for dipping in sauces), slaw, and fish and chips. Portions were huge and prices were very reasonable. Our food was delicious and our 8-year-old loved his fish and chips too, he told me, I have to say, 5 stars.
Food was delicious , service was very good and attentive ! I had the chicken vindaloo and if you dare make it spicy it will be super tasty ! I loved this place

One of the best meals I've had in a long time. Could not believe the atmosphere, service and quality of food especially for the price. My boyfriend and I had the homemade gnocchi and the lamb, both dishes were excellent. I would also recommend the shepard's salad and phyllo cigars. Delicious! Cannot wait to go back.

First time I came to this place, 5-stars But then every other time I have been here, they have something missing in the menu: oh sorry we don't have chicken today. Or we are out of this or that... then they started to strikeout items off the menu! And the best thing is, they have no sweets. ZERO. All sweets crossed off the menu, LOL! I mean, this is a restaurant in the business district of New Orleans. They should do better than that. If they don't have the items, because it's not selling out, just reprint a new menu !
Service was great, menu was priced right, food was amazing and the portions were generous. I'll definitely be back!

Sandwichs are good. Not great. In Cali you pay about 2.50-3 for same thing. Probably would have given better eating but they won't even give you and ice water, gotta buy cheap brand bottled water for $1 ..... Really? At least get some better water.

This location only gets 4 stars versus the 5 stars I gave the Drexel Hill location only because they are a little more pricey than Drexel Hill. The food is still delicious and the service was still good. As far as a comparison to the Drexel Hill location: the Media restaurant is more hip & trendy, offers full bar service and is a little louder than what you will experience at Drexel Hill. In all honesty, I will probably continue to visit both locations its just more of a preference on how far you feel like traveling and if you want to get drinks with dinner.

Definitely my favourite Thai place in all of Tampa! First of, everyone's real nice! 1 or 2 might not speak the best English, but the attitude's really nice with smiles all around. We've had 6 different dishes on the menu so far, and every single item has been good. I'm Asian, and visited with American and Norwegian friends, and we all liked different dishes best, but my favorites are the steamed dumplings and boneless ribs.
Every entree on the menu is amazing! Great service too. The pad Thai is unconventional but delicious.

La atención está fatal la cajero nuevo no saben ni copral y cuando pido orden de atrás no save como cuando el otro cocinero estaba era mejor la señora ni saluda parese que le tiene miedo a la jente me encantaba mi viste mi pechuga mi pecado con ajos que ya no hacen Buenos pero ya encontre mi verdadero cosinero en el rincón latino ese si cocina el tiene su propio restaurante el que cocinaba en el típico ya no vol al típico porque siempre lo dueno tienen cara de enojó y todo ya no es lo mismo

I love the service and much of the food is very good. I don't like the coffee and dinner could be a little less expensive for what you get. You should still try it if you want breakfast that does not echo all others and you like your coffee bold.

if you like a quiet atmosphere and hospitable service, then you should check this place out. The manager and staff are polite and professional. Also sometimes buffets can have a somewhat raunchy feel to them, but that isn't the case with this place. The food is above average, and after eating you don't feel like you compromised on nutrition for the sake of taste. I enjoyed Chef Laddi's special of the day.

If only I could give no stars, seriously, no joke, if you value your life, DO NOT come here, a buddy of mine and myself were forced out at gun point by they're "security" I honestly thought I was gonna die! Please take this seriously! This is not a lie! This really happened!

Amber Indian is easily the best choice for Indian food in the Indianapolis/Carmel area. I've eaten at almost every Indian restaurant in the city, and this place is consistently the best. With a very large and changing buffet, it's hard to go wrong especially with the lunch price being under $10. When you first sit down, the waiter asks you if you'd like anything besides water and also if you would like plain or garlic naan. This is one of my favorite aspects of Amber Indian. Each time you go there, they make you a hot and fresh basket of naan. I almost always go with the garlic naan as it just takes the already flavor-packed dishes out of this world. The korma is probably the staple of the buffet (for good reason), and it is available everyday. The palek paneer is also to die for and is extremely flavorful with a subtle creaminess. My personal favorite dish is the mushroom tikka masala which is usually available on Tuesdays. Although my review may indicate that I'm a vegetarian, that is hardly the case as their chicken dishes (curry, tikka masala, munchurian) are all incredible. The spiciness level for most dishes is around mild to medium, and if you like things a little spicier like me, they have a great hot chili chutney that can add zip to any dish. Finally, if you can manage to save room for dessert which is sometimes difficult, the mango pudding is money. Although the restaurant is a standard open dining room, it is clean, well kept, and usually glowing with satisfied patrons. The service, as with most Indian restaurants I've been to is great, and they keep your much needed water filled to the brim. The next time you're looking for a delicious, ethnic lunch that satisfies your taste buds, hunger, and wallet, Amber Indian should be atop your list.

I like this location! It has the same shabby chic interior that all of the others have, but with so many windows it feels light and spacious. It even has some parking to call it's own, so if you get there early on a Sunday morning like I recently did you won't have any trouble finding a spot for your vehicle (should you drive one). I ordered a flat white with almond milk and it was one of the best coffees I have had in my life, ever. A touch of sweetness, perfectly balanced, just amazing. This location really isn't super convenient to either my workplace or my home but I will make the drive just to come back for this on a regular basis it was so good. Service is pleasant, prices are average for what you see around the city, seating is plentiful and all of those windows let in the sunshine. Perfect coffee shop in a perfect location.

Found this place thanks to yelp. We enjoyed lunch - Acharee chicken(which is gravy) comes with Rice. Garlic Naan was delicious. Our server was very friendly. She suggested rather than ordering biriyani we can use Acharee chicken gravy for the regular & garlic naans we ordered, which we enjoyed very much.

The enthusiastic reviews of my fellow yelpers made me choose this small and brightly colored restaurant as my lunch destination yesterday. The small menu looks interesting, the people behind the counter could not have been nicer. We started with the Harira Soup - bland and thickened in a way that reminded me of soups out of a can. Even though my companion and I were hungry at the beginning of the meal, this soup made us wait for the plates we ordered, the Shawarma Chicken and Lamb Ketban. The chicken was incredibly dry and tasted like cardboard, the lamb (pieces of leg), while cooked freshly, tough and innocuous. The only think we really liked was Zaalouk (sauteed grilled eggplant in garlic and tomatoes with olive oil). It was beautifully spiced and very tasty. When I looked at the Tagine dishes patrons at the next table ate, I regretted that I had not ordered chicken or lamb tagine. They looked so much better than the brittle pieces of chicken on our plate. Because of this and and the wonderful people behind the counter, I give Marrakesh Express three stars instead of two. One more thing: When a place is opening at 11:30 a.m., why is the special of the day not ready at 1:00 p.m.? Even the Moroccan tea was not ready until 1:30! This is not a good way to run a restaurant.

Great food at a reasonable price. Great assortment of Pho and other Vietnamese specialties. I strongly suggest trying the marinated raw beef salad. Doesn't sound that appealing, but once you eat it you'll want another order.

My 1st time trying Afghan food. I was very impressed. Clean Flavors yet very flavorful. We tried the Lamb and Chicken Kabob dishes, both were served with some savory rice and a hint of lentils on them..we also had a the potato flat bread as an appetizer..forget what it's called on the menu..it was very tasty too...
Delightful chicken tikka masala and vegetarian samosas. Owner was very friendly! I'll be back.

I feel like Little Kitchen is one of the few Chinese places around this area, mainly due to it's menu, but I can't be certain. The reason why I say this is because Little Kitchen offers the run of the mill Chinese fare, Thai food, Japanese sushi, and American selections. Wanting to try some Chinese in Philadelphia I ordered some Kung Pao Chicken and beef fried rice. It was late, but delivery was quick. The chicken was good, tender, and the sauce was a nice consistency but not spicy, almost sweet. The rice was not so great, dry and the beef was a bit chewy. Their menu says they have parking in the rear.

The 3 of us thoroughly enjoyed the entire dinner experience at Scannicchio's on Sunday night. From the time we made the reservation to the time we walked out the door (with leftovers), the experience was memorable and excellent. The food and service were exceptional. They offered a wide array of specials along with a very full menu of options that could please most palates. The bread was served hot! They also offer house made ice cream and other desserts. If you want an authentic Italian experience, stop in.

This place has the cutest decor! The atmosphere is really cool with fun light fixtures and beautiful dining ware. They were very accommodating for our reservation for a group of nine, the service was good and fast, and one of the owners was super helpful in taking a group photo for us. I got the drunken noodle, which was a little too spicy for me, but I'm weak and they warned me on the menu. We had a couple people who were vegan, and they were able to find good options to eat.

Nice decor and environment. Friendly, although mediocre service. Food failed to impress, rather bland overall. Thai food is more renowned for being of a spicier experience. Ok place overall but not great.
Really great steamed bun pork tacos and best bun (grilled chicken vermicelli) in New Orleans proper. Not a huge fan of their pho, but service is on par and much more quiet than Magasin and Lily's.

Food-wise, this place is good. Flavors and selection are nice, and portions are good too. I come here during work for lunch sometimes. I get an hour lunch, and sometimes I need a good chunk of that for this place. There is only ever one server (I'm guessing one of the owners/their family). Sometimes they are busy, and having only one server makes them slow. Sometimes they're not busy, and it's fine. I don't really have an issue with it, since the food is good. It's placed oddly next to a go-cart track
Their food is not so good. It is not worth your money. I was not satisfied... it is somewhat expensive for the portion you receive compare to other Jamaican place.

Dishonest business conduct. Owner knows what she's doing when deceiving customers with a Menu that reads one price but when the bill comes they slide in the extra bucks. This happens with quite a few essential dinner orders, like the pad thai, which is listed exactly as "Shrimp and Chicken Pad Thai" for $9.99, You order it. The bill comes charging $12.99 for it, because it has shrimp and chicken and this is extra!! Same with the curry dishes, etc. You will always get overcharged. Most won't even notice it. The portions are small. You order an appetizer for 5 people and it brings a tiny dish with sauce that is only good for one person. When you call waiter for more sauce they will bring it, but then the bill will later reflect a buck extra for that tiny amount of extra sauce that wasn't enough either! It is a shame that the ownership is such a money monger and we can't believe they are still getting away with this. Many locals, including ourselves, have confronted the owner directly about this issue to have her only say that she will change the menu with correct pricing. She told us this during spring last year, but our friends dined there recently and had the exact same menu and billing problem. To top it up, the staff is rude and short-sided. They come across as nice at first, but don't ask them for anything or question anything. The service is very lacking. The food is not bad in general. Pad Thai tastes like the rusty pan, but they can make good strong sauces. Our noodles are always very sticky and gummy as if they were sitting in water for a while, but the sauces are very good. Again, it's a shame we have a local business that takes many of us as fools and disrespects the community blatantly. Until they decide to do better we would not encourage anyone to dine there.

I come here WAY too much because it's pretty much the perfect weeknight, chill, laid back place for when I want to meet up with friends or if I don't feel like cooking. Food is colorful and casual. Service is friendly, speedy, and consistent. Never a wait for a table. Drinks are delicious. I haven't had a bad experience yet...and I've had lots of experiences!

Had take out today. Got three dishes. So delicious. This is my new favorite indonesian restaurant. I usually go to the one on Snyder Avenue. One negative comment was the beef rendang is really tough. I would stay away from that one. Everything else really really good. Check this place out!

Came here for lunch and I quite enjoyed myself. What's great is that they have lunch specials which make the prices more decent and acceptable. I tried the Green Curry with chicken at a spice level of 4 for $7.99. My hubby tried the Pad See Ew with chicken at a spice level of 1 for also $7.99. Both lunch items came with two pieces of Crab Rangoon and of course steamed rice. You can choose to sub stuff with an extra charge. I also got a Thai iced tea which I think was $2.99. So I really liked everything that we got, they were cooked well and tasted really great. Very comparable to all the other great Thai restaurants that I've been to. The only thing is that there wasn't really anything new so nothing really blew my mind. I mean there's nothing wrong with that as long as what they serve is quality. What I did like is that you could choose the level of spiciness you wanted for your dish, I chose the level 4 and for me it was great but actually it wasn't that spicy overall. Just watch out especially if you are more sensitive to spicy stuff though because I just really love spicy food. As for the service it was pretty good. The server was nice and the food came out really quick! The place is actually pretty small but the vibe is great, definitely not as kitschy as other Thai restaurants I've been to. I will for sure definitely be back when I'm in the area and craving curry!

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Well if you're one of those who to explore the understated, authentic, obscure, hole in the wall kind of places, this should be on your todo list. Remember, you have come to this place for the food not the decor! I tried chicken curry (9.99 - good for two with rice) and it turned to be one of the best. Recommended!

Great value and very tasty! First visit: I got the combo comes with ALL of the following: 1/4 Chicken was jerk rubbed and cooked in the smoker, comes with your choice of sauce. Jamaican Patty was excellent; meaty and flaky crust - like a Jamaican hot pocket, plantain was perfect and a nice bed of red beans (they call 'em peas) and rice. Get it to go or eat on the picnic table. I'll be back for sure! I went back during the Yelp dinner club - tried about everything, not a bad item on the menu! Goat curry: as good or better than Indian curry, amazing sauce and tender meat, the goat didn't have that "gamey" taste, just perfect. Red Snapper: not on the menu every day so when they have it - get it! Great taste, flaky and flavorful. Ribs: they were beef ribs, jerk rubbed and slow smoked - as good as the BBQ joints in town - a must have! Try it for yourself - the Yelp dinner club and I loved it - every morsel. Well done JSJ!

Haven't been here in a very long time. I was not disappointed. I came on Friday afternoon for lunch. The service was quick and food was excellent. I had Chicken Kabob platter, which is is Chicken Breast, very juicy, succulent and moist. Comes with brown basmati rice , afghan bread and your choice of salad. The waitress brought the Afghan Salad before I realized and asked if I could switch for Greek salad which was perfect choice for this delicious meal. Nice to know you can still come during your work lunch and have a leisurely, relaxing meal away from the office.
Delicious Thai food. Proper amount of spice and very tender shrimp. Stopped in for dinner with a friend. Was a little empty but we went in anyway and glad we did! Good, quick service and tasty food.

Delicious food. Best I ever had! Prices are good, lunch menu is the bomb. Had the chicken curry, it was the bomb. Friend had the chicken biryani, it was delicious. Spicy is SPIIICY, WATCH OUT! So good. So good. Mango lassi was so tasty, and cooled the palate!
Just tried for the first time. Wonderful flavors. Best Indian cooking we have experienced in local area for a long long time. Welcome to NEWTOWN. We will be back again and again

I like trying new places and that is the reason we tried this few months after they first opened. It turned out to be one of our favorite Chinese food joints in town. The couple who own it are super friendly and he restaurant is named after their first initials. Pretty much all the dishes we have tried are pretty good, I would say it's hard to go wrong here.
I took my coworker to lunch here. It was 12:30 on a Friday and the place was empty. We should have taken that as a cue to run. Fries were good but the burger and crab cake were a total disappointment

We went a few nights ago for the first time. First the service was exceptional, small but very clean inside... second the authentic Vietnamese food is to die for. (We had the sesame chicken which was also good) My husband had the combination pot and I think it is wonderful, fresh, crisp but cooked and has THE best sauce. I had the beef soup and again wonderful, the broth was exceptionally tasting, spicy yet not so much with hints of lemongrass, and they did not make me feel weird about excluding an item ;) I am excited to try other dishes in the future.

Great addition to the Philadelphia food scene. Will definitely be going back. Pros: Food was delicious - some of the best Mediterranean food I've had in Philadelphia. Great variety. Everything is very light and the portions are appropriately sized. Decor is fantastic, and to top it off they're working on opening up the patio in the future. Great little market with spices, chocolate, olive oil, and other specialty cooking items. Servers are very kind and attentive. Cons: We went for brunch on a Saturday so take this with a grain of salt but I feel that an established restaurant should be able to handle busy times, especially with such a large seating area. Made a reservation for 1:30 for 5 people. Didn't get seated until 1:55, which is fine except they said the kitchen closes at 2PM which made us very nervous/anxious. The 5 things we ordered came out at various times and we're pretty sure they completely forgot to make my friends sandwich until we asked where it was. They missed a couple things that the table ordered. Regardless, will definitely be back and highly recommend to everyone.

Guru's is a wonderful restaurant to go to if you are craving Indian food and especially if you also want to BYOB. The ambience is not super hip or formal, but it is casual and cozy. The lamb vindaloo was delicious-the lamb was moist and the sauce was tangy with a touch of sweetness. It also had a nice heat to it, which you should be aware of when ordering. The chicken makhani was rich, buttery and creamy. The samosas were crispy on the outside with a delicious filling that had a subtle heat to it (note: these could be too spicy for some) This restaurant is a great place to take kids. The kids received little mango lassi "tasters" upon being seated. My kids enjoyed the chicken tikka masala at Guru's which was made perfectly for them as it is mild enough for their palates. The service is warm and friendly but sometimes inconsistent. Once when ordering take out my mango lassis were forgotten with an apology upon my return but nothing else to rectify the mistake. And while the service is generally efficient there can be lulls which is why I'm giving it a 4 out of 5.

Driving up Alt 19 and very hungry..my fourteen year old son and I decided to give this place a try. We have only been to three other Thai restaurants, so we are not experienced in this cuisine at all. As the other reviewers have stated, its in a typical Florida strip mall, but we know enough to not let that stop us. The food was great! We split a Nam Sod salad, that would have been a meal on its own, and loved it. SO flavorful. He had the Panang curry with pork and I had Spicy noodle with Chicken. We ordered both dishes "hot" and they were hot enough for us. They will ask you what heat you want and are very gracious about asking questions and answering requests. The place was packed and you could tell that the other customers were NOT new comers. The portions were large, even my son couldn't finish his meal. We will definitely come back again.

**Why am I doing this to myself... Do I love Dominican food this much that I'm willing to be annoyed by it?** __ Attempt #1 - Look what I found! __ Everything was cool order was right on time, portions were really nice. I had oxtail and canoas. Finally able to find decent canoas in Philly near Center City. Plus points for getting here in less than 20 minutes __ Attempt #2 -Curious __ I REALLY want to like this place, but the little things make all the difference. We stopped in to grab food the staff is super sweet and kind, but the portion when you order to go/delivery was WAY(live visibly) smaller then when you eat in. I've ordered the same 3 things here over the course of finding this place. I'm not sure if different staffing effects portioning but this is weird. __ Attempt #3 - It's getting worse __ This is a SUPER unfortunate situation, as I REALLY like this place.. I ordered from Parada today. Normally everything is super on point and I get stuff pretty quickly...However today was no good. My initial order was not on time, and it was stated it was delayed by 15 minutes.... It was then 15 minutes after the 2nd estimated time. (so over 30 additional minutes late) I was like ok it's cool I like this place a lot, so it's cool I then opened my food (Cubano, Pasteles, and pinto beans) and everything was cold... not like cold from the delivery like everything was CLEARLY sitting. So I called... and spoke with a nice young lady who informed me that the delivery guy was out when my order came in and by the time he arrived my sandwich "had already been sitting like 15 minutes, and then the delivery time"... Not sure why a fresh one wouldn't be made... you wouldn't feed that to an in house guest.. I was told to call tomorrow and they would resend it (cause at this point I don't have time to wait.) I know you're saying well you could warm it up... NOBODY warms up pasteles or a cubano... it's meant to be enjoyed as fresh as possible. __ Attempt # 4 - Eat24 had to "track down" this order __ Old rice, and inconsistent portion.. I went from discovering this place and loving it to now being one of my least favorite places to eat or deal with. Not only did it take an hour and 15 minutes to get a dish described as (a la carte) but when it arrived the delivery driver was rude, didn't thank me for his tip (which I regret giving), the rice I received was old (or under cooked), and the portion was way smaller than it was when I order just a week prior. I really REALLY wanted to love this place, but consistent disappointment has turned a great experience to trash. The staff was extremely unhelpful previously and I'm not sure I want to reach out this time as I was literally told "call tomorrow maybe the manager can help you." I guess you need to eat in house to get the proper experience.... EAT24 was amazing with helping me find the order initially, and deal with my issue post delivery... so that's a plus

Friendly staff but personally didn't love the food. The Mac and cheese was okay and so was the chicken, the sauces weren't great. A bit overpriced because I know I can get wings for cheaper. They do have veggies options which was nice for my friend! I don't like that there's no combo options, everything is bought separately. Good location and nice restaurant.

Great ambiance and attentive service, but food did not live up to the expectation. I was so excited to try Spice Finch because the menu looks unreal, but was disappointed... the food was quite bland, and lacked the unique factor that I was hoping for in Mediterranean - Middle Eastern fusion, which screams bold flavors and spices. The dishes are small and meant to be shared. We started with the stuffed grape leaves, blistered shishito peppers, and fattoush salad. For entree, we shared the roasted cauliflower and dry rubbed chicken. That said, I may have missed the point and would give this place another try, if even for a drink at the bar.

We try to come here once a week for a buffet dinner or lunch. The food is spot on, proper Indian (as good as you can make any ethnic food outside of its territory) and my favorite thing about this place, it is a family business and you can feel that. The owner is very attentive, welcoming and involved. We will dine here for as long as we'll live here for sure.

Went for lunch and sat at the bar, thinking that might be quicker since we needed to get in and out quickly. The guac and chips were excellent. Not as excellent as the guac they serve next door at Delicia since there are no pistachios, but nearly as excellent. The guac was served up immediately. Then the looong wait for our other food began. The bartender was attentive to our iced tea refills, so his service skills were high, it must have just taken a long time to cook what we ordered. My husband had the El Carribean dog. Tasty he said, but probably not worth $6. The chips they mention on the menu are crumbled over the dog fixings. I had the Pick 2 with one shrimp taco, which was really nice and a vegetarian cemita which was awesome. Really, the cemita, made with eggplant, roasted red peppers with cheese is so flavorful, you would not miss the meat. I highly recommend it. They had three televisions, all on different sports channels. Audio was not up on any of the televisions and it was easy to have a conversation in this cute space.

I am a super picky eater but Meun Fan is one of my favorites. They have a clean atmosphere, consistency in their food and great service. My favorite is the garlic pepper chicken. Always good chicken breast meat...no slimy gross tendons like you get in thigh meat. Can get a little busy so we prefer takeout.
We did pay by the weight and paid $16 for about 4 servings of bomb Indian food. Why would you NOT go?

I tried the Dosa Hut for the first time today and I have mixed feelings. The food is pretty good, but the atmosphere feels like a fast food restaurant and everything is served on styrofoam with plastic silverware. I had the vegetable biriyani, which was ok. I like the biriyani from Aman's better. My boyfriend got the spinach masala dosa and that was good. I would recommend the Dosa Hut if you want a dosa. I think next time I would prefer to get take out rather than eat in, there isn't much customer service or atmosphere to speak of. I find the eating experience more pleasant at Aman's in East Norriton and they have dosas as well. The staff there is more friendly and have real plates and silver ware.

Food: 4 Decor: 2 Service: 4 Came here to grab some lunch when I was working in downtown. On hindsight, it wasn't a great idea since it was absolutely freezing outside, and I didn't bring gloves. Still worth it. 1. Cap'n Crunch tilapia burrito ~Pretty good. The tilapia is breaded in Cap'n Crunch, but you wouldn't be able to tell it's Cap'n Crunch. Overall, pretty good mix of ingredients. 2. Short rib taco ~Pretty good, although not very memorable. 3. Thai iced tea ~Pretty good. A bit more ice than I would have liked though. Service was fast and friendly.
Delicious fried rice! Decent service...able to grab a quick dinner before the evening started.

Always receive excellent service and good food. The restaurant is very nice with typical Thai furnishing. The waitresses are dressed in Thai clothes. They are good with children too. Good place to have a business meeting or come with friends. Quiet ambience. Love it!

Seriously one of my all time favorite lunch spots in philly. This lunch truck is always worth the wait! I wish they would open a restaurant haha! I would recommend putting in your order early! They are always super friendly and the food is always consistently good. The chicken catsu burrito is amazing and of course the short rib and chicken satay tacos do not disappoint either. Since my boyfriend has graduated we don't get to get over the bridge while they are open so the only thing I wish they would change is have weekend hours.

Excellent Indonesian food. My Indonesian friends all go here as well. Mie Komplit is really good. The Nasi Goreng Special is pretty good, I really like the pickles. And the Kwetiaw Goreng is only ok. I've also had the Nasi Lemak Rendang there...the beef rendang wasn't the best but the side dishes were really good. Be careful of their hot sauce, it is really spicy! Only bad part is, cash only.

Great authentic food! I've had Thai food at other restaurants all around Tampa....hence I am a HUGEE fan of Thai food...anyways, this is the only place where the food actually taste like the pure heaven deliciousness I have tasted while in Thailand. I know what authentic Thai food taste like and this is it! Fully recommend!

This is a GREAT new place that JUST opened up in the same location as an old crappy Chinese take-out place. The interior has been completely renovated with comfortable seating and a great atmosphere. The food is some of the best in the area, and it's great to have a nice new place to go out for dinner. I've had a couple Chinese dishes and a variety of rolls and everything has been great. Their wonton soup is outstanding! After frequenting this establishment a few times the owner, Jay, introduced himself to me. Now when I go in, I let Jay surprise me with a roll of his choice, and they're always delicious! He even can make my favorites from other sushi restaurants that I enjoy. This is my new go-to place for all my Asian favorites!
I visited yesterday for the first time and will definitely be returning. The falafel was delicious as was the hummus. Everything was fresh and delicious!

La.Va isn't bad...but it's not great either. The art is nice. The bar area is clean. There is an assortment of wonderful looking cookies, pastries, and muffins.
