If you're craving any specific sweet breakfast delight, La.Va will probably have it...including those coveted chocolate croissants. If you're lucky enough, day-old pastries are 50% off. The chairs aren't really sit-and-stay-a-while comfy...but there's wireless internet, so you'll probably do so anyhow. The detox tea is warm and peppermint-y and green. It's nice for relaxing and perking up. It's also loose leaf. La.Va offers a variety of these in addition to some bagged teas, which are of the standard grocery store variety.

I was very reluctant to try this restaurant because of my stupid preconceived ideas about Ethiopian food, but I'm very glad that my wife finally talked me into it. The place is clean, bright and cheery, with plenty of cool pieces of African art on the walls. We were immediately greeted by the owner, one of the friendliest people we've ever seen. She was more than happy to talk us virgins through a complete explanation of the food, and how it would be presented. We ordered a combo plate with lamb, gored gored (cubes of spicy beef), ground lentils, and another veggie plate with squash and green beans, all accompanied by lots of the bread used to pick it all up. Every dish was spicy and delicious, and we scarfed it down with gusto. The dark Ethiopian beer was excellent, but we didn't care so much for the honey wine. My wife said that the restroom was one of the cleanest she had ever seen. Other than the location, in a somewhat dicey part of town, this was one of the best restaurant experiences I've had in this town. We will surely return to Zagol many times, and soon!

I must first start out by saying that the food here is delicious. The Jerk chicken is out of this world. Decent portions, excellent flavor, truly a great food experience. The service however, is questionable. I have been going to Jamaican Jerk Hut for over a year now. I usually go there at least once a month and I have no problem dishing out $15 for a platter of food. Recently there was a living social (or Groupon) deal available so I purchased it. I went with my boyfriend and they questioned us upon our arrival regarding whether or not we had a Groupon or living social deal. We said yes, ordered a few platters, plus appetizers, and did not think anything of it. Come to find out when the food arrived that they skimped on the portions. The $9 coconut shrimp appetizer had less shrimp than usual and the meal platters had less meat. They did not however, have any problem charging us full price for the shrimp appetizer, even though they skimped on the portions. Needless to say, we will go back. But I would advise others not to buy a living social or Groupon deal for them. It's not a deal if you're paying 15 dollars for 30 dollars WORTH of food and you don't get that. Also, they will nickel and dime you to death. They advertise 20% off for parties of four or more. Then when the bill comes, the 20% won't be taken off. When questioned about it they say "oh the person that put that up got fired." Well then, TAKE IT DOWN! False advertisement to lure customers much? Come on Jamaican Jerk Hut. They are lucky I love the food.

I can only echo the complimentary posts below. Forget what this place looks like and go for the food. It's unbelievably good. It is obvious when you walk into Zaika that it suffers from an identity crisis. A sparsely stocked grocery meets butcher meets takeout/casual restaurant with tables. What's going on here I asked the waiter/owner during our meal? He said that they initially opened as a grocery and Halal butcher and began making some food on the side for takeout. The food started to take off surpassing the grocery sales so they scaled back on the dry goods and replaced aisles with tables. I applauded their flexibility to do whatever it takes to make it in this economy. They do, however, plan on making some updates to the space so it feels more like a proper casual dining room in the coming year. Good for them. So if you can get past the temporary aesthetics and lack of ambience you might be greatly rewarded with some fine Pakistani (very similar to Indian) food as we were. We started with crisp vegetable samosas full of peas, potato and spices with a sweet vinegar sc on the side. An excellent standard version. For mains we had Chicken Tikka Masala, Chicken Korma, Lamb sagwalla and Paneer Jalfrezi. We added 2 orders of basmati rice and 2 naans, 1 garlic and 1 house specialty with chili. I won't go into every dish but the sauces in each had long layers of balanced flavors. The meat in the chicken and lamb dishes was of very good cuts and quality. The rice was and the naans, with their soft centers and crispy edges, loaded with herbs and spices was spot on. A couple of the best naans we've had. Our 2 friends who've never eaten Indian food (but are surprisingly open to new cuisines and can handle spicy food) were dumfounded that they've never tried this food before let alone this place. I said they were being spoiled because it isn't always this good. Service was very friendly without being intrusive. They made sure we were comfortable with the spicing by providing mild/med/hot options. We went medium not knowing how they gauge. The food was spicy without setting us on fire. Nothing we couldn't handle. Except for that chili naan which made us numb but in a good way if you like spicy food. We love this place and will probably stay at the 4 Points Sheraton again just so we can revisit (when we go to Sesame Place again). I also plan on bringing a good cooler for leftovers. I was so upset to have to leave them at the hotel. Oh, and it's byo too if you like your wine and/or beer (as we do)

Finally! Good indian food on the main line. I had veggie samosas and chana masala, and both were great. The chana masala was so flavorful. I eat a lot of indian food, and this is truly outstanding. There are only a few tables, but I didn't have to wait to be seated. It's cute and quiet inside. Everyone was really friendly -- great service. Next time I think I will go there for lunch. The lunch menu is very reasonably priced and has some great looking options.

Dear Cucina Zapata, Please forgive me, for I have strayed! In a fit of frustration and boredom, I dined today at a different truck with a similar menu and was rewarded with a sub-par lunch. I should have reviewed you months ago and never left! Please accept this overdue review as my penance. Begging for forgiveness, Sarah So I am lucky enough to work at Drexel right across 32nd Street from the row of food trucks. All the way at the end is this gem. There is always a line, which to me is code for 'this truck is awesome and impatient college students will wait for it.' Both the short rib and chicken satay tacos are delish, but my favorite is the chicken green curry. It is always just the right amount of spicy! Their Thai iced tea is good as well, with the bonus of being able to add bubbles to it. As a recovering bubble tea addict from college, this is a nice fallback for times when I relapse. I have even dragged my fiance from his office near City Hall to grab lunch here. He agreed it was worth a (one stop) subway ride west for a delicious meal.
Terrible service!!! Got the order wrong then had to wait 45 mins to get the fixed order because they kept forgetting about it. No apology or offering to comp the meal.

Amazing food. One of the best we have tried so far. We had all vegetarian dinner. Started with the appetizer and have to say that must try is ghobi manchuriyan. We also had shahi panner and kofta with the basked of bread. Everything was delicious. Best part of the restaurant was the people serving the food. They make you feel home.
#1 in Philadelphia the food is a mixed between Jamaican and soul food I go out of my way just to go there

Oh so good. The closest Thai place to where I work now is 15 minutes, and it's Thai Orchid. Their lunch special is a great deal. You get your choice of soup, appetizer, and entree for $10. N and I both got Thai Dumplings, Tom Yum soup, and Drunken noodles - hers with beef, mine with chicken. Everything was really good, and entree is large. I didn't give 5 stars because of the two following reasons: 1) They made hers WAYYY too spicy to the point where she almost couldn't eat. I got mine 1 spice level below hers, and when I tried hers, there was a huge difference! I actually wanted more spice in mine, and my one bite of hers set my mouth on fire. Yes, she probably could have sent hers back but she didn't want to. 2) We paid the bill. I checked my credit card statement later, and I noticed they rounded up my bill! It was only a couple cents but, hey, it's the principle that counts!!! Maybe it was a mistake, maybe it wasn't. Either way, it's never ok to alter someone's bill.

I didn't even know this place was there until the other day. Went for lunch today and really loved it. Our server was really friendly and the food was delicious. When I asked about the cocktails, she actually went and made us four different sample sailed drinks to taste and they were delicious. I ended up getting the lunch special Roja Viejo with rice and beans and a Puerto Rican Punch to drink. We also split an appetizer of Relleno de Papa de Carne and it was wonderful. I'll be going back soon. So excited that we have an authentic Puerto Rican restaurant in Nashville.

I read another users review and headed over. To my surprise it is actually a small drive through with some picnic tables with umbrellas. Now I'm thinking....can good Greek really be fast food? Answer, yes! Fresh, tasty and as the other user described scratch made tzatziki. Good prices, fast and super friendly. What more could you ask?

After years of patronage, I can't believe I haven't written a review for Bui's. This is the perfect food cart in my eyes: family run, cheap, interesting, and delicious. I'm ashamed to say we get the same damn thing every time, because we love both items: Mrs Bui and the Hangover Special with Bui Sauce. I swear, we drive twenty blocks each way just to get our fix on Saturday and Sunday mornings. When you're in the mood for a filling, awesome sandwich, look no further!

We stopped in for dinner tonight. The food was pretty good, I have no complaints on taste. I like that there is another dinner option in downtown as it seems downtown has an abundance of lunch options but not a ton of dinner places. I do think the food is overpriced for what you are getting. If going for dinner this restaurant should really be a $$$ on yelp because the entrees all but a couple are over $30. Besides being overpriced when we walked up we were told we couldn't sit inside only outside. We were a party of two and asked if inside was reserved and they said yes. Not too long after we sat down the hostess sat a party of two inside who did not have reservations (we were sitting right next to the hostess stand so I could hear them say they did not have a reservation). The outside seating was very full but it seems they only let every fourth party sit inside if you did not have a previous reservation, or large parties without reservations sit inside. Besides this strange seating situation the experience was nice and we will probably try this place for lunch when more sandwiches are featured and the prices don't seem to be as overpriced.

First time at Richards traveling with friends who have frequented this establishment in the past. Easy and convenient parking....right outside the front door! Off on the right foot. Gracious and professional greeter. Our friends hadn't arrived so we decided to imbibe at the adjacent bar. Excellent drinks...made very well by a very attractive bartender (shouldn't matter how good looking she was but it certainly added to the already excellent experience....hope the missus is not reading this!). Friends arrived about 15 minutes later and off to our table we went. I won't play NY Times food reviewer only because everything was excellent according to everyone at the table. Well thought out menu, goodly portions, beautiful presentation and, most importantly, great flavors. I do want to mention something that I always take note of at every dining spot I visit: wait staff. They can make or break your dining experience. The gentleman who waited on our table was excellent! Polite, knowlegable about the menu (as well as 'special' orders as requested by one at our table) and very timely. Arrived at the table discretely and at the perfect intervals without being annoying nor disruptive to the conversation at the table. Hats off to him! Great establishment....will return. Highly recommend for intimate dinners i.e. anniversarys, Mom and Dad night out, small birthday evening out or telling your better half it's over (at least they will have enjoyed a great meal!....Kidding!!!!!). Two thumbs up!

Had dinner here for the second time last Saturday and feel compelled to let others know how good it was. It was not merely the food, which was excellent, but also the ambiance, as it is a small, intimate, single room setting where one can hear other people at the table speak without having to shout. It is also a BYOB making it that much more enticing for diners. The food, as I said, was very good Indian cuisine at a reasonable price. We had a chicken appetizer, a lamb entrée and vegetable entrée along with two orders of bread split between three people, which was more than enough, and the bill was only $50.00. The dining room was, surprisingly, not that crowed. I would add that the waiter was very friendly and accommodating. I don't think anyone at the table could have been more pleased by the dining experience and we will surely return.

Great Thai close to home (for me anyway). Have to start with the crab delight and first entree choice is their amazing phad thai, a close second is the Yellow Curry. You will not be dissapointed and the servings are huge which makes for great leftovers!

Came here after hearing some good things about their thai food, and always up for a change of cuisine, I figured I'd give it a go. Sat down in the multi-leveled dining room, which was filled with a handful of other lunch-goers. Not sure if they still run their lunch special, but I got a small salad, soup, and entree for a really good price. The salad was a simple, but fresh garden variety, and the soup, a vegetarian tofu was lightly flavored and not overly salted. I chose the green "Heavenly" curry, with all veggies, and it came out with a scoop of fragrant basmati rice and a delicious vegetable-coconut combo that was perfectly spiced, light, yet rich. All in all, the atmosphere, and meal were excellent, and I will have to try them out for dinner.

Indian food which is to die for. Authenticate and quality, it's doesn't get better than this. They are always super nice. They even thought me how to say thank you in there language, of course i asked first. Very casual. Everything is awesome except for one thing, something which is unavoidable; plan to smell like a delicious Indian cuisine when you leave. So you may not want to go to the movies or hangout in a public place afterward. I know from experience, some one told me I smelled funny. :D Awesome place!

My review is not based on the food since I didn't get to sample it. I called for take out on Sunday night and got a voicemail for Mamita's (the predecessor restaurant) after trying 5 times over an hour. I finally got through to the restaurant and the guy who answered said they are really busy and I should call back later. REALLY? You are a new restaurant and you are telling customers to call back. Busy is fine but take the order and then tell the customer a realistic time period to pick it up. I will wait awhile before trying this work-in-progress restaurant.

This is my favorite local Thai restaurant. There is another closer to my house but I prefer to come here. The lunch specials are great and come with soup and salad or an egg roll. I love their Thai tea, Chicken and Drunken Noodles and Chicken Fried Rice. I had the crunchy salmon roll yesterday and neither myself nor my friend particularly cared for it but it was fresh. I also like the pan fried dumplings. I used to love their coconut juice but they changed brands and I don't like the new one.

This place is basically the same as Kombo Kitchen, which is a good thing. I loved that place. I couldn't tell a difference in my meal. I think they just rebranded (and fixed a door that had perhaps the world's most evil squeak). Thai 5 isn't quite 5 stars good. I had the fried tofu spicy drunken noodles. The tofu was delicious, but the meal was otherwise alright. It had too few vegetables, and the flavors weren't quite right. Still, I enjoyed my meal, and I'll be happy to return. Note: I gave Kombo Kitchen 5 stars, but I was about to change that when Kombo Kitchen closed. They went down hill a little.

The fried rice was pretty good... however thats the only positive thing i have to say. They told me my order would be ready in 15-20 minutes. I came back 30 minutes later and they said it wasnt ready yet. I went back to my car (not much sitting room inside) and waited another 10 minutes and asked again.... it still wasnt ready. I asked how much longer it would be and they said 10 more minutes.... Of course 15 minutes later it still wasnt ready. Long story short it took over an hour just to get some fried rice and a saint paul sandwich. The rice was pretty good, but the main reason i wanted to go there was to try the angry bird saint paul sandwich. Ive always loved saint paul sandwiches, so i was intrigued by the idea of their angry bird. However when i ate it, it wasnt at all what i expected. It was disgusting. I'm thinking that i just got a bad one since it seems to be pretty popular. Not sure that it was cooked thoroughly? But I am sure that it gave me food poisoning!!! I ate this on thursday evening and I got diarrhea friday morning and had leave work early. It's now sunday night and I'm still sick.
The food came out REALLY quick. Almost too quickly for my liking. However it was really tasty. I am still on a search for the best Baklava in Tampa. This was not it. Sorry to say.

I wish I could give two reviews, one for Mojitos the restaurant and the other for Mojitos the Friday night salsa party! As the former, I have to admit that I like it but don't love it. The courtyard is beautiful, the food (especially the appetizers) is good, but the service has been incredibly uneven across the four or five times I've eaten there. Salsa night at Mojitos, on the other hand, is one of my favorite things in the whole world! The atmosphere is just so much fun. The music is pretty varied and you can't really beat their drinks. The watermelon mojito is perfect, I will never dance with a beer in my hand again ;-).

Stopped in on a Wednesday evening around 7pm and was surprised to see how empty the dining area was. Nevertheless, we enjoyed our pad thai, chaing mai chicken, and crab rangoon. The steamed vegetables were a little cold but everything else tasted wonderful. The prices seemed a tad too high but nothing crazy. Overall a delicious dinner with a reasonable amount of lot parking in broad ripple off the river. We'll be back soon!

Great "hole in the wall" family owned BYOB Italian restaurant. I came here for dinner by myself when I was traveling, and was able to have a "reservation" at the bar as all of their tables were full - I didn't mind. I sat at a bar type area (it had bar glasses and probably at one point was a full service bar but since the restaurant is BYOB there was no alcohol) - instead the waiters used it to fill any soft drinks and water, and the hostess stood behind it to answer phones, close out the tabs for the waiters, etc. The hostess was very nice and talked to me while I waited for my food, and had great recommendations about the food at her family's restaurant. I appreciated that the staff was "in the family" as I believe everyone who worked there was either in the family of the owners, or extremely close to them. The hostess recommended the stuffed calamari, which is not something that I'd normally order but I was very glad that I did. The portion was very large and I had plenty of leftovers. My only complaint was that they do not make their own noodles (with the exception of the gnocchi), which I feel took away from it truly being an Italian restaurant. I also ordered a beat arugula salad as an appetizer which was very good, with very fresh greens, and what I felt were proper portions of goat cheese, nuts, greens, tomatoes,and beets. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone in south philly.
Awsome! Authentic and Awsome is all I can say! I had the goat curry spicy with garlic flaan. Authentic and delishish!

My husband and I ate here last night and enjoyed everything. The mojito was YUM (not overly strong, the mint was crushed and flavorful), the tostones w/ ceviche on top perfect (favorite thing), and both of our entrees were great. If you like plantains, you'll love Salsa. Gustavo was a great bartender/server and being Puerto Rican, knew about the food and what to recommend, etc. Oh, and Gustavo also gave us a free sample of the coquito, which was AMAZING. It was like a dessert in a glass with cinnamon on top. The cinnamon added perfection to the drink. I'm sad I didn't order that instead for my drink. But! Was still very pleased with my mojito :-) Salsa also has dancing periodically, which is awesome, since I love latin influenced music! Best dance music. Ever.
The best Korean chicken wings I've ever put in my mouth! It is off the charts awesome!!!
Incredible personable service. Good food for a good price. Family owned. They work hard and it shows recommend it. Love the salt and pepper chicken lunch combo.

I've been back here a few times for dinner buffet on Friday or Saturday night, and I am consistently impressed by this place. Each time I go I say it's the best Indian I've ever had. Their buffet is huge, well stocked, and has new dishes each time. There are easily 25 dishes to choose from. The restaurant is clean, quiet and reasonably priced. The service is friendly and efficient. Can't recommend it highly enough to anyone in the area who likes Indian. I still like House of India, but their buffet just doesn't compare to Ruchi.
Price is good. The service is fast. Food are great. We ordered N1, R1, and R16. Definitely come back and try the other items in the menu.

This place is fantastic. The service was great. Sometimes at these mom and pop joints the servers can be a little aloof, but that was not the case here. We were greeted promptly and sat quickly. The server was very good at not just engaging me, but also my children. She treated them like they were mini adults. She came back quickly with our drinks and asked if we wanted to order anything while we were waiting on our friends. Once our friends got there we ordered some appetizers. We got the taro root and the tofu ones. Both were very good. The sauce served with the taro root was really flavorful. My friend is a vegan and this place is very vegetarian/vegan friendly. Not only to they offer quite a few veggie dishes, but they also offer mock meats as well. She ordered the mock chicken pad thai. My kids ordered the beef with tofu. They were out of the bean sprouts that normally come on the dish, but we didn't feel like it was missing anything. I ordered the monkfish dish. It was very well prepared. Normally that dish comes out spicy, but I asked them to tone it down some since I was sharing with the kiddos. They gladly accommodated my request. Everything was really delicious. I also appreciated that the background music was not too loud. It was just loud enough to here, but not overpowering. I also loved the color of the plates they served on. Kind of a soft greenish color. They also served my food on a fish shaped dish that my daughter loved. I can't wait to go back and try some other dishes. Looking at the food at the other tables has me very excited to try some new things. The prices were very reasonable. And the food did well with reheating the next day for lunch.

I have to say that I was impressed with Ninja Noodle. Received a really cool menu in my mailbox it was enticing to look at - so right from the beginning they have good marketing - & a good approach. I ordered a dinner for two and was really excited about the three entrée choices you get to make from a list which also includes chicken fried rice and spring rolls as well as fortune cookies who doesn't love a good fortune! The food arrived quickly - even during a very busy rush-hour / dinner hour. Oh Ya - & you even have a choice of spring rolls with your combo orders; it's very rare that you can order a Vietnamese spring roll as they are the best ! That was exciting lol. As far the Americanized / Chinese/Thai food they didn't excellent job I would recommend it for a movie night with the family - or a cold fall / winter night - good comfort food. If you are a family of three - you'd be fine with a dinner for two. Free delivery within 5 km & 10% off pick up orders if you pay cash. love the deals
Food doesn't taste good at all! I have had better Vietnamese food! I did not like any dish that we ordered!

I have had tremendous Thai food in Southern California, so I expect a lot. This place delivered. It wasn't amazing, but they didn't make any blunders on the food. The portions are the largest of any Thai restaurant I think I have ever been to. They have a great lunch special that comes with a couple options like side salad and an egg roll. The Thai iced tea is good and also a generous serving. Ask for less condensed milk as its a tad sweet. They were fast on service, and the patrons also very kind. We went there three times in one week, so that tells you something.

Great Vietnamese food that hits the spot. However, their pho when they frosted opened tasted a lot better than what they are serving now but otherwise everything here is pretty good if you don't feel like driving 46 minutes into Philly.
Oustanding food...! A peaceful place with a lot of good things going for it...! A real treasure for Treasure island....!

Went there with a girlfriend for dinner in Friday. We sat down and asked the server what his favorites are from the menu. He recommended Gored Gored (beef dish), Beg Tibs (lamb dish), Gomen (vegetarian dish). We ordered all three and were not disappointed! The food was soooooooo good that we forgot to take photos and just dove in when the food arrived. The bottomless injera compliment the dishes so well. Definitely a must try! The only disappointment was there wasn't many people there.
Interesting place with bright beautiful decor and quite atmosphere. A lot o delicious dishes. High quality service and qualified friendly staff.
Excellent drinks! The food... perfectly prepared. Attentive wait staff.. we dine all over the country. Highly recommended!

SORRY JT...but although your dishes are tasty, they dont taste Thai. Having spent 15 months living in Korat, and falling in love with the people, culture, religious practices and FOOD, I was dissapointed in the taste, the portion size (too small) and the price (too high for the portion size.) I leave any readers of this review with this caveat; I ordered take out. JUST MAYBE the portions are larger for dining in. BOTTOM LINE: OK, but not authentic. My search ccontinuex.

This place so delicious! I'm a vegan and they worked with me to try to find something that would work for me! Their summer rolls were my favorite.y dad enjoyed his lo mein and I enjoyed my basil rice noodle tofu dish.
Such a cute place! Shrimp pad Thai is the yummiest! The owners are the sweetest people ever! Must try!

My husband and I just had a brunch here. The place is really lovely and the staff are very friendly. Baba ganoush is served with Pita bread and the taste is phenomenal! Definitely bring friends over here again.

I had heard great things about this restaurant and was excited to try it, as I love Mediterranean food. I was extremely disappointed. My chicken swarma wrap had 90% onions and 10% chicken and that's being generous on my part. My friend's Kifka wrap was the same. I gave it two stars because the food was fresh and service was good.

Best authentic Dominican Food in the city; that I know of!! My best friend is Dominican so I thought this place would be the perfect place to take her for her birthday dinner and she said she was going to come back the next day!! It's wonderful here!!!

Easily the best dining experience I've ever had and I'm not remotely exaggerating. I've eaten at expensive and exclusive places and this is the first I've felt truly welcomed. We came straight from the airport and we're starving. The food was delicious (plantains, ox tails and goat curry) but most of all was the service. The owner and his son came over and were so personable and welcoming. Not only did they provide a fantastic meal but gave us much advice about the city and offered great conversation. Definitely check this place out.

I'm glad I've finally found a decent place with Thai food that delivers! So far everything I've ordered has been pretty good. The food can be a little on the spicy side so watch for the jalapeños if that's not your thing. I love the freshness of the vegetables especially (still crisp, not cooked to softness). Prices are reasonable and the food is plentiful, so far so good!

Came here for the lunch buffet for $12 and it was fantastic. They had a good selection of vegetarian and meat dishes and they were all tasty! They have naan bread and byriani and salad and dessert as well. I was satisfied with pretty much everything I had there and would recommend this place without a doubt. Great value and authentic Indian food. Also very polite service. The decor is very cozy and houselike.
This place is so awesome! My husband and I have been going here almost every single week for over a year. The panang is the best around! The atmosphere isn't much but the food is great!
Tea glasses are way too small. Owner is a grouch most of time. It has changed and it's too bad. We went almost every week.
La Na Thai up the street is better. Ordered take-out. Gave this place a shot because of the reviews and rating, but my dish was dry and flavorless and I couldn't even finish the Lemon Grass soup. :/
Went to have lunch along with 8 navy professionals at 11:30 am on Saturday 2/21/21015 and they don't open til noon. They just lost allot of business.

I read some reviews and decided to try it out. it was decent. I got a chicken wrap with everything on it. It was huge! and good. the hummus dip I got was a little lack lust in flavor but the Pita chips were hot and fresh so that was a bonus. My wife was not impressed with the salad she got though, kinda boring and I guess the lettuce was a little wilted. I will probably stop here again when I feel like healthier fast food.

Was going for pizza but stumbled in here instead. Red curry and Pad Thai for our table and we weren't disappointed. Reasonably priced and decent beer. Red curry was flavorful but without a ton of salt. No need to carry a water bottle around for the rest of the night, unlike many other Thai places. I do wish chop sticks were standard. While service was good, I was 1/3 through my meal when I finally got sticks. We will return. Lunch specials look especially good.

I don't know how this place only has 3 stars overall! And I also don't know how I've overlooked reviewing it for so long! The bf and I probably eat here 1-2x a week, always for take out. When I call, they usually recognize me and have a pretty good idea of what I want, but they always repeat the names of what I order (I order by number) so there is no confusion. However, unlike the other thai places in the loop (yeah I'm calling you out Thai Cafe and Thai Gai Yang!), their menu online is actually up to date, so there shouldn't be any problems. I always order some combination of the same things. I love the veggie spring rolls (number 2) and the veggie tempura (number 4) as appetizers. The spring rolls come in a group of 4, and are fried and served with light and tasty sweet and sour sauce. The tempura is lightly fried green beans, carrots, onions, broccoli, and baby corn, also served with the same sweet and sour sauce. It is huuuge, and could probably be a meal...for most people. But luckily, I always have room for more! For my entree, I usually order the Lard Nar Sen Sod (number 51), which is a flat rice noodle with baby corn and broccoli (but I always add green onion) in a light but semi-thick brown sauce. Of course with most entrees here, you can choose your protein (chicken, pork, or tofu, or shrimp or beef for 2 dollars extra), but I always get tofu, and theirs is firm but not rubbery like some places. Perfectly cooked, just the way I like it! But y'all know that this girl likes variety, so when I want to mix things up, I order the Yellow Curry Plate (number 65), which consists of potatoes, carrots, and onions, and is served with white rice, that is a bit more moist and sticky (in a gooood way) than chinese white rice. Again, I get it with tofu, and I always request that it not be spicy, even though yellow curry is the most mild of all the curries. The bf orders Khao Lard Kratiem Prik Thai (or I order it for him), which is basically your chosen protein sauteed in garlic and black pepper, and comes with white rice as well. I think it might come with broccoli normally, but I always specify that they keep all veggies and anything else that even resembles green far away from his beef. My orders are always straight out of "When Harry Met Sally," as are the bf's sometimes, and despite me always being difficult, they NEVER get it wrong. I tear open the brown bag without fear of missteps, and I always know that they will have thrown in my little side of fried gaaahlic as well. Yeah that's right...you can fry garlic. Best invention EVER...ok, tied with the fried pickle. And they know that I'm the garlic chick. Now that's some service! Warning: They're closed on Tuesdays. But I'm thinking about starting a petition so I don't have to suffer through another sub par thai meal on Tuesday nights! Wanna sign?
First time trying it today! Very good!!! Had the buffalo chix, the Chinese veggie and the reuben..Delicious!! The service was very good as well. Will be back!

Came here for the first time and the whole experience was wonderful from the moment we walked in. The place is small and cozy but not too small if you happen to have a larger party. The drink menu has an extensive array of cocktails that are quite unique as well as some classics such as an old fashioned. I loved the champagne drink I got with coconut rum, it was delicious and reminded me of the beach! The bartender Will was awesome and knew what he was doing behind the bar. I also ordered the fried risotto as a meal as I wasn't starving and it was the perfect portion as well as delicious. Can't wait to come back and try other dishes when I'm more hungry
Amazing food! Went for dinner and enjoyed it all. Great drinks, apps and entrees. The coffee was even incredible. Well done!

I was starving when I swung into this restaurant, with a craving for a hot bowl of Vietnamese soup and spring rolls. It was a brighter, cleaner, more cheery looking place than a lot of Vietnamese restaurants in the city. I might even call it warm and slightly cozy. Two people were sitting at the front and I caught a glimpse of what they were eating as I walked in and decided I'd get what they were having. It looked warm, good, filling and not too mysterious. I worry about the meat at oriental restaurants, so I try to stick to chicken, but here I ordered the spicy noodle soup with medium-rare beef, and the quality seemed fairly good. The soup was fresh, steaming and delicious. The service was courteous and fast. I also ordered spring rolls with pork and vermicelli and they were very flavourful, served with a tasty, tangy dipping sauce. The neighbourhood's not the greatest around here, but the place was starting to fill up around 11:30 a.m. with the downtown lunchtime business crowd. They must do quite well. I will definitely go back. Next time I want to try the steamed tapioca dumplings, which looked good and the shrimp meatballs grilled on sugarcane.

The first time I had coffee at Remedy in the Garneau district was in May of 2015...it is a very nice looking coffee shop with lots of seating, large windows, and plenty of choices for food & drinks. But the only table I found was dirty, but I didn't have much other choice, so I sat there anyways. The second time I went, which was last night will be the last night. I don't really feel comfy in these types of cafes...there's almost this hipster vibe, or something similar to that, where I just never feel 100% comfortable. Anyways, I ordered my "large" regular coffee, which was okay...but at nearly $4 a cup, it had better be decent! But I waited more than 10 minutes before I got it...it sat for half of that time forgotten under the steeping machine thing-a-ma-bob! It wasn't even hot by the time I had to ask the cashier guy to grab it for me! I can see why many people love or like this place, but it's not for me, and I will avoid it from here on in! #yeglove #yegcoffee

I ordered one large jerk chicken dinner,it came with 2 drumsticks and 2 backs rice peas cabbage.after receiving my so called large jerk chicken dinner.i went to my car to see how the food was ,the chicken was room temperature,the whole entire meal was substandard.the proprietor that operates this establishment should be ashamed of himself.i didn't like the food it all went in the garbage were it belongs!!!

Went here with a couple of friends at lunch on a Friday. The place was empty at 1PM. One of my friends had been there and was thrilled that they had "boat noodles" which he became fond of while living in L.A. The place is open and very nice. Our server was borderline surly, never even attempting to smile, spending most of her time behind the bar starring at her phone. Two boat noodles and one Pad Thai came out with soup, salad and spring roll. I ordered an iced tea and was shocked that it was some really watered down lipton variation, not the orange thai tea. The soup was a clear broth with a few scallions thrown in, but was fine. The salad was tiny with a mustard dressing, again OK. The spring roll was standard fare, but lacked the black pepper zing they usually have. My friend said his Pad Thai was good. The boat noodles did nothing for me. The broth was watery with the aroma of five spice, but lacked any zing or acidity. The noodles were fine but the meat tasted like pot roast. Too many other good Thai places to go back, I'm afraid.
No Hispanic that has any respect for them self eats here. This food is just terrible. Tropi chop was a Tropi slop.

This place was amazing. The main door looks like the front door of a house and then inside is a beautiful staircase which gives you a very home-like feel. Came here with a group of people on Wednesday night it wasn't busy at all. We did family style food so the owner brought out all of the main dishes and smaller portions and everything was delicious. The Jerk Wings had a kick to them and the chicken was spicy. This place is BYOB. The staff are so friendly it's a father-and-son who work here and their story is inspirational. I would highly recommend this place to anyone. It's Trinidadian food and certain dishes are spicy but it's so good.
Although they are still getting their staff trained, I was met with friendly faces and good food. It was my first time here, and I got my order fast during lunch time.

Oh hello there, Kashmiri Chai! How are you? Where did that delicious full-bodied flavor come from? And your green coloring? Hmmm,what sort of magical deliciousness is this that I had not previously experienced? Did you just make this up, Remedy, or is there a whole new type of chai I didn't even know existed? I mean, I rarely drink the stuff so it could be, but I've never seen it on a menu in my home town. Maybe that's because our Indian options suck... but I digress. I know you can't be healthy, rich green chai, because thick, creamy drinks don't come from low fat sources, regardless if it's made non-dairy with a substitution of almond milk. Oh, and thanks for being available in almond milk format. The cow-stuff just doesn't do it for me. I can only imagine how creamy it would be when made with yak butter. Mmm.... yak. I don't really care that the atmosphere is loud and ramshackle, with tables sort of thrown together and all sorts of university folk doing loud things around me. I can slip some ear buds in, leech off of the free wifi and revel in the comfort of your green goodness. Mmmmm... this will be a must-stop next time I'm in Edmonton!

I've eaten here several times and have had nothing but good experiences. What's not to like about Caribbean fast food? Rice, beans, chicken, roasted pork, sancocho and sangria at the ready! I remember when this chain was around back in the 90's, and I was a sad face clown when they all went belly up. So I got really excited when they began cropping up again several years ago. One of my favorites is the Caribbean chicken and spinach wrap, but heed my word, it's really small. The menu picture is very misleading. Other than that, I pretty much stick to (and recommend) the rotisserie chicken. It's got great flavor and the sauces at the bar are awesome for dipping. My recommendation, the TropiChop with pork, rice, beans, green peppers and onions. Very fast. Very CONSISTENT.

Sooo good, AND, they delivered all the way to Jenkintown. That's a big bonus. We got the shrimp Hakka noodles, the sweet and sour chicken, and the chicken tikka masala and wow, they were awesome. The tikka masala might be the best I ever had, and over lots of rice, we couldn't stop eating it! I woke up and had spicy Hakka noodles for breakfast! Can't wait to try more dishes!

This probably was an off night for the restaurant, we ordered the Korean fried chicken due to the rave Yelp reviews and were not impressed. It seemed like there was more batter than actual chicken. But the owner came by and explained to us that " that is how Korean friend chicken is". The sushi was subpar, reminiscent of something you would get out of a supermarket. The fish just was not fresh. I may go back to give it a re-do but the chances are slim.

Fantastic. Love these place. A little pricey but totally worth it. I lived in that area for a few years and this place is my go-to for Indian. I still crave the lamb korma (with whole cashews) and amazing paneer nan. Lunch buffet is an affordable way to try the basics. They offer a student discount for to go orders too! You have to try this place.

We had heard that this was the best Indian food in Delaware County, but it's not. It's definitely Indian for white suburbanites. There's not much flavor, and the spice level is non existent. For approachable Indian, you're much better off at Tiffin or Ekta.

The food here is authentic, close to my house, and the price is decent. I have eaten alot of Malaysian/Indonesian foods and really enjoy it's unique taste. This place provides the "homemade" taste to Indonesian cuisine. The noodle bowls were the best so far.

Came here with a huge group of friends today for lunch. It's quite a walk from where we were, but it was well worth it :) The place itself is fairly small, and so it was quite the effort for the 10+ of us to fit in the only two tables there. Service there was fast and no nonsense, but it is really the food that makes this place. I ordered the oxtail platter (small), which was a sizable portion for a greater price. The oxtail was delicious--flavorful and juicy. I only wished that they could have given more, especially because the bones were so large. I didn't get to order a smoothie, but I'm sure to try one next time!

Amazing food. I had the vegetable panang curry, vegetable potstickers and Thai tea. Great flavor in everything. So upset I didn't save any for lunch the next day. Very good customer service and everyone was very hospitable. The wait for our main entrees was a little long but with good company it was hardly noticeable. Saw quite a few customers come in to get takeout orders. This would be an amazing stretchy pants Netflix marathoning food choice. Also very clean restrooms as a side note.
Pricey but decent food. Some of the servers are wads but most are not bad. Sushi is fresh, I guess that's all that matters!

Its a cute, romantic place with dim lighting and friendly service. The Tom Yum soup wasn't very flavorful but the golden bag appetizer was unbelievable. As reviews mentioned before, the pad thai is a little off. Not necessarily bad, but not the usual, peanut-y sauce that I'm used to. The massaman curry was the best I've had in a while but if you are looking for a good drunken noodle, head to tamarind on south street.

I will start by saying the food is amazing. My favorite is the chicken fried rice, crab rangoon, and lime soda. Each time I go I try something new. That being said let me tell you about Lucy and Kahn the owners. It should be no surprise that the food tastes so good because it comes from good people. They are the kindest and most courteous individuals you could hope to meet. They make my heart happy each time I stop by to get their amazing food. Do yourself a favor and make the trip to see them no matter where you live in Indianapolis. I promise it will not disappoint!! DID I MENTION THE FOOD TASTES AMAZING?!!!! As a matter of fact, after writing this review I'm headed straight there to say hi to my friends and eat until my stomach sings!
We went here for meatless meal. Very happy finding a better Thai restaurant in St Louis than the ones we loved in Phoenix.
A++ for food quality, selection, ambiance, service, and price. This is the best Thai on the Gulf Coast.

They actually have Bo Bun Hue and it was pretty good for West Chester (yes this rating is relative to location and price lol). Stack up to Philly? No. Worth it to get if you are craving some authentic Viet and don't want to drive? Yesssssssssir

Now this is really good food from people who CARE. Does anyone realize how important CARING is when it comes to making food. You know why home cooking tastes to good? Because the person making it (usually Mom or G-Mom) cares. It's made with love and this food is made with love.

Review Based Solely on Chicken Biryani. I'm a chicken biryani guy. I've been living in Saint Louis for 6 months now. Had experiences at some restaurants. The only ones that I could say are worth going to would be Anis and Swagruha. I would rate both of these extremely good. Swagruha though gets extra points for consistency. A trait almost all restaurants fail at. I would recommend Hyderabadi Chicken biryani and 555 chicken biryani.
Their portion sizes are large and brunch is delicious. The service is friendly and I enjoyed the view with our outside seating.

Food is Ok, however their customer service for pick up orders is terrible. Lots of noodles not much of the veggies or protein...not worth the expense. Don't even attempt with their coupons, I've had multiple issues.

They were open on 4th of July which was nice. I believe there where were 8 main dishes to choose from and 4 types of dessert. The rice was a little dry, but the Naan was good. The dishes weren't too spicy which can be good or bad depending on your taste buds. The service was great. He cleared our plates quickly and refilled our water.

The first thing we noticed was the beautiful wood carved tables and the hostess dressed in a stunning red attire. There was thai tea for two of us, one without cream. That was the most stout thai tea I've had, but delicious and we enjoyed edamame for starters. Around the table: Pineapple fried rice. The words "Mmmm" and "This is the best..." was heard between bites. Next, Ginger Salmon and Shrimp. Not a word was heard, only the sound of the fork tapping the plate with each bite...and "Good choice" after the plate was clean. I had the Noodle Soup with chicken. I like soup...I'm a "soupie". A light, clear broth with chicken, scallions and cilantro. I did have some of the noodles, even though I'm not a noodle fan, and they were tasty. The hostess was light spoken, but gave us a great tutorial on which sauces and ingredients would taste good together. I like that. Yes, good choice...

WHAT THE EFF HAPPENED TO THIS PLACE. I used to go here so often, cause their cooking was decent/good. There aren't that many other Asian places to go to. They started expanding their menus, and gaining more customers while the quality of everything was going down. Some of the new items are good, especially the ones in the separate Chinese menu. Once they got a bit more busy though, they couldn't keep up. The employees there suck. They're so disorganized and forgetful, I wondered if they even knew what they were doing. Now, every time I go there I always think "I could do a better job than this." My friend and I waited 40-50 minutes for ONE of my orders to arrive, 25-30 minutes of that time in which I had no water even though I asked. When we finally got the food though, the fried rice wasn't even fried rice. We sent it back and asked for a new one cause we thought it wasn't fried enough. That wasn't the problem. The rice wasn't cooked properly. It was overcooked with too much water, making it lumpy and mushy. We were so disappointed we ended up eating less than half of it and didn't take it to go. When we were ordering, we decided to go out of our comfort zone and try their recently added popcorn chicken for $6. Damn, did we regret it. Popcorn chicken is supposed to be crunchy. I thought I was eating microwaved, then deep-fried frozen Dino nuggets. Also, who charges $4 for fries? There's a Habit across the street. I could go on and on about my disappointments that have been accumulating since my initial experiences with this place. I'm just gonna stick to their pho and egg rolls from now on.

Between the linguine and clams, mussels and squid ink pasta, Zeppoli brings authentic Mediterranean cuisine to life. The rosemary olives were perfect with just enough herb. Highly recommend coming during a weeknight. The service was awesome - cannot say enough good things about the attention to detail throughout our meal.

Most definitely the food was from awesome ... Jerk wings were out of bounds .. But I got jibbed of the sides .. If comes with it .... Put it in the plate out especially take out .. But will most definitely be back thank you

I absolutely love this place and will grab a sandwich there as often as possible. Prices start at $3.25 for a 12 inch sandwich, a real bargain for quality food. It's really not about the fillings, start with the special #1 sandwich and work your way through the menu, you can't go wrong. The real stars are the bread (made with rice flour, not too big around and light as a cloud with a crispy exterior), the delicious veggies and the cilatro. The bread is so light it's easy for a person with a little appetite to eat the whole 12 inch sandwich. I have never tried the bobo drinks but they sure look good! Can hardly wait for my next sandwich - is the new place downtown open yet?

Food quality has gone downhill in the last few years. I've gone twice in the last year and both times I encountered the same horrible female employee. She is vulgar, unprofessional, and made me feel like ordering food there was inconveniencing her since it was a half hour before closing. I used to love this place and the food used to be fresh. Now the food looks like it sits out all day and the place seems unsanitary.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Utterly awesome in every way. Curry++ beer list++ served by the owner who was so friendly and hilarious. Amazing experience
Shout out to the staff at Blue Plate. It was Mother's day and with no reservations we were seated in less than 20 minutes. The service was excellent and as always the food was delicious. Great job!

Wow! This is an amazing place. We were looking for a place that would have some good vegan and vegetarian choices as well as fish and meet offerings. This place did not disappoint! The date truffles, sourdough flat bread, charred carrot hummus, shrimp and lemon yogurt were all amazing!

Ordered to-go from here. The lady who answered sounded like the typical Chinese lady who answers and tries to make the call quick. I ordered 5 dishes from here and she was so quick to ask me "is that it?" (I don't know about you but, I'd like to be the one who ends the order since I'm the customer. Right?!) Anywho, went on to order black pepper beef, sweet & sour chicken (lunch portions on both), salt & pepper calamari, veggie chow fun and Vietnamese udon soup. Price was fair, portions were good but the food tasted awesome!! It was not greasy, every dish had their distinct flavor of what it should be. Hubby, kids and I really enjoyed it.

Dale Wasem's casual West End restaurant serves Greek salads, gyros and more. I ordered at the marble counter and received my basket of food at the table within ten minutes. It takes a little time since each order is prepared when you order. A hot griddle was used to crisp my spanakopita rollup which was crunchy on the outside with tender chicken, spinach and feta on the inside. The two rollups were cut in half for a total of four fair size pieces. As with other weekday specials it came with a side. Mine was slightly tart tomato cucumber salad, also crisp. Of the two big rooms I decided on the one with brick and natural wood ceiling. Wall decor is minimalist which helps to lend a relaxed ambience. I'm not sure the food is better than nearby Kalamatas, but the atmosphere sure is. I'll be back to experience the other daily weekday specials for under $10.
Decent, and affordable. The bread to filling ratio on the sandwiches could use a little tweaking (more filling!). Love the spiciness.

like a true viet, i know my pho. it's the phood of my people! i come here with my family and if it can pass my parents' picky palette, then you all know this place is banging. i order the chicken pho. i ask for it with white meat. the broth is flavorful, hot, and filled to the brim and i get to add all the garnish. mint, beansprouts. limes. don't forget to add the squeeze of lime. i let my lime swim in my soup. hotsauce. hoisin sauce. more hot sauce. the beef pho is also good. the lunch specials seem to go fast, so if you want the special, get there early. order the chicken pho, get the bubble coffee, and for an appetizer, while they still have it, get the fresh/summer spring rolls with crab and shrimp! it is light and perfect for the spring days to come. also, end it with a fresh lime soda. ask for the fresh lime and they will add the carbonated soda. the waiters are nice, the hostess all smiles, my family and i come here to eat pho, talk, get the vietnamese newspapers and eat an authentic vietnamese meal without cooking it ourselves! quality family time. quality pho.

A decent Thai/Japanese restaurant. I only tried the Thai style food and it satisfied. Nice noodles with tasty shrimp. Service was remarkably slow, verging on absent, especially as I visited at 7pm on a Friday night.

I love this place! I come here all the time, especially when I'm craving Asian comfort food. I usually get Pho 17 or the #42 rice/meat, and they're both great. The lady who serves me is always nice and attentive, and one of the main reasons I always return is because of her great service. The Pho they serve here is almost $10 and comes in one size only. I love the shape of the bowls that they serve it in (large and deep), but it's too much to eat in one sitting. It usually takes me two meals to finish it, so I would suggest asking them to split it into two orders (half "for here" and the other half "to go") if you decide to dine in. I do recommend eating in because the place emits a homey feel. For coffee drinkers out there, try the Vietnamese coffee. It'll blow your mind away. If there was such a thing as a rugged (bittersweet) taste, that's how Vietnamese coffee will taste like on your palate. They also have boba! And in my opinion, this place is way better than the Saigon Noodle/Pho place next to KMart.

First time trying this place, and am so happy I tried it. One of the best Cuban sandwiches I have ever had. Perfectly pressed, and delicious. I can't wait to try more. Recommending to everyone I work with! Great place.

Waited for an hour only to find out the staff forgot my order. Couldn't care less about the taste. Horrible staff and management! Will make sure I and the people I know never return to this place. That in the picture is the only thing I kept looking at the whole time.

If this is one of the better thai places in St. Louis then I really feel bad for you. Give me Thai food in Seattle any day. TERRIBLE service. There were only five people in the restaurant, and when I walked in I waited for about seven minutes for the hostess to stop chatting on her cell phone and come and seat me. Barely edible food. After waiting for another ten minutes to order, and then nearly that again to receive the food, we (the boyfriend and I) were brought our Phad Thai and Pad Kee Mao. Clumpy with very little flavor. When we had finished eating, we waited and waited and waited for our check. No go. Finally, again after about ten minutes of waiting, I got up and went to the back room where the hostesses were again chatting and not helping customers. I asked for the check, then sat down. Several minutes later, she brought it. Keep looking, I hope you'll find some place better. The boyfriend, St. Louis born and raised, says that the King and I is the best, but since they were closed when we went to get our thai fix, I can't vouch. They get two stars instead of one because the food was edible and the decor was pretty cute.
Great Byob restaurant...grilled roman salad with fig reduction. And chicken parm so big it hangs off the plate. Yummy also open for lunch

Ok so the food here is good if you can ever figure out when the place is open. Unless you live nearby you would not drive far to eat here. Multiple times we have showed up to find out it's closed. The menu is declining. No more Pho and they have scratched off multiple menu items. Having said that. The food is very good and we have never had a complaint. Every time we came on a weekend it was closed Call ahead. They obviously have a good enough following to justify shorter daily and weekend hours.

Don't be thrown off from the outside (or the decor of the inside), this place is a Thai food Mecca. Came here first on the recommendation of my ol' buddy Brian R., who used to eat here multiple times a week. Great location to stop at for lunch or dinner if you are out at the zoo. I find myself craving their Tom Ka Kai soup at the most inopportune times. Really awesome comfort food. Never tried the buffet, I am kind of averse to them in general, and I like things extra spicy, so I've always ordered off the menu. I especially love the Disco Chicken - try it if you haven't. Very affordable and has stuff that satisfies the vegetarians, too!

Love love love it, Cheap prices, a whole heap of food piled on the plate. For greedy ppl like me that prefer a lot of food for a Little bit of money. Food was scrumptious I had the chicken with yellow rice veggies and plantains and it was just so delicious. Will be returning and bring fam and friends good customer service as well

I've tried Nooddi Thai a few times and had mixed experiences. The first time, I ordered Pad Se Ew with tofu (this is my feel good goto dish at every Thai place)- it was bland and the vegetables tasted old and chewy. The second experience was better; I ordered the Curry Noodle- the heat was well balanced and everything seemed fresh. My hopes of Nooddi being a better restaurant were dashed on the third and final try when I ordered the Kao Soy for lunch. The Chicken was rubbery and seriously tasted days old and the curry milk itself was too spicy when the menu states it's just a little spicy- and to be clear, I enjoy heat. The veggies that accompanied the dish looked like they had been sitting out since 6am. I ended up throwing away the entire entrée (I had ordered take-out). Most people that I had asked about Nooddi also have had mixed comments, but they are more often than not, they lean torwards negative. I'm a big proponent of Thai food so I'd really wish Nooddi was better... but if I had to use two words: Terribly inconsistent. I would not recommend Nooddi.
typical Chinese food - oil, oil and oil. Food portion is huge. Enough for at least two meals. A OK OK place to go.

Indian restaurants are somewhat scarce in the Indy-north 'burbs and Amber is the only one I know of in Carmel proper. Located in a small strip center at the northwest corner of Carmel Drive and Meridian Street, this unassuming Indian eatery combines efficient service with decent fare.....if a bit pricey. Then again, given the price of gas lately, a short drive to Amber more and more frequently trumps the longer drive to some of our more wallet-friendly Indian haunts in the city. The food does not disappoint and personal faves include the Nav Ratan Korma - a vegetable curry that is creamy and deeply satisfying - think Indian comfort food! Lamb Vindaloo is usually what my better half chooses here - so spicy he needs a refreshing Mango Lassi (yogurt and Mango puree -based drink) to vanquish the flames! One thing not to be missed, in my humble opinion, is the Kashmiri Naan bread. It's a bit sweet thanks to its nut, shredded coconut and dried cherry stuffing and boy does it ever pair well with the savory side of the menu! Also, be sure to try the Gulab Jamun (mini fried dough balls in cardamon-infused honey syrup) or Kheer (Indian rice pudding - I often get extra for breakfast the next day..LOL) for dessert. Amber is open seven days per week and offers a lunch buffet from 11:00-2:30 pm. Catering is also offered, though I've not tried that yet.

I love this restaurant. The prices don't bother me because Indian food is EXPENSIVE here, as everywhere else I've seen. I'm a huge fan of the tandoori grill (read: meatatarian), and I've tried everything on the menu that I'm willing to. I've never been disappointed; however, I don't go there for the buffet or seafood. I don't like sea food. The owner is always very kind whenever I come in. I've sat and ordered and ordered take out and have never been disappointed. The first time I ever ate here, the waitstaff explained to my father and myself that Indian tradition is to share all the dishes from the center of the table. I liked that he was willing to take some time to explain it to us "newbies." All in all, I've never been disappointed here. Only minus a star for the reason Kristine and Jeff listed. It can be uncomfortable in the restaurant, but I think that's because the place is small, so it can also feel a little cramped at times, especially if you come in during a dinner rush.

I normally go there at 12:40pm to skip the traffic . I was actually coming their twice every week. Only thing I don't like is the one incident - I ordered a falafel with rice bowl . The person at the counter forgot to put the falafel . When I order it I was in the line and they were out of falafel and someone had to make it in the fryer but unfortunately the guy in the counter just packed it without checking the order . Mistakes happen that is fine . I came back after 20 mins and told them ," I am missing falafel in my order." Instead of apologizing the guy looked at me in a very strange way as if I was lying . He opened the bowl and looked at it . He gave me the falafel straight away . No apologies nothing for wasting my time but giving me that attitude as if he has nothing to do with it . Btw the guy knows I am a regular in the store he has seen me every other day. Since the guy put lot of sauce over the rice it was so soggy had to throw it out . For this reason I am taking back my stars. I can't give you any stars for your rudeness. I don't think I am going their anymore . I do like the food but not their attitude.

Definitely a go-to for thai food in Edmonton.. anyone that has gone for dinner with me at some point will tell you i've taken them to this restaurant...and all of them love it! My family has been going there for years, my cousins and I (in our 20's) love it, as well as my grandparents and parents.. definitely a whole family favorite, there's something for everyone! We love the authentic thai atmosphere, the bowing man (very inviting) and the great food! My only complaint is that I go there way more often than I should... Recommend: tom yum soup (especially in the winter! it warms you to your core), spring rolls, and cashew chicken. for a drink I'd suggest the thai milky iced tea - so refreshing! check it out, and soon!

I came on Yelp to look up the address because I was in town and wanted to go to Wishbone for lunch. (Yes, I specifically want to go out of my way to eat there again.) I'll edit immediately if I find it is no longer as good, but I was so shocked to see all the bad reviews I'm now taking time out of my work day to rectify this injustice! I ate here a month ago and was superbly pleased with the service, quality of food, and hipstery, rustic-chic decor. I had a sampling of several different chicken strips and wings, as well as the pie with the little chocolate bubble thing on top... don't remember what it was but all of it was BANGIN'! They may not fry it on the spot, but service is fast. The chicken was fresh and juicy, and the breading was zesty and not drenched in grease. Incomparable to the dried-out, artery-clogging, guilt-inducing mess that is KFC! Don't know what some of the other reviewers are talking about... The girl at the counter was wonderful and was very patient to help me choose what I wanted (I wanted to try everything but that was obviously an impossibility). I went during an off hour and there were only two other people there, so I can't vouch for how service is when it gets busy or is invaded by hung-over Spring Flingers, but I had a very comfortable and delicious experience. Also love that they weigh everything so you can control your portions and price point. The only downside is that it's a bit pricey, especially as the sauces have to be bought separately. Don't get me wrong, they are so tasty I'm totally willing to pay a little extra, but they should make it just a bit cheaper or offer a deal if you buy x amount of chicken. So sad this place wasn't open when I was a student! You younguns have it good these days.

Dosa hut is just an amazing find. The most authentic south Indian food in the US. The owners concentrate basically on the food, which is amazingly tasty and worth your buck, but not too much on the ambience of the restaurant. Their new offerings include a dinner thaali, which includes a variety of delicacies including UNLIMITED dosas!!! We have really enjoyed this new addition to their menu. Do go and try out all their new combinations at their dinner thaali. Also try their kothu parotta, which is one of my favorites.

By far the worst Thai food I have ever had! The noodles were oily and tasted like burnt oil. There was no flavor to the Pad Kee Mao except the oil. Don't even get me started on the TERRIBLE service. Waited 20 minutes to have our order taken and then never seen the waitress again! Some cute little kid brought the food and check. I will not be back nor would I recommend this place to my enemy.

I've gotten food from this truck multiple times, always pleased. Most recently I got a meal but I could tell the collard greens were canned, I know this because my mother uses canned greens Please don't start getting skimpy, this is one of the few soul food spots in philly that all their food is actually tasty

Oh man, oh man, everything is seasoned perfectly! We had the vegetarian platter so that we could try lots of things at once. I can't even pick a favorite, we ate every last bite. The service is great, it smells fabulous (they burn incense), it's spicy but not too spicy. I'm already planning my return trip! The only downside for me, the huge T.V.'s. There is no need for them. Ethiopian food is about gathering with people you love and sharing tasty food and an experience...the t.v.'s take away from that atmosphere a bit.

In an area seemingly devoid of any type of ethnic food other than Mexican, Shere-E-Punjab is a breathe of fresh air. The restaurant is clean and modern, offering excellent dishes, drinks, and apps. A+ naan selection. An overall wide selection of entres (meat, fish, and vegetarian!) and a friendly, professional staff make this place a favorite for my family.
surprisingly decent bun bo hue! not great, wouldn't make it in SJ but enough to get your fix.

Pho 36 is our favorite place in Indy for Bahn Mi (Vietnamese subs). They have their French bread made to their recipe by a local baker (I didn't think you could get good French bread in indy but they pull it off, it's like a good Parisian French loaf). They make all their own ingredients from the mayo to the pate to the pickled veg. We've tried all of the subs and our favorites are the pork and (wait for it) tofu. Really not a big tofu fan but it takes on the flavors of the sandwich and is a perfect vehicle for the sandwich. Their are other good bahn mi sandwiches in town but none are as good. K&T makes a great sandwich but their bread is delivered frozen from Chicago and it shows. It's very crumbly and the texture is not there. Pho 54 started making bahn mi but they use a Hispanic bakery and the bread is soft (not bad, but not French). Super Pho in westfield makes an excellent sub (4 star) but again not quite as good as Pho 36 (this is our 2nd favorite banh mi shop). Pho 36 also makes a good egg/pork pie, goi con roll and chicken salad. We like many of the other dishes but we go for the Bahn Mi. Hint: this is not far from the airport. We have more than once picked up sandwiches to take on the plane. They will put the wet ingredients in a plastic bag so your bread doesn't get soggy.
Very nice place to come with large groups. The staff and management are super friendly and free of attitude. The food is consistently good at very reasonable prices. The curries are always delicious.

Tonight I called into the store for some information and Brent answered the phone. I have a gluten & dairy allergy, so I'm not the easiest customer. Brent was not only helpful but extremely friendly. I couldn't have asked for better service and my noodle bowl turned out EXCELLENT!

The food has been OK the few times we have eaten here but the service is horrible and I will never be coming back. We asked for limes for our soupand they have us 1 lime. ONE lime cut into a fourth! Then we asked for a to-go box, they charged us 25 cents for the box and 50 cents for the aluminum foil. We've been regulars there had tipped them at the cashier. I wanted to ask them to take it out of the tip. And that little boy had way too much attitude. But the food was OK

I've been going here ever since I moved into the area. It's real easy to miss, but well worth the visit. The Gyro portions are ridiculous, and well prepared. The lamb and chicken are certainly well spiced, and for the price you pay, you'll feel like you made off like a bandit. Great food. Awesome price

We ordered paneer saag and kadhi pakoda with alu paratha . Parathas were really tasty , kadhi pakoda was ok and paneer saag was yum . Customer service is good but needs improvement . Ambience -7/10 Food Taste -8/10 Service -7/10 Value for money - 8/10
The food is good but sometimes I feel the work ethics sucks at this place and that makes me avoid this place.

We went last night with friends that we hadn't seen in a long time - it's good that we had much to catch up on, as the wait for everything, including drinks, was VERY LONG. The waiter kept apologizing, but the service the entire night was consistently slow - it took a good 20 minutes for our first drinks to show up. The staff was friendly, albeit a little odd. Our waiter kept apologizing for menu items as we ordered them. For example, I ordered the eggplant mezze and he informed me that this was the item people complain about most because they expect it to be piping hot. I ordered it anyway and was quite happy with it. He also warned us, in great and unceasing detail, about just how messy and bony the branzini is, and then described a patron from the night before and her escapades with it. He also apologized for the lobster ravioli when one of our friends ordered it, saying it was one of the heavier items on the menu. So it was, to say the least, a quirky experience. In terms of the food quality, it was fine. It wasn't amazing by any stretch, and at these menu prices I would have expected better. Much of the food we ate I could have made just as well at home (granted, I am something of an accomplished cook, but still). My short answer then is that for the cost of a meal here, there are so many much, much much better places in St. Louis. Not at all bad, except for the speed of service, but not great either. Oh a tip. If you do decide to go, make reservations (we did) and ask for a boothe (we didn't but we got lucky). The noise level is incredibly high there, and if we'd been sitting in the main areas we would not have been able to carry on a conversation. The booths are quiet and comfortable.
This place gave the best fresh brewed tea drinks. I tried the mango fruit tea and is amazing! I am totally addicted to this place

Stopped in for lunch - disappointed no lunch buffet. Buffet gear all lined up though. Ordered curry chicken. Meal had good flavor - not great - but chicken was large pieces of bone on dark meat. Constantly bit on bone while taking bite of what I thought was a piece of chicken. On the plus side, clean little place and friendly staff. I'd try again sometime but ask more questions first.

"People will wait for something that's good." That's the phrase I would use to describe my experience at Blueplate. I came here for breakfast this morning and was quite happy with my meal. I decided to keep it simple with an order of blueberry pancakes and a side of scrapple. Being early in the afternoon and ok a Sunday, the restaurant was packed to the brim. I imagine this was why the food took some time to arrive but my drink was kept filled while I waited and I was checked on regularly by the extremely friendly staff. When the food arrived, I was happy to find that it was well worth the time. While pancakes aren't the most difficult thing on the planet, you'll notice when one is executed poorly. Not only were the blueberries fresh and flavorful, but the pancakes themselves had a wonderful flavor as well. (Be warned these pancakes are large, so only go for three if you're particularly hungry) The scrapple was also done to my liking. Sliced thin and fried just long enough kept it crispy on the outside with a creamy interior. This was my first time eating at the Blueplate, but based on my experience it will surely not be the last. I look forward to coming back and trying more of what they have to offer and will surely recommend my friends give them a go.
They close at 8:30, got there at 8:15. Didn't get to even try the food. Was having drinks down the streets, took off a little early to make it before they close. Wham. Closed?
They indeed have something for everyone! I'm not a mac n cheese person like my kids. I ordered zucchini noodles with shrimp scampi. Holy crow it was AMAZING!!

We came to this restaurant after checking the reviews, The place is clean we didn't check the restroom and the waitress was nice and polite. The service was fast, I mean really fast. *Tea- Hot and nice *Fresh spring roll- flavor was ok. The lettuce was old. *Steam dumplings- no flavor, tasted like supermarket the mix and the wrapping was old and dry. *Chicken Satay- was bland no flavor, meat was moist the peanut sauce was terrible. *Sweet & Sour- we got the combination of meat chicken,shrimp and pork. there was no flavor, tasted like everything was boiled in a pot, came with a tiny portion of rice which was dry probably few days old. Overall the experience was extremely mediocre and for the price point of view I won't be recommending. This place definitely lacks freshness and flavor in this dishes.

It has been said that a bad day in New Orleans beats a good day anywhere else, and with only a few exceptions I agree. My advice to avoid a bad day in New Orleans? Eat at Marjie's. Problem solved. There's nothing bad on the menu. The staff is incredible, the soundtrack is always great, the drink I get is restorative (Rad Jam) and the place is funky cool. The place almost embodies New Orleans itself when you see the diversity o the patrons, the friendliness of the people and the quality (and creativity) of the food and the all important presence of music. Find a parking spot around the corner, watch out for driveways and prepare to be impressed. And go ahead and plan your next trip too.

One of the most beautiful markets I've been to. Many items to choose from including dry goods, fresh produce and halal meats. Very friendly staff took time to help me choose a customary tea. Fresh breads and sweets

We had dinner here last night. Based on some of the earlier reviews, it seems like they've gotten their act together and I'm glad we waited a few months before stopping in. We ordered the summer rolls, Pho Tai (steak) and Pho Ga (chicken). For me, the broth is the real taste test. iPho's broth had lots of flavor and was really good on its own. There was a good amount of meat in my Pho Tai and even more chicken in my bf's Pho Ga. The medium sized order was still a pretty big portion and definitely enough for dinner. Can't wait to go back!

Awesome food that is consistent across all the dishes. Being an adventuresome eater I always ask for a recommendation and it has always worked out. Last time I had a fried noodle with vegetables, chicken, beef and shrimp in a brown sauce. It is definitely a repeat meal. I always start with a summer role and it's hard to pay up the pho on a cold night.

It has been months since I've visited Zeppoli and I am still thinking about it; that's how good it was. Chris W and I went with some friends and I think we tried just about everything on the menu. 4 of us could have been fed simply on the antipasto. The plate was huge and had everything you could ever imagine on it: ricotta salata, marinated mozzarella, sundried tomatoes, marinated squash, tuna, proscuitto, stuffed mushrooms, asparagus.. I really could go on and on.. Everything was delicious. For my pasta dish I ordered the spinach gnocchi. I can honestly say I have never had gnocchi that were so light and fluffy. I ordered the small portion which was about 9 gnocchi and was just enough that I didn't feel stuffed. For my main dish I got the chicken. Also good, but definitely not the highlight. Dessert was also awesome. Zeppoles were delicious, interesting flavors of gelati, and yummy cannolis. I can't wait to go back!

I'd say it was mediocre at best. Lots of flies in the restaurant made it hard to concentrate on enjoying my meal. I ordered the Chicken Kabob, but they were out of the kabob?? Settled for the chicken breast and it was decent, but lacked spice. Would I go back? Probably not. Was it horrible, no, but it could have been better.
