What once was a Taco Bell turned Fox Film now turned Thia restaurant. This place is clean with a great wait staff. The food is excellent American Tai. Try the garlic beef or the yellow curry, you can't go wrong. They are often busy with minimal seating so large parties may want to call first. However they do have a pickup/drive thru so that's an option as well.
Fast,convenient , comfortable , and good. Sometimes you don't feel like dealing with going to Chinatown and Washington ave is too out of the way. The rest of the Vit places are bleh

My husband and I wanted to try the dinner buffet so we made the 30+ minute trip from the southside of Indianapolis -- it did not disappoint! My husband and I both had the dinner buffet but my husband also ordered appam. The food was average but we will go back again due to the service and variety of nonveg/veg menu options. We ordered two mango lassis to go and they were delicious. One thing I would note to people interested in trying this restaurant but are unfamiliar with Indian food -- the staff will explain the dishes in great detail and suggest items you may like based on the kind of food and spice you like. There was another patron sitting at the table next to us who was eating Indian food for the first time and she had many questions about what to order -- I watched the waitstaff and manager discuss the different menu options and make numerous suggestions.

I was impressed with my experience at Salsa! BUT I think the key to dining here is to realize this is NOT a Mexican restaurant. Also, despite the name, there are no actual "chips and salsa" offerings here, this is a Puerto Rican and LATIN restaurant, so we are talking rice, plantains, beans, meats, etc. Since Nashville has a very limited amount of Latin restaurants, come here looking for a new experience or just go with the perception that you are eating Latin food if you've had it before and you won't be disappointed! It's located within view of Mercy Lounge/The Cannery, and would be a perfect spot to get a drink before a show. It's located in an interesting building with a bit of an industrial feel, but I love the way the space is decorated and they also have outdoor seating. For dinner, we had the black bean hummus (AMAZING) and Empanadillas de Carne (Ground Meat Bite size Turnovers) with this heavenly sauce to dip them in....mmmm. Off to a great start! Then (based on the incredible looking Yelp pictures) we ordered the chicken stuffed with plantains, ground beef lasagna with sweet plantains, and sides of yuca and mofongo which is green plantains mashed. Every single thing we had was delicious, unique, and prepared well. The waitress was extremely helpful and explained all the dishes to us and answered our questions.We also had to order the Tres Leches for dessert and it did not disappoint! Food was outstanding all around. I enjoy the drinks and they are STRONG, but I must say I was slightly disappointed in the mojitos. Since rum is their primary liquor used here, I had hope for a mojito that would knock my socks off, and it fell a bit flat. However, I adore both the passion fruit and red sangria. Overall, I was very happy with my experience and can't wait to come back!

Thinking about coming here just do it! I ordered the chicken Kebob pita and it was perfect. Chicken was tender and the right amount of sauce and flavors had me eat the whole thing. I was not expecting fries but they came with it and seemed fresh cut and good seasoning. Last I ordered the hummus and it was good too. I'll be back!

Naf, Naf is Mediterranean food served in a Chipotle style atmosphere. The chicken shawarma is so good! Love their fresh pita bread and hummus bowl. It's a little pricey for what you get, but the food is so good.

If I can give zero stars I will. I'm from NYC so I was looking for a Jamaican restaurant to go to here in Philadelphia. Someone recommended here and after I read the reviews on yelp I decided to try it. BIG MISTAKE! The oxtails were beyond disgusting and the rice and peas did not taste good at all. If you're from NYC and you know how quality Caribbean food taste please do not go here.

The chicken 65 was good but the manchurian needed to some work. The indian food looked quite good but I didn't have any. I'm sure this place will get better with a month or two under their belt. The waitress was really nice and accommodating as I changed the lunch special deal. I need to give this place another try and get something other than the chicken manchurian. Maybe next time...
Dizzying selection of very authentic sandwiches that top out at $4, are made on fresh bread by extremely nice people. It's potentially the perfect eating establishment.

Caroline and Cheryl have the best Jamaican food I've had in a while. My friend's oXtail was tender and flavorful with subtle spices and cooked to perfection. My jerk pork was robust and spicy, served with great collard greens and rice and beans. Other sides were good too, plantains, cabbage and green beans. Will definitely return again when in philly, worth the trip out to West Oak Lane! And Cheryl and Caroline are, of course, the perfect hosts. Highly recommended!

I have been eating at this place for the last 20 years. Before Katrina they used to have their location on carrolton. That's where i began to enjoy their cooking. They serve their tabboulli so fresh, the hummus with lamb is so delicious with roasted pine nuts. The mint tea is so good, you see the mint leaves in it. Also, the veggie grape leaves are so yummy.I enjoy eating here so much. It is a little bit farther for me now, but it is worth it. Thanks Waffa and Musa for the awesome food you cook.

Visited Taziki's for the first time this Tuesday and was extremely satisfied! I was in a hurry, but found plenty of parking, the food was easy to order, and it arrived quickly. The special I ordered, the pork sandwich, was delicious. I particularly loved the sauce, which was sweeter than any other I've had before. My girlfriend had the Chicken Pesto Gyro. This had a phenomenal combo of flavors. We'll be back!

Simply amazing!! My kids and i went there a couple of days ago and was blown away by the level of customer service and the super delicious food! I am a BIG lover of thai food i eat it at least once a week, so i have been to almost all thai places around and i can say without hesitation , this one is in the top 3!! Even my 5yrs old boys loved it!! I had my usual pannang and shrimp rolls( HUGE!!!!) and kids split the lomein and the chicken satay . Every single dish was amazing!!!! I am making this place my new go to for thai!!!

The food is delicious and well presented. We had a party of 10 for dinner and the staff stayed on top of all our orders and requests. Ambiance is nice, easy access plenty of parking. Definitely worth the drive. We will be going again and soon!

I went to Scannicchio's on Saturday night with my family. It was good, solid italian food...not my absolute favorite BYO italian place in Philly, but it was good enough to make our trip worthwhile and I'm not opposed to going back. The appetizers were the best part -- the grilled romaine, sausage with figs, caesar salad -- they were all fantastic. We all ordered pasta as our main course. Although I'm not sure if the bread, pasta and sauces were home-made, the meals were solid. The staff were incredibly friendly and our waitress gave us free lemoncello after our meal.
Not my cup of tea, but my brother who is an avid Indian food lover, stated that he loved the lunch buffet and would enjoy coming back again.

My husband and I aren't into the fancy dining, but more into eating well. We saw the reviews for Zaika and decided to give it a shot. It is a small grocery store with tables set up for dining. We overlooked that and brought a small cooler with some beer and wine. I called over the phone to make sure we could and the guy said it was BYOB. So glad we tried this place! The food was delicious! I loved the rice that they served with the meals. We will definately be back.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Excellent Indian food. A must when in Boise. Great and friendly service. Loved the curry!! I loved how the owner came buy to greet us and asked​ if we need anything. Will be back next time we drive through.

I have been to Thailand three times and I have spent time in Chang Mai, Bangkok, and Phuket, and Nadia's in Lansdale has some of the best, most authentic Thai food I've had in the U.S. Often times, Thai food here is toned down for more sensitive American palates, but Nadia keeps it spicy enough. In addition, they have Massaman Curry (my favorite) on the menu, which is sometimes frustratingly difficult to find even in Thailand. Their lunch menu is great and you get soup, an appetizer, and an entree for about $8. An excellent deal for such great food. And their Thai Iced Tea is perfect.

It's always a good sign when you walk into a restaurant and it smells unbelievable. I asked the waitress what it was that I was smelling and she told me that it was their special of the day- mansaf. Obviously, I had to have it. It's the appeal of the "limited edition." Plus, there was that beautiful aroma. So I ordered the Mansaf as my entree but I started with the Fattoush. It's a salad of lettuce, cucumber, and tomato with pomegranate dressing but the best part is... fried pita chips! Before the apps arrived, the waitress brought out warm, chewy pita bread and a bowl of pickled veggies. I wasn't a fan of the veggies but the bread was divine. The salad was amaze-balls and it was a very hearty portion- could definitely be a meal in itself. There's lots to love in that salad, but the fried pita chips are still my favorite. Then the mansaf arrived- basmati rice topped with tender lamb and a bowl of yogurt sauce. The lamb melted off the bone and tasted great with the rice and sauce. I'm definitely going to return and try more off the menu!

One evening, I decided to try the banana tehina shake for dessert. Before ordering it, the cashier offered me a sample of the plain base. After trying that, I was hooked. The sesame flavor was subtle but delicious, and the consistency was thick like a milkshake should be! My only regret is that I didn't order the original flavor. I felt that the banana taste overpowered the sesame. Guess I'll have to come back and try it again sometime!

Salsa is a great place for a solid Puerto Rican meal. My family is Puerto Rican, and to be able to get traditional food in Nashville is a treat! They had a great selection of apps, and some pretty solid mufungo. It's definitely worth a trip!

Their banh mi is decent and they gave so much cha lua when I ordered. I just wish the bread was more fresh though but that was solvable by putting it in the toaster oven. In terms of their bubble teas.....well, I just got back from california so maybe my standards and expectations are higher than most. I ordered their passionfruit gt, taro mt, and I customized my last drink. The syrup drinks were bland (according to my brother). Their boba was slightly hard and bland. Plus I feel like they dont put that much compared to other boba places. Their taro mt was...decent i guess. I'll probably just go back for the food tbh.
This the best Chinese and chicken pattai you ever eat ,,very fast with service they also deliver and they know me by name I love that place this your friend Mohammed

I love the Vietnamese coffee, so fresh. Spring rolls are equally good and the fried rice is perfect. However, the place is a little dirty and poorly decorated. Also, the bathroom is in the back so as you're making your way through the kitchen you can see some poor hygeine habits. The outside seating is nice though.
Great buffet! I love Indian food, but am very rarely impressed by what I get at Indian restaurants. Everything was delicious. And the garlic Naan that they bring out to your table is irresistable!

Although the food was fine we found the attention to customer's comfort was totally missing. We were put in a corner with absolutely no room to move. We saw many other tables and when we asked to move we were told they were reserved. We had made a reservation as well and felt there was no accommodation for our request. Apparently they have their favored customers and we weren't one of them. We felt overlooked the entire night. When a loud party left towards the beginning of our meal, haven't been given our concerns, they could have rearranged the tables to make us more comfortable or asked if we wanted to move. No effort was made to do this. There was no gesture to offer us a complimentary dessert or coffee to appease our discomfort. It was a very unsophisticated waitstaff that didn't know how to properly handle the situation. I called the following day to voice my displeasure and no one have the courtesy of returning my call. Overall it was an unpleasant dining experience. I had picked out the restaurant to take our friends on their anniversary and was totally embarrassed by the treatment we received. Food is not everything. In today's competitive market you need to address all issues.

Food is pretty good and portions are quiet big. The price is not very high and the food is worth the money! For the money you spend you get good food! Servers are nice too! Recommend the beef pho for sure :)

My daughter and I loved this. I had the shrimp and calamari pho, and she had stew flank pho. We also had the pot stickers and they were amazing. We try to gave pho wherever we go and this was one if the best. But even better were the hospitable owners who gave us great attention snd service. We will be back!

My wife and I try to get to the buffet every other week. The food and pricing is great. That's worth 5 stars. What makes me wish I could add a 6th star is the Bollywood Music Video channel they run during lunch. I can watch that for hours.

Edwin, our server was terrific with several special requests from the kitchen and the bar. Food was fun to eat family style, so we ordered a wide variety. It was busy but all the servers were smiling and food was quick. The drinks from the bar were generous, too.

Beware of the owner when you get in. Rude and stubborn. Extremely poor in customer service. We came in at 9 pm with only few tables occupied, did not get the table we wanted. Very disappointed. And then they want the gratuity which is added automatically which is not at all deserved.

#900 Review. Rare Ethnic Food No.11 Small business with hard working people deserve to be recognized for their success. Not only for their home feel cooking but also for the very good rare items they have served. Before we were there, we check the people who posted the review. Many people who posted has less than 2 reviews. And only 9 were posted. No elite has posted until me and my wife visit. They have been open since last November and they have not catch attention of elite Yelper. Little Angel (Angelito) is bringing the love of food in our area. They are Puerto Rico and Latin cuisine. We have the pork shoulder with rice and the rotisserie chicken with mofongo. Both dish is excellent. The pork marinated very well the chicken is excellent. The mofongo is the best I have taste with garlic base. The rice dish have a choice of side. Since they run out of the sweet plantain, they give me a choice of their special made salad - ensalata guineo en escabeche. This salad I have never seen before. It is chicken gizzard with plantain. The sauce or the dressing is out of the chart. Other than their regular menu, they have hot deli food that are cook ready to serve only on weekend. They showcase the special salad I have mentioned above. The pig feet also in Friday only deli dish is excellent. The skin and meat fall off the bone. Service is excellent. Now the secret is out. Go enjoy it.

Great Greek/Mediterranean food! Go in, order, step to the left for your drink, then sit down. They'll put your food in the window when it's ready. I've had their hummus, pita (they also have wheat pita), lamb gyro, chicken plate, and falafel salad - all very good. The chicken is semi-shredded and a little dry but seasoned well. The falafels are huge and look like dinosaur eggs but they're good! Go early especially if you want to park in the same parking lot as the restaurant. They also have valet. Don't you dare park at the neighboring bank. Location - Good. Parking - Sucks. Service - Good. Food - Great. Pricing - Good.

I ordered Jerk Chicken with rice and beans with cole slaw. I must say best tasting and perfectly spiced Jerk Chicken I have ever had. Great spot to eat in or take out pretty quick. Very reasonable prices
Is it really that hard to get a order correct? Ordered the Tuscan Pasta with Parm Chicken. No Chicken. 2nd time I have ordered from this place. Both times they have screwed up the order. Done.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: I have been here several times and the food is genuinely good. Lunch buffet is what I am here mostly for. My family likes the kabaabs, biryani, goat ribs and double ka meetha from Baba's restaurant.
Order the chicken kabob, few pieces were under cooked. Got sick. Won't be ordering from here again.

This is such s great deal for this area. The food is fresh and hot and extremely tasty! It's brand new and has very little kinks if any. Staff are friendly and helpful with nice smiles. Which makes this even more of a joy to visit here. Great prices which makes this a great deal all around. Highly recommended !

This is our usual breakfast stop on our way to the shore. I love the creative offerings found on their menu. This morning I ordered the Mexican Bowl but I was served the Mexican Wrap. They took the wrong order back to make my correct dish. My husband finished his meal before mine came out. It was an honest mistake by the server; she explained that the two dishes are next to each other on her order pad and she pressed the wrong selection. Today, we had to ask for our server numerous times. She did not come to check on us during the entire meal. My husband had to ask another server going by for more coffee, and then more cream after the first request for coffee. Training for the servers and attentiveness to customers will go a long way in bringing us back again. We will give Blue Plate one more try.......

We like eating locally and wanted to try something different. We stopped by this place and ordered two of the dinner specials. Yelp had a 15% off deal but the meals were only $11 each so I didn't use it. The owner was pleasant and helpful and suggested a couple of items we'd like. There was a lot of healthful, tasty food for only $11. Why only 4 stars? When we got home, we realized the pita bread and hummus were missing. Grrrrrrrr!!!! And the guy had even mentioned how much we'd enjoy them, too! Yes, we'll return...but I'll check my order before I leave. Definitely recommended.

I went with my co-workers and everybody loved their food. I got Pad-Thai which was pretty much the best I ever had. Others got Drunken noodles and curry and they all were great. The service was friendly and location was good. I would recommend all my friends to come here
I'm a Chinese visitor in philly and I always had a big problem with my meals, I have to say the Biu's totally solved my eating problem, I just love everything on the menu!!!!!

Best butter chicken that I have had and I lived in DC and CO before Indy. This is one of our go-to takeout options as their spices deliver but they don't mask lackluster protein. They have quality food with superb preparation!!!

Had a DELICIOUS falafel wrap and pita with hummus. Lots of options on the menu. (Vegan options as well! :) They are adding even more soon! The service was kind, caring and prompt. I feel like they genuinely care about customers. Rare these days... Highly recommend!
Very disappointing. Bland food brought by inattentive staff. I left thinking "What a waste of money!".

Food was just ok. Maybe the fried rice could have used more soy sauce or something it was real pale looking. The mixed veggi in garlic sauce that I ordered was just ok. Definitely not one of the good Chinese restaurants

The line says it all. I've never been here at any point of the day and they don't have a line. And quite frankly, I will wait. The food is always good. Full of flavor. I have tried a couple of different food items from this eatery and have never had a bad experience. Today is no exception. Went with the fried fish, mac n cheese and cabbage. And I'm going to tear this food up. So if your in the area stop by and patronize.

I am not too well knowledgeable about Thai food, but their Chicken Pad Thai with Glass Noodles is unbelievable. It's not spicy, but has a peanut sauce that adds great flavor. One of my favorite dinners in STL, and a good deal for the serving given.

The food is excellent but the Asain ladies that work there do not know how to treat customers. I never give reviews but here it goes. So I ordered #50 pork w imperial rolls - excellent although, I asked for fried rice in stead of the noodles and she told me it would be $2 extra so I said "okay that's fine." But she clearly thinks everyone is as cheap as her so she just assumed I said no and I got noodles anyways.
Great cheap lunch. I got the combo - chicken & falafels with a free drink for $5. Cant beat that for lunch around this area. Everything is so flavorful and the salad is so fresh too.

We've been going to Dmitri's for almost a decade, and we've loved many of our visits and introduced it to many people, but after last night we've had enough of the jerky servers, their lackluster service, and the increasingly disappointing food. The service has always been a little cheeky, but in the past they were friendly and they did their jobs well, especially given the space and the way the tables are handled (servers plate a lot of the apps and desserts). But over the past few years the service has declined to being terse, distant, and careless. Last night we weren't asked how any of our dishes were (three were not good), and we ran out of water and bread, though the place was only about half full. We had a few problems with our plates, and the main reason we didn't say anything is that we didn't want to get into it with the server, who gave off a vibe somewhere between "please don't bother me" and "I dare you to try me". We've just had enough of it. Maybe it hasn't gotten worse, and we used to think of it like hip or whatever, and now we're too old to deal, but whatever has happened, fuck it, we don't want to deal anymore. The food has been getting worse over the past few years as well. This time, the spinach pie (which I think they microwave to serve) was barely warm, and holy dill, it had waaay too much dill. Dill for days. Dill for dogs. The grilled octopus, which was cooked perfectly (as usual), swam in a pool of flavorless, low-grade olive oil, with barely a hint of the red wine vinegar that typically makes the dish sing. And lastly, the branzino was lying in a pool of the same shitty, flavorless olive oil. We did our best to pick around it but it was a stupid thing to do to an otherwise excellent dish. The hummus was really good--as usual--but only hitting on 1 out of 4 dishes last night, after a couple of years of wobbly food and the bullshit service, means we're done with Dmitri's. They're not the only place selling octopus and branzino.
The real deal. Good jerk and patties. Closes I've found to JAMAICA. Yeh man. Respect

Driving thru King of Prussia at dinner time. Really in the mood for Indian food. Desi is very convenient to the King of Prussia mall. Parking is very easy as well as is access to the restaurant. Very nice and clean but dated. I ordered the lamb curry and my son ordered the chicken tikka masala and an order of plain naan. The food came piping hot and each order came with its own dish of rice. Usually you get one dish of rice per two guests. We had so much food that we were able to take half home. I've been to many Indian restaurants and have to say Desi is one of the best. The only reason I gave 4 stars rather then 5 there is because the restaurant has no pizazz. If they would modernize the restaurant and brighten it up they would get 5 stars from me. The waiter was very accommodating and made himself readily available if we needed anything. Just a real nice experience.

Great delicious food with good service. I have had alot of thai food and this place is up there. I have been here many times since i have moved. I would totally keep coming back. Pad thai is on point and their sushi is good as well.

Oh my gosh, guys. I drive past this place like, all the time, but finally got to go today with the family. Let me tell you it was DELISH. Like, beyond tasty. We were one of two parties in the place (which is really small) and we were taken care of quickly. The waiter was great. I ordered the salmon pocket, and I died. The sauces, the toppings, the CHIPS, everything was just great. Everyone at the table got something different, and we all cleaned our plates. The prices were reasonable, and I loved the atmosphere, especially the music! They do have cheesecake, but we didn't get any. If you haven't been here, go hop to your car and get to gettin'!

So happy I passed by here on my way home from work. This little, cozy place is clean, doesn't reek of indian food 5 blocks away and is extremely affordable. I especially appreciate the dietary restriction awareness campaign they have going on (aka labeled V, GF, LF etc). I really enjoyed my dinner and the staff was so friendly! Of course I'll go back.

We are definitely a fan of Zoës Kitchen. We enjoy all the plates we have had there and brough home family meals many times. Our two girls who are also picky at times always eat up the plates. My favorite is the steak roll ups and white beans. The beans though at times can be hit or miss depending on if they have been just made or sat around. For the price it's a nice alternative to the other good restautants in the Providence Town Center and we've yet to be disappointed.
Wow, awesome food. Portion size smaller than I would like, but very friendly staff, clean atmosphere and very nice small touches.

Ordered the Mongolian Beef, might as well call it Mongolian Fat. You get better quality of meat from a frozen dinner. The flavoring of the dish was great, but every time i ate a piece of meat it was mushy fat low grade meat. I tried this place because pei wei was closed, i wish pei wei didnt close at 9. Its also more expensive than pei wei.

Excellent mofongo, which is hard to find in Philadelphia (Mixto is my other favorite but they don't open until 4pm weekdays). Very friendly and attentive service. Prepared foods available cafe-style for takeout or can opt for seated waitress service. Cute interior with lots of wood and netting that works to give a kind of island feel.
I love eating here because of the wonderful service and excellent food. The sushi is very authentic and high quality! Just look at the pictures and judge for yourself.
good Italian restaurant with a nice view on the Delaware. Fresh seafood and fish available.

I stumbled upon Mojito's while walking home from bars on Frenchman street along on the Saturday night of my stay in New Orleans. It was exactly what I'd been looking for! Beautiful courtyard on a gorgeous spring night, friendly enthusiastic crowd, live music that felt like New Orleans (Frenchman Street was full of DJ's that night), and fun cocktails! I sat for about an hour and took it all in while drinking a Mr. Funk (which was delicious). This place has the perfect vibe for a nice warm night.
We had a wonderful experience. The food was incredibly flavorful and the service was amazing. It's a great new addition to the stl restaurant scene.
The fried rice and pho are really delicious. The people who work there are also nice.
Incredible sushi and perfect curry. Great atmosphere and staff. I'm going to come here often.
Loved our meal here. hIghly recommend the pasta and the veal parmasian. excellent.
We ordered take out and really liked it. They were very friendly. We both got vegetarian entrees. We'll go back!
Create your own salad, pita, or rice bowl. Choose from chicken, steak or grilled vegetables and more. Delicious, with generous portions. I give it a thumbs up!

The food was okay, but the manager was HORRIBLE. I went with a groupon and I got my money back and I will never return to this place. The food was decent until desert, which was bad- we got mango and sticky rice and the mango was not even close to ready to eat. It would not have ruined my dining experience but for the managers subsequent behavior. When we sent it back the manager came over and gave us an ultimatum on wasting her mango, which is insane, because it never should have been served. We had already paid and tipped 20% on the bill before the groupon and returned food, and without even looking to check what we had left the manager gave us an ultimatum on tipping. The food here is average- but definitely not worth giving business to this person. There are plenty of great Thai places in Philadelphia- you can skip this one.

This place ROCKS!! We had chicken & Steak kabobs with Persian rice. The yogurt cucumber salad was delicious. We dined after lunch about 3pm. Great service and they honor a Military discount! Please try this restaurant. You will not be di
the food was good but the silver wear was dirty and nasty. beside that pretty good tho.
It was bad... The fish was smelly and awe full..i dint like anything about it, be it food ambience or service..

We were in PA for a weekend and were craving Pakistani / Indian food. It wasn't much to look at from the outside, but we were so happy we found this hidden gem! We didn't sit in the restaurant, so I can't comment about the decor... but that's not what we were there for -- the taste and quality of the food is all we cared about. The food was amazing, truly delicious, and it totally hit the spot. If we're ever in the area again, we are going to make a point to stop in for more!
I hate the South of Market development. On many level But I found that this place, which has that South of Market air about it, is as good as the uptown location and is going to be a lunch favorite.

I picked up my take-out order thirty minutes ago and am now in a food coma. Every dish we ordered (paneer tika masala, lamb nehari, alu gobi, chana masala) was absolutely delicious. To those of you concerned about other reviews mentioning that the portions were small: we ordered these four dishes, rice, and naan for two people and ended up only eating 1/3 of it all for one glutinous meal. Unless you plan on hoovering everything up, I think you'll be okay. I ordered spicy, and over the phone the owner asked me if I was sure (understandable, I have the whitest white lady voice ever) and obliged when I said yet. If you order spicy and mean it, it will actually be spicy (but not deadly)! Very friendly service to boot. We'll be back!

I had the grilled pork banh mi which was fairly average: a buttery baguette with pork and pickled vegetables. Nice and spicy too. This was definitely a decent meal for 7-8 bucks, and it satisfied my long neglected banh mi craving. Since we spent a lot, spring rolls were thrown in but I think I would have been disappointed if I had paid for them. The place is just a counter in a convenience store but there are a few tables if you wish to linger. Note that the menu only has one listing for banh mi, so you may want to ask what types of bang mi they have if you aren't familiar with them.

This is my go-to Thai place. I've been coming here since it opened and have never been disappointed. The staff is always helpful and accommodating. The food is always hot and delicious. I'll be coming back as long as they're open. Thank you Basil Spice!

Food: A+++++++++++++ Would eat again. Service: C One server was really nice, the other, not so much. I've been subscribing lately to the idea that restaurants & their employees shouldn't make you feel uncomfortable. So...
Great place where to have coffee and relax. Awesome food and great and very friendly staff! I definitely recommend this cafe!!

Had a good experience from start to finish. Greeted and helped by the young lady behind the counter. Well laid out menu, spice levels clearly displayed, and the three choices of serving style are presented in photos. I would say the rice bowl is traditional, and the naanwich and naan pizza are new to me. Rather an inventive way to serve Indian food. We both had the rice bowls with tandoor chicken. One with tikka sauce (mild spice level) which had very good flavor. And one with vindaloo (highest spice level), which was well balanced with flavor and spice. I like it hot. When I asked how hot it was, I was promptly given a sample spoon taste (so to all reviewers who were sad with their choices and newbie or retuning customers, ask for one and get what you like!). The heat was good but I wanted a little more so as one of my toppings (which there are many), I asked for fresh hot peppers. I liked the choices of the toppings. I went with fresh cucumber, tomato, hot pepper, and cilantro. I eat Indian out at least once a week. I will definitely be coming back here.
Truly delicious food. Warm atmosphere. Genuinely friendly staff. Excellent gluten free options even fried dish with chickpea and buttermilk batter.

This is seriously some of the best Jamaican food in town!!! My husband and I go there at least once a week and we have never been disappointed!! My husband is Jamaican, (born and raised), and is often surprised by the entrées that he finds at this restaurant. The service is even great!! I recommend calling ahead because they are always really busy. In all, the food is amazing and the service is great. The portions are always more than enough!! I always have enough to save for a great lunch the next day. This place is truly a GEM in Trenton. I am so happy to have found it.

I actually created the page for this place because apparently no one's reviewed it and it certainly deserves a place in the yelp registry. However, I don't feel like writing it now. I will in a day or two. But for now, just go there. I highly recommend. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- STILL NO ONE HAS REVIEWED??!! Get on it yelp. Anyways my actually review. Real quick. Workers are super friendly and fairly fast. The woman was actually quite fetching if I do say so myself. But I digress. It's a food cart. No romantic setting. No candles. Tablecloth, not happening. BUT, the one item I got here was pretty freakin fabulous. The whole concept as best I can tell is like a Asian/Mexican fusion food truck. I got the chicken katsu sandwich. Brilliant. It's served on a great Vietnamese type long roll. The chicken is crusted and cooked in cap'n crunch cereal. It adds amazing texture and a fabulous sweetness to it. The whole thing is slathered with a nice Asian slaw with hints of cilantro. Then I believe there was a really nice spicy mayo type sauce to finish it. Simple and superb. I could definitely think of a couple more ingredients to add to give the sandwich some more dimension, but really it would kinda be like looking at the Mona Lisa with 3D glasses on. These folks are the real deal. I will be returning.

Ate here on Sunday after finding out our original destination was closed. The language barrier was a point of frustration. I see why they have all the menu items numbered, that way all you have to do it say a number or point. It took way too long to convey to the waitress that all I wanted for my son was white rice with a few shrimp. I know it adds to the authenticity of the restaurant but come on, when it hampers the ordering process it becomes a nuisance. That being said, the food was pretty good. I am usually hesitant to order something on the spicy side at Thai restaurants as they seem to vary so I went cautious and ordered my Pad Basil with Chicken at a 3 on a scale of 1 to 5. The dish was very tasty, and while it was a bit spicy, it did not have my mouth on fire which is always a good thing. I think I could have easily gotten my dish a 4 out of 5 and been just fine with it. I still don't know if I got the lunch portion or the regular portion (refer back to the language barrier), either way it was fairly small. I'm hoping it was the lunch portion because if there is a smaller lunch portion I don't know who that would feed. One thing that struck me as unique was that when I ordered a Diet Coke, they brought me out a can of Diet Coke and not a fountain drink. That was something I had not seen in a restaurant in a very long time. Basil Spice did not stand out of the crowd on South Grand which is not necessarily a bad thing, but in this instance it didn't do them any favors either.

Although a hole in the wall, their pho is pretty good. Their location is sketchy and parking is desirable, but the food is good. It seems one woman runs the joint which makes it seem challenging at lunch time. I've been more than 1/2 a dozen times and the service is still the same. If she had the courage to hire someone else, this place could have the ability to be a well oiled machine.
I've wandered into here quite a few times now. The drinks are good (and cheap). You can't beat the citywide special! Give Will a holler, he'll take care of you!

Good hearty pho and witty build-your-own noodle bowl. My fav is definitely building my own egg noodle + chicken broth + beef and fish meat balls. Good comfort food and very reasonable priced restaurant.

My partner and I stumbled upon this place after visiting an adjacent business and while we were viewing the menu on the outside window, a customer walked into the door and recommended this restaurant to us. Despite having my 17-month old kidlet in tow on a Friday night, we went in! The decor is beautiful - striking dark wood with ornate gold carvings on the walls. The servers wear traditional Thai dress and there are beautiful painted porcelain pheasant salt/pepper shakers on the tables. The server was very gracious in providing a high chair, because by looking at the decor, I wasn't sure if kidlet would be welcome on a Friday night! They provided a separate little plate of boiled tofu and rice for her even though it was not on the menu. I had the spicy tofu and my partner had the chef's special of crispy duck. We also ordered the spring roll appetizer. The presentation of the dishes were beautiful, with a carved carrot and a flower on each plate. We also received a complimentary order of the curry puffs for the "early bird special" as well as a soup (vegetarian for me, chicken for my partner). Our entrees were delicious as well! My partner's duck was crispy and moist with a subtle ginger sauce and the vegetables in my spicy tofu were tender-crisp and NOT overcooked at all! I would recommend that if you like your Thai food spicy that you ask for something beyond their idea of hot. I got mine spicy but I thought it was mild-medium. I could have ramped it up much more before I was sniffling or sweating! Prices are reasonable, with all the food we ate (including soda and kidlet's tofu), we still made it out for under $40 (before tip). If you're looking for a place near the Brandon mall that serves great food in a beautiful ambient setting for a reasonable price, look no further than Ploy Thai!
Very good experience. The food was very good. Kelly our waitress was very nice and friendly. I recommend the lobster bisque, really good!

i'm not in the habit of giving poor reviews unless it's to bash some douchebag spot, in which case i'm only all too eager. however, based upon my one visit to dmitri's last night, i'd have to say that i'm not sure i went to the same restaurant as all these other people. too add insult to injury, my original plan was to go back to pif night at ansill which is pretty much as sure a thing as there is in this town. i figured seafood would be a little bit lighter after the weeks gorging and i love greek food so i thought i'd try dmitri's (i had one good meal and one laughably bad meal of crap rotisserie chicken at estia where my dad and i got the pre theater dinner before going to the kimmel center) got the grilled octopus which was chopped into slices and precooked before getting a hit of the grill. the octopus was not fresh and this dish tasted like charred rubber bands with olive oil and lemon. a few years ago i spent three weeks in athens and paros with greek friends and we'd eat grilled octopus and salad every day. now i'm not so stupid to think i'd be getting anything like that, but this dish was such a bummer. (to counterpoint: the stuffed squid dish at estia was really delicious). almost got the pasta with blue fish. my question: what is "bluefish"? answer: "its more of a fish eaters fish" what the hell does that mean? instead, i got the cioppino. which essentially tasted like some clams, mussels, shrimp, and a hunk of cod overcooked in a pot of boiling water with a handful of chopped tomatos, bell peppers and onions thrown in. dreadfully overcooked not fresh seafood with nearly no flavor. what a bummer. another counterpoint: the cioppino at mercado (for only 4 dollars more) is delicious although you might ask for the capers and olives on the side as it can get pretty salty. also, i'm not interested in getting people in trouble but the service left a little to be desired and i had to ask for my 2/3rds full bottle of wine to be returned after it had already been stashed in the back. there were a few other things but i'll just keep it to the food. sigh.... i could have eaten at ansill.... :( and little fish was just down the street too.... :(

If you looking for a casual middle eastern restaurant, Petra is the one for you. Great variety of middle eastern meals, from tabooli salad to baba ghanouj, they have it all, plus they have the plat de jour, and it varies from lamb with rice to vegetable and lamb stew. I usually order their daily plate, it require no wait and it is always good.

This is my favorite Vietnamese place in Reno. All the food is great, as well as the service. Try a Vietnamese Sub Sandwich along with any of their Pho soups. Be sure to throw some Hoisin sauce on it and some Siracha... tastes great.

This is a gem of a family run business. Real kind human-to-human interaction - the kind of place you feel good about supporting. I only ever order the roti, because I love it. Shrimp for me, chicken for my guy. We were so excited to find this place in the neighborhood, and will definitely be visiting regularly.

I don't get what the hype is about. I went after the lunch rush so only waited for five minutes, but would not give up my lunch hour to wait for this. I ordered the chicken satay tacos and they were terribly underwhelming. The chicken was fairly bland and dry compared to the satay chicken I've had in restaurants, and the toppings (cabbage, avocado and what looks like an aioli) do nothing to enhance a meh flavor profile. Sriracha helps but not enough to make it a winner, and since it's an add-on I think it should be delicious even without. The whole dish needs more acid and seasoning - ginger, lime, pineapple, tomato - something! Grilling the chicken wouldn't hurt, either. I may go one more time to try the short rib tacos, but it won't be a priority. Two stars for the service, which was very kind, polite, and quick. I know that food trucks are about proximity more than anything, but Tacos Don Memo or Honest Tom's are far superior cheap University City taco experiences. Perhaps it's just that I no longer have undergraduate taste buds...

Came here to recover after Deltopia. The service and food were on point, even though this place gets a bad rep as people claim that it isn't authentic Vietnamese food, I would have to disagree (seeing that the cook was Vietnamese.) Living in IV means rarely being able to find authentic Asian food so if the drive to Noodle City is too far, try out Pho Bistro!

The aesthetics, food and service were nice; however the portions that were served were not commiserate with a fair price point in my opinion. There are way better places to eat in Santa Barbara, so in that regard, this place earns it's 2 star review by being cheapskates with its customers.

Great place to eat in Mount Juliet. The food is always good. The general Tso's is my favorite thing to eat on the menu. You can usually get in and eat without a wait unless it is Friday night. It is pretty similar to PF Changs but not as nice or as pricey.

The food was fresh, I'll give them that, but it was way too expensive for a truck...we could have dined out well for that price. We were told it would be a 30 minute wait and had to wander around just waiting for the food. There is no phone number or menu online to call ahead....30 minutes is way too long to wait. And finally, there was barely any chicken in the red curry dish we had and the Nam Sod was about 3/4 of a cup worth after you took out the ridiculous number of big red onion slices clearly used as filler. No one wants that many raw red onions. Not going there again. Very disappointing after all the good reviews I've read.

It's not every day that I can say a restaurant is truly fantastic. But this is one of those restaurants. It is absolutely beautiful inside and outside (patio) as well. The outdoor patio is a beautiful oasis. Although we did not eat at the outside patio since they do not serve dinner, only drinks and snacks, we did check it out and will be back for drinks in the future. We ordered several appetizers and a delicious lamb main dish. Somehow we were able to have room for the lemon curd based dessert. The food and the service were outstanding. The food seem to be very middle eastern inspired although the restaurant only occasionally played Middle Eastern music and the decor was not middle eastern themed. The restaurant does have an parking right next-door to it. It doesn't look like it's paved or have any lines in it so I'm not sure how many cars it actually fits. It was hard to tell which part of the parking lot was theirs and which was the neighboring buildings. Street parking is available but again unless you know the neighborhood you may be circling around and it may be more trouble than it's worth. We parked at the lot at 1320 N. Front St. for $20 (weekend rate)... well worth it.

Kabobs! We just moved to Philly, and spent our first week trying out various cheap eats, that will potentially become our regular go-to restaurants. There weren't many patrons when we arrived at Sansom Kabob House that night. We ordered two appetizers (eggplant and sambosas), chicken kabobs, and beef kabobs. Everything was fairly tasty...both the chicken kabobs and the beef kubideh were good and moist, and game with some charred onions and tomatoes and such. A few drawbacks: 1) the appetizers are TINY. like seriously tiny. definitely not worth the money. 2) the samosas were sort of small and flat--they were shaped more like Chinese dumplings. These tasted like they were microwaved...which was a little off-putting, especially since it messed with the texture of the "skin." The filling was good, though. All in all, food is good--but don't bother with the appetizers, they're not good value. Stick with entrees--fairly good value (in my DC-colored opinion), decent food...a good standby option to have

Semi-disappointed in this place because I've been wanting to try it for a long time now. There seems to be a mix review of Basil Spice on yelp, either people hate it or love it. Well, I'm going settle that score and rate it mediocre at best. The restaurant is dingy, dungeon-like almost. The decor is strictly Thai but I feel like they just threw a bunch of Thai stuff around and hoped for the best. This place has a tired feel to it... In addition, service took long. Our server took forever to get our checks paid even though there was only two other tables in the joint. The elderly gentleman (probably one of the owners) ended up grabbing our checks for us. On to the food....I got the "Pad Khee Mao" which I didn't enjoy. I thought it was bland. My bf got the "Pad Basil" which was I tasted and thought it was okay. I'll recommend going to the King and I down the street if you are craving thai food.

Composite of 3 visits. 2 on weekends, one on a weekday. First two visits would be a four star. Interesting concept, to me of 'fast' Indian food. I got a thali or waited a few minutes (5-10) for a King dosa that was well worth it. Pakoras a bit on the oily side but other than that, got a nice a la carte lunch option with good portion sizes good taste. Ambience is fine, management - if you meet them - are friendly and helpful. And on the third visit today the lack of process came a tumblin' down. We were the early birds. Got two king dosas. Then a crowd came and the noob at the counter got flustered. Customers started piling up. My kid decided he wanted dessert (rice pudding). Got in line. Got passed over when it was his turn. The adults behind him (shame on you adults btw) jumped in and took his turn.... So i step in and call the counter noob on it, and he blithers. After a few seconds, he fled to get management, who promptly informed me that they don't have the dessert available today. There's a place called Metro Dhaba / Il Forno in Gaithersbirg MD, that has similar good food but bad service processes. I wish my countrymen could get over this weakness. So - pray that this place finds their feet - I think they are worth keeping but they need work. Or go there in off peak hours when you are not in a hurry.

Food is average or below, nothing special at all. I will say that the servers behind the counter were very cheerful and were trying very hard. But the food just wasn't very good. The salted caramel baklava was very stale and just horrible. I'm very sorry to give a bad review, but unfortunately this place didn't earn anything better.

I've had my fair share of Greek food, both in StL & DFW....Soco ranks up there with some of my favorite spots. They're reasonably priced, the food is fresh, the service is good...there seriously hasn't been a misstep anywhere along the way since I've started visiting them in March. The gyro's good, but I've started going out of my way to grab the chicken gyro....chicken breast, lettuce/onions/tomato, tzatziki (sp?), and feta...all well balance, and in a more than generous portion. Add in some pasta salad, whether it's the rotini or tortellini (served cold w/ oil & vinegar dressing and feta), and you'll be full for the rest of the day.

Mi Caribe is new and located on Lindell inside the Del Coronado (down stairs - so don't try to enter at the Residences door). This is not Mexican or Tex-Mex - this is what I would call inspired by Dominican Republic ("DR") fare. The food from DR is a blend of Taínos (indigenous people of DR), African and Spanish cuisine that is affectionately known as comida criolla. Comida criolla focuses on proteins like pork, beef, chicken and even goat yet there are appetizers, soups and entrées that are meat free as well. There is ample space and great sunlight. On my first visit I started with veggie & chicken empanadas. There are typically two types of dough used in the Caribbean when making empanadas, yucca and flour. Here it tastes like they went the latter yet this dough was very thick and not seasoned (it needed salt/pepper). The veggie empanada filling seemed to need seasoning as well; the chicken empanada filling on the other hand was seasoned great! For my entrée I went with arroz con pollo w/ maduro (sweet plantains) - give this dish a try! The rice & chicken were seasoned impeccably & bursting with favor. It was so good, I was sad when I began to feel full. It even came with a side of slaw; I don't normally like slaw but it was bright & tasty. On my next visit, I called in for a vegetarian soup. I cannot recall the name as it isn't on the menu but it was delicious and I've never had anything like it (even though I've spent time in DR). It was a butternut squash base with apple, plantains and curry seasoning. There was some kick but it came across more peppery. Randoms: A major staple in DR is La Bandera and I was surprised not to see it on the menu but they do have another staple called Mofongo. I haven't had a rum based drink yet but my Margarita was solid - not frozen but good all the same. The service was attentive and just enough. Since I don't eat many of the above-mentioned proteins, I would give the food a 3.5 and the service a solid 4. I know this place will be a hit when the Universities are back in and with the uptick of fall traffic. You could easily catch a show and walk down here for some unique eats.

This had been one of my go-to Korean restaurants in St. Louis four years ago. The service and food had been solid, with the barbecued beef (kalbi) being especially good. No more. It has since been displaced by Seoul Garden in St. Ann, which is far, far better in terms of service and food. Over the past couple years, Korea House (formerly known as "Hangook Kwan") has plummeted. The service became rude and inconsistent. The waitresses were bad-mouthing other customers and even made snide remarks about our table while speaking Korean (big problem when one of the folks at our table understands Korean perfectly). Another time we were told that the tabletop grilling was not available due to insufficient staffing... this as two or three waitresses were standing around a largely empty dining area! Nailing the coffin was the growing mediocrity of the dishes overall, even though the barbecued beef (when one could get it) remained decent. Despite the change in management, we were dismayed to learn that the restaurant was simply handed off to the former owner's son, which means the rotten apple has not strayed far from the tree. Avoid this place at all costs!

We ordered from postmaste and found a bug in our pad thai, it's absolutely disgusting and nauseating. We didn't take the chance and threw out everything else we ordered. I can't imagine how the kitchen is kept but after calling the only response I got from the restaurant was "oh we keep our windows open we need to be more careful". It's absolutely sickening

I came here with my friends to try the light bulb bubble tea. We were waiting for our drinks for about 15 mins, when we finally got our drinks it was luke warm, and the tapioca was over cooked.. Would not recommend going here for bubble tea.

Bring cash, an empty stomach, and the patience to wait about 20-30 minutes during "lunch time" hours. After a trip to New York, my cousin decided to take me here. It was the first lunch truck I had been to in years (I moved to a more suburb-y area) and it was definitely the perfect one to start off with. I ordered the $5 Red Curry bowl and an order of Fish Tacos (came with 2) for $3. The red curry bowl was extremely delicious and the rice was so soft and fluffy. However, it could do with some type of meat in it to balance out the amount of vegetables. The fish tacos were superb. We also ordered Strawberry milk tea, which was way too sweet :( But good try! And a Thai tea, which was excellent like always. The people in the truck are extremely busy and overwhelmed but they still manage to smile and not over-rush you.

I have visited this place with friends and co-workers after work many times now. With BYOB we create our own happy hour with kabobs and tandoori chicken for finger food. Good atmosphere, friendly staff and amazing appetizers and entrees with finger licking taste. You've gotta try that Shrimp Pepper Fry. I have been here several time during lunch buffet and dinner time as well with family and love the selection. We may have tried just about everything on their menu that involves meat, and some veggie items as well, Tamarind Eggplant anyone? If you are a tandoori lover definitely try the Lamb Chops. And owner if you are reading this please bring back Sham Savera. My only complaint is I work closer to city and its a drive from there else there would be many more happy hours ;o)
The food was ok. Service was horrible and unwelcome!!! Better to keep money for other places. Never again!!!

First timer with two of my friends. perfect foods and fit the bill too. We had chicken satay for appetizer (a must have), coconut rice with beef rendang, pork dumpling noodles, and a curry tofu noodles. They all tasted so good but I liked my dish the most (the coconut rice and beef dish), so much so that I even order one to go for the boyfriend.

I've been here several times and the food never fails to impress! I love. love. love the tom kha gai. Seriously its addictive. The spring rolls are always fresh and delicious as well. I haven't ventured too far from the pad thai so i can't offer any thoughts on the other dishes. Everyone has always been friendly and I have great service every time we eat here. I've also picked up take-out a few times and everything is always packaged nicely with all of the condiments. In a few words - I'm a fan.

This is one of my go-to restaurants. I've tried several ramen restaurants in Reno and this is definitely the best. The broth in the pork ramen is fantastic. The pork belly buns are also wonderful. I've brought many friends here and they have all enjoyed it. Don't miss Elgin, the bartender's, Lycheetinis - a wonderful complement to the food.
Great place! Great service, great food! Whatever type of Asian food you prefer they have it, a must try is KFC Korean fried chicken!

I have given this high marks in the past, but now I won't be back. The food is still good but the service we received 2 days ago was terrible. We were virtually ignored for most of our stay. Taking into account a previous incident here when picking up take out, I have to speculate that when there are only women in your party they don't value you as customers.

I was excited to see a French bakery in between downtown and Chinatown. They had a variety of cookies, cakes, croissants, and of course macarons. I got two almond croissants, two almond pain au chocolate and one pistachio diamond and one vanilla orange diamond. I was sorely disappointed once I took a bite of my croissant. It was chewy and overly sweet, not at all flakey or buttery like a croissant should be. The pain au chocolate was a similar disappointment. The pistachio diamond did not have any pistachio taste at all. The vanilla orange was slightly better as it had actual orange rind which gave it a fragrant citric flavor. The prices were similar to duchess, and Id much rather wait in line for a melt in my mouth flaky croissant, than return here.

For the uninitiated, BAMBU specializes in Vietnamese desserts called Ché, a traditional Vietnamese sweet beverage, dessert soup or pudding. BAMBU serves a dozen varieties of Chè each of which is made with coconut milk or coconut water and one or more of the following ingredients - mung beans, black-eyed peas,tapioca, jelly (clear or grass) etc. Since I love to experience different cuisines, I decided to give this place a try. I got myself Ché made with Coconut milk, Taro and Pandan jelly. The guys at the counter were very friendly and patient enough to give me a detailed overview of their menu. The Ché was pretty good but the Vietnamese coffee was a let down. I've had better Vietnamese coffee at other restaurants. It was a little too sweet for my liking. However if you are like me, I do recommend their Ché. Pick one that's most appealing to you. I'd love to know what you think.

Tried this place for the first and last time. Coming from Seattle and Portland I am well aware of good Middle Eastern food and have had the best you can get in the Northwest. Anyway, I spent a good amount of time talking to the owner and telling him what I wanted. He told me the meal came with rice, pita, hummus and kabob. So, I very specifically told him I wanted rice and kabob and a side of pita. Maybe, his English is mediocre, but he seemed like he understood me. Anyhow, I waited around 20-30 minutes for my food, despite being the only customer in the establishment. Then, he finally brings out the kabob and bread, with a few sides. I then proceeded to ask him where my rice was after very specifically telling him that I ordered rice. He then gets mad and tell me that I did not want rice and started calling me a liar, basically. SInce I was hungry, knew the guy would only get mad at me for admitting his mistake and just wanted to eat, I told him I would take the food. He did not bother accommodating me with rice and basically told me it was my fault. Great customer service! To make matters worse the bread was stale, overcooked and just plain awful tasting. The kabob was alright, nothing amazing and a little on the tougher side, but edible. The hummus was ok, but really had too much garbanzo and a little lacking in tahini for my tastes and of course you don't get a whole lot of it. Sadly, the whole experienced sucked. I hope the owner is happy about losing another future customer and earning a bad yelp review over giving me .50 worth of rice. I generally want to support small businesses and been desperately searching for good Middle Eastern cuisine in Idaho, which seems to be a losing fight. Despite the service being crappy, I will probably go to the Goodness Land for now on for my Middle Eastern fix while I am stuck in Boise. I will also continue going to Ahmed (Tito) the downtown street shawarma vendor who, in my opinion, is the best Middle Eastern chef in Boise, if not the Northwest. The sad part about Ahmed's food cart is it is expensive, since it is a food cart and mostly for late night bar crowd people. It's a shame, as I wish this guy would start a restaurant here. As with most other Middle Eastern and ethnic restaurants in Boise, the prices of Al Sham are very high and portions are mediocre to what you would get in Portland and Seattle. To make matters worse he serves utterly stale and crappy bread.. The kabobs he doesn't bother giving you any sauces or anything either. I'm sure he would be happy to charge you though, even though he already charges $15 for very mediocre food.

One of the best pho places I've ever tasted. The noodles are the perfect consistency, the beef broth is to die for, and the brisket is tender and flavorful - all in all, it tastes like a little bit of home.
My boyfriend and I use to go to Pho An Hoa all of the time! Pho is not the best, but definitely much better than other Viet restaurants' in Tampa. Rice platters are pretty good, too.

Well well well ! This was my first experience with Indonesian cuisine and wow what a pleasant one!! The food at Sky Cafe was majestic !! I started out with a fried chicken platter. The chicken was perfect ! Then I had a bowl of chicken soup and it was outta this world!!! The broth was so damn good!! It was perfect!!! I also got a spicy fish platter to go. Good homemade eats at a bargain!!!
Love this place...the food is great the staff is even better can't go wrong with anything in the menu

My friends and I have had lunch at Paninoteca a couple of weeks ago. We really enjoyed our lunch. First we have ordered some hummus and it was very very good. We couldn't stop eating it and we had to get some more pita. I had ordered some lamb sandwich or wrap - it was very very good. Highly recommend it.
Very nice selection of dishes. Flavors were great too. The ambiance of the restaurant was good. It's nicely remodeled and spacious. I would come back again.
Love this place. Been eating here once or twice a week since it opened. Tofu + Korma = excellent meat-free meal.

I was surprised to find this place in a strip mall, but the inside is actually quite nice. Come to think of it, this place is one of the nicer looking Viet restaurants I've ever been to. Foodwise, I enjoyed the Bun Thit Nuong. Portions were city sized (on the smaller side), sauce was decent, and the noodles were tasty.

Negative experience. I walked into Angelitos to have lunch. I stood at the front for a couple minutes, no one said a word to me. I picked up a menu off the front counter and looked at it for a few minutes, still no one greeted me. I really wanted to eat at Angelito's. Unfortunately, a complete lack of customer service caused me to eventually walk out the door and go to one of the many other restaurants in the same plaza. I eat lunch out 5 days a week. I work with just under 200 people very close by. I called to speak with the owner after I left the restaurant. He told me that 'I could have just sat down like everyone else'! I was APPALLED! Obviously, as we all know, it is customary to be greeted and then seated. As I said, absolutely zero customer service at Angelito's.
YUM! Had a greek salad and chicken kabob, my friend had the beef and lamb gyro. You can't go wrong with any of those. Best Mediterranean food yet! Must try the Baba Ghanouj!

Finally, a restaurant with authentic Vietnamese taste, the pho broth is excellent, not watered down like some other restaurants in town. So far I've ordered the P1, S1, B1 and they're all great! I can't wait to try the other items on the menu.

The food was good. They made it fresh to order. I got the grilled chicken plate with rice and salad. It was overpriced for the amount of food you received, but tasty. An okay environment for a casual dining experience.

For all the people that gave this place 5 stars, you're Phoking right! Best Vietnamese in Indy area. I like the Pho with rare beef and meatballs. Don't forget to add the Huy Fong special sauce (if you love it, you know what I mean) and every single Pho fixin. The spring rolls are also quite yummy.

I couldn't be more happy that this gem at the top of Frenchman street has finally found it's mojo. The gorgeous courtyard now has live music nightly with an unpretentious atmosphere unlike most of the courtyard places in the FQ. A perfect place to sit and chill out with a cocktail. The menu is just as inviting and tasty. The shrimp ya ya and the breakfast ya ya are two of my favorites. The duck is also perfect and served with a side of mashed sweet potatoes and corn maque choux, my belly couldn't have been happier. (yes I like this place so much I've now eaten there several times). The prices are well within reason as most other places at this price point will give you a nice large helping of the same old tired fried food, that frankly I think as locals we have all grown more than tired of. I'll be back to this place many more times and recommend it to my friends as well.

Wild jungle princess. That's your first thing to know here. The food is great, the ambiance is very cool. It's comforting and not overdone like some of the south pacific restaurants you see. Thai chillies bring to life hints in each meal. The vegetables and rice are done fresh and you never taken a bite wondering "What can was this taken from?" For what you get, the prices are very reasonable. It's a little restaurant hidden in a strip mall, but it stands alone in blue bell.

Finally I got to go to this little place, I was looking forward to it. I will say first and foremost the staff are incredibely awesome :) The food was tasty and I loved the lunch specials! However I thought it would be spicy and it was not at all. I had to order some hot sauce (red sauce, sriracha), as it was not even a tad bit spicy. I will say, it was quick and tasty and a cozy atmosphere.....I shall be back :)

I had the opportunity to taste the food at an event catered by Sister Muhammad's Kitchen, and while all the food was great, I fell in love with the greens. They were fresh, deliciously seasoned, very tender and somehow still vibrantly green. I live in New Jersey an I plan to make a trip back to Philly for those greens.

Best Indian food in St Louis! One of the very few places that reminds me of India!! Authentic taste. Just too delicious. Decent variety on the menu. Very friendly owners. Small place - good for take aways. Not too pricy, totally worth the money. Fabulous kheer, cholay, halwa puri, paneer tikka masala.

I went to this place expecting to get hummus and a gyro. The hummus was below average, bland, and overall boring. I told the waitress I wanted a gyro and there was not one on the menu and she recommended something "just like" a gyro. The "lamb" meat, and I do hope it was lamb, was chewy and reminded me of something you would get from the flea market food court 10 minutes after they already closed for the night. I cannot say for sure but I got sick that night (vomit and diarrhea) and was not well for two days. I can't "prove" this cafe's horrible meal caused my even more horrendous stomach issues but deep down I am pretty sure. Oh yea, the server's use of the english language was very humorous, but funny as it was, did not add any value to my dining experience. Dine at your own risk!!

The absolute best hands down! I never knew about this spot until friends were on Facebook comparing Caribbean spots in Philadelphia. So I had to try Ron's! I was NOT disappointed at all. The fish is everything! Seasoned and tastes great! The cabbage and rice/peas were yummy as well. The ox-tail gravy was yummy!! I loved everything down to my ginger and pineapple Tropical Rhythm.
Don't order here. Unprofessional delivery service. Order all wrong. Food ice cold.

I like the food here, but the portions are small. I always leave slightly hungry. And why do they guard the sodas machine so that not only do I have to walk for a refill, but I have to wait to get an employee's attention to refill it?
Great good, terrific service, clean restaurant!

This place is great if you have never had authentic Korean or Japanese food. Because its not great. I got their ramen and it was packaged noodles and a watery broth. I'm sure if someone is ignorant to the cultures and foods, its good. But for someone who actually knows how that food is supposed to taste, its bad. Just another hipster Asian food place trying to cash in on ignorant people.
I have been coming to Eat-Well since I moved to New Orleans 10 years ago. They have great fresh foods! Staff is terrific! My usual is the BanhMi poboy!
Very quick and great food with a nice atmosphere to eat it in . We drove from Greenwood just to try this location after loving the one by IUPUI

Decided to try a new place and ended up finding this hidden gem! We had the combo platter to start and then I had the curry chicken as my main.. now I wasn't expecting it to be a soup but it was sure amazing! And my rice came out in a heart shape too, so cute! I ended up cutting my meal short as I saw the deep fried ice cream on the dessert menu and could not pass it up and I man I was not disappointed. Everything was very good and the staff was super friendly. I will be back for sure

This place is great! It's a local, hole in the wall kind of spot but the food is great. I love Greek food so thought we would check this out. I had a chicken platter and my his husband had a gyro. All was excellent. I wish the platter came with hummus but it doesn't - next time I'll order some on the side cause I bet it's yummy. Also had a side of falafel which was delicious! Will totally go back here to support a local business with tasty food.
The food is delicious, while the setting is unpretentious and unfussy. We eat here a lot and it is always excellent. The rack of lamb, the Mae Nam, the Cornish hen, the sea bass - every one a winner.

Great quick bite before standing in line for the Presentation Hall concert. It is hard to find a place to take your kids in for a meal this close to Burbon Street. Splitting the combination platter with a kid hit the spot and not the wallet.

The food definitely had more flavor than the magazine street location but the service was less than stellar. At one point every person working there was looking down and on their phones. Even the cooks! Needless to say the lack of care was noticed.

Just happened to drive past this restaurant & decided to stop. What a pleasure! We were warmly greeted & the service was excellent. This was the first time anyone in our party had eaten Puerto Rican food. Everything was flavorful & fresh; not spicy. My son said his steak with chimichurri sauce was the best steak he has ever had. Another plus is this is a family owned restaurant. I highly recommend it!

This Puerto Rican restaurant located in the same Plaza as kaleisia tea Lounge and Panda Hut, right next door to ABC Seafood Restaurant. The interior was nicely decorated with a cozy feeling at the sitting area. We had the relleno de papa . 3 fried potato balls with some ham inside, tasted crunchy and delicious. I tried the guava flavor of lotus brand can juice. It was pretty good. I had Mofongo and rotisserie chicken. The mofongo was so good with crunchy fried garlic inside. The plantain were prepared to a perfect flavor and texture. The half chicken tasted fresh , rich in flavor and it went nicely with the garlic sauce. The owner let us try a special salad only served on weekend. This was my first time tasting the green plantain and chicken gizzard salad . It got cooked plantain cubes, green olive, tiny pieces of chicken gizzard in olive oil and hint of vinegar. what a refreshing and delicious dish for hot summer day! She also let us try their special pig feet stew (not in the menu) and it's only served on Friday. The meat and skin was fell off the bone tender with chickpea and potato in a yummy broth. I was very impressed by their food and the pricing was super friendly. The father and daughter team running this place prepare their food fresh everyday. That means if you come in late, the chicken may sold out already. Very good food, friendly services, it was a pleasant experience dining here.

Zoe's Kitchen is the freshest, healthiest restaurant I have ever been to. Everything on their menu will make your lips tremble and mouth water. The service is always fast and friendly, not to mention they bring the food right to you! My favorite meal is the lean turkey pita with a side of fresh fruit. This pita includes a refreshing mix of lettuce, feta cheese, and lean turkey slices with a variety of cold, fresh fruit that hits the spot. If I could eat lunch and dinner here every day, I would in a heart beat!

This review is about the Lafayette Hill location, but I'm writing it here because I can't seem to find the Yelp page for that location anymore. Anyhow, I'd read good things on Yelp about Nirvana, and had seen it in passing now and then. Based on the raving reviews and the coupons they sent to our house, we decided to try the restaurant out twice this week. Earlier in the week, we ordered some food for takeout. It didn't take long for them to get our food ready, and it all tasted great! We got some chicken dishes and the lamb chops, and I have to say that those lamb chops were tender and delicious! Today, we decided to go there for the lunch buffet, and that was just as impressive! They had a very nice selection out for us to choose from, including veggie, meat, and desserts. There was also masala chai, which was very welcome in the cold weather. In addition to the food being good, the gentleman working there was very friendly and thoughtful. While browsing around, my wife asked him if the yogurts had any flour in them, to which he answered no. Later on, when she wanted to get some syrup from the galub jamun to add to the chai, he approached her to tell her that there is flour in that dish. I thought that was an example of great service! We really enjoyed it here! We'll be back and will tell friends to try it out too!

Couldn't take pictures of the food fast enough! Everything was delicious and so fresh. The restaurant is very tiny and you can't make reservations but totally worth the wait. The food is amazing! Tasted just like Greece. We got with the hummus, shrimp pil pil, meatballs, lamb, calamari, pan seared scallops. By far my favorite are the shrimp pil pil and the scallops. Get the scallops pan seared, they were perfectly cooked, crispy on the outside. I didn't try the meatballs but they were everyone at the tables favorite dish. You cannot go wrong with whatever you order. Can't wait to go back! Don't forget it's BYOB and cash only.

I was pleasantly surprised by Nadia Thai when my husband and I decided to order takeout from here on the way home from a road trip. We knew we wanted Thai and that we didn't want to steer too off course on the way home, so we decided to try Nadia Thai which which was right on our way. I had the drunken noodles and my husband had the green curry. Both dishes were hot and fresh (in fact, when we arrived to pick it up a few minutes early, our order was just being finished up). Everything was nicely packaged so we didn't have any sauce disasters on the car ride home. We dug right in when we got home and everything was delicious and hot. Not only that, but the portions were quite large, so I had enough for a second meal of drunken noodles for lunch the next day. I found the spice to be just right -- not too overpowering, but some heat to give it flavor. As a side note, the place doesn't look like much from the outside, but having gone in to pick up our order, I found the inside of the restaurant to be quite nice. It's nicely decorated, dimly lit, and intimate. It would be great place to take a date!

Food is good and reasonably priced. Not the best Thai that I ever had but still pretty good. I went here with a groupon. Service was good and food came out pretty quick. Portions were decent. Curries were good but I still think Circles has the best Thai in Philly. I would go back if I were in Chinatown but not my favorite Thai in Philly.

My boyfriend brought me here for our anniversary and I couldn't have been happier. We shared hot tea and the vegetarian combo plate. Both were amazing. I had never experienced any African food but I definitely see myself coming back to get the coffee ceremony. The service was fast and friendly. Overall this was a great experience and I would recommend everyone to try this place.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: The best Thai food in Reno at an affordable price. Fresh veggies and meats. I recommend the spring rolls and the brocoli and shrimp entree. Excellent mango sticky rice. Clean environment with friendly and efficient wait staff. Thai cuisine is my absolute favorite and I haven't found a reasonably priced Thai restaurant in town....until now. Made for an easy date night.

This restaurant is amazing. I could eat this stuff all the time. I usually go with the second lamb dish down, and a couple other things. Recently I tried adding salad to my order and it goes really well with the other dishes. She also makes this amazing tea. In the summer it's iced, and in the winter it's hot. It's really worth trying! Last thing I have to add is that it's run by one person. To be able to run a restaurant solo takes some serious talent to begin with, but to make this quality of food AND run the place is amazing. Easily a 5 star review.

Doesn't look like much from the outside, but WOW is the food good! I was meeting some friends for dinner and had gotten a recommendation for this place. We came on a Wednesday night around 7 and the place was pretty busy! Our server was absolutely fantastic. He made some great recommendations and even made one of my DPs a duck special that wasn't on the menu, because she mentioned she was a fan of duck.
