He made suggestions based on what we were considering, that would make our meals more unique and interesting. He really knew his stuff and he really enhanced our experience at Nadia! I got the drunken noodle which I'd highly recommend. Absolutely delicious. I also had a Thai iced tea with my meal and green tea ice cream for dessert. Diet starts tomorrow... By the way, if you're coming from Philly during rush hour like I did, don't make the same mistake I did and drive. This place is literally NEXT to the Lansdale train station. Would've saved me a headache and some gas if I would have bothered to look beforehand... oops! If I'm ever in the area I would definitely return. No frills, just plain good Thai food.

On Sunday mornings, sleepy college students recovering from the previous night's shenanigans wait in line at this food truck for the Hangover Special: sausage, ham, bacon, egg and cheese on a long roll from Amaroso's, plus a Gatorade. The crowd is mostly students. The breakfast sandwiches are standard combinations (steak, sausage, scrapple, bacon, ham, scrambled eggs, cheese). The lunch offerings rance from the pepperoni pizza steak to the Mr. Bui (steak or chicken with bell peppers and teriyaki sause) and Mrs. Bui (steak or chicken with spinach, tomato and the secret mayo-creamy Bui's sauce). Your toppings are salt, pepper, ketchup, hot sauce (I believe Sriracha) and Bui's sauce. This is the mecca for breakfast and lunch sandwiches. Tip: When it's peak time, it's smart to call ahead with your order. Then you can quickly pay and scoop up your sandwich, beating the crowd.
This place is a hole in the wall that serves great tasting typical Puerto Rican and Cuban food.

3.5 stars. I went here with a group of Yelpers after a visit to Dock Street. It's somewhat dingy and dark at night. There are two sections, the main bar and another section with sit down booths and a karaoke machine. Fortunately, or unfortunately depending on your view of karaoke, it was karaoke night. Sort of like American Idol tryouts in real time, without the pompous British arsehole. There were actually some good singers, though by in large it was mostly juiced up partiers with an exaggerated opinion of their singing ability. The highlight was watching this guy dressed in Avril Lavigne arm bands singing and dancing without a care in the world. Drink prices were ridiculously cheap. I think for 4 people we got two gin an tonics an two beers for under 20 bucks. The waitress was attentive and fast. I have to admit this wasn't a place I would have visited if friends hadn't prodded me into going. I'm glad I did.

Tried it for a different Saturday night take out dinner and it did not disappoint ! Everything was fresh, hot and delicious. The family favorite was the Korean beef with the sesame sauce. Skip the dessert egg rolls. Can't wait to try more varieties and even breakfast.

This was my first time at Wishbone, and I was so impressed. The food and desserts were awesome! Homemade SNAP beverages were so tasty. Comfort food without the heavy feeling. Definitely a great place to check out!

I stumbled across this place while walking downtown. I love Pho and this place did it beautifully! The place itself was very clean, but empty. The food was beyond fresh and some of the best Pho I've ever had. Would I come back? I would love to, but their hours don't allow it. They are only open 10 - 3. As a teacher, I don't leave until 3:30.

Good food but oily. I looked at the their menu before we went to see if they labeled vegetarian/vegan options which they did so I was soooo happy about that because while I am not either of those, I do not eat dairy, so I always feel safe getting vegan options because then I'm sure there's no dairy in it. So I really appreciated that. When we got there we saw that they had the lunch buffet special so we definitely got that! (It runs from 12-3pm.) Half of the buffet was vegan options. It was all yummy stuff like a chickpea dish, okra with veggies, different masala dishes, cabbage with peas and veggies, different types of rice, and they also had chicken dishes, goat, and lettuce, cucumbers, and way more. The waiter was helpful in telling me what had dairy and what didn't. (Thank you!!) Food tasted good I just wish it wasn't as oily.

This place is very authentic in terms of food and atmosphere. I'm surprised at the 3.5 star rating it currently has on Yelp. The lamb is amazing and just melts in your mouth. I highly recommend everyone order #16 with lamb. The rice that comes with that dish is amazing.

This is an experience of true India cuisine of cultural spice. From the best of a foodie moment I walked in the place and there was this aroma that brought me highly lifted to a place out of this world. Saffron rice tandoori chicken and charred pepper filled my senses. Peppe explained nann breads in his world. Then we drifted off to a land of. .... ......mamboia I cannot say more. You must must stop here for an authentic fine dining room with Hindu music that that takes you on a journey to a land far away.

We love this place and we try to get there as often as possilble. The variety of specials is always the best part of coming in. You never know what the Chef has on tap for today. The food is always excellent. We usually sit at the bar with Kristen and that is always some entertainment with her good sense of humor. From the outside it doesn't look like much, but you will enjoy your time there.

I love this place! Great service and their rolls are delicious. I especially love the sushi pizza! And they are wonderful with children. Everytime my daughter comes with me they give her special chopsticks.

The staff was friendly but between appetizers and our meals we waited almost 40-45 minutes. It wasn't very busy so I was not sure why it took so long. Our food did come out very hot and delicious. It could use an update on the decor. The one major thing that irked me, wasn't a big deal but if your tell me the specials, let me know it's $40 for a plate. A simple heads up would have been appreciated. Overall pretty good experience, but just can't give it 5 stars.

Food was great, the service was great. Don't order through the app, grub hub does not deliver it. It simple sends the order takes a fee and you have to pick it up. Call the restaurant they will tell you a legit service to use.

We've been driving past Island Breeze Cafe (formerly Montego Bay Cafe) for years with the intention of stopping in one day. Well we just ate here for the first time last night, and 24+ hours later, I'm still salivating over the thought of my meal. My guy and I both had jerk chicken and plantains. He got the spinach & rice and I got the rice & peas. Everything was AMAZING. The rice & peas was delicious and perfectly spiced, but I think I might have preferred his spinach & rice. It was just a notch or two tastier than my side. We were the only diners in the cafe on a Friday night, which was a little discouraging. The dining room was small and poorly lit, but our server was really nice. There was reggae music and a television playing in the room, but it wasn't loud enough to be obnoxious. I've eaten at Jamaicaway and Calypso Cafe, and I've never been overly impressed by either. But our meal at Island Breeze really wowed me. I can't wait to go back again and again! Island Breeze Cafe will definitely be added to the top of the list on our take-out roster.

It's really more of a grocery than a sit down, by the girl working the counter was very attentive to our table. The food was excellent - best flavor rich and full of flavor, fresh, and with attention to detail.
Tofu soup is good...their kalbi was bland. Means I have to find a new place because kalbi is my fav...oh their dukbokki was good too. Maybe it is just their meats :(

I have been to this restaurant many times, and time and time again they succeed at cooking a great flavorful meal and continue to offer excellent service. I recommend any of the curry dishes, which are coconut milk based. What's not to love? You can choose from a variety of proteins and a spice level from 1 to 5. If you feel daring, go for the 5, just make sure to order an ice cold IPA. Appetizers are also excellent and would recommend the pork giozas! They're similar to pot stickers but smaller, crunchier, and just plain better. Prices are moderate and the best part is they are located in a great little town of Columbia, IL, a mere 11 miles from downtown STL. Give it a try, you can thank me later.

India's Kitchen is easy to miss. It's nondescript from the outside and in a strip mall next to the Uncle Sam's military surplus store just down from Uncle Bill's. Inside is nice. The tables are all set with silverware, stemware and tablecloths. But last night when we walked in, there was only one other table seated in the place when we entered. Service, was decent... with one annoying flaw. Three different employees waited on us... one lady and two older dudes. Both of the guys mumbled, and even continued talking to us as they were walking away. It was hard enough figuring out what they were saying through their accents, but the mush-mouth dictation was frustrating. I just shook my head yes every time as they walked away. For all I know, they could be saying, "Do you like to have sex with goats, and eat piles of poo?". The girlfriend and I ordered beef samosas to start. They were handmade, and good. Flaky crust and a hint of sweetness in the meat. That's one fun thing about eating Indian food... they use spices that you can't quite identify. We followed the appetizer order with the #10 feast for two. Go ahead and judge. Only a glutton would order a dish called Feast for Two AND and appetizer. Whatever, this is my review not yours. The 'feast' consisted of Tandoori chicken, Chicken Tikka, Shrimp Tandoori, Sheesh Kebab, Lamb Curry, Vegetable Korma, naan, a boatload of rice, two desserts, and coffee. All this for $37. It was monstrous. We were sitting at a booth for four and our table was FULL. Which got me thinking, they should offer this item as a novelty. If there is any way one person could eat all of this, they should get it free. The two of us hadn't eaten all day and I don't think we made it through half of it. Anyway.... all the items were good... but the veggie Korma was awesome. This creamy pink broth was so yummy. It had hints of coconut milk, almonds, and cashews. I would order this one by itself next time. After dinner we were served some rice pudding mixture that reminded me of horchata, and little pancake balls covered in honey. They were interesting, but I doubt I'd order either if it wasn't included in the feast. Value - great Food - good Service - decent... but get ready to play a game of 'what the hell is he saying'

Basil Spice is located in a great, walkable area near easy street parking. It's a wonderful neighborhood to walk around and enjoy local shops and restaurants. The quality of the food was good, with ingredients tasting fresh and will put together. The dish was flavorful and spiced appropriately given our requests. I do think the portion size on the noodle dish could have been a little larger for the price point and the seafood was a little skimpy on quantity as well. With a large range of Thai places in St Louis, they have ample competition in the market.

Deliverance from the vilest hangovers...now in truck form! Seriously, as attested everywhere in recent Philly history by college students, Bui's is your miracle cure for your nightime indiscretions. No matter what the issue is, bacon, egg and cheese with "salpeppaketcha" on a perfect pillowy white bun will help you regain your footing on the path to tranquility. Take that first bite, bask in the sunshine and smile: bliss PARTING THOUGHT: Bui's staff is great about making unusual sandwiches. For example, I'm a fan of the cheesesteak with egg and siracha!

My girl and I went to try the lunch buffet. The food was decent and great flavor. The service was definitely good. The place does not look good at all and that's why to low rating. Although the food was good the worn booth and floor make us feel the place was a little neglected over the years. They definitely need to renovate the place.

Wow. Just wow. I've eaten take-out from here before when it was just a small grocery shop with tables and seating, and haven't been over since they renovated. The place looks AWESOME now. They still have the grocery shop, but they also have a full-blown restaurant right next door. I've had a lot of good Indian food at several places around the Wayne/KOP area of PA, but dare I say this place far surpasses those restaurants. We ordered several dishes: Chicken Korma, Chicken Tikka Masala, Chicken Vindaloo, and Mattar Paneer. The Korma was my mother's choice. It was new to me, so I took a bite and now it's my new favorite Indian dish. So creamy, buttery and delicious. I wish I ordered it. I actually had the chicken vindaloo. I love the flavor because it reminds me of a Filipino dish I had growing up called Chicken Afritada. Basically potato, chicken thighs (boneless/skinless), and tomato all stewed together. Very yummy. My wife had her go-to, Mattar Paneer... aka... "the peas & cheese". Sauce was creamy, cheese was tasty, and peas had a nice snap to them. Finally, my daughter had the Chicken Tikka Masala. There is something different about their tikka masala than other places that I REALLY enjoy... you can actually taste the smoky, tandoori flavor in the chicken. Most places just put plain chicken in it, but I really liked the subtle smokiness with Zaika's version. Our server was SO super sweet and nice. She asked all of us for our heat levels for each dish, and I told her my daughter wanted her Tikka Masala "as mild as you can make it". When reading back the order, she says, "chicken korma, mild... matar paneer, mild... chicken vindaloo, medium... tikka masala, EXTRA mild"... lol. That made us pop. I wish I had more of a tip to give her than i did. She did an awesome job. The prices are on the higher end, but I feel the quality of the dishes make it well worth it. About $15 a head.

They make delicious sushi! I have ordered it from them multiple times and since they have great coupons right on their grubhub order page I always wind up having leftovers! I highly recommend it! Also their seaweed salad is worth the $6!!

Definitely my new favorite place to eat brunch in the Philly area. The venue is stunning and really bright. The Labne was absolutely delicious. The rose pistachio cruller was lightly sweet but absolutely amazing. Will definitely be coming back soon!

I really love the food here. The Summer rolls are fresh, bright, and delicious. The fried egg rolls are everything I want in an egg roll. Yum! The fried rice has a certain flair that is highly complimented with a light splash of fish sauce and sweet hot pepper sauce. The yellow curry is equally complimented by the addition of the sauces, but does not stand as strongly on its own. I'll be back!

Ohhhhh where to start!!!! I ordered a falafel pita with no hummus, no black olives, no cucumber, and no green pepper!!! Well I got exactly what I did not want!!! I am not being a picky person but unfortunately I'm not a hummus fan (yeah I know I like falafel but not hummus) and I am allergic to cucumbers ( not my fault but makes me puke and gives me a rash) so what happened when I opened up my pita.... Went straight to the trash!!! I am never calling in an order to this place again!

In a world of Metaphorical Midgets Pho An Hoa stands a proud 5 feet tall. I've been on a quest for nearly a month now to find real, authentic, hearty, pho in the Greater Tampa Area and so far my journey has left me with a phoking terrible view of Vietnamese food around here. Pho An Hoa might be the saving grace for this city. I'm not saying it's superb by any means... but it sure is better than the competition so far. As always I ordered the same things. I started with the Cha gio egg rolls ($3 for two). These were the best in this city so far and really the main reason I'll likely return to this shop. They were fluffy on the inside, not burnt like others, had the perfect balance of ingredients, and came with the perfectly sweet but subtle sauce. Definitely a must try. Next I went straight for the Pho. The very reason I eat out all the time. The reason people should stop making soup is because Pho is already perfection. Well... Pho an Hoa isn't, but it's the closest I've found in Tampa. The Tai nam rare steak and well-done flank ($5.75) was actually pretty good. The broth has flavors I expected but none jumped at me. My guess, just a guess, is that the broth was done properly but just not long enough. Maybe dry hop some star anise towards the end of the stock? Just a thought. My only real complaint is the same I make about MOST pho shops. The condiment plate did not come with saw palmetto or cilantro. Those are both staples to pho and I'd really like them in my dish. I know you have Cilantro, I've seen it. Please use it. Give me half the basil and just add a little cilantro to the plate. I'd love that.

Spiros is the best Greek restaurant in St Louis hands down. What a beautiful and classy establishment. This is what a Greek restaurant should be like always. The restaurant reminds me of the same types of places you'd find in Greektown in Chicago at places like Costa's or Rodity's. This is a very nice place to take a date. My girlfriend and I were blown away by our experience here. The presentation and service was excellent. Spiros, the owner, gave us free shots of Ouzo when he found out I was Greek. We had a great conversation in the old language and he took care of us out of genuine respect. The place has more of a fine dining feel but at a reasonable price. I got the pasticcio and Moussaka which I always do at every Greek place and their versions were the best by far from any others I've visited. Spiro's is very elegant and we left very very happy. Euxaristoume para polu Spiros!

The great dining options in midtown/downtown keep getting better. Creazian is a fairly new addition and had hear good things about it. Went last night and was treated to super friendly service and delicious Vietnamese food. Not your typical more casual Pho place, this has a very nice dinning room and more sophisticated offerings. Its in a bit of an non obvious place, but worth seeking out. They have a great happy hour and the owner is super nice and deserves support.
A falafel that is not fried??? Yes!! Super cheap - I think only 3 bucks for this sandwich and add baba topping it came to $4. Great size portion and rather delicious!

So it's summer and I wasn't feeling well and had some extra time before I needed to meet a friend decided maybe something Thai and spicy would be the right choice. Stopped in to PIKPON and the girl behind the counter help me make a choice and even combined one of their spicier soups that has lemongrass mushrooms bell pepper cilantro onions and basil, called Tom Yum soup and added in rice noodles to make it a noodle bowl along with some of the largest chunk of tofu I've ever seen. This was the best noodle bowl I've ever had. It was fresh, the tofu was perfect, the spices and herbs literally had me feeling better as I ate it. It also had the perfect level of heat. I tried something new when I was done which was Thai taro custard. Also delicious. This place is about 45 minutes from my house and yet when I am in the mood again for a noodle bowl I would be willing to take that drive. If you live anywhere near here and have not eaten here you are truly missing out.
Great buffet with more than half of the dishes being vegetarian. I liked the korma the best! Yum!

OMG Ali Baba, how could you hurt me so badly?? I went in last night, a little intoxicated to get my usual falafel sandwich. I encountered an employee I had never seen before, who was on his phone for about a minute while I stood there. He kept winking at me (ew) while still on the phone. I finally ordered my food and was leaving to go meet my party next door, when he asks me if I live here, and generally making me uncomfortable with his questioning and posturing. I come back to grab my food and he continuously called me babe and honey... ick. I later discovered that my falafel had tatziki sauce instead of tahini.. which made me very ill. I will still be going to Ali Baba, but from now on I will bring someone else with me and ensure the dairy-free-edness

We came by here late on a Tuesday night, luckily they're open until 10pm during the week. We were the only ones eating there that late but that was ok, we got all of the attention and the staff were very nice. I loved the low tables and cushioned seats we were sat at. After a quick glance at the menu, I went with the chicken pad Thai and guy went with the cashew chicken I believe. Our food came out really quick and we both inhaled our dinners, both dishes were really tasty and the prices were really cheap. I just moved from Seattle and dishes like that would have easily been $3-4 more so it was nice to have a decent dinner bill for Thai food. This place is also just down the road from my new home so I'm sure we'll be back soon. Parking is easy with a lot just out front with some spots.

One would think a place called Mojito would make a decent Mojito. It was perhaps the worst Mojito I've ever had and I've had a lot. Bartender didn't even bother to muddle the mint. The guac and chips were tasteless as was the steak fajita. A little salt goes a long way. The second star for prime location.

Stopped in here with my boyfriend because we had a groupon. We never had Thai food before but we definitely loved everything about it? We had a fried shrimp appetizer, he had the red curry with pork, and i had the drunken noodles with chicken. Everything was tasty and hot and the service was great! Loved that it was a byob as well.

Being from the Bay Area I love great Asian food and this is the best in Reno. Great food, excellent service, and a warm a inviting place to enjoy your meal. If you're new to Reno or been here a while, you must visit SF Kitchen, you'll love it!

I hate to be the only person who does not give this a 5 star but I never do that on first review. I've been burned too many times by inconsistency in restaurants here. This is a LITTLE place. Very plain. And that's ok. Almost everything is in Spanish and the waitstaff speak mostly Spanish as well. The food is what's the most important thing and the food here is fantastic. Because they do not have paper menus, I can't give the proper names for stuff but here I go anyway. I ordered the thinly sliced steaks. They came with rice, beans (whole beans, not refried), Crispy fried green plantains and a salad. All for 9.99. It was a LOT of food. The steak was cooked well done but was still juicy and tender. The beans were savory but not salty. The rice was soft but not mushy and the salad had a healthy bit of avocado in it. All in all, my plate was fantastic. The Girly ordered the Honduran style taco. Which, to me, looked more like Floutas. 4-5 rolls with crispy outsides stuffed with slow-cooked chicken that, in all honesty, seemed to almost be slow smoked pork. REALLY good. They were covered by a ton of salad. Combined, it made a cheesy, chickeny, crispy mess but it was VERY good. And at 8.99, it wasn't a bad deal at all. With both meals, a melon drink (amazing but a little sweet. Might need water with it), and a coconut drink, it came to 25 bucks. Not too bad. We've had lunches that cost more but wasn't half as good. One caveat. If you are overly hungry or in a hurry, you may want to pass this place up. With 3 tables of people, it took over 25 minutes for the food. But it was worth the wait.

Absolutely one of my favorites in Boise that not many people know about. Their hummus and bread is only $3 and serves like a meal for me. They also have $3 falafel sandwiches that are so tasty! Their bread is freshly baked in house and is some of the best I've ever had. Also attached to a nice market--I highly recommend buying some labne (a strained yogurt cheese) to use in place of cream cheese on breads or to add to your cheese platter. Great with some za'atar sprinkled on top. They also have delicious baked goods!!

A great place to grab some quick Thai in Edmonton. It's definitely in my top 3. In regards to their food: their yellow curry is so amazing. It isn't too thick and has the right amount of spice. Their coconut rice is also super tasty. Their service is a little lackluster, but their food makes up for it.

Fantastic restaurant. We tried this on a random weeknight and couldn't have been more pleasantly surprised. Delicious focacia bread! I had the shrimp pasta, and it was great. Booths also add some privacy to make your dinner more intimate. We'll definitely be back!

The food was amazing and the hosts extremely friendly. They allow you to pick your spiciness level from "mild" to "Indian" depending on your tolerance. And as a bonus my date and I got $30 in movie ticket coupons (more than I spent on the entire dinner for two).

Looking for amazing Trinidadian cuisine? Well this is the place!! Floridian native with West Indian roots!! This food reminded me of back home, Not only is it authentic but it is prepared from scratch and freshly made. The decor is superb and the Soca music reminds you of Carnival. This place is definitely worth visiting for a meet up with friends or date night!! I started out with the Caribbean salad as the appetizer- the spicy dressing goes perfect with it. My Entree entailed Curry Chicken with chick peas and the BEST BUSS UP SHUT ROTI in Philly!!

VEGETARIAN REVIEW: Atmosphere is delightful, especially for a cute date! The food however... well, not so much. For appetizers, the Jasmine soup (which I got based on the great reviews on here) tasted like garlic water, literally. Additionally, there was shredded ginger in the soup, which was not good! I like ginger, but the shreds were too big. Additionally, there was more ginger shreds than there was rice! The noodles that came out were overcooked and had too much of a peanut flavor. Now, of course I understand that its Thai food's main ingredient, but really, the flavor was absolutely overpowering. The pad thai was good, it was really spicy, which I liked. However, there was not enough gravy to mix with your rice. The rice was over cooked. The coconut ice cream was good. In general, it was all overpriced. I paid about $65 for the three of us, 1 jasmine soup, two entrees, one tea, one coconut ice cream and tip. Service was great! Our waiter was sweet and offered good recommendations. All in all, I wouldn't come here again.

I tried this restaurant a few weeks back, after looking at the reviews. This place was amazing the food was great. So much flavor and spicy in every bite. I can't wait to try something new on the menu on my next visit.

My fiancé and I are new to the area and were super excited to try this place for brunch. The aesthetic is great, service was awesome!! However, the food was pure disappointment! The chicken and waffles were the worst I've ever had- chicken was barely seasoned (and that's being generous) and tough. The waffle was DRY DRY DRY! Even after I soaked it in syrup- still dry. We also tried the Chili Plum BBQ wings- the sauce was decent, though for a dish with Chili in the name, I thought there'd be some spice to it. The wings would've been better if they were cooked a little longer, I just don't like soggy wings. The hand cut fries were probably the best thing and those were even pretty bland. I'm really interested to see who's seasoning, rather not seasoning the food back there! I think if we do ever go again, it'll just be for drinks and the live music.
Stuck-up staff, and the food at Zahav is way better than Suraya's for comparable prices. Boo-urns
Yum. Just yum. Don't know what else to say. I love good Indian food and its not easy to find good Indian food in Indy. This place rocks for eat in or delivery.

We tried this place today for the first time. I know it just recently opened next to the Indian grocer in the Trappe Center Plaza and since we lived in India for a period of time we are picky. This place did not disappoint. The lunch buffet was great. The biryani was top notch as was their chicken tikka. The staff was wonderful and checked back on us several times which I thought was nice. The only thing I wish they did was one complimentary naan basket with the buffet like Spice does. Overall we will for sure be back!!

Great example of delicious food in a pretty ambiance. Happy to support this family's small/local business. Right next to the Grand Sierra Resort Hotel - So instead of having GSR's terrible imitation "pacific rim" cuisine, where their pho is made of chicken or vegetarian broth, why not have real Vietnamese & Chinese food at SF kitchen? Egg rolls were crispy perfection and Bun Bo Hue noodle soup had rich spicy broth with filling wide rice noodles. Plus, you can eat without the cigarette smoke that permeates the GSR hotel restaurants.
Your breakfast sausage egg sandwich with Bui's sauce was probably the best breakfast I had this year in Philadelphia. Great portion for the price paid. Wish you were in California.

Very convenient, just bummed out it's not open on weekends. You order off of a kiosk; everything is customizable. Pho is unique, and definitely has a different overall broth compared to Pho 20 or Pho 75. It's pretty clean and meaty. Bean sprouts and other garnishes were fresh and well prepped. Good, quiet spot to grab a bowl of pho on the weekday.

Really great atmosphere, good service. Food was delicious. I asked the waiter to make my food spicy and it was done exactly to my liking. I had the grilled salmon, which was really delicious and presentation was exquisite, as well. I would love to go there again and take my friends there as well.

I feel a little sorry giving this place two stars because it wasn't aggressively bad. It just wasn't good. The Sunday lunch buffet looked like it had been prepared the day before. The chaat, for example, was a bit gray looking and I almost didn't recognize the spicy pickles because they were limp and slightly off-color. All of the dishes were kind of crusty on the outside--like they had been sitting out awhile or the warmers were too hot. Either way, it made for an unappetizing presentation. The naan was so hard, it was almost like crackers. The tamarind sauce was watery. The numerous veggie dishes were edible, except the mushroom mutter, a dish I usually like, was just gross. The staff was attentive, but unfriendly. For those who like Indian desserts, they had a whole separate buffet for those. But, overall, this was a total waste of calories for me.

To be Happy Is Simple (T.H.I.S) Place is the next place in Edmonton where you'll think to yourself, "This place is cute!" I lump it along with my favorite hang out places, the likes of Duchess Bakery on 124 St and ROAST Coffee House, a place where you can order something to nosh on and just relax. Although both Duchess and ROAST have become crowded on most days, T.H.I.S Place seems to be slowly settling into the area. Most definitely underrated and waiting for the crowds to hit! With great press on the place in the last few months of 2012, it was on my list to visit but I never got a chance to until last week. Located near MacEwan on 105 St and 104 Ave, the space is below the Quest condo, hidden away on the southeast corner of the building. Joe and I had time to kill so I mentioned about T.H.I.S Place and how I wanted to try the hot chocolate. Joe responded with, "What place?" and I repeatedly said ,"T.H.I.S Place. This place... is called THIS Place." A look of confusion told me that I wasn't explaining myself very well. Anyways, getting over the name.. they specialize in homemade hot chocolates to fresh fruit popsicle, coffees and teas. With such a small exterior, I was expecting a small space. Not so! High ceilings lined with concrete walls give the place an airy industrial feel. Large abstract local art line the space and unique light fixtures create a gallery persona. Although contrary in a majority of the country, it's still winter here. I didn't try the popsicles although the flavors sound delicious! Instead, I opted for my favorite warm beverage of all time: hot chocolate. Fact: I started off on hot chocolate during the first month of my university years in an effort to not be a caffeine addict (failed miserably, I eventually moved to mochas). Since graduating though, I've cut back quite a bit and only drink coffee on morning shifts now. Everything else is hot chocolate! Boasting homemade hot chocolates which you can purchase to drink or purchase to take home, this was heaven for me. Super cute! And so simple too. I bought a dark hot chocolate to try at work in attempts to cut my Starbucks consumption. Delicious! Although I followed the instructions to the recommended 6oz of hot milk, I found it a bit too rich and creamy. 7oz - 8oz of milk did it for me, which only means more hot chocolate! Can't wait to go back and try the other flavors. They were offering a salted caramel hot chocolate that day, topped with green whipped cream in honor of St. Patrick's Day. YUMMY. One of the best hot chocolates I've had yet! And gigantic too, making it ideal for lounging and relaxing in one of the many seating areas they offer. If you're bored with browsing your smart phone, they offer the latest of most of the local magazines, such as Avenue, The Tomato, and Vue Weekly. Other magazine subscriptions are there for your reading pleasure as well and a mishmash of travel and art books. Most definitely my new favorite place if I want a quieter area to relax in. Hot chocolate for winter, popsicles for summer. Perfect! Next time you're in the area, be sure to drop by and check it out. T.H.I.S Place is super cute!

I ordered the chicken tikka masala and the dal tardka i also ordered the onion kulcha everything i ordered was very good my only complaint was about the rice it had a strong liquorice flavor that i did not enjoy but other then that it was good. i like that i can order online its very convenient. I will be ordering again.

Love, Love, Love! This restaurant will never disappoint know matter what you order. Today I had the make your own mix thing I got the regular portion for $6.50 and could only eat half of it before I was stuffed. Best spanish food short of a "Ma and Pop" Puerto Rican restaurant. If your hungry and pass a Pollo Tropical you should definitely stop and eat. BTW they have this garlic creamy sauce that is absolutely to die for!!!

Pretty good, something different. I had the Cajun shrimp sandwich and my husband had the grilled beef sandwich. We shared shrimp spring rolls. I liked the jalapeño and cilantro in the sandwich as well as the pickled veggies. I would eat here again, don't know that I would go out of my way but if I was hungry and in the area I would :)

I noticed that the reviews from a couple years ago aren't that flattering, but I have to say, they must have changed their act a bit since then. Besides the strange variety of interior selections....none of the lighting matches, there is a scattered string of lights in the window, a rusty suit of armor in the entry way, and a couple pictures that are a framers worst nightmare, but they all just add a little kookiness to the experience. The menu is quite large, and YES there are a lot of Noodle dishes, but it's almost like Thai comfort food. I always get the Drunken Noodles with chicken, which is huge and nice and spicy, and my husband usually gets the Kao Soy, which is a curried coconut chicken soup with noodles, that is very comforty. I recommend trying it for the first time for lunch, because their lunch special is awesome. You get soup, an app, and an entree for like $8.00 or something, but make sure you build in some time, because they tend to always be a little slow. It's a plus that they are a BYO too.

We finally made it to Suraya after a 3 month wait, and surprisingly it was worth it. When you walk in, you are immediately greeted by this beautiful decor. My best friend and I went to Suraya earlier for cocktails and had the pleasure of sitting outside in their courtyard. Everything is very "instagram-able". But, the decor isn't the highlight. The food is. It feels like mediterranean with a twist. It's not your regular hummus + lamb dish. It's a little extra. The service was also on point. Overall, it definitely deserves this year's title of best restaurant in Philadelphia.
Loved it! Had the chicken ramen and pork belly bun. Seasoned very well. We will be back.

Second time here , and the first time wasn't even worth a rating....Ok so Friday night date night we decided to stay local and away from Center City Philly.I very rarely have a taste for "Asian Cultured Cuisine",and I'm not much for a chains either..so as you guess I wasn't too thrilled when my fiancé suggested we eat here. Atmosphere is cool, dim and a good place for two or a whole family. The problem is that most of what can be order here is being served elsewhere for a better price,portion and taste amazing.So I start with a appetizer, Crab wontons, which were okay, however,The sauce they served with it taste like something was missing.For my main course I ordered honey seared shrimp with white rice.The white rice came in the form of a cold gummy lump slapped into a ceramic bowl.Pretty sure my nine year old could have done a better job. The shrimp taste like something I could have ordered from my local Chinese store, and the portion was very small(6 shrimp)...I can't speak for my fiancé 's meal, which looked way more appetizing.(spring rolls and lemon peppered chicken with peppers).After giving my taste buds a wet dream, I decided to order dessert to make up for it.Banana wontons and vanilla ice cream as suggested by my waitress. At last!!!! this was the best part of my night.delicious, sweet and just what I needed to redeem the mediocre meal.Way to go P.F Chang's you have managed to fool us all with your decor and prices into thinking that your food is anything but stereotypical.

If you want a consistently terrific Thai meal, you can't go wrong with this place. We ordered the Thai Basil, Drunken Noodles and Pineapple Curry Special. The Thai Basil was an excellent combination of being slightly spicy and evenly blended with sweetness and saltiness. My daughter thoroughly enjoyed the Pineapple Curry and said it should be a full-time menu item. The Drunken Noodles are thick, hearty and filled with flavor. It's always a hit.

Went back recently and found subpar food quality. Lukewarm pasta dishes as well as coffee during a busy night. Best to go on a week night when the kitchen isn't swamped. Desert cakes probably supermarket quality, nothing exciting and bland. Maybe the owner is spread a little too thin between here and his other locations? Francisco's is loosing its luster!

5/5 service 5/5 taste 5/5 atmosphere Tom and trudie are the fabulous owners of this gem of a place. Everything is made from scratch and if you're feeling adventurous, try the fresh durian Popsicle in the summer. You'll be surprised how creamy and delicious it tastes! My go to in the summer is always the coconut mango Popsicle and in the cold months the five spice hot chocolate isn't far from my hands. Don't be shy when you're walking by to grant Mac, abandon the Starbucks and head into T.H.I.S place!

Pani Puri: 1/5 Idli Sambhar: 2/5 Chole Bhatura: 4.5/5 portions very small. got a groupon. kind of regret it. nice staff but the food is sub par. can find much better indian eateries for better prices.
The live music is ok but this is a tourist trap. The drinks are ok but expensive and the food is terrible. I had a cuban sandwich that Cuba would be ashamed of.

As far as Thai food goes, I admit that I am a bit picky, bc I grew up eating some pretty fabulous Thai food. So as far as Thai Cuisine & Cafe, It was OK, but nothing to write home about. I tried the tom yom soup and the padthai with veggies. The tom yom seemed like the kind of soup you can buy at the store in a can....except they added chicken. I was pretty disappointed in the soup overall- it lacked the lemongrass flavor and spiciness and was pretty watery. My entree earned them a little redemption, but overall the tofu was shriveled and overcooked, and the noodles lacked the full flavor I am accustomed to tasting with pad thai. A bite of green curry from my friend seemed especially salty as well. As for the pros- they have clearly established a nice place, and the cozy decor was cute. We came with a party of 13, so it was nice of them to accommodate us in their small restaurant. The owner seemed pretty nice and eager to please. Parking is not an issue, there is a lot in the back so that is a pro. I dont know how recently they opened, but they have a few kinks to work out. I may try it again, but probably not for a while.

I would definitely go back here! It's BYOB and has speedy service. I think it's due to the limited space, but as long as you go at a good time before there is a long wait, you're golden. My friend and I each got the greek salad WITH greens (if you order it without saying with greens, it's a delicious combo of cucumber, red onion, green pepper, feta, olives, and tomatoes but I like lettuce in my salads). We also split the spanikopita, which was plenty for two and super yummy. Our waitresses were friendly and efficient. We sat at the bar where you get to watch the chefs prepare the food and enjoy the lively environment of the restaurant fully!
Service was excellent from both the server and the host. She was a gem. Perfect end to our vacation. Food was wonderful. Definitely check this place out!

Incredibly nice folks...why they don't have a cool little bar....I don't know...however, the food is outstanding ! Sometimes a bit salty for me....but...I don't put salt on anything...thus my taste is going to be ridiculously sensitive to salt,,,,thus what I write relative to the relative saltiness of something should in fact be taken with a grain of salt. The food is very nearly free...and can be free if you run really fast. Superb value...yup...in a neighborhood that is/would be of concern to yelpers out of the safety of the 465...however...everyone you meet in line will be delightful ! If you can talk them out of it....get as much of their BBQ sauce as possible and use it on everything....like ice cream. They really should bottle the stuff and sell it....although in a desalinated version :) These fine folks will also make things not on the menu with sufficient notice. Don't forget a Ginger Beer,..as this really compliments the food !

You can't like Indian food and not try Ekta...it's some of the best food I've had including the stuff in India. Can't go wrong with anything, but the chicken tikka masala is a classic and the mango lassi is surreal. If I'm wrong you can send me an angry message!

Thai Legacy rocks!! We were so grateful to be accommodated on such a short notice since we had a bigger party and it was so surprising to be presented with the all-vegan menus. We were treated so hospitably and everyone there was so sweet. I can't wait to come back and save room for dessert the next time! Truly a gem of Brandon, I wish them all the best!

Love the pad thai, spouse loves the masaman curry. I don't think the prices are any worse than any other in the area, certainly not more. The thai iced tea is a fun alternative to ice cream in the summer. The ambiance is romantic and cute. The quarters are a little close since the restaurant is so small. Vegetarian options in addition to meat options. BYO

Went here on a whim while waiting at the hospital and was glad to have found it! Very fast and affordable food served in a cute and clean storefront. The staff were all incredibly friendly and the food hit the spot, offering many selections for vegetarians, vegans and those who go gluten free. The complimentary water was a plus for someone like me who goes overboard on the spice! Definitely recommended for those looking for well priced food, some pretty good Indian cuisine or for those with dietary restrictions!

I am always happy with this place. Clean, the staff are very friendly. Great place to have lunch at an affordable price.. I usually like the shrimp and fried rice plates and pot stickers. awesome. I highly recommend this place.
Its so good!! I am definitely going back and if I need to have a party catered. This is the place to go!

Favorite Indian food Northside Indy. Very good chicken dishes and salmon dish is Delicious! Great portion sizes make for great leftovers. Good prices too, Only thing preventing 5 stars has been sporadic service. Sometimes in our 3-4 visits has been quick and friendly and another was slow and server would forget we asked for something. Food quality and taste will bring us back tho...
Delicious food. Amazing atmosphere. You need to go here every chance you get. Try the drunken noodles.

We were very disappointed with our meal this evening. I thought about this review before writing it. If Yelp wasn't an option , I think I would have spoken up at the restaurant. My daughter and I were seated promptly by a friendly host. The decor is modern, clean and inviting . After placing our drink order , we asked for the crab nachos. The chips served with the appetizer were hard and stale and the crab dip was cold and flavorless . Our main course was a pub burger and tuna tacos. The tuna tacos were not seasoned and the tortilla was stale. I did not eat the entree and the server did not ask if I enjoyed it. The burger was way over cooked fries were decent and served in a cute take our box. We decided dessert would probably redeem the experience, but after perusing the options we skipped it. There was music advertised to start at 7pm and it started at 8:30, right as we received our check. After work on a Friday night , I am easily impressed. Didn't have to cook or clean up, that is usually worth 3 stars right there!! Wish I could have shared a better view of the place.

My rating is not based on the food available at Taste of india. If you can handle horrible service from a lady who doesn't seem mildly interested in her customers, this might be your spot. They have the best dishes in the area but are rude beyond belief. I've been seated while the server is talking on a cell phone, hung up on while ordering takeout, yelled at while ordering take out & and am so glad I live in a new area that does not have these problems.

This place is Amazing! The atmosphere is lovely. Its quite a small place but its very well ran by the owners. Service was phenomenal, waitress never let us ran out of water. Food was on time and it was super tasty! The pad thai is a must! So good i cant even put into words! Thank you jesus for this amazing restaurant! Amen!

This place is amazing! They have a vegan menu and non vegan menu. The staff is super friendly and quick. I felt welcomed from the first moment I walked in. The vegan food is amazing and I will definitely be going again. This is def my go to for thai food.

Oddly the same Vietnamese song was played over and over and over during our recent visit at Pho 36. But, that did nothing to mar our dining experience. This place is wonderful. The service is good and their pho and banh mi and spring rolls are great. The Vietnamese chicken wings are delicious but really sticky & messy. And sticky. And, the prices are incredibly reasonable. Huge bowls of Pho for $7.99 and large banh mi sandwiches for $3.50. Dang.

We had the seafood Scannichios on spicy red sauce it costs$27 good for 2 people the gravy / vino it was cooked at was sweepable by the bread, so good. The Manigot! (Manicotti) was a homerun the ragu was divine it was not overpowering and tasted fresh clearly not thecanned kind. The set up of the place was really homey Italian.

This was my second visit to Zac's. First one was fine, the ​second one not so much. Walked​ in on Sunday around noon, waited in line for 10 minutes to be seated, must have been 5-6 empty tables dirty, no one was clearing them off. ​The whole time we were in line, food was stacking up to be served under the lamps. I would say at least 10 plates, meanwhile,​ then waitress​ were chatting​ in the corner​ while the food grew cold. We continued​ to wait for a ​booth, meanwhile,​ people behind us were leaving saying the service was better at McDonald's​​, they were on there way there. We were finally shown a booth and the waitress​ never came over, still in the corner chatting with more food being piled up. Zac's has really gone downhill with service. Also,​ the ladies room was out of service. At that point wasting​ a half an​ hour to be seated we left, as well as other customers. Mj

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Unexpected excellence! We had the Seaweed salad, miso soup, rock shrimp, spicy maki combo, the daily special crazy spider roll, and the waitress-recommended chestnut roll, and because we were hungry, added the shrimp mei fun. Everything was so good! We brought our own wine (an Albariño). The mei fun had fresh crunchy bean sprouts, the specialty rolls were fabulous. Generous amounts of ginger and wasabi. And we brought home half the mei fun, and half of both specialty rolls. We devoured and tried everything else. I wish I could get more of the seaweed salad! Pleasant atmosphere. Thank you with kudos to the chef.

The wife loves to go here for the weekend lunch buffet and I don't mind a bit. There are usually many Indian patrons; always a good sign. Plenty of variety and everything is fresh and cooked appropriately. If you are near the KOP malls, it will take you about 5 minutes to get there. It's located in a plaza so there is plenty of parking. It's a nice change from the joints surrounding the mall.

Really good food chain when you want some middle eastern. Better than a small family run restaurant? No. but worth it yes. The falafel is very good and the spices and assembly are well done and easily worth the reasonable cost. The schwarma was decent. The pita is just ok. The ambiance is clean, friendly, and welcoming. Very busy for lunch. I plan on returning soon.

I ordered a meal with grilled shrimp, beef and pork over rice and spring rolls. Spring rolls are okay. But when i saw the grilled meal, i was surprised by how little meat was in there! Three shrimps and a few cuts of pork and beef for $14+! They just filled it with lots of lettuce, carrots and rice! I am giving this 2 stars just because i got my order on the time that i indicated and because of the "okay" spring rolls and that's it. I would not order from here again. So disappointed.
It's so wonderful to eat somewhere where the owners care as much about their customers as they do at Taste of India. The woman who runs it is fantastic and their food is great!
Terrible Service for delivery order took nearly 2 hours to complete and I live only 7 miles away...No excuse I cancelled the order and will never eat here. I have no opinion on the food.
Although the price range is not cheap, the portion is pretty generous (i had Pad-thai to go). The taste is pretty good.

We woke up late but still hungry for breakfast. BluePlate showed up on Yelp so we eased there. We expected them to have breakfast, but they had better! We had the lobster Reuben and the crab melt. They were so good we couldn't take pictures for the review! Compliments to the chef! I'm not religious, but god bless the chef.

Came here again and was surprised to find that they had fixed their broth! It was significantly beefier and not covered up with pepper, giving it a much simpler and savory flavor. I also ordered the vermicelli bowl with egg roll and pork (bun cha goi thit nuong) and it was delicious! A pretty good blend of noodles, lettuce, cucumbers, and a good portion of meat drenched in slightly sweet and tangy fish sauce. This place just gets better and better!

We had tried take away from Jaipur once, we kinda like the taste but were suprised that they give only 1 rice whether you take one or 5 dishes. Damn expensive. We then thought of trying their lunch buffet and this time we were prepared for high price but we got SHOCK OF OUR LIFE to see pathetic food taste, there were very limited dishes and quantity of those dishes was also like only 4-5 people could eat, which clearly indicates that even the restaurant people DO NOT EXPECT CUSTOMERS. Only thing good about that place is lonliness. IF YOU HAVE MONEY TO WASTE PLEASE DO VISIT

I have only had foo from Desi Village a few times while here on different trips. The service is always good. When I have it delivered they are good at getting it here as soon as they can. The food I have never had a problem with. It has always been good.
This place is awesome. Cool atmosphere, art, and delicious food. Make sure you try the hot sauce, or 'skhug' on your eggs. It's so good with that. Stay cool La Va

Great service, our server was very nice and accommodating (I wish I got her name, but forgot to ask). We always order a lot when we go out for Indian so we have leftovers - and we're kind of picky (one meat eater, one vegetarian) so I wouldn't say we are the easiest table for a server. We're kind of needy and annoying. But she was very sweet and patient. We had our 7 month old baby with us who is new(ish) to food and I was looking forward to her trying a bit of yellow dal. The server let us order kind of a "side portion" (which isn't on the menu) and made sure the kitchen knew it was for a baby. I, of course, know it's something she's allowed to eat and would have made been cautious of any unpredictable spices or large pieces, but it was so nice for the server to do that for me without my even asking. The food is fine. We ordered several entrees to share and the table all enjoyed the shrimp biryani the most. They also serve onion chutney (generally a hit or miss). I like it and was glad to have it. Decent food paired with incredibly thoughtful service gets it four stars

Fantastic Lebanese brunch!! Charming interior - there is a pastry and coffee stand when you walk in where you can grab and go. In that same room, you can find all sorts of trinkets, including sauces, teas, ceramics, clothing for purchase. As you enter the restaurant, there is a bar area, plenty of tables and an open kitchen. Waiters walk around in tan T-shirts that read Suraya, Yalla, or Habibi on them - super cute and was tempted to buy one for myself! Everything from the lighting to the decor and music felt very authentic. As for the food, the menu is super interesting. I was unfamiliar with many of the items on the menu, but quickly learned that you can't really go wrong with anything you order. We ordered the pastry basket to share - the cruller was my personal favorite! Then we ordered the baba ganoush, man'oushe with zatar, cheese and egg, sish taouk, and beet salad with falafel. Super tasty, creative presentation and great service! The hairblended drink coffee was also delicious with hints of citrus and dark chocolate. Excited to come back and check Suraya out for dinner sometime!

Went for lunch and found it very well priced and filling. The buffet is well worth the money and you don't get the sense that the waiters are trying to shoo you out of the buffet. Sometimes that's what I felt like in New Delhi and Sitar which are very similar restaurants in the area.
My yellow curry at hotness #2 was perfect size and spice. It came out quickly. It wad a good portion size. The place is cute, but can get loud or hard to get a table at lunch.

Oh my! What a hidden gem this place is. Our friends live a block away and we are very jealous. This is a seafood lovers dream! We went on a Friday night around 8:30 and it only had a couple people there. We a table of 4 got sat immediately. This is a BYOB place so we brought two bottles of wine. We reviewed the very simple menu and decided to get the start with the Greek salad. It was tasty and easily shareable between 4 people. We then got the shrimp pil pil, meatballs and octopus as the appetizer. The octopus tasted like chicken! It was so good. The shrimp was slightly spicy with some sweet red pepper sauce. The meatballs were good, a little too much filling but tasty. For the main course we got the lamb, seafood combo, bronzino fish and of course the soft shell crab special. The lamb was succulent and juicy, the fish was soft and flavorful. The seafood combo was good. It had muscles clams and tilapia. The soft shell crab was perfect. Our meal all in came to $156. Not bad. Most dishes are $20. Highly recommend! Bring some friends.
When I visit Nashville and have a taste for Indian food this is the place to go. Good food, nice people and the best Biryani in Nashville. Chicken 65 is close 2nd to the Biryani.

A friend recommended Spice-n-Grill to me as a hole in the wall on Olive that puts out fantastic Indian/Pakistani cuisine. He wasn't lying - its no-frills home style cooking does set it apart, even on Olive Blvd. The food was the highlight of the visit. The Lamb Nihari and Goat Pishwari we ordered were both delicately spiced and rich without being overwhelming. The portion size was just right when paired with their plain rice, naan and chappati. Although I wouldn't recommend the naan, the chappati really stood out and I wished I had thought to use it to finish off the curry sauce. Drink options were scant: it would have been nice to have wine or beer, but the homemade chai tea was just what I needed on the cold, snowy night. Spice-n-Grill is built as a take-out spot. Dining in was pleasant, but the high ceilings, bright fluorescent lights and lack of any sort of ambiance were hard to appreciate. We were nearly the only customers all Friday night, so we got to enjoy the full attention of the owner, deeply passionate about his food and eager to help undecided guests with recommendations. Save the stark white walls and strip mall setup, it felt like we were guests at his house. With very reasonable prices, Spice-n-Grill is a no-brainer for delicious Indian/Pakistani take-out on Olive. I'll be back with friends and I hope they work on the eat-in experience in the meantime.

Let's be honest for a second: long distance relationships suck. So, when my boyfriend came to town this weekend, I wanted to take him somewhere amazing! Having visited Thailand this past summer, my standards are pretty high now whenever I'm on the hunt for good Thai food. This place honestly hits the nail on the head. First of all, I love the decor inside--it's super peaceful and cozy, and very intimate, without being stuffy. Most importantly, the food is amazing. We started off with the Veggie Spring Rolls, which were awesome. I hate it when spring rolls get too mushy. These had the perfect amount of crunch! For the main course, I ordered the Chicken Pad Thai (always a crowd favorite) and my other half got the Drunken Noodles. By far the best Thai I've had on the Main Line. The presentation was beautiful. Our waiter was also marvelous. He removed our appetizer right as we were finishing up and brought our entrées out immediately after. He was very attentive and even cracked a few jokes with us. I wish I could remember his name; we gave him a great tip. Siamese Princess helped me have a truly warm and happy reunion with my boyfriend. I will definitely be back! I might even bring my parents here when they come to town next week.

Excellent, if not unique, Mediterranean option, inspired by the owner's Bosnian roots. The food is hearty and delicious. I ordered the beef Cevapi (pronounced cha-vopy) and it was excellent. It's plenty filling, but a little sparse, so it goes well with the red pepper spread. Support Nashville's international community and enjoy a delicious meal while you're at it! Highly recommend!
So good! Love this place from top to bottom. Bento box is on point, thai tea is wonderful, and chicken wings are to die for!! Favorite place in Nashville thus far.

One of my favorite lunch spots. The Hungry Greek has tasty, quick and healthy food options. The line typically isn't long and moves quite quickly. I usually get a pita sandwich but on my last visit I got a greek salad (veggie style loaded with beets, olives, peppers, onions, tomatoes and letruce. The greek salad comes with potato salad in the middle of the plate - an interesting and yummy addition. The staff are cool and friendly. I recommend this joint.

I have had take out twice and dine in once at that tanic. The decor of the restaurant is very nice with hard wood floors, subdued lighting, nice booths, and vine type plants on the ceiling. There take out service is very good, quick, hot, no mistakes. Lunch special portions are huge for the price. The food: cashew chicken: excellent flavor, good alterative to the usual gloopy brown sauce. chicken noodles: too light on flavor, cooked well, chicken was good green curry: my fav thai dish, not sure if they just messed this batch up but it was way too heavy on the coconut and too light on flavor. the vegetables were very fresh however. red curry: better than the green curry, much spicier than the green curry which is odd. Still a bit thick and heavy with coconut milk, i realize its the base of the sauce, but the proper balance should exist. spicy basil noodles: light but nice flavor, lots of fresh basil, a nice dish wonton soup: i was loving it with the broth, glass noodles, fresh veggies and plentiful dumplings, unfortunately, the dumplings were stuffed with a weird green onion dough type thing, eek Overall, the food quality is average, some dishes are above average, some are below. They seem quite good with their more chinese dishes (cashew chicken, chicken with broccoli) but still have not mastered the thai curry--which is very important! I hope the restaurant stays around b/c its a nice place to go and hopefully their curries will improve in quality. I'm not sure it will though as I went on a sunday night at 7 and NOBODY was there...

The plantains are addictive and always sweet! Jolliof rice is my favorite and they make it Great! The place is never really busy on the inside but people are always ordering takeout! This place is definitely a gem!
Amazing place we have great experience there food wow no words, definitely we are coming back ‍

Yelped helped us find this Thai restaurant and the food was good. The best meal we had was the Shrimp Curry. It was a red curry and really very tasty. We had two other things and they were not as memorable. The atmosphere is nice and the service was great.

Was looking for a place close to the turnpike to stop and grab breakfast during a road trip and was happily surprised with this place. Not only were we able to sit at the bar immediately on a decently busy Sunday morning but we also got our food quickly. Great food and excellent service. Also had a good amount of gluten free options.
Great food and great customer service! My personal favorite is their Vietnamese pork BBQ with rice! two thumbs up!!!!
Wonderful, wonderful food! I had the roti, samosa, and chana masla and everything was so delicious. The staff was very friendly and inviting. I will definitely be back.
Stopped in with a friend. The staff was amazing and very attentive. I ordered the Chicken Biryani and was very happy with my order. I will be back there again.

Ok. Food is tasty, but service is woefully slow. Prices are ok for what you get. Coconut rice is sweet and creamy. Chicken curry, regular spice, was good. Lots of rice with it, but not much plaintain. Cabbage was meh.

I came here because of the great food reviews. I loved the wood carvings in the tables, that was really cool to look at. I ordered the Pad Se-Ew and it was good. Not the best I've had, but still delicious. They used regular broccoli instead of chinese broccoli or bok choy. Would definitely go back, but not at the top of my list again.

So. I was driving through the mall thinking I'd hit up QDoba when I saw Noodles and Company and figured I'd give it a try for the first time. Well. I went in with little to no expecations and came out blown away. First of all, it's kind of like a fast food style place where you order your food at the front and wait for it while they are cooking. However, you go sit down and they bring your food out to you. I've tried almost everything on their menu and I now only get a large Thai Curry soup and a large Indonesian Peanut Saute with breaded chicken breast. The thai curry soup is a curry flavored soup with noodles and fresh vegetables. The thing that I love about this place is that all of the stuff that they use is fresh. The soup has fresh tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, spinach leaves all soaked into the soup. It is delicious. The soup alone could fill most people. I am not most people. The indonesian peanut saute is a spicier dish than what you would find on the menu which is good because I like a little more kick to it. They do sprinkle some crumbled up peanuts over the noodles and they have some sort of spicy peanut sauce that goes well with the rice noodles. They also throw in some brocoli, sliced carrots, cabbage and asian sprouts which are all extremely fresh. These two dishes are what I miss most when I had to move from St. Louis to Texas. Well. The pad thai isn't exactly their best dish. I had it once and never got it again. The Pesto cavatappi with grilled chicken is delicious as well. I would sometimes change up the indonesian peanut saute with either this dish, the penne rosa or the japanese pan noodles. I have tried the asian chop salad but that wasn't anything spectacular. The tomato basil bisque is also good but not as good as the thai curry soup. They also have some fried dumplings as appetizers but I have had better dumplings at non-asian restaurants. Wouldn't suggest getting these. When you order your noodles, you can customize the meats that you put on. You can either get grilled chicken, breaded chicken (parmesian crusted chicken breast is what it's called on the menu), slices of beef or shrimp. I kept raving about Noodles and Company to my coworkers (especially the thai curry soup and the indonesian peanut saute) that they finally went there and fell in love. They absolutely loved the indonesian peanut saute and how fresh the vegetables are.
The avocado citrus and steamed seafood were amazing and the cooks prepared the food in front of us. Definitely go on a week night when it is less crowded!

My favorite Thai restaurant. Standard Thai food, great taste and cheap. I used to go all the way to Thai Pepper(I think now called Flavors) in Wayne, which was expensive and more upscale. But the food taste at Thai Place definitely beats Thai Pepper any day.

I've been coming to Dmitris for years now. It was one of my first experiences with BYOBs before they became de rigueur in the restaurant scene in Philly. This place never fails to meet expectations. If you like fresh seafood that is simply prepared in a relaxed and noisy atmosphere then Dmitri's is the place for you. The menu is limited and I think they had "small plates" kinda like tapas style before it was made famous by Jose Garces. If you like quiet restaurants with formal service and cloth napkins then I wouldn't recommend Dmitris. To really enjoy this place you have to expect that there will be a wait for your table sometimes 10 minutes or sometimes over an hour all dependent on what time of day and what day of the week you choose to go because they don't reservations. But if you go with this in mind and are willing to wait either on the benches outside or across the street at New Wave then you're ahead of the game. Whenever I eat here I always order the mussels sauteed (I think they're actually lightly floured and then pan fried), the grilled octopus, the shrimp scampi and the baba ganoush from the small plates section and then typically we'll order a platter to share. You can rarely go wrong if you choose one of the specials for the night. I also love the endless grilled pita they give you dipped in the oil that's left over from the shrimp scampi. It's garlicky goodness :) The next time you're in the mood for some fresh seafood bring your favorite bottle of wine or beer, bring a few friends and check this place out.

This is definitely my favourite spot for Thai food in all of Nashville. I will gladly drive off the East side (a feat for many an East Nashvillian) past a couple of other popular Thai restaurants just to enjoy Siam Cafe. As its been mentioned, the aesthetic is not necessarily on the cutting edge of restaurant interior design. Frankly, so what. If you're worried about matching decor you can always stand in line at a Pei Wei. I have always found the service to be exceptionally friendly, prompt and accurate. Most importantly, the food is excellent! The curries are all delicious and filling, but don't leave you feeling stuffed. The duck dish is fantastic, probably a new favourite. Most of all their Pad Thai is bang on. When trying out a new Thai restaurant, Pad Thai is the gold standard by which I judge the establishment. Like I said, bang on. I love Siam Cafe, if there were a tee shirt that said so, I would wear it.

It's so refreshing to have a place to get a quick dinner/takeout that doesn't cook with harmful and inflammatory vegetable oils. I LOVE the Whole30 options! The service here is always excellent, the establishment is always clean and the food is always tasty.

Harry-West Chester, Pa. Visit Delran, NJ every 12 months (put Christmas decorations on family graves in nearby Riverside) and always stop at Turkish Market on drive home. Miss seeing the old WWII tank out front, but love the new Four Seasons Market, especially the baked goods. The hand made turkish cookies and pastries are "to die for" delicious. Not overly sweet and filled with fresh fruits baked to perfection. At $8 lb-order a variety and enjoy the diverse flavors with your tea. Darn shame Christmas only comes once a year. Enjoy 5*****

I never knew they had a fast food place for my favorite meal: PASTA! Stumbled upon this gem a couple of weeks ago and my bowl was at the table before I could even fill my drink (great when you only have an hour or less for lunch)! My entire meal was about $8 or so and it was on par with the Olive Garden (who cares if it's a chain, it's still good in my opinion). And don't even get me started on their rewards system! I had two rewards in my inbox upon sign up AND feel like I get a new one every time I go! I can not believe I'd never heard of this restaurant chain before, but it's already a staple lunch destination. Give it a shot!
India Palace is back on top of the Indian food game in centers Indianapolis. Absolutely love the renovations and atmosphere inside! Keep up the great work!!

This is a Drexel landmark. If you are on campus during a week day that is not Monday you MUST COME HERE. I have had pretty much everything on the menu, but now I order pretty much solely the captain crunch tilapia burrito, extra spicy. I sadly only get the have this once every few months these days after moving out of West Philly, but just had it last week and it continues to be the best lunch of campus, by far. Do yourself a favor and stop by CZ.

My kids and I are big fans of really good Indian food, but having moved away from our favorite place we were totally out of luck. Until Spice Kitchen opened up in trooper. We do the lunch buffet, for $10 and kids eat free you can't beat the price and the food is fantastic. The Naan is always hot and fresh, and there are always multiple chicken entrees that vary in spice to suit everyone. My son loves a kick and is a huge fan of lemon chicken while I have a more reserved palate and love the chicken makhani. I have seen goat on the buffet and of course several veggie options. There is always a soup and few desserts including fresh fruit. I love that they keep smaller amounts of food on the buffet and refresh them constantly. And my five year old says they have the best mango lassi he has ever had. The staff, especially Grover is polite and attentive, your water glass will never be empty!
This is the best Thai restaurant in the world! The shrimp pad Thai is really good.
Wonderful restaurant. Authentic and fresh food Wide variety of options (lunch buffet), spicy and well flavored. clean restaurant.

The beef was not good there last night. We ordered the beef salad. The beef was very hard and when I are it without the other ingredients and dressing, it tasted horrible. It was either an old piece of beef or it was not stored properly. Disappointing.
Really good fried chicken and mac & cheese. Also a fan of the biscuits. Can't eat it too often because it's so unhealthy, but like it when I do. Only issue is that it's a bit expensive.
Recently moved nearby, and I must say, this place was really great! Friendly waitstaff and the food was delicious, I definitely can't wait to go back.

My husband and I love this place. The food is so fresh, consistant, there are tons of options for everyone, and the owner is super sweet. Oh! And they have a patio where you can bring your dog. Can't say enough great things!

What a charming place! Kind staff, interesting menu items, and a great ambiance inside. Almost every menu item has meat, though, so vegetarians will starve. Also, the juices look so good from the counter, but I think they're just Hawaiian Punch--so sweet my teeth hurt. But other than those two things, a really great experience.

They pack 'em in here at Dmitri's but it's worth the tight quarters and the wait; grab a drink at the bar across the street (New Wave Cafe) and the waitress will come and get you when a table opens up. My wife and I arrived just after 9 on a Friday and ended up spending a half-hour waiting across the street. It's worth it though. We ordered the grilled octopus, which seemed to be a must based on the reviews here. It was so-so..good grill flavor and swimming in olive oil & vinegar. It seemed a bit too tough and hard to cut with the dull knives...maybe it was tougher & dried out because this order was later in the night? I'll have to go back and try it again to see if it was a fluke. The smelts were delicious...lightly dusted and fried crisp, it was like seafood french fries. Just as good as fried anchovies at Amada. The portions here are on the gargantuan size. My wife witnessed the table behind us received a pile of feta cheese blocks the size of a small brick. We split the lamb entree. Roasted, sliced and grilled, the lamb was full of char-flavor...only regret was the lack of decent knife to slice it with. The lamb rested on a bed of roasted peppers and was served with a cucumber-yogurt sauce that smoothed out the intense smoky flavor of the grill. The warm olive oil drizzle greens and rice was a decent & simple side. See my pics of the dishes above. Service was friendly and fast. Great night out for under $45...this is a BYOB that's cash only...and if you're ordering the lamb, make sure you BYOK...Knife!
Awesome lamb saag. I wish that we had (affordable) Indian food like this in Sacramento!

I've been going to Noodi Thai for hangouts with friends frequently since moving to this area. They are a great place for dinner or lunch, but I must say, you can't beat their lunch special which is basically the right amount of food for a perfect and reasonable price. I love being able to get any combination of an appetizer, soup, and entree or two appetizers and an entree if I wanted to mix it up. My favorite soup is the Tom Kha, and appetizer is the moon dumpling. I used to get the Pad Se Ew as my regular meal, but a few months ago they changed their recipe and now the sauce is too sweet! Change it back! As a result I now get the drunken noodle which is good, but not my favorite, or a fried rice dish. I recently took a friend who has dietary restrictions that are more than mine and they were able to make her order as she asked and the service was swift and punctual. Love this place.
I had the turkey chiabatta sandwich with a side of fruit .thus was hands down one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. The service was great I highly recommend it!

OK the only downfall here was a bit of lackluster service. Thats the 1 star deduction. Now for the main event....The food. If I went to some of my Indian friends houses and their Mom cooked for us, this is what I expect it to taste like. I felt like Mom was in the kitchen serving up recipes she has been making for years, and her mother before and so on. The samosas were crunchy and spicy and warm and a great start. The chicken Korma was creamy and spicy apnd all what sauce didnt get mixed with the wonderful basmati rice got sopped up by the pillowy garlic Naan bread. Nothing says good Indian food like a case of the headsweats. This little place is nestled at the end of State near Orange. Make the trek, take a couple extra steps and get here to fulfill that next craving.

Love this place! The atmosphere is great.. we sat outside on their "patio" and it was perfect for a chill summer night. The order system is easy and fluid. I had the tzaziki (?) dip with the pita and it tasted fresh and delicious. Next time I'll get the spicy dip so see which I like better! Make sure you get the greek yogurt topped with baklava.. that stuff was SO GOOD. Excited to go back and get a beer and try the grilled octopus and hang in the back with some friends!
Serving time was awefully long and food too expensive for portion! Wouldn't recommend

I'm in from out of town and it was freezing outside so I got delivery. The gentleman who delivered the food was absolutely professional kind and sweet. Best crab Rangoon I I've ever had the Edamame was delicious. the only thing I would change is I got shrimp with broccoli and asked for extra spicy I wish when you asked for extra spicy in addition they would add the spice on the side. there's never enough and I fear they feel if we asked for extra spicy don't make it too spicy. It's never too spicy for me so add to the side next time. Otherwise great service great food I would definitely order here again thank you

This is one of our favorite Chinese/Vietnamese restaurants here in Reno. The delicious wonton soup is fresh and the broth is light but full of depth! You should try the egg drop soup! They are very friendly and remember us every time. We've ate there at least eight times in the last year. All their soups are expertly made, and their entrees are fantastic. Try their walnut shrimp, it is light and crispy with a sweet creamy sauce. I highly recommend this quality restaurant. They are busy, but we've always been able to be seated right away. The chef is truly talented.

Naan bread sandwich, pizza or a bowl. Wow! Terrific. I had Masala lamb with tiki masala sauce tomato pickled onion green pepper NaanPizza. Washed down with a Leinenkugel to wash it down. YUM!! My 2 vegan sons loved it too (25,20). My third had a yummy chicken NanPizza. Very popular place

I can't say enough good things about this place. The bread is so tasty, soft and fluffy on the inside and perfectly crunchy on the outside. I get the vegetarian ham or veggie ham spring rolls. I usually go in for the boba teas, though. I love the boba green tea; as the name suggests, it's your typical green tea, but with delicious boba in it! I highly recommend the strawberry banana boba smoothie, I think it's their best drink on the menu. The waitstaff is very friendly too!
