The food here is hot, fresh, and not that expensive but it's different from authentic Indian food. Perhaps because of all the gluten-free stuff. Tastes are different than what I'm used to but that happens at almost any Indian restaurant. Or it may have something do with them not using butter or ghee. The naan is also not their own I'm pretty sure. It looks like the frozen kind. I'll still come back every now and then, but only in a group. If it's up to me I'll always pick something else. Not a lot of seats here so the place can fill up fast during lunch. I did like that the samosas were big but they only had 1 type of chutney and I'm a spicy-mint chutney kind of guy, otherwise I can never really enjoy my samosa experience. If you absolutely must have Indian food and don't want to venture out to University city or even a little farther into Center City, then this is an okay spot. When I go out for Indian food, taste is what I am looking for above all else. Other people may really like this place since they are gluten/butter/ghee free. I'm just not one of them. I can't really comment on the service because you serve yourself here. The best thing about this place is that it's consistent and managed well, but other than that, I can't say that this place really impresses me. When it comes to Indian food there are a huge number of recipes for any one dish. It might be a good idea for them to try a few different ones for each and see if they fare any better.

Admittedly, the idea of hipster-themed fried chicken isn't exactly my bag, but this spot did the job. The chicken was pretty good, but the natural soda Spo had was even better. A larger menu would be nice (MORE SIDE DISHES!), but I felt like this was more of a specialty restaurant than one trying to appeal to many.

OK we need to talk about how good these gyros are. They taste as good as the ones I've had in reputable Little Athens-es around the continent! The one thing that irritates me in fast food are bad tomatoes. This place uses legit tomatoes. The bread is fantastic as well. what I would love is if they added some fries to their menu for the combos. Nothing goes better with gyros than some Greek fries.

Went here for the lunch buffet. Never had Indian food so I thought I could try a variety to see what I liked. I was alittle concerned with the quality, being a buffet and my first time. The buffet was good. It was smaller quantities, so the quality wasn't sacrificed. I was able to try a variety and wasn't disappointed. I'm glad I stopped by here to try it. I don't know the names of the dishes but the dish that I called "the yellow stuff" (a yellowish sauce) was awesome. We walked in right when it opened and they were still setting up the buffet. We aren't approached to ask for our drink order until they were completely done setting up the buffet, which was roughly 10 minutes after walking in. Other the that, nice small place, and service was fine after the initial short wait. I'll recommend this.

Got chicken tikka masala & garlic naan! Delivery was super quick which is a huge plus. (We ordered online). The masala was a tad too tomato-y/soupy for my taste, but was delicious nonetheless. The masala includes green peppers and nice portions of white chicken w/ jasmine rice. The size of the masala itself was really surprising as well, I think its the largest delivery serving I've gotten from an Indian place so far!

First visit last week (Sat. lunch) & I was pleasantly surprised! The ordering process was not confusing at all-order, sit, get your food, pay when you finish. The inside was much nicer than I thought it would be (from the pics here). Food was made to order and the staff were kind, responsive, and quick. (Also I don't know if the staff is different than those in other reviews, but the staff all spoke perfect English, were polite, & professional.) Food portions were generous, my meal was very tasty (every one came with a salad, but the dressing was a little strong for my tastes), & they have several different kinds of breads that you can get (the garlic knots were good & they had a pita w/veggies that I'll be getting another time). The falafel was the best surprise! Usually I find it dry & bland, but theirs was super tasty. Had the gyro plate with rice, & the kabob plate with potatoes, which were nice and flavorful. They also had some nice desserts-the chocolate mousse cake & the baklava were both good. I'll definitely be visiting again! :)

Me and a gal friend moved away from Delaware but were back in town and wanted to try a new and good restaurant for a girls dinner. We had heard great things about 8th & Union and the asian fusion/gastropub menu looked DELISH, so we made a reservation and came in. We started with original cocktails that were flavorful and unique. Next were appetizers for dumplings, calamari, and summer rolls - all great! And the munchie popcorn - addictive seasoning! Dinner was 2 kinds of phó, a burger, and I got the chicken/shrimp pad thai. One girl that got phó was a first-timer and LOVED it! All of our dishes were well prepared and flavorful. The restaurant has outdoor seating which i'm sure is great for social outings. Definitely check out this place - THANK GOODNESS Wilmington has a new unique dining option instead of the same-ole boring stuff. *Plus they have quite a few gluten-free options!!
This is a restaurant that has good food but terrible service. It caters to Asians only. I have never been treated so badly at a restaurant . Be aware

I was surprised to see so many good reviews. Not many options on the lunch buffet n Indians will not appreciate the Flavors. Definitely not. But I can understand why Americans like it- all curries r creamy n saucy (even which r not supposed to be).

I bought a groupon for iLuv Pho not knowing what to expect because the name and overall outer appearance of the place looks a little sketchy. But the food was quite good! I ordered Pho and my friend ordered the shrimp fried rice and we both left feeling very satisfied with no complaints. It was also my first time ordering coconut Boba and I will definitely want to try all the different flavors they have.

I've eaten here quite a few times now, and every time I have been extremely pleased with the service and quality. Today I ordered the sweet potato chicken curry with rice, and it was possibly the best food truck lunch I have ever had. Rich and flavorful, but not oily or overly salty. A dish with a good level of spice, deep color, and eye pleasing presentation all served piping hot. I'm always surprised when I get gourmet food for 5$ in a back alley from a hand painted van. I got lucky, as my order of curry was the last one, so go early if you don't want to risk food selling out. Also great - tilapia taco, fresh thai iced tea and coffee, and thai tacos People's choice award winner at this year's Phiadelphia Vendy's as well!

I like this place. It's a no frills establishment that leaves you feeling as if you shortchanged the person who made your sandwich...actually sandwiches as I can't imagine leaving there without at least two in hand. These things are so good, and the price makes it even better. I also like how you're forced into either trying to not make eye contact with the lady shelling pistachios or the few people in line ahead of you, and debating on whether or not to try that can of whatever isn't an American soft drink in the cooler.
Does not even deserve 1 star. Had lunch today during my short business trip. The buffet was so poor quality that I have hardly had in other Indian restaurants. Will never go there again.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: THE REAL DEAL!!! If you need more than that, I will start with... I have been a chef at a Northern Indian/Pakistani restaurant (Kashmir in Portland mid 80's-90's) and traveled to India twice. I also make a point to sample Indian restaurants anytime I travel (in the hundreds) so I feel qualified. Perfectly balanced spices, we prefer mild when trying out a new place and theirs was great. Just a little bit of heat, but not overwhelming. Fresh and flavorful, good atmosphere and great service. We met the owners after dinner and they seem to really care about their restaurant and it's reputation. Very refreshing find for my first Indian meal in Boise. I will be back!

This Indian restaurant is as good if not better than most of the main line restaurants of its ilk. I suspect that it is not more widely known either because of its admittedly odd name or more likely its off the beaten path location. Nonetheless, the food is well prepared and the quality is top notch. Drop what you're doing and go now.
BBQ pork rice plate tastes good! PHO is good too with no MSG! We ordered togo the sandwich w/ free drink :)

business_name: OPA! of Greece West Edmonton Mall - A
text: Opa! What a great place to grab lunch or dinner if your stuck I'm the mall! They have very fresh and tasty food. You have you choice of meat (beef,chicken,lamb or vegetarian) and then your choice of salad(Greek or caesar). You can rather a combo place with meat, rice, potato, bread and salad or you can get a wrap. Personally I'm a huge fan of the chicken skewer plater. The portions are excellent. Unlike some other places you may go to that when you have completed your meal you're still full, opa! has you begging for mercy. Always full and always satisfied! I love only having to spend $10 on it also! Perfect for a mall employee looking for a healthy meal!

I gotta give this place a BIG 5! I went there for lunch and there was a great variety of foods and everything was fresh. For about eight bucks you can have a quality Indian buffet. The Naan was made fresh and brought to the table. They made plain naan and garlic flavor naan. I like the plain naan best. This place can stand head to head to all of the Indian restaurants that I have been before.

Love Greek/Mediterranean fare, so my lady and I stopped in for lunch. In short; this is to Greek what Mas Tacos is to Mexican. If you like it anglicized, this place is for you, maybe. Great job on the inside. Also has a outside bar and tables out back. Nice. I ordered a lamb gyro and she got chicken. When our server brought our meals to the table, I asked for Sriracha. Apparently I mispronounced it as the not-to-happy-with-her-job server quickly corrected me. No matter. We were hungry. The pita was as big as a big pancake, soft and tasty, but that's where it ended. I had little chunks of burnt....meat....in my pita. Not the shaved lamb on a skewer I've had everywhere else. Her chicken wasn't much better. There are 3 Greek places much better less than a mile away so I wish them luck. They'll probably do well in the East with atmosphere and alcohol, but it won't be because of the food.

I ate here once while visiting. We ordered appetizers since it was in between lunch and dinner. I can't remember what we ordered, but I really liked the Afghan bread. The gentlemen who was serving us was very polite also.

Food = 3 stars. One half extra for the wonderfully precocious little waitress. Good enough for what it is. Very basic fare. Sorta cheap. Etc. Definitely no wow factor though. Make sure you look down or you might miss it.
This is one of the best Indian restaurants. We were driving to Philly stopped to get some quick food. My family loved it and so did I. Wasn't expecting it to be this good and authentic.

My daughter recently moved to the area and this has quickly became our "go to" for lunch. It is a beautiful restaurant with patio, delicious food and great service!! You can not beat their luncheon menu. Go and enjoy!

Our long regional nightmare is over: quality Indian food has arrived in Newtown. We took our family of five there and ordered 6 different items; all of them were great. Staff was very friendly, and very accommodating to small children. We'll be back soon, I'm sure...

I've been a fan of Sen Thai for many years - basically since they first moved to the Locust location. They have now moved to Washington Ave -- which is where we were on Friday night. I must admit, the new location is great for them. It was the busiest I have ever seen. I'll admit, this could be part of the problem with my visit. I've only gotten the Drunken Noodles at this restaurant, for my meal. They are fantastic and I highly recommend it. This time, they brought the spicy back, which was nice. Over the past few years I've noticed this dish was a little bland. The heat is nice. Anyway, the restaurant was busy. The hostess clearly hasn't had to deal with a busy restaurant in a long time. She was all over the place trying to seat us -- would get distracted by some other task. They desperately need to hire a restaurant manager with some experience running a busy establishment. We were seated upstairs -- big mistake. The new location is very loud. Part of the charm of the new location is also a downfall -- all that concrete and brick reflects sound. There's nothing to absorb it. Sitting upstairs made it worse. Our waiter was in over his head. There were maybe 18 people sitting in our area. Three tables, including mine (2 people). The rest were a big party split into two tables (young people table, parents table). We ordered, and waited...and waited. Our meals came out before the appetizers -- well one of the apps. The spicy calamari is delicious btw. We usually get Summer Rolls, but they have been left off the new menu, so we opted for Crab Rangoon -- also delicious. However, the calamari came out about 10 minutes after our main dishes arrived. Timing was off. Was it the kitchen? The waiter? I don't know. I will give Sen Thai one more try. Like I said, I've been a long time customer and REALLY love their Drunken Noodles. I just hope the next time's experience isn't as bad as this most recent one was.

I wandered into Erawan a few months ago for lunch, and was so pleasantly surprised. The place is really elegant, the service is always both efficient and welcoming, and the food is probably the best Thai in the area. I've been slowly working my way through every menu item. Good duck is hard to find. Here's it's boneless, crisp, lean and delicious! I'm definitely hooked. You'll find me in there for lunch every day my errands take me near Chinatown. I'm amazed this place isn't packed. Five stars for atmosphere, service and food!. Great job, Erawan!
Awesome bah mi sandwich! Love oversized Vietnamese iced cold coffee and summer rolls. Next time I would love to try their vermicelli dishes!

Holy Shawarma! I am truly shocked that this place hasn't received the recognition it deserves. Absolutely the best shawarma I've had, hands down, anywhere. There's free fixins for those who like that sort of thing (I'd venture a guess that most people do!) and there's also daily soup specials and each one I've tried thus far have been great. But the shawarma... oh, hold me up. Seriously. I literally just ate and the mere thought of having some shawarma from Pita Pocket is making me ridiculously hungry again.
Excellent Pho! And service was friendly, fast, and very accommodating. Would definitely come back!
Fresh and delicious Indian with a southern touch (India, not US!). The lentil soup is fantastic!
The food in there is good and the price is very cheap ~ but Maybe they should hire more waiter .
Still as good as ever after 20-30 visits. Also, I just realized they are in Arabi, not Chalmette. Don't get it twisted, Arabi is the bomb.

This is one of my favourite restaurants in the city. Family owned and home-style afghani food. To me, it is DELICIOUS! And it's a BYO. While they were moving and creating their new space, I had major withdrawal. I miss them being in Center City (15th/Sansom St), but I still try to go as often as possible. The food isn't spicy (indian spicy), but it's flavourful! My fave is the chicken qurma or the fish kabobs. I love the minty yogurt dressing on the salads. I love the firni, it reminds me of a similar indian dessert.

I gave Kalamata's a try even though I thought it looked like another disappointment waiting for me in a strip mall. Clearly I was horribly horribly wrong, Kalamata's is just fantastic. I'm not a big fan of veggies in general, but their falafel was actually great. My food was not only well-seasoned but tasted really fresh, and the tzatziki I so love to sladder on everything was delicious. Even though it is nestled in one of the many ever populating Green Hills strip malls it actually has a great feel to it, not to mention a really cute seating area. I hear through the grapevine that occasionally they host live music. I didn't think that I would find Greek food that would make me want to come back again in Nashville, but this place is definitely worth trying for the first time and then returning a couple more times.
Absolutely phenomenal. Great food, great service. Wonderful experience. This place is BYOB. Appetizers, soup, and main courses were great. Reservations recommended for dinner.

Went specifically for two drinks,which they were both amazing. One was the Very Berry Mojito and the other the Pomegranate Caipirinha. I ended up ordering the ceviche which was perfect to say the least. My son had the fried snapper with the mango salsa which I could not resist taking a few bites off his plate before proceeding to the rooftop to finish my drink.

Ohh how I loved Nadia's! I miss it alot. The Pineapple Fried rice, Pad Thai and all of their soups and salads were perfectly tasty. Finish it off with fried bananas and call it a day! The atmosphere was kind of kooky, and lunch rush and Sat. nights were downright rowdy because of the relatively tiny interior, but all of which was forgivable because of the food and service. Miss it immensely!
Consistently very good Thai dishes. The bold and spicy Shrimp, Thai fried rice, and fortune bags are delicious. I really enjoy this restaurant.

This place was terrible. We went for the lunch buffet. The rice was old and crunchy. The tandoori chicken had a wierd taste. The other dishes were ok but my wife and I have upset stomachs from something we ate. The naan was pretty good. The restaurant wasn't very clean. We also noticed the waiter setting up a table for the next customers and he reused a water glass from the last customers. I will never go back to Taste of India.

This is one of my favorite pho places. Everyone RAVES about their Banh-mi but no one talks about the Pho and other things. So that's what I'm going to do. I always just get the combo pho and an egg roll. It sets me for a couple days (I mean seriously its a 32oz cup of broth + a bowl of noodles and meat) The only reason it gets 4 stars instead of 5 stars is because they lightly cook the ALL the meat when you get it to go instead of letting you cook it in the broth.... it happens no biggy, just a little less rare than I like things. The Vermicelli noodles are freaking incredible. I LOVE the pork and egg roll combo (grab and extra egg roll or 2 with that. You will thank me later) The best thing about all this, its even better the next day. (I just had yesterdays lunch again today) Also they have a parking lot behind the building on broad. Its a small lot so if you've got a big car it might not be fun if the lot is packed (if its empty its easy)

We had nice experience there we had the 3 courses and portions are perfect. Place is very small and noisey but the food makes up for that seems like if you go there for 5:30 reservation the place is not as noisey since not as many people are there. Definitely worth the visit as the staff and food is top notch. Also prices are very reasonable for a highly rated place as this.

Went here yesterday for takeout and got the lamb tikka masala. I was highly disappointed in that the sauce for the tikka masala just tasted like tomato soup, devoid of any spices or flavor. Even the lamb was tough and tasted old, kind of like you might imagine dog food to taste. I was not impressed and will not be back.

This is, arguably, the best Indian restaurant in Indianapolis and the Midwest. Their Friday night buffet offers a unique offering of indo-Chinese food, vegetarian, and South Indian specialities. Their array of South Indian food is hard to find anywhere in the states, let alone Indy. As someone who is staunchly against buffets, I was highly hesitant but I am very glad I tried it. The prices are incredibly cheap and it was recently remodeled. I highly recommend the masala dosas with coconut chutney and the Hyderabadi curry. The staff is always very quick and accommodating, as well.
An excellent little restaurant. We had the Shwarman and kebabs, they were great. A light healthy and well cooked meal. Excellent balance of ingredients. We will certainly be back.

I tried Taza for the first time tonight. The food was amazing and I cannot wait to go back. The food is authentic and the owners were friendly and welcoming. The Gyro and Mediterranean Salad were awesome. I highly recommend this restaurant.

I recently hosted a Ramadan dinner and had the catering done by Sansom. It was SPECTACULAR. Everyone raved about the chicken kabob and ground beef kabob. In addition to kabob, we had lentil soup (amazing) and lamb and chicken qorma. The owner was kind enough to throw in an eggplant dip (I forget the name) which I could have eaten by the spoon. I think I'm going to apply for a job in their kitchen so I can learn all of their secret recipes. Hands down, the BEST KABOB in Philadelphia.

Spice Kitchen always has lovely food. The ambience could do with a bit of improvement, but the food is terrific. I've never eaten anything bad here! I really enjoyed their food, and the service was good too.
I like Pho. Broth makes the Pho. They have great broth. Wifey and Mom loved the Won-Ton soup and the Pork Chow Mien and Sesame Chicken. We would return again next time we visit Reno.

I came here and had lunch with my mother at 1:00 pm and got the buffet and was blown away at the deliciousness and freshness! They have the best Mushroom Matar and Aloo Bharta I have ever had. The ambiance of the restaurant is cozy and relaxing. It's very clean, the staff were very friendly and polite. In a word: perfecti

This was wonderful! So flavorful. We were visiting from out of town and looking for some delicious food truck food. The owner was so kind and gracious. We had our dogs with us and he gave us water for them. He also gave a very large sample of his fish which was fantastic. His portions are huge! Very yummy. Go find this food truck.

Jessica was really great and professional. I hope their cook would take her as example to present his food better. Lamb meatball and fillet tasted good but sides in dish and presenting was disappointing. Half tomato, few beans and 4 meatball thats it. Mussels were good also, but you dont put lettuce in shepard salad specially if its dead lol. Service was good but kitchen need improve much more...

My husband and I eat at a lot of buffets. While the price is very reasonable, the selection is limited, and quality of the food is average. I'd like to say it is great, but, let's face it, the best food is home cooked.

Quick stop for a gyro and every-so-satisfying! Small little place also turned into grocery store, so it doesn't have to be a sit-down place if you don't want to. Feel free to walk in and order deliciousness to-go. I am not a big fan of red meat so I got the chicken, but my boyfriend got the lamb and he loved it. Definitely going back to try others on the menu!

I was looking for falafel place in KOP from long time.My wait is over. I ate falafel at this place and food is good. Fries are not that good but Falafel was delicious.Giving 4 star because of the quantity I get in my falafel bowl.

I ate at Albasha in Gonzales a few months ago. I had the Mousaka Plate for lunch. It was excellent! I was excited to see there was a location in Metairie as I live in New Orleans. I went there today and had the same luncheon plate. It was not good at all! The Mousaka was very salty and greasy and the Bechamel sauce appeared to be burned. The salad had Ranch dressing...a first for me at a Greek/Lebanon restaurant. I'm glad I went by myself. I would have been embarrassed if I had recommended the place to anyone..

I'm halfway into senior year and finally decided to venture out to Gigi and Big R's side of the intersection one day because they didn't have a line. (Note: They do take a while to cook the meat though.) The food is awesome, but I was blown away by how nice they were! They realized I was new since I was trying to read the menu and gave me (and a few loyal customers who were there) a few different samples. The jerk chicken is super good, but way too spicy for me! I wish their fried chicken wings had more meat on them. The potato salad and cabbage are excellent, and their mac and cheese is the best I've tasted in years! I am currently writing this review while drooling-- I mean, deciding which sides to choose with my platter... The only issue is the price. I've learned to get the $13 large and eat it for 2 meals instead of the $11 medium for 1.5 meals. If you like their sides more than their chicken, you should try the $10 "vegetable" platter that comes with 4 sides and is prepared much faster because you don't have to wait for them to fry the chicken!

Hands down the best Kabobs in town. Meats are always cooked perfect, portions are large. All the dishes I have tried have been good here. Qurma Chalaw Dinner Chicken is my fav! Great desserts & appetizers. Atmosphere is chill and the smell of the grill is wonderful! Staff is friendly and food comes out hot! I have never had a bad meal here.
My family really enjoyed everything we ordered, curry goat, curry chicken and jerk chicken. The kids loved the Mac and cheese and the candied yams. Carolyn is really nice.

West Philadelphia is slowly developing into the new spot for eats. So much so I have almost no interest to eat in Center City anymore considering the prices of most of the restaurants and what you get out of them. But enough of that. Marrakesh Express is simply delicious. Carved out of a small row house, the owner spent nearly six months getting it ready to launch. The interior is simple though tasteful with the walls painted a warm red and yellow combination. There are an assortment of pictures from around Morocco on the wall. The owner was also quite gracious, having taken time to converse with us about his menu as well as about his homeland. Ok, down to brass tax: the food. It's Moroccan so of course we had the tangine, ours was the lamb. Cooked with the meat on the bone, the lamb just melted in your mouth. It was simply ridiculous. Prunes and olives..., it was just really amazing. He even had some Moroccan "puffy bread" which my wife had asked about and he just happen to have a batch made. Apparently it's a back-home specialty or something. Anyway, it was very tasty, making a nice combo of crunchy crust and soft inside to sop up the juices with. We started the meal with the harrira soup [a tomato-based soup with cheapeas, herbs and lentils] - he even gave us extra so I could sample some. Very courteous. I also ordered a sandwich: the lamb ketban, which features leg of lamb that has been marinated in olive oil and herbs overnight and then grilled, tossed on one of Amorosso's buns with olives, onions, the kitchen sink. This thing was AMAZING! I could have eaten three. It also comes with a special sauce. Even the fries were good. We'll be heading back soon to sample the couscous, paella, and baked fish [the owner is from Casablanca which is known for its seafood so we're excited to try the baked fish]. I can't say enough really. It's clean, features a gracious owner and offers up some of the tastiest food you are to find in Philly for sure. This is a MUST-STOP joint. Hours: Mon - Sat: 11:30am - 10pm, Sun: 12pm - 8pm. Side note: all meat is halal as well. :)
Great food, try the dosa! Small and cosy. 2x better than Tiffin for the price and quality. Best if all is the friendly staff there. BYOB and Cash btw.

We work a couple blocks away from here and thought let's give it a try. Over all it was ok. Husband had the Thai tea and he said it was really good and even ordered a second. We shared the chicken curry dumplings - these were nothing special. I had the Ultimate Pad Thai with beef. Ultimate? It was good. I like mine to be a bit more flavorful. We didn't finish any of our food - good size portions - took the rest home. Service was ok but there was only one other table with two people. At 5:30pm there was no waiting. Prices are standard. We probably won't go back - unless Husband craves their tea - there are just too many places to eat in the area that we'd like to try.

We were staying in Treasure Island for the week and stumbled upon a raving review for the Pearl. We were not disappointed! Everything was fabulous- atmosphere, food and service. It was by far the best dining experience of our vacation. Our waiter, Nick, was knowledgeable and friendly and made excellent recommendations for wine, entrees and dessert. We were traveling with my husband's 93 year old grandmother, who has a very limited palate, and they were able to accommodate her and served her a dinner she enjoyed immensely (filet mignon with the sauce on the side and potatoes au gratin). She ate every last bite! I had the Shrimp Provencale, which was phenomenal, my husband had the boullabaise and a lobster bisque to start, and my father-in-law had the duck a'la orange. All dishes were extraordinary! The desserts were also wonderful- we had a selection, including the creme brulee, the berries Melba and the profiteroles. I would very highly recommend this restaurant. If you are in the area, this is a must-visit!
This place was great. Super friendly staff, good ambiance, tasty food. Comida criolla- relleno de papa, maduros, cafe con leche yum.

There was hair in our food. For me, hair can be an indicator of lack of sanitation at the facility where the food was prepared. For people who think this isn't a big deal, please keep in mind that other than all the products that people may put in their hair, strands of hair can also carry staph bacteria which can give your diarrhea or stomach problems. Imagine all that swimming in your broth of pho before you ingest.

Three stars cause afterall this is ethnic dining. Recommended by an Ethiopian medical student of mine. I was extremely excited to find out that there is an Ethiopian restaurant in Indy. Greeted well by the waiter, the place is clean and decorated fairly well. There is a corner with traditional seating with a centre table and low set chairs. The place was pretty empty probably for being a weekday. I ordered the beef sambosa as an appetizer which was great and pretty similar to the Indian samosa. Except I was ticked off at the fact that one piece was for $2.5 which is kind of expensive. I ordered the platter TA2 which comes with a little bit of everything namely lentils, veggies, chicken and lamb. Served on a flat bread called injeri it looks quite exotic and appealing! But tasting everything you realize everything has a sour vinegari taste and what they say is spicy is not spicy at all for my taste. I would say for how much I was excited to try this place out I wasn't half as impressed. Probably will only head back if there's a group of friends excited about trying something ethnic. Pricing is also one reason I was not happy. I think the food is way overpriced probably because it's a small business and I understand. But as a customer you think of a hundred different ways you could have eaten with that money. I recommend it for the sake of experience.
Good food! Decent choices if you're vegetarian. I had the stir fried noodles (#48) which was pretty good! Looking forward to trying the pho next!

Dinner started off great with a nice cozy atmosphere and some tasty sambosas but things went downhill quickly after that... I had the lamb corma which was bland and left much to be desired. Overall it was pretty disappointing.

I can NOT say enough good things about this place!!! I always thought I hated Indian food, until I tried here. I was very pleasantly surprised when I tried their buffet during the week. I have never been to a better buffet in my life! Definitely the best $10 I've ever spent on food. There are so many options to choose from and nothing was too heavily spicy. I've been to other restaurants where the food was so overpoweringly spicy that it was impossible to enjoy. Desi Spice makes everything perfectly with the best flavors. The service is amazing and the owner is one of the nicest humans on the planet. Definitely give this place a try!!

great fresh rolls - super dark greens and extra thin skin with wonderful peanut dipping sauce (we had vegetarian version, should have had with shrimp but these were yummy all the same).... nice satay ... not gristly at all, tender white meat, yay! we also had the tom kah gai soup which was good, but watch out for big hunks of fresh lemongrass (delish as a spice but not to chew on or swallow). bf had pineapple curry which was (as I had expected) not spicy or curry-ish at all and more like a bowl of sugary pineapple ... there was as much pineapple as there was meat (beef?). Wait staff was very friendly and attentive, place was clean and upbeat but given it is on a busy street in Mesa, it's more of a strip mall feeling than cute neighborhood place. We called ahead to ask if they had outdoor seating, which they did (a few tables right on the busy street) .... we sat inside so as to not inhale car/bus fumes. I wouldn't go there again as a visitor to SB - it's just not special or authentic enough. It's a fine place to go or get take out if you live in the immediate area.

This place is amazing! Hubby found an advertisement for it and suggested we go up here one night for dinner. We walked in, without a reservation, and was seated within 10 minutes. Any questions I had, my waiter answered in depth for me and explained each dish, asked how much spice I'd like to it ect.... My hubby ordered for me since I was not sure what to get other than Tandoori chicken (which I always ordered), so he helped me, and i do believe it was a lamb dish. Was fabulous!

When you see any Restaurant with "PHO" is part of their name, you gotta try it! And I gave Pho An Hoa 5 stars review base on their excellent Pho. So for those who not quite familiar with Vietnamese food in general or Pho in to be specific, a good Pho is graded base on a following criteria: -Beef Broth: has to be clear and amber in color NOT turbid. Taste: has to balance between sweetness (from slow cook of beef and bones NOT MSG), and salt. Flavor: a well balance of star anise, cinnamon, and cumin not overpower or obnoxious. Also, very important, broth has to HOT to the touch not warm. -Meats : rare beef: gotta be nice and pink in color, under and sweet to the taste. Brisket has to be tender, fully of flavor and sweet not dry nor over cooked. -Noodles: nice soft fresh white (usually comes in packages pre made). None of Pho restaurant in town has real fresh noodles made from scratch ( some Pho restaurant in Orange county California do offer this feature). So this is as good as it get.

We had the dinner for two and asked for samosas instead of soup. They were delicious with the mint sauce. The chicken tikka & veggie korma were the best two of the several dishes we got to sample. My hubby is a major carnivore and he liked the veggie korma the best if that tells you anything. If I could change one thing, I would have ordered it medium rather than mild. I would have liked a little more spice, but that's my fault for not asking for it. The staff was very nice and happy to answer any questions and offer suggestions when asked.

I was so excited to find a place with great reviews in a neutral location (me from Kirkwood and my friend from St. Charles)! We each made the 11 mile trip and met at Spiro's on a Tuesday night. I arrived first and requested a table for 2. The woman, who I suspect to be the owner or relative, slowly walked off (without menus). I stayed in the lobby. After 30-45 seconds, I was wondering if I was supposed to follow her....she came back and then picked up menus seated me. The table she seated me at was awkwardly blocked by a food cart, which I found to be odd, since I thought she was making sure she had a table ready (even though there were plenty). The waiter seemed rushed, annoyed, and in a bad mood... When he asked for our drink order and we told him that we were both okay with water I think he lost interest.. My friend ordered the gyro and asked if she could pay more for a salad as her side. He said "no". I ordered the combo, with lamb, mousaka, and dolma. The server asked if I would like a salad with it, which I said "yes". My lamb was very tasty, but the mousaka and dolma tasted like mushy leftovers, which was very disappointing. When we got the bill, I noticed that I was charged for a salad, which is fine, but peculiar since my friend was unable to order one. On the way out, I apologized to my friend for choosing Spiro's...

I love the set up and decor in this place. The breakfast is great too. Coffee could be better, kind of bitter. Everything was priced pretty good. My server made me feel really welcome and she was extra attentive to my table. I'll be back and can't wait to try their lunch next time.

I was looking forward to trying this place but it was a pretty underwhelming experience as someone trying to order vegan. Deep fried tofu was my only option for anything I'd get so I only ordered one thing- the fried tofu rice vermicelli (I've been wanting to try some rice vermicelli in the area for awhile). The lack of variety though would've been okay if my dish was really good but the tofu was way too greasy for me to enjoy (the oil wasn't drained at all), and although rice vermicelli is always light enough for me to eat and feel good, we ate 3 hours ago and my stomach still hurts :/ My boyfriend liked his chicken bahn mi, however we can get cheaper bahn mi in IV at pho bistro

I was excited to see a new Indian and Thai restaurant open in Hatboro as these are my two favorite foods, but sadly won't be returning. Thai lemongrass soup was really bad. Our vegetable appetizer was just ok. Our Lamb tikka masala and korma were just ok. The waitress took a long time to take our orders, even after we put down our menus. And after the meal she kept trying to push us to get some sort of orange cream dessert. We didn't get it but another table did and it was just orange wedges with whipped cream on the side. The positive thing I can say about the place is the ambiance was nicer than expected for the shopping center it is located in. Hatboro has better Indian food at Biryani Bowl.
I use Taza for catering and their food is amazing! Great vegetarian and healthy options.

The best breakfast sandwich in West Philly (and the best I've had in the city but I've not tried many outside of Univ. City). The rolls are the key. Toasted, light, and fluffy. You tell Ms. Bui your order (probably bacon, egg, and cheese with salt, pepper, and ketchup) and it's up in about 2 minutes, even with a line. Like the others have said, get Sriacha...I love it WITH ketchup as you get sweet and hot. I've been to Bui's so many times it's crazy. It's a Penn staple and it's worth going to if you live in Univ. City. Their lunches aren't bad either. It's about as good of a cheesesteak as you'll ever get off of a truck.

Very take-out style place. You can dine-in, but everything will still be served in styrofoam, which I found a little wasteful. Tried the pad Thai and panang curry. Both incredibly flavorful. The pad Thai was SUCH a huge portion and was very saucy with plenty of crushed peanuts. It was also decently spicy so keep that in mind. Overall, for the price, I think you are getting some great Thai food. It's not the best I've ever had by any means, but I think it's a great option.

I have eaten here twice, and had a really great experience both times. Once was for dinner on a weekend, and there were menu options for myself (a vegetarian, health-conscious eater) as well as my boyfriend and his mom, who both favor meat-heavy traditional dishes. We were hesitant to go after reading some of the reviews but decided to give it a shot, and were really happy with the decision. The staff we came in contact with were professional and friendly. We all loved the food we ordered, and the atmosphere was both comfortable and elegant. The second time I went was for brunch, and I had a very similar experience. The prices were average, but the food was great and we had excellent service. I'm sorry for the negative experiences of other reviewers, but it's possible they have changed their attitude, because I would definitely recommend this restaurant and hope it sticks around.
Store closed. I called, no message indicating closure for renovations. Nor did the website indicate closure. No excuse for not announcing this.

I visited this restaurant this past week. Good marks for cleanliness, atmosphere, and friendliness of staff. I had the lunch buffet and found it to be "ok". While I certainly understood, with a buffet, why they'd need to dial back the 'heat' of the dishes, but it seems that they held back on all of the spices to me. Indian and Pakistani cuisine need not ever be bland, but that's what I found it to be. Indian cuisine is bold and one of the key reasons why I love it. Spice it up a bit, folks!

The slowest Pollo Tropical I've ever been too, none of the workers had no idea what was going on, or what went with the order. Had to go back, I was missing part of my food. They need to hire some management, every time I go there is always something.

My friend recommended I come here for the pho so me and my girlfriend paid a visit and countless since the first!.l Their staff is very courteous and the food is delicious ! They are more than willing to substitute any meat for tofu which is great for the girlfriend who is a vegetarian. Definitely recommend.

My boyfriend and I did a weekend trip to Reno and were looking for some really good pho. As usual I perused through yelp and saw terrible reviews for all the other places near our hotel. This place is about a 7 minute drive from the hotel's but definitely worth it. Food: Spring Rolls: super delicious Salt and pepper Calamari: omg this was the best. The. Best. Calamari I have ever had. Tons of minced garlic (yum) and stir fried onions and green onion. Flavors were definitely on point. Oxtail Pho: I can say that their broth is soo good that it doesn't require additional flavoring. Our party of 7 all agreed, and the rest of the group is used to highly seasoning their noodles with hoisin sauce, Sriracha, etc. Service: we were the only group in the restaurant at the time, the service was impeccable. Gracious and friendly servers. We ordered 5 iced coffees for the road and our server was nice enough to bring them out to us while we waited.

After all the rave reviews I was excited to try Zoes kitchen. Unfortunately my experience was blah. I ordered the chicken orzo with tomatoes. And that is exactly what I got. Plain orzo, with 2 strips of very plain, dried out chicken and what tasted like canned chopped tomatoes. No flavor, no spices and barely warm. My husbands meal wasn't much more exciting. Atmosphere was ok. Filled with kids and moms lunching.
Absolutely Delicious Valentine's Day dinner! Great service too. Best thai food in SB

Let me be clear-- my girlfriend and I came here using a $15 for $30 deal. It was pretty disappointing. Desi Villages loses three stars for the slowness of service, general dinginess of the area where we were sat, and the small portion of food for the high price. The restaurant earns two stars for good flavor of the lamb curry and an eggplant dish. Upon arriving, we were seated immediately at a booth. Some items were missing from the table-- only one water glass and one set of silverware. We were given menus, and our server left for about 10 minutes before coming back to take our order-- garlic naan, lamb curry, and an eggplant dish. It was nice to have papad on the table when we sat down. If I knew better, I wouldn't have snacked through it so quickly. About 15 minutes later our entrees came. During that time, we kept trying to get the attention of any server. The items we ordered came to just about $30, so we wanted a mango lassi. When our entrees arrived, we ordered a lassi. Sadly, they didn't have any even though it was on the menu. Moreover, we ordered garlic naan, and it wasn't ready yet. Another 10 minutes passed and we received our naan. It was also about this time that they started to clear a table adjacent to our booth where a party of 8 made a huge mess before we arrived. When eating, it is not appetizing to have a disgusting, dirty table in your sight line. Thankfully it only took them 30 minutes to start clearing it. I wouldn't go back. There are too many other better places on the mainline for Indian/Pakistani food, and plenty more in Philadelphia.

I have never left a yelp review on anything, but this place is too good. Today was my third time going and I'm still amazed at how perfect it is. First, customer service is out of this world, I had pretty much decided before I even got my food that I liked the place. It was just an added bonus that the food was amazing!!! The first time I went, I got the tofu banh mi and a coconut milk tea and I was floored! The second time, I got the Taro milk tea (amazing!). Today I got the matcha iced coffee and the tofu summer rolls. My favorite menu items by far? The matcha iced coffee and the tofu banh mi!!! Please do yourself a favor and visit this amazing little place, you will thank me later!

Just left and had the" Doro Wot (Chicken Stew)". It was delicious! I will definitely be back to this location. They have a few big screen TVs. The bartender Tony is a pretty friend;y guy. They are going to start having a lunch time buffet with a mix of Ethiopian and American food. Definitely check it out if you are in the area. my only knock would be : They should have a TV behind the bar so I don't have to turn around or to the side. But a good place.
Delicious and cheap! Try the Kari Bunin- delicious savory broth with noodles, fried tofu, fried fish cake. Also the Sky cafe salad is great. BYO!!!

My favorite Thai restaurant to date. I have eaten here several times, both dine-in and carry out. The restaurant is honestly not much to look at. It is sparsely furnished and features numerous Asian knick-knacks. However, whereas the design lacks, the menu more than makes up for it. I think Basil Spice has the best Spring Rolls in the area. They are so crispy, but not burnt. They have a lighter texture, despite being fried. This allows the flavors of the filling to come through. Another appetizer I really enjoy is the Satay Gai, which are basically grilled chicken skewers. These have always been grilled to perfection and taste great. I typically order either the Chicken or Seafood Pad Thai as an entrée. No matter what meat your order, the stir fry is very tasty and comes with bean sprouts, egg, and tofu that is cooked to perfection. They also add chopped peanuts, which enhance the texture of the dish so well. You are also able to control the spiciness of your food, which is nice. They carry a few types of deserts and a couple of different Asian beers and sakes. It is a reasonable place to eat and the food seems to be fresh and well prepared. I have recommended Basil Spice to several friends, who have all enjoyed it. I hope you do too!

Shrimp noodles super tasty. Grabbed order to go late night after starry night. Looking forward to my next work trip to Media so I can repeat visit Shrimp bigger and yummier than expected. Mild one pepper rating perfect for me can't imagine 2, or 3 yowsa

Quite honestly I was impressed by the flavour of this spicy food. It was pretty awesome to have such different dishes presented to me during the Yeg Food Crawl event today. I especially liked the bean sprouts that were served with the spicy fish. The pork was good too especially with the mushroom fungus. The staff here were really enthusiastic and kind when introducing this type of cuisine and the spiciness of the dishes. Apparently cranberry juice is a good trick to try when eating really spicy food (I had never learned this until now). But we didn't need any cranberry juice as the food was just excellent on its own. I really enjoyed it and would definitely return. Part of the appeal is that the food isn't just the standard "chinese" food but rather this really reflects the regional cuisine of the Szechuan area.

Mojitos, on the corner of Esplanade & Frenchmen, between the old Ruby Red's & the Firehouse, across from the US Mint, is now open. Traditional, open dining, big ceiling fans, quiet decor, eclectic Caribbean-meets-South Louisiana menu: Mojitos is an oasis of quiet in a very hectic neighborhood. Indoor & outdoor patio bars, full cocktail menu, & favorite cold beers. We "accidented into" the trial run on Saturday and went back on Sunday. Large commercial parking lot on Elysian Fields side of the block. This is a good spot to meet for forays into the French Quarter, French Market, or Marigny. Expect 3 star rating to become 4 star when kinks are worked out. Local owners & chef. Great new place. Rick New Orleans
Wow what a great place! I really like Ethiopian food and this is as good and authentic as it gets.

Creazian was amazing. The parking lot is easy to access, the price is reasonable, and it's clean. It is very roomy and has lots of atmosphere to relax. You really don't have to worry about anything. Hailey is extremely nice to new and old customers. She always checks on you if you need additional service. If you are getting the Poke bowl (Sushi in a bowl) and you choose wasabi as one of your ingredients, I recommend getting the wasabi separately. If you are a wasabi lover you can keep it in the bowl but it has a extremely strong taste. The food presentation is very alluring, delicious, and very tempting to eat. Highly recommended. We will come back here again every time we visit Reno during holidays. This place is words farther than fantastic! 5 stars for Creazian.
This place is pretty much the shizzle. 2nd time here and its even better. The spring roles are straight dope. And anything with a fried egg on top is gonna be good.
We went during a trade show nearby and craving Indian food... recommend letting go on your craving and settling for something else

Well I was very under-impressed. I saw the reviews and pictures and was excited because everything LOOKED so delicious but, when I tasted the foods that I ordered, I was disappointed. The atmosphere was great, the service was even better but the food just wasn't at all what the pictures described. Maybe it's because all the pics on the reviews are out dated. Either way... I did get pics. The papaya salad was ordered Lao style 5 star hot but was more like a 1 star. The peppers were not fresh. It seemed like dry pepper was used. The fried pork ribs was very dry and barely had any meat. It was super bland. The shumai pork was good, the sauce seem OLD. It had a really bitter after taste. Hubby's red curry pork was good however, (great amount of veggies) the pork was PINK and slimey. The server told him 2 star would be like 4 star hot so he didn't get it anymore spicy. (It was not spicy AT ALL) My sticky rice was not microwaved long enough because it was getting cold and hard fast. The crispy pork and chinese brocoli was pretty good considering it didn't have the real crispy pork. The sauce was perfect but they had sliced red pork in it instead. I hope this review helps, not intended to bash the restaurant.

Wow finally a REAL middle eastern gem comes to tucson from Phoenix!! Had lunch today with family and everything was excellent! Huge portions, go and share unless you eat like a horse ? Will be back soon to further detail my review!
A client urged me to go and so glad that I did. Absolutely delicious!! Space is clean and tidy, buffet is well organized, and the food is fragrant and wonderful!

This is my favorite Indian Buffet in the Main Line area. You can always count on high quality food, and plenty of it. Great variety of offerings. Highlights: - Chicken Tikka Masala (although the refer to it as something else) - Naan - Variety of chutney and fresh salads (chickpea and tomato) Lowlights: - None I can think of

I'm not sure how to review Park Allen, it is kind of like reviewing your Uncles living room. Growing up my family went for Sunday dinners here so often, I feel like it was just an extension of my family. Now, there are two parts to PA. The pizza side, which is de-lish and fairly deep dish to boot. And then there is the Lebanese restaurant side, where my family always eats. Which is wonderful! This is a family owned and operated establishment, the whole family works there, and mama always would have hummus that was extra garlicky, and so amazing, and it is still there! I always go for the fattoush over the tebouleh. The New Zealand rack of lamb is excellent, try pairing it with the Twin Islands sauvignon blanc, which is also from NZ. If you can handle the heat, well get the samaki harrah to come outta the kitchen! Basically it is the catch of the day, in the hottest, spiciest dry rub ever! Let me say it again EVER!!! I love the new renovations; it is quite chic with a wine loft in the center of the tiny space. They have a small patio, however it is not the quietest being right along busy 109th street, and not a great view either. But, that's River City for ya!

I absolutely love Nirvana!! In my opinion, the best Indian food around. My favorite is the butter chicken and samosas. And of course the naan. The prices and service are excellent. Would highly recommend!!

The Pho here is good however it has a sweetness to it which I am not used to. There is better pho and Vietnamese food around but when it comes to location I would choose this place most the time. Bar is nice and egg rolls are good too. I would recommend it!
It's not bad, but it's not great either. I've been here twice and wasn't too impressed either time. Their egg rolls are good, but the curry and lo mein were just fine.

Counter style Jamaican restaurant with a large seating area and vibrant decor. I finally decided to give Hummingbird a try for lunch after passing it so many times on break. I ordered the jerk chicken with rice and beans and a side of mac and cheese. The jerk chicken had a good balance of spice and sweetness while the mac and cheese was on the creamier side. Portions were big even for a small platter. The menu offered a range of traditional Jamaican dishes and is worth returning if only for a beef patty. There is a minimum credit charge so bring cash just in case and order ahead to beat the lunch crowd.

Lunch buffet is good. Decent number of choices. Price is reasonable.Good crowd generally hospital staff which is nearby. Place is a bit small. Difficult to find. Generic Indian food, might wanna try other Indian restaurant if u are looking for authentic taste.

I recommend this especially if you're looking for Halal food. Eggs and meat were delicious and not too salty. French toast was fluffy and not too sweet with Judy the right amount of flavor. Service was fast, kind and attentive. I will definitely be coming back!

This restaurant used to be very good! Now, it seems they are going thru the motions. Restaurant looked like it needed a good cleaning. Couldn't get past the dust. Food was ordinary....very salty. Nothing's remarkable....stay away!
Best indian food restaurant in Nashville... awesome lamb/goat curry... if you like spicy Indian food this is the best... little expensive but it is worth ...
Excellent and always reliable BYOB..great fish dishes, pastas are tasty and fresh, great staff

The food is edible but not a pleasure to. I would rate it at-par with food trucks at Penn. Those are 1/3 the price though. I have eaten at at least 40 thai restaurants cross country, this is bottom-5.
Great food in a very basic atmosphere, delicious humus and you should try the combo plate with gyro meat, chicken, amazing rice, and salad. To top it off, the fruit tea is very good too!

First off I'm not a starving/earthy student so this restaurant isn't geared toward me. I only came in for dessert, but it was really good and I'd still go again. The whole vibe though is not somewhere I fit in though. It's young, earthy students working on laptops or hanging out with friends eating vegan natural foods. The restaurant is shabby chic and somewhat small for how popular it is so sometimes it can be hard to find a place to sit. It does have free wifi which is great if you're not the Starbucks type. Only bad thing is the time the cashier takes because he or she also gets your food so it's a long wait. Change that and I'd give it a higher rating.
Good Pad Thai is hard to find! Very nice employees, beautiful and tranquil setting.

This is my go to place for Latin Food. I think the quality of the food is great, they give you a good portion for the money, and the people who work there are very friendly. Great place to go for lunch or supper.

I enjoyed the chicken Shawarma. They were generous with their chicken. It has a nice flavor and seasoning. The mushroom soup wasn't to my like. Had a different flavor I just cant identify. The gravy on the poutine was pretty good and there was a decent amount of cheese on it. La Shish down the street is a bit better in my opinion. Prices are standard for Lebanese to go. You can eat for under $10.

This is a well kept secret and it shouldn't be. The food is great and the fruit tea is really refreshing. The quality of the food certainly makes up for the lack of decor. It has certainly become one of my faves.

I'm not gonna lie, this place had some good food. I'm very particular about my Afghan food, and this place didn't disappoint. The chicken kaboob was nice and tender and the bread wasnt dry as I had feared from previous reviews. Have I had better Afghan food? Sure...for alot cheaper too...But In Philly? I don't think so. I'd definitely give this place a shot if you are in Center City and want some Afghani food.

I have been wanting to try this place for a while, and it did not disappoint! I started with the samosas, which were spiced and fried to perfection. My entree was the chicken vindaloo, which is my favorite. I topped it all off with some naan. The vindaloo was so generously portioned that I took half of it home. I highly recommend you try this place! I will be coming back to try the mixed grill next!
Some of the best Thai food around. The used Thai tea is amazing. You won't be disappointed.

This is easily my favorite place to go for Indian food. My bf & I come for date night or to catch up with friends. Colorful, clean, intimate atmosphere. Extremely nice owners/managers. The food is incredible-shrimp curry, papdi chaat, vegetable pakora, lasooni gobi, chicken curry, different naan, of course rice pudding for dessert! Decently priced, especially in this expensive town. I always recommend this place to anyone who is looking for a night out or a cute lunch spot

DEEEEEELISH! Went with 2 people and enjoyed every single dish we ordered. It's pricy, for 3 people our bill was $120 (no alcoholic beverages ordered), but it was so good. Definitely recommend the petit filet, the cheese with the bread add on ($1 addl), and the warm grain salad. Date truffles are good too. Next time we go I will try the hummus!

Go-to Indian restaurant in STL! But I've only ever been for lunch so can only comment on their lunch buffet. I like the variety and all the flavors of the dishes. Naan is delicious and so is their dessert.
Very nice food and fast service. We Ordered Aloo Tiki, Lamb Biryani, and Chicken Tikka and everything was delicious!
Brought the Family for Sunday Brunch. Had a great time. The food was hot a good as usual. Recommend for a relaxed Weekend lunch or dinner.

Mumbai bistro is great for convenient Indian food. It's very casual and I typically take my food to go. It's no New Deli, which is all the way in University City, but it curves my craving for Indian food. I always get their Mutter paneer, their chicken tikka masala, and basmati rice from the buffet bar with a side of naan. I haven't gotten anything from their take-out menu yet, but I'd only get the mutter paneer and chicken tikka anyway. Wonder if I'd get a better deal if I got those sides separately, with rice and naan? Definitely coming back when I need my quick fix.

I was expecting big things...and it didn't quite deliver. The Good: The atmosphere was AMAZING. They really did a great job with the decor and feel of place. I am dying to go back to try the lattes and pastries from the front of the house coffee shop. The outdoor garden area looks gorgeous and I'm sure would be a favorite spot in the warmer months. The food was decent. A couple of standouts, but overall, just okay. The drinks were also good. I had the Lace & Linens and loved it.They do have a parking lot on Front which is helpful when in Fishtown. The Bad: We had a reservation but still had to wait an additional half hour. I didn't really care for most of the meat dishes. Seating was nice, but when the table next to us received their two orders of Dorado, the whole restaurant must have known. After my reaction to the smell, my husband suggested I take a pregnancy test. I am not, in fact, pregnant. Just be warned...it is a very strong smell. What we ate: Fatteh - probably one of the very best dishes I've ever had. This is what redeemed this place for me. The flavors are so simple, but together are just amazing. Muhammara - liked this dip a lot. Different than what we normally would get like a Hummus or something similar. Makanek - I did not like this. My husband said it was okay, but would have been better with more than just a sausage. Fried Kibbeh - I did not like this. My husband did. Kafta Kebab - this was okay
awesome pakistani/indian jawn off the beaten path in Ardmore. Great food, no pretensions. Need more of this sort of thing on the Main Line.

They never disappoint! Attentive service, excellent food and now a full bar. Being away from town for a few months this is one of the places I miss the most. Samosas or popdi chat then your favorite protein in a makhani or vindaloo sauce and you'll be hooked.

My father suggested this place based on the reviews he has heard about it. We went for lunch and were both very happy with the results. For lunch the portions and price were perfect! For $9 a person from 11-3 on M-F, will get you a cup of soup, a small appetizer and your entree (decently portioned!). I went back for seconds that same week! Both times I had the pad thai (excellent). I have had the spring rolls, the crab dumplings (both worth it) and the shrimp corn fritters (dont bother with them) as appetizers. For soup I did the lemon grass and coconut. Both were delicious but for me, the coconut takes the prize. I have been craving it ever since. This will absolutely become a place I frequent.

You often hear all the great chefs talk about the secret to great cooking being fresh, pristine ingredients and simple preparation. Well Zeppoli is one of those restaurants that epitomizes that philosophy and brings it to vivid life! Everything we had, while simple in preparation, was phenomenal. Was there with a party of 6 (see Ron C.s review) and we shared so all of us were able to sample a good portion of the menu. We started with the house Antipasta that featured a little of everything including house cured soprasatta and many Sicilian specialties. Next we had various pastas, then fisherman's stew, braised rabbit, beefsteak which I must mention was pre-rubbed in lardo then perfectly grilled and served alongside crisp fresh arugula and cherry tomato... All pasta dishes were incredible and expertly sauced and the meat dishes were perfect in their execution and presentation. When you read the reviews that attempt to describe the menu items or if you just look at the menu, Zeppoli may look somewhat ordinary. But it isn't. Just go and see for yourself. Ambiance is cozy if a bit noisy but if you can get past the noise (drink some wine and start a conversation with your neighbors and have some fun!) while focusing on the food you won't be disappointed. Disclaimer: My nephew Tom is a waiter here but I am being completely honest in my review. They're not a nationwide semi-finalist in the James Beard Best New Restaurants for 2012 because of me.

I've been eating a lot more Taziki's since Kalamatas changed for the worse. I usually get tilapia, salmon, beef, pork, or lamb over the Mediterranean style salad. The meats are well marinated and tender. The hummus doesn't knock me out compared to Kalamatas, but whose does anyway? I like the pimento cheese appetizer but the show stopper is the limited time feta cheese dip topped with pepperoncini, honey and olives. It comes with crispy baked pita chips or warm soft pita pieces. The pro-move is to get the warm soft pita because the dip melts a little on the bottom and enhances the whole experience. I need to learn how to make this at home! The saltiness of the feta and olives contrasted with the sweetness of the honey creates a dangerous obsession. I do like the Taziki's in Green Hills too.
Such amazing food ! When they say spicy they mean spicy!! We love the cauliflower appetizer so delish!

Best THAI Food by Far in years! I've had Thai food in Thailand as well as other international destinations. So i know what i'm talking about. The fried rice is wholesome, tasty and has tomatoes in it! the green curry was sensational and so full with vegetables. I've never had so much veggie in a green curry before, you typically find a few peas and some carrots and bamboo, but this one was so fulfilling and tasty. The penang was delicious, papaya salad was fresh and they made it mild for me. All around, this is the best Thai food i've had in the States by far. Thank you and keep up the love you put into your food.

This place is awesome! Everything from start to finish was excellent. We ordered the calamari, crab avocado toast, steak, scallops, batatas bravas, and the flourless chocolate cake. Would highly recommend everything we tried. The restaurant is beautiful also and the atmosphere was great. Looking forward to going back!

i had gone to Tangelo's a couple of months ago at lunchtime on a tuesday by myself. aside from a couple of other tables, there was no one else there. fine by me. i got to chat with the waitress, the food was good as was the locally made beer. i liked it alot. today i went for lunch on a saturday with my two young boys. there were a few more tables, and the staff seemed genuinely flummoxed and hurried. we sat at the bar and were asked if we wanted brunch. i saw the relatively short brunch menu out of the corner of my eye and said, "we will take whatever is available". she handed me both the brunch and regular lunch menu, but added the caveat, "no burgers and no fish though". problem is, thats the bulk of the lunch menu(as well as most of the kids menu). i tried to order a yogurt and granola parfait off the brunch menu and was told, "sorry, just sold the last one". um ok. i ordered the boys waffles, which arrived flat, dense and tough. no way these were made fresh. my egg cuban sandwich was fine, although the iced tea has a a strong cinnamon flavor. if you offer iced tea, you can offer a herbal tea or something as an option. dont make it your only iced tea. one of my sons was still a little hungry, so i tried to order him some fresh fruit, to which we were once again told they were out of. so to surmise-at lunch on a saturday, you have no fruit, no granola, no yogurt, no burgers and no fish. if you cant have the basics on hand during a weekend, thats a bad sign. sadly, i wont be back.

As you walk into this restaurant, you're greeted by the warmest smile and hospitality which will surely brighten your day! My best friends and I arrived somewhat late on a Saturday afternoon around 4.40 pm and even though the restaurant didn't open for dinner till 5pm, the servers still accommodated us. We were ecstatic as we were starving. I would have to say that the food is good. The palak paneer lacked "oomph" aka flavor but the chicken tikka masala was delicious. Our aloo papri chaat ( Indian street food favorite) was a little different but it was still delicious. I would be a little hesitant to recommend the aloo paratha on how it's made but the peshwari naan was decent :) I think what made me give this restaurant 4 stars is the service. The level of hospitality offered made me feel like I was at home. The manager, shahid, was very kind to stop by and check on us. He asked us how the meal was and I gave him my honest opinion about the palak paneer and he offered to replace it. We certainly did not need to go that way but just the mere suggestion was excellent customer service. Shahid the manager offered us complementary desserts some gulabjamun and rice pudding because the palak paneer was sub par. I have to say that even though this was completely unnecessary, the dessert touch and the service made a lasting impression on our meal. So yes, if you're in the KOP area for some shopping and want an ethnic touch to end your evening or even for lunch, come to desi village. I know for a fact that they've catered our office lunches in Conshohocken as well. Brava!

I feel like this place is hit or miss. Sometimes it's great sometimes it's just okay. Usually pretty fast delivery, unless its peak hours. Seems to be a lack of consistency with dishes. Affordable. Just hope they don't get your order wrong, it's like pulling teeth to get it corrected.

This is one of those diamonds in the rough. Location does not help but probably will in the future if they are able to hang in there. Parking is tough to come by especially safe parking. The restaurant itself is beautiful and nicely decorated. Service is good but a bit more staff would help. Typical Trinidad cuisine at a reasonable cost. The night we went there was live steel drum music. Nice variety of entrees but be sure to question if your dish will be spicy hot, it is not noted on all items especially the Red Snapper which I found out about the hard way!! I talked them into oxtails for my appetizer which was on the menu as an entree and they were happy to accommodate me. All in all a pleasant experience and tasty food they just have to tighten up on a few things before getting that extra star from me.

Thanks, Sarah S., and Thai Country Café, for another successful International Supper Club outing March 13. It was a large group -- I think about 17. The table setup was not perfect. They had set aside two large rectangular tables, so we really didn't all eat together. I got potstickers for an appetizer. Shared. Dang, they were good. The sauce was a little sweeter than what I usually have, but it worked just fine. Charleen and Ben shared their chicken satay. That peanut sauce was just so fabulous to set off the chicken. Who knew? Denzel shared his spring rolls. He didn't like them, so he shared them with everybody. I didn't partake. I got Tom Yum Soup for my entrée. It had some spice to it (that you could see), but, dang, it was really, really good. I'd get that again in a New York second. It's always fun to get together with Yelpers. Everybody's from a different place, a different scope and experiences. Paul K. is right. As usual, Sarah S. sets it all up. All we have to do is walk in, sit down and have a great meal. I took home half of my Tom Yum Soup, which served as a great lunch the next day.
Wow, wonderful service and even better food. Had the Kofta, Dolmades, and Tzatziki. The Tzatziki came out and was wonderful, then the Kofta came out and blew it away. Definitely recommend this place.

We were on North Michigan Rd after going to humane society so we decided to try a new restaurant up there since we mostly eat in central Indianapolis. Picked Curries and Chutneys based on Yelp reviews. Overall satisfied. Staff was very friendly and allowed us to sample to pick what we wanted. 2 curries, rice, and 1 piece of naan for 7.50. Added samosa and drink. I ordered butter chicken and paneer masala. My boyfriend got chicken 65 and chicken tikka masala. It was all tasty. His servings had a lot of chicken in them and my plate ended up with only a few pieces of chicken and a few pieces of paneer. I finished all my food and boyfriend had leftovers and said it was very filling. I have to say that for the same price (7.99) I could go to an lunch buffet at Shalimar or other Indian restaurant and then I can have more variety to food and serve myself the quantities I want. It would be just as quick and the food is better. However if you take it to go, this may be a good option for you.

This place was wonderful! I had the vegetable patia, my husband had chicken tikka masala and we also tried the vegetable korma. Everything was fabulous! The garlic naan and the paneer naan were both delicious and the staff was very helpful. I'll definitely come back if I'm in the area.
I have only been there for lunch, but their buffet is AWESOME. Never had to wait and their wait staff does a great job keeping your water glass full. Note : Coupons available at Coupons4Indy.com
"Great food and great service. Prices are very reasonable and food is always fresh. Ask them for the spice tray to kick it up a notch."

This is the best Thai in St. Louis! I say St. Louis because it's just 10 minutes across 255 to Illinois. We've had King & I, Fork and Stix, Ocha, you name them. This is the one we go out of our way for when we want Thai. The Khanom Jeeb (Dumplings) melt in your mouth. Their Pad See Ew is my wife's favorite. As for me I'm basic, Pad Thai is my go to and you can't beat theirs. Just like their counterparts, be wary of spice level 5

My wife and I had a very bad experience for our first time at this restaurant. We were seated and waited 10mins before anyone asked us for a drink. The problem about this is that it was only 5 other people at tables seated in the restaurant so it was not busy at all. The people that walked in well after we were seated received drinks before anyone thought to ask us. The service was very slow and the food I ordered lacked flavor. The chicken was dry on my salad. I asked for fruit to be added to my salad but instead of just placing it on mine, they placed it on my wife's greek salad which she didn't request. I would not eat at this restaurant again and wouldn't recommend anyone visit it either. Service and the food is not very good. Waste of money and time.
Great drinks, great service and very creative menu. Small plate concept allows for sampling of dishes that one would not normally commit an entire meal to. We'll definitely be back!

This place is a favorite of mine...I come here with coworkers when we feel like taking a long lunch. Forget the "Chinese" part of the menu - what you are coming for is the Vietnamese food. Delicious Pho! Authentic and tasty, it rivals any I've had outside of Indianapolis. Noodle dishes are great too...everything is so fresh and cooked perfectly. Service is attentive - the server is amazing actually, she remembers what everyone likes to eat to the point we really don't need menus anymore. Try a Vietnamese iced coffee, they are yummy! And did I mention they serve bubble (boba) tea! Awesome! Highly recommended!

Driving down Lindell, I always thought Mi Carbine was just another cheesy Mexican restaurant - boy was I wrong! After discovering this was a Caribbean/Cuban inspired restaurant, and checking the Yelp reviews, we knew we wanted to check it out. Walking in, the owner kindly let us know that if we were looking for a quick meal, this wasn't the restaurant for us! We appreciated the transparency and settled in with a few drinks and a few appetizers. Let me just say, when the food did come out, it was fantastic. At our table of eight, everyone ordered something different. There was very little food left on any of the plates following the meal. This is about as authentic as Caribbean cuisine gets in St. Louis. Definitely worth checking out!

This place is great. But, I have no idea if this is "the real stuff". I just know, to me it's good. The sauces are very flavorful and have the right amount of herbs and spices for me. Some of the texture of the food is a bit off, but I have no idea if they are supposed to be mushy or chewy, because it's always been mushy or chewy wherever I had it, and people eat it, and they eat a lot of it, so it must be somewhat spot on. And if it isn't, it's still good to me. I must admit, their chicken Tika Masala, is fantastic. And their barbecued/grilled chicken is also really good. We found this place during the Septa Strike. I met my wife and we were walking home together and the place smelled really good so we went in. We had to waddle back home. There may be other places that are better in flavor, but it's a buffet that is like 11.00 a person. You can't beat it. I wish I could be more descriptive, but my knowledge on Indian cuisine is pretty poor. I just know what I like. happy eating!!
Food is fresh rice and peas is tasty, jerk chicken was ok. Not spicy at all I'm use to my jerk chicken spicy and flavorful. But I'm willing to go back and try something else on the menu

I have tried several Thai restaurants in the area and Jasmine Thai is by far the best. I enjoy eating the Pad Thai, vegetable soup and spring rolls (pretty much my staple order at all Thai restaurants). The dining-in experience was positive. The restaurant has nice decor, friendly staff and decent wait time. The take-out service is very adequate. I have never experienced any mix-ups with my order and the food quality is the same as if I dined in. I highly recommend this restaurant to others.

This was our first time and it was fabulous. Will definitely be back. Staff is very friendly and checked on us regularly. We had the sweet and sour chicken, shrimp with lobster sauce, potstickers, fried wontons and wonton soup. Everything was perfect, except our eyes were bigger than our tummies...lol

This place was a great find. My husband and I love Indian food and recently moved to the area. My husband is a picky eater and most places don't meet his standards. I ate at the lunch buffet one day on my own and thought it was worth a second visit. My husband came with me and now we go once a week for lunch. The food is on the spicier side but it's all very well done and very tasty. My husband likes how they change up the buffet menu every day so it's different every time we go. For $8.00, it's a bargain. We love the chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, and the saag dishes especially. We're looking forward to trying it for dinner.

This is hands down the best overall restaurant in the Brandon area. It offers a very calm and authentic ambience to Thai culture with beautiful woodwork seen in the tables and the decor. The wait staff is nothing less than pleasant as they happily take your order with a smile on their face. And the food is just divine. If you're new to trying Thai cuisine, you can start with something like pad Thai or fried rice, but I highly suggest you step out of your comfort zone and try something different! My favorites(it's too hard to choose one) include the fried springrolls, red curry, fried eggplant, som tam(papaya salad), and fried bananas.
