But, if you're not too keen on any of those, they also offer an extensive sushi menu which is fresh and excellent as well. For me, presentation is key, and this place does not disappoint! They serve their dishes on beautiful fish-shaped platters and form the rice into hearts. Lunch specials here are a steal. They offer a lunch size portion of your favorite dish or two sushi rolls of your choice along with a soup and an springroll for under $10! Can't beat that. Do yourself a favor and try this place out if you haven't already! You'll be happy you did.
This is our favorite place to eat in Florissant! We try to go a few times a month and we always bring guest from out of town here. Thai Chili Stir Fry is our favorite!!
Fun place with a wonderful variety of food. Even for Vegetarians. Cool grocery with specialty food items.

It's not easy finding a decent place to have a drink around here, but this bar does have the cheapest happy hour in town. I would certainly consider this place a bar and not a restaurant; the food is not consistent and can't be trusted. So at the bar, I would recommend paying as you go since the staff has a tendency of double charging when a tab is going (one will pour the drink/ring it up, another will ring it up not knowing the other already did). The staff seems miserable; they look like they need a drink or had too much the night before.

Great little lunch spot with fast service and outdoor seating! I had pad prig with pork (lunch portion) it was the perfect size to fill me up without setting me up for a nap when I got back to my desk. The service was excellent and the prices were very reasonable. Heat scale reference: 3 out of 4 was pleasantly spicy. I definitely *could* have done 4/4, but I might not have enjoyed my food as much

I am usually happy with the food at Blue Plate but that wasn't the case during my last visit. There was five people in our party, four got breakfast and one person got the salmon BLT on a focaccia bun. I got the Spanish egg sandwich on a focaccia bun. On both sandwiches the bread was dense and under cooked, very off putting and not really edible. Everyone's home fries and French fries arrived cold. An order of scrapple came out nice and brown on one side and gray and mushy on the other. Needless to say it was a very disappointing meal. Our waitress came back once to see if we needed more coffee but at no time did she ask his our meal was. Everyone agreed not to bother asking them to take it back because no one would have anything to eat for another 20 minutes. I asked for a comment card at the end because I thought they should at least know about the issues but our waitress just said they don't have them, never asking if there was a problem. Because if this experience I will not bother going back.

The food was delicious and service was quick and prompt.... opted for the chicken kebab which was priced decently at $18 and came with salad and bread... the wait staff was attentive and the bathroom was nicely decorated

Wonderful lunch buffet with veggies chicken and rice a definite recommendation great and spicy you even get ten percent off by checking in on yelp I was there early and everything was fresh and hot Loved that many of the chicken dishes were white meat

My daughter and I began our evening with a festive concert by The Philadelphia Gay Men's Chorus (which was beautiful) but placed our dinner at 10:30 pm. Spice Finch was perfect for the late night bite. We started with beautiful cocktails as well as the charred carrot hummus served with sourdough flatbread. The charred carrot hummus was creamy and included garnishing of northern beans and cucumber. The carrots spread was clean and elegant but in my opinion, lacked just a bit of flavor. The blistered shishito peppers were delicious. But the baked cheese? Shredded phyllo (which added perfect, crunchy texture), ricotta and mozzarella baked with a char with the cheesiest, creamiest center. So lovely. The merguez kabob was delicious as well as the fatoush. The dining room is elegant and beautifully understated with dim, glowy lighting. The service (and our server) was impeccable. The host for the evening was so helpful and gracious. This is a great spot. I will be back to try more delicious food.

Horrendous food. Quality service Ordered lobster roll / ginger chicken The sushi was thick, it would have been nice to see more than just rice Plus what's up with their rice, it feels like extra starchy jasmine rice. And this is really dry down the throat .. Broccoli tastes of chlorine and chicken is also oct cooked / dry as hell. With the money they charge , I would've expected standard service. Didn't live up.

One of our favorite restaurants in Mt Juliet. We're here at least once a month. Their butter chicken and garlic naan are killer. Garlic gobi is really good as well--it tastes like buffalo chicken wings, but it's actually fried cauliflower!!
Bright place with friendly staff and tasty dishes. Beautiful ethnic decor and pleasant atmosphere. High quality service and friendly staff.

This place is pretty good! I had the wheat cashew noodles. It was a bit strange with raisins in my Thai noodles, but it added the right amount of sweetness. The decor is AMAZING. There's a giant mural of a demon thing that's totally metal over the bar. If I lived in STL, I would take a date here or maybe have a nice group of friends out for a dinner. Service was fast. Not the most attentive, but maybe I'm spoiled by living in NYC.

Two months later and this place is a staple. They even launched new menus! Glad to see they didn't lose some of our favorites though! A must if you love Thai and/or are vegan as they have a large dedicated menu!

Great service and good food! I went here with my coworkers at 5 p.m. on a Friday. It was completely empty (I think they were just opening). One of my coworkers was 20 minutes late and I didn't feel rushed at all. This place looks like it should be more expensive than it is. The tablecloth and the atmosphere makes it very nice, but you can get Pad Thai for under $10 (not including tax). Yes please! If you want shrimp or squid it gets more expensive, but your standard chicken/beef/tofu dishes are very reasonably priced. I ordered the Pad Thai with tofu (I know, way to branch out, but I wasn't feel adventurous). Our waiter came over to apologize that there was only one person in the kitchen (another person was on his/her way), so our dishes would be slow coming out. I really commend him for telling us upfront. You cannot believe how many waiters wouldn't say anything and hope you didn't notice, or would tell you after the fact that you waited a long time. Honestly, I didn't even notice the food taking that long. The dish was huge! I shouldn't have eaten it all, because it was basically one and a half meals. I found it a little heavy on the sauce, but other than that it was delicious. I left there stuffed! Even though we all pleaded off dessert, they gave us complimentary fried bananas. It was really good. It is service like this that keeps a customer coming back! Parking is only free street parking and certain times it can get really busy, but not crazy enough that you'll never be able to find someplace to park, you just might have to walk a little.
Great food!! Love the freshness of the food!! You have the option of meat, vegetarian or even vegan!! Very clean and very good!!

I randomly dined at this restaurant last week with a few of my girlfriends. It was a Monday evening, and many of the other restaurants around here were closed. We saw that The Queen and I Thai was open, so that it was! The inside was cozy, and we were able to be seated right away. We were given menus as well as a specials menu and put in drinks and appetizers right away. The pinot noir was nice and arrived in a generously poured glass. I ordered the steamed dumplings appetizer, and they were unlike any I have had before! They did not look like traditional dumplings and were almost like a ball of pork nestled into the dumpling as opposed to being entirely baked into it. Different, but they were delicious! My friend ordered the coconut chicken soup, and it was so good. For my meal, I had the red curry chicken (thai hot!) and it was perfect. It arrived with a side of steamed white rice which I was able to add to my bowl of deliciousness. Others at my table had the yellow curry, pad thai and spicy thai basil noodles. Everyone loved their meals. I would definitely return here again if I was craving thai in the downtown St. Pete area. And a major plus that it's open on Mondays!

We really enjoyed our meal here. I came in w Husband and 2 littles and they were gracious and accommodating (prepped steamed veggies and a sauce just for kids on request). Decor is beautiful and peaceful. Many different level options for sitting. Food was great - husband had the giant steak with an unusual sauce and I had a pho (which I was graciously taught how to pronounce when I asked). Kiddos had the fresh spring rolls and ended up drinking the peanut sauce. Well priced wine list with a good portion- and I can't wait to come back for a lychee martini. Thanks Liam we'll be back!

Be careful and check your receipts. This restaurant cheated and made a bill of 50 dollar to 60 dollar by overwriting the receipt. When confronted the manager apologized and promised to give the money back which ofcourse never happened. He also did not want me to dispute the transaction and I wonder how many similar cases they had open. I ended up disputing anyhow after waiting for 10 days to get my money back. The food also is average but very disappointed with the fraud and cheating the place did. BEWARE!!
The food is good, but the portions are SMALL and they're hella expensive. I only go here if my friends really want to. I mean $20 for seafood pancakes? Ouch.

I love Indian food and eat it on a bi-weekly basis (my wife is Indian). I was expecting a decent meal but ended up being surprised by the fresh, superb cuisine that came out course after course. We started with samosas and 2 types of chat between 4 people. The vegetables were fresh, well spiced, and the samosas were deep fried well so they didn't have that overcooked or sogged-out consistency. The sauces were also very fresh and flavorful. Our main courses which consisted of both meat and vegetarian dishes between the 4 of us were great! Meat was super tender and the vegetables were not over cooked. Every time we go there we are greeted with friendly smiling faces and soon became friends with the staff after only a few visits. I highly recommend it as the best Indian restaurant in the area. You won't be disappointed!

The Industrial chic decor is cool, and the menu is varied nicely. But the noise level is off the charts- it's like a giant echo chamber! Even with a moderate crowd you could not converse across a table. Definitely drawing the 30 something professionals. A bit pricey for the portion sizes and the service was less than good. Might give it another go- but if you can't hear the other person unless your literally next to them, what's the point?
The tofu is spot on. Can't go wrong with $3 sandwiches. The spring rolls are really good as well.

Spiro's is the kind of eating experience that you make of it. You can have a moderately priced meal and leave with a great experience. You can have an expensive meal and leave with a great experience. In any case, you're gonna have a great experience! First off, the owner, Harry, greeted us at the door. He is "salt-of-the-earth" and is a nice guy. You can tell he wants everyone to enjoy themselves. The waiter and the assistant are attentive to needs and I never had to worry about bread, filled water glassess, or other dining details. The chef came out and had a pleasant conversation and things got exciting when we found out he grew up in the East coast area. I felt like I was talking and served by family and not staff. The food was amazing. My mother had lobster (all 2-3 pounds), my father had some spaghetti type dish and calamari, I split a meal with my wife and we ate some chicken garlic noodle dish. We all shared our food with each other because each bite was delectable. We shared cheese cake....oh my, the cheese cake was dee-lish. Also, we were served ouso shots and my kids ate complimentary ice cream. And when I mean ice-cream, we're talking serious sundaes here and not some skimpy one-scoop fare. This place offers cozy romantic dining, or serves moderately large groups comfortably. There were 4 adults and 2 children and we were comfortable and didn't feel claustrophobic. My mother said it was the best dining experience she has had in several years. I would agree with her statement. There is full-service bar with a tv, a nice romantic fire place you can sit by, and outdoor seating that looks cozy and inviting. I think that Harry is a romantic at heart.
the soup sounds lackluster, but WOW!!. recommend anything on the menu. No,really! South Indian good food. Not mention the wait time is no more 10mins

This was sort of a weird place as far as I'm concerned. I did go on a Sunday which may be part of the weirdness. It's a super small joint with a few indoor and outdoor tables, a wine-bar-looking bar area and .... Hookahs. I had the herb roasted lamb pita and a glass of Pinot Grigio. The sandwich was good, nice quality, tasty lamb and homemade tzatziki sauce. The pita was fresh and moist. If you're a fan of extra sauce- holy cow, you get it. There was too much for me so I wished I had ordered it on the side. The server I had was efficient although not friendly at all. When the check came, I was shocked to find out that the miniature glass of Pinot Grigio I ordered was TEN freaking dollars!!! It wasn't even anything special... It was Santa Margherita which I think you can buy a whole bottle for the whopping ten bucks. Nice spot for a quick lunch. Next time I will be ordering the sangria special which everyone on here seemed to be fond of.

Burrata Crostone- a must have appetizer. Great combination of taste and texture. The taste of the jam, pesto, prosciutto, and the sourdough was a great combination, among with the crispiness of the sourdough. Wild Salmon over Greek Salad - wild salmon was cooked really well. The Greek salad was little below average. It seemed like the lettuce was too wet. Artisanal pizza - a friend ordered this so I unfortunately was not able to personally tell you how it tasted but it looked really good, which my friend confirmed tasted really good. From the looks of it the pizza was well drizzled with cheese on top, with the mix of the sausage and prosciutto. I will definitely order this next time I'm there. Gelato (espresso) - 3 scoops that tasted really good. Ricotta Doughnut - takes 10 mins to make! It was fresh. The outside was nice and warm. It's definitely something to share. It was a GREAT combination to eat with the Gelato. Would I go back? For sure, must try the Artisanal pizza.
Amazing food with gracious service in a gorgeous, sensuous setting. Finding a place like Ploy Thai is the reason i LOVE Yelp. Try this restaurant!

I got take out from Chiang Mai this past weekend and it was really tasty! I placed my order online, and it was ready, and most importantly correct when I picked it up. I was hesitant to order from a restaurant in the heart of broad ripple- especially on a weekend- because of parking, but they have their own dedicated parking lot which is great! I also liked that the ambiance was a bit more...modern than your typical hole in the wall Thai restaurant. I had the Red Curry with chicken- add extra veggies. It was a tad pricey, but that's what I get for adding the vegetables. I wish there had been a bit more curry sauce, but the entire container was full of veggies. No complaints there. Next time though I may ask for an extra side of the sauce.
Yes. 5 stars. We had the Pink lady and crazy salmon rolls plus Godzilla roll and eel avocado rolls. The plate was presented beautifully and all the rolls were awesome. We were very satisfied.

Ordered take out last night and it was fantastic! They were fast, friendly and the food was still piping hot when my fiancé brought it home. The yee-ro meet was so tender and the chicken was super moist. Delicious. Will be back!

We drove all the way from North Jersey to visit this place. Reminded me of the middle east. The food was so simple and fresh as arabic food should be. Everything was light, fresh, tasty and beautifully plated. This is like moms cooking, the fresh bread that baked off before it gets to your table is what makes this place worth a visit. If you like arabic food, you'll love Suraya.

Quite possibly the best Wonton Soup! {this is a review that I'm posting to again cause I couldn't leave a 2nd) I ordered here AGAIN! Still can't believe they deliver here. Ordered the same thing just added spring rolls. The dipping sauce is delish and they come 4 in an order. This place is soooo gooood! ORIGINAL REVIEW: Order Delivery and I couldn't believe they delivered to Fishtown. I'm sick so all I wanted was soup. But there's a $15 min for Delivery so I ordered Wonton Soup, Seaweed Tofu soup with Vegetable, and Basil Fried Rice. The wonton soup was BOMB DIGGITY!!! Get it. And you can probably get it delivered!

OMG this was such a huge dissapointment! My husband and I loved this place when it was downtown and we were so excited to see it open again in Gulfport. .. I have been 2 times now thinking the first time was a fluke, both times service was horrible, practically waited on ourselves, had to go inside for refills, ketchup, silverware And Our check... Today was the second and last time I will EVER go there the pork sandwich was cold and total congealed pork fat.. I am shuddering just thinking of my first bite... Do yourselves a favor and go next door to Stella's where the wait staff actually waits on you and the food is scrumptious. ...

I hands down LOVE this place. I eat here weekly, and have been for years. They know me and my family and give us a warm welcome every time. The food is always amazing. The buffet makes it easy to try new things. The chicken tikki marsala is the BEST I've tasted. The mango lassie is to die for. Also try the vegetable samosas. They are the best i have tasted from anywhere in this area. Matter of fact the best EVER. The wait staff is very attentative to your needs. They are excellent. It's very clean in this establishment, and the manager always comes over to make sure your meal is ok. Very humbling, sometimes he'll even serve food which is a plus. They are so good! You must eat here! As of lately, The price for the buffet per person has gone up. I'm guessing due to all the popularity. I remember when it was $12 per person, now it is $15. Considering it is all you can eat, and they offer appetizers, main dishes, and dessert, it still isn't that bad.

Had a late dinner here one evening around 10pm. The restaurant is a bit small, with not much room to feel comfortable. Our server is nice, so no complaint there. Now on to the food. Ordered: duck tacos appetizer, fried wings, Bo ne, and rice with grilled pork. -Duck tacos were ok. Had better elsewhere (pho bistreaux). -Fried wings with butter is a disappointment. I was expecting wings to be deep fried and then cook in some kind of garlic butter sauce. Instead, I got regular fried wings top off with burnt onions. It tasted quite bland. My bf and I each ate one piece. The rest I took home for my babies(dogs). -My bf order the rice with grilled pork. Entree came with white rice,vegetables,and two pieces of grilled pork. Total waste of money. He took one bite of pork and didn't even bother to try another bite. I took one bite myself and that was enough for me too. No seasoning on pork. No flavor. -I had the Bo ne dish. And I must say this is quite tasty. Chunks of beef and two sunny side up eggs cooked a hot skillet. It also came with bread, butter and pate spread. The sauce on the skillet is hot and flavorful. This dish is the only thing that I would recommend trying. So to sum up my experience. Decor C, service B, food C-. I probably won't go back. There are so many other better vietnamese restaurant to choose from in the city.
The best trini food in philadelphia area. The service was beyond great. (5+ stars for service) Had pepper shrimp and it was one of the best things I've ever had.
Chicken tikka masala and butter chicken are phenomenal! Hands down, the best Indian restaurant in Nashville!!!

I've been here a few times now and it never disappoints. The place isn't much to look at (very store front, eat and go) and the neighborhood lends a "be careful about where you park your car" feeling, but even knowing this I will keep coming back. It gets kinda crowded at lunchtime, both in terms of the number of people coming in (there is a hospital right across the street) and the single woman trying to keep up with them, so if you can get there a little earlier or during off hours it may be to your benefit if you don't like waiting. I always get a bowl of Pho and Vietnamese spring rolls, both of which are always fresh and full of flavor and I wash it down with a Thai iced tea. Overall a great little gem of a place that hasn't disappointed me yet!
Very good food .. Loved the South Indian breakfast varieties .. !! Unlimited dosa and appam ! Must go place for a good Indian buffet !

Came here for lunch while visiting for a conference. Service was ok, we didn't know that you have to go up and place your order so we ended up sitting there for some time. Expected amazing flavor since it was on Tripple D however compared to others it was mediocre. Don't get me wrong, the food was good but nothing to write home about. I ordered the honey butter yardbird and beef ribs. The ribs were my fave. The portions in my opinion were small. Wasn't outstanding, just ok.

So, as anyone who knows me can attest, I am a very adventurous eater. Give me your swine, your offal, your game- I'll try just about anything put in front of me. That makes the fact that I only ever order one thing at Basil Spice such an aberrant pattern of behavior. I go to Basil Spice for the best Tom Ka Gai that I have ever had. That's it. I have had transcendent experiences with this soup. I won't go into too much detail about what it does to me, but lets just say its all good. So, what makes their Tom Ka better than all the rest? The answer that keeps coming to mind as i write is that it JUST IS BETTER. I know this seems like a copout, so just let me just try and explain. Its all about the broth. That lemongrass, galangal (a cousin to ginger), and fish sauce concoction- oh, that sweet, sweet fish sauce funk. Throw in whole mushrooms, thai basil, ribbons of tender chicken breast, quartered tomatoes that burst when bitten into, and a dusting of crushed red pepper and you have a symphony on your hands (I guess it would be in your mouth in this case). This soup is all about balance in the broth and Basil Spice has nailed it. The sweet coconut, the biting and almost medicinal galangal, the perfume of lemongrass and basil, the bright acidity of the tomatoes, and the depth of flavor provided by the right amount of fish sauce funkiness... Am I rambling? Anyway, go to Basil Spice. Try their Tom Ka. I've had some of their other food and it has all been good, very good. I just have an addiction that only their Tom Ka can feed. I hope this has been helpful. I'm off for another bowl. Maybe I'll see you there sometime.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: This review comes from a customer service standpoint. For Valentines Day I booked two cooking classes with Lanna. I paid $40 to reserve two seats. Unfortunately the day before the class, I had to cancel. I didn't know how to do so online so I emailed Glenn. He was not only understanding of the situation but genuine and kind. I didn't expect to get my $40 back, but he sent me a refund check that day. It really helped me out and I will definitely be rescheduling the classes. Thank you Lanna Thai for being wonderful.

We had a farewell lunch for one of our colleagues and we decided to give it a try. We were a batch of 8 with indian and american members. Obviously this not to our expectations and most of the colleagues (except 1) were not satisfied with the buffet. The items are very less and they too not so tasty. This is just another restaurant to fill your tummy with some stuff. I would recommend you to go to McD or BK for a sandwish and fries instead of going here.

Jerk chicken with cabbage and rice and beans - Good b bq style jerk nothing mind blowing but a but on the spicy side ( I like!) -Cabbage was mixed with corn and green beans. Different from what I ever see..best part of my meal - rice and beans, if I had hot sauce I would of enjoyed it more. overall it is good but not the best out of trenton area.

Ordered the Orchid Combination Pho and pork & shrimp spring rolls to take out. First, you must order the large Pho to take out......so happy because I have a great midnight snack and all I have to do is reheat the absolutely delicious broth. The spring rolls were filled with crunchy fresh ingredients and tasty pork and shrimp. Great dipping sauce with just the right hint of heat. The Pho flavors are still dancing in my mouth. Beefy broth, freshest veggies, cilantro, basil and bean sprouts. Soooo glad I have seconds in the fridge. I will definitely be returning here before the last day of my vacation.

not the best but not the worst indian food i've eaten. i was in a hurry and grabbed some food from their buffet. for less than 10 bucks, i had a very filling meal of chicken korma, chicken tikka masala, channa dal, and saag paneer over basmati rice. buffet food is based on price by weight and obviously very affordable. the flavor of the different dishes was comme-ci, comme-ca. i'd still head back to the indian restaurant on south st for future meals, but this place is completely acceptable for a quick, filling meal at an affordable price. bonus: staff is friendly. bonus2: the restaurant is super clean.

I had the vegetable spring roll and the yellow curry. I really wish they offered a fried vegetable spring roll. As usual with what is more accurately called a summer roll or salad roll, it's really super bland and the noodles seem wormy when paired with the chewy rice paper. The sauce can sometimes save it, but the sauce was a sort of tamarind cough syrup, as opposed to something light and bright and sweet or something very spicy, which would have worked. The yellow curry did the trick, but it was a touch minimal. Mine only had tofu potatoes and onions in it. Typically, there are other vegetables included.

Not much to look at from the outside, don't let that scare you away though. The food, pho, and service was excellent! Large portions, fresh ingredients, very flavorful. Our first visit here and won't be our last. Definitely a hidden gem in Trenton!
The combo beef pho was PHOnomenal. Broth was spot on. Friendly service. Highly recommend this cute little place ! Park on the side street across from hospital.

Came here a couple nights after opening night and were not disappointed! The whole snapper and duck carnitas were the highlights. The meatballs were unique and reminded me more of a kebab. Chef Fabio was nice enough to greet us which meant a lot. Looking forward to returning.

This is my first time trying Liberian food. I absolutely loved it. I had fried red snapper and jollof rice. The fish was well seasoned and very tasty. I've never had fish with the head on it and I was a little hesitant on ordering it but I am glad that I did. The jollof rice was also delicious. They give you plenty of rice. They were out of the potato greens. I will try that the next time I order. I ordered from UberEats and the food was still hot when it got to me.

So I won't lie this is the only play I have ever tried greek food at, and since i've never had a bad experience with a good truck a good way to get started right? I enjoyed it it was fresh hot, a good gyro, not that I have anything to compare it to LOL. I will be back.

Oh my gosh finally some incredible Thai food that too at reasonable prices. For my palate this area had no decent restaurants, our business is on Flagship Drive and I think I will be eating here at least every other day. Been twice in two days! Tried only Thai food so far, thankfully it's not the sweet version they most places in Tampa have. I have missed good Thai food since I moved from Dubai and have travelled to Thailand so I know how Thai food must taste And this is it :) The owners are lovely too and Joy was such a Joy to chat with. P.S - the place is spotless and hygiene standards seem impeccable. It's not as compact as typical Chinese takeaway and comfortable enough to eat there. If you try Chinese regularly and never tried Thai this is where you can have a super start. Can't wait to take my darling husband here. Will update on sushi when I try some.

Good food. However inconsistent with hours and selection. I've went on multiple times at different times of the day and they did not have jerk, or vegetables. Wish they were more consistent in service and hours.

We went to this location since we were in the area, and I've been wanting to try an Asian restaurant closer to Murfreesboro assuming it'd be better than some of the sub par Asian spots closer to where we live :) I got the Sukiyaki and really enjoyed it. Boyfriend got the Pad Krao Prao and it was pretty good as well. I asked the server for some extra cilantro since cilantro is so good and makes everything taste better. I don't think she was too happy about the request, but she brought it out to me and there was a lot so at least I was happy. I would go back if I'm ever near the area, I'll have to try the location closer to me in the meantime!

Very good restaurant offering dishes from several Asian countries. I had Vietnamese Rolls (Spring Rolls) and Spicy Noodles, and it was more than I could eat. Great flavor, very fresh, healthy and good service. I will go back when traveling in the area again.

This great little coffee house is my favorite, hands down, in the general area. Cozy, eclectic and charming...it really has a homey ambiance. Much of that is due to the way the people working there seem to be an extended family and get along so well. Granted, at times, it may seem impossible to wring a smile out of some of the staff and this may put some off. Personally, I like the challenge. Why the tall Goth(ish) Goddess isn't on the runways in NY or Paris is a mystery to me. Other bagels pale now in comparison to their light, deliciously fresh ones and the coffee is great. To those who bemoan the size of the large cup being too small, I say sip it more slowly. They also have all the fixings to embellish your brew; cinnamon and chocolate. I like the "0h so dirty" spoon cup... Best of all it's not a roosting area for a sea of stressed out students unlike some neighboring coffee shops. The self-entitlement level is low... At any given time you will find a nice mix of people there, including the occasional mommy/ baby parade; testimony to this place's magic is that doesn't trouble me in the slightest. Normally I cringe at coffee shop creche, but there is a such a nice sense of calm here usually, that even the babies seem to succumb . Maybe it's the seemingly endless Michael Jackson soundtrack that entrances them; but even that is forgivable.
Great vegetarian options. For those that love spice, they can make it really spicy which I LOVE!! Very flavorful.
Came down to watch the Cardinals World Series. The crowd is great, minus the Cardinals efforts to botch game 1. Great special through October, 1/2 off bottles of premium wine!

I travel to Blue Bell a couple of times a year, and always make it a point to visit this place. It's not the best Thai food that I've had, but it is the best in the area. The serve with a smile and you almost never have to wait. That's enough to draw me in!

My friend and I decided to check this place out on a whim. I had the red curry with chicken and my friend had the general tsos chicken. Both were absolutely delicious. Best Thai food I've had yet. I'm only in the area for a short time but I will miss this place for sure. Price for these two meals and a sweet tea was $26. Only thing I wasn't impressed with was the sticky floor and the sticky table... Not cool.

Food: 4 Decor: 3.5 Ambiance: 3 Service: 4.5 Value: 4 Very nice atmosphere compared to their suburban competitors. Food isn't quite as good though. It is an affordable byob, so we'll probably be back more.

doesnt taste good... =/ overpriced 9 dollars small portions pho hahah small place I asked for my rare thinly sliced beef on the side It said it came with it on the menu I ordered in vietnamese but had to use english for them =D no problem hah She came back later and said the cook said it doesnt come with rare thin beef I said its on the menu, and i can read the vietnamese XD She said no.. I said forget it just cancel it. She came back and gave me the meat and was like, "Do you still want it?!" I said fk yes! should have said no, it wasnt good. Im pretty sad that I have to stay here for school another few years and theres nothing good to eat around here. ;_;

The atmosphere of this place is funky since they share their dining room with Port O Subs and the back alley of the restaurant leads to the Supermarket but it's all good in the neighborhood if you have good broths for your noodle soups... I had their Spicy Beef Soup and it was pretty good. Noodle Soups always hit the spot after a lot of drinking and a lot of drinking is what we did all weekend so this was definitely comfort food in the middle of our Reno Drinking Binge.... I didn't try their Pho though so I may try that the next time I come here... Be ready to drive out here if you want to try a better option than your Downtown Reno Vietnamese eateries....

Korean Fried Chicken. I almost feel like that's my entire review. The stuff is amazingly addictive. At Umami, Korean Fried Chicken means huge, crispy, saucy, flavorful chicken wings that taste sweet and savory all at once. I think I could eat them for breakfast, lunch, and dinner and still want more. We arrived one Sunday evening after having bookmarked the place for months. There was a huge party in the corner, but otherwise the place was pretty quiet (although it was a Sunday). The staff took a bit to get around to us at first (there was only one waitress - I presume the large party did not call ahead), but service was surprisingly quick after the initial delay. I ordered a beef miso ramen, and my girlfriend ordered the chicken bento. We decided to get Korean Fried Chicken just to try it. I figured a small order would be the size of an appetizer, not a meal (spoiler alert: I was wrong). All of our portions were HUGE. The ramen came out in a stainless steel mixing bowl it was so large. It was good, and there was a lot of variety of ingredients, but I always seem to forget how much I don't really like ramen. My girlfriend's bento was also surprisingly big. She had generous servings of savory-sweet teriyaki chicken, crispy tempura (vegetables and shrimp), and what looked like an entire California roll, all served with a delicious dipping sauce. It was an expensive meal on paper, but the portions are so large that the one meal bought lunch for most of the week. If you aren't big leftover eaters, plan to split some of the portions, but try the fried chicken!

Please avoid this place. As Indians, we went in expecting some good, tasty desi dishes, however, we were really disappointed. We went there for dinner and ordered a pretty standard lamb dish. It tasted like meat swimming in a bucket of tomato ketchup. When we asked the waiter if this was indeed the dish we ordered he said yes, and later, after we paid the bill admitted that the chef had changed the recipe last minute. Not cool! The naan tasted like naan from a packet and they charged us 3.95 a piece for frozen cardboard! Btw, they charged us for the lamb dish (that the chef had changed without telling us!) The place was empty when we walked in, and that should have been our first warning, but oh well. Awful food, very high prices, and a wait staff that clearly does not have customer service as its priority.

Went here for lunch with a few colleagues on one of their suggested places to try out in Tarpon. The place was in a strip mall and looked pretty unassuming from the outside. It seemed pretty busy but we were seated promptly. The service was on the slow side because there was only one person working the dining room and register, not good for a busy Friday during lunch rush. The decor was okay, nothing fancy. Now for the food. It was really good. I had the panang curry with duck. I asked for medium because they said hot was really hot. I should have asked for hot. My friends had pad thai and a tofu dish, soup, salads, and spring rolls. Like I said the food was very good but nothing spectacular, I've had many very good Thai experiences so thats why I will not give more than 3 stars (would prefer to give 3 1/2 stars) especially with the slow service and mediocre atmosphere. Would I come back? definitely if I am in the area and in the mood for Thai. I would not make a special trip to come here. If you are in the area, definitely check this place out.

business_name: Lanna Culinary School and Events Center
text: The misses and I decided to try Lanna Thai cafe a few days ago, instead of our usual bankok cuisine, and we made a huge mistake. Lanna is overpriced, considering how small the portions and quality are, and the experience was definitely disappointing. I ordered the chicken pad Thai, and found a shrimp tail in my noodles. The chicken tasted rubbery, like it had been frozen for too long, (the noodles were dry, and dont hold a candle to bankok cuisine, or a taste of thai.) My wife had the beef Pad si eew, and ew was right. the beef was even worse than the chicken, it took so long to chew it that eventually my gag reflex activated, and my wife stopped eating it. The music was annoying, our waiter, who identified himself as the owner's son, opted to play video games instead of refilling our waters, and I found the atmosphere to be a depressing mix of inconsistent decoration, and bland wastes of imagination in the form of vague statements like "Gourmet" written on the walls. its only redeeming feature was that it was right next to Pathways, where I got a pack of tarot cards, and a piece of quartz that almost made that terrible meal worth it. anyways, my wife and I will go to Bangkok cuisine from now on, and suggest you do too. if you want a to have well made thai food, like we did, avoid Lanna Thai cafe.
Very good Thai Restaurant. My husband and I were very impressed with the food, the service and the entire experience. Very attentive waitress. We will be back soon.

I've had the food and it's very good. But last time I went they were understaffed so we left after 20 minutes of wait to be asked for our order. We didn't even get water. Get your act together Noddi Thai!

This is probably my favorite Thai restaurant in the city. And I say 'probably' because while I had a great dining experience, it was my first and only time to date. So I'll need to update this review after a few more visits, but if first impressions are lasting, I'll remove the 'probably.' Food - authentic! And if you want spicy, ask then to crank it up! The appetizers weren't that big of a deal to me, but the noodle entrees.... Mm mm.. The evil jungle princess and Shrimp pad Thai really did it for me. The pad Thai was the perfect blend of spicy and sweet, and the noodles were just the right chewy consistency. The jungle princess was extremely flavorful - so much coconut flavor. My wife had the drunken noodles and it was great as well. But I got a level 2 spice level, while she got a 3, so I really couldn't eat much of hers. But she loved it. It is a BYOB, which is always fun, and the dessert options seem very authentic as well. My friend could not stop raving about her cup of coffee after, so I guess I'll be trying that next time!

This place was my worst experience of my entire night being ask to leave an establishment after I purchase my drink not allowed to finish an your only reason was my prescription glasses tint was to dark for you, really! Or is their more intent behind this !if you just refunded my money have no problem spending my money where I'm accepted! The people of Nashville is much better then this establishment please support unity

Extremely popular place! They are located in a strip mall with 7-11 as an anchor. Parking is a challenge M-F for lunch is a challenge but worth it. For a tiny Pho restaurant I am shocked they haven't moved to a larger location. HINT: THEY HAVE YUMMY SPRING ROLLS "TO GO". PRICE IS RIGHT OND THE PEANUT DIPPING SAUCE IS CRAZY GOOD.
The premier Afghan restaurant in Philly, few places can give this joint a run for its money.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: This tiny family run restaurant is located inside St. Louis Halal Meat, Groceries and Food in a small strip mall set back off of Page Blvd. Our group tried several dishes and each were simply delicious! We ordered samosas (secret, non-menu item) and they were fried, fat pillows of peas and potatoes and they weren't greasy at all. We also had goat korma, goat Keema, chicken Tikka Masala, Chicken Seekh kebab, chicken curry and basmati rice. The portions were large and service was very attentive. This no frills place serves up great Pakistani food and the owners are very gracious. I highly recommend for a casual night out!

One of the best meals I've had in a long time. Simply awesome...we ordered everything and it was all amazing. We would definitely recommend for a date, social night out or celebration. Make a reservation.

Delicious food. Well prepared. Courteous service. I had mixed vegetable egg foo young. It was fried light, crisp on the edges, not greasy and chock full of fresh vegetables. On the Japanese side, I had the seaweed salad and it was terrific! Included julienned cucumber, pickled ginger and sesame seed garnish. Well pickled, not soggy. BY FAR, THE best Asian cuisine for delivery in my neighborhood. This will be my go-to from now on!! Great Job!!!

Very good food, I had Rad Na Talay which I did not see on the menu, so I asked them and they were very nice to make it up for me and it was absolutely delicious it was so good, and I had a lot, so I had left overs to take for lunch for work the next day so delicious I was very happy with this restaurant.

PLOP PLOP, FIZZ FIZZ, OH WHAT A RELIEF IT IS....GROSS!!! Maybe because "Pho" was in the name I should have ordered that, but come on! Ewwwww I still haven't eaten a full meal since I ate here, I am finally getting back to solid foods. I got the shrimp fried rice and tofu fresh rolls. I knew when I was eating it that something was "wrong." The little shrimp in the fried rice that looked like dirt were "Chernobyl" orange in color and tasted bad. I think there was an uncooked one in there somewhere but I just covered it up by the overly dry, horrible tasting rice. The fresh roll tofu was going slightly bad, and the lettuce inside was old and the rice paper was slightly dry and chewy, but I ate them anyway because the rice was so bad and I was starving. I didn't have full blown food poisioning, but I had a slight version of it that makes me never want to eat Asian food again for a while. The one star goes to the great staff and clean place. Full bar. Everyone else who has written reviews must have been drunk or the pho is better. Sorry but I am being brutally honest here.

This is the ultimate in Afghani food. The chicken, daal, and lamb are all very well done. The eggplant is really flavorful. Their spicy green chutney served with Afghani bread is amazing! Now, why not 5 stars? This place is *only* about food. If you care about ambiance, a super-smiley waiter, or fancy dessert options, don't come here. You'll just join the rest of the reviewers giving this place 3 stars. BUT, if you're into straight-up, authentic Afghani food, this is your neighborhood place. For Philly locals - food quality here is better than 2 leading olde city Afghan counterparts.

This has become one of my favorite spots for now. I've been about 5 times including both take out and eat in. Let's start with the food.. Seafood Potato greens- good, but not my favorite. Made with potatoe greens,plump shrimp, blue crab, a piece of salt smoke fish and accompanied by white rice. Regular potatoe greens-good, but again not my favorite. Made with some smoked meats I beleive and accompanied by white rice. Chuck rice and gravy-good, this is a reddish sauce of peppers ,tomatoes and meats accompanied by a green rice. Palm butter stew-good, it is a brown stew/sauce loaded with seafood (shrimps,crab,fish)and accompanied by white rice. Palava sauce-my favorite. It's made with some type of greens, meat, and palm oil accompanied by white rice. All of these are referred to as "soup", but they seem to contain lots of oil which is very different for me when I think of soup, but a good different. Fried Talipia- fried way too hard, I dont think I'll ever order that again. Fried snapper- soo good, fried to perfection and topped with onions and peppers. Grilled Snapper- very reminiscent of the fried snapper minus the peppers and onions. Country dry rice- soo good that everytime I think of ordering a different rice I can't bring myself to cheat. Aticheke and plantains- just ok, needs some sauce but not bad. And for dessert...Banana bread with pecan ice cream- soooooo good, the bread is not really sweet but it's just right for someone who doesnt really want anything too sweet. Now let's get down to the service.. The place isn't big at all and when it gets busy the wait time its over an hour and a half. The waitresses are super nice, thoughtful, and very accommodating. It just takes a while for the food to be served to you but if you don't mind waiting for at least 30 minutes on a regular day then you should be good to go. Oh and don't forget to BYOB.

You can't go wrong with buffet style Indian food. They have a huge selection with items I had never even heard of-- try the chai tea and make sure to save room for the Gulab Jamun. The restaurant is calm and peaceful, and the staff is super friendly. Definitely will be back!

With so many chain restaurants in Mt. Juliet, this spot is a true gem! We've been 3 times now. The food is on point, and I like that you can request mild, medium or hot. Very authentic indian food. Our server was Justice, and based on other reviewers, they were right; she is friendly and very helpful.

Although it is cheap and quick, the quality of the food has gone down a bit from the first time I ate at this location. The service can be piss poor as long as I get my food done right but it just isn't doing it for me anymore. But it'll do for a quick fix since it is still cheap in price.
Went to food truck Thursdays in faust park. Had the classic beef and lamb gyro. There was a ton of meat on this gyro. Great sauce and topping. Differently be looking for this truck again.

Wow! Super good! The wife's Bun Thit Nuong was excelent! I had the Mi Xao Don was very good and the pho, was super and the wife said better than 777! It looks like we might have found the best Vietnamese place in Northern Nevada when it comes to real Vietnamese food! (And after just spending a month in Saigon, I know!) (Wife spent two months!) BTW, the owner used to work for 777 for over 5 years! Two very big thumbs up and 5 stars! Food: 5 Stars! Service: 5 Stars! Overall: 5 Stars!

While I am not an expert on Indian cuisine, I've had enough to give an honest review. First, the food is well prepared. I had Palek Paneen. Pardon the surely misspelled name. My friend had the Chicken Masala. They were both flavorful. The garlic naan was my absolute favorite. As previous reviews indicated, the prices are a little high for this cuisine and service, but not this area. This restaurant is in the "classy" part of the city. The servers are nice, but not engaging. I don't think anyone there has ever served, they never took any of the dirty dishes away. It looked like we were at the dishwashing station. That is one of my pet peeves, if I'm sitting here knocking around empty dishes every time I grab my water, something is awry. Apparently the place is still under construction as I had to use the restroom hovered over a toolbelt and tools. Tools were scattered all over the floor.

For an adventurous night out, my friends and I skirted off to an untrekked part of town for food -- the informally known as 'International Marketplace' for some truly authentic Ethiopian food. Service was charming. Food incredible. It's what I call experiential dining. You learn a lot about the culture - sharing food with friends from the same large plate, eating with your hands using Ethiopian bread to scoop up lamp, chicken or beef dishes. I'd take a pass on the Ethiopian honey wine and trade that for what I've heard is incredible coffee to top off the night. They roast the beans right in front of you. Will definitely return to the International Marketplace and venture to my next ethnic experience.

I've been supporting this place monthly for 10+ years and seriously love the Vietnamese vegetarian hoagies! used to be 2.50 now I think they're 3.25 big deal, it is worth every penny! WARNING: MAY CAUSE A HEALTHY ADDICTION TO A GREAT HOAGIE!

I like this place. The decor is cool, and my wife and I were getting ideas for when we open our imaginary restaurant someday. The food, pretty great. The menu is a bit hard to navigate as everything on it is pretty unique to la mulita. I had to ask what at least 4 things were. So that being said getting around to ordering took awhile because I couldn't make up my mind. I ended up going with the server recommended tlayuda a sort of mexican pizza. It was awesome. My wife got the fish tacos and they remind me of the fresh catch fish tacos I loved when I was in San Diego. Very good. Washed it down with a mezcal mule, basically tequila that isn't from the tequila region in Mexico. All in all I recommend it. 30 bucks for 2 entrees, an appetizer and a drink. 4 stars because I had no idea what I was doing when ordering. I'm sure once I go more often, I'll be more comfortable with the menu.
Great food. Pricey for Indian food, but food is worth every penny.Sunday for brunch is the best deal with their food. Awesome garlic naan. Byob is always a plus

This restaurant had a great atmosphere and nice clean presentation. The food was was very tasty and good portion sizes. However the service was lacking. We arrived at 7:00 and was not greeted by anyone, we waited to be seated and it wasn't until the bartender discontinued his exchange with a customer and came from behind the bar to ask if how many would be in our party. When stated two and was told to seat ourselves. We then waited at our table to be serve and we observed by several wait staff before one gentleman asked if we had been helped. He provided us with water and menus and said he would attempt to find our waiter. The gentleman would return stating he guess he would be our waiter. He was an excellent waiter and very attentive. We completed our meal and them decided to order dessert, which we rarely do, after making a few choices, we were informed that they had only one of the six selections. I have mix review of this restaurant. The food was excellent however the service was lack luster. Thank you Sergi for making our first our first visit to this establishment pleasurable.

Been going here with my wife for years. Always pleased. Service is good. Takes time for the food to be served but I view this as good since it means that they don't just re-heat, the food is always fresh.

I want to start by saying that I don't typically write reviews unless I am genuinely awed by my experience. In the case of Pikpon Thai, I don't think I could really emphasize enough how incredible this place is. As somewhat of a connoisseur of Asian cuisine, I have become extremely selective of where I bring my business because I have exposed myself to many fine dining establishments. This is a blessing and a curse considering it has made me a much more fastidious eater especially in the realm of Asian cuisine. That being said, Pikpon Thai is your very own slice of Thailand and leaves virtually nothing be desired if you are on the hunt for incredible food, heartfelt staff, and a serene atmosphere. My first visit to Pikpon Thai felt like my hundredth, I was greeted with warmth and appreciation as if I were part of the family. Once seated, I noticed several avant-garde items on the menu and before I could inquire my server walked me through some of the more popular dishes and asked me questions to help decipher what might be ideal for me. I asked about a drink they serve called "Nom-Yen", a creamy pink smoothie reminiscent of bubblegum. I wasn't sure if I wanted to give it a try yet, but I gave her my entree order. Shortly after she returns with a plethora of condiments and explained the difference between the few and advised which ones would work well with my dish. Already highly satisfied with my experience, she returns moments later with a beautifully decorated (eight ounce) sample of this deliciously trendy pink drink. She stood in front of me awaiting the reaction of my first sip and when she saw that I enjoyed it, her eyes lit up in gratitude. This was especially potent to me because it was a true testament to the passion that goes into their cuisine, heightening my excitement and anticipation for my entree. I ordered what I believe is called "Nom Tok Neua", which is similar to Pho, but far more savory, soulful, and customizable. As I waited, I admired the beautifully tranquil and neo-traditional decor contrary to the typical Thai restaurant mugginess. The Pikpon soundtrack is anything but boring or dry, they play stuff like lofi hip-hop and soft-house that bring a fun and modern vibe to pair perfectly with the colorful, energetic aura of the dining room. When my food arrived it was aesthetically nothing short of spectacular; I'm not the Snapchat eats first type of dude, but this was justified. Anyway, I'm sure you can guess what came next. If you guessed mouthgasm, you are correct! An explosion of hearty protein and spices with the soothing balance of warm broth and vibrant greens. I got a 5-star dining experience for less than $20 and that isn't the only reason I keep coming back. I come here because this restaurant is comprised of genuine, caring, passionate, and talented folks who deserve nothing less than success in an overly saturated industry where the passion and compassion are few and far between. This review couldn't possibly help you conceptualize the experiences I have had at Pikpon Thai, I implore you to give this place a shot. Even if you aren't a huge fan of Asian cuisine they will tailor a dish around your preference, you just have to ask! Trust me, you will NOT be disappointed.

Don't let all the white customers fool ya :P they have some tasty Indian fare though maybe not super authentic! When we arrived at 6pm on a Wednesday, we got seated quickly but the place was pretty packed by the time we left at 7:45pm. We ordered everything mild, except the goat curry which we ordered medium, since my in-laws can't handle much spice. It was their first time trying Indian food so we kept it fairly safe and ordered crowd pleasers. What we ordered for Dinner: ** for group favs * Garlic Gobi ** * Samosa (2) ** * Butter Chicken ** * Shrimp Tandoori ** * Goat Curry - I liked it, but goat isn't for everyone * Chicken (bone-in) Biryani ** * Garlic naan & Cheese naan - solid but nothing spectacular * 2 Mango lassi drinks We ate the plates clean among 4 people. Nothing left :D
Stopped in for dinner..Naf naf grill is wonderful place. Good quality of Foods.. I would recommend it for sure..

How on god's green earth to people think this place is good?! Okay, so I'm critical of food but I know good food. And as a former service industry employee, I would NEVER send food back, complain about service, or tip less that 20%...and I didn't...but I wish I did. So allow me to be a little passive aggressive via Yelp. My bf and I checked out Dmitri's on the stellar recommendation of my trusted foodie ex-roomie. Upon arrival, we were seated quickly despite a seemingly long wait potential. The decor was cozy, with an open kitchen and brick walls. Upon realizing it was a BYOB, I snuck away to grab a bottle of good beer from The Foodery nearby. Apparently the whole 20 min I was gone, a server hasn't approached my bf once...this after I told the hostess on the way out that I'd be back and he would like to order while I was gone! So the service was consistently bad. The server took exceedingly long to check in on us, if at all. Maybe of the two hours we were there, she checked in thrice. We were never told the specials and she didn't sound at all enthused in the food. Probably with good reason, because it sucked. I hate to say it because we heard such good things, but service aside, Dmitri's was an overall disappointment. The baba was decent, but that and the cucumber tatziki was completely under salted. The grilled octopus that followed tasted very Sysco--double refrozen and fishy, with a gritty and chewy textures and far too much vinegar as a tenderizer. We didn't eat more than 2 bites of it thinking it was rancid and could cause food poisoning. Next was the plum (tomato) pasta and seafood combination, essentially a mish mosh of not-so-fresh seafood, over cooked to rubberization in tomato juice. It was okay. The pasta was WAY overcooked and not at all seasoned (how does this happen at a food establishment?!). The sauce looked like it was made with canned tomatoes and a few shreds of basil...and nothing else. Again, we barely had two bites of it. Our server had cleared our app plates and never brought us new silverware or plates. We picked at the "food" before packing it up and heading home. I doubt we'll eat the leftovers. I mean, you can't really reheat overcooked spaghetti. The only saving graces were the decor and the sweet couple never to us that sparked up conversation. Sadly, we won't be back to Dmitri's as we both left craving ANYTHING but that. (Like seriously would have rather had McDonald's...ew. And that's sacrilegious to say as a foodie). Maybe you guys will have better experiences but we won't waste our time, money, and tastebuds again.

Very fresh food! You leave here not feeling bad about yourself. I usually get the falafel and the savory spinach pies. They are both delicious. Also, the assortment of iced teas that they have are quite enjoyable. The environment is very welcoming, and the people are extremely friendly and helpful. The assortment of cookies and pastries is also to die for. Another cool thing is that they allow you to pay after you eat.

Family owned Authentic Jamaican food made by owner's mother in the kitchen. Lunch is always great and the prices are very good. Reminds me of the real deal Jamaican food I've had in Jamaica. Lots of slow cooked meats with lots of spice!

Maybe I'm used to my hole in the wall Greek food, but I thought Taziki's was nothing special after my trip this weekend. I stopped in with my BF and it was pretty empty on a Saturday afternoon, but has a very nice atmosphere. The restaurant is clean and open with lots of space. I also noticed right away that they offer wine and beer and they have a nice outdoor seating area. We ordered the grilled lamb gyro and chicken salad with 2 waters, and it was around $18.00. Maybe I was thrown off by expecting the food and prices of my run of the mill Greek places, but I thought it was a bit steep for what we received. The chicken was bland and the lamb was not shaved in strips like most Greek places. The lamb was just OK and I liked the dill sauce but overall it was lacking. I had the tomato cucumber salad on the side that was my favorite part of the meal because it was seasoned well. I also had potato chips on the side, which I found odd. I would have ordered something else if I had known. Overall, I've had better and will go somewhere less glamorous for my Greek food because I feel that you pay for the interior rather than a good meal.

Stopped in for lunch one day last week, and the lunch special was so delicious that I went back for lunch again today with my daughter. We ordered a side of naan and I'm not a big fan (I prefer tandoori naan), but the chicken kabob, sauce, and rice were really delicious!

My favorite thing to order here is the Yemisir Wett (red split lentils in berberre sauce) and Shiro (pureed split peas cooked with onion and garlic). Both come out on one large enjera-lined platter (and another plate piled high with enjera for dipping), and every time we've gone they've added small sample portions of other vegetarian dishes. The Yekik Alecha (garbonzo split beans flavored with curry and herbs) is actually really mild, as is the Denech Alecha (a chunkier dish of carrots and potatoes in sauce). The thing I crave the most is that enjera...it's yeasty, spongy goodness. It is so fun to tear pieces off and pick up mouthfuls of curries (for lack of a better word) with it.
I love this place, always good food. I've been going here since the place opened. I usually get the cashew chicken, or the pad see-ew. We usually eat here at least once every other week. Always solid

I enjoyed visiting this restaurant for the lunch or early bird special. Yesterday I was very disappointed that my favorite dish, Kao Soy made with egg noodles in a curry broth wasn't with egg noodles this time. I started to wrap the noodles around my fork and noticed the texture was really soft and the color was white. I took a bite and realized that it was not egg noodles. I told the server then she asked the chef. The chef said it was egg noodles. Being Asian and growing up eating noodles I knew that what I just ate was white vermicelli rice noodles. How was I supposed to argue with the chef? Should I have asked for the raw form, the package...Now I'm not sure if I will return to the restaurant because my favorite dish was destroyed!

Bitars is nothing special on the inside and that is why I love it so much. It is such a home feeling inside that is simple. The gyro's are probably one of the best I have ever had in my life, but please don't tell my grandmother that. The selection in their market is pretty awesome and their selection of pastry's are super and everything tastes great.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Mediocre at best. Expensive, sloooooow service, and bad tasting food; probably to compensate for the location & rent. Don't believe the positive reviews here. They even recommended a warm bitter beer and charged me $18 for it. Wish they would have told me the price first. Would have had a Diet Coke. Avoid at all costs and head down 2 blocks to the Bombay. Excellent cuisine, reasonable prices, and a homey atmosphere. Don't waste your money
Lovely Kurdish family business near the zoo. Great price. Nice atmosphere. Plenty of food for 30 bucks for three of us. I will be seeking out more Kurdish restaurants because of this one.

I love this place! Best Thai that I've found in Nashville, both atmosphere and authenticity. This is the real deal! If you've never had Thai food, this is where you need to go. The yellow and red curry are delicious and full of vegetables. I especially love the pad see eww with chicken. It's spicy and packed with flavor. The staff are so sweet and generous. I'll come back again and again

I hate reviewing my work day lunch spots in fear that people will find out how delicous this place is and my wait for a banh mi will increase, but this place deserves a 5 star review.. It's yummy as hell and they're super fast and somewhat efficient. Don't piss off the little old lady taking orders and you'll be fine. Try their yakamein and stick to pork banh mi as it is still a corner store and those are safe bets and always good.
Excellent Thai food. Had a Pad type dish with wide noodle that was great and summer rolls with shrimp. 5 stars across the board. You wont be sorry.

One of the best happy hours in the area. They have plenty of options of wine and appetizers. The pizzas were a really good deal and were delicious. They have outdoor and indoor seating. The staff was very flexible with our large group and the food came out fairly quickly.

Spice Finch is impressive. Decor is light and fresh, service is impeccable, food is very good. My companion and I shared 6 dishes and a bottle of wine. Bill was $198.00 before tip. In comparison to Saraya I would say the food at Saraya is a bit better. Spice Finch is more centrally located if you're not driving. Like them both.

Food was generally good although I wasn't as blown away as I was hoping to be. The mushrooms were delicious and meaty although some pieces were dried out from being over roasted. The baba ganoush was quite good and the pomegranate was a nice touch. tbh didn't think it was that much better than my favorite takeout spot in NYC (Sahara's) but it was still good The fatteh is delicious and rich and buttery, and you really do taste the brown butter. Probably horrible for you but it's so yummy. Only gripe is that they don't do takeout for dinner since their kitchen is too busy.
Delicious!!! Enjoyed the tom ka gai soup and pad se ew!! Happy to have read the positive yelp reviews that brought me to this little gem while on business. Forget the chain restaurants and eat local.

Baguette Deli has always been my go to sandwich shop in town. Along with everyone else's comments, I will agree to the lack of friendliness of the people who work here, but that doesn't bother me so much. Everyone used to rant and rave about how good this place was, but each time I go back the owners seem to raise the prices and have become very stingy with things. The average bahn mi sandwich is usually $3-5 anywhere you go. This places prices are now outrageous! Not cheap anymore for the average Vietnamese sandwich shop. They also no longer give free water and you even have to pay for garlic chili sauce, and sriracha. First place I've been to that sells Pho and doesn't have the spicy chili sauces on the table. Don't get me wrong, I love a few of the employees here and the food is great. I just don't see myself or many other regulars coming back if they continue to raise prices and be stingy.

Great, causal place to have lunch. Although the restaurant is known for their Greek food, I was in the mood for something light and healthy. I had the salmon salad with avocado, pine nuts, and red onions. It was absolutely delicious! I appreciated that the creamy dressing was put on the side (without me asking) and not drenched all over the salad.

I went to this restaurant today food is very good and the service when you order is good too but I got my order wrong I order a bowl of soup and I got a cup of soup until I spoke to the lady and she changed and also my kenaf was suppose to come with sauce and two sides I just got one side and no sauces I have to call the lady again for my sauce otherwise the kebab will Tate to me very dry but I wasn't able to ask for my second side missing it was just too much ....

Authentic middle eastern delicious fare. We came here for brunch near noon on Sunday and were graciously greeted and seated immediately. The decor is very clean crisp. I ordered a falafel platter, three fresh made falafels with hummus, tabouli, a fresh pita and some fries. I'd say the fries to be the only part I didn't love, a little too greasy. My wife had the chocolate yogurt; sprinkled with pistachio, dried cherries, honey, mint and cocoa powder. Crisp flavor and would've liked the bowl if we weren't in public. We shall return for dinner one evening and try some of the meat offerings. Great addition to the neighborhood.

I usually get stuck in a rut, not getting to eat here often I really enjoy the Yum Woon Sen (I may have miss spelled that), shrimp salad with bean thread noodles, cashews, tomatoes etc. is Yum, Yum Yummy! Cashew chicken, Larb gai, and last tried the Panang Fish have all been fantastic. Soft shelled crab is heavenly. Appetizers are spot on. The wait staff is always polite, attentive and smiling.
Great atmosphere. Good food. Live music. Friendly staff.

Good pho. Service, meh. Not bad, but not the greatest either. I ordered the P2, which was noodles with steak. This very a very good dish, and I would recommend. If you're looking for a dish with a good amount of meat, not too much but not too little, this is the dish for you. Now there's an option between getting a large size and regular size. I got the large but comparing with my brother, who got the same thing but size regular. There wasn't very much difference, so save yourself a dollar. The regular is already quite big and enough to satisfy a hungry adult. The crowd starts showing up around 7:30ish, and if you want to get seated without having to wait, I suggest arriving before 7:30. Very good family atmosphere. TV wasn't on, so don't expect to be watching sports. Very good for groups, and cool place to hang out overall!

Great Jamaican food. I usually get the curry goat, rice and peas, and cabbage with a beef patty. Very filling meal. Their brown stew chicken and jerk chicken are also very good. I'm gonna try to the red snapper soon. Don't sleep on their drink either. They're very delicious.

This is not the place to go for Greek food. Seriously. The Greek salad was quite pathetic. It had no feta, really ok'd bits of tomato, old green pepper. I took one bite. Very dissatisfied. Will not return.

My coworkers dragged me here for lunch. It's a smaller place but cheerfully decorated. I had the cold cut and my sandwich was tasty and filling. My other friends has miscellaneous other banh mi- lemongrass chicken, satay beef, chicken etc. Their comments were the other sandwiches were a little bit skimpy on the meats. We got there after lunch hour so there was no lineup. Service is efficient although we were a big group so it did take awhile for our sandwiches. I would certainly return if l was working in the area.

Disappointed with the quality of vegetarian food in the buffet. The food was tasteless, lacked spices and salt, and was colder than expected. Added to this, as we were leaving, the waiter was in an unusual rush to clear the tables, and he spilt food on my wife's rather expensive bag and dress, whilst clearing the tables... All in all, a forgettable experience that ensures that I will never visit this restaurant again....
I have been to this place multiple times and the food was great every time. Authentic Indian food. One of the best Indian restaurants I have been to.

What a great little spot! We had just come from St. Pete Beach and were looking for something other than the typical beachy bar menu. Menu is outstanding and offers a plethora of choices. The coconut shrimp app was fantastic and both our entrees came with black beans/rice, corn bread and plantains. YUM!

I never dreamed I would like octopus but it is delicious. The Greek wine pairings went well with my food choice. The Greek salad was fresh and I can't remember when I have had tomato that good in a casual restaurant before.The staff were very friendly and helpful. I can't wait to try more menu options!

I would give them 10 stars if I could. Best Mediterranean food since the Beirut in Toledo, Ohio. Chicken shawarma is absolutely amazing. Hummus is THE best, creamy and tasty. Grape leaves are fabulous and the order is 6-7 which is more than you receive anywhere else. I order fattoush every time and although not on the menu, they always make to order. They need to add to the menu! Owner is very kind and accommodating. The ambience is unassuming, authentic and very clean. Despite the language barrier, the owner and chef make the experience fantastic. I have been there 3 times in the last 5 days, once for just myself (first time), the second time for carry out for a dinner for 3, and the third time a carry out dinner for 5! Yum!! Thank you Palm Arabic! Please patronize this local restaurant so they are with us for years to come.

My boyfriend and I were on vacation in St. Pete and looking for a nice place to eat....The Pearl more than met the bill! We were greated by a very friendly hostess who sat us at a very romantic table next to the fireplace. The waitress, who was also quite friendly, was knowledgeable about the menu and made recommendations for food and wine pairings. We decided on the special, humus sampler and buffalo medallions preceded by fresh bread and salad....it was all nothing short of fabulous! Not only was the food amazing but the ambiance was so romantic with candles, low lighting, and a live acoustic guitarist. Was the perfect dinner to lead into a marriage proposal on the beach under the stars! My fiancé and I will definitely return here if we are ever back in the area!
Great atmosphere. Friendly staff. Amazing food. Grilled trout special was top notch!!

There are a huge wide of variety to choose from the buffet. The staff is polite, and friendly The place is clean and looks new They provide you with fresh baked nan bread as you enter, and its unlimited. They even have masala tea included with the buffet. Plus, its really cheap. Its $8.99 for lunch buffet on a weekend. Highly recommended

I ate here before seeing a movie. I ordered a combo burger. It was served cold, tasted frozen, under seasoned & bland. Never eating here again. Should have expected this from a food court in an almost empty mall.
Excellent! This restaurant easily accommodated our party of 8, and the food was great. They had a full range of vegan options, including tofu and gluten, basically available in any of the dishes.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Really good, but kind of slow. I guess they make everything to-order, and it shows. I chose a Lamb Biryani, and was very happy with the quality and quantity of the main course. I'm not East Indian, but I've eaten enough of that region's cuisine to know the good from the bad, and this is very good indeed.
TK is a gracious host. Very eager to have you try all the dishes he has to offer. If I would have known, he also serves Pho. I plan to get that next time!
great service and great decor the red curry and the pad thai was very good it was a little sweet but quite delightful I will most likely come by here again if I need a thai food fix.

Ok I live in Thailand part time and more than a bit obsessed with Thai food. I've eaten Thai all across the globe as well and I LOVE this place! The food at Meunfan Thai Cafe is fantastic and very authentic....... ok truely I LOVE IT! We had drunken noodles tonight (spectacular!) but I've tried many things from their menu and all have been top notch! Our favorite dishes are the eggplant tofu (amazing!!) and the crab cheese (crab Rangoon) is hands down the best I've eaten ANYWHERE in the world! Super friendly staff and a spotlessly clean restaurant are greatly appreciated! ***and no I'm not family!
Very nice family run restaurant. I take the whole family once a week for the lunch buffet. Good home cooking at a good price. Definitely worthwhile.

My office just ordered lunch from El Tipico unfortunately the order we received was not correct. We called the manager (Owner a woman) that stated that we are human and we make mistakes. Yes, understandable (we are human and we make mistakes)as the owner of the restaurant it is your duty to provide excellent customer service. My order was not completed, the food i ordered was not what i received. I didn't ask for the money back but to have the food made properly as i ordered it. She refused to make what i ordered and started stating i saw her make the plate for i know what was in there. Worst Customer service ever, took my money without giving me the food i paid for.

Terrible service, tasteless salmon, rubbery octopus, and BEWARE the 18% tip on the bill. We went to Dmitri's on Saturday, with 3 friends (a total of 5 in the party). Even though it was prime dinner time (~7 pm on a Saturday), the place was not even half full, so they were able to seat us immediately. The service started out mediocre, and then got progressively worse as the wait staff rushed us through our meal. The waitress made all the 'specials' sound uninteresting, and she took the appetizers off the table before we were finished. When she refilled my water glass, she poured over my partner's food, so that water dripped into his food. For appetizers, the beets were tough; the grilled octopus was so rubbery that we couldn't finish it; the mussels were bland; and the grilled vegetables were mediocre. The hummus was good. I ordered the salmon, and it was TERRIBLE. It was tough, dry, and inedible. The rice had no taste and had the texture of rice that has been sitting out too long. My partner ordered the escarole and garlic pasta. It was also mediocre because the escarole was overcooked and mushy, and the overwhelming flavor was of garlic. We've been to this Dmitri's before, about a year ago, and loved it because the food and service were terrific. In fact, the last time we were at Dmitri's, I raved about the grilled octopus. We specifically went back to Dmitri's for the grilled octopus, but this time, the octopus was among the worst that I have ever had. (Judging from other Yelp posts, the grilled octopus is inconsistent - sometimes good, sometimes rubbery.) Overall, we are very sorry to see that the restaurant has gone downhill.

Finally got an opportunity to go here for lunch and picked my go to Thai fav- pad Thai. The pad Thai with chicken was good and a great quantity for 2 meals which for me is always a plus. The $7.89 lunch portion came with 2 crab Rangoon which were good and freshly cooked. Sometimes the crab Rangoon can taste old and be cold since some places fry more than they should at a time. I also had the opportunity to try Thai ice tea which honestly did not blow me away. It looked pretty and refreshing- seeing a customer with a tall glass of ice with this location lightly brown and slightly orange drink prompted me to ask the waitress what it was, and she told me Thai iced tea. I got one to go. It was basically a black tea with milk and was sweet. It had a little lingering taste I couldn't quite describe- almost like overly brewed strong tea, so it wasn't quite bitterness, but I don't know how else to describe it. It was different. The only reason I gave this 4 stars was the pad Thai did not have any fresh garnish accompaniments- no shredded carrots or cabbage, no tablespoon of finely chopped peanuts. This is the only place in the area I have visited that doesn't have that, and I like to mix in the fresh garnish with the hot steaming pad Thai. Other than that the service was good, the environment was clean and neat and the pricing on the menu was competitive to others in the area.

This is our FAVORITE restaurant! The food has only gotten better since Patrick took over. We have been eating here for about 6 years... we never get tired of it. I am a vegetarian and my husband is not, so it is SO nice to have a place we BOTH equally love. A rare find :).
