We loved the decor before as we really liked the atmosphere, so we are not as thrilled with that now, but we hope the new decor gets finished soon so some of that ambiance is back. That would truly make it perfect! The "fries" are the best in town, the chicken shwarma, the veggie plate, the mujadara plate... YUM YUM YUM! And the pistachio baklava is delish too :). The new breakfast scramble was amazing too!

Not sure why I hadn't tried Ruby Cafe before but had some friends visiting from out of town and decided to give it a shot for lunch and was impressed. Honestly we didn't even look at the menu but instead just ordered the buffet, it was $10.95 and had a nice selection of items. They had 3 different types of rice (Regular Basmati, Dill Rice, and Sweet/Sour Rice), 2 different types of lentil's, Chicken Stew, Eggplant Stew, Chicken and Ground Beef Kabob, Stewed Spinach, Hummus, and a large variety of salad items including Feta Cheese, to top it off they even had dessert items of Baklava and Lemon Cake. The food was very fresh and flavorful, the rice was cooked perfect and the salad items were fresh, not to mention the Chicken Kabob was one of the best I've had in Tampa. There was only a small amount of people dining at the restaurant but the food on the buffet was fresh and quickly refilled when out. The service was also good and the ambiance was comfortable and the waitstaff was attentive. I could eat there every day!
Best Thai in town. Get the duck soup or the jungle curry. You won't be disappointed.
This is a must stop for me when I'm up here for capoeira workshops. Their bubble tea is so yummy. I've tried several plates here and loved them. They can server large groups here.

We've come here twice now, once for the weekend dinner buffet and the second time for their mothers day buffet. This restaurant is in a strip mall next to the Patel Brothers store on Lafayette Rd. Fairly basic in terms of decor, there is a full bar on one end of the restaurant. On our first visit my observation was that the taste of the food was 3-stars. Not bad but certainly not memorable or something that would draw us back alone. Where this restaurant won its extra star is in the service and the selection available in the buffet. Most local Indian buffets have been carrying fewer items in their buffet but India Sizzling II had a lot of variety in their vegetarian, non-vegetarian as well as appetizers/snacks. I enjoy the pani-puri and always order a dosa or appam from the kitchen which is also included in the buffet price. Another unique offering is the dinner buffet - the only one I'm aware of at the moment in Indianapolis for an Indian restaurant. Because of this positive experience we returned for a 2nd visit on Mothers day when they were featuring a special buffet. It had even more items available including 8 different desserts, mango lassi included in the meal. The taste and quality of the food was also noticeably better. 4-stars! We will return here when we're craving Indian buffet for dinner.

The food was great and the service wasn't bad either. Hubby got a chicken roti and I got the jerk chicken meal. If you're in the Millwoods area and want a taste of the West Indies, definitely drop by!

This is a casual joint with tasty food that hits the spot. I lived in Morocco for a year and I'm always up for trying new Moroccan places. This spot is legit. I went for lunch and had a delicious chicken shawarma sandwich. The food was fresh and the portion size large. The owner is friendly and might hook you up with some excellent Moroccan mint tea if you are nice.

Great food the service is exquisite and food is amazing. Exactly how you order it. If you don't know what it is just ask they will help you find something you like and it doesn't have to be spicy. Love their sushi!!!!

Came here for the first time yesterday and was impressed with the pad kee mao I ordered (with tofu). Minus one star because my tofu was cold when it got to me. I will definitely be back to try out their curries etc. Far exceeds Blue Elephant in Clayton in regards to authenticity and flavor.

We have finally found an authentic Thai restaurant in Nashville! Everything tasted good and it even have Mango sticky rice as dessert! Definitely our favorite Thai restaurant in Tennessee by a long shot! Awesome place!!
Everything was really good. Fresh veggies. The scallop cakes tasted more like whole scallops than some mix of seafood & filler!

I have been coming here for about 20 years and I have yet to be disappointed. I frequent this establishment for lunch, at least once a month. Their decor leaves a bit to be desired, but for me it's all about the food. Their Angelo Cataldi is a delicious mix of roasted pepper paste, perfectly marinated and grilled chicken, string cheese and lettuce. A perfect go to wrap for lunch. The Chicken Kebob is incredible, The Gyros are great and they have incredible hummus. The fattouch salad is quickly becoming one of my favorite healthy lunch options. I have tried just about everything on their menu and have yet to be disappointed.

Visited just a few days after Ekta took over management. Ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Paneer Palek. Both were amazingly spiced and fresh stews, served with a generous side of white rice. Tikka Masala was zesty with a great underlying buttery sweetness. One of the best I've had. Paneer Palek was hearty and chuck full of flavorful spinach. Definitely spicier than most Indian places in town, which may not be appealing to some people, but appreciated by true lovers of Indian cuisine. Can't wait to visit the buffet for some more variety of goodies soon!

This was my 2nd time coming here by default because it's near my bank. The first time was unimpressionable, but I wanted to give it a second chance. Thai food is my favorite! It was lunchtime, and I wanted a lunch special. It was hard to decide because no soup was included in the lunches, yet crab Rangoon. The price is set at $7.99 + $1 for fried rice. Wanting a side soup, I reluctantly ordered the noodle soup with chicken. All I can say is the broth was good. The chicken in the soup was horrible! The chicken taste old or something like that. While I was ordering and while I was eating the manager was sitting at the table. When I called the hostess over and inquired about a vegetable soup versus this chicken, she went over to ask the manager. He told her I would be charged with for the soup but can order something else then he left and refused to come back out. It was a horrible unprofessional way to handle a customer who had been there a 2nd time. The hostess told me that he wasn't coming back out and that he said I could leave without paying (I still had the full meal), and that they wasn't going to prepare anything new for me because I probably wouldn't like it. I DO NOT recommend this place at all. Most ppl who choose this are looking for tasty Thai food anyway, so outside of the poor service, the food is a 1 out of a 5.

I have been coming to this place for some time now even the owners have switched a few times, but the TASTE of food hasn't changed at all. Sunday morning they serve amazing 'halwa puri' (a traditional Punjabi breakfast) you have to notify them a few days prior because they have to make a special order. I always enjoy paneer chicken, chicken jalfrezi, tandoori chicken with some mango lassi and its freaking amazing. (rolling eyes amazing !!! ) You have to tell before ordering that you want the spice level to be authentic Pakistani spice level and it just goes amazing with Mango Lassi. This place is relatively inexpensive for the quality of food. I just hope this place stays around

Definitely one of the best Vietnamese restaurants in the area! The pho broth is amazing and so are the summer rolls and banh mi sandwiches. Prices are phenomenal too! They really could charge more considering the location (just because they can) but I'm so glad they keep it affordable and delicious! My belly is always happy and so is my wallet.
Waited one hour for one dish via carry out. Will never go back. Was told 20-30 minutes. Awful!!

When you have had a few too many hand grenades and start to get the drunk munchies, this place is perfect. The gyro was awesome- the meat was flavorful the tzatziki sauce ample. It's all served on a warm fresh pita. My husband remembered this place from his old fraternity days and says this place gets even better the drunker you get. I'm gonna go out on a limb here and say this would probably still be a pretty banging gyro if you haven't overindulged on libations too...it was just that good. We also had some spanikopita which came out piping out and was buttery and flaky. Bottom Line: The perfect accompaniment to all your activities on Bourbon Street. YUM!
I ordered a gyro plate as well as a combination plate. The order was made correctly, and I was offered a drink while I waited. The rice was undercooked, but everything was great other than that.
Great staff, fantastic food and large portions! What an all around great value! Definitely a great place to stop for lunch! Don't miss out if you want some great food with just enough heat!

My husband and I come here so often they put our order in when we walk in. We get the same thing every. single. time. Why? Because it's delicious. Literally every single time we leave so completely contented from our meal. I get the brisket pho and my husband gets the combination pho. We top it off with taro tea and tapioca. We have definitely ventured out and gotten each type of spring roll and they're AMAZING but splitting the spring rolls and eating pho is just too much food for two people. But if you're hungry and you like authentic Vietnamese pho, this is the place to go!

Totally blah experience. Food was mediocre and poorly prepared. The grape leaves were rubbery, dry and impossible to chew. Hummus was nothing special- way too salty. The restaurant also felt a little grubby.

Shut the front door! This place is UH-MAZING.. Tell your family! Tell your friends! If I had a mountain I would shout from it. The best chicken and rice I have EVER had. This cozy place feels like home with warm hospitality and tasty food.

I have been going here since they opened in the CBD. And am delighted they have done well enough to expand their space. Their food is superb and the prices are great. They also do well to get you out within an hour. I especially like their fried calamari dish. Yum!

This place literally sucks at restaurant service... just went to order late dinner and she refused to help me and said they were close... every information resource says open till 11 she still rudely waved me to go away...

My hubby and I had special #3 for dinner which had kung pao chicken. I don't know what they gave us, but it definately did not have pao. It was so bland I couldn't believe it. We thought we got the wrong dish. No spice to it what so ever!!! I have made kung pao before and mine was way better than this bland dish we were served. Will not go there again.

This place gets 5 stars for one reason. Their amazing Beef Noodle Soup (Pho). It costs $5.99 for a small or $6.99 for a large. Unless you plan on sharing, do yourself a favor and just get the small. The broth is absolutely incredible. You can tell they probably let that stock just simmer all day with delicious beef parts and asian spices. I could just have an order of broth and be perfectly happy. But the thin strips of beef, rice noodles, fresh basil, bean sprouts, and lime juice just tops it off. I've had the subs before too which are unique and good for a picnic. But if you have some time just to sit down for a minute and enjoy some lunch, get their Pho. The ladies that work here are very friendly and stay busy. If they have some eggrolls in their display case, pick up a couple to munch on as well. Cheap and tasty. I will be back here MANY times. Definitely get some boba tea or a smoothie as well. The green tea flavor is so refreshing.
Love this place and the food here. I will recommend you to try curry fried rice and thai tea pudding during your visit here. And ofcourse the Thai Ice Tea.
Great middle eastern food not far from NOLA. I love the gyro sandwich. The dinner plates including lamb kabob, felafel, and hummus are all great! I recommend this spot.

I have had food here several times but the food quality has deteriorated adversly, specifically the lunch buffet. The biryani rice was hard, chicken tikka masala and paneer tikka masala had the same gravy with some odd coconut flavor. Goat curry was bland and meat was not chewable or in any way tasty. Naan were dry and cold. Only good things were Tandoori Chicken and gajar ka halwa (carrot pudding). Gave this place a chance number of times but I guess it has lost its charm.

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: When I travel I am looking for hole in the wall places to eat. This place fits the bill. They have a very limited menu, but you will lick your fingers when you taste the authentic meal. If you go for lunch on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday the buffet is perfect. Hope you enjoy the meal as I did.

F I N A L L Y ! A Dominican restaurant in Center City! This place has become a go-to spot whenever I am craving Dominican food but don't wanna drive back down to North Philadelphia to get it. I am dominican so this might be a little biased ( best food in the world). First thing first, this place is in the perfect location as It is not quite downtown which allows you to at least find some kind of parking to eat here ( There is a free parking lot about a block away on 12th street ). You will find that the food is prepared already and waiting for you to choose the different variety. There is Rice ( often white or yellow), beans ( black/red/other), various choice of meat such as pork, chicken, or beef. SWEET PLANTAIN ( because why not?) and several daily specials such as soup or specialty dishes. You order down the line ( cafeteria style) and have the option of eating in or takeout. My personal favorite dish from here is the White rice, black beans and Ropa vieja ( shredded beef). This restaurant is not fancy at ALL but the food will make up for that. Most important, this place is not expensive whatsoever. You can have a full meal for less than $10. The staff speak both English and Spanish and are very catering to all of your needs. During the summer time, there is outside seating which is great if you're trying to enjoy some sun and a nice breeze. Definitely give this place a try. CAUTION: This place is awesome !

With the exception of the price being a little on the high side, I can find nothing to complain about with Ploi Thai. In fact, when you consider similar restaurants, they have a larger seating area, adequate wait staff and amazing food. It is by far one of my favorite restaurants in the Tampa area. One thing I really appreciate is the ambiance that has been created. Having spent a bunch of time in Thailand, this makes you feel like you are right there.
First time here, very tasty and quick. Very nice staff! Two vermicelli noodles with grilled pork bowls.
Brunch here is amazing! Everything is so fresh and authentic tasting. The dishes are unique and flavorful. I would love to try the dinner!

We went on a Monday night for the first time and were excited to find that it was burger night. We started out with some beers which were of good selection. We were offered some spicy popcorn to try and it was pretty good. We both ordered burgers. I the 8th Street Burger (medium) and my wife the American (medium well) (minus aioli). Both came out well done. Mine was to have "crispy pork belly" and Asian pickles. The belly was nothing more then a couple small pieces of what amounted to pulled pork and there were no pickles. The wifes was missing the cheese. We sent hers back after she took a bite and realized. Out came a brand new one but now had the aioli on it. We had also ordered about ten minutes before the couple next to us and they had burgers come out at the same time as ours. I am usually forgiving of a miss here and there on a order, but considering your "special" for the night had this many problems....I wonder what regular items would be like. Not sure if we will be back, which is sad because it was a nice change in scenery.
Spicy, good quality food with some interesting options on the menu. My only complaints are that the food is a bit too rich and the ambiance sometimes a bit stuffy.
We stumbled across this restaurant and dropped in for lunch. The food was excellent and the staff were very friendly. I highly recommend it!

This place is pretty lame if you are used to actual indian food. It costs the same amount of money for a small meal here, as it does for a full, hot, freshly cooked meal at an indian restaurant. The portions are tiny, I was not satisfied with what i was given at all, It lacked flavor, and the amount you get is a joke. I only weigh 130 lbs and it felt like half a meal to me. Its a nice idea, to have an indian restaurant on market street. But honestly this place is a crazy waste of your money, go to india grille, or some other real indian restaurant, there are plenty of options. I will say, if you are in a pinch, the food is absolutely edible, and really not all that bad. Its like some decent food you would find at the airport, with silly high prices for very small portions. But at the airport you would expect that, on market street... not so much.

Absolutely LOVE this place. I've only been here for lunch a few times and can say the buffet is always hot and stocked up. Servers are quick to refill drinks and provide warm naan. Everything is delicious here. They have vegan and gluten free options. 5/5 for quality, services, and price.
Great food amazing prices HUGE portions and super friendly people.

trash.....don't waste your money. 4 shrimp in an order of steamed rice shrimp & w/extra shrimp!!! $4.00 charge for the extra shrimp.............no wonder they have all sales are final on the door............they would not make any money. i essentially paid 10.00 for a box of steamed rice w/4 shrimp. when i called...."oh you can have a credit" sssssseriously???

Five stars across the board! This place is awesome. The food is amazing every time and can be made at various hot levels. I love spicy and go for hot which is so great. Plenty of menu options and they offer vegan options. When I say options, I mean OPTIONS! A dedicated vegan menu which is rare of Florida. When we come we try different things and it never disappoints. The staff is amazing. They greet you and remember your choices down to the beer and hotness preference. They remember our vegan menu every time. Great place with great food and great staff. Check it out, you won't be disappointed.
I only got carry out but this place looks really good. our carry out was delicious. Northern Thai food.

This places was one of the best Thai restaurants I've been to. The service was quick and courteous as well. My daughter and I both had the pineapple duck curry which is in red curry sauce. It was amazing! So good that my daughter keeps going back without me to get it. Lol... This place is a definite must visit if you love Thai as much as we do.

My friend and I stopped for a bite to eat while on Bourbon a couple days ago. I had the chicken shawarma wrap and she had the falafel wrap. Both meals were delicious! I highly recommend this little spot if you like Greek and Mediterranean food.

We had a burial service for my uncle at a nearby cemetery. I was left in charge to find a spot for my family to have a lunch together. I found this via yelp and it looked promising. I called ahead and they told me we wouldn't be able to sit together, the 14 of us. I told them specifically that we just finished a funeral service. We all thought maybe they are just busy and we would wait for a table to fit us all. We get there, half the restaurant is empty. There were so many empty tables, but yet they refused to push them together to fit us all on one table. They responded with "the boss won't like it". Can you believe that?!?!?!! So my father, who was upset by this answer said "your boss doesn't like paying customers?" So then the older "manager" acting unpleasant woman just shook her head and let my father put the tables together. Let me repeat, they had him push the tables together. It was a very rough and emotional day for everyone and for them to treat us this way was ridiculous. The waitstaff was very nice and this is the only saving grace they have. Now, let's get to the food. The quality was so below average and I'm shocked at their high reviews. Their Mac and cheese was a square with melted sliced cheese on top. Something a kid could make. We had a few orders of risotto that looked like jasmine rice with liquid on the side, it totally separated and was flavorless. The salad was three lettuce leaves chopped up and three shrimp. The grilled cheese was one slice of melted cheese. Even my 3 year old didn't want to eat it. Sad place with a really grumpy old lady working at it. Do not recommend wasting your time here.

This is perhaps the most authentic ethiopian atmosphere I've been to - I opted for traditional seating, which are traditional Ethiopian chairs around Ethio basket table called a mesob. Along with my meal, I opted for the traditional Ethiopian Coffee ceremony, and was seriously wowed. For the less adventurous, you can also sit at the regular restaurant tables. I didn't think I needed to talk about hands - because it is a ethiopian restaurant, but yes, you have to eat with your hands. They supply purell next to your table for convenience. The service is very friendly, though I'll say it is extremely slow. However, my only critical remarks are as follows - 1) the food is slightly muted down (perhaps because it's in Indiana) 2) the food is also slightly salty (also, perhaps because it is in Indiana) 3) they should play some sort of background music in the restaurant, I sat in the corner (and no one puts baby in the corner) and could only hear the hum of the air conditioning in the walls. 4) Offer wet naps. For an ethiopian restaurant, this is a gem!

Food the was great. I just wish they would turn on the AC. It is always warm/hot in the restaurant. They have all the fans going but I feel any cool air. It's pretty bad when the outside feels cooler than the inside of the restaurant in the middle of summer. Would have given a 4 star but needed to rate the food as well as the environment. If your so hot and uncomfortable, it's hard to enjoy your food.

It's been several years since I ate at their previous restaurant, Indian Pakistani Food, and the food is still excellent. It's just a step above the rest in terms of freshness and flavor. The place is super simple but don't let that fool you. No buffet but it's better when they make everything to order.
Best curry I've had in the city. Try to go during lunch as prices increase substantially for dinner.

I was very disappointed with the food here. We came because we got a Groupon deal for $10 for $20 worth of food. Even with the Groupon we didn't feel like the food was worth what we spent. The restaurant was very hot and stuffy so we sat outside. We ordered an order of moussaka for $14.99 and a gyro sandwich for $7.99. The gyro sandwich was so-so. I've had much better for cheaper. There wasn't that much meat and other than that the sandwich was filled with a little lettuce, some red onions, a slice of tomato and tzatziki sauce. The moussaka was came with a very small serving of burnt moussaka, bland rice and a piece of pita bread with tzatziki sauce. It definitely was not worth $14.99. Overall, I felt like the food was overpriced and the quality was not that good.

I've been dying to try out Goldie! Today my friend and I went to Franklin's table around 2ish for lunch. Luckily the place was pretty quiet because it was after the lunch rush. We both ordered the falafel salad, trying to be healthier in the new year... The salad was served to us looking beautiful! It was topped with many sunflower seeds and a drizzle of tahini. It was absolutely delicious. It had mint leaves, beets and many multicolored veggies. I'm not a big beets fan, but I enjoyed them in this salad. The lemon date dressing was fresh and light. And the falafel balls were insanely good! They're bright lime green in the middle! They were very fresh and flavorful. Probably the best falafel I've ever had. I will definitely be back for a pita sandwich and a tahini shake!

Wow. Service was amazing, staff attentive, and food was beyond what we expected. Can't wait to go back. Seriously, one of the best restaurants we've been to in years. Had the mixed vegetable appetizer (fried veggies, cheese, and a samosa), and sampled 3 curries, all vegetarian. Unbelievably different, incredibly tasty, and overall a wonderful dinner. Had enough to bring home for lunch tomorrow. Tried one curry spicy - definitely spicy, but exactly what we ordered and hoped for.

Not the fanciest place to take a date, and the food lacks presentation but then again, it isn't a masterchef kitchen. In all the food was delicious and well worth its price. Don't expect 5 star service though. The service was definitely a vice as it was slow and the hostess accidentally switched checks with us and other customers. So once again, come for the food (or take out the food) not for the service.

WOW... Just WOW... Located in the old Sushi Me in Lenox Village Umami is amazing. Its fresh, hip and CLEAN inside. You are always greeted by the owner Michelle at the door with a smile. The servers are so nice. I had Katy this last visit she was attentive and helpful with her food suggestions. The sushi is so fresh and so tasty. Some of the best miso soup I've ever had. Not to mention the calamari is the perfect size, and didn't come frozen in a bag. The attention to detail is next to none. Not the most amazing food presentation but it makes up in food quality, taste, service and value. I'm serious I have eaten food at all of the best sushi restaurants in Nashville and this one takes the cake folks. Their desserts are amazing as well. This time I had the cheesecake which is a multi layered cake with a fruit layer, a cake layer and 2 cheesecake layers.... its to die for... This is the place!

Fantastic Food. I had the sampler for lunch, my friends had the chicken penecetta and grilled chicken salad. The restaurant is clean, great service and parking across the street. So glad we stopped here.

Mmm Mmm!! I have eaten here quite a few times and I have always enjoyed the tasty food! I'm a vegetarian and there's a variety of options on the menu I could choose from. Usually my favorite choices are the veggie samosas for an appetizer, any of the naan breads, rice, sag paneer or channa masala, and a lassi to drink. I ordered for delivery before and they were right on time. I also did take out and dined in the restaurant. It is small in there, but the employees are friendly, and the food is always fresh!

This restaurant is much larger than I expected, and they are expanding outdoors soon into a garden with lots of family-style seating. The décor is modern and tasteful and there is a lot of sound dampening material in the ceiling but it's still fairly loud but not too bad. There were quite a few "rules" that I felt could have been dispensed with such as: you can't stand at the bar, you can't be seated until your whole party is here, if you want a drink while you're waiting go to the back of the restaurant in a waiting room and someone will take your order. We found out all these rules because did all of the above bad things, ha ha. We did get drinks and fairly quickly! My cocktail had arak in it and bubbly and an aperitif that was a cross between Aperol and Campari. Tasty. The service was well done and efficient all night actually and the food was paced well. I'm not sure if anyone has compared Suraya to Zahav (Philly's best Israeli/middle east restaurant whose chef has won many awards) but it beats Zahav in a few categories and not others. Suraya's hummus is good, it has great spices and green herbs on it but it is just hummus. Their baba ghanoush is excellent, great smoky flavor and some pomegranate seeds on top. We had 6 mezzes and all were great. The chicken livers were amazing, the sauce was beautiful and the livers perfectly cooked. The chick pea eggplant combo salad (forgot the name) was out of this world, one of our favorites. Spicy potatoes with long hots were very good. We ordered only two mains due to the amount of mezzes, the lamb and the whole fish. The lamb was melt in your mouth tender and had a perfect crust on top with tons of flavor. Yoghurt and cucumber accompanied it. The fish I thought was slightly overdone but the sauce was great. Suraya is everything people are saying it is, but I was almost disappointed that it is so large, it's hard to explain but sometimes it's hard to believe a large place can be so good!
Wonderful food! Excellent service! The wife and I have been wanting to stop for a while now, and finally did. Highly recommend. The mushrooms I had were very fresh.
had the thai basil with shrimp and it was quite tasty and filling. big bowl of tom kha loaded with vegetables. one tiny girl working all by herself on halloween and did a great job.

Food was excellent. Beef skewers were very tasty like the previous reviews said. The lemongrass spicy soup has deep flavors and was perfectly balanced. My husband enjoyed the soup thoroughly. I had the salad with grilled chicken and egg roll. Very fresh and flavorful. My only wishes- 1) they had boba 2) their soups spoons weren't metal- but they had nice chopsticks. We will be back for more.
Just opened. Wonderful staff!! Highly recommended for hookah and middle eastern food :)

My husband and I drove by Euro Grill all the time and kept saying we should try it out. Well, golly gee, one day we did! We are very glad we did! It always looked like it wasn't busy, but like another reviewer noted, people park in the back and sit outside. The owners are super friendly and with my husband's curiosity I felt like we got their whole life story. We don't even look at the menus anymore, since it's easier to just tell them what we like and have them recommend something. Everything is delicious. I won't go into details about what we've had there, but just know that it has ALL been delicious. Their Greek salad is the best I've ever had. The baklava, yum...and turkish coffee, perfect! I wish we could get there for breakfast sometime during the week, but they don't open until 8am so that's difficult to do. The location is random, I know, but you should definitely make your way there and check it out. You will not be disappointed!

We have visited this location of Aman's at least 8 times now, probably more - the food is nicely prepared, the service is friendly and attentive, and both food and service are consistent. Each time we are there for dinner, choosing from the sit-down menu. I would like to get there for the lunch buffet eventually. I understand the Indian food we find in the area is "Americanized" and that's fine, I'm more than happy to keep coming here.

You have to try it for yourself! We visited Loco Lucho today and we are DEFINITELY going back very soon. My wife and I ordered sandwiches. I had the Frita Cubana and my wife had the Bistec sandwich. Both of them were so good my wife and I made a deal and we both ate half of each other's sandwiches. We also ordered two empanadas: philly cheese steak and prosciutto with manchego cheese. Not one bad thing to say about any of those 4 items we tried. I'll be going back for the Tripleta sandwich and for another prosciutto/manchego empanada! Great service from a very friendly personnel. Thank you guys!
The Dooner Box is the best drunk food ever. But fortunately I was sober both times I've had it so I was able to fully enjoy it.

The mango lassi was good. The tandori chicken was bland, but it did come with a decent amount of onions and peppers. The lamb masala had a good sauce, but little lamb. Luckily, I had a lot of bland tandori chicken to dunk in the sauce. I might go back to try the buffet, but will not return for single dishes.

I was here with Miss Tina last night and it was a totally different experience then the other Dmitri's and I loved every second of it. This location is BYOB and we brought a bottle of chardonnay to kick it with the yummy seafood we were about to eat. We sat right in front of the open grill at the counter and got to watch them make everything for everyone- it was hard to decide what to eat because of this and Tina actually changed her mind when she saw them make the escarole pasta! We started with the now standard grilled octopus, yum yum yummm. I love that they give you oil/vinegar to dip the bread in here as well. I ordered the steamed seafood this time, amazing- seriously. It was a huge bowl of tilapia, clams, mussels, shrimp, calamari and scallops in a tomato sauce that had a bit of a kick to it. It was seriously so good, however I was craving a little pasta with this- I made up for the missing carbs with bread and grilled pita. Tina got the aforementioned escarole pasta which was super yummy and our other friend ordered the calamari which was lightly fried and not greasy at all. I love that both locations offer totally different vibes, one for each mood. This one seems more fast paced and where you go with friends compared to the more mood lighting arena in center city.
Unassuming place in a strip mall. Run by Ukranians, the decor and seating is minimal, but the gyros are wonderful.
Had the lemongrass beef over vermicelli. Presentation was solid, but there was something off about the dish..the sprouts were old and had a funky taste. Service is cool, the guy is friendly.

I have to revise my previous review because I have gone back to Naf Naf about 5 times since and each time its great. The staff is MUCH better. The who I think is the owner is so friendly and really hands on. The food is great. So far my favorite is the veggie feast. I came with my husband and he raved about all the food for the price. This is definitely my go to!!!! Great Job!!!

I came to Remedy on advice from a fellow Yelper whose word I trust. Unfortunately my experience was far from good and bordering on downright horrible. First of all, the parking options are non existent. There is a private lot on either side of the building but both are for other businesses. There is no street parking so you either have to park illegally in one of the private lots or find a spot and walk atleast 2 blocks. I don't know if Remedy had the option to get a few spots in either lot but I would suggest that they try. Even if it cost them revenue to buy some spots this would be returned from the increase in driving clientele (virtually everyone has a car in Edmonton). Anyways, I chose the illegal parking option since I was only planning to be there for 20-30 mins. Little did I know that the employees had different plans for my time. Upon arriving I was the only one at the counter. No one in front or behind me. I was unfamiliar with the menu so I asked for advice for a snack and drink. Two employees advised me of the 2 samosa and chai tea combo which sounded good and was reasonably priced at $7+tax. I paid and my iced chai came pretty quickly. While waiting for my food a 5 person lineup appeared. I waited inside the restaurant to get my food before moving to the patio and taking advantage of the sun. I proceeded to wait what ended up being 34 minutes (I only know this because I texted a friend right when I sat down). I watched as 4 of the 5 people after me received their food. The 4th person ordered the samosas like me and I walked up to get them but was informed that this wasn't my order. This put me over the edge. I expressed my feelings and how long I've been waiting and the employee didn't even apologize, just said they'd go make it now. I was fuming! I waited another 5 minutes from that point and finally received my reheated, fried samosas that weren't even that good. They were greasy and uninspired. Once again I saw no remorse from anyone working there at my horrible user experience. My remedy is to never give any money to this business that clearly doesn't care and hires staff that reflects those same poor ideals. Oh and this is my first 1 star review and I'm not happy that I had to give it. I'd much rather enjoy spending my money and getting respect and thanks for my business.

I've had Thai Taste twice now, both take-out. The place isn't much to talk about visually, but the food is great! It's made to order, and comes out quick. Last time we stopped by for some Pad Thai, they had our orders out in less than 10 min. The people staffing the restaurant are all super friendly and aware of their customers. I am currently on a vegetarian diet, so I ordered my Pad Thai with tofu, and the hostess was aware enough to ask me if I wanted the egg or not. I was impressed she remembered. The vegetables are maybe not the freshest I've tasted, but they aren't overcooked. The food is well seasoned, and they use plenty of spices. Like many Thai places, they have a scale for spiciness. BE CAREFUL! Unlike many places, when they say "hot", they mean it! So if you aren't into spicy food, definitely order mild. If you are into spicy food (like me), then you will not be disappointed! Portions are pretty big, so if you and your friends can agree on a dish, I'd recommend splitting. I got three meals out of my last order!

An exceptional dining experience.. A gem! Wonderful service, diverse menu, warm and inviting ambience. our waitress was very knowledgeable about the menu, and our food was delicious, from a peach and goat cheese salad to Fettucine Bolognese, Farfalle with sausage, fresh tomatoes, porcini mushrooms and olives. served in a timely manner without being rushed. the desserts are homemade and ours were fantastic.. Save room !

I don't know what the hype is. My niece and I tried this place out since she's never had Thai food before and I wanted her to try it out since it's also my favorite Asian cuisine. We were in the outlets and called ahead to make sure they're open on New Year's Day. We called and they said that they normally close around 930pm but since they didn't have a lot of customers, they wanted us to get there by 845 because the kitchen will be closing by 9pm. When we sat down, I was really amazed by their nice decor and the ambience is really nice. I ordered the Chicken Tom Kha, and shrimp Pad Thai. My niece ordered chicken satay and Chicken red curry. My Tom Kha was ok. Not that good. It felt like it was too watered down and the mushrooms they used were not oyster mushrooms but the regular button mushrooms. The pad Thai was not that good but edible. They put too much fish sauce so all you taste is the fish sauce. My niece's chicken satay were pretty tasty and the red curry was pretty good and she liked it. But overall, food wise, this place is not worth going to especially if this is your first time eating Thai food. Also, I felt like they rushed us since we were still eating at 930 when they said they're going to close. I understand that they were closing but the lady kept asking if my niece was done with her food when she was clearly still eating her food.

Not nearly as good as International Market and Restaurant on Belmont Blvd. Siam Cafe had terrible service at lunch, with only one (fairly crazy) lady waiting on the entire place. I was given the wrong food twice before I got my original order. I was underwhelmed by the flavor and quality of the food. I do not plan to go back. Ferdinand may fear that his palate is becoming jaded, but I am pretty sure that the food was just not that good.

Graduation week continues...brought my parents and my baby sister, and had a wonderful late afternoon lunch. Around 2:30 on a drizzly day, you're going to have a restaurant to yourself. I had the pineapple seafood fried rice (sorry, I don't recall the Thai name) on a 3 out of 5 scale of spice (you can order anywhere from 1-5). Loved the dessert....sticky rice and sliced mango and also got the fried banana fritters with ice cream and drizzled honey.

Aroi dee mak na krub! This is AUTHENTIC THAI FOOD 100%. Any reviewers saying the food tastes bad probably have NEVER been outside of the US. Drinks - Thai ice tea, Ice Green Tea - ON POINT!!! I almost laughed when the southern family behind us asked for 1/4 sweet and 3/4 unsweet tea lol! Thai tea is nothing like sweet tea! It's next level. The coconut drink is seriously so fresh - I am pretty sure they crack a coconut in the kitchen and pour it out. All three of those will soothe your tongue if you can't take spicy food. We had: Calamari - 5 STARS - I mean, it's fried and breaded, pretty hard to mess up, but texture was perfect, fresh, and tasted great. Tom Yum - 5 STARS (Sadly we didn't get seafood in ours, was just vegetarian - would have probably made it EVEN BETTER) Kai Jeow Moo Sap - Thai Omelette with minced pork - 5 STARS - I don't think this is on the menu, it's just a personal favorite and I just tried my luck with ordering. Legit! Duck Curry - 5 STARS (This is seriously the best duck I have eaten in the US - and I've been all over Cali, Seattle, NY) Khao Pad Ruammid - Fried Rice with Chicken, Pork, Egg, Shrimp - 5 STARS Oh so good. I have missed this kind of fried rice so much... Honestly nobody does it better than the Thai's... Restaurant was so clean. Service was amazing - the owner walked from table to table to check on everybody, and is obviously such a great people person. This place is divine! I have been searching for a good asian place for THREE years here in Nashville. I have finally found it! Also - If you walk into a Thai restaurant and you see a portrait of the King, you are pretty much assured that the owners are Thai. I have been to Thailand hundreds of times. It was wonderful to order dishes in Thai and actually eat amazing and authentic food. . !
Ordered takeout green curry with chicken. It was okay but likely would not have this again and would consider other menu items.

This was one of the first pho places I went back in 2000, it has always been delicious, consistent and accommodating. It has recently been renamed to delicious pho. The menu is easy to understand for first time phoers and they will add and remove whatever types of meat cuts you prefer. I got the large with brisket, meatballs and tendon. The bowl is huge, like other places xlarge. It came in at $11. The broth was tasty, generous meats, and lots of fresh cilantro, basil(mint), and green onions. It looked nice and fresh, and tasted great! We arrived just before closing, but they didn't say anything and served us. The service was great, accommodating all our special requests... We had the 2 year old with us. My friend ordered the bun and shared a spring roll, which was great, but the bun itself wasn't the best. I didn't try it, so I can't elaborate, but he wasn't blown away. Overall, it's clean, good service and the pho was generous and delicious!

Great small place (40 seats). We had the daily buffet on Sunday 3/13/11 for$10.95/person, plenty of vegetarian (meatless) dishes on the buffet. Nice size pieces of tandoori chicken. We will definitely be back again!

Have had 4 lunches here and that tells you how much I like their food and service. Nice wine list which is important for us mature women who lunch and the service had always been good. PLUS they have a parking lot right next to the place!
3.5 stars. Good food quick service. Quiet restaurant. Not too expensive however 20% gratuity for parties five or more. Tourist trap.
Worst first experience ever.. They offer chicken pulao in buffet :( food wasn't worth.. Will never visit again

We were skeptical at first because of the location but then tried the food. I am happy I went there. We ordered Paneer Kalimirch and yellow dal (both medium spicy) with roti. Excellent food and service also. It just needs a little update with the decor.
I order and eat here all the time, live very close. All the food is very good! The people who work there, especially who I think might be the owner are so nice. Highly recommend.

So far, the best pho I've had in Philly. In general I avoid Pho Hoa like the plague. They are an international chain and I've had them in many cities in the US and Asia. In general, the pho is mediocre or bad. But today it was pouring and I was parked in front of the restaurant, so what else is there to do but go in? Anyway, I was surprised. Compared to Pho 75 and Pho Xe Lua, I liked it. The broth was more complex (e.g. had more spices which are associated with the south, but that I also prefer). The ve don was intermediate (it was best at Pho 75 and worst at Pho Xe Lua). I often think that the quality of the ve don is a good indicator of the pho in general. I prefer the crispy ve don with the texture of cartilage to the beefy/fatty kind. As the broth and ve don is very different between restaurants, while other ingredients are more similar, I take these to be very significant.
Came here a few weeks ago and haven't stopped dreaming of yellow curry. Coming back for more! But I'm disappointed I can't find a menu online for my friends to order from

Ordered on GrubHub, showed up and she no longer told me they took GrubHub orders and non were placed even though they charged my card for the meal. So for that reason, this place is now on my blacklist
Have been here several times for lunch and dinner. Really good food and good prices. Service is okay. Clean. Family oriented. I recommend you give it a try.

This place was just meh. It was a Friday when I came to eat here and i was by myself. My server was just meh; He forgot my fried egg, and basically ignored me. I can understand though because it was semi-busy, and he had multiple tables with parties of 2-6. As someone who is payed in tips I completely understand and don't hold that against him. I ordered the Laab, Larb, Laap depending on who you are and I got it "Native hot". It was basically flavorless, and came with a quartered iceberg lettuce head, like really iceberg lettuce?! It was very spicy! That's basically the only reason I gave three stars was because of the spicy-ness. I'm going to give this place one more try in the future.

I ordered the tandoori chicken, which came with a side of white rice, lamb samosa, which came with 2 pieces, raita, and aloo paratha. The tandori chicken was good but not great. It's not like what it looked like in the picture online. The lamb samosa was not good. The lamb tasted funky. I thought the raita would have larger pieces of vegetables but instead it was more soupy and the vegetables were almost nonexistent. The aloo paratha was tough and dry and lacked flavor. The peas were also hard. The food was not worth what it costed. I was really hoping to like this place since it's close to me however, I will not order from here again.

Great tasting Thai food. Not very spicy, but I bet if you asked they could kick it up a notch for you. Not a very big place, but it was nearly deserted when I went for dinner. I look forward to returning here.

Basil Spice was my lunch of choice for my Birthday. My husband and I had eaten here a couple of winters ago, but this was prior to my yelping experience. I always hear of people loving Basil Spice, despite the lower review on Yelp. Therefore, I chose it over many other Thai food options. Unfortunately, I did could not rate it higher than a three. It is good and we enjoyed our meal, but their was nothing impressive regarding the taste, presentation, service, or environment. The taste and presentation: We selected the stir fry Ginger and the Pad Wun-Sen (glass noodles and veggies in a black sweet soy sauce) . When they came out, the noodles looked great, but the stir fry had more sauce than substance. I like sauce as it compliments rice well, but it was almost an over abundance of sauce compared to the actual food. The flavor reminded me of chicken broth (aka chicken noodle soup) with a hint of ginger. The rice also came out in a bowl, but appeared sloppy. The Service: Friendly. Environment: quaint but not comfortable. Almost too quiet. Overall, I have no regrets and enjoyed my food. I would go back but will not put it on my high priority list.

WOW...now that's a spicy and delicious meal, just how I like it! I had a dish with ground chicken, basil and peppers that was real tasty. My buddy had the cashew chicken and loved it. The Thai iced tea was perfect for cooling down the heat a bit. On top of the great food, the service was friendly and the place is really clean. Lunch specials are $8.95 for a nice portion, Ice tea was $2.50. I still have these great flavors popping in my mouth! Thanks!

I have to say I was excited to eat here and had been watching this place being built (I worked in the area). The atmosphere is just okay, stark white walls and a little industrial, I think they just need to spruce up the place with a little more color or art on the walls. But since they just opened I'll cut them some slack. The waitress was okay, but she seemed not too friendly or helpful. The menu, I agree, had a lot of good options, between burgers to steak etc. I ended up ordering the Chicharrones de Pollo, which is fried chicken seasoned on the bone. The flavor was great, but I nearly chipped a tooth on some of the little bones in the chicken. I've had chicken like this before and it fell off the bone, but this I had to work on to get the meat off the bone. It comes with a side of rice and beans, which was honestly my favorite part of the meal. The portion wasn't very big at all (I kind of left feeling a little hungry), my chicken had about 3 pieces, and they aren't big pieces. Overall, I would probably go back to try the happy hour; I hear it's 2-for-1 and I think they are passing out free appetizers next week maybe? At any rate, I may go back but I may wait for them to get things up and running.

This is my first time on umami but I'm pretty confident that their KFC(Korean Fried Chicken) is one of the best if not the best wings on this part of town. Even though it is hard to imagine that the chicken in the picture is big, I promise that it is bigger that your regular wings that you would normally get. The flavor is called garlic soy which is sticky sweet but savory at the same time. This KFC would make it worth while for you to pick up the crumbs and lick your fingers. The service inside of the place is really good cause the staff and even the manager get to know those people that eat at the restaurant, the manager had a small talk to us about the chicken while we're at the restaurant and she seemed sincere about talking to us and the other customers and is not for show. Even the staff are also friendly and even tried to help us to get a discount but we're too early for the promo where they discount the KFC when there is a Titans/Predators game. I sincerely recommend this restaurant to those who would like to have a new taste of wings or just watch sports with your friends while eating something good.

My boyfriend and I came from out of town and had fantastic service and a fantastic meal. We checked out restaurants in the area on Yelp and thought this would fit the best. Thankfully our instincts were right. My boyfriend got the salmon oriental and I got the rack of lamb (lamb out of New Zealand). Normally I am not a fan on salmon, but the salmon oriental had amazing flavors (the sauce was awesome). The rack of lamb was cooked to perfection and tasted fantastic. We also had a great server with good suggestions. She helped us make good decisions and answered all of our questions. From start to finish, we loved our experience. The bread and oil before dinner, drinks, the house salad with the ginger balsamic vinaigrette and our meals had us very pleased. Add a great waitress and we were in heaven! Please go if you make your way to St. Petersburg!

I have only ever gone here for the lunch buffet, so I can't speak to anything regarding ordering off of the menu. The lunch buffet is usually pretty tasty, and the naan is almost always fresh. Occassionally it comes a bit burnt in spots, as if they left it in for just a minute or two too long, but it isn't a deal breaker by any means. The Tandoori chicken is usually very good, but it has been somewhat dry once or twice. The samosas (when they aren't out) are the best I've had in town!!! The one caveat I really need to mention is kind of a weird one. The ventilation in the restaurant is prety bad--to the point where I won't go there if I have meetings to go to later on that day. The smell of curry and naan and who knows what else kind of lingers on your clothes, and remains noticable to me even hours later. You know when someone puts on way too much cologne or perfume, how eventually they can't smell it anymore? The fact that I CAN still smell the spices makes me think that other people around me can REALLY smell em. It won't stop me from going in the future, but it is worth mentioning.

I found this place overrated. The food was not a standout and they serve a virtual truckload of rice. The atmosphere was convivial, but the food lacked imagination and variety. It was just so so. I would not go back.

Excellent food and service. I recommend the chicken fontina. They have a wide selection of appetizers and I've yet to find one I don't like. Additionally, their red sangria is a great pairing with any of their entrees and if you have room left, their desserts are quite pleasant as well. Try going there on a nice day and sitting outside.

Oh how I love this place... the food is great, the employees are amazing, I just love giving them my money! I would honestly tip everyone if I could afford it. The food is super consistent, as well as the warm & welcoming atmosphere the truck provides. My favs are the hand/homemade veggie burger and the tilapia burrito. Thee best veggie burger I've ever had. I just discovered the sweet green chile sauce that will now go on everything. Oh and the Lemongrass Tea is bomb too. Gabe brightens my day with his beautiful smile and likewise spirit. I just love this truck!

I've ordered from them for the past year and would keep doing it. But as of today, I will be taking a break. I walked in at 2:15 to order take out as they close at 2:30. They turned us away as the other ladies didn't want to cook the food. If you don't take orders at 2:15, advertise your business as closing at 2:15.

Pho is one of God's gifts to mankind. I've become enamored, nay...addicted to this beefy soup from Viet Nam. Thus far, I've not found much to be thrilled about in Reno as far as pho is concerned so when I discovered this place and read the reviews it was difficult to not have high hopes. Put simply, this is the best pho I've found in the Reno area. Though they do not currently offer pho thai chin the pho thai nam makes a satisfying alternative. It has great flavor, with plenty of onions and beef and noodles of near perfect consistency. Additionally, the iced coffee has a bold flavor that is quite pleasing. I found the service quite good and the atmosphere pleasing. As a bonus, this restaurant is easy to find with ample parking.

My office eats here regularly and we haven't been disappointed yet. I can't speak on its "authenticity" because I always get the same thing, mini Greek salad with gyro, but this is Tampa, not Greece. I don't expect authentic anyway. Hungry Greek is a nice break from the surrounding places on Dale Mabry. The portions here are generous and the food has always been fresh. This place is clean, friendly, and provides fast and excellent customer service. Two thumbs up for online ordering!

Delish! Just had lunch here and I am definitely coming back.. The restaurant is clean, food is fast and delicious, what else can you ask for?! The hummus is creamy and fresh, the shwarma is seasoned perfectly and so tender. I will definitely be back!

An amazing dining experience. The flavors, ingredients, and even the texture of dishes created a unique and enjoyable meal. Even the drink selection was impressive. We ordered drinks, appetizers, and main dishes...dessert. Everything was great! The price is on the higher side but it's worth it.
Really really good Puerto Rican food. Grouper sandwich is outstanding, tostones are great, and the mofongo is classically delicious!

Great, fast food Indian place, that's in a perfect spot downtown to grab a bite and go. Love their modern approach to Indian cooking. We had a tandoori chicken naanwich that was perfectly crispy and naan tacos with lamb and vindaloo sauce that were so tasty. Their chicken samosas were fresh and mango lassi was probably one of the better ones that I've tasted. The best thing is that it only took a few minutes to order and get food.This is a great addition to Indy.

Came here on a late night. It was the only one out of three Vietnamese restaurants in the vicinity that was still open. Great news! My roommate and I came in and sat down. I don't think we were noticed, we got up to get menus at the counter. Started off trying to order a bubble tea, but they said they didn't have anymore. (Weird...since it's on the menu.) For the appetizer, we had an order of eggrolls (2)...sans the some nice lettuce to wrap it in. What a bummer. Then we had the "Spicy Noodle Soup" (Bun Bo Hue) and Meatball Pho (Bo Vien). The pho was pretty awesome. The broth was hot and flavorful along with the fresh accompaniments of bean sprouts, lime and basil. The Bun Bo Hue was decent, but not very memorable. I just wasn't a fan of the chewy beef and more adventurous meats like the fatty pork with tendon. Bottomline -- It's a place to get your pho fix.

My first 5 star review in STL! I took a poll at work to see if anyone knew of any good thai food in the Loop area. The verdict was that I had to try Thai Country Kitchen. My girlfriend met up with me and we walked into this random little restaurant with an.... asian country motif? A bit random on the decor, but the food spoke for itself. I had some pad thai that was cooked and seasoned to perfection and my gf had a similar dish with a basil twist. Both of us ate our entire meals and wanted more as soon as the first helping settled. The service was on time and tentative. Will I be going back? 100% Can't wait!

What a find! Family pride in every way. Lovely dining experience. As a Vegan I can vouch for the menu and say there is something on the menu for everyone. Bring your own wine from home or purchase from the wide selection from the wine and spirits store downstairs where many organic wines available. I highly recommend this place and plan many repeat visits. Well worth it. Modestly priced and served with creativity ...

Prepare for the start of an addiction. At least to garlic naan, rice pudding desert and Mango Lassi (yogurt mango drink only rivaled by and w but stronger on flavor than mango shake). It is impossible to stop eating/drinking either one of those until they are gone (and then they start haunting you in your dreams until you come back). The lunch buffet is a great time to sample a bit of everything, but I usually make it to the area at dinner time. Last time tried goat Kahari (where else in Indiana are you going to try goat?) and kept stealing pieces of Amber special chicken and lamb kebob off of the kids' plates. The goat was a stew of traditionally bony chunks. I loved the kebob with spices ground right into the meat, but it was a bit intense for a kid's palate. The winner was the chicken - just right and a crowd pleaser all around. Locally owned, friendly staff. Usually busy, but rarely a wait for a table.

I am so happy I was able to find a Caribbean restaurant in Indianapolis. I ordered the lamb shank which also included rice and peas , plantains and the marinated onions and peppers. I must say everything was really really good. My co-workers also enjoyed their dishes. This is basically a little hole in the wall with really good food and average service. Also the prices cannot be beat. Because the dishes we had would cost twice as much in certain restaurants.

The wife and I ate here for the first time one week ago. We have eaten at other PF Changs and they were pretty good but this was definitely the best experience we ever had at any of them. Besides liking Chinese the other reason we eat at this chain is because of their gluten free options which my wife needs for her food allergy(celiac). We always eat early around 4:30 so we were quickly seated. As usual the food was very good. But the thing that set this apart from other PF Changs was our waiter Andrew. He came to our table quickly after we were seated.They didn't have Blue Moon on tap so he recommended something for me which tasted good. When he had the kitchen prepare our meals he had them do both gluten free so I could share with my wife if I wished. I thought this was a nice touch. He was very friendly and attentive during our meal even though it seemed like he had quite a few other tables. He was definitely one of the best waters or waitresses we had at any restaurant. We will definitely eat here again and asked to be seated at one of Andrews tables.

Lovely little hole in the wall kind of place. Staff very attentive. Had the Roti Cani, Thai WonTon Soup, and the Crispy Basil Duck. All excellent! Will definitely come back when either the daughter or the wife's here with me!

Pho 36 is quickly becoming one our regular stops if we're looking for quick, cheap eats on the west side. Their pho is flavorful and delicious, and the large is plenty for two to share, and it is filling when paired with a banh mi sandwich. The staff is courteous and the establishment is clean.

So i always order the same thing (Pad Woon Sen) and it has almost beat out pizza for my favorite food. The staff is so friendly, it's BYOB, and the food has never disappointed anyone else i've taken there. And to all the haters out there, i love the creepy decor.

I never thought I'd say this, but Chalmette has some pretty good food options! Stella Maris is a Mediterranean restaurant located within an ethnic grocery store on W. Judge Perez Dr. If you're ordering to-go, then meet at the counter, but have a seat if you'd like to sit down and enjoy your food there. Before I talk about the food, I will have to mention that service is hit or miss. I frequent here regularly so I've met every single server and can tell you that they are sweet, but Stella Maris is in the process of training more waitresses and some have yet to try the food or a little slow. The food is very consistent though. My go-to dish is the Gyro Plate (pronounced year-oh, but for some reason they pronounce jai-ro here). It's delicious! You have the choice of ordering with rice or hummus. I alternate since both options are great! I've tried the Lamb Kebab here, but for those who are sensitive to more gamey flavors and meats, then I would avoid it. It's very fresh though! Stella Maris is my favorite lunch spot in the Chalmette area, but service needs work. For that reason I'd give it 4/5 spoons. Minus 1 star for service, but 4 star food! EDIT: Service has much improved the last few times I've been there so I'm changing from 4 to 5 stars!

As many have mentioned, this is set up like Qdoba or Chipotle for Indian food. You select your base (naan pizza, naan sandwich, or rice), your protein (chicken, chickpeas, shrimp, mint and basil, fish, lamb), and then your curry (tikka masala, korma, saag, madras, or vindaloo). You then can add various toppings and additional sauces (chutneys). My usual pick is chicken and rice and then experiment with the different curries and chutneys, along with naan on the side. I have never been disappointed. This is a great restaurant to have, especially when there are lots of chains on campus. When you are looking for something new for lunch, this is a good place to start.

Some real jamaican jerk chicken,rice and beans and mac & cheese, good and spicy enough not to kill the flavors of the food....gotta try it all .....service w a smile w the colorful ambiance...im hooked ....

Used to be one of my favorite restaurants in Media, however the prices have gone up and the quality down. Last two dinners there were eatable but that is about it. Panang Curry Chicken is more expensive than Red Curry because it is supposed to have Coconut Milk in it. The sauce was like water with maybe a teaspoon of Coconut Milk. Had a half of can of canned string beans for the veggies and a couple of peices of red and green pepper for flavor. No cilantro, none of the great spices that make Thai so much better than Chinese food. Also had Pineapple Fried Rice with Chicken that was horrible. Rice was sticky and under cooked, no flavor what so ever, and again chicken was tuff and tasteless. For a couple of bucks more go down the road to Heng's where you can tell you are eating Thai food not some thrown together imposter for Thai.

Amazing atmosphere!!! I had worked for 7 hours from morning and needed a break and this was JUST THE PLACE!!! So serene and full of natural light! And the food is awesome too.....I had the chicken satay and the pad thai....delicious! After lunch and chilling here, I did NOT want to go back to work!

Found this place on Yelp. Don't think I've ever been to this part of Reno before, known as "Midtown" according to Yelp. It seemed kind of hood when we were driving around the area lol. Anyway, Creazian is located across the street from a courthouse. Just look for black awning with a big "C." My party and I parked on the street and fed the meter. We didn't see the parking garage next door until we walked to the restaurant. Lol. Double check the hours before you go. It said "open" on Yelp but we got there around 4:45 and it didn't open until 5pm so yeah not updated. Happy Hour is everyday from 3-6pm! So, we ordered a few items under Starters such as Traditional Spring Rolls, Pork Belly Crepe (Banh Xeo), Calamari & Poke Tacos. These items were half off but some of the portions are smaller vs the regular price (for example, the photos on Yelp showed 5 Poke tacos, our order came with 3). We also got the Dungeness Crab Garlic Noodles (market price $33) & Spring Run Salmon under Entrees. So, the crab noodles were my fav! Good portion; could feed 3-4 in my opinion depending on how hungry your group is lol. The crab is cleaned out fyi (someone in my party was looking forward to eating the brains lol). The calamari was pretty delicious too! It came in like a crispy eggroll wrapper shell and had sweet chili & chipotle aioli sauce. The salmon and spring rolls tasted okay. The rolls had pork belly & shrimp in it but it was just plain and not super special. It was pretty empty inside (maybe because of Easter weekend) but great service and good food. Total bill came out to roughly $70. Would like to return one day to try their pho and ramen.

I went to Shanghai station on a Saturday evening with my girlfriend. It's an underground space which looks tiny from outside, but is deceptively bigger. We got seated right away since there weren't many people at the time. The waitress was very nice and prompt in taking our order. We ordered pork soup dumplings, kung pao chicken with hand drawn noodles, and chili cabbage shredded pork noodles. We were super hungry so were happy to see the food come quickly (under 10m). For some reason, all the dishes came in the noodle soup form. I'm not sure if that's how it was supposed to come or there was some miscommunication during ordering. The soup dumplings were super hot and a little difficult to eat, but I blame my lack of soup-dumpling-eating skills for that. They they were delicious. The same can be said about the cabbage dish though the soup broth was a little low on spice (but not flavor) for my taste. But then again, I like really spicy things. Kung pao was also very delicious and was spicy enough to bring me to tears (yes, that's the way I like it). The waitress was always around to ask if we needed anything. In the end, she brought us the check upon asking. We had some leftover kung pao which she very skillfully poured into a takeout container in front of us, without spilling even a drop of the delish soup. Upon being complimented for her superior pouring skills, she told us that she was trained to do this during her job at a pho restaurant. Way to go! Anyway, the overall experience was great, food was cheap and delicious. Portions are decently sized. One appetizer and two entrees were more than enough food for two really hungry people. I would definitely recommend this place to people, specially living in university city, looking for good Chinese food. Soup dumplings are a must, so don't miss out on those.

The chicken here was absolutely delicious! We tried the chicken pieces with jack's fries which were the best I've tried as well as the 2 piece chicken with rice-so good! The spring rolls were flavorful & the service was so friendly. I would definitely recommend :)
Delicious and reasonably priced, very friendly and attentive staff. Better food and experience for the $$ than some of their Thai competitors on South Grand. Can't wait to go back to try more dishes!

Don't expect a full restaurant with tables and waiters. It is a convenient store. It has only 5 tables and 10 chairs set aside at the corner. But the food is GOOD! The PoBoys are the best! They use French rolls, crusty outside, soft inside. On the corner of Canal and N Broad. Canal Street, street car stops right in front of the store.

They don't serve alcohol, but you can bring in your own. There is a liquor store downstairs. Go Tuesday nights for the Jazz. It's a blast. The food is amazing! We had Jamaican tostadas, the beef ribs, the curried goat and the rum raisin cake. Everything was perfect. They were the best ribs I've ever eaten in my life. A Manager and a cook each came to the table to see how we liked our meal. They were very focused on making sure everything exceeded our expectations. I will go every single time I am in Nashville.

Wow, what a disappointing visit this was. After reading a lot of great reviews and the pictures of some amazing looking food, we decided to give this place a try. Our order was as follows. 1- Miller Lite Bottle 1 - Margarita 1 - Order of Fries w/dipping sauces 1 - Pork Dumplings 1- Crab Cake Dinner 1 - General Tso's Dinner Seems pretty simple right? Well the beer was slightly above room temp and the margarita was tequila with a splash of lime. That pretty much set the tone for things yet to come. Our apps came out and instantly we were let down by how horrible they were. The dumplings tasted like lemon pledge and the fries were cold. Obviously they dont make their fries as ordered. I thought, ok maybe Im over reacting. Then the main course came out. The crab cakes may have been the worst tasting crab cakes I have ever had. The sad part is they were full of lump meat. The bottoms were burnt and tasted like they were cooked in the same pan as the dumplings. They had a weird citrus taste that I couldnt mask with any sauce on the table. The generals chicken was basically chicken strips with teriyaki sauce on it. $66 dollars after the fact, we could have got a better meal at WaWa and still had money left over for Tasteykakes and gas. This place claims to be an American Gastropub but their menu is pretty dominant with Asian cuisine. The experience was so bad that its not even worth a second trip just to see if it was an off night.
Decent Thai food. Nothing special. Nice Thai iced coffee.

This is a bit of a step up for the restaurant. But still not much. I had a seamless gift card, which I had to use before a certain date. So, the only restaurant near to me which delivers is, Desi village. I ordered the Malai Kofta, Bhel Puri, Garlic naan and Aaloo paratha. Malai Kofta was decent but the sauce was a day old. And there was no aaloo (Potato) in aaloo paratha. For Bhel Puri they had all the ingredients seperate, which is good. But again, this will be the last place I will be looking for to have dinner or lunch.

This place is a great little place. It's unlike any other place I've been to in the City. They make chicken. Granted, some of the menu items are a little too "uppity" for me--I like fried chicken, simple old fried chicken--but what I like to eat, they make it and make it well. There are times where it's too crowded, full of the preppy college kids, and there's times when they haven't planned their cook times properly, and are short of food, or the food isn't always prepared perfectly, but those occasional "down times" aren't enough to disuade me from going. I've adopted a more healthy lifestyle, so when I need "fast" food, this is my best option, since there's no Chic-Fil-A closer to my location than S. Philly. GO THERE! ENJOY IT!!!
Good authentic dosa and South Indian food.. ***** very good authentic taste * bad service . you have to ask for water and wait for someone to come to ur table. ** plates look old and used

You know there is a problem, when you find yourself writing a Yelp review while still eating your take-out food. I ordered 3 things. My description is as follows: Duck Fried Rice, Medium Spice: Bland. I'm talking...Midwest, old white people bland. If there is a single flake of pepper, I'll find out. I ordered Medium, kind of on a dare to myself...and, I haven't found the spice yet. The duck is laid on top of the rice, and there isn't much. I'd say, probably 4 ounces total. For $12.95...eh. I'm eating it because I'm starving, but if you like mild or medium...I guess, go with the Thai Hot? Spring Rolls: Extremely tasteless. Over fried. I can taste last Thursdays oil. I'll literally never...ever...order this again from Thai 5 Crab Rangoon: Decent. Over fried, again...same oil that was used in last weeks dishes...but, the filling made up for some of that. Why 2 stars, and not 1? I feel a one star review is often times overused when you spend $25 on takeout, and the disappointment leaves you in reactionary mode. But, I'm not getting sick and I'm still eating it. But, I'll obviously never return. In the "old" days, you could call the restaurant and they'd refund the money. But, not in 2018. Hell would freeze over before a thai food, or Chinese food restaurant refunds your money for serving this.

9 of us went there for lunch and it was great service. Usually with that many people, it is hit or miss if they can figure out the order and figure out the bill, but they did an excellent job. I had the green curry with chicken and it was one of the best Thai dishes I have had in a while. I highly recommend this place.
Kabuli palaw. Get it. This restaurant does it very well. Tastes just like how it would in Peshawar or Kabul. The carrots are perfectly sweet, and the lamb spiced and tender.

Ordered from grub hub. Meal was delivered over after latest delivery time. From 5:16p order time to 6:34p delivery with 6:10p last delivery. Never again. Grub hub CSR was rude too. Never using them again. Food was underwhelming. No where near 4 spice. And saag paneer was like baby food. Over processed and liquified. Garlic naan had hardly any garlic. Rice was awful. Dry and tasteless.
Nice atmosphere the service is great. I came with a large group and we had no problem getting a table. Food was excellent very large portions for the price. Differently will come back again.

We've been to Guru's a handful of times before and last night's dinner was just as satisfying as any of the previous visits. This time wifey took photos of the dishes before we, by we I mean I, gobbled all of the food! We got the Lamb Kadahi, Chicken Makhani, Kulcha and Naan. We like it a little spicy, so we ordered the Lamb Kadahi double indian hot! I prefer lamb over the goat kadahi since the lamb pieces are boneless vs the goat pieces being bone in. The chicken makhani was ordered mild for the kids and for the friend with us who is not used to spicy food. Checkout the photos. Needless to say we enjoyed the food along with a bottle of wine we brought along. The chef and his family are always very friendly and excellent hosts. They brought us free appetizers (yummy onion pakoras) and mango lassi for the kids. The staff is very attentive. We will be going back again whenever we are in the mood for some Indian food! They usually have a groupon offer available so you may want to check it out if you'd like to save a few bucks, but tip generously ;) Btw, they are hosting a charity luncheon this Sunday, 6/12/16 on Peace and Nonviolence and Gandhi's grandson is the guest speaker for the event.

Visited for the first time today to celebrate our wedding anniversary. The food, the service, and the ambience were great. My husband had the salmon bisque and I had the roasted beet salad (dressing on the side), then we had the cannelloni and idaho trout with cauliflower steak. The cauliflower steak was my most favorite part of the whole dinner, the flavors were simply perfect. We finished with tiramisu cheesecake(also my most favorite part of the dinner, loved the strong coffee flavor) and spiced apple mousse cake. Great wine selection, we enjoyed a bottle of 2011 merlot from Tuscany. Soda water on tap. The waiter was very knowledgeable about the menu. They validate valet parking. They also put a candle on each of our desserts as it was our anniversary which I thought was a nice touch. Very happy with our experience!
The food wasn't very good and they give very small portions (why be chintzy with broth??) I really wanted to like this place and we ordered a couple things but it was all "meh"

Just finished a delicious dinner here. Had seen some promo's on TV and Nuvo and thought I'd check it out. Think Chipotle meets New Delhi. You order very similarly to Chipotle or Q Doba as a sandwich or rice bowl, add the protein, sauces and toppings. The food is REALLY flavorful. You can even do "half and half" if you're still experimenting with flavors. That's what I did, and it was great. They have a combo special which includes the entree a samosa and drink. Staff is great and very helpful. I dined in, and I lost count of the customers who said "This is my first time here", so word is getting around. I will definitely be back with friends!!

Dinner for three for $75 we expected a bit more than what we got. My masaman curry was more like a beverage than an entree. It was all sauce with a couple vegetables thrown in. I had so much broth leftover even after pouring it over multiple portions of rice. It's not supposed to be a soup! My husband's and mother's shrimp dishes only had 2-3 tiny shrimp in it. More like a shrimp garnish. How can they call that a shrimp dish, especially for the price? The crab rangoon left something to be desired but it wasn't terrible. Just not great, again especially for the price. It was also called "crab rangoon dinner" when it was clearly an appetizer. All in all, high prices for blah food. We definitely won't be going back.

Wow. I'm currently sitting...I don't know where in the middle of uni city and gorging myself on Cucina Zapata's short rib taco and Captn Crunch tilapia burrito. Yes, I got both because I thought: why not? I'm only here for 24 hrs a la Anthony bourdain. First off, you can't miss the colorful truck, which is a good thing bc that is what caught my eye from 1/4 mile away. When I realized that I had found Cucina Zapata, which I had seen on tv, it was jackpot.
