Tons of people were already waiting and more were coming despite the truck win on what I would consider food truck row. There must have been at least six others there by everyone was hitting up Zapata. My order was easy to put in and, as I waited the five min max for my meal, I watched the owner chat people paying. I thought: oh, that's nice, so many return customers. Yes, most were but when my name was called (correct pronunciation, btw), he was so friendly an we had a great albeit brief convo that only made my experience that much better. I have to say, having such a large following, you would think the owner and the staff would have a big head and feel entitled. NO--they were all so nice and took their time to make EACH customer smile despite the lunch rush. No wonder they have a following. Couldn't wait to eat so found a spot and first bite of the burrito...amazing! It is truly a hybrid created from a passionate love affair between a south Asian fish dish and a suave Mexican burrito. Yes, they had a brief but passion love affair that seriously blows your taste buds out of the water. The fish is fresh, the coating is crispy...it's an experience that really cannot be conveyed via a simple review. The same can be said for the short rib taco. Green Thai sauce with fresh avocado, tomato and red cabbage slices...a beautiful concoction. I did also get the lemongrass ice tea and it's a bit sweet but very refreshing. I only wish I had more time here to try everything. I wasn't planning on eating so much for lunch but it's totally worth it. Philly kids--you guys are so lucky to have CZ at your door step. Do you realize that? Don't take it for granted. Overall: amazing food, amazing service, highly recommended.

I have been here twice and have thoroughly enjoyed both visits. The plates are very large for the price. The pieces of chicken served on the kabob are massive, juicy and flavorful. They serve it with a garlic sauce which is tasty but not quite as strong as I would have hopped. The hummus was nice, again maybe a little under flavored but it was still good. I love that they bake their own bread. On my first trip the pita was a little undercooked and on my second visit it was more or less perfect, maybe a little over toasted for my taste. I like my pita to be foldable without cracking.

My wife and I celebrated my birthday by having dinner there. Our entire experience was wonderful and we will highly recommend Spice Finch to our friends. We plan to return. The restaurant is very attractive and well laid out. We appreciated that the ceilings were constructed so as to lower the volume of sound, allowing us to hear our conversation with each other without any problem. The quality of the food was quite terrific. The flavors were inventive and beautifully presented. The service was attentive and our waitress did an excellent job of explaining the dishes on the menu, as well as the different types of alcoholic beverages. In sum, we thoroughly enjoyed our dining experience there.It appears that this restaurant will "catch on" quickly and become a welcome addition the the neighborhood. It's different, but not intimidating. Bill H.

Cant think of anything faulty about this place. Very decent Afghani food. The price is reasonable. the staff is courteous. I have been visiting Philly on business and stay at one of the hotels in the vicinity. The kebabs are really good. The hummus and bread is made fresh everyday. You have to taste it.

Been eating here for several times now. Has become one of my staple meals of the week! I can't imagine a place that can cook Caribbean food better!! Will continue to eat here for as long as I'm in the Philadelphia area.

Discovered this spot today and so glad I did! Awesome authentic Thai food and a great lunch special - $8.95 for 2 courses. I got the salad and pad thai. Both were exceptional. Salad was delicious, especially the peanut dressing, and I practically licked my plate of the pad thai, that had a delicious sauce and pieces of tofu in addition to the chicken I ordered. Fantastic. As far as I can tell, this is by far the best thai food in the area. Will be back!
Love this place! Even my vegan friend can find something she can eat here. Every time I go here I am happy with the service and food. Defiantly worth a try for everyone.

This place was so much better when it was Souksavanh. The interior, service, and food have all gone down hill. Me husband and I used to visit every Wednesday and the owner was warm and welcoming and the pho was phenomenal! Since management change the food has left something to be desired.. couldn't even finish my bowl of pho and when I asked for sides that originally came on a plate to go in the pho they looked at me like I was crazy.

We were celebrating Birthday in this venue. Checkin was a bit chaotic and since place was packed it was also a bit noisy but besides that our experience here was nothing short of 5 stars. Excellent service who knows inside out each meal and each drink and also can give great recommendations which in my case were spot on. Food was beyond delicious and every bite tasted like heaven in my mouth. Very flavorful. Ambiance with dimmed lights also had its special feel to it. Not a place I can afford to dine at every week but I will be back.

Nice little Thai restaurant in Narberth with good food & friendly staff. A little over priced. When it first opened a few years ago the decor was odd and the food was inconsistent but it has greatly improved. It is now one of my family's favorite spots .
Every time ive gone here it has a been a great experience. Love the food, the service is great, the employees are nice and friendly. One of my favorite places to go
Inexpensive buffet with a lot of variety, nice staff and clean, quiet dining area. Pleasantly surprised to find this while working on the west side. I will be back.
best vietnamese in the land, worth driving to from indy. friendly, clean, fresh. lots of vegetarian options.

Had the signature "Wishboner" sandwich.. Full of flavor; however there wasn't enough chicken to cover two-thirds of the roll. I had to use a chicken finger to cover the other third! The chef should not be sending food out like this. See attached photo of sandwich.

Rare for me to post, but tonight's experience was so disappointing. Hostess was surly, waiter was inexperienced and incompetent. Didn't mention specials, couldn't answer questions about them or the regular menu, didn't mention ice cream, etc when serving dessert menu. Tofu app was great, chicken wings were oversized and disgusting. Who prepares like that? Salmon entree just ok but chicken Pad Thai and fish platter were very good. To add insult to injury, we were seated next to loud table with screaming kids-didn't expect a fast food experience. Seems like this restaurant needs to step up on the training big time. Might retry a year from now.
Delicious food. Great price. All the paneer dishes are so good. Staff is awesome who provided great service. I'll be coming back for some more paneer.

The service was great. The atmosphere and decor was warm and inviting. Great music in the background. The food was tasty. Being from Miami, I didn't think it was as good as home, but the flavors certainly reminded me of home. We will definitely be coming back to try more menu items!
I got the chicken pad Thai and it was delicious! Large portions too. My husband got the Larb salad and it was also delicious. Two thumbs up!

Came across the Parada Maimon while I was super hungry. Left fully satisfied, after choosing from a great selection of meat, lots of rice and beans, fried plantains. Their flan is top notch. I'll have to try their Tres Leches dessert next time I'm nearby!

This place was our first introduction to local Drexel Hill cuisine having just house hunted and found our new home! Small place but intimate (and BYOB). The spring rolls were great as was the fried rice. We like this place a lot

The women working here- this seems like a family operation- were quite friendly and helpful when we explained this was our first visit, and got everyone's orders out in a timely fashion. Just walk up to the counter and check out the menu on the dry-erase board or ask for a paper menu, tell them what you want and pay, then wait for them to call your name when the order is up. Even if you're not eating in, the ska and reggae music make for a relaxing stay. Basic meal plan: one meat, rice with optional beans, and a side of your choice. The meats we tried, oxtail and curry goat, were fall-off-the-bone tender in some seriously flavorful sauces and not gamy at all, though the rice was a tad dry. Side dishes include things like "cabbage" and patties, but we ordered the festival, which tastes exactly like funnel cake, and hummingbird salad, which is like cole slaw, but better (lighter, tangier, more veggies.) Drink options include bottled sodas imported from Jamaica and are more worth your money than Snapples. Unless you're starving or want leftovers, the small option is just fine for lunch, though medium and large are offered as well, all at reasonable prices. tl;dr: Good food, great prices, and an inoffensive atmosphere unless you have something against Bob Marley. If you've never tried Jamaican food, this is a very accessible option.

Food is absolutely wonderful here--I came here with my (Indian) parents and the three of us loved everything we ordered (Bollywood masala dosa, Farmers Market Masala Dosa, and Chicken Tikka). This restaurant does take the term "hole in the wall" to another level though. While I'm sure they must be clean to pass health department standards, it doesn't necessarily exude cleanliness in its aesthetics. Also, while this is minor, pictures on the wall are askew which not only bugs my OCD, but makes it appear as though the owners don't care. I'd encourage the owners to spruce up the place a bit to mirror in aesthetics the great food they serve there. It will go a long way towards making your customers comfortable and coming back for more. That said, I'll still be coming back for more so take that for what it's worth.
I love this place and the people who work here. The food is amazing and the atmosphere is interesting, to say the least. The Green Curry is my favorite.

The food was amazing. Very nice wait staff and the environment was pleasing. I had the Dolamades with out lemon creme sauce. simply delicious. The vegetables that accompany the plate was yummy. Bright and very pleasing to the eye. Fun time had by all. The food looks just like the pictures that you see in the menu or online. Will definitely return.
Standard Noodles & Company restaurant. Very clean, friendly staff, and fast delivery of food. Got the Pesto Cavitappi on their Zoodles and enjoyed it very much. Great folks and a good food. Thank you
Best donair I've had I years! Also very reasonably priced, will definitely come back again.
Pleasant atmosphere with very good food and very good service. The location is great, just off I 170. It is a perfect place for a relaxing meal for anyone who likes Indian cuisine.

Don't order delivery from here. I got the Alu Gobi and I received enough rice for 4 people and half a cup of the stew. It was okay but definitely not worth the price, especially for a vegan dish! I'll stick to the Indian food from Trader Joe's.

This place is so great! It's not the bad sushi place that used to be here, this is a new place, and you need to come! Full bar, great beer and drink specials, amazing menu with all sorts of Asian variety including Thai, Korean, Japanese, etc. There is no sushi bar to sit at, but a regular bar, lots of tables and TVs for entertainment. I had the Galbi and it was huge and very good. My husband ordered a sushi roll as well as the fried rice and both were also good. Lots of fish in the roll and the fried rice was loaded with meat and vegetables. Plenty of parking in the lot or on the street...same parking lot as Burger Republic.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: We were in town on business and decided to go for some different cuisine, very happy that we did! The food was outstanding, made from scratch, the service was great, all the way around it was an incredible dining experience! I rarely take the time to do a Yelp review unless it was an over the top experience as this was! Check them out, you won't be disappointed!

The food was amazing! Best Chicken Tikka Masala hands down, the lamb somasas were tasty and not to spicy, mango Lassi was good and best part was we actually had a lot to take home! Definitely my favorite Indian restaurant to go to now! I also loved that we didnt feel rushed like other Indian restaurant and that the owner came to check on us and others while we were there.
Affordable homemade-style meals. One star off for not willing to share their WiFi.

I have been here twice. Once to-go and once I ate here. The Vietnamese poboy I ordered to go was good. I think it was the meatball. It was long and skinny compared to other Vietnamese po-boys I've had before but still tasty and around $7. The chicken pho is what I had the time when I dined in. The cook/order-taker in back recommended I eat the pho there, "it betta here" were his exact words, I believe. They give ya a big bowl w/tons of steaming noodles that you have to walk on a plastic tray to the small tables area in front. It feels kind of funny balancing a big bowl of soup while passing up old drunks opening and closing the cooler doors to get to their alcohol. The dining area is the main reasons I gave it three stars; it was pretty dirty and they had a homeless couple sleeping and snoring the table over (see picture). Eat well also doesn't give you a cup of ice water bc they want you to buy a bottle of water from the convenience store part of the place. Oh and the napkins they give are brown paper hand towels you use to dry your hands with in bathrooms usually. They have sriracha n hoisin sauce. All in all the pho was good and comforting. The store is a pretty ghetto operation so eating there is kind of adventurous. If you don't mind eating in what feels like Magnolia Mart or IDEAL gas station then I'd say order the pho. That and a bottle of ice tea set me back $9.03. But if you're in a hurry go with the Vietnamese poboy for $7 and some change.
The food tasted great, but they brought out some garlic naan in a basket that had ants crawling out. Good thing my date was all nature-y and it didn't spook her out. I'm not coming back though.
I saw this place off of the interstate near Opry Mills. Good food and great atmosphere. I'd go again.

Ekta is within walking distance from our home and since we moved here six months ago we have been here four times and ordered take out about four times. We love Indian food! I brought an out of town guest here for lunch and she thoroughly enjoyed the experience. She always has a lot of questions and the waiters were more than happy and patient with their responses. We have tried many of the dishes and each one was delicious so we don't have a favorite. The ambience here is beautiful and relaxing.

The owner of this restaurant told me about it every time I went to buy beer from 805 liquor. The food was absolutely amazing. I had never really tried Mediterranean food before, I wasn't to sure of what everything was but the owner came right up to the counter and explained each item while recommending a delicious dinner. I will be going back for more. Also the hummus is the best I've ever had.

Ok so there is really nothing magical or Disney feeling about Aladdin's, in fact at times it's a little sleazy, but for some reason more often than not I end up there. When entering Aladdin's you will usually be seated way to close to a party of 8, have some horrible music video serenading you in the background, and have your vision obscured by the sudden darkness. Once you get over all that, order yourself a hookah and get over it. I can't really speak for the food, having only once had a very mediocre appetizer, but I can speak to my favorite hookah flavor ABRA KADABRA, and yes it's magical. What it lacks in ambiance it marginally makes up in the wide variety of tobacco flavors that they offer. It's not the kind of place you want to spend a lot of time in, but it's definitely a good place to enjoy at least one hookah and a round of beers with some friends.

We were just here today for a family of 8 plus 5 kids. There were only one table with customers and no one greeted us. The waitresses looked grumpy n angry! We ordered a bowl of pho for the kids and asked for no onions but they ended bringing out two orders instead of one. The excuse was you ordered one and your mom ordered the other. Clearly they have listening issues. We just took the other extra order and ate it to not create much of a fuss. However we have small kids and they were playing with the mini bowls in the table and the owner or bus boy told us three times to not put it back in the chopsticks holder for other customers to use. We know better than that and don't need to be told three times. It's really rude to talk to a customer like that while they are still eating! Wtf! Not only that we ordered 3 orders for 3 person bo 7 mon which isn't cheap either. The noodles were over boiled as it was all broken up n the veggies are not fresh looking. You tell them to bring it out a bit later since we want the kids to eat first as the beef dishes are a bit complicated to eat, they don't listen n still bring it out. Overall food was ok but you don't treat customers like that! They need better listening skill n be more welcoming if they are in the restaurant business! We didn't just drop $200+ for you people to treat us nasty like that! You just lost a good customer!

I was super excited to try this place out because we all know, authentic Vietnamese food in SB/Goleta is scarce. Friends and I came on a Sunday night and it wasn't too busy. We were seated quickly. We ordered spring rolls and regular combination pho. The spring rolls were good but it was expensive for 4 rolls ($9) and was stuffed with mainly lettuce. I would've liked it to have more of a balance between that and the rice noodles. The combination pho ($10) was very flavorful and tasty- authentic as it gets. The broth has a bit more fat than I'm used to back in OC but that's ok. The portions were fair... I would've just given a bit more of the pho noodles. This servers were nice and friendly even though they weren't well versed with the food or ingredients. Will be back to try their rice/com plates and banh mi. Overall, a solid start and place for real Vietnamese food. Pho= 4 stars service= 4 stars Price = 3 stars

We went here for my husband's birthday and the food was great! Highly recommend to try this place out if you're looking for something flavorful and new. They offer a wide variety of veg and non-veg options. Portion sizes are small so you have to order multiple dishes for a full meal. I also recommend coming here during a weeknight rather than Friday or Saturday as it was a bit crowded. Overall this is a lovely place in the city with some exotic flavors!

My fiancé and I decided to try a new Thai restaurant and came here. I really wanted to like this place, but the wrong choice of spice level ruined my first dining experience at Thai Legacy. The good: inside the restaurant was pretty spacious, the owner here seemed to genuinely care and the service was attentive. And they give you hugeeeee portions. The bad: ordered tom yum soup, drunken noodle with beef, and sweet chili garlic fish. We asked for mild to avoid anything too spicy, but all of our dishes were bland and served way too mild. I mean not all Thai food is made spicy, but I feel like especially having drunken noodle and tom yum soup bland like that is you're basically doing wrong eating Thai food. Keep this in mind when you order your dishes.

AVOID! nasty place. the shrimp tasted mushy and flavorless. i've never had anything so bad--8 inedible shrimp that went straight in the trash. the pork was crunchy. the noodles soft. the sauce was OK. the carrots overcooked. sweet and greasy. tastes like cheap Americanized Chinese only that it's supposed to be Thai. never again Rearn.

I never got why Bui's is so apparently awesome. I must've missed the memo... It's alright. I've gotten a couple of the specials, and their subs are typically made with a combination or ham, egg, cheese, and/or condiments, wrapped in foil and ready to eat. I get that it's cheap and convenient, but so are most of the food trunks along 38th or Spruce. Someone tell me what I missed, please!!!

The food here is sooooo yummy, and fresh!!! The wait is a bit long, but worth it. This is a small intimate place, very clean and comfy. Oh and very cheap!! I spent 12$ and my meal was delicious. I ordered shrimp tempura rolls and a side of veggie fried rice. I cannot wait to go back again!

We read about this restaurant on Yelp, and as tourists in Santa Barbara, decided to seek it out. The Thai food here is excellent. I encourage prospective diners to savor the Seafood Platter....It was wonderful ! We also had the gorund chicken with chili and basil, and the Japonese eggplant with tofu. Each dish was outstanding. Service was friendly, attentive, and warm. This restaurant is in the Mesa neighborhood, on the periphery of a community shopping center. Were it not for its "secondary" location, I would award it five stars.

Soooo I normally order through this place off Uber eats- but today I ordered from them directly and my fries were horrible- stale- cold and I could barely chew them. I called the restaurant to try and get new fries sent out but they refused. I was hungry and she's telling me to contact chow now to get a refund. My coworker even complained about the crusty cold fries. Not to mention that whoever I was speaking to hung up on me. I even offered her the fries back so they can see that I haven't touched them. Don't order from them!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Everytime we come here and bring new people they never disappoint.... Their food is fresh and delicious always. We been coming here for over 15yrs. Nice hidden gem for sure

This is one of the worst restaurants in Indiana..had ordered karadi paneer and they came with Sahi paneer ..than they apologized and came with Sahi paneer which was made in 5 minutes..fully burn..won't recommend anyone

Let me start off by saying the food was okay. Nothing wrong with the quality. However orderinh from there was different. We ordered on grubhub, and it was a such a pain. It took 20 min for them to accept our order, and we received an estimated time. We received our food an hour after it was supposed to arrive. When the driver got it to us, he pretty much told my friend here's your food, it was too far. And left. And forgot two of our items we ordered! If it was truly outside of their delivery range, please update your information with the services you use.

Having just returned to England .I feel I must express my experiance while in USA .of a lovely Indian restaurant we went to near our hotel ...named THE SPICE KITCHEN in Lansdale ..the food was good .atmosphere was brilliant ...And staff absolutely fantastic . Great help and proffesional advice from Amit And Atul . As we weren't sure Wat to order .. Their help and professional manner was very much appreciated .. As was the friendly approach .. We would definitely come back wen next in Lansdale ..And recommend this restuaraunt to anyone wanting the experiance of something special ...I must also add the magic tricks by Amit were astounding ... He went beyond the call of duty to entertain us ......And make us feel extremely welcome ... Well done Amit .!!And thank you ...hope to see you next time we visit .

This is the best place in the city. Their food is ALWAYS exceptional . Have never had anything from there I did not like. All platters, fish hoagies. Their desserts, banana pudding, carrot cake, bean pie, amazing!

In my last weeks here, I wanted to try out a few more places in the area. I decided I wanted a Vietnamese Sandwich today after not getting one last time I was near a Lee's in SF... I came across the reviews for this place after looking for a good Pho place last week. Came here for lunch today and I gotta say it wasn't too bad. I got the sandwich alone. Who eats Vietnamese sandwiches with chips and a soda? I dunno... I usually eat the sandwich and get spring rolls... which was exactly my order. House Combo Sandwich - 4 stars - They got the flavors spot on. Felt like getting a good ol' sandwich back home. Not bad for $3.25 either - the ones at home are $2.50, but who can complain. The meats were great, the daikon and carrots were a little thin, but added the right flavors and crunch. The baguette was pretty good, too. Spring Rolls - 2 stars - Very disappointing. They looked good, but as soon as I unwrapped the package and checked out the sauce, I noticed it wasn't the stuff I was used to. I usually get a more peanut based sauce to go with spring rolls. "Oh well," I thought, "Maybe they taste better with this sauce..." - Unfortunately, no. My first bite was sauceless just to check the composition of the rolls - they weren't wrapped tightly enough and everything inside was a bit loose and not flavorful at all. The shrimp in particular was extremely bland. The next bite with the sauce didn't really help things. Too bad =/ This is a good place to get a cheap sandwich - I'd avoid the spring rolls. Still, their spring rolls are better than most of the "fresh rolls" I've been getting in the Boise area. There stars based on the average of the food I had. If based on the sandwich itself, I'd give the place a four. Totally agree with Vera M., though - Nice to know Boise is getting more diversity in food, though.

Horrible service this time. Usually this place is good but it has gone down hill. We had to wait for a long time just to get water. Then the guy came to take order after a long time. To top it off, there was hair in the food. I don't think we will be coming back here or recommend it to anyone. Place has gone downhill. Time to look for another Indian restaurant!
Terrible. Their food comes pre made in plastic bags. How do I know? My friend almost ate a piece of the plastic bag in her food. No thanks.

Persia Biriyani Grill is the the only Indian restaurant I love in the area and coming from an Indian this is a huge thing. We usually order carry out but we did get a chance to dine in with our friends one afternoon. We thought the restaurant was small and cozy. If you are a large party, ensure you make a reservation before hand. Ambience: neat clean small restaurant. Friendly staff. Food: We usually get the Lamb Biriyani or Chicken Biriyani. Both are fabulous! The Garlic Naan and Butter Chicken is great too. The Dals are tasty if you are a vegetarian. One of my fav dish is Gobi Manchurian. It is a cauliflower dish and it hits the spot! Service: Service is not too slow but on the slower side.it depends on how busy they are. They can tweak the dishes to your preference. We usually get them spicy and love the heat. We have ordered from Persis on many occasions and absolutely love them. They are on the pricier side but worth it!

I just moved to Philadelphia one month ago and have already been here twice, it's that delicious. A must try! Great prices and a clean establishment with high quality food, you can't beat it! 5/5 stars.
If you enjoy a few bugs floating in your Pho broth, then this is the place to go. I just vomitted a little in my mouth writing this as I go back on the experience. It will haunt me for life....

Made my first visit since the previous Kombo Kitchen. Ordered the crab fried rice, drunken noodles and short ribs. Ordered was messed up and I got the duck fried rice instead of short ribs but it was still delicious so I couldn't be mad. There's no more "1-5" spiciness level, just mild, medium, hot and thai hot. I got medium for the sake of my boyfriend and there was no hint of spiciness. I'm excited to try the Thai got next time. Average $10-12 a dish but portions are huge so you get a couple meals out of them.

This has become our go-to restaurant! The food and service is always excellent, and there is plenty of things on the menu if you are a vegan or vegetarian, or if you just want to eat healthy!!! It's a BYOB, so bring your wine and enjoy a great meal!
A bit pricey but the lamb and the duck dishes are completely worth it! I would save up and go there again! Yum yum yum yum yum!!!!! The service and environment is great too!

We were in the area and looking for a place we could eat with two small kids. Thought it would be a good cultural experience. It took FOREVER for someone to notice that we were there and then to come and take our order. It almost seemed like our waiter did not have a firm grasp on the English language. The food was tasty, but the portions were SO small. If my 1.5 year old can eat an entire entree, you know it's not enough food. Also, the "lamb" was either beef, goat, or some other mystery meat - but def not lamb. We eat a great deal of lamb and this was not it. The pumpkin was very tasty and I'd recommend it if you eat here. The firnee (afghani rice pudding) was gelatinous beyond normal and tasted like it had been in the 'fridge for way too long. Overall, the food was pretty good, but portions required us to eat another meal at home later and we are not particularly big eaters.

Wow this food was soooooo good. Got an amazing soup and chicken dish. The owner and wait staff were wonderfully friendly. All of my tablemates raved about how good their food was too!!! Highly highly reccomend!

Staying at the Hyatt Place Opryland and wanted a quiet place to grab some drinks and dinner without a huge crowd. Immediately got seated and had great service. We ordered a large Saki and 2 beers which came quickly. As well as our soups which were hearty and filling. Had Thom Ka which was delicious. My husband ordered the Pad Thai and I had the Thai Pacific noodles which were both good and huge portions. Went for go karts next door afterwards.

Maybe the best middle eastern place in the city! Prices are great, service was nice, the place is really clean, and the grocery is decent albeit small. They even have legs of lamb for sale and bones all of which are packaged cleanly and looked fresh. The shawarma sandwich I had was the best I've had in New Orleans - super flavorful and great sauces. This is definitely a must see if you're in Arabi!
Very good food. In appetizer, recommend bulana. In main course, I tried kabobs which were nice, also tried palaw which was amazing ! For vegetarian, you can go for banjan.
The Lobster Mac was very flavorful, had a kick to it, but not too much for me, and I generally go with mild to medium spice. Felt happy with my choice!

The food here is good. I've yet to try anything here that I didn't like but my favorite is their tofu salad. It is so refreshing and just perfect. Portions are good, price is reasonable, service is friendly.

The gyros (both lamb and chicken) and so so delicious! The meat is well seasoned and the Taziki sauce is out of this world! The service is fast and all the workers and very friendly and helpful! They don't have French fries or a soda fountain, but the food is well worth it! A great lunch spot!

I was looking for a place that had Thai tea and Pad Thai ... this place satisifedd both of my cravings. Pad Thai was delicious and the tea was sweet and creamy. I even got a Thai Iced Coffee to go ... it was GREAT!!!! It was a blend of coffee and caramel maybe. I'm not sure exactly, but I can tell you that I'll be going back!

I ordered takeout from this restaurant and was pleased with my order. I got the Todd Mun Chicken appetizer - deep fried ground chicken patty with a blended in curry paste. I also ordered the Kanom Bueng entree which is a Asian style crepe stuffed with shrimp, bean sprouts, carrots, and coconut. Both are served with a cucumber sauce. The cucumber sauce is a little deceiving because I was expecting more of a yogurt base sauce with dill (kind of like tzatziki), but that wasn't the case. Their cucumber sauce is just a cucumber salad in a sweet vinaigrette style dressing. Overall, this place is pretty good and I would order again.

Naf Naf! Fun to say and fun to eat! I love how this delightful little establishment has made this type of food more accessible. The set up is just like a chipotle or what have you...start with this base, add that protein, top with these vegetables, and dump a sauce of your choosing atop your creation. So far I've tried the falafel and the chicken. I think I prefer the falafel as they are a bit tidy with the chicken. The hummus is delightful, as is the veggie toppings. I love their pickles, as they are spicy and crunchy bits of heaven. Oh, and the bowls come with a piece of pita bread to scoop up all that goodness stuck to the side of the bowl Naf Naf has fun little add ons too the fries are the tits, and the lentil soup is very filling and tasty. I eyed up the baklava which looks delicious but I am yet to try it. Give Naf Naf a try for something cheap, different, and satisfying!
Great food that is ideal for lunch. The staff maintains fresh options and a clean work area. Wonderful staff as well. Definitely would recommend!
This place is right by my work so I go often for lunch. It's always delicious and the staff is very friendly and accommodating! Try the spring rolls and the bun. So delicious

Best undiscovered Indian buffet in the suburbs. The wife and I have been here 14 times. That's right 14. Their weekday lunch buffet is $8 and is the best deal around. Lots of choices both meat and vege. A fresh basket of Naan delivered to your table. Friendly servers. What's not to like! The weekend lunch buffet is $11 and change. Again a great deal! If you are looking for a great lunch any day of the week give this place a try.
I got the taro milk tea, chicken banh mi, pork buns, and spring rolls. Everything was super delicious and I'd highly recommend everything

My husband and I drive all the way from Lutz to have dinner at Thai Legacy. The service is incredible and the food is even better. We have tried almost everything on their vegan menu, and nothing has ever disappointed. We love this place!

10 stars if I could give it. Excellent food and a large vegan menu. The doctor says no more meat and dairy for me. The spouse can have what she wants, and there is a full standard menu for her. This was the best pad thai I have ever had and all vegan. Spotless restaurant, wonderful people. The owner is wonderful, inviting and very friendly. We loved her. We will be back many times, having driven all the way from the University of South Florida. Thanks for the great experience! And thank you for meeting the needs of special diets.
Excellent food and service! We had the chicharron de cerdo, carne mechada, pastelitos de pollo and queso, plus black beans and rice. Everything was wonderful - we will be regulars here!
Terrible layout of the Restuarant and rude wait staff were the worst part of our dining experience. The food was often too spicy. I don't imagine we will be dining here any time soon.
Excellent Thai food as well add efficient and quick service by Dinny. Lunchtime special was $8.95 that included soup and entre'. Highly recommend!

This is a must visit for any Edmontonian. Remedy is synonymous with the best Chai Lattès. They have a few to choose from but I suggest sticking to the original:) I have ordered hundreds of these... They have a LOT to choose from but I frequent the samosas and dahl/curries. I leave with food sweats every time. It is SO GOOD! (As long as I remember to ask for no cilantro! Why does that stuff exist?...) The atmosphere is also pretty good. A nice spot to sit and read/study or catch up with a friend. Free wifi = happiness

You're hungover. Turkey leftovers are tired. Gyros sound like more the ticket! But mom can't find out you're skipping the remains of her laborious turkey dinner. Okay by now, it's clear I'm talking about my cousin... definitely not me! But I digress. A couple clicks on my Yelp app yielded what would turn out to be a deliciously messy, completely necessary experience with an overstuffed gyro. Sure, Soco Gyros & Deli doesn't look like much on the outside... but tell that to your mouth after putting away one of these stacked sandwiches! Meat: Most excellent! Tzatziki: Luscious. Pita: Very good. Hot sauce (don't judge): Terrific. Presentation: Perfectly swaddled like a newborn baby (read: ain't no meat falling out of this pita!). Only menu item I can live without is our shared appetizer, the hummus, as it lacked that homemade taste and super creamy texture I love. Just a little over $20 for a solid lunch of two gyros, two soft drinks and that ho-hum hummus. And mission accomplished: I got back to my cousin's couch and promptly fell asleep for three hours! That's one hell of a gyro-induced coma doing its job and erasing hangovers all over the StL.
large portions and very nice staff. enjoy! I was glad i saved my meal as I did eat it the next day - only wish it came with more vegetables but can't complain as the price was great, too.

Barely 100 feet from a formidable competitor, L'Angolo, is the bigger and every bit as friendly Scinicchios. Large portions and reasonable prices a bonus as the food is excellent. Pork and chicken dishes savory and moist and the pasta good with the gnocchi marvelous; and just light enough to satisfy those who still like a bit of heft in their little dumplings. Cream and Gorgonzola sauce for the pasta perfect when you need a rich fix.

Suraya was one of the most anticipated restaurants to open in Philadelphia in 2017. I had read about it, and I love Cafe La Maude and was really excited to get there. I really don't know why I waited so long but after a few months of not getting to Suraya, we finally ceased an opportunity on a Sunday afternoon in May for our first visit. Suraya is fairly large space and it is well designed and beautiful. It is also a refined and comfortable setting. The entire staff was very attentive friendly and helpful. The menu is diversified without being too large. We ordered the slow roasted lamb hummus, the éclat chocolate yogurt and the beet salad. All three dishes were excellent and with a delicious array of flavors. Everything was very memorable and that is hard to find these days. The pastries were outstanding also, especially this short bread Lebanese crack thing with a pistachio filling. If you like short bread and pistachio. find this on the menu and order it. Maybe order two. I was very impressed with Suraya and hope to get back here very soon for dinner.

My husband and I love it here. Aroy is our "go to" Thai restaurant in the area. The portions are large for the price you pay especially compared to a couple other locations in neighboring cities. We normally order the Pad See Ew (my favorite), Pad Thai, or Pineapple Fried Rice. We also have been venturing off our usuals and have never been disappointed with anything from the menu. The service is excellent. The wait is typically a quick sit down and an instant order time. The workers are extremely polite and have great timing when it comes to asking for what we need and bringing refills on anything. I highly recommend this restaurant for any Thai favorites or if you want to explore Thai cuisine!

We selected two different entrées from the vegan menu and were delighted with both. We will definitely be going again. It's a nice family restaurant having just celebrated their first anniversary. Everyone was very friendly.

My son and I spent the afternoon gaming at the mall arcade, and our dinner break was at Phan's Kitchen. The service was so friendly, it really made our night. The egg rolls were fantastic! The pad kee maw was quite good, too, and she was kind to take the spice down a few notches for my son. I ordered in a hurry and wished I had tried the fresh spring rolls and Pad Thai instead. Next time! The restaurant certainly isn't a speedy place to eat, but she seemed to make everything fresh for us. I appreciated that a great deal. Expect a similar wait to a take-out place, just not fast food counter service. It's right outside of Target, so it's an easy little side trip if you're heading there. Worth it!

My husband and I really enjoyed this place. We stopped here on our way to a convention center event. It's in walking distance. We started with the premium rum flight. Of coarse we like the most expensive one at the end I think it had a crystal in its name. It was quite tasty. We then each had mojitos and they were the best I have had in a long time, so worth the $10 price. We then shared the mashed potatoe balls that are deep fried with meat in them. I forgot the name. Then I had the beef empanadas and my husband had the fried chicken. Their rice and beans were surprisingly extra flavorful because the white rice was extra salty. We loved it. The hanging light in the circle booths were a little low in my option but I liked the decor and the outside seating. Great place if your craving some PortoRican cuisine.
So upset that they are closed, best Indian food and wonderful friendly service. If this management has opened a different location I would love to know.
Fuimos por recomendacion a este lugar y me queda decir que es un lugar acojedor y la comida es muy sabrosa ; nos decidimos por marisco a la caserola ( muy rico); los precios un poco elevados.

Nice, large, and clean pho spot. I ordered the pho with everything, except tendon. Tendon is gross. The broth was flavorful and the meat was well cooked. I felt for the near $8 price if a small, they could have been a little more generous with the meat. I really wanted to order egg rolls, but i couldn't justify spending $4 for just two of them. I also ordered a secret menu banh mi to go. They have four off menu flavors: chicken, beef, ham, and bbq pork. I ordered the ham because i think that is the generally classic version. It was pretty good for the price. I think it was $4 or $4.50 for one. If you are in the area, I would definitely recommend swinging by to grab one to go.

This is by far my favorite Thai restaurant! I would go here first before going to any Thai places in the St. Louis area or near by restaurants. I always get the kee-mau noodle, or the cashew chicken. Both are amazing dishes!

Excellent find in Nashville. Lorraine is an excellent server. I WILL be back to this place the next time I am in Nashville (in about three weeks). Best Happy Hour in Nashville if you want to relax. Great food (Gyro). Great atmosphere. A rating of 5 is well deserved.

I eat there for lunch a lot. Friendly service. Plenty of seats. Nothing fancy. Consistently delicious. I am no expert. I just like the food. And there's a great hardware store nearby. Eat food you don't understand; buy tools you didn't know existed. The perfect lunch.

I went with my friend. We ordered 1 chicken 65 appetizer, 1 rava masala dosa, 1 rassmalai, 1 salty lassi and 1 Diet Coke. Total bill $33. Taste- We loved chicken and dosa. Sambar was okayish. Rassmalai was thick and great too. Ambience- I do not value the ambience much as food is more important to me. The ambience was decent. They have extensive menu to choose from.

My first impression was seeing personable people working here! While thinking that, I thought there is not much of an environment here. Quite plain! That's okay though! You don't eat that! I met up with a wonderful friend for lunch, and she ordered Panang curry with a spring roll! I ordered mussaman curry and a salad. Our appetizers were pretty small. Her spring roll looked a bit awkward being its single little self. My salad was good served with peanut sauce. Our curries were the best out of everything. They tasted similar. Her's had green beans which I liked. Mine had potatoes. I actually tried a mussaman curry elsewhere for dinner since I liked it so much! I liked Orchid Thai's better! Check this place out! It's good and there seems to be many options on the menu that you can't find elsewhere!

Welcome to the neighborhood Pan d'Olive because you are awesome! From service to dinner fare, my first visit was perfection. Let's start with atmosphere. This place is contemporary and beautiful. My favorite part is that we were seating in an enclosed booth that created a very intimate dining experience. You could see and hear everyone else, but you barely knew they were there. Being so new, I was convinced that the service would be sub-par. How wrong I was! We were treated wonderfully. The perfect balance of not being overbearing, but not forgetting about us - which is probably hard to maintain for a busy server. Everyone seemed so genuine, which was refreshing. The food was excellent. On top of how great it tasted, you get excellent value for the prices. Small plates all sounded fantastic - we tried the roasted red pepper bruschetta (stunning presentation and my favorite taste-wise), the phyllo cigars (good but a little plain, even with the dose of herbs in the filling) and the arancini (stuffed with steak, potato and gorgonzola - good, but hard to taste the filling). The salads and the bread basket were all great. For the main dish, I chose the filet mignon. It was so good - cooked perfectly with a great crust and grill flavor. It was topped with blue cheese sauce and came with spinach. I also got a side of mashed potatoes that were, ironically, a wonderful balance of creamy and chunky. Everything was stellar. This could have easily been my last meal before going to death row and I'd be completely ok with them pulling the switch!

First off, Singha now has a location on Maple Street, between the Starbucks and Babylon Cafe, in a raised house that used to be an Italian restaurant. In a convo with one of the people whose family own it, we learned that one sister is cooking at the CBD location and the other on Maple, but on weekends the CBD sister comes Uptown to help out. We tried it on a Saturday night, and the place was hopping with people. The food was quite good, both in taste and appearance. The fried spring rolls were crispy without being greasy, with a flavorful filling. My friend's coconut milk soup (tom ka?) with chicken got a thumbs up from him in terms of flavor. I had what was described as a sweet curry (which also had a bit of coconut milk that added richness) with potatoes and carrots but had a nice chili kick to it. The spouse loved his Panang duck, which was sweet, crispy, and spicy all at once. And our friend enjoyed his green curry with beef. Portion sizes were about right, leaving us full but not overstuffed. On another tables, we noted that the pineapple fried rice was served in half a carved out pineapple: gorgeous presentation. I marked the rating down one star because of a piece of raw chicken in my friend's soup, which was a bit icky.
Nicely appointed restaurant. The food was good, but nothing special. We found the sauces pretty thin and not as much flavour. Usually Thai soups and sauces are much thicker from my experience.
We were pleasantly surprised by this place We ordered red curry and pad thai. Everything was fresh, flavorful and spicy just the way we like it.

One of my favorite Vietnamese restaurants in Reno! Service: Great service! We were seated immediately. Servers were very friendly and attentive. Food: All four dishes we ordered were simply delicious! We had banh canh - thick udon noodles served with different types of pork meat. Tje portion was huge - enough for 2 people. Charbroiled pork (thit nuong) rice plate was also good. The meat was flavored well. The best was the bun bo hue and ox tail pho. Bun bo hue was very tasty. There were plenty of meat and the flavor was delicious. I was very pleased. Ox tail pho is on point. Again, there was plenty of meat! I highly recommend this place for authentic Vietnamese food. I will defintely come back here again and try out their other dishes.

Best experience here. Really good food, fantastic drink options, nice atmosphere and expert bartender (Stacy of the fabulous mustache). I was happy to have several vegetarian options. The tacos with plantain chips were delish. So was the Chocolate Silk Cake. And if you like craft beer and IPA then try the Big Oyster Sour IPA - yum. Hipsters will feel very at home here. Fun.

The only reason I'm giving a bad review is because we just had the worst experience with " the guy with a clip board"!! Rude very rude! He told us to stand outside in the rain and doesn't offer us a seat in the waiting area! I love this hookah lounge!! But this guy was very rude with us!!!!

Lunch buffet was pretty good for the cost. Overall the restaurant looked nice, the place was fairly busy (good sign) and if that does it for you, great. Made the mistake of stopping by the restroom which is way in the back...past several kitchen areas full of bins full of dirty God knows what. Some things are best not seen. Waited a few hours to post this just in case...no ill effects so guess it was clean enough...but not sure about going back. Plenty of other places downtown.

When the pizza place nearby ran out of cheese, the hosted recommended this place along with the salmon salad. The baba genush was different but very good. It was very lemony and smokey while served with wonderful grilled pita. The spanikopita was amazing. Nice and crispy. While the salmon salad looked great too with a large cut of salmon on top. Service was fash and cheery and the patio was very enjoyable.

La Casona offers excellent authenticate Puerto Rican cuisine. I've been here many times and I've had just about everything on the menu. The downside is that service is very slow and the owner seems to have an attitude with his customers. If the service was better I would give this a four, but the food for the most part is delicious.

This hidden gem is in Washington Square Mall. A great hi-light! The owner is awesome and will make sure you are taken care of. The food is ridiculously good. The food I would best describe as being truly authentic with a lot of soul. It's food that you would have cooked from your Mom or Grandma! You have to go here! It's must. I had the pleasure of having her Pho (Sunday's) and ummm let's just say "Outstanding"! The atmosphere is quiet and spacious. You can see your food prepared right in front of you, fresh. Every order. The staff is friendly. If you are lucky enough to experience the sauté chicken, get it! Great place!!!!

Yay, a restaurant that is open on Monday! I was craving pho and I didn't want to drive all the way to the West Bank. I wanted something on my route to home from work, and I found Pho Cam Ly on Yelp. I ordered the small Pho Tai and a Grilled Pork Bahn Mi. The small pho was a pretty good sized bowl. I was almost too full to eat any of my Bahn Mi, but I am greedy and ate half of it any way. I got the other half to go. I really enjoyed the pho. I didn't even put any sriracha in the broth until I was 2/3 of the way done (I love sriracha in my pho but I was savoring the broth in its original flavors before I added anything to it later). The grilled pork in the bahn mi was less exciting than some other Vietnamese restaurants, but it was a decent sandwich by all means. I will surely be returning.

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: went there the other day with my boyfriend and stepmom, this sushi was so amazing! and it was another one that from the outside didnt look like it would be this good!! we got seaweed salad first which is amazing! some places are much better then others and this was deffinitly one of the best. then i had the dragon roll and it was displayed so nicely and it looked exactly like a dragon and it was so delicious!! the boys stepmom got the rainbow roll and that was so good!! she also got salmon sashimi and that was soo smooth it melted in your mouth!! amazing! dont judge a book by its cover!! go in and try this place and i know you wont be disappointed!
Every meal I've had here has been so good. Thai Fusion is like super good Thai home cooking. I don't even like crab rangoon but I love THEIR crab rangoon.

I was not impressed with this place. I ordered the Veggie Pho. I thought it tasted pretty ordinary. I tried to make it better by squirting the plastic-ketchup-bottle hot sauce into it, but that didn't do much. The bean sprouts it came with seemed sort of weird, almost like they got a bit frozen. The tofu in the soup was nice, but the broth tasted crappy. I know chicken broth pho isn't "real" pho, but it's on the menu, so it should taste good. They have great chicken broth soups at the Pagolac and Phobulous. I also didn't like the atmosphere of this place. It was like trying to be minimalist, but it looked cheap. I mean, just go cheap or go chic--just pick one! I'd be heading to Chinatown next time. Sheesh.

I've been to many different Vietnamese restaurants over the decade + I've been in Philly. This spot I would describe as "pho lite", better than chains like pho 75, but not as authentic tasting as Pho Saigon or some of the Washington Ave spots. The broth tastes more like beef buillon and not as full bodied as some of the other stocks I've tried. Despite that, the cleanliness and service here rates much higher, which is appreciated. I ordered the Tai Gan which came with a large portion of rare steak and soft tendon, not the random pencil eraser stuff you can sometimes find. I will definitely order again!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: The food is consistently amazing. The service is consistently terrible. 15 minutes to get acknowledged for the first time by the server. A half hour to get the first glass of wine. We've been here an hour and a half and our entrees aren't served yet, which would make me upset were it not for the fact that we're too sympathetic to the couple next to us who were here when we arrived and haven't been served yet either. Another table walked out unserved 45 minutes ago and it's not clear that the servers noticed. Seriously, Taj Mahal, invest in basic restaurant service training and you'd be far and away the best Indian restaurant in SW Idaho. The food is worth not destroying the experience with incompetent servers.
Ive reviewed Pho Voorhees already. It was fantastic then and it continues to be fantastic. The food is consistent. Would highly recommend the summer rolls, pho, pad thai and their grilled platters.

This small quiet India bistro has a very extensive menu, very reasonably priced. Their food is authentic, and very fresh. The Decour is beautiful and the restaurant is spotless. The service is above average. I would highly recommend Aroma

The owner was very friendly just like the name! A great place to shop. They sell delicious indonesian foods and snacks. There are also indonesian bakery (martabak manis, lemper, lapis surabaya, lapis legit, etc) and bakery from china town freshly made everyday. The price was reasonable. They sell a lot of intresting things there including the phone card, money gram, etc. If you are in the area this is definitely a must place to be stopped by.

I like this place! it has a wide selection of pasta dishes, and everything I have had so far has been very good. It's fast casual, with a very good service atmosphere. The food has always been delivered really quickly...and the staff has always come around to collect the dishes and check on me. As the others have mentioned, the drink machine here is pretty awesome. I only drink water, but I was told this soda fountain does 200 drink combinations. I had seen this prototype a few years back in a special Coca-Cola was doing. It's really cool to see this thing in action. Another thing that impressed me about this place - I tweeted about being there. And the next day I got a personal message back from them. They are obviously into customer service from the corporate level down to the bellboy.

One word: maqlooba! A friend recommended this place after I expressed my love for Mediterranean Arab food and I am so happy she did. Spoiler alert: I'm coming back. My part of three got a booth immediately. We were given pita halves to nosh on while we deliberated the extensive menu. We ordered the vegetable platter appetizer, which consists of cucumber and tomato salad (I'm not sure if it was supposed to be tabbouleh or not - it was too cuke-heavy to be counted in my book as tabbouleh), falafel, grape leaves, hummus and babaghanouj. The smokey flavors pop in the babaghanouj. I could eat a whole tub of it. For reasons unknown I'd been craving maqlooba for days. Rarely do I see it in restaurants. Lo and behold it was one of their two daily specials. A "half-sized" order ($9) is a heaping plate full of savory basmati and lamb. It fed me for two days. The menu is packed with reasonably priced options. A falafel sandwich is $4 and a kefta sandwich is $5 or $6. Be prepared to spend some time mulling over your options. Every day there's a special. This is a great space for a large party or for an intimate family/friend dinner. And it's perfect for local lovers of Mediterranean Arab food.

Bitar's is a great local middle eastern place. It's half grocery store, half take-out place. I usually stop by here and get a falafel but they got other things too. Their falafel isn't deep fried like what I would normally expect. Instead they just put it on the griddle until its crisp. The result is a light, flavorful sandwich that will only set you back less than 3 bucks. I haven't decided if I prefer Bitar's over Maoz. Usually when I eat at Maoz, I end up stuffing myself silly on the salad bar. At Bitar's you get your sandwich for a nice cheap price and eat a reasonable amount. They're two different experiences. The grocery store half of Bitar's is good too. They sell all kinds of middle eastern foods, among such goods are fresh pitas, hummus, and some pastries. Bitar's is a solid neighborhood establishment and I'm glad to have them right down the street.

Best Indian food in the area! We've been here multiple times, dined in twice and done pick up at least three times. Butter chicken is incredible and the chicken tikka masala is the best I've ever had. Hubs loves chicken vindaloo and he said it's the best he's had. I like that you can specify what level of spice you want - the spicy is seriously hot but so good. Garlic naan is a must too. Service is always super friendly. Highly recommend!

Philadelphia isn't New York. I know in Philly I'm not going to find Ethiopian delivery at 4am. However, I've expected to find a suitable Dominican place - and until now, I really haven't. Today, we found it. Parada Maimón is like any place in the DR you'd want to go after a day at the beach. Amazing seafood and all the typical Dominican food you'd want. It's BYOB, so bring your own Presidentes, but expect your fill of tostones, ceviches and chillo entero. ¡Que rico!

While I enjoy basking in the hippiness of soft music, mismatched furniture, dirty toilets, dreadlocks and yoga mats, I'm definitely underwhelmed by Remedy. I've not been a very active Remedier - having probably been there about 6 times over the last two years. The list of chais that they serve here is an impressive one. While I do enjoy the Kashmiri chai and their regular chai, I happened to have the ginger spiced chai today and was quite disappointed. In general, I'm not very fond of overly sweet chai but that's something that seems to be sell well, so I do consider Remedy to serve great chai. However, in the ginger chai the ginger wasn't mixed at all and the drink was just a regular chai till I go to the last two sips that were extremely pungent. It's okay - it's still a solid 3 star chai. The masala dosa, on the other hand was at the far end of the rating spectrum. I've heard so many Edmontonians speak praises of how good the masala dosa at Remedy is, so I figured I should give it a try. Now, I'm not one of those Indians who generally expects a lot from Indian restaurants. Having said that, this dosa I had today was probably the worst rendition of any Indian dish I've had in Canada (thus far). I say rendition because it is certainly Remedy's interpretation of what a masala dosa is. However, it's an awful interpretation. The batter had a very weird and rubbery texture. The filling (masala) was an unfortunate stir fry of vegetables that had flavors far from those expected in South Indian food. I was extremely disappointed. I don't want to get into how bad the chutneys and sauces were. The whole experience was, coming to think of it, a waste of calorie intake. I have no clue why they make masala dosas if they're going to make it like this. All in all, I'll come back but stick to chai. The wraps and other food is a decent 3 star, but nothing evoking a 'Wow!'. I understand that Remedy is dear to many and I love that they're an Edmontonian food presence. I much prefer the chai at 'Chai Pani' on Whyte.
The food is great and the service is good. I would recommend the vegetarian portions of the menu. The Sunday buffet is great too. The dosas are fantastic!

My husband have tried this restaurant probably four times. We have had breakfast, we've had lunch, and we've had dinner because we sooooo wanted to like this place. We have had some really good food but we have also had some very disappointing food typically at the same meal and that is probably the worst when half the table is super happy and the other extremely unhappy. The service is also hit or miss especially given their typical emptiness. Overall I would say the meals are quite small given the prices that you will pay at this restaurant. The last straw was when we went for breakfast the other Saturday with my mom. We had wanted to go to Simply Good across the street but it was packed like normal so we decided to go to le Gourmet instead which was very conspicuously completely empty (I have never been there that it has been crowded which I suppose should be a sign seeing as everything else in the area has a tendency to be packed). The breakfast menu was relatively expensive but we all ordered and my husband and mother got a reasonably good breakfast, I on the other hand got the mot anemic, sad breakfast sandwich I have ever had (note: unlike most breakfast places their meals do not come with any sides). The sandwich was tasteless tiny and expensive. If this had been a one time bad experience we would probably go back but given the inconsistency of this restaurant I would say that is the last time we will end up there.
Food is fair. They charge extra for everything. AND they tape their outlets so you can't charge your phones or any other electronics. Seriously?

Very disappointed in management today. I have come here two times in the past to the rooftop and had wonderful experiences both times. However, what I experienced today greatly affected my perception of this establishment. The restaurant was so understaffed that our server had ALL of the tables to herself. The sole bartender had to jump in and help her while leaving her bar unattended. Both women were incredibly nice and hospitable. Our server, Ellie, in particular gave us incredible service despite the inconvenience. My displeasure is entirely with management and the fact that there was no manager or owner to be seen. I have worked in the service industry many years and at the very least a sensible manager would be helping out his or her staff and ensuring costumer satisfaction. For the price, they should be able to hire much more experienced and competent managing staff. With that being said, the food was incredible and, once again, our server was incredible. We will be asking for Ellie again next time

The Good: Imperial rolls were crispy with good overall flavor. Just OK: The spring rolls with the peanut sauce were pretty bland. The robust peanut flavor was missing. The contents of the rolls were fresh, however. The Bad: See attached pic of the BBQ Sandwich. Minimal filling with dry, over-cooked, flavorless meat. I took nothing out of the sandwich prior to taking the picture. A sad, inedible sandwich. This was my 3rd visit this year. The service is what it is - I've experienced no better or worse here. Seems like they are going through the motions on many levels.

Fresh ingredients & great flavor. Loved the feta dip w/ pita, Greek salad with chicken, & fries. The Greek salad was topped with fried chick peas, cucumbers, tomatoes, kalamata olives, feta, & shredded chicken (love that it was shredded). The dressing was thicker than I anticipated & not my favorite, I prefer a thinner vinaigrette type Greek dressing but this one was thick & white. My husband had the lamb pita & enjoyed it too but says it had parsley & paprika on the lamb & he found that different than a standard gyro...not bad, just different! 4 stars because the price seemed a bit high.

I had seafood mofongo at La Casona and I have to admit that it did not disappointed me at all. Awesome plátano smash with a good amount of sea food including shrimp. Services was excellent. I'm definitely coming back to try more things in the menu.
This used to be my family's favorite place until recently! We were eating our meal and I look over and I see a cock roach on the edge of the table!! I'm no longer going to eat at this establishment.

On 4/19/2012, we went to this restaurant. We ordered two of their "Char-Broil Meyer's Rum Rib Eye Steaks." We were told that they had no ribeyes and would use a NY strip. What came where two pan fried pieces of meat with some onion on top. One of them was 1/2 fat. Both were terrible but the service was good. We tipped the waiter 20%, asked for a box and brought the leftover meat home to our dogs. They would only accept cash. I didn't want to create a problem and you know once a bad meal is done you don't want to eat anymore. However, the food was so bad that I called the next day and spoke to the owner/manager Mike. He told me that the waiter should have told us not to order steaks because on that night they use a substitute chef that is better at making sandwiches. He thanked me for calling and asked me to call the next day after he looked into the matter. I called back the following day. The owner/manager Mike said I was a "f***ing liar" said we had cleared our plates and followed that with more profanity. We ended the conversation. Anyone interested in seeing the container and the "meat" we brought home for the dogs is welcome to come by before the trash is collected on Friday.

Here we go!! This is what I was looking for. The lunch time buffet is on point! Excellent selection of Marsala, curry, and saga dishes. It was tasty and best of all, incredibly affordable! All you can eat for about 12 bucks! That's a deal anywhere. Highly recommended.

I have eaten here a number of times as well as their Nashville and Gallatin locations. The food is good at this location but I would have to say the best is in Nashville by the stadium. They do have an amazing papaya salad especially when you order it HOT! And the flavor of all of the dishes I have tried have always been very good. Give them a try next time you're near any of their locations

Very convenient for if you need to grab food and go. They have a really small buffet with rice and maybe 6 different entrees, typically with like 2 chicken dishes. You can eat there, but there's only like 4 tables. The food is cheap: $5.75 per pound, or you can alternatively purchase other stuff a la carte. Boo on no naan directly at the buffet. The chicken tikka is really tasty, and so is their saag paneer.
The ONLY Halal truck that I'll ever spend my money! Very friendly cooks and the greatest falafel I've ever had in my life; can't forget the bbq sauce... thank me later!

I went there and was utterly disappointed. There was no one in line, yet it took forever for me to get served. The employee was cleaning the kitchen hood and the serving area while my food was cooking ... and this was only at 6p (way before they close). A friend of mine, who ordered chicken (which is already cooked and sitting in a heated area) got diarrhea the next day. I would not recommend this to anyone.

First time eating Ethiopian, loved the whole experience! The ambiance was great. Service was wonderful! Food hit the spot! I loved eating without silverware! a refreshing change of pace for dinner!! The Ethiopian beer was Tasty! I was very pleased with Zagol!!!

I am a huge fan of Ethiopian food and new to Reno. I'm so glad I found Zagol because it has really great food. We had the veggie combo, beef and lamb and everything was just delicious. Can't wait to try other things on the menu!

I will admit that I have my favorites. I know what I like. Here, 9 times out of 10, I will get the beef kabobs (cooked medium) with the rice, hummus, pita, salad. It is at the corner of a squared off C-shaped strip mall with many other businesses in this strip. Huge parking lot. Friendly wait staff, clean restaurant. I have never seen this place more than half filled, though at times, they have had several large parties. They use some sort of lemon scented polish to clean the tables. The lemon smell in the restrooms is overwhelming, so if you have sensitivities, consider yourself warned. They play Mediterranean pop music videos on several televisions in the restaurant. I really like the staff and service here. Warm and welcoming!

It was about two weeks ago that I had finally a chance to go to Albasha. I have heard so many good things about the restaurant before I went here and I knew pretty much what to order. I still wanted to take a look at the menu. I think the menu was very rich because you can find so many different options from Mediterranean cuisine. I think it was really great that they had this much meza options on the menu. Mousaka was something else that really surprised me when I see it on the appetizers because mousaka is one of the great dish you can have that made by eggplant. I ordered one and it was pretty good. The rest of the menu was all about Mediterranean cuisine that you can expect from all restaurants. When I get to the restaurant, the restaurant wasn't crowded at all and there was no one to take me to any table. The place was so much bigger than I thought it was and it was very clean. I just chose one table and sat. The service wasn't quick enough to make me happy but staff were still not bad at all. They were friendly and smiley face which is really important for me and they have knowledge on almost everything on the menu. My experience of service was quite good but what I heard before I came was the service basically depends on who is working. I ordered lamb shish kebob and a mousaka as an appetizers. They were both really good and tasty. I also ordered the Lebanese tea. Even though, it wasn't bad at all, it just didn't meet with my expectations. What I also really like about this place is that their prices. I think the prices are very reasonable to what they do in this restaurant. The lamb shish kebab plate was only 12.50 $ that really surprised me because I don't think you can really find any Mediterranean restaurant in New Orleans that have this kind of prize, but mousaka was kind of expensive because they charge 7.50 for this. Even though, the taste was good I think it's little bit much for an eggplant appetizer. Also, I think this place could be good option if you come with a group because they have two sections in the restaurant.I think, I would definitely go back to Albasha again because their dishes are just tasty and if you are a eggplant lover, this place offers you couple of different plate that made by eggplant. I think this place is definitely worth to try.

The Saturday buffet is a little different than the one on weekdays, so there are a couple of other dishes available for only $1 more than weekdays. They always have great service, keeping water full. The buffet is fresh and the naan is great.
Friendly service, great food. I had the chicken red curry and it was delicious. Small place but clean with quick service.

Our first time here as we were just passing through the area. We were here for a weekday lunch. It was nice and clean and the staff was helpful and friendly. The water for our hot tea was just warm. The staff replaced it promptly with hot water. My Penang Curry had okay flavor but not as spicy hot as I prefer. But that's okay - it was my first time here. The thing that has me rating this place a 3 was the temperature of my food. My wife's Pad Thai was hot. My food was just warm. I think their pot of sauce for the Penang Curry was only warm - hence a just warm meal for me. I ate it but let staff know so they could make kitchen corrections. Do they ever? Who knows :)

Venue: small, quaint, empty Service: good, quick, friendly Food/drinks: I got the Che ba mau (3 colored dessert/3 beans) and it was good not great. I did ask for less ice cause it typically gets piled on way too much. Good ratio between each ingredient. I overall enjoyed the dessert. Price: horrendously pricey. It's beans..... they charged between 4-5 dollars for beans. It's hard to justify coming again when it costs so much. I can just save my cravings for philly and get the same if not better for half to 2/3s the price. Parking: small lot out front. If this place is ever packed then I imagine it'd be hard to get a spot. But I don't foresee this place ever getting too crowded. It's in an awkward location. Happy eating

My Friends and I stopped to have dinner after going ice-skating. When we walked in the place was quite empty for a saturday evening. There is a buffet for 11.95 which is pretty decent. I wished there were a littl more choice with the dessert and the salad bar. I took some chicken curry and chicken tikka massala. Overall the food tasted good but really didnt think it was the most amazing Indian food I have had. I wish they had some light music for the ambiance as the restaurant sounded very quiet and me and my friends felt like we were too loud in this atmosphere. The service overall was good.

Went here for my birthday on Wednesday night. We had made reservations in advance. The place looks really weird from the outside. You walk in and there are beautiful paintings and teak wood carvings and various other decorations all over. Very elegant touch. The server was pleasant and timely. My family was late, as usual, so she brought us water while we waited. The menu is nicely arranged although I am not sure why they have a separate veggie menu when every dish is made to order. whatever though. the apps were good. the entrees were good. very quick service. They offer take out which my boyfriend and I will take advantage of. Its hard to find veggie food in Abington. We were all satisfied with our experience. I say, if a restaurant is willing to put up with my family, they are ok in my book! Not sure what the total of the bill was but, most dishes are about 12 bucks. Not bad. I will be back!

The food is divine and the atmosphere is serene. I eat here every few months. By far, Spice Kitchen one of my top Indian restaurants. The Chicken Korma is lovely probably my favorite dish, though that is a hard choice. There are a lot of delicious meals to choose from.

I had been here twice...first was a regular sit-down meal, which was actually not too bad. No complaints. Second visit was a few months later, for the buffet...was upset at the general lack of choices compared to other places in the area, but who knows...maybe they make up for it in other ways. Well, I never got to find out, as during my first trip to the buffet I was greeted by a family of roaches walking around the food. Horrified, I immediately told a member of the staff, who just gave me a blank look as if to say "so what?". Needless to say, I walked straight out, never to return (and I mean never).

When we went inside the place was empty and the decor was somewhat unique. But the food was great and fresh. The service is a little unusual to say the least. Also watch out for 18% Indiana tax for more than 5 people. That is not a tip. That is extra.

Found this place on yelp. Was nervous at first because it said small plates and well i was thinking oh no another tapas bar where my kids will be hungry when we leave. Well decided to go in and try it anyway and omg i was so wrong, and so glad i did. The food is amazing. The staff was great. The owner/chef came to our table and greeted us and asked for suggestions and asked how everything was overall. We got the creazian fried rice, porchetta bahn mi, salmon, pork belly lollipops, calamari, and the crepe, it was absolutely wonderful :) We will definitely be going back here again.

Bui's was my first ever Penn food truck experience (thanks to an extremely hungover friend who asked me to get him a Hangover Special from Bui's) and I must say, it blew away the standard I held for food truck breakfast sandwiches! I had ordered a simple ham, egg white, and cheese on a bagel with light ketchup and pepper. Though the sandwich is uncomplicated to make, it's the fact that it wasn't greasy and sloppy - that is what impressed me about Bui's. The egg wasn't wet and slipping out, the cheese wasn't gooey and running down the sides, the bagel wasn't hard to chew - just none of that! It was a simplistic and beautifully prepared sandwich, especially considering since there was a crowd of hungover students waiting to get their food as well. Bui's is definitely a good option to consider whether you're hungover or sober, taking a lunch break, or grabbing food to eat while binge watching Netflix,. Quick, cheap, and made with love, the people at Bui's definitely know how to make breakfast sandwiches.
Best Thai food in the Tampa Bay Area. I have had a variety of dishes and was never disappointed. All dishes are made fresh and great.

Disappointing with rather bland food and sauces. They did rerun my meal and we tried again with some appetizers that worked well and had good flavor, but it's just hit-or-miss. I ordered a ginger-beef dish. There was not any ginger flavor at all (heck, not any "flavor" at all) and the "beef" was bleached white. I've been cooking beef for over 40 years, I've never seen beef come out looking like chicken. My wife ordered a sushi roll and said it was okay but not great. She did like her eggplant but found her shrimp to be overcooked.

Tried a few Thai restaurants since moving to Brandon, Florida many years ago and this place is by far the best! The décor is really nice and the staff is very friendly. I usually get take-out and have never been disappointed. Give it a try!

Went here for lunch with a friend, it was pretty tasty. I had the pad thai and he had the duck curry dish. I think they forgot about our appetizers, they arrived during our lunch. The waiter was super busy, he was the only one working and the place was busy. They need to have another server on staff, it would have been a better experience.

I had such high hopes for this restaurant based on the amazing reviews. Don't get me wrong, my meal was good, but I'm not sure I could give it 5 stars or say it's the best Thai food in Edmonton. The restaurant itself is pretty nondescript from the outside. It's on a great street, though! There is parking behind the restaurant off the alley, with a back entrance which is convenient and much appreciated as the temperature drops (and drops and drops).
