Inside, the decor is your typical Canadian-Asian style. The tables are nicely spread apart so you are able to enjoy your meal and conversation without your neighbour too close. I had the Penang curry, which really was good. However, it's no better than most places I've been, and doesn't rank #1 for me in Edmonton. My dining partner had a fried chicken dish, which he described as bland. It was probably just a poor choice in a restaurant with such a wide variety of curries and rice dishes. I can't complain about the service or the prices. Overall, the meal was good, but not great. I'd go back because it's close to home and there are many more dishes to try. Perhaps my fellow Yelpers just set my expectations too high!

Love! Love! Love Sis. Muhammad's Kitchen! The food is excellent and I am always very satisfied with any meal that I get. My favorite is the fish hoagie. The hoagie is super big and enough for 2 people to share. This spot is very popular so sometimes the wait is long, but it is always well worth the wait. My advice to people is order your food in advance of your hungry point. If you order when you're hungry then you may have an issue.... LOL! Great food! Keep up the good work. Im definitely a fan:)

I always pass by this place, but I finally was able to try this last week. I have been to their Springfield and Bryn Mawr locations. I enjoyed the flavours from these 2 locations, usually a bit more in price range compared to South Philly, but when you are running errands in the suburbs and craving Vietnamese food Pho Street is a great option. The 21st street location is also convenient if you cannot get yourself to South Philly. Unlike the suburban locations this 21st location follows Honeygrow and other modern eateries - using smart screens to order and pay for the food. I don't know how others feel about Pho Street's screen, but I personally felt it was a bit difficult to maneuver compared to my experiences at Honeygrow and other places. It also had difficulty processing my credit card so I had to manually punch in the numbers. The food came out pretty fast, and the flavours were also good. I like the fact that you can customize the ingredients for your dish. Aside from the screen, I was turned off by the dirty tables, and tray rack area where you are supposed to take your tray when you are finished (like IKEA). When I sat down to eat the rack was full, but it wasn't bad. By the time I was done it was overflowing... The table I sat had built in hot sauce where I had to rub really hard with a baby wipe to clean. The tray rack area was a mess, and since the rack was not cleared people just put the trays on a counter where the screens were (to order and pay). There were only few tables occupied so they weren't that busy to wipe the tables and clear the rack. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt, so I probably will go back again and see what happens.

Tried this place twice before. Wanted to like it since it's so close to home. However the fish options are mostly frozen or low cost options. For example tilapia,farm raised salmon, butterfish, and cod are their main entrees. Their food is overpriced and tasteless. Their wait staff is also mixed. Some are really helpful and others are pushing all the options like " you want bottled water, and wheat garlic bread" which are all up charges. Stay away from this pathetic attempt at a gourmet restaurant.

As a restaurant who serves pho I would've expected them to have a good supply of sprouts but nope. They were completely out which I don't understand; they're one of the very few items to put in your pho. Disappointed. Also the basil and cilantro they were able to give me were brown and not fresh.

Sooo glad they are back! The gyro special is a phenomenal bundle of flavors and an amazing deal. Soft shell can barely hold the nearly 3lbs of meat, veggies, & sauce that makes up their gyro. The meat is tender and eases you into a symphony of flavors....savory then spicy with a finale that is truly satisfying. 3 minor changes since they reopened that haven't added to their appeal: 1. The fries are mediocre but the spice they sprinkle on them amps up the taste buds. However, the level of grease and spices are not consistent. 2. The gyro special used to include an ample amount of fresh tomatoes. Now you are lucky if you get 2 slivers...a result of the cost of food? 3. The new paint color leaves the room drab and dingy looking. I thought their previous color (a blend between a dark rust and crimson) was warm and matched the table cloths very well. These aren't make or break for me. I will be back...just maybe for a to-go order with rice instead.
Never disappointed! Wonderful service, great flavorful Thai food and family owned. They have a fantastic selection and variety of foods. You leave satisfied, happy and with a belly full of goodness.

True to their name, this place is definitely a deli. Ordered banh mi thit (vietnamese grilled sandwich), everything was made right in front of you - fresh and fast. Still hungry, I ordered pho tai. Like I said before, this place is true to its name - K&T DELI. The pho tai were unflavored even when adding hoisin sauce & thai basil leaves into the pho broth mixture. Friendly services by the cooks. Flat screen tv hung in the corner, so you can catch a glimpse of Spongebob or some sort of Disney shows in the background - depending on the time of the day. Vietnamese sandwiches are great & cheap for students or workers during lunch break. Definitely must come back again.

Visited Avola last evening for dinner with Mark Smith. I really enjoyed the cheese plate and shrimp cocktail. Chrissy, our server, was excellent. Very knowledgeable about the menu, made recommendations, and overall extremely pleasant. I tried some of the corn risotto which was outstanding. I could have eaten that for my meal alone. Dessert was a deconstructed cannoli which was excellent. Anthony, one of the owners, visited our table a few times and we had a great conversation. I highly recommend Avola. Try this beautiful new restaurant and wonderful food. Ginny Hamilton

On Monday, November 3rd, 2014, my coworkers and I had lunch at Zoe's Kitchen in Collegeville, Pennsylvania. This was my second time eating here. I had mixed reactions to the food the first time, but figured I would give it a second chance. I completely regret my decision to return. I ordered the "pick two" option, and got half of a Turkey Sandwich and the Tomato Bisque. I ordered a Limeade as my beverage. The amount of food I received, compared with the price paid, was pretty underwhelming... but that is the least of my worries. Two of my coworkers also ordered the Tomato Bisque. Within 15 minutes of returning from our lunch break, we all began to feel sick. From around 3pm Monday, until 9pm Tuesday, I was violently ill with food poisoning. I even missed work on Wednesday, as a result of the pain that my body was in, and due to lack of sleep on Monday and Tuesday night. I can't help but notice how Zoe's Kitchen markets themselves as using only the freshest ingredients. Now with that being said, I think they either need to double-check on their fresh ingredients, or on the practices of their employees. Perhaps the bisque had been sitting out for too long, at an incorrect temperature...or maybe it had gone bad before it was even cooked (heated up). Either way, there is no excuse for this and I will NOT be returning. Sorry Zoe's Kitchen. Your employees are friendly and I'll never complain about the service I received...but some changes need to be made on quality control. I've never been this sick with food poisoning in my life, especially from a restaurant that prides itself on freshness and healthy cuisine. ***UPDATE - AS OF 4/7/15*** I was contacted by a Zoe's Kitchen representative and interviewed over the phone, regarding my not so pleasant experience at their restaurant. I was not only promised that the location would be looked into, for obvious reasons... but I was also promised a gift card, as an incentive to give Zoe's Kitchen one more try. Well, it's been nearly 5 months, and still no gift card. I'm starting to think this place isn't all it's cracked up to be. ***UPDATE - AS OF 9/2/15*** Still waiting on that gift card... ***UPDATE - AS OF 9/2/15*** Still waiting. In five week it'll be ONE FULL YEAR since my horrible experience at this establishment. Here's to hoping they haven't poisoned anyone else!

business_name: New South Ocean Chinese & Japanese Restaurant
text: Love the sushi here. Fast friendly service!
This place is relatively new, so I stopped in to try. I have been back Three times since. Good prices, wonderful friendly service, and great Pho will have me returning often.

I was here on 2/9/13 while in town for a business trip. I got the lemongrass chicken, but had to eat it in the car because of time constraints. The restaurant was empty, but this was after Nemo rolled through New England, so I think most people in the region were sluggish this weekend. I ordered and it was ready in 10 min. The atmosphere of the restaurant was very nice and I wish I could have eaten in. Chicken was silky, noodles were delicious. Overally, a decent meal for a decent price. I don't know why people are dinging the place on the price when there are literally 12 major country clubs in a 15 mile radius - I mean it, I was at 6 of them on my trip. Given the demographic of the region, they are very reasonable, even on a Saturday when I couldn't take advantage of their weekday lunch specials. I'd say, if you're in the area, give them a chance...

I went to Zagol for the first time for a fundraiser. I've never had Ethiopian food before, and the only thing I'd heard was that they don't have silverware, so I prepped by wearing something I didn't mind spilling on. Zagol is on 4th Street, which usually freaks me out, but it's located on the corner in a small strip mall and felt pretty safe. We received a very friendly greeting by the owner, who explained the menu to us and what she recommended. I ordered the Kik Alicha, which is vegetarian. At the risk of sounding ignorant, the food reminded me very much of Indian curry, which I love. My dish was mild, but the dish my husband ordered was pretty spicy, so if you're wary of burning your tongue, you may want to ask how hot your dish will be. The food was served with Injera, which is a spongy flatbread that tasted a bit like sourdough. The food went perfectly with the Ethiopian beer that I ordered. Everyone in the restaurant seemed to be enjoying themselves, and it was a very friendly, welcoming environment. Prices were great for the amount of food, and I can't wait to bring people by for the unique dining experience.

I am used to good Indian food as I am english... and that is what er like. I was so happy when Amber Indian opened as the food is really good. If you don't know Indiana food then go for buffet lunch to work out what you like. I eat here often and am never disappointed!

We are regulars at Ekta on weekends buffet..We love their food.We find their chef as the best of Indian cuisine ever,and we tried a lot:,his touch is superb in any dish he makes. The only down side on the buffet is their deserts.We miss Gulab Jamoon,that they make only rarely. On the weekend buffet the desert selection is poor and disappointing. Other then that its fantastic.

The service is lacking. My boyfriend and I both ordered pho and the waiter never brought out the garnish, which is essential to eating pho. We had to ask for it after he brought it the pho. The broth was very simple and lacked flavor. Perhaps it needed to simmer longer? Or needed more spices? We also ordered the pork and crab egg rolls which didn't taste like anything special. You actually can't even tell that there's crab in there so I wouldn't both getting it.

This place is fantastic. Very friendly local feel. The menu always offers great specials, the Brussel sprouts for dinner are amazing. For breakfast they always have great specials. The chef is very talented.

Always good food and friendly staff. Love the burgers and breakfast is always a great weekend stop. Try the Waldorf sandwich which is one of the fav's they make. It can be busy someone's during breakfast hours.
I do takeout here all the time. I love their spring rolls and snow rolls. The pad thai is good but not very exciting. Everything I've had is good. The service is quick and the staff is very pleasant.

I have a meeting in WC and searched this pho by yelp,. Totally disappointed I live in center city and so many pho are better than this one! I ordered a bamboo pho which cost me 10 bucks and only 3 slice of beef and small bowl of noodle. I have been to more than 10 different pho resturants and this with the highest price lowest quality. I went there noon time 1200 and I am the only customer... I dont know why the other people gave they 4-5 stars but I am really not recommed

Wandered in here while waitng for a show at The Cannery Ballroom and was 100% pleasantly surprised. Juan was so nice and throughly explained the traditional Puerto Rican fare on the menu. I decided on his recommended Carne Frites with fomongo. Delish. Drinks were well balanced and...we just happened to be there for happy hour. A must-eat stop in Nashville.

If I could give Phan and her "Egg Roll King", 6, 10, or a million stars, I would. Walking into Washington Square Mall is not for the faint-hearted, but the smells and smiles of Phan's Kitchen can be experienced right around the corner of the front entrance. As I sat down to wait for my pork egg roll, green curry and chicken fried rice (choices based on Yelp suggestions), Phan came from the back and started preparing the food right in front of me. She warmly engaged in conversation and noted she had never seen me in there before, which I appreciated as she made me feel welcomed and that she would tend my aching hunger. While her adorableness in her apron may be deceiving, she has just given me the greatest gift I've gotten since moving to the East side. Comfort food-with the love of a hard-working woman infused in every bite. I literally cannot stop eating, like I took a break to write this so I could slow down because I was shoveling the chicken fried rice in my mouth at the speed of light. Hands down, worth every penny and the adventure into the mall. This woman makes AMAZING food.

Hey Yelp, where is the negative zero?! I came here in 2010 (kind of like last min thing). Viet Pho- You got to be kidding me!?! Pho here is nasty! NOTHING like Pho! Are these people crazy!?!? Gross and overpriced. And their service is slow and the menu sucks! For those of you who gave good star rating... you must not know what you're eating or how good food taste like! Their sign outside is a lie - "Reno's Best Pho".. Haha you a joke.. I literally almost choked laughing while I was driving back to Cali. I have been meaning to post this review. Run far away!

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: Delicious food! Great service! The owner took the time to explain I could have any combination of meat and preparation and heat that I wanted. Organic all-fresh ingredients. Everything made to order. I will definitely be back!

I've been to Morocco a few times: lived Meknes for 7 weeks, and in Fez for month, and travelled all over. I've enjoyed my fair share of Moroccan cuisine in American and abroad, and even threw a few Moroccan themed parties. I have to say that this is some great stuff. This restaurant offers authentic Moroccan food, the kind you will in local food stands or small shops. Most Moroccan restaurants in America are like Disneyland versions of Moroccan food, complete with Belly dancers, bland versions of couscous, and a mixture of bad french food. But Marrakesh gives you the real deal. And you can tell it is good because there are always Moroccans stopping in to get a taste of home. The other major plus for us Maghribiphiles (Morocco lovers) is that we can eat some of the stuff we have to avoid while abroad in order to avoid that nasty travelers' sickness. That means lettuce on my sandwiches and the salads are no problem! The lamb tagine with prunes was absolutely dynamite. The chicken tagine was wonderful, crisp with light notes of citris from the preserved lemons and green olives. I love Moroccan olives and they serve both green and the famous black olives. I also love the sandwiches: Moroccan style shawarma and the delicious ketban sandwiches (lamb marinated overnight). Their eggplant is also super tasty. The owner is super friendly, also another reminder of Morocco's famous hospitality. The restaurant serves zabihah meat and keeps the environment halal. With no alcohol, it is an ideal environment for us teetotalers.

I'm from San Diego and there is a place called Sipz, a Vietnamese restaurant, that serves faux meat in their dishes in addition to the meat options. It is amazing food and the service is excellent. Also, their boba drinks come in two options: tea or blended ice. The drinks are offered in numerous flavors (watermelon, strawberry, lychee, etc) is also great. As a vegetarian, having options available for me is important. Comparatively, this place, which serves a very limited drink menu (and flavor options) and only has a limited vegetarian menu (I was offered tofu that is cooked in meat sauce, a tofu sandwich, or tofu with vermicelli), is underwhelming. Goleta is a college town just as San Diego. I am disappointed with the lack of vegetarian options available here. The one redeeming quality was the service. It was fantastic! I gave the one star for the service (although I had to wait 15 minutes for them to cook tofu and veggies).

What a nice surprise! The food is high quality, the sushi was outstanding! If this wasn't such a well kept secret one would never find a seat. I can hardly believe I was fortunate enough to find this quality restaraunt and this level of genuine service in a strip center off the beaten path outside of a major metro area or business district. Go here!

Staple for me over the last 4 years. Sandwiches are fantastic with the sourced baguettes they use. Always am happy with the quantity/quality balance. Wish they'd put the pitchers of water back out at lunch!

It's a small place but they have big flavor. Another long standing neighborhood business. When we are craving thai flavors ...we will most always order from Siam's. I just love how fresh everything is ...no matter what day or time you order. So consistent in service and product. My Son used to stop by after school with a school mate. They would order the spring roll.

Had beef with broccoli. Steamed rice was good. Wonton soup had tons of pepper. I didn't care for the onions in the beef and broccoli and the B&B was more like soup. Not much flavor at all. Came in at dinner time. Only two people dining were employees. Not surprised. When I noticed that, I really should've turned around and left.

Just stopped there for dinner tonight. Not really impressed. I got the steak shawarma rice bowl. Food wasn't even warm and wasn't especially tasty either. Took a long time to get through the line even though they weren't really busy. The soda tastes very distinctly of tap water, which wasn't pleasant. The fries were good since they came right out of the fryer. Maybe they're still getting up to speed, so I'l probably try once more before I write it off. Staff is friendly.
This is probably my favorite spot to get a sandwich. They are so bright, fresh, and the bread is crispy! Yum!

Had some of the best potstickers here I have ever had, including those from Chinatown in Las Vegas. My wife loved her Pho, and the Mongolian Beef was a hit with my 4 year old son. My Daughter loved the Orange Chicken and the spring rolls. Their peanut sauce is great.

I wasn't sure whether to give Mojito's 3 or 4 stars. I wanted to love it a lot more than I did, I guess and the service needs work. The food is good. My favorite thing is what I had last time, the appetizer of scallops on a bed of grits. The grits were pretty amazing and I am a fool for grits. Nothing else truly knocked my socks off on the couple of visits I have made to this establishment but it has all been nice. I would kind of like to try their brunch. Service can be a bit of a problem here, hence deduction of stars. I want to make it clear that the waitress on my last visit was good and actually quite sweet. The hostess, however...She seats us and my mother asks her for iced tea. She snaps, "I'm your hostess, not your waitress" at my mother. Not cool. A proper response would have been, "I'll get a server for you," in a nice tone of voice. Another reviewer mentioned "bad vibes" and it is true that there is not a real happy vibe from the waitstaff. Still, I give three stars for the patio, the location, and the food. Still, that hostess bothered me.

Cute little Thai restaurant in downtown Narberth. Dimly lit, cute decor. A good "first date" restaurant. However, prices are very expensive here for Thai: $18.95 or something for any of the dishes which contained shrimp or fish. Our dinner was $39 + tip for one order of shrimp dumplings, tofu/veggie pad thai, and tofu green curry (1 appetizer and 2 lower priced entrees since they contained tofu). Zero beverages or desserts. On the west coast this would have cost no more than $25 max (probably with tip!) and the portions would have been by far larger. I'm used to stellar Thai and dishes that contain shrimp rarely exceeding $13 or $14. The green curry was served on a flat plate rather than in a traditional bowl with a tiny (and COLD) ice cream scoop size dollop of white rice. I put my hand on the rice - it wasn't even room temperature - it was COLD. There wasn't enough rice to catch up all the curry and as they don't provide spoons, it was impossible to get to everything. My curry wasn't a traditional green curry either. It had "steamed" veggies tossed into a green curry base - not cooked in the curry as is traditionally done. My partner said his shrimp dumplings weren't anything great and that his pad thai scored a 5 out of 10 on his own personal scale. It's very quiet in this restaurant and they pipe in music from the back, leaving the front area very sound-free. They were playing big band music tonight - an odd choice for a Thai restaurant, though it might have been their idea of appropriate holiday music (today's the day after Christmas). Although they COULD accommodate larger groups by putting together tables, it wouldn't be the right environ. This place is more romantic and quiet than upbeat. Service was very friendly and they did well on their "attentiveness", which brought this up from the 2 stars I would have given them.
We ordered delivery, the food was just terrible. My Pad Thai was gluggy, yet dry. Every dish we ordered was similarly dismal. We will never order here again.

Yes yes yess!!!! This place is great.. Spring rolls large and tasty but most important the Pho!! This broth is amazing and tasty big chunks of beef... And the ice coffee was strong and sweet the perfect finish!!! I'll be back for sure
Fantastic in every way .... Wonderful food and the atmosphere is like a palace . Eat here you will be so happy you did . Love this restaurant !!!

This is absolutely my favorite place. I had been to the one in Scottsdale and nearly died when I found out they opened in Tucson. Where to start. The restaurant itself is beautiful. Each meal starts with a basket of hot flat bread and a plate of herbs and butter. If you look to the corner of the main dining area you can see the bread oven where the flatbread is made all evening. There are so many good choices and our server Jessica helped us pick some great dishes. Service was excellent and the food is just amazing. I had the chicken Shish with zereskh polo...if you've never had any Persian rice dishes, they are all worth trying. This one is basmati rice with saffron and barberries. Barberries have a hint of sweet and a tang that might be something like a sour cherry and dried cranberry taste. Every time I eat here I wonder if the food is really as good as I remember and it always is even better. Also...the portions are quite generous so come hungry, be excited to take food home, or in my case, also place a massive to-go order for all the sad people you left at home.

Absolutely Horrible! The server had zero clue about any items on the menu, he negated the fact I have a severe onion allergy. I told him when he delivered it and said oh there is just a whole onion on the plate for flavor, you don't actually eat it and then walked away We will never be back. Stick to PF Chang's or any sushi place

We stopped in for a late lunch and are already looking forward to a return visit. I wasn't sure what to expect, but there were lots of very intriguing options on the menu. I went with The Tofu and Eggplant with rice, my husband went with the lobster Banh Mi. Both dishes were very good. I was actually expecting a rice bowl, but my meal came with the lightly grilled tofu and tender eggplant and onion on a bed of lettuce with a generous scoop of rice on the side (they were out of brown rice so I had to settle for white). The sauce was piquant and just a hint of heat and the dish was piping hot when it was served. The lobster Banhmi was also good. The lobster was just a little bit "fishy" but the flavor was sweet and spicy, with the spicy having a 30 minute after burn. The French bread was toasted making it super crusty. The filling was drippy, but tasty. The overall experience to the Lobster Bahn Mi was very satisfying. Service was almost too attentive, but they weren't very busy and I think there were more staff than patrons. We were seated, orders taken, and food provided in good fashion. The space looks very nice and seems a lot more open then its previous iterations. I really like the way they incorporated the awkward pole in the middle of the bar area into the decor. The took out the high-top table, and put in a small water feature with bamboo and pants. The metal pole is panted to match the bamboo. It works and makes what is a bit of an awkward architectural feature work. I am looking forward to coming back and trying more items on the menu.

We went to get pho to go and some egg rolls. 4 small egg rolls were $6.50. The beef pho is 8.50. We got 4 small pieces of beef in the order of pho. They only offer one size! The taste is great but for $8.50 I expect more.

This place is so good I try to sneak it in every time I'm in St. Louis. Service is quick & friendly and the food is great every time! They close for a few hours midday so you have to plan around that but it's worth your time. Love love love their pad see ew, chicken satay, summer rolls, various hot teas, pad whun sen, & curry. There are also lots of vegetarian options. Give 'em a try!
Great tasting. Good size portions Great prices. I had the Chicken Vindaloo with Garlic Naan bread. Total was $16 and that's for dinner pricing!

Absolutely awful food. The spicy chicken was bland and gooey. The orange peel beef was also flavorless. The chicken in the lettuce wraps may have come from Popeyes though theirs might actually be better. We did have good service.
Rare Vietnamese place in Santa Barbara that is good for vegetarians. The vegetarian pho was great! Thanks!

Great place for dinner. We started with the seared tuna and finished with the Korean wings. Amazing selection of food. Nice vibe very unassuming place, can't wait till they start opening for lunch. Staff was fantastic and decor matched.

I went here today for luch and the gyro was wonderful. Tender meat with a very good spicey sause. It was excellent and only $5 bucks. I'm only giving 4 stars because of the interior. I ate there and won't do that again. Smells like amonia and the carpet was so dirty. But don't let that stop you because the gyro was really a treat.

This place hits the spot. The pho broth reminds me of the pho I had as a child. The aroma and the beefy dark broth reminded me that some chefs are still keeping pho authentic and not clear and bland like other joints. I have had pho in Socal, Sacramento, and the Bay. I have to say this place is on the top of other pho joints I will go out of my way to eat at. The only part of the pho missing is the variety of meats. I am a combination type of guy. They are missing some of the tendon, tripe, and other stuff but they made it up with the massive amount of meatballs, steak, and brisket in the xl pho to satisfy my protein needs. Top place in reno to get pho. The customer service was top notch from any pho places I have been at.

I have dieing to try Pho for a long time and I herd this place was in the top 5. I didn't know what to expect or how it was supposed to taste but I did not like it. It was bland and needed something. I'm not sure what though lol I also had 2 egg rolls and they were good and crispy. My glass of lemonade tasted like powdered lemonade that someone squeezed a lemon into for the pulp. I would try pho again but doubt I will return to this place.

After looking at the ratings on Yelp and Google, I decided to visit Chaat and chai. The only positive about this place was the decor. The food was horrible. Had ordered bhel puri, samosa chat, Dhaba chicken and kadai paneer. 1. The sauce in the bhel tasted funny. 2. The samosa chat was just horrible, took one bite and gave up on it. 3. The dhaba chicken had no flavor/spice whatsoever . (Turmeric is not a flavouring ingredient. It is primarily used to give color to the food ! ). 4. The paneer was undercooked and had no flavor what so ever. I would not recommend visiting this place. EVER!

My first experience here (for lunch) was shortly after they opened and was less than satisfactory. Food took forever to arrive and was cold. Greg the owner reached out to me directly to apologize and make things right. I finally got a chance to give Suraya another shot and I was blown away. Service was spot on- attentive yet not overbearing. Timing was perfect and nothing was rushed. Atmosphere was A+, food was A++ Everything we ordered was delish and flavorful. I could eat here everyday and be a happy camper. Just absolutely spot on across the board. Truly the best dining experience I have had in a while. Dessert was incredible to boot! Ill be back to eat my way through this menu!

For a Vietnamese restaurant the price are ridiculously high. Place is not fancy with mixed decorations inside and the quality and freshness of the food and ingredients are not good for the price they charge. Also didn't like how they do not have a small or medium size pho but charging customer $9 for a very large bowl of pho which I can't finish and the food goes to waste. The condiments to put in the pho also looks like they been rewash, reuse from past customers who didn't use all their condiments and serve it to the next customer. But overall the broth of the pho is amazing. Authentic. I'll be back if the price on the food drop a little.

We thought we'd give this restaurant a try. My family likes Thai food and we wanted to find a place closer to us. My husband and I ordered the Pad Chicken Garlic, our son ordered the Orange Chicken. They both tasted good. However our they could've added more chicken. There was a ton of sauce but the portion size for Dinner could've been more. Especially if your paying $10.99. I've been to other places where the portion size and taste was worth the price.

Ordered the beef pho!!! I believe it's the only option for pho. Authentic & very tasty! Our food came out within a few minutes. It was around $8 for a bowl, great price. Next time I come back, I want a banh mi!
Delicious curry pinneaple and very friendly people. best thai in santa barbara

I came to Zagol for the first time for a themed dinner with my African literature class at the university, and I fell in love. I was only somewhat familiar with the flavors of Ethiopian food, but Zagol set me on the right path to a true appreciation. The food is primarily served on round pieces of spongy, lemony bread, which you then tear off and use to pinch up the food you are going to eat. I would recommend a medium-bodied beer to combat some of the spicier dishes, but the food is amazing by itself too.

For starters we had spring roll shrimp and pork. It was really good. It comes with a sauce that makes it taste extra nice. We ordered another two right after. We had the Vermicelli Grilled Pork and the Chicken Soup for our entrees. The place is fairly cheap but still good. Comfort food slash hangover food- so many options. The staff is friendly and it's really clean inside. Ask about the two pound noodle/meat challenge

Service was slow even though we were one of 2 parties eating in the restaurant, and the staff was constantly assembling take out orders, but they did apologize and said they were short-staffed that day. My husband grew up in Burma so we were excited to try out this new option for Burmese food in the city. The thai and Malaysian menus looked very good but we only ordered off the Burmese menu. My friend who is not vegetarian ordered the Mohinga which he really enjoyed. We ordered 2 vegetarian dishes on the Burmese menu which were not really authentic Burmese dishes and tasted like lo mein and regular kung pao tofu, although they were good. The tea leaf salad and roti canai appetizers were good but the roti canai curry could have used a bit more flavor and spice. Overall we were disappointed with the lack of authentic Burmese dishes, even though what we got was good.

Ordered in when attending my dad's graduation in Trenton. An unexpected find in Trenton! Let me tell you about the Jerk Chicken, Curry Goat, and Hummingbird salad. The jerk chicken was perfectly seasoned (a touch spicy which I love) and tender. It was refreshing not to have the jerk chicken swimming in jerk sauce too, but covered in a delicious seasoning rub that turned into a thin paste. Also, they give you steamed cabbage and rice and peas. Nothing incredibly special, but a nice compliment to the entree. Rarely having had Caribbean before, I was blown away by the hummingbird salad, which is sort of similar to coleslaw, but 100x better. I took it to go so I didn't have it made fresh, but it still was excellent. The curry goat was amazing as well, but a bit heavy on the sauce, but I'm not heavy on sauces. The spice profile of the dish was heavy on cumin and tumeric, but also some hints of cayenne. The only downside was the location in Trenton, which is quite abandoned even in the middle of the day. However, the Hummingbird Restaurant will remain in the top 5 places Caribbean places I've frequented.

We loved our experience at Kebab Erbil! The staff were so nice and attentive, and the food was amazing! Our favorite was the Kubah, but we like everything we had there! And they had the best baklava of anywhere! We highly recommend this hidden gem!
New to the area and wanted to find a local Thai restaurant, this place did not disappoint! Beyond friendly staff, amazing food, and great pricing. We will definitely be back!

Remedy is primarily known as a hangout for students, activists, and artistic types. The atmosphere is thick with culture and creativity, and the art on the walls rotates on a regular basis. A lot of people come here for the chai, which is delicious and frothy. The food, which mostly consists of Indian and Pakistani cuisine, is also abundantly enjoyed. My favourite is the palak paneer, a thick blend of spinach, potato, and spices topped with cubes of cheese. The chai and samosas are a perfect snack, although the dipping sauce is more reminiscent of a syrup than chutney which is traditionally served with this kind of food. Remedy also serves coffee, beer, and a host of other cold and hot beverages. There is free WiFi for customers, and lots of comfy chairs and couches upon which to relax.

Great little restaurant in Drexel line! 9.95 lunch buffet and has all of the favorites. As per usual palak paneer is amazing. They also provide naan even for the buffet customers. Staff is friendly and quick to clear the dirty dishes and fill the buffet. Not that this really throws me off, but at least one server had absolutely no idea what we were saying. Typically I am understanding but when you are in the service industry and working at a place where people might ask you a question or two you should at least understand what we are asking. Another downer: the question we were asking was about whether we could use our groupon. Waiter one says yes and nods his head. Waiter two who speaks English comes back after our food was ordered and check was handed back to him to let us know that we can't use it. He was also pretty rude.

business_name: Taj Mahal Homestyle Indian & Pakistani Cuisine
text: we were passing through boise and saw the neon signs on the building. we looked at the japanese menu and of course it is a steak house...we are vegan. then we decided to try the taj mahal, even though we have amazing indian in boulder, and so it wasn't really a treat. well, we were wrong! this place was great... from the moment we walked in, we were greeted warmly. everyone who worked there, and the owner, were super friendly and helpful. not only are they vegan friendly, they have VEGAN dishes listed on their menu!!! you're just never sure what dishes they might sneak a little cream in, so it was a nice surprise to see this. we ordered the onion baji. it was good but doesn't quite compare with our own bombay bistro who makes the best baji in the world. so i am probably just too spoiled. the mint chutney was really awesome. for dinner, we got banghan barta (very rarely found in vegan form), and spinach sabzi daal. YUMMMMM!!! it has spice, and it is vegan, and it is yummy delicious. the rice was amazingly tasty as well. i think they listened to these reviews, because there is no way i would ever say they did not use enough spice. very very tasty! to top it off, they had mango juice for junior, and a surprisingly diverse list of belgian and specialty beers! so we got indian food and chimay beer...what a combo! we will definitely come back next time!!!

I literally live three blocks away from Blue Plate but have never tried it. I was very happy with everything! The server Erica was knowledgeable and very friendly! The food was delicious and the ingredients are found locally....very good, I will be back.
Good food, friendly staff. We had the pineapple curry, pepper steak, Thai fried rice and dumplings. The steamed dumplings were the best we've tried. Everything was good.

Tangelo's Grille Tangelo's is a small Cuban centric restaurant with a sidewalk patio in beautiful downtown Gulfport, Florida, reviewed on Wine Dine And Play in August 2018. Gulfport is a town filled with charm known most for the end of summer GeckoFest, farmers markets, little shops, the beach bazaar, and little restaurants like Tangelo's Grill. We dined for brunch enjoying a mimosa flight, bloody mary with fried jalapeno popper garnish, a Huevos Espinacas, classic Latin take on eggs and spinach, scrambled, then mixed with the baby spinach, parmesan cheese as well as an island custard french toast with three toppings. You can read the full review on Wine Dine And Play...

This place is pretty new, which is why I guess it was really empty both times I went. It was perfect though. My friend and I talked to the owner guy for a while. These are the nicest people ever! The first time we went, we thoroughly enjoyed the hookah. I also got a falafel sandwich that was amazing and fresh! The second time we went, we thoroughly enjoyed the hookah, and the owner guy brought out some mint tea for us on the house! The staff made sure our coal was burning evening and didn't get too ashy. The slightest movement to signify that I was done with my food, the guy was there to bus it. I live all the way in Manayunk right now, but I would go back to that place. I've been to two hookah lounges so far, and this one has been the most friendly and intimate.

As an guy of North Indian/Punjabi extraction, I have to say that the standard for "good North Indian" fare is different for me as it is for others. That said, I think Amber is the best choice for Indian food in Indy simply because they don't overdo it with dollops of grease and butter in their food among other reasons. Although I like food spicier than the average Midwesterner, I don't like it flaming hot either (not like other Indian people) and that's why I think Amber reasonably spices the dishes: you won't be breathing fire and slaking your thirst with gallons of water as with your prototypical Indian place. The naan is nice and chewy, as it should be, and all the curries are fairly authentic I have to say. The tandoori chicken is my favorite in Indy and is a must-have. As I said before: they don't load it up with grease and you won't see it pooling on top of the saag or the chana masala as with other places. This place won't punish your digestive tract as a result. For nine bucks, the lunch buffet is a good deal and the variety of veg and non-veg stuff is great bang for your buck. The ambiance is just like a standard Indian place in a strip mall, nothing special but nothing that takes away from the experience. I would definitely go to this place over Shalimar or India Palace or India Garden anyday!

Great service, but fast food south Indian food is not for me! Reminded me of Chipotle in the way it was set up. I went toward the close of the day, so it was a little rough. Older dried out rice, and there was a thin film over all the sauces, as it looks like they stood stagnant for a while. I gave it a shot though! It was flavorful, but the samosa I ordered(sitting under the hot lamp) had the texture as if it was sitting under that same hot lamp for 3 days. They should implement some sort of "samosa'' rule, and swap them bad boys out every 29 minutes or so......just my thoughts! I would never go again.

Recently ordered take out from here and food was excellent overall. I ordered the Chicken Sa-Te and the Eggplant Tempura, both were very good and lots of flavor. Also ordered the Coconut soup and it was OK but I have had better, it was devoid of flavor and tasted a bit over salted. The Pad Thai and Pineapple Fried Rice were excellent and I would order again. I haven't had a lot of experiences with Thai cuisine but this experience very good and I would come back again as a sit down experience. As I stated in some of my other reviews, you lose a lot of the taste experience with take-out.

Was in the neighborhood the other day and decided to chomp on some SE asian food. Saw Sky Cafe on yelp and thought I ended up in the wrong place because I was expecting more people considering the amount of praise it gets on Yelp. But it was only us so whatever we already here. Whatever else we ordered wasn't that memorable but holy crap the Wontons are good. It was cooked to perfection, perfectly flavorful and juicy. Much to the dismay of the lady making in the back, we ordered a second order. I don't speak the language but I can sense the annoyance from my second order lol. In any case everything else wasn't memorable but the wontons are definitely something to try if you come upon Sky Cafe, the wontons that came with the platter however didn't taste anywhere as good. My guess is that they have been sitting a while so order a full order.

If you can't get to P.F. Chang's, this is an almost as good option. Style and food are pretty similar, and they are almost there, just not quite. Worth the trip, especially after a movie since it is right across from it.

Mediocre Asian food that is hardly worth the price (or swipe in this case). The sides are by far the worse with the rice pudding simulating the texture of cheese and the flan bitter beyond all. You're better off with fruit cups. The phu and banh mid are passable but hardly filling. Will not return! Two thumbs down! No spicy chilis!
WOW. Great PhoTai...Hot...Great Taste...Not too salty...Tender beef! Can't wait to go back and try some noodle dishes...REAL SOON.

i have reduced my rating by one star now. i was there again, recently and didnt like the owner's customer service. she really needs to learn how to handle the floor. she stays too focussed on some customers and ignores the rest of the dining room. attitude has worsened too. if it werent for good food quality, i would have reduced my rating to 1 star.
LOVE, LOVE , LOVE the black beans burger and fish hoagies. Those are my favorites but every time I go, never have a problem with order. I love this place and it's very clean

Muy Bien!!! I think Alex M's taste buds are dead; plenty of good flavor in the food here. Why would he screw the server on a tip, when a server isn't involved with the food prep??? All of us had well prepared items: chicken mofongo, yellow rice, goat stew, sweet plantains & pastelitos. There's a little wait for the food - but you know it's not all sitting in steam trays. (el mas excelente)

One of my fav Vietnamese place. I brought my family here and they love it especially my dad. The price is reasonable especially in this economy. The service is fast and the staff are friendly. This place is clean compare to most of the pho place around Bella Vista area. I love their spring rolls and their pho. There also have a a great selection for vegetarians. Very important when you have vegetarian friends.

I ordered delivery over the weekend. A mix of sushi and Chinese food. The portions were certainly enough, if not plentiful. However the flavor was some of the most bland Sushi and Chinese food I have ever had. The spider roll had almost no spices to it and the tuna in my tuna roll tasted like it was out for the entire day and had its flavor sucked out. It is also slightly overpriced overall for sushi, especially for it's location. Then the Chinese food. The egg rolls, again, were bland. Huge for sure, but I needed at least 2 duck sauce packets to get some tiny iota of flavor. I ordered the Sesame Chicken, which had authentic sesame seeds, but the flavor is just nothing in comparison to China House. My girlfriend ordered Buttered Shrimp. It was advertised "with vegetables". The only vegetable it came with was a bed of lettuce. It's safe to say, I will pass on Little Kitchen in the future.

We arrived for dinner not knowing what to expect on any level. I was somewhat excited, as I have an affinity for Puerto Rican food. The beer list only features Corona and three heavier American domestic beers, which was a huge surprise and disappointment. Everything went downhill from that point forward. Our corn fritter appetizers arrived still frozen in the center. We sent them back. The second round of corn fritters arrived still frozen in the center. Back they went, and the staff seemed surprised at our displeasure. Given the price point of the meal, I was shocked that Pernil (pork dish) arrived as a few cubs of slow roasted pork a la carte with four pieces of plantain as the supplement. The standard rice and beans that usually accompany a dish like this was absent, creating an underwhelming and stark presentation. Not to mention a meager portion for and $18. My companion had the chicken soup, which was fine, but salty, however, the mofongo con yucca ordered as supplement arrived still icy in the middle. That was the third frozen offense of the evening. Our bill was nearly $60 for what we concluded was the least pleasant and most disappointing dining experience we have had in Nashville. No serious attempt at service recovery, a price point not aligned with the quality of product (grotesquely overpriced), same preparation error repeated multiple times across different dishes, and an indifferent staff. We tend to be low-maintenance customers, so we just noted the awful experience and pledged to never return. Realizing we could have a much more substantive meal both in terms of quality and value proved bothersome for the next day or so. Give Salsa a wide berth. Nashville can do better.

My boyfriend and I went to this restaurant when it had just opened. As someone from Hawaii with parents who were born and raised in Vietnam, I wasn't expecting much. However, I was proven wrong on many levels, and we have consistently gone back again and again for the good service and great food. Now on to the food reviews. I'm going to say right of the back that the pho is not worth driving to Avon for. The soup is surprisingly thin and rather flavorless, other than a slight overwhelming peppery taste, which does not accurately describe a good bowl of pho. I do not believe they use a traditional pho recipe, which is disappointing. This is the only reason this restaurant did not get 5 stars. For a place named after this dish, I expected it to be the star. However, the food gets much better after that. I can't turn down the appetizer, goi cuon, or the spring rolls. I would advise the shrimp and pork ones with a yummy hoisin/peanut dipping sauce. I could never admit this to my mom, but these rolls might best hers! All the other appetizers were also spot on for me. As far as entrees go, the cha gio (egg rolls) and vermicelli noodles is an amazing dish to try. The pork chops are also really good, as it is marinated in a phenomenal sauce. The bahn mi sandwiches are not as great as I'd like, but it's hard to be picky in Indiana. Overall, there is yet a dish (besides the pho) that I have tried that has disappointed me.

Best Bahn Mi sandwich in town! I also enjoy the rice and grilled shrimp dish for lunch & their phó broth is delicious and comforting. I'll be back to try more! Never a wait and easy parking is a Plus. Attentive and friendly staff too.

Green curry didn't taste much like green curry. It's one of my favorite flavors in the world, but it just wasn't there. Almost positive I wasn't brought out a different curry by mistake. Friendly service gets a star, but I'm not sure I'd go back to this place. I'd like to believe there's better Thai food in the city, but I'm not sure where.

As others have mentioned, this place is the "Chipotle" of Indian food. Best way to explain it! I love Indian food and am lucky enough to have some wonderful Indian friends who spoil me regularly with their home-cooked meals.... So, while I was definitely excited by the idea of this modern, Indian-inspired take on one of my favorite cuisines, I was also a teensy bit unsure of what to expect. Same for you? Let me tell you! First, delicious. Know, though, that it is not like going to a traditional Indian restaurant. (Just like Chipotle is not like going to a traditional Mexican restaurant... Make sense?!) Similar to Chipotle, you select from a rice bowl, Naan sandwich or naan pizza. (There are, of course, other options on the menu, but these are the classic line item starters, if you will.) You can then choose from a number of meats, like lamb, tandoori chicken, ginger shrimp, coconut fish, etc. or vegetarian alternatives like masala chickpeas. Then select your curry (tikka masala, leafy green saac curry, vindaloo, korma, etc.). Continue on and select all of your toppings: choose from tomatoes, onions, spicy onions, carrots, cilantro, peppers, corn, cheese, cucumbers, etc. Last but not least, select a sauce! (Mango chutney, yogurt, tamarind chutney, etc.) PERSONALLY, I got the chicken tandoori rice bowl with green saag curry, topped with carrots, onions, tomatoes, and a yogurt-based chutney sauce on the side. Delish! I will say that, although it was technically the least-spicy option, it was still quite spicy for me! (Disclaimer: I have a weak tolerance for spicy. But I will say it was delicious nonetheless!) My boyfriend instead got the chicken tandoori rice bowl with the madras curry (coconut and spices) and tamarind chutney. We both agreed that, while mine was amazing, his might've won the trophy overall! (Albeit significantly more spicy). We both left happy, satisfied, and full :) Atmosphere was casual, bright (lots of windows) and colorful, and also very clean. We went on a Saturday afternoon around 3ish and it wasn't too busy. Seating was comfortable and cute, with booths that look like small carriages, as well as tables with stools. Great lunch spot!
Lots of room here for big parties. Maduros are yummy though a few pieces are undercooked. The service is fast.

I LOVE their food ! Food is always FRESH and HOT ! Everything is delicious. And the staff is very nice ! Beautiful inside to sit and eat. Warm environment and the prices are good ! If you LOVE spanish food, please visit here ! You can call and order for fast pickup !
shopping 52nd street?? stop in for (soya) Roti and a cold Ting! delicious, inexpensive & quick - portions are large enough to share, or save half for a snack later on.

So we came here a few months ago and I've been meaning to write a review but haven't done so and it's long overdue and deserving. Here goes... We came here right before Christmas after having some snow time and when we called and asked how long the wait was, they said it would be 20 to 30 minutes. So we said why not, let's go. When we got to the restaurant, we saw two groups waiting out front and a dining room that was relatively empty. The way the tables were laid out was extremely weird because there were ton of empty spaces. Anyway we finally sat down and we ordered our food. After about ten minutes the waitress comes up and apologizes for the food being slow and it's because a bunch of their staff was out due to the flu. Now I'm a germaphobe and that freaked me out but those people were out so it was cool. Our food started to arrive, appetizers first and then some entrees came but some other entrees were slower than other. Finally another waiter comes and tells us that they are extremely sorry because what actually happened was the entire kitchen walked out and it was only the owner and his aunt cooking hence the delay. They even then brought out free appetizers to keep us happy while we waited for the rest of the entrees. At the end of dinner after all our food came, the waiter came back and then said our meal was comped and they were really sorry for the long delays. Wow, I mean wow. It's Christmas time, the kitchen staff walked out (not sure the reason but the restaurant still needs money along with the friendly staff that stayed behind) and I mean it was above and beyond. It wasn't really that slow (check out my review in Chicago about a restaurant that was half full and took forever to get two pastas). Anyway it was really cool that they took care of our meal and all. Again I don't know why the staff walked out but if you are in town to play at the casinos or in the snow, stop by and support this business.
I love eat oxtail In here It is amazing. I really like Jamaican Food. My husband is Jamaican so I'm very happy that I can come here and get authentic Jamaican food in town!

The fresh spring roll with grilled pork was delicious. I really liked that the peanut dipping sauce that came with it was served warm. So good. For mains, I tried the house special pho and vermicelli bowl. Both were quite good, especially the grilled meat in the vermicelli bowl. However, I found some slices of beef in the pho to be a tad tough. The avocado shake is pretty decent as well. Restaurant looks super clean and service was excellent. I'll be back!

Nice atmosphere, only thing I'm disappointed with was the fact that this is a hookah lounge, and we didn't get serviced through out the night after we got our hookah. I saw the coal guy only service the hookahs on the floor once and he wasn't seen ever again. Didn't bother getting anymore coals or a refill after that.

This place almost begged for a really bad review. It looked as if they weren't even trying. I'm actually sad to be doing this, as I have been to this place for lunch thali and dosas multiple times, and the food is actually good. Anyway this time we went for dinner thali, which is dosas to your liking; I also ordered a parotta with egg curry; and idli sambhar. First of all it took a long long while for any waiter to come to us to take orders. Finally someone did come, we placed the orders, the waiter told me the parotta with egg curry will take time, and I said it was ok. After another long wait we finally got the Thalis, with cold dosas, cold side dishes. We asked them to bring new hot dosas at least, and again after a long wait that came. We all ate one dosa and wanted another one, which never seemed to be coming. There was a point when we were just looking at each other with empty plates and laughing at the hilarious situation. Meanwhile I asked the waiter what's up with my egg curry and parotta, and also the idli sambhar. He made an expression which clearly indicated he had forgotten that order, and went back to the kitchen. Finally he comes back with the idli sambhar, and said the parotta will be more of a wait and to eat this meanwhile. I said ok; the others were informed the dosas they want is out and to order a different one. It was just unbelievable, anyway they did. After a while, when it's almost close to their closing time, he informs me it's too late for the cook to make my dish as it's time to close. I said I ordered it hours before!! What on earth is the deal. Then he mentioned the restaurant has been busy. Other than us, all we could see was 3 other full tables; I know they have opened a branch in downtown and not sure if that's the reason for this disorganized forgetful messy service and pathetic food; but this restaurant is turning out to be an absolute joke. The only thing still to their merit is that the chutney and sambhar still tasted authentic. All the other dishes were average, cold, and the service unbelievably terrible. They will not see me back there unless they make some major changes to this situation!
We just needed a quick place for lunch along the way that offered something out of the norm. Boy, we were treated to some really delicious food! #báhnmi #phoyum

Decent food. I rarely leave negative reviews...however we were disappointed in the kid in the hoody who successfully made my family and I feel like we were imposing for coming in to eat. We love Indian food but will not be back. Two stars because the food was good.

i have been to three p. f. chang's locations - first the one in warrington, then the one in atlantic city, and finally this location for my nineteenth birthday this past saturday. the wait was SO LONG, even though we had a reservation! the people walking in the door were told that there was an hour and a half wait, and that was at six. if you want to eat here, definitely call ahead. our waitress seemed a little rushed, but that was probably because the restaurant was really, really packed. she got all of our orders right and didn't write everything down, she was really excellent. we ordered the tofu lettuce wraps, dynamite shrimp, and salt and pepper calamari for appetizers. all three were delicious. as for entrees, my mother and i both got the oolong marinated sea bass, which is usually about the size of a deck of cards at the other locations. this piece was three times as big! it was delicious and melted in my mouth. for dessert, i ordered the great wall of chocolate, which they brought out with candles for my birthday. overall, a good experience (:

A GREAT addition to the neighborhood. Wonderful ambiance, pastries, tea/coffee and lunch. We sat near the kitchen and I wanted to eat everything that was brought out! I didn't know what most of it was but it all looked delicious! I look very forward to my next visit, and especially to sitting on the patio when it's warmer. Also, there is a free parking lot across the street (Suraya customers only) which is a huge bonus. My only complaint is that they aren't open for dinner.
This is a great lunch spot for me. Every time I come in everyone is nice and the food is good. Service is fast!

The duck was outstanding- cooked perfectly in curry sauce with a side of rice. Service was great even with a table of ten. Most Asian restaurants tend to serve hot green tea with tea bags. Loved that they have individual tea pots that steep green tea leaves.

This place is hands down one of the best spots in the area. My girlfriend and I come at least once a week whether we eat there or get carry out. The food is always on point and consistently delicious. I've tried just about everything on the menu: my go to's are pad kee mao with beef, red thai curry with chicken (TRY IT- some serious healthy comfort food), and chicken fried rice. And I always get an order of the egg rolls for an app. And my girlfriend always gets the vegetarian red Thai curry with a seaweed salad. The owner is very sweet and always a pleasure to see when coming into the restaurant. We hope this place stays around forever! The Luna S girl's comment below should be completely ignored except for the fact that the Korean fried chicken is awesome. If you're going to eat at a restaurant and barely tip 10% when the only thing you order are chicken wings you should probably just get carry out... Luna doesn't deserve Umami's chicken wings.

The staff is friendly and professional! Just Not Impressed especially for the price! I had been here once in fall 2018 and thought it was decent! Pulled out my menu to buy some to take to friend's in VA! I got 2 dozen cheesesteak rolls. Who knew that the price of a dozen went up $5! Now $60.00 for 2 dozen! For that much I expected them to be absolutely delicious and the most amazing tasting! Sorry they were not!
iPho was a nice experience. The ambiance was nice, the service was average and the food was alright. No real complaints from the evening but not the best Pho I've had!

I absolutely love breakfast sandwiches and I came to Bui's today for the first time...despite the fact that I've lived here for four years. Bui's is a great deal. I was a little worried the man taking my order might have missed something (Mr. Bui?), but everything turned out fine. No complaints. Be sure to be clear when ordering! I'll definitely come back here for a quick, filling lunch or breakfast. You can basically order whatever is on the menu in any combination. Really quick and easy!

This one is not as good as the other magasin that closed on magazine. Portions are smaller. Dishes are different. It's still good but not as good as the one that was on Magazine. Oh and I feel like it's more pricey!

I came here looking for a lighter, fresher meal and that's exactly what I got. The chicken orzo soup was so good. It was light and well flavored. The chicken kebab dish was great as well. I could have just done a whole plate of Greek salad Cuz it was so good. I love that they have Greek dressing on the tables, it was delicious! The chicken was good but could have been marinated a little more

The food is decent. The pork bahn mi and chicken bahn mi are both good. The pho broth is a little sweet for my taste. The staff is always attentive. My one complaint about this place is that I'm never quite sure if it'll be open. Hours are posted as 11am - 2am, closed Wednesday. I've tried to go here several times after 10pm and it's always closed. It'd be nice if the hours on the website and posted on the door were accurate. Definitely go for lunch, but don't count on it for a late dinner.

Was craving Thai food on our way home from the Bay Area- stumbled upon this restaurant on yelp. So glad we stopped in, this place has tasty, well priced dishes. Not only is the food delish, but the service is so attentive and they let out a very home-like environment. If we are in the area next time- we will definitely stop by for there flavorful Thai Tea w/Boba!

Walking around the neighborhood on a Monday night may seem a bit scary at first, but once inside this tiny establishment, you will feel warm and safe. The owner is friendly, the menu descriptive, and the food delicious. I loved the lamb ketban: fresh, tender, and flavorfully spiced. The price for a platter which included hummus, veggies, rice was only $11.50. The beef ketban wasn't as tender as the lamb, but also tasty. The beef kefta was also well made.

Delicious food! I was getting poor service and mediocre sandwiches at a nearby sub way. I'm so glad yelp found me this place! Today was my first visit and I got the Cajun shrimp sandwich, YUM. I'm for sure going back. The prices are excellent too.

This was an easy walk to from my aunt's South Street home. It was packed with young families with children and energy for an early Saturday (or Sunday?) morning. After getting in line I quickly noticed that the majority of menu options are carbohydrate rich breads, bagels alongside a robust selection of coffees, teas, etc. I asked about alternative food options, and was offered the option of an omelette with cheese, veggies, meat, or other ingredients. My order of a cheese and spinach omelette arrived piping hot with a side of veggies and bread. Plenty of food especially for my smaller appetite and I fell at ease with the crowded yet comfortable environment as I ate. I was a bit surprised to see a dog made welcome with a family who came in. I'm not allergic or adverse so it didn't bother me. I suggest they make clear other good options, and and update some of the chairs that seem a bit worse for wear. Pricing was decent.

My husband and I got a gift certificate here, so we decided to give it a try. The food had amazing flavor and there was lots of leftovers. Pricing is typical to Indian restaurants. we had the bread basket, pav bahji, vegetable biryani, and karahi paneer. Would definitely try again.
Nan is always fresh. I really like their service. Prompt and clean. Food is good too. Just what I want. I need something quick and it's all there.

5 starts for the pho - I've tried most of the pho available in indy (I can think of 10 places) and this is my favorite. The broth is fantastic even before adding the basil, hot peppers, lime and other herbs (they have one that I've not seen elsewhere and they didn't know the English name). After adding these accoutrements the pho rises to new levels. I've tried a few of the phos and my favorite is simply raw beef (not officially on the menu but they seem happy to provide it). Their goi rolls are right up there with the best in town (only king wok gets a higher rating and that's because I like their sauce better, it's more peanut). I've also sampled the bahn mi. The grilled pork being my favorite. The Bahn mi bread can be hit or miss though. It's been great and it's been so crumbly we wore most of it on our shirts. This is because the bread comes frozen from Chicago. The Mi Xao Don (my wife's favorite dish) is good but doesn't compare to King Wok's. Although the restaurant sometimes smells of disinfectant and the staff doesn't seem to care that they make one of the best meals in town (try complimenting them and you'll see what I mean) this has become one of my go to comfort restaurants in town.

On the west coast there is a restaurant called "El Pollo Loco" which I miss dearly and I found this place on yelp and it looked pretty similar so I decided to give it a try. I visited on 5/22/17 around 6pm and went through the drive thru. $12.82 got me a 1/2 chicken meal and a kid's meal. Their menu is more Caribbean influenced than El Pollo Loco and they have bowls, salads, grilled chicken meals, sandwiches, and wraps. I got the $6.99 1/2 chicken meal which came with two sides and a roll. I chose black beans and white rice for my two sides. The grilled chicken was so good...The skin was crispy and the inside was moist and flavorful. It had a wonderful salty charred flavor! The sides were prepared well and hot and fresh. Ask for their mustard curry sauce...it's creamy and divine for dipping the grilled chicken into. I poured a bunch over my rice....it's so darn good. For my boy I got the $4.99 kid's grilled breast strips meal with came with one side, a roll, a drink, and a guava bar. For his side I chose the corn which was a bit dried out but he's only 2 and could care less. It was a lot of food for the price! The guava bar....oh my goodness that guava bar...I've been dreaming about that guava bar all day. Imagine tart and sweet guava paste sandwiched between two moist pieces of delicious cake....incredible! I took a bite and handed it to my son and when I went to get it back he snatched it away and finished it. I can't wait to go back! I liked it a lot.

The waiter/management was super friendly. The food came out fairly quick but that was about it. The food was sub par and it came out a little more on the cold side. It was probably one of the worst fusion types of foods I've tasted. If you have another choice, take it. It will probably be better than this place. On the up side, their mango lassi was pretty good.

The food is fairly average Indian food - I've had better but its satisfying enough and for the affordable cost, I would recommend it. It would be hard to find a more inexpensive place for this volume of food, even if it isn't the highest quality. I did particularly enjoy the malai kofta, and this is something I'll order the next time I'm craving quick, cheap Indian food. It's buffet style/by the pound so you pay for however much you get. Very limited seating inside, but most people seem to get the food as takeout during lunch breaks and what not.
August Moon is open until 10. They deliver. Their pho is decent. It wouldn't be my first choice, but it was enjoyable.

Ate at the Kabob House last night. The decor was great, the food was excellent (and healthy), and the service was very attentive. I predict great things for this restaurant in its new location. Congratulations and keep the good times coming!
Excellent food and service. It is a decent portion for 1 person. Definitely coming back here to try the rest of the menu.

I have been interested in finding a Thai joint closer than Rouen Thai in Tampa, so Thai Legacy met that mark. I called my order in then went to go pick it up. The woman who owns the restaurant with her husband greeted me. She was so very friendly! I ordered chicken pad thai and mango w/ black sticky rice. I got it home, and was blown away by the first bite of the pad thai. It is truly the best I have ever had. There were SO many flavors and it was so hard to only eat half (needed to save room for the mango)! The mango with black sticky rice was just as I hoped it would be, fantastic. FFWD to the next day, I reheated my leftover pad thai on the stove top, it was just as amazing as the day before. To say I have been telling my other local thai-loving friends about this place is an understatement! I can't wait to go back.

The first time I ate here I wasn't thrilled. I decided to try it again tonight. I ordered the Tom yum soup and chicken pad Thai (I asked for this to be spicy). Everyone who I encountered while picking up my food was friendly and helpful. The soup was delicious. I got a small but it was plenty for 2 people. There were 3 big shrimp in it, and the broth was super flavorful. The pad Thai was wonderful. It was a large portion size and it had a great flavor. The chicken was all white meat and very tender. I was very happy with my meal and will definitely continue to give this place another shot! .

WAOOOO SO GUD Ambiance: h i d d e n gem in a random plaza in a random part of town (random to me since I am very new to Indy). The interior is very casual and loud (caso cerrado is your background music) but perfect for fun dates and outings with friends. There is freshly made food and cafeteria style food behind a plexi-glass. Order and pay at the cashier can lead to lines (once it starts getting crowded). Price: It's a bit pricey (they aren't listed, which is ... odd.... but they will tell you the price if you ask) but it's food using ingredients that are local to DR Vzla and Colombia so I expected that hike in price. Food: THE EMPANADAS ARE SO GOOD. SO GOOD. I ordered the carne mechada (shredded beef) and cheese empandas. The masa was salty, perfectly fried, and delicious. The carne mechada was seasoned con el sazon perfecto. The cheese was salty yet melting cheese. I also ordered the sancocho de pollo (chicken soup) for lunch the next day since it called for cold rain and my poor Texan blood is sensitive to the weather. I must make a confession, i tried it when I got home :o. It was amazing. It reminded me of my abuelas caldo de pollo and the new years sancocho I grew up eating. I am excited to continue eating at this restaurant that uses authentic ingredients and flavors to spice up my time in Indy. Language barrier: I've seen it mentioned that language barrier was an issue for others but I was able to communicate with the employee in both english and spanish. He was comfortable speaking both so I hope more of you encounter him at the cashiers desk!

So you know when you do the buffet thing and sometimes you get that feeling.. like mebbe some of this could have been there yesterday? Not this place. No. You could litterally be the only one in the place and the owner is going to have fresh naan fried up for you. I mean.. i usually do a thing where i put a tiny scoop of everthing and then just start narrowing down to the favorites. Ahh nuts i liked everything.

Erin read your review as we were headed to Thai. Will get back there. Pho 36 is solid. I had the beef stew. My daughter who is becoming quite the pho snob, put it up with the best. Nice owner. Spring rolls good. Very reasonably priced. Saw the #22 being served. Looked great. Owner said it has 5 meats and is their largest entree.
Delicious pho and banh mi! The owner was very friendly and accommodating as he answered all our questions about the food. Definitely going to come here again.

Here in Nashville for the NP conference, found this place close to our hotel. Was looking for something different & this delivered. WAS ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!!! Service was a little slow, only 2servers & 1chef for entire place, and full- but they were super friendly and apologetic. But once food came, I did not care.... I had the panchang? Curry.... So flavorful, I didn't want to stop eating. My mom had the drunken noodles, one of her favorites, and she said it was great. Fantastic flavor and really hot & spicy... Great!!! Don't be thrown by the outside decor-it's by a go cart place--the food is better than anything we've had here so far!!!

This restaurant has delivered over and over again. The service is very professional , quick and pleasant. It is a casual atmosphere which allows you to relax and just enjoy the experience what the well prepared Indian dishes deliver. The chicken korma is one of my favorites. What is special is that you can dictate the level of spice you need. I usually have it with the stuffed cheese naan which is simply delicious. My husband 's favorite is the lamb korma. We usually travel almost 60-70 miles to get these dishes- right there you see it's worth. Try it if you are in town- well worth it

Delicious, fresh, quality ingredients and home made flavors. Pork is awesome. Tostones were crunchy and full of flavor. Generous portions. Try the flan for dessert, you won't be disappointed. Service is very friendly and the place is spotless.

I work in the neighborhood and this is a great place for me to get a meal that will last me lunch and dinner for less than $10. The ingredients are flavorful, diverse, and different. Most people have a great attitude and are generous with bowl portions, but one woman is problematic. I assume she's an owner. She's an older woman with dark hair and a foreign accent. Lady, let me tell you that me and all my friends change our mind about eating there when we see you're working. For a $9 bowl, you underserve us by about $2. Stop being stingy. It doesn't cost you much for a few extra scoops. Stop hurting for business with your greediness. *EDIT* Now I feel bad because she gave me more on my last visit :( It seems to vary by day and person. I still love you Dooners!!!
Amazing sushi place ! I recommend a thousand times! Wish I could give this place more than 5 stars. Lobster tango & volcano roll.

Godavari jn Brentwood for lunch buffet today Saturday Feb 10th was excellent. There is a big vegetarian selection too but my main feasting was on the Mutton Biriyani and Shrimp Curry. $13.99 + tax + tip brings this in under $20. Great service, fresh food, typical buffet ambiance. Recommend this stop for genuine South Indian meals.
The food is not authentic and just isn't good. friendly service but none of our entrees (10 of us) were good. We won't go back here.

I had the pork steak and it was so dry and hard with no flavor at all; my family ordered a Red snapper fillet and the fish tasted like catfish, and they don't have options for kids. The empananas was very salty, their beans were awful, and their onions with vinegar was nasty. The young girl server was very rude. We have been to Dominican and Puerto Rico and we were very disappointment of the food at this restaurant and pricey. We are Not coming back and we will tell our friend about it. It seems to be a slow night for being Saturday, and the tasteless food it took for ever.

When a new restaurant opens, I typically wait a couple of months to try it out to give them time to make adjustments, but my husband and I were just too excited for iNDO. I recommend reservations because this is not a huge space and can fill up quickly. Although we had a server, the front of the house seems to work as team and everyone we encountered was friendly and knowledgeable. They all seem to be passionate about the food and drinks they are serving which always makes service better. The nigiri was like butter, cabbage salad was refreshing, lamb ribs were tender, and the crab rice was delicious and provided us with a fun table side presentation. This place has a great vibe and we had such a fun dining experience. It's hard to believe they have been open for such a short time. The prices are high, but so is the quality. We can't wait to go back!

AH, I love this place. Best Thai food in Edmonton, in my opinion. Last time we went we ordered the Pa-nang Chicken and Pad Thai. The Pa-nang IS TO DIE FOR. Oh my goodness so tasty! I cannot rave enough about it, I think I could eat that everyday. You must try it! Plus, the prices are incredibly reasonable. What a great place! I almost don't want to review it because I want it to stay hidden so I'll never have to wait for a table :D
This is my go to place for Indian food when I am in Brentwood for lunch. Their buffet never disappoints and never gets old as they vary their selections.

Just got my order delivered right to my door! I got the Dal makhani, shrimp Goan curry, veg Samosa, garlic naan, and mango lassi! Yes, I ordered that for myself:) It was really good. I didn't think they would deliver because I'm about 15 mins from the restaurant, but they did! The guy got here quicker than the estimated time. He was super friendly and even shook my hand:) I will be ordering again!

My first visit here and it was great. It's a small place designed for take out but if you do decide to dine in it's a great experience. The service is great and the food was yummy. I hope they stay around. A lot of good places in that area never get the support they need from the community. I don't live close by but I will visit again with the hubster.

We had such a great experience here! The place is clean. The menu is diverse. And the service is super friendly. I love when a waiter says, "let me recommend something!!!!!"
