The wonton house soup was so good...a big pot of everything on the kitchen! I had the bento box and I was so happy with what I ordered. My husband got the Thai basil with beef and it was great: the meat was super tender. The chef made my son a plate of lo neon and chicken (no veg) and that kid ate like a champ! The pineapple fruit finish was such s sweet way to depart! We are going back!!!

Came here for lunch. We ordered one of each chicken, mac and cheese, a fountain drink, and a biscuit. The chicken was dry and with way too much bread crumbs. It had no taste to it without the sauce. The mac and cheese was a bit spicy with some kind a peppers and perhaps meat in it...doesn't seem like a mac and cheese, but more like chili. NOT the best mac and cheese we ever ate. As for the biscuit, it was good. The top was crunchy and buttery. The inside was nice and soft. Overall, this place is over priced for some dry chicken tenders. Not worth it.
I'm so happy there is a Pollo Tropical in the area now! yummo! Where else can you get 1/2 a chicken and 2 sides for 6 bucks? They also have great sauces, a Guava BBQ and Curry Mustard that I love!

Im from new york , i drive in philly for work nd this place is worth every mile it surpassed my favorite spot in new york. customer service is great can't really find anything bad to say about this place other then i have to drive an 1 and a half away to get there. There portion of food is like no other spot you would defiantly not be disappointed (oxtails rice and peas mac n cheese with candy yams extra gravy)

I come here about once a month and get the same, traditional pho every time. I happened to be there on their grand opening day back in spring of 2007 and fortunately, they have kept it their restaurant clean since then. (I'm sure everyone's been to a pho place with greasy tables and messy decor) The service is always fast for the pho noodle soup no matter how busy they are. The place has a few flat-panel tv's that always has the important games on. If you're lucky, there's parking right in front of the place on 11th. There's also validated parking for the lot on Washington between 9th and 10th. I don't know if that's valid on the weekdays though.
The food here is very fresh. I like that they have a variety of food like Gyros and cheeseburgers. They also have daily lunch specials from 11-2PM. I will definitely come back here again.
One of my regular favs in West Chester. Always quality and different. Service is very good

I was trying to find somewhere to get dinner in philly around Christmas on a busy Saturday. But my the grace of god I was able to get a reservation to Spice Finch at 5:45. I've been to a ton of Mediterranean style places in philly - Vernick, Suraya, Zahav, all the best places. I'd have to say that Spice Finch is very competitive with all these restaurants and definitely has better prices. The wait staff was very very friendly and accommodating. Food cake out very fast. Everything was DELICIOUS. We had the cauliflower, clams, carrot hummus, and chicken. The chicken was probably the best I've ever eaten. If I could give this place more than 5 stars I would!

I'm normally a frequenter of Tiffin (a wonderful restaurant as well) but I heard that Ekta was less expensive and "better," so we tried it on for size! BEYOND EXPECTATIONS!! Food was flavorful and fresh, and the place was not too crowded. Ended up being about $40 for the two of us, which is not too bad for a Sunday splurge. The paneer tikka masala was less salty than the version at Tiffin, and the pricing was better for the (albeit slightly smaller) portion sizes. My boyf especially liked the malai kofta, which I had never tried before and also ended up loving. Definitely check this place out if you haven't already; I love going to college in a town with great Indian food!!

Stopped in on my lunch break and got the gyro plate - comes with a side salad and fresh pita bread. The food was great and the service was wonderful. If you're looking for somewhere to grab a quick bite and you're in the mood for Greek food I'd definitely recommend the place!

The lunch buffet is not bad: standard fare, $11.95. The restaurant is attractive and comfortable. The chicken tandoori was perfect. I enjoyed the cauliflower, but there was not a great deal of it in the aloo gobi dish. I would caution someone who does not like very spicy food that this restaurant will cause your lips to erupt. Water glasses were kept full, which was critical, but no one went out of their way to be friendly or welcoming.
Another home run, with the chicken kabobs for lunch. Super friendly owner and staff. Just ask for their recommendations and you can't go wrong.

I went a time back, and the food was not very memorable. I've lived many places in the world with my family (Army Brat). I can't say it was bad, I can say pricey for what it was. Also my guy threw his away...mind you though he is picky on different flavored food.
Good, cheap, hole-in-the-wall convenience store to grab a quick bite. The fried tofu banh mi was delicious! Don't forget the hoisin sauce and sriracha!

Was good food but extremely expensive. Noticed today they closed up. Priced themselves right out of business once the people trying a new restaurant stopped. $2.50 for one egg when everybody else charges $1. Come on.

Relentlessly predictable with the dinner buffet the compelling reason to go, this friendly place is the default Indian restaurant on campus for Penn and Drexel students and faculty alike. Outstanding Northern India and Moghli influenced specialties the quality and consistency of which hasn't varied an iota in the 20+ years that I have been a fan. Up and across the street from the McDonald's at 40th & Walnut, whose Big Mac, Coke and fries cost not much less than Tandoor's wonderful and light years more healthy lunch. Excellent place with each dish unique and given the quality of ingredients and preparation, one of the very best bargains in town. Vindaloos are authentic, the nan addictive and the chicken issuing from the tandoor outstanding. Bring beer or wine or drink their mango nectar.

On the bright side, it's better than Pho Bistro. I came here for lunch and it sadly was mediocre, as I feared it would be. It's still at a higher price point than your normal joints in the Bay Area, LA, or the OC, but it's something you accept with the cost of transporting traditional Asian goods to Santa Barbara (an ethnic food dead zone). Though I have to say, $6 for banh mi is highway robbery. I got the bun thit nuong (grilled pork) for a light option. If you're a salad fan, I'd usually recommend this, but it was genuinely flavorless and there were even few vegetables. Most of it was just vermicelli, flavored with iceberg lettuce. For the record, romaine is superior. I didn't find the meat portion too small, but it was lacking more of the regulars. It needed bean sprouts, Thai basil, more quick-pickled carrots, and more mint. No complaints about the Thai iced tea, at least. The nuoc mam deserves a special shoutout for tasting just like the first half of its name: nuoc, which means water in Vietnamese. I would've appreciated seeing a chopped up chili or two in there. On the bright side, the service was fast and their menu is easy to read.

Enjoyed a fabulous dinner, with great service. There were 4 of us, and 2 had Hawaiian Butterfish and 2 had Bronzini. Both were wonderful. The Bronzini came with risotto, and the butterfish was served over spinach. We have been to Florentino's several times and I highly recommend it.

darn, I wish i took a picture. I am a UCSB employee and am kicking myself for not trying this place sooner. their calamari salad has to be the BEST calamari i have ever had in my life. i dont know what they did to this to make it so amazing. you should also try their wings both hot and lemon dill. OUT OF THIS WORLD. they need to open another stentorian in SB and not just on UCSB campus. theres not enough Greek places here. it is my favorite kind of food. I cant wait to go back and try what else they have
By far the best and most authentic Afghan food I have ever had and prices were reasonable. Great job on the decor.

Literally so horrible. I just ate there and instead of pita they gave us tortillas, without even warning us. No discount for subpar food. The chicken was way too salty. The lamb was disgusting. The Gyro and Falafel were edible but definitely not great. Will never return and will tell everyone to avoid like the plague.
So delicious! Very beautiful atmosphere! We ordered the lamb chops and the Mahi Mahi! Amazing!! This was our second time.
Really good red curry chicken, perfect amount of spice. Very cozy place friendly staff
Wow. I am in town on business and check the yelp reviews for a restaurant recommendation. Yelp did not disappoint with this recommendation. I would give Nadia another star if allowed.

I have only ordered from her through Caviar and it's a recent discovery. But the eggplant dish and the sticky rice are amazing. Never had such good sticky rice. The appetizers are great as well. Not super spicy - just right. Pad Thai is good but not the best I have ever had. That may be because I am ordering it though. I wish I could just order bowls and bowls of their sticky rice - it's something that's not that easy to make - Thai sticky rice is different from other kinds. Ok - maybe I sound a little looney - but give it a try!

This place is great, it is not fancy, but the food is amazing and the staff is great. I've been there a few times and always have different dishes and have never been disappointed. The staff there are also great with kids. We have a 7 month old and they played with him and nobody cared that he was making noise. There were lots of families there too. Garlic naan stuffed with cheese and some Tika massala sauce is to die for. The portions are good, prices are good, food and service is as well. Can't go wrong. I would suggest making reservations as it fills up quickly.
The buffet wad 4 days old food.Big disappointment.The service was bad .Stinks all over the place. Tried giving a second chance but impossible to eat the food.
Everything was amazing... it's a tapas style restaurant so portions are small, but they are each little morsels of love and flavor. We loved all the veggie dishes. Highly recommended.

Consistently perfect, the pearl delivers again! Started with their perfectly garlicky frog legs, then got talked into the daily specials of pompano & camel, both of which were exquisite!!! Already looking forward to our next trip!

Tried this new spot in Doylestown last night. Cute place, nice updates to the restaurant. Service was excellent, other than that, the place was a disappointment. Food was really bad, grape leaves and hummus almost inedible. Beef kabab was both well done and rare. Host was super nice but unless the food improves, this place won't last long.

The yelp reviews drove me to Orchid Thai, the food and attentive service would keep me coming back (I'm from way out of town...out of state actually). There are plenty of options in the immediate area, but I really felt like Thai tonight. We went in late, 8:30pm, it was empty except for one solo diner. The atmosphere is plain and simple, clean and bright but I was going for the food and not the decor. I was not disappointed. I ordered the Green Curry, vegetables only. It was loaded with vegetables, packed with flavor and generous enough for 2 meals...except I just couldn't stop eating it and ended up with an empty bowl. I usually go for more on the spicy side, this was less spicy than my norm but the flavor really stood out so that I didn't miss the extra heat. My co-worker loves ginger but pork not so much and spice on the mild side. She inquired about the Ginger Curry and Samantha offered to bring her a taste. The pork was so well cooked, amazingly tender, that she too ate her entire bowl. It was more savory than spicy but still had a slight heat at the back of the throat. Yes, I did dip my spoon into get just a taste of the broth. If I get back to this neck of the woods again, I will definitely be back and this time, I'll take a second order to go so I can enjoy it later.

Falafel's are awesome! 5 star for that! We tried the beef in pita, chicken on salad & hummus plate with chicken, all were very good. The baba ganoush wasn't really exactly as per the traditional one, but tasted awesome the first day. On our repeat visit, it wasn't as good. But don;t get me wrong, it's still far better than most of the places out there round US. Certainly going to be a regular, at least on their center city location. Don't forget the fries, those are awesome as well!

Service is nice. I just didnt enjoy my food. I ordered chicken thai curry. I never had it anywhere before. The only thai food i have tried in my life was pad thai. I wanted to try something else. But i didnt like it. My husband ordered siam duck. He said it was good.

It's interesting to compare the pre and post renovation reviews. Clearly people like what they've done with the place. I've always liked this REMEDY, even when it was a hole in the wall. The chai is delicious, the tea options are plentiful and the food is satisfying. The service has always been friendly and quick (especially considering how busy they can be). And now there are lots of great seating options, whether you want counter, table or lounge style. As for parking, you can leave your car in the lot just south of REMEDY, just don't forget to check it in on the ipad before ordering.

Gave this place a try and wasn't pleased. It's nothing compared to many of the pho places in LA. My friend and I got the beef pho bowl and it just didn't have the flavor there. The broth tasted like water.. The people working there was friendly, but the food just wasn't there for me.

Got the pre-prepared red curry chicken and rice as well as the coconut soup with chicken. Both were amazing! The red curry wasn't too spicy and was really tasty. The service was great as well. Highly recommend for a quick, healthy, high-quality take out option on Main St!

business_name: Saint Louis Halal Meat, Grocery & Foods - Baba's Restaurant
text: Have always been a big fan of Saint Louis Halal Meat - each dish has a distinct flavor - which is usually missing in other restaurants. The Biriyani is amazing and every dish outdoes the other. I was very impressed at the lunch buffet they now serve. Such quality of food at a buffet is amazing. Do try Baba's in case you already haven't !

We had an excellent experience from start to finish. Whether it was Food, service, or accommodation of special requests Spice Finch exceeded our expectations. This is a great addition to the Philly food scene.

Went for lunch the other day. Have lunch specials for $10 including a small spring roll and soup. Had Sichuan beef and hot sour soup. Everything tasted very fresh and all dishes were very flavorful. Great lunch spot!

Hands down- always good! It's my go-to place with my husband and no matter where we travel in the world, Thai Place is the gold standard. Must-haves: Tom Yum soup and Pad Woon Sen! If you have room after good size portion- try the black sweet rice. AMAZING. UPDATE: Unfortunately the restaurant is under new ownership/management. The service is very good, but the quality of ingredients and commitment to authentic taste is lacking.

Coworker introduced me to Petra. I am forever grateful. Can't go wrong with mixed grill. A lot of food. Also I am no expert on hummus but I've had it from at least a dozen or so sources... I can't imagine hummus being any better than Petra's.
Good prices, lightning quick service, but the sandwich was only alright. Supposedly great for breakfast, not a great lunch place.

Star #1 for Real (not paper) cups and mugs Star #2 for Greek-infused pastries and lunch specials Star #3 for Nice corner spot with natural light and no parking meters Star #4 for Big foamy lattes Star #5 for Not pretending to be something you're not (such free office space, or carefully focus grouped, or unaffected by the cost of accepting credit cards) Overall: Cute, cozy corner coffee shop with variety and character. Not trying to compete with corporate american coffee, just doing its own thing the best it can and I like it. Support local businesses because they are never perfect. This means they're human.

Got nachos. The chips were stale and needed salt badly. The service was awful. Got our food and drinks and the waiter did not check on us once. Will say the drinks were good...would go back and sit at bar
Very nice undercover spot. From the outside, you'd raise an eyebrow. It is however a very cozy spot and I look forward to visiting again soon.

Others seem to like it and it's been around a long time-so you may like it, but as frequent travelers and people who have lived in many cities, we won't be returning here. The service was appropriately attentive. The Thai dumplings were good. Everything else was REALLY sweet, like unedibly so. BBQ pork, chicken fried rice, and tofu pad Thai. Still looking for a Thai restaurant in South Tampa that we like. :(

They get the job done. Not the best Indian cuisine but it satiates my taste for Indian food. The are great with delivery and are within the time frame that they post. Id order from them again if i'm in a crunch at work and cant run out.

By far my favorite place to go out to eat! Love it and it feels healthy for some reason. Mmmmmm. Try the banana rolls for dessert... The pineapple ice cream that comes with the banana rolls is one of a kind. So delicious!

I really LOVE the bar here. I've attended several happy hours here which is awesome since I can walk my happy/drunk self the half block home afterwards. Bartenders are friendly and they have some good happy hour specials ($3 wine, $2 beer). Besides the booze, I have dined here once. The food was just okay in my opinion. I would probably give it another try as it wasn't bad by any means but it just wasn't that memorable. There's a nice patio on the side of the restaurant that would be nice to dine on when the weather isn't miserable. I also noticed the huge private dining area in the basement. I would definitely suggest it to our office if we were planning an offsite meeting.

Service is good and place is always clean. This is the first Vietnamese restaurant I've (ever, even other cities/states) gotten take out in which the noodles and protein(shrimp; meat or ) aren't served in a styrofoam clam box and it put a huge smile on my face the first time I got take-out from here! THANK YOU! There are biodegradable paper cups with lids that can be used for broth in place of the styrofoam cups for the future maybe? Baby steps thus far I can't wait to make my way down the menu of this great place! Welcome!

My friend and I came here after we had attended PrideFest the whole day. The two of us were hot, hungry, and possibly a little smelly. Out of all the places we walked by, this place felt like it would be the best location for us given our clothes and look. I mean I was wearing purple and red lipstick at the same time people. Anyways, I got their Pad Ginger and it was delicious. The chicken was cooked and sliced perfectly, which to me means that the thickness of the cut was perfect for the amount of time that all the food needed to cook to the level of tastiness that I like. The dish wasn't excessively spicy either, which is a frequent problem with me and Thai. I just don't do spicy all that well. So to me, the spice level in my dish was perfect. I would totally order that again. The service was great really. They didn't mind our crazy look or the fact that we were potentially smelly. Plus, they gave us so much water since we were thirsty from the heat. I really did enjoy the service. I would totally come back again. It is well worth it and so delicious as well. I need to start planning the next trip.

My bf and I were devastated to hear that Cafe Nhu Y was closing. Their banh mi thit nguoi (traditional Vietnamese sandwich), banh mi chay (vegetarian Vietnamese sandwich), banh mi thit ga (chicken Vietnamese sandwich) are sooo much better than any other place in South Philly (e.g. Cafe Cuong, Viet Huong). We're always disappointed when we go to one of those other places... During our last visit before Cafe Nhu Y closed, they gave us a flyer that they would be relocating to somewhere on 4th or 5th and Washington Ave. I figured it would be easy to find so I tossed the flyer into the recycling bin. Since my bf and I are renovating our house, we are on Washington Ave and Columbus Blvd every weekend, shopping for renovation materials. For monthssss, my bf and I have been in search of the new Cafe Nhu Y on Washington Ave to no avail. We drove by very slowly on front through 7th and Washington Ave but could not find the new cafe for the life of us!! It was so frustrating UNTIL we finally spotted the Grand Opening sign early December 2014!! The cafe relocated and has been rebranded as "Lee's Cafe and Bistro" at 522 Washington Ave. We cannnn'tttt wait to try the new place!!! Hopefully, it still has the mom-and-pop shop feel with the mom-and-pop taste and prices!!

we went there with little expectations as there was only one woman behind the counter and no one else in the restaurant. we waited as two young men walked through the door and went behind into the kitchen and started making our food. I'm going to say at this point, I was a little skeptical. we both got gyros, to go. While in the car we both took a quick bite as we were starving. Much to our pleasant surprise they were delicious. The pitas were perfectly crispy. The meat was freshly cut off of one of those spinning things.... and not greasy! A perfect amount of tatziki, tomatoes and onion A pleasant surprise indeed! Bathrooms very clean as well as the restaurant. My new gyro go to!!

My favorite restaurant - you won't find Thai to beat this anywhere in the St. Louis area. When I lived in Columbia I ate here once a week, and more often if I had the time. The appetizers: excellent. The main courses: not to be missed. The service: prompt and attentive. The spiciness: customizable to your heart's content. Upon special request the kitchen will even kick your dish up to authentic Thai levels of spice, although not without plenty of warning from the wait staff. I love the basic dishes like Pad Thai and Pad See Ew, but the Swimming Angel is a family favorite. This is also one of the few restaurants I've found where the take-out and leftovers are just as good as the fresh dishes. Do I give it five stars? Mister, you better believe it.

Food, service, and presentation are excellent. This place is a little on the pricey side, but it seems to be an East Coast thing in general. Whenever I'm in the mood for some good Thai food, this is the spot for me

Great prices. Great and very friendly service. "Toy" brought our three year old son some Thai chips to munch on and also made sure he had extra plates and cups to share with us. Great and cheap Thai Tea. Good was great for the price. Great atmosphere, kind people, good food - we'll be back!
One of the hidden gems of Nashville! We went with our go-to chicken Pad Thai. Literally the best in town! Spice it up if you can stand the heat!

This is the best place in saint louis to have halwa puri and cholay. Their puris are very light, crispy and non oily puris. They serve it with aalo walay cholay and halwa. Too good !! Recently we have tried their samosas too. They were like pakistani baray wala bakery samosas that you have with chai. Delicious!!

I live in St. Albert, and if I can avoid going to Edmonton for food I try to. There are a couple Vietnamese places in St. Albert, and Pho Anh Sang is one of them. Its a hole in the wall restaurant tucked into a mini-mall just off Mckenney ave. The decor is barren and basic but I love it. It is family run, the food is cheap, fresh and fast.

Spice Finch was good, but nothing really blew me away and they have a lot of competition in this market. I had the shabazi fries which were delicious. Then, the baked cheese which was also really good, but I wanted some crostini or something to slather it on or even more shredded phyllo. it simultaneously wasn't salty or sweet enough. The peri peri shrimp and flatbread were the biggest standouts of the meal, but the roasted cauliflower was just meh. The list continues with the lamb shank and warm grains. The shank was delicious, I wanted more of the date glaze, and I wished it was a bit thicker. The roasted veggies that accompanied it were also great, but the pickles interspersed were an unwelcome surprise. The warm grains aka cous cous and puffed rice not so much a delight. There just wasn't much flavor and the puffed rice looked very unappetizing. Finally, the biggest disappointment of the night, and what I strongly discourage, were the two desserts we ordered: the chocolate tahini cake, and the burnt cream. I've had tahini based desserts before so I know they can be sweet and nutty and entirely delicious, but this was not so. The cake was dry, somewhat savory and there was a lingering flavor that just wasn't very pleasant. The buttercream was heavy and had that same savory tinge. My favorite part of the dessert was the orange sorbet, and that says a lot because I'm not inclined towards orange flavored things, but it was light and fresh and altogether wonderful. The burnt cream, which I thought would be a creme brulee of sorts was not that. It was more of a cottage cheese cheesecake with a mildly sweet cheesey texture (that's common of middle eastern desserts). I was not crazy about this mostly because it was a bit bland, but the rose syrup and the fresh fruit were delightful. Neither choice was great, but between the chocolate cake and the burnt cream I would pick the cream. In summary, get the fries, the shrimp, and the shank, and go somewhere else for dessert!

Disclaimer: I have never eaten inside this restaurant. This is my go-to for Indian delivery when I am feeling extra lazy. You can order on Yelp, on their website, and on other delivery sites (e.g., OrderUp). The garlic naan rivals that of a lot of other Indian restaurants in Indy, even after being packaged and toted to my house. The tikka masala isn't as good as India Garden or Delhi Palace's, but they are still good. I also love their Saag Paneer, which might be better than that of the other two places I mentioned. If you order at the beginning of dinner service during the week (around 5ish), delivery is ridiculously fast. Other times it can take up to an hour. It is definitely worth it though for some delicious Indian food at home! Did I mention they are the only Indian place that delivers to the downtown area?!?

This is the best Indian restaurant in Indy..Chicken Biryani (Hyderabadi) at its best compare to other restaurants. Food presentation is awesome!! New branch next to Patel brothers is cool, nice ambiance, good and great staff. Don't know how's their lunch buffet but dine menu is good. Glad they opened up this branch..Movie, groceries and awesome restaurant at one shot...my soul is happy!!!! totally loved it will go there any time.....

Seriously, the most beautiful restaurant I've eaten in. We ate here for weekend brunch with a 4 year old, 2 year old, and 14 month old. Definitely make reservations. Stroller friendly, had high chairs but no kids menu. We ordered several flatbreads, the green salad, the Lebanese omelette, and the crispy chickpea hummus. Everything was amazing! I could eat the green salad and omelette every day - so bright and fresh. The cheese flatbread was great for the kids. The coffee menu was excellent and the spiced chai was warm and delicious (could have done without the dried rose petals). Will definitely be visiting again. There's a beautiful garden outside with tons of seating and it's a nice area to let the kids explore.

This was my intro to Afghan food and it was a fabulous experience. I'm very adventurous and love Indian and have recently had a lot of homemade Pakistani food and this was comparable to that. It was a little spicier than I expected but was still absolutely delicious. The staff was so nice and the ambience was reflective of Afghani culture, which was cool. It wasn't the best food I've ever had but it was still pretty good and I am looking forward to returning.

Bui's sandwiches are perfect for mornings on the go--simple fresh-made goodness that's super affordable for students (cash only). Sandwiches can be topped with "bui's sauce" (which is essentially a delicious spicy mayo), ketchup, and s&p, so be ready to specify your condiments.
Best Indian food I've had in Philadelphia. We ordered the vegetable samosas, paneer naan, kadai chicken, and chicken vindaloo. Everything we had was great! BYOB was a nice added bonus.

This place is small. Lots of yellow. Has about 10 - 12 tables. I came and was impressed. The food is all home made and not frozen or bought and cooked. I ordered the chicken satay. Savory and soft. Loved it. The sauce and cucumbers were a nice touch and gives it that 5 star it deserves. The chicken wings were ok. The beef satay had rice cakes and some gooey yellow curry sauce to it. It was good but not my cup of tea. The next dish is the fried seafood noodles (Gangerang Keawteaw (I think that's how you spell-it). That was spectacular. Loved it. Also ordered a curry vermicelli noodle dish. This was very strong in flavor. Watery. Egg, some sort of flakey fried dough which reminded me of roti's. This for me was ok. Overall, the price is great, the food was great and the service was good. I'd recommend this place to try for those that like authentic foods. I'm gonna make this place one of my local favs in the neighborhood to eat. *wink* Gotta try all the food on the menu to satisfy my eyes and taste buds.
Good food and service. I had the rice with black beans, pollo guisado, and potato salad.
Had the green thai curry, it was amazing! I'm really looking forward to trying more of their menu choices.

We went on a Monday evening and we truly liked the ambiance. It was a light crowd so we were seated right away. We both started with the crispy spring rolls which were good. Three small crispy spring rolls with a side of sweet n sour sauce. We both had Pad Thai. He had Chicken Pad Thai and I had Tofu Pad Thai. He thought the Pad Thai wasn't sweet enough but the flavor was really good. My Tofu Pad Thai was very good. It wasn't too dry or too saucy. It was a nice balance. We had a Mai Thai drink that was good as well. The waitress was very nice and made sure our meal was satisfactory. It was dim in the restaurant so the pic color doesn't give the meal's aesthetics much justice.

Had the mixed plate that feeds two....its bland uninteresting food typical for Louisiana middle Eastern restaurants. It's in a suburban shopping center and although spacious a family with three screaming children was placed next to us. Service was unenthusiastic no reason to go here if you have other options.
Great food and excellent service! Been several times now and everything I have eaten I have throughly enjoyed.

A friend recommended Bui's after he heard me raving about Lyns...I will now only rave about Bui's. Simple concept: egg sandwiches on hoagie rolls. What sets them apart: Lots of ingredients (no skimping on eggs or veggies), fresh veggies (tomatoes, mushrooms and spinach) and of course, the famous special sauce (mix of mayo / ketchup). For $4.50 you get a huge, delicious and warm sandwich - perfect cold day fix. Can't wait to be back!
love mutton and this place's got great mutton!
Definitely good food. You can tell its homemade. The pho ga broth had more flavor than your run of the mill pho place. And I ordered the bean paste shake for dessert. Happy belly :-)

This was my very first meal in Philadelphia. AMAZING. The owners are wonderful. The children are adorable. the food is like..WHOA. This is my place, I take everyone here (even my red state step mother) who walk away raving fans. Rice, kebabs, sesame naan, salad....really folks, this place is off the chain. They don't seem to have a huge dinner crowd so I get scared they will close. Give these people some business!!! Besides, Oscars is next door!

Delicious food in right-sized portions. I had an avocado green bean bowl with fried Rice & a perfect egg over easy. The rice wasn't too heavy or greasy at all. Spouse got avocado spring rolls (made fresh while he watched) & filet mignon fried rice. He liked his dinner too. Very reasonably priced. Would definitely go back.

On recommendation of a restaurant concierge, we visited Sen Thai for lunch on a Saturday afternoon for the first time. The restaurant had a very open, modern look, but still had hints of a traditional Thai restaurant. The service was prompt, friendly, and very attentive. My fiancé ordered the Tonkotsu ramen, I ordered the yellow curry with chicken, and we also shared the spring roll appetizer. The spring rolls were crisp, hot, and very tasty. They were served with a mildly spicy honey sauce that was also very good and paired well with the roll. The yellow curry was excellent. The curry had a great consistency, the contents and rice were cooked perfectly, and it was above all, very tasty. I would definitely order this again and recommend to anyone wanting a mildly spicy coconut curry. Another surprise was the cabbage side salad that had a delicious peanut sauce. While I didn't try my fiancé's ramen, she gave it a thumbs up and I can say that it's smell and presentation was also very good. That says a lot because we are always seeking out authentic ramen and have a large number of restaurants under our belt. Overall, this is a great Thai restaurant that also does Japanese dishes like ramen well too. The only reason why I deducted 1 star is that compared to other Thai restaurants with similar food quality, this place had consistently higher prices, but perhaps that's a result of where it's located. If you are in the area and want great Thai or Japanese food, this is the place to go.
Absolutely delicious. Spicy and creamy tiki marsla. Vindaloo had just the right amount of heat and was perfect with the fluffy rice. Even my husband enjoyed the food and he is an all American eater.

I still think that Spiro's is my favorite Greek place in town. I always go to the location on Watson Road since it's not far from here, but found myself at this location recently while celebrating the life of a family member who passed away. This was one of her favorite places and we luckily got the private room reserved on short notice for a family celebration following her funeral. The private room is cozy but it held our almost 30 people in a U shaped table with some space to stand around and chat. It had a fireplace too. The restaurant had a bad fire a few years ago and the rebuild is very nicely done. We were all brought salads to start - my FAVORITE! I just love Spiro's Greek salad. I could've just eaten that. We also had warm bread. For entrees, we were offered multiple things. I actually ordered something that wasn't offered, that pasta corfu, which is a red sauce with veggies. I got it without chicken. It was a HUGE bowl and I added feta. It was good. We finished with baklava. Again, delicious! I was almost too stuffed... almost! Service was good except for me not getting water for awhile at the beginning. THey brought me out more drinks without me asking. They also brought us more butter, bread, and other things on our request. With almost 30 of us, they had our meals out and plates warmed quickly, and kept things bussed nicely. I'd come back to this location again for sure! Next time with free reign on the menu, I'll order the flaming cheese!

My husband and I are not from the area but found ourselves up here and found this place. DELICIOUS. I wasn't expecting much because of the location but the food was incredible. We're both vegetarian - got mutter paneer and an baingan bharta. Service was nice and decor nothing to write home about but the food was so good I might have to make the trek to come back. YUM!

My best friend and I decided to drop in here for lunch. It's always a little nerve racking going to a new place, especially a new cultural experience. Within the first 3 seconds we walked in, all of that went away. It was late afternoon so there was only one other person eating at the time. We sat down, our waitress (Ru, sorry I'm not sure of the spelling) immediately was one of the most helpful, knowledgeable, and personable waitresses I have ever had. She helped us through the menu and made recommendations, which we went with her suggestion of, basically, a sampler that is eaten with teff. Great choice. While we were chatting with her, the other patron eating overheard our conversation and brought his dish over for us to taste as well. I absolutely loved this place. I loved the atmosphere, the food and I loved hearing her story about coming from Ethiopia herself. I will be back and am looking forward to trying the other dishes, and learning more from Ru

Myself and a few of my friends went for lunch buffet yesterday. We had a very bad experience. Two items were stale, practically rotten. I normally avoid India palace because a few months ago their samosa were totally spoiled. In addition, a number of dishes (chicken tandoori and goat curry) were gone and they never replenished after we requested twice. I would rate this Indian restaurant very low. Also, be careful, check the quality of the food before you eat at this place.

I enjoyed my visit to this clean and inviting place on 38th Street. It is located on the north side of 38th between Moller & Georgetown at Kevin Way. There's a stoplight making it easy to get across traffic and if you make an immediate right on Kevin Way in front of the Planet Fitness, you can drive straight to this bright yellow restaurant. Although it is elevated with several steps to climb, there is a ramp for those who need it. Inside is quite open and spacious. I was seated at one of the raised booths (They do have some tables located in a section that do not require stepping up.) The hostess/waitress was pleasant and efficient. She took my order and within about twelve minutes, I had my small order of Jerk Chicken. Wow! The flavor was fantastic! I got eight small wing halves served wet with lots of napkins. The had a built in heat, but not overwhelming. They also had a nice tangy flavor that was similar to a barbecue sauce, but with a bit of additional spice to lift it to another level. Definitely try these if you visit! I also tried a housemade sweet drink called Byssop that is made from hibiscus flowers. The drink is very sweet for someone who doesn't drink soda. Once I got passed the initial blast of sweet, I adjusted my expectations and noted that it was both fruity and floral. The deep reddish violet color was appealing and the beverage, served over ice, was transparent. Note that an order of the beverage does not come with refills. My main course was from the dinner menu: Oxtail stew which comes with a couple side courses. The stew is made with tail meat which is "bone-in" and floats in a dark brown gravy with stewed carrot chunks. The gravy can be eaten like soup, but note that you may get pieces of thyme stem as I found several lengths in mine. The carrots were tender and tasty. The beef itself was very tender, but because it is submerged in the gravy, becomes difficult to cut off the bone. I suggest asking for an additional small plate that could be used as a cutting board. Good taste, but not a "wow" combination. The only real disappointment was from the sides. I got the mixed veggies since my meal was meat laden. The veggies were colorful, but thoroughly cooked, so they were limp and not as flavorful as I hoped. The Jallof rice was served in great abundance, probably close to three cups worth! The rice was a bit overcooked and had become dry. I probably could have added some of it to the gravy from the stew, but I didn't. The rice, though bright orange in color, was a bit on the bland side as well. I believe they add tomato and onion (traditionally), but any pieces included were unnoticeable. So, like many restaurants that are open all day, you have to choose carefully to get the best flavor for your dollar. Definitely try the wings and if you like sweet drinks, get the Byssop. Otherwise, read the reviews and see what others recommend to maximize your visit. Review #487
Omg!! Our favorite restaurant of all on the beach!! It's Treasure Islands very own hidden gem. We have never had a bad meal or service! Put the Pearl on your to do list today!

We are new to Tampa and went to Thai Legacy to try their vegan menu. We had read good reviews on the Tampa Vegan Facebook group. After an exhausting day of moving and having 2 little ones in tow, Thai Legacy was a wonderful experience. The restaurant was very clean and the staff was very friendly and accommodating. The food was outstanding. I tried the sweet Chili Tofu. It was sweet, tangy and delightful. The portions were large and the food was high quality. Furthermore they went out of their way to take care, accommodate and amuse our grandchildren. I highly recommend Thai Legacy.
Excellent place for a lunch. Their buffet offers very good food, with wide variety of choices. Highly recommend.
Delicious goat roti! Would prefer the goat to not have the bone in it though. Im coming back to this spot though in the near future!

The service was the best we've had in the Boise area, right up there with Barbacoa and Chandler's, but price wise way more competitive with out skimping on selection, quality or quantity. Our waiter David was excellent, a Manhattan transplant, he was smooth and efficient without hovering. Most of the time, we barely knew he was there, but everything was perfect. We were pleased to find a good selection of vegetarian options, since two in our party were so inclined, that didn't comprise of only pasta or lettuce. Being the carnivore, I ordered the prosciutto wrapped chicken with polenta and broccolini and it was excellent. My girlfriend had the fettuccini with marinara which was very good and a salad which came with the house dressing that was fabulous! Friends of ours ordered the linguini with clam sauce and the grilled portabella mushroom respectively. I didn't try the mushroom, but the clams were very good, not over done, not under done, as is so common in restaurants here in Boise. The real surprise was the roasted beet salad, I highly recommend trying that! The wine selection was adequate and well priced. Our overall experience was first rate and we can't wait to eat there again!

The food here was surprisingly good. I love Thai food and have eaten at pretty much every Thai food in St. Louis. I got the Pad See Eu. The sauce was great and stir fried into the noodles, which I like. It was delicious. I had the chicken satay, which was pretty good as well. The rice wrapped spring rolls were pretty good as well. They has great flavor, but we're vegetarian. I prefer some pork or shrimp. The atmosphere is bland and it resembles a Chinese take out place with some dining. It is clean, but not really a date type of place. Id you are looking for some quick and great Thai food, go for it. You will not be disappointed.

This is a little hole in the wall right down from the hospital that has indoor seating and take out. Not much parking is available. I'd been fighting something viral, so was looking for some good Asian soup. We both had the meat soup, (Special Combo eye round streak, brisket, tension, and meatball, as described in the menu) fit $9.50, spring rolls for $2.99, and Vietnamese iced coffee). It was takeout, so they gave us the meats separate from the broth. I over heated the soup and ended up overcooking the beef, which I like medium rare. The portions are huge and have the usual pho vegetables and peppers you can add to taste The older lady who waited in us was very nice. There was a bit of a wait, so I had one of their iced coffees to kill time. They have a wide variety of coffees and bubble teas you can enjoy while waiting.
Great sevice, fast friendly, got the taste of abyssina to get a variety. Will return.

I had the opportunity to attend another Yelp event "Exploring Laotian Cuisine at Phan's Kitchen", and I have to say it did not disappoint. First, the kindness and warmth of the owner is very welcoming. Her love for what she does and sharing her native cuisine with people is inspiring. Now to the food. We had the papaya salad which was awesome! The simplicity yet flavor was incredible. Caution: the hottest version of this dish is made with ten Thai pepper, so this isn't your Thai hot as served at P.F. Chang or other American chain restaurants. This stuff is hot , so order with caution. Then we had the sausage, again fantastic. That was followed with Larb chicken served with sticky rice. Then to top it off we had the chicken jerky. Dinner was outstanding to say the least. I recommend this restaurant to all. If you have never tried Laotian cuisine, pique your curiosity and check out this restaurant, and if you have, well still try it. The restaurant is actually located inside the Washington square mall, right beside Target.

I love the food here! Remedy is currently in some kind of transition stage while undergoing renovations. The new atmosphere is nice and bright, a lot more open and clean looking than the last outfit. The woman taking orders was super pleasant and friendly which is a very nice surprise. On past visits I've always found the staff to be less than friendly and almost rude in some cases. I've come to expect unfriendly service here so that was a nice surprise. Food was delicious as always. My friend and I shared the butter chicken wrap, as they are decent sized portions and we can never finish the whole thing to ourselves. Its always so tasty and I especially love that sauce that goes with it. We both ordered the Kashmir Chai and it was good, although I didn't care much for the rose petals they top it with. It was great for presentation but they kind of took over the chai. I'd order it again without the rose. I would have given 5 stars but there's one thing I didn't like much about the place, I'm hoping its a temporary thing while reno's are happening. They are quite busy here and with all the new tables, which are totally necessary, there's very little room for customers to line up so people are constantly crowded and in each others way. Also the system of picking up your food isn't working... Instead of 2 chai's they only gave us one, no big deal but then when they went back to make another one there was no pick up system in place and people who had ordered after us kept jumping in to swipe the chai we were waiting for. A number system like they have is good if they actually reference the number when calling that an order is ready. All in all, its a good place with great food, even if its full of hipsters.

What can I say...today, we celebrated an early Father's Day and decided to end it with a trip to Bambu Drinks. It was our second time there, but it was the first time for our parents/brother. But really, what made this visit worth writing home about is PHILIP aka "State Champ!!" We've never met someone so passionate about his job and who exhibited such exemplary customer service! He explained the options to us and were so patient with our parents as they went back and forth on what they wanted in their drinks. It's telling when even our own parents could not stop raving about him and PUT IN A TIP (you know this is REAL when Asian parents tip on their own). We were definitely impressed and our experience with Philip will keep us coming back! Our dad even thought/asked if he was the owner because the way he treated us showed us that he cared. The drinks are awesome as well. We all enjoyed the options we chose, and they are generous with their "toppings." LOVE!! So glad this is near us! This place will give Kung Fu Tea a run for their money!

This was exactly what i was looking for. Tasty food in a nice 8 table small Thai place. The pot sticker app and pad thai hit the spot. At 3 sicy it was hot but did not hide the flavor. The raggoon and egg roll as part of the special were tiny... but for $1 well worth the money and a nice addition.

We had the falafel and gyro and enjoyed it very much. The hummus is really good as well. They gave us a spinach pie on the house - it was amazing. The Baklava was also really good - not too sweet. Glad there is a place to get a quick light meal in the Quarter that is open between 2:30 & 5:30. So many places are closed at this time.

I really like this place. I'm no expert on Indian cuisine, but this is just delicious food. Fresh, perfect naan (I'm sure there's a legit tandoor back there), creamy and spicy curries and decent selection of drinks. The rice really stands out too. Service can be a little hit or miss, but recently they've stepped up their game. Try the Lamb Korma: Soft, tender meat and a perfectly balanced sauce. Quick note: I know they have some kind of buffet lunch- this is not a good indicator of what these guys can deliver. Go for dinner and order something legit.

This is now my favorite Indian restaurant in the area. I had dinner here with a couple of friends on a Saturday, and everything we ordered was amazing. It's also a BYOB, so that is another plus. I have passed this place many times before but never considered eating here, but one of my friends suggested it, and I am really glad. We were offered complimentary papadums with 3 chutneys, which were all good. We tried a few different naan, with the Peshwari being my favorite. I ordered chicken biriyani, medium, which was a bit too spicy for me, but absolutely delicious. It was full of complex flavors and also generous on chicken, unlike most of the biriyani in other Indian Restaurants that are mostly just turmeric and has 2 pieces of chicken. My friends got a variety of curries and samosas, and everything was flavorful and cooked well. My only complaint is that the raita was a bit too loose, but it was really just a minor detail. Our server was super friendly and helpful - she may have been the owner as well? Everyone else was really friendly too, and they were very diligent about filling our water glasses. The restaurant was pretty filled by the time we left, so I am sure the secret is out that this place has great food. I am really excited to eat here again.

Lunch today was the 2nd time i've ventured to this establishment. the 1st time was "okay" but today was very, very pleasing to my palate. everything i ordered was on spot: from the thai iced tea and the spring rolls (vegetarian) to the vegetarian pad thai. my friend was introduced to thai food for the first time (she had a chicken dish w/ sweet & sour sauce) and she's now a fan. the dishes are reasonably priced, our service was mediocre (he forgot that my friend's dish was ordered with chicken), and it's very close to my neighborhood. i'll be coming back numerous times.

Food: 1/5 Service: 2/5 I read the reviews on Yelp and then found a Groupon, so I decided to give it a try. Needless to say, I definitely will NOT be returning. We ordered the atomic fire chicken and szechuan beef, both which were supposed to be spicy. The atomic chicken tasted more like sweet and sour chicken. The chicken itself was fine, but the breading was soggy and sauce was definitely on the sweet end. Almost resembled orange chicken. The szechuan beef wasn't spicy at all. The beef strips were tough and difficult to chew through and the sauce tasted like a mixture of other dishes combined. It tasted NOTHING LIKE szechuan sauce. After 3 bites, I threw out my lunch. I'm not sure how this place has received a decent rating, the food is really terrible. The lady at the counter was super nice and helpful. I rated the service 2/5 because I felt it took way too long to receive the food for a carry-out joint. (We waited 10-15 mins.)

I'm not a seasoned Thai eater but love the flavors here! Have eaten here periodically and it is always consistently good! You can't always get good fried wontons full of meat. The ones here are delicious. Be careful of the pad Thai noodles. They are sweet and nutty. This restaurant is my favorite Thai in Tampa.
GREAT food! Fast and fresh! Owner is very personable. Side items are a bit expensive in my opinion but you can get a filling and healthy lunch at a normal price!
